RESULTS: Analysis yielded five categories: (1) expectations and initial attitudes, (2) perceived effects and evaluation of the intervention, (3) therapeutic alliance and group cohesion, (4) experiences with the online format, and (5) anticipated longer-term effects. Participants reported that music facilitated emotional awareness, reflection, and interpersonal exchange. Therapeutic alliance and group cohesion were described as developing over the course of the intervention despite the online setting. The online format improved accessibility by overcoming geographical barriers and reducing physical demands, while reduced in-person interaction, technical issues, and limited program duration were experienced as constraints. Participants described intentions to continue using music- and mindfulness-based strategies in everyday life.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that therapeutic alliance, group cohesion, and relational processes can develop in video-based online group music therapy. Intervention structure, facilitation, and duration appear to play a central role in shaping participants' experiences. Video-based music therapy groups may provide a feasible psycho-oncological support option for patients who face barriers to in-person participation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The overarching intervention study was prospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00032339; registered 3 August 2023).

articles.title: A Study of Pulmonary Functions in Patients with Cirrhosis of the Liver and Its Correlation with the Severity of the Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cirrhosis of the liver is a progressive systemic disorder affecting multiple organ systems. Pulmonary dysfunction is a frequent extrahepatic complication that impacts prognosis, quality of life, and surgical risk. This study aimed to systematically evaluate pulmonary function abnormalities in cirrhotic patients and correlate their severity with disease progression using the Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) classification and the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) scores.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-center cross-sectional study was conducted on 118 adult non-smoking cirrhotic patients admitted to the Department of General Medicine at Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences, Ranchi. Clinical history, biochemical panels, arterial blood gas analysis (on room air and 100% O2), and spirometry were performed.

RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 52.4 ± 11.2 years. Abnormal spirometry was present in 72.9% (n = 86) of patients, with restrictive ventilatory defects being the most common pattern (61.0%, n = 72). Reduced Diffusion Capacity for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO <80% predicted) was observed in 71.2% (n = 84). Hypoxemia (PaO2 <80 mmHg) was present in 52.5% (n = 62), and 20.3% (n = 24) failed to achieve PaO2 >300 mmHg on 100% O2. Pulmonary parameters showed progressive worsening across CTP classes A, B, and C (forced vital capacity FVC % predicted: 82.4 ± 12.6% vs. 70.2 ± 14.8% vs. 56.8 ± 16.4%, P < 0.001). Patients with ascites exhibited significantly lower FVC compared to those without ascites (64.2 ± 17.4% vs. 82.6 ± 14.2%, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Pulmonary dysfunction, particularly restrictive defects and impaired gas exchange, is highly prevalent in patients with liver cirrhosis and strongly correlates with disease severity.

articles.title: Measuring Global Variability in Critical Care Capacity.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Assessment of Frailty and Its Association with the Severity of Liver Disease in Patients with Liver Cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is an important predictor of outcomes in patients with liver cirrhosis, reflecting reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability. Traditional scoring systems such as the Child-Pugh Score and MELD-Na focus on biochemical parameters and may not fully capture functional decline.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate frailty alongside cirrhosis severity using objective tools.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 204 patients with cirrhosis were enrolled after ethics approval. Baseline investigations and etiological assessment were performed. Disease severity was assessed using Child-Pugh and MELD-Na scores, whereas frailty was evaluated using the liver frailty index (LFI) and short physical performance battery (SPPB). Multivariable regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, etiology, serum albumin, and renal function was performed, with P < 0.05 considered significant.

RESULTS: Frailty was highly prevalent, with alcohol as the leading etiology (44.6%). By LFI, 75.0% were frail, 24.5% pre-frail, and 0.5% robust; 54.9% had low SPPB scores. Frailty worsened with increasing Child-Pugh class, with mean LFI rising (4.25-5.22) and SPPB declining (8.57-5.66; P < 0.001). Child-Pugh score correlated positively with LFI (r = 0.541) and negatively with SPPB (r = -0.450). Similar trends were seen across MELD-Na categories. On multivariable analysis, LFI independently predicted worse disease severity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] ≈6.0), whereas higher SPPB was protective (aOR ≈ 0.60; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Frailty is common in cirrhosis and can be reliably assessed using LFI and SPPB. Routine frailty assessment may improve risk stratification and guide management.

articles.title: Effect of Aromatherapy on Sleep Quality among Hospitalized Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbance is a frequent concern among hospitalized patients and is influenced by illness, anxiety, environmental noise, lighting, and routine medical care. Poor sleep during hospitalization can negatively affect immune function, wound healing, and recovery outcomes. Although pharmacological sleep aids are commonly used, they are often associated with adverse effects such as dependency, confusion, and increased risk of falls. Consequently, interest has increased in nonpharmacological interventions such as aromatherapy. Nonpharmacological interventions such as aromatherapy may offer a safe and effective alternative.

OBJECTIVE: To assess sleep quality among hospitalized patients, evaluate the effect of aromatherapy on sleep quality, and determine the association between sleep quality and selected demographic variables.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was conducted among 60 adult patients admitted to selected hospitals in Pimpri, Pune. Participants were selected using purposive sampling and allocated to experimental (n = 30) and control (n = 30) groups. The experimental group received lavender essential oil aromatherapy through diffusion for three consecutive nights, while the control group received routine care. Sleep quality was assessed using a standardized sleep quality assessment tool. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.

RESULTS: The experimental group showed a statistically significant improvement in sleep quality following aromatherapy, with mean scores increasing from 1.9 in the pretest to 3.0 in the posttest (t = 7.50, P < 0.05). No significant improvement was observed in the control group. No significant association was found between sleep quality and selected demographic variables.

CONCLUSION: Aromatherapy using lavender essential oil is an effective, safe, and noninvasive intervention for improving sleep quality among hospitalized patients.

articles.title: Tricuspid valve repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis of different surgical techniques and their long-term results.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The degree of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is related to mortality. The majority of TR is secondary, and surgery consists mainly of annuloplasty repair (TVr), but repair durability is a prerequisite for a lasting treatment effect. We performed a systematic assessment of TVr durability.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed (MEDLINE, Cochrane Library and Web of Science). Follow-up of TVr techniques and TR recurrence rates were used to estimate incidence rates which were then meta-analyzed using a single-arm meta-analysis model with random-effects. Comparisons between techniques were performed to obtain incidence rate ratios (IRR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 50 studies met the criteria for inclusion (5 randomized and 45 observational), with 15,563 patients, representing 79,763 patient-years (mean follow-up: 3.9 years). Overall recurrence rate was 2.73 per 100 person-years (95% CI 2.15-3.47). Ring annuloplasty had lowest rates (1.81; 95% CI 1.17-2.79), followed by band (2.58; 95% CI 1.66-4.00) and suture (4.06; 95% CI 2.93-5.64). There was a large difference in treatment effects within and between groups (P for interaction=0.011). Compared to suture, ring annuloplasty was associated with lower TR recurrence (IRR 0.45; P = 0.003), but not versus band (IRR 0.71; P = 0.26). There was no difference between band and suture (IRR 0.63; P = 0.12).

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term durability of TVr techniques is extremely heterogeneous. We identified the use of rigid rings and flexible bands as being associated with lower recurrence rates compared to suture techniques.

articles.title: Role of Platelet Count and Platelet Volume Indices in Ischemic Heart Disease: An Observational Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with platelet activation playing a crucial role in its pathogenesis. Platelet indices such as mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), platelet-large cell ratio (P-LCR), and plateletcrit (PCT) are increasingly recognized as simple and cost-effective markers of platelet activity and thrombotic risk.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 180 participants divided into three groups: chronic stable angina (CSA), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and healthy controls (60 each). Platelet count and platelet volume indices were measured using an automated hematology analyzer, and statistical analysis was performed to compare differences among groups.

RESULTS: Platelet count was significantly lower in the ACS group compared to CSA and controls. In contrast, MPV, PDW, P-LCR, and PCT were significantly elevated in ACS, reflecting increased platelet activation. MPV emerged as an independent predictor of ischemic heart disease. Among all parameters, P-LCR and MPV demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy. Platelet indices also showed association with cardiovascular risk factors and disease severity.

CONCLUSION: Platelet volume indices, particularly MPV and P-LCR, are reliable and easily accessible markers of platelet activation in ischemic heart disease. They may serve as useful adjuncts in diagnosis and risk stratification in both stable and acute coronary conditions.

articles.title: Clinical Profile and Outcome of Acute Viral Hepatitis in Hospitalized Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute viral hepatitis (AVH) is a major public health concern in developing countries, including India, where it is caused by the hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E viruses. Documenting the clinical profile and outcomes of hospitalized patients with AVH in a systematic way is important for guiding management decisions and informing public health strategies.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective observational study carried out at the Department of Medicine and Gastroenterology, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital Ludhiana, over 12 months (May 2024 to May 2025). A total of 203 adults aged 18 years or older with serologically confirmed AVH were enrolled. Clinical features, biochemical parameters, complications, and outcomes, including discharge, death, and discharge against medical advice, were recorded. Data were analyzed using SPSS v26 with Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests; P < 0.05 was taken as statistically significant.

RESULTS: The mean age was 26.1 ± 6.3 years, and males predominated at 75.4%. Hepatitis A virus (HAV) was the leading cause at 83.3%, followed by hepatitis E virus (HEV) at 8.4% and mixed HAV-HEV co-infection in another 8.4%. Jaundice (93.6%), nausea (86.7%), myalgia (77.3%), and fever (69.5%) were the most common presenting symptoms. Acute liver failure (ALF) occurred in 27.6% of patients and was the most important predictor of outcome; all 11 deaths (5.4%) were confined to the ALF group. Hemolysis was found in 15.3% and was linked to significantly worse outcomes. In all, 89.7% of patients were discharged, 5.4% died, and 4.9% left against medical advice.

CONCLUSION: HAV is now the dominant cause of hospitalized AVH in young adults in this region, reflecting a shift from the traditionally childhood-onset pattern. ALF is the critical determinant of mortality, and early identification of high-risk features such as encephalopathy, coagulopathy, hemolysis, and renal dysfunction is essential for timely intervention. Hepatitis A vaccination and improvements in water safety and sanitation are urgently needed.

articles.title: Association of Serum Adiponectin Levels with Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common debilitating microvascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Adiponectin, an adipocyte-derived hormone with insulin-sensitizing and anti-inflammatory properties, is considered a potential biomarker for neuropathy, but findings remain inconsistent. This study evaluated the association between serum adiponectin levels and DPN among adults with T2DM.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted among 60 adults with T2DM at a tertiary care center in South India. Participants were divided into two groups: with clinically diagnosed DPN (n = 30) and without DPN (n = 30). Serum adiponectin was measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Demographic, anthropometric, glycemic, and lipid parameters were compared between groups. Correlation analyses, receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curve evaluation, and multivariate logistic regression were performed.

RESULTS: Participants with DPN were older, had a longer duration of diabetes, and exhibited higher total cholesterol levels than those without DPN. Serum adiponectin levels were significantly higher in the DPN group (8.05 ± 3.95 µg/mL) compared with the non-DPN group (6.29 ± 2.71 µg/mL; P = 0.049). Adiponectin showed a significant positive correlation with glycated hemoglobin (r = 0.275, P = 0.033) and a borderline negative correlation with triglycerides. ROC analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.634 for adiponectin alone and 0.823 for the multivariate model. In logistic regression, only the duration of diabetes remained an independent predictor of DPN.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum adiponectin levels were elevated in individuals with DPN, possibly a compensatory response to longstanding metabolic stress. Despite diagnostic utility, adiponectin was not an independent predictor of neuropathy. Adiponectin may serve as an adjunctive biomarker when integrated with clinical and metabolic indicators.

articles.title: Optimizing Door-to-Balloon Time in STEMI Care through Structured Quality Improvement at a Tertiary Centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Door-to-balloon (DTB) time is a key performance metric in the management of ST-elevation myocardial infarction, with shorter times strongly associated with improved myocardial salvage and reduced mortality. International cardiology guidelines recommend achieving DTB within 90 minutes for patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention. This quality improvement (QI) initiative aimed to identify determinants of delayed DTB time in a tertiary care hospital and implement structured system-level interventions.

METHODS: Root-cause analysis revealed delays related to financial clearance processes, off-hour Cath lab staffing, concurrent laboratory use, and delayed arrival of consultants and anesthesiologists. Interventions included workflow standardization, staff duty rosters, night supervision protocols, and real-time communication channels linking emergency, cardiology, Cath lab, and administrative teams. Monthly DTB times were monitored from September 2022 to December 2025.

RESULTS: Median DTB times exceeded 100 min during the baseline period (101-111 min) but decreased to 69-84.6 min following implementation of the QI interventions. Achievement of the recommended DTB target (<90 min) became more consistent throughout the postintervention period.

CONCLUSION: A structured multidisciplinary QI strategy focusing on financial workflow reform, staffing readiness, and real-time interdepartmental communication was associated with substantial and sustained reductions in DTB time at a tertiary care center. Continuous monitoring, protocol reinforcement, and adaptive process refinement were essential to maintaining performance near internationally recommended targets.

articles.title: Changes in liver steatosis and liver stiffness following Empagliflozin treatment in patients with MASLD and type 2 diabetes: A single-arm pre-post study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), being linked to a higher risk for the development of liver-related and cardiovascular diseases. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors such as empagliflozin have demonstrated possible hepatoprotective effects in previous research. The purpose of this study was to evaluate changes in liver enzymes, hepatic steatosis, and liver stiffness following 12 weeks of empagliflozin treatment in patients with T2DM and MASLD.

METHODS: In this nonrandomized, single-arm interventional study, 30 patients with T2DM and MASLD were treated simultaneously with empagliflozin 25 mg/day for 12 weeks in addition to the ongoing management. Liver function tests (ALT and AST), hepatic fat content (CAP score), and liver stiffness (LSM) were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks treatment.

RESULTS: There were significant decreases in mean AST (80.27 ± 10.51 vs. 45.20 ± 3.20 U/L, P < 0.001) and ALT (86.33 ± 9.11 vs. 44.63 ± 3.62 U/L, P < 0.001) levels after treatment. The CAP score decreased from 321.83 ± 49.36 to 261.33 ± 35.14 (P < 0.001), and the LSM value decreased from 7.22 ± 1.04 to 6.24 ± 0.41 (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this single-arm pre-post study, 12 weeks of empagliflozin treatment was associated with significant reductions in liver enzyme levels, hepatic steatosis, and liver stiffness in patients with T2DM and MASLD. Larger controlled studies are required to determine whether these changes are attributable to empagliflozin and to assess their durability.

articles.title: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii-associated 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid protects against sepsis via ABCC1-mediated suppression of MAPK/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a modifiable determinant of sepsis susceptibility and outcomes, yet protective commensals and microbiota-associated metabolites with actionable host mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Here, fecal 16S rRNA sequencing of septic and non-septic patients revealed a marked depletion of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii during sepsis. Oral administration of F. prausnitzii improved survival and alleviated multiorgan injury in mice subjected to cecal ligation and puncture. Untargeted metabolomics and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry identified 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid (18β-GA) as a major metabolite enriched in F. prausnitzii culture supernatants, and exogenous 18β-GA recapitulated key protective effects in vivo. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, 18β-GA reduced pro-inflammatory mediator expression and suppressed mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation. Proteomics-guided prioritization and complementary pharmacological and genetic validation implicated ATP-binding cassette subfamily C member 1 (ABCC1) as a mediator involved in the protective effects of 18β-GA. Genetic silencing of ABCC1 attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of 18β-GA, while pharmacological inhibition of ABCC1 by probenecid (PBN) and MK-571 partially reproduced the protective effects of 18β-GA. Collectively, these findings identify a F. prausnitzii-18β-GA-associated ABCC1 regulatory axis that contributes to the control of septic inflammation and highlight microbiota-derived metabolites as potential modulators of host inflammatory responses.IMPORTANCESepsis is a life-threatening syndrome with limited effective therapies beyond supportive care. Gut microbiota disruption is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to sepsis, but the protective microbes, effector metabolites, and host pathways involved are not well understood. Here, we show that F. prausnitzii is markedly depleted in sepsis and that supplementation with this commensal improves outcomes in experimental sepsis. We further identify 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid as a microbiota-associated metabolite with anti-inflammatory and organ-protective activity and implicate ABCC1 as a functionally relevant host target. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how protective commensals can influence sepsis progression and support microbiome-informed, host-directed therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Strongyloides stercoralis VirClia IgG monotest for the diagnosis of strongyloidiasis in a diverse clinical cohort.
articles.abstract: Strongyloides stercoralis is an intestinal nematode with the capacity for lifelong autoinfection and potentially fatal hyperinfection in immunocompromised patients. In non-or-low-endemic settings, serology is central to diagnosis, but most current assays are batch-dependent, labor-intensive, and restricted to referral centers. There is an unmet need for a rapid, robust, random-access screening test. To evaluate the clinical and diagnostic performance of the Strongyloides VirClia IgG monotest, a CE-IVD chemiluminescent immunoassay (Vircell), in a non-endemic setting, we tested stored sera from microbiologically confirmed strongyloidiasis cases, external quality assessment samples, healthy controls, and a broad disease-control panel covering viral, bacterial, protozoal, and other helminth infections. All samples were tested on the VirClia Lotus analyzer and compared with a previously published in-house enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. A total of 69 confirmed cases and 210 controls (171 disease controls, 39 healthy controls) were analyzed. Sensitivity was 98.6% (68/69; 95% confidence interval [CI] 92.2%-99.7%), and specificity was 98.1% (206/210; 95% CI 95.2%-99.3%). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.985 (95% CI 0.961-1.000), with a high positive (LR+ = 52) and near-perfect negative (LR- = 0.015) likelihood ratio. All four false positives occurred in patients with concurrent parasitic infections; cross-reactivity was otherwise only sporadic. Inter-laboratory comparison showed comparable results. The Strongyloides VirClia IgG monotest showed excellent diagnostic accuracy in a diverse, clinically relevant cohort. Combined with its random-access format and short turnaround time, the assay is well suited as a first-line screening tool for strongyloidiasis in non-endemic settings.IMPORTANCEStrongyloides stercoralis is an intestinal roundworm with a substantial global disease burden. Infection is typically chronic and largely asymptomatic, but in severely immunocompromised patients-such as those on immunosuppressive therapy or with hematological malignancies-it can progress to a hyperinfection syndrome, carrying a high risk of complications and mortality. As immunosuppressant use rises and treatment options for hematological malignancies expand, the at-risk population for Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome continues to grow. Medical microbiological laboratories therefore need a reliable and sensitive strongyloidiasis screening assay with a short turnaround time. In this study, we show that the S. stercoralis VirClia IgG monotest can meet this need, with high diagnostic accuracy in a relevant and diverse clinical cohort. These findings support adoption by other laboratories after local verification, without the need for an extensive in-house validation as presented here.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Rapid antigen tests are widely used for point-of-care diagnosis of respiratory tract infection (RTI) in children, but how the sensitivity is influenced by viral load has not been comprehensively characterized across multiple pediatric respiratory viruses. In this prospective, paired-specimen study conducted at the pediatric center, two simultaneous nasopharyngeal swabs were obtained from children with RTI. One swab was tested using antigen-based rapid test kits (ImunoAce series, Tauns Laboratories, Inc.) for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and respiratory syncytial virus; the other was tested using the FilmArray Respiratory Panel (bioMérieux). Specimens positive by either method underwent confirmatory quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load. Sensitivity was stratified by viral load. A total of 1,584 paired specimens from 1,232 children (median age: 3.0 years [IQR: 1.0-6.0]; 53.7% male) were analyzed. Sensitivity of the antigen tests ranged from 20.6% (adenovirus) to 79.7% (hMPV), while specificity exceeded 99% for all six targets and overall agreement ranged from 90.7% to 99.0%. For every virus, antigen test positivity increased steeply with viral load, approaching 90-100% at viral loads ≥106-107 copies/100 µL and falling below 50% at loads ≤104-105 copies/100 µL. Antigen-based rapid tests for common pediatric respiratory viruses showed high specificity and viral-load-dependent sensitivity, detecting nearly all specimens with high viral load regardless of the target virus. These findings support a role for antigen testing in identifying children with the highest viral burden-who are most likely to have acute infection.

IMPORTANCE: The sensitivity of rapid antigen tests for respiratory viruses relative to PCR-based testing has been incompletely characterized. This study evaluated antigen tests for six common pediatric respiratory viruses-SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus-against a multiplex PCR reference standard across 1,584 clinical specimens and linked test performance directly to quantitative viral load. We show that antigen test sensitivity is strongly and consistently dependent on viral load, approaching 90-100% at high viral loads with very high specificity across all six targets. These findings clarify the clinical role of rapid antigen testing: it reliably identifies children with the highest viral burden, who are most likely to have acute, symptomatic infection warranting immediate clinical action.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Bruker IR Biotyper for Streptococcus pyogenes emm typing.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus [GAS]) is a human pathogen with invasive potential. Investigation of isolate relatedness by emm gene sequencing is time- and cost-intensive, warranting the evaluation of alternative technologies for this purpose. In this study, we evaluated the level of discrimination of predominant GAS isolates that can be achieved by Fourier transform-infrared spectroscopy on the Bruker IR Biotyper platform. Separate emm pattern, emm type, and emm1 sublineage classifiers were created and cross-validated using spectra from isolates with known emm types. Next, emm pattern and emm type classifiers were combined into a tiered classifier that was externally validated using novel isolates and evaluated in a mock outbreak scenario. Emm pattern and type classifiers demonstrated >95% accuracy and class precision during cross-validation. The emm1 sublineage classifier had poor accuracy (<90%) and was excluded from the final tiered classifier. The tiered classifier performed well during external validation, with overall accuracies of 98% and 96% for emm pattern and type, respectively. Individual emm type class recall was variable and impacted by the total number of isolates included. The tiered classifier demonstrated 100% accuracy, class recall, and precision in the simulated outbreak. This study demonstrates that the Bruker IR Biotyper can accurately group GAS isolates to emm type when trained with a tiered classifier model. Moreover, it can be used as a rapid and accurate method to exclude GAS isolates of different emm patterns from outbreak strains and therefore has utility in point prevalence screening and contact tracing during outbreak management.

IMPORTANCE: Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus [GAS]) is a human pathogen capable of causing localized as well as invasive infection. The latter is associated with significant mortality and, without correct infection control measures, can result in bacterial transmission to close contacts. Management of a GAS outbreak requires the investigator to demonstrate relatedness between bacterial isolates collected from different patients. Typing is based on molecular analysis of part of the M protein gene (emm) at centralized reference centers. The turnaround time for testing is often quite prolonged, leading to delays in outbreak recognition and patient care cascades. This study therefore sought to first evaluate the ability of a novel Fourier transform-infrared spectroscopy system-the Bruker IR Biotyper-to accurately identify GAS emm types. Secondarily, we validated a GAS classifier model using both emm types and broader emm patterns as a means by which to accurately, and rapidly, categorize isolates.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Multimodal Educational Program on Asthma Control, Quality of Life, and Medication Adherence among Children Diagnosed with Asthma: A Study Protocol for Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximate 80% of cases of poor adherence still occur due to improper inhaler technique and numerous studies show that one of the most important aspects of managing asthma is patient education.

AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: The study aims to evaluate the impact of Multimodal Educational Program [MEP] on asthma control, quality of life, and medication adherence among children diagnosed with asthma.

METHOD/DESIGN: This Randomized Controlled Trial (Parallel group, pre-test post-test design) targets children of age group 7-15 Years, diagnosed with asthma and visiting OPD with their parents. Randomization will be done by adopting the computerized randomized block design. Sequentially Numbered, Opaque, and Sealed Envelopes will be used to ensure allocation concealment. Interventional group will receive Multimodal Educational Program [MEP] that will be provided via VARK Model designed by Neil Fleming. Data on Asthma Control test, quality of life and medication adherence will be collected at baseline, one month, and three months by the data collector who will be blinded.

DISCUSSION: Asthma is a prevalent illness in children, and even with the availability of excellent treatments, the incidence and severity of asthma-related sufferings remain unchanged. Studies show that one of the most important aspects of managing asthma is patient education. This study is planned considering the need and significance of educational interventions among children diagnosed with asthma which is crucial for keeping an eye on symptoms, asthma control and to prevent exacerbations.

articles.title: Antibiotic-loaded cement spacers: a comprehensive review.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYPeriprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) have become a costly complication of total joint arthroplasty, and the incidence continues to rise, given an increasing elderly population requiring total knee and total hip replacements. Traditionally, two-stage exchange (TSE) is the standard of care to combat chronic PJIs. The first stage of a TSE is defined by the removal of the prosthesis with implantation of an antibiotic-loaded cement spacer. There is a lack of guidance regarding the dosing of antimicrobials in cement spacers and a lack of safety data available in the infectious diseases literature. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of antibiotic-loaded cement spacers (ALCS) by reviewing published literature from peer-reviewed journals dating from 1988 to 2024 and discussing the authors' clinical experience. It was noted that with improvements to ALCS over the years, associated complications also evolved. Not only do mechanical challenges such as increased joint subluxation persist, but also complications of nephrotoxicity and allergic reactions occur due to unknown levels of systemic absorption of antibiotics. A multidisciplinary approach involving orthopedic surgeons, infectious diseases specialists, and pharmacists, in conjunction with patient-specific anti-microbial spacer dosing, would likely lead to improved outcomes in patients with chronic PJIs.

articles.title: Musculoskeletal Disorders in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prevalence, Pattern, and Association with Diabetes Mellitus Duration and Glycemic Control in a South-east Nigerian Tertiary Hospital: A Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders are increasingly recognized complications of chronic hyperglycemia in persons living with type 2 diabetes mellitus (people living with diabetes [PLWD]) resulting in various forms of disability. Data from South-East Nigeria are limited. This research aimed at comparing the burden, pattern, and associations of MSK disorders in PLWD with nondiabetic controls.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This comparative, cross-sectional research was conducted at a leading tertiary hospital in South-east Nigeria between January 2017 and July 2017. A total of 300 participants, (equally divided into PLWD and controls, matched for age, sex, and body mass index), were recruited. MSK disorders were assessed using the gait, arms, legs, and spine screening tool, and detailed examination. Participants were classified using standard diagnostic criteria. Glycemic control was assessed using glycated hemoglobin. Logistic regression analysis evaluated associations between MSK disorders, duration of diabetes, and glycemic control.

RESULTS: MSK disorders were significantly more prevalent among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) participants than comparative nondiabetic group (48.0% vs. 18.0%; odds ratio [OR]: 4.21, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.49-7.11; P = 0.001). Knee osteoarthritis (OA) (18.0%) was the most common disorder, followed by limited joint mobility (9.3%). Limited joint mobility (OR 5.52), adhesive capsulitis (OR 4.21), and knee OA (OR 3.87) were significantly associated with T2DM. Among diabetics, disease duration >5 years (OR 4.60, 95% CI 2.04-10.39) and poor glycemic control (OR 4.28, 95% CI 2.02-9.06) independently predicted MSK disorders. Sociodemographic factors were not significantly associated.

CONCLUSION: MSK disorders were observed to be common among this cohort of T2DM patients and occurred significantly more frequently than in the nondiabetic individuals. Longer disease duration and poor glycemic control were key predictors. Improving the standards of diabetes care in Nigeria and regular assessment for MSK disorders are advocated.

articles.title: Steatosis‑associated immune alterations and LIGHT‑signaling in hepatic neoplastic disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with higher incidence of hepatic neoplasia and may influence the tumor microenvironment through immune-metabolic mechanisms. In this study, the contribution of intrahepatic natural killer T (NKT) cells and the LIGHT/LTβR/HVEM axis to MASLD severity in patients with primary hepatic cancer (PHC) or colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRCLM) was investigated. Liver biopsies were analyzed and stratified by intrahepatic triglyceride (TG) content into Group I (LIGHT/LTBR/HVEM expression were assessed. Group II showed higher MASLD activity score (MAS), with the greatest score in CRCLM patients. Fibrosis percentage did not differ between groups, although MMP9 and SOX9 gene expression was elevated in Group II, consistent with enhanced extracellular matrix remodeling. The LIGHT/LTBR/HVEM axis gene expression did not differ between groups, but PHC patients from Group II displayed increased LIGHT/LTBR gene expression. Hepatic NKT2 cells were significantly elevated in Group II, more pronounced in CRCLM. In group II, NK-cell abundance inversely correlated with HVEM expression, an association that remained significant after FDR correction. In addition, TP53 mRNA levels were positively associated with expression of components of the LIGHT/LTBR/HVEM axis. Our data reveal associations between MASLD severity, intrahepatic immune-cell composition and the LIGHT/LTBR/HVEM pathway in patients with hepatic neoplastic disease, supporting further investigation of NKT cell subsets and LIGHT signaling as potential markers of the immune-metabolic alterations accompanying steatotic liver disease in this setting.

articles.title: Clinico-epidemiological Spectrum of Candidemia in the Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Observational Study from a Tertiary Care Center of Central India.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Candidemia represents the most common healthcare-associated bloodstream infection globally, with significant morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs). This study aimed to evaluate the clinico-epidemiological characteristics, species distribution, antifungal susceptibility patterns, and mortality predictors of ICU-acquired candidemia from a tertiary care hospital in Central India.

METHODS: The prospective observational study enrolled adult patients (≥18 years) admitted to the ICU with clinical sepsis. ICU-acquired candidemia was defined as a positive blood culture for Candida species developing ≥48 h after ICU admission. Demographic data, risk factors, antibiotic susceptibility, and clinical outcomes were systematically recorded. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 25.0.

RESULTS: Among 1128 ICU patients with clinical sepsis admitted during the study period, 55 developed candidemia (55/1128, 4.88%). Nonalbicans Candida (NAC) species predominated (81.8%), with Candida parapsilosis being the most common (30.9%), followed by Candida tropicalis (27.3%), and Candida albicans (18.2%). The major risk factors included Foley catheterization (100%), recent antibiotic exposure (67.3%), diabetes (56.4%), chronic kidney disease (CKD)/dialysis, and central venous catheterization (38.2% each). Significant antifungal resistance was observed in NAC species, particularly Candida auris and Candida guilliermondii, showing complete resistance to fluconazole and voriconazole. Overall mortality was 23.6%, with Candida glabrata showing 100% mortality. Factors significantly associated with mortality on univariate analysis included diabetes (P = 0.003), CKD requiring dialysis (P = 0.001), mechanical ventilation (P < 0.001), and central venous catheterization (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates a significant epidemiological shift toward NAC species in ICU-acquired candidemia, with emerging multidrug-resistant pathogens posing therapeutic challenges. Enhanced infection control measures, routine susceptibility testing, and species-specific treatment strategies are essential for improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Parental stress and parent-child dyadic outcomes in preterm populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite established theoretical links between parental stress and parent-child dyadic functioning, no systematic review has examined these associations in preterm samples. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on associations between parental stress and dyadic outcomes across the first year of life with preterm parent-child dyads.

METHODS: Four databases were searched through May 2026 (INPLASY #2025110019). Eligible studies assessed parental stress and parent-child dyadic outcomes in preterm samples within the first year of life. Effects were synthesized based on the timing of stress and dyadic outcome measurement. Parental stress was categorized into four types [parenting, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)-specific, general, and perceived social support] and dyadic outcomes were categorized into three types (caregiving quality, dyadic coordination, and attachment). Risk of bias/certainty of evidence was assessed.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included (N = 3,079 dyads). A significant small association between parental stress and dyadic outcomes was found during NICU hospitalization (r = -.20; low heterogeneity) and at 0-6 months corrected age (r = -.11) postdischarge. No reliable association was found at 7-12 months corrected age.

CONCLUSIONS: Parental stress is most reliably linked to dyadic functioning when measured concurrently during NICU hospitalization and did not reliably predict postdischarge dyadic outcomes. Parenting stress and caregiving quality showed the most consistent associations descriptively, though differences across stress types were not statistically supported. Findings suggest that the NICU stay may be an important period for supporting dyadic functioning, with attention to parenting stress and moment-to-moment caregiver responsiveness.

articles.title: Influence of Pharmacogenomic Variants on Glycemic Control in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Exploratory Association Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inter-individual variability in glycemic control among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may partly be explained by pharmacogenomic differences affecting antidiabetic drug response. This study investigated the association of pharmacogenomic variants with glycemic control and their potential role in personalized diabetes management.

METHODOLOGY: Thirty-two pharmacogenomically relevant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) involved in metformin transport, insulin secretion, glucose metabolism, drug metabolism, and therapeutic response were analyzed using microarray-derived genotype data following standard quality control procedures. Associations between individual SNPs and glycemic control status were evaluated using logistic regression to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Multiple testing was addressed using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction.

RESULTS: None of the evaluated variants remained statistically significant after FDR correction (FDR > 0.05). However, several SNPs demonstrated suggestive associations with glycemic control. The strongest risk association was observed for FTO rs9939609 (OR = 1.586, 95% CI: 0.936-2.688, P = 0.086), followed by SLC22A1 rs628031 (OR = 1.406), SLC22A2 rs316019 (OR = 1.370), and rs7439366 (OR = 1.525). Protective trends were observed for IRS1 rs1801278 (OR = 0.297), ADIPOQ rs2241766 (OR = 0.483), CYP3A4 rs2740574 (OR = 0.613), INSR rs1799817 (OR = 0.660), and ATM rs11212617 (OR = 0.726). Variants in metformin transporter genes (SLC22A1, SLC22A2, SLC47A1, and ATM) demonstrated effect sizes consistent with previously reported pharmacogenomic associations, whereas sulfonylurea-related variants (KCNJ11, ABCC8) showed minimal association with glycemic control.

CONCLUSION: Although no pharmacogenomic variant achieved statistical significance after correction for multiple testing, several biologically plausible variants demonstrated suggestive associations with glycemic outcomes. These findings support further validation in larger cohorts and highlight the potential contribution of pharmacogenomics to precision medicine and individualized antidiabetic therapy in T2DM.

articles.title: Underlying Mechanisms of Helicobacter pylori in Caries Progression and the Corresponding Dual-Responsive Hydrogel-Based Intervention.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infects nearly half of the global population. Given that H. pylori is considered poorly adapted to the oral environment, previous studies have mainly focused on gastric infection. By contrast, how H. pylori persists in the oral cavity and relates to oral diseases remains unclear. This study investigates the role of H. pylori in caries progression. The results show that H. pylori is retained within Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) biofilms, and its presence is associated with transcriptional remodeling in S. mutans, alongside increased overall cariogenic potential of the mixed biofilm. In a rat caries model, H. pylori co-colonization aggravates caries progression and oral microbiota dysbiosis. To address this pathological niche, a multifunctional hydrogel, termed GPAM, is designed by integrating a Cu2O@Pt heterojunction (MCP) with amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP). Under activation by yellow light and ultrasound, MCP generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) to disrupt S. mutans-H. pylori mixed biofilms. Meanwhile, released Cu2+ reduces H. pylori urease activity, and ACP promotes tooth remineralization. GPAM also shows microbiota-modulating potential. Together, these findings provide insight into H. pylori-associated caries progression and support GPAM as a multifunctional therapeutic strategy for mixed biofilms and caries-related damage.

articles.title: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness and Plaque Burden in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Hospital-based Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) accelerates atherosclerosis, and carotid ultrasonographic assessment of intima-media thickness (IMT) and plaque offers a noninvasive method to detect subclinical vascular disease and stratify cardiovascular risk.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the IMT of the common and internal carotid arteries between patients with T2DM and age- and sex-matched healthy individuals.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center, hospital-based analytical case-control study included 40 patients with T2DM and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical and biochemical assessment, and carotid IMT (common and internal carotid arteries) and plaque were measured using high-resolution B-mode ultrasonography.

RESULTS: Among 80 participants (40 T2DM cases and 40 controls), the groups were comparable in age (52.4 ± 14.9 vs. 51.7 ± 18.7 years; P = 0.843), sex and lifestyle factors. Body mass index was slightly higher in cases (26.9 ± 4.9 vs. 25.1 ± 3.0 kg/m2; P = 0.052). Cases had significantly higher systolic blood pressure/diastolic blood pressure (142.6 ± 11.4/87.3 ± 4.6 vs. 127.4 ± 7.2/84.1 ± 5.6 mmHg) and markedly higher glycemic indices (fasting blood sugar 160.9 vs. 90.1; postprandial blood sugar 224.9 vs. 109.9 mg/dL; all P ≤ 0.006). Triglycerides, very-low-density lipoprotein and total cholesterol were higher in cases, while high-density lipoprotein and low-density lipoprotein were similar. Mean carotid IMT was greater in cases (0.72 ± 0.17 vs. 0.61 ± 0.19 mm; P = 0.006) and plaque was more frequent (50% vs. 17.5%; P = 0.002). IMT was not significantly associated with age or lifestyle factors. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed fair discrimination (area under the curve 0.686; P = 0.004); IMT >0.62 mm yielded 70% sensitivity and 65% specificity.

CONCLUSION: Patients with T2DM had significantly higher carotid IMT and plaque prevalence than controls, supporting carotid ultrasonography as a useful tool for detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and aiding cardiovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: Negative Pressure Wound Therapy or Conventional Dressing? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis for Wound Therapy in Excision Surgeries for Pilonidal Disease.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPilonidal disease is a debilitating condition which is caused by an inflammatory process due to the penetration of a hair into the sacrococcygeal region. Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has been growing in several types of surgical wounds; however, the evidence for its use in excision surgery for pilonidal disease is still small and heterogeneous. We conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing this wound closure approach.MethodsPubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from inception to December 2025 to identify studies comparing excision surgery of sacrococcygeal pilonidal disease with NPWT and this surgical technique without NPWT. Statistical synthesis was performed using a random effects model, with results expressed as risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with their 95% confidence intervals.ResultsFive studies in which 244 patients were reported in our analysis; 123 (50.4%) underwent NPWT and 121 (49.6%) underwent conventional dressings. Complete healing time was significantly shorter in the NPWT group compared with conventional dressing, both RCT analyses (MD: -15.88 days; 95% CI: -30.04 to -1.72), observational studies (MD: -31.39 days; 95% CI: -55.03 to -7.75), and overall analysis (MD: -24.02 days; 95% CI: -40.75 to -7.29). There was no statistical difference in terms of recurrence (RR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.15-3.36) and postoperative infection (RR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.20-1.25).ConclusionNegative pressure wound therapy may shorten healing time following open excision for pilonidal disease, but the available evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and methodologically weak.

articles.title: Perimenopause and cardiometabolic risk: emerging evidence, therapeutic opportunities and unanswered questions.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.abstract: Perimenopause is increasingly recognized as a critical period for cardiometabolic health. During the years surrounding the final menstrual period, adverse changes in lipid profiles, insulin sensitivity, body composition and vascular function accelerate beyond those expected from aging alone, concurrent with the emergence and peak severity of menopause symptoms. Accumulating evidence suggests that vasomotor symptoms and sleep disturbance are associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Mechanistic data indicate that autonomic dysregulation, inflammation and neuroendocrine systems may represent shared pathways linking symptom burden and cardiometabolic dysfunction. Complementing these findings, prospective studies demonstrate that poor cardiovascular health and metabolic dysfunction may predict subsequent symptom development, suggesting that cardiometabolic health influences the menopause transition experience itself. Together, these findings support a model in which perimenopause represents a physiologic convergence point where symptom burden and cardiometabolic risk intersect, with implications for symptom management and primary prevention. However, major evidence gaps remain, including the absence of interventional studies during perimenopause and uncertainty regarding whether these relationships are causal or therapeutically modifiable. Future research should determine whether targeting cardiometabolic health during this window can improve both cardiovascular outcomes and the symptom experience of the menopause transition.

articles.title: CT-Guided Navigation for Complex Retropharyngeal Abscesses: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo describe our experience with CT-based neuronavigation-assisted transoral drainage for anatomically complex pediatric retropharyngeal abscesses (RPAs) and to propose selection criteria for its use. Pediatric deep neck infections, particularly RPAs, pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because of complex anatomy and proximity to the internal carotid artery, internal jugular vein, and lower cranial nerves. Standard management combines intravenous antibiotics with selective surgical drainage; however, obscured landmarks, absent mucosal bulging, and adjacent neurovascular structures can compromise accurate localization, especially in high, deep, or multiloculated collections.MethodsWe reviewed three children (aged 12 months to 12 years) who presented with multiloculated RPAs that enlarged or failed to improve despite intravenous antibiotics, including collections extending toward the skull base and adjacent to the internal carotid artery. All underwent transoral incision and drainage with intraoperative CT-based image-guided navigation using a dedicated navigation acquisition protocol.ResultsNavigation enabled complete evacuation of all collections without intraoperative complications. Recovery was uneventful, and follow-up showed complete resolution without recurrence. While most superficial RPAs can be managed safely with standard transoral drainage, high, deep, multiloculated, or distant collections increase the risk of incomplete drainage and complications. Image-guided navigation improved localization and trajectory planning. Because navigation platforms are optimized for rigid (bony) landmarks, accuracy may degrade with head repositioning, retraction, or soft-tissue shift after decompression; therefore, frequent accuracy checks and limited head manipulation are essential. Thin-slice CT navigation protocols may increase radiation exposure, which should be balanced against the morbidity of incomplete drainage, repeat surgery, or external approaches.ConclusionsCT-based neuronavigation-assisted transoral drainage is a safe, precise, minimally invasive option for selected complex pediatric RPAs-particularly skull-base-directed, deep, multiloculated, or mucosally distant collections without obvious bulging.

articles.title: Prevalence and Measurement of the Victim-Offender Overlap: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Research indicates that individuals may experience both victimisation and offending across the life course, known as the victim-offender overlap. We conducted a systematic review with meta-analytic synthesis to examine the prevalence and strength of the victim-offender overlap and assess whether reported estimates vary according to methodological choices. Articles published between 2012 and 2023 were identified through ProQuest, PsycINFO, Embase, and Criminal Justice Abstracts. Studies were included if they reported numerical overlap between direct victimisation (e.g., violent, sexual, and property) and offending (e.g., violent, property, and drug-related) behaviours, operationalised via self-, peer-, teacher-, or official records; gender and offence/victimisation subtypes were extracted where reported. Studies focusing solely on cybercrime, bullying, or indirect victimisation were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Checklist for Prevalence Studies. Sixty-eight studies including 549,377 analytic participants were included. Three random-effects meta-analyses synthesised prevalence (population-level, offender-conditional, and victim-conditional; k = 29-32) and two synthesised association strength (concurrent and lagged; k = 8-14). Population-level prevalence was 11.9% (95% CI [8.2%, 16.9%]; 95% PI [1.4%, 56.0%]), rising to 57% and 50% among offender and victim subsamples, respectively. Concurrent associations were moderate to large (d = 0.87) and significantly stronger in justice-involved samples (Δd = 0.66, p = .002); lagged associations were weaker (d = 0.42) with no statistically significant directional asymmetry. Heterogeneity was extreme across syntheses (I2 = 98.3-99.8%), and was consistent with substantial variation in data sources, operationalisation, and sample characteristics. Findings underscore the need for clearer operational definitions, transparent reporting of analytic decisions, and multi-source longitudinal research designs.

articles.title: Digital Health Literacy in Adults With Heart Failure: Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: de Cassia Gengo E Silva Butcher R
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital technology is increasingly used in heart failure (HF) management. Deficiencies in digital health literacy (DHL) may hinder the delivery of digitally mediated nursing care. Investigating sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with DHL in middle-income countries could inform targeted interventions to reduce disparities in HF management.

OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between DHL and sociodemographic and clinical factors in adults with HF.

METHODS: Descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study. The sample consisted of adult outpatients with HF from a cardiology clinic in João Pessoa, Brazil. Individuals with a clinical diagnosis of HF confirmed in the medical record, regardless of left ventricular ejection fraction, aged ≥18 years, were included. We obtained sociodemographic and clinical data through self-report. We assessed DHL using the eHealth Literacy Scale. We examined associations between sociodemographic and clinical variables and the digital literacy score using the Mann-Whitney or Kruskal-Wallis test and Spearman's correlation.

RESULTS: The study included 109 participants (mean age, 59.1 years; 60% female). DHL was predominantly low. Age, education, and number of comorbidities were significantly associated with DHL.

DISCUSSION: Age, education, and comorbidity burden may affect patients' ability to engage with digital technologies used in HF management in middle-income countries. Supporting patients' technological competencies may expand opportunities for digitally mediated caring relationships, enabling nurses to better understand and support individuals with HF in increasingly digital health care environments.

articles.title: Correction: Emerging investigator series: unpacking PET: comparative analysis of leachable and extractable contaminants from virgin and recycled polyethylene terephthalate bottles and textiles.
articles.abstract: Correction for 'Emerging investigator series: unpacking PET: comparative analysis of leachable and extractable contaminants from virgin and recycled polyethylene terephthalate bottles and textiles' by Yanan Li et al., Environ. Sci.: Processes Impacts, 2025, 27, 3431-3439, https://doi.org/10.1039/D5EM00615E.

articles.title: Corrigendum to SLAMF7 regulates the inflammatory response in macrophages during polymicrobial sepsis.
Corrigendum to TREM-2 promotes Th1 responses by interacting with the CD3ζ-ZAP70 complex following Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
Pulmonary arterial hypertension-associated cerebellar impairment extends evidence linking cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract: Growing evidence shows that the risk of cognitive impairment is increased across a range of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, but underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. One possibility involves activation of microglia, a glial cell type of the central nervous system with morphological and transcriptional features comparable to resident macrophages in other tissues that plays specialized roles in supporting neuronal and brain function. Combining clinical investigation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) cohorts with mouse model and microglial cell culture studies, a study by Okawa, Shi, and colleagues in this issue of the JCI adds compelling, albeit indirect, evidence linking impaired lysosomal lipid handling in both endothelial cells and microglia to a specific neurological disorder associated with PAH. The findings open opportunities for understanding how cardiopulmonary disease predisposes to neurodegeneration.

articles.title: JAK1/2 inhibition promotes aggressive cutaneous carcinogenesis through COT kinase-mediated alternative MAPK pathway activation.
articles.abstract: Secondary malignancies are the most feared adverse effects of cancer therapies. In this study, we explored the cutaneous oncogenic effects of the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib. First, we demonstrated an epidemiological association between ruxolitinib exposure and development of aggressive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) by analyzing international pharmacovigilance data and conducting a large cohort study. We next demonstrated the causal link between ruxolitinib treatment and cSCC development using in vitro and in vivo models. Mechanistically, we revealed that ruxolitinib induces transformation of premalignant keratinocytes by activating the MAPK pathway. This effect is mostly driven by JAK2 inhibition, suggesting a pharmacological class effect. To unravel the mechanistic underpinnings of ruxolitinib-induced MAPK activation, we then applied a phosphoproteomic approach. Alternative MAPK signaling downstream of the kinase COT was pinpointed as the main activator of the pathway in this context. The central role of COT was functionally validated using chemical inhibition, genetic impairment, and inactivated COT mutant expression. Indeed, impairment of COT rescued the pro-oncogenic effect of ruxolitinib. Finally, we determined using a combination of epidemiological, in vitro, and in vivo studies that ruxolitinib-mediated oncogenic effects also result in an increased risk of melanoma, suggesting that the uncovered cellular signaling mechanism might be extrapolated to other cancers with a high dependency on the MAPK pathway.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin attenuates progression from prefrailty to frailty in patients with hypertension and chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDChronic kidney disease (CKD) and hypertension share common pathophysiological pathways contributing to vascular damage, endothelial dysfunction, and physical decline, particularly in older adults with prefrailty. To evaluate the relationship among renal injury, physical performance, and frailty progression in hypertensive older adults with CKD and assess whether dapagliflozin associates with reduced frailty progression, we designed the study DAPA-FORTRESS (DAPAgliflozin and Frailty prOgression in hypeRTension and chRonic kidnEy diSeaSe).METHODSWe enrolled 135 prefrail hypertensive patients with CKD aged >65 years and followed them for 1 year. After coarsened exact matching, our balanced cohort had 105 patients (52 dapagliflozin). Associations between albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and physical performance were analyzed using correlation and regression models. Effect of dapagliflozin on frailty progression was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.RESULTSA significant inverse association between gait speed and albuminuria (r2 = 0.48, P < 0.0001) and significant positive linear association between gait speed and eGFR (r2 = 0.18; P < 0.0001) were observed. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 exhibited significantly worse physical performance than those with higher eGFR (P = 0.0003). In adjusted analyses, receiving dapagliflozin was independently associated with lower odds of progressing to frailty at 1 year (OR = 0.130; CI 0.045-0.381; P < 0.001).CONCLUSIONIn older hypertensive patients with CKD, greater renal injury is associated with worse physical performance, while dapagliflozin use reduces the risk of frailty progression. These findings indicate a potential protective role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition in mitigating functional decline in this high-risk population.FUNDINGNIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (R01-HL146691), National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (R01-DK123259); American Heart Association (AHA- 24IPA1268813, AHA-22-915561, AHA-24-1195524).

articles.title: Neoadjuvant PD-L1/TGF-β blockade can rapidly disrupt the tumor stroma in head and neck cancer patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDTGF-β drives fibroblast activation in cancer and is a resistance biomarker to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.METHODSFocusing on the tumor stroma, we characterized the impact of neoadjuvant treatment with bintrafusp alfa (BA), a dual PD-L1 and TGF-β inhibitor, in a window-of-opportunity study with 6 patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Tumor biopsies before treatment and 3 weeks after therapy were analyzed using scRNA-seq, imaging, and spatial transcriptomics.RESULTSAfter treatment, we observed significantly decreased levels of activated LRRC15+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), remodeled stromal architecture with reduced collagen I and XII content, and increased CD8+ T cell infiltration in immune-excluded tumors. These changes were independently confirmed in an additional neoadjuvant BA-treated cohort of 6 patients with HNSCC. The drastic CAF and stromal compartment reduction observed indicated a fibroblast depletion rather than a fibroblast polarization shift.CONCLUSIONWhile our final clinical cohort does not allow assessment of the treatment effect, this study demonstrated that targeting TGF-β in patients can disrupt the tumor stroma within a short time frame. Further trials and novel biomarkers are now needed to select patients who could benefit.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov NCT04428047.FUNDINGMerck KGaA, ARC Emerging Leaders in Oncology, ANR-10-IDEX-0001-02 PSL, Centre d'Investigation Clinique IGR-Curie 1428, Site de Recherche Intégrée sur le Cancer (INCa-DGOS-Inserm-ITMO cancer_18000), French Government "Investissements d'Avenir" program, France 2030 program, Fondation pour la Recherche Médicale, Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement 847718, Cooperative Research and Development Agreement with EMD Serono, and NIH (ZIA BC 010666).

articles.title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
articles.abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

articles.title: ADAR-mediated RNA editing of Influenza A virus genomes may be age-dependent and inversely correlates with viral load.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly. Influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes belonging to the group of RNA-acting adenosine deaminases (ADARs) play a role in the innate antiviral immune response, partly by inducing mutations in viral RNA. The effect of this mechanismin influenza A virus infection remains unexplained in humans.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients.

METHODS: Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors.

RESULTS: ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.

articles.title: Pregnancy in a Woman with PGM1-CDG: Longitudinal Metabolic Follow-up During a Lactose-Supported Diet.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
articles.abstract: Phosphoglucomutase-1 deficiency (PGM1-CDG) is an ultra-rare, treatable congenital disorder of glycosylation characterized by multisystem involvement. Although galactose supplementation improves biochemical and clinical manifestations, data on pregnancy management and metabolic follow-up in affected women remain extremely limited. We report a woman with genetically confirmed PGM1-CDG who achieved a successful pregnancy with detailed longitudinal metabolic monitoring and maintenance of galactose intake through a lactose-supported diet. The patient was diagnosed during adolescence with a multisystem phenotype including short stature, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatic involvement, elevated creatine kinase, reduced antithrombin III and left ventricular hypertrophy. She harbored a homozygous PGM1 c.1508G>A (p.Arg503Gln) variant. Long-term pharmaceutical D-galactose supplementation was associated with biochemical improvement, while cardiac involvement remained clinically stable. At 25 years of age, pregnancy was achieved through assisted reproductive technology with her spouse, who was heterozygous for a different PGM1 variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). Given the limited safety data on pharmaceutical D-galactose use during pregnancy and uncertainty regarding potential fetal effects, galactose intake was maintained through a lactose-supported diet (estimated galactose intake of approximately 0.5 g/kg/day). Liver enzymes, coagulation parameters and cardiac status remained stable and creatine kinase levels did not worsen. Gestational diabetes was successfully managed with dietary modification alone. No thrombotic, hepatic or cardiac complications occurred. A healthy female infant was delivered by elective cesarean section at 38 weeks. The newborn had a normal metabolic evaluation and was a heterozygous carrier of the maternal PGM1 variant. This case provides detailed longitudinal data on pregnancy in PGM1-CDG and describes the maintenance of dietary galactose intake derived from lactose during a pregnancy with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: In Vitro and In Vivo Immunomodulatory and Protective Effects of Leukemia Inhibitory Factor-Engineered Mesenchymal Stromal Cells in Experimental Endotoxemia.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by dysregulated systemic inflammation and high mortality rates. Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as promising immunomodulatory agents; however, genetic engineering strategies can enhance their therapeutic efficacy. This study evaluated the immunomodulatory and protective effects of MSCs genetically engineered to express leukemia inhibitory factor (MSC-LIF) in vitro and in a mouse model of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia. In vitro, peritoneal macrophages stimulated with LPS + IFN-γ were co-cultured with MSC-LIF or wild-type MSCs (MSC-WT). MSC-LIF significantly reduced the production of TNF-α, IL-12, and nitric oxide compared with stimulated controls and demonstrated enhanced inhibition of IL-12 and nitrite levels relative to MSC-WT. Although IL-6 levels increased in co-cultures, MSC-LIF promoted a regulatory cytokine profile characterized by modulation of pro-inflammatory mediators. In vivo, C57BL/6 mice subjected to lethal endotoxemia with LPS were treated with MSC-LIF, MSC-WT, dexamethasone, or vehicle. MSC-LIF significantly improved survival in a dose-dependent manner, achieving 100% survival at the highest dose (1 × 106 cells), outperforming MSC-WT. Serum cytokine analysis revealed that MSC-LIF markedly reduced TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, and IL-12 levels while significantly increasing IL-10 production, indicating enhanced systemic immunoregulation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that LIF expression potentiates the immunomodulatory and protective effects of MSCs in experimental endotoxemia. MSC-LIF therapy promotes a balanced inflammatory response and significantly improves survival, supporting its potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for severe systemic inflammatory conditions such as sepsis.

articles.title: Statin Intolerance, Treatment Gaps, and Cardiovascular Outcomes: A 24-Year Health System Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statin intolerance may disrupt lipid-lowering therapy (LLT). We characterized clinician-documented intolerance and assessed whether cardiovascular risk was concentrated among patients who discontinued all LLT.

METHODS: We studied new statin users at Mass General Brigham using medication records dated 1987 through November 2025. Temporal trend analyses were restricted to 2001 through 2024. We characterized postintolerance management and examined cardiovascular outcomes using time-varying Cox models. Within the intolerance cohort, we compared patients who discontinued all LLT with those who continued any LLT.

RESULTS: Among 254 035 new statin users, 10 644 (4.2%) developed documented intolerance after a median of 3.1 years. Musculoskeletal symptoms were documented in 68.1%. Within 90 days, 39.9% discontinued all LLT and fewer than 10% received a nonstatin-based strategy. At 3 to 6 months, mean low-density lipoprotein cholesterol increased by 6.8 mg/dL among discontinuers and decreased by 4.9 mg/dL among continuers. Compared with statin-tolerant patients, intolerance was associated with higher risks of coronary artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke (hazard ratios, 1.12-1.55). Within the intolerance cohort, discontinuing all LLT was associated with higher risk across all outcomes, with hazard ratios ranging from 1.38 for mortality to 2.14 for venous thromboembolism.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinician-documented statin intolerance was frequently followed by complete LLT discontinuation and limited use of nonstatin therapy. Complete discontinuation identified a high-risk subgroup with worsening lipid trajectories, supporting systematic reassessment and restoration of statin or nonstatin therapy.

articles.title: Causal inference study on the influence of the anxious/worrier trait on the risk of endometriosis: Two-sample Mendelian randomization.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recent observational studies have identified an association between the anxious/worrier trait and endometriosis. However, the causal nature of this relationship remains unclear.

METHODS: Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies were used to identify independent genetic variants associated with the anxious/worrier trait, which served as instrumental variables in a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Causal estimates for the effect of emotional factors on endometriosis risk were obtained using inverse variance weighting, MR-Egger regression, and weighted median methods. Reverse MR analysis was then used to assess the impact of endometriosis on emotional indicators. Sensitivity analyses included the MR-Egger intercept test, leave-one-out analysis, and Cochran's Q test, which were used to detect potential pleiotropy and heterogeneity.

RESULTS: The inverse variance weighted analysis indicated that the anxious/worrier trait significantly elevated the risk of developing endometriosis (odds ratio 3.84; 95% confidence interval 1.42-10.41, P = 0.008). The results of the reverse MR analysis did not indicate a significant causal effect of endometriosis on emotional indicators (P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: This study provides genetic evidence for a causal relationship between emotional factors (anxious/worrier trait) and endometriosis. However, the specific biological pathways involved warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Association between urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and postpartum resistant hypertension in patients with severe preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to investigate the association between elevated urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia at a tertiary care center in Colombia.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted in Medellín, Colombia. Patients aged >18 years diagnosed with severe preeclampsia who underwent UPCR assessment were included. Associations between elevated UPCR (≥0.3) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization were evaluated using robust Poisson regression models.

RESULTS: A total of 261 patients were included in the study. Bivariate analysis showed that resistant hypertension in the postpartum period was more frequent in the UPCR ≥0.3 group than in the UPCR <0.3 group (43.2% vs. 12.7%; risk ratio 3.69; 95% confidence interval 1.92-7.07). After adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at diagnosis, elevated UPCR remained independently associated with resistant hypertension (adjusted risk ratio 4.87; 95% confidence interval 1.86-12.76). Earlier gestational age at diagnosis was also independently associated with resistant hypertension.

CONCLUSION: The UPCR is independently associated with the development of resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia.

articles.title: Construction of a clinical model for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus based on women of increased maternal age singleton pregnant women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
