PURPOSE: This study develops and validates an early clinical prediction model for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) specifically in women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies, thereby facilitating early identification of high-risk individuals and timely targeted intervention.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 338 women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies (82 diagnosed with GDM) who received prenatal care at the First People's Hospital of Changde between January 2023 and June 2024, comprising the training set. An additional 232 women (70 with GDM) seen between July 2024 and June 2025 comprised the validation set. Clinical data were collected and risk factors for GDM were identified using logistic regression analysis. A prediction model was constructed using R software. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, with internal validation performed via K-fold cross-validation, and external validation carried out in the independent validation set.

RESULTS: A significant between-group difference was observed in assisted reproductive technology history between the training and validation sets (Z = 8.631, P = 0.003). In the training set, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI, calculated as weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters), fasting plasma glucose, uric acid, and triglyceride levels differed significantly between the GDM and non-GDM groups (P < 0.05 for all). Multivariate logistic regression identified all four parameters as independent risk factors for GDM (P < 0.05). The ROC curve analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.773 for the training set and 0.808 for the validation set, indicating good predictive performance.

CONCLUSION: We established a GDM prediction model for women of increased maternal age with singleton pregnancies, incorporating four readily available clinical indicators. The model demonstrated satisfactory discrimination and generalizability upon both internal and external validation.

articles.title: Glyco-engineered mannose-graphene oxide/PVA/CD hybrid coatings: a smart surface functionalization strategy for antibacterial catheter applications.
articles.abstract: Catheter-associated infections are a major clinical concern, emphasizing the need for durable antibacterial coatings on medical device surfaces. In this study, a glyco-engineered hybrid coating based on mannose-functionalized graphene oxide (MAN-GO), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and carbon dots (CDs) was developed to improve surface functionality and infection resistance. The mannose modification of GO enhanced surface hydrophilicity and biological recognition, while the incorporation of carbon dots improved coating uniformity, dispersion, and stability. The composite coatings were applied onto polyurethane, PVC, and rubber substrates and characterized using FTIR, XRD, and FESEM, and detailed wettability studies, confirming successful hybrid formation and smooth surface morphology. Antibacterial studies demonstrated strong activity, with a pronounced inhibitory effect against Gram-negative Escherichia coli and substantial reduction of Staphylococcus aureus growth. Furthermore, the coatings exhibited 77.57% antibiofilm inhibition, indicating excellent resistance to bacterial colonization. The results highlight the potential of glyco-engineered MAN-GO/PVA/CD composites as promising antibacterial coatings for urinary catheters, offering a simple and effective strategy to prevent device-associated infections.

articles.title: Synthesis and bioactivity investigation of polymyxin B analogues with Thr2, Dab3, and Thr10 modifications.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the structure-activity (SAR) and structure-toxicity (STR) relationships of the three polar-face positions Thr2, Dab3, and Thr10 in polymyxin B (PMB) and identify substitutions retaining antibacterial potency while reducing HK-2 cytotoxicity.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-two PMB analogues were synthesized and evaluated for antibacterial activity and HK-2 cytotoxicity. New compound 22 was further assessed in a mouse systemic infection model. Its lipopolysaccharide (LPS) binding was examined by biolayer interferometry (BLI). Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) characterized peptide-membrane interactions.

RESULTS: Ser substitution at Thr2 or Thr10 retained antibacterial activity with modestly reduced HK-2 cytotoxicity. Replacing Dab3 with 2,3-diaminopropionic acid (Dap) or ornithine (Orn) preserved activity and markedly reduced HK-2 cytotoxicity. Compound 7 showed a selectivity index (SI) range of >2000.0 to >8000.0. Combining Dap3 with reduced hydrophobicity at Leu7 maintained or improved activity and increased selectivity. Compound 22 showed an SI range of >2000.0 to >16666.7, efficacy comparable to PMB in a preliminary mouse infection model, LPS binding, and a smaller ITC response than PMB.

CONCLUSIONS: At positions 2 and 10, hydroxyl-bearing residues best preserved antibacterial activity, position 10 showed greater substitution tolerance. Position 3 required cationic character and offered the clearest opportunity to improve selectivity.

articles.title: Validation of the PREVENT-HF Risk Prediction Equation in US Veterans.
Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.

RESULTS: Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

articles.title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness.

RESULTS: At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0-8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8-5.8] kPa; P=0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m2; P=0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20-15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90).

CONCLUSIONS: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

articles.title: Sleep and Cardiometabolic Disease: A Wearable-Electronic Health Record Study in the US All of Us Research Program.
articles.abstract: Background: Sleep health spans duration, quality, regularity, and timing, yet Life's Essential 8 scores sleep by duration alone, and regularity studies used about 1 week of data. How these dimensions, measured over months, relate to incident cardiometabolic disease is unknown, as is whether nightly sleep-cycle structure adds information. Methods: This cohort study included US adults in the All of Us Research Program with linked Fitbit and electronic health records (2009-2023). We derived 11 sleep metrics over a 180-day baseline (≥90 valid nights). Incident diagnoses, grouped into phecodes, were counted after a 180-day washout to limit reverse causation. Primary analyses related these metrics to prespecified endpoints, including a CVD composite (myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiomyopathy, or ischemic stroke), heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. Cox models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and comorbidity factors. Exploratory analyses examined wearable-estimated sleep cycles (7,199 participants; 1,017,812 sleep-stage nights). Results: Among 10,362 participants (median age, 53 years; 70% female), 230 developed the CVD composite (median follow-up, 3.7 years). Each 1-SD (29-minute) higher night-to-night variability in sleep duration was associated with higher CVD composite risk (hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.09-1.41]), as was higher variability in bedtime (1.23 [1.10-1.37]), waketime (1.20 [1.09-1.32]), and midpoint (1.21 [1.09-1.35]); mean sleep duration was not (0.96 [0.85-1.08]). Variability in sleep duration was also associated with heart failure (1.32 [1.13-1.55]), hypertension (1.16 [1.08-1.25]), and type 2 diabetes (1.20 [1.07-1.35]). More sleep cycles were associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk (0.72 [0.58-0.89]), independent of sleep duration, regularity, and timing (0.58 [0.44-0.77]). Conclusions: Night-to-night irregularity in sleep duration and timing was associated with the CVD composite, heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes; mean duration was not associated with the CVD composite. More wearable-estimated sleep cycles were associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk beyond conventional sleep metrics, a novel finding requiring confirmation.

articles.title: ACHD Care Wheel: A Stakeholder- and Theory-Driven Framework to Improve Specialized Adult Congenital Heart Disease Care.
articles.abstract: Background: Patients with adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) experience significant gaps in guideline-recommended care, associated with higher morbidity and mortality compared to those without care gaps. We evaluated barriers and facilitators to specialized care to inform patient-centered solutions. Methods: We purposively sampled ACHD patients and clinicians from UCSF and across the United States and conducted semi-structured interviews in 2023-2024. Patients were ≥18 years, spoke English or Spanish, and could provide informed consent; clinicians were cardiologists or other staff involved in ACHD care. Zoom interviews were conducted using Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, and Behavior (COM-B)-informed guides and were recorded, professionally transcribed, and translated when applicable. Data were analyzed using inductive coding and rapid qualitative analysis, with independent dual coding, consensus resolution, concurrent analysis, and member checking. Identified categories were subsequently mapped to the Theoretical Domains Framework and COM-B. Results: We interviewed 54 participants (37 patients, 17 clinicians). For patients, the median age was 32 years; 57% were women, 62% were people of color, and 35% had gaps in care of ≥3 years. Findings were organized into six interdependent categories: healthcare system and institutional structure; knowledge and education; sources of support; personal development; identity and personal resources; and ACHD's placement in one's life. Two novel findings emerged: a paradoxical facilitating role of parental language barriers and the complex impact of caregiver support on patients' independent care skills. We developed the ACHD Care Wheel, a theory-guided framework to support the design and evaluation of future interventions. Conclusions: The ACHD Care Wheel is a stakeholder-derived, theory-grounded framework for developing and evaluating interventions to improve ACHD care. Interventions targeting the three priority categories (healthcare system and institutional structure, knowledge and education, and sources of support) are likely to produce effects across multiple domains simultaneously, offering a theoretically grounded path forward for this growing population.

articles.title: Supplement Use and Diet Quality Among U.S. Adults by Eligibility for Lipid-Lowering Therapy.
articles.abstract: Background: The 2026 American Heart Association/ American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) dyslipidemia guideline advises against supplements for lipid lowering. Whether supplement use reflects broader engagement in cardiovascular prevention, including healthy eating, remains uncertain. We examined supplement use and selected dietary characteristics across lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) treatment and eligibility groups. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (2015-2020) from adults aged 30-75 years. Participants were classified as current LLT users or untreated adults. Untreated adults were further classified as recommended, reasonable/selectively consider, or not routinely recommended for LLT, using the 2026 AHA/ACC guideline. Outcomes were self-reported heart health or cholesterol supplement use and dietary misalignment burden, defined as the number of unmet benchmarks across nine selected recall-day indicators informed by 2026 AHA dietary guidance. Analyses incorporated the complex survey design and fasting subsample weights to generate national estimates and compare supplement use across burden categories. Results: We analyzed 3,743 participants, representing 147.3 million US adults; 49.0% were female, and 25.0% were receiving LLT. Overall, 11.3% [9.4-13.6] reported supplement use. Supplement use was highest among adults receiving LLT (19.5% [14.9-25.1]) and lowest among untreated adults for whom LLT was not routinely recommended (3.6% [2.6-5.1]). Among untreated adults for whom LLT was recommended, 4.2 million (12.8% [10.5-15.4]) used supplements. Dietary inadequacies were common across measured domains and LLT eligibility strata; the weighted median misalignment burden was 7 (IQR 6-8). Supplement use did not differ significantly across dietary misalignment burden categories. Conclusions: Millions of US adults recommended for LLT were untreated while using heart health or cholesterol supplements, and supplement use did not differ significantly across selected dietary misalignment burden categories. Proactive assessment of supplement use may help redirect prevention counseling toward guideline-directed LLT and heart-healthy dietary patterns.

articles.title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment.

METHODS: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF.

RESULTS: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040).

CONCLUSIONS: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

articles.title: Restitution properties during ventricular fibrillation and the effects of cardiac pacing location on ventricular electrophysiology in the rabbit heart.
articles.abstract: Sudden cardiac death is a cause of mortality due to malignant arrhythmias such as ventricular fibrillation (VF). Although action potential duration (APD) restitution is a method to assess arrhythmic susceptibility, repolarisation may depend on prior activation history, a phenomenon known as cardiac memory. Cardiac memory describes the persistence of repolarisation effects from previous beats, such that APD reflects not only the immediately preceding diastolic interval (DI) but also earlier activation effects. This may be relevant during VF, where continuously varying activation patterns prevent a steady electrophysiological state. This study investigated how pacing location affects ventricular electrophysiology and whether repolarisation during VF exhibits short-term cardiac memory. Langendorff-perfused rabbit hearts were used to record monophasic action potentials from the left ventricular apex and base. Pacing was conducted from five sites. Steady-state APD was assessed during constant pacing. Effective refractory period (ERP), APD restitution and conduction time restitution (CTR) were assessed using an S1-S2 extra-stimulus protocol (S1, conditioning stimuli; S2, premature extra-stimulus). Additionally, APD-DI and APD-APD relationships were analysed during early VF. Pacing location significantly influenced S1 and S2 conduction delays, consistent with site-dependent activation timing. However, steady-state APD, ERP and CTR were not significantly affected by pacing location. In contrast, during VF, APD exhibited a significant dependence on preceding DI and preceding APD over approximately the first 30 beats, with these relationships progressively deteriorating thereafter. These findings demonstrate that while pacing location alters activation timing, repolarisation dynamics under stable activation histories are robust. During VF, continuously changing activation patterns unmask short-term cardiac memory.

articles.title: Experience of Individuals Living with Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Gastroenterology nursing : the official journal of the Society of Gastroenterology Nurses and Associates
articles.abstract: Persons with decompensated cirrhosis are influenced not only physically but also psychologically and socially, as they are repeatedly hospitalized and discharged due to various physical symptoms. This study aimed to clarify the experiences of individuals with decompensated cirrhosis. Six individuals with cirrhosis after chronic hepatitis, treated as outpatients or inpatients at the Hepatology Department of two medical facilities by full-time hepatologists, were included in semi-structured interviews. The results were analyzed individually and comprehensively using a qualitative synthesis method (KJ method). The management of individuals with decompensated cirrhosis included "continued management" and "management that prioritizes daily life." Management was supported by two aspects: "recuperation supported by a connection with others" and "recuperation far from others." Furthermore, despite managing their disease and being conscious of the gradual progression of their condition, participants with decompensated cirrhosis oscillated between their "reluctance to accept life with illness" and "unrelieved anxiety about their future"; their "elusive body" influenced their management and emotions in their daily living. Although individuals with decompensated cirrhosis have managed their illness for many years, they may not fully understand the evolving physical changes in their bodies. Additionally, they may experience growing concerns about the future.

articles.title: Exploring Factors Impacting the Self-Management of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Black African and Afro-Caribbean People (BAACP): A Qualitative Evidence Synthesis.
articles.journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this qualitative evidence synthesis (QES) was to synthesize qualitative evidence on perceived barriers and facilitators influencing self-management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among older Black African and Afro-Caribbean adults.

METHODS: A QES of qualitative and mixed-methods studies with extractable qualitative findings was conducted using the PICO (Population, Phenomena of Interest, Context) framework and PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidance. Searches were undertaken in MEDLINE, PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, African Journals Online, and Worldviews on Evidence-Based Nursing for studies published between January 2010 and June 2025. Studies were screened against predefined eligibility criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program checklist, and findings were synthesized thematically.

RESULTS: From 5092 records, 12 studies met the inclusion criteria. Five overarching themes were identified. Key facilitators included spirituality, culturally responsive health care, and strong family or community support networks. Major barriers included limited health literacy, mistrust of health care systems, cultural conflicts with biomedical advice, and structural barriers such as financial constraints, limited access to health care services, and racial discrimination.

CONCLUSION: Self-management of T2DM in older Black African and Afro-Caribbean adults is shaped by interconnected cultural, relational, and structural influences. Diabetes services should prioritize culturally tailored education, trust-building clinical relationships, family and community-engaged interventions, and addressing social determinants and racial inequalities to improve self-management outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Analysis and Identification of Risk Factors for Intradialytic Hypotension in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This paper aimed to identify factors associated with intradialytic hypotension (IDH) in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) and to develop a practical risk prediction model for early clinical assessment.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis included 142 patients on MHD, divided into an IDH group (n = 48) and a non-IDH group (n = 94) based on intradialytic systolic blood pressure decline and related clinical intervention. Blood pressure parameters, demographic characteristics, dialysis prescription, biochemical indicators, and bone mineral metabolism markers were collected. Independent risk factors for IDH were identified via multivariate logistic regression of univariate significant variables, and a nomogram was constructed based on regression coefficients. Model performance was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, calibration curve, ROC analysis, and bootstrap internal validation.

RESULTS: Patients with IDH showed lower intradialytic SBP/DBP and greater blood pressure reduction than those without IDH (p < 0.05). Older age, higher dry weight (DW), transferrin saturation, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels were associated with IDH in univariate analysis (p < 0.05). Multivariate analysis confirmed age (OR = 1.059), DW (OR = 1.043), and PTH (OR = 1.001) as independent risk factors (p < 0.05). Based on these three factors, the constructed nomogram model showed good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.249), with an AUC of 0.750 (95% CI 0.674-0.837), and an internally validated corrected C-index of 0.740 (95% CI 0.662-0.825).

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, increased DW, and elevated PTH are significant predictors of IDH in MHD patients. The nomogram provides a reliable tool for individualized early warning and risk evaluation.

articles.title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Physical Activity, and Diet in Law Enforcement Officers: A 6-Year Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Law enforcement officers (LEOs) often display poor cardiovascular health, which can impair job performance and increase cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. While many cross-sectional studies have documented these issues, few have examined the progression of CVD risk factors over time, and none appear to have used a longitudinal design assessing incidence in relation to healthy lifestyle behaviors within a sex-representative sample of this occupation.

METHODS: This prospective study followed 228 LEOs (28% women) over 6 years using online questionnaires assessing CVD risk factors, physical activity, and fruit and vegetable intake. Incidence of CVD risk factors was analyzed according to baseline physical activity (active vs. inactive), fruit and vegetable intake (≥5 vs. <5 servings/day), and their combined adherence.

FINDINGS: Over time, participants showed significant increases in weight (p < .001, Cohen's d = .49), body mass index (p < .001, Cohen's d = .53), and prevalence of most CVD risk factors. Physically inactive LEOs demonstrated higher incidence of dyslipidemia (7% vs. 0%, p = .04, Cramer's V = .15) compared to active counterparts. Those consuming <5 daily servings of fruits and vegetables were more likely to develop hypertension (7% vs. 0%, p < .01, Cramer's V = .19) and dyslipidemia (8% vs. 1%, p = .01, Cramer's V = .18). The lowest cumulative incidence was observed among participants meeting both lifestyle recommendations.

CONCLUSIONS/APPLICATION TO PRACTICE: CVD risk factors increased over time in this LEO sample, with baseline physical inactivity and poor diet tending to predict greater incidence. These findings suggest the need for workplace health promotion programs targeting physical activity and healthy eating to reduce long-term CVD risk in this population.

articles.title: Blood and urinary NT-proBNP: atrial fibrillation-associated patterns and cardiac dysfunction in acute chest pain.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: NT-proBNP is the gold-standard biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring congestive heart failure (CHF); however, its role in detecting atrial fibrillation (AFib) is gaining attention. This study assessed the influence of aberrant cardiac rhythms on plasma NT-proBNP (pNT) considering urinary NT-proBNP (uNT) as a noninvasive alternative in selected clinical scenarios.

METHODS: In 824 patients presenting with chest pain at the emergency department of the University Hospital of Regensburg, pNT was assessed. A subset of 355 patients additionally provided uNT.

RESULTS: Both pNT and uNT were significantly increased in AFib, and lesser in atrial flutter (AFlut) and right ventricular (RV) pacing compared to SR (each p < 0.05). A pNT cutoff of 900 pg/mL yielded 74% sensitivity and 83% specificity for discriminating AFib from SR (AUC = 0.85). In multivariate regression, pNT or uNT and history of AFib were independent predictors of AFib (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Both pNT and uNT are significantly elevated in AFib, and to a lesser extent AFlut, and RV pacing independently of heart failure. These findings align with prior observations and provide further evidence supporting adequately powered prospective studies to evaluate rhythm-adjusted diagnostic thresholds for CHF in AFib. In addition, uNT may complement pNT when venous access is difficult or serial remote monitoring is required.

articles.title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

articles.title: Increased Myocardial Tissue Heterogeneity on T1 Mapping in Preclinical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
Prevalence of Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in Systolic Heart Failure Without Infarct-Pattern Late Gadolinium Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Rest late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) identifies infarct-pattern scar but does not assess coronary anatomy. We estimated the prevalence of angiographic coronary artery disease (CAD) among adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or otherwise unexplained left ventricular systolic dysfunction without infarct-pattern LGE.

METHODS AND RESULTS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 27 July 2026. Eligible studies provided separable scar-negative denominators and corresponding angiographic CAD counts from invasive coronary angiography (ICA). Scar-negative was defined as the absence of subendocardial or transmural LGE in a coronary distribution. Random-effects logit meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Twenty-two reports representing 20 studies included 2,236 paired LGE-CMR and ICA. 818 patients had infarct-pattern scar, and 1,418 were scar-negative. Eight studies contributed 44 CAD cases among 468 scar-negative patients for ≥50% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 10.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 7.4-15.4). Five studies contributed 19 CAD cases among 271 scar-negative patients for ≥70% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 7.6% (95% CI 4.4-12.6). Seven studies contributed 33 CAD cases among 679 scar-negative patients for high-risk-pattern CAD, giving a pooled prevalence of 4.9% (95% CI 2.2-10.6) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8-24.8%. These strata represented different study subsets and were not nested.

CONCLUSION: Among selected adults with HFrEF or otherwise unexplained LVSD who underwent paired LGE-CMR and ICA, absence of infarct-pattern LGE did not exclude angiographic CAD. Further coronary assessment should be considered when resolving that uncertainty would alter diagnosis or management.

articles.title: Early Renal microRNA Signatures of Septic Acute Kidney Injury in Neonatal Pigs.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a major complication of neonatal sepsis, yet the early molecular events underlying sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI) in the maturing kidney remain poorly defined. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression that may contribute to the inflammatory, stress, and remodeling responses associated with SA-AKI. We profiled renal miRNA expression in neonatal pigs 12 h after cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced polymicrobial sepsis. CLP increased plasma lactate, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin and was accompanied by evidence of kidney injury, including increased plasma creatinine, symmetric dimethylarginine, and urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin. NanoString profiling of 803 endogenous miRNAs, followed by sequence-based porcine annotation, identified a distinct renal miRNA signature that separated CLP and sham kidneys by principal component analysis. Differential expression analysis identified 14 upregulated and 5 downregulated miRNAs in septic kidneys. Several differentially expressed miRNAs were associated with biomarkers of systemic inflammation and kidney injury. Integrating miRNA profiles with target-gene expression revealed inverse miRNA-mRNA relationships involving PTGS2, FOS, AKT1, KLF6, NF-κB1, and SMAD2, with ssc-miR-374b-5p showing the broadest inverse relationship with these upregulated targets. Pathway enrichment analysis further implicated HIF-1, TGF-β, FoxO, autophagy/mitophagy, cell-cycle regulation, focal adhesion, and cellular senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate rapid remodeling of the renal miRNA landscape during early polymicrobial sepsis and identify candidate miRNA-mRNA regulatory networks that may contribute to the early pathogenesis of neonatal SA-AKI.

articles.title: Tissue-Specific Regulation of Glucose and Lipid Metabolism by miR-29a in Insulin Resistance and Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: MicroRNA-29a (miR-29a) has emerged as a context-dependent regulator of glucose and lipid metabolism in insulin-sensitive tissues, yet its tissue-specific actions in insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes remain incompletely understood. We synthesized peer-reviewed evidence retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost on the role of miR-29a across skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, liver, and pancreatic β-cells. We first define the nomenclature and genomic organization of the miR-29 family, its upstream transcriptional regulators, and the Argonaute-based evidence that separates direct target repression from correlative association. Across these tissues, miR-29a modulates oxidative metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and mitochondrial adaptation, largely through the PPARδ/PGC-1α axis, exerting complex and sometimes opposing effects depending on the tissue environment. We further examine miR-29a as a mediator of interorgan communication through extracellular vesicles, its responsiveness to exercise, and its emerging value as a biomarker and therapeutic target, while highlighting unresolved contradictions and translational hurdles. Because miR-29 family members act as tumor suppressors in most epithelial tissues, we also address the oncogenic risk inherent in nucleic acid strategies that lower miR-29a levels. Collectively, this mini-review positions miR-29a as a physiology-oriented integrator of metabolic remodeling and tissue-specific adaptation in metabolic disease.

articles.title: Factors influencing breastfeeding intention among hepatitis B virus-infected mothers: An ABC-X cross-sectional analysis.
articles.abstract: Despite international guideline recommendations supporting breastfeeding among HBV-infected mothers, breastfeeding rates remain suboptimal. This study investigated factors influencing breastfeeding intention among HBV-infected mothers using the ABC-X theoretical framework. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2025 among 119 HBV-infected pregnant women. Structured questionnaires assessed demographic characteristics, disease-related factors, social support, self-efficacy, stigma, breastfeeding attitudes, and breastfeeding intention. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, chi-square tests, and multivariate logistic regression were performed. Among participants, 45.3% (n = 54) intended to breastfeed. Univariate analysis showed significant differences in self-efficacy (p = 0.003) and breastfeeding attitude scores (p = 0.046) between mothers with and without breastfeeding intention. After adjustment for potential confounders, self-efficacy was the only independent predictor of breastfeeding intention (OR = 3.71, 95% CI: 1.35-10.19, p = 0.011). The prediction model showed good discrimination, with an area under the ROC curve of 0.782. Maternal self-efficacy was the strongest predictor of breastfeeding intention among HBV-infected mothers. Interventions enhancing self-efficacy and clearly communicating breastfeeding safety with immunoprophylaxis may improve breastfeeding support in this population.

articles.title: Flexible and Bridge-Free CuI Mutual Capacitive Arrays for Machine Learning-Assisted Three-Dimensional Spatial Interactive Interfaces.
articles.abstract: Flexible transparent human-machine interfaces (HMIs) are fundamentally bottlenecked by the brittleness of conventional indium tin oxide (ITO), the mechanical vulnerability of photolithographic bridged structures, and the complex hardware shielding required to suppress capacitive crosstalk. Herein, we propose a hardware-algorithm co-design strategy featuring a bridge-free double-sided (BFDS) mutual capacitive sensor array based on magnetron-sputtered p-type γ-CuI thin films. By employing a simplified floating-electrode readout scheme, the transparent flexible array not only captures high-fidelity two-dimensional (2D) tactile signals (signal-to-noise ratio of 268.5 ± 5.6) but also unlocks highly sensitive three-dimensional (3D) proximity perception (0-5 cm) driven by fringing electric fields. To overcome the global spatial crosstalk intrinsically induced by the unshielded hardware, a customized lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is integrated. The CNN robustly decodes the complex nonlinear capacitance matrices, achieving an overall test accuracy of 86.2%. Furthermore, the CuI/PET structure exhibits good robustness over 10,000 extreme bending cycles (radius of 2.5 mm), where the grain-boundary scattering serves as a strain-release mechanism while preserving a continuous percolating conductive network. This work demonstrates that algorithmic compensation can relax stringent hardware shielding constraints, paving a novel avenue for ultra-simplified, touchless, and intelligent wearable electronics.

articles.title: Assessment of the health literacy mediating role in the relationship between fatalistic tendency and family planning among women.
articles.abstract: Promoting family planning is an essential public health goal for improving maternal and infant health; however, sociocultural barriers-particularly fatalism-continue to shape women's behaviors and attitudes. This study examined the mediating role of health literacy in the relationship between women's fatalistic tendencies and their family planning attitudes. Using a cross-sectional correlational design, data were collected from 657 married women aged 18-49 in Kırşehir, Türkiye, through 30-cluster sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews conducted during home visits between February 28 and June 1, 2022, using structured questionnaires. Measures included the Fatalistic Tendency Scale, Family Planning Attitude Scale, and the Turkey Health Literacy Scale-32. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics v23. Mediation analysis was conducted using PROCESS v3.5 with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Fatalistic tendency was negatively associated with health literacy, while health literacy showed a positive association with family planning attitudes. An indirect effect of fatalistic tendency on family planning attitudes through health literacy was identified. Findings highlight the importance of improving health literacy to mitigate fatalistic beliefs and support informed reproductive decision-making, emphasizing culturally sensitive, interdisciplinary interventions.

articles.title: Role of reverse remodelling in recurrence of atrial fibrillation after patient-tailored catheter ablation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Catheter ablation (CA) is a curative treatment for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet success rates remain sub-optimal, with ∼50% of patients with persistent AF experiencing recurrence after 1 year. This may be due to the self-perpetuating nature of AF, which remodels atrial structure and cellular properties, while successful treatment can induce reverse remodelling (RR). This study develops a patient-specific CA strategy to directly target re-entrant drivers (RDs) and investigates the role of RR in AF recurrence.

METHODS: Left atrial (LA) models were reconstructed from LGE-MRI scans of AF patients (n = 15) and coupled with the Courtemanche-Ramirez-Nattel (CRN) electrophysiology model. RDs were induced via pacing, identified using DGM analysis, and targeted ablation was performed in-silico. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was applied as a reference. Following termination, AF recurrence was tested under three levels of electrical reverse remodelling (ERR: 0%, 50%, and 100%), with and without structural reverse remodelling (SRR).

RESULTS: Targeted ablation acutely terminated AF in all patient-specific models. After the first procedure, AF recurrence decreased progressively from 55% at 0% ERR to 36.7% at 50% ERR and 5% at 100% ERR; with additional SRR, recurrence was further reduced to 46.7%, 26.7%, and 0%, respectively. After the second CA procedure, AF recurrence rate was 42.9%, 17.9%, and 0% without SRR and 25%, 14.3%, and 0% with SRR.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the importance of RR for therapy success, with a novel targeted CA technique ensuring <5% AF recurrence in patient-specific simulations. After clinical validation, this approach can help improve long-term patient outcomes.

articles.title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke-Pro and Contra.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

articles.title: Remote activity and rhythm monitoring using patient-owned consumer devices after first-time pulmonary vein isolation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Passively collected physical activity data from consumer devices could provide a scalable, objective measure of functional status in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study assessed the feasibility of remotely collecting activity and rhythm data from patients undergoing index pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).

METHODS: AF patients enrolled in the prospective TRUST registry who underwent index PVI and reported owning an eligible smartphone were re-contacted to provide informed consent and share their smartphone- and smartwatch-generated data. Pre-specified feasibility criteria were participation rate, technical success, and temporal data coverage. The primary functional outcome was the mean daily step-count change between the one-year pre-PVI and two-year post-PVI windows. Exploratory analyses examined associations of daily activity with AF recurrence and AF burden.

RESULTS: Of 280 eligible patients, 172 (61%) attempted and 154/172 (90%) completed data transfer, of whom 123 met pre-specified completeness criteria. Median monitoring duration was 6.0 [3.6, 6.6] years, with 98% [77, 100] coverage. Mean daily step count increased from 5731±2808 to 6220±2816 steps/day after PVI (+488 steps/day [187, 789]; p=0.002). In 35 smartwatch users, AF burden decreased from 3.6% [1.6, 10.8] to 0.0% [0.0, 0.3] after PVI (p<0.001). Baseline AF burden was inversely correlated with daily step count (ρ=-0.36, p=0.035).

CONCLUSION: Remote collection of activity and rhythm data from consumer smartphones and smartwatches is feasible, yielding high-coverage, multi-year research data. This enables scalable, objective quantification of longitudinal functional outcomes. Daily step count increased after PVI in this exploratory cohort and was inversely related to baseline AF burden.

articles.title: Post-COVID symptoms and work status 18 months following work-related COVID-19.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A proportion of the working population sustained COVID-19 infections due to exposures at work, but the association between persistent post-COVID symptoms and work status is unknown.

AIMS: To describe symptoms associated with work-related COVID-19 infections, 18 months post-infection, and examine the relationship between symptoms and working status.

METHODS: Survey data was collected from 605 respondents with accepted workers' compensation claims in Ontario, Canada, for COVID-19 infections, 18 months after their infection. Information collected included COVID-19 symptoms in the last 4 weeks, current work status and several potential confounders. Symptom clusters were created using latent class analysis, and multinomial logistic regression examined the relationship between symptom clusters and work status.

RESULTS: Four symptom clusters were identified: no symptoms (n = 349, 59%); high burden of constitutional symptoms with moderate burden of neuropsychiatric and respiratory symptoms (n = 97, 16%); low burden of constitutional symptoms with moderate burden of neuropsychiatric and respiratory symptoms (n = 100, 17%); and high burden across all symptom domains (n = 51, 9%). Compared to respondents with no symptoms, those in the high burden group across all symptoms were more likely to be not working at 18 months post-infection (OR = 4.27, 95% CI 1.77-10.29).

CONCLUSIONS: For a proportion of workers, COVID-19 symptoms persist following a work-related infection. Managing work disability among those with high constitutional symptoms represents an important strategy to support return-to-work.

articles.title: Flow dynamics and systemic arterial stiffness distinguish bicuspid aortic valve aortopathy from heritable thoracic aortic disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Bicuspid aortic valve-associated aortopathy (BAVA) and heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) share clinical manifestations but may represent distinct pathophysiological entities. We aimed to compare morphological and haemodynamic profiles between both groups using cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and non-invasive systemic haemodynamic assessment.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 185 patients (111 BAVA, 74 HTAD) were prospectively enrolled. CMR 4D-flow assessed aortic distensibility (ADCMR), pulse wave velocity (PWVCMR), global wall shear stress (WSSCMR) and energy loss (ELCMR). Oscillometry assessed systemic PWVM, augmentation index (AIxM) and systemic vascular resistance (SVRM). Composite adverse aortic events (AAE) comprised acute aortic syndrome, cardiovascular death or guideline diameter-based indication for surgery over 42.1±17.6 months. BAVA showed greater tubular ascending aorta and sinotubular junction dilation, ascending aorta WSSCMR (0.42±0.18 vs 0.28±0.12 Pa, p=0.020), ELCMR (19.8±8.4 vs. 12.3±6.1 mW, p<0.001) and ADCMR (6.1 ± 3.5 vs. 4.8 ± 2.9 ×10-3 mmHg-1, p=0.023), yet lower systemic stiffness than HTAD (PWVM 6.2±1.7 vs 7.8±2.1 m/s; AIxM 12.1±7.6 vs 18.4±9.2%; both p<0.001). AAE rates were similar. In exploratory aetiology-specific analyses, ascending aorta WSSCMR was associated with events in BAVA (HR 8.92, 95% CI 2.85-27.95) and systemic PWVM in HTAD (HR 2.16, 95% CI 1.30-3.57).

CONCLUSION: BAVA and HTAD show distinct morphological and haemodynamic phenotypes: BAVA with focal dilation, elevated WSSCMR/ELCMR and preserved systemic function; HTAD with reduced local distensibility and greater systemic stiffness. These aetiology-specific predictors are exploratory and require external validation.

articles.title: Screening for Hepatic Fibrosis Using an Automatically Calculated FIB-4 Score in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Single-Center Study.
articles.journal: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at high risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, which may progress to advanced fibrosis but remains underdiagnosed in routine clinical practice. Automated laboratory-based tools may improve early identification of at-risk patients.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study between January 2023 and August 2025 including 445 patients with T2D. The Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score was automatically calculated through the laboratory information system. Its diagnostic performance was assessed in patients who underwent transient elastography (TE).

RESULTS: The median age was 58 years, 64% of patients were obese, and 55% were men. Men had a higher risk of elevated FIB-4 (odds ratio = 1.32, P < 0.05). FIB-4 was ≥1.3 in 36.9% of patients. Among the 43 patients referred for TE, 26 (60.5%) had significant fibrosis. FIB-4 correlated with liver stiffness (r = 0.48; P < 0.01), with an area under the ROC curve of 0.74 (95% CI, 0.58-0.89) for detecting significant fibrosis (≥8 kPa) using a cutoff of 1.33 (sensitivity 84.6%; specificity 47.1%). Patients with significant fibrosis had significantly higher alkaline phosphatase (P = 0.03) and C-reactive protein levels (P = 0.01). Only 14% of at-risk patients underwent TE.

CONCLUSIONS: Automated calculation of FIB-4 enables identification of patients with T2D at risk of liver fibrosis in routine practice. However, its clinical impact may be limited by low referral rates for confirmatory testing. The diagnostic performance estimates reported here derive from a selected TE subcohort and should therefore be interpreted with caution. Integration of such laboratory-based tools into clinical workflows may support earlier detection, provided that appropriate care pathways are implemented.

articles.title: Targeted Metabolites Associated with the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet and Blood Pressure Changes in the DASH and DASH-Sodium Feeding Trials.
articles.journal: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood pressure decreases in response to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet. Previous studies have identified metabolites associated with DASH diet and blood pressure reduction. Yet, these metabolites were quantified in relative units using untargeted approaches, which is not directly translatable to clinical use. The extent to which these diet-related metabolites correlate with absolute measures from targeted assays remains poorly characterized.

METHODS: We measured serum concentrations of 15 metabolites previously identified as key differentiators between the DASH and control diets using targeted assays in the DASH (n = 216) and DASH-Sodium (n = 345) randomized controlled feeding trials. Spearman correlation coefficients were calculated to assess pairwise correlations between targeted and untargeted measurements. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess associations between targeted and untargeted measurements of DASH-related metabolites, to assess associations between metabolites and changes in blood pressure, and test for interactions by diet assignment.

RESULTS: In the DASH trial, relative and absolute concentrations of 7 serum metabolites were strongly correlated (r = 0.91 to 0.99). The DASH diet intervention increased absolute serum concentrations of N-methylproline the most, and significantly decreased theobromine. Absolute concentrations of 12 metabolites in the DASH trial and 10 in the DASH-Sodium trial were significantly different between DASH vs control diet interventions. Eight significant metabolite-diet interactions were observed for changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure in both trials (all P for interaction <0.05).

CONCLUSION: Targeted metabolomics confirmed key DASH-related biomarkers and enhanced the reproducibility of identified mechanisms through which the DASH diet lowers blood pressure.

articles.title: Persistence of Anti-cardiolipin and Anti-β2 Glycoprotein-1 Antibodies across Isotypes and Titers.
articles.journal: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology antiphospholipid syndrome classification criteria gave higher scores to IgG than IgM anti-β2 glycoprotein-1 (aB2GP1) and anticardiolipin (aCL) antibodies. The objective of this study is to correlate aB2GP1/aCL antibody titers and isotypes with persistence.

METHODS: Results from 6863 and 4755 unique patients who underwent repeat testing (>80 days) for aB2GP1-IgG/IgM and aCL-IgG/IgM antibodies, respectively, were categorized into 4 groups based on titer: negative (<10), weak-positive (10-39), moderate-positive (40-79), and high-positive (≥80). The percentage of persistence of each antibody across the 4 titer groups was calculated.

RESULTS: At repeat testing, >95% of negative aB2GP1-IgM/IgG and aCL-IgG results remained negative. However, 16.2% of negative aCL-IgM patients became weak-positive. Weak-positive titers are more likely to change to moderate/high-positive (2.6%-7.8%) than negative (0.1%-0.7%). Among weak-positive patients, aCL-IgM persisted longer and was less likely to become negative (21.1%) than aCL-IgG (47.6%). In the high-positive range, 91.3% of aB2GP1-IgG, 92% of aCL-IgG, and 87.5% of aB2GP1-IgM patients remained moderate/high-positive. aCL-IgM was the least persistent, with 19.4% decreasing to weak-positive/negative on repeat testing. In a 7-year period, only the mean titers of aCL-IgM were transiently elevated, possibly due to population-wide COVID-19 infections and/or vaccinations.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher titers correlate with persistence. aB2GP1-IgM/IgG and aCL-IgG antibodies show no notable differences in persistence. aCL-IgM is more prone to titer changes, and in the weak-positive range, it may indicate non-antiphospholipid syndrome-specific responses.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists: heart failure medications that also produce weight loss?
Lower ischaemic stroke risk in atrial flutter vs fibrillation? The jury is still out.
AMPK/USP10 loop activation of ACE2 in pulmonary hypertension: extending the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic continuum to the pulmonary circulation?
Selective Electrical Muscle Stimulation of the Vastus Medialis in a Patient With Knee Osteoarthritis, With Changes in Muscle Quality, Symptoms, and Physical Activity: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Fat accumulation in the vastus medialis has been associated with the progression of knee osteoarthritis. Electrical muscle stimulation may reduce intramuscular fat accumulation by inducing contractions of the targeted muscle. We hypothesized that electrical stimulation of the vastus medialis would be associated with a reduction in intramuscular fat and improvement in self-reported symptoms during the observation period in a patient with knee osteoarthritis. CASE REPORT The patient was a 77-year-old man with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 right knee osteoarthritis. Because he also had hypertension and hyperlipidemia, he had maintained regular exercise habits, including aquatic walking; however, he discontinued these activities because of knee pain. Electrical stimulation was applied to the vastus medialis for 30 minutes per session, 3 times per week, for 4 weeks. Ultrasound echo intensity, an indirect indicator of intramuscular fat, and the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score were assessed before and after the intervention. Compared with the pre-intervention value, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased by 13.7 arbitrary units (25.3%), and knee symptoms improved during the observation period. He resumed aquatic walking 2 weeks after electrical stimulation was initiated. CONCLUSIONS During the observation period, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score scores improved, and he resumed aquatic walking. However, because this was a single uncontrolled case and physical activity resumed during the intervention, these changes cannot be attributed to electrical stimulation alone; spontaneous improvement, behavioral reactivation, or a combination of these factors remain plausible. Controlled studies across different levels of disease severity are needed.

articles.title: A TiVCrMoC3 MXene-Based Sustained-Release Vancomycin Nanoplatform Mitigates Septic Arthritis through Modulation of Bacterial Acetate Metabolism.
articles.abstract: Acute septic arthritis caused by bacterial infection is a common and serious orthopedic disease. The formation of bacterial biofilms severely limits antibiotic penetration, rendering conventional therapy ineffective and short‑acting. In this study, we developed a novel nanodrug delivery system by loading vancomycin onto high‑entropy TiVCrMoC3 MXene (VCM@NPs). Featuring a sheet‑like porous structure, this material enables efficient drug loading via electrostatic interactions and sustains release in the weakly acidic infection microenvironment, achieving a cumulative release of 67% over 20 days. In vitro, VCM@NPs exhibited potent bactericidal activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with complete colony eradication by day 5, and markedly disrupted biofilm architecture, as shown by electron and confocal microscopy. In a rat septic arthritis model, a single intra‑articular injection of VCM@NPs effectively inhibited bacterial growth, alleviated joint inflammation, and improved cartilage and bone damage. By day 10, OARSI scores in the VCM@NPs group were significantly lower than those in the free vancomycin group, and micro‑CT analysis revealed increased bone volume and trabecular thickness, confirming sustained therapeutic efficacy. Notably, mass spectrometry imaging demonstrated that VCM@NPs reprogrammed the joint metabolic microenvironment by suppressing the bacterial acetate metabolic pathway, thereby destabilizing biofilms-a mechanism that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been previously reported in the context of nanoparticle-mediated modulation of this pathway. Collectively, this study offers a new nanodrug delivery strategy that integrates sustained release with biofilm disruption, holding promise for clinical translation in septic arthritis.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors for Early Major Neurologic Complications in Lung Transplantation: From Restrictive Cardiopulmonary Bypass to ECMO by Criteria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hemodynamic instability and hypoxemia may contribute to early major neurologic complications (EMNC) following lung transplantation. Mechanical circulatory support can mitigate cerebral hypoperfusion, but cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is an independent risk factor for EMNC. This study examines the incidence of EMNC transitioning from a restrictive CPB strategy to criteria-based use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO-BC).

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study on 389 lung transplant recipients comparing patients managed with restrictive CPB (PRE-ECMO, 2012-2017, n = 288) to those managed with criteria-based ECMO (ECMO-BC, 2022-2024, n = 101). The incidence of EMNC was compared between groups.

RESULTS: EMNC occurred in 29 of 280 patients in the PRE-ECMO group and in 5 of 101 patients in the ECMO-BC group (10% versus 5%; P = 0.152), with 78 versus 8 total events, corresponding to an incidence rate ratio of 3.5 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.7-7.4, P < 0.001). Ischemic stroke was significantly less frequent in the ECMO-BC group (2% versus 9%; P = 0.022). Intraoperative mechanical circulatory support was used in 20% of PRE-ECMO and 43% of ECMO-BC cases (P < 0.001). Patients in the ECMO-BC group were older, had more cardiopulmonary comorbidities, greater intraoperative blood loss (2489 versus 1861 cc; P < 0.001), and more severe primary graft dysfunction at 24 and 72 h (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Transition to ECMO-BC was associated with lower EMNC events and fewer ischemic strokes, but increased intraoperative blood loss and worse early graft function, generating hypotheses for prospective studies that define optimal ECMO indications in lung transplantation.

articles.title: Persistent Elbow Pain After Stroke: An Unexpected Case.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation

articles.title: Muscle, Nutritional, and Videofluoroscopic Factors Associated With 6-Month Oral Intake Recovery in Post-Stroke Dysphagia.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether muscle, nutritional, and videofluoroscopic factors were associated with 6-month oral intake recovery after stroke.

DESIGN: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,286 adults with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, oropharyngeal dysphagia, baseline Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) scores of 1 to 4, and index videofluoroscopy within 180 days of stroke onset. The primary analysis was restricted to the 1,241 patients alive at 6 months. Successful oral intake recovery was defined as achievement of total oral intake with multiple consistencies (FOIS ≥5) at 180±30 days; death before 6 months was analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 1,241 six-month survivors, 748 (60.3%) achieved successful oral intake recovery. Lower odds of recovery were associated with low skeletal muscle mass index (adjusted odds ratio, 0.67; 95% confidence interval, 0.50-0.90), low grip strength (0.69; 0.51-0.92), Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index less than 98 (0.75; 0.56-1.00), Penetration-Aspiration Scale score of 6 or higher (0.60; 0.43-0.83), moderate or severe vallecular residue (0.65; 0.49-0.85), and moderate or severe pyriform sinus residue (0.57; 0.42-0.77).

CONCLUSION: Videofluoroscopic swallowing findings and indirect systemic vulnerability markers provided complementary information regarding 6-month oral intake recovery among stroke survivors after adjustment for stroke severity, cognition, aphasia, lesion characteristics, and major comorbidities.

articles.title: PCSK9-Targeting Therapies and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria.

RESULTS: Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent.

CONCLUSION: PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

articles.title: Effect of combined sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy in patients with chronic kidney disease: a real-world analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the kidney, cardiovascular, and mortality outcomes of combined sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) therapy compared with SGLT2i monotherapy in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: Using TriNetX electronic health records, we compared patients initiating combined therapy with those initiating SGLT2i alone. Propensity score matching (1:1) was applied. The index date was defined as treatment initiation, with patients required to maintain the assigned treatment strategy during the first 6 months. Outcome follow-up began 6 months after the index date and continued to 2 years after the index date. Primary outcomes were major adverse kidney events (MAKE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and the secondary outcome was all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Among 178,930 patients, 1,154 (0.65%) initiated combined therapy of SGLT2i and GLP-1RA, and 24,134 (13.49%) initiated monotherapy of SGLT2i. After matching, each group included 1,150 patients. Combined therapy was associated with a lower risk of MAKE (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48-0.80; p < 0.01) and all-cause mortality (aHR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40-0.83; p < 0.01) compared with SGLT2i alone. There was no significant reduction in risk of MACE (aHR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.70-1.11; p = 0.29).

CONCLUSION: Among patients with CKD, initiation of combined SGLT2i and GLP-1RA therapy was associated with lower risks of MAKE and all-cause mortality compared with SGLT2i monotherapy. Further studies are needed to clarify effects on kidney and mortality outcomes.

articles.title: Identification of plasma biomarkers for chronic kidney disease by integrating proteomics and machine learning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, and early identification of individuals at risk remains challenging. This study aimed to identify plasma proteomic biomarkers associated with incident CKD and develop a machine learning-based prediction model integrating proteomic and clinical data.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 27,429 UK Biobank participants without baseline CKD after excluding those with estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥3 mg/mmol. Among 2,920 plasma proteins, protein-wide Cox regression with Bonferroni correction was followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-based feature selection. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration metrics, reclassification indices, and landmark-based prediction analyses, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Kaplan-Meier, and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 205 proteins were significantly associated with incident CKD. LASSO identified 23 candidates, and LightGBM identified four key proteins (EDA2R, GDF15, HAVCR1, and SCARB2). The four-protein model showed comparable performance to the demographic model (AUC, 0.796 vs. 0.805; p = 0.14), while their combination improved discrimination (AUC, 0.830 [95% confidence interval, 0.806-0.855]; p < 0.001). The combined model also showed improved performance across 5-year, 10-year, and >10-year CKD prediction horizons. SHAP and Kaplan-Meier analyses consistently supported the predictive value of these proteins, and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness.

CONCLUSION: Integrating plasma proteomics with machine learning improves internal risk prediction for incident CKD. The parsimonious four-protein panel may provide complementary information for CKD risk stratification, although external validation is needed before clinical application.

articles.title: Staff retention in echocardiography: a formal exploration of workforce drivers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retention of diagnostic imaging staff is a growing concern within the NHS, with echocardiography services facing particular pressure due to high demand, workforce shortages, and post-pandemic backlogs. While factors influencing NHS staff retention are well documented, limited research has focused specifically on echocardiography staff, a highly skilled and specialised workforce.

AIM: This study aimed to explore intention to leave among NHS echocardiography staff and to identify factors that encourage retention, alongside perceived barriers to staying within the role or organisation.

METHODS: As a part of business as usual, Trust staff support psychologists offered to meet with echocardiography colleagues for a general support session and to advertise the services they offer. The psychological support aspect of the team session has an evidence base in the Trust that was used to form the session content. All echocardiography staff were invited to attend a facilitated two-hour group or individual sessions combining survey completion, structured discussion, and psychological support. Quantitative data on job satisfaction and intention to leave were collected alongside qualitative discussion data, which were anonymised and analysed thematically. This mixed-methods service evaluation was conducted within a large acute NHS Trust.

RESULTS: Forty-five staff participated, including Band 7 echocardiographers (n = 37) and Band 8 team leaders (n = 8). Retention intent differed by role: 88% of Band 8 leaders reported low intention to leave, compared with 39% of Band 7 staff indicating potential intention to leave within two years. Key retention factors included supportive management, positive team relationships, individualised flexibility, professional autonomy, and individualised plans around work-life balance. Barriers to retention centred on workload pressure, burnout (including musculoskeletal injury risk), limited career progression, and financial concerns. Younger staff were more likely to report thoughts of leaving. Participants highlighted meaningful relationships with patients and colleagues as protective against disengagement, alongside concerns regarding role narrowing and future AI integration. Impressions during the psychological support aspect involved the individualised understanding of flexibility, work-life balance and therefore a variety of potentially helpful solutions. The connection between colleagues generated in the group seemed of benefit.

CONCLUSIONS: Retention among echocardiography staff is influenced by a complex interaction of organisational, professional, and wellbeing factors rather than pay alone. Multifaceted, individualised, targeted retention strategies focusing on workload management, career development, psychological support, and clear communication around service evolution are essential to sustaining this critical workforce.

articles.title: The role of animals in the epidemiology and pathogenesis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS): a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis with a high case-fatality rate and expanding geographic range. Its persistence depends on complex cycles involving ticks and vertebrate animal hosts. A comprehensive understanding of animal roles is critical for predicting spillover risk and developing effective interventions under a One Health framework. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize existing evidence on the roles of domestic animals, wildlife, and companion animals in the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and transmission of SFTSV.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Multiple databases (MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang) and grey literature sources were searched from January 1, 2011 to October 21, 2025. Eligible studies involved non-human animals or ticks and confirmed SFTSV infection or exposure. Evidence was narratively synthesized across prespecified themes: animal host roles, clinical manifestations, transmission dynamics, and prevention strategies. We mapped the distribution of evidence across animal species, study designs, geographic regions, diagnostic approaches, and thematic domains.

RESULTS: The review identified a broad animal host range comprising at least 15 vertebrate species across domestic, wildlife, and companion categories. Domestic ruminants show high seroprevalence and act as primary amplification hosts. Wildlife (e.g., rodents, shrews) contribute to enzootic maintenance. Cats are highly susceptible, develop severe disease with high viral loads, and are a major source of direct non-vector transmission to humans. Dogs often have mild illness but can shed virus persistently. Transmission primarily occurs via the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis, but direct transmission via contact with blood/secretions of sick animals (especially cats and farmed mink) is significant. Prevention requires integrated tick management, biosecurity in veterinary/farm settings, and public education.

CONCLUSIONS: Animals are central to the ecology of SFTSV. Current evidence underscores the necessity of integrated, multisectoral One Health strategies for surveillance, risk communication, and control. Future research priorities include standardizing host-competence studies, harmonizing diagnostics, elucidating comparative immunopathology, and evaluating the feasibility and impact of intervention bundles, including potential veterinary vaccines.
