articles.title: Prognostic value of modified thrombelastometry for thromboembolic risk stratification in neurosurgical patients: protocol for a prospective, multicenter, observational study (TENS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Neurosurgical patients, particularly those with intracranial tumours such as glioma or meningioma, face a markedly elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), with reported rates of deep vein thrombosis between 15% and 70% depending on tumour entity and surgical extent. Current prophylactic strategies rely predominantly on pharmacological and mechanical measures and do not account for the individual complexity of coagulation dynamics. Modified thromboelastometry, employing a low-dose tissue plasminogen activator (TPA) test, enables functional assessment of both fibrinolytic capacity and prothrombotic states at the point of care. We hypothesize that preoperative and perioperative thromboelastometric parameters - in particular lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test - are associated with the occurrence of thromboembolic events in neurosurgical patients.

METHODS: TENS is a prospective, multicenter, observational prognostic factor study targeting 350 evaluable participants (up to 369 enrolled to account for attrition) across four university hospitals in Cologne, Munich (two centres), and Oldenburg. Eligible patients are adults (≥ 18 years) scheduled for neurosurgical procedures involving intracranial tumour resection or with an anticipated operative duration of ≥ 4 h. Thromboelastometric measurements (EXTEM, INTEM, FIBTEM, low-dose TPA test) are performed at three defined time points: before surgery, at the end of surgery, and on postoperative day 1. The primary objective is to assess the prognostic association between lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test and objectively imaging-confirmed venous thromboembolic events occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints comprise further thromboelastometric parameters, standard coagulation laboratory values, and clinical outcomes including length of hospital stay, duration of surgery, ICU stay, and days at home at day 30.

CONCLUSIONS: Modified thromboelastometry has the potential to improve individualised risk stratification for thromboembolism in neurosurgical patients. If lysis time in the low-dose TPA test demonstrates prognostic value for thromboembolic events, this could inform the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic algorithms for high-risk surgical populations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION, DATE: Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien (DRKS), No. DRKS00034388, registered October 8, 2024. Anonymised participant-level data and the statistical analysis code will be made available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author following publication of the primary results, subject to applicable data protection regulations and the terms of the institutional data sharing agreement (see chapter The full study protocol will be publicly accessible via the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS, No. DRKS00034388).

TRIAL STATUS: The study is currently in active recruitment. Recruitment was initiated at the coordinating centre in Cologne on 19 December 2024, with additional centres opening after completion of their local approval and site-initiation processes. As of March 2026, fewer than 50% of the target sample of 350 evaluable participants had been enrolled. Recruitment is expected to be completed by March 2027.

articles.title: Genotype refines risk stratification in dilated cardiomyopathy.
Ultrasound-based assessment of cardiac and hepatic dysfunction: current status and future directions.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a systemic syndrome in which venous congestion and impaired perfusion can produce clinically important hepatic dysfunction. The term cardiohepatic syndrome (CHS) describes this bidirectional interaction, but cardiac and hepatic abnormalities are still often evaluated in parallel rather than as a connected hemodynamic process. Ultrasound is uniquely suited to an integrated assessment because it can characterize cardiac structure and function, systemic venous congestion, hepatic hemodynamics, tissue stiffness, and treatment-related change at the bedside. Conventional transthoracic echocardiography remains the foundation of evaluation, while three-dimensional echocardiography and speckle-tracking techniques improve quantification of right ventricular, atrial, and subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Abdominal Doppler ultrasound, venous congestion scoring, and liver elastography add complementary information, although liver stiffness must be interpreted cautiously because congestion, inflammation, cholestasis, and fibrosis can produce overlapping signals. Artificial intelligence may improve acquisition, measurement reproducibility, and multimodal data integration, but external validation and transparent reporting remain essential. This review summarizes contemporary evidence and proposes a practical, sequential pathway that combines echocardiography, venous Doppler findings, liver stiffness, laboratory biomarkers, and dynamic reassessment after decongestion. The central clinical principle is that CHS should be evaluated as a time-varying cardiohepatic phenotype rather than diagnosed from a single cardiac, hepatic, or biochemical measurement.

articles.title: Central and peripheral Neurolymphomatosis, a rare involvement of DLBCL on PET/CT.
articles.abstract: In this paper we present two rare cases of patients suffering from diffuse large B-cell lymphoma initially treated with chemotherapy. During follow-up, they presented with central and peripheral neurological symptoms, respectively. On PET/CT, intense uptake of FDG was seen indicating neurolymphomatosis. Because of the localization it was not possible to take a biopsy for histological examination, but clinicians relied on imaging, clinical course and laboratory tests for a final diagnosis. Both patients died shortly after this examination underlining the poor prognosis of neurolymphomatosis.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant concurrent or sequential anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and HER2-targeted agents for HER2-positive breast cancer: a randomized phase 2 study (METIS).
articles.abstract: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

articles.title: Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency.

METHODS: In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs.

RESULTS: Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%).

CONCLUSION: Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

articles.title: Precision Social Medicine: Bridging the Gap Between Social Care and Health Systems Integration.
articles.abstract: Health systems serving children have increasingly invested in social care initiatives, yet these programs frequently demonstrate inconsistent effectiveness and face challenges in sustainability and scalability. Precision social medicine (PSM) offers a framework for addressing this gap by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models to match social care interventions to patients' clinical and social context. This article presents a practical, 3-step approach for operationalizing PSM within health systems serving children. These steps are to (1) codefine precision in social care with patients and frontline staff, (2) translate that definition into an AI/ML-informed strategy for identifying risk and assigning services, and (3) test the approach in workflows before it impacts care. We highlight integrating such a framework using pediatric asthma as a case example, tailored for the pediatric hospitalist managing the transition from hospital to home.

articles.title: Diagnosing periprosthetic joint infection: current and novel technologies.
Serum sclerostin in relation to insulin resistance and epicardial fat thickness in obese women.
articles.journal: Hormone molecular biology and clinical investigation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Visceral obesity is closely linked to insulin resistance and cardiometabolic risk. Epicardial adipose tissue, commonly assessed by epicardial fat thickness (EFT), is a clinically relevant fat depot associated with early cardiac remodelling. Sclerostin, a bone-derived protein, may play a role in crosstalk between the skeleton and adipose tissue. However, its relationship with insulin resistance and cardiac visceral fat remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate serum sclerostin levels and their association with insulin resistance and EFT in obese women.

METHODS: This case-control study included 90 women (55 obese and 35 age-matched controls). Participants underwent anthropometric and metabolic assessment, including serum sclerostin measurement. Insulin resistance was evaluated using HOMA-IR, and EFT was assessed by echocardiography. Correlation, ROC, and regression analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Serum sclerostin levels were significantly higher in obese women than in controls (p<0.001). Sclerostin was positively correlated with fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and EFT. Levels were higher in insulin-resistant obese participants than in metabolically healthier obese individuals. ROC analysis showed good discriminative ability for insulin resistance (AUC=0.89) and moderate accuracy for identifying increased EFT (AUC=0.80). In multivariate analysis, BMI, but not sclerostin, remained an independent predictor of increased EFT.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum sclerostin is elevated in obese women and is associated with insulin resistance and adverse metabolic profiles. Although not independently associated with epicardial fat thickness, it reflects metabolic dysfunction related to visceral adiposity and may serve as an indicator of metabolically unhealthy obesity within this cohort.

articles.title: Sequence-Engineered Multifunctional Peptide Nanozyme Gel for Catalytic Microenvironment Regulation in Diabetic Infected Wounds.
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent infection, redox imbalance, and dysregulated enzymatic activity, yet current biomaterials largely function as passive dressings, with limited capacity to actively intervene in the stalled healing cascade. Here, we report a sequence-programmed peptide nanozyme that encodes multiple enzyme-mimetic activities within a single supramolecular framework for adaptive microenvironment regulation. By mimicking the coordination motifs of natural hydrolases and superoxide dismutase, a de novo peptide sequence, C7-RD(S)HHEEH, was rationally engineered to encode integrated nitrogen/oxygen metal-binding sites. The incorporation of a side-chain-modified serine enhances coordination adaptability, while glutamate residues facilitate catalytic functionality. Upon Cu2+ coordination, the peptide self-assembles into a nanozyme exhibiting hydrolase (HYD)-, oxidase (OXD)-, peroxidase (POD)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a unified framework, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of enzymatic debridement, antibacterial defense, and redox homeostasis. Incorporated into a sprayable gelatin hydrogel, the nanozyme provides conformal wound coverage while maintaining excellent biocompatibility and sustained catalytic functionality. In a diabetic bacteria-infected wound model, the nanozyme gel significantly accelerates wound closure, enhances angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and restores tissue regeneration. Our work demonstrates that rational peptide sequence design can encode complex, multimodal catalysis into synthetic nanozymes, offering a programmable approach for active regulation of pathological microenvironments in chronic wound therapy.

articles.title: Utilizing evidence-based diagnosis and treatment for central venous thrombosis: closing the gaps where guidelines fail.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Catheter-related thrombosis (CRT) is a frequent complication of central venous catheters and accounts for most upper extremity deep vein thrombosis events. Despite its increasing clinical burden, management remains poorly standardized because recommendations are largely extrapolated from general venous thromboembolism studies rather than CRT-specific evidence.

AREAS COVERED: We performed a structured comparative review of major international, European, and North American guidelines, consensus documents, and position statements identified through PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus searches covering January 2016 to March 2026. Nineteen documents from vascular medicine, oncology, and vascular access societies were included. Recommendations on diagnostic strategies, imaging modalities, catheter management, anticoagulant selection, treatment duration, and invasive interventions were systematically compared.

EXPERT OPINION: Considerable heterogeneity persists across recommendations. Ultrasound is consistently endorsed as the first-line imaging modality, whereas the role of clinical prediction scores and D-dimer remains uncertain because neither has been validated in CRT populations. Catheters should be preserved when functional, correctly positioned, and free from infection. Anticoagulation for at least 3 months is universally recommended, while invasive procedures should be reserved for selected patients with extensive thrombosis or life- or limb-threatening complications. Prospective studies are urgently needed to validate diagnostic algorithms, optimize anticoagulant strategies, and develop CRT-specific evidence-based pathways.

articles.title: Cytoplasmic mRNA recapping is essential for stress recovery and intracellular proliferation in Trypanosoma cruzi.
articles.abstract: Trypanosoma cruzi, the causative agent of Chagas disease, regulates gene expression predominantly after transcription because it lacks conventional gene-specific promoters. Cytoplasmic mRNA recapping has been proposed to restore translation-competent mRNAs from silenced transcripts, but its physiological role in kinetoplastids has remained unclear. Here, we show that the cytoplasmic capping enzyme TcCe1 supports transcriptome homeostasis, an effective heat-shock response, and productive intracellular infection of host cells. TcCe1 loss was associated with reduced transcript abundance across extended polycistronic transcription units, impaired induction of proteostasis factors under stress, altered steady-state abundance of uncapped transcripts detected by ligation-mediated RT-qPCR, and marked defects in recovery and infectivity. Because cytoplasmic recapping in kinetoplastids is mechanistically distinct from host pathways, TcCe1 may represent a promising target for parasite-selective therapeutics. Together, our findings highlight the importance of TcCe1 in RNA-level regulation, environmental responsiveness, and host adaptation in this early-branching eukaryote.

articles.title: Firearm Injury Prevention in Undergraduate Medical Education in the United States: Current Landscape, Barriers, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Firearm injuries remain a leading cause of preventable death in the United States (US), with physicians uniquely positioned to contribute to firearm injury prevention (FIP). Despite this, there is a lack of recent national assessment of FIP inclusion in US undergraduate medical education (UME). Thus, we looked to assess how medical schools currently incorporate FIP into curricula and what challenges affect its implementation.

METHODS: We distributed a REDCap-based survey to medical education leadership at all LCME- and COCA- accredited medical schools in the US between April and December 2024, assessing FIP curricular content, timing, modes and settings of instruction, assessment strategies, extracurricular opportunities, and perceived barriers to implementation.

RESULTS: Fifty-five institutions (27%) responded, with 64% reporting the inclusion of FIP content in their curricula. Most schools (62%) introduced FIP during clinical years, particularly in pediatrics, emergency medicine, and surgery, and some schools (51%) integrated content preclinically. Common curricular topics included firearm safety counseling, access screening, and identifying risk factors. Only 27% of schools reported formally assessing FIP knowledge. The most frequently cited barriers to implementation were limited curricular time and political/ideological concerns.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest encouraging progress in the incorporation of FIP education within UME compared to the most recent previous data, but they also highlight significant variability and persistent gaps. Broader adoption of standardized FIP curricula, earlier integration during training, and development of robust assessment strategies may enhance awareness and preparedness among future physicians to address firearm injury as a vital public health issue.

articles.title: An Elusive Diagnosis of Strongyloides Infection Masquerading as Daptomycin-Induced Eosinophilic Pneumonitis.
articles.abstract: Daptomycin-induced eosinophilic pneumonitis, characterized by peripheral eosinophilia, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and respiratory symptoms, is a recognized adverse drug effect. However, these findings overlap significantly with pulmonary strongyloidiasis, in which transpulmonary larval migration provokes a similar eosinophil-rich inflammatory response. Failure to distinguish between these entities carries serious consequences, as untreated Strongyloides infection can progress to hyperinfection syndrome with high mortality. We describe a middle-aged male with alcoholic liver cirrhosis who developed peripheral eosinophilia, bilateral pulmonary nodules, migratory consolidative opacities, and pleural effusions while receiving daptomycin for polymicrobial bacteremia. The findings were initially attributed to daptomycin-induced eosinophilic pneumonitis, and the drug was discontinued. However, given clinical suspicion for a parasitic etiology, Strongyloides testing was pursued. Stool ova-and-parasite examination and bronchoalveolar lavage were both negative; however, Strongyloides serology returned positive, confirming the diagnosis. The patient improved both clinically and radiographically following treatment with ivermectin and albendazole. The negative stool and bronchoalveolar lavage results further underscore the suboptimal sensitivity of conventional diagnostic methods and the essential role of serologic testing. Clinicians evaluating eosinophilia with pulmonary infiltrates in patients receiving daptomycin should systematically consider parasitic etiologies, including Strongyloides serology, before attributing findings solely to a drug-related cause.

articles.title: Norovirus outbreaks: maintaining infection prevention standards in community nursing.
articles.abstract: This article explores the evolving evidence surrounding norovirus outbreaks, considers lessons learned since the COVID-19 pandemic and discusses practical implications for community nursing practice in light of current UK guidance and infection prevention standards.

articles.title: Reducing diabetes care costs and district nurse visits through novel insulin regimens.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An increasingly frail and ageing population has resulted in an unsustainable demand on district nurse teams in terms of insulin administration.

AIMS: This quality improvement initiative aimed to reduce district nursing team visits by adjusting the insulin regimens of people with type 2 diabetes from twice to once daily, where possible.

METHODS: The integrated community care team audited all people receiving district nursing visits for insulin administration. Community diabetes specialist nurses provided personalised insulin adjustment guides. HbA1c levels before and after the intervention were assessed over a 3-year follow-up period.

FINDINGS: Twice daily visits were reduced by 77%. Mean HbA1c significantly decreased by 16.3 mmol/mol (1.5%) (from 94.9 [10.8%] to 78.6 [9.3%]) at 12 months. The mortality rate was 30%, and median follow up was 18 months.

CONCLUSIONS: This innovative way of working and change of insulin regimens lessened the burden of insulin administration on district nursing teams, while improving glycaemia and yielding estimated savings of approximately £839 500 annually.

articles.title: MSC-Integrated CuPB-BTB Coaxial Nanofibrous Scaffold for pH-Responsive Infection Monitoring and Antibacterial-Regenerative Wound Therapy.
articles.abstract: The healing process of chronic wounds is often hindered by recurring bacterial infections, inflammation, and inadequate tissue regeneration, which necessitates the development of innovative dressing materials capable of both infection detection and treatment. Herein, we report the development of a coaxial nanofiber scaffold made up of PCL-gelatin integrated with copper-doped prussian blue nanoparticles (CuPB), bromothymol blue (BTB), and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) for concurrent pH-sensitive detection of infection, drug delivery, and tissue regeneration. The coaxial architecture allowed compartmentalized integration of functional elements within the scaffold while preserving its biomimetic fibrous structure for wound dressing application. The release of CuPB nanoparticles, which serve as the source of the antibacterial copper component, imparted antibacterial properties, while BTB facilitated visual colorimetric detection of infection-associated pH changes, allowing real-time monitoring of wound status. The addition of the MSCs further augmented the regenerative potential of the scaffold through the paracrine mediated modulation of inflammation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix remodeling. In vitro assessment indicated the cytocompatibility, MSC compatibility, and hemocompatibility of the scaffold, with hemolysis less than 2%. In vivo assessment revealed that MSC-loaded CuPB-BTB coaxial nanofibers promoted wound healing more efficiently than the control group. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses further revealed improved tissue organization, enhanced angiogenesis as evidenced by VEGF expression, and increased α-SMA associated tissue remodeling. Hence, this multifunctional scaffold represents a promising theranostic wound dressing capable of integrating infection monitoring, antibacterial action, and MSC-mediated tissue regeneration for chronic wound management.

articles.title: Nano-emulsification and soft gel encapsulation to improve the delivery of anti-diabetic drug ertugliflozin-L-pyroglutamic acid via SNEDDS: an in vitro assessment using RP-HPLC.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop and evaluate a novel soft gelatin capsule formulation of ertugliflozin-L-pyroglutamic acid (ERT) using a self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (SNEDDS) to enhance its solubility, physicochemical stability, and in vitro drug dissolution relative to the commercial Steglatro® tablets.

SIGNIFICANCE: Poor aqueous solubility and limited dissolution behavior are two major challenges that hinder the therapeutic performance of many antidiabetic drugs. Herein, for the first time, we formulated ERT as a SNEDDS-based soft gelatin capsule, providing a promising strategy for enhancing an oral drug delivery system that manages Type 2 diabetes more efficiently.

METHODS: ERT was encapsulated in a SNEDDS formulation matrix of Labrasol® (surfactant), PEG-200 (co-surfactant), and cardamom oil in an optimized ratio. Stability studies were conducted across varied pH ranges, mimicking the gastrointestinal tract environment. Advanced characterization techniques, including AFM, DLS, Zetasizer, and FT-IR spectroscopy, confirmed consistent particle size and desirable morphological attributes. RP-HPLC, as per ICH guidelines, evaluated the dissolution profile and assay recovery against the commercial Steglatro® tablets.

RESULTS: The optimized ERT-SNEDDS soft gel formulation demonstrated high stability across various pH conditions, with an assay recovery of 98.78 ± 0.04%. The complete dissolution profile (CDP) at three different pH values (0.1 N HCl, pH 4.5 and pH 6.8 buffers) showed significantly superior in vitro drug release compared to the established Steglatro® tablet.

CONCLUSION: The developed SNEDDS-based soft gelatin capsule demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics and rapid in vitro dissolution of ERT, supporting its potential as an alternative lipid-based oral dosage form to the marketed tablet.

articles.title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

METHODS: A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure.

RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

articles.title: Nanomaterial Design for Macrophage Reprogramming: Emerging Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Inflammation and Tumor Therapy.
articles.abstract: Macrophages play a paradoxical role in inflammation and tumor. They can protect the host during acute inflammation but act as the main driver for the chronic inflammation which is a common characteristic of several diseases including rheumatoid arthritis, atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. In the tumor microenvironment, macrophages switch their phenotype to the immunosuppressive M2 state that promotes tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis. Emerging nanomaterial platforms are trying to offer transformative solutions by enabling the precise delivery of immunomodulatory drugs directly to disease-site macrophages. This review will provide comprehensive comparative analysis of these emerging nanomaterial designs strategies across two disease paradigms: inflammatory diseases and tumor. The discussion will focus on various strategies which include inhibiting chemokine axis (CCL2-CCR2 axis), selective elimination of macrophages through apoptosis, metabolic reprogramming, biomimetic and apoptotic cell-inspired nanoparticles leveraging natural macrophage clearance pathways to promote M2 polarization in inflammation, and the activation of tumor-associated macrophages via TLR and STING agonist. We highlight the role of nanoparticle surface chemistry, composition, and targeting ligands in achieving the two opposite therapeutic outcomes of these two diseases while maintaining some common design principles including EPR-mediated accumulation at the disease sites and biomimetic modifications. We also mentioned novel next-generation nanoparticle-based platforms that are currently in clinical trials for the treatment of tumor and inflammatory diseases. Finally, we discuss the barriers that limit the clinical translational potential of broad nanoparticles, with particular emphasis on nanoparticle-related immunotoxicity, macrophage heterogeneity, and manufacturing reproducibility of the nanoparticles.

articles.title: Redox-Active Nanoceria Integrated with Glucose Oxidase for Glucose-Triggered Metformin Release: Promising Nanocarrier for Managing Oxidative Stress and Hyperglycemia in Diabetes Pathophysiology.
articles.abstract: Development of a glucose-responsive drug delivery platform remains a promising strategy for self-regulated treatment of diabetes mellitus. In the present study, we developed a multifunctional nanocarrier system for the glucose-sensitive delivery of metformin (Met) based upon amine-functionalized nanoceria (NC-NH2) coupled with glucose oxidase (GOx) and capped with dextran. Nanoceria's inherent ability to scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) was made possible by its nanozyme feature, and GOx converts glucose into gluconic acid, and thereby causing drug release in a glucose-responsive manner. Drug release was controlled by the dextran shell, which served as a biocompatible gatekeeper. Under hyperglycemic conditions, the synthesized nanocarrier (NC-GOx-Met-Dex) demonstrated regulated, glucose-triggered metformin release with little release at normoglycemic levels. NC-GOx-Met-Dex showed good structural stability under physiologically simulated circumstances, selective glucose-dependent drug release kinetics in cell-free, in vitro, and ex vivo systems, and promising cellular uptake in muscle cells without causing any cytotoxicity. NC-GOx-Met-Dex enhanced glucose uptake, glucose utilization and translocation of glucose transporter protein (GLUT4) compared to the metformin-alone-treated group in palmitic acid-treated (PA, 0.75 mM) muscle cells. Further in vivo studies showed that compared to metformin alone-treated group, the nanocarrier group showed remarkable glycemic management, improvement of insulin levels, and increased metformin bioavailability in muscle tissues in animal models of diabetes mellitus. Nevertheless, NC-GOx-Met-Dex gavaging to untreated animals did not cause any abnormal behavior or adverse effects, and levels of hepato-renal biomarkers, as well as blood cell profiling, were comparable to the untreated group. In general, this research provides a viable strategy for personalized diabetes therapy through the use of a dual and multifunctional nanosystem capable of responding to hyperglycemia while preventing oxidative stress.

articles.title: Tricuspid Regurgitation: Choosing the Right Treatment for the Right Patient at the Right Time.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery

articles.title: Effects of LBBAP pacing-site position under a modelled proximal LBBB: a 24-model electrophysiological simulation study.
articles.abstract: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) may recruit the distal left-sided conduction system, but the electrical effect of pacing-site position along the left bundle branch (LBB) remains incompletely defined. We evaluated this effect in 24 four-chamber virtual heart anatomies using a Reaction-Eikonal finite-element model with rule-based myocardial fibres and algorithmically generated His-Purkinje networks. A modelled proximal His-to-LBB disconnection preserved the distal LBB-Purkinje network while interrupting its proximal connection. Six conditions were simulated in each anatomy: a sinoatrial-node-initiated left bundle branch block control, right ventricular apical pacing, right ventricular outflow-tract pacing and a modelled non-selective LBB capture configuration at proximal, nominal and distal positions. The primary outcome was BiV_TAT95, the 95th percentile of activation times across left-ventricular, right-ventricular and interventricular-septal nodes. The control-versus-paced analysis used a common simulation-clock origin and was interpreted as contextual benchmarking, whereas the positional analysis used matched direct ventricular stimulation. In the matched positional analysis, median BiV_TAT95 was 104.5, 93.5 and 88.5 ms for proximal, nominal and distal LBBAP, respectively (Friedman chi-square = 48.000,P< 0.001, Kendall'sW= 1.000); every anatomy followed distal < nominal < proximal. In three selected anatomies, a 20% decrease or increase in the prescribed myocardial conduction speeds altered absolute activation times but preserved this ordering in all nine anatomy-by-speed combinations. Under the tested homogeneous substrate and modelled non-selective capture configuration, the distal tested position produced the lowest simulated BiV_TAT95; this does not imply superiority for every activation metric. This conditional prediction requires validation against patient-specific electrical data.

articles.title: Design of Smart Antifouling Surfaces Using Enzyme-Responsive Surface Topographies.
articles.abstract: Biofilm accumulation on polymeric surfaces remains a persistent challenge in biomedical, industrial, and environmental systems. Here, we report an enzyme-responsive antifouling surface that integrates particle-generated topography with biologically activated surface renewal. Microparticles of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) and the chitinase-responsive polymer PHEVD were generated by mechanical abrasion and embedded into poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) to create polymer-composite surfaces with three-dimensionally distributed microparticles. PET served as a nonenzyme-responsive control while PHEVD provided an enzyme-degradable phase designed to respond to bacterial activity. Particle-containing PDMS surfaces significantly reduced 24 h Escherichia coli RP437/pRSH109 biofilm biomass, with 2000-grit PHEVD surfaces producing the strongest inhibition and reducing biomass by 86 ± 3% relative to flat PDMS. In contrast, Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 biofilm biomass after 24 h was not significantly reduced by either PET- or PHEVD-containing surfaces, indicating species-dependent early-stage antibiofilm behavior. However, after 7 days, PHEVD-containing surfaces significantly reduced mature PAO1 biofilm biomass. Under static culture, 600- and 2000-grit PHEVD surfaces reduced PAO1 biomass by 60.0 ± 5.5% and 71.0 ± 13.4%, respectively. Under shaking culture at 200 rpm, 600-grit PHEVD reduced retained PAO1 biomass by 93.6 ± 0.03% compared with flat PDMS and by 93.1 ± 0.03% compared with 600-grit PET. These results suggest that PHEVD-containing surfaces do not primarily prevent early PAO1 attachment but instead promote mature biofilm destabilization and removal. The observed 7-day PAO1 reduction is consistent with a coupled mechanism in which mechanical disturbance exposes PHEVD-rich domains, enabling PAO1-associated enzymatic activity to degrade the exposed PHEVD phase and weaken the biofilm-surface interface. This work establishes a facile strategy for designing biologically activated antifouling surfaces that convert microbial enzymatic activity into a trigger for prolonged biofilm control.

articles.title: Demographic and clinical factors associated with Syphilis treatment initiation in a tribal health system: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) individuals are disproportionately burdened by syphilis compared with other racial and ethnic groups. Early syphilis treatment is important to reduce transmission and prevent negative health outcomes. Understanding the characteristics of individuals who test positive and the factors associated with initiating treatment will support syphilis prevention and treatment efforts.

METHODS: Cherokee Nation conducted a retrospective cohort study of individuals who tested positive for syphilis between 2016 and 2023. Data were collected from electronic health records and analyzed descriptively using counts and percentages and inferentially using Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Overall, 356 individuals tested positive for syphilis and 314 (88.2%) initiated treatment. Most individuals who tested positive were ≤ 34 years (60.7%), single (83.4%), diagnosed during the COVID-19 pandemic (75.8%), residing in a county with a Cherokee Nation clinic (84.3%), and had a non-emergency healthcare visit within one year (70.5%). Approximately half (52.0%) had documented substance use and 31.2% had an STI co-infection within one year. Individuals diagnosed outside of an emergency department or urgent care setting had higher odds of initiating treatment compared with those diagnosed in an emergency department or urgent care setting (aOR=2.01, 95% CI: 1.02-3.97). Individuals with an STI co-infection had higher odds of initiating treatment compared with those without an STI co-infection (aOR=2.96, 95% CI: 1.19-7.33).

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that focusing public health and clinical syphilis treatment efforts on emergency department and urgent care providers and patients may increase syphilis treatment initiation.

articles.title: Dissecting diastolic stiffness.
articles.abstract: JGP study (Shahid et al. https://doi.org/10.1085/jgp.202614028) reveals sex-based differences in the contributors to diastolic stress in cardiomyocytes from heart failure with preserved ejection fraction model mice.

articles.title: Peptide profiling of casein peptide reveals its anti-diabetic effects via DPP-IV inhibition and IRS1/PI3K/AKT signaling.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a growing global health burden, increasing demand for safe food-derived strategies for glycemic control. Casein-derived peptides have potential metabolic benefits, but their antidiabetic mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, casein peptide (CNP), enriched in low-molecular-weight peptides (<3 kDa), was investigated as the principal bioactive intervention for T2DM regulation. LC-MS/MS identified 880 peptides; among the 50 most abundant, all were predicted to inhibit DPP-IV, 26 to inhibit α-glucosidase, and one to inhibit α-amylase. CNP inhibited DPP-IV in vitro in a concentration-dependent manner (IC50 = 5.06 ± 0.41 mg mL-1) and crossed Caco-2 monolayers partly through endocytosis and PepT1-mediated transport. In HFD/STZ-induced T2DM mice, CNP improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, ameliorated dyslipidemia, attenuated tissue injury and systemic inflammation, and restored GLP-1/DPP-IV balance and IRS1/PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings identify CNP as a key food-derived bioactive peptide system that modulates T2DM through complementary effects on intestinal transport, incretin regulation, glucose-lipid homeostasis, inflammation, and insulin signaling, supporting its potential for development as a functional food ingredient for T2DM management.

articles.title: Anterior Quadratus Lumborum Block for Postoperative Analgesia in Hip Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials with Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pain following hip surgery remains challenging to manage despite the use of multimodal analgesia. Anterior quadratus lumborum block (aQLB) has been proposed as an effective regional analgesic technique; however, its clinical efficacy remains uncertain.

AIMS: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate whether aQLB reduces postoperative opioid consumption and pain following hip surgery.

STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science were systematically searched through March 2026. The primary outcome was 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption. Random-effects models were used for all pooled analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were also performed.

RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs involving 994 patients were included in the analysis. aQLB reduced 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption, expressed as morphine milligram equivalents (MME) (mean difference, -6.60 mg; 95% confidence interval, -10.46 to -2.74; p = 0.003; I² = 94%). aQLB also reduced pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), and rescue analgesic requirements, with no significant differences in time to rescue analgesia, mobilization, or hospital stay. The certainty of evidence was low for 24-hour MME, pain at rest across all assessed time points, and rescue analgesic requirements, and moderate for pain during movement at 6 hours and PONV.

CONCLUSION: aQLB was associated with statistically significant reductions in 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption, early postoperative pain at rest, rescue analgesic requirements, and PONV after hip surgery. However, the magnitude of these benefits was small and did not consistently exceed established thresholds for clinical importance, and the certainty of evidence remained low.

articles.title: Bioglass-Doped Hydroxyapatite Sol-Gel Coatings Enhance Curcumin Release and Biological Performance of Ti6Al4V Orthopedic Implants.
articles.abstract: Curcumin is a bioactive polyphenol exhibiting antibacterial and antiosteosarcoma properties; however, its clinical translation is constrained by poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability. In this work, bioglass (BG) was incorporated into sol-gel-derived hydroxyapatite (HA) coatings on Ti6Al4V substrates to enable compositional control over curcumin release and biological response. HA coatings containing 1, 2.5, and 5 wt % BG were fabricated to investigate the influence of BG content on release behavior and multifunctional performance. Increasing BG content enhanced curcumin release by up to 1.4-fold at pH 5.0 and 1.6-fold at pH 7.4 relative to HA controls, consistent with increased coating degradation and microstructural changes associated with increasing BG content. The release profiles exhibited an initial burst followed by an asymptotic plateau, consistent with sustained release from the coating. BG-containing coatings also promoted osteoblast viability, increasing metabolic activity by up to 70% with BG alone and up to 86% in BG-containing curcumin-loaded coatings. In contrast, curcumin selectively reduced osteosarcoma cell viability by 67% after 11 days, accompanied by increased reactive oxygen species generation and mitochondrial dysfunction, suggesting oxidative stress-mediated cytotoxicity. Antibacterial testing demonstrated up to 78% reduction in Staphylococcus aureus viability after 72 h. These results demonstrate that compositional tuning of BG within HA coatings enables simultaneous control of drug release and selective biological responses, providing a multifunctional platform for orthopedic implants that supports osteoblast activity while mitigating infection and tumor recurrence risks.

articles.title: Spatial sampling for triaxial OPM-MEG: understanding the neurodevelopmental trajectory.
articles.abstract: Objective. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures magnetic fields generated by current flow in neural assemblies, providing a non-invasive means to track brain function. In recent years, the MEG field has been revolutionised by a new class of field sensor called an optically pumped magnetometer (OPM). OPMs are small and lightweight, allowing for the construction of wearable and reconfigurable arrays of 'triaxial' field sensors (that measure magnetic fields along three axes simultaneously). These systems can be used to capture MEG data across the lifespan, from infancy to adulthood. With such multi-axis sensing arrays coming into routine use, here we aimed to determine how dense a sensor array is required to adequately capture the spatial variation of neuromagnetic fields across the scalp.Approach. We simulated neuromagnetic fields based on realistic head geometries of individuals aged 15 months to 34 years. We then used two independent approaches to determine the sensor spacing required to capture the highest spatial variation of the field across the scalp surface: one method was based on spherical harmonic decomposition of neuromagnetic fields, and the other based on evaluating sensor redundancy in densely sampled arrays.Main results. Both methods agree in showing that the required sensor separation increases with age, from ∼40 mm in a 1 year-old to ∼55 mm in an adult.Significance. The sensor spacings obtained in our simulations represent upper bounds for the required values: separations above these bounds will not adequately capture spatial field variation; however, reducing sensor separation below these limits will continue to improve performance. These findings are important for the future development of OPM-MEG technology, particularly the construction of systems for neurodevelopmental applications.

articles.title: Highly neutralizing anti-IFN-ω autoantibodies underlie severe pediatric adenovirus infection.
articles.abstract: Neutralizing autoantibodies (auto-Abs) against type I IFNs (IFN-α and IFN-ω) have emerged as major acquired risk factors for severe viral infections. Human adenovirus (HAdV) is highly prevalent in children and can cause severe pneumonia, but the host determinants of disease severity remain poorly understood. We describe here a 5-year-old child with life-threatening HAdV-B7 pneumonia requiring intensive care who carried high-titer anti-IFN-ω auto-Abs of the IgG1 and IgG3 subclasses. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells produced normal amounts of IFN-α and IFN-ω ex vivo; however, IFN-ω was undetectable in the plasma during acute illness. Functional assays demonstrated that the patient's plasma strongly neutralized IFN-ω, abolishing its antiviral signaling and protective effects, resulting in high levels of adenovirus replication and virus-induced cytotoxicity. These findings implicate anti-IFN-ω auto-Abs in severe adenoviral infection and support immunological screening of pediatric patients with unexplained severe viral pneumonia, which may guide targeted management.

articles.title: IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency: Clinical features and transplant outcomes.
articles.abstract: IRF4 is a transcription factor within the interferon regulatory factor family that controls key aspects of lymphocyte differentiation and adaptive immunity. The heterozygous IRF4 p.Thr95Arg (p.T95R) variant affecting the DNA-binding domain was recently identified to cause a new inborn error of immunity, but the longitudinal clinical course and therapeutic implications remain incompletely defined. We performed detailed clinical characterization and follow-up of all 10 known patients. Each presented with early-onset combined immunodeficiency characterized by hypo- or agammaglobulinemia and marked susceptibility to opportunistic infections. Pulmonary disease was universal, and gastrointestinal involvement was associated with a more severe clinical course. Four patients underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation; two survived, and two died. Notably, both deaths occurred in patients transplanted in the setting of active infection. These findings define IRF4 p.T95R as a profound combined immunodeficiency with high infectious burden and demonstrate that disease severity and intervention timing may contribute to transplant outcomes, supporting early diagnosis and timely transplantation before uncontrolled infection.

articles.title: Lipid remodeling enables adaptation to chronic hyperosmotic stress.
articles.abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) accumulate in response to diverse cellular stresses. However, their regulation and physiological roles remain poorly understood in most contexts. Here, we show that in budding yeast, chronic hyperosmotic stress induces sustained LD accumulation. Unlike the transient LD response observed during acute osmotic shock, chronic stress triggers prolonged, Dga1-dependent triacylglycerol synthesis. In the absence of triacylglycerol synthesis, cellular fitness is impaired. Lipidomic profiling reveals extensive membrane remodeling during chronic hyperosmotic stress, most notably an increase in phosphatidylcholine (PC) resulting in changes to membrane properties. In LD-deficient cells, the hyperosmotic stress-induced PC increase is blunted, while enhancing PC synthesis improves the fitness of triacylglycerol-deficient cells. Thus, LD accumulation and phospholipid remodeling underlie an adaptive response to chronic hyperosmotic stress.

articles.title: Short-term bioavailability of EPA and DHA from an algae oil-fortified soymilk compared with algae oil capsules.
articles.abstract: Although dietary guidelines emphasize consuming foods rich in eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), intakes remain below recommended levels in many populations worldwide. To address this concern, we developed an algae oil-fortified soymilk beverage and assessed its short-term chronic bioavailability compared to algae oil capsules. In a 4-week, open-label, randomized parallel trial, 21 healthy adults consumed either an algae oil-fortified soymilk beverage (200 mg EPA, 320 mg DHA) or a closely matching dose of algae oil-fortified capsules (230 mg EPA, 380 mg DHA) daily. The primary endpoint was the change in red blood cell (RBC) EPA and DHA, with plasma and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) profiles assessed secondarily. Both groups exhibited significantly increased EPA and DHA across all blood compartments over the 4-week intervention. Although the capsule group showed a greater unadjusted increase in RBC and plasma DHA, no significant difference in EPA or DHA accumulation remained after normalizing for dose and compliance. Therefore, fortified soymilk is a well-tolerated delivery vehicle for algae oil which increases RBC EPA and DHA offering a comparable food-based alternative to traditional capsules.

articles.title: Microbiota-derived urolithins and cortical thickness in cognitively healthy older adults: a longitudinal MRI analysis of the WAHA trial.
articles.abstract: Cortical thickness, assessed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), is a biomarker of age-related neurodegeneration. Walnut ellagitannins may influence brain structure via gut microbiota-derived urolithins. We examined whether longitudinal changes in urinary urolithins are associated with concurrent changes in cortical thickness in cognitively healthy older adults. This longitudinal MRI sub-study was conducted within the Walnuts and Healthy Aging study, a two-center (Barcelona, Spain and Loma Linda, California) randomized controlled trial testing the effects of 2-year daily walnut consumption vs. a control diet on age-related health outcomes in older individuals. A subset of participants from the Barcelona center underwent structural MRI at baseline and after 2 years. Urinary urolithin concentrations were quantified by liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry, and their changes were related to concurrent changes in cortical thickness using multivariable-adjusted linear regression models, with analyses stratified by urolithin metabotype to account for inter-individual variability. A total of 104 participants were included. Among those allocated to the walnut diet (n = 55), greater increases in urolithin A (β = 0.023 [95% CI, 0.003-0.043] per 1-SD), urolithin C (β = 0.015 [95% CI, <0.001-0.029] per 1-SD), and its glucuronide conjugate (β = 0.017 [95% CI, 0.002-0.031] per 1-SD) were associated longitudinally with preservation of cortical thickness, predominantly in right-hemisphere regions. Associations were more pronounced among metabotype B individuals. These findings provide novel clinical evidence linking microbiota-derived (poly)phenol metabolites to brain aging and support a precision nutrition framework. Trial registration: Clinical trials.gov as NCT01634841.

articles.title: Minimally Invasive Tricuspid Valve Operations: Three Decades of Leipzig Experience.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Data on minimally invasive tricuspid valve (TV) surgery for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) remain limited, particularly regarding long-term outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included adult patients who underwent minimally invasive TV surgery through right mini-thoracotomy for severe TR as the primary indication between 1996 and 2024. Patients with endocarditis or tricuspid stenosis, as well as those undergoing left-sided valve surgery, were excluded. The primary end-point was all-cause mortality during follow-up.

RESULTS: A total of 199 patients with a median age of 70.0 years, including 110 (55%) women, were analysed. Sixty-four (32%) had previous cardiac surgery. The median EuroSCORE II was 3.6% (1.8-6.0), and the median TRI-SCORE-predicted mortality was 5.0% (3.0-14.0). Three patients (1.5%) required conversion to sternotomy. Tricuspid valve repair was performed in 108 patients (54%). In-hospital mortality was 6% for the entire cohort (12/199). Discharge echocardiography demonstrated no or mild residual TR in 176/194 patients (91%). Estimated overall survival was 85% (95% confidence interval, 80%-90%) at 1 year, 69% (62%-75%) at 5 years, and 53% (46%-61%) at 10 years. Repeat TV surgery was recorded in 7 patients (4%). In multivariable analysis, older age, male sex, urgent/emergent operation, atrial fibrillation/flutter, diabetes mellitus, signs of right heart failure, lower glomerular filtration rate, and lower preoperative haemoglobin independently predicted mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive TV surgery for severe TR was associated with low conversion rates and provided good early and late outcomes. Repair was performed in over half of the patients.

articles.title: The gut-kidney-brain axis in chronic kidney disease: mechanisms and nutritional interventions for cognitive protection.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasingly recognised as a systemic disorder extending beyond renal impairment to include cognitive decline. The present review focuses on the mechanisms through which CKD and cognitive impairment are connected in the gut-kidney-brain axis, especially when considering the role played by nutrition as a possible target for interventions. Sources of literature were identified in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar up until 2026 and included in the present analysis clinical trials, systematic reviews and studies in peer-reviewed journals related to nutritional, microbial and cognitive outcomes in CKD. From both interventional and observational data, CKD is characterised by a reduction in short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Roseburia spp., as well as an increase in proteolytic organisms responsible for uremic toxin production with a consequent elevation in indoxyl sulphate (IS) and p-cresyl sulphate (PCS). Metabolic abnormalities in IS and PCS have been linked to the disruption of blood-brain barrier (BBB), microglial activation, and impaired attention, executive function and memory in human subjects, while animal studies suggest additional impairments including neuronal cell death and learning impairment in hippocampus, although causality cannot be confirmed in humans. Deficiencies of proteins, vitamin B, vitamin D, magnesium, and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) are frequently found in CKD and contribute to the above-mentioned problems. Renal-adapted Mediterranean diet, supplementation with micronutrients guided by biomarkers and synbiotics reduce levels of PCS and inflammation, while prebiotics and synbiotics perform better than probiotics, although no cognitive endpoints were defined in most studies.

articles.title: Role of host nitrogen use efficiency in determining arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi responses to nitrogen enrichment.
articles.abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) form widespread symbiotic relationships with plants, influencing nutrient acquisition and ecosystem functioning. Although nitrogen (N) enrichment effects on AMF have been widely studied, whether host N-use efficiency (NUE) mediates these responses remains unclear. Here, we integrated a global meta-analysis with a greenhouse experiment using low- and high-NUE maize (Zea mays) cultivars Xianyu335 (XY335) and Qianyu568 (QY568) and a decade-long field experiment using low-NUE Sidan19 (SD19) and high-NUE Jidan27 (JD27). The global synthesis revealed a nonlinear response of AMF to increasing N addition, while the complementary experiments showed that host NUE altered both the response direction and its underlying regulatory pathway. In the field, AMF abundance and richness of SD19 declined linearly with increasing N availability, largely through root morphological plasticity. By contrast, JD27 exhibited a hump-shaped response to N addition, mediated by N-induced soil acidification. Furthermore, N addition altered AMF community composition, inducing taxonomic trade-offs between Glomeraceae and Paraglomeraceae, which contributed to the hump-shaped response of AMF in JD27. Together, our findings identify host NUE as a biological filter that modifies how established plant, soil, and fungal mechanisms regulate mycorrhizal responses to N enrichment, offering critical insights for sustainable agricultural management under future global change scenarios.

articles.title: The IKKε-GABPA axis regulates STING transcription to orchestrate antiviral immunity and inflammation.
articles.abstract: The cGAS-STING pathway plays a critical role in antiviral defense and inflammatory homeostasis. While posttranslational regulation of STING is well characterized, the transcriptional networks directly governing Sting1 expression remain unclear. Here, we identify the transcription factor GA-binding protein alpha (GABPA) as a critical regulator of STING-dependent type I IFN (IFN-I) responses in macrophages. Mechanistically, GABPA directly binds to the Sting1 promoter, thereby transcriptionally sustaining basal STING expression. Upon viral infection, activated IκB kinase epsilon (IKKε) phosphorylates GABPA at S447, which further enhances its transcriptional activity and amplifies the STING-IFN-I signaling cascade. Notably, Gabpa deficiency protects mice from DSS-induced colitis, and this protective effect is abolished upon Sting1 deletion. Strikingly, patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) exhibit elevated GABPA expression that positively correlates with STING hyperactivation and enhanced inflammatory signatures. Moreover, a GABPA-blocking peptide effectively suppresses aberrant IFN-β production in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from SLE patients, highlighting its therapeutic potential for interferonopathies.

articles.title: HUCMSCs-Derived Exosomes Attenuate Keloid Fibroblast Pathological Phenotypes with Associated Metabolic-Redox-Matrix Network Remodeling: A Proteomic and In Vivo Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (HUCMSCs-Exo) have emerged as investigational cell-free candidates for the treatment of fibrotic diseases.

AIMS: To examine the phenotypic effects of HUCMSCs-Exo on keloid fibroblasts (KFs) in vitro, characterize associated proteomic, hub-protein, and redox-mitochondrial changes, and evaluate their in vivo effects using a nude mouse xenograft model.

STUDY DESIGN: In vitro and in vivo study.

METHODS: HUCMSCs-Exo were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and characterized using transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and Western blotting for CD9, CD63, and CD81. Label-free quantitative proteomics, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis were performed. Western blot validation, DCFH-DA, JC-1, and MitoSOX assays, and peritumoral administration of HUCMSCs-Exo in vivo, together with biosafety evaluations based on hematology, serum biochemistry, and organ histopathology, were performed.

RESULTS: PKH67-labeled exosomes were internalized by KFs in a time-dependent manner. In vitro, HUCMSCs-Exo inhibited KF proliferation in a dose- and time-dependent manner, induced apoptosis, caused cell-cycle arrest at the G0/G1 phase, and suppressed migration. The expression of fibrosis-associated markers, including fibronectin (FN1), alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), collagen type I (COL-I), and collagen type III (COL-III), was downregulated at both the mRNA and protein levels. Label-free quantitative proteomics identified 951 differentially expressed proteins. KEGG enrichment analysis demonstrated enrichment in metabolic pathways, carbon metabolism, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis. PPI network analysis identified seven candidates hub proteins, of which APEX1, MMP2, and HMOX1 remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction; the other four candidates, including TGFB1, did not survive correction. Therefore, the matrix- and TGF-beta-related findings are supported by orthogonal validation rather than by the corrected proteomic screen alone. Western blot validation demonstrated reduced abundance of TGFB1, MMP2, TIMP1, and TXN2 and increased abundance of APEX1 after HUCMSCs-Exo treatment. The DCFH-DA, JC-1, and MitoSOX assays indicated reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species levels, preservation of mitochondrial membrane potential, and reduced mitochondrial superoxide signals. In vivo, peritumoral administration of HUCMSCs-Exo suppressed keloid xenograft growth and was accompanied by reduced collagen deposition and lower expression of FN1, α-SMA, COL-I, and COL-III. Biosafety evaluation revealed no detectable abnormalities in hematology, serum biochemistry, or organ histopathology under the conditions tested.

CONCLUSION: The combined data indicate that HUCMSCs-Exo attenuate KF proliferation and fibrogenic phenotypes and are accompanied by proteomic, hub-protein, and redox-mitochondrial changes consistent with metabolic-redox-matrix network remodeling. These molecular associations are correlative and were not tested using perturbation experiments.

articles.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of [18F]FDG and [68Ga]/[18F]PSMA PET/CT Images via Data-Centric Deep Learning.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study was to develop and validate lesion identification in oncologic nuclear imaging (LION), an open-source PET-only tumor segmentation pipeline for [18F]FDG and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted PET/CT, and to investigate how training data characteristics influence segmentation performance. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study, 5209 [18F]FDG PET/CT scans spanning 19 disease types and 2046 PSMA-targeted PET/CT scans were used to train PET-only segmentation models. Tumor segmentation incorporated organs with physiologic uptake as auxiliary classes to enable PET-only inference. Tumor occurrence maps (TOMs) quantified tumor spatial diversity across the training data. For [18F]FDG, disease-specific and mixed-disease models trained on progressively larger subsets were compared to test whether increasing spatial diversity improves generalization. Scanner-related domain shift was analyzed using DINOv2 embeddings. Models were evaluated on multicenter holdout cohorts (616 [18F]FDG scans across 4 diseases; 443 PSMA-targeted prostate cancer scans) and compared with 3 open-source tools. Results: Organ context improved median Dice from 0.62 to 0.71 for [18F]FDG and from 0.75 to 0.83 for PSMA, on the complete holdout cohorts. Spatial diversity measured by TOMs was strongly associated with Dice (Spearman ρ = 0.80, P = 0.003). A mixed-disease model trained on 500 patients matched the performance of a lymphoma specialist model trained on 3031 cases. DINOv2 embeddings revealed scanner-induced domain shift between same-disease cohorts. LION achieved median Dice scores of 0.71 for [18F]FDG and 0.85 for PSMA and outperformed other open-source approaches on the model-comparison test set, which excluded the AutoPET test cases. Conclusion: LION enables PET-only automated segmentation for [18F]FDG and PSMA-targeted PET. Training data composition, particularly spatial diversity quantified by TOMs, was strongly associated with segmentation performance.

articles.title: Autologous Blood Pleurodesis for Postoperative Air Leakage Following Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Postoperative air leakage following lung surgery prolongs chest drainage duration and length of hospitalization and the evidence regarding treatment with autologous blood pleurodesis (ABP) is scarce. We decided to investigate if ABP would influence postoperative air leakage when used on the first postoperative day following elective video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).

METHODS: In this multicentre randomized controlled trial, patients with an air leakage greater than 40 mL/min during cough and mobilization on their first postoperative day following elective VATS were randomized 1:1 to standard chest drain management with or without ABP (stratified by lobectomy or wedge resection). The chest drain was removed after standardized digital drainage criteria, and the primary endpoint was time to chest drain removal. Patients with persistent air leakage beyond postoperative day 7 were censored to allow for individualized management.

RESULTS: A total of 268 patients were randomized (134 in each group), after lobectomy (n = 238) or wedge (n = 30). Median chest drain duration was 3.4 days (95% CI, 3.0-4.9) in the ABP group vs 5.0 days (95% CI, 4.0-6.8) in the control group (P = .007). By postoperative day 7, chest drains had been removed in 74% vs 62% of patients, respectively. ABP significantly increased the rate of chest drain removal (HR 1.49; 95% CI, 1.11-2.01; P = .007). The treatment effect was consistent across both participating centres.

CONCLUSIONS: Early autologous blood pleurodesis significantly shortens chest drain duration in patients with postoperative air leakage following VATS. This simple and low-cost intervention should be considered in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery protocols after thoracic surgery.

articles.title: Fucoidan as an anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory agent in humans: a systematic review of clinical evidence and translational potential.
articles.abstract: Purpose: fucoidan is a sulphated polysaccharide from brown seaweeds, commonly used as a dietary supplement due to its proposed anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and potential tumour-related properties. However, despite substantial preclinical evidence, its clinical effects in humans remain unclear. This systematic review aims to evaluate and synthesise current clinical evidence on the effects of fucoidan on inflammatory, immune, metabolic, and tumour-related outcomes in humans. Methods: a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Human interventional studies evaluating fucoidan supplementation and reporting clinically relevant outcomes were included. Eligible populations comprised healthy adults, individuals with metabolic or inflammatory conditions, and patients with cancer. Outcomes included immune function, inflammatory biomarkers, metabolic parameters, tumour-related outcomes, quality of life, and safety. Risk of bias was assessed using the OHAT tool. Due to heterogeneity in study design and outcomes, meta-analysis was not performed. Results: five clinical studies met the inclusion criteria, including three randomised controlled trials and two open-label studies involving patients with cancer, with intervention durations of 2 to 24 weeks. Fucoidan was consistently well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported. Individual controlled trials reported reductions in selected pro-inflammatory cytokines, sex-specific changes in NK cell activity, and changes in gut microbiota composition in individuals with metabolic risk. However, these findings were not consistently replicated across studies. Studies involving patients with cancer reported short-term reductions in inflammatory markers and stable quality-of-life (QOL) measures; however, tumour-related outcomes were inconclusive. Conclusions: current evidence suggests that fucoidan may exert modest anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects under selected clinical conditions; however, the available evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and inconsistent. Although oral fucoidan was generally well tolerated, the small number of studies, limited replication of findings, heterogeneity in study populations and fucoidan characteristics, and methodological limitations preclude definitive conclusions regarding clinical efficacy. Well-designed, adequately powered randomised controlled trials using well-characterised fucoidan and clinically meaningful outcomes are required to establish the clinical efficacy of fucoidan in humans.

articles.title: Endocrine therapy adherence and 10-year cardiometabolic risk in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant endocrine therapy (AET) reduces breast cancer (BC) recurrence but may adversely affect cardiometabolic health. We evaluated the association between AET adherence duration and 10-year risk of hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and mortality among postmenopausal women with early-stage hormone receptor-positive BC.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 8365 postmenopausal women with stage I-III hormone receptor-positive BC within Kaiser Permanente Northern California who initiated AET between 2005 and 2013. Adherence (proportion of days covered >80%) was assessed annually using prescription dispensing data. We estimated 10-year cumulative incidence (CI) under 6 adherence duration strategies (0-5 years) using sequentially doubly robust estimation, adjusting for demographic, clinical, lifestyle, and tumor characteristics. Analyses were stratified by AET type (aromatase inhibitor [AI]; tamoxifen [TAM]).

RESULTS: Overall, 42.7% were adherent for ≥5 years. Compared with nonadherence, 5-year adherence was associated with higher 10-year CI of hypertension (absolute CI difference = 8.81% [95% confidence interval: 4.25 to 13.4]), dyslipidemia (5.16% [0.31 to 10.0]), and diabetes (2.58% [0.02 to 5.14]) but lower all-cause death (10.7% [7.74 to 13.7]) and BC-specific death (5.37% [3.36 to 7.38]). Five-year AI adherence was associated with increased hypertension (9.37% [4.54 to 14.2]), dyslipidemia (6.84% [1.76 to 11.9]), and diabetes (3.29% [0.58 to 6.00]), whereas TAM adherence was associated only with hypertension (9.37% [4.54 to 14.2]). AI adherence was associated with higher dyslipidemia risk than TAM (9.86% [5.09 to 14.6]).

CONCLUSIONS: AI adherence was associated with increased cardiometabolic risk, whereas TAM was associated only with hypertension risk. Despite these risks, AET was associated with improved survival. Further research should evaluate whether cardiometabolic risk factors influence cardiovascular events among BC survivors.

articles.title: Beyond Tumour Size: Integrating Tumour Biology and Technical Quality to Select the Extent of Resection in Early-Stage NSCLC.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Randomized trials have established anatomical segmentectomy as an acceptable alternative to lobectomy for selected patients with peripheral, node-negative Non Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) ≤2 cm. However, trial populations were highly selected, and tumour diameter alone does not capture the biological heterogeneity of early-stage disease.

OBJECTIVE: To critically review the importance of tumour biology on outcomes following lobectomy or segmentectomy.

DESIGN: A structured search of Undermind and PubMed identified comparative studies, randomized trials, meta-analyses, and consensus evidence available through August 10, 2026. Evidence was critically appraised and synthesized narratively, with emphasis on recurrence, survival, staging, and technical quality.

RESULTS: Segmentectomy provides excellent outcomes when adequate margins, anatomical completeness, and rigorous nodal assessment are achieved. Ground-glass opacity (GGO)-dominant tumours, particularly those with low consolidation-to-tumour ratio (CTR), represent the strongest candidates for parenchymal preservation. Increasing CTR, pure-solid morphology, larger size, high Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake, micropapillary or solid histology, spread through air spaces (STAS), visceral pleural invasion, and lymphovascular invasion identify progressively higher-risk phenotypes, but none alone consistently proves that lobectomy improves survival. Micropapillary components exceeding approximately 5%, STAS, inadequate margins, incomplete staging, and multiple coexisting adverse features strengthen the rationale for lobectomy. Segmentectomy is generally preferable to wedge resection for solid, deeper, or biologically aggressive lesions, whereas wedge resection remains reasonable for carefully selected small, peripheral, GGO-dominant tumours. The favourable results of randomized trials depend on accurate preoperative and intraoperative staging and should not be generalized to unselected cT1c or biologically aggressive tumours.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Sublobar resection should be viewed as refined selection rather than replacement of lobectomy. Tumour size defines eligibility, but biology increasingly determines suitability. Precision surgery will require prospective validation of integrated models combining morphology, metabolism, pathology, molecular biomarkers, patient physiology, and technical quality.

articles.title: Optimizing the Therapeutic Index: Sequential Intraarterial-Intravenous PRRT with Personalized Volumetric-Adjusted Dosing.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) frequently present with liver-dominant metastases, which significantly impact prognosis and limit curative options. Although standard intravenous peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with 177Lu-DOTATATE is effective, strategies to intensify the radiation dose to hepatic lesions are needed to improve outcomes. This prospective clinical trial investigated the feasibility, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of a personalized treatment schedule combining intraarterial and intravenous administrations of 177Lu-DOTATATE. Methods: Ten consecutive adults with progressive, nonresectable, liver-dominant metastatic gastroenteropancreatic NETs expressing somatostatin receptors were enrolled. The treatment protocol comprised 4 cycles of 177Lu-DOTATATE administered every 2 mo (2 initial intraarterial cycles followed by 2 intravenous cycles). Intraarterial administration involved angiographically guided, selective catheterization of the hepatic arteries with volumetrically adjusted activity to maximize targeted delivery. Safety monitoring, radiation protection, and dosimetry comparisons between intraarterial and intravenous routes were performed. Results: The intraarterial administration procedure was feasible in 100% of patients. Radiation exposure to staff and patients remained within regulatory limits, with no contamination events.
