Removal through a right upper labial mucosal incision yielded an intact straight 5-cm barbed thread extending toward the left alar base, consistent with presumed migration of a left midface thread. Delayed focal ecchymosis and perioral symptoms after thread lifting may indicate a migration-predominant mechanical complication rather than an infection-dominant process and should prompt early evaluation.

articles.title: Beyond Vascular Territories: The Dual Pathology of Posterior Cerebral Artery Stroke With Reversible Cytotoxic Splenial Lesion.
articles.abstract: The authors present a case highlighting an important stroke mimic: a cytotoxic lesion of the corpus callosum (CLOCC). This case report describes a 28-year-old male with pre-existing hypertension, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, high BMI, and multiple atherosclerotic risk factors, including polysubstance use (cannabis, cigarettes, vaping), who presented with acute-onset left-sided weakness, blurred vision, and paraesthesia. Initial non-contrast CT head was unremarkable. Subsequent MRI demonstrated acute signal changes involving the splenium of the corpus callosum and the tail of the right hippocampus. CT angiography revealed an occlusion of the right posterior cerebral artery at the P2 segment; however, the atypical location for conventional ischaemia raised suspicion for an alternative or concurrent cytotoxic aetiology. Given the patient's markedly poor glycaemic control, a metabolic trigger was strongly considered. Serial MRI imaging was performed, and further supported this hypothesis by demonstrating near-complete regression of the abnormal signal within the splenium following glycaemic optimisation, whilst also correlating with clinical improvement. Management comprised dual anti-platelet therapy, strict glucose and blood pressure control, and lifestyle modification. This case underscores the importance of considering metabolic and cytotoxic aetiologies alongside conventional ischaemia in young stroke presentations, particularly where imaging findings are atypical for vascular territory. It highlights the diagnostic complexity of acute neurological presentations in young patients with significant vascular and metabolic risk factors, demonstrating how severe hyperglycaemia can mimic or coexist with acute ischaemic stroke. Atypical MRI findings for a PCA occlusion seen in this case emphasise the importance of considering reversible cytotoxic lesions, such as CLOCCs, as a differential diagnosis.

articles.title: Fatal Autopsy-Proven Coinfection With Strongyloidiasis and Invasive Aspergillosis in Alcoholic Cirrhosis Without Travel History.
articles.abstract: Coinfection with Strongyloides stercoralis and invasive aspergillosis is rare and often fatal. We report a 70-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis receiving methotrexate who died of respiratory failure. Autopsy revealed intestinal strongyloidiasis and invasive aspergillosis involving the lungs and jejunum, highlighting the diagnostic challenge in immunocompromised patients without endemic-area travel.

articles.title: Trajectory as the Diagnostic Signal: Persistent Multifactorial Anemia Leading to a Diagnosis of Coeliac Disease.
articles.abstract: A man in his late 50s with no documented prior medical history and no laboratory contact for several years presented with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. Initial bloodwork showed hemoglobin of 170-182 g/L with normal red cell indices, possibly reflecting haemoconcentration during acute illness. Hemoglobin then declined to 126-130 g/L and remained persistently low. The decline was accompanied by transient macrocytosis, vitamin B12 deficiency, severe folate deficiency, and progressive iron-store depletion, with ferritin falling from 186 to 55 μg/L alongside falling serum iron and transferrin saturation, although these values stayed within reference ranges. Repletion of B12 and folate normalized the mean corpuscular volume but produced negligible hemoglobin recovery, and a reticulocyte production index of approximately 0.65 confirmed a hypoproliferative marrow response. Renal function was preserved, serum protein electrophoresis was unremarkable, and haemolysis was not supported by the overall pattern. Total IgA was preserved, anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA exceeded 2500 KIU/L (upper limit of normal 15.0 KIU/L; > 166× ULN), and duodenal biopsy demonstrated intraepithelial lymphocytosis with villous blunting. Five months after starting a gluten-free diet, hemoglobin normalized to 142 g/L for the first time in the documented course, anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA fell to 54.1 KIU/L, and transferrin saturation rose to 0.27. Ferritin remained low at 51 μg/L, consistent with recovering erythropoiesis before iron stores are replete. The trajectory, not any single value, was the diagnostic signal: persistent anemia after B12 and folate correction, with iron stores falling inside the reference range, should prompt coeliac testing.

articles.title: Prognostic Factors for Reoperation After Distal Femur Fracture Fixation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal femur fractures (DFFs) carry high rates of nonunion and reoperation despite decades of implant innovation, yet the factors driving these outcomes and the role of dual-implant constructs in high-risk settings remain poorly defined. The primary aim of this systematic review was to identify patient-, fracture-, and technical prognostic factors associated with reoperation for nonunion after DFF fixation; its secondary aim was to evaluate whether dual implant constructs demonstrated improved outcomes in adverse prognostic settings.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through December 2025. Studies enrolling patients aged 16 years or older with DFFs, assessing single- or dual-implant constructs and at least 1 prognostic factor against a clinical or radiographic outcome, were included. Random-effects meta-analyses used unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for dichotomous outcomes, and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence was rated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). The primary outcome was reoperation for nonunion.

RESULTS: A total of 121 studies (9,749 fractures) were included, with 18 contributing to meta-analysis. Four factors achieved moderate certainty of association with reoperation for nonunion: higher body mass index (BMI) (SMD 0.6, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.4-0.7), diabetes (aOR 2.3, 95% CI 0.8-6.0), open fracture (aOR 3.3, 95% CI 1.8-5.8), and stainless steel implant material (aOR 6.1, 95% CI 4.0-9.3). Preoperative infection (aOR 7.3, 95% CI 2.0-27.8) and medial bone gap greater than 1 cm (aOR 4.5, 95% CI 2.8-7.3) were associated with reoperation at low certainty. Most construct parameters showed no consistent independent associations, with technical factors appearing to matter most in the context of higher baseline fracture risk. Dual-implant constructs demonstrated superior outcomes in metaphyseal comminution and medial column deficiency, though no studies formally evaluated prognostic factors within these cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: Open fracture, higher BMI, diabetes, and stainless steel material were the most consistently supported prognostic factors for reoperation, all at moderate certainty. Implant material is the only one of these directly modifiable by the surgeon; the remaining factors may represent candidate targets for dual-implant augmentation, pending confirmation in prognostic studies conducted within dual-implant cohorts. Technical construct parameters showed limited independent associations with reoperation; this likely reflects a floor effect of generally acceptable surgical quality, with their effects depending on clinical context, such as fracture severity or patient risk, rather than indicating these parameters are truly unimportant. Future research should prioritize prospective cohorts with harmonized variable definitions, prognostic analyses within dual implant cohorts, and reporting of all-cause reoperations.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

articles.title: Green-Lyte: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project to Optimize Electrolyte Replacement and Reduce Environmental Burden in ICUs at a Comprehensive Cancer Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrolyte replacement therapies are commonly prescribed in ICUs. However, studies have shown that electrolytes are frequently administered to patients with no clear clinical indications and, in most cases, the IV route is used. In this study, we evaluated the impact of a multidisciplinary quality improvement project, Green-Lyte, on electrolyte replacement and on the environmental burden.

METHODS: This was a quality improvement retrospective study conducted in the adult ICUs at a comprehensive cancer center comparing preimplementation (September 2024 to February 2025) and postimplementation (May 2025 to October 2025) phases of the Green-Lyte project. Green-Lyte consisted of defined criteria to guide both the indication and route of administration for potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus replacement, along with ongoing education and follow-up. Outcomes included the number of electrolyte prescriptions, concordance with Green-Lyte criteria for indication and route of administration, as well as the generated waste and estimated material-associated carbon footprint. Outcomes were standardized per 100 ICU patient-days.

RESULTS: Over the study period, a total of 603 IV and oral electrolyte replacement doses were prescribed in the pre-Green-Lyte phase, and 573 IV and oral electrolyte replacement doses were prescribed in the post-Green-Lyte phase. When adjusted per 100 ICU patient-days, 30.7 doses vs. 19.4 doses were dispensed in the pre- and postimplementation phases, respectively, representing a 36.9% reduction in prescribed electrolytes. Concordance with the Green-Lyte criteria for indication increased from 57.8% to 72.8%, representing a 26% relative improvement, whereas concordance with the criteria for route of administration increased from 22.5% to 45.9%, representing a 104% relative improvement. In addition, the generated waste and the estimated material-associated carbon footprint decreased by 61.8% and 63.2%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The Green-Lyte project was associated with decreased utilization of electrolytes and reduced environmental burden, as demonstrated by decreases in generated waste and estimated material-associated carbon footprint.

articles.title: Ventilator Modes Used to Facilitate Liberation From Mechanical Ventilation: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Liberation from invasive ventilation involves gradual decrements in respiratory support, spontaneous breathing trials, or both. Although various ventilator modes have been studied to facilitate weaning, the approaches used across trials for the highest risk patients are not well summarized. We sought to summarize the different ventilator modes and liberation strategies that have been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of critically ill adults at risk for difficult or prolonged weaning from invasive ventilation.

DATA SOURCES: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: We conducted a scoping review of RCTs that enrolled critically ill adults (≥ 18 yr) who received invasive ventilation for greater than or equal to 24 hours and were considered to have either difficult or prolonged weaning (Weaning according to a New Definition [WIND] group "no wean," "difficult weaning," or "prolonged weaning") and compared two or more assisted ventilatory modes. We excluded trials that compared ventilatory modes for spontaneous breathing test (SBT) conduct, invasive vs. noninvasive ventilation, or tracheostomized patients at the time of randomization.

DATA EXTRACTION: We extracted data related to eligibility criteria, outcomes, and weaning protocols and assessed risk of bias using a modified Cochrane risk of bias tool in duplicate.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Among 38 eligible trials, the most studied ventilatory modes were pressure support ventilation (71.1%, 27 trials) and synchronized intermittent or intermittent mandatory ventilation (31.6%, 12 trials). The most frequently studied automated modes were SmartCare/pressure support (15.8%, six trials) and proportional assist ventilation (15.8%, six trials). Weaning typically used a gradual reduction in support without a mode change (52.6%, 20 trials), or with intermittent SBTs (31.6%, 12 trials). Overall risk of bias was commonly high due to a probably high risk of selective reporting.

CONCLUSIONS: Diverse modes and strategies have been evaluated to achieve liberation. Future research should focus on adequately powered, high-quality trials of the effect of commonly used and widely available modes and strategies on clinically important outcomes for liberation from mechanical ventilation of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Association of obstetric factors with maternal morbidity and mortality in patients who gave birth preterm.
authors: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Units (MFMU) Network
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth is associated with an increased rate of serious maternal complication compared with those who deliver at term. However, data are limited on risk factors for maternal morbidity and mortality specifically in the setting of preterm birth. Improved understanding of risk factors for morbidity in patients with preterm birth can help optimize interventions to best support patients experiencing preterm birth.

OBJECTIVE: To assess associations between obstetric factors and maternal morbidities and mortality among patients who gave birth less than 35 weeks' gestation.

STUDY DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of a multicenter registry of gravidas carrying singletons or twins who gave birth at 16 0/7 to 34 6/7 weeks' gestation January through August 2019. The primary outcome was a maternal morbidity and mortality composite (blood transfusion, postpartum hemorrhage, maternal sepsis, stroke, thromboembolism, intensive care unit admission, or death) during the delivery hospitalization. Factors were compared between those with and without the composite outcome to identify statistically significant variables. Those factors were then used to create a parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model with adjusted odds ratio (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a backward strategy. We estimated area under the curve to quantify the predictive ability of these factors for the primary outcome.

RESULTS: The analysis was based on 6660 patients, of whom 15.1% experienced the primary composite outcome. Factors associated with increased odds of the outcome included increasing maternal age, use of assisted reproductive technology, twin gestation, preeclampsia, placental abruption and cesarean delivery-aOR ranged from 1.02 [1.01-1.04] for maternal age (continuous) to 2.55 [2.08-3.14] for abruption. In contrast, nulliparity, gestational diabetes, preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM), and later birth gestational age were associated with decreased odds of the primary outcome-aOR ranging from 0.96 [0.95-0.98] for gestational age (continuous) to 0.54 [0.44-0.66] for PPROM. The model with these factors had low to moderate predictive ability (AUC 0.68 [0.66-0.69]).

CONCLUSION: Among individuals who experienced preterm birth before 35 weeks, multiple factors were associated with maternal morbidity and mortality. The factors together modestly discriminate maternal morbidity or mortality.

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended virtual and in-person prenatal care model in integrated healthcare systems.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional US prenatal care typically includes 12-14 standardized in-person visits. COVID-19-related barriers accelerated adoption of blended virtual/in-person prenatal care, but evidence from large, diverse populations is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended prenatal care model versus traditional in-person care in a large health maintenance organization.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study in Kaiser Permanente Northwest and Southern California comparing blended care (cases, July 22, 2022 to December 31, 2024) with traditional in-person care (controls, January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019). Groups were compared using t-tests/Wilcoxon and chi-square tests; multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 47,577 patients (473 cases; 47,104 controls), cases were older at delivery (mean = 32.0 [SD = 4.6] vs. 30.4 [4.9] years, p < 0.0001), more likely to be non-Hispanic White (68.9% vs. 26.5%, p < 0.0001), had higher median household income, and higher rates of publicly funded coverage (15.9% vs. 9.1%, p < 0.0001). Cases had fewer nulliparous women (20.9% vs. 47.5%, p < 0.0001), higher smoking rates (9.5% vs. 2.7%), and less likely to initiate prenatal care in the first trimester (92.6% vs. 96.8%). Cases had fewer in-person visits (mean = 6.2 [2.7] vs. 15.7 [6.2], p < 0.0001), more virtual visits (3.2 [1.4] vs. 1.0 [1.4], p < 0.0001), and fewer total visits (9.4 [3.2] vs. 16.7 [6.5], p < 0.0001). Depression screening was more frequent in cases (84.1% vs. 45.9%, p < 0.0001). Compared to controls, cases had lower odds of preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) (aOR, 0.17; 95% CI, 0.05-0.58), preterm birth <37 weeks (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.22-0.61), and stillbirth (aOR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.03-0.70), but higher odds of non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing (aOR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.06-1.60), gestational diabetes (aOR, 3.75; 95% CI, 2.80-5.01), and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR; aOR, 2.46; 95% CI, 1.42-4.25). No significant differences were observed in placenta previa, chorioamnionitis, cesarean birth, postpartum hemorrhage, macrosomia, placental abruption, preeclampsia/eclampsia, or maternal length of stay more than 2 days.

CONCLUSIONS: Blended virtual/in-person prenatal care was associated with comparable perinatal outcomes despite fewer visits. Lower odds of preterm birth, PPROM, and stillbirth and higher odds of non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracings, gestational diabetes, and IUGR suggest that blended care is feasible for low-risk pregnancies, with attention to strengthening monitoring.

articles.title: Morphological Diversity of Basal Ganglia Enlarged Perivascular Spaces in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: A Report of Two Cases.
articles.abstract: In cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD), apathy, gait impairment, and executive dysfunction may coexist as the apathy, gait impairment, and executive dysfunction (AGED) triad, particularly in association with hypertensive arteriopathy. Major magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) markers of CSVD include lacunes, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and enlarged perivascular spaces (ePVS). The total CSVD score, which integrates these imaging markers, is widely used as a simple measure of the overall imaging burden of CSVD. We compared two older female patients with CSVD who had hypertension as the major vascular risk factor and shared the apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε3/ε3 genotype. Both patients exhibited clinical features consistent with the AGED triad, although their cognitive profiles and functional impairments differed. Case 1 had numerous ePVS in the basal ganglia (BG) and centrum semiovale (CSO), accompanied by WMH, but showed neither lacunes nor hemorrhagic CSVD imaging markers, resulting in a total CSVD score of 2. In contrast, Case 2 exhibited multiple CSVD imaging markers, including numerous BG-ePVS, WMH, lacunes, and CMBs, with a total CSVD score of 4, as well as intracerebral hemorrhage and cortical superficial siderosis. Although BG-ePVS were graded as Potter grade 4 (the highest grade) in both cases, their bilateral counts differed (106 in Case 1 and 83 in Case 2), and differences in morphological characteristics were observed. In Case 1, BG-ePVS exhibited diverse morphologies, including round, oval, linear, curvilinear, and tortuous-appearing configurations, whereas those in Case 2 predominantly appeared round, oval, or linear. Visual assessment of brain perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) suggested predominantly frontal and BG hypoperfusion in Case 1, whereas Case 2 showed a predominantly bilateral temporal hypoperfusion pattern. Gait impairment and functional disability were more pronounced in Case 1 despite a lower total CSVD score and the same Potter grade of BG-ePVS. These descriptive observations suggest that qualitative assessment of BG-ePVS morphology may provide information complementary to conventional semiquantitative grading and counting. Whether these morphological differences are associated with clinical manifestations or frontal-subcortical network dysfunction remains uncertain and requires further investigation.

articles.title: Suspected Clinical Ellis-Yale-Winter Syndrome in an Infant With Unilateral Renal Agenesis, Contralateral Renal Ectopia, Microcephaly, and Congenital Heart Defects: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Ellis-Yale-Winter syndrome (EYWS) is an exceptionally rare multiple congenital anomaly syndrome characterized by microcephaly and congenital heart disease, variably associated with unilateral renal agenesis and abnormal pulmonary lobation. Its phenotype derives from a single original sibship, no validated diagnostic criteria exist, and no causative gene has been established. We report a male infant with congenital microcephaly, right renal agenesis with a contralateral ectopic solitary kidney, congenital heart defects, craniofacial dysmorphic features, and neurological abnormalities. The findings showed phenotypic overlap with the original cases, leading a multidisciplinary team to a suspected clinical diagnosis of EYWS. This diagnosis is not molecularly confirmed, as no genetic testing was performed. Pulmonary lobation and segmentation could not be assessed, which is a major limitation; their presence or absence cannot be inferred. The contralateral renal ectopia may represent a coincidental malformation or a hypothetical phenotypic variant. Long-term outcome and vital status are undetermined. This report does not establish new diagnostic features or an expanded phenotypic spectrum. Dedicated pulmonary imaging, exome or genome sequencing, DNA banking, and longitudinal follow-up are recommended in future cases.

articles.title: Drug Adherence Among Patients With Hypertension and Diabetes Attending Non-Communicable Disease Corners at Sub-District Hospitals of Bangladesh in 2024: A Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and diabetes mellitus are major non-communicable diseases in Bangladesh. Sustained medication adherence is essential for disease control but is influenced by both patient- and health-system factors. This study assessed medication adherence and factors associated with low adherence among patients with hypertension and/or diabetes attending Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) Corners at sub-district hospitals in Bangladesh.

METHODS: The study employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design conducted at four Upazila Health Complexes in Gopalganj district, Bangladesh. Quantitative data were collected through face-to-face interviews with 301 adults receiving treatment for hypertension and/or diabetes for at least 6 months. Medication adherence was assessed using the eight-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale. Factors associated with low adherence were identified using Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Qualitative data from eight in-depth interviews with healthcare providers and two focus group discussions with patients were analysed thematically.

RESULTS: Among 301 participants, 76.4% were female, 57.1% were aged 40-59 years, and 68.8% were housewives. Overall, 57.1% had low adherence, 40.2% had moderate adherence, and 2.7% had high adherence. Low adherence was independently associated with being a housewife, missing doses due to drug unavailability or work pressure, and incomplete or absent medicine dispensing from NCD Corners. The strongest association was observed among patients receiving no drugs from the NCD Corner. Qualitative findings complemented these results by identifying medicine stock-outs, inadequate counselling, travel costs, and misconceptions about lifelong treatment as key barriers to medication adherence.

CONCLUSION: Low medication adherence was common among patients attending NCD Corners. Strengthening medicine availability, prescription fulfilment, adherence counselling, and patient-friendly refill mechanisms may improve medication adherence in primary healthcare NCD services in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Current Approaches to the Treatment of Hepatorenal Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a life-threatening complication of advanced cirrhosis that requires early recognition, treatment of precipitating factors, and coordinated transplant assessment. This narrative review examines pharmacological treatment, fluid management, kidney replacement therapy (KRT), transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), and liver transplantation in adults, with emphasis on HRS with acute kidney injury (AKI). Contemporary diagnostic criteria recognize that hepatorenal physiology can coexist with tubular injury or chronic kidney disease (CKD) and discourage a routine 48-hour albumin challenge. Clinical assessment should integrate perfusion, oxygenation, and congestion, with ultrasound used as an adjunct when available. Terlipressin with individualized albumin improves renal reversal in suitable patients, but a consistent overall survival benefit has not been established, and respiratory failure remains a major safety concern. Norepinephrine is an important alternative where appropriate monitoring is available; midodrine with octreotide has a limited fallback role. Albumin dosing should reflect serial volume assessment rather than a serum albumin target. Kidney replacement therapy supports patients with metabolic or volume complications, while evidence for routine shunt placement in acute HRS remains insufficient. Liver transplantation addresses the underlying disease, although kidney recovery is variable. Biomarkers may assist clinical phenotyping, but their use to guide treatment requires prospective validation. The review emphasizes timely diagnosis, individualized treatment, and distinguishing renal recovery from survival.

articles.title: Post-ERCP Pancreatitis Complicated by Abdominal Compartment Syndrome in the Setting of Lemmel Syndrome: A Fatal Case Report.
articles.abstract: Abdominal compartment syndrome should be suspected early in severe post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography pancreatitis with abdominal distension, oliguria, respiratory deterioration, and shock. Routine intra-abdominal pressure monitoring and timely decompressive surgery are critical, as delayed recognition may rapidly progress to multiorgan failure, septic shock, and death, especially in Lemmel syndrome cases.

articles.title: DNAH5-Associated Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia With Natural Paternity and Advanced Bronchiectasis.
articles.abstract: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited disorder of motile cilia that may remain unrecognised until adulthood. We report a 43-year-old lifelong non-smoker with recurrent respiratory infections since childhood, chronic rhinosinusitis, situs inversus totalis, advanced bilateral bronchiectasis, severe non-reversible airflow obstruction, and chronic hypoxemic respiratory failure. His course was complicated by chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway infection and frequent exacerbations. Despite a characteristic Kartagener phenotype, he had fathered six biological children conceived without assisted reproductive techniques. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous pathogenic frameshift variant in DNAH5 (NM_001369.3:c.5563dup; p.(Ile1855Asnfs*6)), establishing the molecular diagnosis. This case highlights the reproductive phenotypic variability of DNAH5-associated PCD and emphasises that natural paternity does not exclude PCD or justify delaying molecular genetic evaluation.

articles.title: Immunogenicity of Hantavirus and evaluation of vaccine protective efficacy: A comparative neutralizing antibody study of vaccine strains and representative epidemic strains from selected provinces in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantavirus (HV) remains a significant public health burden in the world. HFRS bivalent inactivated vaccine (HFRSbiv) with Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) strains isolated 20 years ago have been used in key HFRS endemic provinces in China for HFRS prevention. After decades of effective implementation of comprehensive prevention and control measures, HFRS has entered a stage of epidemic fluctuation at low-level in China. However, the continuous transmission of the virus among rodent host animals may lead to dynamic changes in genetic diversity and immunogenicity of the virus, which may affect the pathogenic mechanism of the virus and the protective effect of vaccines. It is necessary to carry out timely monitoring and evaluation of the immunogenicity of HV.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A panel of sera was established by screening serum samples from HFRS patients at convalescent phase and individuals who had received standardized immunization with HFRSbiv. Neutralizing antibody titers against HTNV vaccine strain 84FLi, SEOV vaccine strain L99, and three representative epidemic strains from different genotypes (HTNV: SX26, SEOV: LN03 and FJ-17) were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay-based microneutralization test (MN-ELISA). HV-neutralizing antibodies were detected from all the selected serum samples. Among HFRS patients, 47.92% (23/48) were identified as HTNV infection, 27.08% (13/48) were with SEOV infection, and 25% (12/48) were untypable. There is a significant difference in the titers of neutralizing antibodies against vaccine strains and epidemic strains detected in the serum samples. For HTNV, both patient and vaccinee sera exhibited significantly higher geometric mean titer (GMT) against vaccine strain 84FLi than against epidemic strain SX26 (1:386.08 vs. 1:223.04, 𝑃 < 0.001; 1:137.94 vs. 1:110.37, 𝑃 < 0.05, respectively). For SEOV, patient sera showed significantly lower GMT against vaccine strain L99 than against epidemic strain LN03 (1:177.02 vs. 1:297.71, 𝑃 < 0.01), and vaccinee sera showed significantly lower GMT against L99 than against epidemic strain FJ-17 (1:97.52 vs. 1:243.71, 𝑃 < 0.001). Significant immunogenicity heterogeneity was observed between SEOV epidemic strains LN03 and FJ-17.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: The genetic diversity and immunogenicity of HV, which causes HFRS, have certain geographical regional characteristics. The levels of cross neutralizing antibodies induced by infection of HV from different genotypes may vary significantly, but still provide sufficient cross protection. The HFRSbiv currently used in China could induce broad neutralizing antibody, the cross-protective efficacy might vary against different circulating strains and genotypes. It is of great significance to strengthen the monitoring of genetic characteristics of regional specific circulating viral strains, regularly evaluate the matching degree between vaccine protection effectiveness and epidemic strains, predict and evaluate the transmission and pathogenic risks of HV, and timely optimize HFRS prevention and control strategies and measures.

articles.title: Development and validation of an explainable artificial intelligence model to predict in-hospital adverse events for patients with acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: In-hospital adverse events after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) can occur abruptly and adversely affect short-term prognosis. We developed and externally validated explainable machine learning models to predict a composite of in-hospital atrial fibrillation (AF), ventricular fibrillation (VF), cardiac arrest (CA), or death using routinely available admission data. We retrospectively analyzed 7,496 patients from the MIMIC-IV database as the development cohort and 2,776 patients from Xuanwu Hospital as the external validation cohort. Predictors included demographics, medical history, and admission laboratory tests. Logistic regression, random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), multilayer perceptron, and TabNet models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using discrimination, classification, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Latent class analysis identified three outcome clusters with distinct event-probability profiles. XGBoost achieved the best performance for the composite outcome in the development cohort (AUROC, 0.798). Predictive performance was moderate to good for AF and in-hospital death, with AUROCs of up to 0.834 and 0.870 in the development cohort and 0.803 and 0.849 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Discrimination was lower for VF and CA. SHapley Additive exPlanations highlighted neutrophil and leukocyte counts, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, renal function, glucose, glycated hemoglobin A1c, and prior AF as important predictors. These explainable models may support early risk stratification and help guide monitoring intensity and timely intervention in patients with AMI.

articles.title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension in adult congenital heart disease: prevalence, outcomes and treatment patterns.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive, life-threatening complication of congenital heart disease (CHD). We aimed to determine the burden of clinically relevant PAH in a well-characterised adult CHD population.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 35 235 adult CHD patients from the Australian National CHD Registry, of whom 392 had clinically significant PAH (mean±sd age 43.4±13.9) (prevalence 1.11%). We prospectively defined clinically significant PAH as 1) prescription of PAH-specific therapy and/or 2) known Eisenmenger syndrome. 330 patients (84.2%) received PAH pharmacotherapy during the study period and 193 patients (49.2%) had Eisenmenger syndrome, 62 (32.1%) of whom were untreated.

RESULTS: During the study period, 141 (36.0%) patients died, PAH treatment was associated with a numerically lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio (HR) 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.11; p=0.22). Patients with moderate complexity CHD had a significantly higher risk of death than the mild group (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.08-2.92; p=0.023), whilst severe complexity patients had >2.5 times the risk of death (p<0.001). At last follow-up, 211 (63.9%) of treated patients were prescribed monotherapy, 90 (27.3%) dual and 29 (8.8%) triple therapy. From initial treatment to last follow-up, 123 (37.3%) of the treated group had switched therapy, 100 (30.3%) died, 75 (22.7%) continued their initial pharmacotherapy, 25 (7.6%) added additional drugs and seven (2.1%) underwent transplantation.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1.11% of a large adult CHD population had clinically significant PAH. Mortality is high (6.9% at age 30 years, 35.7% at age 50 years) and treatment has shifted towards increased utilisation of combination therapy.

articles.title: Suboptimal peak inspiratory flow, COPD exacerbations, hospitalisations and disease burden: a longitudinal follow-up in a multicentre real-world study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peak inspiratory flow (PIF) is a critical determinant of dry powder inhaler (DPI) effectiveness in managing patients with COPD. Suboptimal PIF may compromise drug delivery and clinical outcomes. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the association between repeated PIF measures and disease exacerbations, hospitalisations, and symptom burden in patients with stable COPD.

METHODS: In this multi-country, observational cohort, 415 participants aged ≥40 years with confirmed COPD and a smoking history underwent PIF measurements at their prescribed inhaler's resistance, and low- and high-resistance levels using the In-Check DIAL G16. Clinical assessments occurred at 3 months (follow-up 1 (FU1)) and 6 months (follow-up 2 (FU2)) including spirometry, COPD Assessment Test scores, medication use and exacerbation/hospitalisation rates.

RESULTS: At FU1, 29.4% (n=113/384) had typical suboptimal PIF and 28.6% (n=108/377) remained suboptimal at FU2. Participants with suboptimal PIF were more often female and current smokers, with consistently poorer lung function across both visits. Lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (33.7±9.1% pred versus 45.7±9.2% pred, p=0.01), actual forced vital capacity and inspiratory capacity were observed. Suboptimal PIF significantly predicted moderate (p=0.03) and severe (p=0.01) exacerbations, was associated with higher hospitalisation risks (p=0.05) and with greater use of short-acting beta agonist, oral corticosteroid and triple therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Suboptimal PIF is a stable, clinically meaningful marker of worse COPD outcomes and may guide more personalised inhaler selection.

articles.title: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E status prior to COPD- or cardiovascular-related death: a nationwide study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: COPD is the third leading cause of death worldwide. However, little is known about the characteristics of patients who die from COPD. The aim of this study was to determine the relationship between change or persistence in Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E (GOLD-E) status over time and COPD- and cardiovascular (CV)-related death.

METHODS: Patients with COPD were identified by International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the French national health insurance database. Patients who died from COPD or CV diseases between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2022 were matched with living COPD patients. We performed a case-control analysis to compare the impact of the change in GOLD-E status between two periods: 13-24 months (period 2 (2026)) and 0-12 months (period 1 (2025)) prior to death or the index date.

RESULTS: A total of 500 673 COPD patients died during the study period. Of these, 67 250 died from COPD and 41 585 from CV events. Of the patients whose deaths were COPD related, the proportion of patients with GOLD-E 2026 status increased between the two periods (58.3% versus 79.2%), but decreased in their matched living controls (58.3% versus 36.9%). Of the patients with GOLD-E 2026 status during period 2, becoming and remaining GOLD-E 2026 within their final 12 months was associated with COPD-related death (odds ratios 5.40 (95% CI 5.03-5.79) and 4.16 (95% CI 3.87-4.48), respectively; p<0.0001).

INTERPRETATION: These data demonstrate that being GOLD-E for 2 years in a row is associated with a high risk of COPD-related death, of the same magnitude as being GOLD-E for 1 year.

articles.title: Acute small-bowel obstruction caused by coiling of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt catheter: a case report.
articles.abstract: Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunting is widely used for the treatment of hydrocephalus, but abdominal complications can occasionally cause significant morbidity. We report a rare case of acute small-bowel obstruction caused by coiling of a distal VP shunt catheter around the ileum. A 65-year-old man with diabetes mellitus and hypertension presented with a 2-day history of abdominal pain, vomiting, progressive abdominal distension, and hiccups, three weeks after VP shunt placement for hydrocephalus. Abdominal radiography demonstrated features of mechanical small-bowel obstruction with an abnormal configuration of the distal shunt catheter. Emergency exploratory laparotomy revealed marked proximal small-bowel dilatation and the distal catheter coiled around the mid-ileum, producing a mechanical transition point. The bowel remained viable without ischaemia, necrosis, or perforation. The catheter was released and shortened, and no bowel resection was required. Early recognition of shunt-related intestinal obstruction and prompt surgical intervention may prevent irreversible bowel injury.

articles.title: Fulminant myocarditis mimicking catastrophic surgical failure after mitral valve repair.
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of a 43-year-old woman who developed severe acute left ventricular dysfunction after minimally invasive endoscopic mitral and tricuspid valve repair. Coronary angiography excluded an ischemic complication, while endomyocardial biopsy showed interstitial edema and sparse inflammatory infiltrates without definitive evidence of active myocarditis. Systemic glucocorticoid therapy was initiated after the biopsy result. Temporary mechanical circulatory support with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella CP enabled myocardial recovery and a favorable clinical outcome.

articles.title: Updated Scientific Opinion on the risks for animal and human health related to the presence of phomopsins in feed and food.
authors: EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM)
articles.journal: EFSA journal. European Food Safety Authority
articles.abstract: The EFSA CONTAM Panel assessed the risks for animal and human health related to the presence of phomopsins in feed and food. Lupins are considered the main source of phomopsins. Since the previous CONTAM Panel 2012 Opinion on phomopsins, new studies investigated the structural diversity of phomopsins. Improvements in the analytical methods, particularly by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) lowered the limits of quantification. Despite the availability of 5437 analytical occurrence results on food and 104 analytical results on feed for phomopsin A, only few quantified data were available for food and feed. The lack of occurrence data for the relevant food category, i.e. lupins, hindered human dietary exposure assessment and risk characterisation. For animals, the data available on sweet lupins, i.e. the main contributor of phomopsin in feed, was sufficient to assess animal dietary exposure. Mean lower bound-upper bound (LB-UB) dietary exposure ranged from 0.51 ng/kg bw per day for horses to 90.2 ng/kg bw per day for chickens for fattening. In sheep, phomopsins affected survival, liver, kidney and the appetite of animals. A no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) of 2.2 μg phomopsins/kg bw per day was established for sheep, based on decreased appetite and moderate liver disease. This corresponds to a NOAEL concentration in feed of 98 μg phomopsins/kg complete feed for lambs for fattening (i.e. 112 μg phomopsins/kg feed DM) and 64 μg phomopsins/kg complete feed for dairy sheep (i.e. 73 μg phomopsins/kg feed DM). The P95 exposure to phomopsins, as a % of the NOAEL concentration in feed, ranged between 0.51% and 2.04% for lambs for fattening and was 2.91% for dairy sheep. Regarding animals, the CONTAM Panel concludes that current dietary exposure to phomopsin A does not raise a concern for sheep health. No conclusion can be made for other animal species due to insufficient hazard data.

articles.title: A Cross-Sectional Study of the Association Between Spiritual Well-Being and Self-Efficacy Among Adolescents Aged 11-15 Years in Southeastern Iran.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Spiritual health is a fundamental concept that may influence how individuals deal with problems and tensions arising from different life situations. Higher levels of spiritual well-being have been associated with greater adaptability to difficulties. Spiritual well-being in adolescents is of particular importance because it may be related to learning, educational decisions, and overall well-being.

METHODS: This cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among adolescents aged 11-15 years in southeastern Iran. A sample of 150 adolescents was selected using convenience sampling. The Spiritual Well-Being Questionnaire and the Self-Efficacy Scale were used to collect data. Descriptive statistics, independent t-test, analysis of variance, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and Spearman correlation coefficient tests were used for data analysis. Stepwise multiple regression analysis was conducted to identify factors associated with self-efficacy scores. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: The mean spiritual well-being score of the adolescents was 163.81 ± 21.94, which was higher than the questionnaire's median score of 120. The mean self-efficacy score was 91.33 ± 11.73, with 90.7% (n = 136) of the adolescents demonstrating good. A direct, moderate, and significant association was observed between spiritual well-being and self-efficacy (r = 0.472, p < 0.001). The spiritual well-being score was significantly lower among 15-year-old adolescents than among 12-year-old adolescents. Stepwise multiple regression analysis showed that spiritual well-being accounted for 23.2% of the variance in self-efficacy.

CONCLUSION: Higher spiritual well-being was significantly associated with higher self-efficacy among adolescents. This finding suggests that spiritual well-being may be a relevant factor to consider in broader adolescent health and educational programs. Longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to determine whether changes in spiritual well-being are temporally associated with changes in self-efficacy.

articles.title: Nomophobia Among Adolescents in Kyrgyzstan: Scores, Dimensions, and Associations With Smartphone-Use Patterns.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: This study examines overall and dimension-specific nomophobia scores among adolescents in Kyrgyzstan and analyzes their associations with demographic characteristics and smartphone-use patterns.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, descriptive, and correlational study was conducted in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, between June 2 and June 25, 2026. Data were collected from 400 adolescents aged 13-17 years using a culturally adapted Russian-language 5-point version of the Nomophobia Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation, and hierarchical multiple regression.

RESULTS: The overall item-level nomophobia score was 2.62 (SD = 0.81). Among the four dimensions, Not Being Able to Communicate had the highest mean score, whereas Losing Connectedness had the lowest. Female adolescents reported significantly higher observed nomophobia scores than males; however, measurement invariance across gender was not examined, and this comparison should therefore be interpreted cautiously. No significant differences were found according to age, grade level, or parental attitudes toward internet and social media use. Significant omnibus ANOVA results were observed for both years of smartphone use and daily smartphone-use duration. However, none of the Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons for years of smartphone use reached statistical significance; therefore, no differences between specific smartphone-ownership-duration groups were identified. Tukey-adjusted post hoc comparisons for daily smartphone use showed that adolescents using smartphones for 4-6 h and 7 h or more per day had higher nomophobia scores than those using them for 1-3 h per day. The final regression model was statistically significant and explained 19.3% of the variance; in this model, the 1-3-h category was associated with lower nomophobia scores than the 4-6-h reference category.

CONCLUSION: Nomophobia among adolescents in Kyrgyzstan was primarily associated with communication-related concerns, gender, and current daily smartphone-use patterns. Female gender and more intensive daily smartphone use showed stronger associations with nomophobia than age, grade level, parental attitudes, or duration of smartphone ownership. Given the cross-sectional design, convenience sampling, self-report data, and limited explained variance, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal or clinical evidence.

articles.title: Prescription Patterns and Adherence to GOLD 2021 Guidelines for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Management in Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Global Initiative for chronic obstructive lung disease (GOLD) offers evidence-based recommendations for the management of COPD, but compliance with the guidelines amongst physicians in LMC countries is varied. The objective of this study was to determine the prescribing pattern of inhaled COPD medications in Pakistan and to evaluate the adherence of pulmonologists with the GOLD 2021 guidelines and to assess all the factors that would affect the adherence.

METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study was undertaken at secondary health care facilities Rawalpindi and Islamabad between the period of April-September, 2022. Spirometry, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) and Modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scores were used to classify outpatients ≥ 40 years old who had COPD confirmed by spirometry into GOLD 2021 ABCD groups. Pharmacological regimens recommended by GOLD were compared with prescribed regimens. Adherence was rated as appropriate, overtreatment or undertreatment. Demographic and clinical variables were correlated with adherence using chi-square and t-test.

RESULTS: Among 400 patients (mean age 61.8 ± 10.0 years; 74.8% male), Group B was most frequent (40.3%), followed by C (24.0%), A (23.8%), and D (12.0%). Overall, 57.0% (228/400; 95% CI: 52.1-61.9%) received guideline-concordant therapy, while 43.0% (172/400; 95% CI: 38.1-47.9%) were inappropriately managed. The 80 patients were considered to be overtreated and 92 patients were considered to be undertreated among the inappropriate prescriptions. Cardiovascular comorbidity was associated with treatment inappropriateness (OR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.05-2.34; p = 0.026), and male sex was also significantly associated with inappropriate prescribing (OR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.44-3.85; p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: More than two-fifths of patients received pharmacological treatment that was not concordant with GOLD 2021 recommendations. Both overtreatment and undertreatment were observed. Strengthening spirometry-based assessment, clinician education, and access to appropriate inhaled therapies may improve guideline-concordant COPD management in Pakistan.

articles.title: Impact of Preoperative Hospital Stay on Postoperative Complications in Elective Neurosurgical Procedures: A Retrospective Observational Study in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Nepal.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Preoperative stay varies with patient and institutional factors. In Neurosurgery, at least 1 day of admission before any procedure is usually the norm. This study evaluates the correlation between preoperative length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications, classified by the Clavien-Dindo classification, among patients undergoing elective neurosurgical procedures at a university hospital in Nepal.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed records of 110 patients who underwent elective neurosurgery from June 2022 to June 2023. Data included demographics, comorbidities, preoperative LOS, total LOS, diagnosis, treatment, postoperative complications, and 3-month outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 110 patients, 54.5% (60/110) were male, with a median age of 35 years. Most (78.2%) had no comorbidities; hypertension was the most common (10.9%). The median total hospital stay was 13 days, with a median preoperative stay of 5.5 days. Postoperatively, 80.0% of patients required at least 1 day in the intensive care unit. The incidence of postoperative complications was 33.6% (37/110). Complications occurred in 33.6% of patients. Preoperative LOS was significantly associated with postoperative complications (p = 0.045) but not with Clavien-Dindo grade (p = 0.063). Total LOS was strongly associated with both postoperative complications (p < 0.001) and complication severity by Clavien-Dindo classification (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Longer preoperative and total hospital stays were associated with increased postoperative complications, while total LOS was also linked with complication severity. These findings emphasize the influence of preoperative hospitalization on surgical outcomes. Optimizing preoperative management and minimizing unnecessary delays may reduce morbidity following neurosurgical procedures.

articles.title: Assessment of the application for modification of the terms of authorisation of the feed additive consisting of lanthanum carbonate octahydrate (4d23) for cats and dogs (Porus GmbH).
authors: EFSA Panel on Additives and Products or Substances used in Animal Feed (FEEDAP)
articles.journal: EFSA journal. European Food Safety Authority
articles.abstract: Following a request from the European Commission, EFSA was asked to deliver a scientific opinion on the modification of the terms of authorisation of the feed additive consisting of lanthanum carbonate octahydrate for cats and dogs. The additive is currently authorised as a zootechnical additive for use in feed for adult cats and dogs with minimum and maximum use levels of 1500 and 7500 mg/kg complete feed, respectively. The applicant requested that the authorisation be modified to allow the additive to be mixed directly into feed by pet holders immediately before consumption. The FEEDAP Panel considered that the proposed mode of administration does not affect its previous conclusions on the safety of the additive for adult cats and dogs and for users, provided that the maximum authorised level is not exceeded. The Panel also concluded that the additive has the potential to be efficacious as a phosphate binder when administered according to the proposed mode of use, provided that the minimum efficacious level is achieved, and the additive is adequately mixed with the feed.

articles.title: Cardiovascular effects and mortality of short-acting bronchodilators in asthma and COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior research has focused on short-acting β2-agonist (SABA) overuse-related adverse outcomes in asthma patients. Evidence on the association between use of short-acting bronchodilators in general and cardiovascular events in asthma/COPD populations remains limited.

METHODS: Adult patients with chronic treatment of asthma or COPD were identified in a Belgian nationwide cohort between 2017 and 2022. A Cox model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, socioeconomic status, exacerbation history, comorbidities and medication use, was used to investigate the association between SABA, short-acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA) and SABA+SAMA use with cardiovascular risk and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: The cohort included 226 314 asthma patients (mean age 57.8 years, 60.5% females) and 57 446 COPD patients (mean age 72.2 years, 38.0% females). Compared with no use, SAMA and SABA+SAMA use (1-2 and ≥3 canisters per baseline year) was associated with increased heart failure (1.2-1.4-fold), arrhythmia (1.1-1.4-fold) and mortality risk (1.1-1.7-fold) in asthma and COPD patients. Among asthma patients, use of 1-2, and ≥3 SABA+SAMA canisters per year were additionally associated with increased myocardial infarction (1.2-1.4-fold) and ischaemic stroke risk (1.2-1.3-fold), and ≥3 SABA+SAMA canisters per year with a 1.4-fold myocardial infarction risk in COPD patients. Compared with no SABA users, ≥3 SABA canisters per year was associated with a 1.1-fold increased heart failure and mortality risk in asthma and COPD patients, while no increased risks were observed for 1-2 SABA canisters.

CONCLUSION: Increased use of SAMA or SABA+SAMA was associated with increased risks of cardiovascular events and mortality in patients with asthma and COPD. Collecting three or more SABA canisters per year was associated with increased mortality.

articles.title: Light-chain amyloidosis causing left ventricular outflow tract obstruction managed with a dual-chamber pacemaker: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amyloid light-chain (AL) cardiac amyloidosis can rarely mimic hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy with systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve and resultant left ventricular (LV) outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO). Dual-chamber pacing with a right ventricular (RV) apical lead may be another option for LVOT gradient reduction and symptomatic relief for these patients.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old man presented with subacute bilateral lower extremity oedema and syncope. Examination revealed a systolic murmur increasing with Valsalva, bibasilar crackles, and pitting oedema. Electrocardiogram showed low QRS voltage disproportionate to the degree of LV wall thickening. Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated severe concentric LV hypertrophy with SAM of the mitral valve and LVOTO (65 mmHg at rest, 100 mmHg with Valsalva). Laboratory tests and renal biopsy confirmed lambda AL amyloidosis, and endomyocardial biopsy confirmed cardiac amyloid infiltration. Medical therapy included cautious beta-blockade and midodrine, but the patient experienced refractory syncope. Septal reduction therapy was not anatomically feasible. Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation with RV apical pacing resulted in an improvement in the LVOT gradient and orthostatic symptoms. At more than 1 year after initiation of dual-chamber pacing and therapy directed at his underlying plasma cell dyscrasia, the patient had no further hospitalizations and endorsed sustained symptomatic improvement.

DISCUSSION: Management of LVOTO in patients with AL cardiac amyloidosis is challenging due to competing restrictive physiology and the absence of guideline-recommended practices. Dual-chamber pacing may reduce LVOT gradients and improve symptoms in cases refractory to medical management.

articles.title: Discordant associations between type 2 biomarkers and severity of asthma and COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergic and type 2 (T2) inflammatory biomarkers are increasingly used to predict outcomes and guide treatment in asthma and COPD. The objective of this cross-sectional study was to determine the prevalence of allergic sensitisation and T2 biomarkers and their clinical associations among patients with diagnoses of asthma and/or COPD in NOVELTY, a large multinational, observational study.

METHODS: Participants were enrolled from primary/specialist care, stratified by physician-assigned diagnosis and severity. We assessed fractional exhaled nitric oxide (≥25 ppb), blood eosinophils (≥300 cells·µL-1) and allergen-specific IgE sensitisation (≥0.35 kU·L-1 to any of 11 aeroallergens). Associations between biomarkers and clinical outcomes were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index and smoking status.

RESULTS: Data for all biomarkers were available for 4352 participants (asthma: n=2194; asthma+COPD: n=633; COPD: n=1525). Overall, 63% participants had at least one positive biomarker (asthma: 77%; asthma+COPD: 60%; COPD: 45%); only 8%, 4% and 1% of participants, respectively, were positive for all three biomarkers. Women and current smokers were more likely to be triple-negative. Among participants with asthma, having more positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease, lower lung function and exacerbations. By contrast, in COPD, having no positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease and lower lung function.

CONCLUSIONS: Allergic and T2 biomarkers are highly prevalent in asthma and asthma+COPD but less frequent in COPD. Their patterns show distinct associations, sometimes with opposite trends, across diagnostic groups, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms that differ.

articles.title: Spatial Patterns of Chronic Diseases in an Urban Setting and Their Association With Household Characteristics: A Cross‑Sectional Study From Iran.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic diseases represent a major contributor to disease burden and mortality in Iran. Understanding their local spatial patterns may help inform future health planning. Despite their rising prevalence, region-based analyses at the urban level remain underexplored. This study aimed to investigate the spatial distribution patterns of four major groups of chronic diseases in the metropolitan area of Tabriz and their associations with household economic characteristics and structure.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 on 602 households residing in the nine municipal districts of Tabriz. Sampling employed a multi-stage stratified cluster method, proportional to district populations. Data were collected via a household information form covering age, sex, education, and disease types, administered through telephone interviews. Analyses were performed using SPSS software. To visualize the spatial distribution of chronic diseases, disease prevalence was calculated as the ratio of reported cases to the total number of respondents in each district, and spatial maps were produced using Geographic Information System (GIS) software.

RESULTS: Approximately 36% of households reported at least one member with a chronic disease. Cardiovascular diseases (18.7%) and type 2 diabetes (16.9%) exhibited the highest prevalence. District 8 showed the highest density of three major chronic disease types, whereas District 10 had the highest prevalence of gastrointestinal disorders. Household income in the 10-15 million Iranian Rials range and household sizes of 2-3 members were significantly associated with reduced odds of chronic diseases (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of chronic diseases varied across different areas of Tabriz, while household income and household size were associated with the likelihood of reporting chronic disease. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating spatial and household-level characteristics into healthcare planning and resource allocation. However, given the cross-sectional design of the study, the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal relationships.

articles.title: Diagnostic Utility of Fasting Blood Glucose and Glycated Hemoglobin Compared to Oral Glucose Tolerance Test for Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fasting blood glucose (FBG), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) may classify individuals differently when used to assess diabetes mellitus. This exploratory study compared diabetes classification by these methods and evaluated the agreement and diagnostic performance of HbA1c and FBG relative to the study's 2-h post-glucose-load criterion among adults at increased risk of diabetes attending the University of Cape Coast Hospital, Ghana.

METHOD: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 50 adults with one or more diabetes mellitus risk factors attending the University of Cape Coast Hospital, Ghana. Participants underwent FBG, HbA1c, and a 75-g OGTT on the same day. Diabetes mellitus was defined as FBG ≥ 7.0 mmol/L, 2-h post-glucose-load glucose ≥ 11.1 mmol/L, or HbA1c ≥ 6.5%, according to international diagnostic criteria. Diagnostic agreement between HbA1c and the 2-h post-glucose-load classification was assessed using Cohen's kappa statistic, while sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) of HbA1c and FBG were calculated using the 2-h post-glucose-load classification as the reference standard.

RESULTS: Among 50 participants, seven (14.0%) met the study's 2-h post-glucose-load criterion for diabetes mellitus, two (4.0%) met the HbA1c criterion, and none met the FBG criterion. Agreement between HbA1c and the post-load classification was 86.0% (Cohen's κ = 0.17). Relative to the post-load criterion, HbA1c sensitivity was 14.3% (95% CI: 0.4%-57.9%) and specificity was 97.7% (95% CI: 87.7%-99.9%). FBG sensitivity was 0.0% (95% CI: 0.0%-41.0%), and specificity was 100.0% (95% CI: 91.8%-100.0%).

CONCLUSION: The 2-h post-glucose-load criterion identified more participants with diabetes-range results than HbA1c or FBG in this sample. Although HbA1c demonstrated excellent specificity, its low sensitivity suggests that it may miss a considerable proportion of diabetes cases when used as a standalone diagnostic test. These findings support the continued use of OGTT as the reference method for diagnosing diabetes mellitus in high-risk individuals, particularly where early detection is critical. However, larger, well-powered multicentre studies are needed to validate these results.

articles.title: Successful Thromboembolectomy for PTE in an Adolescent Patient With Catastrophic APS and SLE.
articles.abstract: In a 14-year-old with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and lupus anticoagulant, improper switching from warfarin and low-dose aspirin to rivaroxaban led to life-threatening recurrent thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and pulmonary hypertension. Prompt return to standard anticoagulation plus immunosuppression stabilized the condition. This case underscores that DOACs are contraindicated in high-risk APS.

articles.title: Sex and Etiology Differences in Overall Survival and Adverse Liver Events in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An International Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Sex-associated differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prognosis remain incompletely characterized across major etiologies. In this retrospective international multicenter cohort study, we included 7623 consecutive patients with newly diagnosed HCC from 41 centers in five countries and evaluated the associations of sex and four-level etiology with overall survival (OS) and the first adverse liver event (hepatic decompensation, liver failure, or liver-related death). Sex-related OS was evaluated in the full cohort, after 1:1 propensity-score matching (1351 men and 1351 women), and in a multivariable Cox model including recorded initial treatment modality; cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray models evaluated adverse liver events. Five-year OS was 24.3% in women and 22.0% in men. Female sex was associated with lower mortality before matching (hazard ratio [HR], 0.90; 95% CI, 0.85-0.97), after matching (HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99; p = 0.024), and after multivariable adjustment (HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.85-0.98; p = 0.010). Male sex was associated with a higher hazard of adverse liver events (cause-specific HR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.43; subdistribution HR [sHR], 1.23; 95% CI, 1.08-1.40). Alcohol-related and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-related HCC had higher liver-event hazards than hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related HCC. For OS, the global sex-by-etiology interaction was not significant (p = 0.866). Female sex was associated with modestly better outcomes, although the China-dominant cohort limits generalizability.

articles.title: Calpain-1 Deficiency Attenuates Atherosclerosis and Improves Cardiac Function Through Vascular-Cardiac Coupling Mechanisms in ApoE-Deficient Mice.
articles.abstract: Calpain-1 has emerged as an important regulator of vascular remodeling and inflammation; however, its systemic role in atherosclerosis and cardiac dysfunction remains incompletely understood. This study investigated whether genetic deletion of calpain-1 attenuates atherosclerosis and improves cardiac function in apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE KO) mice. ApoE KO mice and ApoE/calpain-1 double knockout (A × C DKO) mice were fed a high-fat diet for 8 weeks, while C57BL/6 mice served as controls. Atherosclerotic lesions, serum lipid profiles, endothelial function, cardiac structure and function, and global proteomic changes were evaluated. A × C DKO mice exhibited significantly reduced atherosclerotic plaque burden and decreased CD68-positive macrophage infiltration compared with ApoE KO mice. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed that ApoE KO mice developed ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction characterized by increased LVESV and LVEDV and reduced LVEF. Calpain-1 deficiency partially normalized ventricular volumes and significantly improved LVEF, LVSV, and cardiac output. Notably, serum total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL-cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol, and glucose levels were not significantly altered by calpain-1 deletion, indicating that the protective effects occurred independently of systemic lipid metabolism. Mechanistically, calpain-1 deficiency suppressed foam-cell related pathways by downregulating SR-A and CD36 while restoring cholesterol efflux regulators PPAR-γ and LXR-α. Endothelial function was improved as evidenced by increased eNOS activity and NO bioavailability. Aortic DIA proteomic analysis further revealed that calpain-1 ablation reversed multiple pathogenic pathways including cytoskeletal remodeling, extracellular matrix destabilization, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and endothelial barrier impairment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that calpain-1 deficiency attenuates atherosclerotic plaque development and improves cardiac function in ApoE-deficient mice through lipid-independent mechanisms involving endothelial protection, reduced foam cell formation, and restoration of vascular homeostasis. Calpain-1 therefore represents a promising therapeutic target linking vascular pathology with cardiac dysfunction in atherosclerosis.

articles.title: Leadless Pacemaker Implantation in Fabry Disease With Permanent Atrial Fibrillation and Bradycardia: Diagnostic and Implantation Guidance by Preprocedural Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
articles.abstract: In advanced Fabry cardiomyopathy, preprocedural cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may reveal a lower septal region spared from otherwise extensive septal late gadolinium enhancement. This information, combined with pre-fixation electrical mapping, may help identify an optimal site for leadless pacemaker implantation and minimize repeated fixation attempts.

articles.title: Digital Phenotyping, Remote Monitoring, and Risk Prediction of Heart Failure in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review With Narrative Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), particularly preeclampsia, are associated with acute cardiovascular morbidity and future heart failure (HF). Current surveillance relies largely on blood pressure, symptoms, laboratory abnormalities, and clinician-triggered evaluation. Digital phenotyping, remote monitoring, electronic health record-based prediction, and machine learning may enable earlier cardiovascular risk identification.

OBJECTIVES: To systematically identify and narratively synthesize studies evaluating remote monitoring, digital health, machine learning, or risk-prediction approaches for HF-related phenotypes or cardiovascular morbidity in HDPs.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published from January 2020 through April 10, 2025. Studies evaluating prediction or monitoring approaches in HDPs underwent sequential assessment for HF-related or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes. Screening and full-text reviews were performed by 2 independent reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Given substantial heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Of 3366 records imported for screening, 6 studies met the inclusion criteria. Studies used clinical prediction models, electronic health record (EHR)-based models, and remote monitoring to evaluate acute cardiovascular morbidity, HFpEF, cardiac remodeling, and cardiovascular readmission. Model discrimination ranged from modest to strong (AUROC approximately 0.70-0.94). Recurrent predictors included severe hypertensive disease, earlier gestational age at delivery, kidney disease, pre-existing cardiac disease, pulmonary hypertension, maternal age, obesity-related measures, blood pressure, and postpartum volume retention. Most prediction models lacked external validation.

CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary evidence suggests that clinical, EHR-derived, and remotely monitored data may support risk stratification for selected cardiovascular morbidity and HF-related phenotypes after HDPs. Prospective validation, physiological marker integration, and evaluation of risk-guided interventions are needed.

articles.title: Elevated Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Predicts Early Aggravation of Organ Dysfunction in Septic Patients in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), a simple marker of immune dysregulation, is associated with early organ dysfunction progression in emergency department (ED) patients with sepsis.

DESIGN: Exploratory secondary analysis of observational clustering cohort.

SETTING: Single-center ED.

PATIENTS/SUBJECTS: Among 999 patients with adjudicated infection, 364 fulfilled Sepsis-3 criteria for sepsis or septic shock and had available Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores at admission and 24 hours.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Organ dysfunction trajectory was defined according to the evolution in SOFA score during the first 24 hours (ΔSOFA) and categorized as improving (ΔSOFA ≤ -2), stable (ΔSOFA -1 to +1), or worsening (ΔSOFA ≥ +2). Of the 364 patients, 135 (37%) were classified as improving, 187 (51%) as stable, and 42 (12%) as worsening. NLR differed significantly across trajectory groups, with median values of 12 (7-21), 12 (7-22), and 23 (10-37), respectively (p = 0.015). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, lactate concentration, and baseline SOFA score, NLR remained independently associated with worsening organ dysfunction trajectory (odds ratio [OR] 5.55, 95% CI, 1.86-18.18; p = 0.003). Patients with worsening trajectories more frequently required ICU admission (26% vs. 5% vs. 4%; p < 0.001) and experienced higher 28-day mortality (36% vs 17% vs 17%; p = 0.013).

CONCLUSIONS: NLR was independently associated with early worsening of organ dysfunction in ED patients with sepsis. Beyond its prognostic value, NLR may provide complementary information to conventional severity assessment by reflecting immune dysregulation.

articles.title: International Consensus Meeting on Preclinical Models of Osteoarthritis: Summary From the Aging Section.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a highly heterogeneous disease, with aging as its strongest risk factor. However, much of the preclinical OA research disproportionately relies on post-traumatic OA (PTOA) models in young animals. To address this gap, the Aging Section of the 2026 International Consensus Meeting (ICM) on Preclinical Models of OA convened experts and used the Delphi method to provide consensus guidance on studying age-associated OA. Eighteen questions concerning pain, biomechanics, genetics, metabolism, sex/hormonal differences and translational modeling were evaluated and voted upon at the 2026 Orthopedic Research Society (ORS) annual meeting. The consensus concluded that although age-associated OA and post-traumatic OA (PTOA) share pathological features, they are characterized by distinct mechanistic profiles, particularly in their inflammatory responses, mitochondrial dysfunction, and tissue-remodeling processes. Furthermore, delegates concluded that age-associated OA is a manifestation of broader aging biology, influenced by the hallmarks of aging, systemic physiology and interacting joint tissues. When evaluating these complex interactions, the available data demonstrate that no single ideal animal model exists. Instead, researchers must utilize a fit-for-purpose model ecosystem that explicitly accounts for sex, endocrine aging, and genetic background. The consensus also recommends employing multimodal outcome measures spanning structural, behavioral, and molecular domains rather than relying solely on structural pathology. Ultimately, age-associated models should serve as a complementary framework to PTOA models. Integrating this specific biological context is essential to improve translational relevance and identify biologically relevant mechanism-based interventions for the aging patient populations most affected by the disorder.

articles.title: Valve Expectoration After Endobronchial Valve Placement: Potential Utility of Computed Tomography-Based Airway Sizing-A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A 75-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease underwent endobronchial valve (EBV) placement in the left lower lobe and expectorated the valve from left B10 1 month later. Retrospective analysis of preprocedural dynamic computed tomography (CT) images showed that the median B10 luminal diameter increased from 4.25 mm at end-expiration to 6.55 mm at end-inspiration, approaching the upper limit of the recommended working range (4.0-7.0 mm) for the initially placed size 4.0 valve. A size 5.5 valve was subsequently placed without further expectoration. Bronchoscopic sizing under general anaesthesia with neuromuscular blockade and positive-pressure ventilation may underestimate the maximum airway calibre encountered during spontaneous breathing, particularly in dependent bronchi. Inspiratory CT-based airway assessment may provide useful complementary information for planning EBV placement and selecting an appropriate valve size.

articles.title: Ortner's syndrome associated with a saccular aortic arch aneurysm presenting as isolated unilateral vocal cord paralysis: a case report.
articles.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ortner's syndrome, or cardiovocal syndrome, is an uncommon cause of recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy due to cardiovascular pathology. Thoracic aortic aneurysm is a rare but important etiology that may present only with hoarseness.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and a history of chronic smoking presented with progressive hoarseness for 1 month. Flexible laryngoscopy showed paralysis of the left vocal cord without laryngeal pathology. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a 22 × 17 mm saccular aneurysm arising from the distal aortic arch at the aortopulmonary window, with mural thrombus and in close proximity to the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. No cervical, mediastinal, pulmonary, or laryngeal malignancy was detected. Echocardiography showed preserved systolic function without significant valvular disease or pulmonary hypertension. Ortner's syndrome associated with the distal aortic arch aneurysm was considered the most likely diagnosis based on the clinical and radiological findings and the exclusion of other identifiable causes. Surgical repair was advised, but the patient declined and was managed conservatively. At the 11-month clinical follow-up, he remained stable with persistent hoarseness; no follow-up CT was performed.
