CLINICAL DISCUSSION: Aortic arch aneurysm is a rare cause of Ortner's syndrome and may mimic more common causes of unilateral vocal cord paralysis, particularly malignancy. Imaging along the recurrent laryngeal nerve pathway, including the thorax, is essential when laryngoscopy does not reveal a local cause.

CONCLUSION: Unexplained left vocal cord paralysis should prompt an evaluation for cardiovascular causes. Early cross-sectional imaging can identify a thoracic aortic aneurysm and guide timely multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Delayed presentation of type I jejunal atresia radiologically mimicking malrotation in an infant with Down syndrome and congenital heart disease: a case report.
articles.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type I jejunal atresia presenting beyond the neonatal period is exceptionally rare and may mimic other obstructive gastrointestinal pathologies. Concurrent syndromic and cardiopulmonary comorbidities add substantial complexity to diagnosis and perioperative management.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 2-month-old male infant with Down syndrome and complex congenital heart disease (large patent ductus arteriosus, atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, and moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation) presented with a 3-week history of progressive bilious vomiting and acute-onset, severe metabolic acidosis. Preoperative upper gastrointestinal contrast study demonstrated delayed transit with proximal dilatation, raising concern for intestinal malrotation. Cardiac surgery had been deferred due to a preceding episode of culture-negative sepsis. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a type I jejunal atresia (intraluminal web) located approximately 20 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz, with no intraoperative evidence of malrotation or volvulus. A short-segment bowel resection with primary end-to-end anastomosis was performed.

CONCLUSION: Late-presenting type I jejunal atresia can radiologically simulate malrotation, particularly when chronic partial obstruction has produced marked proximal dilatation. In syndromic neonates and infants with significant cardiopulmonary disease, a structured multidisciplinary approach - including aggressive metabolic resuscitation and appropriately timed surgical intervention - is essential for optimizing outcomes.

articles.title: Severe Motor Deterioration of Young-Onset Parkinson's Disease in Pregnancy Following Medication Rationalisation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) in pregnancy is rare, and there are no agreed guidelines for its management. We report a 34-year-old primigravida with a three-year history of young-onset PD who presented at eight weeks' gestation with an unplanned pregnancy. She had previously tolerated levodopa poorly, with nausea and early peak-dose dyskinesia, and before conception her symptoms were reasonably controlled on amantadine, selegiline and procyclidine. Because of the potential teratogenicity of amantadine and limited safety data for the other agents, her treatment was changed to co-careldopa (carbidopa/levodopa) with domperidone. Her condition deteriorated soon after the switch. Despite stepwise increases in levodopa to 400-450 mg/day, by 31 weeks she was wheelchair-dependent, with severe peak-dose dyskinesia alternating with "off" periods and freezing, and she relied on her husband for feeding and personal care. Other drug options and deep brain stimulation were deferred until after delivery. Her care involved neurology, obstetric medicine, obstetric anaesthesia, safeguarding midwives, physiotherapy and occupational therapy, and she received thromboprophylaxis for immobility. She presented in spontaneous labour at 37+5 weeks and underwent a category 2 caesarean section under general anaesthesia, as constant tremor precluded neuraxial anaesthesia. Estimated blood loss was 750 mL. Her daughter had Apgar scores of 4, 7 and 9 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively, and weighed 2250 g (3.4th centile). Postpartum, dyskinesia and tremor temporarily prevented her from holding her baby, and trihexyphenidyl was started; her symptoms were unchanged five weeks after delivery. In young-onset PD, withdrawal of an effective pre-pregnancy regimen may be followed by significant functional decline, and previous levodopa intolerance may be a warning sign. This case highlights the importance of pre-conception counselling, early multidisciplinary planning and postnatal support.

articles.title: Severe Organ Involvement in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Retrospective Single-Center Study From Morocco.
articles.abstract: Introduction Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by multisystem inflammatory involvement and an unpredictable clinical course. SLE is among the most prevalent autoimmune diseases in Morocco, yet epidemiological and clinical data from this region remain limited. Disease management relies mainly on conventional therapies, with restricted access to advanced targeted treatments. Objective To describe the epidemiological, clinical, biological, and therapeutic characteristics of patients diagnosed with SLE in an internal medicine department in Morocco, with a particular focus on severe renal, hematological, and neurological manifestations. Methods We conducted a retrospective descriptive study including 61 patients diagnosed with SLE between January 2017 and September 2022 at the Internal Medicine Department of the International University Hospital Cheikh Khalifa Ibn Zaid in Casablanca, Morocco. Diagnosis was established according to the 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology (EULAR/ACR) and/or the 2012 Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics (SLICC) classification criteria. Data were collected from medical records and analyzed using descriptive statistical methods. Results The study population was predominantly female (n=55; 90.2%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 40.3 years (SD 14.2; median 40; range 13-74). The most common manifestations were fatigue (82.0%), arthralgia (70.5%), and malar rash (59.0%). Hematological involvement was prominent: anemia was present in 29 patients (47.5%), of whom 10 (16.4%) had confirmed autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA). Renal involvement was identified in 10 patients (16.4%); among the seven who underwent biopsy, class IV lupus nephritis predominated (n=5; 71.4%). Neurological involvement was documented in 14 patients (22.5%), with the majority comprising nonfocal manifestations such as persistent headaches and mood disorders. Most patients were treated with hydroxychloroquine (n=48; 78.7%) and systemic corticosteroids (n=38; 62.3%); immunomodulatory therapy was required in 18 patients (29.5%). Of the 39 patients with complete follow-up (median 28 months), 14 (35.9%) achieved complete remission, 19 (48.7%) achieved partial remission, 13 (33.3%) experienced disease relapse, and six (15.4%) achieved neither. Conclusion This single-center Moroccan cohort highlights a substantial burden of hematological involvement and reveals a treatment landscape defined by restricted access to biologic therapies. The findings underscore the need for region-specific epidemiological data, improved access to targeted treatments, and dedicated prospective research to better characterize SLE in North African populations.

articles.title: Hemorrhagic Cardiac Tamponade in an End-Stage Renal Disease Patient on Apixaban.
articles.abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants are used for stroke prevention in selected patients with atrial fibrillation who receive hemodialysis. Randomized trial data remain limited in this population, and the anticoagulant effect of a given dose may vary considerably between patients. We report a 56-year-old man receiving hemodialysis three times weekly who was taking apixaban 5 mg twice daily and developed persistent hypotension and abdominal pain during dialysis. The early findings suggested dialysis-associated hypotension or sepsis. Emergency department point-of-care cardiac ultrasound showed a large circumferential pericardial effusion, leading to urgent cardiology evaluation for obstructive shock. Computed tomography obtained during the same evaluation described the effusion as large and possibly hemorrhagic. Pericardiocentesis was unsuccessful because most of the fluid was posterior. Shortly after transfer to the intensive care unit, the patient developed pulseless electrical activity arrest and underwent an emergent subxiphoid pericardial window. Approximately 450 mL of bloody fluid was drained, followed by hemodynamic improvement. Cytology showed no malignant cells, and fluid cultures were negative. This case also highlights the uncertainty surrounding the use of full-dose apixaban in patients receiving hemodialysis, particularly after a major bleeding event.

articles.title: Small Airway-Predominant Asthma Revealed During Oscillometry Mannitol Challenge Despite Normal Spirometry.
articles.abstract: Objective confirmation of asthma commonly relies on spirometry, which may not capture distal airway dysfunction. A 58-year-old woman with episodic exertional dyspnoea and chest tightness had normal baseline spirometry, including forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), FEV1/forced vital capacity and forced expiratory flow at 25%-75% of vital capacity. Mannitol challenge was negative by the conventional FEV1 criterion, with no clear obstructive change in the flow-volume curves. Functional computed tomography demonstrated widespread lobular air trapping and ventilation heterogeneity, confirming small-airway involvement. At peak exposure, oscillometry showed abnormal resistance and reactance that improved after bronchodilator: R5 by 30%, R5-R20 by 56% and reactance area by 73%. After inhaled triple therapy, symptoms resolved and oscillometry normalised. The concordant clinical, imaging, physiological and longitudinal findings established small airway-predominant asthma. Oscillometry provided complementary physiological confirmation when standard spirometric indices remained normal.

articles.title: The Blind Spot of Bone Disease: Adult Hypophosphatasia in a Middle-Aged Man With Prolonged Fracture Healing.
articles.abstract: Hypophosphatasia (HPP) is a rare inherited disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the ALPL gene, which encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase. In adults, it presents with nonspecific musculoskeletal features and is often mistaken for osteoporosis. We describe a 47-year-old man referred to endocrinology with a previous diagnosis of osteoporosis and recurrent femoral fractures with markedly delayed healing, at ages 30 and 39 years. He also had chronic musculoskeletal pain and atraumatic loss of teeth early in childhood, at age four; a bone scan showed multiple metatarsal fractures, and nephrocalcinosis was present. Serum alkaline phosphatase was persistently low and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate was elevated at 494 mcg/L (reference range: 5-50 mcg/L), while thyroid, parathyroid, cortisol, pituitary, renal, hepatic, and vitamin D evaluations were unremarkable. Several relatives had related manifestations. Adult HPP was diagnosed clinically in 2017, and genetic testing later identified an apparently homozygous, likely pathogenic ALPL variant (c.214A>G, p.Ile72Val). Treatment with asfotase alfa was associated with marked improvement, and he regained the ability to walk without a cane. This case shows that persistently low alkaline phosphatase in an adult with recurrent fractures and poor fracture healing should prompt evaluation for HPP before osteoporosis is assumed and that the diagnosis need not wait for genetic confirmation. Greater clinical awareness may shorten diagnostic delay.

articles.title: Changes in Staff Knowledge and Clinical Confidence Following a Structured Teaching Programme on Functional Neurological Disorders: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
articles.abstract: Background Functional neurological disorder (FND) is a common neurological condition requiring accurate diagnosis, effective communication, and coordinated multidisciplinary management. Healthcare professionals' knowledge and confidence can influence the quality of care provided to patients with FND. This study evaluated baseline staff knowledge, awareness and confidence in managing FND and assessed the impact of a structured multidisciplinary teaching programme on a tertiary neurology ward. Methods A questionnaire-based study was conducted among healthcare professionals and support staff involved in patient care on a tertiary neurology ward. Participants included doctors, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacy technicians, physiotherapists, occupational therapists and ward clerks. The questionnaire explored knowledge of FND, recognition of positive clinical signs, attitudes towards FND, understanding of treatment options, confidence in clinical management and perception of services in place. Following the baseline assessment, a dedicated teaching week was delivered, comprising daily sessions on the clinical features of FND, underlying mechanisms, dissociative seizures, nursing management and available treatment resources. A second questionnaire was administered following the intervention to the same set of participants. Responses from the two cycles were compared. Results The pre-teaching survey included 45 respondents, and the post-teaching survey included 30. Despite frequent clinical exposure to FND, 73.3% of baseline respondents reported no previous formal FND teaching. Higher self-reported confidence ratings were observed in the post-teaching group across all five assessed domains. The proportion reporting higher confidence (scores of 4-5) in recognising FND was 46.7% before teaching and 86.7% afterwards, while confidence in explaining the diagnosis was 48.9% and 90.0%, respectively. The proportion identifying the complete set of positive clinical signs was 17.8% in the pre-teaching group and 63.3% in the post-teaching group. Recognition that FND can be diagnosed clinically using positive signs was reported by 37.8% and 76.7%, respectively. Recognition of multidisciplinary management was high in both groups (88.9% and 96.7%). These findings represent descriptive differences between anonymous, potentially overlapping respondent groups rather than measured individual improvements. Conclusion A dedicated multidisciplinary teaching week was associated with higher self-reported confidence and greater recognition of positive clinical signs of FND among post-teaching respondents. The findings highlight a potential educational gap among staff who frequently encounter FND in clinical practice and suggest that structured, recurring teaching may be beneficial. However, the small sample size, anonymous questionnaires, absence of a control group, and lack of longer-term follow-up or patient outcome measures limit causal interpretation and assessment of sustained benefits.

articles.title: Music-4-MS to Improve Cognition and Psychosocial Well-Being in People Living With Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) affects over 2.8 million people worldwide, and up to 70% of people with MS experience cognitive impairment. Unlike conventional cognitive rehabilitation, music offers a complex, multidomain stimulus activating bilateral brain networks involved in cognitive, verbal, motor, and emotional processes. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of Music-4-MS, an online music-learning intervention, in people with MS.

METHODS: A randomized controlled trial of 29 people with MS randomly assigned them to the Music-4-MS intervention (n = 16) or a music-listening active control (n = 13). Feasibility data were collected, and semistructured interviews assessed acceptability. Outcomes measured at baseline (T1), immediately after the intervention (T2), and 1 month after the intervention (T3) assessed psychosocial and functional well-being and cognitive performance on neuropsychological tests. Descriptive statistics summarized feasibility metrics, whereas content analysis examined qualitative data. Analysis of covariance compared T2 and T3 scores between groups, controlling for baseline values.

RESULTS: Participants who completed the study (79%) demonstrated high adherence and acceptability. Acceptability data revealed 6 themes: emotional resonance, navigating challenges, fostering connection and meaning, fluctuating motivation, adaptive learning strategies, and future recommendations. At T2, the Music-4-MS group exhibited lower anxiety and depression scores compared with controls (P < .01). At T3, intervention participants outperformed controls on the Trail Making Test Part B, with moderate to large effect sizes for most cognitive and some psychosocial outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Music-4-MS was acceptable to participants and showed partial feasibility. Preliminary evidence suggests Music-4-MS has the potential to improve psychosocial well-being and cognitive functioning.

articles.title: Liquiritigenin Ameliorates Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease via AMPK-Mediated Dual Activation of PPARα/PPARγ.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by hepatic triglyceride accumulation and chronic inflammation resulting from impaired fatty acid (FA) oxidation and dysregulated metabolic signaling. Liquiritigenin (LQ) exhibits diverse pharmacological activities; however, its role in MASLD and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effects of LQ against MASLD and elucidate its molecular mechanisms, focusing on PPARα/PPARγ activation and AMPK signaling. The effects of LQ were examined in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MASLD mouse model and in free fatty acid (FFA)-treated HepG2 cells. Male C57BL/6J mice were fed an HFD for 14 weeks, and LQ was administered during the final 2 weeks. Metabolic parameters, hepatic lipid accumulation, and signaling pathways were analyzed using biochemical and molecular assays and glucose and insulin tolerance tests. LQ markedly reduced hepatic triglyceride content and serum AST and ALT levels in HFD-fed mice and improved glucose intolerance and insulin resistance. LQ increased AMPK phosphorylation and the expression of SIRT1, PGC-1α, PPARα, and PPARγ while suppressing SREBF1 expression and upregulating FA oxidation-related genes. In FFA-treated HepG2 cells, LQ activated AMPK, improved insulin signaling (p-AKT and p-IRS1), enhanced FA oxidation-related gene expression, and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Pharmacological inhibition of AMPK abolished LQ-induced metabolic improvements. In conclusion, LQ attenuates MASLD progression by restoring hepatic metabolic homeostasis through AMPK activation and dual induction of PPARα and PPARγ, promoting FA oxidation and improving insulin sensitivity. Hence, LQ could be a potential natural therapeutic candidate for MASLD.

articles.title: Serum Very-Long-Chain Saturated Fatty Acids and the Mediating Role of Systemic Immune Inflammation in Cardiovascular Disease Risk.
articles.abstract: Very-long-chain saturated fatty acids (VLCSFAs) represent a distinct class of saturated fatty acids whose cardiovascular associations remain underexplored and controversial. This study investigated the associations of serum VLCSFAs-C20:0, C22:0, C23:0, and C24:0, and their sum (total VLCSFAs)-with myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and stroke in 3456 NHANES 2011-2014 participants. Binary logistic and restricted cubic spline regression models were employed, with mediation analysis examining neutrophil-related inflammatory markers. With the middle tertile as the reference, participants in the lowest tertile had higher odds of MI for C20:0 (OR 2.11, 95% CI: 1.30-3.43, p = 0.003) and C23:0 (OR 2.55, 95% CI: 1.54-4.22, p < 0.001); higher odds of HF for C22:0 (OR 1.77, 95% CI: 1.08-2.90, p = 0.023), C24:0 (OR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.29-3.54, p = 0.003), and total VLCSFAs (OR 2.02, 95% CI: 1.22-3.33, p = 0.006); and higher odds of stroke for C24:0 (OR 1.77, 95% CI: 1.10-2.84, p = 0.019). Conversely, the highest tertile of C24:0 was associated with lower odds of MI (OR 0.49, 95% CI: 0.28-0.89, p = 0.018), whereas the highest tertiles of the remaining VLCSFAs showed no further risk reduction. SII, NER, NHR, and NLR partially mediated the associations of C23:0, C24:0, and total VLCSFAs with HF, and NER, NHR, and NLR partially mediated that of C22:0 with HF. These findings reveal novel associations of serum VLCSFAs with MI, HF, and stroke that were most evident in the lowest tertile of serum concentrations, suggesting that VLCSFA deficiency may contribute to cardiovascular risk, partly through neutrophil-related inflammatory pathways.

articles.title: Primary Systemic Carnitine Deficiency Complicated With Severe Cardiomyopathy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a 6-year-2-month-old girl with SLC22A5-related PSCD presenting with severe cardiomyopathy, pneumonia, and anemia. Trio-WES confirmed the c.338G>A homozygous variant. L-carnitine replacement, combined with standard heart-failure therapy, was followed by prominent cardiac recovery, alerting clinicians to suspect PSCD in unexplained pediatric cardiomyopathy accompanied by hepatosplenomegaly and anemia.

articles.title: The Challenges in Investigating and Managing Dyspnoea in a Young Athlete With Asthma and Sickle Cell Trait.
articles.abstract: Asthma and sickle cell trait (SCT) are common conditions in adolescents and do not usually preclude high-level athletic participation. Both may be associated with exertional symptoms, creating diagnostic uncertainty and management challenges in athletes. We report the case of a 17-year-old football player with asthma and SCT who presented with exertional dyspnoea and muscle cramps. Routine investigations, including lung function tests, chest imaging and echocardiography, were within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) demonstrated exercise-induced dynamic hyperinflation, consistent with active asthma physiology during exercise. However, preserved peak oxygen uptake, anaerobic threshold and breathing reserve indicated this was not severe enough to be the predominant driver of his exercise limitation. Exercise was ultimately terminated volitionally due to leg fatigue, rather than significant ventilatory, cardiac or metabolic limitations, allowing reassurance and targeted management.

articles.title: Clinical and Invasive Hemodynamic Correlates of the TAPSE/sPAP Ratio in Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) adaptation to increased pulmonary afterload is a major determinant of prognosis in pulmonary hypertension (PH), yet comprehensive validation of simple noninvasive markers against invasive hemodynamic parameters remains limited. We investigated whether the tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to systolic pulmonary artery pressure (TAPSE/sPAP) ratio reflects the clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic spectrum of PH.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 209 consecutive patients with right heart catheterization-confirmed PH who underwent comprehensive clinical assessment, transthoracic echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamic evaluation between 2016 and 2024. Patients were stratified into quartiles according to the TAPSE/sPAP ratio, and clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic characteristics were compared.

RESULTS: The mean age was 58.8 ± 16.5 years, and 61% of patients were female. Lower TAPSE/sPAP ratios were associated with older age, higher NT-proBNP and serum uric acid levels, and lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (all p < 0.05). Decreasing TAPSE/sPAP ratios were also associated with larger right atrial and right ventricular dimensions, lower TAPSE, and higher tricuspid regurgitation velocity and estimated sPAP (all p < 0.001). Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated progressively higher right ventricular systolic pressure, mean pulmonary artery pressure, and pulmonary vascular resistance (all p < 0.001), whereas mixed venous oxygen saturation increased across quartiles (p = 0.036).

CONCLUSIONS: The TAPSE/sPAP ratio is a practical, noninvasive marker that closely reflects right ventricular remodeling and invasive hemodynamic impairment in pulmonary hypertension. Lower TAPSE/sPAP ratios identify patients with more advanced RV-pulmonary arterial uncoupling and may improve bedside hemodynamic risk stratification.

articles.title: Same-Source Bias Confounds Pulmonary Hypertension Functional Class Self-Report Validation in Pulmonary Hypertension.

Building Consensus Among Intensive Care Nurses on the Scope of Practice for Registered Nurses Deployed to Intensive Care During Surge Events: A Real-Time Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disaster events that overwhelm health system capacity often require the deployment of nurses from non-critical care clinical areas to supplement the specialist intensive care workforce. However, the role of deployed registered nurses in intensive care is poorly defined and without clear role boundaries, experienced intensive care nurses often bear disproportionate supervisory burdens, and deployed staff may assume clinical responsibilities for which they are inadequately prepared. Developing a scope of practice for deployed nurses is essential for safe, effective surge responses.

AIM: To achieve expert consensus on the scope of practice of deployed registered nurses in a surged intensive care unit.

STUDY DESIGN: A Real-Time Delphi study was conducted using a web-based platform. A 65-item survey was administered to a panel of experienced Australian intensive care nurses and educators with expertise in training and/or supervising nurses deployed to intensive care during surge events. Participants rated activities that could potentially be undertaken by deployed registered nurses in a surged intensive care setting using a 5-point Likert scale across two dimensions: appropriateness for delegation and importance within a tiered nursing model. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥ 70% agreement. Free-text comments were analysed thematically.

RESULTS: Fifteen expert panellists completed the survey. Of the 69 items assessed, 33 reached consensus and were retained as constituting the scope of practice for registered nurses deployed to intensive care. Consensus items spanned neurological observation, basic cardiovascular monitoring, gastrointestinal care, fluid balance documentation, and essential nursing cares. No consensus was reached for mechanical ventilation, non-invasive ventilation or renal replacement therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: This study resulted in a consensus-derived scope of practice for deployed registered nurses in a surged intensive care. The findings establish clear role boundaries to support safe, tiered nursing care during future surge events and provide a foundation for developing targeted upskilling programs.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The findings offer intensive care clinicians, educators, and health services a practical foundation for planning surge nursing models before surge events occur. Clearer role delineation may also reduce uncertainty for deployed nurses and lessen the supervisory burden on experienced intensive care staff.

articles.title: Acute Appendicitis During Pregnancy: A Seven-Year Retrospective Case Series at a United Kingdom Tertiary Hospital.
articles.abstract: Background Acute appendicitis is the most common surgical problem encountered during pregnancy. Our case series was conducted to evaluate the clinical presentation, diagnosis, management, and outcomes of acute appendicitis in pregnant women. Methods  A retrospective analysis of nine pregnant women diagnosed with acute appendicitis at James Cook University Hospital, United Kingdom, from 2017 to 2024 was conducted. Patients were evaluated according to age, clinical presentation, gestational age, diagnostic modalities, histopathology, time interval from admission to surgery, type of surgery, outcomes, and complications. Results The mean age was 26.6 years. Cases occurred in the first trimester (n = 1/9, 11.1%), second trimester (n = 3/9, 33.3%), third trimester (n = 4/9, 44.4%), and postpartum period (n = 1/9, 11.1%). Right iliac fossa pain was the most common presentation. WBC counts and CRP levels were elevated in all cases. Imaging was used to support the diagnosis in 7/9 patients (77.8%). Ultrasound was performed in 5/9 patients (55.6%), yielding positive findings in 1/5 (20.0%), inconclusive findings in 1/5 (20.0%), and false-negative findings in 3/5 (60.0%). MRI was performed in 7/9 patients (77.8%) and identified appendicitis in all clinically suspected cases, although 2/5 examinations (40.0%) were subsequently considered false-positive. The mean interval from presentation to surgery was 3.4 days. All patients (n = 9/9, 100%) underwent surgery, including laparoscopic appendicectomy in 6/9 (66.7%) and open appendicectomy in 3/9 (33.3%). Histopathological confirmation of acute appendicitis was obtained in 5/9 cases (55.6%). The negative appendicectomy rate was 4/9 (44.4%). Complications among confirmed cases included peritonitis in 5/9 patients (55.6%), sepsis in 2/9 (22.2%), perforation in 1/9 (11.1%), and preterm labour in 1/9 (11.1%). Conclusion  Our case series demonstrates the continued challenges in the accurate and timely diagnosis of acute appendicitis, coupled with a reluctance to operate on pregnant women, which leads to delays in surgical intervention, thereby increasing the risk of complications. The surgical approach (laparoscopic/open) did not change outcomes. MRI demonstrates superior diagnostic reliability; however, despite advances in diagnostic modalities, the negative laparotomy rate remains high during pregnancy.

articles.title: Effects of Danhong Injection on 90-Day Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Adaptive, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase IV Trial.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic options for neurological recovery remain limited in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients ineligible for thrombolysis, and while multitarget drugs like Danhong injection (DHI) demonstrate efficacy, their polypharmacological mechanisms remain understood. In this trial including 1505 thrombolysis-ineligible AIS patients with anterior-circulation and blood stasis syndrome (NCT01677208), 14-day treatment with DHI (n = 1002) versus placebo (n = 503) demonstrated superior 90-day outcomes (modified Rankin scale [mRS] score ≤1: 64.57 vs. 59.24%; adjusted odds ratio 1.43, 95%CI 1.10-1.86, p = 0.007), particularly in females and hypertensive patients, and no significant between-group differences in any serious adverse events (all p > 0.05). In the exploratory RNA-sequencing substudy of 39 patients (24 DHI, 15 placebo), we identified 19 differentially expressed modules, including two paired targeted modules "HBG2" and "TMEM108," whose topological features showed opposite correlations with the primary clinical outcome (δmRS at Day 90). Furthermore, a combination effect model was introduced to describe the time-dependent joint association of these modules with outcome (combination effect score: -0.729 at Day 0, 0.227 at Day 14, and 1 at Day 90). These findings demonstrate DHI may be a favorable treatment option for thrombolysis-ineligible AIS patients and provide a proposed analytical framework for future, independently validated studies of multitarget drug actions in complex diseases.

articles.title: A Pan-Hepatic T-Cell Atlas Identifies Disease-Specific Immune Dysfunction and Therapeutic Targets for Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics has greatly advanced insight into hepatic immunity and immunotherapy. However, the absence of an integrated atlas spanning multiple hepatic diseases limits systematic comparisons of immune heterogeneity and dynamics. Here, we established a Pan-HEpatic single-cell Atlas of T cells (Pheat), covering 139 donors, 255 blood and liver samples spanning chronic hepatitis (chronic hepatitis B/C [CHB/CHC], alcohol-associated hepatitis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis), cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and healthy controls (HC), and delineated profound population-, tissue-, and disease-level heterogeneity of 624,215 T cells, with emphasis on CD8+ exhausted T cells (Tex) and CD4+ regulatory T cells (Treg). Within Tex, intrahepatic precursor Tex (Texpre) were depleted in CHB compared with healthy controls and other hepatic diseases. Disease-specific checkpoint dominance (4-1BB in CHB, TIGIT in HCC) in Texpre was identified and experimentally validated. Panobinostat was predicted and validated to reinvigorate Texpre in CHB patients. In parallel, effector Treg (eTreg) accumulated in diseased livers and exhibited divergent IL-2-STAT5 signaling-hyperactive in CHB and HCC, suppressed in cirrhosis-indicating distinct immunosuppressive status. Lapatinib/olopatadine enhanced Treg suppressive markers in cirrhosis. Pheat provides a high-resolution atlas of hepatic T cells, revealing disease-specific immune heterogeneity and regulatory programs that inform cellular and molecular targets for potential immunotherapy.

articles.title: Chest Pain in Vain: Spontaneous Portal Vein Thrombosis.
articles.abstract: A 53-year-old man with a patient-reported history of ultrasound-diagnosed fatty liver disease presented with sudden-onset severe chest pain and a brief loss of consciousness, followed by progressive abdominal pain and a single episode of bloody diarrhoea. Admission investigations approximately 24 hours after the chest pain episode showed a D-dimer of 14,502 µg/L and high-sensitivity troponin I below 3 ng/L. An arterial-phase computed tomography (CT) aortogram showed no aortic dissection but did not establish portal venous patency. Following specialist thoracic radiology review, the aortogram was considered satisfactory to exclude pulmonary embolism down to the segmental level, and dedicated pulmonary angiography was not performed. Portal venous-phase CT performed 72 hours after the aortogram demonstrated extensive portal, superior mesenteric, and splenic vein thrombosis, with equivocal caecal and ascending colonic changes. Symptoms improved during anticoagulation. Repeat CT three months later showed resolution of thrombosis, with all three affected veins patent. This case illustrates the importance of selecting an imaging protocol appropriate to the evolving clinical presentation. An unrevealing arterial-phase examination did not exclude portal venous thrombosis. The relationship between the thrombosis and the initial chest pain and collapse remains uncertain, as does the contribution of the patient's reported fatty liver disease.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Extended Resection (Cecal Resection or Right Hemicolectomy) in Patients With Acute Appendicitis at a Tertiary Private Hospital: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute appendicitis may require surgical procedures beyond conventional appendectomy, including cecal resection and right hemicolectomy. This study aimed to identify clinical factors associated with extended resection in adults undergoing surgery for acute appendicitis.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 360 adults treated surgically for acute appendicitis at a tertiary care hospital between 2018 and 2023. Extended resection was defined as cecal resection or right hemicolectomy. Associations were assessed using univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, symptom duration, previous abdominal surgery, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. Appendicitis severity was evaluated in a secondary model using grouped phases. Missing data were not imputed. The study received ethics committee approval (2024-EXT-871).

RESULTS: Extended resection occurred in 50 of 351 patients with available outcome data (14.2%). Longer symptom duration (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.185; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.004-1.398; p=0.045) and older age (aOR 1.022; 95% CI 1.001-1.045; p=0.045) were associated with extended resection in the primary model. In the secondary model, advanced appendicitis phases were strongly associated with extended resection (aOR 10.273; 95% CI 4.694-22.481; p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Longer symptom duration was associated with extended resection, including after adjustment for grouped appendicitis severity. These findings warrant cautious interpretation given the retrospective design and limited number of events.

articles.title: Diagnostic Pitfall: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension Presenting With Postpartum Right-Sided Heart Failure in a 21-Year-Old-Case Report.
articles.abstract: Mixed connective tissue disease is a multisystem autoimmune condition characterized by overlapping clinical and serological features related to anti-U1-RNP antibodies of at least two connective tissue diseases. It may present with myocarditis, pericarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and, less commonly, heart failure. We present a 21-year-old female with bilateral foot swelling, cough, and shortness of breath 3 months after a vaginal delivery. On examination, she was hypotensive (90/70 mmHg), with an elevated jugular venous pressure, a pulmonary systolic murmur with loud P2, and a tricuspid regurgitation murmur. Bronchial breath sounds and fine crepitations were present in both lower lung fields. She was evaluated initially for suspected postpartum cardiomyopathy. Transthoracic echocardiography was suggestive of a probable moderate to severe PAH. High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral moderate pleural effusions, honeycombing with partial atelectasis of the underlying lung, and cardiomegaly. Computed Tomography Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA) showed findings likely consistent with probable mild pulmonary hypertension. An antinuclear antibody panel was performed and was positive for anti-U1-RNP, SS-A, SS-B, and Jo-1 antibodies. She was started on Lasix 40 mg, Aldactone 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, and heparin. Treatment with 20 mg of prednisolone was started and gradually tapered. Her anasarca and dyspnea improved, and she was discharged with follow-up arranged with cardiology and rheumatology. Timely identification of MCTD-associated pulmonary hypertension and its cardiovascular complications is essential and allows early commencement of treatment, which further prevents the patients from developing heart failure.

articles.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Laterality Disorder Associated With NME7 Variants.
articles.abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital laterality disorder characterized by a mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Although isolated SIT is generally associated with a favorable prognosis, prenatal diagnosis requires careful evaluation to exclude associated structural malformations and syndromic presentations, as well as genetic investigation to identify a possible underlying etiology and improve prognostic assessment. The genetic basis of SIT is complex and remains incompletely understood. To date, genotype-phenotype correlations for SIT-associated genetic variants remain poorly established. We report the prenatal and postnatal clinical course of a fetus with isolated SIT carrying a homozygous intragenic deletion of the NME7 gene, identified by whole-exome sequencing. A primigravida woman was referred at 22 + 2 weeks of gestation after dextrocardia was identified during the second-trimester morphology scan. Detailed ultrasound and fetal echocardiography were performed to assess organ laterality and exclude associated structural abnormalities. An invasive diagnostic procedure (amniocentesis) was performed, including chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) and trio whole-exome sequencing. Ultrasound confirmed isolated SIT, characterized by dextrocardia, a right-sided stomach, and a left-sided liver and gallbladder. Echocardiography revealed normal cardiac anatomy and function. CMA identified a maternally inherited Xp22.33 deletion encompassing the entire SHOX gene, which was detected in the mother but not in the father and was considered an incidental finding. Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous, likely pathogenic intragenic deletion involving exons 2-7 of the NME7 gene. Targeted parental DNA analysis confirmed that both parents were heterozygous carriers of the deletion. The pregnancy was continued based on the present molecular findings, since the implication of NME7 variants seemed to be responsible for a non-syndromic form of SIT. A healthy female infant was delivered at term. Postnatal evaluation confirmed SIT with a small atrial septal defect with no hemodynamic impact and no other associated anomalies.  This case highlights the additional diagnostic value of whole-exome sequencing in fetuses with apparently isolated laterality abnormalities. It adds to the currently limited evidence linking NME7 variants to isolated SIT. This case also emphasizes the importance of multidisciplinary assessment and genetic counseling to optimize diagnosis, prognostic evaluation, parental counseling, and postnatal management.

articles.title: Exploring Environmental Influences on Mono(2-Ethylhexyl) Phthalate (MEHP) Exposure in Common Bottlenose Dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) in Sarasota Bay, FL, USA.
articles.abstract: Phthalates, endocrine-disrupting, persistent organic pollutants widely used in plastic manufacturing, can readily enter aquatic environments and contaminate estuaries. As apex predators, resident bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) provide critical insights into ecosystem health. Prior work documented phthalate exposure in the long-term resident bottlenose dolphin community of Sarasota Bay, Florida, with evidence of temporal and spatial variability, particularly for mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), a metabolite of the commonly used plasticizer di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP). We predicted that environmental factors, such as large-scale storm events, rainfall, and harmful algal blooms (HABs), may influence this variability. Urine samples collected from 138 free-ranging dolphins during 1993-2024 were screened for phthalate metabolites, reliable biomarkers of exposure. MEHP was the most common metabolite, detected in 78.3% of samples (Regression on Order Statistics mean = 6.19 ng mL-1, s.d. = 11.29 ng mL-1, range = 0.04-76.6 ng mL-1), and concentrations did not vary significantly by sex or age (p > 0.05). MEHP concentrations were positively correlated with rainfall occurring 3 days prior to sampling (p = 0.01), and concentrations were significantly lower among dolphins sampled within 6 months of a major storm event (p = 0.007). No significant associations between MEHP and HABs were discerned (p > 0.05). Such findings suggest increased phthalate-contaminated runoff during short-term rainfall events, as well as the dilution or offshore transport of phthalates via storm-related processes. Despite documented toxicity of MEHP to humans and other marine species, health impacts on Sarasota Bay dolphins remain poorly understood. As sentinels of estuarine health, long-term exposure may signal chronic ecotoxicological risks, and observed environmental influences highlight the need for continued monitoring, research, and mitigation.

articles.title: Asthma Exacerbations Following Wildfire Smoke PM2.5 Exposure Among U.S. Adults.
articles.abstract: Asthma exacerbation can be triggered by various forms of air pollution, including PM2.5 from wildfire smoke. This study aims to investigate the association between wildfire smoke PM2.5 exposure and asthma exacerbations in adults during the warm months (April-August) between 2006 and 2019. Using a case-crossover design, we analyzed 18,935 asthma exacerbation events and four matched control periods per event from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) All of Us research program. We used the conditional logistic regression to estimate the association (odds ratios [ORs]) between wildfire smoke PM2.5 exposure and asthma exacerbation, considering lag periods of 0-7 days and adjusting for temperature, precipitation, and humidity. Significant positive associations were observed across all lag periods, with adjusted ORs ranging from 1.27 (95% CI: 1.22-1.33) to 1.38 (95% CI: 1.32-1.44). Stratified analyses showed higher odds of asthma exacerbation among older adults, non-Hispanic Whites, midwestern residents, and those exposed in May. These findings highlight the potential contribution of wildfire smoke PM2.5 to asthma exacerbations in adults and the importance of targeted public health strategies to reduce exposure during wildfire events.

articles.title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
articles.abstract: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up. In patients with severe pregnancy-induced hypertension, PRES warrants recognition as a potential complication; management should prioritize rigorous blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, alleviation of pregnancy-related physiological stress, and timely neuroimaging to guide treatment, with strategies balancing maternal and fetal safety-early recognition and intervention underpinned by standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration being critical to improving prognosis and reducing complications.

articles.title: Symmetrical Peripheral Gangrene in a Child With Plasmodium falciparum Cerebral Malaria: A Rare but Serious Complication.
articles.abstract: Symmetrical peripheral gangrene is a rare, limb-threatening complication associated with severe infection and disseminated intravascular coagulation. We report a case of a 6-year-old girl with cerebral malaria who developed gangrene of all toes during treatment. Management included antimalarials, antibiotics, supportive care, debridement, and subsequent skin grafting after adequate wound granulation.

articles.title: Epidemiological Profile and Temporal Trends of Exogenous Poisoning in the State of São Paulo and Brazil From 2010 to 2020.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exogenous poisoning is a compulsorily notifiable condition in Brazil, but analyses of its temporal trends in the state of São Paulo remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological profile of exogenous poisoning in the state of São Paulo from 2010 to 2020 and its distribution across Regional Health Care Networks (Redes Regionais de Atenção à Saúde (RRAS)) and to analyze temporal trends in incidence, mortality, and case fatality compared with Brazil.

METHODS: An observational time-series study was conducted using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)), obtained through the TabNet platform of the Brazilian Ministry of Health, and population estimates from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics. Sociodemographic, exposure, and outcome variables were analyzed. Incidence, mortality, and case fatality rates were calculated, and notifications were stratified by RRAS. Temporal trends were assessed by joinpoint regression, estimating the annual percent change (APC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each segment and for the entire period, with sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 315,266 notifications and 3,209 deaths were recorded in São Paulo, accounting for 25.7% of notifications and 27.4% of deaths in Brazil. Cases predominated among females (n=169,740; 53.8%), individuals aged 20-39 years (n=142,989; 45.4%), and White individuals (n=166,896; 52.9%). Medications were the main toxic agent (n=144,567; 45.9%), and suicide attempt was the main circumstance (n=125,491; 39.8%). Incidence was 64.7 cases per 100,000 inhabitants per year (Brazil: 54.8), mortality was 6.6 deaths per 1,000,000 inhabitants per year (Brazil: 5.2), and case fatality was 1.02% (Brazil: 0.95%). Incidence (APC=13.9%; p<0.001) and mortality (APC=11.7%; p<0.001) increased over the period, whereas case fatality showed no significant trend over the entire period; a decline between 2016 and 2020 (APC=-14.8%; p=0.031) was not statistically significant in sensitivity analyses. The highest incidence was observed in RRAS 12 (São José do Rio Preto/Araçatuba; 126.2 per 100,000 inhabitants per year), a region of intense agricultural activity.

CONCLUSIONS: Exogenous poisoning in São Paulo showed increasing incidence and mortality, at levels above the national average, with a decline in case fatality after 2016 that should be interpreted with caution, and marked regional heterogeneity. These findings support strengthening toxicological surveillance and tailoring prevention strategies to regional and epidemiological characteristics.

articles.title: Hybrid Osteosynthesis for Septic Humeral Shaft Nonunion in a Patient with Obesity: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Septic humeral shaft nonunion represents a complex reconstructive challenge in orthopedic surgery, particularly in patients with obesity, in whom increased lever arms and greater mechanical loading of the upper extremity substantially compromise fixation stability. Recurrent failure of isolated fixation constructs, including intramedullary nails or compression plates, necessitates hybrid strategies that combine enhanced biomechanical stability with effective eradication of microbial infection. This article presents the case of a middle-aged man with obesity and a history of a left humeral shaft fracture initially treated with intramedullary nailing in December 2020 who developed persistent nonunion. Following revision surgery with dynamic compression plating, fixation failure occurred secondary to implant fatigue. A second revision procedure was performed through a posterior approach, including nerve neurolysis, extensive debridement, and hybrid fixation using a 240 x 8 mm Targon™ H intramedullary nail (B. Braun, Melsungen, Germany) combined with a narrow 4.5-mm dynamic compression plate (DCP; DePuy Synthes, Warsaw, IN, USA). Cancellous bone chip grafting was also performed. Intraoperative cultures yielded Staphylococcus epidermidis, establishing the diagnosis of septic nonunion, and targeted oral clindamycin therapy was initiated. Despite transient postoperative radial neuropraxia, which resolved with pregabalin treatment and structured physical rehabilitation, the patient achieved complete osseous union, eradication of infection, and an Upper Extremity Functional Scale (UEFS) score of 69/80, corresponding to 86% of maximal functional capacity. In conclusion, hybrid fixation combining an intramedullary nail with a narrow 4.5-mm DCP, together with pathogen-directed antimicrobial therapy, provides excellent axial and rotational stability and represents an effective salvage strategy for septic humeral shaft nonunion in patients with increased biomechanical demands.

articles.title: Enteric Fever Presenting With Acute Bilateral Lower Limb Weakness due to Para Infectious Myopathy With Elevated Serum Creatine Kinase: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Parainfectious myopathy is a rare complication of Salmonella infection. We report an immunocompetent young patient presenting with acute bilateral lower limb weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase. Blood cultures confirmed Salmonella sp. Prompt treatment with meropenem and azithromycin resulted in reducing CK level from 1854 to 240 U/L.

articles.title: Spatial Prediction of Opisthorchis viverrini Infection Risk Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing, Hexagonal Grid Optimization, and Ensemble Machine Learning: A Case Study From Northeastern Thailand.
articles.abstract: Opisthorchis viverrini (OV) infection is a major public health problem in northeastern Thailand, where it causes cholangiocarcinoma. This study developed a spatial prediction model for OV infection risk in Sakon Nakhon Province by integrating Sentinel-2, Sentinel-3, and CHIRPS data with hexagonal grid optimization and ensemble machine learning. Eleven environmental indices were aggregated using a newly developed Hd index, which identified an optimal hexagonal grid size of d = 2,100 m. Three models-Random Forest, XGBoost, and Multi-scale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR)-were compared using R 2, root mean square error, ROC-AUC at exceedance thresholds (1%, 2%, 3%), 5-fold cross-validation, and SHAP analysis. XGBoost outperformed the other models, achieving the highest test-set R 2 (0.894) and AUC (0.955) at the >3% threshold, with stable cross-validated performance (mean R 2 = 0.83). SHAP analysis identified GVMI as the most influential predictor (mean |SHAP| = 0.125), followed by MNDWI (0.090) and SPI-6 (0.070). Moderate moisture conditions and above-average rainfall increased risk, whereas deep open water reduced it. The resulting risk map supports targeted surveillance and resource allocation for OV control in endemic areas.

articles.title: Mitral regurgitation and left atrial phasic function and atrioventricular coupling in patients with myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
articles.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral regurgitation (MR) after myocardial infarction (MI) may increase left atrial (LA) pressure and contribute to cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated the incremental association of MR with LA phasic function and strain and identified independent factors associated with LA deformation in patients with MI.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 189 patients with MI (111 without MR and 78 with MR: mild, 27; moderate, 33; severe, 18) and 86 normal controls who underwent 3.0-T cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). MR severity was graded by the CMR-derived MR fraction: mild <30%, moderate 30% to <50%, and severe ≥50%. CMR-derived LA phasic function and strain (reservoir strain, epsilon-s; booster strain, epsilon-a; conduit strain, epsilon-e), left ventricular (LV) function and strain, infarct size, and MR fraction were measured. Between-group comparisons were performed using one-way analysis of variance or the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc correction, and multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent factors associated with LA strain. A two-sided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Patients with MI and MR had lower LA reservoir strains [22.14%±10.91% vs. 28.65% (22.78%, 38.30%) vs. 41.70% (36.15%, 53.15%)], booster strains [11.52%±6.19% vs. 13.80% (10.20%, 19.80%) vs. 19.25% (15.10%, 24.05%)], and conduit strains [9.40% (6.03%, 14.85%) vs. 14.60% (9.60%, 20.50%) vs. 22.55% (17.75%, 30.43%)] than patients with MI without MR and controls (all P<0.05). They also had higher LA maximum volume [68.43 (57.44, 91.51) mL] and minimum volume [35.93 (24.43, 61.15) mL] and lower LA total ejection fraction (45.39%±14.97%) than the other groups (all P<0.05). In multivariable analysis, MR degree was independently associated with reservoir strain (β=-0.194, P=0.048) and conduit strain (β=-0.208, P=0.038). Anterior wall MI (reservoir strain: β=-0.245, P=0.014; booster strain: β=-0.231, P=0.028; conduit strain: β=-0.224, P=0.027) and posteromedial papillary muscle infarction (reservoir strain: β=-0.329, P=0.004; booster strain: β=-0.370, P=0.003) were also independently associated with LA strain.

CONCLUSIONS: MR was associated with further deterioration of LA myocardial strain in patients with MI. Posteromedial papillary muscle infarction, anterior wall MI, beta-blocker use, and dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus clopidogrel were independently associated with LA strain. CMR-derived functional and strain parameters may help characterize LV-LA coupling and support risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Value of left atrial to left ventricular volume ratio in left heart remodeling classification and postoperative prognosis assessment in patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis.
articles.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) patients exhibit heterogeneous left heart remodeling, with unclear impacts on postoperative prognosis. This study aimed to classify left heart remodeling subtypes using the left atrial (LA) to left ventricular (LV) volume ratio, analyze subtype differences, and validate the ratio's predictive value for 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 350 RMS patients who underwent mitral valve surgery between February 2021 and October 2024. Preoperative LA end-systolic volume (LAESV) and LV end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) were measured by three-dimensional (3D) echocardiography to calculate the LA/LV volume ratio. The optimal cutoff value was determined by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Patients were divided into predominantly LV remodeling (PLVR) and predominantly LA remodeling (PLAR) groups. Clinical data, echocardiographic parameters, and 1-year adverse outcomes [a composite of heart failure (HF) rehospitalization and all-cause mortality] were compared. Risk factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses.

RESULTS: The LA/LV volume ratio yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.723 (P<0.001) for predicting 1-year adverse outcomes, with an optimal cutoff of 0.61. PLAR patients (LA/LV >0.61, n=168) were older, more frequently female, had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), more severe mitral stenosis, and larger right atrial volume (all P<0.001). PLVR patients (LA/LV ≤0.61, n=182) had a higher rate of ischemic heart disease, lower LV ejection fraction (LVEF), and a higher proportion of moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (all P<0.001). The 1-year composite adverse event rate was 20.6% overall, significantly higher in the PLAR group than in the PLVR group (34.3% vs. 15.1%, P<0.001). Multivariate Cox regression identified PLAR [hazard ratio (HR) =1.72, P=0.008], preoperative N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) >3,000 pg/mL (HR =1.91, P=0.002), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV (HR =2.15, P=0.002), moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (HR =1.58, P=0.036), and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR =1.63, P=0.029) as independent risk factors.

CONCLUSIONS: The LA/LV volume ratio (optimal cutoff 0.61) effectively classifies RMS left heart remodeling subtypes. PLAR is associated with increased 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes, and integrating mitral/tricuspid regurgitation assessment and extended echocardiographic parameters enhances prognostic accuracy. This provides a robust tool for preoperative risk stratification and individualized treatment in RMS patients.

articles.title: Medicaid Coverage Withdrawal and Dispensing of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists for Obesity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Five state Medicaid programs withdrew coverage of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for obesity in late 2025 and January 2026, and others have narrowed coverage or are reconsidering it. The benefits of these drugs appear to depend on continued use, but whether withdrawal interrupts treatment for current users is unknown. This study examined changes in dispensing of obesity-indicated GLP-1 RAs after state Medicaid programs withdrew or restricted coverage.

METHODS: This quasi-experimental study used quarterly Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data for 50 states and the District of Columbia from 2021 through the first quarter of 2026. Difference-in-differences and event-study models compared dispensing in states that withdrew coverage with dispensing in states that continued it, using each state's dispensing of diabetes-indicated GLP-1 RAs as a within-state comparison. The exposure was withdrawal or restriction of Medicaid coverage of GLP-1 RAs for obesity, identified from state agency documents. The main outcome was reimbursed prescriptions for obesity-indicated GLP-1 RAs per 1,000 enrollees per quarter. Estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Data were analyzed from September to October 2026.

RESULTS: The five withdrawing states accounted for 2,428,709 (65.2%) of 3,725,732 obesity-indicated GLP-1 RA prescriptions reimbursed by Medicaid in 2025. Compared with 12 continuing states, withdrawal was associated with an 84.7% decline in obesity-indicated dispensing (95% CI: 64.5%-93.4%; exact permutation p < 0.001), or 29.1 fewer prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees per quarter (95% CI: 14.3-43.9). No significant change was detected in diabetes-indicated dispensing (-3.2%; 95% CI: -23.4% to 22.2%), and differences between the two groups before the withdrawals were announced were small and not statistically significant. In the first quarter without coverage, obesity-indicated dispensing fell by 61% to 96% in individual withdrawing states. The four states that withdrew on January 1, 2026, reimbursed 661,353 obesity-indicated prescriptions in the preceding quarter and 134,647 in the next, a decline of 526,706 (79.6%). Dispensing of older antiobesity medications increased by at most 2.9 prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees. Narrower criteria in two states were followed by declines of 23%-37%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this quasi-experimental study, withdrawal of Medicaid coverage was associated with the loss of most reimbursed dispensing of GLP-1 RAs for obesity within one quarter, with little replacement by other agents. Protecting enrollees already receiving these drugs, for example, by honoring existing authorizations, might limit treatment interruption, but this has not been evaluated.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology for non-experts: decoding key terms and understanding machine learning methodologies. A Scientific Statement of the ESC Working Group on e-Cardiology, the European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA), the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC), the Heart Failure Association (HFA), the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI), the European Association of Preventive Cardiology (EAPC), and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC, the ESC Regulatory Affairs Committee, and the ESC Digital Cardiology and Artificial Intelligence Committee.
articles.abstract: Evidence-based medicine represents the systematic approach through which physicians today use the best available scientific evidence from clinical research to guide their clinical decision-making process. However, the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), with its diverse models and potential applications in medicine, is leading to a new form of research driven by 'big data' and heterogeneous datasets, extending beyond conventional statistical analysis and thereby making AI literacy an increasingly essential competence for clinicians. Artificial intelligence applications in cardiology have shown potential to support disease diagnosis, risk prediction, workflow efficiency, and therapeutic decision-making. However, despite these opportunities, AI may also represent a technological barrier for many physicians, due to its mathematical foundations and the speed at which models evolve. A solid understanding of AI concepts is therefore necessary for cardiologists to critically interpret results and engage with this new research landscape. This scientific statement explores AI in cardiology from an educational perspective, outlining the key knowledge required to build adequate AI literacy. The goal is to enable cardiologists not only to avoid reliance on external experts for methodological decisions, but also to collaborate with greater insight and informed judgment.

articles.title: Acute Myocardial Injury in Patients Presenting With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Prevalence, Predictors, Troponin Dynamics, and In-Hospital Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) may cause anemia, hypovolemia, and hemodynamic compromise, potentially contributing to myocardial injury during the acute illness. Troponin elevation in this setting requires careful interpretation because an isolated measurement cannot reliably distinguish acute injury from elevation without qualifying change or establish myocardial infarction. The frequency, temporal evolution, and clinical significance of acute myocardial injury in patients with UGIB remain incompletely characterized. This prospective multicenter study evaluated its prevalence, associated admission factors, serial troponin dynamics, and relationship with in-hospital outcomes, including subsequent mortality among patients surviving the first 24 hours.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter observational cohort study enrolled 1,000 adults at tertiary care hospitals in Punjab, Pakistan, between January 2025 and August 2026. Cardiac troponin I measurements were scheduled at presentation, 3-6 hours, and 20-24 hours. Acute injury required a concentration above the applicable 99th-percentile reference limit and a serial maximum-minimum range of ≥10 ng/L and ≥20% of the earliest observed concentration, using at least two measurements spanning ≥3 hours. Prevalence was estimated with Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression examined admission factors associated with injury. A 24-hour landmark analysis evaluated subsequent mortality among patients alive and still hospitalized with classifiable injury status.

RESULTS: Injury status was classifiable in 960 patients; 104 had acute injury, giving a prevalence of 10.8% (95% CI: 9.0-13.0%). A further 131 patients (13.6% of classifiable assessments) had troponin elevation without qualifying change, while 40 assessments were indeterminate. Older age (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per decade: 1.40; 95% CI: 1.21-1.63), coronary artery disease (aOR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.06-3.10), and lower hemoglobin (aOR per 1 g/dL decrease: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.06-1.51) were associated with acute injury. Fourteen acute-injury cases (13.5%) first met the classification criterion at the late measurement. Among 810 landmark patients with known outcomes, 34 died. Subsequent mortality was 15.2% with acute injury versus 2.8% without acute injury (aOR: 3.47; 95% CI: 1.58-7.62; p=0.002). An adverse differential assignment of unresolved mortality outcomes attenuated this association (aOR: 1.86; 95% CI: 0.94-3.69).

CONCLUSIONS: Acute myocardial injury affected approximately one in 10 classifiable patients with UGIB and was associated with older age, coronary artery disease, lower hemoglobin, and higher subsequent in-hospital mortality. Serial measurements distinguished acute changes from elevation without qualifying change. The mortality association requires cautious interpretation because of limited events, residual confounding, and incomplete follow-up.

articles.title: Unexplained Optic Neuritis and New Heart Block: A Diagnostically Challenging Case of Probable Sarcoidosis.
articles.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown etiology and manifests in multiple forms. It can affect several organs within the body; however, the lungs and intra-thoracic lymph nodes are involved in the majority of cases. Diagnosis can be challenging due to the diversity of presentation and similarities to other systemic diseases. Although biopsy is often used to confirm the diagnosis, areas of disease involvement can be difficult to access. This case involves a patient with 2 years of unexplained recurrent optic neuritis who presented to the emergency room with a new third-degree heart block. Her optic neuritis had previously responded to high-dose prednisone, but she was unable to achieve steroid-sparing disease control with the addition of rituximab despite receiving it for over a year. Imaging identified areas of nervous system and cardiac inflammation. She had elevated inflammatory markers and soluble IL-2 receptor level suspicious for systemic inflammation. Extensive evaluation for infection and other autoimmune disease was negative. A subsequent PET/CT scan was eventually able to identify lymph node involvement. Probable sarcoidosis remained the leading differential, and a bronchoscopy with endobronchial biopsy was performed 2 weeks later. Unfortunately, the yield was insufficient due to immunosuppression from ongoing steroid use. The patient was able to achieve remission after methotrexate and infliximab were added to her prednisone. Her steroids were tapered off without recurrence of disease activity. High-grade heart block is a well-established manifestation of cardiac sarcoidosis. However, the preceding unexplained optic neuritis in the absence of typical pulmonary involvement or histological confirmation complicated the diagnosis of sarcoidosis. This case highlights the importance of considering sarcoidosis in the differential of multisystemic inflammatory disease and the challenges associated with its diagnosis.

articles.title: Guide-sheath-assisted bailout technique for intra-procedural single-leaflet device attachment using the PASCAL system: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-leaflet device attachment (SLDA) is a rare but serious complication of mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (MTEER). When SLDA occurs after full device release, management options are limited. In contrast, intra-procedural SLDA recognized before full implant release may allow a specific bailout strategy.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man with severe degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR) underwent MTEER using the PASCAL Ace system because of high surgical risk. Initial device implantation reduced MR from severe to mild. However, after removal of both clasp lines during the release process, SLDA occurred at the posterior leaflet, resulting in recurrent severe MR. Although standard retrieval was no longer feasible, the implant remained connected to the steerable catheter. Under fluoroscopic and transoesophageal echocardiographic guidance, a guide sheath was advanced coaxially towards the implant. Controlled insertion of the guide sheath between the clasp and paddle, followed by gradual paddle opening, enabled leaflet disengagement and successful device retrieval without leaflet injury. A second implantation achieved a sufficient reduction in mitral regurgitation.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates a novel bailout technique for intra-procedural SLDA. Successful retrieval requires precise coaxial device alignment, careful catheter manipulation, continuous monitoring of leaflet tension, and meticulous guidance using fluoroscopy and transoesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Importantly, prompt recognition of SLDA by TEE is a prerequisite for this technique. In conclusion, the guide-sheath-assisted retrieval technique can represent a potential bailout strategy for intra-procedural SLDA before full implant release during MTEER.

articles.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

articles.title: Posterior Circulation Stroke From Paradoxical Embolism in a Patient With Patent Foramen Ovale Dislodged During Masturbation.
articles.abstract: Diagnosis of stroke in young and otherwise healthy individuals is rare, but early detection and treatment are crucial to patient outcomes. There may be unusual factors that lead to a presentation of stroke as seen in this case.

articles.title: Chronic Bilateral Knee Pain Following Total Knee Arthroplasty Due to Titanium Allergy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS) is a rare proliferative joint disease that can necessitate total joint arthroplasty. While titanium is widely regarded as a biocompatible material, this case of titanium hypersensitivity introduces an important diagnostic consideration in patients with persistent, unexplained post-operative symptoms.

CASE REPORT: A 46-year-old woman with bilateral PVNS underwent multiple arthroscopies and eventually bilateral total knee arthroplasties in 2012. Despite revision surgeries and a range of pain management interventions, she continued to experience chronic pain, recurrent inflammation, and systemic flares. Imaging and laboratory evaluations failed to show infection or mechanical failure. After multiple inconclusive diagnostic evaluations by orthopedic surgery, rheumatology, and pain management, allergy testing revealed a titanium allergy, providing a definitive diagnosis and shifting her management approach.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the rare but impactful phenomenon of titanium hypersensitivity and emphasizes its role in unexplained arthroplasty failure. Clinicians should consider implant allergies when standard causes have been excluded.

articles.title: Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Emerging Therapeutic Targets.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) represents a leading cause of preventable liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite its growing global burden, no pharmacological therapies targeting disease progression have achieved clinical approval, with management still centered on alcohol abstinence and supportive care. Classic pathogenic mechanisms, including ethanol metabolism, oxidative stress, innate immune activation, and regulated cell death, are well recognized, yet emerging evidence highlights the gut-liver axis and intestinal dysbiosis as critical, interactive drivers of disease pathophysiology. However, how gut microbial imbalance mechanistically intersects with these canonical pathways to accelerate ALD progression remains insufficiently integrated. This article summarizes the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and pathogenesis of ALD. Importantly, we focus specifically on changes in the gut microbiota (including bacteria, fungi, and viruses) and microbial metabolites. We further discuss the interactive relationships between dysbiosis and these core mechanisms. Finally, we summarize progress in preclinical and clinical research on targeted strategies such as probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and phage therapy. By synthesizing the research findings, we propose a stage-based, mechanism-oriented framework aimed at advancing the development of safer and more precise therapeutic interventions for ALD.

articles.title: A Single Smart Nanomaterial for Near-Infrared-Switchable Theranostics of Hemorrhage and Thrombosis via Photoacoustic Imaging.
articles.abstract: The clinical management of hemorrhagic patients remains a significant challenge, as current therapeutic approaches lack real-time diagnostic capability and spatiotemporal precision. Conventional materials (e.g., hydrogels) require surgical intervention, while molecular targeting strategies are limited by slow kinetics and uncontrollable thrombotic risks. To address these limitations, we developed a smart nanomaterial based on a NiFe-layered double hydroxide decorated with both Ag single atoms and nanoparticles (AgSA + NP/NiFe-LDH). This platform can bind plasminogen activators, achieving rapid hemostasis with approximately 30% reduced fibrinolysis in vitro and approximately 50% reduced blood loss in vivo in models of intracranial and abdominal hemorrhage. Under pulsed near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the dominant photoelectric effect enhances hemostatic efficacy, reducing blood loss by about 50% compared to the unexposed part; under sustained NIR exposure, strong photothermal effects inactivate clot-enriched thrombin and alter fibrin structure, thereby promoting controlled thrombolysis. This dual functionality is consistently demonstrated in arterial models and in cryopreserved human blood samples from healthy individuals and hemorrhagic patients. Moreover, the material enables real-time visualization of active bleeding (as low as 3 μL) via photoacoustic imaging, as validated in an intracranial hemorrhage model. Our work demonstrates a proof-of-concept NIR-based strategy for externally modulated management with potential applications in dynamic vascular emergencies.

articles.title: ABCB4 Deficiency Presenting as a Pruritus-Free Continuous Spectrum From Childhood Cholestasis to Adult Cirrhosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 3 (PFIC3) is caused by biallelic mutations in the ABCB4 gene and typically presents in childhood. However, the full phenotypic spectrum-particularly adult-onset and pruritus-free forms-remains under-recognized. We report the case of a 28-year-old male who presented with pruritus-free decompensated cirrhosis after a 10-year diagnostic delay.
