Genetic testing revealed compound heterozygous ABCB4 variants [c.249C>A (p.Asp83Glu) and c.1466A>G (p.Asn489Ser)], which were initially classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Proactive family screening identified his asymptomatic 14-year-old sister, who carried the same genotype and exhibited significant gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) elevation (142.1 U/L) but no pruritus. Perfect genotype-phenotype cosegregation in the two siblings, combined with the absence of these variants in population databases (PM2 and PP1 criteria per American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics [ACMG] guidelines), provided decisive evidence for reclassifying the VUS as "Likely Pathogenic." This family defines a pruritus-free continuous PFIC3 spectrum and demonstrates that systematic screening of all first-degree relatives upon proband diagnosis is essential for enabling pre-symptomatic intervention. The key learning point is that ABCB4 deficiency should be considered in adults with cryptogenic cirrhosis even without pruritus, and family screening can resolve diagnostic uncertainty while facilitating early therapy.

articles.title: Hypoxic Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes Release Large Extracellular Vesicles That Promote a Pro-Inflammatory Phenotype in Macrophages.
articles.abstract: Directly post-infarction, myocardial tissue release signals that trigger an acute inflammatory response to clear debris and initiate cardiac repair. However, prolonged inflammation may drive adverse remodelling and heart failure in the long-term. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms of acute and chronic inflammation after myocardial infarction (MI) is crucial for developing targeted treatments. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate intercellular communication by carrying diverse biomolecules, such as proteins, that influence recipient cell behaviour. Cardiomyocyte-derived EVs (CM-EVs) are known to play a role in both cardiac repair and the progression of heart failure following MI. However, little is known about CM-EV subpopulations and how they modulate post-infarction inflammation. Here, we demonstrate that human CM-EV subpopulations can modulate macrophage phenotype. We identified three EV subpopulations, defined by their sedimentation coefficients, with distinct density and proteome profiles released by human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). The 2K, 10K and 100K pellets, collected by differential ultracentrifugation of the conditioned medium, are enriched, respectively, in sarcomeric components, metabolic proteins and proteins involved in transport to the plasma membrane. Proteomic analysis revealed that hypoxia changes the proteome of EV-containing pellets, enriching for proteins involved in cellular stress responses, such as chaperones, ribosomal, proteasomal and metabolic proteins. Next, we observed that both normoxic and hypoxic CM-EVs are internalized by macrophages, and the hypoxic 10K pellet induces a pro-inflammatory phenotype in these cells. Future research should elucidate whether CM-EVs contribute to excessive inflammation and adverse cardiac remodelling post-MI in vivo and if this can be modulated by blocking the release of specific CM-EV subpopulations.

articles.title: A Shock to the System: Vasopressors for Sepsis in Africa and Beyond.
Noninvasive Sweat Patch Collection of Neuroinjury Biomarkers in Critically Ill Children: A Feasibility Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Critically ill children experience neurologic injury that is associated with specific biomarkers. Monitoring of these biomarkers in this population is limited by invasive sampling methods and single timepoint measurements. We sought to evaluate the feasibility of using a novel noninvasive sweat patch to collect cumulative concentrations of neuroinjury-associated biomarkers over time in the PICU.

DESIGN: Single-center prospective pilot feasibility study conducted across three sequential enrollment cohorts.

SETTING: A tertiary-care PICU.

PATIENTS: Forty-two children admitted to the PICU 5 weeks to 17 years old.

INTERVENTIONS: Sweat patches were placed and worn for 24-96 hours. Sweat samples were analyzed for four neuroinjury-associated biomarkers: glial fibrillary acidic protein, ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1, tau, and neurofilament light chain using single-molecule array assays.

MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: Biomarkers were reported as total cumulative concentrations and concentrations per hour of patch wear. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, safety, protocol adherence, and assay success. All approached families consented, and no patch-related adverse effects were observed. One patch was removed early due to uncertainty regarding MRI compatibility. Adequate sweat volumes required for assay were obtained from all 41 analyzed patches, and biomarker levels were measured successfully in each, with 97% of samples maintaining coefficient of variation (CV) within an acceptable range (< 20%) and 100% of samples within a borderline CV range (< 25%).

CONCLUSIONS: Sweat patch collection of neurologic injury biomarkers was feasible, safe, and acceptable to families in a PICU setting. This minimally invasive method yielded consistently adequate and analyzable volumes in infants through adolescents and may support future studies designed to evaluate the relationship between elements of critical care and neurologic injury in children admitted to the PICU.

articles.title: Pain Management in Elective Orthopaedic Surgery: A Delphi Consensus of the Academic Orthopaedic Consortium.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain management is a critical component of orthopaedic care, aimed at minimizing discomfort, facilitating recovery, and enhancing functional outcomes. The purpose of this study was to establish consensus statements through the Delphi process on pain management from preoperatively to postoperatively at the time of elective orthopaedic sports medicine and arthroplasty surgery.

METHODS: A consensus process using the Delphi technique was conducted. Thirty-seven orthopaedic surgeons, anaesthesiologist pain management physicians, and musculoskeletal researchers participated in these consensus statements. Consensus was defined as achieving 80 to 89% agreement, strong consensus was defined as 90 to 99% agreement, and unanimous consensus was indicated by 100% agreement with a proposed statement.

RESULTS: Of the 40 total questions and consensus statements in this group, four achieved unanimous consensus, 21 achieved strong consensus, 14 achieved consensus, and one did not reach any consensus.

CONCLUSION: The majority of statements reached some degree of consensus, with most achieving at least strong consensus. The statements that achieved unanimous consensus were on preoperative patient counselling for those with opioid addiction risk factors, including preoperative plans, preoperative education, frank discussions on expectations of pain after surgery, and pain management contracts. In addition, unanimous consensus was achieved that practices should have a standard opioid prescribing protocol to minimize prescribing, based on the procedure performed and with a maximum prescribing amount, and regarding the advantages of e-prescribing for opioids. Finally, unanimous consensus was determined that acetaminophen is always indicated, except when there is a medical contraindication such as liver impairment.

articles.title: European Guidelines on Multidisciplinary Management of Obstructed Defecation Syndrome-ESCP, UEG, ESGAR, EAGEN, ESGENA, ESNM and ESPCG.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The goal of this project was to develop a joint European clinical practice guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS), based on the best available evidence. These guidelines are intended to support all healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients with ODS, such as general practitioners, colorectal surgeons, gastroenterologists, gynecologists, radiologists, physiotherapists, and psychologists, as well as to provide accessible information for patients themselves.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary Guideline Development Group representing seven European scientific societies and including patient representatives formulated PICO-based clinical questions. Evidence was identified through a systematic literature review and assessed using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were formulated according to the available evidence and, where evidence was insufficient, as expert opinions.

RESULTS: The final guideline includes 28 statements (1 moderate grade evidence, 2 low grade evidence, 3 very low grade evidence, 22 expert opinion) covering the diagnosis, conservative and surgical management of ODS, including indications for various imaging modalities, functional tests, and both transanal and transabdominal surgical approaches. Multidisciplinary assessment is recommended throughout the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Conservative treatment represents the initial management strategy, with biofeedback recommended before surgery in patients with ODS and dyssynergic defecation who fail dietary and laxative treatment. Surgery should be reserved for selected patients with persistent symptoms after conservative treatment and considered following multidisciplinary pelvic floor evaluation.

CONCLUSION: These multidisciplinary European guidelines offer a comprehensive and evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of ODS. They are intended to promote standardized, high-quality care across Europe and to improve outcomes and quality of life for individuals affected by this complex condition. Given the limited quality of evidence supporting many interventions, individualized decision-making within a multidisciplinary setting remains central to ODS management.

articles.title: The impact of temporal resampling on the safety of clinical reinforcement learning: A simulated trial.
articles.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a type of artificial intelligence for making optimal choices. In healthcare, researchers generally use offline RL (ORL), where models are trained and evaluated from retrospective observational data. To accommodate naturally irregular clinical records, researchers often resample the data into uniform time intervals before training (known as binning). However, binning may create counterfactual trajectories that do not represent clinical practice. We first quantified these distortions in patients receiving continuous insulin infusions in the MIMIC-IV intensive care database. Binning reversed the apparent causal order for over 70% of paired glucose measurements and insulin adjustments within the same interval, and frequently masked significant dysglycaemic events and merged distinct treatment decisions together. We then conducted an in silico clinical trial using 30 virtual patients with type 1 diabetes from the FDA-approved UVA/Padova simulator. The simulator was modified to include stochastic intervals between decisions and used to generate a training dataset for offline RL. We trained three ORL algorithms on both the unprocessed dataset and equivalent datasets resampled at 10-minute, 2-hour, and 4-hour intervals. When deployed back into the simulated environment, temporal resampling was found to reduce model performance by up to 60% relative to unprocessed data, with 4-hour binning causing all agents to perform worse than the dataset's baseline. Retrospective evaluation on resampled data actively obscured this effect, predicting 1.5-3x better returns than agents achieved in practice. We recommend that future research in this area prioritises datasets with natural clinical timings between decisions, which may be a necessary step before these models can be safely deployed into patient care.

articles.title: The state of leprosy: increasing trends of Hansen's disease in Florida, USA, 1996-2025.
articles.abstract: Leprosy, also known as Hansen´s disease (HD), is a chronic infectious disease which mainly affects the skin, the peripheral nerves, mucosa of the upper respiratory tract, and the eyes. According to the National Hansen's Disease Program (NHDP), there were 225 new cases of leprosy reported in the United States of America (USA) in 2023, with Florida ranking as one of the top reporting states. Using publicly available data, we analysed the overall trend of leprosy in Florida from 1996-2025. A total of 359 confirmed cases of leprosy was reported in the state during the study period. The annual incidence rate increased from 0.01 per 100,000 population to 0.15 per 100,000 population, showing a fifteen-fold increase over the 30-year study period. With a total of 113 cases reported for the study duration, Brevard County was observed to be a hotspot for confirmed leprosy cases and locally acquired infections represented the largest category of cases with known acquisition mode.

articles.title: Multidrug therapy does not eliminate the risk of ocular disability in leprosy.
articles.abstract: Whilst multidrug therapy can provide a microbiological cure for leprosy infection, it does not reverse nerve damage that is already established, nor remove the risk of the occurrence of future ocular complications. Ocular conditions associated with leprosy such as lagophthalmos, reduced corneal sensation, exposure keratopathy, uveitis and other sight and eye threatening conditions may be present at diagnosis, develop during treatment, or even progress long after treatment has already been completed. Existing guidance already recommends eye assessment during treatment, but continuity after treatment varies between settings. This viewpoint therefore argues for implementing these recommendations through a minimum pathway which links assessment during treatment to risk-stratified follow-up after treatment completion, clear referral responsibilities, supported self-care and monitoring, and routine assessment of visual outcomes in paper or electronic records. To be successful these measures should be integrated within existing leprosy, primary-care and eye-care services, with links to non-communicable disease programmes where these can support long-term care. Achieving zero disability due to leprosy requires recognising that treatment completion is not the end of ocular risk.

articles.title: Coronary artery disease and cardiac pathology in cerebral small vessel disease and post-stroke dementia: Implications for Alzheimer's disease.
articles.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationships between coronary or cardiac pathology, cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), Alzheimer's disease pathology, and vascular cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID) remain unclear.

METHODS: We performed a clinicopathological study in 75 stroke patients enrolled in the prospective Cognitive Function After Stroke (CogFAST) cohort. Comprehensive histopathological examination was performed to characterize the spectrum of pathologies in samples of the main coronary arteries (CorA), and cardiac and brain tissues from stroke survivors diagnosed with post-stroke dementia (PSD; mean age, standard deviation, range, % sex; 88 ± 8 years, 65-99, 55% female) or without dementia (PSND; 86 ± 4 years, 79-94, 45% female).

RESULTS: All subjects exhibited occult or obstructive CorA disease with > 50% clinically defined stenosis in at least one of the main coronary arteries. Linear correlation analysis showed that CorA stenosis was positively related to internal carotid artery stenosis (P < 0.03). CorA stenosis was not associated with pathological measures of cerebral SVD per se or neurodegenerative disorders. Cardiac pathology was highly prevalent, with ≈ 80% of the subjects having at least one feature of cardiac pathology including fibrosis, disarray, and myocyte damage and 62% exhibiting myocardial infarcts. CorA stenosis was associated with higher cardiac pathology score, which was also related to cardiac sympathetic denervation and α-synuclein accumulation in the stellate ganglia. We noted low heart weights (P < 0.001), greater myocardial infarcts (P < 0.001), and greater general cardiac atrophy (P = 0.024) in the PSD compared to the PSND group.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest there is a relationship between CorA disease and carotid artery disease and that cardiac pathology in elderly stroke survivors may be a factor in the development of delayed dementia after the stroke injury and VCID.

articles.title: Secondary Pasteurella multocida Infection Complicating Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis During Dupilumab Therapy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report the case of a 54-year-old woman with asthma, eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis, eosinophilic gastroenteritis and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA). She had long-term cat exposure and received low-dose prednisolone. Chest computed tomography showed mucus plugging in the right middle and left upper lobes, and laboratory findings showed eosinophilia, elevated serum immunoglobulin E (IgE), and positive Aspergillus-specific IgE and IgG. Following initiation of dupilumab to minimize systemic corticosteroid exposure, ABPA, sinonasal disease and lung function improved. Fourteen months later, a new opacity appeared in a bronchiectatic lesion of the right middle lobe, raising concern for ABPA relapse. Bronchoscopy revealed purulent secretions, and Pasteurella multocida (P. multocida) was isolated from bronchoscopic specimens, supporting secondary bacterial infection. The infection improved with antimicrobial therapy. Dupilumab was continued, and oral corticosteroids were eventually discontinued without recurrence of infection. This case highlights the importance of distinguishing secondary infection from ABPA relapse when new opacities develop during biologic therapy.

articles.title: Biomarker Testing, Imaging, and Outcomes in Cardiology-Referred Acute Breathlessness: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
articles.abstract: Background Breathlessness is a leading cause of emergency hospital attendances, and its multifactorial nature often reflects overlapping cardiopulmonary pathologies such as pulmonary embolism (PE), heart failure (HF), and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is frequently used, often without documented pretest probability assessments. This audit primarily assessed the diagnostic yield of CTPA for suspected PE against the Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standard of ≥15% and secondarily described biomarker testing, imaging, and outcomes across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways in patients referred to cardiology with acute breathlessness. Methods We conducted a retrospective audit of 70 adults referred to cardiology with breathlessness through the electronic patient record or multiprofessional team list (MPTL) referral systems at a district general hospital in the United Kingdom between March 1 and June 30, 2025. Biomarker testing for D-dimer, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hs-TnI), together with imaging and outcomes, was reviewed and described across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways, with diagnostic yields restricted to CTPA for suspected PE and coronary angiography for suspected ACS. Yields were reported with Wilson 95% CIs and compared using exploratory Fisher's exact tests. Additional analyses examined biomarker concentrations by outcome and overlap in biomarker and imaging use. Results Seventy patients were included (median age, 69.5 years; 52.9% male). D-dimer, NT-proBNP, and hs-TnI were tested in 68.6%, 58.6%, and 81.4% of patients, respectively. Overall, seven of 54 CTPAs performed for suspected PE were positive (13.0%, 95% CI, 6.4-24.4), numerically below the RCR benchmark of ≥15%. A clinically relevant alternative diagnosis was reported in 44.4% (target, ≥50%), and pretest probability was documented in 22.2% (target, 100%). PE yield was 15.0% (6/40) among patients with an elevated D-dimer, 0% (0/4) among those with a normal D-dimer, and 10.0% (1/10) among those without D-dimer testing (p = 1.000 for both comparisons). Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) was found on transthoracic echocardiography in 40.0% (8/20) of patients with elevated NT-proBNP, 23.1% (3/13) of those with non-elevated NT-proBNP, and 26.3% (5/19) of those without testing (p = 0.456 and p = 0.501, respectively). Of 47 patients with elevated hs-TnI, 10 (21.3%) underwent coronary angiography for suspected ACS, with percutaneous coronary intervention performed in four (40.0%). Overall, 29 of 57 patients tested (50.9%) had hs-TnI levels above the sex-specific 99th-percentile upper reference limit. Conclusions Cardiology-referred breathlessness frequently involved multiple biomarker and imaging pathways during the same admission. CTPA yield, alternative diagnosis rates, and pretest probability documentation fell below RCR standards. LVSD was more frequent with elevated NT-proBNP, although differences were not statistically significant. No hs-TnI comparison was possible because all patients undergoing angiography for suspected ACS had elevated levels. Given the small, single-center sample and selective imaging, these findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy or pathway effectiveness. Larger multicenter studies are needed. The findings support reviewing pretest probability documentation and investigation decisions, followed by reaudit against RCR standards.

articles.title: Management of advanced mycosis fungoides and Sézary Syndrome: International Recommendations for systemic treatments and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation from the European Hematology Association, the EORTC Cutaneous Lymphoma Tumours Group, the International Society for Cutaneous Lymphoma, and the Lymphoma Working Party of the EBMT.
articles.abstract: Advanced mycosis fungoides (MF) and Sézary syndrome (SS) are the most aggressive forms of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and remain associated with a poor prognosis and heterogeneous therapeutic approaches. Recent advances, including targeted therapies and improved transplant strategies, have substantially expanded treatment options, highlighting the need for updated international guidance integrating dermatologic, hematologic, and transplant perspectives. An international multidisciplinary panel convened by the European Hematology Association (EHA), the EORTC Cutaneous Lymphoma Tumours Group (EORTC-CLTG), the International Society for Cutaneous Lymphoma (ISCL), and the EBMT Lymphoma Working Party reviewed the available evidence and developed consensus recommendations for the management of advanced MF and SS. Thirty international experts participated in the process. Recommendations address diagnostic work-up, systemic therapies, treatment sequencing, combination strategies, and indications for allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT). The consensus supports a stage-adapted and compartment-oriented therapeutic approach. Immunomodulatory strategies remain central in advanced CTCL: extracorporeal photopheresis is commonly used as first-line therapy in SS and in patients with significant blood involvement, while interferon-α and retinoids are widely used in MF, often in combination with skin-directed therapies. Mogamulizumab and brentuximab vedotin represent key options after prior systemic therapy, with differential activity across skin, blood, and nodal compartments. Combination approaches integrating systemic and skin-directed treatments may improve response depth and durability. Practical treatment algorithms for advanced MF and SS are proposed to support therapeutic sequencing and multidisciplinary management. Allo-HCT remains the only potentially curative treatment and should be considered early in selected patients with high-risk disease features.

articles.title: Late coronary artery perforation with subsequent cardiac tamponade 3 days after primary percutaneous coronary intervention in a young woman with spontaneous coronary artery dissection-induced ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an important cause of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), which affects young women. Treatment with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is indicated in clinically and haemodynamically unstable patients. Late coronary artery perforation (CAP) is an uncommon, but potentially fatal complication of a PCI that can occur 30 min to 9 days after the procedure.

CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old woman was admitted to our hospital with STEMI. Coronarography showed a type 2A SCAD of the LAD. We proceeded with PCI-stenting and the result appeared optimal. After 3 days of uneventful postinterventional stay, the patient became hypotensive and clinically unstable, with echocardiography revealing a cardiac tamponade. We performed an urgent pericardiocentesis and coronarography, detecting a type 3 coronary artery perforation of the LAD in-stent, which we covered with a graft stent. Following the intervention, the patient had pericardial inflammation for the next month with intermittent fever and persisting pericardial effusion. After administering Colchicine for 3 months, the effusion completely subsided, with control echocardiographies showing normal pericardium.

DISCUSSION: PCI in patients with SCAD-induced STEMI can be challenging and has a risk of complications. Late CAP is a rare complication that can easily be overlooked, especially when we think that the result of the intervention was optimal. In our case, we think that the cause of CAP is the post-dilatation with a high-pressure non-compliant balloon. The goal of this case report is to remind us of the possibility of CAP even if three days have passed following the procedure.

articles.title: Danon disease due to a de novo LAMP2 variant in a girl with d-transposition of the great arteries and a maternally inherited GDF1 variant: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Danon disease, caused by loss-of-function variants in LAMP2, is an X-linked cardioskeletal disorder with cardiac manifestations in heterozygous females that are often underrecognized. The co-occurrence of surgically corrected dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) and subsequent Danon cardiomyopathy in a patient carrying a maternally inherited GDF1 variant of uncertain significance has not previously been reported.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a girl with d-TGA repaired in the neonatal period who later presented at 12 years of age with progressive dyspnoea on exertion (New York Heart Association class III). She was found to have severe left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), biventricular outflow tract obstruction, myocardial fibrosis, and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia on ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring. Whole-exome sequencing revealed a de novo pathogenic LAMP2 variant, c.98del (p.Leu33Ter), predicted to disrupt all LAMP2 isoforms, establishing the diagnosis of Danon disease. A maternally inherited GDF1 in-frame deletion, c.651_656del (p.Ala218_Leu219del), was also identified and classified as a variant of uncertain significance; while its clinical significance remains unresolved, it is biologically plausible that the GDF1 variant may have contributed to the congenital heart disease substrate.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights two mechanistically distinct genetic events operating across different developmental windows: a likely susceptibility allele for congenital heart disease and a de novo lysosomal cardiomyopathy causing Danon disease. In patients with repaired congenital heart disease who subsequently develop an otherwise unexplained hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) phenotype, comprehensive cardiomyopathy-focused genetic evaluation may reveal a second diagnosis with major prognostic, therapeutic, and family-screening implications.

articles.title: Long IVUS-attenuated plaque without no-reflow: histological findings of captured embolic debris and implications for the interpretation of IVUS attenuation: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The no-reflow phenomenon during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is commonly associated with distal embolization from high-risk coronary plaques, including lesions with intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-defined attenuation. Histopathological analysis of embolic debris captured during PCI is rarely reported and may provide additional insights into the relationship between plaque characteristics and coronary flow outcomes.

CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man presented with acute coronary syndrome and decompensated heart failure. Coronary angiography demonstrated severe multi-vessel coronary artery disease, including a long right coronary artery lesion with extensive IVUS attenuation. Given the high risk of distal embolization, PCI was performed using a distal protection device. Drug-eluting stents were successfully implanted, and Thrombolysis In Myocardial Infarction flow grade 3 was maintained throughout the procedure without slow flow or no reflow. Histopathological examination of debris captured by the distal protection device demonstrated predominantly fibrin- and collagen-rich thrombotic material with macrophage infiltration and no apparent abundant lipid component. The patient experienced an uneventful recovery and was discharged without procedural complications.

DISCUSSION: The composition of retrieved embolic debris captured during PCI differed from the expected imaging phenotype. This case highlights the potential discrepancy between intracoronary imaging appearance and embolized material and underscores the multifactorial nature of coronary slow flow and no reflow. Careful interpretation of IVUS attenuation and embolic pathology is warranted when assessing procedural risk.

articles.title: Right mainstem intubation improves transoesophageal echocardiographic guidance during mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
Left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy in a dextrocardia patient: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mirror-image dextrocardia presents unique challenges for cardiac device implantation. Here, we report a case of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) for a patient with dextrocardia and heart failure with mid-range ejection fraction (HFmrEF).

CASE SUMMARY: A 69-year-old woman with mirror-image dextrocardia was electively admitted to our hospital with a complaint of chest distress and shortness of breath. Twenty-four-hour Holter showed sinus arrest with junctional rhythm, intermittent first-degree atrioventricular block with complete left bundle branch block (QRS 154 ms). Echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 46%. In contrast to previous research utilizing the modified C315 sheath, the LOT-CRT implant was successfully achieved using a standard-curve C315 delivery sheath. At the 9-month follow-up, the patient demonstrated a significant improvement in LVEF compared with baseline (60% vs. 46%).

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates the clinical viability of LOT-CRT as a physiologic pacing strategy in patients with congenital heart disease. By directly targeting the conduction system, this approach may circumvent the anatomical challenges posed by traditional biventricular pacing in complex cardiac anatomies, offering a promising therapeutic alternative for resynchronization in select populations.

articles.title: Non-atrial/non-ventricular functional tricuspid valve regurgitation: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional tricuspid regurgitation (fTR) is usually caused by annular dilation and leaflet tethering secondary to right atrial (RA) or right ventricular (RV) remodelling. Rarely, extrinsic factors may impair annular motion.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a 83-year-old woman with constrictive pericarditis who presented with right-sided heart failure and moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Multimodality imaging revealed a thickened pericardium, preserved RA and RV size, and a non-dilated, saddle-shaped annulus with markedly reduced motion. Following pericardiectomy, tricuspid annular mobility normalized, right-sided pressures decreased, and TR improved from moderate to mild. We introduce the term non-atrial/non-ventricular functional tricuspid regurgitation to describe this rare mechanism of isolated annular dysfunction caused by pericardial tethering.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights a novel, distinct, and reversible form of fTR caused by pericardial constraint rather than chamber remodelling. We propose the term non-atrial/non-ventricular fTR to describe this mechanism. Recognizing this entity may guide surgical decision-making and avoid unnecessary tricuspid valve intervention.

articles.title: A transformer-based deep learning model for predicting the use of atherectomy devices during PCI from preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), often necessitating atherectomy-based debulking devices that increase procedural complexity and risk. We aimed to develop and externally validate a Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) to predict atherectomy device use during PCI and compare its performance with that of blinded human readers, including general cardiologists and PCI experts.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective multicentre study included 498 calcified coronary lesions from 419 patients who underwent PCI after preprocedural CCTA. Data from 12 institutions were used for training and validation with four-fold cross-validation, and data from two independent institutions (97 lesions) served as an external test cohort. The model combined a convolutional neural network feature extractor with Transformer-based multiple instance learning, and clinical variables were evaluated for incremental value. In the external test cohort, the CCTA-only model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.788 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.691-0.873) for predicting atherectomy device use. Adding clinical variables resulted in an AUC of 0.805 (95% CI, 0.713-0.886), indicating limited incremental value. In the reader comparison, the model showed higher accuracy than general cardiologists (0.742 vs. 0.619; P = 0.029) and numerically similar accuracy to PCI experts (0.742 vs. 0.670; P = 0.230).

CONCLUSION: A Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural CCTA showed clinically relevant performance for predicting atherectomy device use during PCI in an independent external test cohort. These findings suggest that the model may support lesion assessment and procedural planning.

articles.title: Genotype and Phenotype Description in Individuals With GYG1 Variants-A Case Report and Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Glycogen Storage Disease Type XV (GSD XV) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in GYG1, encoding glycogenin-1. Although primarily a myopathic disease, cardiac involvement is increasingly recognized and overlapping features with other neuromuscular disorders contribute to underdiagnosis. We performed a systematic search of databases without restrictions on publication dates. Twenty-one articles describing individuals with GSD XV were included, providing clinical, histological, and genetic data. In addition to the systematic review, we present an illustrative case of GSD XV diagnosed at our institution. We identified 49 individuals, of whom 98% were symptomatic with onset ranging from childhood to late adulthood; manifestations were isolated neuromuscular (81.6%), cardiac (8.2%), or mixed (8.2%). One case (2.0%) was asymptomatic. Among neuromuscular cases, 12% required a walking aid, while four cardiac patients required implantable cardioverter-defibrillators and two underwent heart transplantation. Muscle biopsy frequently revealed PAS-positive, diastase-resistant polyglucosan bodies, although polyglucosan bodies were not consistently identified by electron microscopy. Molecular diagnosis was confirmed in all cases, with c.143+3G>C in GYG1 being the most prevalent variant, homozygous in 36.7% of patients and associated with both juvenile and adult-onset phenotypes. GSD XV should be considered in cases with unexplained myopathy or cardiomyopathy, regardless of age at onset. Genetic testing remains the gold standard for diagnosis, although muscle biopsy can guide investigations, particularly in atypical cases or when genetic analysis is inconclusive. Further studies are needed to clarify the full clinical spectrum, refine genotype-phenotype correlations, and guide long-term management strategies.

articles.title: Phenytoin Toxicity Presenting With Ataxia and Nystagmus: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Phenytoin has a narrow therapeutic window, and elderly patients with multiple comorbidities are more susceptible to developing toxicity. This report details a patient who developed cerebellar symptoms during admission. Elevated phenytoin levels were identified and were higher still when corrected for low serum albumin. Structural, central infective, and epileptic causes were excluded. Despite repeated dose adjustments, therapeutic levels could not be maintained. Establishing therapeutic levels may have been further complicated by declining renal function and concurrent infection, and phenobarbitone levels were also supratherapeutic. He deteriorated and subsequently died. This case highlights the need for early phenytoin level monitoring when toxicity is suspected, particularly in frail patients with hypoalbuminemia, renal impairment, or acute illness, where dose titration is challenging.

articles.title: Circulating extracellular vesicle-enriched fraction in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and incident cancer.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Previous studies found increased cancer incidence in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). We sought to explore the biological correlates of the association of HFrEF with cancer in humans.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Among participants in the Gruppo Italiano per lo Studio della Sopravvivenza nell'Insufficienza Cardiaca-Heart Failure (GISSI-HF) trial with HFrEF and available baseline plasma samples, we selected those who developed solid cancer (cases) and matched them with controls without cancer by age, sex, New York Heart Association class, and follow-up duration. We isolated the plasma extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction, in which EVs were confirmed by western blot for CD9, FLOTILLIN-1, ALIX, and TSG101, and by nanoparticle tracking analysis (mean particle diameter <200 nm). The protein content of EV preparations was characterized by nanoliquid chromatography-high=resolution tandem mass spectrometry. Of the 940 identified proteins, 148 were differentially expressed between EV preparations from cases (EVs-cases) and controls (EVs-controls) and were related to biological functions implicated in cancer growth, particularly apoptosis and spliceosome/transcriptome regulation. Next, we explored the effects of EVs-cases and EVs-controls in MCF7 breast cancer cells and ran confirmatory experiments with another two cell lines, HCT116 (colon) and A549 (lung). Apoptosis, as determined by caspase 3 cleavage, was blunted by EVs-cases in MCF7, but not in HCT116 and A549 cells. Screening qPCR identified NR3C1, encoding the glucocorticoid receptor, as a spliceosome/transcription modulator affected by EVs-cases. Targeted qPCR confirmed that it was reduced by EVs-cases in A549 cells.

CONCLUSION: Circulating EV-enriched fractions from patients with HFrEF and incident cancer have a distinct proteomic signature and might modulate human cancer cell biology.

articles.title: Successful ablation of lower loop re-entry after Starnes procedure in an infant with severe tricuspid valve dysplasia: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tricuspid valve dysplasia (TVD) is a rare right-sided congenital heart disease characterized by severe tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial enlargement, which may predispose to atrial arrhythmias. In severe neonatal cases, the Starnes procedure can be life-saving, but postoperative anatomical alterations may complicate subsequent arrhythmia management.

CASE SUMMARY: A 2-month-old female infant with TVD and pulmonary atresia developed drug-refractory atypical atrial flutter after the Starnes procedure. Three-dimensional electroanatomical mapping identified lower loop re-entry involving the cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI). Radiofrequency catheter ablation across the CTI successfully terminated the tachycardia. However, atypical flutter recurred 1 week later. During subsequent systemic pulmonary shunt surgery, additional surgical ablation was performed using the prior catheter ablation site as an anatomical landmark. After detaching the tricuspid valve patch, the CTI line was extended to the tricuspid annulus, resulting in complete arrhythmia control.

DISCUSSION: The outcome of this case suggests that foetal-onset volume overload from severe tricuspid regurgitation may promote early atrial remodelling and arrhythmogenic substrate formation in TVD. Although CTI ablation after the Starnes procedure may be feasible in a small infant, patch-related anatomic barriers may prevent complete lesion formation. Prior catheter ablation sites may be useful intraoperative landmarks for successful surgical ablation.

articles.title: Angina in the young: a right coronary artery malignant course-a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery anomalies are rare congenital defects that often remain undetected due to their asymptomatic nature. However, in certain cases, they represent an important cause of sudden cardiac death, particularly among younger individuals with low to intermediate risk factors for coronary artery disease.

CASE SUMMARY: We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented to the cardiology outpatient clinic with intermittent typical anginal chest pain. Despite having a low-to-moderate risk profile for ischaemic heart disease, limited to well-controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia, further evaluation with computed tomographic coronary angiography revealed an anomalous right coronary artery originating from the left coronary sinus with a malignant course. An exercise stress echocardiogram demonstrated ischaemic electrocardiographic changes in the absence of physical symptoms. Her cardiovascular risk factors were managed with medications; however, due to evidence of inducible ischaemia, she was referred to a tertiary adult congenital heart disease centre for ongoing surveillance and consideration of appropriately timed surgical intervention.

CONCLUSION: Although rare, anomalous coronary artery disease may represent a significant cause of angina in younger patients. A thorough clinical history remains essential in identifying this condition and facilitating potentially life-saving management.

articles.title: Posttraumatic Stress Symptoms, Buffering Resources, and Avoidant Coping Strategies in Patients With Cirrhosis: A Latent Class Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify latent classes of posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS), buffering resources (social support and sense of control), and avoidant coping strategies among patients with cirrhosis, and to examine demographic and clinical factors associated with class membership.

METHODS: From October 2024 to May 2025, patients with cirrhosis were recruited by convenience sampling from a tertiary hospital in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Participants completed the Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS), PTSD Checklist-Civilian Version (PCL-C), Spheres of Control Scale (SCS), and Self-Report Coping Scale (SRCS). Latent class analysis was used to identify subgroups, followed by multinomial logistic regression to examine associated factors.

RESULTS: A total of 316 patients were included. Mean scores were 60.78 ± 16.00 for social support, 30.67 ± 11.99 for PTSS, 48.42 ± 12.07 for sense of control, and 29.53 ± 9.26 for avoidant coping. Three latent classes were identified: the Buffering Type-Low Avoidance/Symptoms Group (64.2%), the Buffering Deficiency- Symptoms/Avoidance Dilemma Group (7.5%), and the Avoidant Coping-Symptoms Dilemma Group (28.2%). In the pooled adjusted model, decompensated cirrhosis differentiated Class 2 from Class 1, while unmarried status, monthly income < 5000 RMB, unemployment, and decompensated cirrhosis differentiated Class 3 from Class 1. Although gender differed across classes in univariate analysis, the adjusted C1-versus-C3 gender effect was not statistically significant (OR = 0.780, 95% CI 0.365-1.667, p = 0.523). Because Class 2 contained only 24 participants, estimates involving this class should be interpreted cautiously.

CONCLUSION: Patients with cirrhosis showed heterogeneous profiles of PTSS, buffering resources, and avoidant coping. Disease stage and selected social and economic characteristics were associated with class membership. The small Class 2 should be considered a provisional profile requiring replication before firm class-specific clinical conclusions are drawn.

articles.title: Clinical Phenotype and Outcomes of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children According to SARS-CoV-2 Laboratory Status During 2020-2021: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) is a post-infectious inflammatory condition associated with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) that can affect multiple organ systems. Data comparing clinical features and outcomes between MIS-C patients with and without laboratory evidence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain limited.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study was conducted at Mofid Children's Hospital, a pediatric referral center in Tehran, Iran, between March 2020 and July 2021. Children diagnosed with MIS-C based on World Health Organization (WHO) criteria were included and classified into groups with and without laboratory evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection according to PCR and/or IgG serology results. Demographic data, clinical manifestations, laboratory and imaging findings, treatments, and outcomes were compared between the groups using univariate and multivariable analyses. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: A total of 121 patients with MIS-C were included, of whom 44 (36.4%) had laboratory evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The mean age was 4.74 ± 3.99 years, and 61.2% were male. ICU admission occurred in 21.5% and mortality was 2.5%. In univariate analysis, fever during the first 24 h of hospitalization and antiviral use were more frequent in the group with laboratory evidence, whereas conjunctivitis and elevated C-reactive protein levels were more common among the group without laboratory evidence; however, CRP did not differ significantly between groups when analyzed as a continuous variable. In multivariable analysis, fever during the first 24 h of hospitalization was the only variable associated with laboratory evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection (aOR 2.57; 95% CI 1.05-6.30; p = 0.040).

CONCLUSION: MIS-C presents with broad and largely overlapping clinical, laboratory, and imaging features regardless of SARS-CoV-2 laboratory status, and the few observed differences were exploratory and of limited discriminative value. These findings highlight the importance of considering MIS-C even in the absence of laboratory confirmation of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

articles.title: Association of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A +936 C/T Polymorphism With Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in a Bangladeshi Population: A Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) ranges from hepatic steatosis to advanced cirrhosis. Polymorphisms in the vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) gene can change its expression, potentially altering angiogenesis and advancing disease stage. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the VEGFA +936 C/T polymorphism and susceptibility to NAFLD in a Bangladeshi population.

METHODS: A case-control study was conducted including 100 NAFLD patients and 100 controls. NAFLD was diagnosed by ultrasonography. Genotyping was performed using allele-specific polymerase chain reaction followed by gel electrophoresis. Biochemical parameters were measured using standard enzymatic methods following the manufacturer's instructions.

RESULTS: The frequency of the T allele was significantly higher in NAFLD patients compared to controls (22.5% vs. 12%). The control genotype distribution was consistent with Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (χ 2 = 0.2812, p = 0.60). The Cochran-Armitage trend test indicated an association between increasing T-allele dosage and NAFLD (Z = 2.68, p = 0.007). In logistic regression, the T-allele was associated with NAFLD in the crude additive model (OR = 2.05, 95% CI: 1.20-3.51, p = 0.009) and after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and fasting blood glucose (OR = 2.14, 95% CI: 1.13-4.08, p = 0.02). Under the dominant model, the association remained significant in both crude (OR = 2.27, 95% CI: 1.22-4.22, p = 0.01) and adjusted analyses (OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.18-5.33, p = 0.02). NAFLD patients showed significantly higher blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, ALT, and AST, with lower HDL, while body mass index didn't differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated a significant association between the VEGFA +936 C/T polymorphism and susceptibility to NAFLD in a Bangladeshi population. However, due to the small sample size and limited number of TT individuals, further large-scale and functional studies are required to validate these findings.

articles.title: Lung Cancer Screening Recommendations in the Elderly: International Society for Geriatric Oncology Consensus Statement.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Current or former smokers with a 20-pack-year history between the ages of 50 and 80 years are eligible for lung cancer screening (LCS) under current guidelines. Despite age restrictions for screening, older patients remain at risk for lung cancer and, without screening, are diagnosed with advanced-stage disease that limits curative treatment options.Treatment for early-stage lung cancer has improved with minimally invasive surgical techniques and reduced toxicity associated with stereotactic body radiation therapy. Robust older patients can tolerate surgical resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy with rates of recovery similar to those of their younger peers. Given the advancements in treatment and the improved tools available to identify frailty, chronological age should not be a gatekeeper for LCS.

METHODS: A taskforce within the International Society of Geriatric Oncology was created to address challenges of LCS within older patients. Taskforce members represented five different specialties with clinical expertise in lung cancer and the care of older adults.

RESULTS: For patients above 80 years old who qualify for LCS, we recommend performing a geriatric assessment (GA) to assess functional status and age-related vulnerabilities. Robust patients, as determined by GA, should be eligible for screening and discuss their health care priorities in shared decision-making conversations. GA should be performed every 2 years while patients are enrolled in LCS to determine the appropriateness of continued screening efforts.

CONCLUSIONS: Age should not be an exclusion criterion for LCS. Patients above 80 years old should be thoughtfully co-managed by geriatric and lung cancer specialists to determine which older patients would benefit from screening efforts.

articles.title: Prostate cancer screening beyond opportunistic testing: A Delphi consensus and evidence integration.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prostate cancer has become the most common male malignancy in Korea, yet prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based screening remains excluded from the national cancer screening program and is performed predominantly on an opportunistic basis. Long-term randomized evidence comparing organized PSA-based screening with opportunistic testing is complex and variably interpreted. This study aimed to assess expert consensus on whether an organized early-detection framework offers advantages over the current opportunistic model in Korea.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured, three-round Delphi study was conducted among 15 Korean urologists with expertise in prostate cancer management and PSA-based early detection. Statements were informed by international guidelines, long-term randomized trial evidence, and Korean epidemiologic data, covering conceptual justification and screening parameters. Consensus was predefined using Likert-scale agreement/disagreement thresholds and a within-group agreement index (rwg ≥0.80).

RESULTS: All panelists completed all three rounds. Consensus was achieved that PSA-based early detection provides a net population-level benefit; that organized, invitation-based screening is preferable to opportunistic testing; and that active surveillance should be the default for low-risk disease. Initiation at age 55 reached stable consensus, whereas discontinuation at age 80 reached consensus only in the final round, indicating an upper bound within an individualized 75- to 80-year stopping range. No fixed screening interval achieved sustained agreement, supporting risk-adapted approaches.

CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi study supports the feasibility of an organized, risk-adapted PSA-based early detection framework in Korea. Subsequent multidisciplinary input from preventive medicine, primary care, health economics, and patient perspectives is required before policy implementation.

articles.title: Diagnosis and Management of Achalasia in Children, BSPGHAN and BAPS Consensus Statement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achalasia is a rare but significant esophageal motility disorder in children, characterized by impaired lower esophageal sphincter relaxation and absent peristalsis, with incidence up to 0.43 children per 100,000 annually in the United Kingdom. International guidelines exist for adults but there are no pediatric-specific clinical guidelines.

AIM: To produce the first pediatric consensus recommendation on the diagnosis and management of achalasia in children.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: An expert panel from the British Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (BSPGHAN) Motility and Endoscopy Working Groups and the British Association of Pediatric Surgeons (BAPS) was formed and used a modified Delphi process to formulate and vote on 21 consensus recommendations spanning diagnosis, treatment, follow-up, transition to adult care, and research priorities.

RESULTS: A systematic review included 121 pediatric studies (low quality evidence) and a consensus was reached in 21 recommendations (> 80% agreement).

DISCUSSION: Key recommendations include the use of high-resolution manometry as the primary diagnostic investigation, with timed barium oesophagogram and endoscopy as complementary modalities. Both peroral endoscopic myotomy and laparoscopic Heller's myotomy are recommended as first-line definitive treatments, with the choice guided by achalasia subtype, center expertise, and family preference. Structured transition to adult services and long-term surveillance are strongly endorsed.

CONCLUSION: These recommendations aim to standardize clinical practice, improve outcomes, and drive collaborative research in pediatric achalasia.

articles.title: Beyond Consensus: Translating the APLAR Reproductive Rheumatology Recommendations Into Measurable Care Across the Asia-Pacific Region.
BMP3: a new kid on the block in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Targeting neutrophilic inflammation in COPD: rethinking, refining and reprogramming.
International Multiprofessional Expert Consensus on Acute Minor Wounds: A Practical Decision Framework.
articles.abstract: Acute minor wounds are among the most common injuries encountered in daily life, affecting individuals of all ages and frequently managed in home, pharmacy and primary care settings. Despite their high prevalence and potential for preventable complications, most recommendations focus on chronic or complex wounds, leaving a gap in practical, evidence-informed guidance for acute minor wounds. This international consensus convened wound care professionals from four continents to develop a pragmatic framework for assessing and managing acute minor wounds across community settings. Based on a structured literature review and a modified e-Delphi process, the panel produced statements and operational decision tools to support triage, self-management, reassessment and referral. The consensus delineates boundaries between simple and complex wounds according to depth, contamination, anatomical location, host factors and expected healing trajectory; identifies red flags for escalation; and uses 10 common wound types as practical anchors. Core principles include haemorrhage control, cleansing, protection, moisture balance, tetanus assessment, infection prevention and communication with people with wounds. This consensus provides a practical and internationally adaptable guide for the safer management of acute minor wounds, aiming to reduce avoidable complications, delays in escalation and unnecessary healthcare utilization.

articles.title: [Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Coronary Arteritis Induced by Myeloproliferative Neoplasms:Report of a Case].
articles.journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
articles.abstract: In a 60-year-old man with a history of stroke, coronary angiography revealed triple vessel disease, comprising left anterior descending artery (LAD) #6-7 with 99% diffuse stenosis within the stent, #11 and #12 with 90% stenosis, and right coronary artery (RCA) #1 stent with 50% stenosis. Cardiac ultrasonography showed 34% left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) without mitral regurgitation (MR) or tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Following median sternotomy, the bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) was harvested by skeletonization;however, dissection was confirmed at the distal end of the right internal thoracic artery (RITA). Owing to severe apical adhesions, we decided to perform on-pump beating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for this patient. Cardiopulmonary bypass was initiated via proximal aortic arch inflow and bicaval drainage without left ventricule (LV) venting. Subsequently, a left internal thoracic surgery (LITA)-free RITA composite Y-graft was prepared. On-pump beating CABG was performed in the graft design of the LITA-LAD (onlay patch, 4.5 cm), LITA-free RITA composite Y-graft to the obtuse marginal (OM) artery, and AO-saphenous vein graft (SVG)-4 posterior descending artery (PD)-4AV by sequential anastomosis. Many inflammatory cells invaded the RITA and coronary artery, and distal vessel thickening was confirmed but not in the ascending aorta. Coronary arteritis induced by myeloproliferative neoplasms was diagnosed based on pathology. Coronary computed tomography (CT) revealed the patency of all grafts.

articles.title: [Efficacy of Inhaled Nitric Oxide Therapy During the Perioperative Period of Cardiac and Aortic Surgery:a Four-case Report Featuring Reactive and Prophylactic Initiation Strategies].
articles.journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
articles.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that reduces pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) without compromising systemic blood pressure, making it useful in perioperative management during cardiac and aortic surgery. We report four cases in which iNO was administered either therapeutically or prophylactically according to intraoperative or postoperative hemodynamic and respiratory conditions. Therapeutic use improved pulmonary artery pressure and oxygenation during cardiopulmonary bypass weaning and extubation. Prophylactic administration before separation from cardiopulmonary bypass was effective in a patient with severe preoperative pulmonary hypertension, allowing stable weaning. iNO also contributed to hemodynamic and oxygenation improvement in extracorporeal membrane oxygeration (ECMO)-managed cases. These findings suggest that iNO, when used according to pathophysiology, is a valuable adjunctive therapy in high-risk perioperative settings.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Pediatric Lung Transplantation: An Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry Study, 2000-2022.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to identify factors associated with greater odds of survival, as well as odds of successful lung transplantation (LTx) in pediatric patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) as a bridge-to-LTx (BTT) or supported with ECMO after LTx.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry.

SETTING: International ECMO centers submitting data to the ELSO registry.

PATIENTS: Pediatric patients younger than 19 years old who were supported with ECMO before or after LTx between 2000 and 2022.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We identified 194 pediatric patients who used ECMO as a bridge to LTx, and 63% survived to hospital discharge. We failed to identify an association between ECMO modality (i.e., venovenous vs. venoarterial) and odds of survival. Central venoarterial ECMO cannulation was associated with greater odds of receiving a LTx compared with not receiving a LTx (30/85 [35%] vs. 15/109 [14%]; odds ratio [OR], 3.42; 95% CI, 1.69-6.91). In the 109 patients who did not receive a LTx, ECMO cannulation delayed after hospital day 7 was associated with lower odds of survival (OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.15-0.75). ECMO post-LTx occurred in 95 patients, 62% received venoarterial or veno-venoarterial ECMO, and 48 of 95 (51%) survived to hospital discharge. In patients requiring ECMO post-LTx, cystic fibrosis was associated with lower odds of survival (OR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.12-0.79) and pulmonary hypertension was associated with greater odds of survival (OR, 5.04; 95% CI, 1.68-15.1).

CONCLUSIONS: Our data show that ECMO was used to support children as a BTT and for stabilization of postoperative LTx recipients. Early initiation of ECMO was associated with greater odds of survival in patients undergoing BTT who did not receive LTx. Further studies, including additional patients and focused LTx-related data, are needed to better characterize and delineate treatment options in this population.

articles.title: Prognostic Implications of High HFpEF Probability in Patients With Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and left heart disease, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), show overlapping clinical features despite distinct pathophysiology.

OBJECTIVES: The HFpEF-ABA algorithm (age, body mass index, atrial fibrillation) was used to characterize HFpEF pretest probability in patients with CTEPH and evaluate its association with left heart disease and clinical worsening.

METHODS: Among 466 patients with CTEPH stratified by HFpEF-ABA score (low < 25%, intermediate 25%-74%, high ≥ 75%), Spearman's correlation assessed associations with common left heart disease comorbidities. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression evaluated associations with clinical worsening, with restricted cubic splines assessing the dose-response relationship and non-linearity. Subgroup analyses by sex, smoking, alcohol use, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and obstructive sleep apnea assessed the consistency. We also evaluated whether adding the HFpEF-ABA score improved COMPERA 2.0 discrimination for clinical worsening.

RESULTS: Intermediate and high HFpEF probability was found in 52.4% (n = 244) and 9.0% (n = 42), respectively. After adjustment, each standard deviation increase in HFpEF probability was associated with an approximately 73% increase in clinical worsening (p < 0.001). Results were consistent for HFpEF probability (p < 0.05), with no significant subgroup interactions. Adding HFpEF-ABA with COMPERA 2.0 improved discrimination, increasing the C-index increasing from 0.532 to 0.634 (p = 0.012).

CONCLUSIONS: Assessing HFpEF probability in patients with CTEPH identifies those at high risk for this comorbidity and improves the precision when integrated with existing risk models.

articles.title: Inflammatory and Insulin Resistance Indicator for Predicting Repeat Revascularization and In-Stent Restenosis in Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index (CTI) has been associated with cardiovascular risk. This study evaluated its prognostic value for repeat revascularization and in-stent restenosis (ISR) in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHODS: A total of 2147 CCS patients undergoing PCI were stratified into CTI tertiles. The primary endpoint was a composite of repeat revascularization and ISR. Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests was used to compare event rates. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analyses were applied to assess associations. Predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 60 months, 992 patients (46.2%) experienced the primary endpoint. Event rates increased progressively across CTI tertiles. After multivariable adjustment, CTI remained independently associated with the primary endpoint (HR 1.11; 95% CI 1.01-1.22; p = 0.028). Compared with the lowest tertile, the highest CTI tertile was associated with a 31% higher risk (HR 1.31; 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p = 0.002). A linear dose-response relationship was observed (p for non-linearity = 0.172; p overall = 0.040). The multivariable model incorporating CTI showed modest discrimination, with AUCs of 0.627 (95% CI 0.602-0.651) at 3 years and 0.651 (95% CI 0.627-0.674) at 5 years.

CONCLUSIONS: CTI is independently associated with increased risks of repeat revascularization and ISR after PCI in patients with CCS. However, its incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors appears limited and requires further validation.

articles.title: Context-driven mHealth solutions to improve maternal healthcare uptake in Ethiopia: Integrating stakeholder preferences and expert priorities using qualitative and nominal group techniques.
articles.abstract: Maternal continuum of care during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period is essential for reducing maternal and child morbidity and mortality, yet access remains limited in low- and middle-income countries. In Ethiopia, only about one-quarter of women complete the continuum of maternal healthcare. Although mobile health interventions have shown promise in improving access in resource-constrained settings, successful implementation depends on cultural appropriateness and alignment with local contexts. This study explored context-driven mobile health solutions and implementation challenges in Ethiopia by integrating stakeholder preferences with expert priorities. We conducted a qualitative exploratory and consensus-prioritization study involving interviews and focus group discussions with 72 perinatal women, male partners, and key informants, complemented by a nominal group technique workshop with 14 multidisciplinary experts. Data were collected in August 2025 using semi-structured guides in Gamoththo and Amharic. Qualitative data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis in NVivo, and descriptive statistics summarized expert rankings. Preferred mobile health components included video-based maternal health education, short message reminders with follow-up calls, and engagement of perinatal women with their spouses or support persons. Community health workers were identified as key to developing and sharing educational videos at women's gatherings. Participants preferred reminders between sunrise and midday on the day before appointments. Expert rankings prioritized reminders with follow-up calls (93.1%), engagement of perinatal women and their support persons (91.7%), and reminder timing between sunrise and midday (95.6%). Integrating stakeholder perspectives with expert rankings showed consensus on locally acceptable mobile health components and identified implementation challenges, including limited device access, poor network coverage, and low digital literacy. These findings provide a foundation for the co-design, feasibility testing, and pilot evaluation of contextually tailored mobile health interventions to improve maternal healthcare. Future implementation should address barriers related to device access, digital literacy, network connectivity, cost, and collaboration with telecommunications providers.

articles.title: Genomic ascertainment refines the population prevalence and phenotype associations of germline TERT variants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with deleterious germline variants in telomerase (encoded by TERT) are at high risk of pulmonary fibrosis (PF), liver disease (LD), bone marrow failure, head/neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and other complications. Clinically ascertained cohorts are subject to biased ascertainment of affected individuals and families with early onset, complex disease. This study used genomic ascertainment to determine prevalence of deleterious TERT variants and the associated risks of telomere biology disorder (TBD) phenotypes.

METHODS: TERT variants were extracted from exome sequencing data in UK Biobank (UKB, 469,377 exomes) and Geisinger-Regeneron DiscovEHR collaboration (DiscovEHR, 170,503 exomes). Cases were individuals with heterozygous deleterious TERT variants classified per modified ACMG/AMP criteria. Controls excluded rare, exonic, and splice site TERT variants. Electronic health records were assessed for TBD-related ICD10 codes. Case-control comparisons were done separately for UKB and DiscovEHR, accounting for smoking, alcohol, BMI, sex, genetic ancestry, and birthyear.

RESULTS: There were 64 deleterious TERT variants in 203 UKB participants and 32 in 138 DiscovEHR participants. Prevalence estimates were 1:2,312 in UKB and 1:1,235 in DiscovEHR. Risk of PF was significantly increased for TERT heterozygotes compared with controls (UKB: odds ratio [OR] 10.9 95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.11-19.45, p < 0.001; DiscovEHR: OR 6.64, 95% CI: 3.31-13.3, p < 0.001). Deleterious TERT variants were also associated with higher risk of LD (OR 2.4, 95% CI:1.25-4.59, p = 0.038) and HNSCC (OR 5.75, 95% CI: 2.36-14.02, p = 0.001) in UKB but not in DiscovEHR.

CONCLUSIONS: Rare deleterious TERT variants were present in 0.04 to 0.08% of the populations studied. Genomic ascertainment shows a predominance of pulmonary phenotypes, with PF associated with deleterious TERT variants in both cohorts. Associations with LD and HNSCC were observed only in UKB, possibly reflecting cohort differences including healthy volunteer bias. These findings illustrate the clinical importance of genetic diagnosis, and need for TBD-specific clinical trials.

articles.title: More common than we thought: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, comorbidity burden, and long COVID risk in a national cohort.
articles.abstract: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) is a complex, underdiagnosed connective tissue disorder characterized by widespread symptoms affecting multiple organ systems. Recent clinical observations suggest that individuals with hEDS may be at increased risk for persistent symptoms following COVID-19, commonly referred to as Long COVID. Using data from over 19 million patients across the United States, we examined associations between hEDS, COVID-19 infection, Long COVID, and related chronic conditions. We identified just over 25,000 individuals with hEDS and estimated a prevalence of approximately 1 in 800, which is higher than previously recognized. Despite similar rates of COVID-19 infection between patients with hEDS and matched controls, patients with hEDS were nearly three times more likely to develop Long COVID. This risk was concentrated among patients with hEDS who also had overlapping conditions commonly seen in post-viral syndromes, including autonomic dysfunction (POTS), immune dysregulation (MCAS), and chronic fatigue (ME/CFS). Patients with hEDS also exhibited higher odds of having additional risk factors for severe or prolonged illness, including chronic lung and autoimmune conditions, depression, and cerebrovascular disease. A subgroup of patients received their hEDS diagnosis only after a COVID-19 or Long COVID diagnosis, and this subgroup was highly enriched for multimorbidity, particularly POTS and MCAS. These findings establish hEDS as more prevalent than previously recognized and identify a substantially elevated, comorbidity-driven risk of Long COVID in this population. Improved screening, earlier diagnosis, and integrated care pathways are urgently needed to support this complex and underserved patient group.

articles.title: Are You Ready to Tackle the Troll? New Guidelines for the Management of Posttransplant Cytomegalovirus Infection.
articles.abstract: Posttransplant cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection has long been known as the "troll of transplantation"-a hidden threat that can emerge after solid organ transplant (SOT) or hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) and jeopardize patient well-being. CMV infection is associated with increased morbidity, mortality, graft loss, and hospitalization, as well as a substantial patient burden that many clinicians may underappreciate. Management becomes even more challenging when infection is refractory or resistant to treatment. To improve outcomes, healthcare professionals must be able to identify patients at risk for CMV infection and refractory/resistant disease, interpret diagnostic findings, apply updated guideline recommendations, and individualize antiviral therapy using current evidence. This comic-based, expert-led case activity follows a transplant recipient from the initial presentation of CMV infection through refractory/resistant disease, with patient perspectives woven throughout. Expert faculty perspectives and patient commentary will explore the clinical and psychosocial burden of CMV infection, risk assessment, diagnosis, treatment selection, resistance testing, and shared decision-making in posttransplant CMV care. To view this activity and obtain CME/CE credit, visit www.cmeologyce.org/cmv.

articles.title: Correction to "Impact of Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio on Adverse Outcomes in Patients With Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension".
Longitudinal Trajectories and Determinants of Post-Discharge Frailty in Older Adults Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A 2-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To elucidate longitudinal changes in frailty and identify factors associated with its improvement or progression in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort study used data from the Japanese Cardiovascular Physiotherapy Network registry. Patients aged 65-89 years who underwent elective cardiac surgeries between May 2021 and December 2022 were included. Frailty was assessed using the Kihon Checklist (KCL) preoperatively and at 6, 12, and 24 months after discharge. Group-based trajectory modeling identified distinct frailty trajectories over 2 years. Multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with trajectory group membership. Longitudinal changes in KCL scores were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Among 588 patients (mean age, 74.7 years; 41.0% female), three trajectories were identified. Group 1 (50.5%) showed persistently low and improving KCL scores, indicating favorable recovery. Group 2 (36.1%) exhibited moderate and stable frailty. Group 3 (13.3%) demonstrated persistently high and progressively worsening frailty. Compared with Group 1, membership in Group 3 was significantly associated with postoperative delirium, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lower hemoglobin levels, lower Barthel index scores, more advanced age, lower body mass index, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and impaired renal function. Linear mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant group-by-time interaction (p < 0.001), with sustained frailty increases occurring only in Group 3.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty trajectories following cardiac surgery are heterogeneous; approximately one in eight patients experience persistent and progressive frailty over the first 2 postoperative years. Early identification of high-risk patients may enable targeted multidisciplinary interventions to improve long-term functional outcomes.

articles.title: Ethnic Differences in Clinical Manifestations of Behçet's Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Turkic and Non-Turkic Patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis with clinical heterogeneity that may vary across ethnic groups within the same country. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included.

RESULTS: Patients were stratified by ethnicity into Turkic (N = 1037; 38.5%) and non-Turkic (N = 1660; 61.5% [with Persian/Fars, N = 980 subgrouping]) groups, and demographic, clinical manifestations, and immunogenic laboratory findings were extracted from medical records. Mean age at BD onset was 25.72 ± 10.02 years in Turkic patients and 24.69 ± 10.23 years in non-Turkic patients, and males comprised 61.3% and 57.1% of the two groups, respectively. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-B5 positivity was 55.1% in Turkic versus 53.1% in non-Turkic patients, and HLA-B51 positivity was 48.7% versus 46.5%, respectively. Most clinical manifestations showed similar prevalence across groups, including oral aphthous ulcers (98.7% vs. 99.0%), genital aphthous ulcers (60.5% vs. 62.0%), uveitis (50.1% vs. 53.2%), and deep vein thrombosis (5.3% vs. 5.1%). Superficial phlebitis was more frequent in Turkic patients (p = 0.02), and oral aphthous ulcers occurred earlier in Turkic patients (p = 0.023). A three-class latent class model demonstrated the best fit (BIC = 14,986.58).
