In multinomial logistic regression analysis, Turkic patients had slightly higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.91-1.33; p = 0.320) and slightly lower odds ratio of the multisystem phenotype (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.68-1.30; p = 0.692); however, neither association was statistically significant. Female gender was associated with higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype than the mucocutaneous-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.14-1.67; p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this large Iranian BD cohort, Turkic and non-Turkic patients exhibited broadly similar disease phenotypes and comparable HLA-B51 frequencies, with small but potentially relevant ethnic differences in the timing of oral ulcers and the frequency of superficial phlebitis. These findings suggest that ethnicity may influence BD phenotype through mechanisms beyond HLA-B51, possibly involving other immune-related genetic variants such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1(ERAP1), Interleukin (IL)-10. Of note, the significant differences observed in Turkic versus non-Turkic comparisons were not present in the Turkic versus Persian (Fars) comparison, indicating that the findings are not driven by a single ethnic subgroup.

articles.title: Sex Differences in the Association Between the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and Coronary Lesion Severity in Acute Coronary Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) correlates with increased coronary artery disease (CAD) prevalence and severity in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The aim of this study was to evaluate the influence of sex on SII and its association with coronary stenosis in ACS.

METHODS: A total of 130 patients with ACS, who had performed coronary angiography, were enrolled. Gensini Score (GS) was used to reflect the degree of coronary stenosis. The association of SII and GS were studied.

RESULTS: The mean values of SII and GS were significantly higher (p = 0.048 and 0.001, respectively) in male individuals compared with female counterparts. There was a significant correlation between SII and GS (r = 0.306, p = 0.006) in male participants. However, the positive correlation between SII and GS was not found in female subjects. SII was independently associated with GS (B = 0.030, p = 0.007) after controlling for age, smoking, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in male participants. LDL-C (B = 11.741, p = 0.003), smoking (B = 39.018, p = 0.016) and age (B = 1.139, p = 0.030), but not SII (B = 0.027, p = 0.101) were found to be independently correlated with the degree of coronary stenosis in females.

CONCLUSIONS: SII was a associated marker for evaluating the extent of coronary lesions in male subjects with ACS, but not in female counterparts.

articles.title: Therapeutic Approaches and Clinical Outcomes of Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms With Eosinophilia Harboring FLT3 Rearrangements: A Systematic Review of 39 Cases.
articles.abstract: MLN-Eo (Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia) harboring FLT3 rearrangement is an extremely rare hematologic malignancy for which standardized treatment guidelines are currently lacking. This systematic review synthesizes the largest cohort (39 cases) to date of FLT3-rearranged MLN-Eo. The available evidence supports the role of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as the cornerstone for achieving long-term survival and as a potentially curative intervention under current treatment modalities. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) can be used as bridging therapy to transplantation by inducing remission and reducing tumor burden. For patients ineligible for HSCT, TKI-based regimens (combined with chemotherapy) are recommended for disease control, while chemotherapy alone is strongly discouraged due to uniformly poor outcomes. These findings provide a practical treatment framework based on the currently available evidence and may help inform clinical decision-making for this rare and challenging disease.

articles.title: Comment on "Identifying Foundational Drug Knowledge in Pharmacy Education Using a Structured Consensus Framework".
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP

articles.title: Domino Liver Transplantation Using the Explanted Native Liver of a Multivisceral Transplant Recipient: A Pediatric Case Report and Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children awaiting liver transplantation face donor scarcity and waitlist mortality. Domino liver transplantation (DLT), or re-use of a structurally normal explanted liver, has expanded the donor pool in metabolic disease, but the multivisceral transplant (MVT) recipient, whose normal native liver is removed when a liver-inclusive visceral allograft is implanted, is rarely used. We report a pediatric DLT from an infant MVT explant and review all prior reports.

METHODS: Our case report presentation is followed by a systematic review using PRISMA 2020. MEDLINE, Embase, and PubMed were used from inception to August 21, 2025, with conference-proceedings and citation searching for any report of DLT using the explanted native liver from a MVT recipient or combined liver-intestine transplant recipient, without age or language restriction. Two reviewers screened and appraised the evidence.

RESULTS: Our case was a 4-month-old boy who underwent a MVT for near-total enterectomy complicated with a gastric, duodenal, and bladder fistula. His structurally normal native liver was transplanted across ABO incompatibility into an 11-month-old girl with biliary atresia and ~1% predicted survival. The MVT recipient remains well at last follow-up; the domino recipient died of intracranial hemorrhage three weeks after transplantation, with normal liver function. Three prior reports including 4 cases exist worldwide (1997-2023): one adult-recipient case, one pediatric abstract, and one series of two children given domino left-lateral-lobe grafts from combined liver-intestine recipients. Index recipients consistently retained stable graft function; domino recipients were prone to biliary and vascular complications.

CONCLUSIONS: DLT from an MVT explant is feasible, including across ABO incompatibility, and can create two recipients from one donor. In our case the domino graft functioned immediately, but the recipient died from complications of her pretransplant critical illness; consistent with the literature, domino outcomes appeared to be driven more by recipient pretransplant severity than by graft quality. Standardized protocols, staged consent, and registry tracking are needed before wider adoption.

articles.title: Long-Term Follow-up of Azathioprine-Induced Portosinusoidal Vascular Disease in a Patient With Crohn's Disease.
articles.abstract: Azathioprine is widely used to treat inflammatory bowel disease, organ transplantation, and autoimmune disorders. Hepatotoxicity is a rare but serious complication. We report a 48-year-old man with ileocolonic Crohn's disease who developed azathioprine-induced portosinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD) after 15 years of treatment. Diagnosis was suspected due to persistent cytopenia (leukopenia and thrombocytopenia) and when transabdominal ultrasonography and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed signs of portal hypertension. There was also an extensive portal thrombosis in the right portal vein, portal bifurcation, and origin of the left portal vein. Liver biopsy confirmed PSVD, showing nodular regenerative hyperplasia, sinusoidal dilation, and obliterative portal venopathy without cirrhosis. Treatment included azathioprine discontinuation, carvedilol, and anticoagulants. After 4 years of follow-up, Crohn's disease remained in deep remission, portal thrombosis recanalized, and portal hypertension stabilized. This case highlights the importance of monitoring for PSVD in long-term thiopurine users.

articles.title: Emotional stress-induced hot phases in a patient with a desmoplakin-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Desmoplakin (DSP) mutations are a common cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), frequently presenting with recurrent myocarditis-like 'hot phases' that contribute to myocardial injury and increased arrhythmic risk.

CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain and marked troponin elevation following emotional stress. Her history was notable for recurrent stress-related myocarditis episodes and a diagnosis of biventricular arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy due to a pathogenic DSP mutation. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated diffuse myocardial oedema and a characteristic circumferential subepicardial ring-like pattern of late gadolinium enhancement, consistent with an active hot phase. Given the high-risk pathogenic DSP mutation with multiple high-risk features, including documented non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, frequent ventricular ectopy, and mild left ventricular disfunction (resulting in a calculated 5-year arrhythmic risk of 12% according to the novel DSP risk score)-and the presence of frequent hot phases recurrences and high burden of late gadolinium enhancement-a primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted after clinical stabilization. Medical therapy was optimized with β-blocker up-titration and low-dose selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor therapy targeting recurrent stress-related triggers. At follow-up, the patient reported sustained clinical well-being with no recurrence of hot phases or arrhythmic events.

CONCLUSION: This case exemplifies DSP-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy marked by recurrent, stress-triggered 'hot phases,' highlighting the pivotal interplay between inflammation and arrhythmic risk, and underscoring the need for refined, disease-specific risk stratification and targeted management strategies.

articles.title: Feasibility of steerable sheath-guided left atrial appendage closure in challenging anatomy.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an established treatment option for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulation. However, an anatomically challenging left atrial appendage (LAA) can limit optimal device positioning and complete occlusion with conventional fixed-curve sheaths.Two elderly men with NVAF and high bleeding risk underwent LAAC using Watchman FLX Pro devices (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA). Pre-procedural imaging revealed anatomically challenging LAAs. With a standard double-curve sheath, one case showed unacceptable posterior protrusion of a large 40-mm device. In another case, tilting of the device led to incomplete coverage of the posterior lobe, resulting in a residual peri-device leak. After switching to the TruSteer™ Access System (Boston Scientific), a bidirectional steerable sheath, improved coaxial alignment, enabled acceptable device protrusion, complete sealing with no residual leak, and stable device release in both cases. These cases suggest that a steerable sheath can overcome the limitations of fixed-curve sheaths in anatomically challenging LAAs by enabling coaxial alignment and optimized posterior wall apposition during LAAC.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: In wide-neck, shallow, or multilobed left atrial appendages (LAAs), failure to meet PASS criteria with a conventional fixed-curve sheath may reflect non-coaxial deployment and, with very large devices, sheath instability due to kick-back at release, leading to device tilt. A bidirectional steerable sheath provides real-time control of the delivery axis and may prevent kick-back at release, enabling reproducible optimal device positioning in anatomically challenging LAAs where fixed-curve sheaths are inadequate.

articles.title: Inhaled Nanomedicines for Lung Diseases and Injuries: Pharmacological Advances and Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Respiratory diseases remain major causes of morbidity and mortality; however, inadequate pulmonary drug exposure and systemic toxicity continue to limit treatment efficacy. Inhaled nanomedicines offer opportunities for localized, sustained, and targeted therapy. This review examines how disease biology informs pulmonary delivery design across pulmonary fibrosis, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pulmonary infections, and acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome. It outlines anatomical and biological barriers and compares liposomes, lipid nanoparticles, polymeric and hybrid systems, biomimetic carriers, and stimuli-responsive formulations. Particular attention is given to matching therapeutic cargo and carrier properties to fibroblasts, macrophages, tumor cells, and alveolar type II cells. Emerging approaches include mRNA delivery, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, antisense oligonucleotides, and CRISPR-based editing, alongside alveolar regeneration and biomarker-guided treatment. These strategies are evaluated in relation to their delivery requirements and stage of development. The review also addresses aerosol-device compatibility, manufacturing, repeated-dose safety, regulatory considerations, and clinical outcomes. By connecting delivery mechanisms with disease-specific applications and clinical evidence, this review identifies both therapeutic opportunities and barriers to translation. This integrated perspective can guide the development of inhaled nanomedicines with more reproducible pulmonary delivery, improved treatment efficacy, and acceptable safety.

articles.title: Persistent mitral regurgitation due to subvalvular fusion in hypereosinophilic syndrome despite imatinib therapy.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Cardiac involvement is a major cause of morbidity in hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES). We report a rare case of severe mitral regurgitation (MR) associated with HES in which apparent echocardiographic regression after imatinib therapy masked irreversible structural disease. A 63-year-old man presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and heart failure caused by severe MR. Marked eosinophilia led to the diagnosis of a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with PDGFRB rearrangement. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed infiltrative thickening of the posterior mitral leaflet with vegetation-like subvalvular structures. Imatinib therapy rapidly normalized eosinophil counts, and follow-up echocardiography demonstrated disappearance of the vegetation-like structures; however, MR persisted. Because of progressive symptoms, mitral valve replacement was performed. Intraoperative findings revealed firm fusion of the posterior mitral leaflet and subvalvular apparatus to the left ventricular wall. The postoperative course was uneventful. This case highlights that apparent regression of valvular lesions after imatinib therapy does not necessarily indicate reversibility of structural disease in HES.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: To understand that hypereosinophilic syndrome can cause irreversible subvalvular fusion leading to persistent mitral regurgitation despite adequate medical therapy, including imatinib. This case highlights the importance of careful echocardiographic evaluation of subvalvular involvement and timely consideration of surgical intervention when structural valvular damage progresses.

articles.title: Ivabradine for inappropriate sinus node-mediated tachycardia associated with hemodynamic deterioration after acute myocardial infarction: A case report.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Sinus tachycardia is common after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but persistent tachycardia disproportionate to clinical status may worsen hemodynamics. We report a case of refractory sinus tachycardia associated with hemodynamic deterioration following AMI that responded to ivabradine. A 57-year-old woman developed cardiogenic shock due to anterior myocardial infarction and underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention with mechanical circulatory support. During recovery, she developed persistent sinus tachycardia exceeding 120 bpm, accompanied by worsening pulmonary congestion and increased pulmonary artery wedge pressure. Electrocardiography demonstrated sinus rhythm with gradual warm-up and cool-down patterns, without abrupt onset or termination, suggesting inappropriate sinus node-mediated tachycardia. Beta-blockers were avoided because of hypotension and ongoing inotropic support. Ivabradine was initiated, resulting in prompt heart rate reduction and improvement in hemodynamics, including decreased pulmonary artery wedge pressure and improved left ventricular filling. Dobutamine may have contributed to the tachycardia; however, the persistent and disproportionate nature of the sinus tachycardia suggested enhanced sinus node automaticity. This case highlights that inappropriate sinus node-mediated tachycardia may contribute to hemodynamic deterioration after AMI and that ivabradine can be an effective therapeutic option when beta-blockers are not tolerated.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: Disproportionate sinus tachycardia can occur even during the acute phase of myocardial infarction and may worsen hemodynamic status. When sinus tachycardia persists despite correction of reversible causes and appears excessive relative to the clinical condition, inappropriate sinus node-mediated tachycardia should be considered. Ivabradine may be an effective therapeutic option when beta-blockers are not suitable.

articles.title: Multimodality imaging features of dasatinib-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Dasatinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor used to treat chronic myelogenous leukemia, is associated with drug-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). We report two cases of dasatinib-induced PAH evaluated using advanced noninvasive multimodality imaging. A comprehensive pulmonary hypertension-targeted computed tomography (CT) protocol showed no structural lung abnormalities or pulmonary embolism. However, CT pulmonary perfusion imaging revealed diffuse heterogeneous hypoperfusion in both lungs, suggesting functional pulmonary circulatory impairment. Myocardial delayed-enhancement CT demonstrated late iodine enhancement and increased extracellular volume at the right ventricular insertion points, indicating myocardial involvement related to right ventricular pressure overload. Cardiac magnetic resonance confirmed right ventricular remodeling, and right heart catheterization (RHC) established precapillary pulmonary hypertension. After discontinuation of dasatinib and initiation of pulmonary vasodilator therapy, one patient achieved partial remission and the other normalization of pulmonary hemodynamics on follow-up RHC. These findings underscore the clinical value of advanced imaging in diagnosing and characterizing drug-induced PAH.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: To understand the clinical significance of noninvasive multimodality imaging, including a comprehensive pulmonary hypertension-targeted computed tomography protocol, in dasatinib-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension and to integrate imaging findings for a systematic assessment of its pathophysiology and clinical presentation.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence versus physician decision-making in acute heart failure: a comparative evaluation of four contemporary AI systems.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by the public and healthcare professionals for clinical reasoning. However, they were developed as general-purpose language models rather than dedicated clinical decision-support tools, and their performance in real-world acute heart failure (AHF) management remains insufficiently evaluated. We compared four contemporary AI models with physician decision-making.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This single-centre retrospective observational study incorporated a cross-sectional AI evaluation of consecutive patients treated at Sotiria General Hospital between July and November 2025, excluding acute coronary syndrome. ChatGPT, ChatGPT Plus, DeepSeek, and an ESC guideline-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) model independently assessed identical standardized cases. Recommendations were compared with physician decisions on diagnosis, treatment, guideline-directed medical therapy, timing, and prognosis using Cohen's kappa, McNemar's test, Cochran's Q, Wilcoxon signed-rank testing, and multivariable logistic regression. Diagnostic performance differed significantly across systems (Cochran's Q = 8.477, P = 0.037). In the balanced diagnostic cohort, ChatGPT Plus achieved the highest heart failure (HF) accuracy (accuracy 86.5%, sensitivity 87.0%, and specificity 86.0%), followed by RAG (accuracy 77.5%), ChatGPT (accuracy 77.0%), and DeepSeek (accuracy 69.0%). For HF within the top three differential diagnoses, sensitivity was 90.0-97.0%; specificity was 70.0% for ChatGPT Plus, 68.0% for RAG, 19.0% for DeepSeek, and 15.0% for ChatGPT. Physician agreement was highest for guideline-directed therapies, with greater variability in prognosis and escalation of care. RAG more closely matched physician therapeutic timing but did not consistently outperform general-purpose models.

CONCLUSION: Contemporary AI models show promise in AHF decision support but substantial task-specific variability, supporting use as complements rather than replacements for physician judgement.

articles.title: Valvular Heart Disease and the Importance of Inspiratory Muscle Training in Cardiovascular Rehabilitation.
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD) is a major cause of global cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Treatment is either surgical or transcatheter, as there is currently no conservative pharmacological approach. Cardiovascular rehabilitation (CR) is indicated before or after invasive medical interventions to facilitate the patient's functional recovery. While CR is common practice for many cardiovascular conditions, guidelines specifically addressing VHD are lacking. Another gap concerns the use of inspiratory muscle training (IMT). This narrative review discusses the importance of routinely incorporating IMT into CR programmes, offering hypotheses and recommendations for setting IMT parameters from the perspective of the Italian Association for Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (AIRC). Further research is needed to improve our understanding of rehabilitation and VHD.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Machine-Learning Model for Predicting Suboptimal Clinical Response After Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Suboptimal clinical response (SCR) after sleeve gastrectomy (SG) remains a major clinical challenge, yet reliable preoperative risk stratification is lacking. Therefore, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine-learning model for predicting SCR after SG using multicenter data from three tertiary hospitals in China. Overall, 1312 patients were included, comprising a derivation cohort (n = 1094) and two external validation cohorts (n = 84 and n = 134). SCR, defined as percentage of total weight loss < 25% at 1 year, occurred in 374 (34.2%), 34 (40.5%), and 45 (33.6%) patients, respectively. Among six machine-learning algorithms, XGB achieved the best performance. The final model incorporated eight routinely available predictors. In internal validation, the model showed excellent discrimination, with an AUC of 0.821 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.752-0.871), sensitivity of 0.803, and specificity of 0.714. External validation confirmed satisfactory discrimination (AUC 0.761; 95% CI, 0.688-0.823), good calibration, and clinical benefit. Notably, the XGB model significantly outperformed 10 clinicians across experience levels and remained superior in clinically challenging cases. SHAP analysis enhanced interpretability, with predictor importance ranked as BMI, age, fasting glucose, type 2 diabetes, vitamin B12, calcium, total cholesterol, and gamma-glutamyl transferase. This interpretable XGB model may enable precise preoperative risk stratification and support personalized management for patients undergoing SG.

articles.title: A Rare Case of Appendiceal Metastasis From Prostate Adenocarcinoma in an Asymptomatic Patient With Biochemical Recurrence.
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of appendiceal metastasis from prostate adenocarcinoma in a 73-year-old male with a prior Gleason score 7 prostate cancer, initially treated with radical prostatectomy and adjuvant radiation in 2014. The patient presented in 2025 with a rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and modest prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) uptake on positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) at the tip of the appendix. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a corresponding appendiceal lesion with restricted diffusion and enhancement. Pathology following laparoscopic appendectomy confirmed metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma involving the appendix and periappendiceal lymph nodes. This case highlights the importance of correlating atypical PSMA PET/CT findings with anatomic imaging and, when needed, histologic confirmation in patients with biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.

articles.title: Simultaneous two-vessel occlusion causing ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction associated with elevated lipoprotein (a): A case report.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Simultaneous occlusion of two coronary arteries during ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is rare and often associated with hemodynamic instability and poor prognosis. Identification of predisposing factors is crucial for prevention and risk stratification. A 53-year-old man with no classic cardiovascular risk factors other than smoking presented with inferoposterior STEMI complicated by syncope. Emergency coronary angiography revealed simultaneous occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery and distal left circumflex artery. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention was successfully performed in both vessels using intravascular imaging guidance. Subsequent evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated lipoprotein(a) levels (88 mg/dL) in the absence of other thrombotic or inflammatory disorders. Multimodality imaging revealed lipid-rich, macrophage-infiltrated plaques in multiple coronary arteries. Intensive lipid-lowering therapy achieved plaque stabilization during follow-up. This case suggests that elevated lipoprotein(a) may be associated with simultaneous multivessel coronary thrombosis and could contribute to plaque vulnerability and thrombogenicity, highlighting the importance of aggressive lipid management.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: Simultaneous multivessel coronary occlusion is a rare but life-threatening presentation of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. This case illustrates that markedly elevated lipoprotein(a) may be associated with widespread plaque vulnerability, emphasizing the importance of considering lipoprotein(a) measurement and intensive lipid-lowering therapy even in patients without traditional cardiovascular risk factors.

articles.title: Fondaparinux as an alternative anticoagulant in a pregnant woman with heparin-induced delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Heparin is commonly administered to prevent and treat venous thromboembolism during pregnancy. However, alternative anticoagulants should be considered in case of adverse reactions. Herein, we present a case of a heparin-induced delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction successfully managed with fondaparinux. The patient, a 40-year-old pregnant woman, developed acute pain and swelling in the left lower limb at 11 weeks of gestation; she was subsequently diagnosed with deep venous thrombosis. Anticoagulation therapy was initiated with intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH), subsequently switched to subcutaneous UFH. However, three weeks following therapy initiation, she developed multiple pruritic erythematous plaques at the injection sites. An intradermal test for UFH was positive at 48 h, confirming a diagnosis of delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction. In subsequent testing, cross-reactivity was observed with low-molecular-weight heparin, but not with fondaparinux. The patient was successfully managed with subcutaneous fondaparinux and delivered without complications, with a reduction in thrombus size.This case highlights that fondaparinux may serve as a safe and effective alternative anticoagulant for pregnant patients with heparin intolerance.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: Pregnancy is associated with a hypercoagulable state and an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Anticoagulant options are limited in pregnant women, and subcutaneous heparin is the first-line treatment for VTE during pregnancy. However, subcutaneous heparin is contraindicated in some cases due to allergic reactions, including delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions. Fondaparinux may be considered as an alternative anticoagulant for patients with heparin intolerance during pregnancy.

articles.title: Histopathological insights into a swinging cardiac calcified amorphous tumor associated with mitral annular calcification: A case report.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is the most common calcific disorder of the mitral valve; however, other calcified lesions, including cardiac calcified amorphous tumor (CAT) and its highly mobile subtype, swinging CAT (S-CAT), have been reported. These entities differ markedly in their growth patterns and structural characteristics. This study aimed to clarify the mechanism underlying the development of S-CAT arising from MAC by focusing on detailed pathological findings of resected specimens, particularly along the long-axis. Histopathological analysis demonstrated that the lesion could be divided into three distinct zones, each characterized by different morphologies of calcified nodules and varying degrees of inflammatory cell infiltration. In particular, the distribution of macrophages and neutrophils differed among these regions, suggesting heterogeneity in inflammatory exposure over time. These findings indicate that localized and time-dependent inflammatory processes associated with circulating blood components may contribute to the development of S-CAT on the roughened endocardial surface overlying pre-existing MAC. Furthermore, clinical backgrounds frequently included end-stage renal disease, diabetes mellitus, obesity, and hypercholesterolemia, supporting the role of systemic metabolic and inflammatory conditions in this process. Understanding these pathological features may provide insight into the pathogenesis of S-CAT and its clinical behavior.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE: Previous pathological reports of swinging cardiac calcified amorphous tumor (S-CAT) have mainly focused on the distal tip of the lesion. By examining longitudinal pathological specimens from root to tip, this case demonstrates distinct regional histological differences and suggests that S-CAT develops through a chronological process involving thrombosis, inflammation, and progressive calcification arising from mitral annular calcification.

articles.title: Absence of Documented Standard Modifiable Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Catheterized Admissions in Bangladesh: Frequency and Coronary Angiographic Phenotype in a 20-Year Registry Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease may occur without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs), but the frequency and angiographic phenotype of such presentations in South Asian catheterization cohorts remain uncertain. We estimated registry-defined SMuRF-less frequency, tested alternative dyslipidaemia definitions, and compared angiographic phenotypes by SMuRF status.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, registry-based cross-sectional analysis of 51,864 admissions with matched catheterization records at a Bangladeshi tertiary cardiac centre from 2005 to 2024. Admissions were classified as SMuRF-less when no qualifying hypertension, diabetes, smoking, or dyslipidaemia was documented or identified; dyslipidaemia reflected a documented diagnosis or qualifying lipid measurement. Documented-only and statin-inclusive definitions were sensitivity analyses. We calculated unadjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Under the primary definition, 3172 admissions (6.1%) were SMuRF-less, compared with 6.5% under the documented-only definition and 1.6% under the statin-inclusive definition. Among admissions with a classifiable angiographic phenotype, SMuRF-less admissions more frequently had normal coronary arteries (24.9% vs. 10.7%; PR, 2.34; 95% CI, 2.18-2.50) and less frequently had obstructive coronary artery disease (56.6% vs. 71.2%; PR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.77-0.82). Among admissions with obstructive disease, multivessel disease was less frequent (49.6% vs. 57.8%; PR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.82-0.90), whereas recorded intracoronary thrombus was more frequent (5.3% vs. 3.2%; PR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.33-2.04). Of 6635 ST-elevation myocardial infarction admissions, 355 (5.4%) were SMuRF-less; 318 (89.6%) had obstructive disease.

CONCLUSION: Registry-defined SMuRF-less admissions, reflecting absence of documented qualifying factors rather than prospectively verified biological absence, were uncommon, and their estimated frequency depended on risk-factor ascertainment. Although their recorded angiographic burden was generally lower, obstructive disease remained common, particularly in ST-elevation myocardial infarction. The absence of documented SMuRFs should not provide clinical reassurance. Prospective patient-level studies with standardized risk-factor assessment and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

articles.title: One bullet, five compartments: a transregional gunshot trajectory and the limits of operative intervention.
articles.abstract: Gunshot wounds with transregional bullet trajectories present significant diagnostic and management challenges. We report the case of an 20-year-old male who sustained a single gunshot wound entering at the left angle of the mandible, traversing the neck with injury to the thyroid cartilage, ricocheting off the right sternoclavicular joint and tracking through the right lung causing haemopneumothorax, before lodging in the perinephric fat adjacent to the right kidney. Pan-scan computed tomography (CT) was pivotal in delineating this complex trajectory. Management required a multidisciplinary approach involving Head & Neck surgery, Trauma surgery, Cardiothoracics, and Intensive Care. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed no peritoneal breach, supporting selective non-operative management (SNOM) of the retroperitoneal bullet. This case highlights the importance of thorough CT imaging from head to pelvis, the safety of SNOM for retroperitoneal bullets in stable patients, and the necessity of coordinated multidisciplinary surgical care for managing complex transregional gunshot injuries.

articles.title: Postoperative spontaneous coronary artery dissection after major abdominal oncological surgery: a case report.
articles.abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an uncommon non-atherosclerotic cause of acute coronary syndrome that can present as ST-elevation myocardial infarction (MI) and is particularly challenging because postoperative thrombosis and bleeding risks coexist. We report the case of a 44-year-old woman who underwent major abdominal oncologic surgery and developed a minor pulmonary embolism treated with anticoagulation. On postoperative day 4, she developed acute chest pain with ST-segment elevation. Emergency coronary angiography showed a long lesion involving the second diagonal branch, consistent with SCAD, with otherwise normal coronary arteries. She was managed conservatively. Her course was complicated by right JP drain-site bleeding, which required permanent heparin discontinuation and blood transfusion. This case illustrates SCAD as a cause of postoperative ST-elevation MI and the difficulty of balancing thrombosis and bleeding risk after major surgery.

articles.title: Beta-blockers after acute coronary syndrome: insights across the ejection fraction spectrum.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association between beta-blocker (BB) prescription and long-term all-cause mortality after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and to assess whether this varies across the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) spectrum.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed ACS patients from the retrospective multicentre CardioMining study (NCT05176769). The primary analysis used inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and restricted mean survival time (RMST) derived from weighted Kaplan-Meier curves. RMST and survival differences were estimated at 1 and 5 years. A landmark analysis evaluated survival between years 1 and 5 among first-year survivors. Among 6049 ACS patients (age 66.8 ± 13.2 years; 74.9% male), 5107 (84.4%) were discharged on BBs. During a median 4.6-year follow-up, 1912 deaths (31.6%) occurred. Overall, the 1-year RMST difference associated with BBs was 6.3 days (95%CI 0.0 to 13.2), which attenuated further by 5 years (11.3 days, 95%CI -30.7 to 63.9). The largest 1-year RMST difference was observed among patients with LVEF ≤40% (18.8 days, 95%CI 1.1 to 37.4), whereas associations were smaller and non-significant among patients with LVEF 41-49% and LVEF ≥50%. At 5 years, confidence intervals crossed the null across all LVEF categories. Continuous LVEF analyses suggested greater short-term benefit at lower values, with progressive attenuation across the LVEF spectrum. Among 1-year survivors, no significant RMST differences were observed between years 1 and 5.

CONCLUSION: Discharge BB prescription was not associated with a clear long-term survival advantage after ACS in this large real-world cohort. Apparent associations were strongest at lower LVEF values and attenuated during longer follow-up.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of ramucirumab Combined With Nab-paclitaxel, Lobaplatin, and S-1 in Conversion Therapy for Unresectable Advanced Gastric Cancer: Preliminary Results of Conversion Therapy Cohort of RNPLS-01 Trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This single-center randomized controlled trial assessed the efficacy and safety of the ramucirumab plus nab-paclitaxel, lobaplatin, and S-1(RNPLS) regimen for conversion therapy in unresectable advanced gastric cancer. Seventy patients were equally assigned to receive either ramucirumab, nab-paclitaxel, lobaplatin, and S-1(RNPLS) therapy or nab-paclitaxel, lobaplatin, and S-1(NPLS) chemotherapy alone. Primary endpoints included pathological complete response (pCR) and secondary endpoints encompassed R0 resection rate, objective response rate (ORR), the disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), duration of response (DOR), and adverse events (AE). Although the difference in pCR rate was statistically insignificant between the two groups, the RNPLS group achieved significantly higher ORR, DCR, and R0 resection rate. Moreover, the RNPLS regimen yielded prolonged PFS, longer duration of response, and promising preliminary OS. While hypertension occurred more frequently in the RNPLS group, the incidence of grade ≥3 AEs was low and comparable in both cohorts. This exploratory single-center randomized trial showed preliminary favorable efficacy of RNPLS regimen for conversion therapy in unresectable advanced gastric cancer with manageable toxicity.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06169410.

articles.title: Destructive spondyloarthropathy mimicking infectious spondylitis in long-term hemodialysis patients: a two-case report with contrasting outcomes.
articles.abstract: Destructive spondyloarthropathy (DSA) is a rare complication of long-term hemodialysis that often mimics infectious spondylitis, making diagnosis challenging. We report two patients with chronic kidney disease on long-term hemodialysis who presented with progressive neurological deficits and destructive spinal lesions suggestive of infection. In both cases, percutaneous biopsy of the lumbar destructive lesions showed no definitive evidence of infection, although occult infection could not be completely excluded. A 56-year-old woman underwent cervical reconstruction and achieved significant neurological recovery with solid fusion at 24 months. In contrast, a 62-year-old man underwent lumbar reconstruction but developed severe postoperative wound complications and died following a fatal cardiac event. These cases highlight the importance of considering DSA in the differential diagnosis of destructive spinal lesions in hemodialysis patients. Histological confirmation is essential before definitive treatment, and surgical outcomes depend not only on technical success but also on the patient's systemic condition and comorbidities.

articles.title: Pulmonary Sarcoidosis Presenting as a Solitary Pulmonary Nodule With Probable Neurosarcoidosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A 51-year-old woman presented with a solitary pulmonary nodule, hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy and progressive sensory disturbances. FDG-PET demonstrated intense uptake in the pulmonary and hilar lesions, while spinal MRI showed thoracic cord enhancement. Lung cancer-associated paraneoplastic neurological syndrome was initially suspected. Biopsies of the endobronchial lesion and a mediastinal lymph node revealed noncaseating granulomas without malignancy. Ocular involvement and neurological findings supported pulmonary sarcoidosis with probable neurosarcoidosis. Corticosteroid therapy improved neurological symptoms. Long-term follow-up showed a stable pulmonary nodule and sustained neurological improvement. This case highlights the importance of tissue diagnosis and careful neurological assessment when pulmonary nodules and sensory disturbances suggest malignancy.

articles.title: Emergency pancreaticoduodenectomy for traumatic pancreaticoduodenal injury with celiac axis stenosis.
articles.abstract: Emergency pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) for trauma is technically demanding, and unrecognized celiac axis stenosis (CAS) may compromise hepatic arterial inflow after gastroduodenal artery (GDA) division. A 59-year-old man presented in hemorrhagic shock after blunt abdominal trauma. Computed tomography demonstrated destructive pancreaticoduodenal injury, active bleeding, and proximal CAS with a hooked configuration suggesting median arcuate ligament (MAL) compression. After inferior pancreaticoduodenal arterial embolization, superior mesenteric arteriography showed retrograde filling of the celiac territory. Persistent hemodynamic instability necessitated emergency laparotomy and PD. Temporary GDA clamping markedly weakened common hepatic artery pulsation, confirming collateral-dependent hepatic arterial inflow. MAL release promptly restored pulsation, allowing PD with immediate reconstruction. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 34. In emergency PD for trauma, CAS or retrograde celiac filling should prompt temporary GDA clamping before irreversible division to guide MAL release or another inflow-preserving strategy.

articles.title: Factors Influencing Hospital Nurses' Patient Safety Competency: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recognizing the critical role of nurses in patient safety, various organizations have made sustained efforts to strengthen nurses' patient safety competency. However, there is a lack of systematic reviews examining the factors influencing hospital nurses' patient safety competency.

AIM: To analyze the factors influencing patient safety competency among hospital nurses from both individual and organizational perspectives.

METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guideline and the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for systematic reviews. Searches were conducted in four electronic databases (Ovid MEDLINE, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Embase) from January 2012 to March 2025. Due to the heterogeneity of the included studies, synthesis without meta-analysis using a vote-counting strategy was conducted to organize the findings.

RESULTS: The included studies examined 19 individual factors and five organizational factors influencing hospital nurses' patient safety competency. Individual factors were grouped into four domains: (1) demographic factors (age, gender, education level, work experience, and unit tenure), (2) job-related factors (professional qualification, employment status, and number of night shifts), (3) patient safety training and experience (participation in patient safety training, patient safety activities, and error reporting), and (4) other competencies (systems thinking, critical thinking, reflective thinking, professionalism, safety values, safety control, self-determined motivation, and proactive behavior). Organizational factors included organizational climate, psychological safety, psychological support, teamwork, and department type.

CONCLUSION: By categorizing influencing factors at the individual and organizational levels, this systematic review clarified the understanding of patient safety competency. Strategies that support nurses' individual characteristics and create supportive organizational environments can strengthen patient safety competency and promote safer care.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Healthcare organizations should tailor educational programs to nurses' experience and competency and foster safety-oriented environments that encourage teamwork, psychological safety, nonpunitive reporting, and learning from safety events.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42023422486.

articles.title: Erratum: Multicenter Study of MRI Features in Uterine Myxoid Leiomyosarcoma: Revealing and Overcoming a Critical Pitfall in Current Consensus Criteria.
articles.abstract: This corrects the article on p. 878 in vol. 27, PMID: 42683640.

articles.title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.

RESULTS: Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

articles.title: The PRISM Consensus: The First Major Step Towards Standardizing MRI for Population-Based Prostate Cancer Screening.
Mind the Academic Gap: Industry Support in the United States for Pediatric Versus Adult Rheumatologist-Authors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cognitive pediatric subspecialties, including rheumatology, struggle more than their adult counterparts to recruit young physicians. Commercial industry often subsidizes biomedical research and supplements physician income. Reasoning that availability and extent of extramural financial support may steer budding academically oriented practitioners toward or away from particular disciplines, we used published authors as surrogates for academic physicians and compared industry support to pediatric rheumatologist-authors (PRAs) and adult rheumatologist-authors (ARAs).

METHODS: We vetted authors of publications in the American College of Rheumatology journals in calendar years 2023 to 2024 for US affiliation, subspecialty, sex, h-index (measure of author impact), and receipt of industry payments during the 2017 to 2023 interval. Differences between PRAs and ARAs in frequency and magnitude of research-associated and nonresearch-associated payments were determined. Associations among industry payments, author sex, and h-index were also determined.

RESULTS: A total of 152 of 199 US PRAs (76.4%) and 567 of 710 US ARAs (79.9%) received industry payments (P = 0.286). Median total, nonresearch-associated, and research-associated payments to PRAs were 27% ($5,744 vs $21,030), 5% ($244 vs $4,905), and 0% ($0 vs $270) of those to ARAs (P < 0.001, P = 0.018, P < 0.001, respectively). These differences cannot be explained by differences in sex distribution or author impact. Among recipients of research-associated payments, nonresearch-associated payments were considerably lower to PRAs than to ARAs at any level of research-associated payment.

CONCLUSION: Although both US PRAs and ARAs commonly receive industry payments, the magnitude of payment per recipient is far lower to PRAs than to ARAs. We appeal to industry and to the rheumatology community to boost support of academic pediatric rheumatology.

articles.title: Evaluating the accuracy of brief cognitive assessments for the early detection of cognitive impairment in adults across primary and specialty care settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the accuracy of brief (i.e., ≤15 minutes), freely available cognitive tests for the early detection of cognitive impairment (including mild cognitive impairment and dementia) in adults 55 years and older in primary and specialty care.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases was conducted to identify studies published between January 1999 and August 2024 that evaluated the accuracy of brief, freely available cognitive tests for early detection of cognitive impairment. The tests included 5-Cog, Eight-item Informant Interview to Differentiate Aging and Dementia (AD8), General Practitioner assessment of Cognition (GPCOG), Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE), Mini-Cog, Memory Impairment Screen (MIS), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Quick Dementia Rating System (QDRS), Rowland Universal Dementia Assessment Scale (RUDAS), and Saint Louis University Mental Status (SLUMS). Though widely used, the Mini-Mental State Examination did not meet eligibility criteria and was not considered. Accuracy measures were extracted from eligible studies and pooled where possible. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2, and certainty of evidence was assigned according to the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

RESULTS: Forty-seven studies evaluating 10 index tests, including short versions of IQCODE and MoCA, were included. Test accuracy varied widely among tests and data pooling was not possible for most analyses. Studies conducted in both primary and specialty care were identified for AD8, Mini-Cog, MIS, MoCA, QDRS, Short IQCODE, and SLUMS, while evidence for IQCODE, short MoCA, and RUDAS was limited to a single setting. No studies meeting eligibility criteria were found for 5-Cog and GPCOG. Across all tests, in primary care, sensitivity ranged from 0.17 to 0.98, and specificity ranged from 0.10 to 0.98. Across all tests and assuming the same prevalence in specialty care, sensitivity ranged from 0.73 to 0.97, and specificity ranged from 0.45 to 0.90.

CONCLUSION: This systematic review provides a synthesis of the evidence on the accuracy of brief, freely available cognitive assessment tools for the early detection of cognitive impairment in primary and specialty care. Results from primary care settings informed the development of evidence-based recommendations presented in the accompanying clinical practice guideline on the use of brief cognitive tests in primary care.

articles.title: The shared genetic architecture of the TDP-43 spectrum: Bridging clinical FTLD and neuropathological endophenotypes.
articles.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) proteinopathies encompass a spectrum of conditions including frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 inclusions (FTLD-TDP), limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE-NC), and hippocampal sclerosis (HS). FTLD-TDP is further classified into several pathological subtypes (A, B, C, D, and E), which differ in the distribution and morphology of TDP-43 inclusions. Clinical and neuropathological variability across FTLD, FTLD-TDP, LATE-NC, and HS has hindered the translatability of genetic discoveries between clinical and pathological disease categories. By leveraging their genetic convergence, we aimed to refine effect size estimates and uncover variants that influence the TDP-43 spectrum.

METHODS: We conducted an inverse variance weighted fixed-effects meta-analysis using METAL, combining neuropathological datasets (FTLD-TDP subtypes: A [Ncases = 193], B [Ncases = 288], C [Ncases = 467], and controls [Ncontrols = 3153]), HS (Ncases = 751; Ncontrols = 6413), or LATE-NC (Ncases = 1325; Ncontrols = 1787). Additionally, we performed a random-effects meta-analysis that included clinically diagnosed FTLD (Ncases = 4685; Ncontrols = 15,308) and neuropathological datasets. Moreover, we performed colocalization, fine-mapping, and functional annotation analyses.

RESULTS: Three loci reached genome-wide significance. The GRN (rs5848) and TMEM106B (rs3807865) loci were associated with FTLD-TDP (A and B), LATE-NC, and HS.  Colocalization and fine-mapping analyses supported genetic signals at GRN and TMEM106B loci, while functional annotation suggested that rs3807865 and rs3807866 influence regulatory activity and TMEM106B expression in glial cells. MAPT demonstrated association across all combinations of TDP-43 proteinopathies (except FTLD-TDP B and C) and clinical FTLD, specifically the H1c haplotype.

DISCUSSION: Our results extend the known role of GRN and TMEM106B beyond FTLD-TDP subtype A, while MAPT involvement suggests a role beyond traditional tauopathies.

articles.title: Emotion Regulation in Universal Adolescent Mental Health Prevention Programs Delivered by Schools: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a developmental period marked by rapid biological, cognitive, and social changes that may precede psychological disorders. Emotion regulation (ER) is critical in adolescence as a transdiagnostic factor relevant to mental health disorders. Universal prevention programs can reduce emerging psychological disorders and fit well within school-based social-emotional learning; however, it is unclear how these programs address adolescents' unique needs, including ER development.

METHODS: School-based universal mental health programs were systematically reviewed for inclusion of ER skills and strategies. Four databases yielded 43 articles and 34 unique programs, 19 of which included ER strategies.

RESULTS: While 48 distinct ER strategies were identified, the most common were cognitive approaches, mindfulness, and problem solving. Programs without ER components focused more on mental health knowledge and stigma than on skills. Programs with ER skills generally provided more comprehensive psychological content.

IMPLICATIONS FOR SCHOOL HEALTH POLICY, PRACTICE, AND EQUITY: ER preventive interventions can serve as broad, population-based strategies to promote mental health, filling important gaps in SEL curricula.

CONCLUSIONS: ER content may offer unique benefits by targeting a critical transdiagnostic factor underlying adolescent mental health problems, though further research is needed to establish clear effectiveness and cultural appropriateness.

articles.title: Rehabilitation Wearable Boots and Offloading Methods for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Treatment: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a serious and common complication of diabetes, primarily affecting the plantar surface and toes. They are associated with high rates of recurrence, amputation and mortality, making effective treatment strategies essential. This review explores the current landscape of offloading methods and rehabilitation wearable boots used in DFU management, with an emphasis on clinical efficacy, patient adherence and the integration of emerging technologies. Total contact casts (TCCs), the gold standard, achieve healing rates exceeding 80%-90% but face limited adoption due to discomfort, stigma, and lifestyle disruption. Meta-analyses indicate that custom orthotics may reduce ulcer recurrence by up to 50% compared with standard footwear, although the magnitude of benefit varies across studies. In contrast, recent advances in smart wearable devices, multimodal sensors, custom orthotics and AI-driven adaptive systems demonstrate potential to enhance patient compliance and therapeutic outcomes. Despite the availability of evidence-based guidelines, a significant gap persists in their consistent application in clinical settings. Bridging this gap requires the development of patient-centric solutions that integrate technological innovation with usability, comfort and accessibility. This review highlights the need and future for innovative approaches that integrate technology and design to support healing, rehabilitation, adherence and quality of life providing pathways for more effective and sustainable DFU management.

articles.title: Quantifying a Neglected Burden: Pregnancy-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Maternal Death in South Africa.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during pregnancy is rare, with the literature confined to isolated case reports and small series. Women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) face disproportionate risk due to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection acquired perinatally, HCC in noncirrhotic livers at a young age, and fertility rates nearly three times those of Europe. To our knowledge, we report the largest cohort of pregnancy-associated HCC from SSA, drawn from a single South African center, and the first quantitative estimate of regional disparity versus Europe.

METHODS: Pregnant women with HCC at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, over 24 years (2001-2025) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry. A model integrating HCC incidence, age-at-diagnosis, fertility rates, and 1-year mortality compared the probability of pregnancy-associated HCC and maternal death in SSA versus Europe.

RESULTS: Of the 728 registry patients, 192 (26.4%) were female and 10 (5.2%) were pregnant or within 1 year postpartum. The median age was 32.5 (IQR, 28.5-35.3), 70% had chronic HBV infection, and three had cirrhosis. Seven (70%) died, six within 90 days. Two patients survived beyond 10 years following curative resection. Four pregnancies ended in intrauterine fetal demise and five in live births. The modeled probability of pregnancy-associated HCC was 16 per 100,000 women in SSA versus 0.14 per 100,000 in Europe-a 114-fold difference-with a 187-fold greater risk of maternal death.

CONCLUSION: Pregnancy-associated HCC in SSA is a quantifiable, preventable contributor to maternal mortality-nearly two orders of magnitude greater than in Europe. HBV endemicity, early-onset noncirrhotic HCC, and high fertility rates create a hostile environment for women of reproductive age. HBV-aware liver surveillance in antenatal care, strengthened prevention of mother-to-child transmission programs, and improved maternal mortality data systems are urgently needed.

articles.title: Digital reminder systems for improving adherence to anti-rabies vaccination among animal bite victims: A systematic review.
articles.journal: The Indian journal of medical research
articles.abstract: Background and objectives Digital reminder systems may improve adherence to scheduled vaccination visits. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of digital reminder interventions in improving adherence to and completion of anti-rabies vaccination among animal bite patients. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted on September 28, 2025 following a registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD420251148817). Two reviewers independently screened studies using NESTED Knowledge, extracted data, and assessed study quality using the Cochrane RoB-2 tool and the JBI critical appraisal checklist. Results Of 733 records identified, 436 remained after duplicate record removal and were screened by the title and abstract. Twelve studies underwent full-text assessment, and three that met the inclusion criteria were conducted in Tanzania, Kenya, and India. Two quasi-experimental studies evaluated SMS reminder systems, and one randomised controlled trial evaluated telephonic reminders. All studies reported improved adherence to scheduled anti-rabies vaccination compared with routine care. Vaccination completion was 70% vs 53% in the telephonic reminder trial and 93% vs 78% in the SMS reminder study. In the Tanzanian study adherence improved across four doses (62%, 50%, 29%, 13%) with SMS reminders compared with controls (48%, 41%, 22%, 7%). Differences in study design, vaccination regimens, and intervention modalities limited direct comparison across studies. Interpretation and conclusions Digital reminder interventions may improve adherence to anti-rabies vaccination schedules, but available evidence is limited and heterogeneous, resulting in low certainty of evidence. Larger randomised trials are required to determine the effectiveness and scalability of digital reminder systems.

articles.title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

articles.title: Comparability of Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of Canakinumab Administration With One Injection (200 mg) of Pre-Filled Syringe or Auto-Injector Versus Two Injections (150 and 50 mg) of Pre-Filled Syringe in Healthy Subjects.
articles.abstract: This phase 1, randomized, open-label, single-dose, parallel-group study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetic (PK) comparability and safety of canakinumab administered as a single 200 mg subcutaneous injection via pre-filled syringes assembled within a needle safety device (PFS-NSD) by HCP and auto-injector (AI) by subject self-administration versus two injections of 150 + 50 mg via PFS-NSD by HCP. Healthy adults (18-55 years) were allocated to three arms: canakinumab 150 + 50 mg (PFS-NSD; n = 78), canakinumab 200 mg (AI; n = 76), and canakinumab 200 mg (PFS-NSD; n = 76). Multiplicity was addressed as two tests were compared with the same reference. Primary PK parameters were comparable across arms. The geometric mean ratios and 95% CI values of AUCinf, AUClast, and Cmax were within bioequivalence limits of 0.80-1.25 for both comparisons: (a) canakinumab 200 mg AI versus canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD and (b) canakinumab 200 mg PFS-NSD versus canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD. Median Tmax was comparable: 7, 9, and 7 days for canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD, 200 mg AI, and 200 mg PFS-NSD, respectively. Exploratory post-hoc analyses, assessing the impact of pause during the pandemic (N = 131 subjects recruited pre-pandemic) and evaluating partial AUC4weeks, suggested similar results. Canakinumab was well-tolerated, and no treatment-induced immunogenicity was observed.

articles.title: Expert panel agreement with large language model responses to uro-oncology guideline-based questions: insights from seven Delphi consensus panels across major urological cancers.
Reply to Musch et al.
