Exercise and Nutritional Interventions for Muscle Strength, Physical Performance, and Body Composition Among Older Adults With Sarcopenia or Pre-Sarcopenia: A Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the relative effects of exercise and nutritional interventions on muscle strength, physical performance, muscle mass, and body composition-related outcomes in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia using network meta-analysis.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to August 8, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing exercise, nutritional, or combined interventions with control strategies in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia were included. A frequentist network meta-analysis compared four intervention nodes (Control, Exercise, Nutrition, and Combined). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, and certainty of evidence with CINeMA.

RESULTS: Sixty-five reports representing 57 RCTs and 6017 participants were included. Compared with Control, Combined, Nutrition, and Exercise improved handgrip strength, with the largest estimate for Combined (mean difference [MD] 4.29 kg, 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.50-6.07; p-score 0.877). For physical function, Exercise improved the Timed Up and Go test (TUG; MD 1.19 s, 95% CI, 0.72-1.66) and ranked highly for gait speed (MD 0.11 m/s, 95% CI, 0.06-0.17). For appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI), Combined, Exercise, and Nutrition increased ASMI, with Combined ranked highest (MD 0.32 kg/m2, 95% CI, 0.17-0.48; p-score 0.831). Overall certainty of evidence was limited according to CINeMA.

CONCLUSIONS: Exercise and nutritional strategies showed different relative effects across clinical outcomes in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia. Combined exercise and nutrition ranked more favorably for selected muscle-related outcomes, whereas exercise showed a more consistent pattern of benefit for physical performance. These findings require confirmation in high-quality trials because the overall certainty of evidence was limited.

articles.title: The Limits of Pharmacogenetics and Clinical Trials.
Prognostic Implication of CYP2C19 Genotype During Chronic Clopidogrel Monotherapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent clinical trials have demonstrated that clopidogrel monotherapy is superior to aspirin for long-term maintenance after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, evidence remains limited regarding whether the clinical benefit of chronic clopidogrel monotherapy differs according to CYP2C19 genotype.

OBJECTIVES: The study sought to investigate the prognostic impact of CYP2C19 genotype in patients with clopidogrel monotherapy for long-term maintenance following PCI.

METHODS: From the SMART-CHOICE 3 (SMart Angioplasty Research Team: CHoice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) trial and the nationwide PTRG-DES (Platelet Function and genoType-Related Long-term progGosis in DES-treated Patients) consortium, we analyzed patients with CYP2C19 genotyping who completed the standard duration of dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI without cardiovascular events. Patients were classified according to CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele status: rapid or normal metabolizer vs intermediate or poor metabolizer (IM/PM). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, and stroke at 3 years after switching to clopidogrel monotherapy.

RESULTS: Of 1,352 patients, 807 patients were carriers of a loss-of-function allele (IM/PM). The risk of primary outcome did not differ between the IM/PM and rapid or normal metabolizer groups (1.2% vs 2.2%; adjusted HR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.20-1.44; P = 0.215). Likewise, the risk of major bleeding was comparable between the groups (1.1% vs 2.0%; adjusted HR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.14-1.14; P = 0.086). Subgroup analyses consistently showed no significant interaction between CYP2C19 genotype and primary outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients who completed the standard duration of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clinical effects of clopidogrel monotherapy were consistent across CYP2C19 genotypes. These findings provide clinical reassurance that clopidogrel monotherapy can be used effectively for long-term maintenance, regardless of CYP2C19 genotype. (SMart Angioplasty Research Team: CHoice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3 [SMART-CHOICE 3]; NCT04418479; Platelet Function and genoType-Related Long-term progGosis in DES-treated Patients [PTRG-DES]; NCT04734028).

articles.title: Antithrombotic Treatment After PCI in Older Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Bleeding, Mortality, and Clinical Complexity.
Clinical Phenotypes and Integrated Care in Atrial Fibrillation: Toward Precision Implementation.
Beyond Bone and Muscle: Osteosarcopenia as a Novel Substrate for Atrial Fibrillation.
Management of Coronary Calcified Nodules: A Position Statement.
authors: Interventional Cardiology Council of the Asian Heart Society
articles.abstract: Coronary calcified nodules are an uncommon but important substrate for acute coronary syndromes, stent underexpansion, and recurrent target lesion revascularization. This consensus integrates pathologic, imaging, prognostic, and interventional evidence to guide practical decision-making. Intravascular imaging is essential for diagnosis, mechanism definition, and procedural optimization. Optical coherence tomography provides superior assessment of cap disruption and thrombus, whereas intravascular ultrasound remains valuable when contrast exposure or lesion crossing limits optical coherence tomography. Treatment should be tailored to lesion crossability, calcium distribution, and the need for mechanical scaffolding. No calcium-modification device or drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon strategy has demonstrated consistent superiority. The proposed type IIa/IIb framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Calcified nodule-related target lesion failure should be managed by correcting the dominant mechanical mechanism before antiproliferative therapy. These recommendations emphasize individualized, imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention and identify priorities for prospective comparative research.

articles.title: Prevalence and Geographic Distribution of Molar-Incisor Hypomineralisation in Spain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To systematically evaluate the prevalence of molar-incisor hypomineralisation (MIH) among Spanish children and adolescents and to investigate methodological and geographical factors contributing to the variability of prevalence estimates.

MATERIALS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261411600). PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, CINAHL and grey literature sources were searched. Cross-sectional studies reporting MIH prevalence in Spanish children aged 6-18 years were included. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Prevalence Studies. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects logistic regression models. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression and sex-specific analyses were performed to explore sources of heterogeneity.

CONCLUSION: Approximately one in six Spanish children is affected by MIH, placing Spain among the European countries with the highest reported prevalence. Significant geographical variation and methodological heterogeneity persist, highlighting the need for standardized diagnostic protocols and nationally representative epidemiological studies to improve comparability and support preventive oral health strategies.

articles.title: Pain-Related Outcome Domains and Measures in Randomized Controlled Trials of Treatment for Acute Abdominal Pain: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Acute abdominal pain frequently presents to emergency departments, yet outcome domains in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remain poorly characterized. This review identified pain-related domains and outcome measures used in RCTs on acute abdominal pain.

DATABASES AND DATA TREATMENT: This PRISMA-guided systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025630171). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for RCTs (January 2000-February 2025). Eligible studies included adult and paediatric patients with acute abdominal pain reporting pain assessment. Outcome domains extracted included pain intensity, rescue analgesia, adverse effects, pain interference, quality of life (QoL), and psychological function. Bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB2.

RESULTS: Of 826 records, 43 RCTs were included; eight included children. In adult trials, pain intensity was assessed using the visual analogue scale (n = 19) or the numeric rating scale (n = 15). Rescue analgesia (44%) and adverse effects (84%) were frequently reported. No study assessed pain interference or psychological function, and QoL was listed as an outcome in one trial. All were conducted in emergency settings, with short-term follow-up within the first hours.

CONCLUSIONS: Pain assessment in acute abdominal pain RCTs is predominantly limited to intensity measures and short-term outcomes. While appropriate for immediate analgesic effects, this approach may be insufficient when broader treatment goals or longer follow-up are relevant. Context-specific outcome selection is needed, aligning domains with clinical purpose and time frame.

SIGNIFICANCE: RCTs on acute abdominal pain assess pain incompletely, focusing predominantly on intensity rather than broader domains such as pain interference and psychological function. None adhered to the INTEGRATE framework for pain assessment. This review provides the first systematic mapping of outcome domains in this area, offering a foundation for context-specific outcome selection aligned with what matters to patients.

articles.title: Association of ambulatory waveform-derived pulse wave velocity with blood pressure response to exercise: role of fitness correction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Exercise blood pressure response (EBPR) is influenced by arterial stiffness, reflected by pulse wave velocity (PWV). Adjustment for cardiorespiratory fitness may refine its interpretation. Brachial waveform-derived PWV remains underused due to concerns about age and SBP dependence, and single-point office PWV may inadequately represent the dynamic vascular load driving EBPR. We hypothesized that 24-h PWV would outperform office PWV in predicting EBPR, and that indexing exercise SBP to aerobic fitness would strengthen these associations.

METHODS: We studied 228 adults (46% men; age 53 ± 12 years) with adequately controlled blood pressure, irrespective of hypertension diagnosis. Individuals with coronary artery disease, valvular disease, or heart failure were excluded. All participants underwent office and 24-h blood pressure monitoring with integrated pulse wave analysis (Mobil-O-Graph), cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and echocardiography. Exercise SBP at submaximal and peak workloads was normalized to peak oxygen uptake (VO2).

RESULTS: Fitness-corrected SBP showed stronger associations with PWV than uncorrected values (r = 0.64 vs. 0.15; P < 0.001). Both submaximal and peak SBP indexed to peak VO2 increased stepwise across 24-h PWV tertiles; this gradient was attenuated without fitness correction. After adjustment for age, sex, SBP, BMI, and left ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction, 24-h PWV remained an independent predictor of fitness-corrected EBPR, whereas office PWV was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Brachial BP-waveform-derived PWV independently predicts EBPR. Ambulatory 24-h PWV demonstrates stronger associations with exercise BP behaviour compared with single-time-point office PWV, and fitness-corrected SBP outperforms conventional uncorrected measures.

articles.abstract: FitPreV assessed the feasibility of integrating polygenic risk scores and wearable health devices into cardiovascular primary prevention in general practice. In this four-arm pilot randomized trial, 120 adults with metabolic syndrome were followed for 12 months. Recruitment was high and acceptability was favourable, with low anxiety after polygenic risk score (Prs) disclosure. However, 12-month follow-up completeness and GP willingness to implement the intervention require improvement.

Extracellular Vesicles Enhance The Coupling of Neurogenesis and Angiogenesis and Neurological Recovery By Transfer of Micrornas After Stroke.
articles.abstract: Intercellular communications underlying stroke-induced angiogenesis and neurogenesis remain largely unknown. We tested the hypothesis that extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from ischemic cerebral endothelial cells (ECs) and neural stem cells (NSCs) via their cargo microRNAs (miRNAs) mediate the coupling of angiogenesis and neurogenesis following stroke. Cell-type-specific EVs were isolated from conditioned media of cultured ECs and NSCs harvested from non-ischemic and ischemic rats. EV cargo miRNA profile analyses revealed that ischemic EC-EVs were enriched with miR-125a and -146a, whereas ischemic NSC-EVs were enriched with miR-106b and -125b. In vitro, treatment of non-ischemic NSCs with ischemic EC-EVs significantly increased NSC proliferation and differentiation, and augmented their miR-146a and -125a contents. Incubation of non-ischemic ECs with ischemic NSC-EVs robustly increased in vitro angiogenesis, with elevations of EC miR-106b and -125b. To determine whether ischemic EV cargo miRNAs mediate these effects, we engineered non-ischemic EC-EVs and NSC-EVs to carry specific miRNA mimics. Treatment of non-ischemic NSCs with the engineered EC-EVs containing miR-125a or -146a mimics significantly increased neurogenesis, while treatment of non-ischemic ECs with engineered NSC-EVs containing miR-106b or -125b mimics significantly promoted angiogenesis. Furthermore, intranasal administration of ischemic NSC-EVs or EC-EVs to rats subjected to 24-h middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), administered every other day for two consecutive weeks, markedly improved neurological and cognitive recovery. Collectively, our data suggest that ischemic EC- and NSC-EV cargo, particularly miRNAs, facilitates the coupling of stroke-induced neurogenesis and angiogenesis during stroke recovery.

articles.title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel Gemella species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.

CASE SUMMARY: A 55-year-old Japanese man presented with fatigue, anorexia, and altered mental status. Echocardiography revealed vegetations on the mitral and tricuspid valves with severe mitral regurgitation, and imaging demonstrated multiple systemic embolic events. Blood cultures grew gram-positive cocci that were initially identified as Gemella bergeri by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. The patient received antimicrobial therapy and underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve repair. Culture of the excised valve tissue was negative. Metagenomic sequencing of the valve vegetation detected a Gemella species distinct from G. bergeri. Genome assembly from sequencing data showed 94.5% average nucleotide identity with a reference G. bergeri genome, supporting classification as a novel species. Whole-genome sequencing of the blood culture isolate demonstrated near-complete concordance with the organism detected in the valve tissue. The patient recovered with a 6-week course of intravenous penicillin G after blood cultures became sterile.

CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that rare Gemella infections may be misidentified by routine mass spectrometry. It underscores the importance of sequencing-based methods for accurate pathogen identification and highlights a diagnostic pitfall associated with database-dependent identification in infective endocarditis.

articles.title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy With Superimposed Pre-Eclampsia in a Grand Multiparous Woman.
articles.abstract: This case report highlights the importance of clinical vigilance, the role of echocardiography, and the benefits of guideline-directed multidisciplinary management of pregnant women with HCM in resource-limited settings. Advocating for comprehensive multidisciplinary care models is essential in optimizing maternal and fetal health outcomes among pregnant women with cardiac pathologies.

articles.title: Severe Doxycycline-Induced Oesophagitis With Granulomatous Inflammation Managed in a Rural Australian Hospital: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Pill-induced oesophageal injury or pill oesophagitis typically presents with acute retrosternal pain, odynophagia, and dysphagia. While often self-limiting, cases may mimic acute coronary syndrome, food bolus, oesophageal perforation, and mediastinitis. Doxycycline is among the most commonly implicated medications. We report the case of a 32-year-old woman with severe mid-oesophageal ulceration secondary to doxycycline commenced for rosacea, managed at a rural Australian hospital. The histopathology finding of granulomatous inflammation was deemed reactive and secondary to severe ulceration, in the absence of infection or sarcoidosis. The patient was treated supportively with complete clinical and endoscopic resolution. Clinicians should consider pill oesophagitis in patients with acute retrosternal pain and odynophagia after starting doxycycline, and conservative management can be successful.

articles.title: Qianjin Baoyun Wan reduces spontaneous abortion and the prothrombotic state in pregnant rats.
articles.journal: Journal of traditional and complementary medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) is closely associated with a prothrombotic state (PTS) in the first trimester of pregnancy. Qianjin Baoyun Wan (QBW), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, has historically been prescribed to prevent threatened miscarriage and pregnancy-related lumbago, while its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in RSA complicated by PTS remain to be elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and potential pharmacological mechanisms of QBW in a rat model of RSA with PTS.

EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE: Spontaneous abortion was induced in pregnant rats by mifepristone, and PTS was established via epinephrine administration. The therapeutic effects of QBW were assessed by measuring miscarriage rate, uterine contractility, and uterine microcirculation morphology. Coagulation-related parameters (APTT, TT, PT, fibrinogen) were evaluated. Thrombosis-related and pregnancy-related biomarkers were quantified by ELISA. In addition, network pharmacology and network toxicology were employed to predict the potential pharmacodynamic targets and toxicological profiles of QBW.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSION: QBW reduced miscarriage rates and uterine contractility while improving pregnancy-related biomarkers. It restored uterine microcirculation (capillary density and diameter), prolonged coagulation time, lowered fibrinogen, and restored the balance between antithrombotic factors (e.g., AT-III, 6-keto-PGF1α) and prothrombotic factors (e.g., D-dimer, TXB2). Network pharmacology predicted immunoregulatory, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant mechanisms underlying its effects against RSA with PTS, though potential signals of hepatic and reproductive organ effects were noted. These findings suggest that QBW may have therapeutic potential for RSA with PTS, although further preclinical and clinical validation is required.

articles.title: Coinfections With Respiratory Syncytial Virus in a Cohort of Adults With High-Risk Conditions, 2015-2020: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Coinfections may influence the clinical outcome of respiratory illness. Data are limited regarding RSV coinfections in adults with high-risk conditions. Residual respiratory specimens from community-dwelling adults (≥ 18 years) with ≥ 1 high-risk condition were retested using a multiplex panel for multiple viral pathogens. We compared demographic and clinical characteristics between those with RSV coinfection versus RSV single infection. RSV coinfections comprised 5.9% of all RSV infections among adults with ≥ 1 high-risk condition. No statistically significant differences were observed between those with RSV coinfections and single infections according to presence of specific high-risk conditions or clinical disease presentation.

articles.title: Association Between Adherence to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet and Diminished Ovarian Reserve: A Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the fact that dietary intakes are suggested to affect fecundity and reproductive outcomes, data about the favorable impacts of dietary quality indicators on diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is scarce. So, we aimed to examine the relationship between the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score and odds of DOR.

METHODS: This case-control study was conducted among 370 women (120 with DOR as the case group and 250 with normal ovarian reserve as the control group). Cases and controls were frequency-matched according to age and body mass index (BMI) at the study-design stage. Dietary information derived from a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was used to count energy-adjusted DASH score based on eight components. Markers of ovarian reserve, including anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) and antral follicle count (AFC) which were measured in serum samples and by transvaginal ultrasound, respectively. The multivariable-adjusted binary logistic regression was used to identify the association between energy-adjusted DASH score and odds of DOR.

RESULTS: Higher energy-adjusted DASH score was related to lower diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in women with DOR (p = 0.006). No statistically significant association was observed between DASH adherence and the odds of DOR. In the crude model, compared with the lowest tertile (T1), the odds ratios for DOR were 0.87 (95% CI: 0.51-1.49) for T2 and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.46-1.33) for T3 (P-trend = 0.370). After adjustment for potential confounders, the association remained non-significant in Model 1 (T2: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.53-1.63; T3: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.43-1.33; P-trend = 0.328) and Model 2 (T2: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.49-1.56; T3: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.42-1.30; P-trend = 0.288). Nevertheless, in an exploratory unadjusted analysis among women with DOR, AFC differed significantly across energy-adjusted DASH tertiles, with higher AFC observed among women in the higher DASH adherence categories (p = 0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher adherence to the DASH dietary pattern was not significantly associated with the odds of DOR. Further prospective studies are warranted to clarify the potential relationship between dietary patterns and ovarian reserve.

articles.title: Optimizing Preexposure Prophylaxis Adherence: Evaluating Point-of-Care Urine Tenofovir Testing and Tailored Counseling Among Young South African Women.
articles.abstract: Among South African women using oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis, we compared a urine tenofovir point-of-care test with dried blood spot tenofovir diphosphate concentrations for recent vs longer-term adherence and assessed acceptability. The test demonstrated 76% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, and 69% specificity for high adherence (tenofovir diphosphate ≥700 fmol/punch) and was highly acceptable. Clinical Trials Registration: NCT04038060.

articles.title: Triple Total Coronary Occlusions in a Young Adult: Looking Beyond Conventional Atherosclerotic Risk Factors.
articles.abstract: Severe coronary artery disease is uncommon in young adults, particularly when conventional cardiovascular risk factors are limited. We describe a 26-year-old man who presented with exertional chest pain and was found to have total occlusions affecting all three major coronary arteries. Extensive investigation for inherited, metabolic, autoimmune, and inflammatory causes did not identify a definitive aetiology. His history of heavy electronic-cigarette use and a prolonged febrile illness in childhood were considered potentially relevant but could not be established as causal. He ultimately underwent successful three-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting. This case highlights the importance of investigating unusual causes of severe premature coronary disease while avoiding over-attribution to unconfirmed risk factors.

articles.title: Suspected Endomyocardial Fibrosis With Extensive Left Ventricular Thrombus: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
articles.abstract: We report a case of a 64-year-old man with biventricular dysfunction and a large left ventricular (LV) thrombus in whom endomyocardial fibrosis (EMF) was suspected. Despite extensive evaluation for eosinophilic, autoimmune, infective, and haematological causes, no secondary aetiology was identified. He was managed with guideline-directed heart failure therapy and anticoagulation. His condition progressively deteriorated, and he died within a year, highlighting the diagnostic challenge of suspected EMF when characteristic imaging findings coexist with atypical features and definitive histological confirmation cannot be obtained, as well as the therapeutic challenges of this rare cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Spontaneous Enterococcus faecalis Meningitis in an Elderly Patient: A Rare Cause of Community-Acquired Bacterial Meningitis.
articles.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis) is an uncommon cause of bacterial meningitis in adults, typically associated with neurosurgical procedures, central nervous system devices, or underlying comorbidities. Community-acquired meningitis caused by this microorganism is particularly rare. We report the case of a 76-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with acute prostration and altered mental status, without classical meningeal signs. Initial cranial CT revealed no acute abnormalities. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed findings strongly suggestive of bacterial meningitis, and E. faecalis was subsequently identified as the causative pathogen. Intravenous ampicillin and ceftriaxone were administered, with progressive neurological improvement. An extensive diagnostic workup, including cranial MRI, transthoracic echocardiography, thoracoabdominal CT, and colonoscopy, failed to identify a definitive source of infection. This case report highlights the diagnostic challenges of E. faecalis meningitis in older adults, particularly in the absence of classical meningeal manifestations and an identifiable infectious source. It also underscores the importance of early recognition, comprehensive microbiological investigation, and appropriate antimicrobial therapy in the management of this rare clinical entity.

articles.title: A Pilot Study of Linezolid for Early Syphilis Treatment.
articles.abstract: In a study of oral linezolid among 18 patients with early syphilis, 15 showed adequate serological response by 6 months. Among 6 patients treated with benzathine penicillin G, 5 showed adequate serological response. There were no serious adverse events. Linezolid shows promise for the treatment of early syphilis.

articles.title: Probable brucellosis-associated myocarditis presenting as myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brucellosis remains an important zoonotic disease in endemic regions and has heterogeneous clinical presentations. Cardiovascular involvement is uncommon, with myocarditis representing a rare but potentially serious manifestation. Brucellosis-associated myocarditis may mimic acute coronary syndrome (ACS), creating diagnostic uncertainty when obstructive coronary artery disease is absent.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a case of probable brucellosis-associated myocarditis in a 27-year-old previously healthy man with recently diagnosed brucellosis who developed acute chest pain and dyspnea accompanied by ischemic electrocardiographic changes and marked troponin elevation. Transthoracic echocardiography showed preserved biventricular systolic function without regional wall-motion abnormalities, significant valvular disease, or pericardial effusion. Coronary angiography demonstrated normal coronary arteries without obstructive disease, establishing a working diagnosis of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). In the absence of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or endomyocardial biopsy, the suspected myocarditis etiology was supported by the temporal relationship with active brucellosis, dynamic biomarkers, and electrocardiographic changes, exclusion of obstructive coronary artery disease, and subsequent clinical recovery. Because antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory therapies were administered concurrently, the response cannot be attributed to either intervention alone. No relapse or recurrent cardiac symptoms occurred during six months of follow-up.

CONCLUSION: In endemic regions, brucellosis-associated myocarditis should be considered among infectious causes of myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries. MINOCA is a working syndrome rather than an etiologic diagnosis. When cardiac MRI or endomyocardial biopsy is unavailable, epidemiologic exposure, microbiologic data, serial biomarkers, ECG evolution, echocardiography, and coronary angiography may support a probable diagnosis while acknowledging residual uncertainty.

articles.title: OVER-TIME II trial: design and rationale of a multicentre randomized study evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery ectasia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is characterized by diffuse coronary dilatation and increased thrombotic risk. In patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and CAE, the optimal antithrombotic strategy remains unclear. Previously, an exploratory trial suggested that the combination of antiplatelet monotherapy plus oral anticoagulation may reduce ischaemic events without increasing bleeding risk compared to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), although it was underpowered for definitive conclusions.

AIMS: The aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of antiplatelet monotherapy plus direct oral anticoagulation compared with DAPT in patients with ACS and culprit-vessel CAE in a multicentre randomized setting.

METHODS AND RESULTS: OVER-TIME II is a multicentre, multinational, randomized, open-label clinical trial with 1:1 allocation comparing acetylsalicylic acid 100 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg vs. clopidogrel 75 mg plus rivaroxaban 15 mg daily. The study will include 326 patients with ACS and culprit-vessel CAE. Patients will be followed for 12 months. The co-primary efficacy endpoint is the time to first occurrence of a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or repeat revascularization. The co-primary safety endpoint is the time to first occurrence of major or minor bleeding defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium criteria. Secondary endpoints include individual components of the primary outcomes. Exploratory analyses will include genomic and transcriptomic profiling through DNA and RNA sampling to identify molecular signatures associated with thrombotic risk, treatment response, and clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: OVER-TIME II is designed to provide robust multicentre randomized evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of an anticoagulation-based strategy in patients with ACS and CAE, with the potential to contribute to future clinical research and guideline development.

REGISTRATION: NCT07511257. The trial is registered and publicly available on ClinicalTrials.gov and is currently actively recruiting patients.

articles.title: Molecular smugglers in obesity-driven MASLD: Snitching on adipose-derived extracellular vesicles.
articles.abstract: Obesity-related adipose tissue (AT) dysfunction is closely associated with the development and progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the most prevalent chronic liver disease. Emerging evidence highlights that the AT-liver crosstalk is mediated by AT-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) that exacerbate the progression of MASLD during obesity. During obesity development, AT undergoes pathological remodeling characterized by hypertrophic adipocytes, pro-inflammatory macrophages, dysfunctional adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs), and increased cellular heterogeneity, which collectively alter the composition and function of secreted EVs. AT-derived EVs enter the circulation and transport bioactive cargo, including microRNAs (miRNAs), mtDNA, proteins and lipids to the liver, where they can modulate hepatocellular metabolism, liver inflammation and fibrogenesis. This review outlines the current state of knowledge on AT-derived EVs during MASLD, emphasizing the dynamic changes in AT under metabolic stress as well as the interactions between AT-derived EVs and the liver. We further explore the potential of EVs and their associated molecules as noninvasive biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets and underscore that understanding AT-liver communication via EVs offers perspectives for precision medicine in MASLD.

articles.title: Biphasic dysregulation of non-muscle myosin IIA drives the AKI-to-CKD transition via an ALDH1A1-retinoic acid-HBEGF/EGFR signaling axis in tubular cells.
articles.abstract: The decision between successful repair and pathological fibrosis following kidney injury remains a pivotal yet poorly understood process. Here, we identify non-muscle myosin IIA (NM IIA) as a master regulator of renal tubular fate whose biphasic dysregulation dictates the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Using integrated single-cell transcriptomics and multi-model validation, we define this dysregulation as stage-dependent alterations in NM IIA expression and subcellular localization: it is downregulated in AKI, impairing regenerative repair, but pathologically overexpressed and aberrantly localized to the nucleus in CKD, where it drives maladaptive fibrosis. Mechanistically, upon nuclear translocation in tubular epithelial cells, NM IIA directly transactivates Aldh1a1, thereby enhancing local retinoic acid (RA) biosynthesis. This RA signal subsequently propagates through HBEGF/EGFR signaling to influence repair outcomes. Collectively, our work delineates an NM IIA/ALDH1A1-RA-HBEGF/EGFR axis, revealing how NM IIA, beyond its cytoskeletal function, acts as a transcriptional regulator that integrates mechanical and metabolic cues in the kidney. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for the AKI-to-CKD transition and highlight potential stage-specific therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Verruconis gallopava pulmonary infection in a patient with Cushing's syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Verruconis gallopava is a dematiaceous mold that rarely causes human infection except in immunocompromised patients, such as those with solid organ transplants or hematologic malignancies. We describe an unusual case of pulmonary V. gallopava infection in a patient with undiagnosed Cushing's syndrome.

CASE SUMMARY: A 48-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital for Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, along with a history of recurrent falls and uncontrolled atrial fibrillation. As part of her investigations, she was noted to have an incidental lung nodule that was progressing in size, with evidence of cavitation over a 3-month period. A transbronchial biopsy revealed histopathologic findings consistent with phaeohyphomycosis, and bronchoscopy specimens grew V. gallopava. Fungal identification was confirmed via internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 sequencing, as well as with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. After further investigation, the patient was diagnosed with Cushing's syndrome secondary to an adrenal secretory mass and underwent left adrenalectomy, with subsequent clinical improvement. Repeat imaging following adrenalectomy showed radiographic resolution of her pulmonary nodule without initiation of antifungal treatment, consistent with clearance following immune reconstitution.

CONCLUSION: This is the first reported case of invasive V. gallopava infection that self-resolved following immune reconstitution and without the need for antifungal therapy. V. gallopava is a rare cause of invasive fungal disease in immunocompetent patients, and workup for possible underlying immunodeficiency should be considered in patients with V. gallopava infection.

articles.title: The Trend of Out-of-Pocket Costs for Child Delivery Care in Bangladesh During 2014-2022: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: In Bangladesh, out-of-pocket payments are the primary means of covering childbirth-related expenses, often placing a substantial financial burden on households and disrupting family livelihoods. This study examines trends in out-of-pocket (OOP) expenditures and identifies the factors influencing childbirth costs between 2014 and 2022, highlighting differences across delivery types and socio-demographic groups.

METHODS: This study analyzed 12,752 ever-married women aged 15-49 who reported out-of-pocket costs for childbirth within 2 years before each survey, we pooled data from the 2014, 2017-2018, and 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Surveys (BDHS). Out-of-pocket costs for home delivery, institutional normal delivery, and cesarean section (C-section) delivery expenses were the main outcome variables. Maternal age, employment status, antenatal care (ANC) visits, household wealth, body mass index (BMI), husband's education, birth order, geographic division, and place of residence were important independent variables. Descriptive statistics, ANOVA, t-tests, and log-linear regression were used to investigate associations.

RESULTS: The mean OOP of C-section delivery was the highest ($369.84), followed by institutional normal delivery ($102.78) and home delivery ($27.38). The mean cost of C-section delivery decreased from $501.46 in 2014 to $285.14 in 2022, while the cost of institutional normal delivery decreased from $116.23 to $93.03. The difference in costs between survey years was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Pooled regression analysis showed that higher household wealth was associated with higher costs in the selected delivery-type models. Other associated factors varied by delivery type and included maternal age, employment status, ANC visits, BMI, husband's age and education, birth order, geographic region, and place of residence.

CONCLUSION: There were significant differences in the amount of OOP costs of childbirth by type of delivery and year of survey. Despite a decline in average costs between 2014 and 2022, costs for C-section deliveries remained consistently the highest. Socioeconomic and geographic disparities highlight the unequal financial burden of childbirth in Bangladesh and support the need for policies to improve financial protection and equitable access to maternal health care.

articles.title: Perioperative Anaphylaxis and Respiratory Failure During AVF Surgery in an End-Stage Renal Disease Patient.
articles.abstract: Perioperative anaphylaxis can cause sudden, catastrophic respiratory and cardiovascular collapse in high-risk ESRD patients, even during regional anesthesia. Early recognition, prompt epinephrine administration, serum tryptase measurement, vigilant respiratory monitoring, and multidisciplinary preparedness-including ECMO capability-are critical to improving survival and preventing recurrent perioperative events.

articles.title: Scimitar Syndrome in Adolescence.
articles.abstract: Scimitar syndrome has infantile and childhood/adult variants. We describe an adolescent girl with recurrent wheeze in whom chest radiography and multimodality CT demonstrated the characteristic scimitar vein and associated bronchovascular abnormalities, with normal right ventricular function and no pulmonary hypertension.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation phenotypes derived from multimodal data exhibit distinct electrophysiological substrate characteristics, symptom trajectories, and ablation outcomes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The heterogeneity in response to catheter ablation amongst atrial fibrillation (AF) patients classified according to arrhythmia duration highlights the need for improved phenotyping. Multimodal assessment may better characterize the spectrum of pathophysiology present amongst patients classified as having paroxysmal or persistent AF. This study aimed to perform comprehensive multimodal pre-ablation phenotyping in patients undergoing AF ablation and evaluate associations with post-ablation arrhythmia recurrence, symptom burden, and bi-atrial substrate remodelling.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicentre prospective cohort study, 86 patients referred for first-time AF ablation (42% persistent AF) underwent pre-ablation phenotyping beyond usual care, incorporating patch-based ambulatory rhythm monitoring, atrial structural and functional MRI assessment, and formal symptom evaluation. Unsupervised K-means clustering was used to derive phenotypes. The primary outcome was 12-month arrhythmia recurrence; secondary analyses assessed symptom trajectories and bi-atrial substrate characteristics. Four AF phenotypes were identified. Arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 56.0%, 42.9%, 22.2%, and 19.0% of patients in Phenotypes 1-4, respectively (log-rank P = 0.032). Symptom trajectories differed across phenotypes, with the greatest improvements observed in Phenotypes 3 and 4. Exploratory electroanatomic mapping analyses demonstrated significant between-phenotype differences in bi-atrial bipolar voltage aligned with clinical trajectories. Importantly, phenotypes were not fully explained by conventional classification: Phenotype 2 experienced relatively high recurrence despite comprising predominantly paroxysmal AF patients whilst Phenotype 3 demonstrated favourable outcomes despite a high prevalence of persistent AF.

CONCLUSION: Multimodal phenotyping identified distinct AF subgroups associated with differences in post-ablation recurrence, symptom trajectories, and electrophysiological substrate. This approach could improve pre-ablation risk stratification and shared decision-making.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05057507.

articles.title: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors initiation and mortality in non-proteinuric chronic kidney disease: a target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment options for nonproteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. While renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs) are cornerstone therapies for proteinuric CKD, evidence supporting the clinical benefit of RASIs initiation in nonproteinuric CKD is lacking.

METHODS: We emulated sequential target trials using a retrospective cohort from the China Renal Data System. Adults with nonproteinuric CKD (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio <30 mg/g) were included to assess the intention-to-treat effect of initiating RASIs on all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The primary estimate was the 3-year risk difference. A composite kidney outcome (>25% eGFR decline with stage deterioration or kidney replacement therapy) was also explored.

RESULTS: A total of 17 382 eligible person-trials (10 101 unique persons) were included. The 3-year cumulative incidence of all-cause mortality was 14.88% (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.65% to 16.51%) and 18.26% (95% CI, 17.67% to 19.42%) in the RASIs initiation group and the control group, respectively, corresponding to a risk difference of -3.39% (95% CI, -4.71% to -2.07%). A significant association favoring RASIs initiation was also observed in terms of cardiovascular mortality, with a 3-year risk difference of -1.46% (95%CI, -2.57% to -0.52%). Estimates from the subgroup and the sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary analysis. A similar trend of association was observed for composite kidney outcomes, though the 3-year cumulative risk difference between groups did not reach statistical significance (risk difference, -0.88%; 95% CI, -2.42%-1.40%).

CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of RASIs may be associated with lower risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with nonproteinuric CKD.

articles.title: Carbapenem Renal Dose Discordance and Acute Kidney Injury in the Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal function changes rapidly in the intensive care unit (ICU), and carbapenem dosing above renal-adjusted recommendations is a potentially preventable medication safety issue.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between carbapenem renal dose discordance and acute kidney injury (AKI); treatment failure was exploratory.

METHODS: This ethics-approved retrospective cohort included adults receiving carbapenems for at least 48 hours in a Vietnamese hospital ICU (January 2024-April 2026). Discordance was at least 1 day above renal-adjusted recommendations based on estimated Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance and clinical indication. Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria defined AKI. Robust Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs). Matched outcome models additionally adjusted for Glasgow Coma Scale category and septic shock. A post hoc Bonferroni threshold of α = .003125 was applied.

RESULTS: Of 490 patients, 78 (15.9%) had discordant dosing. Acute kidney injury occurred in 28/78 (35.9%) with discordant dosing versus 18/412 (4.4%) with concordant dosing. Discordance was associated with AKI in the primary analysis (aRR, 8.061; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.135-15.714; P < .001) and among 68 matched pairs (aRR, 5.937; 95% CI, 2.112-16.694; P = .001). Associations with treatment failure did not meet the corrected threshold in the primary analysis (aRR, 1.586; 95% CI, 1.023-2.458; P = .039) or among matched pairs (aRR, 1.164; 95% CI, 0.723-1.875; P = .532).

CONCLUSIONS: Carbapenem renal dose discordance was associated with AKI, although causation cannot be established. Daily renal dose review by pharmacists is a practical medication safety target that warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: A Delphi-Based Item Set for Pre-Test Asthma Probability Assessment in Children Undergoing Methacholine Challenge Test.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To select, through a Delphi consensus process, the clinical items most relevant to pre-test probability of asthma (PTPA) in children undergoing methacholine challenge test (MCT) and to explore their association with expert-estimated PTPA.

WORKING HYPOTHESIS: Delphi-selected items are associated with PTPA estimated independently by pediatric pulmonologists.

STUDY DESIGN: Three-round e-Delphi, followed by a retrospective analysis of item association with expert-estimated PTPA.

PATIENT-SUBJECT SELECTION: A database of 92 children referred for MCT at a tertiary center.

METHODOLOGY: A steering committee proposed 11 candidate items, rated by 23 experts (consensus threshold ≥ 80%). Five pediatric pulmonologists, blinded to MCT results and not involved in the Delphi, independently estimated PTPA from clinical history. Agreement was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Associations between retained items and mean PTPA were assessed using a multivariable linear regression.

RESULTS: Ten items were retained (nine reached consensus; pneumonia/atelectasis was retained by steering-committee judgment). Single-rater ICC was 0.78 (95% CI 0.70-0.85); average-measures ICC was 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.97). Multivariable linear regression retained all ten items; each positively associated with PTPA. The strongest associations were seen with wheezing after age 3 years (β 15, 95% CI 7.4-23), wheezing within the last 3 years (β 14, 95% CI 6.4-22) and complete response to anti-asthma treatment with relapse after treatment cessation (β 34, 95% CI 27-41).

CONCLUSION: Delphi consensus identified ten clinically relevant items, all associated with expert-estimated PTPA. As the outcome was expert judgement rather than confirmed asthma, diagnostic value remains unestablished; outcome-based studies are needed.

articles.title: Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema: Current Status and Future Perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE) is a clinical syndrome defined by the coexistence of upper-lobe emphysema and lower-lobe pulmonary fibrosis. It is characterized by clinical, functional, and radiologic features that differ significantly from isolated idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

SUMMARY: This review summarizes recent advances in CPFE, focusing on etiologic classification, clinical and radiologic features, diagnosis and treatment, prognostic evaluation, and emerging perspectives in artificial intelligence (AI). Based on current research, we summarize the etiologic classification of CPFE into four types: smoking-related, systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated, occupational- and environmental-related, and idiopathic. These types differ in epidemiologic characteristics, imaging patterns, and disease progression. Consequently, future research is expected to focus on mechanism-driven phenotyping and quantitative imaging analysis, where AI may provide additional value in disease identification, risk stratification, and dynamic prognostic assessment.

KEY MESSAGE: This review proposes a novel framework for CPFE, integrating etiologic subtyping and a diagnostic algorithm to guide precise management, and highlights AI-powered strategies for future personalized interventions.

articles.title: Longitudinal Remodeling and Network Architecture of the Proximal Aorta in Children and Adolescents With Marfan Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortopathy is the main cardiovascular manifestation of Marfan syndrome, but the joint evolution of the different segments of the proximal aorta during pediatric growth remains insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate longitudinal remodeling and the interindividual and intraindividual architecture of the proximal aorta in children and adolescents with Marfan syndrome.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of data from the Pediatric Heart Network Marfan trial. Participants aged <18 years at randomization with acceptable echocardiograms obtained at baseline and at 6, 12, 24, and 36 months were included. The aortic annulus, sinuses of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, and ascending aorta were analyzed using absolute diameters and Z-scores. Partial correlation networks were estimated, separating interindividual and intraindividual components. Uncertainty was assessed using participant-level bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: A total of 515 participants were included; 445 (86.4%) had five acceptable visits. From baseline to 36 months, all absolute diameters increased, whereas Z-scores decreased (-0.688 to -0.454; all p < 0.001). Exploratory age-stratified analyses showed larger decreases among participants aged 6-11 years. The interindividual network was stronger than the intraindividual network (global strength 1.783 vs 1.020; difference 0.763; 95% CI 0.526-1.101; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses using inverse-probability weighting and an alternative Pediatric Heart Network Z-score system showed the same overall pattern of declining Z-scores.

CONCLUSIONS: The proximal aorta shows a multisegment architecture in which organization across patients is stronger than within-patient coordination of change. Network findings complement, but do not replace, serial measurement of individual aortic levels, and their prognostic value requires independent validation.

articles.title: Primary Erythrocytosis (Polycythaemia) in a Neutered Male Dog Presenting With Right Hindlimb Lameness.
articles.abstract: A 2-year-old male entire Cocker Spaniel was referred for investigation of progressive right hindlimb lameness and polyuria and polydipsia. Investigations conducted by the primary care veterinary surgeon revealed erythrocytosis (haematocrit of 78%, reference interval: 37%-55%) and urine concentration consistent with polyuria and polydipsia (specific gravity 1.014). Upon referral, physical examination revealed a dark red oral mucosa and right hindlimb lameness, characterised by intermittent non-weight bearing of the limb when standing. Neurological examination only revealed a mild short-strided gait, and orthopaedic examination was unremarkable. Secondary causes of erythrocytosis were excluded by normal arterial blood gas, low erythropoietin levels and normal thoracic and abdominal imaging, resulting in a diagnosis of primary erythrocytosis (PE). Focal ultrasonography identified a right external iliac venous thrombus, suspected to be the cause of the right hindlimb lameness and presumed to be associated with the PE. Initial management involved repeated phlebotomies, followed by long-term treatment with hydroxyurea (31 mg/kg twice weekly) and rivaroxaban (2 mg/kg once daily). At the 5-month recheck, the dog was asymptomatic, with resolution of the iliac thrombus and a normal haematocrit. This case highlights an unusual presentation of PE in a dog, not previously described in the veterinary literature, and re-examines the discussion on the optimal management of this rare condition, with a focus on the necessity of antithrombotic therapy.

articles.title: Patterns and Potential Relationships of Organizational Silence Types Among Clinical Nurses: A Qualitative Meta-Synthesis and Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To synthesize qualitative evidence on organizational silence among clinical nurses and examine relationships among motives, earlier organizational responses, and subsequent communication choices.

DESIGN: A qualitative systematic review and meta-synthesis.

REVIEW METHODS: One reviewer screened titles, abstracts, and full texts. A second reviewer verified extracted data. Two reviewers independently coded findings and appraised quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute qualitative checklist. Thomas and Harden's thematic synthesis was applied, followed by interpretation using social information processing theory.

DATA SOURCES: Scopus, Embase, PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, and the Chinese Scientific Journals Database were searched from inception to 6 October 2026. Initial searches were completed on 25 April 2026. Grey literature was not systematically searched.

RESULTS: Nineteen reports yielded four analytical themes encompassing 12 subthemes: (1) Motives distinguished forms of organizational silence; (2) Earlier responses informed later expression and participation; (3) Communication route and timing shaped the distinction between expression and withholding; and (4) Organizational conditions constrained expression across motives. Nurses' accounts linked withholding to anticipated adverse consequences, perceived futility, and efforts to preserve working relationships. The synthesis distinguished delayed or indirect communication from continued withholding.

CONCLUSION: Established silence types describe motives rather than fixed categories of nurses. Shared contexts may inform different motives, but the synthesis does not establish transitions or causal pathways.

IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: Clear escalation pathways, constructive responses from leaders, timely feedback, and a psychologically safe work environment may help nurses offer suggestions and voice work-related concerns. These pathways should facilitate prompt escalation of urgent patient safety concerns.

IMPACT: The review addresses the interpretation of nurses' silence and communication choices. Findings clarify motivational boundaries and alternative expression, informing clinical supervision, debriefing, and speaking-up systems for nurses and clinical leaders.

REPORTING METHOD: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, supplemented by Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patients or members of the public were involved in this systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis because the study was based exclusively on previously published research.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420261379111.

articles.title: Toxoplasma gondii in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Infection Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors in Humans and Animals.
articles.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a protozoan parasite with significant animal and public health implications. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of toxoplasmosis in ruminants and humans in Ethiopia and to determine the major risk factors associated with the disease. Five databases were used to search for all articles published between 2012 and 2025. The pooled prevalence of toxoplasmosis was calculated using a random-effects model. I2 statistics were used to assess heterogeneity among the included studies. Publication bias was assessed through a meta-analysis Egger regression asymmetry test. The overall pooled prevalence of T. gondii was 42.0% (95% CI: 35.0%-49.0%) in ruminants and 61.0% (95% CI: 49.0%-74.0%) in humans. Female animals have higher odds of acquiring T. gondii (OR = 1.76; 95% CI: 1.56-2.00) than males. Similarly, adult animals were more likely to be exposed to the disease (OR = 2.39; 95% CI: 2.10-2.74) than young age groups. In humans, rural residence (OR = 1.23; 95% CI: 1.07-1.42) and cat ownership (OR = 2.04; 95% CI: 1.79-2.32) were significantly associated with T. gondii seropositivity. These results highlight the necessity of targeted monitoring and preventative measures to reduce T. gondii exposure in both animal and human populations in Ethiopia.

articles.title: Transplantation of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Positive or Viremic Kidneys: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the evidence related to the use of HBV positive kidneys into non-viremic kidney transplant recipients (KTRs).

METHODS: We searched PubMed and Embase through November 2025 and identified studies of recipients of hepatitis B surface antigen positive (HBsAg+) or viremic kidneys. Studies with a comparison group of KTRs of HBV negative kidneys that reported on patient and allograft survivals were included in the meta-analysis. The risk ratios (RR) for patient and allograft survivals were pooled to obtain the estimate and 95% confidence interval, at 1-, 3-, and 5-years post-transplant. Viral transmission including HBsAg development, HBV viremia, or hepatitis was also reviewed.

RESULTS: Eleven studies were included in the systematic review and 6 in the meta-analysis. They included 638 KTRs of HBV positive kidneys and 2800 recipients of HBsAg negative non viremic kidneys. At 1, 3, and 5 years, the RR of allograft survival was not statistically different between the 2 groups and was 1 [0.98-1.01], 1.01 [0.98-1.04], and 1.00 [0.91-1.09] respectively. Similarly, the RR of patient survival was comparable between the 2 groups. The rate of HBV transmission was low (4.94%), especially when prophylaxis was used and when recipients were immune pre transplant.

CONCLUSION: Kidneys from HBV infected donors confer similar patient and allograft survival than those from HBV negative donors. They may be used to expand the donor pool, in immune KTRs and with appropriate prophylaxis, in light of this emerging evidence of safety with very low reported rates of transmission.

articles.title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve With Preserved Ejection Fraction: One-Year Changes in Ventricular and Atrial Mechanics.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease may precede ejection fraction (EF) decline. We assessed 1-year changes in LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain and myocardial work in BAV with preserved EF.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 82 adults with BAV and sinus rhythm who had preserved LVEF (≥50%) at two echocardiograms 363 ± 15 days apart without interim surgery; 40 age- and sex-matched controls with tricuspid aortic valves were imaged once. Primary outcomes were changes in absolute GLS and LA reservoir strain (LASr); myocardial work, corrected for the transaortic gradient in aortic stenosis, was exploratory. Reader reproducibility was tested on stored images.

RESULTS: At baseline, patients had lower absolute GLS (17.8 ± 2.8% vs. 21.8 ± 1.0%) and LASr (38.5 ± 5.2% vs. 40.8 ± 3.4%) than controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004). At 1 year, mean LVEF and LV volumes did not change significantly, whereas absolute GLS decreased by 0.8% points (95% CI 0.5-1.1) and LASr by 2.4 points (1.7-3.0; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Gradient-corrected global work index decreased by 47 mmHg% (27-68). The GLS decrease exceeded the intra-observer minimal detectable change in 22 patients (27%), versus an increase in 4 (5%). The GLS change was not significantly associated with valve lesion type or severity.

CONCLUSION: In selected patients with BAV who maintained preserved LVEF without valve or aortic surgery, LV GLS and LA reservoir strain decreased slightly over 1 year. Their clinical significance requires validation with longitudinal controls and test-retest data.

articles.title: Nursing Students' Knowledge of and Attitudes to Pressure Injury Prevention: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to examine existing evidence about undergraduate nursing students' knowledge of and attitudes towards pressure injury prevention. A systematic review of primary qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods studies was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A convergent mixed-methods synthesis was undertaken. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). MEDLINE, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC were searched on 21 August 2025 for literature published between January 2010 and 21 August 2025. Fifty-eight studies from 26 countries met the inclusion criteria. Nursing students demonstrated suboptimal knowledge of pressure injury prevention, with mean scores on validated tools (PUKAT/PUKAT 2.0) ranging from 23.5% to 61%, and a pooled mean of 39.2%. Attitudes towards pressure injury prevention were generally positive, with most studies reporting scores > 75% on the APUP instrument and similar tools. Qualitative findings highlighted gaps between theoretical instruction and clinical practice and a need for experiential and simulation-based learning. Despite positive attitudes, nursing students' knowledge of pressure injury prevention remains inadequate globally. Curriculum redesign incorporating active learning strategies, simulation, and integration of theory with practice is essential.

articles.title: What Is the Evidence for Silver Resistance in Chronic Wounds? A Systematic Review of Prevalence and In Vitro Studies.
articles.abstract: Silver-containing wound dressings are among the most widely used topical antimicrobial interventions in chronic wound management. Amid escalating antimicrobial resistance and increasing scrutiny of antiseptic stewardship, there is growing debate regarding the prevalence and clinical relevance of bacterial resistance to silver, yet the available evidence has not previously been systematically evaluated with a specific focus on chronic wound populations. This review aimed to evaluate the published evidence on the prevalence of silver resistance in bacteria isolated from chronic wounds and to summarise experimental evidence on the capacity of wound-associated isolates to acquire reduced silver susceptibility in vitro. We searched MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, identifying 2190 records, of which five publications met eligibility criteria. Two publications investigating overlapping isolates were consolidated, yielding four independent datasets. Three prevalence datasets reported markedly different rates: studies from the United Kingdom and Sweden identified low phenotypic resistance (0 of 112 and 1 of 56 isolates) and sil gene prevalence (< 2% in both), while a study from Bangladesh reported substantially higher phenotypic resistance (31.5%) and sil carriage (30.9%). Regional differences in antibiotic use offer a plausible explanation but were not directly tested in any included study and concordance between genotypic and phenotypic resistance was poor throughout. Two in vitro induction studies produced divergent results by endpoint: reduced planktonic susceptibility reverted towards baseline once silver exposure was withdrawn, whereas substantial increases in biofilm eradication concentration in Pseudomonas aeruginosa persisted. Prevalence was low where examined, but three datasets from three countries cannot establish the global burden of silver resistance in chronic wounds and critical gaps remain in geographic representation, methodological standardisation and validated breakpoints. Current evidence is insufficient to support changes to guidelines or policy in either direction.

articles.title: Practical Algorithm Guiding Seborrheic Dermatitis Treatment in Adults and Adolescents: New Evidence and Consensus Expert Opinion.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Seborrheic dermatitis (SD) is a common, chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by greasy, scaly plaques on the scalp or body, often with pruritus and impaired quality of life. The pathogenesis involves dysbiosis, including Malassezia colonization, excess sebum production, and immune dysregulation with Th17/Th22 activation. Although therapy historically targeted Malassezia, growing evidence supports anti-inflammatory strategies.

METHODS: A systematic literature review identified current treatments and management strategies for SD. Of 399 articles screened, 77 met inclusion criteria and informed algorithm development. A draft algorithm was created from these data and refined through a virtual workshop with 6 board-certified dermatologists and 1 physician assistant.

RESULTS: Experts recommended initial evaluation of disease extent and relevant comorbidities or lifestyle factors, along with patient education on disease etiology and scalp/hair care. Management is divided into (1) scalp and (2) face, trunk, or intertriginous involvement. First-line therapy emphasizes anti-inflammatory treatment with topical roflumilast 0.3% foam or corticosteroids. If disease persists, adjunctive antifungals are recommended. For nonscalp areas, alternatives include topicals, calcineurin inhibitors, tapinarof, or ruxolitinib. Recalcitrant or high-impact disease may warrant off-label systemic therapy such as isotretinoin, anti-IL-12/23 biologics, or oral antifungals.

CONCLUSIONS: This algorithm integrates an updated understanding of SD pathophysiology, prioritizing anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating therapies in management. It provides a practical framework for clinicians to tailor therapy based on disease location, severity, and response to prior treatment. Future studies are needed to validate outcomes and optimize long-term management strategies in diverse patient populations. Further research should clarify mechanisms and refine targeted therapeutic approaches further.

articles.title: Randomized Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of a Supplement and Serum on Grey Hair.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract: Worldwide, 74% of men and women between the ages of 45 and 65 have some grey hair. Currently, there is no treatment that has been shown in a clinical trial to repigment or slow the development of grey hair. In this study, we investigated the efficacy of a topical and supplement regimen (To The Root® serum and Not Today Grey supplement (Two Lines Inc.). A total of 173 men and women aged 28 to 65 years, with 5–25% grey hair, completed the study. Participants were randomized to include at least 40 subjects in each of the 4 groups: combination (supplement + serum), supplement (supplement + placebo serum), serum (serum + placebo supplement), and placebo (placebo supplement + placebo serum). There was a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in the number of grey hairs in the group that received the combination of supplement and serum. This group had a 9.2% reduction in grey hair at week 12 (P=0.034 vs baseline) and a 13.0% reduction at week 24 (P=0.016 vs baseline). The placebo group had 9.7% increase (worsening) in the mean number of grey hairs from baseline to week 24. The comparison of the combination group vs the placebo group at week 24 showed a significant difference (P=0.004). These results were confirmed by photo grading of grey hair (P=0.002, week 24 vs baseline) and by subject observation of grey hair (P=0.002 vs baseline). These results represent synergistic effects of the proprietary blends in the oral supplement and the patented topical serum. &nbsp.

articles.title: Evaluating the Clinical Efficacy, Utility, and Role of the 40-Gene Expression Profiling Test in Assessing Prognosis of Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Expert Consensus Panel.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 40-gene expression profiling (40-GEP) test has been validated to identify patients at highest risk for nodal or distant metastasis, as well as those most likely to benefit from adjuvant radiation therapy (ART). The purpose of this expert consensus panel was to review the published literature on the clinical efficacy, utility, and role of the 40-GEP test in providing prognostic information for high-risk cSCC.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was completed using a combination of keywords "40-gene expression profiling," "cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma," "prognosis," "clinical efficacy," and "clinical utility". A panel of 8 dermatologists with significant expertise in management of cSCC gathered to review the articles and create consensus statements. A modified Delphi process was used to approve each statement, and a strength of recommendation was assigned.

RESULTS: The literature search produced 55 articles. Screening resulted in 18 articles that met criteria. The panel unanimously "voted to adopt 8 consensus statements and recommendations: 5 with strength "A", 2 with strength "B", and 1 with strength "C.

CONCLUSION: The 40-GEP test augments staging accuracy by improving metastatic and local recurrence risk stratification beyond traditional staging systems. It also has clinical utility in informing decisions regarding adjuvant radiation therapy and guiding broader management strategies. &nbsp.

articles.title: A Moisturizer With Centella asiatica and Mandelic Acid Reduces Bruising and Speeds Recovery in Mature Skin.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dermatoporosis is a chronic cutaneous insufficiency syndrome characterized by skin atrophy, purpura, bruising, delayed healing, and increased injury susceptibility. This study evaluated an investigational cream, GC (Galderma Laboratories, L.P., Fort Worth, TX), in subjects with mature, crepey, bruise-prone skin, using a novel method to assess bruise severity and duration.

METHODS: This 12-week multicenter, randomized, blinded, in-use study recruited men and women aged 40 to 60 years with fragile, bruise-prone skin to apply GC cream twice daily to knees and thighs. A subset of 15 subjects underwent electric cupping on 1 randomized upper knee at baseline and week 12 to induce localized ecchymosis. Bruise severity was evaluated 15 minutes postinduction by investigators using standardized photography, and subjects captured daily images until resolution. Safety, tolerability, and subject satisfaction were assessed throughout.

RESULTS: After 12 weeks of GC cream use, investigator-assessed bruise severity score was significantly lower than baseline (mean [SD] 3.27 [1.33] vs 4.13 [1.02]; [P=.0087]). Days to bruise resolution were also numerically shorter at week 12 compared with baseline (mean [SE] 6.33 [0.91] vs 8.00 [0.56]; [log-rank P=.3134]). Serial photography confirmed expected temporal evolution and resolution of bruising and supported improvement in investigator-assessed severity. Subject satisfaction was high, and there were no related adverse events.

CONCLUSION: Twelve weeks of twice-daily GC cream use significantly reduced bruise severity induced by electric cupping and helped bruises resolve faster. These findings support GC cream as an important new option to reduce bruise potential and improve skin health of subjects with dermatoporosis. &nbsp.

articles.title: Peptides for Hair Growth and Treatment of Hair Loss and Alopecia: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients desire products that will result in hair growth and treatments to address concerns of hair loss in alopecia. Peptide-based formulations represent established, promising, and safe therapeutics that target hair growth pathways.

METHODS: On November 3, 2025, PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched per PRISMA guidelines for English-language clinical trials assessing peptide-containing therapies for hair loss in human subjects.

RESULTS: Of the 981 studies identified, 14 met the inclusion criteria. Grade of recommendation: B for formulations with acetyl tetrapeptide-3, biotinoyl tripeptide-1, glycyl-histidyl-lysine peptide, and penta-peptide Gly-Pro-Ile-Gly-Ser. Grade of recommendation: C for QR678 and QR678 Neo®.

CONCLUSION: Clinical data support peptide-based formulations, particularly combinations containing acetyl tetrapeptide-3, biotinoyl tripeptide-1, and glycyl-histidyl-lysine peptide as effective, well-tolerated alternatives to conventional hair-growth therapies. &nbsp.

articles.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Augmentation of a Clinical Trial of a Dermo-cosmetic Intervention for Acne Remission Maintenance.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A practical application of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare is to generate artificial datasets that capture the characteristics of a real source dataset without exposing protected health information. This approach is particularly relevant to research settings where recruitment and long-term follow-up are barriers to generating robust clinical evidence.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the protocol of a study incorporating augmented patient datasets to assess the efficacy of a dermo-cosmetic product (Cleanance Comedomed+®) in maintaining acne remission after discontinuation of oral isotretinoin.

METHODS: In a randomized, placebo-controlled, blinded clinical trial, patients will receive the dermo-cosmetic product or placebo for up to 12 months. Study outcomes are the number of observed relapses and time to first relapse. To overcome recruitment constraints and reach the 400 patients required to ensure sufficient precision for a time-dependent event criterion, a cohort augmentation strategy using artificial data is implemented. The technology relies on generative models of the Riemannian Hamiltonian Variational Autoencoder type, which learn a compact and geometrically structured latent representation of real clinical data. Generation of artificial patients will occur iteratively, and the initial dataset will be progressively enriched as new real inclusions become available. Reliability of generated data will be assessed and validated through human oversight using quantitative and qualitative metrics covering 4 dimensions: (1) statistical fidelity; (2) diversity and utility; (3) confidentiality; and (4) clinical plausibility.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Structured integration of artificial data into this clinical trial illustrates the potential of generative AI as a methodological tool complementing conventional approaches in clinical research. &nbsp.

articles.title: Bruton Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic relapsing autoimmune disease with frequent cutaneous involvement and unmet treatment need. Given safety and efficacy concerns with first-line therapies and no US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved treatment for cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE), Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) has emerged as a biologically relevant target.

METHODS: On January 20, 2026, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched per PRISMA guidelines. Clinical trials investigating BTK inhibitors for the treatment of SLE were included.

RESULTS: Of 579 records, 5 randomized clinical trials met inclusion criteria, evaluating elsubrutinib (2), evobrutinib (1), fenebrutinib (1), and orelabrutinib (1). Efficacy across SLE endpoints was variable. Elsubrutinib- and orelabrutinib-based regimens improved cutaneous disease. Evobrutinib and fenebrutinib showed limited or nonsignificant differences in primary endpoints compared with placebo. Safety was generally acceptable; adverse events included infections and elevations in transaminase levels.

CONCLUSIONS: BTK inhibitors showed variable efficacy in SLE but potential for cutaneous disease improvement. To date, no clinical trials have evaluated BTK inhibition in CLE. Given promising clinical and mouse model data, dedicated CLE-focused randomized controlled trials are warranted. &nbsp.

articles.title: Monotonic additive modeling reveals candidate biomarkers of cardio-renal-metabolic disorder susceptibility.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus form an interconnected disease continuum driven by shared risk factors, overlapping molecular pathways and reciprocal progression. This convergence has led to the recognition of cardio-renal-metabolic disorder (CRMD) as a unified systemic condition in which dysregulation of metabolic, vascular, inflammatory and renal pathways precedes organ-specific pathology. Despite this understanding, current diagnostic strategies remain disease-centric and are typically initiated after substantial tissue damage, limiting opportunities for early intervention.
