Identification of early non-invasive biomarkers capturing shared CRMD susceptibility is therefore of utmost clinical importance. In this study, we developed an explainable monotonic additive machine learning framework to identify blood-based molecular biomarkers associated with CRMD susceptibility. Transcriptomic profiles representing cardiovascular, renal and metabolic disease states were analysed within a unified CRMD paradigm. Following transcriptomic harmonization and batch correction, a monotonic additive XGBoost model combined with integrated biomarker score, gene-response analysis and differential expression analysis was implemented to identify biologically interpretable and directionally consistent biomarkers reflective of shared CRMD-associated dysregulation. Six biomarkers, including EEF1D, RPL27A, ERO1LB, JUN, POSTN and SERPINE2, were identified as potential CRMD susceptibility biomarkers spanning translational regulation, proteostasis, endoplasmic-reticulum function, systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, vascular dysfunction, extracellular remodeling and fibrosis. Importantly, these biomarkers have potential for blood-based detection using established assays such as ELISA, multiplex immunoassays and quantitative PCR, underscoring their translational potential for early CRMD screening, susceptibility assessment and risk stratification.

articles.title: Possible sarcopenia, abdominal obesity, and all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults with chronic kidney disease: a dual-cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Possible sarcopenia (low muscle strength) is a strong predictor of mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD). While abdominal obesity is prevalent, whether it predicts mortality or modifies the association between muscle weakness and mortality remains controversial. We investigated their independent and joint associations with all-cause mortality in CKD.

METHODS: This study analyzed adults with CKD aged ≥45 years from CHARLS (n = 1005) and NHANES (n = 1070). Participants were categorized into four phenotypes: NPS/NAO (neither condition), NPS/AO (abdominal obesity alone), PS/NAO (possible sarcopenia alone), and PS/AO (both conditions). Mortality risk was evaluated using multivariable Cox models and restricted cubic splines.

RESULTS: PS/NAO was associated with elevated all-cause mortality (adjusted HR in CHARLS: 1.980, 95% CI 1.333-2.941; NHANES: 2.191, 1.194-4.020). The estimate for PS/AO was less precise and did not reach statistical significance (CHARLS: 1.288, 0.711-2.333; NHANES: 1.171, 0.661-2.075). Direct comparisons and interaction analyses revealed no evidence that abdominal obesity modified the mortality risk associated with possible sarcopenia. No significant association was observed between NPS/AO and mortality. Handgrip strength showed an inverse linear association with mortality, whereas waist circumference provided neither independent nor incremental prognostic value.

CONCLUSIONS: Possible sarcopenia independently predicts all-cause mortality in CKD, though this association did not retain statistical significance in CHARLS when restricted to participants with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Waist circumference provides no incremental prognostic value beyond handgrip strength, and the study was underpowered to characterize the concurrent phenotype. Prognostic evaluation in CKD should focus on routine muscle strength assessment rather than abdominal adiposity.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.

articles.title: Context effects in intensity discrimination.
articles.journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
articles.abstract: Animal studies have shown that auditory neurons adapt their firing rate depending on sound level statistics. This dynamic range adaptation (DRA) has been measured by presenting short segments of noise or tones with some levels being presented more often than others. DRA manifests as a shift of the rate-level function of the neurons toward the most frequently presented levels. It produces a change in sensitivity enhancing the coding of these most probable levels. The aim of this study was to search for a perceptual correlate of DRA in normal hearing participants. Intensity discrimination thresholds were measured for pure-tone and for broadband pulse-spreading harmonic complex test signals embedded in different contexts, with the hypothesis that discrimination thresholds should be lower when the context mean level matches the test signal level. For broadband signals, the results were fully consistent with this hypothesis, while for pure tones, intensity discrimination always degraded with increases in context level, independently from the level of the test signals. Additional experiments suggest that partial masking and confusion may have obscured the effects of DRA for pure tones.

articles.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
articles.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to the tail. Phage A1002 exhibits a distinctly elongated tail morphology distinct from other reported podophages. Notably, the A1002 nozzle employs a distinct assembly strategy, featuring the unique nozzle-rope protein and nozzle-base protein, which may have evolved through modular evolution and horizontal gene transfer. Furthermore, the nozzle-rope protein provides 11 adsorption sites for fiber dimers, and these dimers are assembled from two proteins, giving rise to two types of dimers: dimers 1-7 correspond to fiber I (gp40), and dimers 8-11 correspond to fiber II (gp41). The nozzle-rope protein and these dimers combine to form a chain-like fiber. The tail tube comprises a double-layered, elongated tube structure that functions to simultaneously increase tail length and provide docking sites for six chain-like fibers. These distinctive structural features provide the molecular basis for A1002's broad-spectrum infection of drug-resistant P. aeruginosa and offer a novel molecular blueprint for rational design of structure-guided phage therapeutics.

articles.title: Modulation of riboflavin biosynthesis enzymes in non-typhoidal Salmonella isolates differentially impacts human MAIT cell activation.
articles.abstract: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) sequence type 313 (ST313) isolates have emerged in sub-Saharan Africa, with a high incidence of multidrug resistance, enhanced intracellular persistence, increased dissemination and immune evasion. ST313 isolate D23580 was shown to avoid activation of mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells compared with a genetically similar, non-invasive Salmonella Typhimurium (S.Tm) 4/74 strain, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, we studied immune responses to infection with typhoidal strains and ST313 isolates using comparative transcriptomic profiling of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). MAIT cells responded to typhoidal strains but not to D23580. To uncover underlying mechanisms, we engineered an inducible CRISPRi system targeting riboflavin biosynthesis enzymes (rib), which process MAIT ligands, in D23580 and 4/74 strains. Several rib hypomorphs exhibited prolonged lag time in minimal media, which was more pronounced in D23580 than in 4/74. In PBMC infection, knockdown of lumazine synthase (RibH) and riboflavin synthase (RibE) resulted in contrasting MAIT cell activation phenotypes. RibH knockdown restored MAIT cell activation in D23580 but did not affect activation in 4/74. Conversely, RibE knockdown diminished MAIT cell activation by 4/74 but had no impact on MAIT cell activation by D23580. Metabolomic analysis revealed accumulation of the biosynthetic intermediate DMRL in RibE knockdown and a differential impact on riboflavin biosynthesis end products between D23580 and 4/74 RibH knockdown, suggesting altered pathway flux between the strains. Our results indicate RibH and RibE as pivotal nodes for strain-specific MAIT-activation during Salmonella infection of human PBMCs, illustrating teir central role in the complex interplay between bacterial metabolism and host immunity.

articles.title: Transforming pandemic influenza antiviral stockpiling using a capacity-based approach: A modeling study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pandemic influenza preparedness in high-resource nations has traditionally relied on large antiviral stockpiles, typically targeting coverage for 25% of the population. This inventory-based benchmark focuses on cumulative disease burden but often overlooks the inelastic capacity of healthcare systems to manage acute surges. As multi-billion-dollar inventories reach expiration, we evaluated whether static stockpiles remain a viable strategy for preventing healthcare system collapse during future pandemics.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We projected daily hospital bed demand using three complementary frameworks: a static lower-bound estimation, a dynamic deterministic Susceptible-Infectious-Hospitalized-Recovered transmission model, and historical reconstructions of the 1918, 1957, and 1968 pandemics using mortality data. We evaluated official planning scenarios for the United Kingdom, Japan, and the United States, comparing projected demand against national surge capacities (i.e., staffed beds). To test the theoretical limits of the stockpile strategy, we applied best-case assumptions, including perfect distribution of antivirals to 100% of symptomatic cases and high clinical effectiveness (30% to 60% reduction in hospitalization). Our models identified a critical feasibility gap. While stockpiles successfully suppressed demand to manageable levels in moderate scenarios (analogous to 1957/1968), they were structurally insufficient for severe events. In high-severity scenarios (analogous to 1918 or CDC Very Severe parameters), the daily surge of patients exceeded available hospital capacity by a factor of 5-9. This inundation occurred even under the assumption of 100% treatment coverage, rendering antivirals incapable of preventing transition to crisis standards of care. Although this analysis is subject to the inherent uncertainties of future pandemics, our use of optimistic best-case assumptions suggests that the identified structural failures are a lower-bound estimate. Realistic operational hurdles would only widen the disparity between stockpile targets and system capacity. The main limitations of this study's methodology are its inherent optimistic bias, specifically the use of a conservative 4-day hospital length of stay that underestimates prolonged intensive care needs, the reliance on general hospital beds as a proxy that abstracts away from critical sub-system bottlenecks, and the assumption of guaranteed antiviral efficacy against novel strains.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that large reserves cannot overcome the rigid physical constraints of healthcare systems, even under the optimistic assumption of perfect distribution. Consequently, the conventional 25% coverage target for antiviral stockpiles, a hallmark of legacy planning, presents a critical opportunity for re-evaluation. As global stocks near expiration, policymakers are uniquely positioned to leverage this inflection point by exploring a capacity-based framework. This adaptive paradigm suggests incorporating a synergistic mix of targeted reserves, temporary non-pharmaceutical interventions, and flexible delivery options, such as decentralized home-first care. Together, these integrated measures could serve as a vital temporal bridge, preserving system integrity until vaccine deployment.

articles.title: Phase 2 Trial of 89Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
articles.abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) imaging is currently suboptimal, which may limit patient care. Zirconium 89 (89Zr) deferoxamine (DFO)-daratumumab is a novel CD38-targeted immuno-PET tracer. Purpose To compare 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT against standard-of-care fluorine 18 (18F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT for detection of MM. Materials and Methods Participants with MM were accrued to this prospective phase 2 trial between March 2022 and July 2025. Standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT and bone marrow biopsy were performed, along with research 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT. If there were discrepant lesions between the two scans, image-guided biopsy was considered as the reference standard. The McNemar test was used to compare disease detection between the two imaging modalities. Results This study included 60 participants (median age, 63 years [IQR, 57-71 years]; 32 women). 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 43% (26 of 60; 95% CI: 31, 57) of participants, and 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 47% (28 of 60; 95% CI: 33, 60) of participants. While there was no overall difference in disease detection between the two imaging modalities (P = .81), MM was demonstrated only with 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT in 13% (eight of 60) of participants, with subsequent biopsy confirmation of active myeloma. Conclusion In participants with MM, CD38-targeted 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab immuno-PET helped detect active myeloma in some participants with no signs of disease at 18F-FDG PET/CT. Clinical trial registration no. NCT04814615 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Choyke in this issue.

articles.title: Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions (PROCEM): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Background Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) is increasingly used in breast cancer diagnostics; however, randomized trials assessing the added value of CEM in preoperative staging of breast cancer beyond digital mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, and US are lacking. Purpose To assess the added value of CEM for preoperative breast cancer staging in a randomized controlled trial. Materials and Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial (Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions) enrolled women diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer eligible for primary surgery at two breast centers in Sweden. Participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative CEM or control from November 2020 through April 2024. The primary outcome was a 10% change in treatment due to preoperative CEM findings. Secondary outcomes included differences in reoperation and mastectomy rates between groups and accuracy of malignant extent estimation with CEM, mammography/tomosynthesis, and US using histopathologic extent as the reference, assessed with Bland-Altman statistics and concordance analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to menopausal status, breast density, histopathologic type of cancer, lesion size, and presence of microcalcifications at baseline imaging. Results In total, 415 participants (median age, 66 years; IQR, 56-73 years) completed the trial: 202 in the CEM group and 213 in the control group. Treatment was changed in 17 of 202 participants (8.4%; 95% CI: 5.3, 13.1) based on CEM findings. No evidence of differences was observed between the CEM and control groups with regard to mastectomy (17% [35 of 202] vs 18% [39 of 213]; P = .78) or reoperation (7.9% [16 of 202] vs 10% [22 of 213]; P = .39) rates. CEM showed the closest agreement with histopathologic malignant extent (bias, 3.5 mm), outperforming mammography and/or tomosynthesis (4.8 mm) and US (10.7 mm) overall and in nine of 10 predefined subgroups, except for ductal carcinoma in situ. Conclusion This trial did not meet its primary end point of a 10% treatment change; however, preoperative CEM improved malignant extent estimation. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04437602 © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Mesurolle and El Khoury in this issue.

articles.title: Exosomes in Traumatic Brain Injury: From Secondary Injury Mechanisms to Cell-Free Neurorepair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of death and long-term neurological disability worldwide. Exosomes (EXOs) have attracted increasing attention because they mediate intercellular communication and show promise as diagnostic biomarkers and cell-free therapeutics. However, the overall research landscape and evolving priorities of exosomes studies in TBI remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: We performed a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus (search date: October 24, 2025) using equivalent search strategies combining traumatic brain injury and exosome/extracellular vesicle terms. English-language original research and review articles published between January 1, 2012 and October 24, 2025 were eligible; editorials, letters, conference abstracts, and non-English publications were excluded. After deduplication and screening, 609 publications were retained. A multi-tool analytical framework was employed: CiteSpace (v6.4.R1) for citation-burst detection, co-occurrence clustering, and timeline visualization; VOSviewer (v1.6.18) for collaboration network mapping and keyword co-occurrence analysis; and the Bibliometrix R package (v4.4.3) for descriptive statistics, productivity indicators (h-index, g-index, m-index), and performance metrics.

RESULTS: From 2012 to 2025, research on exosomes in TBI expanded steadily, with accelerated growth after 2017. Keyword co-occurrence, citation-burst detection, and reference co-citation analyses showed a clear thematic evolution. Early studies and highly co-cited references primarily addressed secondary-injury mechanisms, particularly neuroinflammation, microglial activation, glial-neuronal interactions, and blood-brain barrier dysfunction. Influential work by frequently co-cited authors (e.g., Chopp M and Zhang Y) helped establish exosomes-mediated neuroprotection and neurovascular remodeling as central themes. More recently, burst keywords and emerging co-citation clusters have shifted toward mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes, cell-free therapeutic strategies, engineered exosomes, drug delivery systems, and regenerative medicine, reflecting a transition from mechanistic exploration to translational application. This shift has coincided with the growing prominence of journals such as the International Journal of Molecular Sciences, Journal of Neurotrauma, Cells, and Neural Regeneration Research as major publication venues for the field.

CONCLUSION: This study maps the global landscape of exosomes research in TBI and traces its evolution from pathogenesis to regenerative therapy. The United States and China stand out as complementary leaders, with American groups focusing on mechanisms and biomarkers and Chinese groups driving therapeutic translation. Future priorities for clinical translation include standardized isolation protocols, optimal dosing regimens, and rigorous clinical trials. Together, these findings offer a practical framework to guide the development of exosome-based therapies for TBI.

articles.title: Effects of Vitamin D 3 Supplementation on Glycaemic Parameters and Insulin Sensitivity in Pre-diabetic Adults: A Prospective Controlled Interventional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-diabetes precedes type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and is characterised by impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance or both. Vitamin D deficiency is prevalent in India and implicated in impaired glucose metabolism and insulin resistance, yet interventional data from Indian pre-diabetic populations remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of oral Vitamin D 3 supplementation on fasting blood glucose (FBG), post-prandial blood glucose (PPBG) and Homeostatic Model Assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) in pre-diabetic adults.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective controlled interventional study enrolled 90 pre-diabetic adults (aged 18-65 years) at SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Chennai. Participants were allocated into a Vitamin D group ( n = 45; oral Vitamin D 3 2000 IU once daily for 3 months plus lifestyle advice) and a control group ( n = 45; lifestyle advice alone). FBG, PPBG, HbA1c, fasting insulin, serum 25(OH) D and HOMA-IR were assessed at baseline and 3 months.

RESULTS: The Vitamin D group demonstrated significant reductions in FBG (112.6 ± 8.4-102.4 ± 7.3 mg/dL), PPBG (168.5 ± 15.2-150.8 ± 13.6 mg/dL), HOMA-IR (4.38 ± 1.02-3.41 ± 0.89) and HbA1c (6.1% ±0.3% to 5.7% ±0.2%) ( P < 0.001 for all), with significantly greater improvements than controls ( P < 0.001). Serum 25(OH) D rose from 18.4 ± 4.5 to 27.6 ± 2.8 ng/mL ( P < 0.001). Glycaemic normalisation occurred in 40% versus 11% of controls ( P = 0.002). A significant inverse correlation was observed between Δ25(OH) D and ΔHOMA-IR ( r = -0.62, P < 0.001). No serious adverse events were recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: Vitamin D 3 supplementation significantly improved glycaemic control and insulin sensitivity in pre-diabetic adults, supporting its role as a safe, cost-effective adjunct to lifestyle modification in pre-diabetes management.

articles.title: Impact of Medication Therapy Management on Patient Knowledge and Adherence in Oral Anticoagulant Use.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The deficiencies in patient knowledge and adherence constitute a significant obstacle to optimal utilisation of oral anticoagulants, resulting in diminished safety and effectiveness.

AIM: The aim of the study was to assess the impact of pharmacist-led medication therapy management (MTM) on knowledge and adherence outcomes in patients on oral anticoagulants.

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: An observational-cohort study was conducted in the surgery, cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery departments. A clinical pharmacist trained in MTM services conducted the MTM sessions according to the guidelines. The follow-up of the patients was conducted at scheduled visits to the hospital at 0, 4 and 8 months. The knowledge and adherence outcomes were assessed through a repeated measures analysis of variance, with P < 0.05 was statistically significant.

RESULTS: Out of 100 patients, 94 patients were followed up on, and their data were analysed. The commonly prescribed oral anticoagulants were acenocoumarol (34%) and warfarin (29%). The baseline knowledge and adherence scores on oral anticoagulant medications were 43.40 ± 19.37 and 51.59 ± 25.34. The MTM services were provided after 4-month and 8-month intervals, knowledge scores were 71.38 ± 14.99 and 82.97 ± 9.92, and the adherence scores were 80.45 ± 11.95 and 88.56 ± 9.64, respectively. Thirty-four adverse drug reactions were reported, with an International Normalized Ratio range >6 for which anticoagulation reversal agents were used.

CONCLUSION: The clinical pharmacist-led MTM services significantly improved knowledge ( P < 0.001) and adherence ( P < 0.001) of patients treated with oral anticoagulants at different time intervals. The pharmacist's role in anticoagulation management service will be helpful for physicians to optimise and maintain the dose.

articles.title: Comparison of Traumatic Complications following Prostate Biopsy in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Due to Prostate Disease Using Biopty Gun versus Semiautomatic Needle.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate biopsy has evolved to improve yield and reduce complications. The development of biopty guns added to this trend. It is an improvement on the semiautomatic needle.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare semi-automatic and fully-automatic biopsy devices used for digitally guided transrectal prostate biopsy for the rate and extent of post-biopsy pain and bleeding complications.

METHODOLOGY: Sixty-four patients were randomised into two groups, each with 32 patients. Group 1 patients were biopsied with 16G Medplus ® semi-automatic biopsy needles, whereas Bard-Magnum ® biopty gun with 16G needles was used for Group 2. Twelve systematic cores were taken from both groups. Post-biopsy pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale and Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale. The rate and extent of post-biopsy haematuria/urethral bleeding and rectal bleeding were evaluated. Data were collected using a structured pro forma and analysed using IBM-SPSS.

RESULTS: Sixty-four men participated in the study. Haematuria/urethral bleeding occurred in 37.5% (12) and 31.25% (10) patients in Groups 1 and 2, respectively. Bladder irrigation was done for 8.3% (1) and 20% (2) of those who bled from Groups 1 and 2, respectively. Significant rectal bleeding occurred in 31.25% (10) and 28.13% (9) patients from Groups 1 and 2, respectively. More pain was noted in Group 1. These differences in bleeding complications and pain were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: The two devices did not exhibit significant differences in terms of pain or bleeding complications when used for prostate biopsy.

articles.title: Dynamics of the Prevalence of Non-communicable Diseases in the Urban Double Cotonou - Abomey-Calavi (South of Benin).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The on going demographic transition in African countries like Benin is promoting changes in lifestyle and intensifying the emergence of non communicable diseases (NCDs), a marker of the epidemiological transition.

OBJECTIVE: This research aims to analyse the influence of demographic dynamics on NCDs in Cotonou and Abomey Calavi.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: The methodological approach is based on documentary research and interviews with stakeholders. Technical and general documents were consulted throughout all phases of the research. In total, 58 semi structured interviews were conducted with medical practitioners identified through purposive sampling, as well as 761 questionnaires addressed to heads of households (409) and individuals diagnosed with NCDs (352). The sample size was determined according to the principle of empirical saturation and the Cochran formula. The prevalence of each pathology is obtained based on the variables provided in the survey questionnaires. The prevalence of a disease is the proportion of people affected by that disease observed at a given point in time. The analysis of multiple correspondence and multinomial logistic regression allowed for the assessment of interrelations and the contribution of variables to the prevalence of NCDs.

RESULTS: The results show that the gender structure of the population in the pair shows a slight predominance of women. The indicators of youth and old age show a significant young population, still marked by gradual aging, but which bodes well for the prospects of a demographic dividend. Similarly, the results show that hypertension is the most prevalent condition at 48.1%, followed by diabetes (14.6%), chronic respiratory diseases (10%) and cancers (2.5%). Research into risk factors proves that age, gender, place of residence education level, size of siblings and household and marital status significantly influence the risk of NCDs. Thus, the probability of having an NCD increases with age. A higher level of education is associated with a lower risk of diabetes and chronic kidney disease. Married individuals or those in a monogamous partnership have a lower risk of hypertension, which could be related to better social support. Urban living is associated with a higher risk of hypertension and cancers, probably due to environmental and lifestyle factors. Similarly, physical activity is associated with a reduced risk of NCDs. A higher intake of fruits and vegetables is linked to a reduced risk of diabetes, whereas alcohol consumption is inversely associated.

CONCLUSION: Demographic dynamics and lifestyle changes in the Cotonou-Abomey-Calavi urban area contribute significantly to the increase in non-communicable diseases, highlighting the need to strengthen prevention policies and promote healthy lifestyles.

articles.title: A Comparative Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Two Misoprostol Regimens for Labour Induction at Term in Delta State: A Two-centre Triple-blind Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal administration of misoprostol for induction of labour (IOL), including its efficacy and safety, remains an issue in obstetrics.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate and compare the efficacy and safety of hourly Titrated oral misoprostol (TOM) doses and four-hourly vaginal misoprostol (VM) for labour induction at term in a multi-centre setting in Delta State, Nigeria.

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A total of 260 singleton term pregnancies were randomised using computer-generated numbers and opaque envelopes. The study compared the efficacy of hourly titrated oral misoprostol solution against four-hourly 25 mcg vaginal tablets. The primary outcome measure was the vaginal delivery rate within 24 h. The secondary outcomes included duration of active labour, time from induction initiation to delivery, caesarean section rate, total oxytocin dosage, presence of foetal heart rate abnormalities, abnormal uterine contractions and uterine rupture. Data analysis, utilising Chi-square and Student's t -tests, was conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows (Version 28.0; IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).

RESULTS: Women in the hourly titrated oral misoprostol group demonstrated a significantly higher rate of vaginal delivery within 24 h (96.2%) compared to the four-hourly VM group (83.1%) ( P < 0.338). Significant differences were observed between the groups in the rates of abnormal uterine contractions ( χ2 = 5.969, P = 0.015), abnormal foetal heart rate patterns ( χ2 = 6.660, P = 0.018) and caesarean section rates ( χ2 = 5.426, P = 0.015). No cases of uterine rupture occurred in either group during the study period.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated comparable efficacy between hourly titrated oral misoprostol and four-hourly VM for labour induction. However, hourly titrated oral misoprostol exhibited a more favourable safety profile, as regards abnormal uterine contractions, foetal heart rate patterns and caesarean section rate.

articles.title: Urinary Volatile Organic Compounds as Pharmacodynamic Biomarkers in Sodium-glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor-treated Diabetic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors confer renoprotection in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) through haemodynamic, anti-inflammatory and metabolic mechanisms, including hepatic ketogenesis induction. A recent investigation by Hara et al . demonstrated measurable elevations in urinary volatile organic compounds (VOCs), specifically acetone and 2-pentanone, in SGLT2 inhibitor-treated DKD patients using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, providing direct metabolomic evidence of pharmacodynamic ketogenic interaction. This review contextualises these findings within the mechanistic framework of SGLT2 inhibitor-mediated renoprotection, particularly ketone body-induced suppression of mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 in proximal tubular cells. This manuscript proposes three clinically actionable roles for urinary VOC monitoring: as a pharmacodynamic biomarker of drug engagement, a longitudinal marker of renoprotective responsiveness and a non-invasive early warning signal for euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis. A pragmatic four-step algorithmic framework is presented to guide clinicians in integrating urinary VOC profiling with established DKD monitoring parameters. The key limitations including analytical confounders, acetoacetate instability and the need for point-of-care technology development are discussed in this minireview. Urinary VOC metabolomics represents a promising frontier in precision nephrology and individualised SGLT2 inhibitor-mediated DKD management.

articles.title: Alcohol Consumption in Nigerian Pregnant Women and Maternal and Foetal Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: The objectives of this systematic review were to provide a comprehensive overview of existing knowledge, assess the quality of the evidence, identify research gaps and propose directions for future research on the prevalence, predictors and maternal and foetal effects of alcohol consumption among pregnant Nigerian women. Eligibility Criteria: The Inclusion Criteria: Scientific research studies published in, or translated into the English language, in peer-reviewed local or international journals, presented at scientific conferences or published as technical reports from 1 June 2015 to 31 May 2025. These included observational studies such as cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies. Exclusion Criteria: Editorials, commentaries and opinion pieces on the themes of study with no original research data; case reports and series with a sample size of <10, which may provide insufficient data for a comprehensive analysis; non-peer-reviewed articles and unpublished theses/dissertations, due to concerns about the verifiability of data and research quality; studies in which full texts were not accessible and studies not published in, or translated into English. Information Sources: Search engines and databases, including Google Scholar, PubMed, EBSCOhost, Medline, ScienceDirect, Directory of Open Access Journals and African Index Medicus (AIM), as well as the websites of the Federal Ministry of Health, Nigeria; the World Health Organization, Africa region and UNFPA, Nigeria. Risk of bias: The AXIS appraisal tool was used to assess the risk of bias/quality of cross-sectional studies, while the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa quality assessment scale was used for cohort studies included in this study. Synthesis of results: A narrative synthesis approach was used to summarise the eligible literature. We included information on the authors and date of publication, research design, description of the population and setting, research results, study characteristics, methodologies and outcomes, limitations of the research and the quality of the selected studies (risk of bias assessment), while noting patterns and discrepancies across studies. Included studies: 14 hospital-based studies; 13 cross-sectional and one cohort study. Synthesis of results. Prevalence of alcohol consumption: All 14 studies reviewed reported on the prevalence of alcohol consumption during pregnancy. The highest prevalence of 59.3% was reported in the South-South, while the lowest prevalence of 4.0% was reported in the Southwest Geopolitical Zone. There was no data available in the reviewed studies on the prevalence of alcohol consumption during the first, second and third trimesters of pregnancy. Predictors of alcohol use: Five studies explored the predictors or determinants of alcohol use during pregnancy in Nigeria. The studies consistently reported behavioural factors, including marital dissatisfaction, pre-pregnancy alcohol consumption and lack of awareness of the harmful effects of alcohol use on the foetus and tobacco smoking, as predictors of alcohol use. The studies also consistently reported that marital status, the level of family wealth, body mass index, history of stillbirth, history of induced abortion, history of miscarriage and grandmultiparity were protective against alcohol consumption. The findings regarding the effects of younger maternal age, educational status and affiliation with different Christian congregations on alcohol consumption during pregnancy were inconsistent. The study unearthed gaps in knowledge, including whether many obstetric and behavioral factors, like unplanned pregnancies, teenage pregnancy, partner alcohol consumption and co-consumption of other psychoactive drugs, such as tobacco, among others, are predictors of alcohol consumption during pregnancy. No data were available in the reviewed studies on the effects of alcohol consumption on the mother and the foetus.

articles.title: Transcranial Pulse Stimulation in Parkinson's Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS) is an emerging ultrasound-based neuromodulation technique with potential applications in Parkinson's disease (PD). This systematic review evaluated its clinical efficacy, neurophysiological and neuroimaging effects, safety, and certainty of evidence.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were systematically searched for clinical studies investigating TPS in adults with idiopathic PD. Motor, non-motor, cognitive, neurophysiological, neuroimaging, and safety outcomes were narratively synthesized because of methodological heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed, and evidence certainty was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: Four studies involving 80 participants were included: two sham-controlled studies, one prospective open-label pilot study, and one retrospective uncontrolled study. Uncontrolled studies reported improvements in motor function, non-motor symptoms, cognition, mood, and quality of life. However, a randomized double-blind crossover trial demonstrated no superiority of active TPS over sham for global motor scores (MDS-UPDRS Part III). Significant improvements in left-hand manual dexterity persisted for one month and were accompanied by sensorimotor activation and white-matter changes. A single-session study reported immediate resting-tremor reduction, although sustained superiority over sham remained uncertain. Electroencephalographic findings suggested cortical oscillatory modulation. No serious treatment-related adverse events were reported. Evidence certainty ranged from moderate to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: TPS shows preliminary potential to modulate sensorimotor networks and improve selected motor outcomes in PD. However, evidence remains insufficient to establish overall clinical efficacy. Larger, rigorously controlled trials are required to determine sustained benefits, optimal stimulation protocols, and long-term safety.

articles.title: Subcutaneous Furosemide for Ambulatory Decongestion in Heart Failure: Outcomes From a High-Risk Real-World Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Volume overload remains a primary driver of heart failure hospitalization (HFH). Diuretic resistance limits the efficacy of oral loop diuretics during decompensation, often necessitating intravenous therapy. Subcutaneous (SC) furosemide (Furoscix, 80 mg/10 mL) represents a novel outpatient alternative for patients who remain symptomatic despite oral diuretic therapy.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical outcomes of SC furosemide in ambulatory heart failure (HF) patients inadequately managed with oral loop diuretics.

METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of HF patients prescribed SC furosemide as an adjunct to oral loop diuretics between May 2023 and 2025. The primary outcome was HFH within 30 days of initiation. Secondary outcomes included a composite of HFH or urgent care or emergency department visits requiring intravenous diuresis, change in body weight, and New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class.

RESULTS: Fifty patients met the inclusion criteria; one was excluded for incomplete follow-up. SC furosemide was prescribed as two to three doses per week. Within 30 days, 10 patients (20.4%) experienced HFH; six had been hospitalized in the preceding 30 days, suggesting a high-risk baseline cohort. The composite endpoint occurred in 16 patients (32.7%). Among patients who avoided hospitalization, median NYHA class improved from III to II, and mean body weight decreased by 2.6 kg (5.7 lbs). Adverse events were infrequent; no deaths occurred within the 30-day follow-up period.

CONCLUSION: In ambulatory HF patients with persistent congestion despite oral diuretic therapy, SC furosemide was well tolerated and associated with improvements in functional status and volume burden.

articles.title: Joint Associations of Cumulative Triglyceride-Glucose-A Body Shape Index and Frailty Trajectories With Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Middle-Aged and Older Chinese Adults.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine the independent and joint associations of cumulative triglyceride-glucose-a body shape index (TyG-ABSI) and frailty trajectories with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) in middle-aged and older Chinese adults.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. We calculated cumulative TyG-ABSI as the mean of fasting measurements in 2011 and 2015; we identified frailty trajectories from frailty-index measurements in 2011, 2013, and 2015 using latent class linear mixed models. Survey-ascertained incident CVD was a newly reported physician diagnosis of heart disease or stroke in 2018 or 2020. We used complementary log-log discrete-time survival models with cluster-robust standard errors because exact onset dates were unavailable.

RESULTS: Among 3026 participants, 606 met the study definition of incident CVD. Each 1-SD increase in cumulative TyG-ABSI was associated with higher CVD risk (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.06-1.26), and the higher frailty trajectory was associated with greater risk (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.53-2.39). Relative to low TyG-ABSI/lower frailty, HRs were 1.26 (95% CI 1.04-1.53), 1.87 (1.34-2.61), and 2.43 (1.79-3.29) for high/lower, low/higher, and high/higher groups. Multiplicative and additive interactions were not significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative TyG-ABSI and frailty trajectory were independently associated with survey-ascertained incident CVD. Their joint distribution showed a cumulative risk gradient without statistical synergy. These observational findings support complementary risk stratification, not a validated clinical threshold or causal effect.

articles.title: Phase 1 Evaluation of the Pharmacokinetics of Sevasemten (EDG-5506) for Potential Food Effect and Drug-Drug Interaction With a CYP3A4 Moderate Inhibitor.
articles.abstract: Sevasemten (EDG-5506) is an investigational, small molecule, in development for the treatment of Becker and Duchenne muscular dystrophy. In vitro data suggest sevasemten is a substrate for cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A4. Here, we investigate whether the pharmacokinetics (PK) of sevasemten are affected when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, verapamil. The impact of a high-fat meal on the PK of sevasemten was also investigated. This Phase 1, open-label, parallel study of healthy subjects dosed three unique cohorts (sevasemten alone, sevasemten co-administered with verapamil, and sevasemten under fed conditions). Administration of a single dose of sevasemten with daily dosing of verapamil had no significant effect on the maximum concentration (Cmax) or area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC) of sevasemten compared to a single dose of sevasemten under fasted conditions (Geometric mean ratios of 101.6% and 97.5%, respectively), indicating that the PK of sevasemten may not be influenced by verapamil, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Administration of a single dose of sevasemten under fed conditions increased the AUCs of sevasemten by 20% to 38%, while the Cmax remained comparable to that under fasted conditions. Together, these data support allowing patients who benefit from sevasemten to also use a moderate CYP3A inhibitor without dose modification and support administration of sevasemten without regard to food intake.

articles.title: Primary Tracheal Lymphoma Mimicking Asthma Exacerbation.
articles.abstract: A 88-year-old woman with refractory wheezing and a transient response to corticosteroids was diagnosed with primary tracheal B-cell lymphoma causing airway stenosis. Emergency radiotherapy markedly improved the stenosis. Tracheal lymphoma should be considered in patients with recurrent wheezing despite asthma treatment, even when corticosteroids provide temporary relief.

articles.title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Composition and Tissue Heterogeneity as Predictors of Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large Ischemic Core.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent trials established endovascular thrombectomy efficacy in large ischemic cores, yet outcomes remain heterogeneous despite similar infarct volumes, suggesting that current volumetric assessments may not fully capture tissue viability. We examined whether tissue composition quantified by apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) distribution and tissue heterogeneity within baseline diffusion-weighted imaging lesions are associated with functional outcomes in large-core patients after successful endovascular thrombectomy.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with large vessel occlusion with large ischemic cores (diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume ≥50 mL) achieving successful reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy. We quantified ADC tissue composition as proportions within 3 ADC ranges relative to total diffusion-weighted imaging lesion volume: low (<540), mid (540-700), and high (>700 × 10-6 mm2/s). Separately, tissue heterogeneity was assessed using Shannon entropy, a metric quantifying ADC distribution heterogeneity. The primary outcome was 3-month good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-3), analyzed via adjusted logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 126 patients (age, 70.8±12.4 years; 60.3% men; diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume, 93.7±41.2 mL), 39.7% achieved a good functional outcome. Both tissue heterogeneity (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 per 0.1-unit increase, 1.09-1.93, P=0.011, area under the curve, 0.671) and mid-ADC fraction (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78 per 5% increase, 1.20-2.63, P=0.004, area under the curve, 0.688) were associated with good functional outcomes. Neither low-ADC nor high-ADC fractions showed significant associations with functional outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher mid-ADC (540-700 × 10-6 mm2/s) fraction and greater tissue heterogeneity predicted favorable outcomes in patients with large ischemic core, indicating that tissue composition within the ischemic core, beyond its volume, is associated with functional outcome after reperfusion. Among large-core patients who achieved successful reperfusion, ADC-based tissue characterization may help predict functional outcome.

articles.title: Outcomes Following First-Pass Direct Aspiration Versus Stent Retriever for Endovascular Thrombectomy in Primary Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: An Analysis of the SVIN Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy is increasingly performed for acute ischemic stroke due to medium vessel occlusion (MeVO); however, recent randomized trials-primarily using stent retriever (SR) techniques-have not demonstrated a clear benefit over medical management. This study aimed to compare the direct aspiration first-pass technique (ADAPT) and SR in MeVO using a multicenter endovascular thrombectomy consortium.

METHODS: The Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology registry was queried for all primary MeVO cases treated with ADAPT or SR as the first-pass technique. MeVO was defined as an occlusion of A1, P1, M2, or beyond. Outcomes included time to recanalization, recanalization rates, first-pass effect (defined as Treatment in Cerebral Infarction-3 after first pass), intracranial hemorrhage, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 1391 patients with MeVO were identified; 415 (29.8%) in the ADAPT group and 976 (70.2%) in the SR group. The most common location of occlusion was the middle cerebral artery-M2 (75.9%), followed by the middle cerebral artery-M3 (11.4%). The median age was 70, and 698 (50.4%) patients were men. Time from angio-suite arrival to expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) ≥2b (54 versus 60, P=0.002), time from endovascular access to final recanalization (42 versus 52, P<0.001), time from endovascular access to eTICI 2b (31 versus 39, P<0.001), and eTICI 3 (26 versus 34, P<0.001) were shorter for the ADAPT group. Conversely, the SR group had higher rates of eTICI ≥2b (91.6% versus 86.3%, P=0.002) and first-pass effect (31.7% versus 23.4%, P=0.002). Rates of good outcome, excellent outcome, intracranial hemorrhage, and sICH were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Although ADAPT yielded faster recanalization, SR achieved a higher first-pass effect and slightly higher recanalization rates. Intracranial hemorrhage, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and clinical outcomes were comparable between groups. This study suggests that both techniques may offer distinct advantages. Prospective randomized controlled studies are warranted to further understand the safety and efficacy of ADAPT versus the SR technique in patients with MeVO.

articles.title: Superbore Aspiration Catheters: An Innovation in Mechanical Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has become the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusion. Aspiration thrombectomy has evolved substantially over the past decade; however, conventional large-bore aspiration catheters (inner diameter ≥0.068″) may be limited by incomplete clot ingestion, distal embolization, and dependence on adjunctive devices such as balloon guide catheters to achieve proximal flow arrest. Superbore aspiration catheters, typically defined by an inner diameter ≥0.080 inches, are the most recent technological advancement in aspiration thrombectomy. Superbore catheters have the ability to navigate to the M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery, facilitating local flow control, complete clot ingestion, and distal flow reversal during aspiration. Since 2020, several superbore systems have been developed, including Zoom 88 (Imperative Care), HiPoint 88 (Route 92 Medical), Millipede88 (Perfuze), SOFIA 88 (Terumo), Broadway 8 (Stryker Neurovascular), and Cereglide 92 (Johnson & Johnson MedTech). Early clinical studies suggest that superbore catheters may improve first-pass effect and final reperfusion rates compared with standard aspiration thrombectomy devices, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile. This review summarizes the design characteristics, clinical evidence, and procedural considerations associated with currently available superbore systems. Although preliminary data are promising, further randomized clinical trials are needed to determine the optimal role of superbore aspiration in large vessel occlusion treatment.

articles.title: Shockwave Lithotripsy for Severe Calcified Extracranial Vertebral and Carotid Disease Treated With Percutaneous Stenting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients harboring heavily calcified concentric or eccentric type lesions in the carotid or vertebral artery pose a challenge in placing a stent to reduce the lesion. These lesions yield suboptimal results due to poor stent expansion. Shockwave lithotripsy offers a potential solution for achieving luminal gain.

METHODS: We present a retrospective study of all patients at our institution who were treated with lithotripsy for extracranial carotid or vertebral artery stenosis associated with heavily calcified lesions from July 2022 to February 2026. Data were maintained in our procedural database and retrospectively analyzed for patients treated with lithotripsy. All consecutive patients were analyzed for demographic information, procedural data, perioperative complications, and 6-month midterm follow-up imaging for restenosis.

RESULTS: A total of 41 patients (8 vertebral artery lesions and 33 carotid lesions) were treated with intravascular lithotripsy at our institution between July 2022 and February 2026. The mean age for the cohort was 70.7 ± 8.7. The mean lesion pretreatment for the carotid stenosis was 77 ± 13% and for the vertebral artery treated patients 81 ± 11%. All patients were successfully treated with stenting and lithotripsy, and the mean stenosis posttreatment was 15 ± 14% for the carotid stenosis and 8 ± 5% for the vertebral artery lesions. There were 2 groin complications (5%) with femoral artery pseudoaneurysms treated with thrombin injection and 1 perioperative stroke (3%) secondary to a dissection in the carotid stent cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: The current study demonstrates the feasibility of lithotripsy for heavily calcified lesions treated with transfemoral stenting. Future prospective core laboratory adjudicated studies are warranted to determine the efficacy of this technique.

articles.title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome.

RESULTS: Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979]; P=0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes (P=0.115).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

articles.title: The Two Cultures of Prevalence Mapping: Small Area Estimation and Model-Based Geostatistics.
articles.journal: Statistical science : a review journal of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics
articles.abstract: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), accurate estimates of subnational health and demographic indicators are critical for guiding policy and identifying disparities. Many indicators of interest are proportions of binary outcomes and the task of estimating these fractions is often called prevalence mapping. In LMICs, health and vital records data are limited, so prevalence mapping relies on data from household surveys with complex sampling designs. However, estimates are often desired at spatial resolutions at which data are insufficient for reliable weighted estimation. We review two families of approaches to prevalence mapping: small area estimation (SAE) methods (from the survey statistics literature) and model-based geostatistics (MBG) methods (from the spatial statistics literature). SAE models can be "area-level" or "unit-level" and commonly use area-specific random effects and rely upon high-quality covariate data, often obtained from administrative sources. Unit-level models for binary responses are relatively underdeveloped. MBG approaches explicitly specify binary response models, incorporate continuous spatial random effects, and leverage alternative sources of data such as those arising from satellite imagery. These models are usually studied under a Bayesian framework. SAE methods often address the design by incorporating sampling weights or modeling the sampling mechanism. Two delicate issues arise when using MBG methods for prevalence mapping. First, aggregating unit level predictions to create area-level summaries requires population-level information that is rarely directly available. Second, MBG approaches typically assume the sampling design is ignorable. We review both SAE and MBG approaches to prevalence mapping, and argue that binary response models can be improved using insights from both the survey sampling and the spatial statistics literature. We highlight these issues using household survey data from the Zambia 2018 Demographic Health Survey to estimate subnational HIV prevalence for woman aged 15-49.

articles.title: Osseous and Vascular Course Anomalies in Nontraumatic Vertebral Artery Dissection: A Per-Vessel Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vertebral artery (VA) dissection (VAD) is a common cause of stroke in young and middle-aged adults. Although many cases are idiopathic, we hypothesized that overlooked osseous and vascular course anomalies (hereafter, structural anomalies) may be associated with VAD. In this study, we investigated the prevalence of these structural anomalies in patients with nontraumatic VAD using per-vessel analysis.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center case-control study, we analyzed structural anomalies in 13 consecutive patients (26 vessels) diagnosed with nontraumatic VAD at our institution between January 2022 and December 2025. For comparison, all eligible control patients during the same period whose computed tomography angiography field of view fully included the cervical region required to assess high-entry VA were included (50 patients, 100 vessels). The anatomic relationship between the VA and adjacent cervical osseous structures was evaluated using 3-dimensional computed tomography angiography. Primary end points were arcuate foramen presence, high-entry VA, and craniovertebral junction malformation with persistent first intersegmental artery. Images were independently evaluated by 2 neurosurgeons.

RESULTS: Structural anomalies were identified in 76.9% (20/26) of the vessels in the VAD group, compared with 11.0% (11/100) in the control group (P=1.21 × 10-10; odds ratio, 25.75 [95% CI, 7.99-96.9]). At the patient level, structural anomalies were present on the ipsilateral side in 12 out of 13 patients (92.3%) and on the contralateral side in 8 out of 13 (61.5%); this paired difference did not reach statistical significance (exact McNemar test, P=0.219). The arcuate foramen (50.0%) and high-entry VA (19.2%) were the most common sites in the VAD group. Interrater reliability was excellent (raw agreement, 99.0%; κ=0.95 [95% CI, 0.86-1.00]).

CONCLUSIONS: The findings support the possibility that some VADs traditionally considered idiopathic may be associated with mechanically mediated injury within a broader spectrum related to the concept of bony stroke.

articles.title: High-Volume Thrombectomy Centers Reduce In-Hospital Mortality in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Results From the German Stroke Registers Study Group.
Site Versus Core Lab-Adjudicated First- and Final-Pass eTICI Scores Compared During Off and Normal Hours: Insights From the ASSIST Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data from the ASSIST registry were analyzed to assess whether site-reported expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) scores differ from those reported by the core lab during off hours compared with normal hours. We also assessed whether outcomes are worse in procedures performed during off hours.

METHODS: Details from the registry have been previously published. Regression models were performed for first-pass treatment of target occlusion resulting in ≥2c by the core lab, agreement for final pass ≥2c, modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2 at 90 days, and whether first-pass eTICI ≥2c agreed between the core lab and site-reported assessments.

RESULTS: A total of 1318 patients were included. Overall, agreement between core-lab and site-reported eTICI for first-pass eTICI ≥2c occurred in 86.7% and 78.5% for final eTICI ≥2c. Agreement for first-pass and final-pass eTICI ≥2c occurred in 87.2% and 77.7% during normal hours and 86.1% and 79.3% during off hours. Good functional outcomes occurred in 55.5% of patients presenting during normal hours and 53.8% of patients presenting during off hours. Off-hour versus normal-hour procedures were not significantly associated with first-pass efficacy, modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2 at 90 days, or whether first-pass eTICI agreed between the core lab and site-reported assessments in adjusted regression analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: There was a higher level of agreement between core-lab and site-reported first-pass eTICI scores during all hours, while agreement occurred less often for final reperfusion. These results suggest a high level of correlation regardless of the time of the procedure between site-adjudicated and core-lab-adjudicated successful reperfusion grading. There were no significant differences in outcomes irrespective of the timing of thrombectomy.

articles.title: Impact of White Matter Hyperintensities on Reperfusion Injury and Clinical Outcome After Successful Recanalization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reperfusion injury (RI) is a major contributor to poor outcomes after successful recanalization in anterior circulation-large vessel occlusion. White matter hyperintensities (WMH) reflect chronic microvascular injury and are often associated with blood-brain barrier dysfunction or cerebral autoregulation impairment and may increase vulnerability to RI. We examined the association between WMH severity, RI, and clinical outcomes after successful recanalization.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 236 patients with anterior circulation-large vessel occlusion who achieved modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥2b. WMH severity was assessed using the Fazekas scale and dichotomized into absent-to-mild (score 0-3) and severe (score 4-6). RI was defined as parenchymal hematoma or malignant cerebral edema. Risk ratio (RR) was calculated, and causal mediation analysis was performed to assess the indirect effect of WMH on poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale of 3-6).

RESULTS: Severe WMH burden was present in 60 (25.4%) cases, RI occurred in 40 (16.9%) cases, and 128 (54.2%) cases had poor outcomes. Severe WMH was associated with an increased risk of RI (RR, 3.52 [95% CI, 1.97-6.29]; P<0.001). RI was independently associated with poor outcome (RR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.01-1.62]; P=0.042), whereas WMH alone was not. In mediation analysis, severe WMH burden was not associated with poor outcome in terms of the total effect (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.78-1.31]; P=0.744), but there was a significant indirect effect of severe WMH on poor outcome through RI (RR, 1.13 [95% CI, 1.04-1.30]; P=0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: Severe WMH burden increases the risk of RI, which in turn adversely affects functional outcomes despite successful recanalization. WMH assessment may aid in identifying patients at higher risk of RI and support clinical risk stratification in anterior circulation-large vessel occlusion.

articles.title: Predictors of Hemorrhagic Transformation After IV Continuous Cangrelor Infusion Initiated During Mechanical Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cangrelor, a fast-acting intravenous P2Y12 receptor inhibitor, is increasingly used during mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke to treat or prevent thrombotic complications. While effective, its use may increase the risk of hemorrhagic transformation (HT). We investigated clinical, imaging, and procedural predictors of HT in this specific patient population.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective post hoc single-center study including 101 patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with intravenous cangrelor initiated directly after mechanical thrombectomy and continued for 12 hours between January 2021 and June 2024. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations between HT and clinical, radiological, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Among the 101 patients included, 25 (24.7%) developed HT, and 9 (8.9%) experienced symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In multivariable analysis, baseline blood glucose (adjusted odds ratio, 6.51 [95% CI, 1.35-31.4]; P=0.02), leukocytosis (adjusted odds ratio, 1.18 [95% CI, 1.00-1.38]; P=0.047), and subarachnoid hemorrhage on postmechanical thrombectomy cone-beam computed tomography (adjusted odds ratio, 16.60 [95% CI, 2.97-92.8]; P=0.0014) were independent predictors of HT. Contrast enhancement was associated with HT in univariate analysis but did not remain significant after adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline blood glucose, leukocytosis, and isolated subarachnoid hemorrhage on postmechanical thrombectomy cone-beam computed tomography emerged as independent predictors of HT. Identifying high-risk patients using readily available clinical and imaging markers may support individualized antiplatelet strategies and help reduce hemorrhagic complications during cangrelor treatment.

articles.title: A Rare Endobronchial Lipoma of the Right Middle Lobe Causing Middle Lobe Syndrome and Recurrent Post-Obstructive Infection in a Patient With Interstitial Lung Disease, Managed by Lung-Sparing Bronchoscopy.
articles.abstract: Endobronchial lipomas are rare benign tumours that can cause airway obstruction and recurrent infection. A 70-year-old smoker with combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema presented with recurrent right middle lobe infections and declining pulmonary function. Computed tomography revealed a fat-density lesion obstructing the middle lobe bronchus, with atelectasis and consolidation. Bronchoscopy and histology confirmed lipoma. Given limited respiratory reserve, lung-sparing flexible bronchoscopy with snare electrocautery and argon plasma coagulation restored airway patency; retained purulent secretions were drained and infection treated. At 2 months, the patient was asymptomatic with radiological resolution; FVC improved from 75% to 83% predicted and DLCO from 35% to 50% predicted. Recovery followed concurrent recanalization, drainage and antimicrobial treatment, whose individual contributions cannot be separated. This case highlights bronchoscopic diagnosis and treatment of benign obstruction in persistent middle lobe disease. Longer surveillance is needed to assess durability.

articles.title: OCEANIC-STROKE: The Wave of the New Antithrombotic Therapy Era.
Risk Factors for Colonization With Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria Among Hospitalized Patients in Bangladesh: An Antibiotic Resistance in Communities and Hospitals (ARCH) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) are frequently linked with healthcare settings, but specific factors associated with colonization within healthcare settings in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain poorly understood. This study explores risk factors for ARB colonization among hospitalized patients in Bangladesh, where 82% were colonized with extended-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (ESCrE), 37% with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), and 21% with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

METHODS: Hospitalized adults from 3 hospitals in Dhaka completed interviews and underwent chart review to assess healthcare exposures. We used bivariate analyses, random forest variable selection, and multivariate logistic regression to identify factors associated with ESCrE, CRE, and MRSA colonization.

RESULTS: ESCrE colonization was associated with admission to a non-medical ward (aOR 2.16-8.57, 95% CI 1.14, 64.4) and hospitalization ≥ 3 days before specimen collection (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.13, 2.69) while being inversely associated with age (≥45 years, aOR 0.54-0.58, 95% CI .29, .99) and carbapenem use (aOR 0.02, 95% CI < .01, .14). CRE colonization was associated with hospitalization ≥ 3 days before specimen collection (aOR 1.56, 95% CI 1.08, 2.23), third-generation cephalosporin use (aOR 2.93, 95% CI 2.02, 4.23), and other beta-lactam use (aOR 4.83, 95% CI 2.65, 8.81). MRSA colonization was inversely associated with third-generation cephalosporin use (OR 0.60, 95% CI .38, .95).

CONCLUSIONS: Antibiotic use, duration of hospitalization, age, and ward type were associated with ARB colonization among hospitalized patients. Further investigations into antibiotic use patterns and infection prevention and control practices may identify modifiable risk factors to reduce ARB in healthcare settings in LMICs.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Stent-Assisted Coiling Versus Coiling Alone for Ruptured Multilobed Aneurysms: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ruptured multilobed intracranial aneurysms present significant procedural challenges and high recurrence risks in endovascular treatment due to complex geometry and turbulent hemodynamics. Currently, the safety and long-term efficacy of stent-assisted coiling (SAC) versus coiling alone in treating this high-risk morphological subgroup remain clinically controversial; high-quality, large-scale evidence is required.

METHODS: Based on a multicenter, prospective registry study (the SANE trial [Subarachnoid Aneurysm Endovascular Cohort Study in China]), 627 consecutive patients with ruptured multilobed intracranial aneurysm treated with SAC or coiling alone were included. Baseline demographics, perioperative safety outcomes (including intraprocedural thrombosis, ischemic stroke, cerebral vasospasm, and rerupture), clinical functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score and mortality), and angiographic morphological outcomes (Raymond-Roy Occlusion Classification) were systematically collected. Overlap weighting (average treatment effect in the overlap population) and doubly robust logistic regression models were applied to evaluate the independent clinical effects of different modalities after strict adjustment for confounders, including anatomic morphology and perioperative parameters.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 173 patients treated with coiling alone and 454 treated with SAC. The primary average treatment effect in the overlap population analysis included 610 patients and yielded a pooled Kish effective sample size of 438.74. Before weighting, perioperative ischemic stroke and intraprocedural thrombosis were more frequent with SAC. After weighting, all 16 prespecified covariates had absolute standardized mean differences <0.10. At follow-up, Raymond-Roy Occlusion Classification class I occlusion was observed in 75.8% of the SAC group and 53.9% of the coiling-alone group (P<0.001). Doubly robust models detected no statistically significant associations between SAC and the evaluated safety outcomes, poor functional outcome at discharge or follow-up, or all-cause mortality (all P≥0.071). SAC was associated with lower odds of follow-up Raymond-Roy Occlusion Classification class II versus I (odds ratio, 0.401 [95% CI, 0.203-0.795]; P=0.012) and class III versus I (odds ratio, 0.583 [95% CI, 0.307-0.806]; P=0.014).

CONCLUSIONS: In this observational ruptured multilobed intracranial aneurysm cohort, SAC was associated with more favorable follow-up angiographic occlusion than coiling alone, without detected differences in perioperative safety or clinical outcomes. These findings do not establish functional superiority and remain subject to residual confounding.
