articles.title: Endovascular Therapy in Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis-Related Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Brief Practice Update and Consensus Statement From the SVIN.
articles.abstract: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis-related large vessel occlusion (ICAS-LVO) represents a distinct subset of acute ischemic stroke with unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges during endovascular therapy. Compared with embolic LVO, ICAS-LVO is associated with higher rates of reocclusion and the frequent use of adjunctive interventions. This Brief Practice Update summarizes current evidence and expert consensus to guide the identification and management of ICAS-LVO during endovascular therapy. The Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards committee convened a multidisciplinary writing group of neurointerventionalists to review available literature and define key clinical questions on ICAS-LVO and endovascular therapy. Evidence was appraised using the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology framework for Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence, adapted from the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association. Draft statements were iteratively refined and approved by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards Quality Committee for adherence to internal standards and endorsed by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Board of Directors. Evidence was derived from randomized trials, multicenter registries, cohort studies, post hoc analyses, and meta-analyses addressing diagnostic features, first-line thrombectomy strategies, and adjunctive therapies in ICAS-LVO. Both stent retriever and direct aspiration approaches are acceptable initial strategies; however, durable recanalization is only achieved in about half of patients. Adjunctive use of intravenous or intra-arterial glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors, balloon angioplasty, and rescue stenting has demonstrated improved recanalization rates and favorable functional outcomes in observational studies, without increased hemorrhagic complications. However, the quality of evidence remains weak. A summary of recommendations is provided to guide practice in common procedural scenarios. This Brief Practice Update provides evidence-based and expert consensus recommendations for the diagnosis and endovascular treatment of ICAS-LVO. Management should be individualized by incorporating the clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and operator expertise. While adjunctive therapy may be beneficial in select cases, high-quality randomized trials are needed to define optimal strategies and establish standardized algorithms for this challenging stroke subtype.

articles.title: Hepatic Overexpression of Lysophospholipid Acyltransferase LPLAT14/MBOAT1 Ameliorates Mild Liver Injury During Early High-Fat Diet Feeding.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) encompasses a spectrum of conditions progressing from simple steatosis to severe steatohepatitis. During this progression, liver injury associated with lipotoxicity and altered membrane phospholipid homeostasis is thought to contribute to disease aggravation. Although lysophospholipid acyltransferases (LPLATs) regulate membrane lipid remodeling and contribute to cellular integrity, the physiological roles of several LPLATs have only partially been characterized, and the in vivo functions of LPLAT14 remain largely unknown. Here, we investigated the effects of hepatic overexpression of LPLAT14 on high-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic disorders and mild liver injury in mice using an improved adenovirus (Ad) vector. Hepatic LPLAT14 overexpression did not significantly alter body weight, systemic glucose tolerance, or hepatic lipid accumulation. Targeted lipidomics revealed that LPLAT14 overexpression selectively significantly increased oleic acid (OA)-containing phosphatidylserine (PS) species in the liver, suggesting selective incorporation of OA into lysophosphatidylserine. This specific lipidomic remodeling significantly attenuated mild liver injury during early HFD feeding, as evidenced by reduced serum alanine aminotransferase levels at 2 weeks after Ad-LPLAT14 treatment. However, this hepatoprotective effect was not observed in the later phase (8 weeks), when severe lipid accumulation had developed, suggesting that LPLAT14 primarily attenuates mild liver injury during early HFD feeding. Collectively, our findings suggest that LPLAT14-mediated enrichment of OA-containing PS attenuates mild liver injury during early HFD feeding, possibly through protection against early cellular stress.

articles.title: A Case of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Thumb-Sized Calcification Detected on Panoramic Radiograph.
articles.abstract: A 73-year-old male with dyslipidemia and chronic kidney disease exhibited carotid calcification on a dental panoramic radiograph. Ultrasonography confirmed 30% asymptomatic carotid stenosis. This case highlights intimal calcification's link to kidney disease and atherosclerosis. Prompt medical-dental collaboration and diagnostic imaging remain crucial to prevent cerebrovascular events, extending healthy life expectancy.

articles.title: Oscillometry bronchodilator response testing identifies distinct pathophysiological phenotypes: a post hoc analysis of the ATLANTIS study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spirometry with bronchodilator response (BDR) testing is the first-line test for asthma in international guidelines; however, it has been shown to have suboptimal sensitivity for asthma diagnosis and detecting small airways dysfunction. Oscillometry with BDR may identify bronchodilator response in patients with no significant BDR by spirometry. The aims of the present study were to determine whether oscillometry identifies additional BDR in the Assessment of Small Airways Involvement in Asthma (ATLANTIS) study asthma cohort compared to spirometry (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT02123667), and to characterise phenotypic differences between BDR groups.

METHODS: Baseline data from 518 adults with objectively confirmed asthma enrolled in ATLANTIS were analysed. Differences in clinical, biomarker and physiological characteristics were assessed between BDR groups. A subset with computed tomography (CT) imaging (208 out of 518) and nasal RNA-sequencing data (236 out of 518) underwent CT biomarker and differential gene expression analysis to investigate differences in airway morphology and pathways underlying a small airways bronchodilator responsive phenotype.

RESULTS: Oscillometry detected significant bronchodilator response in an additional 11% of participants not identified by spirometry, although spirometry identified more responders overall. Spirometry-positive BDR-only cases (group 1) had greater airway obstruction and exhaled nitric oxide fraction (p<0.05) compared with oscillometry-only BDR (group 2). Subgroup analysis identified differentially expressed genes related to mitochondrial stress and cell adhesion in group 3 (BDR in both) versus group 1 and reduced luminal area and greater gas trapping on CT imaging (p<0.05).

INTERPRETATION: Oscillometry identified additional bronchodilator-responsive participants beyond spirometry, indicating complementary physiological information. Distinct BDR patterns were associated with differing inflammatory, physiological and structural features, suggesting distinct asthma phenotypes.

articles.title: D-dimer/NT-proBNP ratio in acute pulmonary embolism patients stratifies risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are ongoing efforts to identify patients at risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during acute pulmonary embolism (APE). Lower D-dimer levels and right heart overload at APE diagnosis were reported to predict CTEPH. We hypothesised that plasma D-dimer to N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ratio assessed during APE may be useful for early CTEPH screening.

METHODS: We followed 342 APE survivors (median age 64.5 years, female 56.1%), for a median of 39 (25-64) months.

RESULTS: Despite ≥3 months anticoagulation CTEPH was diagnosed in 22 (6.4%) patients (CTEPH(+)). At APE diagnosis, CTEPH(+) compared with subjects without this sequela (CTEPH(-)) presented with advanced right ventricular overload: increased tricuspid regurgitation peak gradient (TRPG) (46.5 mmHg versus 32.0 mmHg; p<0.001) and NT-proBNP (1860 ng·L-1 versus 515 ng·L-1; p=0.02). Despite no differences in plasma D-dimer (4210 μg·L-1 versus 5330 μg·L-1; p=0.10), the ratio of D-dimer to NT-proBNP (DD/NT-proBNP) was significantly lower in the CTEPH(+) cohort versus the CTEPH(-) cohort (2.89 μg·ng-1 versus 12.0 μg·ng-1; p<0.001). In patients with DD/NT-proBNP≤10 CTEPH was diagnosed in 20 cases (11.7%), whereas in the group with DD/NT-proBNP> 10 CTEPH could only be detected in 2 of 171 cases (1.2%) with an OR 0.09 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.38; p=0.0013), a sensitivity of 90.9% (95% CI 70.8-98.9%), a specificity 52.8% (95% CI 47.2-58.4%), a negative predictive value 98.8% (95% CI 95.8-99.9%), a and positive predictive value of 11.7% (95% CI 7.3-17.5%). Combination of DD/NT-proBNP≤10 with TRPG≥36 mmHg detected in 87 patients, including 17 patients with CTEPH (19.5% CTEPH incidence).

CONCLUSION: DD/NT-proBNP>10 μg·ng-1 identifies patients with a low risk of subsequent CTEPH diagnosis, whereas DD/NT-proBNP≤10, especially presenting TRPG≥36 mmHg at echocardiography, forms a high risk group at follow-up.

articles.title: A Rare Constellation of Omphalocele, Myelomeningocele, and Encephalocele in a Neonate Born to a Mother With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Pre-gestational diabetes with reported poor glycemic control may be associated with rare and severe multiple congenital anomalies, such as omphalocele and multiple concurrent neural tube defects (NTDs). Early antenatal screening, strict maternal glycemic control, and multidisciplinary neonatal management are crucial to improving outcomes.

articles.title: Five-year outcomes of the STOP-AD randomised controlled trial: Long-term effects of early emollient therapy in high-risk infants.
articles.journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-life skin barrier enhancement has been proposed as a strategy to prevent atopic dermatitis (AD), but results from emollient prevention trials have been inconsistent, and long-term outcomes remain poorly defined. The STOP-AD trial previously demonstrated a reduction in AD incidence following brief early emollient use in high-risk infants. Whether these effects persist beyond infancy is unknown.

METHODS: This study reports the blinded five-year follow-up of the STOP-AD single-centre, randomised controlled trial. Term infants at high risk of AD were randomised within 4 days of birth to either twice-daily whole-body emollient application for the first 8 weeks of life or to standard routine skin care. At 5 years, participants underwent blinded, in-person clinical assessment. AD was diagnosed using UK Working Party Diagnostic Criteria, and disease severity was assessed using SCORAD. Primary outcome was point prevalence of AD at 5 years. Secondary outcomes included AD severity. Complete-case analyses were supplemented by multiple imputation to assess the impact of missing data.

RESULTS: A total of 177 children completed the five-year follow-up. The point prevalence of AD at 5 years was lower in the intervention group than in the control group (12.3% vs. 24.0%; RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.26-1.02; p = .048). Among children with AD, disease severity was also lower in the intervention group (median SCORAD 12.0 [IQR 8.2-15.2] vs. 19.6 [IQR 11.8-23.4]; p = .034). Multiple imputation to account for missing outcome data produced a similar treatment effect (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.19-1.03; p = .060), although with greater uncertainty.

CONCLUSIONS: Early, short-term emollient use initiated in the neonatal period was associated with lower AD prevalence and severity at 5 years in high-risk children. Although the effect estimate remained similar following multiple imputation, uncertainty due to attrition remained. These findings suggest that brief early-life barrier support may influence longer-term AD outcomes and support further investigation of the timing and formulation of preventive skin-barrier interventions.

articles.title: Effect of Exercise Interventions on Sarcopenia-Related Outcomes in Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To systematically evaluate the effects of exercise interventions on sarcopenia-related outcomes and glycemic control in older adults with type 2 diabetes (T2DM).

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-October 2025) for RCTs in adults with T2DM (mean age ≥ 65 years) comparing structured exercise (≥ 4 weeks) with nonexercise control. Co-primary outcomes were lean/appendicular lean mass, muscle strength, and physical performance; secondary outcomes were HbA1c, FPG, and HOMA-IR. Random-effects meta-analyses used Hedges' g for sarcopenia outcomes and mean differences for metabolic outcomes from pre-post changes.

RESULTS: Eleven RCTs (≈740 participants) were included. Exercise produced a small, nonsignificant effect on lean mass (6 trials; g = 0.14, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.37; I2 = 0%). Significant moderate-to-large improvements were found in muscle strength (nine trials; g = 0.67, 95% CI 0.46-0.88; I2 = 11.7%) and physical performance (nine trials; g = 0.74, 95% CI 0.44-1.03; I2 = 64.4%). HbA1c was reduced by 0.32 percentage points (seven trials; I2 = 0%), HOMA-IR improved by 0.51 units (three trials; I2 = 0%), while FPG changes were small and nonsignificant. Adverse events were rare and no serious exercise-related complications occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with T2DM, structured exercise training yields meaningful gains in muscle strength, physical performance, and glycemic control despite only modest effects on lean mass. These findings support resistance-based or multicomponent programs as a core component of care to address both sarcopenia-related impairments and metabolic abnormalities in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Impact of correlated PBPK parameters on intra-patient global sensitivity analysis in molecular radiotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models integrated into digital twins provide a robust framework for optimizing individualized molecular radiotherapy (MRT). Nevertheless, uncertainties in PBPK-model-derived dosimetry can compromise the reliability of dosimetry-guided treatment planning and individualized therapy decisions.

PURPOSE: This study employs intra-patient global sensitivity analysis (GSA) to assess the influence of uncertainty and correlations among PBPK model parameters on estimated kidney and tumor absorbed doses (ADs) in prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted theragnostics.

METHODS: Data from 10 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who underwent pre-therapeutic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-I&T PET/CT and a cycle of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-I&T therapy, followed by post-therapeutic SPECT/CT scans at Days 1 and 4 post-injection, were analyzed. A previously established whole-body PBPK model for PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy was used as the baseline model. Fifteen model parameters, their standard errors, and inter-parameter correlations were estimated by fitting to measured time-activity data and subsequently evaluated using intra-patient GSA based on the Kucherenko method implemented in UQLab. In one approach, correlations were ignored to identify the direct influences of uncertainty in input parameters on ADs. In a second approach, correlations were included to reflect realistic parameter distributions and to capture indirect effects arising from parameter interdependencies. Pharmacokinetics were simulated to estimate therapeutic kidney and tumor ADs as well as main- and total-effect indices (  S i , S i T )   . Sensitivity indices, ADs, and their associated uncertainty metrics were compared between scenarios with and without parameter correlations.

RESULTS: Including parameter correlations in the GSA yielded kidney ADs of 4.2 Gy [3.0-7.2 Gy] (median [min-max]) with standard deviations (SDs) of 0.5 Gy [0.4-0.9 Gy] and tumor ADs of 10.1 Gy [2.0-26.8 Gy] with SDs of 1.7 Gy [0.6-3.4 Gy]. Neglecting correlations resulted in significantly higher uncertainties in ADs, by a factor of 1.2 [1.0-1.8] for both kidneys and tumors. Kidney ADs were most sensitive to kidney receptor density (  S i = 0.3  [ 0.1 -  0.6 ] ,   S i T = 0.7  [ 0.6 - 0.8 ]   ) and to the filtered fraction of renal blood flow ( S i = 0.2  [ 0.1 - 0.3 ] ,   S i T = 0.3  [ 0.1 - 0.4 ] )   . Tumor ADs were most affected by tumor receptor density (  S i = 0.7  [ 0.1 - 1.0 ] ,   S i T = 0.8  [ 0.3 - 1.0 ]   ). The involvement of parameter correlations did not alter the identification of the parameters most influential on AD estimates and further reduced computational runtime.

CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating parameter correlations into intra-patient GSA reduced the estimated uncertainty associated with ADs, underscoring the importance of preserving parameter dependencies when propagating uncertainty in PBPK-based individualized MRT. The identification of key PBPK parameters governing kidney and tumor ADs remained stable when including correlation, confirming the robustness of the underlying model structure.

articles.title: Genotypic-Phenotypic Correlations in Non-HbE β-Thalassemia Intermedia: A Geographic Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: β-thalassemia intermedia (β-TI), now more commonly classified within the spectrum of non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia (NTDT), is a clinically heterogeneous disorder in which disease severity is determined not only by β-globin mutations but also by co-inherited genetic modifiers that vary across populations. These include α-globin gene alterations, fetal haemoglobin (HbF)-inducing polymorphisms, and other regulatory loci that influence globin chain balance.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed was searched from inception to May 2026, supplemented by citation tracking and manual screening. Studies reporting genotype-phenotype correlations in β-TI were included. Data were synthesized qualitatively by geographic region.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included. The available evidence suggests Mediterranean populations are primarily influenced by mild β-globin mutations. In Middle Eastern populations, HbF-inducing polymorphisms, particularly the XmnI variant, played a prominent role, often mitigating severe genotypes. Among the included studies, Asian populations exhibited the greatest molecular heterogeneity, with α-globin gene dosage alterations, including triplication, contributing substantially to disease expression.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests regional differences in the contribution of genetic modifiers to the β-thalassemia intermedia phenotype. Recognition of these patterns may improve understanding of genotype-phenotype variability and may help inform future approaches to diagnosis, prognostication, and individualized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Effect of Wall Motion Sampling on CFD-Derived Left Atrial Flow Metrics.
articles.journal: International journal for numerical methods in biomedical engineering
articles.abstract: The temporal resolution of medical imaging sequences used to drive patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations remains limited, typically providing 10-20 frames per cardiac cycle. Therefore, temporal interpolation to reconstruct left atrial (LA) wall motion and boundary conditions is required, but its impact on hemodynamic predictions has not been systematically characterized. To investigate this, we constructed high-temporal-resolution reference wall-motion data using electromechanical (EM) simulations on five patient-specific atrial geometries with a history of atrial fibrillation. We then generated temporally downsampled datasets to emulate clinical frame rates (5, 10, 20, and 40 frames per cycle) and performed CFD simulations to isolate the effects of temporal undersampling on hemodynamic metrics. The focus was placed on kinetic energy, KE, and residence time,  T R   , particularly in the left atrial appendage (LAA), where thrombosis is most likely to occur. We employed an immersed boundary method to prescribe the wall motion and computed blood  T R   through a passive scalar transport equation. Results indicate that while global LA hemodynamic indices were marginally affected by the frame rate (errors < 9 %  ), LAA metrics were more sensitive with errors up to 31% compared to reference values. The results based on 20 and 40 frames per cycle yielded favorable agreement with reference results, while 5- and 10-frame reconstructions showed larger, though not systematically biased, deviations from the reference. Importantly, patient ranking by blood-stasis indices was largely preserved. The analysis suggests that patient-specific LA reconstructions derived from dynamic CT imaging provide a reliable basis for estimating LAA blood-stasis indices. Higher frame rates ( ≥ 20  per cycle) offer improved quantitative accuracy, while lower temporal resolutions may remain informative for patient stratification purposes, where relative ranking is more relevant than absolute accuracy.

articles.title: Fully automated AI-based quantification of tumour volume on PSMA PET-CT images is associated with overall survival in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models can quantify tumour volume in positron emission tomography (PET) examinations using prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA). It is, however, unknown whether this measurement of tumour volume contains prognostic information. The purpose of this study was to examine whether tumour volume measured by AI is associated with overall survival in patients with prostate cancer.

METHODS: Patients who had undergone [18F]PSMA-1007 PET-CT due to primary staging or biochemical recurrence (BCR) of prostate cancer at our centre were retrospectively included and followed for 5 years. Automatic quantification of tumour volume was performed using a previously developed fully automated AI model from our research group for PSMA PET-CT analysis, without manual corrections. The tumour volume for the prostate, lymph nodes, and bone was calculated and summarized as Total Lesion Volume (TLV) and divided categorically (no detectable tumour, low, and high) as well as aggregated to whole-body TLV and divided into tertiles (low, intermediate, and high). Mortality rates were compared using Cox-regression and adjusted for age.

RESULTS: Among 267 patients in the final analysis, 48 (18%) died during follow-up. Whole-body TLV was significantly associated with mortality in the combined cohort (p = 0.001) and in the primary staging cohort (p = 0.014) but did not reach statistical significance in the BCR cohort (p = 0.061).

CONCLUSIONS: Fully automated AI-derived TLV from PSMA PET-CT was associated with overall survival. These findings support the potential role of AI-based tumour quantification as a potential prognostic biomarker in prostate cancer.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on multidisciplinary sequential diagnosis and treatment of sleep-disordered breathing in children].
authors: Otorhinolaryngology Subspecialty Group and Stomatology Subspecialty Group
Sleep Medicine Specialized Committee，Chinese Medical Doctor Association
articles.journal: Lin chuang er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Journal of clinical otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
articles.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing（SDB） has a relatively high prevalence in children, and its pathogenesis is complex, involving interdisciplinary issues. Among its subtypes, obstructive sleep apnea （OSA） is the most common, accounting for approximately 90% of cases. Untreated SDB can impair growth and development, cognitive function, and cardiovascular health in affected children. At present, its diagnosis and treatment remain constrained by inadequate multidisciplinary collaboration, single-dimensional assessment, fragmented care, and the lack of a sequential care concept. This consensus was jointly developed by a multidisciplinary panel of experts in otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, orthodontics and stomatology, pediatrics, endocrinology, and psychiatry and psychology. In accordance with the principles of relevant guidelines issued by the World Health Organization （WHO） and the Chinese Medical Association, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation （GRADE） system was adopted to assess the quality of evidence and grade the strength of recommendations. Recommendations were formulated covering diagnostic assessment, multidisciplinary collaboration, sequential treatment, management of special populations, follow-up and health education, and future research directions, and a child-centered, stage-based, and dynamically adjusted multidisciplinary framework for sequential diagnosis and treatment was established, with the aim of standardizing clinical practice, enhancing comprehensive management, and improving the quality of life and long-term prognosis of affected children.

articles.title: Pilot Implementation of an Adapted Online Clinic-Community Model for Childhood Obesity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive health-behaviour lifestyle treatment is recommended for paediatric obesity, but evidence for young children and synchronous online delivery remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of an adapted online clinic-community model for children aged 4 to < 8 years with overweight or obesity.

METHODS: In this two-arm randomized controlled trial, children were randomized to an online family-based intervention or usual care. The primary outcome was treatment dose at 6 months, defined as intervention contact hours. Secondary outcomes included BMI z-score, percentage of the 95th BMI percentile, health-related quality of life, eating behaviours, and perceived movement skills at 3 and 6 months.

RESULTS: Forty children were enrolled; mean age was 6.6 ± 1.0 years and 58% were male. At 6 months, 70% of intervention participants achieved at least 26 treatment hours. Although the between-group differences were not statistically significant, the intervention group demonstrated numerically greater reductions in BMI z-score (-0.2 ± 0.3 vs. -0.1 ± 0.1; p = 0.091) and percentage of the 95th BMI percentile (-3.5 ± 6.4 vs. -0.2 ± 4.0; p = 0.075). Physical quality of life improved at 3 and 6 months, object control skills at 3 months, and perceived locomotor skills at 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: The adapted online model was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements in physical quality of life, movement skills, and BMI metrics. Larger adequately powered trials are needed to confirm effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Discordance Between Height- and BMI-Adjusted AWGS 2025 Definitions of Confirmed Sarcopenia After Stroke.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 allows height- or body mass index (BMI)-adjusted muscle mass in diagnosing confirmed sarcopenia. We evaluated classification discordance and associated clinical characteristics after stroke.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 864 patients undergoing post-acute stroke rehabilitation. Confirmed sarcopenia was defined using low handgrip strength combined with either height- or BMI-adjusted muscle mass. Patients were classified into four groups: Neither, Height-only, BMI-only, and Both. Agreement between definitions was quantified, and the two discordant groups were compared using multivariable logistic regression. Model robustness and discharge outcomes were examined in sensitivity and exploratory analyses, respectively.

RESULTS: Discordant classification occurred in 183 patients (21.2%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 18.6%-24.0%), with moderate agreement between definitions (κ = 0.578). Compared with the Height-only group, the BMI-only group had higher BMI, serum albumin, and phase angle. In adjusted analyses of 182 patients, higher albumin (odds ratio [OR] per 0.5 g/dL, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10-2.64), phase angle (OR per degree, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.23-3.04), and medication count (OR per drug, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32) were associated with BMI-only classification. Firth estimates were similar, but internal validation indicated overfitting. Adjusted discharge outcomes did not clearly differ between discordant groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Height- and BMI-adjusted AWGS 2025 criteria classified approximately one in five patients differently after stroke. Beyond expected body-size differences, discordant groups exhibited distinct clinical characteristics, highlighting the importance of considering the indexing method when interpreting sarcopenia classifications.

articles.title: Current Status and Temporal Changes in Lupus Nephritis in Japan: Analysis of the Japan Renal Biopsy Registry.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study evaluated temporal changes in the clinical and histological features of lupus nephritis at first renal biopsy in Japan.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study used Japan Renal Biopsy Registry data. Patients undergoing their first renal biopsy in 2018-2021 were compared with a historical cohort from 2007 to 2012. Clinical characteristics and histological classes based on the International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society classification were compared.

RESULTS: The study included 331 patients in the historical cohort and 682 in the recent cohort. The recent cohort was older (median age, 42 vs. 37 years; p = 0.014), with a higher proportion aged 60 years or older (19.2% vs. 10.6%; p < 0.001). Histological class distribution differed significantly between cohorts. Class IV (±V) lesions were less frequent in the recent cohort (34.3% vs. 44.1%), whereas Class II and Class III (±V) lesions were numerically more frequent. The lower odds of Class IV (±V) lesions persisted after adjustment for age group (odds ratio, 0.676; 95% confidence interval, 0.516-0.886; p = 0.005). Amongst patients with Class III/IV lesions, pure Class III lesions were more frequent and pure Class IV lesions were less frequent in the recent cohort.

CONCLUSION: The recent first-biopsy cohort was older and had a lower proportion of Class IV (±V) lesions than the historical cohort, even after age adjustment. These findings suggest temporal changes in LN in Japan, although the greater proportion of missing histological classification data in the historical cohort should be considered when interpreting the histological differences.

articles.title: China-PAR-based cardiovascular risk assessment in East Shenzhen using Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays: A prospective cross-sectional and retrospective study.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.abstract: ObjectiveHypertension and dyslipidemia are two well-established risk factors for cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical performance of homocysteine and lipid assays, estimate the 10-year cardiovascular disease risk among individuals with hypertension, and determine the proportions of hyperhomocysteinemia-type hypertension and dyslipidemia in a hospital-based population in East Shenzhen, China.MethodsThe analytical performances of the Biossays homocysteine, total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol assays were evaluated according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute documents. A cross-sectional hypertension cohort comprising 400 eligible participants was recruited from Pingshan People's Hospital between April 2024 and April 2025 to assess the risk of cardiovascular disease and prevalence of hyperhomocysteinemia-type hypertension. Additionally, a retrospective analysis was performed involving 55,575 unique individuals with complete lipid data identified from the hospital laboratory database in 2024, following the exclusion of participants with incomplete and duplicate records, to assess the proportion of participants with dyslipidemia.ResultsThe Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays demonstrated satisfactory precision, trueness, sensitivity, and linearity. The 10-year cardiovascular disease risk, based in the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China, differed across ages but not across sexes. The proportions of individuals with hypertension and hyperhomocysteinemia, defined as homocysteine levels ≥10 μmol/L and ≥15 μmol/L, were 85.50% (342) and 33.75% (135), respectively, with no difference in the risk distribution between the two criteria. At least one abnormal lipid parameter was observed in 68.00% (272) of the participants in the hypertension cohort and in 62.35% (34,651) of individuals from the annual laboratory dataset.ConclusionsThe Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays demonstrated satisfactory analytical performance. Among individuals with hypertension, the estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease risk differed across ages but not between sexes, and hyperhomocysteinemia was frequently observed. Lipid abnormalities were also common in the hospital-based population. These findings may support cardiovascular risk assessment and preventive management in similar clinical populations.

articles.title: Identifying High-Risk Patients: Using the HFpEF-ABA Score for Clinical Trial Enrichment and EMR Screening.

Unboxing the "Pretreatment" Black Box in Cardio-Oncology: Mechanistic Substrates and Clinical Trade-Offs of Deep Learning.

Does Different Coronary Blood Flow and Endothelial Shear Stress Explain Sex Differences in CAD?: It Took More Than a CENTURY (Trial) To Get Here.
Machine learning prediction of 30-day mortality in adults with a positive blood culture.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A positive blood culture is a clinically heterogeneous finding that may represent true bloodstream infection, transient bacteremia or contamination-diagnostic uncertainty that complicates early clinical decision-making. We aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models to predict 30-day all-cause mortality in adults with a positive blood culture.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV. Adult hospitalizations with at least one positive blood culture were included (first positive culture per admission); potential contaminants were retained to reflect real-world uncertainty. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, organ support and microbiological variables were used as predictors. Nine supervised machine learning algorithms were trained with repeated 10-fold cross-validation, evaluated in an independent test cohort and calibrated; thresholds were optimized with the Youden index.

RESULTS: Of 5731 episodes, 742 patients (12.9%) died within 30 days. Test-set ROC AUC ranged from 0.759 to 0.801. After threshold optimization, the random forest model showed the best overall performance (sensitivity 0.788, specificity 0.707, balanced accuracy 0.748; Brier score 0.0999, calibration slope 1.03). ICU admission at onset, mechanical ventilation, bilirubin, urea and the Charlson comorbidity index were the main predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning models can provide clinically meaningful early prediction of 30-day mortality in patients with a positive blood culture using routinely available data. Focusing on the moment of blood culture positivity rather than established sepsis syndromes, this approach supports early risk stratification in a diagnostically heterogeneous population.

articles.title: Mycobacterium abscessus bacteremia: A narrative literature review based on a case report.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mycobacterium abscessus is a highly virulent nontuberculous mycobacterial complex (NTM) that frequently exhibits high-level antimicrobial resistance. Bacteremia is uncommon and occurs predominantly in immunocompromised patients. We report a catheter-associated bloodstream infection by M. abscessus subsp. massiliense, and review M. abscessus bacteremia published over the past 10 years.

METHODS: A PubMed search was conducted from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2025, using the terms "M. abscessus bacteremia" and "M. abscessus catheter infection and bacteremia". Clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and outcome variables were analyzed.

RESULTS: 22 episodes of M. abscessus bacteremia were documented (ours included). The most frequent sources were catheter related infections (8 cases), skin and soft-tissue infection (4), surgical procedures (4) and underlying pulmonary disease (3). 86% of patients had underlying conditions considered risk factors for infection. Overall mortality was 31.8%. Amikacin, macrolides, and carbapenems were the most commonly used agents, with prolonged treatment durations and frequent regimen modifications due to resistance or toxicity.

CONCLUSIONS: M. abscessus bacteremia is rare event with a significant mortality. Rapid microbiological identification and early initiation of appropriate empiric therapy are critical to improving outcomes.

articles.title: Salivary biomarkers in periodontal diseases: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontal diagnosis relies on past clinical damage. Salivary biomarkers offer noninvasive insight into current disease activity and the potential for progression, prompting evaluation of their diagnostic and prognostic value in patients with periodontitis.

TYPES OF STUDIES REVIEWED: Original human studies assessing salivary biomarkers in systemically healthy people with periodontitis were included. A comprehensive literature search was performed using the PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane databases. Designs comprised cross-sectional and interventional studies that identified and evaluated biomarker levels, their association with disease severity, and changes after nonsurgical periodontal therapy across different clinical settings.

RESULTS: Across 11 included studies, several biomarkers were significantly associated with periodontitis. However, sample sizes varied, and outcome measures were reported inconsistently across studies (1.5-10 mL). Oxidative stress biomarkers were elevated, whereas antioxidant capacity was reduced. Proinflammatory cytokines, particularly interleukin 1β and tumor necrosis factor-α, were associated with active disease and decreased after therapy. Alterations in bone metabolism, including reduced osteoprotegerin levels, correlated with periodontal tissue destruction. Matrix metalloproteinase-8 consistently reflected periodontal breakdown and responded sensitively to treatment.

CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Overall, biomarker levels were associated with disease severity and generally improved after successful periodontal interventions. Matrix metalloproteinase-8 showed promising diagnostic and monitoring potential. Collectively, inflammatory, oxidative stress, and bone metabolism biomarkers may provide valuable information regarding disease activity and response to periodontal treatment. Salivary biomarkers may enable noninvasive identification of active periodontitis, risk stratification, and treatment monitoring, complementing clinical measures and improving personalized periodontal care pending further standardized longitudinal validation for routine practice. This systematic review was registered in Open Science Framework (registration doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/3THU6).

articles.title: Effects of insulin resistance on pregnancy outcomes and complications in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate whether early-pregnancy insulin resistance in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with adverse maternal pregnancy complications and neonatal/perinatal outcomes after adjustment for common metabolic confounders.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 168 pregnant women diagnosed with PCOS who were consecutively enrolled at Tongren Hospital from July 2023 to December 2024. Of these, 52 patients with insulin resistance (homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance ≥ 2.77) were assigned to the PCOS with insulin resistance group, whereas 116 patients without insulin resistance were assigned to the PCOS without insulin resistance group. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to estimate adjusted associations between insulin resistance and gestational diabetes mellitus, adjusting for age, body mass index, family history of diabetes, and conception mode.ResultsBody mass index was significantly higher in the PCOS with insulin resistance group (p = 0.02). No significant differences were found in thyroid function indices or blood lipid levels across trimesters, neonatal birth weight, or perinatal outcomes (all p > 0.05). The incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus was higher in the PCOS with insulin resistance group than in the PCOS without insulin resistance group (30.77% vs. 17.24%, p = 0.04). After adjustment for potential confounders, insulin resistance (adjusted odds ratio = 2.09, 95% confidence interval: 1.02-4.28, p = 0.044) and higher body mass index (odds ratio = 1.19 per kg/m2, p = 0.038) remained independently associated with increased odds of gestational diabetes mellitus. No significant differences were observed in gestational hypertension, polyhydramnios, or premature rupture of membranes.ConclusionsIn this observational cohort, early-pregnancy insulin resistance was associated with a higher incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus after adjustment for body mass index and other confounders. These findings do not establish a causal relationship. Early standardized screening and targeted metabolic management of insulin resistance may help reduce gestational diabetes mellitus incidence; however, prospective studies are warranted to confirm this association.

articles.title: [Venous thrombosis at unusual sites].
articles.abstract: Venous thrombosis at unusual sites such as the upper extremity, the splanchnic and cerebral veins, and rarer ovarian, renal and retinal sites has long been managed in analogy to lower-limb deep vein thrombosis because dedicated trials were lacking. This has changed substantially. The 2023 German S2k guideline now addresses these sites explicitly, and a growing body of randomized and prospective evidence supports the use of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). For upper-extremity thrombosis, therapeutic anticoagulation is first-line and is managed according to deep vein thrombosis. A functioning, still-needed catheter can remain in situ. For splanchnic vein thrombosis, anticoagulation reduces recurrence and mortality and improves recanalization, including in cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis (Child-Pugh A/B). In cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis DOACs are possible depending on the liver function (rivaroxaban/edoxaban in Child A, apixaban in Child B, low molecular weight heparin in Child C). A JAK2-V617F screen identifies an underlying myeloproliferative neoplasm before blood-count changes appear and should be part of the etiological work-up of a non-cirrhotic splanchnic vein thrombosis. For cerebral venous thrombosis, DOACs have shown to be as effective as vitamin K antagonists with fewer major, particularly intracranial, bleeds, while vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) requires non-heparin anticoagulation. For ovarian, renal and retinal veins, robust data remains absent. This article summarizes the practice-relevant advances for the general internist, focusing on the upper extremity and the splanchnic veins.

articles.title: Nurses' perceptions of trauma-informed care in NICU practice: A qualitative content analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Trauma-informed care (TIC) is a patient-centered framework that addresses the psychological and emotional impacts of traumatic experiences. In the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), where infants and families encounter critical conditions, TIC is essential for enhancing care quality. This study examined nurses' perceptions and lived experiences of TIC in this setting.

METHODS: This qualitative study used a conventional content analysis approach with a hybrid inductive-deductive orientation. Data were collected through seven individual semi-structured interviews and two dyadic interviews with 11 nurses working in the NICU of a referral hospital in the city of Semnan, Iran. Interviews were conducted until data saturation was achieved. Data were analyzed using MAXQDA 2020, and trustworthiness was established according to Lincoln and Guba's criteria.

RESULTS: The findings included the theme of Relationally empowering care and the two-tiered approach to facilitating mothers' empowerment and synergy in the caregiving experience. Nurses can helped reduce stress and improve mothers' psychological well-being by establishing a supportive and trusting relationship with them. Additionally, sharing experiences among mothers and instilling hope in them are other important aspects of this approach.

CONCLUSION: NICU nurses perceived trauma-informed care as a relational and empowering approach embedded in everyday practice. Through supportive communication, maternal involvement, and fostering hope, nurses helped families cope with the psychological burden of NICU hospitalization. Supporting these relational practices may strengthen trauma-informed care implementation in neonatal settings.

articles.title: Trends in real-world atropine prescribing for myopia control across evidence eras.
articles.journal: Optometry and vision science : official publication of the American Academy of Optometry
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Identify trends in atropine prescribing and concentration adjustments for pediatric myopia control across multiple U.S. academic eye centers.

METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective chart review was conducted of children (ages 3-17 years) prescribed low-concentration atropine for myopia management at three academic medical centers in the United States: the Casey Eye Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, the Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago, and the Rady Children's Hospital Orange County. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the data and summarize prescribing patterns, concentration changes, and follow-up rates by enrollment period and initial atropine concentration.

RESULTS: A total of 435 patients were identified across all study sites. In the Early Low-Dose Atropine Era, 0.01% atropine was the only starting concentration prescribed. Prescribing subsequently shifted toward higher concentrations. Prescribing of 0.05% atropine increased substantially, accounting for 45.7% of baseline prescriptions. Across subsequent evidence eras, changes in concentration increased in frequency, with greater concentration escalation over time, and these increases were most frequent during the Post-LAMP Era (24.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: A clear shift in atropine prescribing patterns for pediatric myopia management was identified over the course of the study period. During the Early Low-Dose Atropine Era, clinicians exclusively prescribed the lowest concentration of atropine (0.01%), and only a small proportion of patients were escalated to a higher concentration at 12 months. In the Post-LAMP Era, there was a broader distribution of baseline dosing, with increased use of 0.02%/0.025% and 0.05% atropine and a higher proportion of patients having concentration increases. During the Contemporary Evidence Era, 0.05% became the predominant starting concentration. The shifts in prescribing patterns highlight the dynamic and responsive nature of clinical decision-making and underscore a growing trend toward comfortability with personalized myopia management in pediatric eye care, suggesting evolving individualized titration strategies and experimental dosage management methods.

articles.title: American Indian and Alaska Native Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery: A National Retrospective Cohort Study Between 2016 and 2022.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Racial and ethnic disparities have been reported in the treatment of hip fractures; however, American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) patients are often excluded. No existing racial disparity studies have evaluated the management and outcomes of hip fractures among AI/AN patients. We aim to assess whether there are disparities in risk factors, management, and complications in the surgical treatment of hip fractures among AI/AN patients.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) database to analyze AI/AN and White patients undergoing surgical treatment of hip fractures between 2016 and 2022. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, chi-squared tests, and multiple regression models were used to assess differences in patient demographics, preoperative comorbidities, time to surgery (TTS), and postoperative complications.

RESULTS: AI/AN patients were significantly younger than White patients yet had higher rates of preoperative comorbidities (diabetes [P < 0.001], smoking [P < 0.001], dialysis [P < 0.001], anemia [P = 0.007], and delirium [P < 0.001]). When controlling for patient characteristics, TTS and mortality were similar between AI/AN and White patients (P = 0.31, P = 0.38, respectively). However, AI/AN patients had significantly more postoperative complications including stroke (P = 0.04) and pneumonia (P < 0.01), had a shorter length of stay (LOS) (P < 0.001), and were less likely to be discharged to a facility (P < 0.001).

DISCUSSION: AI/AN patients with hip fractures had a higher burden of preoperative comorbidities and postoperative complications when compared with White patients. Reassuringly, AI/AN and White patients had similar TTS and 30-day mortality. When controlling for patient characteristics, AI/AN patients had a shorter LOS and were more likely to be discharged home. This may be inferred as a lack of access to rehabilitation facilities on discharge or more support from patient families and communities at home. Overall, AI/AN patients should be included in current and future research to better assess disparities in orthopaedic care.

articles.title: Ninety-Day Overall Healthcare Reimbursements and Their Drivers for Primary Arthroscopic Bankart Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arthroscopic Bankart repair (ABR) is a widely performed procedure for anterior glenohumeral instability. The aim of this study was to characterize variability and identify drivers of 90-day healthcare reimbursement after primary ABR.

METHODS: Primary ABR patients were identified in the PearlDiver M170 database (January 2010-April 2023). Patients who were inactive within 90 days preoperatively or postoperatively or who were coded for neoplasm or infection within 90 days preoperatively were excluded. Variables analyzed included patient characteristics (age, sex, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index [ECI]), nonclinical factors (insurance plan, geographic region), postoperative events (any adverse event [AAE], emergency department [ED] visit, hospital readmission), and total 90-day reimbursements. Multivariable linear regression was conducted to identify independent predictors of reimbursement.

RESULTS: Overall, 135,144 primary ABR patients were identified, representing $596,112,149 in total reimbursements. The mean ± SD reimbursement was $4450 ± $5268. The median (25th quartile-75th quartile) reimbursement was $3192 ($1751-$5465).Variables independently associated with the greatest 90-day reimbursement were readmission (+$18060), AAE (+$1169), and ED visit ($1044). Weaker associations were observed for geographic region, ECI, and male sex (P < 0.0001 for all). Compared with commercial insurance, Medicare (-$2072) and Medicaid (-$1371) were associated with lower reimbursement (P < 0.0001 for both). Notably, over the course of the study period, median overall reimbursement increased from $1930 to $3540 (P < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: This longitudinal, national analysis identified cost variability and key drivers related to ABR. Preventing readmissions may yield the largest cost reductions while observed disparities across insurance plans and regions highlight opportunities for standardization and equity in reimbursement.

articles.title: Orthoplastic Limb Salvage Using Transtibial Transport and Free-Flap Reconstruction in Patients With Diabetes-Related Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
articles.abstract: Early revascularization-through endovascular or open surgery-is the cornerstone of treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, some patients are deemed "no-option" because of diffuse infrapopliteal disease, poor distal runoff, or failed previous interventions, leaving limited limb-salvage strategies. We report an orthoplastic limb-salvage case in a 56-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes, severe peripheral arterial disease, and a chronic foot ulcer complicated by toe gangrene after unsuccessful revascularization. After urgent radical débridement, ray amputation, culture-directed antibiotics, and negative-pressure wound therapy, transtibial transport (TTT) was done to improve microcirculation. After infection control and wound stabilization, definitive reconstruction was achieved using a large anterolateral thigh perforator free flap with a flow-through microsurgical technique to provide durable coverage while preserving distal perfusion. At 12-month follow-up, the flap remained viable with complete epithelialization, no ulcer recurrence, preserved foot architecture, and independent ambulation with protective footwear, indicating meaningful functional recovery. This case highlights the potential role of combining TTT with microsurgical reconstruction in orthoplastic management of "no-option" CLTI. Enhancing microcirculation alongside robust soft-tissue coverage may expand limb-salvage possibilities when traditional revascularization is not feasible.

articles.title: [Chronic cough - a review].
articles.abstract: Chronic cough is common in the general population, with a prevalence of about 10% among adults. It can be caused by a range of conditions within and outside the airways, such as asthma, COPD, cancer, infections, and smoking, or it can occur as an adverse effect of medication, among other causes. Chronic cough can also be a disease in its own right. It generally has a major impact on patients' quality of life. The workup of cough should always include spirometry and a chest radiograph, and further investigations are guided by the clinical presentation. When cough persists despite treatment of possible underlying causes, or when no cause is found after workup, it is most often because the neural reflex that triggers cough has become hypersensitive. The reasons for this are not fully understood, but studies have shown that the network of sensory nerves in the airways is often more dense and that the central nervous system's ability to suppress cough is reduced. In these cases, treatments aimed at dampening the cough reflex can be used. This review covers the workup, pathophysiology, and management of patients with chronic cough in more detail, describes new developments in treatment, and current Icelandic research projects on chronic cough.

articles.title: [Aortic root replacement with a stentless xenograft (Freestyle®) in Iceland - indications and outcome].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Aortic root replacement (ARR) can be performed with a stentless porcine xenograft (Freestyle®) as an alternative to the conventional Bentall-procedure, where mechanical or stented bioprosthetic are sewn into a wov-en tube-graft. We examined early and late outcomes of Freestyle®-ARR in a whole-nation cohort, focusing on indications and surgical outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis that included 44 consecutive Freestyle®-ARR performed at Landspitali 2002-2018. Primary outcomes were 30-day and long-term survival (Kaplan-Meier), with a median follow-up of 111 months. Secondary outcomes included early postoperative complications and late reoperations.

RESULTS: A median of three cases was performed per year (range 0-5). The most common indication was dilated aortic root (70%), followed by Type-A aortic dissection (9%) and small aortic annulus during aortic valve replacement (9%). Average age was 62 years and 65% were male. Median EuroSCORE-II was 11% (range 3-71%), cardiopulmonary bypass time 234 min. and cross-clamp time 157 min. The most common postoperative complications were new-onset atrial fibrillation (51%) and perioperative myocardial infarction (14%). Postoperative length of stay was 12 days median and 30-day mortality 14% (n=6). At follow-up, 1- and 5-year survival rates were 81% and 74%, respectively. For patients surviving the first 30 days, 5-year survival was 86%, and at long-term follow-up only three patients (7%) had undergone reoperation.

CONCLUSIONS: Freestyle®-ARR is a technically challenging operation and is associated with high short-term mortality rates compared with regular AVR. However, long term survival was favourable, and reoperations were uncommon in those surviving to discharge.

articles.title: Cefepime Dose Individualization in Early Sepsis: A Pragmatic Feasibility Trial Protocol.
authors: Beta-Lactam Optimization and Outcomes Management (BLOOM) Study Group
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cefepime is a core antibiotic in sepsis treatment, yet standard dosing yields 10- to 30-fold exposure variability in critical illness. In the early "golden hours" of sepsis, low cefepime levels (affecting up to 70% of cases) may lead to organ dysfunction progression, treatment failure, and antimicrobial resistance. Empiric dose escalation to overcome low levels can increase the risk of dose-dependent neurotoxicity. We developed and qualified a population pharmacokinetic model using patient weight and estimated glomerular filtration rate from creatinine and cystatin C that, in simulation, improved attainment of effective and safe drug levels.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the Beta-Lactam Optimization and Outcomes Management (BLOOM) 1 pragmatic feasibility trial.

DESIGN SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, cluster-randomized, pragmatic feasibility trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07287332) was approved with a waiver of informed consent. Participants are critically ill adults (age ≥ 18 yr), hospitalized at Mayo Clinic (Rochester, MN), who are receiving cefepime for suspected or documented sepsis. A screening tool embedded in the electronic health record (EHR) identifies eligible patients newly initiated on cefepime (≤ 1 previous dose in 48 hr) who are then randomized to care groups (clusters) that use an individualized dosing algorithm (intervention) or usual-care dosing (control). Exclusions are cephalosporin allergy, acute kidney injury, kidney replacement therapy, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and missing inputs required for the algorithm (weight, creatinine, cystatin C). Recruitment began on January 15, 2026, and is expected to conclude by January 2027 (target enrollment, ≥ 300 patients).

INTERVENTIONS OUTCOMES AND ANALYSIS: For eligible patients, EHR-embedded clinical decision support prompts the cluster-assigned dosing approach, with final dose decisions made by the clinical team. Feasibility, fidelity, and exploratory pharmacokinetic and clinical outcomes will be assessed using mixed methods.

CONCLUSIONS: This workflow-integrated pragmatic feasibility trial will determine whether personalized cefepime dosing can be implemented in routine practice to optimize timely sepsis therapy while maintaining safety.

articles.title: Tirzepatide-associated severe euvolemic hyponatremia with syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion-compatible biochemical features.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide is a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist that is being increasingly used for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. Gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with incretin-based therapies can influence water balance through nonosmotic vasopressin release and reduced oral solute intake. In this case report, we report a patient who developed severe symptomatic hyponatremia with biochemical features compatible with the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion temporally associated with tirzepatide therapy. A woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus and morbid obesity on regular insulin and chronic torsemide therapy presented with anorexia, weakness, and drowsiness 10 days after tirzepatide administration. Serum sodium was 104 mmol/L, and she was clinically euvolemic. Renal, hepatic, hematologic, acid-base, and other endocrine parameters were normal. The calculated serum osmolality was 224 mOsm/kg. Urinary sodium remained elevated after withdrawal of the diuretic. The patient was managed with fluid restriction and hypertonic saline, and this resulted in progressive correction of sodium and clinical improvement. This case suggests a potential association between tirzepatide therapy and severe euvolemic hyponatremia. Clinicians should consider electrolyte monitoring in patients receiving incretin-based therapy who develop significant gastrointestinal symptoms or reduced oral intake.

articles.title: Wernicke's encephalopathy secondary to hyperemesis gravidarum in pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Wernicke's encephalopathy (WE) is a rare, acute neurological condition that develops due to thiamine deficiency in pregnant women with severe hyperemesis gravidarum (HG). This is a case report of a 28-year-old woman at 17 weeks of gestation with a prior spontaneous abortion and a history of laparotomy surgery to treat infertility. The patient had three out of four diagnostic requirements as put by the European Federation of Neurological Societies. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed symmetrical medial thalamic hyperintensities consistent with WE. Notably, thyroid function tests revealed gestational thyrotoxicosis, which contributed to HG severity but did not explain the cerebellar dysfunction or characteristic MRI changes, indicating superimposed thiamine deficiency and coexistence of HG-related thyrotoxicosis and WE. WE is significantly underdiagnosed in the nonalcoholic population, especially in pregnant women who generally have a high demand for thiamine. This case highlights the need to consider WE in pregnant women presenting with prolonged HG and to initiate parenteral thiamine promptly to prevent irreversible neurological injury.

articles.title: Role of magnesium as a protective agent in cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity in head and neck cancer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study seeks to evaluate the safety and efficacy of magnesium (MgSO4) as a protective agent against cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity (CIN) in cases with head and neck cancers (HNC).

METHODS: One-hundred newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma HNC were randomly allocated into 4 groups: 25 cases in each. Group 1 (control group) received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 for 7 cycles (each cycle is 1 week). Group 2 received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and 1 g of parenteral MgSO4 intravenous infusion (IVI) for 7 cycles. Group 3 received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and 2 g of parenteral MgSO4 IVI for 7 cycles. Group 4 received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and 3 g of parenteral MgSO4 for 7 cycles. All four groups received radiotherapy concurrent with cisplatin for 7 cycles.

RESULTS: The groups containing Mg IVI as (MgSO4) had a significant improvement (lower level) in Urine kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) and Urine Neutrophil gelatinase associated lipocalin (NGAL) than Group I (control group) (P < 0.05). Serum soluble Fas ligand (sFasL) and Malondialdehyde (MDA) after the end cycle (7 cycle) was significantly decreased in Group IV than group I (control group) (P < 0.05), MgSo4 was significantly decreased in Group IV (3 g Mg) than Group III (2 g Mg) (P < 0.001) and Group II (1 g Mg).

CONCLUSIONS: Mg can serve as a protective agent against CIN, as it reduces renal injury biomarkers, including urinary KIM-1, urinary NGAL, serum sFasL, and serum MDA when incorporated into treatment regimens at different doses, compared to cisplatin alone. Moreover, Mg had a promising role in the improvement of quality of life in cases with HNC receiving cisplatin.

articles.title: Medication profile and treatment response in acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A prospective longitudinal observational study in a tertiary care hospital.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the medication use profile, treatment outcomes, and postdischarge responsiveness and adherence in hospitalized patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective longitudinal observational study enrolled consenting adults hospitalized for AECOPD at a tertiary care hospital in Kolkata. Medication details (drug, route, dose, frequency, and duration) were recorded from admission to discharge. In-hospital and postdischarge outcomes, symptom burden (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Assessment Test [CAT]), quality of life (St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire), and medication adherence (Medication Adherence Rating Scale-10) were evaluated. Data were analyzed using Jamovi statistical software.

RESULTS: Fifty-one participants were enrolled (mean age: 62.9 years, 80.4% males). 76.4% had severe exacerbations (Rome criteria). In-hospital, 98% received parenteral antibiotics (median duration: 8 days), with dual therapy being the most common pattern. In addition, 88.2% received short-course systemic steroids. Bronchodilators, short-acting beta-2 agonists + short-acting muscarinic antagonists and long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) + inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) were initiated in 92.2% and 88.2% of participants, respectively. Following stabilization, 21.6% were started on long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA) therapy in-hospital. Ventilatory support was required by 64.7%, and the in-hospital mortality rate was 23.5%. Admission CAT score was an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratios: 2.13, 95% confidence interval: 1.21-3.76, P = 0.009). At discharge, inhaled therapy was centered on LABA + ICS inhalers (84.6%), and in 71.8%, a LAMA-based inhaler was added. 43.5% participants required readmission within 6 months. Participants with correct inhaler technique and good medication adherence showed a significant increase from the 1st to the 6th month of follow-up (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: AECOPD pharmacotherapy largely aligned with established guidelines. However, high readmission rates and initial poor inhaler technique highlight the need for prioritized strategies in medication adherence and device training.

articles.title: Drug prescribing patterns among burn patients in a tertiary care teaching hospital in Assam, India: A prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Burn injuries are a significant public health concern, particularly in developing countries, resulting in high morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Management of burn patients requires integrative pharmacotherapy with multiple drugs, encompassing polypharmacy which necessitate inviting rational prescribing and antibiotic stewardship.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prescribing patterns among burn inpatients in a tertiary medical college hospital and assess the compliance with essential medicines lists (EMLs).

METHODS: A prospective observational study was organized in the burn unit over 1 year (January-December 2023). Data on demographics, burn characteristics, including total body surface area (TBSA) estimation, and prescribed drugs for 109 admitted patients were recorded using a data collection form. Drug utilization patterns were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Adherence to the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) and the World Health Organization Essential Medicines List (WHO-EML) was estimated.

RESULTS: The mean age of patients was 25.2 ± 16.3 years, with a male prevalence of 68.8%. Most burns were accidental (97.2%), with a mean TBSA of 28%. Polypharmacy pattern was observed with an average 6.8 numbers of drugs per prescription. Antibiotics, analgesics, gastroprotectives, and intravenous fluids were routinely prescribed. Cephalosporins (75.22%) and nitroimidazoles (70.64%) were the most frequently used antibiotic groups, with ceftriaxone being the most common. Paracetamol and tramadol were the most prescribed analgesics. Adherence to NLEM and WHO-EML was 100% and 90%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The study demonstrates extensive use of multiple drugs in burn management, with a predominance of empirical antibiotics. Strengthening antimicrobial stewardship and promoting rational prescribing habits are essential to optimize patient outcomes and reduce antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Protective effect of glyburide on wound healing in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats via alteration of NF-κB/transforming growth factor-β and cellular jun/platelet-derived growth factor-vascular endothelial growth factor signaling pathways.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes-induced abnormal wound healing is characterized by prolonged oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration, largely due to excessive production of oxidative stress and inflammatory mediators. Glyburide is a well-known antidiabetic drug. In this experimental study, we scrutinized the protective effect of glyburide against streptozotocin (STZ) induced wound healing in rats and explored the underlying mechanism.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Swiss Wistar rats were randomly assigned to groups and intraperitoneally injected with STZ to induce diabetes. The rats received the oral administration of glyburide (1.25, 2.5, and 5 mg/kg). We estimated the wound area, body weight, glucose level, insulin level, food intake, water intake, protein, albumin, glucosamine, hydroxyproline, collagen, macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF), hexosamine, lipid parameters, antioxidant parameters, apoptosis parameters, inflammatory cytokines, and inflammatory parameters. The mRNA expression levels were estimated in the rats' skin.

RESULTS: Dose-dependent treatment of glyburide decreased the wound area, glucose level, food intake, and water intake, and enhanced the body weight and insulin. Glyburide treatment altered the level of protein, albumin, glucosamine, hydroxyproline, collagen, MIF, hexosamine, lipid parameters (total cholesterol, triglyceride, low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and high-density lipoprotein, very LDL), oxidative stress (malonaldehyde, glutathione, glutathione peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, and catalase), inflammatory cytokines (tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1 β (IL-1 β), IL-6, IL-10, and IL-17), apoptosis parameters (B-cell lymphoma 2 [Bcl-2]-associated X protein [Bax], Bcl-2, cysteine-aspartic acid protease 3 [caspase-3]), inflammatory parameters (cyclooxygenase-2, prostaglandin (PGE2), inducible nitric oxide synthase, nuclear kappa B factor (NF-κB), transforming growth factor-β [TGF-β]). Glyburide treatment altered the mRNA expression of cellular jun (c-Jun), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), chemokine-1 (CXCL1), chemokine-2 (CXCL2), tyrosine kinase with immunoglobulin-like and EGF-like domains Tyrosine Kinase (Tie-2), angiopoietin-1, mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 2 and 3 (Smad2/3), and Transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β).

CONCLUSION: The result clearly showed the protective effect of glyburide against STZ-induced diabetic wound via alteration of NF-κB/TGF-β and c-Jun/PDGF-VEGF Signaling Pathways.

articles.title: Aromadendrin attenuates dexamethasone-induced osteoporosis in rats by modulating oxidative stress, inflammation, and bone remodeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are used in the treatment of asthma, autoimmune and allergic disease, but long-term GC therapy increased the bone resorption, oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired bone formation. Aromadendrin is a flavonol (flavonoid) exhibited the potent effect against oxidative stress and inflammatory disease. The aim of the experimental study was to investigate the antiosteoporosis effect of aromadendrin against dexamethasone (DEX) induced osteoporosis (OS) in the rats.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Female Sprague Dawley rats were used in this study and subcutaneous administration of DEX (2.5 mg/kg/day) was used for the induction of OS in the rats. The rats were received the oral administration of aromadendrin (2.5, 5 and 10 mg/kg) and alendronate for 20 weeks. The body weight, organ weight, transverse diameter, bone length, microcomputed tomography (MicroCT) parameters, oxidative stress parameters, inflammatory cytokines, caspase parameters, inflammatory parameters and messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) expression were estimated.

RESULTS: Aromadendrin treatment improved the body weight and altered the organ weight (vagina, uterus, and femoral weight); bone weight, transverse diameter, bine length, bone mineral density and bone mineral content level. Aromadendrin altered the level of MicroCT parameters, bone parameters (osteocalcin [OC], border gateway protocol, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase, beta-CrossLaps, alkaline phosphatase, acid phosphatase); nutrient (phosphorus, magnesium, calcium, 1,25(OH)2-vitamin D3); hormone level (calcitonin, parathyroid hormone, E2), oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, inflammatory parameters (nuclear factor-κB [NF-κB], C-reactive protein, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1); caspase parameters (caspase-3, caspase-8, caspase-9), receptor activator of nuclear factor B ligand (RANKL), Osteoprotegerin (OPG), and OPG/RANKL ratio, respectively. Aromadendrin treatment altered the mRNA expression of RANKL, OPG, OPG/RANKL ratio.

CONCLUSION: Aromadendrin exerts an anti-OS effect against DEX-induced OS in rats via alteration of NF-κB and RANKL/OPG signaling pathway.

articles.title: A prospective observational study on geriatric and pediatric prescribing patterns, medication adherence, and cost analysis in a tertiary care hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric and geriatric patients are at risk of adverse drug effects as a consequence of age factors on pharmacokinetics, multimorbidity, and multicomplicated therapy regimens. The purpose of this study was to assess the quality of prescriptions as far as adherence and pharmacoeconomic burden are concerned in these vulnerable groups.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prescribing patterns, polypharmacy, and Potentially inappropriate medications (PIMs) use, medication adherence, drug-drug interaction, and direct medication expenditure in pediatric and geriatric patients in a tertiary care unit.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a six-month prospective observational study on major clinical departments. The World Health Organization prescribing indicators, 2019 Beers Criteria, and Morisky Medication Adherence Scale-8 (MMAS-8) adherence scale were used to evaluate the prescriptions. A pharmacoeconomic study was also conducted by comparing the direct medication costs of prescription of brand and generic medicines. Descriptive statistics were used in analyzing data.

RESULTS: 604 patients were used (432 geriatric and 172 pediatric). The average number of drugs per prescription was 3.82. The percentage of prescriptions in generic form was 39.2%, and injectable prescriptions accounted for 41.2%. Polypharmacy was noted in 35.4% geriatric patients, and PIMs were 20.6% of prescriptions. Medication adherence was only found to be high in 21.5% of the patients, with forgetfulness being the most prevalent reason for nonadherence. The cost analysis based on pharmacoeconomics indicated the possible cost savings of about 60.8% by substituting the generic.

CONCLUSIONS: The improvement of the situation in the geriatric and pediatric population could be achieved through the enhancement of the rational prescribing and generic-first policies.

articles.title: Comparison of the opioid-sparing effects of a combination of dexamethasone, paracetamol, and ketorolac versus paracetamol and ketorolac in patients undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH) is quickly replacing the open abdominal hysterectomy, but is associated with unexpectedly high levels of pain.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to compare the analgesic efficacy of adding dexamethasone to paracetamol and ketorolac (PaK) combination versus PaK combination in female patients undergoing elective TLH.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: After approval from the institutional ethical committee, 100 American Society of Anesthesiologists I and II patients aged 18-60 years undergoing TLH under general anesthesia were included in this study. The patients were assigned to one of the two treatment groups (C and D). Patients in Group D received dexamethasone (0.2 mg/kg) intravenously (IV) dissolved in 100 ml of 0.9% saline 1 h before surgery and ketorolac 30 mg + paracetamol (PCM) 1 g IV prior to anesthesia being induced, while the patient in Group C received a placebo (100 ml of 0.9% normal saline) 1 h before surgery and ketorolac 30 mg + PCM 1 g IV before induction of anesthesia.

RESULTS: Fentanyl consumption in the first 24 h was significantly higher in Group C (231.72 ± 84.07 μg) than in Group D (138 ± 48.7 μg) (P < 0.0001). Pain scores on the 0-100 Visual Analog Scale demonstrated notable variations at each point among the groups (P < 0.05). Postoperative nausea and vomiting scores differed at 15 and 30 min (P < 0.05). A transient rise in blood glucose occurred in Group D at 16 h (122 g/dl vs. 115 g/dl in Group C, P = 0.013).

CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing TLH, a combination of dexamethasone, PCM, and ketorolac reduced 24-h opioid use, improved pain scores, and minimized immediate postoperative nausea and vomiting.

articles.title: Drug-drug interactions between statins and antibiotics: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract: Statins are frequently prescribed for the prevention of cardiovascular diseases. Certain antibiotics, especially macrolides, can raise the risk of side effects related to muscles and inhibit the metabolism of statins.
