Although results have been mixed, evidence from separate observational studies has pointed to a potential rise in statin-associated muscle toxicity when these drugs are used together. To evaluate whether the concurrent use of interacting antibiotics raises the risk of statin-associated muscle toxicity in comparison to statin therapy alone by conducting a systematic review and quantitative synthesis of observational data. A systematic literature search was conducted in various databases. Observational studies reporting risk estimates for statin-associated myopathy or rhabdomyolysis with concomitant antibiotic use were included. Data were extracted independently and pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated. Relative risks were treated as approximations of ORs due to the rarity of outcomes. Sensitivity analysis was performed using a leave-one-out approach. The meta-analysis included three observational studies that met the inclusion criteria. A markedly elevated risk of muscle toxicity was linked to the concurrent use of statins and interacting antibiotics. With a 95% confidence interval of 1.82-2.50, the pooled OR was 2.13. Sensitivity analysis showed that the results were robust since the pooled estimate did not change when individual studies were excluded. Concurrent use of interacting antibiotics with statins is associated with an increased risk of statin-associated muscle toxicity. Clinicians should exercise caution when prescribing such combinations, particularly in high-risk patients. Further large-scale studies are needed to better quantify risk across different statins and antibiotic classes.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.
articles.abstract: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05143177.

articles.title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules: The NODULE-SHOCK Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs.

METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B.

RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm2; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm2; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873).

CONCLUSIONS: RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).

articles.title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year.

METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT).

RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days).

CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

articles.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.

METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.

RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.

CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

articles.title: Six-Month Music Practice Versus Psychomotor Interventions in Mild Cognitive Impairment: Behavioral and Hippocampal Outcomes.
articles.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
articles.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is characterized by measurable cognitive decline with largely preserved daily functioning and increased risk of dementia. MCI patients may also exhibit sensorimotor and communication impairments, while hippocampal atrophy and altered functional connectivity are prominent neural features associated with further cognitive decline. Evidence from nonpharmacological interventions integrating cognitive challenge, coordinated movement, and emotional engagement remains limited in early-stage MCI. In this pilot intervention study, we examined whether 6 months of intensive musical instrument training versus psychomotor interventions were associated with changes in cognitive and sensorimotor performance, hippocampal gray matter volume, and functional connectivity. Outcomes were compared between randomized MCI groups, with matched healthy controls as reference for test-retest and age-related neural effects. Improvements in global cognition were modest, reaching marginal significance only in the music group, while both interventions were associated with complementary domain-specific cognitive and sensorimotor gains. Hippocampal gray matter volume remained stable across all three groups, whereas hippocampal functional connectivity declined in healthy controls but remained stable in both intervention groups, consistent with possible functional neural maintenance. These preliminary findings suggest that group-based, low-risk music and psychomotor interventions may support cognitive, sensorimotor, and neural functioning in early MCI, warranting further investigation in larger controlled trials.

articles.title: Adjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy for periodontitis in type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether adjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy added to conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy provides greater improvement in baseline-adjusted 6-month probing depth than conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy alone in patients with periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus.MethodsThis randomized controlled trial included 120 patients with periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the laser group (conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy plus adjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy, n = 60) or the control group (conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy alone, n = 60). Conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy comprised scaling and root planing with standardized home oral-hygiene instruction and reinforcement. Periodontal and glycemic outcomes were assessed at baseline and 6 months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the 6-month mean probing depth, adjusted for baseline probing depth using analysis of covariance. Secondary outcomes included baseline-adjusted between-group differences in clinical attachment level, bleeding on probing-positive sites, gingival recession, glycosylated hemoglobin, and fasting plasma glucose level.ResultsBaseline characteristics were generally comparable between groups, except a modest difference in mean gingival recession. Based on the primary analysis, the baseline-adjusted 6-month mean probing depth was significantly lower in the laser group than in the control group (adjusted difference, -0.70 mm (95% confidence interval, -0.84 to -0.56) p < 0.001). Baseline-adjusted differences also favored the laser group for clinical attachment level (-0.67 mm; 95% confidence interval, -0.79 to -0.55), bleeding on probing-positive sites (-11.3 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.9 to -8.7), glycosylated hemoglobin (-0.26%; 95% confidence interval, -0.34 to -0.17), and fasting plasma glucose level (-0.62 mmol/L; 95% confidence interval, -0.81 to -0.44) (all p < 0.001). Gingival recession was slightly higher in the laser group after baseline adjustment (+0.09 mm; 95% confidence interval, 0.03 to 0.14; p = 0.004). No serious treatment-related adverse events were recorded.ConclusionsAdjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy was associated with greater short-term improvement in periodontal clinical outcomes than conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy alone. Favorable changes in secondary glycemic outcomes were also observed; however, these results should be interpreted cautiously because cautiously because glycemic variables were secondary endpoints, and the follow-up duration was limited to 6 months.Research registration numberresearchregistry12005.

articles.title: Prospective Evaluation of Hepatitis B Virus Reactivation in Cancer Patients Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Data on hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) during tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy remain limited. We prospectively enrolled patients with chronic or resolved HBV receiving TKIs for lung cancer or chronic myeloid leukemia at one Taiwanese center (January 2023-March 2025). HBV DNA and liver enzymes were monitored 12-weekly and HBsAg 24-weekly. HBVr was defined by AASLD criteria, with APASL and EASL definitions applied secondarily. Among 79 patients (20 HBsAg-positive, 59 resolved HBV), none received antiviral prophylaxis. Median follow-up was 42 weeks (IQR, 19-65). HBVr occurred in 7 (8.9%; 95% CI, 4.4%-17.2%): 5 HBsAg-positive (25.0%; 95% CI, 11.2%-46.9%), and 2 with resolved HBV (3.4%; 95% CI, 0.9%-11.5%). APASL and EASL definitions yielded 30.0% and 35.0% in HBsAg-positive patients, with no additional events in resolved HBV. No HBVr-associated hepatitis flare meeting the study definition was observed, although transient flares between assessments could not be excluded and deterioration in one fatal case was attributed clinically to sepsis. Median HBVr detection time was 19 weeks (IQR, 14-30). Week-48 Kaplan-Meier HBVr incidence was 37.5% (95% CI, 17.0%-69.5%) in HBsAg-positive and 5.6% (95% CI, 1.4%-21.2%) in resolved HBV (log-rank p < 0.001); Aalen-Johansen estimates were 28.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-50.9%) and 4.3% (95% CI, 0.8%-13.2%), respectively. In exploratory Firth-corrected regression, HBsAg positivity was associated with HBVr (HR, 6.95; 95% CI, 1.60-40.19), while osimertinib exposure was not. HBVr was common among HBsAg-positive patients and less common but not negligible among those with resolved HBV receiving TKIs.

articles.title: An integrative view of human nociceptor diversity: from microneurography to molecular identity.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain arises from dysfunction of the peripheral or central nervous system and affects up to 10% of the population worldwide. Aberrant activity in injured sensory nerve fibers, particularly spontaneous firing and altered conduction properties of nociceptors, is tightly linked to pain, yet its molecular underpinnings in humans have long remained elusive. Over recent years, major technological advances have transformed both functional and molecular analyses of sensory neurons. High-resolution single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have produced detailed atlases of sensory neuron diversity, while traditional electrophysiological approaches such as patch-clamp and microneurography have provided unparalleled insight into nerve fiber properties. Despite their individual strengths, molecular and functional classifications of sensory neurons have largely evolved in parallel. This review focuses on emerging strategies that bridge these approaches to achieve an integrated, mechanistic understanding of neuropathic pain. We discuss how microneurography-defined biophysical hallmarks, such as activity-dependent slowing, recovery cycle signatures, and following frequency, can be transferred into in vitro patch-clamp paradigms, enabling direct functional comparison with dissociated human and large-animal sensory neurons. The incorporation of Patch-seq approaches has further enabled the assignment of molecular identity to functionally defined nociceptor subtypes, exemplified by the characterization of the mechano-insensitive "sleeping" nociceptors. Finally, we highlight how multimodal datasets combining electrophysiology, transcriptomics, and computational modeling provide new opportunities to unravel the ion channel mechanisms, particularly sodium channel subtypes, that shape pathological firing states. By directly linking human nerve fiber function to molecular programs, this integrative framework paves the way toward stratified, mechanism-based therapies for neuropathic pain.

articles.title: Comment on 'Prevalence of blood eosinophilia and its impact on lung functions in stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients'.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society

articles.title: Treating without harming: An urgent call to action for sustainable inhaler disposal in India.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease remain leading causes of chronic respiratory morbidity and mortality worldwide, with India having a significant share of the global burden. Inhalers are the cornerstone of treatment for these patients. However, their environmental impact is a growing concern. Pressurised metred-dose inhalers, widely prescribed in India, use hydrofluoroalkane propellants with global warming potentials up to 3000 times higher than carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). Improper disposal further increases emissions and introduces non-degradable components into ecosystems. Surveys suggest that nearly 79% of Indian patients discard used inhalers in regular household waste. This highlights huge gaps in awareness and infrastructure. While the United Kingdom's "Take AIR" programme has demonstrated success, India also has some promising initiatives such as Kerala's IMAGE and nPROUD. These, alongside industry-led efforts, offer scalable solutions. This article reviews India's inhaler disposal scenario and proposes strategies to reduce environmental impact while ensuring responsible inhaler use.

articles.title: Seven versus 14 days of polymyxin-based therapy for ventilator-associated pneumonia due to carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii : A randomised feasibility trial.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) due to carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii ( CRAB ) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs), yet the optimal antibiotic duration of therapy remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of 7-day versus 14-day polymyxin-based therapy for CRAB-VAP.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre, open-label, randomised feasibility trial in a tertiary-care respiratory ICU from March 2017 to October 2024. Patients with microbiologically confirmed CRAB-VAP who met predefined clinical stability criteria on day 7 were randomised 1:1 to either discontinue antibiotics on day 7 or continue treatment for 14 days. Treatment comprised intravenous colistin or polymyxin B with adjunctive nebulised colistin. The primary outcome was relapse of CRAB-VAP. Secondary outcomes included antibiotic-free days through day 28, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, and 28-day all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: We randomised 41 patients (7-day n = 22; 14-day n = 19). Relapse occurred in 1 (4.5%) versus 2 (10.5%) patients (risk ratio [RR] 0.43; 95% CI: 0.04, 4.31) in the 7-day versus 14-day groups, respectively. The 7-day group had more antibiotic-free days (mean difference: 6.9 days; 95% CI: 5.1, 8.7 days). Acute kidney injury occurred in 0% versus 31.6% (RR 0.07; 95% CI: 0.004, 1.15). Other outcomes, including 28-day mortality (45.5 vs 63.2%; RR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.40, 1.30), were similar.

CONCLUSION: In clinically improving CRAB-VAP, a 7-day discontinuation strategy was feasible. Clinical outcome estimates, including relapse and mortality, were imprecise and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. These findings support evaluation in larger, adequately powered multicentre trials.

articles.title: The "Masking Effect" of emphysema in bronchiectasis-chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap syndrome: Why chest radiography is diagnostically futile.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The coexistence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and bronchiectasis, termed bronchiectasis-COPD overlap syndrome (BCOS), represents a high-risk clinical phenotype associated with increased mortality and exacerbations. While high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) is the gold standard for diagnosis, chest X-ray (CXR) remains the primary screening tool in many settings. This study aims to quantify the "masking effect" of emphysema on bronchial markings by evaluating the correlation between CXR grading and validated HRCT severity scores (Bhalla and Smith) in confirmed BCOS patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-centre study analysed 78 patients confirmed with BCOS based on spirometry and radiological evidence of emphysema. To ensure internal validity, patients with acute exacerbations or pneumonia within the preceding 6 weeks were strictly excluded. Posterior-anterior chest radiographs were scored for hyperinflation, parenchymal opacities and subjective bronchiectasis severity. The relationship between plain radiographic findings and tomographic scores was analysed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.

RESULTS: The study population exhibited a mean Smith Score of 1.41 ± 0.75 and a mean Bhalla Extent Score of 1.66 ± 0.88, indicating mild-to-moderate disease severity on average. While a strong positive correlation was observed between the two HRCT-based scores (r = 0.85, P < 0.001), indicating high internal concordance between scoring systems, the correlation coefficients between CXR and HRCT were near zero (Spearman's rho ≈ 0), indicating a random relationship between CXR sensitivity and true morphological damage.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate a fundamental "radiological decoupling" in BCOS. Due to the parenchymal masking effect of emphysema - driven by reduced background lung attenuation - plain radiography is not merely less sensitive but diagnostically unreliable in BCOS. Therefore, HRCT should be mandatory for the clinical phenotyping and management of BCOS, regardless of "mild" or "non-specific" findings on CXRs.

articles.title: Association between platelet/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio and asthma in American adults: A population-based study.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease in adults, in which systemic inflammation plays a key pathogenic role. The platelet-to-high-density lipoprotein ratio (PHR) has emerged as a biomarker of systemic inflammation. Although studied in relation to asthma, its association with adult asthma remains inadequately characterized, and evidence from large-scale epidemiological studies is limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between the PHR and asthma in adults, using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011-2018.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was performed on 22,617 adult participants from NHANES. Asthma status was defined based on self-report, and PHR was calculated as platelet count (1,000/μL) divided by high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (mg/dL). We used multivariable logistic regression to examine the association between PHR (analyzed as both continuous and categorical variables by quartiles) and asthma. Nonlinearity was assessed using restricted cubic splines, and the robustness of findings was evaluated through a series of sensitivity analyses, including weighted regression and multiple imputation for missing data.

RESULTS: Using multivariable logistic regression, we found a significant positive association between PHR and adult asthma (OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05; P = 0.009). When PHR was divided into quartiles, the Q2 and Q4 groups had higher asthma risk than Q1 (risk ratios of 1.19 and 1.20, respectively). Asthma prevalence increased significantly across PHR quartiles ( P for trend <0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis indicated a linear relationship, with the odds of asthma rising as PHR increased. These results remained robust in both weighted and sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings show that higher PHR is associated with an increased prevalence of asthma, suggesting that higher PHR may be linked to asthma diagnosis in US adults.

articles.title: Role of early lung ultrasound in predicting disease progression of acute bronchiolitis.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although clinical assessment is typically diagnostic for bronchiolitis in children, recent literature suggests that early lung ultrasound (LUS) can predict disease progression and help identify children at risk of developing severe illness. This is due to its non-invasive nature, safety, and ability to provide real-time, rapid findings.

PURPOSE: The aim of the study was to determine the correlation between early LUS findings and clinical severity scores. Additionally, the study sought to evaluate the role of early LUS in predicting disease progression and the severity of bronchiolitis, specifically in relation to the need for oxygen supplementation, the duration of oxygen therapy, the length of hospitalization, and intensive care unit (ICU) stay.

METHODS: This was a single-centre prospective observational study conducted at a tertiary hospital in South India. Infants with mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis, as determined by clinical severity scores, underwent early LUS within the first 24 hours of their presentation to the hospital. They were categorized into mild, moderate, and severe groups based on bronchiolitis-specific early LUS findings. Daily clinical scores were recorded, and the highest clinical score was used to assess disease progression correlation.

RESULTS: A total of 127 children, with a mean age of 5.02 ± 3 months, were recruited for the study. According to the modified TAL clinical bronchiolitis severity score, 71 children were classified as having mild bronchiolitis, while 56 had moderate bronchiolitis. The final analysis revealed that the early LUS score had a strong correlation with disease progression (rho = 0.869, P < 0.001). Additionally, the early LUS score significantly correlated with the need for supplemental oxygen (rho = 0.889, P < 0.001), length of hospital stay (rho = 0.851, P < 0.001), and ICU stay (rho = 0.904, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Early LUS demonstrated a strong correlation with disease progression, as indicated by highest clinical scores in mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis.

articles.title: Mortality-related prognostic factors in older adult patients with nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease: A single centre, retrospective cohort study in Japan.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease (NTM-PD) is becoming increasingly prevalent worldwide and is associated with substantial mortality. However, data on older adult patients with NTM-PD are limited. We aimed to characterize the clinical course and prognostic factors of older adult patients with NTM-PD.

METHODS: From 2011 to 2025, NTM-PD patients aged 65 years or older at a single centre in Japan were screened, and clinical course and characteristics were reviewed retrospectively. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis and log-rank analyses were performed to identify risk factors for all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 110 older adult patients with NTM-PD were included (deceased group, n = 31; survived group, n = 79). The median age of all patients was 77 years. In univariable analysis, male sex, smoking history, low albumin levels, and high C-reactive protein levels were associated with mortality. In multivariate analysis, smoking history (hazard ratio [HR]: 6.68; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.08-21.46) and low albumin level (HR: 3.54; 95% CI: 1.60-7.82) were independently associated with mortality. Log-rank analysis demonstrated poorer survival among patients with low albumin levels and a smoking history. After stratification by sex, smoking history remained associated with mortality in both men and women. Radiologically, mortality was the highest in the unclassified pattern, followed by the fibrocavitary and nodular bronchiectatic patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: Smoking history and low albumin levels were associated with increased all-cause mortality in older adult patients with NTM-PD. These factors may help identify patients who require closer monitoring.

articles.title: How Does Place of Residence Influence the Experience and Management of Chronic Non-Malignant Pain? A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Chronic non-malignant pain (CNMP) affects up to half of the UK population and one third of adults globally. Rural populations experience poorer health outcomes across several chronic conditions; however, the influence of place of residence on CNMP management, outcomes and experiences remains unclear. This systematic review examined how place of residence (urban or rural) impacts CNMP management, outcomes and experiences.

METHODS: PubMed, psycINFO, Medline, Embase and CINAHL databases were searched for qualitative and quantitative studies. Dual title/abstract screening and full-text review were undertaken against pre-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria. A narrative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: Of 2341 titles screened, 16 studies were included (12 observational, three qualitative and one mixed-methods study). Most studies were rated as fair quality, with limitations including unsatisfactory response rates and non-validated outcome measures. Rural residents were more likely to use primary care and opioid-based treatments, whereas urban residents had greater access to specialist pain services. Outcomes were less consistent; several studies reported poorer pain-related outcomes among rural residents, although some identified no significant differences compared with urban populations. Long travel distances, prolonged waiting times and limited specialist and non-pharmacological services were barriers to care.

CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights geographic inequalities in CNMP management and experiences. Findings should be interpreted in light of methodological limitations and study heterogeneity. Targeted approaches are needed to improve equitable access to pain management across settings.

SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This systematic review synthesises evidence on how geographic location influences the management, outcomes and experiences of people with chronic non-malignant pain. The findings identify consistent rural-urban disparities in access to evidence-based pain care and highlight important gaps in the current literature, including the limited availability of high-quality comparative studies. These findings provide a foundation for future research and inform the development of more equitable pain services.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO number: CRD42024522734.

articles.title: Comment on "Impact of Chronic Kidney Disease Severity on Clinical Outcomes After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis".
Treprostinil: Mechanism of Action, Clinical, and Translational Science.
articles.abstract: Treprostinil is a synthetic prostacyclin analogue with a tricyclic benzindene structure that confers markedly enhanced metabolic stability relative to native prostacyclin, enabling delivery by four distinct routes-intravenous, subcutaneous, inhaled, and oral-that together constitute a mainstay of pharmacotherapy for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Herein, we review the mechanism of action, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) characteristics, and clinical development of treprostinil, with primary emphasis on its well-established role in PAH, including detailed dosing and PK data across all four approved routes, and secondary emphasis on its recently approved role in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and its investigational, plausible-future role in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) without a pulmonary hypertension requirement. Treprostinil activates the Gαs-coupled prostacyclin (IP) receptor to generate a sustained nuclear cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signal that is qualitatively distinct from earlier prostacyclin analogues, underlying both its established vasodilatory, antiproliferative, and antiplatelet effects in PAH and a mechanistic hypothesis of antifibrotic activity relevant to IPF. Treprostinil also engages the prostaglandin EP₂ and DP₁ receptors and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, and inhibits transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-driven extracellular matrix synthesis through mechanisms only partially explained by cAMP magnitude. Across the four approved routes, treprostinil exhibits route-specific pharmacokinetics-near-complete subcutaneous bioavailability with a 4-hour terminal half-life, oral bioavailability of approximately 17% with extensive first-pass CYP2C8 metabolism, and inhaled systemic bioavailability of approximately 64%-72%-that inform the distinct dosing and titration strategies detailed in this review. In a plausible, still-investigational extension of this pharmacology beyond PAH, two replicate Phase 3 trials (TETON-1 and TETON-2) have reported that inhaled treprostinil reduces the decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) and the risk of clinical worsening in patients with IPF without a pulmonary hypertension requirement. These findings support a plausible antifibrotic hypothesis pending confirmatory evidence and regulatory review; treprostinil is not currently approved for an IPF indication, and this signal should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than establishing disease modification.

articles.title: Welcoming Novelty in the Treatment of Coronary Artery Disease: FDA Approves the Use of Drug-Coated Balloon for Angioplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, with in-stent restenosis (ISR) posing a significant challenge following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Drug-eluting stents (DES) have been widely used to mitigate ISR; however, until recently, no drug-coated balloon (DCB) catheter had been approved for use in the United States. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has now approved AGENT DCB, a paclitaxel-coated balloon catheter, offering a novel approach to treating ISR.

HYPOTHESIS: The approval of AGENT DCB represents a pivotal advancement in PCI, providing an effective alternative to traditional balloon angioplasty for ISR.

METHODS: This article is an editorial review and does not involve original research, statistical analysis, or software-based evaluations. The findings and discussion are based on the results of the AGENT IDE trial and related literature on the efficacy of DCB catheters in the treatment of ISR.

RESULTS: The AGENT IDE trial, a randomized, multicenter study involving 600 participants across 40 US sites, demonstrated that the paclitaxel-coated balloon group had a significantly lower target lesion failure rate at 12 months compared to the uncoated balloon group (17.9% vs. 28.6%, p = 0.003). The reduction was primarily driven by a lower incidence of target lesion revascularization (13.0% vs. 24.7%, p = 0.001) and myocardial infarction related to the target vessel (5.8% vs. 11.1%, p = 0.02). Additionally, no cases of stent thrombosis were observed in the DCB group compared to 3.2% in the control group (p = 0.001), reinforcing the device's safety and efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: The FDA approval of AGENT DCB marks a significant milestone in the management of ISR, offering a promising alternative to conventional interventions. With its ability to deliver antiproliferative therapy while avoiding the complications associated with permanent stents, DCB may revolutionize PCI strategies in the United States. Further studies assessing the long-term impact of this technology, as well as its application in broader patient populations, will be essential to solidify its role in clinical practice.

articles.title: Navigating the Challenges of Shared Decision-Making in Amyloid Immunotherapy for Alzheimer's Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-amyloid therapies (AATs), such as lecanemab and donanemab, represent a major therapeutic development for early Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, safety risks and uncertainties regarding long-term effects make treatment decisions complex. These decisions arise when patients remain legally capable of providing informed consent but may experience cognitive vulnerabilities affecting their ability to engage in complex decisions. Shared decision-making (SDM) is therefore particularly relevant, yet its implementation raises ethical and practical challenges.

METHODS: This position paper draws on a multidisciplinary reflection on decision-making, informed consent, and cognitive vulnerability in early AD and AATs. The authors, with expertise in neurology, geriatrics, law, and history, examined challenges to patient participation and developed a relational framework integrating SDM and supported decision-making.

RESULTS: Impairments in memory, insight, and executive function, together with cognitive biases, stigma, and the complexity of AAT-related information, may compromise patient participation despite preserved legal capacity. Formal capacity assessments and improved information delivery may address some difficulties but are unlikely to provide comprehensive support. We propose a relational framework involving assessment of patients' cognitive vulnerabilities, values, preferences, and informational needs; tailored information; and involvement of a patient-designated care partner to support information exchange, deliberation, and expression of preferences. Consent should be iterative, with safeguards to preserve autonomy and confidentiality, prevent coercion, and avoid excluding socially isolated individuals.

CONCLUSION: Combining SDM with supported decision-making may provide an ethical and practical framework for autonomous treatment decisions regarding AATs in early AD.

articles.title: United Kingdom Professional Consensus on Candidate Items and Domains for Age Specific Paediatric Bronchiectasis Quality of Life Questionnaires: An e-Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric bronchiectasis (PB) unrelated to cystic fibrosis or primary ciliary dyskinesia causes significant morbidity and impairs quality of life (QoL) for children and their families. An international consensus ranked a paediatric-specific QoL measure as the highest research priority, yet no self-report instrument exists for children and young people. We aimed to establish professional consensus on candidate items and domains to inform the development of age specific PB QoL questionnaires.

METHODS: Candidate items were drawn verbatim from two validated paediatric respiratory instruments (QOL-PCD and CFQ-R), guided by published evidence. Multidisciplinary professionals from the Paediatric Bronchiectasis Network, United Kingdom (PBNetUK) rated items for child (6-12 years), young person (13-17 years) and parent proxy (6-12 years) over 2 e-Delphi rounds (≥ 70% agreement). A core group, including a parent representative finalised item sets. Feasibility was checked with 30 patients and parents.

RESULTS: Of 34 professionals invited, 26, 21 and 20 rated the child (28 items), young person (36 items) and parent-proxy (33 items) versions in round one; round two retention was 90%-96%. Final versions comprised 19, 27 and 20 items across eight domains, with a 4-week recall period. For feasibility, participants rated length as appropriate (28/30) and items as easy to understand (mean 8.0-9.4/10).

CONCLUSIONS: This professional consensus provides a candidate item pool and proposed domain framework that will guide the next stages of QoL questionnaire development - establishing content validity through concept elicitation and cognitive interviews with children, young people and parents, followed by psychometric validation to produce a validated QoL.

articles.title: Extended Wearable ECG Monitoring Detects Unrecognised Arrhythmias After COPD Exacerbation: The PRECURSOR Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The period after hospitalisation for an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with cardiovascular vulnerability. Clinically important rhythm disturbances may be intermittent or asymptomatic and escape routine postdischarge assessment; however, the diagnostic yield of prolonged monitoring is intrinsically influenced by monitoring duration.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre observational pilot, 18 adults recently hospitalised for COPD exacerbation underwent continuous remote monitoring for 21 days between September 2019 and February 2020. The three-lead ZENSOR wearable recorded electrocardiographic rhythm, heart rate and respiratory rate and transmitted full-disclosure data and predefined alerts for clinician review. The primary outcome was participant-level detection of previously unrecognised, cardiologist-confirmed arrhythmias warranting therapeutic evaluation or intervention. Outcomes were analysed descriptively with exact 95% binomial confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Participants were predominantly male (15/18; 83.3%), with a mean age of 73 ± 6 years. Seven had GOLD grade 3-4 airflow limitation, seven received long-term oxygen therapy, five had coronary artery disease and four had chronic atrial fibrillation. During the planned 21-day monitoring period, previously unrecognized clinically actionable arrhythmias were detected in 9/18 participants (50.0%; 95% CI: 26.0-74.0). Nonmutually exclusive findings included trigeminy (2/18), third-degree atrioventricular block (2/18), bradycardia (5/18), newly detected atrial fibrillation (1/18), supraventricular tachycardia (2/18) and nocturnal atrial or ventricular ectopy (8/18). Sixteen participants (88.9%; 95% CI: 65.3-98.6) reported satisfaction with monitoring.

CONCLUSIONS: Extended wearable electrocardiographic monitoring produced a high participant-level detection yield of previously unrecognised arrhythmias during early recovery from hospitalised COPD exacerbation. This finding supports targeted postdischarge rhythm surveillance but does not distinguish biological post-exacerbation vulnerability from the greater ascertainment achieved by prolonged monitoring. Confirmation requires larger controlled studies with comprehensive cardiopulmonary phenotyping, standardised monitoring-performance metrics and comparative clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Optimal Exercise Dose for Improving Multidimensional Health Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the dose-response relationships between exercise prescription parameters and a range of health outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). The following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of five databases was conducted. The inclusion criteria were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise interventions lasting ≥ 4 weeks in patients with CRC. Robust Variance Estimation (RVE) was used to synthesize the overall effects of exercise interventions across six outcome domains, including cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) and muscular fitness (MF). Univariable RVE regression models and MetaForest analyses were employed to examine the moderating effects of two groups of variables: exercise prescription moderators and patient background characteristics. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool, and the quality of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. A total of 26 RCTs, involving 1731 CRC patients and 266 effect sizes, were included. CRF (ES = 0.35, p < 0.01) and MF (ES = 0.45, p < 0.01) showed statistically significant improvements. Regression analyses revealed threshold effects for both CRF and MF, with maximal improvements requiring sustained engagement in moderate-to-high intensity exercise. Subgroup analyses indicated that prehabilitation interventions were the most effective, while interventions during active treatment exhibited a decline-rebound trend over time. Based on these findings, high-frequency and moderate-to-high volume interventions with individualized load regulation are recommended during the pre-treatment phase. During active treatment, a more cautious approach is advised, involving reduced exercise volume during peak symptom periods and gradual progression during recovery.

articles.title: Double Consecutive Electrical Countershock for Atrial and Ventricular Fibrillation: A Narrative Critical Review.
articles.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent strategies for refractory ventricular fibrillation (VF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) employ two consecutive, biphasic shocks with varying evidence of success. Due to their electrophysiological similarities, the strategies used for VF and AF can be collectively referred to as double consecutive electrical countershock (DCEC). This review aims to identify and synthesize outcome data on the effectiveness of DCEC across both VF and AF.

METHODS: This narrative critical review with systematic search methods was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA checklist where applicable. From 672 identified articles, 262 duplicates were removed and 410 screened; 316 articles irrelevant to the study were excluded. Of 94 sought for retrieval, 8 were unavailable and 67 failed full-text screening, leaving 19 included articles (16 VF, 3 AF). All 19 underwent risk-of-bias assessment (RoB2, ROBINS-I, or AMSTAR-2) and data extraction.

RESULTS: Full-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) showed low risk of bias, pilot RCTs had "some concerns," observational studies carried serious risk of bias, and meta-analyses showed "low confidence." High-quality randomized evidence showed improved primary outcomes for DCEC in both refractory VF (survival to discharge, return of spontaneous circulation, good neurological outcome) and high-BMI AF (arrhythmia termination). Non-randomized observational studies predominantly showed non-statistically significant differences.

CONCLUSIONS: DCEC shows potential to improve arrhythmia termination in refractory VF and high-BMI AF. Randomized evidence supports its efficacy, while observational findings remain neutral due to confounding. Success in high-BMI AF supports elevated BMI as a hypothetical indication for DCEC in VF.

articles.title: Kinesin motor proteins as host factors regulating viral infection: Mechanisms of exploitation, emerging paradigms, and therapeutic horizons.
articles.abstract: Intracellular transport via microtubules is integral to eukaryotic cell function, and viruses have developed intricate mechanisms to exploit this system at nearly every stage of their replication cycle. The mammalian kinesin superfamily, consisting of 14 distinct families, enables anterograde transport that is used by both DNA and RNA viruses. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of how a wide range of viral pathogens-including herpesviruses, human immunodeficiency virus type 1, vaccinia virus, hepatitis B virus (HBV), influenza virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-interact with specific kinesin family members to promote viral entry, genome trafficking, organization of replication compartments, assembly, and egress. Recent findings underscore the role of the kinesin-4 family member KIF4A as a novel host factor for HBV. The therapeutic potential of modulating the surface expression of the HBV-entry receptor (NTCP) is discussed, either by suppressing KIF4 expression-necessary for anti-retrograde transport of NTCP to the cell surface-or by disrupting the NTCP-KIF4 interaction. Additionally, emerging pharmacological approaches targeting kinesin-dependent transport are evaluated. By establishing a unified framework that connects motor protein biology to virology, this review identifies key knowledge gaps and outlines future research directions for the development of broad-spectrum, host-targeted, antiviral therapies.

articles.title: Right ventricular infarction with a culprit lesion in the distal right coronary artery: incidence and clinical characteristics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Right ventricular infarction (RVI) is commonly observed in patients with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction and typically results from proximal right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. However, the occurrence of RVI and its clinical characteristics in patients with distal RCA lesions are not well defined.

METHODS: We retrospectively investigated 128 patients with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction caused by RCA occlusion who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention at our institution between January 2020 and December 2023. RVI was diagnosed based on echocardiographic evidence and hemodynamic instability. Clinical characteristics and incidence rates were compared between patients with RVI [the RVI (+) group] and those without RVI [the RVI (-) group]. Findings on coronary angiography were assessed in detail for patients with distal RCA lesions.

RESULTS: RVI was identified in 24/128 patients (18.8%), including 3/31 patients (9.7%) with distal RCA lesions. Right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly lower in the RVI (+) group (-14.0% [-16.4, -11.6] vs. -16.4% [-18.7, -13.9]; p=0.004), as was right ventricular free wall strain (RVFWS) (-14.7% [-18.5, -10.6] vs. -17.7% [-20.7, -15.0]; p=0.01). RVGLS and RVFWS values were comparable in the RVI (+) group regardless of whether the RCA lesion was distal or proximal. There was no significant difference in TIMI flow before or after percutaneous coronary intervention or in the distribution of lesions.

CONCLUSIONS: RVI can be caused by distal RCA lesions, albeit less often than by proximal RCA lesions. No significant differences in RV strain parameters were observed between distal and proximal lesions.

articles.title: Recurrent venous thromboembolism despite natural cycle frozen embryo transfer in a woman with a history of pregnancy-related venous thromboembolism: A case report.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Pregnancies achieved by in vitro fertilization carry an increased risk of VTE, particularly during early gestation. A 33-year-old woman developed deep vein thrombosis during late pregnancy in her first spontaneous conception despite no identifiable thrombophilia. During a subsequent pregnancy achieved by natural cycle frozen embryo transfer, which was selected to avoid exogenous estrogen exposure and potentially reduce the thrombotic risk compared with hormone replacement cycles, she developed recurrent VTE at 8 weeks of gestation. Anticoagulation therapy was initiated, and an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter was placed in late pregnancy because of persistent thrombus and delivery-related risk. A cesarean section was successfully performed, and the IVC filter was removed postpartum after regression of the thrombus. Although natural cycle frozen embryo transfer may reduce the thrombotic risk compared with hormone replacement cycles, it does not eliminate the risk of recurrent VTE in women with a history of pregnancy-associated thrombosis. Early initiation of anticoagulation and careful peripartum management, including selective use of IVC filters, are essential in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Transcatheter closure of a quadriform atrial septal defect with a custom double-fenestrated occluder: A case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quadriform atrial septal defect (ASD) is a rare anatomical and functional variant of ASD. Its rarity and complex morphology pose significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, distinguishing it from more common forms of ASD. Although surgical closure has traditionally been the standard treatment, this case demonstrates the feasibility and efficacy of a minimally invasive transcatheter approach.

CASE REPORT: A 71-year-old woman presented with shortness of breath. Physical examination and transthoracic echocardiography revealed an interatrial septal defect. Right heart catheterization combined with transesophageal echocardiography confirmed a complex ostium secundum ASD with a cribriform morphology resembling a quadriform ASD and associated high-flow, low-resistance pulmonary hypertension. Device deployment required additional manual modification and manipulation by the operators. Successful ASD closure was achieved using a single 40-mm occluder with double fenestrations. The patient remained asymptomatic at the 3-month follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Transcatheter device closure may be an effective treatment option for quadriform ASD, although close follow-up is required to ensure proper device positioning. The increasing complexity of ASD presentations, particularly secundum defects, underscores the importance of continued discussion and experience sharing within the cardiovascular community.

articles.title: Epidemiological and nursing perspectives on insulin-derived amyloidosis: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Insulin-related amyloidosis (IDA) is a subcutaneous complication that may interfere with insulin absorption. Although early detection may prevent the deterioration of glycemic control, this condition is often overlooked. In this scoping review, we aimed to summarize the epidemiological characteristics of IDA and identify future research challenges from a nursing perspective.

METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Japan Medical Abstracts Society database. The eligible studies comprised original articles and case reports regarding patients with histopathologically confirmed IDA published in English or Japanese between January 2009 and August 2022.

RESULTS: No epidemiological research articles, but a total of 29 case-based reports regarding 38 patients, were identified. Most of the patients were male (n=29), they were aged 27-87 years, and both type 1 and type 2 diabetes were represented. The abdominal region was the most common site of lesions (n=23). Histopathology was the primary diagnostic method, although some patients were also evaluated using diagnostic imaging. Many of the patients noticed subcutaneous masses but delayed seeking medical care, and some continued injecting insulin into the affected sites. Medical consultations were often prompted by poor glycemic control or complications of diabetes.

CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the paucity of epidemiological research on IDA and underscores the importance of early detection and education. Limited awareness regarding injection-site abnormalities and the lack of early assessments may contribute to delays in diagnosis.

articles.title: Practice report on a credit-based internship for Medical Sciences students: Examining educational effects through fundamental skills for working adults and qualitative content analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study examined the educational outcomes of a credit-based internship program for third-year university students majoring in Medical Sciences, focusing on changes in their Fundamental Skills for Working Adults and career awareness.

METHODS: Participants were 57 third-year students from the Faculty of Medical Sciences at University A enrolled in a credit-based internship course. On completion of the internship, a web-based questionnaire was administered. The survey included self-evaluations of Fundamental Skills for Working Adults, Likert scales to evaluate subjective learning outcomes, and open-ended responses. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were categorized using qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: Forty-two students responded to the questionnaire (response rate: 73.7%). For Fundamental Skills for Working Adults, more than 80% reported improvements in Proactivity, Active Listening, Situational Awareness, and Discipline. Subjective evaluations showed high overall satisfaction, with 97.6% of respondents reporting being either "very satisfied" or "satisfied," and 95.2% reporting changes in future vision and career awareness. Qualitative analysis yielded five categories, including "multifaceted understanding of medical settings and workplaces" and "concretization of career visions."

CONCLUSION: Credit-based internships can effectively contribute to the development of Fundamental Skills for Working Adults and enhance career awareness among Medical Sciences students.

articles.title: Proposed step training with auditory feedback for post-stroke hemiparetic patients with knee hyperextension.
articles.abstract: [Purpose] The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of a treatment combining auditory feedback regarding knee flexion angle with gait training utilizing proprioceptive feedback in reducing knee hyperextension, focusing on knee joint angles in gait. [Participants and Methods] Six post-stroke hemiparetic patients underwent the intervention, and we measured the knee flexion angle and the shank tilt angle while they were walking with their own ankle-foot orthoses pre- and post-intervention and evaluate the therapeutic effects. [Results] The knee flexion angles in each phase of the gait cycle did not differ significantly between pre- and post-intervention, but the forward tilt angles of the lower leg in the mid-stance phase and the terminal stance phase were significantly higher post-intervention. [Conclusion] These findings suggest that the treatment described in this study alleviated knee hyperextension.

articles.title: Genetic dissection of soybean cyst nematode HG type 2.5.7 resistance reveals a multilocus architecture and favorable alleles from both parents.
articles.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Soybean cyst nematode (SCN; Heterodera glycines) is a major pathogen affecting soybean production worldwide. Understanding the genetic architecture of SCN resistance can facilitate the identification and utilization of favorable resistance alleles. We investigated resistance to SCN HG type 2.5.7 using an F₂ population (n = 184) and a recombinant inbred line (RIL; F₂:₇, n = 323) population derived from Longken336 × Kangxian12, together with seven additional F2 populations. The eight F₂ populations exhibited broad transgressive phenotypic segregation, including progeny with female index (FI) values extending beyond the corresponding parental range. QTL analysis identified six FI-associated loci in the Longken336 × Kangxian12 F₂ population on chromosomes 6, 7, 8, 11, 17, and 18, explaining 4.9-17.0% of the phenotypic variance, with one exceeding the permutation-derived significance threshold. High-density mapping in the RIL population identified resistance-associated loci across 17 chromosomes, with individual loci explaining 2.8-33.5% of the phenotypic variance. Seven QTL were consistently detected across both RIL evaluations, including four that exceeded the corresponding permutation-derived significance thresholds in both RIL evaluations. QTL regions colocalizing with the known resistance loci Rhg1 and Rhg4 were detected, along with favorable alleles contributed by both parental, including the phenotypically susceptible Longken336. Transcriptomic profiling identified contrasting infection-responsive expression patterns in both parental genotypes and prioritized candidate genes within selected QTL regions. These results highlight differences in QTL detection between the F2 and RIL populations and support a multilocus basis for resistance to SCN HG type 2.5.7, with favorable alleles contributed by both parental backgrounds.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s11032-026-01735-9.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Effects on Food-Related Cognition: A Cognitive Neuroscience Framework.
articles.journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity by reducing appetite, cravings and caloric intake. Growing evidence suggests effects on the central nervous system, with cognitive and neuroprotective benefits that cannot be explained by weight loss or glycaemic control alone. However, the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms remain unclear. This review proposes a cognitive neuroscience framework for investigating the effects of GLP-1RAs across multiple levels of food-related information processing. Theoretical models and experimental paradigms are integrated to dissociate perceptual, attentional, motivational, semantic and executive components. The model identifies four levels: (1) early perceptual processing, in which the brain extracts properties including caloric content and transformation; (2) attentional capture and motivational salience, which determine priorities and wanting; (3) semantic organisation, which integrates sensory and functional characteristics of foods and (4) decision-making and executive control, including inhibitory control and effort allocation. GLP-1RAs may differentially modulate these levels, which can be investigated using specific experimental paradigms. This cognitive neuroscience-based approach goes beyond descriptive measures to identify the mechanisms through which GLP-1RAs influence perception, motivation and food decisions. This framework can guide future studies, improve the interpretation of cognitive effects and contribute to the development of more targeted interventions.

articles.title: Consensus recommendations on diagnosis and management of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in paediatric haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
articles.abstract: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication following paediatric allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Its heterogeneous presentation and the absence of standardized guidance contribute to variability in diagnosis and management. The aim was to develop multidisciplinary, consensus-based recommendations for the diagnosis, management and follow-up of PRES in paediatric allogeneic HSCT recipients. A modified Delphi process was conducted between February and September 2025. An international panel comprising transplant physicians, neurologists, neuro-oncologists and neuroradiologists participated in four iterative rounds. A systematic literature review informed statement development across five domains: pathogenesis, clinical features, diagnostics, management and follow-up. Predefined agreement thresholds determined consensus. Thirty-eight statements achieved consensus in the first round, indicating strong agreement. Key recommendations addressed risk factors, early clinical recognition, appropriate neuroimaging and management of contributory factors including hypertension and immunosuppressive therapy. Emphasis was placed on multidisciplinary care, prompt diagnosis and tailored management. Guidance on neurological monitoring and long-term follow-up was also established. These consensus recommendations provide a standardized framework for the management of PRES in paediatric allogeneic HSCT recipients. Their implementation may improve early recognition, optimize treatment and enhance outcomes, while highlighting priorities for future research and prospective guideline development.

articles.title: Thrombolysis and Carotid Stenting for Acute Ischemic Stroke in Severe Hemophilia A: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia

articles.title: Frontal Cerebral Blood Flow Deficits in Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia: Associations With Clinical Symptoms, Peripheral Vascular Biomarkers, and Neuroimaging Measures.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to characterize regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) alterations in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), examine their associations with clinical symptoms and peripheral vascular/synaptic biomarkers, evaluate spatial concordance with gray matter volume (GMV) loss and glucose hypometabolism, and explore CBF's mediating role between biomarkers and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Thirty-five bvFTD patients and 27 matched normal controls (NC) underwent clinical assessments, ASL MRI, 18F-FDG PET, and structural MRI. Plasma vascular (VEGFA, PDGF-BB) and synaptic (NPTXR, NPTX2) biomarkers were measured via the Olink platform. Statistical analyses included group comparisons, ROC analysis, multiple linear regression, and mediation analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with normal controls, bvFTD patients exhibited significantly reduced CBF in both frontal and temporal regions, which showed regional spatial concordance with GMV and FDG uptake in corresponding areas. Frontal CBF demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy and was significantly associated with multiple clinical measures including MMSE, MoCA, ADL, and behavioral scales, as well as with peripheral vascular and synaptic biomarkers. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested statistical indirect associations linking peripheral vascular biomarkers to clinical symptoms through frontal CBF and linking frontal CBF to behavioral outcomes through frontal GMV.

CONCLUSIONS: BvFTD is characterized by frontotemporal hypoperfusion, with frontal CBF closely associated with cognitive, behavioral, and functional impairment. The regional concordance of ASL-derived CBF with gray matter atrophy and glucose hypometabolism supports its potential role as an accessible, non-invasive, and radiation-free complementary neuroimaging biomarker. The mediation findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because they did not remain significant after FDR correction and require validation in larger longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Deciphering Nazi Racial Sorting: The Challenges of Attempting a Big Data Approach.
articles.abstract: In 2019 I started analyzing a large set of "race cards" preserved in the German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv). These cards document anthropometric measurements performed by SS experts during WWII in the territories occupied by the Nazi regime. Applying a big data approach, my goal was to use those cards to study the inner dynamics of the racial selection process and its underlying logic. In the attempts to digitize and analyze the cards I encountered a variety of challenges, from recruiting funding and manpower to programming a suitable software. Decisions taken during this phase were later found to have had various unforeseen implications for the unfolding of the project. Moreover, the seemingly technical task of inserting the data extracted from the cards into a database raised principal interpretative challenges which influenced our understanding of the racial sorting process itself. This paper is dedicated to sharing with the community of researchers some of the experiences accumulated, and methodological insights gained, during the execution of the project.

articles.title: Longitudinal Changes in the Cortico-Reticulospinal Tract Associated with High-Intensity Locomotor Training in Chronic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: High-intensity locomotor training (HIT) is recommended for improving walking capacity, but treatment responses are variable. Understanding the brain changes underlying responsiveness to training could provide insight into this variability. Emerging evidence suggests upregulation of the contralesional cortico-reticulospinal tract (CRST) may contribute to walking function after stroke. However, it is unclear whether CRST upregulation is supportive or maladaptive, and no studies have examined CRST changes after HIT. This study investigated how CRST and corticospinal tract (CST) strength and laterality reorganize, and their relationship with walking capacity after locomotor HIT.

METHODS: Ten participants with chronic stroke completed a 4-week no-intervention control phase then 4 weeks of HIT. Diffusion MRI and 6-minute walk distance were obtained at weeks 0, 4, and 8. Analysis tested changes in ipsilesional and contralesional CRST and CST strength and laterality. Associations between changes in tract laterality and walking capacity were examined.

RESULTS: During the treatment phase (vs the control phase), there were significantly greater increases in contralesional CRST strength (1.02 SD [95% CI: 0.25, 1.79]), contralesional CRST laterality (4.44 [2.15, 6.72]), and 6-minute walk distance (33 meters [17, 50]). Walking capacity improvements were associated with changes in CRST laterality (r = 0.77, P = .01), but not CST laterality (r = -0.01, P = 0.98).

DISCUSSION: Following HIT, increases in contralesional CRST strength and laterality were observed. CRST laterality changes were strongly associated with walking improvements, suggesting an association between contralesional CRST changes and training-related improvements.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02858349, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02858349?term=NCT02858349&rank=1.

articles.title: Biological and epigenetic pathways linking PTSD to accelerated aging: a systematic review and narrative synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) may accelerate biological aging, but the pathways and evidence remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed associations between PTSD and epigenetic and other aging biomarkers.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus through 1 March 2026 for studies of adults with validated PTSD assessment. Two reviewers screened records and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Findings were synthesized narratively because study designs and outcomes were heterogeneous.

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies including 512,768 participants met the inclusion criteria. Twenty-two (91.7%) reported positive associations between PTSD and accelerated biological aging across epigenetic clocks, telomere length, and transcriptional measures; GrimAge acceleration ranged from 1.83 to 2.53 years in veterans. Epigenome-wide association study findings implicated immune- and inflammation-related genes. Longitudinal and twin studies supported temporal precedence and partial independence from genetic confounding. However, 79.2% of studies were United States-based, 45.8% involved military or veteran samples, and most were cross-sectional, limiting generalizability and causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: PTSD is associated with faster biological aging across several biomarkers, but diverse longitudinal and intervention studies are needed before causality or reversibility can be established. More diverse long-term studies and treatment trials areneeded before these measures can guide routine care.

articles.title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency.

CASE DESCRIPTION: We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder.

CONCLUSION: Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

articles.title: Temporal evaluation of antimicrobial resistance development in serial Pseudomonas aeruginosa blood culture isolates.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate antibiotic-specific temporal patterns of the first detection of phenotypic resistance in serial Pseudomonas aeruginosa blood culture isolates and within-patient susceptibility transitions over time.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included P. aeruginosa blood culture isolates from hospitalized patients between 2010 and 2025. In patients with repeated blood cultures, antimicrobial susceptibility was evaluated by antibiotic. We analyzed changes in resistance between the first and last isolates using the McNemar test, and assessed time-to-resistance using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 1086 blood culture isolates from 523 patients were analyzed. 144 patients had repeated blood cultures and were included in the serial-isolate analyses. McNemar analysis showed more frequent transitions to resistance for imipenem, meropenem, piperacillin/tazobactam, cefepime, and amikacin. Phenotypic resistance was detected earlier for carbapenems (median 118 days for imipenem and 119 days for meropenem), whereas amikacin showed a longer median time to first detection of phenotypic resistance (403 days). Sensitivity analyses under alternative event-time assumptions showed broadly consistent temporal patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: The timing of first detection of phenotypic resistance in P. aeruginosa bacteremia varied across antibiotic classes, indicating that susceptibility profiles may change during serial follow-up.

articles.title: The association between cardiovascular diseases and their risk factors in Austria and Slovakia: regression analyses based on the European Health Interview Survey (2019).
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) account for one in three deaths in the European Union. Slovakia has twice the rate of amenable mortality than neighboring Austria. This study aimed to examine the association between CVDs and risk factors and to describe similarities and differences in the observed patterns.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Weighted 2019 European Health Interview Survey data were analyzed for adults aged ≥ 45 in Austria and Slovakia. Multivariable logistic regression analyses assessed associations between CVDs and its risk factors, adjusting for socioeconomic and demographic characteristics, and regions.

RESULTS: The Austrian sample included 9,501 respondents and the SK sample 3,505. CVD prevalence was 8.8% in Austria and 15.3% in Slovakia. In both countries, sleep problems (Austria: OR: 1.90, 95% CI: 1.57-2.32; Slovakia: OR: 2.44, 95% CI: 1.95-3.04) were associated with reporting CVDs. In Austria, hypertension (OR: 1.88, 95% CI: 1.54-2.30), and diabetes (OR: 1.81, 95% CI: 1.42-2.31) were also associated with CVDs, as were diabetes (OR: 1.69, 95% CI: 1.31-2.20) and physical inactivity (OR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.16-2.36) in Slovakia. Regional associations were more pronounced in Austria than in Slovakia.

CONCLUSIONS: Although causality cannot be inferred, patterns in CVD prevalence and associated risk factors may support targeted national and regional prevention strategies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: conceptual framework, clinical implications, and therapeutic perspectives with a focus on SGLT2 inhibitors.
articles.abstract:
