PURPOSE: The increasing prevalence and frequent coexistence of cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic diseases represent a major challenge to contemporary preventive cardiology, substantially contributing to adverse clinical outcomes and premature cardiovascular mortality. In response to this growing burden, a recent presidential scientific statement from the American Heart Association introduced the concept of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome as an integrated clinical construct that captures the complex and bidirectional interactions among these conditions, with a primary focus on cardiovascular risk stratification and mortality prevention.

METHODS: This review summarises and critically evaluates the conceptual foundations, clinical implications, and therapeutic considerations of CKM syndrome from a national and multidisciplinary perspective, with particular emphasis on the positioning of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) across the CKM continuum.

RESULTS: The introduction of the CKM framework is particularly timely in the era of disease-modifying therapies with proven cardiorenal protective effects, notably sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i). However, the real-world implementation of the proposed CKM definition and staging system may be influenced by regional epidemiology, healthcare structures, and patterns of comorbidity. Given the high and rising prevalence of cardiometabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular mortality in Türkiye, a critical appraisal of the CKM syndrome from a national and multidisciplinary perspective is warranted.

CONCLUSION: Practical challenges and opportunities related to patient identification, risk stratification, and integrated management strategies in routine clinical practice are discussed, with the aim of informing preventive cardiology approaches and guiding future research priorities within and beyond the Turkish healthcare context.

articles.title: Resource utilization and costs of managing severe adverse events associated with chemotherapy and immunotherapy in lung cancer: a consensus-based microcosting study in Jordan.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To estimate the direct medical costs of managing panel‑selected Grade III/IV adverse events that were considered most relevant to the Jordanian clinical setting associated with chemo-immunotherapy regimens in lung cancer patients from the Jordanian healthcare provider perspective and to identify the principal cost drivers.

METHODS: A microcosting approach was employed, utilizing consensus-based management protocols derived through a two-round modified Delphi process in Jordan. Fourteen Grade III/IV adverse events were evaluated. Episode costs were estimated from adverse-event detection to acute clinical resolution in 6 months where applicable or 6 months of treatment for chronic adverse events, using multiple Jordanian cost sources. One-way deterministic sensitivity analysis was performed. No discount rate was applied due to the costing of one episode less than a year duration.

RESULTS: Base-case episode costs ranged from $55.06 for maculopapular rash to $5118.17 for pneumonitis. The five most costly adverse events per episode were pneumonitis ($5118.17), myocarditis ($3872.05), diarrhea and colitis ($3008.23), febrile neutropenia ($2,876.81), and thrombocytopenia ($2867.94). Hospitalization was the dominant cost driver, accounting for 47.4% of mean episode costs across all adverse events.

CONCLUSION: These consensus-derived unit cost estimates provide critical inputs for future cost-effectiveness analyses of lung cancer systemic therapies in Jordan.

articles.title: The Synergistic Antibacterial Activity of Curcumin and Quercetin Against Nocardia seriolae and Evaluate Their Therapeutic Effects in the Infected Largemouth Bass.
articles.abstract: Nocardia seriolae is an important bacterial pathogen causing chronic granulomatous disease in cultured fish, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to identify natural compounds with synergistic antibacterial activity against N. seriolae and evaluate their protective effects in largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides). A structure-guided screening strategy targeting N. seriolae isocitrate lyase (ICL) was performed using molecular docking, ADMET prediction, and in vitro antibacterial assays. Curcumin and quercetin were selected as candidate compounds based on their predicted interactions with ICL and antibacterial activity. The combination of curcumin and quercetin exhibited a synergistic effect against N. seriolae, with a fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) of 0.25 at a fixed 1:1 ratio, reducing the effective concentration of each compound eightfold compared with individual treatments. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable interactions between the two compounds and the ICL model, while enzyme activity analysis showed that the combination significantly reduced intracellular ICL activity. Furthermore, the combined treatment inhibited bacterial growth, decreased metabolic activity, and caused severe disruption of bacterial cell envelope integrity, as demonstrated by transmission electron microscopy and alkaline phosphatase leakage assays. Acute toxicity evaluation showed that the 96-h LC50 of the curcumin-quercetin mixture in largemouth bass was 24 mg/L, indicating relatively low short-term toxicity at the therapeutic concentration. In an experimental infection model, immersion treatment with the curcumin-quercetin combination reduced bacterial burden, alleviated granulomatous lesions in visceral organs, and improved survival of infected fish. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that curcumin and quercetin provide a promising natural-compound combination for controlling N. seriolae infection and provide a potential strategy for managing fish nocardiosis.

articles.title: The Cytokine Response of Circulating Immune Cells to Rhinovirus (RV-A16) is Reduced in Severe Asthma.
articles.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
articles.abstract: Severe asthma patients (SA) are more susceptible to respiratory infections with human rhinoviruses (HRV) than healthy subjects (H), causing exacerbations. In response to HRV, circulating immune cells are recruited to and activated at the local sites of infection. Hypothesis: The activation of circulating immune cells in response to HRV is impaired in severe asthma. We infected peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of H (n = 20) and SA (n = 50) with RV-A16 ex vivo. Cytokines were measured in culture supernatants by ELISA. Data were compared between SA and H and correlated to asthma phenotype biomarkers. RV-A16 induced IFNα, IFNγ, CCL2, CCL5, TNFα, IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-8. Except for CCL2, these cytokine responses were reduced in SA versus H. In SA, IFNα, IL-6 and CCL5 responses correlated negatively, but IL-1β correlated positively to FeNO. IFNγ correlated positively to blood eosinophils and serum IL-33, and INFα correlated positively to serum total IgE. Cytokine responses of circulating immune cells to RV-A16 are reduced in SA. Cytokines are differentially affected in allergic, eosinophilic or T2 low asthma. This could help to explain the increased risk for exacerbations in HRV infections in severe asthma and differences between phenotypes. Circulating immune cells might be considered as drug targets to reduce exacerbation rates.

articles.title: Assessing effects of low-dose CT attenuation correction on quantification and image quality on a LAFOV PET system with a modified NEMA-IQ phantom.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over the past decades, efforts have been directed toward increasing the sensitivity of PET systems to enable low-dose PET imaging and shorter scan times. The Biograph Vision Quadra PET/CT scanner (Siemens Healthineers, Knoxville, TN, USA) combines an increased solid angle coverage with time of flight, enabling a significant reduction in administered activity. To fully benefit from low-dose PET imaging, the dose of the CT scan should ideally also be reduced.

PURPOSE: The CT radiation dose can be reduced by lowering the tube voltage and exposure as well as by the use of tin filtration. Reducing the CT dose must be carefully aligned with any impact that changing CT image quality and quantitative metrics may have on the PET quantification, for example via linear attenuation coefficients. We evaluate the impact of low-dose CT protocols on the PET quantification in soft-tissue-like and bone-equivalent materials using a customized phantom.

METHODS: The phantom was assembled out of a NEMA-IQ phantom, several layers of saline and two bovine long bones, to simulate a patient positioned with arms down. A 10-min PET scan with 47 different accompanying CT scans was acquired. The CT tube voltage and exposure were varied between 70  k V  to  140  k V  , with and without tin filtration, and 7  mAs  to  400  mAs  , respectively. The effect of the different CT parameters on the PET image quality and quantitative accuracy was assessed via several quantitative metrics, including standardized uptake value (SUV) and signal-to-noise ratio, along with the CT dose length product (DLP).

RESULTS: The recorded DLP values suggest that using all tube voltages except 140  k V  combined with exposures in the range of 7  m A s  to  30  m A s  , can result in dose savings of ≥ 80  %  compared to a typical clinical protocol ( 120  k V  , 50  mAs  ). Compared to this typical protocol, HU differed more in bone ( 10  %  to  40  %  difference) than in soft tissue ( 1  %  to  30  %  difference), and more streak artefacts and photon starvation were seen when configuring low tube voltages and exposures, with an accompanying increase in CT noise. The observed artefacts were transferred with low intensity to the PET images via the attenuation map. The SUV mean  remained within 2  %  of the SUV mean  of the typical clinical protocol for most tested protocols. The presence of artefacts in the CT images had a bigger impact on PET quantification in both soft tissue and bone ( SUV mean  difference of 10  %  to  20  %  ) than any difference in HU. Protocols that resulted in artefacts showed an increased inaccuracy in attenuation correction and scatter estimation, as assessed via the "lung" residual error (up to 10  %  to  20  %  increase).

CONCLUSIONS: Even for low-dose CT protocols, PET quantification remained consistent in all NEMA-IQ spheres for many materials. Beam hardening and photon starvation in the CT image are likely to occur in specific body regions such as hips, shoulders or the abdomen for an arms-down scan and these effects had a bigger impact on the quantification than any difference in HU in both soft tissue and bone. This therefore should be considered when selecting suitable CT imaging parameters.

articles.title: Relationships Among MHC Diversity, Parasites and Secondary Sexual Colouration.
articles.abstract: Sexual selection via honest (costly) signals of fitness can generate patterns in immunogenetic diversity at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). MHC diversity explains variation in immunocompetence-and therefore fitness-thus impacting the ability to generate honest signals. Differences in guppy (Poecilia reticulata) colour patterns can be driven by opposing selection pressures of predation and female mate choice, but the effect of parasitism has received less attention. By studying 21 wild guppy populations in Trinidad, we sought to quantify covariation among parasitic Gyrodactylus spp. infections, male sexual ornamentation (orange and black colouration) and genetic variation at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) at both individual and population levels. We found population level support for a correlation between MHC diversity and Gyrodactylus prevalence, including an overall association between MHC supertype composition and prevalence. At the individual level, supertype (functional) diversity again emerged as a more informative measure than allelic richness alone. Predation was associated with Gyrodactylus prevalence and orange, but not black, colouration. Notably, some of these relationships differed between the individual and population levels. Further, much of this variation was explained by processes acting at a broader geographic scale within river drainages, which comprise divergent guppy lineages. These findings suggest that evolutionary history and processes such as genetic drift and gene flow contribute substantially to these relationships, but that ecological variation (i.e., predation) interacts with these processes. Our findings indicate that multi-trait relationships between colour, immunogenetic diversity and infection are best examined within their broader evolutionary and ecological contexts.

articles.title: Dual-Lumen Microcatheters in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Five Useful Techniques to Facilitate Coronary Wiring in Non-CTO Lesions.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual-lumen microcatheters (DLMs) are adjunctive devices that has been increasingly incorporated into contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). These catheters contain two independent working lumens, a rapid-exchange (RX) port and an over-the-wire (OTW) port, within a single low-profile shaft, permitting guidewire advancement and exchange within a shared working space. Published consensus documents have focused predominantly on chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions, with less on non-CTO lesions.

METHODS: This narrative review describes five practical applications of DLMs in non-CTO lesions. For each technique, we outlined the procedural rationale, a stepwise approach, and technical considerations.

RESULTS: Five applications are presented: (1) aorto-ostial wiring in the setting of a protruding ostial stent or anomalous coronary takeoff; (2) reverse wiring of a side branch with an acute or angulated takeoff; (3) side-branch re-entry after stent deployment; (4) contrast injection through the OTW port; and (5) parallel wiring for complex lesions.

CONCLUSIONS: DLMs offer several practical applications beyond CTO PCI. Familiarity with these techniques and their technical considerations may help operators select and apply DLM-assisted strategies in complex non-CTO lesions.

articles.title: Myeloid-Derived Growth Factor Alleviates Diabetic Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease by Up-Regulating ABCA1 and ABCG1 Expression via the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα Pathway.
articles.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
articles.abstract: The regulatory role of bone marrow in systemic metabolic processes remains incompletely characterized. Myeloid-derived growth factor (MYDGF) is a myeloid cell-secreted factor with emerging metabolic functions, but its action in diabetes-associated non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (DM NAFLD) is undefined. To investigate the influence of myeloid cell-derived MYDGF on DM NAFLD, both loss- and gain-of-function approaches were applied in vivo. DM NAFLD models were established in Mydgf-knockout (KO) mice, PpargΔLyz2 mice and PpargΔLyz2/KO (DKO) mice. For in vitro studies, primary Kupffer cells (KCs) were stimulated with high glucose and recombinant MYDGF (rMYDGF) and bone marrow cells (BMCs) were co-cultured with KCs via a transwell system. Protein levels related to DM NAFLD pathology and signalling pathways were quantified. In this study, we found that MYDGF was significantly downregulated in DM NAFLD mouse liver. Myeloid MYDGF deficiency exacerbated hepatic inflammation, lipogenesis, steatosis and macrophage infiltration, while reconstituting myeloid MYDGF reversed these phenotypes. rMYDGF attenuated inflammation, reduced macrophage foaming, decreased cholesterol content and increased efferocytosis. Mechanistically, MYDGF induced AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation, which subsequently activated the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ)/liver X receptor α (LXRα) pathway in KCs and upregulated downstream ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression. These results identify the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 cascade as the core signalling axis mediating MYDGF's metabolic regulatory effects, which bridges the previously unrecognized functional linkage between myeloid cell function and hepatic lipid homeostasis, and explains the protective phenotype observed in MYDGF-reconstituted DM NAFLD mice. In conclusion, myeloid cell-derived MYDGF ameliorates DM NAFLD, decreases cholesterol content in macrophages and reduces lipid accumulation via the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα pathway. MYDGF serves as a key mediator for bone marrow-liver metabolic crosstalk, indicating that the bone marrow may act as a potential endocrine target for the prevention and treatment of diabetes-related metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Direct and Indirect Effects of Historic Residential Redlining on Prevalence of Cardiometabolic Diseases via Food Access.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated food access as a potential pathway between structural racism and the prevalence of cardiometabolic disease.

METHODS: A total of 11,457 census tracts across 201 counties, within 38 states, were combined for a final analytic sample. Direct and indirect relationships between redlining and each cardiometabolic disease via food access were investigated using structural equation modeling run in Stata v17, controlling for the population of each census tract.

RESULTS: Mean prevalence of diabetes was 11.8%, high blood pressure 31.9%, coronary heart disease 6.0%, and obesity 31.8%. Redlining (0.22, p < 0.001) and lower food access (-0.11, p < 0.001) were directly associated with higher prevalence of diabetes. Redlining (0.10, p < 0.001) and lower food access (-0.10, p < 0.001) were directly associated with higher prevalence of high blood pressure. Redlining (0.12, p < 0.001) and lower food access (-0.04, p < 0.001) were directly associated with higher prevalence of coronary heart disease. Redlining (0.18, p < 0.001) and lower food access (-0.12, p < 0.001) were directly associated with higher prevalence of obesity. Redlining was also significantly indirectly associated with each condition via food access.

CONCLUSIONS: Structural racism was associated with higher cardiometabolic disease prevalence via decreased food access. Interventions to improve access to healthy food at the community level may be needed to address the impact of structural racism on health.

articles.title: Final 5-Year Results of Abluminal Groove-Filled Biodegradable-Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stent Versus Durable-Polymer Everolimus-Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM.

AIMS: In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5-year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus-eluting stent (EES).

METHODS: TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non-stratified outcomes in DM versus non-DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia-driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis.

RESULTS: Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non-DM patients, TLF (p < 0.001), cardiac death (p < 0.001), TVMI (p = 0.002), ischemia-driven TLR (p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis (p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM.

CONCLUSION: This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.

articles.title: Optimal power load ranges for the power clean and hang power clean weight-lifting derivatives: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to systematically evaluate the impact of different loads on the output power of the power clean (PC) and hang power clean (HPC). A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, EMBASE, and EBSCO identified 14 eligible studies involving 197 participants. The results of the meta-analysis showed that compared to low loads (≤40% one-repetition maximum [1RM]), moderate-to-high (>40% to ≤70% 1RM), high (>70% to ≤85% 1RM), and very high loads (>85% 1RM) produced greater acute peak power in both the PC (SMD = 0.58, 95% CI [0.17, 0.98]; SMD = 0.80, 95% CI [0.39, 1.21]; SMD = 0.68, 95% CI [0.16, 1.20] respectively) and the HPC (SMD = 0.58, 95% CI [0.28, 0.88]; SMD = 0.80, 95% CI [0.20, 1.40]; SMD = 0.94, 95% CI [0.55, 1.32] respectively) (all p < 0.01). In contrast, pairwise differences among Zones 2-4 were small to trivial and statistically nonsignificant for both the PC (SMD = 0.23, 0.19, and 0.06, respectively) and the HPC (SMD = 0.18, 0.01, and -0.21, respectively), consistent with a plateau in the power-load relationship once loads exceed 40% 1RM. Thus, the present evidence supports loads >40% 1RM as a broad range for high acute peak power expression. Pairwise comparisons among the >40% to ≤70%, >70% to ≤85%, and >85% 1RM zones did not demonstrate statistical superiority of any single higher-load range.

articles.title: Things We Do for No Reason™: Routinely withholding IV iron in hospitalized patients with infection.
articles.abstract: Withholding intravenous (IV) iron to treat iron-deficiency anemia (IDA) is a common practice in patients hospitalized with acute bacterial infection, driven by the theoretical risk from in vitro studies that iron may support bacterial growth. However, IV iron administration is beneficial for multiple patient populations with IDA, such as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease, inflammatory bowel disease, and malignancy. Additionally, recent data suggest that administering IV iron in patients with infections does not worsen clinical outcomes. Routine withholding of IV iron in patients with adequately controlled infections should be avoided.

articles.title: EUS-PPG Measured Distal to the Thrombus: A Reliable Way to Detect the Pressure Gradient in Patients With Cirrhosis and Portal Vein Thrombosis.
articles.journal: Digestive endoscopy : official journal of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In patients with portal vein thrombosis (PVT), hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) does not accurately reflect portal pressure. This study aimed to evaluate the application of endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided portal pressure gradient (PPG) in cirrhotic patients with PVT.

METHODS: In patients with cirrhosis who had gastroesophageal varices (GEV) and PVT were included. The PPG proximal to the PVT (Pro-PVT PPG), PPG distal to the PVT (Dis-PVT PPG), and gastric variceal pressure gradient (GVPG) were measured by puncturing the target vessels under the guidance of EUS. The pressure gradients measured using different methods were compared and correlated with clinical characteristics.

RESULTS: A total of 51 patients with GEV and PVT were included in the final analysis. There was a substantial agreement between Dis-PVT PPG and GVPG, with an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of 0.693 (0.514-0.813). Dis-PVT PPG and GVPG were significantly higher in the patients with bleeding history than in those without (17.0 mmHg vs. 11.3 mmHg, and 18.0 mmHg vs. 7.0 mmHg, p < 0.01 for both). In addition, patients with a Dis-PVT PPG ≥ 12 mmHg had a higher incidence of red sign (odds ratio [OR] = 5.6, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.6-20.2) and bleeding history (OR = 7.0, 95% CI = 2.0-26.4).

CONCLUSIONS: Dis-PVT PPG may be a preferred index that reflects the status of portal hypertension in cirrhotic patients with PVT and is associated with a bleeding history of GEV.

articles.title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling to Predict the Exposure and Provide Dosage Regimens of Oseltamivir in Pregnant Women with Comorbid CES1 Polymorphism and Hepatic Cirrhosis.
articles.abstract: Oseltamivir (OSE) is widely prescribed for pregnant women with influenza; however, its optimal dosing strategy remains undefined in cases involving carboxylesterase 1 (CES1) gene polymorphism and hepatic cirrhosis. This study aimed to explore OSE dosing regimens for pregnant patients with comorbid CES1 polymorphism and hepatic cirrhosis. A mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of OSE was first built and verified in healthy populations, then extrapolated to adult patients with CES1 polymorphism, hepatic cirrhosis, and pregnant patients. The PBPK model successfully predicted and verified the PKs of OSE and its active metabolite oseltamivir carboxylate (OSC) in both non-pregnant and pregnant women. Simulation results showed that the fold errors of the predicted and observed values of the area under the curve (AUC) and peak plasma concentration (Cmax) values ranged from 0.5 to 2.0, with the average folding error and absolute average folding error for all concentration-time data points reaching 0.89 and 1.38, respectively. Importantly, for pregnant patients, OSE administration is recommended to be tailored by CES1 genotype, cirrhosis severity, and pregnancy trimester, to achieve post-dosing AUC levels comparable to those of the non-pregnant reference population. This integrated pregnancy PBPK model enables us to comprehensively and extensively explore the PK characteristics of OSE and OSC in pregnant women under complex scenarios, thereby providing valuable guidance for clinical applications and precise management of influenza during pregnancy.

articles.title: The Cognitive Functions of Youth With Obesity: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis examined the associations between obesity and performance across seven cognitive domains (inhibition, cognitive flexibility, working memory, verbal fluency, planning, attention, and intelligence quotient [IQ]) in youth under 18 years. Developmental stage (school-aged children vs. adolescents) and sample sex composition examined as moderators. Evidence on executive function in youth with comorbid obesity and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) was synthesized qualitatively.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, 22 studies comparing youth with obesity to normal-weight peers were included. Effect sizes (Hedges' g) were pooled using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses compared school-aged children and adolescents; meta-regression examined age and proportion of female participants as study-level moderators.

RESULTS: Youth with obesity performed significantly worse than normal-weight peers on inhibition (g+ = -0.193), cognitive flexibility (g+ = -0.499), working memory (g+ = -0.652), verbal fluency (g+ = -0.420), attention (g+ = -0.526), and IQ (g+ = -0.288); planning could not be estimated. School-aged children showed deficits on inhibition, working memory, and attention; adolescents on working memory and attention only. Between-subgroup tests were non-significant for all domains (p ≥ 0.26), so developmental differences should be interpreted with caution. Meta-regression showed that a higher proportion of female participants in a study sample, a study-level characteristic rather than an individual-level effect, was associated with larger working memory deficits (p = 0.002); age did not moderate any domain. Two ADHD-comorbidity studies received qualitative synthesis only.

DISCUSSION: Obesity is associated with poorer cognitive performance in youth across several domains, with sex composition of the study sample emerging as a moderator of the working memory finding; differences between school-aged children and adolescents were not significant and should be interpreted cautiously. Substantial heterogeneity, predominantly observational designs, inconsistent BMI criteria, and limited ADHD-stratified data constrain causal inference. Future studies should standardize weight definitions, report age- and ADHD-stratified data, and consider bidirectional pathways.

articles.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of a Peer-Delivered Group Intervention to Mitigate Risk of Disordered Eating Among Pregnant Individuals: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The International journal of eating disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pregnancy and postpartum are high-risk periods for body dissatisfaction and disordered eating, which adversely affect the wellbeing of pregnant people and their children. The Pregnant Body Project (PBP) is a peer-led intervention based on an empirically supported eating disorder prevention program, adapted to address the unique context and risks of pregnant individuals who have a prior history of disordered eating.

METHOD: Pregnant individuals with a history of disordered eating (N = 65) were randomized to a 6-week virtual peer-led PBP group (n = 32) or an active time- and dose-matched health education control (n = 33). Participants completed measures of feasibility, engagement, acceptability, satisfaction, and clinical outcomes (e.g., disordered eating) at pre- and post-test. Descriptive statistics summarize primary implementation outcomes. Secondary clinical outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed effects models with time, treatment group, and their interaction, estimated using full information maximum likelihood under an intent to-treat approach.

RESULTS: Recruitment, retention, and data collection met or exceeded preregistered thresholds. Program completion (88%) and homework completion (88%) indicated strong engagement, and PBP participants' average ratings for satisfaction, appropriateness, and acceptability were above the midpoint. Group leaders demonstrated high fidelity and competency. While not statistically significant, small effect sizes favored PBP for improvements in eating disorder symptoms and body image satisfaction (between group d = -0.10 to -0.26; within group d = -0.13 to -0.46).

DISCUSSION: Findings support the feasibility and acceptability of a virtual, peer-led intervention tailored to pregnant individuals with a history of disordered eating. These findings provide a foundation for a larger-scale hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial.

articles.title: Population Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Model of Propofol in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Propofol is a commonly used intravenous anesthetic. Although the kidney plays a minor role in elimination, pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) have been found to be significantly affected in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The study was a prospective, single-centre study in CKD patients undergoing surgery under general anaesthesia. A total of 9-10 blood samples were collected from each of 38 patients at prespecified sampling time points for propofol quantification. Time to loss of consciousness and time to eye opening were recorded, along with the bispectral index (BIS), as PD endpoints. The concentration time profile (287 samples) and BIS data from 35 patients were included in model development. Creatinine clearance was identified as an important covariate affecting the PK model. Stage 3 and 4 patients achieved higher plasma concentrations at the same induction and maintenance propofol doses and tended to have lower BIS. The propofol Cmax was higher in stage 4 patients than in stages 1 or 2. The average concentration at LOC was significantly higher in stage 4 (6.61 ± 6.28 µg/mL) as compared to stages 1 (2.06 ± 1.69 µg/mL) or stage 2 (1.64 ± 1.77 µg/mL). Average time to eye opening was also higher in stages 3 and 4 (12.9 ± 4.7 and 9.5 ± 3.1 min, respectively) as compared to stages 1 and 2 (7 ± 3.2 and 7.9 ± 2.4 min, respectively). The moderate-severe renal impairment status decreases the requirement of the induction dose of propofol to achieve surgical anesthesia compared to those with normal creatinine clearance. Prolonged clearance also leads to prolonged emergence from anesthesia.

articles.title: A First-In-Human, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Single and Multiple Ascending Dose Study of Izicopan (INF904), A Second-Generation Oral Small Molecule C5a Receptor Inhibitor, in Healthy Participants.
articles.abstract: This was a first-in-human, single-center, Phase 1 study of izicopan (formerly INF904), a potent oral, second-generation small molecule antagonist of C5aR1, in healthy adults. Participants were randomized to a single oral dose of izicopan 3-240 mg or matched placebo (single ascending dose [SAD]), or multiple doses of izicopan 30 mg once daily (QD), 30 or 90 mg twice daily (BID), or matched placebo, for 14 days (multiple ascending dose [MAD]). In the SAD study, izicopan plasma concentration increased with dose from 3 to 240 mg; the mean maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) was 21.5-1216.0 ng/mL, reached at a median time (tmax) of 3.5-6.0 h, followed by a biphasic decline. In the MAD study, a steady state appeared to have been reached within 14 days, and AUC0-tau exhibited an accumulation ratio of ∼2-fold following BID dosing, suggesting an effective half-life of ∼12 h. In an ex vivo whole blood PD assay, izicopan resulted in >90% blockade of CD11b upregulation by recombinant human C5a across almost all dose cohorts from Days 2-15. Adverse events were mild or moderate in severity. In conclusion, izicopan was safe across all single and multiple doses evaluated. Sufficient izicopan exposure was achieved rapidly to exert >90% blockade of C5a-C5aR1 signaling.

articles.title: Early and Long-Term Outcomes of Carotid Endarterectomy in Patients With Carotid Near-Occlusion Versus Preocclusive Carotid Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical role of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with carotid near-occlusion (CNO) remains a subject of ongoing debate, and comparative data regarding its long-term efficacy versus preocclusive carotid stenosis is limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of CEA in these two distinct subsets of high-grade carotid disease.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a prospectively maintained database of 1775 consecutive CEAs performed at a single center between January 2014 and September 2025. The study cohort included 81 procedures for CNO (Group 1) and 144 for preocclusive carotid stenosis > 95% with distal lumen recovery (Group 2). CNO was defined by distal internal carotid artery caliber reduction and further stratified by the presence of full distal collapse.

RESULTS: Results showed that patients in Group 2 were significantly older than those in Group 1 (76 ± 8 vs. 72 ± 8 years; p < 0.001). Symptomatic presentation was more frequent in Group 1 (35.8% vs. 24.3%; p = 0.06), and concordant ipsilateral ischemic brain lesions were significantly more common in CNO patients (24.5% vs. 9%; p = 0.001). Regarding perioperative safety, no 30-day deaths or major neurologic events occurred in Group 1, while Group 2 had a 30-day stroke/death rate of 3.4% (p = 0.08 vs. Group 1). During a median follow-up of 30 months (range 1-140), the estimated 6-year overall survival was 84% for Group 1% and 73% for Group 2 (p = 0.1). Notably, ipsilateral stroke at 6 years occurred in 0% of CNO patients compared with 8.5% in the preocclusive group (p = 0.03). Stroke-free survival at 6 years was 84% in Group 1% and 71% in Group 2 (p = 0.09). While freedom from restenosis was comparable (78.5% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.2), late carotid occlusion was significantly more frequent in the CNO group (6% vs. 0%; p = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center series, patients undergoing CEA for carotid near-occlusion demonstrated favorable perioperative safety and a lower observed incidence of long-term ipsilateral stroke during follow-up compared with those treated for preocclusive stenosis, even in the presence of full distal collapse. The absence of a medically managed control group and the small number of events made these findings hypothesis-generating. However, the higher incidence of late restenosis and occlusion in near-occlusion highlights the importance of a personalized, intensified postoperative surveillance, particularly for patients with full distal collapse.

articles.title: The Use of Maternal Race in Antenatal Screening Tests: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: The historical legacy of white supremacy in the United States has been institutionalized in ways that contribute to maternal health care inequities, including the treatment of race as a biological risk factor in health care. Race is a social construct with neither a genetic nor biological basis, and racism is the major contributor to adverse outcomes. Recently, medical specialties have identified and reduced the use of race in clinical tests and decision-making. Identifying the use of race in antenatal care is essential to dismantling institutional racism and improving perinatal outcomes. We conducted a narrative review to describe the role of race in currently recommended antenatal care tests. We identified tests considered routine and gold standard for antenatal care in the United States based on the 2025 American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists Clinical Consensus for Tailored Prenatal Care Delivery. We searched bibliographic databases and reference lists. Of the 18 tests found in routine antenatal care, 3 currently use race, 3 previously used race, and 12 do not and have not used race. Currently, Black race is considered a moderate risk factor for preeclampsia, and race-specific adjustment factors remain embedded in the first-trimester combined and second-trimester quadruple aneuploidy screening for the interpretation of maternal serum markers. Historically, anemia diagnosis definitions included race-specific thresholds, and race and ethnicity were considered alongside other risk factors when recommending screening for hemoglobinopathies and gestational diabetes. Although the inclusion of race was likely an attempt to address maternal health care inequities, it can perpetuate racist rhetoric that an individual's increased risk is attributable to inherent biological differences. These findings reinforce the need to review antenatal care practices and eliminate race-based clinical guidelines to provide evidence-based health care and advance perinatal health equity.

articles.title: Evaluating plasma phosphorylated tau217 for clinical rule-out of cerebral amyloid pathology: Evidence from a memory clinic cohort.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPlasma phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217) is a promising biomarker for Alzheimer's disease amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology, but cut-offs require validation.ObjectiveThe aim was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of plasma phosphorylated tau 217 for identifying cerebral amyloid pathology to reduce the need for more invasive or resource-intensive confirmatory testing by identifying individuals with a low likelihood of amyloid pathology.MethodsElecsys® pTau217 was evaluated in a memory clinic cohort using ROC analysis. Cut-offs were derived using sensitivity-weighted Euclidean distance and bootstrap resampling.ResultspTau217 discriminated Aβ-positive from Aβ-negative individuals (AUC 0.854). The cut-off was 0.169 pg/mL (95% CI 0.140-0.200), with 87.7% sensitivity and 77.0% specificity. Age and sex adjustment did not improve performance.ConclusionsThe threshold was consistent with previously reported low cut-offs, supporting potential rule-out utility; however, its sensitivity precludes stand-alone exclusion of Aβ pathology in memory clinic populations.

articles.title: Pulsed Field Versus Contact Force Radiofrequency Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) remains a challenging arrhythmia to manage, and catheter ablation is a cornerstone therapy. Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) has recently emerged as a novel non-thermal alternative to Contact Force Radiofrequency (CF-RF) ablation. This meta-analysis compares the efficacy, safety, and procedural efficiency of PFA versus CF-RF in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using randomized controlled trials and cohort studies identified from MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases. Primary outcomes included 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia (AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia), procedure duration, fluoroscopy time, and major complications. Subgroup analyses were performed based on PFA device type (Farapulse vs. HT-9000Pro) and patient characteristics, including left atrial size and AF duration.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies met inclusion criteria. PFA was associated with significantly higher 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia compared with CF-RF (OR = 1.36, 95% CI 1.26-1.47, p < 0.001). Procedure time was markedly shorter with PFA (MD = -40.5 minutes, p < 0.001), while fluoroscopy time also showed a significant reduction (MD = -1.8 minutes, p = 0.001). Major complications were significantly lower with PFA (1.2% vs. 2.8%; OR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.35-0.57, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In persistent AF, PFA, demonstrates superior efficacy, safety, and procedural efficiency compared with CF-RFA, supporting its role as a potential first-line ablation strategy. Larger multicenter trials with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm durability and device-specific outcomes.

articles.title: Dry, but not wet, age-related macular degeneration increases Alzheimer's disease risk: Findings from a multidimensional analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAge-related macular degeneration (AMD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) share pathophysiological features along the eye-brain axis, but epidemiological, molecular, and causal evidence has not been systematically integrated.ObjectiveTo determine whether AMD, particularly its dry subtype, is causally associated with AD by integrating global epidemiological, bibliometric, molecular, and genetic evidence.MethodsWe analyzed Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, performed a bibliometric analysis, explored shared molecular targets using GeneCards and STRING, and conducted bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) using genome-wide association study summary statistics.ResultsFrom 1990 to 2021, AMD and AD prevalence rose in parallel and peaked in high socio-demographic index regions. Bibliometric analysis of 498 publications showed increasing attention to cellular senescence and MR. Bioinformatics identified 241 shared genes between dry AMD and AD, enriched in complement cascades, MAPK/PI3K-Akt signaling, and lipid metabolism. MR showed that dry AMD causally increased AD risk (OR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.06-1.24, p = 0.0005), whereas overall AMD showed no causal effect and reverse causality was absent.ConclusionsDry AMD, but not AMD overall, is a causal risk factor for AD, providing genetic support for the eye-brain axis hypothesis. Shared pathways, particularly complement dysregulation, may inform risk stratification and therapeutic development.

articles.title: Biphasic Biochemical Pattern Suggestive of Second-Wave Muscle Injury in Exertional Rhabdomyolysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundExertional rhabdomyolysis is an important cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) in otherwise healthy individuals following strenuous physical activity. Serum creatine kinase (CK) typically peaks within 24 to 72 h and progressively declines with appropriate supportive management. A secondary biochemical rise after initial improvement is uncommon and may reflect ongoing skeletal muscle injury.Case PresentationA 21-year-old previously healthy man presented with severe generalized myalgia, dark-colored urine, and progressive oliguria progressing to anuria following a prolonged trekking expedition. Initial investigations revealed severe rhabdomyolysis with a CK of 18,500 U/L, dialysis-requiring AKI (serum creatinine 9.0 mg/dL), hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, metabolic acidosis, and myoglobinuria. Intermittent hemodialysis was initiated because of severe AKI with persistent anuria and metabolic complications. Serial biochemical monitoring initially demonstrated improvement; however, on the fourth hospital day, an unexpected secondary rise in CK (14,900-22,600 U/L) occurred, accompanied by recurrent hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, worsening metabolic acidosis, and increased AST and LDH, despite ongoing renal replacement therapy. This biphasic biochemical pattern was considered suggestive of delayed or "second-wave" skeletal muscle injury. The patient received a total of 5 hemodialysis sessions with continued supportive care, following which urine output progressively improved, biochemical abnormalities resolved, and renal function recovered completely.ConclusionThis case highlights a rare biphasic biochemical pattern in severe exertional rhabdomyolysis, characterized by a secondary surge in muscle injury markers and metabolic abnormalities after initial improvement. Recognition of this potential "second-wave" phenomenon emphasizes the importance of continued serial CK and biochemical monitoring in patients with severe rhabdomyolysis.

articles.title: Electrolyte and acid-base disturbances in acute kidney injury in a tropical tertiary care centre: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Electrolyte and acid-base disturbances in acute kidney injury are important indicators related to in-hospital mortality in a low-resource tertiary care setting. This deserved a prospective observational study.

articles.title: Quality and patient-safety content of Instagram videos on ophthalmic emergencies: A cross-sectional content analysis.
articles.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the quality, reliability, and safety-related content of Instagram videos on common ophthalmic emergencies.MethodsThis cross-sectional content analysis included 175 publicly available English-language Instagram videos across eight ophthalmic emergency topics. Two ophthalmologists independently assessed videos using the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) Benchmark Criteria, Global Quality Score (GQS), and a study-specific exploratory Eye Safety Score (ESS). Misinformation, harmful advice, emergency referral guidance, red-flag information, creator type, and engagement were recorded. Adjusted ordinal regression evaluated associations between engagement and ESS while accounting for topic, creator category, and repeated creators.ResultsMean JAMA, GQS, and ESS values were 2.55 ± 0.52, 2.96 ± 0.77, and 3.07 ± 1.18. Misinformation occurred in 10.9% of videos, harmful advice in 9.7%, emergency referral guidance in 64.0%, and red-flag information in 63.4%. Ophthalmologist-authored videos had higher reliability and quality scores and no detected misinformation in this sample. Views and likes showed weak inverse correlations with ESS; adjusted associations remained significant (views: adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.47, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.29-0.75; likes: aOR = 0.38, 95% CI 0.22-0.66).ConclusionIn this cross-sectional sample of English-language Instagram videos on ophthalmic emergencies, safety-related omissions were common. Higher engagement was associated with lower ESS, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Hyperammonemia in cats with acute (on chronic) kidney disease: associations with urea cycle amino acids, azotemia and acid-base status.
articles.journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery
articles.abstract: ObjectivesHyperammonemia occurs in cats with kidney disease although the pathophysiology is poorly understood. The objective of this study was to determine if hyperammonemia in cats with kidney disease is associated with decreased concentrations of plasma amino acids involved in the urea cycle and more severe acid-base derangements.MethodsTwenty cats presenting with acute kidney injury (AKI) and acute on chronic kidney disease (AoCKD) were prospectively enrolled. Fasting blood samples were analyzed for ammonia, pH, anion gap, electrolytes, lactate, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine and phosphorus. Plasma was frozen at -80oC and shipped for amino acid analysis.ResultsFive of 20 cats had an AKI and 15/20 had AoCKD. Median age and weight were 12 years (range 3-14) and 4.5 kg (range 3-5.6), respectively. Seven cats were hyperammonemic (median 252 µmol/l, range 113-886) and 13 were not (median 23 µmol/l, range 11-49). Creatinine, BUN and phosphorus were significantly higher in hyperammonemic cats. BUN and phosphorus correlated with ammonia. Fifteen of 20 cats (75%) were acidotic but there was no difference in lactate or blood and urine pH between the cats with and without hyperammonemia. The anion gap was higher (29.6, range 27-40 vs 25.1, range 11-34) and serum bicarbonate lower (9 mEq/L, range 4.8-13.5 vs 11.9, range 8-24.2) in hyperammonemic cats. Median plasma citrulline (47 nMol/mL, range 31-128 vs 22, range 12-37) and ornithine (20 nMol/mL, range 12-33 vs 10, range 7-35) but not arginine concentrations were significantly higher in hyperammonemic cats (p<0.05). Plasma citrulline concentrations were positively correlated with serum creatinine (r = 0.621, p = 0.003).Conclusions and relevanceHyperammonemic cats with AKI/AoCKD do not have deficiencies in urea cycle amino acid concentrations but do have more severe azotemia with accompanying high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Increases in citrulline may reflect decreased kidney function.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Feline granulocytic anaplasmosis in Europe: anamnesis, clinicopathological abnormalities, bacterial DNA load, treatment, and outcome.
articles.journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery
articles.abstract: Feline granulocytic anaplasmosis (FGA) is caused by Anaplasma (A.) phagocytophilum. Fever and thrombocytopenia are the most common clinicopathological abnormalities.ObjectivesThe aim was to investigate regionality, seasonality, clinicopathological parameters, treatment, and outcomes in cats with FGA.MethodsThe database of a commercial laboratory was retrospectively screened for A. phagocytophilum-polymerase chain (PCR)-results on EDTA-blood submitted by European veterinarians from 01/2022 to 12/2025. Hematological data and bacterial DNA loads quantified by digital droplet-PCR were analyzed. Questionnaires were sent to the veterinarians asking for underlying diseases, anamnesis, clinicopathological abnormalities, treatment, and outcome in cats with FGA.Results43/702 cats (6.1%) tested positive by A. phagocytophilum-PCR in Europe. Questionnaires were available for 29/43 cats (67.4%), all of which had outdoor access. Lethargy (23/29; 79.3%), anorexia (22/29, 75.9%), and fever (>39.5°C, 18/29, 62.0%) were the most reported findings. Thrombocytopenia was detected in 14/18 cats (77.8%) without concurrent diseases, anemia and leukopenia in 2/20 cats each (10.0%), eosinopenia in 10/17 (58.8%), and lymphopenia in 8/17 cats (47.1%). The bacterial DNA load was available for 27/43 cats (25 x 102-87 x 106, median 124 x 105/ml EDTA-blood), revealing no significant correlation with hematological parameters. 20/21 cats (95.2%) were treated with doxycycline and one (4.8%) with enrofloxacin. Uncomplicated course of disease was reported in 19/21 cats (90.5%). In one cat treated with doxycycline for 10 days, another positive PCR was recorded one month later. Clinical signs recurred immediately in another cat treated with doxycycline for five days only.Conclusions and relevanceFGA should be considered in cats with outdoor access, lethargy, inappetence, and most often mild thrombocytopenia and/or anemia, regardless of fever. Infected cats usually responded well to doxycycline with individual relapses if treated for 10 days or shorter. Treatment for 14 days to clear the infection, and PCR monitoring after finishing treatment are recommended.

articles.title: The Hna Phage Defence Protein: A DNA-Stimulated Helicase With Cryptic Nuclease Activity.
articles.abstract: The Hna phage defence system consists of a single protein containing helicase and nuclease motifs. Hna provides defence through abortive infection, meaning that it prevents production of new phages without saving the infected cell, but its specific mechanism of action is currently unknown. We previously observed that Hna causes cell death when phage 5A single-stranded DNA binding protein (SSB) is expressed in Sinorhizobium meliloti. Here, we recreated this response by expressing Hna and phage SSB in the heterologous host Escherichia coli, indicating that no other host-specific proteins are required for Hna-mediated cell death. We also find that increased expression of Hna is lethal in E. coli even in the absence of phage SSB. We tagged and purified the Hna protein from S. meliloti, as well as helicase and nuclease motif mutants, and show that wildtype Hna binds ssDNA, performs DNA-stimulated ATP hydrolysis and unwinds short DNA duplexes. The nuclease mutant exhibits increased DNA-dependent stimulation of ATPase activity. Hna demonstrates cryptic nuclease activity: we do not observe nuclease activity in vivo, but the purified protein showed inefficient degradation of phage and bacterial genomic DNA and a ssDNA oligonucleotide in vitro. Further research should elucidate how these activities contribute to cell death.

articles.title: Double Scaffold of Retirement on Subsequent Health: Revisiting Spatio-Temporality and Finance Through the Feature-Wide Effect Heterogeneity.
articles.abstract: This study investigates how retirement's effect on subsequent health varies by individual attributes and their interaction. Instead of spotlighting heterogeneity for a specific, theoretically predetermined feature, I consider the feature-wide effect heterogeneity to find possible data-driven candidates that generate this heterogeneity. To accomplish this, I use causal forests and harmonized data from the Gateway to Global Aging Data (the Gateway). The results show that temporal dimensions (such as age and birth cohort) and financial dimensions (such as income and wealth) are the most important features in heterogenizing retirement's effect on health. Based on these findings, I suggest the "double scaffold" model to comprehensively explain feature-wide effect heterogeneity.

articles.title: When red eyes signal glomerular disease: IgA nephropathy presenting as recurrent episcleritis and scleritis.
articles.abstract: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a primary chronic glomerulopathy that can rarely present with extrarenal ocular manifestations. We describe three patients presenting with chronic, anterior ocular inflammation two with recurrent episcleritis and one with scleritis that significantly preceded the renal diagnosis. Subsequent baseline urinalysis unmasked active urinary sediment with microscopic dysmorphic hematuria and marked proteinuria (2.0-4.0 g/day), with renal impairment in two patients. Histopathological evaluation via renal biopsy confirmed IgAN in all cases, including one with crescent formation. Following systemic immunosuppressive therapy and optimized supportive care, all patients achieved complete resolution of ocular inflammation and significant renal recovery, with marked reductions in proteinuria. These cases underline the clinical association between recurrent episcleritis/scleritis and underlying IgAN. Incorporating simple, cost-effective urine dipstick screening into the routine workup of inflammatory eye disease is crucial for prompt diagnosis and preventing progression to chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: The largest staghorn calculus reported to date, treated by nephron-preserving anatrophic nephrolithotomy.
articles.abstract: Staghorn calculi occupying the renal pelvis and extending into multiple calyces are associated with infection, progressive renal impairment and eventual loss of renal function if left untreated. Percutaneous nephrolithotomy remains the standard treatment for most staghorn calculi. However, exceptionally large complete staghorn calculi may require multiple access tracts, staged procedures or combined approaches. The largest kidney stone listed by Guinness World Records measures 13.37 cm. We report the complete staghorn calculus to be 13.8 cm on definitive ex vivo assessment, which, to our knowledge, represents the largest staghorn calculus reported to date.

articles.title: Retrospective Chart Review Indicates Earlier Age of Endometrial Cancer Diagnosis and Elevated Housing and Transportation Vulnerability in Hispanic and Native American Populations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2025, Endometrial cancer (EC) is the 6th most common cancer in women globally, with rising cases in younger patients and communities of color. EC risk factors include postmenopausal status, family history, diabetes, and hyperestrogenic state conditions.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed charts of patients who received hysterectomies or hysteroscopies for either cancerous and/or benign diagnoses between 2016 and 2021 at a university hospital in Phoenix (AZ). Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected. The Arizona Social Vulnerability Index was utilized to understand contributors to EC diagnosis outcomes. Kruskal-Wallis, Fisher's exact, and multinomial logistic regression tests were used to compare EC to benign conditions.

RESULTS: Two hundred sixty-one patients were diagnosed with benign conditions (n = 31), hyperplasia (n = 53), or EC (n = 168). EC patients were older (p = 0.016), mostly post-menopausal (p = 0.008), and more frequently had diabetes (p = 0.001) compared to patients with benign conditions. Native Americans had a higher percentage of EC cases relative to other races (p = 0.07) and presented with EC at significantly younger ages (49.79 years, p = 0.001) and with more comorbid diagnoses of diabetes (38.5%, p = 0.051) compared to Whites (61.99 years, 27.1%). Hispanic patients also presented with EC at younger ages (53.74,p = 0.006) compared to non-Hispanics (61.56 years). Higher vulnerability in Housing Type and Transportation scores (p = 0.045) among patients diagnosed with EC was observed.

CONCLUSION: Public health initiatives should target modifiable risk factors contributing to increased EC rates at younger ages, especially in Native American and Hispanic communities. Differences in housing and transportation highlight social structures and health accessibility as areas for improving EC outcomes.

articles.title: Sexuality and Glycosylated Hemoglobin Levels in Partnered Older Adults With Diabetes.
articles.abstract: We examined associations between sexual activity, sexual quality, and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels among partnered older adults with diabetes. Using longitudinal data from the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project, we studied 620 partnered respondents with diabetes aged 57 to 85 at baseline. We estimated mixed-effects models of sexual activity, frequency, and quality on HbA1c trajectories over ten years, including tests for gender differences. Results indicated that being sexually active and having sex a few times a month were associated with more favorable HbA1c trajectories compared to being sexually inactive. Emotional satisfaction was associated with worsening HbA1c trajectories for women but stable trajectories for men. Physical pleasure showed no gender differences. The findings suggest that partnered sexuality is a meaningful, gendered aspect of older adults' metabolic health that deserves greater attention as a dimension of diabetes care in later life.

articles.title: Supportive Environmental Design for Post-stroke Rehabilitation: A Participatory Concept Mapping Study.
articles.abstract: PurposeTo explore home and neighborhood environment aspects that support post-stroke rehabilitation.BackgroundThe design of healthcare environments influences rehabilitation outcomes, however, evidence for outpatient contexts, particularly the home and neighborhood remain limited.MethodWe used descriptive statistics and cluster analysis to explore stakeholders' perspectives on environmental factors that support rehabilitation and to identify patterns in how environmental features were organized and rated.ResultsSeveral home and nearby environmental features were clustered around engagement in rehabilitation and participation in everyday activities. Patterns suggested that accessibility, proximity to routine services, and opportunities for social contact tended to co-occur with higher perceived support for rehabilitation.ConclusionsThe immediate environment appears to play a role in community-based recovery after stroke, with design, social context, and care processes intertwined. The findings highlight that many feasible actions such as strengthening communication, ensuring adaptive home environments, and improving neighborhood accessibility can help align housing and local planning with everyday rehabilitation after stroke. While recognizing the exploratory nature of the findings, architectural planners and healthcare practitioners could draw on these insights to inform housing planning and more inclusive environments.

articles.title: From Surviving to Thriving: ACS Survivors' Experiences in Lifestyle Transformation to Prevent Recurrence-A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract: The recurrence of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) can be reduced through healthy lifestyle modification; however, many survivors struggle to sustain behavioral changes after hospital discharge. Previous studies have primarily focused on biomedical and behavioral outcomes, with limited attention to the psychosocial, emotional, and cultural processes involved in long-term recovery. This study explored the lived experiences of ACS survivors as they adapted to lifestyle changes within their social and cultural contexts. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 15 ACS survivors between three months and one year after the cardiac event and analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Three interconnected themes emerged: (1) creating new habits, (2) reconciling with the situation, and (3) the dual role of family. Lifestyle modification was experienced as a continuous struggle involving deeply rooted habits, emotional dependence, declining motivation, and the process of self-acceptance in seeking inner peace. Some participants gradually developed self-regulation and adaptive coping strategies, whereas others remained trapped in smoking behaviors, emotional distress, and hopelessness. Participants perceived psychosocial support from healthcare professionals as limited and expressed a need for greater emotional reassurance and coping assistance. Psychospiritual adaptation was shaped by the Javanese values of nrimo and ikhlas. These values helped participants accept physical limitations, reduce fear, and reconstruct meaning after illness. Family relationships served both as sources of support and stress, while patriarchal family dynamics sometimes hindered open communication. These findings suggest that recovery after ACS involves identity reconstruction, emotional regulation, and culturally embedded coping processes that extend beyond medical adherence alone.

articles.title: The Mediating Role of Self-Efficacy in the Relationship Between Knowledge and Palliative Care Practices Among ICU Nurses in Timor-Leste: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to palliative care remains limited in low- and middle-income countries, including Timor-Leste, where healthcare systems face structural and resource constraints. In intensive care units (ICUs), nurses play a critical role in delivering PC. However, the translation of knowledge into clinical practice remains inconsistent. Self-efficacy has been proposed as a key psychological mechanism that may bridge this gap.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to examine the mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between knowledge and palliative care practices among ICU nurses in Timor-Leste.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 107 ICU nurses. Data were collected using convenience sampling with validated instruments: the Palliative Care Knowledge Test (PCKT), the Self-Efficacy in Palliative Care Scale (PCSE-S), and the Palliative Care Self-Reported Practices Scale (PCPS). Rasch analysis was applied to transform ordinal data into interval-level measures. Pearson correlation and regression-based mediation analyses were performed using Jamovi.

RESULTS: A total of 107 ICU nurses participated in this study. The mean Rasch person measures were 0.515 (SD = 0.985) for palliative care practice, 0.136 (SD = 1.210) for self-efficacy, and -2.623 (SD = 0.973) for knowledge. Knowledge was significantly associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.316, p < 0.001), while self-efficacy was significantly associated with palliative care practice (β = 0.514, p < 0.001). In contrast, knowledge was not directly associated with palliative care practice (β = 0.0002, p = 0.998). Mediation analysis using bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals demonstrated a significant indirect effect of knowledge on palliative care practice through self-efficacy (β = 0.163, p = 0.003, 95% BC CI [0.0548, 0.365]), indicating that self-efficacy significantly mediated the relationship between knowledge and palliative care practice.

CONCLUSION: Self-efficacy may represent an important pathway linking palliative care knowledge with practice among ICU nurses. Interventions may consider strengthening both palliative care knowledge and self-efficacy, particularly in resource-limited ICU settings.

IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING: Nursing education and clinical practice should incorporate strategies that strengthen nurses' self-efficacy alongside palliative care knowledge. Practice-based training, simulation, clinical mentoring, and supportive supervision may help nurses apply their knowledge more confidently in palliative care delivery, particularly in resource-limited ICU settings.

articles.title: Reactivity of Rh(I) Complexes Toward Fluorinated Ethers: Activation of Inhalation Anesthetics.
articles.abstract: The reactivity of [Rh(H)(PEt3)3] (1) toward α-fluorinated ethers that are commonly used as inhalational anesthetics was studied. Unprecedented reactivity pathways include hydrodehalogenation of sp3 C─F and C─Cl bonds under mild conditions. The reaction of 1 with sevoflurane (CF3)2CHOCH2F provides an efficient route to obtain [Rh(F)(PEt3)3] (2) by C(sp3)─F bond activation. Furthermore, the phosphine ligand takes part in this reaction, and an F/Et exchange at [Rh(H)(F)2(PEt3)3] results in the formation of the fluorophosphine complex trans-[Rh(F)(Et2PF)(PEt3)2] (5) upon the release of ethane. On the other hand, an oxidative addition of enflurane CClFHCF2OCF2H at 1 yielded [Rh(H)(Cl)(CFHCF2OCF2H)(PEt3)3] (8), which is followed by a reductive elimination step to yield [Rh(Cl)(PEt3)3] (7) and the hydrofluoroether CFH2CF2OCF2H. When an isomer of enflurane, isoflurane CF3CClHOCF2H, was treated with 1, complex 7 and CF3CH2OCF2H are generated by C(sp3)─Cl bond activation. Additionally, an in situ nucleophilic attack of triethylphosphine at the hydrofluoroether CF3CH2OCF2H gave a unique fluorinated phosphonium salt [CF3CH2PEt3]2[SiF6] (9). Catalytic hydrodechlorination of isoflurane at a mild condition was achieved in the presence of silane HSiPh3 using 1 as a catalyst.

articles.title: Predictors of Success Outcomes in Nurse-Led Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy for Nephrolithiasis: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To identify clinical, anatomical, and technical predictors associated with successful extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) outcomes in patients with nephrolithiasis undergoing nurse-led ESWL treatment.

DESIGN: Prospective descriptive observational study.

METHODS: A total of 461 ESWL treatments for nephrolithiasis performed between November 2016 and June 2024 at St. Olav's University Hospital, a tertiary university hospital in Trondheim, were analysed. A consecutive sampling strategy was used to minimize selection bias. Data on stone characteristics (size, density, and anatomical location) and treatment-related parameters were extracted from patient records. These variables were selected based on recommendations from the European Association of Urology. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of treatment success (defined as stone-free or residual fragments ≤ 4 mm).

RESULTS: Three variables were associated with treatment success: stone laterality, size and density. Right-sided stones were more likely to be successfully treated (OR 1.77, p = 0.004), while larger and denser stones were less likely to achieve complete clearance (OR 0.91, p = 0.003 and OR 0.99, p = 0.012 respectively). The overall success rate was comparable to outcomes reported for urologist-led procedures.

CONCLUSION: ESWL performed by trained nurses seems to be safe and effective. Findings support an expanded nursing role in advanced urological procedures and provide knowledge that can improve patient selection and resource utilization.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurse-led ESWL appears to achieve success rates comparable to physician-led models when delivered by appropriately trained nurses.

IMPACT: This study adds evidence for task shifting in specialized healthcare settings and demonstrates that nurses can deliver high-quality treatment. The findings have implications for competence development, patient access, and efficient use of urological resources.

REPORTING METHOD: STROBE.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION REPORTING METHOD: No Patient or Public Contribution.

articles.title: Beyond lung function: the changing landscape of cystic fibrosis-related diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society

articles.title: Corrigendum to "CPAP adherence and depressive symptoms in post-stroke/TIA patients with OSA" [Sleep Med 148, (2026), 109286].
Electrodiagnostic Classification of Sensory Neuropathies: Severity Clusters and Clinical Correlates.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Grading sensory neuropathy severity on nerve conduction studies (NCS) is operator dependent, which limits comparisons across patients, laboratories, and studies. We aimed to develop an objective severity classification to standardize NCS reporting and support clinical decision-making.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed NCS performed at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital (2018-2024), extracted with a validated parser. Adult studies with sensory involvement were selected using sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude thresholds after excluding motor abnormalities. Hierarchical clustering combined normalized sural and "best" upper-limb (UL) SNAP amplitudes with binary indicators for absent responses. Classes were ordered by an NCS severity index and validated against clinical scales.

RESULTS: Among 15,744 consecutive examinations, 308 met inclusion criteria. Three well-separated NCS severity classes emerged: mild (reduced but present sural and present UL SNAPs), moderate (absent sural, present UL SNAPs), and severe (absent sural and UL SNAPs). Clinical severity increased monotonically across classes. Patients in the severe class had younger age at symptom onset than those in mild-moderate classes and were more disabled (modified Rankin scale ≥ 2: 50.0% in severe vs 30.4% in moderate vs 16.2% in mild). The severe class was enriched in immune/paraneoplastic (12.5%) and genetic (40.6%) causes.

DISCUSSION: By stratifying patients based on SNAP amplitudes, we identified a differential etiologic enrichment rather than a continuum of disease progression. Severe electrophysiology with motor sparing should prompt RFC1 testing and immune/paraneoplastic work-up, whereas mild to moderate abnormalities should lead to assessment for diabetes and toxic or nutritional exposures.

articles.title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included.

EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores.

RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Childhood Adversity and Self-Reported Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Structural Equation Modeling Analysis of the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to examine the association between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and self-reported rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and to investigate potential psychosocial and behavioural mediators of this relationship.

METHODS: Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses (EFA; CFA) were conducted to assess the dimensionality of ACEs. Hypothesized direct and indirect pathways from a latent ACEs construct to RA were tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) with data (N = 44,142) from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging. Putative mediation through depression, anxiety, obesity, and smoking was examined. Analyses adjusted for sociodemographic factors, asthma, and childhood passive smoking. Moderation by birth sex was tested with multigroup SEM.

RESULTS: EFA and CFA supported a higher-order latent childhood adversity factor with three first-order factors (physical abuse, sexual abuse, household dysfunction). SEM showed a small but significant direct ACEs-RA association, as well as significant associations operating through depression, obesity, and smoking. Birth sex appeared to moderate the indirect pathway through obesity, with a stronger association for men. An indirect association through smoking was observed only in men, though the between-group difference was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: ACEs were significantly associated with self-reported RA, partially through indirect pathways involving depression, obesity, and smoking, with evidence of sex-specific effects on the obesity pathway. Targeted screening and intervention for ACEs-affected individuals with psychosocial and behavioural risk factors may help reduce RA burden. Prospective mediation research examining gene-environment interactions (e.g., smoking × RA risk alleles) and sex-specific mechanisms is warranted.

articles.title: Prevalence of Diabetes in Low- and Middle-Income Countries' Incarcerated Populations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major global health concern, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Incarcerated populations in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face increased health risks and limited care access, yet remain understudied. No prior systematic review has synthesized prevalence data for this group. This review aims to estimate diabetes prevalence among incarcerated individuals in LMICs.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis per PRISMA and GATHER guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science and regional databases were searched till May 2025. Random-effects models with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation were applied in R (version 4.5.1). Publication bias was assessed using DOI plots. Study quality was evaluated with the Joanna Briggs Institute tool, and certainty of evidence was appraised using an adapted GRADE approach.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (107,473 participants) were included. Mean participant ages varied from 29 ± 9.6 to 40.5 ± 9.8 years. The tentative pooled estimate of diabetes prevalence was 3.7% (95% CI: [2.5%-5.1%], Prediction Interval [0%-12.2%]), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). The pooled prevalence estimate was highest in Asia (5.2%), particularly Pakistan (9.8%), and lowest in South America (2.3%). The DOI plot revealed major asymmetry, indicating a high possibility of publication bias. Overall certainty of evidence was rated as very low for diabetes prevalence due to risk of bias and publication bias.
