Interpretation of the pooled estimate is limited by substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the primary studies, including differences in diabetes ascertainment methods.

CONCLUSION: Diabetes is an important health concern among incarcerated populations in LMICs. Differences in diabetes ascertainment methods, participant characteristics and correctional healthcare systems may have potentially contributed to the variability of the pooled estimates. A hypothesis is that there may also be potentially limited detection or underdiagnosis which possibly could have contributed to the observed prevalence estimates.

articles.title: Severe Infection Outcomes With SGLT2 Versus DPP-4 Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Active-Comparator Meta-Analysis of Real-World Cohorts.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To update and methodologically refine the synthesis of real-world evidence on severe infection outcomes with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i), emphasising limits of causal interpretation.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 29 June 2026. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to DPP-4i active-comparator estimates. Incident pneumonia and sepsis were prespecified co-primary outcomes. Hazard ratios and incidence rate ratios were pooled as related but non-identical estimands using restricted maximum likelihood with modified Hartung-Knapp inference, with leave-one-out, prediction-interval and effect-measure-stratified analyses. ROBINS-I and GRADE were applied.

RESULTS: Eighteen cohorts were included; the 11 contributing quantitatively were all at moderate risk of bias. For incident pneumonia (five studies), the pooled ratio was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.55-0.75; prediction interval 0.45-0.93; I2 = 89.8%; very low certainty); omitting one multinational cohort whose follow-up began 2 years after drug initiation yielded 0.61 (0.56-0.67; I2 = 0%). For incident sepsis (five studies), the prediction interval crossed the null (0.38-1.13); the exploratory pooled ratio was 0.65 (0.53-0.80; I2 = 90.6%, and 88.1%-92.4% after every omission; very low certainty). Hazard-ratio-only point estimates were similar, although the sepsis estimate was imprecise (95% CI including 1.0). Two cohorts reported identical, unpooled estimates for infection-related hospitalisation (0.74 each; low certainty). Comparisons with GLP-1 receptor agonists did not show a consistent lower-risk pattern across four cohorts, two in selected populations, and randomised-trial syntheses have not shown a consistent class-wide preventive effect.

CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence did not suggest an increased average risk of severe infection with SGLT2i compared with DPP-4i. Given low to very low certainty and substantial heterogeneity, the lower pooled estimates should not be interpreted as a preventive effect.

REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420261390509.

articles.title: Framings of Patient Knowledge and Proximal Technologies in Type 1 Diabetes: A Hermeneutic Review Using Meta-Narrative Methods.
articles.abstract: Some people living with type 1 diabetes (T1D) wear glucose sensors and pumps which use algorithms to deliver insulin automatically. These technologies require practical knowledge, yet how patients develop this knowledge remains undertheorised. We conducted a hermeneutic review, informed by meta-narrative methods, to examine how different research traditions have conceptualised patient knowledge concerning T1D proximal or wearable technologies. Using databases and snowball searches, we classified 74 articles into four research traditions, each carrying assumptions about how patients acquire, develop or enact knowledge. In biomedical literature, patients were typically seen as passive recipients of technology, with knowledge framed as factual or skills-based. Health psychology literature emphasised individual empowerment through mastery of technical skills. Design and innovation studies treated patient knowledge as an instrument for design. Social science-informed approaches focused on knowledge as a social process distributed between patients through communities of practice or centred on enacting embodied and situated knowledge. Our review shows how narrow framings risk undermining the richness of T1D knowledge practices with implications for technology development and implementation in the context of diabetes care. We argue for stronger engagement with sociologically informed approaches in future research to attend to the multiplicity of knowledge practices.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Saroglitazar and Dapagliflozin on Hepatic Steatosis and Glycemic Control in Patients With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A 25-Week Prospective Multicenter Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the leading cause of chronic liver disease globally, driven by rising obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Existing medications provide minimal fibrosis regression, highlighting the need for comparative evidence on agents with metabolic and hepatic benefits. This study compared the efficacy and safety of saroglitazar 4 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg in patients with MASLD.

METHODS: This 25-week, prospective, multicentre, open-label active-controlled comparative cohort study enrolled adults aged 18-70 years with MASLD confirmed by FibroScan (steatosis grade S3, controlled attenuation parameter [CAP] ≥ 292 dB/m, and/or fibrosis stage ≥F2, liver stiffness measurement [LSM] ≥ 8.0 kPa). Participants received saroglitazar (n = 27) or dapagliflozin (n = 27) once daily, added to standard of care per physician discretion. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in hepatic steatosis (CAP) and fibrosis (LSM); secondary endpoints included HbA1c, hepatic enzymes, lipid profile, and adverse events.

RESULTS: All 54 participants completed follow-up. CAP decreased from 314.7 to 278.7 dB/m with saroglitazar and from 310.2 to 287.0 dB/m with dapagliflozin (between-group p = 0.44). LSM decreased in both arms (saroglitazar -0.96 kPa; dapagliflozin -0.46 kPa; between-group p = 0.80). HbA1c improved in both groups (saroglitazar 8.28%-6.76%; dapagliflozin 8.14%-7.30%), with a significantly greater reduction with saroglitazar (between-group p = 0.04). ALT and AST declined similarly in both arms despite higher baseline ALT with saroglitazar. Triglycerides decreased significantly within both groups (saroglitazar -62.5 mg/dL; dapagliflozin -28.3 mg/dL), with no significant between-group difference. No treatment-emergent adverse events, including edema, occurred in either group.

CONCLUSIONS: Both saroglitazar and dapagliflozin improved hepatic steatosis, fibrosis markers, liver enzymes, and glycemic control over 25 weeks, with comparable hepatic benefit. Saroglitazar produced a significantly greater reduction in HbA1c, suggesting a possible glycemic-preferential advantage in patients requiring simultaneous glycemic and hepatic control; larger randomized trials are needed to confirm any differential hepatic efficacy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry of India, CTRI/2024/08/071848.

articles.title: Ultrasound as a Multifunctional Physical Platform for Whole-Grape Valorization: From Field Management to Green Extraction, Quality Modulation, and Intelligent Scale-Up.
articles.journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety
articles.abstract: The grape and wine industry faces prolonged barrel aging, microbial spoilage, protein haze, chemical additives, and inefficient by-product valorization. These challenges motivate nonthermal technologies that reduce chemical inputs. Ultrasound operates in two mechanistically distinct regimes: sensing, based on acoustic propagation, reflection, and echo detection, and processing, driven mainly by acoustic cavitation and its physical and chemical effects, including microjets, shock waves, localized hotspots, and reactive radicals. These complementary modes provide a versatile physical platform. This review covers ultrasound across the grape-wine continuum: acoustic imaging for precision viticulture; postharvest preservation with green activated water; green extraction enhanced by natural deep eutectic solvents; grape protein modification for ingredient assembly; modulation of wine color, aroma, and colloidal stability; selected aging-associated reactions involving 1-hydroxyethyl radicals; selective microbial inactivation and fermentation modulation; and scale-up based on energy characterization, continuous-flow reactors, and data-driven modeling. Current evidence indicates that ultrasound is evolving from an empirically optimized unit operation toward a mechanistically informed and quantitatively characterized physical-field platform. Reported effects include accelerated aging-related transformations, modified protein structure and stability, and selective microbial responses, although they depend on treatment conditions and matrix properties. Absorbed energy density supports quantitative comparison of treatments, but reliable scale-up also requires acoustic-field distribution, residence time, temperature, and reactor geometry. Future progress will require standardized energy reporting, pilot- and continuous-flow validation, physics-informed data-driven modeling, and integration of process analytical technologies with closed-loop control. These advances would support more reproducible, scalable, and sustainable ultrasound processing in the grape and wine sector.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Fitness Methods on Depressive Symptoms and Glycaemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Comorbid Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Taijiquan and Baduanjin.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the overall effectiveness of traditional Chinese fitness methods (TCFMs)-specifically Taijiquan and Baduanjin-on depressive symptoms and glycaemic control in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and comorbid depression.

METHODS: RCTs evaluating the effectiveness of TCFMs were identified through 10 major English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, ProQuest, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by intervention duration, frequency, and sample size.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs of Taijiquan and Baduanjin were included. All studies were conducted in China, and most had small sample sizes. Most had a high risk of bias, mainly due to a lack of blinding of participants and personnel. TCFMs were associated with significant improvements in depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.39, 95% CI [-2.22, -0.57], p = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed for HbA1c (MD = -0.82, 95% CI [-1.18, -0.45], p < 0.0001) and FPG (MD = -0.70, 95% CI [-0.97, -0.42], p < 0.00001). The effect on 2hPBG remains inconclusive owing to limited studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant effect modifiers for depressive symptoms or HbA1c (all interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings, though heterogeneity decreased substantially after excluding high-risk studies.

CONCLUSIONS: This review provides preliminary evidence that TCFMs may confer benefits on mental health and glycaemic regulation in patients with T2DM and comorbid depression. However, given the low certainty of the evidence, high heterogeneity, and methodological limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The conclusions are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, rigorously designed studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The protocol of this systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261287519).

articles.title: Exploring the Therapeutic Potential of Metformin and Vitamin D3 Combination in the Management of Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterised by hyperglycaemia, dyslipidaemia, hepatic dysfunction, and loss of pancreatic β-cells. Vitamin D3 (D3) may influence glucose and lipid metabolism and has been investigated for its potential complementary effects when administered with metformin (MT). In the present study, the anti-diabetic activity of D3 alone and when combined with MT was evaluated in Streptozotocin (STZ) induced diabetic mice.

METHODS: Swiss albino mice were made diabetic using STZ (45 mg/kg) injected intraperitoneally for 3 days. Diabetic mice were treated with MT (250 mg/kg), D3 (100 μg/kg), or MT + D3 for 21 days. The fasting blood glucose, serum lipid profile, body weight, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and pancreatic histopathology were assessed. The data were analysed by ANOVA and Tukey's post hoc test, and a p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: The diabetic STZ mice showed sustained hyperglycaemia, weight loss, dyslipidaemia, increased ALT activity and degeneration of the islets of Langerhans. MT and D3 treatments were associated with improvements in glycaemic control, and the combination treatment showed the greatest effect. Combined treatment was found to lower the level of total cholesterol (93.06 ± 2.89 mg/dL), LDL (28.66 mg/dL), triglycerides (120.33 ± 2.10 mg/dL) and ALT activity (52.60 ± 3.05 IU/L) and increase HDL (40.33 ± 2.10 mg/dL) when compared with diabetic controls. Moreover, the MT + D3 group exhibited significant changes in the total cholesterol/HDL and LDL/HDL ratio and preserved the histoarchitecture of the pancreas.

CONCLUSION: Metformin and vitamin D3, administered individually or in combination, were associated with improvements in several diabetes-related metabolic parameters. The combination group showed greater observed metabolic outcomes than either treatment alone in STZ-induced diabetic mice. Further adequately powered preclinical and clinical studies are required to determine the therapeutic relevance of this combination.

articles.title: Clinical management of pyogenic liver abscess: a point-by-point synthesis of the available evidence and existing gaps.
articles.abstract: Pyogenic liver abscess (PLA) is an infectious disease characterized by increasing incidence and non-negligible mortality. Notwithstanding its impact, no international guideline on PLA management has been enacted. There exists a critical unmet need for in-depth mapping of the existing evidence and gaps,. In the present review, a list of eight practical questions on PLA management was established based on clinical significance, including radiological, medical, surgical and general considerations. Summary of these findings showed no evident cut-off size for antibiotics-only PLA treatment. Optimized antimicrobial treatment remains to be defined, as regards both antibiotic duration and whether and when to carry out an intravenous-to-oral switch. Among the proposed percutaneous treatments, drainage appeared superior to needle aspiration. Multiloculated PLA should be managed in the same way as uniloculated PLA. From a pragmatic standpoint, indications for surgery include concomitant surgical indications (e.g., appendicitis), PLA rupture or cavities not amenable to percutaneous drainage. While the role of follow-up imaging remains unclear, colonoscopy should be recommended following the diagnosis of cryptogenic PLA. Present-day management of PLA essentially relies on a low level of evidence. Our findings underscore a need to intensify and synergize relevant research, the objective being to update and optimize management of PLA patients.

articles.title: Reply to "Oxidative balance metabolite signatures in PREDIMED: interpreting the divergent cardiovascular and diabetes findings".
Prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction measured by cardiac magnetic resonance in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an important role in both the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), as it provides information on cardiac function, structure, and tissue characterization. Moreover, it is the gold standard for right ventricular (RV) assessment. However, evidence regarding the prognostic value of RV systolic dysfunction in this population remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) measured by CMR in patients with ATTR-CM. MéTODOS: This was a single-center, observational, retrospective cohort study. We included patients from an institutional ATTR-CM registry who underwent CMR within 6 months of diagnosis between 2011 and 2025. Patients with other types of amyloidosis were excluded. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CMR variables were collected. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed according to the presence or absence of RV dysfunction on CMR, defined as RVEF <50%. Univariate and multivariable Cox regression models were performed to identify predictors of the primary endpoint. TAPSE was not included in the multivariable models to avoid collinearity.

RESULTADOS: A total of 100 patients were included, with a median age of 79 years [IQR 73-84]; 84% were men. Median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% [IQR 42-62], and median RVEF was 48% [IQR 38-57]. Patients with lower RVEF had higher all-cause mortality (log-rank p = 0.008, Figure). In the multivariable model including age, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP, RVEF was independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98; p = 0.002, Table).

CONCLUSIONES: In our cohort of patients with ATTR-CM, RVEF assessed by CMR was independently associated with all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that RV assessment may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist and SGLT2 inhibitor use with outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes undergoing pacemaker implantation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure (HF) remains prevalent following pacemaker implantation, with patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) representing a particularly vulnerable population. Whether use of contemporary glucose-lowering therapies is associated with subsequent clinical outcomes has not been well characterized. We investigated the associations of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) therapy, individually and in combination, with post-implantation clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Electronic health records identified 3,609 patients with T2DM who underwent pacemaker implantation from 2016-2023. Based on peri-implantation medication dispensing, patients were classified as SGLT2i (n = 438), GLP-1RA (n = 193), combined therapy (n = 231), or neither (n = 2,747). Following a 90-day landmark period, three-year risks of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization were evaluated using multinomial propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Overall, 463 patients (12.8%) died. All treatment groups showed lower all-cause mortality than controls, with the greatest reduction observed in the combination therapy group (HR 0.41; 95% CI, 0.22-0.77; P = 0.006). HF hospitalization occurred in 295 patients (8.2%), significantly reduced in combination therapy (HR 0.35; 95% CI, 0.17-0.74; P = 0.006), with trends toward benefit in monotherapy groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with T2DM undergoing permanent pacemaker implantation, SGLT2i and GLP-1RA therapy were associated with lower all-cause mortality, while combined therapy was additionally associated with fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support further evaluation of cardiometabolic therapies after pacemaker implantation in randomized trials.

articles.title: National Trends, Disparities, and Inpatient Outcomes of Cardiac Amyloidosis Hospitalizations in the United States During the Era of Disease-Modifying Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tafamidis, approved in 2019, was the first disease-modifying therapy for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Disparities in cardiac amyloidosis outcomes remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize US trends in cardiac amyloidosis hospitalizations, subtypes, and risk-adjusted mortality from 2017 to 2022, including changes around tafamidis approval.

METHODS: We analyzed the 2017-2022 National Inpatient Sample, defining cases by an amyloidosis code (E85.x) paired with a heart failure or restrictive cardiomyopathy code. Survey-weighted regression assessed outcomes; Joinpoint and segmented regression tested for a 2019 trend inflection.

RESULTS: Of an estimated 111,450 hospitalizations, 83% were coded as Other/Unspecified amyloidosis. In-hospital mortality was 7.1%, highest in light-chain (AL) amyloidosis (9.4%) and lowest in wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (4.9%; adjusted odds ratio 0.48 vs AL). The age-standardized hospitalization rate nearly doubled, from 4.2 to 8.0 per 100,000 adults, with no inflection detected at 2019. Private and "Other" payer status were associated with higher adjusted mortality than Medicare, the mortality difference for uninsured patients increased over time, and Black patients had lower adjusted odds of pacemaker implantation. Black patients accounted for a larger share of hereditary ATTR admissions than of other subtypes in every year.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac amyloidosis hospitalizations rose steadily from 2017 to 2022, and no inflection was detected at the 2019 approval of tafamidis. Because the NIS lacks data on treatment exposure, diagnostic testing, and disease severity, these findings cannot establish whether tafamidis influenced hospitalization trends. Differences in in-hospital mortality by payer and in pacemaker implantation by race persisted and warrant investigation with patient-level clinical data.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of growth hormone against methylmalonic acid-mediated hippocampal damage in methylmalonic aciduria: implication of NRF2/HO-1 pathway.
articles.abstract: Methylmalonic aciduria is an inherited metabolic disease accompanied by hippocampal damage and neurological impairment. Growth hormone (GH) has been reported to play important roles in the nervous system, but its role and underlying mechanism in methylmalonic aciduria remains poorly understood. Here, a rat model of methylmalonic aciduria was established via subcutaneous injection of methylmalonic acid (MMA). GH treatment improved cognitive function and spatial memory and alleviated hippocampal neuronal damage in MMA rats. GH also reduced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in the hippocampal tissues, as evidenced by decreased levels of ROS and MDA, attenuated loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), and increased SOD, CAT, GSH and ATP. In addition, MMA-induced apoptosis, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction were prevented by GH treatment in PC12 cells. Notably, GH upregulated the expression of NRF2 and HO-1 in both MMA rats and MMA-treated PC12 cells. Rescue experiments further indicated that the protective effects of GH in PC12 cells might be mediated via the NRF2 pathway. In summary, our findings demonstrated that GH attenuates MMA-induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction through the NRF2/HO-1 pathway. This study highlights the potential mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of GH in methylmalonic aciduria.

articles.title: Positive-call rates and agreement of two artificial intelligence electrocardiogram models for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and cardiac amyloidosis in competitive athletes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) models detect hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and cardiac amyloidosis in clinical populations; whether two independently developed models agree in athletes is unknown.

METHODS: We applied two independently developed AI-ECG models to the screening electrocardiograms (ECGs) of 716 competitive athletes aged 40 years or younger, screened by ECG alone and presumed free of structural heart disease. The RST algorithms return per-condition probabilities dichotomized at published operating points; the AZ model, a four-class ECG-image classifier, assigns one class per ECG. The primary outcome was each model's positive-call rate (proportion of athletes flagged) for HCM and cardiac amyloidosis; agreement was described with Cohen kappa and positive agreement. Because the cohort was presumed disease-free, sensitivity was not assessed.

RESULTS: Median age was 22.1 years; 86.0% were men. The RST algorithms flagged HCM in 13 athletes (1.8%; 95% CI, 1.0-3.1) and cardiac amyloidosis in 2 (0.3%; 0.0-1.0); the AZ model flagged HCM in 29 (4.1%; 2.7-5.8) and cardiac amyloidosis in 18 (2.5%; 1.5-3.9). Of 60 athletes flagged by either model, 2 were flagged by both (kappa 0.07 and - 0.01; positive agreement 0.10 and 0.00); continuous outputs were uncorrelated for HCM (Spearman rho 0.00). Of 59 flagged athletes with a stored cardiologist interpretation under the international criteria, 39 had a normal ECG. All 18 AZ amyloidosis calls occurred in men.

CONCLUSIONS: The two models flagged different athletes at different rates. Without verified cases these rates describe referral burden, not accuracy; whether either detects disease requires validation against verified diagnoses.

articles.title: Updated Staging System to Define Cardiogenic Shock Severity A Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) severity is defined by the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stages and modifications from the Cardiogenic Shock Working Group (CSWG). Lactate thresholds, treatment intensity, and cardiac arrest modifiers remain incompletely defined. We aimed to refine the 2022 CSWG staging criteria using contemporary data.

METHODS: Patients with CS from heart failure (HF-CS) or myocardial infarction (MI-CS) enrolled in the multicenter CSWG registry (2021-2025) were analyzed. Associations between systolic blood pressure (SBP), lactate, treatment intensity, and in-hospital mortality, which is considered a surrogate for CS severity, were examined. External application of the updated system was performed in an independent U.S. health system.

RESULTS: Among 11,640 patients (60.5% HF-CS, 26.1% MI-CS), SBP and lactate demonstrated graded relationships with mortality across thresholds (SBP<60, 60-<90, ≥90 mmHg; lactate 0-2, >2-5, >5-10, >10 mmol/L). Mortality increased incrementally with treatment intensity. The 2026 staging system incorporating these thresholds and the number of vasoactive drugs and temporary mechanical circulatory support devices (stage C: 1-2, D: 3-4, E: ≥5) demonstrated progressive mortality across stages. Compared with prior CSWG staging, 28.4% of stage D and 56.4% of stage E patients were reclassified, with lower mortality among those reclassified to less severe stages. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest functioned best as a stage modifier, whereas in-hospital cardiac arrest corresponded to stage E. Findings were consistent across HF-CS and MI-CS. The 2026 CS staging system was evaluated in 1,417,637 patients in a geographically and structurally diverse healthcare system and demonstrated a graded, monotonic increase in mortality across stages A-E.

CONCLUSIONS: Using fewer clinical variables, the 2026 CSWG criteria provide a simple framework for CS severity staging that is applicable among HF-CS and MI-CS patients, and can be standardized across clinical trials and healthcare settings.

articles.title: Potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: Rationale and design of the STARS DAPT randomized pilot trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 12 months is the current standard of care for patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Recent evidence indicates that potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) after 1 to 3 months of DAPT following drug-eluting-stent (DES) implantation reduces major bleeding events without increasing the risk of major ischemic outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome. However, the optimal timing of aspirin discontinuation in STEMI patients treated with P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT remains uncertain.

DESIGN: STARS DAPT is an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, open-label, precision-based, randomized controlled pilot trial with a blinded outcome assessment. Patients with STEMI who underwent successful primary PCI of the culprit lesion with a newer-generation polymer-free DES will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT (with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge) for 12 months vs. standard DAPT for 12 months. The primary efficacy endpoint is the rate of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as the composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial re-infarction, non-fatal stroke, urgent target vessel revascularization, or definite/probable stent thrombosis, at 12 months. The primary safety endpoint is Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) class 3 or 5 major bleeding at 12 months. The study is designed to provide estimates of treatment effects and their precision to inform the design of a subsequent larger randomized trial.

ENROLMENT STATUS: The trial aims to recruit a total of 350 patients. The first patient was enrolled on December 1, 2025.

CONCLUSION: STARS DAPT is a randomized pilot study assessing the safety and efficacy of a potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT strategy, with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge, following primary PCI with a newer-generation polymer-free DES in patients with STEMI. The findings will inform future large-scale trial design and may help optimize antiplatelet strategies and guide clinical decision-making after primary PCI.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: Identifier, NCT05785897.

FUNDING SOURCE: Unrestricted research grant from Concept Medical (Tampa, FL, USA) to Geneva University Hospitals, Switzerland.

articles.title: Mechanistic Biomarker Responses in Human Bronchial Epithelial Air-Liquid Interface Cultures Following Exposure to Spray Cleaning Products.
articles.abstract: There are strong links between routine exposure to aerosolized cleaning products and epidemiologically observed adverse respiratory health outcomes, such as occupational asthma. However, because safety assessment relies largely on constituent-level information and mixture-classification rules, mechanistic data on the effects of complete cleaning formulations remain limited. In this study three commercially available all-purpose spray cleaners were investigated for early, localized cellular effects using an in vitro primary bronchial epithelial cells (PBEC) Air-Liquid Interface (ALI) model across three concentrations (10, 100, and 1000 ppm (v/v)). Transcriptional markers for oxidative stress, barrier integrity, and innate immunity were evaluated after 6hours of exposure, followed by protein quantification for IL-6, IL-8, MMP-9, and TIMP-1 at 18hours post-exposure period. Exposure to these three cleaning product formulations showed a persistent downregulation in GPX1 transcription across all products, indicating alterations in redox balance. Furthermore, one of the investigated formulations induced marked transcriptional changes in genes associated with epithelial barrier integrity (CDH1, CLDN1, CLDN4, and OCLN). Additionally, IL-8 secretion levels were significantly increased for all formulations. These findings demonstrated that these spray cleaners induce cellular responses in bronchial epithelial models in a formulation-dependent manner. By investigating distinct cellular pathways critical to integrity and their responses following chemical assault, these findings provide insights into the pathogenic processes of respiratory effects associated to cleaning-product-exposures.

articles.title: Self-augmenting procoagulant microspheres potentiate microvessel embolization and hypoxia-activated prodrug activation against hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) persists a cornerstone therapy for hypervascular tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet clinical limitations remain due to inefficient occlusion of tumor microvessels and hypoxia-induced drug resistance. Here, self-augmenting procoagulant microspheres (SPM) were developed for sustained co-delivery of thrombin (Th) and hypoxia-activated prodrug AQ4N (Th/AQ@SPM) to potentiate TACE therapy in HCC. SPM induced primary embolization by obstructing major tumor vasculature, affording vascular disruption and procoagulant factor exposure to establish a localized hypercoagulable microenvironment. Th-triggered secondary thrombosis through platelet aggregation and fibrinogen-to-fibrin conversion within residual vasculature extended occlusion to inter-microsphere spaces and distal microvessels beyond direct microsphere reach. Concurrently, hypoxia-potentiated activation of AQ4N to its cytotoxic form enabled targeted chemotherapy within the ischemic tumors. In rabbit renal and auricular artery models, Th@SPM demonstrated significant microvessel embolization through dual-phase vascular occlusion. Orthotopic VX2 liver tumor models revealed that TACE treatment with Th/AQ@SPM achieved superior tumor suppression without adverse toxic effects. Thus, Th/AQ@SPM establishes a self-augmenting embolic cascade that couples progressive microvascular occlusion with hypoxia-activated chemotherapy, providing a potent strategy to overcome key limitations of conventional TACE for HCC.

articles.title: Multidrug-Resistant Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Infections in Critically Ill and Immunocompromised Patients: Clinical Characteristics and Therapeutic Outcomes.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly among critically ill and immunocompromised patients. Data on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX)-resistant isolates remain limited globally and in Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary care center including adult patients with TMP-SMX-resistant S. maltophilia isolated from blood or respiratory specimens between May 2016 and April 2025. Demographic, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data were analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 949 blood or respiratory S. maltophilia isolates screened, 79 TMP-SMX-resistant cases were identified (8.3%). Respiratory specimens accounted for 89.9% of resistant isolates, while blood culture isolates represented 10.1%. True infections accounted for 36 cases (45.6%), while the remaining 43 cases (54.4%) were classified as colonization. TMP-SMX resistance increased from 3.4% of isolates in 2017 to approximately 10% in 2024, with a marked rise after 2020. Patients were predominantly older adults (median age 66 years), with frequent ICU exposure (84.8%) and significant comorbidities. Overall 30-day and 180-day mortality rates were 34.2% and 49.4%, respectively. Minocycline demonstrated the highest susceptibility (75%), whereas levofloxacin susceptibility was limited (33.3%). Combination therapy was associated with numerically higher survival compared with monotherapy at both 30 and 180 days, although these differences were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: TMP-SMX-resistant S. maltophilia isolates are increasingly identified during the study periord, particularly among critically ill patients, and are associated with substantial mortality. Combination therapy was associated with numerically higher survival, but differences were not statistically significant. Larger comparative studies are needed to determine whether combination therapy improves clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Pectin fine structure modulates the catalytic performance and regioselectivity of AA17 lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases from Phytophthora infestans.
articles.abstract: Lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs) catalyze the peroxidative cleavage of complex cell wall polysaccharides, yet how polysaccharide fine structure modulates their catalytic performance remains poorly understood. Here, we quantitatively investigate the catalytic performance of the recently established Auxiliary Activity family 17 (AA17) LPMOs using real-time electrochemical monitoring of H2O2 consumption. Two AA17 enzymes from the plant-pathogenic oomycete Phytophthora infestans, PiAA17C and PiAA17D, were analyzed on pectic homogalacturonan (HG) substrates differing in degrees (DM 0, 20, 60 and 92) and pattern of methyl-esterification. Both enzymes exhibited DM-dependent catalytic behavior on HG. Detailed characterization of PiAA17C identified moderately methyl-esterified HG (DM20) as providing the highest catalytic efficiency and operational stability, reflecting an optimal balance between turnover rate and hydrogen peroxide sensitivity. In addition, HG with randomly distributed methyl esters, characteristic of pathogenic pectin methylesterase (PME) activity, supported better catalytic performance than blockwise-esterified HG. Beyond HG, both enzymes were found to oxidatively cleave β-(1 → 4)-galactan side chains of rhamnogalacturonan I, identifying galactan as a previously unrecognized substrate class. In-depth product analysis revealed C1-oxidation on galactan, in contrast to the C4-oxidation observed on HG, demonstrating a substrate-dependent switch in oxidative regioselectivity. Co-expression analysis showed that PiAA17 genes are upregulated together with putative PMEs and galactan-active enzymes during plant infection, supporting their key roles in breaking down pectic polysaccharides.

articles.title: Development of an albumin-binding domain-fused GLP-1 analog: Structural insights, receptor activation, and functional characterization.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are established therapeutic agents for metabolic disease, whereas the pharmacological use of native GLP-1 is constrained by its extremely short circulating lifetime. Alb8-GA, a G-related albumin-binding domain, binds human serum albumin (HSA) with high affinity. Here, we engineered a chimeric GLP-1 protein (GLP-1-ABD) by combining GLP-1 with a truncated Alb8-GA sequence. Following recombinant expression and purification, GLP-1-ABD was characterized using mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and one-dimensional proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1D 1H NMR). Size exclusion chromatography demonstrated association of GLP-1-ABD with HSA, while molecular modeling provided structural insight into the corresponding binding interface. In GLP-1R-expressing cells, GLP-1-ABD stimulated intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) accumulation, with an EC50 of 1.25 ± 0.16 nM, compared with 0.97 ± 0.14 nM for liraglutide (p = 0.15). Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated that the GLP-1 moiety maintained key receptor interactions despite fusion to the albumin-binding domain. In MIN6 cells, GLP-1-ABD enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and produced responses similar to liraglutide across most of the tested concentrations. In diabetic rats, GLP-1-ABD improved the glucose-response profile during oral glucose tolerance testing and increased circulating insulin relative to untreated diabetic animals (p = 0.03), while insulin levels did not differ significantly from those observed with liraglutide (p = 0.44). Collectively, these findings show that the truncated ABD fusion preserves GLP-1R agonist activity while enabling HSA association and supporting sustained glucose-lowering effects, thereby providing a basis for further pharmacokinetic and efficacy studies of GLP-1-ABD.

articles.title: Decision tree models highlight lower social and physical function in individuals with recurrent plantar diabetes-related foot ulcers: A 1-year prospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We investigated whether decision tree (DT) models and predictor selection strategies can improve stratification of individuals with diabetes at high risk of plantar foot ulcer recurrence.

METHODS: In a 12-month prospective cohort of 58 participants (mean age 65 years, 83% men) at high risk of diabetes-related plantar ulcer recurrence, three DT models were developed: a predefined model with predictors linked to cumulative plantar tissue stress, and two data-driven models with predictors selected using univariate or elastic net-regularized logistic regression. Performance evaluation included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Twenty-two participants (38%) developed a recurrent plantar ulcer. The predefined model showed low sensitivity (57%) and specificity (64%). The univariate selection model showed higher performance estimates (sensitivity 71% and specificity 82%). This DT was based on social and physical functioning (36-Item Short Form Health Survey) and self-selected walking speed, with lower social and physical functioning scores indicating higher risk of recurrence.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, data-driven DT models identified quality-of-life domains as candidate predictors of plantar ulcer recurrence. If validated in larger cohorts, quality-of-life assessments could represent a low-cost addition to current risk stratification in diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a mindfulness-based cognitive behavioral program on glycemic control and quality of life among adults with diabetes in Damascus, Syria: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Depression and diabetes distress worsen glycemic control and quality of life (QoL). This randomized controlled trial evaluated a 14-week mindfulness-based cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) program on Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) and QoL among adults with diabetes in Damascus, Syria.

METHODS: Adults with diabetes and mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms were randomized to mindfulness-based CBT or routine care. Per-protocol analysis included 40 completers (n = 20/group). Post-intervention HbA1c was evaluated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) adjusting for baseline levels. Secondary QoL was assessed across four WHOQOL-BREF domains.

RESULTS: Intervention participants achieved significant reduction in HbA1c levels (9.0 ± 1.7% to 7.2 ± 1.4%, p = 0.021), while controls experienced an increase in HbA1c levels (9.1 ± 1.8% to 9.9 ± 1.7%, p < 0.001). ANCOVA demonstrated a significant intervention effect (F (1,37) = 13.53, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.268). Adjusted post-intervention HbA1c was lower in the intervention group (7.48% vs. 9.34%; adjusted mean difference: -1.86%, 95% CI: -2.89 to -0.84, p < 0.001). All WHOQOL-BREF domains improved significantly within the intervention arm (all p ≤ 0.001), with consistent glycemic benefits across subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: Mindfulness-based CBT produced clinically meaningful glycemic and QoL improvements, supporting psychosocial care integration into routine diabetes management in crisis-affected settings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07779044.

articles.title: Diabetes and central adiposity are associated with elevated liver stiffness despite low fibrosis-4 index in adults at metabolic risk.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To estimate how often elevated liver stiffness occurs despite a low fibrosis-4 index using age-stratified cutoffs (FIB-4) in adults at metabolic risk and whether diabetes and central adiposity characterize this discordant subgroup.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of prospectively collected baseline data from a metabolic-risk screening programme. Adults aged ≥ 35 years with recorded FIB-4 and quality-confirmed vibration-controlled transient elastography were included. Low FIB-4 was < 1.3 at age 35-64 years and < 2.0 at age ≥ 65 years. The outcome was liver stiffness measurement (LSM) ≥ 8 kPa.

RESULTS: Among 351 participants, 264 (75.2 %) had low FIB-4. LSM ≥ 8 kPa occurred in 17/264 (6.4 %) with low FIB-4 and 16/87 (18.4 %) with intermediate-to-high FIB-4 (OR 3.27, 95 % CI 1.57-6.81). Within the low-FIB-4 subgroup, diabetes was present in 70.6 % versus 20.0 %, and median waist-to-height ratio was 0.679 versus 0.620, in participants with versus without LSM ≥ 8 kPa. Adjusted ORs were 8.61 (95 % CI 2.59-28.64) for diabetes and 2.48 (1.23-4.99) per 0.1 higher waist-to-height ratio.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated liver stiffness was uncommon but not absent after a low FIB-4 result and was concentrated in participants with diabetes and central adiposity. Prospective validation should test whether these features improve selection for second-line liver assessment.

articles.title: Decoding PRRS Resilience: The Metabolic differences of High- and low- resilience Pigs.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) is a highly contagious viral disease causing severe economic losses worldwide. This study applied untargeted metabolomics to lung and lymph node tissues from high‑ versus low‑resilience Min pigs following PRRSV infection, aiming to identify differential metabolites and pathways associated with resilience. In lung tissue, 13 differential metabolites were identified, including acylcarnitine species, glycocholic acid, and phosphatidylcholine; in lymph node tissue, 27 metabolites differed significantly, notably propionylcarnitine, epoxidized fatty acids, and deoxyadenosine. Pathway enrichment revealed common enrichment in the oxidation of branched‑chain fatty acids in both tissues. Deoxyadenosine, up‑regulated in lymph node tissues of high‑resilience animals, promoted proliferation of porcine macrophages (3D4/21 cells), as confirmed by CCK‑8 assays. These findings indicate that carnitine‑related metabolites and branched‑chain fatty acid oxidation are associated with the host recovery process after PRRSV infection, while deoxyadenosine may enhance immune cell function. This study provides exploratory, hypothesis-generating metabolic features associated with the resilience phenotype in PRRS‑endemic herds.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes as nanocarriers for curcumin: from fundamental research to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Curcumin has diverse pharmacological activities but poor water solubility, rapid degradation, extensive metabolism, and very low oral bioavailability limit its therapeutic use. This review evaluates mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Exo; MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles per MISEV2023) as natural nanocarriers for curcumin delivery and the barriers to clinical translation. Curcumin-loaded MSC-Exo (Cur@Exos) can improve curcumin stability, sustain release, enhance target-tissue accumulation, and cross biological barriers such as the blood-brain barrier. Compared with synthetic nanocarriers, MSC-Exo may offer better biocompatibility, immune evasion, and tissue tropism, but these properties depend on source and preparation; proteomes, miRNA cargoes, and functions differ among bone marrow-, umbilical cord-, and adipose-derived MSCs. Encapsulation efficiency, batch consistency, scalability, and storage stability also remain suboptimal. Preclinical studies show Cur@Exos benefits in neurodegenerative diseases, rheumatoid arthritis, liver disease, wound healing, bone defects, and sepsis-associated kidney injury. However, findings are limited by heterogeneity in exosome sources, preparation, loading methods, and animal models; small samples and short follow-up; inconsistent dose metrics (particle number vs. protein content); and lack of standardized process and outcome criteria, reference materials, and potency assays. Long-term safety remains inadequately established: current evidence covers only short-term single or repeated dosing; ≥ 6-month repeat-dose toxicology with anti-drug antibody and complement monitoring, predictive immunogenicity screening, tumorigenicity assessment, potency-based batch release testing, and clinical efficacy data are lacking. MSC-Exo is a promising curcumin-delivery platform, but translation requires standardized manufacturing, globally harmonized quality control, improved scalability, systematic safety evaluation, well-designed multicenter trials, and a clarified international regulatory pathway.

articles.title: Identification of GSK3β as a molecular target of Alternaria mycotoxin-induced reproductive toxicity using integrated network toxicology and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) validation.
articles.abstract: Alternaria mycotoxins are emerging foodborne contaminants associated with reproductive toxicity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) to identify potential molecular targets of reproductive toxicity induced by two Alternaria mycotoxins, alternariol (AOH) and alternariol monomethyl ether (AME). The CCK-8 assay revealed that both toxins induced time- and dose-dependent cytotoxicity in TM3 mouse Leydig cells and HTR-8/SVneo human trophoblast cells. Network toxicology identified 76 overlapping targets associated with mycotoxin-induced reproductive toxicity. Enrichment analysis revealed that these targets were significantly enriched in pathways related to cancer and viral infection. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed and analyzed in Cytoscape. Based on this network, the robust rank aggregation method was employed to prioritize ten core targets: CASP3, DNMT1, ABL1, ESR1, RELA, CDK2, GSK3β, CDK4, CHEK1, and SRC. Molecular docking showed favorable binding between AOH/AME and these targets, with GSK3β displaying the lowest binding energy scores for both toxins. Subsequently, SPR analysis confirmed direct molecular interactions between GSK3β and both AOH and AME, with dissociation constants in the micromolar range. This study provides experimental evidence of direct binding of AOH/AME to GSK3β, suggesting that GSK3β is a candidate molecular target mediating the reproductive toxicity induced by Alternaria mycotoxins and providing a mechanistic basis for future risk assessment.

articles.title: Exploring a hybrid workflow on current adaptive radiotherapy systems.
articles.journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We introduce a novel hybrid workflow in adaptive radiotherapy that combines traditional image guidance capabilities with an AI-based adaptive radiotherapy platform.

METHOD: The Ethos adaptive radiotherapy system currently lacks the capability for manual couch shifts at the time of treatment delivery. It offers two options: 1) a scheduled (non-adaptive) plan and 2) a daily reoptimized adaptive plan. Our hybrid workflow simulates optimal couch shifts applied to the scheduled plan to maximize target dose and minimize dose to critical organs while reducing patient time on the couch. We evaluated five prostate patients previously treated on the Ethos system. For each patient, data included one reference plan, 20 scheduled plans, and 20 adapted plans. Dose-volume statistics of PTV and organs-at-risk were compared among the scheduled, hybrid, and adapted plans.

RESULTS: The optimal couch shifts determined using the hybrid workflow ranged from -7 to 10 mm and increased the PTV coverage by up to 21.0 % compared with the scheduled plan. Adapted plans provided the highest target coverage, with a maximum improvement of 16.4 % over the hybrid workflow plans. Rectal and bladder sparing were similar between our hybrid workflow and the scheduled plan. However, compared with the adapted plan, the hybrid workflow reduced rectal V45 in 4/5 patients and bladder V45 in 2/5 patients, with maximum reductions of 9.4 % and 5.7 %, respectively.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that incorporating manual couch shifts into adaptive radiotherapy could substantially enhance treatment quality and influence the decision when choosing between an adapted and non-adapted plan.

articles.title: Candida albicans vaccines: from cell wall architecture to protective immunity.
articles.abstract: Candida albicans is an opportunistic fungal pathogen that colonizes the oral cavity, gastrointestinal tract, and vaginal mucosa. Immunosuppression or increased fungal virulence permits extensive mucosal replication and tissue invasion, driving either recurrent superficial infection or life-threatening systemic disease. Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is predominantly caused by. It substantially impairs quality of life in women of reproductive age. Although azoles such as fluconazole are effective, emerging resistance and frequent recurrence limit their long-term utility. These constraints highlight the urgent need for preventive strategies against VVC. This review summarizes the landscape of cell wall antigens and their immunobiology, identifies key translational barriers, and proposes targeted strategies to advance next-generation antifungal vaccines, thereby providing a reference for future vaccine development.

articles.title: Transvascular neurosurgery.
articles.abstract: Major advances in cerebrovascular neurosurgery have repeatedly emerged from the convergence of a transformative idea with enabling technology. The introduction of the operating microscope and microsurgical instrumentation in the late 1960s redefined the limits of safe access to deep cerebrovascular structures and gave rise to microneurosurgery. The advent of catheter-based intracranial navigation in the late 20th century created the field of endovascular neurosurgery, transforming the management of aneurysms, arteriovenous malformations, dural arteriovenous fistulas, atherosclerosis, and large-vessel occlusion stroke. Throughout this evolution, the vessel wall has been treated as an inviolable barrier; the cardinal rule of endovascular practice has been to avoid perforating it. Herein, it is argued that the deliberate and controlled crossing of the vessel wall-transvascular neurosurgery-represents a third paradigm shift, whereby the neurovascular arterial and venous networks are repurposed as a natural operative corridor to access the subdural, subarachnoid, parenchymal, and ventricular compartments of the brain without a craniotomy or burr hole. Early clinical work has shown that controlled transvascular exit from the meningeal vasculature is feasible and can enable a range of intracranial procedures, from implantation of biomimetic shunts and combined middle meningeal artery embolization with transarterial evacuation of nonacute subdural hematoma. The authors review the historical arc that brought us to this point, summarize the technical and biological rationale for meningeal-vascular access, and outline a roadmap by which a broad ecosystem of transvascular neurosurgical procedures could be performed through rapid, outpatient, catheter-based workflows.

articles.title: Dynamic craniotomy: translational development, biomechanical validation, and early clinical experience of an adaptive cranial bone flap fixation platform.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postoperative cerebral swelling, recurrent hemorrhage, and the trade-off between rigid bone flap fixation and decompressive craniectomy remain unresolved problems in cranial neurosurgery. The authors describe the translational development, biomechanical validation, and early clinical implementation of dynamic craniotomy using the NuCrani reversibly expandable plate and the KTC PEEK telescopic burr hole cover, and position this platform within the contemporary innovation continuum of cranial fixation devices.

METHODS: The authors synthesized the device development pathway for dynamic craniotomy, integrating 1) the unmet clinical need and engineering rationale; 2) cadaveric intracranial pressure (ICP)-control studies and biomechanical static compression, static shear, and fatigue testing; 3) a first-in-human technical report; 4) a 25-patient consecutive series in traumatic brain injury (TBI); 5) a propensity score-matched comparison of dynamic versus fixed craniotomy in TBI; 6) a comparative series in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage; and 7) a posterior fossa case series. Outcomes examined included ICP control, bone flap migration behavior, midline shift, reoperation rate, wound complications, cranioplasty avoidance, and Glasgow Outcome Scale score at 3 months.

RESULTS: Cadaveric and biomechanical testing demonstrated greater ICP buffering (120-mL volume challenge: ICP rise from 2.8 to 13.4 mm Hg with dynamic craniotomy vs 11.4 to 100.1 mm Hg with fixed craniotomy, p = 0.04), a peak inward displacement load resistance of 643.3 ± 26.1 N, an expansion tolerance up to 71.6 mm, and zero failure across 500 fatigue cycles at 15 mm of excursion. Across the clinical series (≥ 60 patients), outward bone flap migration ≥ 5 mm occurred in 84%-100% of cases with worsening edema, with reciprocal decreases in midline shift; ≥ 8 mm migration occurred in approximately 40%-56%. No fixation failures, paradoxical sinking, rescue craniectomies, or cranioplasty procedures were required. In the propensity score-matched TBI cohort, dynamic craniotomy was associated with lower postoperative midline shift, lower mortality, and a higher proportion of favorable outcomes than fixed craniotomy. Because these comparative data derive from small, single-center, retrospective cohorts, they should be interpreted as preliminary and hypothesis generating.

CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic craniotomy is an adaptive, pressure-responsive cranial reconstruction platform that bridges the gap between fixed-plate craniotomy and decompressive craniectomy. Its translational pathway from concept and biomechanics to early clinical experience supports its feasibility and preliminary safety; however, because the comparative clinical data are limited, retrospective, single center, and generated by the device developers, the reported outcome advantages over conventional fixation remain unproven and require confirmation in prospective, independently conducted, multicenter studies. The platform nonetheless exemplifies a stepwise, low-disruption model for neurosurgical device innovation.

articles.title: Residual Shunt at 6 Months Follow-up After Percutaneous Patent Foramen Ovale Closure in CAHAL: A Comparison of Occlutech and Amplatzer.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual shunt is a known complication in percutaneous patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure, and moderate to large residual shunt has been associated with an increased risk of recurrent stroke. Device-related factors, such as device size, have been associated with residual shunt, but comparative data per device type are scarce.

AIMS: We compared the prevalence of moderate to large residual shunt at 6 months between the Amplatzer and Occlutech devices.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing successful percutaneous PFO closure with an Amplatzer or Occlutech dedicated closure device within the CAHAL centers Amsterdam UMC and Leiden UMC between 2018 and 2024 were included. The study population was divided into patients treated with an Occlutech and an Amplatzer device. The prevalence of moderate/large residual shunt at 6 months of follow-up was compared between the two groups. As a sensitivity analysis, a logistic regression was conducted to determine the association between the treatment groups and moderate/large residual shunt. The logistic regression was conducted in a weighted population using inverse probability weighting (IPTW), correcting for age, sex, smoking status, shunt size at baseline, device size, and atrial septal aneurysm.

RESULTS: A total of 413 patients were included with an average age of 45.8 ± 11.3 years and 51.6% were male. Of the included patients, 279 were treated with an Amplatzer- and 134 with an Occlutech device. In the group treated with an Amplatzer, 22.2% of the patients had a moderate or large residual shunt at 6 months compared to 14.9% in the Occlutech group (p = 0.11). The sensitivity analysis did not show an association between device type and moderate/large shunt OR 0.71 (95% CI: 0.39-1.28, p = 0.25).

CONCLUSION: In this study, no significant difference was observed in moderate/large residual shunt prevalence at 6 months of follow-up between the Occlutech and Amplatzer devices.

articles.title: Variation in Anticoagulation Practice for Atrial High-Rate Episodes: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial high-rate episodes (AHRE) detected by cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) are associated with increased thromboembolic risk, yet their clinical significance and optimal anticoagulation strategy remain uncertain, particularly in the absence of electrocardiogram (ECG)-confirmed atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey of UK clinicians involved in CIED follow-up. The survey assessed anticoagulation decision-making in AHRE, including episode-duration thresholds, cumulative burden, CHA2DS2-VA use, additional ECG monitoring, and anticoagulant choice. Only responses from UK-based consultant clinicians were included and analysed descriptively.

RESULTS: A total of 51 responses were received; 38 met the inclusion criteria and were analysed. Most respondents (86.8%) reported having reviewed AHRE alerts within the preceding 6 months, indicating that AHRE are commonly encountered in clinical practice. A ≥ 24-h episode was the most common threshold for anticoagulation (44.7%), although many clinicians reported lower thresholds or individualised approaches. Nearly half (44.7%) did not consider cumulative AHRE burden in decision-making. CHA2DS2-VA thresholds also varied, most commonly ≥ 2 or ≥ 1. Additional ECG monitoring was infrequently performed. Direct oral anticoagulants were universally preferred, with apixaban the most commonly selected agent (73.7%).

CONCLUSION: There is substantial variation in UK clinical practice regarding anticoagulation for AHRE, reflecting ongoing uncertainty and lack of clear guidance. These findings highlight the need for evidence-based thresholds to support consistent and informed clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Biomaterial-assisted culture of mesenchymal stem cells for enhanced extracellular vesicle production and cartilage regeneration: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Articular cartilage has limited self-repair capacity, prompting interest in cell-free therapies such as extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). This systematic review assessed whether MSCs cultured with biomaterials produce more EVs, and EVs with greater chondrogenic or cartilage-regenerative efficacy, than MSCs in conventional culture. The publications were searched on PubMed, Scopus, and EBSCO (2016-2026), and the synthesis of the evidence was done narratively, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From 576 unique records, we included 14 preclinical studies: 12 used biomaterials in a three-dimensional format, and two cultured MSCs on decellularized extracellular matrix. Eleven compared biomaterial-culture EVs head-to-head with conventional-culture EVs for chondrogenic or cartilage-repair outcomes. EV yield was higher with the biomaterial in all ten studies that compared it (about 1.2- to 7.5-fold per cell or per unit of protein). In all 11 comparisons, biomaterial-culture EVs matched or exceeded conventional-culture EVs in chondrocyte proliferation, chondrogenic marker expression, matrix deposition, or in vivo cartilage repair. Cargo-target mechanisms were functionally validated in six studies, although in one the microRNA had been enriched by transfection rather than by the culture platform. Certainty of evidence was low for yield and very low for chondrogenic, cartilage-repair, and anti-inflammatory outcomes. Risk of bias was probably low in seven studies and probably high in seven. The comparator arms often differed in more than the biomaterial, and EV characterization was frequently incomplete. In conclusion, biomaterial-assisted culture is a promising but not yet standardized route to more chondrogenic MSC-derived EVs and requires further study.

articles.title: Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of the left atrium in daily practice: a practical guide.
articles.abstract: The left atrium (LA) is a crucial component of cardiovascular performance. A thorough understanding of LA anatomy, physiology, and pathology is necessary for diagnostic and prognostic purposes in daily clinical practice. LA volume is widely recognized as a novel biomarker for cardiovascular risks in the general population. Furthermore, it has been shown to be a significant prognostic factor in various cardiac conditions, such as atrial fibrillation, ischemic heart disease, valvular heart disease, and heart failure. The assessment of LA function in physiologic and pathologic states has gathered interest with expanding research supporting its utility as a biomarker for outcomes in different cardiovascular abnormalities. Utilizing basic and advanced echocardiographic modalities and integrating multiple parameters helps in both qualitative and quantitative assessment of LA size and function. This is a narrative review provides a comprehensive approach to assessing LA size and function by interpreting existing English-language literature, including landmark studies, reviews and consensus documents from leading echocardiography societies. The literature search focused on key terms, such as LA size, phasic function, strain, and Doppler hemodynamics. By collecting, analyzing, and grouping the echocardiographic parameters, we introduce a simplified approach to guide clinicians through a comprehensive LA assessment ranging from standard 2D dimensions to advanced deformational tracking tailored to specific clinical indications.

articles.title: Reply to "Clarification of age-term coding in a pediatric tracheal tube prediction model".
Upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate sourced from waste plastic bottles into graphene oxide and its evaluation for CO2 absorption.
articles.abstract: The human-made "plastic" resource has turned into an environmental concern for years now. The ideal solution to the problem is still under research. Our research aims to deplete the huge amount of plastic waste on Earth by converting it into a functional material. The carbon chain of this polymer cannot be broken; however, it can be altered into a different category. Plastic waste, specifically PET, was chosen for the experiment and was converted finally into graphene oxide. Catalytic graphitization was used to convert one carbon form into another. The obtained graphene oxide was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, energy dispersive spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. The FT-IR and EDS results confirm the synthesis of graphene oxide. The thermal stability and magnetic behavior of graphene oxide are satisfactory. Catalytic behavior toward CO2 adsorption is a potent application of PETGO. The desorption curve indicates CO2 adsorption on the surface through chemisorption. A high amount of desorbed CO2 indicates a high reaction surface area and electronic interaction.

articles.title: Intraoperative hypotension in older adults with hip fracture: a comparative analysis of different definitions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with adverse outcomes, but its definition varies widely and most definitions are derived from younger or mixed-age populations. Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery are particularly susceptible due to reduced physiological reserve. This study compared absolute, relative, and duration-based definitions of IOH and evaluated their associations with postoperative adverse outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included all patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent hip fracture surgery at Maastricht University Medical Centre+ between January 2021 and December 2022. IOH was defined using absolute thresholds (MAP < 65 mmHg, SBP < 100 mmHg), relative reductions (≥  20%), post-induction decreases, and duration below thresholds. Outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI, KDIGO criteria), and 30 day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, ASA classification, medication use, and nursing home residency.

RESULTS: A total of 473 patients were included (mean age 80.9 years, 69.8% female). Postoperative AKI occurred in 9.9% and 30 day mortality in 5.5%. Absolute and relative IOH thresholds were not significantly associated with outcomes. In contrast, longer IOH duration (SBP < 100 mmHg) was associated with 30 day mortality (OR 1.09 per minute, 95%CI 1.02-1.16). After adjustment, higher ASA classification remained associated with AKI, while IOH duration remained significantly associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, the duration of IOH, rather than static thresholds, appeared more strongly associated with adverse outcomes, particularly 30 day mortality. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of hypotension duration and support further prospective research to establish geriatric-specific IOH definitions and optimal perioperative blood pressure management strategies.

articles.title: Is fear of recurrence a determinant of breast self-examination awareness in women who have survived breast cancer?
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fear of cancer recurrence is one of the most prevalent and enduring psychosocial challenges encountered by breast cancer survivors. Although this fear can prompt health-monitoring behaviors such as breast self-examination (BSE), comprehensive survivorship care models addressing these psychological dynamics remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study was aimed at determining the level of fear of cancer recurrence in women who have survived breast cancer and examining its relationship with their health beliefs and awareness regarding breast self-examination.

METHODS: This descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study was conducted between June 2024 and October 2024 with 259 breast cancer survivors registered at the radiation oncology outpatient clinic of a tertiary hospital in Türkiye. Data were collected using a Patient Information Form, the Champion Health Belief Model Scale, and the Fear of Cancer Recurrence Inventory. The study was reported in accordance with the STROBE checklist. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent samples t test, ANOVA, and linear regression analysis.

RESULTS: The mean total score for fear of cancer recurrence among the survivors was 1.42 ± 0.82 points. A statistically significant positive correlation was identified between fear of recurrence and health belief model dimensions, particularly perceived severity and health motivation (p < 0.05). Linear regression analysis revealed that fear of cancer recurrence had a significant positive effect on the health belief model (F = 31.690, p < 0.001), explaining 11% of the total variance (R2 = 0.110).

CONCLUSIONS: Fear of cancer recurrence is common among breast cancer survivors and significantly influences their health beliefs and self-monitoring behaviors. While moderate fear may heighten surveillance awareness through BSE, structured psychosocial support and educational programs are essential to help survivors manage recurrence concerns adaptively within holistic nursing care.

articles.title: Chronic disease burden and health-related quality of life among missouri adults.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This cross-sectional study examined associations between chronic disease burden, specific chronic conditions, and Short Form 36 (SF-36) health-related quality of life (HRQoL) scores among Missouri adults 18 years of age or older.

METHODS: We analyzed survey-weighted data from the 2024 Center for Medical Epidemiology and Population Health Adult Health Survey (N = 547). The primary chronic condition count included cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, arthritis, diabetes, depressive disorder, non-skin cancer, and kidney disease and was categorized as zero, one, or two or more conditions. Obesity was examined as a condition-specific exposure and in sensitivity analyses. Survey-weighted linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, educational attainment, employment status, and rurality. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was used to control the false discovery rate across the 10 HRQoL outcomes.

RESULTS: Overall, 30.0% of Missouri adults had two or more of the seven selected chronic conditions. Compared with adults with no chronic conditions, adults with two or more conditions had lower scores for nine of the 10 HRQoL outcomes after false discovery rate correction. The largest adjusted differences were observed for Role-Physical (β = -30.65; 95% CI, -46.56 to -14.74), Physical Functioning (β = -28.70; 95% CI, - 38.60 to -18.81), Bodily Pain (β = -28.28; 95% CI, -38.96 to -17.59), Social Functioning (β = -26.18; 95% CI, -35.43 to -16.92), and General Health (β = -24.18; 95% CI, - 30.75 to - 17.62). Physical Component Summary (PCS) was 12.82 points lower (95% CI, -16.98 to -8.66), and Mental Component Summary (MCS) was 6.10 points lower (95% CI, -9.47 to -2.73). Arthritis and cardiovascular disease had the strongest associations with lower PCS, while depressive disorder had the strongest association with lower MCS. In supplementary continuous-count models, each additional condition was associated with a 4.57-point lower PCS score and a 2.20-point lower MCS score.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater chronic disease burden was associated with poorer physical and mental HRQoL among Missouri adults. Adding HRQoL assessment to chronic disease surveillance and clinical follow-up may help identify functional limitations and mental health needs that are not apparent from diagnoses alone.

articles.title: Liposomal irinotecan and capecitabine plus bevacizumab as second-line therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer: A multicenter, single-arm study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liposomal irinotecan, characterized by its favorable pharmacologic properties and reduced systemic toxicity compared to irinotecan, has demonstrated superior therapeutic potential. This multicenter, single-arm study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of liposomal irinotecan, capecitabine, and bevacizumab as a second-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC).

METHODS: Patients with histologically confirmed mCRC who had progressed following first-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy were enrolled in this study. The treatment regimen was liposomal irinotecan (70 mg/m2, d1), capecitabine (1000 mg/m2, twice daily, d1-10), and bevacizumab (5 mg/kg, d1). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, overall survival, and safety.

RESULTS: Between March 2024 and July 2024, 63 patients were enrolled, with a median age of 60.0 years (range: 37.0-79.0). Among the patients who received at least one tumor assessment, the objective response rate and disease control rate were 22.9% (11/48; 95% CI, 12.0-37.3) and 89.6% (43/48; 95% CI, 77.3-96.5), respectively. With a median follow-up of 16.2 months (range: 0.5-28.5), the median progression-free survival was 8.1 months (95% CI, 7.3-8.9), and the median overall survival was 19.5 months (95% CI, 15.2-23.8). The most common grade 3 to 4 adverse events were diarrhea (12.7%), neutropenia (11.1%), and fatigue (6.3%).

CONCLUSIONS: The combination of liposomal irinotecan, capecitabine, and bevacizumab demonstrated promising antitumor activity and a manageable safety profile in patients with mCRC who had failed first-line oxaliplatin-based therapy. These results suggested that this regimen is a clinically feasible second-line treatment option for mCRC.

articles.title: The State of Health in Jordan, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Jordan's health system has evolved amid rapid urbanization and the strain of hosting one of the world's largest refugee populations per capita. This study comprehensively evaluates national disease burden trends in Jordan from 1990 to 2023 to inform health priorities.

METHODS: Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 framework, we analyzed age-standardized rates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) across 370 diseases and 88 risk factors. Data were derived from national censuses, health surveys, disease registries, and hospital records, and harmonized using standardized GBD modeling and estimation procedures. Analyses were stratified by age, sex, and cause.

RESULTS: Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized DALYs declined by 33.88% (95% UI: -37.38 to -30.59), with greater reductions in males (-38.83%; -42.22 to -35.60) than females (-27.22%; -31.33 to -23.58). YLLs decreased by 49.38% (-50.93 to -47.68), while YLDs remained comparatively stable (2.49%; -2.37 to 7.47). Using mutually exclusive GBD Level 3 causes, ischemic heart disease and diabetes mellitus were the two leading causes of DALYs in 2023. Diabetes mellitus rose from 7th place in 1990 to 2nd place in 2023, while neonatal disorders declined from 1st to 7th place. Metabolic risks remained important contributors to the overall disease burden. Jordan's age-standardized diabetes DALY rate in 2023 was approximately 1.56 times the global rate.

CONCLUSION: Jordan's health profile has shifted toward a greater burden from noncommunicable diseases, while age-standardized health loss and premature mortality have declined substantially. In contrast, nonfatal disability changed comparatively little.
