These findings provide an evidence base for primary prevention of NCDs and for long-term strategies addressing the country's evolving health challenges.

articles.title: Extensive Stray-Dog Mauling as Major Contaminated Crush Trauma Causing Severe Rhabdomyolysis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Overt Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: Recovery Without Renal Replacement Therapy.
articles.abstract: An adolescent male developed severe rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, overt disseminated intravascular coagulation, and respiratory fluid overload after extensive stray-dog mauling. The course reflected overlapping traumatic, inflammatory, and infectious mechanisms. He recovered without renal replacement therapy through source control, individualized antimicrobials, conservative renal support, and timely transition to de-resuscitation.

articles.title: A Spatiotemporal Causal Machine Learning Framework for Quantifying the Impact of PM2.5 on Asthma at the Community Level.
articles.abstract: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 μm or smaller (PM2.5), is a leading environmental risk factor for respiratory diseases. While previous studies have investigated the biological mechanisms linking PM2.5 to asthma exacerbation, these studies are unable to scale for population-level assessments. In contrast, most regional analyses rely on traditional statistical models that primarily quantify associations, limiting estimation of health changes under hypothetical pollution interventions. This study introduces a spatiotemporal causal machine learning framework to estimate PM2.5-related changes in asthma outcomes at the county level. Using county-level monthly hospitalization and emergency department records from 2011 to 2019 in Colorado, the framework integrates spatial and temporal representation learning to model geographic interdependence and temporal dynamics in exposure-response relationships. Further, through a causal inference approach, the model estimates model-based counterfactual health outcomes under hypothetical PM2.5 interventions, moving beyond regression-based correlation analysis. Results show that the model-based counterfactual estimates exhibit spatial and population heterogeneity. Larger estimated effects were observed in several communities experiencing compounded environmental and social stressors, while uncertainty was greater in data-sparse counties.

articles.title: First-Hand Experience and the Value of Telerehabilitation for Chronic Knee Pain: A Discrete Choice Experiment Nested in a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess whether first-hand experience of receiving physical therapy via telerehabilitation affected patient preferences and willingness to pay for telerehabilitation. DESIGN: This study used a discrete choice experiment nested within a randomized controlled trial. METHODS: We recruited 319 Australian adults aged 45 years or over, with chronic knee pain consistent with osteoarthritis, who had completed a clinical trial where they were randomized to receive physical therapy via telerehabilitation or in-person. Participants were presented hypothetical scenarios and asked to choose between physical therapy delivered via telerehabilitation or in-person. Each scenario presented seven attributes of consultations at varying levels. Data were analyzed using a generalized multinomial logit and latent class models. RESULTS: There were 164 participants from the in-person trial arm (80% of those randomized) and 155 from the telerehabilitation arm (82% of those randomized) who participated. Participants in the telerehabilitation arm (ie, with first-hand experience of telerehabilitation) were willing to pay AU$ 87.49 (95% confidence interval: 72.83, 102.14) more than people in the in-person arm for telerehabilitation consultations (all other attributes fixed at reference values for categorical variables and at mean values for continuous variables). Four subgroups were identified. In the telerehabilitation arm, 105 (68% of 155) participants preferred telerehabilitation, and 50 (32%) preferred in-person consultations. In the in-person arm, 63 (39% of 164) held a strong preference for in-person consultations, and 101 (61%) had a mild preference for in-person consultations. CONCLUSION: People with first-hand experience using telerehabilitation for physical therapy expressed a greater willingness to use and pay for it than people who experienced in-person care. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(11):735-744. Epub 23 September 2026. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.14073.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of aerobic exercise, resistance exercise, and combined interventions on pain, function, and quality of life (QoL) in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA) at the short term (≤12 weeks) and long term (>12 weeks). DESIGN: Intervention systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA). LITERATURE SEARCH: MEDLINE, PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, CINAHL, PEDro, AMED, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception until July 2025. STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials of patients with knee OA that evaluated exercise interventions aimed at improving pain, function, and QoL. DATA SYNTHESIS: Using random-effects models, the NMA synthesized effect sizes and ranked interventions by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), with evidence certainty assessed via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. RESULTS: Thirty-five trials (n = 3808 patients) were included. For pain, short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect among the interventions (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.937, low certainty). For function, short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect estimates (SMD = -0.590, low certainty), followed by long-term aerobic exercise (SMD = -0.540, very low certainty). Short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect (SMD = 0.663, low certainty) for improving QoL. CONCLUSION: Aerobic and resistance exercise, alone or in combination, and delivered over the short- or long-term, improved pain, function, and QoL for patients with knee OA. Short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had clinically meaningful improvements for pain, with relatively favorable effects on function and QoL. Evidence regarding the clinical significance of long-term exercise interventions was limited. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(11):724-734. Epub 24 July 2026. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.13875.

articles.title: Broad Conclusions From a Narrow Evidence Base: Comments on a Systematic Review of ESWT for Achilles Tendinopathy.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.abstract: Letter to the Editor-in-Chief in response to JOSPT article "Shockwave Therapy for Midportion and Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy: A Nail in the coffin? A Systematic Review With Meta-analysis" by Korakakis et al. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(11):745-746. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.0203.

articles.title: Prevalence of Sleep Disorders in Patients With Knee, Hip, and Hand Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled prevalences of insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome, and narcolepsy in patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis. DESIGN: Prevalence systematic review with meta-analyses. The review protocol was preregistered at PROSPERO (CRD420251005836). LITERATURE SEARCH: We conducted systematic searches in Embase, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to August 2025, supplemented by citation screening and reference checking. STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: We identified observational and interventional studies reporting prevalence data on sleep disorders among patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis. DATA SYNTHESIS: Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation tool. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects proportion meta-analyses, with subgroup analyses based on diagnostic criteria and patient characteristics. RESULTS: Eighteen studies (202 847 participants) were included (three cohort, five case-control, 12 cross-sectional), of which nine studies were of very good to good or high quality. Insomnia was the most prevalent sleep disorder, 42% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 34% to 51%), followed by sleep apnea (37% [95% CI: 6% to 67%]) and restless legs syndrome (35% [95% CI: 10% to 61%]). No studies reported on narcolepsy. Estimates varied by diagnostic criteria and sample characteristics across studies, and the certainty of evidence was very low. CONCLUSION: Sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, were common among patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis, supporting the need to raise clinical awareness. Future studies may alter prevalence estimates, as only a small number of high-quality studies were identified and large between-study heterogeneity was observed. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(11):710-723. Epub 27 Aug 2026. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.14210.

articles.title: Can Clinicians Predict Which Patients Respond Best to a Specific Treatment? A Systematic Review of Low Back Pain Moderators in Primary Care.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To synthesize and critically evaluate evidence on treatment effect moderators in the primary care management of low back pain (LBP). DESIGN: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and secondary analyses of RCTs. LITERATURE SEARCH: Medline, EMBASE, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2025. STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: We included RCTs investigating moderators for primary care interventions in nonspecific LBP. DATA SYNTHESIS: Data were synthesized by exploring data clusters (similar intervention-moderator combinations) and examining high-quality evidence with promising effects. The quality of moderation analyses was assessed using the Instrument for assessing the Credibility of Effect Modification Analyses tool, and trial quality was assessed using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale. Study diversity precluded meta-analysis. RESULTS: Seventy-three studies were identified. The studies were highly heterogeneous with almost no repeated investigations of the same intervention-moderator combination. While RCT quality was generally high, moderation analysis quality was poor. Six studies (8% of 73) prioritized effect moderation as the primary aim. The remaining studies tended to analyze available data post hoc rather than assessing theory driven moderators. Ten higher-quality analyses did not identify any clearly important moderators. Results were inconclusive due to high uncertainty (eg, wide confidence intervals, lack of statistical significance) and conflicting findings. Some promising moderators were identified in fair-quality analyses; for example, graded exposure appeared more effective for those with high catastrophizing. CONCLUSION: We identified a broad but superficial body of literature on effect moderation in LBP primary care. The promising moderators identified require further testing before they can be recommended for clinical practice. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(11):699-709. Epub 2 Sep 2026. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.14384.

articles.title: Short-Term Pain Outcomes of Trigger Point Injection Versus Dry Needling for Acute Myofascial Low Back Pain in the Emergency Department: A Prospective Randomized Comparative Study.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Acute myofascial low back pain prompts emergency department visits, where rapid pain relief matters. Trigger point injection and dry needling are used for myofascial trigger points, but comparative evidence in emergency care is limited. This study compared the short-term analgesic effectiveness of trigger point injection and dry needling in patients with acute myofascial low back pain presenting to the emergency department. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective, randomized, comparative study randomized 52 patients; 49 patients who completed at least 1 post-procedure pain assessment were included in the analysis. Pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at baseline and 5, 15, 30, and 60 minutes after the procedure. The principal effectiveness outcome was the between-group difference in percentage pain reduction at 30 minutes. Intravenous fentanyl (1 µg/kg) was administered as rescue analgesia after the 60-minute assessment when required. RESULTS Baseline NRS scores were similar between groups (P=0.191). Percentage pain reduction at 30 minutes was greater after trigger point injection than after dry needling (86.85±17.53% vs 32.98±13.48%; mean difference, 53.86 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 44.78-62.94; P<0.001). Pain scores were lower and pain reduction was greater after trigger point injection at all post-procedure timepoints (all P<0.001). Rescue analgesia was required in 0 of 26 patients after trigger point injection and 15 of 23 patients (65.2%) after dry needling (P<0.001). No procedure-related adverse events were observed. CONCLUSIONS Trigger point injection was associated with greater short-term pain reduction and less frequent rescue analgesia than dry needling during the first hour of emergency department care. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Meibomian gland epithelial cells demonstrate enhanced reliance on glycolysis for energy metabolism and differentiation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Meibomian gland dysfunction is a leading cause of dry eye disease. Previous studies have established that the meibomian gland exists in a physiological hypoxic environment, with hypoxia-inducible factor 1α playing a regulatory role. However, the metabolic strategy of this gland remains unclear. This study aimed to test the hypothesis that glycolysis serves as an important metabolic pathway in meibomian gland epithelial cells in vivo and that these cells have an enhanced glycolytic phenotype during differentiation.

METHODS: We combined clinical imaging, tissue analysis, and in vitro experiments to test our hypothesis.

RESULTS: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography revealed significantly higher glucose uptake in human meibomian glands than in the orbicularis oculi muscle and surrounding subcutaneous connective tissues outside the tarsal plate, indicating substantial glycolytic activity in vivo. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed strong expression of glycolytic markers, including hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, glucose transporter type 1, hexokinase 2, 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-biphosphatase 3, and pyruvate kinase M2, and lactate dehydrogenase A, in both human and mouse meibomian gland tissues. In immortalized human meibomian gland epithelial cells, differentiation induced a metabolic shift favoring glycolysis with increased extracellular acidification rate, elevated lactate production, and upregulated glycolytic enzyme expression. Three-dimensional spheroid cultures further revealed state-dependent metabolic heterogeneity.

CONCLUSION: The findings indicate that meibomian gland epithelial cells have a highly glycolytic phenotype in vivo and markedly enhanced glycolytic dependence during differentiation. These support their specialized secretory functions and adaptation to hypoxic microenvironments.

articles.title: Assessing EHR Cohort Fitness With Partially Paired Registry Data: A New Statistical Approach Applied to Maternal Health in OneFlorida.
articles.abstract: Cohort discovery using electronic health records (EHR) supports research recruitment and pragmatic clinical trials; however, the validity of EHR-derived cohorts depends on whether patient characteristics recorded in EHR are representative of the target population. While methods exist for assessing internal validity, no published methods address continuous outcomes when EHR and reference population data partially overlap at the individual level. We present a novel statistical approach for assessing EHR data cohort fitness when partially overlapping data are available from an EHR and a registry. For continuous outcomes, we derived an explicit test accommodating unequal variances and correlation between paired records. For binary outcomes, we recommend generalized linear mixed models with a binomial distribution and logit link. We demonstrate the new approach using maternal health data from the OneFlorida+ Data Trust (n = 37,200) and Florida birth certificate records (n = 210,910) from 2021. OneFlorida+ EHR had higher rates of Black race identification, residence in areas of higher social deprivation, and pre-existing diabetes or hypertension, while showing lower probabilities of gestational complications. Maternal age, height, and cesarean delivery rates were not meaningfully different between data sources. Observed differences may reflect the academic health center composition of OneFlorida+ partner sites; however, substantially higher missingness in OneFlorida+ EHR than birth certificate records for race, ethnicity, and location of residence suggests that data capture differences play a role. This replicable statistical method provides researchers with quantitative tools to assess cohort fitness and is applicable to other clinical research networks where EHR and registry data overlap.

articles.title: Social and Environmental Exposures and the Developing Gut of Newborns With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysbiotic gut microbiomes are linked to morbidity, mortality, and poor outcomes, so it is critical to understand their influencing factors.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of nosocomial and socioecological factors on the gut microbiome in newborns with congenital heart disease (CHD).

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort of newborns with CHD matched to healthy newborns by age, sex, and race and ethnicity. Data on feeding type and routes and disease-related factors were collected from electronic medical records. Stool samples were collected at 3 perioperative time points. Gut microbiome diversity and abundance were analyzed using QIIME 2.

RESULTS: Newborns with CHD (n = 41) showed higher alpha diversity (P = .007) and dissimilar beta diversity (P = .001) versus controls (n = 40). Beta diversity was dissimilar between those receiving human milk versus formula (P = .05), between those receiving fortified versus nonfortified human milk (P = .04), and between those receiving naso-orogastric tube feeds versus other routes (P = .02). Newborns with CHD fed only human milk had higher relative abundance of Haemophilus (P = .04), those with longer duration of aortic cross-clamping had lower relative abundance of Streptococcus (P = .10), and those of higher socioeconomic deprivation had higher relative abundance of Enterococcus (P = .03).

CONCLUSIONS: Feeding tubes, formula exposure, aortic cross-clamp, and socioeconomic status were associated with altered gut microbiome diversity. Further study is needed to determine the causal relationships leading to gut microbial dysbiosis in newborns in the cardiac intensive care unit.

articles.title: When In-Person Interpretation Matters: Perspectives From ICUs and Acute Inpatient Care Settings.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinicians often care for multilingual patients and generally prefer in-person rather than remote interpretation. However, little is known about the reasons for selecting specific interpretation modalities in intensive care units (ICUs) and acute inpatient care settings.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the context and application of in-person interpretation in ICUs and acute care settings.

METHODS: Semistructured interviews of interprofessional stakeholders were conducted to understand the advantages and limitations of in-person and remote interpretation modalities in ICUs and acute care settings. Thematic analysis of the interviews was performed.

RESULTS: Forty-one interviews were completed. Certain contexts motivated preferences for selecting in-person rather than remote interpretation in ICUs and acute care settings. Three overarching themes were identified: (1) specific types of conversations (eg, goals-of-care, end-of-life, and difficult conversations), (2) additional patient-related communication barriers (eg, hearing problems, delirium), and (3) other considerations related to in-person interpreter expertise (cultural contexts and prebriefing) and barriers to use (eg, delays, difficulty contacting interpreters).

CONCLUSIONS: Acute care clinicians often prefer in-person interpretation owing to factors that are either specific to in-person interpretation or cannot be fully replicated via remote modalities. Acute care clinicians consider conversation complexity, patient factors, and unique benefits versus logistical barriers when considering in-person interpretation. Overall, in-person interpretation provides advantages over alternative modalities for several scenarios to improve the quality of care for patients with non-English language preference in ICUs and acute care settings.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Versus Standard-Dose Alteplase to Treat High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal dosing of alteplase in patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism is widely debated.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate outcomes in patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism who received alteplase at a low dose or a standard dose.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort analysis of 65 patients who received alteplase for high-risk pulmonary embolism at a large academic medical center between June 1, 2011, and August 31, 2022. Patients were placed in 2 cohorts according to initial dose: low-dose alteplase (50 mg) and standard-dose alteplase (100 mg). The primary outcome was sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours of the start of alteplase infusion. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, hospital and intensive care unit length of stay, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: The primary outcome of sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours did not differ significantly between the 2 cohorts (achieved in 32% of patients in the low-dose group and 38% in the standard-dose group; P = .65). In-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between groups (48% in the low-dose group vs 45% in the standard-dose group; P = .81). Patients in the low-dose group had fewer days of mechanical ventilation than patients in the standard-dose group (1.5 vs 6 days; P = .03) and a smaller percentage had major bleeding (12% vs 25%; P = .34).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism, sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours did not differ significantly between low-dose and standard-dose alteplase treatment strategies. Low-dose alteplase may be an appropriate alternative dosing strategy for patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism.

articles.title: Pilot Testing of the Teaching Engagement and Caregiving Help in the Intensive Care Unit (TEACH-ICU) Scale.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family members often assume caregiving responsibilities after a patient's discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU). Many family members are inadequately prepared due to limited training and support. Intensive care unit nurses can prepare family members to perform caregiving by proactively teaching family members in the ICU. However, no quantitative measure exists to examine nurses' willingness to teach caregiving skills to family members.

OBJECTIVES: To examine the Teaching Engagement and Caregiving Help in the ICU (TEACH-ICU) scale, adapted from the Family Willingness for Caregiving Scale. Refinements from cognitive interviews readied the TEACH-ICU scale for pilot testing to assess the broader survey process before examining the scale's validity and reliability in a larger-scale study.

METHODS: This was a descriptive, cross-sectional study of 30 adult ICU nurses recruited via convenience and snowball sampling through social media platforms and the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses Participate in Research website. Relationship testing was conducted between the TEACH-ICU scale, Hospital Ethical Climate Survey (HECS), and Marlowe-Crowne Social Desirability Scale-Short Form (MCSDS-Short Form).

RESULTS: The TEACH-ICU scale showed high mean willingness scores across all items. The TEACH-ICU total scores significantly correlated with HECS total scores and 4 subscales: peers, managers, hospital, and physicians. No significant relationship was observed between TEACH-ICU scores and social desirability scores.

CONCLUSIONS: The scale and survey process were modified based on this pilot study's results, in preparation for examining the validity and reliability of the TEACH-ICU scale.

articles.title: Effects of Skin Pigmentation on Pulse Oximetry: A Pilot Study.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulse oximetry is an essential, noninvasive tool in critical care, yet mounting evidence indicates that readings may be inaccurate in patients with darker skin pigmentation. These discrepancies can delay recognition of hypoxemia and contribute to racial disparities in clinical outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify the difference between oxygen saturation as measured by pulse oximetry and arterial blood gas measurements across a spectrum of skin pigmentation using objective measures of melanin and skin tone.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in an adult critical care unit. Skin pigmentation was measured using reflectance spectrophotometry. Simultaneous pulse oximetry and arterial blood gas readings were collected during routine arterial blood gas sampling. Bias (pulse oximetry value - arterial blood gas value) was calculated for each measurement pair. Multivariate linear regression models were used to assess the association between skin pigmentation and measurement bias, adjusting for potential confounders such as age, sex, and perfusion index.

RESULTS: Forty-two measurement pairs were analyzed. A weak and nonsignificant relationship was found between the individual typology angle and melanin index and the difference between pulse oximetry and arterial blood gas measures.

CONCLUSIONS: Individual typology angle and melanin index are not strong predictors of the difference in oxygen readings between pulse oximeters and arterial blood gas measurements, even in critically ill patients. The weak fit of all models and the lack of statistical significance indicate that other unmeasured factors may play a more substantial role in explaining the variability.

articles.title: Dysphagia in Patients With High-Flow Nasal Cannulas: Risk and Practice Implications.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is often used in critical care, but its effects on swallowing function remain unclear. Dysphagia in hospitalized patients is associated with complications and prolonged length of stay, yet screening and referral practices vary widely. Limited evidence exists to guide evaluation of dysphagia risk factors among patients receiving HFNC therapy.

OBJECTIVES: To identify patients most at risk for developing dysphagia during HFNC therapy and to examine differences in clinical outcomes based on dysphagia status.

METHODS: This retrospective chart audit reviewed adult inpatients (≥21 years) who received HFNC therapy between 2022 and 2024. Of 1038 eligible patients, 210 were randomly selected for chart audit; 195 were included after exclusions. Data included HFNC settings, dysphagia status, and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: No dose-response relationship was identified between dysphagia and HFNC settings, including flow rate, fraction of inspired oxygen, or duration. Dysphagia during admission was not associated with mortality (all P's > .36) or preexisting dysphagia status (χ2 = 3.7, P = .16). However, patients with dysphagia had longer intensive care unit stays than patients without dysphagia and patients with unknown dysphagia status (P = .04 and P = .09, respectively), and dysphagia status was associated with intubation (χ2 = 13.6, P = .001), with intubation most common among patients with dysphagia.

CONCLUSIONS: This cohort showed no association of HFNC settings with dysphagia status, and no specific triggers were identified to inform standardized dysphagia screening protocols for patients receiving HFNC therapy. Dysphagia was associated with intubation and prolonged intensive care unit stay.

articles.title: Determining the Prevalence of Hospital-Acquired Anemia in the Intensive Care Unit at a Florida Hospital.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital-acquired anemia (HAA), which negatively affects morbidity, mortality, and resource use, is a common iatrogenic effect of hospitalization, especially in intensive care units. Contributing factors include phlebotomy, intravenous fluid resuscitation, and medications.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of HAA among adult patients in a southwest Florida intensive care unit and evaluate the relationship between decline in hemoglobin level and length of intensive care unit stay.

METHODS: A retrospective, exploratory medical record review of a 6-month convenience sample (N = 151) was conducted. Hospital-acquired anemia was defined as a 10% or greater decline in hemoglobin level from admission to discharge.

RESULTS: Of 108 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 69 (64%) developed HAA. Stays were significantly longer for the 69 patients with HAA than for the 39 patients without HAA (mean [SD], 5.9 [5.8] days vs 3.3 [3.6] days; P = .005). The mean (SD) decline in hemoglobin level was 20% (8%) for patients with HAA and 4% (2%) for patients without HAA (P < .001). A sensitivity analysis excluding 6 outliers (n = 102) confirmed that stays were significantly longer for patients with HAA than for patients without HAA (mean [SD], 5.1 [4.2] days vs 2.8 [1.7] days; P < .001).

CONCLUSION: Hospital-acquired anemia is prevalent in this intensive care unit and correlates with longer stays. Although causality regarding phlebotomy was not directly measured, the high prevalence of HAA supports implementing blood conservation strategies to improve clinical outcomes and reduce iatrogenic blood loss.

articles.title: Eco-Conscious Nursing in Critical Care: Nurses' Perspectives and Practices Related to Environmental Sustainability.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses

articles.title: Management of Intensive Care Unit Admission of Patients With Blood Cancer.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with blood cancer are at high risk of complications requiring intensive care. Admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) involves ethical and organizational complexities.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the perspectives of hematologists and intensivists making ICU admission decisions in France.

METHODS: A nationwide survey of French hematologists and intensivists was conducted using clinical vignettes to assess ICU admission criteria. The influence of institutional practices, individual experiences, and cancer status on ICU transfer decisions was explored.

RESULTS: All 174 participating physicians agreed on ICU admission for patients with immediately life-threatening conditions. Although the general principle of early ICU admission was supported by 75% of hematologists and 54% of intensivists, responses to specific clinical scenarios showed that intensivists recommended broader ICU access and earlier involvement, particularly for patients with noncritical but high-risk conditions. Hematologists more often deferred ICU discussions until clinical deterioration had occurred. Structural barriers such as lack of shared protocols, variations in training, and absence of ICU staff members in hematology decision-making contributed to inconsistent practices. Ethical guidelines were underrecognized and unevenly applied. Neither physician group routinely included nurses in discussions despite nurses' critical role in ICU care.

CONCLUSIONS: In France, ICU admission practices for patients with blood cancer vary between hematologists and intensivists. Harmonizing practices through common training, early multidisciplinary discussions, risk assessment models, and improved knowledge of ethical standards is urgently needed. These findings may reflect global challenges in aligning ICU triage with evolving cancer care.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic Pupil Assessment in Patients With Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with severe traumatic brain injury, accurate pupillary assessment is critical for neurological monitoring but is often hindered by periorbital edema, trauma, or dressings that preclude direct visualization.

OBJECTIVE: To validate the feasibility and accuracy of ultrasonographic pupil assessment performed through the closed eyelid as an alternative to direct pupillometry in patients with traumatic brain injury.

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 45 intensive care unit patients (36 male; mean [SD] age, 67.1 [12.9] years). Both direct pupillometry and ultrasonographic pupil assessment were sequentially completed within a 3-minute interval under standardized low-light conditions for both eyes. Direct pupillometry involved video recording of the exposed pupil with a calibrated reference scale. Ultrasonographic pupil assessment was performed by using a high-frequency linear probe placed on the closed eyelid. The primary outcome was the agreement between methods for calculating the percentage of pupillary constriction. Secondary outcomes included agreement on resting and minimum pupil diameters.

RESULTS: Ultrasonographic pupil assessment showed excellent agreement with direct pupillometry for percent pupillary constriction (median [IQR] difference, 0.44% [-2.78% to 2.83%]; Wilcoxon P ≥ .48). Bland-Altman analysis showed narrow limits of agreement. Strong correlations were also noted for resting and minimum pupil diameters (0.6 ≤ r2 ≤ 0.873).

CONCLUSION: Ultrasonographic pupil assessment is a reliable and accurate method for objective pupillary evaluation when direct visualization is obstructed. By enabling quantitative measurement of the pupillary light reflex through the closed eyelid, ultrasonographic pupil assessment addresses an important monitoring gap in the management of patients with severe traumatic brain injury and periorbital swelling.

articles.title: Lower waitlist failure without loss of transplant or exception access after the 2023 pediatric liver allocation update: a national interrupted time-series study.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: The 2023 Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network pediatric medical urgency update revised the Pediatric End-Stage Liver Disease (PELD) calculation, pediatric Status 1A/1B rules, and National Liver Review Board guidance. Using registry data linked to exception records, we performed an interrupted time-series analysis among candidates younger than 12 years listed from January 2019 through December 2024, excluding June-July 2023 as the implementation interval (2,791 registrations; 368,761 person-days). The primary outcome was waitlist death or delisting for clinical deterioration. The update was not associated with an immediate change in this outcome (incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57-2.46), but was associated with a lower post-policy trajectory (slope-change IRR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99; P=0.047). This association attenuated when severity was measured identically in both eras (IRR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.90-1.01; P=0.14). Removal for death was unchanged (0.21 vs 0.20 per 1,000 person-days), whereas removal as too sick to transplant fell (0.21 vs 0.09). Transplant rates, exception request rates, and exception approval probability did not decline. The update was associated with lower severity-adjusted waitlist death/delisting without detectable loss of transplant or exception access; however, era-invariant severity adjustment and component analyses indicate that the magnitude and mechanism of this association remain uncertain.

articles.title: Congenital Ichthyosis.
articles.abstract: See bonus NeoBriefs videos and downloadable teaching slides on this article's homepage Congenital ichthyosis (CI) encompasses a heterogenous group of skin disorders characterized by abnormal epidermal differentiation. Many present in the newborn period, and affected patients are at risk of serious complications. A compromised skin barrier places these infants at risk for transepidermal water loss, temperature dysregulation, compromised limb perfusion, and sepsis. It is important for neonatal clinicians to identify these disorders at birth and to create individualized management plans. This review seeks to summarize the signs of CI in the neonatal period and common management strategies.

articles.title: Green Vaginal Discharge in a Late-Preterm Neonate With Massive Ascites.
articles.abstract: A late-preterm girl (35 + 1 weeks; birth weight 2440 g) was born after preterm labor in the setting of meconium-stained amniotic fluid and a tight body cord. At birth, she presented with abdominal distension and right upper quadrant ecchymosis. Within hours, she developed progressive respiratory distress requiring escalation from continuous positive airway pressure to intubation in the setting of worsening abdominal distension. Gastric decompression yielded bilious fluid, and she was started on intravenous fluids and antibiotics. Initial radiographs demonstrated paucity of bowel gas without pneumoperitoneum or calcifications. After transfer to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit for suspected intra-abdominal pathology, she was pale with sluggish capillary refill and had a tense, distended abdomen with absent bowel sounds. Laboratory evaluation revealed anemia and coagulopathy, and abdominal ultrasonography demonstrated massive ascites with internal debris and abnormal hepatic venous flow. Despite stabilization, abdominal distension progressed over several days. On day of life 4, thin dark-green fluid drained from the vaginal introitus in the setting of otherwise normal external genitalia and anorectal anatomy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

articles.title: Consensus guidelines in the management of paediatric flexible flatfoot : a Delphi study of the British Society of Children's Orthopaedic Surgery.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children is inconsistent, reflecting a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. This study aimed to develop a British Society for Children's Orthopaedic Surgery (BSCOS)-led consensus guideline for the multidisciplinary assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children.

METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus opinion study was conducted among the membership of the BSCOS. A multidisciplinary steering committee developed an initial set of statements based on clinical expertise, current evidence, and recognized variation in practice. A total of 33 statements addressing assessment, conservative, and surgical management were scored over two Delphi rounds using a nine-point Likert scale. Participant responses were anonymized. Consensus was defined prospectively as ≥ 75%. Statements that did not meet the consensus threshold were revised and rescored, or discussed and voted on by the steering committee.

RESULTS: A total of 169 clinicians participated in Round One and 167 in Round Two. Most respondents were consultant orthopaedic surgeons (80%; n = 136), with further representation from registrars/fellows (5%; n = 9), and allied health professionals (AHPs) and advanced nurse practitioners (14%; n = 24). Overall, 24 of 33 statements met the consensus threshold. A further two statements were included following steering committee voting, resulting in 26 final statements. Areas of uncertainty were highlighted in the statements that did not reach consensus, particularly regarding the selection of specific surgical procedures.

CONCLUSION: This national consensus guideline provides a framework for clinicians managing children's flexible flatfoot, establishing a benchmark for future evaluation.

articles.title: Supervised physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises provide limited additional benefit at 24 months in braced adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis: a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE) are used as an adjunct to bracing in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), although evidence for their long-term benefit remains limited. This randomized trial assessed whether supervised PSSE provide clinically important radiological and patient-reported benefits compared with self-directed exercise in patients with AIS undergoing brace treatment.

METHODS: Patients with AIS (major Cobb angle 25° to 45°; Risser grade 0 to 2) were recruited from a tertiary scoliosis centre between December 2018 and December 2022. Patients were randomized to supervised Schroth-based PSSE, consisting of physiotherapist-led sessions plus daily home exercises, or to self-directed general exercise. The co-primary outcomes were change in major Cobb angle and change in health-related quality of life measured using the Chinese Brace Questionnaire-34. A 5° between-group difference in Cobb angle was prespecified as the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). To provide a clinically anchored interpretation, 24-month radiological outcomes were classified as improved (> 5° decrease), stable (-5° to +5°), or worsened (> 5° increase), and compared using adjusted ordinal logistic regression in intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) analyses.

RESULTS: Supervised PSSE resulted in a greater reduction in major Cobb angle than self-directed exercise at 24 months (adjusted between-group difference -3.23° (95% CI -3.51 to -2.96); p < 0.001); however, this did not reach the prespecified MCID. There was no clinically meaningful difference in quality of life. Using the 5° threshold, radiological status was similar between groups. In the intention-to-treat analysis, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for improved/stable/worsened status was 1.08 (95% CI 0.58 to 2.03; p = 0.805); per-protocol findings were similar (OR 1.48 (95% CI 0.75 to 2.92); p = 0.263).

CONCLUSION: Supervised PSSE provided a statistically significant but clinically modest radiological benefit over self-directed exercise. This did not translate into a higher likelihood of clinically meaningful radiological improvement. No sustained clinically meaningful quality-of-life benefit was shown.

articles.title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA).

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

articles.title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Cemented arthroplasty has previously been recommended for treating metastatic bone disease (MBD) around the hip. However, cementing has disadvantages, including restricted femoral component length, loosening due to disease progression, and bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). A long uncemented implant spanning the whole femur could negate these disadvantages; however, there is a paucity of data regarding their use. Our aim was to assess the outcomes of a long uncemented femoral component in MBD.

METHODS: A total of 205 patients with MBD underwent femoral reconstruction using the Restoration Modular Revision Hip System Plasma stem between January 2008 and December 2025. They were identified from the prospectively collected database of a tertiary MBD service. Any patient with symptomatic bone metastases involving the acetabulum or femur, with completed or impending pathological fracture, were included. The primary endpoint was reintervention for femoral implant failure, with exclusion of reintervention for deep infection and/or instability.

RESULTS: Indications for surgery included pathological fracture (46 of 205; 22%) or lesions at risk of fracture (78%; n = 159). The mean follow-up was 45 months (12 to 131). A total of 140 patients (68%) died during the study period (mean 20 months (0.1 to 128) postoperatively). The mean distance from the centre of the femoral head to the most distal femoral metastasis was 126 mm (5 to 369). Using death as a competing risk, two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and probability of death was 0.507 (95% CI 0.436 to 0.577). At five years, probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and the risk of death was 0.703 (95% CI 0.629 to 0.776). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205) with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure (all periprosthetic femoral fractures).

CONCLUSION: This implant demonstrates promising short- to mid-term survivorship, with no patient requiring femoral revision for loosening and a comparatively low complication rate. A long uncemented femoral component may be an appropriate option in selected patients presenting with symptomatic bone metastases around the hip.

articles.title: The diagnostic value of quantitative 99mTc-MDP SPECT/CT fusion imaging in the differential diagnosis of spinal infections.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the value of quantitative 99mTc-labelled methylene diphosphonate (99mTc-MDP) single-photon emission CT (SPECT)/CT fusion imaging in the differential diagnosis of spinal infections.

METHODS: A total of 90 patients with confirmed spinal infections, prior to any clinical treatment, underwent 99mTc-MDP SPECT/CT fusion imaging. The maximum, mean, and minimum standardized uptake values (SUVmax, SUVmean, SUVmin), bone metabolic volume (MBV), total bone uptake (TBU), and CT Hounsfield unit (HU) values were measured in both affected and normal vertebrae. Multidimensional comparisons of SPECT/CT parameters were performed, including within-subject analyses comparing affected and adjacent normal vertebrae in the same infection type, as well as inter-group comparisons across different types of spinal infections. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to determine the area under the curve (AUC) and optimal cut-off values, while the linear associations between quantitative SPECT/CT parameters of affected vertebrae and laboratory biomarkers were evaluated.

RESULTS: The median SUVmax of affected vertebrae in pyogenic spondylitis (PS) was 21.17 (IQR 17.19 to 22.01), significantly higher than that observed in spinal tuberculosis (STB) (17.57 (IQR 15.02 to 18.98)) and brucellar spondylitis (BS) (15.63 (IQR 14.28 to 16.90)). SUVmax demonstrated strong diagnostic performance in differentiating PS from BS, with an AUC of 0.852, yielding 95.0% sensitivity and 71.7% specificity at an optimal cut-off value of 18.51. Similarly, CT HU values showed moderate discriminative ability for distinguishing BS from STB, achieving an AUC of 0.741, with 80.0% sensitivity and 65.0% specificity at a cut-off of 706 HU. Furthermore, a strong positive correlation was observed between SUVmax and CT HU values across all three infection groups. In addition, SUVmax exhibited a significant positive correlation with serum inflammatory markers in patients with PS.

CONCLUSION: Quantitative 99mTc-MDP SPECT/CT fusion imaging enables objective assessment of spinal infection severity, thereby facilitating the differential diagnosis of distinct aetiological types of spondylitis.

articles.title: A Structured Approach to Teaching Volumetric Fetal Echocardiography Using Fetal Intelligent Navigation Echocardiography (FINE).
articles.abstract: Fetal volumetric echocardiography using Fetal Intelligent Navigation Echocardiography (FINE) enables automated reconstruction of standardized echocardiographic views from a cardiac volume dataset. However, automation of navigation does not eliminate dependence on technically adequate acquisition or the need for operator quality control. We describe the PROBE Educational Workflow, a structured educational approach comprising five sequential steps-Position, Refine, Obtain, Build and Evaluate-designed to organize the teaching of the process from preparation of the two-dimensional image and acquisition of the Spatio-Temporal Image Correlation (STIC) volume to construction of the navigation and systematic assessment of the reconstructed views. PROBE was conceived as an iterative workflow: when the quality of a step is considered insufficient, the operator should identify the probable origin of the problem and return to the corresponding step before proceeding. The workflow does not modify the FINE algorithm and does not constitute a diagnostic protocol; its purpose is to provide a simple and reproducible cognitive framework for technical training in volumetric fetal echocardiography. Future studies should assess its impact on competency acquisition, volume quality, reproducibility and training efficiency.

articles.title: S1P receptors in ulcerative colitis: spotlight on etrasimod.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a rising global incidence. Small molecules have transformed the treatment of UC. Specifically, sphingosine‑1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulators are a newly available and expanding therapeutic option for patients with UC.

AREAS COVERED: This review analyzes the biology, efficacy, and safety of S1P receptor modulators. A literature search in PubMed regarding clinical studies published up to 1 June  2026, involving S1P receptor modulators in UC was analyzed. Clinical trial data and real-world evidence for approved S1P receptor modulators (ozanimod and etrasimod) and investigational agents (tamuzimod, mocravimod, and amiselimod) in UC treatment were gathered. Ozanimod and etrasimod both demonstrated superior efficacy over placebo in moderately to severely active UC. Both agents showed greater efficacy in biologic-naïve patients compared with biologic-exposed populations. Meta-analyses favored S1P receptor modulators over other UC therapies, particularly for inducing histologic improvement. Commonly reported adverse effects of S1P receptor modulators include elevated liver enzymes and transient asymptomatic bradycardia. Serious adverse events, including macular edema and severe infections, are rare, with infection rates comparable to those of placebo in the clinical trials.

EXPERT OPINION: S1P receptor modulators represent a new and promising oral class of treatment for UC, showing effective results with a manageable safety profile. They are especially beneficial for patients with moderate disease severity and serve as an important option for those transitioning from traditional to advanced therapies. Although these agents have some unique safety concerns, most are mild and reversible.

articles.title: Intranuclear localisation of KLF3-AS1 under the balance of histone acetylation and methylation in BMSCs ameliorates cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischaemic stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is obstructed. Rapid restoration of blood supply frequently induces cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury (CIRI). Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)-derived exosomes exhibit promising therapeutic potential for CIRI. In-depth exploration of their therapeutic mechanisms holds crucial significance for CIRI management.

METHODS: The middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO) model was established in mice. An in vitro ischaemic stroke model was established by treating BV-2 cells with oxygen‒glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Exosomes were isolated from BMSCs and intranasally administrated into mice or added into BV-2 cells. Neurological deficits, grasping and coordination function were evaluated. Cell viability, apoptosis, proliferation and migration were examined. The localisation of KLF3-AS1 was examined by combined staining of immunofluorescence and fluorescence in situ hybridisation. Intracellular Ca2+ and adenosine triphosphate levels, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and membrane potential were assessed.

RESULTS: KLF3-AS1 enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation and migration, accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming at its promoter characterised by increased H3K27 acetylation (H3K27Ac) and decreased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27Me3). BMSC-derived KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes indicated therapeutic efficacy in both in vivo and in vitro models of cerebral ischaemia. In MCAO-induced mice, these exosomes alleviated neurological deficits and shifted microglial polarisation from pro-inflammatory M1-like to anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotypes. Similar effects were observed in OGD/R-treated BV-2 microglia, where KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes attenuated oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction while upregulating Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3) expression. Mechanistically, KLF3-AS1 facilitated ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) nuclear translocation to activate SIRT3 transcription in microglia, and inhibition of SIRT3 abolished the neuroprotective effects of exosomal KLF3-AS1.

CONCLUSION: BMSC-derived exosomes delivering KLF3-AS1 ameliorates CIRI by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation, highlighting KLF3-AS1 as a critical epigenetic regulator and exosome-mediated therapeutic agent for CIRI through the ETV4/SIRT3 axis.

KEY POINTS/HIGHLIGHTS: KLF3-AS1 enhances bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) function via promoter H3K27Ac/H3K27Me3 reprogramming. KLF3‑AS1 directly binds ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) to activate Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3), preserving mitochondrial integrity. BMSC‑derived exosomal KLF3‑AS1 promotes M2 microglial polarisation and ameliorates cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Timing of Cardiac Contractility Modulation Therapy Implementation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Symptomatic chronic heart failure (HF) despite medical treatment can be addressed with cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) therapy, which has yet to have been investigated regarding outcome differences between early versus late implementation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: CCM recipients from the Mannheim Cardiac Contractility Modulation Observational Registry (MAINTAINED) aged ≤ 70 years at implantation were grouped with regard to implantation time after the first diagnosis of CCM indicating HF (New York Heart Association classification (NYHA) ≥ 2 and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) = 25%-45%) into either Early- (EC, n = 50, implantation < 13 months after diagnosis) or Late-Implantation Group (LC, n = 81, implantation ≥ 13 months after diagnosis). Both groups were compared regarding survival, NYHA, LVEF, and HF-related hospitalizations for up to 60 months. The mean implantation time after the first diagnosis were 5.85 ± 3.1 versus 92 ± 70.2 months (first values EC, p < 0.05). Mean survival was better for EC (55.2 ± 1.7 vs. 52.8 ± 1.6 months, p < 0.05). Improvements in NYHA (2.98 ± 0.47 to 2.0 ± 0.73 vs. 3.01 ± 0.46 to 2.25 ± 0.8, both p < 0.05) and LVEF (23.2 ± 7.5 to ± 38.82 ± 12.85 vs. 23.9 ± 7 to 29.92 ± 8.9%, each p < 0.05) were comparable, with differences in terms of grouping. Hospitalizations due to HF were more frequent to LC patients (39 vs. 110 events, Odds Ratio 2.1).

CONCLUSIONS: Heart failure patients might experience improvements in functional status and left ventricular reverse remodeling following CCM therapy, regardless of the timing of implantation. Early implementation of CCM within the first year of CCM suitable HF might provide additional benefits regarding survival, left ventricular systolic recovery and protection against heart failure hospitalizations.

articles.title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Predicts Recurrent Myocardial Infarction in Diabetic Patients Following Acute Coronary Syndromes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who experience acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events despite secondary prevention. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] contributes to residual cardiovascular risk, but its prognostic impact on recurrent myocardial infarction (MI) and repeat revascularization in diabetic patients after ACS or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.

HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that elevated Lp(a) is associated with increased risk of recurrent MI and repeat coronary revascularization in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, EBSCOhost, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies evaluating Lp(a) and recurrent cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI. Observational studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were included. Pooled HRs were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Seven studies comprising 7887 patients with diabetes and prior ACS or PCI were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with increased risk of recurrent MI (pooled HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.02-4.62; I2 = 75%) but not repeat coronary revascularization (pooled HR 1.68, 95% CI 0.79-3.57; I2 = 78%).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with increased risk of recurrent MI in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI. Findings should be interpreted considering the observational study designs, substantial heterogeneity, and limited evidence for repeat revascularization. These findings support Lp(a) as a contributor to residual cardiovascular risk and its potential role in post-ACS risk stratification.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420261296821).

articles.title: Right Ventricular Dysfunction and Ventriculo-Arterial Uncoupling in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Phenotype-Specific Review of Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of all global heart failure cases. Historically viewed as a left-centric diastolic disorder, emerging evidence identifies right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and impaired ventriculo-arterial (RV-PA) coupling as central drivers of exercise intolerance, functional decline, and adverse clinical outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiological mechanisms, advanced diagnostic modalities, prognostic implications, and phenotype-specific therapies for RV dysfunction in HFpEF, advocating for a transition to systematic biventricular evaluation.

METHODS: A structured, PRISMA-informed search of PubMed and Scopus (2015-2024) identified 74 eligible studies evaluating RV structure, function, and hemodynamics in HFpEF cohorts.

RESULTS: RV dysfunction is prevalent in 19% to 33% of HFpEF patients and independently predicts all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations. Key pathophysiological drivers include post-capillary pulmonary hypertension, impaired RV lusitropy, systemic inflammation, and inter-ventricular dependence. Non-invasive markers notably speckle-tracking echocardiography, 4D-flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and the TAPSE/PASP ratio enable early identification of subclinical RV-PA uncoupling. While traditional heart failure therapies show limited efficacy, emerging options including SGLT2 inhibitors, interatrial shunt devices, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and targeted pulmonary vasodilators demonstrate potential to preserve RV strain and restore hemodynamics across distinct clinical phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: RV dysfunction is a major prognostic marker in HFpEF. Routine inclusion of RV-PA coupling indices in diagnostic and risk-stratification algorithms is essential to guide precision-based, phenotype-guided management and improve clinical trajectories.

articles.title: An Evaluation of ICU Follow-Up Clinic Attendance and Subsequent Healthcare Resource Utilization in Wales, United Kingdom: A Retrospective, Population-Level Data-Linkage Study.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postintensive care syndrome encapsulates the long-term physical, psychologic, and cognitive impairments often seen among ICU survivors. Post-ICU follow-up clinics may support recovery and reduce avoidable healthcare utilization, but population-level evidence remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: To identify patient characteristics associated with follow-up clinic attendance and evaluate differences in healthcare resource utilization (HRU) across three groups: invited and attended, invited but did not attend, and not invited.

DESIGN SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: A retrospective cohort study using anonymised, linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank in Wales, United Kingdom. Adults (≥ 18 yr) with ICU admissions between 2016 and 2023 who survived to discharge were included. Follow-up clinic data were obtained from three regional health boards (healthcare organizations responsible for delivering National Health Services in Wales) with follow-up clinic availability.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: HRU outcomes included ICU readmissions, emergency department attendances, hospital admissions (elective and emergency), hospital bed days, outpatient appointments, and general practitioner (GP) events. Multivariable models assessed associations between clinic attendance and HRU.

RESULTS: Of 6491 eligible patients, 761 attended a follow-up clinic, 1473 were invited but did not attend, and 4257 were not invited. Among invited patients, attendance was associated with increasing age, comorbidity, deprivation, and ICU length of stay. Compared with attendees, nonattendees and those not invited had higher adjusted odds of ICU readmission (odds ratio [OR] = 2.81 and 2.22, respectively), elective admissions, and hospital bed days. No significant differences were observed for emergency admissions or GP events. Attendees were more likely to have 4 or more (non-follow-up clinic) outpatient appointments.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Clinic attendance was associated with differences in several HRU domains. Variability in access and engagement suggests potential inequalities in post‑ICU recovery pathways. Standardizing referral practices and expanding clinic availability may improve outcomes for ICU survivors.

articles.title: Small-Bowel Obstruction due to AA Amyloidosis in Presumed Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: AA amyloidosis is rare in resource-rich settings, but remains prevalent in regions with untreated infection, particularly tuberculosis. We describe a case in Australia of a 68-year-old Somali-born woman with recurrent small-bowel obstruction, weight loss, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. While colonoscopy was macroscopically normal, small-bowel biopsies revealed Congo red-positive AA amyloidosis. Lymph-node biopsy showed histiocytes with granulomatous inflammation, and tuberculosis testing was negative. Given epidemiologic factors and chronic inflammation, culture-negative tuberculosis with AA amyloidosis sequelae was presumed. Empirical tuberculous treatment led to clinical improvement and resolution of PET-avid lymphadenopathy, highlighting an unusual case of infiltrative small-bowel disease.

articles.title: Pharmacological Interventions for Osteoporosis in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
RATIONAL & OBJECTIVE: Osteoporosis is a common complication after kidney transplantation and contributes to fracture risk and morbidity among kidney transplant recipients (KTRs). However, the efficacy of pharmacological interventions for osteoporosis in this population remains uncertain.

STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: KTRs.

SELECTION CRITERIA FOR STUDIES: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through December 2024 for randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatments' effects on bone turnover markers, bone mineral density (BMD), and fracture incidence in KTRs.

DATA EXTRACTION: Three independent reviewers extracted study characteristics, type of pharmacological interventions and comparators, and outcomes, including bone turnover markers, BMD, and fracture rates.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: A random-effects model was used to calculate weighted mean differences (WMD) for continuous outcomes and relative risks for categorical outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 33 randomized controlled trials (2,623 KTRs) were included in this meta-analysis. Pharmacological treatment was not associated with significant changes in parathyroid hormone, bone alkaline phosphatase, and osteocalcin levels. In subgroup analysis, only active vitamin D showed a significant reduction in parathyroid hormone levels (WMD -25.18 pg/mL [-32.59 to -17.77]). Interestingly, pharmacological therapy significantly improved BMD at lumbar spine (WMD 0.04 g/cm2 [0.00 to 0.08]; P = 0.04), radius (WMD 0.14 g/cm2 [0.08-0.19]; P < 0.001), and femoral neck (WMD 0.05 g/cm2 [0.03-0.07]; P < 0.001). However, no significant improvement in BMD was observed at the hip (WMD 0.03 g/cm2 [-0.01 to 0.07]; P = 0.12). Furthermore, there was no statistically significant reduction in fracture risk (RR 0.38 [0.14-1.01]; P = 0.05).

LIMITATIONS: Significant clinical and statistical heterogeneity (I2) because of varied pharmacological agents, initiation timing, and recipient characteristics.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacological interventions for osteoporosis in KTRs significantly improved BMD at several skeletal sites, particularly radius site. However, a nonsignificant trend toward reduced fracture incidence was observed.

articles.title: Clinical Application of Hemadsorption in Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients: An Adapted English Republication of the Chinese HA-MHD Consensus.
authors: Nephrology Branch of the Shanghai Medical Association and the 2025 HA–MHD Consensus Working Group
articles.abstract: The accumulation of protein-bound uremic toxins and middle- to large-molecular-weight toxins in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) results in long-term complications. Hemadsorption (HA) can efficiently remove these uremic toxins and reduce the risk of long-term complications in MHD patients. The Chinese HA-MHD Consensus Working Group has revised and updated the 2021 Shanghai Expert Consensus on the Clinical Application of Haemoadsorption in Maintenance Haemodialysis Patients to further standardize clinical application of HA and reflect the latest evidence. Based on an extensive literature search, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework, and the modified Delphi method, the working group formulated 27 evidence-based recommendations regarding patient populations, session frequency, treatment modalities, precautions, and adverse reactions. This consensus systematically delineates the clinical thresholds and rationales for utilizing HA across three core dimensions: routine treatment regimens, intensive treatment regimens, and long-term complication risk management to provide comprehensive guidance. Furthermore, the consensus provides detailed guidance on individualized operational parameters to maximize both safety and treatment efficacy. This consensus aims to provide the latest guiding opinions for the rational and standardized application of HA therapy in patients receiving MHD.

articles.title: Drug Rescue for Paxlovid-Induced Tacrolimus Toxicity: A Pooled Analysis of Case Reports.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Despite case reports suggesting the use of cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) inducers for the treatment of Paxlovid-induced tacrolimus (TAC) toxicity, systematic validation is lacking. This study aimed to investigate whether inducers (rifampin or phenytoin) could reduce TAC concentrations and restore renal function more effectively and safely than drug withdrawal alone.

STUDY DESIGN: A case report and a pooled analysis of case reports registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251138667).

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: The patients presented, and 51 individual patients from 41 publications were categorized into drug rescue (n=23) and natural recovery (n=29) groups.

SEARCH STRATEGY & SOURCES: Case reports and series were identified from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Chinese databases (from January 1, 2020, to December 1, 2025), with a primary search strategy of "(Tacrolimus OR FK506) AND (Ritonavir OR Paxlovid OR "Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir").

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Kaplan-Meier curves and directed acyclic graph-informed multivariable linear regression analysis.

RESULTS: In a posttransplant female, Paxlovid-induced supratherapeutic TAC levels resolved within 2 days of rifampin initiation, and acute kidney injury recovered within 3 days. Pooled analysis showed that, compared with natural recovery, drug rescue therapy demonstrated significantly faster recoveries of TAC (median, 4.0 vs 6.0 days; log-rank P < 0.001) and serum creatinine (SCr; median, 3.0 vs 7.0 days; P = 0.024) levels. Drug rescue was independently associated with a 2.6-day (P < 0.001) shorter recovery time for TAC levels and a 4.0-day (P = 0.043) shorter recovery time for SCr levels. Rifampin and phenytoin showed no significant difference in the recovery time for TAC or SCr levels. No serious adverse events or secondary toxicity were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: CYP3A4 inducers were significantly associated with accelerated TAC clearance and renal recovery in patients with Paxlovid-induced TAC toxicity and appeared safe for clinical use.

articles.title: Food Insecurity and Academic Performance among Postsecondary Students: A Global Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Food insecurity is increasingly recognized as a significant public health concern among postsecondary students worldwide. Emerging evidence suggests that inadequate access to food may negatively affect academic success; however, the scope and consistency of this relationship have not been comprehensively synthesized. This scoping review aimed to systematically identify, map, and summarize the existing literature on the relationship between food insecurity and academic performance among postsecondary students worldwide. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Six electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and ERIC) were searched from inception to November 2025. Eligibility criteria were defined using the Population, Concept, Context framework. Data were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Of 3078 records identified, 86 studies met the inclusion criteria, including 67 quantitative studies, 11 qualitative studies, and 8 mixed-methods studies. Most studies were conducted in the United States (n = 69). Across study designs, food insecurity was consistently associated with poorer academic outcomes, including lower grade point average, reduced academic achievement, impaired concentration, lower class attendance and engagement, increased course withdrawal and failure, delayed graduation, and lower educational attainment. Several studies identified anxiety, depression, psychological undefined distress, sleep disturbances, and financial strain as potential mechanisms linking food insecurity to academic performance. Qualitative evidence highlighted students' experiences of hunger, fatigue, stress, competing financial demands, and work-study disagreement as barriers to academic success. The available evidence consistently indicates that food insecurity is associated with poorer academic performance among postsecondary students. Addressing food insecurity is a strategic opportunity to support student success, retention, and educational attainment. Additional longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to strengthen causal inference and identify effective approaches to improving both food security and academic outcomes in higher education settings.

articles.title: Drug Dosing in Chronic Kidney Disease: Comparison of Standardized eGFR and eGFR Adjusted for Body Surface Area.
Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis in a Patient With Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic Challenges.
articles.abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome with nonspecific clinical manifestations that can mimic common conditions in patients with alcohol dependence. Early clinical suspicion and rapid initiation of treatment are essential to prevent fatal outcomes.

articles.title: Severe Thrombocytopenia Induced by Re-Exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam: A Case Report in Critically Ill Patient With COVID-19.
articles.abstract: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia is a condition where certain medications can significantly reduce the platelets in the blood. This can increase the risk of bleeding and bruising. We reported a case of a 73-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities who was admitted to the hospital with COVID-19. Upon admission, the patient received multiple antibiotics, including Piperacillin/Tazobactam. In the following days, she developed severe thrombocytopenia upon re-exposure to Piperacillin/Tazobactam. Other causes of thrombocytopenia were systematically excluded. After discontinuing the Piperacillin/Tazobactam and administering intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), the thrombocytopenia resolved. A Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score was calculated and indicated a probable (i.e., 6 points) adverse drug reaction. This case underscores the importance of considering Piperacillin/Tazobactam as a potential cause of severe thrombocytopenia in critically ill patients, even in the presence of confounding factors such as COVID-19. To our knowledge, this is a rarely reported presentation in a patient with a recent COVID-19 infection. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between COVID-19 and drug-induced thrombocytopenia.

articles.title: Neutrophil fate in bone infection: Mechanisms, microenvironment, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: The clinical challenge of eradicating bone infection stems from microbial persistence within a distinct skeletal niche that is poorly perfused, hypoxic, mineralised, and highly susceptible to collateral damage. Neutrophils are central arbiters of this process and function as a double-edged sword: they are indispensable for initial pathogen containment, yet can become major drivers of chronic osteolysis, biofilm persistence, and inflammation when their effector programmes turn maladaptive. Recent high-resolution single-cell and spatial analyses have overturned the traditional view of neutrophils as short-lived, homogeneous cells, instead revealing a complex spectrum of functional states shaped by the infected bone microenvironment. In this Review, we use a neutrophil fate framework that distinguishes three related but non-equivalent levels: irreversible terminal fates, non-terminal tissue-disposition states and outcomes, and upstream fate-biasing states or processes. Terminal fates include apoptosis with subsequent efferocytic clearance, suicidal NETosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, mitochondrial permeability transition-driven necrosis, and secondary necrosis.
