By contrast, non-lytic (vital) NET release is considered an effector process rather than a terminal fate. Reverse migration is treated as a non-terminal tissue-exit outcome, whereas inflammatory retention is considered a non-terminal persistence state. Upstream fate-biasing factors include phenotypic or activation states, such as cellular ageing, NET-prone activation, and apoptosis delay, as well as regulatory processes including autophagy and metabolic or redox stress; none of these is classified as an independent terminal fate. We further examine how these terminal fates, non-terminal tissue-disposition states and outcomes, and upstream fate-biasing states and processes are spatially organised across osteomyelitic lesions and biofilm-associated interfaces, and how they govern interactions with osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and macrophages to determine the balance between antimicrobial control and progressive skeletal destruction. We also discuss emerging therapeutic paradigms aimed not at broadly suppressing neutrophil recruitment, but at precisely redirecting neutrophil fate, thereby providing a conceptual basis for stage-specific immunomodulation in orthopaedic infection. The Translational Potential of this Article This Review provides a fate-based framework for understanding how neutrophils shape the balance between pathogen control, biofilm persistence, osteolysis, and tissue repair in orthopaedic infection. By linking neutrophil fate programmes to distinct lesion microenvironments, including osteomyelitic lesions, implant-associated biofilms, contiguous soft-tissue infection, and fracture-related infection, this article highlights potential translational opportunities for stage- and compartment-specific immune modulation. These include improving patient stratification, guiding the timing of surgical source control and implant retention or removal, optimising dead-space management and local antimicrobial delivery, supporting vascularised soft-tissue reconstruction, and developing biomarkers that distinguish protective antimicrobial neutrophil responses from destructive inflammatory persistence. This framework may help shift future orthopaedic infection management from nonspecific suppression of inflammation toward precision redirection of maladaptive neutrophil fate while preserving early host defence and tissue repair capacity.

articles.title: Defining the clinical benefits of disease-modifying therapy in people living with spinal muscular atrophy who require permanent ventilation: a UK-based modified Delphi consensus process.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare inherited neuromuscular disorder that may require permanent ventilation (PV) in severe cases. Although disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) have transformed outcomes for many, prior to this research, access in the UK was restricted for patients receiving PV (SMA-PV). This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations on DMT use and to define clinical benefit in SMA-PV.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary UK-based expert panel conducted a modified Delphi consensus process between 08 April and 09 June 2025. Draft statements informed by published evidence and expert insights were anonymously voted on for up to three rounds, with consensus defined as ≥75% agreement. Statements not achieving consensus were revised and re-evaluated. Input from a non-voting patient advisory panel (PAP) was also considered. The study was not prospectively registered.

FINDINGS: Excluding the Chair, 18 participants evaluated 22 statements across seven thematic areas specific to SMA-PV: DMT access; treatment initiation; treatment monitoring; defining clinical benefit; functional outcomes; quality of life (QoL); and future research priorities. All 22 statements achieved consensus after two voting rounds (100% participation; agreement range 89-100%). Two statements were revised and re-voted in round 2: one after narrowly missing consensus (72% agreement) and the other to incorporate PAP feedback despite achieving 100% agreement in round 1. The panel agreed that PV alone should not preclude access to DMTs and that trial access with personalised treatment goals may be appropriate. The panel also emphasised broader definitions of clinical benefit, including subtle changes in function and QoL, alongside sensitive assessment approaches and harmonised outcome measurement.

INTERPRETATION: These consensus-based recommendations support careful reconsideration of treatment exclusions for patients with SMA-PV and more inclusive, patient-centred approaches to evaluating treatment benefit.

FUNDING: Roche Products Ltd.

articles.title: Persistent COVID-19 Symptoms in General Population and Healthcare Workers: Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: COVID-19 can cause persistent symptoms that continue after the infection, condition known as long COVID. This study aimed to identify the prevalence of persistent signs and symptoms of COVID-19 in individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and among healthcare workers.

METHODS: This is a systematic review with meta-analysis guided by PRISMA and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023460632). Cohort studies with a minimum follow-up of 12 weeks after COVID-19 infection were included. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Scielo, and LILACS/BVS databases and gray literature, in November 2023. Rayyan was used for article selection, and pooled prevalence meta-analysis for each symptom was conducted in R. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: A total of 2,456 studies were identified, with 59 articles included in the systematic review and 58 in the meta-analysis, comprising 196,863 participants. The symptoms with the highest pooled prevalence (95% CI) were fatigue (0.29[0.24-0.36], 95% PI: 0.05-0.78) and dyspnea (0.16[0.12-0.22], 95% PI: 0.01-0.71).

CONCLUSION: Healthcare workers showed lower prevalence rates for some persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, cough, taste changes, and gastrointestinal symptoms) than the general population. Most studies were of fair quality. Despite the findings of a high prevalence of persistent symptoms, high heterogeneity remained a key limitation.

articles.title: All-cause mortality in people with type 2 diabetes and lipodystrophy-like metabolic phenotype.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We wanted to investigate whether the lipodystrophy (LD)-like phenotype increases mortality in type 2 diabetes. To this end we first developed and confirmed the triglyceride/BMI ratio (TBR index) as an inexpensive and widely available marker of the LD-like metabolic phenotype. The TBR index was then tested for association with all-cause mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Associations between TBR and mortality were assessed by Cox in 3 type 2 diabetes cohorts (n = 2137, n = 960, and n = 5060). A 20-SNP genotype risk score (GRS), associated with LD-like phenotype was investigated to identify the molecular basis of TBR variability.

MAIN FINDING: In all cohorts, the highest TBR decile showed features of LD-like phenotype, including atherogenic dyslipidemia, lower BMI, worse glycemic control, insulin resistance, elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase, and hypoadiponectinemia. In the meta-analysis, decile 10 had higher mortality risk (HR = 1.46, P < .0001). Finally, in a subset of 1 of the 3 cohorts, the LD-like GRS was significantly associated with TBR.

CONCLUSION: The TBR is a novel, inexpensive and easily available marker that identifies a subgroup of type 2 diabetes patients with a LD-like phenotype, partly explained by genetic factors. Our findings help disentangle the heterogeneity of death risk in diabetes, refine diagnostic and follow-up algorithms and enable specific treatments for improving long-term outcomes in LD-like individuals.

articles.title: The lungs in Alström syndrome: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alström syndrome (AS) is a rare multisystemic disorder frequently associated with respiratory complications, which are a major cause of premature death. While fibrosis in multiple organs has been historically suggested as a hallmark of AS, including the lungs, definitive evidence in adult patients remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients diagnosed as AS seen in our National Multidisciplianry AS clinic from 2010 to 2024. Lung function test and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax was performed in a subset of patients. Postmortem lung tissue analysis was available from four patients.

FINDINGS: A total of 25/41 (61%) of the patients were unable to complete full lung function testing. Among those who did, 67% exhibited reduced lung volumes, with 47% showing decreased diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide but normal or elevated transfer coefficient for carbon monoxide, indicating extrapulmonary restrictive physiology. HRCT scans in 39 patients showed no evidence of diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis; however, breathing artefacts were common. Historical infantile cardiomyopathy was identified as a risk factor for adult pulmonary dysfunction. Post-mortem pathology reports were obtained from four patients and no diffuse fibrosis in the lung tissue was identified in any of the patients. Pulmonary hypertension and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome were identified as potential causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality, despite the absence of intrinsic interstitial lung disease.

INTERPRETATION: This is the first large cohort study to depict the lung in adult patients with AS. This study provides no evidence for diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis in adult patients with AS, challenging prior assumptions. Pulmonary dysfunction appears mainly due to extrapulmonary restrictive physiology, with infantile cardiomyopathy as a possible risk factor. Pulmonary hypertension and acute respiratory distress syndrome, rather than intrinsic lung disease, likely underlie respiratory morbidity and mortality, highlighting the need for focused cardiopulmonary care. Although this study represents one of the largest single-centre cohorts of patients with AS reported to date, the overall sample size remains limited due to the ultra-rare nature of the disease and findings should be interpreted with caution.

FUNDING: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

articles.title: Effect of Melatonin on 24-Hour Urinary Protein Excretion and Sleep Quality in Patients With Stage 3-4 Chronic Kidney Disease: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Proteinuria is an established marker of renal injury and is closely associated with adverse outcomes in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Melatonin has attracted interest as a potential renoprotective agent because of its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and regulatory effects on several pathways implicated in kidney injury. However, clinical data regarding its effects on proteinuria in patients with non-dialysis CKD are limited. This trial investigated whether melatonin supplementation alters 24-h urinary protein excretion in adults with stage 3-4 CKD.

METHODS: We conducted a 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in adults with stage 3-4 CKD and persistent proteinuria. Seventy-three participants were allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive either oral melatonin (3 mg at bedtime) or a matching placebo. The prespecified primary endpoint was the change in 24-h urinary protein excretion between baseline and week 12. Secondary assessments included renal function, blood pressure, sleep quality, metabolic and laboratory parameters, and treatment safety.

RESULTS: A reduction in 24-h urinary protein excretion was observed in both treatment groups. The mean reduction was 52.45 ± 128.19 mg/day with melatonin and 28.69 ± 82.59 mg/day with placebo, yielding a between-group difference of -23.76 mg/day (95% CI, -74.08 to 26.56; p = 0.92). Serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate remained largely stable during follow-up. Compared with placebo, melatonin was associated with a significant reduction in total cholesterol. Sleep quality also showed a statistically significant difference in the change in PSQI score between groups, with mean changes of -0.18 ± 0.84 and -0.69 ± 1.06 in the melatonin and placebo groups, respectively (p = 0.047). No treatment-related serious adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: In adults with stage 3-4 CKD, 12 weeks of melatonin supplementation at 3 mg nightly did not demonstrate a clinically meaningful reduction in 24-h urinary protein excretion compared with placebo. Although the point estimate favored melatonin, the confidence interval was compatible with both a modest benefit and no treatment effect. Melatonin was generally well tolerated and was associated with modest changes in selected metabolic and sleep-related outcomes. Larger, multicenter trials with longer follow-up and adequate statistical power are needed to determine whether melatonin has clinically relevant renal effects in specific CKD populations. Trial Registration: This clinical trial was registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT No. IRCT20160412027346N12).

articles.title: Recognizing a duplicated inferior vena cava during radical nephrectomy for papillary renal cell carcinoma: A case report.
articles.abstract: Duplication of the inferior vena cava (DIVC) is a rare congenital venous anomaly with important implications during retroperitoneal surgery. A 40-year-old man presented with 3-month hematuria and mild left flank pain. CT revealed a 7-cm left renal mass, pulmonary and osseous lesions, and two separate IVC channels near the aortic bifurcation. PET/CT confirmed DIVC and suspected metastases. Open radical nephrectomy with lymph-node dissection was performed without vascular injury. Histopathology showed papillary renal cell carcinoma, ISUP grade 3, confined to the renal capsule. This case highlights the importance of recognizing DIVC before renal surgery.

articles.title: Hyperdominant Left Circumflex Artery Challenging Conventional Paradigms and Current Guideline Recommendations: A Comprehensive Literature Review and Case Series.
articles.abstract: Despite its rarity in the general population, left dominant coronary circulation with a hyperdominant left circumflex artery (LCx) has been associated with a more severe risk for ischemic and coronary artery disease. The concealment of an isolated posterior myocardial infarction (IPMI) on a standard 12-lead ECG among these patients with distinctive coronary anatomy can be concerning, especially when clinicians become trapped within conventional guideline-based diagnostic criteria, a circumstance that may ultimately be linked to a poorer prognosis. We present two cases that posed unique diagnostic challenges in this specific anatomical context. Case 1: A 63-year-old man presented to the emergency department (ED) with typical anginal chest pain and severe fatigue. Although the patient was initially diagnosed with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), eventually a catastrophic occlusion of the left posterior descending artery (PDA) in the setting of a hyperdominant LCx was seen during coronary angiography (CAG). Case 2: A 69-year-old man arrived at the ED with typical angina, described as pressure-like. Although the serial 12-lead ECGs were completely normal, given the clinical context, the patient underwent an immediate invasive strategy in < 2 h. CAG revealed complete occlusion of the ostio-proximal segment of the left PDA. In both cases, hyperdominant LCx anatomy created a diagnostic blind spot within the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI paradigm, because the infarct territory was insufficiently captured by standard ECG criteria and failed to trigger guideline-based use of posterior leads or adjunctive imaging, thereby obscuring the diagnosis of IPMI. These cases warn clinicians about the diagnostic complexity of IPMI in a hyperdominant LCx setting. In such cases, ECG findings can be ambiguous or even completely absent, and the clinical presentation may not meet current unclear guideline-based indications for adjunctive diagnostic assessment, leading to delayed recognition of high-risk ischemia, particularly IPMI.

articles.title: Adipsic Hypernatremia Complicated by Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State and Extensive Venous Thromboembolism After Traumatic Brain Injury: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Adipsic hypernatremia is a rare disorder characterized by impaired thirst perception despite severe hyperosmolality, most commonly resulting from hypothalamic dysfunction. Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS) may further aggravate dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, increasing the risk of neurologic injury, acute kidney injury (AKI), and thromboembolic complications. Reports describing the coexistence of adipsic hypernatremia, HHS, and extensive venous thromboembolism are limited. A 42-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes and recent traumatic brain injury presented with neurologic decline, severe dehydration without thirst, severe hypernatremia, HHS, and transient renal dysfunction consistent with prerenal injury. Persistent severe hypernatremia despite improvement in hyperglycemia, together with preserved urinary concentrating ability, supported adipsic hypernatremia. Further evaluation revealed extensive deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary embolism (PE), while brain imaging showed only mild diffuse cerebral atrophy. The patient was treated with controlled volume and free-water replacement, intravenous insulin therapy, anticoagulation, and close monitoring of serum sodium, glucose, renal function, and urine output. Gradual correction of hypernatremia resulted in significant improvement in neurologic manifestations, renal function, and metabolic abnormalities. Following stabilization, he was discharged on apixaban therapy with scheduled oral hydration instructions and outpatient follow-up. This case highlights a possible synergistic interaction between adipsic hypernatremia and HHS, which may have contributed to severe hyperosmolar stress and extensive thromboembolic complications. Adipsic hypernatremia should be considered in patients with severe hypernatremia and absent thirst sensation, particularly after traumatic brain injury, even when neuroimaging findings are unremarkable.

articles.title: Low-dose prednisolone and B vitamins for post-COVID-19 syndrome in Germany: the PreVitaCOV randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-COVID-19 syndrome is burdensome and not yet adequately treatable, with persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnoea, and cognitive impairment. The Pan American Health Organisation recommends rigorous evaluation of potentially beneficial interventions. We investigated the efficacy and safety of prednisolone and vitamins B1, B6, and B12 in patients with post-COVID-19.

METHODS: This randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (2 × 2 factorial design) was conducted in adults with post-COVID-19 at three university sites in Germany. Adult patients with persistent symptoms after a documented SARS-CoV-2 infection ≥12 weeks ago and without acute COVID-19, major comorbidities, pregnancy or breastfeeding, prior intensive care treatment for COVID-19, recent use of trial drugs, or potentially interacting concomitant medications were included. From January 13, 2023 until July 25, 2024 participants were randomly assigned to 28 days of once-daily oral treatment with prednisolone (20 mg on days 1-5, 5 mg on days 6-28), B vitamins (thiamine nitrate [B1], 100 mg, pyridoxine hydrochloride [B6] 50 mg, and cyanocobalamin [B12] 500 μg), prednisolone and B vitamins, or placebo. The primary outcome was change in overall symptom severity from baseline to day 28, assessed in the intention-to-treat population (participants who received at least one dose of study drug) at the first follow-up visit after randomisation with a customised Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) total T-score. A change of ≥3 points was considered clinically meaningful. Efficacy was assessed using a pre-specified factorial analysis of the main effects of prednisolone and B vitamins. Safety was assessed by analysing frequency and severity of adverse events in all randomised patients (safety population). This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05638633).

FINDINGS: Of 2498 patients assessed for eligibility, 323 were randomised and 310 patients had evaluable data for the outcomes. The mean age was 44 (standard deviation (SD) 13) years, 200 participants were women. The mean change in PROMIS T-score was -4·3 (SD 5·1) with prednisolone, -3·2 (SD 5·0) with B vitamins, -4·5 (SD 4·5) with prednisolone plus B vitamins, and -2·9 (SD 4·6) with placebo. The adjusted mean difference between participants treated with prednisolone and those not treated was -1·4 points (95% confidence interval (CI), -2·5 to -0·4; p = 0·008), driven primarily by the change in the fatigue subscore (-6·4 points, p < 0·001). B vitamins showed no statistically significant or clinically meaningful difference compared with no B vitamins (adjusted mean difference (MD), -0·1 points; 95% CI, -1·2 to +1·0; p = 0·85). Adverse events were equally distributed between groups, with no study-drug-related serious adverse events.

INTERPRETATION: This trial showed a statistically significant short-term reduction in symptom severity in the five dimensions of the PROMIS score in patients with post-COVID with low-dose prednisolone. However, the effect did not reach the prespecified threshold for clinical relevance. Further research is needed to confirm the efficacy of prednisolone and to determine the optimal dose and treatment duration while balancing benefits against longer-term adverse effects.

FUNDING: German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, Vogel Stiftung Dr. Eckernkamp, Hevert-Arzneimittel GmbH & Co. KG.

articles.title: COMBO-RATE: An Experimentally Validated Bioinformatic Tool to Identify Promiscuous HLA Restrictions.
articles.abstract: Defining HLA restriction of T cell epitopes is essential for understanding immune responses in infectious disease, autoimmunity and vaccine design. Current bioinformatic programmes, including the IEDB RATE tool, enable inference of single-HLA restrictions from immune response data of HLA-typed donors. However, T cell epitopes are frequently presented by multiple HLA alleles, a phenomenon termed promiscuous restriction, limiting the utility of single-allele approaches. To address this limitation, we developed COMBO-RATE, an extension of RATE that systematically evaluates combinations of HLA alleles to identify multi-allelic restriction patterns. Analysis of three independent datasets spanning distinct antigen systems and different epitope discovery strategies revealed that promiscuous restriction is a near-universal feature of immunodominant epitopes. Focusing on the 43 immunodominant CD4+ T cell epitopes identified in a B. pertussis genome-wide screen, COMBO-RATE outperformed conventional RATE, identifying restrictions for 35 of 43 epitopes, compared to 24 by RATE alone, and uncovered 64 additional allele restrictions, including 29 unique alleles. Experimental validation using single-HLA transfected cell lines and antigen presentation assays confirmed COMBO-RATE-inferred restrictions, demonstrating that a single epitope can be independently presented by distinct HLA alleles. Overall, COMBO-RATE provides a robust and scalable framework for defining complete HLA restriction profiles from existing population response data, with important implications for the design of vaccines requiring broad HLA coverage across genetically diverse populations. This pipeline is available as both a Python package and a user-friendly web application.

articles.title: Comment on "Understanding the Immune Response Changes to Clinical Interventions for Epstein-Barr Virus Infection Prior to Lymphoma Development in Children After Organ Transplants (UNEARTH)".
Ascites Presenting as a Peritonitis-Like Manifestation and Liver Injury due to Trabectedin Monotherapy in a Patient With Myxoid Liposarcoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trabectedin is a synthetic, marine-derived antitumor agent that exerts cytotoxic effects by binding to the minor groove of DNA. While trabectedin has demonstrated efficacy in advanced soft tissue sarcomas, hepatotoxicity and other adverse events remain concerns. However, cases involving drug-induced liver injury with ascites are rare.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of an 82-year-old woman with recurrent metastatic myxoid liposarcoma who developed simultaneous liver dysfunction and ascites after 12 cycles of trabectedin monotherapy. Laboratory tests revealed Grade 3 hepatic dysfunction, and imaging showed accumulation of ascitic fluid. In the absence of infection or thrombosis, a diagnosis of trabectedin-induced liver injury with ascites was made. Supportive care, including hepatoprotective therapy, led to clinical improvement and resolution of the ascites.

DISCUSSION: Hepatotoxicity is a recognized adverse effect of trabectedin, with proposed mechanisms including direct hepatocellular injury and cytokine-mediated damage. Peritonitis-like symptoms may arise from ascites secondary to hepatic dysfunction. In this case, hepatic dysfunction due to trabectedin may be the trigger for ascites presenting as a peritonitis-like manifestation.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the importance of vigilant monitoring during trabectedin therapy. Early recognition and management of liver injury and ascites presenting as a peritonitis-like manifestation are crucial. Further research is warranted to elucidate the mechanisms and risk factors associated with these toxicities.

articles.title: A multicenter, prospective, phase 2 trial on proton re-irradiation for patients with previously treated head and neck cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Re-irradiation (re-RT) for recurrent head and neck cancer (HNC) can be potentially curative but is constrained by significant toxicity. Proton therapy may improve the therapeutic ratio. This multicenter phase 2 trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of proton re-RT in patients with HNC.

METHODS: Patients received prior HNC radiotherapy at a dose of ≥40 gray (Gy). Salvage surgery and/or systemic therapy before re-RT were permitted. Considering clinical status, two pragmatic treatment approaches were used: fractionated re-RT (F-Re-RT; 60-70 Gy) or QUAD shot re-RT (QS-Re-RT; 14.8 Gy per cycle, up to four cycles; maximum total, 59.2 Gy). Primary end points were locoregional recurrence-free rates at 12 months for F-Re-RT and at 6 months for QS-Re-RT, and a fixed-time, binary proportion analyzed using 90% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (CIs) and prespecified success thresholds (lower bound, >55% and >10%, respectively). Secondary end points included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival, the cumulative incidence of distant metastasis and locoregional recurrence, clinician-reported toxicity, and patient-reported outcomes.

RESULTS: From July 2017 to November 2022, 85 patients received either F-Re-RT (n = 57) or QS-Re-RT (n = 28), with a median follow-up of 38 months. The locoregional recurrence-free rates were 71% (90% CI, 59%-81%) at 12 months for F-Re-RT and 76% (90% CI, 58%-89%) at 6 months for QS-Re-RT, surpassing prespecified success thresholds. The highest late toxicity attributable to re-RT was grade 3 in 20% of patients, grade 4 in 11%, and grade 5 in 4%. The 5-year OS rate was 29%, and the 5-year progression-free survival rate was 23%. Patient-reported outcomes were stable at 1 year after F-Re-RT and after QS-Re-RT.

CONCLUSIONS: Proton re-RT demonstrated encouraging locoregional control and survival in heavily pretreated patients, although late toxicities remain important concerns (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03217188).

articles.title: Eltrombopag during induction chemotherapy in older patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia is safe and reduces platelet transfusion requirements: The EPAG-2015 French Innovative Leukemia Organization phase 2 randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treated with intensive chemotherapy are at risk of developing thrombopenia, which requires platelet transfusions. It would be interesting to provide them with thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as eltrombopag.

METHODS: The EPAG-2015 multicenter phase 2 trial (18 French hospitals from October 2018 to June 2021) blindly randomized elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) with placebo or eltrombopag administered on Day 11 after induction chemotherapy and continued until AML response evaluation (Day 45) or a platelet count of >100 × 109/L. A cohort of 110 patients with a median age of 70 years was included and randomized (55 per arm) to receive placebo or eltrombopag.

RESULTS: After induction, 90 patients (81.8%) achieved complete response (CR) or CR with incomplete reconstitution (CRi) (45 in each group), including 74 patients with CR (38 with eltrombopag and 36 with placebo). With a median follow-up for alive patients of 20.9 months the primary objective was not reached, given that there was no difference in overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 0.65-3.89; p = .31). Eltrombopag, however, did not lead to increased grade 3/4 adverse events, and was associated with a lower median number of platelet transfusions (eight; interquartile range [IQR], 6-14; vs. 10; IQR, 7-14; i.e., a 20% benefit).

CONCLUSIONS: This study failed to demonstrate a survival advantage after eltrombopag addition, at variance with previous reports, but shows that initiating eltrombopag after chemotherapy washout is feasible and safe, and resulted in a decreased need for platelet transfusions.

articles.title: Male mice are more susceptible than females to obesity-induced muscle atrophy when fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet.
articles.abstract: Obesity-related skeletal muscle atrophy poses a significant health burden, with marked sex differences in this condition. However, the mechanisms underlying these sex differences remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether and to what extent skeletal muscle quality was impaired in C57BL/6 mice fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol (HFHC) diet, focusing on sexual dimorphism. Male and female mice were assigned to control or HFHC groups for 40 weeks. The results showed that both sexes fed the HFHC diet developed obesity and dyslipidemia, with males exhibiting a more severe phenotype. Notably, males experienced more pronounced obesity-induced muscle atrophy than females. This study further revealed that HFHC feeding disrupted physiological homeostasis in both sexes, leading to sexual dimorphism in gut microbial composition and short-chain fatty acid levels, with males displaying a diminished capacity to maintain metabolic homeostasis. Furthermore, males exhibited more severe mitochondrial dysfunction and higher oxidative stress levels compared to females, manifesting as reduced muscle strength and upregulated atrophy-related gene expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that long-term HFHC feeding disrupts gut microbiota and glucolipid metabolic homeostasis, further impairing mitochondrial function and exacerbating muscle atrophy preferentially in males, whereas females are relatively protected through superior maintenance of physiological homeostasis, resulting in milder muscle atrophy.

articles.title: Do Adverse Intrauterine Environments Affect Body Mass Index in Infants and Preschool Children?
articles.journal: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Exposure to adverse intrauterine environments resulting from different maternal clinical conditions may alter childhood growth patterns. This study investigated the influence of such environments on body mass index-for-age (BMI-for-age) trajectories from birth to preschool age.

METHODS: A total of 342 mother-child dyads recruited from three hospitals in southern Brazil were allocated into five groups: diabetes mellitus (DM), systemic arterial hypertension (SAH), maternal smoking, small for gestational age (SGA, used here as a proxy for impaired fetal growth), and a control group. Children were assessed at seven time points from birth to preschool age using anthropometric measurements to calculate BMI-for-age z-scores.

RESULTS: Generalized estimating equations (GEE) identified a significant interaction between group and time (p < 0.001). Among girls, at birth, the DM group presented higher BMI-for-age z-scores than the smoking group and reached elevated BMI-for-age z-scores at preschool age, differing from the control group. At 6 months of age, girls in the SGA group showed a marked increase in BMI-for-age. Among boys, the SGA group reached higher BMI-for-age values at preschool age than the DM and control groups. Differences were observed across time, group, and sex in the SGA and control groups (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that adverse intrauterine environments may influence BMI-for-age trajectories during early life, with greater variability and evidence of catch-up growth among children exposed to maternal DM and SGA. Results should be interpreted cautiously due to unequal subgroup sizes and substantial loss to follow-up at preschool age.

articles.title: Longitudinal Facial Growth in Extant Humans: Examining the Association of BMI and Sex.
articles.journal: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Understanding patterns of growth elucidates the mechanism by which adult morphology arises, potentially informing us about the evolutionary history of these traits. We utilize the true longitudinal data from the Iowa Facial Growth Study (IFGS) to examine patterns of facial growth and development in relation to body mass index (BMI) and sex.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our sample (n = 77; 36 female) includes lateral cephalogram data at ages 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. Coordinate landmarks capturing facial shape were used to study facial size, facial shape, and facial form across growth. Cervical vertebral maturation was used as a secondary metric for skeletal maturation. We employed traditional and longitudinal statistics, such as mixed effects models, to examine trends in the data by BMI and sex.

RESULTS: High BMI children have larger facial centroid sizes at Age 4 and maintain this trend through growth. Interestingly, unlike what is seen in dental development, this advanced skeletal development is not coupled with an apparent acceleration in the rate of skeletal development. We further can detect sex differences in facial size as young as the starting Age 4 timepoint (p = 0.0014). Longitudinal analysis revealed differences in facial form early in ontogeny (Age 4), with all BMI groups nearing convergence at the final timepoint (Age 14).

DISCUSSION: Our work demonstrates that variation in facial growth patterns related to BMI and sex is established early and maintained across growth. The growth of the craniofacial skeleton is likely influenced by a complex combination of genetic and environmental factors.

articles.title: Is SARS-CoV-2 Infection (COVID-19) Associated With Congenital Anomalies? A Population Study of Congenital Anomaly Surveillance Data and Maternal SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Wales.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Explore the relationship between maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and congenital anomalies in Wales.

STUDY DESIGN: Mixed observational epidemiological cross-sectional and cohort.

METHODS: Congenital anomaly prevalence data were provided by the Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service. Two comparisons were made using these data: firstly, congenital anomaly subgroup prevalence prior to and during the pandemic at population level, and in a cohort of women with laboratory-confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with the population trend.

RESULTS: Prevalence of congenital anomalies in Wales was lower during the pandemic (mean 365 per 10,000 in 2020-22 vs. 454 per 10,000 in 2009-19) showing stable trends. However, the mean for abdominal wall defects increased from 9.8 per 10,000 births between 2009 and 2019 to 13.9 per 10,000 births in 2020-2022, largely attributed to an increase in omphalocele. A cohort of 486 confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infections led to 181 births affected by congenital anomalies, and the trimester of infection did not impact the adjusted odds of this occurring. Circulatory anomalies were most frequently reported, consistent with pre-pandemic population-level data. Urinary and cardiac anomalies were more prevalent in this cohort group than at population level.

CONCLUSIONS: There was no clear evidence at population-level of an association between congenital anomalies and maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wales. However, a potential association with specific congenital anomalies cannot be excluded. Increased omphalocele is consistent with a Europe-wide trend that pre-dated COVID-19. National surveillance registries should remain vigilant.

articles.title: DBT Modulates Copper-Dependent Cuproptosis-Related Injury in Experimental Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
articles.abstract: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a severe cardiovascular complication of chronic alcohol consumption, but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Cuproptosis is a recently identified copper-dependent form of regulated cell death; however, its role in ACM remains unclear. In this study, male C57BL/6 mice were fed an ethanol-containing Lieber-DeCarli liquid diet to establish an ACM model, and RNA sequencing combined with bioinformatics analysis was performed to identify cuproptosis-related genes. Among the candidate genes, dihydrolipoamide branched-chain transacylase E2 (DBT) showed a consistent trend of downregulation across both independent RNA-seq cohorts, and was further validated by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. ACM mice exhibited increased serum and cardiomyocyte copper content, altered cuproptosis-related markers and impaired cardiac function. In AC16 cells, DBT knockdown induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, which were markedly alleviated by the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate. Conversely, DBT overexpression attenuated EtOH-induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, with effects similar to those of tetrathiomolybdate. These findings suggest that DBT regulates ACM-related cardiomyocyte injury through cuproptosis-associated processes at the cellular level and may represent a potential therapeutic target for alcohol-induced myocardial injury.

articles.title: Anxiety and Mindfulness in the Relationship Between Stress and Depression in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Parallel Mediation Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine the indirect effect of anxiety and mindfulness on the relationship between stress and depression in patients with coronary artery disease.

DESIGN: A correlational, cross-sectional design was used.

METHODS: Participants of this study comprised 112 patients with coronary artery disease recruited from a general hospital in South Korea between January and September 2021. The Korean versions of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 and Mindful Attention Awareness Scale were used. Data were analysed using parallel multiple mediation analysis (PROCESS macro Model 4).

RESULTS: Stress, anxiety, mindfulness and depression were significantly correlated. The total indirect effect through anxiety and mindfulness on the relationship between stress and depression was significant (B = 0.37, 95% CI [0.200, 0.592]). The specific indirect effect through mindfulness was significant (B = 0.26, 95% CI [0.122, 0.423]), whereas the indirect effect through anxiety was not statistically significant (B = 0.11, 95% CI [-0.003, 0.268]).

CONCLUSION: Mindfulness may be an important psychological factor associated with the relationship between stress and depression in patients with coronary artery disease. Further research is needed to clarify the role of anxiety in this relationship.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND PATIENT CARE: Mindfulness-based approaches may be considered as complementary strategies for managing psychological distress and depressive symptoms in patients with coronary artery disease. Anxiety should also be assessed as part of comprehensive psychological care.

articles.title: Effects of a Nurse-Led Multicomponent Exercise Intervention for Haemodialysis Patients With Possible or Confirmed Sarcopenia: A Cluster Randomised Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess the potential effects, safety and feasibility of a nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention on skeletal muscle function and quality of life in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia.

DESIGN: A cluster randomised trial with clusters defined by fixed haemodialysis schedules.

METHODS: A total of 56 eligible participants were enrolled and allocated through cluster randomisation. The intervention group (n = 28) received a 12-week nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention in addition to standard care, whereas the control group (n = 28) received standard care. The primary outcomes included skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), handgrip strength, gait speed and short physical performance battery (SPPB) scores. Secondary outcomes included scores on the Kidney Disease Quality of Life 36-Item Short-Form Survey (KDQOL-36) and C-reactive protein levels. Handgrip strength, gait speed, SPPB scores and KDQOL-36 scores were assessed at baseline and at Weeks 4, 8 and 12 during the intervention period, whereas SMI and C-reactive protein were assessed at baseline and Week 12. An intention-to-treat analysis was employed, and the effects of the intervention were evaluated using linear mixed models.

RESULTS: Of the 56 participants, 50 completed the study. The intervention group showed favourable trends in handgrip strength, gait speed and SPPB scores, with moderate-to-large effect sizes; however, these differences were not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Furthermore, no significant between-group differences were found in skeletal muscle mass index, health-related quality of life, or C-reactive protein levels. No serious intervention-related adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: The nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention was safe and feasible and showed favourable trends in muscle strength and physical function, although statistically significant between-group differences were not retained after correction for multiple comparisons.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PATIENT CARE: A nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention may have the potential to increase muscle strength and physical function in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia.

IMPACT: What problem did the study address? This study assessed the potential effects, safety, and feasibility of a nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention designed for haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. What were the main findings? A nurse-led exercise intervention appeared safe and feasible and may help to improve muscle strength and physical function in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. However, future studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are needed to assess the long-term effects. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The results of this study may inform the development and future implementation of nurse-led exercise interventions for haemodialysis patients with sarcopenia.

PATIENT AND PUBLIC CONTRIBUTIONS: Patients and family members were invited to collaborate with healthcare professionals in designing a nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention programme. Their contributions helped improve the feasibility and practicality of the exercise intervention.

REPORTING METHOD: The CONSORT 2025 checklist was used in the reporting of the study.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered at www.chictr.org.cn (registration number: ChiCTR2200065863).

articles.title: Association Between Exercise Adherence and Long-Term Quality of Life in Ischemic Stroke Survivors: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate factors associated with quality of life within 2 years post-discharge, with a particular focus on exercise adherence.

DESIGN: A prospective observational cohort study.

METHODS: Participants were enrolled during hospitalisation and followed up at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months post-discharge via questionnaires. Linear mixed-effects models were used to identify factors associated with quality of life.

DATA SOURCES: Data were collected from ischemic stroke patients (discharged from The First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College, January to August 2021) using structured questionnaires, medical records and validated scales.

RESULTS: Of 355 enrolled stroke survivors, 242 (68.2%) completed the two-year follow-up. Functional disability, exercise adherence, family history of stroke and prior stroke were independently associated with long-term quality of life.

CONCLUSION: Greater exercise adherence is independently associated with better quality of life on average over the 24-month follow-up period among stroke survivors.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurses and rehabilitation guidelines should prioritise exercise adherence support during long-term follow-up to sustain post-stroke quality of life.

articles.title: The Effect of Implementing Orem's Self-Care Model on Balance and Fatigue in Patients With Diabetic Neuropathy: A Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aims to determine the effect of applying Orem's self-care model on balance and fatigue in patients with diabetic neuropathy.

DESIGN: Randomized clinical trial.

METHODS: Seventy diabetic neuropathy patients referred to Shahid Mofateh Clinic, affiliated with Yasuj University of Medical Sciences (YUMS), were chosen for this clinical trial study via convenience sampling and randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 35) or a control group (n = 35). The intervention group received care based on Orem's self-care model from a graduate nursing student over 2 months, followed by 1 month of self-care at home. The control group received no intervention. Both groups completed the research questionnaires (the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory and the Berg Balance Test) at pretest and posttest. Data were analysed in SPSS version 27 using an ANCOVA test.

RESULTS: Before the intervention, there were no significant between-group differences (p > 0.05). After the intervention, fatigue was significantly lower in the intervention group, with an adjusted mean difference of -9.40 points (95% CI: -11.09 to -7.71; p < 0.001; partial η2 = 0.647). Balance scores were significantly higher in the intervention group across low, mean, and high baseline levels, with adjusted mean differences of 7.01, 5.77, and 4.52 points, respectively (all p < 0.001). The group × baseline balance interaction was significant (F(1,66) = 5.69, p = 0.020; partial η2 = 0.079).

IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING: Nurses are recommended to apply Orem's self-care model as an effective structured intervention to reduce fatigue and improve balance in patients with diabetic neuropathy.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (diagnosed by an internist using TCSS) who participated in this randomized clinical trial evaluating Orem's self-care model effects on balance and fatigue.

articles.title: Effect of Food on the Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Safety of Zastaprazan, a Potassium-Competitive Acid Blocker, in Healthy Participants.
articles.abstract: Zastaprazan (JP-1366) is a novel potassium-competitive acid blocker characterized by rapid onset and sustained acid suppression. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of food on the pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), and safety of zastaprazan in healthy participants. In this randomized, open-label, two-period crossover phase 1 study, 24 healthy participants received a single oral dose of zastaprazan 20 mg under fasted and fed conditions. PK parameters were evaluated using noncompartmental analysis, and PD effects were assessed through continuous intragastric pH monitoring. Under fed conditions, peak exposure (Cmax) decreased (geometric mean ratio [GMR], 0.6997; 90% confidence interval [CI], 0.6292-0.7781), whereas systemic exposure (AUClast) increased (GMR, 1.3783; 90% CI, 1.2688-1.4973), accompanied by a delayed Tmax. Despite these PK differences, PD outcomes were comparable between fed and fasted conditions. The percentage of time with intragastric pH ≥ 4 over 24 h was similar under fed and fasted conditions (70.01% vs. 69.19%), with no meaningful differences observed in other pH-based parameters. Zastaprazan was well tolerated, and no clinically significant safety concerns were identified. Food altered the rate and extent of zastaprazan absorption but did not affect its PD response. These findings indicate that food-related PK changes do not meaningfully affect PD outcomes and support the administration of zastaprazan without regard to meals. This flexibility may enhance its clinical utility as an acid-suppressive therapy. Trial Registration: The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05712681).

articles.title: The Metabolic-Microvascular Axis in Systemic Sclerosis: Decoding the Potential Influence of Insulin Resistance on Nailfold Capillaroscopic Findings.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Insulin resistance (IR) exerts negative effects on vascular homeostasis and endothelial functionality. Its relationship with microvascular damage in systemic sclerosis (SSc) is lacking. This study aimed to investigate the association between IR and nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) abnormalities in SSc.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study including patients diagnosed with SSc according to 2013 American College Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology criteria. IR was assessed using the Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR), with a cut-off ≥ 2.5. NVC findings, including qualitative categorization (early, active, and late pattern) and semiquantitative assessment, were compared between two groups based on the presence of IR. Chi-square, Fischer exact, T-student, and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for univariable analysis. p for trend was calculated for semiquantitative grading. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with HOMA-IR ≥ 2.5.

RESULTS: A total of 124 SSc patients were recruited. Thirty-seven patients (29.8%) had HOMA-IR ≥ 2.5. Compared with patients with HOMA-IR < 2.5 (87 patients, 71.2%), IR patients had a higher prevalence of dyslipidemia and higher body mass index (BMI). NVC analysis revealed that the late pattern was more frequent among patients with IR (p = 0.007), while the early pattern was in patients without IR (p = 0.0037). Vascular bed disorganization and neoangiogenesis/ramifications were more frequently observed in the IR group (0.017 and 0.02, respectively). Multivariable analysis revealed that the late pattern was independently associated with IR (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.001-1.19; p = 0.048), after correction for age and BMI.

CONCLUSIONS: IR is associated with microvascular damage in SSc, suggesting a conceptual link between metabolic dysfunction and microangiopathy.

articles.title: Exercise-Based Management of Diabetic Cardiomyopathy: Preclinical Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Translational Strategies.
articles.abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is characterized by progressive metabolic dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, impaired calcium handling, and ventricular remodeling, yet effective strategies for reversing established cardiac injury remain limited. Exercise training has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological approach, although its clinical application is constrained by heterogeneous intervention protocols, inconsistent dose reporting, and limited evidence from well-characterized diabetic cardiomyopathy populations. This narrative review synthesizes current preclinical and clinical evidence on exercise-based management of diabetes-associated myocardial dysfunction, with particular emphasis on underlying mechanisms, exercise prescription, and translational implementation. Experimental studies indicate that exercise may improve myocardial function through enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic flexibility, attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammatory-fibrotic signaling, restoration of calcium homeostasis, and regulation of apoptosis, pyroptosis, and microRNA-related pathways. Clinical evidence, derived predominantly from individuals with Type 2 diabetes and subclinical or early cardiac abnormalities, suggests that combined aerobic and resistance training can improve cardiorespiratory fitness, insulin sensitivity, vascular function, and selected indices of left ventricular performance. High-intensity interval training may provide additional benefits in appropriately selected patients, but its safety and effectiveness require individualized assessment. To improve translation, exercise intensity should be reported using physiologically comparable metrics, while treatment response should be evaluated through integrated measures of cardiac imaging, functional capacity, biomarkers, glycemic control, and adverse events. Overall, exercise represents a biologically plausible and clinically relevant adjunctive strategy for diabetic cardiomyopathy, particularly in early-stage disease; however, adequately powered trials in clearly defined patient populations are still needed to establish optimal dose, safety, and long-term cardiovascular benefit.

articles.title: Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107).

RESULTS: Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH

articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
