articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP

articles.title: Australian Standards of Care for Genetic and Genomic Testing in Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Genetic and genomic testing can refine diagnosis, prognosis, treatment, transplant assessment and family counselling for kidney disease, yet access remains uneven across Australia. These National Kidney Genomics Guidelines define a standard of care for genetic and genomic testing in nephrology and support the mainstreaming of genomic care while maintaining quality, governance and equity. The guidelines were developed by the KidGen Collaborative, comprising nephrologists, clinical geneticists, genetic counsellors, diagnostic laboratories, scientists and consumer advocates, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander representatives. They underwent open review. Recommendations are graded by strength and by the quality of evidence. The document covers governance and multidisciplinary models; patient selection and phenotyping; clinical indications, including transplantation; test selection; consent; requesting and funding; interpretation of results; post-test management and re-analysis; familial variant testing; and patient and clinician support. Equitable access for rural and remote communities, culturally and linguistically diverse groups, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples is prioritised. Predictive testing of asymptomatic relatives and testing of children without immediate medical benefit should be conducted through specialised genetics services. Variants of uncertain significance should not guide management. The guidelines are intended for nephrologists, clinical geneticists, genetic counsellors and health-service decision-makers, and will be reviewed every three to five years, or sooner if practice-changing evidence emerges.

articles.title: Flexible perovskite light-emitting diodes based on polybenzimidazole substrates.
articles.abstract: Flexible perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) are promising for wearable and foldable displays, but their performance is often limited by substrate-related issues like high roughness and poor thermal stability. This work reports a highly efficient, mechanically robust red PeLED utilizing polybenzimidazole (PBI) as the flexible substrate. Compared with the traditional PET substrates, PBI has lower surface roughness and better wettability for the functional layer. As a result, the PeLED based on the PBI substrate achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 15.7% and a maximum luminance of 3680 cd m-2, demonstrating excellent mechanical stability. This study proves that PBI, as a high-performance flexible substrate, holds immense potential for realizing high-efficiency and mechanically stable PeLEDs.

articles.title: Tailoring 3D non-Rayleigh speckles via physics-informed neural networks.
articles.abstract: Optical speckles, a disordered photonic phenomenon that originates from the interference of multiple scattered coherent waves, typically obey Rayleigh statistics. Beyond this classical regime, featuring customizable statistical properties and high-order correlations, non-Rayleigh speckles present potential in both fundamental and applied research. Here, we introduce a physics-informed neural network for designing three-dimensional non-Rayleigh speckle fields. As a proof of concept, we experimentally realize volumetric sub-Rayleigh and propagation-persistent super-Rayleigh speckles on this versatile framework. Our work paves a novel, to the best of our knowledge, way for statistical light manipulation and engineering implementation.

articles.title: Respirasome Persistence Without Efficient Electron Channeling in Cardiac Mitochondria From an Animal Model of Hypertension.
articles.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
articles.abstract: Cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to hypertensive remodeling, but whether respiratory supercomplex organization preserves electron transfer efficiency during disease progression remains unresolved. Here, we examined the structural and functional organization of the respiratory complexes in cardiac mitochondria from stroke-resistant and stroke-prone spontaneously hypertensive rats exposed to normal or Japanese diet regimens. In both models, supramolecular analyses revealed the persistence of N-respirasome and Q-respirasome assemblies, indicating that major respiratory supercomplex species are maintained during sustained hypertension and in the pre-stroke state. However, metabolic flux control analysis consistently showed that cytochrome c oxidase or Complex IV exerted only limited control over respiratory flux, with control coefficients below those expected for tightly channeled nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH)-dependent electron transfer. Thus, structural preservation of respirasomes was not matched by evidence of kinetically optimized coupling. These findings uncouple supercomplex detectability from functional electron channeling and suggest that, in the hypertensive heart, respiratory performance is constrained by qualitative defects in supercomplex organization rather than by their overt loss.

articles.title: Localized Cutaneous Fusarium Infection on a Leg Mimicking Scrofuloderma in an Immunocompetent Adult.
Cutaneous Cytomegalovirus Infections in Immunocompromised Individuals.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection is a rare entity, despite a significant seroprevalence of CMV globally. It is most often encountered as an opportunistic infection among immunosuppressed individuals. Skin involvement in CMV infection could be the heralding sign of a more disseminated disease. We report a case series of five immunocompromised patients who manifested varied morphological features of cutaneous CMV infection. All patients were diagnosed based on histopathology, supplemented with immunohistochemistry or serology. The clinical presentations seen in our patients include punched-out ulcers in the perineal region and distal extremities, vesicobullous lesions, truncal ulcers with scalloped margins, crusted hyperpigmented papules, and oral erosions. After a thorough evaluation, patients were initiated on oral valganciclovir or intravenous ganciclovir. Being a rarity, this case series highlights the clinical manifestations and management of cutaneous CMV infection.

articles.title: [Juvenile oligoarthritis and uveitis: everything unchanged?].
articles.abstract: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis and associated uveitis may persist into adulthood. This article addresses the clinical aspects and trajectory of oligoarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and associated uveitis in the pediatric and young adult age. Specific challenges in diagnosis and treatment at the interface between pediatric and adult rheumatology (transition) are discussed.

articles.title: Is Undiagnosed Dysglycemia Common in Orthopaedic Surgery and Is it Associated With 30-day Outcomes? A Large-database Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given that patients undergoing orthopaedic surgery frequently share risk factors that are associated with metabolic syndrome, the patients orthopaedic surgeons treat may be especially likely to have undiagnosed dysglycemia. Although its broader impact is documented in other specialties, its specific prevalence and association with postoperative outcomes after orthopaedic procedures remains incompletely defined. Quantifying this hidden burden is important to developing individual risk profiles, refining perioperative decision-making, and establishing targeted preoperative medical management strategies for patients considering orthopaedic surgery.

QUESTIONS/PURPOSES: In a large-database study, we asked: (1) In adults who underwent orthopaedic surgery, what proportion of patients had previously undiagnosed dysglycemia? (2) Was undiagnosed dysglycemia associated with increased odds of 30-day readmission and reoperation compared with patients with normoglycemia? (3) What was the relationship between preoperative HbA1c levels and the 30-day risk of complications in patients who underwent orthopaedic surgery?

METHODS: Among the 2,990,063 procedures recorded in the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database (2021-2023), 25% (735,259 of 2,990,063) were orthopaedic. After excluding 75% (2,254,804 of 2,990,063) of nonorthopaedic procedures and 16% (493,272 of 2,990,063) of orthopaedic procedures without documented preoperative HbA1c, 8% (241,987 of 2,990,063) of all procedures were analyzed. Patients were assigned to one of eight glycemic groups (normoglycemic, undiagnosed prediabetes, undiagnosed diabetes, or diagnosed diabetes with near-normal, very good, good, poor, and very poor glycemic control) based on diabetes diagnosis and HbA1c level. The study cohort included patients undergoing a range of procedures, primarily consisting of total joint arthroplasty, fracture fixation, and spine surgery. The mean ± SD patient age was 66 ± 12 years and 56% [134,741 of 241,987] of patients were female. To address the first research question, the percentage of patients with previously undiagnosed dysglycemia in each cohort was measured, supplemented by a best-case sensitivity analysis to provide a conservative estimate for the entire surgical population. The second and third research questions investigated the association of undiagnosed dysglycemia on 30-day odds of readmission and reoperation and the relationship between preoperative HbA1c and 30-day odds of complications, using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, comorbidity, and procedural factors. To illustrate variation across operations, the 30-day complication rate of patients across HbA1c strata was evaluated for the 10 most frequent primary Current Procedural Terminology-coded procedures.

RESULTS: We found that 22% (52,609 of 241,987) of patients with a recorded preoperative HbA1c had undiagnosed prediabetes and 4% (10,690 of 241,987) of patients met the criteria for undiagnosed diabetes. In a best-case sensitivity analysis in which we assumed that all patients without an HbA1c measurement did not have diabetes and had normoglycemia, the smallest percentage of patients with previously undiagnosed dysglycemia would have been 9% (63,299) across all 735,259 patients who underwent orthopaedic surgery. After adjusting for potentially confounding variables, neither prediabetes nor diabetes was independently associated with increased odds of 30-day readmission (adjusted OR 0.95 [95% CI 0.88 to 1.0]; p = 0.12 and adjusted OR 0.99 [95% CI 0.84 to 1.2]; p = 0.94) or reoperation (adjusted OR 0.94 [95% CI 0.85 to 1.0]; p = 0.25 and adjusted OR 0.99 [95% CI 0.84 to 1.2]; p = 0.94) compared with patients with normoglycemia. The adjusted ORs for any 30-day complication were higher in patients with undiagnosed diabetes (adjusted OR 1.1 [95% CI 1.0 to 1.2]; p = 0.03) and increased across HbA1c strata in those with diagnosed diabetes (adjusted OR 1.2, 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, and 2.0; all p ≤ 0.009) compared with patients with normoglycemia. Procedure-level analyses showed consistent patterns with variable magnitude: 30-day rates of any complication in THA rose from 5% (1425 of 27,812) to 17% (49 of 294) across HbA1c strata, whereas 30-day complication rates peaked at 30% (203 of 675) in hinged TKA and at 22% (11 of 49) in revision TKA. On the other hand, 30-day complication rates in shoulder procedures and knee arthroscopy remained uniformly low (< 6%) with minimal variation by HbA1c.

CONCLUSION: Unrecognized dysglycemia is common among patients undergoing orthopaedic surgery and is associated with postoperative morbidity. Selective preoperative HbA1c assessment and procedure-specific targets may improve perioperative risk stratification. Examining these effects in clinical studies with procedure-specific preoperative HbA1c screening to identify and appropriately treat patients at risk could help to further validate these findings.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Comparison of Wildtype and Recombinant Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV) Production Reveals Distinct Productivity and Content Ratio Profiles.
articles.abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus is a leading viral vector for gene therapy. However, recombinant adeno-associated virus production systems have low titer and content ratio (ratio of genome-containing to total adeno-associated virus capsids), making it difficult to generate the large number of vector genomes required for clinical or commercial use. In contrast, wildtype adeno-associated virus achieves over ten-fold higher titer compared to recombinant adeno-associated virus and a content ratio of over 95% full. Despite the higher productivity of wildtype adeno-associated virus, the mechanisms behind its productivity remain poorly understood. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel wildtype adeno-associated virus production platform in suspension human embryonic kidney cells across varying multiplicities of infection of adeno-associated virus to adenovirus. The impact of cellular viral genome delivery mechanisms and the interplay between adeno-associated virus and its adenoviral helper were investigated by comparing infection-based systems with transfection-based and infection-transfection hybrid systems. Wildtype and hybrid infection systems had remarkably different host cell growth profiles and viral gene expression patterns, and achieved over a log-fold higher titers and 45% higher content ratios, reaching 8.1 × 1012 vector genomes/mL culture and 72.2% full, compared to recombinant transfection systems (1.63 × 1011 vector genomes/mL and 26.9% full).

articles.title: Comprehenders' Error Correction Mechanisms Are Finely Calibrated to Language Production Statistics.
articles.abstract: An essential feature of human communication is robustness to errors: even when speakers and writers make mistakes, listeners and readers can usually determine the intended meaning. A leading hypothesis is that comprehenders achieve robust error correction by internally deploying a "noisy-channel" model of the language production process. Crucially, to best achieve error robustness, a comprehender's noisy-channel model should be finely calibrated to the environmental statistics of language production, incorporating not only prior expectations about communicative intents but also structure-sensitive likelihoods of different types of speaker error. This environmentally calibrated noisy-channel hypothesis has been difficult to test, because the rates of most types of language production errors are hard to estimate. Here, we test this hypothesis by experimentally investigating comprehenders' interpretations of subject-verb agreement errors, for which context-contingent language production error rates are feasible to estimate. In a novel free-form error correction task, participants edited sentences with subject-verb agreement mismatches to indicate what they think was intended. Bayesian analysis of the resulting data shows that comprehenders' interpretations reflect both item-specific prior expectations and structure-sensitive error likelihoods that closely correspond to error rates in language production. These results provide quantitative evidence that humans closely track prior statistics over linguistic forms and deploy a noisy-channel model finely calibrated to statistics of the linguistic environment to achieve robust language understanding.

articles.title: Effects and Moderators of High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) on Physiological Adaptations Among Team-Sport Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
articles.abstract: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is widely used in team sports, but the influence of participant and programme characteristics on physiological adaptations remains unclear. Five databases (Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CNKI) were searched initially on 25 April 2025 and updated on 21 December 2025. Mixed-effects models were used to estimate Hedges' g and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Forty-six studies involving 1204 athletes were included. Compared with regular sport-specific training alone, HIIT produced positive effects on maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max; g = 0.76, 95% CI [0.61, 0.92]), maximal aerobic power (g = 0.43, 95% CI [0.04, 0.82]), ventilatory threshold (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.53, 0.88]), Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test performance (g = 1.02, 95% CI [0.76, 1.28]), and 30-s Wingate peak (g = 0.91, 95% CI [0.67, 1.16]) and mean power (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.39, 1.01]). Effects on body composition were generally unclear. Mutually adjusted multivariable meta-regression identified no convincing evidence of differences in VO2max or Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test performance effects by sex or training level. Longer training duration was associated with greater VO2max effects. In exploratory analyses, model predictions indicated increases in VO2max of 2.56 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI [1.54, 3.58]) after approximately 5 weeks and 5.11 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI [3.32, 6.91]) after approximately 10 weeks. Shorter between-repetition recovery was associated with greater VO2max effects, although other programme variables were estimated imprecisely. Overall, adding HIIT to regular sport-specific training improves aerobic and anaerobic performance in trained team-sport athletes, whereas effects on body composition are limited. Associations involving programme characteristics should be interpreted cautiously because they were derived from study-level meta-regression. Trial Registration: PROSPERO Registration CRD42024609379.

articles.title: Long-Term Marginal Bone Stability of BOPT Restorations on Bone-Level vs. Tissue-Level Implants: An 8-Year Prospective Clinical Study.
articles.journal: Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Biologically Oriented Preparation Technique (BOPT) has been applied to implant-supported restorations to promote peri-implant tissue stability. However, long-term evidence regarding marginal bone behavior remains limited. This study evaluated marginal bone loss after eight years of functional loading in bone-level and tissue-level implants restored according to the BOPT concept, as well as the influence of prosthesis type and arch location.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective randomized clinical study included 122 posterior implants in 71 patients after eight years of follow-up: 57 bone-level implants and 65 tissue-level implants. All implants were restored with cement-retained metal-ceramic single crowns or fixed partial dentures. Marginal bone loss was assessed using standardized periapical radiographs obtained at prosthetic loading and after eight years. Generalized estimating equation models were used to account for multiple implants within the same patient.

RESULTS: Tissue-level implants showed significantly lower mesial marginal bone loss than bone-level implants (0.49 ± 0.77 mm versus 0.78 ± 0.93 mm; p = 0.031). No significant differences were observed for distal or mean marginal bone loss. Fixed partial dentures were associated with greater mesial bone loss than single crowns (p = 0.025), whereas arch location did not significantly affect bone remodeling (p = 0.838).

DISCUSSION: Both implant systems demonstrated limited long-term marginal bone remodeling. Nevertheless, the significant difference was restricted to the mesial aspect, and the findings cannot be attributed exclusively to implant placement level or to the BOPT concept because the two implant systems differed in macrogeometry, surface characteristics and transmucosal configuration.

CONCLUSIONS: Tissue-level implants showed lower mesial marginal bone loss after eight years, whereas distal and mean marginal bone loss did not differ significantly between systems. These findings should be interpreted considering the differences between the implant systems and the limitations of two-dimensional radiographic assessment.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for Assessing the Relationship Between Mandibular Third Molars and the Inferior Alveolar Nerve on Panoramic Radiographs: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracting mandibular third molars is a common procedure that carries a risk of injury to the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN). Panoramic radiographs (PR) are commonly used for preoperative assessment of the mandibular third molars, but they are not very reliable for evaluating the relationship of the IAN. This systematic review aims to evaluate the accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI) models in assessing the relationship between mandibular third molars and the IAN.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted systematic searches in MEDLINE (via PubMed), the Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus for studies published between January 2020 and April 2026. Eligible studies evaluated artificial intelligence systems that analyze panoramic radiographs to assess the relationship between mandibular third molars and the IAN, using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) or expert assessments as references. The studies had to report key diagnostic performance metrics. Two independent reviewers carried out study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessments using the QUADAS-2 tool.

RESULTS: We included eleven studies with more than 9,700 patients. The AI models reviewed, including architectures such as ResNet, VGG, and YOLO, demonstrated promising diagnostic performance. Their accuracy ranged from 0.630 to 0.896, with sensitivity and specificity reaching up to 0.92 and 0.95, respectively. No single architecture was consistently superior, but AI models outperformed less experienced human observers in the studies that included this comparison. Validation against CBCT usually yielded more reliable performance metrics than validation based solely on expert opinion.

CONCLUSIONS: AI models show promise as decision-support tools in the radiographic assessment of the relationship between mandibular third molars and the inferior alveolar nerve on panoramic radiographs. However, variations in datasets, reference standards, and validation methods across studies mean that no single architecture can yet be considered superior. Larger, multicenter, prospective studies with external validation are necessary to confirm these systems' performance before they can be widely used in clinical practice.

articles.title: Evaluation of Jawbone Changes in Pediatric Asthmatic Patients Receiving Inhaled Corticosteroids Using Fractal Dimension and Mandibular Radiomorphometric Indices.
articles.journal: Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate mandibular bone quality and microarchitecture in pediatric asthmatic patients using inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) through fractal dimension (FD) analysis and panoramic radiomorphometric indices, and to compare the findings with healthy controls.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective, matched case-control study included panoramic radiographs of 34 asthmatic children aged 5-14 years who had used ICS for at least two years and 68 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. FD values were calculated using the box-counting method from regions of interest in the mandibular condyle, angulus, and interdental regions. Radiomorphometric assessment included the mental index (MI), panoramic mandibular index (PMI), and mandibular cortical index (MCI). Interobserver agreement was evaluated using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).

RESULTS: MI and PMI values were significantly lower in the asthma group than in controls (p<0.001), while MCI distribution was similar between groups (p>0.05). FD values in the angulus region were higher in the asthma group before Bonferroni correction (p=0.025); however, this finding did not remain statistically significant after adjustment. No differences were observed in the condylar or interdental regions (p>0.05). No association was found between ICS duration and FD or radiomorphometric indices (p>0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric asthmatic patients using ICS demonstrated lower MI and PMI values than healthy controls, suggesting potential alterations in mandibular cortical bone quality. FD-related differences were not statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Further studies are needed to clarify the effects of long-term ICS use on mandibular bone structure.

articles.title: 15O-water PET-detected myocardial ischaemia and CT-derived FFR: Predicting the functional significance of anatomical stenosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical assessment of coronary stenoses, its ability to determine their functional significance is limited. Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) has emerged as a non-invasive method for lesion-specific ischaemia assessment. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR using 15O-water positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging as the reference standard.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively reviewed 193 patients who underwent hybrid CCTA and 15O-water PET at Kuopio University Hospital between 2017 and 2022. Patients with low-to-moderate pretest probability of CAD in whom CAD could not be ruled out by CCTA were eligible. After exclusions, 165 patients were included. CT-FFR values were calculated using a research prototype algorithm and compared with PET-derived perfusion abnormalities. In the overall cohort, CT-FFR showed moderate diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.672-0.740. In a subgroup of 83 patients with high-quality CCTA and stenosis >50%, diagnostic performance improved substantially (AUC 0.836). Using a CT-FFR threshold of 0.80, sensitivity and specificity were 85% and 87%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: In an unselected clinical population referred for PET perfusion imaging after CCTA, CT-FFR did not significantly improve diagnostic performance compared with CCTA alone. However, in patients with high-quality CCTA and obstructive coronary stenoses, CT-FFR demonstrated good accuracy for identifying functionally significant disease, supporting its role as a complementary non-invasive diagnostic tool.

articles.title: Hookworm Parasitism Shapes Energy Status and Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Northeast Madagascar.
articles.journal: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiometabolic diseases are rising in low- and middle-income countries, which also bear high burdens of helminth infection and malnutrition. Untangling the relationships among helminth infection, energy status, and cardiovascular disease is important for reducing these burdens.

METHODS: We investigated the interacting risks and moderating variables associated with cardiometabolic health using demographic, health, and hookworm infection data from 874 participants in rural northeast Madagascar.

RESULTS: We observed wide variation in body-mass index (BMI) and blood pressure, alongside high prevalences of two helminth infections: the human hookworm Necator americanus (53.6%) and the zoonotic hookworm Ancylostoma ceylanicum (20.4%). We hypothesized that hookworm infections would be associated with reduced BMI and lower blood pressure through energetic and immunomodulatory pathways. Yet, the two hookworm species showed different associations, with N. americanus infection negatively associated with BMI and A. ceylanicum infection positively associated with blood pressure. Wealthier individuals had higher BMI, but this positive effect was attenuated if they were infected with A. ceylanicum. Coinfection with both hookworms did not significantly modify these associations with BMI or blood pressure. Structural equation modeling indicated that N. americanus infection was associated with reduced blood pressure both directly and through its negative association with BMI, while A. ceylanicum infection was associated with increased blood pressure independent of BMI.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings shed new light on the interacting burdens of malnutrition, parasitism, and chronic diseases with implications for public health, highlighting that these associations are dependent on parasite species.

articles.title: Machine Learning for Composite Biomaterials in Bone Implants and Scaffolds: A Systematic Review of Manufacturing and the Process-Structure-Property-Performance Relationships.
articles.journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part B, Applied biomaterials
articles.abstract: Bone-implant and scaffold research is beginning to use machine learning (ML) alongside biomaterials design and advanced manufacturing, but the literature is scattered across different material classes and stages of development. We therefore reviewed ML studies relevant to composite, multiphase, coated, graded, and multimaterial systems and organized them using the process-structure-property-performance (PSPP) sequence. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were used as the formal bibliographic databases; IEEE Xplore screening, targeted OpenAlex searches, and Google Scholar citation chasing provided supplementary coverage. The frozen dataset contained 46 primary studies. Twenty-five satisfied a strict composite/multimaterial definition, whereas 21 were retained as boundary-supporting evidence for the sensitivity analysis. The studies show that ML is being used for property prediction, surrogate modeling, inverse design, multi-objective optimization, and material screening. Validation, however, did not advance at the same pace as modeling. Physical or experimental confirmation was identified in 32/46 studies (69.6%), in vitro or in vivo experiments, including antibacterial assays, in 11/46 (23.9%), and external validation in only 2/46 (4.3%); none reported prospective clinical validation. Explicit uncertainty analysis and strong reproducibility were also uncommon. Taken together, the literature suggests that the main challenge is no longer demonstrating that an ML model can fit a biomaterials dataset. The more difficult task is showing that a model-guided choice remains useful after fabrication and biological testing. Priorities therefore include better-described multimodal datasets, independent and leakage-resistant validation, characterization of the manufactured rather than only nominal structure, uncertainty-aware design, physics-informed modeling, and prospective biological testing.

articles.title: The effect of biphasic cuirass ventilation on peripheral lymphatic function in young adults.
articles.abstract: Positive pressure ventilation increases the intrathoracic pressure and the central venous pressure, impeding venous return to the heart. Likewise, both central and peripheral lymphatic function is haltered during positive pressure ventilation, presenting as a possible explanation for fluid retention and edema in post-operative and intensive care unit patients. We aimed to examine the effects of biphasic cuirass ventilation on the peripheral lymphatic system. Peripheral lymphatic function was examined in twenty healthy, young adults during spontaneous breathing and during biphasic cuirass ventilation. The peripheral lymphatic function was assessed with near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and the microvascular circulation was assessed with strain gauge plethysmography. Mean peripheral lymphatic contraction frequency (mean ± SD) was 1.46 ±  0.73/min at baseline and 1.43 ±  0.76/min during biphasic cuirass ventilation. There was no significant difference (mean difference = 0.03, 95% CI: -0.23-0.29, p = 0.81, n = 19). Capillary filtration rates did not differ between baseline and biphasic cuirass ventilation across all pressure levels (F(1,18) = 1.13, p = 0.30). Likewise, there were no significant differences in isovolumetric pressures (mean difference = -2.61, 95% CI: -8.92-3.71, p = 0.39, n = 15), or capillary filtration coefficients (mean difference = 1.21 × 10-4, 95% CI: -4,87 × 10-4 - 7.29 × 10-4, p = 0.68, n = 19). We observed no changes in peripheral lymphatic activity in awake, healthy, young adults during BCV.

articles.title: Response to "Accidental Ingestion of Highly Toxic Drugs in Young Children: A Multicenter Study From Spanish Pediatric Emergency Medicine Departments".
Response to "Accidental Ingestion of Highly Toxic Drugs in Young Children: A Multicenter Study From Spanish Pediatric Emergency Medicine Departments".
Pediatric Musculoskeletal Infections: Who Needs a Tap or MRI? From Kocher to PEMCRC.
articles.abstract: Bacterial musculoskeletal infections (MSKIs), including septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, and pyomyositis, are challenging diagnoses to make in pediatric emergency medicine because their presentation frequently overlaps with more common conditions, including transient synovitis, Lyme arthritis, reactive arthritis, and other inflammatory arthritides. While delayed diagnosis may result in significant morbidity, over-testing may expose children to invasive procedures, advanced imaging, sedation, hospitalization, and unnecessary antimicrobial therapy. Pediatric emergency clinicians must therefore balance the competing risks of missed infection and excessive diagnostic evaluation and treatment. Numerous tools exist to aid clinicians, including blood biomarkers-white blood cell (WBC) count, absolute neutrophil count (ANC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and procalcitonin (PCT). However, blood biomarkers have limited diagnostic accuracy when used in isolation. To address this limitation, clinical prediction tools that combine laboratory values with clinical features to stratify risk have been developed. In this review, we summarize the data for clinically available biomarkers and clinical prediction tools for the evaluation of pediatric bacterial MSKIs and discuss their practical application, limitations, and integration into clinical decision-making in the emergency department (ED). Ultimately, we provide a framework to help pediatric emergency clinicians identify children who require advanced testing and interventions while avoiding unnecessary evaluation and treatment in low-risk patients.

articles.title: Associations of Coexisting Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sarcopenia-Related Abnormalities With Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Obesity States.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with adverse liver and non-liver outcomes, but the impact of coexisting sarcopenia-related abnormalities (e.g., low muscle strength [MS], muscle mass, and physical performance) remains unclear. In a prospective UK Biobank cohort (n = 438,748), we evaluated their joint associations with incidence and risks of all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), non-liver cancers, and obesity-related cancers across MASLD and sarcopenia-related abnormality status. Over a median follow-up of 13.8 years, 401 HCC, 1714 cirrhosis, 39,534 CVD, 19,637 CKD, 38,240 non-liver cancers, 12,536 obesity-related cancers, and 34,801 deaths occurred. A stepwise increase in both incidence and adjusted risk of liver and non-liver outcomes was observed across MASLD and sarcopenia strata. Within the coexistence group, the obesity (vs. non-obesity) subgroup generally had higher risks. For example, for cirrhosis, adjusted hazard ratios increased from 3.93 to 7.36 then 8.48 with MASLD alone, coexisting MASLD with low MS overall and coexisting MASLD, low MS and obesity, respectively. Similar findings were observed in external validation analyses using the 2011-2018 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort. Together, these observations inform risk stratification strategy and management of MASLD to include sarcopenia assessment.

articles.title: Evaluating access to care from the perspective of companion animal "care deserts" in Ontario.
articles.journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The proportion of companion animals requiring veterinary attention is on the rise and access to care is a growing concern. Accessibility is a multifactorial concept and is affected by cultural, sociodemographic, and financial considerations, including language spoken, place of residence, required travel distance to the nearest medical facility, and ability to pay for necessary medical care. This research focused on how accessibility is affected by service density through the identification of low- and high-density companion animal hospital clusters in the province of Ontario.

PROCEDURE: Data based on Census Subdivision and Forward Sortation Area administrative boundaries from the 2021 Canadian census were combined with a repository of provincial general practice companion animal hospitals. Using the spatial scan statistic with a Poisson model, we identified spatial clusters of low and high companion animal hospital density, using households and population as denominators based on Census Subdivision and Forward Sortation Area boundaries.

RESULTS: A low-density clinic cluster was consistently located in the Greater Toronto Area (i.e., a high-density urban population), despite the assumption that large urban centers are well serviced. The locations of high-density clinic clusters varied with choice of geographic boundary and population denominator. However, unlike low-density clusters, these were centered around smaller and/or more rural communities. Potential biases associated with the lack of available pet ownership-level data are referenced in the Discussion.

CONCLUSION AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The potential socioeconomic causes of these clusters and their One Health implications are important to consider when allocating additional resources for veterinary care in these populations.

articles.title: Clinical and 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging features in a dog with bacterial sepsis of unknown origin.
articles.journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne
articles.abstract: Positron emission tomography with 2-deoxy-2-[fluorine-18] fluoro-D-glucose integrated with computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) imaging identified infection and inflammation earlier and with higher sensitivity than other imaging modalities in human medicine. A small case series explored the use of 18F-FDG PET/CT for detecting the cause of fever of unknown origin in dogs. This report details clinical aspects and 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging in the workup and treatment of a 12-year-old dog that was presented obtunded with severe neutropenia and hypoglycemia secondary to suspected sepsis. The 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed moderate, patchy FDG avidity and soft-tissue swelling of the left carpus and tarsus (SUV max: 7.18 and SUV max: 5.58, respectively), moderate heterogeneous splenic and hepatic hypermetabolic activity (SUV max: 3.42), and bilaterally symmetric renal hypermetabolic activity (SUV max: 6.22) without appropriate flourine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) excretion. Other notable findings included marked, diffuse 18F-FDG uptake within all bone marrow spaces (SUV max: 15.47) and a generalized, mild lymphadenopathy with moderate hypermetabolic activity. Positive blood cultures confirmed sepsis. Clinical deterioration despite appropriate antibiotic and supportive therapy prompted euthanasia. Necropsy revealed lymphohistiocytic and neutrophilic necrotizing vasculitis with thrombosis and necrosis in heart, spleen, brain, and liver, consistent with septicemia. Enterococcus faecium was isolated from lungs, kidneys, and spleen; Serratia marcescens was isolated from lungs and kidneys. This is the first documented report of the use of 18F-FDG PET/CT for the diagnostic workup of a septic patient in veterinary medicine with corroborative necropsy findings to confirm PET/CT suspicion of disseminated septicemia. Key clinical message: Positron emission tomography with 2-deoxy-2-[fluorine-18] fluoro-D-glucose integrated with computed tomography imaging, which combines the functional, metabolic information from a PET scan with the high-resolution anatomical detail from a CT scan, should be considered as an adjunctive imaging modality for the diagnostic workup to identify focal and systemic infections in veterinary medicine. This is critical for immunocompromised animals in which timely and accurate diagnosis is of utmost importance, either for guiding case management and clinical outcome or for guiding owners through difficult decisions when the prognosis is guarded to poor.

articles.title: Climate and Other Human Causes of Spatial Variation in Mallard Mortality and Population Dynamics.
articles.abstract: Wildlife population dynamics change across time and space, but few studies use formal spatiotemporal statistical models to understand these patterns. The population distribution of mallards (Anas platyrhyncos) in the Prairie Pothole Region of central North America (PPR) has shifted dramatically over the past several decades as agricultural intensity and climate have changed. We examined spatiotemporal variation in survival, natural mortality, and harvest mortality rates for mallards in the PPR from 1974 to 2023 using intrinsic conditional autoregressive models in a Bayesian framework. There was substantial variation over time and space for all demographic rates, and relationships between mortality and habitat variables varied by age and sex cohort. Specifically, environmental relationships indicate that habitats with less agricultural activity and more wetlands decrease survival via increased natural mortality driven by reproductive risks. We also found a worrying trend: females exhibited declining survival probabilities since the late 1980s and early 1990s. Our analyses demonstrate major variation in survival rates of a well-studied organism across an environmental gradient, reveal subtle but critical differences relative to inference obtained from pooled data, and provide a clear roadmap to future research that can inform spatially explicit conservation and management goals.

articles.title: Antineoplastic therapies associated with venous thromboembolism: disproportionality analysis of the WHO database.
articles.abstract: The risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) is elevated in patients with active cancer. Recent antineoplastic therapies, including immunotherapies and targeted therapies, may further increase VTE risk, although evidence is limited. In March 2024, we conducted a disproportionality analysis using reporting odds ratios (Reporting-OR) in VigiBase, the World Health Organization's (WHO's) pharmacovigilance database, to assess the association between 280 antineoplastic therapies approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and/or the European Medicines Agency and VTE (symptomatic or not), defined as deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism. Reporting-OR were adjusted (aReporting-OR) for case characteristics, including primary tumor site and metastatic status. A total of 37 803 VTE reports associated with at least 1 antineoplastic therapy were identified. We identified 19 antineoplastic therapies significantly associated with an increased reporting of VTE, with nintedanib emerging as a newly recognized association. The strongest associations were observed for lenalidomide (aReporting-OR, 3.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.47-3.82), bevacizumab (aReporting-OR, 3.64; 95% CI, 3.43-3.86), and cyproterone (aReporting-OR, 3.52; 95% CI, 2.55-4.87). The median time to VTE onset was 64 days (interquartile range, 27-143), with 81% of VTE events occurring within the first 6 months after antineoplastic therapy initiation. Future studies should include antineoplastic therapies in VTE risk assessments and evaluate the management of VTE when recurrences occur while under treatment. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT04696250.

articles.title: Video laryngoscopy versus direct laryngoscopy for pediatric emergency tracheal intubation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation ILCOR Pediatric Life Support Task Force
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare video laryngoscopy with direct laryngoscopy for pediatric intubation during cardiac arrest and peri-arrest scenarios.

METHODS: This systematic review (PROSPERO CRD420251081694) searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane from inception to May 1, 2026. Two authors independently screened studies; data were extracted by one and independently verified by a second reviewer. Eligible studies compared video versus direct laryngoscopy in pediatric acute care; emergency department, intensive care, and prehospital settings. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and RoB2. Critical outcomes were survival to hospital discharge, first-pass intubation success, overall intubation success, and severe tracheal intubation-associated events. Additional data included study design, setting, age, operator type, and device. Meta-analyses used random-effects Mantel-Haenszel models reporting risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies (17 observational, 1 RCT). First-pass success was higher with video laryngoscopy (72.2% vs 69.0%; RR 1.11, 95% CI 1.06-1.16; very low certainty). Severe adverse events were less frequent with video laryngoscopy (7.7% vs 11.8%; RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62-0.93; very low certainty). Overall success (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.01) and desaturation (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77-1.01) were similar. No studies reported survival outcomes or data specific to cardiac arrest.

CONCLUSION: Among children undergoing emergency tracheal intubation, video laryngoscopy may be associated with improved first-pass success and fewer adverse events, although the certainty of evidence is very low and causal inferences are limited. No data were available for survival outcomes and cardiac arrest.

articles.title: A Rare Case Report of Type II Kounis Syndrome With Literature Review: Acute Anterior ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction Following Bee Sting.
articles.abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS), also known as allergic angina, is a rare but serious condition defined by acute coronary syndrome occurring alongside a hypersensitivity reaction. We report the case of a 42-year-old male smoker who developed Type II KS after a hymenoptera sting. The patient came to the emergency department with a sudden decreased level of consciousness and retrosternal chest pain. Electrocardiography showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads, and coronary angiography revealed total proximal left anterior descending artery occlusion. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed successfully. Echocardiography documented a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with regional wall motion abnormalities, indicating significant myocardial injury. The patient was discharged with a treatment plan that included valsartan, spironolactone, bisoprolol, ticagrelor, acetylsalicylic acid, and atorvastatin. This case highlights the diagnostic and treatment challenges of KS and stresses the need for early recognition and a team-based approach to achieve better clinical results.

articles.title: Additional B-Lymphocyte Stimulator Inhibitors Treatment Facilitated Glucocorticoid Withdrawal in Lupus Nephritis Patients: A Real-World Retrospective Observational Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoid (GC) withdrawal remains a major challenge for lupus nephritis (LN). In this 20-year retrospective cohort, we evaluated whether B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) inhibitors facilitated GC discontinuation. Among 702 LN patients, 553 were treated with standard-of-care alone, and 149 received add-on BLyS inhibitors (belimumab or telitacicept). Patients receiving BLyS inhibitors achieved a higher rate of GC withdrawal than those receiving standard-of-care alone (10.7% vs. 5.61%, p = 0.026). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed a higher cumulative incidence of GC withdrawal in the BLyS inhibitor group (p = 0.001). After adjusting for age, sex, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index, acute kidney injury, nephrotic syndrome, and renal histopathology, time-dependent Cox regression revealed that BLyS inhibitor therapy was independently associated with a higher GC withdrawal rate (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.97, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.11-15.5, p < 0.001). Exploratory subgroup analyses indicated that among GC‑discontinued patients, Class IV LN predominated in the BLyS inhibitor group, whereas Class V LN was more prevalent in controls. During follow-up, no renal flares occurred in BLyS inhibitor-treated patients who discontinued GCs, though there was no significant between-group difference. In conclusion, add-on BLyS inhibitor therapy may serve as a potential steroid withdrawal-permissive approach for LN, pending further prospective validation of its clinical applicability.

articles.title: Associations Between the Nutritional Risk Index for Japanese Hemodialysis Patients and the Risk of Bone Fractures in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis: The Q-Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis have elevated fracture risk, partly owing to undernutrition and protein-energy wasting. The Nutritional Risk Index for Japanese Hemodialysis Patients (NRI-JH) has been proposed as a surrogate marker of protein-energy wasting; however, its association with fracture risk has not been evaluated.

STUDY DESIGN: Multicenter, prospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: This study analyzed 3,038 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis, enrolled in the Q-Cohort Study.

EXPOSURE: The baseline NRI-JH was calculated based on age, sex, body mass index, and serum levels of albumin, creatinine, and total cholesterol, and patients were categorized into 3 groups based on baseline NRI-JH values: group 1, 0-2; group 2, 3-6; and group 3, 7-13.

OUTCOME: First occurrence of clinically diagnosed bone fractures.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Incidence rates were evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risk models (with death as a competing event) were used to estimate HRs and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up period of 4 years, 140 fractures occurred. Groups 2 and 3 had a significantly higher incidence of fractures than group 1 (log-rank test; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, fracture risk remained higher in group 2 (HR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.24-3.06) and group 3 (HR, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.25-3.38) than in group 1. Competing risk analyses yielded similar results. Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across age, sex, diabetic nephropathy, inflammation, and chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder parameters without significant interactions.

LIMITATIONS: Single baseline measurement of exposure; lack of differentiation between fracture types; potential residual confounding.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher NRI-JH values were independently associated with an increased fracture risk in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. The NRI-JH may serve as a comprehensive nutritional marker for identifying individuals at an elevated risk of fractures.

articles.title: Progression rates of aortic stenosis in patients with calcific and rheumatic heart disease in Saudi Arabia.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is the most prevalent type of AS in developed countries. However, in developing countries, rheumatic heart disease (RHD), which has a low progression rate, remains the prevalent type. This study compared the progression rates of AS between the National Guard cohort and Western populations.

DESIGN: This was a retrospective single-center cohort study.

PARTICIPANTS: Involving patients who underwent two echocardiographic examinations within an interval of at least 2 years.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Progression of aortic valve stenosis was assessed by measuring changes in the aortic valve area (AVA), peak aortic velocity, and mean aortic valve gradient.

RESULTS: In total, 1669 patients (median follow-up: 6.9 years) were included in the analysis. The overall annual AVA progression rate was 0.074 ± 0.1 cm2/year (median: -0.061 cm2/year). Patients with RHD had lower progression rates than those without RHD (25%-35%; AVA: -0.036 [-0.042, -0.030] cm2/year). Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who exhibited calcific AS had the highest progression rate (AVA: -0.102 ± 0.096 cm2/year). The overall progression rate of AS for the National Guard cohort was lower across all groups compared with that in Western populations (AVA: -0.08 to 0.12 cm2/year).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ESRD who had calcific AS had the highest progression rate. Meanwhile, patients with RHD exhibited the lowest progression rate. The high prevalence of calcific AS in our study shows the importance of adherence to the American College of Cardiology/European Society of Cardiology guidelines for disease management.

articles.title: Impact of body composition on toxicity and response in patients with advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma treated with BV-AVD.
articles.abstract: BV-AVD (brentuximab vedotin, doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine) has improved outcomes in advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma (ASHL); however, toxicity such as peripheral neuropathy (PN) remains a concern. Previous studies in oncology have demonstrated an association between sarcopenia and chemotoxicity. Therefore, we examined the effects of body composition parameters, including skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous fat (SF), and visceral fat (VF), along with quantitative biomarkers including metabolic tumor volume (MTV), on PN, treatment response, and progression-free survival. This study retrospectively reviewed the baseline, interim, and end-of-treatment (EOT) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) for 39 patients with ASHL treated with BV-AVD and assessed changes in MTV and body composition. MTV declined significantly from baseline to interim PET and EOT PET-CT (EOT PET), with no significant difference between the latter time points, indicating an early treatment response. SM:VF and SF:VF ratios followed a similar pattern, suggesting that changes in body composition including SM loss (sarcopenia) and changes in fat distribution (SF:VF), occurred early during treatment. Patients with stable SM:VF ratios were more likely to achieve a complete response (CR), whereas larger changes in SM:VF and SF:VF ratios and an early increase in VF were associated with failure to achieve CR, possibly due to increased inflammation. Stage IV disease and higher MTV were both associated with increased PN and may reflect the wider distribution of BV and an amplified inflammatory response. These findings demonstrate that body composition and PET-CT indices are relevant biomarkers in ASHL, and their integration with MTV may enhance risk stratification and deepen our understanding of toxicity risk.

articles.title: Stuck in the Traffic-Light: Moving Past Color Signals to Real Decisions in Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Therapy Management.
articles.journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
articles.abstract: Historically, the complexity of patients being evaluated for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge therapy (M-TEER) has been divided into 3 main categories: green zone: defined as cases where M-TEER is straightforward and not complex, yellow zone: cases with medium complexity where M-TEER is feasible but not entirely straightforward, and red zone: cases where you would not consider M-TEER as the first option and may be swayed toward consideration of other options like transcatheter mitral valve (MV) replacement or surgical management. However, the advancement in preprocedural planning with precise anatomical definition by 3-dimensional imaging modalities has changed how we address complex mitral regurgitation cases. The expansion of available devices for management of MV disease has changed the way we think about undertaking challenging M-TEER procedures. Management in the current era emphasizes meticulous preprocedural assessment of mitral regurgitation pathology, strategic planning for device implantation, judicious device choice, and early consideration of transcatheter MV replacement or other innovative transcatheter devices. This review article provides a comprehensive overview of the available data on M-TEER and outlines treatment strategies for complex cases within the context of contemporary transcatheter technologies.

articles.title: Fulminant necrotizing pancreatitis in 2 chinchillas (Chinchilla lanigera).
articles.journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne
articles.abstract: Two pet chinchillas were presented with acute anorexia and lethargy. Biochemistry revealed severe hyperglycemia and azotemia in both cases, with severe hyperkalemia in Case 1 and hyperphosphatemia in Case 2. Acidic urine with glucosuria and ketonuria was also observed in Case 1. Despite medical treatment including insulin therapy, both animals experienced a fulminant clinical course and died. Postmortem examination identified severe necrotizing pancreatitis with pulmonary congestion and edema in both cases. In addition, the chinchilla in Case 1 showed vasodilation with vascular necrosis and thrombosis in the pancreas and surrounding adipose tissues, whereas the animal in Case 2 displayed extensive renal medullary tubular necrosis with hemorrhage. The pathological findings suggested systemic inflammatory response syndrome with secondary hypotensive shock, acute renal failure, and multiple-organ dysfunction as the presumed causes of death. Key clinical message: Necrotizing pancreatitis should be considered early as a differential diagnosis in a chinchilla presented with acute circulatory compromise, renal dysfunction, and marked debilitation, particularly when severe hyperglycemia or diabetic-like metabolic abnormalities are present.

articles.title: Rationale and design of RECOVER - a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. Hence, they are becoming less capable of accounting for an increasingly diverse patient cohort. With a prospective long-term cohort, we aim to achieve an in-depth characterization of CR patients, enabling the delivery of more personalized care in the contemporary era.

METHODS: In this non-interventional, monocentric, prospective cohort study named RECOVER (Cardiac REhabilitation COhort at the Medicine Campus DaVos to invEstigate Recovery), we plan to include 10,000 patients over 10 years across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, heart failure) with data collected across the full spectrum of inpatient CR. Data acquisition is complemented through extensive biobanking allowing detailed phenotyping and biomarker profiling of patients. Follow-up assessments are conducted at 3 and 6 months, and yearly thereafter, up to 10 years. By harnessing novel devices, digital monitoring is employed to continuously capture a wealth of health-related parameters, such as blood pressure and accelerometry-based physical activity.

ADDITION TO THE FIELD AND LIMITATIONS: Given the substantial research gap in personalized CR, the RECOVER study provides the opportunity to systematically evaluate recovery patterns and treatment response across distinct cardiovascular subgroups. Due to the unique and highly innovative infrastructure available at the recruiting site, the monocentric design enables performance of an extensive standardized assessment. By incorporating digital technologies in conjunction with deep phenotypic and biomarker data, RECOVER holds promise to enable tailored CR strategies.

articles.title: Hepatoid Carcinoma of the Lung: A Rare Presentation.
articles.abstract: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the lung (HAL) is a rare pulmonary malignancy that resembles hepatocellular carcinoma morphologically and poses diagnostic challenges, particularly when alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is absent. We report a man in his 50s with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and a solitary 1.9-cm right upper lobe nodule. Percutaneous biopsy identified non-small cell carcinoma without establishing the subtype. Video-assisted thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymphadenectomy revealed a hepatoid tumour expressing HepPar-1 and CK7 but not AFP, arginase-1 or glypican-3. The absence of a hepatic lesion on staging imaging supported a pulmonary primary. The tumour was pT1bN0 with no clinically detected metastases. At 6 months after resection, there was no evidence of recurrence. This case illustrates the limitations of small biopsies and isolated immunohistochemical markers in diagnosing an AFP-negative pulmonary hepatoid tumour.

articles.title: Probable Stevens-Johnson Syndrome During Taletrectinib Treatment After Crizotinib-Related Rash in ROS1-Positive Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions to taletrectinib, a next-generation ROS1 inhibitor for ROS1-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer, remain poorly described. A 52-year-old woman with ROS1-rearranged lung adenocarcinoma developed a Grade 3 rash during crizotinib therapy. After improvement, taletrectinib was initiated. On Day 21, conjunctival hyperaemia appeared, followed by high fever, neutropenia, widespread trunk-dominant erythema, and lower-lip mucosal involvement. Although epidermal detachment, a positive Nikolsky sign, and characteristic epidermal necrosis were absent, and typical target lesions were not documented during the acute phase, the clinical course was considered consistent with probable Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Fever and ocular symptoms rapidly improved after taletrectinib discontinuation and systemic corticosteroid therapy. Infection and human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) reactivation were not identified, and ALDEN and Naranjo assessments supported a probable association with taletrectinib. During ROS1-TKI therapy, fever and neutropenia should prompt consideration of severe cutaneous adverse reactions as well as infection.

articles.title: Mixed Invasive Fungal Pneumonia Caused by Aspergillus, Candida, Mucor in an Immunocompromised Host.
articles.abstract: Invasive fungal pneumonia (IFP) is a life-threatening complication in immunocompromised patients, particularly those with hematologic malignancies. Mixed IFP are uncommon, given its substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a case of rapidly progressive mixed IFP caused by Aspergillus, Candida and Mucor species in a 60-year-old man with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma following chemotherapy. Despite early empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics and prompt initiation of antifungal therapy guided by serum galactomannan positivity and radiologic progression, the patient's clinical condition deteriorated. Bronchoscopy revealed extensive necrotic endobronchial lesions, and histopathologic examination confirmed simultaneous infection with three fungal pathogens. Although intensive treatment with an antifungal agent and mechanical ventilation were provided, the patient died of refractory respiratory failure within 1 week of hospitalization. This case highlights that clinicians should actively consider mixed fungal infection as a potential aetiology of IFP in immunocompromised patients, rather than assuming a single-pathogen process.

articles.title: Visualizing a Lung Opacity Behind Pleural Effusion Using Dynamic Chest Radiography.
articles.abstract: Dynamic chest radiography with bone suppression and pixel-value change analysis delineated a parenchymal abnormality obscured by pleural effusion on conventional portable chest radiography. This case demonstrates the visualization of a subtle lung abnormality using post-processed dynamic chest radiography.

articles.title: Hemorrhagic Papilledema in a Patient With End-Stage Renal Disease and Meningioma: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Anterior cranial fossa meningioma can present with a constellation of symptoms that pose a diagnostic challenge, especially in patients with significant comorbidities like end-stage renal disease (ESRD). We report a case where the classic triad of visual loss, headache, and anosmia was initially complicated by the patient's renal background and systemic inflammation. A 53-year-old woman with ESRD and hypertension presented with a one-month history of progressive, non-correctable bilateral visual loss and a two-week history of headache. She also reported complete anosmia. Her medication regimen was comprehensive for her comorbidities. Uncorrected and corrected visual acuity was 6/10 OD and 7/10 OS. Funduscopy revealed bilateral optic disc edema with peripapillary hemorrhages. The Marcus Gunn test was negative. Systemic inflammation was evidenced by an elevated ESR (51 mm/h) and a positive CRP. Brain MRI confirmed the presence of a meningioma. Her blood pressure was controlled at 130/83 mmHg. The patient's presentation is a classic depiction of an anterior cranial fossa meningioma, likely originating from the olfactory groove or planum sphenoidale. The tumor explains the anosmia via direct nerve compression and the papilledema via obstruction of CSF pathways and elevated intracranial pressure. The controlled blood pressure and the specific nature of the triad helped exclude hypertensive emergency and uremic encephalopathy as primary causes. The elevated inflammatory markers, while raising initial suspicion for vasculitis or other inflammatory conditions, are also a known, though less common, associated finding with meningioma. This case underscores the critical importance of pursuing a central nervous system (CNS) etiology for neurological symptoms, even in medically complex patients. The triad of papilledema, headache, and anosmia is highly suggestive of an anterior cranial fossa mass lesion and warrants prompt neuroimaging. Systemic inflammation should not prematurely divert the diagnostic workup from considering primary CNS tumors.

articles.title: Pinhole-Like Central Bronchial Narrowing: A Rare Reversible Manifestation of Eosinophilic Bronchial Inflammation.
articles.abstract: Recurrent atelectasis is occasionally encountered in clinical practice but may be attributed to repeated respiratory infections without thorough investigation, potentially delaying the diagnosis of the underlying cause. We report a 78-year-old woman with well-controlled asthma who developed recurrent right middle lobe and lingular atelectasis. Bronchoscopy revealed severe pinhole-like narrowing of multiple central bronchi. Although allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis and post-infectious cicatricial stenosis were initially considered, characteristic eosinophilic mucus impaction was absent, and endobronchial biopsy demonstrated marked eosinophilic inflammation of the bronchial wall with airway remodelling. Oral corticosteroid therapy resulted in resolution of the atelectasis and improvement of the bronchial narrowing. This case highlights eosinophilic bronchial inflammation as a rare but reversible cause of central bronchial narrowing and underscores the diagnostic value of endobronchial biopsy in patients with unexplained recurrent atelectasis.

articles.title: Tubulointerstitial Nephritis With Uveitis Syndrome: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
articles.abstract: TINU syndrome should be considered in any child presenting with unexplained renal dysfunction and uveitis. Early recognition and a multidisciplinary approach involving nephrology and ophthalmology are essential to prevent irreversible renal and ocular damage.

articles.title: Characteristics of Patients Involved With the Kidney Supportive Care Program: A Cohort Study of Routinely Collected Data.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: People with kidney failure face a significantly higher risk of death and symptom burden. We sought insights into the survival and symptom burden of people receiving medical management of kidney failure without dialysis.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: People with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≤ 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 receiving nondialytic/conservative/palliative management and known to the Kidney Supportive Care Team in a tertiary care hospital.

PREDICTORS: eGFR at cohort entry, living arrangement, and history of ischemic heart disease, heart failure, or stroke, according to routine care databases.

OUTCOMES: Primary: median survival. Secondary: number of hospitalizations and symptom burden assessed through the Integrated Palliative Care Outcome Scale-Renal score.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cox regression survival modeling and descriptive statistics for hospitalizations and symptom burden.

RESULTS: The cohort included 223 people receiving care between January 2016 and April 2023, with a median age of 84 (interquartile range, 77-87) years. Median survival was 452 days (95% CI, 351-552). People with an eGFR of 11-15 mL/min/1.73 m2 at cohort entry had a median survival of 517 days (95% CI, 406-623); those with an eGFR of 6-10 mL/min/1.73 m2 had a median survival of 260 days (95% CI, 138-382), whereas people with an eGFR of < 5 mL/min/1.73 m2 had a median survival of 61 days (95% CI, 46-107). People living independently at home had significantly higher median survival (538 days), compared with assisted living at home (356 days) or living in a nursing home (232 days) (P < 0.05). The studied comorbidities were not predictive of survival. At year 1, the most prevalent symptom was weakness (60%) with median "moderate" severity, with similar findings at year 2.

LIMITATIONS: Single-center, retrospective study with univariable analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: The study provided valuable insights into life expectancy and symptom burden with kidney failure managed without dialysis, including the prognostic value of considering the baseline living situation in anticipating survival, to help guide clinicians facing the uncertainty of this clinical scenario.

articles.title: Low-Sodium Peritoneal Dialysis Solution (Na 126 mmol/L) for Enhanced Sodium Removal: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Fluid overload is a major cause of treatment failure in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD), and insufficient sodium removal is involved with this condition. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a novel low-sodium (LS) PD solution (Na 126 mmol/L, glucose 1.6%) combined with standard-sodium (SS) PD solutions as a new approach to enhance sodium removal.

STUDY DESIGN & PARTICIPANTS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group study, outpatient PD patients at 20 facilities in Japan were randomly assigned (2:1) to the LS PD solution group or the SS PD solution group (Na 135 mmol/L, glucose 1.35%).

EXPOSURE: The test solution replaced 1 daily exchange and was combined with at least 1 standard PD solution. Patients who met dose-escalation criteria at week 4 switched to twice-daily dosing.

OUTCOMES: The primary outcome was the change in daily peritoneal sodium removal from baseline to week 8. Secondary outcomes included peritoneal sodium removal per bag exchange, total daily (peritoneal and urinary) sodium, water removal, and dialysis adequacy.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Efficacy, including sodium removal in PD treatment, was analyzed in the full analysis set; safety was assessed in all patients.

RESULTS: The mean change in daily peritoneal sodium removal was significantly higher in the LS PD solution group (n = 51, 28.7 ± 36.2 mmol/d) than in the SS PD solution group (n = 27, -6.3 ± 26.2 mmol/d; P < 0.001). Other outcomes showed no significant differences. Drug-related adverse events (mainly hyponatremia) were observed in the LS PD solution group; however, they were generally mild and completely reversible.

LIMITATIONS: Participants with relatively preserved residual kidney function and incremental PD were overrepresented.

CONCLUSIONS: The LS PD solution, when combined with standard PD solutions, increased sodium removal without compromising dialysis adequacy or residual kidney function.

articles.title: Protein-bound Uremic Toxin Lowering Effects of Sevelamer in Hyperphosphatemic Hemodialysis Patients: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: p-Cresyl sulfate (pCS) is an important protein-bound uremic toxin associated with high cardiovascular mortality in patients receiving long-term hemodialysis (HD). Data regarding pCS lowering and the pleiotropic effects of sevelamer are limited in patients receiving long-term HD.

STUDY DESIGN: Open-label, multicenter randomized controlled trial.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients with hyperphosphatemia receiving long-term HD.

EXPOSURES: Patients were randomly assigned to receive either sevelamer or calcium carbonate as phosphate binders for 24 weeks.

OUTCOMES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in pCS change over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels, intact parathyroid hormone levels, cardio-ankle vascular index, and adverse event rates.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Mean differences between groups were analyzed using a linear mixed model. Multivariate logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with decreased pCS levels.

RESULTS: A total of 128 patients were enrolled, 4 dropped out, and 124 were analyzed. Residual kidney function (RKF) ≥100 mL/day was present in 47.7%. Both groups achieved significant phosphate reduction. Mean changes in pCS did not differ significantly between groups: 0.70 mg/L (95% CI, -1.04 to 2.44) in the sevelamer group versus -0.09 mg/L (95% CI, -1.70 to 1.51) in the calcium carbonate group (P = 0.07). However, sevelamer was associated with a smaller increase in cardio-ankle vascular index than calcium carbonate (adjusted mean change difference -0.63 [95% CI, -1.22 to -0.04]; P = 0.04). Preserved RKF and high-dose phosphate binders were independently associated with decreased pCS levels.

LIMITATIONS: Change in pCS is only a surrogate marker for cardiovascular events. The study may have been underpowered, or the sevelamer dose and treatment duration may have been insufficient.

CONCLUSIONS: pCS levels were not significantly changed in both groups. However, the increase in cardio-ankle vascular index was smaller with sevelamer than with calcium carbonate, independent of pCS change. Further trials with larger samples and longer treatment durations are warranted.

articles.title: Hepatoprotective Effect of Nicotinamide Mononucleotide on High-Fat Diet-Induced Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Mice.
articles.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a significant global public health issue characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is a crucial cofactor in cellular metabolism across mammalian organs. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), an important intermediate in NAD+ salvage synthesis, may influence high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hepatic steatosis. An HFD-induced NAFLD mouse model was established in C57BL/6 mice, followed by NMN administration for 8 weeks. HepG2 cells were treated with palmitic acid and co-incubated with NMN to establish an in vitro lipid accumulation model. Network pharmacology analysis and transcriptomic profiling were performed to identify potential molecular targets and pathways involved in the protective effects of NMN against NAFLD. Lipid accumulation was evaluated by H&E staining and Oil Red O staining. Serum lipid metabolism parameters were measured using assay kits. Quantitative RT-PCR and Western blotting were used to examine the expression of pathway-related genes and proteins to investigate the potential mechanism by which NMN alleviates hepatic steatosis. Compared with the HFD model group, NMN intervention significantly reduced body weight and alleviated hepatic steatosis. It also lowered levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), triglycerides, total cholesterol, and fasting blood glucose, while increasing high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels. Liver PPAR-γ levels decreased, while HNF4α and SHBG levels increased. These findings suggest that the protective effects of NMN on HFD-induced hepatic steatosis are associated with decreased hepatic PPAR-γ expression and increased HNF4α and SHBG expression. NMN showed protective effects against HFD-induced NAFLD, which were associated with improvements in hepatic lipid metabolism. By integrating network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, and experimental validation, this study provides initial evidence regarding molecular changes associated with the effects of NMN in NAFLD.

Short- and Long-Term Control of Hypertension After Bariatric Surgery: A 10-Year Prospective Study.
articles.abstract: Current guidelines support bariatric surgery (BS) as an effective treatment mainly for patients with severe obesity and poorly controlled hypertension. However, evidence in non-severely obese Asian populations remains limited. This multicenter prospective cohort study included 248 Chinese patients with obesity and hypertension who underwent BS between 2010 and 2019 and were followed for up to 10 years. An exploratory mechanistic substudy (n = 14) evaluated 24-h ambulatory blood pressure (BP), various biomarkers, and urinary electrolytes before and after BS. Compared with baseline, adjusted mean systolic blood pressure (SBP) was lower by 16.4, 14.8, 15.1, 18.0, and 15.2 mmHg, while diastolic blood pressure (DBP) decreased by 11.4, 9.1, 9.9, 10.5, and 11.4 mmHg at 3 months, 6 months, and 1, 5, 10 years postoperatively. During postoperative Days 1 to 7 (POD1-7), mean SBP and DBP dropped by 8.6 and 10.4 mmHg, and the proportion achieving BP < 140/90 mmHg increased to 62.9% and remained at 70.8% even 10 years later. The substudy has observed that early BP reduction was accompanied by increased electrolytes and water excretion, as well as a transient suppression of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS)-related biomarkers, providing a direction for future in-depth exploration. These findings suggest that BS in Chinese patients was followed by rapid BP reductions, with lower BP observed among the smaller subsets assessed longer term, including those without severe obesity. Trial Registration: NCT07183137.
