articles.title: Rosa rugosa Root Extract as a Functional Food Ingredient, Mitigating UVB-Induced Skin Aging Through MAPK/AP-1 and AGE-RAGE Pathway Modulation.
articles.abstract: Rosa rugosa root extract (RR-r) has been used in East Asian medicine to treat metabolic disorders, including diabetes and alcohol-induced liver toxicity. Although RR-r has been demonstrated to exhibit anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, further research is required to elucidate its protective effects against ultraviolet B (UVB)-induced skin photoaging. In this study, high-performance liquid chromatography was used to identify rutin as the major indicator compound of RR-r. The photoprotective activity of RR-r was evaluated using a mouse model of UVB-induced skin damage. Mice were orally administered RR-r (100 or 200 mg/kg) for 8 weeks during UVB irradiation. RR-r significantly alleviated UVB-induced wrinkle formation, epidermal thickening, and collagen fiber degradation. The assessment of skin morphology and hydration was conducted through the use of histological staining (H&E and Masson's trichrome), wrinkle and moisture analysis, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay quantification of hyaluronic acid. Western blotting revealed that RR-r increased pro-collagen type I, tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 1, hyaluronan, collagen-1 while reducing the matrix metalloproteinase family, hyaluronidase 1 and hyaluronidase 2. A further mechanistic analysis revealed that RR-r inhibited UVB-induced phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway components and downstream activator protein-1 factors. Furthermore, RR-r significantly suppressed UVB-induced accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and expression of their receptor, RAGE. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that oral RR-r effectively protects against UVB-induced photoaging by regulating wrinkle-related proteins, enhancing skin hydration, and modulating MAPK/AP-1 and AGE-RAGE signaling. Thus, RR-r may represent a promising natural candidate for skin anti-aging interventions.

articles.title: Quercetin and Cardiovascular Health: An Evidence-Based Review of Risk Factors and Treatments.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) encompass a variety of conditions, including coronary heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, rheumatic heart disease, and venous thromboembolism. Natural products exhibit a range of pharmacological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunoregulatory effects. This review evaluates the potential therapeutic effects of quercetin on factors contributing to cardiovascular disease risk. Quercetin, a flavonoid recognized for its strong antioxidant capabilities, has demonstrated beneficial effects in alleviating pathological cardiac conditions such as hypertrophy and ischemia across multiple in vitro and in vivo experimental models. This review compiles evidence demonstrating quercetin's ability to reduce cardiac hypertrophy and apoptosis in cardiomyocytes through modulation of key signaling pathways. Specifically, quercetin treatment resulted in significant upregulation of protective proteins such as silent information regulatory factor 1 (SIRT1), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator-1α (PGC-1α), and Bcl-2, coupled with downregulation of pro-apoptotic Bax. Quercetin improved calcium channel function, enhanced myocardial contractility, and decreased oxidative stress markers, leading to improved survival rates of cardiomyocytes under ischemic conditions. Quercetin administration has been shown to lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure and reduce cardiac hypertrophy. Additionally, quercetin positively influences lipid profiles by decreasing total cholesterol, triglycerides, and low-density lipoprotein while enhancing overall lipid metabolism. Collectively, these findings highlight quercetin as a promising candidate in preclinical models of cardiac hypertrophy and ischemia. However, further research-particularly well-designed clinical trials-is essential to validate these findings and determine the translational potential through dietary interventions of quercetin in human cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Right Angle, Wrong Assumptions: A Case of Endobronchial Mucormycosis Presenting as a Pedunculated Mass Mimicking Malignancy.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary mucormycosis is an aggressive, angioinvasive fungal infection that carries high mortality. Endobronchial involvement is rare and may present as a pedunculated mass with associated parenchymal consolidation, mimicking lung cancer. We present a case of a 52-year-old male smoker with poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a history of pulmonary tuberculosis 19 years prior presented with a 6-month history of cough and hemoptysis. Suspecting tuberculosis reactivation, he was empirically treated with anti-tuberculosis therapy (ATT) for 6 months without clinical response. High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the chest revealed a 4.9 cm hyperdense necrotic consolidation patch with internal calcification in the right upper lobe (RUL). Flexible video-bronchoscopy demonstrated a pedunculated mass in the posterior segment of the RUL, clinically concerning for lung cancer. Biopsy of tissue revealed extensive necrosis, hyalinization and thick-walled, broad, non-septate fungal hyphae with characteristic right-angle branching and spores, confirming pulmonary mucormycosis without evidence of malignancy or granulomatous disease. Endobronchial mucormycosis should be considered in patients with diabetes, chronic airway disease or post-tuberculosis lung disease who present with non-resolving endobronchial masses. Early bronchoscopic tissue sampling is essential to avoid delayed diagnosis and inappropriate empirical therapy.

articles.title: A Mixed-Methods Assessment of Health Care Professionals' Perspectives on CRRT Delivery and Opportunities for Improvement.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the preferred dialysis modality for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury, yet its delivery and quality vary across institutions. This study aimed to identify gaps in CRRT practice and explore strategies to improve CRRT delivery from the perspective of multidisciplinary health care professionals.

STUDY DESIGN: Convergent parallel mixed methods.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: This study was conducted during the 2024 CRRT Academy and included multidisciplinary participants comprising trainees (residents and fellows), clinicians (nephrologists and intensivists), clinical staff (nurses, nurse practitioners, and pharmacists), and industry/research affiliates.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Quantitative data were collected using a survey assessing CRRT practices, standardization, and collection of quality metrics. Qualitative data were obtained through 5 semistructured focus group discussions (4 with participants and 1 with CRRT Academy faculty) and were analyzed using a combined inductive-deductive thematic approach in NVivo 15.

RESULTS: There were 83 participants: 54 trainees, 19 clinicians, 8 clinical staff, and 2 industry/research affiliates, with 10-24 participants in each focus group. The following 4 key themes were identified as relevant to improve CRRT delivery from participant focus groups: (1) teamwork and multidisciplinary communication, (2) collection and tracking of CRRT-relevant metrics, (3) protocol standardization while allowing flexibility to individualize care, and (4) education for clinicians and clinical staff. The faculty focus group emphasized the need for institutional financial support and leadership-driven quality improvement (QI) initiatives, highlighting the importance of nephrologist advocacy. Participants reported significant variability in CRRT processes, QI data collection, and education across institutions, with limited adoption of CRRT key performance indicators owing to lack of consensus and workflow integration challenges.

LIMITATIONS: Participants primarily represented academic centers and the majority were trainees, which may limit generalizability of the findings. However, given the paucity of mixed-methods evidence about current CRRT practice, this study provides novel insights that can help advance standardization.

CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores key areas for improving CRRT delivery, including interprofessional collaboration, data-driven QI, protocol standardization, and targeted education. Addressing these themes may help improve CRRT processes of care and patient-centered outcomes.

articles.title: Comment on "Adequate enrollment of women in cardiovascular drug trials and the need for sex-specific assessment and reporting".
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

articles.title: A Fatal Case of Pulmonary Tumor Thrombotic Microangiopathy Originating From Primary Bladder Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy is a rare, fatal complication of malignancy, with few reports involving bladder cancer.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 81-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presented with hematuria and progressive exertional dyspnea. Imaging showed an invasive bladder tumor with lymph node metastases. Echocardiography suggested pulmonary hypertension, although invasive confirmation was unavailable. Recurrent perioperative oxygen desaturation preceded fatal deterioration 2 days after transurethral resection. Autopsy revealed primary bladder adenocarcinoma, signet ring cell subtype, and microscopic pulmonary tumor emboli with fibrin thrombi, fibrous intimal thickening, and recanalization. These findings supported pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy. Distinct gastrointestinal tumors and matching bladder and metastatic morphology supported a bladder origin.

CONCLUSION: Pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy should be considered in patients with bladder tumors and progressive dyspnea. Recurrent desaturation and right heart abnormalities warrant reassessment despite preserved oxygen saturation. Autopsy vascular findings were essential to distinguish this condition from simple pulmonary tumor embolism.

articles.title: May the POCUS Be With You! A Call to Radiologists and Sonographers. A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: Australasian journal of ultrasound in medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinicians across many specialties now perform point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) as a question-driven bedside examination. Emergency physicians, intensivists, cardiologists (focused cardiac ultrasound), anaesthetists, respiratory physicians, gastroenterologists and gynaecologists all perform bedside scans. A comprehensive, protocol-driven study with a multi-organ survey, Doppler interrogation and structured report remains the work of radiologists and sonographers. Confusion at this interface breeds friction among professionals.

DISCUSSION: This narrative review synthesises the POCUS literature with position statements from the ASUM, ACEM, ACEP, ASE, SRU/ACR, ANZCA, CICM, RANZCOG, RACS, RANZCR, EFSUMB, EuSEM and WFUMB. Three axes define POCUS: setting, completeness and operator credentials. POCUS is a spectrum. Depending on the operator's skill, qualification and available time, a clinician scan can answer a focused question in seconds or approach a comprehensive examination. We compared the Australasian and United States regulatory environments, where United States reimbursement drives stronger governance, and addressed quality assurance, false-positive and false-negative risk, image archiving, the sonographer-clinician relationship and POCUS practice across the specialties that scan at the bedside.

CONCLUSION: POCUS and comprehensive departmental ultrasound complement each other. Clinician-performed ultrasonography has become a genuine multispecialty movement. The overdue step is to invite radiologists and sonographers, the workforce that anchors comprehensive ultrasound, into this movement. Now is the time for interdisciplinary teaching and knowledge sharing: shared image archives, joint credentialing, combined audits, reciprocal teaching, joint research and shared simulations across every specialty that performs bedside scans.

articles.title: A look into adverse renal effects of proton pump inhibitors.
Morinda Officinalis Oligosaccharides Alleviate Post-Stroke Depression-Like Behaviors Alongside Increased Gut Microbial Diversity and Butyrate Levels and Reduced Hippocampal Pla2g4a Expression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a common and debilitating complication after cerebral ischemia, yet mechanism-based therapies remain an urgent unmet need. The microbiota-gut-brain axis has been implicated in PSD pathophysiology, but the precise molecular pathways are largely elusive. Morinda officinalis oligosaccharides (MOO), a clinically approved antidepressant in China, exhibit poor oral absorption, raising the possibility of a gut-dependent mechanism.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Male C57BL/6J mice were subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) followed by 21 days of chronic restraint stress (CRS) to establish a PSD model. MOO (50 mg/kg/day) was administered via gavage from Day 7 to 27. Depression-like behaviors, 16S rRNA-based gut microbiota profiling, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) quantification, intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity assessments, and hippocampal proteomics were performed. The transferability of MOO-associated fecal effects was assessed using a donor-controlled fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) design. The butyrate-Pla2g4a relationship was further examined by sodium butyrate supplementation and AAV-mediated hippocampal Pla2g4a overexpression.

KEY RESULTS: MOO administration altered gut microbial composition, increased the abundance of probiotics and decreased the abundance of harmful bacteria, and was accompanied by increased fecal butyrate levels. The donor-controlled FMT experiment provided preliminary evidence that fecally transferable factors from MOO-treated PSD donors may contribute to behavioral improvements in PSD recipients. MOO and sodium butyrate treatment were associated with improved indices of intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity. Hippocampal proteomics identified Pla2g4a, a phospholipase linked to neuroinflammation, as a candidate molecule related to the observed effects. Both MOO and sodium butyrate treatment were associated with reduced hippocampal Pla2g4a expression, and Pla2g4a expression was inversely correlated with butyrate levels. Hippocampal Pla2g4a overexpression attenuated the behavioral improvements associated with sodium butyrate treatment, supporting the functional involvement of Pla2g4a in the response to sodium butyrate.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: MOO treatment was associated with improved depression-like behaviors in PSD mice, accompanied by gut microbial alterations, increased fecal butyrate, improved barrier integrity, and reduced hippocampal Pla2g4a expression. FMT findings provided preliminary evidence that fecally transferable factors from MOO-treated donors may contribute to behavioral improvements, while Pla2g4a overexpression attenuated the behavioral effects of sodium butyrate. These findings highlight a potential association among MOO, gut-derived butyrate, barrier integrity, and hippocampal Pla2g4a in PSD.

articles.title: Parent's and Service Provider's Perceptions of Family Involvement in Inclusive Early Childhood Education: Adaptation and Psychometric Validation of the Arabic Family Involvement Questionnaire.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to adapt the Family Involvement Questionnaire (FIQ) into Arabic for use in the Saudi research context. The adaptation involved translating the instrument, producing the Arabic version (FIQ-A) and culturally modifying selected items. The study then examined the psychometric properties and suitability of the FIQ-A for exploring parents' and service providers' perceptions of family involvement in inclusive early childhood education settings in Saudi Arabia.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The FIQ-A instrument created for this study was administered to participants from inclusive early childhood settings in Riyadh. The sample consisted of 100 parents and 35 service providers. The instrument measured three dimensions of family involvement: school-based involvement, home-based involvement and home-school conferencing. Descriptive statistics and reliability analyses were conducted to evaluate the psychometric properties of the scale and participants' perceptions of family involvement.

RESULTS: Cronbach's alpha coefficients were α = 0.73 for school-based involvement, α = 0.89 for home-based involvement and α = 0.86 for home-school conferencing, demonstrating acceptable to high reliability across the three dimensions. Parents reported higher levels of home-based activities (M = 3.43 vs. 2.64) and home-school conferencing (M = 3.40 vs. 2.66) compared with school-based involvement (M = 3.07 vs. 2.56) than service providers (all p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The FIQ-A instrument demonstrated suitable psychometric properties, and the findings indicated that families were willing and prepared to engage in their children's education. Service providers were also ready to facilitate and support this engagement. Overall, these findings underscore the importance of strengthening multiple forms of family involvement to promote inclusive practices and support the participation of children with disabilities in high-quality early childhood education settings.

articles.title: The Experiences and Needs of Nursing Staff During Patients' ICU-To-Ward Transition: A Meta-Synthesis of Qualitative Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care unit (ICU) transitional care ensures continuous care for patients transferring from the ICU to general wards. Relevant qualitative studies show that nurses play a vital role here, so exploring their real experiences and needs is essential for nursing development.

AIM: To summarise the current qualitative evidence on the experiences and needs of nursing staff during ICU transitional care.

STUDY DESIGN: A meta-synthesis of qualitative studies retrieved through a search conducted in China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang, VIP Database, Cochrane Library, PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL and Embase from inception to June 2025. All studies that presented qualitative findings on the experiences, feelings and needs of nursing staff, based on participants' reports, were included. Data extracted included publication year, location, sample size, study design, data collection method, phenomenon of interest and all qualitative themes identified.

FINDINGS: Thirteen studies were selected for inclusion, resulting in four synthesised findings: the practical challenges faced by nursing staff during the ICU transition period, their perceptions and attitudes towards transitional care, their supportive needs for transitional care and recommendations for improving transitional care.

CONCLUSIONS: The provision of transitional care services by nursing staff is influenced by factors such as existing medical resources, psychological support, workflows and organisational structures. These can guide nursing administrators and healthcare institutions in addressing the occupational needs of nursing personnel, optimising transitional care interventions and promoting the high-quality development of transitional care practices.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Despite cultural differences, the experiences and needs of nursing staff during the transition period in the ICU reflect commonalities across cultures. The review gives specific advice for ICU transition care, including establishing effective communication models, psychological support and professional training, establishing ICU liaison nurses and formulating standardised ICU transition procedures.

articles.title: Apigenin and Placental β-Endorphin Signaling: A Hypothesis-Generating Mechanistic Review.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.abstract: The placenta functions as a dynamic endocrine hub that translates maternal exposures into offspring developmental programming, consistent with the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) framework. Beta-endorphin (β-EP), a placental POMC-derived opioid peptide, signals through MOR/DOR/KOR receptors to regulate angiogenesis, immune tolerance, oxidative stress, inflammation, and nutrient transport. Apigenin, a dietary flavone found in parsley, chamomile, and celery, modulates several pathways that overlap with this axis, including CREB/PKA signaling, DNA methyltransferase activity, Nrf2, NF-κB/NLRP3, and Foxp3+ Treg differentiation, although most supporting evidence derives from non-placental systems such as cancer lines, keratinocytes, and macrophages. This review proposes that apigenin may amplify placental β-EP signaling across three conceptual tiers: a biosynthetic tier involving CREB/PKA-mediated POMC activation and 11β-HSD1 inhibition; a receptor-level tier involving DNMT1/3a inhibition and OPRM1 demethylation; and an effector-level tier involving Nrf2 activation, NF-κB/NLRP3 suppression, and Treg expansion, the last representing the strongest trophoblast-level evidence. Given reported β-EP dysregulation in preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and intrauterine growth restriction, apigenin's relevance to these disorders remains an untested hypothesis rather than a validated therapeutic strategy, informed by a structured, non-systematic literature search (1986-2026).

articles.title: Estimating magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction from ultrasound attenuation and clinical parameters in pediatric hepatic steatosis: development of a prediction model.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter (UGAP) for pediatric hepatic steatosis and developed a multivariable model to estimate magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) from ultrasound and clinical variables.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included pediatric patients who underwent UGAP measurement and MRI-PDFF assessment within 3 months of each other. UGAP performance in detecting moderate-to-severe (≥S2) and severe (S3) steatosis was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Multivariable models were developed using linear regression and a random forest algorithm with five-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Among 45 patients (33 male and 12 female; median age, 12 years), median UGAP and MRI-PDFF values were 0.83 dB/cm/MHz and 22%, respectively. UGAP correlated moderately with MRI-PDFF (ρ=0.596, P<0.001). The AUC was 0.74 for both ≥S2 and S3 steatosis (95% confidence intervals [CIs], 0.58 to 0.91 and 0.60 to 0.89, respectively), and two discordant cases were identified. A model incorporating UGAP, age, height, and liver size outperformed UGAP alone in detecting ≥S2 steatosis (optimism-corrected AUC, 0.882 vs. 0.744; P=0.01). In the machine learning analysis, the model showed stable performance during cross-validation, with an AUC of 0.789 (95% CI, 0.649 to 0.928) for ≥S2 steatosis and an R² of 0.663 for continuous MRI-PDFF prediction.

CONCLUSION: UGAP correlated moderately with MRI-PDFF and showed fair performance in grading pediatric hepatic steatosis. Combining UGAP with clinical parameters significantly improved MRI-PDFF estimation, providing a practical screening tool for hepatic steatosis when MRI is unavailable. External validation is needed.

articles.title: The role of artificial intelligence in predicting late-onset intrauterine growth restriction in singleton pregnancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Late-onset intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is difficult to detect and is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning, for predicting late-onset IUGR in singleton pregnancies.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies published during the past decade that used AI to predict IUGR. Nineteen studies including 13,379 pregnancies were analyzed. Sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratios were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was estimated in STATA.

RESULTS: In the primary analysis (one model per study, k=17), pooled sensitivity was 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89), specificity was 0.89 (95% CI, 0.85 to 0.91), the positive and negative likelihood ratios were 6.6 (95% CI, 5.3 to 8.1) and 0.22 (95% CI, 0.16 to 0.30), and the AUC was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.91 to 0.95). Estimates were unchanged when all model entries were included (k=51). No threshold effect or funnel-plot asymmetry was detected. Subgroup estimates for support vector machines, random forests, and logistic regression were similar but reflected indirect comparisons.

CONCLUSION: AI/ML models showed high pooled discriminative accuracy for late-onset IUGR. However, the evidence derives mainly from retrospective, single-center case-control studies without external validation; calibration was reported in six of 19 studies and decision-curve analysis in none. These estimates are an optimistic upper bound, not evidence of superiority over current ultrasound practice.

articles.title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
articles.abstract: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

articles.title: Assessing the Relative Contribution of Pre-Deployment Abroad Versus In-Mission Dirofilaria immitis Infections in French Military Working Dogs Screened Post-Mission: A Quantitative Risk Assessment.
articles.journal: Risk analysis : an official publication of the Society for Risk Analysis
articles.abstract: Dirofilaria immitis (D. immitis) is a mosquito-borne nematode responsible for canine cardiopulmonary dirofilariasis, a parasitic infection widely distributed worldwide and established in mainland France, particularly in southern regions. Military working dogs (MWDs) may be at increased risk of exposure to vector-borne pathogens because of their predominantly outdoor lifestyle and frequent missions abroad. Nevertheless, D. immitis infection remains sporadic in this population, likely due to well-implemented medical prophylaxis. The aim of this study was to investigate the likely origin of D. immitis infections detected in MWD during post-mission screening using a quantitative risk analysis approach. Scenario trees were developed to describe the sequences of events leading to the return of an infected dog from a mission abroad, accounting for parasite biology, prophylactic measures, and compliance. The model estimated a mean annual number of 4.25 infected MWD returning from missions out of an average annual population of 466 returning dogs, of which 79% were detected through post-mission screening. Most infections were likely acquired before deployment, either during previous missions, at the breeding facility before purchase, or within mainland France. Only 7.9% of infections acquired during missions were expected to be detected by testing performed at the end of the post-mission quarantine period. Alternative scenarios highlighted the effectiveness of chemoprophylaxis, as its absence was associated with a 3.2-fold increase in the number of infected dogs. Simulations also showed that extending the interval between return and testing would substantially improve the detection of mission-acquired infections. These findings support the continued use of preventive measures while questioning the adequacy of current post-mission screening alone for identifying D. immitis infections acquired during deployment.

articles.title: The impact of defects of the atrial septum on procedural complexity, complications, and outcomes of transvenous lead extraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with defects of the atrial septum (DAS) undergoing transvenous lead extraction (TLE) may be at increased risk of systemic embolism due to transient right-to-left shunting. However, data on the prevalence and clinical relevance of DAS in patients undergoing TLE remain limited.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 3637 patients undergoing TLE between 2006 and 2024 with complete preprocedural assessment of the atrial septum and at least 3 years of follow-up. We evaluated the prevalence of DAS and its association with procedural complexity, major complications, and survival.

RESULTS: DAS was identified in 3.71% of patients. Patent foramen ovale was present in 2.45%, secundum atrial septal defect in 1.15%, and both defects in 0.08%. Most defects were small, with predominant left-to-right shunting. Patients with DAS more frequently had lead-related infective endocarditis and vegetations on transesophageal echocardiography (p < 0.001). TLE procedures in patients with DAS were more complex, with longer extraction times and more frequent use of advanced extraction tools. Despite higher predicted procedural risk, the incidence of major complications, including stroke, was low. DAS was not associated with increased in-hospital, 30-day, 1-year, or 3-year mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large TLE cohort, DAS was uncommon and associated with greater procedural complexity, but not with a higher incidence of major complications or worse long-term survival. Clinically apparent systemic embolic events were rare.

articles.title: Single-cell transcriptome atlas reveals a WRKY33-HSP81 regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid-mediated defense against Sclerotium rolfsii in Dendrobium officinale.
articles.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Plants employ cell-type-specific transcriptional programs to defend against pathogens, yet the cellular heterogeneity of immune responses in the medicinal orchid Dendrobium officinale Kimura et Migo remains largely unexplored. A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the D. officinale stem base upon Sclerotium rolfsii infection was constructed, profiling over 20 000 cells across 12 and 24 h post-infection. A total of 21 cell clusters were resolved into 6 major cell types-epidermal, ground tissue parenchyma, proliferating, xylem, phloem, and vascular bundle parenchyma cells-with identities validated by fluorescence in situ hybridization. Cell-type-specific analyses revealed that epidermal and phloem cells mounted early defense responses, while xylem cells exhibited the most extensive transcriptional reprogramming at 24 hpi, coinciding with the activation of lignin biosynthesis pathways. WRKY33 was identified as a central transcriptional activator that directly binds W-box motifs in the promoters of lignin biosynthetic genes C4H and HCT, promoting lignin deposition and enhancing disease resistance. Conversely, the nuclear-localized chaperone HSP81 physically interacts with WRKY33 and functions as a broad regulator of multiple transcription factors via co-factor sequestration, thereby compromising defense when overexpressed. These findings uncover a WRKY33-HSP81 regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid-mediated defense in D. officinale, providing a high-resolution cellular framework for understanding plant immunity and offering potential targets for improving disease resistance in this economically valuable species.

articles.title: Huaier Attenuates Renal Injury in Type 2 Diabetic Nephropathy by Ameliorating Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Inhibiting Tubular Epithelial Cell Apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major microvascular complication of Type 2 diabetes, with renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) apoptosis playing a pivotal role in its progression. The aqueous extract of Trametes robiniophila Murr. (Huaier) has shown renoprotective effects, but its specific molecular mechanisms in DN remain to be fully elucidated.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of Huaier aqueous extract on DN and verify whether its anti-apoptotic mechanism is mediated through the Wnt/β-catenin pathway using the pathway activator SKL2001.

METHODS: In vivo, KKAy Type 2 diabetic mice were treated with Huaier (5 g/kg/day) for 12 weeks to evaluate renal function and histopathology. In vitro, HK-2 cells were treated with high glucose and palmitate (HG + PA) to induce injury. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway activator SKL2001 was employed to determine if activating this pathway could abolish the protective effects of Huaier.

RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis indicates that the regulation of apoptosis is the primary mechanism by which Huaier improves DN. In vivo, Huaier reduced UACR and improved renal histopathology in KKAy mice. Consistently, TUNEL staining and molecular analysis confirmed that Huaier significantly suppressed RTECs apoptosis within the renal tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that Huaier significantly inhibited HG + PA-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and RTECs apoptosis. Notably, the administration of SKL2001 effectively reversed these protective effects, leading to increased β-catenin expression and elevated apoptosis levels despite Huaier treatment.

CONCLUSION: Huaier aqueous extract mitigates RTECs apoptosis and renal injury in Type 2 diabetic nephropathy by suppressing the Wnt5a/β-catenin signaling pathway.

articles.title: Correction to "Impact of Imatinib Therapy on Immunometabolism to Promote β-Cell Survival in Diabetes".
A Pilot Study to Describe Symptomatic Hyperammonemia Secondary to Recombinant Erwinia Asparaginase.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asparaginase therapy is essential for the treatment of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LLy). For patients who develop hypersensitivity to a first-line Escherichia coli (E. coli)-derived product, the standard of care is to transition to an Erwinia-derived product. Given that all asparaginase products exert their antileukemic effects by enzymatically breaking down asparagine to aspartic acid and ammonia, elevations in ammonia levels are anticipated during asparaginase treatment. However, symptomatic hyperammonemia is not expected. Recombinant Erwinia asparaginase is relatively new to the market, and there have been several case reports of symptomatic hyperammonemia with this specific formulation.

OBJECTIVES: The primary objective of this prospective study was to establish the incidence of symptomatic hyperammonemia secondary to recombinant Erwinia asparaginase and to determine if a larger, multicenter trial was warranted. Additional objectives included identifying potential risk factors for symptomatic hyperammonemia.

METHODS: This single-center, prospective trial received institutional review board approval. Funding was provided by the Mayo Clinic Clinical and Translational Science Award (grant number: UL1TR002377) and the Mayo Clinic Department of Pharmacy. All patients treated by the pediatric hematology/oncology team at our institution who were receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase were eligible. Patients were excluded if they were less than 1 year of age at study entry. Enrolled participants had a baseline plasma ammonia level obtained, followed by twice weekly ammonia levels while receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase. Aside from baseline, all ammonia levels were trough levels measured either 48 h or 72 h after the previous dose.

RESULTS: Five patients were included, three of whom were male (60%). Three patients had T-cell ALL (60%), one patient had B-cell ALL (20%), and one patient had infantile B-cell ALL (20%). The median age was 5 years (range 1-14). Two patients were followed for two courses of recombinant Erwinia asparaginase, and the remaining patients were followed for a single course. Median baseline plasma ammonia level was 12 μmol/L. Median ammonia level while receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase was 146 μmol/L. Three patients (60%) developed symptomatic hyperammonemia with a median ammonia level of 174 μmol/L (range 108-343). The reported symptoms were nausea (100%), fatigue (66.7%), and decreased appetite (33.3%). The remaining two patients experienced asymptomatic hyperammonemia with a median ammonia level of 125 μmol/L (range 55-304).

CONCLUSIONS: Based on our small cohort, symptomatic hyperammonemia may be a common adverse effect for patients receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase. Evaluating plasma ammonia levels appears reasonable in patients who are experiencing nausea or other symptoms of hyperammonemia. Additional studies are warranted to further characterize this toxicity.

articles.title: Effects of Physical Activity Interventions on Body Composition in Korean Students With Intellectual Disabilities: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis examined the effects of physical activity interventions on body composition among students with intellectual disabilities in Korea and whether intervention characteristics explained differences in effects.

METHODS: A total of 21 studies yielding 76 effect sizes were synthesized using a multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with a correlated and hierarchical effects model and CR2 robust variance estimation.

RESULTS: Physical activity interventions produced a significant small-to-moderate positive effect on body composition (Hedges' g = 0.403, 95% CI = [0.209-0.597], p < 0.001), with significant heterogeneity. Categorical and continuous moderators were nonsignificant. Sensitivity analyses supported the positive effect, although the RCT-specific estimate was less precise and heterogeneous. GRADE certainty was low for both RCT and non-randomized evidence.

CONCLUSIONS: Physical activity appears beneficial for body composition, but the low certainty of evidence and lack of significant moderators preclude identification of a consistently superior intervention profile. Further rigorous research is needed to clarify optimal intervention characteristics.

articles.title: Inferior Frontal Gyrus Alterations in Freezing of Gait in Parkinson's Disease Without Evidence for Overall Hemispheric Lateralization: A Systematic Review and Activation Likelihood Estimation Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Freezing of gait (FOG) is one of the most debilitating motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD). Prior studies have suggested a potential right-hemispheric preference in the pathophysiology of FOG. Yet, there is limited evidence regarding which brain regions are most consistently associated with FOG and whether these alterations indeed show right-hemispheric lateralization. We aimed to identify brain regions associated with FOG based on multimodal neuroimaging findings and to examine their hemispheric lateralization. A systematic review across multiple neuroimaging modalities was performed, followed by an activation likelihood estimation (ALE) coordinate-based meta-analysis to assess convergent brain alterations in PD patients with FOG (freezers) versus those without FOG (nonfreezers). Hemispheric lateralization was assessed using the distribution of reported stereotactic coordinates. The systematic review included 108 articles, of which 33 were included in the primary ALE meta-analysis. We identified a significant convergent cluster in the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) pars opercularis/dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in PD freezers compared with nonfreezers. No evidence of overall hemispheric lateralization was observed based on the distribution of reported coordinates. Our findings identify the right IFG as a consistent neural correlate of FOG, potentially reflecting heightened frontal recruitment, with no clear evidence of hemispheric lateralization. The lack of further consistency in brain regions could reflect the known heterogeneity in the pathophysiology of FOG.

articles.title: Compression Stockings as Core Therapy for Symptomatic Orthostatic Hypertension in an Older Male: A Case Report.
Clinical PET/Computed Tomography Today: Essential Principles, Multimodality Applications, and Emerging Frontiers.
Interpreting Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/Computed Tomography: Challenges and Strategies for Diagnostic Precision.
articles.abstract: This article provides a practical, regionally organized approach to fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (CT) interpretation in oncology, highlighting key malignancies, characteristic metabolic patterns, common pitfalls, and the complementary roles of CT and MR imaging across the brain, head and neck, thorax, gastrointestinal tract, and musculoskeletal system.

articles.title: 18F-FDG PET/CT in Oncology Biologic, Technical, and Quantitative Foundations for Interpretation.
articles.abstract: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/computed tomography is a cornerstone of oncologic imaging, widely used for cancer diagnosis, staging, and surveillance. Accurate interpretation requires knowledge of the biological, technical, and quantitative factors influencing image formation and tracer uptake. This article reviews key determinants of FDG accumulation, including the Warburg effect, glycolytic enzyme expression, standardized uptake values measurements, and limitations of FDG PET/CT. It also discusses false-negative findings and common physiologic, inflammatory, and benign uptake patterns that may mimic malignancy, along with strategies for differentiation. Finally, technical factors affecting image quality, such as patient preparation and image reconstruction, are addressed.

articles.title: Key Technologies in PET Instrumentation and Image Generation.
articles.abstract: This article reviews PET instrumentation from the physical principles of positron decay and coincidence detection through detector technologies, image reconstruction, correction methods, quantitative interpretation, and emerging scanner designs. Emphasis is placed on how scintillator choice, photodetector readout, time-of-flight performance, attenuation and scatter correction, and reconstruction algorithms affect image quality, quantitative accuracy, radiation dose, acquisition time, and clinical workflow. The article also highlights current directions in total-body PET, dedicated organ-specific PET, PET/MR, PET/gamma imaging, and artificial intelligence-assisted reconstruction and image enhancement.

articles.title: The Principles of Radiopharmaceuticals in PET.
articles.abstract: PET is a functional imaging modality whose diagnostic power is dictated by the physical properties of positron-emitting radionuclides and the biological specificity of their carrier molecules. The article explores the paradigm shift from traditional metabolic imaging with [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose to the rapidly expanding field of theranostics, where receptor-specific agents targeting somatostatin receptors and prostate-specific membrane antigen are currently being used to drive precision oncology and predictive dosimetry. For the practicing radiologist or nuclear medicine physician, mastery of these underlying principles is essential for ensuring diagnostic accuracy, quantitative reliability, and safe clinical workflows.

articles.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in PET Imaging.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming positron emission tomography (PET) across the clinical workflow. This article reviews current clinical applications, including automated scheduling and protocoling, Food and Drug Administration-cleared deep learning reconstruction, and commercial lesion detection. Emerging research includes physics-informed reconstruction, diffusion models, and large language models for automated reporting. Implementation challenges include algorithmic bias, data drift, human-AI interaction, and evolving regulatory frameworks. Future directions encompass transformer architectures, total-body PET integration, and multimodal fusion. Understanding both the capabilities and limitations of these technologies can help radiologists and nuclear medicine physicians evaluate their clinical utility and integrate AI responsibly into patient care.

articles.title: Novel Radiotracers in PET Imaging.
articles.abstract: This article reviews emerging PET radiopharmaceuticals in late preclinical and early clinical development. The discussed tracers have broad applications for disease staging, theranostic patient selection, and treatment monitoring. For oncology, tracers targeting fibroblast activation protein, prostate-specific membrane antigen, delta-like ligand 3, trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2, claudin 18.2, and amino-acid transporters are highlighted alongside immune-targeted tracers imaging cluster of differentiation proteins, the programmed death-1 receptor and ligand, granzyme B, and macrophages. In neurology, tracers targeting amyloid-beta, tau, translocator protein, and synaptic vesicle protein 2A are discussed. Highlighted cardiology tracers focus on imaging of myocardial perfusion, amyloidosis, and vascular inflammation.

articles.title: Long Axial Field of View PET: Sensitivity, Clinical Applications, and Implementation.
articles.abstract: Long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET/CT represents a major hardware evolution that expands detector coverage to dramatically increase geometric sensitivity. This amplified signal enables significantly shorter acquisitions, reduced administered radiotracer dose, improved lesion conspicuity, and delayed or low-count imaging. Rather than representing distinct platforms, extended-AFOV and long-AFOV systems exist along a continuum extending from conventional short-axis scanners. Both configurations share substantial functional overlap, driving profound workflow and dose-reduction benefits while supporting advanced dynamic and multiparametric protocols. For radiologists, maximizing this technology requires transitioning from static image assessment to managing complex quantitative data, fundamentally advancing molecular imaging across diverse medical specialties.

articles.title: PET in Theranostics: Patient Selection, Treatment Planning, and Response Assessment.
articles.abstract: Theranostics pairs molecular imaging with a therapeutic radiopharmaceutical directed at the same target, with PET assessing target expression, disease extent, interlesional heterogeneity, and FDG discordance. Three established applications are reviewed: PSMA PET-guided selection for lutetium-177-PSMA-617 in metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer, somatostatin receptor PET-guided peptide receptor radionuclide therapy in neuroendocrine tumors, and iodine-124/FDG PET within radioiodine therapy for differentiated thyroid cancer. Practical guidance covers patient selection, image interpretation, treatment planning, response assessment, and reporting. A key paradigm: diagnostic uptake confirms target availability but neither measures delivered dose nor guarantees response; biomarkers, dosimetry, and response frameworks remain variably validated.

articles.title: Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen PET/Computed Tomography in Prostate Cancer: Staging, Restaging, Interpretation, and Clinical Management.
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/computed tomography has transformed prostate cancer imaging, offering superior diagnostic accuracy over conventional modalities. This article provides radiology professionals with a practical guide to available PSMA PET agents, interpretation, appropriate use criteria, standardized reporting frameworks, and common interpretation pitfalls.

articles.title: A Practical Guide to Somatostatin Receptor Imaging with PET/Computed Tomography.
articles.abstract: Somatostatin receptor (SSTR) imaging with PET/computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation for diagnosis, staging, restaging and evaluation of potential suitability for radionuclide therapy in patients with neuroendocrine tumors and other neoplasms. An understanding of the physiologic distribution of somatostatin receptors, patterns of nonmalignant SSTR expression as well as the technical factors that influence lesion intensity are essential for accurate reporting of SSTR PET/CT. Here we present a practical guide to SSTR PET/CT, highlighting important biological concepts and common pitfalls to assist with accurate reporting.

articles.title: PET Imaging of Infection, Inflammation, and Immune-mediated Disease: From Fluorodeoxyglucose to Pathogen-specific and Immune-targeted Tracers.
articles.abstract: PET/computed tomography (CT) is an important tool for evaluating infectious, inflammatory, and immune-mediated diseases when conventional testing is inconclusive. This article reviews the clinical applications of fluorodeoxyglucose-PET/CT in fever of unknown origin, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal infections, large-vessel vasculitis, sarcoidosis, autoimmune disorders, and transplant rejection. Emphasis is placed on practical interpretation, characteristic imaging patterns, and factors affecting diagnostic accuracy, including patient preparation, myocardial suppression protocols, glucocorticoid therapy, and postoperative inflammation. Emerging PET approaches, such as immuno-PET, radiolabeled leukocyte PET, and bacteria-specific tracers, are also discussed, highlighting the shift toward more biologically specific imaging of infection, inflammation, and immune activity.

articles.title: Cardiac PET Imaging in Coronary Artery Disease: Myocardial Perfusion and Flow Reserve Assessment.
articles.abstract: PET myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) provides excellent diagnostic and prognostic performance for ischemic heart disease. It offers multiparametric evaluation of myocardial perfusion, left ventricular function at rest and peak stress, coronary calcium (on PET/computed tomography scanners), and myocardial blood flow, which can diagnose epicardial and microvascular coronary disease, stratify risk, and guide management patients with known or suspected ischemic heart disease. The purpose of this article is to deliver a practical approach of PET MPI techniques and interpretation.

articles.title: PET for Evaluation of Neurologic Diseases: Part Two: Epilepsy and Neuro-Oncology.
articles.abstract: This review of PET for evaluation of neurological diseases is divided into two parts; part two examines the clinical use of positron emission tomography (PET) in epilepsy and neuro-oncology. In epilepsy, 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET can localize epileptogenic cortex and guide surgical planning, particularly in temporal lobe epilepsy and MRI-negative cases. In neuro-oncology, amino acid PET tracers, including 18F-fluoroethyl-L-tyrosine (FET), 11C-methionine (MET), 18F-fluoro-L-DOPA (FDOPA), and fluciclovine, complement MRI in evaluating gliomas and brain metastases, particularly for distinguishing viable tumor from treatment-related change. Somatostatin receptor PET, including DOTATATE, complements MRI in meningioma assessment and may also identify candidates for radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: PET for Evaluation of Neurologic Diseases: Part one: Neurodegenerative Diseases.
articles.abstract: This review of PET for evaluation of neurological diseases is divided into two parts; part one examines the clinical use of positron emission tomography (PET) in neurodegenerative diseases. FDG-PET can identify characteristic patterns of cerebral metabolism and help distinguish among neurodegenerative disorders. Amyloid and tau PET have expanding diagnostic and theranostic roles in Alzheimer's disease, including assessment of disease-specific pathology and treatment eligibility. FDOPA-PET evaluates presynaptic dopamine synthesis and supports assessment of Parkinson's disease and other parkinsonian syndromes. Combined with structural imaging and clinical evaluation, PET can improve diagnostic confidence, refine prognosis, and inform treatment decisions.

articles.title: The Effects of Virtual Reality Group Reminiscence Therapy on Agitation, Cognition, Depression and Social Function in Patients With Alzheimer's Disease.
articles.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the impact of multisensory virtual reality (VR) group reminiscence therapy on behavioural, cognitive and psychosocial outcomes in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients, while evaluating intervention feasibility and safety.

METHODS: An assessor-blinded randomised controlled trial was employed. Sixty participants with AD were randomly allocated to either the intervention group (n = 30) or the control group (n = 30). The intervention group underwent VR-based reminiscence sessions twice weekly, each lasting 40 min, for 8 weeks. The control group received routine care. Outcomes were measured before and after the intervention using the NPI-agitation subscale, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), the 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15) and Short Form-36 (SF-36). Questionnaires including Presence Questionnaire (PQ), Motivation Inventory (IMI) and Virtual Reality Sickness Questionnaire (VRSQ) were used to assess intervention acceptance and side effects. The Autobiographical Memory Test (AMT) was used to evaluate memory specificity.

RESULTS: Post-intervention, VR participants showed markedly lower agitation scores (NPI) (4.2 ± 1.9 vs. 1.7 ± 1.2, p < 0.001), MMSE scores (23.5 ± 2.1 vs. 27.1 ± 1.4, p < 0.01), GDS-15 scores (9.8 ± 1.3 vs. 3.1 ± 1.2, p < 0.001) and SF-36 subscales of social function and mental health (both p < 0.05), compared with the control group. PQ and IMI scores indicated high acceptance of the intervention. VRSQ scores showed minor side effects (e.g., eye fatigue < 1.3). AMT results also improved significantly (event specificity: 3.2 vs. 6.2, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: VR group reminiscence therapy significantly improved agitation, cognition and mood in AD patients and enhanced their quality of life. The method is safe, feasible and provides a novel non-pharmacological option with an interactive and immersive experience.

articles.title: Decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide versus busulfan-cyclophosphamide myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for reducing risk of relapse in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia in China: an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning.

METHODS: In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m2 once a day on days -14 to -10, intravenous busulfan 3·2 mg/kg once a day on days -7 to -4, and intravenous cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg once a day on days -3 to -2) or BuCy (same dose and duration of busulfan and cyclophosphamide). Randomisation was done with permuted blocks (block size four) with no stratification and was implemented through an independent, interactive, web-based response system. The primary endpoint was 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse in the intention-to-treat population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03596892) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group.

INTERPRETATION: The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population.

FUNDING: The National Natural Science Foundation of China, the National Key Research and Development Program of China, the Science and Technology Program of Guangdong Province, the Non-communicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, the Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province, the Science and Technology Planning Project of Guangzhou, and the Outstanding Youth Cultivation Program of Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University.

TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Speaking up for safety: A structured communication-based approach to reducing Type 2 workplace violence in inpatient settings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 workplace violence (WPV), defined as violence perpetrated by patients or visitors against health care workers, remains a significant threat to nurse safety, well-being, and retention. Inadequate communication regarding patients' history of violent behavior may leave nurses unprepared to manage escalating situations and contribute to underreporting of WPV incidents.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the impact of a structured Potentially Violent Patient Handoff (PVPH) tool on nurses' confidence in managing potentially violent patients and on Type 2 WPV reporting within an inpatient neurology/neurosurgery unit.

METHODS: This quality improvement project used a pre-post design over 6 months in a high-risk inpatient unit. The PVPH tool was implemented through education, stakeholder engagement, and Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles. Outcomes included nurse confidence measured by the Clinical Confidence in Coping with Patient Aggression scale, perceptions of handoff effectiveness and safety, and Type 2 WPV event reports.

RESULTS: Mean confidence scores increased from 58.1 to 66.3 following implementation. Nurses reported improvements in perceived safety, support, collaboration, and adequacy of handoff information. Agreement regarding the importance of reporting violent events increased from 69% to 88%. Although reported violent events increased from 19 to 37, reporting trends declined over the intervention period, suggesting improved awareness and reporting behaviors alongside enhanced preparedness.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured violence-focused handoff tool improved nurses' confidence and perceptions of safety while promoting communication about behavioral risks during care transitions. Standardized violence-related handoff processes may support safer work environments and strengthen WPV prevention efforts in inpatient settings.

articles.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) in Patients With Persistent Pain Are Associated With Low Health-Related Quality of Life and Distress-Perceived Injustice Mediates the Association Between ACEs and Pain Interference.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with poor health in adulthood and may predispose individuals to anxiety-related problems and somatic morbidity. However, their role in persistent pain is not fully understood. This study assessed several factors that may link ACEs with persistent pain and offer possible treatment targets.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included two cohorts of patients attending tertiary pain care (total n = 644). We examined associations between ACEs, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), comorbid conditions, pain-related measures and psychological factors, including perceived injustice related to pain.

RESULTS: Increases in the number of ACEs from two to three and from five to six were associated with lower HRQoL and more comorbid conditions. Medium ACE burden (3-5 ACEs) associated with more depression and other psychiatric comorbidities than low ACE burden (0-2 ACEs) (34.5% vs. 22.9%, p < 0.05; 12.2% vs. 3.3%, p < 0.05, respectively). High ACE burden (≥ 6 ACEs) associated also with more asthma (29.3% vs. 13.7%, p < 0.05). ACEs were associated with all anxiety- and distress-related factors, correlations being relevant with depression (r = 0.26), trait anxiety (r = 0.25) and worry (r = 0.24). Among the pain-related outcomes, only pain interference was significantly associated with ACEs (r = 0.13), and this association was statistically fully mediated by injustice perceptions.

CONCLUSIONS: ACE burden was associated with reduced HRQoL, psychological distress and pain interference. Perceived injustice mediated the association between ACEs and pain interference, possibly representing a treatment target for patients with pain and high ACE burden.

SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study shows that patients treated in tertiary pain care report a high number of ACEs, stress- and anxiety-related processes and perceptions of injustice, which may contribute to pain persistence and may offer potential targets for treatment.

articles.title: The Effect of Bupropion in Peripheral Neuropathic Pain A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoamine reuptake inhibitors are evidenced first-line treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. The aim was to investigate if bupropion, a drug that specifically inhibits neuronal noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake, relieves neuropathic pain and if a potential effect depends on status of conditioned pain modulation (CPM) and sensory phenotype (irritable vs. non-irritable nociceptor).

METHOD: Study design was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and cross-over. Patients with peripheral neuropathic pain were treated with bupropion and placebo in a random order, with treatment periods lasting 6 weeks preceded by a 1-week baseline. Change in daily average pain was the primary outcome. Other outcomes included pain relief and 30% and 50% pain reduction.

RESULTS: 67 patients were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean daily average pain changed from NRS 6.4 to 5.5 after bupropion treatment with an average effect as compared with placebo of -0.5 (95% CI -0.8 to -0.1, p = 0.005). No relation was found between response to treatment and efficiency of CPM or sensory phenotype. There was no significant effect on the pain relief scale. A 30% and 50% pain reduction was found in 10 and 6 patients respectively with a NNT for 50% pain reduction of 15. Bupropion was well tolerated.

CONCLUSION: Bupropion had a pain-relieving effect independent of CPM efficiency and sensory phenotype. NNT for 50% pain reduction was higher than reported for first-line treatments, but bupropion treatment may still be an option in patients with insufficient response or intolerable side effects on such treatments.

SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study finds a modest pain-relieving effect of bupropion on peripheral neuropathic pain independent of function of conditioned pain modulation. Bupropion could be an alternative treatment for patients with a lack of effect or intolerable side effects to first-choice treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. Further, larger studies are needed to determine optimal dosage.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered with the EU clinical trials Register (EudraCT 2019-000243-27) on March 15th 2019. The study is approved by the Ethical Committee of the Region of Southern Denmark (also included approval for Regions of Central Denmark; no. S-20190010) and the Danish Medicine Agency (no. 2019012986) and is registered with the Danish Data Protection Agency (via the Region of Southern Denmark's internal notification; no. 19/17111).

articles.title: The Relationship Between Skeletal Muscle Mitochondrial Function and Cardiac Workload During Exercise in Young Healthy Subjects.
articles.abstract: Exaggerated cardiac workload responses to incremental exercise are associated with the development of hypertension and future cardiovascular events. We hypothesized that skeletal muscle mitochondrial function is associated with cardiac workload, quantified as Rate Pressure Product (RPP), during exercise. Healthy adults (n = 18; 9 females; age 25 ± 4 years) performed a maximal exercise test on a cycle ergometer. The test began at 0 W and followed an incremental protocol starting at 40 W, with load increases every 2 minutes until exhaustion. Breath-by-breath gas exchange was measured to determine peak oxygen uptake and the respiratory compensatory point (RCP). Heart rate (HR) and systolic blood pressure (BP) were recorded at each load to calculate RPP. The cardiac workload response to exercise was defined as the change in RPP from 0 W to the intensity corresponding to RCP (ΔRPP). Muscle biopsies from the vastus lateralis were collected on separate days to assess mitochondrial respiration. ΔRPP from 0 W to RCP intensity was 18181 ± 2147 mmHg·bpm and Complex I mediated respiration was 31.9 ± 13.7 pmol·mg-1 s-1. ΔRPP was correlated only with Complex I (r = -0.69, p = 0.002) and sex (r = 0.50, p = 0.035). In a forward stepwise linear regression analysis with ΔRPP as the dependent variable and baseline RPP, sex, and complex I mediated respiration as predictors, complex I mediated respiration was the only variable significantly associated with ΔRPP (adjusted R2 = 0.44; unstandardized β = -107; 95% CI:-167 to -47; p = 0.002). The cardiac workload response to exercise is strongly associated with skeletal muscle mitochondrial function in young normotensive individuals.

articles.title: Plasma Lipidomic Features of Adolescent Major Depressive Disorder and Lipid Changes After Fluoxetine Treatment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) in adolescents is a major public health concern, yet objective biological markers and treatment-related metabolic changes remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to characterize plasma lipidomic alterations in adolescent MDD and explore lipid changes associated with fluoxetine treatment.

METHODS: This study enrolled 75 adolescents with MDD and 75 matched healthy controls (HCs). Among the adolescents with MDD, 44 had paired baseline and week-8 plasma samples available and were included in the longitudinal analysis. Plasma lipidomic profiles were analyzed using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS).

RESULTS: A total of 865 lipid species were detected. Compared with HCs, adolescents with MDD showed distinct plasma lipidomic profiles, with 82 differentially abundant lipid species identified, primarily involving triglycerides, lysophospholipids, free fatty acids, membrane phospholipids, and sphingolipids. Among the machine-learning models, logistic regression showed the highest discriminative performance, with a pooled out-of-fold AUC of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.79-0.91). Longitudinal analysis identified 21 lipid species meeting the differential criteria following fluoxetine treatment, mainly involving triglycerides and bile acid-related metabolites. Integrative pathway and target analyses suggested that fluoxetine-associated lipid changes may involve neurotransmitter signaling, inflammatory lipid metabolism, PI3K-Akt signaling, and nuclear receptor-related pathways.

CONCLUSION: This study characterizes alterations in plasma lipid metabolism in adolescent MDD and the lipidomic changes following fluoxetine treatment, providing new lipidomic evidence for candidate lipid signatures and potential treatment-associated biological pathways.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05814640. Registered 20 February 2023, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05814640.

articles.title: Advancements in Natural Product-Based Ischemic Stroke Treatment: Mechanisms, Key Compounds, and Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains the leading global cause of permanent neurological disability and mortality. Narrow therapeutic time windows and elevated hemorrhagic transformation risks restrict conventional clinical interventions, including intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. Single-target neuroprotective agents fail to sustain long-term neurological functional recovery, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. Natural products (NPs) derived from traditional Chinese medicine exert protective effects against cerebral ischemia via multiple pathways. However, their poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, low aqueous solubility, and inadequate in vivo bioavailability greatly hinder clinical translational application. This review systematically summarizes the pathological mechanisms of natural monomers for the treatment of ischemic stroke and four types of brain-targeted nanocarriers over the past decade. We reconstructed the pathological cascades of cerebral ischemia across the acute, subacute, and chronic repair phases, and critically discussed the inherent limitations of the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and existing monomer-based preclinical studies. This work provides systematic structure-activity relationship evidence and insights into nano-delivery strategies for the development of natural product-based anti-stroke therapeutics. We also propose future research directions, such as staged, sequential administration, precise multi-omics intervention, and standardized nanoformulation development, to accelerate the clinical translation of bioactive ingredients derived from traditional Chinese medicine.

articles.title: Consensus and persistent uncertainty in fetal ventriculomegaly: Delphi study mapping unresolved clinical domains and research priorities.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Fetal ventriculomegaly (VM) is a common prenatal finding with heterogeneous etiology and unpredictable outcome, yet its management remains among the least standardized in fetal medicine. This study aimed to establish expert consensus on key decision points in the prenatal management of fetal VM, and to systematically map the domains of persistent uncertainty as a structured framework for future research priorities.

METHODS: A two-round modified Delphi study was conducted with an international panel of experts in fetal medicine, selected through a systematic review of publications that included more than 50 cases of VM over the preceding decade. Round 1 comprised 39 multiple-choice questions, with consensus achieved when ≥ 75% of panelists selected a single answer option; items that did not reach consensus were reformulated into Likert-scale statements for Round 2, which comprised 60 statements rated on a 9-point Likert scale. In Round 2, consensus was defined by two simultaneous criteria: ≥ 75% of valid respondents scoring in the agreement (score, 7-9) or disagreement (score, 1-3) zone, with an interquartile range of ≤ 2. Non-consensus domains were classified using a post-hoc taxonomic framework into three categories: absent evidence (Type 1), divergent clinical frameworks (Type 2) and undefined construct (Type 3), which could occur independently or in combination.

RESULTS: Of 56 experts who completed Round 1, 45 (80%) also completed Round 2. In Round 1, consensus was reached on 20/39 (51%) questions. In Round 2, 6/60 (10%) statements reached positive consensus and four (7%) reached negative consensus; 50 (83%) did not reach consensus. Over the two rounds, consensus was achieved on standardized measurement technique, three-tier grading, comprehensive neurosonographic and investigative work-up, individualization of the timing of fetal magnetic resonance imaging, stepwise neurosurgical referral and delivery management of fetal VM. Classification of non-consensus domains identified 15/50 (30%) items as Type 1, 16/50 (32%) as Type 2, 4/50 (8%) as Type 3 and 15/50 (30%) as Type 1+3. Ventricular asymmetry, the largest non-consensus cluster with 12 items, was classified as Type 1+3 in 11/12 (92%) statements, reflecting the simultaneous absence of prospective outcome data and of a universally accepted operational definition.

CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi study provides structured expert-derived guidance, primarily applicable to specialist and referral settings, on the prenatal management of fetal VM across key clinical domains. Beyond consensus recommendations, we propose that the original contribution of this study is a hypothesis-generating taxonomic map of persistent uncertainty, classifying unresolved domains by the nature of the underlying evidence gap and identifying the specific prerequisites (definitional, methodological or empirical) required before consensus can be achieved. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Our objective was to evaluate metformin prescribed at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the risk of developing Long COVID (LC) in electronic health record data. We conducted a new user analysis of metformin prescribed within 6 days of documented infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) versus experimental control: prescription for fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast.

INCLUSION CRITERIA: a clinic visit in the 0-6 months and the 6-12 months before infection.

EXCLUSION CRITERIA: metformin or control within 12 months.

PRIMARY OUTCOME: LC or death (LC/D), to address death as a competing risk, among patients prescribed drug within Days 0-6 of infection. LC was defined by diagnosis code or computable phenotype. We used entropy balancing to estimate the average treatment effect with a weighted log-linear model. After weighting, there were 248 in the metformin and control groups; the average age was 53 (16); 16% were Black; and 16% were Hispanic. In the primary analysis, 10/248 (4.0%) in the metformin group developed LC/D versus 21/248 (8.5%) in the control group, adjusted risk ratio (aRR) 0.47 (95% CI 0.25-0.89, p = 0.02). For prescriptions on Days 0-1 relative to infection, aRR was 0.39 (95% CI 0.12-1.24); for prescriptions on Days 0-14, the aRR was 0.75 (95% CI 0.52-1.08). In this observational analysis, metformin prescribed within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a 53% lower risk of LC over 6 months than comparator medications. With the aRR of 0.47 (95% CI 0.25-0.89), any risk reduction between 75% and 11% is highly compatible with our data. This analysis of electronic health record diagnoses is important for the reproducibility of clinical trial results that ascertained the same outcome but via participant-report.

articles.title: Introduction and Spread of West Nile Virus in Lazio, Italy, 2025: Molecular Epidemiology and Genomic Characterization.
articles.abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) is a flavivirus whose cycle involves mosquitoes and avian hosts that occasionally may infect horses and humans as "dead-end hosts." Human infection is mostly asymptomatic, sometimes leading to febrile or neuroinvasive disease. In 2025, Italy experienced its largest epidemic with an unprecedented geographic spread (79 provinces; 52% of cases in central Italy). Here we report whole‑genome sequencing and phylogeographic analysis of 39 WNV lineage 2 samples collected in Lazio and Campania regions between July and September 2025 from humans and animal samples. All 2025 strains belonged to a Southern Italian clade that diversified around 2020, with evidence of earlier circulation in 2024. All the 2025 genomes shared a substitution that lies in envelope protein domain III (K399R), potentially influencing interactions with the viral membrane. The same mutation was previously detected in Eastern European strains, leading to the hypothesis of introductions in Italy via migratory birds from these regions. Phylogeography identified strong viral dispersal routes within Central Italy supporting a pattern of short‑range spread and local overwintering. Overall, results highlight the roles of ecological conditions and cross‑border transmission dynamics in shaping the 2025 Italian epidemic, underscoring the need for integrated genomic/ecological surveillance.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Late Gadolinium Enhancement on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events and Time-Varying Attenuation of Risk in Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patients and characterize the dynamic pattern of its risk effect over time.
