METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients who underwent Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) between 2020 and 2024, with MACE (cardiac death, heart failure re-hospitalization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmia) as the endpoint. Patients were stratified by MACE occurrence. Schoenfeld residual testing showed borderline deviation of the proportional hazards (PH) assumption for LGE extent (LV mass percentage). Thus, a time-dependent Cox model (Extended Cox PHs Model) with an LGE extent × follow-up time interaction term was built to assess dynamic hazard ratio changes, and independent MACE risk factors were identified.

RESULTS: Among 173 DCM patients (age 47 ± 15 years, 105 males), 46 (26.6%) experienced MACE after a mean follow-up of 27 ± 16 months. The time-dependent Cox model identified LGE extent (baseline HR: 1.243, 95% CI: 1.162-1.329, p < 0.001), the LGE extent × time interaction (HR: 0.993, 95% CI: 0.989-0.997, p = 0.001), and LV end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi; HR = 1.008, 95% CI: 1.003-1.014, p = 0.001) as independent MACE predictors. Notably, the risk effect of LGE extent demonstrated time-dependent attenuation.

CONCLUSION: LV LGE extent and LVEDVi independently predict MACE in DCM patients. The early prognostic value of LGE extent suggests a critical time window for early fibrosis intervention.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin Inhibits BK Polyomavirus Replication via AMPK Signaling.
articles.abstract: BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) infection is a significant contributor of graft loss in kidney transplant recipients, yet no effective antiviral therapy is currently approved. This study investigated whether the SGLT2 inhibitor dapagliflozin could suppress BKPyV replication. BKPyV-infected HK-2 cells were treated with dapagliflozin, and viral load, protein expression, and noncoding control region (NCCR) transcriptional activity were analyzed. siRNA-mediated knockdown of AMPK was used to verify its role in dapagliflozin-mediated response. Dapagliflozin treatment at 10 and 20 μM resulted in a dose-dependent suppression of BKPyV progeny release into the supernatant and a concomitant reduction in large T-antigen (TAg) and VP1 protein expressions. These antiviral effects were achieved without compromising host cell viability, as no significant cytotoxicity was observed at the doses utilized. Luciferase reporter assays revealed that dapagliflozin markedly attenuated TAg-driven NCCR transcriptional activity in both early and late orientations, effectively disrupting viral autoregulation. While high-glucose conditions (25 mM) enhanced BKPyV replication and reduced baseline AMPK phosphorylation, the inhibitory efficacy of dapagliflozin remained consistent. Mechanistically, dapagliflozin increased AMPK phosphorylation even under hyperglycemic stress. The suppression of viral progeny and NCCR activity was significantly reversed upon AMPK knockdown, demonstrating that AMPK activation is required for dapagliflozin-mediated viral suppression regardless of the glucose environment. Dapagliflozin inhibits BKPyV replication through an AMPK-dependent pathway. These results provide a strong rationale for evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors as a novel strategy to reduce the severity of BKPyV infection in transplant recipients.

articles.title: Effect of Progressive Muscle Relaxation and Nature Sounds on Alarm Fatigue in Intensive Care Unit Nurses: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care unit (ICU) nurses are exposed to numerous alarms, many of which are unnecessary and lead to alarm fatigue. This phenomenon, caused by desensitization to alarm sounds, reduces nurses' responsiveness to critical alerts and threatens both their well-being and patient safety. Alarm fatigue has been linked to elevated stress, burnout and errors in patient care, underscoring the need for effective interventions. Progressive muscle relaxation involves the gradual and systematic contraction and relaxation of different muscle groups throughout the body and nature sounds use for decrease stress and alarm fatigue.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) and exposure to nature sounds in reducing alarm fatigue among ICU nurses.

STUDY DESIGN: A three-arm, parallel, single-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted.

RESULTS: Ninety-six ICU nurses from three hospitals in southern Iran, were randomly assigned to one of three groups: PMR (n = 32), nature sounds (n = 32) or control (n = 32). Alarm fatigue was assessed using a validated alarm fatigue scale at baseline, immediately after the intervention and 2 months post-intervention. Both PMR and nature sound interventions significantly reduced alarm fatigue among ICU nurses (p < 0.001). Between-group comparisons showed significant differences between the PMR and control groups (p < 0.001) and between the nature sound and control groups (p < 0.001). No significant difference was observed between the PMR and nature sound groups (p = 0.650).

CONCLUSION: PMR and exposure to nature sounds significantly reduced alarm fatigue among ICU nurses, as reflected in lower fatigue scores. These interventions improved nurses' capacity to manage stress and fatigue, thereby supporting better job performance and enhanced patient safety. Given their simplicity and accessibility, both approaches represent promising strategies for addressing alarm fatigue in critical care settings.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Progressive muscle relaxation and nature sounds may offer practical, non-pharmacological approaches to managing alarm fatigue among intensive care unit nurses. These interventions could be incorporated into nurses' work routines, although further research is needed to confirm their effectiveness and long-term benefits.

articles.title: The Effects of Force-Velocity Profile-Based Load Prescription on Muscle Power and Functional Performance in Velocity-Deficient Older Adults.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
articles.abstract: Muscle power is essential for functional capacity in older adults and can be improved through power-focused resistance training (PRT). PRT adaptations are load- and velocity-specific, yet optimal load prescription remains unclear. As force and velocity capacities vary between individuals, this 12-week intervention compared two force-velocity (F-V) profile-guided loading strategies: training at loads matched versus not matched to the F-V deficit. F-V profiles of 80 adults ≥ 65 years were assessed on a pneumatic leg press, with maximal force (F0) and velocity (V0) expressed as z-scores relative to a younger reference group (n = 60, 20-35 years). A difference ≥ 1 between z-scores was considered indicative of a deficit, with the direction determining a force- or velocity-deficit profile. As force deficits were rare (n = 4), the intervention only included participants with a velocity deficit (n = 59), of whom 57 initiated the intervention. Participants were randomly assigned to train at loads matched to their deficit (individualized; IND) or at loads deliberately not matched to their deficit (non-individualized; NON-IND). Maximal power, F-V profile parameters and functional performance were assessed at baseline, 6 and 12 weeks. From baseline to 12 weeks, F0 increased more in NON-IND than IND (p = 0.040), while V0 increased more in IND than NON-IND (p = 0.009). Changes in power and functional performance did not differ between groups (all p ≥ 0.065). In velocity-deficient older adults, differences in F-V-guided load prescription led to distinct F-V adaptations but did not lead to differences in power or functional performance. Trial Registration: The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06449716).

articles.title: Endoplasmic Reticulum Autophagy Enhancement Alleviates Synaptic Plasticity Dysfunction and Ameliorates Cognitive Impairment in SAE Mice by Relieving STING-Associated Inhibition of PKM2 Activity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pathogenesis of cognitive impairment in patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) remains unclear. This study investigated whether enhancing micro-endoplasmic reticulum autophagy (micro-ER-phagy) could alleviate synaptic dysfunction and improve cognitive impairment in SAE mice models by relieving stimulator of interferon gene (STING)-associated inhibition of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) activity.

METHODS: Male wild-type and neuron-specific PKM2 conditional knockout mice (PKM2fl/fl; hSyn-Cre+) were used. Cognitive function in SAE mice models was assessed using the Y-maze and contextual fear conditioning tests. Neuronal plasticity was examined using transmission electron microscopy and Golgi staining, whereas immunofluorescence staining and Western blotting were employed to determine the temporal and spatial expression patterns of related proteins.

RESULTS: Septic mice developed cognitive impairment. Hippocampal tissues of SAE mice exhibited synaptic plasticity dysfunction and glycolysis enhancement. Meanwhile, the hippocampus showed increased PKM2 expression and an altered ratio of PKM2 tetramers and dimers. In addition, phosphorylated STING significantly increased in concentration in hippocampal neurones and its knockdown improved cognitive function. However, this cognitive rescue failed in PKM2 conditional knockout mice treated with SAE. Finally, Sec62-mediated micro-ER-phagy promoted lysosomal degradation of STING, which relieved STING-mediated inhibition of PKM2 and improved synaptic plasticity and cognitive dysfunction in SAE mice.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated micro-ER-phagy may relieve the STING-associated inhibition of PKM2 activity, improve neuronal glycolysis and synaptic plasticity, and alleviate cognitive dysfunction in SAE mice.

articles.title: Potential Locations for Noninvasive Brain Stimulation in Treating Poststroke Deficits: Exploration From Multimodal Neuroimaging.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Noninvasive brain stimulation (NIBS) shows promise for poststroke deficits (PSDs), but efficacy may be limited by inconsistent stimulation sites.

METHODS: By integrating neuroimaging meta-analysis, lesion-symptom mapping (LSM), and resting-state functional connectivity (FC) analysis, we employed three analytical pipelines to explore potential NIBS targets for alexia, aphasia, apraxia, ataxia, dysarthria, hemiplegia, paresthesia, and dysphagia. Pipeline 1 identified cortical regions directly associated with each PSD via coordinate-based meta-analysis using Neurosynth Compose. Pipeline 2 identified cortical regions exhibiting maximal functional connectivity with neurosynth-derived regions of interest (ROI). Pipeline 3 identified cortical regions functionally connected to ROIs from a prior large-scale LSM study. During Pipeline 2 and 3, ROIs were used for seed-to-voxel FC analysis using resting-state fMRI data from 100 healthy subjects. Identified cortical targets were mapped onto the scalp and referenced by the 10-20 system and continuous proportional coordinates.

RESULTS: Potential cortical targets and scalp locations were identified for all eight PSDs. For instance, for hemiplegia, validated targets included primary motor and somatosensory cortices and supplementary motor area; novel targets included angular gyrus, superior frontal gyrus, inferior parietal lobule, medial prefrontal cortex, and precuneus.

CONCLUSIONS: This multimodal approach systematically identified precise NIBS targets, confirming established sites and revealing novel regions to broaden neuromodulation strategies for poststroke recovery.

articles.title: Clinical Impact of Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Among Patients With HIV/AIDS and Disseminated Histoplasmosis in a Hyperendemic Region of Northeastern Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may occur in people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA), often triggered by opportunistic infections such as disseminated histoplasmosis (DH). The substantial overlap in clinical and laboratory features between HLH and DH complicates timely diagnosis.

OBJECTIVES: To describe HLH among PLWHA with DH and compare clinical, laboratory and outcome characteristics between patients with and without HLH.

PATIENTS/METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted at São José Hospital of Infectious Diseases, Fortaleza, Brazil, between March 2023 and June 2024. Hospitalised PLWHA with DH were evaluated for HLH based on the presence of ≥ 3 HLH-2004 criteria and an H-Score ≥ 169. Baseline clinical, laboratory and outcome parameters were compared between patients with and without HLH.

RESULTS: Among 61 patients diagnosed with DH, 11 (18.0%) met the study criteria for HLH. Patients with HLH were more likely to present with hepatomegaly (p = 0.036), haemoptysis (p = 0.030) and lower platelet counts (p = 0.029). In-hospital mortality was significantly higher among patients with HLH (54.5% versus 18.0%; p = 0.019). These patients more frequently required renal replacement therapy (p = 0.028) and intensive care unit admission (p = 0.048). Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing demonstrated significantly reduced in-hospital survival among patients with HLH (p = 0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: HLH represents a severe complication in PLWHA with DH and is associated with increased mortality and greater need for intensive care. Early recognition and use of adjunctive diagnostic tools may facilitate timely management and improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome in Late Pregnancy Following Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
articles.abstract: The diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) relies on evolving clinical features, supported by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), laboratory investigations, and electrodiagnostic studies. Early investigations may be nondiagnostic and should not delay treatment when progressive neurological deterioration raises clinical suspicion of GBS. Timely treatment is crucial in optimizing maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Improved range of motion following correction osteotomy for varus malunited proximal humerus fractures with 3-dimensional planned cutting guides: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varus malunion of the proximal humerus can lead to persistent pain and restricted shoulder mobility. When symptoms persist despite conservative treatment, valgus wedge osteotomy may be considered. This case series reports the outcomes of corrective osteotomy for varus malunion of 2-part proximal humerus fractures using patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) cutting guides, fixed with a PHILOS plate (Synthes) in patients aged less than 65 years. We hypothesized that this technique would improve forward flexion, restoring at least 80% of the forward flexion of the contralateral, unaffected shoulder.

METHODS: All patients in this study were referred to our clinic for further treatment and had received at least 6 months of physiotherapy prior to this. The patients were dissatisfied with their shoulder after conservative treatment, for most primarily due to the limited elevation. Patients were eligible if they were aged less than 65 years, had closed epiphyses, and presented with an untreated varus malunion of the proximal humerus. Exclusion criteria included frozen shoulder, signs of rotator cuff tear, or neurologic abnormalities. The primary outcome measure was the difference in forward flexion, assessed by a single observer using a goniometer pre-operatively and at a minimum of 1-year follow-up. Secondary outcomes included the Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand score, the Oxford Shoulder Score, visual analog scale scores for pain and satisfaction, correction of the head-shaft angle, and complications.

RESULTS: Eleven patients underwent 3D planned corrective osteotomy. At a 1-year follow-up, median forward flexion improved from 100° to 148°, corresponding to 94% of the contralateral side (P = .005), and median abduction improved from 80° to 145° (P = .005). Patient-reported outcomes improved significantly, with the median Oxford Shoulder Score decreasing from 25 to 17 (P = .01), the median Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand score from 34 to 13 (P = .02), and median visual analog scale satisfaction increasing from 3 to 9 (P = .02). The median humeral head-shaft angle increased from 95° pre-operatively to 121° post-operatively (P = .003). Three major complications (low-grade infection, hardware breakout, and frozen shoulder) and one minor complication (hypertrophic scarring) were observed. Seven patients (64%) experienced hardware irritation requiring removal.

CONCLUSION: In this case series, 3D planned corrective osteotomy for varus malunited proximal humerus fractures resulted in clinically relevant improvements in forward flexion and overall shoulder range of motion. Post-operative anterior flexion was better than the presumed 80% of the contralateral side in most patients. These findings suggest that patient-specific 3D planning may be a valuable adjunct in the correction of proximal humerus malunions.

articles.title: A Novel Resource-Adapted Neurocritical Care Education Program in Tanzania: Implementation, Outcomes, and a Framework for Sustainable Training.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE/OBJECTIVE: Neurologic emergencies contribute disproportionately to morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, yet structured neurocritical care training remains limited. Emergency Neurologic Life Support (ENLS) standardizes early management of neurologic emergencies, but implementation in resource-limited settings requires contextual adaptation. Limited access to neuroimaging and monitoring compounds diagnostic uncertainty. Portable neuroultrasound (NeuroUS) offers a feasible bedside adjunct. We developed, implemented, and evaluated Tanzania's first resource-adapted neurocritical care educational program, including hands-on NeuroUS training in a low- and middle-income country (LMIC) setting.

DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: We conducted a prospective observational study during a 2-day in-person training program (October 2025). Multidisciplinary healthcare professionals caring for neurocritical care patients completed pre- and postcourse assessments evaluating medical knowledge, self-reported knowledge, and confidence across ENLS and NeuroUS domains (5-point Likert scale). Ordinal Likert outcomes were summarized using median and interquartile range (IQR) and compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Correct-response proportions were compared using Fisher exact tests. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment was applied within each outcome family.

RESULTS: Twenty-two participants completed precourse assessments; 17 completed postcourse assessments. Self-reported medical knowledge improved across 15 of 16 domains. The largest effects were observed for NeuroUS knowledge, which increased from a median of 1.5 (IQR, 1-2) to 4 (IQR, 4-5; rank-biserial, r = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.64-1.00; q < 0.001); Broad-Reaching Acute Interventions in Neurocritical Care, from 3 (IQR, 2-3) to 4 (IQR, 4-5; r = 0.73; 95% CI, 0.48-0.93; q < 0.001); and intracranial hypertension and herniation, from 3 (IQR, 3-4) to 5 (IQR, 4-5; r = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.45-0.89; q < 0.001). Confidence scores were higher in eight of 16 domains after adjustment. Both NeuroUS diagnostic-application items demonstrated large postcourse differences (q < 0.001). Correct-response proportions increased across all six exploratory knowledge items, but none remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Ninety-four percent found the program relevant to their practice.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementation of resource-limited ENLS integrated with structured neuroultrasound is feasible and significantly improved knowledge and confidence. This hybrid approach represents a scalable education model for LMICs.

articles.title: Assessing the Epidemiological Trend of Gastric Cancer: A Retrospective Analysis From a Tertiary Care Hospital in Bangladesh.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Gastric cancer is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, affecting a substantial proportion of the population, and exhibits a geographical heterogeneity in incidence. Data on the epidemiology and trends of gastric cancer in Bangladesh remain limited. The study aimed to observe the trends in gastric cancer at a tertiary care hospital in Bangladesh.

METHODS: This hospital-based retrospective study was conducted in the department of Gastroenterology of Rajshahi Medical College from January 2018 to December 2025. All the patients who underwent upper GI endoscopy during the study period were initially enrolled. From the hospital records, including histopathology reports, confirmed cases of gastric cancers were included for this study.

RESULTS: A total of 17,298 patients underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital from 2018 to 2025. Among them, 364 patients were diagnosed with gastric cancer (mean age: 56.7 ± 14.6 years; males 61.8%; male-female ratio 1.6:1). Adenocarcinoma was the most common histological type (98.3%). Significant female predominance was noticed among gastric cancer patients younger than 40 years (p = 0.01). Overall, a declining trend in the detection of gastric cancer was observed, although age-specific analysis revealed variable patterns. The antrum (180/364, 49.4%) was the most frequent tumor location, followed by the body (108/364, 29.6%) and fundus (76/364, 20.8%). An apparent increase in the proportion of antral tumors was noticed since 2021, whereas involvement of the body and fundus demonstrated inconsistent variations.

CONCLUSIONS: Gastric cancer detection at this center declined overall, but the female predominance among younger patients and the rising antral proportion suggest a possible shifting epidemiological pattern that warrants population-based research and targeted early detection strategies.

articles.title: Global Burden, Temporal Trends, Extrapolation Based on Past Trends, and Population Attributable Fractions of Risk Factors for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Ecological Study Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Amidst the rising global impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), long-term extrapolations and attributable risk estimations are essential for strategic healthcare planning. This study aimed to investigate the T2DM burden among adults aged ≥ 25 years, extrapolate trends to 2040, and quantify the population attributable fractions (PAFs) of major risk factors.

METHODS: We extracted the prevalence, incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of T2DM from 1990 to 2021 using data from the GBD 2021 release. Joinpoint regression was used to analyze the trend in the burden of disease. Then, using the AAPC in the previous step, we extrapolated the burden indicators up to 2040. To determine the independent contribution of each risk factor to the disease burden, we calculated the adjusted PAF.

RESULTS: All burden indicators and their extrapolations showed a significant increasing trend (p < 0.001). Globally, the prevalence of T2DM increased from 4.82% in 1990 to 10.60% in 2021. Similarly, incidence rose from 255.21 in 1990 to 463.10 per 100,000 in 2021. Mortality and DALYs rates increased from 24.35 to 34.42 per 100,000 and 945.70 to 1594.20 per 100,000, respectively, over the same period (all p < 0.001). Among the risk factors examined, based on adjusted PAF and its extrapolation, high body mass index (BMI) was the most important contributing factor (25.99% to 32.52%).

CONCLUSIONS: The results of this study indicate that the global burden of T2DM is projected to rise significantly, and high BMI, which is associated with multiple metabolic disorders, significantly increases the risk of T2DM. Accordingly, integrating and implementing comprehensive interventions at three levels of prevention (primary, secondary, and tertiary), with a special focus on controlling and reducing obesity and overweight, is essential to control and reduce the burden of diabetes.

articles.title: Kidney Health Biomarkers and Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate Among Indonesian Tofu Production Workers: A Pilot Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Small-scale food-production workers may experience heat strain, dehydration, and combustion-related exposures, but evidence on early kidney injury in these settings remains limited. This pilot study aimed to describe serum and urinary kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) and neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) profiles and to assess, exploratorily, whether these biomarkers discriminated an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-defined kidney-function category among Indonesian tofu production workers.

METHODS: A cross-sectional complete-case analysis included 32 workers from small-scale tofu production units in East Java, Indonesia. Serum creatinine, serum and urinary KIM-1, and serum and urinary NGAL were measured using laboratory microplate-based assays. eGFR was calculated using the CKD-EPI creatinine equation; < 90 mL/min/1.73 m2 was a study-defined exploratory category, not a CKD diagnosis. Descriptive statistics, Mann-Whitney U tests, Spearman correlations, and receiver operating characteristic analysis with 2000-resample bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were performed.

RESULTS: Ten of 32 workers (31.3%) had eGFR < 90 mL/min/1.73 m2, and four of 32 (12.5%) had serum creatinine above the laboratory threshold. Median KIM-1 and NGAL concentrations were lower in the eGFR < 90 group across all four biomarker measures. Discriminatory performance was limited, with area-under-the-curve values ranging from 0.327 to 0.416. Urinary KIM-1 and NGAL were analysed as absolute concentrations without urinary creatinine normalisation; hydration-related variation in urine concentration may have increased measurement variability and weakened observed associations and discrimination. With 32 workers and 10 eGFR < 90 observations, the AUC estimates are imprecise and not definitive measures of diagnostic performance.

CONCLUSION: KIM-1 and NGAL showed limited discrimination of the study-defined eGFR < 90 category; this result does not indicate poor overall utility as tubular injury biomarkers. Larger exposure-informed studies should incorporate creatinine-normalised urinary biomarkers, albuminuria, repeated kidney-function measurements, and objective assessment of heat and nephrotoxic exposures.

articles.title: Left atrial appendage morphology and thrombus risk: considerations for interpretation in valvular heart disease.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

articles.title: Developing proficiency in a transcatheter aortic valve replacement program: lessons from a single academic center's learning curve.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a prevalent and high-mortality valve disease. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is a minimally invasive treatment with outcomes often better than surgery, requiring a multidisciplinary team. This study analyzes outcomes and trends from a high-volume TAVR program in an urban, low-income setting since 2017 to guide future practices.

METHODS: Medical records of patients that underwent TAVR were analyzed retrospectively from 2018 to 2023, dividing them into two cohorts to analyze trends in operative details, complications, length of stay (LOS), and readmission/mortality rates. The learning curve (LC) was assessed by operative time.

RESULTS: Risk-adjusted cumulative sum (RA-CUSUM) analysis identified the transition point at case 76, dividing the cohort into early LC phase group (n = 76) and post-LC phase group (n = 190). Median operative time decreased from 106 to 80 minutes. After adjustment, operative time was 14% shorter in the post-learning-curve cohort (GMR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.96; p = 0.005).

CONCLUSION: Operative time serves as a useful benchmark for institutional maturation. In our program, reaching 76 cases represented a key transition point toward optimized workflows, enhanced efficiency, and improved resource utilization.

articles.title: Testosterone replacement therapy and aneurysm biology: current evidence and clinical implications.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is increasingly used to treat male hypogonadism, but its role in aneurysm biology remains unclear. Because aneurysm formation is driven by inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation, and vascular remodeling, testosterone may influence disease progression through androgen receptor-mediated pathways.

METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Google Scholar (August-September 2025). Studies examining testosterone, TRT, vascular inflammation, and aneurysm-related outcomes, including experimental, preclinical, and clinical studies, were included.

EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Available evidence is mostly mechanistic and preclinical. Animal studies indicate vascular bed-specific effects: physiological androgen signaling seems protective in abdominal aortic aneurysm models by reducing macrophage infiltration and inflammatory cytokine signaling, whereas exogenous or supraphysiologic testosterone may exacerbate oxidative stress and vascular injury in intracranial aneurysm models. Human data remain indirect, with no prospective studies specifically assessing aneurysm formation, growth, or rupture in TRT users. Large randomized trials and meta-analyses indicate cardiovascular safety comparable to placebo in appropriately selected patients, though higher rates of atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, and erythrocytosis have been reported.

CONCLUSION: Testosterone has context-, dose-, and vascular bed-specific effects on aneurysm biology. Until clinical studies on aneurysm outcomes are available, TRT should be individualized, dosed to meet physiological needs, and closely monitored for cardiovascular and vascular health. No evidence-based recommendation can currently be made to initiate, withhold, or modify TRT solely on the basis of aneurysm status. Multidisciplinary discussion and continued standard aneurysm surveillance are advisable for hypogonadal patients with known aneurysmal disease.

articles.title: Anomalous systemic arterial supply to the basal segment of the left lung with large vessel giant cell arteritis demonstrated by 18F-FDG PET/CT.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of anomalous systemic arterial supply to the basal segment of the left lung (ABLL) coexisting with large-vessel giant cell arteritis (LV-GCA) in a 73-year-old woman. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) demonstrated inflammatory involvement of both the aorta and the anomalous artery. To reduce vascular and perioperative risks, immunosuppressive therapy was initiated first, resulting in improvement in clinical and radiological findings. This case highlights the importance of controlling active vasculitis before definitive surgical treatment.

articles.title: Complete resection and left ventricular reconstruction for giant cardiac fibroma in a 2-year-old child.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract: Complete surgical excision is the preferred treatment for selected cardiac fibromas, although reconstruction depends on tumor location and myocardial involvement. Cardiac fibromas are the second most common primary cardiac tumor in children. They most commonly arise from the ventricular free wall or interventricular septum. Several treatment strategies have been reported, including surgical resection, single-ventricle palliation, heart transplantation, and conservative management for primary benign cardiac tumors. Recent evidence suggests that surgical resection can be curative in selected patients, eliminating the long-term dependence on antiarrhythmic drugs and avoiding the necessity for implantable defibrillators. Although this approach is now considered standard practice in some institutions-even for extensive fibromas-its adoption remains limited. We report the case of a 2-year-old child with a giant cardiac fibroma treated with complete tumor excision using a combined endocardial patch and two-layered ventricular reconstruction. The early postoperative course was uneventful, with preserved ventricular function at short-term follow-up.

articles.title: Counting hearts, missing hands: The untested variable behind India's congenital heart disease burden estimates.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

articles.title: Use of thigh-based recipient vessels for free flap reconstruction in gustilo anderson type IIIC lower extremity open fractures: Description of two cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Free tissue transfer is central to reconstruction of Gustilo IIIC lower-extremity injuries, but recipient vessel selection is challenging when local vasculature is compromised. We describe two Gustilo IIIC injuries reconstructed using thigh-based recipient vessels.

CASE PRESENTATIONS: Case 1: A 50-year-old man sustained an open tibial fracture with popliteal artery thrombosis and extensive tibial vessel injury. Following revascularization and serial debridement, a 25 × 15 cm tibial defect was reconstructed with a contralateral anterolateral thigh (ALT) free flap to the descending genicular artery (DGA), using an interposition great saphenous vein graft. The flap survived without complication.Case 2: A 35-year-old man sustained an open tibial fracture with complete popliteal artery transection requiring vascular reconstruction. A 20 × 14 cm defect was initially reconstructed with a free latissimus dorsi flap to the DGA using an interposition vein graft, complicated by venous thrombosis and flap loss. Subsequent reconstruction with an ALT flap and radial forearm flow-through flap to the superficial femoral vessels (SFA) achieved successful soft-tissue coverage.

DISCUSSION: The DGA provides an accessible recipient outside the primary zone of injury, with consistent anatomy and suitable calibre for microsurgical anastomosis. Its location facilitates a two-team approach, avoids popliteal fossa exploration, and may reduce interference with subsequent skeletal procedures. The SFA is a valuable alternative recipient vessel, offering robust and reliable inflow with a good arterial pressure head.

CONCLUSION: Thigh-based recipient vessels, particularly the DGA and SFA, should be considered in severe lower-limb trauma when conventional below-knee recipient vessels are unavailable or compromised.

articles.title: CHAMPION-AF and left atrial appendage closure: non-inferiority or a trade-off in risk?
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract: The Watchman FLX versus Novel Oral Anticoagulation for Embolic Protection in the Management of Patients with Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation (CHAMPION-AF) trial compared left atrial appendage (LAA) closure using the Watchman FLX device with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation eligible for long-term anticoagulation. LAA closure demonstrated non-inferiority for the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death, stroke, or systemic embolism and reduced non-procedure-related bleeding. However, interpretation is limited by a permissive non-inferiority margin, reliance on a composite endpoint, exclusion of procedural bleeding from the primary safety outcome, and a numerical excess of ischaemic strokes. Overall, CHAMPION-AF represents a shift in risk profile rather than therapeutic equivalence, supporting LAA closure in selected patients rather than as a routine first-line alternative to NOAC therapy.

articles.title: Intraoperative ventilatory air leak as a predictor of prolonged air leak following lung resection: a pilot prospective comparative study.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged air leak (PAL) remains a common complication following pulmonary resection and is associated with increased morbidity, prolonged hospitalisation, and higher healthcare costs. The Brunelli Score (BS) is a validated clinical prediction model for PAL, while intraoperative ventilatory air leak (VAL) has emerged as a potential physiological predictor. This pilot study evaluated the predictive value of VAL and compared its performance with BS.

METHODS: This prospective observational pilot study included 109 patients undergoing pulmonary resection between September 2022 and December 2024. Preoperative BS and intraoperative VAL measurements were recorded. PAL was defined as air leak persisting beyond postoperative day 5. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, logistic regression, and three-group comparative analysis were performed.

RESULTS: PAL occurred in 24 patients (22%). VAL demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.818 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.715-0.921), while BS demonstrated an AUC of 0.656 (95% CI 0.536 to 0.776). The optimal VAL cut-off (≥ 11.1%) yielded 58.3% sensitivity and 94.1% specificity, whereas BS (≥ 2.5) also demonstrated the same sensitivity but a lower specificity (64.7%). The difference in AUC was 0.162 (95% CI 0.003 to 0.322) and reached nominal statistical significance on DeLong comparison (p = 0.046). On multivariable analysis, VAL ≥ 11.1% remained independently associated with PAL (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 17.22, 95% CI 4.56 to 65.07, p < 0.001), whereas the BS was not independently predictive after adjustment (adjusted OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.12 to 2.55, p = 0.446). Lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), open thoracotomy, major resection, dense pleural adhesions, and infective pulmonary pathology were associated with PAL on univariable analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: VAL demonstrated higher discrimination and a stronger independent association with PAL than the BS. The difference between the two AUCs was of borderline statistical significance in a cohort well short of the calculated sample size, so definitive superiority cannot be claimed on these data. The BS and VAL may have complementary roles in preoperative risk stratification and intraoperative physiological assessment of PAL risk. Larger multicentre studies are required for validation.

GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT: Intraoperative ventilatory air leak (VAL) and the preoperative Brunelli Score were compared as predictors of prolonged air leak in 109 consecutive patients undergoing elective pulmonary resection. Prolonged air leak occurred in 24 patients (22.0%). VAL discriminated better than the Brunelli Score (area under the curve 0.818 versus 0.656), and the difference reached borderline statistical significance on DeLong testing (p = 0.046). VAL was the only variable retaining independent significance after adjustment for surgical approach, extent of resection and dense pleural adhesions. AUC, area under the curve; ROC, receiver operating characteristic curve; BMI, body mass index; CI, confidence interval; FEV₁, forced expiratory volume in 1 second; VAL, ventilatory air leak.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12055-026-02276-8.

articles.title: Nanoplastic Exposure Impairs Host Fitness and Parasite Transmission With Transgenerational Maternal Reproductive Costs in the Daphnia-Fungal Parasite System.
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging contaminants in aquatic ecosystems, but their direct and maternally transmitted effects on host-parasite interactions remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects of polystyrene nanoplastic exposure (50 nm, 5 mg L-1) on Daphnia magna infected with the fungal parasite Australozyma monospora across two host generations. Direct nanoplastic exposure occurred in the parental generation (F0), whereas F1 offspring were raised in nanoplastic-free medium to isolate maternal nanoplastic effects. Direct nanoplastic exposure severely impaired F0 host fitness, reduced reproductive probability and total offspring production, while halving median survival time relative to controls. Nanoplastic exposure also impaired parasite maturation likelihood by decreasing host survival prior to transmission. Infection prevalence and spore production did not differ between nanoplastic-exposed and control hosts among individuals that survived to the transmission stage, suggesting that nanoplastic exposure compromises parasite fitness primarily through accelerated host mortality rather than through within-host suppression. In the F1 generation, offspring of nanoplastic-exposed mothers had lower reproductive probability and delayed age at first clutch, despite experiencing no direct nanoplastic exposure. Host survival and parasite fitness outcomes were not altered in F1. Together, these results demonstrate that nanoplastic pollution disrupts host-parasite dynamics both directly and across generations, imposing reproductive costs that persist in unexposed offspring through maternal effects. Such transgenerational effects compromise host population recovery and amplify parasite transmission in nanoplastic-contaminated freshwater environments.

articles.title: Six-month real-world glycemic improvement after Smart MDI system in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Smart multiple daily injection (Smart MDI) system integrating continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin pens, and decision-support tools may optimize glycemic control in type 1 diabetes (T1D). However, real-world data remain limited. We evaluated 6-month glycemic outcomes following transition to Smart MDI in adults with T1D and explored differences according to carbohydrate counting status.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study included 24 adults with T1D on MDI who transitioned to Smart MDI. CGM metrics were analyzed at baseline and after 1, 3, and 6 months. The primary outcome was change in time in range (TIR 70-180 mg/dL). Secondary outcomes included time above range (TAR), time below range (TBR), mean glucose, glucose management indicator (GMI), coefficient of variation, and HbA1c. Exploratory analyses compared individuals practicing carbohydrate counting (n = 12) with those who did not (n = 12).

RESULTS: TIR increased progressively from 56.1 ± 20.4% to 66.3 ± 17.5% (median change +9.0%, P < .01). TAR and TBR significantly decreased. HbA1c declined from 7.6 ± 1.1% to 7.3 ± 0.9% (median change -0.2%, P = .01). While between-group differences were not significant, individuals not practicing carbohydrate counting showed preliminary within-group improvements in TIR, TAR, mean glucose, GMI, and HbA1c, without increased TBR, whereas changes in the carbohydrate counting group were smaller.

CONCLUSIONS: Transition to the Smart MDI system was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in CGM metrics and HbA1c over 6 months. Improvements among individuals not practicing carbohydrate counting suggest that the Smart MDI system may provide standardized decision support also beneficial in less structured self-management settings. Larger studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Deep learning analysis of sinus-rhythm echocardiography for the identification of patients with atrial fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) is underdiagnosed due to its intermittent and asymptomatic nature. We evaluated whether a deep neural network (DNN) applied to transthoracic echocardiograms (TTEs) acquired in sinus rhythm can discriminate between patients with and without documented AF and identify individuals at increased risk for subsequent AF documentation and adverse outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed 85 686 TTE studies (2009-21). A DNN was applied to apical four-chamber and parasternal long-axis videos without Doppler. AF ground truth was based on International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes, electrocardiogram, Holter, or prior echocardiographic documentation of AF. The dataset was split into training (60%), validation (20%), and an independent test set (20%). In the test cohort, we assessed discrimination performance. Among patients without prior AF, we evaluated associations between model classification and subsequent AF documentation and a composite outcome of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or stroke. The test set included 17 121 patients (median age 66 years [interquartile range, IQR 54-75]; 57.6% male), of whom 3449 (20.1%) had prior AF. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.85, with sensitivity 0.80 and specificity 0.72. At the selected threshold, 6581 patients (38.4%) were classified as model-positive, including 3832 (58.2%) without prior AF. Among patients without prior AF, model-positive classification was associated with subsequent AF documentation [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.64; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.33-2.04] and with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 1.24; 95% CI 1.13-1.35).

CONCLUSION: Deep learning applied to sinus-rhythm TTE demonstrates discrimination for AF and identifies an imaging-derived signal associated with subsequent AF documentation and adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Investigating the Effect of Photovoice on the Resilience and Perceived Social Stigma of Patients With Type 1 Diabetes: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with type 1 diabetes often experience high levels of perceived social stigma, which can severely impact their psychological resilience. Photovoice is an innovative visual participatory method, but its efficacy in this population remains unexplored. This study protocol aims to evaluate the effect of a photovoice intervention on resilience and perceived social stigma in patients with type 1 diabetes.

METHODS: This is a single-blind, two-group, three-stage clinical trial with a pretest-posttest design and 1-month follow-up. A total of 56 patients with type 1 diabetes will be selected fromIsfahan Comprehensive Health Centers using cluster sampling before being divided into two intervention and control groups by a simple randomization method. The intervention group will undergo a 4-week photovoice intervention, which focuses on topics such as identity recovery, management of fear and negative emotions, compatibility with family and friends, and management of emotions resulting from judgments and blame. During the intervention, participants will prepare photos with specified topics and analyze and discuss them in group sessions using the SHOWED technique. The control group will receive routine care at the health centers. Resilience and perceived social stigma in both groups will be measured before, immediately after, and 1 month after the intervention using standard questionnaires. The data will be analyzed through SPSS-20 software using t-tests and repeated measures ANOVA.

RESULTS: Results will be reported in accordance with CONSORT guidelines following the completion of the trial. This paper presents the rationale and methodology for the study.

CONCLUSION: This study will evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of the photovoice intervention in enhancing psychological resilience and reducing perceived social stigma in patients with type 1 diabetes, and will provide evidence for the application of this approach in nursing care.

articles.title: Challenges in managing tracheal adenoid cystic carcinoma of the proximal trachea complicated by COVID-19 and bilateral vocal cord palsy.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is primarily a salivary gland tumor that rarely involves the respiratory tract. Primary malignant tumors of the trachea are very rare, with an incidence of less than two cases per 1,000,000 people per year, and only 10 to 15% of them are ACCs. We present a rare case of ACC of the proximal trachea in a 68-year-old female patient. The patient initially presented with stridor that was first recognized as a symptom of asthma, but a multislice computed tomography scan revealed a tracheal tumor. She afterwards underwent a tracheostomy, during which a biopsy was performed, establishing the diagnosis of an ACC. Subsequently, a surgical resection with a cricotracheal anastomosis was performed. The postoperative course was complicated by bilateral dysfunction of the vocal cords on the third postoperative day and by coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection with bilateral pneumonia on the tenth postoperative day. A combination of ACC of the proximal part of the trachea with postoperative development of bilateral vocal cord dysfunction and postoperative COVID-19 infection makes this case uncommon and instructive.

articles.title: Cardiac myxoma with glandular differentiation: a rare diagnostic pitfall.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac myxomas are the most common primary benign tumors of the heart, with the majority occurring in the left atrium. They are typically composed of gelatinous connective tissue, but rare cases exhibit unusual histological features, including glandular differentiation, which can mimic malignant neoplasms and pose diagnostic challenges. While these tumors are benign, rare cases of tumor embolism to the brain have been reported. Surgical resection remains the treatment of choice, with excellent long-term outcomes in most cases.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 27-year-old woman presented with progressive palpitations, shortness of breath, chest pain, and cough. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a large, mobile mass in the left atrium. Surgical excision was performed, revealing a gelatinous tumor with areas of glandular differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed the epithelial origin of the glandular structures, with a diagnosis of cardiac myxoma with glandular differentiation.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac myxomas with glandular differentiation are rare but important entities that require careful histological and immunohistochemical evaluation to avoid misdiagnosis as primary or metastatic adenocarcinoma. Patients should be monitored for recurrence and potential embolic complications.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12055-026-02247-z.

articles.title: Lifetime management of aortic stenosis: a strategy, or a euphemism?
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

articles.title: Atrial septal defect associated with suspected left ventricular non-compaction supported by histopathological findings in a child.
articles.journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract: Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) is a rare cardiomyopathy characterized by excessive trabeculation of the left ventricular myocardium. The debate over whether LVNC is a distinct disease entity limits the estimates on its prevalence and incidence as there is a significant overlap with other known cardiomyopathies like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, apical hypertrophy, and dilated cardiomyopathy. This condition is defined by excessive trabeculation of the myocardium, with deep intertrabecular recesses that communicate directly with the ventricular cavity. We report an 11-year-old boy with ostium secundum atrial septal defect (ASD), unexplained left ventricular dysfunction, and intraoperative findings suggestive of LVNC, in whom histopathological examination provided supportive evidence for the diagnosis. The decision for fenestrated ASD closure was based on reduced left ventricular compliance demonstrated during preoperative assessment. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of LVNC when classical echocardiographic criteria are not fulfilled and emphasizes the complementary role of histopathological findings in selected cases.

articles.title: Abnormal Resting-State Functional Connectivity in Individuals with Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) leads to sensorimotor deficits and secondary health complications, such as pain and cognitive impairment. At the brain level, functional reorganization phenomena occur, affecting resting-state (rs) networks devoted to higher-order information processing. However, most studies have focused on changes of the sensorimotor cortex, and current results are partially conflicting. This systematic review aims to synthesize studies on rs networks implicated in SCI and to investigate whether functional connectivity (FC) is affected beyond the somatomotor network, which may be linked to secondary health conditions. Original seed-based whole-brain rs FC (rsFC) studies comparing individuals with SCI and controls were retrieved from Medline, Embase, and Web of Science (last searched on 02.09.2024). Each seed was assigned to a standard rs network, and studies were grouped based on seed network and direction of changed rsFC. Risk of bias was assessed using the quality assessment tool by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. The study was registered in Prospero (CRD42024574397). Nine included studies provided 11 datasets (151 SCI individuals, 208 controls). RsFC changes were found between the somatomotor and ventral attentional network, between the ventral attention network and the frontal pole, and between the cerebellum and regions of the attentional and default-mode networks in SCI compared with controls. We propose a model of SCI with widespread network changes that extend beyond the somatomotor network. Our findings call for deeper examination of functional brain changes following SCI in clinical settings and thorough investigations of higher-order cognitive functions.

articles.title: How Preceptors Can Cultivate Professional Identity Formation Through Meaningful Participation in Experiential Learning.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
articles.abstract: When engaged in experiential learning, trainees enter a complex ecosystem where expertise relies on collaboration and the intentional use of environmental resources. To better explain this learning environment, this paper will define and describe concepts of educational theory related to situativity theory and the cognitive ecosystems perspective and offer ways to apply them to experiential learning design using an intensive care unit (ICU) as an example practice setting. By viewing the ICU as a cognitive ecosystem, we highlight how recognition and use of available resources and opportunities can support trainee growth and development of a contextualized, or situated, professional identity. Traditionally, experiential learning has emphasized internal mental processes, focusing on how trainees assess patients and recognize medication-related problems. However, expertise extends beyond individual knowledge and includes the ability to recognize and interact with the physical and social elements that exist within the clinical environment. Although the interconnected nature of clinical practice is widely recognized, limited guidance exists for applying situativity theory and cognitive ecosystems to experiential learning design. Viewing a practice setting as a cognitive ecosystem provides a lens for intentionally immersing trainees within the environment to promote meaningful participation in clinical practice. When viewed through this lens, microsystems within the practice setting emerge that support clinical reasoning, communication, and patient care. Across these microsystems, interactions with the resources and people within the environment may promote the development of clinical reasoning and situated professional identity. Intentional interactions within each microsystem can help trainees progress from an observational role to active participation in patient care, progressing beyond basic knowledge acquisition and recall. Using the ICU as an example, we argue that viewing the practice area as a cognitive ecosystem offers opportunities for experiential learning design for preceptors, along with enriching experiences for trainees that are critical for professional identity formation.

articles.title: Between Skin and Brain: A Systematic Review of 712 Cases 1976-2025 Reveals a Highly Diverse Disease Spectrum in Chaetothyriales.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Black yeast-like species of the order Chaetothyriales cause superficial to life-threatening systemic infections. Comprehensive global epidemiology data remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to analyze the global epidemiology, spectrum of pathogens, clinical manifestations and outcomes of Chaetothyriales infections.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 712 cases reported between 1976 and 2025.

RESULTS: The analysis revealed a steady increase in diagnosed cases, with Cladophialophora bantiana (21%), Exophiala dermatitidis (19%), and E. jeanselmei (15%) being the predominant causative agents; notably, the proportion of E. jeanselmei declined from 18%-28% in 1976-2015 to 7% in 2016-2025. Published cases were more frequent in tropical/subtropical regions; however, cases were reported from Africa. Although 42% of infections occurred in immunocompetent individuals, transplant recipients, diabetics, and those with CARD9 deficiency showed higher risk. Deep infections exhibited substantially greater mortality than cutaneous forms (47% vs. 7%; p < 0.001); particularly, central nervous system infections (58%) and disseminated disease (53%) were involved.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights a seemingly growing burden of Chaetothyriales infections, possibly partly due to better recognition, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, and targeted prevention in high-risk populations.

articles.title: Clinical Phenotypes, Machine-Learning Risk Stratification and Treatment Outcomes of Constipation in Stroke Patients Receiving Enteral Nutrition: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke-related complications and frequent feeding interruptions often compromise nutritional intake, making enteral nutrition (EN) a cornerstone therapy to improve nutritional status and support recovery. Nevertheless, constipation is highly prevalent and clinically consequential among stroke patients receiving EN, particularly in critically ill populations, where enteral nutrition-associated constipation can impede rehabilitation, increase complications and prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay.

AIM: This study aimed to explore potentially important determinants of enteral nutrition-associated constipation (ENAC) in patients with stroke using artificial intelligence approaches, characterise relevant clinical subgroups, compare internally validated machine-learning models and examine how the temporal availability of candidate predictors may influence model performance.

STUDY DESIGN: Clinical data from patients admitted to a neurological intensive care unit between December 2019 and December 2023 were retrospectively analysed. K-means clustering was used to identify clinical subgroups. Six algorithms-logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting tree, XGBoost, LightGBM and Table PFN-3-were compared under temporally restricted and expanded retrospective feature frameworks using five repeats of nested five-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using ROC-AUC, average precision, Brier score, calibration and decision-curve analysis. Treatment outcomes were summarised descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 362 patients, 233 (64.4%) had documented constipation. Table PFN-3 achieved the highest discrimination in both frameworks. The temporally restricted model yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.629 (95% CI 0.567-0.689), whereas the expanded retrospective model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.771 (95% CI 0.715-0.820), average precision of 0.857, Brier score of 0.177 and calibration slope of 0.965. The ROC-AUC increased by 0.142 (95% CI 0.090-0.201) after full-hospitalisation information was included. K-means clustering retained three subgroups (K = 3; silhouette coefficient = 0.108), with constipation frequencies of 67.35%, 56.98% and 88.89% in Clusters 0, 1 and 2, respectively. Among evaluable patients, observed relief was 80.3% with glycerin enema, 60.0% with lactulose, 72.7% with combination treatment and 65.7% with neither treatment; these treatment comparisons were descriptive.

CONCLUSIONS: Table PFN-3 achieved the strongest internally validated performance, with the expanded retrospective framework combining good discrimination, strong precision-recall performance and close calibration. The 0.142 increase in ROC-AUC after completed hospital-course variables were incorporated quantifies the substantial discriminative information that emerges as hospitalisation evolves. Together with the distinct clinical phenotypes and descriptive treatment findings, these results establish a clinically relevant framework for trajectory-aware bowel monitoring and provide a clear rationale for developing dynamic, time-updated prediction models.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: By integrating machine-learning benchmarking, clinical phenotyping and observed treatment outcomes, this study identifies prolonged, treatment-intensive hospital trajectories as a particularly high-burden constipation phenotype and demonstrates that classification performance changes materially as hospital-course information accumulates. These findings support structured reassessment of bowel risk during neurological intensive care rather than reliance on a single static evaluation and provide a practical rationale for future dynamic monitoring tools.

articles.title: SU5, a Stable Auraptene Analog, Ameliorates Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis Through Modulation of the FXR Signaling Pathway.
articles.abstract: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH), a metabolic liver disease severely threatening public health, is characterized by hepatic steatosis, inflammatory infiltration, and fibrotic progression. Currently, there is still a lack of specific therapeutic approaches for MASH in clinical practice. Auraptene (AUR), a natural citrus-derived compound with demonstrated therapeutic potential against MASH, is limited in clinical translation by poor metabolic stability. To address this challenge, we evaluated the effects and mechanisms of SU5, a novel auraptene analog engineered for enhanced metabolic stability, in a MASH mouse model induced by a high-fat/high-sugar diet combined with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4). SU5 treatment effectively reduced hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis in MASH mice. It activated the FXR pathway, regulating bile acid metabolism-related genes. SU5 also suppressed lipogenic genes, decreased inflammatory factors, and restored lipid homeostasis. Outperforming auraptene, SU5 is a promising MASH treatment option due to its enhanced stability.

articles.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Creating Educational Material for Critical Care Clinicians: A Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: One Minute Wonders (OMWs) are workplace-based microlearning resources that support continuing professional development in healthcare. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to create educational materials, but little is known about its application in OMWs development.

AIMS: To examine the use, experiences, opportunities and challenges related to AI-assisted generation of OMWs as perceived among healthcare professionals participating in the German-speaking OMW Network.

STUDY DESIGN: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among members of the German-speaking OMW Network in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. A study-specific questionnaire assessed AI use, quality assurance practices, perceived benefits and risks and educational support needs. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, and free-text responses underwent qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 136 healthcare professionals were included, predominantly nurses (n = 128, 94.1%). Overall, n = 63 (46.3%) reported using AI to create OMW. Among AI users, AI was most used for generating figures (n = 41, 65.1%), graphics (n = 35, 55.6%) and design elements (n = 33, 52.4%), with ChatGPT being the most frequently used tool (n = 60, 95.2%). Most AI users critically reviewed AI-generated content (n = 50, 79.4%). Inaccuracies requiring revision were reported by all AI users, most commonly ambiguous wording (n = 32, 50.8%), inappropriate images (n = 32, 50.8%) and incorrect content (n = 29, 46.0%). The content analysis identified a main theme for opportunities: AI as a facilitator of educational resource development and knowledge translation and a main theme for risks: AI as a potential threat to the trustworthiness and professional integrity of educational resources.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of AI for developing educational materials such as OMWs seems to be established practice among participants of this study. AI offers benefits for efficiency and content creation but requires careful human oversight because inaccuracies and fabricated information are common.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: AI can support the rapid development of workplace-based educational resources. However, critical review and quality assurance are essential to ensure accuracy and safety.

articles.title: Rapid Response System Escalation During Recovery of Hospital Bed Occupancy: An Observational Longitudinal Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early warning scores (EWS) identify patient deterioration, but their impact depends on how they are integrated into workflows and escalation culture, particularly as hospitals recover from pandemic-related bed pressures.

AIMS: To evaluate changes in rapid response system (RRS) escalation processes and rare safety outcomes after embedding an EWS within proactive Critical Care Outreach Team (CCOT) rounds as hospital bed occupancy recovered.

STUDY DESIGN: Observational longitudinal study at a single tertiary hospital in Japan comparing one pre-intervention year (2021) with three post-intervention years (2022-2024). In January 2022, a standardised EWS was embedded into proactive CCOT rounds and used as a prompt for shared clinical reasoning rather than a strict numeric trigger. Monthly aggregated ward-level data were analysed using Poisson regression, adjusting for seasonality, patient characteristics and bed occupancy.

RESULTS: Across 71 985 admissions and 692 942 general-ward patient-days, rates of nurse-initiated escalations, RRS activations and resuscitation-status updates per 1000 patient-days increased in post-intervention analyses, but these differences were attenuated after full adjustment. In fully adjusted models, post-intervention incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were close to 1.0 for all process outcomes. For nurse-initiated escalations, IRRs ranged from 0.94 to 1.14, and all 95% confidence intervals included 1.0. Rates of unexpected in-hospital cardiac arrest and unplanned ICU admission remained low and stable. Bed occupancy increased over the study period, but within-year associations with outcomes were weak.

CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital bed occupancy, embedding an EWS within proactive CCOT rounds was associated with broadly stable escalation process indicators and no clear evidence of deterioration in rare safety outcomes.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: These findings suggest that approaches to the RRS afferent limb that embed EWS use within structured dialogue between ward nurses and outreach teams may provide one plausible mechanism for sustaining escalation behaviours under operational pressure.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rg1 Alleviates Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Partially Through Regulating ABCB1-Mediated Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.abstract: To investigate the protective effects of ginsenoside Rg1 on lung injury in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and to elucidate the underlying mechanism involving ATP-binding cassette subfamily B member 1 (ABCB1)-mediated regulation of mitochondrial function. A COPD rat model was established by cigarette smoke exposure, followed by in vivo administration of different doses of ginsenoside Rg1. ABCB1 knockdown was achieved by tail vein injection of short hairpin RNA (shRNA). Hematoxylin and eosin (HE) and Masson staining were performed to evaluate lung histopathology and collagen deposition. Pulmonary function was assessed by measuring inspiratory resistance (Ri), dynamic lung compliance (Cdyn), and the ratio of forced expiratory volume at 0.3 s to forced vital capacity (FEV0.3/FVC). In vitro, cigarette smoke extract (CSE) was used to induce injury in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells, followed by Rg1 treatment and ABCB1 overexpression or knockdown. Advanced glycation end products-receptor for advanced glycation end products (AGEs-RAGE) and early growth response protein 1-c-Jun N-terminal kinase (EGR1-JNK) signaling pathways were detected. In COPD rats, Rg1 markedly attenuated alveolar structural destruction and collagen deposition, decreased Ri, increased Cdyn and FEV0.3/FVC. ABCB1 knockdown partially reversed these protective effects. In HBE cells, Rg1 enhanced cell viability, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced apoptosis, decreased ROS accumulation, and rescued intracellular ATP depletion. Rg1 inhibited the activation of the AGEs-RAGE and EGR1-JNK pathways in a manner associated with upregulation of ABCB1 expression. Ginsenoside Rg1 enhances mitochondrial function partially through upregulation of ABCB1 expression, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction in COPD rats and CSE-treated HBE cells.

articles.title: Evidence Meeting Reality: Sepsis in Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
The impact of patient weight status on healthcare students' attitudes: Two experimental studies in midwifery and dental students.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight stigma refers to prejudice and discrimination based on body weight. Healthcare professionals often hold negative attitudes towards patients with overweight, which can negatively affect patient care and health outcomes. However, weight stigma is yet to be explored in midwifery and dental students.

METHODS: Two online experimental studies using hypothetical patient vignettes were conducted in midwifery (n = 281; Study 1) and dental and non-dental students (n = 528; Study 2). Participants were randomly assigned to view a healthy-weight, overweight or obese patient vignette and then reported their attitudes, predicted time, advice they would provide and beliefs about obesity. Data were analysed using ANOVA and logistic regression.

RESULTS: In Study 1, midwifery students held significantly more stigmatizing attitudes towards patients who were overweight than healthy-weight patients; however, there was no significant difference in attitudes towards patients with obesity. Predicted time spent with patients did not significantly differ as a function of patient weight status. In Study 2, dental and non-dental students reported more stigmatizing attitudes towards overweight and obese patients compared to healthy-weight patients. Predicted time spent with patients did not differ significantly. Dental and non-dental students were more likely to offer lifestyle-related advice to overweight and obese patients. There was no significant relationship between beliefs about obesity and attitudes towards treating patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Weight stigma is evident among healthcare students and can affect healthcare advice. Increased awareness of potential biases in midwives and dental students is needed and should form formal training to improve equitable healthcare delivery.

articles.title: Psychological Distress Among Black Surrogates of Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.abstract: Anticipatory grief and Post-Intensive Care Syndrome-Family (PICS-F) are increasingly recognised as important sources of psychological distress among family members of critically ill patients. However, these experiences remain understudied among Black surrogate decision-makers. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between anticipatory grief and PICS-F and to examine whether emotional closeness and positive religious coping were associated with anticipatory grief among Black family surrogates of intensive care unit (ICU) patients. In this cross-sectional survey study, 70 Black surrogate decision-makers of adult ICU patients were recruited from ICUs at a large metropolitan hospital in the Midwestern United States. Participants completed measures of emotional closeness, positive religious coping, anticipatory grief, anxiety, depression and post-traumatic stress symptoms. Multivariable linear regression analyses examined associations among study variables. Emotional closeness and positive religious coping were not statistically significantly associated with anticipatory grief. Anticipatory grief was statistically significantly associated with higher PICS-F symptoms. Among Black ICU surrogate decision-makers, anticipatory grief was associated with greater psychological distress, suggesting it may represent an important target for future supportive interventions and research.

articles.title: Virtual Social Interaction and Psychological Capital in Chemotherapy Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-related psychological distress remains underaddressed globally. Virtual interventions offer promising alternatives but lack evidence for enhancing Psychological Capital (PsyCap) in chemotherapy patients.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a virtual social interaction intervention on PsyCap in patients undergoing chemotherapy.

METHODS: This single-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 76 chemotherapy patients hospitalized in the oncology ward of Imam Sajjad Hospital, Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran. Participants were selected via convenience sampling and then allocated to intervention or control groups using an odd-even (alternating) assignment method. The intervention group participated in 6 weeks of virtual social interactions, consisting of asynchronous materials (recorded audio, short videos, images, PDF, and PowerPoint files) uploaded weekly to Iranian messaging platforms (Eitaa), as well as live synchronous group sessions conducted on the Skyroom platform with a minimum of 10 participants per session. The control group received standard care. The PsyCap was measured using Luthans' Psychological Capital Questionnaire at both baseline and post-intervention. The Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) models (A/B) were adjusted for baseline scores and age.

RESULTS: The intervention group showed improvements across all outcomes, with the total PsyCap score increasing by 23.6 points. Components significantly increased: self-efficacy by 5.8 points, resilience by 5.8, hope by 5.5, and optimism by 6.5 (p < 0.0001). ANCOVA models confirmed robust effects after adjusting for baseline scores and age (Δ SMD > 1).

CONCLUSIONS: Virtual social interactions significantly enhance PsyCap in chemotherapy patients. However, to confidently generalize these findings and make recommendations, similar studies need to be conducted and replicated in larger, multicenter trials.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods.

AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method.

STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025.

RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59).

CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

articles.title: Sense of Coherence in Patients After Intensive Care Treatment: A 1-Year Follow-Up Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients endure physical, mental and cognitive symptoms after critical illness, and coping is vital to their healing process. Little research exists on associations between sense of coherence (SOC) and patients' health improvements after intensive care unit (ICU) discharge.

AIMS: To describe the trajectory of SOC and how demographic, clinical and psychosocial variables affect SOC in discharged ICU patients during 12 months of follow-up.

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective cohort substudy of a neutral randomized controlled trial in Norway involving discharged ICU patients receiving nurse-led follow-up consultations or standard care. Data were collected in the ward (baseline) and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Univariate and multivariate linear mixed models for repeated measures were fitted with SOC-13 score as the dependent variable.

RESULTS: We included 523 patients with a median of three ICU days, median age 57 years, 47% females, 54% receiving mechanical ventilation and stable SOC during follow-up. Higher SOC was associated with increased age (B = 0.12, 95% CI [0.05, 0.18]), no prior mental health problems (B = 6.69, 95% CI [4.19, 9.19]), no prior use of psychotropics (B = 2.37, 95% CI [0.16, 4.58]) and lower post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) at baseline (B = 5.56, 95% CI [3.50, 7.61]).
