Low educational level (B = -2.25, 95% CI [-4.10, -0.40]), higher pain interference at baseline (B = -0.46, 95% CI [-0.84, -0.08]) and less social support 3 months later (B = -5.93, 95% CI [-7.87, -3.99]) were associated with lower SOC.

CONCLUSIONS: During 12 months after ICU discharge, SOC remained stable. Higher age, no previous mental health problems or use of psychotropics, and lower PTSS were associated with higher SOC. Low education, more pain and low social support were associated with lower SOC.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: More vulnerable patients deserve greater attention during general rehabilitation after ICU treatment due to low SOC.

articles.title: Family Engagement and Shared Decision-Making in Adult Intensive Care Nursing: A Bibliometric Review and Thematic Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family members contribute information, emotional support, bedside care and surrogate decision-making in adult intensive care, yet the nursing literature on family engagement remains conceptually and geographically fragmented.

AIMS: To map the development, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns and thematic evolution of research on family engagement and shared decision-making in adult intensive care nursing.

STUDY DESIGN: This study was a bibliometric review with complementary thematic content analysis. Following the framework of Donthu et al., Scopus was searched on 16 July 2026 from inception, with bibliometric coverage restricted to complete calendar years through 31 December 2025. Scopus was used because it provides the cited-reference data required for co-citation and bibliographic-coupling analyses. Eligible records were journal articles and reviews concerning adult intensive care that examined family engagement or shared decision-making and included an identifiable nursing component. Performance analysis, co-authorship analysis, reference co-citation, bibliographic coupling, and keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted using Python and VOSviewer, while cluster content was interpreted using inductive qualitative content analysis. Reporting followed the BIBLIO guideline.

RESULTS: The review included 278 publications (1993-2025) from 117 journals and 47 countries. Annual output increased from two publications in 1993 to 32 publications in 2025; 141 publications (50.7%) were published during 2020-2025. Nursing journals produced most publications, whereas two multidisciplinary critical care journals produced 23 publications (8.3%) but 3090 of 11 220 citations (27.5%). The United States led with 104 publications; 23.9% were internationally co-authored. Co-citation analysis identified four intellectual foundations and bibliographic coupling five research fronts, led by family participation and nurse-family engagement. Thirty-nine author keywords formed six themes spanning end-of-life communication and ethics, family-centred nursing engagement and surrogate participation, family support and visitation, family presence in high-acuity care, caregiver experience and bereavement. Keyword trends moved from family needs and withholding treatment towards active engagement, implementation barriers and family nursing.

CONCLUSION: The field has progressed towards partnership but continues to under-specify nurses' roles, use inconsistent terminology and draw disproportionately on high-income Western settings.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Critical care services should formalise nurses' responsibilities in family assessment, communication, advocacy and decision support while developing culturally responsive and implementable engagement models.

articles.title: Associations Between Parity and Parasympathetic Regulation in Response to Infant Crying.
articles.abstract: Research suggests that women's parasympathetic response to infant crying reflects regulation of arousal and is associated with caregiving behaviors. In particular, respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) withdrawal in response to infant cry stimuli has been associated with maternal sensitivity. However, the ways in which multiple reproductive and caregiving experiences (in terms of giving birth and raising a child) can modulate women's RSA in response to infant crying are still unknown. Our aim was to test whether women's RSA in response to infant crying is associated with parity. Participants included 184 women (62 nulliparous women; 86 primiparous women; 36 multiparous women). RSA was measured while women were watching a neutral video, followed by videos of crying infants. Analyses revealed that perception of infant crying was associated with a significant RSA withdrawal, compared to the baseline condition, in both multiparous and nulliparous women. A statistically significant RSA withdrawal was absent among primiparous women, possibly reflecting a more sustained physiological arousal to infant crying. We discuss the potential challenges in physiological regulation, indexed by RSA withdrawal, among primiparous women in response to infant crying. More sustained arousal may support an increased focus on infant signals but also predispose new mothers to perceive greater stress.

articles.title: QUIET Care: A Nursing-Led Conceptual Analysis of Alarm-Related Acoustic Burden in Adult Critical Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult intensive care units (ICUs) generate a persistent acoustic burden from alarms, care activity, equipment and communication. This burden can undermine patient rest and contribute to alarm fatigue, cognitive workload and distress among nurses.

AIM: To present a nursing-led conceptual framework for addressing alarm-related acoustic burden in adult critical care.

STUDY DESIGN: Literature-informed conceptual analysis. A structured purposive evidence map was audited using two PubMed searches run on 9 September 2026 (3377 unique records after PMID deduplication) and citation checking. Twenty-nine selected sources were charted against the five domains. This was not a systematic review; no original data, formal consensus or framework validation was undertaken.

RESULTS: QUIET Care proposes five connected practice domains: quantify and qualify the sound environment; use patient-specific monitoring and alarms; integrate quiet into workflow; engage people and culture; and track, test and learn. It treats the domains as locally adaptable hypotheses and requires explicit safety balancing measures.

CONCLUSIONS: QUIET Care is a pragmatic proposal for local co-design and evaluation, not a validated intervention or universal sound target.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The framework may help critical care nurses and leaders organise source mapping, alarm customisation, workflow redesign, team ownership and small safety-monitored tests of change while preserving the audibility of urgent alerts.

articles.title: RSV Disease Among Hospitalized Children: Second vs. First Year of Life Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric hospitalization, yet data on children hospitalized with RSV in their second year of life are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics and management practices of children hospitalized with RSV during their second versus first year of life.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included children aged 0-23 months hospitalized with RSV infection across 11 medical centers between 2017 and 2021. We compared demographics, outcomes (length of stay [LOS] > 3 days, and pediatric intensive care unit [PICU] admission), and systemic corticosteroid and antibiotic use between the second and first years of life, adjusting for prematurity, comorbidities, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

RESULTS: Among 6260 children hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, 1321 (21%) were hospitalized during their second year of life. Compared with first-year admissions, second-year patients had higher rates of prematurity (18.0% vs. 13.4%) and comorbidities (6.3% vs. 2.6%) (both p < 0.001). They more frequently received corticosteroids (53.5% vs. 23.2%) and antibiotics (63.4% vs. 45.9%) (both p < 0.001) and had lower PICU admission rates (4.6% vs. 7.0%; p < 0 0.001) and similar rates of prolonged LOS (35.0% vs. 35.6%; p = 0.64). In adjusted analyses, second-year hospitalization was associated with increased corticosteroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.28; 95% CI, 3.67-4.99) and antibiotic use (aOR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.80-2.43), and lower odds of PICU admission (aOR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.40-0.79).

CONCLUSIONS: RSV hospitalization in the second year of life carries a significant burden, with higher antibiotic and corticosteroid use despite lower PICU rates and similar LOS. These findings highlight the need for better characterization of this age group to optimize future immunoprophylaxis strategies.

articles.title: Ex Vivo Thrombin Generation Assessment of Four Anticoagulants in Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolic events (VTE) are a serious complication in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Currently, there is no consensus regarding anticoagulant treatment or prevention in this setting, and the role of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) has not been extensively studied. The recent approval of DOACs for the treatment of VTE in children supports their further evaluation in pediatric patients with ALL. We prospectively evaluated the effects of four anticoagulant agents in 67 pediatric patients with ALL, compared with healthy controls, using the global coagulation assay thrombin generation (TG). The first 21 patients formed the calibration cohort, and we performed the primary TG analysis in the subsequent 46 patients. Measurements were performed before and after asparaginase therapy, with and without ex vivo spiking of the different anticoagulants. Low-molecular-weight heparin demonstrated preserved anticoagulant activity both before and after asparaginase therapy, with reductions of 29% and 31% in thrombin peak height, respectively, similar to healthy controls. However, the direct factor Xa inhibitors apixaban and rivaroxaban showed minimal anticoagulant effect (7%-13% reduction in thrombin peak height compared with reductions of 48%-59%, in controls). Notably, dabigatran, an oral direct thrombin inhibitor, demonstrated substantial anticoagulant activity before and after asparaginase therapy, with 180% and 134% prolongation of lag time, respectively, comparable to controls. These ex vivo pharmacodynamics findings support the anticoagulant activity of LMWH and dabigatran. The clinical efficacy of dabigatran in pediatric patients with ALL should be further investigated and confirmed in prospective in vivo studies.

articles.title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been associated with cardiovascular complications including cardiac arrhythmias. However, the relative contributions of respiratory, oxygenation, and sleep architecture indices to composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index remain incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the sequential associations of sleep architecture, nocturnal oxygenation, and respiratory disturbance indices with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index in patients undergoing polysomnography (PSG).

METHODS: Demographic, respiratory, oxygenation and sleep-architecture variables were extracted from PSG records. The primary outcome was a composite PSG-derived rhythm-event count, estimated as round(arrhythmia index × TST_hours) from the PSG-exported arrhythmia index, which was calculated during total sleep time only. Negative binomial regression used an offset of log(TST_hours). Because the outcome demonstrated overdispersion, negative binomial regression with an offset of log(TST hours) was used. Because the original 14-predictor model was over-parameterized for the sample size, a six-predictor model (age, sex, BMI, AHI, T90, and sleep efficiency) was chosen post hoc. This reduced model was not prespecified before the original analysis. Sleep efficiency was retained because it showed a strong signal in the exploratory 14-predictor model. The resulting p-values should therefore be interpreted as optimistic and exploratory. A sequential model-building approach (Model 1: age, sex, BMI, AHI; Model 2: plus T90; Model 3: plus sleep efficiency) was used to document the incremental contribution of each domain. A fully adjusted 14-predictor model was fitted only as a supplementary analysis. Wald 95% CIs and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (2000 resamples) are reported.

RESULTS: Forty-one participants were included (mean age 47.8 ± 13.5 years; median BMI 29.4 kg/m2). Severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30 events/hour) was present in 56.1%. Median arrhythmia index was 3.2 events/hour, with marked overdispersion. In the six-predictor model, only higher sleep efficiency was associated with lower arrhythmia rate (IRR = 0.946 per 1 percentage-point increase, 95% CI 0.921-0.972, p < 0.001; bootstrap 95% CI 0.888-0.984). T90 was associated in the Wald inference (IRR = 1.034, 95% CI 1.006-1.063, p = 0.016) but this association was not robust under bootstrap resampling (95% CI 0.979-1.067). AHI was not associated with arrhythmia rate (IRR = 1.000, 95% CI 0.987-1.014, p = 0.954). Age, sex and BMI were also not significant. A 14-predictor exploratory model had a marginally lower AIC (411.4) but a substantially higher BIC (438.8), consistent with overfitting.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory selected sleep-center cohort, AHI and other respiratory-event indices were not independently associated with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index. Only higher sleep efficiency showed a robust association with lower arrhythmia rate, but this finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect unmeasured confounding. These results require confirmation in larger prospective studies and should not guide clinical risk stratification.

articles.title: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk.

AIM: The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups.

STUDY DESIGN: This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC).

RESULTS: This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons.

CONCLUSIONS: Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

articles.title: Living Liver Donors With Obesity and Metabolic Risk: Review and Guidance on Donor Triage and Care.
articles.abstract: With the increasing prevalence of obesity in the United States, potential living liver donors (LLDs) are similarly impacted. Historically, LLDs with obesity are deemed too high risk for donation due to concern for hepatic steatosis (HS) or post-surgical complications. Evolving data show that obesity is not the absolute indicator of HS and metabolic risk. Instead, distribution of fat in the visceral area as well as body composition drive the risk for metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Prior practice patterns of denial of obese LLDs with metabolic risk require a change in mindset from the liver transplant community with a thoughtful, individualized risk assessment of all LLDs. By losing weight utilizing various dietary and procedural strategies, these "gray zone" LLDs improve their metabolic risk profile and can move into a low risk "green zone", thus expanding the donor pool. Little data exist whether "gray zone" LLDs who succeed in weight loss have long-term consequences to their own health if they regain their weight or the clinical impact on their LDLT recipients. Ethical and financial questions remain as to the LDLT centers' direct responsibility to maintaining donor health. Future studies evaluating interventions and outcomes are needed.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Caring Roles and Fatigue in Intensive Care Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care nurses experience significant levels of fatigue while providing care to their patients. High levels of fatigue may negatively impact nurses' orientation to their caring roles, and this orientation may also be a cause of fatigue.

AIM: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between intensive care nurses' orientations towards their caregiving roles and their fatigue levels.

STUDY DESIGN: The sample of this cross-sectional and correlational study was conducted with nurses working in the intensive care units of a hospital in northwestern Turkey. The 'Personal Information Form', 'Chalder Fatigue Scale' and 'Nursing Care Role Orientation Scale' were used for collecting research data.

RESULTS: In this study, conducted with 110 nurses, the average fatigue score for intensive care nurses was 19.00 ± 7.60, with a physical fatigue score of 13.13 ± 5.20 and a mental fatigue score of 5.87 ± 2.81. The average score of nurses' orientation towards caregiving roles was 82.00 ± 7.68. Female nurses and those working in critical care for less than a year experienced greater fatigue levels (t = 2.131, p = 0.035 and F = 2.858, p = 0.041, respectively). Nurses' orientation towards caregiving roles differed based on their education level and professional experience (p < 0.05). There was a positive correlation between nurses' fatigue scores and orientation towards caregiving roles (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Intensive care nurses were able to effectively adapt to their nursing care roles despite high levels of fatigue and there was a positive relationship between nurses' physical and mental fatigue levels and their adaptation to their care roles. The results of this study, which cannot be generalised to all intensive care nurses because it was conducted in a single hospital, reveal that as nurses' orientation towards their caring roles increases, their fatigue levels also increase.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: For intensive care nurses to effectively care for their patients, they need to be well oriented in their caregiving roles. However, efforts to be well oriented in caregiving can increase nurses' fatigue levels. Considering that reducing physical and mental fatigue will increase the success of the care nurses provide, the importance of providing work environments that will facilitate intensive care nurses' orientation to their caregiving roles in reducing the fatigue levels they experience becomes evident.

articles.title: Psychological Detachment Among Intensive Care Unit Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care unit nurses face sustained workload, vigilance and emotionally demanding care. Psychological detachment during non-work time is an important recovery experience, but evidence in this population remains limited.

AIM: To describe psychological detachment among intensive care unit nurses and identify demographic, departmental psychological support resources availability, social support and burnout dimensions associated with it.

STUDY DESIGN: A single-centre cross-sectional survey. Registered intensive care unit nurses from a tertiary grade A general hospital in eastern China were recruited by convenience sampling between June and July 2025. Participants completed demographic, psychological detachment, burnout and social support questionnaires. Descriptive analyses, univariate comparisons, correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression were performed. The study was reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology checklist.

RESULTS: Of 220 questionnaires submitted, 199 valid responses were analysed (90.45%). The mean psychological detachment score was 11.68 ± 3.85. Mean emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation and personal accomplishment scores were 37.75 ± 8.15, 16.93 ± 4.87 and 25.91 ± 6.25, respectively. Psychological detachment correlated negatively with emotional exhaustion (r = -0.230, p = 0.001) and positively with subjective support (r = 0.175, p = 0.013). Departmental psychological support resources availability (B = 1.674, β = 0.216, p = 0.001), head-nurse position (B = -4.776, β = -0.195, p = 0.004) and emotional exhaustion (B = -0.115, β = -0.243, p < 0.001) were independently associated with psychological detachment.

CONCLUSION: In this single-centre sample of intensive care unit nurses, the reported availability of departmental psychological support resources was associated with higher psychological detachment, whereas head-nurse position and emotional exhaustion were associated with lower psychological detachment.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: These findings suggest that critical care nursing managers may consider departmental psychological support resources availability, nursing position and emotional exhaustion when assessing recovery needs among intensive care unit nurses.

articles.title: Immediate drug hypersensitivity severity is associated with cardiovascular risk.
articles.abstract: Background: Drug hypersensitivity reactions (DHR) exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity. Although established cardiovascular disease is a known risk factor for severe anaphylaxis, the impact of subclinical cardiovascular risk on DHR severity remains poorly understood. Objective: This study investigated the association between Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2 (SCORE2) estimated cardiovascular risk and the severity of immediate-type DHRs. Methods: This retrospective study included 161 patients ages 40-69 years (median age, 49 years; 79.5% women) with immediate-type DHRs. To assess the subclinical risk, those with known cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease were excluded. Reaction severity was graded by using the Brown system, and SCORE2 was calculated by using clinical data from the 12 months preceding the reaction. Results: Reaction severity was graded as mild (35.4%), moderate (34.8%), or severe (29.8%). The median SCORE2 values were significantly higher in the severe group versus the mild group (4.10% versus 2.50%; p = 0.022). The proportion of patients in high or very high SCORE2 risk categories increased stepwise with reaction severity (35.1% in the mild group versus 64.6% in the severe group; p = 0.011). In an univariable ordinal logistic regression, each 1-point increase in SCORE2 percentage was associated with higher odds of greater reaction severity (odds ratio 1.144 [95% confidence interval, 1.041-1.257]; p = 0.005). This association remained significant after adjusting for the culprit drug class (p = 0.008). Conclusion: Higher subclinical cardiovascular risk, as estimated by SCORE2, is significantly associated with increased DHR severity. Analysis of these findings suggests that vascular reserve may modulate the clinical presentation of drug-induced allergic reactions, potentially aiding in clinical risk stratification.

articles.title: Art and storytelling in allergy and immunology.
articles.abstract: Background: Graphic medicine can provide a level of clinical connection when words fail. Objective: The objective was to describe the ways in which art and storytelling have contributed to the landscape of allergy and immunology communication. Methods: Narrative review of allergy/immunology literature that focused on art, artistry, and storytelling in allergy/immunology. Results: Art can provide an emotional connection that can facilitate learning and impact clinical outcomes. Across conditions treated in the allergy/immunology clinic, there is low-certainty evidence of potential improvements in clinical communication related to atopic dermatitis, asthma, and even anaphylaxis. Art can help to address challenges with patient literacy, clinician compassion, and feelings of patient and clinician isolation and stigmatization. Several artistic innovations have promoted medical education. Conclusion: Nonverbal communication is a powerful tool in clinical medicine. Leveraging art as a medium for storytelling and connection can serve as a tool to help deliver the right care, at the right time, every time. Graphic medicine and visual storytelling may complement traditional communication and educational approaches in allergy/immunology. Additional rigorous studies are needed to determine their effects on clinical outcomes and identify the patients and settings most likely to benefit.

articles.title: Adverse childhood experiences and allergic diseases: A scoping review.
articles.abstract: Background: One in seven individuals experience at least four adverse childhood experiences (ACE). These experiences have been associated with poor health outcomes. Objectives: The objective was to map the association between ACEs and asthma, food allergy, allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, urticaria, and mast cell activation syndrome. Methods: Original research that evaluated the association between ACEs and asthma, food allergy, allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, urticaria, or mast cell activation syndrome was selected and abstracted. Review articles and non-peer-reviewed literature were excluded. Sources of evidence included several medical literature databases from inception to April 3, 2026. Each article was reviewed in duplicate at title and abstract, full text, and data extraction, with conflicts resolved by consensus or independent review. Quality assessment was conducted by using a modified assessment tool. Results: After duplicate removal (181 articles), 357 full-text articles were evaluated, with 267 studies excluded. The full text of 90 articles was assessed for eligibility, with 31 studies excluded (1 preprint, 11 wrong outcome, 1 wrong exposure, 17 wrong study design, 1 wrong population). The studies were subject to recall bias and limitations in terms of diagnostic accuracy of the outcome. Of 59 studies selected for inclusion in the review, 57 focused primarily on asthma/lung disease, 6 variably reported on poorly described allergy outcomes, and 2 reported on atopic dermatitis. No studies were identified that explored the association between ACEs and food allergy, urticaria, or mast cell activation syndrome. There is available evidence of an association of ACEs and asthma risk with a potential dose-response effect noted, indicating the possibility of a greater risk with greater ACE exposure. Conclusion: An association between ACEs and asthma is suggested. More research is needed to understand the impact of ACEs on other conditions evaluated by allergist/immunologists.

articles.title: Association of type 2 diabetes, obesity, and metabolic syndrome with patient-reported response to aeroallergen subcutaneous immunotherapy: A real-world cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Background: Although recent studies have examined the impact of metabolic diseases on the immune system, limited data exist on how these conditions and their treatments affect therapeutic approaches for atopic diseases, including subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT). Objective: The objective was to evaluate the association of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, metabolic syndrome, and patient-reported clinical response to SCIT in a real-world setting. Methods: We conducted an observational cross-sectional study of adults receiving SCIT at Montefiore Medical Center, Bronx, New York, between July and September 2024. The SCIT response was assessed by using visual analog scale scores for overall allergic rhinitis (AR) symptoms, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and ocular symptoms, stratified by T2DM, obesity (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m²), and metabolic syndrome. Results: Overall, 95 patients were included, with a mean ± standard deviation age of 51 ± 16 years, the majority being women (71%). Twenty-five patients (26%) had T2DM, 53 (56%) were obese, and 27 (28%) had metabolic syndrome. In the entire cohort, 67% had improvement in overall AR symptoms with SCIT, 72% in nasal congestion, 67% in rhinorrhea, and 63% in ocular symptoms. T2DM was associated with significantly reduced odds of overall symptom improvement (odds ratio [OR] 0.23 [95% confidence interval {CI}, 0.06-0.89]; p = 0.037). The patients with metabolic syndrome had significantly lower odds of improvement in overall AR symptoms (OR 0.21 [95% CI, 0.03-0.61]; p = 0.010), nasal congestion (OR 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.88]; p = 0.036), and rhinorrhea (OR 0.22 [95% CI, 0.06- 0.75]; p = 0.019) while on SCIT. Use of metformin, insulin, sulfonylureas, or glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists did not significantly influence the SCIT response. Conclusion: T2DM and metabolic syndrome may identify a subgroup of patients with lower improvement after SCIT. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether metabolic disorders predict SCIT-associated responsiveness.

articles.title: Residual exacerbation phenotypes during anti-IL-5/IL-5R (IL-5 receptor) therapy in severe eosinophilic asthma.
articles.abstract: Background: Although anti-interleukin (IL) 5/IL-5 receptor therapies effectively reduce the exacerbation burden in severe eosinophilic asthma, some patients continue to experience residual exacerbations despite biologic treatment. The inflammatory characteristics of these exacerbations remain insufficiently defined. Objective: The objective was to evaluate the clinical and inflammatory phenotypes of asthma exacerbations that occur during mepolizumab or benralizumab therapy in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma. Methods: This retrospective real-world study included patients with severe eosinophilic asthma who experienced exacerbations despite anti-IL-5/IL-5 receptor therapy. Exacerbations were classified as eosinophilic, neutrophilic, paucigranulocytic, or mixed granulocytic according to peripheral blood eosinophil and neutrophil counts. Clinical characteristics, inflammatory phenotypes, pulmonary function parameters, eosinophil levels, and annual exacerbation frequencies were evaluated. Results: Forty-two patients who experienced 63 exacerbations during biologic therapy were included. The median age was 48.5 years, and 66.7% of the patients were women. The annual exacerbation frequency significantly decreased after biologic treatment initiation in both treatment groups. Among the patients who completed the first treatment year, 66.7% of the patients treated with benralizumab and 55.1% of the patients treated with mepolizumab remained exacerbation-free. No significant differences were observed between biologic agents with regard to infectious exacerbation frequency or inflammatory exacerbation phenotypes. Paucigranulocytic exacerbations represented the most common phenotype in both treatment groups, whereas mixed granulocytic exacerbations were rare. Pulmonary function parameters and eosinophil levels during exacerbations were comparable between the biologic agents. Conclusion: Residual exacerbations that occurred during anti-IL-5/IL-5 receptor therapy demonstrated heterogeneous inflammatory phenotypes rather than a uniformly eosinophilic pattern. The predominance of paucigranulocytic exacerbations suggests that mechanisms beyond persistent eosinophilic inflammation may contribute to residual exacerbations during biologic therapy in severe eosinophilic asthma.

articles.title: Role of the SGK1/GSK-3β/β-Catenin Signaling Pathway in Thalamic Hemorrhage-Induced Central Post-Stroke Pain in Mice.
articles.abstract: Central post-stroke pain (CPSP) is a chronic neuropathic pain condition associated with thalamic injury and frequently accompanied by affective disturbances. Although SGK1 has been implicated in neuroinflammation and behavioral regulation, its role and underlying mechanisms in CPSP remain unclear. In this study, a thalamic hemorrhage mouse model was established by collagenase injection to investigate the contribution of SGK1 to CPSP-like phenotypes. Behavioral assessments were performed to evaluate pain hypersensitivity, cold allodynia, and anxiety-like behaviors. Pharmacological inhibition and viral-mediated overexpression of SGK1 were used to examine its effects on pathological injury, inflammatory responses, and the GSK-3β/β-catenin signaling pathway. Thalamic hemorrhage induced persistent mechanical allodynia, cold hypersensitivity, and anxiety-like behaviors. SGK1 expression was upregulated in microglia and astrocytes, peaked at day 7, and remained elevated until day 28 after hemorrhage. SGK1 inhibition alleviated pain-related behaviors, pathological damage, and neuroinflammation, whereas SGK1 overexpression produced opposite effects. Mechanistically, SGK1 modulation was associated with changes in GSK-3β Ser9 phosphorylation, β-catenin accumulation, and inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings identify SGK1 as a critical regulator of CPSP progression and suggest that targeting the SGK1/GSK-3β/β-catenin signaling axis may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for post-stroke pain.

articles.title: Copper-Mediated Radiofluorination of the Excitatory Amino Acid Transporter 2 (EAAT2)-Targeted PET Tracer [18F]RP-115: Alternate Synthetic Method.
articles.abstract: Excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2) is a key regulator of extracellular glutamate in the central nervous system. Dysregulated EAAT2 is implicated in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), highlighting EAAT2 as a potential target for PET imaging. We previously reported a multistep radiosynthesis of [18F]RP-115, a CNS-permeable prodrug that undergoes esterase-mediated hydrolysis in the CNS to yield the active EAAT2-binding carboxylate. Motivated by recent advances in copper-mediated radiofluorination (CMRF), we sought to develop a more efficient late-stage radiosynthesis of [18F]RP-115. A two-step radiosynthesis of [18F]RP-115 using CMRF provided [18F]RP-115 in high radiochemical yield (52.8% ± 2.1 %, decay-corrected from starting [18F]fluoride ion, n = 4), high molar activity (355 ± 61 GBq/μmol), and high radiochemical purity (> 99%) with a total synthesis time of 70 min. Chiral HPLC analysis demonstrated that the configuration of the aspartic acid residue remained intact without racemization during both the CMRF and trifluoroacetic acid mediated deprotection. We developed an efficient radiosynthesis of [18F]RP-115 via CMRF, achieving high radiochemical yield and molar activity. This efficient synthesis may serve as a basis for the future implementation of a CMRF-based automated radiosynthesis of [18F]RP-115.

articles.title: PSMA Theranostics for Prostate Cancer: Evidence, Pitfalls, and Implementation in Japan.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a Type II transmembrane glycoprotein markedly overexpressed on prostate cancer cells, enabling a single molecular target to support both positron emission tomography (PET) imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy. Over the past decade, PSMA-PET/CT has been incorporated into international guidelines for primary staging of high-risk prostate cancer and for biochemical recurrence, with the landmark proPSMA trial establishing its diagnostic superiority over conventional imaging; whether PSMA-PET-guided management improves long-term oncologic outcomes, however, remains an open question addressable only by prospective PSMA-specific trials. On the therapeutic side, 177Lu-PSMA-617 has become a standard treatment option for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) after androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) and taxane chemotherapy, and is moving into earlier lines of disease. Alpha-emitting and next-generation ligands, together with quantitative whole-body imaging and artificial intelligence, are redefining both patient selection and response assessment, although randomized evidence for many of these approaches remains limited. In Japan, the concurrent 2025 approval of 177Lu-vipivotide tetraxetan and its companion PSMA diagnostic has initiated a national roll-out that will depend on a hub-and-spoke framework of regional PSMA-PET centers and therapy spokes, a prepared nuclear medicine workforce, and domestic registries to refine Japanese-specific evidence. This review summarizes the current clinical evidence for PSMA-PET/CT and 177Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy, highlights interpretive and implementation pitfalls, and outlines practical priorities for the Japanese clinical and academic community.

articles.title: When Two Wood Units Matter: From Measurement Bias to Clinical Reclassification in Pediatric Pulmonary Hypertension.

Author Response to "Comment on 'Association of Body Mass Index With SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Inflammatory Arthritis Patients Receiving Biologic Therapy: Singapore National Biologics Register Findings'".
"Life and Lower Limb Threatening Condition" Clinical Features, Management and Outcomes of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Complicated by Gas Gangrene: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common complication of diabetes in low- and middle-income countries and may be complicated by gas gangrene (GG), a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection. This prospective study assessed whether GG can be diagnosed clinically in low-resource primary care and explored factors associated with wound-healing outcomes in DFU complicated by GG. From December 2021 to June 2025, consecutive patients with diabetic foot infection and clinically active GG were enrolled. Data included demographics, ulcer history and examination, SINBAD classification, GG signs, sepsis status, comorbidities, management, and outcomes. All participants had classical clinical features of GG and were admitted for urgent surgical treatment. Ninety-nine patients (58 male) with classical GG were admitted for urgent surgery. Initial amputation was required in 18% (major 12%, minor 6%). Ten patients were lost to follow-up; that included six who died from foot-ulcer-related causes. Of 89 followed, 30 (33.7%) healed in 225.5 ± 126.9 days, while 59 remained unhealed after 146.1 ± 175.4 days; major amputations during treatment were more frequent in the healed group. Having a previous history of ulcer showed to increase the time to heal by 136 days. A one-day increase in treatment duration was associated with a 1% decrease in both the chance of healing or risk of amputation. Early diagnosis, aggressive medical and surgical intervention are the keys to decreasing morbidity and mortality of diabetic patients with gas gangrene; and remain the mainstay treatment of this dangerous condition globally. Patient's with previous ulcer history were found to need longer time to heal. Increasing treatment duration seems to be a double-edged sword, as while it is associated with reduced risk of amputation, it also decreases the chance of ulcer healing.

articles.title: Combined Use of Adhesive Mesh Closure and Closed-Incision Negative Pressure Therapy for High-Risk Surgical Wounds: A Proof-Of-Concept Study.
articles.abstract: Surgical wound complications remain a major challenge, particularly in high-risk patients. Closed-incision negative pressure wound therapy (ciNPWT) and adhesive mesh closure systems have shown benefits independently, but their combined use has not been previously evaluated. This single-centre prospective proof-of-concept study included consecutive patients at extremely high risk of wound complications undergoing complex surgical procedures. All patients were treated with adhesive mesh closure (Dermabond Prineo) and ciNPWT (PICO) using a standardized protocol. Outcomes were compared with a historical cohort treated with conventional skin closure. Primary outcomes were wound healing and surgical site complications; secondary outcomes included persistent drainage, delayed healing, readmissions and duration of therapy. Seventeen surgical procedures (16 patients) were included in the prospective cohort and 39 in the historical cohort. The combined strategy achieved consistent wound healing without device-related or allergic complications. Compared with controls, no significant difference was observed for the composite outcome of surgical site complications (17.6% vs. 23.1%), although lower rates were observed for persistent drainage (0 vs. 23.1%, p = 0.045), delayed healing (5.9% vs. 20.5%) and readmissions (0 vs. 20.5%); only persistent drainage reached statistical significance. ciNPWT duration was shorter (12.3 vs. 17.3 days; p = 0.006). This combined approach appears feasible and safe in a highly selected cohort of high-risk patients, with preliminary findings suggesting potential reductions in wound-related complications.

articles.title: Clinical, safety, and patient-reported outcomes associated with second-line and later therapies in primary biliary cholangitis: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a rare, chronic, cholestatic disease that can result in cirrhosis, liver failure, and death. While biochemical markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and total bilirubin (TB) measure disease activity and progression, definitions of biochemical response vary. This systematic literature review (SLR) identified clinical studies for investigational and approved treatments in patients with PBC with inadequate response or intolerance to ursodeoxycholic acid requiring second-line (2L) or later (2L+) therapies.

METHODS: Electronic databases were searched on August 7, 2025 (MEDLINE; Embase) or September 30, 2025 (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews; CENTRAL), and conference proceedings (2021-2025), bibliographies, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched on August 15, 2025, following a pre-specified protocol (PROSPERO ID: CRD42023382262). Interventional and observational studies in the 2L/2L+ setting were prioritized for inclusion, and randomized controlled trials for extraction.

RESULTS: A total of 149 publications on 44 unique studies were included. Phase III trials evaluated elafibranor, seladelpar, budenoside, bezafibrate, and obeticholic acid. Various composite biochemical response endpoints were reported across 34% of studies, most frequently the POISE criteria (18%). Biochemical markers were assessed frequently (ALP: 89%; TB: 71%); however, upper limits of normal and response thresholds varied substantially. Response rates in placebo-controlled trials favored active treatment, although placebo responses were highly variable. Non-invasive fibrosis measures were reported in 16% of studies and showed small short-term changes. Patient-reported outcomes assessed pruritus (52%) and fatigue (32%) using a variety of scales.

CONCLUSION: The evidence base for 2L/2L+ PBC therapies is extensive but heterogeneous in study designs, patient populations, and treatment assessment scales and outcome definitions, limiting cross-trial comparisons. This SLR provides a robust foundation for contextualizing study outcomes within the broader landscape and supporting clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Sotagliflozin improves mitral regurgitation symptoms in rats.
Social and clinical determinants of liver transplant evaluation in hepatocellular carcinoma: A multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation (LT) is curative for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) but requires timely referral. Comprehensive data on factors impacting LT referral and outcomes for HCC are limited. We evaluated social, system, and clinical factors associated with listing, LT, mortality, HCC stage at referral, and time from HCC diagnosis to referral.

METHODS: The California Liver Network is a consortium of 6 LT centers comprising >75% of adult LTs in California. Demographic, clinical, psychosocial, and social determinants of health and outcome data were collected for adults referred for LT. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 9987 adults referred, 1573 (15.7%) had HCC. Median age was 63.3 years; 73% males, 40% Hispanic, and 26.1% Medicaid insurance. Median MELD was 12.7 (IQR 8-16), and median time from HCC diagnosis to LT referral was 124 days (IQR 32-410). In all, 10% were T1 and 70.5% were T2 at referral. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (OR 0.99), HCC stage, Medicaid insurance (OR 0.55), LT site, and marital status (OR 1.90) were associated with listing. Transplantation was associated with HCC stage (OR 0.42) and LT site. Mortality was associated with MELD (OR 1.02), hypertension (OR 1.44), dialysis (OR 2.48), hepatic encephalopathy (OR 1.54), and portal vein thrombosis (OR 1.44). Referral at more advanced HCC stage was associated with male sex (OR 1.55), AFP (OR 1.01), Medicaid insurance (OR 1.40), primary language (OR 0.70), and prior HCC treatment type. Longer time to referral was associated with HCV/alcohol liver disease and prior HCC treatment type.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter study of adults with HCC, Medicaid insurance, LT site, HCC treatment history, and psychosocial factors were key determinants of HCC care cascade progression, identifying targets to improve LT access.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Screening for Detection of Low Ejection Fraction in Routine Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies.

CONCLUSION: AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.

articles.title: Liquid Compared to Solid Oral Formulations of the Thyroid Hormone Receptor Agonist Elunetirom Under Fasted and Fed Conditions in Healthy Participants.
articles.abstract: Elunetirom (ABX-002) is a brain-targeted, oral prodrug being developed for the adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder and bipolar depression. The active moiety, LL-340001, is a thyroid hormone receptor agonist with modest selectivity for beta over alpha thyroid hormone receptors. Upon entering the brain, the intended site of action, elunetirom is hydrolyzed by fatty acid amide hydrolase to LL-340001. In this 3-way randomized, crossover, bioequivalence study, the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety of an oral liquid formulation used in early clinical development were compared with those of an oral solid formulation intended for later-stage development and potential commercialization, under fasted and fed conditions. Healthy adult participants received single doses of elunetirom (45 μg) as a liquid formulation under fasted conditions and as a solid formulation under fasted conditions and 30 min after consumption of a high-fat meal. Administration of the solid formulation under fasted conditions resulted in elunetirom and LL-340001 exposures similar to those observed with the liquid formulation and is therefore considered to have comparative bioavailability. Food intake increased elunetirom total exposure (AUC) compared with the fasted state but did not affect maximum exposure (Cmax). In contrast, administration with food reduced LL-340001 Cmax compared with the fasted state but did not affect AUC. Food intake delayed the time to reach Cmax (Tmax) for both elunetirom and LL-340001. Elunetirom, administered orally as a liquid and as a solid formulation, was safe and well tolerated under fed and fasted conditions.

articles.title: Phase 1 Study of Safety and PK With A Combination of Omeprazole and Trimetazidine for Fatty Acid Oxidation Inhibition in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors.
articles.abstract: Fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a metabolic vulnerability in cancer cells, making pharmacologic FAO inhibition a promising therapeutic strategy. This Phase I, open-label, 3 + 3 dose-escalation study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of two oral FAO inhibitors-omeprazole (KN510), a carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase inhibitor, and trimetazidine (KN713), an acetyl-CoA acyltransferase inhibitor-given once daily in combination to patients with advanced solid tumors. Twelve patients were enrolled across four dose cohorts (omeprazole and trimetazidine, each 60-120 mg/day). The maximum tolerated dose was not reached; the recommended Phase 2 dose was set at 120 mg once daily for each agent. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with most adverse events Grade 1-2; the most common were flu-like symptoms (25.0%), constipation (16.7%), nausea (16.7%), and dizziness (16.7%). Omeprazole showed time-dependent pharmacokinetics consistent with auto-inhibition of its own metabolism, whereas trimetazidine showed dose-proportional pharmacokinetics across the studied range. The best response was stable disease in five patients (disease control rate 41.7%). Median progression-free survival was 1.66 months (95% CI, 1.18-3.55) and median overall survival was 9.13 months (95% CI, 3.29-not reached). Dual pharmacologic FAO inhibition with oral omeprazole and trimetazidine was feasible and well tolerated, supporting the mechanistic rationale for combination dosing. Disease stabilization observed in this heavily pretreated population warrants further clinical evaluation, particularly in combination with standard chemotherapy regimens. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06012708; registered August 25, 2023.

articles.title: Adaptive immune plasticity in MASH: Functional states, pathological consequences, and regulatory mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease driven by both metabolic stress and immune dysregulation. A growing body of evidence suggests that adaptive immune cells exhibit significant functional plasticity during the progression and resolution of MASH. CD8+ T cells can assume various states, including pathogenic cytotoxicity, functional exhaustion, and tissue repair; CD4+ T cells exhibit enhanced Th1/Th17 programming, reduced Treg stability, and a functional shift toward Th17/Treg; and B cells undergo remodeling between regulatory, pro-inflammatory, and antibody-effect states. These functional states determine disease outcomes through distinct effector mechanisms. The cytotoxicity and inflammatory factors of pathogenic T cells promote hepatocyte damage, metabolic dysregulation, and hepatocyte stellate cell activation, while B-cell antigen presentation, cytokine, and antibody responses further amplify inflammation and fibrosis; conversely, Tregs, Bregs, and tissue-resident CD8+ T cells with reparative functions can limit inflammation or promote the resolution of fibrosis. Adaptive immune plasticity is, in turn, continuously shaped by the hepatic metabolic environment, in which glycolipid and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming determine the metabolic basis of different functional states, while metabolite-driven epigenetic remodeling stabilizes corresponding transcriptional programs. Microbiome components and metabolic signals originating from the gut-liver axis further regulate the state of T and B cells within the liver. Consequently, the functional states of adaptive immune cells, their pathological effects, and their metabolic regulation collectively constitute a critical immunometabolic network linking metabolic dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and the progression of fibrosis, providing a unified mechanistic framework for understanding the sustained progression of MASH and tissue repair.

articles.title: Hippocampal Subfield Volumes and Spatial Memory Performance in Older Adults At-Risk for Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Older adults at risk for type 2 diabetes (T2D) are more likely to experience accelerated cognitive aging and neurodegeneration due to impaired metabolism in the hippocampus. However, the precise relationship between T2D risk factors, brain volumes (i.e., gray matter, white matter, hippocampus subfields), and hippocampus-dependent functions (i.e., spatial pattern separation, a component of spatial memory) remains unexplored. To investigate these relationships in this cross-sectional study, 60 older adults at risk for T2D (e.g., high BMI or elevated A1c levels) completed a touchscreen-based spatial pattern separation behavioral task-the Trial-Unique delayed Nonmatching-to-Location (TUNL) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). HippUnfold was utilized to segment the hippocampus from high-resolution, T1-weighted images. We found positive correlations between A1c levels and volumes of the dentate gyrus (DG) and cornu ammonis (CA) 2, indicating that higher A1c was associated with larger volumes of hippocampal subregions. Additionally, TUNL accuracy was correlated with gray matter and distinct hippocampus subfield volumes (i.e., subiculum, CA1, and CA4), with larger volumes associated with better spatial memory performance. Understanding early structural changes in T2D risk allows us to further characterize changes in brain health associated with metabolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Assessment of Risks, Efficiency, Costs, and Gain of Natural Hazard (Catastrophe) Consequences Prevention Based on Geophysical Monitoring.
articles.journal: Risk analysis : an official publication of the Society for Risk Analysis
articles.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to quantitatively estimate the efficiency of forecasting hazards and catastrophic processes induced by high-energy terrestrial sources, based on an integrated monitoring of the state of geophysical processes. Using methods of mathematical statistics and detection theory, relations have been obtained that can be used to calculate the coefficients of the efficiency of warning of catastrophes and the costs associated with a predicted event. The hazard (catastrophe) prevention efficiency coefficient has been shown to be dependent only on the conditional probability of missing a hazard. The relative cost parameter is a function of five parameters: a priori probability of the unwanted event, a conditional false alarm probability, a conditional missed detect probability, relative costs in the case of false alarm probability, and costs to minimize consequences of the hazardous event in case it has been accurately forecast. The gain from organizing geophysical monitoring has been estimated for a few dangers and catastrophes of terrestrial nature. The gain has been shown to be significant in many cases. An energy-based classification of the most important natural sources of hazards and catastrophes, as well as their consequences, is proposed or improved.

articles.title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention.

AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool.

RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

articles.title: Network Analysis of Factors Influencing ICU Patient Transfer Readiness: A Social-Ecological Model Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ICU transfer readiness is a multidimensional state influenced by informational, functional, emotional and support-related needs. Network analysis can clarify how readiness indicators and emotional distress co-occur as a system, rather than as independent factors.

AIMS: To (1) model conditional associations among ICU transfer-readiness indicators and anxiety/depressive symptoms and (2) identify highly connected and highly predictable targets that may be prioritised in transitional-care interventions.

STUDY DESIGN: Transfer readiness was measured using the ICU Transfer Readiness Scale (15 items; 0-10) and emotional distress using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS; 14 items; 0-3). A regularised mixed graphical model (MGM) was estimated to accommodate mixed/ordinal data. Edge-weight accuracy, centrality robustness and node predictability (R2) were assessed using bootstrap procedures. Age and gender were included as background variables.

RESULTS: A total of 276 ICU patients were included in the analysis. The estimated network showed a clear modular structure: transfer-readiness indicators clustered into personal status, disease knowledge, coping after transition and expected-support domains; HADS symptoms clustered into anxiety and depression domains. Within transfer readiness, the strongest association occurred between two expected-support indicators, suggesting perceived support is tightly interlinked. Within HADS, multiple strong within-subscale connections were observed for both anxiety and depression symptoms. Node predictability ranged from 0.224 to 0.633 (mean 0.434), with the highest predictability for key readiness indicators in the knowledge/coping domains (R2 ≈0.63). Bootstrap analyses supported acceptable stability of the main edge and centrality patterns. Demographic nodes showed comparatively weaker and more cautious-to-interpret associations.

CONCLUSIONS: ICU transfer readiness and emotional symptoms form structured conditional interdependencies, indicating readiness should be conceptualised and addressed as a connected system rather than isolated determinants.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Transitional-care strategies may be strengthened by prioritising highly connected/predictable readiness targets-particularly expected support and key knowledge/coping indicators-while concurrently screening for and addressing anxiety/depressive symptoms to improve transfer preparation and early post-transfer adjustment.

articles.title: Two-Stage Estimation for Causal Inference Involving Semi-Continuous Exposures.
articles.abstract: Methods for causal inference are well developed for binary and continuous exposures, but in many settings, the exposure has a substantial mass at zero-such exposures are called semi-continuous. We propose a general causal framework for such semi-continuous exposures, together with a two-stage estimation strategy. A two-part propensity structure is introduced for the semi-continuous exposure, with one component for exposure status (exposed vs unexposed) and another for the exposure level among those exposed, and incorporates both into a marginal structural model that disentangles the effects of exposure status and dose. The two-stage procedure sequentially targets the causal dose-response among exposed individuals and the causal effect of exposure status at a reference dose, allowing flexibility in the choice of propensity score methods in the second stage. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the resulting estimators, and characterize their limiting values under misspecification of the propensity score models. Simulation studies evaluate finite sample performance and robustness, and an application to a study of prenatal alcohol exposure and child cognition demonstrates how the proposed methods can be used to address a range of scientific questions about both exposure status and exposure intensity.

articles.title: The role of laparoscopic and robotic surgery in epithelial ovarian cancer: A consensus statement of the Taiwan Association of Minimally Invasive Gynecology (TAMIG).
authors: Board of Directors and consultants of the Taiwan Association of Minimally Invasive Gynecology (TAMIG)

articles.title: A rare cause of postpartum hemoperitoneum: Uterine laceration secondary to sustained transabdominal uterine massage following vaginal delivery: A case report.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a case of postpartum hemoperitoneum caused by uterine laceration in an unscarred uterus, likely secondary to sustained transabdominal uterine massage.

CASE REPORT: We report a case of postpartum hemorrhage resulting from a partial myometrial and serosal laceration in an unscarred uterus following vaginal delivery. Initial uterine atony was managed with uterotonics and transabdominal massage. However, the patient subsequently developed hypovolemic shock and abdominal tenderness. Bedside ultrasonography revealed hemoperitoneum, and exploratory laparotomy confirmed a superficial uterine laceration, likely related to sustained uterine massage.

CONCLUSION: Uterine massage rarely causes myometrium injury and should be the first-line management approach for postpartum hemorrhage. Early diagnosis and timely intervention for myometrium laceration caused by uterine massage allowed for successful surgical repair, thereby avoiding irreversible injury.

articles.title: Cutaneous clues: Malignant acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms as first signs of recurrent endometrial carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: 'Tripe palm' is a rare cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by velvety thickening of the palms with a ridged or rugose appearance. The condition, either on its own or in combination with acanthosis nigricans, is strongly associated with internal malignancies, particularly gastric and lung cancers. Reports linking malignant acanthosis nigricans to endometrial cancer are scarce. Even more uncommon is its presentation as an initial sign of recurrent disease.

CASE REPORT: We report a rare case of acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms in a 73-year-old woman who had completed treatment for stage IB endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma and remained disease-free for six years. She was referred by a dermatologist for evaluation of potential underlying malignancy. Chest CT, panendoscopy, and colonoscopy showed no significant findings. However, a PET/CT scan revealed a suspicious lymph node metastasis in the portocaval region. Laparoscopic excision of the retroperitoneal lymph nodes was performed, and pathological examination confirmed metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma with microscopic features consistent with the original endometrial carcinoma.

CONCLUSION: Acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms are rarely linked to endometrial cancer, especially as indicators of recurrence. Gynecologic oncologists should recognize these cutaneous clues during patient surveillance, even if the patient has been disease-free for many years following treatment.

articles.title: Associations of sFlt-1 and PlGF levels with hematologic and biochemical parameters in normotensive pregnant women.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by hypertension accompanied by hematologic and biochemical changes. In PE, these changes are linked to soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and placental growth factor (PlGF), but their relationships during normotensive pregnancy remain unclear. We aimed to investigate the associations of sFlt-1 and PlGF with routine hematologic and biochemical parameters in normotensive pregnancy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 780 pregnant women who did not develop PE or superimposed PE by measuring sFlt-1 and PlGF at 18 + 0-21 + 6 weeks of gestation with same-day routine hematology/biochemistry results.

RESULTS: Spearman's rank correlations showed weak but statistically significant associations between sFlt-1 and aspartate aminotransferase (AST; ρ = 0.19), alanine aminotransferase (ALT; ρ = 0.16), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH; ρ = 0.15). In multivariable analyses, these associations remained independent of maternal characteristics.

CONCLUSION: Even within physiologic ranges, sFlt-1 may reflect subclinical hepatic or hemolysis-related responses, consistent with its pathogenic role in PE.

articles.title: Metabolic markers for risk stratification of diabetic ketoacidosis and perinatal mortality in pregestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify metabolic markers associated with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in pregnant women with pregestational diabetes mellitus (PDM) and to evaluate their utility in risk stratification and the prediction of perinatal mortality.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2000 to 2022, including singleton pregnancies in women with PDM. Maternal metabolic parameters such as glucose levels, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), lipid profiles (high-density lipoprotein [HDL] and low-density lipoprotein [LDL]), arterial pH, electrolytes, and anion gap were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and logistic regression models were used to identify metabolic predictors of DKA and perinatal mortality.

RESULTS: Among 219 pregnant women with PDM, 21 (9.6%) developed DKA. Affected women had significantly higher glucose levels (395.33 vs. 126.91 mg/dL, P < 0.001), higher HbA1c (8.45% vs. 6.73%, P = 0.001), lower HDL (38.71 vs. 57.96 mg/dL, P < 0.001), and higher LDL (152.86 vs. 119.25 mg/dL, P = 0.012) compared with those without DKA. Perinatal mortality occurred in 6 cases (28.6%) and was associated with metabolic acidosis, including lower arterial pH (7.07 vs. 7.20, P = 0.030), lower bicarbonate (3.90 vs. 9.96 mEq/L, P = 0.001), and a wider anion gap (22.50 vs. 15.17 mEq/L, P = 0.014). Additionally, higher HbA1c (10.00% vs. 7.83%, P = 0.026) and hyperkalemia (5.77 vs. 4.23 mEq/L, P = 0.022) were associated with perinatal mortality. The ROC analyses demonstrated strong predictive value for DKA (area under the ROC curve [AUC] = 0.99) and perinatal mortality (AUC = 0.98) using combined metabolic markers. The logistic regression analyses identified higher HbA1c (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13-4.75), lower HDL (aOR 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.96), and higher glucose (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.05) as independent predictors of DKA. Lower bicarbonate (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.96) was independently associated with an increased risk of perinatal mortality. The Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated a significant association between bicarbonate <6.50 mEq/L and increased perinatal mortality (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Key metabolic markers can aid with risk stratification for DKA and perinatal mortality in women with PDM, supporting early identification and guiding targeted clinical interventions.

articles.title: Changes in postpartum glucose testing behaviors after the implementation of a gestational diabetes mellitus screening policy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: On July 1, 2021, Taiwan implemented a national policy incorporating gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) screening into routine prenatal care and adopted a standardized 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). This initiative aimed to normalize prenatal GDM screening; however, its impact on postpartum glucose testing behaviors remains uncertain. We assessed changes in postpartum glucose testing after policy implementation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database. We compared maternal records from 1.5 years before policy implementation (January 1, 2020-June 30, 2021) with those from 1.5 years after implementation (July 1, 2021-December 31, 2022). Outcomes included postpartum glucose testing, timing of testing, and follow-up specialty.

RESULTS: After policy implementation, the proportion of women who received postpartum glucose testing within 3 months of delivery increased by 12.10 percentage points. Testing shifted toward the first 3 months postpartum (overall χ2 (df = 2) = 53.83; p < 0.0001). Follow-up in obstetrics and gynecology increased by 3.02 percentage points, and follow-up in endocrinology increased by 1.74 percentage points (both p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: After GDM screening was incorporated into routine prenatal care, postpartum glucose testing occurred earlier and became more concentrated, with postpartum follow-up more frequently occurring in obstetrics and gynecology and endocrinology. Even in the absence of a specific intervention targeting postpartum glucose testing, changes in postpartum testing behavior were observed, suggesting a spillover effect from the integration of GDM screening into routine prenatal care.

articles.title: A pilot study of electromagnetic therapy versus biofeedback-based pelvic floor muscle training for pelvic organ prolapse: A mixed-methods approach.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This pilot study aimed to: (1) evaluate the effects of high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) therapy on pelvic organ prolapse (POP) symptoms and pelvic floor function; (2) compare outcomes across HIFEM, pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) with biofeedback and/or electrostimulation, and usual care; and (3) explore participant acceptability of the interventions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mixed-methods pilot study was conducted in women aged >20 years with stage I-III POP. Participants were randomized to HIFEM, PFMT, or usual care. The HIFEM group underwent twice-weekly 28-min sessions for eight weeks using a non-invasive electromagnetic chair. PFMT consisted of supervised sessions incorporating biofeedback and/or electrostimulation. Usual care included lifestyle advice. Outcomes were assessed using validated questionnaires for POP symptoms and pelvic floor distress, digital palpation, and transperineal ultrasound.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight women completed the study (HIFEM, n = 10; PFMT, n = 9; usual care, n = 9). Compared with usual care, HIFEM significantly improved pelvic floor muscle endurance (p = 0.001), whereas PFMT significantly improved muscle strength (p = 0.034), endurance (p = 0.023), and rapid contractions (p = 0.019). Only HIFEM demonstrated significant improvements in POP symptom severity (p = 0.015) and pelvic floor distress (p = 0.041). No serious adverse events were reported. Participant satisfaction was highest in the HIFEM group (100%). Qualitative analysis supported intervention acceptability, with participants reporting increased pelvic floor awareness, improved symptom control, and enhanced psychological well-being.

CONCLUSIONS: Both HIFEM and PFMT with biofeedback appear to be safe, acceptable, and effective non-surgical treatment options for women with POP. Although no significant differences were observed between the two interventions, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of the small sample size. Larger studies are needed to confirm comparative efficacy and inform clinical implementation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06532292. URL OF THE REGISTRATION SITE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06532292?cond=Pelvic%20Organ%20Prolapse&intr=high-intensity&rank=1.

articles.title: Risk factors for adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies with early- and late-onset extreme fetal growth restriction, estimated fetal weight ≤ 1st centile: A multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the risk factors associated with adverse perinatal outcome in early-onset (<32 weeks) and late-onset (≥32 weeks) extreme fetal growth restriction (FGR), defined as estimated fetal weight (EFW) ≤ 1st centile.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective cohort study was performed on pregnancies complicated by early- and late-onset extreme FGR within a week of delivery between 2018 and 2021. Doppler indices were converted as percentile adjusted for gestational age (GA). Composite adverse perinatal outcome (APO) was defined as fetal or neonatal death or at least one of the after severe perinatal morbidities: respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, intraventricular hemorrhage, proven sepsis or necrotizing enterocolitis. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Overall, 261 cases were included: 135 cases of early- and 126 cases of late-onset extreme FGR. The perinatal mortality rate was 7.4% in early- and 1.6% in late-onset extreme FGR. Composite APO was 54.1% and 12.7% in the early- and late-onset extreme FGR groups, respectively. The risk factors for the composite APO were GA at delivery (aOR 0.52, 95% CI 0.36-0.74), the presence of non-reassuring cardiotocography (aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.12-0.95), and EFW within 1 week before delivery (aOR 1.003, 95% CI 1.000-1.005) in early-, and GA at delivery (aOR 0.79, 95% CI 0.64-0.98) and diabetes during pregnancy (aOR 1.87, 95% CI 1.47-9.58) in late-onset extreme FGR.

CONCLUSIONS: Composite APO in early- and late-onset extreme FGR were comparable. GA at delivery may be the significant risk factor for the composite APO in early- and late-onset extreme FGR.

articles.title: Myo-inositol in placental metabolism and function: Implications for gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is a prevalent metabolic disorder affecting approximately 14% of pregnancies worldwide, with increasing incidence linked to rising obesity rates among women of reproductive age. GDM significantly impacts placental structure and function, leading to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Inositols, particularly myo-inositol (myo-Ins), play important roles in cellular signaling, glucose homeostasis, and insulin sensitivity, making them relevant to GDM pathophysiology. Myo-Ins, the most abundant inositol stereoisomer, is obtained through dietary intake and biosynthesis, with its metabolism intricately linked to insulin signaling. This review explores the role of myo-Ins in placental metabolism and its potential implications for GDM management.
