We discuss the potential mechanisms by which myo-Ins might influence glucose homeostasis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and lipid metabolism in the placenta, highlighting potential protective effects against GDM-induced placental dysfunction. Some clinical evidence suggests that myo-Ins supplementation may reduce the risk of GDM, improve insulin sensitivity, and mitigate adverse pregnancy outcomes. However, the timing, dosage, and specific placental effects require further investigation to optimize therapeutic efficacy. This review underscores the potential of myo-Ins as an adjunctive therapy for GDM, emphasizing the need for further research to elucidate mechanisms of action and long-term benefits for maternal and fetal health.

articles.title: The Effects of Mind-Body Exercise on Cognitive Function and Peripheral Blood BDNF in Elderly People With Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of mind-body exercise (MBE) on cognitive function and peripheral blood brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) levels in older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and to explore its intervention effects and potential biological mechanisms.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating various MBE interventions, including Tai Chi, Baduanjin, yoga, and mindfulness/meditation, in older adults with MCI. The primary outcomes included cognitive function (global cognitive function, verbal fluency, executive function, episodic memory, short-term memory, working memory, and processing speed and attention) and peripheral blood BDNF levels. Effect sizes were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and pooled using fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses and funnel plots were used to assess robustness and publication bias.

RESULTS: Seventeen randomized controlled trials involving 1251 participants were included. MBE significantly improved global cognitive function (SMD = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.55 to 1.09, p < 0.001), verbal fluency (SMD = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.25 to 0.91, p = 0.001), executive function (SMD = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.12 to 0.67, p = 0.005), episodic memory (SMD = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.26 to 0.92, p < 0.001), and short-term memory (SMD = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.27 to 0.81, p < 0.001) in older adults with MCI. Working memory showed a potential improvement, but the result was not robust in sensitivity analysis. No significant effects were observed for processing speed/attention (SMD = 0.12; 95% CI: -0.04 to 0.28; p = 0.131) or peripheral blood BDNF (SMD = 0.89; 95% CI: -0.12 to 1.89; p = 0.085). Subgroup analyses suggested greater benefits for Tai Chi-based interventions and for verbal fluency when intervention duration exceeded 12 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Mind-body exercise is beneficial for improving global cognitive function, verbal fluency, executive function, episodic memory, and short-term memory in older adults with MCI; however, evidence remains insufficient regarding its effects on processing speed and attention and peripheral blood BDNF levels. Tai Chi-based mind-body exercise and longer intervention durations may yield greater benefits. These findings support the use of mind-body exercise as an important adjunctive strategy for comprehensive intervention in older adults with MCI and provide a reference for optimizing exercise-based intervention programs in clinical and practical settings.

articles.title: The present and future of HIV and viral hepatitis co-infection.
articles.abstract: HIV and hepatitis virus co-infection remains a major global health challenge, driven by shared transmission routes, populations with overlapping modes of acquisition, and potentially compounded disease progression. Co-infections of HIV and hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) remain prevalent, particularly among people who live in endemic areas, key populations, people who inject drugs, men who have sex with men, and migrants from endemic regions. Antiretroviral therapy is shifting towards regimens without HBV activity, increasing the risk for HBV infection or reactivation in some individuals. Although direct-acting antivirals have reduced active HCV infection considerably in many high-income settings, residual disease burden, reinfections, and inequitable access to treatment persist. Hepatitis delta virus continues to represent a severe but underdiagnosed co-infection among individuals with HIV-HBV co-infection, with insufficient global surveillance data. Acute hepatitis A and E increasingly affect people with HIV, presenting both as outbreak-related and sporadic cases, particularly in the context of suboptimal vaccination coverage. Contemporary management emphasises systematic screening, vaccination, integrated antiviral strategies, and public health interventions to reduce liver-related morbidity and mortality in people with HIV.

articles.title: Interfacility Variation in Diagnosis and Tocolysis for Threatened Preterm Labor and Its Association With Gestational Age Threshold for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Perinatal Centers in the Chugoku-Shikoku Region of Western Japan.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe interfacility variation in threatened preterm labor (TPL) management in a perinatal care network in western Japan and the association between the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission threshold and the long-term tocolysis policy.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, facility-level questionnaire survey was conducted for all 43 perinatal maternal and child health centers in the Chugoku-Shikoku region of western Japan in 2024. Centers reported diagnostic criteria for TPL, use of objective scoring systems, first-line intravenous tocolytic drugs, NICU admission gestational age threshold, and institutional policies regarding planned duration of intravenous tocolysis (short-term, ≤ 48 h; long-term, > 48 h). Factors related to the adoption of long-term tocolysis were evaluated using logistic regression.

RESULTS: Valid responses were obtained from 32 centers (74.4%). A long-term-only tocolysis policy was reported by 65.6% (21/32) of centers. Diagnostic criteria and thresholds for intervention varied widely, and only three centers (9.4%) used an objective severity score, such as the preterm labor index or tocolysis index. Ritodrine hydrochloride was used as the first-line intravenous tocolytic drug in 93.8% (30/32) of centers. The NICU admission threshold differed among centers. In multivariable analysis, centers with a higher NICU admission threshold were more likely to report a long-term-only policy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.38 per 1-week increase; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-1.83; p = 0.028).

CONCLUSIONS: Management of TPL showed marked interfacility variation in the regional perinatal care network. The NICU admission threshold was associated with the institutional tocolysis-duration policy, suggesting that regional perinatal system structure should be considered when discussing optimal tocolysis duration.

articles.title: Conjoined Twin Separation and Reconstruction: An Anatomical Classification System, Techniques, and Outcomes at a Tertiary Pediatric Care Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conjoined twin separation is highly complex. Existing taxonomies describe morphology but not the extent of sharing across regions-a key determinant of feasibility, planning, and outcomes. The authors introduce the Texas Children's Hospital classification system and report their institutional experience, supplemented by a structured literature review.

METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective review of conjoined twins (2014 to 2024). The Texas Children's Hospital system assigns 1 point per domain (eg, skin/soft tissue, deep viscera, major vascular, central neurological, and bone) within 4 regions (eg, cranium, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis); region scores yield a composite fusion score. Two reviewers scored cases. The authors described outcomes and compared composite fusion scores between separated and nonseparated twins. A PubMed review identified cases with anatomical detail for scoring.

RESULTS: Seventeen cases were identified; 12 of 17 (70.6%) were viable at birth, and 4 of 12 (33.3%; 4 of 17, 23.5% overall) underwent elective separation. Tissue expansion preceded separation in 3 of 4 pairs (75%); hepatic artery embolization was performed in 1 of 4 (25%). Device complications occurred in 2 of 3 tissue expansion pairs; sternal hardware complications occurred in 2 of 3 plated patients. Infection and seroma each occurred in 2 of 8 patients (25%). Three of 8 patients (37.5%) required tracheostomy and 3 (37.5%), gastrostomy. All separated twins survived (follow-up 9 to 117 months). Composite fusion score was lower in separated versus nonseparated twins in both institutional (mean [SD], 5.2 [2.8] versus 9.3 [3.2]; P = 0.041) and literature cohorts (4.7 [1.9] versus 7.1 [1.8]; P = 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: The Texas Children's Hospital classification offers an adjunctive, anatomy-based framework capturing the burden of shared structures and is associated with separation feasibility. Although not predictive, it provides a common language to align teams, structure operative strategy, and support counseling.

articles.title: Regularization in multiplexed PET image reconstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiplexed PET (mPET) using one tracer labeled with a positron plus prompt gamma ray emitter is limited by low sensitivity to triple-photon coincidences (two annihilation photons and one prompt gamma photon), leading to high noise in the reconstructed images.

PURPOSE: The use of regularization has been previously shown to increase the image quality of single tracer PET images under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions. We will demonstrate the use of regularization in simultaneously acquired multi-tracer mPET data reconstruction.

METHODS: First, we present how a maximum a posteriori expectation maximization solution can be obtained for simultaneously acquired multi-isotope PET data. Next, we use a Monte Carlo simulation of an image quality phantom mPET acquisition with a pure positron (18F) and a positron plus prompt gamma (44Sc) emitter to evaluate the performance of different regularization methods.

RESULTS: For a baseline regularization method to simultaneously reconstruct both activity distributions, we show that a relative difference penalty (RDP) provides the best tradeoff of the penalty functions tested in image quality and quantitative accuracy for a simulated hot sphere phantom compared to quadratic and log-cosh penalty functions, with a contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in 18F/44Sc of over 60% higher on average for the RDP compared to the quadratic penalty in the largest spheres. However, this regularization approach has up to 2x worse reconstructed inter-tracer crosstalk ratio compared to unregularized reconstruction. Finally, we present a further optimization by alternating reconstruction of the two individual tracer images with regularization to achieve a CNR in the largest 18F/44Sc spheres with an up to 35% improvement on average over the simultaneous RDP-based regularization reconstruction results described above, while maintaining a 10%-20% lower inter-tracer crosstalk ratio over the unregularized reconstruction.

CONCLUSIONS: For the selected radionuclides, simulated system and phantom, we demonstrate proof-of-principle that using regularization applied to an alternating update form of EM achieves significantly higher CNR in both tracers compared to unregularized alternating update OSEM and regularized simultaneous OSEM, with significantly lower crosstalk in the prompt gamma emitter reconstruction than the regularized simultaneous OSEM.

articles.title: The Effect of Using Heated IV Fluids With Underbody Warmers on Maternal and Neonatal Well-Being in Cesarean Delivery Operations: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of underbody warming and heated IV fluids on maternal and neonatal outcomes during cesarean delivery. In a university hospital, 105 pregnant patients were randomized into three groups that dictated heating methods applied during their cesarean delivery: underbody warmer only, underbody warmer plus heated IV fluids, or passive heating with blankets. Primary outcomes were maternal and neonatal body temperatures. Secondary maternal outcomes included intraoperative blood loss, analgesic use, and time to first gas and urination. Secondary neonatal outcomes included cord blood cortisol levels, glucose levels, and Apgar scores. Neonatal temperature, Apgar scores, and maternal intraoperative temperature were significantly higher in the intervention groups. Active warming was associated with lower cortisol levels, reduced analgesic use, and faster recovery. In total, active warming improved maternal recovery and neonatal adaptation, and its routine use as a simple, safe, and effective strategy to enhance perioperative outcomes may be warranted.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a Ceramide-Based Lamellar Emulsion on Skin Barrier Function in Surgical Nurses: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Surgical nurses frequently perform perioperative hand hygiene, predisposing them to hand dryness and skin barrier impairment. This single-center randomized controlled trial evaluated a ceramide-based lamellar emulsion for improving hand skin barrier function among surgical nurses. Thirty-five nurses were assigned to an intervention group (n = 18) applying the emulsion twice daily for seven days or a control group (n = 17) receiving usual care. Transepidermal water loss, stratum corneum hydration, skin surface pH, and dry skin scores were assessed at baseline and follow-up. Transepidermal water loss significantly decreased in the intervention group from day 1 and remained lower than in the control group. Hydration increased and dry skin scores improved in the intervention group, whereas minimal changes occurred in the control group. Short-term use of the emulsion improved barrier function and may help reduce occupational skin damage in perioperative nurses. These findings support integrating moisturizing protocols into perioperative hand hygiene.

articles.title: Airborne and Surface Bacteria in ORs: Integration of ASHRAE-Compliant Ventilation and Active UV-C Air Treatment.
articles.abstract: Bacteria in ORs increase surgical site infection risk. The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers Standard 170 defines OR ventilation standards, but the added benefit of in-room supplemental ultraviolet C air treatment remains uncertain. We compared bacterial counts before and after installing active ultraviolet C air treatment in an OR with Standard 170-compliant ventilation, using a similar OR as a control with Standard 170-compliant ventilation alone. After installation, the intervention OR showed 80% fewer airborne bacteria and 61% fewer settled surface bacteria. The control OR showed a 219% increase in airborne colony-forming units per cubic meter and a 24% increase in settled surface bacteria over the same period, reflecting potential confounders. Although the intervention was associated with lower bacterial levels in two assays, more evidence is needed given the limited number of ORs tested and the variation in the control OR.

articles.title: From Conventional to Nano-Enabled Combination Therapies to Address Therapeutic Challenges of Malaria.
articles.abstract: Malaria, a poverty-related disease, is a significant global health burden. Combination therapy is one of the most efficient approaches currently used to treat malaria infections, with artemisinin-based combination therapies being the recommended first-line treatment. Nevertheless, the emergence of resistance to artemisinin and its derivatives underscores the importance of developing new alternative antimalarial combinations as well as innovative therapeutic strategies to combat the disease. Intersecting combination therapy with nanotechnology could create innovative and highly effective nano-based combination therapies. This approach has shown notable benefits in treating various diseases, particularly cancer, and holds great potential in infectious disease treatment. Initial preclinical studies have demonstrated the potential of nano-based combination therapies in malaria treatment. This narrative review provides a panoramic overview of regulatory-approved and internationally endorsed conventional combination therapies for malaria and explores ongoing research into developing novel conventional and nano-based combination therapies. It aims to guide future research funding, inspires the development of innovative next-generation nano-based combination therapies, and supports their clinical translation, thereby maximizing efforts to fight malaria and accelerating disease elimination.

articles.title: Effects of a Multicomponent App-Based Exercise Program on Motor Skill Development in Children With Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Secondary Outcome Analysis of a Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
articles.abstract: Motor skill deficits are common in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), while traditional face-to-face exercise interventions are often limited by cost and accessibility. This secondary outcome analysis of a three-arm randomized controlled trial examined the effects of a multicomponent app-based exercise program on motor skill outcomes in children with ADHD. A total of 145 children aged 6-10 years were assigned to an app-based exercise group (Experimental Group 1, EG1; n = 53), a traditional offline exercise group (Experimental Group 2, EG2; n = 45), or a minimal-intervention control group (CG, n = 47). Both intervention groups received a 12-week program (3 sessions/week, 45-60 min/session) involving integrated physical and cognitive exercises, delivered either through a custom-developed WeChat applet ("LeDongYing") or through coach-led in-person sessions. Motor skills were assessed using the Test of Gross Motor Development, Third Edition (TGMD-3) for locomotor and ball skills, and the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (MABC-2) for manual dexterity, aiming and catching, and balance. Intervention effects were examined using linear mixed-effects models. Both EG1 and EG2 showed significant improvements across all motor skill domains (all p < 0.01), whereas the CG showed no significant changes. Pairwise comparisons showed that both intervention groups were superior to the CG on all motor skill outcomes (all p < 0.05), with no statistically significant differences between EG1 and EG2. These findings support the short-term efficacy of a multicomponent app-based exercise intervention for motor-test performance in children with ADHD compared with minimal intervention, suggesting potential as an alternative delivery when access to face-to-face exercise services is limited.

articles.title: A generalizable 3D dose prediction across heterogeneous cohorts: A framework developed for the 2025 AAPM GDP-HMM challenge.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Manual radiotherapy treatment planning is labor-intensive, subjective, and highly variable across planners and institutions. Deep learning has emerged as a promising approach for estimating achievable three-dimensional (3D) dose distributions for a given plan (hereafter: dose prediction) by directly mapping patient anatomy and beam geometry to voxel-wise dose. However, achieving robust generalization across diverse anatomical sites, prescriptions, and institutions remains a major challenge, particularly under computational constraints required for clinical deployment.

PURPOSE: We sought to develop and evaluate a generalizable, computationally efficient 3D dose prediction framework capable of spanning heterogeneous multi-site and multi-cohort datasets, as defined in the 2025 AAPM Generalizable Dose Prediction for Heterogeneous Multi-Cohort and Multi-Site (GDP-HMM) Grand Challenge. Our goal was to design a model that not only achieved state-of-the-art voxel-wise accuracy but also maintained clinically meaningful dose-volume and geometric characteristics across diverse cases.

METHODS: We implemented a fully convolutional 3D dose-prediction model adapted from the MedNeXt architecture, which was originally introduced as a high-capacity convolutional backbone for medical image segmentation and is well suited to volumetric dense prediction tasks. The network accepted multimodal inputs comprising CT, PTV/OAR masks, beam and angle plates, and scalar plan metadata. A composite loss function combined voxel-wise L1, body-masked weighted L1, structure-wise moment-matching, and gradient-based penalties to jointly preserve spatial fidelity and dosimetric accuracy. The model was trained on the fixed GDP-HMM dataset consisting of 2876 training plans, 356 validation plans, and a held-out test set of 498 plans using random 3D patches and evaluated by mean absolute error (MAE), homogeneity index (HI), and conformity indices (CI100%, CI50%). Ablation studies quantified the contribution of each loss component to overall performance. Statistical comparisons used paired Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction.

RESULTS: The proposed model achieved a mean voxel-wise MAE of 2.04 Gy on the validation set, outperforming the challenge baseline (2.54 Gy). An ensemble with the baseline further improved MAE to 1.94 Gy on the validation set and 2.071 Gy on the held-out test set, corresponding to the lowest test-set MAE and first-place overall ranking in the GDP-HMM Challenge. Predicted dose distributions preserved key plan characteristics, with ΔHI, ΔCI100%, and ΔCI50% narrowly centered around zero, indicating consistent target coverage and dose conformity. Protocol-specific evaluations for head-and-neck and lung cohorts demonstrated close alignment with reference plans, with no systematic degradation in OAR endpoints. Ablation experiments showed that removing gradient-based terms increased MAE by 0.50 Gy, while excluding the moment-matching term increased MAE by 0.06 Gy confirming that both gradient- and moment-based constraints enhanced spatial and dosimetric fidelity.

CONCLUSION: We present a generalizable 3D dose prediction framework that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while satisfying stringent runtime requirements (< 3s per case on < 24 GB GPU memory). By integrating gradient-aware and moment-based constraints within a MedNeXt backbone, the model preserved clinical DVH endpoints and geometric plan features. These findings demonstrate that carefully engineered loss formulations are pivotal for cross-institutional generalization. The framework offers a foundation for rapid dose prediction that could accelerate treatment planning, reduce inter-planner variability, and enable intelligent automation in radiotherapy workflows.

articles.title: Digital Twins in Clinical Neurology: From Concept to Clinical Application in Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patient digital twins (DT) are emerging as a promising paradigm for personalised and predictive healthcare. In neurology, and particularly in multiple sclerosis (MS), the availability of longitudinal, multimodal data provides a strong foundation for developing patient-specific digital models, including simulation-based and mechanistic approaches. However, it remains unclear to what extent current approaches represent integrated, clinically embedded DT systems.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review to synthesise current concepts, modelling approaches and translational challenges of DT in neurology, using MS as an illustrative use case. Existing approaches were mapped to core DT components, including data integration, predictive modelling, dynamic updating and clinical integration.

RESULTS: Current DT-related approaches in MS demonstrate substantial progress across complementary development tracks, including multimodal data integration, predictive modelling, digital biomarkers, mechanistic simulations, virtual-patient frameworks and in silico trials. These capabilities represent important building blocks of DT development but have not yet been fully integrated into continuously operating clinical systems. Core DT functionalities, including continuous bidirectional data exchange, real-time model updating and closed-loop interaction with clinical workflows, remain limited. Key challenges include data fragmentation, limited interoperability, lack of standardised validation, and regulatory, ethical and economic constraints.

CONCLUSION: MS represents a highly suitable model domain for DT development. Future progress will depend on further maturing and validating individual modelling and data-integration capabilities, as well as on their integration into continuously updating, clinically embedded systems. Robust validation, scalable infrastructures and appropriate governance frameworks will be essential to establish safe, effective and clinically actionable use in practice.

articles.title: Correction to "Italian Delphi Consensus on Maternity Care in Multiple Sclerosis: Toward an Interdisciplinary Model of Care".

B-Cell Follicles in the Secondary Lymphatic Tissues Act as a Critical Microanatomical Niche for Sustained Viral Replication, Virus-Host Interaction and Damage During Chronic SIV Infection of Rhesus Macaques.
articles.abstract: Most people living with HIV-1 (HIV) are diagnosed during the chronic stage of infection, at which point viral setpoint has been established and a substantial immunopathologic damage in the secondary lymphatic tissues (LTs) has been induced. To better characterize virus-host interaction and immunopathologic damage in LTs, we investigated viral spatial distribution patterns and the corresponding LT structural alterations in SIV chronically infected rhesus macaques. Using RNAscope in-situ hybridization (RNAscope) and a combination of CODEX with RNAscope (Comb-CODEX-RNAscope), we demonstrated that in chronic infection, SIV viral RNA (vRNA) is predominantly resides within B-cell follicles with minimal presence in T-cell zones, and there is significant B-cell follicular damage, encompassing follicular hyperplasia, fibrosis, and disintegration of the germinal center. Using high-resolution quantitative spatial Comb-CODEX-RNAscope, our results confirm that the B-cell follicles act as a critical microanatomical niche for sustained viral replication, virus-host interaction and tissue damage during SIV chronic infection.

articles.title: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy With Low Appendicular Muscle Mass Is Associated With Osteoporosis, Falls, and Fractures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) and low appendicular muscle mass (LAMM) may jointly contribute to adverse skeletal outcomes, but their combined effects remain unclear. We examined their associations with osteoporosis, falls, and fractures in patients with Type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: We explored associations of diabetes and grip strength with skeletal outcomes using SHARE v8.0.0 (327 248 participants). The primary analysis used a cohort of patients with Type 2 diabetes from the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University. LAMM was defined using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass index. Associations of clinically diagnosed DPN, LAMM, and their coexistence with osteoporosis, falls, and fractures were evaluated using logistic regression and Cox survival models. Exploratory serum antibody omics was performed.

RESULTS: In SHARE, grip strength was inversely associated with all three outcomes. In the local cohort, coexisting DPN and LAMM were associated with higher odds of osteoporosis (OR 2.151, 95% CI 1.645-2.805), falls (OR 4.667, 95% CI 3.406-6.376), and fractures (OR 2.416, 95% CI 1.367-3.515; all p < 0.001). Cox analyses showed higher hazards of osteoporosis (HR 3.410, 95% CI 1.579-7.362; p = 0.002) and falls (HR 4.385, 95% CI 1.838-10.459; p < 0.001), but not fractures (HR 0.708, 95% CI 0.187-2.675; p = 0.611). Antibody omics suggested a reactivity profile involving endoplasmic reticulum protein processing and neurodegeneration-related pathways.

CONCLUSION: Coexisting DPN and LAMM were associated with higher odds of all three skeletal outcomes and higher longitudinal hazards of osteoporosis and falls, but not fractures. The exploratory omics findings require functional validation.

articles.title: Reply to Darroudi et al.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

articles.title: Rapid assessment of diabetes mellitus and diabetic retinopathy in the rural-tribal population of Tapi district of western India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The present study assessed the prevalence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and diabetic retinopathy (DR) in a rural-tribal population in western India.

METHODS: The standard RAAB (Rapid Assessment of Avoidable Blindness) methodology with DR module was used in this survey. A total of 139 clusters of 60 people each aged ≥50 years were selected by cluster random sampling with probability proportionate to size. The participants were classified as having DM if they were known to have DM or if their random blood glucose (RBG) level was ≥200 mg/dL, detected by the test offered at the doorstep. Dilated retinal examination and Scottish DR grading were performed for all diabetics.

RESULTS: In total, 7835 (93.9%) out of 8344 eligible participants were examined. The prevalence of DM (381/7835) was 4.9% (95% confidence interval (CI): 4.2-5.6). Of these, 68.5% (261/381) were known diabetics and 31.5% (120/381) were identified by spot RBG test. Fifty-five per cent (n = 144/261) of known diabetics had RBG ≥200 mg/dL. The prevalence of any DR, any maculopathy, and sight-threatening DR was 16.3% (95% CI: 12.5 to 20.1), 9.2% (95% CI: 6.2 to 12.2), and 2.1% (95% CI: 0.7 to 3.5), respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of DM and DR in the rural tribal population was lower than the national average but is emerging. More than half of the diabetics had uncontrolled DM, which needs improved awareness and accessibility to health care services for this underprivileged population. Further studies are needed to establish predictors and causal relationship between prevalence of DM/DR in the rural-tribal population.

articles.title: Ethnolinguistic differences in diabetic retinopathy within a shared geographic setting in South India: The Gudalur diabetic retinopathy study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence and severity between Tamil- and Malayalam-speaking adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) living within a shared geographic setting and to examine differences in clinical, behavioral, and dietary characteristics.

DESIGN: Community-based cross-sectional screening study.

METHODS: Adults aged ≥40 years with self-reported T2DM, ≥10 years' residence in Gudalur taluk (Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu), and mother tongue Tamil or Malayalam were recruited through 12 outreach eye camps conducted between January and December 2024. Participants underwent dilated fundus examinations by indirect ophthalmoscopy. Sociodemographic and socioeconomic characteristics, anthropometry, diabetes duration, physical activity, knowledge and screening practices, and dietary intake were assessed using standardized instruments. Between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate tests, and logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between mother tongue and any DR.

RESULTS: Among 295 participants (Malayalam n = 171; Tamil n = 124), Malayalam speakers were older ( P = 0.008) and had longer diabetes duration ( P < 0.001), while HbA1c was comparable. DR was more prevalent among Malayalam speakers (49.7% vs 30.6%; P = 0.002). Malayalam mother tongue remained associated with any DR after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.88; 95% CI 1.10-3.22; P = 0.021). Awareness and annual eye examination uptake were higher among Malayalam speakers, who also had higher total energy intake and a greater contribution of saturated fat in the dietary subset ( P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Within a shared geographic setting, Malayalam-speaking adults with T2DM had higher DR prevalence and severity than Tamil-speaking adults, after adjustment for age and diabetes duration, alongside differences in awareness and dietary fat patterns.

articles.title: Toward a comparative endocrinology of aging: insights from insects.
articles.abstract: Insulin-like signaling modulates aging and lifespan in insects. Here, we discuss a novel view of this control: insulin hormone in the adult regulates the production of the sesquiterpenoid juvenile hormone (JH) that in turn acts as the systemic regulator of aging and lifespan. Work in Drosophila establishes that insulin signaling is allatotropic - it stimulates the production and secretion of JH from the corpora allata. JH then exerts systemic effects on adult survival through its control of specific proteins, translation and proteostasis. The interdependent functions of insulin and JH allow reproduction and longevity to be coupled in many insects or decoupled in social insects with long-lived queens and in some long-lived genetic mutants of Drosophila. Features of these insulin-regulated life history syndromes are also found in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. Recognizing the systemic role of JH in aging provides grounds to search for analogous systems in mammals that might modulate human lifespan.

articles.title: Renal Function and 4-Year Outcomes in Edoxaban-Treated Patients: A Sub-Analysis From the ETNA-AF Europe Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants, like edoxaban, are essential in managing atrial fibrillation (AF). The impact of renal function on edoxaban dosages in real-world settings remains unclear. This 4-year ETNA-AF-Europe study follow-up analysis investigated how chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages affect the safety and effectiveness of usual edoxaban doses.

METHODS: ETNA-AF-Europe (NCT02944019) was an observational study conducted from 2016 to 2022 across 776 centres in 10 European countries. Hazard ratios (HR) and annualized event rates were calculated for all-cause death, cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and bleeding events for the overall population and participants stratified by dose (30/60 mg) and CKD stages at baseline.

RESULTS: Of the 13,164 participants in the full analysis set, 9114 participants with CKD (Stage 1, n = 2064; Stage 2, n = 4855; Stage 3, n = 1985; Stage 4, n = 135; missing, n = 75) received label-recommended edoxaban doses. Compared with CKD Stage 1, higher CKD stages were associated with increased risks for stroke (Stage 3: HR [95% CI]: 1.889 [1.240-2.878], p = 0.003) and CV death (HR [95% CI]; Stage 4: 14.450 [8.270-25.247], Stage 3: 4.672 [3.312-6.969], Stage 2: 2.066 [1.394-3.062], all p < 0.001). All-cause death followed a similar trend. After adjusting for age, sex, body weight, CHA2DS2-VASc and modified HAS-BLED scores, most bleeding and effectiveness outcomes showed no nominally significant differences across CKD stages.

CONCLUSIONS: Edoxaban in patients with AF is effective and well tolerated across CKD stages and appropriate label dosing can offset the risk from renal impairment.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction of clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The expected clinical and functional trajectory after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with left ventricular dysfunction remains uncertain. Recent trials have highlighted substantial heterogeneity in both clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement, underscoring the need for improved post-PCI prognostic risk stratification in this high-risk population. This study aimed to develop machine learning models predicting clinical outcomes and LVEF improvement after PCI in patients with reduced LVEF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective single-centre study included adults undergoing PCI between 2004 and 2025 with baseline LVEF <45%. Two CatBoost models were developed using 53 routinely available pre- and intra-procedural predictors. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of death, myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or coronary artery bypass grafting. The secondary endpoint was an absolute LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), and enrichment analysis. The dataset included 3336 procedures from 2793 patients (median LVEF 35%). For the primary endpoint (n = 2152; event rate 37.5%), the model achieved an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.73-0.83) and a PR-AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.63-0.77), with event rates of 83.7% in the highest-risk decile and 9.3% in the lowest-risk decile. For LVEF improvement (n = 2551; 34.7% improved), performance was moderate (AUC 0.73), with enrichment to 76.9% in the highest-probability decile.

CONCLUSION: Machine learning models using routinely available patient and procedural data enabled meaningful prognostic stratification in patients with left ventricular dysfunction undergoing PCI, supporting individualized estimation of clinical and functional trajectories after revascularization.

articles.title: Global research trends in clinical studies of ginseng: a bibliometric and text-as-data analysis.
articles.abstract: Clinical research on ginseng has expanded considerably, yet most bibliometric syntheses still rely on publication counts and co-occurrence maps. We mapped research on Panax ginseng and demonstrated a text-as-data and network pipeline. English-language publications indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded (2004-2026) were retrieved using ginseng- and clinical-study-related terms and screened by two reviewers. CiteSpace and R-based clustering and citation-burst analyses were supplemented with topic modelling, word embeddings, a cross-validated study-type classifier, social-network analysis, negative-binomial citation modelling, Gini concentration, and disease-intervention and pathway mapping. Of 1386 records, 270 met inclusion criteria. Annual publications increased from six in 2004 to 26 in 2021, accumulating 6990 citations (h-index 44). South Korea produced 53.7% of publications, whereas Australia had the highest network centrality; international co-authorship remained low (24.4%) and did not increase. Seventeen CiteSpace clusters and eight validated topics indicated a shift from herb-drug-interaction safety toward supplementation, type 2 diabetes, cognition, and sexual or hormonal health. The author-keyword network showed a small-world structure centered on the intervention rather than a disease. Citations were concentrated (Gini 0.562), and only team size predicted citation rate (IRR 1.06). The classifier achieved 89.6% accuracy, while ginsenosides, NF-κB/inflammation, and insulin/AMPK were the molecular terms most frequently co-mentioned in mechanism-focused abstracts. Randomized designs comprised 190 studies (70.4%), with 10 observational (3.7%) and 70 (25.9%) other designs (uncontrolled, single-arm, pharmacokinetic, or mechanistic sub-studies). Clinical ginseng research is increasingly disease-specific but remains geographically concentrated, fragmented, and dependent on short-term trials. This pipeline quantifies uncertainty, reveals patterns beyond counts, and highlights the need for international collaboration, standardized ginsenoside reporting, and long-term cohorts.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rh2, a putative functional modulator of Annexin A2, attenuates post-hemorrhagic stroke cerebral edema via inhibiting vesicular transcytosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) causes mechanical damage and cerebral edema. Annexin A2, expressed in endothelial cells, regulates cerebral edema, but its mechanisms in ICH remain unclear.

METHODS: A mouse ICH model was established using collagenase VII-S. We measured Annexin A2 expression, transcytosis, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability. AAV was used to specifically knock down Annexin A2 in cerebrovascular endothelial cells. Protein interactions were identified by co-immunoprecipitation and label-free LC-MS. Ginsenoside Rh2 was tested for effects on protein binding (biolayer interferometry and competition assays) and on neurological/motor function, BBB integrity, and transcytosis.

RESULTS: ICH increased Annexin A2 expression, transcytosis, and BBB permeability. Annexin A2 knockdown worsened neurological deficits and motor function, increased BBB permeability, exacerbated tight junction disruption, but significantly reduced transcytosis. Six cytoskeletal proteins, Alpha-actinin-4, Actin-related protein 2, Actin alpha skeletal muscle, Actin cytoplasmic 1, Actin cytoplasmic 2, and Myosin-9, interacted with Annexin A2. Rh2 reduced binding affinity between Annexin A2 and these proteins, specifically inhibiting Annexin A2-Alpha-actinin-4 binding. Rh2 treatment improved neurological and motor function, reversed BBB disruption and tight junction damage, and suppressed transcytosis without altering Annexin A2 expression.

CONCLUSION: Annexin A2 knockdown inhibited transcytosis but disrupted tight junctions and aggravated edema. In contrast, Rh2 inhibited transcytosis and exerts potential protective effect tight junctions, which may suggest a trend toward alleviation of cerebral edema to a certain extent. Selectively targeting Annexin A2-mediated transcytosis may be a promising therapy for ICH.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rd alleviates atherosclerosis by inhibiting adipocyte ferroptosis in perivascular adipose tissues.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ginsenoside Rd (Rd) is an active ingredient in Panax ginseng Meyer and can be absorbed into the adipose tissue. Here, we aimed to investigate the impact of Rd on atherosclerosis (AS) and explore the mechanism.

METHODS: We constructed an AS model by feeding ApoE-/- mice with a standard Western high-fat diet, treated with Rd, and combined RORC and TIGAR adipocyte-specific adeno-associated virus infection. An inflammatory adipocyte model (3T3-L1) was induced by LPS, and a lipid accumulation model in adipocytes was induced by palmitic acid. We investigated the role of the Rd-mediated RORC/TIGAR axis in adipocyte inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis through lentiviral vectors and the ferroptosis activator erastin. The interactions between RORC and TIGAR were examined. Next, the degree of lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis within perivascular adipose tissues (PVAT) in mice and 3T3-L1 cells was assessed.

RESULTS: Rd improved PVAT dysfunction and alleviated endothelial inflammation in AS mice. Rd targeted and inhibited RORC expression in adipocytes within the PVAT of mice. The transcription factor RORC occupied the TIGAR promoter to repress TIGAR transcription. Reactivation of RORC reversed the therapeutic benefit of Rd on AS, and reactivation of TIGAR also alleviated AS exacerbated by RORC. Rd reached therapeutic benefits by inhibiting RORC expression in adipocytes within PVAT, weakening its inhibitory effect on TIGAR, and further inhibiting adipocyte ferroptosis.

CONCLUSION: Rd targets RORC to activate TIGAR expression and block adipocyte ferroptosis in PVAT, thereby inhibiting AS.

articles.title: Rapid Progression of Acute Acalculous Cholecystitis to Gangrenous Cholecystitis in an Initially Non-Critically Ill Patient: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Acute acalculous cholecystitis (AAC) is not confined to the critically ill and may behave like calculous disease. A 65-year-old hypertensive man with localized, stone-free cholecystitis deteriorated on hospital Day 4 with peritonism, acidosis, and acute kidney injury. Emergency open cholecystectomy confirmed gangrene; deterioration warrants urgent source control.

articles.title: Knowledge of Nipah Virus and Associated Factors Among Rural Population in Bangladesh: Evidence From a Community-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic threat and posing serious public health risks in Bangladesh due to its high fatality rate, high transmissibility, and the lack of particular licensed vaccinations.

METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out among 415 adult rural respondents. Data were collected using a paper-based structured questionnaire consisting of respondents' sociodemographic characteristics and knowledge-related questions regarding NiV. Participants' sociodemographic characteristics and knowledge level were summarized using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. The statistical significance level was set at p < 0.05, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 37.56 ± 14.63 years, and 66.5% were male. Although 71.1% of participants had heard of the NiV, only 16.4% demonstrated good knowledge (≥ 65% of total score). The mean knowledge score was 7.99 ± 3.86. Knowledge was particularly limited regarding routes of transmission, including person-to-person transmission, clinical manifestations, treatment availability, and the ineffectiveness of antibiotics. In the adjusted analysis, participants aged 25-34 years (AOR = 2.85, 95% CI: 1.13-7.63), females (AOR = 2.73, 95% CI: 1.09-7.09), and those with graduation or higher education (AOR = 10.70, 95% CI: 2.10-67.70) were significantly more likely to have good knowledge. Conversely, participants who consumed fresh date palm sap had significantly lower odds of good knowledge (AOR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.17-0.68).

CONCLUSION: The rural respondents in this study area demonstrated inadequate awareness of the NiV. Participants' understanding of disease symptoms, treatment limitations, disease transmission, and prophylactic measures was remarkably poor. To prevent NiV transmission and outbreaks in Bangladesh, these findings highlight the significance of targeted, culturally appropriate, and community-based health education programs that focus on safe date palm sap consumption, early symptom recognition, and other effective preventive measures.

articles.title: Integration of Aromatherapy and Essential Oils in Asthma Symptom Relief: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Asthma affects 262 million people globally, causing 455,000 preventable deaths, with higher mortality in low-resource areas due to limited diagnosis and treatment. Aromatherapy, using bioactive essential oils (EOs), has emerged as a promising complementary approach for asthma symptom management.

METHODS: This review synthesizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of EOs in alleviating asthma-related inflammation, bronchoconstriction, and immune dysregulation through anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and immunomodulatory mechanisms.

RESULTS: Key oils such as lavender, eucalyptus, and peppermint demonstrate efficacy in reducing airway hyperresponsiveness, oxidative stress, and Th2-mediated inflammation, supported by preclinical and clinical studies. Methods of application, including inhalation, topical use, and environmental diffusion, are evaluated for their physiological and psychological benefits, particularly in stress and sleep modulation, which are critical to asthma control. Safety considerations, such as allergenicity, proper dosing, and potential drug interactions, are emphasized to ensure safe integration with conventional therapies.

CONCLUSION: Despite the promising findings, further large-scale clinical trials are needed to validate the efficacy, optimize protocols, and explore personalized approaches based on genetic and phenotypic variability. This review underscores aromatherapy's role as an adjunctive therapy within a holistic asthma management framework, bridging traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific validation to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: The Moderating Role of Social Support in the Relationship Between Diabetes Distress and Psychological Well-Being Among Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study Protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Type 2 diabetes imposes a considerable psychological burden on older adults, including elevated diabetes distress and diminished psychological well-being. Social support may buffer the harmful mental-health effects of chronic disease-related stress, yet whether it moderates the link between diabetes distress and psychological well-being remains rarely examined among older Iranian adults with type 2 diabetes. This protocol aims to determine the moderating role of social support in that relationship in this population.

METHODS: This descriptive-analytic cross-sectional protocol will recruit 300 adults aged 60 years or above with type 2 diabetes from the Bandar Abbas Diabetes Clinic through simple random sampling from the clinic electronic registry. Trained interviewers will administer a demographic and clinical form, the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, the PAID-5 (diabetes distress), the MSSS-5 (social support), and the WHO-5 Well-Being Index in person or by telephone using identical structured interviews. Hierarchical multiple regression will test the diabetes distress by social support interaction on WHO-5 scores, in an unadjusted model and a model adjusted for a pre-specified demographic and clinical covariate set, with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors, bootstrapped confidence intervals, and simple-slopes and Johnson-Neyman probing. Missing data will be handled with multiple imputation. Analyses will use IBM SPSS Statistics version 28 with two-sided tests at α = 0.05.

RESULTS: As a protocol, no empirical results are reported. The completed study will yield estimates of diabetes distress, social support, and psychological well-being levels, their bivariate associations, and the moderation effect with appropriate uncertainty quantification.

CONCLUSION: The findings are expected to provide a scientific basis for nursing and psychosocial interventions that strengthen social support networks to protect the psychological well-being of older adults with type 2 diabetes. Ethical approval has been obtained (IR.HUMS.REC.1405.013); written or audio-recorded verbal informed consent will be obtained from all participants.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infection with Entamoeba histolytica in children can seriously affect individual and public health. Moreover, the prevalence of this disease varies significantly across different regions of the world, and comprehensive and accurate data on its global prevalence among children are lacking. The present study aims to determine the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children.

METHODS: This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing evidence on the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children, conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 statement criteria. The search was conducted using the (AND) and (OR) operators, and the retrieved data were transferred to the EndNote reference management software. The quality assessment of the studies included in the study was conducted based on the STROBE checklist, considering the nature of the cross-sectional studies included in the study. I2 index was used to evaluate heterogeneity. Funnel Plot and Begg and mazumdar correlation test were used to evaluate the publication bias. Data were analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis software (Version 2).

RESULTS: A total of 119 studies with a sample size of 70,259 children were included. The I 2 heterogeneity test indicated high heterogeneity (I 2: 97.7%); therefore, a random-effects model was used for data analysis. Based on the meta-analysis, the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children was reported as 8.4% (95% CI: 7.1-10). However, given the results of the publication bias test, the results should be considered with caution, and it is also stated that the geographically heterogeneous distribution of the studies is also a limitation of this study. the pooled prevalence estimate should be interpreted with caution despite the subgroup and meta-regression analyses performed.

CONCLUSION: According to the results of the meta-analysis, the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children was reported as 8.4%; therefore, although the final prevalence is relatively high, it should be investigated and considered in light of the transmissibility of this disease in children and its impact.

articles.title: Time to Discontinuation and Risk Factors for Outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy in Primary Care: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Survival Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical nutrition therapy (MNT) provided by registered dietitians is effective for managing non-communicable diseases, but patient discontinuation remains common in clinical practice. Studies examining the timing and predictors of MNT discontinuation are limited. This study aimed to identify the timing and patient factors associated with MNT discontinuation in primary care settings.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who initiated outpatient MNT at a primary care clinic between April 2018 and March 2023. Patients aged < 18 years and those with cancer- or malnutrition-related conditions were excluded. Discontinuation was defined as no MNT visit or scheduled appointment within 3 months after the last visit. Patients were followed for up to 24 months through March 2025. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated continuation rates, and multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models identified factors associated with discontinuation. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 470 patients (median age, 63 years; 59.4% women), 241 (51.3%) discontinued MNT during follow-up. Median time to discontinuation was 15 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 12-21). Continuation rates were 88.3% at 3 months, 70.4% at 6 months, and 43.5% at 24 months. Obesity, dyslipidemia, and medication use were associated with lower discontinuation risk, whereas complications, living with family, and preparation stage of behavior change were associated with higher risk. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results.

CONCLUSIONS: MNT continuation declined rapidly within 6 months. Multiple patient factors were associated with discontinuation risk, suggesting the need for early risk identification and individualized support strategies.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rk2 combined with dexamethasone enhances the anti neutrophilic asthma effect via STAT1/NLRP3-NETs-Th17/Treg axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neutrophilic asthma (NA) is a severe, corticosteroid-resistant phenotype associated with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and Th17/Treg imbalance. Cold exposure exacerbates NA progression, increasing the global clinical burden. Currently, combination therapy with corticosteroids is considered a viable approach. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential and mechanisms of ginsenoside Rk2 (Rk2) combined with dexamethasone (DEX) against cold-stimulated neutrophilic asthma (CSNA).

METHODS: A corticosteroid-resistant BEAS-2B cell model was established by NTHi stimulation. A CSNA mouse model was established via ovalbumin sensitization, NTHi infection, and cold stimulation, followed by Rk2 and/or DEX treatment. Airway hyperresponsiveness, histopathology, and neutrophil infiltration were measured to assess therapeutic efficacy. Th17/Treg populations were analyzed by flow cytometry. NETs formation was quantified in PMA-stimulated primary mouse neutrophils. A NETs-naïve CD4+ T cell co-culture system was used to examine the causal role of NETs in Th17/Treg imbalance. Transcriptomics and agonist-based gain-of-function experiments were conducted to validate the mechanism of Rk2 combined with DEX.

RESULTS: Rk2 reversed DEX resistance by rebalancing GRα/GRβ, upregulating HDAC2, and promoting GRα nuclear translocation. Compared with monotherapy, Rk2 combined with DEX ameliorated airway inflammation and restored Th17/Treg homeostasis. Mechanistically, this combination therapy suppressed NETs formation by reducing NETs components, DNA release and ROS generation. NETs drove Th17/Treg imbalance via STAT1/NLRP3 inflammasome axis. Pharmacological activation of either STAT1 or NLRP3 reversed the beneficial effects.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate for the first time that Rk2, a potent natural corticosteroid potentiator, acts in combination with DEX to alleviate CSNA by suppressing the STAT1/NLRP3 inflammasome-NETs-Th17/Treg cascade.

articles.title: Multifaceted neuroprotection of ginsenosides: Mechanisms, nano-delivery advances, and therapeutic potential in central nervous system disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central nervous system (CNS) diseases remain therapeutic challenges due to complex pathology and poor drug penetration across the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Ginsenosides, the active components of Panax ginseng, possess multi-target neuroprotective properties but exhibit low bioavailability.

PURPOSE: This review synthesizes current evidence on ginsenoside mechanisms and evaluates the role of nanotechnology in enhancing their delivery and efficacy for CNS disorders.

STUDY DESIGN: A systematic search was conducted following PRISMA guidelines across PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and Google Scholar (2015-present). Included studies investigated ginsenosides in neurological disease models and nano-formulation strategies.

RESULTS: Ginsenosides modulate neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and calcium homeostasis through pathways involving NF-κB, Nrf2, and Bcl-2/Bax. Nano-delivery systems-such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, and biomimetic vesicles-significantly improve ginsenoside stability, BBB traversal, and brain-targeted accumulation. Functionalization with ligands (e.g., Angiopep-2) or cell membranes further enhances specificity and therapeutic outcomes in ischemic stroke, glioma, Alzheimer's disease, and spinal cord injury models.

CONCLUSION: Nanotechnology-based delivery systems potently augment the neuroprotective potential of ginsenosides, offering a promising strategy for multi-target CNS therapy. Future efforts should focus on translational safety, scalable production, and clinical validation.

articles.title: Tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP) modulates hyperuricemia by regulating the expression of renal urate transporters OAT1, URAT1, and GLUT9.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Hyperuricemia is a common metabolic disease. Epidemiological studies have suggested an association between hyperuricemia and tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP), yet the mechanism underlying their interaction and relevant empirical research remain lacking. This study used Kunming mice as subjects and conducted an 8-group controlled experiment (including a control group, TCEP exposure group, hyperuricemia group, and different intervention groups) over 40 days. Detection was performed from three aspects: oxidative stress and inflammation, uric acid metabolism and organ damage, and molecular mechanisms. The study aimed to verify the toxicological association between TCEP and hyperuricemia, as well as to clarify the uric acid-lowering effect and mechanism of caffeic acid. The experimental results showed that TCEP exposure further increased the uric acid level in hyperuricemic mice; further detection revealed that the plasma xanthine oxidase (XOD) activity in mice of the TCEP exposure group was significantly higher than that in the non-exposure group. Meanwhile, TCEP exposure induced a significant inflammatory response in mice without increasing the malondialdehyde (MDA) level, and was accompanied by signs of renal damage, specifically manifested as renal tubular dilation and glomerular atrophy. After intervention with caffeic acid, the uric acid level and abnormally increased organ coefficients of mice were significantly reduced; further analysis via qPCR and Western blotting experiments indicated that caffeic acid might reduce uric acid concentration by downregulating the protein expression of GLUT9 and upregulating the protein expression of OAT1.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s43188-026-00344-0.

articles.title: Study on the anti-asthmatic effect of Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair and its mechanisms in regulating the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair is a classic representative one of the "combination of tonification and astringency" in traditional Chinese medicine. Ginseng tonifies lung Qi and benefits heart Qi, while Schisandra restrains the lung, nourishes the kidney, calms the mind, and soothes the spirit. When they are used in combination, one can play a tonifying role and another can serve as an astringency, with tonification but without stagnation and with astringency but without depression, so the combination can not only enhance the efficacy of replenishing Qi and nourishing Yin but also strengthen the effect of astringing and consolidating. However, the underlying mechanism and action of its combined use in the prevention and treatment of asthma remain unclear.

METHODS: An asthma model in mice was established by using ovalbumin (OVA) combined with aluminum hydroxide (Al(OH)3), so as to evaluate the anti-asthmatic effect of Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair and determine its optimal compatibility ratio. For further validation, an in vitro asthma model was developed by stimulating human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) with interleukin-4 (IL-4) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). The chemical profile of the herb pair extract was comprehensively analyzed by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Potential bioactive components and anti-asthma mechanisms were predicted through network pharmacology analysis and subsequently verified by Western blot and immunofluorescence assays.

RESULTS: Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair could improve the behavior of asthmatic mice, alleviate the pathological damage of lung tissue, reduce the levels of inflammatory factors in the serum of asthmatic mice and the asthma model BEAS-2B cells, increase the activity of superoxide dismutase (SOD), and decrease the levels of malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS). A total of 72 bioactive components were identified from the Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair extract, and the herb pair could inhibit the expression of PI3K-AKT pathway-related proteins in the lung tissue of asthmatic mice and BEAS-2B cells.

CONCLUSION: Ginseng-Schisandra herb pair can effectively alleviate the airway inflammatory response and oxidative stress injury by regulating the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in mice to exert an anti-asthmatic effect. Among different compatibility ratios and compared with single herbs, the 2:1 ratio of the herb pair exhibits the optimal therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Association of the ADAMTS14 rs4747096 Polymorphism and C-Reactive Protein Levels With Knee Osteoarthritis Severity: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The rs4747096 polymorphism in the ADAMTS14 gene and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels have been associated with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) severity; however, evidence from Vietnam remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of rs4747096 genotypes, assess CRP levels, and examine their associations with KOA severity.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 120 patients with KOA treated at Tien Giang General Hospital from July to December 2025. rs4747096 genotyping and serum CRP measurement were performed, and radiographic severity was graded using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) classification. Severe KOA was defined as KL grade ≥III.

RESULTS: The mean age was 51.98 ± 10.24 years. KL grades II, III, and IV were observed in 66/120 (55.0%), 37/120 (30.8%), and 17/120 (14.2%) patients, respectively. KL grade distribution differed significantly by CRP category (p = 0.008), with grade IV disease more frequent in patients with CRP > 8.0 mg/L than in those with CRP ≤ 8.0 mg/L [12/49 (24.5%) vs. 5/71 (7.0%)]. Genotype frequencies were 41/120 (34.2%) for AA, 52/120 (43.3%) for AG, and 27/120 (22.5%) for GG. In univariable analysis, AG + GG genotypes (OR = 2.32; 95% CI, 1.05-5.13; p = 0.035) and CRP > 8.0 mg/L (OR = 2.67; 95% CI, 1.26-5.64; p = 0.009) were associated with severe KOA. In multivariable analysis, age ≥ 60 years (aOR = 4.59; 95% CI, 1.52-13.90; p = 0.007), overweight or obesity (aOR = 4.86; 95% CI, 1.96-12.06; p < 0.001), dyslipidemia (aOR = 2.81; 95% CI, 1.02-7.76; p = 0.047), and CRP > 8.0 mg/L (aOR = 3.43; 95% CI, 1.24-9.53; p = 0.018) remained independently associated with severe KOA, whereas rs4747096 did not.

CONCLUSION: Elevated CRP was independently associated with severe KOA, whereas the association with rs4747096 was attenuated after adjustment. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the independent role of this polymorphism.

articles.title: Therapeutic Potential of [(AP)2M]: A Rationally Designed Polyherbal Formulation for Antidiabetic and Antihyperlipidemic Effects in Alloxan-Induced Diabetic Mice.
articles.abstract: Medicinal plants are widely used in diabetes management due to their multi-targeted bioactive constituents. Phyllanthus emblica, Piper nigrum, Aegle marmelos, Moringa oleifera, and Azadirachta indica possess well-documented antidiabetic properties, providing a scientific basis for developing a rationally designed polyherbal formulation. This study evaluated the basic phytochemical characterization, antioxidant, antidiabetic, antihyperlipidemic, and preliminary toxicity profiles of a polyherbal formulation (designated as [(AP)2M]) in an alloxan-induced type 1 diabetic mouse model. Polyphenolic (phenolic and flavonoid) contents, antioxidant activity (DPPH & metal-chelating assays), and α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities were determined. Acute oral toxicity was assessed according to OECD Guideline 423, with LD50 estimation to establish the preliminary toxicity profile and effective dosing. Diabetic mice received the formulation [(AP)2M] (30-120 mg/kg) orally for 3 weeks, after which blood glucose, the lipid profile, SGPT, SGOT, and histopathological changes in the liver, kidneys, and pancreas were evaluated. The formulation exhibited substantial phenolic (111.52 ± 0.444 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid (211.30 ± 5.129 mg CAE/g) contents together with strong antioxidant and antidiabetic enzyme inhibitory activity. Acute oral toxicity assessment estimated an LD50 of 900 mg/kg (GHS Category 4). At 120 mg/kg, it reduced blood glucose to a level comparable with glibenclamide and significantly improved lipid profile, SGPT, and SGOT levels (p < 0.001). Histopathological examination demonstrated improvement in pancreatic, hepatic, and renal tissues. Since the formulation demonstrated promising antioxidant, antihyperglycemic, and antihyperlipidemic activities in a diabetic mouse model, it could be a potential alternative for further investigation as a complementary therapeutic approach for diabetes management.

articles.title: Ginsenoside CK, a major active metabolite of ginsenosides, ameliorates calcium overload-induced arrhythmias and myocardial oxidative injury by targeting CaMKII.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcium overload is a central pathological factor in cardiovascular disorders, including arrhythmia and myocardial injury. Recent studies suggest that ginsenoside metabolites may alleviate calcium overload; however, the principal active metabolite and its direct molecular target remain unclear.

METHODS: This study systematically screened the active components of enzymatically hydrolyzed total ginsenosides by integrating UPLC-Q/TOF-MS, principal component analysis, and calcium antagonistic activity assays. An alkynylated probe of the key active component was then synthesized for target identification using chemical biology approaches. Molecular biology methods were used to investigate the binding mechanisms. Rat models of arrhythmia and myocardial oxidative injury were further used to evaluate its pharmacological effects in vivo and to examine the associated signaling pathway.

RESULTS: The study revealed that the calcium antagonistic activity of ginsenosides was closely associated with secondary saponins, particularly ginsenoside CK (G-CK). CaMKII was identified as a key target through which G-CK alleviates calcium overload. G-CK bound to CaMKII and suppressed its autophosphorylation. Molecular biology experiments collectively supported an ATP-competitive mode of CaMKII inhibition by G-CK. Functionally, G-CK reduced intracellular calcium overload, attenuated mitochondrial Ca2+ accumulation and ROS generation, and ameliorated calcium overload-induced arrhythmia and myocardial oxidative injury in vivo.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify G-CK as a major active metabolite of ginsenosides that alleviates calcium overload-associated cardiac injury by targeting CaMKII. This work provides mechanistic insight into the cardiovascular protective effects of ginseng metabolites and suggests that G-CK may serve as a potential lead compound for the development of novel calcium antagonists.

articles.title: Baseline Clinical Predictors and Toxicological Drivers of In-Hospital Poisoning Mortality in Resource-Constrained Emergency Care: A Firth Penalized Regression Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding clinical characteristics and determinants of mortality among patients with acute poisoning in agricultural regions of Ethiopia remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate baseline clinical predictors associated with in-hospital mortality among acutely poisoned patients in a low-resource tertiary emergency department.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted among consecutive acute poisoning cases presenting to Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital (October 2022-September 2024). Of 372 screened cases, 7 patients who left against medical advice were excluded, yielding a final analytical cohort of 365 patients. Sociodemographic, toxicological, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was performed to minimize small-sample bias given sparse outcome events (15 deaths). A sensitivity model additionally adjusted for sex and rural residence.

RESULTS: The median age of patients was 22.0 years (IQR: 19.0-27.0); 230 (61.8%) were aged 15-24 years, 199 (53.5%) were female, and 245 (65.9%) were rural residents. Insecticides were the predominant poisoning category (157; 42.2%). Aluminum Phosphide (AlP) exposure occurred in 43 (11.6%) patients, resulting in 12 deaths (case-fatality rate: 27.9%; 95% CI 15.3%-43.7%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (15/365; 95% CI 2.3%-6.6%), with AlP accounting for 80.0% of all cohort deaths. In the primary multivariable Firth model, AlP exposure (aOR 30.48, 95% CI 7.88-117.95) and admission Glasgow Coma Scale < 15 (aOR 19.90, 95% CI 5.09-77.88) were strongly and independently associated with in-hospital mortality. These associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Impaired consciousness at admission (GCS < 15) and Aluminum Phosphide exposure serve as critical baseline indicators for rapid, low-cost risk stratification. While these exploratory parameters highlight high-risk groups, prospective multi-center validation across diverse hospital tiers is required before formal integration into clinical triage algorithms.

articles.title: Sepsis: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, and Management.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality despite advances in recognition, antimicrobial therapy, and organ support, reflecting its biological heterogeneity and the absence of broadly effective host-directed treatments. Here, we synthesize recent evidence across the three domains that define contemporary sepsis: epidemiology, pathophysiology, and management. Global and regional data indicate a persistently high but uneven burden, shaped by differences in case definitions, population structure, healthcare resources, and ascertainment. Mechanistically, sepsis is best viewed as an interconnected systems disorder in which hyperinflammation and immunoparalysis coexist with oxidative stress, endothelial and coagulation injury, immunometabolic dysfunction, gut dysbiosis, mitochondrial damage, and dysregulated programmed cell death, collectively driving organ dysfunction. Current management remains centered on timely antimicrobials, source control, individualized fluid and vasopressor therapy, corticosteroids, and organ support, while biomarker-guided immunotherapy and other host-directed strategies remain investigational. Recent randomized trials have mainly refined how established treatments are delivered rather than identified a universally effective new therapy. We also evaluate preclinical evidence for natural compounds targeting inflammatory and cell-death networks and highlight persistent methodological, pharmacokinetic, and translational barriers. Integrating rigorous phenotyping, mechanistic biomarkers, and guideline-based care may provide a more realistic path toward precision sepsis therapy.

articles.title: An 8-year-old boy with recurrent jaundice.
articles.abstract: An 8-year-old boy presented with recurrent jaundice since early infancy. He had normal growth and development and no clinical features of chronic liver disease. Investigations repeatedly demonstrated predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, with normal liver enzymes and preserved synthetic function. Haemolytic evaluation was negative, and abdominal ultrasonography showed mild hepatomegaly with normal echotexture, without biliary dilatation, gallstones, chronic liver disease, or portal hypertension. Whole-exome sequencing confirmed the diagnosis of Dubin-Johnson syndrome, a benign disorder due to defective bilirubin transport. The child remains clinically well, with stable biochemical parameters, and requires no specific treatment. This case highlights the importance of recognizing benign hereditary bilirubin transport disorders in children with isolated conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia and normal liver function, thereby avoiding unnecessary investigations and providing appropriate reassurance and counselling to families.

articles.title: La prise en charge des infections bactériennes de la peau et des tissus mous d'origine communautaire et la prévention des récurrences chez les enfants.
articles.abstract: Les infections de la peau et des tissus mous comptent parmi les maladies infectieuses les plus fréquentes chez les enfants. Leur gravité varie entre des infections simples spontanément résolutives et de graves syndromes nécrosants qui exigent la prise d'antibiotiques par voie intraveineuse, une intervention chirurgicale et des soins intensifs. Une barrière cutanée incomplète, découlant d'affections pédiatriques courantes comme l'eczéma et les abrasions cutanées, prédispose à l'infection. Lorsqu'il faut administrer des antibiotiques, le choix et la durée du traitement devraient dépendre des organismes les plus probables en cause, des profils de sensibilité possibles et des différences épidémiologiques selon les régions. Des traitements inappropriés au moyen d'antibiotiques à trop large spectre ou d'une durée trop prolongée sont nuisibles au microbiome, accroissent les effets secondaires des antimicrobiens, perpétuent la colonisation des organismes résistants et précipitent ainsi la résistance aux antimicrobiens. Le présent document de principes fournit aux prestataires de soins une boîte à outils pour la prise en charge optimale des infections bactériennes de la peau et des tissus mous, y compris les épisodes récurrents. Il n'aborde pas les principes thérapeutiques de ce type d'infections chez les patients immunodéprimés ou brûlés, en raison de la prise en charge complexe nécessaire dans ces deux contextes.

articles.title: Recommendations for transitioning diabetes, epilepsy, and ADHD youth. The TransiDEA Project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The transition from pediatric to adult health care is a critical yet often challenging process for young adults with chronic conditions, marked by fragmented communication, scarce resources, and a lack of standardized guidelines. The Italian TransiDEA project aimed to address these gaps by developing tailored transition recommendations for three clinical populations: young adults with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Type 1 diabetes (T1D), or epilepsy.

METHODS: Using a Delphi consensus method, three multidisciplinary panels including clinicians, young adults, caregivers, and association members were conducted in parallel, each addressing one of the three clinical targets. Participants assessed and revised the transition guidelines adapted from international frameworks over two rounds of evaluation.

RESULTS: After the first round, the overall agreement was above 75% for all three chronic conditions. The changes made to the statements based on the ratings and suggestions, led to high agreement (100%) in the second round.

DISCUSSION: The final recommendations share key elements, including early transition planning (starting around age 16), the assignment of a named transition worker, and using standardized tools (e.g., transition readiness questionnaires). Condition-specific adaptations addressed unique needs, such as psychological support in ADHD, tailoring the process on a case-by-case basis depending on the clinical picture in epilepsy, and extended transition timelines (up to age 22) in T1D.

CONCLUSION: The TransiDEA project demonstrates the feasibility of structured yet flexible recommendations for transition pathways across chronic conditions, while encouraging systemic improvements to enhance care continuity. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including the need for future validation of the guidelines and tools and increased resource and institutional support to ensure equitable access.

articles.title: Beyond the heart: supporting development in children and adolescents with complex CHD.
articles.abstract: Children and adolescents with complex congenital heart disease (CHD) face a high risk of neurodevelopmental challenges, including motor, language, cognitive, behavioural, and socio-emotional difficulties. Although the American Heart Association released statements in 2012 and 2024 outlining risk-stratified follow-up recommendations, access to systematic developmental monitoring remains limited in Canada.
