Only half of centers performing pediatric cardiac surgery offer structured follow-up, and services rarely extend beyond early childhood, despite evidence that many difficulties emerge at school age or adolescence. Neurodevelopmental concerns span motor delays, language impairments, executive dysfunction, attention deficits, learning disorders, and elevated rates of anxiety, depression, and behavioural problems. These challenges are more pronounced in children with severe CHD and in socioeconomically disadvantaged families, and are associated with parenting stress and parental mental health. This commentary aims to raise awareness among Canadian health care providers, support early identification, and guide appropriate referral pathways to the complex developmental needs of CHD survivors.

articles.title: Validation of the French version of the patient-reported outcome measure in pediatric chronic kidney disease (PRO-Kid).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Children living with chronic kidney disease (CKD) experience a high symptom burden. The PRO-Kid tool is a validated 14-item questionnaire for the assessment of symptom burden in youth aged 8 to 18 years living with CKD. The objective of this study was to evaluate the understandability of the French version of PRO-Kid.

METHODS: Participants were a cohort of French-speaking Canadian children aged 8 to 18 years living with CKD stage 3 to 5, including dialysis. Participants were recruited from the Montreal Children's Hospital and the Centre hopitalier universitaire Sainte-Justine (Montreal, Canada). The English version of the PRO-Kid was translated into French and back-translated to English by an accredited translator as well as two French-speaking investigators. Participants were asked to complete the French version of the questionnaire. Cognitive interviews were conducted to evaluate the understandability of the tool and relevance of each questionnaire item, and analyzed using NVivo.

RESULTS: Ten children completed the study, with a median age of 13 years (IQR, 11.7, 15.6). All children reported that the questionnaire was easy to complete. The participants' feedback revealed that no changes were warranted to the items, although some qualifiers were added to the item Itchiness (Démangeaisons) to improve clarity. Participants found the wording of the scale appropriate and easy to understand.

CONCLUSION: This study supports content and face validity of the French version of PRO-Kid (8 to 18 years old). This tool can now be implemented into CKD clinics for French-speaking children. It has the potential to improve communication between children with CKD and their health care providers.

articles.title: Online Updating Mixture Cure Models for Large-Scale Survival Data Streams.
articles.abstract: The growing availability of large-scale survival data streams present significant challenges for statistical inference particularly in the presence of a cure fraction, which complicates estimation and increases computational burden. To address these challenges, we propose an online updating mixture cure model framework. Our approach employs a batchwise renewable estimation procedure that aggregates historical information into summary statistics to update the model without retaining historical individual-level data, and thus eliminating the need for full data storage. A renewable penalized expectation-maximization algorithm is developed to enable simultaneous parameter estimation and variable selection. Furthermore, a tuning-free strategy is incorporated to enhance computational efficiency. The asymptotic properties of the proposed method are established. Simulation studies and an application to breast cancer data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database demonstrate the method's estimation accuracy, predictive performance, and computational scalability.

articles.title: From Framework to Toolkit: Practical Guidance for Using the PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) framework was developed to support systematic evaluation of Context, Fidelity, Dose, Reach, and an integrative assessment of Quality of Delivery (QoD). Its practical use, however, requires explicit guidance on selecting measures, constructing QoD, assessing changing context, and governing prospective use.

METHODS: We undertook a retrospective comparative synthesis of process evaluations embedded in four randomized U.K. critical care trials: Biomarker-guided antibiotic stewardship in suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAPrapid-2), Provision of Psychological Support to People in Intensive Care (POPPI), Sedation AND Weaning In CHildren (SANDWICH), and Alpha-2 agonists for sedation to produce Better outcomes from critical illness (A2B). We selected them because they informed POETIC's development or application and provided sufficiently detailed quantitative and qualitative evidence. We mapped the reports, protocols, and process evaluation findings to the five dimensions; compared recurring and contradictory patterns, quantitative-qualitative agreement, measurement and interpretation problems, and mechanism-specific limitations; and translated our learning into guidance for applying the framework.

RESULTS: The relevance and measurement of POETIC dimensions varied according to how each intervention was expected to work. Contextual influences changed over time and differed between sites. Combined assessments of QoD required explicit decisions about component selection, weighting, thresholds, aggregation, and missing data. VAPrapid-2 showed why a separate Dose measure and a QoD composite were not meaningful for a one-off diagnostic recommendation; POPPI used a weighted site composite; SANDWICH summarized delivery of four intervention components, staff training, and patient Reach; and A2B combined four equally weighted indicators in a 0-12 site score. This cross-trial learning informed practical guidance on selecting measures, assessing context over time, integrating quantitative and qualitative findings, constructing QoD, and governing prospective use.

CONCLUSIONS: POETIC is best used as a mechanism-aligned, mixed-method scaffold rather than a requirement to measure every dimension or calculate a universal composite. Prospective use is feasible when outputs, recipients, review times, permitted actions, and safeguards are prespecified. The framework and accompanying toolkit support reproducible assessment while protecting trial integrity.

articles.title: Genomic and Clinical Analysis of Influenza A in Hospitalized Adults, 2019-2024: Exploratory Evidence on Neuraminidase and Polymerase Acidic Protein Mutation-Outcome Associations From a Single Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antivirals are widely used to treat influenza, but potential resistance mutations remain a major challenge, and clinical data on key resistance mutations are limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 765 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A admitted to Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, between 2019 and 2024 to determine whether specific NA/PA mutations are associated with severe outcomes or prolonged length of stay (LOS) when analyzed alongside key host factors. PA and NA sequences were obtained and linked to the clinical cohort for mutation-clinical outcome analyses. Multiple testing was addressed by controlling the false discovery rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.

RESULTS: Among 765 inpatients with influenza A virus infection, the median age was 68 years; 5.0% were severe disease and 9.9% died. Older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, whereas antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Adjusted observational analyses showed a lower estimate for severe disease with baloxavir but no association with in-hospital death. Major high-level resistance mutations were absent; detected NA/PA mutations showed no robust association with severe disease or mortality. PA-F105L showed an exploratory association with longer LOS, but this finding was attenuated after adjustment and was confounded by clade and calendar period.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical outcomes were driven mainly by host factors and admission severity. Detected NA/PA mutations were not robustly associated with severe outcomes, while high-level resistance could not be assessed; PA-F105L-LOS association requires phenotypic and external validation.

articles.title: Pars plana vitrectomy with silicone oil versus pars plana vitrectomy alone for postoperative endophthalmitis: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The role of silicone oil (SO) tamponade in pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) for postoperative endophthalmitis remains controversial. This study compared outcomes of PPV with SO versus PPV alone in severe cases, incorporating intraocular cytokine profiling and regression analysis.

METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 40 eyes with post-phacoemulsification postoperative endophthalmitis unresponsive to initial intravitreal antibiotics were randomized to PPV alone (n = 20) or PPV with 1000-cSt SO tamponade (n = 20). The primary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included recurrence of infection, retinal detachment (RD), and intraocular cytokine levels (interleukin [IL]-6, IL-8). Correlation and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of final visual outcome.

RESULTS: Final BCVA improved more in the SO group (1.5 ± 0.3 logMAR) compared with the PPV-alone group (1.7 ± 0.4 logMAR), although this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.289). Recurrence was observed in two eyes (10%) within the SO cohort compared to eight eyes (40%) in the PPV-alone cohort (P = 0.021). At 8 weeks, intraocular cytokine levels were markedly reduced in the SO group (IL-6: 142 pg/mL vs. 298 pg/mL, P = 0.018; IL-8: 84 pg/mL vs. 176 pg/mL, P = 0.024). In the PPV-alone group, 8-week IL-6 levels strongly correlated with final BCVA (r = 0.712, P = 0.006). Multivariate regression identified recurrence of infection (β = 0.31, P = 0.009) and 8-week IL-6 levels (β = 0.001, P = 0.003) as independent predictors of worse visual outcomes.

CONCLUSION: PPV with SO tamponade significantly reduces recurrent infection and intraocular inflammation in severe postoperative endophthalmitis, leading to trends toward improved visual outcomes. These benefits appear mediated by both anti-infective and anti-inflammatory mechanisms, supporting the use of SO in complex cases.

articles.title: Pharmacological and Therapeutic Potential of Garlic (Allium sativum): Integrating Phytochemistry, Molecular Mechanisms, and Clinical and Preclinical Evidence.
articles.abstract: Garlic (Allium sativum) is a medicinal plant with diverse pharmacological properties and therapeutic potential in metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, immune, inflammatory, infectious, and neoplastic disorders. However, comprehensive integration of clinical and preclinical evidence remains limited. This review synthesized randomized controlled trials, crossover studies, therapeutic clinical investigations, and experimental animal studies evaluating garlic supplementation. Allicin was identified as the principal intermediate precursor generating numerous bioactive organosulfur compounds. Clinical evidence demonstrated reductions in systolic blood pressure of 5.2%-10.5% and diastolic blood pressure of 4.0%, decreases in LDL cholesterol of 11.8%-14.2% and total cholesterol of 7.6%-14.2%, and increases in HDL cholesterol of 11.5%. Fasting glucose decreased by 7.01 mg/dL, and HbA1c by 0.66%. Inflammatory markers, including TNF-α and C-reactive protein, declined by up to 24.7%, whereas antioxidant capacity increased. Preclinical studies demonstrated reduced tumor growth, improved renal function, enhanced epithelial regeneration, and increased survival in experimental infection models. Garlic demonstrates consistent therapeutic benefits across multiple conditions. Nevertheless, additional high-quality, large-scale clinical trials are required to establish optimal dosing, long-term safety, and clinical efficacy.

articles.title: Swallowing-Related Time Measured by a Neck-Worn Electronic Stethoscope and Its Associations With Age, Sex, and Masticatory Function in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Objective assessment of swallowing function in community-dwelling older adults remains challenging. A neck-worn electronic stethoscope (NWES) can measure swallowing-related time noninvasively. This study aimed to examine age- and sex-related differences in NWES-derived swallowing-related time metrics and their relationship with masticatory function.

METHODS: Older adults from the Itabashi Longitudinal Study on Aging in 2024 were included. Swallowing-related time was measured using NWES as pharyngeal clearance time (PCT), representing the duration of pharyngeal swallowing during water swallowing, and oral processing and swallowing time (OPST), reflecting the duration from oral processing to swallowing completion during cracker ingestion. Masticatory function was assessed using a gummy jelly test.

RESULTS: Four hundred and sixty-two participants (mean age 76.1 ± 3.4 years) were included. Median (interquartile range) PCT was 0.88 (0.70-1.01) s in men and 0.75 (0.61-0.92) s in women; corresponding OPST values were 34.51 (28.89-42.93) and 43.46 (34.33-54.09) s, respectively. PCT was significantly longer in men, whereas OPST was significantly longer in women. OPST correlated with age in men (r = 0.17) and women (r = 0.20). Masticatory function was not significantly associated with PCT in either sex. After adjustment for age, body mass index, number of functional teeth, stroke history, and PCT, higher masticatory function scores were significantly associated with shorter OPST only in men (B = -0.67).

CONCLUSION: NWES-derived PCT and OPST showed different associations with age and masticatory function, with OPST associated with age in both sexes and with masticatory function in men. PCT and OPST may offer practical approaches for evaluating oral processing performance in older adults.

articles.title: Nipah Virus (NiV) in Focus: Molecular Insights Into Pathogenesis, Transmission Dynamics, and Evolving Epidemiology From Malaysia to Recent Indian Outbreaks.
articles.abstract: Since the emergence of the Nipah virus (NiV) in Malaysia in 1998, it has returned multiple times and continues to pose a significant threat to global public health. It is characterised by high mortality and fatality rates and increasing evidence of human-to-human transmission. The epidemiological pattern of NiV has shifted considerably over the past 2 decades, from transmission primarily associated with infected pigs to repeated spillover events linked to Pteropus fruit bats, contaminated food sources, and close human contact. NiV infection is marked by severe respiratory involvement, immune dysregulation, acute encephalitis and widespread endothelial damage contributing to rapid clinical deterioration and poor outcomes. The World Health Organisation classified the Nipah virus as a priority pathogen with high mortality and pandemic potential, with recognised outbreaks showing case fatalities ranging from 40% to 100%. The virus has been detected in the Indian subcontinent and is carried by fruit bats. Recent outbreaks reported in India through 2026 have further highlighted the ongoing threat posed by the virus and the challenges of outbreak containment in densely populated regions. Current advances in serological and Molecular diagnostics have improved early detection; however, therapeutic options remain limited, and no licenced vaccine is currently available for human use. Ongoing therapeutics research involving monoclonal antibodies, recombinant vaccines, and antiviral agent platforms continues to expand the prospects for future prevention and disease control. Outbreaks must be prevented by prompt diagnosis and the application of infection control measures. However, the lack of knowledge regarding the pathophysiology, clinical features, and current treatment of Nipah virus disease makes it difficult to design such trials. The current advances summarised herein strengthen the scientific foundation for improved diagnostic platforms, antiviral interventions, vaccine development, and integrated One Health surveillance approaches targeting Nipah Virus.

articles.title: High-Fat Diet Intake Enhances Ultraviolet-Induced Melanin Production in the Skin.
articles.abstract: The intake of a high-fat diet (HFD) increases the risk of metabolic diseases such as obesity and type 2 diabetes and has also been associated with age-related changes in various organs. However, its effects on the skin remain poorly understood. Ultraviolet (UV) exposure is a major environmental factor that induces skin pigmentation through enhanced melanogenesis. However, little is known about the effects of HFD intake on UV-induced skin pigmentation. This study investigated whether HFD intake modulates UV-induced melanogenesis. HRM-2 mice were fed either a standard diet or an HFD for 5 weeks. The melanin content in the dorsal skin of UV-exposed HFD-fed mice (UV + HFD group) was significantly greater than that in the dorsal skin of UV-exposed mice fed a standard diet (UV group). The mRNA levels of tyrosinase (Tyr), dopachrome tautomerase (Dct), and tyrosinase-related protein-1 (Tyrp1) were higher in the UV + HFD group than in the UV group. The protein expression of TYR and microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF) was significantly greater in the UV + HFD group than in the UV group. HFD intake enhances the UV-induced upregulation of the expression of MITF and melanogenic enzymes, resulting in exacerbated skin pigmentation. These findings suggest that nutritional status may influence susceptibility to UV-induced pigmentation and that dietary modulation represents a potential strategy to control UV-induced hyperpigmentation.

articles.title: Efficacy of High-Frequency Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Therapy for Depression With Insomnia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Based on Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) in patients with comorbid depression and insomnia.

METHODS: This analysis incorporated 7 studies, involving 709 subjects (control: 342; repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [rTMS]: 367). All included studies employed left DLPFC-targeted HF-rTMS. Treatment effectiveness for comorbid depression and insomnia was assessed. Subgroup analyses were conducted to explore possible sources of heterogeneity.

RESULTS: HF-rTMS significantly improved sleep quality (standardized mean difference [SMD] [95% confidence interval (CI)]: 0.97 [0.23 to 1.71], p = 0.01) and depressive symptoms (0.61 [0.38 to 0.84], p < 0.00001). There was a non-significant trend toward reduced sleep latency (0.50 [-0.17 to 1.18], p = 0.14). No significant difference in adverse reactions was observed (risk ratio [95% CI]: 1.09 [0.80 to 1.48], p = 0.57). Substantial heterogeneity was identified for the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index outcomes (I2 = 91%). Subgroup analyses indicated that this heterogeneity was attributed to variations in stimulation frequency and baseline antidepressant use.

CONCLUSION: Very‑low to low certainty evidence suggests that left DLPFC‑targeted HF‑rTMS may improve sleep quality and depressive symptoms in patients with depression and insomnia symptoms, with a favorable safety profile. However, due to substantial heterogeneity and methodological limitations, these findings should be considered exploratory and warrant confirmation by future high‑quality trials.

articles.title: Predicting cardiovascular disease in peritoneal dialysis patients using glycated proteomics and machine learning: A prospective multicentre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients, yet PD-specific biomarkers and prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to identify glycated peptide biomarkers associated with CVD in PD patients and develop a prediction model integrating glycated proteomics and clinical indicators using machine learning.

METHODS: In Phase I, a matched discovery cohort (48 PD patients with CVD and 48 without CVD) was used to identify glycated peptides by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with glmnet used to prioritise candidate biomarkers. In Phase II, candidate biomarkers were quantified in a prospective internal derivation cohort (n = 240) and a multicentre external validation cohort (n = 102). The combined model was developed using F-test feature selection and elastic-net logistic regression. Its predictive performance was compared with three published cardiovascular risk models. Patients were stratified using a training-derived Youden cutoff.

RESULTS: In the discovery cohort, 257 glycated peptides were differentially abundant between groups. Four candidate biomarkers were prioritised, and two peptides, GEAFTLK(g)ATVLNYLPK and K(g)QHLFVK, were retained in the final model together with six clinical indicators: phosphate, diabetes, total Kt/V, albumin, cardiac troponin T, and glycated albumin. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.784 in the training set, 0.781 in the internal testing set, and 0.822 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Using the training-derived cutoff of 0.373, higher 1-year CVD incidence was observed in the high-risk group in both validation cohorts. The combined model also achieved higher ROC-AUCs than the published cardiovascular risk models.

CONCLUSION: We developed and externally validated a PD-specific CVD prediction model by integrating glycated peptide biomarkers with clinical indicators, which may facilitate earlier risk stratification and targeted prevention.

articles.title: Age-Related Differences in Decision-Making Roles and End-of-Life Care Trajectories Among Adults With Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As populations age, older adults represent a growing proportion of patients with cancer nearing the end of life. However, age-related differences in treatment decision-making and patterns of end-of-life care in routine cancer practice remain insufficiently described.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with cancer who received palliative care consultations at a tertiary hospital in Korea between 2018 and 2022. Clinical data were linked with national health insurance claims. Patients were categorized into five age groups (18-44, 45-64, 65-74, 75-84, and ≥ 85 years), and age-related differences in referral timing, decision-making roles, and end-of-life care patterns were examined.

RESULTS: Among 6151 patients, 54.3% were aged ≥ 65 years, including 3.3% who were aged ≥ 85 years. Older patients were referred earlier. Advance statements were completed by 59.2% overall, with the lowest completion (52.2%) and fewer patient-determined decisions to withhold or withdraw life-sustaining treatment (62.0%) in the oldest group. Intensive care unit admission rates were similar across age groups, while cardiopulmonary resuscitation and ventilation were less frequent among patients aged ≥ 85 years. Hospice use declined with age. Total medical costs during the last 6 months of life decreased with age yet remained considerable among older patients. Most deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals (26.9%-31.9%), while deaths in nursing care facilities increased with advancing age.

CONCLUSIONS: Although older adults were referred earlier to palliative care, they were less likely to make their own treatment decisions, and aggressive care remained common. These findings indicate a need for age-sensitive approaches to improve end-of-life care.

articles.title: From Daily Attitudes to Alcohol-Related Harm: A Within-Person Serial Mediation Test Informed by the Theory of Planned Behavior.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) posits that attitudes influence behavior through intentions, yet this pathway has not been thoroughly examined at the within-person level in the alcohol literature. This study tested whether daily fluctuations in attitudes toward heavy drinking predicted same-day alcohol-related consequences and alcohol-induced blackouts through a serial mediation involving daily drinking intentions and alcohol consumption.

METHODS: Participants were 87 heavy-drinking young adults (53.4% female; Mage = 22.22 years) enrolled in the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial who completed up to 30 consecutive days of morning diary assessments. Multilevel models separated within-and between-person variance by person-mean centering daily predictors. Serial mediation pathways were estimated using multilevel regression models, and specific indirect effects were tested using Monte Carlo confidence intervals.

RESULTS: On days when participants reported more favorable attitudes toward heavy drinking than their own average, they also reported stronger intentions to drink, which predicted greater same-day alcohol consumption. Greater drinking, in turn, predicted increased odds of both alcohol-related consequences and blackout. Significant serial indirect effects supported the hypothesized pathway from attitudes to consequences and blackout through intentions and drinking. Drinking intentions also directly predicted alcohol-related consequences independent of drinking quantity but did not directly predict blackout after accounting for drinking, suggesting differences in the mechanisms underlying these outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Findings provide day-level support for a TPB-informed pathway linking within-person fluctuations in drinking attitudes to alcohol-related harm through drinking intentions and alcohol consumption. Results extend prior between-person TPB research by demonstrating that attitudes and intentions function as dynamic, day-to-day processes that help explain when individuals are at elevated risk for harmful drinking outcomes. Daily attitudes and intentions may represent promising targets for ecological momentary interventions designed to reduce alcohol-related harm.

articles.title: Comment on "Antihyperglycemic Drugs and Risk of Asthma Exacerbation in Patients With Asthma and Type 2 Diabetes: A Multinational Retrospective Cohort Study".
Comparing the Risk of Maternal Complications and Adverse Infant Outcomes Among Pregnancies With and Without COVID-19 in the Sentinel System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, but knowledge about the timing of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy on these outcomes is limited.

OBJECTIVES: We implemented the CONSIGN protocol to examine the impact of COVID-19 on pregnancy-related complications and adverse infant outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: We identified eligible females with live-birth deliveries who had a COVID-19 diagnosis or a positive-confirmed test for SARS-CoV-2. Pregnancies with COVID-19 were propensity score (PS) matched 1:1 to pregnancies without COVID-19 during the 6 months prior to or during pregnancy.

RESULTS: From 2020 to 2023, we identified 69 901 pregnancies with COVID-19 and 1:1 matched pregnancies without COVID-19. Most pregnancies with COVID-19 were diagnosed in the third trimester (49%, 33 979/69 901) and < 5% (1860/69 901) were classified as severe. Pregnancies with severe COVID-19 in the first trimester had a higher rate of preterm delivery, and pregnancies with severe COVID-19 in the second trimester had a higher rate of cesarean section compared to those without COVID-19. No increased risk of adverse infant outcomes was observed among 22 865 linked mother-infant pairs with COVID-19 although a slightly increased risk of low birth weight was noted among pregnancies exposed to severe COVID-19 in the third trimester.

CONCLUSION: Among nearly 70 000 live-birth pregnancies with COVID-19, severe COVID-19 was associated with cesarean section and preterm delivery. No association with adverse infant outcomes was noted. Our study enabled assessment of the timing and severity of COVID-19 on adverse pregnancy outcomes, although changing treatment and prevention recommendations might impact trends of these outcomes.

articles.title: Advances in Pediatric Hepatology-2027 Update.
Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Children.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease among children and adolescents worldwide. Pediatric MASLD is associated with significant morbidity during childhood, including progressive liver fibrosis and incident diabetes, and significantly increases risk of premature mortality in early adulthood. In comparison to MASLD in adults, youth-onset MASLD exhibits distinct histologic patterns, lacks well-validated noninvasive tests for risk stratification and approved pharmacotherapy, and may carry higher risk of long-term liver-related mortality. Critical areas of unmet need include improving rates of recommended screening, development of pediatric-specific risk stratification tools and developing more effective prevention and treatment strategies.

articles.title: Gestational Alloimmune Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Gestational alloimmune liver disease (GALD) is a top cause of neonatal acute liver failure that is highly preventable in subsequent pregnancies after the index case. The understood mechanism involves placental passage of maternal antibodies targeting an unknown fetal hepatocyte antigen, leading to complement activation and extensive hepatocyte damage and fibrosis. This disease mechanism explains the clinical presentation of liver failure shortly after birth. Intravenous immunoglobulin and double volume exchange transfusion can improve neonatal outcomes, likely due to dampening the effect of circulating maternal antibodies. Early recognition of GALD depends on a high index of clinical suspicion.

articles.title: Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Fontan-associated liver disease develops in nearly everyone living with Fontan physiology, most commonly presenting with asymptomatic hepatic fibrosis. Guidelines for monitoring for progression of disease and risk factors for more severe disease are not well described. Collaboration between cardiologists, hepatologists and surgeons from both pediatric and adult medicine backgrounds in the management of these patients are necessary to provide the best care for these complex patients.

articles.title: Intestinal Failure-Associated Liver Disease: Current Understanding and Recent Advances.
articles.abstract: Intestinal failure (IF) can result from diverse etiologies, including surgical interventions and congenital defects, often leading to parenteral nutrition dependence. IF-associated liver disease (IFALD) is a serious and life-threatening complication of IF. IFALD is multifactorial leading to cholestasis during phase I, and steatosis and fibrosis during phase II. Diagnosis and screening remain challenging due to the lack of consensus criteria, and management requires a multidisciplinary intestinal rehabilitation approach. Despite these challenges, outcomes including survival and quality of life of patients with IF have improved over the past decade leading to lower rates of liver and small bowel transplants.

articles.title: Emerging Role of Activated T cells in Pediatric Acute Liver Failure.
articles.abstract: Activated T-cell hepatitis (TC-Hep) is an immune-mediated liver disease that presents in children aged 1 to 17 years with jaundice and high aminotransferases; severity ranges from severe hepatitis to acute liver failure (ALF). Many children previously labeled indeterminate ALF can be reclassified as TC-Hep. TC-Hep patients have liver tissue with diffuse portal and lobular CD8 T-cell inflammation and peripheral blood markers of T-cell activation. Treatment includes supportive care and consideration of immunosuppression, with optimal regimens yet to be determined. TC-Hep is not a chronic or recurrent disease, but patients are at a uniquely increased risk of developing aplastic anemia.

articles.title: Cystic Fibrosis-Associated Hepatobiliary Involvement.
articles.abstract: Cystic Fibrosis-associated Hepatobiliary involvement (CFHBI) refers to a wide range of liver and biliary-related clinical and/or biochemical abnormalities that impact people with cystic fibrosis. Advanced cystic fibrosis liver disease (aCFLD) describes individuals with advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis and/or portal hypertension. The current review discusses both CFHBI and aCFLD in terms of pathogenesis; clinical, imaging and biochemical manifestations; screening, monitoring, and management recommendations; and the impact of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy.

articles.title: Genetic and Familial Forms of Pediatric Intrahepatic Cholestasis.
articles.abstract: This review explores the expanding landscape of genetic and familial forms of pediatric intrahepatic cholestasis-noting a pivot from the labeling of discrete progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis disorders to a classification system based on mechanistic understandings of the specific genetic and molecular etiologies that lead to the wide-ranging spectrum of cholestatic phenotypes. This review suggests a novel pediatric intrahepatic cholestasis classification-by the mechanism of etiology-and reviews new and emerging advancements in the management of cholestasis and progression of liver disease.

articles.title: Positive Impact of Hypertension in Patients with Early-stage Lung Cancer Treated With Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: This study aimed to analyze the effect of hypertension on recurrence and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with early-stage lung cancer who underwent curative stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study included 100 patients with T1-T3N0M0 lung cancer who underwent lung SBRT using CyberKnife or volumetric-modulated arc therapy at Inha University Hospital between July 2008 and June 2025. Recurrence rates and PFS were analyzed. Data on hypertension and specific types of antihypertensive medications were retrospectively reviewed from electronic medical records.

RESULTS: The median follow-up period was 31.0 months (range=0.7-136.7 months). Of the 100 patients, 52 had hypertension. Recurrence occurred in 38 patients, including 25 with locoregional failure and 13 with distant metastases. Recurrence rates were significantly lower in patients with hypertension (p=0.015), with reduced locoregional recurrence (p=0.022), whereas distant metastasis showed no significant correlation with hypertension (p=0.315). Hypertensive drug users (n=37) had lower recurrence rates (p=0.003). Recurrence was higher in male patients (p=0.049) and lower in those aged >70 years (p=0.033). Patients with hypertension showed significantly improved PFS (p=0.010) but no difference in overall survival based on hypertension status (p=0.319). Other factors that positively affected PFS included female sex and age >70 years. Patients actively receiving antihypertensive medication showed greater PFS than those who did not (p=0.016). In particular, those using beta-blockers showed a low recurrence rate (0%, p=0.033).

CONCLUSION: The therapeutic effects of lung SBRT appear more pronounced in patients with hypertension. This favorable outcome may be related to the administration of antihypertensive medications, suggesting the need for further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Detection of locoregional lymph node (LN) metastases is a critical prognostic factor in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is limited by insufficient specificity, potentially leading to overtreatment. We evaluated gallium-68 fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI-04) positron-emission tomography (PET)/CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in this setting, using CT as comparator.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT scans of 15 patients with gynecologic SCC (nine cervical, six vulvar carcinomas; mean age 56.3 years, range=38-86 years) were analyzed. PET/CT and CT were read independently by two blinded readers. Histopathology and/or clinical and radiological follow-up (12-18 months) served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was calculated on a patient-based level; maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were compared using Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test.

RESULTS: Histopathological confirmation was available in 12 patients; three were classified by follow-up. LN metastases were confirmed in five patients. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieved a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and accuracy of 100%. CT achieved a sensitivity and NPV of 100% but produced false-positive findings in three patients (specificity=70%, PPV=62.5%, accuracy=80%), caused by tattoo-associated lymphadenopathy, sarcoidosis and reactive nodal enlargement, none of which showed pathological tracer uptake. Metastatic LNs exhibited higher SUVmax (mean 23.2±6.0) than nodes false-positive on CT (mean 4.5±4.6; p=0.004 and p=0.036). Primary tumors were visualized in all patients undergoing initial staging; peritoneal nodules down to 7 mm were detected.

CONCLUSION: In this small cohort, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed a higher observed specificity than contrast-enhanced CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in gynecologic SCC, with no false-negative cases observed.

articles.title: Cranial and Spinal Epithelioid Hemangioma: Systematic Review and Illustrative Calvarial Case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Cranial and neuraxial epithelioid hemangioma (EH) is exceptionally rare and anatomically heterogeneous. We systematically reviewed reported cerebral, cranial osseous, primary non-osseous spinal epidural, and vertebral-origin EH with clinically relevant neuraxial extension and present an illustrative hypervascular calvarial case.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Electronic searches of MEDLINE via PubMed were supplemented by Google Scholar, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, publisher archives, conference/supplement searches, and backward and forward citation tracking through 19 August 2026. Histologically confirmed EH involving brain parenchyma, cranial bone with relevant intracranial or craniovertebral extension, primary non-osseous spinal epidural space, or vertebral bone with secondary intraspinal/foraminal extension was eligible.

RESULTS: Twenty-two reports were included: 14 (63.6%) vertebral-origin and eight (36.4%) cerebral, combined calvarial-cerebral, cranial osseous, or primary non-osseous spinal epidural. Surgery was reported in 19/22 publications (86.4%), radiotherapy in 10/22 (45.5%), and preoperative embolization in 3/22 (13.6%). Recurrence, progression, or new post-treatment disease was explicitly described in three reports, but heterogeneous follow-up precluded pooled recurrence estimates. The illustrative 32-year-old man had a histomorphologically diagnosed hypervascular parasagittal calvarial EH compressing a patent superior sagittal sinus and underwent Onyx embolization followed by excision and cranioplasty.

CONCLUSION: Cranial and neuraxial EH is rare, with published evidence dominated by vertebral disease. Management should be individualized according to anatomical compartment, neural compression, structural instability, and vascularity. Histological distinction from epithelioid hemangioendothelioma and angiosarcoma is essential, while the available evidence is insufficient to establish comparative efficacy of radiotherapy or embolization.

articles.title: Semaglutide and Panic Attacks: Active-Comparator Disproportionality Analysis, Temporal Assessment of Notoriety Bias and Evidence Triangulation in Post-Marketing Pharmacovigilance.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate how confounding by indication and notoriety bias shape the apparent semaglutide-panic attack signal in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and to interpret this signal using an evidence-triangulation framework integrating randomized and observational studies.

METHODS: We conducted an active-comparator restricted disproportionality analysis of FAERS (2018Q1-2024Q4), including individual case safety reports in which semaglutide, dulaglutide or empagliflozin was the primary suspect drug. Panic attack was identified using the MedDRA preferred term. Crude and adjusted reporting odds ratios (RORs, aRORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using logistic regression, adjusting for age, sex and indication (Type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight management). Notoriety bias was assessed using prespecified temporal analyses (analyses restricted to reports received before July 1, 2023 and a drug-by-period comparison of 2018-2022 with 2023-2024) and reporting proportions per 10 000 reports. A sensitivity analysis used all other primary-suspect drugs in FAERS as the reference set. In parallel, we conducted a systematic review (MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL to November 24, 2025) of randomized trials, cohort and cross-sectional studies, pharmacovigilance analyses and case reports reporting panic attacks or acute anxiety outcomes with semaglutide.

RESULTS: Among 33 267 semaglutide, 54 282 dulaglutide and 25 380 empagliflozin reports, panic attacks were recorded in 87 (0.26%), 28 (0.05%) and 13 (0.05%) cases, respectively. Crude RORs were 5.08 (95% CI 3.32-7.78) versus dulaglutide and 5.12 (95% CI 2.86-9.17) versus empagliflozin, attenuating after adjustment to 2.82 (95% CI 1.74-4.56) and 2.75 (95% CI 1.41-5.36). In the pre-warning period crude RORs were 2.24 (95% CI 1.23-4.07) and 2.15 (95% CI 1.00-4.58), attenuating to 1.38 (95% CI 0.69-2.75) and 1.14 (95% CI 0.48-2.68) after adjustment. Panic-attack reports per 10 000 semaglutide reports rose from 6.7 in 2018-2022 to 42.0 in 2023-2024 (drug-by-period interaction p = 0.007). Against all other primary-suspect drugs, the aROR was 1.48 (95% CI 1.18-1.87) overall and 0.76 (95% CI 0.48-1.18) before July 1, 2023. Across 12 studies, randomized trials and active-comparator observational cohorts did not show a consistent increase in panic attacks or anxiety-related outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Crude FAERS analyses suggested a semaglutide-panic attack signal that attenuated after adjustment was no longer significant before the July 2023 regulatory communication and rose sharply thereafter in a pattern consistent with notoriety bias. Triangulation with randomized trials and active-comparator observational studies does not support a consistent pharmacological association. Disproportionality analyses are hypothesis-generating and cannot estimate incidence or establish causality. This case study illustrates how active-comparator design, temporal assessment of notoriety bias and evidence triangulation can improve the interpretation of post-marketing safety signals.

articles.title: Measuring the impact of migraine: a systematic review of the measurement properties of MIDAS, HIT-6, and MSQoL.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migraine is a leading cause of global disability. Valid, reliable instruments are essential for quantifying its impact. The Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS), Headache Impact Test (HIT-6), and Migraine-Specific Quality-of-Life questionnaire (MSQoL) are widely used, yet their comparative measurement properties across populations remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and compare the measurement properties of MIDAS, HIT-6, and MSQoL following the Consensus-Based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) methodology.

METHODS: This systematic review followed the COSMIN guidelines for systematic reviews of outcome measurement instruments and was reported per the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-COSMIN guideline. In total, seven databases were searched from study inception to January 31, 2025, restricted to English-language full-text studies. Methodological quality was appraised with the COSMIN Risk of Bias checklist; results were rated against criteria for good measurement properties, and evidence was graded using a modified Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

RESULTS: Of 2,674 records, 22 studies (20,455 participants) were included. All three instruments showed sufficient internal consistency and construct validity. The HIT-6 showed sufficient ratings across all properties (moderate-to-high quality evidence). Also, the MIDAS showed sufficient core properties but limited responsiveness and inconsistent reliability across cultural versions. Finally, MSQoL showed sufficient structural validity and internal consistency but insufficient test-retest reliability.

CONCLUSION: Both HIT-6 and MIDAS can be recommended for measuring migraine impact (Category A), whereas MSQoL shows potential but requires further reliability and responsiveness research (Category B). A combined approach is recommended for comprehensive migraine burden evaluation.

articles.title: Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) levels in the cerebrospinal fluid have neither been validated as a reliable diagnostic marker nor sufficiently studied in patients with tropical diseases and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)ADA levels in different central nervous system (CNS) infections, define a cutoff value, and assess correlations between CSF-ADA and other laboratory parameters.

METHODS: In 206 patients whose CSF-ADA levels were measured, we analyzed data on baseline characteristics, diagnoses, CSF-ADA levels, and additional laboratory parameters. These CSF-ADA levels were compared according to microbiological diagnosis, and correlations with other CSF and blood parameters were analyzed.

RESULTS: Compared with the non-CNS infectious control group (n = 40), 2 subgroups showed significantly higher CSF-ADA levels: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (n = 45, p < 0.0001) and Neisseria meningitidis (n = 11, p = 0.0400). The identified cutoff values were 5.5 and 7.3 IU/L for M. tuberculosis and CNS coinfections, respectively. For M. tuberculosis, sensitivity was 61.2% and specificity was 72.4%, whereas coinfections demonstrated 50% of sensitivity and 82.8% of specificity. The CSF-ADA levels correlated positively with CSF protein (Spearman rank correlation coefficient [rs] = 0.3009, p < 0.0003) and weakly correlated negatively with CSF glucose (rs = -0.1895, p < 0.0254). Patients with M. tuberculosis infection exhibited significantly higher CSF-ADA levels, as reflected by the mean, median, and standard deviation, than those with other infectious etiologies combined (n = 121) and those with bacterial and viral infections analyzed separately (p < 0.05). When stratified according to HIV status, a significant difference in CSF-ADA levels was observed only among patients with varicella-zoster virus infection (p = 0.0428).

CONCLUSION: The CSF-ADA levels were elevated in tuberculous and meningococcal meningitis. Higher cutoff values may occur in CNS coinfections. Therefore, CSF-ADA may serve as a supportive diagnostic tool in cases of suspected TBM, meningococcal meningitis, and CNS coinfections.

articles.title: Biologic therapy: A paradigm shift in asthma management.
Biologic therapy: A paradigm shift in asthma management.
articles.abstract: Biologic medications provide opportunities to improve the health, safety, quality of life, and long-term outcomes of patients with moderate-to-severe uncontrolled asthma. This article provides primary care nurse practitioners with an overview of the pathophysiology of Type 2 inflammation in asthma, the mechanism of action of biologics approved for asthma, monitoring considerations, and practice considerations.

articles.title: Time-resolved coherent X-ray scattering analysis of nanorod colloids: dynamics and photon-statistical effects in angular X-ray cross-correlation analysis.
articles.abstract: Understanding the dynamic fluctuations of anisotropic particles is essential for elucidating the mechanisms of order formation through self-organization. Because anisotropic particles possess both translational and rotational degrees of freedom, their dynamics are intrinsically more complex than those of spherical particles. Time-resolved coherent X-ray scattering has the potential to probe such complex dynamics. Translational motion can be evaluated by X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS), whereas orientational information can be extracted using the angular X-ray cross-correlation function (AXCCF). In this study, we investigated dynamic fluctuations in a colloidal nanorod system at concentrations near the coexistence region of isotropic and liquid-crystalline phases using time-resolved coherent X-ray scattering at 17.4 kHz. XPCS analysis revealed a pronounced slowing down of translational motion as the isotropic phase approached the liquid-crystalline phase. To examine possible temporal fluctuations in orientational order near the coexistence region, we applied a statistical approach based on AXCCF and principal component analysis. Temporal variations were indeed observed in the AXCCF. However, quantitative analysis showed that the magnitude and distribution of these variations are largely explained by photon-counting statistics expected for coherent scattering under low-count conditions. Although the present experiment did not provide definitive evidence for intrinsic orientational fluctuations beyond statistical noise, the analysis establishes an important framework for evaluating the detectability of orientational dynamics in time-resolved coherent X-ray scattering experiments and provides practical guidance for future measurements and validation.

articles.title: [Iodinated and gadolinium-based contrast agents and kidney disease: consensus statement of the Austrian Society for Radiology (OERG) and the Austrian Society of Nephrology (ÖGN)].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Iodinated and gadolinium-based contrast agents are indispensable in radiological diagnostics; however, they were previously considered problematic in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) due to potential side effects. Study data from the past 15 years have led to the realization that the nephrotoxic potential of contrast agents has been overstated and that a reassessment is warranted. This consensus paper aims to standardize the intravascular use of contrast agents in the CKD population in a practical manner, based on scientific evidence and international guidelines, enabling both optimal diagnostic yield and maximum patient safety.

METHODS: The Austrian Radiological Society (OERG) and the Austrian Society of Nephrology each nominated four experts in a working group to draft consensus guidelines regarding the safe use of contrast agents in patients with impaired kidney function. Following an initial meeting of this working group a literature search was conducted in various medical databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials) and pertinent guidelines of various international specialist societies were identified. The scientific work and guidelines were evaluated in five further meetings of the working group. The recommendations for the safe use of contrast agents were compiled in a consensus.

RESULTS/CONSENSUS: The recommendations could be summarized in 11 consensus statements. In addition, an algorithm for the administration of iodinated contrast agents in patients with impaired kidney function was created.

CONCLUSION: This consensus paper, endorsed by the OERG and ÖGN provides a standardized approach for the intravascular administration of contrast agents in individuals with CKD. Emphasis is placed on the diagnostic benefits of a contrast agent-assisted investigation in comparison to the potential risk of an associated kidney damage.

articles.title: Long-term gynecological symptoms and ultrasound and reproductive outcomes after monofilament vs multifilament uterine closure at Cesarean delivery: secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term gynecological symptoms and reproductive and ultrasound outcomes among women originally enrolled in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing monofilament and multifilament sutures for uterine closure after Cesarean delivery.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a RCT including women who underwent Cesarean delivery, who were originally assigned to monofilament or multifilament absorbable sutures for uterine closure. In this secondary analysis, participants were contacted 4-6 years after delivery and invited to a follow-up evaluation, comprising a clinical interview and a voluntary transvaginal ultrasound examination. The primary outcome was the presence of postmenstrual spotting at long-term follow-up. Secondary outcomes were other gynecological symptoms, reproductive outcomes and ultrasound outcomes. Analyses were performed according to the original randomized allocation. Effect estimates are reported as relative risk (RR) with 95% CI.

RESULTS: Of the 300 women included in the original RCT, 117 (39.0%) were included in the long-term follow-up analysis, comprising 51 in the monofilament group and 66 in the multifilament group. There was no significant difference in the primary outcome of postmenstrual spotting between the monofilament and multifilament groups (23.5% vs 22.7%; RR, 1.04 (95% CI, 0.53-2.01)). Similarly, no significant differences were observed between groups for other gynecological symptoms. Ultrasound data were available for 21 women, of whom 13 had a Cesarean-scar defect. The overall prevalence of Cesarean-scar defects was similar between groups, although defects ≥ 4 mm were more frequent in the multifilament group (RR, 0.42 (95% CI, 0.18-0.97); P = 0.04). Most reproductive outcomes, including infertility and pregnancy outcomes among women who conceived, were comparable between groups. However, subsequent pregnancy occurred more frequently in the monofilament group (29.4% vs 12.1%; RR, 2.43 (95% CI, 1.12-5.27)).

CONCLUSIONS: In this long-term follow-up of a RCT, monofilament and multifilament sutures for uterine closure were associated with similar long-term gynecological symptoms. Differences observed in selected ultrasound and reproductive outcomes should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size and exploratory nature of these analyses. Further studies are needed to better evaluate the potential impact of suture material on long-term reproductive outcomes and sonographic Cesarean-scar characteristics. © 2026 The Author(s). articles.title: Postoperative Pain Treatment After Pancreatic Surgery: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analyses and Trial Sequential Analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major pancreatic surgery is associated with significant postoperative pain that impairs early mobilisation and recovery. ERAS guidelines for pancreaticoduodenectomy recommend multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, with a strong recommendation for epidural analgesia and continuous wound infiltration as an alternative. Other techniques may be beneficial, but their efficacy and safety remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy and adverse events of different postoperative analgesic modalities for patients undergoing total pancreatectomy, pancreaticoduodenectomy and distal pancreatectomy.

DATABASES AND DATA TREATMENT: This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (ID CRD420251085003) reported in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. A search for randomised controlled trials was conducted in Medline, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and Embase. Meta-analyses were performed in Review Manger, risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, trial sequential analyses were performed, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs comprising 1468 patients were included, and 10 meta-analyses were performed. Meta-analyses demonstrated reduced pain scores at rest on postoperative day (POD) two with COX-inhibitors compared with placebo/no intervention. Pain scores were similar when comparing epidural analgesia with less invasive strategies (paravertebral block and wound infiltration) on POD1-POD2, but lower with the less invasive techniques on POD3. Meta-analyses were small, and GRADE recommendations ranged from very low to low.

CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence was insufficient to establish the superiority of any single analgesic strategy after major pancreatic surgery. Several analgesic strategies, including COX inhibitors, paravertebral block and continuous wound infiltration, showed promising results. Larger RCTs are needed to provide stronger evidence-based recommendations.

SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Epidural analgesia has long been considered the gold standard for treatment of postoperative pain after major pancreatic surgery. The present review adds to the field by demonstrating that less invasive strategies as continuous wound infiltration and paravertebral block provide comparable pain scores in the first postoperative days, with a significantly lower score on postoperative day three. This supports positioning less invasive strategies as viable alternatives to epidural analgesia.

articles.title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
articles.abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., 111Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation Burden as an Outcome in Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: AbstractAtrial fibrillation is the most common cardiac arrhythmia in the world. In clinical trials evaluating interventions for atrial fibrillation, outcomes have been traditionally defined using a thirty second arrhythmia end point. In this Clinical Trials Workshop, we evaluate the role of atrial fibrillation burden as a primary outcome for atrial fibrillation intervention trials. In particular, we evaluate key considerations for ascertainment, definition, and analysis of atrial fibrillation burden while further considering regulatory implications of its use as a primary end point.

articles.title: Next-Generation Bed Nets to Control Malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Next-generation long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) treated with more than one insecticide have been insufficiently evaluated in West Africa.

METHODS: In this cluster randomized clinical trial, 33 clusters of villages (1-3 villages per cluster) in Côte d'Ivoire were randomly assigned (11 clusters per group) to use pyrethroid-only (py-only; MAGNet) (control), piperonyl butoxide-pyrethroid (PBO-py; Veeralin), or chlorfenapyr-pyrethroid (CFP-py; Interceptor G2) LLINs. One net was distributed for every two people, followed by door-to-door visits to assist with hanging the nets and to promote their use. The primary outcome was the incidence of malaria cases among children aged 6 months to 9 years over the year following net distribution. Incidence rate ratios compared cases per child-year between clusters randomly assigned to use PBO-py versus py-only nets and CFP-py versus py-only nets.

RESULTS: A total of 25,660 LLINs were distributed to 11,283 households (py-only, n=3797; PBO-py, n=3559; and CFP-py, n=3927). The primary outcome analyses included 549, 551, and 549 children in the py-only, PBO-py, and CFP-py groups, respectively. Mean malaria incidence over 12 months was 1.11 cases per child-year in the py-only group (control), 0.84 in the PBO-py group, and 0.65 in the CFP-py group. The incidence rate ratios were as follows: PBO-py versus py-only nets, 0.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.99; P=0.045); and CFP-py versus py-only nets, 0.57 (95% CI, 0.43 to 0.75; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Malaria incidence over 12 months was significantly reduced among children aged 6 months to 9 years residing in clusters of villages in Côte d'Ivoire that were randomly assigned to use CFP-py versus py-only LLINs and PBO-py versus py-only LLINs. (Funded by The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05796193.).

articles.title: E-Cigarettes with and without Behavioral Support for Smoking Cessation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trials that have shown that e-cigarettes are effective in helping people quit smoking typically provided behavioral support in addition to e-cigarettes. Behavioral support is not always available or wanted, but it is not known whether e-cigarettes are effective without it.

METHODS: Participants who smoked and were motivated to quit were randomly assigned to National Health Service SmokeFree automated email messages (supportive messages), an e-cigarette starter pack alone (EC-only), or an e-cigarette starter pack plus multisession telephone-based behavioral support (EC+). The primary outcome was biochemically validated sustained abstinence from smoking at 6 months. Participants who were lost to follow-up or did not provide biochemical validation were assumed to continue to smoke. A significance level of 0.025 was prespecified for each of the two primary comparisons (EC-only vs. supportive messages and EC+ vs. EC-only).

RESULTS: The 6-month abstinence rates were 6.4% in the supportive messages group, 11.3% in the EC-only group (EC-only vs. supportive messages relative risk 1.76; 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 1.03 to 3.01; P=0.018), and 21.1% in the EC+ group, (EC+ vs. EC-only relative risk 1.87; 97.5% CI, 1.27 to 2.75; P<0.001). Serious adverse events were reported by 8.1%, 10.8%, and 10.7% of participants in the supportive messages, EC-only, and EC+ groups, respectively. There were four deaths, two in the EC-only group and two in the EC+ group.

CONCLUSIONS: E-cigarettes without further support were more effective than supportive messaging in helping people achieve sustained validated abstinence from smoking at 6 months. E-cigarettes with multisession telephone-based support were more effective than e-cigarettes alone. (Funded by The National Institute for Health and Care Research Health Technology Assessment programme (NIHR129627); ISRCTN number, 61193406.).

articles.title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
articles.abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

articles.title: [Regional network for advanced heart failure in Tuscany: analysis of referrals and patient pathways for heart transplantation and left ventricular assist device implantation (2020-2025)].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced heart failure requires regional care pathways capable of identifying patients before clinical deterioration prevents access to heart transplantation (HTx) or left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. The available data mainly describe patients who have already been selected for, or treated with, advanced therapies, whereas analyses of the entire referral are less frequent. The aim of this study was to describe referral volume, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of patients referred to the Tuscany regional center for evaluation for HTx and/or LVAD implantation in the period 2020-2025, with specific attention to temporal referral trends and distribution of INTERMACS profiles.

METHODS: Prospective observational registry including 468 consecutive adult patients referred to the regional reference center between January 2020 and December 2025. INTERMACS profile was assigned during the initial assessment. Candidacy for advanced therapies, pathway status of eligible patients, and temporal trend in INTERMACS groups 1-3, 4-5, and 6-7 were analyzed.

RESULTS: During the observation period, a significant increase in referral volume between 2020-2022 and 2023-2025 was observed (incidence rate ratio 1.46; 95% confidence interval 1.22-1.76; p<0.001). The distribution of aggregated INTERMACS profiles changed over time, with an increase in profiles 6-7 from 3.3% to 20.9% and a reduction in profiles 4-5. Overall, 340 patients (72.6%) were potentially eligible for advanced therapies. Of these, 144 patients, corresponding to 30.8% of the entire cohort, were considered candidates for HTx and/or LVAD. Of these, 123 (36.2%) were listed for HTx, including 5 patients with LVAD support as bridge to transplant. Among listed patients, 75 (61.0%) underwent transplantation, 46 (37.4%) remained on the active waiting list, and 2 (1.6%) died while on the waiting list. Twenty patients underwent LVAD implantation as destination therapy and 1 patient as bridge to candidacy (21 patients in total, corresponding to 6.2% of eligible patients) and 130 eligible patients (38.2%) remained under follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In this regional experience, the number of referrals to the reference center increased over time. The increasing representation of INTERMACS profiles 6-7, along with the reduction in profiles 4-5, is consistent with earlier patient management. These results demonstrate the consolidation of the regional network for advanced heart failure, but multicenter studies with systematic follow-up are needed to evaluate its impact on clinical outcomes.

articles.title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
articles.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

articles.title: [Advanced heart failure: definition, epidemiology, diagnosis and treatment].
articles.abstract: Advanced heart failure represents the most severe and complex stage of a chronic and progressive clinical syndrome that remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in industrialized countries. A substantial proportion of patients progress to a condition characterized by persistent symptoms, recurrent episodes of decompensation, and marked functional impairment despite optimized medical therapy and the appropriate use of cardiac devices. This advanced stage is associated with a considerable clinical, healthcare, and economic burden, together with a profound negative impact on the quality of life of both patients and caregivers. Early recognition of advanced heart failure remains a major challenge in everyday clinical practice, partly due to the heterogeneity of clinical presentations. Consequently, increasing clinician awareness, establishing standardized diagnostic criteria, and implementing dedicated care pathways are essential to ensure timely identification and appropriate patient management. In this context, the present review aims to provide an updated overview of advanced heart failure, with a particular focus on diagnostic criteria, currently available therapeutic strategies, and the most effective organizational models for optimizing the care of this complex and high-risk patient population.

articles.title: [Multimodality imaging in heart failure: phenotyping and clinical decision-making].
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a global health priority traditionally managed based on ejection fraction (EF). However, EF is now recognized as insufficient to represent the pathophysiological complexity and clinical heterogeneity of the syndrome. Modern diagnostics have shifted toward multimodality imaging, acting as an integrated platform for phenotyping. Transthoracic echocardiography remains the first-line tool, evolving into a multiparametric approach that includes global longitudinal strain, right ventricular-arterial coupling assessment, and congestion monitoring via lung ultrasound and venous excess ultrasound. Cardiac magnetic resonance is the gold standard for tissue characterization, which is crucial for etiological definition and arrhythmic risk stratification through fibrosis identification (late gadolinium enhancement). Cardiac computed tomography is essential for coronary anatomy evaluation and procedural planning, while nuclear imaging (single-photon emission computed tomography/positron emission tomography) provides unique insights into metabolism, inflammation, and sympathetic innervation. Integrating these modalities, guided by clinical questions, enables personalized therapeutic management, tracking of disease trajectories (such as improved HF), and optimization of clinical decision-making.

articles.title: [2026 ESC heart failure guidelines: what really changes from 2021?].
Age-Period-Cohort Analysis on Diabetes Awareness among Koreans: 2010-2023 Korea Community Health Surveys.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: While increasing age is known to be associated with a greater prevalence of diagnosed diabetes, or diabetes awareness, period and cohort effects on diabetes awareness remains unclear. We estimated the age-period-cohort effects on diabetes awareness among community-dwelling Koreans using a mechanism-based approach.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data from 3208979 2010-2023 Korea Community Health Survey participants were used for analysis. Age was grouped at 2-year intervals (19-20 to 99-100), period at 1-year intervals (2010 to 2023), and cohort at 5-year intervals (1910-1914 to 2000-2004). Diabetes awareness was defined as the self-reported doctor-diagnosed diabetes. Subgroup analyses stratified by household income, body mass index (BMI), sex, and region of residence were conducted. Sensitivity analyses with alternative age and cohort intervals and an analysis using the 2010-2023 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) diabetes prevalence data were conducted.

RESULTS: Age effect increased significantly after 40, peaking at the 77-78 interval [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 9.39, 95% confidence interval (CI) 8.45-10.44]. Period effect was significantly higher since 2011, peaking in 2023 (aOR 1.49, 95% CI 1.43-1.54). Cohort effect was significant in 1935-1959 (aORs 1.14-1.33) and 1985-2004 (aORs 1.12-1.35). The participants with high household income showed significant cohort effect in older generations, and the participants with low household income showed significant cohort effect in younger generations. The participants with BMI ≥25 kg/m² showed significant cohort effect in younger generations. Analyses using different categorization intervals showed consistent results. Sensitivity analyses using KNHANES showed consistent age and period effects.

CONCLUSION: Age, cohort, and period effects significantly influenced diagnosed diabetes prevalence in the Korean community.

articles.title: Quantification of Aortic Cusp Parameters Using Computed Tomography in Valve-Sparing Aortic Root Replacement Surgery: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Determining the feasibility of valve-sparing aortic root replacement (VSRR) requires accurate preoperative assessment of aortic valve cusp geometry. However, the reliability of computed tomography (CT) for measuring cusp parameters remains unclear. This study evaluated the agreement between CT-derived cusp measurements and intraoperative measurements and explored the potential of CT-based cusp asymmetry to predict intraoperative cusp plication.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 32 consecutive patients undergoing VSRR with the reimplantation technique were enrolled. Preoperative CT was used to measure cusp free margin length and geometric height. Agreement between CT-derived and intraoperative measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). An exploratory analysis evaluated whether CT-derived cusp asymmetry predicted the need for intraoperative cusp plication.

RESULTS: CT measurements demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative measurements for cusp free margin length (ICC 0.80-0.87). In contrast, geometric height showed only moderate agreement (ICC 0.44-0.69). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminative ability of CT-derived cusp asymmetry for predicting intraoperative cusp plication (area under the curve, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.49-0.91), although the association did not reach statistical significance (p=0.06). Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated none-to-mild aortic insufficiency in 96.9% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative CT demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative measurements for cusp free margin length in tricuspid valves, although the absolute limits of agreement were wide. CT-based quantification of cusp asymmetry may provide additional information for preoperative surgical planning; however, its association with intraoperative cusp plication remains exploratory and requires validation in larger studies.

CLINICAL RESEARCH INFORMATION SERVICE (CRIS) REGISTRATION NUMBER: KCT0006180.

articles.title: Molecular Epidemiology of Varicella-Zoster Virus Among Patients From Two French Tertiary Care Hospitals: Differential Distribution of Clades According to Demographic Criteria.
articles.abstract: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) nomenclature currently recognizes seven established clades (designated 1-6 and 9). A geographical segregation of VZV clades has been shown, with Clades 1, 3, and 6 predominating in Europe, Americas, and Australia, Clade 2 in Japan and East-Asia, and Clades 4 and 5 in Asia and Africa. This distribution of VZV clades is dependent on the importation of viral strains, because of immigration and travels, and the implementation of varicella vaccine. The surveillance of VZV epidemiology is therefore necessary. VZV genotyping strategies rely on evaluating a panel of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) across the different open reading frames (ORFs) of the viral genome. We described retrospectively the VZV clade distribution among 339 patients in Pitié-Salpêtrière (Paris) and Bordeaux University hospitals from 2018 to 2023. Clade 1 was detected in 27.1%, Clade 3 in 37.2%, Clade 5 in 31.9%, and other clades in 3.8% of the patients. The distribution of clades did not differ according to sex, immune status of the patients, and clinical presentation of VZV infection.
