However, patients infected with Clade 5 were statistically younger than those infected with other clades, especially European-born patients. This epidemiological characteristic of VZV Clade 5 may have multifactorial etiology, including the combination of viral, host, and environmental factors.

articles.title: The X-ray crystallographic structure of a designed, self-assembling, and heme-binding protein.
articles.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
articles.abstract: De novo heme-binding proteins offer powerful minimal scaffolds for elucidating how sequence, oligomerization, and environment rule cofactor coordination, yet high-resolution structural data for these systems remain scarce. Here, we report the high-resolution crystal structure of a designed, self-assembling α-helical and heme-binding protein determined at 1.9 Å resolution, that undergoes a pronounced pH- and cofactor-driven reorganization. The structure crystallized in the orthorhombic P212121 space group (a = 44.8 Å, b = 46.3 Å, c = 101.2 Å), with one tetramer per asymmetric unit and refinement statistics of Rfac/Rfree = 23.5/25.5%. The apo protein folds into a three-stranded coiled coil, whereas heme binding under strongly basic conditions disrupts register-specific interactions and drives a major helix shift. This transition yields a four-stranded coiled coil with an out-of-register ABAB arrangement that accommodates two bis-histidine-ligated hemes. Cofactors are His-coordinated via the ε-nitrogen (Fe-NHis ≈ 2.0 Å), separated by 38 Å (tetrapyrroles edge-to-edge) and arranged nearly coplanar with a 67° rotation offset relative to one another. Imidazole dihedral angles (99° and 108°) indicate near-orthogonal geometry for the His axial ligands to the heme. Crystallization is promoted by a heme-templated packing in which interactions between macrocycles of neighboring assemblies and several salt-bridges generate an extended supramolecular lattice. These results demonstrate how heme binding and proton concentration reshape oligomeric topology and promote ordered assembly in minimal protein systems, highlighting the varied structural effects of heme binding and providing principles for stabilizing specific coordination and exploiting cofactor-cofactor interactions to guide high-order organization in de novo metalloproteins.

articles.title: Geometry-aware modeling with cellPACK for evaluating spatial trends in intracellular organization.
articles.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
articles.abstract: Cells appear extraordinarily complex, yet aspects of their organization may arise from a small number of influences acting within geometric constraints. Here, we extend and use cellPACK, an open-source framework for rule-based spatial modeling, to compare observed and simulated 3D distributions of peroxisomes and endosomes (puncta) in human induced pluripotent stem cells. Simulations conditioned on observed cell and nuclear geometries along with puncta counts show that geometric variation can generate apparent structure in organelle localization, highlighting the need to account for geometry when interpreting spatial statistics. We therefore employ an occupancy-based metric that normalizes puncta density by available intracellular volume, revealing modest enrichment near the nuclear surface against an otherwise near-uniform cytoplasmic distribution. We use these occupancy patterns to fit combinations of predefined spatial bias models and evaluate the resulting 3D packings against observed data. To support open and reproducible modeling while enabling a more intuitive visual exploration, we present cellPACK Studio, a browser-based interface that allows users to generate, modify, and visualize the 3D cell packings used in this study (available at cellpack.allencell.org). Together, these results and tools illustrate how spatial modeling can transform descriptive imaging data into testable, interpretable hypotheses of intracellular organization.

articles.title: Clinical Efficacy of Low-Intensity Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Male Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Retrospective Pilot Study.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-intensity extracorporeal shock wave therapy (Li-ESWT) using the Morenova system in men with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), including chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS), and to identify pretreatment factors associated with post-treatment symptom severity.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 61 men treated with Li-ESWT. The treatment was administered once weekly for six consecutive weeks. Symptom severity was assessed before and one month after treatment using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS), Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Impact Index (BII), and National Institutes of Health Chronic Prostatitis Symptom Index (NIH-CPSI). Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify pretreatment factors independently associated with the post-treatment NIH-CPSI total score after adjustment for baseline NIH-CPSI.

RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed in total IPSS (from 11.1 to 7.3), OABSS (from 3.8 to 2.8), BII (from 4.9 to 2.7), and NIH-CPSI (from 11.8 to 7.0) (all p < 0.001). Notably, pain improved significantly in patients with baseline pain (from 4.1 to 1.8, p < 0.001). Post-micturition dribbling improved in approximately one-third of patients. Higher PSA and lower baseline OABSS were independently associated with lower post-treatment NIH-CPSI scores after adjustment for baseline NIH-CPSI. No adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Li-ESWT was associated with improvements across voiding, storage, pain, and QOL domains, with no adverse events observed. These findings suggest that Li-ESWT may have potential as a treatment option for male LUTS, although prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm its efficacy.

articles.title: Real-world implementation of AI-assisted PERT-workflow and its association with care processes and budget impact: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. In intermediate-high and high-risk PE, timely escalation beyond anticoagulation is critical, yet real-world pathways are often delayed. Pulmonary embolism response teams (PERTs) improve decision-making, but activation remains inconsistent. Whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled triage strengthens PERT and improves acute PE care has not been elucidated so far.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively screened 2500 patients presenting to our university hospital with a symptomatic central or segmental PE between 08/2022 and 07/2024. Clinical and economic outcomes were compared during a 1-year timeframe before and after implementation of an AI algorithm that analyses CT scans, flags suspected PE, and supports PERT triage. 424 patients met inclusion criteria. AI-supported triage increased PERT activation from 9.2% to 84.5% (P < 0.001). Time from CT completion to PE diagnosis decreased from 2.1 to 1.3 h (P < 0.01). Time from PE diagnosis to interventional therapy was reduced by 50% (P < 0.05). Hospital/ICU length-of-stay and 30-day mortality showed non-significant reductions. Model-based economic analysis showed lower 1-year per-patient costs and annual savings associated with AI-supported PERT.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of an AI-supported PERT workflow was associated with significant improvements in PE care processes, including higher PERT activation rates and shorter diagnostic and treatment intervals. Numerical reductions in mortality, hospital/ICU length-of-stay did not reach statistical significance. The exploratory budget impact model suggested potential cost savings, mainly driven by trends in reduced resource utilization; however, these findings require prospective validation using adequately powered clinical endpoints.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Perceived Organizational Justice and Workplace Alienation Among Nurses in Northern Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Perceived organizational justice may influence nurses' workplace alienation. This study examined the relationship between perceived organizational justice and workplace alienation among nurses in Northern Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 183 nurses working in government hospitals in the Al-Jouf region, Saudi Arabia. Participants completed the Colquitt Organizational Justice Scale and the Work Alienation Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, group-comparison tests, and simple linear regression.

RESULTS: Mean perceived organizational justice was 4.04 (SD, 0.39) and mean workplace alienation was 2.71 (SD, 0.47), each scored from 1 to 5. Perceived organizational justice was inversely associated with workplace alienation (   r = - 0.455    ,   p < 0. 001    ). Perceived organizational justice explained 20.7% of the variance in workplace alienation (    R 2 = 0.207    ,   p < 0. 001    ).

CONCLUSION: Higher perceived organizational justice was associated with lower workplace alienation among nurses. Longitudinal research is needed to examine temporal and causal relationships.

articles.title: Kidney Pathology of Megalin Deficiency in Adulthood.
articles.abstract: Megalin belongs to the large low-density lipoprotein receptor--related protein subfamily and is pivotal in the tubular reabsorption of low-molecular-weight proteins freely filtered through the glomerular filter. Megalin deficiency is an ultrarare inherited disease (faciooculoacousticorenal or Donnay-Barrow syndrome) mostly diagnosed in childhood. In this study, we report an exceptional case of biallelic mutations in LRP2, the gene encoding the endocytic receptor megalin, diagnosed in a 51-year-old woman and characterized by chronic kidney disease (CKD) with incomplete proximal tubule dysfunction, moderate sensorineural hearing loss, severe myopia, and convergent strabismus. Kidney biopsy showed mild interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy but severe glomerulosclerosis. Other causes of CKD were ruled out. This case highlights the following aspects: (1) although megalin is mainly recognized as a key factor of proximal tubule physiology, megalin deficiency was associated with predominantly glomerular scarring lesions in humans, promoting slowly progressive CKD similar to mouse models; (2) megalin can contribute to podocyte physiology; and (3) LRP2 should be included in kidney gene panels for the evaluation of nephropathy of unknown origin, even in adulthood.

articles.title: Spontaneous ureteral rupture secondary to distal ureteric stone presenting as perinephric urinoma: A case report of a rare urological emergency.
articles.abstract: Spontaneous ureteral rupture is a rare complication of obstructive uropathy that may mimic infection and delay diagnosis. We report a 48-year-old man with persistent left flank pain initially treated as pyelonephritis. Imaging showed worsening hydronephrosis and perinephric fluid. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a <3 mm distal ureteric stone at the ureterovesical junction with contrast extravasation, confirming ureteral rupture and urinoma. The patient underwent emergency ureteral stenting followed by delayed ureteroscopy and lithotripsy, with complete recovery. Early CT imaging and prompt decompression are essential for accurate diagnosis and optimal outcomes in such cases.

articles.title: Acute Angina in Anomalous Left Main Coronary Artery With Prepulmonic Course: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Although a prepulmonic left main coronary artery is usually considered a lower-risk AAOCA subtype, it may still be associated with acute ischemic symptoms when significant atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is present. Multimodality imaging is essential for defining the coronary anatomy, and coronary artery bypass grafting may be the preferred strategy when severe multivessel disease coexists.

articles.title: Intracranial phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor mimicking meningioma and causing tumor-induced osteomalacia: a case report.
articles.abstract: A 32-yr-old woman presented with a 2-year history of progressive bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, worsening ambulation, and bilateral hip insufficiency fractures without preceding trauma. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe hypophosphatemia (1.1 mg/dL), elevated bone-specific alkaline phosphatase, progressive secondary hyperparathyroidism, and inappropriately elevated circulating FGF-23, with fasting paired serum and urine studies confirming renal phosphate wasting (tubular maximum phosphate reabsorption per glomerular filtration rate 1.88 mg/dL; fractional excretion of phosphate 14.6%), consistent with tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO). Functional imaging with 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrated intense tracer uptake in a small anterior cranial lesion. Brain MRI revealed a dural-based olfactory groove lesion interpreted radiographically as a meningioma. Selective venous sampling demonstrated a cranial-to-peripheral gradient in intact FGF-23 consistent with drainage from the anterior cranial fossa. Surgical resection produced postoperative normalization of FGF-23 and rapid correction of hypophosphatemia. Histology showed meningioma-like architecture with whorls and psammoma bodies, but expanded molecular testing did not identify canonical meningioma-associated alterations, and DNA methylation profiling classified the lesion as a mesenchymal neoplasm not elsewhere classified and fusion negative. FGF-23 in situ hybridization was positive, and the final surgical pathology diagnosis was mesenchymal tumor favoring phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor over meningioma. This case illustrates how a mesenchymal tumor arising in the meninges can mimic meningioma radiographically and histologically while producing the endocrine phenotype of TIO.

articles.title: The Prescription Pattern, Care-Seeking Behavior and Glycemic Status Among the Diabetic Patients in a Tertiary-Level Hospital of Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The prevalence of diabetes mellitus is on the rise globally, presenting a significant challenge to healthcare systems, particularly in developing countries like Bangladesh. However, treatment modalities, care-seeking attitudes and clinical profiles among these patients are not well explored. This descriptive cross-sectional study examines the prescription patterns, care-seeking behavior and glycemic status among the diabetic patients in a tertiary-level hospital in Bangladesh.

METHODS: A total of 231 previously diagnosed type II diabetic patients from outpatient services, comprising 129 males and 102 females, were approached using a well-structured questionnaire. Socio-demographic characteristics, along with physical activity, tobacco smoking, adherence to a diet chart, and consultation with pharmacists, were obtained through participants' recall. 'Patients' biochemical parameters, such as blood pressure and glucose level were also taken into consideration.

RESULTS: The majority of respondents were in the 40-59 age group (55.8%), with a mean age of 50.67 ± 11.9 (SD) years. On average, 4.23 ± 1.23 (mean ± SD) drugs were prescribed for the management of diabetes and its comorbidities. A moderate correlation (r = 0.546, p < 0.01) was found between the average number of drugs and patients mean age. A single antidiabetic drug was prescribed to 121 patients (52.4%), two drugs to 82 (35.5%), and three drugs to 28 patients (12.1%) only. Although antidiabetic medications were prescribed, uncontrolled glycemic control was reported in 186 patients (80.5%). A weak association was found between glycemic status and the types of antidiabetic therapy among the diabetic patients, with a chi-square statistic of 6.10 (p < 0.01). Mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and fasting and 2-h postprandial blood glucose levels were significantly higher in aged diabetic patients (p < 0.001). The majority of participants (211, 91.3%) followed the diet chart advised by their physicians, which was associated with better control of diabetes-related complications (χ2 value 3.36, p < 0.1).

CONCLUSION: Given the heavy drug burden and comorbidities, these findings support regular glycemic monitoring, timely review and adjustment of medication, adherence to diet and lifestyle counseling, and closer attention to aged diabetic patients. The insights from this research may provide valuable guidance to healthcare providers and policymakers in devising patient-centered treatment strategies for the diabetic patients in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Epidemiology of hospitalized strongyloidiasis in Japan: A nationwide administrative database study.
articles.abstract: Strongyloidiasis remains endemic in parts of Japan, particularly Okinawa Prefecture, and can progress to disseminated disease with high mortality; however, nationwide data on hospitalized patients, including regional differences and the impact of disseminated disease, are limited. We conducted a retrospective nationwide study using the Diagnosis Procedure Combination database to identify hospitalized patients with strongyloidiasis in Japan between fiscal years 2014 and 2020, using ICD-10 code B78, with disseminated cases defined as B78.7. Demographic characteristics, geographic distribution, and outcomes were analyzed, with a focus on disseminated disease and regional differences between Okinawa and other areas. After excluding duplicate cases, 252 hospitalized patients were included (mean age, 77.6 years; male-to-female ratio, 1.47). Most patients were from the Kyushu and Okinawa regions, with Okinawa accounting for 82.1% of cases. Disseminated strongyloidiasis was identified in 44 patients (17.5%) and was associated with poorer neurological status at admission and higher in-hospital mortality; 11 patients with disseminated disease died during hospitalization (25.0%). Severe complications, including sepsis (54.5%) and meningitis (25.0%), were frequently observed in disseminated cases. Patients hospitalized outside Okinawa were younger than those hospitalized in Okinawa, whereas the proportions of disseminated disease and in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between regions. In Japan, hospitalized patients diagnosed with strongyloidiasis were predominantly concentrated in Okinawa; however, severe cases also occurred in other regions. These findings highlight the importance of considering strongyloidiasis in patients with relevant epidemiological backgrounds, particularly in the setting of immunosuppression, regardless of their current geographic location.

articles.title: Real-world effectiveness of liraglutide in children with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Since liraglutide's approval for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D) in children, no real-world studies have examined its clinical outcomes in adolescents.

OBJECTIVE: Compare hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) changes in adolescents with T2D taking liraglutide in a clinical setting.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study from 2020 to 2023.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients with T2D ages <18 years who were prescribed liraglutide. Patients were divided into 2 groups: treated (those with evidence of taking liraglutide for ≥26 weeks) and control (those prescribed but who did not take liraglutide).

MAIN OUTCOMES: Changes in HbA1c after 26 weeks of treatment were calculated. Secondary outcomes included HbA1c changes after 52 weeks, and body mass index (BMI) z score changes and lipid markers at 26 and/or 52 weeks.

RESULTS: There was a strong trend toward a decrease in HbA1c after 26 weeks of liraglutide treatment compared with control (-0.40 [-1.90, 0.20] vs +0.15 [-1.30, 0.88], P = .064; n = 85 vs n = 30); no difference was observed at 52 weeks (-0.20 [-1.23,0.93] vs 0.50 [-1.13,1.70], P = .15; n = 100 vs n = 44). BMI z score was stable in both groups, with no differences between groups. Lipid levels were available in a small subset of patients. The liraglutide-treated group had a decrease in total cholesterol (-0.21 [-0.60, 0.16] mmol/L vs 0.49 [0.06, 0.76] mmol/L, P = .005; n = 36 vs n = 12) and low-density lipoprotein (-0.23 [-0.56, 0.16] mmol/L vs 0.35 [0.14, 0.63] mmol/L, P < .01; n = 31 vs n = 12) vs control.

CONCLUSION: Liraglutide shows potential benefits for lowering HbA1c and cholesterol in children with T2D in a clinical setting. Additional work is needed to understand how to optimize HbA1c improvements with liraglutide.

articles.title: Microbiological Spectrum and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in Tubo-Ovarian Abscesses Managed by Surgery or Drainage at a Tertiary Hospital in Vietnam: A Retrospective Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Tubo-ovarian abscess requires empirical antimicrobial therapy before culture results are available, but local antimicrobial resistance data are limited in Vietnam. We described the microbiological spectrum and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of tubo-ovarian abscesses managed by surgery or drainage.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of 66 patients with tubo-ovarian abscess who underwent surgery or drainage and had procedure-obtained abscess material submitted for culture at Nhan Dan Gia Dinh Hospital from January 2021 to May 2025. Antimicrobial susceptibility data were summarized for recovered isolates when available. Descriptive statistics and Wilson 95% confidence intervals were used for key proportions. Antimicrobial susceptibility was summarized using the number of isolates tested for each agent as the denominator.

RESULTS: The analytic sample comprised 66 surgically treated or drained patients. Culture positivity was 43.9% (29/66; 95% CI, 32.6%-55.9%), with 39 bacterial isolates reported. Escherichia coli was the most frequent isolate (19/39, 48.7%), followed by Streptococcus spp. (9/39, 23.1%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (7/39, 17.9%). Among E. coli isolates, 6/19 (31.6%) were extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producers and 1/19 (5.3%) was an AmpC producer. Resistance among tested E. coli isolates was 13/14 (92.9%) to ampicillin, 7/14 (50.0%) to ceftriaxone, and 10/19 (52.6%) to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Antibiotic-specific denominators were small and variable.

CONCLUSION: Tubo-ovarian abscesses managed by surgery or drainage in this Vietnamese case series frequently yielded enteric Gram-negative organisms and streptococci, with substantial E. coli resistance to commonly used agents among tested isolates. These findings support procedure-obtained abscess culture, local antibiograms, clinically indicated anaerobic coverage, and antimicrobial stewardship; they should not be generalized to all patients with tubo-ovarian abscess.

articles.title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength.

OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional.

PARTICIPANTS: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728).

EXPOSURE: CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3).

OUTCOME MEASURES: Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis.

METHODS: Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated.

RESULTS: Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women.

CONCLUSION: In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

articles.title: Association of SDF-1β (rs1801157) and TCF7L2 (rs12255372) Gene Polymorphisms With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in the Bangladeshi Population: A Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has a strong genetic component and variations in specific gene alleles can significantly influence individual susceptibility. Stromal cell-derived factor-1 beta (SDF-1β) plays a crucial role in inflammatory responses, glucose regulation, and the maintenance of pancreatic β-cell function, while TCF7L2, a key regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway, governs insulin secretion and overall glucose homeostasis. The present study evaluated the association of the SDF-1β rs1801157 and TCF7L2 rs12255372 polymorphisms with T2DM development in the Bangladeshi population.

METHODS: In this case-control study, 140 clinically diagnosed T2DM patients and 95 healthy controls, were enrolled after obtaining approval from the institutional ethics committee. Genomic DNA was genotyped for SDF-1β (rs1801157) and TCF7L2 (rs12255372) SNPs using PCR-RFLP, with MspI used for SDF-1β digestion and MluCI for the TCF7L2 fragment. The resulting genotypes were then identified through agarose gel electrophoresis. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was tested in both groups. Genotype and allele frequencies were compared using Fisher's exact test, with crude and adjusted (for age, sex, BMI) odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: All genotype distributions were in the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Using the homozygous dominant genotype (GG) as the reference, a statistically significant association was observed for SDF-1β (rs1801157) with the AA genotype (p < 0.05), whereas TCF7L2 (rs12255372) showed no significant association. Additionally, the allele frequency distributions for both SDF-1β and TCF7L2 did not differ significantly between cases and controls (p > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The SDF-1β (rs1801157) AA genotype was significantly less frequent among T2DM patients, suggesting a possible protective association, whereas TCF7L2 (rs12255372) showed no such association. Given the modest sample size and limited statistical power, these findings indicate a possible association rather than a definitive marker of susceptibility and require replication.

articles.title: SLE Complicated With AIHA and Parvovirus B19 Infection Secondary to PRCA: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a woman in her 30s with SLE and AIHA who developed parvovirus B19 infection and secondary PRCA. Hemoglobin did not increase significantly after IVIG treatment; her condition improved significantly following the addition of foscarnet, providing a practical treatment option for secondary PRCA.

articles.title: Suspected Gluteal Epithelioid Sarcoma Complicated by Secondary Infection and Sciatic Neuropathy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Secondary infection can coexist with and obscure an underlying soft-tissue sarcoma. A deep mass that persists or progresses despite drainage and appropriate antibiotics, especially with progressive neurological deficit, warrants image-guided core biopsy and sarcoma-center referral before further surgery.

articles.title: Diabetic Retinopathy Risk in SGLT2i vs GLP1RA Initiators With CKD Stages 3-4 and Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1RA) have demonstrated renal and cardiovascular benefits among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, their comparative effects on diabetic retinopathy (DR) outcomes in patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D remain unclear. This study aimed to demonstrate the effect of SGLT2i vs GLP1RA in this population.

STUDY DESIGN: Population-based, new-user, active comparator cohort study comparing SGLT2i versus GLP1RA initiators. Subjects were divided into 2 cohorts: (1) incident nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) and (2) DR progression cohort.

SETTING & STUDY POPULATION: Patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D across 3 US health care databases: Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database (2014-2024), Merative MarketScan (2014-2022), and Medicare Fee-for-Service (2014-2020).

SELECTION CRITERIA FOR STUDIES: Adults with a new prescription for either SGLT2i or GLP1RA without prior use in the preceding 365 days. The primary outcomes were incident NPDR and DR progression, identified through ICD-9/10 diagnosis codes and procedural codes for retinopathy treatments.

DATA EXTRACTION: Exposures, covariates, and outcomes were obtained from structured claims fields.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Both cohorts were analyzed using propensity score matching (1:1) to control for confounding. Incidence rates (IRs), rate differences, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated.

RESULTS: After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 20,135 matched patient pairs in the incident NPDR cohort and 7,763 matched pairs in the DR progression cohort. For incident NPDR, there was no difference between SGLT2i and GLP1RA groups (IR 29.55 vs 30.38 per 1,000 person-years, respectively; HR 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87-1.10]). Similarly, DR progression was not different between groups (IR 32.73 vs 35.24 per 1,000 person-years; HR 0.92 [95% CI, 0.76-1.12]). Subgroup analyses showed no differences in HRs for both incident NPDR and DR progression across multiple predefined subgroups.

LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding, outcome misclassification, and limited generalizability to non-U.S. populations.

CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of SGLT2i was not associated with a different risk of incident NPDR or DR progression compared with GLP1RA among patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D. Additional studies with extended follow-up are needed to better characterize long-term retinal safety profiles of these therapies.

articles.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Traditional Uvulectomy: A Study Done Among Infants at University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional uvulectomy remains a significant public health concern in Ethiopia. Despite multiple complications associated with this traditional malpractice like bleeding and infection transmission the practice continues. This traditional practice is more commonly performed on infants. This study provides evidence on the prevalence and associated factors of traditional uvulectomy.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of and associated factors for traditional uvulectomy among infants under 12 months of age who visited the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, 2024/2025.

METHOD: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among infants under 12 months of age who visited the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital from August 2024 to January 2025. A pretested, researcher-administered questionnaire was used to interview caregivers and extract data from medical records. The data were collected using the Kobo Toolbox by two trained general practitioners and analyzed using STATA version 17 software. Binary and multivariable logistic regressions were employed to determine factors associated with traditional uvulectomy and the presence of multicollinearity was checked and no value more than 3 was there. The statistical association between dependent and independent variables was declared at p-value of ≤ 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 426 participants were included in this study, with ages ranging from 3 days to 12 months and a median age of 3 months (interquartile range [IQR] = 0.9-9 months). The prevalence of traditional uvulectomy was 69.7%. Among the participants, poor maternal knowledge and poor attitude were prevalent, accounting for 69.3% and 65.3%, respectively. Identified factors for traditional uvulectomy were: mothers with no postnatal counseling (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 3.08, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.65-5.73), mothers with poor attitude (AOR = 4.41, 95% CI: 1.87-8.96), and mothers with poor knowledge (AOR = 8.30, 95% CI: 3.70-18.61) toward traditional uvulectomy. The model had good performance, with a Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test p-value of 0.236.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of traditional uvulectomy was high. Lack of postnatal counseling about traditional uvulectomy, poor attitude, and poor knowledge were found to be independent contributing factors for traditional uvulectomy. Practicing comprehensive and consistent parental and postnatal health education and counseling about traditional uvulectomy is very important to overcome this malpractice.

articles.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.
articles.abstract: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

articles.title: Potential harms to rescuers during cardiac arrest response and resuscitation: a scoping review.
authors: International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Basic Life Support Task Force†
International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Basic Life Support Task Force
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rescuer safety during cardiac arrest response and resuscitation is an important consideration that may influence willingness to intervene. This scoping review identifies potential unintentional harms to rescuers responding to cardiac arrest and performing resuscitation.

METHODS: This scoping review was reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched EMBASE, Medline, and Cochrane from inception to June 16, 2026, including all human studies reporting physical harms during cardiac arrest response or resuscitation (compressions, ventilation, defibrillation). Two investigators screened studies and extracted data. Synthesis was guided by Joanna Briggs Institute methods, with narrative synthesis by harm category.

RESULTS: Twenty studies were included: sixteen provided direct evidence from cardiac arrest or resuscitation, and four provided indirect evidence from elective cardioversion. Of the direct-evidence studies, nine examined infection transmission during CPR, two evaluated electrical exposure from implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) during CPR, two reported physical injuries en route to arrest, and three documented drowning during rescue. Infection transmission rates varied by pathogen but were mitigated by personal protective equipment (PPE). CPR near implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) showed potential for higher leakage. In the four indirect-evidence studies, current leakage to rescuers during external shocks delivered for elective cardioversion remained below safe thresholds. One study reported minor injuries from incorrect opening of locked AED cabinets, and another found that injuries en route to patients were rare (<0.7%). Rescue-related drowning fatalities ranged from 0.02 to 0.08 per 100,000 population annually.

CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review suggests harms to rescuers during response or resuscitation are rare. Fatal harms have been reported during water rescue. Minor harms include unsafe AED removal, current leakage during ICD shock delivery, performing CPR without appropriate PPE, and minor injuries en route to a cardiac arrest. Indirect evidence from elective cardioversion suggests external defibrillation poses minimal electrical risk.

articles.title: Nailfold Capillary Density and Kidney Injury in CKD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular dysfunction plays a key role in the development and progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Evaluation of capillaries by microscopy of the nailfolds may provide noninvasive insight into systemic microvascular health, but its relationship with kidney function, proteinuria, and kidney histopathology in patients with CKD remains unknown.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of adults with CKD stages 2-5 (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] < 90 ml/min per 1.73 m2) recruited from nephrology outpatient clinics at a single academic medical center between January 2023 and December 2025. Participants underwent assessment of third and fourth finger nailfold microvascular structure and function using high-resolution video capillaroscopy at 100× magnification. The density of erythrocyte-perfused capillaries (capillaries/mm2) was quantified at baseline, after the release of arterial occlusion (HA) (hyperemic response), and during venous congestion (OA) using a deep learning-based image analysis pipeline. Associations between capillary density measures and kidney function (eGFR) and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (uPCR) were evaluated using multivariable regression models. In a subset of participants who underwent clinically indicated kidney biopsy, capillary density measures were examined for associations with histopathologic findings, including glomerulosclerosis (GS) and interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA), using similar multivariable models.

RESULTS: Among 189 participants with CKD, mean (standard deviation [SD]) age was 63 (16) years; 49% were female, 42% had diabetes, and 87% had hypertension. Mean (SD) baseline capillary density was 54 (15) capillaries/mm2. The mean eGFR was 41 (22) ml/min per 1.73 m2 and median (interquartile range [IQR]) uPCR was 0.31 [IQR: 0.11-1.8] mg/mg. In adjusted models, higher capillary density was associated with higher eGFR (β, 0.33; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.25-0.41) and lower uPCR (β -1.1; 95% CI -1.7 to -0.5) independent of CKD risk factors. Results were similar evaluating capillary count at HA and OA. Among the subset of 36 participants with kidney biopsy data, lower capillary density was associated with greater GS and IFTA severity, which remained significant after adjustment for demographic factors, eGFR, and proteinuria.

CONCLUSION: Finger nailfold capillary density is associated with kidney function, proteinuria, and biopsy markers of chronic kidney injury among adults with CKD. Capillaroscopy may provide a noninvasive tool to identify vascular and interstitial damage above and beyond eGFR and proteinuria in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Effects of RhBNP combined with immune modulation on immune function and short-term clinical outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation and heart failure.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexist, sharing underlying pathophysiology and risk factors, which leads to high morbidity and complex clinical management. While recombinant human B-type natriuretic peptide (rhBNP) is used for acute HF, its combined effect with traditional Chinese medicine for immune regulation in HF patients with persistent AF remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and immunological impact of rhBNP combined with an immunomodulatory therapy in patients with HF and permanent AF.

METHODS: In this randomized, prospective, controlled trial, 40 hospitalized patients with HF (NYHA class II-III, LVEF ≤40%) and permanent AF were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to receive conventional therapy alone (Control group, n = 20) or conventional therapy plus intravenous rhBNP and oral Zhenqi Fuzheng Granules for 7 days (Treatment group, n = 20).

RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the treatment group showed significantly greater reductions in BNP levels and greater improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Immunophenotyping analysis revealed that the treatment group had significantly increased absolute counts of CD3+ and CD4+ T lymphocytes and a higher CD4+/CD8+ ratio.

CONCLUSION: Adjunctive therapy combining rhBNP and immunomodulation in HF-AF patients significantly improves cardiac function, and is associated with improved short-term clinical outcomes. This suggests a promising multi-mechanistic therapeutic approach for this patient population.

articles.title: Comparative risk assessment of cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes using cystatin C and creatinine in DECLARE-TIMI 58.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between cystatin C and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes is not well explored in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and normal or mild kidney dysfunction.

METHODS: This nested prospective biomarker study included patients enrolled in DECLARE-TIMI 58. Participants were categorized into quartiles of CysC/creatinine and eGFRCysC/eGFRCr and classified according to Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk categories. Hazard ratios were estimated for a composite of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure (CVD/HHF), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and a kidney-specific composite outcome (persistent ≥40% decrease in eGFR, end-stage renal disease, or renal death).

RESULTS: Among 1899 placebo-treated patients, higher baseline CysC was associated with higher risk for CVD/HHF, MACE, and the kidney-specific composite outcome. A gradient of risk across quartiles was observed for CVD/HHF [Q4 v Q1: 1.33 (0.98-1.80), p-trend = 0.016]; MACE [1.34 (1.06-1.69), p-trend = 0.013]; and kidney-specific composite outcome [1.95 (0.95-3.99), p-trend = 0.036]. When compared with creatinine, CysC showed more pronounced and statistically significant risk gradients (CVD/HHF: KDIGO-CysC p-trend < 0.001 vs. p-trend Cr 0.34; MACE: CysC p-trend < 0.001 vs. Cr p-trend 0.52). No heterogeneity was observed in the effect of dapagliflozin across CysC concentrations (p-interactions >0.05).

CONCLUSION: In patients with T2D and predominantly preserved Cr-based eGFR, CysC was associated with increased cardiovascular and kidney risk. Although discrimination assessed by c-statistic was similar for CysC and Cr, risk gradients seen with CysC became attenuated and no longer statistically significant when using Cr-based analogs. The effect of dapagliflozin was consistent irrespective of baseline CysC.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01730534.

articles.title: Next-Generation Immunotherapies for Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Monoclonal Antibodies and Immune Checkpoint Modulation.
articles.journal: APMIS : acta pathologica, microbiologica, et immunologica Scandinavica
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa represents a critical healthcare challenge, accounting for 7%-10% of hospital-acquired infections globally, with particularly high prevalence in intensive care, burn, and respiratory units, alongside escalating rates of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains. The bacterium evades host immunity through multiple mechanisms, including Type III Secretion System effector translocation and biofilm formation via polysaccharide matrices (alginate, Psl, Pel). Antibiotic-based therapies are increasingly ineffective, necessitating host-directed immunotherapeutic strategies. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on monoclonal antibody therapy and immune checkpoint modulation for P. aeruginosa infections. Bispecific antibodies targeting PcrV and Psl enhance opsonophagocytic killing and biofilm disruption through Fc-mediated mechanisms. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1/PD-L1) reverse T-cell exhaustion from chronic antigen exposure and LPS-driven upregulation of inhibitory receptors, restoring antimicrobial function. Combination approaches integrating mAbs with antibiotics and checkpoint blockade show potential for synergistic bacterial clearance in preclinical pneumonia and burn wound models. Clinical translation remains limited by antigen variability (Psl and PcrV epitope polymorphisms), biofilm heterogeneity, and host immunogenetic diversity (Fc receptor polymorphisms, HLA variants, cytokine profiles). Multi-omics profiling may enable personalized treatment selection. Safety concerns regarding immune hyperactivation require carefully dosed, biomarker-guided strategies. Future development demands genomic stratification of responders and optimized therapeutic windows for maximal clinical benefit.

articles.title: PAs in Latvia.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: The physician assistant (PA) or associate profession in Latvia has its root in the feldšeris, or feldsher, profession of eastern Europe. Initially trained for military service, Latvian feldshers began receiving education to provide care to civilians in 1954. The profession changed its name to ārsta palīgs ("physician assistant") in the early 2000s. Latvian PAs are trained in a 3-year diploma program consisting of basic sciences, clinical sciences, and clinical placements in core medical disciplines, and have the option to obtain a specialized credential in emergency medicine or outpatient medicine with an additional year of study. Approximately 2600 PAs in Latvia practice in primary and specialty care across the country, and there are twice as many PAs per capita in Latvia as there are in the United States. PAs are an important part of Latvia's health care workforce solution to a significant provider shortage.

articles.title: Increasing use of SGLT-2 inhibitors among patients with heart failure.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this quality improvement project was to identify and address barriers contributing to the underutilization of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors in eligible patients with heart failure across the health system.

METHODS: The heart failure registry was used to identify the prescription percentage of SGLT-2 inhibitors pre- and postintervention. Interventions to increase prescribing included pharmacist education to primary care providers and use of a cost information handout.

RESULTS: Following the intervention, SGLT-2 inhibitor prescription for eligible patients improved from 7.1% (n = 630) to 9.0% (n = 814), representing a relative increase of 26.8% from baseline.

CONCLUSION: A multimodal approach involving pharmacy and primary care effectively increased SGLT-2 inhibitor prescribing in patients with heart failure. Physician associates, a key part of the primary care workforce, play an important role initiating guideline-directed medical therapy.

articles.title: Atopic dermatitis.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that commonly begins in childhood and can persist or first appear in adulthood. Its burden reflects pruritus, sleep loss, pain, infection, psychosocial effects, and treatment demands rather than visible extent alone. Diagnosis is clinical and requires recognition of age- and skin tone-specific morphology and exclusion of mimics. AD management begins with moisturization, gentle bathing, topical anti-inflammatory therapy, education, and proactive maintenance. Newer nonsteroidal topical agents and targeted systemic therapies have expanded options, but treatment should be individualized according to age, disease severity and control, comorbidities, safety, access, and patient preference. Routine elimination diets, topical antimicrobials for uninfected disease, antihistamines as primary antipruritic therapy, and systemic corticosteroids are generally not recommended for AD. This review provides physician associates with a practical approach to diagnosis, severity assessment, stepwise treatment, complication recognition, and timely referral.

articles.title: Female infertility in the 21st century.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: More than 12% of reproductive-age women in the United States seek infertility services each year. Infertility is commonly defined as failure to conceive after 12 months of regular, unprotected sexual intercourse. Common gynecologic causes of female infertility include endometriosis; diminished ovarian reserve; ovulatory dysfunction and anovulation; and other cervical, uterine, or tubal factors. Advances in medicine and assisted reproductive technology have expanded treatment options for women and couples experiencing infertility. This article provides an updated review of female infertility to support PAs in delivering informed patient counseling on treatment options, recognizing potential complications, and facilitating timely and appropriate referrals.

articles.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of the PD-1 Inhibitor Cetrelimab in Chronic Hepatitis B.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-induced T-cell exhaustion may be reversed using a programmed death receptor 1 (PD-1) inhibitor such as cetrelimab, an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody targeting PD-1. To evaluate the safety, activity and pharmacokinetics of low-dose (i.e., a dose lower than that used in oncology) cetrelimab in participants with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) virologically suppressed (VS) on a stable nucleos(t)ide analog (NA). Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-cohort, single-dose escalation study of cetrelimab administered subcutaneously or intravenously. Due to a strategic decision, and not to any safety concern, only one cohort (45 mg subcutaneous) was executed. Participants maintained their NA treatment to avoid HBV reactivation. Serum cetrelimab concentrations, HBV biomarkers, PD-1 receptor occupancy (RO) and safety were collected over 24 weeks. Eleven participants were enrolled and randomized, eight to cetrelimab and three to placebo and all 11 completed the study. Mean cetrelimab half-life was 16.3 days with median time to maximum cetrelimab concentration 10.4 days post-dose. Near-maximal RO was achieved 6 h post-dose which waned over time. There were no clinically relevant changes in HBV biomarkers or laboratory values including liver function tests and thyroid-stimulating hormone. No clinically relevant adverse events were reported. A single 45 mg dose of cetrelimab administered subcutaneously in VS participants with CHB was safe and well tolerated. There was no change in HBV biomarkers and further development of cetrelimab for HBV was abandoned. Clinical Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05242445; EudraCT Number: 2021-004857-21.

articles.title: Correlates of Glycemic Control in Type 2 Diabetes Adults With and Without Comorbid Heart Failure.
articles.journal: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Attaining good glycemic control (GC) in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is critical, yet the presence of comorbidities like heart failure (HF) presents overwhelming self-care complexities. The aim of this study was to investigate and compare the demographic, psychosocial, and clinical factors associated with glycemic control among T2D adults with and without comorbid HF.

DESIGN: A comparative cross-sectional study.

METHODS: A total of 210 adult T2D patients (105 with comorbid HF, 105 without comorbid HF) in Tikur Anbessa Specialized Referral Hospital (TASRH), the largest tertiary healthcare setting in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, were enrolled. Data gathered included demographic traits, clinical parameters including the outcome variable HbA1c (categorized as "good glycemic control" for HbA1c < 7% and "poor glycemic control" for HbA1c ≥ 7%), and standardized psychosocial scales (SDSCA, PDSMS, DKT2, PHQ-9, and ESSI). Bivariate analysis (Chi-square and biserial correlation) and Enter method logistic regression analysis were performed.

RESULT: Across both groups, good GC (HbA1c < 7%) was alarmingly low, only 10.43% in the non-HF and 9.52% in the HF comorbid group (p = 0.818). In the non-HF group, the multivariate model revealed that only a higher social support (ESSI) score significantly predicted a higher likelihood of good GC (AOR = 1.518, 95% CI: 1.002, 2.302, p = 0.049). Conversely, for those with comorbid HF, a higher diabetes self-efficacy (PDSMS) score (AOR = 1.569, 95% CI: 1.045, 2.355, p = 0.030) and taking a higher number of daily medications (AOR = 2.502, 95% CI: 1.050, 5.962, p = 0.038) significantly predicted good GC.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights a critical gap in glycemic control regardless of HF status. However, the actionable drivers of glycemic success diverge fundamentally: social support systems are vital for GC success in uncomplicated T2D, whereas promoting self-efficacy and total count of daily medications dictates success in the face of complex HF comorbidity.

articles.title: The Indirect Association of Psychological Well-Being in the Relationship Between Social Anxiety and Loneliness Among Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study in Tehran.
articles.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population ageing and its associated challenges have become a significant public health issue globally. Like other countries, Iran is witnessing a rapid increase in the number of older adults. It is estimated that the population aged 60 years and older will constitute 10.5% and 21.7% of Iran's population in 2025 and 2050, respectively. These figures emphasize the necessity of finding appropriate strategies for healthy ageing. This study aimed to examine the indirect association of psychological well-being in the relationship between social anxiety and loneliness among older adults in Tehran. Pet ownership was an inclusion criterion and was not analysed as a study variable.

METHODS: This descriptive-correlational study was conducted in Tehran, Iran, between October 2025 and March 2026. A total of 430 older adults with pets were recruited and completed the study. After removing six outliers, 424 participants were included in the final analysis. Data were collected using the Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale, Psychological Well-Being Scale and Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS-SR). The collected data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM).

RESULTS: Based on the findings of this cross-sectional study among 424 older adults in Tehran, most participants were aged 60-70 years and female. The mean scores of psychological well-being (39.73), loneliness (32.26) and social anxiety (47.68) were moderate. Social anxiety was associated with higher levels of loneliness directly (β = 0.496) and showed a positive indirect association with loneliness through lower levels of psychological well-being (β = 0.083). Moreover, psychological well-being was negatively correlated with loneliness (β = -0.192) and social anxiety (β = -0.432). In general, the results showed that psychological well-being and social anxiety were significantly associated with loneliness.

CONCLUSION: According to the results of this study, social anxiety had the strongest association with loneliness among older adults. There was a partial indirect association through psychological well-being in the relationship between social anxiety and loneliness. Thus, the findings highlight the need to pay more attention to social anxiety and psychological well-being among older adults with pets.

articles.title: Calibrated Bayes Analysis of Cluster-Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract: In cluster-randomized trials (CRTs), entire clusters of individuals are randomized to treatment, and outcomes within a cluster are typically correlated. While frequentist approaches are standard practice for CRT analysis, Bayesian methods have emerged as a strong alternative. Previous work has investigated the use of Bayesian hierarchical models for continuous, binary, and count outcomes in CRTs, but these approaches focus on model-based treatment effect coefficients as the target estimands, which may have ambiguous interpretation under model misspecification and informative cluster size. In this article, we introduce a calibrated Bayesian procedure for estimand-aligned analysis of CRTs even in the presence of potentially misspecified models. We propose estimators targeting both the cluster-average treatment effect (cluster-ATE) and individual-average treatment effect (individual-ATE), particularly in scenarios with informative cluster sizes. We additionally explore strategies for summarizing the posterior samples that can achieve the frequentist coverage even under working model misspecification. We provide simulation evidence to demonstrate the model-robustness property of the proposed estimators in CRTs, and further investigate the impact of covariate adjustment as well as the use of more flexible Bayesian nonparametric working models in the CRT context.

articles.title: Factors Influencing Intention to Quit Tobacco Use Among Patients With Non-Communicable Diseases in Bangladesh: A Multilevel Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tobacco use is a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCD), contributing to disease progression, comorbidities and reduced quality of life. This study aimed to assess the distribution and correlates of intention to quit tobacco use among patients with NCDs attending selected government sub-district hospitals in Bangladesh.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 660 patients aged ≥ 18 years attending NCD corners in eight selected government sub-district hospitals in Bangladesh. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic, clinical and healthcare, and tobacco use characteristics from 26 May to 14 June 2025. Patients were nested within sub-district hospitals, and multivariable multilevel logistic regression was used to identify the factors associated with quit intentions while accounting for clustering of patients within hospitals.

RESULTS: In the multilevel multivariable logistic regression model, patients with moderate to high levels of knowledge of cessation services (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.2; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.19-4.24), heart disease (AOR 2.0; 95% CI 1.18-3.59), stroke (AOR 2.4; 95% CI 1.09-5.12) and ≤ 10 years of tobacco use (AOR 2.1; 95% CI 1.24-3.38) were more likely to express an intention to quit. Among facility-level factors, being asked about tobacco use by healthcare providers (AOR 2.2; 95% CI 1.29-3.69) and receiving advice to quit (AOR 1.8; 95% CI 1.10-2.96) were associated with higher odds of intending to quit.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: Addressing both individual- and facility-level factors through structured cessation support integrated into routine NCD care could strengthen tobacco control efforts in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations.
articles.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

articles.title: Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20-CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma.

METHODS: DALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866).

FINDINGS: Between Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; p<0·0001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 63 (83%) of 76 with zamto-cel and in 65 (86%) of 76 with R-GemOx. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (28 [37%] with zamto-cel and 17 [22%] with R-GemOx), anaemia (11 [14%] and 12 [16%]), and decreased neutrophil count (20 [26%] and seven [9%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 31 (41%) patients with zamto-cel and 50 (66%) with R-GemOx, most commonly malignant neoplasm progression (11 [14%] and 38 [50%]), cytokine release syndrome (CRS; six [8%] and none), and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (four [5%] and none). Treatment-related deaths occurred in two (3%) of 82 patients with zamto-cel (due to CRS and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) and in one (1%) of 78 with R-GemOx (malignant lymphoma progression).

INTERPRETATION: The risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.

FUNDING: Miltenyi Biomedicine.

articles.title: Prepregnancy Prediabetes and Large-for-Gestational-Age Birth Independent of Gestational Diabetes Among Asian Women.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.abstract:
AIM: Prediabetes may increase the likelihood of adverse perinatal outcomes, but evidence regarding prepregnancy prediabetes remains limited. This study examined its associations with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and the delivery of a large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infant.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included women who delivered at 12 obstetric facilities in Japan between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2024, and had undergone hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) measurement within 1 year before conception. The primary maternal and fetal outcomes were GDM and LGA birth, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate each outcome, with adjustment for maternal age, assisted reproductive technology, prepregnancy body mass index, and primiparity.

RESULTS: A total of 282 pregnancies were included, of which 19 (6.7%) were complicated by prepregnancy prediabetes. Prepregnancy prediabetes showed a more than twofold increase in the estimated odds of GDM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.15; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-8.66), although the association was not statistically significant. In contrast, it was significantly associated with the delivery of an LGA infant (aOR, 3.48; 95% CI, 1.14-10.66). After women who developed GDM were excluded, 262 women remained, including 16 (6.1%) with prepregnancy prediabetes. In this subgroup, prepregnancy prediabetes remained significantly associated with the delivery of an LGA infant (aOR, 3.49; 95% CI, 1.09-11.57).

CONCLUSION: Prepregnancy prediabetes was independently associated with higher odds of delivering an LGA infant among Asian women, including those without a diagnosis of GDM. These findings suggest that preconception dysglycemia may help identify women at increased risk of excessive fetal growth beyond GDM diagnosis and warrant further evaluation in larger studies.

articles.title: Clinical tolerability and reproductive outcomes following intrauterine administration of allogeneic platelet lysate in mares resistant to post-breeding induced endometritis.
articles.abstract: Platelet-based therapies have gained interest in broodmare practice due to their immunomodulatory and antimicrobial effects. Platelet lysate (PL) is produced by freeze-thawing platelet-rich plasma (PRP), releasing growth factors and cytokines. As an acellular product, PL reduces immunogenic risk, allows long-term storage, and enables allogeneic use, supporting its application in human and veterinary medicine. Therefore, this study evaluated the safety and post-breeding reproductive outcomes in mares treated with allogeneic PL. Platelet lysate (PL) was prepared from 11 healthy mares using a double-centrifugation PRP protocol. PRP was divided and subjected to three freeze-thaw cycles (-196 °C to 37 °C), then filtered (0.22 µm). Post-filtration PL was aliquoted: samples were stored at -196 °C or -20 °C for PDGF-BB analysis, and the remaining volume was reserved for intrauterine therapy. Each mare provided autologous PL (A-PL), and pooled PL (P-PL) was also generated. Nine mares resistant to endometritis underwent three cycles, randomly assigned to receive A-PL, P-PL, or placebo (LRS) 6 h post-breeding. Mares were inseminated with fresh semen; cytology and ultrasonography were performed before, and 24 and 48 h post-breeding. Embryo flushing was conducted 8 days post-ovulation. PDGF-BB concentrations were similar between A-PL and P-PL (P = 0.97) and between PL samples stored at -20 °C and -196 °C (P = 0.57). Additionally, no differences were detected among groups in uterine ultrasonographic findings, endometrial inflammation, or embryo recovery rates (A-PL, 87.5%; P-PL, 87.5%; LRS, 71.4%; P = 0.65). These results support the absence of observed adverse reactions following intrauterine allogeneic PL and suggest that its use does not adversely affect post-breeding uterine response or embryo recovery in resistant mares.

articles.title: Psychological distress is differentially associated with resting cardiovascular indices in cisgender LGBQ and heterosexual young adults.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Sexual minority populations experience disproportionate psychosocial stress and cardiovascular disease risk, yet the relationship between psychological distress and cardiovascular regulation early in adulthood remains incompletely understood. We examined associations between depression, anxiety, and stress and resting cardiovascular indices in 96 cisgender young adults (39 queer, 57 heterosexual; age: 18-35 yr). Participants completed the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), and resting systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and heart rate (HR) were assessed. Queer participants reported greater depression (12.5 ± 9.2 vs. 7.5 ± 5.7), anxiety (13.0 ± 7.1 vs. 7.4 ± 6.4), and stress (18.7 ± 8.7 vs. 12.3 ± 7.7; all P ≤ 0.004) than heterosexual participants, whereas resting SBP, DBP, and HR did not differ between groups. In multivariable regression analyses stratified by sexual orientation, anxiety was positively associated with DBP in queer participants (β = 0.43, P = 0.0495), whereas stress was inversely associated with HR (β = -0.58, P = 0.044). Neither association was observed in heterosexual participants or the overall aggregated sample. Exploratory item-level analyses further identified distinct associations between individual DASS-21 symptoms and HR across sexual orientation groups. These findings demonstrate that psychological distress is differentially associated with resting cardiovascular regulation in queer and heterosexual young adults despite similar resting hemodynamic profiles. Distinct relationships between psychosocial factors and cardiovascular indices may precede overt cardiovascular differences and provide insight into early pathways contributing to cardiovascular health inequities in sexual minority populations.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Many studies of BP and cardiovascular function in queer people rely on self-report cardiovascular data, often using dichotomous hypertension/normotension. In our study using direct measurements of HR and BP, we found that queer young adults displayed greater depression, anxiety, and stress than heterosexual peers. Importantly, psychological variables were differentially associated with cardiovascular indices by sexual orientation. Our findings suggest that differences in psychosocial-cardiovascular coupling may be detectable before overt resting cardiovascular disparities emerge in young adulthood.

articles.title: Characterization of von Willebrand factor-enriched extracellular vesicles and their association with platelet adhesion in COVID-19.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Microvascular thrombosis is a hallmark of severe COVID-19 and a major contributor to adverse clinical outcomes. Extracellular vesicles have emerged as key mediators of thromboinflammation, yet their functional and molecular characteristics remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the prothrombotic activity, cellular origin, and von Willebrand factor (VWF) composition of plasma-derived small extracellular vesicles (SEVs) from hospitalized patients with COVID-19. We demonstrate that SEVs from critically ill patients with COVID-19 markedly enhance platelet adhesion and thrombus formation under arterial shear conditions and promote endothelial activation, as evidenced by increased release of ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. These SEVs were highly enriched in ultra-large VWF multimers, with significantly elevated high-to-low molecular weight ratios compared with controls. Flow cytometric analysis showed increased circulating SEVs derived from leukocytes, platelets, and endothelial cells in severe disease, with VWF-positive SEVs predominantly originating from endothelial cells. The enrichment of VWF-SEVs was independent of gender and diabetes status, suggesting a primary association with disease severity. Collectively, these findings indicate that SEVs, particularly those rich in endothelial-derived VWF, are associated with platelet activation and may contribute to the prothrombotic milieu in COVID-19. These findings underscore the importance of VWF-positive SEVs as biomarkers of disease severity and warrant further investigation into their role in COVID-19-related vascular pathology.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Circulating small extracellular vesicles in patients with COVID-19 carrying ultra-large VWF multimers boost platelet adhesion and activate endothelial cells, highlighting a potential driver and biomarker of COVID-19-associated coagulopathy.

articles.title: Osteopontin contributes to uterine artery dysfunction during chronic hypertensive pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Successful pregnancy requires maternal cardiovascular adaptation, including expansion and remodeling of the uterine arteries, to accommodate a progressive rise in uteroplacental blood flow. Chronic maternal hypertension is associated with impaired uterine artery adaptation and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including fetal growth restriction, yet the mechanisms driving these vascular changes remain incompletely understood. Osteopontin, a matricellular protein implicated in vascular pathology in hypertension, is a potential mediator of impaired uterine artery adaptation during pregnancy. In this study, we compared uterine artery remodeling in pregnant normotensive Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats and spontaneously hypertensive stroke-prone rats (SHRSP), a model of chronic hypertension. To investigate the contribution of osteopontin, we characterized an osteopontin-deficient SHRSP strain. Uterine artery hemodynamics were assessed by Doppler ultrasound, arterial structure was evaluated by histology, and molecular profiles were characterized by RNA sequencing. Fetal weight and length were measured at mid- and late gestation. We found that, compared with WKY, SHRSP fetuses were smaller and uterine arteries exhibited inward hypertrophic remodeling, including increased wall thickness, reduced lumen area, and an elevated resistance index. SHRSP uterine arteries also showed enrichment of pathways related to inflammation and vascular pathology. Among the most highly upregulated genes was Spp1, which encodes osteopontin. Compared with control SHRSP, osteopontin-deficient SHRSP had larger uterine artery lumen areas, lower resistance indices, and reduced expression of select inflammation-associated genes. Fetal growth trajectories were also improved. These findings identify osteopontin as a contributor to uterine artery dysfunction in chronic hypertensive pregnancy and demonstrate that osteopontin deficiency improves vascular adaptation and fetal growth.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study characterizes uterine artery dysfunction in a rat model of chronic maternal hypertension and identifies inflammation-related and matrix remodeling pathways associated with vascular pathology. We further demonstrate that osteopontin contributes to uterine artery dysfunction and introduce a novel osteopontin-deficient hypertensive rat model that exhibits improved uterine artery adaptation and fetal growth trajectory despite persistent maternal hypertension.

articles.title: Exploring cardiac kinetic energy in children with atrial septal defects: a case-control study.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Kinetic energy (KE) of intracardiac blood flow constitutes an important part of the heart's energy expenditure and can be quantified using four-dimensional (4-D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Pediatric patients with atrial septal defect (ASD) have volume-loaded right ventricles and underfilled left ventricles due to left-to-right shunting, which could make ASD a useful model to study such altered ventricular loading conditions in congenital heart disease to explore related pathophysiological changes to KE. To characterize ventricular KE in children with ASD before and after treatment, we matched patients to controls. We recruited 22 patients with ASD (8 males, median/[IQR]: 8.5/[5-12] yr) and performed repeat CMR in 16/22 (72.7%) at means ± SD: 7.7 ± 1.7 mo following treatment. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) KE were assessed by 4-D flow CMR. Results were compared with 11 controls. Before treatment, RV peak diastolic KE was higher in patients with ASD compared with controls (P = 0.02) and normalized afterward (P = 0.42) with abolishment of diastolic ASD streaming.
