Indexed for ventricular volume at the time of peak KE (iKE), RV peak systolic and peak diastolic iKE decreased among repeatedly assessed ASD after treatment (both: P < 0.01), suggesting altered RV energetics not only attributable to RV volume changes. After treatment, RV iKE was comparable between patients and controls (systolic: P = 0.18; diastolic: P = 0.87). Within the ASD group, LV peak systolic KE increased with increased LV volumes after treatment (P < 0.01), whereas LV peak diastolic KE did not change (P = 0.09). How the different RV and LV peak diastolic KE responses reflect different diastolic ventricular remodeling warrants further investigation.NEW & NOTEWORTHY During systole, RV peak KE among patients with ASD decreased after treatment independent of peak RV volumes, whereas LV peak systolic KE increased after ASD treatment due to improved LV filling conditions. During diastole, RV peak KE is higher than normal and reflects both the large ventricular blood volume and the streaming shunt volume from the ASD and normalizes after treatment.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle adaptation to home-based exercise in chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is commonly associated with decreased physical activity and skeletal muscle dysfunction. It has previously been shown that skeletal muscle fibrosis, impaired regeneration, and decreased vascularization occur in CKD. Independently, exercise can lead to increased muscle fiber size, satellite cells, capillary density, collagen synthesis, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. To determine the impact of exercise within a CKD population on muscle tissue properties, muscle tissue was examined before and after an exercise program. Twenty-five patients (19 exercisers and 6 usual care) with stages 3-5 CKD underwent a randomized controlled trial of a 12-wk home-based, personalized exercise program consisting of high-intensity interval training, power walking, and strength training versus usual care. Patients had a vastus lateralis muscle biopsy before and after interventions to assess muscle changes. Patients in the exercise cohort did not have significant changes in fiber size, fiber type, or number of satellite cells. Although there were no changes in measures of fibrosis (collagen content or ECM area), fibroadipogenic progenitors decreased with exercise, suggesting that there may be reduced accumulation of fibrosis in the future. There were parallel increases in muscle capillarization, increased in vivo muscle oxidative capacity, and a trending increase in walking distance, showing patients responded to exercise. This highlights that muscle in patients with CKD responded to an endurance-focused, home-based exercise program.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study investigates the impact of a home-based, video-monitored 12-wk exercise program, consisting of both endurance and resistance exercise, on skeletal muscle structural remodeling in persons with chronic kidney disease. We found this program increased capillaries and decreased fibroadipogenic progenitors after exercise.

articles.title: Autonomic dysregulation and high arterial blood pressure in male Crtc1-deficient mice.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence links cardiovascular disease, sympathetic nervous system overactivity, obesity, and depression. Whether this association is causal and what mechanisms may be involved remains unknown. Mice deficient in the cAMP response element-binding protein-regulated transcription coactivator 1 (CRTC1) show depression-related behavior and a metabolic profile resembling the metabolic syndrome. This study aimed to characterize arterial blood pressure regulation in these mice to determine whether global CRTC1 deficiency is also associated with arterial hypertension, another key characteristic of the metabolic syndrome. Telemetric measurements in unrestrained male mice revealed high blood pressure in Crtc1-deficient animals before the onset of obesity or hypertrophy of arterioles, accompanied by decreased heart rate variability, increased systolic blood pressure variability, enhanced environmental stress sensitivity and increased urinary catecholamine excretion. Pharmacological α1-adrenoceptor blockade with prazosin induced greater blood pressure reductions in Crtc1-deficient mice and eliminated genotype-dependent pressure differences, whereas the β1-adrenoceptor antagonist metoprolol showed no genotype-specific effect. Regulation of renal sodium transport proteins, activity of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, and cardiac systolic function were unchanged between genotypes. Crtc1-deficient animals also exhibited impaired glucose tolerance and a depression-related phenotype associated with reduced locomotion, increased agmatinase, and decreased cerebral brain-derived neurotrophic factor (Bdnf) and c-fos expression. These findings indicate that CRTC1 deficiency leads to high blood pressure, likely driven by excessive peripheral α1-adrenoceptor-mediated vasoconstriction caused by autonomic dysregulation. The co-occurrence of increased blood pressure, metabolic dysregulation, and the depressive-like phenotype in male Crtc1-deficient mice suggests a regulatory role of CRTC1 in the complex central network of signaling pathways involved in the frequent comorbidity of metabolic syndrome and depression.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Male Crtc1-deficient mice develop autonomic dysfunction and high arterial blood pressure, likely driven by enhanced α1-adrenergic vasoconstriction and independent of obesity or increased arteriolar wall thickness. The co-occurrence of elevated sympathetic activity, early cardiac remodeling, impaired glucose tolerance, and depression-related behavior suggests an involvement of CRTC1-dependent signaling in the coordination of autonomic, metabolic, and affective phenotypes.

articles.title: Effects of stellate ganglion blockade on pulmonary artery pressure and sympathetic baroreflex function at high altitude: a case study in treated hypertension.
articles.abstract: In this case study, we explored whether transient inhibition of sympathetic outflow with stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) modifies pulmonary artery pressure and sympathetic arterial baroreflex regulation during high-altitude (HA) exposure in an individual with treated hypertension. A 44-yr-old man with treated hypertension underwent physiological assessments at sea level (220 m) and after 5-8 days of exposure to HA (3,800 m). Pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), beat-by-beat blood pressure (BP), carotid artery diameter, and spontaneous sympathetic baroreflex function (integrative and mechanical components) were assessed at sea level and during HA exposure. During HA exposure, these measurements were obtained following a right-sided ultrasound-guided SGB and compared with those obtained in subsequent time-control visits. HA exposure increased PASP, MSNA, BP, and BP variability compared with sea level. SGB reduced PASP, whereas no meaningful change occurred during the time-control visit. BP variability was lower following SGB than during the control visit. The integrative sympathetic arterial baroreflex relationship appeared steeper following SGB, and the mechanical component demonstrated a greater slope than during the time-control visit, consistent with altered mechanical baroreceptor transduction. These observations suggest that regional sympathetic inhibition may exert distinct influences on pulmonary artery pressure and sympathetic baroreflex regulation during sustained high-altitude exposure in treated hypertension.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This physiological case study examined the effects of stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) during sustained high-altitude exposure in an individual with treated hypertension. Unilateral SGB reduced pulmonary artery systolic pressure and was associated with changes in sympathetic arterial baroreflex regulation and carotid pressure-diameter behavior. These observations provide preliminary evidence that regional sympathetic activity may influence pulmonary vascular and carotid mechanical responses during sustained hypoxic exposure.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle oxidative capacity and tissue composition in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract: Increasing evidence suggests that exercise intolerance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is related to peripheral abnormalities; however, the roles of muscle oxidative capacity and muscle steatosis remain incompletely understood. To address this knowledge gap, 38 HFpEF patients [mean age 69.8 ± 6.1 yr, body mass index (BMI) 37.6 ± 6.9 kg/m2] and 17 healthy older adults (HOAs; mean age 67.6 ± 5.4 yr, BMI 27.3 ± 4.8 kg/m2) performed a graded exercise test on a cycle ergometer to assess exercise tolerance (peak watts) and whole body aerobic capacity [peak O2 uptake (V̇o2peak)]. In vivo quadriceps oxidative capacity [phosphocreatine recovery time constant (τPCr)] and thigh tissue composition [i.e., lean thigh mass (LTM); intermuscular fat % (IMF%)] were measured separately via 31P-magnetic resonance spectroscopy (31P-MRS) and T2-weighted MRI, respectively. LTM was similar between HFpEF patients and HOAs (P = 0.854), but IMF% was significantly greater in HFpEF (P ≤ 0.001). Peak watts and V̇o2peak normalized to LTM were lower and quadriceps τPCr was slower in HFpEF patients compared to HOAs (all P < 0.03). Although IMF% was associated with peak watts normalized to LTM (R2 = 0.148) and whole body V̇o2peak normalized to body mass (R2 = 0.347), it was not associated with V̇o2peak normalized to LTM (R2 < 0.001) or τPCr (R2 = 0.020). In contrast, V̇o2peak normalized to LTM and quadriceps τPCr were both associated with peak watts (R2 = 0.509 and 0.252, respectively) and with each other (R2 = 0.298). Taken together, these data suggest that exercise intolerance in HFpEF is associated with increased muscle steatosis and impaired whole body and quadriceps muscle oxidative capacity. However, the lack of association between IMF% and measures of oxidative capacity suggest that they affect exercise tolerance via different physiological mechanisms.NEW & NOTEWORTHY We compared peripheral mechanisms of exercise intolerance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) patients and healthy older adults. HFpEF patients exhibited significantly greater intermuscular steatosis and impaired whole body and quadriceps oxidative capacity [i.e., peak O2 uptake (V̇o2peak) and phosphocreatine recovery time constant (τPCr), respectively], all of which were associated with impaired exercise tolerance. However, increased intermuscular steatosis was not associated with impaired V̇o2peak and τPCr, suggesting that steatosis and impaired oxidative capacity affect exercise tolerance through different physiological mechanisms.

articles.title: Effect of diet-induced plasma ceramide on human in vivo microvascular endothelial function.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Elevated plasma ceramides and microvascular endothelial dysfunction are separately implicated in the incidence of cardiovascular disease. Exogenous exposure and endogenous accumulation of ceramide causes microvascular endothelial dysfunction in isolated human microvessels ex vivo; however, the impact of increased plasma ceramide on in vivo human microvascular function is unknown. We measured peripheral microvascular endothelial function in young, healthy adults before and after increasing plasma ceramide levels via high-fat meal. We hypothesized that acute increases in plasma ceramide would induce peripheral microvascular dysfunction. Twenty-three healthy adults (12 males and 11 females) participated in this double-blind, randomized controlled, crossover trial. In vivo microvascular function and perfusion were assessed with laser Doppler flowmetry (LDF) using local heating and incident dark-field microscopy imaging, respectively. Plasma ceramides were quantified and microvascular function was assessed at baseline and 2 and 4 h post ingestion of a meal rich in long (LCT)- or medium (MCT)-chain fatty acids. Acute consumption of a LCT meal increased (P < 0.001) circulating ceramide concentrations in female participants only. Nitric oxide-dependent and maximal dilation, assessed via LDF, were similarly reduced after the intake of either a MCT or LCT meal, with no sex differences observed. No change in microvascular density and perfusion was observed after the consumption of either meal. Results suggest that an acute increase in plasma ceramide is not sufficient to further impair postprandial microvascular function, as both meals similarly reduced microvascular function despite ceramide elevations occurring only after the LCT meal. Future studies should investigate how repeated elevations in ceramide levels affect microvascular function.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Acute consumption of a long-chain fatty acid-rich meal increased circulating ceramides in a sex-specific manner, with elevations observed only in females. Despite this, in vivo microvascular endothelial function was similarly impaired after both medium- and long-chain fatty acid-rich meals, with no differences observed between sexes. Further studies are needed to define the role of ceramide-induced microvascular dysfunction and the long-term cardiovascular impact of repeated exposure.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Auscultation to Identify Left Ventricular Dysfunction - Development and External Validation in Prospective Multicenter Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular dysfunction (LVD) is common and associated with adverse prognosis, even in asymptomatic individuals. Early treatment improves outcomes, underscoring the need for efficient strategies to identify patients who may benefit from echocardiographic evaluation. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an AI auscultation method to detect LVD among patients referred for clinically indicated echocardiography.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter study, adult patients referred for echocardiography were enrolled to undergo digital auscultation at four standard auscultation sites with simultaneous single-lead ECGs. LVD was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) less than or equal to 40% on concurrent echocardiography. An ensemble model combining a transformer-based network and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network was trained on multicenter data and externally validated. The model's performance was compared with a seven-cardiologist reader substudy and clinical logistic regression models incorporating clinical variables, single-lead ECG-derived features, and B-type natriuretic peptide levels.

RESULTS: The multicenter training cohort included 2359 patients (mean age, 69.7±13.5 years; 40.4% female; 8.9% with reduced LVEF). The external validation cohort of 964 patients (mean age, 68.6±15.4 years; 38.9% female; 7.6% with reduced LVEF) was obtained from another independent multicenter registry. The four-site AI auscultation outperformed ECG-only models and the clinical logistic models, achieving an area under the receiver operator curve (AUROC) of 0.926 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.911 to 0.939) in the training cohort. In the external validation cohort, AUROC was 0.904 (95% CI, 0.876 to 0.930) and sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 86.3%, 74.2%, and 75.1%, respectively. In a 100-patient reader substudy, AI auscultation outperformed cardiologist consensus in accuracy (82.0% vs. 62.0%; P=0.004). Model performance was consistent across prespecified subgroups. The simplified two-site auscultation model retained high accuracy in the external validation cohort (AUROC, 0.903; 95% CI, 0.878 to 0.927).

CONCLUSIONS: AI auscultation accurately detected LVD among patients referred for clinically indicated echocardiography, supporting its potential as a scalable and accessible pre-echocardiographic risk-enrichment tool. Further validation is warranted before broader screening applications. (Funded by AMI Inc. and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI program [grant number 25K19371].).

articles.title: Effect of Previsit AI-Generated Document Summaries on Consultation Time and Patient-Physician Communication - The AI-INFOCARE Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited health literacy, clinical jargon, and time-constrained consultations often impair patients' understanding of medical findings. We evaluated whether AI-generated, quality-checked lay language summaries provided before consultations improve communication-related outcomes.

METHODS: In this single-center, randomized trial in an outpatient neurosurgical setting, 300 adults were randomly assigned 1:1 to standard care with or without a quality-checked, AI-generated layperson summary of their medical findings (Simply Onno) before consultation. The primary end point was patient-reported quality of physician-patient interaction (Fragebogen zur Arzt-Patient-Interaktion [FAPI]). Secondary end points included autonomy support (Health Care Climate Questionnaire [HCCQ]), encounter difficulty (Difficult Doctor-Patient Relationship Questionnaire [DDPRQ-10]), and consultation duration (minutes).

RESULTS: The mean FAPI score was higher in the intervention group (4.42±0.51 vs. 4.25±0.54; difference, 0.17; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.05 to 0.29; P=0.005; Hedges' g=0.33), driven by shared decision-making (difference, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.15 to 0.42), with no evidence of a difference in perceived empathy. Patient-rated autonomy support was higher (difference, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.06 to 0.23), whereas physicians rated their own autonomy support slightly lower (difference, -0.12; cluster-robust 95% CI, -0.21 to -0.04). Median consultation time was 25 versus 33 minutes in the intervention group versus the control group, respectively, an approximate 21% relative reduction (ratio of geometric means, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.70 to 0.88). For encounter difficulty (DDPRQ-10), we found potential evidence of a small increase (difference, 0.09; cluster-robust 95% CI, -0.03 to 0.21). Secondary end point confidence intervals were unadjusted for multiplicity.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-generated summaries provided before outpatient neurosurgical consultations were associated with better patient-reported interaction quality and autonomy support and shorter consultations. Physicians rated their own autonomy support as slightly lower in the intervention group; evidence for increased encounter difficulty was limited, with confidence intervals compatible with no difference. These findings support further evaluation of quality-checked, patient-facing document translation; effects on clinical outcomes and clinician workload require confirmation before routine adoption.

articles.title: Correction to: 2026 Guideline for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery: A Guideline From the American Heart Association and American Stroke Association.
Reimagining Stroke Research Infrastructure: Lessons From NIH Center Models to Build Community-Engaged Systems That Enhance Participation and Implementation.
Advances in Pediatric Stroke.
Caseous Mitral Annular Necrosis: A Diagnostic Role for Cardiac CT in Recurrent Embolic Stroke.
Type A Aortic Dissection Presenting as Common TIA.
Cytoprotection for Acute Ischemic Stroke: Critical Appraisal of Recent Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Several phase III clinical trials testing cytoprotective approaches have recently been completed, and many of these studies report a clinical benefit. Reviewing the outcomes of these trials in light of their specific designs reveals intriguing results. Trials designed with shorter treatment time windows (≤24 hours) and featuring high rates of recanalization therapies predominantly show neutral outcomes, that is, no therapeutic benefit. Studies using later time points (>24 hours to 14 days) and often enrolling patients in whom recanalization is not or only infrequently established show clear treatment effects. These results challenge our current understanding of cytoprotective approaches, which are believed to primarily target the penumbra as the key to therapeutic success. The reasons for this are unclear. They may include other, potentially unknown mechanisms of action that improve clinical outcome even when applied within longer time windows rather than exerting acute cytoprotection. Here, we discuss such potential mechanisms, to what extent they could explain the results of recent cytoprotection trials, and review consequences for future translational and clinical research.

Outcome-specific risk factors for dehydration and acute kidney injury readmission after ileostomy: A US National Cohort Study, 2016-2022.
articles.journal: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
articles.abstract:
AIM: Single-centre pathways have reduced dehydration and acute kidney injury (AKI)-specific readmission after ileostomy from 17%-28% to single-digit rates, but whether these gains translated nationally is unknown. We examined how discharge destination relates to outcome-specific readmission, quantified 30-day readmission rates and encounter costs from 2016 to 2022 and identified risk factors at the population level.

METHOD: Retrospective cohort study using the United States Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD, 2016-2022). Adults undergoing ileostomy creation were included. The primary outcome was 30-day readmission for dehydration or AKI. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified risk factors for composite readmission, with home-discharge effects compared between dehydration- and AKI-specific outcomes. Inflation-adjusted encounter costs were calculated.

RESULTS: Among 189,829 patients (176,150 discharged alive), 24,024 were readmitted within 30 days (13.5%, 95% CI 13.3-13.7). Home discharge had opposing associations by outcome subtype. Dehydration-specific readmission increased (aOR 1.25) and AKI-specific readmission decreased (aOR 0.92, p < 0.001 for interaction). The strongest risk factors were extended length of stay >7 days (aOR 1.48), complicated diabetes (aOR 1.46) and age ≥ 65 years (aOR 1.46). Annual rates were stable (p for trend = 0.826). Readmission encounters totalled $1.51 billion in inflation-adjusted dollars. The principal-diagnosis lower-bound estimate was $0.40 billion.

CONCLUSION: Home discharge had divergent associations by outcome subtype, identifying the post-discharge transition as a candidate for prospective intervention testing. Stagnant national rates over 7 years despite established prevention evidence, an income-dependent gradient and a graded rate across cumulative risk-factor burden together motivate prospective evaluation of risk-stratified discharge protocols incorporating community stoma-output monitoring.

articles.title: In Vivo Study of Topical Bimatoprost, Latanoprost, Travoprost in Comparison with Minoxidil on Hair Growth in C57BL/6 Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alopecia significantly affects psychological well-being and social functioning. Standard treatments, like minoxidil and finasteride, are limited by delayed efficacy, need for lifelong use, and adverse effects. Prostaglandin analogs (PGAs), originally developed for ocular hypertension, have shown promise in promoting hair growth. This study compares their effects with minoxidil in a murine model.

AIM AND OBJECTIVES: To compare the effects of bimatoprost, latanoprost, and travoprost on hair growth in C57BL/6 mice, with evaluation of hair density, follicle diameter, and growth rate using minoxidil as the comparator.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: After Institutional Animal Ethics Committee approval, 40 male C57BL/6 mice (aged 6-7 weeks, weighing 20-25 g) were randomized into five groups ( n = 8 in each group): (1) vehicle control, (2) minoxidil 5%, (3) latanoprost 0.005%, (4) bimatoprost 0.03%, and (5) travoprost 0.004%. Drugs were applied topically to shaved dorsal skin daily for 28 days. Hair growth was assessed by follicle density, bulb diameter, and area of regrowth using ImageJ from photographs taken on days 1, 7, 15, and 28.

RESULTS: All PGAs significantly increased hair density compared to vehicle control (vehicle control: 1.50 ± 0.55 vs. latanoprost: 7.50 ± 1.69, bimatoprost: 7.75 ± 2.87, travoprost: 6.87 ± 3.40; P = 0.001). Latanoprost and bimatoprost showed higher hair density than minoxidil (3.75 ± 2.87; P = 0.038 and 0.010, respectively). Hair follicle diameter was greater with PGAs (latanoprost: 53.12 ± 5.30, bimatoprost: 51.87 ± 7.52, travoprost: 48.12 ± 3.47 µm) versus vehicle control (27.91 ± 5.57 µm, P = 0.001) and minoxidil (38.12 ± 5.46 µm, P = 0.001). Bimatoprost showed the greatest regrowth by day 28, while latanoprost demonstrated earlier onset by day 15. PGAs also caused darker pigmentation and longer hair.

LIMITATIONS: The present study duration was limited to 4 weeks. Minoxidil (positive control) did not show noticeable hair growth because its effects usually take 6-8 weeks to appear.

CONCLUSION: Topical PGAs improved key hair growth parameters. Bimatoprost and latanoprost showed early and superior efficacy by day 28.

articles.title: Short Versus Long Maribavir Treatment Duration for Cytomegalovirus Infection in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: A Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Maribavir (MBV) is an oral antiviral approved for refractory or resistant CMV, with an 8-week regimen used in the pivotal clinical trial. We compared outcomes of longer versus shorter MBV courses in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of all adult SOT recipients from three centers in Catalonia, Spain, treated with MBV through November 30, 2024. Patients were followed up for 3 months and categorized as receiving ≥ 42 days (long-duration group, LDG) or < 42 days (short-duration group, SDG). Primary outcomes were CMV clearance and recurrence. Sixty-one SOT recipients received MBV (29 in LDG; 32 in SDG). Median treatment duration was 64 versus 24 days (p < 0.001). LDG patients had higher baseline CMV load (15 000 vs. 2005 IU/mL, p = 0.001), more high-risk transplants (lung transplant: 8 vs. 1; CMV D + /R- mismatch: 52% vs. 28%), and more refractory/resistant infection, while intolerance was more common in SDG. CMV clearance was similar between groups (59% in LDG vs. 62% in SDG, p = 0.481), though clearance occurred later in LDG (27 vs. 13 days, p = 0.009). Recurrence rates were comparable (35% vs. 38%, p = 0.966). Refractory/resistance vs intolerance as the indication for MBV was the only factor associated with recurrence (51.6% vs. 21.4%, p = 0.017). Adverse events were generally mild (mainly dysgeusia), but four patients discontinued therapy because of this. In this real-world cohort of SOT recipients with refractory, resistant, or valganciclovir-intolerant CMV infection, selected patients receiving shorter MBV courses achieved viral clearance and recurrence rates comparable to the standard regimen.

articles.title: Clinical Pathway Management for Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy in Kellgren-Lawrence Grade I and II Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective, Multicenter, Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of sports medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical outcomes after platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment for knee osteoarthritis are inconsistent, and some well-designed trials show no benefit. Whether a standardized multicomponent pathway improves outcomes relative to conventional PRP care is uncertain.

PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy, safety, satisfaction, and costs of a standardized PRP pathway versus physician-directed conventional PRP care in Kellgren-Lawrence grade I and II knee osteoarthritis.

STUDY DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial; Level of evidence, 1.

METHODS: At 3 hospitals, 240 patients were randomized 1:1 to a standardized PRP clinical pathway (PRP-CP; n = 120) or physician-directed conventional PRP care (PRP-C; n = 120). PRP-CP combined standardized selection, quality-controlled leukocyte-poor PRP, ultrasound-guided injections, staged rehabilitation, and systematic follow-up. Primary 12-month outcomes were visual analog scale (VAS) pain, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) total, and International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) scores; secondary outcomes included achievement of the minimal clinically important difference, satisfaction, adverse events, and costs.

RESULTS: At 12 months, PRP-CP produced greater changes than PRP-C in VAS (mean difference [MD], -2.98 [95% CI, -3.64 to -2.32]), WOMAC total (MD, -8.63 [95% CI, -11.35 to -5.90]), and IKDC (MD, 10.25 [95% CI, 8.37 to 12.13]) scores (all P < .001). Achievement of the minimal clinically important difference favored PRP-CP at 3, 6, and 12 months for the VAS and at 6 and 12 months for the IKDC and WOMAC (P < .05). Satisfaction was greater with PRP-CP (odds ratio, 1.79 [95% CI, 1.11-2.89]; P = .017). An adverse event occurred in 17 of 115 patients in the PRP-CP group (14.8%) versus 36 of 113 patients in the PRP-C group (31.9%) (Fisher exact test: P = .003). Mean costs were CN¥15,199.9 versus CN¥14,754.4, respectively; the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was CN¥66.0 per WOMAC point. Effects were generally consistent across centers, and blinding was maintained.

CONCLUSION: The standardized multicomponent pathway produced greater 12-month improvements in pain and function than conventional PRP care, with fewer adverse events. Because components were bundled and no placebo group was included, the trial does not establish PRP efficacy or component-specific effects.

articles.title: Investigation of Torque Teno Virus Loads as a Marker of Immunosuppression in Pediatric Chronic Renal Failure: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Torque Teno Virus (TTV), family Anelloviridae, is a small, non-enveloped, single-stranded DNA virus that has not been linked with any specific human illness but nevertheless constitutes a major component of the human virome. An association between TTV loads and the immune status of the host with reference to other viral infections, immunosuppression therapy, and acute rejection is reported in adult and pediatric kidney transplant recipients. We sought to investigate the feasibility of TTV as a surrogate marker of the degree of immunosuppression in pediatric kidney transplant patients.

METHODS: 185 children attending the Nephrology clinic in Children's Health Ireland at Temple Street were studied over a four-year period from September 2019 until November 2023, ranging from 0 to 17 years of age. Patients were enrolled from pre-transplant undergoing kidney replacement therapy (n = 12), from post-transplant (n = 124) groups, and from patients with chronic renal failure (n = 20) (without kidney replacement therapy), all of which were compared to controls (n = 35). TTV loads were quantified using a standardized TTV R-gene kit.

RESULTS: TTV loads were significantly higher compared to controls from 3 months post-transplantation onward (p < 0.001), with the greatest increase observed between 3 and 6 months post-transplantation. Immunosuppression exerted a significant independent effect on TTV loads after adjusting for age (p < 0.001). Overall, females exhibited significantly higher TTV loads than males (p = 0.01). Furthermore, a significant interaction was observed between patient group and gender (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that both immunosuppressive status and gender-related factors contribute to TTV kinetics after transplantation and should be considered when interpreting TTV as a biomarker of immune function. Larger studies are required to confirm our findings.

articles.title: Effects of Whey Protein Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Hepatic Stress, and Inflammatory Markers in Power- and Endurance-Trained Athletes.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the effects of 8 weeks of whey protein supplementation (30 g/day) on biomarkers of liver function, inflammation, and muscle damage in trained power-trained (predominantly speed-power/anaerobic-power disciplines) and endurance-trained athletes, in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design. Fifty-nine male athletes were stratified into power (n = 30) and endurance (n = 29) groups, then randomly assigned to a whey protein group (WG) or a placebo control group (CG). Biomarkers assessed pre- and post-intervention included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), C-reactive protein (CRP), and creatine kinase (CK). Significant reductions in ALT, AST, and CK were observed in both endurance- and power-trained athletes after supplementation (p = 0.001, p = 0.015, p = 0.001, and p = 0.003 respectively), indicating attenuated hepatic and muscular stress. Among the four biomarkers, only ALT displayed a statistically significant three-way interaction (Time × Supplementation × Training modality; p = 0.003), identifying it as the sole marker showing a genuine modality-specific differential response to supplementation. A significant within-group reduction in CRP was additionally observed in the supplemented power-trained athletes (p = 0.039), whereas endurance athletes showed only minor, non-significant changes; because the omnibus three-way interaction for CRP was not significant, this finding is reported as a within-group trend rather than evidence of a differential effect between modalities. Placebo groups demonstrated stable or increased enzyme and CRP values, particularly in endurance athletes. These findings suggest that whey protein may attenuate exercise-induced hepatic and muscular stress across training modalities, with a modality-specific effect on hepatic stress markers (ALT) observed in power-trained athletes. The results highlight whey protein's potential as a nutritional aid to promote recovery and physiological adaptation, possibly mediated by antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Further studies are warranted to examine long-term outcomes and dose-response effects across different training profiles.

articles.title: Combining Cognitive Training and Brain Stimulation: A Novel Approach to Address Disordered Eating and Antipsychotic-Induced Weight Gain in People With Severe Mental Illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antipsychotic-induced weight gain is a distressing side effect that most often occurs within the first 3-6 months of pharmacological initiation, significantly increasing cardiometabolic risk and mortality in individuals with severe mental illness.

AIMS: To assess the feasibility of reducing food craving and binge eating using Approach Bias Modification Training (ABMT) combined with real or sham Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS).

METHOD: In this double-blind, parallel-group, two-arm, sham-controlled trial, adults with schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder on stable doses of antipsychotics were randomly allocated to a total of five ABMT sessions together with either real or sham tDCS administered over 3 weeks. Assessments were made at baseline (T0), post-treatment (T1) and at a 2-week follow-up (T2). Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, attendance, retention, tDCS safety, acceptability, tolerability, and blinding. Secondary outcomes were changes in food craving, binge eating, approach bias to food, body mass index, and psychological symptoms.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight participants were recruited (93% of target). Retention was high (T1 = 85.7% and T2 = 78.6%); blinding accuracy was 46.4%. Medium effect sizes favoured 'ABMT + real tDCS' for reducing binge eating (d = -0.6, 95% CI -1.5, 0.3), and 'ABMT + sham tDCS' for reducing food cravings (d = 0.5, 95% CI -0.4, 1.4). Within-groups, only the 'ABMT + real tDCS' arm showed reduced approach bias to food and approach-avoidance bias to food, and increased avoidance bias to food (all p < 0.05). This was followed by reduced binge eating episodes (p < 0.05). Both groups reported frequent binge-eating episodes ('ABMT + tDCS' = 43%; 'ABMT + sham tDCS' = 28.6%).

CONCLUSION: The initiation of antipsychotic therapy is a critical clinical window for early intervention to mitigate the long-term metabolic and psychiatric consequences of antipsychotic-induced weight gain. Combining ABMT + tDCS is acceptable and may help reduce binge eating in individuals on antipsychotics, with a potential synergistic effect between cognitive training and brain stimulation. A confirmatory trial is needed to assess its effectiveness and should include BED diagnosis as a stratification criterion.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN Identifier: 13280178.

articles.title: Endohepatology in the Management of Portal Hypertension in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. This biology is compounded by a diagnostic gap: non-invasive tests such as liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography, FIB-4, ANTICIPATE-NASH, spleen stiffness and the NICER model, are degraded by obesity through technical limitations and altered diagnostic thresholds, even when test discrimination is preserved. Moreover, no non-invasive rule-in for clinically significant portal hypertension reaches a 90% positive predictive value in obese MASLD, leaving a clinically meaningful grey zone. Endohepatology addresses these diagnostic limitations by providing complementary hemodynamic, elastographic, and histological information. Within a single sedated session, EUS-guided shear-wave elastography and EUS-guided liver biopsy can adjudicate F2-F3 fibrosis when treatment eligibility is uncertain; EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement can provide a direct gradient when HVPG or non-invasive tests are discordant with the clinical phenotype; and EUS-based vascular assessment can characterize collateral and variceal anatomy. The same platform extends to therapy, including EUS-guided gastric variceal obliteration and pre-bariatric risk stratification. Current evidence is largely early-phase and requires prospective validation. Rather than replacing established tools, endohepatology offers an integrated pathway tailored to the diagnostic and therapeutic problems most characteristic of MASLD.

articles.title: Blood- and Liver Stiffness-Based Non-Invasive Tests for Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension in Patients With cACLD and HCC.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The applicability of non-invasive tests (NITs) for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is controversial. We performed a head-to-head comparison of various NITs for CSPH and evaluated rule-in/-out criteria.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study including 283 patients with HCC undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement at the Vienna Hepatic Haemodynamic Lab with available, same-day data on NITs (i.e., liver stiffness measurement [LSM], platelet count [PLT], von Willebrand factor antigen [VWF:Ag], and the ratio of VWF:Ag and PLT [VITRO]). For the subsequent analysis, we focused on patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD).

RESULTS: Among 164 patients with cACLD, most were BCLC 0/A (50.6%) and CSPH prevalence was 46.3%, the median LSM was 20.0 kPa (IQR: 13.3-37.9), and mean VWF:Ag/VITRO was 266 ± 119%/2.30 ± 1.81. The VITRO score yielded the highest discriminative ability to detect CSPH (AUROC: 0.834), followed by ANTICIPATE ± NASH (AUROC: 0.822), PLT (AUROC: 0.803), LSM (AUROC: 0.779), and VWF:Ag (AUROC: 0.707). The application of the Baveno VII criterium (LSM ≤ 15 kPa & PLT ≥ 150G/L) and the VITRO score (≤ 1.0) individually showed an excellent performance for ruling-out CSPH (sensitivities: ≥ 95%, NPV: 100%/87.9%). For ruling-in CSPH by individual criteria, the VITRO score provided the highest PPV (≥ 2.5, specificity/PPV: 89.8%/83.0%), followed by the Baveno VII criteria (specificity/PPV: 81.8%/74.6%). When sequentially applying Baveno VII criteria and VITRO, the grey zone could be significantly reduced to 16% (sensitivity/NPV: 94.7%/92.2%; specificity/PPV: 73.9%/84.4%).

CONCLUSION: The discriminative ability in patients with cACLD and HCC was comparable to patients without HCC. However, PPVs of established criteria were < 90%, which may be explained by the comparatively low prevalence of CSPH in this context.

articles.title: Albuminuria, glomerular filtration rate, and fracture among U.S. adults with and without type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: CKD and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are established risk factors for fracture. Albuminuria and reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), the most commonly used measures to diagnose CKD, may confer fracture risk through distinct mechanisms. Clarifying the associations of albuminuria, reduced eGFR, and T2D status with fracture risk and potential interactions between these exposures may improve fracture risk assessment. We performed a cross-sectional study of 20 034 participants 50 yr or older in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 1999 to 2020. Albuminuria was defined by spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g; reduced eGFR was defined as <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Outcomes were prevalent hip and any fracture-the composite of any hip, wrist, or spine fracture-ascertained using self-report of physician diagnosis. Mean age was 63 yr; 53% were female, 9% were non-Hispanic Black, and 5% were Mexican-American. Participants reported 417 hip and 2703 any fractures. After adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates, including osteoporosis diagnosis and treatment, albuminuria was associated with increased odds of hip fracture (OR 1.59, 95% CI: 1.13-2.22), with no significant interaction by eGFR or T2D status. Neither reduced eGFR (OR 1.02; 95% CI: 0.73-1.44) nor T2D status (OR 0.94; 95% CI: 0.63-1.39) was associated with higher odds of hip fracture. Albuminuria, reduced eGFR, and T2D were not significantly associated with any fracture. In a subset of 7005 participants with BMD measurements, additional adjustment for FN BMD partially attenuated the association of albuminuria with hip fracture (OR 1.35; 95% CI: 0.72-2.53). In conclusion, albuminuria is associated with hip fracture in adults with and without T2D, independent of eGFR.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Lucitanib in Advanced Thymic Carcinoma: A Randomized Phase II Trial.
articles.abstract: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Negative impact of single housing on chronic kidney disease mineral and bone disorder outcomes.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a disorder of acquired disrupted mineral metabolism that affects millions in the United States and has no cure. Due to disturbed mineral homeostasis bones are particularly affected showing substantial bone loss during CKD and intricately linked with morbidity and mortality. Animal models serve as a crucial platform to investigate and elucidate the tissue cross-communication that facilitates pathogenic changes during CKD. One preclinical rodent model gaining in popularity is the adenine-diet induced CKD, which negates the requirement for highly technical surgical interventions and displays several of the CKD disrupted mineral metabolism hallmarks observed in patients. Interestingly, although CKD alone can negatively impact bone, other factors, such as individual housing, can impair normal bone homeostasis. This could be encountered experimentally especially when generating experimental animals in-house, in particular, using males that maintain aggressive territorial actions. We sought to evaluate the impact of reduced cage housing numbers, replicating potentially encountered cage number conditions, on the progression of CKD. We hypothesized that single housing alone would accelerate bone loss and therefore exacerbate CKD mineral dysregulation and related outcomes. To test this, C57BL/6J male mice at 10 wk old were maintained at 5-, 3-, or 1-mice per cage while receiving casein-control or the CKD-inducing adenine diet. We found that within 4 wk of diet administration, individually housed mice had more profound weight loss corresponding with increased circulating urea, hyperphosphatemia, and bone loss compared to mice maintained at 5 per cage. Additionally, 50% of the individually housed CKD animals developed cardiovascular calcifications, a sequelae of impaired mineral excretion. These data demonstrate housing density significantly impacts outcomes related to CKD and an important variable to consider when conducting basic and translational mouse CKD studies.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure.

RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.

articles.title: Four weeks of isometric handgrip training results in lower awake ambulatory blood pressure compared with control: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: We compared the effects of upper-limb (handgrip) and lower-limb (knee extension) isometric training on ambulatory blood pressure in individuals with controlled hypertension. In this randomized controlled trial, 67 adults receiving antihypertensive medication were allocated to a control group (CG, n = 22), small muscle mass isometric training (SMM, handgrip; n = 22), or large muscle mass isometric training (LMM, knee extension; n = 23). Participants completed 12 supervised sessions over 4 weeks, with the exercise protocols performed at 30% of upper-limb MVC or lower-limb maximal isometric load, respectively. Ambulatory blood pressure outcomes were compared using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for the corresponding baseline office blood pressure. Hourly 24-h profiles were analyzed using generalized estimating equations with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Significant between-group differences were observed only for awake ambulatory blood pressure. Compared with CG, SMM showed lower awake systolic blood pressure (121.8 ± 3.1 vs. 124.2 ± 2.6 mmHg; p = 0.017) and awake diastolic blood pressure (76.3 ± 3.6 vs. 80.8 ± 4.2 mmHg; p = 0.009). No significant differences were observed between LMM and CG, between the two exercise groups, or for 24-h and sleep blood pressure. These findings indicate that, after 4 weeks of supervised isometric training, modest between-group differences in awake ambulatory blood pressure were observed only for handgrip training compared with the control group. Greater muscle mass recruitment did not result in superior antihypertensive effects, suggesting that the chronic blood pressure response to isometric exercise is not determined solely by the amount of muscle mass involved. Trial registration: "ClinicalTrials.gov," "NCT07147595."

articles.title: Presentation of the AGA William Beaumont Prize in Gastroenterology to Stuart Jon Spechler, MD, AGAF.
Effects of Lens Status and Prophylactic Transscleral Retinopexy on Vision Outcomes in Boston Terriers Following Phacoemulsification.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the effects of surgical lens status (pseudophakia or intentional aphakia) and prophylactic transscleral retinopexy (PTR) on postoperative ocular hypertension (POH), glaucoma, retinal detachment, and vision loss following phacoemulsification in Boston Terriers.

ANIMALS STUDIED: Thirty-seven Boston Terriers.

PROCEDURE: A retrospective single-cohort study was conducted on Boston Terriers that underwent phacoemulsification between January 1997 and June 2025, with pseudophakia or intentional aphakia. Time-to-event analyses were performed using parametric interval-censored survival models. Analyses were performed unadjusted and adjusted separately for 4 potential confounders identified using a directed acyclic graph (of which year of surgery was considered the most important).

RESULTS: POH occurred in 22/63 (35%) eyes (46% of pseudophakic and 26% of aphakic eyes), glaucoma in 21/62 (34%) eyes (52% of pseudophakic and 20% of aphakic eyes), and vision loss in 16/61 (26%) eyes (36% of pseudophakic and 18% of aphakic eyes). Only 3 cases of retinal detachment precluded further analysis. Estimated hazard ratios (pseudophakia compared to aphakia, unadjusted and adjusted for year of surgery) were, respectively, 2.0 (95% CI = 0.8 to 5.5; p = 0.157) to 2.8 (95% CI = 1.0 to 7.9; p = 0.052) for POH and 2.9 (95% CI = 0.9 to 9.2; p = 0.075) to 2.7 (95% CI = 1.0 to 7.3; p = 0.050) for glaucoma. Estimated effects of lens status on vision loss and effects of PTR on all three outcomes were imprecise and inconclusive.

CONCLUSIONS: In Boston Terrier eyes undergoing phacoemulsification, pseudophakia may result in higher risks of postoperative ocular hypertension and glaucoma compared to intentional aphakia.

articles.title: Nonlinear Aging of the Human TCR Repertoire Is Influenced by Sex, CMV, and Cancer.
articles.abstract: Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in immune function, increasing susceptibility to infections, cancer, and poorer treatment outcomes. The diversity of the T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, reflecting the capacity to recognize diverse antigens, is known to decline with age. However, how intrinsic and extrinsic factors jointly shape TCR diversity and its rate of decline, as well as the extent to which this diversity influences clinical outcomes in cancer, remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrate TCR sequencing data from 1.32 billion unique T cell clones, derived from 798 patients with cancer and 5052 individuals without cancer across 14 independent cohorts, to systematically characterize the effects of age, sex, and chronic cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection on peripheral blood repertoire diversity. We identify a nonlinear trajectory of diversity loss that accelerates after midlife, with a marked increase in the rate of decline beyond approximately 50 years of age, which is further modified by sex and CMV infection. In patients with cancer, higher peripheral TCR diversity was associated with improved overall survival across multiple cancer types, even when accounting for the impact of age, sex, and CMV on diversity. Together, these findings underline peripheral TCR repertoire diversity as a dynamic marker of immune aging shaped by demographic and chronic viral factors.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.

METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.

FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.

INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

FUNDING: Key Clinical Research Initiative Program of Union Hospital, National Key Technology Research and Development Programme of Hubei Province, and Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Genetic Insights Into Cardiomyopathy With Restrictive Phenotype: Implications for Diagnosis and Personalized Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype is uncommon, genetically heterogeneous, and difficult to distinguish from advanced hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy. We aimed primarily to determine the diagnostic yield and spectrum of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants among patients with an echocardiographically defined restrictive phenotype; genotype-imaging and survival comparisons were prespecified exploratory analyses.

METHODS: We screened 568 patients with cardiomyopathy who underwent whole-exome sequencing and comprehensive echocardiography. Thirty-three met the operational definition of restrictive phenotype. Variants were classified. Genotype-imaging associations and survival were analyzed exploratorily.

RESULTS: Among the 568 patients, 33 exhibited a restrictive phenotype: 7 had restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), 20 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HRCM), and 6 had dilated cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HDRCM). Variant carriers had a smaller aortic sinus diameter. In addition, MYBPC3 variant carriers had greater ventricular wall thickness and more frequent septal hypertrophy. Both the HRCM and HDRCM groups showed hypertrophic features, with interventricular septal hypertrophy occurring more frequently in the HDRCM group. The estimated 5-year survival was 54.5%, and survival did not differ significantly according to genetic-variant status.

CONCLUSIONS: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were frequent in this single-center cohort with restrictive physiology and were associated with selected imaging features. These exploratory findings support integrated genetic and echocardiographic evaluation.

articles.title: Prohibitive Effects of ω-3 on Pancreatic Damage in an Experimental Diabetes Model: Blood Glucose, Insulin, Lipid Profiles, Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, Pancreatic Tissue Morphology, and Apoptotic Pathways.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of Omega-3 (ω-3) against damage to pancreatic tissue in rats with experimentally induced diabetes using streptozotocin. Twenty-eight male Wistar Albino rats were divided into four groups: Control, Diabetes Mellitus (DM), ω-3, and DM + ω-3, with seven rats in each group. STZ was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) into the DM group, and blood glucose levels were measured on the fourth day after injection. Rats with blood glucose levels of ≥ 200 mg/dL were diagnosed with DM. The ω-3 group received 500 mg/kg of ω-3. After the 42-day experiment, pancreatic tissue and blood samples were collected from the rats. The DM group showed increased levels of malondialdehyde (MDA), total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), glucose, LDL, triglycerides, caspase-3 immunoreactivity, and histopathological abnormalities in pancreatic tissue. At the same time, there were decreases in superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), total antioxidant status (TAS), HDL, and insulin levels. Blood, biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical parameters negatively impacted by ω-3 administration have improved. This study demonstrated that in STZ-induced DM rats, DM increased oxidative capacity and led to oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and tissue damage. It was found that ω-3 has strong antioxidant, pro-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory, and protective effects.

articles.title: Persistent Endothelial Glycocalyx Disruption in Sepsis: Translational Evidence for Melatonin-Mediated Vascular Protection.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome driven by a dysregulated host response to infection, with endothelial dysfunction and glycocalyx disruption playing central roles in vascular failure. Despite growing recognition of the glycocalyx as a therapeutic target, its temporal dynamics and potential pharmacological modulation remain poorly understood. We performed a translational study combining longitudinal clinical observations in septic patients with mechanistic investigations in a murine cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model. Plasma from patients was collected at intensive care unit admission and after clinical recovery to assess inflammatory mediators, coagulation parameters, and glycocalyx-related biomarkers. In parallel, the CLP model evaluated systemic and tissue-specific glycocalyx alterations and the effects of injectable melatonin. Acute sepsis induced marked alterations in multiple glycocalyx-related biomarkers in patients, with several changes persisting despite normalization of organ dysfunction and standard inflammatory indices, indicating ongoing endothelial injury and repair. In the CLP model, sepsis reproduced these alterations, while melatonin treatment significantly attenuated systemic cytokine responses and partially restored circulating and tissue glycocalyx components in an organ- and gene-specific manner. These results highlight persistent, dynamic glycocalyx disruption as a key driver of sepsis pathology and support pharmacological stabilization of the glycocalyx as a promising therapeutic strategy. Melatonin emerges as a potential endothelial-protective agent capable of promoting vascular recovery and homeostasis, providing translational insight for interventions targeting microvascular integrity in sepsis.

articles.title: Evaluating cardiopulmonary resuscitation in "The Pitt": accuracy, clinical realism, and adherence to international resuscitation guidelines.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Medical television dramas shape public perceptions of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The Pitt has been praised for its clinical realism but has not been systematically evaluated. We assessed adherence of televised CPR to current European Resuscitation Council (ERC) and American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines.

METHODS: All cardiac arrest (CA) scenarios requiring chest compressions or defibrillation in seasons 1 & 2 (30 episodes) of The Pitt were prospectively analysed using a standardized assessment via an electronic case report form based on Utstein-style variables by at least 2 emergency and/or intensive care physicians experienced in CA management.

RESULTS: Seventeen CA were identified. Most occurred in hospital (65%, n = 11/17) and had medical causes (59%, n = 10/17). ROSC was achieved in 56% (n = 9/16), and survival to discharge in 46% (n = 6/13). Key elements of the initial assessment, including consciousness and pulse checks, were fully guideline compliant, and correct hand placement was observed in 94% (n = 15/16). In contrast, guideline-compliant compression rate were achieved in only 19% (n = 3/16) of assessable cases, respectively, and pre-airway 30:2 compression-to-ventilation ratios were absent. Immediate post-shock rhythm reassessments were observed in 78% (n = 7/9) of appropriate cases. Nevertheless, no inappropriate shocks were delivered during asystole, and rhythm-based pharmacotherapy was appropriate, although medication timing and sequence could not be reliably assessed.

CONCLUSION: The Pitt provides a highly realistic portrayal of cardiac arrest, although manual CPR technique and some algorithmic details remain imperfect.

articles.title: Understanding veteran perspectives surrounding implantable cardioverter- defibrillator decision-making.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2018, the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) mandated the use of evidence-based shared decision-making (SDM) tools for cardiovascular decisions, including implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) implantation for primary prevention in patients with systolic heart failure. Military Veterans are a unique population with experiences including combat, and heightened rates of anxiety, depression and post-traumatic stress disorder. Understanding Veteran perspectives on ICD decision-making processes is necessary to inform the Veteran Health Administration's (VHA) ICD care model.

STUDY OBJECTIVE: To understand factors influencing Veterans' ICD decision-making, semi-structured interviews were conducted with Veteran patients with an ICD (Implanters), those referred for consideration (Deliberators), and those who declined (Decliners).

METHODS: Interviews explored experiences with being offered an ICD, understanding of the device, and factors influencing personal decisions. Data were analyzed using content and thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Interviews with 13 participants revealed four primary themes that guided ICD decision-making: (1) desire for information and involvement in personal decisions, (2) quality of life values, (3) views of spirituality (4) Decliners and Deliberators accepted natural death and expressed desire to not intervene medically to prolong life.Participants valued consultation with providers and personal networks, yet ultimately prioritized autonomy. The role of mental health experiences and cohort-level differences on decision-making was inconclusive.

CONCLUSION: Participants' ICD implantation decision-making were influenced by considerations around quality of life, spiritual beliefs, and reluctance to invasively interfere with disease progression. These insights highlight the importance of personalized patient-provider interactions and the need for decision-support tools tailored to VHA Veteran care.

articles.title: Comment on "Mechanical circulatory support for haemodynamic protection in patients with heart failure during non-cardiac surgery".
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

articles.title: Potential Association of BRCA Mutation and Lymphocytic Lobulitis.
articles.abstract: Lymphocytic lobulitis (LL) is a rare fibroinflammatory breast lesion historically associated with long-standing Type 1 diabetes mellitus and autoimmune conditions. Recent evidence suggests possible links between LL and hereditary breast cancer syndromes, particularly BRCA mutations. We present the case of a BRCA1 mutation carrier who developed bilateral lymphocytic lobulitis with B-cell predominance, discuss its clinicopathologic features, and review current literature on the intersection of autoimmune, metabolic, and genetic risk pathways.

articles.title: Two Eruptive Calcified Nodules in the Same Artery.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous calcified nodule destabilization may occur in a multifocal manner, analogous to the phenomenon of multiple plaque ruptures, leading to an acute coronary syndrome. Optical coherence tomography can identify multiple eruptive calcified nodules in the same coronary artery and can influence treatment planning.

articles.title: Durability of a novel mechanical aortic valve closure technique during left ventricular assist device support: A comparative case report.
articles.abstract: Mechanical aortic valve management during left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support remains challenging. Herein, we report a novel mechanical aortic valve closure technique and its structural outcomes after >6 years of LVAD support. Compared with the conventional sandwich technique, the gap-filler technique required a shorter aortic cross-clamp time (28 vs. 69 min) and demonstrated complete structural integrity at heart explantation without patch dislocation or gross thrombus formation, suggesting superior long-term durability.

articles.title: Disparities in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and severe maternal morbidity: Evidence from a statewide birth cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) complicate 15% of pregnancies nationally and are a major contributor to severe maternal morbidity (SMM). We aimed to characterize temporal trends and demographic disparities in HDP incidence and evaluate the association between HDP and SMM in a statewide cohort.

METHODS: This study is a descriptive and regression-based analysis of a retrospective cohort of Wisconsin births from 2017 to 2023. Data were obtained from the Wisconsin Hospital Association (WHA). Subtypes of HDP were identified using ICD-10 codes. Incidence rates of HDP per 10,000 births and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were estimated using Poisson regression and examined across demographic variables. Outcomes measured included SMM incidence, AAPCs, and SMM indicators by HDP.

RESULTS: Among 388,250 pregnancies, the incidence of nearly all HDP subtypes rose from 2017 to 2023. Severe pre-eclampsia had the highest AAPC (11.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10.6%-13.0%). HDP incidence was highest in urban areas, though the AAPC in preeclampsia was greater in rural areas (8.7%; 95% CI, 7.1%-10.3%; p = 0.004). Black patients experienced higher incidences of HDP, with significant differences in AAPC for HDP overall, chronic hypertension, and severe preeclampsia (p < 0.001). Patients with HDP had higher SMM rates compared to those without, though the AAPC in SMM did not differ by HDP status.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a growing burden of HDP in Wisconsin, with an increase in severe preeclampsia incidence and disparities by geography and race. Targeted interventions in rural areas and for Black patients are needed to improve disparities in HDP incidence and reduce SMM across Wisconsin.

articles.title: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation.
articles.abstract: This practical guidance was developed by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine in collaboration with the Perinatal Medicine Foundation to support antenatal diagnosis and clinical management in pregnancies at risk for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). It provides an evidence-informed approach to screening, diagnosis, referral, and peripartum planning across healthcare settings with different resources. PAS is increasingly encountered alongside rising cesarean delivery rates, use of in vitro fertilization, and a history of uterine surgery. It remains associated with severe maternal morbidity, including massive hemorrhage, large-volume transfusion, uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, pelvic organ injury, intensive care admission, and maternal death. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are therefore central to management. Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is considered a potential precursor of PAS. Women with a low implantation site and a previous cesarean delivery are at increased risk. Early transvaginal ultrasound is advised in women with a previous cesarean delivery to establish the implantation site, identify CSP, and support counseling and timely consideration of uterine-preserving treatment. In the second and third trimesters, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound assesses placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, and the uterovesical interface. Sonographic markers include placental lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity, and bridging vessels, which may occur individually or in combination. Two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three-dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non-anterior or non-previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

articles.title: Enhanced structural reverse remodeling following LVAD support in patients with TTN truncating variants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial recovery sufficient for left ventricular assist device (LVAD) explantation remains uncommon. Titin truncating variant (TTNtv)-associated cardiomyopathy demonstrates favorable reverse remodeling with medical therapy, but its remodeling potential during durable mechanical unloading is unknown.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study of adults undergoing HeartMate 3 LVAD implantation from 2016-2025. Patients were categorized as TTNtv-associated cardiomyopathy, other genetically characterized nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM), or ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM). The primary endpoint was absolute change in left ventricular end-systolic volume index (LVESVI) during LVAD support. Multivariable and sensitivity analyses evaluated potential confounding and influential observations.

RESULTS: Among 51 patients, 7 had TTNtv-associated cardiomyopathy, 9 other NICM, and 35 ICM. TTNtv patients were younger than other NICM and ICM patients (40.5±15.8 vs 45.8±11.0 vs 67.4±9.3 years; P<0.001). Mean LVESVI decreased by 87.7±71.8 mL/m² in TTNtv patients compared with 30.4±28.3 mL/m² in other NICM and 32.6±30.6 mL/m² in ICM (P=0.039). Compared with ICM, TTNtv status remained associated with greater LVESVI reduction after adjustment for baseline LV end-diastolic diameter (β=-47.2 mL/m²; 95% CI, -75.9 to -18.4; P=0.002). Findings were directionally consistent across sensitivity analyses addressing age, post-LVAD guideline-directed medical therapy, follow-up duration, cardiomyopathy substrate, and influential observations. TTNtv patients more frequently met volumetric reverse remodeling criteria (85.7% vs 22.2% vs 57.1%; P=0.044).

CONCLUSIONS: TTNtv-associated cardiomyopathy was associated with greater structural reverse remodeling during LVAD support, particularly LVESVI reduction. Although limited by the small TTNtv cohort and potential residual confounding, these hypothesis-generating findings suggest that genetic substrate may contribute to myocardial remodeling during mechanical unloading.

articles.title: Acute eGFR Changes With Finerenone Examined in a Prespecified Analysis of FINE-ONE.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist finerenone reduces urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) in people with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). This prespecified analysis evaluated acute changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) with finerenone and their impact on safety.

METHODS: Adults with T1D and CKD (n = 242; eGFR ≥ 25-< 90 ml/min per 1.73 m2; UACR ≥ 200 to < 5000 mg/g) receiving stable renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition were randomized 1:1 to finerenone or placebo. The primary outcome was acute change in eGFR (from baseline to month 1), termed "eGFR dip." Reversibility of eGFR change was assessed from end of the treatment (month 6) to follow-up (month 7). Change in eGFR was assessed across eGFR dip subgroups (eGFR > 0 to ≤ 10% decline, > 10% decline, and ≥ 0% increase) and prespecified characteristics (baseline eGFR, UACR, history of cardiovascular disease [CVD], and diuretic use).

RESULTS: Mean acute eGFR decline at month 1 was greater with finerenone (-2.78 ml/min per 1.73 m2 [95% confidence interval [CI], -4.15 to -1.40]) versus placebo (-0.78 ml/min per 1.73 m2; [95% CI, -2.22 to 0.66]); treatment difference was -1.99 ml/min per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -3.97 to -0.01 [P = 0.049]). Placebo-corrected eGFR increased during the washout period across the groups. Acute eGFR changes did not differ according to prespecified characteristics. The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) was comparable across eGFR dip subgroups in both the treatment groups. Greater declines in eGFR were associated with greater reductions in UACR at month 3.

CONCLUSION: In people with T1D and CKD, finerenone induced an acute eGFR dip that was well tolerated without unexpected safety signals.
