articles.title: Global disparities in intestinal helminth infection dynamics among food handlers from 1990 to 2022: A call for targeted interventions.
articles.abstract: Intestinal helminths infect over 1.5 billion people globally, with food handlers serving as critical vectors in their transmission. This study aimed to quantify the transmission dynamics of intestinal helminths among food handlers by estimating the Force of Infection (FoI) and Infection Clearance Rate (ICR), providing evidence for targeted public health interventions. We employed a Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible (SIS) compartmental model, formalized by ordinary differential equations (ODEs), to estimate FoI and ICR. Crucially, these parameters were inferred from cross-sectional prevalence data rather than longitudinal individual follow-up. Models were calibrated using data from a global meta-analysis comprising 220,705 food handlers across 29 countries. We assessed variations in transmission dynamics across regions, parasite species, demographics, sample sources, environments, and diagnostic methods. Parameter optimization was performed using a differential evolution algorithm to ensure robustness. Global FoI and ICR estimates were 0.0050 and 0.0087, respectively. Since the clearance rate exceeds the force of infection, the model indicates a net decline in the prevalence of infection. Declining trends predominated across most strata, including all three regions, most demographic subgroups, and 3 of 10 parasite species. However, India and Kenya showed expanding burdens. Regionally, Asia and South America had higher transmission parameters than Africa. Nationally, Iran exhibited the highest FoI and ICR (declining trend), while Kenya showed the lowest point estimates. Trichostrongylus spp. showed the highest species-level parameters; E. vermicularis the lowest. Elevated values were observed in males, the 26-30 age group, high-HDI countries (with declining trend due to effective surveillance), illiterate individuals, and shops/restaurants. This study provides the first global estimates of FoI and ICR for intestinal helminths among food handlers, revealing significant regional, species-related, and demographic differences. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health interventions including mass drug administration (MDA), hygiene education, improved diagnostics, and stricter regulatory measures-in strata with elevated transmission pressure.

articles.title: Sex work or male-with-male sexual activity and the risks of HIV and hepatitis C acquisition among people who inject drugs: a global systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People who inject drugs (PWID) may engage in sexual behaviours that increase their HIV and hepatitis C virus (HCV) risk, including sex work and male-with-male sexual activity. We undertook a global systematic review to assess whether PWID who engage in these behaviours have higher HIV and HCV acquisition risks.

METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO for studies among PWID published between 01/01/2000 and 09/06/2026 that included estimates of the association between male-with-male sex or sex work and our primary outcomes of HIV or HCV incidence. Studies that estimated incidence by longitudinally re-testing people at risk of infection or by using assays for recent infection were eligible for inclusion. We also contacted authors for unpublished estimates. We pooled estimates using random-effects meta-analysis. We used I2 to assess heterogeneity, and we used Egger's test to assess publication asymmetry. This review is registered with Prospero (CRD42020220884).

FINDINGS: We included 57 studies comprising 164 estimates. Among men, recent male-with-male sex was associated with higher HIV acquisition (pooled incidence rate ratio (IRR):2.35; 95% CI: 1.51-3.66; I2: 51%).) but not HCV (IRR: 1.28; 95% CI: 0.95-1.72; I2: 21%). Recent sex work had a 1.72-fold (95% CI: 1.30-2.28; I2: 65%) and 1.59-fold (95% CI: 1.29-1.96; I2: 60%) higher HIV and HCV acquisition risk among all PWID, respectively. When stratified, sex work was associated with higher HIV acquisition among women (IRR: 2.30; 95% CI: 1.44-3.68; I2: 68%) but not men (IRR: 1.43; 95% CI: 0.92-2.22; I2: 51%), and was associated with HCV acquisition among men (IRR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.22-1.87; I2: 0%), but not women (IRR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.90-1.77; I2: 55%). For lifetime behaviours, only male-with-male sex was associated with HIV acquisition (IRR: 2.44; 95% CI: 1.18-5.02; I2 = 87%). Results from Egger's tests did not provide evidence of asymmetry bias for our pooled estimates, while I2 measures suggested considerable heterogeneity for many outcomes.

INTERPRETATION: PWID who also engage in sex work or male-with-male sex were found to have higher HIV or HCV acquisition risks. Future research should aim to understand the mechanisms driving these associations.

FUNDING: Medical Research Council Greater Western Four Partnership Doctoral Training Partnership, Wellcome Trust, Canadian Institutes of Health Research and Medical Research Council.

articles.title: Latest findings on complications following trans- catheter aortic valve replacement: A literature review.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis (As) is the most common valvular heart disease in developed countries, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has expanded across surgical risk groups. However, procedure-related complications remain clinically important, and their reported incidence and management have evolved with newer-generation devices and techniques. This review summarizes major TAVR complications, including their incidence and pathophysiology, risk factors, clinical impact, prevention and management, and outlines remaining knowledge gaps.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted for studies published between 2012 and 2026, including randomized trials, registries, cohort studies, and systematic reviews.

RESULTS: Major complications reviewed included Stroke, Delirium, Conduction disturbances (CD) and Arrhythmias, Bleeding/Vascular(access) site injuries/Paravalvular leak (PVL), Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), Structural valve degeneration and thrombosis, Infective Endocarditis (IE) and Coronary Obstruction (CO).

CONCLUSIONS: TAVR complications remain multifactorial, and their incidence and management continue to shift with device evolution and procedural experience. Optimized patient selection, procedural refinement, frailty assessment, and individualized antithrombotic strategies remain important areas for improving outcomes.

articles.title: Belimumab With Rituximab for the Treatment of Primary Membranous Nephropathy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: B cell depletion with rituximab (RTX) leads to complete or partial remission (CR or PR) in approximately 60% of patients with primary membranous nephropathy (PMN). Adding belimumab (BEL) to RTX may result in greater depletion of memory B cells, limit the reemergence of autoreactive B cells, and improve clinical responses.

METHODS: REBOOT Part A (NCT03949855) is a single arm, open-label, pharmacokinetic study where all participants had proteinuria (≥ 4 g/d) and detectable serum anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (anti-PLA2R) antibodies. Participants received BEL 200 mg subcutaneously weekly for 52 weeks and RTX 1000 mg intravenously at weeks 4 and 6. Assessments included BEL exposure at week 4 and CR or PR at week 104.

RESULTS: A total of 17 participants started BEL. BEL exposure was not significantly reduced in those with high proteinuria (≥8 g/day) at week 4. Among all treated participants, 10/17 (59%) achieved CR or PR at week 104, whereas in per protocol analyses, 10/11 (91%) achieved CR or PR at week 104. All participants in per protocol analyses had normal serum albumin and undetectable serum anti-PLA2R by week 104. Circulating memory B cells increased before RTX and were depleted by RTX. B cell reconstitution occurred after week 52 with primarily naive and transitional B cells. BEL with RTX was well-tolerated, with 1 participant discontinuing BEL due to infection.

CONCLUSION: In this study, a high proportion of participants receiving BEL with RTX achieved CR or PR. Therefore, a multitargeted approach to B cell depletion may improve immunologic and clinical outcomes in PMN and is being studied in a larger, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial.

articles.title: Excluding nonuniversity-certified professionals from Spain's personal training sector: a narrative review of epidemiological, legal, and economic implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spain is considering restricting personal training to university graduates, which would exclude vocationally trained professionals (NUCPs).

OBJECTIVES: To conduct an exploratory policy scenario analysis, integrating narrative evidence synthesis, descriptive epidemiology, legal proportionality assessment, and economic modeling, to examine potential public health, legal, and economic implications of excluding NUCPs, under the explicit assumption that such exclusion reduces client access to professional supervision.

METHODS: We synthesized legal, institutional, and scientific sources (January-May 2025) and developed illustrative scenario models using official workforce statistics and published injury and cost parameters.

RESULTS: Under a hypothetical supervision-reduction scenario, not empirically observed consequences of the regulation, illustrative projections suggested 8812 additional injury events annually (probabilistic 95% uncertainty interval: 3552-14,802) among clients losing supervision, with an estimated productivity cost from temporary work disability of €16,504,725 (direct healthcare costs not included). A supply elasticity model projected short-term price increases of 18% (Es = 0.5) to 30% (Es = 0.3). Available evidence did not demonstrate that university qualification per se reduces injury risk.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed exclusion lacks direct empirical support; modeled scenarios indicate potential adverse consequences under conservative assumptions. Less restrictive alternatives merit consideration.

articles.title: Predictive Performance of Polygenic Risk Scores for Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the predictive accuracy of polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and quantify associations between polygenic burden and POAG risk, predictive performance, and glaucoma-related clinical features.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: The protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Review (CRD420251067047). A systematic search of PubMed identified 161 records; 41 articles underwent full-text review and 14 met inclusion criteria. Eligible studies included adult participants from population-based cohorts, case-control data sets, and randomized or observational designs assessing genetic susceptibility to POAG, with pooled analyses restricted to European-ancestry participants. The exposure was PRS derived from genome-wide association studies; primary outcomes were predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC]) and odds ratios for POAG. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and subgroup analyses examined PRS construction method and study design as potential sources. Secondary outcomes were associations between PRS and glaucoma-related structural or functional changes. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger test, and random-effects models were applied given the substantial heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Across 14 studies (1 416 665 participants; nominal sum, reduced to approximately 692 000 after collapsing confirmed overlapping cohorts-UK Biobank and the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study), PRS showed moderate predictive performance: individual study AUCs ranged from 0.65 to 0.82, with a pooled AUC of 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.72-0.78; 10 of 14 studies with a usable AUC). Higher PRS was significantly associated with increased POAG risk on the harmonized per-standard deviation‑equivalent scale (pooled odds ratio, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.48-1.95; 9 of 14 studies). No conclusive evidence of publication bias was detected. Between-study heterogeneity was substantial, likely reflecting differences in genetic background, PRS construction, phenotype definitions, and study design; however, effect direction was consistent across studies, and influence diagnostics confirmed the robustness of the findings. Secondary outcomes, including higher intraocular pressure, faster visual field progression, and greater likelihood of glaucoma surgery, were also significantly associated with higher PRS.

CONCLUSIONS: Polygenic risk score offers moderate but consistent risk stratification for POAG and demonstrates moderate predictive accuracy across diverse study designs. Although PRS shows promise for identifying genetically high-risk individuals earlier, substantial heterogeneity and limited ancestral diversity highlight the need for large-scale, multiethnic validation before PRS can enter routine clinical practice.

FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

articles.title: A comparison of health care utilization among insured working-age adults in the state of Virginia, U.S. by long COVID and disabling condition status in 2022.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Americans with disabilities experience more medical interactions and greater access barriers than those without. After the COVID-19 pandemic, Long COVID (LCOVID) emerged as a chronic condition. Few studies examine patterns among people with disabling conditions who develop LCOVID. This study compared healthcare utilization rates among individuals with and without LCOVID and/or a potentially disabling condition (PDC) among working-age adults in Virginia's insurance plans in 2022.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis using 2021-22 administrative claims data from Virginia's All-Payer Claims Database estimated rates of primary, emergency, and inpatient care among adults aged 18-64 with PDC(s) and LCOVID. Disabling conditions were identified using specifications from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, and LCOVID was identified using the ICD-10 code U09.9. Members were grouped by PDC/LCOVID status, sex and age. We applied regression models to estimate rates and compare differences across diagnostic groups.

RESULTS: Among most groups, individuals with both PDCs and LCOVID had the highest rates of primary, emergency, and inpatient utilization. Those with LCOVID or PDC alone also often had higher utilization than those with neither.

CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the need for accessible, cost-effective care for people with disabling conditions and Long COVID.

articles.title: Procurement and Waste in Hemodialysis: A Detailed Life Cycle Assessment to Reduce Environmental Impact.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Hemodialysis (HD) is a resource-intensive treatment associated with high environmental impact. This study aimed to quantify the environmental burden of HD procurement and waste and identify key contributors to emissions, energy use, and water consumption.

STUDY DESIGN: Life cycle assessment study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Data were collected from the Nephrology Dialysis and Kidney Transplant Unit at the University Hospital Policlinico of Modena, Italy. The analysis reflects 1 patient-year of HD treatment.

EXPOSURES OR PREDICTORS: Procurement and life cycle of HD consumables and equipment.

OUTCOMES: Greenhouse gas emissions (kg CO2-equivalent), primary energy demand (MJ), and water use (m3).

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: A life cycle assessment was conducted in accordance with the International Organization for Standardization 14040/14044 standards using the OpenLCA software and the Ecoinvent database. Ten key HD products were analyzed across all life cycle stages from raw material extraction to disposal.

RESULTS: The dialyzer and bicarbonate cartridge were the largest contributors, together accounting for ∼70% of total carbon emissions. Additional impacts arose from saline solution, blood tubing, and dialysate bags. Plastic production, transport, and waste incineration were key drivers of environmental burden. Electricity use from HD machine operation also contributed substantially to total energy demand.

LIMITATIONS: This study was based on data from a single center and relied on life cycle databases that may not fully capture variability in manufacturing and disposal processes. Some consumables and clinical variations were not included.

CONCLUSIONS: HD procurement is a major source of environmental impact, largely driven by a small number of high-impact consumables. Targeted strategies including product redesign, reduction of single-use materials, and improved waste management may reduce the environmental footprint of dialysis care.

articles.title: A systematic review of observational and report-based measures of caregiver sensitivity: A Latin American perspective.
articles.abstract: Sensitivity is a cornerstone of early childhood mental health; however, its measurement relies heavily on tools developed in English-speaking, high-resource contexts. This systematic review identified observational and report-based instruments used to assess sensitivity in caregivers of children aged 0-6 years. It evaluated the methodological robustness and usability of these instruments within Latin American contexts. Following a systematic search in Web of Science, Scopus, PsycInfo, and Redalyc, 732 eligible studies were identified. Based on a frequency-of-use threshold, 16 instruments (14 observational and 2 report-based) represented across 616 papers were selected for in-depth evaluation. Measures were coded for theoretical alignment with Ainsworth's sensitivity definition, psychometric evidence, and usability-specifically training accessibility, administration complexity, and evidence of use with diverse Latin American populations (e.g., caregivers in rural settings or with lower educational levels). Results revealed that only a minority of measures adhered explicitly to Ainsworth's original definition. Most instruments prioritized warmth and positive affect, potentially leading to cross-cultural underdetection in contexts where responsiveness is expressed through proximity and routine-based care. While observational tools predominated, report-based measures showed limited validation and minimal regional use. These findings highlight the urgent need for culturally grounded validation and the development of accessible training programs for the region.

articles.title: Local Delivery of Interferon-β1a for Respiratory Viral Infections: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Respiratory viral infections represent a major global health burden, with impaired antiviral interferon responses contributing to disease progression in several respiratory conditions. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biological effects of locally delivered intranasal or inhaled interferon-β1a (IFN-β1a), a host-directed antiviral therapy, across prophylactic, therapeutic, and experimental models of respiratory viral infections. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, patent databases, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to July 2025. Peer-reviewed clinical and experimental studies, as well as relevant patent records, were identified. Patent and grey-literature sources were examined to provide a comprehensive overview of the development of locally delivered IFN-β1a and to identify relevant technological approaches that might not be captured in conventional bibliographic databases; however, these records were not considered evidence of clinical efficacy or safety. Eligible clinical and experimental evidence included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), in vitro, and in vivo studies. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised using a structured narrative and stratified approach rather than quantitative pooling. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for RCTs, ToxRTool for in vitro studies, and the SYRCLE tool for in vivo studies. Twenty-four studies met the inclusion criteria, including 12 RCTs, seven in vitro studies, one in vivo study, and four patent reports. Preclinical evidence consistently demonstrated antiviral and immunomodulatory activity, including reduced viral replication and induction of interferon-stimulated genes. Clinical studies demonstrated consistent antiviral activity and immune modulation (e.g., ISG upregulation, viral load reduction). However, clinically meaningful benefit varied across populations and was most consistent in asthma, COPD, and hospitalised COVID-19 patients, whereas other trials did not demonstrate significant improvements in their primary clinical outcomes. Early prophylactic studies in rhinovirus infection showed limited and inconsistent clinical preventive efficacy despite detectable antiviral activity. Pharmacokinetic studies supported effective airway delivery, while safety findings indicated generally favourable tolerability with predominantly mild, transient adverse events. Available evidence indicates that intranasal or inhaled IFN-β may enhance antiviral immunity and provide clinical benefit in selected respiratory viral conditions, particularly among individuals with impaired antiviral responses. However, evidence for prophylactic efficacy against community-acquired upper respiratory tract infections remains limited, and further studies are required to define optimal indications, dosing strategies, and target populations.

articles.title: Consequences of opioid exposure in disease-free cancer survivors: A systematic literature review.
articles.journal: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic pain affects a substantial proportion of cancer survivors, and opioid therapy is commonly used to manage persistent symptoms. However, as survivors transition from active treatment to disease-free survivorship, the long-term consequences of persistent opioid exposure remain poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize the consequences of opioid exposure after curative-intent treatment in disease-free cancer survivors, focusing on outcomes including survival, recurrence, opioid-related harms, opioid use disorder (OUD), and health care resource use (HRU).

METHODS: A systematic literature review was conducted, and MEDLINE and Embase were searched (January 2009-October 2024) for studies evaluating opioid exposure in cancer survivors and its association with survival, recurrence, opioid-related harms, OUD, and HRU.

RESULTS: Thirteen observational studies were included, with substantial variation in definitions of cancer survivorship and persistent opioid use. Findings regarding the association between survival and opioid exposure were mixed. Although some studies reported modest association with cancer recurrence among persistent opioid users, others reported no association at all. Opioid-related harm and health care use were the most frequently reported outcomes, which generally indicate higher risk among persistent opioid users. Only one study assessed association between persistent opioid exposure and OUD, which found no statistically significant association after adjustment for confounders.

CONCLUSIONS: Only 13 studies were reviewed, underscoring the limited and heterogeneous evidence on opioid use in disease-free cancer survivors and reflecting a high-priority knowledge gap. Although opioid exposure was consistently associated with higher risks of adverse drug events and greater HRU, findings for survival were mixed, including for cancer recurrence and OUD.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Exercise Snacks in Mitigating Adolescent Problematic Smartphone Use: A Four-Wave Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
articles.abstract: Prolonged sedentary behavior and physical inactivity are important concerns in secondary-school settings. This 6-month, four-wave cluster randomized controlled trial evaluated whether integrating high-intensity exercise snacks into the school schedule could reduce adolescent problematic smartphone use. A total of 386 adolescents from 12 classes were randomized at the class level to an intervention group, which performed four daily 2-minute bouts of vigorous physical activity during scheduled school breaks, or a wait-list control group that maintained standard routines. Primary outcomes were smartphone addiction severity and device-derived daily screen time. Secondary outcomes included psychological measures and device-derived physical activity. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and months two, four, and six. The intervention group showed lower mean SAS-SV scores and daily screen time at month four than at baseline, alongside increases in daily steps and improvements in several psychological measures. The unadjusted between-group differences in change from baseline to month four were -6.356 SAS-SV points and -46.829 min/day of screen time. The pooled model-adjusted between-group differences in change from baseline to month four were -6.55 SAS-SV points (95% CI, -7.38 to -5.71) and -52.22 min/day of screen time (95% CI, -67.21 to -37.23). During the 2-month unguided follow-up, some improvements attenuated. These findings suggest that school-based exercise snacks may help reduce problematic smartphone use. The psychological mechanisms and clinical importance of the observed changes require further investigation.

articles.title: Fertility Treatment and Risk of Melanoma: A Certainty-Rated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 3,733,499 Women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer safety after fertility treatment is well studied for breast and gynaecological tumours, but melanoma risk remains poorly characterized. We synthesized internally controlled evidence on this association.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov (2000-2025) were searched for comparative observational studies of melanoma incidence. The primary outcome was incident melanoma; treatment-pathway/SIR analyses were secondary. Hazard ratios and case-cohort relative risks (rare-disease approximation) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Hartung-Knapp) in R; SIRs were synthesized separately. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty graded using GRADE.

RESULTS: Twelve observational studies (3,733,499 women; 219,357 exposed) were included. ROBINS-E rated no study overall low risk of bias (83% some concerns, 17% high risk), reflecting incomplete ultraviolet-exposure adjustment. Melanoma risk was modestly elevated (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.02-1.50; I2 = 0%; prediction interval 0.97-1.58); drug-only ovulation induction showed a stronger association (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.01-1.92), while ART/IVF was near-null (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.81-1.48). Corresponding absolute increases were approximately 3-8, 5-13, and 1-3 per 10,000 women over 10 years (baseline 13.3-33.1/100,000/year). Certainty was very low for any fertility treatment and drug-only treatment, and low for ART/IVF. SIR-based analyses were non-significant and highly heterogeneous (SIR 1.25, 95% CI 0.66-2.38; I2 = 80%).

CONCLUSIONS: Observed associations are small and of very low to low certainty, reflecting incomplete ultraviolet-exposure and risk-factor adjustment; causality cannot be established. Current evidence does not justify changes in fertility-treatment practice. Future studies require cycle-level exposure data and rigorous ultraviolet-exposure control.

articles.title: Concept Analysis of Building Rapport in the ICU.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Building rapport, understood as establishing a meaningful and trusting relationship through interpersonal interactions between healthcare professionals and patients or their family members, was described in research as early as the 1960s. Although studies highlight its importance in clinical relationships, the concept remains largely undefined, with limited research on experiences of rapport among family members of intensive care unit patients. This concept analysis can help to provide conceptual clarity for future practice and research.

AIM: This paper aimed to analyse and define the concept of 'building rapport' with ICU family members.

STUDY DESIGN: The concept analysis framework of Walker and Avant was used, following the systematic steps of identifying uses, attributes, antecedents, consequences and model cases. Data were obtained from Swedish and English dictionaries and peer-reviewed articles identified through a systematic literature search and screening. Titles and abstracts were reviewed, and six studies were selected based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria.

RESULTS: This analysis clarifies the previously undefined concept of building rapport from the perspective of ICU family members. Building rapport is characterized by empathy and mutual understanding. Key antecedents include communication, time and relationships, while consequences are increased trust and the development of a care partnership. An empirical referent is a shift from family members as passive recipients to active participants in care.

CONCLUSIONS: Key features of building rapport with ICU family members are empathy and mutual understanding, supported by communication, time and relationships. The findings suggest that rapport may facilitate family participation and care partnerships in intensive care. However, the findings should be interpreted in light of the limited empirical basis and the absence of formal quality appraisal.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Clarifying the concept of building rapport may support communication training, reflective practice and active listening strategies that strengthen partnerships with ICU family members.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Moral Distress and Quiet Quitting in Intensive Care Nurses: The Mediating Role of Moral Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care nurses encounter numerous ethical problems in clinical practice. When these morally challenging situations remain unresolved, they may lead to moral distress and moral injury among nurses and may ultimately result in quiet quitting behaviours. Studies examining the relationships among moral distress, moral injury and quiet quitting among intensive care nurses within a comprehensive model are limited.

AIM: This study aimed to examine the relationships among moral distress, quiet quitting and moral injury among intensive care nurses.

STUDY DESIGN: The study employed a cross-sectional correlational design. It was conducted between 1 April and 31 October 2025 among intensive care nurses working in a university hospital in Türkiye. The data were collected using the Nurse Introductory Information Form, the Moral Distress-Appraisal Scale, the Moral Injury Symptom Scale-Healthcare Professional, and the Quiet Quitting Scale. The relationships among moral distress, moral injury, and quiet quitting were examined using the Pearson correlation coefficient. The statistical significance of the mediating effects was evaluated using 95% confidence intervals from 5000 bootstrap samples.

RESULTS: The study included 138 intensive care nurses. A moderate positive relationship was found between moral distress and moral injury among intensive care nurses (r = 0.524, p < 0.001). In addition, a low but statistically significant positive relationship was identified between quiet quitting and both moral injury (r = 0.258, p < 0.001) and moral distress (r = 0.201, p < 0.001). The mediation analysis revealed that moral injury played a full mediating role in the relationship between moral distress and quiet quitting (B = 0.083; 95% CI [0.003, 0.170]).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that the relationship between moral distress and quiet quitting among intensive care nurses operates through moral injury. The findings indicate that moral injury constitutes a key mechanism that negatively affects nurses' professional engagement and organisational commitment. In this context, quiet quitting may be seen as an outcome arising from unresolved ethical problems. Strengthening ethical support mechanisms to prevent moral injury is therefore important for the professional sustainability of nurses.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: These findings highlight the clinical importance of recognising and addressing moral distress and moral injury among intensive care nurses, as early interventions targeting these ethical challenges may help reduce quiet quitting tendencies and support sustained professional engagement. Accordingly, strengthening ethical support mechanisms and improving working conditions may foster a more supportive clinical environment and help sustain nurses' engagement in intensive care practice.

articles.title: Defining the conformational landscape of glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3β).
articles.journal: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology
articles.abstract: Glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3β) is a serine/threonine kinase implicated in Alzheimer's disease, type 2 diabetes, oncology and bipolar disorder, and represents an extensively pursued therapeutic target. Despite the substantial accumulation of GSK3β crystal structures in the Protein Data Bank (PDB), no systematic consolidation and conformational analysis of this dataset have been performed. Here, we manually classified all deposited GSK3β crystal structures, comprising 111 unique PDB entries and 88 distinct co-crystallized ligands (data extracted March 11th, 2026). Using the pre-existing KinCoRe dataset and standardized nomenclature, we assigned conformational states across the complete GSK3β structural ensemble and evaluated their relationships with bound ligands. All structures adopt the DFG-in kinase conformation but populate eight distinct conformational substates defined by combinations of activation-loop geometry, αC-helix orientation, regulatory salt-bridge status, αC-β5-loop and phosphorylation state. Our structural analysis reveals that chemically distinct Type I inhibitors stabilize distinct conformational substates, including variation in activation-loop arrangement and activity-like states. These relationships have not previously been characterized across the complete GSK3β crystal structure ensemble. This work provides the first comprehensive conformational landscape of resolved GSK3β crystal structures, a curated structural reference to guide the selection of potentially biologically relevant conformations for structure-based drug design and a systematic framework for analogous kinase-wide conformational analyses.

articles.title: Crystal structure of tyrosine-tRNA synthetase from Helicobacter pylori G27.
articles.journal: Acta crystallographica. Section F, Structural biology communications
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori, a major cause of gastric ulcers and cancers, infects nearly half of the world's population. The crystal structure of a potential H. pylori structure-guided drug-discovery target, tyrosine-tRNA synthetase (HpTyrRS), has been determined by the Seattle Structural Genomics Center for Infectious Disease (SSGCID). HpTyrRS is an enzyme that catalyzes the ATP-dependent attachment of tyrosine to tRNA. HpTyrRS was produced and crystallized, and its structure was determined at 2.2 Å resolution. HpTyrRS has a prototypical bacterial TyrRS topology and forms dimers in solution. HpTyrRS shares a conserved binding cavity for a previously identified Staphylococcus aureus TyrRS inhibitor (SB-219383). The reported structure and analysis establish HpTyrRS as a potential target for structure-guided drug discovery and repurposing.

articles.title: In Vivo Partial Cell Reprogramming With Yamanaka Factors Reduced Ischemic Brain Damage in Aging Mice.
articles.abstract: Aging is associated with functional decline and reduced regenerative capacity in the brain, is also the strongest risk factor for ischemic stroke, which remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, and is associated with impaired functional recovery. Here, we investigated whether short-term partial cellular reprogramming through cyclic expression of Yamanaka factors (OSKM) in a Tet-ON mouse model under Rosa-26 promoter has any impact on ischemic damage in aged mice. To assess ischemic resilience, mice underwent permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAo). Forty-eight hours after ischemia, OSKM-induced mice displayed significantly smaller damaged area compared with wild-type controls, accompanied by improved neurological scores and enhanced performance in the tightrope test, suggesting preserved sensorimotor abilities. Notably, myelin integrity was preserved in OSKM-treated mice, as shown by Black-Gold staining and stable MAG and MBP expression, whereas wild-type mice exhibited pronounced demyelination. Given the role of oligodendrocytes in myelin maintenance, we quantified the abundance of their different populations. OSKM induction significantly increased total oligodendrocytes (Olig2+) and oligodendrocyte precursor cells (PDGFRα+) following ischemia, suggesting an enhanced reparative response. Moreover, partial reprogramming preserved neuronal density in the ischemic cortex and prevented the marked astrocytic activation observed in wild-type mice, while microglial responses remained comparable across genotypes. These findings demonstrate that cyclic partial reprogramming in aged mice reduces ischemic damage, highlighting OSKM induction as a promising strategy for enhancing brain resilience during cerebrovascular accidents.

articles.title: Coptisine Protects Against Cisplatin-Induced Acute Kidney Injury With Involvement of PI3K/Akt Signaling.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin is an effective chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical use is limited by nephrotoxicity. This study investigated the protective effects of coptisine, a bioactive alkaloid from Coptis chinensis, against cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). Network pharmacology was used to predict potential targets and pathways. Cisplatin-treated HK-2 cells and lipopolysaccharide-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were used to evaluate oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation. LY294002 was used to assess the functional contribution of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling. A cisplatin-induced AKI mouse model was used to evaluate renal injury, oxidative stress, and early profibrotic remodeling. Network pharmacology identified PI3K/Akt as a potential pathway associated with coptisine. In HK-2 cells, coptisine improved cell viability, reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and apoptosis, and restored antioxidant defenses. In RAW264.7 macrophages, coptisine reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production and inducible nitric oxide synthase and cyclooxygenase-2 expression. In mice, coptisine decreased serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine levels, reduced renal levels of kidney injury molecule-1 and neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin, and attenuated tubular injury, collagen deposition, and α-smooth muscle actin expression. Cisplatin reduced the p-PI3K/PI3K and p-Akt/Akt ratios in HK-2 cells and kidney tissues, whereas coptisine restored both ratios. LY294002 partially attenuated the cytoprotective, antioxidant, and anti-apoptotic effects of coptisine in HK-2 cells. Collectively, coptisine alleviates cisplatin-induced AKI by suppressing oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, with PI3K/Akt signaling contributing to its cytoprotective effects.

articles.title: Core concepts in statistics and research methods. Part 8: randomised trials.
Point-of-care ultrasound in shock.
Renal Transplantation in Recipients With Modified Lower Urinary Tract: A Systematic Review and Implications for Adult Transplant Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with a modified lower urinary tract (MLUT) represent a growing but understudied population in renal transplantation. Concerns regarding long-term graft survival, infection, and urological morbidity persist, yet adult-specific outcome synthesis and clinically useful guidance are lacking.

METHODS: We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review of studies reporting posttransplant outcomes in adults with abnormal or surgically MLUT anatomy. Primary outcomes were 1- and 5-y graft and patient survival. Secondary outcomes included urological complications. Given substantial heterogeneity, data were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies, including 511 MLUT recipients, were identified. Most were retrospective single-center series, and only a minority included comparator cohorts. Several studies included mixed adult-pediatric cohorts where adult-only outcomes could not be separated. Across comparative studies, 1-y graft survival appeared broadly similar between MLUT and control recipients, whereas 5-y graft survival was more often lower in MLUT cohorts. Patient survival was comparable, although long-term comparative data were limited. Urological morbidity was consistently greater in MLUT recipients, particularly recurrent urinary tract infection and the need for further urological intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Renal transplantation in selected adults with MLUT is achievable with acceptable early outcomes, but the burden of urological morbidity is substantial, and longer-term graft outcomes are less favorable. These findings support careful pretransplant lower urinary tract assessment and highlight the need for pragmatic optimization pathways, although higher-quality prospective data remain necessary.

articles.title: Enterococcus faecalis bacteraemia and infective endocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of infective endocarditis (IE) in Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection (EF-BSI) vary more than 20-fold across published cohorts. We aimed to estimate the true IE prevalence, quantify the role of echocardiographic ascertainment in driving this variation, and assess the diagnostic performance of IE prediction scores.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science searched from inception to 16 August 2026; PROSPERO registration CRD420251240242) of observational studies reporting IE prevalence in confirmed EF-BSI episodes. Risk of bias was assessed with the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool. Pooled prevalence was estimated with a generalised linear mixed model (logit scale). Meta-regression with echocardiographic coverage as the moderator was used to derive an ascertainment-adjusted prevalence. Diagnostic performance of the NOVA, DENOVA, and MEFIER scores was summarised by random-effects pooling.

FINDINGS: Fifteen studies (11,157 EF-BSI episodes) were included. Crude pooled IE prevalence was 11.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 8.1-16.8; I2 = 97.3%). In studies with systematic echocardiography (k = 2), pooled prevalence was 24.2% (21.5-27.2; I2 = 0.0%). Meta-regression explained up to 91.5% of between-study variance; estimated plateau IE prevalence was approximately 30%. Pooled DENOVA sensitivity was 88.7% (78.9-94.3%) and specificity 84.0% (77.8-88.7%); prospective validation yielded sensitivity 79.2% (negative predictive value [NPV] 93.0%). NOVA had high sensitivity (95.6%) but low specificity (30.7%). Certainty of evidence was low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation [GRADE]).

INTERPRETATION: Once ascertainment is accounted for, approximately one quarter of EF-BSI episodes are complicated by IE. These findings support a shift from selective to routine echocardiography, with transoesophageal echocardiography (TEE) as the definitive modality. Existing scores can prioritise and sequence imaging but do not identify a subgroup in whom it may be safely omitted.

FUNDING: Cassa di Risparmio di Trento e Rovereto (GRAM+ TN project).

articles.title: Impact of Elderly Donors on Patient Survival and Postoperative Complications in Liver Transplantation: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation is the gold standard treatment for end-stage liver disease, yet approximately 23% of candidates die or are removed from the waitlist because of organ shortages. To expand the donor pool, elderly donors are increasingly used, but their impact on outcomes and postoperative complications remains controversial. Livers from elderly donors often show reduced regenerative capacity and diminished blood flow, which may increase posttransplant risks.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 950 adult deceased-donor liver transplantations performed at Huashan Hospital between August 1, 2017, and November 30, 2023. Recipients were divided into an elderly donor group (≥60 y; n = 201) and a younger donor group (<60 y; n = 749). The study compared overall survival, disease-free survival for hepatocellular carcinoma, and various complications.

RESULTS: Overall survival (P = 0.681) and hepatocellular carcinoma disease-free survival (P = 0.486) were similar between groups. The elderly donor group had higher incidences of primary nonfunction (PNF; 4.0% versus 0.9%; P = 0.002), acute rejection (AR; 29.4% versus 10.9%; P = 0.001), and splenic artery steal syndrome (SASS; 2.0% versus 0.5%; P = 0.045). Retransplantation was numerically more frequent in the elderly donor group (4.0% versus 1.9%; P = 0.077). After adjustment, elderly donor status remained associated with PNF (odds ratio [OR], 3.199; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.131-4.802), AR (OR, 5.314; 95% CI, 1.720-16.420), and SASS (OR, 5.881; 95% CI, 1.043-33.149), but not overall survival or retransplantation.

CONCLUSIONS: Elderly donor grafts were not associated with inferior long-term recipient survival but were associated with higher risks of PNF, AR, and SASS.

articles.title: Research progress in ocular manifestations of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis: Clinical features, mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives (Review).
articles.abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a cytokine storm-driven immune dysregulation syndrome in which ocular involvement remains critically underreported. Although isolated case reports have documented ocular findings since 1968, no prior work has systematically mapped the full phenotypic spectrum across all ocular structures, to the best of our knowledge. This gap spans both ophthalmology and hematology, where such manifestations are routinely misattributed to primary infection, autoimmunity or neoplasia. Addressing this lack of information, the present scoping review consolidates 40 peer-reviewed sources via a structured PubMed scoping search, providing the first dedicated synthesis of HLH ocular disease, to the best of our knowledge. Among the published case reports, uveitis, particularly intermediate uveitis or panuveitis, was frequently reported, and retinal pathology encompassed hemorrhage, vascular occlusive changes, serous detachment and distinct acute macular neuroretinopathy-like outer retinal atrophy. Optic nerve involvement may present as disc edema or optic neuritis, occasionally antedating systemic diagnosis, and orbital inflammation frequently mimics cellulitis. Multimodal imaging, including optical coherence tomography, optical coherence tomography angiography and fluorescein fundus angiography, delineates microstructural and microvascular alterations, contextualizing infectious etiologies, such as cytomegalovirus, human herpesvirus 8 and fungal retinitis, alongside primary HLH phenotypes. Consistent with the heterogeneous nature of the current evidence, the present scoping review maps these phenotypes without differentiating between direct HLH-mediated injury and sequelae related to immunosuppression or therapy. Despite the absence of standardized classifications, these findings underscore that ocular assessment may be informative for the early recognition and interdisciplinary management of atypical HLH presentations.

articles.title: Appearance Over Health: A Phenomenological Study of Obese Adolescents With a Family History of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in a Collectivistic Indonesian Context.
articles.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), and Indonesia ranks fifth in the prevalence of diabetes worldwide, coupled with the increasing rate of youth obesity. This phenomenological study explored adolescent obesity as a high-risk group within Indonesia's collectivistic cultural context to generate qualitative insights that may inform culturally grounded, family- and peer-supported interventions for T2DM prevention. The study does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific intervention.

METHODS: Conducted in Surakarta, Central Java, Indonesia (March 2021-April 2022), the study recruited 11 adolescents, 11 parents, and 9 peers from four primary care clinics using purposive sampling until data saturation. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's method.

RESULTS: The majority of adolescents reported being more concerned about their appearance than about their health. The findings also indicated that all groups had limited awareness of T2DM risks. Adolescents perceived intimate relationships as important in shaping healthy lifestyle choices. Peers offered emotional support and encouragement for healthier behaviors, while parents were described as supervising diet and promoting physical exercise.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that health education could potentially address adolescents' appearance-related concerns as an initial entry point to enhance engagement. For Indonesian adolescents to effectively avoid obesity and lower their risk of T2DM, strategies involving peers and parents may be an important consideration; however, these are presented as implications derived from the qualitative findings, rather than as interventions whose effectiveness has been demonstrated. Future research is needed to empirically test such culturally tailored approaches.

articles.title: Frailty in anaesthesia and intensive care.
A study of the factors associated with retinopathy of prematurity.
articles.abstract: The present study aimed to identify independent risk factors for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) in preterm infants and to evaluate the predictive utility of maternal third-trimester apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) for early risk stratification. The present retrospective case-control study enrolled preterm infants who underwent ROP screening in the Departments of Neonatology and Ophthalmology in Hebei General Hospital (Shijiazhuang, China) between September 2018 and July 2023. Infants were stratified into a no-ROP group (n=22) or an ROP group (n=80) based on findings from dilated fundus examination. Maternal third-trimester lipid profiles and serial neonatal hematological and biochemical indices (collected within 24 h of birth and at 1 week of age) were extracted from electronic medical records. Binary logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to evaluate predictive performance. Univariate analysis revealed statistically significant differences between the no-ROP and ROP groups with regard to gestational age, birth weight, 1-min Apgar score, neonatal pneumonia, neonatal bronchopulmonary dysplasia, neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, blood transfusion, maternal apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), platelet count at 24 h and 1 week, 1-week mean platelet volume, 1-week hemoglobin, 1-week neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and 1-week lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (all P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified reduced maternal third-trimester ApoA1 as the sole independent risk factor for ROP (P<0.05). ROC analysis demonstrated that maternal ApoA1 <0.584 g/l predicted increased ROP risk with 90.9% sensitivity and 67.5% specificity (area under the curve, 0.768; 95% confidence interval, 0.661-0.875; P<0.001). In conclusion, teduced maternal third-trimester ApoA1 is an independent predictor of ROP development, demonstrating high sensitivity for early risk identification. These findings support the integration of maternal lipid profiling into ROP screening algorithms and underscore the clinical importance of enhanced surveillance for infants born to mothers with reduced ApoA1 levels.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of explainable machine learning models for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Early ambulation is a notable component of postoperative recovery after cesarean delivery, but some women fail to complete first ambulation within the early postoperative period because of pain, dizziness, orthostatic discomfort, residual lower limb numbness, nausea or vomiting, hypotension or poor activity tolerance. Early identification of women at high risk of ambulation failure may support timely and individualized nursing interventions. The present study aimed to develop and internally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery using routinely collected obstetric perioperative nursing assessment data. The present single-center retrospective cohort study included relatively stable women who underwent cesarean delivery between January 2022 and December 2025 and were considered clinically eligible for early mobilization. The primary outcome was failure of first ambulation within 12 h after surgery, defined as no documented successful ambulation within 12 h or discontinuation of an ambulation attempt because of nursing-documented intolerance. Candidate predictors included demographic, obstetric, pregnancy-related, laboratory, anesthetic, surgical and early postoperative nursing assessment variables. Postoperative symptoms and vital signs were assessed within predefined early postoperative intervals, whereas first turning time was treated as a dynamically updated indicator that became available when the first spontaneous or assisted turning event was documented. The model was therefore interpreted as a dynamic early postoperative risk-assessment approach rather than a prediction model applied exclusively at a fixed 4-h time point. The final analytic dataset contained no item-level missing values; therefore, no imputation was performed. The cohort was randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts at a ratio of 7:3. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and LightGBM models were developed and compared. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, classification metrics, calibration, Brier score and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the final model. A total of 1,486 women were included, and 326 women experienced failure of first ambulation within 12 h, with an incidence of 21.9%. The training and validation cohorts included 1,040 and 446 women, respectively. In the validation cohort, LightGBM achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.809 and a Brier score of 0.132, whereas XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.805 and a Brier score of 0.134. The paired DeLong test showed no statistically significant difference between the validation AUCs of the two models (P=0.647). XGBoost achieved higher sensitivity, negative predictive value and F1 score than LightGBM (0.714 vs. 0.653, 0.906 vs. 0.892 and 0.567 vs. 0.561, respectively). Because these metrics were particularly relevant to identifying high-risk women and minimizing missed high-risk cases, XGBoost was selected as the final model. Calibration curves showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks, and decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit across relevant threshold probabilities. The 10 highest-ranked predictors according to mean absolute SHAP value were postoperative pain NRS score at 2 h, emergency cesarean delivery, time to first documented turning, lower limb numbness within 0-4 h, systolic blood pressure at 2 h, body mass index, preoperative hemoglobin, age, intraoperative fluid volume and dizziness or orthostatic discomfort within 0-4 h. In conclusion, in the present single-center retrospective cohort of relatively stable women considered clinically eligible for early mobilization, the explainable XGBoost model showed promising internal performance for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery. The model should not be extrapolated to women transferred to intensive care, women with severe postpartum hemorrhage, women with explicit medical restrictions on ambulation or women with severe postoperative complications. These findings support further evaluation but do not establish clinical utility, transportability or readiness for implementation. Temporal and external validation, followed by prospective assessment of workflow feasibility and clinical impact, is required before clinical use can be considered.

articles.title: Cilostazol ameliorates high glucose-induced osteoblast dysfunction by modulating mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling and the OPG/RANKL axis.
articles.abstract: Diabetic osteopathy, characterized by impaired bone formation and increased fracture risk, is a complication of diabetes mellitus, with chronic hyperglycemia-induced oxidative stress contributing to osteoblast dysfunction. Cilostazol (CLZ) is a selective phosphodiesterase 3 inhibitor; however, its effects on bone cell function under metabolic stress remain unclear. The present study investigated the effects of CLZ on osteoblast function and the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling network under oxidative stress induced by high glucose (HG) and glucose oxidase (GOx) in MC3T3-E1 osteoblastic cells. Osteogenic marker expression and MAPK signaling were evaluated by western blotting, while osteoblast differentiation was assessed using alkaline phosphatase and Alizarin Red S assays. Exposure to 50 mM HG and 5 mU/ml GOx markedly suppressed key osteogenic markers, including bone morphogenetic protein 2 and 7, Runt-related transcription factor 2, Osterix and collagen type I α1 chain, decreased osteoprotegerin (OPG) expression and increased receptor activator of NF-κB ligand (RANKL) expression. However, CLZ (0.1 and 1 µM) restored the expression of these osteogenic factors, increased OPG expression, decreased RANKL expression and restored alkaline phosphatase activity and mineralized nodule formation. CLZ treatment was associated with increased p38 and ERK phosphorylation and decreased JNK phosphorylation in HG/GOx-treated cells. These findings suggest that CLZ may attenuate HG/GOx-induced osteoblast dysfunction through modulation of MAPK signaling and the OPG/RANKL axis. However, further in vivo studies are required to determine its translational relevance in diabetic bone healing.

articles.title: Dyspnea Reduction With L-Menthol Inhalation Improves High-Intensity Endurance Running Performance in Healthy Trained Adults.
articles.abstract: Dyspnea occurs during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals and may limit endurance performance. Given that L-menthol inhalation can alleviate dyspnea in other contexts, we investigated whether L-menthol inhalation reduces dyspnea and improves endurance performance during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals. Nine females (mean ± standard deviation;  V ˙   O2peak = 55.8 ± 6.8 mL/kg/min) and nine males (  V ˙   O2peak = 60.3 ± 4.6 mL/kg/min) endurance runners with normal spirometry completed a randomized crossover counterbalanced trial with L-menthol inhalation or a strawberry scent (placebo). Performance was measured with a treadmill time-to-exhaustion (TTE) test at 85% of the peak velocity achieved during a preliminary cardiopulmonary exercise test. Cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and perceptual responses were measured throughout. Compared with the placebo, L-menthol inhalation reduced dyspnea across the TTE test (∼1 AU; p = 0.004) and extended the TTE test duration (406 ± 94 vs. 445 ± 106 s; p = 0.009). Pulmonary ventilation (p = 0.377), tidal volume (p = 0.298), O2 consumption (p = 0.277), CO2 production (p = 0.786), pulse O2 saturation (p = 0.766), and heart rate (p = 0.974) did not differ between conditions. Breathing frequency was lower with L-menthol inhalation than with placebo (p = 0.045). L-menthol inhalation attenuated dyspnea and enhanced high-intensity running endurance performance without substantial changes in cardiorespiratory and metabolic responses to exercise. These results suggest that dyspnea constitutes an important constraint on endurance performance during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals, and identify acute L-menthol inhalation as an effective ergogenic strategy for this exercise modality and population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (U1111-1289-3438).

articles.title: Enhancing Understanding of the Association Between Ductular Reaction and Portal Hypertension in Biliary Atresia.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

articles.title: Renal Safety and Antiviral Effectiveness of Tenofovir Alafenamide Versus Entecavir in Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B and Chronic Kidney Disease: A Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Real-world data on tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), especially in patients with advanced renal impairment, are scarce. We evaluated its renal safety and antiviral effectiveness versus entecavir (ETV) in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD). In this retrospective single-centre study, CHB patients with pre-existing CKD treated with TAF or ETV were included. The primary outcome was change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over 48 weeks. Secondary outcomes included virological, biochemical and metabolic responses. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed by CKD stage and dialysis status. Among 54 patients (35 TAF, 19 ETV), renal function remained stable in both groups. eGFR change from baseline to week 48 was not significantly different between the TAF and ETV groups (1.56 ± 8.14 vs. -0.53 ± 9.78 mL/min/1.73 m2; Δchange, 2.09; 95% CI, -0.35 to 7.68; p = 0.46). Both groups achieved sustained viral suppression, with no significant difference in undetectable HBV DNA in week-48. HBsAg reduction was greater with TAF than with ETV (-0.36 ± 0.42 vs. 0.02 ± 0.34 log10 IU/mL; p = 0.01). Exploratory analyses in patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, TAF showed effective viral suppression and renal safety regardless of dialysis status. Metabolic parameters remained stable, without complex dose adjustments. TAF was safe and effective in CHB patients with CKD, including those with advanced renal impairment. Its renal safety and antiviral effectiveness did not differ significantly from those of ETV, with the practical advantage of fixed dosing without complex adjustment.

articles.title: Rare and Novel Hepatitis C Virus Genotype Subtypes and Response to Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir in A5360 (MINMON) Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: The introduction of potent, well-tolerated direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) has transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) therapy and spurred global elimination efforts. However, the extensive genetic diversity of HCV may affect antiviral efficacy, particularly in low and middle-income regions where limited data currently exist. Using samples from the ACTG A5360 (MINMON) trial, which evaluated a minimal-monitoring strategy with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) across five countries, we characterized rare and novel HCV subtypes and assessed baseline resistance-associated substitutions (RASs) and treatment response. Genotype/subtype assignments were obtained by NS5B short-fragment sequencing and confirmed through next-generation and whole-genome sequencing. Among 399 participants, 389 (97.5%) were successfully genotyped; whole-genome sequencing in unresolved genotypes identified several provisional novel genotype 4 subtypes and a putative new genotype 7 subtype (7c). Despite the presence of baseline NS5A RASs, all participants with initially unsubtyped infections achieved sustained virologic response (SVR12). Reduced SVR was observed primarily among genotype 3b infections (78%), consistent with prior data linking A30K + L31M RASs to decreased NS5A inhibitor susceptibility. Overall, SOF/VEL achieved high SVR across genotypes, including rare and novel subtypes. These findings underscore both the increased recognition of global HCV genetic diversity and the robust performance of pangenotypic DAA regimens, supporting universal adoption of simplified treatment strategies, as proposed by the MINMON trial, towards HCV elimination. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03512210.

articles.title: Taiwan GEST-TASL-TMASO Joint Position Statement in Managing Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Obesity.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and obesity share common pathogenesis and are increasingly relevant in clinical care. This joint statement addresses the need for comprehensive guidance in Taiwan for MASLD patients with obesity. The Gastroenterological Society of Taiwan, the Taiwan Association for the Study of the Liver, and the Taiwan Medical Association for the Study of Obesity conducted an evidence-based review, integrating epidemiological data, clinical trial outcomes, and expert consensus to develop position statements covering diagnosis, disease burden, pathogenesis, surveillance, and therapeutic strategies. MASLD prevalence in Taiwanese adults is 30%-45%, reaching 60%-70% in individuals with obesity, with similar high prevalence in children and adolescents. Obesity accelerates hepatic and extrahepatic disease progression, including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and cardiovascular complications. Lifestyle interventions, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, resmetirom, and bariatric surgery demonstrate efficacy in improving hepatic and metabolic outcomes. Risk stratification using noninvasive tools such as Fibrosis-4 and vibration-controlled transient elastography effectively guides referral and management. A multidisciplinary, precision-based approach, integrating lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, surgical options, and risk stratification, is essential for effective MASLD management in patients with obesity, while research into artificial intelligence-driven biomarkers, gut microbiota modulation, and genetic factors represents future directions.

articles.title: Impact of dose reduction and multi-parametric harmonization on multi-organ radiomics robustness in total-body PET imaging: Methodological implications for quantitative theranostics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiomic features derived from positron emission tomography (PET) are sensitive to count statistics and acquisition protocol variability, thereby limiting quantitative reliability in low-dose and multi-center total-body PET imaging.

PURPOSE: This study evaluated dose robustness of PET radiomics and assessed the impact of multi-parameter ComBat harmonization on feature reproducibility.

METHODS: A multi-center total-body PET dataset comprising 550 patients from two institutions was retrospectively analyzed. Seven dose levels were simulated from list-mode data (Standard; dose reduction factors (DRF) of 2, 4, 10, 20, 50, and 100). Automatic deep learning-based segmentation was applied. A total of 107 Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI)-compliant radiomic features were extracted from standardized uptake value (SUV)-normalized images. Feature-level ComBat harmonization was performed under five configurations (scanner manufacturer, pixel spacing, radiopharmaceutical, scatter correction, and non-harmonized baseline). Reproducibility was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC (2,1)) across dose levels, organs, and harmonization settings.

RESULTS: Dose reduction produced organ- and feature-dependent effects. Overall, 32.7% of the features achieved good or excellent reproducibility (ICC ≥ 0.75) in at least one anatomical region. Selected first-order and intensity-associated features retained good reproducibility in several anatomical regions under moderate dose reduction (DRF ≤ 20), whereas severe count reduction (DRF 50-100) was associated with greater organ- and feature-dependent instability, particularly among higher-order texture features in vascular and lower-contrast soft-tissue regions. Harmonization produced organ and feature-dependent changes but did not uniformly improve cross-dose reproducibility or compensate for noise-induced instability.

CONCLUSION: Radiomics robustness in total-body PET is strongly influenced by dose level, anatomy, and acquisition variability. Moderate dose reduction preserves selected intensity-based features, while extreme count reduction compromises higher-order textures. Harmonization altered reproducibility patterns but did not uniformly improve cross-dose agreement or fully offset noise-induced instability, underscoring the need for dose-aware feature selection in multi-center PET radiomics.

articles.title: The Pros & Cons of Measuring Plasma Ammonia in the Management of Patients With Cirrhosis: An ISHEN Debate.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Ammonia is a nitrogenous molecule which is primarily generated in the gastrointestinal tract. The neurotoxicity of ammonia plays a critical role in the liver's regulation of circulating ammonia levels. In liver disease, an increase in blood ammonia has been long implicated in the pathogenesis of hepatic encephalopathy (HE), a neurological complication of liver disease. However, the clinical value of measuring plasma ammonia in patients with cirrhosis remains controversial. This dilemma was the subject of a debate held at the International Society of Hepatic Encephalopathy and Nitrogen Metabolism (ISHEN) meeting in St-Paulin, Québec, Canada in October 2025. This review illustrates the pros & cons of measuring plasma ammonia in the management of patients with cirrhosis.

articles.title: Is Cardiometabolic Risk Screening Redundant for MASLD Diagnosis in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus? A Call for Action.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

articles.title: Self-Determination in Students With Intellectual Disability: Parents' Perceptions and Associated Predictors.
articles.journal: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parents play a critical role in supporting the self-determination of students with intellectual disability. However, little is known about Chinese parents' ratings of self-determination in this population and related factors, particularly within the framework of Causal Agency Theory.

METHOD: Guided by Causal Agency Theory, this study examined Chinese parents' ratings of self-determination in students with intellectual disability and the factors predicting those ratings. A total of 262 parents completed the Self-Determination Inventory: Parent/Teacher Report Chinese Translation and a Student Information Questionnaire. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, group difference tests, Pearson correlations and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: Parents rated students' self-determination at a moderate level. Severity of intellectual disability was the only significant predictor of parents' ratings.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the need to help parents create opportunities for self-determined action across levels of intellectual disability and provide support that is responsive to students' individual needs.

articles.title: Disarming the Heat-Shock Response: Rosmarinic Acid Potentiates Mild Hyperthermia-Induced Apoptosis in A549 Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Cells.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.abstract: This study investigated the biochemical mechanisms by which rosmarinic acid (RA), a natural polyphenol, sensitizes A549 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells to mild hyperthermia (43°C). A549 cells were treated with RA (100 or 200 μM) and exposed to mild hyperthermia (43°C, 30 min), after which we performed a comprehensive analysis of cell viability, clonogenic potential, and migratory recovery. The molecular underpinnings were explored through flow cytometry for reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cell cycle progression, together with western blotting for MAPK signaling (JNK, ERK), apoptosis-related proteins (Bcl-xL, survivin, caspases), and the heat-shock response (HSP27, 70, 90, and HSF1). Our results show that the combination of RA and hyperthermia impaired cell proliferation and migration while promoting S-phase accumulation and apoptosis. At the biochemical level, combined RA and hyperthermia increased intracellular ROS beyond the level produced by either treatment alone. This rise in ROS occurred alongside an altered p-JNK/total JNK profile and caspase activation-associated apoptosis. Importantly, RA suppressed the canonical heat-shock response, lowering the p-HSF1/total HSF1 ratio and reducing the expression of the molecular chaperones HSP27, 70, and 90. Pretreatment with N-acetylcysteine (NAC) attenuated the observed ROS, Annexin V, and immunoblot changes, consistent with a contribution of redox imbalance to this sensitization process. In conclusion, RA enhanced hyperthermia-induced oxidative stress and suppressed the HSF1-HSP axis in A549 cells, providing a rationale for its further preclinical evaluation as a biochemical adjuvant in hyperthermic lung cancer therapy.

articles.title: An Individual Meta-Analysis of Psychological Treatments for Mood and Personality Disorders Using the Severity Diagnostic System of ICD-11.
articles.abstract: An individual patient meta-analysis was carried out to investigate the impact of the four levels of severity of ICD-11 personality disorder on the short-term outcome (12-24 m) of anxiety and depressive symptoms and social function in 1384 patients included in four randomised trials in which psychological treatments, mainly linked to cognitive-behaviour therapy, were compared with standard controls. In each of these trials, a proxy form of the ICD-11 classification system was used to assess personality status. The results showed that in those with more severe personality pathology, mood symptomatology was greater and showed a consistent linear trend with normal personality showing the least pathology and severe personality the most. Improvement in anxiety symptoms was significantly less in those with moderate and severe personality disorder compared with those with no personality disorder. Depressive symptoms did not show the same changes except in one trial. Social function improved in all patients in the studies. Treatment effects were small and not significantly different. The findings give some support to the dimensional system of classifying personality disorder and confirmed that all levels of personality dysfunction, including the sub-syndromal condition of personality difficulty, have an impact on mental health symptomatology and function. Suggestions for improving the utility of the classification are made. In particular, the domain structure appears to have a major influence on clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines for pediatric hepatoblastoma: a systematic review and expert recommendations from Korea.
articles.abstract: Hepatoblastoma (HB) is the most common primary liver malignancy in children, predominantly affecting those younger than 3 years of age. Although the overall survival rate has improved significantly over the past few decades, standardized clinical practice guidelines for HB in Korea have been lacking. This clinical practice guideline was developed to provide evidence-based recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of HB in children. A multidisciplinary working group comprising pediatric hematologists/oncologists, radiologists, surgeons, pathologists, and methodologists systematically reviewed the literature published up to May 2023. For pretreatment imaging, both abdominal computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are useful for PRE-Treatment EXTent of disease (PRETEXT) staging, with each modality offering distinct advantages. PRETEXT staging at diagnosis is recommended as it provides valuable prognostic information. For standard-risk HB (PRETEXT I-III without metastasis and alpha-fetoprotein ≥100 ng/mL), cisplatinbased chemotherapy without doxorubicin is recommended over cisplatin-doxorubicin combination therapy, as it demonstrates equivalent survival outcomes with fewer adverse effects. In carefully selected patients who are eligible for complete resection at diagnosis, upfront surgery without neoadjuvant chemotherapy should be considered to spare unnecessary chemotherapy and its toxicities. For patients with residual pulmonary metastases after chemotherapy, pulmonary metastasectomy should be considered. Sodium thiosulfate administration following cisplatin should be considered to reduce ototoxicity, although the supporting evidence is derived predominantly from standard-risk patients and its availability in Korea remains limited. Regarding histological subtypes, well-differentiated fetal HB is associated with favorable outcomes and may be treated with surgery alone, whereas the small cell undifferentiated pattern is no longer classified as a HB subtype and requires immunohistochemical and molecular testing to distinguish it from malignant rhabdoid tumor and other small round cell tumors. This guideline represents the first evidence-based clinical practice guideline for pediatric HB in Korea. It aims to standardize the diagnostic and therapeutic approaches, ultimately improving outcomes for Korean children with HB. Given the rarity of this tumor, international collaboration and prospective data collection remain essential for future guideline updates.

articles.title: National Trends and Predictors of Adverse Outcomes in Hypoglycemia Hospitalizations in the United States, 2017-2022.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess national trends and inpatient outcomes among adults hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of hypoglycemia in the United States from 2017 to 2022.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample.
