Adult hospitalizations aged 18 years or older with a principal ICD-10-CM diagnosis of hypoglycemia were included. The annual share of primary hypoglycemia hospitalizations was calculated per 100,000 adult NIS discharges. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay(LOS), and inflation-adjusted hospital cost standardized to 2022 US dollars. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression was used for mortality, a survey-weighted generalized linear model (GLM) with a quasi-Poisson distribution and log link was used for LOS, and a survey-weighted GLM with a gamma distribution and log link was used for inflation-adjusted hospital cost.

RESULTS: The analysis included 330,910 weighted hypoglycemia hospitalizations. Mean age was 67 years; 52% were women; and 70% were Medicare-insured. Diabetes mellitus (91%) was the most common comorbidity, while obesity (17%) was least common. Primary-hypoglycemia discharges peaked in 2019 (195 per 100,000 adult NIS discharges), declined in 2021 (180), and increased again in 2022 (190). Mortality occurred in 1.6%, and median LOS was 3 days. Compared with 2017, adjusted mortality odds were higher in 2020 (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.04-1.61), 2021 (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.16-1.79), and 2022 (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.07-1.65). Similarly, LOS and hospital costs were also higher in 2020, 2021, and 2022 compared to 2017. Congestive heart failure (CHF) and AF were associated with higher mortality odds, LOS, and cost.

CONCLUSION: Primary hypoglycemia hospitalizations declined during the pandemic years but became more severe and resource-intensive over time. Patients with CHF or AF had higher mortality, higher LOS, and higher hospital costs, highlighting the need for integrated hypoglycemia surveillance and cardiometabolic care.

articles.title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number and Mitochondrial Homeostasis Genes in Acute and Stable Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in coronary artery disease (CAD), but the relationship between mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) and mitochondrial homeostasis across CAD presentations remains unclear. We investigated mtDNA-CN together with the expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α and TFAM) and mitophagy (PINK1) in patients with stable angina (SA) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

METHODS: This observational study included 334 patients: 170 ACS, 117 SA and 47 individuals with non-obstructive coronary arteries (NCA). Peripheral blood mtDNA-CN and the expression of PGC-1α, TFAM and PINK1 were quantified by real-time PCR. Associations with clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were evaluated.

RESULTS: ACS patients exhibited significantly lower mtDNA-CN than SA and NCA groups (p = 0.01 and p = 0.004, respectively). PINK1 expression was reduced in both ACS (p = 0.005) and SA (p = 0.01) compared with NCA. TFAM expression was increased in SA (p = 0.009), while PGC-1α expression was higher in ACS (p = 0.02). MtDNA-CN and mitochondrial biomarkers were inversely associated with inflammatory markers, whereas mtDNA-CN and TFAM correlated positively with LVEF. Lower mtDNA-CN was independently associated with ACS (OR = 0.98, p = 0.0004) and SA (OR = 0.99, p = 0.04), while higher PINK1 expression was associated with reduced odds of SA (p = 0.03) and ACS (p = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Mitochondrial markers are altered across CAD phenotypes. ACS is characterized by lower mtDNA-CN and altered expression of mitochondrial homeostasis-related genes, whereas SA shows a pattern consistent with a possible compensatory response. Combined assessment of mtDNA-CN and mitochondrial homeostasis-related gene expression may provide a novel biomarker strategy for CAD risk stratification and targeted therapies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: VICTORIA study, (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06313645).

articles.title: Leptin Neutralization Attenuates Inflammaging in Endothelial and Immune Cell Models.
articles.abstract: Leptin, a proinflammatory adipokine, contributes to the chronic low-grade inflammation seen in obesity, but its role in age-related inflammation, that is inflammaging, has been poorly studied. We thus tested the effect of blocking leptin receptor (LEP-R) binding in five models of inflammaging, that is replicative senescent endothelial cells, hyperglycemia-treated macrophages or endothelial cells, lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-exposed macrophages, and TCR-stimulated CD4+ T cells. In endothelial cells, leptin enhanced senescence, while leptin neutralization suppressed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, two effects mediated in part by the mTOR pathway. In both macrophages and endothelial cells, leptin blockade blunted hyperglycemia-induced inflammation, while in macrophages, it also suppressed the LPS-induced senescent and proinflammatory phenotype. In T cells, leptin neutralization produced divergent effects, attenuating the expression of inflammatory and senescence markers in conventional T cells but not in regulatory T cells. To assess translational relevance, we measured leptin and inflammaging markers in plasma samples from two independent cohorts, one of healthy individuals (n = 121) and another of people with Type 2 diabetes (n = 93). In healthy subjects, leptin levels were higher in people with hs-CRP ≥ 3 mg/dL compared with those below such threshold, also after adjustment for BMI. Leptin levels showed BMI-adjusted positive correlations with IL-6 and hs-CRP in healthy individuals and with hs-CRP and IL-8 in people with diabetes. These findings suggest that leptin might fuel inflammaging and that its neutralization exerts anti-inflammatory effects across multiple, related models.

articles.title: Multi-Omics Insights Into Circulating T-Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and Treg Dysfunction in Moyamoya Disease.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disease linked to immune dysregulation, yet T-cell metabolic reprogramming and regulatory T-cell (Treg) function remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated multi-omics approaches, including mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and flow cytometry to characterize T-cell metabolic alterations and Treg dysfunction in MMD, uncovering a key metabolic-immune axis. Compared with healthy controls, MMD patients showed chronic immune activation and broad suppression of amino acid, glycolytic, and fatty acid metabolic pathways. Although Tregs were aberrantly expanded, they displayed metabolic inflexibility, together with impaired intercellular communication. Single-cell transcriptomics indicated Treg-to-Th17 conversion, while flow cytometry confirmed increased IL-17A+ cells within the CD4+FOXP3+ compartment. Besides, these dysfunctional Tregs correlated with advanced Suzuki stages, ischemic stroke, and posterior cerebral artery involvement. Bulk transcriptomic and serum metabolomic analyses further confirmed coordinated immune activation and metabolic suppression at the gene, protein, pathway, and metabolite levels. These findings define a metabolic-immune axis in MMD in which metabolically constrained, functionally unstable Tregs may contribute to neuroinflammation and vascular remodeling, suggesting that restoring Treg metabolic fitness could represent a therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Recurrent Fetal Intracranial Hemorrhage and a Maternally Inherited COL4A1 Variant of Uncertain Significance: A Case Report With Maternal Reverse Phenotyping.
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old woman with two consecutive pregnancies affected by fetal left periventricular germinal matrix hemorrhage (Grade IV) and progressive ventriculomegaly underwent trio whole-exome sequencing. A heterozygous COL4A1 c.4249G>C (p.Gly1417Arg) variant, classified as a variant of uncertain significance, was identified in the fetus of the current pregnancy and found to be maternally inherited; concurrent copy-number analysis incidentally detected a maternal 17p12 microdeletion encompassing PMP22, which was not inherited by the fetus. Systematic reverse phenotyping of the mother revealed right corticospinal tract Wallerian degeneration, persistent microscopic hematuria, a renal cyst, and retinal arteriolar changes-a phenotype compatible with the COL4A1-associated spectrum, although molecular causality remains unproven. Following multidisciplinary review, the pregnancy was terminated at 29 weeks, primarily on the basis of the grave fetal prognosis, with early-onset preeclampsia contributing to the overall maternal risk assessment; the mother's post-termination course was uneventful, with resolution of hypertension and proteinuria. This case illustrates that recurrent anatomically congruent fetal intracranial hemorrhages may prompt maternal reverse phenotyping that identifies maternally inherited COL4A1 variants of uncertain significance, and underscores the need to distinguish phenotypic concordance from proven molecular causality in prenatal counseling.

articles.title: Klebsiella pneumoniae Epidural Abscess Presenting as Tubercular Spondylodiscitis: A Diagnostic Pitfall in a Diabetic Patient From Nepal.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae spinal epidural abscess is rare and can mimic tuberculous spondylodiscitis in endemic regions. We report a diabetic patient with pulmonary tuberculosis presenting with lumbar spondylodiscitis and epidural abscess. CT-guided biopsy identified Klebsiella pneumoniae, with no evidence of tuberculosis. Ceftriaxone led to recovery, highlighting the importance of tissue-based diagnosis.

articles.title: Perspective: Water and Electrolytes in Daily Hydration Compared with Acute Rehydration: Expert Consensus and Research Priorities.
articles.abstract: Adequate hydration is essential for the normal functioning of the body and health. Adequate hydration is affected by the diet, environmental conditions, social norms, personal preferences, cultural traditions, medical issues, and physical activity. Much research has been conducted on how to best measure various states of hydration, as well as the physiology underlying the regulation of osmolality and hydration. The most current evidence suggests that there is no single reference standard for measuring hydration status, and the most reliable biomarker can vary across situations. Much research has been conducted to understand the physiological processes that regulate hydration (e.g., vasopressin), as well as the associations between hydration, diet, and health. Much of this research has been conducted in animals or as observational studies. There is a need for clinical trials to evaluate causal relationships among diet and lifestyle, physiological regulation, hydration status, and health outcomes. On the basis of the most current evidence, consensus statements, action items, and future research needs were developed.

articles.title: Access to Genetic Testing in Patients With Suspected Genetic Kidney Disease in Europe.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A genetic diagnosis can transform care for patients with monogenic kidney disease-guiding treatment, prognosis, family-planning, and care for relatives. Despite technological advancements, nephrologists still experience barriers to implementing diagnostic genetic testing in daily practice.

METHODS: We surveyed 240 pediatric nephrologists, adult nephrologists, and clinical geneticists across 39 European countries on the accessibility of and barriers to genetic testing for suspected genetic kidney disease. Using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) model, we assessed barriers at national, hospital, individual, and implementation-process levels. Results were stratified by region (North, East, South, West Europe, and non-Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries). Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with barrier experience.

RESULTS: Overall, 97% regarded genetic testing an important tool to improve care, yet 50% experienced barriers in daily practice. Median barrier severity score was 4.0 (interquartile range [IQR] 4, scale 1-10). Non-OECD countries showed higher scores (6.8 (IQR 3.6), P < 0.001). Most reported national-level barriers were lacking clear professional guidelines and concerns about posttest insurability. Hospital-level barriers included insufficient clinic's resources (costs, time, technical facilities, and staffing), missing protocols for eligible patients or workflow and turnaround time (nonurgent: 12 weeks [IQR 12], urgent: 3 weeks [IQR 2]). Ranking barriers by region revealed a gradient from fewest barriers in Northern Europe, followed by West, South, East, and most in non-OECD countries. Lack of external funding and non-OECD origin were associated with barriers.

CONCLUSION: We identified barriers that must be addressed at a European level and within regions. We provide recommendations to promote equitable care for patients with suspected hereditary kidney disease in Europe.

articles.title: Monocyte to large platelet ratio as a diagnostic marker for acute pulmonary embolism.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially life-threatening diagnosis that commonly presents to the emergency department with nonspecific symptoms. Despite advances in diagnostic algorithms, rapid identification remains challenging, particularly when definitive imaging is delayed or unavailable. Simple and readily available biomarkers may assist in the early evaluation of patients with suspected PE. This study investigated the diagnostic value of the monocyte-to-large platelet ratio (MLPR), a novel inflammation- and thrombosis-related biomarker, in acute PE.

METHODS: This retrospective exploratory study reviewed 115 medical records of patients presenting with suspected PE to the emergency department between January and December 2024 who underwent computed tomography pulmonary angiography. After applying exclusion criteria, 53 patients were included (25 PE, 28 non-PE). Admission complete blood count parameters, including MLPR, monocyte and lymphocyte counts, and derived ratios, were analyzed.

RESULTS: Age and sex distribution were similar between groups. Total leukocyte, monocyte, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts were significantly higher in the PE group, alongside significantly elevated MLPR (1.19 ± 0.45 vs. 0.61 ± 0.39; P < 0.001), while NLR did not differ significantly (P = 0.4235). MLPR demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance among individual hematological markers (AUC 0.854, 95% CI 0.752-0.956; P < 0.001). Combining MLPR with lymphocyte count further improved diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.907, 95% CI 0.827-0.986), achieving 92% sensitivity and 85.7% specificity.

CONCLUSION: MLPR is a promising, readily available biomarker for diagnosing acute PE, with enhanced performance when combined with lymphocyte count.

articles.title: Persistent Body Mass Index Profiles During Adolescence: Associations With Brain Maturation and DNA Methylation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical period for the emergence of obesity and disordered eating behaviors, yet the biological mechanisms underlying persistent differences in body mass index (BMI) development remain poorly understood. We investigated whether longitudinal BMI profiles are associated with behavioral, neurodevelopmental, and epigenetic variation during adolescence.

METHODS: Participants from the IMAGEN cohort (N = 1296) were followed from ages 14 to 23 years. Latent profile analysis identified longitudinal BMI profiles. Disordered eating behaviors were repeatedly assessed across adolescence. Structural magnetic resonance images acquired at ages 14 and 23 characterized longitudinal changes in gray matter volume (GMV), cortical thickness (CT), and sulcal depth. Genome-wide DNA methylation (DNAm) was measured in whole blood at age 14. We conducted epigenome-wide association studies (EWASs) and functional enrichment analyses and evaluated a DNAm-based BMI risk score (bmiMRS).

RESULTS: Two distinct BMI profiles were identified: a persistently overweight group and a persistently normal-weight group. Adolescents with persistent overweight showed progressively increasing BMI; greater eating-, weight-, and shape-related concerns; and more frequent dieting and binge-eating behaviors. They also exhibited atypical cortical maturation, characterized by attenuated cortical thinning, accelerated reductions in sulcal depth, and reduced gray matter volume loss within frontal and temporal association cortices. EWAS identified 29 BMI-associated CpGs (Bonferroni-corrected p < 1.3 × 10-7), enriched for genes involved in adipogenesis, immune and inflammatory signaling, type 2 diabetes, and brain-related biological processes. The bmiMRS predicted BMI, cumulative BMI across adolescence, and membership of the persistently overweight group and remained significantly associated with BMI in an independent cohort. Longitudinal analyses further suggested reciprocal associations between BMI and brain maturation, with higher BMI in early adolescence predicting subsequent regional GMV changes, whereas lower baseline CT predicted greater BMI increases independently of baseline BMI.

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent adolescent overweight is associated with distinct behavioral, neurodevelopmental, and peripheral epigenetic signatures. Integrating longitudinal neuroimaging and DNAm identifies molecular biomarkers and brain developmental features associated with sustained BMI elevation, providing a framework for earlier risk stratification and informing biologically grounded approaches to obesity prevention.

articles.title: Inflammatory Biomarkers as Predictors of In-Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill COVID-19 Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Inflammatory biomarkers have been proposed as prognostic indicators in COVID-19; however, their prognostic associations within critically ill ICU-admitted patients remain of interest. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of selected inflammatory biomarkers with in-hospital mortality and their discriminatory performance among critically ill COVID-19 patients.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 244 adult patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia admitted to the ICU between August 2020 and June 2021 were analyzed. Disease severity was assessed using the ISARIC 4 C Mortality Score. Associations between inflammatory biomarkers and mortality were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and discriminatory performance was assessed using ROC curve analysis.

RESULTS: The in-hospital mortality rate was 90.6%. ESR and LDH levels were significantly higher in non-survivors. In a biomarker-restricted multivariable logistic regression model, ESR (OR 1.023 per 1 mm/h increase; 95% CI 1.004-1.042; p = 0.016) and LDH (OR 1.002 per 1 U/L increase; 95% CI 1.000-1.003; p = 0.009) remained significantly associated with in-hospital mortality after mutual adjustment for the other prespecified inflammatory biomarkers. LDH demonstrated good discriminatory performance (AUC 0.725; 95% CI 0.645-0.805). ESR showed modest discriminatory performance (AUC 0.646; 95% CI 0.559-0.732).

CONCLUSION: ESR and LDH remained significantly associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for the other prespecified inflammatory biomarkers. These findings suggest that ESR and LDH may provide adjunctive prognostic information in critically ill ICU patients; however, they should be interpreted in the context of the biomarker-restricted model and the limited adjustment set. Confirmation in larger prospective studies incorporating established clinical prognostic factors is warranted.

articles.title: Navigating Professional Code of Conduct Among Undergraduate Dental Students in Pakistan: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non-maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. In Pakistan, these expectations are shaped by international bioethical principles, national professional regulation, and local social and religious contexts.

AIM: To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences.

METHODS: A qualitative narrative inquiry was conducted over 6 months (November 2020-April 2021) at two dental colleges in Peshawar, Pakistan, one public and one private. Purposive sampling was used to recruit clinically exposed undergraduate dental students. Fifty students were approached and 37 participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Template Analysis. The report follows the COREQ framework and makes the analytic, reflexive, and trustworthiness procedures explicit.

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 20.9 ± 1.96 years (range 17-25); 29 (78.4%) were female and 8 (21.6%) male. Four interconnected themes were identified: unprofessionalism, harassment, poor communication, and discrimination. The accounts included concerns about infection control, empathy, accountability for clinical error, dishonesty, physical/verbal/emotional harassment, inadequate instruction, failures of informed consent, abuse of power, victimization, and targeting.

CONCLUSION: Students' accounts point primarily to breaches of professional conduct and to tensions between formal ethical expectations and the hidden curriculum of clinical learning. Professionalism education should therefore be embedded longitudinally in dental curricula and reinforced through faculty role-modeling, safe reporting pathways, supervised clinical practice, and context-sensitive ethical reasoning that can hold universal duties together with legitimate cultural and religious considerations.

articles.title: The Effects of Poor Self-Care Behaviors on Uncontrolled Hypertension in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hypertension affects nearly one in five adults in Ethiopia. Effective self-care behaviors, including medication adherence, regular physical activity, healthy dietary practices, weight management, moderation of alcohol intake, and avoidance of tobacco, are essential for optimal blood pressure (BP) control. Although individual studies have examined these behaviors, their combined contribution to uncontrolled hypertension in Ethiopia has not been comprehensively synthesized. This study aimed to evaluate the pooled effects of inadequate self-care behaviors on uncontrolled BP among hypertensive patients in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Electronic databases and gray literature sources were searched to identify observational studies reporting associations between self-care behaviors and uncontrolled hypertension in Ethiopia. Eligible studies were screened, and data were extracted using standardized tools. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using STATA version 17.0 to estimate pooled odds ratios (PORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Inadequate self-care behaviors were significantly associated with uncontrolled hypertension. Medication non-adherence (POR: 2.29, 95% CI: 1.90-2.77), poor salt restriction (POR: 3.33, 95% CI: 1.83-6.07), insufficient physical activity (POR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.53-2.77), inadequate weight management (POR: 2.31, 95% CI: 1.85-2.88), alcohol consumption (POR: 2.54, 95% CI: 1.37-4.73), and smoking (POR: 2.73, 95% CI: 1.51-4.94) were associated with higher odds of uncontrolled BP. Moderate to high heterogeneity was observed across studies. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of findings, and no significant publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: Poor self-care practices substantially contribute to uncontrolled hypertension in Ethiopia. Strengthening patient-centered interventions targeting adherence and lifestyle modification is essential to improve BP control and reduce hypertension-related complications.

articles.title: Beyond Pigmentation: Interplay of Metabolic Profile, Carotid Intima-Media Thickness, and Fatty Liver in Vitiligo: An Age- and Sex-Matched Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Vitiligo shares inflammatory and metabolic pathways with cardiovascular and hepatic steatosis. Carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) is an established marker of early subclinical atherosclerosis, whereas non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) reflects hepatic involvement in chronic inflammatory and metabolic dysregulation. This study aimed to evaluate subclinical vascular and hepatic changes in patients with vitiligo and to explore their associations with disease characteristics and metabolic parameters.

METHODS: In this age- and sex-matched case-control study, adults with mild vitiligo (Vitiligo Area Severity Index [VASI] < 5%) and no metabolic syndrome were compared with healthy controls. Participants underwent carotid duplex ultrasonography to assess common carotid IMT and atherosclerotic plaques, liver ultrasonography for steatosis grading, and laboratory testing, including lipid profile (total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein [LDL], high-density lipoprotein [HDL], and triglycerides [TG]), fasting blood glucose (FBS), and body mass index (BMI). Disease duration and VASI score were also assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 46 participants (23 patients with vitiligo and 23 healthy controls) completed all assessments. Common carotid IMT measurements and liver ultrasound findings were comparable between groups. However, abnormal HDL levels were more frequent among patients with vitiligo (69.6% vs. 39.1%, p = 0.03). Greater disease severity, measured by VASI score, and higher BMI were independently associated with increased right carotid IMT (p = 0.01, 0.02, respectively). Exploratory interaction analyses demonstrated significant sex-dependent associations of HDL, triglycerides, and fatty liver status with carotid IMT. Post hoc analyses identified higher carotid IMT among male patients with abnormal HDL.

CONCLUSION: Selected subgroups of patients with vitiligo, particularly men with HDL metabolic abnormalities, may exhibit differences in subclinical carotid atherosclerosis. Disease severity and BMI may also contribute to the vascular risk. Although exploratory, these findings warrant further investigation of cardiovascular and hepatic risk profiles in selected patients with vitiligo.

articles.title: Lung-Reporting and Data System Category (Lung-RADS) and Adherence to Low-Dose Computed Tomography Screening and Recommended Follow-Up: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adherence to guideline-recommended low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening and follow-up remains suboptimal, and determinants may vary by Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) category.

METHODS: This retrospective, multi-site cohort study used electronic medical records from adults aged 50 to 80 years. Eligible individuals had at least one primary care visit in the previous 12 months, no lung cancer diagnosis in the preceding 5 years, and underwent an index low-dose CT between 2016 and 2021. Participants were followed through 2022. Adherence to follow-up chest CT within 11 to 15 months (Lung-RADS 1-2) and category-specific recommended follow-up (Lung-RADS 3-4X) was assessed using mixed-effects logistic regression to estimate adjusted ORs (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 22,034 individuals with Lung-RADS 1 to 2, 21.67% completed follow-up CT within 11 to 15 months. The odds of adherence were higher among individuals aged 65 or more years (versus <65) (aOR = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.14-1.31) and those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (aOR = 1.18; 95% CI: 1.09-1.27) and lower among black (versus white) individuals (aOR = 0.87; 95% CI: 0.79-0.96) and frail (versus non-frail) individuals (aOR = 0.88; 95% CI: 0.80-0.98). Among 4518 individuals with Lung-RADS 3 to 4X, 28.51% adhered to category-specific follow-up; COPD was the only factor independently associated with adherence (aOR = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.06-1.40).

CONCLUSION: Adherence to follow-up CT and recommended care remains low in real-world settings; older age and COPD predicted higher adherence, while lower adherence among black individuals identifies a key target for improving lung cancer screening retention.

articles.title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear.

METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed.

RESULTS: Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01, P = .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70, P < .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (P for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33, P for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

articles.title: Alder-Reilly Anomaly Leading to Incidental Diagnosis of MPS VII in an Asymptomatic Adult.
articles.abstract: Mucopolysaccharidosis type VII (MPS VII; Sly syndrome) is a rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of β-glucuronidase due to pathogenic variants in the GUSB gene. Impaired degradation of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) results in multiorgan dysfunction with highly variable clinical presentation, ranging from severe neonatal disease to attenuated adult phenotypes. We report an incidental diagnosis of MPS VII in a 31-year-old woman identified through routine laboratory testing. Review of a peripheral blood smear was prompted by automated hematology analyzer flags and revealed Alder-Reilly anomaly with characteristic aberrant leukocyte granulation. Subsequent biochemical analysis showed elevated urinary dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate, alongside reduced β-glucuronidase activity (~2%-3% of normal). Genetic testing of GUSB identified compound heterozygosity for a likely pathogenic frameshift variant (c.133_134del) and a missense variant (c.454G>A) previously associated with pseudodeficiency. Despite biochemical and genetic findings consistent with MPS VII, the patient exhibited no typical clinical manifestations, and detailed phenotyping showed no organ involvement. This case illustrates an atypical, asymptomatic presentation of MPS VII diagnosed in adulthood, in which Alder-Reilly anomaly served as a critical diagnostic clue. The combination of a null allele with a pseudodeficiency-associated variant resulted in reduced enzyme activity without overt disease. These findings highlight the importance of peripheral blood smear evaluation in identifying lysosomal storage disorders and underscore the complexity of genotype-phenotype correlations in MPS VII.

articles.title: Endurance Training Improves Insulin Sensitivity, Metabolic Flexibility, and Mitochondrial Function in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
articles.abstract: To determine how endurance training influences insulin sensitivity, metabolic flexibility, and mitochondrial function in individuals with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D). Insulin sensitivity (2-step hyperinsulinaemic-isoglycaemic clamp), metabolic flexibility, and mitochondrial respiratory capacity and H2O2 emission were assessed in participants with T2D (n = 15) and controls (n = 14) before and after 12 weeks of supervised endurance training. Sensitivity analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models including all available participants. At baseline, glucose clearance was lower in individuals with T2D compared with controls. Training increased glucose clearance (mL/min/kg FFM) in both groups, with larger model-derived improvements in T2D (Step 1: +1.43 [0.88-1.97]; Step 2: +3.18 [2.12-4.23]) than in controls (Step 1: +0.76 [0.21-1.31]; Step 2: +1.49 [0.53-2.45]). The group × time interaction was significant at the higher insulin step. Metabolic flexibility to fat-but not glucose-was reduced in T2D and improved modestly with training. Mitochondrial respiratory capacity did not differ between groups; however, training decreased mitochondria-specific respiration and H2O2 emission normalized to CS activity and respiration. Endurance training enhances insulin sensitivity and fat oxidation in individuals with T2D and induces favorable mitochondrial adaptations, despite the absence of intrinsic mitochondrial dysfunction.

articles.title: Diastereomer-selective developmental toxicity of cis- and trans-permethrin in zebrafish (Danio rerio) embryos: AI-assisted analysis of seizure-like behaviors.
articles.abstract: Permethrin (PM) has been widely used to control insect pests, including mosquitoes, flies, scabies, and mites. Its use for agricultural purposes is strongly restricted because of its high toxicity to aquatic organisms. Nevertheless, PM continues to be detected in aquatic environments, and formulations containing different diastereomeric ratios of cis-PM and trans-PM (40:60 or 25:75) are still used in the field. In this study, the developmental toxicities associated with the diastereomeric properties of PM were evaluated using zebrafish (Danio rerio) embryos. Although neither PM diastereomer significantly affected survival or hatching rates, cis-PM induced dose-dependent developmental toxicity in zebrafish embryos, including reductions in body length and eye area, as well as yolk sac abnormalities, whereas trans-PM did not cause noticeable morphological alterations. Regarding cardiotoxicity, both cis-PM and trans-PM increased heart rate, while cis-PM additionally elevated stroke volume and ejection fraction. Neither PM diastereomer showed severe toxicity toward liver development; however, only cis-PM caused pronounced neurological disorders, including significant reductions in midbrain and hindbrain area, decreased locomotor activity, and seizure-like events identified using AI-assisted analysis. In addition, cis-PM produced more pronounced region-specific apoptotic responses and increased reactive oxygen species generation compared with trans-PM. Furthermore, oxidative stress- and estrogen-related genes were downregulated in cis-PM-treated embryos. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that cis-PM exerts stronger developmental toxicity in zebrafish embryos than trans-PM, particularly with respect to brain development and behavioral abnormalities, including seizure-like events.

articles.title: The entorhinal cortex atrophy score for diagnostic distinction between phases of the Alzheimer's disease continuum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common type of dementia, causing functional impairment in millions of individuals and accounting for a large amount of healthcare costs. The entorhinal cortex appears to be one of the first brain structures affected by AD in its early stages. The Entorhinal Cortex Atrophy (ERICA) score is a visual atrophy score used by neuroradiologists in clinical practice for the diagnosis of AD.

OBJECTIVE: To analyze the effectiveness of the ERICA score for distinguishing between patients with subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD dementia.

METHODS: A systematic review of the literature was conducted on the Science Direct, PubMed, Virtual Health Library, and Cochrane databases, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Of 1,413 studies identified, 6 were ultimately included in the present review, comprising 844 participants: 2 retrospective cohort studies and 4 cross-sectional studies. The methodological quality of the studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. The focus was on the diagnostic performance of the ERICA score in the continuum phases of AD.

RESULTS: The ERICA score had lower sensitivity than the medial temporal lobe atrophy (MTA) score but higher specificity, reinforcing its importance for diagnostic accuracy, especially in contexts of clinical uncertainty. The ERICA score showed reproducibility between examiners similar to or greater than that of the MTA score. There are a few heterogeneous studies in the current literature on the applicability of the ERICA score in clinical practice.

CONCLUSION: Diagnostic accuracy of the ERICA score is satisfactory in differentiating SCD or MCI from AD dementia.

articles.title: Unexpected coagulopathy in thrombolyzed stroke: experience from a single center in Chile.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent, and waiting for coagulation tests (COT) may delay treatment initiation. In several countries, IVT is initiated without waiting COT results; this approach has not been evaluated in South America. In this region, excessive alcohol consumption may increase the prevalence of unrecognized chronic liver disease.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the frequency of unsuspected coagulation abnormalities among patients with AIS treated with IVT at a single tertiary care center in Chile.

METHODS: A prospective analysis of all patients treated with IVT at Clínica Alemana between June 2016 and July 2025, assessing the proportion of individuals with unexpected coagulation abnormalities.

RESULTS: A total of 480 patients with AIS received IVT. The COTs were normal in 445 patients (92.7%), abnormal in 9 (1.88%), and incomplete or not performed in 26 (5.42%). No clinical differences were observed among the three groups. Patients with coagulation abnormalities or incomplete/not performed COT were significantly less frequent in the Emergency Room (ER) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (p = 0.001). Among those with abnormal COT results, significant differences were found in international normalized ratio (INR) values (p < 0.000) and platelet count (p = 0.001). The functional outcomes at 3 months, as well as mortality and rate of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, did not differ across groups.

CONCLUSION: Unexpected coagulation disorders are an infrequent finding in patients with AIS treated with IVT at our center in Santiago, Chile. Therefore, blood test results should not be awaited before initiating IVT.

articles.title: AGA/AASLD Clinical Practice Guideline on Management of Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease associated with progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, liver transplantation, and premature mortality. Despite effective therapies, important challenges remain in the diagnosis and management of PBC, including identification of antimitochondrial antibody-negative disease, assessment of response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), risk stratification, treatment of patients with inadequate response, management of cholestatic pruritus, and prevention of recurrent disease after liver transplantation. The aim of this guideline was to develop evidence-based recommendations addressing these key areas of clinical care.

METHODS: The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) convened a multidisciplinary panel to develop clinical practice recommendations for adults with PBC. Systematic reviews were performed for 6 prioritized clinical questions. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to prioritize clinical outcomes and assess evidence, and its Evidence to Decision Framework was used to develop recommendations.

RESULTS: The guideline panel agreed on 6 recommendations. These recommendations address the use of PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies in antimitochondrial antibody-negative suspected PBC, UDCA as first-line therapy, liver stiffness measurement for prognostication, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA, linerixibat for moderate to severe pruritus, and UDCA prophylaxis post-transplantation to reduce disease recurrence. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: The guideline emphasizes early diagnosis, optimization of first-line therapy, risk-based treatment escalation, symptom management, and prevention of post-transplantation disease recurrence to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents.

METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336.

RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

articles.title: A nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with coagulase-negative staphylococcus bloodstream infections.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) have emerged as significant pathogens in bloodstream infections (BSIs). Currently, no validated models exist for specifically predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with CoNS-BSIs.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on adult patients with CoNS-BSIs using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) database. Participants were randomly allocated into a training set (n = 366) and a validation set (n = 157). Demographic characteristics, severity scores, comorbidities and laboratory examinations from the first 24 h of ICU admission were analyzed. The optimal predictive variables for establishing a nomogram were screened through univariate, multivariate logistic regression and stepwise regression analyses. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA) and clinical impact curve (CIC).

RESULTS: Among 523 patients enrolled, the overall in-hospital mortality was 22.9%. Four independent predictors were incorporated into the nomogram: age (OR = 1.04), anion gap (AG: OR = 1.11), total bilirubin (TBil: OR = 1.26) and respiratory failure (OR = 1.97). The area under the curve (AUC) values in the training set and validation set were 0.758 and 0.823, respectively. The P-values of the calibration curve in two sets were 0.258 and 0.432. The DCA curves were above the two extreme curves. The CIC analysis revealed a high concordance between predicted high-risk cases and observed clinical events when the risk threshold exceeded 60%.

CONCLUSION: Age, AG, TBil and respiratory failure were independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality among patients with CoNS-BSIs. The nomogram based on these four parameters demonstrated good performance and clinical utility for risk assessment.

articles.title: Seminars in Thrombosis and Hemostasis: 2025 Impact Factor, Most Highly Cited Papers, and Other Journal Metrics.
Laboratory Diagnostics for Thrombosis and Hemostasis Testing-Part V.
Body mass index at diagnosis, postdiagnosis change, and role of metabolic comorbidities in relation to survival in nonmetastatic renal cell carcinoma patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a recognized risk factor for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) incidence, but higher body mass index (BMI) measured at diagnosis has been paradoxically associated with improved survival. This study investigated whether postdiagnosis changes in BMI and metabolic comorbidities combined with BMI at diagnosis are associated with survival.

METHODS: This study examined 1289 patients with nonmetastatic RCC (stage I-III) from the Oncology Research Information Exchange Network. BMI was assessed at diagnosis and at 2 and 3 years postdiagnosis. Multivariable Cox regression and restricted cubic spline models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS).

RESULTS: Modest weight gain (<10%) and stability were most favorable trajectories. Compared with modest weight gain, postdiagnosis weight loss was associated with worse OS and DFS (>10% loss at 2 years: OS HR, 7.77; 95% CI, 3.00-20.16; DFS HR, 3.13; 95% CI, 1.68-5.82), independent of BMI at diagnosis, whereas substantial weight gain was associated with worse OS (>10% gain at 3 years: OS HR, 3.26; 95% CI, 1.14-9.32). Nonobese patients with diabetes had significantly worse DFS (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.22-2.76), whereas the association between obesity and improved survival was mainly limited to patients without diabetes (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.58-0.97).

CONCLUSIONS: Postdiagnosis weight trajectory and metabolic health are important prognostic factors for nonmetastatic RCC. Weight stability and absence of diabetes were associated with more favorable outcomes. Incorporating repeated BMI measurements and diabetes status may improve risk stratification during RCC survivorship.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of psilocybin-assisted therapy for alcohol use disorder: Open-label extension of a phase II randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psilocybin-assisted therapy (PAT) has shown promise for alcohol use disorder (AUD) in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). It remains unknown, however, whether patients derive additional benefit when psilocybin is administered open-label after completion of blinded treatment. Here, we report safety and efficacy outcomes from an open-label extension of a Phase II RCT of PAT for AUD (NCT02061293).

METHODS: Fifty-nine adults with AUD received a single open-label administration of psilocybin (25-40mg/70kg) accompanied by four hours of manualized therapy. During the preceding double-blind phase, 29 of these participants had received psilocybin (psilocybin-psilocybin group; PP) and 30 had received the active placebo diphenhydramine (diphenhydramine-psilocybin group; DP). Mixed-effects models for repeated measures evaluated alcohol consumption (percent heavy drinking days [PHDD], drinks per day [DpD], and percent drinking days [PDD]), alcohol craving, abstinence self-efficacy, and treatment readiness across a four-month follow-up.

RESULTS: Psilocybin was well tolerated, and no serious adverse events occurred. Among participants with higher drinking intensity at extension entry, decreases in PHDD, DpD, and PDD were observed at Month 1 but returned to entry levels thereafter. Craving, abstinence self-efficacy, and treatment readiness improved in both PP and DP groups one week after administration, with variable trajectories thereafter.

DISCUSSION: After completion of the double-blind trial, a single open-label psilocybin administration was associated with maintained remission among most participants who entered abstinent and with acute but largely transient reductions among those who were still drinking heavily. Whether the limited durability reflects the lower intensity of extension treatment, the relative treatment resistance of residual drinking, differences in motivation, or other design-related factors cannot be determined from these data.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02061293, A Double-Blind Trial of Psilocybin-Assisted Treatment of Alcohol Dependence, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02061293.

articles.title: Prejudicial essentialist bias in cognitive neuroscience studies with people who use drugs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Professional judgement can be biased (or prejudiced) by the incidental social characteristics of marginalised clients. Perhaps unexpectedly, psychologists have been hypothesised to express prejudicial essentialist bias in their writing; disproportionately invoking pathological constitutional deficits to explain observed differences in study participants with marginalised social characteristics.

METHODS: To test whether this bias exists in cognitive neuroscience publications, 67 case-controlled studies reporting lower cognitive task performance in people who use drugs (PWUD) versus controls were collated. The percentage of explanations of PWUD's performance using essentialist terms ('deficits', 'dysfunction', 'impairments') versus neutral-agnostic terms ('difference', 'change', 'alteration' etc.) were tested for associations with PWUD's social characteristics, study effect size and publication year.

RESULTS: Deficit descriptions were used on 64% of occasions and were significantly associated with PWUD's social characteristics including their mean age (r = 0.40), percent male (r = 0.24), primary drug (η2 = 0.24), and dependence severity indexed by their recruitment from clinical sources (η2 = 0.12) and characterisation using clinical diagnostics (η2 = 0.15); but not with the effect size of the task performance difference (r = 0.029) or publication year (r = -0.18).

CONCLUSIONS: Psychologists' unwarranted causal inference that task performance differences arise from constitutional pathogenic origins may be prejudiced by the incidental social characteristics of their PWUD sample. This bias may be explained by professional incentives, journal remit and author training influencing narrative construction. Solutions for the bias may involve meta-scientific auditing, strengthening of language guidelines, and critical reflective practice implemented through positionality statements in quantitative research.

articles.title: Clinical factors associated with noninvasive ventilation-associated pneumonia in acute respiratory failure: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is preferred to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) as treatment for acute respiratory failure due to its lower complication rate, but NIV may still be associated with serious complications such as nosocomial pneumonia. However, risk factors associated with NIV-associated pneumonia remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate factors associated with NIV-associated pneumonia in patients treated with NIV for acute respiratory failure in a respiratory intensive care unit.

METHOD: In this prospective cohort study, we followed adult patients who were admitted to a respiratory intensive care unit in a tertiary hospital for acute respiratory failure. None of the patients had pneumonia on admission. All patients were treated with NIV and monitored daily for the development of nosocomial pneumonia, which was defined using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia.

RESULT: Among 191 eligible patients admitted between March 2023 and May 2024, 84 developed NIV-associated pneumonia. Age was not independently associated with pneumonia development. In multivariable analysis, poor oral hygiene, poor secretion control, and longer NIV duration were independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia. Patients who developed pneumonia also had longer ICU stay and higher rates of antibiotic modification.

CONCLUSION: In patients receiving NIV for acute respiratory failure, poor oral hygiene, poor secretion control, and prolonged NIV exposure were independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia, whereas chronological age, sepsis, and frailty were not. These findings suggest that clinical factors related to bedside care and NIV exposure may be more relevant to pneumonia development than age alone.

articles.title: Comment on 'Lean, Non-Autoimmune Young-Onset Diabetes in Bangladesh: A Metabolically Obese Phenotype With Disproportionate Insulin Secretory Defect'.
Association Between Genetically Predicted 25-Hydroxyvitamin D and Type 2 Diabetes Risk in South Asians: An Exploratory Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin D deficiency and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) are highly prevalent in South Asian populations. Observational studies report inverse associations between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and T2D risk, but these findings may reflect confounding or reverse causation. We used Mendelian randomization (MR) to assess the association between genetically predicted 25(OH)D and T2D risk in South Asians.

METHODS: We conducted a two-sample MR analysis using publicly available OpenGWAS summary statistics. One variant (rs3755967) met the conventional genome-wide significance threshold (p < 5 × 10-8), while two additional variants (rs2459139 and rs72744878) met an exploratory threshold (p < 1 × 10-6). The three variants served as instruments for serum 25(OH)D in a South Asian GWAS (ukb-e-30890_CSA; n = 7380; mean F-statistic = 29.6; total R2 = 1.06%). The primary outcome was BMI-unadjusted T2D (ebi-a-GCST90093109; n = 50,533; 16,677 cases), with a BMI-adjusted GWAS used for sensitivity analysis. The primary estimator was inverse-variance weighted (IVW), supported by weighted-median, MR-Egger, simple-mode, and weighted-mode analyses. Heterogeneity and directional pleiotropy were assessed using Cochran's Q and the MR-Egger intercept, respectively. Partial participant overlap could not be excluded because UK Biobank contributed to both datasets.

RESULTS: The primary IVW analysis showed no statistically significant association between genetically predicted 25(OH)D and T2D risk (β = 0.058, SE = 0.120, p = 0.630; OR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.83-1.36). Weighted-median and mode-based estimates were also non-significant. The MR-Egger estimate was highly imprecise (OR = 32.0, 95% CI: 0.11-9103) because only three instruments were available. No significant heterogeneity or directional pleiotropy was detected, although these tests had limited power. The BMI-adjusted sensitivity analysis produced similar findings.

CONCLUSIONS: We found no statistically significant evidence of a linear association between genetically predicted serum 25(OH)D and T2D risk. However, the small exposure GWAS, limited instrument set, exploratory instrument threshold, and possible sample overlap mean that small-to-moderate causal effects cannot be excluded. Larger South Asian GWAS are needed for more definitive inference.

articles.title: Real-Time Continuous Glucose Monitoring Use and Kidney Function Among People With Diabetes and CKD or At-Risk for CKD.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) use may benefit people with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD). In this propensity-matched, retrospective analysis using Truveta-provided de-identified EMR data, changes in kidney function and glycemia were compared between cohorts starting real-time CGM (RT-CGM) use and CGM non-users (No CGM).

METHODS: Adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, treated with any insulin, with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 15-89 mL/min/1.73 m2 were included. Changes in eGFR, albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), and HbA1c between baseline and 3-year follow-up were assessed.

RESULTS: RT-CGM initiation (N = 518 per cohort) was associated with a significantly slower decline in eGFR compared to No CGM. There was no significant difference in change in ACR between the groups (N = 138 per cohort). RT-CGM use (N = 461 per cohort) was associated with a significantly greater decrease in HbA1c compared to No CGM.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support RT-CGM initiation among people with diabetes and CKD or at risk for CKD.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Overweight and Obesity Among Adolescents in South Asia: A Narrative Review of Recent Evidence.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adolescent overweight and obesity are increasing across South Asia, contributing to diabetes and other noncommunicable diseases. Previous reviews have examined prevalence and selected associated factors, but evidence remains heterogeneous across countries, populations and adiposity definitions. This narrative review synthesised recent evidence on prevalence and factors associated with overweight and obesity among South Asian adolescents.

METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2015 to March 2025, supplemented by targeted searches through August 2026. Studies of adolescents aged 10-19 years and predominantly adolescent populations with overlapping age ranges were considered. Primary studies and evidence syntheses were analysed separately. Methodological quality was evaluated using design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists, and findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Thirteen publications were included: eight primary studies and five systematic reviews or meta-analyses. Prevalence varied by population, setting, adiposity measure and classification system. Regional meta-analytic estimates were 12.4% for overweight, 6.6% for obesity and 19.3% for combined overweight/obesity, although these were not directly comparable with adolescent-specific primary studies. More consistent evidence concerned physical inactivity, sedentary behaviour and unhealthy dietary practices. Associations with socioeconomic position, urban residence, sex and gender, familial factors and media exposure were more limited and context dependent. Sleep, mental health, food insecurity and neighbourhood environments were insufficiently examined. Most primary evidence was cross-sectional and school based.

CONCLUSIONS: Adolescent overweight and obesity in South Asia are associated with behavioural, dietary and socio-environmental factors within changing food and urban environments. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneous definitions, uneven country coverage and predominantly cross-sectional designs. Standardised population-based and longitudinal studies, including out-of-school adolescents, are needed to guide context-specific prevention.

articles.title: PROTAC degraders for lymphoid malignancies - current status and future directions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite remarkable advances in targeted therapy, some patients with lymphoid malignancies develop resistance to all available treatment modalities. Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate both catalytic and scaffolding protein functions of disease-causing proteins, offering a strategy to overcome this resistance.

AREAS COVERED: This review discusses the mechanisms of PROTAC activity, current preclinical and clinical data across lymphoid malignancies, and challenges for this emerging therapeutic class. PubMed, Google Scholar, and major hematology conference proceedings (ASH, ASCO, EHA) from 2017 to April 2026 were reviewed. Search terms included combinations of: PROTAC, targeted protein degradation, cereblon, von Hippel-Lindau, combined with individual disease terms and target names.

EXPERT OPINION: Among PROTACs, BTK degraders, tacabrutideg (BGB-16673) and bexobrutideg (NX-5948), have demonstrated overall response rates exceeding 75% in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL. The STAT3 degrader KT-333 and the IKZF1/3 degrader cemsidomide (the so-called molecular glue) have shown proof-of-concept clinical activity in T-cell and Hodgkin lymphomas. The durability of responses, long-term safety and predictive biomarkers have yet to be defined. The ongoing phase III trial of tacabrutideg will likely determine whether PROTACs become an established treatment option in lymphoid malignancies.

articles.title: Systemic Spiroplasma turonicum Infection Manifested as Knee Arthritis, France, 2025.
articles.abstract: We report on an immunocompromised patient in southeast France who sought care for fever, knee arthritis, and skin erythema. Blood and joint samples were positive for Spiroplasma turonicum, an intracellular gram-negative bacterium generally found in plants, insects, and ticks. Clinicians should be aware of possible S. turonicum infection in immunocompromised patients.

articles.title: Post-COVID-19 Expansion of Streptococcus pyogenes Lineages Causing Toxic Shock Syndrome, Japan, 2023-2024.
authors: Working Group for Beta-Hemolytic Streptococci in Japan
articles.abstract: We analyzed 919 Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from laboratory-confirmed streptococcal toxic shock syndrome cases in Japan during 2023-2024. Post-COVID-19 resurgence was driven by expansion of M1UK (49.8%) and emerging M113SNPs (37.4%) lineages, replacing ancestral M1global. M113SNPs were associated with younger patient age and higher death rates in unadjusted analyses.

articles.title: The association between parental health numeracy and medication adherence among children with asthma in Jordan: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Parental health numeracy is relevant to pediatric asthma management because caregivers often interpret medication quantities, risk information, and peak-flow thresholds. This study examined the adjusted association between parental health numeracy and medication adherence among children with asthma in Jordan.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 400 parents or legal guardians of children with physician-diagnosed asthma at the University of Jordan Hospital between May and August 2024. The children had a median age of 6 years (IQR: 3-11). Parental numeracy was assessed using the Arabic version of the Asthma Numeracy Questionnaire (Ar-ANQ), and adherence was assessed using the Arabic version of the Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5).

RESULTS: The median Ar-ANQ score was 3 (IQR: 1-4), and 178 children (44.5%) were classified as having high medication adherence. In adjusted logistic regression, each one-point increase in the Ar-ANQ score was associated with greater odds of high adherence (adjusted OR = 1.404, 95% CI: 1.179-1.672, p < 0.001). Parental education and household income were not significantly associated with adherence.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher parental health numeracy was associated with greater odds of high medication adherence, whereas parental education and household income were not significantly associated with adherence.

articles.title: Digital Therapeutic Interventions for Suicide Prevention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Their Effectiveness in Reducing Suicidal Ideation and Suicide Attempts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although digital interventions show potential for reducing suicidal ideation and behavior, the evidence base is mixed and characterized by methodological variability. This study synthesizes randomized clinical trials that have evaluated their effectiveness.

METHOD: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Seventeen studies (N = 5.089) met the inclusion criteria. Effect sizes were estimated using random-effects models, and we conducted analyses for type of control group (traditional vs. active), moderators (age, delivery setting, and intervention format), and follow-up. Heterogeneity and publication bias were also examined.

RESULTS: Digital interventions significantly reduced suicidal ideation (g = -0.61), with effects maintained at follow up (g = -0.77). Significant effects were observed with respect to both traditional and active controls. There was a moderate reduction in relative risk of suicide attempts, although it was not statistically significant. Moderator analysis indicated a greater effect for clinical populations, self-guided interventions, and younger participants. There was no robust evidence of publication bias.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital interventions may represent a promising complementary approach for reducing suicidal ideation and potentially lowering suicide risk. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously given the heterogeneity of the studies and the limited evidence regarding suicide attempts.

articles.title: Neuroendocrine dysfunction after TBI: A guide for the clinical neuropsychologist.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This review aims to provide neuropsychologists with a comprehensive understanding of neuroendocrine dysfunction following traumatic brain injury (TBI), emphasizing post-traumatic hypopituitarism (PTHP) and its implications for cognitive function and rehabilitation.

METHOD: A critical review of current literature on neuroendocrine dysfunction following TBI, including studies on pituitary function, hormone deficiencies, and their effects on cognition, mood, and fatigue. The review integrates findings from endocrinology, neuroscience, and clinical neuropsychology to highlight the importance of interdisciplinary management.

RESULTS: Research indicates that a high proportion of moderate to severe TBI cases may develop PTHP, with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) as the most prevalent dysfunction. While less extensively studied, evidence suggests that individuals with persistent post-mild TBI symptoms may exhibit neuroendocrine dysfunction at similar rates to moderate to severe TBI patients. The impact of hormonal dysregulation on cognition and neuropsychological performance underscores the need for targeted assessment and intervention. Emerging data also suggest that metabolic disturbances, such as altered gut microbiota and amino acid imbalances, may contribute to post-TBI fatigue and cognitive impairment.

CONCLUSIONS: Neuropsychologists play a vital role in identifying and referring patients with suspected neuroendocrine dysfunction for appropriate testing and treatment. Recognizing PTHP as a potential contributor to chronic TBI symptoms may lead to improved patient outcomes through targeted hormonal therapies and interdisciplinary rehabilitation strategies. Increased awareness of the relationship between TBI, pituitary dysfunction, and cognition is essential for optimizing clinical care.

articles.title: It's about time: modeling circadian regulation of cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology models resolve processes ranging from millisecond-scale ion-channel gating to hour-scale protein trafficking; yet, most do not explicitly represent circadian time. Consequently, ion-channel conductance, autonomic input, body temperature, and clock-regulated gene expression are often treated as fixed parameters or time-invariant inputs, causing simulated cardiac cells to correspond to an implicit and potentially arbitrary biological phase. In vivo, however, these factors vary across the ∼24-h cycle and jointly shape sinoatrial nodal pacemaking, ventricular repolarization, arrhythmia susceptibility, and drug response. In this mini-review, we examine recent efforts to incorporate circadian regulation into computational models of cardiac electrophysiology, including sinoatrial nodal and ventricular myocyte models of pacemaking, arrhythmogenesis, seizure-induced sinus arrhythmias, and drug-induced proarrhythmic risk. We synthesize these studies using a layered "source-transfer-target" organization in which intrinsic and systemic circadian sources act through source-specific transfer processes-including transcription, translation, channel trafficking, receptor-mediated signaling, and direct thermal modulation-to regulate shared electrophysiological targets. Building on this synthesis, we propose a general current-level formulation for incorporating circadian regulation of maximal conductance, channel gating, and ionic driving force into Hodgkin-Huxley-type models. Finally, we identify the experimental, computational, and clinical advances needed to translate these formulations into human-specific, personalized models of cardiac rhythm and arrhythmogenesis, with the long-term goal of enabling circadian-aware cardiac digital twins for time-resolved risk prediction and chronotherapeutic optimization.

articles.title: New dyslipidemia guideline makes more than half of U.S. adults eligible for statin therapy.
Combined PET imaging of tumor hypoxia and proliferation in Glioblastoma using a single injection of 18F-FMISO and 18F-FLT: Association with sites of subsequent recurrence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by intra-tumoral heterogeneity, rapid proliferation, hypoxia-driven radio-resistance, and early recurrence. Gadolinium-Enhanced MRI, the standard of care imaging modality for surgical and radiotherapy planning, lacks specificity for viable tumor burden, particularly in non-enhancing regions.

PURPOSE: This pilot study aimed to evaluate whether preoperative dual-tracer PET using a combined dose of 18FMISO (hypoxia) and 18FLT (proliferation) improves tumor delineation and predicts subsequent local recurrence compared with MRI.

METHODS: Seven patients with WHO grade 4 gliomas (5 GBM, 2 IDH-mutant astrocytomas) underwent preoperative dual-[FMISO+FLT] static PET at 180 min post-injection, and MRI. 6/7 patients underwent resection. Tumor volumes were segmented from PET, contrast-enhanced T1 (T1-Gd), and T2-FLAIR. Postoperative resection cavities were delineated, and follow-up MRI every 3 months was used to identify recurrence. PET-defined tumor volumes extending beyond resection were correlated with subsequent recurrence sites.

RESULTS: Thirteen lesions were analyzed; all showed [FMISO+FLT] uptake (mean activity concentration ratio 1.6 with the cerebellar cortex used as reference region). PET-defined tumor volumes (9.2 cc) were slightly larger than T1-Gd (7.9 cc) but smaller than T2-FLAIR (28.8 cc). PET-defined volumes frequently extended beyond MRI-defined contours (mean non-overlap 6.4 cc vs T1-Gd; 1.5 cc vs. T2-FLAIR). Of six patients undergoing resection, four developed local recurrence within 3.3 months. In all cases, recurrence arose within PET-avid regions outside the resection cavity. The other two patients with complete resection of PET-defined volumes showed a relatively prolonged progression-free-survival (PFS) and including one patient with overall survival exceeding 36 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Dual-[FMISO+FLT] PET is feasible, safe, and can allow delineation of biologically viable tumor subregions, in particular within the MRI T2-FLAIR volume. This approach prospectively identified sites of subsequent local recurrence and may improve surgical planning and radiotherapy dose escalation. Larger validation studies are warranted to establish dual-tracer PET as a precision imaging paradigm in GBM.

articles.title: Response to Comment on "Antihyperglycemic Drugs and Risk of Asthma Exacerbation in Patients With Asthma and Type 2 Diabetes: A Multinational Retrospective Cohort Study".
Efficacy and Safety of Benmelstobart Plus Anlotinib in Advanced Endometrial Cancer: Results of a Multi-Cohort, Phase II Study (ETER200).
articles.abstract: Patients with advanced endometrial cancer (EC) have a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options after failure of prior systemic therapy. In this multi-cohort Phase II study (ETER200), patients with metastatic or recurrent EC who had received at least one chemotherapy regimen were enrolled. Based on MSI/MMR status, patients received benmelstobart plus anlotinib (Cohort 1), benmelstobart (Cohort 2), or anlotinib (Cohort 3) every 3 weeks. Primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Here, the results of Cohort 1 expansion stage were reported. As of May 9, 2024, 85 of the 107 non-MSI-H/pMMR EC patients enrolled in Cohort 1 constituted the expansion stage population for primary efficacy analysis. The IRC-assessed ORR was 34.1% (95% CI, 24.2-45.2), with a median duration of response of 15.2 months (95% CI, 6.9-not evaluable). Median progression-free and overall survival were 8.8 months (95% CI, 5.8-15.2) and 21.8 months (95% CI, 19.5-29.1), respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 69.2% of patients, most commonly hypertension (21.2%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (9.4%). Overall, benmelstobart plus anlotinib showed promising anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in advanced non-MSI-H/pMMR EC, supporting further evaluation of this combination in randomized Phase III studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04574284.

articles.title: Spontaneous Renal Hemorrhage Secondary to MRSA Renal Abscess Requiring Nephrectomy After Failed Percutaneous Drainage: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spontaneous renal hemorrhage (SRH) caused by renal infection is extremely rare. Furthermore, sepsis caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has a high mortality rate and requires prompt source control.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old man with severe diabetes presented to the emergency department in shock. Computed tomography revealed a left renal subcapsular hematoma. Based on his clinical course and history, infection-induced SRH was suspected. Blood and urine cultures yielded MRSA. Although percutaneous drainage was performed after the initial bleeding stabilized, persistent infection was followed by rebleeding, necessitating left nephrectomy. The patient recovered postoperatively. Histopathology confirmed abscess formation and chronic inflammation without malignancy.

CONCLUSION: For inadequately controlled infections following percutaneous drainage, particularly when recurrent hemorrhage is suspected, early nephrectomy may be considered for definitive source control.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology: an evidence map across subspecialties, 2014-26.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in healthcare, including cardiology, with growing interest in its potential to support diagnosis, prognosis, and clinical decision-making. The rapid pace of technological advancements is not matched by equivalent progress in the regulation and appraisal of these systems. This review aims to provide a structured evidence map of AI models in cardiology, by grading the robustness of clinical validation and mapping it against the quantity of publications across main subspecialties.

METHODS AND RESULTS: To assess the strength of evidence, we defined, developed, and applied a novel classification tailored for AI models that ranks evidence into five Grades of Validation according to the level of clinical validity. We screened literature from 2014 to 2026 according to the PRISMA guidelines, identifying a total of 2807 articles on AI applications within cardiology, 490 of which met the inclusion criteria (validation was performed in at least one external, independent patient population), revealing a highly heterogeneous distribution of evidence across subspecialties. Most studies in AI focused on improved diagnostics (n = 322, 65.7%); however, advanced integration in prognostic (n = 122, 24.9%) and therapeutic applications remains limited (n = 46, 9.4%). Cardiovascular imaging leads AI applications, especially in coronary computed tomography and echocardiography, followed by non-invasive electrophysiology, predominantly in atrial fibrillation screening and ventricular dysfunction detection.

CONCLUSION: The scarcity of prospective validations across different resources and geographical settings (n = 134, 27.3%) and randomized controlled trials (n = 35, 3.8%) limits the adoption by clinical guidelines and widespread implementation of AI algorithms.

articles.title: Hippo signaling-linked circulating microRNA networks are associated with cardiovascular disease in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) markedly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers for patient stratification and may provide mechanistic insight into dysregulated pathways in T2D-associated CVD.

OBJECTIVE: This work aimed to identify circulating miRNA signatures in T2D patients with CVD (T2D-CVD) vs T2D patients without CVD using a novel network-based medicine approach.

METHODS: Patients (n = 110) were stratified into T2D and T2D-CVD groups based on the absence or presence of macrovascular complications. Circulating miRNAs, proinflammatory cytokines, and growth factors were profiled in a discovery cohort (n = 80) and confirmed in a validation cohort (n = 30).
