Differential expression, network-based approaches, and pathway enrichment analyses identified miRNA signatures, coexpression communities, hub miRNAs, and associated signaling pathways.

RESULTS: T2D-CVD patients showed a set of elevated inflammatory cytokines and circulating miRNAs. Particularly, 19 miRNAs were differentially expressed between T2D-CVD and T2D patients. Pathway enrichment of these miRNAs highlighted Hippo signaling together with transforming growth factor-β, mechanistic target of rapamycin, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt pathways. Network analysis identified a coexpression community of 34 miRNAs, including hub miRNAs let-7a-5p, miR-132-3p, and miR-1306-3p, all linked to Hippo signaling. Key miRNA interactions were validated, and differentially expressed and hub miRNAs both correlated with inflammatory mediators such as PAR-1, CXCL1, and NEMO, which are linked to Hippo pathway regulation.

CONCLUSION: This study identified a network of circulating miRNAs associated with inflammatory cytokines and Hippo signaling pathway in T2D-CVD. These findings reveal novel molecular aspects of the systemic inflammation characterizing T2D-CVD and support the potential of Hippo-related circulating miRNAs as mechanistic biomarkers for cardiovascular risk in T2D.

articles.title: Predictors and Patterns of Metastatic Candidozyma auris Infection, Spain, 2016-2024.
articles.abstract: Metastatic infection after Candidozyma auris candidemia remains poorly characterized. We retrospectively studied patients with C. auris candidemia at a tertiary hospital in Spain during 2016-2024. Of 108 patients, 24 (22.2%) experienced metastatic infections; endocarditis was most frequent (7.4%), followed by osteoarticular infection, meningitis, and hepatosplenic infection (3.7% each). In multivariable Fine-Gray regression, a cardiac device or prosthetic valve was independently associated with metastatic infection (subdistribution hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 [95% CI 1.21-6.91]), although that association was attenuated in a sensitivity analysis restricted to echocardiographed patients. Persistent candidemia showed a higher, nonsignificant risk for metastatic infection in the day-5 landmark analysis (subdistribution HR 2.67 [95% CI 0.86-8.32]). Metastatic infection was associated with increased deaths in time-dependent analyses at 60 days (adjusted HR 2.21 [95% CI 1.04-4.67]) and 90 days (adjusted HR 2.26 [95% CI 1.09-4.67]). Our findings support echocardiography in patients with intracardiac devices.

articles.title: Emergence of Novel Macrolide-Resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae Sequence Type 3 Subclades in Children after COVID-19 Pandemic, Taiwan.
articles.abstract: Post-COVID-19 pandemic Mycoplasma pneumoniae resurgences have occurred globally and have been particularly severe in Taiwan. We conducted a multicenter study to assess M. pneumoniae trends in children. Compared with the 2019 peak, 2024 data revealed a doubling of incidence (546/100,000 population), a 2.2-fold increase in intensive care unit admissions (10.9/100,000 population), and a 13.7-fold surge in central nervous system complications (6.1/100,000 population). In a 2023-2024 prospective cohort (n = 226), intensive care unit admission risk factors were neutrophils >7,000/μL (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.2 [95% CI 1.3-29.9]), platelets >400 × 103/μL (aOR 12.5 [95% CI 2.7-57.9]), pleural effusion (aOR 9.7 [95% CI 1.6-58.1]), and central nervous system involvement (aOR 27.9 [95% CI 4.1-188.3]). Phylogenetic analysis of 698 genomes demonstrated that 4 emerging subclades replaced pre-COVID-19 lineages by mid-2024; 1 subclade was associated with severe outcomes, highlighting evolving resistant, neurotropic lineages and calling for enhanced surveillance.

articles.title: Trophoblast-derived extracellular vesicles elicit long-term effects on maternal cardiovascular function in a postpartum model of chronic hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: The hypertensive disease of pregnancy, preeclampsia, is a risk factor for future maternal cardiovascular disease while normal pregnancy is cardioprotective in the long term. Trophoblast-derived extracellular vesicles (T-EVs) released by the placenta are implicated in the development of vascular dysfunction and are widely thought to have a role in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia. This study tested the effects of T-EVs from both normotensive and preeclamptic pregnancies on long-term cardiovascular outcomes in a pregnant hypertensive model. Spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) received intravenous vehicle control (CTEV; n = 11), and T-EVs from normotensive (NT; n = 10), early onset preeclamptic (EOPE; n = 10), or late-onset preeclamptic (LOPE; n = 10) pregnancies between days 8.5 and 18.5 of pregnancy (term = 22.5 days). SHRs were monitored during pregnancy and up to 12 mo postpartum, with noninvasive blood pressure plethysmography and echocardiography, followed by wire myography and histology. The NT group demonstrated significantly lower postpartum systolic blood pressure (SBP) compared with CTEV (P < 0.0001), whereas SBP in the EOPE group was increased (P < 0.0001). SBP was not significantly different between the CTEV and LOPE groups (P > 0.05). Terminal wire myography revealed that vessels from the NT group were more vasodilatory in response to acetylcholine (P = 0.0103) and less contractile in response to phenylephrine (P = 0.0435) and endothelin-1 (P < 0.0001). Vascular structure, cardiac function, and cardiac morphology were not different between all four T-EV groups. Exposure to T-EVs during pregnancy continued to influence maternal vascular function long after their administration. These findings confirm the role of T-EVs in regulating maternal vasculature long after the removal of the placenta at birth.NEW & NOTEWORTHY We have shown that normotensive T-EVs reduce blood pressure and promote a provasodilatory vascular phenotype for at least 12 mo after administration during pregnancy in a rat model. Administration of EOPE preeclamptic T-EVs prevented the natural decrease in blood pressure during pregnancy and increased blood pressure long-term. Together, these results suggest T-EVs play a key role in modulating maternal vascular function not only in pregnancy but also in determining future cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Inhaled nitric oxide: Expanding indications beyond traditional boundaries.
articles.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that improves ventilation-perfusion matching with minimal effect on systemic blood pressure. Although the FDA approval is restricted to neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure associated with pulmonary hypertension, many clinicians now use iNO in adults with conditions where elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular dysfunction threaten stability and hypoxic respiratory failure. This review examines both the mechanistic rationale and the available evidence for such off-label use. Examples range from acute RV failure in the ICU to perioperative support in cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, including COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). In these settings, iNO offers rapid afterload reduction and short-term improvement in oxygenation, but randomized trials are lacking and limited studies to date have failed to consistently show outcome benefits. Adverse effects such as methemoglobinemia, nitrogen dioxide toxicity, rebound pulmonary hypertension, and a potential increase in acute kidney injury risk in certain non-cardiac surgical populations. Additionally, cost considerations and other practical limitations must be weighed carefully. Overall, current evidence supports the use of iNO as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected critically ill patients.

articles.title: The Obesity Paradox in Chronic Kidney Disease: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Is Associated With Mortality Independent of Body Mass Index.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: The obesity paradox, in which a higher body mass index (BMI) is associated with better survival, has been observed in chronic disease populations. However, the interaction between BMI, cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), and mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains incompletely understood. We examined the association between BMI, age-adjusted CRF, and all-cause mortality in a large CKD cohort.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 13,521 predominantly male US veterans (97.4% male) with CKD from the Exercise Testing and Health Outcomes Study within the Veterans Affairs health care system.

PREDICTORS: BMI categories (normal weight <25.0, overweight 25.0-29.9, and obese ≥30.0 kg/m2) and age-adjusted CRF quartiles based on metabolic equivalents achieved during maximal exercise tolerance testing using the Bruce protocol. The index date was the date of exercise testing.

OUTCOME: All-cause mortality.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease assessed mortality risk across BMI-fitness combinations, with normal BMI and least fit as references.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up period of 7.4 years, 5,144 (38.0%) deaths occurred. A higher BMI was associated with a lower mortality risk: overweight (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95) and obese (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.61-0.82) versus normal BMI. Higher CRF was associated with progressively lower mortality: moderate fit (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.50-0.74) and most fit (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.40-0.60) versus least fit. The combination of obese BMI and highest fitness was associated with a 64% lower mortality risk (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.25-0.51).

LIMITATIONS: Predominantly male veteran population; single baseline BMI and fitness measurements; observational design precludes causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: In this predominantly male veteran CKD cohort, a higher BMI was associated with lower all-cause mortality across all fitness levels. Age-adjusted CRF demonstrated a strong, graded inverse association with mortality independent of BMI. These observational findings support integrating fitness assessment into CKD management.

articles.title: Early identification and prevention of cardiometabolic risk in Gulf Cooperation Council countries: a scoping review relevant to primary care and family medicine.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This scoping review was aimed at mapping and identifying the current evidence on the early identification and prevention of cardiometabolic risks in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, in the context of primary care and family medicine, and to identify where evidence is concentrated or absent.

METHODS: Original studies in English were searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, between January 2020 and February 2026. The eligible studies were conducted in Gulf Cooperation Council countries and focused on cardiometabolic risk, early identification, screening, prevention, risk reduction, lifestyle interventions, health education, or preventive strategies. Data were charted using a structured form and synthesised descriptively.

RESULTS: The evidence indicated that the high and clustered burden of dysglycemia, prediabetes, diabetes, metabolic syndrome, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and central obesity existed among adults, children, adolescents, university students, community populations, primary care settings, and biobank-based studies. Studies demonstrated the value of risk scores, anthropometric measurements, biomarkers, and community screening strategies. Prevention and early-intervention studies were less frequently represented and heterogeneous across settings.

CONCLUSION: Current Gulf Cooperation Council evidence supports the importance of early cardiometabolic risk identification and prevention but also highlights the need for integrated prevention pathways within primary care and family medicine.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Prevalence and Distribution of Electrocardiographic Variants in Healthy Vietnamese Freshmen.
articles.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on ECG characteristics and qualitative ECG variants in healthy young Vietnamese adults remain limited. We evaluated sex-specific ECG differences and factors independently associated with common ECG variants in first-year Vietnamese university students.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 6099 healthy students (3440 female [56.4%], 2659 male [43.6%]; mean age, 17.85 ± 0.65 years) undergoing standardized cardiovascular screening. Resting 12-lead ECGs were analyzed for quantitative parameters and qualitative variants.

RESULTS: All four core ECG parameters differed by sex (all p < 0.001). Females had higher heart rates (84.64 vs. 81.55 bpm) and longer QTc intervals (423.54 vs. 406.46 ms), whereas males had longer PR intervals (141.99 vs. 138.99 ms) and wider QRS complexes (91.44 vs. 80.81 ms). Males had higher prevalences of sinus arrhythmia (22.7% vs. 19.2%), early repolarization pattern (6.1% vs. 0.1%), right bundle branch block (4.4% vs. 0.3%), and sinus bradycardia (4.5% vs. 1.3%; all p < 0.001). Male sex was independently associated with early repolarization pattern (aOR, 37.7; 95% CI, 17.2-107) and right bundle branch block (aOR, 13.1; 95% CI, 7.55-25.2; both p < 0.001), but not sinus arrhythmia (aOR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.84-1.21; p = 0.896).

CONCLUSIONS: ECG parameters and several qualitative variants differed by sex. These findings provide descriptive, population-specific data on ECG characteristics and common qualitative variants in healthy young Vietnamese university students.

articles.title: Informal Caregiver-Observed Fall Risk Indicators and Caregiver Responses to Prevent Falls Among Community-Dwelling Older People: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Informal caregivers are uniquely positioned to recognize subtle changes that precede falls because of their continuous presence in older people's everyday environments. However, caregiver-observed indicators of escalating fall risk have not been systematically synthesized. This systematic review synthesizes the evidence on informal caregiver-observed fall risk indicators and caregiver responses to prevent falls among community-dwelling older people.

METHODS: A targeted synthesis of peer-reviewed literature was undertaken using six electronic databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and Embase) that were searched. Qualitative content analysis was used to synthesize the findings. A total of 16 studies were included in the review.

RESULTS: Caregivers recognized a broad range of observable indicators associated with increased fall risk, including: (1) mobility and gait changes; (2) cognitive and neurobehavioral changes; (3) functional decline and increasing dependence in activities of daily living; (4) physiological warning signs; (5) environmental hazards; and (6) behavioral risk indicators. The synthesis further revealed an observation-to-response pathway, whereby caregivers translated perceived fall-risk indicators into: (1) increased surveillance and protective monitoring; (2) providing mobility and functional assistance; (3) implementing environmental modifications; (4) promoting safety behaviors; and (5) seeking health care support through care coordination and professional consultation.

CONCLUSIONS: Informal caregivers detect early signs of fall risk and initiate preventive responses that may reduce fall risk among community-dwelling older people.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Nurses should systematically incorporate caregiver observations into routine fall-risk assessment and care planning to improve the early identification of escalating fall risk and support timely, individualized fall-prevention interventions. Health policies should recognize informal caregivers as essential partners in fall prevention by promoting standardized caregiver education, documentation of caregiver observations, and their integration into routine fall-risk assessment and community-based care.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of human neutrophils reveals neutrophil heterogeneity across health and disease.
articles.abstract: Neutrophils, the most abundant leukocytes in human blood, have multifaceted roles in health and disease. Here we assembled a single-cell atlas of human neutrophils (SCAHN) by integrating transcriptome data from 1 million human neutrophils from 781 samples and 43 independent datasets. Using SCAHN, we identified multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and robust changes in gene expression and subset proportions in infection, cancer, immune suppression and sex differences at single-cell resolution. Cross-species reference mapping of mouse and nonhuman primate neutrophils onto SCAHN revealed both conserved and species-specific features. Using 17,023 bulk blood transcriptome profiles from 40 datasets, we found that neutrophil-specific signatures predicted mortality in acutely ill patients at presentation, were associated with cancer diagnosis and survival, and correlated with metabolic dysfunction and long-term all-cause mortality. Our study highlights how neutrophil biology can improve immune risk stratification and develop effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: KDOQI Commentary on the 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Hypertension prevention, diagnosis, and management are central to modifying the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although the nephrology community has long recognized CKD as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease, CKD has not historically been incorporated in cardiovascular risk prediction models. The new 2025 American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults addresses this gap by formally adopting the PREVENT calculator, which combines cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic health parameters to guide risk assessment and clinical decision making. The AHA/ACC guideline reinforces the broad blood pressure target of <130/80 mm Hg as well as makes recommendations for complex and resistant hypertension. Given the impact of these recommendations on persons living with kidney disease, the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) convened an expert work group to review and comment on the guideline. This KDOQI commentary focuses on recommendations from the AHA/ACC guideline that are pertinent to individuals at risk of CKD or with non-dialysis-dependent CKD (stages 1-5), hence excluding commentary on hypertension management in patients receiving maintenance dialysis. In areas where the AHA/ACC guideline does not offer formal recommendations (eg, medication interactions, electrolyte imbalances, and kidney injury), the work group provides expert commentary about implications for people with CKD. Overall, the work group supports the majority of the AHA/ACC recommendations and identifies areas where evidence remains limited or management in CKD warrants additional consideration.

articles.title: Resistance Exercise for Body Composition in Children Who Are Overweight or Obese.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Childhood obesity is a major public health issue linked to long-term metabolic disorders. Although aerobic exercise is often emphasized, evidence suggests that resistance exercise may also improve body composition in youth who are overweight or obese. This study aims to examine the effects of resistance-based exercise programs on fat mass, lean mass, body fat percentage, body weight, and body mass index in children and adolescents who are overweight or obese and to identify potential moderators of these effects.

METHODS: Eight electronic databases and 3 gray literature databases were searched from inception to May 2025. Randomized controlled trials involving resistance-based exercise programs in children and adolescents classified as overweight or obese were included. Data were extracted independently in duplicate, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-four trials (n = 846 participants) were included. Resistance exercise significantly reduced fat mass (-2.06 kg), body fat percentage (-2.1%), and body weight (-1.3 kg), and increased lean mass (+0.8 kg), with small-to-moderate effect sizes (standardized mean difference = -0.35 to 0.33; P < .05). No significant moderating effects of age, sex, duration, volume, or intensity were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: Resistance exercise improves body composition in children and adolescents who are overweight or obese.

articles.title: A hypothesis-generating study of collateral reactivation: a reanalysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes from 119 recurrent tuberculosis cases.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Recurrent tuberculosis is traditionally classified as exogenous reinfection or endogenous reactivation. We previously proposed "collateral reactivation," in which distinct Mycobacterium tuberculosis subclones derived from a hypothetical original clone are involved in separate disease episodes, in contrast to traditional endogenous ("direct-descent") reactivation. To explore whether collateral reactivation occurs beyond the single case we previously reported, we reanalyzed publicly available whole-genome sequencing data from 123 recurrent tuberculosis cases. After curation, 119 cases (pairwise single-nucleotide variant [SNV] distance, 0-18) were classified as cases of collateral or direct-descent reactivation. In 21 cases (17.6%), a hypothetical original clone could be inferred, and these cases were classified as collateral reactivation. These cases showed a higher rate of SNVs/genome/year (median 3 vs. 0.4, p < 0.0001) and a higher proportion of drug resistance-associated SNVs (23.8% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.009) than direct-descent reactivation cases. These observations support the view that collateral reactivation is not restricted to the single case we previously reported, although mixed infection or exogenous reinfection caused by closely related strains cannot be excluded as alternative explanations. To determine whether collateral reactivation should be recognized as a concept distinct from direct-descent reactivation, future studies integrating whole-genome sequencing of single colonies, lesion-specific sampling, longitudinal sampling, deep sequencing, imaging, clinical follow-up, and epidemiological exposure information will be required.

articles.title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy.

METHODS: In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality.

RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS.

CONCLUSIONS: RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.

articles.title: Individualizing Diagnosis and Management of Stress Urinary Incontinence in Neurogenic Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI), defined as involuntary leakage with effort, exertion, sneezing, or coughing, remains a significant cause of morbidity. While well characterized in the general population, SUI in the setting of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (NLUTD) poses unique diagnostic and management challenges. This review outlines sex-specific epidemiology, diagnostic strategies, and evolving management approaches for SUI in NLUTD, emphasizing individualized and mechanism-based care.

RECENT FINDINGS: Incontinence prevalence varies by neurologic diagnosis, with estimates ranging from 23.6% in patients who suffered from stroke to over 50% in patients with spinal cord injury (SCI) and multiple sclerosis (MS). The underlying pathophysiology is highly variable, with neurologic disease influencing detrusor and sphincter function in unpredictable ways. Urodynamic studies have proven especially valuable in this population for distinguishing between sphincteric incompetence and detrusor-driven incontinence, guiding treatment decisions that help safeguard renal function. Noninvasive strategies, including pelvic floor therapy, mechanical devices, and limited pharmacologic options, offer modest benefit and often are constrained by neurologic deficits. Surgical interventions, such as urethral slings, artificial urinary sphincters (AUS), and, in select salvage cases, bladder neck closure, remain central for refractory disease. Recent multicenter studies highlight variable outcomes, with AUS demonstrating durable efficacy, while urethral slings remain appropriate in carefully selected patients with variable anatomy.

articles.title: Subcutaneous Fat Density Is a Unique Form of Frailty, Reversible by Liver Transplantation.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

articles.title: Impact of YAQ001 on the Gut Microbiome, Permeability and Markers of Systemic Inflammation in Patients With Cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: YAQ001 is a novel, non-absorbable, gut-restricted, multiporous, carbon bead adsorbent. Pre-clinical studies and a clinical trial suggested its therapeutic potential and safety in patients with cirrhosis. This substudy aimed to explore the effects of YAQ001 on the gut microbiome and their exploratory association with biomarkers of gut permeability and systemic inflammation.

METHODS: Twenty-eight-patients with cirrhosis were randomized (double-blind) to receive YAQ001 (4 g once daily) or placebo. Gut microbiome and biomarkers of inflammation and gut permeability were assessed at baseline, after 4 and 12 weeks. Changes in biomarkers and relationship with microbiome composition and gene profiling were assessed. The effect of YAQ001 on Klebsiella pneumoniae biofilms was assessed in vitro.

RESULTS: Overall alpha and beta diversity remained unaltered. YAQ001 increased the abundance of bacteria associated with improved gut health such as Adlercreutzia equolifaciens, a bacterium commonly depleted in liver disease, and decreased the abundance of bacteria associated with infections and poor outcomes such as Klebsiella pneumonia, and Streptococcus mutans. YAQ001 impacted positively on virulence factors such as siderophores, fimbriae structures, and lipopolysaccharides that are associated with inflammation and invasion. Antibiotic resistance genes decreased significantly in the YAQ001 group. These changes were associated with a reduction in markers of gut permeability and systemic inflammation. YAQ001 prevented K. pneumoniae biofilms in vitro.

CONCLUSION: YAQ001 was associated with favourable compositional shifts and trends towards reduced virulence-related gene signatures in the gut microbiome, alongside trends towards improved inflammatory biomarkers. The in vitro anti-biofilm effect of YAQ001 warrants further mechanistic investigation. The findings position YAQ001 as a potential microbiome therapeutic.

articles.title: [Sepsis-induced coagulopathy].
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) represents a frequent and prognostically highly relevant complication of sepsis, characterized by a dysregulated interaction between inflammation, endothelial activation and coagulation. Pathophysiologically, the excessive host immune response to pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMP), activation of the complement cascade, formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NET) and disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx collectively promote a prothrombotic and antifibrinolytic microenvironment, resulting in microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Approximately 20-25% of critically ill patients with sepsis fulfil the diagnostic criteria for SIC. Current diagnostic approaches rely on scoring systems such as the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH)-SIC, ISTH overt-disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and Japanese Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (JSTH)-DIC scores; however, their clinical utility remains limited as they predominantly collate hemorrhagic parameters even though sepsis is typically characterized by a thrombotically dominated phenotype. Viscoelastic point-of-care assays enable dynamic bedside assessment of coagulation and fibrinolysis, including the frequently occurring hypofibrinolysis or fibrinolytic shutdown, which is associated with an unfavorable outcome; however, for this specific purpose, these methods have not yet been sufficiently validated or established as a diagnostic standard. Data and recommendations on specific therapeutic options are limited. A consistent pharmacological thromboprophylaxis remains the cornerstone in patients with sepsis, with low-molecular weight heparins demonstrating advantages over unfractionated heparin regarding venous thromboembolic complications. Coagulation modulating treatment, such as antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin or activated protein C, have thus far failed to demonstrate consistent survival benefits in large randomized clinical trials. Experimental approaches targeting NET formation, complement activation or fibrinolytic modulation appear mechanistically promising but require further clinical validation. Overall, SIC necessitates an individualized, pathophysiology-driven diagnostic and therapeutic approach integrating inflammatory, endothelial, thrombotic and fibrinolytic alterations.

articles.title: Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® in treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
articles.abstract: Aim: To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® drug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database. Materials & methods: This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI. Results: A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup. Conclusion: Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

articles.title: The Effect of Acute Beetroot Juice and Caffeine Supplementation on Specific Judo Performance During a Simulated Competition Day in Judo Athletes.
articles.abstract: Beetroot juice (BJ) and caffeine (CAF) are well-established ergogenic aids for exercise performance. However, little is known about their efficacy and interaction within the specific context of a judo competition day. This study investigated the acute effects of BJ, CAF, and their combination (BJCAF) on judo-specific performance across a simulated competition day. Using a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design, 35 competitive judo athletes (age 23 ± 5 years; body mass 74 ± 13 kg) completed 4 sessions (BJ, CAF, BJCAF, and placebo), each consisting of 5 trials of judo randori and a Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT), followed by neuromuscular and cognitive assessments. Compared with placebo, CAF enhanced SJFT performance, neuromuscular function, and cognition in trials 1-3 but not in trial 5 (p < 0.05). Conversely, BJ improved these same metrics in trial 5 (p < 0.05). BJCAF enhanced SJFT performance across trials 1-3 and 5, cognitive functions in trials 1, 2, and 4, and neuromuscular performance in all trials (p < 0.05). Importantly, in trial 5, both BJ and BJCAF conditions yielded improved SJFT performance, neuromuscular function, and cognitive outcomes compared to CAF alone (p < 0.05). The results demonstrate that the ergogenic effect of CAF was not maintained throughout the simulated competition day, whereas BJ provided late-stage benefits. Co-ingestion effectively counteracted the later-session decline observed with CAF alone while maintaining its early advantages. This highlights the importance of considering temporal dynamics and metabolic costs when designing nutritional strategies for multi-bout, high-intensity sports tournaments such as judo.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Q Fever in Camels: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Studies From Africa and Asia.
articles.abstract: Q fever is a neglected zoonotic disease caused by Coxiella burnetii with a global distribution. It has a significant public health implication in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis was designed to comprehensively analyse the global prevalence of Q fever in camels. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, online searches were conducted in Pubmed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar from 9 to 20 December 2025, to retrieve articles published between 1 January 2000 and 30 November 2025. After excluding articles that did not meet the inclusion criteria, this systematic review and meta-analysis identified 35 articles. After heterogeneity assessment, random effects model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence, and the overall pooled prevalence of Q fever in camels was 33.37% (95% CI: [23.14; 45.44]), combining serological evidence of previous or recent exposure with molecular evidence of C. burnetii detection. Diagnostic-method-specific analyses showed substantially different pooled estimates for ELISA (44.06%) and PCR (7.76%), reflecting distinct biological endpoints. The prevalence of Q fever was 37.17% in Africa and 26.87% in Asia. This meta-analysis result showed that the prevalence of Q fever is high in camels, but it is still neglected in several regions, posing significant impact to human and animal health. Expanded epidemiological investigations to underrepresented geographic regions and production systems will provide critical evidence to inform global surveillance strategies and support evidence-based policy for zoonotic disease prevention in camel populations and beyond.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Achievement of a Pharmacodynamic Target of Piperacillin-Tazobactam for the Population With Obesity: An Open Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study (TAZO-OBESITY Trial).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Observational studies report that prolonged infusions of piperacillin-tazobactam may enable the achievement of an optimal clinically targeted free drug concentration above the minimum inhibitory concentration (fT > MIC).

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the feasibility of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing standard to prolonged infusions of piperacillin-tazobactam in the obese population.

METHODS: In this open-label RCT, patients with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2 or higher who initiated piperacillin-tazobactam were recruited and randomly assigned to receive either standard or prolonged infusions of the antibiotic. Feasibility and safety outcomes were assessed. A blood sample was collected 24 h after the intervention to measure total piperacillin concentrations, with an exploratory aim of determining the proportion of patients who achieved 100% fT > MIC.

RESULTS: A total of 45 patients were recruited at a rate of 7.2 patients per month with a consent rate of 42.1%, achieving these feasibility objectives. Adherence to blood sampling was 77.8%, below the 80% objective. On an exploratory basis, the proportion of patients who achieved 100% fT > MIC 24 h postintervention was 64.3% in the prolonged-infusion group and 55.6% in the standard-infusion group (p = 0.725). There was no significant difference in the safety outcomes (p = 0.756).

CONCLUSION: This first RCT evaluating prolonged infusions of piperacillin-tazobactam in the obese population demonstrated the feasibility of the protocol. Although not statistically significant, the results suggest a favorable trend for fT > MIC attainment and no safety signal for prolonged infusions and support the conduct of a larger scale RCT.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registration: NCT #06690905.

articles.title: Moving Beyond the Checklist: A Three-Tier Model for Integrating Geriatrics Expertise into the CMS Age-Friendly Era.
articles.journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
articles.abstract: As the Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement enters a new phase of policy integration, hospitals face a pivotal moment. The U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Age Friendly Hospital Measure has created regulatory conditions necessary for hospital systems to institute high-quality, personalized care for older adults. As the CMS is expected to transition from pay-for-reporting to pay-for-performance for age-friendly care in the coming years, health systems must urgently move beyond reporting compliance toward true care redesign. The authors highlight three interrelated strategic risks and challenges that hospital leaders and executives must navigate in the current environment. First, there is the danger of reducing age-friendly care processes to siloed checklist exercises to satisfy reporting requirements, a risk that hospitals must mitigate by ensuring age-friendly care bundles are implemented as synchronized, outcome-driven approaches that respond to changes in the clinical status of patients and their transitions of care. Second, hospitals must account for older adults who are suffering from complex care needs, or multicomplexity, particularly because these patients disproportionately drive high costs and utilization metrics. Hospitals with constrained resources may also treat the 4Ms (What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility) framework as a substitute for specialized care, shifting investment away from geriatric specialists, palliative care practitioners, and allied interdisciplinary teams. Third, given the profound shortage of geriatric expertise, health systems must accept that they cannot provide specialist-level care to every patient 65 years of age or older. Even well-resourced health systems often struggle with risk-stratification blindness, failing to distinguish between universal age-friendly interventions appropriate for all inpatients and the subset of patients who require more intensive care with interdisciplinary geriatric teams. Without clear risk stratification, implementation efforts may become fragmented, inefficient, and difficult to sustain. To mitigate these risks, the authors propose a risk-stratified, three-tier operational framework that hospital leaders can utilize for age-friendly system redesign. This paradigm treats the 4Ms and other geriatric care processes enshrined in the CMS Age Friendly Hospital Measure as a foundation that should be delivered to all hospitalized older adults 65 years of age or older. It then builds on this foundation to identify strata of higher-risk older adults who require greater resource allocation, ranging from specialized interdisciplinary programs and protocols (such as hip fracture protocols and Geriatric Surgery Verification), which can be delivered primarily by generalists with geriatrician oversight, to higher-intensity models of care (such as acute care for elders units or geriatric-surgical comanagement), which require more intensive involvement from specialist geriatric teams. This operational roadmap will help hospital systems better match limited geriatric workforce resources to patient complexity, reducing inefficient care and improving both clinical and operational outcomes in alignment with the triple aim of health care.

articles.title: Age-Friendly Health System Recognition and Its Association with Improved Clinical Outcome Measures.
articles.journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
articles.abstract: The number of adults 65 years of age and older is rapidly increasing, as is health care utilization by older adults with multiple chronic conditions. The Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement, with a focus on What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility (the 4Ms), was launched in 2017 to improve management of older adults across health care settings. However, evidence of impact on outcomes remains limited. Using a national cohort of 4002 hospitals (388 with AFHS recognition from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement, as of December 31, 2024, and 3614 controls), the authors explore the associations between AFHS recognition and hospital readmission rates, mortality, and patient-reported experiences. Using difference-in-differences analyses, the authors find that level 2 AFHS recognition (i.e., hospitals with at least 3 months of data of older patients who have received 4Ms care) is associated with lower 30-day mortality rates for acute myocardial infarction (-0.41 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.75 to -0.06), pneumonia (-0.71; 95% CI, -1.29 to -0.13), and stroke (-0.56; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.07). Level 1 recognition (i.e., hospitals that have successfully developed plans to implement the 4Ms) is associated with lower readmission rates only for pneumonia (-0.40; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.10). Furthermore, both level 1 and level 2 recognition are associated with modest reductions in Medicare spending per beneficiary. No determinative associations were identified between AFHS recognition and patient-reported experience measures. These findings provide one of the first national studies to suggest that organizations with AFHS recognition could be associated with improvement in certain outcomes and spending.

articles.title: The aMAP Score Effectively Stratifies Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk in the Steatotic Liver Disease Population.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is an increasingly important cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet validated risk stratification tools remain limited. We aim to evaluate the aMAP score, initially developed for HCC risk prediction mainly in viral hepatitis across international cohorts, in the SLD population.

METHODS: 156 406 SLD participants were included from the UK Biobank (UKB) and 3166 SLD patients with virally suppressed chronic hepatitis B from a Chinese cohort. The predictive and stratification performance of the aMAP score was assessed and compared with the PAGE-B, mPAGE-B, CAMD and MASLD-HCC scores. A refined stratification of the aMAP-defined high-risk population identified a subgroup exceeding the recommended surveillance threshold.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 13.64 years in UKB and 9.97 years in the Chinese cohort, with 287 and 58 patients developing HCC, respectively. The aMAP score showed favourable discrimination (C-indices: 0.80 [95% CI, 0.78-0.83] in UKB; 0.79 [95% CI, 0.73-0.85] in the Chinese cohort). The 15-year cumulative HCC incidence by aMAP in UKB was 0.06% (95% CI, 0.04%-0.08%), 0.26% (95% CI, 0.21%-0.31%) and 1.43% (95% CI, 1.14%-1.72%) for low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups (high vs. low risk, sHR: 28.51; 95% CI, 19.58-41.52; Gray's test p < 0.001). Consistent results were found across etiological subgroups and in the other cohort (Gray's test p < 0.001). The refined cutoff (aMAP > 64) identified a very-high-risk subgroup in UKB with 15-year cumulative incidences of 3.08% (training; 95% CI, 1.29%-4.87%) and 5.35% (validation; 95% CI, 3.04%-7.67%).

CONCLUSIONS: The aMAP score is an effective tool for HCC risk stratification among SLD patients. The refined aMAP threshold accurately identifies very-high-risk patients qualifying for guideline-recommended surveillance.

articles.title: Association between serum magnesium status and bronchial asthma severity: a gender-matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypomagnesaemia has been implicated as a potentially modifiable correlate of poorer asthma control, but evidence from Indian outpatient populations remains limited. We evaluated the association between serum magnesium status (hypomagnesaemia versus normal or raised) and bronchial asthma severity, classified by National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) criteria, in a gender-matched retrospective cohort, adjusting for age and gender. We hypothesized a priori that hypomagnesaemia would be associated with a higher NAEPP severity grade.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Surat, Gujarat, India. Outpatient medical records were reviewed over a six-month period; 96 patients were included following 1:2 gender-based matching (32 hypomagnesaemic, 64 controls). Asthma severity was graded as mild (Grade 1), moderate (Grade 2), or severe (Grade 3) per NAEPP criteria. Association was assessed using chi-square analysis, unadjusted ordinal logistic regression, and a multivariable ordinal logistic regression adjusting for age and gender. Because the proportional-odds assumption could not be formally tested, two sensitivity analyses of severe versus non-severe asthma were performed.

RESULTS: The hypomagnesaemia group had markedly higher asthma severity: 78.1% had severe asthma versus 7.8% in controls, and no hypomagnesaemic patient had mild asthma. Chi-square analysis confirmed a highly significant association (chi-square = 49.4, df = 2, p < 0.001). In the primary adjusted ordinal model, hypomagnesaemic patients had substantially greater odds of being in a higher severity category (OR = 50.53; 95% CI 15.13 to 210.1; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses of severe versus non-severe asthma gave concordant but more conservative estimates (exact conditional OR = 39.3, 95% CI 10.75 to 178.6; Firth penalized OR = 36.8, 95% CI 11.0 to 123.0). Neither age (p = 0.096) nor gender (p = 0.935) was independently associated with severity.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypomagnesaemia was strongly associated with greater asthma severity in this cohort, and the study hypothesis was supported in this sample. Because exposure and outcome were ascertained contemporaneously from retrospective records, these data cannot establish whether hypomagnesaemia contributes to severe asthma, arises as a consequence of severe disease or its treatment, or reflects a shared cause. The wide confidence intervals reflect sparse data in the extreme severity categories. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not support a change in current practice; prospective studies with serial magnesium measurement and adjustment for treatment, renal, and nutritional confounders are required.

articles.title: Endothelial indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 drives high-tryptophan diet-mediated thrombosis in cancer-bearing mice.
articles.abstract: Cancer-associated venous thromboembolism is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with solid tumors and is driven, in part, by tumor-induced metabolic reprogramming. The tryptophan (Trp)-kynurenine (Kyn) pathway, regulated by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), is frequently upregulated in cancer and generates bioactive metabolites with immunomodulatory and vascular effects. Although pharmacologic inhibition of IDO1 reduces thrombosis in tumor-bearing mice, the endothelial-specific contribution of IDO1 to cancer-associated thrombogenesis has not been genetically defined. Here, we used IDO1 global knockout and inducible IDO1 endothelial-specific knockout mice in a syngeneic MC38 tumor model combined with dietary Trp modulation to delineate the vascular role of IDO1. Global genetic deletion of IDO1 significantly reduced systemic Kyn accumulation and attenuated thrombus formation in the inferior vena cava of tumor-bearing mice. Endothelial-specific deletion of IDO1 led to reduced Kyn levels in the plasma, suppressed tumor-induced deep vein thrombosis, and downregulated expression of key prothrombotic mediators such as tissue factor, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, and von Willebrand factor while preserving thrombomodulin expression. This suggested a selective amplification of procoagulant signaling by the Trp-IDO1-Kyn axis. Collectively, these findings provide direct genetic evidence that endothelial IDO1 is a contributing metabolic driver of cancer-associated thrombosis. Targeted control of the endothelial Trp-IDO1-Kyn pathway may represent a mechanistically informed strategy to mitigate thrombotic risk in patients with cancer.

articles.title: Thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risks after mastectomy with vs without direct-to-implant reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Immediate direct-to-implant (DTI) breast reconstruction after mastectomy provides aesthetic and logistic advantages, including single-stage restoration and avoidance of tissue expansion. However, concerns persist that increased operative duration and procedural complexity may elevate thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risk. This study compared 90-day postoperative complication rates between mastectomy and mastectomy+DTI reconstruction. A multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult female patients with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy with or without immediate DTI between 2010 and 2025 were included; autologous and staged reconstructions were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced demographics, body mass index, comorbidities, oncologic history, and preoperative medications. Outcomes included hematoma, acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE). After matching, 11 538 patients (5769 pairs) were analyzed. Mastectomy+DTI was associated with lower hematoma rates (54 patients [0.94%] vs 81 [1.40%]; risk ratio [RR], 0.675; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48-0.95; P = .024) and fewer DVT events (22 patients [0.38%] vs 48 [0.83%]; RR, 0.458; 95% CI, 0.28-0.76; P = .002). PE occurred in 17 patients (0.29%) vs 29 (0.50%) (RR, 0.586; 95% CI, 0.32-1.07; P = .076). Immediate DTI after mastectomy was associated with lower short-term rates of hematoma and DVT, with a nonsignificant trend toward lower PE rates. These findings suggest that immediate DTI was not associated with increased short-term thromboembolic or hemorrhagic morbidity in this matched cohort. Given the limitations of coding-based observational data and potential residual confounding, prospective multicenter studies incorporating granular perioperative variables are required to confirm these associations and refine risk-stratified decision-making in reconstructive care.

articles.title: Real-world thrombotic and survival outcomes with ESAs in cancer-related anemia.
articles.abstract: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are commonly used to treat cancer-related anemia by increasing hemoglobin levels and reducing transfusion requirements. However, randomized trials and meta-analyses have linked ESA use to increased thrombotic risk. Contemporary real-world data across diverse cancer populations and ESA formulations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (from 1 January 2015 to 31 July 2024) evaluating adult patients with cancer-related anemia. Patients receiving ESAs were propensity score-matched 1:1 with patients not receiving ESAs based on demographics, cancer type, and comorbidities. Individuals with previous thrombotic events or anticoagulant use were excluded. Outcomes included incident deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), new anticoagulant use, and 1-year survival. Risk differences, relative risks, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed. After matching, 1606 patients were included in each cohort, with prostate, breast, bladder, colon, and kidney cancers being the predominant cancer. There was no significant difference in DVT (1.5% vs 2.1%; P = .19) or PE (0.75% vs 1.1%; P = .27) between ESA and non-ESA groups. New anticoagulant use was significantly lower in patients treated with ESAs (6.3% vs 10.2%; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49-0.78; P < .001). One-year survival was higher in the ESA cohort (73% vs 69%; hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72-0.94; P = .004). In this large real-world cohort, ESA use was not associated with increased short-term thrombotic risk and was associated with lower anticoagulant use and improved 1-year survival. These findings suggest that guideline-concordant ESA use may be safe in selected patients with cancer-related anemia.

articles.title: Association between dual sensory impairments and new-onset cardiovascular disease among American middle-aged and older adults: the mediating role of depression.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the association between dual sensory impairment (DSI) and incident cardiovascular disease (CVD), and to evaluate the potential mediating role of depression in this relationship.

METHODS: The data were sourced from 2017/2018 (Wave 14) to 2021/2022 (Wave 16) of the University of Michigan Health and Retirement Study (HRS) of the American aged 50 and above. A counterfactual-based causal mediation framework was employed to evaluate the mediating role of continuous depression scores in the association between DSI and new-onset CVD.

RESULTS: A total of 7582 participants were included, the incidence density of CVD is 23.67/1000 person-years. Compared with the people without VI (vision impairment) and HI (hearing impairment), those with DSI were associated with a significantly higher risk of CVD (HR: 1.52, 95%CI: 1.25, 1.85). Specifically, DSI was associated with a higher risk of cardiac events (HR: 1.41, 95%CI: 1.14, 1.75) and stroke (HR: 2.25, 95%CI: 1.50, 3.36). Notably, depression mediated 25.33% of the association between DSI and new-onset CVD. Mediation effects for cardiac events and stroke were 27.04% and 17.39%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: DSI was associated with a higher risk of CVD among middle-aged and older adults. The association was partially mediated by depression.

articles.title: Limiting collateral damage: Nosocomial infections in patients with temporary mechanical circulatory support.
articles.abstract: The use of temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for patients with cardiopulmonary compromise is on the rise. While these tMCS systems provide life-saving interventions, they also pose a significant risk of nosocomial infections, which are associated with higher mortality rates. Patients receiving tMCS are critically ill and require intensive care, increasing their vulnerability to infections. Common nosocomial infections include bloodstream infections (BSI) and ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in patients with ECMO and wound-related complications in patients with microaxial temporary ventricular assist devices (tVADs). Key preventative measures include the incorporation of sound ICU practices such as chlorhexidine washes, minimizing disconnections, instituting VAP bundles, and promoting enteral nutrition. The practice of continuing prophylactic antibiotics while patients are on ECMO is not routinely recommended. While treatment strategies hinge primarily on antibiotics, ensuring adequate therapeutic levels of antibiotics is challenging and may contribute to suboptimal response to systemic antibiotics in these patients. A strategy of early liberation of patients from ECMO and conversion to temporary ventricular support (temporary LVAD, RVAD, or both) may promote early extubation and patient mobilization. Whether this strategy independently reduces infectious complications remains unknown. This review examines the epidemiology and etiology of nosocomial infections in patients receiving tMCS, summarizes current prevention and treatment strategies, and discusses the impact of infection on clinical outcomes.

articles.title: PET/CT-guided navigation-assisted debridement for tibial fracture-related infection: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fracture-related infection (FRI) is a serious complication secondary to fractures. Debridement plays a decisive role in the treatment of FRI, but precise debridement remains a surgical challenge. In this study, [18F]FDG PET/CT-guided navigation-assisted debridement was applied to the treatment of tibial FRI, and its efficacy was compared with that of conventional surgical approaches. This novel technique holds promise for achieving accurate and complete debridement of FRI lesions.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients with tibial FRI treated at our hospital between April 2021 and April 2024. A total of 78 patients were enrolled and divided into a navigation group (37 cases) and a conventional group (41 cases). Both groups underwent the two-stage Masquelet technique surgery. In the navigation group, the first-stage debridement of the infectious focus was performed under the full-process intelligent digital orthopedic operating system (Navi-OR 1) using preoperative [18F]FDG PET/CT for lesion delineation, while in the conventional group, debridement was carried out based on the surgeon's experience. The primary outcome was infection recurrence rate. Secondary outcomes included visual analogue scale (VAS), self-rating anxiety scale (SAS), lower extremity functional scale (LEFS), and activities of daily living (ADL) scores.

RESULTS: The navigation group had a significantly lower infection recurrence rate than the conventional group (10.8% [4/37] vs. 29.3% [12/41]; χ2 = 4.064, p = 0.044; absolute risk reduction: 18.5 percentage points; odds ratio: 0.293, 95% CI: 0.096 - 0.971). The mean follow-up duration was 29.5 ± 3.8 months (range: 24 - 37 months) for the navigation group and 31.0 ± 7.9 months (range: 24 - 56 months) for the conventional group. At the final follow-up, the navigation group demonstrated significantly better ADL and LEFS scores (p < 0.05) and significantly lower VAS and SAS scores (p < 0.05) compared with the conventional group.

CONCLUSION: PET/CT-guided navigation-assisted debridement appears to be a feasible surgical approach for tibial FRI, with potential benefits in reducing infection recurrence and improving functional outcomes. However, further prospective multi-center studies with standardized protocols are warranted to confirm its clinical utility.

THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS ARTICLE: This study is the first to apply PET/CT-guided navigation-assisted debridement surgery for tibial FRI, in which preoperative PET/CT assists in delineating the suspected infectious focus and intraoperative real-time guidance with an optical navigation system enables accurate and complete debridement of the infected lesion, maximizes preservation of healthy tissue, and significantly reduces the infection recurrence rate.
