articles.title: Weight loss and blood pressure lowering with GLP-1 receptor agonists and multi-hormone receptor modulators in overweight and obesity: a systematic review and meta-regression of phase 3 clinical trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity and hypertension frequently coexist, and weight-reduction is recommended as a core strategy for blood pressure (BP) management in adults with overweight or obesity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and emerging multi-hormone receptor modulators (MHRMs) induce substantial weight loss alongside modest BP reductions. However, the extent to which weight-loss is associated with BP lowering across these therapies remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of phase 3 randomized controlled trials evaluating GLP-1RAs and MHRMs in adults with overweight or obesity (PROSPERO: CRD420251146441). We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from 1946 to December 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Placebo-adjusted changes in body weight and BP at each trial's primary endpoint were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with inverse-variance weighting. Meta-regression assessed the association between weight loss and BP reduction.

FINDINGS: Thirty-seven trials including 50,171 participants were analysed. Thirty-six trials had low risk of bias across all domains. Across all trials, 50% of participants were females, 16% had type 2 diabetes and 57% had hypertension. Median treatment duration was 68 weeks. Mean placebo-adjusted weight loss was -10.1% (95% CI -11.3 to -9.0) accompanied by a -4.9 mmHg (95% CI -5.5 to -4.3) reduction in systolic BP. Between-trial meta-regression showed that 76% of the variance in systolic BP reduction was explained by differences in weight loss (R2 = 0.76; P < 0.01), corresponding to a reduction of 0.37 mmHg (95% CI 0.28 to 0.45) per 1% change in body weight.

INTERPRETATION: Across phase 3 trials of GLP-1RAs and MHRMs, greater weight loss was strongly associated with larger reductions in BP, supporting pharmacological weight-loss therapies as an adjunct strategy for BP management in obesity.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement: Clinical Challenges, Evolving Indications, and Future Directions.
articles.journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
articles.abstract: Mitral regurgitation is a highly prevalent valvular heart disease and, when hemodynamically significant, is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite advances in surgical techniques and catheter-based edge-to-edge repair, a large number of patients remain untreated due to high surgical risk or anatomical limitations. Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) has emerged as a promising therapeutic option for these patients. Over the past 15 years, the TMVR field has substantially progressed, with multiple devices advancing to human clinical evaluation. This review aims to provide an overview of the key milestones in TMVR development, patient selection pathways, and the transition from transapical to transseptal delivery. We further summarize the available clinical outcomes across different platforms and discuss remaining knowledge gaps, as well as future directions for this evolving field.

articles.title: Agreement Between In-Person and Telephone Application of the Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly.
articles.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Remote cognitive assessment has gained prominence due to limited access to in-person services. The purpose was to investigate the agreement between in-person and telephone administration of the Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE).

METHODS: For this methodological study, the IQCODE was administered to the caregiver or family member of the older adults in-person and by telephone. The order of the administration modalities was randomized, with the assessments conducted 5-7 days apart. Each participant was assessed by two different and previously trained researchers, who were blinded to the previous assessment. The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was used to assess the level of agreement between the total and item scores obtained using the two methods.

RESULTS: The study included 51 individuals. There were no statistically significant differences between the two methods (p = 0.227). Regarding the total score, a high ICC (ICC = 0.74) was observed. Regarding the items, the ICCs ranged from 0.17 to 0.98, representing low to high agreement.

CONCLUSION: The telephone assessment of the IQCODE showed adequate agreement with the in-person assessment for evaluating cognitive decline in older adults. Therefore, telephone-based assessments may be used in clinical and research settings via telephone interviews, expanding access to cognitive assessment and contributing to more inclusive care strategies.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Precision nephrology identified tumor necrosis factor activation variability in minimal change disease and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis." Kidney International 2023;103,565-579.
The Case | A man with kidney failure and an unusual abdominal CT scan.
The Case | Pulmonary nodules and acute kidney injury.
Fetal growth restriction and lifelong risk of acute kidney injury: advancing the developmental origins of kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Fetal growth restriction has long been associated with reduced nephron number and chronic kidney disease, but its relationship with acute kidney injury has remained unclear. Fog-Høyer et al. demonstrated that fetal growth restriction increases acute kidney injury risk from infancy through early adulthood, particularly in children with congenital anomalies. We examine the study's strengths, limitations, biological basis, and clinical relevance, highlighting opportunities for targeted risk stratification, preventive care, and future research.

articles.title: Estimating GFR: what it is, what it is not, and why prediction cannot settle the question.
articles.abstract: Schultheiss et al. show that replacing Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration with European Kidney Function Consortium cystatin C-based equations reclassifies women, but not men, into milder chronic kidney disease stages, while outcome prediction is unchanged. We argue that prediction of kidney failure cannot validate a glomerular filtration rate equation: dialysis initiation is a clinical decision, not a filtration measurement. The analysis is cross-sectional, leaving longitudinal performance untested. Equations are population tools; at the bedside, non-glomerular filtration rate determinants of both creatinine and cystatin C can mislead.

articles.title: Gut-targeted interventions to complement PTH-lowering therapy.
articles.abstract: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is a major contributor to skeletal fragility in chronic kidney disease, yet fracture risk remains high despite parathyroid hormone-lowering therapy. In a rat model of chronic kidney disease, Allen et al. showed that combining the prebiotic fiber inulin with a calcimimetic further suppresses elevated bone turnover while improving cortical bone architecture and mechanical properties. These findings highlight the potential of gut-targeted interventions to complement established parathyroid hormone-lowering strategies for improving skeletal health.

articles.title: Patient Preferences or Pathology: Which Takes Precedence?: November 2026 Annals of Emergency Medicine Journal Club.
In vitro inhibitory activity of recombinant olive flounder interferon-γ produced in Chlorella vulgaris against viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus infection.
articles.abstract: Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) is a major viral pathogen that causes substantial and persistent economic losses in olive flounder aquaculture. In this study, recombinant olive flounder interferon-γ (IFN-γ) was produced in the eukaryotic green microalga Chlorella vulgaris PKVL7422, and its in vitro antiviral activity was evaluated in epithelioma papulosum cyprini (EPC) cells. A codon-optimized olive flounder IFN-γ gene was introduced into C. vulgaris, and Western blot analysis showed that the recombinant protein was detected mainly in the culture supernatant. Cytotoxicity assays showed no detectable cytotoxicity at the concentrations tested in the antiviral assays, and cell viability remained above 85.6% even at 10,000 ng/mL. Antiviral activity was evaluated using recombinant VHSV expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP). Plaque assay showed that recombinant IFN-γ reduced VHSV infectivity in a dose-dependent manner, with an IC50 of 15.42 ng/mL and reduced infectivity to approximately 0% at concentrations of 100 ng/mL or higher. Fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometric analysis showed that recombinant IFN-γ reduced the VHSV-positive EPC cell population from 60.22% in the infected control group to 28.47%, 9.57%, and 4.92% at concentrations of 20, 50, and 100 ng/mL, respectively. In addition, recombinant IFN-γ induced the expression of antiviral immune-related genes, including STAT1 and ISG15, in EPC cells. These findings suggest that recombinant olive flounder IFN-γ produced in C. vulgaris retains biological activity after purification and exerts a dose-dependent antiviral effect against VHSV in a fish cell model.

articles.title: Appropriate administration of tazobactam/piperacillin for urinary and genital tract infections based on antibiotic susceptibility testing: a single-center retrospective analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tazobactam/piperacillin (TAZ/PIPC) is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent. However, improper administration may contribute to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The objectives of this study were to evaluate the appropriateness of TAZ/PIPC administration for UGTI based on antibiotic susceptibility testing and to elucidate the patients for whom alternative antibiotics can be utilized as the initial empiric therapy.

METHODS: Patients diagnosed with UGTI at the University of Toyama Hospital between January 2022 and December 2024 who received TAZ/PIPC as initial empirical therapy were analyzed retrospectively. The appropriateness of alternative agents was determined by assessing bacterial culture and antimicrobial susceptibility results.

RESULTS: Sixty-two UGTI episodes were analyzed. TAZ/PIPC utilization appeared appropriate in 91.9% of cases. Enterococcus faecalis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa were isolated more frequently in UGTI with devices or ileal urinary diversions compared to UGTI without devices. For patients with ileal urinary diversions or devices, the differences in the appropriateness rates of TAZ/PIPC versus CFPM, CTRX, and SBT/ABPC were higher than those for patients without devices. In patients without devices, the appropriateness rates of TAZ/PIPC, CFPM, CTRX, and SBT/ABPC were 96.7% (29/30), 86.7% (26/30), 83.3% (25/30), and 80.0% (24/30), respectively. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that only the presence of an ileal urinary diversion, a urethral catheter, or a ureteral stent was a risk factor for the inappropriateness (p < 0.05) for CFPM, CTRX, and SBT/ABPC.

CONCLUSION: Based on antibiotic susceptibility testing, TAZ/PIPC may be considered for UGTI using devices or ileal urinary diversions. However, alternative antibiotics may be considered for UGTIs without indwelling devices.

articles.title: Outcomes of Mindful Mood Balance for Moms, online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for perinatal depressive relapse prevention in the USA: a two-arm, single-blind, pragmatic randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective and accessible approaches to prevent depressive relapse and reduce symptoms are crucial for addressing the major public health problem of depression among perinatal women. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Mindful Mood Balance (MMB) for Moms plus usual care (hereafter MMB for Moms)-a web-based mindfulness-based cognitive therapy programme customised for perinatal women-compared with usual care only, in reducing depressive relapse and symptoms.

METHODS: This single-blind, randomised clinical trial was done across the USA, in euthymic pregnant women with recurrent depression who were on recent or current antidepressant medication. Recruitment occurred from March 7, 2019, to July 8, 2020 (data collection was completed Sept 12, 2021). Participants were randomly assigned to MMB for Moms, or usual care. Primary outcomes were reduction in depressive relapse risk and symptom burden, assessed using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and Patient Health Questionaire-9, respectively, across the study period. Outcomes were assessed from baseline until 6-months postpartum in three phases (intervention, end of intervention to delivery, and postpartum). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03623620, and is complete.

FINDINGS: Participants were recruited between March 7, 2019, and July 8, 2020. Data from 500 randomly assigned participants (mean age 32 years [SD 4·5] and mean 11·5 [2·8] weeks gestation), were analysed as the intention-to-treat sample. Of the 500 participants (249 assigned to MMB for Moms and 251 assigned to usual care), 383 [77%] provided assessment data at 3 months and 389 [78%] at 6 months postpartum. MMB for Moms had significantly lower risk of depressive relapse compared with usual care during the full trial period (up to 6 months postpartum): 81 (33%) of 249 participants assigned to MMB for Moms and 111 (44%) of 251 participants in usual care had depressive relapse (hazard ratio 0·74 [95% CI 0·56-0·99]; p=0·045; adjusted false discovery rate p=0·045). MMB for Moms was also associated with a significant reduction in depression symptom burden during the 12 week intervention phase (average decrease of 0·75 [SE 0·13] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·31 [0·13] in the usual care group) but not during the full trial period (average decrease of 0·61 [SE 0·18] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·54 [0·17] in the usual care group).

INTERPRETATION: MMB for Moms resulted in lower risk of relapse compared with usual care, and lower depression symptom burden during the intervention phase, potentially offering an effective non-pharmacological support option for depression relapse prevention during the perinatal period with positive implications for public health practice.

FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health and US National Institute of Mental Health.

articles.title: A multifaceted intervention to increase bystander CPR rates after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in France: a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a key determinant of survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but rates remain suboptimal worldwide. We evaluated whether a multifaceted intervention targeting emergency dispatch systems and community response could increase bystander-initiated CPR before emergency medical service (EMS) arrival.

METHODS: We conducted a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised trial in 15 French EMS agencies. The intervention combined dispatcher training for early recognition of cardiac arrest and telephone-assisted CPR, activation of trained volunteers through a geolocation smartphone application, and structured audit and feedback provided to EMS agencies. Consecutive adults (≥18 years) with non-traumatic OHCA were included. Randomisation was stratified by tercile of OHCA volume managed by each EMS in 2015. The intervention was implemented during a 1-month transition period before the intervention period at each EMS centre. A dedicated protocol guided dispatchers to identify cardiac arrest from unresponsiveness and abnormal breathing, then gave scripted compression-only instructions and activated volunteers, targeting recognition within 60 s of call pick-up and first compression within a further 60 s. The primary outcome was bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival. The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03633370) and is completed.

FINDINGS: Of the 15 EMS agencies initially randomised, two withdrew before recruitment began and were replaced, and one enrolled no patients. Therefore, between Aug 27, 2018, and Feb 20, 2022, 14 EMS agencies recruited a total of 2160 patients. The intention-to-treat analysis included 1684 patients (686 control, 998 intervention) enrolled across the 12 originally randomised EMS agencies. The mean age for all patients included in the intention-to-treat analysis was 67 years (SD 15), and 1205 (71·6%) were male. Bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival occurred in 421 (61·4%) patients in the control group and 708 (70·9%) patients in the intervention group (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·54 [95% CI 1·09-2·19]; p=0·017). Estimates were consistent across six prespecified sensitivity analyses (OR range, 1·38-1·55), remaining significant in four, but not after adjustment for cluster-specific secular trends (1·38 [0·98-1·94]) or baseline characteristics (1·39 [0·97-1·98]). No intervention-related adverse events were reported.

INTERPRETATION: A multifaceted intervention was associated with increased bystander-initiated CPR after OHCA, although the estimate was sensitive to the modelling of secular trends, and it did not translate into improved clinical outcomes. These findings support further investigation of coordinated community-based strategies to strengthen the early links in the chain of survival at a population level.

FUNDING: Direction Générale de l'Offre de Soins.

articles.title: Patient-month modeling for longitudinal blood culture contamination surveillance during a major healthcare-system disruption: a single-center interrupted time-series study.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Blood culture contamination (BCC) is an important diagnostic quality indicator, but crude temporal comparisons may be misleading when repeated sampling within patients is not considered. We evaluated longitudinal changes in BCC rates before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic using patient-month Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included blood culture sets obtained at a tertiary hospital in Japan from April 2017 to June 2025. Eligible episodes had at least two sets drawn within 24 h. Interrupted time-series analysis estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for level and slope changes at pandemic and post-reclassification transitions, with the number of sets as an offset and adjustment for seasonality and within-patient correlation.

RESULTS: Among 85,955 blood culture sets, 84,213 sets from 41,732 episodes in 23,705 patients were analyzed. Crude BCC rates were 1.05%, 1.55%, and 1.49% in the prepandemic, pandemic, and post-reclassification periods. No significant overall level or slope changes were observed: prepandemic-to-pandemic level-change IRR, 1.23 (95% CI, 0.93-1.62); slope-change IRR, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.99-1.01); pandemic-to-post-reclassification level-change IRR, 0.88 (95% CI, 0.68-1.14); and slope-change IRR, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.98-1.01). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested setting-specific post-reclassification changes in the intensive care unit. Sensitivity analyses were generally consistent, although the Omicron-era breakpoint analysis suggested sensitivity to breakpoint specification.

CONCLUSION: Patient-month Poisson GEE-based analysis showed that crude increases in BCC rates were not accompanied by statistically significant overall level or slope changes after accounting for repeated patient-level sampling and seasonality. Crude BCC trends should therefore be interpreted cautiously in longitudinal microbiology surveillance.

articles.title: Diagnostic image quality of shoulder magnetic resonance imaging at 0.55T in healthy subjects and patients with rotator cuff injury: Prospective comparison with 1.5T.
articles.journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower‑field 0.55 T MRI scanners with large‑bore design could offer patients more comfortable feeling and flexible position. With the advances in deep‑learning reconstruction and hardware optimization, 0.55T have greatly improved their image quality and cost‑effectiveness for musculoskeletal applications. However, its feasibility for shoulder evaluation remains unstudied.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the image quality of shoulder using 0.55T MRI in volunteers and patients with rotator cuff injury with comparison of conventional 1.5T.

METHODS: Fifty participants (25 volunteers, 25 patients) were prospectively enrolled. All participants underwent shoulder MRI both at open 0.55T with contour coils and deep learning (DL) and 1.5T MR without DL. The nonparametric method was utilized to compare image quality scores and quantitative metrics (signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (|CNR|)). Arthroscopy have been conducted in 16 patients. Kappa statistics was used to assess interobserver and interstudy agreement for lesion evaluation. Comfort feeling was also compared.

RESULTS: The scan time was 11'25″ for 0.55T MRI and 11'42″ for 1.5T MRI. The interobserver analyses showed high consistency (κ = 0.771-1.000, P: 0.008 ∼ < 0.001) among 3 readers. The scores for coronal fat suppressed T2 weighted imaging (fsT2WI) and coronal T1 weighted imaging (T1WI) were significantly higher for 0.55T MRI. Most sequences at 0.55T demonstrated significantly higher SNRs (P:0.04 ∼ < 0.001). Additionally, |CNR| values for lesions were significantly higher in fs proton weighted imaging (PDWI) and fsT2WI at 0.55T. Perfect interstudy agreement between 0.55T and 1.5T was observed between 2 readers (Kappa = 1, P < 0.001) for lesion assessment. Agreement between MRI findings and arthroscopic results was perfect or good. The 0.55T system received higher scores in comfort ratings.

CONCLUSION: The 0.55T MRI with DL, showed comparable or better image quality in healthy subjects and patients with rotator cuff injury to 1.5T MRI without DL.

articles.title: [Sport as an offer in institutions of open child and youth work : Study results on the use of sports facilities in youth centres, especially from the perspective of young people].
articles.abstract: According to Social Code Book VIII § 11, institutions of open child and youth work in Germany are a place of child and youth welfare where the interests of young people are in the foreground. Young people use this place in a self-organized way to practice sports.This article provides an overview of elected findings of the state of research on sport in open child and youth work, beginning with a look at the official child and youth welfare statistics (2021) and the youth centre survey by the German Youth Institute (2018). Based on this, the focus of this article is on the results of a qualitative, subject-oriented interview study conducted in 2023 as part of the "Move for health project" and a quantitative online survey of adolescents. It is shown how sport is practiced by young people in institutions of open child and youth work and what significance it has for them.

articles.title: [Physical activity and mental health in childhood and adolescence: a summary of the evidence from three national studies].
articles.abstract: Young people are increasingly burdened by global crises. Physical activity (PA) is considered a key factor for mental health; however, for Germany, an integrated synthesis of population-based evidence is still lacking. The aim of this narrative overview is therefore to consolidate current findings on the association between PA and mental health.The analysis draws on three population-based studies conducted as module or follow-up studies in cooperation with the KiGGS study: the MoMo study (motor performance/physical activity), the BELLA and COPSY studies (mental health), and the COMO study (interdisciplinary integration). Nationwide representative samples of children and adolescents aged 4 to 23 years were examined using validated instruments to assess PA and mental health. Findings are synthesised narratively and reported by type of activity, age, sex and socioeconomic status.Overall, positive associations between PA and mental health are observed. Higher levels of PA are associated with fewer psychological problems and higher health-related quality of life. There is evidence of protective effects, particularly in relation to leisure-time sport, both within and outside sports clubs. Self-reported PA shows stronger associations with well-being than objectively measured PA. Children from socioeconomically disadvantaged families are less likely to be physically active and experience more mental health problems. Social integration and sense of competence in sport have been identified as further key psychosocial factors. PA can therefore be considered an important resource for promoting mental health. There is a need to promote low-threshold access to physical activity programmes that specifically target disadvantaged groups in order to reduce health inequalities.

articles.title: Distinct immune signatures define hepatitis D- versus hepatitis B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108). Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators (SIMs) were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients [HBV-HCC (n=50), HDV-HCC (n=30), and matched non-HCC controls (HBV=19, HDV=17)].

RESULTS: At the time of HCC diagnosis, patients with CHD were younger, had more impaired liver synthesis and detoxification function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCCs presented with smaller tumors, less frequent portal vein infiltration, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria (all p<0.01). Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between both etiologies. Compared with HBV-HCC, HDV-HCC was characterized by a comparatively stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, whereas HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile involving IL-6- and phosphorylation- and proliferation-associated signaling. Despite these differences, event-free survival did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: HBV-HCC more frequently presented with advanced tumor stage, whereas HDV-HCC was associated with more severe underlying liver disease but smaller tumors. Importantly, HBV-associated and HDV-associated HCC exhibit distinct systemic inflammatory signatures, potentially reflecting differences in systemic immune regulation between etiologies. These findings may have implications for biomarker development and future etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Gaps in awareness of metabolic liver disease among high-risk populations in the United States.
Prospective comparative assessment of liver stiffness and steatosis between iLivTouch and FibroScan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease currently represents the leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide. FibroScan and iLivTouch are 2 devices that employ similar principles to estimate liver steatosis and fibrosis, although few studies have directly compared their results.

AIM: To evaluate the concordance of 2 transient elastography devices for the estimation of liver steatosis and fibrosis.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted. Each participant underwent liver elastography with both devices consecutively under standardized conditions. Clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical variables were collected. The diagnostic accuracy of iLivTouch was calculated using FibroScan and noninvasive scores as references.

RESULTS: A total of 1004 patients were enrolled, with a median body mass index of 25.7 kg/m2 [IQR=23.6-28.7]. Median of attenuation values was 250 dB/m [IQR=214-291] with FibroScan, 262 dB/m [IQR=239-310] with iLivTouch. Median liver stiffness measurements were 4.1 kPa [IQR=3.4-4.8] for FibroScan and 6.2 kPa [IQR=5.5-7.1] for iLivTouch. Bland-Altman analysis revealed mean differences of -19.45±49.62 dB/m for steatosis and -2.43±2.51 kPa for stiffness. Using FibroScan (>269 dB/m) as the reference, iLivTouch ≥244 dB/m demonstrated 90% sensitivity for detecting liver steatosis. The correlation between the FAST scores of the 2 devices was very strong (rho=0.90, p≤0.0001).

CONCLUSION: iLivTouch serves as an effective alternative to assess liver fibrosis and steatosis in the general population, including overweight and obese individuals.

articles.title: Effects of the GnRH agonist leuprorelin on liver volume in premenopausal women with severe polycystic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic liver disease (PLD) is characterized by multiple liver cysts, sometimes leading to severe liver enlargement, with associated physical and psychosocial complaints. Treatment options are limited. Female gender is a risk factor for PLD; estrogen supplementation increases liver size in women with PLD, whereas the polycystic liver decreases after menopause. Estrogens may therefore be a target for therapy.

METHODS: In this prospective, open-label study, premenopausal women aged 18-45 years with severe PLD were randomized 1:1 to a direct start of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist leuprorelin (n=6) or to standard care with delayed start of leuprorelin 18 months after randomization (n=8). The gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (11.25 mg injections once every 3 mo) leads to a reduction in estrogens and progesterone, and consequently to medically induced menopause. The primary outcome was liver growth rate at 18 months. Secondary outcomes comprised quality of life, menopausal side effects, and adverse events. An interim analysis was performed when all participants had reached month 18, as notable side effects were expressed.

RESULTS: In the group with direct start of leuprorelin, liver volume still increased in half of the participants, with the median liver growth rate not significantly different from the standard care group (4.04 [-4.62 to 6.84] vs. 11.0 [0.70-13.2] %/year, respectively, p=0.15). Importantly, PLD-related quality of life did not improve with treatment, whereas menopausal side effects were severe, leading one participant to stop treatment early. The total number of adverse events in the direct versus standard care group was 38 versus 9, respectively (p<0.001). Because of these results, the study was terminated early.

CONCLUSIONS: leuprorelin treatment did not reverse liver volume, while menopausal side effects and adverse events were substantial.

articles.title: Enhanced liver fibrosis score is associated with cognitive performance during an 11-year follow-up period.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has been associated with poorer cognitive performance and greater cognitive decline. However, the liver-brain axis and the role of liver health in cognitive decline are still poorly understood. Thus, using both cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, we aimed to study how liver fibrosis score (ELF), an indicator of liver fibrosis, is associated with cognitive performance.

METHODS: This study was based on the Health 2000 Survey and its follow-up, the Health 2011 survey, which collected data from a nationally representative sample of the Finnish adult population. At baseline, verbal fluency, wordlist learning, delayed wordlist recall, and simple and multiple-choice reaction time tests were conducted. At follow-up, all tests except the reaction time tests were repeated. A global z-score was derived from the individual cognitive domains. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to study the association between ELF and cognitive performance while adjusting for demographic, metabolic, and cardiovascular covariates.

RESULTS: Cross-sectionally (n=5115; mean age 53.2 y; 58.6% women), high ELF was associated with poorer global cognition and slower simple and multiple-choice reaction times compared with low ELF. High ELF was also associated with worse global cognition and performance in the wordlist learning test, both cross-sectionally and longitudinally (n=2490; mean age 48.7 y at baseline; 58.0% women).

DISCUSSION: High ELF, an indicator of liver fibrosis, was associated with poorer global cognition both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. Worse performance was observed in cognitive domains that reflect poorer processing speed and executive function, verbal learning, attention, and working memory. These results imply that liver fibrosis could represent an early modifiable marker of cognitive vulnerability.

articles.title: Current and emerging sublingual immunotherapies for dust mite allergy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: House dust mites (HDMs) are the most prevalent inhalant allergens globally, inducing a spectrum of allergic diseases including allergic rhinitis (AR) and asthma, which substantially impair patients' quality of life. Sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) is recognized as a promising disease-modifying intervention for HDM-related allergic disorders.

AREAS COVERED: This paper presents a narrative review of up-to-date clinical evidence regarding SLIT for HDM allergy (HDM-SLIT), covering its therapeutic efficacy, patient selection criteria, dose optimization strategies, safety profiles, underlying immunological mechanisms, and unresolved clinical challenges.

EXPERT OPINION: HDM-SLIT has been established as a disease-modifying therapy for HDM-induced AR and asthma, with supporting evidence demonstrating its clinical efficacy, favorable safety profile, and long-lasting tolerability. Future developments in precision allergology, including multiomics-derived biomarkers and digital health applications, show considerable potential to guide clinical decision-making. However, the translation of these advances into routine clinical practice remains limited by gaps in insurance reimbursement, suboptimal patient adherence, inconsistent regulatory standards across regions, insufficient product standardization, and inequitable access to healthcare resources.

articles.title: Sleep Disturbances in Chronic Kidney Disease - The CKD-REIN Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Insomnia and excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) are common in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their determinants are poorly understood. We analyzed multiple factors likely to affect sleep with the aim of disentangling the contributions of CKD markers and symptoms from those of social factors, lifestyle, comorbid conditions, and drug-induced effects, with the latter 2 highly prevalent in this population.

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: In total, 2,765 patients with CKD stages 2-5 not receiving dialysis (mean age, 67 ± 13 years; 66% men) from a representative sample of 40 nephrology clinics in France.

EXPOSURES: Albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate, CKD symptoms, lifestyle, comorbid conditions, and medications collected annually.

OUTCOMES: Insomnia and EDS ≥ 3 times/week in the past 3 months assessed with a standardized questionnaire at baseline, 1-, 3-, and 5-year follow-ups, providing 7,264 observations overall.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Adjusted odds ratios of insomnia and EDS associated with time-updated exposures estimated with mixed effects logistic regressions.

RESULTS: Baseline prevalence of reported insomnia was 22% (95% confidence interval, 21%-24%) and that of EDS, 15% (14%-16%). Based on the 7,264 observations, neither prevalence was associated with albuminuria after adjustment for age and gender. The odds ratio of EDS alone increased significantly with decreasing estimated glomerular filtration rate, 1.16 (1.05-1.28 mL/min/1.73 m2) per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2, independent of social factors, physical activity, obesity, heart failure, and long half-life benzodiazepine use. It was no longer significant after adjustment for fatigue, which displayed a strong dose-effect relation with EDS, depression, insomnia, and sleep apnea. Insomnia prevalence increased strongly with severity of cramps, itching, and stress, independent of other determinants including female gender, heart failure, thyroid hormone use, depression, and sleep apnea.

LIMITATIONS: Self-reported sleep disturbances and limited longitudinal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the multifactorial nature of sleep disturbances in CKD and the potentially modifiable contribution of CKD symptoms and drug-induced effects.

articles.title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications. Of these, 160 studies met the inclusion criteria. Only studies applying fully automated DL networks to echocardiographic loops were considered. Performance estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. The studies were categorized into five distinct groups: prediction of disease or mortality, replication of established measures, segmentation of cardiac chambers, classification of chamber views, and assessment of image quality. High heterogeneity that could not be resolved was observed in studies focusing on cardiac chamber segmentation and classification. Model performance was influenced by a variety of different factors, including medical target and input characteristics such as video resolution, number of frames used, and total participants included during training.

CONCLUSION: DL models achieve high performance across various applications in echocardiography. In selected tasks, they may reduce reliance on expert input and support greater automation of echocardiographic workflows. However, further validation, assessment of clinical utility, and evaluation in real-world settings are required before widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: Polyomavirus Drives Cerebellar Lesions in AIDS Monkeys With Ataxia.
articles.abstract: Cognitive and motor dysfunction occurs in 30%-50% of people with HIV/AIDS. Within this clinical spectrum, HIV-associated ataxia is an uncommon but debilitating disorder with poorly defined neuropathological mechanisms. This study investigated two rhesus macaques with chronic simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infection that developed progressive ataxia, characterized by postural imbalance and nystagmus. Comparative neuropathological profiling of cerebellar tissue from ataxic SIV-infected macaques, non-ataxic SIV-infected macaques, and uninfected controls revealed that ataxia was associated with diffuse cerebellar atrophy, disrupted tissue organization, Purkinje cell degeneration, demyelination, glial nodule formation, and prominent microglial neuroinflammation. Cerebellar infection with simian polyomavirus 40 (SV40), a member of the Polyomaviridae family, was identified as the cause of the lesions, with viral tropism primarily involving cerebellar granule neurons. Mechanistically, SV40 infection induced neuronal pyroptosis and inflammatory cytokine release, promoting microglial recruitment and activation, amplifying local neuroinflammation, and culminating in nodular aggregate formation. Collectively, these findings establish SV40 infection as a direct driver of cerebellar pathology in SIV-associated ataxia and define a pathogenic sequence linking granule neuron pyroptosis, microglial activation, and progressive cerebellar injury-a cascade that may parallel polyomavirus-induced ataxia in people living with HIV-1.

articles.title: The Role of Astrocytes in the Inflammatory Response in Neurodiseases.
articles.abstract: Astrocytes have emerged as central regulators of neuroinflammation, extending far beyond their traditional roles as structural and metabolic support cells. In neurological disorders, astrocytes undergo reactive remodeling that encompasses morphological, transcriptional, metabolic, and functional changes. Rather than fitting into a fixed A1/A2 dichotomy, reactive astrocytes exist along a disease-, region-, and stage-dependent continuum shaped by local pathology and intercellular crosstalk. This review summarizes how astrocytes contribute to neuroinflammatory processes in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, central nervous system injury, infection, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder. We highlight convergent mechanisms, including cytokine and chemokine release, complement activation, glutamate and ion homeostasis disruption, oxidative stress, metabolic reprogramming, and blood-brain barrier regulation, while emphasizing disease-specific astrocytic programs. We further discuss astrocyte interactions with microglia, neurons, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells, and peripheral immune cells, as well as key regulatory pathways, epigenetic remodeling, and lipid-dependent metabolic signaling. Finally, we evaluate current and emerging astrocyte-targeted therapeutic strategies, including metabolic modulation, receptor targeting, gene editing, nanodelivery, and gut-brain axis interventions. Defining functionally validated astrocyte states and developing biomarker-guided, stage-adaptive therapies may enable more precise intervention in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Cognitive frailty and mortality among patients on the heart transplant waiting list: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Frailty is an important prognostic factor in patients with heart failure and in transplant candidates, while cognitive impairment remains an under-recognized component that may further worsen clinical outcomes. This prospective study aimed to determine the prevalence of physical and cognitive frailty among heart transplant candidates and their association with mortality. Physical frailty was assessed using the Fried criteria; cognition was evaluated using the MoCA (cognitive screening) and WASI (general intellectual functioning); and depressive symptoms were measured using the BDI. Cognitive frailty was defined as the presence of ≥3 of 6 criteria in a modified Fried phenotype, which incorporated cognitive impairment as an additional domain. A total of 150 patients listed for heart transplantation within the previous 30 days were included at a tertiary center in Brazil. The study population was predominantly male (70%), with Chagas disease etiology (35%), and a mean age of 49.8 ± 10.4 years. Physical frailty was present in 78.7% of patients, cognitive frailty in 88.7% (MoCA) and 86.7% (WASI), and depressive symptoms in 44%, which were significantly associated with physical frailty (p = 0.021). During 1-year follow-up, 41.3% of patients died and 67.3% underwent transplantation. Physical frailty was associated with an increased risk of early mortality after listing (initial SHR = 5.47; p = 0.023), with significant attenuation of this effect over time (TVC SHR = 0.99; p = 0.008). A similar pattern was observed for cognitive frailty, measured by both MoCA (initial SHR = 1.61; p = 0.011; TVC SHR = 1.00; p = 0.011) and WASI (initial SHR = 1.57; p = 0.012; TVC SHR = 1.00; p = 0.007), indicating a reduction in its impact on mortality risk over time. However, after multivariable adjustment, neither physical nor cognitive frailty remained independently associated with overall mortality. Physical and cognitive frailty were highly prevalent among heart transplant candidates and showed a time-dependent association with early mortality risk. After adjustment for disease severity markers, this association lost significance, suggesting that frailty may, at least in part, reflect the underlying clinical status at the time of listing rather than acting as an independent prognostic factor. These findings also raise questions regarding the adequacy of the Fried phenotype as a frailty assessment tool in this specific population.

articles.title: Incident Type 2 Diabetes in Individuals With CKD: The REGARDS Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and diabetes are comorbid metabolic diseases that share common factors such as insulin resistance. Few studies have examined the association between CKD and incident diabetes, with limited consensus and associated risk factors. We conducted an analysis of participants in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in stroke study to investigate incident diabetes among participants with CKD compared with non-CKD participants.

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Total of 7,511 participants who completed 10 years of follow-up were included in the analysis, of whom 994 had CKD (an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73m2 or albumin-to-creatinine ratio >30mg/g) at baseline.

EXPOSURE: CKD.

OUTCOME: Incident diabetes.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Logistic regression analysis was performed to estimate the odds of incident diabetes among CKD participants, with odds ratio (OR) and 95% CI. Risk factors for incident diabetes among CKD participants were also examined.

RESULTS: After 10 years of follow-up, 11.0% (717) of non-CKD participants and 15.8% (157) of CKD participants developed diabetes. Incident diabetes was higher among CKD participants than in non-CKD participants using creatinine-based equations, which was not seen when using a creatinine-based and cystatin C-based equation for CKD. Several risk factors such as race, prediabetes, age, body mass index, hypertension, current smoking, and exercise ≥ 4 times/week increased the odds of incident diabetes, whereas current alcohol use had a lower risk of incident diabetes. Prediabetes had the highest risk of incident diabetes (OR = 4.94, 95% Cl: 4.22-5.78; P < 0.01).

LIMITATIONS: Attrition bias, limited generalizability, and limited diagnostic classification.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between CKD and incident diabetes depends on how CKD is defined. These findings highlight the need for future studies to explore how renal function is assessed when determining adverse outcomes related to CKD.

articles.title: Development and validation of a model using routine clinical features to improve diabetes diagnosis.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Hemoglobin A1c (A1c) and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) miss diabetes diagnosis in many individuals, but the alternative, oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT), is difficult to obtain.

OBJECTIVE: This work aimed to develop and validate a model to identify diabetes missed by A1c and FPG but detected by OGTT and associate its outcomes with mortality.

METHODS: We trained machine-learning models using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data, applied them to corresponding National Center for Health Statistics mortality data, and externally validated the models with Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study (DPPOS) data. We tested models including the A1c, vital signs, complete blood count, and comprehensive metabolic panel with and without the FPG. This retrospective analysis included NHANES study participants from 1999 to 2016 and DPPOS study participants from 1996 to 2020. Main outcome measures included the area under the receiver operating curve, sensitivity, and specificity of models to detect diabetes.

RESULTS: The A1c/FPG+ model had better sensitivity for DPPOS individuals with A1c less than 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) and FPG less than 126 mg/dL compared to a logistic regression of A1c and FPG and recalibrated FPG for individuals both on (0.69 vs 0.53 vs 0.57, respectively) and off (0.75 vs 0.65 vs 0.68, respectively) medication. NHANES participants without diabetes but with A1c/FPG+-predicted diabetes had elevated risk of mortality compared to those without A1c/FPG+-predicted diabetes (HR = 1.4; P < 2 × 10-16).

CONCLUSION: Machine-learning models can improve the detection of individuals who would need OGTT assessment to diagnose diabetes using standard nonfasting laboratory values and vital signs with and without FPG.

articles.title: Association between early intravenous magnesium sulfate administration and mortality according to systemic immune-inflammation index in critically ill patients with acute heart failure: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnesium sulfate is commonly administered in acute heart failure (AHF). We investigated the association between early intravenous magnesium sulfate and mortality across baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) strata in critically ill patients with AHF.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using the MIMIC-IV database of critically ill patients with AHF. Early intravenous magnesium sulfate was defined as treatment initiated from 6 h before to 24 h after intensive care unit admission. SII was categorized into quartiles. The primary and secondary outcomes were 30-day and 90-day all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline, and sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 4293 patients, 1561 (36.4%) received intravenous magnesium sulfate. Magnesium sulfate administration was associated with lower 30-day (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.82) and 90-day mortality (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.86). For 30-day mortality, multivariable Cox regression demonstrated significant associations in the lowest (aHR 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.95) and highest (aHR 0.52, 95% CI 0.36-0.75) SII quartiles, whereas no significant associations were identified in the intermediate quartiles. Comparable patterns were observed for 90-day mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses showed visual separation between treatment groups at the extremes of the SII distribution, although formal interaction testing was not significant. Sensitivity analyses consistently reproduced the association in the highest SII quartile.

CONCLUSIONS: Stratified analyses suggested that the association between early magnesium sulfate administration and lower mortality was most evident in the highest SII quartile and less consistent in the lowest quartile. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Predictive value of monocyte-to-HDL and neutrophil-to-HDL cholesterol ratio for obstructive coronary artery disease in Patients undergoing coronary angiography.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) and neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (NHR) are emerging composite biomarkers that reflect systemic inflammatory status and lipid metabolism. Although both indices have individually been associated with coronary artery disease (CAD), evidence directly comparing their diagnostic performance for obstructive CAD remains scarce.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to compare the diagnostic performance of MHR and NHR in identifying obstructive CAD among patients undergoing elective coronary angiography.

METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted involving patients who underwent diagnostic coronary angiography in Jordan. Obstructive CAD was defined as stenosis of 50% or more in a major epicardial vessel on invasive coronary angiography.

RESULTS: A total of 215 patients were included, of whom 129 (60%) were male, with a mean age of 58.4 ± 11.4 years; 43.7% had obstructive CAD. After adjusting for age, sex, and prior CAD history in multivariate regression analysis, MHR remained an independent predictor of obstructive CAD (OR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.34-2.97, p < 0.001), whereas NHR was not independently associated (OR = 1.66, 95%CI: 0.74-3.69, p = 0.21). The clinical model integrating MHR demonstrated an AUC of 0.801 (95% CI: 0.74-0.86); however, this numerical increase was not statistically significant (DeLong test, p = 0.216).

CONCLUSION: MHR may have potential value for risk stratification in obstructive CAD. Although adding MHR to the clinical model resulted in a numerically higher AUC, the incremental improvement in discrimination was not statistically significant. Further studies involving larger, multicenter cohorts are needed to establish the incremental predictive and clinical utility of MHR.

articles.title: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion versus oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: A pragmatic meta-analysis of randomized trials within the DOAC era.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC). However, its safety and efficacy boundaries remain incompletely defined in dedicated comparisons against direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).

OBJECTIVE: This study applied a pragmatic framework to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of LAAO versus OAC in a DOAC-predominant setting.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAO with OAC, restricted to a DOAC-predominant comparator. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated via a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model.

RESULTS: Four trials comprising 5890 patients were included (96.4% of controls assigned to DOACs). Overall stroke (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.87-1.60; p = 0.28), systemic embolism (RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.29-4.08; p = 0.89), major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.81-1.19; p = 0.85), hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.45-1.51; p = 0.53), and all-cause mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85-1.17; p = 0.99) did not differ significantly. Ischemic stroke presented numerical asymmetry favoring OAC that approached statistical significance (RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.89; p = 0.06). Conversely, within available protocol-defined datasets, LAAO significantly reduced nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.43-0.60; p < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: In a pragmatic analysis of the DOAC era, randomized data show no statistically significant differences for hard individual endpoints, though broad confidence intervals reflect precision limits. A numerical asymmetry for ischemic stroke favored OAC, while LAAO reduced nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding. Current evidence remains non-definitive, warranting shared clinical decision-making to balance individual thromboembolic risks against long-term bleeding susceptibility.

articles.title: Early efficacy of oral lipid lowering therapy in achieving LDL-C targets following acute coronary syndrome: A real-world observational study.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity statins are the cornerstone of post-ACS management. Real-world data frequently indicate suboptimal adherence and low attainment of guideline-recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the early efficacy of oral lipid-lowering therapy in achieving LDL-C targets following ACS in a recent cohort of Indian patients.

METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 511 statin-naive ACS patients. High-intensity statin monotherapy (atorvastatin 80 mg daily or rosuvastatin 40 mg daily) was initiated following diagnosis. Lipid profile, including total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, and VLDL-C, were assessed at baseline, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28. Primary endpoints included the proportion of patients achieving LDL-C goals at Day 28.

RESULTS: 50.5% of patients achieved the 2019 ESC/EAS LDL-C target (<55 mg/dL) at day 28. Similarly, 68.9% achieved the 2018 ACC/AHA target (<70 mg/dL), and 44.6% achieved the 2020 Lipid Association of India (LAI) target (<50 mg/dL) at day 28. The mean LDL-C reduced from 73.43 ± 13.99 mg/dL at Day 0 to 61.26 ± 27.00 mg/dL at Day 28, corresponding to a 16.6% reduction from baseline. On multivariate analysis, baseline LDL-C, type 2 diabetes mellitus and multivessel coronary disease were found to be independent negative predictors for achieving LDL-C goal <50 mg/dL at day 28.

CONCLUSION: LDL-C target attainment following ACS remains suboptimal despite high-intensity statin therapy, highlighting the need for earlier and more intensive lipid-lowering strategies in high-risk Indian patients.

articles.title: The impact of an adaptive patient-centered web application on medication optimization in patients with HFrEF: Rationale and design of the SmartHF trial.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart failure (HF) remains a significant public health burden, with frequent readmissions often driven by a lack of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) optimization. While clinical decision support (CDS) can improve healthcare processes, patient-centered tools that empower individuals to participate in their own care are increasingly needed. We developed SmartHF, an adaptive web application that provides patients with tailored HFrEF GDMT recommendations based on their clinical data.

METHODS: This 12-week, multicenter randomized controlled trial enrolled adults with HFrEF (LVEF </=40%). Participants were randomized 1:1 to either the SmartHF intervention or usual care. The application uses a computable algorithm to integrate electronic health record (EHR) data, including medications, laboratory results, and vitals, via patient portal authorization. The primary endpoint is the change in a GDMT medication optimization score from baseline to Week 12.

RESULTS: Enrollment concluded in August 2025 with a total of 225 participants. The study population had a mean age of 61.9 years, with 36% identifying as female and 52% as Black or African American. At baseline, 84% of participants were prescribed an ACEi/ARB/ARNI, 90% were on beta-blockers, 67% were prescribed an SGLT2i, while only 53% were on a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA). The mean baseline medication optimization score was 68.5. Final trial results are expected in Winter 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: SmartHF is an innovative, low-touch digital health intervention that leverages EHR integration to facilitate patient-provider discussions on medication optimization. By providing personalized, guideline-based recommendations, the tool aims to improve GDMT prescribing in patients with HFrEF.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05858320.
