articles.title: Spiked Helmet Sign in the Early Post-Heart Transplantation Period: A Dramatic STEMI Mimic in a Structurally Normal Donor Heart.
articles.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
articles.abstract: A 36-year-old woman with severe dilated cardiomyopathy (LVEF 14%, NYHA IV) underwent heart transplantation. Postoperatively, she developed subarachnoid hemorrhage and septic shock. The ECG revealed a spiked helmet sign (SHS) pattern, with repolarization abnormalities and QT prolongation. Despite transient clinical improvement and resolution of the ECG changes after intensive support, the patient died due to infectious complications. This case highlights the occurrence of SHS in the early posttransplant period in a structurally normal donor heart, a previously unreported presentation, reinforcing its extracardiac origin and association with critical illness and poor prognosis.

articles.title: Effects of Aerobic Exercise on Autonomic and Endothelial Function and Splanchnic Hemodynamics in Compensated Cirrhosis: RCT Study.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with cirrhosis often develop autonomic dysfunction (AD) and endothelial dysfunction (ED), which correlate with higher mortality. Aerobic exercise (AE) is a potential intervention, yet its effects on the autonomic nervous system (ANS) and hemodynamics remain underinvestigated in cirrhosis.

METHODS: We conducted a parallel-group randomized controlled trial including 50 sedentary patients with compensated cirrhosis. Participants were randomized to a 16-week moderate-intensity AE plus nutritional consultation (AE group; n = 25) or nutritional consultation alone (control group, CG; n = 25). Outcomes included heart rate variability (HRV), flow-mediated dilation (FMD) for peripheral circulation, mesenteric Doppler ultrasound for splanchnic hemodynamics, and sarcopenia-related outcomes (body composition, handgrip strength dynamometry, and the 6-min walk test [6MWT]). Data were analysed using intention-to-treat (ITT), modified ITT (mITT), and per-protocol approaches, as well as general linear mixed models (LMM).

RESULTS: Of the 50 participants (mean age, 62.6 ± 7.0 years; 60% female), 44 participants completed the study. Although most outcomes showed no statistically significant between-group differences, LMM analysis confirmed a significant reduction in the low-frequency to high-frequency (LF/HF) (β = -0.87, p = 0.04), indicating worsening ANS while AE remained stable. Based on mITT analysis, the AE group showed a significant with-in group increase in portal vein volume flow (median Δ = 350.66 mL/min, p = 0.003). Additionally, AE demonstrated significant improvement in 6MWT compared with CG (mean Δ = 32 m, IQR: 12.00-51.60 m, p < 0.01). No major adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: AE is safe and effectively improves functional capacity in compensated cirrhosis. However, positive signals in autonomic and hepatic parameters were not between-group significant, necessitating a cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Excess Liver Fat in Type 2 Diabetes Stratified by Intrapancreatic Fat Deposition: A Meta-Analysis of Dual-Organ MRI Studies.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Both liver fat content (LFC) and intrapancreatic fat deposition (IPFD) are frequently increased in Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We meta-analysed dual-organ MRI studies comparing LFC between individuals with T2DM and non-diabetic controls and explored whether study-level differences in LFC varied according to IPFD burden. Seventeen studies (2142 participants) were included. Individuals with T2DM had significantly higher LFC than non-diabetic controls (standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.89, 95% CI 0.60-1.18). In exploratory subgroup analyses, liver fat excess was larger in studies with mean IPFD ≥ 10% than in those with IPFD < 10% (SMD 1.20 vs. 0.62; p = 0.04), though this finding was not consistently retained in leave-one-out analyses. Alternative IPFD cutoffs yielded directionally similar but non-significant subgroup differences. Study-level differences in IPFD were associated with differences in LFC (β = 0.383, p = 0.006) in univariable meta-regression, but not after BMI adjustment. These findings suggest that higher IPFD is associated with greater liver fat excess in T2DM at the study level. Individual-level analyses are now warranted to clarify this relationship.

articles.title: Similar Long-Term Incidence of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B Initiating Entecavir Versus Tenofovir Alafenamide: A REAL-B Study.
articles.abstract: Data on potential differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients are limited. This retrospective multinational study included treatment-naïve adults with CHB without a history of HCC who initiated ETV or TAF therapy since 2016 at 23 centres in 4 countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). HCC incidence and the association between antiviral regimen and HCC were analysed using competing-risk analysis. A total of 1437 patients (710 ETV, 727 TAF) were included, with similar mean follow-up durations (55.5 ± 29.8 vs. 58.0 ± 25.5 months; p = 0.077). ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis. After IPTW, both groups had balanced characteristics (all standardised differences < 0.1). After IPTW adjustment, during follow-up, 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively (p = 0.853). There was no statistically significant difference in HCC risk between the groups (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.44-2.65; p = 0.851), with consistent findings across subgroups by age, sex, cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, HBeAg, baseline liver enzymes, HBV DNA levels, diabetes mellitus and in sensitivity analysis using PSM. In this real-world multinational study of treatment-naïve CHB patients, HCC incidence did not significantly differ between ETV and TAF groups, suggesting therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors.

articles.title: Renin-Angiotensin System Activation Drives Early Cardiorenal Dysfunction in Normotensive Prediabetes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prediabetes is increasingly recognised as a stage at which cardiovascular and renal dysfunction begin to develop despite the absence of overt metabolic disease. The mechanisms underlying these early alterations remain poorly understood. Because adipose tissues surrounding blood vessels and kidneys can locally generate components of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), we hypothesised that subclinical RAS activation contributes to early cardiorenal dysfunction in prediabetes.

METHODS: Using a pre-established normotensive, non-obese rat model of prediabetes induced by 12 weeks of mild hypercaloric feeding, we examined the impact of systemic angiotensin II (AngII) elevation and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibition on cardio-, cerebro- and renovascular function by invasive hemodynamics, ex vivo pressure myography, and ex vivo renal perfusion experiments, respectively.

RESULTS: Prediabetic rats exhibited impaired parasympathetic baroreceptor sensitivity and altered renovascular endothelium-dependent vasodilation despite preserved blood pressure and cardiac function. Systemic AngII infusion further exacerbated autonomic and renovascular dysfunction. In contrast, treatment with a non-hypotensive dose of the ACE inhibitor captopril restored baroreceptor sensitivity, improved renovascular endothelial function, reduced brainstem inflammation, and attenuated renal tubular fibrosis. Examination of perivascular and perirenal adipose tissues revealed significantly higher protein concentration of ACE1 in prediabetic rats compared to controls.

CONCLUSION: These findings are consistent with an early activation of RAS contributing to subclinical cardiovascular and renal dysfunction during prediabetes independently of hypertension. Targeting RAS signalling at this early stage may therefore represent a strategy to limit progression of cardiorenal complications along the continuum from prediabetes to diabetes.

articles.title: Innovative therapies in rheumatoid arthritis: CAR T cells and bispecific antibodies.
authors: Club for Innovative Immunotherapies in Immune-mediated Inflammatory Diseases
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease, and therapeutic strategies predominantly rely on continuous immunomodulation. Despite major advances with biological and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, some patients develop persistent, objectively active inflammatory disease that remains refractory to multiple therapeutic mechanisms. Durable drug-free remission is rare, highlighting a major unmet need. Emerging deep B-cell depleting therapies, including bispecific T-cell engagers and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell-based therapies, challenge the current treatment framework by aiming to eradicate or reprogramme pathogenic immune memory rather than chronically suppress inflammatory pathways. Early clinical evidence in rheumatoid arthritis suggests that CD19-directed T-cell engagers and B-cell depleting CAR T cells might induce profound immunological remodelling and sustained drug-free remission in some individuals. This Review critically appraises the available clinical and translational evidence supporting deep B-cell depleting therapies in rheumatoid arthritis, compares their mechanisms, feasibility, and harms, and discusses their potential positioning across the disease spectrum. Finally, this Review proposes a research agenda that prioritises innovative trial designs, deep immunomonitoring, tissue-based analyses, and long-term safety surveillance to responsibly translate deep B-cell depleting strategies into rheumatology practice.

articles.title: Identification of Risk-Related Prenatal Medication Exposure Profiles for Childhood Asthma Using the Bayesian Profile Regression: A Cohort Study Using the POMME Cohort.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify prenatal medication exposure profiles associated with childhood asthma.

METHODS: This population-based cohort study used data from the POMME (PrescriptiOn Médicaments Mères Enfants) cohort, including 18 851 children born in the Haute-Garonne area (France) in 2010 and 2015, and followed until 2023. Prenatal exposure was defined as medications dispensed to mothers during pregnancy, classified by Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical subclasses, assessed separately for each trimester as none, one dispensing, or at least two dispensings. Childhood asthma from Age 4 years onward was identified using an algorithm based on dispensing of asthma medications. Bayesian profile regression was applied to simultaneously cluster children according to prenatal medication exposure profiles and asthma occurrence. High-risk profiles were characterised by predominant medication classes, timing of exposure and maternal and infant characteristics.

RESULTS: Seventeen prenatal medication exposure profiles were identified. Six profiles were associated with a higher average risk of childhood asthma compared with the overall population risk (15.2%). High-risk profiles were characterised by repeated exposure throughout pregnancy to medications for acid-related disorders, thyroid hormones, antibiotics, asthma medications and antihistamines, as well as by combinations involving antibiotics, nasal medications and cold medicines in late pregnancy. Mothers in high-risk profiles more frequently presented chronic conditions and pregnancy-related complications.

CONCLUSION: This exploratory study identified prenatal medication exposure profiles associated with childhood asthma using a semi-supervised Bayesian approach. This method highlights combinations and critical windows that may warrant further investigation and supports Bayesian profile regression as a useful tool for signal detection in perinatal pharmacoepidemiology.

articles.title: Prehospital Pediatric Ventilation Quality Following Use of a Feedback Device: A Randomized Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Manual ventilation is a lifesaving intervention for children in respiratory arrest, yet the quality of pediatric ventilation delivered by emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians across geographically distinct sites is poorly characterized. We evaluated baseline EMS ventilation performance and whether a ventilation feedback device (VFD) improves adherence to national and international ventilation guidelines for ventilation rate, tidal volume, and mask seal.

METHODS: We conducted a single-anonymized, randomized, crossover study of EMS clinicians from 5 EMS agencies across 3 metropolitan sites in the United States. Using a simulated 3-year-old toddler manikin, participants completed 2 sequential 2-minute respiratory arrest scenarios separated by a 10-minute washout period. Participants performed ventilation with and without real-time VFD feedback in randomized order. The EOLifeX VFD recorded ventilation rate, tidal volume, and mask leak with each breath. Adherence to age-based guidelines was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models with participants nested within sites.

RESULTS: We enrolled 123 participants across 5 agencies. With VFD feedback, guideline-recommended tidal volumes were achieved in 87% of breaths compared with 16.2% without feedback. Ventilation rate adherence improved from 65% to 88.6%. Mask leak of less than 30% occurred in 88.4% of ventilations with feedback vs 80% without feedback.

CONCLUSION: In our simulation study, EMS clinicians rarely met manual ventilation guidelines for pediatric patients in respiratory arrest. The use of a VFD substantially improved guideline adherence, suggesting broad potential to improve ventilation performance.

articles.title: Emergency Department-Administered Extended-Release Buprenorphine After Fentanyl Overdose Reversed by Emergency Medical Services With Naloxone.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) providers are on the frontline of the opioid epidemic and administered naloxone to reverse suspected overdose over 442,000 times in 2024. Interest in EMS-initiated sublingual (SL) buprenorphine (BUP) exists; however, initiation of month-long extended-release buprenorphine (XR-BUP) in the immediate postoverdose period has not yet been described. The high risk of death from repeat overdose in patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) could be reduced by administration of XR-BUP. The purpose of this case report is to highlight the utility of EMS-initiated SL-BUP followed by XR-BUP to potentially improve care linkage and adherence to medication-assisted OUD treatment.

CASE REPORT: A bystander call to 911 dispatched a Basic Life Support (BLS) unit to an unresponsive 30-year-old man found with fentanyl-smoking paraphernalia. First responders administered 8 mg of intranasal naloxone. Paramedics arrived 8 min later and assessed the patient to be in opioid withdrawal with a Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS) score of 22. The patient reported using heroin or fentanyl and methamphetamine daily. After consent, paramedics administered 16 mg of SL-BUP. In the ED, an addiction medicine consult service administered a 300-mg monthly XR-BUP formulation. WHY SHOULD AN EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN BE AWARE OF THIS?: We report that rapid transition from naloxone reversal of overdose and EMS initiated SL-BUP to month-long XR-BUP is possible during a single emergency medicine encounter using a stepwise clinical pathway. We hope our observations encourage further prospective study of the intervention described as this may link patients to medication assisted OUD treatment, which decreases mortality in patients with OUD.

articles.title: [Branchial cleft anomalies of the neck : Embryology, clinical presentation, and management].
articles.abstract: Branchial cleft anomalies are the second most common congenital neck lesion. They present as cysts, sinuses, or fistulas arising from remnants of the pharyngeal apparatus; second arch anomalies predominate. The embryologic origin determines their anatomical relationships to nerves, vessels, and the pharynx and guides diagnosis and surgical planning. Typical findings are cervical swelling, cutaneous discharge, or recurrent infection. Third and fourth branchial anomalies may cause recurrent neck abscesses or acute suppurative thyroiditis, particularly in children. Ultrasonography is the primary imaging modality. Complete excision during a non-acute inflammatory interval remains the treatment of choice. Endoscopic treatments have become established as the first-line approach for pyriform sinus tract anomalies due to lower morbidity. Branchio-oto-renal syndrome should be considered in patients with ear malformations, hearing impairment, or renal abnormalities.

articles.title: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis after Measles Outbreaks, the Philippines, 2007-2022.
articles.abstract: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a delayed, almost uniformly fatal complication of measles. The Philippines had measles outbreaks in 2010-2011, 2013, and 2018-2019; the last was the largest in the World Health Organization Western Pacific Region. Published SSPE data from the Philippines end in 2015. We reviewed all 20 children admitted with SSPE to a tertiary pediatric hospital in Quezon City during 2007-2022 and estimated year of measles infection. Median patient age was 6.2 years at hospital admission and 0.7 years at reported measles illness. Five (25.0%) of 20 admissions occurred in 2022, and estimated infection dates placed 4 patients within the 2018-2019 outbreak; all were admitted during 2020-2022. Given the multiyear latency of SSPE, additional cases might emerge over coming years. Reported measles history could not be established in one quarter of patients. Strengthened measles surveillance and sustained 2-dose vaccination coverage are needed.

articles.title: Comprehensive cardiac, vascular and pulmonary characterization of a cardiometabolic model of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which translational progress is limited by experimental models that insufficiently reflect the cardiometabolic phenotype while affecting endogenous endothelial function. We aimed to characterize a cardiometabolic 'two-hit' HFpEF model combining metabolic stress (db/db) with chronic mineralocorticoid excess (d-aldosterone). Female db/db mice received 4-week d-aldosterone (0.3 μg/h) or vehicle via osmotic minipumps. Metabolic profiling, high-resolution echocardiography including strain and left atrial mechanics, invasive right-heart catheterization and thoracic aortic wire myography were performed. Aldosterone-treated db/db mice developed cardiac hypertrophy and pulmonary congestion with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction but marked diastolic dysfunction, left atrial remodeling with increased stiffness and impaired global longitudinal left ventricular strain. Pulmonary hypertension with right ventricular dysfunction was evidenced by elevated right ventricular systolic pressure, reduced ratio of pulmonary acceleration time to pulmonary ejection time, and reduced tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Thoracic aortae from untreated db/db mice already showed impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation, which was further aggravated by aldosterone, whereas maximal endothelium-independent relaxation remained largely preserved. The db/db+d-aldosterone model recapitulates key features of cardiometabolic HFpEF across the cardiac-vascular-pulmonary axis and provides a translational platform for mechanistic and therapeutic studies targeting endothelial and ventricular-vascular dysfunction in HFpEF.

articles.title: National trends and disparities in coronary artery disease and depression-related mortality in the United States, 1999-2025: A population-based CDC WONDER analysis.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) and depressive disorders frequently coexist, but national mortality patterns involving both conditions remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate temporal trends and demographic and geographic disparities in mortality involving CAD and depressive or depressive-anxiety disorders in the United States from 1999 to 2025.

METHODS: We analyzed U.S. residents aged ≥25 years using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database. Deaths were included when CAD (ICD-10 I20-I25) and a depressive or depressive-anxiety disorder (F32, F33, or F41.2) were both recorded on the same death certificate, irrespective of underlying or contributing cause. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were standardized to the 2000 U.S. population, and temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Data were extracted April 10, 2026; 2025 mortality data were provisional. Urbanization analyses were limited to 1999-2020.

RESULTS: Among 85,806 deaths, the mean annual AAMR was 1.42 per 100,000 population. AAMR declined from 1.81 (95% CI, 1.75-1.87) in 1999 to 1.31 (95% CI, 1.26-1.35) in 2025 (AAPC, -1.38%; 95% CI, -2.24 to -0.50; p = 0.002), despite an increase during 2017-2020. Mean annual AAMRs were higher among males than females (1.52 vs 1.33), White individuals (1.59), the Midwest (1.91), and nonmetropolitan versus metropolitan areas during 1999-2020 (1.94 vs 1.33). Mortality increased among adults aged 35-44 and 55-64 years and among Black individuals from 2014 to 2025.

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality involving both conditions declined overall but varied substantially across demographic and geographic subgroups, with increases in some younger and middle-aged populations.

articles.title: Dynamic change in soluble suppressor of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) during acute decompensated heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction, and its mortality implications.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) concentrations measured at clinician-determined decompensation and recompensation, and their change between these states, with one-year mortality in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF).

METHODS: Paired sST2 samples were obtained at decompensation and recompensation from 168 patients hospitalized with ADHF and a left ventricular ejection fraction of <50%. Associations with one-year all-cause mortality were assessed using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, with exploratory cut-offs derived using Youden's index.

RESULTS: The median age was 71.5 years (IQR 62-80.8), 39 (23.2%) were women, median LVEF was 26% (IQR 17.5-32.5), and 158 (94.1%) had NYHA class III or IV symptoms. During one-year follow-up, 34 patients (20.2%) died. Each doubling of decompensation sST2 was associated with higher mortality after adjustment for creatinine (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.23-2.25). Recompensation sST2 remained associated with mortality after adjustment for creatinine and NT-proBNP (HR per doubling 1.71, 95% CI 1.18-2.48). The respective areas under the curve were 0.686 and 0.688, with exploratory cut-offs of 66.5 and 57 ng/mL. Unchanged or increased sST2 was associated with higher mortality than decreased sST2 in unadjusted analysis (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.37-5.59, p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: Elevated sST2 at decompensation and unchanged or increased concentrations during recompensation were associated with one-year mortality in patients with ADHF. These findings support further evaluation of sST2 as an adjunctive prognostic biomarker in this setting; the cohort-derived cut-offs require validation.

articles.title: Epimeric Vitamin D is Not Associated With Arterial Stiffness or Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Advanced CKD.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: 3-epi-25(OH)D3, an epimeric form of 25(OH)D3 generated by C-3 epimerization, declines with advancing chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its role in vascular health and related outcomes remains largely unknown. We aimed to determine whether circulating 3-epi-25(OH)D3 levels are associated with arterial stiffness and longitudinal cardiovascular (CV) outcomes in advanced CKD (stages 5 and 5D).

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective observational study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: A total of 270 patients with advanced CKD using the Cambridge Coventry Vascular cohort.

EXPOSURE S OR PREDICTOR S: Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D3 measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.

OUTCOME S: Arterial stiffness was assessed by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (AIx75). Longitudinal outcomes included a composite of major CV events and all-cause mortality.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D3 was categorized into quartiles. Associations were assessed using multivariable regression adjusted for age, race, and dialysis status. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed longitudinal outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 270 participants, quartiles were Q1 < 0.30 ng/mL (n = 64), Q2: 0.30-0.456 ng/mL (n = 71), Q3: 0.457-0.729 ng/mL (n = 68), and Q4 ≥ 0.73 ng/mL (n = 67). Strata were similar in age (44.9 years), sex, and BMI (all P > 0.05). Race differed by quartile (P < 0.001); 87.4% were White. 24.8% were pre-dialytic, 61.1% treated with hemodialysis, and 14.1% treated with peritoneal dialysis. Arterial stiffness was similar across quartiles (AIx75 ∼20-21%, P = 0.99; PWV: 7.8-8.0 m/s, P = 0.94). 3-epi-25(OH)D3 showed no association with AIx75 or PWV before or after adjustment using multiple regression modeling. Over 9.3 years, 115 composite events occurred (97 CV events, 18 deaths). Kaplan-Meier analysis did not discriminate risk across 3-epi-25(OH)D3 quartiles for the composite outcome (log-rank P = 0.23), and adjusted Cox models showed no association.

LIMITATIONS: Observational design with possible residual confounding.

CONCLUSION: In advanced CKD, 3-epi-25(OH)D3 showed no independent association with arterial stiffness or CV events and mortality. Further studies are needed to determine the role of epimeric vitamin D in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Functional disability, diabetes and hypertension among adults in the United States, August 2021-August 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe diabetes and hypertension prevalence, diagnosis status and measured-threshold outcomes by functional disability.

METHODS: We analyzed the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted in the United States during August 2021-August 2023. Adults aged 18 years or older were classified using six Washington Group functioning domains. Outcome-specific weights and direct age standardization were used. Disability-minus-no-disability differences and 95% confidence intervals accounted for the complex survey design.

RESULTS: Among 8101 adults with complete functioning data, total diabetes and hypertension were classifiable in 5974 and 6172. Standardized total-disease differences were 9.3 percentage points (5.8, 12.7) for diabetes and 8.3 (3.1, 13.6) for hypertension. Undiagnosed-disease differences among eligible adults were 0.6 (-0.4, 1.7) and -3.4 (-7.2, 0.5), respectively. Among hypertension cases with known diagnosis status, the undiagnosed fraction was lower with disability: -14.1 (-19.9, -8.3). Conditional diabetes estimates were imprecise and sensitive to sparse younger-age cells.

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with functional disability had higher standardized total diabetes and hypertension prevalence. Diagnosis-status and measured-threshold findings depended on the condition and denominator; they do not establish equivalent care or explain the origins of prevalence differences.

articles.title: Myosin inhibitor therapy in Fabry cardiomyopathy with dynamic left ventricular outflow obstruction.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract: A 56-year-old woman with presumed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was diagnosed with Fabry disease (GLA: p.Glu358del) and a concomitant PLN variant. Imaging revealed advanced Fabry cardiomyopathy with dynamic LVOT obstruction. Despite optimized medical and enzyme replacement therapy, symptoms progressed (NYHA-class III) with a marked increase in LVOT gradient. Mavacamten was initiated and uptitrated under echocardiographic monitoring. At three months, LVOT gradient significantly decreased and functional status improved (NYHA-class I), while systolic function remained preserved. This case highlights the importance of detailed phenotyping and suggests that myosin inhibition may represent a therapeutic option for LVOT obstruction beyond classical sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: The German National Cohort: Ophthalmic Assessment, Baseline Profile, and Potential for Artificial Intelligence-Based Eye Research.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the ophthalmic examination protocol within the German National Cohort (NAKO)/NAKO Gesundheitsstudie, to report the baseline profile of participants undergoing ophthalmic assessment, and to illustrate the potential as a population-based resource for artificial intelligence (AI) research in eye health.

DESIGN: Baseline analysis of ophthalmic data within the nationwide, population-based multicenter prospective NAKO study.

PARTICIPANTS: Forty-eight thousand four hundred and sixty adults in the ophthalmic level 2 module of 205 053 adults enrolled in NAKO, aged 19-74 years, with a mean age 48.9 ± 12.5 years, and 52.7% were male.

METHODS: All participants underwent standardized biomedical examinations and detailed questionnaire-based data collection, including nondilated color fundus imaging, visual acuity testing, and a brief ocular history. Ocular health was summarized using descriptive statistics. Fundus image quality and morphological features (e.g., cup-to-disc ratio and arteriolar-to-venular ratio) were assessed using open-source deep learning models. Standard deep learning architectures were trained on the fundus images to predict age, sex, and blood pressure.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Percentage of fundus images graded as good quality; mean absolute error (MAE) for age and blood pressure prediction; accuracy for sex prediction.

RESULTS: The analysis includes 48 460 participants who completed the ophthalmic baseline examination of NAKO. Mean visual acuity (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution) was 0.01 ± 0.20 (left eye, mean ± standard deviation) and 0.03 ± 0.21 (right eye). Self-reported ocular disease prevalence was 4.2% for cataract, 2.0% for glaucoma, and 0.9% for macular degeneration; 68.2% of fundus images were classified as gradable using 4 deep learning-based quality grading models. Morphological features showed systematic differences across age groups. Standard deep learning architectures showed comparative performance to the state-of-the-art for age, sex, and blood pressure prediction (2.96 MAE for age prediction, 0.84 accuracy for sex prediction, and 10.78 and 6.97 MAE for systolic and diastolic blood pressure prediction).

CONCLUSIONS: The German National Cohort provides a large-scale, nationwide population-based resource with visual acuity measurements and systemic health indicators, as well as color fundus images in about 50 000 NAKO participants. These data lay the groundwork for studying eye health in the general adult population in Germany and can serve as a strong foundation for developing and validating AI tools in eye health research.

FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.
