articles.title: Predicting the Risk of Unplanned Hospital Encounters in Hemodialysis Patients: A Comparison Between Clinicians and a Machine Learning Prediction Algorithm.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Dialysis patients have a higher risk of hospitalization than the age-matched general population. Unplanned hospital encounters (UHEs), including emergency department visits and hospitalizations, may be preventable but are difficult to anticipate. We aimed to stratify dialysis patients' risk of UHE, using a machine learning (ML)-based prediction model.

STUDY DESIGN: We created an ML-based prediction model to stratify hemodialysis (HD) patients' risk of UHE in the subsequent 7 and 30 days. We compared the performance of this prediction model with that of clinicians.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 627 patients who received maintenance HD at an academic hospital from October 2015 to April 2022 for model development and 285 patients for a comparison with clinician predictions.

PREDICTORS: Demographic and clinical data as well as data derived from the dialysis treatment sessions, updated weekly.

OUTCOMES ANALYTICAL APPROACH & RESULTS: Clinicians demonstrated a higher positive predictive value (PPV) for a UHE in the subsequent 7 days (0.14 for clinicians vs 0.07 for the ML model; P < 0.001) but lower sensitivity (0.25 for clinicians vs 0.63 for the ML model; P < 0.001). The PPV for the 30-day UHE was comparable between clinicians and the model (0.25 for clinicians vs 0.21 for the ML model; P = 0.54), but sensitivity was nearly three-fold higher for our ML model relative to clinicians (0.24 for clinicians vs 0.73 for the ML model; P < 0.001).

LIMITATIONS: Our ML-based prediction model was only developed within a cohort comprising HD recipients at a single center, limiting external validation.

CONCLUSIONS: Using ML, we were able to anticipate UHE with greater sensitivity than clinician predictions with comparable PPV. Further research will determine if integration of our prediction tool into clinical care will lead to fewer UHEs.

articles.title: Proteomic markers associated with blood pressure, hypertension, and treatment-resistant hypertension.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to investigate associations between 92 proteins and blood pressure (BP), prevalent hypertension (HT) and apparent treatment-resistant HT (aTRH) in a population-derived sub cohort.

METHODS: Excluding subjects with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (n = 189), linear regression models assessed associations between proteins and systolic BP. Proteins showing significant associations (false discovery rate 5%) with systolic BP were analysed adjusting for clinically relevant covariates. Associated proteins were further analysed for associations with diastolic BP, prevalent HT, and aTRH, in multivariable regression models.

RESULTS: Complete data was available in 1527 individuals (mean age 67.1 ± 6.0 years; 30.5% women). Interleukin-1 receptor type 2 (IL1R2) associated with systolic BP (β 2.79, p 0.008), diastolic BP (β 1.78, p < 0.001), HT (odds ratio (OR), 1.34 [95% CI, 1.01-1.78]) and aTRH (OR, 1.94 [1.11-3.39]) while chitinase-3-like-protein 1 (CHI3L1) associated with systolic BP (β 1.53, p 0.004) and prevalent HT (OR 1.20, [1.04-1.38]). Pathway analysis suggested "metabolism of angiotensinogen to angiotensins", "neutrophil degranulation" and "peptide hormone metabolism" as significantly enriched, in relation to blood pressure.

CONCLUSIONS: Among 1527 individuals without established ASCVD, IL1R2 was associated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure, as well as with both HT and aTRH, while CHI3L1 associated with systolic blood pressure and prevalent HT. These findings may offer novel insights and inspire future research on HT and inflammation.

articles.title: Rethinking Guideline Delivery in Nephrology: From Access to Action.
Post-Discharge Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Arthroplasty and Spine Surgery: A Narrative Review of Evidence, Harms, and a Stewardship Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implant-based orthopaedic procedures, such as total hip and knee arthroplasty and instrumented spinal fusion, are vulnerable to postoperative infection because implants facilitate microbial adherence and biofilm formation, and infections carry substantial morbidity, revision burden, and cost. Although major guidance emphasizes time-limited perioperative prophylaxis, some clinicians extend antibiotics after discharge, most commonly as extended oral antibiotic prophylaxis, particularly in patients perceived to be high risk.

MAIN BODY: We performed a structured, search-informed narrative synthesis of English-language evidence published from January 2015 through January 2026 and summarized major guideline and consensus positions to characterize procedure-specific prescribing patterns, comparative outcomes, and stewardship-relevant trade-offs. In total joint arthroplasty, supportive findings largely derive from retrospective cohorts in selected high-risk populations, but definitions of high risk, antibiotic regimens, and follow-up windows vary substantially, and conflicting observational studies and matched analyses limit certainty and generalizability. In instrumented spine surgery, post-discharge prescribing variation is well documented, yet comparative evidence generally does not demonstrate a consistent reduction in surgical site infection with prolonged postoperative or post-discharge prophylaxis. Across procedures, extended antibiotic exposure plausibly increases patient-centered harms, including gastrointestinal intolerance, drug reactions, acute kidney injury, and Clostridioides difficile infection, while population-level concerns include resistance selection and inefficient resource use when baseline infection risk is low.

CONCLUSION: A stewardship-aligned approach should prioritize standard short-course prophylaxis for most clean elective cases and reserve post-discharge prophylaxis for narrowly defined very-high-risk subgroups within protocolized governance, explicit stop dates, early reassessment, and adverse-event monitoring. Key research priorities include standardized risk definitions, rigorous outcome adjudication, and scalable pragmatic or registry-randomized designs.

articles.title: Integrating Proteomics and Mendelian Randomization to Evaluate HGF as a Potential Mediator of Stroke Risk Factors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Stroke prediction remains suboptimal. We aimed to identify plasma proteins associated with stroke risk and evaluate their potential as clinical biomarkers and causal mediators.

EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We used a multitiered proteomic approach in the UK Biobank (UKB). In a matched nested case-control study (672 cases, 2,688 controls), 2,920 proteins were analyzed. Findings were internally validated in the UKB-PPP cohort and cross-validated using genetic instruments from seven large-scale protein GWAS meta-analyses. Mendelian randomization (MR) and mediation analyses were employed to assess causality.

RESULTS: We identified 122 proteins significantly associated with stroke risk. A 122-protein panel improved the C-index from 0.610 to 0.693. MR analysis provided genetic evidence supporting an association between higher genetically predicted Hepatocyte Growth Factor (HGF) levels and stroke risk (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.09-1.28). Mediation analysis indicated that HGF mediated 39.15% of the effect of weight and 37.28% of waist circumference on stroke risk.

CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Our findings support HGF as a potential mediator linking metabolic risk factors to stroke. The identified protein panel offers a robust tool for stroke risk stratification and highlights HGF as a biologically plausible candidate for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Caring for a patient with Fournier gangrene.
articles.abstract: Fournier gangrene (FG) is a form of necrotizing fasciitis that affects the genital and perineal tissues. This life-threatening condition is most often caused by a polymicrobial bacterial infection of the tissues. Predisposing factors include obesity, advanced age, chronic alcohol abuse, and immunosuppression. Although rare, FG can be life-threatening and can significantly impact the patient's quality of life. Adept nursing care can improve patient outcomes. This article discusses the pathophysiology and common complications of FG and outlines expected nursing considerations for patients with this type of infection.

articles.title: A Phase 1 Study of MK-1942, a Negative Allosteric Modulator of mGluR2, in Healthy Japanese to Flexibly Assess Factors Including CYP2C19 Phenotype.
articles.abstract: MK-1942 is a negative allosteric modulator of the metabotropic glutamate receptor 2 that was investigated for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and depression. Nonclinical studies with recombinant human CYPs and genotyped human hepatocytes suggested that CYP2C19 is involved in the metabolism of MK-1942. Given the high incidence of different CYP2C19 polymorphisms in the Japanese population, a Phase 1 single and multiple dose study in healthy Japanese participants provided an opportunity to determine the involvement of CYP2C19 phenotype on the clinical PK of MK-1942. Also, since a first-in-human study in non-Japanese showed a decrease in exposures after administration with high-fat meal, we further tested an effect of low-fat meal on PK in the Japan study. The study was designed with flexibility which enabled dose selection for the multiple dose panels, based on the totality of safety and PK data. Oral administration of single and multiple doses of MK-1942 in Japanese participants was generally well tolerated. AUC0-inf was comparable between fasted and fed (low-fat meal) state. Following a single dose of MK-1942, AUC0-inf was ~70% increased in CYP2C19 poor metabolizer (PM) vs. extensive metabolizer (EM). Therefore, a decision was made to test the multiple dose separately for each CYP2C19 phenotype, rather than grouping them into a single panel. As opposed to the expectation from the single dose result, steady state exposures were similar among CYP2C19 phenotypes. These data supported the subsequent global Phase 2 study to permit a low-fat meal around dosing and no dose adjustment for any CYP2C19 phenotype.

articles.title: Evaluating Darbepoetin Treatment Strategies for Managing Anaemia in Haemodialysis Patients: Effects on All-Cause Mortality From a Target Trial Emulation Using Electronic Health Record Data.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Anaemia is a common complication of chronic kidney disease, often treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs), but the optimal haemoglobin (Hb) target remains uncertain. Using electronic health records, we emulated a target trial comparing different Hb targets in haemodialysis patients to estimate their effects on mortality.

METHODS: We used electronic health records from UK kidney centres reporting to the UK Renal Registry. Adults aged ≥ 18 years, receiving haemodialysis for ≥ 3 months, and without marked ESA resistance were eligible. Using the clone-censor-weight method, we emulated trials comparing Hb targets: (1) 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L and (2) 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L. Darbepoetin dosing followed a standardised protocol with predefined dose adjustments and a maximum dose of 150 μg/week. The outcome was all-cause mortality over 8 months.

RESULTS: The study included 8628 patients from 10 centres between 2004 and 2016; 62% male, median age 66 years (IQR 52-76). At baseline, mean Hb was 97.7 g/L (SD 15.1), and 79% of patients were receiving darbepoetin. The hazard ratio for mortality was 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.12) for the 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L comparison, and 1.20 (95% CI 0.94-1.54) for the 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L comparison. Adherence to the highest Hb target was lower, limiting precision.

CONCLUSIONS: Targeting an Hb range of 105-125 g/L under controlled ESA dosing was not associated with increased mortality compared with 95-115 g/L. Targeting Hb levels above 125 g/L may increase mortality risk, consistent with previous trial findings.

articles.title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Efficacy Study of Porcine and Rabbit Antithymocyte Globulin in the Treatment of Patients With Severe Aplastic Anemia: A Multicenter, Prospective, Randomized, Open-Label Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a T lymphocyte-mediated bone marrow failure disorder. Only porcine ATG (p-ATG) and rabbit ATG (r-ATG) are available in mainland China, with the optimal first-line regimen undetermined. This study compared their pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Ninety-three SAA patients ineligible for transplantation or lacking a suitable donor (p-ATG, n = 55; r-ATG, n = 38) who were receiving immunosuppressive therapy were prospectively enrolled between 2020 and 2024. The primary endpoint was dynamic changes in lymphocyte subsets. Both ATGs peaked on treatment Day 5; r-ATG cleared significantly faster, with comparable peak active concentrations. The p-ATG group showed a stable early neutrophil increase, whereas the r-ATG group had an initial decline, with comparable recovery at 1 month. The r-ATG group exhibited prolonger lymphopenia, lower CD3+/CD4+ T cells, reduced Treg cells, and higher CD19+ B-cell proportions. IL-10 was significantly elevated on day 2 after ATG administration. At 6 months, the CRR was 18.87% with p-ATG and 18.92% with r-ATG; ORR was 69.81% with p-ATG and 56.76% with r-ATG. Two-year ORR and overall survival were similar, with no significant differences in infection or serum sickness. P-ATG and r-ATG have distinct pharmacokinetic and immunomodulatory but comparable efficacy and safety profiles, supporting interchangeable use in clinical practice.

articles.title: Endothelium-targeted and untargeted nanoparticle therapies in thromboinflammatory vascular diseases.
articles.abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) line the vasculature and integrate hemodynamic, inflammatory, and metabolic cues that are crucial in maintaining vascular health. Endothelial dysfunction is a driver of thromboinflammatory conditions including atherosclerosis, thrombosis, stroke, and sepsis-induced multiorgan dysfunction syndrome. Therapies for these conditions that are given systemically fail to target the site of disease and can be associated with off-target side effects. EC-targeted nanoparticles represent a novel method of concentrating the drug- or gene-based therapy in ECs at the site of disease. Here, we describe studies of EC-directed nanoparticles in thromboinflammatory vascular diseases. We discuss challenges in the development of EC-targeted nanoparticle therapies, including issues with biosafety, delivery efficiency, scalability, and clinical translation. To target ECs, nanoparticle surfaces have been coated with ligand-directed antibodies or peptides against EC markers. EC targeting has also been achieved by coating nanoparticles with cell-mimicking membranes to leverage native homing pathways to sites of vascular injury. Stimuli-responsive nanoparticles have used EC or disease-specific cues to trigger drug release, for instance via reactive oxygen species or shear stress stimuli. EC-targeted nanoparticles extend the therapy circulation time, enhance drug accumulation at target sites, improve therapeutic efficacy, and reduce toxicity. In preclinical studies, EC-targeted nanoparticles have stabilized atherosclerotic plaques, degraded venous thrombi, and reduced cerebral infarct volume. Although EC-targeted nanoparticle therapies have not yet been approved for clinical use, advances in the design and safety of nanoparticles are narrowing the gap between experimental promise and clinical reality.

articles.title: Life Participation in Parents of Children With CKD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The caregiver burden among parents of children with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is high and can impair their life participation, which may in turn have negative consequences on their children's care and outcomes. We aim to describe effects on life participation in parents of children with CKD, from the perspectives of their children, health professionals, and the parents themselves.

METHODS: We thematically analyzed data from the Standardized Outcomes in Nephrology-Children and Adolescents Initiative (SONG-Kids) life participation workshops involving children with childhood CKD, parents or caregivers, and health professionals, for content related to perspectives on life participation among parents of children with CKD.

RESULTS: A total of 4 international consensus workshops were conducted (1 in-person in English and 3 online-2 in English and 1 in Spanish) with 171 participants, including 79 patients and parents or caregivers and 92 health professionals from 16 countries. Overall, 4 themes were identified-health priorities undermining ability to participate in activities and socialize; medical responsibilities conflicting with the nurturing parental role; impeding ability to work; and measuring and addressing life participation in parents of children with CKD.

CONCLUSION: Managing parental and disease-related responsibilities can impair life participation in parents of children with CKD, particularly in the areas of work and social activities. Strategies to identify and address parental life participation appear to be needed, which may include interventions to alleviate caregiver burden and distress.

articles.title: ICD-Coded Versus Undiagnosed Acute Kidney Injury in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common among older adults and associated with adverse outcomes, yet it often goes undiagnosed. We aimed to compare the prevalence of undiagnosed versus International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-coded AKI as well as their clinical and molecular characteristics and evaluate their associations with clinical outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: A total of 5,692 adults with proteomic and metabolomic profiling from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study, excluding individuals with end-stage kidney disease at baseline (2011-2013).

EXPOSURES: AKI, defined as either ICD-coded or undiagnosed based on 3 abstracted levels of serum creatinine measured during hospitalizations.

OUTCOMES: Incident coronary heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and all-cause mortality.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: ICD-coded AKI was compared with undiagnosed AKI across all hospitalizations. Risk factors for ICD-coded and undiagnosed AKI were assessed separately using Cox proportional hazards models from study visit to the first AKI encounter. Time-varying Cox models were used to evaluate the associations of ICD-coded and undiagnosed AKI with adverse outcomes.

RESULTS: ICD codes identified 51.4% of AKI defined based on changes in serum creatinine, with higher sensitivity for more severe stages and a specificity of 87.0%. Undiagnosed AKI was more common in women; otherwise, clinical risk factors for undiagnosed AKI were similar to those for ICD-coded AKI, as were proteomic and metabolomic risk factors. Both AKI groups were strongly associated with coronary heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and mortality.

LIMITATIONS: AKI was estimated using 3 values of serum creatinine only and not urinary output. Diagnosed AKI was identified using billing codes, which may underestimate clinical diagnosis of AKI.

CONCLUSIONS: Undiagnosed AKI is prevalent, especially among women, and is biologically and prognostically similar to ICD-coded AKI, motivating efforts to improve AKI recognition and diagnosis.

articles.title: Health system readiness for out-of-hospital-cardiac-arrest management in resource limited settings: A mixed-method study from rural and suburban Sindh, Pakistan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-hospital-cardiac-arrest requires a robust emergency response system for survival. In low-resource settings like suburban and rural Sindh in Pakistan, little is known about the readiness of healthcare systems and communities.

AIM: The aim of this study was to comprehensively assess the system-readiness for out-of-hospital-cardiac-arrest management in rural and suburban areas of Sindh, Pakistan by studying out-of-hospital and in-hospital elements of chain of survival in these areas.

METHODS: A triangulation mixed-methods design was used. The study was conducted in seven hospitals in the suburban and rural areas of upper, central and southern parts of the province of Sindh, Pakistan. Quantitative data from exit interviews (n = 163) using the Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire-18 and a facility readiness checklist (n = 7 hospitals) were analysed using descriptive statistics. Qualitative data were collected through focus group discussions with community members and ambulance crew, in-depth interviews with emergency room doctors and nurses, and key informant interviews with emergency room supervisors and cardiologists and were analysed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Exit interviews with 163 patients showed that the lowest proportions satisfied were for communication (26.4%), financial aspects (31.3%), accessibility and convenience (32.5%), technical quality of emergency room staff (40.5%), and time spent with doctors (47.2%). Among the seven facilities assessed, defibrillators were available in two, but neither was functional; epinephrine was available in four, pulse oximeters in three, and endotracheal tubes in three, while laryngeal mask airways were unavailable in all facilities. Qualitative data from 12 focus group discussions, 15 in-depth interviews, and three key informant interviews identified limited recognition of cardiac arrest, inadequate ambulance availability, poor road access, shortages of trained staff and resuscitation equipment, sociocultural and gender-related barriers, and weaknesses in emergency care governance and data systems.

CONCLUSION: Triangulation of quantitative and qualitative findings showed that the Chain of Survival in rural and suburban Sindh is weak at several points, including the community, prehospital care, health facilities, and governance.The study shows that there is a need to strengthen the system at multiple levels. This includes training community members, ambulance crew and emergency room staff in cardiopulmonary resuscitation, setting minimum standards for resuscitation readiness, and creating out-of-hospital-cardiac-arrest registries.

articles.title: Selective mGlu1 Receptor Activation Restores Cortical Inhibitory Tone and Improves Cognitive Performance in a Subchronic Phencyclidine NMDA Hypofunction Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deficits in prefrontal cortex (PFC) inhibitory transmission are thought to underlie the cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia that remain untreated by current pharmacotherapies. The metabotropic glutamate 1 (mGlu1) receptor, a subtype of the mGlu receptor family, is a promising therapeutic target because its activation enhances inhibitory transmission in the PFC through the excitation of somatostatin-expressing GABAergic (gamma-aminobutyric acidergic) interneurons (SST-INs).

METHODS: We used a subchronic phencyclidine (PCP) NMDA receptor antagonist mouse model, mGlu1 positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), and mice with selective deletion of mGlu1 receptors from SST-INs to examine the cell type-specific role of mGlu1 signaling in cortical inhibition and cognition. We used ex vivo whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology to assess inhibitory transmission in the PFC, and cognitive performance was evaluated using tests of working memory and novel object recognition.

RESULTS: Subchronic PCP treatment impaired inhibitory synaptic transmission in the PFC, particularly onto layer V pyramidal neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens. Pharmacological activation of mGlu1 restored inhibitory drive and reversed PCP-induced deficits in working memory and novel object recognition. Importantly, selective deletion of mGlu1 receptors from SST-INs abolished the ability of mGlu1 activation to restore cortical inhibition and cognitive function, demonstrating that these receptors are required for the therapeutic effects of mGlu1 PAMs.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify SST-IN-expressed mGlu1 receptors as critical regulators of prefrontal cortical inhibition and cognition. Positive allosteric modulation of mGlu1 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for treating cognitive deficits associated with schizophrenia by restoring inhibitory circuit function.

articles.title: Ticagrelor versus prasugrel following PCI in acute coronary syndromes and high-risk coronary artery disease: A meta-analysis of one-year randomized trial outcomes.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend potent P2Y12 inhibitors over clopidogrel following percutaneous coronary intervention. Whether ticagrelor- or prasugrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) provides superior clinical outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain, particularly across acute coronary syndromes (ACS) and high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) populations.

METHODS: We searched databases for randomized controlled trials comparing ticagrelor- and prasugrel-based DAPT in patients with CAD undergoing PCI with 1-year follow-up. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, stent thrombosis, and major bleeding. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses were performed in ACS populations.

RESULTS: Three trials randomized a total of 7048 patients. In the primary analysis, prasugrel-based therapy was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in MACE compared with ticagrelor-based therapy (HR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.67-1.03; p = 0.09). All-cause mortality (HR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.68-1.08; p = 0.20), cardiovascular death (HR = 0.93; 95% CI: 0.72-1.21; p = 0.60), myocardial infarction (HR = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.56-1.14; p = 0.22), stroke (HR = 1.04; 95% CI: 0.63-1.73; p = 0.87), stent thrombosis (HR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.45-1.11; p = 0.13), and major bleeding (HR = 0.89; 95% CI: 0.68-1.17; p = 0.41) were comparable between strategies. ACS-restricted sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent findings across all outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ACS and high-risk CAD undergoing PCI, current randomized evidence does not establish conclusive superiority between ticagrelor- and prasugrel-based DAPT for 1-year ischemic or bleeding endpoints.

articles.title: Beyond thrombosis: a scoping review of patient-reported outcomes in antiphospholipid syndrome.
articles.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by thrombosis and pregnancy morbidity, with heterogeneous nonthrombotic manifestations that may substantially affect daily functioning and well-being. Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) offer a direct assessment of symptom burden and quality of life but remain underutilized in APS. We performed a scoping review of PubMed from inception through July 2025 using terms related to APS and PROs (quality of life, fatigue, pain, depression, psychological well-being, and health surveys). We included eligible English-language studies that reported PROs in APS. Both qualitative and quantitative studies were included. Twelve cohort studies evaluated PROs in APS. Most studies used legacy instruments such as the 36-item short form health survey. A few recent studies have used patient-reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) tools. Across studies, patients with APS reported impairments in multiple domains of health-related quality of life (HRQOL) as well as overall HRQOL compared with population norms, which are associated with comorbid systemic lupus erythematosus (secondary APS), a history of thrombosis, and greater end-organ damage. Anticoagulation monitoring and international normalized ratio lability contributed to treatment dissatisfaction and reduced HRQOL. Major gaps include the longitudinal assessment of PROs and their temporal relation to clinical events and the evaluation of PROs in obstetric APS and children and older adults with APS. No APS-specific PRO instruments have been developed. There is a need to either develop APS-specific instruments or validate generic instruments such as PROMIS measures in large representative APS cohorts. Incorporating PROs into clinical practice and research can enhance clinical care and facilitate patient-centered, personalized management of APS.

articles.title: Indications and outcomes of ventricular assist devices in children and young adults with neuromuscular diseases: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) are frequently complicated by progressive cardiomyopathy leading to advanced heart failure. Ventricular assist device (VAD) implantation has emerged as a potential option in selected pediatric and young adult patients, but evidence on indications and outcomes is limited. We aimed to systematically review evidence on VAD implantation in children and young adults with NMDs, focusing on device strategies and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Systematic review following Cochrane methodology and reported per the PRISMA guidelines. Six major biomedical databases were searched from inception to October 1, 2025. Studies including patients aged ≤25 years with NMDs undergoing VAD implantation were eligible. The primary outcome was clinical status at last reported follow-up, classified as alive on device support, alive after heart transplantation (HT), or deceased.

RESULTS: Six retrospective studies comprising 37 patients were included. Duchenne muscular dystrophy was the most common diagnosis (48.6%). Destination therapy was the most frequently reported strategy (45.9%), followed by bridge-to-transplant (37.8%) and bridge-to-decision (16.2%). At last follow-up, 75.7% were alive: 43.2% on device support and 32.4% after undergoing HT; 24.3% had died. Complications were common, most frequently bleeding and infection, whereas neurologic events were the leading cause of death. Reporting of functional outcomes and quality of life was sparse and heterogeneous.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on VAD use in this population is limited to small retrospective cohorts. Although most patients were alive at last reported follow-up, morbidity remains substantial and patient-centered outcomes are poorly characterized. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized outcome definitions are needed.

articles.title: Clinical significance of elevated body temperature without infection following removal of VA-ECMO.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have reported elevated body temperature following the removal of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). However, the clinical implications of elevated body temperature after the removal of VA-ECMO remain unknown.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize elevated body temperature after VA-ECMO removal in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS).

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 163 CS patients undergoing VA-ECMO removal. All patients did not exhibit any evidence of infection. Blood temperature was continuously monitored using a Swan-Ganz catheter. Elevated body temperature was defined as a maximum body temperature ≥38.0 °C within 24 h after VA-ECMO removal. All-cause mortality was compared between patients with and without elevated body temperature.

RESULTS: Elevated body temperature was observed in 58.9% (96/163) of study subjects. Patients with elevated body temperature had higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (11.1 ± 8.6 vs. 8.5 ± 6.1 mg/dL, p = 0.027), accompanied by reductions in systolic blood pressure and systemic vascular resistance, and increased lactate levels. CRP levels independently predicted elevated body temperature (OR=1.050, 95%CI=1.003-1.100, p = 0.037). All-cause mortality did not differ between the two groups (30.2%vs. 29.9%, log-rank p = 0.983). However, among patients with elevated body temperature, an increase in body temperature, especially ≥1.1 °C, was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR=1.968, 95%CI=1.096-3.535, p = 0.023).

CONCLUSIONS: In CS patients requiring VA-ECMO, body temperature elevated in 58.9% patients after the removal of VA-ECMO. In those with elevated body temperature, a greater rise in body temperature was associated with higher mortality, suggesting body temperature as a potential signature to stratify risks of mortality in CS patients without any infectious signs.

articles.title: Massive Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in an Adolescent Patient: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding in pediatric patients arises from diverse etiologies that vary across age groups. Although it is an uncommon cause of life-threatening hemorrhagic shock, prompt recognition and management are essential. Owing to the infrequency of hemorrhagic shock from GI bleeding in pediatrics, emergency physicians may lack familiarity with its diagnosis and management. Furthermore, multiple etiologies may coexist and may not be detected during the initial esophagogastroduodenoscopy, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure.

CASE REPORT: A 17-year-old boy with a history of plaque psoriasis was transported by ambulance to the pediatric emergency department of an urban level one trauma center, presenting with copious hematemesis and hemodynamic instability. Initial resuscitation in the emergency department included blood transfusion, followed by admission to the pediatric intensive care unit. The first endoscopic evaluation by pediatric gastroenterology identified duodenal erosion; however, the patient experienced further large-volume bleeding out of proportion to these findings. A subsequent endoscopy revealed a Dieulafoy lesion, which was treated successfully. The patient was ultimately discharged home and has remained stable during long-term follow-up. WHY SHOULD AN EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN BE AWARE OF THIS?: Although severe GI bleeding in pediatric patients is uncommon, emergency physicians must quickly identify hemorrhagic shock across all age groups and be familiar with the broad differential diagnoses that vary by age. Initial management must prioritize airway protection and hemodynamic stabilization as a bridge to definitive intervention. Clinicians should recognize the limitations of endoscopic gastroduodenoscopy and consider the potential for concurrent sources of bleeding that may necessitate additional intervention. © 2025 Elsevier Inc. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, artificial intelligence training, and similar technologies.

articles.title: Comparative effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on cognitive domains in children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to compare the effects of non-pharmacological intervention categories on attention, working memory, comprehensive executive function, and social-emotional cognition in children with autism spectrum disorder. Five databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 2005-12 April 2026. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses and frequentist network meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Risk of bias and confidence in network estimates were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and CINeMA, respectively. Thirty-six reports met the eligibility criteria, and 35 reports involving 1694 children contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Non-pharmacological interventions produced a statistically significant moderate overall improvement in cognitive outcomes (standardized mean difference = 0.54, 95% confidence interval 0.36-0.71), with significant benefits for working memory (0.61, 0.09-1.13) and social-emotional cognition (0.47, 0.30-0.65). Social-emotional cognition was the only domain with a sufficiently connected network for comparisons across intervention categories; social-behavioral and technology- and robot-assisted interventions showed the clearest benefits relative to active controls. Evidence networks for attention, working memory, and comprehensive executive function were sparse or disconnected. Confidence was moderate for selected social-emotional cognition comparisons but low or very low for most estimates. Non-pharmacological interventions may improve selected cognitive outcomes in children with autism spectrum disorder, but effects appear domain specific. More adequately powered head-to-head trials using standardized outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies.

AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE.

RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

articles.title: Microplastic pollution characteristics in global marine sediments: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution in marine environments has attracted widespread attention worldwide. Sediments are hotspots of MPs pollution. However, a comprehensive understanding of the distribution characteristics and driving factors of microplastics in coastal sediments is still lacking. The results revealed substantial variation in sediment MP abundance, with values ranging from 7.6 to 4213 particles/kg; the overall pooled abundance was 186.24 particles/kg (95% CI: 132.39-262.00), with substantial residual heterogeneity among the included estimates. Smaller MPs (<1 mm) accounted for over 60% of all detected MPs in global sediments. Transparent, fibrous and Polyethylene were the most common color, morphology and polymer type of MPs, respectively. Based on redundancy analysis (RDA), driving factors of MP morphological characteristics were explored. The results showed that flotation density and identification methods were the main sources of methodological bias in the observed MP characteristics. Significant differences in microplastic color distribution were observed among different countries. We divided the studies into four subgroups according to the distance from the coast. Although MP abundance exhibited certain spatial variations across regions, regional factors could explain only a small fraction of the observed heterogeneity. In contrast, the multivariable model explained 48.3% of the heterogeneity, highlighting the importance of methodological variability and the need for more standardized sampling and analytical procedures. This study identified small MPs and low-density polymers as key components of global sedimentary MP pollution and highlighted the need for standardized detection methods, supporting targeted monitoring of these MPs and harmonized protocols for global marine sediment assessment.

articles.title: Eicosanoids as Biomarkers of Hyperfiltration-Mediated Injury in CKD.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early biomarkers of hyperfiltration-induced injury are not known. We previously reported elevated urinary prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) preceding albuminuria in children with solitary kidney, and upregulated cyclooxygenase-2 (COX2)-PGE2-EP2 axis in unilaterally nephrectomized mice. To determine chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage-associated changes in urinary eicosanoids, baseline urine samples from the CKD in children (CKiD) biorepository (n = 318) and a comparator group of children with enuresis (n = 72) were analyzed.

METHODS: Liquid or gas chromatography-mass spectrometry was used to measure metabolites of arachidonic acid and linoleic acid (ng/mg creatinine, P ≤ 0.05).

RESULTS: The CKiD cohort included children with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) (71%, n = 226) and glomerular disease (29%, n = 92). Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) measurement (Iohexol) showed 27% and 73% of CAKUT subjects at CKD stages 2 and 3, respectively. Among those with glomerular disease, 42% and 58% were at CKD stages 2 and 3, respectively. Comparisons across CKD stages identified increase in urinary PGE2, thromboxane, and dihydroxy eicosatrienoic acids (DHETs), with a decrease in prostacyclin, F2-isoprostane, and 9,10-dihydroxy-octadecenoic acids (DiHOMEs) from CKD stage 2 to 3 indicating perturbed metabolism through COX and cytochrome P-450 (CYP450) pathways. In unadjusted mixed models quantifying the associations of a 2-times higher baseline eicosanoid with initial GFR found prostacyclin, PGE2/prostacyclin ratio, thromboxane/prostacyclin ratio, LTE4, 9,10-DiHOME, and F2-Isoprostane were significantly associated with higher initial GFR and remained significant after adjusting for CAKUT diagnosis, sex and baseline age, proteinuria, and hypertension. However, none of the eicosanoids were associated with change in GFR over time or time to kidney replacement therapy.

CONCLUSION: We report for the first time linoleic acid-derived metabolites in children with CKD. A longitudinal study is needed to validate selected urinary eicosanoids as early biomarkers of hyperfiltration.

articles.title: Comment on "Barrier identification and strategic design for hypertriglyceridemia management in the post-acute coronary syndrome patient population at a large integrated health system".
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

articles.title: Bulk peripheral-blood transcriptomic analysis identifies a STAT3/ARG1-associated myeloid immunosuppressive signature in sepsis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Sepsis involves immune dysregulation with myeloid activation and impaired antigen presentation. This study identified a compact immunosuppressive transcriptional signature associated with signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and arginase 1 (ARG1) using public peripheral-blood transcriptomic datasets. GSE28750, including 10 sepsis samples and 20 healthy controls, was used for discovery; GSE65682, including 120 sepsis-related baseline/ICU-admission samples and 40 healthy controls, was used for external validation. Differential expression, enrichment, ssGSEA, and correlation analyses were performed in GSE28750, whereas candidate-gene directionality and composite-signature performance were reproduced in GSE65682. Differential expression analysis identified 482 genes, with 301 upregulated and 181 downregulated. Representative STAT3/ARG1-associated myeloid and immunoregulatory genes were upregulated, whereas HLA-DRA and HLA-DRB1 were downregulated. Enrichment analysis highlighted myeloid activation, IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, arginine metabolism, and impaired antigen processing and presentation. Sepsis samples had higher myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC)-like scores than controls (0.72 ± 0.21 vs. -0.36 ± 0.18, P = 1.1 × 10 - 7). The composite signature showed exploratory diagnostic performance, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.94 and 0.88 in the discovery and validation cohorts, respectively. This study provides a reproducible bioinformatic framework and candidate transcriptional signature for assessing sepsis-related myeloid immunosuppressive remodeling.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05087-1.

articles.title: Renal Abscess Secondary to Urinary Tract Obstruction Caused by Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Report of Two Cases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic organ prolapse can cause urinary tract obstruction, leading to hydronephrosis, pyelonephritis, and in rare cases, renal abscess.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report two elderly women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse who developed renal abscesses. Both presented with pyelonephritis and acute renal impairment accompanied by bilateral hydronephrosis. Imaging demonstrated poorly enhanced renal lesions consistent with renal abscess. Infection was successfully controlled with antimicrobial therapy, followed by surgical correction. Renal function improved, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Advanced pelvic organ prolapse can cause severe urinary tract obstruction, leading to pyelonephritis and, in rare cases, renal abscess. Early recognition of advanced pelvic organ prolapse and urinary dysfunction, prompt infection control, and timely surgical management are essential to prevent serious complications.

articles.title: Four Pillars in Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease G4-G5: Mission Impossible-or Not Too Late to Start?
articles.abstract: The 4-pillar therapy-renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, the nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist finerenone, and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists-is increasingly applied to improve kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, landmark trials underpinning current recommendations largely enrolled participants down to estimated glomerular filtration rate thresholds of ∼20-30 mL/min/1.73 m2, leaving uncertainty in CKD G4-G5. This uncertainty contributes to an implementation gap in advanced CKD, which is as follows: missing pillars are often not initiated, therapies are interrupted during clinical complications, and they are not reinitiated once acute triggers resolve despite high absolute kidney and cardiovascular risk. This narrative review summarizes what current evidence does-and does not-support for initiating, continuing, temporarily withholding, discontinuing, and reinitiating each pillar in type 2 diabetes and CKD G4-G5. We integrate posthoc and subgroup analyses of landmark trials, meta-analyses, and pooled analyses, including low-estimated glomerular filtration rate strata and observational real-world data. The main practical message is that current evidence generally supports a monitoring-based approach to 4-pillar therapy in CKD G4, whereas decisions in CKD G5 remain more individualized and explicitly extrapolative. For clinicians, the key priority is to identify missing pillars, avoid unnecessary permanent discontinuation, and use structured reinitiation when clinically appropriate.

articles.title: Renal Outcomes in Hereditary Fibrinogen A Alpha-Chain Amyloidosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hereditary fibrinogen A alpha-chain (AFib) amyloidosis is characterized by progressive proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) and early progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). A large series published in 2009 showed renal survival <5 years from diagnosis and renal transplant survival of <10 years. Since then, advances in diagnostic techniques and nephroprotective care have transformed both nephrology and amyloidosis. We evaluated contemporary diagnostic and renal outcomes in the largest cohort of patients with AFib amyloidosis to date.

METHODS: A total of 194 patients with confirmed AFib amyloidosis who were followed at a large national center and diagnosed between 1993 and 2025 were included. Patients were stratified by the era of diagnosis, pre- or post-2009. Diagnostic approaches, renal outcomes, transplant outcomes, and patient survival were evaluated.

RESULTS: Median age at diagnosis was 60 years with mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 37 ml/min per 1.73 m2. Proteomics-based amyloid typing became the predominant diagnostic modality post-2009 (60.5%). 62.8% progressed to ESRD. The mean annual rate of eGFR decline was 6.7 ml/min per 1.73 m2 in the pre-2009 era and 4.8 ml/min per 1.73 m2 in the post-2009 era. Renal survival improved post-2009, particularly among patients with CKD stage IIIA or B at diagnosis. Median renal allograft survival improved from 7.7 years in the pre-2009 era to 15.5 years in the post-2009 era (P = 0.006) (hazard ratio [HR], 4.5 [95% confidence interval [CI], 1.2-22.6]). Overall patient survival did not differ significantly between eras (median, 12 years; P = 0.69, log-rank).

CONCLUSIONS: Renal and allograft survival have improved since 2009, likely reflecting advances in supportive nephrology care. Isolated kidney transplantation is associated with favorable long-term outcomes. Despite improvements in renal survival, overall survival remains unchanged, underscoring the need for effective amyloid-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Pruritus in Danish Dialysis Patients: A Cross-Sectional Multicenter Study of Prevalence, Disease Burden, and Current Treatment Practices.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus (CKD-aP) is rarely systematically assessed despite the potential negative impact on quality of life (QoL). This study investigated prevalence, disease burden, physician awareness, and treatment practices.

STUDY DESIGN: Multicenter cross-sectional study using patient-reported outcome measures and a physician practice survey.

SETTING & POPULATION: Adult patients with chronic kidney failure requiring replacement therapy and nephrologists from 8 Danish hospitals.

EXPOSURE: Kidney failure requiring replacement therapy and dialysis modality.

OUTCOMES: CKD-aP prevalence (score, >4) and pruritus severity (range, 0-10) according to the Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (WI-NRS). QoL and skin distribution assessed with the 5-D itch scale (range, 5-25). Physician awareness and treatment practices (self-invented questionnaire).

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Descriptive statistics were used.

RESULTS: We recruited 642 patients (∼25% of the Danish dialysis population): 83% receiving hemodialysis (HD), 13% receiving peritoneal dialysis, and 4% receiving home HD (HHD). The median WI-NRS score (IQR) was 0 (0-4). CKD-aP prevalence (95% CI) was 21% (18%-24%) (WI-NRS, >4). Moderate to very severe pruritus (WI-NRS, ≥4) was found in 25% (19%-32%). The median 5-D score (IQR) was 5 (5-10) (all patients). Peritoneal dialysis patients had significantly higher WI-NRS and 5-D scores than HD and HHD patients. Overall, the impact of CKD-aP on daily activities was minimal, but sleep disability (score, >1) was found in 20%. Sleep disability correlated significantly with higher WI-NRS scores. Based on 75 questionnaires (nephrologists/residents: 46/25), most physicians overestimated CKD-aP prevalence and favored dialysis, and fatty cream and phosphate-lowering treatment, rather than systemic treatment with gabapentinoids or difelikefalin.

LIMITATIONS: Single time-point estimate of CKD-aP and few HHD patients. No dermatologic evaluation was performed to exclude other pruritic conditions.

CONCLUSIONS: About 1 of 5 to 1 of 4 dialysis patients had CKD-aP, which mainly impaired QoL via sleep disturbance. Physicians demonstrated adequate awareness, but treatment remained largely limited to dialysis and fatty cream. Simple patient-reported outcome measures facilitated systematic assessment.

articles.title: Structure-based development of Glypican-3-targeting peptide candidates for hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains highly lethal, and extracellular GPC3 provides a tumor-associated surface target for structure-guided peptide design. This study established an entirely in silico workflow for de novo discovery and prioritization of GPC3-targeting peptide candidates using the human GPC3 structure from Protein Data Bank entry 7ZAW. W260, Y264, and M269 were selected as coordinate-resolved hotspot residues. A single 100 ns apo-GPC3 simulation was performed, and the centroid of the most populated cluster, accounting for 35.6% of the stable trajectory, was used for downstream design. RFdiffusion generated 100 peptide backbones near the hotspot surface, and ProteinMPNN generated a nonredundant peptide sequence library from the retained backbones. PepPAP was used as a sequence-level prediction model to rank candidates by its model output, which was treated as a relative computational prediction value rather than an experimentally measured binding free energy. The top 120 PepPAP-ranked sequences were refined with Rosetta FlexPepDock, generating 600 receptor-peptide poses, of which 565 satisfied the applied geometry/contact criteria. The top 30 docked peptides were evaluated using in silico solubility and toxicity predictors; 21 passed both filters. Integrated ranking identified five final priority candidates with Rosetta interface energies from - 20.459 to -18.255 REU. These peptides are computationally prioritized candidates for future experimental validation.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05092-4.

articles.title: Frailty as a Predictor of Mortality in Dialysis: A Multicenter Validation of the Clinical Frailty Scale.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Frailty is highly prevalent in dialysis and is associated with poor outcomes, yet scalable assessment in routine care remains challenging. We evaluated the feasibility and prognostic performance of the clinical frailty scale (CFS) applied by dialysis nurses and compared it with the REIN predictive score (RPS), a comorbidity-based mortality tool routinely available in French dialysis care.

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective multicenter observational cohort.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Adults receiving maintenance dialysis at 6 centers in northeastern France (n = 792 prevalent patients).

PREDICTORS: Nurse-rated 9-point CFS (analyzed both continuously and in 3 categories: 1-3 well, 4-5 vulnerable, and 6-9 frail) and RPS calculated at the time of CFS assessment.

OUTCOMES: All-cause mortality at 12 and 24 months; kidney transplant treated as a competing event.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Frailty ratings were obtained by trained dialysis nurses; interrater reliability was assessed in a subset with duplicate ratings. Cumulative incidence functions for death and transplantation were estimated using competing-risk methods. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, and central venous catheter use, plus CFS and RPS. Discrimination was assessed with C-statistics at 12 and 24 months.

RESULTS: Two independent CFS ratings were available for 509 patients; agreement was moderate when grouped into 3 categories (κ = 0.60). Twelve-month and 24-month mortality increased stepwise across CFS categories (well: 3.56% and 9.78%; vulnerable: 10.49% and 21.30%; frail: 27.27% and 45.87%). In multivariable models, both higher CFS (sHR per point 1.33; 95% CI, 1.19-1.49) and higher RPS (sHR per point 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.09) were independently associated with mortality. Discrimination was good: at 12 months, C-statistics were 0.73 (95% CI, 0.68-0.79) for CFS and 0.69 (95% CI, 0.63-0.75) for RPS; at 24 months, 0.71 (95% CI, 0.66-0.75) and 0.67 (95% CI, 0.62-0.72), respectively. A CFS score ≥6 identified an exploratory high-risk group for 12-month mortality.

LIMITATIONS: Prevalent cohort from a single region; nonstandardized timing of CFS assessments; no systematic ethnicity data.

CONCLUSIONS: In routine dialysis practice, nurse-applied CFS is feasible, reproducible when grouped into 3 categories, and predicts mortality over 36 months with performance comparable to, and independent of, a comorbidity-based mortality score. These findings support integrating the CFS into longitudinal risk assessment in dialysis, with external validation needed before using specific cut points to guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Retinal Arterial Wall Reflectivity and Incident Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether retinal arterial wall reflectivity is associated with future cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a large community-based Japanese cohort.

DESIGN: Community-based cohort study.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 6264 adults from the Nagahama Study (baseline 2012-2016) without a history of CVD.

METHODS: Retinal arterial wall reflectivity was measured on peripapillary OCT images at baseline. Participants were followed for approximately 7 years, and incident CVD events, including stroke and coronary artery disease (CAD), were identified through medical records. Associations were evaluated using Fine-Gray competing risk models and expressed as subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs). Retinal arterial caliber was included in multivariable analyses.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident CVD events, including stroke and CAD.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 6.7 years, 125 incident CVD events occurred. In the full cohort, retinal arterial wall reflectivity was not independently associated with CVD (SHR per 10 arbitrary units, 1.026; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.920-1.145). A continuous age-by-reflectivity interaction was observed (P = 0.029). In post hoc exploratory analyses among participants younger than 70 years, parsimonious models suggested possible associations with CVD (SHR, 1.173; 95% CI, 1.031-1.334) and stroke (SHR, 1.280; 95% CI, 1.088-1.506).

CONCLUSIONS: Retinal arterial wall reflectivity was not independently associated with incident CVD in the full cohort. Post hoc exploratory analyses among participants younger than 70 years suggested possible modest associations with CVD, particularly stroke-related outcomes. These findings suggest that retinal arterial wall reflectivity may reflect subclinical vascular alterations, but require external validation.

FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

articles.title: Target Trial Emulation or Target Trial Approximation?
articles.abstract: Target trial emulation has contributed to improvements in the design and interpretation of observational studies aimed at causal inference. By encouraging researchers to think explicitly about the design of a hypothetical randomized trial, it has helped identify and address avoidable design flaws. However, the framework cannot overcome biases and limitations inherent in observational data. Despite the aim of emulating a randomized trial, observational data cannot reproduce random treatment assignment or blinding, and may not necessarily provide greater generalizability than a randomized trial. Thus, the term "emulation" may imply a degree of similarity to a randomized trial that observational data cannot realistically achieve and deserves critical reconsideration to better reflect the limitations of observational data.

articles.title: Hepatic Progenitor Cells and the Ductular Reaction: Pathophysiological Role in the Progression of Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Ductular reaction (DR), a defining histological hallmark of diverse acute and chronic liver injuries, is fundamentally driven by the activation of hepatic progenitor cells (HPCs) and their complex, spatiotemporal bidirectional crosstalk within the hepatic niche. As bipotent precursor cells, HPCs initiate compensatory regeneration when mature hepatocyte proliferation is compromised. However, DR is not a uniform process but a multiphase dynamic reaction: transient early activation facilitates parenchymal restoration, whereas persistent, dysregulated HPC expansion fuels progressive fibrogenesis. The convergence of conserved developmental signalling cascades-including Hippo-YAP, Hedgehog, Notch and TGF-β-strictly governs HPC fate commitment and biliary epithelial proliferation. Concurrently, DR orchestrates intricate inflammatory circuitries by recruiting innate and adaptive immune cells, activating hepatic stellate cells and remodelling the extracellular matrix, thereby establishing a pro-fibrotic niche that perpetuates chronic injury. This review systematically categorizes the disease-specific morphological and molecular subtypes of DR across heterogeneous liver disorders, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), viral hepatitis and cholestatic liver diseases, highlighting its robust value as an independent histological and serological prognostic biomarker. Leveraging recent mechanistic breakthroughs from single-cell transcriptomics, lineage tracing and spatial imaging, we comprehensively evaluate widely adopted preclinical models and summarise emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the HPC-DR axis, such as small-molecule compounds, phytochemicals and cytokine modulators. Despite substantial advances in deciphering the HPC-DR axis, critical translational bottlenecks impede its clinical application. Collectively, this review integrates state-of-the-art multidimensional evidence to reconstruct the pathogenic network of HPC-DR interactions, providing mechanistic insights to facilitate precise prognostic evaluation and the development of novel targeted interventions for chronic liver diseases.

articles.title: The Impact of Anaesthesia Method on the Use of Anaesthesia Department Resources in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health-related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact. In this study, we analysed time, costs, and disposable materials associated with spinal anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia during total knee arthroplasty.

METHODS: A total of 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to spinal or general anaesthesia. Outcomes were total operating room time, non-operative operating room time, post-anaesthesia care unit time, use of drugs affecting haemodynamics, and the need for arterial cannulation and urinary catheterisation. In addition, we evaluated the financial costs and waste produced by single-use equipment and medicines in both anaesthesia methods.

RESULTS: Anaesthesia method did not affect operating room time (median 152 min [interquartile range 136-168 min] vs. 150 min [137-165 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 2 min [95% CI -3 to 6 min], p = 0.49). However, after spinal anaesthesia, patients appeared to spend more time in the postanaesthesia care unit than after general anaesthesia (median 104 min [71-148 min] vs. 73 min [49-98 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 32 min [95% CI 23-42 min], p < 0.001). Medication for hypotension was more common in the general anaesthesia group, whereas medication for hypertension was more common in the spinal anaesthesia group. General anaesthesia generated more disposable material (1252 vs. 611 g), and both medicine and equipment expenses were higher (total costs €83 vs. €36).

CONCLUSION: With this anaesthesia regimen, knee arthroplasty patients occupied the operating room for a similar duration regardless of anaesthesia method, but patients required longer recovery in the postanaesthesia care unit after spinal anaesthesia. Regarding disposable material and medicine use, spinal anaesthesia appeared to be more economical and material-sparing than total intravenous anaesthesia. Furthermore, spinal anaesthesia appeared to cause less hypotension requiring haemodynamic interventions than general anaesthesia.

EDITORIAL COMMENT: This health-economic analysis estimates for how different aspects of general or spinal anaesthesia care contribute to process flow and item costs. Findings suggest that there may be measurably more costs associated with one of the anaesthesia type choices compared with the other, though this will depend on choices for materials and more.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: EudraCT (2016-002035-15).

articles.title: Global and Regional Risk Factors for Vision Impairment in 2020 and Multi-decadal Trends 1990-2020: A Meta-Analysis and Visual Display Based on Prevalence Data From the Global Burden of Disease study and Vision Loss Expert Group.
authors: Vision Loss Expert Group of the Global Burden of Disease Study
articles.journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate global and regional risk factors for blindness and vision impairment pertaining to all geographical locations between 1990 and 2020.

METHODS: (1) Twenty-four covariates were selected with a potential link to vision impairment from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) Covariates database as predictive factors. (2) From these, the linear association was investigated, with crude and age-standardised prevalence estimates of blindness and distance and near vision impairment in 2020 by using data for the whole population, sex and 5-year age groups, and by stratifying severity through mild, moderate, severe and total impairment. (3) Analysis investigated whether percentage rates of change in risk factors were associated with rates of change in prevalence in 1990-2020.

RESULTS: For adults (50+ years), for crude and age-standardised vision loss prevalence estimates for the year 2020, a significant negative association of smoking prevalence was found initially for all persons and for each sex, which appears to be due to ecological confounding and became a positive association using more granular regional and age group data. Maternal care and immunisation, sanitation proportion, Health Access and Quality Index and Socio-demographic Index were other significant age-standardised negative associations. Ophthalmologists/million population had a weak but significant protective effect, and positive associations were found for pollution (outdoor and indoor), stronger for greater vision impairment severities. Years in education per capita were weakly, negatively associated with vision loss prevalence, yet zero education proportion had a stronger but positive association for both sexes.

CONCLUSIONS: This study confirmed associations at population level globally, which appear to be stable over decades. In addition, the study quantified the contribution of epidemiologically-based risk factors to vision loss at a GBD super-regional level, which is novel. This opens useful avenues for targeted intervention by policymakers. For example, reduction in sex inequity in blindness rates over 30 years has been positively associated with reducing overall prevalence of blindness.

articles.title: Optimal exercise modalities and doses for blood pressure management in adults with prehypertension and hypertension: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify the most effective exercise modalities and optimal estimated dose range for reducing blood pressure in adults with prehypertension and hypertension, to support more precise exercise prescription.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to December 28, 2025. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if they included adults with prehypertension or stage 1 or stage 2 hypertension, evaluated structured exercise interventions, and reported resting systolic blood pressure and/or diastolic blood pressure.

RESULTS: A total of 284 randomized controlled trials, including 18,750 participants with a mean age of 56.8 years, covering ten exercise modalities were included. Aquatic exercise achieved the greatest reduction in systolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -10.28 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -13.05 to -7.49; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 93.26%. Whole-body vibration and cycling also showed favorable estimates for systolic blood pressure. Mind-body exercise showed the largest estimated reduction in diastolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -4.69 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -6.45 to -2.92; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 85.90%. Aquatic exercise and isometric exercise training also showed favorable effect estimates. Dose-response modelling indicated that 750 metabolic equivalent task minutes per week was the estimated dose associated with maximal modeled systolic blood pressure benefit for isometric exercise training, with a mean difference of -13.52 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -23.22 to -3.86. In contrast, 3600 metabolic equivalent task minutes per week was the estimated dose associated with maximal modeled diastolic blood pressure benefit for aerobic exercise, with a mean difference of -7.11 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -11.89 to -2.18.

CONCLUSION: Ten exercise modalities were associated with reductions in blood pressure, with particularly strong effects for aquatic, mind-body, and isometric exercise at specific doses. These findings may inform more tailored exercise prescription strategies for adults across hypertension phenotypes.

articles.title: The restore-adapt-abandon framework: supporting safe and meaningful living after ventricular assist device implantation.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular assist device (VAD) therapy improves survival and symptoms in patients with advanced heart failure but can impose lifestyle restrictions that challenge meaningful living. Engagement in meaningful activities is protective against all-cause mortality and positively impacts health, well-being, and quality of life, yet little is known about how VAD recipients adapt these activities post-implantation.

OBJECTIVES: To explore how VAD recipients navigate meaningful activity engagement post-implantation, and present a clinically-relevant framework characterizing how VAD recipients engage in meaningful activities across the post-implant trajectory.

METHODS: We analyzed semi‑structured interview data from VAD recipients in the Southeastern U.S. and used thematic analysis to explore patterns of activity engagement and adaptation.

RESULTS: Two major themes emerged: (1) symptom relief enables restoration of activities and social roles; and (2) identity shifts and risk management prompt modified engagement. Across themes, patients described strategies and constraints including planning over spontaneity, managing device visibility and stigma, out-of-pocket costs, caregiver-linked mobility, and climate sensitivity. These patterns informed a "restore-adapt-abandon" framework for meaningful activity engagement across the post-VAD trajectory.

CONCLUSION: Based on the findings, we recommend structured values elicitation, patient-clinician co-planning of activity adaptations, and identity-focused psychosocial support into routine VAD care. These strategies can optimize meaningful living alongside safety and redefine success in VAD therapy from survival alone to living well.

articles.title: Aflatoxin M1 in Milk and Aflatoxin B1 in Animal Feed in Bangladesh: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Literature-Based Dietary Risk Assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aflatoxin M1 (AFM1), the carcinogenic metabolite of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), passes into the milk of animals fed mould-contaminated feed. Bangladeshi feed and milk surveillance have developed separately, and integrated dietary-risk estimates are scarce.

OBJECTIVE AND DESIGN: To pool AFM1 occurrence in Bangladeshi milk, summarise feed AFB1 and characterise age-stratified dietary risk. The assessment is literature-based and modular: no Bangladeshi study reports paired feed and milk data, so compartments are joined by parameter transfer.

METHODS: Prevalences were pooled by DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with prediction intervals, subgroup, meta-regression, leave-one-out and small-study analyses. Exposure was modelled deterministically and probabilistically (100,000 iterations), with uncertainty tabulated following EFSA guidance.

RESULTS: Across 20 datasets (N = 605), pooled prevalence was 58.7% (95% CI 51.6%-65.5%; I2 = 61.9%; 95% prediction interval 32.1%-81.1%). Heterogeneity was structured by region (p = 0.001), not milk type (p = 0.980). The sample-weighted mean was 143 ng L-1 (geometric mean 92); 83% of milk exceeded the EU maximum level. Reconstruction from feed AFB1 predicted 24-282 ng L-1, containing 18 of 20 dataset means. Margins of exposure were 95 (infants) and 175 (toddlers), with probabilistic medians 157 and 286; the deterministic hazard index exceeded unity in every age group, the probabilistic median in every group except adults.

CONCLUSIONS: Infant and child margins of exposure remain far below the 10,000 benchmark under every scenario and robustness check. The estimate is screening-level, resting on transferred parameters and ELISA-based measurement. Monsoon-aware feed management, enforcement of the national milk standard and paired feed-milk surveillance are indicated.

articles.title: Effects of Single-Session High-Definition Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (HD-tACS) Combined with Robot-Assisted Hand Exercises on Corticospinal Excitability in Chronic Stroke.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This preliminary study investigated whether a single session of high-definition transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD-tACS) could improve corticospinal tract (CST) excitability compared with sham stimulation in healthy individuals and individuals with chronic stroke.

DESIGN: Twelve healthy adults and 7 individuals with chronic stroke received active and sham HD-tACS over the primary motor cortex (M1) flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) hotspot, ipsilesional in stroke subjects, for 30 minutes at 2mA and 21 Hz in a randomized crossover design. All subjects performed robot-assisted grasp-and-open hand exercises during active and sham stimulation.

RESULTS: HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in the healthy group (15.3%). In the stroke group, FDS MEP amplitudes were increased by ∼22.3% after HD-tACS, but this change was not statistically significant. When MEP amplitudes were normalized as percentage change, HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in both groups compared with the sham condition. No significant extensor digitorum communis (EDC) modulation was observed in either group.

CONCLUSION: HD-tACS combined with robot-assisted hand exercises may enhance CST excitability compared with robot-assisted hand exercises alone after a single session in both healthy and stroke subjects. However, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Gut-heart-kidney communication in cardiovascular disease: from a single-metabolite hypothesis to a context-dependent metabolite network.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites are increasingly recognized as key mediators of interorgan communication in cardiovascular disease. However, the field has often relied on a single-metabolite hypothesis, particularly centered on trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), which does not fully capture the complexity of host-microbe-organ interactions. In this review, we argue that cardiovascular risk is better understood as a network of interacting gut-derived molecules, in which TMAO functions as a node within a broader system that includes phenylacetylglutamine, indole-related metabolites, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and lipopolysaccharide. Within this framework, the TMAO two-hit model, in which pre-existing organ vulnerability (first hit) is exacerbated by metabolite elevations (second hit), exemplifies context-dependent pathogenicity, particularly in chronic kidney disease or other pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerabilities. We further discuss how this network-based view may refine biomarker interpretation, improve patient stratification, and guide the development of biomarker-guided strategies for microbiome-targeted interventions. By reframing gut-derived metabolites as part of an interorgan communication network rather than isolated mediators, this review aims to provide a more integrated translational perspective for cardiovascular pathophysiology and patient stratification.

articles.title: The pathophysiology of wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis: implications for exercise intolerance.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRwt) is an age-associated protein misfolding disorder marked by extracellular deposition of transthyretin fibrils within the myocardium, peripheral nerves, lungs, blood vessels, and musculoskeletal tissues. ATTRwt typically presents as a restrictive cardiomyopathy with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction that contributes to the development of hallmark symptoms such as exercise intolerance. Amyloid infiltration severely impairs ventricular compliance and diastolic reserve, limiting stroke volume and cardiac output augmentation during exercise, and is frequently accompanied by coronary microvascular dysfunction. These central limitations are compounded by autonomic dysfunction, including chronotropic incompetence and impaired sympathetic vasomotor control, which blunt heart rate responses and disrupt appropriate blood flow responses.
