Pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular-pulmonary artery uncoupling, and ventilatory inefficiency further constrain oxygen transport and contribute to exertional dyspnea and early fatigue. Other peripheral factors such as amyloid-related derangements in vascular endothelial function and musculoskeletal pathologies likely result in impaired hyperemic responses to exercise and accelerated cardiovascular deconditioning, further limiting physical capacity. Together, these integrated cardiac, pulmonary, autonomic, and peripheral abnormalities convergently impair exercise performance in ATTRwt. Considering the universal presentation of exercise intolerance in ATTRwt, therapies that may have favorable effects on physical capacity are of great interest to patients, physicians, and scientists alike. This review seeks to synthesize current evidence describing the central and peripheral pathophysiological mechanisms underlying exercise intolerance in ATTRwt and discuss the potential of pharmacologic and exercise-based interventions that may improve physical capacity in this population.

articles.title: Non-Relapse Mortality With Bispecific Antibodies in Hematologic Malignancies: A Dual Systematic Review and Pharmacovigilance Analysis.
articles.abstract: Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) redirect T-cells to tumor antigens in an MHC-independent manner. These universally available, off-the-shelf products have demonstrated unprecedented efficacy in heavily pretreated patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) hematological malignancies (HMs). The indefinite treatment duration associated with most BsAb products, coupled with neutropenia, B-cell aplasia, and hypogammaglobulinemia result in significant immune-related toxicities and infections. Hence, non-relapse mortality (NRM) which represents the cumulative burden of treatment-related toxicities, defined as death from any cause other than disease relapse or progression, is a patient-centric endpoint across cellular therapy platforms. While recent NRM estimates with CAR T-cell therapy have identified infections as major drivers of NRM, real-world NRM estimates remain limited with BsAbs. To mitigate the limitations associated with each of the methods, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of the existing literature, supplemented concurrently by a pharmacovigilance analysis using the FAERS database, to estimate NRM with BsAbs and compare real-world findings between commercially available BsAb products approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) and NHL. The primary endpoint was NRM; secondary endpoints included CRS, ICANS, infections, and death. Teclistamab demonstrated a high toxicity burden across both analytic methods, with the highest ICANS incidences, significantly greater infection rates (particularly grade > 3), and a non-negligible NRM estimate in the SRMA as well in FAERS. Glofitamab was associated with severe toxicities, including increased reporting odds for NRM and overall mortality. Mosunetuzumab showed lower pooled estimates and lower reporting odds, as seen in both analytic approaches. Low pooled incidences of infections, and ICANS were calculated in the SRMA. FAERS analyses also suggested reduced reporting odds for NRM and neurotoxicity. While trial-level data and real-world reporting largely converged for severe toxicities, divergences in other agents underscore the importance of continuous post-marketing surveillance. Given the risks associated with prolonged treatment, future protocols must prioritize infection management and adopt NRM as a standardized endpoint to guide appropriate therapeutic selection and sequencing.

articles.title: Intensive Care Unit Patients' Perspectives and Experiences in Using Virtual Reality Technology: A Qualitative Meta-Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As Intensive Care Unit (ICU) survival improves, attention has shifted towards patients' psychological well-being and recovery. Although Virtual Reality (VR) is increasingly used in critical care, patients' experiences of VR interventions have not been comprehensively synthesised.

AIM: To synthesise qualitative and mixed-methods evidence regarding ICU patients' perceptions, experiences and implementation-related considerations associated with VR interventions.

METHODS: A qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis following Thomas and Harden's three-stage approach was conducted. Eight databases were searched from inception to September 2025. Studies employing qualitative methods or components of mixed methods exploring ICU patients' firsthand VR experiences were included. Methodological quality was appraised using the JBI checklist.

RESULTS: Eight studies involving 247 participants were included. Four analytical themes were synthesised: (A) VR as a restorative escape, (B) VR as a route from passive endurance to active participation, (C) Patient readiness and personal preference shape VR engagement, and (D) VR as a co-produced intervention requiring contextual and relational adaptation.

CONCLUSIONS: ICU patients perceived VR as a valuable tool that provided restorative escape and enabled active recovery, yet multiple barriers shaped its feasibility. Implementation should consider comfortable devices, customisable content and staff training. These findings inform patient-centred VR design in the ICU.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: VR offers a non-pharmacological approach that may support patient well-being and recovery during an ICU stay. It can provide meaningful focus and relief from distress, while encouraging engagement with rehabilitation. Nurses play a key role in facilitating sessions and assessing patient readiness. Implementation may be enhanced by comfortable, bed-compatible devices, customisable content and staff training. While not all patients may be suitable candidates, VR appears generally acceptable and could be integrated into individualised care plans.

REVIEW REGISTRATION: The review protocol had been registered in PROSPERO (International prospective register of systematic reviews). The registration number is CRD420251074650.

articles.title: Nurse-Led Interventions to Mitigate High-Alert Medication Errors in Critical Care: A Systematic Review of Effectiveness and Implementation Strategies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care units (ICUs) are high-risk environments where nurses administer the majority of high-alert medications, making them the final checkpoint in the medication-use process. However, evidence on nurse-led interventions specifically targeting high-alert medication errors has not been systematically synthesized across all ICU populations.

AIM: This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions in reducing high-alert medication errors in neonatal, paediatric and adult intensive care units and examined implementation strategies that enhance patient safety.

STUDY DESIGN: We followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus for studies published between January 2000 and June 2026. Inclusion criteria required nurse-led interventions, measurement of high-alert medication error rates and critical care settings. The risk of bias was assessed. A narrative synthesis was performed due to heterogeneity in study designs and outcome measures.

RESULTS: Six studies met the inclusion criteria. Interventions included simulation-based training, staff education, smart pump integration, clinical decision support systems and standardization of medication orders and protocols. All studies reported improvements in medication safety outcomes, including reductions in medication error rates, improved compliance, enhanced accuracy and increased efficiency. Secondary outcomes included improved compliance with PRN orders (from 62.0% ± 9.2% to 77.7% ± 10.1%), reduced medication dispensing time (to < 1 min) and cost savings ($90 000-$130 000 per year). Risk of bias was moderate to low in five studies and high in one study.

CONCLUSION: Nurse-led multicomponent interventions are associated with reductions in high-alert medication errors and improvements in safety outcomes in critical care settings. However, technology alone is insufficient without workflow integration and nursing education. Education and standardization require concurrent process redesign for sustained improvement.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Nurses should advocate for multicomponent strategies combining training, technology and standardized protocols. Healthcare organizations must ensure workflow integration to maximize the benefits of smart pumps and clinical decision support systems. Future research should employ rigorous designs, include diverse ICU settings and low- to middle-income countries and evaluate long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Nursing Mechanisms of Intravenous Medication Loss in Adult Intensive Care: A Mixed-Methods Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult ICU medication loss is reported using non-equivalent forms and denominators, limiting interpretation and intervention design.

AIMS: To examine loss measurement, nursing mechanisms, intervention evidence and balancing outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: Convergent segregated mixed-methods systematic review. Three databases were searched to 1 July 2026, with citation searching, metadata checks and an uncapped rerun of two capped PubMed arms. Quantitative results remained in native units; qualitative findings were synthesised separately and integrated. MMAT 2018 was applied by design category; two reviewers checked screening, extraction and appraisal.

RESULTS: Of 768 screened records (576 primary; 192 rerun), 79 reports were assessed with retained sources. Four reports could not be retrieved. Twenty-five reports from 21 independent studies were included; the rerun added none. Categories were prepared-unused medication (11), post-order or post-event loss (7), partial-container residual (8), delivery-system residual (3) and material-flow loss (4); categories were nonexclusive. Denominators were explicit in 10 studies, partial in 5 and absent in 6. No studies met pooling criteria. Two qualitative studies generated six low-confidence CERQual findings. Intervention evidence was uncontrolled, modelled or proposal-based; balancing outcomes were uncommon.

CONCLUSIONS: Adult ICU loss comprised non-equivalent quantities, not one waste prevalence, and no study related it to a patient outcome. Studies would need to specify loss form, numerator, denominator, observation window, workflow node, result origin and balancing outcomes alongside resource use.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Order review before non-urgent preparation, reconstitution and checking, storage and return pathways, and syringe, pump and line handling are candidate targets; no controlled adult ICU study has shown reduced loss without affecting access, dose delivery, sterility, compatibility or workload.

articles.title: Featured video: Complications of chronic liver disease.
Turning down the ammonia dial: Phase 2a evidence for YAQ007 in cirrhosis.
A gentler squeeze: A first signal from OCE-205, a selective V1a mixed agonist-antagonist for hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury.
Inside the 'Black Box' of Pharmaceuticalisation: NICE, the Permissive Principle and the Case of Anticoagulants.
articles.abstract: Sociological interest in pharmaceuticalisation continues to grow, especially regarding the expansion of pharmaceutical use in society. This article presents the first major empirical study focusing on the directionality of pharmaceuticalisation by taking cost-effectiveness assessment and regulation of anticoagulants in England by the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence (NICE) as a case study. During this century, anticoagulant therapy for the prevention of stroke and systemic embolism has changed direction profoundly away from warfarin towards newer and markedly more expensive direct oral anticoagulants. Drawing on established theoretical frameworks of pharmaceuticalisation, together with years of documentary research, interviews and observations of stakeholder meetings, it is demonstrated that this directional change cannot be adequately accounted for solely by reference to biomedicalism. Rather, such change must also be explained by key sociological factors, including the adoption of the permissive principle towards the newer drugs by the NICE regulatory system, pharmaceutical industry influence on governance processes, the 'coincidence' of expansion in diagnostic criteria for stroke risk with the introduction of the new direct oral anticoagulants, and the promotion of neoliberal patient choice and innovation by the regulatory state. Finally, the generalisability and policy implications of our findings for other therapeutic and institutional contexts are considered.

articles.title: Updating Korean Reimbursement Criteria for Endovascular Thrombectomy in Contemporary Stroke Care.
Key Predictors of Cerebral Vasospasm Following Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a life-threatening condition often leading to complications such as cerebral vasospasm, which causes delayed cerebral ischemia and increases mortality. In intensive care, early identification of vasospasm risk factors by nurses is essential for timely intervention and improved outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: We sought to review and synthesize evidence on risk factors associated with cerebral vasospasm after SAH and inform early risk assessment and nursing care strategies in intensive care.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies. A comprehensive search was conducted on August 30 to 31, 2024, across 8 databases. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist and the Risk of Bias (RoB 2.0) tool.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight studies were included in the systematic review, of which 27 were included in the meta-analysis, involving 19 033 patients. Clinical severity measures were most strongly associated with cerebral vasospasm, including Modified Fisher grade (odds ratio (OR) = 2.88; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.04-4.07), Fisher grade (OR = 2.27; 95% CI, 1.91-2.69), and hemodynamic status (OR = 2.56; 95% CI, 1.17-5.59). Aneurysm-related factors and comorbid conditions were associated with increased risk of cerebral vasospasm, whereas clinical biomarkers and inflammatory markers showed relatively smaller effect sizes.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical severity scales and hemodynamic status are the strongest predictors of cerebral vasospasm following SAH. These findings support early risk stratification and the implementation of structured monitoring strategies to improve patient outcomes.PROSPERO trial registration number:CRD42024605605 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024605605).

articles.title: Active Helicobacter pylori Infection and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection may promote systemic inflammation and has been proposed as a contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF), but clinical evidence is inconsistent. The aim of the study was to explore whether active H. pylori infection was associated with AF in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included adults from a two-center observational AMI cohort. Active H. pylori infection was assessed during hospitalization using a urea breath test (UBT). AF was defined as AF documented before admission or identified during the index hospitalization. Associations were estimated using logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, center, and smoking. Exploratory multivariable interaction analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: Of 310 enrolled patients, 300 had conclusive H. pylori screening results; 60 (20.0%) were positive. AF was recorded in 4 of 60 H. pylori-positive patients (6.7%) and 30 of 240 H. pylori-negative patients (12.5%). H. pylori positivity was not significantly associated with recorded AF (unadjusted OR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.17-1.41; p = 0.228; adjusted OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.16-1.46; p = 0.235). These estimates refer to pooled AF; only four AF cases occurred among patients testing positive.

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant association was detected between H. pylori breath-test positivity and pooled documented AF among patients hospitalized with AMI, but a clinically meaningful association cannot be excluded. Larger prospective studies with longitudinal follow-up are needed to clarify whether active H. pylori infection is associated with incident AF after AMI.

articles.title: Investigating Fibrinolysis Resistance in Sepsis Using High-Multiplex Plasma Proteomics: A Statistical Analysis Plan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy is characterised by consumptive coagulation abnormalities and resistance to fibrinolysis, which is increasingly recognised as a driver of microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and mortality. The molecular determinants of the fibrinolysis-resistant phenotype remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVE: To present a pre-specified statistical analysis plan for a plasma proteomic investigation of fibrinolysis resistance in 89 samples collected serially from 32 critically ill patients with sepsis, using the Olink Explore HT platform (approximately 5400 proteins). The plan is designed to characterise protein associations with a validated bedside measure of fibrinolysis resistance, the ratio of tissue plasminogen activator-induced lysis time to fibrin clot amplitude (TPA-LT/FIBA10). The associations will be examined across the fibrinolysis resistance severity continuum and between three ordinal severity grades, and over time within individual patients.

METHODS: The analytic framework combines five complementary approaches: (i) limit-of-detection-based data filtering, (ii) continuous-variable modelling of protein abundance against TPA-LT/FIBA10 using limma-trend regression, (iii) categorical comparison across severity grades using empirical Bayes moderated statistics, (iv) linear mixed-effects modelling of longitudinal intra-patient trajectories and (v) pathway-level enrichment analysis to translate statistical associations into mechanistic hypotheses. A semi-supervised pathway clustering analysis will describe how proteins change by fibrinolysis resistance in eight a priori defined domains.

DISCUSSION: This multi-model design is intended to define genuine biological signals in a high-dimensional dataset while remaining transparent about the exploratory nature of several components. The statistical reasoning behind each method is discussed alongside anticipated limitations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06680180.

articles.title: Update of Korean Medicine Clinical Practice Guidelines for Obesity Management: An Evidence-Based GRADE Approach.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Obesity is a major health challenge associated with multiple chronic diseases. Korean traditional medicine (KM) offers diverse therapeutic approaches for obesity management. This study aims to update the Korean Medicine Clinical Practice Guidelines (KMCPGs) by incorporating recent evidence to improve the effectiveness of KM-based obesity care.

METHODS: The KMCPGs were updated through systematic searches of eight databases for studies published up to December 31, 2022. Evidence quality and recommendation strength were evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: The updated KMCPGs present 20 clinical recommendations, including 7 for KM monotherapies and 13 for KM combination therapies. The recommendations include herbal medicine (A/high), individualized ephedra-containing prescriptions (GPP), acupuncture (B/low), auricular acupuncture (C/low), electroacupuncture (B/low), pharmacopuncture (B/moderate), TEA (C/low), and 13 combination therapies ranging from grade B to C or GPP. Most recommendations focus on anthropometric outcomes, including body weight, BMI, WC, and body fat-related measures.

CONCLUSIONS: The update of the KMCPGs underscores the clinical value of KM interventions in obesity management while emphasizing the need for further high-quality studies to strengthen the evidence. Addressing implementation barriers and ensuring regular guideline updates are essential for optimizing clinical application and improving patient outcomes in obesity care.

articles.title: Atrial cardiomyopathy: from knowledge gaps to clinical impact : The role of the EmbRACE Network.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is increasingly recognised as an underlying atrial substrate contributing to atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), and cardio-embolic stroke. However, diagnostic criteria, disease thresholds, and targeted treatment strategies remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the rationale, structure, and translational strategy of the EmbRACE (Electro-Molecular Basis and the theRapeutic management of Atrial Cardiomyopathy, fibrillation and associated outcomEs) network, a national consortium established to address key knowledge gaps in AtCM.

METHODS: EmbRACE integrates mechanistic research, computational modelling, clinical trials, and implementation science within seven interconnected work packages. Human atrial tissue biobanking and deep phenotyping (WP1) enable molecular profiling of candidate pathways (WP2), which are validated in experimental models (WP3). Computational modelling and artificial intelligence (WP4) integrate multimodal clinical and biological data to derive composite AtCM phenotypes and severity frameworks. Substrate-targeting clinical trials evaluate AF ablation (RACE X; WP5), weight reduction using GLP‑1 agonists (DUTCH-WAIST; WP6), and optimised rate control using calcium channel antagonists (SMART-VERAPAF; WP6). Implementation science (WP7) focuses on guideline integration, decision-support tools, and governance of AI-based risk models. EmbRACE establishes a translational pipeline from mechanistic discovery to clinical application. By integrating tissue-level insights with multimodal risk modelling and interventional trials, the consortium aims to define clinically meaningful AtCM thresholds, to validate indirect markers, and to determine whether targeted treatment modifies disease progression and clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: EmbRACE provides a multidisciplinary framework to transform AtCM from a theoretical construct into a clinically actionable entity, enabling earlier detection, improved risk stratification, and AtCM-directed therapy in cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: Persistent Opioid Exposure in Older Adults With Rheumatic Disease: National Patterns, Disparities, and Cross-Specialty Prescribing.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate national prevalence of opioid use, including chronic and high-risk use, among older adults with rheumatic diseases (RDs); to identify sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with chronic opioid use; and to characterize prescribing patterns by clinician specialty in a contemporary Medicare-linked national registry cohort.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of the Rheumatology Informatics System for Effectiveness (RISE) registry linked to Medicare Part D (2016-2021). Patients were aged ≥ 65 years with qualifying RDs and continuous Medicare enrollment in 2021. Opioid use was identified from Part D claims. Chronic use was defined as ≥ 90-day supply in 2021. High-risk use was assessed using Office of Inspector General indicators. Generalized estimating equations modeled factors associated with chronic opioid use.

RESULTS: Among 45,455 patients (mean age 75.8 years; 76.88% women), 43.13% filled ≥ 1 opioid prescription and 17.93% met criteria for chronic use in 2021. Very high-risk prescribing was rare (< 1%). Chronic use was most prevalent in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA; 26.19%) and least prevalent in polymyalgia rheumatica (11.58%). In adjusted analyses, axSpA (odds ratio [OR] 1.63, 95% CI 1.35-1.98), fibromyalgia (OR 2.68, 95% CI 2.39-3.00), mood disorder (OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.31-1.52), anxiety disorder (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.35-1.57), higher comorbidity burden (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.62-2.06), American Indian/Alaska Native race (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.09-2.45), and greater socioeconomic deprivation (OR 1.91, 95% CI 1.71-2.13) were independently associated with chronic use. Nonrheumatology clinicians wrote most opioid prescriptions (62.60%) and more high-dose prescriptions (≥ 50 morphine mg equivalents/day).

CONCLUSION: Opioid exposure remains common among Medicare-insured older adults with RDs, although very high-risk prescribing is rare. Coordinated, guideline-concordant pain management across specialties may help preserve appropriate opioid use for patients who may benefit while reducing avoidable long-term exposure.

articles.title: Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Estimating Causal Effects: Fluoroquinolones and Tendon Rupture.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare services, potentially affecting causal effect estimation using real-world data. As a case study, we replicated a cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum to evaluate whether pandemic-related disruptions influenced the measured association between fluoroquinolone use and tendon rupture.

METHODS: We included adults initiating fluoroquinolones/cephalosporins during 1 January 2006-31 March 2023. Four analyses compared treatment effect estimates using different periods for exposure and outcome ascertainment: pre-pandemic only, pre-pandemic exposure with follow-up extending through the pandemic, all available data and post-pandemic only. We estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for tendon rupture using Cox regression.

RESULTS: Among 891 968 fluoroquinolone users and 895 229 cephalosporin users, fluoroquinolone users had more comorbidities than cephalosporin users in the pre-pandemic period but fewer in the post-pandemic period. Pre-pandemic analysis showed an increased risk of tendon rupture associated with fluoroquinolones (Propensity score weighted [PSW]-HR: 1.94; 95% CI: 1.46-2.59), consistent with previous evidence. Estimates using all available data were similar for the overall study period (PSW-HR: 1.91; 95% CI: 1.46-2.51) and the pre-pandemic period (PSW-HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.47-2.61) but were less precise during/post-pandemic period (PSW-HR: 1.57; 95% CI: 0.72-3.41) with no evidence of a period-treatment interaction (PSW-HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.35-1.84). Post-pandemic analysis showed very few events among cephalosporin users but not fluoroquinolone users with a larger but imprecise estimate (PSW-HR: 3.32; 95% CI: 0.62-17.72).

CONCLUSION: In this case study, there was no clear evidence that pandemic-related healthcare disruptions materially altered causal estimates, albeit with limited power to detect differences between before and during/post-pandemic effects. Studies using real-world data across the pandemic should routinely examine temporal changes in baseline characteristics and outcome incidence.

articles.title: Social Risk Screening and Referrals in the Pediatric Inpatient Setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Many professional organizations recently recommended inpatient screening for social risks. Although prior studies have explored social risk screening rates in children's hospitals, many excluded community hospitals and lacked detail on screening practices. We aimed to describe national social risk screening and referral practices among hospitals caring for children.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey (August 2023-November 2023) through the Pediatric Research in Inpatient Settings Network. One clinical leader per institution was surveyed on inpatient social risk screening and referral processes, populations, tools and data tracking, and barriers/facilitators to social care. Descriptive statistics summarized survey responses.

RESULTS: Of the hospitals contacted, 80.2% (77/96) completed the survey. Overall, 66.7% of hospitals reported screening for social risks in some capacity, most commonly performed by nurses. Screening tools and domains varied widely, with 21.9% using a published tool and 12.5% using internally developed questions. Food insecurity was the most frequently screened domain (91.9%), whereas screening for legal needs was least common (0%). Most hospitals had systems to refer patients to in-hospital (98.4%) and out-of-hospital (96.8%) services, primarily through social work consultations (96.5%) and printed handouts (54.4%). Fewer than 10% partnered with community-based organizations. Less than 45% of screening hospitals had a data-tracking system for referrals, and only 2.5% collected patient health care use data. Staffing was the most cited barrier to screening.

CONCLUSIONS: Social risk screening and referral practices vary widely among hospitals caring for children. Standardized policies and support mechanisms may reduce variability and promote equitable social care practices across hospitals.

articles.title: Blood proteome-wide Mendelian randomization reveals molecular pleiotropy in coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a common cardiovascular disease characterized by the development of atheromatous plaques. Recent large-scale association study (GWAS) offers an opportunity to better understand the underpinnings of this pathology.

METHODS: To investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms of CAD, we interrogated genetic association data for the blood proteome (216,063 cases and 1,246,152 controls for GWAS data and 53,480 individuals for pQTLs datasets). Data were analysed by using Mendelian randomization, inference of ligand-receptor interactions, molecular phenome-wide analysis of genetic variants and tissue-specific protein expression analysis. Pharmacological repositioning study on prioritized proteins was conducted.

RESULTS: Using a two-tier replication MR approach with strong instrumental variables (PpQTL<5E-08) we identified 29 blood proteins associated with the risk of CAD, which were common to at least 2 exposition cohorts. Among those proteins, 17 are newly associated with CAD and were not previously reported or mapped in CAD-GWAS. CAD-associated proteome was enriched in ligands whose cognate receptors were expressed in cardiac macrophages and endothelial cells. Molecular phenome-wide association study (MolPheWAS) revealed a group of 10 blood proteins forming a pleiotropic network enriched in functions pertaining to cell migration-differentiation, inflammation and lipid metabolism. Mediation analysis identified TIMD4-APOC3, KLKB1-APOB and COLEC11-ANGPTL4 as strong putative candidate pairs involved in CAD risk. Pharmacological repositioning and tissue-specific protein expression analyses have highlighted 15 possible targets for follow-up investigations, a subset of which is specifically expressed in the liver.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrative analyses presented here provide evidence for the involvement of 29 blood proteins in CAD. Those candidate proteins take part directly or through pleiotropic effects in functions pertaining to cell migration-differentiation, inflammation and metabolism.

articles.title: Lysine degradation-related metabolic remodeling in sarcopenia: Mendelian randomization prioritization and multi-omics-based characterization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Previous metabolomic studies have implicated mitochondrial energy metabolism, lipid remodeling, and carnitine-related pathways in sarcopenia, but broader metabolic pathways linking these abnormalities remain unclear. We aimed to identify sarcopenia-related metabolic pathways by integrating metabolome-wide Mendelian Randomization (MR) with patient-derived serum and skeletal muscle multi-omics analysis.

METHODS: Two-sample MR analyses were performed using genome-wide association study summary statistics for 1400 circulating metabolite-related traits and three sarcopenia-related traits, appendicular lean mass (ALM), handgrip strength, and walking speed. Candidate metabolites retained after MR sensitivity filtering were subjected to Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG)-based pathway enrichment. The MR-prioritized pathway was then examined in an independent cohort of 40 postmenopausal women with or without sarcopenia using untargeted serum and skeletal muscle metabolomics. Patient-derived and the external public skeletal muscle transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to evaluate pathway-related transcriptomic patterns.

RESULTS: Lysine degradation was the only pathway meeting the predefined pathway-level FDR criterion in the ALM-negative direction. Lysine, carnitine, and N6,N6,N6-trimethyllysine contributed nominal negative MR associations to this pathway. Colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared causal signal for one carnitine locus (rs1171617; PP.H4 = 0.995). In the validation cohort, nine lysine degradation-related metabolites detected in serum and skeletal muscle were grouped according to three biochemical processes: free lysine oxidation, methyllysine turnover, and trimethyllysine-derived carnitine biosynthesis. In serum, dl-lysine was nominally higher (log2FC = 0.796, P = 0.047) and dl-carnitine was nominally lower (log2FC = -0.130, P = 0.047) in sarcopenia, while the trimethyllysine-derived carnitine biosynthesis score was significantly lower (adjusted P < 0.001). In skeletal muscle, γ-butyrobetaine (log2FC = 1.178, P = 0.029) and N-acetyl-L-2-aminoadipic acid (log2FC = 2.240, P = 0.035) were nominally higher in sarcopenia, whereas none of the three biochemical group scores differed significantly between groups. Patient-derived skeletal muscle transcriptomics were evaluated using predefined Reactome pathways for lysine catabolism and carnitine synthesis; the carnitine synthesis pathway score was lower in sarcopenia (P = 0.049), with significant downregulation of TMLHE (log2FC = -0.411, adjusted P = 0.023) and DLD (log2FC = -0.468, adjusted P = 0.004). In the external skeletal muscle dataset, TMLHE and DLD showed concordant decreases at nominal significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Lysine degradation was prioritized as an ALM-related metabolic pathway through exploratory MR-based pathway analysis. Multi-omics characterization indicated heterogeneous and compartment-specific remodeling rather than uniform alteration of the entire pathway, with the most coherent cross-omics pattern involving trimethyllysine-derived carnitine metabolism. These findings support lysine-related metabolism as a candidate metabolic framework for sarcopenia while warranting further mechanistic and longitudinal validation.

articles.title: Nationwide trends of six medications for alcohol use disorder prescriptions post-discharge in patients hospitalized with alcohol-associated liver disease between 2015 and 2024.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol associated liver disease (ALD) carries a high risk of hospitalization and recidivism, yet post-discharge medications for alcohol use disorder (MAUD) are not universally prescribed. MAUD prescriptions have been associated with reduced recidivism and hepatic decompensation. However, national data on prescribing patterns is limited. We examined ten-year trends in six MAUD prescriptions after hospitalization for ALD.

METHODS: We identified 150,241 US adults hospitalized with ALD between 2015 and 2024 using electronic health records from TriNetX. Outcomes included annual prevalence, incidence rate, and incidence proportion of post-discharge MAUD prescriptions. FDA-approved agents included disulfiram, acamprosate, and naltrexone; off-label agents included topiramate, baclofen, and gabapentin. Trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression with annual percentage change (APC) and average annual percentage change (AAPC). Subgroup analyses were stratified by cirrhosis status and sex.

RESULTS: FDA-approved MAUD had consistently lower prescription rates than off-label agents over the past decade. From 2015-2024, disulfiram was the only FDA-approved agent with a declining trend, while acamprosate (AAPC 20.35%) and naltrexone (AAPC 17.83%) demonstrated significant increases for new prescriptions. By 2024, the prevalence of FDA-approved and off-label MAUD prescriptions were 17.98% and 41.96%, respectively. Patients with cirrhosis had lower prescribing rates but exhibited greater relative increases in FDA-approved MAUD prescriptions. Women were more likely to receive off-label prescriptions, though both sexes showed similar upward trends.

CONCLUSION: Post-discharge MAUD prescribing for ALD has risen significantly, but less than 20% of patients receive FDA-approved MAUD. Expanding access to evidence-based medications is critical to improve outcomes in this high-risk population.

articles.title: 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and pregnancy : Statement of endorsement by the NVVC.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: This article contextualises the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines for managing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and pregnancy in the Netherlands. The guideline addendum provides additional recommendations for situations where the ESC guidelines may not fully align with Dutch clinical practice. By endorsing the ESC guidelines through this addendum, the Netherlands Society of Cardiology (Nederlandse Vereniging Voor Cardiologie) supports its members in adhering to evidence-based management strategies for CVD and pregnancy.

articles.title: [Invasive intracoronary imaging : Role in routine cardiology].
articles.abstract: Intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, provides detailed insights into plaque morphology and facilitates the precise planning and guidance of percutaneous coronary interventions, especially in patients with complex coronary lesions. Based on the results of multiple randomized clinical trials, current clinical guidelines recommend the use of intracoronary imaging for the treatment of complex coronary lesions. However, the appropriate application of both imaging modalities requires a thorough understanding of their technical principles, as well as their respective strengths and limitations. This article therefore reviews the technical fundamentals of optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, illustrates their clinical application through selected case examples, and summarizes the current evidence supporting their use.

articles.title: Hepatocyte senescence in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a major global health challenge, with particularly high morbidity and disease burden. Cellular senescence has been identified as one of the core mechanisms driving the onset and progression of MASLD. Hepatocytes, the primary functional cells of the liver, can undergo a senescent state under metabolic stress. These senescent hepatocytes secrete a series of pro-inflammatory and profibrotic factors, directly exacerbating hepatic inflammation and activating hepatic stellate cells, thereby leading to pathological fibrosis. The purpose of this review is to explore the key molecular pathways of hepatocyte senescence and their impact on MASLD progression. Finally, we discuss relevant intervention strategies that can be used for the prevention and treatment of MASLD.

articles.title: Lower circulating angiotensinogen levels across ACLD stages are associated with hepatic dysfunction and mortality.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The liver produces angiotensinogen (AGT), the key upstream precursor of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). We measured AGT levels in patients across distinct advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) stages and investigated the impact of AGT levels on clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We included clinically stable ACLD outpatients undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement between May 2018 and October 2023, as well as healthy controls (HCs) recruited in the prospective Vienna Cirrhosis Study (VICIS; NCT03267615). AGT was assessed by converting it to angiotensin I (Ang I) through incubation with excess recombinant human renin. RAS parameters were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Patients were stratified as compensated (cACLD), single decompensated (sdACLD), or further decompensated ACLD (fdACLD).

RESULTS: Overall, 60 individuals (cACLD: n=16; sdACLD: n=22; fdACLD: n=12; HC: n=10) were included. AGT levels decreased significantly compared with HC and with increasing ACLD severity (HC: 943.2 vs. cACLD: 550.4 vs. sdACLD: 476.9 vs. fdACLD: 439.8 nmol/L; p<0.001). In contrast, plasma concentrations of Ang II (cACLD: 23.1 vs. sdACLD: 156.0 vs. fdACLD: 162.4 pmol/L; p=0.002) and Ang 1-7 (cACLD: 3.0 vs. sdACLD: 3.2 vs. fdACLD: 8.5 pmol/L; p=0.022) increased significantly with ACLD severity. AGT did not correlate with Ang II (ρ=-0.23; p=0.101), but with Ang 1-7 (ρ=0.32; p=0.022) and MELD-Na (ρ=-0.29; p=0.042). Exploratory survival analyses, limited by the small sample size, showed that lower AGT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted for age and MELD-Na: asHR: 1.59; 95% CI: 1.09-2.27; p=0.012/adjusted for age and albumin: asHR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.05-2.21; p=0.026).

CONCLUSIONS: AGT levels decreased in ACLD, correlated with hepatic dysfunction, and were linked to all-cause mortality in exploratory survival analyses. Still, classical and alternative RAS parameters increased in parallel to ACLD severity.

articles.title: Patient-reported and caregiver-reported outcomes in refractory ascites secondary to cirrhosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refractory ascites (RA) secondary to advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) results in poor health-related quality of life (HRQL), high symptom burden, and caregiver workload. Patient/caregiver-reported outcomes (PROs) remain uncharacterized in this cohort. This review summarises the available evidence on this topic.

METHODS: MEDLINE/Embase/Cochrane/PsycINFO/Web of Science/CINAHL were searched for articles that included PROs in RA secondary to ACLD. A structured narrative synthesis and a meta-analysis were undertaken.

RESULTS: Sixteen articles were included, comprising 1040 patients and 47 caregivers. Fourteen PRO measures were used, most commonly the Short Form-36 (SF-36) and the Chronic Liver Disease Questionnaire (CLDQ). Domain scores were pooled from 4 SF-36 and 3 CLDQ studies. Pooled domain scores were lower than those reported in stable outpatients with cirrhosis in 3/8 SF-36 domains: Social functioning (mean difference -18.8 [95% CI: -30.2 to -7.3]), Mental health (-17.9 [-33.5 to -2.3]), and Physical functioning (-13.6 [-24.5 to -2.7]); and 4/6 CLDQ domains: Abdominal symptoms (-1.5 [-2.3 to -0.7]), Activity (-0.9 [-1.4 to -0.5]), Worry (-1.2 [-2.1 to -0.3]), and Emotional function (-0.7 [-1.3 to -0.1]). Disease-specific tools had broader domain coverage and were more sensitive at picking up impairments in HRQL compared with generic ones. One symptom tool (the Ascites Questionnaire) had been validated in RA. The Short-Form Liver Disease Quality of Life questionnaire (SFLDQoL), the only HRQL measure validated in decompensated ACLD, was used once. Only 2 studies assessed informal caregivers.

CONCLUSIONS: RA in ACLD detrimentally impacts HRQL across multiple domains. However, the lack of validated tools remains a barrier to assessing PROs and conducting well-designed RCTs in this cohort. This review highlights potential domains for the future development of such tools, which could drive equitable, patient-centered care in ACLD.

articles.title: Clinical and patient-reported predictors of days alive and out of hospital in decompensated cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Days alive and out of hospital (DAOH) is a patient-centered outcome, but has not been studied in decompensated cirrhosis (DCC). We aimed to quantify DAOH and to identify clinical and patient-reported factors associated with DAOH.

METHODS: Using an ongoing prospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with DCC, DAOH was calculated by subtracting days hospitalized, transplanted, or deceased from 90 days post-discharge from index hospitalization. Univariable and multivariable negative binomial hurdle models were used to identify clinical and patient-reported variables associated with DAOH, where DAOH was treated both as a categorical (any readmission, transplant, death vs. all 90-DAOH) and continuous (proportion of event days) outcome.

RESULTS: Among 363 adults (median age 54 y; MELD 3.0 score 23), 40% experienced all 90-DAOH while 90-day readmission, death, and transplant occurred in 49%, 21%, 11%, respectively. Mean DAOH was 68.3 (SD: 29.0). In multivariable models, transplant evaluation status (listed vs. not listed/evaluated: OR 7.55, p=0.004) was associated with experiencing an event within 90 days. In comparison, when considering the number of event days, higher PROMIS Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities scores were independently associated with a lower proportion of event days (rate ratio, RR 0.91 per 3-point increase, p=0.030) in addition to MELD 3.0 >25 (vs. <15, RR 2.75, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DAOH is a holistic, patient-centered outcome for decompensated cirrhosis that integrates readmission, transplantation, and mortality into a single measure of post-discharge burden. By using DAOH and moving beyond readmissions, we show that lower MELD 3.0 and higher patient-reported social well-being were independently associated with more days at home after hospitalization.

articles.title: Impact of body composition on clinical outcomes in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormalities in body composition are common in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, their impact across different treatment modalities remains poorly understood. We systematically reviewed the prognostic value of body composition in patients with HCC, stratified by curative, locoregional, and systemic therapies.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (January 2015-March 2025) for studies reporting associations between CT/MRI or bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-assessed body composition and outcomes in HCC.

RESULTS: Ninety-two studies were included (35 curative, 10 locoregional, 39 systemic, 8 mixed). Sarcopenia prevalence ranged from 6.4% to 62.8% (median study-level prevalence 38%-50% depending on treatment stratum). Sarcopenia independently predicted worse overall survival across all strata: curative (HR 1.52-3.76), locoregional (HR 1.72-2.51), and systemic therapies (HR 1.34-2.20). Sarcopenic obesity conferred the highest risk in the curative setting (HR up to 3.15). In systemic therapy, myosteatosis independently predicted mortality (HR 1.45-2.01), whereas visceral adiposity was protective (HR 0.56-0.66). In a random-effects meta-analysis of 44 studies, sarcopenia was associated with a pooled HR of 1.85 (95% CI 1.75-1.94; I2=0%), with consistent effects across curative (HR 1.86), locoregional (HR 2.10), and systemic strata (HR 1.71). Sarcopenia also predicted recurrence after curative treatment (pooled HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.61-1.82; k=14).

CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia predicts mortality in HCC, independently of treatment modality. Visceral adiposity appears detrimental after curative treatment but may be paradoxically protective during systemic therapy. Body composition should be integrated into clinical decision-making in HCC, though a clear consensus on measurement standardization is needed.

articles.title: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms.
authors: American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists' Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines–Gynecology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms related to spontaneous menopause and induced menopause (at or beyond age 40 years).

TARGET POPULATION: Perimenopausal and postmenopausal individuals assigned female sex at birth (ie, women, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals) with vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms related to spontaneous or induced menopause.

METHODS: This guideline was developed using an a priori protocol in conjunction with a writing team consisting of a subspecialist in reproductive endocrinology and infertility, a Menopause Society Certified Practitioner and subspecialist in reproductive endocrinology and infertility, and a specialist in obstetrics and gynecology. Studies that moved forward to the full-text screening stage were assessed by two authors from the writing team based on standardized inclusion and exclusion criteria. Included studies underwent quality assessment, and a modified GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) evidence-to-decision framework was applied to interpret and translate the evidence into recommendation statements.

RECOMMENDATIONS: This Clinical Practice Guideline includes recommendations on pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions for the management of menopause-related vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms. Recommendations are classified by strength and evidence quality. Ungraded Good Practice Points are included to provide clinical guidance when a formal recommendation could not be made because of inadequate or nonexistent evidence.

articles.title: The durability of different anchoring points and anchoring types in the left ventricle in an ex vivo porcine model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Surgical mitral valve repair, including anchoring in different parts of the mitral apparatus, is the standard of care for severe mitral regurgitation. Various percutaneous approaches have been developed and are currently under development, but are struggling with durable results. This study investigates the durability of different anatomic anchoring points and anchoring types in the left ventricle.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Anchoring was tested with PTFE sutures or a 5 mm helix at three locations: the head of the papillary muscle, the lateral wall of the ventricle, and the apex of the ventricle. An accelerated life test was performed with 300 cycles at 3 N for each anchoring. Durability was assessed by measuring compliance (strain in mm until 3 N is reached), migration (change in strain from the first to the last cycle), and the occurrence of dehiscence.

RESULTS: The lowest numerical strain/compliance in the first cycle was observed at the head of the papillary muscle anchoring (both surgical and helix). Migration of strain limits over 300 cycles was seen for all locations. The lowest migration was numerically for helix in the papillary muscle.

CONCLUSION: PTFE in the head of the papillary muscle is standard practice in mitral valve repair and was used as a reference in the present study. The anchoring that yielded the most similar results was a helix in the papillary muscle, whereas other anchoring points showed greater compliance and/or migration.

articles.title: Health Literacy and Communication in Stroke Prevention, Management, and Recovery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Council Stroke and Neurovascular Nursing Science Committee of the Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Stroke Council
articles.abstract: Health literacy is a critical component of high-quality stroke care. Across the continuum from prevention through recovery, health literacy is strongly associated with functional outcomes and stroke-related morbidity. Despite its importance, it is often overlooked, leaving patients and caregivers overwhelmed by communication demands that exceed their capacity. These mismatches are especially pronounced among individuals with stroke-related cognitive or language impairments, limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantage, or limited digital literacy. This scientific statement synthesizes current evidence on the role of health literacy and communication within stroke systems of care and identifies nurse-led opportunities to advance equity and patient-centered outcomes while recognizing this as a shared interprofessional responsibility. Nurse-led interventions, including teach-back-based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support, have demonstrated improvements in stroke knowledge, self-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness. However, the literature is marked by methodological heterogeneity. Many studies are underpowered and infrequently use validated health literacy or communication measures. Future directions include standardized assessment of health literacy; literacy-sensitive, nurse-led, and interprofessional care models; workforce training in plain-language and culturally responsive communication; and organizational health literacy principles. Emerging technologies, including telehealth and artificial intelligence, offer promise for improving communication and personalization but require rigorous evaluation to minimize bias and ensure equity and usability.

articles.title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients.
articles.abstract: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 59.2% and 72.1% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.

articles.title: Evidence on Glutathione and Boosters for Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) adversely affects treatment efficacy and quality of life. Despite studies on glutathione (GSH) or GSH boosters' antioxidative effects for prevention, optimal management remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to consolidate and critically appraise the current evidence and to compare the efficacy of GSH and GSH boosters for the prevention of CIPN. The MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL databases were searched through March 2025. Twenty-five RCTs involving 1625 patients were included. No intervention significantly reduced all-grade CIPN compared with placebo. N-acetylcysteine (odds ratio [OR] 0.19, 95% credible intervals [CrI] 0.05-0.63), GSH (OR 0.34, 95% CrI 0.13-0.79) and vitamin E (OR 0.33, 95% CrI 0.11-0.91) were associated with a reduced incidence of grade 3/4 CIPN compared with placebo. N-acetylcysteine ranked highest for both all-grade and grade 3/4 CIPN prevention. These findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with pre-existing neuropathy but were not retained in analyses restricted to double-blind studies. Overall, N-acetylcysteine, GSH, and vitamin E were associated with potential reductions in severe CIPN, with N-acetylcysteine consistently ranking highest, although these associations should be regarded as preliminary. Further rigorously conducted and adequately powered trials are warranted to confirm these findings and evaluate agents demonstrating potential benefits.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Clinical Prediction Rule to Identify Preoperatively Patients With Acute Refractory Pain After Lumbar Spine Surgery.
articles.journal: Pain practice : the official journal of World Institute of Pain
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative risk stratification to identify patients who develop acute refractory pain after lumbar spine surgery is a first step to prevent unfavorable outcomes. In this study, we aimed to develop and internally validate a clinically relevant, multidimensional prediction rule for preoperative risk assessment.

METHODS: This is a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data conducted at an orthopedic hospital specialized in spine care. Baseline and outcome data on patients who underwent lumbar spine surgery between July 2012 and December 2022 were included in this study. 105 factors were considered as potential predictive factors for acute refractory pain after lumbar spine surgery. Multivariable logistic lasso regression analysis and multivariable logistic regression analysis were performed to develop a prediction model. Performance measures (ROC-AUC and Nagelkerke's R2) and a prediction rule for clinical use were presented.

RESULTS: Data on 1156 patients was included in this analysis. The prevalence of patients developing acute refractory pain was 19.6% (n = 228/1156). Multivariable logistic lasso regression identified 13 relevant predictive factors for acute refractory pain after lumbar spine surgery: age, prior hospital treatment for back pain, professional sports participation, duration of back pain, back pain before age 45, numeric pain rating scale for back pain, preoperative opioid use, circumferent surgery, instrumented surgery, anxiety, catastrophizing, return-to-work attitude, high score for psychosocial burden of low back pain. Five of these were selected by logistic regression. The discriminative ability of the multivariable logistic lasso regression model was ROC-AUC of 0.69 (95% CI 0.66-0.73), and the multivariable logistic regression model 0.67 (95% CI 0.63-0.71). Nagelkerke's R2 of the logistic regression model was 8.4%.

CONCLUSION: Multidimensional predictive factors for acute refractory pain were identified using a clinical prediction rule. This rule creates a patient profile which can help anesthesiologists to preoperatively determine the individual risk for developing acute refractory pain despite the use of a standardized multimodal analgesic treatment.

articles.title: Radial Tiny Golden Angle UTE (tyGA-UTE) for Cardiac MRI in the Small Animal Model.
articles.abstract: Robust cardiorespiratory motion correction is critical for high-quality ultra-high-field (UHF) preclinical cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Whereas radial tiny golden angle (tyGA) sampling, data-driven self-gating (sg), compressed sensing (CS), and ultrashort echo time (UTE) are individually well-established techniques, their integration into a unified acquisition and reconstruction pipeline, together with systematic validation at 11.7 T remains insufficiently explored. This study presents and validates a UHF-optimized tyGA-based UTE workflow that enables high-temporal-resolution sliding-window dynamic imaging (SW-tyGA-UTE) and high-spatial-resolution cardiorespiratory self-gated cine imaging (Gated-tyGA-UTE) from a single continuous acquired tyGA acquisition. All experiments were performed on an 11.7-T small-animal MRI system in 16 healthy wild-type mice. Cardiac functional parameters, image quality metrics (signal-to-noise ratio [SNR] and contrast-to-noise ratio [CNR]), and inter-/intra-observer reproducibility were systematically compared between the proposed tyGA-UTE pipeline and two navigator-gated reference techniques: retrospectively gated FLASH and UTE methodologies. SW-tyGA-UTE and Gated-tyGA-UTE reconstructions yielded global left ventricular functional parameters comparable to those obtained with the reference methods (all p > 0.05). All functional metrics showed excellent intra-observer (ICC = 0.94-0.99) and inter-observer (ICC = 0.90-0.98) reproducibility, with ejection fraction showing the highest measurement consistency. Image quality was evaluated using an image-based within-ROI noise quantification approach that captures both thermal noise and reconstruction-related artifacts. In this analysis, the Gated-tyGA-UTE protocol showed no statistically significant differences in left ventricular blood-pool SNR, myocardial SNR, or CNR relative to the reference sequences. In contrast, the high-temporal-resolution sliding-window reconstruction showed significantly reduced image quality across all three metrics, consistent with the expected spatiotemporal trade-off of undersampled dynamic imaging. This study validates a robust, UHF-optimized tyGA-UTE imaging workflow that generates both high-fidelity quantitative cine data and ultra-fast dynamic cardiac images from a single acquisition. The unified pipeline eliminates the need for sequential repeated scans, minimizes anesthesia-related physiological variability, and improves experimental efficiency, providing a practical tool for preclinical cardiac phenotyping, longitudinal studies, and drug screening.

articles.title: Dynamic edge-event-based consensus of nonlinear multi-agent systems with sampled-data measurement.
articles.abstract: This paper investigates the leader-following consensus problem for a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) by developing a novel edge-event-triggered control framework. To alleviate communication burdens, an edge-based triggering strategy is employed, wherein both the control protocols and triggering conditions depend exclusively on local relative information, eliminating the reliance on global network knowledge. Recognizing the constraints of practical communication scenarios, asynchronous information interactions across different edges are explicitly considered. As a core contribution, we seamlessly integrate sampled-data measurements with the edge-triggering paradigm, proposing a sampled-data edge-event triggered mechanism. This framework fundamentally circumvents the stringent requirement of continuous state monitoring and intrinsically excludes Zeno behavior, thereby significantly saving computational and communication resources. Furthermore, the framework is extended to a dynamic sampled-data-based edge-event-triggered mechanism, which introduces an auxiliary variable to provide greater flexibility in communication scheduling. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed methods are demonstrated through an application example and comparative simulations.

articles.title: Interventions to Support Parents Whose Babies Cry Excessively: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Parents report that around 10% to 20% of babies cry a lot without an apparent reason during early infancy. This "excessive" infant crying can lead to adverse outcomes, including parental depression, breastfeeding cessation, impaired parent-child relationships, and, in extreme cases, infant abuse. Cost-effective parent-support services are needed.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of interventions designed to support parents of excessively crying babies.

DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, Embase, EconLit, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, CINAHL and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 8th April 2025. The NIHR CRN database and handsearching were used to identify further studies.

STUDY SELECTION: Comparative studies reporting parental outcomes for any intervention supporting parents of excessively crying infants aged ≤1 year were included.

DATA EXTRACTION: Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and assessed risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed when possible; otherwise, narrative synthesis was conducted.

RESULTS: Meta-analysis found that educational interventions significantly reduced parental stress or anxiety. Narrative analyses produced mixed findings, but components common to successful educational interventions were indicated. Meta-analyses of studies administering probiotics to infants found significant improvements in parents' quality of life but not in parental depression. No safety data and limited economic evidence were found.

LIMITATIONS: Few studies measured similar enough parental outcomes to be pooled in meta-analysis. Risk of bias ranged from unclear to high risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Educational and probiotic interventions show promise for supporting parents of excessively crying babies. Additional controlled trials employing evidence-based interventions and outcome measures and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed to build on these findings.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of delpacibart zotadirsen in Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations amenable to exon 44 skipping in the USA (EXPLORE44): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 1/2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are no approved exon skipping therapies to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy due to DMD variants amenable to exon 44 skipping (DMD44). Delpacibart zotadirsen (del-zota, also known as AOC 1044) is a first-in-class antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate designed to deliver an exon 44-skipping phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer to muscle to restore dystrophin expression for individuals with DMD44. EXPLORE44 was a first-in-human trial to evaluate del-zota's safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy.

METHODS: EXPLORE44 was a two-part randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 1/2 study in healthy adult men (aged 18-55 years; part A) and ambulatory and non-ambulatory male participants with DMD44 (aged 7-27 years; part B) at ten clinical research sites in the USA. Dosing in part B was informed by safety, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic data from part A. In part B, participants with DMD44 were randomised (3:1 del-zota:placebo) within two dose cohorts to receive three intravenous doses of del-zota (5 mg/kg every 6 weeks, or 10 mg/kg every 8 weeks) or matching placebo. A computer-generated permuted-block randomisation schedule was prepared by an independent statistician with no further role in the study. Infusions were prepared by an unmasked pharmacist under supervision of the masked investigator; other site staff, participants, and sponsor team members were masked to allocation. The primary objective was safety and tolerability measured by the incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events. Secondary endpoints assessing target engagement were change from baseline in exon skipping (ie, defined as the percentage of dystrophin mRNA transcripts in which exon 44 is excluded from the mature mRNA relative to total dystrophin mRNA transcripts) and dystrophin level to month 4 (5 mg/kg cohort) or month 5 (10 mg/kg cohort). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05670730) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between Dec 5, 2022, and June 27, 2024, we enrolled and randomly assigned 45 healthy volunteers and 26 men and boys with DMD44. In part A, three (30%) of ten healthy volunteers who received placebo and 21 (62%) of 34 who received del-zota reported at least one adverse event, none of which were severe or serious. In part B, nine participants with DMD44 received del-zota at 5 mg/kg, ten at 10 mg/kg, and seven received placebo; mean age 13·3 years (SD 4·2). 16 (84%) participants with DMD44 treated with del-zota and six (86%) treated with placebo reported at least one adverse event, most of which were mild or moderate; two participants, both in the 5 mg/kg del-zota group, discontinued due to adverse events (anaphylactic reaction and infusion-related reaction). Mean increases from baseline in exon 44 skipping were 36·6% (95% CI 20·8 to 52·4, SD 17·1, nominal p=0·0013) at 5 mg/kg, 43·4% (32·8 to 54·0, 14·9, nominal p<0·0001) at 10 mg/kg, and 1·6% (-3·4 to 6·7, 4·8, nominal p=0·44) with placebo. Mean increases from baseline in dystrophin levels were 25·0% (9·2 to 40·7, 17·0, nominal p=0·0082) at 5 mg/kg, 25·6% (13·0 to 38·3, 17·7, nominal p=0·0013) at 10 mg/kg, and -0·7% (-4·8 to 3·3, 3·9, nominal p=0·66) with placebo.

INTERPRETATION: Del-zota had an acceptable safety profile, produced increases in exon 44 skipping and dystrophin expression, and decreased biomarkers of muscle damage in participants with DMD44. Findings from this study support further investigation of del-zota in a phase 3 study to assess efficacy and long-term safety.

FUNDING: Avidity Biosciences, A Novartis Company.

articles.title: Climate change: aggravation and adaptation in neurology.
Antibody-mediated encephalitides: distinct diseases with transdisciplinary implications.
articles.abstract: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. Antibody-mediated disorders targeting glial aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein are distinct nosological entities, defined by specific targets, mechanisms, syndromes, and therapeutic implications. By contrast, antibody-mediated disorders targeting neuronal antigens (ie, autoimmune encephalitides) are still frequently analysed collectively, with data from different disorders pooled as if they represent a single disease rather than distinct entities. Evidence from anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and anti-IgLON5 disease (used here as exemplars of autoimmune encephalitides) indicates that individual autoimmune encephalitides differ in demographics, triggers, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, post-acute trajectories, and treatment requirements. The broad, heterogeneous presentations of autoimmune encephalitides require coordinated multidisciplinary care within and beyond neurology, involving specialists in paediatrics, infectious diseases, epilepsy, movement disorders, sleep medicine, intensive care, cognitive rehabilitation, and other relevant disciplines. Such interdisciplinary collaboration facilitates the recognition of new diseases and elucidation of the causes of previously unclassified disorders. Improving patient care requires not only aetiological and mechanistic insight to enable development of targeted therapies but also strengthened cross-specialty expertise to optimise diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Reframing traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury as chronic multisystem disorders: toward integrated, long-term care.
authors: Global Coalition for TBI as a Notifiable and Chronic Condition
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. However, most health systems still treat neurotrauma (TBI and SCI, collectively) as a time-limited event, leaving long-term surveillance of these patients fragmented or absent, which leads to preventable mortality and avoidable readmissions. TBI and SCI in adults should be reclassified as acute-onset multisystem chronic-risk conditions. Existing cardiovascular, endocrine, and psychiatric services do not capture neurotrauma-specific risks, including trauma-induced hypopituitarism, autonomic dysregulation, accelerated ageing, and cognitive-behavioural impairment, so neurotrauma care is best framed as a missing node in chronic neurological care. We propose a risk-stratified pathway of care navigation, multisystem screening, and telehealth; convergence with adjacent stroke, cardiometabolic, memory, psychiatric, pain, and epilepsy services; and the financing, workforce, and registry reforms needed to deliver measurable reductions in 5-year mortality, avoidable rehospitalisation, and long-term disability.

articles.title: Long-term health, criminal justice, and socioeconomic outcomes among people subject to compulsory mental health care in Norway: a nationwide registry cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Compulsory mental health care aims to manage risk and treatment needs among people with severe mental illness, but evidence on long-term outcomes across health, justice, and socioeconomic domains is scarce. We aimed to compare long-term outcomes across adult groups defined by community treatment orders (CTOs), compulsory hospitalisation, compulsory observation, and voluntary mental health care, and the general population.

METHODS: In this nationwide registry cohort study, we identified all individuals aged 18-65 years with specialist mental health-care contact in Norway from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2016 and general population comparators sampled via Statistics Norway based on age and sex. Follow-up was through 2021-23, depending on registry availability. Study groups were defined hierarchically: CTO, compulsory hospitalisation without CTO, compulsory observation without compulsory hospitalisation or CTO, voluntary mental health care, and no specialist mental health-care contact (ie, the general population). Outcomes included mortality and cause of death, self-harm treated in emergency departments or hospital, substance use disorder, victimisation, violent or sexual offence charges or imprisonment, subsequent compulsory care, acute admissions, and socioeconomic outcomes. Data for all groups were sourced from linked nationwide registries. Separate binomial regressions estimated sex-specific probabilities by group, adjusting for birth year. People with lived experience of mental health services advised study design and interpretation.

FINDINGS: The final study sample comprised 321 708 individuals (mean age 36·5 years, range 18-65) across five mutually exclusive groups: CTO (n=3331), compulsory hospitalisation (n=2907), compulsory observation (n=2554), voluntary care (n=177 396), and general population (n=135 520), 193 473 (60·1%) were female and 128 235 (39·9%) were male; ethnicity data were unavailable. Compulsory care groups were associated with substantially worse long-term outcomes across health, criminal justice, and socioeconomic domains than voluntary patients and the general population. Across compulsory care groups, female participants had higher adjusted probabilities of self-harm or suicide than male participants, whereas male participants had higher adjusted probabilities of substance use disorder and of being charged with or imprisoned for violent or sexual offences compared with female participants. The compulsory observation group had the highest adjusted probabilities of self-harm or suicide and substance use disorder across the five groups. Self-harm or suicide was recorded in 135 (12·1%) of 1115 female participants (adjusted probability 12% [95% CI 10-14]) and 75 (5·7%) of 1308 male participants (5·5% [4·4-6·9]). Substance use disorder was recorded in 407 (39·1%) of 1041 female participants (39% [36-42]) and 639 (53·2%) of 1202 male participants (53% [50-56]). Charges or imprisonment for violent or sexual offences were recorded in 146 (14·2%) of 1030 female participants (14% [12-16]) and 446 (37·4% [34-40]) of 1194 male participants. During 2015-21, including the inclusion period, suicide and other external causes accounted for 132 (55·7%) of 237 classified deaths in compulsory observation, compared with 1818 (38·2%) of 4754 in voluntary care and 174 (18·6%) of 938 in the general population. The CTO group had the highest adjusted probability of disability benefit receipt: 89% (95% CI 87-91) in female participants and 93% (92-94) in male participants; a substantial minority of disability-benefit recipients in the CTO group also had earned income.

INTERPRETATION: Compulsory care groups were associated with distinct long-term prognoses from the voluntary care and general population groups. These findings provide population-level benchmarks for service planning and policy evaluation and show that legally defined compulsory care groups should not be treated as a single prognostic population.

FUNDING: Research Council of Norway.

articles.title: Association of beta-blocker therapy with outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction stratified by GRACE risk score: A nationwide registry analysis.
authors: Korea Acute Myocardial Infarction Registry (KAMIR) Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between beta-blocker use following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and clinical outcomes remain uncertain in the contemporary era of near-universal early revascularization and drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly for patients with preserved left ventricular function. We sought to determine whether associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied across Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) risk strata.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of 11,866 STEMI survivors from two prospective nationwide Korean registries who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with second-generation DES. Patients were categorized by beta-blocker prescription at discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at one year; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability treatment weighting were employed to mitigate confounding. Variation in associations was examined across the continuous GRACE risk spectrum, categorized into low-risk (GRACE <85), intermediate-risk (GRACE 85-179), and high-risk (GRACE ≥180) strata.

RESULTS: Beta-blockers were prescribed to 83.8% of the cohort. After propensity matching, beta-blocker use was associated with lower one-year all-cause mortality (2.7% vs. 4.2%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.91) and MACE (6.0% vs. 8.3%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.55-0.92).
