These associations attenuated by three years. The GRACE 2.0 score exhibited robust discrimination for mortality (AUC = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.76-0.82). Continuous interaction analyses showed small model-estimated absolute risk differences in low-risk patients (GRACE <85), whereas the largest model-estimated absolute risk difference was observed in intermediate-risk individuals (GRACE 85-179).

CONCLUSIONS: Among STEMI survivors treated with contemporary PCI, associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied according to baseline GRACE risk. No statistically significant association was observed in low-risk individuals (GRACE <85), whereas the association with lower mortality was most evident in the intermediate-risk group (GRACE 85-179). These hypothesis-generating findings warrant evaluation in randomized trials before being used to guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Efficacy of Inhaled Methoxyflurane for Acute Trauma Pain Management: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute traumatic pain is common in emergency settings and inadequate analgesia can worsen physiological, psychological, and functional outcomes.

STUDY OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy, onset of action, safety, and clinical practicality of inhaled methoxyflurane compared with control analgesic treatments for acute trauma-related pain.

METHODS: Four databases were searched from inception through February 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating inhaled methoxyflurane for acute traumatic pain were eligible. Outcomes included visual analogue scale and numerical rating scale pain scores, rescue analgesia, time to first pain relief, and adverse events (AEs). Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and RevMan was used for quantitative synthesis.

RESULTS: Seven studies involving 1585 participants were analyzed. Methoxyflurane significantly reduced the time to first pain relief compared with controls (mean difference -5.93 min, 95% confidence interval [CI] -6.86 to -5.00, p < 0.00001, I2 = 0%). Pain intensity also favored methoxyflurane at 5, 10, 15, and 20 min. Methoxyflurane also significantly reduced the need for rescue analgesia (risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.90, p = 0.03). Overall AEs were comparable, but dizziness, drowsiness, and cough were more frequent with methoxyflurane.

CONCLUSION: Inhaled methoxyflurane provides rapid and effective analgesia for acute traumatic pain and may reduce rescue analgesia needs. Further high-quality randomized trials are needed to clarify comparative effectiveness across trauma populations and emergency care settings.

articles.title: Association Between Neuropsychological Test Performance and Neuroimaging Findings in Cognitive Impairment: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Psychogeriatrics : the official journal of the Japanese Psychogeriatric Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) provide different information about cognitive impairment, but the additional contribution of FDG-PET beyond MRI across cognitive outcomes remains unclear. This study examined associations between neuropsychological performance and MRI/FDG-PET findings.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 200 patients with mild cognitive impairment or dementia. Neuropsychological assessment covered global cognition and memory, executive, visuospatial and language domains. Structural MRI was evaluated using the Modified Visual Magnetic Resonance Rating Scale; FDG-PET data were available for 68 patients. MRI-only, FDG-PET-only and combined models were compared.

RESULTS: Structural MRI abnormalities showed broad associations with global and domain-level cognitive performance. Sulcal and ventricular atrophy were associated with multiple cognitive domains, while regional FDG-PET findings aligned with corresponding domains. The additional contribution of FDG-PET beyond MRI appeared most evident for global cognition, more modest for executive performance and limited for several other outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Structural MRI showed broad multidomain associations, while regional FDG-PET findings corresponded to cognitive performance. The additional explanatory contribution of FDG-PET appeared to vary across cognitive outcomes, warranting cautious interpretation and further evaluation.

articles.title: Shock Synopsis November 2026.
The Scaleup Costs, Size, and Statistics Challenge to Democratic Deliberation on Health Policy.
articles.abstract: Current fashion supports aligning health policy with the recommendations of deliberative forums, or mini-publics. These forums' participants are selected randomly from the general public (sometimes with overrepresentation of direct stakeholders or of underrepresented sectors). After being informed and exchanging public reasons with fellow participants under discursive rules that engage all as equals, participants vote on and sometimes rank policy recommendations. According to supporters, a deliberative democratic process that holds such forums and translates their recommendations to policy legitimizes resulting policy. That's thanks to this process's tendencies to strengthen democratic consent, to uncover which policy option is objectively best, to align policy with lay normative outlooks, and to educate the public. I argue that one tri-partite feature of nearly all instances of democratic deliberation on regional, national, and global health policy under current best practice, which I call the "Scaleup costs, Size, and Statistics" ("3S") challenge, largely blocks these alleged welcome tendencies. In particular, barring radical changes, true democratic deliberation is expensive to scale, keeping feasible mini-publics small and irregular. That makes concluding from mini-public recommendations about the population's hypothetical consent, values, and will statistically unreliable. It also caps low mini-publics' contribution to public education. In these ways and in others, the long list of alleged welcome tendencies of proper democratic deliberation on health policy, and the related contribution to political legitimacy, is largely a fiction. Public deliberation does have modest true merit, for example, providing relevant qualitative input about the lay public's occasional factual insights and many endemic errors; and making the public feel "listened to," whether or not it is. But those merits are modest, contingent, and most accentuated under different institutions than envisaged in deliberative democratic literature. Certainly there is room for democratic deliberation, potentially of new breeds, but only as part of the mosaic of health policy design, alongside familiar methods like general elections, public surveys, representative government, and expert decisionmaking. The main question is which method to use when.

articles.title: High Burden and Phenotype-Specific Variability of Pain Polypharmacy in Early Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases: A 14-Year Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain drives disability and medication use in autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARDs), even when inflammation is controlled. The extent of pain-related polypharmacy across ARDs and chronic overlapping pain conditions (COPCs) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify first-year pain medication burden following ARD diagnosis and examine variations by disease, COPC status, and time.

METHODS: Using the Merative MarketScan Commercial Claims database, we identified adults newly diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, Sjögren's disease, or systemic sclerosis (2008-2021). We analyzed pain-related medications across 10 pharmacologic categories during the first year postdiagnosis. Polypharmacy measures included counts of distinct pain medications, medication categories, ≥ 5 and ≥ 10 medication thresholds, and the Medication Quantification Scale.

FINDINGS: Among 149 742 adults with newly diagnosed ARDs, 57.6% had at least one COPC. During the first year after diagnosis, patients filled a mean of 9.0 distinct pain medications and 47.9% met criteria for ≥ 5 medications; 30.5% met criteria for ≥ 10 medications. Ankylosing spondylitis demonstrated the highest medication burden (mean 11.6 medications; 57.5% with ≥ 5 medications; 37.9% with ≥ 10 medications). Patients with fibromyalgia had consistently higher medication burden across ARDs and were the only COPC group in whom prescribing increased from 2015 onward. Overall medication burden rose from 2008 to 2014-2015 and declined thereafter; however, absolute levels remained high.

INTERPRETATION: Pain-related polypharmacy is common early after ARD diagnosis and varies substantially by disease and pain phenotype. Despite modest declines from 2015 onward, medication burden remains high, underscoring the need for phenotype-informed, nonpharmacologic, and deprescribing strategies in rheumatology.

articles.title: From catheterization to ultrasound: echocardiographic approaches to pulmonary arterial compliance.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

articles.title: Restoration of frequency-dependent myocardial reserve after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis: an invasive hemodynamic study.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic pressure overload may impair frequency-dependent myocardial reserve despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We investigated whether acute afterload reduction with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) restores force-frequency relationships (FFR) and relaxation frequency relationships (RFR). In this prospective study, patients with severe normal-flow, high-gradient AS and preserved LVEF underwent invasive left ventricular pressure recording during incremental atrial pacing at 80 and 100 beats/min before and immediately after TAVI. Systolic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmax and preload-adjusted indices [dP/dtmax/left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and left ventricular peak systolic pressure (LVSP)/LVEDP], whereas lusitropic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmin, the relaxation constant τ, and LVEDP. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and 3 mo. Forty-six patients completed the pacing protocol. Before TAVI, pacing produced only a modest increase in dP/dtmax (Δ + 150 mmHg/s; P = 0.004), without improvement in dP/dtmin (P = 0.329) or τ (P = 0.182). Immediately after TAVI, pacing increased dP/dtmax (P < 0.001), dP/dtmax/LVEDP (P = 0.004), and LVSP/LVEDP (P = 0.031), while improving dP/dtmin (Δ + 56 mmHg/s; P = 0.050) and τ (P = 0.033) and reducing LVEDP (P = 0.017). Correlation analyses supported the emergence of physiological FFR and RFR after valve implantation. At 3 mo, echocardiography showed lower pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.002), improved left atrial reservoir strain, and lower diastolic dysfunction grade (P = 0.006). Thus, acute afterload relief with TAVI reveals preserved dynamic systolic and lusitropic reserve in severe AS, with subsequent group-level improvement in diastolic function.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study provides direct invasive human evidence that frequency-dependent myocardial reserve is acutely restored after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis. Controlled atrial pacing revealed blunted force-frequency and relaxation-frequency responses before valve replacement, despite preserved ejection fraction, with rapid recovery after afterload relief. These findings show that impaired myocardial reserve in pressure-overload remodeling is functionally reversible and tightly linked to loading conditions.

articles.title: Noninvasive pulse waveform monitoring in HFrEF: methodological considerations from complementary cardiovascular cohorts.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

articles.title: Emerging therapeutic strategies and clinical trials in severe asthma management: current evidence and future directions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biologic therapies have transformed the management of severe asthma, particularly in type 2-high disease, but important unmet needs remain. Incomplete responses, uncertainty in treatment positioning, and the lack of effective options for non-type 2 or mixed inflammatory endotypes continue to limit the achievement of deeper and more durable disease control.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines the evolving therapeutic landscape of severe asthma, moving from currently approved biologics to emerging strategies directed at upstream mediators and novel pathways, including alarmins, tumor necrosis factor-like cytokine 1A (TL1A)-related signaling, multi-target biologics, and next-generation anti-immunoglobulin E (IgE) approaches. It also discusses how recent clinical trials have expanded traditional efficacy outcomes by incorporating inhaled corticosteroid reduction, biomarker modulation, small airway dysfunction, mucus plugging, treatment burden, remission, and possible disease modification.

EXPERT OPINION: The field is moving beyond exacerbation reduction toward deeper and more durable disease control. Future progress will depend on improved biological stratification, more informative biomarkers, comparative effectiveness data, and therapeutic strategies capable of extending benefit beyond conventional type 2-high disease. In parallel, greater emphasis on remission-oriented and potentially disease-modifying care is likely to reshape both trial design and clinical practice in severe asthma.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Interest and Progression to Postgraduate Year Two Residency Training: A Survey of Residency Program Director Perspectives.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A decrease in postgraduate year 2 (PGY2) match participation has been observed in recent years. This study focuses on postgraduate year 1 (PGY1) Residency Program Director (RPD) perceptions of factors associated with interest in and progression to PGY2 training.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study assessed RPD perceptions regarding factors associated with pursuit of PGY2 training by PGY1 residents. In collaboration with the American Society of Health System Pharmacists, a survey was distributed to all PGY1 RPDs of accredited residency programs. The survey collected both quantitative data and qualitative data through encouraged open response questions. Quantitative analysis included descriptive statistics and χ2 test or Fisher's exact test as appropriate. A qualitative thematic analysis was conducted on open-response comments.

RESULTS: A total of 410 survey responses were included in the analysis. A majority of respondents (74%) perceived no difference or an increase in PGY1 resident progression to PGY2 training. Observed trends in the number of PGY1 residents pursuing a PGY2 differed based on institution type (p = 0.0055). The most frequently selected reason for not pursuing PGY2 residency was "Not interested in further training" (n = 76; 19.8%), followed by "Perceived lack of need for career goal(s)" (n = 60; 15.7%). Four major themes were identified through qualitative analysis: tradeoffs outweigh potential benefits, lack of need for specialization to enter the workforce, geography drives the decision, and early commitment is a barrier.

CONCLUSION: For RPDs that have observed a decrease in progression to PGY2 residency training, the results of the study suggest the benefit of further training may not align with the professional goals of recent graduates and that there is an opportunity to improve the current experience to encourage pharmacy residents to seek PGY2 training.

articles.title: Radiographic Comparison of Pulmonary Lobar Vasculature Dimensions in Medically Managed and Drug-Naive Dogs With Left Heart Failure Secondary to Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease.
articles.journal: Veterinary radiology & ultrasound : the official journal of the American College of Veterinary Radiology and the International Veterinary Radiology Association
articles.abstract: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cause of left heart failure (LHF) in dogs, and radiographic identification of pulmonary venous enlargement is traditionally used to support the diagnosis of LHF. However, the absence of venous enlargement has been anecdotally observed after initiation of therapy. Therefore, we aimed to compare radiographic pulmonary vessel size in LHF patients with ongoing medical management ± receiving acute rescue therapy. Dogs with echocardiographically confirmed MMVD and radiographic cardiogenic pulmonary edema were retrospectively selected. Pulmonary lobar artery and vein widths were measured using standardized rib-to-vessel ratios: cranial vessels at the intersection with the fourth rib on lateral projections and caudal vessels at the ninth rib on ventrodorsal/dorsoventral projections. Pulmonary vein-to-artery (PV/PA) and vessel-to-rib ratios were calculated, with enlargement defined as >1.2 and small vessel size as <0.8, and treatment groups were compared using Welch-corrected t-tests. 200 radiographic studies from 163 dogs were reviewed. In all dogs, the veins measured larger than the arteries in all lung lobes. Chronically untreated dogs who received furosemide immediately before radiographs had no venous enlargement. All other groups had vascular asymmetry or venous enlargement in at least two lung lobes. All control dogs with reoccurrence of LHF had absence of venous enlargement after initiation of therapy. Pulmonary venous enlargement was most pronounced in the right caudal lung lobe. These findings indicate that dogs chronically managed for MMVD may decompensate into LHF without radiographic pulmonary venous enlargement and that furosemide administration prior to imaging can normalize vessel size.

articles.title: Remimazolam-Based Total Intravenous Anesthesia for Cardiac Surgery in an Infant With a Pathogenic RYR1 Variant.
articles.abstract: The ryanodine receptor 1 (RYR1) gene encodes a protein channel located on the terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum of skeletal muscle, thereby playing a key role in regulation of skeletal muscle contraction. RYR1 gene mutations may result in inherited neuromuscular conditions with a wide range of clinical manifestations including profound hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness, facial weakness, respiratory involvement, and orthopedic disorders (scoliosis, hip dislocation, and arthrogryposis). Affected individuals may also be malignant hyperthermia susceptible. We present an infant with RYR1 gene mutation who presented for anesthetic care during cardiac surgery for congenital heart disease. The clinical spectrum of RYR1 gene mutation disorders is presented, previous reports of anesthetic care reviewed, and options for perioperative care discussed.

articles.title: Myeloperoxidase-Anti-Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody Vasculitis With Isolated Renal Presentation in an Older Female Patient: A Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenge.
articles.abstract: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides are rare systemic autoimmune diseases, the incidence of which increases in older individuals. We report the case of a 76-year-old woman whose routine laboratory workup revealed acute kidney injury with a serum creatinine level of 155 µmol/L and significant proteinuria (2.5 g/24 h). ANCA testing was strongly positive for anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) antibodies. A renal biopsy confirmed pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with moderate interstitial fibrosis and glomerulosclerosis, consistent with ANCA-associated vasculitis. Induction therapy consisted of corticosteroids and rituximab, which was discontinued following a suspected drug-related cutaneous reaction. Cyclophosphamide was successfully used as an alternative induction treatment. Following negative allergological evaluation and cautious re-exposure, rituximab was subsequently resumed for maintenance therapy and was well tolerated. Late-onset MPO-ANCA-associated vasculitis can have a favorable prognosis when diagnosed early and managed with appropriate immunosuppressive regimens.

articles.title: Asymptomatic Intracardiac Migration of a Cane-Shaped Polymethylmethacrylate Cement Embolus Following Percutaneous Vertebroplasty.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) is a minimally invasive and effective treatment for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Although generally safe, cement leakage is a relatively common complication and may rarely result in intracardiac embolism. We report the case of a 75-year-old woman who underwent PVP for an L2 compression fracture after failed conservative treatment. Postoperative imaging revealed venous cement leakage, but she remained asymptomatic. Six months later, during a routine health examination, echocardiography incidentally detected an abnormal structure in the right atrium. Cardiac computed tomography demonstrated a linear, cane-shaped polymethylmethacrylate embolus extending from the right atrium to the right ventricle. Despite the absence of cardiopulmonary symptoms, surgical removal was performed because of the elongated and sharp morphology of the embolus and the associated risk of cardiac perforation. Open-heart surgery was successfully completed without major complications. Although many intracardiac cement embolisms are asymptomatic and can be managed conservatively, embolus morphology and location should guide treatment decisions. Early recognition and individualized management are essential to prevent life-threatening complications.

articles.title: Unilateral mixed corticomedullary tumor of the adrenal gland with a synchronous contralateral pheochromocytoma: A case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: A 37-year-old man had two years of fatigue, weakness, and mood changes, initially misdiagnosed as depression. Workup showed hypertension, elevated urinary normetanephrine, elevated free cortisol, and suppressed ACTH. Imaging revealed bilateral adrenal masses (7.5 cm left, 4.7 cm right) with left adrenal vein thrombosis; MIBG scintigraphy showed bilateral uptake. After alpha-blockade, he underwent bilateral adrenalectomy. Inhibin positivity in the left mass's cortical region suggested a possible first-reported unilateral mixed corticomedullary tumor with synchronous contralateral pheochromocytoma, though entrapped cortical cells couldn't be excluded without further markers. Elevated Ki-67 and bilateral involvement warrant long-term follow-up and genetic evaluation.

articles.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
articles.abstract: Motor vehicle collisions (MVCs) are among the most common mechanisms of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), and a meaningful proportion of affected individuals develop persistent post-concussion syndrome (PPCS) characterized by prolonged multidomain dysfunction. Conventional neuroimaging frequently fails to capture the underlying pathophysiology, leaving clinicians without objective diagnostic evidence. We describe a 57-year-old woman who sustained mTBI in a rear-end MVC in March 2023. Head computed tomography (CT) performed at the emergency department and a subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were both unremarkable. Despite normal structural neuroimaging, comprehensive multimodal functional assessment identified functional abnormalities across eight domains: vestibular function (videonystagmography (VNG)), cortical electrophysiology (quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG)), pupillary autonomics (automated infrared pupillometry), postural stability (computerized dynamic posturography (CDP)), oculomotor control (saccadometry), cardiac autonomic regulation (24-h heart rate variability (HRV)), olfaction (University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT)), and computerized concussion assessment (C3 Logix). Standardized psychological assessments confirmed moderate depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) = 14), moderate anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) = 12), clinically significant post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms (PTSD Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) (PCL-5 = 38)), and substantial headache impact (Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) = 58). The patient underwent a 10-modality individualized rehabilitation program. Concussion Symptom Checklist (CSC) scores declined from 92 at initial presentation to 0 by July 2023 (17 weeks post-injury), with near-complete re-resolution to 8 by February 2024 following a transient stress-related exacerbation. When conventional neuroimaging is unremarkable, comprehensive multimodal functional testing may provide evidence consistent with mTBI pathophysiology and help guide targeted rehabilitation. This case illustrates the potential value of a systematic, multimodal approach in PPCS management, while acknowledging that definitive attribution of findings to the index injury is constrained by the single-case design and absence of a pre-injury functional baseline.

articles.title: Maximizing cardiopulmonary support as a minimally invasive platform-using peripheral parallel veno-venous and veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and axillary impella 5.5 as a bridge to heart-lung transplantation.
articles.abstract: Combined heart-lung transplantation (HLTx) in patients with cardiopulmonary failure requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) presents a major physiologic challenge. Conventional ECMO strategies may inadequately address simultaneous refractory hypoxemia, circulatory failure, and left ventricular (LV) distension without central cannulation and sternotomy. A 65-year-old man with severe heart failure (LVEF <10%) and rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease presented with cardiogenic shock and hypercapnic hypoxemic respiratory failure. Initial V-AV ECMO provided stabilization and allowed extubation and expedited HLTx evaluation. Progressive hypoxemia and acute kidney injury despite maximal V-AV support prompted escalation to peripheral parallel VV-VA ECMO. Echocardiography demonstrated LV distension, prompting axillary Impella 5.5 placement for decompression. The patient remained awake and extubated on parallel VV-VA ECMO and Impella 5.5 for 60 hours prior to successful heart-lung transplantation. We report the novel application of a fully peripheral cardiopulmonary support platform as a viable bridge strategy for HLTx candidates.

articles.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Supported Diagnosis of Acute Myocarditis Mimicking Acute Coronary Syndrome in a Patient With Sepsis Due to a Massive Perianal Abscess.
articles.abstract: Acute myocarditis is a rare but potentially life-threatening inflammatory disease that may mimic acute myocardial infarction, particularly in septic patients where myocardial injury may have other causes. We report the case of a 46-year-old man with sepsis secondary to a massive perianal abscess who underwent emergency surgical drainage under general anesthesia. Postoperatively, persistent respiratory deterioration and elevated cardiac biomarkers prompted further cardiac evaluation. Echocardiography showed newly reduced left ventricular (LV) systolic function, with an ejection fraction (EF) of 35%, and moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (MR). Although acute myocardial infarction was initially suspected, coronary angiography showed non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), with only a 40% right coronary artery stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) demonstrated elevated T2 values and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of the interventricular septum, with additional enhancement of the LV lateral wall, consistent with myocardial edema and inflammation and supportive of acute myocarditis. The patient received source control, broad-spectrum antibiotics, intravenous diuretics, norepinephrine and dobutamine, oxygen therapy, and heart failure-directed therapy. EF improved to 45% at 10 days, with complete recovery of cardiac function and resolution of MR at the 3-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of acute myocarditis in septic surgical patients and suggests that early multidisciplinary assessment, coronary evaluation, and CMR may help clarify the diagnosis and guide management.

articles.title: Primary bladder diffuse large B-cell lymphoma causing unilateral ureterovesical junction obstruction: A case report.
articles.abstract: Primary bladder diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is a rare extranodal malignancy that often mimics urothelial carcinoma. We report a 65-year-old male with flank pain and hematuria found to have a bladder mass extending to the ureterovesical junction with hydroureteronephrosis; urine cytology was repeatedly negative. Cystoscopic biopsy confirmed DLBCL, with no marrow involvement. Transurethral resection plus R-CHOP chemotherapy produced complete metabolic response on FDG-PET/CT, with stable residual uptake later deemed post-treatment change (Deauville 3). This case highlights ureteral obstruction as an unusual presentation and serial PET/CT as valuable for distinguishing residual lymphoma from fibrosis after therapy.

articles.title: Assessment of knowledge, attitudes, and practices among livestock farmers regarding ticks and tick-borne diseases in Bangladesh: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Ticks and tick-borne diseases (TTBDs) remain a major constraint to livestock productivity and a growing public health concern in tropical settings such as Bangladesh. This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of livestock farmers regarding TTBDs and to identify associated determinants. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from 5 January to 15 February 2026 among 530 randomly selected livestock farmers across eight districts using a structured questionnaire, with data analyzed through descriptive statistics, logistic regression, and Spearman's correlation. Only 27.7% of respondents demonstrated good knowledge, despite a high positive attitude (85.5%) and moderately satisfactory practices (45.3%). In multivariate analysis, higher education emerged as a strong predictor of good knowledge, with graduates significantly more likely to be knowledgeable compared to those without formal education (AOR = 10.3, 95% CI: 3.33-36.4, p < 0.001), while larger herd size (>50 animals) was also associated with improved knowledge (AOR = 9.20, 95% CI: 3.15-29.7, p < 0.001). Receipt of formal training significantly increased the likelihood of satisfactory practices (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.70-4.62, p < 0.001). Knowledge showed a moderate positive correlation with attitudes (ρ = 0.574, p < 0.001) and practices (ρ = 0.410, p < 0.001). Despite generally favorable attitudes, critical gaps in knowledge and implementation persist, particularly regarding zoonotic risks and appropriate control strategies. These findings underscore the need for targeted farmer education, strengthened veterinary extension services, and integrated tick management to improve livestock health and productivity. The findings may also inform future One Health-oriented strategies for the prevention and control of tick-borne diseases in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Machine learning-driven discovery of TGFBR1 inhibitors from Mangifera indica for Atorvastatin-based antidiabetic therapy.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mangiferin, a C-glucosyl xanthone from Mangifera indica, has known antidiabetic activity, but the specific protein target underlying this activity, and its compatibility with existing antidiabetic drugs such as Atorvastatin, were not defined. In this work, machine learning, network pharmacology, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation identified and validated TGFBR1 as a novel molecular target of Mangiferin and evaluated a Mangiferin-Atorvastatin combination for diabetes therapy. A curated collection of TGFBR1 inhibitors from BindingDB was used to train several supervised learning models, with the best performance from Random Forest (94.68% accuracy, κ = 0.8981) and robust external validation (79.35%) on 868 unseen compounds. Screening of 545 M. indica phytochemicals with this model identified Mangiferin, Fisetin, Isochinomin, Mangiferolic acid, and Astragalin as high-confidence TGFBR1 inhibitors. Network pharmacology identified TGF-β as the most central protein in the interaction network (cumulative score 350), and molecular docking showed that Mangiferin forms stable hydrogen bonds with SER-287, ILE-211, and GLU-208 at the TGFBR1 binding site, together with hydrophobic contacts. This binding pose remained structurally stable (RMSD 1.50-1.75 Å) over 100 nanoseconds of molecular dynamics simulation, with ligand-residue occupancy > 85%. ADMET profiling showed favorable drug-likeness (Lipinski compliance, low predicted toxicity) with a moderate permeability limitation (TPSA 201.28 Å²), and DFT analysis showed a HOMO-LUMO gap of 2.85937 eV, supporting antioxidant activity. In cultured cells, Atorvastatin combined with Mangiferin increased apoptosis through the mitochondrial pathway (Bcl-xL downregulation, BAK upregulation, cytochrome c release, caspase-7/8 activation) and enhanced insulin sensitivity, shown by increased glucose uptake (2-NBDG assay) and higher GLUT-4 and pIRS-1(Tyr896) expression. In high-fat diet-fed rats, Atorvastatin plus Mangiferin given for 24 weeks significantly improved glucose tolerance and reduced HbA1c, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and random blood sugar relative to untreated high-fat diet controls, with preserved pancreatic architecture and increased muscle GLUT-4 expression. These findings identify TGFBR1 as a plausible molecular target of Mangiferin and provide a mechanistic rationale for the Mangiferin-Atorvastatin combination as a candidate antidiabetic therapy.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05088-0.

articles.title: Modeling heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) likelihood among women with suspected coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD).
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) can precede development of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in patients with ischemia and no obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA). The H2FPEF score is used to estimate HFpEF likelihood but has not been evaluated among women with suspected INOCA.

METHODS: Women (n = 98) with suspected INOCA enrolled in prospective cohort studies at a single center with both cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography to calculate H2FPEF score. CMR evaluated left ventricular (LV) structure, function, myocardial perfusion reserve index (MPRI) and fibrosis. Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression were performed.

RESULTS: Group mean age was 56 years, BMI 27 kg/m2, 39% had hypertension, and 12% had diabetes. Median H2FPEF score was 2 (range 0-7), with 43 (44%), 53 (54%), and 2 (2%) ranked as having low (0-1), intermediate (2-5), or high (6-9) probability of HFpEF, respectively.H2FPEF score was inversely related to MPRI, native T1, extracellular volume, and Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) physical limitation score (all p < 0.05), but not related to LV strain or remodeling. Regression modeling demonstrated that low MPRI, SAQ physical limitation, and diabetes were independent predictors of H2FPEF, adjusted for dyslipidemia and native T1.

CONCLUSIONS: Among women with suspected INOCA, 54% had an intermediate or higher H2FPEF score. Compromised microvascular perfusion, fibrosis, angina, and history of diabetes predicted H2FPEF score. These findings support the hypothesis that CMD may contribute to development of HFpEF in women with INOCA. Longitudinal studies and intervention trials are needed.

articles.title: Moyamoya disease presenting as galactorrhea.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular condition marked by carotid narrowing and collateral vessel formation. Patients are often diagnosed after a stroke, but here we describe a case of galactorrhea as the presenting symptom of MMD. A 30-year-old gravida 1, para 0 woman noted milky, nonbloody discharge leaking from both breasts after manual compression during sexual intercourse. Prolactin was mildly elevated at 29.4 ng/mL (SI [International System of Units]: 29.4 µg/L) (reference range, 3-23.1 ng/mL [SI: 3-23.1 µg/L]). Magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary gland showed no microadenoma but incidentally revealed a tortuous right internal carotid artery compressing the pituitary, raising the possibility of vascular compression contributing to galactorrhea and mild hyperprolactinemia. Magnetic resonance angiography and catheter angiography confirmed MMD. Mild cognitive impairment, persistent headaches, and secondary hypertension eventually necessitated neurosurgical revascularization. After surgery, the patient experienced a significant reduction in symptoms although challenges with memory and headaches have persisted. This case underscores the importance of brain imaging in evaluating hyperprolactinemia and highlights the potential for endocrinologic sequelae when MMD involves vessels in proximity to the pituitary gland.

articles.title: When anorexia nervosa conceals Cushing syndrome: a diagnostic pitfall in hypercortisolemia.
articles.abstract: A 37-year-old woman presented with severe hypertension, mood changes, and weight loss (body mass index 14.6 kg/m2). She exhibited restrictive eating behaviors consistent with anorexia nervosa, alongside biochemical hypercortisolemia with serum cortisol 43.6 µg/dL (1204 nmol/L; reference range: 6.2-18.1 µg/dL; 170-500 nmol/L), 24-hour urinary free cortisol 430.3 µg/24 hours (1187 nmol/24 hours; reference range: <60.2 µg/24 hours; <166 nmol/24 hours), and unsuppressed adrenocorticotropic hormone of 19.1 pg/mL (4.2 pmol/L; reference range: 7.3-63.1 pg/mL; 1.6-13.9 pmol/L). The cortisol level after the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test was 23.9 µg/dL (659 nmol/L; reference range: <1.8 µg/dL; <50 nmol/L). Cortisol remained markedly elevated after nasogastric feeding and weight restoration. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a 4 mm left anterior pituitary lesion. High-dose dexamethasone suppression, corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation, and inferior petrosal sinus sampling confirmed a pituitary source of adrenocorticotropic hormone. The patient underwent transsphenoidal resection of a corticotroph adenoma. Eleven months later, her hypertension and restrictive eating behaviors had resolved, and her mood significantly improved. Cushing syndrome can coexist with anorexia nervosa, masking typical cushingoid features and presenting with psychiatric manifestations and weight loss. Persistent hypercortisolemia despite nutritional rehabilitation should prompt dynamic endocrine testing and pituitary evaluation to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Aortic coarctation and McArdle disease in histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome: expanding the SLC29A3 spectrum.
articles.abstract: Histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome (HLPS) is a rare inherited disorder caused by SLC29A3 variants. We report 2 Pakistani brothers with HLPS and markedly different clinical features despite identical genotypes. The 15-year-old had severe growth failure, facial dysmorphism, insulin-dependent diabetes, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring balloon dilatation. Genetic testing identified SLC29A3 and PYGM variants, indicating concurrent HLPS and McArdle disease. His 20-year-old brother had insulin-dependent diabetes and celiac disease from age 3, later developing hypertension, proteinuria, and characteristic skin changes. This case highlights marked intrafamilial variability in HLPS and identifies CoA as a rare cardiovascular feature. It also supports comprehensive genetic testing in patients with early-onset diabetes and multisystem disease.

articles.title: Primary Hepatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Systematic Review and Expert Pathologist Reappraisal Using the WHO 6th Edition Framework.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Primary hepatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PHNENs) are exceedingly rare. Published evidence often lacks adequate clinicopathological support for a primary hepatic origin and uses inconsistent historical terminology. Previous reviews have pooled well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), and mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs), despite differences in biology, prognosis, and management. We systematically reviewed reported PHNENs using PRISMA-based screening and expert pathology reappraisal within the WHO 6th edition morphology-first framework. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened according to predefined eligibility criteria; eligible articles underwent second-level expert assessment of pathology, including morphology (including NET G3 vs. NEC and MiNEN vs. amphicrine carcinoma), immunohistochemistry (expression of at least two NE markers), proliferation (Ki-67/mitotic activity), as well as clinical/imaging work-up to exclude metastases from extrahepatic primaries. Of the 67 potentially eligible studies submitted to expert pathology-based reappraisal, 28 studies (49.1%) were retained in the final dataset with 57 likely NEN cases (mainly case reports/small case series). Among the 57 cases, most were well-differentiated NETs (78.9%); NECs (8.8%), MiNENs (3.5%), and amphicrine carcinomas (1.8%) were less frequent. Some cases were high-grade NENs that could not be distinguished as well or poorly differentiated (7%). PHNEN literature is constrained by rarity, uncertainty of hepatic origin, and historical misclassification. Future studies and registries should report a minimum diagnostic dataset with standardised terminology according to the WHO 6th edition framework and in-depth clinical/imaging studies.

articles.title: Physical Activity Levels and Lung-Kidney Function in a Cohort of COVID-19 Survivors.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between physical activity levels and overall health among survivors of moderate to severe COVID-19 remains underexplored in target organs, such as lungs and kidneys. We examined the association between physical activity levels and lung-kidney abnormalities in survivors of COVID-19 hospitalization.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was performed within a prospective cohort of survivors of COVID-19 hospitalization. Physical activity levels were assessed with the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (short form), and physical inactivity was classified according to the World Health Organization guidelines (<150 min/week of physical activity). Abnormal kidney function was defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, whereas pulmonary involvement was defined as chest X-ray pulmonary lesion, and/or forced vital capacity less than the lower limit of normal, and/or altered oximetry.

RESULTS: In total, 653 survivors (46% female and 28% ≥65 years) were assessed 8 ± 2 months posthospital discharge. Physical inactivity was found in 53% of the cohort. Lung and kidney abnormalities were observed in 36% and 20% of survivors, respectively, whereas coexistence was observed in 7%. Physically active survivors had lower odds of lung abnormality (32% vs 41%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.67, 95% confidence interval [CI]:0.47 to 0.97), but not of kidney (17% vs 23%; aOR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.52 to 1.26) nor lung-kidney abnormality (6% vs 9%; aOR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.29 to 1.20), compared with those physically inactive. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses showed distinct associations for lung abnormalities by age and among survivors without severe oxygen desaturation or very low kidney function. The restricted cubic spline curve for lung-kidney abnormalities showed a nonlinear dose-response relationship, with higher odds below and lower odds above 150 min/week.

CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors of COVID-19 hospitalization, being physically active was associated with better lung function outcomes, but not kidney or composite outcomes. This association was modified by age and baseline clinical status and followed a non-linear dose-response pattern.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison.

CONCLUSION: Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Eye Movements in Dizziness and Vertigo: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Dizziness and vertigo, common neurologic complaints, remain challenging to diagnose accurately in both emergency and outpatient settings. Although complex, these conditions frequently present with specific abnormalities of eye movement that contain precise signals allowing for localization and diagnosis. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning have enabled automated analysis of eye-movement recordings obtained using video-oculography and related technologies, reducing barriers to their clinical use. In this review, AI-based approaches to eye movement are analyzed to diagnose dizziness and vertigo, organized using several clinical diagnostic tasks, including benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, acute vestibular syndrome and stroke triage.

articles.title: Rural Health and Atypical Stroke: Technology-Based Posterior Circulation Stroke Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Diagnostic errors cause an estimated 900,000 deaths and disabilities annually in the United States, and stroke is the leading cause of diagnostic error-related harm in US emergency departments. Posterior circulation strokes (PCS's) are frequently misdiagnosed due to atypical presentations such as dizziness. Key contributors to rural-urban care gaps in PCS diagnosis are highlighted for rural care (eg, challenges in bedside diagnosis and limited access to neurologists). Emerging technologies (eg, telestroke, video-oculography-based teledizzy programs, mobile stroke units, and smartphone tools) can improve diagnostic access, timeliness and accuracy for patients living in rural communities.

articles.title: Hospital-Based Video-Oculography for Acute Vertigo and Dizziness.
articles.abstract: In this article, we review studies that bring video-oculography (VOG) to the emergency department and inpatient settings, with an emphasis on acute vestibular syndrome. We find that most current studies are research-based, rather than pilot clinical programs. Many focus on the use of VOG to differentiate central disorders (eg, ischemic stroke) from peripheral (eg, inner ear) mimics. We critically appraise the classes of eye movements studied by each, and then provide an update on recent work in leveraging artificial intelligence, telemedicine, and the use of consumer devices and smartphones for VOG-applications, to expand reach and improve vestibular diagnosis.

articles.title: Multi-domain interventions for the prevention of motoric cognitive risk syndrome among Chinese older adults: An application of the parametric G-formula based on an intrinsic capacity framework.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Evidence on large-scale prevention of motoric cognitive risk syndrome remains limited. This study aimed to identify potentially modifiable targets for the prevention of motoric cognitive risk syndrome within an intrinsic capacity framework and to estimate their potential effects using hypothetical intervention scenarios.

METHODS: 2299 individuals aged ≥60 years were included from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (2011-2015). Candidate targets were selected using theory-driven and data-driven approaches. Behavioral targets included social participation and physical activity. The parametric g-formula was used to estimate 4-year risks under hypothetical interventions and the natural course.

RESULTS: During the 4-year follow-up, 443 participants (19.3%) developed incident motoric cognitive risk syndrome. The joint hypothetical interventions targeting peak expiratory flow, depression symptoms, and pain achieved the largest estimated risk reduction (risk ratio 0.74, 95% confidence interval 0.59-0.90). The joint scenario targeting social participation and physical activity also yielded a lower estimated risk (risk ratio 0.78, 95% confidence interval 0.58-0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: An intervention integrating enhanced respiratory function and psychological resilience with pain management may be a promising strategy in the prevention of motoric cognitive risk syndrome among older adults. Combinations of social participation and physical activity also warrant further evaluation. Future randomized controlled trials are needed to determine the potential causal efficacy of these multi-domain interventions for the prevention of motoric cognitive risk syndrome.

articles.title: Medication adherence and health-related quality of life among patients with heart failure: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) continues to be a significant public health concern. Adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is essential for improving clinical outcomes and quality of life (QoL) in these patients.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate how well patients with chronic HF adhere to GDMT and to assess their health-related QoL.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted using data collected between March and May 2025. Eligible participants were adult outpatients with a confirmed diagnosis of HF who were able to complete the study questionnaires. Medication adherence was assessed using the 8-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8), while health-related QoL was evaluated with the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among 300 HF patients (64.7% male; median age of 63), sixty-nine percent had reduced ejection fraction (median EF 30%), with 62.4% classified as NYHA III or IV. Medication adherence was low in 25%, moderate in 44.6%, and high in 30.3%. Patients with more severe HF symptoms (higher NYHA class) reported significantly lower QoL, while higher adherence correlated significantly with better QoL. Older patients had a lower risk of low adherence, while intracardiac devices were linked to a higher risk.

CONCLUSION: Despite GDMT's critical role in HF management, a notable proportion of patients demonstrated low adherence, which was associated with diminished QoL. Special attention and targeted interventions for high-risk groups, particularly patients with intracardiac devices, are imperative for enhancing outcomes.

articles.title: Taiwanese expert consensus on the assessment and management of agitation in dementia: A modified Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Agitation in dementia is clinically heterogeneous and requires individualized assessment, nonpharmacological strategies, and cautious pharmacological treatment. However, evidence-based consensus guidance addressing the broader care process across different care settings remains limited.

METHODS: This two-round modified Delphi study was jointly conducted by the Taiwanese Society for Geriatric Psychiatry and the Taiwan Dementia Society. A working group developed preliminary statements based on targeted evidence review, statement-level evidence assessment, and clinical relevance to Taiwan. A panel of 30 experts, including 20 geriatric psychiatrists and 10 neurologists, participated in structured discussion, anonymous prioritization voting, post-round revision, and final anonymous voting. Consensus thresholds were predefined for evidence-based recommendations and good practice statements (GPS).

RESULTS: Of 14 preliminary statements generated by the working group, 10 were retained and organized into three clinical domains: diagnosis and assessment, nonpharmacological management, and pharmacological management by the panel. Four statements were classified as GPS, and six were evidence-based recommendations. Two statements received strong recommendations and four received conditional recommendations. All final statements met predefined consensus thresholds, with agreement ranging from 71% to 100%; eight statements achieved agreement of 90% or higher. The consensus supports structured assessment, identification of contributing factors, nonpharmacological and community-based care when feasible, pharmacological treatment only in clinically appropriate situations, and low-dose, short-term medication use with regular reassessment.

CONCLUSIONS: The consensus provides a practice-oriented framework for the assessment and management of agitation in dementia within the Taiwanese healthcare context. It may support stepwise clinical decision-making while identifying areas requiring further agitation-specific evidence.

articles.title: [Chances and challenges in the prevention and treatment of early childhood hearing loss: the AWMF guideline on congenital CMV infection].
articles.abstract: After genetic causes, congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) infection is the leading infectious cause of congenital and early childhood hearing loss. The 2025 German S2k guideline on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of CMV infection in pregnant women and congenital CMV infection in neonates and children published by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF; 093-003 [24]) provides corresponding recommendations and summarizes the current evidence. Hygiene counseling of pregnant women, targeted diagnostic testing during pregnancy and in neonates, and antiviral therapeutic options are important measures for prevention and treatment of congenital CMV infection. Universal newborn hearing screening (UNHS) is decisive for the diagnosis of congenital hearing loss. If abnormal results are revealed in the initial and follow-up testing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of CMV DNA in urine (gold standard) or saliva should be performed immediately-as it should be in the case of other symptoms-preferably in the maternity or pediatric hospital and certainly not later than in the second to third week of life. In the case of symptomatic congenital CMV infection, causal treatment of congenital hearing loss can be offered as early as during the first 30 days of life-both for clinically symptomatic infants and for those with isolated hearing loss. Treatment may reduce the severity of hearing loss, stabilize hearing, or prevent progression. Long-term aftercare is essential to recognize progression or a late onset of hearing loss and to ensure adequate management. In addition to dissemination of these guideline recommendations, interdisciplinary cooperation-particularly between the maternity and neonatal departments performing UNHS and otorhinolaryngology and pediatric audiology departments-is essential.

articles.title: [Osteoporosis in rheumatology-Diagnostics, risk assessment and modern treatment strategies].
articles.abstract: Inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) lead to local periarticular demineralization through localized arthritis in one or more joints; however, the autoimmune-mediated systemic inflammatory process is also a driver of systemic bone loss, osteoporosis, which leads to an increased risk of fractures. The Umbrella Organization Osteology (DVO) guidelines 2023 recommend a risk-adapted approach involving systematic fracture risk assessment, early baseline diagnostics and consistent specific osteoporosis treatment, including antiresorptive and osteoanabolic strategies. For rheumatology practice this means firmly integrating osteological assessment, including fracture risk management as well as pharmacological and nonpharmacological osteological treatment into the structured care of patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases.

articles.title: Comparative Chemical and Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of Different Purification Procedures for Yangxin Dingji Capsules.
articles.abstract: Yangxin Dingji Capsules (YXDJ), derived from Zhigancao Decoction, are used clinically for arrhythmia. Four D101 macroporous-resin purification procedures involving different Asini Corii Colla incorporation modes and elution solvents were compared; the co-decoction procedures additionally included centrifugation and filtration before resin purification. The unpurified preparation and four purified preparations were characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and evaluated in a barium chloride-induced rat arrhythmia model using electrocardiographic, biochemical, and histopathological indicators. Fifty-five constituents were tentatively identified. The 60% ethanol-eluted preparations CF1 and CF3 retained 52 and 51 constituents, respectively, whereas the water-eluted preparations CF2 and CF4 retained 21 and 14. CF1 showed the highest Pearson correlation with YXDJ among the purified preparations (r = 0.520), while CF3 had the highest five-indicator comprehensive pharmacodynamic score among the purified preparations (CPS5 = 3.540); unpurified YXDJ scored 3.827. Compared with the model group, CF3 significantly increased heart rate, shortened QRS duration, reduced serum lactate dehydrogenase, and increased Na+/K+-ATPase activity. Exploratory one-component partial least-squares variable-importance and gray relational analyses generated a provisional list of 12 constituents for subsequent targeted quantification and pharmacological verification.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Enlicitide in Hypercholesterolemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high-risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL-C targets. Enlicitide (MK-0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9-directed therapies.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlicitide in adults with hypercholesterolemia and assess its dose-dependent effects on lipid parameters.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through March 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed. The primary outcome was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline. Secondary outcomes included non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), lipoprotein(a), triglycerides, and safety outcomes. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2.0 and GRADE.

RESULTS: Three placebo-controlled RCTs involving 3593 participants were included. Enlicitide significantly reduced LDL-C compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], -56.19%; 95% CI, -64.14 to -48.25; p < 0.0001), with moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 56.9%). Significant reductions were also observed in non-HDL-C (MD, -51.36%), ApoB (MD, -47.09%), lipoprotein(a) (MD, -20.10%), and triglycerides (MD, -13.12%). A numerical dose-response gradient was observed, although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were comparable between groups.

CONCLUSION: Enlicitide produced substantial reductions in LDL-C and other atherogenic lipid parameters without an apparent increase in adverse events. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, moderate heterogeneity, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Dose-response, duration-related lipoprotein(a), and triglyceride findings were exploratory and substantially driven by single trials. Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trials are needed to establish clinical benefit.

articles.title: The role of anti-factor Xa in patients with cancer receiving prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) is a mainstay in the prevention of cancer-associated thrombosis. However, there is a lack of clear guidelines around routine monitoring of anti-factor Xa (AFXa) levels in patients with cancer receiving LMWH for prophylaxis. This study compares fixed vs laboratory-based dosing of LMWH in patients with cancer to elucidate if there are significant differences in venous thromboembolism (VTE) and bleeding outcomes for this population. To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis that evaluates AFXa monitoring, specifically in patients with cancer. A total of 561 articles were screened, and 5 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Two studies directly compared outcomes of fixed dosing vs AFXa-based dosing, and 4 studies evaluated outcomes based on whether AFXa values were subprophylactic, prophylactic, or supraprophylactic. The relative risk (RR) of VTE was higher in fixed dosing vs adjusting for AFXa levels, although this failed to reach statistical significance (RR, 9.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90-95.29; I 2 = 0.0%). Surprisingly, patients with subprophylactic AFXa levels experienced bleeding events at 6% (95% CI, 0.00-0.24; I 2 = 73.3%) compared to 2% at prophylactic levels (95% CI, 0.00-0.08; I 2 = 3.1%), although the difference was not statistically significant. Our findings suggest a lack of benefit in monitoring AFXa in prophylaxis for preventing VTE; however, further investigation into high-risk malignancies or patients undergoing cancer surgery may elucidate differences in VTE and bleeding outcomes that guide future prophylactic anticoagulation.

articles.title: "It's Not Like My Old Life, But It's Still Freedom": An ACTION learning network mixed methods analysis of the adolescent ventricular assist device experience at home.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric patients supported with durable ventricular assist devices (VAD) are increasingly discharged home on device. Little is known about adolescent and young adult (AYA) experiences during this unique time. This study aims to further understand AYA VAD experience to improve supports and interventions upon discharge.

METHODS: An 8-domain, 34-item semi-structured interview guide was developed, informed by prior adult VAD interview, pediatric literature, and multidisciplinary VAD team review, including patient/family advocates. AYAs currently or recently discharged home on durable VAD at an ACTION site were approached. Two authors independently coded qualitative responses using a priori codes for thematic analysis. Inter-rater reliability was achieved.

RESULTS: Seventeen AYAs (M=17.40 years) completed semi-structured interviews. The majority were male (76%) and half were White race (53%). All were supported on HeartMate3, most commonly with underlying diagnosis of dilated cardiomyopathy (76%). Length of heart failure ranged from 2 weeks to 9 years prior to device implant. AYAs provided insights across several domains. Most common worries were emergency situations (82%), infection (71%), and bleeding (71%). All reported some limitations, including engagement with friends (71%), sports (59%), and freedom of movement (47%).

CONCLUSION: Significant life disruptions and coping challenges are prevalent among AYAs discharged home on VAD. Robust psychosocial supports are indicated, including access to multidisciplinary care providers who are aware of the intricacies of managing VAD outpatient. Given remarks from AYAs regarding importance of peer connection, results highlight AYA peer and caregiver support groups and online communities as future directions.

articles.title: Right ventricular remodeling after veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation bridge to lung transplantation in adults with severe lung disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a common complication of advanced lung disease, yet data on RV remodeling and long-term outcomes following veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) as a bridge to lung transplantation remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult patients bridged to lung transplant on VV-ECMO from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2022. Transthoracic echocardiograms were analyzed pre-transplant (on VV-ECMO) and post-transplant in the "early" ( ≤ 3 months) and "late" (3-12 months) phases. Within-patient changes in echocardiographic parameters were assessed using paired nonparametric tests. The association between pre-transplant RV systolic function, quantified by RV fractional area of change (RVFAC), and 3-year post-transplant survival was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards modeling.

RESULTS: Twenty patients were included (65.0% male, median age 47.5 [IQR: 41.5-56.4]) with primary etiologies of interstitial lung disease (50.0%) and COVID-19 (30.0%). In the "early" post-transplant phase, median RV systolic pressure decreased from 70.0 to 31.2 mm Hg (p < 0.001) and RVFAC increased from 25.9% to 31.9% (p = 0.004), whereas tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion decreased from 15.0 to 10.3 mm (p < 0.001). RV and right atrial dilation improved, while RV free-wall thickness remained unchanged (5.4-5.8 mm, p = 0.601). Among patients with greater baseline RV dysfunction, substantial functional and structural recovery was observed at 1-year. Three-year survival was 85.0% and preoperative RV dysfunction was not associated with mortality (HR: 0.96 [95% CI: 0.14-6.87]).

CONCLUSIONS: Meaningful RV recovery and favorable 3-year survival appear achievable after VV-ECMO bridge to transplantation, even among patients with moderate-to-severe pre-transplant RV dysfunction.

articles.title: Mature Adipocyte-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Activate Hepatic Stellate Cells and Promote Liver Fibrosis via Inflammation.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) play a crucial role in intercellular communication, particularly in metabolic regulation and liver disease. This study aimed to investigate the differential effects of EVs derived from pre-adipocytes (PA) and mature adipocytes (MA) on hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation in vitro and their role in promoting liver fibrosis in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice.

METHODS: EVs were isolated from PA and MA following transdifferentiation, which was confirmed by assessing adipogenic markers (PPAR-γ, perilipin, adiponectin, leptin, and Glut4). EVs were characterized by size and CD9 expression. LX-2 cells were treated with PA- or MA-derived EVs to assess fibrotic and inflammatory gene expression. In vivo, C57BL/6 mice on HFD were administered PA-EVs or MA-EVs to evaluate liver pathology.

RESULTS: MA-EVs exhibited a distinct transcriptomic profile and significantly upregulated fibrotic (α-SMA, COL1A1) and inflammatory markers in LX-2 cells, indicating HSC activation. Conversely, PA-EVs had minimal effects. In HFD-fed mice, MA-EVs injection led to pronounced liver damage, including steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, compared with mice receiving PA-EVs, which showed no major pathological changes.

CONCLUSIONS: MA-EVs aggravate liver fibrosis and inflammation both in vitro and In vivo, while PA-EVs appear to have relatively limited effects. These findings highlight the functional heterogeneity of adipocyte-derived EVs and suggest MA-EVs as potential contributors to the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Targeting specific EV subpopulations may present novel therapeutic strategy for MASLD.

articles.title: Evaluating Perfusion Quantification for Phase-Resolved Functional Lung MRI Using Gaussian Filtering.
articles.abstract: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI enables contrast-free lung perfusion quantification (QQuant). Current quantification uses a single median value per slice of maximal blood exchange fraction (ΔS), which limits regional assessment, whereas regional ΔS causes artifacts. This retrospective study aims to optimize QQuant by applying Gaussian filtering to ΔS to improve intrascan/interscan repeatability in healthy volunteers, while evaluating whether the optimized QQuant retains agreement with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) patients and exhibits a physiologically plausible gravity-dependent perfusion gradient. Analysis was performed on 29 healthy subjects (11 female, age: 19-33 years), 20 COPD patients (three female, age: 46-76 years) and 15 CTEPH patients (six female, age: 44-82 years), scanned at 1.5 T. Healthy subjects underwent four PREFUL scans in two sessions. Patients just underwent one PREFUL and DCE scan. QQuant maps were calculated while applying different Gaussian filter options to ΔS. In patients, PREFUL-derived QQuant maps were coregistered to DCE-derived pulmonary blood flow (PBF) maps for global and voxel-wise correlations. In healthy subjects, the gravity-dependent perfusion gradient was quantified by linear regression of slice-wise QQuant across five coronal slices. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved intrascan and interscan repeatability in healthy subjects (mean bias: ≤ 2.94 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.2) compared with the current slice median setting (mean bias: ≥ 3.75 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.68). Correlations with PBF remained stable after filtering (σ = 1.5) in COPD (filtered vs. default ΔS: global r = 0.57 vs. r = 0.59, voxel-wise r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.32) and CTEPH (global r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.28, voxel-wise r = 0.40 vs. r = 0.41), all significant except global CTEPH. The filtered QQuant maps showed a significant gravity-dependent perfusion gradient (ΔS filtered σ = 1.5) of 1.47 mL/min/100 mL/cm. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved QQuant repeatability while preserving DCE-MRI agreement and is therefore recommended. The observed gravity-dependent perfusion gradient confirms physiological plausibility, supporting potential in clinical use.

articles.title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST-HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase IIa Study.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study.

METHODS: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN.

RESULTS: At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p < 0.001). Two-thirds of treated patients achieved a > 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts.

CONCLUSION: GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959.

articles.title: The psychological experience of body image change in adult stoma patients: A systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Previous research demonstrates that body image concerns are highly prevalent in stoma patients and can significantly limit quality of life, yet the psychological processes underlying these changes remain under-theorized in the literature. This review aims to develop an understanding of the psychological experience of body image change in adult stoma patients.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-ethnography was undertaken of primary, qualitative, English-language research focusing on the psychological experience of body image change in adult stoma patients. Eight hundred and forty-three studies were initially obtained from backwards citation chaining and three databases: Medline, CINAHL and PsychINFO. Methodological quality and risk of bias were evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute Qualitative Checklist.

RESULTS: After screening, 18 studies (n = 602) were included in the synthesis. Three third-order constructs were found across two time phases (immediately after surgery, and living with the stoma): all-consuming shock, visible 'otherness' and fluctuating acceptance. Findings map the trajectory of body image change following stoma formation and identify psychological, social and relational processes associated with continuing distress and adaptation.

CONCLUSIONS: This review moves beyond documenting body image distress in stoma patients to explain the psychological mechanisms through which it develops and fluctuates over time. Stoma formation can disrupt bodily integrity and identity, with distress maintained through self-scrutiny, shame and perceived social exposure. The mechanisms identified provide clear targets for tailored psychosocial support beginning pre-surgery and continuing through recovery to reduce long-term body image distress and improve health-related quality of life.

articles.title: Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin Limits Glucocorticoid-Induced Muscle Wasting by Preserving Estrogen-Dependent Repression of Catabolic Signaling.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Chronic glucocorticoid (GC) therapy induces severe metabolic complications, notably secondary sarcopenia driven by excessive glucocorticoid receptor (GR)-mediated catabolism. Although sex steroids protect skeletal muscle metabolism, the role of sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), the primary determinant of sex steroid bioavailability, in modulating local endocrine crosstalk under GC stress remains unknown.

METHODS: We evaluated the clinical correlation between serum SHBG and endocrine factors in a rheumatology cohort frequently exposed to GC. To establish causality and underlying mechanisms, male and female human SHBG-transgenic (hSHBG-Tg) mice, with or without gonadectomy, and C2C12 myoblasts were challenged with dexamethasone (DXM) to simulate GC-induced muscle atrophy.

RESULTS: In patients with high cumulative GC exposure (≥ 10,000 mg), circulating SHBG strongly inversely correlated with serum myostatin (r = -0.7153, p = 0.0076). In mice, hSHBG-Tg significantly rescued DXM-induced loss of muscle mass (quadriceps, gastrocnemius, tibialis anterior) and grip strength in females; notably, this protection was entirely abolished by ovariectomy. Mechanistically, hSHBG-Tg blunted GR Ser211 phosphorylation and downregulated the ubiquitin ligases Fbxo32 and Trim63, while preserving estrogen receptor (ER) target genes (Tff1 and Pgr).
