In vitro, estradiol antagonized DXM-induced Trim63 transcription via ER, and co-treatment with SHBG sustained this anti-catabolic effect by extending estradiol bioavailability.

CONCLUSIONS: SHBG acts as a promoter of estrogen bioavailability that coordinates a protective endocrine crosstalk, counteracting GR-driven catabolism in female skeletal muscle. These findings identify SHBG as a key metabolic determinant and a promising therapeutic target to prevent corticosteroid-induced muscle wasting.

articles.title: The Process to Caregiver Expertise: A Constructivist Grounded Theory Study of Parents of Infants With Critical Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caregivers of hospitalized infants with critical congenital heart disease (CCHD) experience stress, emotions and contextual challenges with staff and unit culture during their infant's stay in critical care units, especially if the stay is lengthy. These compounding adverse conditions impact a caregiver's ability to learn to care for their infant. The purpose of this constructivist grounded theory study was to construct an explanatory theory, based on the analysis of the caregivers' perspectives, uncovering the process caregivers of hospitalized infants go through to become experts in their infant's care in the critical care setting.

METHODS: Fifteen mothers and one father participated in semistructured and intensive interviews. Data collection, data analysis and theory formation transpired through an iterative process of constant comparison within and among data cases, theoretical sampling, memos, member-checking and participant feedback.

RESULTS: The result was a co-constructed overarching framework, the Process Model to Caregiver Expertise, progressing through four sequential phases-disorienting, orienting, adapting and knowing-showing how caregiver confidence develops over time and through active participation in caregiving tasks. Findings also indicate that caregivers need prompt peer and mentorship connections and early active participation in caregiving tasks to hasten their transformation into independent, expert caregivers.

CONCLUSION: Knowing this process may empower caregivers to understand their journey and guide education, support and tool development for healthcare providers. Additional research is needed to explore the paternal caregiver role, healthcare professionals' perceptions of this process and how the model develops as the child ages.

articles.title: The role of fibrinogen concentrate in the reduction of allogeneic blood product requirements: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrinogen concentrate (FC) has a well-established safety profile and is recommended for treating acquired fibrinogen deficiency. However, its comparative effectiveness vs other treatments regarding transfusions and patient outcomes remains uncertain.

METHODS: Comparative studies from a range of clinical settings in which patients received FC for acquired hypofibrinogenaemia and that evaluated blood product needs, mortality, thromboembolic events, or hospital length of stay were included in a systematic literature review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42024602804). Meta-analyses used pooled data to provide an estimate of the difference in outcome between FC and all other treatments; separate analyses were conducted for adult and paediatric patients.

RESULTS: Overall, 58 studies (N=13 530 patients) were analysed. Adult FC recipients received significantly fewer red blood cell, fresh frozen plasma, and platelet units than with other treatments: 28% (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-0.89; P=0.002), 31% (IRR 0.69; 95% CI 0.54-0.89; P=0.004), and 44% less (IRR 0.56; 95% CI 0.33-0.95; P=0.03), respectively. These results were largely driven by cardiac surgery studies. In an RCT subanalysis, the use and quantity of blood products were significantly reduced with FC. No significant difference in mortality or thromboembolic events was found between treatments in adult patients or in any outcomes analysed in paediatric patients.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests fibrinogen concentrate administered for acquired hypofibrinogenaemia can reduce blood product transfusions in adults, with no obvious safety concerns, compared with other treatments.

articles.title: Association of Caregiver Mental Health and a Childhood Parenting Intervention in China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study examines whether and how caregiver mental health symptoms influence the impacts of a center-based parenting intervention on child development.

METHODS: We conducted a clustered randomized controlled trial across 100 rural villages in China between 2016 and 2019. Villages were randomly assigned to a treatment group that received weekly 1-on-1 parenting sessions through parenting centers or to a pure comparison group. A total of 2554 caregiver-child dyads with children aged 6 to 24 months were surveyed at baseline, and 2044 completed the endline survey after 1 year (follow-up rate: 80.0%). Child development was assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development, Third Edition. Caregiver mental health was measured using the Depression Anxiety and Stress Scale-21. Ordinary least squares regressions with interaction terms were used for analysis.

RESULTS: The intervention significantly improved cognitive (β = 0.17 SD; 95% CI 0.045-0.29) and language development (β = 0.10 SD; 95% CI 0.00-0.21) among children whose caregivers did not exhibit depressive symptoms at baseline. Positive cognitive effects were also observed among children of caregivers with low anxiety (β = 0.13 SD; 95% CI 0.00-0.26) or low stress (β = 0.15 SD; 95% CI 0.03-0.27). In contrast, no significant effects were detected across developmental domains among children whose caregivers exhibited mental health symptoms. Heterogeneous impacts were driven by differences in stimulating parenting practices rather than program attendance or parenting beliefs.

CONCLUSIONS: The intervention primarily benefited children whose caregivers had no baseline mental health symptoms, suggesting caregiver mental health moderates intervention effects.

articles.title: Mycoplasma genitalium prevalence, bacterial load, and antibiotic resistance in paired vaginal and anal specimens from Chlamydia trachomatis-infected women.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and public health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycoplasma genitalium (MG) frequently co-infects women with Chlamydia trachomatis (CT), but the epidemiology and clinical significance of this association remain poorly understood. This study assessed MG positivity, antimicrobial resistance, mgpB genotyping and bacterial load in paired self-collected vaginal and anal swabs from 426 women with urogenital CT infection, and assessed the risk factors for CT/MG coinfection compared with CT monoinfection.

METHODS: MG detection and quantification were carried out using an in-house quantitative PCR targeting the MgPa adhesin gene. Macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance-associated mutations were determined by sequencing the 23S RNA gene and the parC gene, respectively. The mgpB types were determined by sequencing a 281-bp region of the mgpB gene. Clinical, demographic, and behavioural characteristics were compared between women with CT monoinfection and CT/MG coinfection.

RESULTS: MG was detected in 22.8% of women, more frequently in vaginal than anal specimens (18.5% vs 12.9%, p = 0.03). Among MG-positive women, 43.3% had vaginal-only infection, 18.6% anal-only infection, and 38.1% infection at both sites. Macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance were detected in 16.7% and 9.1% of evaluable cases, respectively. Anal MG was usually asymptomatic and unrelated to reported anal intercourse. MG bacterial load was significantly higher in vaginal than anal samples, and paired specimens shared identical mgpB genotypes, supporting the hypothesis of secondary anal colonization from the vagina. Being born in France was the only factor associated with CT/MG coinfection, compared with CT monoinfection in the multivariate analysis. MG coinfection did not influence the CT bacterial load.

CONCLUSIONS: MG coinfection was common among women with CT infection but was not associated with higher CT bacterial load, more severe clinical manifestations, or distinct behavioural characteristics. Further studies are warranted to clarify the biological interactions between these two pathogens in women.

articles.title: A 12-week randomized controlled trial of the dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH) diet in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis: Effects on disease activity and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Dietary interventions may improve rheumatoid arthritis (RA) outcomes through anti-inflammatory and metabolic pathways. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on disease activity and treatment outcomes in patients with seropositive RA.

METHODS: In this 12-week parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 82 patients with seropositive RA were randomly assigned to a DASH diet intervention (n = 40) or a control group maintaining their usual diet (n = 42). The primary outcome was change in disease activity assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS-28 E SR). Secondary outcomes included change in DAS-28 based on C-reactive protein (DAS-28 CRP), as well as tender and swollen joint counts, ESR, CRP, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for pain and general health, the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), and the Short Form-36 (SF-36). Adherence to the intervention was evaluated using the DASH diet score. Assessments were performed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Data were analyzed according to the intention-to-treat principle. Repeated clinical outcomes were analyzed using robust mixed ANOVA or generalized estimating equations (GEE), as appropriate.

RESULTS: Of the 82 randomized patients, 49 completed the 12-week study. Adherence to the DASH diet increased significantly in the intervention group compared with the control group (p < 0.001). From baseline to Week 12, DAS-28 ESR decreased by 0.92 points in the DASH group versus 0.17 points in the control group, corresponding to a 0.75-point greater reduction (group × time interaction, p = 0.001). Significant between-group differences in change were also observed for DAS-28 CRP (-0.62), ESR (-3.90 mm/h), VAS-pain (-2.19), VAS-general health (-2.12), and HAQ (-0.38) (all group × time p˂0.05). For SF-36, significant between-group differences in change were observed for physical functioning (+10.15), role-physical (+47.30), bodily pain (+22.17), vitality (+18.52), role-emotional (+38.61), and mental health (+12.06) (all group × time p < 0.05). CRP, tender and swollen joint counts did not show significant group × time interactions (p > 0.05). Furthermore, in the intervention group, improvements in DASH diet adherence were negatively correlated with changes in DAS-28 ESR and DAS-28 CRP scores (both p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: A 12-week DASH dietary intervention may provide clinically meaningful improvements in disease activity and patient-reported outcomes in patients with seropositive RA. These findings support the potential role of the DASH dietary pattern as a promising dietary approach to complement the management of RA. However, the relatively high attrition rate should be considered when interpreting the findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered with Clinicaltrials.gov (ID: NCT07170033). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07170033.

articles.title: Expanded Longitudinal Validation of Adaptive Learning Stability in AI-Assisted Neurosurgical Residency Training.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the longitudinal stability, reproducibility, and robustness of Adaptive Learning Stability (ALS) within an expanded AI-assisted neurosurgical residency cohort during a 12-month observation cycle.

DESIGN: This was a prospective controlled educational study. Residents completed 4 consecutive quarterly checkpoints integrating cognitive, technical, and decision-making assessments over 12 months. The RCKaS-AI framework incorporated predictive analytics, individualized adaptive remediation, and mentor-validated feedback pathways. Primary analysis evaluated longitudinal entrustment trajectory stability across checkpoints. Secondary analyses included inter-resident variance dynamics, remediation frequency, faculty workload, and predictive agreement between forecasted and observed competency progression.

SETTING: Two accredited neurosurgical residency programs in Kazakhstan, from January 2025 to January 2026.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixty-four neurosurgical residents randomized into standard RCKaS (n = 32) and AI-enhanced RCKaS-AI (n = 32) cohorts.

RESULTS: Both cohorts demonstrated progressive improvement in entrustment scores across sequential checkpoints. In the RCKaS-AI cohort, mean entrustment scores increased from 59.1 ± 12.8 at CP1 to 94.3 ± 6.9 at CP4, compared with 58.4 ± 13.1 to 85.7 ± 10.4 under standard RCKaS conditions (p = 0.001). Inter-resident variance decreased by 41% in the AI-assisted cohort versus 18% in the standard cohort. Residents within the RCKaS-AI framework achieved entrustment level 4 significantly earlier than controls (38 ± 7 weeks vs 50 ± 9 weeks, p = 0.003). Mean remediation frequency decreased from 3.4 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 0.7 sessions per resident, while faculty workload declined by 34%. Predictive analytics demonstrated strong agreement between forecasted and observed competency trajectories (r = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77-0.89).

CONCLUSIONS: Expanded longitudinal implementation of the RCKaS-AI framework demonstrated reproducible stabilization of competency trajectories during neurosurgical residency training. These findings support the robustness of adaptive AI-assisted feedback systems as a practical mechanism for longitudinal competency regulation within structured surgical education programs. Further multicenter validation is required to evaluate external reproducibility across broader residency environments.

articles.title: Effectiveness of psychosocial interventions addressing informal caregivers' mental health: an umbrella systematic review with 26,481 participants.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions on informal caregivers' mental health, organized by the clinical condition(s) of the care recipient.

METHODS: We conducted an umbrella systematic review and random-effects meta-analyses to pool the results of the included studies for each combination of clinical condition, intervention type, comparison and outcome.

RESULTS: We included 19 systematic reviews and 50 meta-analyses, with 26,481 participants. Several interventions improved mental health outcomes in caregivers, and across various clinical conditions of the care recipients. In dementia caregivers, multicomponent interventions significantly reduced depressive and anxiety symptoms, and caregiver burden (SMD from -0.65 to -0.19). For caregivers of people with lung cancer, psychoeducation and psychological support reduced depressive (SMD = -1.66, 95% CI -3.19 to -0.13) and anxiety symptoms (SMD = -1.37, 95% CI -2.54 to -0.21). Multicomponent interventions reduced depressive and anxiety symptoms in parents of children with cancer (SMD = -0.38, 95% CI -0.64 to -0.12; SMD = -0.89, 95% CI -1.33 to -0.45). Caregiver burden of caregivers of people with psychosis and schizophrenia decreased after psychoeducation and skills-training (SMD = -2.10, 95% CI -3.46 to -0.74; SMD = -0.94, 95% CI -1.72 to -0.17). Certainty of evidence was low to moderate, and the strength of association was overall weak.

CONCLUSIONS: We rigorously assessed the quality, certainty of evidence, and the strength of associations. Despite the appraisals highlighting the need for further high-quality research, our results can inform policy and practice on the use of psychosocial interventions for caregivers of people with different clinical conditions.

articles.title: Digital health technologies for the prevention and management of urinary tract infections in menopausal women: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary tract infections are among the most common infectious diseases in women, with incidence increasing after menopause. The genitourinary syndrome of menopause increases susceptibility to recurrent urinary tract infections through urogenital atrophy and microbiome disruption, compounding the risk of antimicrobial resistance.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesise evidence on digital health technologies for the prevention and management of urinary tract infections in menopausal women.

METHODS: Four databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane) were systematically searched from January 2000 to March 2026 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Study quality was assessed using risk-of-bias and critical appraisal tools. Menopausal status was classified as explicitly, proxy or not reported.

RESULTS: Of 9935 records identified, 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Four technology clusters emerged: patient-facing digital interventions (n = 4), predictive machine-learning models (n = 7), clinician-facing electronic health record-integrated decision support systems (n = 2), and point-of-care biosensors (n = 1). Digital tools reduced inappropriate antibiotic prescribing by up to 60% and ciprofloxacin use by 80.5%. Predictive models achieved discrimination values of 0.57-0.96 but lacked prospective validation. No study applied formal staging criteria for reproductive aging or integrated hormonal variables. Time to diagnosis and treatment were not assessed.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital health technologies show potential for antimicrobial stewardship in menopausal women with urinary tract infections but remain largely insensitive to menopause-specific biological factors. One randomised controlled trial demonstrated increased uptake of vaginal oestrogen therapy with the use of these technologies, providing evidence of digitally supported non-antibiotic prevention. Future research should integrate menopausal staging, hormonal variables, and user-centred design.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251052764.

articles.title: Toxic cascade from oxidative stress to metabolic imbalance in Manila clams exposed to polyethylene terephthalate microplastics.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most abundant plastic pollutants in marine environments. However, compared with other polymers, research on PET microplastics (MPs)-particularly their impact on benthic organisms in sediment environments-remains relatively scarce. In this study, we exposed Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) to PET MPs in fragments and fibers of five sizes at concentrations of 0.8, 8, and 80 mg/kg dry weight (dw) of sediment for 21 days using a water-sediment exposure system. Mortality in Manila clams exposed to PET MPs remained unchanged, and each MP group accumulated in the digestive glands and gills. Chronic exposure to PET MPs increased reactive oxygen species production and SOD, IL-1β, and CASP8 levels in the gill and digestive gland tissues of clams. Integrated biomarker response analysis showed stronger correlations for fragments than for fibers, and for larger than smaller sizes, in both gill and digestive gland tissues. Furthermore, omics analysis confirmed a strong response in inflammation-related factors to fragment MPs, suggesting that PET MPs induce oxidative stress, inflammation, and cellular responses that lead to digestive and secretory dysfunction, which may cause morphological and metabolic changes in clams and ultimately adversely affect their health and survival. This study contributes to our understanding of the toxic mechanisms of PET MPs, focusing on their size and shape, and ultimately raises awareness of their harmful effects in the environment.

articles.title: Structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders: an ESGE-ESHRE-IFFS international consensus†ǂ.
authors: International Hysteroscopy Working Group of ESGE, ESHRE and IFFS
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: How should the findings of diagnostic hysteroscopy in women with reproductive disorders be reported?

SUMMARY ANSWER: This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders.

WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups.

STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: A dedicated working group from ESGE, ESHRE, and IFFS collaborated to develop a consensus for comprehensive structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive problems.

PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: This consensus paper focuses on grouping diagnostic hysteroscopic findings, structuring their reporting, and adopting standardized terminology for women with reproductive disorders. The virtual Nominal Group Technique, a structured consensus-building method, was adopted to ensure equal contribution from all members in the development of the final consensus.

MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia.

LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: The inclusion of a finding in this structured report is not a proof of its clinical significance, but it could be used as a validation tool for further research.

WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: The standardized reporting of hysteroscopic findings promotes consistent data collection across centers and could help inform research and exchange of clinical experience, enhancing the value of hysteroscopy in fertility evaluation.

FUNDING: No external funding was received for the development of the consensus process or manuscript preparation.

DISCLOSURES: All authors declare that they have no competing interests.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

articles.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
articles.abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Male Partner Treatment for Bacterial Vaginosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is the commonest vaginal infection globally, resulting from a shift from Lactobacillus-dominant microbiota to an overgrowth of anaerobes. Although standard antibiotic therapy achieves short-term cure, recurrence remains high. Recent evidence suggests that male genital microbiota is a potential reservoir for BV-associated bacteria (BVAB), prompting investigation into the role of concurrent male partner treatment (MPT). We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to assess the effect of MPT on BV recurrence and cure. The study followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251132582). Embase, Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed databases were searched independently, from 1980 to September 2025. Pooled risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2 and GRADE. Eight randomized controlled trials were included. MPT showed no significant effect on BV recurrence (RR 0.92; 95% CI 0.69-1.23; I2 = 64%) or cure rate (RR 1.01; 95% CI 0.94-1.07; I2 = 46%). Adverse events were mild and similar across groups (RD 0.04; 95% CI 0.02-0.11). However, lower recurrence was observed among fully adherent couples, particularly in a recent trial using combined oral and topical therapy. While the overall pooled effect of routine partner treatment is neutral, a benefit may exist among fully adherent couples receiving intensive regimens. Targeted approaches that optimize regimen intensity and adherence warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Understanding the Mortality Trends in Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and Cardiomyopathy: A 25-Year Retrospective Analysis From 1999-2024.
articles.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular Arrhythmias (VA) associated with Cardiomyopathy (CM) continues to be the major cause of death. However, a national longitudinal study examining mortality trends from these conditions is still lacking. This study assessed mortality trends due to these conditions among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2024.

METHODS: An observational analysis of U.S. mortalities due to VA in patients with CM (ICD-10 I47.2, I49.0 and I25.5, I42 respectively), was conducted using CDC WONDER. Adjusted Mortality Rates (AAMR) per 100,000 calculated and trends were assessed by calculating Average and Annual Percent Change (AAPC, APC), using joinpoint regression stratified by year, sex, race, and region.

RESULTS: From 1999 to 2024, 81,204 VA with CM-related deaths occurred with the overall AAMR declined from 2.54 in 1999 to 1.01 in 2024 (AAPC: -3.55%; p < 0.000001). AAMRs decreased from 1999 to 2007 (APC: -7.93), remained stable till 2022 (APC: -0.66), and dropped by 2024 (APC: -6.87). Men exhibited greater AAMRs (2.42) than women (0.68). Racially, the AAMRs were most pronounced in Non-Hispanic (NH) Blacks (1.97), followed by NH Whites (1.42), whereas Hispanics and NH Others experienced similar AAMRs of 0.97. Geographically, Delaware and the Western regions experienced the highest rates of mortality (2.2 and 1.53, respectively). Urban areas had higher AAMRs than rural settings (1.45 vs. 1.4) CONCLUSION: Although VA-CM mortality has declined over the past two decades, differences by race, sex, and geography remain, underscoring the need for targeted healthcare strategies.

articles.title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.

articles.title: Remission in moderate-to-severe pediatric asthma: Definitions, assessment, prevalence, predictors, and outcomes-a scoping review.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remission is emerging as a novel therapeutic target in asthma, particularly with the advent of biologic therapies. Although spontaneous remission is recognized in mild childhood asthma, little is known about the concept of remission in children with moderate-to-severe asthma.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to synthesize available evidence on definitions, assessment methods, prevalence, predictors, and long-term outcomes of remission in children with moderate-to-severe asthma.

METHODS: This scoping review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidance. MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched from 2003 onward. Eligible studies included randomized clinical trials and observational studies involving children or adolescents with moderate-to-severe asthma that reported remission or remission-related subdomains.

RESULTS: Of 2076 records identified, 8 studies met inclusion criteria (1 trial, 7 observational). Definitions of remission varied substantially and predominantly relied on clinical criteria (absence of symptoms or medication use), with inconsistent incorporation of lung function and none including inflammatory biomarkers. Remission prevalence ranged widely, from 4% to 41.9%, with the highest rates observed in a recent biologic trial; however, assessment periods were highly variable, ranging from 24 weeks to 3 years. Predictors of a lower likelihood of remission included female sex, atopy, and older age at initial diagnosis. Available evidence suggests a persistent risk of subclinical inflammation and relapse despite achieving clinical remission.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on remission in moderate-to-severe pediatric asthma remains limited and heterogeneous, often in the context of ongoing treatment. Standardized, multidomain definitions are urgently needed to inform treat-to-target strategies and future clinical trials.

articles.title: "I don't have to choose between everything": Self-reported fruit and vegetable affordability, purchasing shifts, and healthcare utilization among produce prescription program participants in North Carolina.
articles.abstract: Objective. Examine self-reported fruit and vegetable affordability, purchasing shifts, and healthcare utilization among produce prescription program participants in North Carolina, US. Methods. We conducted cross-sectional online surveys in September-October 2022 and July 2023 among participants in two produce prescription programs (total n = 726) in North Carolina, US. We report descriptive statistics for whether participants could afford fruits, vegetables, and other items, and use bivariate regression models to explore if these vary by demographic characteristics and food insecurity risk. We additionally describe the non-fruit-and-vegetable items participants purchased. Results. One-quarter (27.3%) of participants reported being able to afford fruits and vegetables before participating whereas 91.2% reported being able to afford them while participating. Over half (59.2%) of participants reported that they were able to reallocate personal funds to purchase other items (e.g., meat/proteins, staple foods, dairy, household supplies) and could thus support their families and children. Fewer participants reported shopping at mass merchandisers (-15.5%-point), dollar stores (-8.3%-point), and warehouse club stores (-6.5%-point) while participating, and over one-third (38.9%) of participants were more likely to go to their healthcare provider. Conclusions. Produce prescription programs in North Carolina improve self-reported affordability and access to health-promoting foods, support household needs, and enhance healthcare utilization.

articles.title: Familiarity With and Use of Clinical Prediction Models in Nephrology Practice in Poland.
Network Meta-Analysis: Treatments for Acute Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol-related hepatitis (AH) is an acute form of liver disease with a high short-term mortality. A variety of treatments have been explored in randomised studies. Recent consensus on study outcomes has identified 90-day survival as the primary outcome metric.

AIMS: This systematic review and network meta-analysis is to update understanding of the comparative efficacy of treatments for AH, based on 90-day survival, to inform future Phase III studies.

METHODS: PubMed, Ovid-Medline and Embase were searched for randomised studies of treatments of AH. The risk of bias in included papers was measured using the Cochrane risk of bias 2 tool. Data were synthesised with network meta-analysis to estimate risk ratio (RR) of survival at 90 days after randomisation. Heterogeneity was assessed with the magnitude of the between-study variance (tau2).

RESULTS: Thirty five studies including 5045 participants were identified that examined 24 treatments for AH. Twenty-three studies were considered to be at low risk of bias. In network meta-analysis considering placebo as the reference treatment, only granulocyte colony stimulating factor (GCSF) showed a statistically significant benefit on 90-day mortality (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.28-0.84; p = 0.009). In subgroup analysis of studies at low risk of bias, no treatments showed a significant effect on mortality at 90 days.

CONCLUSIONS: Individual studies are small and heterogeneity is marked; however, some agents show promise to improve survival at 90 days in people with AH. This information should inform adequately powered studies to explore potential treatments for AH.

articles.title: Missed Diagnosis in Alcohol-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Call for Alcohol Consumption and Liver Disease Early Detection.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma is an increasingly prevalent consequence of alcohol use and the often-silent progression of alcohol-related liver disease. A substantial proportion of patients with alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma are diagnosed at an advanced stage, frequently because underlying liver disease has not been previously identified and surveillance has not been implemented. This review summarizes recent epidemiological trends and clinical features of alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma, with a particular focus on the high proportion of undiagnosed cirrhosis and the challenges posed by alcohol use disorder, comorbidities and socioeconomic vulnerability. Strengthening collaboration between hepatology and addiction medicine, alongside population-level strategies to reduce alcohol use, will be essential to enhance surveillance uptake and ultimately improve outcomes in alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma.

articles.title: Can't Name It, Can't Log Off: Alexithymia and Problematic Internet-Related Behaviors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Alexithymia has been proposed as a ransdiagnostic vulnerability for behavioral addictions, but its role in problematic Internet-related behaviors (PIB) has not been quantified across phenotypes and populations. We conducted a preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses. Major databases were searched in October 2025 for studies reporting quantitative associations between alexithymia and PIB (problematic Internet, smartphone, social media, gaming use, or cyberbullying). Risk of bias was appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Random-effects models pooled correlations and standardized regression coefficients; three-level and robust-variance models accounted for multiple effects per study and examined moderators and adjustment for internalizing symptoms. Eighty-three studies met inclusion criteria; 78 independent samples (N = 42,478; 369 effect sizes total, comprising 302 zero-order correlations and 67 standardized regression coefficients) contributed to the meta-analysis. The pooled correlation between alexithymia and PIB was r = 0.36 (95% confidence interval 0.34-0.38; I2 = 77.6%). Associations were stronger for addictive-use PIB (r = 0.37) than for cyberbullying (r = 0.29), broadly comparable across world regions, and tended to be larger in adults than adolescents. In multivariable models, coefficients attenuated from about β = 0.37 to β = 0.18 after controlling for depression, anxiety, and other internalizing symptoms, but remained statistically significant. Sensitivity and publication-bias analyses indicated that the association was robust. Alexithymia shows a moderate association with PIB across age groups, partly via shared variance with internalizing psychopathology but also through unique pathways. Longitudinal and mechanistic studies should test whether targeting emotional awareness can help prevent or reduce PIB.

articles.title: Postoperative Vasoactive Exposure Patterns and Outcomes After Non-Cardiac Surgery: A Prespecified Analysis of the SQUEEZE Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative vasoactive therapy is usually summarised by its presence or duration, although haemodynamic support evolves over time. We investigated whether reproducible postoperative vasoactive exposure patterns provide prognostic information beyond the duration of postoperative vasoactive therapy.

METHODS: We performed a prespecified substudy of the international SQUEEZE cohort. Adults receiving postoperative vasoactive infusion within seven postoperative days after non-cardiac surgery were included. Unsupervised k-means clustering identified exposure patterns using duration of postoperative vasoactive infusion, cumulative vasoactive agent-days, and peak number of concurrent agents. Associations with 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and hospital length of stay were assessed using multivariable regression. A prespecified landmark analysis evaluated early postoperative vasoactive exposure burden during postoperative days 0-1.

RESULTS: Among 25,672 patients, 6676 (26.0%) received postoperative vasoactive infusion. Four reproducible exposure patterns were identified. Adjusted 30-day mortality ranged from 9.7% in the low-burden pattern to 35.3% in the high-burden pattern but was not strictly monotonic, whereas adjusted AKI risk increased from 28.0% to 56.0% across patterns. In covariate-adjusted models fitted to the same complete-case cohort, discrimination was higher when exposure pattern rather than duration was included (AUC 0.818 vs. 0.795), while adding duration to pattern classification resulted in little additional discrimination (AUC 0.819). Findings were consistent in the early postoperative landmark analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative vasoactive exposure follows reproducible patterns characterised by persistence and overall treatment burden rather than binary classification alone. These patterns were associated with mortality, AKI, and hospital length of stay, and provided prognostic information beyond duration alone.

EDITORIAL COMMENT: This substudy and analysis of the SQUEEZE cohort, which represents a large sample of cases with focus on post-operative vasopressor treatments, shows that more intensive vasopressor therapy was associated with worse postoperative outcomes, including for mortality and 30 days and postoperative acute kidney injury occurrence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03805230.

articles.title: Impaired lung function as an important risk factor for blood stream infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association of impaired lung function with blood stream infections has only been studied for a limited number of pathogens. We tested the hypothesis that impaired lung function is independently associated with higher risk of any blood stream infections and by specific pathogens in the general population.

METHODS: Copenhagen General Population Study participants had spirometry performed at baseline and were followed for up to 10 years with linkage to the Danish Microbiology Database. The 10-year absolute risk, multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR), and population attributable fraction for blood stream infections were determined according to impaired lung function. Outcomes were any and pathogen-specific blood stream infections.

RESULTS: In 118,565 participants, we identified 4160 blood stream infections among 3438 individuals during 950,718 person-years of follow-up. The HR was 1.5 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.4-1.7) for individuals with obstructive spirometric pattern and 1.4 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.2-1.5) for individuals with PRISm. The HR for blood stream infections were 1.4 (95% CI: 1.3-1.6) for forced expiratory volume 1-s (FEV1) 50-79% predicted and HR 2.5 (95% CI: 2.0-3.2) for FEV1 below 50% of predicted. A similar pattern was seen for all pathogen specific blood stream infections. The 10-year risk of blood stream infections was 5.4.3% (95% CI: 5.1-5.9) and 4.3% (95% CI: 3.9-4.7) for individuals with PRISm and obstructive spirometric pattern, respectively. The population-attributable fraction of blood stream infections attributable to abnormal spirometric pattern was 9.5% (95% CI: 6.4%-12.7%).

CONCLUSION: Impaired lung function is an important risk factor for blood stream infections and not limited to respiratory tract pathogens.

articles.title: Emerging novel therapies for the treatment of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.
articles.abstract: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is the second most common heritable bleeding disorder worldwide, with a prevalence more than twice that of haemophilia, and is the most morbid inherited bleeding disorder of women. As an autosomal dominant vasculopathy due to dysregulated angiogenic signalling, patients with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia develop telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations which cause numerous complications. These complications include moderate-to-severe chronic epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, iron deficiency anemia, and requirement for intravenous iron or red cell transfusion. Additionally, incidence of intracranial haemorrhage is high and morbid non-bleeding complications, such as venous thromboembolism, stroke, and liver disease, are common. Despite this serious disease burden, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia remains without licensed therapies worldwide. However, many novel, investigational agents targeting vascular and haemostatic systems are now rapidly undergoing formal development specifically in hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia. These agents include the selective AKT1/AKT2 inhibitor engasertib, AKT1-selective inhibitors ATV-1601 and TER-4480, plasminogen siRNA agent ALN-6400, activin receptor-like kinase 1-bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II (ALK1-BMPRII) bispecific clustering antibody DIAG723, and apelin receptor antagonist antibody TX2100. This comprehensive Review provides essential background information and illustrations summarising relevant hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia pathophysiology, followed by focused, detailed discussions of each of the novel agents in development, including the mechanisms, therapeutic rationale, clinical trial programmes, and potential therapeutic effects.

articles.title: Altered stimulus-intensity encoding occurs in the primary somatosensory cortex of a central post-stroke pain rat model.
articles.abstract: Central post-stroke pain (CPSP) is a chronic form of pain that develops after ventral posterolateral thalamus (VPL) lesions and may involve maladaptive plasticity within central somatosensory pathways. Although abnormalities in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) are observed in patients and animal models, the mechanism by which thalamic lesions alter cortical processing of sensory stimuli remains unclear. Here, we investigated stimulus intensity encoding and dendritic remodeling in S1 using a VPL-lesion CPSP rat model. Behavioral assessments were conducted, and mechanical allodynia was observed 3 weeks after lesion induction. Accordingly, the animals were examined during the early (1 week) and late (4-5 weeks) phases after VPL lesions. A distorted stimulus-response relationship was observed in S1 during the late phase, as indicated from voltage-sensitive dye imaging. The responses to low-intensity stimuli were enhanced, and response scaling at higher stimulus intensities was reduced. Increased cortical sensitivity to weak stimuli was associated with the severity of mechanical allodynia. Additionally, morphological analyses were conducted on layer II/III pyramidal neurons. Distinct patterns of dendritic remodeling were observed. Apical dendritic length and branching diminished during the early phase, while basal dendritic arborization increased during the late phase. These findings suggest that time-dependent structural and functional reorganization occurs in S1 following thalamic injury. This reorganization may contribute to abnormal sensory processing in patients with CPSP and offer new insights into the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

articles.title: Real-world effectiveness of dupilumab in patients with severe asthma in Europe: Findings from the EU-ADVANTAGE study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dupilumab is approved in Europe for severe asthma (SA) characterized by type 2 inflammation. However, real-world effectiveness data from European countries are limited. EU-ADVANTAGE study aimed to evaluate the real-world effectiveness of dupilumab across five European Union (EU) countries: France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and Spain.

METHODS: This retrospective chart review study leveraged patient medical records captured by physicians within their clinical practice across 5 EU countries. Patients (≥12 years) with physician-confirmed SA who initiated dupilumab (index) between May 2019 and February 2022 and had 12 months of pre- and post-index data were included. SA exacerbations, oral corticosteroid (OCS) prescriptions, and healthcare resource utilization were compared between the 12-month pre- and post-dupilumab initiation. Poisson regression models with robust variance were used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for SA exacerbations and OCS prescriptions, after adjusting for COVID-19 and seasonality.

RESULTS: Overall, 1281 patient records (mean ± standard deviation age, 46.0 ± 15.6 years; males, 61.4%) were extracted by 547 physicians. Most patients (91.3%) were biologic naïve before dupilumab initiation. A significant 50% reduction in SA exacerbations (IRR, 0.50; 95%CI, 0.41-0.61) was observed post-dupilumab initiation despite a concurrent 68% reduction in OCS prescriptions (IRR, 0.32; 95%CI, 0.25-0.41) (both P < 0.001). Consistent reductions were observed in patients with type 2 inflammatory subgroup. Overall, 9.2% and 3.1% of patients had ≥1 hospitalization during the pre- and post-dupilumab initiation, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study, dupilumab was associated with a significant reduction in SA exacerbations and OCS prescriptions, confirming its utility in routine clinical settings.

articles.title: Hernia, mesh, microbes, and phage promise: Mapping 35 years of evidence through a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and public health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthetic mesh is the standard of care for hernia repair; however, mesh-related infections remain a significant biological challenge, with pooled data showing significant morbidity, recurrence, and elevated explantation risk. This study summarises microbiological trends documented over three decades of research, characterises the microbial landscape associated with mesh infections, and investigates how various mesh materials are associated with pathogen colonisation.

AIMS: The objectives are to (i) analyse the aetiology and microbial distribution in mesh-associated infections, (ii) assess the frequency of infection-related events, including mesh removal and postoperative complications, across mesh types and surgical approaches, (iii) describe study population characteristics and procedural contexts where infections occurred, (iv) identify temporal patterns in published reports, and (v) evaluate variables associated with infection-related outcomes as reported in the literature.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, systematic searches (1990-2025) yielded 4000 records; 584 studies met inclusion criteria, and 32 were eligible for meta-analysis, with uniform groupings by mesh type (polypropylene, biologic, composite, biosynthetic) and period (1990-2007, 2008-2025). Analytical outcomes included incisional hernia rates, surgical site infections (SSIs), explantations, and relevant patient factors, using random-effects modelling.

RESULTS: Of the 1213 studies screened, 584 met the inclusion criteria, and 32 were included in the meta-analysis. Mesh use did not correlate with a consistent reduction of surgical site infections (HR: 0.90; p = 0.396). Mesh explantation was significantly correlated with chronic infections (HR: 6.11; p < 0.0001). Polypropylene meshes are most commonly associated with polymicrobial infections, mostly caused by S. aureus, E. coli, and P. aeruginosa. This trend may be a reporting bias, as polypropylene meshes are the most commonly used meshes worldwide. No clinical studies were found for phage-coated meshes. Preclinical evidence demonstrates the strong antimicrobial potential of phage therapy on mesh materials, but clinical efficacy has not been studied yet.

CONCLUSION: The review summarises over 3 decades of hernia mesh research covering the use of mesh composition and materials, associated complications and infection management. With the rise of antibiotic resistance, bacteriophages are becoming a promising alternative for the treatment of mesh infections.

articles.title: Dietary patterns and adverse pregnancy outcomes: Complementary insights from a priori and a posteriori approaches in a prospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Maternal diet during pregnancy may influence fetal growth, but evidence based on dietary-pattern approaches remains scarce. We characterized prenatal dietary patterns in a pregnancy cohort using two a priori diet-quality indices and an unsupervised a posteriori data-driven approach, and evaluated their associations with gestational and neonatal outcomes, and assessed the overlap between both methodological approaches.

METHODS: We analyzed 595 mother-infant dyads from the Nutrition in Early Life and Asthma (NELA) birth cohort. Maternal diet at 19-22 weeks' gestation was assessed using a validated 123-item food frequency questionnaire. Adherence to the Mediterranean diet and to the Planetary Health diet was quantified using the relative Mediterranean Diet score (rMED) and the Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI). In addition, we used principal components analysis (PCA) on energy-adjusted food groups, and then hierarchical clustering on the retained scores to identify real-world dietary patterns. Multivariable linear regression analysis was used to explore the association between dietary patterns and gestational weight gain (GWG), neonatal birth weight, and head circumference. A multinomial logistic regression model assessed the capacity of a priori indices to predict cluster membership, evaluated through McFadden's pseudo-R2, overall accuracy, and Cohen's kappa.

RESULTS: Five dietary clusters were identified, with the following proportion of the population in each cluster: Cluster I (9.7%), Cluster II (31.1%), Cluster III (46.7%), Cluster IV (11.4%), and Cluster V (1.0%). Cluster II showed the highest adherence to both indices (mean rMED 9.4; mean PHDI 85.6). Cluster IV (second highest adherence) was consistently associated with lower GWG and higher birth weight compared with Cluster II in adjusted models (-1.28 kg; 95% CI -2.55 to -0.02 and 134.4 g; 95% CI 30.42 to 238.4, respectively) but not head circumference. No associations were found for the rest of clusters or rMED and PHDI indexes. The comparison between approaches revealed poor classification accuracy (55.5%), and slight-to-fair agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.24).

CONCLUSION: An empirically derived dietary profile characterized by vegetables, tubers, legumes, and dairy intake, was associated with lower GWG and higher birth weight. The limited agreement between approaches highlights that a priori indices and data-driven methods capture complementary dimensions of diet, supporting their combined use.

articles.title: Interactions between vaginal, periurethral and urinary microbiota in genitourinary syndrome of menopause and the effects of local estrogen therapy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Alterations to the vaginal microbiota have been investigated in genitourinary syndrome of menopause but data regarding periurethral and urinary microbiota remain limited. We aimed to characterize vaginal, periurethral, and urinary microbiota in clinically stratified postmenopausal women and to evaluate the effects of estrogen therapy.

STUDY DESIGN: In this prospective study, postmenopausal women were categorized as controls without atrophy or symptoms, women with clinical atrophy without symptoms, symptomatic women, and symptomatic women receiving 12 weeks of vaginal estriol. Vaginal, periurethral, and bladder samples were collected.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Microbiota composition and diversity (alpha diversity - Shannon index; and beta diversity - Bray-Curtis dissimilarity) across urogenital niches and changes in these following estrogen therapy.

RESULTS: Vaginal and periurethral alpha diversity was higher in women with asymptomatic atrophy and symptomatic women at baseline than in controls and estrogen-treated women. Beta diversity analyses demonstrated separation of controls and estrogen-treated women from the atrophy groups at baseline. Controls exhibited Lactobacillus-enriched periurethral communities and Klebsiella-dominant urinary profiles. Women with asymptomatic atrophy and symptomatic women showed reduced Lactobacillus and increased anaerobic taxa in vaginal and periurethral niches, while urinary samples were characterized by Escherichia predominance. Notably, in women with asymptomatic atrophy, Lactobacillus abundance was higher in periurethral than vaginal samples. Estrogen therapy increased Lactobacillus abundance in vaginal and periurethral compartments and shifted urinary microbiota toward a control-like composition. Periurethral Streptococcus abundance correlated with sexual symptom scores.

CONCLUSIONS: Microbial alterations in genitourinary syndrome of menopause are compartment-specific and extend beyond the vagina. Periurethral microbiota may contribute to symptom expression, while local estrogen therapy promotes restoration of Lactobacillus-dominant urogenital microbiota.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov registration: NCT06633705.

articles.title: Guidelines for Decisions to Withhold or Withdraw Life-Sustaining Treatments (LST) in Adult ICU.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine (Société française d'anesthésie et de réanimation, SFAR) and the French Society of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (Société Française de Médecine Physique et de Réadaptation (SOFMER)) aimed at providing guidelines for decisions to withhold or withdraw life-sustaining treatments (LST) in adult ICU.

DESIGN: A consensus committee of 20 experts from the SFAR and the SOFMER was convened. A formal conﬂict-of-interest (COI) policy was developed at the beginning of the process and enforced throughout. The entire guideline construction process was conducted independently of any industrial funding (i.e., pharmaceutical, medical devices). The authors were required to follow the rules of the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system to guide the assessment of the quality of evidence. The potential drawbacks of making strong recommendations in the presence of low-quality evidence were emphasized.

METHODS: 3 fields were defined: (1) modalities of the LST decision-making process; (2) modalities for implementing an LST decision; (3) Relationships with family members, communication, disagreements, and conflicts. For each field, the objective of the recommendations was to answer a number of questions formulated according to the PICO model (population, intervention, comparison, and outcomes). Based on these questions, an extensive bibliographic search was carried out using predefined keywords according to PRISMA guidelines and analyzed using the GRADE® methodology. The recommendations were formulated according to the GRADE® methodology and then voted on by all the experts according to the GRADE® grid method.

RESULTS: The experts' work on synthesis and application of the GRADE® method resulted in 9 recommendations. Among the formalized recommendations, 1 was found to have a high level of evidence (GRADE 1), and 2 had low levels of evidence (GRADE 2). For 6 recommendations, the GRADE® methodology could not be fully applied, resulting in an expert's opinion. 2 questions could not be answered due to a lack of literature. After 1 round of rating, strong agreement was reached for all the recommendations.

CONCLUSIONS: There was strong agreement among experts to provide recommendations to improve practices for decisions to withhold or withdraw LST in the adult ICU.

articles.title: Dynamic change patterns in suicidal ideation differ in Brief Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (BCBT) and Present-Centered Therapy (PCT).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although Brief Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (BCBT) is more effective than Present-Centered Therapy (PCT) for preventing suicide attempts, the two treatments have similar efficacy for reducing suicidal ideation severity. Traditional severity scores may obscure meaningful differences in how specific dimensions of suicidal ideation actually change during treatment. This study examined how quickly and consistently different dimensions of suicidal ideation changed during BCBT and PCT.

METHOD: The first five items of the Scale for Suicidal Ideation (wish to live, wish to die, reasons for living versus dying, suicidal desire, and passive desire for death) were administered at every scheduled therapy session during a randomized clinical trial comparing BCBT to PCT among high-risk U.S. military personnel and veterans. We estimated separate continuous-time multivariate change models for each item and applied eigen-decomposition to the matrix of regression coefficients to characterize dominant change patterns.

RESULTS: In both treatments, some dimensions of suicidal ideation changed quickly while others changed slowly, and change was not evenly distributed across all five dimensions. Dimensions of suicidal ideation changed faster and in greater synchrony during BCBT than PCT.

CONCLUSIONS: Suicidal ideation reductions may arise through qualitatively different change processes across treatments even when the overall magnitude of change is similar. BCBT appeared to produce faster, more coordinated change across dimensions of suicidal ideation whereas PCT produced slower change that was less consistent across dimensions. These findings highlight the value of dynamical systems approaches for understanding mechanisms of therapeutic change that go beyond mean-level severity scores.

articles.title: Incentivizing Faculty and Promoting Engagement in General Surgery Residency Entrustable Professional Activities Assessments.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The American Board of Surgery (ABS) implemented Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) to facilitate transition to competency-based resident assessments in July 2023. To improve faculty engagement, our institution established an intervention with a required target of less than 25% expired faculty EPA assessments for the 2024 to 2025 academic year (AY) to qualify for a shortened end-of-rotation resident evaluation form.

DESIGN: A retrospective review of de-identified institutional EPA data for the AYs 2023 to 2024, preintervention, and 2024 to 2025, postintervention, obtained from the ABS website was conducted. Faculty rater, division, activity name, phase of care, entrustability score, and narrative feedback were analyzed. Descriptive statistics were employed to assess EPA assessment volume, number of faculty raters and evaluations by division, expired assessments, and details by postgraduate training year (PGY). Chi-Square, 2-proportion z-tests, and paired t-tests were employed to compare pre and postintervention EPA assessment completion and qualities.

SETTING: Affiliate hospitals of the Medical College of Wisconsin including Froedtert Hospital, a tertiary referral center in Milwaukee; Clement J. Zablocki Veteran's Affairs Hospital; and 3 community hospitals in the Milwaukee area.

PARTICIPANTS: De-identified data from general surgery residents and faculty who completed any EPA assessment in AYs 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 were included.

RESULTS: A total of 1111 and 1464 EPA assessments were completed for the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 AYs, respectively, yielding a 1.32-fold increase post-intervention. There was a 1.27-fold increase in participating faculty raters (63 vs 80). Meaningful narrative feedback increased from 53.3% to 57.8% (p = 0.02). Of 11 service rotations with participating faculty raters, 5 met the <25% EPA assessment expiration metric in 2023 to 2024, compared to 8 in 2024 to 2025. The overall EPA assessment expiration rate decreased from 40.0% pre-intervention to 13.9% postintervention (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Incentivizing faculty to improve upon expired EPA assessments using a shortened end-of-rotation resident evaluation form increased EPA assessment completion, improved narrative feedback quality, and decreased expired EPA assessments. Initiatives to motivate faculty and residents to engage in timely and high-quality feedback will aid the ongoing transition to competency-based surgical education.

articles.title: The utility of magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord in paediatric transverse myelitis: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to the diagnosis of paediatric acute transverse myelitis (ATM), yet its true diagnostic yield, concordance with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) inflammation, and prognostic value remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify the diagnostic yield of spinal cord MRI in paediatric ATM, evaluate agreement with CSF inflammatory markers, and explore associations between MRI features and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered (CRD42024504846). MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO and CENTRAL were searched from 2006 to October 2025. Observational studies including ≥5 children (≤18 years) with monophasic ATM who underwent spinal cord MRI were eligible. The primary outcome was the proportion of clinically diagnosed ATM cases demonstrating inflammatory spinal cord lesions on MRI. Secondary outcomes included MRI-CSF concordance and associations between imaging findings and long-term outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2.

RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 330 children were included. The pooled diagnostic yield of spinal cord MRI was 97.6% (95% CI 92.2 to 100.0%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=71.8%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 71.2 to 99.6%, indicating that a future paediatric cohort could plausibly report a yield anywhere within that range. Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and gadolinium enhancement were the most frequently reported features. Paired MRI-CSF data were available for 61 patients; discordance was observed in 36%, most commonly MRI-positive with normal CSF. Follow-up data (n = 237) showed 64% achieved good recovery, whereas 30% had severe residual deficits; persistent bladder dysfunction occurred in 31%. Baseline MRI positivity did not reliably predict outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Spinal cord MRI demonstrates a high diagnostic yield in imaged children with clinically diagnosed ATM, but imaging was a condition of cohort entry in most included studies and the pooled estimate is strongly influenced by study design. MRI should be interpreted alongside CSF findings, and baseline imaging alone does not reliably stratify prognosis. Standardised prospective studies are required to refine the diagnostic and prognostic role of MRI in paediatric inflammatory myelopathies.

articles.title: Does COVID-19 Vaccination Protect Against Post-COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, representing an important cause of long-term morbidity and mortality. In addition to preventing primary infection, COVID-19 vaccination has emerged as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to analyse the evidence supporting a causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, based on classical and contemporary epidemiological criteria, including the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model. A qualitative synthesis of the evidence was performed according to the nine BHC and the SCC model. Scientific evidence indicates that COVID-19 vaccination meets four of the nine BHC as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, namely strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. Three criteria, biological plausibility, coherence, and analogy, were partially met. Specificity and experimental evidence were not supported by the available literature. The SCC model highlights the fundamental role of vaccination as a preventive causal component. It also contributes to two criteria, strength of association and temporality, while emphasising the limitation of specificity in causal inference. COVID-19 vaccination has proven effective beyond the acute phase of the disease, with protection extending to a reduced risk of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Comprehensive immunisation strategies and reinfection prevention are essential to mitigate the burden of post-COVID conditions. Additional studies are needed to explore the underlying biological mechanisms, interactions, and the role of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing post-COVID complications.

articles.title: Current review of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists and risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Emerging data has identified a potential association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a typically sudden, painless, and irreversible cause of optic nerve-mediated vision loss. This review synthesizes the current clinical, epidemiologic, and potential mechanism linking GLP-1RA-based therapies to NAION risk, informing balanced risk assessment and interdisciplinary clinical decision-making. A structured PubMed search was performed using terms including "GLP-1 receptor agonist," "semaglutide," "liraglutide," "tirzepatide," and "nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy," in addition to NAION risk factors, including disc-at-risk anatomy, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, renal disease, and ischemic heart disease. A small cup-to-disc ratio ("disc-at-risk") was found to be the most robust anatomical predictor of NAION. Systemic microvascular disease (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia) and conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea and end-stage renal disease were also linked to increased susceptibility to optic nerve head ischemia. Although data across electronic health records, national registries, and pharmacovigilance analyses suggest a very low absolute incidence of NAION, the use of GLP-1RAs demonstrates a statistically significant association with NAION development, yielding relative risk estimates between 1.2 and 4.3. At this time, the potential association between GLP-1RA therapy and NAION should be interpreted as a safety signal rather than a contraindication. Screening for disc-at-risk anatomy, consideration of prior NAION history, and patient counseling regarding acute visual symptoms may be warranted prior to initiation of therapy. As evidence evolves, collaboration between endocrinologists and ophthalmologists will be essential to support safe and effective patient care.

articles.title: Regional diversity of major house dust mite allergens in Spain: Molecular profiles and clinical correlates.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: House dust mites (HDMs) are a major cause of respiratory allergies worldwide. Molecular diagnosis has allowed a more precise characterization of sensitization patterns, which may have clinical and therapeutic relevance. However, large-scale data on molecular HDM sensitization profiles in real-world settings remain limited in Spain.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to determine the seroprevalence and major allergens of HDM molecular components across different Spanish regions and to explore their association with allergic phenotypes, including allergic rhinitis (AR) and asthma.

METHODS: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in 5 Spanish regions. A total of 458 serum samples from patients with suspected HDM allergy were analyzed using a multiplex molecular diagnostic platform. Sensitization was defined as specific IgE ≥ 0.3 kUA/L. Allergens with a prevalence ≥50% were considered major allergens. Associations with AR and asthma were evaluated by prevalence odds ratios (PORs) and chi-square tests.

RESULTS: The most prevalent HDM allergens were Der p 23 (85.2%), Der f 2 (82.3%), Der p 2 (81.0%), Der p 1 (77.5%), and Der f 1 (71.0%). Regional differences were observed, with Galicia showing high sensitization to Gly d 2 and Lep d 2 (both 57%). In the Canary Islands, >50% of patients were sensitized to Gly d 2, Lep d 2, Der p 21, Der p 5, Der p 7, and Blot 5. Sensitization to Blot 5 showed a moderate association with asthma (POR, 3.64), whereas Tyr p 2 was linked to persistent AR (POR, 2.33). Sensitization to Lep d 2 had variable associations with AR severity across regions.

CONCLUSIONS: Der p 23, Der f 2, Der p 2, Der p 1, and Der f 1 are the major HDM allergens in Spain, with regional variability suggesting environmental or genetic modifiers. Certain molecular allergens are associated with more severe or persistent allergic phenotypes, highlighting the value of component-resolved diagnosis for risk stratification and immunotherapy planning.

articles.title: Standardized postpartum blood pressure protocol and lower rates of hypertension at 6 weeks postpartum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) increase the risk of chronic hypertension (HTN) and cardiovascular (CV) disease later in life. It is unknown how strict blood pressure (BP) monitoring postpartum (PP) may affect rates of HTN at 6 weeks PP.

OBJECTIVE: We evaluate the effect of a PP HTN standardized clinical assessment and management plan (SCAMP) on HTN at 6 weeks PP.

STUDY DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study of patients with PP HTN at a quaternary care center for 6 months after enacting an institution-wide SCAMP. The prospective group was compared with historical controls who delivered prior to initiation of the SCAMP. The SCAMP included (1) initiation or uptitration of medication for any BP ≥150/100 or any 2 BPs ≥140/90 within a 24-h period with a goal of BP <140/90 12 h prior to discharge and (2) enrollment in a remote BP monitoring system upon discharge. Inclusion criteria were an existing diagnosis of chronic HTN or HDP and a documented BP at a 6-week PP visit. The primary outcome was HTN, defined as systolic BP (SBP) ≥140 or diastolic BP (DBP) ≥90, at 6 weeks PP. Secondary outcomes included mean BP values as measured in the outpatient setting at 6 weeks PP and use of anti-HTNs at the time of the 6-week PP visit. For all analyses, p values were two-way, and the level of statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Of 780 PP HTN patients in the prospective cohort study, 627 (80.4%) met inclusion criteria for the secondary analysis, 305 in the SCAMP cohort and 322 historical controls. The SCAMP cohort had lower rates of chronic HTN, more patients on anti-HTNs, and higher rate of nifedipine use. The primary outcome of HTN at 6 weeks PP was significantly lower in the SCAMP group (10.5% vs. 18.3%, p = 0.005). After adjusting for confounding variables, multivariable logistic regression showed that the SCAMP group had 38% reduced odds of HTN at 6 weeks PP compared to controls (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.38-0.996; p = 0.048). Mean SBP at 6 weeks PP was significantly lower in the SCAMP group (120 ± 12 vs. 124 ± 14 mmHg, p < 0.001), as was mean DBP (76 ± 8 vs. 81 ± 8 mmHg, p < 0.001). A subanalysis only including patients with diagnosed HDP and excluding those with only chronic HTN demonstrated similar findings.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of a SCAMP was associated with reduced rates of HTN at 6 weeks PP, with lower mean SBP and DBP. More data are needed to evaluate how these findings mitigate long-term HTN risk.

articles.title: Dropout from individual cognitive behavioral psychotherapy for schizophrenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a recommended psychological treatment for schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs), often delivered alongside pharmacotherapy, but dropout may limit its effectiveness. In this secondary analysis of a parent systematic review and meta-analysis focused on negative-symptom outcomes, we synthesized dropout among individual, face-to-face, outpatient CBT arms identified within that parent-review dataset. We investigated exploratory associations between dropout and arm-level sociodemographic, clinical, treatment-related, and study-design characteristics.

STUDY DESIGN: This study was a secondary analysis of a comprehensive database from a recent systematic review and meta-analysis of treatments for SSDs, which searched PsycINFO and all Web of Knowledge databases. Eligible studies were randomized clinical trials that included at least one arm delivering in-person, individual CBT in outpatient settings and reported dropout. Thirteen studies, comprising 16 psychotherapy arms and 865 participants, met eligibility criteria. Random-effects models were used to estimate the pooled dropout rate, and mixed-effects meta-regression models were conducted to examine sociodemographic, clinical, treatment-related, and study-design moderators.

STUDY RESULTS: Across this heterogeneous set of individual CBT arms, the pooled dropout estimate was approximately one in five participants, with substantial between-arm heterogeneity. Associations with available arm-level moderators were exploratory and should not be interpreted as causal or as evidence that a moderator has no effect when the analysis was underpowered.

CONCLUSIONS: This secondary analysis provides a descriptive estimate of dropout within the individual CBT arms retained by the parent review. The estimate is an average across heterogeneous studies and settings, and the moderator analyses are exploratory.

articles.title: Predictors of improvement in personal recovery and activity engagement among mental health service users following a group-based sensory modulation intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health service users often have sensory processing difficulties affecting activity engagement and personal recovery. Since interventions targeting this area are scarce, a group-based sensory modulation intervention was developed.
