To determine in which settings and for whom this intervention has clinical value, this study aimed to investigate whether sociodemographic and clinical baseline characteristics were associated with improvement in personal recovery and activity engagement.

METHODS: This study included participants from the intervention group (N = 107) of a trial (reg.nr: NCT06432114) evaluating an 11-week group-based sensory modulation intervention in mental health outpatient units. Data were collected at baseline, post-intervention, and at 6-month follow-up. Analysis included descriptive statistics and baseline-adjusted multiple linear regression models.

RESULTS: Results showed that the absence of a psychosis diagnosis was associated with a higher mean score of personal recovery at post-intervention (p = 0.003), but not at 6-months follow-up (p = 0.826). There were no significant associations between the predictors and activity engagement.

CONCLUSION: Most predictors in the models were not significantly associated with improvement across any of the outcomes. This suggests that improvement in personal recovery and activity engagement, following the intervention, was accessible to the diverse group of mental health service users, independent of their baseline characteristics.

articles.title: Negotiating Care Over Time: A Systematic Review of Alzheimer's Disease Caregiving Through a Life Course Approach.
articles.abstract: The global ageing of the population has significantly increased the demand for long-term informal care, particularly in the context of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although research on caregiver burden and coping strategies is extensive, limited attention has been paid to the temporal evolution of caregiving roles and their intersections with caregivers' life trajectories. This systematic review, conducted across literature published between 2004 and 2024, examines how the life course perspective has been applied in sociological research on family caregiving for people with AD, aiming to analyse the interplay between caregiving timing, biographical transitions, and socio-institutional contexts. The selected studies reveal that caregiving is not a static or homogeneous role but evolves across the life span, shaped by transitions, linked lives and structural conditions. Adopting a life course perspective enhances the understanding of caregiving as a dynamic and socially embedded process. This approach underscores the need for policies that are temporally sensitive, culturally reflexive and capable of supporting caregivers across different life stages.

articles.title: How Do Mindfulness-Based and Cognitive Behavioral Therapies Help Adults With Opioid-Treated Chronic Low Back Pain? A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Pain practice : the official journal of World Institute of Pain
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is common and often refractory to existing treatments, necessitating long-term opioid therapy, which has substantial risks. Mindfulness-based (MBT) and cognitive behavioral (CBT) therapies are safe and can be effective for CLBP.

AIMS: To better understand how MBT and CBT may help improve opioid-treated CLBP: METHODS: This qualitative study involved a subgroup of participants with opioid-treated CLBP who completed a 12-month randomized clinical trial comparing the effects of MBT versus CBT. Participants who reported improvements at 12 months, compared to baseline, in main outcomes (assessed with validated "quantitative" questionnaires) and experience with the study intervention, and who attended the intervention sessions were invited to in-depth exit interviews. The interviews achieved thematic saturation. Thematic analysis of transcribed interviews summarized qualitative findings.

RESULTS: Fifty participants (26 MBT, 24 CBT) were interviewed. They were, on average, 58.5 (SD = 10.0) years old. Most were female (60.0%), non-Hispanic (94.0%), and White (82.0%). At baseline, both groups were, on average, moderately-to-severely impacted by CLBP and treated with moderate-to-high daily opioid doses; at 12 months, they quantitatively reported improved pain, function and QoL scores and reduced daily opioid dose. In their qualitative responses, these participants corroborated the quantitative findings, reporting reductions in back pain (98.0% of interviewed participants), functional limitations (100.0%), and opioid dose (98.0%), with the majority attributing these changes to the study intervention they had received (98.0%, 94.0%, and 90.0%, respectively). Participants also reported the interventions helped them cope with emotional challenges and life stressors, and opioid-related adverse effects. Participants did not raise concerns about interventions' safety. Qualitative themes identified intervention-taught techniques participants most frequently used to manage their symptoms.

CONCLUSION: MBT and CBT can improve health and QoL and reduce opioid dose in adults with opioid-treated refractory CLBP, calling for improved access to these safe treatments.

articles.title: Non-Canonical Function of ORC1: Regulating Notch-VEGFR2-Mediated Angiogenesis in Melanoma Progression.
articles.abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer characterized by high metastatic potential and substantial genetic heterogeneity. Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous susceptibility loci, the functional roles of risk variants, most of which reside in non-coding regions, remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify genetic susceptibility genes involved in melanoma progression and investigate their non-canonical roles in the tumor microenvironment. GWAS summary statistics from the GWAS Catalog, FinnGen, and UK Biobank were integrated using MAGMA and FUSION to prioritize candidate genes, which were subsequently evaluated using TCGA-SKCM transcriptomic and survival data. ORC1 emerged as a key susceptibility gene that was significantly upregulated in metastatic melanoma and associated with poor overall survival. Bioinformatic analyses further showed that ORC1 expression was positively correlated with Notch signaling activity and alterations in the immune microenvironment. The functional effects of ORC1 were examined using in vitro co-culture systems in which human umbilical vein endothelial cells were exposed to melanoma-derived conditioned medium. ORC1 overexpression in melanoma cells promoted endothelial prol iferation, migration, tube formation, and vascular permeability in a paracrine manner. Dual-luciferase reporter assays, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting indicated that ORC1 was associated with enhanced NOTCH1 promoter-reporter activity, activation of Notch-related signaling, and induction of downstream angiogenic programs. In xenograft models, ORC1 overexpression was associated with increased tumor growth and microvascular density, whereas pharmacological inhibition of Notch pathway activity with the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT attenuated ORC1-overexpression-associated tumor growth and vascular changes. Collectively, these findings identify a non-canonical pro-angiogenic role for ORC1 in melanoma progression that is mediated, at least in part, through Notch-VEGFR2 signaling. The ORC1-Notch-VEGFR2 axis may therefore represent a potential therapeutic target for modulating the melanoma microenvironment and limiting disease progression.

articles.title: The H3K27me3-NR1D1-IFN-γ axis in trained macrophages induced by early respiratory virus infection drives non-T2 asthma in children.
articles.abstract: Unlike that of T2 asthma, the pathophysiology of non-T2 asthma remains largely unexplored. However, increasing evidence supports a role for trained macrophages in asthma. In this study, we utilized a non-T2 asthma mouse model associated with early respiratory viral infection to identify the H3K27me3-NR1D1-IFN-γ axis in lung-trained macrophages, which drives non-T2 asthma by promoting Th1 differentiation. Early infection combined with allergen sensitization induced the formation of trained macrophages, which displayed hyperactive methionine cycling and elevated levels of S-adenosylmethionine (SAM). As a substrate for methyltransferase, SAM enhanced the trimethylation of H3K27, subsequently suppressing the expression of the nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group D member 1 (NR1D1) gene through enrichment at its promoter. Interestingly, NR1D1 interacted with the Ifng gene and negatively regulated its expression. High levels of IFN-γ from trained macrophages were observed because NR1D1 was inhibited by elevated H3K27me3 levels. Following allergen challenge, the increased expression of IFN-γ, MHC-II, and CD80/CD86 in trained macrophages positively regulated the activation and differentiation of Th1 cells, which subsequently produced more IFN-γ, thereby promoting non-T2 asthma. Consistently, in patients with asthma, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and monocytes downregulated NR1D1 expression, resulting in elevated IFN-γ levels. Conversely, treatment of patient monocytes with an NR1D1 agonist led to a marked decrease in IFN-γ production. In mice, non-T2 asthma was significantly inhibited by either the inhibition of H3K27me3, the activation of NR1D1, or the neutralization of IFN-γ. Our results demonstrate that the H3K27me3-NR1D1-IFN-γ axis in lung-trained macrophages, which is associated with early infection, drives non-T2 asthma during childhood in mice. Consequently, SAM, NR1D1, and IFN-γ may serve as potential drug targets for the treatment of non-T2 asthma.

articles.title: Bone health in myelodysplastic neoplasms: results from the prospective longitudinal BoHemE study.
articles.abstract: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are characterized by insufficient hematopoiesis and alterations of the bone marrow microenvironment. However, bone health in MDS has not been evaluated in a prospective, longitudinal setting. Within the Bone and Hematology in Elderly (BoHemE) study, bone mineral density (represented as T-score) and bone-specific serum markers were assessed in patients with MDS (n = 111; 36% female) and age-matched controls (n = 84; 55% female) at baseline and after 3 years. At baseline, patients with MDS had a lower T-score [-0.2; p < 0.05] compared to controls, which was mainly attributed to the lower T-score in women with MDS [-0.3; p < 0.05]. Furthermore, the DNMT3A mutation was associated with a lower T-score within the MDS cohort [-0.7; p < 0.05], but the occurrence in controls had no effect. Albumin-adjusted calcium and phosphate levels correlated with T-scores within the MDS cohort [p < 0.0001 and p < 0.01, respectively], independent of age, sex, MDS duration, IPSS-M score, or transfusion dependence. Quality of life was lower in patients with MDS [p < 0.01], and remained stable over 3 years, whereas T-scores declined [-0.3; p < 0.05]. The presence of osteoporosis was associated with poor overall survival in MDS [p < 0.01]. In conclusion, bone health should be evaluated as part of the diagnostic work-up and clinical management of MDS.

articles.title: PET/MR Imaging of the Gastrointestinal Tract.
articles.journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
articles.abstract: PET/MR imaging combines molecular PET data with multiparametric MR imaging in a single reduced-radiation examination of the gastrointestinal tract. For oncologic indications, the hybrid modality adds value in hepatic metastasis detection, locoregional staging, and posttreatment response assessment. Radiotracers beyond fluorodeoxyglucose, including fibroblast activation protein inhibitor ligands and somatostatin receptor analogs, expand diagnostic reach in tumors with low glycolytic activity and in neuroendocrine disease. For inflammatory bowel disease, PET/MR enterography assists with selected questions such as differentiation of inflammatory from fibrotic strictures. This review evaluates current evidence supporting PET/MR imaging across oncologic and nononcologic gastrointestinal applications.

articles.title: MR Imaging of Anal Cancer.
articles.journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
articles.abstract: High-resolution pelvic MR imaging is central to the diagnosis, staging, treatment planning, and posttreatment assessment of anal squamous cell carcinoma (SCCA), the most common malignancy of the anal canal. Accurate imaging interpretation requires detailed knowledge of anal canal anatomy, lymphatic drainage, and optimized MR imaging technique. MR imaging provides excellent evaluation of primary tumor extent, while nodal and distant staging are enhanced by computed tomography (CT) and FDG-PET/CT. Imaging directly informs contemporary chemoradiation strategies and surveillance. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is implicated in nearly 90% of SCCA, is vaccine-preventable, and HPV ctDNA shows promise for response assessment and relapse prediction.

articles.title: Effects of complementary therapies on physiological and psychological outcomes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is the cornerstone intervention for improving respiratory function and symptoms in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, evidence on the effects of complementary therapies (CTs), such as yoga, tai chi/qigong, music therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), relaxation techniques, and water-based exercise, remains limited.

METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving patients with COPD were systematically searched in Embase, Scopus, PubMed, and MEDLINE (Ovid). Study selection followed PRISMA guidelines. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs) using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Thirty-six RCTs involving 3148 participants were included. Compared with usual care, effects on exercise capacity varied across different CTs, with improvements observed primarily in exercise-based approaches (6-min walk distance [6MWD]; MD = 58.73 m), pulmonary function (FEV1% predicted; MD = 4.65), dyspnea (modified Borg scale; MD = -0.79; CRQ dyspnea; MD = 1.03), symptom burden (COPD Assessment Test; MD = -3.36), and health-related quality of life (SGRQ total score; MD = -8.40). Anxiety and depression (HADS-A and HADS-D) were also reduced (MD = -1.70 and -1.02, respectively). Compared with PR, CTs showed greater improvements in 6MWD (MD = 8.17) and HADS-D (MD = -0.74).

CONCLUSION: Complementary therapies may improve both physiological and psychological outcomes in patients with COPD and may serve as adjunctive strategies to conventional pulmonary rehabilitation. Further research is needed to identify optimal modalities and patient-specific responses.

articles.title: Lateralized amyloid PET uptake and beta-band connectivity in relation to cognition in temporal lobe epilepsy.
articles.abstract: We examined focus-relative amyloid PET asymmetry and its associations with resting-state EEG connectivity and processing speed in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE). Thirty adults with clinically assigned MTLE (19 right-focus, 11 left-focus) underwent 18F-florapronol PET and resting-state EEG. Regional standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and sensor-level weighted phase lag index (wPLI) were evaluated using paired comparisons, rank correlations and exploratory bootstrap indirect-association models. Cognitive data were available for 26 participants, including Digit Symbol Coding (DSC) for 25. Under the original analytical convention, mean medial temporal SUVR was 1.066 ipsilaterally and 1.013 contralaterally (difference 0.053, 95% CI [0.013, 0.093]; p = 0.011; Cohen's dz = 0.500). The contrast differed by focus side (interaction p = 0.002) and was 0.038 under source-table reconstruction (p = 0.075). Ipsilateral SUVR correlated with inter-hemispheric beta wPLI (ρ = 0.617, q = 0.034 across 240 tests). The intra-contralateral association (ρ = 0.536) did not survive this broader correction. Indirect estimates for Trail Making Test A (0.279, 95% bootstrap CI [0.043, 0.761]) and DSC (0.151, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.114, 0.476]) did not survive correction across 136 models. Regional medial temporal PET uptake was associated with beta-band scalp connectivity in this small cohort, while focus-side heterogeneity and labeling sensitivity limit a uniform ipsilateral interpretation. Processing-speed indirect associations were exploratory and did not establish compensation or causality. Replication with structural correction, longer EEG sampling and longitudinal cognitive follow-up is required.

articles.title: Allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis associated with Talaromyces boninensis: A case report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is a chronic inflammatory pulmonary disorder characterized by type I and III hypersensitivity reactions to Aspergillus fumigatus in the airways of patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis. However, other filamentous fungi can cause similar pathophysiological changes, a condition referred to as allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis (ABPM). Data on ABPM involving non-Aspergillus fungi remain limited. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first case of ABPM associated with Talaromyces boninensis. The patient met the diagnostic criteria proposed by the Japan ABPM Research Program, and T. boninensis was isolated from bronchial lavage fluid and identified by molecular analysis.

articles.title: Long-lasting survival, migration and functional maturation of transplanted human reprogrammed neurons in vivo.
articles.abstract: Direct reprogramming of glial progenitor cells (GPCs) into induced neurons (iNs) represents a promising strategy for future brain regenerative therapies. This approach uses forced expression of neuronal fate-determining genes to convert non-neuronal cells into neurons, bypassing a pluripotent intermediate stage and enabling potential in vivo applications. However, evidence for long-term survival and maturation of human reprogrammed neurons in vivo remains limited. Here, we present a longitudinal in vivo analysis of human iNs following transplantation into the immunodeficient mouse cortex. Using 3D cultures of reprogrammed iNs to enhance graft survival, we demonstrate survival for up to 5 months post-transplantation with a proportion of iNs remaining up to 10 months. The transplanted cells exhibit widespread migration from the grafted core into anatomically connected brain regions and a protracted neuronal maturation, reflected by increased cellular complexity and expression of neuronal markers. Functional analyses reveal gradual electrophysiological maturation and the establishment of afferent synaptic connectivity with host circuits. Importantly, non-reprogrammed GPC grafts retain their glial identity. Together, these findings provide in vivo evidence for long-term survival, neuronal maturation and long-range migration of human iNs in the intact mouse brain, supporting their potential for future cell repair strategies.

articles.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography.

METHODS: TOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing.

FINDINGS: Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). Invasive interval cancers were detected within 12 months in 22 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (4·5 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 31 women in the digital mammography group (6·3 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; OR 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·97]).

INTERPRETATION: TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening.

FUNDING: Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (German Research Foundation).

articles.title: Challenging historical associations and reassuring women: an updated meta-analysis of multiple sclerosis relapse risk following assisted reproductive technology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Historical studies suggested that assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) may increase relapse rates in women with multiple sclerosis (WwMS). We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify the effects of ART on MS relapse risk and assess whether ART is associated with incident MS in previously healthy women.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched four databases until May 2026. Cohorts, case-controls, and case series (>5 participants) evaluating relapse risk after ART or incident MS following ART were eligible. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled adjusted rate ratios (aRRs), with prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Risk-of-bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

RESULTS: Twelve studies (11 of good quality), including four nationwide cohorts, met the criteria. Ten assessed relapse risk (n = 680); 2 assessed incident MS risk (n = 586,656). We found an insignificant relapse risk with minimal heterogeneity (95% CI 0.85-1.39; I²=4.6%). No significant increase in risk was observed among women not receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) during fertility treatment, with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist or GnRH antagonist protocols. Women achieving pregnancy following ART experienced significantly fewer relapses (aRR 0.50, 95% CI 0.29-0.84); failed ART showed a nonsignificant trend towards increased relapse risk (aRR 1.31, 95% CI 0.96-1.79). ART was not associated with an increased risk of incident MS in 2 studies.

INTERPRETATION: Contemporary evidence suggests that ART does not independently increase relapse risk in WwMS or the risk of developing de novo MS. These findings support individualized fertility counselling focused on optimizing disease control rather than discouraging ART. Prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy and age-dependent prognostic confounding of kappa free light chain parameters in multiple sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The kappa free light chain (κ-FLC) index is widely recognized as an alternative to oligoclonal bands for demonstrating intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis in multiple sclerosis (MS). However, its prognostic value remains controversial. We investigated whether physiological age-related changes confound κ-FLC parameters and their reported prognostic associations.

METHODS: In this retrospective study across two tertiary centers, we included patients with MS and controls with non-immunological neurological disease. Paired cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum samples were analyzed by nephelometry in a single laboratory. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Prognostic endpoints included time to confirmed Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 3.0 and of 6.0, as well as conversion to progressive MS. Biomarker cut-offs were derived using maximally selected rank statistics, and associations were assessed via Cox proportional hazards regression.

RESULTS: We evaluated 61 patients with MS and 18 non-immunological neurological diseases over a median follow-up of 8.1 years. The κ-FLC index discriminated MS from controls with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.93 (cut-off: 5.7), performing comparably to CSF κ-FLC (AUC: 0.94) and Qκ-FLC (AUC: 0.97). Serum κ-FLC positively correlated with age (ρ = 0.48, p < 0.001), whereas CSF κ-FLC showed no age dependence (ρ = -0.01, p = 0.93), resulting in an age-dependent decline in the κ-FLC index (ρ = -0.26, p = 0.049). Serum albumin did not change with age (ρ = 0.12, p = 0.36), while the serum κ-FLC-to-albumin ratio increased (ρ = 0.52, p < 0.001). The IgG index was unaffected by age. Although unadjusted cut-offs appeared predictive on standard log-rank testing, no κ-FLC metric retained prognostic significance after correction for threshold optimization or multivariable adjustment for age at onset. Age at onset was the sole independent predictor across all disability endpoints (hazard ratios: 1.12-1.15).

CONCLUSIONS: Age selectively elevates the denominator of the κ-FLC index while leaving its intrathecally driven numerator unaffected. Consequently, the index carries an age signal that is not corrected by Qalbumin. This physiological dissociation likely explains previous discrepancies in the prognostic literature and underscores the necessity of adjusting for age in future κ-FLC outcome studies.

articles.title: Copper nanoparticles as a precision nutrition strategy to enhance reproductive resilience and in vitro sperm fertilizing capacity in heat stressed breeding bulls.
articles.abstract: Heat stress (HS) is a major environmental challenge that compromises fertility in breeding bulls by disrupting physiological homeostasis and reproductive function. This study evaluated the potential of dietary copper nanoparticles (CuNPs) to improve reproductive resilience and thermotolerance in Sahiwal breeding bulls exposed to summer HS. Eighteen clinically healthy bulls were randomly assigned to three dietary treatments (n = 6/group): control (no CuNPs), S1 (10 mg CuNPs/kg dry matter (DM), and S2 (20 mg CuNPs/kg DM), and maintained under peak HS conditions for 16 weeks. The supplementation of CuNPs significantly improved thermoregulation by reducing rectal temperature, pulse rate, respiration rate, and circulating cortisol while preserving rumen motility. Supplemented bulls exhibited greater semen quality and sperm functional competence, including improved plasma membrane integrity, acrosome integrity, and DNA stability. These modifications were accompanied by enhanced testicular blood perfusion and preservation of ultrasonographic echotexture. Oxidative stress was also attenuated by CuNPs, as indicated by reduced malondialdehyde concentrations and enhanced antioxidant defenses, including superoxide dismutase, catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and total antioxidant capacity. Improved redox status was associated with higher reproductive hormone levels and enhanced immune function. During in vitro fertilization, semen from supplemented bulls achieved higher cleavage and blastocyst rates and produced a greater proportion of transferable grade embryos than the control group. The beneficial effects were more pronounced in the S2 group. These findings demonstrate that dietary copper supplementation in nanoparticle form enhance thermotolerance, redox homeostasis, testicular function, and in vitro sperm fertilizing capacity in heat-stressed Sahiwal breeding bulls.

articles.title: One-year outcomes in patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease: differences according to the type of heart failure and kidney disease stages.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To analyze the differences in clinical characteristics, treatment and 1-year outcomes between patients with HFrEF, HFmrEF and HFpEF according to CKD stage (4-5 versus 1-3).

METHODS: We analyzed data from 2,245 patients with HF included between 2019 and 2024 by 68 specialized HF units. Clinical characteristics, treatment and 1-year mortality and HF hospitalization rates were compared in HFrEF, HFmrEF and HFpEF patients according to CKD stages4-5 versus 1-3.

RESULTS: Of the 2,245 patients, 54.2% were HFrEF, 12% HFmrEF and 33.8% HFpEF. CKD stages4-5 were present in 9.9% (8.9% of HFrEF, 11.5% of HFmrEF and 11.3% of HFpEF patients). Median age was 73years (IQR: 63-80), being older in CKD 4-5 stages, and 37.3% were female. CKD 4-5 patients received in significantly lower proportion ARNI, MRA, betablockers and SGLT2i in HFrEF and HFmrEF. One-year mortality and 1-year rate of HF hospitalizations were significantly higher in patients with HFrEF and lower in those with HFmrEF and HFpEF in cases of CKD 4-5, but there were no differences among the three types of HF in the CKD 1-3 subgroup. There was significant interaction between ERC severity and HF subtypes (P=.025 for mortality and P=.046 for HF hospitalizations).

CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary cohort of patients with HF, an association between renal dysfunction and type of HF was observed in terms of 1-year outcomes, with significant differences in event rates between HF types only in cases of more severe CKD.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Ischemic stroke and intracranial large-artery disease risk in familial hypercholesterolemia: A prospective Japanese study" [Atherosclerosis, 415, (2026), 120674].
Immune-inflammatory profiles, coronary artery disease, and peripheral artery disease in people with HIV.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: People with HIV (PWH) have high risk of coronary (CAD) and peripheral (PAD) artery disease independent of traditional risk factors. Single immune-inflammatory biomarkers provide limited insight into disease risk and phenotypes, whereas integrative profiling may reveal novel mechanisms. Here we investigated associations between immune-inflammatory profiles, CAD, and PAD in PWH.

METHODS: We included PWH from the Copenhagen Comorbidity in HIV Infection (COCOMO) Study with undetectable HIV RNA and measurements of 25 immune-inflammatory biomarkers. Participants underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements to assess for CAD and PAD. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering on principal components grouped participants by immune-inflammatory clusters, and we assessed their associations with CAD and PAD.

RESULTS: Among 651 PWH, we identified three immune-inflammatory clusters: one with low senescent T cell proportions; one with low concentrations of inflammation, innate activation, and endothelial dysfunction markers (reference cluster); and one with high senescent T cell proportions and concentrations of inflammation, innate activation, and endothelial dysfunction markers (high inflammation cluster). The high inflammation cluster was associated with obstructive CAD (adjusted OR 2.42 [95% CI: 1.06; 5.33]), higher lipid-rich plaque volumes (adjusted β = 8.47 [95% 0.84; 16.1] μL), and lower ABI (adjusted β = -0.07 [95% CI: -0.13;-0.01]) among those with PAD compared to the reference cluster, after adjustment for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidaemia.

CONCLUSIONS: An immune-inflammatory profile characterised by T cell senescence, inflammation, innate activation, and endothelial dysfunction was associated with high-risk CAD severity, highlighting immunopathogenic pathways associated with atherosclerosis in PWH.

articles.title: A pilot randomized controlled trial assessing the feasibility and preliminary effects of a text message intervention to promote secure storage and disposal of prescription opioids.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unused prescription opioids are a major source of diversion and nonmedical use, yet adoption of secure storage and disposal practices remains low. Scalable behavioral interventions are needed to promote medication safety. We pilot tested a theory-informed short message service (SMS) text-based intervention designed to encourage secure storage during treatment and disposal of unused prescription opioids following treatment.

METHODS: We conducted a two-arm, single-blinded randomized controlled pilot trial (June-December 2024) among adults prescribed an opioid medication (≤30 days). Participants (N = 479) were randomized to receive a 45-day SMS intervention or standard care. Surveys were administered at baseline, mid-intervention, and post-intervention. Primary outcomes were self-reported locked storage (mid- and post-intervention) and disposal of unused medication (post-intervention). Feasibility metrics included recruitment, retention, intervention delivery, and acceptability. Logistic regression models assessed group differences using a modified intention-to-treat approach.

RESULTS: Recruitment via electronic health record outreach was feasible, and retention was reasonable (76.6%). Most intervention participants reported the messages were helpful, acceptable, and non-burdensome. A higher proportion of intervention participants compared to control reported storing opioid medications in a locked location. The pilot study was underpowered to detect differences between conditions for disposing of unused medication.

CONCLUSION: A theory-informed SMS intervention to promote opioid medication safety was feasible, acceptable, and associated with improved storage behaviors. Findings support further evaluation through a hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial.

articles.title: Medical School Performance Evaluations (MSPEs) Lack Objectivity: A Challenge in the Surgery Residency Selection Process.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In the past several years, the methods used to evaluate medical students have undergone significant shifts. The United States Medical Licensing Examination Step 1 grading has become pass/fail, as has clinical grading at many institutions. Residency program directors have lamented the loss of objective data in applications.

OBJECTIVE: To assess and compare current practices of medical school performance evaluations among MD, DO, and Top 40 schools.

DESIGN: A retrospective review was performed of the Medical Student Performance Evaluations. Grading systems, formulas, and distribution for surgery clerkships were measured. Statistics were performed using Chi-square tests.

SETTING: This study was performed at a single general surgery residency program.

PARTICIPANTS: Medical schools associated with applications during the 2024 to 2025 application cycle to the residency program. Medical schools located within the United States, both MD and DO, were included. Medical school rankings were determined using the Blue Ridge Institute's 2024 Schools in Medicine report.

RESULTS: Applications were received from 138 MD schools and 26 DO schools. Seventy-six schools (46.3%) ranked the students, 143 (87.2%) graded clerkships, and 77 (47%) displayed the formula used for grading. Top 40 schools were less likely to use class rank (26.3% vs 52.4%, p < 0.01) or give clerkship grades (71.1% vs 92.1%, p < 0.001). For Top 40 schools, the shelf exam was less likely to constitute more than 40% of the clerkship grade (0% vs 27.1%, p < 0.05). These schools were more generous with grading, with no Top 40 schools bestowing less than 25% of their class honors (0% vs 27.4%, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: There is little available to distinguish academic performance in Medical Student Performance Evaluations and Top 40 medical schools are less discerning in the evaluation of medical students.

articles.title: Demographic and epidemiological patterns of reported malaria cases in Aseer Region, Saudi Arabia: An eight-year surveillance analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and public health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial progress toward malaria elimination in Saudi Arabia, imported infections continue to threaten re-establishment of transmission, particularly in southwestern regions. Aseer Region, contains diverse ecological settings that may support malaria vectors. This study examined the demographic and epidemiological characteristics of malaria cases reported in Aseer between 2016 and 2023.

METHODS: A retrospective surveillance analysis of malaria surveillance records was conducted using data from the Vector Diseases Control Unit of the Ministry of Health. All laboratory-confirmed malaria cases reported from January 2016 to December 2023 were included. Demographic variables and malaria species were analyzed. Cases were classified as imported, introduced, or local according to World Health Organization definitions. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed using R software, and spatial distribution was mapped using QGIS.

RESULTS: A total of 1254 laboratory-confirmed malaria cases were identified during the study period. Annual case numbers declined from 266 in 2016-63 in 2018 before increasing to 343 cases in 2023. Imported infections accounted for 799 cases (63.7%), followed by local (303, 24.2%) and introduced cases (152, 12.1%). Case classification varied significantly by year (χ²=570.54, df=14, p < 0.001). Males represented 84.4% of cases, and the median age was 26 years, with the highest burden among individuals aged 25-34 years (32.9%) and 15-24 years (31.0%). Non-Saudi nationals accounted for 65.1%, with Ethiopian, Sudanese, and Yemeni. Plasmodium falciparum was the predominant species (75.2%), followed by P. vivax (24.3%). In multivariable analysis, nationality and P. vivax infection were independently associated with importation-related malaria, whereas sex was not.

CONCLUSION: Malaria in Aseer during 2016-2023 was characterized by fluctuating incidence, increasing predominance of importation-related infections. Multivariable analysis identified non-Saudi nationality and P. vivax infection as factors associated with importation-related malaria. Sustained surveillance, targeted interventions for mobile populations, and continued vector control are essential to prevent re-establishment of indigenous malaria transmission and support national elimination goals.

articles.title: Home versus centre exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise-based home-based cardiac rehabilitation (HBCR) is an alternative to exercise-based centre-based cardiac rehabilitation (CBCR) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, its effects on functional capacity, psychological outcomes, and health-related quality of life remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate exercise-based HBCR compared with exercise-based CBCR or usual care (UC) after CABG.

METHODS: The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251238099) on 23 November 2025, followed by the formal systematic search on 25 November 2025 in PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and CINAHL. Randomized controlled trials comparing exercise-based HBCR with CBCR or UC were included. Outcomes included peak oxygen uptake (VO₂), waist-hip ratio (WHR), health-related quality of life (HRQoL), anxiety, and depression. Mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled.

RESULTS: Nine trials (n = 991) were included. No significant difference in peak VO₂ was observed between HBCR and CBCR (MD = -0.22, 95% CI -1.24 to 0.80; I² = 0%). Anxiety favored HBCR over UC (MD = -2.85, 95% CI -5.05 to -0.65), but heterogeneity was extreme (I² = 90%). No significant difference in depression was observed (MD = -1.83, 95% CI -4.15 to 0.48; I² = 95%). HRQoL and body composition were each reported by only two studies and were not meta-analyzed.

CONCLUSION: Evidence suggests no significant difference in functional capacity between exercise-based HBCR and CBCR. Evidence for patient-reported and psychosocial outcomes remains limited and inconclusive, and no firm conclusions can be drawn. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of studies and substantial heterogeneity.

articles.title: Impact of sex and age on long-term prognosis in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown inconsistent conclusions regarding the prognosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) patients based on sex.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to explore sex differences across different age groups and long-term prognosis of HCM.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 2781 patients diagnosed with HCM. The median follow-up duration for the overall cohort was 4.54 years (interquartile range: 2.13-7.99 years), and 61.7% (n = 1717) were male patients. The main outcomes assessed were all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation and cardiovascular events, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression analysis. Furthermore, competing risks regression analysis was performed. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to examine the potential association between age and prognosis across different sex groups.

RESULTS: A total of 519 patients (18.7%) experienced all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation, with 292 patients (10.5%) succumbing to cardiovascular events. Female patients demonstrated a higher risk of both all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation (P = 0.001) and cardiovascular events (P = 0.001) compared to males. Significant age-related differences were observed for both all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation (P < 0.0001) and cardiovascular events (P < 0.0001) across sex. Multivariate Cox regression analysis indicated that age was an independent predictor of all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation [HR: 1.038; 95% CI: 1.027-1.049; P < 0.001] and cardiovascular events [HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 1.006-1.033; P = 0.004] in males. Conversely, in females, age was the only independent predictor of all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation [HR: 1.016; 95% CI: 1.004-1.028; P = 0.01].

CONCLUSION: Female HCM patients face higher all-cause mortality/cardiac transplantation and cardiovascular events than males. Advancing age increases both risks in the whole population and within each sex subgroup.

articles.title: Prognostic significance of isolated left bundle branch block in patients presenting with chest pain without prior cardiometabolic disease.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch block (LBBB) is a cardiac abnormality frequently associated with structural heart disease and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, its prognostic significance in patients without prior cardiometabolic disease remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate cardiovascular outcomes in patients presenting with chest pain with versus without LBBB in the absence of prior cardiometabolic or structural heart disease.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using TriNetX. Adults presenting with chest pain were divided into two cohorts: patients with LBBB and patients without LBBB. Patients with prior cardiometabolic or structural heart disease were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed, yielding 12,035 patients in each cohort. Outcomes included myocardial infarction, heart failure, and incident heart disease.

RESULTS: After matching, patients with LBBB had higher rates of myocardial infarction compared with patients without LBBB (3.8%vs 1.4%, p<0.001). Heart failure was also more common in the LBBB cohort (13.2%vs 4.5%, p<0.001). Incident heart disease occurred in 3.4% of patients with LBBB compared with 0.9% of patients without LBBB (p<0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly worse event-free survival for myocardial infarction, heart failure, and heart disease among patients with LBBB.

CONCLUSION: Among patients presenting with chest pain without prior cardiometabolic or structural heart disease, LBBB was associated with increased risks of MI, HF, and heart disease. These findings suggest an association between LBBB and adverse cardiovascular outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Near-complete Response of Bilateral Adrenal Metastases to 177Lu-PSMA Therapy in Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer on Posttherapeutic SPECT-CT Follow Up.
articles.abstract: A 72-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for restaging due to significantly increased PSA levels during chemotherapy. Imaging revealed high 68Ga-PSMA-11 uptake in bilateral adrenal uptake, with additional uptake in the prostate and few sclerotic bone lesions. MRI and afterwards adrenal gland biopsy confirmed adrenal metastases, an uncommon metastatic site. As the patient was oligometastatic, refractory to previous systemic therapies, and ineligible for surgery or radiotherapy, 177Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy was initiated. After four treatment cycles, PSA levels progressively decreased, and post-therapeutic follow-up SPECT/CT demonstrated a near-complete response in adrenal and bone metastases without treatment-related adverse effects.

articles.title: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT Detection of Hypertrophic Osteoarthropathy in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma Following Anti-GD2 Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: A 5-year-old boy with high-risk neuroblastoma underwent 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT as part of a clinical trial to assess treatment response after anti-GD2 immunotherapy. The scan showed symmetric increased uptake in bilateral femora and tibiae with periostosis. 18F-MFBG PET/CT revealed no abnormal uptake, and no metastasis was found. The diagnosis was hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. This case demonstrates that hypertrophic osteoarthropathy can occur as a rare complication after anti-GD2 therapy and can be detected by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

articles.title: 18F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessing Inflammation-related Activity in Recurrent In-Stent Restenosis After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Prospective Comparison With 18F-FDG.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent inflammatory activity may contribute to recurrent in-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of 18F-FAPI PET/CT for detecting inflammation-related activity in recurrent ISR and to compare it with 18F-FDG PET/CT.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with recurrent ISR after PCI and suspected persistent inflammatory mechanisms were prospectively enrolled. All patients underwent 18F-FAPI PET/CT, and 32 also underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT within 1 week. Patients were classified as having inflammation-related ISR or non-inflammation-related ISR by multidisciplinary adjudication. Visual and semiquantitative PET parameters were compared between groups and tracers.

RESULTS: Forty-four patients (mean age, 56.8±10.3 y) were included, including 31 with inflammation-related ISR and 13 with non-inflammation-related ISR. 18F-FAPI PET/CT showed positive findings in all 31 patients with inflammation-related ISR, compared with 3 of 13 patients with non-inflammation-related ISR (100% vs. 23.1%). Visual score, SUVmax, SUVmean, TBRblood, and TBRliver were all significantly higher in inflammation-related ISR than in non-inflammation-related ISR (all P<0.001). In the dual-tracer subgroup (n=32), 18F-FAPI PET/CT detected all inflammation-related ISR cases (20/20, 100%), whereas 18F-FDG PET/CT detected 8 of 20 (40.0%) (P<0.001). Compared with 18F-FDG, 18F-FAPI showed higher visual scores and significantly greater tracer uptake in inflammation-related ISR (all P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: 18F-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher detectability of inflammation-related activity in recurrent ISR and provided better lesion-to-background contrast than 18F-FDG PET/CT. These findings support its potential role in the noninvasive assessment of coronary inflammatory activity after PCI.

articles.title: Acute partial sleep deprivation attenuates cardiac output during moderate-intensity cycling in young adults.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Acute partial sleep deprivation (PSD) can attenuate systolic blood pressure (BP) during cycling exercise; however, the mechanisms responsible are unknown. This study aimed to test whether acute PSD attenuates cardiac output (Q̇) during cycling. Twenty-five adults (22 ± 3 yr; 13 females; [Formula: see text]: 40.1 ± 7.7 mL/kg/min) completed a randomized, crossover trial where they slept normally or underwent acute PSD (early awakening; 40% of normal sleep duration). BP, Q̇ (impedance cardiography), and middle and posterior cerebral artery blood velocity (transcranial Doppler ultrasound) were assessed at rest, throughout 60 min of moderate-intensity cycling (81 ± 35 W), and recovery. Systolic and diastolic BP did not differ at rest and exercise (both, P ≥ 0.19). Q̇ did not differ at rest (control: 5.0 ± 0.9 L/min vs. PSD: 4.9 ± 0.7 L/min, P > 0.99) or 30 min of cycling (control: 11.5 ± 2.7 L/min vs. PSD: 11.0 ± 2.5 L/min, P = 0.16), but was attenuated at 60 min of cycling (control: 12.3 ± 3.1 L/min vs. PSD: 11.5 ± 2.6 L/min, P = 0.003) and recovery following PSD (control: 7.7 ± 1.9 L/min vs. PSD: 7.2 ± 1.4 L/min, P = 0.04). Heart rate and estimated end-diastolic volume did not differ (both, P ≥ 0.82); however, stroke volume tended to be lower (P = 0.07), estimated ejection fraction was lower (P = 0.02), and total peripheral resistance was augmented (P = 0.04) following PSD. Plasma norepinephrine and epinephrine were unchanged at rest but exhibited attenuated increases at 60 min of cycling following PSD (both, P ≤ 0.045). Acute PSD can attenuate exercise Q̇ after 30 min of moderate-intensity cycling secondary to a blunted stroke volume, without compensation by increased heart rate.NEW & NOTEWORTHY The effects of a single night of partial sleep deprivation (PSD) on blood pressure (BP) regulation during cycling exercise remain unclear. We found no differences in BP but attenuated cardiac output during moderate-intensity cycling exercise and recovery following acute PSD in young adults. The blunted cardiac output response following acute PSD occurred after 30 min of cycling and was mediated by an attenuated stroke volume, in concert with an attenuated rise in exercise catecholamines.

articles.title: [Transition: between recommendations and real-world care : Results from the InfoTrans project].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transition from pediatric to adult rheumatology care represents a particular challenge for young people with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA).

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the continuity of care, disease burden, transition competence and unmet needs among young adults with JIA.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Within the Innovation Fund project InfoTrans, a cross-sectional survey was conducted among- individuals insured with the Barmer health insurance aged 16-25 years with JIA and pseudonymously linked with health insurance claims data. For the present analysis, young adults aged 20 years and older with prior pediatric rheumatology care were included. Data collected comprised current healthcare utilization, patient-reported outcomes, transition competence (Transitions-KompAZ), and psychological well-being (WHO-5).

RESULTS: Among 269 surveyed young adults with JIA, 45% were receiving specialist rheumatology care. Participants receiving rheumatology care showed higher transition competence (22.7 vs. 19.0; p < 0.001), had more frequently attended a transition consultation (17% vs. 9%), and were more often aware of the website "mein-rheuma-wird-erwachsen.de" (33% vs. 20%; p = 0.013). Despite comparable disease burden, participants without specialist care received DMARD therapy less frequently (18% vs. 63%). Gaps in care were also observed among participants receiving rheumatology care: the average interval between the last pediatric rheumatology and first adult rheumatology visit was 9.9 months. Overall, 35% had not received a medical transfer summary report, more than 40% were dissatisfied with preparation for transfer, and approximately 1 in 5 participants reported relevant depressive symptoms.

CONCLUSION: Relevant discrepancies remain between recommendations for structured transitional care and actual care delivery. Disease-related knowledge appears to be a central factor for continuous follow-up in rheumatology. The findings underline the importance of early patient education and better integration of support services.

articles.title: [Anti-amyloid antibodies against Alzheimer's disease : Lecanemab and donanemab in practice-Clinical importance, patient selection and safety management].
articles.abstract: Lecanemab and donanemab are the first disease-modifying therapies for early Alzheimer's disease. These humanized IgG1 antibodies promote the clearance of aggregated amyloid-beta peptides and, in the pivotal CLARITY AD and TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trials, significantly delayed cognitive and functional decline, with an approximately 30% relative risk reduction for the clinical stage progression; however, the clinical meaningfulness remains contested: critics point to the small between-group difference in relation to the total score. This is weighed against the first disease-modifying effect and the first pharmacotherapy for mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease. A prerequisite is the biological diagnosis: the reference standard is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET), potentially complemented in the future by blood biomarkers such as plasma p‑Tau217. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) are the key adverse event, manageable through patient selection, ApoE-ε4 genotyping and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) monitoring. The indications and follow-up belong in specialized centers.

articles.title: [Infection with Orientia tsutsugamushi and hospital-acquired pneumonia].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tsutsugamushi fever is an infection caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi that is rarely diagnosed in Europe but endemic in several Asian countries and in Chile. Its clinical presentation is often nonspecific, ranging from fever, myalgia, lymphadenopathy, and a maculopapular rash to severe disease with multiorgan involvement.

CASE REPORT: A 34-year-old man presented with fever, myalgia, lymphadenopathy, and a maculopapular rash after returning from Thailand. Despite empiric antimicrobial therapy, his condition deteriorated rapidly, with respiratory failure, impaired consciousness, and hypotension. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of peripheral blood confirmed O. tsutsugamushi. Treatment with doxycycline, along with meropenem for hospital-acquired pneumonia, resulted in rapid clinical improvement.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of considering tsutsugamushi fever in febrile travelers returning from endemic regions. Timely presumptive or PCR-based diagnosis and initiation of effective therapy are crucial to prevent severe disease with multiorgan involvement and secondary complications.

articles.title: Predictive value of exercise PETO2 changes for major adverse cardiovascular events in ischaemic heart disease: An exploratory study.
articles.abstract: The difference in end-tidal oxygen partial pressure (ΔPETO2) between rest and anaerobic threshold exercise is reportedly a predictor of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in heart disease patients, but its predictive accuracy has not been verified in ischaemic heart disease (IHD). We analyzed the incidence of MACE within 3 years after cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in IHD patients, and calculated ΔPETO2 from the CPET data. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified the ΔPETO2 cutoff value in predicting MACE occurrence, after which patients were divided into low ΔPETO2 and high ΔPETO2 groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis using the log-rank test was performed to compare the incidence of MACE within 3 years, and multiple regression analysis was conducted with ΔPETO2 as the dependent variable. Among 168 cases (mean age 66.2 ± 10.1 years; 143 males), 22 patients (13%) experienced MACE. The optimal ΔPETO2 cutoff value in predicting MACE was 2.5 mmHg (area under the curve 0.888, sensitivity 77%, specificity 90%). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that the MACE incidence rate was significantly higher in the ΔPETO2 ≤ 2.5 group compared to the ΔPETO2 > 2.5 group. Multiple regression analysis identified peak oxygen pulse (peak O2 pulse), ankle-brachial index (ABI), and dyslipidemia (DL) as independent factors associated with ΔPETO2. ΔPETO2 may serve as a useful early indicator for predicting high risk of MACE in IHD before the onset of heart failure. Additionally, peak O2 pulse, ABI, and DL were identified as factors influencing ΔPETO2, suggesting that blood flow to the lower limbs may impact ΔPETO2.

articles.title: Post-Exercise R-1,3-Butanediol did not Improve Markers of Fatigue or Recovery During a Multi-Stage Mountain Bike Race.
articles.abstract: Evidence suggests that exogenous ketosis (EK) induced by ketone monoester (KME) supports recovery and attenuates physiological stress during endurance exercise. However, the potential benefits of the ketone precursor R-1,3-butanediol (BDO) during real-world multi-stage cycling remain unknown. We investigated the effects of post-exercise BDO supplementation on physiological strain, dietary intake, hydration, cognitive function, sleep, and subjective recovery during the 2025 Absa Cape Epic mountain bike race. In this double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 18 trained mountain bikers (10 teams) completed an 8-day multi-stage race. Participants received either 87.5 mL ketone IQ (BDO) or a placebo (CON) twice daily (post-stage and pre-sleep). Heart rate, energy intake, sleep metrics, cognitive performance, and subjective stress-recovery were monitored throughout the race. BDO induced mild post-stage ketosis (∼1.0 mM β-hydroxybutyrate) from stage 1 onwards. Across the race, both groups demonstrated lower exercise heart rate, increased resting heart rate, increased energy and carbohydrate intake, and slower reaction time by stage 6, indicating accumulating physiological strain. BDO did not alter any of these effects compared with placebo. These findings suggest that the modest ketosis achieved with BDO was not effective under real-world racing conditions, highlighting the importance of formulation-specific and ecologically valid evaluations of exogenous ketosis strategies in future studies.

articles.title: Longer sleep duration and the incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep duration has been linked to adverse health outcomes, but its association with diabetic nephropathy remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the association between sleep duration and a composite endpoint of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy.

METHODS: The study participants were 678 Japanese outpatients with type 2 diabetes. Lifestyle habits were assessed at baseline and at years 2 and/or 5. Mean values of lifestyle factors were calculated by averaging measurements from baseline to the date of endpoint onset or the end of follow-up. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used.

RESULTS: During a follow-up of 6.0 ± 2.7 years, 215 participants experienced the endpoint. Among lifestyle factors, mean sleep duration was the only factor associated with the endpoint. Compared with participants sleeping <6 hours, the multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for mean sleep duration of 6 to <7, 7 to <8, and ≥8 hours were 1.08 (95% CI, 0.74-1.57), 1.56 (95% CI, 1.05-2.31), and 1.92 (95% CI, 1.15-3.19), respectively (P for trend = .003). This association remained significant after adjustment for key lifestyle and diabetes-related factors. The association was stronger in older participants and those with microalbuminuria or reduced kidney function.

CONCLUSION: Longer, but not shorter, sleep duration is associated with an increased risk of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy.

articles.title: Stage IIIB pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma treated with spatially fractionated radiotherapy combined with antiangiogenic therapy and sequential chemo-immunotherapy: A case report.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is a rare subtype of non-small-cell lung cancer, characterized by high invasiveness and treatment resistance. Patients with PSC often exhibit poor treatment outcomes, short median survival and a dismal prognosis, necessitating novel comprehensive treatment strategies to address this clinical challenge. A 64-year-old man with PSC was initially diagnosed with stage cT4N2M0 IIIB disease and was negative for programmed cell death-ligand 1 expression. Owing to the large tumor size and unfavorable performance status, treatment initially involved an induction regimen that combined tomotherapy-based spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT) with recombinant human endostatin injection (Endostar). As the condition of the patient improved, two additional cycles of low-dose albumin-bound paclitaxel were administered as concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Following radiotherapy, the patient received two sequential cycles of systemic therapy with paclitaxel liposome and ivonescimab. This combined regimen demonstrated favorable short-term efficacy with improved performance status. However, the patient developed pneumonia caused by infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii and aspergillus, subsequently succumbing to respiratory failure (with an overall survival of 5.5 months). The present case provides a clinical reference for the selection of treatment strategies in locally advanced, large PSC, highlighting the potential of SFRT combined with antiangiogenic therapy as a promising, novel local treatment option. However, the ultimate survival outcome of this patient should serve as a stark warning that heightened vigilance against opportunistic infections is essential during combination therapy in such patients.

articles.title: A thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: A case report.
articles.abstract: Thoracic SWI/SNF-related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit ATPase 4 (SMARCA4)-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a newly recognized, high-grade malignant neoplasm that is rare in clinical practice. There is no standardized or clearly defined treatment protocol for SMARCA4-UT in clinical guidelines. The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough. Bronchoscopy demonstrated a neoplasm in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe bronchus, which almost obstructed the lumen, with a hypervascular surface, suggestive of a right upper lobe carcinoma. Histopathological examination confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a SMARCA4 gene mutation in exon 4, classifying the tumor as SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated lung carcinoma. The patient developed superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS), requiring emergent percutaneous stent placement. Treatment also included computed tomography-guided cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), alongside targeted molecular therapy with crizotinib. Despite aggressive multimodal therapy, the patient succumbed to tumor thrombosis at 1 month post-treatment. Overall, SMARCA4-UT is rare and diagnostically challenging, lacking standardized treatment guidelines. In clinical practice, cryoablation with argon-helium and RFA may provide palliative benefits by alleviating tumor burden and improving quality of life. Endovascular intervention provides a rapid and effective approach to alleviate tumor-induced SVCS. However, subsequent anticoagulation and antineoplastic therapies require further investigation to determine their efficacy in the management of such cases.

articles.title: C. butyricum Combined With Resmetirom Provides Therapeutic Benefits in MASH Associated With Gut-Liver-Brain Axis Modulation.
articles.journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Resmetirom has emerged as a major advance in MASH pharmacotherapy as the first approved liver-targeted THR-β agonist; however, variable therapeutic efficacy and adverse responses may limit its clinical benefits. This study investigated whether C. butyricum could provide additional therapeutic benefits when combined with resmetirom and attenuate nausea/vomiting-like responses in association with changes across the gut-liver-brain axis.

METHODS: In this study, we established a high-fat diet-induced MASH mouse model and administered C. butyricum, resmetirom, or their combination. Comprehensive biochemical, histological, molecular, 16S rRNA sequencing-based microbiome profiling, and gut-brain axis-related analyses were performed to evaluate the effects of combination therapy on hepatic metabolism, inflammation, fibrosis, intestinal barrier integrity, gut microbiota remodelling, microbial metabolites, and resmetirom-associated adverse responses.

RESULTS: Combined treatment with C. butyricum and resmetirom produced additional therapeutic benefits compared with either monotherapy, markedly improving hepatic steatosis, lipid accumulation, insulin resistance, inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis in MASH mice. At the molecular level, combination treatment was associated with increased hepatic THR-β expression and coordinated changes in AMPK-related lipid metabolism, NRF2/HO-1 antioxidant, and TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB inflammatory markers. Furthermore, combination therapy restored intestinal barrier integrity, alleviated MASH-associated gut microbial dysbiosis, increased beneficial bacterial taxa, and increased faecal butyrate levels. Notably, C. butyricum attenuated resmetirom-induced nausea/vomiting-like responses, accompanied by reduced colonic and cerebral 5-HT/SP signalling, decreased brain Htr3a and Tacr1 mRNA expression, and suppressed neuronal FOS activation. Faecal butyrate levels were inversely associated with hepatic lipid burden and brain 5-HT/SP levels.

CONCLUSIONS: C. butyricum combined with resmetirom provides additional therapeutic benefits and attenuates nausea/vomiting-like responses in MASH, accompanied by coordinated changes across the gut-liver-brain axis. This combination strategy provides a potential microbiota-based adjunctive approach for optimizing the therapeutic benefits of resmetirom in MASH.

articles.title: Incidence and Influencing Factors of Pain Crisis in Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To systematically evaluate the incidence and influencing factors of pain crisis in cancer patients, providing evidence for targeted preventive interventions and optimized clinical nursing strategies.

DESIGN: A systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, SinoMed, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP were searched from inception to February 2026.

REVIEW METHODS: Literature screening, quality assessment, and data extraction were performed independently by two researchers. Meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and effect sizes were expressed as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Seven studies involving 1865 cancer patients were included. The pooled incidence of pain crisis was 37%. Significant influencing factors included bone metastasis (OR = 3.91), radiotherapy and chemotherapy (OR = 3.23), social support (OR = 0.88), and age (OR = 0.92). Anxiety (mild OR = 8.00, moderate OR = 9.15, severe OR = 10.99) and depression (mild OR = 6.54, moderate OR = 6.46) were also significant predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of pain crisis in cancer patients is relatively high and is influenced by bone metastasis, chemoradiotherapy, social support, age, and emotional states. Nurses should dynamically assess risk, identify factors, and implement individualized interventions to prevent pain crisis and improve quality of life.

IMPACT: This meta-analysis provides robust evidence for identifying high-risk cancer patients for pain crisis. The findings underscore the need for integrating routine psychological assessment and tailored pain management strategies into clinical oncology nursing practice to reduce the occurrence of pain crises and enhance patient well-being.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Daylight Photodynamic Therapy Alone or Combined With Transepidermal Drug Delivery Techniques for Skin Field Cancerization: An Immunohistochemical Study of Epidermal Carcinogenesis and Dermal Remodeling Markers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Daylight photodynamic therapy (DL-PDT) has been combined with transepidermal drug delivery (TED) techniques to enhance photosensitizer penetration. Although studies have suggested improved clinical and histological outcomes with DL-PDT combined with ablative laser, evidence regarding carcinogenesis and dermal remodeling markers remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in epidermal carcinogenesis and dermal remodeling markers after standard DL-PDT compared with DL-PDT combined with TED techniques for facial field cancerization.

METHODS: Forty patients were randomized into four groups (n = 10): standard DL-PDT, DL-PDT with microneedling, DL-PDT with CO2 laser, and DL-PDT with microdermabrasion. All underwent two treatment sessions 1 month apart using methyl aminolevulinate cream followed by 2 h of daylight exposure. Skin biopsies were obtained at baseline and 3 months after the second session. Immunohistochemistry evaluated p53, Ki67, Collagens I and III, metalloproteinases (MMP-1, MMP-3, MMP-9), and TIMP-1.

RESULTS: A reduction in the vertical extent of Ki67 expression (from two-thirds to one-third of the epidermis) was observed mainly in the microneedling and CO2 laser groups, although it was not statistically significant. No significant differences in Ki67 or p53 expression were observed within or between groups. Increased Type III collagen, MMP-3, and MMP-9 expression and decreased MMP-1 and TIMP-1 expression were observed, with only TIMP-1 reduction being statistically significant (p = 0.041) in the overall analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: A trend toward reduced vertical Ki67 expression suggests potential benefit of DL-PDT combined with microneedling and CO2 laser, and favorable changes in dermal remodeling markers were observed overall. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger randomized studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03963765.

articles.title: Comparison of Clinical, Metabolic, and Hormonal Profiles in Obese Versus Lean Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Obesity substantially influences clinical and metabolic manifestations of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). However, differences in clinical, metabolic, and hormonal profiles between obese and lean women with PCOS have not been explored in large-scale meta-analyses.

METHODS: Databases were searched from inception through 31 December 2025 for studies reporting clinical, metabolic, and hormonal profiles in obese and lean PCOS phenotypes. Random-effects meta-analyses in R yielded mean differences (MDs) or risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Forty-two studies (N = 5363; 3078 obese, 2285 lean PCOS) met inclusion criteria. Menstrual irregularity (84.7% vs. 70.9%; RR 1.19), hirsutism (65.9% vs. 58.8%; RR 1.10), acne (44.9% vs. 36.8%; RR 1.25), acanthosis nigricans (52.7% vs. 22.6%; RR 1.94), and biochemical hyperandrogenism (45.6% vs. 31.8%; RR 1.49) were more prevalent in obese than in lean PCOS. Obese PCOS was associated with a less favourable cardiometabolic profile, with higher HOMA-IR (MD 2.03), fasting (MD 5.12 mg/dL), and 2-h (MD 9.91 mg/dL) plasma glucose, and greater risks of prediabetes (25.3% vs. 12.1%; RR 1.84), diabetes (8.6% vs. 2.7%; RR 2.58), and metabolic syndrome (51.2% vs. 11.9%; RR 3.59). Mean lipid levels were worse in obese PCOS, with higher total cholesterol, triglycerides, and LDL cholesterol, and lower HDL cholesterol. Nonetheless, lean PCOS exhibited substantial burdens of menstrual dysfunction, hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, dysglycemia, and dyslipidemia.

CONCLUSION: Obesity in PCOS is associated with more severe reproductive, metabolic, and hormonal abnormalities, but lean PCOS still carries substantial reproductive and metabolic burdens. However, the observational design of the included studies and substantial heterogeneity across several outcomes warrant cautious interpretation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The meta-analysis was registered with PROSPERO under registration number CRD420251240521. The review protocol summary is available on the PROSPERO website.

articles.title: Impact of Evolocumab on LDL-Cholesterol and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Established CVD: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and many high-risk patients fail to reach LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) targets on statins alone. Evolocumab, a PCSK9 inhibitor, offers potent LDL-C lowering, but a synthesis of its lipid and clinical benefits in secondary prevention is needed.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating evolocumab in adults with established cardiovascular disease. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2025. Outcomes included lipid parameters, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), individual cardiovascular endpoints, and safety, with pooled risk ratios (RR) and mean differences calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Nine trials enrolling 67,662 patients were included. Evolocumab significantly reduced LDL-C (mean difference -57.73 mg/dL), total cholesterol (-52.27 mg/dL), triglycerides (-21.21 mg/dL), and lipoprotein(a) (-10.99 mg/dL), while increasing HDL-cholesterol (3.69 mg/dL). Evolocumab was associated with lower MACE (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.40-0.71), though this estimate should be interpreted cautiously given heterogeneity in endpoint definitions and study designs. Myocardial infarction (RR 0.74) and coronary revascularisation (RR 0.80) were significantly reduced, while cardiovascular mortality and stroke showed no statistically definitive reduction. Serious adverse events and neurocognitive effects were comparable between groups, though injection-site reactions were more frequent with evolocumab.

CONCLUSION: In patients with established cardiovascular disease, evolocumab provides substantial lipid lowering and reduces ischemic events without major safety concerns, supporting its use as an adjunct to statin therapy in secondary prevention.

articles.title: Vitamin D: Physiology, Pharmacology and Clinical Evidence for Supplementation-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

articles.title: Imaging in Rheumatic Diseases of the Head and Neck.
articles.journal: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America
articles.abstract: Multimodality imaging is essential for evaluating head and neck rheumatologic disease. Computed tomography (CT) can demonstrate osseous erosions, mineralization, and structural complications, including temporomandibular joint and cervical spine involvement in JIA/RA, crowned dens in pseudogout, and sinonasal or airway disease in giant cell arteritis (GCA) and relapsing polychondritis (RP). Ultrasound is useful for detecting synovitis in JIA/RA, auricular chondritis in RP, salivary gland abnormalities in Sjögren's syndrome, and vascular changes in GCA. FDG-PET/CT can identify metabolically active inflammation. MRI is useful for evaluating early inflammatory changes, cartilage involvement, orbital disease, vascular wall inflammation, and salivary gland involvement.

articles.title: Therapeutic Horseback Riding for Youth With Autism and Psychiatric Comorbidities: A Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
