METHODS: In this single-arm exploratory study, adults with CKD stage 3-5 and a guideline-based primary-prevention indication received an EMBLEM MRI S-ICD at eight Korean centers. The primary endpoint, appropriate ICD therapy, was hypothesized at 18% versus a historical rate of 7.8% (α = 0.05, 80% power, planned N = 77; exact binomial test).

RESULTS: The study was terminated early after 39 patients (51% of target; achieved power ≈61%). Mean LVEF was 27.8% and median eGFR 11.7 mL/min/1.73 m2; 71.8% had CKD stage 5 and 69.2% were on hemodialysis. Over a median follow-up of 361 days, appropriate ICD therapy occurred in 2 patients (5.1%; 95% CI, 1.4-16.9), significantly below the hypothesized 18% (p = 0.036). Inappropriate shocks occurred in 5 patients (12.8%; 95% CI, 5.6-26.7; 8 shocks), a proportion 2.5 times that of appropriate therapy, from external electromagnetic interference (2 patients), multiple counting after automatic SMART Pass deactivation (2), and supraventricular misclassification (1). Three deaths (7.7%) occurred, none device-related or documented as arrhythmic (one undetermined); all hospitalizations were for heart failure, and no systemic device infection occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single-arm study, appropriate ICD therapy was infrequent and exceeded by inappropriate shocks, while non-arrhythmic competing mortality dominated the clinical course. These hypothesis-generating findings support cautious patient selection, verification of filter status during follow-up, and larger comparative studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), Republic of Korea; identifier KCT0005596.

articles.title: MRI markers of cerebral small vessel disease prior to first-ever spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a retrospective case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major contributor to stroke, cognitive decline, and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). While post-ICH MRI markers of CSVD are well described, their role in predicting first-ever ICH remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case-control study at a tertiary stroke center, including patients with first-ever spontaneous ICH between 2012 and 2024 who had a prior brain MRI, with controls frequency-matched by age and sex. MRI markers of CSVD were rated according to STRIVE-2, including white matter hyperintensities (WMH), lacunes, perivascular spaces (PVS), cerebral microbleeds (CMB), cortical infarcts, superficial siderosis (SS), and acute cortical microinfarcts (CMI). Associations between MRI markers and ICH risk were evaluated using logistic regression.

RESULTS: Altogether, of 2,734 ICH cases, 63 met inclusion criteria and were compared with 63 controls (age 68 ± 13 years). The median interval between MRI and ICH was 14.6 months (IQR 8.3-29.5). In adjusted analyses, any CMB (OR 10.96, 95% CI 4.00-30.02), PVS > 20 in either region (OR 4.31, 1.52-12.22), and WMH (OR 2.60, 1.21-5.60) were associated with ICH. In a multivariable model, CMB (OR 10.50,95% CI 3.63-30.42) remained independently associated with ICH, whereas PVS > 20 did not reach significance (OR 3.35, 0.95-11.75). Acute CMI showed a suggestive association based on few cases (5/63 vs. 0/63).

CONCLUSIONS: MRI-defined CSVD markers on pre-ICH scan were associated with first-ever ICH. The present study is the first to describe the association between CMI and future ICH risk. Brain imaging may help identify high-risk patients and guide preventive strategies.

articles.title: Cancer in Seychelles: A Population-Based Study on Incidence, Trends and Stage at Diagnosis (2005-2024).
articles.abstract: Seychelles, the smallest country in Africa but with the highest GDP per capita, has experienced rapid socioeconomic development. We analysed 20-year cancer incidence trends (2005-2024) using data from the Seychelles National Cancer Registry (SNCR). Annual age-standardised incidence rates (ASRs), average annual percentage changes (AAPCs), and stage at diagnosis (for the four major cancers) were calculated. Incidence rates for the most recent decade (2015-2024) were also compared with those in selected African countries and high Human Development Index (HDI) countries. Among men, prostate cancer had the highest incidence (ASR 73.9 per 100,000) and increased significantly over time (AAPC +6.7%), reaching an ASR of 90.3 per 100,000 in 2015-2024. Significant declines were observed for oesophageal (AAPC -4.3%) and laryngeal cancers (AAPC -5.6%). Among women, breast cancer was the most common cancer (ASR 54.7 per 100,000), increasing by 3.4% annually and reaching an ASR of 70.5 per 100,000 in the most recent decade, comparable to rates in Europe. Significant increases were also observed for colorectal, cervical, and corpus uteri cancers. The observed trends reflect Seychelles' epidemiological transition, with a shift from infection-related cancers towards cancers associated with ageing and lifestyle factors, resembling the cancer profile of high-income countries. Nevertheless, the major cancers-prostate, breast, colorectal, and cervical-continue to be diagnosed at relatively advanced stages, highlighting the need for improved early detection and timely diagnosis.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis comparing advanced hybrid closed-loop automated insulin delivery with multiple daily insulin injections and continuous glucose monitoring in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The use of automated insulin delivery systems, including the MiniMed™ 780G advanced hybrid closed-loop system, has been shown to improve glycemic management in people with type 1 diabetes (T1D). The aim was to assess the cost-effectiveness of the MiniMed 780G system versus multiple daily injections (MDI) of insulin in combination with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in the management of people with T1D with elevated HbA1c levels in Japan.

METHODS: Modeling was performed using the IQVIA Core Diabetes Model and clinical input data were sourced from a randomized controlled trial. A time horizon of 55 years, a discount rate of 2.0% per annum, and a payer perspective were used. Sensitivity analyses were used to examine the robustness of base-case results.

RESULTS: In the base-case, an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of JPY 4,723,991 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained was found, with an incremental benefit of 2.83 quality-adjusted life years with the MiniMed 780G system versus MDI + CGM. The MiniMed 780G system was therefore cost-effective, assuming a willingness-to-pay threshold of JPY 5,000,000 per QALY. Although treatment costs were found to be JPY 16,226,167 higher for the MiniMed 780G, costs associated with managing long-term complications were lower. A probabilistic sensitivity analysis found the intervention to have a 76.9% probability of being cost-effective in Japan.

CONCLUSION: The MiniMed 780G system was projected to be cost-effective in the management of people with T1D in Japan with HbA1c above target levels. Its use was also predicted to improve clinical outcomes when compared with MDI + CGM.

articles.title: MetabDB: an integrated resource for human metabolic measures, disease associations, and genetic evidence.
articles.abstract: Population-scale metabolomics studies have linked metabolic measures to diseases, quantitative traits, and genetic variation, but the results are scattered across assay platforms, phenotype definitions, and analytical formats. MetabDB integrates 16 public studies spanning nuclear magnetic resonance, mass spectrometry, and lipidomics. The current release contains 2663 metabolic measures, 3524 diseases and outcomes, 3382 other genome-wide association traits, and 2025 molecular quantitative trait locus (QTL) targets. MetabDB links genomic variants, genes and proteins, metabolic measures, and diseases or traits through variant/QTL associations, fine-mapping, rare-variant or burden analyses, colocalization, Mendelian randomization, and population associations. Metabolic measures areretained in their source-reported forms, including compounds, lipid species, lipoprotein measures, ratios, percentages, and derived traits. Gene- and protein-level evidence can be examined alongside genomic signals and related disease or trait evidence for the same metabolic measure. Source information and reported analytical details are retained, including the source study, original variable or phenotype definition, assay, unit, exposure scale, analytical model, and statistics where available. Search, browse, and colocalization pages, together with gene evidence breadth and disease-association profiles, provide access to these records. MetabDB is freely available at http://www.mulinlab.org/metabdb/.

articles.title: Body Mass Index-Specific Central Adiposity and Risk of Incident Type 2 Diabetes Among Aging Women.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Body mass index (BMI) does not capture central adiposity, which may provide additional information for type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk stratification.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate BMI-specific waist circumference (WC) categories in relation to incident T2D and assess their performance across independent cohorts.

METHODS: Prospective analyses included 133,620 Women's Health Initiative (WHI) participants free of T2D at baseline, randomly assigned to training (70%; n=93,463) and test (30%; n=40,157) samples. External validation included the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n=2,885) and Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS; n=1,037). Cox models estimated T2D risk across BMI and BMI-specific WC categories. Discrimination was assessed using Harrell's C-statistic.

RESULTS: In WHI, T2D risk increased progressively across BMI categories (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.51-3.30) and joint BMI-WC categories (HRs, 1.40-4.43). Within BMI strata, higher WC generally identified greater T2D risk. Associations were directionally consistent in HRS and HANDLS. Age modified associations, with stronger gradients at younger ages, whereas race and ethnicity interactions were not statistically significant. Model discrimination was modest (C-statistics approximately 0.60-0.75).

CONCLUSIONS: BMI-specific WC categories refine adiposity-related T2D risk stratification beyond BMI alone but provide modest individual-level discrimination. WC may complement BMI in identifying women warranting more comprehensive metabolic risk assessment rather than serving as a stand-alone T2D prediction tool.

articles.title: Divergent T cell programs in plaque rupture and erosion revealed by single-cell multiomics in the OPTICO-ACS study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Plaque erosion accounts for up to 40% of acute coronary syndromes. Unlike plaque rupture, erosion is characterized by thrombus formation on an intact fibrous cap following endothelial denudation. Rupture is associated with broad inflammatory activation, whereas erosion features accumulation of specific immune cells, particularly CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Their functional programming remains insufficiently defined.The objective was to characterize intracoronary and peripheral T cell phenotypes, activation programs, and clonal architecture in acute coronary syndromes caused by plaque erosion compared with plaque rupture.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We prospectively enrolled 133 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndromes in whom plaque erosion or rupture was classified by optical coherence tomography. Blood was sampled from the coronary segment proximal to the lesion and from the peripheral circulation. T cell phenotypes were assessed by flow cytometry and plasma proteomics. In a subgroup, intracoronary samples underwent CITE-seq, integrating single-cell transcriptomics with surface protein profiling, together with paired T cell receptor sequencing.

RESULTS: Flow cytometry demonstrated enrichment of activated memory helper and cytotoxic T cells with anti-inflammatory features at erosion sites, in contrast to predominantly naive and pro-inflammatory T cells in rupture. CITE-seq revealed erosion-specific activation of pathways related to proliferation, adhesion, and tissue repair, whereas T cells in rupture displayed enhanced inflammatory pathways. Functional validation confirmed greater IL-2/IFN-γ induction in rupture-associated memory T cells and greater IL-10 induction in erosion-associated Tregs. T cell receptor sequencing showed greater clonal expansion in erosion, suggesting antigen-experienced clonal selection, whereas rupture exhibited broader and less focused clonal diversity.

CONCLUSIONS: Plaque erosion and plaque rupture show fundamentally different T cell immune profiles. Erosion is marked by memory-skewed, clonally expanded regulatory and cytotoxic T cell subsets, while rupture is characterized by proinflammatory phenotypes, diverse T cell receptor repertoires, and heightened inflammatory signaling. These findings support morphology-tailored immunotherapeutic approaches, including established anti-inflammatory strategies for rupture and selective T cell-directed interventions for erosion.

articles.title: Unveiling Asymptomatic Atrioventricular Reciprocating Tachycardia in a Patient With Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome and Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Intermittent accessory pathway conduction can obscure the electrocardiographic diagnosis of Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome on resting electrocardiograms (ECGs). Furthermore, sensory disruptions characteristic of multiple sclerosis (MS) can blunt symptom perception, masking potentially life-threatening hemodynamic instability. CASE REPORT A 54-year-old woman with secondary-progressive MS (SPMS) was admitted for a complicated urinary tract infection. The admitting ECG demonstrated sinus tachycardia without preexcitation. Telemetry subsequently revealed narrow-complex tachycardia at 220 beats per minute (BPM) with concurrent hypotension. Despite hemodynamic instability, the patient explicitly denied palpitations, chest pain, or presyncope. She had discontinued fingolimod several years earlier because of palpitations, a detail retrospectively suggestive of an accessory pathway. Review of records identified historical ECGs with intermittent delta waves and short PR intervals, confirming the presence of an accessory pathway with intermittent antegrade conduction. A 12-lead ECG during the acute event confirmed orthodromic atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia (AVRT). The patient underwent successful synchronized cardioversion followed by radiofrequency ablation of a left-sided anterolateral accessory pathway via electrophysiological study (EPS). CONCLUSIONS This case illustrates the "ECG dilemma" of intermittent preexcitation, in which the absence of delta waves on a resting tracing does not exclude accessory pathway-mediated tachycardia. It further highlights that patients with neuro-modulating diseases, such as MS, may lack classical "alarm" symptoms for arrhythmia due to progressive autonomic and sensory dysfunction. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for concealed arrhythmias in this population, as neurological impairment can dissociate hemodynamic instability from subjective symptom perception. Objective monitoring with telemetry is essential to prevent adverse outcomes in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Drp1-Mediated Mitochondrial Fission Coordinates Mineral Precursor Transport and Mitochondrial Homeostasis During Osteogenesis.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND During the osteogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs), amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) precursors within mitochondria are transported to the extracellular matrix via PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitochondrial autophagy, thereby initiating mineralization. However, the mechanisms by which mitochondria maintain functional homeostasis in the face of such extensive consumption remain to be elucidated. The present study investigated the role of Drp1-mediated mitochondrial fission in coordinating ACP transport and maintaining mitochondrial function. MATERIAL AND METHODS hMSCs were treated with shRNA to knock down Drp1 or with pharmacological inhibitors (Mdivi-1, CsA). Mitochondrial morphology, ACP transport, energy metabolism, and osteogenic differentiation were assessed using transmission electron microscopy, ATP assays, qPCR, western blot, and eosin staining. In vivo skeletal mineralization phenotypes were validated using a zebrafish model. RESULTS Following osteogenic induction, Drp1 Ser616 phosphorylation increased while Ser637 phosphorylation decreased; mitochondrial fission increased, producing fragments approximately 450 nm in diameter, matching the size of autolysosomes, which facilitates ACP encapsulation and clearance. Inhibition of Drp1 resulted in abnormal mitochondrial elongation, ACP accumulation, and reduced ATP production (decreased to 59.2% in the sh-Drp1 group), and significantly suppressed RUNX2 and ALPL expression as well as mineralization (mineralization area decreased to 36.7%). In zebrafish, treatment with Mdivi-1 or CsA similarly led to reduced craniofacial mineralization and downregulation of osteogenic gene expression. CONCLUSIONS Drp1-mediated mitochondrial fission strikes a balance between the efficient transport of ACP precursors and mitochondrial functional homeostasis via the fission-clearance-regeneration cycle. This process serves as a key regulatory node in osteogenic differentiation. Further investigation of Drp1-associated mitochondrial dynamics in bone metabolic disease models is warranted.

articles.title: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells-derived exosomes ameliorate doxorubicin-induced nephrotoxicity via the modulation of pyroptosis-associated signaling.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical application is constrained by nephrotoxicity, with no therapeutic interventions currently available. This study aimed to delineate the ameliorative potential of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) derived exosomes (EXO) in an experimental model of DOX-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). Twenty-four rats were divided into 4 groups: Control, DOX intoxicated, DOX + EXO, and EXO only groups. Nephrotoxicity was induced in the DOX and DOX + EXO groups using a single dose of DOX (15 mg/ kg i.p.). After 24 h, DOX + EXO and EXO only groups were given BM-MSCs-derived exosomes (100 μg i.v.). DOX was associated with a decline in renal function, activation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and modulation of pyroptosis-associated inflammasome-related signaling. BM-MSCs-derived exosomes significantly improved renal function, as evidenced by histopathological examination, reduction in KIM-1, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine, and renal somatic index (RSI). Exosomes mitigated oxidative stress by enhancing endogenous antioxidant catalase activity and reducing the lipid peroxidation marker MDA, while also suppressing inflammatory mediators, as shown by a reduction in IL-18 and IL-1β. Furthermore, exosomal treatment attenuated the expression of NLRP3, caspase-1 (CASP-1), and gasdermin-D (GSDMD), reduced ELAVL1, IRAK1 and NF-κB levels, while upregulating miR-146a-5p. In Silico analysis identified multiple putative molecular targets for miR-146a-5p, revealing strong interconnection among key targets, including ELAVL1, NF-κB, and IRAK1. These findings provide evidence to support the ameliorative role of BM-MSC-derived exosomes in mitigating DOX-induced AKI, associated with upregulation of miR-146a-5p and concurrent modulation of ELAVL1, IRAK1, and NF-κB, as well as NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling, supporting the biological plausibility of a candidate miR-146a-5p/ELAVL1/IRAK1/NF-κB/NLRP3 regulatory network in AKI pathogenesis. Harnessing the reno-protective properties of exosomal therapy, as well as targeting the inflammasome-related signaling pathways, represents a compelling therapeutic paradigm warranting further mechanistic validation.

articles.title: Chronic Non-Infectious Osteomyelitis in India: Striking the Balance Between Early Recognition and Excluding Infection.
Analysis of Pancreatic Cystic Lesions and Risk Factors Associated with Advanced Neoplasia: Predictors Beyond Five Years of Surveillance.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: There has been an increasing incidence of pancreatic cystic lesions on imaging. Management of pancreatic cysts has been dictated by advanced neoplasia (high-grade dysplasia or pancreas adenocarcinoma) risk; however, the appropriate surveillance strategy is not well characterized for all cyst subtypes.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed at MD Anderson Cancer Center evaluating pancreatic cysts identified on EUS and cross-sectional imaging between January 2000 and April 2023. Patient demographics, clinical factors, and cyst characteristics were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to ascertain factors predicting advanced neoplasia.

RESULTS: 3817 EUS reports were identified with 763 lesions meeting inclusion and exclusion criteria. There were 137 (18.0%) unclassified cysts, 108 (14.2%) serous cystadenomas, 494 (64.7%) IPMNs, 25 (3.33%) MCNs, and 5 (0.7%) unspecified mucinous cysts. 85 (11.1%) patients underwent surgical resection with advanced neoplasia identified in 35 (41.2%) specimens. Beyond five years of surveillance, risk factors that persisted for advanced neoplasia among all cysts included change in cyst size to ≥ 30 mm (OR 4.38; 95% CI 1.18-16.19), development of an associated mass (OR 3.97; 95% CI 1.08-14.57), and history of diabetes (OR 7.45; 95% CI 1.87-29.70). For IPMNs, risk factors after five years for advanced neoplasia included mass on final imaging (OR 13.21; 95% CI 1.51-115.49), final cyst size on imaging per-millimeter increase (OR 1.08; 95% CI 1.02-1.15), and history of diabetes (OR 12.33; 95% CI 1.99-76.34).

CONCLUSIONS: Consensus worrisome features predicted advanced neoplasia consistent with prior literature, but this baseline signal was not retained in multivariable models beyond five years of surveillance, where interval changes were the stronger predictors instead. Increasing cyst size, growth to ≥ 30 mm, and development of an associated mass remained associated with advanced neoplasia after five years. These findings suggest that interval changes in cysts should be considered in long-term risk stratification.

articles.title: Dietary patterns and cardiovascular risk in adult survivors of childhood cancer: findings from the SCCSS-Nutrition Study.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify dietary patterns among adult childhood cancer survivors (CCSs), examine their determinants, and assess whether they differ according to cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk profiles.

METHODS: CCSs from the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study diagnosed before age 21 years (1976-2005), surviving ≥ 5 years and aged ≥ 18 years in 2017, completed a food frequency questionnaire (SCCSS-Nutrition). Factor and hierarchical cluster analyses of 52 food groups identified dietary patterns. We categorised CCSs as having CVD, CVD risk factors (obesity, hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol), or being CVD risk-free. Multinomial logistic regression assessed associations between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles.

RESULTS: Among 802 CCSs (median age: 35 years; IQR: 29-41; 50% male), we identified five dietary patterns: Mediterranean-inspired diet (22%), Western indulgence diet (38%), Western sweet & fatty diet (26%), restrained indulgence diet (9%), plant-based & alcohol-rich diet (6%). Male sex, younger age, German-speaking region, smoking, and living with others were associated with Western indulgence, Western sweet & fatty, and restrained indulgence diets. Higher Swiss socioeconomic position (Swiss-SEP) and education, and not having children, were associated with the plant-based & alcohol-rich diet, higher Swiss-SEP was also associated with the Western indulgence diet. No associations were observed between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles.

CONCLUSIONS: Dietary patterns among adult CCSs were socially patterned and differed according to sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics, but were not associated with CVD risk profiles.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Dietary counselling and broader lifestyle support should be considered as part of long-term survivorship care for CCSs.

articles.title: MRGPRX2 in Allergic and Immune-Mediated Diseases: Mechanisms, Clinical Relevance, and Therapeutic Translation.
articles.abstract: Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2) is a mast-cell-enriched receptor that mediates immunoglobulin E-independent activation by structurally diverse neuropeptides, host-defense peptides, microbial products, and selected cationic drugs. Its biology links tissue stress and neuroimmune signaling to degranulation, vascular responses, pruritus, barrier dysfunction, and inflammatory amplification, but the extent to which individual diseases depend on this pathway remains uncertain. The strongest clinical rationale begins with non-IgE-mediated immediate drug hypersensitivity, for which MRGPRX2 provides a direct mechanistic framework, although rocuronium illustrates the need to distinguish human MRGPRX2 pharmacology from murine Mrgprb2 and from IgE-mediated perioperative allergy. In atopic dermatitis, preclinical and human skin data support a potential amplifier role in type 2 inflammation and itch, but a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 did not demonstrate efficacy in an unselected population. In chronic urticaria, challenge, biomarker, and genetic studies suggest an MRGPRX2-responsive subgroup within a heterogeneous disease, whereas a randomized phase 2b study of EVO756 in unselected chronic spontaneous urticaria was also negative despite earlier pharmacodynamic activity. Ulcerative colitis provides additional human tissue evidence for an MRGPRX2-associated mast-cell circuit, although murine Mrgprb2 studies show context-dependent protective and pathogenic effects. Emerging evidence in chronic prurigo, allergic contact dermatitis, asthma, mastocytosis, rheumatoid arthritis, synovial inflammation, and neurogenic inflammation is also considered, with explicit separation of human observations from mouse-model evidence. We integrate these findings with receptor pharmacology and early clinical development, emphasizing evidence hierarchy, validated biomarker needs, patient selection, tissue target engagement, safety, and trial design. Current data support MRGPRX2 as an investigational endotype-defining pathway rather than a universal driver of allergic or immune-mediated disease.

articles.title: Remote Ischemic Post-Conditioning Modulates Brain Expression of PIWI Proteins After Experimental Cerebral Ischemia.
articles.abstract: This study explores the involvement of PIWI family proteins in cerebral ischemia and their potential contribution to the neuroprotective effects of remote ischemic post-conditioning (RIC), a promising intervention for ischemic stroke whose underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. Using a mouse model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAo), we evaluated the effects of RIC induced by femoral artery occlusion (FAo) on brain injury, inflammation, and PIWI proteins expression in the brain. RIC significantly reduced infarct volume, cerebral edema, and neurological deficits, while attenuating the ischemia-induced upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-1β and TNF-α, in the brain cortex. The ischemic insult induced a robust upregulation of PIWIL2 and PIWIL4 in the ipsilateral cortex, primarily in neurons, with PIWIL4 also detected in astrocytes, few microglia and numerous infiltrating myeloid cells. Notably, RIC suppressed this cortical upregulation, suggesting a potential link between PIWI proteins and ischemic damage. By contrast, in neurogenic regions of the hippocampus, RIC selectively enhanced PIWIL4 expression, particularly in neurons of the CA3 region and dentate gyrus. This increase was associated with elevated expression of the neurogenic and repair-related factors TGF-β1 and TREM2. Accordingly, in the subventricular zone of post-conditioned mice, PIWIL4 was localized in SOX2-positive neural progenitor cells that also express the proliferation marker Ki67. These findings reveal a region- and cell-specific modulation of PIWILs expression in cerebral ischemia and RIC, strongly supporting the concept that PIWI pathways may represent promising targets for neuroprotection and recovery following stroke.

articles.title: Caffeic Acid Regulates High Glucose-Induced Inflammatory Responses in BV-2 Microglial Cells: Implications for Purinergic Signaling.
articles.abstract: High glucose-induced microglial activation contributes to inflammatory processes associated with diabetic complications. Thus, the effects of caffeic acid (CA) on inflammatory responses and purinergic signaling parameters in high glucose-challenged BV-2 microglial cells were investigated. A) Oxidative stress; b) Enzymatic activities of Ecto-nucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase (E-NTPDase), Ecto-5-nucleotidase (E-5'-NT), and Adenosine deaminase (ADA); c) Density of P2X7R, A1R, and A2AR purinoceptors; d) Inflammatory markers (IBA-1, NLRP3, and IL-1β); and e) Apoptosis and cell cycle were assessed. Treatment with CA (50 and 75 µM, 24 h) in cells exposed to high glucose medium (GL 25 mM, 48 h) increased viability and reduced nitric oxide (NO), reactive species (RS), and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) levels compared to high glucose-challenged cells. CA also restored ATP and ADP hydrolysis and reduced ADA activity. Furthermore, CA increased the density of the A1R while reversing the high glucose-induced increase in P2X7R and A2AR densities. Moreover, CA treatment attenuated the increase in IL-1β density in high glucose medium, whereas only CA (75 µM) treatment reduced NLRP3 and IBA-1 densities. Besides, this phenolic compound decreased apoptosis and promoted cell cycle progression by increasing the proportion of cells in the S and G2/M phases. Overall, findings suggest that CA attenuates high glucose-induced inflammatory and oxidative alterations in BV-2 microglial cells, besides modulating purinergic enzyme activities and purinoceptor density. These results support the potential involvement of purinergic signaling in the cellular effects of CA and provide possible mechanistic insights into its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions under high glucose conditions.

articles.title: Clinical effects of multi-strain probiotics in extremely preterm infants: a multicenter pre-post implementation study in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Probiotics may reduce the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), late-onset sepsis (LOS), and mortality in preterm infants. However, their efficacy in extremely preterm infants (gestational age < 28 weeks) is still regularly questioned due to limited data and safety concerns. In Dutch Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs), a three-strain probiotic product (ProPrems®; Bifidobacterium infantis Bb-02, Bifidobacterium lactis BB-12, and Streptococcus thermophilus TH-4) was implemented as standard of care from 2021 onwards. This study evaluates the clinical effects of these probiotics in extremely preterm infants. Pre- and postimplementation cohorts of extremely preterm infants from 6 Dutch NICUs (2018-2023) were compared. Clinical data from the first 29 days of life were collected. Incidence of NEC (modified Bell's stage ≥ IIA), LOS, and mortality were compared with logistic regression; growth velocity with linear regression; and time to full enteral feeds (tFEF) with survival analyses. In total, 481 extremely preterm infants (212 pre-, 269 post-implementation) were included. After implementation, the adjusted odds ratio was 0.49 (0.25-0.99; p = 0.049) for NEC; 0.87 (0.59-1.28; p = 0.49) for LOS; and 0.67 (0.35-1.27; p = 0.22) for all-cause mortality. Furthermore, tFEF decreased by 2 days (p < 0.001) and probiotic use was associated with an increase in growth velocity of 1.8 g/kg/day (p < 0.001). One infant (0.4%) developed probiotic-associated sepsis.

CONCLUSION: This multicenter pre-postimplementation study showed that multi-strain probiotic administration was associated with lower NEC incidence, shorter tFEF, and greater growth velocity in extremely preterm infants during the first four weeks of life. Probiotic-associated sepsis was rare. These results support continued use of probiotics in this vulnerable population.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Certain probiotic strains effectively reduce incidence of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm infants, but the efficacy and safety for extremely preterm infants (GA < 28 weeks) remain under debate.

WHAT IS NEW: • This study shows that a multi-strain probiotic supplement was associated with lower NEC incidence, shorter time to full enteral feeds, and greater early postnatal growth in a Dutch multicenter cohort of extremely preterm infants. • The incidence of probiotic-associated sepsis in extremely preterm infants was very low in our cohort with just 1 case (0.4%), consistent with the rare occurrence reported previously.

articles.title: Cultural adaptation of nutritional recommendations in the comprehensive care of adults with type 2 diabetes: An updated transcultural diabetes nutrition algorithm (tDNA) framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transcultural Diabetes Nutrition Algorithm (tDNA) applies medical nutrition therapy (MNT) for adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) by aligning evidence-based dietary principles with cultural food patterns, clinical workflows, and health-system realities.

OBJECTIVE: To review the evidence underpinning the tDNA framework, describe its role in culturally adapting MNT across current treatment contexts, and identify priorities for research, education, and implementation.

METHODS: Sources include concept and framework papers, regional adaptations, randomized and pragmatic evaluations of tDNA-aligned programs, clinician toolkit assessments, and practice statements. Evidence was abstracted around tDNA decision nodes: risk stratification, carbohydrate quality and distribution, portion guidance, meal timing, physical activity prompts, use of diabetes-specific formulas (DSFs) as a meal replacement or supplement when indicated, and digitally enabled monitoring.

RESULTS: Regional tDNA adaptations for Asian Indian, Malaysian, Canadian, Middle Eastern, Brazilian and Venezuelan settings are expert consensus documents specifying culturally appropriate modifications. A published randomized controlled trial reports that calorie-prescribed, glycemic index/load-guided tDNA integrating DSFs and augmented by structured behavior counseling improves glycemic control and body weight over 6 to 12 months, with gains in eating self-efficacy supporting adherence. We propose that MNT as a co-therapy be aligned to dosing when pharmacotherapy is initiated. For the highly effective glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, culturally adapted standardized nutrition checkpoints are proposed to support nutritional adequacy. Whether structured nutrition therapy using DSFs preserves lean mass in this setting is an area for further research.

CONCLUSIONS: The tDNA framework offers a structure for culturally adapted nutrition care in T2D. We propose its extension to current pharmacotherapy and digitally enabled delivery; these extensions require prospective evaluation. Recommendations include early localization, integration with drug titration, structured nutrition support where indicated, standardized nutrition checkpoints, digitized implementation, and audit of remission, time in range, weight, and adherence.

articles.title: Research culture methods detect more anaerobes compared to conventional clinical workflows in periprosthetic joint infection: a pilot study of 14 cases.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most challenging complications of total joint arthroplasty, often complicated by limitations in diagnostic sensitivity. Standard clinical culture methods fail to identify pathogens in 20%-50% of cases, leading to potential under- or overtreatment. This pilot study aimed to compare the microbial detection capabilities of standard clinical culture methods with enhanced research laboratory techniques, and to explore whether additional microbial findings might have the potential to influence antibiotic treatment planning.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirteen patients undergoing surgery for PJI, as defined by the 2018 International Consensus Meeting (ICM) on Infection criteria, were prospectively enrolled at a single academic medical center between August 2023 and September 2024. Intraoperative synovial fluid, periprosthetic tissue, and implant swabs were collected and processed using both standard clinical workflows and optimized research protocols. Culture results and treatment decisions were reviewed in collaboration with Infectious Disease specialists.

RESULTS: Both methods identified primary organisms. However, research techniques detected additional organisms not captured by clinical cultures (p = 0.013). Despite these differences, overall detection rates were comparable (57.1% vs. 59.5%; p = 0.963), with the research workflow achieving similar yield with fewer samples. The potential impact of additional isolate identification on antibiotic selection, if deemed clinically significant, did not appear to result in meaningful changes to antibiotic regimens, although this may have been influenced by the empiric use broad-spectrum antibiotics.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical culture methods may not detect all organisms in PJI, highlighting possible limitations in current diagnostic approaches. Although this pilot study did not directly assess the impact of enhanced microbial detection on antibiotic prescribing and treatment decisions were largely unchanged, these findings suggest that a more comprehensive microbial detection could potentially inform antibiotic selection and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Empirical linezolid target attainment in critically ill patients: integrating local susceptibility data and dosing strategies.
articles.abstract: Linezolid is important for treating infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria resistant to first-line agents. Severe infections often require empirical therapy before pathogen identification and susceptibility testing. This evaluation aims to compare different empirical linezolid dosing strategies in intensive care unit (ICU) patients to improve pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic target attainment while minimising toxicities. Three dosing strategies were compared: (i) standard dosing, (ii) therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)-guided dosing, and (iii) a theoretical model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) strategy based on Bayesian forecasting with a population pharmacokinetic model. Each scenario was combined with an ICU-specific minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) distribution comprising more than 19,000 isolates collected over 10 years. Data from 117 critically ill patients with 2184 TDM samples were available. Linezolid resistance was highest in ICU isolates (9.6%) compared with isolates from the intermediate care unit (4.3%), general wards (3.6%), and emergency room (1.6%). Among ICU isolates, resistance increased significantly over the 10-year study period, from 6.3% in 2015 to 11.4% in 2024. Empirical target attainment was 36.6% with standard dosing and 48.5% with TDM-guided dose adaptation, in two different ICU cohorts that showed 35.9% and 59.4% baseline target attainment, respectively. Theoretical MIPD projected target attainment in 71.4-81.6% of patients. After excluding resistant isolates, the corresponding values were 40.5%, 53.7%, and 79.0-90.3%, respectively. Integrating a large contemporary ICU-specific MIC distribution with patient-level pharmacokinetic data, our results suggest MIPD may represent a promising strategy improving target attainment, in contrast to standard regimens and TDM-guided dosing which failed to achieve adequate target exposure in ICU patients.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in Ireland: a cross-sectional survey of practice, education and governance among healthcare professionals.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anecdotal evidence suggests widespread Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) use in Ireland, but it is underexplored. Some professional societies have issued curricula and guidelines, but little is known about access to ultrasound education and guidance. This cross-sectional survey explores the current landscape of POCUS among healthcare professionals in Ireland.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, online survey explored POCUS use, education pathways, and governance practices among healthcare professionals in Ireland. A novel 44-item survey was developed using SurveyMonkey and disseminated through national professional organisations from May-August 2023.

RESULTS: From 411 responses, 38% (n = 158/411) use or previously used POCUS, with the highest uptake in emergency medicine (67%, n = 68/101), intensive care (82%, n = 14/17), and anaesthesiology (81%, n = 13/16), likely due to recognised pathways. POCUS use remains low in general practice (31%, n = 15/49) and sports medicine (30%, n = 10/33). Governance concerns highlighted include 56% (n = 78/139) of POCUS users operate within a scope of practice and 68% have no protocol for escalating incidental findings. 57% (n = 59/103 store) store their images-72% (n = 42/58) on the device itself, and 36% (n = 21/58) on USB drives. Just 51% (n = 77/151) had a mentor during their training. Respondents who completed competency assessments were significantly more likely to store their images (68% vs 40%, p = 0.006) and reported higher self-reported confidence scores for ultrasound machine parameters.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide an initial snapshot of the POCUS landscape in Ireland, highlighting both the high levels of interest and the uneven nature of current implementation.

articles.title: Urinary and sexual functional outcomes in female patients following elective lumbar spine surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Urinary and sexual functional changes are associated with spine surgery, with reported incidences of approximately 20% for postoperative urinary retention (POUR) and 5-38% for sexual functional changes in mixed-sex cohorts, but sex-disaggregated outcomes are poorly characterized in females. We aimed to synthesize the available evidence on postoperative urinary and sexual functional outcomes in female patients undergoing elective lumbar fusion or disc replacement and to quantify pooled incidence rates, sex-based differences, and variation by surgical approach. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus in accordance with PRISMA guidelines for studies reporting postoperative urinary or sexual functional outcomes in female patients undergoing lumbar spine surgery. Both study sets were restricted to elective lumbar fusion or disc replacement for the primary analyses; decompression-only, mixed, and adolescent scoliosis cohorts were retained as sensitivity analyses. POUR was defined by each study's own criteria, and analyses were stratified by definition and by surgical approach (posterior fusion versus anterior or lateral interbody fusion or disc replacement). Impaired sexual function was defined as a pathological score on a validated instrument or a patient-reported decline in sexual frequency, satisfaction, or comfort. Pooled proportions were estimated with random-effects models, with meta-regression on publication year and procedure category. Seventeen studies were included in the POUR review and 12 in the sexual functional outcome review. Seven cohorts (1,758 female patients) undergoing lumbar fusion or disc replacement contributed to the primary POUR meta-analysis: pooled incidence 14% (95% CI, 7-26; I², 89%). Six posterior fusion cohorts gave 12% (95% CI, 7-21); only one anterior or lateral interbody cohort reported POUR (41%; 95% CI, 29-54), so that stratum could not be pooled. Surgical approach accounted for 60% of the between-study variance (p = 0.007). Adding decompression-only and mixed cohorts (13 cohorts, 15,741 patients) gave 12% (95% CI, 7-18). Multivariable odds ratios comparing males with females ranged from 1.04 to 3.05. An exploratory estimate of impaired postoperative sexual function, from six cohorts and 283 patients assessed largely with non-validated instruments, was 23% (95% CI, 12-38; I², 56%). Neither temporal trend was statistically significant. All POUR studies were at low risk of bias; seven sexual-function studies were low risk and the remainder unclear. In female patients undergoing elective lumbar fusion or disc replacement, postoperative urinary and sexual functional changes are present and probably underrecognized rather than rare. Because the evidence is observational, heterogeneous, and largely without baseline functional assessment, it does not establish causality or support definitive clinical recommendations. Surgeons may consider sex-specific counseling and monitoring of urinary and sexual function in follow-up. The sexual function estimate is exploratory; prospective, female-focused studies with validated instruments and preoperative baselines are needed.

articles.title: Regional Divergence in Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: A Multi-center Analysis of Clinical Practice vs. International Guidelines from the Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA).
articles.abstract: Current infective endocarditis (IE) prophylaxis guidelines recommend a restrictive approach, excluding low-risk lesions such as patent ductus arteriosus, isolated ventricular septal defect, and valvular stenosis. In many countries, delayed cardiac defect repair and a high prevalence of dental disease may create a distinct risk profile that warrants further investigation. The Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA) conducted a multinational cross-sectional online survey targeting cardiovascular specialists to evaluate perceptions of IE prophylaxis guidelines, adherence patterns, and the influence of oral health and socioeconomic factors on clinical decision-making. Statistical analyses included Spearman rank correlation, Chi-square testing, Fisher's exact test, and qualitative thematic synthesis. The questionnaire was completed by 72 specialists, of whom only 25% reported strict adherence to restrictive international guidelines for isolated simple congenital heart defects. Respondents who identified socioeconomic barriers (e.g., poverty and limited access to dental care) as a primary concern were more likely to deviate from restrictive guideline recommendations than their peers (83.7% vs. 41.4%; p = 0.001). Clinicians with higher IE case exposure (> 5 IE cases in the preceding 5 years) also demonstrated significantly greater rates of guideline deviation (p = 0.047). Fewer than 50% of respondents considered current AHA/ESC guidelines "fit for purpose" in their local practice. Many cardiovascular specialists across the Arab/MENA region perceive current international IE prophylaxis recommendations as insufficiently reflective of local clinical and socioeconomic realities. However, these findings represent clinician perceptions and practice patterns rather than patient-level outcomes and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. The observed divergence between guideline recommendations and clinical practice highlights the need for regional epidemiological and outcome-based studies to determine whether local factors influence IE risk and whether adaptation of current prophylaxis strategies is warranted.

articles.title: The systemic administration of multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells alters the inflammatory response in the lung during murine polymicrobial sepsis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction and a major cause of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as a potential immunomodulatory therapy, yet preclinical data remain inconsistent. This study investigated the early effects of human MSCs derived from different tissue sources-bone marrow (BMMSCs) and adipose tissue (ASCs)-on systemic and pulmonary inflammation in a murine model of polymicrobial sepsis. 60 male C57BL/6 mice underwent sham treatment, cecal ligation and puncture (CLP), or CLP followed by a single intravenous administration of BMMSCs or ASCs, manufactured according to GMP-compliant protocols. Analyses were performed 8, 24, and 72 h after CLP. Systemic inflammatory mediators were quantified by multiplex analysis, while pulmonary inflammation was assessed by mRNA and protein expression, histology, and immunofluorescence. CLP induced elevated systemic levels of pro-inflammatory mediators, which were not significantly reduced by MSC treatment. In lung tissue, however, MSC administration resulted in selective immunomodulatory effects. Expression of NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (Nlrp3) was reduced in both MSC-treated groups, while ASC treatment additionally decreased pulmonary interleukin 6 (Il6) and complement 3a receptor (C3ar) mRNA expression at early time points. Protein levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α were not significantly altered, although NLRP3 protein expression was reduced following ASC treatment. No significant differences in histological lung injury scores were observed between groups. In summary, MSC treatment induced modest, time-dependent attenuation of pulmonary inflammatory responses in polymicrobial sepsis without improving structural lung injury. No significant differences in pulmonary inflammatory gene expression, protein levels, or histological lung injury scores were observed between BMMSC- and ASC-treated groups, indicating that neither source demonstrated a clear immunomodulatory advantage over the other at the molecular endpoints assessed in this model.

articles.title: Closed reduction in distal radius fractures: manual manipulation vs. finger trap traction-a prospective randomized controlled clinical trial.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Initial treatment of distal radius fractures (DRF) can be either performed without reduction or with a reduction method as finger-trap traction (FTT) only or by additional manual reduction (MR) under hematoma block. There is no clear evidence on which reduction method is superior, however, MR is more invasive and seems to lead to higher pain levels and more post reduction complications. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical relevance of MR compared to FTT in acute DRFs.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Study design was a prospective, single-centre, balanced randomized [1:1], and parallel grouped, controlled trial. Inclusion criteria were patients with a DRF type A2, A3 or C according to the AO classification and a dorsal tilt of ≥ 10°. The patients were randomized either in the FTT or in the MR group. Depending on the patient's functional demand and the fracture configuration, conservative or operative treatment was initiated. Over one year, clinical and radiological data were assessed at six follow-ups.

RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were included. Regarding radiological results neither FTT nor MR achieved sufficient reduction results (median dorsal tilt was - 16 to -18 after one year) and none of the techniques was superior. The clinical results between the conservatively treated groups were comparable and showed no significant difference. Complications included one CRPS in the conservative MR group, one CRPS after FTT and operation, one secondary carpal tunnel syndrome in the conservative FTT group and one skin lesion after MR.

CONCLUSION: Manual reduction under haematoma block showed no benefit. In patients with AO type A2, A3 and type C fractures and a dorsal tilt ≥ 10° only FTT (if required under a haematoma block or comparable analgesia) is recommended regardless of whether surgery is performed or not.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level I randomized controlled trial.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07697976, registered 06/22/2026, retrospectively registered, www.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov .

articles.title: The case for targeted heart failure case finding in obesity.

Assessing an educational strategy to improve community health provider-led provision of cervical cancer screening services in western Kenya: A secondary analysis of the Elimisha-HPV cluster-randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer disproportionately impacts women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where over 90% of global cervical cancer deaths occur. Lay health workers, such as community health promoters (CHPs), with appropriate training and support, can play a pivotal role in cervical cancer prevention. Our team developed a multi-level intervention, Elimisha-HPV, to support CHP-delivered human papillomavirus (HPV) testing in Kenya. The present analysis evaluates impact of Elimisha-HPV on the following CHP outcomes: i) knowledge of screening delivery and privacy, confidentiality, and professionalism; ii) stigma associated with cervical cancer, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and HPV; and iii) confidence to counsel in screening delivery. We used descriptive statistics and linear mixed effects regression models to evaluate intervention effects (intervention group, n = 64; control group, n = 60). For knowledge and privacy, no statistically significant effects were observed (knowledge: β= -0.08 [95% CI, -0.22 to 0.07]; privacy: β= 0.04 [95% CI, -0.05 to 0.13]). No statistically significant intervention effects were observed for stigma associated with cervical cancer, HIV, or HPV (cervical cancer: β= 0.02 [95% CI, -0.13 to 0.16]; HIV: β= 0.01 [95% CI, -0.11 to 0.13]; HPV: β= 0.02 [95% CI, -0.11 to 0.14]). For the confidence to counsel Likert scale-style questions, evaluated using descriptive and regression approaches, proportional increases were observed across both arms, but the main effect was not statistically significant ( β= 0.01 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.11]). Our findings align with previous work demonstrating that stigma surrounding cervical cancer in LMICs is difficult to effectively influence, and provide a foundation for shaping future stigma-reduction campaigns. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05736588.

articles.title: Association of steatotic liver disease with long-term oncological outcomes after hepatic resection for hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Hepatic steatosis manifests in obesity and systemic metabolic disorders. The nomenclature has recently shifted from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease/nonalcoholic steatohepatitis to steatotic liver disease (SLD), which includes metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with increased alcohol intake, and alcohol-related liver disease. This study retrospectively evaluated the association between SLD and long-term oncological outcomes in 85 patients undergoing hepatic resection for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) between 2018 and 2022. SLD was histologically defined as steatosis involving ≥ 5% of non-tumorous hepatocytes. Of these patients, 47 did not have SLD (non-SLD group) and 38 had SLD. We compared recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) between these groups. Patients with SLD exhibited a higher body mass index and more advanced fibrosis than those without SLD, whereas lifestyle-related diseases were comparably prevalent. Median RFS was not reached in the non-SLD group and was 21 months in the SLD group (log-rank p = 0.054). In exploratory multivariable analysis, SLD was associated with a higher cause-specific hazard of recurrence after adjustment for age, Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage, viral hepatitis status, and diabetes mellitus (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.939; 95% confidence interval, 1.003-3.748). No significant association between SLD and OS was noted (hazard ratio, 0.962; 95% confidence interval, 0.399-2.315). These findings suggest a possible association between SLD and HCC recurrence after hepatic resection, whereas its association with OS remains uncertain.

articles.title: Association between maternal dysglycaemia and adverse perinatal outcomes: A retrospective cohort study using a Japanese mother-infant-linked claims database.
articles.abstract: Claims-based perinatal studies in Japan are limited because normal pregnancies are not covered by health insurance. This study aimed to examine the association between maternal dysglycaemia and perinatal outcomes using a mother-infant-linked claims database. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the JMDC Claims Database from April 2012 to March 2023. Singleton mother-infant pairs were presumed by family ID and categorised into six mutually exclusive claims-based categories: anti-diabetic prescriptions both before and during pregnancy with (Category 1) or without (Category 2) a pre-pregnancy type 1 diabetes code, prescriptions in prenatal period only (Category 3), prescriptions before pregnancy only (Category 4), a gestational diabetes (GDM) management-fee claim without anti-diabetic prescriptions (Category 5) and no identified claims-based indicator of dysglycaemia (Category 6). Outcomes included caesarean section, macrosomia, preterm birth, neonatal asphyxia, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission and congenital malformations of the circulatory system. Among 115,113 presumed mother-infant pairs, 21.5% of mothers underwent caesarean section, with higher proportions in Categories 1 and 2 (40.6% and 48.3%). Highest point estimates were observed in Category 1 for most outcomes. Category 2 was associated with increased risks of caesarean section (adjusted risk ratio 2.04, 95% confidence interval 1.77-2.35), preterm birth (3.69, 2.57-5.28) and NICU admission (3.88, 3.02-4.99). Category 5 was positively associated with macrosomia (2.43, 1.64-3.62). Claims-based indicators of maternal dysglycaemia were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. These findings suggest potential utility of mother-infant-linked claims data for Japanese perinatal monitoring, subject to further validation.

articles.title: Infectious disease communication for international students: A survey of association-accredited Japanese language schools in Japan.
articles.abstract: Japanese language schools are in daily contact with many newly arrived international students, yet little is known about how they obtain and communicate infectious disease information. In February-March 2025, we mailed a newly developed questionnaire to all 103 Japanese language schools accredited by the Association for the Promotion of Japanese Language Education; 38 (36.9%) responded. Of the responding schools, 32/38 (84%) had an infirmary, and 7/38 (18%) had a staff member designated for health matters. In total, 29/38 (76%) collected infectious disease information, mainly from government sources via websites (22/29, 76%). Of all schools, 32/38 (84%) provided information to students; among these, 22/32 (69%) used plain Japanese and 18/32 (56%) used students' native languages, most often through explanations during classes (25/32, 78%). Among schools providing information, reported challenges included language barriers (14/32, 44%), cultural differences as perceived by staff (11/32, 34%), and confirming students' understanding (10/32, 31%). These exploratory institutional observations suggest that ready-to-use materials in plain Japanese and students' languages, and closer links with local public health centers, could be considered; their usefulness for students warrants further evaluation.

articles.title: ACCESS Japan Registry: Toward a nationwide evidence platform for foreign visitors requiring emergency hospitalization in Japan-Rationale, design, and governance of a multicenter registry.
articles.abstract: Japan has experienced a rapid increase in inbound tourism, with a record 42,683,600 foreign visitors in 2025, a 15.8% increase from the previous year and well above the pre-pandemic peak of 31.88 million in 2019, but such short-term visitors are excluded from Japan's public health insurance system, exposing patients and institutions to substantial financial and clinical risks. Despite growing clinical and policy demand, no comprehensive national database of emergency hospitalizations among inbound foreign visitors exists. Against this background, we established the ACCESS Japan Registry (Assessment of Cross-Cultural Medical Access and Emergency & Support Systems for Foreign Patients in Japan), the first multicenter registry in Japan that is designed for nationwide expansion and that targets inbound foreign visitors who require emergency hospitalization in Japan. Foreign nationals on short-term visas who require emergency hospitalization are registered in the registry, and patient demographics, clinical data (diagnosis per the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10), length of stay, outcomes), administrative and financial data (hospitalization costs, unpaid bills), and language support information are collected via Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap). The ACCESS Japan Registry will provide the first systematic, multicenter evidence base on emergency hospitalizations of inbound foreign visitors in Japan, informing healthcare policy, international emergency medicine, and global travel medicine research. Here we describe why such a platform is needed, how it was developed, how it is governed, and what it can and cannot deliver.

articles.title: Rusfertide for the treatment of polycythemia vera.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The US Food and Drug Administration recently approved rusfertide, a hepcidin mimetic, for the treatment of patients with polycythemia vera (PV) whose disease is inadequately controlled with available therapies.

AREAS COVERED: Hepcidin is a liver-produced hormone that regulates systemic iron availability. By restricting iron supply to erythroid progenitor cells in PV, hepcidin reduces red blood cell production and erythrocytosis. In the double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 VERIFY study, clinical response during weeks 20-32 was achieved by 76.9% of patients receiving rusfertide compared with 32.9% receiving placebo, with marked reductions in phlebotomy requirements. Rusfertide is administered weekly with subcutaneous injections, with dose titration from 20 mg, to maintain hematocrit levels below 45%. The most common adverse events were injection-site reactions, anemia, and fatigue. A targeted literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE through October 2026, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, regulatory documents, and abstracts from major hematology meetings.

EXPERT OPINION: Rusfertide is the first of a novel class of agents targeting the hepcidin regulatory axis. Following its approval, it may become part of the therapeutic armamentarium for selected patients. Future studies are needed to confirm its efficacy and to further characterize its safety and its potential impact on thrombosis, clonal evolution, and disease progression.

articles.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement.

FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH.

INTERPRETATION: Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design.

FUNDING: Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking.

articles.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
authors: Paediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators Network
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS.

METHODS: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment.

FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group.

INTERPRETATION: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended.

FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

articles.title: Excessive Dietary n-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids Aggravate Asthma via the Arachidonic Acid Pathway.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the association between dietary n-6 PUFA intake and asthma risk and to investigate the underlying mechanisms using animal and cellular models. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from 13 805 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 2003-2020). Weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and subgroup analyses were performed to assess the association between n-6 PUFA intake and asthma risk. In animal experiments, female C57BL/6 mice were intragastrically administered low-dose (50 mg/kg/day) or high-dose (500 mg/kg/day) linoleic acid (LA) followed by house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway inflammation. Airway hyperresponsiveness, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cell counts, histopathology, and lung arachidonic acid (AA) levels were evaluated. In vitro, BEAS-2B human bronchial epithelial cells were treated with AA and interleukin-13 (IL-13), and the expression of Type 2 chemokines (CCL11, CCL24, and CCL26) was measured. In the NHANES population, dietary n-6 PUFA intake showed a nonlinear dose-response relationship with asthma risk in females, with a threshold of 21.13 g/day. Above this level, asthma risk increased significantly (OR per 1 g/day increase = 1.032, 95% CI: 1.015-1.049, p = 0.002). No significant association was observed in males. In the mouse model, high-dose LA, but not low-dose LA, significantly exacerbated HDM-induced airway hyperresponsiveness, eosinophilic inflammation, mucus secretion, and lung AA accumulation. In vitro, AA (100 μg/mL) significantly upregulated IL-13-induced CCL11 and CCL26 expression in BEAS-2B cells. High dietary n-6 PUFA intake is associated with an increased risk of asthma in a nonlinear, dose-dependent, and female-specific manner. High-dose linoleic acid promotes AA accumulation and aggravates Type 2 airway epithelial inflammation, suggesting that n-6 PUFAs act as metabolic regulators rather than simple nutrients. These findings highlight the importance of considering dietary fatty acid composition and individualized thresholds in asthma prevention and management.

articles.title: TNFAIP1 Facilitates the Progression of Diabetic Cardiomyopathy Through the p38 MAPK-Mediated ER Stress-Apoptosis Axis.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), a diabetes-specific myocardial pathology, is a significant contributor to diabetes-related heart failure. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress plays a crucial role in DCM, yet its upstream regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Cellular heterogeneity in DCM was investigated by analyzing single-cell transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus. A mouse DCM model was established and validated using echocardiography, serum biochemical assays, and histological analysis. TNFAIP1 expression was detected by Western blot. A high glucose-induced DCM cellular model was constructed using HL-1 cardiomyocytes and neonatal cardiomyocytes (NMCMs). Cell injury and TNFAIP1 expression were assessed via TUNEL staining, Annexin V/PI staining, CellRox probe, RT-qPCR, and Western blot. Finally, a TNFAIP1-knockdown DCM mouse model was constructed, and the in vitro results were further validated by echocardiography, serum biochemical assays, histological analysis, and other methods. Single-cell analyses revealed the enrichment of TNFAIP1+ cardiomyocytes in DCM, with their differentially expressed genes enriched in p38 MAPK and apoptosis signaling pathways. TNFAIP1 expression was significantly upregulated in both DCM mouse and cellular models. TNFAIP1 overexpression activated p38 MAPK-mediated ER stress, increased ROS levels, and promoted apoptosis, whereas TNFAIP1 knockdown produced the opposite effects. These effects were significantly reversed by the p38 MAPK pathway inhibitor SB203580, the ER stress inhibitor TUDCA, and the ER stress inducer Thapsigargin. Finally, in vivo experiments further confirmed that TNFAIP1 knockdown ameliorated the progression of myocardial injury in DCM mice. TNFAIP1 promotes DCM progression via the p38 MAPK-mediated ER stress-apoptosis axis, identifying TNFAIP1 as a novel potential therapeutic target for DCM.

articles.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.

METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.

INTERPRETATION: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

FUNDING: The Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development.

articles.title: Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial.
articles.abstract:
