In contrast, miRNA-132 expression was lowest in HC (0.90 ± 0.63; 95% CI, 0.67 - 1.14), significantly increased in PD (2.50 ± 1.86; 95% CI, 1.74 - 3.26), and highest in T2DM (3.56 ± 2.04; 95% CI, 2.80 - 4.32), with highly significant differences between HC and PD and between HC and T2DM (P < 0.001), as well as between PD and T2DM (P = 0.045). Additionally, miRNA-126 expression was lowest in HC (1.22 ± 0.52; 95% CI, 1.03 - 1.42), moderately elevated in T2DM (1.29 ± 0.85; 95% CI, 0.97 - 1.61), and highest in PD (1.70 ± 0.74; 95% CI, 1.41 - 1.98), with significant differences between PD and HC (P = 0.021) and between PD and T2DM (P = 0.029), while no significant difference was observed between HC and T2DM (P = 0.252).

CONCLUSIONS: The identified interconnections among glycemic, lipid, and renal indicators underscore the importance of early identification, comprehensive biochemical evaluation, and timely care during the PD phase to prevent progression to overt DM and its associated complications.

articles.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Model Integrating Chest CT and Cardiac Ultrasound for the Auxiliary Diagnosis of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by elevated pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular dysfunction. Conventional imaging modalities, chest computed tomography (CT) and cardiac ultrasound (echocardiography), provide complementary structural and functional information but exhibit incomplete sensitivity and specificity when used alone. This study aimed to evaluate a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model integrating chest CT and cardiac ultrasound for auxiliary PAH diagnosis, benchmarked against right heart catheterization (RHC) as the reference standard. A retrospective observational study was conducted on 100 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 15.2 years; 56% female) with suspected PAH between January 2020 and December 2024. Each underwent high-resolution chest CT, transthoracic echocardiography, and RHC within a 2-week interval. Imaging-derived structural and functional features were integrated within an attention-based multimodal AI framework. Diagnostic metrics were calculated for chest CT, cardiac ultrasound, and multimodal AI against the archived RHC clinical classification. The multimodal AI system achieved sensitivity of 92.2%, specificity of 88.9%, accuracy of 91.0%, and AUC of 0.930, compared with CT (sensitivity 84.4%, specificity 80.6%, accuracy 83.0%, AUC 0.860) and echocardiography (sensitivity 79.7%, specificity 77.8%, accuracy 79.0%, AUC 0.840). McNemar tests of paired binary classifications favored AI over CT (p = 0.0078) and echocardiography (p = 0.00049). Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed for borderline pulmonary artery diameter and connective tissue disease. The multimodal approach showed improved overall discrimination in this internal retrospective evaluation and should be considered an auxiliary, noninvasive tool that requires external prospective validation.

articles.title: Diagnostic model based on machine learning with multi-feature analysis for diabetic peripheral neuropathy in type 2 diabetes: A single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common and serious complication of diabetes, which imposes a significant economic burden on both society and individuals. Therefore, early identification and diagnosis are crucial for the prevention and treatment of DPN. This study aims to develop machine learning (ML) models based on a variety of different characteristics to predict the risk of DPN in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the data of 770 patients screened for DPN with type 2 diabetes mellitus in the Department of General Practice, Jiangwan Town Subdistrict Community Health Service Center between May 2024 and July 2024. The data included 91 variables for baseline description analysis. The dataset was divided into a training and test set for the model evaluation in a 7:3 ratio, and feature selection was performed with the Boruta algorithm. Eleven ML algorithms were used to develop diagnostic models for DPN. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, and decision curves analysis were applied to evaluate the performance of the models, and the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) method was adopted to interpret the performance of the models and the importance of features.

RESULTS: The study included 770 type 2 diabetes mellitus inpatients, with a mean age of 70.88 ± 5.88 years, and 26.62% (205/770) had DPN. Integrated with the results of evaluation, we selected logistic regression (LR), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and light gradient boosting machine (LGBM) models including neurological examinations as the top-performing algorithms. Based on variable importance ranking from the three models with overlap analysis, we identified 12 key predictors. Among the three models, the tuning fork test, ankle reflex, and temperature sensation test were all identified as the top three important predictors. Meanwhile, the low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in the XGBoost model and the total cholesterol (Tch) in the LGBM were the important features for predicting DPN. In addition, excluding neurological examination findings, both LDL-C and Tch were important indicators with high contribution degree.

CONCLUSIONS: The ML approach helped establish diagnostic models with stable performance. Meanwhile, the use of interpretable SHAP methods can enhance the clinical applicability of the models.

articles.title: Maternal Intensive Care Admission, Unplanned Peripartum Hysterectomy, and Breast Milk Feeding by Hospital Discharge: A Population Based Repeated Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Characterize trends and factors associated with breast milk feeding among patients undergoing maternal ICU admission or peripartum unplanned hysterectomy.

DESIGN: Population-level repeated cross-sectional study.

SETTING: United States National Vital Statistics System data between 2016 and 2023.

POPULATION: Liveborn singleton, non-anomalous deliveries from 34 + 0 to 42 + 6 weeks.

METHODS: Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression reported as annual average percentage change (AAPC). Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to assess the association between morbidity and breast milk feeding by hospital discharge.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Temporal trends in severe morbidity defined as maternal ICU admission and/or unplanned hysterectomy and associated breast milk feeding by hospital discharge.

RESULTS: Of the 23 589 073 births included, 33 121 (0.14%) were complicated by severe morbidity. Any severe morbidity increased from 102 to 157 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.1%, 95% CI: 1.3% to 7.2%) with increased hysterectomy only from 15 to 24 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.2%, 95% CI: 0.7% to 8.2%), ICU admission only from 75 to 117 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.5%, 95% CI: 1.5% to 7.8%), and no change in concurrent hysterectomy and ICU admission. Patients with any severe morbidity had lower breast milk feeding by hospital discharge (65.2% vs. 84.1%, adjusted OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.45-0.47). Despite temporal increases in breast milk feeding by hospital discharge for patients without severe morbidity, the same was not seen for those with severe morbidity.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify a population in whom additional support and services would help individuals who wish to breastfeed or provide expressed breast milk, when clinically appropriate.

articles.title: Nutritional management, dietary intervention, and long-term monitoring in pediatric Prader-Willi syndrome: A 3-year case-based clinical observation.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract: Nutritional management is fundamental in Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS), but longitudinal data from routine pediatric practice are limited. We describe a 3-year nutritional follow-up of a boy with PWS complicated by obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, hyperuricemia, and fatty liver. Management consisted of an energy-restricted, nutritionally balanced diet, structured meal timing, portion control, family-based supervision, exercise guidance, and serial monitoring of anthropometry, body composition, metabolic markers, liver enzymes, growth, and pubertal development. Weight and metabolic status improved initially, but weight later showed a U-shaped trajectory during puberty, likely related to slower growth, delayed pubertal progression, and reduced adherence after school transition. These findings support the need for ongoing, developmentally tailored nutritional monitoring in children with PWS.

articles.title: Association of tirofiban with discharge functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Tirofiban, a glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor antagonist, has been investigated for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but its association with early discharge functional outcomes remains uncertain. This study evaluated the association between tirofiban use and discharge outcomes in AIS patients.

METHODS: We enrolled 344 consecutive AIS patients, including 191 who received tirofiban and 153 who did not. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Analyses included propensity score matching, multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors, ordinal logistic regression, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, restricted cubic spline analysis, and E-value analysis. Primary outcomes were discharge modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores.

RESULTS: After adjusting for nine relevant covariates, tirofiban use was associated with significantly lower discharge mRS scores (β = -0.352, 95% CI -0.625 to -0.079, p = 0.011). This remained robust under HC3 robust standard errors (p = 0.020), ordinal logistic regression (OR = 0.434, 95% CI 0.267-0.706, p < 0.001), and propensity score matching (mean difference = -0.456, 95% CI -0.879 to -0.033, p = 0.035). The association was consistent across age, sex, and admission NIHSS subgroups, with an E-value of 2.40. No significant association was observed between tirofiban use and discharge NIHSS scores.

DISCUSSION: These findings suggest tirofiban use is associated with better early functional outcomes in AIS patients, as reflected by lower discharge mRS scores. The robustness across multiple analytical approaches strengthens the validity of these observations. Further prospective multicenter randomized controlled trials are warranted.

articles.title: Poly-β-Hydroxybutyrate Nanoparticles Improve Septic Immunoparalysis and Prognosis by Energy-Refreshing via Controlled Release of β-Hydroxybutyrate.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated immunoparalysis remains a key driver of poor clinical outcomes, yet no targeted pharmacotherapies have received clinical approval. Accumulating evidence identifies cellular metabolic dysfunction as a core pathogenic driver of this state, positioning metabolic modulation as a rational therapeutic approach. Biodegradable poly-β-hydroxybutyrate nanoparticles (PHB NPs) are fabricated via emulsion-solvent evaporation to address the short in vivo half-life and systemic adverse effects of free β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), leveraging the intrinsic integrated carrier-prodrug nature of the PHB polymer.The optimized PHB NPs formulation exhibits uniform spherical morphology, extended circulation half-life, good biocompatibility, and broad tissue biodistribution. PHB NPs attenuate immunoparalysis both in vitro and in vivo, improve survival and restore immune responsiveness to LPS rechallenge in septic mice, and preserve cognitive function in surviving animals. Mechanistically, sustained BHB release from the nanoparticles restores cellular bioenergetics in immunoparalyzed cells through the tricarboxylic acid cycle-oxidative phosphorylation (TCA-OXPHOS) axis. These protective effects are recapitulated ex vivo in immunoparalyzed peripheral blood monocytes from a small cohort of septic patients.Collectively, these data indicate that PHB NPs ameliorate sepsis-induced immunoparalysis by restoring immune cell bioenergetics, and represent an energy-targeted nanotherapeutic candidate for further clinical development.

articles.title: Weather-driven infection events as indicators of severe wheat stripe rust.
articles.abstract: Plant pathologists, agronomists and crop consultants are often called on to help growers evaluate in-season disease risk and determine if management actions are needed to suppress disease development. Tools that help disease specialists and other practitioners better evaluate the influence of environment on disease development could help guide these recommendations. The objectives of this research were to identify weather conditions influencing the infection of wheat by stripe rust (Puccinia striiformis f.sp. tritici) in field environments, to develop models estimating the probability of infection based on environment, and to evaluate if the predicted infection events were an indicator that weather conditions were favorable for severe stripe rust development in commercial wheat fields. The influence of environment on infection was studied using a bioassay approach that involved exposing inoculated, susceptible wheat seedlings within a wheat field environment. Following the exposure, the plants were incubated with a diurnal temperature cycle of 12-20°C and stripe rust incidence and severity visually evaluated after 14 days. The bioassay was conducted 116 times over three wheat growing seasons. Infection was coded as a binary variable with ≥1% incidence considered an infection event and logistic regression used to model the probability of infection based on weather during the exposure period. Multiple predictive models of stripe rust infection in field environments were developed based on the bioassay results. Several of the identified models correctly classified days as favorable for infection with more than 80% accuracy. The infection models confirmed the importance of extended periods of high relative humidity and favorable temperature on the infection processes of P. striiformis f.sp. tritici and provided guidance on specific thresholds that were conducive for infection in field environments (e.g. > 8 h of RH ≥ 87% and a temperature between 5-25°C). The experimental approach also helped evaluate the influence of wind speed and rainfall events on the infection process that are difficult to accurately simulate in controlled environments. The resulting infection models were combined with simulations of wheat growth and used to estimate the risk of severe stripe rust developing at locations throughout Kansas (n=104). This analysis identified that the accumulation of infection events between jointing and flowering stages of growth were influential on the development of severe disease in research plots and commercial wheat fields. Models estimating the risk of severe disease correctly classified 79% of disease observations collected over 17 years. The timing of these predictions relative to crop growth and disease development could help disease specialists evaluate and communicate the risk of stripe rust in the future.

articles.title: Comparative treatment effects of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation in clinical practice vary over time due to channelling.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Temporal shifts in patient characteristics can influence comparative treatment effects within a certain indication. We investigated patient characteristics and comparative effectiveness and safety for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and warfarin over the time period where DOACs replaced warfarin as preferred stroke prophylaxis in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF).

METHODS: We applied the cohort design to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and created 12 sequential subcohorts of patients with NVAF between 2011 and 2023. Patients with a DOAC or warfarin prescription following a 1-year prescription-free period were included. Baseline characteristics were compared between subcohorts. Survival analysis was used to evaluate the risk of ischaemic stroke (effectiveness outcome) and major bleeds (safety outcome).

RESULTS: We included 207 393 patients with NVAF (45% women, 77% DOAC users, mean age 76 years). In early subcohorts, a history of stroke/transient ischaemic attack was more common among DOAC users. In later subcohorts, diabetes, deep venous thrombosis/pulmonary embolism and antihypertensive use were more common among warfarin users. History of other cardiovascular disease, renal failure and diuretic use were consistently higher among warfarin users. Over time, the crude stroke hazard ratio for DOAC users compared with warfarin users shifted from 2.66 (95% CI 2.00-3.52) to 0.62 (0.23-1.67). This trend was attenuated in adjusted analyses. No such trends were seen for major bleeds.

CONCLUSION: DOACs had unfavourable effectiveness estimates in earlier subcohorts, potentially due to preferential prescribing to higher risk patients. Early observational studies may encounter initial biases, underscoring the need for robust methodological approaches when evaluating newly introduced medicines.

articles.title: Bayesian Additive Regression Trees modeling of pharmacogenomic and clinical data predicts amlodipine response in hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The adoption of precision medicine in antihypertensive treatment remains challenging, largely because of substantial interindividual variability in drug response. This study aimed to determine whether genotyping combined with Bayesian machine-learning methods could improve the prediction of response to amlodipine.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study of 292 Chinese patients with hypertension treated with amlodipine. Eight single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in key pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic pathways were sequenced. After excluding two SNPs with insufficient variation, six SNPs were integrated with clinical variables to develop prediction models. The outcome, blood pressure control as a measure of treatment efficacy, was defined as achieving office SBP less than 140 mmHg and DBP less than 90 mmHg after treatment. Using a rigorous validation framework, we compared Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART) with Random Forest Classification (RFC) and Bayesian linear modeling through repeated cross-validation and external validation.

RESULTS: At the rs5065 locus, 217 individuals (99.5%) carried the wild-type genotype, and rs2740574 was exclusively homozygous for the mutant allele. Therefore, only the remaining six SNPs were used for model development, comparison, and evaluation. The BART model achieved an external validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) value of 0.846, notably outperforming RFC (AUC = 0.61) and Bayesian linear models (AUC = 0.644-0.665).

CONCLUSION: BART substantially improves prediction of blood pressure control in patients with hypertension treated with amlodipine monotherapy. Integrating pharmacogenomic data with advanced Bayesian machine learning offers a robust framework for personalized antihypertensive therapy.

articles.title: Transcranial Doppler for Bedside Assessment of Cerebral Hemodynamics following Mechanical Thrombectomy in Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Prospective Observational Feasibility Case Series from a Low- and Middle-Income Country.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) represents an uncommon yet potentially reversible form of stroke, predominantly affecting young adults. Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is increasingly used in patients with extensive thrombus burden or medically refractory cases. In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where repeated neuroimaging may not be readily feasible, transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography offers a non-invasive, bedside, and low-cost approach to assess cerebral hemodynamics. Its role in CVT remains underexplored.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the changes in middle cerebral artery (MCA) flow velocities measured by TCD ultrasonography in patients with CVT at baseline, day 1, and day 2 following MT.

METHODS: Fourteen patients (15-60 years) with magnetic resonance venography-confirmed CVT undergoing MT were prospectively studied. Bilateral MCA peak systolic velocity (PSV), mean flow velocity (MFV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), and pulsatility index (PI) were recorded at baseline and on days 1 and 2 postprocedure. Serial MCA flow parameters across baseline, day 1 and day 2 were compared using repeated-measures analysis of variance, with paired t-tests for pre-specified comparisons against baseline (confirmed by Wilcoxon signed-rank tests); a two-sided P < 0.05 was considered significant.

RESULTS: We observed a predominantly young male cohort (57%) of mean age 34.4 ± 11 years. Venous involvement was left (42.8%), right (42.8%), or bilateral (14.2%), with raised intracranial pressure in 78.6%. No significant MCA flow changes occurred on day 1. By day 2, right MCA EDV showed a decreasing trend, though statistically not significant (P = 0.06). Other parameters, such as PSV, MFV, and PI, showed non-significant trends. The left MCA parameters remained stable.

CONCLUSION: TCD assessment of the MCA may have limited sensitivity in detecting early hemodynamic changes following MT in CVT. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up durations are needed to better define the role of TCD in this setting.

articles.title: Association of Middle Cerebral Artery Doppler Parameters With Neonatal Outcomes in Idiopathic Polyhydramnios: A Prospective Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler parameters in patients diagnosed with idiopathic polyhydramnios and those with a normal amniotic fluid index (AFI) and to investigate the effects of MCA Doppler findings on neonatal outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was designed as a prospective case-control study and conducted at a single tertiary care center. A total of 166 patients, including 83 with idiopathic polyhydramnios and 83 healthy controls between 24 and 35 weeks of gestation were included. We divided the patients diagnosed with polyhydramnios into three groups as mild, moderate, and severe. MCA Doppler evaluations were performed for each patient.

RESULTS: MCA Doppler parameters pulsatility index (PI) and resistive index (RI) were significantly lower in pregnancies with idiopathic polyhydramnios (p < 0.05). A significant difference was observed in neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions between the two groups (p < 0.05). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that the optimal cut-off value of the MCA PI for predicting NICU admissions was 1.37, with a sensitivity of 69% and a specificity of 50% (area under the curve = 0.759; p = 0.021). There was no difference in UA-PI and CPR levels between both groups (p > 0.05). Univariable regression analysis showed that polyhydramnios was associated with a 7.48-fold increase in the odds of NICU admission. The MCA PI level, gestational age at birth, and first minute Apgar score were lower in the severe polyhydramnios group compared to the mild polyhydramnios group.

CONCLUSION: MCA PI and RI values were found to be lower in fetuses with idiopathic polyhydramnios compared to those with a normal AFI, suggesting altered fetal cerebral vascular resistance that may be compatible with blood-flow redistribution. MCA Doppler parameters showed an exploratory association with NICU admission and may provide additional information for neonatal risk assessment; they do not prove fetal hypoxia.

articles.title: Microduplication Overlapping YY1 at 14q32.2 Narrows the Candidate Interval for Cortical Malformation and Early-Onset Arterial Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: YY1 encodes a zinc-finger transcription factor that regulates chromatin remodeling and plays a critical role in brain development and vascular remodeling. Its nuclear co-activator, YY1AP1, causes Grange syndrome, a systemic arteriopathy with impaired vascular smooth-muscle-cell proliferation and differentiation. Haploinsufficiency of YY1 causes Gabriele-de Vries syndrome, whereas the phenotypic consequences of increased YY1 dosage have not been well characterized. We describe a 3.6-year-old girl with prenatal ventriculomegaly, growth restriction, and complex brain malformations including septo-optic dysplasia, dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, diffuse cortical dysgyria, and focal cortical dysplasia. At 7 months, she presented with acute left hemiparesis due to an acute right striatal/internal capsule arterial ischemic stroke and a subacute left striatal infarct, without clear arteriopathy. Head CT demonstrated bilateral basal ganglia and subcortical white matter calcifications. Echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale (PFO) but was otherwise normal; metabolic and thrombophilia workups were normal. She later developed drug-resistant epilepsy requiring hemispherotomy. Examination showed mild microcephaly, hemiparesis, and moderate developmental delay. Chromosomal microarray identified a 14q32.2 duplication encompassing the first exon and promoter region of YY1, classified as a variant of unknown significance. This duplication is the smallest reported copy-number gain overlapping YY1 and therefore potentially narrows the candidate genomic interval, given the reported phenotype. The overlapping phenotype with larger distal 14q duplications that also include YY1 supports the hypothesis that increased YY1 dosage contributes to this phenotype, although other potential mechanisms are plausible. Identification of additional patients and functional studies are necessary to delineate the precise pathogenic role of YY1 in this complex observed phenotype.

articles.title: Efficacy of a training program to support the application of the Guideline Evidence-based Health Information: a randomized controlled trial and process evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Guideline Evidence-based Health Information addresses health information providers and aims to improve the quality of health information. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a training program for health information providers to support the application of the guideline. We expected the intervention to improve the quality of health information compared with providing the guideline alone.

METHODS: In this superiority randomized controlled trial, providers responsible for producing and publishing health information were allocated 1:1 to the intervention (guideline and training program) and control (publicly available guideline) groups using computer-generated block randomization. The e-learning program (31 h, offered over 6-7 weeks) comprised modules on evidence-based medicine and the application of the guideline. Each provider committed to producing a single piece of health information informing a health-related decision on the topic of their choice. The primary outcome was the quality of health information, operationalized as adherence to the guideline recommendations, as measured using the Mapping Health Information Quality (MAPPinfo) checklist. Means were compared between groups using a t-test. The assessment and analyses were blinded to the group allocation. An accompanying process evaluation was conducted.

RESULTS: We included 18 health information providers (nine in each group), with a total of 54 individual participants. Eight health information items were assessed in each group. The primary analysis estimated the mean MAPPinfo checklist values at 30.2% (95% CI, 24.6 to 35.9) for the intervention and at 22.7% (95% CI, 17.4 to 27.9) for the control group. The difference between groups was estimated at 7.6% (95% CI, - 0.2 to 15.3; p = 0.055). Individual and structural implementation barriers of the guideline recommendations were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: We did not achieve the targeted sample size of 26 providers. A lack of resources was one of the main barriers to recruitment. Although our study did not provide conclusive evidence regarding the primary outcome, the participants rated the training program as relevant. Therefore, the training program will be made available to health information providers upon request.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN registry, ID: ISRCTN96941060. Registered on March 7, 2019.

STUDY PROTOCOL: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13063-020-04287-1 (Trials 2020).

articles.title: Factors associated with missed video directly observed therapy sessions among persons with TB.
articles.journal: The international journal of tuberculosis and lung disease : the official journal of the International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease
articles.abstract: <sec><title>BACKGROUND</title>Advanced digital technologies, such as video directly observed therapy (VDOT), are increasingly used to support TB treatment adherence monitoring. However, missed VDOT sessions remain a challenge, particularly in low-resource settings. This study aimed to determine the factors associated with the number of missed VDOT submissions among patients using VDOT.</sec><sec><title>METHODS</title>We conducted a secondary analysis of data from the DOT Selfie randomised controlled trial implemented in Uganda. The outcome of interest was the number of missed VDOT sessions throughout treatment. A negative binomial regression model was used to examine factors associated with the outcome. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals were reported.</sec><sec><title>RESULTS</title>Among the 71 patients included in the analysis, 32% were HIV positive. HIV co-infection (cIRR = 2.2; 1.2-4.0), age >30 years (cIRR = 2.0; 1.1-3.6), alcohol consumption (aIRR = 2.3; 1.1-5.1), being married (aIRR = 2.2; 1.1-4.1), and having ≤4 household members (aIRR = 1.9; 1.1-3.3) were associated with a higher incidence rate of missed VDOT sessions.</sec><sec><title>CONCLUSION</title>In this study, alcohol use and HIV co-infection independently affected missed video sessions. However, after adjusting for confounding, marital status and household size remained important factors that should be further studied.</sec>.

articles.title: How do adult migrants with active TB adhere to care in high-income countries? A systematic review.
articles.journal: The international journal of tuberculosis and lung disease : the official journal of the International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease
articles.abstract: <sec><title>BACKGROUND</title>In high-income countries (HICs), adult migrants treated for active TB could face barriers that hinder adherence to the TB care pathway.</sec><sec><title>OBJECTIVE</title>To identify the specific features of adherence to the TB care process among adult migrants in HICs.</sec><sec><title>METHODS</title>Three researchers independently selected empirical studies on adult migrant's adherence to the TB care process published between 1 January 2010 and 1 November 2024 in MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. Outcomes included treatment adherence and retention in care.</sec><sec><title>RESULTS</title>Of 355 records screened, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. All used quantitative designs, and most (67%, n = 16) were conducted in Europe. Among the four studies reporting statistically significant associations, all found that migrant status was linked to poorer adherence outcomes. Descriptions of migrant characteristics were limited: legal status appeared in only four studies, and none assessed migration motives. Several individual and structural barriers to adherence were identified. The year of arrival emerged as an informative variable, reflecting combined social determinants shaping care access and treatment continuity.</sec><sec><title>CONCLUSION</title>Adult migrants face substantial challenges in adhering to the TB care process in HICs. Future research should more precisely characterise this population, which is currently described in insufficient detail.</sec>.

articles.title: Second-hand smoke exposure linked to TB infection or disease in children/adolescents: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The international journal of tuberculosis and lung disease : the official journal of the International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease
articles.abstract: <sec><title>BACKGROUND</title>TB, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection and TB disease, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among children and adolescents aged 0-18 years in low-resource settings. Second-hand smoke (SHS) exposure is a widespread public health threat, and children are especially vulnerable due to their developing immune and respiratory systems. However, evidence regarding the association between SHS exposure and childhood TB risk remains inconsistent across observational studies.</sec><sec><title>METHODS</title>This PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis (CRD420261354572) searched seven databases and grey literature from 2000 to December 2025. We included English observational studies of 0-18-year-old children/adolescents in low-resource settings. Study quality was assessed via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated.</sec><sec><title>RESULTS</title>Twelve eligible studies with a total of 6,411 participants were pooled for analysis. Compared with children and adolescents without household SHS exposure, those exposed to SHS had significantly elevated combined odds of Mtb infection or TB disease. The pooled OR was 2.689 (95% confidence interval: 2.384, P < 0.001), with negligible between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.0%). Egger's test suggested mild publication bias across included studies.</sec><sec><title>CONCLUSION</title>SHS exposure is significantly associated with higher pooled odds of Mtb infection or TB disease among children and adolescents in low-resource settings.</sec>.

articles.title: Mass TB screening in a Brazilian prison: prevalence and implications for control.
articles.journal: The international journal of tuberculosis and lung disease : the official journal of the International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease
articles.abstract: <sec><title>BACKGROUND</title>TB remains a major public health challenge in prisons due to overcrowding and limited health care access. Evidence on integrated mass screening strategies using molecular testing and computer-aided detection (CAD) in Brazilian prisons is scarce.</sec><sec><title>METHODS</title>A cross-sectional mass screening study was conducted in a male prison in southern Brazil. Screening included symptom assessment, digital chest X-ray with automated interpretation (LunitTB), and GeneXpert MTB/RIF testing. TB infection (TBI) was assessed using interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA). Socio-demographic, clinical, and behavioural data were analysed to identify factors associated with TB.</sec><sec><title>RESULTS</title>A total of 652 (96.3%) of 677 individuals completed screening; 120 (18.4%) underwent IGRA testing. Active TB prevalence was 4.7% (31 cases). TB was associated with contact with a TB case within the same cell, alcohol use disorder, weight loss, chest pain, and night sweats. Among 117 individuals tested, 62% were TBI-positive. The CAD system showed strong performance (area under the curve: 0.90; optimal threshold: 43.5).</sec><sec><title>CONCLUSION</title>Systematic screening revealed a high burden of TB and TBI in this setting. Chest X-ray combined with CAD was effective, identifying cases likely missed by symptom-based screening alone.</sec>.

articles.title: Phosphorylation of RpoD upregulates suilysin and enhances Streptococcus suis virulence.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is a prevalent zoonotic pathogen that severely threatens the swine industry and human public health. Suilysin (SLY), a major pore-forming toxin of S. suis, is indispensable for bacterial hemolytic activity and systemic pathogenicity, yet the upstream regulatory mechanism controlling SLY production remains unclear. Serine/threonine kinase (STK) has been characterized to modulate bacterial physiology and virulence by phosphorylating multiple substrate proteins. Our previous phosphoproteomics analysis indicated that the housekeeping sigma factor RpoD was a potential STK substrate. In vitro phosphorylation assays combined with mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation and site-directed mutagenesis confirmed that STK directly phosphorylated RpoD at Thr-208 residue. Phenotypic tests revealed that RpoD phosphorylation had no obvious impact on bacterial growth and biofilm formation but specifically promoted the thermotolerance and hemolytic activity of S. suis. Notably, the rpoD overexpression mutant strain SC19-rpoD significantly upregulated the transcription and protein production of SLY, whereas the phosphorylation-deficient mutant SC19-rpoD T208A abolished this promotion effect, indicating that Thr-208 phosphorylation is required for sly upregulation, although the underlying molecular mechanism remains to be fully defined. Furthermore, mouse infection models demonstrated that the SC19-rpoD T208A mutant exhibited alleviated splenic pathological injury, reduced bacterial loads in multiple organs, and significantly improved host survival, indicating that the loss of RpoD phosphorylation impairs S. suis virulence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that STK-mediated phosphorylation of RpoD at Thr-208 is required for sly upregulation and contributes to the S. suis pathogenesis.

articles.title: Evolution and function of genetic polymorphisms in the Helicobacter pylori type IV secretion pilus protein CagL in gastric carcinogenesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cytotoxin-associated genes (cag) type IV secretion system (T4SS) of the gastric pathogen Helicobacter pylori constitutes a key determinant in gastric cancer (GC) development. The CagL protein represents a VirB5 ortholog that acts as a signalling factor at the surface of the T4SS pilus, which facilitates binding to host target cells to inject T4SS substrates such as the CagA oncoprotein and ADP-heptose. Previous studies reported the presence of a hypervariable region in CagL at amino acid positions 58 and 59 with a proposed role in GC progression, however, studies using a large number of H. pylori strains as well as detailed functional experiments are yet missing.

METHODS: Here, we investigated the CagL status in 2,267 worldwide H. pylori genomes from an evolutionary point of view, concerning gastric disease status, and directly compared the Y58/E59 versus N58/K59 polymorphism in CagL in the GC-associated H. pylori strain 7.13 with regard to T4SS-pilus formation and cancer signalling during infection of gastric epithelial cells in vitro and infection of Mongolian gerbils in vivo.

RESULTS: Structural analysis showed that the genetic polymorphism, located in an amino acid loop flanked by two α-helices, affects CagL conformation and functional activity. Remarkably, both strains revealed similar robust T4SS-pilus formation, but functional differences. We demonstrate that wild-type H. pylori 7.13 encoding N58/K59 CagL triggered GC development in Mongolian gerbils and characteristic GC signalling events in gastric epithelial cells, including CagA phosphorylation, activation of MAP kinases (p38, ERK1/2 and JNK), β-catenin and cell motility as well as pronounced induction of pro-inflammatory transcription factor NF-κB-dependent interleukin-8 (IL-8) production and DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), whereas H. pylori encoding Y58/E59 CagL elicited markedly attenuated responses.

CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that the Y58/E59 mutation impairs translocation of CagA into host cells, but retains T4SS-pilus formation and ADP-heptose-dependent NF-κB activation. This implies that CagL mutation may act as molecular regulator of the T4SS for "finetuning" CagA delivery, host inflammation and other oncogenic responses. Interestingly, this scenario is similar to previously reported CagY, another T4SS-pilus protein, which can cause the gain or loss of IL-8 production by genetic polymorphisms that occur through recombination events.

articles.title: Retrospective analysis of the transmission of difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa - genotype beats phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTRPA) represents a challenging resistance phenotype with carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa playing a major role. However, carbapenemase-negative DTRPA (CN-DTRPA) are more susceptible to reserve antibiotics and rarely reported in outbreaks, differing from frequently outbreak-associated carbapenemase-producing DTRPA (CP-DTRPA) with limited therapeutic options. Despite, international guidelines recommend equal infection prevention and control (IPC) measures. Here, we analysed the transmission of CP-DTRPA and CN-DTRPA using epidemiology and whole-genome sequencing (WGS).

METHODS: Clinical DTRPA isolates collected between 2019 and 2024 were subjected to WGS. Genetic clusters were defined using cgMLST thresholds of ≤ 11 and ≤ 3 allelic differences. Epidemiological relatedness was estimated on hospital stay, interpatient contact and environmental exposures. For possibly epidemiologically linked cases, precolonisation with carbapenem-susceptible P. aeruginosa (CSPA) and antibiotic exposure during hospitalisation were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 190 DTRPA isolates, CN-DTRPA (79.5%) was predominant compared to 20.5% CP-DTRPA, mainly carrying blaVIM-2. Twelve genetic clusters involving 39 patients were identified. Seven clusters (CP-DTRPA n = 4; CN-DTRPA n = 2, CP-DTRPA/CN-DTRPA-mixed n = 1) showed possible epidemiological relatedness. CP-DTRPA isolates were frequently associated with clusters (OR 17.47, 95% CI 7.43-41.08) and environmental transmission. Diverse CN-DTRPA were rather linked to interpatient CSPA-transmission following CN-DTRPA emergence after prolonged antibiotic exposure.

CONCLUSION: CN-DTRPA predominated and displayed high diversity, consistent with possible antibiotic-driven resistance development in precolonised patients. In contrast, less frequent and less diverse CP-DTRPA were associated to outbreaks. These findings highlight the need to evaluate differentiated IPC strategies, including targeted screening and environmental interventions for CP-DTRPA, while further investigating the potential role of antimicrobial stewardship in preventing the emergence of CN-DTRPA. Multicentre studies are required for evidence-based IPC strategies.

articles.title: Empagliflozin's role in cardiometabolic disease treatment: an Egyptian expert's view.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given the expanding therapeutic indications of empagliflozin (EMPA) beyond glycemic control and the growing burden of cardiometabolic diseases, this review evaluated its efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness in the Egyptian population within the global context.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature review of PubMed and Google Scholar identified clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical guidelines published in English up to July 2025. We included studies reporting EMPA's pharmacological profile, mechanisms of action, and clinical outcomes on diabetes mellitus, cardiometabolic diseases, renal and hepatic functions, safety during Ramadan fasting, and cost-effectiveness.

RESULTS: EMPA, as monotherapy or combination therapy, improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes through Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibition. For type 1 diabetes mellitus, despite improving glycemic control as an adjunct therapy, it is not recommended due to the increased risk of diabetic ketoacidosis. EMPA reduces major cardiovascular events, heart failure hospitalization, and chronic kidney disease progression, with modest weight loss and blood pressure reduction, in patients with or without diabetes. Emerging evidence suggests benefits in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), although it is not approved for this indication. EMPA demonstrates a favorable safety profile and low hypoglycemia risk during Ramadan fasting. It enhances patients' quality of life and is considered cost-effective.

CONCLUSIONS: EMPA extends beyond glucose-lowering by reducing cardiorenal morbidity and mortality in patients with or without diabetes. It shows a favorable safety profile, even during Ramadan fasting, supporting its suitability for the large Muslim population. Further research should evaluate its role in MASLD and assess cost-effectiveness in Egypt.

articles.title: In vivo minimally invasive reduction and fixation of sacroiliac luxation using a dedicated novel instrument system.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of a dedicated sacroiliac luxation instrument system (SILIS) featuring a minimally invasive lucent aiming device (MILAD) during osteosynthesis of sacroiliac luxation/fracture (SIL/F). We hypothesized that SILIS-MILAD assisted surgeries would be safe and as or more accurate than reported minimally invasive osteosynthesis (MIO) and open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) techniques.

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective, observational case series.

ANIMALS: A total of 10 client owned dogs with traumatic SIL/F.

METHODS: Dogs with SIL/F were treated using SILIS-MILAD assisted techniques. Outcome measures included shallow dose equivalent (SDE [mrem]), percent of reduction (PoR) and hemipelvic canal width ratio (HCWR), and sacral screw orientation angles in the transverse (dorsoventral angle, DVA) and dorsal (craniocaudal, CCA) planes. Data were reported as mean ± SD using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 10 dogs with 13 SIL/Fs were included. Mean patient SDE was ~122 mrem ± 55 mrem. In contrast, operating room (OR) personnel SDEs were negligible (~0.8 mrem ± 0.4 mrem). Mean PoR and HCWR were 95.6% ± 5.0% and 0.9 ± 0.2, respectively. Mean DVA and CCA were 1.1° ± 0.8° and 2.3° ± 1.8°, respectively. All patients were ambulatory when discharged.

CONCLUSION: Clinical SILIS-MILAD assisted SIL/F fixation eliminated surgeon and OR personnel exposure to radiation and consistently provided near anatomical reduction and as or more accurate sacral screw placement than previously reported in ORIF and MIO studies.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: This study demonstrates that SILIS-MILAD assisted surgeries can be safe and accurate and therefore provide a valid alternative to current open and minimally invasive techniques.

articles.title: Nocturnal intravenous gamma-hydroxybutyrate and sleep architecture in non-sedated intensive care unit patients: a polysomnographic experience.
Validated small Col-like accessory elements in a near-clonal same-host stool-blood Salmonella pair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontyphoidal Salmonella can cause bloodstream infection in vulnerable hosts, yet the bacterial differences that remain when paired stool and blood isolates are already near-clonal are not well defined. Core-genome SNP analysis is useful for assessing relatedness, but may overlook small circular accessory elements that are difficult to resolve using standard assembly workflows. This study investigated whether a clinically linked same-host stool-blood Salmonella pair contained validated small Col-like accessory elements not apparent from core SNP analysis alone.

METHODS: We analyzed a temporally adjacent same-host stool-blood Salmonella index pair, FB1-XY1, together with two short-interval stool-stool comparator pairs. The analysis integrated strict reads-backed core SNP filtering, accessory-element analysis, Illumina and ONT read-level support, PCR/Sanger/qPCR validation and public-genome background screening.

RESULTS: Strict reads-backed filtering retained only four core SNPs in the FB1-XY1 pair, whereas both stool-stool comparator pairs had no retained strict core SNPs. Despite this minimal core-genome divergence, the blood isolate XY1 carried two validated small Col-like accessory elements. The first was an assembly-resolved 13.8-kb ColRNAI-like plasmid containing ColRNAI-like replicon hits and duplicated cka/colicin K-like annotations, with a Proteinase K-sensitive inhibitory phenotype. The second was a 5,241-bp Col156-like circular element, contig_40, which was not represented as a near-full-length replicon in the final XY1 closed-assembly output but was supported by full-length XY1 Illumina and ONT read coverage, 116 ONT junction-spanning reads, PCR, Sanger sequencing, multi-colony screening and qPCR. FB1 Illumina reads showed no corresponding support for contig_40. In a screened public Salmonella background of 16,456 genomes, strict full-length hits were rare for both elements: 2 hits for the 13.8-kb plasmid and 15 hits for contig_40. Neither element had a strict full-length hit among 402 screened Muenster genomes.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify small Col-like circular accessory elements as a validated, assembly-sensitive layer of genomic variation in a near-clonal same-host stool-blood Salmonella pair. By showing that clinically linked stool-blood isolates can differ at the level of small circular accessory elements despite minimal core-genome divergence, this study extends paired-isolate interpretation beyond core SNP relatedness alone. Integrating read-level evidence, molecular validation and public-genome context may improve the interpretation of small circular elements in clinical microbial genomics.

articles.title: Association of Maternal Immune Activation With Pruritic Urticarial Papules and Plaques of Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP) is a common dermatosis of pregnancy, but its etiology remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify whether maternal immune activation (MIA) is associated with PUPPP.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of pregnant patients using a population-based administrative cohort of all live births in California from 2016 to 2021. Patients with PUPPP were identified using ICD-10 code O26.86. MIA was defined by ICD-10 diagnoses of infection, autoimmune disease, or atopic disease during pregnancy. Poisson log-linear regression was used to estimate crude and adjusted risk ratios (RR, aRR) for associations between PUPPP and MIA.

RESULTS: Among 2,275,929 pregnancies, there were 3286 (0.14%) patients with PUPPP. Compared with patients without PUPPP, patients with PUPPP had higher rates of gestational hypertension (6.2% vs. 4.0%, p < 0.0001) and preeclampsia (10.9% vs. 5.2%, p < 0.0001). Atopy was associated with increased risk of PUPPP (aRR 1.7, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.6-1.9), as was autoimmunity (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.1) and maternal infection (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.4-1.7). Patients with PUPPP were less likely to have a pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2 (21.2% vs. 25.4%, p < 0.0001) but more likely to exceed recommended gestational weight gain (64.3% vs. 52.4%, p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: MIA during pregnancy, including atopy, autoimmunity, and infection, was independently associated with increased risk of PUPPP. These findings suggest immune dysregulation may contribute to PUPPP pathogenesis. The association with excessive gestational weight gain further supports a potential role for inflammation secondary to connective tissue injury from abdominal distension.

articles.title: The effect of early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
articles.journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECT: This study aimed to investigate the effect of implementing early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function indices and prognosis after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) treatment in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

METHODS: Patients diagnosed with AMI and treated with PCI between March 2020 and May 2024 were selected as the study participants. This was a prospective randomised controlled trial; patients were randomly allocated to an observation group and a control group using a random number table method (157 cases per group). The control group received routine nursing after surgery, whereas the observation group received structured early rehabilitation nursing. After 6 months of intervention, cardiac function indices, the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and quality of life were compared between the two groups. Cardiac function indices included stroke volume (SV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) and 6-minute walking distance (6MWD). The World Health Organization Quality of Life Measurement Brief Form was used to evaluate quality of life.

RESULTS: After nursing intervention, the levels of SV, LVEF and 6MWD in the cardiac function indices of the observation group were higher than those of the control group, whereas the levels of LVEDV were lower than those of the control group; the differences between the two groups were significant (p < 0.05). The total incidence of MACE in the observation group was lower than that in the control group (p < 0.05). In the comparison of quality-of-life scores, the observation group scored higher than the control group in five domains (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Early rehabilitation nursing for patients with AMI can effectively improve patients' cardiac function indices and reduce the risk of MACE, thereby improving their quality of life.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: ISRCTN18094960.

articles.title: Benralizumab Inhibits Upper Airway Expression of Thymic Stromal Lymphopoietin in Severe Asthma.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology

articles.title: Stroke-CORE: master study protocol of the national cohort of the specialty network stroke within the network university medicine in Germany.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although Germany has a strong history of stroke research, it currently lacks a national harmonised infrastructure for clinical stroke research. To address this gap, the stroke-specific Specialty Network (SN Stroke) of the Network University Medicine (NUM) was established as a comprehensive research platform. Hereby we present the protocol of the Stroke-CORE cohort (COhort for REsearch in Stroke) within SN Stroke enrolling a large representative cohort of patients with acute ischeamic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage in Germany.

METHODS: Stroke-CORE is a national, prospective, longitudinal, multi-centre cohort study with a decentralised biobank, structured as a modular umbrella protocol. Adult patients with acute ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage, and paediatric stroke patients are enrolled at participating hospitals. Data collection follows four adaptive levels, ranging from a core clinical data set (Level 1) to modules covering the whole stroke care pathway (Level 2), biosamples (Level 3), and voluntary additional modules (Level 4), with follow-up at discharge, 90 days, 180 days (optional), and annually. Enrolment started in August 2026 across 12 initial sites, with a target of 12,750 patients being recruited by 2030.

PERSPECTIVE: Stroke-CORE represents a nationally harmonised cohort spanning prehospital care, acute treatment, rehabilitation, prevention, aftercare, and paediatric stroke. Its adaptive modular design allows continuous expansion with new modules, data streams, and biobanking initiatives without protocol revision. As a sustainable national research platform, Stroke-CORE aims to address key knowledge gaps, facilitate recruitment for clinical trials, and accelerate translational, clinical and outcomes research.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The protocol is registered at German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00039775, July 8th, 2026).

articles.title: Stroke care in Germany: evidence gaps and priorities for health services research and quality assurance.
authors: Commission Health Services Research and Quality Assurance of the German Stroke Society (“Deutsche Schlaganfall Gesellschaft, DSG”)
articles.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Germany and worldwide. Within this position paper by the Commission Health Services Research and Quality Assurance of the German Stroke Society, we summarize current data on stroke epidemiology, healthcare delivery, and quality assurance of stroke in Germany, identify evidence and knowledge gaps across the stroke care pathway, and derive priorities for future health services research and quality assurance. Based on registry and routine administrative data, approximately 253,000 incident and recurrent strokes were estimated to occur in Germany in 2023. Although age-standardized stroke mortality rates had declined substantially since the 1980s, this trend has reached a plateau since 2018. Acute care is predominantly administered in certified stroke units, characterized by high process and outcome quality. However, areas for improvement remain in post-acute care and in structured outpatient aftercare, particularly regarding appropriate care for patients with persistent functional impairments and unmet needs. Future research priorities include for example the utilization of real-world data to document long-term outcomes, the expansion of quality assurance to specific entities such as subarachnoid hemorrhage, and the evaluation of telemedical frameworks in pre-hospital settings. Systematic implementation of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) in research and clinical practice could facilitate the identification of unmet needs and the development of patient-centered care models. In light of recent legislative advancements (e.g., the Health Data Use Act, European Health Data Space) and technological innovations (e.g., AI-driven applications), new opportunities are emerging to bolster health services research and further optimize the management of stroke patients.

articles.title: A Precision-Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non-specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen (1O2) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light-controlled generation of 1O2. Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β-cells and primary islet β-cells and induces localized β-cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

articles.title: Strain and cell type dependent induction of tunnelling nanotube-like projections by African swine fever virus.
articles.abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a devastating viral disease of pigs, causing mortality rates of up to 100%. The causative agent, African swine fever virus (ASFV), preferentially targets cells of the mononuclear phagocytic system (MPS). Despite its severe economic and animal health impact, effective antiviral treatments remain unavailable in Europe. We previously showed that ASFV strain Belgium 2018/01 induces tunnelling nanotube (TNT)-like projections in monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), enabling physical connections between distant cells. Here, we investigated the broader relevance of this phenomenon across porcine myeloid cell populations and ASFV strains. We assessed TNT-like projection formation in monocytes, pulmonary alveolar macrophages (PAMs), splenic macrophages, polarized and non-polarized MDMs and Vero cells following ASFV infection. We further compared 20 ASFV strains representing diverse genotypes and virulence levels. Interestingly, luminal monocytes and PAMs did not develop ASFV-induced projections, whereas projection formation increased during monocyte differentiation into MDMs. Splenic macrophages also formed projections, suggesting that interstitial tissue macrophages acquire the ability to induce protrusions. Polarized MDMs exhibited reduced projection formation compared with non-polarized MDMs. Similar structures were induced in Ba71V-infected Vero cells, providing a standardized model for mechanistic studies. Importantly, all 20 ASFV strains induced TNT-like projections in MDMs, although the extent varied substantially and was independent of viral genotype or virulence. Our findings demonstrate that ASFV-induced TNT-like projection formation is a conserved, cell-state-dependent phenotype across diverse ASFV strains. These findings provide a foundation for identifying the cellular and viral determinants of TNT formation and defining its potential contribution to ASFV dissemination and pathogenesis.

articles.title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes.

RESULTS: We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Postreperfusion venovenous bypass for hemodynamic stabilization in liver transplantation with hepatic outflow obstruction: a case report.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic inferior vena cava (IVC) stenosis is an uncommon yet serious vascular complication that can significantly impact the success of liver transplantation. We report a case in which postreperfusion venovenous bypass (VVB) was used as a temporizing strategy to achieve hemodynamic stabilization in the setting of severe hepatic venous congestion caused by a fixed suprahepatic IVC obstruction.

CLINICAL FEATURES: A 58-yr-old male with a history of orthotopic liver transplantation complicated by recurrent IVC stenosis and end-stage kidney disease underwent a simultaneous liver and kidney transplant. Intraoperatively, dense fibrosis was encountered proximal to the suprahepatic IVC, preventing resection of the stenotic segment. Although the liver graft was successfully implanted and reperfused, severe hepatic congestion and refractory hemodynamic instability developed. Venovenous bypass was initiated to augment venous return and stabilize systemic hemodynamics. The kidney transplant was aborted owing to the patient's instability. Postoperatively, the patient initially tolerated the procedure, however, he ultimately died in the intensive care unit.

CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates an unconventional postreperfusion application of VVB as a rescue measure for refractory hemodynamic instability. Given the presence of a fixed suprahepatic IVC obstruction, VVB only provided temporary hemodynamic support and did not result in graft recovery. This underscores the physiologic limitations of VVB in the presence of irreversible mechanical outflow obstruction and highlights the importance of early recognition and surgical adaptability in anatomically complex cases.

articles.title: Quantified Brain Atrophy and Risk of Severe Mass Effect in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large middle cerebral artery (MCA) infarctions can result in life-threatening cerebral edema. Quantitative brain atrophy may improve risk stratification for severe edema. We examined whether quantitative brain atrophy is associated with severe midline shift after large ischemic stroke and whether incorporating atrophy improves prediction beyond established clinical and radiographic predictors.

METHODS: This was a retrospective observational cohort study of patients with greater than or equal to half MCA ischemic infarction, presentation within 24 h of last known well time, and at least one follow-up head computed tomography (CT), admitted to two academic hospitals with comprehensive stroke centers between 2006 and 2024. The study was approved by the institutional review boards of both centers. Brain atrophy was quantified as the inverse of standardized brain volume on admission head CT. The primary outcome was severe radiographic mass effect, defined as midline shift ≥ 5 mm on follow-up CT. The secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable regression models assessed associations between quantified atrophy and outcomes. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing models with and without atrophy using measures of goodness of fit, calibration, and discrimination.

RESULTS: Among 565 patients (mean age 67.5 ± 15.7 years; 49.9% female), 223 (39.5%) developed severe mass effect. Greater atrophy was associated with lower odds of midline shift ≥ 5 mm [odds ratio (OR) 0.44, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.58], but not with in-hospital mortality. Incorporation of atrophy improved prediction of severe mass effect compared with the baseline model [likelihood ratio test χ2 (1) = 41, p < 0.001; Akaike information criterion (AIC) 703 vs. 741; Bayesian information criterion (BIC) 733 vs. 767; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.68 vs. 0.60].

CONCLUSIONS: Quantified brain atrophy is independently associated with a reduced risk of severe mass effect after large MCA stroke and improved the performance of established predictive models. Incorporation of this imaging biomarker may enhance early risk stratification, monitoring, and intervention planning for patients at risk of life-threatening cerebral edema.

articles.title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory arrhythmia in a neonate carrying an SCN5A variant: a case report.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal malignant arrhythmias refractory to conventional antiarrhythmic therapy are life-threatening and pose a major therapeutic challenge, particularly in premature infants.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a premature infant born at 36 + 2 weeks of gestation who developed ventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest following resuscitation for perinatal asphyxia. As lidocaine and amiodarone failed to control the rhythm, veno‑arterial ECMO was initiated shortly thereafter. After ECMO support, the rhythm converted to sinus and cardiac function improved, allowing successful weaning. Electrocardiography subsequently revealed a prolonged QT interval, which responded to oral mexiletine. Whole‑exome sequencing identified a heterozygous SCN5A c.1960G > A (p.Glu654Lys) variant inherited from the father, classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS).

CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that this specific VUS may be a candidate pathogenic variant, and that early ECMO can be an effective salvage therapy when conventional drugs fail. Additionally, when genetic testing yields a VUS, the clinical phenotype and treatment response appear valuable for assessing pathogenicity in neonatal cases.

articles.title: Irrational antibiotic prescriptions in pediatric care across Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inappropriate antibiotic use, including deviations from guideline recommendations, incorrect dosages, and over-prescription, is a critical public health concern. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the prevalence and factors associated with inappropriate antibiotic use in pediatric populations across Africa.

METHOD: A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and African Journals Online, following PRISMA guidelines and the PICOC framework. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Meta-analysis was performed with STATA 17 using a random-effects model.

RESULT: From 3,085 records, 11 studies met inclusion. The pooled prevalence of inappropriate antibiotic use was 44%. Rates reached 75.1%, 73.9%, and 71.5% in some countries, while lower rates of 11% and 19.3% were reported elsewhere. Retrospective studies showed a pooled prevalence of 51.2% (I² = 99.5%), and prospective studies 35.4% (I² = 99%). Commonly prescribed antibiotics included cotrimoxazole, amoxicillin, and ceftriaxone. Inappropriate practices involved incorrect dosages (10.1%-19.5%) and durations (17.47-18.8%). Risk factors included younger age, three or more antibiotics (AOR: 2.8, 95% CI: 1.245-6.462, p = 0.013), and prolonged hospitalization.

CONCLUSION: Inappropriate pediatric antibiotic use in Africa is highly prevalent, driven by age, hospitalization, and polypharmacy, underscoring the need for targeted stewardship interventions.

IMPACT: This study is the first to bring together evidence across Africa showing that nearly half of antibiotics prescribed to children are used inappropriately. The findings call for stronger, targeted antibiotic stewardship efforts to improve prescribing practices and curb the growing threat of resistance in African healthcare settings.

articles.title: Association between baseline systemic immune-inflammation index and subsequent stroke in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is reportedly an effective predictor of poor outcomes in malignancies and inflammatory diseases. Therefore, this study investigated the association between baseline SII and subsequent stroke in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV).

METHODS: We selected 339 immunosuppressive drug-naïve patients newly diagnosed with AAV from an observational AAV cohort and retrospectively reviewed their medical records. The baseline Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS) was reviewed, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded. Baseline SII was calculated thus: SII = neutrophil count × platelet count/lymphocyte count. Subsequent stroke was defined as ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke that occurred after diagnosis.

RESULTS: The 339 AAV patients had a median age of 61.0 years; the majority were women. The median baseline BVAS and SII were 12.0 and 1229.9, respectively. Of the 339 patients, 20 (5.9%) experienced a subsequent stroke. Baseline SII was significantly correlated with ESR (r = 0.361) and CRP levels (r = 0.485). Baseline SII (standardised β 0.117) was independently correlated with BVAS, as seen on multivariable linear regression analysis. Baseline SII showed modest discrimination for subsequent stroke (AUC 0.662, 95% CI 0.532-0.793), and a cohort-derived cutoff of 2390.5 was identified. Patients with baseline SII ≥ 2390.5 and those in the upper half of baseline SII showed significantly lower cumulative stroke-free survival rates. However, baseline SII was not independently associated with subsequent stroke in the primary multivariable Cox analyses.

CONCLUSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate an association between baseline SII and subsequent stroke in patients with AAV. Further studies are required to establish its independent and incremental prognostic value. Key Points • Baseline SII was significantly correlated with cross-sectional BVAS, ESR, and CRP levels. • Individuals with baseline SII ≥ 2390.5 and those with the upper half of baseline SII showed significantly reduced cumulative stroke-free survival rates compared to those without. • Higher baseline SII was associated with subsequent stroke in patients with AAV; however, its independent and incremental prognostic value remains to be established.

articles.title: [Dapagliflozin reduces the incidence of acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery].
Selective blockade of microRNA-31-5p-calcitonin receptor interaction reverses established atrial fibrosis and atrial arrhythmia burden.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is promoted by atrial fibrosis, a form of structural remodelling for which effective therapies are lacking. MicroRNA-31-5p (miR-31-5p), an aging-associated, atrial-enriched microRNA, has been linked to AF, but its role in atrial fibrosis is unknown. Here we show that atrial fibroblasts from patients with persistent AF exhibit increased miR-31-5p expression and reduced expression of the calcitonin receptor (CTR, encoded by CALCR). MiR-31-5p directly represses CTR and promotes pro-fibrotic fibroblast responses, whereas its inhibition restores CTR expression. Fibroblast-specific overexpression of miR-31 in mice reduces atrial CTR expression, increases atrial fibrosis and enhances arrhythmia susceptibility. Selective disruption of miR-31-5p-CALCR binding using a locked nucleic acid target site blocker restores atrial CTR expression, prevents fibrosis progression and reduces arrhythmia burden. In mice with established atrial remodeling, this strategy promotes fibrosis regression, identifying the miR-31-5p-CTR axis as a potential therapeutic target in AF.

articles.title: Hypertension accelerates osteoarthritis.
Prognostic significance of ejection fraction derived from prospectively ECG-triggered coronary CT angiography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prospective electrocardiogram (ECG)-triggered coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography is widely used for noninvasive evaluation of coronary artery disease, with relatively low radiation exposure. However, its limited temporal sampling restricts comprehensive assessment of left ventricular (LV) systolic function. Therefore, novel functional parameters derived from restricted acquisition windows may provide additional prognostic information without increasing radiation dose.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic significance of LVEF120ms, a novel systolic functional parameter derived from LV volume change over a 120-ms systolic acquisition window.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 356 patients who underwent prospectively ECG-triggered coronary CT angiography between 2021 and 2023. We calculated LVEF120ms from three systolic phases using semi-automated volumetric analysis. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined the optimal cut-off value, and Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses were used to assess outcomes.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 36 months, 31 patients (8.7%) experienced MACE. Median LVEF120ms was significantly lower in patients with MACE (5.6% vs. 10.2%, p < 0.001). The optimal cut-off was 7.2% (area under the ROC curve [AUC]: 0.712). Patients with LVEF120ms ≤ 7.2% had significantly reduced MACE-free survival (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, LVEF120ms ≤ 7.2% remained an independent predictor of MACE (hazard ratio [HR]: 3.42; p = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: The parameter LVEF120ms derived from prospectively ECG-triggered cardiac CT independently predicts adverse cardiovascular events and may improve risk stratification without additional radiation.

articles.title: Identification of fluid endocannabinoid and sphingolipid biomarkers in schizophrenia. A machine learning approach toward clinical value.
articles.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) diagnosis relies on subjective clinical evaluation, with symptoms often overlapping between psychiatric conditions, hindering early intervention, and creating an urgent need for objective, accessible biomarkers. Lipids, especially endocannabinoid system (ECS) and sphingolipid metabolism members, are promising candidates given their implication in SCZ pathogenesis and measurability in accessible biofluids, with minimally invasive procedures. Our study conducted the first comprehensive crossover of endocannabinoids (eCBs) and sphingolipids in matched cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum samples from antipsychotic-naïve SCZ patients (SCZnaïve, n = 49), antipsychotic-treated patients (SCZtreat, n = 56), and healthy volunteers (HVs, n = 51). The machine learning Integrated Disease Explanation and Risk Scoring (IDEARS) platform was applied to eCBs, N-acylethanolamines, ceramides, and sphingomyelins quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, identifying key discriminatory features across biofluids and conditions (CSF AUC: SCZnaïve = 0.87, SCZtreat = 0.94; serum AUC: SCZnaïve = 0.87, SCZtreat = 0.90). Anandamide emerged as the top CSF feature in SCZnaïve patients, showing significantly elevated levels (q = 0.010) compared to HVs. Notably, though not statistically significant under conventional statistics, IDEARS identified anandamide as a top ten serum feature. Additionally, elevated sphingadiene backbone (d18:2) sphingolipids were conserved between the CSF and serum of SCZnaïve (q < 0.05), highlighting their potential as peripheral surrogate markers.
