Treatment-specific ceramide patterns were also evident, with elevated C16-C18 and reduced long-chain (>C24) species potentially reflecting antipsychotic metabolic effects. Our results support the involvement of the ECS and sphingolipid imbalances in SCZ, highlighting the potential of machine learning for novel biomarker discovery, including stratification across biofluids, and therapeutic monitoring toward more objective psychiatric care.

articles.title: Pancreatic β-cell mitogenic regeneration in type 1 diabetes: A preclinical review.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is caused by autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells, resulting in hyperglycaemia. The first-line treatment for symptomatic T1D is exogenous insulin replacement to maintain glycaemic control. Islet transplant therapy is available to a small number of individuals, and stem cell-derived islet transplant therapies are in clinical development. Recent advances in immunotherapy for T1D enable β-cells to be protected from autoimmune destruction, delaying disease progression. Set against this therapeutic landscape, innate pancreatic β-cell regeneration strategies have the potential to reverse β-cell loss in T1D, restoring regulated, endogenous insulin secretion and stable glycaemic control. In this review, we evaluate the preclinical literature investigating β-cell regeneration strategies via proliferation of residual β-cells. We cover therapeutic goals for a potential regenerative therapy, drawing on lessons from studies of residual β-cell function, immunotherapy and islet transplantation in T1D. We review the role of 14 distinct targets/mechanisms with in vitro and/or in vivo data supporting their role in β-cell proliferation and potential for therapeutic regeneration. In particular, we focus on the role of DYRK1A in β-cell proliferation, evaluating the range of small molecule inhibitors and in vivo studies underpinning this well-validated target. We provide perspectives on how future clinical translation could be optimised, including improved drug development, considerations for clinical trial metrics, patient stratification and the potential for combinatorial regenerative and immunotherapy approaches to shield nascent regenerating β-cells.

articles.title: A Cross-Sectional Study Exploring the Nature, Contributing Factors and Consequences of Violence Against Nurses in Emergency Departments.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore the nature, contributing factors, and consequences of violence against emergency department nurses by patients and visitors in tertiary hospitals in a major city in China.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional descriptive study.

METHODS: Data were collected between December 2023 and February 2024 using a translated and adapted questionnaire examining the prevalence, forms, contributing factors, and consequences of violence. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 336 emergency nurses were included, of whom 66.7% reported violence exposure within the past year. Visitor-perpetrated violence was reported more frequently than patient-perpetrated violence. Psychological violence was more common than physical violence and most frequently involved verbal abuse, disruptive speech, and blame. Illness-related impairment was prominent in patient-perpetrated physical violence, whereas alcohol impairment was frequently reported in visitor-perpetrated violence. Dissatisfaction with medical staff outside the emergency department and delayed or inadequate security responses were also commonly reported as contributing factors. Among the variables included in the exploratory regression model (n = 298), uncertainty or absence of workplace violence policies was the only factor significantly associated with reported lifetime violence exposure. Peer support was more commonly reported than managerial assistance following incidents, and visitor-perpetrated incidents generally received higher short-term impact ratings, including impacts on work motivation and personal and psychological well-being.

CONCLUSION: Violence against emergency department nurses was common, with visitors reported more frequently as perpetrators than patients. Patient- and visitor-perpetrated violence showed different patterns, particularly in the circumstances surrounding incidents and in short-term impact ratings. The findings support differentiated prevention and response strategies, together with clearer workplace violence policies, timely security responses, and structured post-incident organisational support.

IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: Emergency nursing education and organisational responses should distinguish between patient violence associated with illness-related impairment and visitor violence occurring in contexts such as alcohol impairment, dissatisfaction, or unmet expectations. De-escalation for patient-perpetrated violence should consider the patient's clinical condition, whereas visitor-related incidents may require expectation-focused communication, behavioural boundaries, and timely security involvement. Structured post-incident support should form part of the organisational response to both types of violence.

REPORTING METHOD: This study adhered to the STROBE reporting guidelines.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: There was no patient or public involvement in the design, conduct, or reporting of this study.

IMPACT: WHAT PROBLEM DID THE STUDY ADDRESS?: Violence against emergency nurses is a persistent global problem, yet limited evidence has examined patient- and visitor-perpetrated violence separately in Chinese emergency care settings. WHAT WERE THE MAIN FINDINGS?: Visitor-perpetrated violence was reported more frequently than patient-perpetrated violence and generally received higher short-term impact ratings. Illness-related impairment was prominent in patient-perpetrated physical violence, whereas alcohol impairment was frequently reported in visitor-perpetrated violence. Among the variables examined in the exploratory regression, uncertainty or absence of workplace violence policies was associated with reported lifetime violence exposure. WHERE AND ON WHOM WILL THE RESEARCH HAVE AN IMPACT?: The findings may inform nursing educators, hospital administrators, and policymakers developing differentiated prevention, visitor management, and organisational response strategies for emergency nurses.

articles.title: Pediatric Recurrent Croup: An International Delphi Consensus Statement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent croup lacks a consistent diagnostic definition, resulting in substantial variation in investigation and management. We aimed to develop international consensus-based recommendations for the evaluation and management of pediatric recurrent croup.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE searched from 1st January 2000 to 15th August 2026, with results reported in accordance with PRISMA guidelines.

REVIEW METHODS: An international modified Delphi consensus process was conducted. Panelists rated statements using a 9-point Likert scale across two rounds. Strong consensus was defined as a mean ≥ 8.00 with no outliers; consensus as mean ≥ 7.00 with no more than one outlier.

RESULTS: Review of 28 studies confirmed substantial heterogeneity in the definition and investigation of recurrent croup, with most studies at moderate to high risk of bias. Strong consensus was achieved on prioritizing direct laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy in atypical presentations, including subglottic sizing and exclusion of a laryngeal cleft, and limiting allergy testing to children with clinical suspicion of atopic disease. Consensus supported shared otolaryngology-respiratory management, avoidance of routine imaging, and reserving advanced reflux investigation for refractory cases. No consensus was reached on empirical inhaled corticosteroids or antireflux therapy.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first international multidisciplinary consensus guidance for the evaluation and management of recurrent croup, supported by a proposed risk-stratified management algorithm. Agreement on core diagnostic and endoscopic priorities may help standardize clinical practice, while the absence of consensus on optimal medical management identifies clear priorities for future research in a field where high-quality prospective data remain lacking.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

articles.title: Three-year real-world effectiveness of dupilumab in eosinophilic CRSwNP across upper and lower airways.
articles.journal: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term real-world data on dupilumab in refractory eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) are limited, particularly regarding concurrent upper- and lower-airway control, inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) withdrawal in comorbid asthma, and olfactory recovery.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 104 patients with refractory CRSwNP who continued dupilumab for >3 years. Outcomes were evaluated at baseline, 3 months, and years 1-3. In patients with comorbid asthma, ICS exposure was quantified as the daily budesonide-equivalent dose and categorized according to a GINA-based inhaled maintenance step excluding biologics. Maintenance ICS withdrawal was defined as operational clinical remission with withdrawal of maintenance ICS-containing therapy. Predictors of persistent olfactory dysfunction were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses.

RESULTS: Upper airway outcomes, including nasal polyp score, CT score, and olfactory function, improved within 3 months and were maintained over 3 years. In patients with comorbid asthma, mean budesonide-equivalent ICS dose decreased from 625.1 to 241.6 μg/day at year 3, with step-down of inhaled maintenance therapy and increased maintenance ICS withdrawal. Persistent olfactory dysfunction occurred in 21.2% and was associated with age and disease duration (cut-offs 47.5 and 7.5 years), with an increased risk in the high-risk group (OR 6.2).

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term dupilumab provided sustained benefits across both the upper and lower airways and enabled progressive, ICS-sparing de-escalation of background asthma therapy, including maintenance ICS withdrawal. These findings suggest a shift toward remission off conventional therapy. Age and disease duration may enable risk stratification for persistent olfactory dysfunction and inform personalized management.

articles.title: Activities of daily living and health status benefits of semaglutide in very old patients with heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and obesity: Real-world practice study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in patients with heart failure has not been widely described. We aimed to analyze the efficacy of once-weekly semaglutide in very old patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure in terms of activities of daily living performance and health status.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This real-world observational study included patients ≥80 years with heart failure, diabetes, and obesity treated with semaglutide (Sema-Old Group) and patients not treated with glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (Control-Old Group). The co-primary outcomes were improvement in activities of daily living performance (measured using the Barthel Index) and health status (measured using the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire) at 24 months.

RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 232 patients were included in each group. The use of once-weekly semaglutide was associated with greater improvement in activities of daily living performance and health status in the Sema-Old Group compared to the Control-Old Group (Odds Ratio: 4.03; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.82-7.31; p<.01; Odds Ratio: 4.65; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.92-7.71; p<.01; respectively). There were also reductions in heart failure and all-cause hospitalizations, and cardiovascular death. Semaglutide use was associated with improved glycemic control and reduced body weight. Negative correlations were observed between activities of daily living performance and heart failure health status with the body weight and NT-proBNP levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Once-weekly semaglutide use was associated with improvements in activities of daily living performance and heart failure health status in very old patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure.

articles.title: Prognostic value of the sPESI score in critically ill patients with severe pulmonary embolism admitted to the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intermediate-high- and high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. However, uncertainty remains regarding the usefulness of prognostic scores for identifying patients at risk of progression to more severe forms of PE. This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with intermediate-high- and high-risk PE admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) and to explore the association between baseline simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (sPESI) and subsequent progression to high-risk PE among patients initially classified as intermediate-high risk.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of the University Hospital of Salamanca between 2021 and 2022 with a diagnosis of intermediate-high or high-risk PE. Clinical variables, prognostic scores, biomarkers, treatment strategies, and mortality were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 64 patients were included; 57 (89.1%) were initially classified as intermediate-high risk and 7 (10.9%) as high risk. Among the 57 patients initially classified as intermediate-high risk, 4 (7.0%) subsequently progressed to high-risk PE. Patients who progressed had higher baseline sPESI scores than those who remained haemodynamically stable (3.5 [IQR: 2.5-4.2] vs 2.0 [IQR: 1.0-2.0]; P=.029). In exploratory Firth penalised logistic regression, a higher baseline sPESI score was associated with progression to high-risk PE (OR per 1-point increase: 2.75; 95%CI: 1.23-8.44; P=.012). In-hospital mortality was 7.8%.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with PE initially classified as intermediate-high risk, a higher baseline sPESI score was associated with subsequent progression to high-risk PE.

A novel 1-minute clamping bean test (CBT1) for screening covert hepatic encephalopathy: feasibility and diagnostic performance.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE) is frequently under-recognized in clinical practice. This study evaluated a novel 1-minute Clamping Bean Test (CBT1) for CHE screening.

METHODS: In this two-center study conducted from September 2023 to September 2026, participants underwent both the Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) and CBT1. Cirrhotic patients were followed for 1 year.

RESULTS: In total, 336 healthy individuals and 130 cirrhotic patients were enrolled. In healthy individuals, CBT1 was independent of sex and declined with age, particularly beyond 50 years, and to a lesser extent with education. In cirrhotic patients, CBT1 was significantly lower in those with than without CHE (21.3 ± 5.4 vs. 27.8 ± 5.4 beans, P < 0.001). With a cut-off of 24.5, CBT1 achieved an AUC of 0.799 (95% CI: 0.724-0.873), with a sensitivity 74.0%, specificity71.7%, and accuracy 73.1%. CBT1 correlated significantly with all five PHES subtests (all P < 0.001). In a subgroup of 8 patients, CBT1 improved significantly after 10 days of lactulose therapy (median 14.5 to 17 beans, P = 0.008). Over 1-year follow-up, CBT1 positivity was associated with mortality (P = 0.024) and hospital readmission (P = 0.046).

CONCLUSIONS: CBT1 showed diagnostic accuracy comparable to PHES, with additional advantages of being time-saving and home-applicable. By translating a fundamental daily motor skill into a quantifiable biomarker, CBT1 is a promising screening tool for CHE.

articles.title: Estimated pulse wave velocity and 20-year cumulative incidence of type 2 diabetes: The ATTICA cohort study (2002-2022).
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV), a composite marker derived from age and mean blood pressure, reflects integrated vascular ageing and haemodynamic load. This study aimed to investigate the association between baseline ePWV and the 20-year cumulative incidence of type 2 diabetes (T2D) in a population-based cohort of initially healthy adults.

METHODS: A total of 2000 adults from the ATTICA cohort (2002-2022), free of cardiovascular disease and T2D at baseline, were included and followed-up for 20-years (2002-2022). Incidence of T2D was the outcome of interest; ePWV was derived using a validated equation based on age and mean blood pressure.

RESULTS: Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with 22% higher odds of T2D over 20 years (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.03-1.44; p = 0.017). In sex-stratified analyses, the association was significant in men (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.01-1.60), although no significant interaction with sex was observed (p for interaction = 0.453). A significant interaction was observed between ePWV and physical activity trajectories (p for interaction < 0.001); no significant association was observed among consistently active participants (OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.83-1.24). No significant interactions were observed for smoking (p for interaction = 0.752), various food groups, or MedDietScore (all remaining p for interaction > 0.500).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline ePWV was associated with increased odds of T2D over 20-year observation. Exploratory analyses suggested potential effect modification by physical activity trajectories; however, these findings require independent confirmation.

articles.title: Role of 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose PET Combined with Computed Tomography in Sarcoidosis: A Clinical Review.
articles.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disorder characterized by non-caseating granulomas and a highly variable clinical course. Diagnosis relies on compatible clinical and radiologic findings, histologic evidence of non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation when appropriate, along with exclusion of alternate causes. While chest radiography and high-resolution computed tomography (CT) remain essential for structural evaluation, they cannot reliably differentiate active inflammation from fibrosis. 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose PET combined with CT enables whole-body assessment of inflammatory activity, detection of occult disease, biopsy guidance, and monitoring of selected patients. Its greatest value is in cardiac sarcoidosis, although limited specificity and lack of standardized response criteria remain important challenges.

articles.title: 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose PET Combined with Computed Tomography in Musculoskeletal and Spine Infections.
articles.abstract: 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose PET combined with computed tomography (18F-FDG-PET/CT) is an established, whole-body technique for musculoskeletal/spinal infections. Its high sensitivity, tomographic localization and relatively preserved interpretability in patients with metallic-implants make it especially useful in chronic/low-grade osteomyelitis, the instrumented/postoperative spine, and spondylodiscitis. Activated neutrophils, macrophages, and lymphocytes at sites of infection upregulate glucose-transporters and hexokinase, driving increased radiotracer uptake, independent of bone turnover and largely unaffected by metallic-hardware. Whole-body coverage detects synchronous foci in septic prosthetic-joint infection and maps multilevel/disseminated tuberculous spondylitis in endemic-regions such as India, guiding biopsy and enabling objective, serial treatment response monitoring. Its chief limitation is limited specificity.

articles.title: Role of FDG PET in Fungal Infections.
articles.abstract: Fungal infections are increasingly common in immunocompromised, diabetic, critically ill, transplant, and patients with cancer, where they contribute to substantial morbidity and mortality. Diagnosis is often difficult because symptoms are nonspecific, microbiological tests may be delayed or negative, and tissue sampling is not always feasible. While computed tomography (CT), MR imaging, and ultrasonography are essential, they may underestimate disease extent or fail to distinguish active infection from residual changes. F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT offers whole-body metabolic assessment, enabling detection of occult lesions, evaluation of disease burden, biopsy guidance, treatment monitoring, and identification of recurrence.

articles.title: Personal nighttime indoor temperature and sleep characteristics in adults with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine whether personal nighttime indoor temperature is associated with actigraphy-derived sleep outcomes among community-dwelling adults with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: We analyzed repeated-night data from 108 adults with type 2 diabetes, contributing 1307 paired sleep-temperature nights. Personal nighttime indoor temperature was measured with temperature loggers and averaged across each participant-specific nocturnal sleep episode. Sleep outcomes included sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, total sleep time, and number of awakenings. Linear mixed-effects models examined within-person and between-person temperature-sleep associations. Generalized additive mixed models evaluated nonlinearity. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic, clinical, and seasonal covariates.

RESULTS: Personal nighttime indoor temperature and sleep outcomes varied across nights, with both showing seasonal patterns. In adjusted linear mixed-effects models, warmer-than-usual nights were associated with higher sleep efficiency and fewer awakenings, whereas between-person average temperature was not associated with any sleep outcomes. Generalized additive mixed models showed nonlinear associations with sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, and awakenings, but not total sleep time. Model-predicted sleep outcomes remained largely unchanged across moderate nighttime indoor temperatures. Above approximately 27 °C [80.6 °F], the fitted curves suggested higher sleep efficiency, lower wake after sleep onset, and fewer awakenings; however, observations in this upper range were sparse, and sensitivity analyses excluding these observations attenuated the nonlinear patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes, personal nighttime indoor temperature was associated with actigraphy-derived sleep outcomes in a within-person, nonlinear, and outcome-specific manner. Findings suggest that nighttime indoor temperature may be relevant to sleep health promotion and diabetes-related sleep counseling, particularly for adults reporting poor sleep or limited control over indoor temperature.

articles.title: Mesoporous Silica Nanoplatforms: From Controllable Synthesis to Versatile Biomedical Applications.
articles.abstract: The increasing global burden of severe diseases, such as cancers, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disorders, highlights the urgent need for advanced diagnostic and therapeutic agents. Although techniques like computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and chemotherapy show promise, their effectiveness is frequently constrained by the inherent drawbacks of conventional agents, such as poor solubility, low stability, and lack of targeting ability, as well as physiological barriers like the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which limit bioavailability and induce systemic toxicity. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) have emerged as promising platforms to overcome these challenges, offering high surface area, tunable pore size, and facile surface functionalization for efficient cargo loading. Therefore, in this work, the recent advances in the synthesis, structural control, and functional design of MSNs-based composites are systematically reviewed, with a focus on their biomedical applications in diagnosis (e.g., fluorescence imaging (FLI)/MRI/PET), therapy (e.g., chemo-, dynamic, thermal, and gas therapy), and tissue engineering. Key strategies for performance optimization and structure-property relationships are discussed in depth. Finally, we delineate prevailing challenges and future directions for the clinical translation of MSNs-based nanomaterials, providing an integrated perspective to guide their rational design and biomedical implementation.

articles.title: DNA Immunotherapy (INO-3107) Long-Term Efficacy Supported by Enhanced Immunogenicity in HPV-6/11 RRP.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), caused by chronic HPV-6/11 infection, leads to repeated papilloma growth requiring frequent surgical removal. DNA immunotherapy INO-3107 aims to induce HPV antigen-specific T-cell responses and reduce surgical burden. This analysis evaluated HPV-specific immune responses after INO-3107 and their association with long-term clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Adults with HPV-6/11-associated RRP received INO-3107 in a Phase 1/2 trial and were followed for one year, with additional clinical follow-up in a long-term extension. Number of surgeries in Years 1 and 2 was compared with the pre-treatment year. Blood and laryngotracheal tissue collected at Day 0 and Year 1 were analyzed for treatment-related changes in T-cell activity. Safety was assessed throughout.

RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were treated; 28 continued into Year 2. At Year 1, most evaluable patients showed increased T-cell activity: 73% (19/26) demonstrated persistent expanded T-cell populations in blood, 71% (12/17) showed higher T-cell clone counts in laryngotracheal tissue, indicating site-specific immune infiltration. Antiviral T-cell signatures were enriched in 88% for CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ cytotoxic, and 71% for CD8+ effector memory, suggesting durable proinflammatory and memory responses in airway tissue. Mean annual surgeries decreased over time in the overall population (Baseline: 4.1, Year 1: 1.7, Year 2: 0.9). Similar durable reductions were observed in Responder subgroups. INO-3107 was well-tolerated, with no treatment-related serious adverse events.

CONCLUSION: INO-3107 generates increased HPV-directed T-cell responses and substantially reduced surgical procedures over two years, supporting its ability to provide long-term clinical benefit in RRP without requiring additional surgeries during the dosing window.

articles.title: Defining the Components of a Nurse Practitioner-Led Home Visit Intervention for Frail Patients: An International Delphi Consensus Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Aging in place has become a central objective of health and social policies across the world, yet frailty and multimorbidity undermine individuals' capacity to remain safely at home. The aim was to identify the components of a home visit intervention led by nurse practitioners for frail populations.

DESIGN: A consensus study using a two-round Delphi method.

METHODS: A two-round Delphi study was conducted in 2024 with 15 experts from four French-speaking countries (Quebec-Canada, Switzerland, Belgium, and France). Experts included healthcare professionals with expertise in home care, rural healthcare services, or access to care for frail populations. The questionnaires were based on documented needs of frail patients and their caregivers.

RESULTS: Experts identified the target population as older adults needing home care, people with physical or cognitive impairments, those requiring end-of-life care, and individuals experiencing difficulties remaining at home. Eligibility criteria included frailty, multiple chronic conditions, mobility issues, social isolation, and low socio-economic status. The nurse practitioner's role should include clinical assessment, treatment adjustments, care coordination, therapeutic education, support for patients and families, and promotion of self-care. Nurse practitioners may serve as a reference for healthcare professionals. Home visits should be initiated by healthcare providers, patients, or family members, with visit frequency and duration adapted to individual needs.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified components of a nurse practitioner-led home visit intervention for frail individuals that achieved expert consensus, while highlighting areas where consensus was not reached.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings will inform the development and evaluation of such an intervention.

articles.title: CT density gradient texture is associated with blood gene expression and immune cell subtypes in smokers susceptible to COPD.
Performance-Metacognition Dissociation During Fear Memory Recall: Role of Task Sequence and Prefrontal TMS.
articles.abstract: Metacognitive processing-the ability to monitor and evaluate one's decisions-has been extensively studied in perceptual tasks but never examined in fear conditioning. We investigated whether metacognitive sensitivity can be quantified in emotional learning and how testing order and neuromodulation of the anterior prefrontal cortex (aPFC) influence metacognitive access to the memory of a shock-associated cue. Eighty-one participants (51 females and 30 males) underwent fear conditioning and received either active or sham TMS over the aPFC. They were tested with implicit (skin conductance) and explicit (two-interval forced-choice with confidence ratings) tasks in counterbalanced order. Behavioral performance (d') and metacognitive sensitivity (meta-d') were quantified using signal detection theory. While d' remained stable across conditions, meta-d' and confidence were significantly higher when the explicit task preceded the implicit task. TMS did not affect metacognitive sensitivity. To our knowledge, these results provide the first evidence that metacognitive frameworks can be applied to a fear-conditioning paradigm, revealing that confidence judgments are dynamically modulated by task sequence and remain intact even when bodily arousal is reduced. We propose that metacognitive sensitivity may decline faster than first-order performance, pointing to a functional dissociation between decision accuracy and metacognition in emotionally salient contexts.Significance Statement This study provides the first evidence that metacognitive monitoring can be quantified within a fear-conditioning paradigm, extending metacognitive research beyond perceptual decision-making into emotional learning. We show that confidence in recognizing a shock-associated cue can be dissociated from first-order performance: task sequence critically modulates metacognitive sensitivity even when first-order performance remains stable. Notably, confidence judgments persist despite reduced autonomic arousal following prefrontal stimulation, suggesting that metacognitive access does not require intact bodily signals. These findings indicate that fear conditioning offers a viable paradigm for investigating metacognition and suggest a partial dissociation between first-order performance and self-monitoring in emotional memory. This work opens new avenues for understanding confidence disruptions in anxiety disorders in which threat detection and metacognitive evaluation are impaired.

Implementation and use of EHR-integrated large language model-generated draft responses in patient portal messaging: a 1-year prospective observational study in a tertiary hospital.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the implementation and use of electronic health record (EHR)-integrated large language model (LLM)-generated draft responses in patient portal messaging, including adoption over time, draft reuse and associations with message handling time.

DESIGN: One-year prospective observational study using in-system EHR log data, complemented by a post-implementation clinician survey.

SETTING: A tertiary academic hospital in the Netherlands.

PARTICIPANTS: Patient portal messages with clinician replies during the study period (March 2024–March 2025; n=10 786). A voluntary clinician survey was completed by 241 respondents.

INTERVENTIONS: An EHR-integrated LLM automatically generated draft replies for incoming patient portal messages. Clinicians could use, edit or discard drafts as part of routine clinical workflow.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were adoption of draft replies, textual similarity between drafts and final replies (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE-1) and Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) scores), relative word-count change and message handling time metrics (read-to-action time, draft time and total completion time). Secondary outcomes included temporal trends in adoption, variation across clinical departments and clinician-reported experiences.

RESULTS: Draft replies were initiated in 42% of patient messages. Among drafted replies, 52% met the predefined substantial-retention threshold (BLEU ≥10). Messages with higher draft retention (BLEU ≥10) were associated with shorter median draft time (70 s (IQR 37–124)) and total handling time (140 s (IQR 81–232)) compared with messages with no draft initiation (86 s (IQR 47–154) and 155 s (IQR 87–258), respectively) or minimal draft retention (99 s (IQR 53–174) and 175 s (IQR 103–285)). Adoption declined over time to approximately 35–40% and varied across departments, with higher use in orthopaedics, otolaryngology and neurology and lower use in oncology, rheumatology and gastroenterology. Survey responses indicated mixed perceptions, with commonly reported benefits including a structured starting point and frequently cited limitations related to tone and contextual relevance.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: EHR-integrated LLM-generated draft responses showed moderate and variable uptake and were reused to differing extents across messages and specialties. Meaningful draft reuse was associated with shorter message handling times, although adoption declined over time. These findings highlight the importance of workflow integration, specialty-specific fit and ongoing evaluation when implementing generative artificial intelligence tools in clinical communication.

Endovascular Thrombectomy for Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke in Patients with Metastatic Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke is supported by high-quality evidence, but the safety and efficacy of EVT for patients with concomitant metastatic cancer is unclear. We aimed to compare outcomes of EVT versus best medical management (BMM) for LVO stroke patients with metastatic cancer.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study of the 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database includes adult patients with LVO stroke (internal carotid, middle cerebral, or basilar artery occlusion) and metastatic cancer. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using 1-to-1 nearest-neighbor matching. The primary outcome was early functional independence at hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes included discharge to home, hospital length of stay, in-hospital mortality, and 180-day mortality. Outcomes were compared between those treated with EVT or BMM, and treatment effects are reported as risk differences (RD), risk ratios (RR), or hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Of 5629 patients, 3590 remained after PSM (1833 EVT, 1757 BMM). Compared to BMM, EVT was associated with significantly higher rates of early functional independence (17.8% vs 8.7%; RD 9.1% [95%CI 5.1 to 13.1], RR 2.04 [95%CI 1.51-2.76]) and discharge to home (42.3% vs 34.1%; RD 8.2% [95%CI 3.2 to 13.2], RR 1.24 [95%CI 1.09-1.42]), with no difference in hospital length of stay (median 7 vs 6 days; P=0.34), in-hospital mortality (22.8% vs 24.3%; RD -1.5% [95%CI -5.6 to 2.6]), or 180-day mortality (30.3% vs 30.0%; HR 0.99 [95%CI 0.83-1.18]). Among patients who suffered in-hospital mortality (n=845), there was no significant difference in length of stay (median 5 vs 4 days, p=0.52). Among patients who survived the index hospitalization but later died within 180 days (N=185), EVT was associated with higher rates of interim functional independence (26.8% vs 12.7%; RR 2.11 [95%CI 1.02-4.37]).

CONCLUSIONS: Among LVO stroke patients with metastatic cancer, EVT was associated with significantly higher rates of functional independence compared to BMM, without altering overall survival.

Development and external validation of a preprocedural prediction model for 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established treatment for severe aortic stenosis but not recommended for patients with a life-expectancy below 1 year. Nevertheless, 1 year mortality after TAVI is around 15% in current reports. Accurate prediction models are thus needed to prevent futile interventions.

METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI were prospectively recruited between 2008 and 2021 from a single-centre registry in Zurich, Switzerland and data split into derivation and validation datasets. Four expert cardiologists defined relevant candidate predictors. A prediction model was developed using multiple logistic regression after imputation of missing data. An independent cohort undergoing TAVI from 2008 to 2018 in London, UK served as an external validation dataset. Performance of the prediction model was assessed through internal and external validation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calibration plots were used for discrimination and calibration.

RESULTS: A total of 1702 patients were included from the Swiss cohort. Among these 1278 were used for model development and 424 for validation. 12 predictors were incorporated including age, male sex, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, haemoglobin, creatinine, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, troponin, left ventricular ejection fraction, mean transaortic pressure gradient and severe mitral regurgitation. The prediction model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.72 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.81) in internal validation and showed optimal sensitivity and specificity for 1-year mortality prediction at a probability threshold of 20%, outperforming European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II and Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) score. In the external validation dataset consisting of 851 patients from the UK cohort, the AUC was 0.64 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.70).

CONCLUSION: The TAVI-specific risk model demonstrated acceptable performance for prediction of 1-year mortality after TAVI across two contemporary real-world cohorts, highlighting its potential for clinical application instead of EuroSCORE II or STS-PROM.

articles.title: Assessing vasculitis in Takayasu arteritis by ultrasound: results of OMERACT patient-based reliability exercises.
authors: Large-Vessel Vasculitis-Ultrasound Subgroup of the OMERACT Ultrasound Working Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the inter-rater and intrarater reliability of consensus-based definitions of elementary ultrasound lesions in Takayasu arteritis (TAK) in live patient-based reliability exercises.

METHODS: Two live exercises with two rounds each were conducted, each involving 12 vascular sonographers who independently examined five patients with TAK and one control subject. Bilateral common carotid, subclavian and axillary arteries and the abdominal aorta were investigated to identify key elementary ultrasound lesions in TAK: ‘macaroni sign’, stenosis and occlusion. Inter-rater and intrarater reliability were calculated using Fleiss’ and Cohen’s kappa (κ), respectively.

RESULTS: Overall, inter-rater reliability across the two rounds of both exercises was moderate to good for the ‘macaroni sign’ (κ 0.51-0.74 across the two rounds of both exercises), fair for stenosis (0.24–0.38) and variable for occlusion (0.02–0.60). Intrarater reliability across the two exercises was good to excellent for the ‘macaroni sign’ (0.74–0.81) and moderate for stenosis (0.55–0.64) and occlusion (0.64–1.00; the latter based on a limited number of assessments). In both exercises, inter-rater reliability was good to excellent for the ‘macaroni sign’ in carotids but worse across other vessels and lesion types; intrarater reliability was good to excellent when analysed per single vessel and lesion though limited for occlusions and for the abdominal aorta.

CONCLUSION: Among the ultrasound elementary lesions for TAK, the ‘macaroni sign’ revealed moderate to good reliability, while the reproducibility of stenosis and occlusion was worse and more variable. These results provide the methodological basis to develop a new global Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT) ultrasound score in TAK.

articles.title: The impact of cumulative lipoprotein(a) exposure on stroke recurrence: a population-based prospective study.
Study on the protective mechanism of Astragaloside IV by regulating the NETs pathway against ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ischemic stroke (IS) triggers systemic inflammatory immune response, increasing blood neutrophil count. Inflammatory factors from ischemic area recruit neutrophils to form neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), worsening injury. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) exhibits proven neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia, potentially through suppressing NETs. This study examines how AS-IV prevents cerebral ischemic injury by blocking NETs formation (NETosis).

METHODS: The Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced mouse bone marrow-derived neutrophils (BMNs) injury model was built to evaluate AS-IV's impact on NETosis, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and marker proteins via scanning electron microscopy, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence techniques. AS-IV's protective action against NETs-damaged HT22 cells was elucidated via untargeted metabolomics. Targeted metabolomics for differential metabolites was carried out on a ultra-high performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometry. AS-IV's impact on neurological features, regional cerebral blood flow (CBF), and inflammatory infiltrates in transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) was evaluated by behavioral assessment, laser speckle contrast imaging, histological sectioning. Combined with peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibitor Cl-amidine, NETs-associated proteins in cerebral tissue were detected by western blot (WB) and immunohistochemistry (IHC), and serum MPO-DNA and NE-DNA levels were tested using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to further elucidate AS-IV's mechanism against ischemic brain injury.

RESULT: AS-IV dose-dependently inhibited NETs formation in PMA-induced mouse BMNs by reducing ROS levels and alleviating NETs-damaged HT22 cells. AS-IV reversed metabolic disorders in NETs-induced HT22 cells. Of the 14 differential metabolites detected, purine metabolism represented the predominantly altered metabolic pathway. Our in vivo data demonstrate that AS-IV improves neurological function, rescues impaired regional cerebral perfusion, and mitigates inflammatory cell infiltration. Mechanistically, these neuroprotective outcomes are largely attributed to the inhibition of PAD4-mediated NETosis..

CONCLUSION: AS-IV protects against ischemic brain injury by inhibiting PAD4-mediated NETosis.

articles.title: Atrial Leadless Pacemaker Implantation at the Superior Right Atrial Site.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right atrial appendage (RAA) pacing may produce nonphysiological atrial activation.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and electrocardiographic characteristics of atrial leadless pacemaker implantation at the superior right atrium (RA).

METHODS: Sixty-eight consecutive patients undergoing dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation were studied. Procedural, device, electrocardiographic, and clinical outcomes were compared between superior RA and RAA base pacing.

RESULTS: Superior RA implantation succeeded in 26/46 attempts (56.5%), increasing from 27.8% to 60.0% and 92.3% across sequential periods. In noncrossover cases, procedure (72.7±16.4 vs 76.8±27.2 minutes; P=0.533) and fluoroscopy times (15.4±5.8 vs 18.6±11.9 minutes; P=0.249) were comparable. P-wave duration remained unchanged with superior RA pacing (99.7±29.9 to 98.1±25.6 ms; P=0.543) but increased with RAA pacing (106.7±23.1 to 134.9±25.6 ms; P<0.001); P-wave terminal force in V1 changed from 3.6% to 3.6% versus 10.0% to 45.0%, respectively (P<0.001 for RAA). PR intervals increased from 228.4±72.8 to 229.7±77.5 ms (P=0.038) and from 205.5±72.0 to 234.4±72.6 ms (P<0.001), respectively; the increase was smaller with superior RA pacing (+5.7±11.7 vs +38.6±31.3 ms; P<0.001). At 3 months, sensing amplitudes (3.4±1.5 vs 2.4±1.1 mV; P=0.091) and pacing thresholds (0.8±0.5 vs 0.8±0.3 V; P=0.785) were comparable. No pericardial tamponade occurred. During 10.4±4.6 months, mortality, heart failure events, and atrial fibrillation incidence did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Superior RA pacing was feasible, showed a marked learning curve, and better preserved intrinsic atrial activation than RAA pacing.

articles.title: Heterogeneity of Treatment Effect of ABC Pathway-Based Care in Older Atrial Fibrillation: Insights from the mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF Trials Using a Causal Machine Learning Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrated care based on the Atrial fibrillation Better Care (ABC) pathway improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but whether treatment effects differ across older patients remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate heterogeneity of treatment effect (HTE) of ABC pathway-based care and assess its transportability across healthcare settings using causal machine learning (ML).

METHODS: Individual participant data from the cluster-randomised mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF trials were analysed, including 3,209 patients aged ≥65 years. Three causal ML models were developed in mAFA-II and externally validated in MIRACLE-AF. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, ischaemic stroke, intracranial haemorrhage, heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, or major bleeding.

RESULTS: The uplift random forest demonstrated the best performance and identified meaningful HTE. In the mAFA-II testing cohort, ABC pathway-based care was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome in patients predicted to benefit, whereas no benefit and possible harm were observed in those predicted to derive harm (P-interaction=0.002). In external validation, benefit was preserved in the predicted benefit group but not in the predicted harm group, although treatment discrimination was attenuated. Patients predicted to derive limited benefit had greater clinical complexity, including higher comorbidity burden and CHA2DS2-VASc scores. Sex, heart failure, and hypertension were the strongest predictors of treatment effect.

CONCLUSIONS: ABC pathway-based integrated care demonstrates clinically meaningful treatment heterogeneity among older patients with AF. These findings support more personalised implementation of integrated care and highlight the potential of causal ML to guide precision management in AF.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: MAFA-II trial (ChiCTR-OOC-17014138 || http://www.chictr.org.cn/, registered on 26 December 2017), MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514 || https://clinicaltrials.gov/, registered on 10 November 2020).

articles.title: Genipin-crosslinked cellulose/chitosan/β-cyclodextrin molecularly imprinted hydrogel for green selective extraction of chlorogenic acid and bioactive wound dressing application.
articles.abstract: Chlorogenic acid (CGA) is a naturally occurring polyphenol with multifaceted therapeutic potential, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, and regenerative activities; however, its conventional isolation process often relies on organic solvents, raising significant ecological and environmental concerns. In this study, a cellulose-based molecularly imprinted hydrogel (MDH@SMIP) was prepared using cellulose-based hydrogel (MDH) as the substrate by genipin cross-linking (β-cyclodextrin and chitosan functional monomers). MDH@SMIP is capable of extracting CGA from crude extracts of lingonberry (Vaccinium vitis-idaea L.) to produce an antibacterial and antioxidant hydrogel dressing (MDH@SMIP-CGA), which can then be used directly for wound healing. MDH@SMIP-CGA enables stimuli-responsive and controlled delivery of CGA in response to the wound microenvironment to achieve wound bacterial inhibition and reactive oxygen species clearance. MDH@SMIP-CGA exhibits excellent biocompatibility and promotes cell proliferation and migration. Distinct from conventional workflows that rely on organic solvents to extract phytochemicals and then re-load them onto dressings, this work integrates green molecular imprinting directly into a biocompatible cellulose hydrogel. The imprinted network simultaneously recognizes, enriches and delivers CGA from crude lingonberry extract, while responding to the mildly acidic wound microenvironment for on-demand release. This all-in-one recognition-and-dressing strategy thus offers a more environmentally friendly route from crude plant biomass to a precision wound therapy that combines infection control, anti-inflammation and tissue regeneration.

articles.title: Nanobodies targeting a conserved henipavirus G glycoprotein receptor-binding region potently protect against Nipah virus infection.
articles.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV) are highly lethal zoonotic henipaviruses with pandemic potential, yet no approved antiviral therapeutics are currently available. Here, we identified four nanobodies targeting the viral attachment glycoprotein (G) with strong neutralizing activity. All candidates potently neutralized NiV-Malaysia (NiVM) and NiV-Bangladesh (NiVB) in authentic virus assays, with IC50 values in the low ng/mL range (2.50-18.3 ng/mL). 2E2 shows the most potent activity, with an IC50 of 2.50 ng/mL. These candidates cross-neutralized HeV in pseudovirus assays at levels comparable to those against NiV, yet authentic HeV neutralization was reduced with the most potent clone reaching an IC₅₀ of 160 ng/mL and the remaining clones showing variable potency. In Syrian hamsters challenged with 1000 LD50 NiVM, prophylactic administration of 1C3, 2E2, or 5A3 provides complete protection. Notably, 2E2 confers superior therapeutic protection (66.7% survival) when administered 24 h post-infection. Additionally, 2E2 provides 50% prophylactic protection against lethal HeV. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis indicated that the nanobodies recognize a conserved region within the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of G, with distinct sensitivities to individual residue substitutions. Notably, 2E2 exhibited minimal sensitivity to the tested NiV G mutations and retained neutralizing activity against the m102.4 escape-associated substitutions NiV G-V507I and HeV G-D582N. These findings identify 2E2 as a candidate RBD-targeting nanobody with potent prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy against NiV and cross-neutralizing activity against HeV, warranting further evaluation as a countermeasure for NiV outbreaks.

articles.title: Chitosan/cellulose based multilayer dressing with directional exudate transport for sequential hemostasis and anti-infection in wound management.
articles.abstract: A multilayer fibrous dressing based on chitosan (CS) and wood pulp cellulose (WPC) fibers was designed, integrated with hydrophilic/hydrophobic heterogeneous polyester and superhydrophobic polytetrafluoroethylene layers, to achieve sequential functions of hemostasis, directional exudate transport, and anti-infection. The wound-facing hydrophilic/hydrophobic fiber layer creates directional microchannels which pump exudate spontaneously toward the intermediate layer. The polysaccharide composite in intermediate layer rapidly absorbs exudate, promotes hemostasis via platelet activation, and provides antibacterial activity. The outer superhydrophobic fiber layer acts as a physical bacterial barrier. Compared with gauze, the dressing reduced blood loss by 66% and shortened hemostasis time by 30%. The dressing also showed 39% reduction in rewetting rate, blocked the endotoxin back-diffusion, and achieved excellent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, along with good biocompatibility and anti-adhesion properties. The dressings showed synergistic hemostasis, exudate management, and anti-infection functions to the time-programmed requirements of wound healing; thereby creating an optimal wound-healing microenvironment. In an infected rat model, it resulted in 92% wound closure rate by day 14, and promoted orderly collagen deposition for high-quality repair. The work demonstrates that a chitosan/cellulose-based multilayer dressing can achieve spatiotemporally sequential wound management, providing a polysaccharide-driven strategy for advanced wound care.

articles.title: Negative-Pressure Wound Therapy for Surgical Site Infection Prevention After Elective Open Abdominal Surgery: A Risk-Stratified Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical-site infection (SSI) is a major source of morbidity after elective open abdominal surgery. Prophylactic negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT) may reduce SSI, but evidence specific to elective surgery remains limited.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026 for RCTs comparing prophylactic NPWT with standard wound dressing (SWD) in adults undergoing elective open abdominal surgery. The prespecified primary outcome was overall SSI within 30 days. Random-effects (REML) meta-analysis generated risk ratios or mean differences with 95% confidence and prediction intervals; certainty was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2 639 patients) were included; 13 were at low risk of bias. NPWT reduced overall SSI (15 RCTs, 2 134 patients; RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.43-0.84; low certainty; absolute risk 12.6% vs 19.5%, approximately 7% reduction; NNT≈15), superficial SSI (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.98), and seroma (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.86; both high certainty). No significant differences were observed in deep SSI, hematoma, dehiscence, readmission, length of stay, blood loss, operative time, or mortality. Benefit was concentrated in lower-income-country trials and high-risk patients, whereas high-income multicenter trials showed no benefit. Prediction intervals crossed the null, and funnel asymmetry suggested possible publication bias.

CONCLUSIONS: NPWT may reduce overall SSI, superficial SSI, and seroma after elective open abdominal surgery, but effects appear context-dependent and were absent in the highest-quality multicenter trials. Routine use in unselected elective patients is not supported; selective use in high-risk patients may be appropriate, pending confirmatory trials such as PROPEL-2.

articles.title: From historical samples to future application: temporal stability and catheter applicability boundaries of a CLABSI prediction model.
Predictors of spontaneous passage of ureteral stones <10 mm in emergency pre-stented patients: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify the rate and predictive factors of spontaneous passage of ureteral stones <10 mm in patients with indwelling ureteral stents.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A focused literature review was conducted in May 2025 using PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science, focusing on English-language original studies reporting spontaneous passage of ureteral stones <10mm in adult patients with a ureteral stent placed in an emergency context (e.g., obstructive uropathy, acute renal colic, or sepsis).

RESULTS: The database search identified 40 records after removal of duplicates. Following title and abstract screening, nine full-text articles were assessed for eligibility. Two articles were excluded at the full-text stage, one because it was not published in English and one because it did not exclusively concern ureteral stones. Seven studies were ultimately included in the narrative review. These studies involved symptomatic patients with single ureteral stones <10 mm initially managed with a double-J stent. Reported spontaneous stone passage (SSP) rates ranged from 8% to 61%. Stones ≤5 mm were significantly more likely to pass (up to 50%), while SSP was rare for stones ≥7 mm. Distal location and low stone density (<1000 HU) were also consistently identified as independent predictors of SSP. Prolonged stent dwell time (>4 weeks), female sex, and stone ureteral migration during stenting were also identified as contributing factors in some studies.

CONCLUSION: Stone size ≤5 mm, distal location, and low density appear to be the most consistently reported factors associated with spontaneous stone passage in patients with indwelling ureteral stents. However, given the limited number of retrospective single-center studies and their heterogeneity, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Rather than supporting definitive decision-making, these factors may help inform individualized clinical assessment.

articles.title: Ivermectin Mass Drug Administration Coverage Against Onchocerciasis in Cameroon, 2000-2025: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent onchocerciasis transmission has been documented in some Cameroonian foci despite long-term ivermectin mass drug administration (MDA). We synthesized treatment coverage, adherence and determinants.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed seven databases and grey literature (2000-2025). District-year coverage observations were standardized to total-population epidemiological coverage and pooled using logit-transformed random-effects meta-analysis with Restricted Maximum Likelihood estimation and study/district cluster-robust inference. Adherence, infection prevalence and barriers to treatment were described separately.

RESULTS: Thirty-two studies/reports were included among which 20 independent sources contributed 116 observations to the primary meta-analysis. Standardized survey coverage averaged 66.5% (range 32.0-88.3%); 45/116 (38.8%) observations were below the 65% recommendation. Programme-reported coverage exceeded survey estimates in 97/98 paired observations by a mean 21.7 percentage points. Pooled coverage was 67.3% (95% CI 65.0-69.5%; I²=98.5%; prediction interval 40.6-86.1%); the cluster-robust 95% CI was 56.8-76.3%. Five-year adherence ranged from 24% to 67%, while systematic non-adherence ranged from 6.8% to 35% across reported settings. Qualitative synthesis identified setting-specific combinations of missed contact, absence, distribution failures, refusal or hesitancy, adverse-effect concerns, information and trust barriers, mobility and temporary ineligibility. Microfilarial prevalence declined substantially from baseline (52% to 95%) but remained highly heterogeneous across long-treated settings, with the latest reported post-CDTI prevalence ranging from 0% to 47.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: Ivermectin mass drug administration (MDA) coverage in Cameroon was highly heterogeneous, mirroring variations in infection prevalence. Programme-reported coverage consistently exceeded survey-based estimates. Coverage gaps reflected context-specific operational and community acceptance barriers. Elimination monitoring should therefore triangulate survey-based coverage and adherence, local delivery barriers, and transmission indicators to guide targeted programme improvements and onchocerciasis elimination decisions.

articles.title: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever in Spain (2016-2025): Epidemiology, public health coordination and laboratory diagnosis at the National Reference Laboratory.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) became a mandatory notifiable disease in Spain after the first autochthonous human cases in 2016. This study characterised suspected cases referred to the National Reference Laboratory (NRL) between 2016 and 2025 and compared them with laboratory-confirmed infections.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from patients tested for suspected CCHFV infection at the NRL. Demographic, temporal, and geographical variables were analysed. Diagnosis combined two RT-PCR assays targeting different genomic regions and serological methods.

RESULTS: Of the 174 suspected cases tested between 2016 and 2025, 18 (10.3%) were laboratory-confirmed. Investigated cases increased from an annual average of 11 (2016-2020) to 23.8 (2021-2025). Confirmed cases were detected annually from 2020. Most suspected cases (89%) occurred between April and October, peaking in June-July; confirmed cases were diagnosed between April and September and peaked in July-August. Men represented 74.1% of suspected and 83.3% of confirmed cases, with most confirmed infections in males aged 61-70 years.

CONCLUSIONS: The increase in suspected cases reflects enhanced surveillance, awareness, and broader testing rather than a proportional rise in confirmed infections. Annual detection supports endemic CCHFV circulation in Spain, underscoring the importance of surveillance, laboratory preparedness, and rapid diagnostic capacity.

articles.title: Preparing for Next-Generation Vaccines: Breakthrough Invasive Pneumococcal Disease Patterns Post-PCV13 and Post-PPSV23 in Australia.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumococcal conjugate (PCV) and polysaccharide (PPSV) vaccines have reduced invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in Australia. We evaluated breakthrough IPD following PCV13 and PPSV23 immunization (2009-2023) to inform next-generation vaccine strategies.

METHODS: We analyzed laboratory-confirmed IPD cases from the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System to estimate the vaccine-type proportion among vaccinated IPD cases (those meeting the minimum age-specific dose threshold), whose vaccine-type infections constitute breakthrough IPD. Temporal trends were assessed using logistic regression, and subgroup differences using chi-square or Fisher's tests. Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models with five-fold cross-validation classified IPD due to PPSV23-type serotypes.

RESULTS: Across 25,643 IPD cases, annual notifications increased while PCV13-type proportions declined. PCV13-type proportions were 19.4% in infants and 37.5% at 2-14 years; PPSV23-type proportions were 47.5% at 15-69 and 48.4% at ≥70 years, with serotype 3 the largest contributor. Vaccinated individuals showed lower vaccine-type proportions than non- or partially vaccinated cases across age groups. Vaccine-type proportions were highest for pneumonia and in the Northern Territory, with greatest residual burden among older adults and Indigenous Australians. Machine-learning models classifying PPSV23-type IPD (accuracy ≈92%) identified vaccination-related variables, clinical presentation, and year of infection as key predictors; excluding these variables reduced AUC from 0.97-0.98 to 0.69.

CONCLUSION: PCV13-type proportions declined over time, most markedly in infants, whereas PPSV23-type proportions remained persistently high in older adults and Indigenous Australians despite higher documented vaccination. Serotype 3, included in all current conjugate formulations, dominated breakthrough for both vaccines, and in descriptive comparisons limited by small subgroup sizes, neither additional doses nor sequential vaccination was associated with lower vaccine-type proportions.

articles.title: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve.

DESIGN: Modified Delphi-based global consensus study.

PARTICIPANTS: International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases.

METHODS: A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. Experts responded anonymously to statements assessing consensus and to revised items addressing indications, contraindications, timing, preoperative workup, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative management. Results are reported using item-specific denominators because occasional non-response occurred across the survey items.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement among the experts. Agreement between 60% and 69.9% was considered to be near consensus.

RESULTS: The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.

articles.title: Molecular Characterization and Regulatory Role of UBE2A in Inflammatory Responses in the Manila Clam (Ruditapes philippinarum).
articles.abstract: Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 A (UBE2A) is a core component of the ubiquitination machinery that plays an important role in innate immunity, however, its immune function in the bivalve mollusk Ruditapes philippinarum has not been experimentally defined. In this study, we identified a UBE2A homolog (RpUBE2A) encoding a protein with a conserved ubiquitin-conjugating (UBC) domain. Phylogenetic analysis placed RpUBE2A within the molluscan UBE2A clade. RpUBE2A was constitutively expressed across all examined tissues, with highest transcript levels in immune-related tissues, particularly the gill and siphon. Following Vibrio parahaemolyticus challenge, both RpUBE2A mRNA and protein were significantly upregulated. Functional assays revealed that RpUBE2A overexpression enhanced global ubiquitination, upregulated the key inflammatory cytokine RpIL-17, and increased inflammatory cell infiltration as evidenced by H&E staining, whereas it significantly reduced cell viability. Conversely, RNA interference-mediated knockdown of RpUBE2A markedly attenuated the inflammatory response triggered by V. parahaemolyticus challenge. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that RpUBE2A is rapidly induced upon infection and, through modulating inflammatory genes and ubiquitination, serves as a positive regulator of the antibacterial innate immune response, likely contributing to the initiation and amplification of gill inflammation during V. parahaemolyticus challenge. These results reveal a previously unrecognized immune function for UBE2A and provide the first evidence for UBE2A-dependent host-pathogen interactions in bivalves.

articles.title: Not All PVR Reductions Are Created Equal: Lessons From the CADENCE Trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: The CADENCE trial evaluated sotatercept in combined post- and pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CpcPH-HFpEF). We analyzed the pathophysiological implications of the observed pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) reduction.A hemodynamic comparison was conducted contrasting the mechanistic effects of sotaercept with conventional pulmonary vasodilators.In CADENCE, PVR and pressure reductions occurred without marked cardiac output augmentation, contrasting with flow-mediated recruitment typical of traditional vasodilators. Sotatercept-induced PVR reduction may reflect true vascular reverse remodeling rather than vasodilation, underscoring the need to discriminate resistance reduction mechanisms in CpcPHHFpEF.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Lenalidomide-Dexamethasone in Combination With Radiotherapy in Solitary Plasmacytoma.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Radiotherapy achieves excellent local control in solitary plasmacytoma, but systemic progression remains a major limitation. We evaluated the long-term association between lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy and disease outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included 75 consecutive patients with solitary plasmacytoma treated between 2004 and 2025. All patients underwent bone marrow assessment, serum free light-chain testing, and magnetic resonance imaging, with PET/CT routinely incorporated into staging from late 2008 onward. Patients received radiotherapy alone (n=42) or radiotherapy combined with lenalidomide-dexamethasone (n=33). Primary endpoints were progression-free survival and multiple myeloma-free survival. Systemic progression-free survival, defined by progression to multiple myeloma, multiple plasmacytomas, or distant solitary plasmacytoma, was additionally evaluated.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 6.31 years. Only three local recurrences occurred. Lenalidomide-dexamethasone was associated with longer progression-free survival (HR, 0.315; 95% CI, 0.128-0.775; p=0.012), with 10-year rates of 71.8% versus 26.7% after radiotherapy alone. Among the six patients progressing after combined treatment, three (50.0%) developed multiple myeloma and three (50.0%) developed multiple plasmacytomas. Multiple myeloma-free survival did not differ significantly between groups (10-year rates, 86.6% vs 65.9%; p=0.19).

CONCLUSION: Lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy was associated with sustained improvement in progression-free survival in solitary plasmacytoma. These long-term findings support prospective evaluation of upfront lenalidomide-dexamethasone in combination with radiotherapy for solitary plasmacytoma.

articles.title: Staphylococcal coagulases amplify fibrinogen-dependent NETosis by S. aureus in human neutrophils and exacerbate early thromboinflammation in mice.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Bloodstream Staphylococcus aureus infections activate the host's thromboinflammatory response. Staphylocoagulases (Coa and vWbp) are virulence factors that manipulate the host coagulation system that may influence downstream neutrophil responses. We therefore investigated how coagulase-host interactions influence neutrophil activation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and systemic thromboinflammation.

METHODS: Human neutrophils were stimulated with methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) USA300 wild-type (WT) or coagulase-deficient (ΔcoaΔvwb) strains, and functional activation was analyzed by flow cytometry. NET formation was evaluated from bacteria that had been pre-incubated with fibrinogen, prothrombin, or both. We modeled sepsis in C57BL/6J mice by intravenous injection of WT or ΔcoaΔvwb MRSA. Responses in peripheral blood (differential counts, thromboinflammatory parameters), and hepatic immunothrombosis were examined at timepoints before mice reached moribundity.

RESULTS: MRSA induced rapid neutrophil activation, characterized by CD11b conformational activation and robust degranulation, independent of coagulase expression. USA300 WT, but not ΔcoaΔvwb, strains triggered NET formation that was enhanced by fibrinogen and not by staphylothrombin alone or S. aureus-generated fibrin. This was independent of CD11b activation or degranulation. In vivo, coagulases were associated with early increase of acute-phase reactants, including fibrinogen, von Willebrand factor, and interleukin-6. In the liver, coagulases promoted early neutrophil recruitment and altered thrombus composition, reflected by an increase in VWF-rich thrombi at day 4.

CONCLUSIONS: Fibrinogen amplifies S. aureus-induced NET formation through mechanisms potentially linked to coagulase expression but independent of canonical neutrophil activation pathways. Staphylocoagulases predominantly enhance early inflammatory and endothelial responses without driving sustained coagulation activation, indicating a temporally restricted role in shaping thromboinflammation.

articles.title: The metabolic-brain axis: GLP-1 signaling, insulin resistance, and obesity pharmacotherapy in neurodegeneration.
articles.abstract: The intersection of metabolic disease and neurodegeneration represents one of the most consequential frontiers in translational neuroscience. Converging epidemiological, mechanistic, and pharmacological evidence supports a bidirectional metabolic-brain axis in which systemic insulin resistance, obesity, and chronic metabolic inflammation are associated with and may contribute to alterations in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, and neuroimmune homeostasis. GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for glycemic control and weight management, have therefore been investigated as potential disease-modifying therapies across Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related neurodegenerative conditions through mechanisms including neuronal PKA activation, microglial NLRP3 suppression, mitochondrial biogenesis, and restoration of AQP4 perivascular localization that may contribute to glymphatic waste clearance. Direct human evidence for these CNS mechanisms remains limited or absent, with current support derived primarily from preclinical models and indirect human data, as detailed in Table 1, warranting dedicated investigation in the context of GLP-1 receptor agonism. Importantly, the two pivotal phase 3 programs designed to test this hypothesis in humans - EVOKE/EVOKE+ in early Alzheimer's disease and Exenatide-PD3 in Parkinson's disease - have both now reported, and neither demonstrated a statistically significant benefit on its primary clinical endpoint, despite favorable biomarker and epidemiological signals preceding these results. This review synthesizes current knowledge on brain insulin signaling, GLP-1 neurobiology, obesity-driven neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence for metabolic therapeutics in neurodegeneration, and uses the dissociation between mechanistic plausibility, epidemiological association, and null confirmatory trial results to identify critical knowledge gaps and translational barriers related to CNS target engagement, optimal dosing, and disease-modifying efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The review is organized into four major themes: brain insulin signaling, central GLP-1 biology, obesity-associated neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence supporting metabolic therapies for neurodegenerative disease.

articles.title: Oxidative balance metabolite signatures in PREDIMED: Interpreting the divergent cardiovascular and diabetes findings.
Symptoms That Walk Away: The Walk-Through Phenomenon and Severe Coronary Artery Disease.
Guideline-directed medical therapy implementation and its association with cardiac adverse events across cardiac and noncardiac risk domains.
authors: West Tokyo Heart Failure (WET-HF) Registry Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) improves prognosis in heart failure (HF), but its implementation remains suboptimal, particularly in patients with multiple risk domains.

METHODS: We analyzed the association between GDMT achievement and the 2-year composite endpoint of cardiac death or HF hospitalization across cardiac and noncardiac risk domains using the WET-HF2 registry, a prospective multicenter Japanese registry. GDMT achievement was quantified using a dose-weighted GDMT score (0-12). Cardiac and noncardiac risk domains were assessed using MAGGIC risk score components.

RESULTS: Among 2,702 patients, median GDMT and MAGGIC risk scores were 5 (3-6) and 23 (18-27), respectively. Each 1-point increase in noncardiac risk domain was associated with lower GDMT achievement (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.93; 95% CI 0.90-0.95), whereas each 1-point increase in cardiac risk domain was associated with greater GDMT achievement (aOR, 1.08; 95% CI 1.06-1.10). Among patients in the highest tertile of noncardiac risk, no documented reason for non-prescription of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists was identified in 11% and 16%, respectively. During 2-year follow-up, 652 patients (24%) experienced the composite endpoint. A higher GDMT score was associated with lower risk of the composite endpoint (adjusted hazard ratio per point, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.91-0.98), consistently across tertiles of cardiac and noncardiac risk (P for interaction=0.784 and 0.359).
