CONCLUSIONS: Higher cardiac risk was associated with greater GDMT achievement, while higher noncardiac risk was associated with lower achievement. The favorable association between GDMT achievement and clinical outcomes was observed across both risk domains.

articles.title: An Old Infarct Tracer Uncovers a Second Cardiomyopathy.
Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors in Chronic Kidney Disease and Type 2 Diabetes: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is the leading cause of chronic kidney disease worldwide, and for decades renin-angiotensin-system (RAAS) blockade was the only proven strategy to slow its progression. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have since been shown to slow kidney function decline and reduce cardiorenal events through benefits disproportionate to their modest glycemic effect. Beginning with EMPA-REG OUTCOME, and confirmed by CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, and EMPA-KIDNEY, these agents significantly reduce major cardiorenal composite outcomes, largely independent of diabetes status, through restored tubuloglomerular feedback, reduced intraglomerular pressure, and hemodynamic and metabolic effects. Their safety profile is favorable, dominated by genital mycotic infection, with euglycemic ketoacidosis and, for some agents, amputation as rare but important considerations. Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes, the American Diabetes Association, and the European Society of Cardiology now recommend SGLT2 inhibitors as foundational, disease-modifying therapy in diabetic kidney disease. This review synthesizes that evidence for the practicing internist, whose prescribing choices will determine whether it reaches eligible patients.

articles.title: Decoding silent hosts: perspectives on asymptomatic Leishmania carriage dynamics.
articles.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
articles.abstract: Leishmaniasis, a neglected tropical disease caused by protozoan parasites of the genus Leishmania, constitutes a spectrum of diseases ranging from asymptomatic cases to symptomatic visceral and integumentary (cutaneous and mucous membranes) leishmaniasis. Asymptomatic carriers are suspected to represent a major hidden reservoir in endemic regions, which constitutes a main challenge for the control and potential elimination of the disease. This review discusses current knowledge on the immune dynamics, diagnostic challenges and transcriptomic signatures associated with asymptomatic Leishmania infection and immune dynamics of symptomatic cases, concentrating on the visceral and cutaneous forms of the disease. Understanding the molecular and immune processes behind asymptomatic carriage is essential for the strategies to be taken at many levels: therapy, transmission, as well as control. We show further that transcriptomics, proteomics and other advanced approaches represent powerful tools to identify and compare differential gene expression, immune pathways, and metabolic changes in symptomatic and asymptomatic cases. ONE SENTENCE SUMMARY: Asymptomatic infections constitute a major underestimated hidden reservoir for Leishmania infections in endemic regions ("silent host"), a main challenge for the control and potential elimination of the disease.

articles.title: Ticagrelor pretreatment and angiographic no-reflow in STEMI: a multicentre observational study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We examined the association between ticagrelor pretreatment and angiographic no-reflow in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), with in-hospital mortality as a secondary outcome and clinical phenotyping as an exploratory objective.

METHODS: In a retrospective multicentre registry (2018-2021), 623 patients referred for percutaneous coronary intervention were compared by loading strategy: pretreatment at first medical contact or deferred before PCI. Cohort-wide inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), using a clinical covariate-balancing propensity model and 50 imputations, estimated adjusted risk ratios (RRs). Outcome-blind latent class analysis preceded a treatment-weighted comparison of class-specific no-reflow risks.

RESULTS: No-reflow occurred in 28/464 pretreated patients versus 27/159 comparators (6.0% versus 17.0%); the crude RR was 0.36 (95% CI 0.22-0.58), and the IPTW-adjusted RR was 0.43 (95% CI 0.24-0.74; P = 0.003). Ten patients died (adjusted RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.13-1.67). Three classes comprised 328, 231 and 64 patients, but their pretreatment-standardised no-reflow risks did not establish prognostic separation.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticagrelor pretreatment was associated with lower angiographic no-reflow after propensity weighting. The adjusted mortality and exploratory class-risk findings did not reach statistical significance. Residual confounding and uncertain covariate timing limit causal interpretation, and prospective validation is required.

articles.title: EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework reveals mechanistic insights of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in ischemic stroke with experimental validation.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHWD), a classical formula recorded in Yilin Gaicuo, has been widely used for the treatment of stroke and post-stroke sequelae in traditional Chinese medicine.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to establish a novel framework based on the EWMCRITIC-VIKOR algorithm to prioritize potential BYHWD targets against IS by integrating multi-dimensional biological features, with validation through in vivo experiments.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: 14 biological features across 4 dimensions were quantified. Feature weights were calculated using EWM and CRITIC, and integrated via VIKOR for MCDM on BYHWD-IS overlapping targets. The therapeutic effects of BYHWD were validated in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model. Anti-inflammatory effects were assessed by RT-qPCR and ELISA, while western blotting were used to evaluate signaling via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway.

RESULTS: The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework prioritized 5 key targets (FOS, IL1β, AKT1, TP53, and IL6) from 239 overlapping targets. The VIKOR compromise solution exhibited a distinct low-Q priority set, in which the top targets jointly minimized group utility and individual regret, and the overall ranking showed weak association with logFC, indicating that prioritization was not driven by expression effect size alone. BYHWD treatment significantly improved MCAO-induced brain injury. RT-qPCR and ELISA showed marked downregulation of IL1B and IL6 after BYHWD treatment, and western blotting indicated altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling status.

CONCLUSION: The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework enables robust prioritization of therapeutic targets by integrating heterogeneous biological data. This approach enhances mechanistic understanding of BYHWD in IS and offers a reliable strategy for target discovery in herbal interventions.

articles.title: Treponema pallidum lipoprotein Tp0768 induces endothelial ferroptosis to promote monocyte recruitment.
articles.abstract: Syphilis is a serious infectious disease that poses a significant risk to human health, typically characterized by vascular inflammatory damage. Previous studies have indicated that Treponema pallidum (T. pallidum) infection enhances the migration of monocytes and their adhesion to endothelial cells, exacerbating endothelial dysfunction and facilitating pathogen dissemination. However, the exact underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we assessed the occurrence of ferroptosis in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) following exposure to the T. pallidum lipoprotein Tp0768 by measuring cell viability, lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS), the expression of ferroptosis-related genes and proteins, and the activation of relevant signaling molecules. Tp0768 significantly induced an increase in ROS levels in HUVECs, upregulation of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), ferritin heavy chain (FTH), and ferritin light chain (FTL), along with downregulation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11). This ferroptosis response led to enhanced secretion of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), and interleukin-8 (IL-8) from HUVECs, promoting increased migration and adhesion of THP-1 cells. Notably, the inhibition of ferroptosis or blockade of related signaling pathways effectively reversed these changes. In summary, Tp0768 induces ferroptosis in HUVECs through the PERK-ATF4-NRF2-HO-1 signaling pathway, thereby enhancing the migration and adhesion of THP-1 cells. These findings reveal a novel mechanism of vascular injury in syphilis and propose potential therapeutic intervention targets.

articles.title: Alginate-microsphere delivery prolongs pulmonary culture recovery of Acinetobacter baumannii XH386 in immunocompetent mice.
articles.abstract: Murine models of Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia predominantly reproduce acute infection, limiting investigation of later pulmonary host-pathogen interactions. We evaluated whether calcium-crosslinked alginate microencapsulation could prolong pulmonary culture recovery of A. baumannii XH386 in immunocompetent mice. After challenge with free XH386, pulmonary bacterial burdens declined rapidly, and viable bacteria were no longer recovered on days 6 or 7. Alginate-encapsulated XH386 also underwent a marked early reduction but remained culture recoverable throughout the extended observation period. Mean pulmonary burdens remained on the order of 103 CFU/lung from days 5 to 13 and declined to approximately 2 × 102 CFU/lung on days 15 and 18; all mice examined on day 18 remained culture positive (3/3). Histopathological abnormalities remained evident through day 7 after alginate-XH386 challenge, whereas scores had declined substantially after free-XH386 challenge. BALF TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL1 remained within the quantitative range in all alginate-XH386 samples through day 4, while below-quantitative-range measurements appeared earlier after free-XH386 challenge. Blank alginate microspheres were associated with low early histopathology scores and transient BALF inflammatory responses. Alginate microencapsulation therefore prolonged pulmonary culture recovery of XH386 and generated a low-burden culture-positive phase beyond that observed after free-bacterial challenge. This model provides an experimental window for examining bacterial and host responses after the acute phase of pulmonary infection.

articles.title: Cefiderocol for the treatment of bloodstream infection due to MBL-producing Enterobacterales: a single-center retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) caused by metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing Enterobacterales are associated with high mortality and limited therapeutic options. Real-world data on cefiderocol remain scarce.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre study (January 2023-April 2025) including adult patients with MBL-producing Enterobacterales BSI who received cefiderocol for ≥72 hours. The main study outcome was 14-day clinical cure rate.

RESULTS: Nineteen patients were included (mean age: 62.1 ± 12.1 years; median Charlson comorbidity index: 2.0 [IQR: 1.0 - 4.0]). Most (84.2%) had some form of immunosuppression. BSI sources were intra-abdominal (31.6%), respiratory (21.1%), and urinary tract (21.1%). Septic shock occurred in 10.5% of patients, and 26.3% required ICU admission. Median SOFA score at the initiation of cefiderocol was 5.0 days (4.5 - 8.5). Klebsiella spp. (89.5%) was the most common MBL-producing Enterobacterales (VIM [63.2%], NDM/OXA-48-like [26.3%], NDM [10.5%]). Prior colonization was observed in 36.8% of patients. Empirical therapy mainly included ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam for a median duration of 2 days (IQR 0.5-3.5). Cefiderocol was administered for a median of 8.0 days [4.0-14.0], as monotherapy in 79% and as combination therapy in 10.5%. Clinical cure rate was achieved by day +14 in 78.9% (15/19) of patients. All-cause mortality by day +14 was 10.5% (2/19). Cefiderocol resistance emerged during therapy in three out of four patients not achieving clinical and microbiological cure (15.8% [3/19] of the cohort), and mainly involved NDM/OXA-48-like-coproducing K. pneumoniae.

CONCLUSIONS: Cefiderocol is a potential option for MBL-producing Enterobacterales BSIs, although its efficacy may be limited by the development of treatment-emergent resistance.

articles.title: Strain-level proteotyping and expression of specific toxins in patients with recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) remains a major clinical challenge, and routine diagnostics that detect toxin genes rarely confirm toxin expression or resolve strain relatedness. We assessed whether combining whole-genome sequencing (WGS) with mass spectrometry proteotyping could resolve recurrence mechanisms and confirm toxin production.

METHODS: WGS, protein-level toxin typing and liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) proteotyping were combined. Of 33 isolates, 31 were collected at discrete time points from 14 patients and two lacked patient attribution. Datasets comprised 32 genomes and 29 proteomes (28 matched). Average nucleotide identity (ANI) and core-SNP distances were assessed.

RESULTS: Most serial isolates in the high-molecular-weight (HMW)-selected cohort shared ANI groups (>99% ANI), including persistence over 353 days, consistent with relapse; one patient showed two ANI groups compatible with reinfection. Six isolates from three patients formed a divergent lineage uniquely carrying cdtA/cdtB, an A3/B5 toxin background, and the only reported acquired resistance-gene hits. LC-MS/MS detected TcdA- and TcdB-derived peptides in all 29 profiled isolates, spanning conserved and subtype-discriminating regions.

CONCLUSIONS: LC-MS/MS proteotyping provides an expression-level layer concordant with genotype and, integrated with WGS, distinguishes relapse from reinfection and links divergent lineages to specific toxin and resistance profiles, complementing genomic and immunoassay-based CDI characterisation.

articles.title: Sex differences in the clinical phenotype of difficult-to-treat asthma in adults.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex disparity has been demonstrated within difficult-to-treat (difficult) asthma, with females reported to have greater disease severity and more comorbidities. Deeper understanding of these differences could help personalise management approaches.

OBJECTIVE: To assess differences in disease characteristics between males and females with difficult asthma.

METHODS: The Wessex AsThma CoHort study collected data from 500 patients across Southern England. Patient demographics, asthma and its treatment history, allergies, comorbidities, radiology, biological samples, lung function, and questionnaire data were subjected to univariable analyses to identify sex differences. Variables were then further assessed in multivariable regression models.

RESULTS: Males were older at disease onset and were more often ex-smokers. In multivariable regression models they had higher serum immunoglobulin E (ratio 1.95, 95% CI 1.19 to 3.20) and plasma inflammatory cytokine expression (interleukin-17, tumour necrosis factor - alpha, C-C motif ligands 3 and 11 and chitinase 3-like 1). Males had poorer lung function (forced expiratory volume in 1 second effect -9.98, 95% CI -15.21 to -4.74) and more frequently had nasal polyps. Females had higher Body Mass Index, and in multivariable regression higher plasma adipokine (ratio 1.25, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.37) and interleukin-5 expression (effect 3.52, 95% CI 2.65 to 4.39), multimorbidity burden (score effect 0.60, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.92), anxiety/depression, and inducible laryngeal obstruction (odds ratio 2.38, 95% CI 1.20 to 4.76). They self-reported worse Hull Cough Hypersensitivity, Nijmegen and Sino-Nasal Outcome Test scores. We observed no difference in treatment and healthcare utilisation, or composite asthma severity score.

CONCLUSION: Sex influences difficult asthma phenotype but contrasting factors are associated with similar overall disease severity in both sexes. Males have worse lung function and systemic inflammatory profiles, whilst females experience greater psychophysiological comorbidity and multimorbidity burden. Recognising differences and considering them clinically to fine-tune management may help improve difficult asthma outcomes.

articles.title: Pre-Rituximab Immunoglobulin Testing and Baseline Hypogammaglobulinemia Across Rituximab Indications in Adults: A Multisite Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Baseline immunoglobulin assessment before initiating B-cell-targeted therapies identifies pre-existing hypogammaglobulinemia (HG) and facilitates interpretation of post-treatment immune dysfunction. Historically, pre-treatment IgG testing rates have been low (<15%), and contemporary practice patterns remain poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize pre-rituximab serum total IgG testing, baseline HG, and pre-treatment immunoglobulin replacement therapy (IgRT) use across rituximab indications.

METHODS: We performed a multisite retrospective study of 1184 patients receiving their first rituximab infusion at Mayo Clinic between November 1, 2024, and November 1, 2025. We assessed IgG testing within 1 year and 60 days before rituximab, baseline IgG levels (HG defined as IgG <700 mg/dL), and pre-treatment IgRT use. Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with IgG testing and levels.

RESULTS: In a predominantly adult (1159/1184 [98%]) cohort, IgG was measured within 1 year before rituximab in 663/1184 patients (56%) and within 60 days in 514/1184 (43%). Testing rates varied by disease specialty, from 5/37 (14%) in dermatology to 60/74 (81%) in neurology (overall P<.001). Among patients tested within 60 days, 144/514 (28%) had HG and 35/514 (7%) had IgG <400 mg/dL. HG prevalence varied by disease category, including 16/20 (80%) in nephrotic syndrome and 24/40 (60%) in chronic/indolent leukemia. Among patients with baseline HG, 15/144 (10%) received pre-treatment IgRT: 11 replacement-dose IVIG, 4 immunomodulatory-dose IVIG, and 0 subcutaneous immunoglobulin.

CONCLUSION: In contemporary rituximab practice, baseline IgG testing has increased but remains incomplete, and HG is common among those tested. Specialty- and disease-specific variation identifies opportunities to standardize pre-treatment immunoglobulin assessment. Optimal management of baseline HG remains undefined.

articles.title: Association of Long-acting Bronchodilator Use with Cardiovascular Adverse Events in Patients with Asthma: A Population-based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A recent meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with cardiovascular adverse events (AEs) leading to treatment discontinuation in asthma, although the certainty of evidence was low.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cardiovascular safety of long-acting bronchodilators in a real-world asthma population.

METHODS: This population-based cohort study used UK Biobank data from patients with asthma (2006-2010). Exposure was categorized into three mutually exclusive groups: LABA alone, LAMA alone, or combined LABA/LAMA therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular AEs, including coronary heart disease, arrhythmia, hypertension, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Pre-specified subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 14,677 patients were included (median follow-up 14.68 years). Long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with an increased risk of total cardiovascular AEs (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.15). This was primarily driven by arrhythmia (HR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.06-1.42), heart failure (HR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.02-1.65), and cerebrovascular disease (HR: 1.35, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79). When stratified by regimen, the association was confined to the LABA group (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.001-1.13) and the combined group (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.09-1.59). The association was more pronounced in patients using short-acting bronchodilators (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.07-1.23; interaction P = 0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: The observed positive associations are more plausibly attributable to confounding rather than to a causal drug effect. Future research should prioritize new-user designs to clarify whether these signals are drug-specific or confounded by disease severity.

articles.title: Informing sample size and power calculations for clone-censor-weight analyses: a Monte Carlo simulation study of the variance inflation factor relative to the underlying target trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clone-censor-weighting (CCW) is a causal inference method used in target trial emulation in settings in which the time of application of the treatment occurs during follow-up. An important component of study design is determining the sample size required for a specified level of statistical power or to determine the statistical power associated with a specific sample size. Determining statistical power is relatively straightforward for the underlying randomized controlled trial (RCT) that one is emulating. In contrast, conducting power and sample size calculations for observational studies that employ CCW is not straightforward because the analysis incorporates inverse probability of censoring weights, which are only known at the analysis phase, and not during the design phase.

METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations (270 scenarios varying sample size, treatment prevalence, threshold for defining early treatment, and covariate-treatment odds ratios) were used to estimate the variance inflation factor (VIF) of a CCW analysis compared to the underlying target RCT, across two estimands: the risk difference and the relative risk.

RESULTS: In settings with 10 baseline covariates, the use of a CCW design tended to result in more precise estimation of risk differences and relative risks compared to the underlying RCT when the magnitude of confounding was low to moderate. The magnitude of the VIF depended on treatment prevalence, sample size, the time horizon at which risk was estimated, and the strength of the baseline covariates' association with treatment initiation. In secondary simulations, it was observed that the VIF comparing a CCW design to the underlying RCT tended to increase as the number of baseline covariates increased.

CONCLUSIONS: Researchers designing CCW studies can use the simulation results and the accompanying R code, available in a public GitHub repository, to obtain study-specific VIF estimates for incorporation into a priori power calculations.

articles.title: Statistical Pitfalls in Large Language Model Evaluation: A Practical Guide to Study Design and Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies evaluating large language models in medicine increasingly follow a common design in which a fixed set of clinical questions is posed to several sources, such as different language models, clinicians, or patient-education resources. The responses are then scored for outcomes including accuracy, completeness, readability, or similar measures. Because each source answers the same set of questions, the resulting observations are inherently paired: the question functions as the repeated unit across sources. Despite this structure, many studies analyze the resulting data using statistical procedures that assume independent observations.

DISCUSSION: Treating paired observations as independent introduces a mismatch between the study design and the statistical analysis. In evaluations where multiple sources respond to the same questions, the responses are naturally correlated because they are influenced by shared characteristics of the question, such as difficulty or ambiguity. Ignoring this dependence can reduce statistical power and distort the nominal type I error rate. These issues arise when commonly used independent-sample procedures, including the Mann-Whitney test, the Kruskal-Wallis test, one-way analysis of variance, or unpaired t-tests, are applied to datasets generated from identical question sets. The appropriate analytical framework instead treats the question as the unit of pairing. Methods designed for repeated or paired observations, such as the Friedman test or repeated-measures analysis of variance for overall comparisons, followed by paired contrasts using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test or paired t-tests with appropriate multiplicity correction, provide analyses that align with the underlying design. Effect sizes and regression approaches that account for the paired structure, including mixed-effects models with question treated as a random effect, may further strengthen inference. Recognizing the repeated-measures nature of these evaluations provides a straightforward path toward more statistically coherent analyses.

articles.title: Student Perceptions of Competency-Based Cut Scores and Assessment Design in a Pharmacokinetics Course.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate student perceptions of competency-based cut scores and assessment design following implementation within a pharmacokinetics course and examine whether perceptions were associated with achievement goal orientation.

METHODS: This exploratory, cross-sectional mixed-methods survey study included students enrolled in a first-year pharmacokinetics course. The survey assessed perceptions of competency-based cut scores, assessment preferences, learning behaviors, and achievement goal orientation using structured items, discrete-choice scenarios, and open-ended responses. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlations, and conjoint analysis; qualitative responses were analyzed thematically.

RESULTS: Of 150 eligible first-year students, 102 (68%) completed the survey. Among respondents, cut scores of 70%-75% were most often rated appropriate/fair. Students preferred lower cut score thresholds, lower-stakes assessments, and opportunities for reassessment. Mastery and performance-approach orientations were associated with stronger competency-based framing, while performance orientation was associated with fewer negative perceptions of cut scores. Qualitative responses indicated that students viewed cut scores as representing minimum competency and reported reduced stress and greater focus on core concepts. However, students also expressed concerns regarding reduced study intensity, minimum-effort behaviors, and maintaining academic rigor.

CONCLUSION: Respondents generally supported competency-based assessment while simultaneously expressing concerns regarding rigor and differentiation among learners. Achievement goal orientation may influence how students interpret competency-based assessment systems and their educational value.

articles.title: Radiological outcomes of metacarpal fractures fixed with intramedullary headless compression screws compared to dorsal plates.
articles.abstract: Intramedullary headless compression screws (IHCS) and dorsal plates are both established implants for operative fixation of metacarpal shaft fractures, but their comparative effects on radiological and clinical outcomes remain incompletely documented. We retrospectively reviewed 109 patients treated between 2014 and 2024 at our institution: 28 patients in the IHCS group and 81 patients in the plate group. Metacarpal length was assessed using a radiographic prediction model. The IHCS group showed a significantly greater absolute deviation from predicted metacarpal length (1.7 mm (95% CI 1.1 to 2.3) versus 0.8 mm (95% CI 0.7 to 1.0), p = 0.007), and shortening was more frequent than lengthening in both groups, with a significantly higher shortening in the IHCS group (-1.1 mm (95% CI -1.9 to -0.3) versus -0.2 mm (95% CI -0.4 to 0.0), p = 0.040). Despite this radiological difference, no statistically significant differences in total active motion (258° vs 266°, p = 0.345), fist closure rate (100% vs 96%, p = 0.900), rotational deformity (0/13 vs 1/33, p = 0.536) and grip strength relative to the contralateral hand (94% vs 99% in dominant-hand injuries, p = 0.496) were detected between the two groups. No nonunions occurred in either group. In the plate group, 36 patients (44%) underwent hardware removal; only one secondary procedure (tenolysis) was required in the IHCS group. The greater shortening observed after IHCS is biomechanically consistent with the compressive properties of this intramedullary implant. In conclusion, dorsal plating may provide more predictable length restoration, whereas IHCS fixation may decrease the need for secondary implant removal. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Integrative multi-omics and multi-trait analysis prioritizes regulatory mechanisms and genes for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent condition that progresses from simple steatosis to advanced fibrosis, significantly affecting liver function and systemic health. Despite its widespread impact, therapeutic options remain limited, highlighting the urgent need for comprehensive exploration to identify potential therapeutic targets.

METHODS: We developed an analysis pipeline anchored on liver gene expression, integrating differential meta-analysis of transcriptomic data across three MASLD stages, transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR), and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) to identify candidate genes potentially involved in MASLD progression. We further prioritized these genes using a scoring system that incorporated gene expression-clinical phenotype correlation meta-analysis, proteome-wide association studies (PWAS), and external genetic data from the GWAS Catalog and ExPheWAS. In addition, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis was performed to characterize the expression patterns of prioritized genes across liver cell types and disease stages.

RESULTS: By integrating transcriptomic, genetic, and phenotypic evidence, we prioritized 39 candidate regulators of MASLD. snRNA-seq analysis of liver cells from healthy to cirrhotic stages revealed stage- and cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes. Through experimental validation in a lipid overload hepatocyte model, we confirmed a role for MLIP in lipid metabolism. To facilitate community access and data exploration, these data were organized and deposited into a publicly accessible interactive web portal (www.masldportal.net).

CONCLUSIONS: Our integrative, liver expression-anchored multi-omics framework prioritized 39 candidate regulators of MASLD and highlighted MLIP as a functional modulator of hepatocellular lipid accumulation. These results provide a systematic foundation for understanding MASLD biology and for guiding future mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

articles.title: 'Hepatitis Delta in Spain: A Nationwide Prospective Characterization of Active Infection and Liver Disease Severity' - Author's reply.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

articles.title: Implementation and Impacts of Maternal and Perinatal Quality Collaboratives across U.S. States: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal and Perinatal Quality Care Collaboratives (M/PQCs) are voluntary state-based initiatives that leverage shared data systems, evidence-based toolkits, and quality improvement science to reduce preventable maternal and infant harm.

METHODS: A scoping review of academic and grey literature was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and registered in Open Science Framework. Seven databases were searched for U.S.-based M/PQC studies published between January 2000 - November 2024, analyzed in 2025. Two independent reviewers screened 456 deduplicated records; 31 met eligibility criteria. Quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by implementation theme and intervention topic.

RESULTS: Thirty-one studies spanning 16 states and one national analysis were included. Five themes were identified across two domains. Implementation approaches included: (A) building statewide governance infrastructure; (B) translating evidence into practice through standardized toolkits; and (C) strengthening communication, teamwork, and process outcomes. Impacts included: (D) demonstrated reductions in maternal and birth morbidity, including 45-95% reductions in early elective deliveries, 76-87% improvements in timely hypertension treatment, and national-level reductions in eclampsia and intensive care unit admissions; and (E) expansion of the collaborative mission toward contraceptive access, opioid use disorder care, and racial health equity.

DISCUSSION: M/PQCs function as a form of primary and secondary prevention, institutionalizing evidence-based protocols before obstetric emergencies occur. M/PQCs' evolution from clinical safety bundles toward equity, access, and social determinants signals an expanding mandate. Future initiatives should prioritize disaggregated outcome reporting, health equity frameworks, and inclusion of community birth and outpatient settings to ensure M/PQC gains are equitably distributed.

articles.title: Contralateral Major Amputation Following Diabetes- and Peripheral Artery Disease-Related Limb Loss: A Systematic Review and Pooled Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.

DESIGN/METHOD: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or prior ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.

RESULTS: Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was 6 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 3-9), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P=.622), geographic region (P=.662), study era (P=.893), or DM prevalence (P=.127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI versus non-CLTI PAD or DM versus post-ipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P<.001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11-64%).

CONCLUSIONS: NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

articles.title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.

METHODS: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

articles.title: Verapamil versus other calcium channel blockers and risk of incident type 2 diabetes mellitus: emerging evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Verapamil has attracted interest as a potential means of preserving pancreatic β-cell function through suppression of thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP), raising the question of whether it differs from other calcium channel blockers in the risk of incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to quantify that association and assess the certainty of the evidence. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched from inception to 10 September 2026. Randomised trials and observational cohort studies comparing verapamil with another calcium channel blocker and reporting incident T2DM were eligible. Adjusted hazard ratios were pooled using a random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Two population-based cohort studies were included, one from Taiwan and one from Australia. The pooled estimate favoured verapamil but was imprecise (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.48-1.26), and was compatible with a substantial reduction in risk, with no difference, and with a modest increase. Statistical significance depended on the method used to account for between-study uncertainty, being present under the DerSimonian-Laird estimator (0.78, 95% CI 0.68-0.88) but not under the primary analysis. Both studies were at serious risk of bias from residual confounding, and the certainty of evidence was very low. The available evidence is insufficient to inform the choice of calcium channel blocker, and a randomised comparison with prespecified glycaemic ascertainment is required.

articles.title: The Asthma Impairment and Risk Questionnaire supports the GINA goal of minimization of exacerbation risk.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Instruments combining asthma symptom impairment with exacerbation history could help to quantitatively measure important control domains. The composite Asthma Impairment and Risk Questionnaire (AIRQ) is a validated 10-item assessment for patients aged ≥12 years that categorizes control and predicts exacerbations better than impairment-only measures or specialty physicians. The AIRQ rescue medication question could result in patients with daily use of short-acting beta2-agonists classified as well-controlled.

OBJECTIVE: Determine how a 'yes' response to using rescue daily, affects exacerbation occurrence in AIRQ-identified well-controlled patients.

METHODS: Among participants in an AIRQ exacerbation prediction study, number of well-controlled patients responding 'yes' to daily rescue use in the prior 2 weeks who experienced a subsequent exacerbation over 12 months was determined. Analogous analyses were performed when the AIRQ rescue question was substituted with a consensus-based item of rescue use >4 times in the prior 2 weeks.

RESULTS: Daily rescue use was reported by 8/375 AIRQ well-controlled patients (2.1%). Rescue use >4 times was reported by 21/359 well-controlled patients (5.8%) via AIRQ with the consensus-based rescue item. Among well-controlled populations, 1/375 with daily rescue use (0.3%) and 7/359 with rescue use >4 times (1.9%) in the prior 2 weeks had exacerbations. The number of well-controlled patients with subsequent exacerbations responding 'yes' to any one of the impairment or risk questions was similar between assessments (AIRQ: 55/375 [14.7%]; AIRQ with the consensus rescue item: 52/359 [14.5%]; P=.94).

CONCLUSION: A "yes" response to daily rescue use does not place patients identified as well-controlled by AIRQ at increased exacerbation risk.

articles.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor-23 as a biomarker to refine cardiovascular risk identification: A cross-sectional study in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Postmenopausal osteoporosis presents with heterogeneous comorbidities including cardiovascular disease. Objectives of this study were the identification of clusters of osteoporotic patients in relation to the cardiovascular risk, comorbidities, and levels of intact Fibroblast Growth Factor (iFGF23), a key player of the bone-cardiovascular axis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis took place in the Rheumatology Department, University Hospital Clermont-Ferrand, France. Twelve variables representative of comorbidities were selected according to their associations and clinical relevance: age, bone mineral density, flow-mediated dilation, cardiovascular risk (SCORE2/2OP), muscle mass, handgrip, sleep, quality of life, pain and plasma iFGF23. Multiple correspondence analysis followed by hierarchical clustering was used to propose profiles of patients and associations related to iFGF23 and cardiovascular risk.

RESULTS: Three comorbidity clusters were identified in 102 women (69.1 ± 7.7 years old): clusters of older age with worse outcomes, of younger age with better results and an intermediate cluster. iFGF23 is unveiled as a marker of the cardiovascular risk even in patients with normal renal function, with a threshold of 94.14 ng/L, and is significantly associated with age, fat mass, poor handgrip, poor quality of life, pain and impaired sleep.

CONCLUSIONS: Comorbidity clusters of post-menopausal osteoporosis based on the severity of health impairment highlight in this exploratory study iFGF23 as a possible biomarker of the cardiovascular risk. We suggest that iFGF23 measurement may complement SCORE2/2OP calculation to better predict the cardiovascular risk of osteoporosis patients. A suggested hypothesis-generating algorithm is proposed and future validation in a larger prospective study is warranted.

articles.title: AGE-RELATED BIOMECHANICAL AND STRUCTURAL REMODELING OF HUMAN MIDDLE CEREBRAL ARTERIES.
articles.abstract: Proper cerebral artery function is essential for maintaining the brain's microenvironment. The multilayered organization of cellular and extracellular matrix (ECM) constituents enables large cerebral arteries to accommodate pulse pressure and ensure both effective blood distribution and protection of the microcirculation. However, aging and disease induce compositional and structural remodeling in cerebral arteries, such as the middle cerebral artery (MCA), which can alter biomechanical properties and increase susceptibility to cerebrovascular conditions including atherosclerosis and aneurysms, both major contributors to stroke. Understanding how age-related changes in arterial structure and composition influence biomechanical behavior is critical for improving prediction of cerebrovascular risk. In this study, we characterized the age-dependent elastic and viscoelastic properties of human MCAs and related these changes to ECM structure and composition using imaging and biochemical assays. Our results demonstrate that aging is associated with increased stiffness and stress relaxation in MCAs. Biochemical analyses revealed age-related increases in collagen and glycosaminoglycan (GAG) content, both of which correlated with altered mechanical properties. Histological staining further showed denser collagen organization within the adventitia and elevated GAG presence, consistent with mechanical and biochemical findings. Additionally, multiphoton imaging under mechanical loading provided insight into layer-specific collagen reorganization in the adventitia. Collectively, these findings elucidate key age-dependent alterations in the structure-function relationship of human cerebral arteries and provide a mechanistic basis for increased cerebrovascular risk with aging. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Age-related remodeling of the extracellular matrix is a fundamental driver of tissue dysfunction, yet its effects on human cerebral artery mechanics remain poorly understood. In this study, we combine biomechanical testing, biochemical assays, histology, and multiphoton microscopy to characterize structural and functional remodeling of human middle cerebral arteries across a broad age range. We demonstrate that aging is associated with increased arterial stiffness and viscoelastic relaxation, accompanied by elevated collagen and glycosaminoglycan content. By directly linking extracellular matrix composition and organization to biomechanical function, this work provides new insights into the mechanisms governing cerebrovascular aging. These findings establish an important structure function framework for understanding vascular tissue remodeling and have broader implications for age related vascular dysfunction, mechanobiology, and biomaterials research.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Return to Work After Ischemic Stroke in Young Adults in Northwest China: A retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke increasingly affects working-age individuals. Returning to work (RTW) is a critical rehabilitation goal for these patients. This study investigated the proportion of young adults in Northwest China who did not return to work (NRTW) 12 months after an ischemic stroke and identified factors associated with NRTW.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of young patients (18-49 years) with ischemic stroke, admitted between January 2017 to August 2019, who had stable employment before onset. Data collected included demographics, lifestyle, comorbidities, stroke etiology classification, clinical features (including NIHSS score and specific functional impairments at admission) and medical interventions. RTW status was determined at the 12-month follow-up. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations (20 imputed datasets). Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions were applied to identify factors associated with NRTW.

RESULTS: Among 339 previously employed patients (median age 44; 284 [83.78%] males), 106 (31.3%) had not returned to work at 12 months. Multivariable analysis identified female (OR = 3.02, 95% CI 1.21-7.52, P = 0.017) and pre-stroke manual labor (OR = 4.66, 95% CI 2.50-8.66, P < 0.001) as significant demographic factors positively associated with NRTW. A higher NIHSS score at admission was associated with NRTW (NIHSS 5-9 vs. 0-4: OR = 3.12, 95% CI 1.46-6.69, P = 0.003; NIHSS ≥ 10 vs. 0-4: OR = 6.69, 95% CI 2.35-19.04, P < 0.001). Regarding specific impairments, aphasia was significantly associated with NRTW (OR = 3.67, 95% CI 1.32-10.20, P = 0.013), while motor dysfunction showed a marginal positive association (OR = 1.83, 95% CI 0.99-3.35, P = 0.052). Cardioembolic stroke showed significant association in the model including specific clinical features (OR = 4.12, 95% CI 1.36-12.46, P = 0.012, Model 2), a finding that requires confirmation in larger studies.

CONCLUSION: A proportion of young stroke survivors in Northwest China do not resume work at 12 months after stroke. Key factors associated with failure to RTW include female sex, pre-stroke manual labor, greater stroke severity (higher NIHSS), and the presence of aphasia. Motor dysfunction may also be an important factor in RTW. The association of stroke etiology with RTW may be influenced by neurological severity. These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve RTW outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Pharmacist test-and-treat services: Bridging the gap from certification to practice integration.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Florida's House Bill 389 expanded community pharmacists' scope of practice to include testing and treating minor, nonchronic conditions through collaborative practice agreements with physicians. While pharmacist certification training programs have facilitated implementation of these services, limited evidence exists regarding the extent to which certified pharmacists have incorporated test-and-treat services into routine pharmacy practice.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the extent to which certified Florida pharmacists have integrated test-and-treat services into clinical practice.

METHODS: A cross-sectional electronic survey was conducted among Florida pharmacists who completed state-specific certification to provide test-and-treat services in the Florida Department of Health portal (N=3,379). The survey assessed pharmacists' practice settings, certification pathways, implementation of test-and-treat services, conditions managed, and confidence level in providing clinical activities. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize pharmacist characteristics and service utilization.

RESULTS: A total of 266 responses were recorded (7.9% response rate). Respondents were primarily female (62%), over the age of 47, and employed within large chain community pharmacies. Walgreens was the leading certification provider (44%), followed by the University of Florida (19%) and Walmart (18%). Pharmacists expressed confidence in referring patients and in interpreting point-of-care test results. Implementation of test-and-treat services showed 97% of pharmacists saw fewer than 10 patients weekly. The greatest barriers noted by pharmacists were a lack of reimbursement or unclear billing procedures, a lack of time, and a lack of staff.

CONCLUSION: Survey data indicate there is a significant gap between test-and-treat certification and clinical use within Florida. Pharmacists feel clinically confident and are well trained to implement test-and-treat clinical services; however, staff shortages, time constraints, and the lack of reimbursement are restricting these services. Future success will depend on consistent revenue and corporate investment in clinical work flows to advance policies necessary to secure insurer reimbursement.

articles.title: STUDY OF THE PREVALENCE OF HEREDITARY HEMOCHROMATOSIS (HFE) AND SECONDARY CAUSES OF HYPERFERRITINEMIA IN PATIENTS TREATED IN A BLOODLETTING PROGRAMME.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Phlebotomy is the cornerstone of treatment for patients with hereditary hemochromatosis (HH) (C282Y/C282Y). Its role in patients with hyperferritinaemia (HF) and moderate iron overload remains controversial. In recent years, HF due to metabolic syndrome and obesity has increased significantly.

AIMS & METHODS: To study the causes and indications for bloodletting in patients undergoing treatment at our hospital's Gastroenterology Department and to determine the prevalence of HH and compare iron profiles between patients with confirmed HH and patients with other causes of HF.

RESULTS: A total of 179 patients were included. There were 48 women and 131 men. The median age was 55. In the homozygous C282Y group, it was 49.5, and in the rest, it was 60 (p: 0.0019), requiring earlier treatment in the HH group. The indication for bloodletting was correct (HH with significant hepatic iron overload) in 48% of cases. HFE mutations: C282Y/C282Y 70 (39.55%), C282Y/H63D 50 (28.25%). Patients with metabolic syndrome and hyperferritinaemia (33%) were placed on a bloodletting programme. Obesity (BMI>30) was present in 37.76% of patients. A significant alcohol consumption was present in 38.22% of patients. In the MRI study, only 25.50% of patients had elevated iron overload (>80 mmol/g), with 47.65% having moderate overload (>36<80). LIC was significantly higher in C282Y/C282Y patients (101.22 vs 51.98) (p: 0.0000). Laboratory: Serum ferritin (p:0.0268), IST (p:0.0000) and Fe (p:0.0000) values were significantly higher in patients with HH (C282Y/C282Y).

CONCLUSION: We must re-evaluate patients undergoing chronic bloodletting, as a high percentage do not benefit from it.

articles.title: Dementia, Treatment Intensity, and Outcomes in Acute Myocardial Infarction with Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia is associated with lower use of invasive therapies and poorer outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). However, its impact in AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMICS), where timely invasive management is critical for survival, remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the association between dementia, treatment intensity, and in-hospital outcomes in AMICS.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2019). Adults hospitalized with AMICS were identified using ICD-10-CM codes and stratified according to pre-existing dementia. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and use of invasive and supportive therapies. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, hospital, socioeconomic, presentation, and comorbidity characteristics estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We additionally performed 1:1 propensity score matching.

RESULTS: Among 226,570 patients with AMICS, 10,895 (4.8%) had dementia. Patients with dementia were older, more frequently female, had greater comorbidity burden, and fewer markers of acute disease severity. They underwent coronary angiography (50.2% vs. 70.4%), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (39.3% vs. 55.0%), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (5.2% vs. 17.5%), mechanical ventilation (34.1% vs. 45.5%), and circulatory support (23.7% vs. 46.4%) less frequently than those without dementia (all p < 0.001). Dementia was independently associated with lower odds of coronary angiography (aOR 0.50, 95% CI 0.48-0.52), PCI (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.55-0.61), CABG (aOR 0.31, 95% CI 0.28-0.34), and circulatory support (aOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.46-0.51), as well as higher odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.12-1.22) and MACCE (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.09-1.18). Results were consistent in the propensity-matched pairs.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalized with AMICS, dementia was independently associated with lower treatment intensity and worse in-hospital outcomes despite fewer markers of acute clinical severity. These findings highlight the importance of individualized, goal-concordant decision-making while avoiding unwarranted limitation of potentially life-saving therapies.

articles.title: Pulmonary function impairment, exercise intolerance, and clinical outcomes in symptomatic patients with HFpEF undergoing exercise stress echocardiography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary function impairment is common in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). However, its relationships with exercise capacity, cardiovascular reserve capacity, and prognosis in HFpEF remain uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied symptomatic patients undergoing exercise stress echocardiography with simultaneous expired gas analysis. Cross-sectional analyses were performed to compare pulmonary function in patients with HFpEF and symptomatic controls in the cohort with available data on percent predicted vital capacity (%VC) and forced expiratory volume in 1 s (%FEV₁). Outcome assessment was also performed in a subset of patients.

RESULTS: Among 486 patients in the cross-sectional cohort, 178 had HFpEF and 308 were symptomatic controls. Patients with HFpEF had lower %VC and %FEV₁ than controls. After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index, lower %VC and %FEV₁ were consistently associated with reduced exercise capacity, higher echocardiographic estimates of left ventricular filling pressure (E/e') and reduced right ventricular systolic function during exercise. Prognostic analyses were performed in the HFpEF cohort with follow-up data (N = 148). There were 37 primary composite events of all-cause death or worsening heart failure over a median follow-up of 935 days. Lower %VC was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint and remained associated in multivariable models. The %FEV₁ showed a weaker but concordant association.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower %VC and %FEV₁ were associated with reduced exercise capacity and hemodynamic derangements in the overall cohort and with worse clinical outcomes in patients with HFpEF.

articles.title: Multimodality imaging of the right heart: Translating quantitative assessment into therapeutic strategy.
articles.abstract: The right heart is a crucial determinant of prognosis across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular diseases, including pulmonary hypertension, tricuspid regurgitation, and heart failure. In the contemporary era of transcatheter device-based therapies, accurate assessment of right ventricular (RV) and right atrial anatomical and functional remodeling is critical for clinical decision-making. Although echocardiography remains the cornerstone of right heart evaluation, its interpretation is often limited by complex geometry of the RV and the load dependency of some parameters. Recent advances in multimodality imaging have enabled more robust and quantitative characterization of right heart structure and function. Three-dimensional echocardiography and RV strain provide improved functional assessment beyond conventional parameters of RV function. Cardiac magnetic resonance offers reference-standard quantification of RV volumes and mass, enhancing reproducibility and risk stratification. Computed tomography contributes complementary anatomical, functional and volumetric information, particularly relevant in structural heart interventions and evaluation of systemic venous congestion. Importantly, imaging biomarkers reflecting RV-pulmonary arterial coupling, atrial remodeling, and systemic venous congestion have demonstrated incremental prognostic value. Integration of these quantitative metrics into clinical practice may refine risk stratification, optimize timing of intervention, and identify patients unlikely to benefit from invasive therapies. This review summarizes contemporary advances in right heart imaging and proposes a practical framework for integrating echocardiography, Cardiac magnetic resonance, and computed tomography into therapeutic strategy in patients with right heart disease.

articles.title: Transgenerational responses of invasive cocklebur species to microplastic stress: Stage specificity and interspecific divergence.
articles.abstract: Microplastic pollution and plant invasions are converging threats to terrestrial ecosystems. Whether microplastics elicit adaptive transgenerational responses in invasive plants-rather than exerting uniform toxicity-remains untested. We hypothesize that parental microplastic exposure alters offspring performance, with the direction and magnitude of effects depending on polymer type, particle size, and abundance. Using a three-factor fully randomized design, we exposed three invasive cocklebur species (Cyclachaena xanthiifolia, Xanthium italicum, and Xanthium spinosum) to polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polypropylene (PP) at three sizes (5, 50, and 500 μm) and three abundances (519, 2074, and 4148 items kg-1), and quantified responses across parental life-history stages and F1 germination. Contemporary responses were stage-specific: germination in C. xanthiifolia and X. italicum was governed by three-way interactions, whereas later traits shifted toward polymer-type-dominated effects; X. spinosum showed size-dominated germination and type- or type × size-dependent later traits. Transgenerational effects diverged among species: C. xanthiifolia exhibited size-mediated F1 facilitation concurrent with type-driven parental inhibition; X. italicum showed direct, type-dependent facilitation; and X. spinosum showed no systematic transgenerational transmission. PLS-SEM supported these species-specific pathways. Because F1 performance was assayed only under control conditions, these patterns are consistent with-but do not demonstrate-a predictive adaptive response. Our results indicate that microplastics can act as species-specific modulators of invasive plant life histories across generations, highlighting the need to incorporate multi-factor, stage-specific, and transgenerational endpoints into microplastic risk assessment.

articles.title: Remote ischemic preconditioning protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury through lactate-dependent AMPK/ULK1 signaling and autophagy.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to ischemic cerebral damage and poor functional outcomes following ischemic stroke, and effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy. Using an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in PC12 cells and a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in rats, we demonstrate that I/R impairs autophagic flux, as evidenced by p62 accumulation and reduced LC3-II and Beclin-1 expression, leading to increased cellular apoptosis and injury. Lactate supplementation restored autophagic flux, enhanced cell viability, and suppressed apoptosis under OGD/R conditions. Mechanistically, lactate activated the AMPK/ULK1 signaling pathway, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK or ULK1 attenuated lactate-induced autophagy and cytoprotection. In vivo, RIPC elevated plasma and cerebral lactate levels, activated AMPK/ULK1 signaling, promoted autophagy, reduced infarct volume, and improved acute neurological outcomes. Notably, blockade of lactate transport or inhibition of AMPK/ULK1 signaling attenuated these protective effects. Collectively, our findings suggest that lactate serves as an important mediator of RIPC-induced neuroprotection and reveal a novel lactate-AMPK/ULK1-autophagy axis that mitigates cerebral I/R injury. These results provide mechanistic insight into RIPC and suggest potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: A contrastive decision transformer with TLA+ formal verification for sepsis treatment recommendation.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening disease with a high mortality rate, and its treatment involves multiple interventions, placing stringent demands on the timeliness and safety of clinical decision-making. Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated considerable potential in generative sequence modeling and decision recommendation tasks, providing a new paradigm for treatment decision-making in complex clinical settings. However, existing studies have mainly focused on improving long-term policy returns and offline evaluation performance, while lacking safety verification of decision outcomes. In addition, Decision Transformer often struggles to accurately achieve specified target returns because of limitations in target-return alignment. To address these issues, this study proposes a decision verification framework integrated with TLA+. An action-contrastive module is introduced into the original Decision Transformer, resulting in the proposed AC-DT model, which explicitly models the matching relationship between state contexts and actions through a contrastive loss, thereby enhancing the model's ability to distinguish among different treatment strategies. Furthermore, SHAP attribution analysis is employed to select key state variables, and the treatment trajectories generated by the model are abstracted into symbolic sequences with explicit clinical semantics to support TLA+ specification modeling and TLC model checking. Experimental results show that AC-DT achieves favorable estimated returns on MIMIC-III and in external evaluation on eICU. Moreover, the TLC model checker can effectively identify abnormal decision trajectories that violate predefined clinical safety properties.

articles.title: Genomic structural equation modeling elucidates the shared genetic architecture of vascular ageing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular ageing is a central driver of age-related cardiovascular morbidity and systemic ageing, encompassing arterial stiffening, hemodynamic alterations, subclinical atherosclerosis, and vascular calcification. The shared genetic architecture underlying these multidimensional phenotypes remains incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We applied genomic structural equation modeling (Genomic SEM) to GWAS summary statistics for five vascular-ageing traits in European-ancestry populations-arterial stiffness, pulse pressure, carotid artery thickness, coronary artery calcification, and carotid plaque. A common-factor model defined a latent vascular-ageing phenotype, followed by functional annotation, Bayesian fine-mapping, cross-tissue sCCA-TWAS with colocalization, pathway and cell-type enrichment, partitioned heritability, and polygenic risk score analyses.

RESULTS: The common-factor model showed good fit (CFI = 0.998; SRMR = 0.047). The resulting multivariate GWAS identified 372 independent lead SNPs across 249 genomic risk loci, including three loci newly implicated in vascular ageing. Bayesian fine-mapping prioritized 49 high-confidence causal SNPs, and transcriptomic prioritization (TWAS-FOCUS-colocalization) yielded 69 putative causal genes. Three-CDH13, FES, and CCN3-converged across MAGMA, fine-mapping, and TWAS evidence, implicating endothelial adhesion, vascular inflammation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Enrichment analyses highlighted the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, circulatory system processes, and extracellular matrix organization, implicating fibroblast-stromal compartments, smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells, and monocytes/macrophages as candidate cellular substrates.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first multivariate genomic characterization of vascular ageing using Genomic SEM, uncovering loci newly implicated in vascular ageing, convergent putative causal genes, and cellular substrates that link vascular biology to systemic ageing and may inform precision prevention of age-related vascular disorders.

articles.title: Association of Cognitive Frailty and Its Changes With Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Multimorbidity: Findings From the CHARLS Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical frailty has been linked to cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) multimorbidity, but the role of cognitive frailty and its dynamic changes in CKM progression remains unclear. We investigated the associations of baseline cognitive frailty and changes in cognitive frailty status with incident CKM multimorbidity.

METHODS: This cohort study included participants aged ≥45 years from the CHARLS (2011-2018). Cognitive frailty was classified as Robust, reversible cognitive frailty (RCF), or potentially reversible cognitive frailty (PRCF). A five-level score quantified the magnitude of cognitive change (Δscore). CKM multimorbidity was defined as ≥2 of cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disease. Cox models and trend tests estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Among 9,816 participants, 3,836 were included in baseline CKM analysis and 1,891 in transition analysis. Both RCF (HR=2.74, 95%CI:2.25-3.34) and PRCF (HR=2.51, 95%CI:1.96-3.21) were associated with increased CKM risk (both P<0.001). Cognitive status provided additional risk stratification beyond physical frailty. RCF-to-Robust improvement reduced CKM risk by 56% (HR=0.44, 95%CI:0.23-0.85, P=0.015), while deterioration markedly increased risk (HR≈5.3, P<0.001). The Δscore trend test showed a significant dose-response relationship (P<0.001). Substantial improvement (Δscore=-3) significantly reduced risk, whereas minor improvements showed protective trends without statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Cognitive frailty is independently associated with CKM multimorbidity progression. Within each direction of cognitive change, the magnitude of change provided additional prognostic information beyond direction alone.  These findings support the brain-CKM interconnection framework and suggest cognitive screening should be considered in CKM prevention strategies.

LAY SUMMARY: Cognitive frailty-a condition where physical decline and memory problems occur together-is common in older adults. In this study, we analysed data from nearly 10,000 middle-aged and older adults in China to understand whether cognitive frailty increases the risk of developing cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) multimorbidity, a cluster of conditions including heart disease, kidney disease, and diabetes. We found that people with cognitive frailty had significantly higher risks of developing CKM multimorbidity. More importantly, we found that the magnitude of change in cognitive function added prognostic information on top of its direction-greater worsening tracked with higher CKM risk. These findings suggest that monitoring changes in cognitive function over time could help identify individuals at high risk of CKM multimorbidity, and that interventions aimed at improving cognitive health may need to achieve meaningful improvement to reduce this risk.

articles.title: Surveillance of C. auris and Other Potentially Pathogenic Yeast Among Anesthesia Workspace Reservoirs, Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Candida auris has raised concern about fungal healthcare-associated infections in perioperative and critical care settings. We evaluated anesthesia workspaces to identify high-risk reservoirs and inform optimization of infection prevention practices.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicenter observational study of patients across 11 geographically dispersed U.S. hospitals from March 2023 to July 2025. A total of 6,074 reservoirs were sampled during 605 surgical cases and 273 consecutive operating room case pairs to detect C. auris and other potentially pathogenic yeast, including C. pseudohaemulonii, C. vulturna, C. diddensiae, C. metapsilosis, and Naganishia diffluens.

RESULTS: No anesthesia workspace reservoirs tested positive for C. auris (95% CI 0%-0.61% for surgical cases and 0-1.34% for case pairs). Other potentially pathogenic yeast (24 isolates) were detected in 1.16% (7/605) of cases. Most isolates were recovered from patient skin (92%), with fewer from environmental surfaces (4%) and practitioner hands (4%). Potential transmission patterns reflected known C. auris epidemiology, including patient-to-environment and patient-to-patient spread.

CONCLUSIONS: Outside outbreak settings, the anesthesia workspace for the studied population appears to be a low-risk reservoir for C. auris, making routine empirical environmental interventions such as high-dose ultraviolet-C irradiation difficult to justify. Surveillance for other potentially pathogenic yeast may provide a more practical approach to guide targeted infection prevention efforts.

articles.title: Longitudinal evaluation of a multidisciplinary infection prevention and control bundle in a high AMR prevalence ICU.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance is a major threat in intensive care units (ICUs). We evaluated changes associated with a multidisciplinary infection prevention and control (IPC) bundle in a high-AMR-prevalence setting.

METHODS: This longitudinal quasi-experimental ICU study (2022-2024) involved sequential, cumulative implementation of a bundle integrating infection prevention, rapid diagnostics and colonization screening, antimicrobial stewardship, and surveillance with data feedback.

RESULTS: Hand hygiene compliance increased from 29.5% at baseline to 64.6% during sustainment, while PPE compliance increased from 67.1% to 73.3% after monitoring was introduced. Piperacillin/tazobactam consumption increased (+3.33 DDD/100 patient-days per phase; 95% CI, 1.92-4.73), whereas colistin (-5.85; 95% CI, -9.17 to -2.54) and tigecycline (-2.50; 95% CI, -4.25 to -0.75) decreased. Klebsiella pneumoniae meropenem resistance decreased (OR per phase, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.43-0.69), whereas colistin resistance showed a borderline increase in Acinetobacter baumannii (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.00-1.65). ICU-acquired bloodstream infections decreased across implementation phases for CRE (IRR per phase, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.26-0.51) and CRAB (IRR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46-0.68), as did CLABSI (IRR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.56-0.73) and ICU-acquired rectal colonization with CRE (IRR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.63-0.84) and CRAB (IRR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.70-0.87), whereas CRPA ICU-acquired colonization increased (IRR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.32-1.85).

CONCLUSIONS: IPC bundle implementation was followed by improved IPC practices and reductions in several ICU-acquired infections and colonization outcomes; continued surveillance and stewardship are essential.

articles.title: Staged acellular perfusion, rewarming, and seamless transition to blood-based normothermic machine perfusion of the kidney: a paired porcine study.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) is a promising platform for assessment and treatment of kidneys prior to transplantation. Initial cool acellular perfusion with a graduated transition to normothermia might offer advantages over direct NMP reperfusion by 1) reducing ischaemia reperfusion injury, and 2) flushing donor-derived blood components from the microvasculature prior to the addition of red cells. 8 pairs of porcine kidneys were assigned randomly to up to 24 hours of NMP, or to an adapted protocol including initial sub-normothermic acellular (SNAP) and transition phases prior to NMP. Outcomes were assessed in six included pairs using injury markers (GST-Pi, IL-18, extracellular cardiolipin), NMP assessment metrics (urine production, vascular resistance), and histological and perfusate markers of microthrombosis, with comparison to human trial samples. Kidneys exposed to the intervention produced more urine but had higher vascular resistance and showed more evidence of mitochondrial injury, with no improvement in damage markers that in our human trial were correlated with outcome. Standard NMP provided better flush-out of donor derived intravascular debris, however the overall pre-perfusion burden of microvascular thrombosis was unexpectedly low, which was supported by analysis of human trial samples. Staged reperfusion by this protocol did not demonstrate an advantage compared to direct NMP.

articles.title: Hormone replacement after radiotherapy for premenopausal patients with cervical cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Radiotherapy is integral to cervical cancer management, but can cause iatrogenic premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) or early menopause, leading to vasomotor symptoms, sexual dysfunction, mood changes, and long-term health risks. Systemic menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is recommended to mitigate these effects in women with POI. Its role is physiologic hormone replacement, termed menopausal replacement therapy (MRT). This study assessed systemic MHT use and prescribing patterns in premenopausal patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer in British Columbia.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women aged 18-45 years, diagnosed with cervical cancer, and treated with curative intent primary or adjuvant radiotherapy between January 1 and December 31, 2022. Data was obtained from the BC Cancer Registry and extracted through chart review. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Fifty-one patients met inclusion criteria (median age 38 years). Most received primary chemoradiotherapy (86.3%), while 13.7% received adjuvant radiotherapy. Overall, 74.5% (n = 38/51) were prescribed MHT after treatment. The proportion of patients receiving MHT was higher among those treated with adjuvant radiotherapy compared to those who received primary chemoradiotherapy (85.7% vs. 72.7%, P = 0.66).
