Median time to first MHT prescription was 3.47 months after completing radiotherapy (range 2 weeks-2 years). All MHT prescriptions were provided following completion of radiotherapy. Among those prescribed MHT, 63.2% required dose escalation, 78.9% had formulation changes, 18.4% had dose reductions, and 18.4% discontinued therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Three quarters of patients were prescribed MHT. Initiation was delayed until after radiotherapy completion. Frequent dose and formulation adjustments highlight the complexity of survivorship care and the need for standardized counseling and management pathways to improve quality of life.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Abnormalities among Normal-Weight Adults: Prevalence and Associated Sociodemographic and Lifestyle Factors in a Large Spanish Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although body mass index (BMI) is widely used to assess obesity-related health risks, it may fail to detect individuals with normal weight who present with significant cardiometabolic abnormalities. This phenotype, often overlooked in clinical practice, is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence and determinants of cardiometabolic abnormalities in a large cohort of Spanish adults with normal BMI and to explore their associations with sociodemographic and lifestyle variables.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 163,254 workers aged 18-69 years who underwent occupational health examinations between 2021 and 2024. Only individuals with a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 kg/m² were included. Cardiometabolic abnormalities were defined as the presence of hypertension, dyslipidemia, or hyperglycemia. Sociodemographic data, smoking status, alcohol intake (measured in standard drinking units), physical activity (assessed with the IPAQ), and Mediterranean diet adherence (assessed using the MEDAS-14 questionnaire) were collected. Multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with the presence of one or more cardiometabolic abnormalities.

RESULTS: Among normal-weight adults, 49.0% presented at least one cardiometabolic abnormality. The prevalence was higher in men (54.3%) than in women (44.5%). Cardiometabolic risk was significantly higher among men, older individuals, smokers, those with low physical activity, poor adherence to the Mediterranean diet, and high alcohol consumption. Lower occupational social class was also associated with greater risk. The likelihood of presenting ≥1 cardiometabolic abnormality increased progressively with the accumulation of unhealthy lifestyle habits.

CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of normal-weight individuals exhibit cardiometabolic abnormalities, underscoring the need to move beyond BMI in clinical risk stratification. Preventive strategies should incorporate metabolic screening and lifestyle assessments for all individuals, regardless of weight status, to identify those at silent cardiometabolic risk.

articles.title: Scallops as an emerging platform toward functional reproductive endocrinology.
articles.abstract: Scallops have become one of the few molluscan systems in which reproductive endocrinology can be examined beyond descriptive molecular surveys. This review summarizes a series of studies that have progressively positioned scallops as an emerging experimental platform for advancing functional approaches in comparative reproductive endocrinology. Early work identified GnRH/CRZ-superfamily peptides and their receptors in scallops, showing that these ancient neuropeptide-GPCR modules are present in bivalves and may have multifunctional roles, but should not be interpreted as direct counterparts of the vertebrate hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Molecular analyses of sterol-related and nuclear-receptor-related pathways, together with sex-identification markers, further suggest that scallops provide a useful system for examining candidate mechanisms associated with gametogenesis, sex differentiation, and the stable maintenance of sexual phenotypes, without assuming vertebrate-type sex steroid regulation. At the cellular level, studies of germ cells and gonadal somatic cells have revealed the importance of the gonadal niche, whereas scallop hemocytes have emerged as experimentally accessible primary cells for cellular-level functional assays, rather than as established reproductive endocrine target cells. A major technical breakthrough has been the discovery and application of a strong OsHV-1 promoter, which has enabled transient transgene expression in scallop cells. Combined with primary hemocyte culture, this system has supported subcellular localization assays, recombinant protein production, and functional assessment of genes of interest, thereby providing a complementary route to gene function analysis in bivalves where individual-based functional genetics remains difficult. Despite current limitations, including low transfection efficiency, interindividual variability, and the limited extrapolation of hemocyte-based phenotypes to gonadal or organism-level reproductive physiology, scallop cell-based platforms provide a promising foundation for hypothesis-driven comparative endocrinology. These advances illustrate how non-model molluscs can be developed from observational subjects into experimentally testable systems, offering new perspectives on endocrine evolution, reproductive regulation, and physiological integration in marine invertebrates.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor: 'Association between dietary magnesium intake and all-cause mortality in patients with chronic kidney disease: Insights from NHANES 1999-2018'.
articles.abstract: Xu et al. (2026) reported that higher dietary magnesium was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality among adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD). This letter discusses some potential explanations for this association and explores some areas for further investigation. Firstly, the observations may partly reflect the importance of broader dietary and nutritional behaviours within this cohort. Secondly, further subgroup analysis of those with advanced CKD may elucidate the role of magnesium in this population. In particular, research should look to pair dietary intake with serum magnesium to understand if the observed association is also seen in the context of mild hypermagnesemia, which is more often seen in those with advanced CKD. Finally, engagement with dietary advice, follow-up and other aspects of chronic disease management may represent confounding factors. These considerations highlight the need for further research to clarify if the observed association is a specific effect of magnesium or representative of broader nutritional and health-related behaviours.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes and Trends in Simultaneous Liver-Kidney Transplantation: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Long-term outcomes after simultaneous liver-kidney transplantation (SLKT) are incompletely characterized. We aimed to estimate overall survival, survival with functioning grafts, kidney graft function over time, and temporal trends in SLKT practice.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective multicenter cohort of adults undergoing SLKT between 2003 and 2025 across 21 transplant centers in 7 Latin American countries. Overall survival and survival with functioning grafts were estimated up to 10 years after transplantation. Outcomes, recipient and donor characteristics were described across transplant eras.

RESULTS: Among 305 SLKT recipients, cirrhosis was the main liver indication (67.9%), whereas chronic kidney disease was the main renal indication (93.1%), most commonly due to polycystic kidney disease. Recipient profiles evolved over time toward greater metabolic burden, with more diabetes and MASLD, and increasing use of MELD exceptions - primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma - compared with earlier transplant eras. Overall survival was 78.5% at 1 year and 57.3% at 10 years, with 1-year survival exceeding 90% in 2022-2025; survival with functioning grafts was 77.4% and 50.9%, respectively. Early mortality predominated: 64% of deaths occurred in the first year, mainly due to bacterial infections (39%). Median eGFR among survivors remained in the mid-60s through 10 years.

CONCLUSIONS: SLKT achieved acceptable long-term patient, graft, and kidney function outcomes, with improved 1-year survival in recent eras. Early mortality remained concentrated in the first year and was often infection-related, highlighting an important target for post-transplant care as recipient metabolic complexity increases. These multicenter data provide long-term benchmarks to inform counseling and program planning amid an evolving metabolic burden.

articles.title: Physical Activity and Pregnancy Outcomes: An Observational Study of Greek Pregnant Women.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical Activity during pregnancy has been a controversial field for years, despite its widely proven benefits in general population. The benefits of PA in both mother and the fetus should be highlighted to provide new insights.

OBJECTIVE: Examine the association of PA in Greek pregnant women with pregnancy outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: This is a multicenter, prospective, observational study. The participants completed the Greek PPAQ and pregnancy outcomes were collected after birth. The level of PA and consistency with the international PA recommendations was evaluated with the use of METs. All pregnant women speaking greek fluently were eligible. The study was approved by the Ethical Committee of the University Hospital of Ioannina. Statistical analysis was conducted with the R program version 4.3.1. A regression analysis was also conducted for all pregnancy outcomes adjusted to potential cofounders.

RESULTS: A total of 915 pregnant women filled the PPAQ Greek version and were contacted postnatally for the outcomes. Neonates of active pregnant women had a lower median birthweight (3100 g vs 3170g, OR: 1.12, 95% CI:0.54- 2.11), lower incidence of admission to NICU (6.2% vs. 8.2%, OR: 0.76, 95% CI:0.33- 1.54) or neonatal complications (4.7% vs. 7.1%, OR: 0.64, 95% CI:0.24- 1.40). Moreover, pregnancy related hypertensive disorders and gestational diabetes mellitus were lower in the active group (0.01% vs. 3.8% OR: 0.20, 95% CI:0- 1.21 and 11.6% vs. 13.5%, OR: 0.85, 95% CI:0.46- 1.47 respectively). Vaginal delivery was more common in the active group (43% vs. 37.5% OR: 0.81, 95% CI:0.56- 1.19), as well as the incidence of PTB< 37 weeks (6.2% vs. 7.4%, OR: 0.84, 95% CI:0.36- 1.72). After adjusting for confounders, only birthweight differences were statistically significant (p = 0.036; 95% CI: -153, -5.5).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that PA during pregnancy is safe and beneficial for maternal-fetal health in several aspects of pregnancy outcomes. Clinicians should encourage incorporating PA in prenatal care in the absence of complications, while further studies using objective measures are needed to strengthen these findings.

articles.title: ASSESSMENT OF TREATMENT RESPONSE RESPONSE AND THE ROLE OF COMPLETION SURGERY AFTER CONCURRENT CRTAND BRACHYTHERAPY FOR LOCALLY ADVANCED CERVICAL CANCER - A REVIEW FROM THE FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP.
authors: members from the FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by brachytherapy is the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer. However, post-treatment management remains challenging. Accurate response assessment is essential because it informs subsequent management, particularly the indication for completion surgery. Radiation-induced tissue changes may impair the reliability of clinical examination and conventional imaging, while the respective roles of advanced imaging modalities and completion surgery remain debated. Functional lumbopelvic MRI incorporating diffusion-weighted and perfusion sequences is the reference imaging modality for response assessment and provides greater diagnostic performance than clinical examination alone. FDG PET-CT offers complementary information, particularly regarding nodal disease and early metabolic response, but the routine combination of FDG PET-CT with MRI has not been shown to improve diagnostic accuracy. MRI performed early during CRT may help differentiate responders from nonresponders based on changes in the apparent diffusion coefficient. However, the optimal timing of MRI after treatment completion remains uncertain. Available evidence does not support the routine use of conization for response assessment. Completion surgery provides no prognostic benefit and increases morbidity in patients with squamous cell carcinoma who achieve a complete response after CRT and brachytherapy. Evidence remains insufficient to establish its role in adenocarcinoma. When completion surgery is indicated, delaying the procedure until at least 6-8 weeks after CRT may reduce postoperative morbidity. Simple hysterectomy should be favored over radical hysterectomy, which increases morbidity without improving survival. Current evidence demonstrates no superiority of minimally invasive surgery or laparotomy in terms of oncologic outcomes or overall morbidity.

articles.title: Validity Evidence for the Competency-Based Leadership Assessment Resource (CLAR) Tool in Assessing Pediatric Fellows.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Our goal was to obtain validity evidence (response process, internal structure, and relationship to other variables) for a novel Competency-based Leadership Assessment Resource (CLAR) tool for providing formative assessments of pediatric subspecialty fellows.

METHOD: Faculty from 49 U.S. pediatric fellowships completed assessments over 2 cycles (2021-2022). Faculty and program directors provided feedback on content, value, and ease of use. Internal structure was assessed through Cronbach's alpha. Generalizability theory analysis explored sources of variance. Correlations were measured between the CLAR score and ACGME leadership Milestones levels, and supervision levels for the "Leading an Interprofessional Healthcare Team" Entrustable Professional Activity (EPA). Relationships between CLAR score and other variables were examined using linear mixed effect regression models.

RESULTS: 288 faculty provided 1,035 assessments on 266 fellows over 2 cycles. The median number of assessments per fellow in each cycle was 3 (IQR 3-3 Cycle 1, IQR 2-3 Cycle 2). Fellowship training year was evenly distributed (34% 1st, 35% 2nd, 30% 3rd-5th). Critical care, child abuse, and hospital medicine were the most common subspecialties. Most program directors rated the tool as valuable. Faculty found the tool easy to use. Internal consistency was high (alpha 0.97). The greatest sources of variance were the fellow (34%), faculty in a program (17%), and subspecialty (11%). Correlation between the CLAR score and the EPA supervision levels and leadership-related Milestones were positive. Scores also increased with time in training.

DISCUSSION: The validity evidence for the CLAR tool supports use in formative assessment of pediatric fellows.

articles.title: Scoping Review of Education on Palliative and End-of-Life Care for Health Care Professionals in the NICU.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the published literature on education for neonatal palliative care and end-of-life care for NICU personnel and to identify educational needs and key components of existing education programs.

DATA SOURCES: Medline (OVID), Embase (OVID), Emcare (OVID), PsycINFO (OVID), and CINAHL (EBSCO).

STUDY SELECTION: Two reviewers independently screened 2,791 records and 144 full text reports for inclusion. We included 23 reports of original research studies in which researchers focused on educational needs or the provision of education for health care staff who worked in the NICU.

DATA EXTRACTION: We extracted the following data from each included study: author(s), publication year, country, aims, study design, methods, sample, data collection method, learning needs, educational interventions, intervention characteristics (including content, delivery mode, and duration), and key study findings. We compiled data in an Excel spreadsheet, organized them according to study characteristics and intervention themes, and described them narratively.

DATA SYNTHESIS: We identified pain and symptom management, communication, and caring for the dying infant as educational needs. Education interventions comprised face-to-face workshops, online modules, case-based discussions, and PowerPoint presentations. Outcome evaluations primarily focused on self-reported confidence, knowledge, and perceived competence rather than objective changes in clinical practice or family experiences.

CONCLUSION: The evidence base for education on neonatal palliative and end-of-life care for NICU staff remains limited and fragmented. Current initiatives may lack relevance, specificity, or practical applicability. If education is approached solely from a professional perspective, it might not reflect family-centered care principles. The development of theory-informed program evaluation is needed to ensure that training effectively addresses practical and emotional complexities of neonatal palliative care.

articles.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)(⁎)
American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)(⁎)
Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL)
Latin American Association for the Study of the Liver (ALEH)
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA)
articles.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

articles.title: Workup of Encephalopathy in Patients Receiving Cancer Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed many areas of oncologic care. Neurological immune-related adverse events, particularly encephalopathy, represent potentially life-threatening complications requiring prompt recognition and intervention. Encephalopathic syndromes occur across immunotherapy modalities, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor-T cell therapy, and bispecific antibodies. The diagnostic challenge lies in distinguishing immune-mediated neurotoxicity from infection, metabolic derangements, disease progression, and paraneoplastic syndromes. A systematic evaluation incorporates detailed clinical assessment with neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, electroencephalography, and autoimmune antibody testing as appropriate. This review provides a practical approach to recognizing and assessing encephalopathy in patients receiving immunotherapy. Early multidisciplinary collaboration between neurology and oncology teams is critical for recognizing symptoms, managing adverse effects, and guiding cancer-directed treatment.

articles.title: Integrating UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and Network Pharmacology to Reveal the Mechanism of Jinbei Oral Liquid in Radiation-Induced Lung Injury with Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) with pulmonary hypertension (PAH) commonly arises in advanced radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) stages. Jinbei Oral Liquid (JBOL) has certified in clinical studies to enhance pulmonary function indicators and 6MWD in PF patients. The clinical improvement impact on the comorbidity is obvious while its molecular mechanism remains unclear. In this study, Active fraction identification in lung tissues was conducted using UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. Potential targets of effective active compounds were predicted using TCMSP, SwissTargetPrediction, HERB, GeneCards and DrugBank. JBOL and RILI-PAH targets were obtained from GeneCards, DisGeNET, Harmonizome and GEO dataset. The herb-pathway-target-disease network and PPI of intersection targets were constructed using STRING and Cytoscape. We further performed GO and KEGG enrichment analysis on these targets. Molecular docking was performed to validate the docking activity of the core active compounds and targets. We tentatively annotated 34 prototype lung-inhaled components via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. Network pharmacology may potentially alleviate RILI-PAH by utilizing active compounds like Daidzein, Calycosin, Cnidilide, Glycyrrhetinic acid, Hesperidin, Liquiritigenin, and Protocatechualdehyde to modulate targets such as PGF, IGF1, MMP9, MMP8, CCR1, ALOX5AP, and CCND1, and influence signaling pathways like PI3K-Akt, AGE-RAGE, and HIF-1. This intervention could impact inflammatory responses, promote cell migration and motility, and influence cellular reactions to nitrogen compounds. The molecular docking results showed that hesperdin, daidzein, calycosin and Glycyrrhetinic acid have higher affinity with CCR1, MMP8 and ALOX5AP. The results suggest that JBOL may treats RILI-PAH through multiple components and pathways, providing a clinical reference for the principle of treating different diseases with the same method.

Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.

METHODS: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).

FINDINGS: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group).

INTERPRETATION: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.

FUNDING: Eli Lilly and Company.

TRANSLATION: For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]).

FINDINGS: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups.

INTERPRETATION: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes.

FUNDING: BreakthroughT1D, German Research Foundation (DFG), German Center for Diabetes Research (DZD), Schmutzler Stiftung, German Federal Ministry of Health, Ministry of Culture and Science of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia, and German Federal Ministry of Education and Research.

TRANSLATION: For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy (SIC) Update 2026: Simplifying the Diagnosis and Dynamic Monitoring of Sepsis-Associated DIC.
articles.abstract: Coagulation abnormalities are a fundamental component of sepsis pathophysiology and contribute directly to organ dysfunction and mortality. The sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) criteria, introduced in 2017 by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH), represented a major advance by providing a practical framework for identifying early sepsis-associated coagulopathy and predicting progression to overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). However, after nearly a decade of clinical experience, several limitations have become apparent. In particular, incorporation of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score complicates bedside application and blurs the distinction between coagulation-specific abnormalities and global illness severity. The newly proposed SIC-2 removes the SOFA component and relies exclusively on platelet count and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio (PT-INR), thereby preserving conceptual clarity and improving feasibility. Emerging evidence suggests that SIC-2 maintains the ability to identify patients at risk of developing DIC while simplifying serial monitoring. Although an effective anticoagulant therapy for sepsis has not yet been established, serial assessment of coagulation trajectories may facilitate risk stratification. Whether changes in SIC-2 can identify patients likely to benefit from anticoagulant therapy or determine the optimal timing of treatment remains an important hypothesis that requires prospective validation. This perspective discusses the evolution from the original SIC criteria to SIC-2 and considers the future role of coagulation monitoring in sepsis-associated DIC.

articles.title: The Role of Oxygen Therapy in Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Pulmonary Diseases.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is a major cause of hospitalization, respiratory failure, and mortality worldwide. The pathophysiological complexity of AECOPD, characterized by ventilation-perfusion mismatch, alveolar hypoventilation, dynamic hyperinflation, respiratory muscle dysfunction, and carbon dioxide retention, underscores the pivotal role of oxygen therapy in respiratory support. However, oxygen administration in AECOPD extends beyond the correction of hypoxemia, as excessive oxygen supplementation may precipitate oxygen-induced hypercapnia and worsen clinical outcomes. Consequently, individualized oxygen delivery strategies that balance adequate oxygenation with ventilatory support have become an essential component of contemporary AECOPD management. This review summarizes the physiological rationale, mechanisms of action, clinical evidence, advantages, and limitations of the three principal oxygen delivery modalities currently used in AECOPD, namely conventional oxygen therapy (COT), noninvasive ventilation (NIV), and high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC). COT remains the preferred initial strategy for patients with isolated hypoxemia when oxygen is carefully titrated to achieve guideline-recommended oxygen saturation targets. NIV continues to represent the first-line respiratory support modality for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure because of its well-established ability to improve alveolar ventilation, reduce respiratory muscle workload, correct respiratory acidosis, and decrease intubation and mortality. HFNC has emerged as an important complementary modality by providing stable oxygen delivery, anatomical dead-space washout, low-level positive airway pressure, and heated humidification, thereby improving oxygenation, secretion clearance, and patient comfort. Nevertheless, current evidence does not support replacing NIV with HFNC in patients with moderate-to-severe hypercapnic respiratory failure. Future respiratory support strategies should move beyond a one-size-fits-all approach toward precision oxygen therapy guided by pathophysiological phenotyping, respiratory mechanics, neural respiratory drive, and dynamic physiological monitoring. Integrating evidence-based respiratory support modalities with individualized physiological assessment may further optimize outcomes and represents the future direction of AECOPD management.

articles.title: Metabolic endotyping for mechanism-informed Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease trials.
articles.abstract: Metabolically targeted therapies for Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease have yielded mixed results despite convergent evidence implicating three interconnected axes of metabolic dysfunction: insulin signaling, cellular bioenergetics, and lipid-lysosomal biology. We argue that this pattern partly reflects a trial-design problem: therapeutics such as glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, terazosin, and stearoyl-CoA desaturase inhibitors generally have been tested in biologically unselected populations, with endpoints often distal to the targeted mechanism. We propose as a testable hypothesis that a metabolic endotype-a measurable, biomarker-supported pattern of metabolic dysfunction-spans subsets of both diseases and that failure to enrich for this endotype could dilute therapeutic signals in all-comer trials. We outline a modular four-tier framework integrating prodromal risk, metabolic vulnerability, pathway-specific confirmation, and mechanistic deep phenotyping to make Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease trials more interpretable and therapeutically informative.

articles.title: Association of Neutrophil-to-Prognostic Nutritional Index Ratio With Prognosis in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Gastric Procedures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inflammation and malnutrition frequently coexist in critically ill patients, yet single inflammatory or nutritional indices capture only part of this state. We examined how the preoperative neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio (NPNI), a composite of both, relates to mortality across follow-up in patients undergoing gastric procedures.

METHODS: We studied 1821 adults in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV database who underwent a gastric procedure. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included 15-d, 30-d, 60-d, 90-d, 1-y, 3-y, and 5-y mortality. Logistic regression, time-window Cox models, and landmark analysis were used to assess the association between NPNI and mortality. Receiver operating characteristic curves were generated to calculate the area under the curve. The signal source of NPNI was explored through interaction analysis between the inflammatory axis (neutrophils) and the nutritional axis (Onodera Prognostic Nutritional Index).

RESULTS: Higher NPNI was associated with greater odds of death at every horizon (per 1 standard deviation, odds ratio (OR)in-hospital = 1.24, 95% confidence interval: 1.10-1.40; OR5-y = 1.28, 95% confidence interval: 1.15-1.42). NPNI demonstrated "cross-temporal stability," maintaining significant associations in both the early mortality (0-30 d) and late mortality (30 d-5 y) windows. Time-window analysis revealed that the nutritional axis was associated with early mortality (heart rate = 0.81, P = 0.032), while the inflammatory axis was associated with late mortality (heart rate = 1.13, P < 0.001). The interaction between the two axes was subadditive (relative excess risk due to interaction = -0.32). NPNI showed modest discriminative ability (area under the curve: 0.568), inferior to Simplified Acute Physiology Score II (0.647) and Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score (0.625).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated NPNI is an independent risk factor for mortality in critically ill patients undergoing gastric procedures. Its value lies in cross-temporal risk integration rather than discriminative ability.

articles.title: Prevention of Abdominal Compartment Syndrome in Acute Care Surgery: A Scoping Review of Risk Factors and Management Strategies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) is a life-threatening complication of sustained intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) that can lead to organ dysfunction and substantial morbidity and mortality. Early identification and prevention are critical to limiting progression. This scoping review evaluates risk factors and preventive and therapeutic strategies for ACS in acute care surgical populations.

METHODS: This scoping review systematically searched PubMed, Cochrane, and ProQuest, supplemented by a search of the ScienceDirect full-text platform, to identify studies evaluating preventive and early-intervention strategies for ACS in acute care surgery populations through April 2026.

RESULTS: Twelve studies were included. Preventive surgical strategies were associated with decreases in intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) and ACS progression. Percutaneous catheter decompression reported a statistically significant decrease in IAP (P = 0.001), whereas prophylactic decompressive laparotomy was associated with a decrease in IAP from 24.4 ± 8.5 mmHg to 13.4 ± 4.0 mmHg (P < 0.0001). Reduced crystalloid resuscitation was associated with a lower incidence of ACS (7.4% in 2006 versus 0% in 2011, P < 0.001) and lower mortality (22.8% versus 10.6%, P < 0.001). Independent risk factors for the development of ACS included abdominal distention (odds ratio [OR]: 4.951, P < 0.001), obesity (body mass index >30; OR: 3.413, P < 0.001), positive fluid balance, and elevated base deficit. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality (OR: 1.09, P = 0.017). Limited evidence suggested early enteral nutrition may reduce the progression of IAH without increasing IAP.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe injury burden, prolonged IAH, obesity, abdominal distention, positive fluid balance, and aggressive crystalloid resuscitation were consistently associated with increased ACS risk. Preventive strategies, including balanced resuscitation, routine IAP monitoring, early enteral nutrition, and timely decompressive interventions, were associated with lower ACS incidence and improved outcomes.

articles.title: Differential expression of lung-homing chemokine receptors in severe COVID-19: distinct profiles between Alpha and Omicron.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), is characterized by excessive pulmonary immune cell recruitment mediated by chemokine - chemokine receptor signaling. Variant-specific differences in lung-homing chemokine receptor expression remain insufficiently defined.

METHODS: This retrospective case-control study analyzed Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid (BALF) samples from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admitted patients with severe COVID-19 during the Alpha (hICU-α) and Omicron (hICU-Ο) waves, along with SARS-CoV-2 - negative controls. Messenger RNA expression of CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CCR2, and CCR6 was quantified by Real-Time quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR). Protein expression of selected receptors was assessed by western blotting in available samples.

RESULTS: CXCR1 expression was significantly increased in hICU-α patients compared with controls (p = 0.02) but not in hICU-Ο patients. CXCR2 expression was elevated in both hICU-α and hICU-Ο groups versus controls (p = 0.008 and p = 0.006, respectively) and was higher in hICU-α than hICU-Ο patients (p = 0.009). CXCR3 expression was increased in both COVID-19 groups compared with controls (p = 0.03 and p = 0.001). CCR6 expression was highest in hICU-Ο patients compared with hICU-α and controls (p = 0.04 and p = 0.001). Increased CXCR2 and CXCR3 protein expression was confirmed in hICU-Ο patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe COVID-19 is associated with variant-specific alterations in lung chemokine receptor expression, highlighting differential immune trafficking patterns during Alpha and Omicron waves.

articles.title: Towards modeling the hemodynamic impact of mitral and aortic valve repair in patients with left ventricular assist devices.
articles.abstract: Valve dysfunction is a major threat to long-term success in left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy, with direct implications for right heart performance. In this study, we apply a patient-specific, image-based computational modeling framework to evaluate the hemodynamic impact of simulated mitral and aortic valve repair in five LVAD-supported patients. Each patient was modeled under four conditions: (patient-specific LVAD-supported state), simulated mitral valve (MV) repair, simulated aortic valve (AV) repair, and simulated combined MV&AV repair. Because validation data for valve repair were unavailable, the simulated repair scenarios are exploratory in silico interventions based on clinically validated patient-specific models. The models integrate dynamic CT imaging, echocardiography, catheterization data, and device-specific LVAD parameters into a coupled 3D-0D simulation pipeline. Valve dynamics are governed by transvalvular pressure and flow, allowing physiological modeling of regurgitant lesions and surgical repair. The right ventricular (RV) was assessed using a combination of model-derived metrics, including right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi), and RV-PA coupling. In addition, we performed blood residence time (RT) analysis to evaluate blood stasis within the left heart and aorta. The simulations suggest that valve repair improved cardiac output, reduced pulmonary congestion, and enhanced right ventricular loading conditions. Notably, mitral valve repair restored aortic valve opening during the cardiac cycle, which improved sinus washout and reduced blood residence time within the aortic root-factors associated with lower thrombotic risk. Overall, these findings suggest a potential role for valve repair in LVAD-supported hearts, though larger, validated patient cohorts are needed to confirm these results.

articles.title: Gut microbial functional associations with subsequent irritable bowel syndrome in a prospective, paediatric case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The infant gut microbiome undergoes rapid maturation that shapes lifelong gastrointestinal health. Although adults with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) show characteristic microbial and metabolic alterations, it remains unclear whether these differences precede disease onset. Here, microbiome composition and function in infancy were prospectively associated with future IBS development.

METHODS: Stool samples collected from the All Babies in Southeast Sweden (ABIS) cohort at a mean age of 12.4 (±1.5) months, were analysed using a nested case-control design. Cases included future IBS and/or pelvic and abdominal pain, with the average time between age at stool collection and diagnosis being 11.8 (±5.2) years and a mean age at diagnosis of 12.8 (±5.2) years. Microbial composition was profiled with 16S rRNA gene sequencing (n = 396). Data were processed with DADA2, taxonomically assigned using SILVA database, and predicted functionally with PICRUSt2. Descriptive statistics were analysed using χ2 or Fisher's exact test, global differences with PERMANOVA, differential abundance with ANCOM-BC2, and pathway enrichment with GSEA.

FINDINGS: Infants with future IBS risk demonstrated microbial divergence, marked by depletion of short-chain fatty acid producers and expansion of facultative and mucosa-disruptive taxa. Inferred functional profiles exhibited reduced fermentative capacity, greater respiratory potential, accelerated degradation of neuroactive aromatic amines, and case-enrichment of cytochrome bc1 complex respiratory unit.

INTERPRETATION: Gut microbiome dysbiosis in infants with IBS risk is present many years prior to diagnosis and includes early disruptions in fermentation, redox balance, and amine metabolism that potentially compromise epithelial resilience and promote visceral hypersensitivity. Early detection of microbiome dysbiosis suggests probiotic-based interventions.

FUNDING: Barndiabetesfonden; Swedish Council for Working Life and Social Research; Swedish Research Council; Östgöta Brandstodsbolag; Medical Research Council of Southeast Sweden; JDRF-Wallenberg Foundation; Linköping University; Horizon Europe INITIALISE grant.

articles.title: Climate change and declining reproductive efficiency in dairy cattle: Global trends and adaptive solutions.
articles.abstract: Climate change is progressively limiting reproductive efficiency in dairy cattle, which has significant consequences for productivity, profitability and global food security. Increasing ambient temperatures, increased temperature-humidity index (THI), recurrent heat waves and climatic variability interfere with reproduction via interconnected endocrine, metabolic and cellular pathways. Heat stress affects the activity of the HPA and HPG axes, leading to increased cortisol levels, altered gonadotropin secretion, disruption of follicular dynamics and compromised luteal progesterone support. At the cellular and molecular levels, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, heat shock protein responses and genomic-epigenetic alterations diminish oocyte competence, compromise sperm integrity and hinder early embryonic development, often resulting in embryonic loss and pregnancy failure. While Bos indicus and other climate-adapted genotypes show improved thermotolerance, there remains significant variability among individuals regarding reproductive resilience. This review combines global and regional evidence to clarify the mechanisms behind climate-induced reproductive decline and assesses adaptive strategies such as heat-abatement management, nutritional interventions, timed artificial insemination (TAI), assisted reproductive technologies, genetic selection for heat tolerance and precision monitoring. These insights collectively offer a framework for maintaining dairy reproductive performance considering future climate scenarios.

articles.title: FOXM1/LncRNA COPD-R regulates pulmonary inflammation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease induced by biomass-related PM2.5.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is closely associated with biomass fuel (BMF) exposure. Biomass-related PM2.5 (BRPM2.5), a fine particulate component of BMF smoke, may contribute to BMF-associated pulmonary inflammation, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role of the FOXM1/lncRNA COPD-R axis in BRPM2.5-induced pulmonary inflammatory responses. A BMF-induced COPD rat model was established, followed by lung tissue RNA sequencing. Rat L2 cells were treated with lncRNA COPD-R knockdown or overexpression with or without BRPM2.5 exposure. qPCR, FISH, Western blotting, ELISA, ChIP, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to assess lncRNA COPD-R expression, localization, inflammatory responses and transcriptional regulation. After 7 months of BMF exposure in rats, 312 differentially expressed lncRNAs were identified, including 294 upregulated and 18 downregulated transcripts. lncRNA COPD-R expression increased from 0.1505 ± 0.04259 in controls to 1.054 ± 0.2983 in the BMF group (P < 0.01). RNA sequencing of L2 cells following lncRNA COPD-R knockdown revealed enrichment of differentially expressed genes in the IL-17 and other inflammatory signaling pathways. Transcription factor prediction, ChIP and dual-luciferase assays supported FOXM1-mediated transcriptional regulation of lncRNA COPD-R through promoter binding. BRPM2.5 increased lncRNA COPD-R expression, whereas lncRNA COPD-R knockdown reduced BRPM2.5-induced CCL2, IL-17F, MMP-9 and TIMP-1 expression. FOXM1 knockdown or overexpression affected lncRNA COPD-R expression and inflammatory responses, whereas lncRNA COPD-R overexpression rescued these effects following FOXM1 knockdown. Collectively, our findings provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying BRPM2.5-induced pulmonary inflammation and suggest that the FOXM1/lncRNA COPD-R axis may play an important role in this process.

articles.title: Fertility and family-building in sickle cell disease: A qualitative analysis of hematologist perspectives.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract: As survival for people with sickle cell disease (SCD) improves, fertility and family-building have become increasing priorities. This shift is especially important with the broader use of disease-modifying treatments that impact fertility. This qualitative study assessed pediatric hematologists' perspectives and practices regarding adolescents with SCD who may have fertility and family-building concerns. We interviewed 20 hematology providers about their roles, perceived barriers and facilitators, and recommendations for reproductive healthcare for adolescents with SCD. Ten participants (n = 5 men; n = 5 women; n = 5 within 5 years post-fellowship) specifically discussed fertility and family-building. We transcribed the interviews and coded them using applied thematic analysis. Three major themes emerged: the impact of disease-modifying, curative, and transformative therapies; patient-level factors that influence the timing and scope of fertility discussions; and the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration. Participants described uncertainty about the evidence surrounding fertility risks of treatments and the need to balance these with health benefits, patient age, and their care journey. Conversations about fertility and family-building in SCD are nuanced and benefit from multidisciplinary expertise. Future work should create standardized, age-based counseling and train clinic teams to address fertility concerns among adolescents with SCD.

articles.title: Depressive Symptoms and 6-Year KCCQ Health Status in Chronic Heart Failure: Findings From the Cognition.Matters-HF Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term disease-specific health status trajectories in ambulatory chronic heart failure (HF) are incompletely characterized, and the contribution of depressive symptoms remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize 6-year Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OSS) trajectories and distinguish persistent and visit-specific depressive symptom associations with health status.

METHODS: In the prospective Cognition.Matters-HF cohort, 148 patients with HF underwent assessments at baseline and 6, 12, 36, and 69 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated KCCQ-OSS trajectories and prespecified correlates. Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores were decomposed into between-person and within-person components. Sensitivity analyses addressed missingness, and exploratory lagged analyses assessed whether recent PHQ-9 worsening predicted subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.

RESULTS: KCCQ-OSS remained stable over 69 months (78.0-76.6; change: -1.4; 95% CI: -4.6 to 1.8; P for time = 0.065), despite substantial individual variation. Higher between-person PHQ-9 burden (β: -3.44 per point; 95% CI: -4.00 to -2.88; P < 0.001) and within-person PHQ-9 worsening (β: -1.80; 95% CI: -2.50 to -1.11; P < 0.001) were associated with lower concurrent KCCQ-OSS. Recent PHQ-9 worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ-OSS, a ≥5-point KCCQ decline, or all-cause death/HF hospitalization. NYHA functional class and 6-min walking distance, but not N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, left ventricular ejection fraction, or executive function, were independently associated with KCCQ-OSS.

CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory chronic HF, average KCCQ-based health status remained stable over 6 years despite substantial individual variation. Depressive symptoms were strongly associated with concurrent health status, but recent worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.

articles.title: Pharmacological profiling reveals sensitivity of vitamin D/TGF-β cooperative gene regulation to epigenetic and transcription-associated inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Synergistic gene regulation by the active vitamin D metabolite, 1,25(OH)2D3 and transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) has been reported for a limited number of target genes. Among these, 5-lipoxygenase (5-LO), a key enzyme in leukotriene biosynthesis and innate immune signaling, represents a well-established example of this cooperative regulation. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this synergy between vitamin D and TGF-β remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the involvement of chromatin-associated and transcriptional regulators in 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β mediated gene regulation in monocytic cell lines. Pharmacological perturbation revealed sensitivity of the cooperative response to inhibition of epigenetic regulators, including class I histone deacetylases (HDACs), bromodomain-containing proteins (BRDs), as well as molecular chaperone heat shock protein (HSP90) and transcriptional/signaling kinases such as cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 9 and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs). Further analysis demonstrated differential regulation of ALOX5 (5-LO), CD14 (CD14) and CXCL8 (interleukin-8 (IL-8)) upon modulation of these regulatory pathways in the monocytic cell lines MonoMac-6 and THP-1. RNA-Sequencing identified additional genes synergistically regulated by combined 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β stimulation that were enriched for immune-related functions and displayed similar sensitivity to pharmacological disruption of transcriptional and chromatin regulatory mechanisms. Furthermore, VDR knockout experiments demonstrated that intact VDR signaling is required for 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β mediated cooperative gene regulation. These findings reveal a broader set of immune-associated genes regulated by 1,25(OH)2D3/TGF-β cooperation and identify chromatin and transcriptional regulators as important modulators of this response in monocytic cells.

articles.title: Urinary tract and genital infections with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin across type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease: An indication- and sex-stratified disproportionality analysis of eudravigilance reports.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), chronic heart failure (CHF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although their cardiovascular and renal benefits are well established, urogenital infections remain a relevant safety concern. Comparative post-marketing data on dapagliflozin (DAPA) and empagliflozin (EMPA) across therapeutic indications are limited. A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis of the EudraVigilance database (January 2021-July 2025) was conducted using a case/non-case approach. Cases were defined as individual case safety reports (ICSRs) containing at least one urogenital infection-coded reaction and a confirmed indication (T2DM, CHF, or CKD). The primary analysis was restricted to reports originating from the European Economic Area (EEA), where reporting rules are identical for both drugs; reports with unspecified patient age were excluded. Among 16,102 EEA ICSRs, 8156 adult reports with a confirmed indication were analyzed, of which 1109 met the case definition. Non-EEA reports were analyzed separately as a sensitivity analysis. Urogenital infection reporting did not differ between DAPA and EMPA, overall (ROR 0.91; 95% CI 0.80-1.03) or within any indication (T2DM: 13.9% vs 14.9%, ROR 0.92; 95% CI 0.79-1.07; CHF: 11.5% vs 12.6%, ROR 0.90; 95% CI 0.69-1.18; CKD: 11.0% vs 6.7%, ROR 1.73; 95% CI 0.75-3.99). For both drugs, reporting was higher in T2DM than in CHF (DAPA ROR 1.25; 95% CI 1.00-1.56; EMPA ROR 1.22; 95% CI 0.99-1.51), a difference confined to female patients (DAPA 1.38; EMPA 1.56) and, in the endpoint disaggregation, to genital mycotic infections (DAPA 2.24; EMPA 1.79) rather than non-mycotic urogenital infections. Female sex was the strongest determinant of urogenital infection reporting for both drugs (ROR female/male 1.85 for DAPA and 1.58 for EMPA). In non-EEA reports, an apparent excess of urogenital infection reporting with DAPA over EMPA (ROR 1.85; 95% CI 1.59-2.16) was explained by a different composition of the reports forwarded for the two drugs rather than by a drug effect. Urogenital infection reporting with SGLT2 inhibitors depends on indication and sex rather than on the molecule, and between-drug comparisons in EudraVigilance are sensitive to the geographic origin of reports.

articles.title: Metformin and Thrombosis in MPNs: A Cautious Interpretation.
Levosimendan and Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning: Still an Open Question?

articles.title: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931): cytoarchitectonic roots of modern network neuroscience.
articles.abstract: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931) is widely remembered for his seminal description of encephalitis lethargica, yet his broader contribution to cortical organization remains underappreciated. Beyond clinical neurology, von Economo and Georg Koskinas, a neurologist-psychiatrist, contributed to the broader cytoarchitectonic tradition by developing one of the most detailed architectonic frameworks of the human cerebral cortex, emphasizing laminar heterogeneity, regional transition, and structural specialization. These concepts can be reconsidered in relation to contemporary models of large-scale brain organization. In particular, cortical territories associated with von Economo's work, including the anterior insula and anterior cingulate region, are now recognized as key hubs in salience processing and contain the distinctive spindle-shaped neurons later termed von Economo neurons. Recent advances in connectomics, cortical gradient mapping, and laminar neuroimaging have renewed interest in the relationship between cortical microstructure and distributed functional networks. From this perspective, von Economo's work may be viewed not simply as a landmark in classical neuroanatomy, but as a historically important structural framework that can be reinterpreted in relation to modern ideas of structure-function coupling and network-level brain organization. This historical vignette revisits his life, scientific contributions, and enduring relevance to contemporary neuroscience and neurosurgical thinking.

articles.title: Outcomes and Complications of Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Axillary intra-aortic balloon pump (axi-IABP) support has emerged as an alternative to femoral access for patients with advanced heart failure, offering improved mobility and potential benefits in pretransplant conditioning; however, data on associated complications remain limited. We conducted a retrospective study of 55 patients who underwent axi-IABP placement between January 2019 and July 2025 at our institution. The cohort had a median age of 59 (interquartile range [IQR], 52-65) years and presented with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Axi-IABP successfully bridged 87.3% of patients to advanced therapies. A total of 83 complications were identified in 60.0% of patients, most commonly malposition in 23.6% of patients, gas leak alarms in 16.4% of patients, and kinking in 16.4% of patients. Serious vascular complications were infrequent. The median time to first complication was 10.5 (IQR, 2.75-25.5) days. Female sex was associated with a higher hazard of first complication when controlled for height (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04-7.27; p = 0.041). In conclusion, axi-IABP is an effective bridging strategy that enhances patient mobility but is associated with a high rate of device-related complications, predominantly mechanical in nature, underscoring the importance of careful patient selection and monitoring.

articles.title: Optimizing remote mechanical thrombectomy training using causal machine learning: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Remote, live-streamed mechanical thrombectomy (MT) training is a novel educational strategy, but its impact on patient outcomes remains unclear. The authors aimed to move beyond average treatment effects to identify which clinician subgroups derive the most significant clinical gains from cumulative training exposure.

METHODS: In this prospective multicenter cohort study, 1010 clinicians participated in standardized, live-streamed MT training. The authors applied causal inference techniques, including double/debiased machine learning (DML), causal forest analysis, and Bayesian mixed-effects models, to evaluate the impact of cumulative training hours on 90-day patient outcomes. A Bayesian generalized linear mixed model was used to map personalized dose-response trajectories stratified by baseline clinical competency and surgical experience.

RESULTS: Longer cumulative training hours was associated with improved procedural performance and better 90-day functional outcomes. DML models consistently showed significant treatment effects (0.83-0.85, p < 0.001). Bayesian mixed-effects modeling confirmed a strong association between training duration (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.58-3.02) and clinician competency (score range 0-100; OR 3.7, 95% CI 2.79-4.86). Notably, while the training conferred universal clinical benefits across all baseline levels, the learning curve demonstrated continuous, linear improvements that were particularly pronounced among high-competency practitioners.

CONCLUSIONS: Structured remote MT training was linked to improved procedural efficiency and functional recovery after stroke. These findings support the use of data-driven, personalized, and experience-stratified training strategies to enhance clinical practice and patient outcomes in stroke care.

articles.title: Iliohypogastric and Ilioinguinal Nerve Block for Awake ECPella Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Nonpostcardiotomy Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: In pediatric cardiogenic shock, endotracheal intubation may carry a high risk of cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction. This single-center retrospective case series (2020-2025) evaluated the feasibility, safety, and outcomes of ultrasound (US)-guided ilioinguinal-iliohypogastric (IhIG) nerve blocks (0.05-0.1 ml/kg of 0.25% ropivacaine) under light sedation to facilitate awake venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella (ECPella) surgical cannulation. Five adolescents (median age: 13 years, range: 7-17; median weight: 45 kg, range: 21-58) with nonpostcardiotomy cardiogenic shock underwent successful IhIG block placement in the pediatric intensive care unit by anesthesia-trained intensivists, followed by surgical cannulation in the catheterization laboratory. Intubation and mechanical ventilation were avoided during initial cannulation and throughout ECPella duration. Three patients required a modified chimney Y-graft for cannula placement, and two experienced local surgical bleeding. All five patients survived to hospital discharge, with three achieving direct biventricular recovery. Based on these preliminary data, US-guided IhIG nerve block seems a feasible and safe strategy for awake ECPella cannulation in selected pediatric patients, successfully avoiding high-risk invasive ventilation and general anesthesia.

articles.title: Effects of Parent-Involved Digital Health Interventions on Adiposity-Related Outcomes and Behaviors in Children and Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parental involvement in obesity interventions is considered essential for sustainable behavior change in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity; yet, the effectiveness of parent-involved digital health interventions (DHIs) and the influence of different delivery modalities remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to synthesize the effects of parent-involved DHIs on adiposity-related outcomes and behaviors and explore potential moderators.

METHODS: Nine databases were searched from inception to December 2025 to identify eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Primary outcomes were adiposity-related outcomes such as BMI; secondary outcomes were adiposity-related behaviors, including dietary behavior, physical activity, and sedentary behavior. Standardized mean differences (SMDs; Hedges g) on primary outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Prespecified subgroup analyses examined DHI delivery modalities and parent-involved strategies. Secondary outcomes were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2), and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

RESULTS: Twenty-nine RCTs (4156 participants) were included, of which 22 contributed to the meta-analysis. Parent-involved DHIs produced a small but statistically significant reduction in BMI-related outcomes compared with controls (SMD=-0.11, 95% CI -0.19 to -0.04; P=.004; I²=0%). When stratified by control type, the pooled effect remained significant in trials using inactive controls (SMD=-0.15, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.04; P=.006; I²=0%), but not in trials using active controls (SMD=-0.07, 95% CI -0.19 to 0.04; P=.20; I²=0%). Subgroup differences on DHI delivery modalities and parent-involved strategies were not statistically significant. For adiposity-related behaviors, significant improvements were reported in 5 of 16 trials for dietary behaviors, 2 of 17 for physical activity, and 2 of 12 for sedentary behavior. The risk of bias was generally low to some concerns, and the overall certainty of evidence for BMI-related outcomes was moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that parent-involved DHIs may produce a small improvement in BMI-related outcomes among children and adolescents with overweight or obesity. However, evidence for improvements in adiposity-related behaviors remains limited, and neither the optimal digital delivery modality nor the most effective parent-involved strategy has been established. Future research should refine these interventions to identify optimal strategies and confirm their effectiveness.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251239829; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251239829.

articles.title: Family-Supported mHealth Coaching for Middle-Aged Men With Chronic Liver Disease and Metabolic Risk Factors: Protocol for a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic liver disease (CLD) remains a substantial public health burden, particularly among middle-aged men with metabolic risk factors. Sustained lifestyle modification is essential for preventing disease progression, but long-term self-management in this population is often suboptimal. Although mobile health (mHealth) interventions may support self-management, most are patient-centered and rarely incorporate structured family participation.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop a family-supported mHealth coaching intervention for middle-aged men with CLD and metabolic risk factors, evaluate the feasibility of the intervention and trial procedures, and explore preliminary app usability and changes in patient- and family-related outcomes through a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT).

METHODS: This 2-arm, parallel-group pilot RCT was conducted at the Liver Center of Severance Hospital, Yonsei University Health System, Seoul, Republic of Korea. Eligible patients were male outpatients aged 40 to 64 years who had CLD for at least 6 months and at least 1 metabolic risk factor. The planned sample size was 82 patients, with 41 patients per group. Enrolled patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to a 12-week family-supported mHealth coaching intervention or usual outpatient care plus a standardized educational video delivered via text message. Guided by the information-motivation-behavioral skills (IMB) model, the intervention integrates app-based self-monitoring, individualized feedback, online coaching, and opportunities for family participation. The feasibility and acceptability of the intervention and trial procedures will be evaluated. Primary outcomes are self-management behavior, perceived social support, depressive symptoms, and sleep quality; secondary outcomes include physical and clinical indicators and family experiences. Outcomes were assessed at baseline (week 0) and postintervention (week 12). Between-group changes will be examined using appropriate parametric or nonparametric tests, with an analysis of covariance used for baseline-adjusted comparisons. Effect estimates will be reported with 95% CIs and interpreted as preliminary. Complete-case analyses will be conducted without imputation of missing data.

RESULTS: This study was funded in March 2023 and received institutional review board approval on April 9, 2025 (approval 4-2025-0117). The first participant was enrolled in May 2025, and data collection was completed in March 2026. A total of 52 patient participants were enrolled and randomized, of whom 35 completed the 12-week follow-up, corresponding to an overall attrition rate of 32.7%. Data analysis and preparation of the main trial manuscript are currently underway, with submission for publication anticipated in winter 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot RCT evaluates an IMB model-informed, family-supported mHealth coaching intervention integrating app-based self-monitoring and individualized coaching. The findings will provide preliminary evidence regarding feasibility, acceptability, and changes in patient- and family-related outcomes and will inform intervention refinement and the design of a future definitive RCT.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service KCT0010494; https://tinyurl.com/75m6c7c6.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/95490.

articles.title: Constructing a Theoretical Hybrid Care Pathway From Stakeholder Perspectives: User-Centered Design Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by acute exacerbations that frequently result in hospitalization, highlighting the need for improved follow-up care. Hybrid care incorporates digital health strategies such as remote patient monitoring (RPM). This could offer the opportunity to detect early signs of disease worsening by remotely tracking selected health indicators. However, it is unknown how RPM can effectively be integrated into current practice.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to cocreate a theoretical hybrid COPD care pathway integrating RPM into the existing care trajectory, considering the expertise of participating care pathway stakeholders.

METHODS: This 2-phase study was conducted between May and August 2025. At first, semistructured interviews were conducted with stakeholders (ie, patients and health care professionals [HCPs]) involved in COPD care to map the existing care pathway in a single tertiary care hospital in Belgium. Patients were approached during hospitalization based on predefined eligibility criteria, whereas HCPs were recruited through convenience sampling. In phase 2, patient representatives and HCPs were recruited through patient-organization networks and professional referral, respectively, using convenience sampling, and participated in separate interactive workshops. These workshops reviewed existing care pathway phases and HCP roles and explored the integration of RPM, including timing, duration, implementation, data monitoring, and follow-up responsibilities, to codevelop a theoretical hybrid care pathway. Interview and workshop data were independently reviewed by 2 researchers to extract information on care pathway elements, stakeholder roles, limitations, and proposed adaptations. Findings were organized according to the relevant care pathway phase, independently summarized and compared, with discrepancies resolved through discussion and consensus. Interview findings informed the development of an initial infographic representing the existing care pathway, which was subsequently adapted based on workshop findings to represent the proposed cocreated theoretical hybrid care pathway.

RESULTS: In total, 10 stakeholders participated in the interviews (5 patients and 5 HCPs), and 6 stakeholders participated in the workshops (3 patient representatives and 3 HCPs). The existing COPD care pathway involves multiple stakeholders whose activities can be organized into 5 functional domains: support, treatment, medical advice, patient education, and monitoring. Stakeholders can be divided into hospital-based, community-based, or cross-setting. The workshop participants identified the need for a stakeholder dedicated to RPM activities in order to integrate RPM strategies into the care pathway. This individual could be responsible for all RPM-related activities (ie, RPM device installation, providing RPM-related education, data review, alert management, and RPM discontinuation) and could serve as the bridge between patients and physicians, ensuring close communication.

CONCLUSIONS: This study resulted in a cocreated theoretical hybrid COPD care pathway. Stakeholders highlighted the potential value of a dedicated RPM role to coordinate and deliver RPM activities as part of the COPD care pathway. Further research is needed to assess its feasibility and clinical applicability.

articles.title: The APLC 2025 consensus recommendations on the assessment and management of measurable residual disease in adults with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
articles.abstract: The Asia-Pacific Leukemia Consortium (APLC) working group for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (APLC ALLWG) recognized the critical need for standardized approaches to measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment and management in adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). This paper presents consensus statements from APLC ALLWG experts addressing three key areas: (i) MRD assessment technologies and platforms; (ii) optimal timing for MRD evaluation across different patient populations; and (iii) clinical management strategies based on MRD levels. These evidence-based recommendations provide hematologists throughout the Asia-Pacific region with a structured framework for interpreting MRD data and making informed decisions to improve clinical outcomes in adult ALL patients.

articles.title: Asymptomatic Tattoo-Associated Cutaneous Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Infection: Case Report.
articles.abstract: Tattoo-associated nontuberculous mycobacterial infections can present in a variety of ways, including papular, pustular, nodular, and abscess-like morphologies. We report the case of an immunocompetent 28-year-old male who presented with diffusely distributed monomorphic papules with collarettes of scale confined to recently tattooed skin. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated an atypical lichenoid vacuolar interface dermatitis, and tissue culture ultimately confirmed infection with Mycobacterium abscessus complex following prolonged incubation. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges posed by atypical clinical and histopathologic features of tattoo-associated nontuberculous mycobacterial infections, emphasizing the importance of early biopsy, mycobacterial culture, and prolonged combination antimicrobial therapy for optimal patient outcomes.

articles.title: Using Cognitive Interviewing to Assess the Feasibility and Acceptability of the Network Canvas Platform for Social Network Data Collection Among Adolescent and Young Adult Survivors of Cancer: Pilot Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about the composition and function of the social networks of adolescent and young adult survivors of cancer, despite the importance of social health for adolescent and young adult development. For adolescent and young adult survivors of cancer, social networks may be particularly important sources of support and coping. Understanding this group's social health through understanding their social networks can inform intervention development to improve various facets of health and life productivity.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this descriptive study was to explore the feasibility and acceptability of collecting and analyzing social network data using the Network Canvas platform among a subset of adolescent and young adult survivors of childhood cancer.

METHODS: We used cognitive interviewing, a qualitative method to assess survey comprehension and usability, to assess the feasibility and acceptability of using the Network Canvas social network data collection platform among 10 adolescent and young adult survivors of cancer. Participants (ie, egos) were asked about people (ie, alters) in their networks before cancer diagnosis (via recall) and currently (after cancer diagnosis). Feasibility was explored in three ways: (1) the proportion of participants who completed the full Network Canvas survey; (2) qualitative analysis of cognitive interviews addressing usability and comprehension; and (3) demonstration of whether self-administered, role-anonymized responses yielded data complete enough to support the creation of standard egocentric network measures through preliminary descriptive statistics. Acceptability was explored through qualitative analysis of the desire of participants to use Network Canvas again and features they liked when using Network Canvas.

RESULTS: In terms of feasibility, all 10 participants completed the Network Canvas survey. In qualitative analysis, participants described the ease of using Network Canvas (including engagement) while also describing ways to improve its usability. In terms of acceptability, when asked if they would use Network Canvas again, participants overall answered positively.

CONCLUSIONS: Network Canvas use among our sample of adolescent and young adult survivors of cancer was feasible and acceptable based on this exploratory analysis.
