The collection and analysis of social network data using Network Canvas was feasible in this pilot study. Additionally, the potentially therapeutic experience reported by some participants after completing the Network Canvas survey deserves further exploration. This work provides a starting point for future social health studies, psychosocial programming, and identification of those at risk of social disconnect.

articles.title: Real-World Implementation and Evaluation of a Digital Health Platform for Children Living With Type 1 Diabetes: Protocol for a Real-World Implementation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital platforms that integrate continuous glucose monitoring, patient-generated data, and clinical decision support could enable more proactive pediatric type 1 diabetes (T1D) care. Sustained uptake of digital platforms in routine practice is limited, and the evidence of effectiveness is mixed. Implementation science approaches are needed to clarify how context, workflows, and strategies shape adoption and outcomes. Haibu Diabetes is a new platform that brings together wearable, patient-reported, and clinical diabetes data to generate personalized, data-driven insights for patients and clinicians.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness and implementation processes of Haibu Diabetes in routine pediatric T1D care using a hybrid design guided by an Implementation Research Logic Model.

METHODS: We will conduct a nonrandomized, quasi-experimental, type 2 hybrid implementation-effectiveness trial at a hospital that provides multidisciplinary pediatric diabetes care. Youth aged 3 to less than 18 years with T1D and caregivers will be onboarded to Haibu Diabetes as part of routine workflows; health care providers will use a clinician dashboard to review data, assign tasks/forms, and communicate asynchronously. Effectiveness analyses will compare Haibu Diabetes users to a matched control group drawn from the BC Pediatric Diabetes Registry. Effectiveness outcomes are hemoglobin A1c, continuous glucose monitoring device-derived time in range over 12 months, and diabetes self-care behaviors. Implementation outcomes will be assessed using mixed methods guided by an Implementation Research Logic Model that links determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes. These outcomes will include reach, adoption, feasibility, acceptability, and maintenance. Health care improvement outcomes will include patient and caregiver experience, clinician experience, and operational workflow indicators.

RESULTS: Study funding commenced in January 2023. Patient recruitment began in September 2026, and 7 participants had consented as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by December 2027, with analysis to follow. Study findings are expected to be published in summer 2028.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial will generate real-world evidence on both effectiveness and the conditions required to implement and sustain a data-integrating digital platform in pediatric T1D care, informing scale-up and optimization.

articles.title: From Academic Integrity to Professional Formation in Generative AI-Supported Nursing Education: Integrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rapid integration of generative AI (GenAI) into nursing education has prompted widespread concern about academic integrity and assessment validity. However, this dominant discourse may obscure a more fundamental challenge: preparing nursing students for clinical practice environments where AI already mediates triage, diagnostics, documentation, and clinical decision-making.

OBJECTIVE: This integrative review examines how GenAI is conceptualized within the nursing education literature and investigates the extent to which current discourse addresses professional formation rather than academic compliance.

METHODS: Following Whittemore and Knafl's integrative review methodology, a systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, and SciSpace (Typeset) was conducted for literature published between January 2022 and February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened 456 records, with 119 papers meeting the inclusion criteria. The methodological quality of empirical studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Corpus-level descriptive mapping quantified dominant themes and conceptual patterns, while an interpretive synthesis examined how GenAI was framed and the extent to which professional formation elements, including identity, moral agency, and clinical judgment, were addressed.

RESULTS: Of the 119 unique studies analyzed, 84% (n=100) predominantly framed GenAI as a content-generation tool and academic integrity threat. Only 35.3% (n=42) conceptualized AI as a pedagogical tool, and a critical gap was identified in professional formation: identity formation was addressed in only 10% (n=12) of papers and moral agency in just 5% (n=6). Explicit acknowledgment that AI already routinely mediates frontline clinical decisions (eg, sepsis alerts and fall risk algorithms) in current practice settings was notably absent. The discourse emphasizes governance and faculty literacy, but sustained curricula addressing nurse identity in AI-mediated care remain underdeveloped.

CONCLUSIONS: Current nursing education discourse predominantly frames AI as a writing tool and an academic integrity concern, failing to prepare students for the algorithmic practice environments they will inhabit. Nursing education must reframe AI as a professional formation issue, explicitly addressing how algorithms reshape clinical judgment, moral agency, and professional identity.

articles.title: Integrated Metabolomic and Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals the Response Mechanisms of Phallus rubrovolvatus to Yeast Pathogen Infection.
articles.abstract: Phallus rubrovolvatus is a valuable edible and medicinal mushroom, but its cultivation is severely hindered by yellow rot disease caused by Saccharomycopsis phalli, which shows a 60 to 80% incidence and causes severe fruiting body rot, yield loss, and quality decline. The molecular mechanisms, particularly the dynamic transcriptional and metabolic responses, underlying the defense of P. rubrovolvatus against S. phalli remain poorly understood, limiting the development of targeted control strategies. To address this gap, we conducted an integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis, identifying differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially accumulated metabolites (DAMs) at 8, 16, 32, and 48 hours post-inoculation (hpi). Results showed significant changes in the pentose and glucuronate interconversion pathway, with reduced expression of related genes (e.g., ARD1, XR) and decreased accumulation of metabolites (e.g., D-glucuronic acid). Conversely, the arginine biosynthesis pathway was significantly enriched, with accumulated intermediates (e.g., citrulline, argininosuccinic acid) and upregulated biosynthesis genes (e.g., glnA, rocF). Alanine, aspartate and glutamate metabolism was also implicated in the infection response, mediating carbon-nitrogen skeleton flux and energy allocation to meet physiological demands. Additionally, glutathione metabolism was significantly enriched, accompanied by upregulated glutathione S-transferase (GST) genes. Overall, this study reveals a multi-pathway defense response in P. rubrovolvatus against S. phalli across the infection time course, involving coordinated carbon-nitrogen metabolic reprogramming and antioxidant defense activation, offering theoretical insight into its disease resistance mechanisms and supporting breeding of yellow rot-resistant varieties.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitude, and practices towards anthrax among Communities in the Southern and South-western Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis is an endemic zoonotic disease in Ethiopia, primarily affecting domestic and wild ruminants and often resulting in severe and potentially fatal infection in humans.

METHODOLOGY: A cross-sectional study was conducted from February to November 2025 to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to anthrax among communities in 10 districts of the southern and southwestern part of Ethiopia. A total of 382 household heads aged 18 years and above were interviewed using structured questionnaires with open and closed-ended questions. Descriptive analysis, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson's correlation analysis were used to report frequenciesy, percentages and mean scores to quantify and assess associations of the knowledge, attitudes and practices of the communities toward anthrax.

RESULTS: Respondents had a mean age of 39.8 ± 12.7 years, with males comprising 92.7% of participants, and 28.3% had no formal education, while the majority were farmers (79.8%). Among the 382 participants, 60.2% had adequate knowledge. 93.7% had heard about anthrax, primarily from veterinary professionals. Two hundred twenty-seven (59.4%) of respondents were aware of the modes of transmission, 58.9% and 77.0% understood prevention measures in humans and animals, respectively. Two hundred fourteen (56.2%) of the respondents had a positive attitude towards anthrax, and 91.6% perceived anthrax as a serious disease affecting both humans and animals. A total of 187 (49.0%) of the respondents had good practices toward anthrax prevention, and vaccination practices were commonly reported, with 81.4% of them believing that vaccinating animals is important to protect human health and 98.2% to protect livestock. Among the respondents, 42.2% reported that they manage carcasses of animals suspected of sudden death by burying and burning, 36.7% reported to local veterinary authorities, 10.7% shared and ate the meat with the community and their family, and 3.6% disposed of the carcasses into the environment. Overall, the mean scores (5.9 ± 2.6 out of 10, 5.4 ± 1.2 out of 6, and 2.34 ± 1.3 out of 5) were recorded for knowledge, attitude, and practices, respectively. Participants' knowledge mean score about anthrax was significantly associated with gender (male), level of education (degree), and occupation (government employed) (p < 0.001). There was also a positive significant correlation between knowledge-attitude (r = 0.690, p < 0.001), knowledge-practice (r = 0.417, p < 0.001), and attitude-practice (r = 0.378, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Findings from the current study provided essential insights into community awareness and preventive practices, which are critical for strengthening anthrax control and prevention strategies.

articles.title: Persistence of viral full-length genomic RNA and replication-associated RNA transcripts and proteins in sheep tissues following acute Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus infection.
articles.abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is a tick-borne RNA virus responsible for a severe hemorrhagic disease in humans. In contrast, the virus appears to cause only a brief viremia without overt clinical signs in animals such as livestock, following which the infection is traditionally assumed to end with complete viral clearance. Here, we challenge this prevailing view by reporting the recovery of full-length viral genomic RNA sequences from tissues of CCHFV-infected sheep long after the resolution of acute viremia. While viral RNA persistence in these tissues was largely characterized by a lack of extensive viral replication, we detected the sporadic presence of replication-associated viral RNA transcripts and viral proteins. These findings suggest that the biology of CCHFV in animals extends well beyond an acute infection. The possibility that the virus can transition into a dormant state, with potential for reactivation to resume gene expression or replication, a phenomenon documented in other RNA viruses, warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Antibodies to distinct epitopes on MPXV enveloped virion provide additive and complete protection.
articles.abstract: The continuing evolution of monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades capable of sustained human-to-human transmission poses an escalating global health risk, yet no effective therapy exists for poxvirus infection. Here, we investigate a panel of human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), derived from an antibody library, which targets A35 and B6 antigens located on the extracellular enveloped virion (EV). Four high-affinity mAbs target the central groove of the A35 dimer, whereas one targets a previously unidentified epitope on the A35 protruding loop. Three other mAbs recognize distinct, previously unmapped epitopes on the multidomain B6 antigen. Those epitopes are conserved across most orthopoxviruses. A combination of an anti-A35 and an anti-B6 antibody provides additive and complete protection from both morbidity and mortality in a lethal VACV mouse model, challenging the previous assumption that targeting both the EV and mature virion (MV) forms is required for full protection. These studies uncover critical information for next-generation therapeutics and vaccines against emerging MPXV as well as other Orthopoxvirus threats.

articles.title: Snakebite epidemiology and health-seeking behavior in fringe communities of the Kakum Conservation Area in Ghana.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Snakebite envenomation (SE) is a significant yet under reported public health challenge, especially in rural and forest-fringe communities in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite its recognition by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD), epidemiological data on SE remain scarce in Ghana, particularly in communities fringing protected forest areas such as the Kakum Conservation Area (KCA).

OBJECTIVE: This study sought to examine snakebite epidemiology in the fringe communities of the Kakum Conservation Area (KCA) in the Central region of Ghana.

METHODS: A cross-sectional household survey was conducted between April and May 2024 in 18 communities fringing the KCA in Ghana's Central Region. The data collection instrument was pretested in a non-study community (n = 30), with Cronbach's alpha ranging from 0.72 to 0.86 for key scales, indicating acceptable internal consistency. A two-stage sampling approach was employed to enumerate a total of 1,445 households for snakebite victims. Descriptive statistics included frequencies, proportions, means, and standard deviations with 95% confidence intervals calculated using binomial approximation. Inferential statistics included chi-square tests for bivariate associations and multivariable logistic regression to calculate adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: In this study, the reported lifetime occurrence of snakebites was 394/8,518 (4.63%, 95% CI: 4.18-5.07), compared with 164/8,518 (1.93%, 95% CI: 1.63-2.22) and 41/8,518 (0.48%, 95% CI: 0.33-0.63) in the preceding five years and one year, respectively. The mean age of victims was 44.69 (SD ± 18.64) years. Most victims were female (212/394, 53.81%), married (231/394, 58.63%) and engaged in farming (289/394, 73.35%). Most bites occurred in farms/forests (258/394, 65.48%) and affected the lower limbs (345/394, 87.56%). First aid was applied by 295/394 (74.87%) victims, predominantly involving tourniquets (103/295, 34.92%). Overall, 239/394 (60.66%) sought treatment, of whom 170/239 (71.13%) accessed formal healthcare facilities. Among treatment seekers, 124/239 (51.88%) travelled by motor vehicle, while 97/239 (40.59%) travelled on foot. Additionally, 92/239 (38.49%) waited at least one hour before seeking care, while 89/239 (37.24%) spent at least one hour travelling for care. Following snakebite, 373/394 (94.67%) victims recovered, 15/394 (3.81%) experienced disability and 6/394 (1.52%) died. Compared with victims aged under 20 years, those aged 30-39 years had higher adjusted odds of experiencing snakebite in farm/forest settings (AOR = 3.39, 95% CI: 1.07-10.67). Farming was also associated with increased odds of farm/forest snakebite (AOR = 1.88, 95% CI: 1.04-3.40). Regarding facility-based care, victims aged 20-29 years (AOR = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.05-0.88) and ≥60 years (AOR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.02-0.69) had lower adjusted odds of seeking care compared with those aged under 20 years.

CONCLUSION: Snakebites constitute a major public health concern in communities fringing forested conservation areas, especially for people whose livelihood activities revolve around agricultural activities. Overall, the study underscores the need to establish and strengthen collaborative efforts among primary health authorities, forest conservation managers, and community leaders in the design and implementation of effective interventions to avert snakebite incidents and improve outcomes for victims.

articles.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
articles.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti-lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody-functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 103-fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 103-fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74-NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline-deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74-NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

articles.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
articles.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair-bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type-specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α-responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α-expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

articles.title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus-induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its "microelectrode-drug reservoir-nanopore" configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus-induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

articles.title: kri-1/KRIT1 promotes innate immune and lipid homeostasis in the C. elegans intestine.
articles.abstract: Animals must differentially allocate essential metabolic resources in response to changing environmental conditions to ensure reproductive success. For example, adult C. elegans coordinate innate immune defenses during infection and also allocate fat stores to the germline, each of which are required for evolutionary fitness. The genetic mechanisms that integrate resource allocation and host defenses in this context, however, are not fully understood. From a forward genetic screen for novel regulators of innate immune gene transcription, we identified kri-1, the nematode homolog of human Krev interaction trapped protein KRIT1. Mutations in human KRIT1 underlie cerebral cavernous malformations, a disease marked by defects in vascular integrity. Similarly, C. elegans kri-1/KRIT1 is required for the integrity of the intestinal epithelial cell barrier. We find also that kri-1/KRIT1 is required for host tolerance to bacterial infection, fecundity, and normal development. In this context, kri-1/KRIT1 restrains the activity of the cytoprotective transcription factor skn-1/NRF2 to control immune gene transcription and likely intestinal lipid mobilization during aging, a process necessary for healthy reproduction, but functions independently of skn-1/NRF2 to promote epithelial integrity and pathogen tolerance. These data reveal a broad role for a strongly conserved regulator in essential physiological processes that are required for reproductive fidelity and evolutionary success.

articles.title: Persistent viral carriage of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus in canine: A potential canine-to-human transmission event in a family cluster.
articles.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne viral disease with a substantial case-fatality rate. Here, we reported a family cluster of SFTS cases in Southeast China. The index case was a 57-year-old man, whose son and wife subsequently developed SFTS-compatible symptoms at two and three days after his onset, respectively. All three cases were laboratory-confirmed for SFTS, and retrospectively reported close care to a sick golden retriever prior to symptom onset. In contrast, the other two family members without such canine exposure remained serologically and clinically uninfected. All three cases denied a tick-biting history before illness onset. Subsequent testing confirmed SFTS virus (SFTSV) infection in the golden retriever, and SFTSV was also detected in a tick collected from the dog. Longitudinal viral screening of serial canine samples revealed persistent SFTSV shedding: viral positivity was sustained for 23 days in nasal swabs and urethral swabs, 27 days in serum samples, and at least 30 days in rectal swabs following its symptom onset. Genomic analysis showed near-identical SFTSV sequences from the index case and the infected dog, with identities of 99.94% for the small segment, 100% for the medium segment, and 99.98% for the large segment. This study reveals prolonged SFTSV shedding in infected canine, suggests a plausible risk of canine-to-human SFTSV transmission, and highlights the potential role of dogs in the spread and evolution of SFTSV.

articles.title: SR-A1 cooperates with TLR4-NF-κB signaling to drive macrophage TGF-β1 expression and Treg induction during schistosome infection.
articles.abstract: Helminths induce regulatory T cells (Tregs) to establish chronic infections, promoting long-term persistence of both parasites and hosts. TGF-β1 is essential for Treg induction by initiating Foxp3 expression. Helminth infections are typically associated with high TGF-β1 levels, yet the mechanisms by which helminths drive its production are not fully understood. Here, we uncover a mechanism whereby the scavenger receptor class A1 (SR-A1) cooperates with TLR4 signaling to drive TGF-β1 production by macrophages. Mechanistically, schistosome egg antigens activate TLR4-p50 (NF-κB1) while concurrently engaging SR-A1 to upregulate c-Jun, thereby assembling c-Jun-p50 transcription complexes at the Tgfb1 promoter and enhancing TGF-β1 expression, subsequently inducing Tregs and mitigating liver immunopathology in Schistosoma japonicum-infected mice. Thus, we identify a previously unrecognized host-parasite interaction wherein SR-A1-TLR4 cooperation enables helminths to manipulate macrophage transcriptional programs for TGF-β1 expression and Treg induction, identifying a potential therapeutic target in the host for inflammatory helminthiasis.

articles.title: Short and long-term outcomes after gestational diabetes diagnosis using different glycemic criteria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Lower gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic criteria on an oral glucose tolerance test are widely recommended, but their impacts on maternal, neonatal, long-term and economic outcomes remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To compare outcomes after GDM diagnosis using lower versus higher diagnostic strategies.

METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing outcomes following assessment for GDM and treatment if indicated, using lower versus higher glycemic diagnostic criteria or thresholds in four databases and four trial registries (PROSPERO registration CRD420251183179) to 27th July 2026. Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias, conducted random-effects meta-analyses and evaluated GRADE certainty.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included, with nine RCTs and one cohort study contributing to the meta-analysis (81,528 women). Lower diagnostic criteria or thresholds, compared with higher diagnostic criteria or thresholds, doubled GDM diagnosis and pharmacotherapy use, increased neonatal hypoglycemia (RCTs: 18 more per 1,000; 95% CI 11 to 25 more) and maternal-neonatal separation (RCTs: 6 more per 1,000; 95% CI 1 to 12 more), but had little to no effect on other short-term outcomes. Longer-term evidence was limited to follow-up of one RCT reporting reduced maternal hypertension and child neurodevelopmental impairment but increased subsequent GDM at five-year follow-up with use of lower criteria or thresholds. Findings on GDM-related healthcare costs were inconsistent, with no long-term economic data.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower diagnostic criteria increased the diagnosis of GDM and some aspects of healthcare utilization, without improving short-term outcomes. Limited evidence suggested possible longer-term benefits, warranting further long-term follow-up from high-quality RCTs.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Prognostic Significance of Interventricular Septal Thickness in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interventricular septal (IVS) thickness is routinely measured by echocardiography, yet its prognostic significance in heart failure (HF), and whether it differs by sex, remains uncertain.

METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with HF from the SHEBAHEART registry (2009-2025). IVS thickness was classified as normal (<1.1 cm), mildly thickened (≥1.1 to ≤1.3 cm), or severely thickened (>1.3 cm), using identical thresholds by sex. Associations with all-cause mortality were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, comorbidities, and left ventricular ejection fraction, with formal testing for sex-by-IVS interaction.

RESULTS: Among 20,836 patients (median age, 74 years; 39% women), 41% had mild and 18% had severe IVS thickening. During a median follow-up of 4 years, 11,930 patients (57%) died; 4-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative mortality increased across IVS categories (35%, 39%, and 42%; P < 0.001). In primary complete-case analysis (n = 13,902), the sex-by-IVS interaction was significant (P = 0.030). Adjusted hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) for mild and severe thickening were 1.16 (1.07-1.26) and 1.19 (1.08-1.32) in women, compared with 1.02 (0.96-1.09) and 1.07 (0.99-1.16) in men. The sex-by-IVS interaction remained significant in multiple-imputation and time-varying Cox analyses, but not with sex-specific IVS reference partitions.

CONCLUSIONS: With common absolute IVS thresholds, increased septal thickness was more strongly associated with all-cause mortality in women than in men with HF. These findings support evaluation of IVS thickness as a potential component of sex-specific risk stratification in HF.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Mechanisms and Therapeutics in Heart Failure: Translating Biology into Personalized Care.
articles.abstract: Sex is one of the most consistent, yet clinically underexploited, determinants of heart failure phenotype, mechanism and outcome. Building on landmark reviews and the 2024 scientific statement of the Heart Failure Association, which documented well-recognized phenotypic differences but noted that their mechanisms remain only partially defined, this review examines how sex differences in heart failure arise and how firmly they should guide practice. Epidemiologically, female predominance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is age- and menopause-dependent rather than lifelong. Mechanistically, sex-divergent hormonal signalling, autonomic tone, coronary microvascular dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis often produce similar phenotypes through different mechanisms: microvascular dysfunction is similarly prevalent in both sexes but linked to fibrosis in women and to atherosclerotic risk factors in men, and oestradiol regulates collagen synthesis in opposite directions in female and male cardiac fibroblasts. Clinically, comorbidities carry divergent prognostic weight by sex. Graded against the strength of evidence, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors show established sex-neutral efficacy, whereas the greater benefit of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism in women rests on subgroup signals that await confirmation. Natriuretic peptide concentrations are substantially sex-dependent, yet diagnostic thresholds remain sex-neutral, although sex-specific calibration is methodologically achievable. Women remain underrepresented in heart failure trials and less often referred to specialized care. Heart failure is therefore best understood as a sex-differentiated syndrome whose frameworks were built largely around male-pattern disease. Sex-calibrated trial enrolment, sex-specific biomarker and ejection fraction thresholds, and stratification by menopausal stage are concrete next steps towards personalized care.

articles.title: Pregnancy in patients with type 1 diabetes and diabetic nephropathy: sailing between Scylla and Charybdis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy in women with type 1 diabetes (T1D) complicated by overt diabetic nephropathy (DN) remains a major clinical challenge, with limited data on maternal-foetal outcomes. This study describes the clinical course and outcomes of pregnancies in women with overt DN followed in a dedicated nephrology-obstetric care setting.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis including 15 pregnancies, 13 of which had complete baseline and delivery data, in women with T1D and overt DN followed at Policlinico Umberto I (Rome-Italy), between 2010 and 2022. Maternal characteristics, renal and obstetric complications, and perinatal outcomes were analysed from baseline to six months postpartum.

RESULTS: Thirteen pregnancies were analysed. Median baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 67.6 (42.9-95.8) ml/min/1.73m2, median proteinuria 0.8 (0.5-1.6) g/day; 69% had chronic hypertension and 84% diabetic retinopathy. Proteinuria increased during pregnancy in 9/13 cases. Two patients developed acute kidney injury, one of whom required haemodialysis during pregnancy and remained dialysis-dependent thereafter. Superimposed preeclampsia occurred in five cases and was associated with lower baseline eGFR. Preterm delivery was common; all the patients delivered by caesarean section. A decline ≥10 mL/min/1.73 m2 in eGFR or dialysis initiation was observed in 4 patients at 6-month follow-up; in the remaining patients, no significant changes were observed, although the follow-up was limited to 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy in women with overt DN continues to entail substantial maternal and foetal risk. Early nephrology referral, strict metabolic and blood pressure control, and systematic preconception counselling are crucial to optimising outcomes and preventing irreversible renal decline.

articles.title: Development of iADJUST: a theory-informed, patient co-designed digital psychological intervention for adjustment in chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological distress is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and associated with reduced quality of life and worse clinical outcomes, partly reflecting difficulties adjusting to illness demands. Psychological support remains inconsistently integrated within kidney care pathways, and existing interventions rarely specify or target the mechanisms underpinning adjustment to CKD. This paper describes the systematic development of iADJUST, a theory-informed patient co-designed digital psychological intervention targeting key cognitive and behavioural mechanisms involved in adjustment to CKD.

METHODS: Intervention development was guided by the Medical Research Council framework and integrated empirical evidence, psychological theory, and patient and public involvement and engagement. The Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation and cognitive behavioural theories informed identification of modifiable maintaining mechanisms of adjustment to CKD. Intervention components were mapped onto these mechanisms and refined through co-design with people living with CKD.

RESULTS: iADJUST is a six-session, primarily self-guided digital psychological intervention for adults with CKD who are not on dialysis or transplanted, delivered over 12 weeks with brief therapist support. It targets illness-related uncertainty, fatigue-related activity dysregulation, catastrophic "what-if" thinking, self-critical evaluation, behavioural withdrawal, and self-regulation processes relevant to maintenance and relapse prevention. It integrates psychoeducation, cognitive and behavioural strategies, maintenance planning, and elements from acceptance and commitment therapy and compassion-focused approaches, delivered through video, audio, and guided tasks and activities.

CONCLUSIONS: iADJUST provides a theory- and evidence-informed psychological intervention for CKD explicitly mapping intervention components to maintaining cognitive and behavioural mechanisms of adjustment. Its feasibility is being evaluated in a randomised waitlist-controlled feasibility trial (ISRCTN91507822).

articles.title: Toward a Brighter Future in Vaccine Safety Science: A Call For Investments, Capitalizing on Scientific Opportunities and A National Vaccine Safety Board.
Influenza virus antagonizes self-sensing by RIG-I to enhance viral replication.
articles.abstract: Innate immune sensors must finely distinguish pathogens from the host to mount a response only during infection. RIG-I is a cytoplasmic sensor that triggers a broad antiviral response in response to sensing foreign RNAs. Here, we show that RIG-I not only binds viral RNAs but is activated by host RNAs. These are primarily non-coding RNAs transcribed by RNA polymerase III. They are benign under normal conditions but become immunogenic during influenza virus infection, where they signal via RIG-I to suppress viral replication. These RNAs are also bound by influenza virus nucleoprotein (NP), which normally functions to encapsidate the viral genome. NP interacts with RIG-I via an RNA bridge and antagonizes sensing of self-RNAs to counter innate immune responses. Overall, we demonstrate that self-sensing is strategically deployed by the cell to amplify the antiviral response and reveal a newly identified viral countermeasure that disrupts RIG-I activation by host RNAs.

articles.title: From Consensus to Clinical Decisions: Translating the Global Consensus for Clinical Guidelines into Practice.

Correction to: Pathophysiology, prevention, and management of coronary microvascular obstruction: A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Working Group on Coronary Pathophysiology & Microcirculation, the ESC Working Group on Thrombosis, and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC.
Lipidomes of placenta-derived extracellular vesicles reveal disrupted metabolic adaptation in type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Placental metabolic adaptation is dynamically orchestrated across gestation to support fetal development, yet how this process is disrupted in type 1 diabetes (T1D) and contributes to altered fetal metabolic outcomes remains unclear. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) may provide a minimally invasive window into placental metabolic state during pregnancy.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether lipidomic profiling of placental sEVs (P-sEVs) in maternal circulation captures dynamic placental metabolic adaptation and its dysregulation in T1D pregnancy.

DESIGN AND SETTING: Prospective longitudinal cohort study conducted within the Ontario Birth Study and the Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Pregnant Women with Type 1 Diabetes (CONCEPTT) study.

PARTICIPANTS: Maternal plasma samples were collected across gestation (10-14, 24-32, and 34-40 weeks of gestation) from 200 normoglycemic pregnancies and 151 pregnancies from individuals with preexisting T1D.

METHODS: Placental sEVs were isolated and characterized, and lipid composition was quantified using shotgun mass spectrometry-based lipidomics. Multivariate and machine learning approaches were applied to define gestational lipid trajectories and assess associations with fetal metabolic outcomes.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Gestational lipid trajectories in P-sEVs from normoglycemic and T1D, and their association with maternal and fetal risk factors and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Placental sEVs from T1D pregnancies exhibited increased vesicle size and reduced abundance. Lipidomic profiling revealed divergence in the magnitude, direction, and timing of gestational lipid trajectories compared with controls. Lipid species involved in membrane remodeling and bioactive signaling distinguished pregnancies with high vs low cord blood C-peptide, a marker of fetal endogenous insulin secretion, with strong discrimination (area under the characteristic curve = 0.85).

CONCLUSION: Circulating P-sEV lipid profiles reflect disrupted placental metabolic adaptation in T1D pregnancy and are associated with fetal hyperinsulinemia at birth, supporting their potential for minimally invasive assessment of placental function.

articles.title: Flavonoids From Sophora tonkinensis Disrupt STING-TBK1-IRF3 Complex Assembly and Ameliorate Inflammatory Diseases by Modulating cGAS-STING Signaling.
articles.abstract: cGAS-STING pathway is a core regulator of innate immunity and inflammatory responses. Aberrant activation of the cGAS-STING pathway is closely associated with the progression of multiple inflammatory disorders. Flavonoids from Sophora tonkinensis (STF) are the main ingredients of this traditional Chinese medicine with definite anti-inflammatory activity, whereas its molecular mechanism against inflammation remains unclear. This work aimed to explore the regulatory effect and underlying molecular mechanism of STF on the cGAS-STING pathway, and verify its therapeutic efficacy on typical inflammatory diseases in vivo. BMDMs and human THP-1 were used for in vitro experiments. Western blot, RT-qPCR, ELISA, Co-IP, and Native-PAGE were performed to detect protein phosphorylation, gene expression, protein-protein interaction, and STING oligomerization. Lipopolysaccharide/D-galactosamine (LPS/D-GalN)-induced acute liver injury and LPS-induced sepsis mouse models were established to evaluate the in vivo anti-inflammatory and organ-protective effects of STF. Serum biochemical detection and gene expression analysis were carried out for in vivo sample evaluation. STF suppressed ISD-triggered activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) and STING, as well as decreased expression of downstream inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, STF did not interfere with STING oligomerization but blocked the assembly of the STING-TBK1 complex and the interaction between IRF3 and TBK1. In vivo experiments demonstrated that STF dose-dependently alleviated hepatic pathological damage and hepatocyte apoptosis in a mouse model of acute liver injury. Furthermore, STF improved survival rates and attenuated multi-organ injury in septic mice by reducing the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. STF exerts targeted anti-inflammatory activity via disrupting STING-TBK1 and TBK1-IRF3 complex assembly and inhibiting the cGAS-STING signaling cascade. It provides experimental evidence for the clinical application and translational research of Sophora tonkinensis and its flavonoid components in the treatment of cGAS-STING-related inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: A Flexible Meal-Building Web Application for Food Is Medicine Programs: Development and Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food is Medicine (FIM) interventions are increasingly integrated into healthcare and community settings. Although FIM interventions show promise for improving diet and clinical outcomes, results have been mixed, and positive effects may attenuate over time. Digital nutrition and cooking applications have emerged in FIM interventions and may help FIM participants apply nutrition education to build meal-preparation skills. The GRACE Framework provides the foundation to integrate ways to create and adapt meals: Get a base, round out with Real produce and proteins, add Aromatics, Cook gently, and Enhance with flavor. The GRACE Kitchen progressive web application (PWA) prototype was designed to operationalize this framework.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the development of the GRACE Framework, its translation into the GRACE Kitchen PWA prototype, and to examine preliminary user feedback on the prototype.

METHODS: An iterative developmental design based on two separate pilots (FIM-HT and FIM-BCS) was organized into three developmental stages. In stage 1, qualitative interviews (n=17) with participants with hypertension from a 12-week pilot FIM intervention (FIM-HT) were analyzed to identify facilitators and barriers to sustaining DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension)-aligned eating, including produce delivery and nutrition education. Themes elicited from the FIM-HT interviews informed the development of the GRACE Framework, and in stage 2, the GRACE Framework was translated into the GRACE Kitchen prototype. In stage 3, breast cancer survivors (n=12) participated in an 8-week FIM pilot (FIM-BCS) while also undergoing preliminary testing of GRACE Kitchen. User experiences were assessed using a modified Mobile App Usability Questionnaire (MAUQ) and focus group data.

RESULTS: Across the three developmental stages, feedback from 29 participants contributed to the development of the GRACE Framework and the GRACE Kitchen prototype. During stage 1, initial conceptual ideas for the GRACE Framework were based on three themes from the FIM-HT interview data: changes in eating behaviors, challenges to cooking, and the maintenance of healthy cooking and eating behaviors. Participants emphasized finding new ways to incorporate vegetables, spices, and herbs; swapping in healthier ingredients; adapting recipes to their preferences; and navigating the challenges of meal preparation and cooking. Using this feedback, stage 2 developed the GRACE Kitchen PWA. During the PWA testing (stage 3), FIM-BCS participants (n=12) reported ease of use (2.70/4), satisfaction (2.67/4), and usefulness (2.71/4). The FIM-BCS participants also provided qualitative findings indicating strong acceptability of GRACE Kitchen's guidance on making meals easier to prepare. However, they found the interface challenging and preferred a mobile-forward, easier-to-navigate approach.

CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary feedback suggests that GRACE Kitchen was perceived as moderately useful and highly acceptable while also identifying important usability limitations. Although participants reported support for the GRACE Framework, further evaluation is needed to determine whether GRACE Kitchen can sustain dietary practices.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of a Dual Sensor System in Assessment of Coronary Calcification: An Ex Vivo Cadaveric Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of coronary calcification informs procedural planning in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet neither optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) nor intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) alone provides comprehensive diagnostic information. The dual sensor system (DSS) was developed to integrate and complement both imaging modalities.

AIMS: To determine the diagnostic value of DSS for detecting and characterizing calcification compared with either modality alone.

METHODS: Twenty coronary arteries from 17 cadaver hearts underwent DSS pullbacks. Eighty-seven histological sections and their co-registered DSS images were analyzed, with histology serving as the reference standard. Four cardiologists blinded to histology independently assessed calcification using OFDI alone, IVUS alone, and DSS. OFDI signal attenuation and IVUS reverberation artifacts were examined as potential indicators of maximum calcification thickness.

RESULTS: DSS demonstrated the highest sensitivity (DSS 98.0%; OFDI 85.5%, p < 0.001; IVUS 94.4%, p = 0.019) and accuracy (DSS, 97.7%; OFDI, 86.5%, p < 0.001; IVUS, 92.8%, p = 0.004) for detecting calcification. Inter-observer agreement was also highest in DSS (κ: DSS, 0.82; OFDI, 0.53; IVUS, 0.53). In subgroup analysis, sensitivity was significantly higher in DSS for sections with calcification arc < 180° (DSS, 98.6%; OFDI, 83.8%; IVUS, 94.0%), but not for those with ≥ 180°. Maximum calcification thickness was greater in calcifications only with OFDI attenuation than in those without (1423.8 [988.8-1994.1] vs. 686.4 [552.8-906.3] µm, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DSS provides accurate and consistent detection of coronary calcification and may help stratify calcification by thickness. Future studies should assess whether these advantages translate into clinical benefits.

articles.title: Confidence in the wild: the educational impact of a wilderness medicine workshop on emergency medicine resident self-confidence and perceptions.
articles.abstract: Wilderness medicine education has become an increasingly valued component of emergency medicine residency curricula but remains inconsistently integrated across programs. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a wilderness medicine educational workshop on residents' confidence in their provision of wilderness medicine care and their overall perception of wilderness medicine. A pre-test-post-test design was employed. The intervention of interest was an educational workshop composed of a lecture, rotating skills stations, and multiple simulated wilderness medicine scenarios. Data were collected through a survey completed prior to and immediately following the intervention. Twelve confidence and six perception competencies were assessed by the survey. A total of 22 participants comprised the study sample. Statistically significant differences were found post-intervention across wilderness medicine confidence outcomes as well as the confidence composite score (p < 0.001, r=0.905). All 12 competencies demonstrated moderate to large effect sizes (r > 0.50). Participants maintained favorable perceptions of wilderness medicine training across the workshop, with no significant post-intervention difference detected (p = 0.42). Our study highlights residents' favorable perceptions of wilderness medicine training and demonstrates the effectiveness of a single-day workshop in improving residents' confidence in wilderness medicine skills. This study supports the use of such interventions to further enhance medical residents' learning and self-reported confidence in important medical skills.

articles.title: Static and dynamic characteristics of the pupil light reflex obtained in Indian eyes using a hand-held, objective pupillometer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To establish the baseline data of static and dynamic characteristics of the pupil light reflex in Indian eyes across a wide age range using Pupil N, a newly developed handheld, objective pupillometer and thereby compare the present outcomes with a comparable dataset in Indian eyes obtained using the NPi-200, the current standard of care in objective pupillometry.

METHODS: Pupil N elicits the light reflex by delivering two 1-s-long visible light pulses of 125 lx intensity onto the eye with 4-s of interstimulus interval, all after initial 6-s of dark adaptation. Pupil diameters recorded using an infrared sensitive camera (30 fps) are processed using a commercial smartphone to derive six outcome variables: pre- and post-stimulated diameter, miosis (normalized to pre-stimulation values), constriction and dilation peak velocities and response latency. Baseline data were collected in this study in both eyes on 290 healthy participants (3-86 years of age) and the right eye data of adults were compared with those obtained using NPi-200 by Rattan et al. [37].

RESULTS: Baseline values calculated for each age decade showed younger eyes having larger pre-and post-stimulation diameters, faster constriction and dilation peak velocities, relative to older eyes (p < 0.001). The magnitude of miosis and response latency were similar across ages, except for larger miosis and shorter latencies in the first decade of life (p < 0.001). Data trends were similar to Rattan et al., but the absolute values differed across outcome variables (p < 0.001), except for pre-stimulation diameter (p = 0.06).

CONCLUSIONS: The baseline values of pupil light reflex reported here for Pupil N may be used as future reference standards for interpreting data of individuals with neurological dysfunction. The inter-device differences reported here call for caution while using these devices interchangeably for eliciting/interpreting the pupil light reflex in clinical and research environments.

articles.title: Massive intra-aortic thrombus detected by transesophageal echocardiography during impella support.
The impact of leaflet thrombosis on transcatheter aortic valve degeneration: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has expanded into younger and lower-risk patients, making long-term valve durability increasingly important. Leaflet thrombosis, most commonly identified on computed tomography as hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), is common after TAVI. Whether leaflet thrombosis contributes to structural valve deterioration (SVD) remains incompletely understood. To summarize the current evidence on the relationship between leaflet thrombosis and SVD after TAVI, with a focus on clinical outcomes, imaging findings, antithrombotic therapy, and pathophysiological mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes available clinical, imaging, mechanistic, histopathological and antithrombotic literature addressing leaflet thrombosis and valve durability after TAVI. CT studies show that leaflet thrombosis occurs in 13-32% of patients within the first post-procedural year. Although some lesions resolve spontaneously, longitudinal imaging studies demonstrate persistence in a substantial proportion of patients, supporting the presence of an underlying valve-related substrate. HALT has not consistently been associated with adverse valve hemodynamics during the first year after implantation. Long-term TAVI durability studies report low rates of severe SVD (0.8-1.5% up to 10 years), although outcomes vary according to valve generation and study population. The 10-year NOTION and PARTNER 2A data provide important long-term durability information, but neither study included systematic longitudinal CT assessment of leaflet thrombosis. Observational studies linking early HALT to subsequent hemodynamic valve deterioration have yielded conflicting results. Indirect evidence from anticoagulation studies and histopathological investigations supports biological plausibility for a relationship between leaflet thrombosis and progressive leaflet injury, but does not establish causality. Leaflet thrombosis is a frequent imaging finding after TAVI and may persist over time, but its contribution to long-term SVD remains uncertain. Current evidence supports a potential biological relationship between leaflet thrombosis and valve degeneration but does not demonstrate that HALT is a causal precursor of clinically relevant SVD. Prospective studies combining serial CT imaging with long-term, standardized assessment of structural valve outcomes are required to resolve this question.

articles.title: Anticoagulation stewardship quality improvement project to decrease incidence of supratherapeutic activated partial thromboplastic time in overweight cancer patients on unfractionated heparin infusions.
articles.abstract: Unfractionated Heparin (UFH) is widely used to treat multiple conditions in hospitalized patients. Standard dosing based on actual body weight (ABW) may lead to over-anticoagulation in overweight patients due to the limited vascularity of adipose tissue. Historically, ABW was used when BMI ≤ 40 kg/m2, and adjusted body weight (AdjBW) when BMI > 40 kg/m2. However, patients with ABW >130% of ideal body weight (IBW) and BMI ≤ 40 kg/m2 experienced increased rates of supratherapeutic activated partial thromboplastin times (aPTTs). The objective of this project was to evaluate whether use of AdjBW for initial UFH dosing reduces supratherapeutic aPTTs in cancer patients with ABW >130% of IBW and BMI ≤ 40 kg/m2. A new high intensity UFH protocol utilizing AdjBW UFH dosing was implemented on July 9, 2024. This single-center quality improvement study compared the pre- and post-intervention aPTTs in hospitalized cancer patients. In the bolus/transition cohort the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs decreased by 37% (RR 0.63; 95% CI: [0.46-0.86], p = 0.004 and the percentage of first therapeutic aPTTs increased by 82.1% (RR 1.82; 95% CI: [1.12-2.97], p = 0.03. In the no bolus cohort, the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs decreased by 39.2% (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.38-0.97, p = 0.04). Time to therapeutic aPTT was shorter in the post-implementation arm compared to pre-implementation. In conclusion, AdjBW-based UFH dosing significantly reduced the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs and decreased the time to first therapeutic aPTT in obese cancer patients on the high-intensity UFH protocol.

articles.title: Clot waveform analysis in haemostatic and systemic disorders: current applications and clinical potential.
articles.abstract: Clot waveform analysis (CWA), originate from conventional coagulation assays, particularly the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and prothrombin time (PT), offers enhanced sensitivity and dynamic profiling of haemostatic processes. By capturing real-time changes in clot formation kinetics, CWA patterns provide disease specific changes beyond traditional clotting time. It has potential clinical utility in identifying bleeding risk in inherited and acquired bleeding disorders, as well as prothrombotic states in condition such as infections and myocardial infarction. A unique APTT second-derivative curves have been reported in COVID-19 infection. In malignancy, it may help clinicians to mitigate the risk of developing thrombotic complications due to cancer-associated hypercoagulability. This review covers the principles, analytical parameters, and clinical applications of CWA. As evidence continues to grow, integrating CWA into standard coagulation testing algorithms, particularly with the use of artificial intelligence, may potentially lead to improvements in patient stratification, monitoring and management in both acute and chronic haemostatic disorders.

articles.title: High Spatial Resolution 23Na-MRI for Ischemic Brain Injury Detection.
articles.abstract: High spatial resolution sodium (23Na) imaging of brain lesions remains challenging due to the intrinsically low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 23Na-MRI compared with conventional proton (1H) MRI. In this preclinical mouse study, we developed a high-resolution 23Na-MRI platform based on a 14 T preclinical scanner using a dual-tuned head-implanted RF coil. This implanted coil configuration enabled longitudinal multimodal imaging in the same animal, including 11H-based T2-weighted anatomical and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and high-resolution 23Na-MRI. To evaluate the capability of this approach for detecting acute ischemic injury, ischemic stroke was induced in mice using the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. Brain-wide 23Na-MRI was acquired within the first 4 hours following MCAO at an in-plane resolution of 300 × 300 µm². Hyperintense 23Na-MRI signals were observed in the ischemic brain regions, presenting a contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) that exceeded that of T2-weighted images. Infarct regions can be well identified by elevated 23Na-MRI signal, which is spatially consistent with regions of reduced apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values, indicating water restriction in the ischemic core. This work established implanted dual-tuned 1H/23Na RF coils as a powerful approach for high-resolution 23Na-MRI readout, facilitating the early detection of ischemic brain injury.

articles.title: The Effects of Spiritual and Religious Interventions on Health Outcomes Among Mothers of Infants Hospitalized in Neonatal Intensive Care Units: A Systematic Review of Interventional Studies.
articles.abstract: The present systematic review aimed to systematically examine the available evidence regarding the effects of spiritual and religious interventions on the psychological and spiritual outcomes and adjustment of mothers of preterm infants or infants hospitalized in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs). This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, Magiran, and the Scientific Information Database (SID) were searched without any date restrictions from inception to August 17, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, clinical trials, and quasi-experimental studies that examined the effects of spiritual or religious interventions among mothers of preterm infants or infants hospitalized in NICUs. Study identification, screening, and selection were performed independently by two researchers, and the methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. The systematic review included 17 studies involving approximately 1070 mothers (533 in the intervention group and 537 in the control group) from a total of 1692 identified records. These comprised 14 randomized controlled trials or clinical trials and three quasi-experimental studies. The studies were conducted between 2014 and 2026, predominantly in Iran, with one study conducted in Turkey. The interventions included person-centered spiritual care, spiritual self-care education, theory-based spiritual care, spiritual intelligence education, prayer and Quran recitation, and culturally tailored spiritual programs based on Islamic beliefs and practices. Overall, the findings indicated that spiritual interventions were associated with reductions in anxiety, stress, psychological distress, and caregiver burden, as well as improvements in spiritual well-being, comfort, quality of life, hope, self-efficacy, mother-infant attachment, and post-traumatic growth. However, Variations in interventions and study characteristics limited direct comparisons and identification of the most effective approach. Spiritual interventions may offer a complementary, person-centered approach to nursing care. However, 16 of the 17 studies were conducted in Iran, limiting the generalizability of findings to other cultural and religious contexts.

articles.title: Cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1 is a novel prognostic biomarker in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibits great prognostic heterogeneity, necessitating the identification of high-risk patients for timely treatment. This study aimed to find novel prognostic biomarkers directly from diseased cardiac tissue to improve risk stratification of HCM. We utilized a myocardial transcriptome discovery cohort (n = 246; median follow-up 6.8 years) alongside two independent plasma validation cohorts (Beijing, n = 1,238; follow-up 2.5 years; Xi'an, n = 402; follow-up 4.8 years). The primary and secondary endpoints were cardiovascular death and sudden cardiac death (SCD), respectively. In the discovery cohort, myocardial expression of CECR1 (cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1, also known as ADA2, Adenosine Deaminase 2) demonstrated the strongest association with cardiovascular death (P = 9.6 × 10-5). Plasma CECR1 levels correlated modestly but significantly with myocardial expression. In the Beijing validation cohort, decreased plasma CECR1 predicted increased risks of cardiovascular death (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 3.731, P < 0.001) and SCD (adjusted HR 7.398, P < 0.001), with areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.720 and 0.798, respectively. These findings were replicated in the Xi'an validation cohort. Integrating plasma CECR1 into the HCM Risk-SCD model significantly enhanced its predictive performance, increasing the AUC from 0.723 to 0.845 (P = 0.031) in the Beijing validation cohort and consistently improving it from 0.600 to 0.781 (P = 0.018) in the Xi'an validation cohort. In conclusion, CECR1 represents a novel prognostic biomarker of HCM. Measurement of CECR1 may improve risk stratification by facilitating the identification of individuals at higher risk of cardiovascular mortality. CECR1 assessment may provide additional information for SCD risk evaluation and support clinical decision-making regarding implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy.

articles.title: Predictive and risk stratification performance of CCTA-derived pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events: retrospective development and prospective validation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the predictive efficacy and risk stratification potential of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent CCTA at our hospital between June 2017 and June 2020, with 5-year follow-up for MACE occurrence. Patients were grouped by MACE status. Machine learning was applied to construct and compare three models: PCAT radiomics model, fat attenuation index (FAI) model, and clinical model. Prospective validation was conducted in 578 patients with suspected CAD undergoing CCTA, who were stratified into high- and low-risk groups by the optimal cutoff of the PCAT radiomics model. The predictive and risk stratification performance of all models was assessed.

RESULTS: Fourteen PCAT radiomics features (5 first-order and 9 texture features) were finally screened. The PCAT radiomics model showed significantly superior MACE predictive performance over the FAI and clinical models (P < 0.001). Only the PCAT radiomics model identified significantly higher MACE risk in the high-risk versus low-risk group (HR=2.611, 95% CI: 1.806-3.775, P < 0.001), with progressively reduced MACE-free survival in the high-risk group during follow-up (P < 0.001). No such significant between-group differences were found in the FAI and clinical models (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The PCAT radiomics model showed favorable performance for predicting the composite MACE endpoint, which was predominantly driven by worsening stable or unstable angina, and provided better risk stratification than the FAI and clinical models.

articles.title: Rethinking glycemic monitoring: a HTA of glycated albumin for type 2 diabetes with stage IV-V CKD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to evaluate the multidimensional implications of introducing glycated albumin (GA) into Italian clinical practice as an innovative glycemic marker for monitoring type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in patients with stage IV-V chronic kidney disease (CKD), compared with the current gold standard, glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c).

METHODS: A Health Technology Assessment (HTA) was conducted from the perspective of the Italian National Health Service (NHS), adopting the EUnetHTA Core Model framework and using a comparative approach to assess the clinical and non-clinical domains of clinical pathways with and without the inclusion of GA. The analysis integrated evidence from a systematic literature review, health economics evaluations, and stakeholder perceptions gathered through validated questionnaires.

RESULTS: The systematic literature review demonstrated that GA more accurately identifies poor glycaemic control than HbA1c alone (52% vs. 19.2%), with benefits in reducing adverse events, in T2DM patients with advanced CKD. From an economic point of view, GA would lead to an overall economic saving equal to 2.02%, on annual basis, thus representing the strategy with the most favorable trade-off between costs and effectiveness. Healthcare professionals' perceptions (collected using a 7-point Likert scale, ranging from -3 to + 3), confirmed these findings, with higher ratings for GA in terms of safety (1.60 vs. 1.01) and effectiveness (2.12 vs. 1.02). Improvements were also reported in perceived quality of life for both patients and caregivers (2.00 vs. 0.88). Organizationally, although minimal investments would be required for training and equipment updates, the adoption of GA was associated with a significant enhancement in the management of the patient care pathway (2.25 vs. 0.63).

CONCLUSIONS: The results highlight the strategic value of GA as a complementary biomarker in the monitoring of glycemic control among T2DM patients with advanced CKD, offering clinical benefits and potential efficiency gains for the healthcare system.

articles.title: HPV-associated extracellular vesicles and the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms of immune modulation and translational implications.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus infections are a major cause of cervical cancer and are also associated with several anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Persistent infection with high-risk HPV types and sustained expression of viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 contribute to malignant transformation. Extracellular vesicles are increasingly recognized as important mediators of intercellular communication and can transfer proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and other regulatory molecules between cells. HPV-associated changes in EV cargo, such as viral transcripts, may influence immune and stromal cells within the tumor microenvironment. Experimental studies have implicated HPV-associated EVs in the regulation of dendritic cell function, macrophage polarization, T-cell responses, immune checkpoint signaling, chronic inflammation, and mechanisms related to viral persistence and immune evasion. Cell-based and preclinical studies also suggest that EVs released by HPV-positive tumor cells may contribute to related disorders including angiogenesis and metastatic progression. On the other hand, human studies have primarily provided observational evidence linking EV-associated molecular profiles with HPV status or disease characteristics. Beyond these mechanistic insights, a growing body of work explores the translational potential of EVs, including their use as liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as engineered delivery platforms such as Nefmut-based vesicles carrying HPV16 E7 that elicit protective CD8 + T-cell responses in preclinical models. This narrative review, with emphasis on tumor-immune interactions, and also discusses emerging diagnostic and therapeutic applications together with the methodological and clinical barriers that must be addressed before EV-based strategies can be translated into routine practice.

articles.title: Polihexanide 0.8 mg/mL to Manage Acanthamoeba Keratitis in Clinical Practice: A Multicentre, Retrospective Study in Poland.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acanthamoeba keratitis (AK) is a rare, sight-threatening corneal disease caused by Acanthamoeba spp., ubiquitous free-living amoebae. The purpose of this study is to present the first real-world experience in Poland of AK management with polihexanide 0.8 mg/mL (PHMB 0.08% w/w).

METHODS: This was a retrospective descriptive analysis of clinical records from patients with AK who received PHMB 0.08% (Akantior®) as part of their management for AK (i.e. with other interventions if clinically needed) through an early access programme in two centres in Poland. Disease characteristics, treatment details and clinical outcomes after PHMB 0.08% treatment were assessed. AK resolution was defined as the absence of clinical signs of active infection or inflammation of the cornea after epithelial closure, along with in vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM) criteria.

RESULTS: A total of 11 patients were included (age range: 16-54 years; stage ≥ II disease: 81.8%; best-corrected visual acuity [BCVA] ≤ 0.3: 90.9%). Prior treatments consisted mostly of antibiotics and corticosteroids, and 27.3% of patients received prior anti-amoebic therapy (chlorhexidine 0.02% ± propamidine 0.1%). The mean delay to PHMB 0.08% therapy start was 93.7 days. Overall, 10 of 11 (90.9%) patients achieved disease resolution after a mean 187.8 days after symptom onset (range: 60-684 days). The remaining patient was still receiving treatment at time of writing. BCVA improved in all cases of AK resolution. No safety events of clinical relevance were detected. AK disease course and management differed across patients, including cases of bacterial co-infections and the use of various pharmacological and surgical interventions along with PHMB 0.08% therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: We report the use of PHMB 0.08% for AK management in routine clinical practice in a cohort of patients with relatively advanced disease and poor vision, where most patients achieved disease resolution with BCVA improvements and no clinically relevant safety events were observed.

articles.title: Estimating the effect of familiarity in surgical teams on procedure time under a causal graphical model.
articles.abstract: This study estimates the causal impact of surgical team familiarity on surgery duration across various procedures in a hospital, under an assumed Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure. While existing literature indicates that greater familiarity among surgical team members, measured by their shared work experience, is linked to reduced surgery times, these studies typically focus on a specific type of surgical procedure and only suggest a correlational relationship. Our study is the first to examine the hospital-wide relationship between surgical team familiarity and procedure duration using a formal causal inference framework. To explore this relationship, team familiarity is measured based on interaction frequency, and data across procedures are standardized to facilitate analysis via structural causal modeling and regression analysis. An analysis of 33,374 procedures performed in a high-volume academic medical center in the US from January 2017 to November 2023 reveals a negative causal relationship between surgeon-scrub familiarity and surgery duration under our DAG assumptions. Specifically, increasing familiarity by one standard deviation leads to a reduction of 1.9 to 3.7 minutes in surgery duration. Similar, albeit smaller, effects are observed for surgeon-circulator familiarity, whereas no significant impact is found for scrub-circulator familiarity. To our knowledge, this is the first study to estimate the causal effect of surgical team familiarity across an entire hospital's surgical portfolio under the assumptions of a DAG, moving beyond prior correlational analyses limited to specific specialties or methods. Ultimately, the study reveals that improving team familiarity, particularly between surgeons and scrub nurses, could hold significant implications for improving surgical team efficiency. This is especially relevant in high-volume hospitals, where even minor time savings can accumulate significantly, underscoring the value of leveraging team familiarity to optimize performance in hospital operating rooms.

articles.title: Identification of broad-spectrum inhibitors for the cryptic binding site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 across multiple variants using molecular dynamics simulation.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Non-structural protein 1 (NSP1) is a critical viral virulence factor expressed early during SARS-CoV-2 infection that facilitates host immune evasion by supressing host gene expression through its interaction with the 40S ribosomal subunit. NSP1 occludes the mRNA entry channel, thereby inhibiting translation of host transcripts while selectively permitting viral mRNA translation. Recent advances in structural biology have revealed previously unrecognized cryptic binding pocket within NSP1, expanding the repertoire of viable drug targets. In this study, we systematically investigated an allosteric pocket of NSP1 as a novel intervention strategy to disrupt NSP1-mRNA interactions. Virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs identified sorafenib as a promising allosteric inhibitor. For the broad-spectrum efficacy evaluation, sorafenib inhibitory potential against a variety of clinically relevant NSP1 mutants was tested. Detailed molecular dynamics simulations of the wild-type and mutant systems showed that sorafenib binding leads to different conformational and dynamic changes, that result in protein stabilization. Residue-level fluctuation analyses indicated that sorafenib had relatively stable interactions within the allosteric pocket even in the presence of destabilizing mutations, suggesting resilience against mutation-driven resistance. We have identified allosteric targeting as a viable approach to blocking the functional role of NSP1 in host translation shutdown. Sorafenib emerges as a promising broad-spectrum NSP1 inhibitor for additional experimental testing and development of NSP1-directed antiviral therapeutics.

METHODS: All FDA-approved drugs were first optimized using the semi-empirical PM6 method. The optimized structures were subsequently subjected to virtual screening against the cryptic binding site of NSP1 using AutoDock. MD simulations of the selected protein-ligand complexes were carried out using GROMACSv2023. Binding free energies were estimated using the MM/PBSA method and steered molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate ligand dissociation. Post-MD trajectory analyses were performed using various built-in GROMACS tools and PyMol.
