articles.title: Farnesol, lyticase, and tyrosol against Candida albicans biofilms: Interactions with fluconazole and micafungin.
articles.abstract: Biofilm-associated reductions in antifungal susceptibility complicate Candida albicans infection management. This in vitro study assessed farnesol, lyticase, and tyrosol, alone and in combination with fluconazole or micafungin, against established C. albicans biofilms. We screened 25 clinical isolates from patients with suspected vulvovaginal candidiasis using crystal violet staining. Sessile minimum inhibitory concentrations (SMICs), defined as ≥80% reductions in metabolic activity, were determined by a tetrazolium reduction assay. Checkerboard interactions were evaluated using fractional inhibitory concentration indices, with upper-bound estimates for fluconazole due to single-agent values reaching the assay ceiling. Twenty-one isolates (84%) formed biofilms. All three compounds alone reduced biofilm metabolic activity. Fluconazole SMICs were ≥64 µg/mL, while micafungin SMICs ranged from 0.5-2 µg/mL. Fluconazole-farnesol and micafungin-farnesol combinations demonstrated synergy in 61.9% and 57.1% of isolates, respectively, with no observed antagonism. Farnesol reduced fluconazole SMICs to 2-8 µg/mL and median micafungin SMICs from 1 to 0.25 µg/mL (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Micafungin-lyticase interactions were predominantly indifferent (90.5%). In contrast, tyrosol combinations were antagonistic with fluconazole in 33.3% of isolates and with micafungin in 28.6%. Farnesol combinations consistently exhibited the most potent antibiofilm effects. However, the small sample size, unreplicated biofilm susceptibility assays, and estimated fluconazole interaction indices necessitate cautious interpretation. Future research should investigate reproducibility, safety, and in vivo efficacy.

articles.title: AI-Enabled Digital Stethoscope for Early Detection of Congenital Heart Disease: Prospective Study.
articles.abstract: Early detection of congenital heart disease (CHD) is critical, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to congenital cardiac services is limited. While auscultation remains a first-line screening tool, its accuracy is operator dependent. Advances in digital stethoscopes and artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance diagnostic performance. To evaluate the accuracy of an AI-based algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope for detecting CHD in children and young adults, using echocardiography as the reference standard. In this prospective single centre study, heart sounds were recorded from 721 subjects (382 with CHD, 339 controls) using the digital stethoscope at four standard auscultatory sites. Of these, 301 recordings were used for algorithm training and 420 for blinded forward testing, which was divided temporally with the data collected in first 5 months used for training and the data collected after that used for forward testing. Recordings were denoised, transformed into mel-spectrograms, and analyzed using a convolutional neural network (CovNN) to classify CHD probability. A threshold probability of > 0.5 across > 2 sites was used to predict CHD. Performance was compared against echocardiography. In forward testing, the AI algorithm correctly identified 222 of 233 CHD cases and 171 of 187 controls, yielding a sensitivity of 95.2% and specificity of 91.4%. The algorithm remained effective in noisy environments and in uncooperative children, where conventional auscultation is challenging. An AI algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for CHD detection in children and young adults. By leveraging mel-spectrogram features, it overcomes key limitations of isolated time-domain or frequency domain analysis and shows promise as a scalable, non-invasive screening tool for early CHD detection, particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Effect of Intravenous Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide on Left Ventricular Function After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite timely reperfusion and guideline-directed therapies, the recovery of left ventricular function after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains suboptimal. Adjunctive metabolic therapy may enhance post-infarction cardiac repair. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺), a key regulator of cellular bioenergetics and redox homeostasis, has cardioprotective effects in experimental ischemia-reperfusion injury. However, its clinical impact in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.

METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 120 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI were assigned to receive intravenous NAD⁺ (10 mg/day) or placebo for 7 days, in addition to standard medical therapy. The primary endpoint was the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) at 30 days. The secondary endpoints included N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels at 7 and 30 days, echocardiographic parameters at 30 days, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) at 6 months.

RESULTS: At 30 days, the NAD⁺ group demonstrated a modest but significant improvement in LVEF compared with the placebo group (56.32 ± 8.04% vs. 53.37 ± 8.12%, p = 0.048). NT-proBNP levels were lower in the NAD⁺ group at follow-up. However, findings for LV remodeling parameters were mixed, and no significant between-group difference was observed in 6-month MACCE rates.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term intravenous NAD⁺ therapy following primary PCI improved left ventricular systolic function and reduced NT-proBNP levels in patients with STEMI. These findings suggest that restoring NAD⁺ availability may facilitate post-ischemic cardiac recovery, potentially through mechanisms related to mitochondrial energy metabolism and NAD⁺-dependent stress-response signaling. Larger trials are required to confirm its long-term clinical benefits and elucidate the underlying biological pathways.

REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier number ChiCTR2200059333.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of the Normandy score for infective endocarditis in native bone and joint infections.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The Normandy score was developed to estimate the risk of typical cardiac lesions of infective endocarditis (IE) among patients with native bone and joint infections (NBJI). The aim of this study was to externally validate the Normandy score for the prediction typical cardiac lesions and IE in patients with NBJI.

METHODS: Retrospective study.

SETTING: This study included adult patients with NBJI (2014-2025). Typical cardiac lesions included vegetations, abscess, leaflet perforation, prosthetic valve dehiscence, aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, or fistula identified by echocardiography or cardiac CT, and abnormal metabolic activity on [18F]FDG-PET/CT. IE was diagnosed according to the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria. The primary outcome was the negative likelihood ratio (NLR), with a threshold of < 0.10 to safely rule out IE or typical cardiac lesions.

RESULTS: Among 462 NBJI episodes, typical cardiac lesions were identified in 101 (22%) and IE was diagnosed in 151 (33%). The Normandy score classified 415 (90%) episodes as high risk compared to 450 (97%) that actually had echocardiography. Against the typical cardiac lesion reference standard, the NLR was 0.08 (95% CI 0.01-0.56). Against the IE reference standard, the NLR was 0.14 (0.04-0.44).

CONCLUSIONS: In this highly selected population (89% bacteremic, 33% with IE), the Normandy score met the prespecified NLR threshold for typical cardiac lesions, but not for IE overall. Because it classified 90% of episodes as high risk, it would have reduced echocardiography by only 7 percentage points A more discriminatory prediction tool is needed to meaningfully optimize resource utilization in this population.

articles.title: Intercellular Mitochondria Transfer as a Bioenergetic Rescue Mechanism in CNS Injury: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Potential, and Translational Barriers.
articles.abstract: Acute central nervous system (CNS) injuries, including ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury, and spinal cord injury, are characterized by profound mitochondrial dysfunction that drives secondary neuronal damage through ATP depletion, oxidative stress, and calcium dysregulation. Neuronal survival is critically dependent on mitochondrial integrity, making bioenergetic failure a central determinant of injury progression. In this context, intercellular mitochondria transfer has emerged as a potential adaptive mechanism through which functional mitochondria are delivered from donor cells-primarily astrocytes, microglia, and mesenchymal stem cells-to metabolically compromised neurons. Mitochondria transfer occurs via both contact-dependent pathways, such as tunneling nanotubes, and contact-independent mechanisms, including extracellular vesicles and free mitochondrial release. These processes are regulated by signaling pathways such as CD38/cADPR-mediated calcium flux and MIRO1-dependent mitochondrial trafficking, facilitating organelle mobilization and uptake. Functionally, transferred mitochondria have been associated with improved oxidative phosphorylation, reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, altered calcium homeostasis, and modulation of survival pathways including PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signaling in selected experimental models; however, the extent to which these effects are directly dependent on mitochondria transfer remains incompletely established. Preclinical evidence across multiple CNS injury models demonstrates improved neuronal viability, enhanced synaptic function, and attenuation of neurodegenerative processes following mitochondria transfer. However, whether mitochondria transfer represents a primary driver of neurorepair or a secondary compensatory response remains unresolved. In addition, inconsistencies in mechanistic pathways, variability in transfer efficiency, and limited reproducibility across experimental systems hinder translational interpretation. Therapeutic approaches including exogenous mitochondria transplantation, stem cell-mediated delivery, and bioengineered mitochondrial systems show promise but face substantial barriers related to targeting specificity, mitochondrial viability, immunogenicity, and lack of standardized protocols. This review critically evaluates the molecular mechanisms, functional consequences, and therapeutic potential of intercellular mitochondria transfer in CNS injury. It further highlights key limitations and knowledge gaps that must be addressed to determine whether mitochondria transfer can be effectively harnessed as a clinically viable strategy for neuro-restoration.

articles.title: Risk of Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Psoriasis, Psoriatic Arthritis, and/or Other Forms of Spondyloarthritis: A Cohort of 72,291 Biologic New Users.
articles.journal: BioDrugs : clinical immunotherapeutics, biopharmaceuticals and gene therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of biologic therapies (biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs [bDMARD]) used in psoriasis (Pso), psoriatic arthritis (PsA), and other forms of spondyloarthritis (SpA) on the risk of major cardiovascular events (MACE) remains controversial.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the risk of MACE after initiation of a bDMARD among patients with Pso, PsA, or SpA, in a real-world clinical setting.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults with Pso, PsA, or SpA who initiated a bDMARD (tumor necrosis factor inhibitors [TNFi]; interleukin [IL] inhibitors: IL-12/23i, IL-23i, IL-17i) between 1 July, 2016, and 31 July, 2023 were eligible for inclusion. The primary outcome was incident MACE, defined as cardiovascular death and/or hospitalization for acute myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke. Inverse probability-weighted Cox models were used to estimate weighted hazard ratios and their confidence intervals. Models were further adjusted for time-varying concomitant treatments, treatment indication, year of initiation, and prior non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. An interaction term between bDMARD exposure and history of cardiovascular disease was included.

RESULTS: A total of 72,291 patients were included (mean age 46.1 ± 14.2 years, 49.4% female): 10,703 IL-17i (14.8%), 7952 IL-23i (11.0%), 5962 IL-12/23i (8.2%), and 47,674TNFi (66.0%). Compared with initiators of other bDMARDs, TNFi initiators were younger and had fewer comorbidities and cardiovascular risk factors at baseline. During follow-up, 438 patients (0.6%) experienced a MACE, including 107 (0.1%) cardiovascular deaths. The median time to event was 13.5 months (interquartile range, 5.1-30.4). In crude analyses, initiation of IL-17i, IL-23i, and IL-12/23i was associated with a higher risk of MACE compared withTNFi drugs. However, among patients without a history of cardiovascular disease, after inverse probability of treatment weighting and adjustment, no significant association was observed (weighted hazard ratio [95% confidence interval]: 0.90 [0.57-1.43] for IL-12/23i, 1.12 [0.66-1.88] for IL-23i, and 1.07 [0.74-1.55] for IL-17i). Findings held across most sensitivity analyses, except for the short-term analysis restricted to the first 6 months after treatment initiation, in which a trend toward a higher MACE risk with IL-17i was observed. A trend toward a higher MACE risk with IL-17i was also observed among men, patients aged ≥ 50 years, and those with a history of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. However, the number of events was low, and the results did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: No significant increase in MACE risk was observed with IL-12/23i, IL-23i, or IL-17i compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors. However, the study lacked sufficient power to draw definitive conclusions regarding a possible increased risk associated with IL-17i in patients with a high baseline cardiovascular risk profile, or the potentiation of this risk by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use.

articles.title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of SHR-2004, a Novel Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: An Open-Label Phase 1b Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SHR-2004, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting factor XI (FXI), demonstrates potential for preventing and treating thrombotic events with reduced bleeding risk. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of SHR-2004 in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).

METHODS: In this open-label dose-escalation phase 1b study, patients with AF aged ≥ 40 and < 80 years with a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥ 1 (male) or ≥ 2 (female) were enrolled to receive six doses of SHR-2004. The primary endpoints were safety and tolerability. PK and PD parameters, including activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and FXI activity, were also assessed.

RESULTS: From 10 April 2024 to 6 May 2024, ten patients were enrolled to receive SHR-2004 (180 mg subcutaneously, every 2 weeks), with a median age of 68.0 years, and male being in the majority (9/10). The median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 2.5 (range 1-6). The trial was terminated after completion of the 180 mg cohort. SHR-2004 was well tolerated. Treatment-emergent adverse events (AEs) occurred in eight (80.0%) patients, and treatment-related AEs were reported in six (60.0%) patients. All AEs were mild or moderate. Notably, no major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events were reported. Plasma exposure of SHR-2004 increased rapidly after administration and reached steady state by day 57 with the geometric mean (CV%) plasma concentration of 24,000 (26.4) ng/mL. This exposure resulted in median FXI activity after the first dose of 1.40% (IQR 1.40-1.40%). The outcomes of PD effects, FXI activity and aPTT prolongation, reached a plateau during the treatment period from day 3 to day 85 indicating that the 180 mg dosage regimen achieved and maintained therapeutic pharmacodynamic steady state.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple subcutaneous doses of SHR-2004 were generally well tolerated in patients with AF. These preliminary findings support further clinical development of SHR-2004 in this population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT06280768. Trial registration date: 28 February 2024.

articles.title: The effect of acupuncture-rehabilitation therapy on brain functional plasticity in motor aphasia after ischemic stroke: a randomized clinical neuroimaging trial.
articles.abstract: Motor aphasia is the most prevalent type of aphasia following ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and underlying neural mechanisms of acupuncture-rehabilitation (A-R) therapy on motor aphasia after IS. Twenty-six patients with post-IS motor aphasia were randomly assigned to either the A-R group or the Conventional Rehabilitation (CR) group in a 1:1 ratio, and matched by age and gender with 26 healthy controls (HCs). The CR group received standard treatment and language training, while the A-R group additionally underwent scalp acupoint cluster acupuncture. Behavioral assessments and Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (BOLD-fMRI) scans were conducted before and after the four-week intervention to evaluate therapeutic outcomes and underlying mechanisms. Compared to HCs, patients exhibited decreased Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations (ALFF) in the right precuneus (p < 0.05) and reduced Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) in the left precuneus/postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). Enhanced functional connectivity (FC) was observed in regions including the left Broca's area and right superior temporal gyrus, left Broca's area and right inferior frontal orbitalis gyrus, left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus, left Broca's area and right postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). After intervention, significant improvements were observed in Aphasia Quotient (AQ) scores and sub-item performance in both patient groups (p < 0.05), with the A-R group showing greater gains in AQ and spontaneous speech scores compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FMRI results indicated a significant increase in mean ALFF (mALFF) in the left inferior temporal gyrus after A-R treatment (p < 0.05) compared to before, and higher szReHo in the left anterior central gyrus compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FC between the left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus decreased in the A-R group (p < 0.05). Additionally, a negative correlation was observed between the right anterior central gyrus and listening comprehension (r = -0.574, p = 0.020). The findings suggest that both A-R and CR therapies enhance language function in patients with motor aphasia post-IS, with A-R therapy demonstrating superior efficacy. The therapeutic mechanism of A-R likely involves activating left hemisphere brain regions, suppressing right hemisphere activity, and restoring hemispheric balance to facilitate functional recovery.

articles.title: Economic Evaluation Methods in Post-Injury Care: A Global Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal of Their Suitability for Decision-Making.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Over 4 million people (8% of all deaths) worldwide die from traumatic injuries annually. For people aged 5-29 years, three of the top five causes of death are injury related, namely road traffic injuries, homicide, and suicide. Investments in injury care need to consider budget constraints, and economic evaluation studies can be employed to understand the costs and outcomes of competing interventions for injury care. However, these studies should be designed to meet the information requirements of decision makers. This systematic review aims to critically appraise the methodologies used in economic evaluations of injury care, assessing their suitability for informing decision-making.

METHODS: We conducted a global systematic review in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. We searched six databases, from inception to June 2023, for eligible full economic evaluations of injury care. The primary population was persons who have suffered acute traumatic injuries. Only full economic evaluations were eligible for inclusion, and studies that met the inclusion criteria were appraised using the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards statement and critiqued against the decision-making guidelines developed by Sculpher et al. (2009).

RESULTS: A total of 259 studies were included in the final review. An overwhelming majority of the studies (92%) were conducted in high-income countries, and they predominantly evaluated in-hospital interventions (93% vs 1% pre-hospital and 6% post-discharge). Fractures were the most commonly studied injury type, while the provider perspective was the most frequent analytic perspective. We found that just over half of the studies synthesised effectiveness evidence from multiple sources; nearly a quarter of the studies compared more than two competing interventions; and 84% of the studies considered costs and outcomes over an appropriate time horizon.

DISCUSSION: We found key gaps in the existing evidence: limited synthesis of evidence to inform treatment effects, inadequate alignment of time horizons with intervention outcomes, geographic disparities in the scope and quality of evidence, and limited coverage across the full patient pathway. These limitations hinder the usefulness of study findings in decision-making. Future economic evaluations should address key gaps to improve the utility of economic evaluations in healthcare decision-making.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42022351978.

articles.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: a global multisociety consensus on definitions.
authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)
American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)
Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL)
Latin American Association for the Study of the Liver (ALEH)
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA)
articles.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

articles.title: Correction: Diabetes-related foot disease and sarcopenia-related traits: evidence from US and Chinese cohorts and mendelian randomization.
Berberine improves cognitive impairment in diabetic mice by mitigating 4-HNE-induced oxidative stress and enhancing hippocampal insulin sensitivity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Berberine (BBR), a component of the Chinese herb, is used for treating diabetes and diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD), although the underlying mechanism is still unclear. Diabetes is a metabolic disease that raises the risk of developing cognitive impairment. The hippocampus within the forebrain has large number of insulin receptors linked to cognitive function and is crucial in the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative disorders. Herein, we examined whether BBR could improve DACD and explored the possible underlying mechanisms.

METHOD: Streptozotocin (STZ) was used to induce diabetes in mice. BBR was administered before and after STZ administration for 4 weeks. The impact of BBR on 4-hydroxy 2-nonenal (4-HNE) adducts formation in diabetic mice was analyzed. Further, insulin signaling pathway was assessed to uncover the underlying molecular mechanism of BBR.

RESULTS: BBR significantly ameliorates cognitive dysfunction in diabetic mice by decreasing 4-HNE adduct formation while increasing the levels of insulin and insulin receptor in the hippocampus of diabetic mice, indicating increased insulin uptake in the brain. BBR treatment increased the mRNA levels of PI3K, AKT, mTOR, and S6 kinase in the diabetic mice hippocampus, while decreasing BAD and NF-κB mRNA levels and tau hyperphosphorylation. Moreover, BBR increased the mRNA levels of CREB and CBP in the diabetic mice confirming the neuro-regenerative role of BBR.

CONCLUSION: BBR improves hippocampal insulin resistance by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and improving tau hyperphosphorylation in diabetic mice. Our study highlights a novel therapeutic target in DACD and a new mechanism of action of BBR.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of production and kinetic assay conditions and parameters for SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro): a systematic review.
articles.abstract: The main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 plays a crucial role in the viral replication cycle and is a key target for COVID-19 antiviral drugs. In this review, we conducted an extensive bibliographic search on the main challenges and experimental limitations reported in the production and biochemical characterization of the Mpro. A large variability in the kinetic parameters was revealed, which compromises comparisons across various studies and the evaluation of inhibitor efficacy. The studies indicate that these discrepancies are mainly associated with experimental limitations, such as low substrate solubility, optical irregularity due to the inner-filter effect, and variations in the oligomeric state of Mpro. This review summarizes and discusses the different strategies for Mpro expression in Escherichia coli and purification, with emphasis on obtaining an N-terminal tag-free enzyme, essential for homodimerization into a highly active form for structural and functional characterization. The main FRET-based substrates used in enzymatic assays were compiled and analyzed, as well as alternative methodologies for assessing Mpro enzymatic activity. Furthermore, the effects of assay conditions, such as buffer composition, pH, and the presence of reducing agents were addressed. The intrinsic structural features of Mpro that impact its catalytic function are discussed, including functional asymmetry in substrate binding and the positive allosteric cooperation between monomers. Overall, this review provides a critical and integrated perspective on the main experimental limitations in the production and characterization of Mpro, applicable to other proteases, contributing to the standardization of approaches and advances in the development of more effective inhibitors.

articles.title: A comprehensive review of mixed-species biofilm infections and innovative therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Mixed-species biofilm infections are important causes of persistent and difficult-to-treat infections. Compared with monospecies biofilms, mixed-species communities contain microorganisms with different physiological and genetic characteristics that interact through metabolic cooperation, chemical signaling, competition, and modification of the local environment. These interactions, together with the EPS matrix, physiological heterogeneity, and HGT, can increase antimicrobial tolerance, contributing to treatment failure and infection recurrence. Polymicrobial biofilms are associated with chronic wounds, respiratory infections, catheter- and device-associated infections, and other persistent infections. However, treatment of polymicrobial biofilms remains challenging because their complex structure and interspecies interactions can reduce antimicrobial efficacy. This review summarizes the clinical significance, formation, and persistence of mixed-species biofilms and discusses recent therapeutic strategies for their control. We also discuss recent approaches for controlling polymicrobial biofilms, including natural compounds, QS inhibition, CRISPR-Cas-based approaches, biofilm matrix targeting, metabolic and nutrient disruption, nanotechnology, and phage therapy. Recent studies show that these approaches can inhibit biofilm formation, disrupt established biofilms, enhance antimicrobial activity, and selectively target specific microbial populations. However, their effectiveness varies with microbial composition, biofilm maturity, matrix characteristics, and treatment conditions. Overall, current evidence supports the development of targeted and combination-based strategies for mixed-species biofilms. Further studies using clinically relevant models are needed to exactly define treatment efficacy and support the translation of these approaches into clinical practice.

articles.title: Auricular point acupressure for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is common and persistent, with limited management options. This trial primarily examines whether auricular point acupressure (APA) improved CIPN outcomes versus usual care; a secondary pragmatic aim compared in-person mobile support (mAPA) with virtual (vAPA) delivery.

METHODS: Two hundred twenty-seven cancer survivors with CIPN were randomized to mAPA (n = 80), vAPA (n = 75), or usual care (n = 72). Both APA arms received the same 4-week auricular point protocol; mAPA received in-person seed placement, and vAPA received video instruction for self-placement, with one coaching session for both. Usual care was standard oncologic and supportive care with no study-delivered APA. Primary outcome was a ≥20% reduction from baseline in an individualized composite outcome (ICO); each participant's highest-rated symptom-by-location item at baseline. Secondary outcomes were neuropathy interference, functional status, and quality of life. Intention-to-treat analyses used generalized estimating equations with multiple imputation and delta-adjusted sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: At Week 1, both APA arms exceeded usual care (mAPA OR = 2.60, 95% CI 1.27-5.33; vAPA OR = 3.22; 95% CI 1.48-7.01; p < 0.01). The mAPA advantage persisted at Week 2 (OR = 2.49, p = 0.02). For neuropathy interference, mAPA benefits exceeded usual care every week (OR = 3.29-4.28, all p < 0.01). Among exploratory domains, anxiety, depression, and pain interference improved only in mAPA.

CONCLUSION: APA produced a short-lived advantage in CIPN severity and more consistent improvement in interference, specifically with in-person delivery. Findings are preliminary: no blinding or attention control, differential attrition (52% vAPA versus 96% usual care), and exploratory quality-of-life analyses.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, ID NCT04920097 registered on 3 June 2021.

articles.title: Preoperative prediction of major postoperative morbidity after ventral hernia repair: a parsimonious model developed and internally validated in a single-center cohort.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Major morbidity after ventral hernia repair (VHR) is common, yet preoperative tools to estimate it at the point of surgical decision-making are scarce. We aimed to develop and internally validate a parsimonious model predicting 90-day Clavien-Dindo ≥ II morbidity using only preoperative variables.

METHODS: We analyzed 1,263 ventral hernia repairs (511 incisional, 752 primary) from a prospectively maintained institutional registry (2020-2026). Nine prespecified routinely available preoperative predictors - age, BMI, active smoking, type 2 diabetes, ASA ≥ III, incisional hernia phenotype, recurrent hernia, large defect (≥ 4 cm) and emergency surgery - were entered into a LASSO logistic regression model. Discrimination (area under the ROC curve, AUC) and calibration (graphically, Brier score) were assessed; internal validation used bootstrap resampling (B = 1,000). A simplified integer score was derived.

RESULTS: Major morbidity occurred in 121 patients (9.6%). All nine were retained, emergency surgery and large defect size weighing most heavily. The model showed good discrimination (apparent AUC 0.766, 95% CI 0.718-0.810; optimism-corrected 0.751) and satisfactory calibration (Brier score 0.076). The score stratified patients across a wide gradient, from 4.3% observed morbidity in the lowest-risk group to 40.0% in the highest. A binary threshold (≥ 35 points) classified 21.9% of patients as high-risk, with a 5.6-fold higher morbidity rate and a negative predictive value of 95.2%.

CONCLUSION: A parsimonious nine-variable preoperative score predicts 90-day major morbidity after VHR with good discrimination and calibration. Its high negative predictive value may help identify patients potentially suitable for ambulatory or fast-track pathways. External multicenter validation is required before routine adoption.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes with High-Volume Hemodiafiltration Versus High-Flux Hemodialysis Across Clinical Subgroups: Results from the CONVINCE Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-volume hemodiafiltration (HDF) improves survival and attenuates decline in selected patient-reported outcome (PRO) domains versus high-flux hemodialysis (HD). Whether benefits differ across clinically relevant subgroups remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a prespecified subgroup analysis of the multicenter CONVINCE randomized controlled trial comparing high-volume post-dilution HDF (≥23 L/session) with high-flux HD in adults receiving maintenance dialysis. Eight PROMIS domains were assessed quarterly over a median follow-up of 30 months. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal PRO changes and treatment-by-subgroup interactions by prespecified baseline characteristics: age, sex, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, dialysis vintage, vascular access type, and residual urine volume. Joint-model sensitivity analyses of all eight longitudinal PROMIS trajectories and time to death assessed informative dropout due to death.

RESULTS: Of 1360 randomized participants, 1211 with baseline and follow-up PRO assessments were included. PRO treatment effects were broadly consistent across prespecified clinical subgroups, without evidence of clinically meaningful heterogeneity. Models adjusted for baseline sociodemographic and clinical characteristics showed nominal treatment-by-subgroup interactions for dialysis vintage and physical function (P = 0.03), age and pain interference (P = 0.02), and dialysis vintage and sleep disturbance (P = 0.04). Joint-model sensitivity analyses accounting for informative dropout due to mortality reproduced the first two interactions and identified nominal interactions for vascular access type and sleep disturbance (P = 0.03) and cardiovascular disease status and cognitive function (P = 0.05). Interactions were modest in magnitude, exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and not consistently observed across related PROMIS domains.

CONCLUSIONS: This prespecified exploratory subgroup analysis found no convincing evidence of clinically meaningful treatment-effect heterogeneity across baseline characteristics examined. Nominal interactions were unadjusted for multiple comparisons and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Findings should not guide selection or exclusion of patients for high-volume HDF based on patient-reported outcomes.

articles.title: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome in Youth: Early Detection, Management, and Innovative Frameworks to Shift Care Paradigms.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders, particularly those related to abnormal adiposity and insulin resistance, are among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite significant improvements in detection and treatment over the past 30 years. Epidemiological and clinical trial data have increasingly shown that these conditions are causally interconnected and whose individual treatments provide additional indirect beneficial effects on morbidity and mortality risk reduction. The American Heart Association coined the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome to better conceptualize that cardiovascular disease is a multisystem disease with major contributions from kidney and metabolic health. This provides a useful framework to guide opportunities for prevention and care optimization. As CKM syndrome and its antecedents can begin from preconception through early childhood, this new syndrome is particularly valuable for conceptualizing health in youth because it incorporates the developmental origins of health and disease, life course, and social determinants of health frameworks. This review contextualizes recent advances in understanding CKM syndrome screening and management in pediatric populations and introduces an innovative approach to integrating important frameworks to shape future clinical care models integrated with research strategies using transdisciplinary teams within academic learning healthcare systems. We emphasize innovations such as autonomy-focused coaching in transitioning care from pediatric to adult periods of life and a conceptual roadmap for healthcare systems as they design, implement, and evaluate these models of care. We introduce an opportunity to better leverage the value added by patients, families, caregivers, communities, and other key healthcare system partners such as dietitians, pharmacists, social workers, counselors, and nurse coordinators. This transdisciplinary care model can transform current CKM health paradigms to ultimately equitably optimize CKM health and quality of life across the life course, through a shared longitudinal plan that empowers patients with agency and autonomy to define and achieve their goals.

articles.title: Practice variation and interdisciplinary care gaps in idiopathic intracranial hypertension : A cross-sectional nationwide survey.
authors: AN4IH Network of the Austrian Neurological Society (ÖGN) Neuroophthalmology Working Group
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a rare disorder requiring coordinated interdisciplinary management. The Austrian Network for IIH (AN4IH) has developed consensus-based recommendations to standardize its diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring; however, their uptake in clinical practice remains unassessed.

METHODS: Between October 2025 and January 2026, all 1460 members of the Austrian Neurological Society (ÖGN) were invited to complete an anonymized online survey on diagnostic and therapeutic practices and AN4IH recommendation awareness, with a response rate of 3.7%. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: Of the 54 respondents 64.8% worked in a hospital setting. Nearly 80% treated 5 or fewer IIH patients per year. Low confidence in IIH management was reported by 33.3%, with a tendency toward greater confidence in hospital-based physicians (odds ratio, OR 2.55, 95% confidence interval, CI 0.68-9.86) and those treating 6 or more patients annually (OR 2.62, 95% CI 0.46-27.96). Interdisciplinary pathways were lacking in 55.6% of settings. Routine diagnostics included brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI, 98.1%), neurological examination (94.4%), ophthalmological assessment (85.2%), and lumbar puncture (77.8%). Venous MR angiography (53.7%), perimetry (46.3%), optical coherence tomography (31.5%), and optic nerve sonography (14.8%) were used less consistently. Acetazolamide (98.1%) and weight reduction (90.7%) were the dominant treatment strategies. The AN4IH recommendations were partially known to 44.5% of respondents. Of those, 95.8% perceived them as a valuable clinical resource.

DISCUSSION: Substantial practice variation in IIH management was observed among survey respondents. The AN4IH recommendations are widely perceived as supportive and may help standardize care. Yet implementation requires broader interdisciplinary structures in specialized settings.

articles.title: Senotherapeutics for Age-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders: A Systematic Review of Preclinical Evidence.
articles.abstract: Aging is an important risk factor for musculoskeletal disorders such as osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, and sarcopenia. Cellular senescence contributes to age-related tissue deterioration by promoting functional alterations and a pro-inflammatory environment, making senotherapeutics promising strategies to selectively eliminate senescent cells or limit their deleterious effects. Our systematic review synthesized the available preclinical evidence on the efficacy of senotherapeutics in murine models of osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, and sarcopenia, analyzing structural and functional outcomes and the main molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of cellular senescence. A literature search was conducted in the MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases according to PRISMA guidelines, while the methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the SYRCLE RoB tool. 26 experimental studies were included, of which 15 involved osteoarthritis models, 6 osteoporosis models, and 5 sarcopenic models. Overall, senotherapeutics demonstrated protective effects on musculoskeletal tissues by reducing inflammation and improving the evaluated outcomes through the modulation of pathways associated with cellular senescence. However, the heterogeneity of experimental models, therapeutic protocols, and outcome measures limits the possibility of drawing definitive conclusions. Further studies will be necessary to clarify the molecular mechanisms involved, optimize therapeutic strategies, and promote the translation of experimental evidence into clinical practice.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells protect grafted islets against endoplasmic reticulum stress-induced mitochondrial dysfunction via modulating XBP1-based calcium homeostasis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Although islet transplantation is an ideal option for individuals with diabetes, early graft failure due to beta cell apoptosis and stress-induced dysfunction severely limits long-term efficacy. Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSCs) have multiple functions including maintaining cellular homeostasis. However, it remains unknown as to whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from hucMSCs (hucMSC-EVs) provide protective effects against transplant-related trauma-induced islet injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of hucMSC-EVs on islet graft survival in a syngeneic mouse model of islet transplantation and to examine the mechanism of protection.

METHODS: EVs were isolated from cultured hucMSCs and characterised by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking and western blotting. The effects of hucMSC-EVs on islet graft function were evaluated in a mouse model of streptozocin-induced diabetes via co-transplantation under the kidney capsule. Beta cell survival and function were assessed by immunofluorescence, TUNEL staining, insulin secretion assays and in vivo imaging. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) and mitochondrial dysfunction were further analysed in primary islets and NIT-1 beta cells under thapsigargin- or tunicamycin-stimulated ERS models. Further calcium imaging, JC-1 staining, western blotting and Seahorse assays were performed. microRNA sequencing was conducted and the role of miR-182-5p and XBP1 in mediating hucMSC-EV function was verified using knockdown, overexpression and dual-luciferase assays.

RESULTS: Co-transplantation of hucMSC-EVs with 250 islet equivalents significantly improved glycaemic control (p<0.01) and glucose tolerance (p<0.01) in diabetic mice. Apoptotic beta cells were significantly reduced in grafts receiving EVs, as shown by TUNEL assays (p<0.05) and cleaved caspase 3 staining (p<0.05). Ex vivo, hucMSC-EVs were internalised by beta cells and protected against tunicamycin-induced apoptosis (p<0.01), preserved insulin expression and restored glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. While ERS enhanced interactions between endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, hucMSC-EVs maintained calcium homeostasis, improved mitochondrial energy metabolism and alleviated ERS. Small RNA sequencing and functional analysis identified that XBP1-targeted miR-182-5p was enriched in hucMSC-EVs, which further fine-tuned endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria communication via reducing inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors at mitochondria-associated membranes and activated Nrf2 to restore mitochondrial calcium homeostasis under ERS. miR-182-5p inhibition reversed the protective effects of EVs on beta cell calcium homeostasis and viability. In vivo, depletion of miR-182-5p in hucMSC-EVs abolished the ability to prevent beta cell apoptosis and improve glycaemic control in diabetic mice.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: hucMSC-EVs significantly improved the survival and function of islet grafts by delivering miR-182-5p, which targeted XBP1 to modulate mitochondria-associated membranes, attenuate ERS and restore mitochondrial calcium homeostasis. These findings highlight a novel cell-free EV-based therapeutic strategy for improving the outcome of islet transplantation.

articles.title: Cardiovascular safety of romosozumab versus alendronate in postmenopausal women with severe osteoporosis: a propensity-matched real-world study.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Romosozumab is highly effective for severe osteoporosis, but its cardiovascular safety is debated. The ARCH trial found more major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) with romosozumab than with alendronate, whereas the placebo-controlled FRAME trial found no signal. Real-world head-to-head data against alendronate are lacking.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network, we identified women aged ≥55 years with severe osteoporosis (pathological, lumbar vertebral, or hip fracture within 2 years) who initiated romosozumab or alendronate, excluding those with any MACE in the prior 12 months. Cohorts were matched 1:1 by propensity score on demographics, cardiovascular comorbidities, medications, and laboratory parameters, and followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was a composite of MACE; secondary outcomes were myocardial infarction (MI), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and ischemic stroke. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models.

RESULTS: After matching, 5930 women remained per group (mean age 72 years; median follow-up 365 days). Romosozumab was not associated with an increased risk of MACE (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.70-1.07), MI (HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.67-1.28), or ACS (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.72-1.32). Ischemic stroke was significantly lower with romosozumab (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.46-0.89; P=0.008). Findings were consistent in event-naïve analyses and across subgroups, including chronic kidney disease and diabetes; however, the advanced-CKD stratum (stage 4-5 or end-stage renal disease) could not be analyzed because event counts were too small for estimation.

CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women with severe osteoporosis, romosozumab was not associated with higher 12-month cardiovascular risk than alendronate. These findings are reassuring in the populations that could be evaluated, although cardiovascular safety in advanced CKD remains uncertain and prospective confirmation is warranted.

articles.title: Tunneled Dialysis Catheter for KRT for Acute Kidney Injury in the Intensive Care Unit: CON.
Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026.

EXPOSURES: Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index.

RESULTS: Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

articles.title: Molecular Detection of Cryptosporidium spp. in Coypu (Myocastor coypus) in China: Genetic Diversity and Zoonotic Potential.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cryptosporidium is a globally important enteric pathogen commonly reported in rodents. The coypu (Myocastor coypus) is a large rodent adapted to semi-aquatic environments and is increasingly farmed as a fur-bearing animal.

METHODS: To assess the occurrence and zoonotic potential of Cryptosporidium in farmed coypus across China, a total of 308 faecal samples were collected from seven cities and screened via PCR targeting the small subunit (SSU) rRNA gene. Positive samples were further analysed with nested PCR targeting the 60-kDa glycoprotein (gp60) gene.

RESULTS: The overall infection rate was 8.8% (27/308), with city-level prevalence ranging from 0% (0/22) to 19.4% (19/98). Four distinct Cryptosporidium species/genotypes were identified: C. ubiquitum (n = 15), C. myocastoris (n = 5), C. parvum (n = 1), and the Cryptosporidium deer mouse genotype IV (n = 6). Further subtyping classified the C. parvum isolate as IIaA18G1R1 (n = 1) and revealed a novel C. ubiquitum subtype family, designated XIIk (n = 13). Phylogenetically, XIIk clustered with the zoonotic XIIa group.

CONCLUSIONS: These results reveal the genetic diversity of Cryptosporidium in farmed coypus and highlight the need for further investigation of its zoonotic potential.

articles.title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the precursor of angiotensin peptides and a key determinant of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity. ART101 is an investigational N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA (GalNAc-siRNA) designed to durably suppress hepatic AGT synthesis.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA in healthy volunteers and to provide an initial exploratory assessment of blood pressure effects in patients with hypertension.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase I study was conducted from January 2025 to April 2026 with 24-week follow-up. Part A was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending-dose trial; part B was an open-label, single-dose study. The study took place at Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China. Part A enrolled 40 healthy adults randomized 6:2 to receive the GalNAc-siRNA (25-600 mg) or placebo; 39 completed the study. Part B enrolled 8 patients with hypertension receiving the GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg; all completed the study.

INTERVENTIONS: A single subcutaneous injection of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA (25, 75, 150, 300, or 600 mg) or placebo in part A; a single open-label subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg, in part B.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exploratory blood pressure assessments, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers.

RESULTS: Among 40 healthy volunteers (27 [67.5%] male; mean [SD] age, 40.4 [7.8] years) and 8 patients (6 [75.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 47.3 [10.3] years) with hypertension, the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA was well tolerated. In part A, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 23 of 30 active-treatment participants (76.7%) vs 7 of 10 placebo recipients (70.0%); in part B, 6 of 8 patients (75.0%) had TEAEs. No serious adverse events, injection site reactions, or hyperkalemia were observed; all TEAEs were mild to moderate. Plasma exposure (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] and area under the plasma concentration-time curve [AUC]) increased with dose over the wide dose range from 25 mg to 600 mg. Mean maximum serum AGT reductions of 93% (at 600 mg) in healthy volunteers and 90% (at 600 mg) in patients with hypertension were observed. At 24 weeks after a single 600-mg dose, the placebo-corrected 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure decreased by 12.9 mm Hg in healthy participants.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this phase I study, no serious treatment-related safety signals were identified. Sustained, dose-dependent AGT reductions and exploratory blood pressure lowering were observed. These findings support further investigation of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA as a potential long-acting therapeutic for hypertension.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: China Drug Clinical Registry Identifiers: CTR20250041 (part A) and CTR20253973 (part B).

articles.title: RNAi Targeting Hepatic AGT to Block RAAS Pathway in Hypertension.
Intensive vs More Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Plaque Regression in Statin-Naive Patients: Prespecified Analyses From the FLOWPROMOTE Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Prior imaging studies (predominantly using intravascular ultrasound) have demonstrated modest plaque regression with lipid-lowering therapy in stable coronary artery disease (CAD). The effect of initiating intensive lipid-lowering therapy on coronary plaque regression across the entire coronary tree in treatment-naive patients remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To report the prespecified secondary imaging end points of the FLOWPROMOTE trial by comparing the effects of intensive vs more intensive lipid-lowering therapy on plaque regression in statin-naive patients with stable CAD and to assess the association between achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and plaque regression.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: FLOWPROMOTE was a multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolling statin-naive patients with newly diagnosed stable CAD, defined by a coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) stenosis greater than 50% and fractional flow reserve CT less than or equal to 0.80. Coronary CTA was performed at baseline and repeated at 9 and 18 months. Study data were analyzed from February 2025 to January 2026.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to intensive lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg) or more intensive lipid-lowering therapy (rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg) for 18 months.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prespecified secondary end points included changes in total plaque volume (TPV), noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV), and calcified plaque volume (CPV) across all coronary vessels at 9 and 18 months compared with baseline.

RESULTS: A total of 104 patients (mean [SD] age, 64 [9] years; 82 male [79%]) were included in this analysis, with 52 patients in the intensive group and 52 patients in the more intensive group. LDL-C levels decreased from 119.7 to 69.5 mg/dL (-38%) with intensive therapy and from 127.4 to 42.5 mg/dL (-65%) with more intensive therapy (between-group P < .001). At 18 months, both TPV and NCPV decreased in both groups, with significantly greater regression in the more intensive-therapy group. TPV was reduced by -69.8 mm3 (-21.1%) with more intensive therapy vs -39.0 mm3 (-13.6%) with intensive therapy (between-group difference, -30.9 mm3; 95% CI, -57.2 to -4.5 mm3; P = .02), and NCPV was reduced by -82.3 mm3 (-28.2%) vs -53.5 mm3 (-20.0%), respectively (between-group difference, -28.9 mm3; 95% CI, -53.2 to -4.6 mm3; P = .02). CPV increased similarly in both groups. Regression of TPV occurred in 90% of patients receiving more intensive therapy compared with 76% receiving intensive therapy (47 of 52 [90%] vs 38 of 51 [75%]; P = .05), and regression of NCPV was observed in 98% vs 77% (51 of 52 [98%] vs 39 of 51 [77%]; P =.001). Lower achieved LDL-C levels were linearly associated with greater regression of TPV and NCPV.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This secondary analysis of the FLOWPROMOTE randomized clinical trial demonstrated that in statin-naive patients with CAD, more intensive lipid-lowering therapy was associated with significantly greater regression of total and noncalcified coronary plaque burden compared with intensive therapy. The extent of plaque regression was related to achieved LDL-C levels, supporting the potential for partial reversal of coronary atherosclerosis with intensive lipid reduction.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04737408.

articles.title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Concern for ototoxicity hinders loop diuretic (LD) dosing in heart failure (HF); given the mechanism by which LDs affect the ear, high-dose LDs should produce transient, not permanent, hearing changes.

OBJECTIVE: To measure the association of LD dose with permanent and temporary ototoxicity.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cohort 1 received a randomized sequence of LD doses (bumetanide, 1.25-10 mg) across study visits with serial audiometry assessments. Cohort 2 received serial LD up to furosemide 500-mg doses during a HF hospitalization with audiometry at baseline and prior to discharge. Cohort 3 retrospectively characterized clinically diagnosed ototoxicity in HF hospitalizations was defined using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. Cohorts 1 and 2 were single center, while cohort 3 was multicenter. Cohort 1 studied outpatient participants with stable HF, while cohort 2 (n = 40) and cohort 3 studied hospitalized patients with acute HF.

EXPOSURE: Intravenous LD.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were clinically diagnosed ototoxicity and hearing changes via audiometry.

RESULTS: Cohort 1 contained 50 participants, cohort 2 contained 40 participants, and cohort 3 contained 22 656 participants. In cohort 1, mean (SD) participant age was 63.2 (10.4) years, and 21 of 50 participants (42%) were women. In cohorts 1 and 2, clinically diagnosed ototoxicity was not observed. In cohort 1, at peak diuretic concentration, worsening hearing shifts were infrequent (24 ears of 400 doses [6%]) but were more common with higher doses (odds ratio [OR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.21-3.28 per doubling dose; P = .007). Within hours, hearing shifts largely resolved and were absent in 98% of measurements (393 ears of 400 doses). No significant association between LD dose and hearing shifts was present at any time aside from peak LD concentration. In cohort 2, hearing shifts were not different across groups divided by the median daily LD dose and were not associated with LD dose (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.71-1.98 per doubling dose; P = .52). In cohort 3, 608 HF hospitalizations (2.7%) had clinically diagnosed ototoxicity. In multivariable analyses, peak dose of 160 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.52-1.31; P = .43) and 400 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.71-2.31; P = .41) were not associated with greater clinically diagnosed ototoxicity risk relative to less than 160 mg.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this analysis of 2 small HF cohorts, short-term exposure to high-dose LD was not associated with permanent ototoxicity, although concomitant ototoxin use was excluded. Future studies are needed to understand the risk of ototoxicity with repeated LD exposure and in broader HF populations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04481919 and NCT05323487.

articles.title: Intersection of Patient and Hospital Rurality in Heart Failure Care and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Rural-urban disparities in heart failure (HF) care delivery and outcomes are well documented. However, it remains unclear if differences in outcomes after HF hospitalization are primarily driven by patient rural residence, hospital resources, or both.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of patient and hospital rurality with quality of care and postdischarge outcomes after hospitalization for HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries in US hospitals with HFrEF with an index hospitalization from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2021. Included were Medicare beneficiaries discharged alive after an index hospitalization for HFrEF. Participants were classified as rural patients hospitalized in rural hospitals (rural-rural), rural patients in urban hospitals (rural-urban), urban patients in urban hospitals (urban-urban), and urban patients in rural hospitals (urban-rural). Study data were analyzed from July to September 2026.

EXPOSURES: Patient rural residence and hospital rurality.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality after hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included inpatient cardiology consultation, 90-day postdischarge guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use based on prescription fills, and HF readmission at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 735 460 beneficiaries (median [IQR] age, 77 [70-85] years; 415 077 male [56.4%]), 69 061 (9.4%) were rural-rural, 65 510 (8.9%) rural-urban, 582 947 (79.3%) urban-urban, and 17 942 (2.4%) urban-rural. Compared with rural patients treated in rural hospitals, rural patients treated in urban hospitals were more likely to receive inpatient cardiology consultation (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.84-2.22) and initiation of several GDMT classes, including β-blockers (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.16-1.25), ARNIs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.13-1.34), MRAs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.15-1.31), and SGLT2Is (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.32-1.67). They also had lower rates of HF readmission and mortality at all time points (HF readmission 1-year: OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.88; mortality 1-year: OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.89-0.94) than rural-rural patients. Compared with urban patients hospitalized at urban hospitals, rural patients hospitalized at urban hospitals more often received inpatient cardiology consultation (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.31-1.44), whereas postdischarge GDMT differences were modest (absolute difference in GDMT score 0.09 points; 95% CI, 0.05-0.14). Rural patients also had lower HF readmission (1-year OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79-0.82) but higher 30- and 90-day mortality than urban patients (30-day OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; 90-day OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results suggest that hospital rurality was associated with lower odds of GDMT use and higher rates of all-cause mortality, whereas rural residence was associated with mortality differences despite treatment in urban hospitals. Interventions addressing both inpatient resource disparities and postdischarge transitions of care may reduce rural-urban inequities in HF outcomes.

articles.title: Histologically Confirmed Myxedematous Myocardial Involvement in Severe Hypothyroidism With Concomitant Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histologically confirmed myxedematous myocardial involvement is rare and may be difficult to recognize when another cause of ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis coexists.

CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old man with longstanding, inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism presented with exertional dyspnea and a large goiter. Echocardiography showed severe bicuspid aortic stenosis, moderate aortic regurgitation, marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 26% of myocardial mass. After thyroid optimization, he underwent aortic valve replacement. Myocardial biopsy showed severe cardiomyocyte atrophy, interstitial mucin deposition, and extensive replacement fibrosis; Congo red staining was negative.

DISCUSSION: Severe aortic stenosis provided an alternative explanation for the myocardial phenotype, and multimodality imaging alone could not distinguish pressure-overload remodeling from hypothyroidism-related myocardial injury.

CONCLUSION: Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.

articles.title: South African Flag Sign on Electrocardiogram: Not Always an Obstructive Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The South African Flag Sign (SAFS) is a rare electrocardiographic pattern associated with occlusion myocardial infarction, typically involving the first diagonal branch.

CASE SUMMARY: A 74-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain and a transient neurological deficit following intense emotional stress. The admission electrocardiogram demonstrated the SAFS. Emergency coronary angiography revealed nonobstructive coronary artery disease, whereas echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance confirmed Takotsubo syndrome with apical ballooning and an initial left ventricular ejection fraction of 36%. Clinical and functional recovery was achieved with guideline-directed medical therapy.

DISCUSSION: High-risk ST-segment elevation equivalents like the SAFS, though excluded from standard ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction criteria, indicate occlusion myocardial infarction requiring emergent reperfusion. This case illustrates how severe catecholaminergic discharge in Takotsubo syndrome can induce microvascular dysfunction and vasospasm, faithfully mimicking epicardial occlusions and acute cerebrovascular events.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: High-risk electrocardiogram patterns such as the SAFS are not exclusive to occlusion myocardial infarction and may indicate other mechanisms of acute myocardial injury.

articles.title: NeuroPOCUS: what every intensivist should know.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound has become a paramount tool in critical care. Nowadays, it is common for intensivists to use ultrasound to evaluate cardiac function, pulmonary alterations, guide vascular access, and monitor systemic venous congestion through ultrasound-based techniques. However, the brain remains often overlooked in the point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) practice. NeuroPOCUS encompasses cerebral hemodynamic assessment, mainly at the level of the middle cerebral artery, as well as evaluation of hydrocephalus, hematoma size, midline shift and intracranial pressure. Most of these are basic or basic-plus skills. In this manuscript, we present a concise guide on what every intensivist should know about NeuroPOCUS, including basic key concepts, technique and several real illustrative figures.

articles.title: Integrating planetary health into clinical and public health evidence-informed practice guidelines in oral health.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change, pollution, and biodiversity loss are emerging global health threats associated with planetary boundaries. Clinical and public health guidelines can contribute to planetary health by means of integrating considerations of planetary boundaries into evidence-informed decision making. The authors operationalized the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) Guidance 46 for oral health, conceptualizing how planetary boundaries can be embedded in clinical and public health guideline development.

TYPES OF STUDIES REVIEWED: Drawing on GRADE Guidance 46 and other methodological documents, the framework maps environmental evidence to guideline development steps and specifies how panels can summarize environmental effects alongside person-important outcomes through 2 complementary mechanisms: a dedicated planetary boundaries evidence-to-decision criterion and a planetary health subjudgment within the existing equity criterion.

RESULTS: Incorporating planetary health within the GRADE Evidence-to-Decision framework is feasible through 2 complementary mechanisms. The planetary boundaries criterion (domain 6) records per-boundary judgments on the direction and absolute magnitude of effect, together with an overall cross-boundary determination. The planetary health equity subjudgment (domain 7b) addresses equity across species, generations, and within this generation (everyone alive today), with emphasis on disadvantaged populations. Life cycle assessments can inform recommendations on visit frequency, single-use vs reusable pathways, and optimized reprocessing and procurement.

CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Planetary health and evidence-informed practice can align through an environmentally conscious guideline development framework. Integrating life cycle assessments into guideline development can provide a transparent, reproducible outline for reporting environmental trade-offs without compromising infection prevention and control, effectiveness and safety, or equity, thereby supporting actionable, planetary health-sensible oral health recommendations.

articles.title: Understanding Trade-Offs Between Modeling Approaches to Forecast Plant Disease Spread and Risk.
articles.abstract: Modeling disease spread and risk is crucial for disease management, with numerous options for models. Multiple factors affect model selection, including the model's spatial and temporal dimensions, the quantity and quality of infection data, management objectives, and the research questions being addressed. We developed a workflow to filter model types based on pathogen biology and infection data availability, then select the appropriate model for the research question and management objectives. We applied the workflow to two case study pathosystems (late blight and sudden oak death) and evaluated three modeling approaches representing different spatial and temporal dimensions: a temporally focused weather-risk model (WRM), a spatially focused species distribution model (SDM), and a spatiotemporal spread model, the Pest or Pathogen Spread (PoPS) model. We qualitatively compared how each model's spatiotemporal outputs affected predicted disease risk or spread. Additionally, we conducted a simulation study in which infection data were reduced to determine the minimum data density required to obtain reliable parameter estimates with PoPS. Our results suggest that the temporal WRM model is suitable for disease management in agricultural pathosystems, where stakeholders possess sufficient spatial knowledge. In the natural pathosystem, the spatiotemporal model's greater accuracy reduced the total high-risk infection area by >99% compared with the other models. We found that although a spatiotemporal model is more accurate and helps with resource allocation, performance dropped significantly when data density fell below 50%. The effect of decreasing data density on SDM performance varied with pathosystem. Our work underscores the need for scalable disease-detection methods.

articles.title: An Approach to Navigating the Lorazepam Challenge Test for Catatonia in Critical Care Settings.
articles.abstract: Catatonia often occurs in the setting of psychiatric illness; however, it is also found in other medical conditions, especially within critical care settings. The lorazepam challenge test (LCT) is a key diagnostic and therapeutic intervention for catatonia; however, no specific guidance exists for patients within the intensive care unit (ICU). This review synthesizes psychiatric and critical care literature to propose a structured LCT framework adapted to the ICU. Specific indications and contraindications across gradients of catatonia likelihood and medical complexity are reviewed, along with practical dosing and monitoring recommendations. An interdisciplinary collaborative workflow is also outlined along with post-LCT documentation standards. Our structured approach offers a practical foundation for future standardized protocols, education, and catatonia research in critical care.

articles.title: Probing polymer effects on interfacial Li-ion transport in hybrid solid electrolytes: LLZO-PCL compared with LLZO-PEO.
articles.abstract: Hybrid polymer-ceramic electrolytes are promising candidates for solid-state lithium-ion batteries, making it essential to identify the key factors governing interfacial ion transport. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations at elevated temperatures are used to investigate differences in Li+ transport between PCL- and PEO-based polymer-ceramic interfaces. The investigated interface is built of Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) ceramic and poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) polymer doped with bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) (LLZO-PCL), and a direct comparison is established with an analogous interface composed of LiTFSI-doped poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and LLZO (LLZO-PEO). The LLZO-PCL interface exhibits pronounced interfacial structuring, including strong adsorption of hydroxyl oxygen atoms at the ceramic surface. Li+ transfer across the interface is quantified from transition statistics and analyzed using free-energy profiles. Remarkably, LLZO-PCL exhibits an approximately 35-fold larger phase-exchange barrier (PEB) rate than LLZO-PEO, primarily due to a significantly lower PEB height for polymer-ceramic transfer. Analysis within the framework of overdamped Kramers theory indicates strongly damped interfacial dynamics and suggests spatially heterogeneous friction along the reaction coordinate. Overall, the results demonstrate that the substantially different interfacial Li+ transfer in PCL and PEO is mainly associated with differences in the PEB height. Our previously developed multiscale framework is used to evaluate which of the two polymer systems is more likely to enhance the overall conductivity in hybrid solid electrolytes by facilitating Li+ transport through the fast ceramic phase. Finally, effective Li-polymer coordination strength and polymer adhesion at the ceramic surface emerge as key factors governing interfacial ion transport and the efficient utilization of ceramic transport pathways in hybrid solid electrolytes.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Analog-Type Amyloidosis: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract: Amyloidosis is a heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by extracellular deposition of insoluble proteins. Glucagon-like peptide-1 analog (AGLP1)-type amyloidosis is a rare iatrogenic form of amyloidosis localized to areas of glucagon-like peptide-1 analog injections. In this study, we describe a case of AGLP1-type amyloidosis presenting as a subcutaneous mass on the abdomen of a 71-year-old woman with a history of liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide use. Biopsy, including Congo red stain, was consistent with an amyloid deposit. Amyloid protein identification by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry showed a typical amyloid profile with low spectra for liraglutide. Immunohistochemistry, subsequently performed, showed that the amyloid deposits were positive for glucagon; there is an extensive peptide homology between liraglutide and glucagon. Only 3 cases of AGLP1-type amyloidosis have been previously reported. It is vital for clinicians and pathologists to be aware of AGLP1-type amyloidosis given the increasing worldwide use of GLP-1 agonists, as well as the potential for misdiagnosis of systemic amyloidosis, which has profound therapeutic and prognostic implications.

articles.title: Upper Limb Neurorehabilitation Using a Hybrid Technology-Enabled Therapy Approach-A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: There is growing evidence of benefits for a multimodal or 'hybrid' technology approach where more than one technology type is applied for upper limb (UL) neurorehabilitation. However, translation of this approach into real world clinical settings remains unclear. Exploration of multimodal technology use for UL neurorehabilitation in hospital settings is warranted to determine practice trends, efficacy, benefits and barriers. A scoping review was conducted to explore hybrid technology-enabled rehabilitation approaches for UL neurorehabilitation focusing on combined use of robotics, virtual reality and sensor-based therapy. Seven electronic databases were searched for studies on adult participants with neurological UL impairment who participated in hospital rehabilitation and used two or more technology devices. Of 25 333 articles screened, full text review was completed on 20 articles with nine progressed for data extraction. An additional article found from hand searching was included for data extraction resulting in ten articles in total.
