Included studies found hybrid technology-enabled UL rehabilitation was used mainly with stroke participants ranging from 25 to 91 years in a hospital setting. Most studies were observational or pilot in nature and focused on clinical feasibility. All studies showed positive patient outcomes and feasibility studies reported on factors to support implementation in the clinical setting. Further research is warranted to determine impact on participation, long-term outcomes, sustainability, and economic impacts in the clinical hospital setting.

articles.title: Identifying key components for psychosocial interventions in neurorehabilitation: a realist evaluation on young adults with an acquired brain injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acquired brain injuries (ABIs), including stroke, lead to younger adults exhibiting a range of psychosocial challenges such as isolation or diminished quality of life. Healthcare services including multidisciplinary teams and nurses play a pivotal role in helping individuals navigate a post-ABI world, but the mechanisms underlying psychosocial support in a younger population remain largely unknown.

METHODS: This realist evaluation explores ten initial programme theories derived from a realist review literature. Realist interviews were also conducted to refine these programme theories and clarify which causal and contextual factors are most important for intervention development, as guided by the Six steps in Quality Intervention Development (6SQuID). Six young adults with experience of ABI and seventeen service providers from across the four countries of the UK participated in this theory refinement.

RESULTS: The co-construction refinement process with the participants focusing on psychosocial support to people with ABI resulted in three refined programme theories expressed as context, mechanism, outcome configurations: (1) "Engaging the Individual;" (2) "Empowering the Community," and (3) "Equipping the Professionals."

CONCLUSION: This realist interview evaluation highlights crucial elements that both experts by experience and service providers identify as necessary to be incorporated into future psychosocial interventions.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life in adult patients with moyamoya disease in Japan: a single-center study.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a chronic cerebrovascular disorder associated with stroke and functional impairment that may adversely affect health-related quality of life (HRQOL). This study assessed HRQOL and explored its associated factors in Japanese adults with MMD.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: The 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) and EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level questionnaire (EQ-5D-5 L) were mailed to adults with MMD attending outpatient clinics at Hokkaido University Hospital between January 2023 and March 2025. HRQOL scores were compared with age- and sex-specific Japanese population norms. Multivariable regression analyses revealed factors associated with HRQOL.

RESULTS: Of 213 eligible patients, 140 provided informed consent. Among patients with self-reported outcomes, mean differences from population norms (95% confidence intervals) were 0.005 (-0.011 to 0.021) for EQ-5D values, - -1.4 (-2.7 to 0.01) for the SF-36 physical component summary, 4.4 (2.7 to 6.0) for the mental component summary, and 1.7 (0.1 to 3.3) for the role/social component summary. HRQOL was associated with the modified Rankin Scale score.

CONCLUSIONS: HRQOL in Japanese adults with MMD was generally comparable to that of the general population, although physical health scores tended to be lower. These findings warrant cautious interpretation because of the study's cross-sectional, single-center design.

articles.title: Controversies and reappraisal in the management of distal deep vein thrombosis: From evidence-based discrepancies to risk-stratified individualized strategies.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDistal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) confined to the infrapopliteal deep venous system, commonly termed isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), accounts for a substantial proportion of lower-extremity DVT. Its optimal management remains controversial because randomized evidence is limited, patient populations are heterogeneous, and guideline recommendations differ.ObjectiveThis narrative review critically examines the evidence for anticoagulation and serial ultrasonographic surveillance in IDDVT, evaluates sources of uncertainty, compares major guideline recommendations, and proposes a cautious, risk-adapted framework for individualized management.MethodsWe searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library to identify English-language guidelines, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and relevant observational studies addressing IDDVT management, thrombus extension, pulmonary embolism, bleeding, post-thrombotic syndrome, and treatment duration. The search was updated through July 2026. Priority was given to major guidelines, randomized trials, and contemporary systematic reviews/meta-analyses, with older studies retained when providing foundational evidence.ResultsCurrent evidence does not support a uniform treatment strategy for IDDVT. The choice between anticoagulation and serial imaging should consider symptom severity, extension risk factors, bleeding risk, thrombus location, patient preferences, and feasibility of follow-up imaging. Randomized trials support surveillance in selected patients and suggest reduced recurrent VTE with extended anticoagulation in patients who tolerate initial treatment. However, evidence remains limited by small or selected populations, heterogeneous outcomes, and extrapolation from proximal DVT or pulmonary embolism.ConclusionIDDVT should be managed according to individual risk rather than as a homogeneous condition. Decisions regarding anticoagulation initiation and treatment duration should be considered separately. Serial imaging is reasonable for selected patients without severe symptoms or major extension risk factors, whereas anticoagulation is generally favored in those with severe symptoms or recognized extension risk factors. No IDDVT-specific risk score has been validated, and interventional treatment should remain exceptional because direct evidence is lacking.

articles.title: Contemporary pharmacotherapeutic management of severe pediatric asthma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Severe asthma affects a small proportion of children but causes disproportionate morbidity, corticosteroid exposure, educational and family disruption, and concern about growth and development. Management requires diagnostic confirmation, optimization of inhaled therapy, and age-appropriate use of targeted biologics.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines diagnostic reassessment, biomarker-informed treatment selection, optimization of non-biologic therapy, and corticosteroid stewardship. It discusses the mechanisms, regulatory status, pediatric evidence, effectiveness, and safety of omalizumab, mepolizumab, benralizumab, depemokimab, dupilumab, and tezepelumab, and addresses response assessment, switching, remission, withdrawal, and immunogenicity. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for English-language evidence published from 1 January 2006 through 31 August 2026; guidelines and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) documents were also reviewed.

EXPERT OPINION: Biologics reduce severe exacerbations and systemic-corticosteroid exposure in eligible children, but the directness of pediatric evidence differs substantially among agents. Biomarkers and type 2 comorbidities inform eligibility and the probability of response but do not establish a treatment hierarchy. Selection should be individualized and evaluated as a therapeutic trial against prespecified multidimensional targets. Key priorities are age-specific comparative and withdrawal studies, harmonized pediatric remission criteria, and prospective registries addressing developmental safety and long-term treatment strategies.

articles.title: Ropeginterferon alfa-2b for adults with polycythemia vera: an updated perspective from approval to real-world clinical treatment.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ropeginterferon alfa-2b (ROPEG) is an established long-acting interferon option for adults with polycythemia vera (PV). Since its regulatory approval, evidence from randomized trials has been complemented by long-term analyses, prospective studies, and an expanding real-world experience.

AREAS COVERED: This review critically evaluates the evidence supporting ROPEG in adult PV, including PEGINVERA, PROUD-PV/CONTINUATION-PV and LOW-PV trials, long-term clinical and molecular outcomes, emerging biomarkers of clonal and inflammatory control, slow vs. accelerated dose titration, real-world effectiveness and safety, switching from peginterferon alfa-2a, cost-effectiveness, and the BESREMi® Pen approval.

EXPERT OPINION: ROPEG has a strong evidence for durable hematologic control and progressive molecular responses, with real-world studies supporting its effectiveness in older, previously treated and hydroxyurea-intolerant patients. However, evidence for disease modification and prevention of thrombosis or transformation remains suggestive rather than definitive. Accelerated titration may shorten the time to response with manageable toxicities, but current evidence does not justify replacing the approved titration schedule routinely. Cost-effectiveness appears favorable in several healthcare models but remains highly dependent on drug prices, treatment persistence, and assumptions regarding long-term disease modification. The major priorities are prospective, harmonized real-world studies and randomized trials addressing clinically meaningful outcomes, optimal titration, treatment discontinuation, and patient selection.

articles.title: Associations of Adaptive Coping, Self-Efficacy, and Hope With Psychological Resilience in Women Receiving Chemotherapy for Gynecological Cancer: A Descriptive Correlational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological resilience is important for women coping with the physical and emotional challenges of chemotherapy for gynecological cancer. However, the associations of psychological resources with resilience during treatment remain insufficiently understood.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the associations of hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies with psychological resilience among women receiving chemotherapy for gynecological cancer.

METHODS: A descriptive correlational design was used. The study sample consisted of 144 women receiving outpatient chemotherapy in Turkey. Data were collected using standardized self-report measures assessing psychological resilience, hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies. Descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, and hierarchical linear regression analyses were conducted to examine the associations between psychological resilience and hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies.

RESULTS: The mean psychological resilience score indicated a moderate level of resilience. Psychological resilience was positively associated with hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies. In the final regression model, self-efficacy showed the strongest independent association with psychological resilience (β = 0.524, P = .001), followed by hope (β = 0.257, P = .001) and adaptive coping (β = 0.146, P = .015). Together, these variables explained 56.2% of the variance in psychological resilience.

CONCLUSIONS: Hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping were positively associated with psychological resilience among women undergoing chemotherapy for gynecological cancer. These findings may inform nurse-led psychosocial support approaches that address self-efficacy, hope, and adaptive coping strategies as part of resilience-related care. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to examine whether changes in these psychological resources are followed by changes in resilience and other psychosocial outcomes during cancer treatment.

articles.title: MASH Cirrhosis: A Stage-Specific Framework for Care and Clinical Trial Design.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is an increasingly important cause of cirrhosis, yet no pharmacological therapy is approved specifically for MASH cirrhosis. Completed trials indicate that this therapeutic gap reflects limitations in biological targeting, population definition, treatment duration, and endpoint selection rather than evidence that established disease is immutable. Most agents evaluated in compensated MASH cirrhosis did not meet their prespecified primary endpoints; aldafermin met an enhanced liver fibrosis endpoint without establishing histological benefit, and later assessment of efruxifermin suggested that structural change may require longer exposure. MASH cirrhosis should therefore not be investigated as a simple extension of precirrhotic MASH. Disease stage, clinically significant portal hypertension, metabolic comorbidity, and frailty influence both prognosis and treatment tolerance. Selected invasive and cross-sectional studies suggest heterogeneity in the relationship between hepatic venous pressure gradient and clinical events in advanced MASLD or MASH, but prospective data confirm that hepatic venous pressure gradient remains prognostic; these observations do not establish a universally distinct hemodynamic phenotype. Mechanistic findings involving sinusoidal endothelium, bile handling, and canalicular architecture are translational leads rather than validated clinical markers. We propose a stage-specific framework that separates current care from trial design; prioritizes clinical outcome endpoints in compensated disease with portal hypertension and in decompensated disease; and treats biopsy, liver stiffness, enhanced liver fibrosis, hemodynamic, and frailty measures according to their context and level of validation. Prospective MASH-cirrhosis cohorts and competing-risk-aware trials are now required.

articles.title: An lncRNA containing tandem 66-nt repeats recruits PTBP1 to disrupt PB2-NP assembly and restrict influenza virus replication in vivo.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Influenza virus replication relies on coordinated assembly of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes in the nucleus, yet how host long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify the lncRNA AL645608.7 as a potent antiviral factor and show that its two splice variants restrict influenza replication. Mechanistically, AL645608.7 contains eight tandem 66-nt repeats that recruit the RNA-binding protein PTBP1, primarily through PTBP1's RRM3 domain. The AL645608.7-PTBP1 assembly then engages key viral RNP components-PB2 and NP-and functionally disrupts the PB2-NP interface, thereby suppressing viral RNA synthesis. Domain-mapping analyses further distinguish the regions responsible for PTBP1 recruitment from those involved in PB2 and NP engagement, demonstrating that distinct structural elements of AL645608.7 coordinate host-protein recruitment and viral RNP interference. Importantly, lipid nanoparticle delivery of AL645608.7 markedly reduces viral burden and improves disease outcomes in mice, providing a proof-of-concept nucleic-acid therapeutic strategy. Together, our findings reveal a repeat-programmed lncRNA mechanism that rewires a host RNA-binding protein to dismantle influenza RNP organization and support the therapeutic potential of lncRNA-based intervention against influenza virus infection.

IMPORTANCE: This study identified that influenza virus infection significantly upregulated the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) AL645608.7. Both of its transcripts, AL645608.7-v1 and AL645608.7-v2, exhibited antiviral activity against influenza virus. Mechanistically, AL645608.7 was shown to directly bind to the host protein PTBP1. Furthermore, the nuclear-localized AL645608.7 recruits PTBP1 via a 66-base repeat motif. Importantly, PTBP1 interacts with both the N- and C-terminal regions of the influenza virus polymerase subunit PB2 as well as the NP, thereby disrupting the NP-PB2 interaction. The AL645608.7-PTBP1 complex amplifies this inhibitory effect, ultimately impairing vRNA synthesis and blocking efficient viral replication. These findings offer novel insights into the functional role of noncoding RNAs in host-influenza virus interactions.

articles.title: Establishment of urinary hydrogen peroxide as an early indicator for AKI monitoring and its electrochemical detection.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) features high incidence and mortality rates, delayed diagnosis, and oxidative stress as its core mechanism. Urinary hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) has biomarker potential, but it is only confirmed that its level rises synchronously with serum creatinine (SCr) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) in the late stage of AKI. The temporal sequence is unclear, and thus, it is unable to prove its diagnostic value in early AKI. In this study, cellular experiments reveal that the onset of cisplatin-induced cellular oxidative stress is far earlier than the node of decline in cell viability. Animal experiments further confirm that, in an AKI mouse model constructed via tail vein injection of cisplatin, H2O2 levels in the kidney and urine significantly increase 3 hours after injection, at which time no substantial necrosis is observed in the kidney. In contrast, traditional indicators SCr and BUN show significant abnormalities only after 24 hours and 48 hours, respectively. This finding clarifies the biological basis of urinary H2O2 as an early detection indicator for AKI. On this basis, a CuO/ZnPc-Cu composite material is prepared. After the performance of the glassy carbon electrode system is verified, the material is modified onto a screen-printed electrode, successfully realizing the precise and rapid quantitative detection of low-concentration H2O2 in real mouse urine. This study provides a new indicator for the rapid and convenient diagnosis of early AKI and also lays a foundation for the future development of detection terminals to achieve low-cost, home-based, non-invasive screening for high-risk AKI patients.

articles.title: Automated Insulin Delivery in Older Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Better Time in Range Does Not by Itself Define the Right Target.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology

articles.title: Understanding the roles of interleukin-33: is there promise for therapeutic targeting?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: IL-33 is a chromatin-associated alarmin of the IL-1 cytokine family involved in tissue homeostasis and immune responses following epithelial or endothelial injury. Although the IL-33/ST2 axis is an attractive therapeutic target, clinical outcomes with IL-33- or ST2-directed agents have varied across diseases and patient populations.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines IL-33 biology and the clinical development of tozorakimab, itepekimab, astegolimab and emerging multispecific antibodies across COPD, asthma, atopic dermatitis, food allergy, diabetic kidney disease and viral pneumonia. Particular attention is given to IL-33 oxidation, RAGE/EGFR-associated signaling, soluble ST2, tissue compartment, therapeutic modality and trial design, and to the distinction between pathway activation and pathogenic dependence.

EXPERT OPINION: IL-33 remains a promising but context-dependent therapeutic target. Phase 3 COPD trials provide the strongest evidence, particularly for tozorakimab, whereas outcomes with other agents and indications remain inconsistent. Future development should define disease- and endotype-specific dependence on IL-33, clarify the relevance of ST2-independent signaling and soluble ST2, and validate predictive biomarkers using form-resolved assays. Structural differences among anti-IL-33 antibodies may also influence activity, but comparative clinical evidence is lacking. Multispecific approaches may broaden efficacy, but their advantages over established biologics remain to be demonstrated and require prospective evaluation in biomarker-defined patient populations.

articles.title: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of microplastics in chicken based on portable near-infrared spectroscopy and interpretable machine learning.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Portable near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with interpretable machine learning was employed for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of polypropylene (PP), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) in chicken. A total of 244 samples were prepared, including pure chicken and PP-, PVC-, and PET-spiked chicken (61 samples per type, mass fractions: 0.01-0.8%). NIR spectra were acquired over 900-1700 nm. After optimal preprocessing and outlier removal via Monte Carlo cross-validation (MCCV), competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) was selected over the successive projections algorithm (SPA) for characteristic wavelength extraction prior to modeling. For qualitative analysis, a data-driven soft independent modeling of class analogy (DD-SIMCA) model was constructed, achieving sensitivities of 85.71-92.86% and specificities of 82.93-100%. For quantitative analysis, the optimal model varied with microplastic (MP) type: CARS-SVR (support vector regression) for PET (Rp2 = 0.8923, RPD = 3.0468); CARS-ElasticNet for PP (Rp2 = 0.8267, RPD = 2.4022), and CARS-PLS (partial least squares) for PVC (Rp2 = 0.8969, RPD = 3.0397). SHAP-based interpretability analysis was further employed to quantify each wavelength's spectral contribution and identify MP-specific absorption bands. This study innovatively integrates portable NIR spectroscopy with SHAP-based interpretable machine learning for MP detection in chicken and demonstrates the potential of this strategy for rapid on-site screening of MP contamination in poultry products.

articles.title: An economic evaluation alongside a randomised controlled trial of Scanning Eye trAining as a Rehabilitation Choice compared to sham training for Hemianopia after stroke (the SEARCH trial).
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the cost-effectiveness of visual scanning training for hemianopia compared to sham training.DesignRandomised controlled trial.SettingAcute stroke unit and outpatient eye clinics.ParticipantsAdult stroke survivors with homonymous hemianopia.InterventionVisual scanning training.ComparatorSham eye pursuit movements.Main measuresCost-utility and cost-effectiveness analyses were conducted from UK National Health Service (NHS) and wider societal perspectives. The primary analysis was a cost-utility analysis using EQ-5D-5L utility values. Cost-effectiveness analyses using changes in National Eye Institute-Visual Function Questionnaire-25 item composite and Brain Injury-associated Visual Impairment-Impact Questionnaire scores formed the secondary analyses.ResultsBoth intervention and sham training packages cost £9.58 (printing costs, clinician time to explain self-administration). Mean total health resource use costs at 26-weeks were higher in the intervention (£1406) than in the sham group (£1339). At 26-weeks, the intervention group gained 0.001 (95%CI:-0.018, 0.021) Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY) while the sham group evidenced a QALY loss of -0.002 (95%CI:-0.017, 0.012); not statistically significant (p = 0.71). The Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio of visual scanning training compared to sham was £19,790/QALY, below the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) threshold of £20,000-£30,000/QALY. Sensitivity analysis (5000 replications) suggested potential cost-effectiveness of visual scanning training, which had a 67% probability of being cost-effective at £20,000/QALY; this was not significant.ConclusionsThis is the first economic evaluation comparing visual scanning training to sham training for treating post-stroke hemianopia. While both interventions had similar costs, the costs were slightly under NICE thresholds. The intervention evidenced marginal but non-significant QALY gain over sham.

articles.title: Prevalence of fall risk and fear of falling among older adults in the Middle East and North Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, falls are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in older adults (individuals aged ≥60 years). In the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, home to over 57 million older adults, data on key fall-related risk factors are limited, constraining targeted prevention efforts. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of fall risk and fear of falling among older adults in the 20 MENA countries.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Google (up to November 2025). Two independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality. We estimated pooled prevalence using random-effects meta-analysis and conducted meta-regression to explore heterogeneity.

RESULTS: We included 109 studies with 213,877 older adults. The mean age ranged from 63.1 (standard deviation (SD) = 2.5) to 77.2 (SD = 4.6) years across studies. The pooled prevalence of older adults at higher fall risk was 54.2% (95% confidence interval (CI) = 35.1, 72.8) based on the Missouri Alliance for Home Care Fall Risk Assessment and 33.4% (95% CI = 18.4, 53.8) based on the Morse Fall Scale. The pooled prevalence of older adults classified at higher fall risk was 41.7% (95% CI = 27.6, 57.2) based on balance performance using the Berg Balance Scale and 58.0% (95% CI = 39.4, 74.5) based on functional mobility using the Timed Up and Go Test. Studies reporting fear of falling mainly used validated tools assessing concern about falling and fall-related self-efficacy. The pooled prevalence of moderate to high concern about falling, measured by the Falls Efficacy Scale-International, was 82.7% (95% CI = 60.4, 93.8). The pooled prevalence of reduced fall-related self-efficacy, assessed by the Modified Falls Efficacy Scale, was 67.1% (95% CI = 44.9, 83.6). We observed substantial heterogeneity across studies, with no significant differences by population type, sex, or country-income level in meta-regression analyses. We detected no evidence of publication bias for fear of falling, while minor asymmetry was observed for fall risk; however, data were unavailable for ten MENA countries.

CONCLUSIONS: This review shows a substantial prevalence of fall risk and fear of falling among older adults in the MENA countries represented in the available evidence, underscoring the need for region-specific fall prevention interventions. These findings support integrating routine fall-risk screening and standardised assessment tools into primary and geriatric care to address both physical and psychological risk factors and to inform targeted interventions across the region.

REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework: https://osf.io/3cu4q/overview.

articles.title: PANoptosis gene signatures identify candidate biomarkers and genetically associated genes in COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PANoptosis contributes to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) pathogenesis. We aimed to identify PANoptosis-related gene signatures as candidate biomarkers and evaluate their genetic associations with COPD risk.

METHODS: Three transcriptomic data sets were integrated to identify differentially expressed PANoptosis-related genes in COPD, followed by enrichment analyses and immune infiltration profiling using CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. We selected feature genes using machine learning and evaluated their discriminative performance. We used Mendelian randomisation (MR) and multivariable MR (MVMR) to assess genetic associations with COPD risk, using the forced expiratory volume in one second/forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) ratio as a proxy for airflow limitation and adjusting for smoking. We validated candidate genes by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) in human lung tissues from COPD patients and controls.

RESULTS: Seven PANoptosis-related genes (IL1B, IRF1, NTRK2, PIK3CG, SFN, TNFSF10, and UACA) were differentially expressed in COPD. Immune profiling suggested immune microenvironment remodelling, characterised by increased memory B cells, activated mast cells, and CD4+ T helper cell subsets, with decreased M2 macrophages, monocytes, and neutrophils. PIK3CG and IL1B were positively associated with adaptive immune-related signals, whereas UACA showed predominantly negative immune correlations. PIK3CG showed moderate and variable discriminative performance, with an area under the curve of 0.775 in the training data set and 0.614 and 0.743 in validation data sets. The MR and MVMR analyses suggested that IRF1- and UACA-mediated increases in FEV1/FVC were associated with lower COPD risk independently of smoking. Additionally, qRT-PCR confirmed PIK3CG up-regulation in COPD lung tissues, whereas IRF1 and UACA showed no remarkable expression changes.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that PIK3CG is a computationally and experimentally supported biomarker for COPD, while IRF1 and UACA act as genetically implicated regulators of airflow limitation. Together, these findings show the potential importance of PANoptosis-driven immune microenvironmental remodelling as a therapeutic direction warranting further functional validation.

articles.title: Constructing event graph and mining critical paths of Ebola virus disease: a public health emergency analysis based on WHO disease outbreak news.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most Ebola virus disease research focuses on clinical diagnosis or static knowledge networks, limiting dynamic spatiotemporal analysis of epidemic evolution. We examined whether an event graph derived from World Health Organization (WHO) Disease Outbreak News (DONs) could reconstruct outbreak evolution across reports and identify response-timing patterns, including delayed interventions, unactioned risk assessments, and cross-border escalation.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 346 Ebola-related DON reports published through August 2025. We used a large language model-assisted framework to extract events and their relationships. We built an event graph in Neo4j and applied a bounded depth-first search procedure that removed cycles, generated candidate paths, and selected critical paths across six dimensions: case burden, spatial spread, international risk signals, intervention measures, path length, and graph structural importance.

RESULTS: The graph comprised 2233 event nodes and 10,479 relations across 155 event groups; 47 representative critical paths were selected. Laboratory confirmation often marked the shift from uncertain signals to an organised response. Healthcare-facility exposure and community deaths served as sentinel events for infection-control review and transmission-chain investigation. Preparedness, surveillance, and contact tracing generally followed spatial spread and international-risk signals rather than general border restrictions. Repeated burden updates without documented interventions indicated potential response or reporting gaps. Although established control measures aligned with WHO advice, the report defined explicit triggers, deadlines, inter-agency handoffs, and completion indicators less clearly.

CONCLUSIONS: The event graph reconstructed longitudinal outbreak and response trajectories that are difficult to capture through descriptive summaries or entity-centred knowledge graphs. Effective Ebola response depends not only on available control measures but also on activating them at appropriate transition points. This framework complements, rather than replaces, WHO guidance, real-time surveillance, and formal epidemiological causal inference.

articles.title: Recent trial evidence supports enhanced influenza vaccines for older adults: implications for Belgian practice.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize evidence on enhanced influenza vaccine effectiveness in older adults and contextualize the 2026-2027 Belgian recommendations for clinical practice.

METHODS: Narrative review of randomized trials, observational studies, and meta-analyses examining HD-IIV and A-IIV in adults aged ≥ 65 years, with emphasis on European data published between 2020 and 2026.

RESULTS: The FLUNITY-HD pooled analysis of European pragmatic trials (DANFLU-2 and GALFLU; n = 466,320) demonstrated relative vaccine effectiveness (rVE) of 31.9% (95% CI 19.7-42.2) for HD-IIV versus SD-IIV against laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization. DANFLU-2 subgroup analyses identified chronic kidney disease (CKD) as a modifier of enhanced vaccine benefit (rVE 68.6% in CKD versus 30.6% in non-CKD). A-IIV demonstrates comparable benefits in observational studies, though randomized trial evidence remains less extensive. Both enhanced vaccines demonstrated clinical superiority over standard-dose vaccines. Randomized trial evidence supports HD-IIV whereas clinical effectiveness data for A-IIV rely primarily on observational studies. Both formulations show acceptable safety profiles. The Superior Health Council (SHC) recommends HD-IIV or A-IIV for adults aged ≥ 65 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Randomized trial evidence supports HD-IIV whereas clinical effectiveness data for A-IIV rely primarily on observational studies. The SHC guidelines introduce age-stratified recommendation strength (conditional for 65-74 years; strong for ≥75 years) and extend consideration of enhanced vaccines to adults aged 50-64 years with CKD.

articles.title: Effects of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) on the Endometrium.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is the most common reproductive, endocrine, and metabolic disorder affecting 11-13% of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age. Although anovulation has traditionally been considered the primary cause of PMOS-associated infertility, accumulating evidence demonstrates that impaired endometrial receptivity and decidualization also contribute substantially to embryo implantation failure, recurrent pregnancy loss, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes, including miscarriage, gestational diabetes, pregnancy-induced hypertension, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. In addition to reproductive disorders, women with PMOS also commonly present with obesity, insulin resistance, and other long-term health conditions. This review summarizes current knowledge of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which PMOS disrupts endometrial function. We discuss how hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, obesity, and chronic inflammation, both independently and collectively, impair endometrial receptivity by altering androgen receptor (AR) signaling, glucose metabolism, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, immune homeostasis, cell-cell junctions, adhesion molecules, and key regulators of decidualization. We also highlight recent advances in transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing studies that have revealed cell type-specific alterations and molecular heterogeneity within the PMOS endometrium. Despite substantial progress, the mechanisms linking endocrine and metabolic abnormalities to impaired endometrial function remain incompletely understood. A better understanding of PMOS-associated endometrial dysfunction will facilitate the identification of novel therapeutic targets and improve embryo implantation success, pregnancy outcomes, and reproductive health in women with PMOS.

articles.title: Implementation of a Guideline for Short-Course Amikacin to Treat Multidrug-Resistant Urinary Tract Infections in Children.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract: We implemented an institutional guideline to facilitate extended-interval amikacin dosing for multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections. Amikacin was recommended as a single dose for uncomplicated cystitis and as three once-daily doses for pyelonephritis. After policy implementation, use of extended-interval amikacin became routine, and approximately one-quarter of amikacin-treated patients avoided admission.

articles.title: Changes in respiratory and gut microbiota in asthma and depression associate with disease markers.
articles.abstract: Asthma is heterogeneous and frequently accompanied by depression, affecting disease mechanisms and management. Both asthma and depression have been associated with inflammation and microbiota alterations, but their combined impact on microbial compositions remains unclear. Our exploratory study analyzed lung and gut microbiota in patients with asthma and depression to identify associations between microbiota composition and disease markers. This cross-sectional study included 20 healthy controls, 20 patients with asthma, and 20 patients with asthma and comorbid depression. Participants underwent clinical characterization and assessment of asthma control, depression, anxiety, and perceived stress. Induced sputum and fecal samples were collected for microbiota analysis, and inflammatory cytokines were measured in serum and sputum. Microbial profiling was performed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Lung function and FeNO levels were comparable between all groups. Asthma control scores were lower, and psychological scores were significantly higher in patients with asthma and comorbid depression compared with asthma alone and controls. Despite similar alpha and beta diversity across groups, sputum and fecal microbiota, particularly of healthy controls and comorbid patients, significantly differed in genus-level taxonomic composition. Correlation analyses demonstrated associations between clinical and psychological parameters and microbial profiles, including a consistent negative correlation between psychological scores and Neisseria abundance in both sputum and fecal samples. Asthma with comorbid depression is associated with distinct alterations in respiratory and gut microbiota, including reduced Neisseria perflava abundance correlating with psychological symptom severity.IMPORTANCEAsthma and depression frequently coexist, yet the potential contribution of microbial alterations to this comorbidity remains poorly understood. Because both respiratory and gut microbiota have been implicated in immune regulation and disease pathophysiology, characterizing microbiota patterns associated with asthma and depression may provide new insights into the biological links between these conditions. In this exploratory study, we investigated respiratory and gut microbiota in individuals with asthma, with and without comorbid depression, and healthy controls. Genus-level community composition differed between groups, particularly between controls and patients with asthma and depression. Notably, reduced abundance of Neisseria perflava in sputum and fecal samples was consistently associated with greater psychological symptom severity. These findings suggest that asthma accompanied by depression is associated with distinct alterations in microbial communities at multiple body sites. Further studies are warranted to determine whether such microbiota-psychological associations contribute to disease mechanisms or may serve as biomarkers of asthma-depression comorbidity.

articles.title: Microbiota-dependent citrulline metabolism alleviates sepsis by activating the aryl hydrocarbon receptor/IL-22 pathway to restore intestinal homeostasis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study investigated whether citrulline ameliorates sepsis-associated immune inflammation and intestinal barrier injury by modulating gut microbiota metabolites. Using an in vitro co-culture system and a cecal ligation and puncture mouse model, we found that citrulline fermentation products significantly increased the production of short-chain fatty acids and indole derivatives. These metabolic changes activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) pathway, upregulated interleukin-22 (IL-22) secretion, STAT3 phosphorylation, and restored the Treg/Th17 cell balance. Consequently, intestinal barrier function was improved, as evidenced by enhanced expression and membrane localization of tight junction proteins, and increased antimicrobial peptide production. Inhibition of AhR or STAT3 weakened the immunoregulatory and barrier-restorative effects of citrulline fermentation products in vitro. In vivo, citrulline treatment improved sepsis severity scores, reduced intestinal neutrophil infiltration, attenuated intestinal mucosal injury, increased goblet cell numbers, and decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines while increasing IL-10 levels in serum. Citrulline also alleviated CLP-induced lung and liver inflammatory injury. These protective effects were diminished by antibiotic treatment or AhR inhibition. RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that citrulline activates AhR and IL-22-responsive barrier gene programs while suppressing NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling. In conclusion, citrulline modulates the gut microbial metabolic environment to activate the AhR/IL-22/STAT3 axis, thereby rectifying immune imbalance, restoring intestinal integrity, and alleviating systemic inflammation in sepsis. These findings provide a novel theoretical foundation for nutritional and immune interventions in sepsis management.

IMPORTANCE: Sepsis, a life-threatening response to infection, often damages the gut, leading to a vicious cycle of inflammation and organ failure. While gut bacteria are known to influence health, how specific nutrients shape their protective effects in sepsis is unclear. This study reveals that the amino acid citrulline acts as a fuel for beneficial gut bacteria. When these bacteria metabolize citrulline, they produce molecules that act as signals to the body's immune system. These signals help calm harmful inflammation, repair the gut lining, and restore immune balance during sepsis. Our findings identify citrulline not just as a nutrient, but as a targeted regulator of the gut-immune axis, offering a promising new dietary strategy to support sepsis treatment by working with the body's microbial allies.

articles.title: Ecological role of the heterotrophic protist Aurantiochytrium (Labyrinthulomycetes) as a key consumer of viral-induced dissolved organic matter following the lysis of the red tide-forming microalga Heterosigma akashiwo.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Marine algal blooms play a vital role in oceanic carbon cycling. However, the ecological consequences of the organic matter released following bloom collapse via viral infection are poorly understood. Recent studies have shown that viral infection dramatically alters the intracellular metabolite composition of the host, and that the resulting viral lysate selectively promotes the growth of specific prokaryotic populations. This study aimed to elucidate the effects of organic matter derived from healthy and virus-infected cells of the bloom-forming alga Heterosigma akashiwo on the growth of heterotrophic eukaryotes, specifically labyrinthulomycetes. These marine protists are primarily saprotrophic or predatory and contribute to dissolved organic matter (DOM) decomposition and nutrient cycling. Field monitoring conducted in Osaka Bay over a 12-month period revealed that, although the overall Labyrinthulomycetes community showed no clear seasonality, specific populations of these protists co-occurred with Heterosigma akashiwo. To mechanistically investigate the potential trophic linkage suggested by these field observations, a co-culture system comprising H. akashiwo, its specific virus (HaV53), and Aurantiochytrium sp. NBRC102614, used as a model labyrinthulomycete, was established. In co-culture experiments, viral lysis of H. akashiwo led to a significant increase in the cell density of Aurantiochytrium sp., demonstrating that Aurantiochytrium can thrive on substrates derived from virus-infected algae, including viral-induced dissolved organic matter (vDOM). These findings highlight that heterotrophic Labyrinthulomycetes are key consumers of virus-modified organic matter, playing a pivotal role in carbon cycling following the collapse of harmful algal blooms and influencing carbon transfer within coastal microbial food webs.

IMPORTANCE: Marine ecosystems are shaped by interactions among microalgae, viruses, and heterotrophic eukaryotes, although the ecological roles of heterotrophic protists remain poorly understood. This study investigated the dynamics of oceanic microalgae and heterotrophic eukaryotes, namely Heterosigma species and Labyrinthulomycetes, and examined the effects of viral infection of Heterosigma akashiwo on the growth and proliferation of Aurantiochytrium species, members of the heterotrophic Labyrinthulomycetes. Our results revealed the dynamics of several Labyrinthulomycetes associated with Heterosigma populations and suggested that Aurantiochytrium species can redistribute carbon by utilizing the vDOM released during Heterosigma bloom termination induced by viral infection. These findings also reposition Aurantiochytrium from a passive heterotrophic component to an active ecological agent associated with Heterosigma viral infection, thereby influencing microalgal community dynamics. Overall, this study provides new insights into the fate of virus-infected Heterosigma in coastal marine systems, mediated by heterotrophic Labyrinthulomycetes, particularly Aurantiochytrium species, thereby filling an important knowledge gap in microbial ecology.

articles.title: Heat-responsive genes in Bemisia tabaci: roles in thermotolerance and neonicotinoid resistance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temperature strongly influences insect physiology and can affect responses to chemical stress. However, the molecular basis underlying the relationship between thermal responses and insecticide resistance in the whitefly Bemisia tabaci remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify conserved temperature-responsive genes and determine their functional roles in thermotolerance and neonicotinoid resistance.

RESULTS: Comparative transcriptomic analyses of B. tabaci reared on cotton, soybean, and tomato identified 22 commonly up-regulated and seven commonly down-regulated genes under 32 °C compared with 25 °C. Nine shared temperature-responsive genes were selected for further analysis, and temporal expression profiling identified HSP70, HSP68, CYP6DW5, and CYP6A20 as prominent temperature-responsive candidates. RNA interference showed that silencing either HSP70 or HSP68 significantly increased mortality at 32 °C but had limited effects at 25 °C, supporting their roles in thermotolerance. In addition, silencing either CYP6DW5 or CYP6A20 significantly increased mortality following exposure to thiamethoxam, acetamiprid, and thiacloprid in the resistant population, but not in the susceptible population, demonstrating their contribution to neonicotinoid resistance.

CONCLUSION: High temperature induces a conserved but functionally diverse transcriptional response in B. tabaci, with HSP70 and HSP68 contributing to thermotolerance and CYP6DW5 and CYP6A20 contributing to resistance against multiple neonicotinoids. These findings indicate that temperature-responsive genes can participate in distinct processes underlying thermal adaptation and insecticide resistance. Further investigation of the interaction between environmental temperature and resistance-associated pathways will improve our understanding of resistance phenotypes and may inform insecticide management under changing climatic conditions. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Ligilactobacillus salivarius inhibits GII.4[P16] human norovirus replication in zebrafish larvae.
articles.abstract: Human gut bacteria can modulate human norovirus (HuNoV) infection, underscoring the need to characterize virus-bacterium interactions. This study evaluated the effect of Ligilactobacillus salivarius on HuNoV GII.4[P16] replication using a zebrafish larva model. A GII.4[P16]-positive stool specimen was resuspended in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), centrifuged, and the supernatant stored at -80°C. L. salivarius was grown overnight in de Man, Rogosa, and Sharpe broth, from which bacterial cells and cell-free supernatant (CFS) were collected. The overnight broth (OB), cells, and CFS were each mixed with virus suspension at a 1:1 ratio, and 3 nL were microinjected into 3-day post-fertilization larvae; controls received PBS with virus. Daily until 4 days post-infection (dpi), 2 samples of 10 pooled larvae were collected, and RNA was extracted and quantified by droplet digital PCR. Two-way analysis of variance showed that treatment and time significantly influenced viral RNA levels (P < 0.001), with a marginal interaction (P = 0.051) indicating consistent inhibitory trends across the study period. CFS-injected larvae showed replication comparable to controls (P > 0.05), peaking at 5.31 log RNA copies/larva at 1 dpi, whereas cell-containing treatments (cells and OB) significantly reduced replication (P < 0.01) throughout the 4-day period. An in vitro binding assay showed that 67% of the virus inoculum physically bound to L. salivarius. In a further comparison, both live and heat-killed bacteria reduced replication initially; live L. salivarius significantly inhibited replication at 3 dpi (P < 0.05). These findings support the hypothesis that L. salivarius physically binds to HuNoV GII.4[P16] and inhibits viral replication, highlighting its potential as a probiotic intervention for HuNoV infection.IMPORTANCENorovirus remains the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, responsible for nearly 700 million cases and substantial economic burden annually, yet no vaccine or antiviral therapy currently exists. This study's findings are significant because they identify a specific probiotic strain, Ligilactobacillus salivarius, capable of directly binding to and inhibiting replication of a clinically relevant norovirus genotype (GII.4[P16]), which is responsible for many recent outbreaks globally. By demonstrating that live bacterial cells-not just secreted metabolites-drive this antiviral effect, the study points toward a mechanistic, cell-mediated mode of action that could inform targeted probiotic formulations. The use of a zebrafish larva model also offers a valuable, scalable in vivo system for studying norovirus-microbiome interactions, addressing a major bottleneck in norovirus research caused by the lack of robust cell culture systems. Together, these findings advance understanding of bacterium-virus interactions and support further development of probiotic-based strategies for preventing or reducing norovirus infection severity.

articles.title: Performance of mCIM/eCIM in Enterobacterales strains co-encoding NDM and OXA-48-like carbapenemases from South India.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) are an increasing public health concern, particularly as carbapenemase-producing isolates, such as NDM and OXA-48-like producers, become more prevalent. Rapid and accurate identification of carbapenemases is crucial to guide appropriate antibiotic therapy. Although recent epidemiologic data show that CRE increasingly harbor multiple carbapenemases, the performance of common phenotypic tests-the modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified CIM (eCIM)-has not been well defined in these isolates. We examined the performance of mCIM and eCIM among CRE-encoding NDM, OXA-48-like, or both. We included 172 genotypically confirmed carbapenemase-encoding CRE isolates from perirectal swabs collected from patients admitted to two intensive care units at a hospital in South India. Isolates included Escherichia coli (53.5%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (41.3%), and Enterobacter species (5.3%). Overall, 112 isolates (65.1%) encoded NDM alone, 23 (13.4%) encoded OXA-48-like alone, and 37 (21.5%) encoded both NDM and OXA-48-like. mCIM positivity was 98.2% for NDM, 47.8% for OXA-48-like, and 94.6% for NDM+OXA-48-like encoders; among mCIM-positive isolates, eCIM positivity rates were 99.1%, 91%, and 97.1%, respectively. When compared to molecular carbapenemase gene detection, mCIM/eCIM was highly sensitive for classifying isolates encoding NDM as metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) producers, but significantly misclassified isolates encoding OXA-48-like as having an MBL or lacking a carbapenemase. In the largest collection of NDM and OXA-48-like co-encoding CRE isolates to date, mCIM/eCIM typically reported these as MBL producers.

IMPORTANCE: Carbapenemase-encoding Enterobacterales infections are associated with substantial adverse health outcomes, making rapid and accurate carbapenemase detection essential for guiding antibiotic therapy. Although Enterobacterales carrying multiple carbapenemases are increasingly reported worldwide, the performance of common phenotypic assays, mCIM and eCIM, remains insufficiently defined for these strains. In this study of 172 genotypically confirmed carbapenemase-encoding Enterobacterales isolates from hospitalized patients in South India, mCIM/eCIM consistently classified NDM-encoding isolates as metallo-β-lactamase encoders. Additionally, mCIM/eCIM frequently misclassified OXA-48-like-encoding isolates as either metallo-β-lactamase encoders or carbapenemase-negative, highlighting the need to better understand the mechanisms underlying this variable activity. In the largest collection of NDM and OXA co-encoding Enterobacterales isolates reported to date, mCIM/eCIM generally reported co-encoding isolates as metallo-β-lactamase producers. Our results suggest that mCIM/eCIM performance may vary geographically due to variable activity, distribution, and combinations of carbapenemases.

articles.title: Differential Effect of Endovascular Treatment in Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: A Distal Secondary Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion stroke are heterogeneous. Randomized trials show no net benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) over best medical treatment (BMT) alone, which may mask heterogeneity of treatment effect. We used an externally developed machine learning model to predict excellent early neurological outcome (EENO) with BMT alone and examined whether the effect of EVT differed across predicted risk.

METHODS: A Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) model was trained to predict EENO (24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score of 0-2) in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion treated with BMT alone in a local Bernese Stroke Registry. This model was applied to patients from the DISTAL randomized trial (55 centers and 11 countries), who were randomized to EVT plus BMT or BMT alone. We tested for interaction between predicted EENO and treatment allocation on the primary outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale shift), repeating this using admission NIHSS alone.

RESULTS: In the development cohort (n=257, 42% female, and mean age 70.4±14.8 years), 54% achieved EENO. In the DISTAL cohort (270 BMT alone, 269 EVT plus BMT, 44% female, and mean age 74.9±12.0 years), the model showed moderate external discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.73). A significant interaction was found between predicted EENO and treatment effect (Pinteraction=0.012): in 152 patients predicted to achieve EENO, EVT was associated with worse 90-day modified Rankin Scale score (common odds ratio, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.27-0.84]), whereas no treatment effect was seen in 387 patients predicted not to achieve EENO (common odds ratio 1.13 [95% CI, 0.79-1.60]). A model using admission NIHSS alone showed comparable discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.71) and a common odds ratio for EVT of 0.47 (95% CI, 0.25-0.89) in patients with an NIHSS score of ≤4 and a common odds ratio of 1.05 (95% CI, 0.75-1.47) in patients with an NIHSS score of >4 (Pinteraction=0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: EVT was harmful in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion predicted to achieve EENO with BMT alone, and an NIHSS-alone model performed comparably to the multivariable model.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05029414.

articles.title: Oya virus reporter systems for high-throughput screening of viral replication inhibitors in mosquito cells.
articles.abstract: Orthobunyaviruses are a diverse group of arboviruses, yet reporter virus-based inhibitor screening in mosquito-derived cells remains underexplored. Oya virus (OYAV), a Simbu serogroup orthobunyavirus detected in humans, mosquitoes, and midges, currently lacks reverse genetics tools and quantitative compound screening platforms. In this study, we established the first plasmid-based reverse genetics system for OYAV, successfully rescuing recombinant wild-type virus (rOYAV/WT) alongside fluorescent reporter viruses expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (rOYAV/eGFP/S) or mCherry (rOYAV/mCherry/S). Both reporter viruses maintained stable reporter expression and infectivity across multiple vertebrate and mosquito-derived cell lines, although reporter insertion resulted in attenuated replication compared with the parental virus. Leveraging the robust fluorescence signal and retention of the reporter-containing region during serial passage, we developed a mosquito cell-based high-content screening platform to identify compounds inhibiting OYAV replication in C6/36 cells. The assay demonstrated high robustness and reproducibility, with a Z' factor of 0.755, and showed strong correlation with wild-type virus replication profiles. By screening an 800-compound library, we identified 10 candidates exhibiting >95% inhibitory activity against OYAV replication. Among these, saikosaponin B2, fingolimod (hydrochloride), and fangchinoline displayed micromolar inhibitory effects against both reporter and wild-type OYAV replication, with limited cytotoxicity in C6/36 cells. Collectively, this study establishes the reverse genetics system for OYAV and a quantitative mosquito-cell-based screening platform for orthobunyavirus replication inhibitors, providing a valuable tool for studying OYAV replication and evaluating antiviral compounds in mosquito-derived cells.IMPORTANCEOya virus (OYAV) is an emerging arbovirus circulating in Asia, with documented infection in humans and arthropod vectors. However, the absence of reverse genetics and reporter systems has limited mechanistic studies and inhibitor discovery for OYAV, particularly in arthropod-derived cells. Here, we established a reverse genetics system and generated fluorescent reporter viruses that enable real-time monitoring of OYAV replication. The optimized reporter virus was further used to establish a high-throughput inhibitor screening platform in mosquito C6/36 cells, leading to the identification of three compounds with inhibitory activity and low cytotoxicity in this system. These tools provide a foundation for investigating OYAV biology and facilitate the discovery and evaluation of inhibitors in vector cells and potentially in live vectors.

articles.title: LPC(16:0) and prothrombin time as mortality predictors in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome.
articles.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with a high fatality rate. However, the impact of the SFTS virus (SFTSV) on host lipid metabolism and its relationship with the prognosis of patients remain unclear. To determine the lipid metabolism profile of SFTSV-infected and identify prognostic biomarkers, targeted lipidomics analysis was conducted on SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and serum samples from 71 subjects (including 15 healthy controls, 35 SFTS survivors, and 21 SFTS deceased patients) in this study. Our findings revealed that glycerophospholipid metabolism was the most significantly disrupted pathway in both SFTSV-infected Huh7 cells and SFTS patients, with lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) species, including LPC(16:1), LPC(18:1), LPC(16:0), and LPC(18:0), showing decreased levels. Together with clinical parameters, prothrombin time (PT) and LPC(16:0) were further identified as prognostic factors, and the combined model incorporating these two markers predicted mortality with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.937. These findings provide a foundation for mortality prediction and mechanistic understanding of SFTS.IMPORTANCEEffective prognostic tools and targeted therapies for SFTS remain urgently needed, as current clinical management relies largely on supportive care and lacks reliable indicators for early risk stratification. This study enhances our understanding of lipid alterations following SFTSV infection, opens potential avenues for metabolism-targeted intervention, and may aid in assessing disease progression and guiding appropriate clinical interventions.

articles.title: Positive Urine Cultures for Enterococcus spp. vs. Escherichia coli in Febrile Infants Younger Than 90 Days: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare febrile infants aged 90 days or younger with Enterococcus spp. or Escherichia coli in urine cultures, overall and by urine dipstick findings.

METHODS: Matched cohort study in three Spanish paediatric emergency departments (2011-2023). Infants with Enterococcus spp. were matched 1:1 by age and sex with infants with E. coli and compared using paired tests; dipstick-stratified analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: Of 4006 febrile infants, 77 (1.9%) had Enterococcus spp. Abnormal dipstick findings were less frequent than with E. coli (27.3% vs. 80.5%; p < 0.001), and blood inflammatory markers were lower, largely reflecting the higher proportion of normal dipsticks. Abnormal voiding cystourethrogram findings were more frequent with Enterococcus spp., with abnormal (70.0% vs. 27.6%; p = 0.03) and normal dipsticks (33.3% vs. 0%; p = 0.04). With abnormal dipsticks, abnormal dimercaptosuccinic acid scans (6/11 vs. 0/17; p = 0.001) and recurrent urinary tract infections (33.3% vs. 8.1%; p = 0.009) were more frequent with Enterococcus spp.

CONCLUSION: In these infants, Enterococcus spp. in urine usually had a normal dipstick but was associated with more urinary tract abnormalities than E. coli. Enterococcal infections with abnormal dipsticks were associated with more renal scan abnormalities and recurrences; the significance of isolates with normal dipsticks remains uncertain.

articles.title: ApoB/ApoA-I Ratio Identifies Hidden Atherogenic Risk Beyond Conventional Lipid Parameters in Normolipidemic Adults.
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is a major modifiable risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (ASCVD). However, conventional lipid parameters may underestimate cardiovascular risk in individuals with normolipidemic profiles. The apolipoprotein B (ApoB)/apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I) ratio has emerged as a sensitive marker reflecting the balance between proatherogenic and antiatherogenic lipoproteins. This cross-sectional analytical study included 104 apparently healthy adults aged 23-68 years with normal lipid profiles. Serum lipid and apolipoprotein levels were measured using standard enzymatic and immunoturbidimetric methods. Statistical analyses included correlation, group comparison, and multivariate regression analysis. Males demonstrated significantly higher triglycerides, lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and elevated ApoB/ApoA-I ratios compared with females (p < 0.05). Participants with an ApoB/ApoA-I ratio > 0.8 showed significantly higher total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), non-HDL-C, triglycerides, and atherogenic indices, along with lower HDL-C (p < 0.05), despite having lipid values within normal ranges. Strong positive correlations were observed between the ApoB/ApoA-I ratio and atherogenic lipid markers. Multivariate regression identified LDL-C and LDL/ApoB ratio as independent predictors of the ApoB/ApoA-I ratio. The ApoB/ApoA-I ratio can identify hidden atherogenic risk not detected by conventional lipid parameters, indicating possible misclassification of cardiovascular risk in normolipidemic individuals. Additional assessment using apolipoproteins could enhance risk stratification in the initial phases. However, further longitudinal studies are required to establish the predictive value for clinical cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Pasteurella canis sepsis in alcoholic liver cirrhosis without an animal bite or scratch: A case report.
articles.abstract: Pasteurella canis is a commensal of the oral flora of domestic animals. In humans, it clinically manifests as localised soft-tissue infections and rarely presents with bacteraemia or sepsis. We present a case of a male in his early 30s with pre-existing alcoholic liver cirrhosis who presented with low-grade fever, was allergic to penicillin and reported close contact with three domestic cats with no history of bites, scratches, or local infection. Haematological investigations suggested bacterial sepsis with a diagnostic tap ruling out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. P. canis was isolated from the blood and was successfully treated with intravenous doxycycline.

articles.title: Diabetes-Related Stigma in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aims to identify the extent of the stigma experienced by patients with type 2 diabetes, determine its associated predictors, and explore the patients' experiences.

DESIGN: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed.

METHODS: A cross-sectional design was employed in the quantitative phase; subsequently, in the qualitative phase, interviews were conducted using a phenomenological approach. Quantitative data were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, and hierarchical regression analysis, while qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis.

FINDINGS: In the multiple regression analysis of the quantitative findings, it was determined that education level (β = 0.169, p < 0.001), duration of diabetes diagnosis (β = -0.094, p = 0.033), history of diabetes-related complications (β = -0.197, p < 0.001), HbA1c level (β = 0.381, p < 0.001), and age (β = -0.309, p < 0.001) were statistically significant predictors of the participants' levels of stigmatization (p < 0.001). Qualitative findings were organized into four main themes: (1) sources of stigma, (2) emotional burnout and feelings of exclusion, (3) social life with diabetes, and (4) coping and support mechanisms.

CONCLUSION: Stigmatization in patients with diabetes is associated with clinical findings, younger age, a higher level of education, and diabetes-related complications; it can stem from various sources and lead to emotional distress, a sense of exclusion, and social isolation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: By recognizing the risk of stigmatization, nurses can provide guidance in the planning and implementation of intervention programs tailored to the patient's social context, as well as in the delivery of education and counseling services.

articles.title: Clinical and toxicological factors associated with pediatric intensive care unit admission in pediatric acute poisoning: a 10-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute poisoning is an important cause of emergency department visits among children and adolescents. Early identification of patients requiring escalation-of-care or pediatric intensive care unit-level monitoring remains clinically challenging. The purpose of this study is to evaluate clinical and toxicological factors associated with pediatric intensive care unit admission in pediatric acute poisoning.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 652 patients younger than 18 years managed for acute poisoning between 2015 and 2024 at a tertiary university hospital. Demographic, exposure-related, toxicological, clinical, and laboratory variables were analyzed. Pediatric intensive care unit admission was evaluated as an escalation-of-care and healthcare utilization outcome. Three multivariable logistic regression models were constructed, including models excluding variables closely related to admission decisions to reduce potential incorporation bias.

RESULTS: Of 652 patients, 99 (15.2%) were admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit. Across the primary and sensitivity models, delayed presentation, psychiatric disorder history, and multiple-drug ingestion remained independently associated with admission. Lower Glasgow Coma Scale score and cardiovascular findings were associated with admission in models including clinical severity variables. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses demonstrated poor discriminatory performance of individual parameters, indicating that none were suitable as stand-alone triage tools. No deaths occurred, invasive mechanical ventilation was required in one patient, and advanced organ-support interventions were uncommon.

DISCUSSION: Pediatric intensive care unit admission appeared to reflect both observed clinical instability and anticipated toxicological risk rather than poisoning severity alone. The poor discriminatory performance of individual parameters suggests that admission decisions are multifactorial and should not rely on a single clinical or laboratory variable.

CONCLUSION: Delayed presentation, multiple-drug ingestion, psychiatric disorder history, and clinical severity indicators were associated with pediatric intensive care unit admission. These findings should be interpreted as observational evidence regarding escalation-of-care decisions rather than as a validated prediction model or triage tool in this single-center pediatric poisoning cohort.

articles.title: Letter: The Q425R Variant in Chronic Hepatitis Delta-Distinguishing Cirrhosis Prevalence From Portal Hypertension Severity. Authors' Reply.
Field Medical Observations from a Remote High-Altitude Community on the Route to K2 (Askole Study I).
articles.abstract: BackgroundAskole (9843 ft [≈3000 m], Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan), the last village on the route to K2 Base Camp, is a remote high-altitude community with limited healthcare access, unsafe water, and infrastructural constraints. No systematic data describe its health burden, although such information is needed to plan future medical expeditions.MethodsFrom September 8 to 18, 2025 (11 working days), 2 Italian Alpine Club physicians provided medical care and health education at the Lorenzo Mazzoleni Dispensary. Clinical evaluation was supplemented by electrocardiography, ultrasonography, pulse oximetry, blood pressure measurement, and point-of-care glucometer and urine dipstick testing. School-based vision screening with the Lang stereotest was performed in Korphe.Results and DiscussionA total of 171 patients (174 visits; mean age 23.6 years) were evaluated. Gastrointestinal infectious diseases were most frequent, likely related to unsafe water and poor hygiene, followed by musculoskeletal disorders, chiefly lumbosacral radiculopathy, in adults. Skin, genitourinary, oral, ear, and ocular conditions were also common. Respiratory and cardiovascular symptoms occurred in relatively young individuals, without electrocardiographic evidence of ischemia, structural abnormality, or infarction; chronic mountain sickness was not systematically assessed. Vision screening identified stereoacuity deficits in 1.9% of children examined, all referred for ophthalmological evaluation. One new case of diabetes mellitus was diagnosed.ConclusionsInfectious disease is the main health burden in this setting. Improvements in water safety and infrastructure are essential, as health education alone is insufficient. These observations, limited by a small sample and short observation period, can nonetheless inform the planning of future medical expeditions.

articles.title: Four-dimensional CT angiography-derived dynamic collaterals and perfusion deficits as predictors of stroke recurrence in moderate middle cerebral artery stenosis: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundNon-cardioembolic non-disabling minor ischemic stroke carries a considerable risk of early recurrence that is not fully captured by clinical severity scales. Hemodynamic impairment and collateral status may improve risk stratification.PurposeTo assess the prognostic value of four-dimensional computed tomography angiography (4D-CTA)-derived collateral status and CT perfusion parameters for predicting recurrence in patients with minor stroke and moderate middle cerebral artery (MCA) stenosis.Material and MethodsIn this prospective study (July 2024 to June 2025), 183 patients with minor ischemic stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS)  ≤ 5) and symptomatic moderate (50%-69%) MCA stenosis were enrolled. All underwent multimodal CT imaging and received standardized dual antiplatelet therapy. Collateral status was graded using 4D-CTA (modified American Society of Interventional and Therapeutic Neuroradiology/Society of Interventional Radiology (ASITN/SIR)), and perfusion parameters, including relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and Tmax, were quantified. The primary endpoint was recurrent ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed.ResultsOver a median follow-up of approximately 10 months, rCBF < 30% volume was the only independent predictor of recurrence (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.168, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.039-1.314; P = 0.010). Poor collateral status showed a non-significant trend overall (HR = 2.079; P = 0.093) but was strongly associated with recurrence in patients without limb weakness (HR = 9.875; P = 0.030).ConclusionMultimodal CT-derived hemodynamic parameters outperform clinical scores in predicting recurrence. rCBF <30% is a robust predictor, while 4D-CTA collateral assessment is particularly valuable in clinically mild patients without motor deficits.

articles.title: Angiographic findings, revascularisations and mortality in childhood cancer survivors with ischaemic heart disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of childhood cancer (CCS) have higher risk of developing ischaemic heart disease (IHD), however, data on coronary anatomy, revascularisations, and prognosis remain limited. The objective was to investigate angiographic findings, invasive treatment patterns and mortality in CCS with IHD compared with controls without a history of childhood cancer.

METHODS: This was a nationwide retrospective cohort-study of all 5-year survivors of leukaemia, lymphoma, or central nervous system cancer who subsequently developed IHD, with index cancer between 1958-2021. CCS were compared with population-based controls with IHD matched on cancer date by age, sex and residence.

RESULTS: 136 CCS and 667 controls with IHD were included. CCS were a median of 5.2 years younger than controls at diagnosis of IHD. CCS had a higher prevalence of left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis (25.0% vs. 6.5%; p < 0.001) and multivessel disease (51.2% vs. 39.4%; p = 0.043). Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) was more frequently performed in CCS (22.8% vs. 11.4%; p < 0.001), although after adjusting for relevant covariates the difference was attenuated. After a median follow-up of 5.4 years following IHD diagnosis, CCS had higher hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 1.83, 95% CI 1.31-2.54; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.42-2.95; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: CCS who developed IHD demonstrate a higher burden of extensive coronary artery disease, characterized by increased prevalence of LMCA stenosis and multivessel disease. Although overall revascularisation rates were similar, CCS experienced significantly higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality following IHD-diagnosis compared with controls.

articles.title: Dietary patterns and odds of prevalent gout comorbidity in diabetes mellitus: a mediation analysis of glucose metabolism and renal function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While independent associations between dietary patterns and diabetes mellitus (DM) or gout have been established, their relationship in comorbid conditions remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations between distinct dietary patterns and prevalent gout among individuals with DM.

METHODS: We retrieved data in this cross-sectional study from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. We used logistic regression models and Restricted cubic splines to explore associations between five dietary patterns (healthy eating index 2020 (HEI-2020), dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH), alternate Mediterranean diet score (aMED), dietary inflammatory index, and alternative healthy diet index). We also conducted subgroup and mediation analyses.

RESULTS: In multivariable-adjusted models, HEI-2020 (odds ratio (OR) = 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.70-0.96, P = 0.015), DASH (OR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.70-0.98, P = 0.031), and aMED (OR = 0.86; 95% CI = 0.74-0.99, P = 0.041) scores were significantly associated with lower odds of prevalent gout among individuals with DM, with no nonlinear trends observed. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant interactions. Mediation analyses suggested that the triglyceride-glucose index-ratio of waist circumference to height mediated 40.2% and 22.8% of the effects of the DASH and HEI-2020 patterns, respectively. Serum uric acid showed evidence of mediation for the aMED pattern accounting for 16.3% of the association.

CONCLUSIONS: Among people with DM in the USA, adherence to HEI-2020, DASH, and aMED dietary patterns is associated with lower odds of prevalent gout comorbidity in people with DM. Dietary structure improvement may therefore be associated with a lower burden of gout comorbidity in this population.

articles.title: Multimodal imaging features of primary jaw lymphoma: a retrospective analysis of 53 cases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study systematically evaluated imaging characteristics of primary jaw lymphoma using multiple modalities to improve diagnostic accuracy and differentiation from other maxillofacial pathoses.

METHODS: Fifty-three patients with histopathologically confirmed jaw lymphoma (January 2000-March 2025) were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical data including chief complaints and misdiagnosis history were investigated. Imaging features-lesion location, soft-tissue swelling, cortical destruction pattern, internal structure, and metabolic activity-were assessed using panoramic radiography, CT, MRI, and PET.

RESULTS: Initial misdiagnoses as odontogenic infection or inflammation led to inappropriate treatments in 27 of 53 cases (50.9%). Lesions most commonly involved the maxillary tuberosity (24.5%), with maxillary sinus extension in 74.2% of maxillary cases. Prominent soft-tissue swelling was observed in 50.9%, while severe cortical destruction predominated (61.2%). CT evaluation revealed cortical micro-perforations in 48.9% of cases occurring exclusively within the maxilla-though predominant in only 16.3%. PET imaging commonly demonstrated multi-site involvement with intense FDG uptake comparable to brain activity.
