CONCLUSIONS: Primary jaw lymphoma demonstrated characteristic features including severe cortical destruction with micro-perforation and prominent soft-tissue swelling. Frequent cortical micro-perforations highlight the importance of careful CT evaluation for subtle cortical breakthrough. Recognition of these features, particularly with non-specific clinical symptoms, may improve early diagnostic suspicion, reduce misdiagnosis as odontogenic infection, and facilitate timely biopsy and management.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This is the first study to systematically characterize cortical micro-perforation as a distinctive imaging feature of primary jaw lymphoma. This finding may help reduce misdiagnosis as an odontogenic infection.

articles.title: Plasma magnesium levels and postoperative atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after cardiac surgery, and hypomagnesemia has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor. In centers with active magnesium repletion protocols, however, overt hypomagnesemia has become uncommon. We aimed to determine whether postoperative plasma magnesium concentration is independently associated with POAF.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 435 adults undergoing cardiac surgery at a hospital specializing in cardiovascular disease. Postoperative plasma magnesium concentration, assessed at intensive care unit admission, as the mean value, and as the lowest value, was evaluated as the primary exposure in multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for relevant preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative covariates.

RESULTS: Isolated coronary artery bypass grafting was the most frequent procedure (46.6%). Overall mortality was 3.2%, and POAF incidence was 16.8%. Under active repletion, hypomagnesemia occurred in only 3.4% of patients. None of the three magnesium measures was independently associated with POAF. In contrast, age, type of surgical procedure, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and postoperative acute kidney injury were independently associated with POAF.

CONCLUSIONS: Under a protocol of active postoperative magnesium repletion, we did not detect an independent association between plasma magnesium concentration-within the observed normal-to-high range-and POAF. This complication was primarily related to age, type of surgery, and severe ventricular dysfunction, factors that should guide postoperative risk stratification; acute kidney injury showed a concurrent association with POAF and may act as a marker of shared postoperative risk factors rather than a causal factor.

articles.title: Severe COPD - A proposed individualized and comprehensive clinical definition.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

articles.title: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload: A case-based analysis illustrating a multiple-hit framework for clinical practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO) is a leading cause of transfusion-related morbidity and mortality, yet it may be difficult to recognise in acutely ill patients without established cardiac or renal disease. In such cases, risk may reflect the interaction of biological vulnerability, inflammatory milieu, component-related exposure and clinical workflow rather than transfused volume alone.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 52-year-old man with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukaemia who developed acute hypertensive pulmonary oedema during plasma transfusion despite preserved systolic function. Pre-event findings included bilateral pleural effusions, a moderate-to-large pericardial effusion without tamponade, systemic inflammation, thrombocytopenia and mildly abnormal coagulation parameters. Documented component and medication-related fluid exposure was 1.82 L before deterioration and 1.82-2.14 L before/around onset. At onset, he developed sudden dyspnoea, hypertension, tachycardia and hypoxaemia, with SpO2 81% on 3 L/min nasal oxygen. Post-event imaging showed new bilateral pulmonary oedema and interstitial changes. NT-proBNP increased from 971.7 to 2143 pg/mL, approximately 2.2-fold. He improved after transfusion cessation, oxygen escalation and intravenous furosemide. Overall, the episode was clinically diagnosed as TACO rather than transfusion-related acute lung injury or transfusion-associated dyspnoea.

ANALYSIS: The episode was best understood as a multi-hit event. Pre-existing effusions, systemic inflammation, repeated component and medication-related exposure and incomplete reassessment between units narrowed the patient's reserve. The key issue was not volume alone, but the patient's reduced ability to tolerate further exposure.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: This case supports a practical multiple-hit approach to TACO prevention and recognition. Blood transfusion therapy should be managed as a dynamic intervention requiring repeated evaluation of indication, rate, volume and patient reserve. This approach may help clinicians stratify risk before and between units, recognise warning signs earlier and individualise transfusion practice.

articles.title: Drug-induced QT prolongation in oncology: A precision-medicine.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionProlongation of the heart-rate-corrected QT interval (QTc) is a defining safety concern in oncology, where patients face an expanding array of repolarization-altering agents superimposed on supportive drugs, electrolyte disturbgances, and organ dysfunction. The anchoring event, torsade de pointes, is uncommon but potentially lethal, and arrhythmic risk must be balanced against the survival benefit of effective cancer therapy.MethodsThe literature was identified through structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science covering the mechanistic, drug-class, pharmacovigilance, pharmacogenomic, risk-prediction, and management aspects of drug-induced QT prolongation in oncology, and was synthesized narratively with an emphasis on precision-medicine dimensions.ResultsQT liability is heterogeneous across tyrosine kinase inhibitors, cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, arsenic trioxide, and supportive agents such as antiemetics, antifungals, opioids, and antibiotics, and is frequently amplified by electrolyte derangement and drug-drug interactions. Genetic susceptibility, real-world pharmacovigilance, and machine-learning risk prediction are emerging but remain underdeveloped in oncology. Pragmatic management rests on baseline and serial Fridericia-corrected electrocardiography, electrolyte optimization, judicious agent selection and dose modification, medication review within a multidisciplinary team, and selection of structured lower-risk alternatives.ConclusionsDrug-induced QT prolongation in oncology is manageable rather than inevitable. Combining genomic susceptibility, pharmacovigilance, and validated prediction tools offers a route to individualized risk stratification, although prospective oncology-specific evidence and data from under-represented populations remain limited. Early identification and disciplined monitoring allow clinicians to protect the heart without compromising effective cancer treatment.

articles.title: Longitudinal PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0 response assessment in vorasidenib-treated IDH-mutant gliomas: the VORAFET study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional MRI may not fully reflect the biological activity of vorasidenib. PET may detect treatment-related metabolic changes before structural changes become evident on MRI. We evaluated longitudinal PET and MRI changes in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas receiving vorasidenib.

METHODS: VORAFET is a longitudinal study of adults with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with vorasidenib. Eligible patients had predominantly non-enhancing WHO grade 2 or 3 gliomas, had not received prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was longitudinal metabolic and structural imaging response according to PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0. Integrated [¹⁸F]FET PET/MRI was performed at baseline and every 3 months.

RESULTS: Thirty-nine patients were included; at baseline, 23 and 29 had PET and MRI-measurable disease. As best response, PET RANO 1.0 identified 2 complete and 12 partial responses, yielding an ORR of 60.9%; median time to first response was 4.5 months (range 3-12 months). RANO 2.0 showed no complete or partial responses, whereas 5 patients achieved minor response at a median of 9 months (range 6-12 months). Progressive disease occurred in 6 of 39 patients (15.4%) according to PET RANO 1.0 and in 1 of 39 (2.6%) according to RANO 2.0. Patients with PET-PD more often had subtle contrast enhancement and showed higher baseline FLAIR volume, MTV, TBRmax, and TBRmean.

CONCLUSIONS: PET RANO 1.0 identified metabolic changes during vorasidenib treatment that were not always reflected by RANO 2.0 assessment. Longer follow-up is needed to clarify the relationship between PET metabolic changes and MRI findings and to determine their clinical significance.

articles.title: Pragmatic trial of a self-directed intervention for weight loss in obstructive sleep apnea (POWER).
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Self-directed lifestyle interventions may improve access to weight loss care in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but effectiveness in routine practice is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: Test whether a proactively delivered self-directed lifestyle intervention improves weight and sleep-related quality of life versus usual care.

METHODS: POWER enrolled patients with OSA and body mass index of 30-45 kg/m2, recruited from Veteran Affairs (VA) sites nationwide, and randomized participants to a self-directed intervention based on the Diabetes Prevention Program with video-based sessions, readings, and regular coaching reminders or usual care. Co-primary outcomes were change in Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) and clinical weight in kilograms (kg) from baseline to 12 months post-randomization. Given two primary outcomes, we defined significance at p = 0.025.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: This trial randomized 696 participants. Mean age was 56.2 years (SD 12.2), with 19.7% identifying as female. Clinical weights at 12 months were available for 81.9% of intervention and 83.6% of control participants. Unadjusted weight declined 2.1 kg (SD 6.8) in intervention and 0.9 kg (SD 5.9) in control (adjusted between-group difference: -1.1 kg, 95%CI -2.0, -0.1; p = 0.037). FOSQ measures were available at 12 months for 78.2% of intervention and 90.5% of control participants. From baseline to 12 months, unadjusted FOSQ improved 1.4 (SD 2.7) points in intervention and 0.9 (SD 2.9) points in control (adjusted between-group difference: 0.6 points, 95%CI 0.2, 1.0; p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Among participants with OSA and obesity, a self-directed lifestyle intervention did not improve weight loss and led to improvements in sleep-related quality of life that are of limited clinical importance.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05104450, registered 10/19/2021.

articles.title: Effect of the Medicare Competitive Bidding Program on the Supplemental Oxygen Supplier Market Among Patients with COPD.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

articles.title: Comprehensive hemodynamic assessment of the Fontan pathway using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Conventional hemodynamic assessment of Fontan circulation relies on limited quantitative measurements. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical value of comprehensive flow visualization using four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging to characterize patient-specific hemodynamic patterns in extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection.

METHODS: Eight patients with extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection underwent four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging at a median of 13.7 years postoperatively (interquartile range: 9.0-16.4 years). The Fontan pathway was segmented into five regions: extracardiac conduit, superior vena cava, central confluence, left pulmonary artery, and right pulmonary artery. Energy loss, maximum velocity, and kinetic energy were quantified for each segment using iTFlow software. Clinical outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

RESULTS: Median age at total cavopulmonary connection was 1.8 years (interquartile range: 1.5-3.5), with 18 mm conduits in seven patients and 22 mm conduit in one patient. During a median follow-up of 17.3 years, two patients underwent re-operation after magnetic resonance imaging evaluation (tricuspid valve replacement and ascending aortic reconstruction); all remained alive without Fontan failure. Energy loss differed significantly across segments (p = 0.011), being highest in the conduit and central confluence, with remarkable inter-patient variability superimposed (conduit values varying 35-fold from 0.025 to 0.887 mW). Maximum velocity strongly correlated with energy loss (r = 0.92, p = 0.001), suggesting velocity may serve as an accessible surrogate. Atrioventricular valve regurgitation severity did not consistently correlate with energy loss.

CONCLUSIONS: Four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging with iTFlow software enables comprehensive hemodynamic assessment throughout the Fontan pathway, revealing substantial patient-specific heterogeneity in energy efficiency. With larger cohorts and correlation with clinical outcomes, this technique may become a valuable screening tool for post-Fontan evaluation and long-term surveillance.

articles.title: Clinical and psychosocial factors associated with clinician-driven allocation to hybrid versus in-person care in chronic disease management: a Colombian retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Hybrid care is increasingly used for chronic disease management, yet how patients are allocated to these modalities in routine practice remains poorly understood.

AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To characterize baseline factors associated with physician-driven allocation to hybrid versus in-person care and examine three-year clinical outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort included adults with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and/or dyslipidemia enrolled in a programme in Alma Mater Hospital of Antioquia, Medellín, Colombia (2019-2025). Care modality was determined by treating physicians. Associations between baseline clinical, functional-behavioural, and psychosocial characteristics, care allocation, and follow-up outcomes were examined using logistic regression and interpreted as associational rather than causal.

RESULTS: Among 638 participants (319 hybrid; 319 in-person), higher baseline glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.68 per 1% increase; 95% CI 2.17-3.31) and inadequate medication adherence (aOR 1.96; 95% CI 1.17-3.28) were associated with hybrid care allocation, whereas higher educational attainment was inversely associated (middle vs low: aOR 0.43; 95% CI 0.25-0.72; high vs low: aOR 0.19; 95% CI 0.10-0.33). A strong gradient was observed in the secondary complexity analysis. Hybrid care was associated with higher three-year therapeutic goal attainment (OR 7.34; 95% CI 4.96-10.86) and lower chronic disease-related emergency department utilization (OR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.79).

CONCLUSION: Hybrid care allocation was systematically associated with baseline clinical and contextual characteristics. Outcome differences should be interpreted cautiously given clinician-driven allocation and baseline differences.

articles.title: The secretory life of pets: bites from western hognose snakes reported to the California Poison Control System.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The western hognose snake (Heterodon nasicus) is a popular pet reptile. While sometimes classified as nonvenomous, it produces mildly toxic saliva from a low-pressure secretory organ in the temporal region (Duvernoy's gland), causing local reactions following snakebites. We aim to review cases from a statewide poison control system to characterize clinical effects and outcomes.

METHODS: This is a 10-year retrospective review of calls about western hognose snakebite to the California Poison Control System, using product-substance codes and a free-text keyword search. Demographic, clinical, and bite-circumstance data were summarized and analyzed.

RESULTS: There were 35 cases from January 2016 to March 2026, ranging from 11 to 82 years (median 22; IQR 18-29 years), of whom 69% were female and 46% were aged 21 years or younger. A large majority (89%) were bitten by their own pets; one bite occurred at a reptile exposition. All bites affected the hands, typically during feeding, handling, or enclosure cleaning. Local swelling occurred in 91% of cases, with extension to the wrist or forearm in 43%. Skin changes (ecchymosis, erythema or blistering) were noted in 26%, and 6% developed nausea and vomiting. Vital signs and labs, checked in 23% and 11% of cases respectively, were unremarkable. Management typically included wound care, tetanus vaccination update, and anticipatory guidance for infectious complications. Two patients required hospitalization for two or more days for treatment of presumed cellulitis. In one case with extensive edema, rattlesnake antivenom was administered due to doubts about the reported bite history; in the second case, antivenom was recommended for similar reasons, but withheld after photographic identification confirmed the pet snake.

DISCUSSION: The western hognose snakebite can cause cytotoxic edema, and prolonged bites may pose a higher risk of severe injury. Clinical care should focus on pain control, wound care, and anticipatory guidance for post-bite infection and hypersensitivity reactions due to the components of snake saliva, which may require specific treatment with antibiotics or anti-inflammatory medications. Rattlesnake antivenom has no role in managing this type of snakebite.

CONCLUSION: Western hognose envenomation can lead to mild to moderate soft tissue injuries, which require supportive and symptomatic care and, rarely, hospital admission. Many bites occurred in pet owner adolescents, who may benefit from preventive safety education.

articles.title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in the Middle East and North Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region are limited. We synthesized available evidence on post-TAVR clinical outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through May 2025 for studies reporting TAVR outcomes in this region. Outcomes included device success, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, new-onset atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe paravalvular leak, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Overall incidence rates were pooled via Poisson analysis and reported per 100 person-years with 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Forty-eight studies encompassing 7331 patients (mean age, 76.9±8.5 years; 52.4% women) were included. Pooled device success rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.0%). At latest follow-up, pooled incidence rates per 100 person-years were 13.7 for all-cause death (95% CI, 12.9-14.6), 4.8 for cardiovascular death (95% CI, 4.1-5.7), 1.0 for myocardial infarction (95% CI, 0.7-1.4), 1.6 for stroke (95% CI, 1.3-1.9), 2.7 for moderate to severe paravalvular leak (95% CI, 2.2-3.4), 6.5 for new-onset atrial fibrillation (95% CI, 5.5-7.7), and 10.0 for permanent pacemaker implantation (95% CI, 9.2-10.9). Post hoc exploratory meta-regression identified significant study-level modifying effects, with higher mean age and greater use of first-generation versus second-generation valves associated with higher overall all-cause mortality incidence following TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: TAVR in the Middle East and North Africa region was associated with high device success rate and relatively low cardiovascular death. Permanent pacemaker implantation was the most prevalent post-TAVR complication. Further studies are warranted to optimize TAVR practice in this region.

articles.title: Modulating Electronic Structure and Morphology in Nb-NiCoS for PET Plastic Upcycling.
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic polyethylene terephthalate (PET) upcycling coupled with green hydrogen production offers an energy-efficient route for plastic waste valorization. Herein, Nb-incorporated NiCoS electrocatalysts are synthesized on nickel foam via a one-step chemical bath deposition route for PET electro-upcycling. Nb incorporation modulates the electronic structure and morphology of NiCoS, producing defect-rich vertically interconnected nanosheets with abundant electrochemically dynamic Ni3+/Co3+ active sites. The optimized electronic structure promotes reconstruction into active NiOOH/CoOOH species, resulting in enhanced performance toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), oxygen evolution reaction (OER), ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), and PET hydrolysate oxidation reaction (POR). Nb-NiCoS requires 1.32 and 1.34 V vs RHE to achieve 100 mA cm-2 for EGOR and POR, respectively, significantly lower than OER (1.52 V vs RHE). Mechanistic analysis reveals an indirect oxy-hydroxide-mediated oxidation pathway, enabling selective conversion of PET-derived EG into formic acid with a Faradaic efficiency of 93.3% (with ~100% selectivity) and a production rate of 1.16 mmol h-1 cm-2 at 100 mA cm-2. Coupling PET electro-upcycling with hydrogen production reduces the energy consumption to 3.52 kWh Nm-3 from 4.49 kWh Nm-3 for conventional water electrolysis, enabling energy saving of 21.3%, highlighting a scalable strategy for simultaneous plastic waste valorization and hydrogen production.

articles.title: Management of complex combat-related pelvic organ injuries: Case series and review of complications.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ injuries in combat conditions are relatively uncommon but are associated with a high risk of complications, particularly urinary injuries combined with pelvic fractures, vascular trauma, and other abdominal injuries in the setting of polytrauma. The provision of effective medical care in modern conflicts is complicated by logistical constraints, including delayed evacuation, limited imaging capabilities, and shortages of specialized personnel. This study analyzes diagnosis, treatment, and complications of combat-related urinary injuries and identifies approaches to optimize medical care. A series of clinical cases was reviewed, including five patients treated at various stages of medical evacuation. Diagnostic strategies, surgical tactics, complications, and outcomes were evaluated. Challenges included delayed diagnosis, underestimation of injury severity, unjustified conservative management of intraperitoneal ruptures, technical shortcomings in bladder repair, and insufficient interdisciplinary coordination. Complications such as urinary extravasation, peritonitis, infection, and secondary fistula formation were observed. Favorable outcomes were associated with timely injury recognition, urgent surgical intervention, continuity of staged evacuation, and early involvement of urological expertise. Optimization of diagnostic and treatment pathways and strengthening multidisciplinary collaboration are essential to reduce morbidity in combat-related pelvic organ injury trauma.

articles.title: Association of APOA5 rs3135506 and CETP rs708272 Polymorphisms with Metabolic Syndrome in a Moroccan Population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a multifactorial condition and a major public health concern due to its strong association with cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Genetic factors contribute to its development. This study aims to evaluate the association between polymorphisms in genes APOA5 and CETP and susceptibility to MetS and its components in a Moroccan population.

METHODS: A case-control study was conducted, including 136 MetS patients and 138 controls recruited from the Doukkala region (Morocco). The APOA5 rs3135506 (C>G) and CETP rs708272 (G>A) polymorphisms were genotyped using PCR-RFLP.

RESULTS: The APOA5 rs3135506 polymorphism was significantly associated with increased MetS risk. The CG and GG genotypes conferred 2.39-fold (OR = 2.39; p = 0.0008) and 7.17-fold (OR = 7.17; p = 0.0007) higher risks, respectively, with significant associations also observed under dominant (OR = 2.76; p < 0.0001), recessive (OR = 4.79; p = 0.006), and allelic (OR = 2.36; p < 0.0001) models. The GG genotype was also associated with general and abdominal obesity, hypertension, and hyperglycemia, whereas the CG genotype was associated with dyslipidemia. For CETP rs708272, the AA genotype was associated with increased MetS risk (OR = 3.31; p = 0.0078), with significant associations under dominant (OR = 1.81; p = 0.0160), recessive (OR = 2.80; p = 0.0185), and allelic (OR = 1.81; p = 0.0023) models. However, these associations were no longer significant after adjustment for age and sex. Combined genotype analysis revealed increased MetS risk for the CG-GG, CG-GA, and GG-AA combinations (OR = 4.64, 2.98, and 7.35, respectively).

CONCLUSION: The APOA5 rs3135506 and CETP rs708272 polymorphisms may contribute to MetS susceptibility in the Moroccan population, with certain combined genotypes associated with increased risk. These findings support their potential as genetic biomarkers for early risk assessment but require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: From metabolic therapy to addiction care: a clinical pharmacology roadmap for GLP-1 receptor agonists in substance use disorders.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), established treatments for type 2 diabetes and obesity, are being investigated for substance use disorders (SUDs). Randomized evidence is emerging in alcohol use disorder (AUD), while evidence for opioid, nicotine, cocaine, cannabis, and stimulant use disorders remains mixed, observational, or investigational.

AREAS COVERED: This targeted narrative review integrates PubMed/MEDLINE literature, US Food and Drug Administration guidance and labeling, and ClinicalTrials.gov records available through 15 July 2026, with targeted literature and registry updates through 20 October 2026. It evaluates mechanistic plausibility, randomized and real-world human evidence, agent- and dose-specific pharmacology, co-treatment with established SUD medications, safety, adherence, benefit-risk assessment, harm reduction, equity, and trial design.

EXPERT OPINION: The evidence is sufficient to justify indication-specific clinical development, especially for AUD, but currently insufficient for routine off-label treatment of SUDs for patients without an approved metabolic indication. Near-term research should test GLP-1 RAs as adjuncts rather than replacements for established SUD care, distinguish direct reward effects from weight loss and adverse-effect pathways, and embed risk minimization, patient-important outcomes, and equitable access into development from the outset.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Determinants of Bowel Ischemia and Associated Risk After Elective Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bowel ischemia (BI) is an uncommon but devastating complication of elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify patient- and procedure-related risk factors for BI after elective EVAR.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Cochrane Library, Scielo, and Lilacs from database inception through March 31, 2024, without language or date restrictions. We included observational studies of adults who underwent elective EVAR and reported postoperative BI and extractable risk-factor data. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, extracted data, and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For factors reported in multiple sufficiently homogeneous studies, random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs), with heterogeneity assessed using I2.

RESULTS: Twenty-three retrospective cohort studies, including 306 344 elective EVAR procedures, met the inclusion criteria, and 10 provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. Across all studies, 1535 patients developed postoperative BI, corresponding to an overall incidence of approximately 0.5%. Female sex was associated with increased BI risk (RR, 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.06-3.43; I2 = 0%). Larger aneurysm diameter was also associated with increased risk (MD, 4.05 mm; 95% CI, 0.09-8.02; I2 = 0%). Renal dysfunction was a consistent predictor, with chronic kidney disease (RR, 2.93; 95% CI, 1.01-8.47; I2 = 29%) and dialysis dependence (RR, 5.35; 95% CI, 2.38-12.05; I2 = 0%) associated with BI. Major intraoperative blood loss >1 L conferred the highest relative risk among pooled factors (RR, 7.45; 95% CI, 2.80-19.85; I2 = 0%). Age, systemic arterial hypertension, and active smoking were not significantly associated with BI in pooled analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Bowel ischemia after elective EVAR is uncommon but clinically important because delayed recognition carries substantial morbidity and mortality. Female sex, larger aneurysm diameter, chronic kidney disease, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss identify patients who may warrant heightened perioperative vigilance. The certainty of evidence remains very low, and future studies should standardize reporting of bowel segment, mesenteric vessel involvement, inferior mesenteric artery and internal iliac artery status, endograft configuration, and overlapping registry populations.Clinical RelevanceBowel ischemia after elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare, but its low incidence should not be interpreted as low clinical importance because delayed diagnosis is often catastrophic. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes the largest available elective EVAR evidence focused on bowel ischemia and identifies reproducible risk signals, including female sex, aneurysm size, renal dysfunction, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss. The practical gain for readers is not a definitive prediction score, but a clearer framework for perioperative judgment: recognize vulnerable patients, avoid overinterpreting weak or non-poolable associations, and apply heightened postoperative vigilance when embolic, hypoperfusion, pelvic collateral, or renal-risk features coexist.

articles.title: Non-Classical Apparent Mineralocorticoid Excess Syndrome: Current Evidence and Future Challenges.
articles.abstract: Hypertension affects over 1.3 billion people worldwide and is the leading modifiable cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Approximately one-third of individuals with hypertension exhibit a low-renin phenotype, a clinically heterogeneous subgroup in whom the underlying etiology remains uncharacterized in most cases. Among its mechanistic contributors, non-classical apparent mineralocorticoid excess (NC-AME), defined by partial insufficiency of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2), represents a prevalent and underrecognized cause of cortisol-mediated mineralocorticoid receptor overactivation that has, to date, lacked a formal clinical definition, standardized diagnostic criteria, or evidence-based therapeutic framework. This Scientific Statement addresses that gap. The panel formally defines NC-AME as a syndrome of partial 11β-HSD2 insufficiency occurring in the absence of biallelic HSD11B2 variants, biochemically characterized by an elevated cortisol-to-cortisone (F/E) ratio and low cortisone concentration, and typically associated with low plasma renin, normal-to-low aldosterone, and elevated blood pressure. The Statement consolidates evidence across three mechanistic domains, genetic and epigenetic dysregulation of HSD11B2, endogenous and exogenous enzyme inhibition, and patient-specific alterations (i.e. age, sex, renal function), and proposes both a structured, an LC-MS/MS-based diagnostic algorithm, and a resource-adapted diagnostic approach. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists are endorsed as mechanism-directed first-line therapy, with blood pressure and renin normalization as co-primary treatment targets. Acquired and reversible causes are classified separately to guide clinical management. A research agenda is advanced to drive threshold standardization, multicenter validation, and integration of NC-AME into hypertension guidelines across endocrinology, cardiology, and nephrology.

articles.title: A Potent Antifouling and Antimicrobial Wound Dressing to Accelerate Diabetic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are a severe and prevalent complication of diabetes, often resulting in high healthcare costs and an increased risk of amputation. Infection and insufficient angiogenesis are two primary factors that severely impede diabetic wound healing. In this study, we developed a potent antifouling and antimicrobial SBHA hydrogel incorporating zwitterionic and N-halamine moieties. The zwitterionic moieties effectively resist protein adsorption and bacterial adhesion while simultaneously promoting angiogenesis, thereby accelerating wound repair. Meanwhile, the N-halamine moieties exhibit excellent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, achieving a bactericidal efficacy of 99.999% within 5 min of contact. Importantly, in vivo studies demonstrate that SBHA hydrogels used as wound dressings significantly accelerate the healing of diabetic infected wounds in rats, reaching a healing rate of up to 93.3% on day 13 compared with the control group. This enhanced therapeutic outcome may be attributed to the ability of the SBHA dressing to prevent infection, promote angiogenesis, modulate macrophage polarization, upregulate the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, and suppress the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of SBHA hydrogels as advanced wound dressings and provide a promising strategy for diabetic wound healing.

articles.title: The cardiometabolic health effects of the hard cheese matrix.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in food science and nutrition
articles.abstract: Total dairy intake is often associated with positive health outcomes, including reduced incidences of cardio metabolic disease. Dairy foods are diverse in their nutrient composition and structure, or "matrix", and less is known about the bioactive effects of individual dairy foods and their influences on human health. Cheese has a complex matrix that contains beneficial dairy proteins, bacteria, and micronutrients but also contains saturated fats and sodium, nutrients generally associated with unfavorable effects on cardiometabolic disease risk. The nutrient composition of cheese raises unique questions about the impact of cheese consumption on human health outcomes. The current literature suggests that cheese consumption as a whole food has positive or neutral effects on several cardiometabolic outcomes, likely driven by bioactive proteins, fats, micronutrients, and bacteria in the cheese matrix, and, interestingly, appears to be protective against the negative effects of sodium and saturated fats that are otherwise observed when consumed in nondairy products. However, further studies are needed to identify the specific components, structural characteristics, and molecular interactions in cheese that confer these health effects. This review discusses what is currently understood about the influence of the cheese matrix on human health, particularly cardiometabolic health, and the potential mechanisms mediating these effects.

articles.title: Factors Affecting Tacrolimus Levels in Pediatric Liver Transplant Recipients During the Early Posttransplant Period.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tacrolimus is the cornerstone of immunosuppression in pediatric liver transplantation (LT) but exhibits high pharmacokinetic variability.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory determinants of tacrolimus trough levels (C0) during the initial 14 days posttransplant.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed pediatric LT recipients (January 2020-October 2025). We evaluated continuous variables for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk test and analyzed them with nonparametric bivariate tests, including Spearman's rank correlation and Mann-Whitney U tests. To account for repeated measurements within individual patients, we fitted a linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept. Backward elimination with a conservative threshold of p > 0.50 was applied to remove nonsignificant variables, while retaining predefined clinical covariates. Model fit was evaluated using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), and the final parsimonious model was selected by minimizing BIC while excluding individual antimicrobial treatments to prevent overfitting. To quantify complex polypharmacy and avoid overfitting, we created a Pharmacological Interaction Score (PIS) by assigning weighted positive or negative values to co-administered medications based on their known CYP3A4/5 inhibitory or inducing effects on tacrolimus.

RESULTS: In 33 patients, hemoglobin (β = 0.78, P < .001) and serum creatinine (β = 3.41, P < .001) were positively associated with tacrolimus levels, while INR showed a negative association (β = -1.00, P = .036). The model included albumin, a pharmacologic interaction score designed to simplify complex polypharmacy into a single numerical value, as well as platelet counts, which were retained but not statistically significant. Tacrolimus levels were not significantly influenced by sepsis, nutrition (enteral/parenteral), or extracorporeal therapies.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort, clinical complications such as sepsis, nutritional support methods, and extracorporeal therapies did not significantly affect drug trough levels. These results suggest that early postoperative fluctuations in whole-blood tacrolimus levels are mainly driven by patient hematological status, renal function, and graft recovery. Clinically, including hematological and biochemical parameters in routine drug monitoring could improve dose management and help prevent unnecessary empirical changes during critical care.

articles.title: Caregiver burden, depression, and anxiety among relatives of patients undergoing hemodialysis in a tertiary care center in South India.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects an estimated 115 million individuals in India, many of whom rely on unpaid caregivers who are often physically overwhelmed and emotionally unsupported. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and severity of caregiver burden, depression, and anxiety among relatives of patients undergoing hemodialysis. A cross-sectional study was conducted at a tertiary care center over a six-month period, involving 100 caregivers. Caregiver burden was assessed using the Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI-12), depression using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), and anxiety using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7). Among caregivers, 70% experienced moderate to high burden, while 57% had depressive symptoms and 57% had anxiety symptoms. Burden correlated positively with depression (ρ = 0.62) and anxiety (ρ = 0.59). Caregivers without social support had higher burden scores (p = .009). These findings highlight the need for caregiver-centered mental health screening and psychosocial interventions in chronic illness management.

articles.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
authors: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)
European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)
Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL)
Latin American Association for the Study of the Liver (ALEH)
Society on Liver Disease in Africa (SOLDA)
articles.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

articles.title: Outcomes of a Culturally Adapted Family Model of Diabetes Education and Support for Marshallese Persons With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study is to evaluate a culturally adapted family model of a diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) intervention (Family-DSMES) called Ājjmuurur Baamḷe DSMES among Marshallese persons living in the United States.

METHODS: Marshallese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (PWDs) in Washington state and Hawai'i were enrolled in the Ājjmuurur Baamḷe DSMES intervention, which was delivered by community health workers in faith-based organizations (churches). Changes in A1C, self-reported diabetes-related knowledge and behaviors, and family support for management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were measured at baseline and postintervention.

RESULTS: A total of 337 participants were consented or assented and enrolled (164 PWDs and 173 family members). Two hundred seven (207) participants (110 PWDs and 97 family members) completed the Ājjmuurur Baamḷe DSMES and provided baseline and postintervention A1C data. PWDs saw significant reductions in their A1C and significant improvements in self-reported diabetes-related behavioral and psychosocial outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Improvements in outcome measures support the use of Ājjmuurur Baamḷe DSMES in the Marshallese PWDs community. The findings also support the feasibility of collaboration with faith-based organizations such as churches for the delivery of DSMES. It further highlights the clinical efficacy of the delivery of diabetes health education by community health workers and supports family-based DSMES as an option for achieving value-based care and improvements in primary and secondary prevention of T2DM.

articles.title: Treprostinil Inhalation Powder for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Evidence and Clinical Positioning Among Inhaled Formulations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe treprostinil inhalation powder (Yutrepia) and evaluate its role among inhaled treprostinil formulations for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through September 10, 2026 using terms related to PAH, treprostinil, inhaled treprostinil, dry powder inhalers, Tyvaso, Tyvaso dry powder inhalation (DPI), Yutrepia, and LIQ861. The search identified 258 records; reference lists and prescribing information were also reviewed.

STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Twelve original reports addressing efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, transition, or administration were included. One author performed initial screening and study selection, and a second author independently verified inclusion and exclusion decisions.

DATA SYNTHESIS: TRIUMPH I demonstrated a placebo-corrected median improvement of 20 m in peak 6MWD at week 12 with nebulized treprostinil added to oral PAH therapy. BREEZE supported transition feasibility, comparable exposure, and greater device satisfaction after transition to treprostinil DPI; INSPIRE supported Yutrepia tolerability and acceptability, but its exploratory efficacy outcomes were descriptive. No head-to-head trial has established superiority.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:Both dry powder formulations reduce nebulizer equipment burden, but current evidence does not establish greater efficacy, safety, adherence, or convenience for one dry powder product over the other. Selection should consider disease risk, device technique, tolerability, treatment burden, cost, coverage, and access.

CONCLUSIONS: Yutrepia expands inhaled prostacyclin options for PAH. Selection should be individualized, and inhaled therapy should not be considered equivalent to parenteral prostacyclin when parenteral treatment is clinically indicated.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of NTQ5082 in Complement Inhibitor-Naïve Patients With Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
articles.abstract: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) is a clonal hematologic disorder characterized by complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis, pancytopenia, and thrombosis. NTQ5082 is a novel oral selective complement factor B (CFB) inhibitor that suppresses alternative pathway activity, thereby inhibiting intravascular hemolysis in PNH. We conducted a randomized, open-label Phase 2 study to investigate NTQ5082 monotherapy in adults with PNH who had not previously received complement inhibitors. Twenty-five patients were assigned to receive oral NTQ5082 once daily (QD) at 100 mg (group A) or 200 mg (group B) for 12 weeks. In both groups, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels rapidly decreased, and hemoglobin (Hb) levels increased within 1 week after treatment initiation, with no further transfusions needed. At week 12, the mean LDH concentration was 239.4 ± 63.5 U/L in group A and 245.8 ± 72.6 U/L in group B. The Hb concentration increased to ≥ 20 g/L from baseline in 100% of patients, while 50% and 61.5% of patients in groups A and B, respectively, achieved Hb concentrations ≥ 120 g/L. The most frequently reported treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were headache (12%), upper respiratory tract infection (8%), and decreased neutrophil count (8%); no grade ≥ 3 adverse events (AEs) were reported. Oral NTQ5082 administered at 100 or 200 mg QD effectively controlled hemolysis, significantly increased Hb levels, and improved quality of life, with a satisfactory safety profile, suggesting that NTQ5082 may represent a promising therapeutic option for complement inhibitor-naïve patients with PNH.

articles.title: Exercise-only interventions for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent, and exercise is recommended as a first-line therapy. However, it remains unclear whether reductions in liver fat content are accompanied by consistent changes in other hepatic, metabolic, and anthropometric outcomes when exercise is evaluated in isolation. This review assessed the effects of different exercise modalities on these outcomes and the certainty of the evidence. Nine databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing supervised exercise interventions (aerobic, resistance training, or high-intensity interval training) versus controls in individuals with MASLD were included. Studies combining exercise with diet or pharmacotherapy were excluded. Forty-one studies (n = 1517) were included; 24 were meta-analyzed. Resistance training was associated with reductions in liver fat content compared with control (standardized mean difference = -0.77, 95% confidence interval: -1.14 to -0.39), followed by moderate-intensity aerobic exercise (standardized mean difference = -0.50, 95% confidence interval: -0.95 to -0.04). High-intensity interval training showed no clear effect. Changes in liver enzymes were inconsistent, suggesting dissociation from liver fat responses. Moderate-intensity aerobic exercise improved transaminases and triglycerides, while resistance training improved fasting glucose and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Effects on BMI, body fat, and glycated hemoglobin were negligible. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. Exercise, particularly resistance training and moderate-intensity aerobic training, reduces liver fat in MASLD without consistent changes in adiposity-related outcomes. Low certainty of evidence precludes precise exercise recommendations. Well designed randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Stress Reactivity and Dementia Risk: A Pilot Study of Older Adults With Problematic or Frequent Cannabis Use.
articles.journal: Journal of geriatric psychiatry and neurology
articles.abstract: IntroductionWe conducted a pilot study of older cannabis users with problematic or frequent (i.e. ≥4/7 days/week) use as a preliminary test of the hypothesis that compared to men, women would demonstrate greater stress reactivity and dementia risk.Methods47 participants ages 50-75 (55.3% male, 68% with cannabis use disorder) completed the Trier Social Stress Test, neuropsychological testing, 3T brain MRI, and blood draw.ResultsMen demonstrated: greater salivary cortisol, systolic blood pressure, and craving post-stress induction; worse memory and executive function; greater risk of heart disease or stroke and white matter hyperintensity volumes. There were no sex differences in Alzheimer's disease plasma biomarkers.ConclusionsAmong non-treatment-seeking older adults with problematic or frequent cannabis use, men may have greater risk for dementia due to stress reactivity and vascular risk factors. Future work must replicate and verify this unexpected sex difference and the specificity of these effects to cannabis use.

articles.title: Examining the multivariate genetic architectures of posttraumatic stress disorder and cardiovascular disease phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but the extent of shared inherited liability is unclear. Large genome-wide association studies (GWAS) allow for multivariate evaluation of common genetic architecture. We analyzed European-ancestry GWAS summary statistics for PTSD (N_eff ≈ 1.22 million), CVD outcomes (CVDoutcomes; coronary artery disease, stroke, hypertension; N_eff = 126,000-574,000), and CVD risk factors (CVDrisk; high-density lipoprotein, triglycerides, fasting glucose, waist circumference; N = 211,000-526,000). Using genomic structural equation modeling, we modeled latent genetic structure across PTSD and CVD phenotypes and conducted multivariate GWAS of latent factors with gene and gene-set annotation. A three-factor model distinguishing PTSD, CVDrisk, and CVDoutcomes best fit the data, χ2 = 256.9, CFI = .990, SRMR = .040. PTSD showed a moderate genetic correlation with CVDrisk, rg = .340, p < .001, and a significant but negligible genetic correlation with CVDoutcomes, rg = 0.030, p < .001, suggesting minimal shared genetic liability at the latent-factor level. Multivariate GWAS identified seven loci for PTSD, 96 for CVDrisk, and 51 for CVDoutcomes. Gene-based tests implicated 85, 910, and 390 genes, respectively, with 18 overlapping between PTSD and CVDrisk. Enrichment highlighted RNA metabolism for PTSD and lipid/vascular pathways for CVD traits. Additional locus-level overlaps emerged, including a genomic hub in the major histocompatibility complex region on Chromosome 6 for both phenotypes. PTSD shares moderate polygenic overlap with CVD, particularly CVDrisk, but many loci are trait-specific, implicating lipid metabolism, vascular tone, immune/inflammatory pathways, and RNA regulation as potential links.

articles.title: Letter to the editor on "Comparative risk of fibrosis progression with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 vs. dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus with low-to-intermediate fibrosis".

Clarifying response thresholds and regional reporting in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease cost-effectiveness: Letter to the Editor on "Evaluating treatment response thresholds for cost-effective treatment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease".

Correspondence to letter to the editor on "Histological severity and hepatic outcomes in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and discrepant FIB-4 and liver stiffness measurement".
Correspondence to letter to the editor on "DNMT1 facilitates the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease by impeding transcription mediated by HNF4α and PPARα".
Type 2 Diabetes and Continuous Glucose Monitoring: A Pilot Cross-Sectional Study of Medication Adherence and Self-Management Behaviors.
articles.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is associated with improved glycemic outcomes, largely in insulin-treated populations, potentially through enhanced engagement and self-management. Its relationship with adherence to oral diabetes medications remains unclear. This study aimed to assess medication adherence among CGM users prescribed oral diabetes medications and explore perceived behavioral changes associated with CGM use. A cross-sectional pilot survey was conducted among adults with type 2 diabetes using CGM and at least one oral diabetes medication, recruited from a community pharmacy. Concurrent insulin use was not exclusionary and was not recorded. Adherence was measured using the 9-item Hill-Bone Medication Adherence Scale (HB-MAS). Quantitative data were summarized descriptively, and qualitative responses underwent thematic analysis. Twenty-nine participants completed the survey (mean age 54.7, SD 12.9 years; 59% female). CGM use was well established (62% ≥ 12 months; 90% checked glucose multiple times daily). Self-reported adherence was high (mean HB-MAS 34.1 ± 2.2; median 35), with 72% classified as excellent (≥33). No differences were observed across age groups (P = .46). Most participants reported CGM improved medication consistency (72%) and dietary choices (69%), with smaller effects on physical activity (31%). Themes included convenience, real-time feedback, and reduced finger sticks. Among established CGM users, self-reported adherence was high and perceived to improve with CGM use, suggesting CGM feedback may support medication-taking behaviors. Because concurrent insulin use was not recorded, findings may not generalize to individuals treated with oral agents alone. Further study using objective adherence measures and longitudinal designs is warranted.

articles.title: The Association of Amyloid-β and Tau With Synaptic Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clarify the relative contributions of amyloid and tau to synaptic dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD).

METHODS: We included 109 cognitively unimpaired and impaired individuals from the Geneva Memory Center with available CSF synaptic biomarkers (neurogranin, SNAP-25, GAP-43). Participants were stratified according to amyloid (A) and tau (T) status, and group comparisons and correlations between synaptic and AD biomarkers were assessed. Multiple linear regression models evaluated the independent associations of amyloid and tau with synaptic markers: Model I (n = 109) included CSF Aβ42 and p-tau181, while Model II (n = 69) included amyloid PET centiloid and CSF p-tau181. Mediation analyses were performed to further investigate these relationships. Findings were replicated in the ADNI cohort (n = 787).

RESULTS: Synaptic biomarker levels were significantly higher in A+/T+ individuals compared with A-/T- and A+/T- groups (p < 0.001). CSF p-tau181 strongly correlated with synaptic markers. In Model I, GAP43 was positively associated with both CSF Aβ42 (β = 0.31, 95% CI 0.23-0.40) and p-tau181 (β = 0.94, 95% CI 0.84-1.04; p < 0.001). In Model II, lower amyloid PET centiloid (β = -0.31, 95% CI -0.46 to -0.16) and higher p-tau181 (β = 1.02, 95% CI 0.86-1.19) predicted increased GAP43 (p < 0.001), with the same pattern of associations observed for neurogranin and SNAP-25. The association between amyloid burden and synaptic biomarkers was largely indirect, statistically mediated by CSF p-tau181. Results were replicated in ADNI.

INTERPRETATION: Tau pathology showed strong associations with synaptic biomarkers, with a potential mediating role in the association between amyloid pathology and synaptic dysfunction. These findings support a central role of tau-related processes in synaptic dysfunction in AD.

articles.title: Motor memory consolidation during sleep after stroke: the rehabilitation timing hypothesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motor recovery after stroke depends on neuroplasticity-driven reorganisation of surviving cortical circuits. A growing body of evidence implicates sleep as an active consolidator of motor memories acquired during rehabilitation. Yet stroke disrupts the very sleep architecture required for this process, and current clinical practice schedules rehabilitation without regard for its temporal proximity to sleep.

OBJECTIVE: This review synthesizes the mechanistic, preclinical, and emerging clinical evidence underlying the rehabilitation timing hypothesis.

RESULTS: Sleep spindles, nested within slow oscillations during NREM sleep, are a principal electrophysiological substrate for motor memory consolidation, and emerging evidence implicates cerebellar-cortical dynamics during spindles. Stroke disrupts this oscillatory coupling through lesion-related alterations in thalamocortical circuitry, GABAergic signalling, and interhemispheric synchrony. Preclinical studies demonstrate that optogenetically-enhanced slow waves during sleep accelerate motor recovery, while pharmacological GABA modulation restores consolidation-promoting oscillations. Chronobiological evidence from healthy adults and older populations suggests that evening training followed by nocturnal sleep may produce superior long-term motor retention compared with morning training.

CONCLUSION: The rehabilitation timing hypothesis is plausible and clinically testable, but direct evidence in stroke populations is currently lacking. Scheduling motor therapy close to sleep is a low-cost strategy that warrants formal evaluation as a means of enhancing stroke recovery. Formal clinical trials testing therapy timing as an independent variable are urgently needed.

articles.title: Wearable Microfluidic Electrochemical Platform Based on One-Pot Prussian Blue-Embedded Molecularly Imprinted Polymers for Simultaneous Detection of Sweat Uric Acid and Urea.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive wearable sensing of sweat uric acid (UA) and urea provides a promising strategy for early chronic kidney disease screening. Nevertheless, most electrochemical sensors for UA and urea detection suffer from insufficient anti-interference and require exogenous redox probes, restricting reagent-free on-body measurement. Herein, we develop a wearable microfluidic electrochemical platform based on Prussian blue-embedded molecularly imprinted polymer (PB-MIP) composite materials for reagent-free, enzyme-free dual-biomarker quantification. Urea-specific and UA-specific PB-MIP composites are prepared via a facile one-step ultraviolet polymerization strategy. PB uniformly embedded within the imprinted framework acts as an intrinsic solid-state redox mediator, integrating specific molecular recognition and built-in electrochemical signal transduction into a single functional material. The two PB-MIP composites are drop-coated on dual working electrodes of a screen-printed carbon electrode, coupled with a capillary-driven microfluidic chip to construct a wearable electrochemical platform. Benefiting from the microfluidic design, the system enables pump-free spontaneous collection of trace sweat samples and achieves simultaneous quantification of sweat UA and urea. The platform exhibits wide linear ranges (0.1-600 μM for uric acid, 0.1-300 mM for urea), low limits of detection, excellent anti-interference capacity, recyclability, and favorable storage stability. On-body dietary intervention tests capture clear postprandial biomarker fluctuations, and detection results show good agreement with HPLC-MS reference values. This work offers a straightforward material-engineering strategy to develop probe-free MIP sensing interfaces and integrated wearable microfluidic devices, showing promising prospects for noninvasive preliminary screening of kidney function.

articles.title: Plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain measured by Simoa and Lumipulse: an inter-platform comparison across neurological disorders.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an accessible biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but clinical implementation requires robust analytical comparability across platforms. We evaluated plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse across neurological disorders, including paired CSF analyses to anchor plasma findings to the central compartment.

METHODS: We included 383 individuals, comprising healthy controls and patients with neurodegenerative diseases, multiple sclerosis, and ischemic stroke. Plasma NfL was measured in all participants using Simoa and Lumipulse; paired CSF measurements were available in 92 individuals. Lumipulse intermediate precision and between-day repeatability were assessed according to CLSI EP15. Cross-platform agreement was evaluated using Spearman correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, and Bland-Altman analysis. Plasma-CSF associations and age-adjusted diagnostic differences were assessed separately for each platform.

RESULTS: Plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse showed strong concordance in the whole cohort (ρ=0.90), with similarly strong CSF concordance in paired samples (ρ=0.90). Method-comparison analyses demonstrated constant and proportional bias, with systematically higher absolute plasma NfL values measured by Lumipulse. Plasma and CSF NfL were significantly correlated within each platform (ρ=0.72 for Simoa; ρ=0.77 for Lumipulse). Lumipulse blood and CSF assays showed high precision. Across both platforms, plasma NfL increased with age and was higher in neurological disorders than in healthy controls.

CONCLUSIONS: Simoa and Lumipulse capture a consistent plasma NfL signal across neurological disorders, but absolute concentrations differ, supporting platform-specific, age-aware interpretation in clinical practice.

articles.title: Motor Cortex Disinhibition Is Dissociated from Clinical Motor Features in Parkinson's Disease: Longitudinal Evidence.
articles.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Parkinson's disease, motor dysfunction largely reflects dopamine-dependent pathophysiological alterations and compensatory mechanisms that progress over time and are partially reversible with dopaminergic treatment. Our recent cross-sectional observations suggest that disinhibition of the primary motor cortex-assessed with short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) using transcranial magnetic stimulation-does not correlate with clinical motor features, does not progress across disease stages, and instead correlates with olfactory dysfunction, a common prodromal and dopamine-independent feature.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to provide longitudinal evidence for or against the hypothesis that motor cortex disinhibition is dissociated from clinical motor features in Parkinson's disease.

METHODS: We compared SICI across three cohorts (total n = 95 patients): (1) baseline and 2-year follow-up (n = 43), with concurrent motor assessment and 18F-DOPA positron emission tomography (PET) imaging (n = 24); (2) before and after levodopa administration (n = 30); and (3) before and after focused ultrasound subthalamotomy (n = 22). We also included a pooled healthy control group (n = 75) from two previously published studies. Bayesian statistics was applied to formally assess evidence for the presence or the absence of an effect.

RESULTS: SICI was expectedly reduced, with very strong to extreme Bayesian evidence, in patients compared with control subjects. We found evidence that cortical disinhibition did not worsen with clinically evident disease progression confirmed with 18F-DOPA PET and did not improve following a clinically effective dose of levodopa or subthalamotomy. Moreover, changes in SICI did not correlate with changes in motor features across cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide longitudinal evidence that motor cortex disinhibition is largely dissociated from clinical motor features in Parkinson's disease. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

articles.title: Percutaneous Removal of Cement Extending to the Right Atrium and Causing Pulmonary Embolism After Percutaneous Vertebroplasty: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Percutaneous vertebroplasty is a minimally invasive procedure injecting polymethylmethacrylate cement to increase vertebral stability in vertebral compression fractures. We present a patient who presented with recurrent pulmonary embolism due to intracardiac cement embolism after vertebroplasty with successful percutaneous cement removal. A 72-year-old woman presented with chest pain, dyspnea, hypotension, and atrial fibrillation 1 month after vertebroplasty. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a freely mobile hyperechoic linear structure in the right atrium; estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure was 45 mmHg. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a cement cast extending from L2 vertebra through the inferior vena cava into the right atrium and cement emboli in distal pulmonary arterial branches. Intracardiac cement was successfully removed using a three-lobed snare with balloon assist. Intracardiac cement embolism is a rare, potentially life-threatening complication following vertebroplasty. Percutaneous removal may be considered a safe and effective alternative to open surgery in selected patients.

articles.title: Glycemic And Patient-Reported Outcomes After Transition To Advanced Hybrid Closed-Loop System In Patients After Total Pancreatectomy.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate glycemic and patient-reported outcomes associated with transition from multiple daily injections (MDI) to Advanced Hybrid Closed-Loop (AHCL) therapy in adults with diabetes shortly after total pancreatectomy (TP).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this single-center prospective observational study, 15 adults with diabetes after TP transitioned from MDI to AHCL therapy. The prespecified primary outcome was time in range (TIR; 70-180 mg/dL) during the first month of AHCL compared with the last month of MDI. Secondary outcomes included other continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics, hypoglycemic events, and patient-reported outcomes; CGM outcomes were followed for 6 months. An exploratory comparison was also performed with 28 patients who remained on MDI.

RESULTS: Median TIR increased from 53.9% to 72.0% (P < 0.01). TAR, mean glucose, GRI, and coefficient of variation also decreased (all P < 0.05), and CGM outcomes remained broadly stable throughout the 6-month follow-up. TBR and hypoglycemic-event frequency did not differ significantly. Median hypoglycemic-event duration decreased from 55.2 to 35.0 minutes (P < 0.01). Anxiety and fear of hypoglycemia decreased while other patient reported outcomes did not change significantly. In an exploratory comparison, AHCL recipients had higher TIR and lower GRI than 28 patients who remained on MDI.

CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, transition to AHCL was associated with improved TIR and favourable changes in CGM-derived glycemic outcomes, without a significant increase in TBR. These exploratory findings suggest that AHCL may be a feasible therapeutic option for selected adults with diabetes after TP. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm its clinical benefits and long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Endothelial Cell-Expressed Prion Protein Prnd/Doppel Promotes Long-Term Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recovery after ischemic stroke is limited by persistent cerebrovascular dysfunction, but the mechanisms regulating vascular repair remain poorly understood. Prnd (Prnd/Doppel) is a prion family protein expressed in the cerebrovascular endothelium during development. We tested the hypothesis that endothelial Prnd promotes vascular repair and functional recovery in the adult brain after stroke.

METHODS: Using middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice, we compared wild-type and Prnd-null mice and evaluated endothelial-specific Prnd overexpression. Functional recovery was assessed by behavioral testing, while infarct volume, brain atrophy, vascular architecture, blood-brain barrier integrity, and macrophage/microglia infiltration were evaluated histologically. Vascular signaling and endothelial cell junctional proteins were examined mechanistically.

RESULTS: Acute infarct volumes were comparable between wild-type and Prnd-null mice, indicating that Prnd does not substantially affect initial ischemic injury. During recovery, however, Prnd-null mice exhibited disrupted cerebrovascular architecture, increased blood-brain barrier disruption, greater brain atrophy, and increased macrophage/microglial infiltration. Conversely, endothelial Prnd overexpression improved long-term functional recovery without altering acute infarct size and was associated with enhanced blood-brain barrier integrity and vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, Prnd manipulation was associated with enhanced VEGF-A (vascular endothelial growth factor-A) signaling and increased endothelial cell tight junction protein expression.

CONCLUSIONS: Prnd is dispensable for acute ischemic injury but promotes cerebrovascular remodeling, blood-brain barrier restoration, and functional recovery after stroke. These findings identify endothelial Prnd as a regulator of poststroke vascular repair and a potential therapeutic target for enhancing long-term recovery.

articles.title: ABCD2 Score and 90-Day Stroke Risk After Transient Neurological Events by Diffusion-Weighted Imaging Positivity: An Analysis of Pooled Data From 3 Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ABCD2 score is widely used to stratify stroke risk after transient neurological events. We aimed to evaluate the association between the ABCD2 score and the risk of subsequent ischemic stroke among patients with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-positive (DWI+) or DWI-negative (DWI-) findings for the index event.

METHODS: We pooled individual participant data from 3 multicenter cohorts including patients presenting with transient or minor neurological events. Patients presenting with transient neurological symptoms, a normal neurological examination, and available DWI for the index event were included. Associations between the ABCD2 score and 90-day ischemic stroke risk were analyzed separately in the DWI+ and DWI- groups using logistic regression models adjusted for sex, atrial fibrillation, and study source.

RESULTS: Among 2014 patients (1143 [56.8%] men; median age 67 years), the median ABCD2 score was 4 (interquartile range, 3-5), and 504 (25.0%) were DWI+. Ischemic stroke occurred within 90 days in 20 patients (4.0%) in the DWI+ group and 33 (2.2%) in the DWI- group. The ABCD2 score was associated with stroke risk in the DWI- group (per 1-point increase, odds ratio, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.79]), but this relationship was not significant in the DWI+ group (per 1-point increase, odds ratio, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.76-1.53]). When stratified ABCD2 score into 0 to 3, 4 to 5, and 6 to 7, the predicted 90-day stroke risks were 3.2%, 3.9%, and 4.5% in the DWI+ group (per 1-category increase, odds ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 0.63-2.40]) and 1.0%, 2.3%, and 4.1% in the DWI- group (per 1-category increase, odds ratio, 1.88 [95% CI, 1.11-3.20]), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The ABCD2 score was associated with 90-day stroke risk among patients with DWI- findings. Patients with both a low ABCD2 score and DWI- findings had a particularly low risk of subsequent stroke, which may inform risk stratification and clinical decision-making after transient neurological events.

articles.title: IVUS-Guided Dobutamine Challenge to Guide Anomalous RCA PCI: An Interesting Case Report.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Congenital coronary artery anomalies are quite uncommon-they are observed in 1.3% of the coronary angiograms. Although most of them are benign, some coronary anomalies are associated with poor clinical outcomes. The exact mechanism of these outcomes in patients with anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with interarterial course is hypothesized to be either compression of the coronary artery during its course between the aorta and the pulmonary artery, or obstruction of the coronary flow during exercise due to the acute angulation of the RCA ostium. We present the case of a 54 y/o patient with NSTEMI, who, after a diagnostic coronary angiogram and coronary CT, was found to have complex coronary artery disease, including an anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with "malignant" interarterial course. In order to determine the optimal treatment, we proceeded with IVUS assessment of the ostial and proximal RCA with dobutamine challenge, which showed significant stenosis of both the RCA ostium and the interarterial segment at the peak dose of the dobutamine challenge. As a result a decision was made to treat both the RCA ostium and its interarterial segment with PCI, producing an excellent final result. Our case underscores the importance of the combination of IVUS and dobutamine challenge in order to answer the ever-important pathophysiologic mechanism of a lesion and accordingly provide tailor-made treatment for anomalous coronary arteries.

articles.title: CMR Characterization of Hypertrophic Heart Diseases.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic heart disease comprises a heterogeneous group of myocardial disorders characterized by increased left ventricular wall thickness arising from diverse pathologic processes. Despite differing etiologies, these diseases frequently demonstrate overlapping phenotypic features, which can create significant diagnostic challenges. Accurate differentiation is clinically important, given the prognostic implications associated with each condition, and the application of disease-specific therapeutic strategies. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) has become central to the evaluation of hypertrophic heart disease due to its high spatial resolution and unique capability for comprehensive multiparametric tissue characterization. Beyond standardized assessment of ventricular volumes, function, mass, and wall thickness, CMR provides detailed characterization of myocardial fibrosis, edema, and tissue composition through late gadolinium enhancement imaging and parametric mapping techniques, including native T1, T2, and extracellular volume mapping. This review summarizes the contemporary role of CMR in the assessment of hypertrophic heart diseases, with emphasis on imaging features that aid differential diagnosis, and clinically relevant findings that influence management and prognosis.

articles.title: Polyphyllin I Alleviates Alcoholic Liver Disease via Modulation of the Phosphodiesterase 6D-Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Protein Kinase G Axis.
articles.abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a multifaceted disorder in which oxidative injury, iron-dependent ferroptosis, steatosis, and inflammation are closely intertwined. Consequently, therapeutic strategies targeting a single pathway often produce limited clinical benefits. In this study, we identified polyphyllin I (PPI), a bioactive constituent isolated from Paris polyphylla, as a potent hepatoprotective agent that concurrently ameliorates these pathological phenotypes in ethanol-exposed hepatocytes and a murine ALD model. Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) confirmed cellular engagement between PPI and PDE6D. Mechanistically, PPI regulates PDE6D to elevate intracellular cGMP levels and subsequently activate PKG signaling. Genetic perturbation experiments revealed that PDE6D exacerbates ethanol-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis via cGMP downregulation, and the hepatoprotective effects of PPI could be recapitulated by the PDE6D degrader TMX-4100. Downstream of PKG activation, PPI simultaneously restores xCT/GPX4 expression, suppresses ACSL4-mediated lipid peroxidation to inhibit ferroptosis, promotes NRF2 nuclear translocation to strengthen antioxidant defenses, restores autophagic flux to eliminate lipid droplets, and attenuates canonical NF-κB activation to alleviate hepatic and systemic inflammation. Pharmacological inhibition of PKG abrogated all four aforementioned effects, verifying pathway dependency. These findings establish PDE6D as a druggable vulnerability in ALD and suggest that PPI simultaneously suppresses ferroptosis and reprograms metabolic and immune homeostasis through the PDE6D-cGMP-PKG axis.

articles.title: Transitioning: From Pregnancy to Lifelong Cardiovascular Care.
articles.abstract: Women who have had certain pregnancy complications have an increased risk of future cardiovascular disease. The first year postpartum is an ideal window of opportunity for cardiovascular risk screening, management, and cardiovascular disease prevention. Recognizing that access to postpartum care can be challenging, particularly for those who live in rural or remote areas, it is the role of the obstetrical care providers to identify the women who are at risk and to initiate discussions about the importance of postpartum blood pressure monitoring and cardiovascular risk screening and to identify who is responsible for both the short-term and longer-term medical follow-up.

articles.title: Vertebrobasilar Circulation Involvement in Histiocytic Neoplasms: The Coated Artery Sign.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Histiocytic neoplasms, particularly Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD), exhibit perivascular infiltration, and vertebrobasilar circulation involvement remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe intracranial vertebrobasilar involvement.
