METHODS: We conducted a case series nested within an observational cohort at a tertiary referral center. We identified patients from a predefined cohort of biopsy-proven histiocytic neoplasms. We included patients with ECD, Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH), or Rosai-Dorfman-Destombes disease (RDD) who demonstrated intracranial vertebrobasilar periarterial involvement, defined by MRI evidence of histiocytic infiltration encasing the vertebral and/or basilar arteries.

RESULTS: Vertebrobasilar coated artery involvement was present in 3 patients with ECD (3/183, 1.6%), including 1 with mixed ECD-LCH, and 1 patient with RDD (1/88, 1.1%); no cases occurred in isolated LCH (0/144). Two patients with multisystemic ECD had incidental imaging findings without neurological symptoms. One patient developed a progressive brainstem syndrome due to an enlarging perivascular lesion, and 1 patient with RDD developed chronic progressive myelopathy from a cervicomedullary lesion encasing both vertebral arteries.

CONCLUSIONS: Vertebrobasilar coated artery involvement can occur in histiocytic neoplasms, particularly ECD. Recognition of this imaging pattern may aid neurologists in diagnosis and help prevent neurological complications from compression or ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Mapping the Evolving Research Landscape of Frontobasal and Anterior Skull Base Trauma.
articles.abstract: Frontobasal and anterior skull base fractures represent a subset of traumatic brain injury that is clinically complicated, with management spanning multiple fields such as neurosurgery, otorhinolaryngology, and critical care. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Web of Science Core Collection, with publication, citation, authorship, institutional, geographic, keyword, and network data analyzed using VOSviewer to map research trends, collaborative structures, and thematic evolution across the indexed literature. A total of 3415 publications were identified, demonstrating sustained growth peaking at 224 articles in 2025, with output concentrated in Clinical Neurology (47.2%) and Surgery (38.5%), led by US institutions and authors including Schievink WI (75 publications), and organized into 4 bibliographic coupling clusters spanning epidemiology, operative reconstruction, endoscopic approaches, and neuroendocrine complications. Publication and collaborative networks are concentrated among a small number of high-volume academic centers in North America and Europe. Emerging keyword trends include a focus on cerebrospinal fluid(CSF) leaks and spontaneous intracranial hypotension. This bibliometric analysis establishes a comprehensive map of the frontobasal skull base fracture literature and the need for multicenter collaboration and prospective outcomes-based research.

articles.title: Atraumatic Subcapital Femoral Neck Fracture as the Initial Presentation of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: A Case-Based Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Atraumatic subcapital femoral neck fracture associated with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is rare and may be difficult to recognize before surgery, while the available evidence regarding its diagnosis and management remains limited. We therefore aimed to describe an atypical presentation of ONFH as an atraumatic subcapital femoral neck fracture and to synthesize the available evidence on its diagnostic features, treatment patterns, and outcomes through a systematic review.

METHODS: A CARE-compliant case report was combined with a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review registered in PROSPERO. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from inception to February 28, 2026, for reports of atraumatic subcapital or transcervical femoral neck fractures associated with ONFH. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists. Findings were synthesized descriptively because of substantial clinical heterogeneity and the absence of comparative studies.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 50 patients (58 fractured hips) were included. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was reported in 38 of 50 patients (76%). Reported primary-treatment failures occurred in 3 of 8 internally fixed hips and 1 of 41 hips treated with arthroplasty; however, these uncontrolled descriptive findings do not permit comparative or causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: ONFH should be considered in atraumatic femoral neck fractures with atypical radiographic features. The available evidence is insufficient to determine the comparative effectiveness of arthroplasty and internal fixation, and treatment decisions should therefore remain individualized.

articles.title: Verticillium dahliae CFEM Effector VdCR Stabilises the Susceptibility Factor GhAGP31 to Suppress Host Vascular Immunity and Promote Cotton Verticillium Wilt.
articles.abstract: Plant pathogenic fungi secrete a wide array of effector proteins to manipulate host immunity, including those containing CFEM (Common in Fungal Extracellular Membranes) domains. Here, we identified a CFEM domain-containing effector VdCR from Verticillium dahliae, the causal agent of cotton Verticillium wilt. The expression of VdCR was drastically upregulated during cotton infection. Targeted deletion of VdCR compromised fungal oxidative stress resistance and pathogenicity on cotton, establishing it as a key virulence factor. VdCR physically targets cotton non-classical arabinogalactan protein GhAGP31 via its CFEM domain. Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) of GhAGP31 significantly enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, callose and lignin deposition, and plant resistance to V. dahliae, confirming that GhAGP31 acts as a negative regulator of vascular immunity. In addition, we identified GhAGP31 as a negative regulator of cotton vascular development, revealing its dual roles in coordinating plant immunity and development. We further verified that VdCR stabilises GhAGP31 to promote its accumulation both in vitro and in planta. Collectively, this study demonstrates that GhAGP31 functions as a novel cotton susceptibility factor that suppresses both vascular immunity and development and can be stabilised by the V. dahliae CFEM effector VdCR to facilitate fungal infection.

articles.title: Complex arrhythmias in the absence of severe valvulitis: a paediatric case of acute rheumatic fever.
articles.abstract: A 15-year-old boy was admitted to the emergency department with arthralgia of the knee. He was diagnosed with acute rheumatic fever based on clinical examination, electrocardiography, echocardiography, and elevated inflammatory markers including C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and anti-streptolysin O titre. First-degree and second-degree Mobitz type 1 atrioventricular blocks, moderate frequency uniform ventricular premature beats, as well as non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, were detected on 24-hour Holter electrocardiography monitoring.

articles.title: Cross-reactive T cell immunity against novel coronaviruses with pandemic potential, predictable from spike sequence conservation.
articles.abstract: Widespread SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination have reshaped global immunity to coronaviruses. Whether this immunity extends to animal sarbecoviruses with spillover potential remains unknown. We assessed cross-reactive memory T-cell responses to spike proteins from five relevant human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (hACE2)-dependent sarbecoviruses and MERS-CoV in healthcare workers in the UK and Vietnam. Limited SARS-CoV-2 specific or cross-reactive responses were seen in pre-pandemic samples. However, in samples collected from vaccinated donors at 3-24 months after booster vaccination, cross-reactive T-cell responses across the hACE2-dependent sarbecoviruses were detected. There was a strong correlation between the magnitude of responses and the level of viral sequence identity. This relationship was reproduced across cohorts in the UK and Vietnam. These findings indicate that post-pandemic populations possess measurable cellular immunity to genetically related sarbecoviruses and suggest that the degree of T-cell cross-recognition can be predicted from the spike protein sequence conservation. Such data provide an immunological framework for assessing vulnerability to future sarbecovirus spillover.

articles.title: Electrophysiological properties of mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive.
articles.abstract: The neocortex has the largest volume, whereas the cerebellum houses the most neurons of the mammalian brain, underscoring paramount functions for interactions between them. Neocortical projections to the cerebellum involve both the mossy fibre and climbing fibre systems; mossy fibres find their origin predominantly in the pons, whereas the climbing fibres are relayed via subnuclei of the inferior olive (IO) that receive cortical input via the mesodiencephalic junction (MDJ). Given that climbing fibres regulate cerebellar plasticity in a timing-dependent manner, the MDJ-IO pathway probably contributes to both sensorimotor and cognitive learning. However, the physiological properties of IO-projecting MDJ neurons remain largely unknown. Here, we made targeted whole-cell recordings in brain slices of the mouse MDJ, separating IO- from non-IO-projecting neurons following retrograde tracing. We show that IO-projecting neurons are, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, highly spontaneously active and capable of high-frequency bursts of ≤350 Hz during current injections. Optogenetic stimulation shows that excitatory neocortical inputs to IO-projecting MDJ neurons can be integrated directly with excitatory inputs from the cerebellar nuclei. Moreover, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, IO-projecting MDJ neurons depolarize and repolarize quickly, and hyperpolarizing inputs consistently trigger rebound action potentials upon stimulus offset. This hyperpolarization is probably induced predominantly by inhibitory inputs from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey, which provide prominent bilateral inputs to MDJ neurons, as revealed by viral tracing in Gad2-Cre mice. Our results highlight how neocortical inputs to the MDJ can be transformed into diverse IO firing patterns and thereby contribute to the required specifics of cerebellar learning. KEY POINTS: The mesodiencephalic junction is an important brainstem region connecting the cerebral cortex with the cerebellum through its projection to the inferior olive, the sole source of the climbing fibres that drive cerebellar learning. We find that mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive represent a population of physiologically distinct neurons, capable of high firing frequencies and rebound activity following hyperpolarization. We reveal that mesodiencephalic junction neurons receive prominent excitatory inputs from neocortex and cerebellar nuclei, whereas their main inhibitory inputs are derived from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey. These findings shed light on how the activity of neurons in the mesodiencephalic junction can be regulated and how these neurons might influence activity in the inferior olive, and thereby cerebellar learning.

articles.title: Heat Stroke Cooling Devices for Prehospital Use: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Heat stroke and heat exhaustion (HS/HE) are life-threatening conditions requiring immediate intervention. Cooling devices play a critical role in emergency and prehospital care, yet their effectiveness and field readiness are inconsistently reported. This systematic review evaluates commercially available cooling devices for the treatment of HS/HE with an emphasis on device feasibility, performance, and suitability for prehospital and remote deployment.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in August/October 2025 across academic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Compendex, Engineering Village, and IEEE Xplore) and gray literature via Google Advanced Search. Academic records were screened using Rayyan, while gray literature was organized in Excel with the aid of a custom HTML scraper. Devices were included if they met the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) definition of a medical device, were designed for adult human use, and specifically addressed HS/HE. Parameters extracted included working principle, cooling rate, weight, dimensions, volume, power requirements, external resource demands, and reusability. Cooling performance was benchmarked using thresholds reported by McDermott, et al, and portability was assessed using the MIL-STD-1472H single-person carriage limit of ≤16kg.

RESULTS: A total of 18 devices were identified and evaluated. Only three met the ideal cooling rate threshold (≥0.155°C/minute), and two others achieved acceptable performance (0.078-0.154°C/minute). Approximately 61% of devices did not report cooling rate data. Five devices met field portability criteria (≤16kg), though most were limited by reliance on water, power, or disposable components. Only one device demonstrated feasibility for remote use; this device, however, lacked full reusability.

CONCLUSIONS: No device meets the combined criteria of effectiveness, portability, field readiness, and reusability for HS/HE treatment. Current FDA pathways do not require reporting of key performance metrics, highlighting a regulatory gap. There is a need for development of field-appropriate solutions and revised evaluation standards that prioritize cooling performance, resource independence, and usability in austere environments.

articles.title: NAD+ replenishment reduces cardiomyocyte senescence and improves diastolic function in the aged male heart.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Cardiomyocyte senescence is a hallmark of cardiac aging and closely associated with diastolic dysfunction and heart failure in older adults. Strategies to effectively delay or reverse cardiomyocyte senescence in the aged heart remain limited. We investigated whether NAD+ replenishment regulates cardiomyocyte senescence and cardiac function in aging.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Ventricular NAD+ metabolism, senescence markers, and cardiac function were assessed in young and aged mice of both sexes. Aged male mice exhibited reduced cardiac NAD+ levels due to impaired biosynthesis, limited mitochondrial mobilization, and increased consumption, leading to suppressed SIRT1 and SIRT6 activity and accumulation of senescent cardiomyocytes. These changes were accompanied by diastolic dysfunction, myocardial hypertrophy, and fibrosis. In cultured cardiomyocytes, NAD+ depletion induced cellular senescence, which was reversed by supplementation with the NAD+ precursors nicotinamide riboside (NR) and dihydronicotinamide riboside (NRH). In aged male mice, two months of NR or NRH treatment suppressed senescence markers, improved diastolic function, and reduced hypertrophy and fibrosis. Mechanistically, both NR and NRH activated SIRT1 and suppressed cell cycle arrest markers. NRH induced more robust SIRT1 activation, which deacetylated SIRT6, promoting its binding to histones and enhancing DNA damage repair. In contrast, aged female mice exhibited diastolic dysfunction without significant decline in cardiac NAD+ levels and did not respond to NR or NRH treatment.

CONCLUSION: NAD+ is a critical regulator of cardiomyocyte senescence in aging male hearts. NAD+ replenishment, particularly with NRH, reverses senescence-associated cardiac dysfunction through coordinated activation of SIRT1 and SIRT6. The sex-specific differences observed highlight distinct mechanisms underlying cardiac aging and emphasize the importance of considering biological sex in the development of NAD+-based therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Dysphagia and feeding outcomes in paediatric patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries undergoing pulmonary artery intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major aortopulmonary collateral arteries represent a complex subgroup of CHD with unique cardiopulmonary physiology. While surgical outcomes have been well described, feeding and swallowing outcomes remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterise dysphagia prevalence and functional feeding outcomes in these paediatric patients undergoing pulmonary artery intervention.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of paediatric patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries at a tertiary paediatric cardiac centre between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2025. Swallowing outcomes were assessed using the Penetration-Aspiration Scale, and functional feeding outcomes were measured using the Pediatric Functional Oral Intake Scale. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise patient characteristics and feeding outcomes. Pre- and post-intervention outcomes were compared among patients with paired data.

RESULTS: Nineteen patients were included. Genetic diagnoses were present in 58% of the cohort, most commonly 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. Prolonged intubation occurred in 53% of patients, and vocal fold motion impairment and necrotising enterocolitis were each observed in 42%. Among patients with paired data, median Penetration-Aspiration Scale increased from 3 pre-operatively to 6 post-operatively, and aspiration was observed in 50% post-operatively. Enteral tube use increased from 57% pre-operatively to 79% post-operatively among patients with paired data. Persistent oral aversion at six months was documented in 26% of the cohort.

CONCLUSION: Patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries demonstrate high rates of dysphagia and enteral feeding dependence across the perioperative period. Preliminary findings highlight the need for early, multidisciplinary feeding evaluation to optimise developmental outcomes in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: Tumour-anchored Purkinje-mediated ventricular tachycardia in a child with cardiac rhabdomyoma.
articles.abstract: Cardiac rhabdomyomas are associated with ventricular arrhythmias, but mechanisms remain uncertain. A 10-year-old boy with tuberous sclerosis complex developed verapamil-sensitive fascicular ventricular tachycardia adjacent to a residual cardiac rhabdomyoma. Electrophysiological mapping demonstrated Purkinje-mediated reentry. Catheter ablation at a tumour-adjacent site eliminated the arrhythmia, suggesting that residual rhabdomyoma may anchor a localised reentrant substrate.

articles.title: When the skin speaks but the heart remains silent: acute rheumatic fever with three major Jones manifestations without carditis.
articles.abstract: Acute rheumatic fever is classically associated with carditis, particularly when erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules are present. We report a 13-year-old boy who fulfilled three major Jones manifestations-migratory polyarthritis, erythema marginatum, and subcutaneous nodules-supported by evidence of recent streptococcal infection, yet had no clinical, electrocardiographic, or echocardiographic evidence of carditis on serial assessment over three months. Serial photographs documented the evolving morphology of erythema marginatum in dark skin. A transient ocular inflammatory episode occurred during convalescence. This case highlights an uncommon phenotype of acute rheumatic fever and underscores the importance of recognising major extracardiac manifestations even when the heart remains unaffected.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Noncompaction Cardiomyopathy and Thromboembolic Complications: A Case Report and Focused Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy (LVNC) is a rare myocardial disorder characterized by prominent trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses. Thromboembolic complications represent a major source of morbidity and mortality, yet optimal risk stratification and anticoagulation strategies remain poorly defined. The authors have reported the case of a patient with previously undiagnosed LVNC who presented with rapidly progressive heart failure and developed acute, recurrent cardioembolic strokes. Cardiac imaging revealed extensive left ventricular trabeculations, a severely reduced ejection fraction, and bilateral atrial appendage thrombi. Despite systemic anticoagulation, the patient experienced rapid respiratory and hemodynamic decompensation resulting in death. LVNC is associated with a substantial chance of thromboembolic events, particularly in patients with ventricular dysfunction. This case highlighted the crucial importance of early recognition and the need for individualized anticoagulation strategies in patients at high risk.

articles.title: Assessment of pathogen reduction strategies in reducing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) transmission in acute-care hospitals: an agent-based model study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) infections are an urgent public health threat in the United States. Despite infection prevention and control measures, hospital CRE rates have not declined in the past decade. Novel drug-based pathogen reduction approaches may decrease CRE incidence, and mathematical models can assess implementation strategies.

METHODS: We used agent-based modeling to evaluate a hypothetical drug with pathogen reduction properties for reducing CRE transmission in an example acute-care hospital. We compared a strategy that treated only clinically detected CRE-colonized patients-using three drug effectiveness (DE) levels (25%, 50%, 75%)-with strategies that treated patients identified through surveillance screening in addition to clinical cultures. Surveillance screenings (intensive care unit (ICU) or all-admission screenings) were implemented at 50% and 100% patient participation (PP). Model parameters were informed by administrative healthcare data and published literature.

RESULTS: The baseline mean CRE colonization incidence was 27.4 per 10,000 patient-days (interquartile range [IQR]: 11.7-39.9). Compared to baseline, at DE = 25% the reduction in mean colonization incidence was 1.2% (-0.8%-3.2%) for the treatment-only strategy. At DE = 50%, treatment + ICU screening reduced incidence by 9.0% (7.1%-11.0%) at PP = 50% and 13.2% (11.4%-15.1%) at PP = 100%. The reduction reached 38.5% (37.1%-40.0%) for treatment + all-admission screening at DE = 75% and PP = 100%.

CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores the potential of novel drugs as pathogen reduction measures to reduce CRE incidence in US hospitals if deployed strategically. Findings highlight the value of developing pathogen reduction strategies for colonized patients to prevent CRE transmission and infections.

articles.title: Phenome-wide Longitudinal Association Study of Hospital-recorded Comorbidity in Psoriasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: International guidelines recommend screening individuals with psoriasis, a common chronic inflammatory skin condition, for a range of conditions across the spectrum of human disease. Despite this, gaps may remain within our knowledge of the full breadth of comorbidity in psoriasis.

OBJECTIVES: To perform a phenome-wide longitudinal association study of psoriasis and its comorbidities.

METHOD: We conducted cohort studies (matched for age, sex and general practice) for each block (group of related conditions) of outcomes within the International Classification of Diseases - Clinical Modification (10th ed.) using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum primary care data linked to secondary care Hospital Episode Statistics (to define ICD outcomes) within the United Kingdom. We evaluated the association between psoriasis and outcomes in the first year of diagnosis and in the subsequent period. We estimated hazard ratios (HR) with 99% confidence intervals from Cox regression, with covariate models adjusted for alcohol, smoking, BMI and measures of social deprivation.

RESULTS: We compared 320,220 individuals with psoriasis to 1,706,424 matched individuals. In 225 ICD blocks evaluated, psoriasis was associated with numerous outcomes across organ systems. Strong, non-dermatological associations in the long-term included liver disease (HR 1.47 [1.42-1.51], RD 1.16), substance (including alcohol and tobacco) misuse (HR 1.26 [1.25-1.28], RD 3.27) and other respiratory diseases principally affecting the interstitium (HR 1.33 [1.27-1.40], RD 0.31).

CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence of association between psoriasis and a range of comorbidity and may serve to generate hypotheses on previously underappreciated associations.

articles.title: Space changes after premature loss of mandibular second primary molars: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deciduous dentition plays a crucial role in mastication, phonetics, and maintaining arch space for permanent successors. While several systematic reviews have quantified spatial changes following first primary molar loss, specific evidence synthesis for second primary molars is lacking. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantify space loss following premature extraction of second primary molars and evaluate the clinical necessity of space maintenance.

METHODS: Five electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, LILACS, EMBASE, and Cochrane libraries) were searched without date restrictions (last search 03/06/2025). Inclusion criteria included randomized, quasi-randomized, and non-randomized clinical trials involving children aged 4-9 years with second primary molar indicated for extraction. Two independent investigators assessed studies for inclusion, evaluated risk of bias using ROBINS-I tool, and extracted data. Random-effects models with 95% confidence intervals calculated mean differences as effect measures.

RESULTS: Four studies were included in qualitative synthesis, with three studies involving 38 children included in meta-analysis. Meta-analysis demonstrated mean mandibular space loss of 0.80 mm (95% CI: -1.00 to -0.60; p < 0.0001) at 3 months, 1.10 mm (95% CI: -1.24 to -0.96; p < 0.0001) at 6 months, and 1.24 mm (95% CI: -1.48 to -1.02; p < 0.0001) at 9-10 months post-extraction. Arch hemi-perimeter decreased by 1.06 mm (95% CI: -1.26 to -0.31; p = 0.001) at 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Current limited short‑term evidence suggests that premature mandibular second primary molar loss in children with erupted first permanent molars results in mean space loss of approximately 1.24 mm over 9‑10 months. Whether this short‑term space loss translates into long‑term malocclusion or orthodontic treatment need remains unknown. Therefore, clinical decisions regarding space maintenance should remain individualized and based on arch length discrepancy, occlusal development, crowding, molar relationship, and long‑term orthodontic risk. The current evidence is insufficient to support routine space maintainer use. Maxillary arch evidence is too limited to support any conclusion.

articles.title: Human organotypic skin explant culture (hOSEC): an alternative approach to Staphylococcus aureus colonization assays.
articles.journal: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: hOSEC provides a relevant ex vivo platform to study Staphylococcus aureus infection, preserving the structural and immune components of human skin while reducing animal use. This pilot study aimed to standardize hOSEC for S. aureus colonization and infection, supporting translational research and novel therapeutic approaches, compared to other models in offering a cost-effective platform.

METHODS: hOSEC was established from surgical samples (N = 06) using dermatological punch biopsies. Tissue viability was assessed by TTC assay. Staphylococcus aureus ATCC® 25923™ (susceptible), ATCC® BAA-1026™ and NCTC 12,493™ (resistant) strains were isolated and cultured. Infection assays were performed by epidermal colonization and intradermal inoculation, followed by bacterial curve analysis (CFU counts). Antimicrobial treatments were applied, and efficacy was evaluated through quantitative bacteriological analysis.

RESULTS: The hOSEC model maintained structural integrity and mitochondrial activity throughout the study. Explants exposed retained high viability across antibiotic treatments (97.0%) and in untreated controls (98.0%). Intradermal inoculation (skin infection model) with 10⁶ CFU/mL led to bacterial proliferation (> 1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL) in untreated explants, while antibiotic-treated tissues showed strong suppression (average 2 × 10² CFU/mL). During epidermal colonization with wound and resistant strain, saline-treated explants maintained high bacterial counts: >10⁸ CFU/mL at 0-6 h, 4.5 × 104 CFU/mL at 12 h (p = 0.002), and persisted longer but were significantly reduced by antibiotic treatment (from 1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL at 0-6 h to 2 CFU/mL at 24 h). Notably, viable bacteria were still detectable in explants for up to 7 days (2.5 × 102 CFU/mL). Histopathological analysis revealed tissue damage characterized by acantholysis, necrosis, and apoptosis.

CONCLUSIONS: The hOSEC model preserved tissue viability under bacterial inoculation and antibiotic exposure, supporting its use for ex vivo antimicrobial testing. Although intradermal inoculation (skin infection model) maintained high bacterial viability and effectively modeled deep tissue infection, injury-associated colonization (skin wound model) provided better spatial control of the infectious site by restricting bacterial growth to the injury area. Additionally, it was possible to identify histopathological alterations induced by bacterial infection, as histopathological analysis revealed acantholysis, necrosis, and apoptosis. These results demonstrate the model's utility for evaluating antibiotic penetration, local efficacy, and bacterial dynamics in controlled human skin-mimetic conditions.

articles.title: Evaluation of Umbilical Cord Blood Culture for Detection of Early Onset Sepsis in Neonates with Spontaneous Preterm Birth: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) is associated with early-onset sepsis (EOS) in neonates. The authors aimed to compare the umbilical cord blood culture (UCBC) positivity (as a marker of intra-amniotic infection) in neonates with sPTB to those born at term, and evaluate its ability to detect EOS.

METHODS: In a prospective cohort study design, the authors included neonates (<35 wk) born via sPTB and term neonates (37-41 wk) born between June 2021 to May 2022 at a level III neonatal intensive care unit in north India. The primary outcome was to evaluate the proportion of neonates with positive UCBC in preterm and term groups. The authors also evaluated the role of UCBC positivity in those neonates who developed EOS.

RESULTS: The authors enrolled 47 neonates born via sPTB and 40 term neonates. In the preterm group, 10 neonates (21%) developed EOS (two culture-positive and eight culture-negative). UCBC positivity was 19% (9/47) in preterm vs. 2% (1/40) in the term group (RR 7.6; 95% CI 1.0%, 57.9%; p = 0.015). Escherichia coli was the predominant organism (n = 4). Of nine UCBC positive cases in the preterm group, six developed EOS (2 culture-positive and 4 culture-negative). Both the preterm neonates with culture-proven sepsis had concordant growth of the same organism in umbilical and peripheral blood culture. UCBC demonstrated a sensitivity of 100% (95% CI 15.8%-100%) and specificity of 94.8% (95% CI 87.2%-98.6%) to detect culture-proven sepsis.

CONCLUSIONS: Preterm neonates with sPTB exhibit a higher rate of UCBC positivity, compared to term neonates with low risk of EOS. Preliminary findings suggest the potential utility of UCBC to detect EOS. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: First-in-Human Phase 1b/2a Trial Shows Safety with MEK 1/2 Inhibitor EDV2209 as A Novel Treatment for Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: We report findings from a Phase 1/2a clinical trial (EUCT No. 2024-514590-22-00, STOP-DCI), an interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending-dose, first-in-human trial to determine safety and evaluate clinical outcome for the MEK 1/2 inhibitor EDV2209 in patients with severe spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). In Phase 1b (N = 11), three cohorts received a single intracerebral ventricular (ICV) bolus (8.55 µg, 17-28.5 µg). In Phase 2a (N = 16), two cohorts were given three ICV injections of 28.5 µg EDV2209 or placebo over 18 h, beginning within 8 h of SAH onset.The study found an equal distribution of adverse events between treatment and placebo with no treatment-associated safety concerns. Outcomes and mortality were as expected or better for patients with severe SAH in the patients treated with EDV2209. Pharmacokinetics were reproducibly stable in the CSF with no detectable levels of EDV2209 in plasma.Treatment with EDV2209 was considered safe and was interpreted to provide potential benefit for improving patient outcome following severe SAH. These results provide a rationale to continue with a Phase 2b / 3 study powered to determine efficacy as well as safety.

articles.title: Italian guideline on palliative care in adult patients with grade 3/4 gliomas.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The palliative and supportive care needs of adults with glioma are complex. In 2017, the European Association for Neuro-Oncology (EANO) published the guideline on palliative care (PC) in this population.

OBJECTIVE: To develop a clinical practice guideline for the PC of adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 gliomas by updating and adapting the EANO guideline to the Italian context.

METHODS: The guideline was produced by an interdisciplinary, consumer-inclusive panel appointed by the three main Italian scientific associations for neurology, neuro-oncology and PC, following the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: The panel formulated two clinical questions, addressed by three recommendations (all based on very-low-certainty evidence) and one Good Practice Statement: (1) We suggest the use of structured communication interventions to convey diagnosis, prognosis, and/or therapeutic and care options (conditional recommendation). (2) We recommend using approaches/tools to facilitate information processing in adults with glioma with reduced decision-making capacity (strong recommendation). (3) We believe it is appropriate to monitor the emotional impact that communication can have, and to provide support to adults with glioma and their caregivers (Good Practice Statement). (4) We suggest offering adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 glioma a healthcare model that integrates the best anti-tumor and palliative treatments through early, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and multi-professional management of emerging health needs. The integrated model should be aligned with patients' care preferences and caregivers' needs and provided throughout the whole disease trajectory and across all care settings (conditional recommendation).

CONCLUSIONS: This guideline provides recommendations for improving communication and integrated PC for adults with glioma and their caregivers. It also provides indications for future research priorities in this population.

articles.title: Survival Outcomes in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients with BRAF Mutations Undergoing Targeted Chemotherapy: A Reconstructed Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) represents an aggressive molecular subtype associated with poor prognosis and limited response to conventional chemotherapy. Although multiple targeted strategies, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and BRAF-directed therapies, are used in clinical practice, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. We performed a reconstructed individual patient-data (IPD) meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate survival outcomes across targeted therapeutic classes in BRAF-mutant mCRC.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane databases was conducted through July 2025 to identify RCTs reporting survival outcomes for BRAF-mutant mCRC. Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized and IPD reconstructed using established methods. A one-stage meta-analysis using Cox proportional hazards models was performed to estimate pooled overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Models were adjusted for study-level covariates and clustering, with Bonferroni correction applied for multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs comprising 11,931 participants were included. Pooled median OS was 22.3 months for BRAF-directed regimens, 17.1 months for VEGF-targeted therapy, and 10.1 months for EGFR-directed therapy across studies evaluating first-line therapy. Across first-line studies, BRAF inhibitor directed regimen was associated with significantly improved OS compared with EGFR inhibition (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31-0.60; P < 0.001) and improved PFS (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.42-0.53; P < 0.001). VEGF inhibition also demonstrated superior OS compared with EGFR inhibition (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.38-0.81; p < 0.001). EGFR-directed regimen consistently demonstrated the poorest survival outcomes across analyses.

DISCUSSION: In this reconstructed IPD meta-analysis, BRAF-directed therapies were associated with the most favourable survival outcomes, whereas EGFR directed regimen demonstrated limited clinical benefit in BRAF-mutant mCRC. These results highlight the importance of biologically aligned pathway-targeted therapy and provide comparative evidence to inform treatment selection in this aggressive molecular subtype.

articles.title: Exercise and Mitophagy in Cerebral Ischemia: Mechanistic Evidence, Exercise Strategies, and Translational Challenges.
articles.abstract: Following ischemic stroke, energy depletion, mitochondrial depolarization, oxidative stress, and disrupted calcium homeostasis lead to the accumulation of damaged mitochondria, which in turn amplifies neuroinflammation and cell death. As a selective mechanism for eliminating damaged mitochondria, mitophagy contributes to mitochondrial quality control and may represent one of the mechanisms involved in exercise-mediated neuroprotection after ischemic stroke. This review synthesizes evidence on mitophagy in cerebral ischemia and its regulation by exercise. We discuss the ubiquitin-dependent PINK1/Parkin pathway, the receptor-dependent BNIP3L/NIX and FUNDC1 pathways, and their upstream regulation by AMPK/ULK1, SIRT3, Sesn2/AMPK/TFEB, and PGC-1α/FNDC5/irisin signaling. We also compare exercise preconditioning with post-stroke training in terms of initiation time, modality, intensity, and dose. Preclinical evidence indicates that exercise improves neurobehavioral outcomes after cerebral ischemia and enhances mitochondrial respiration, dynamics, and biogenesis. However, direct evidence that exercise protects ischemic brain tissue through mitophagy remains limited. Most studies rely on static markers, including LC3, p62, PINK1, Parkin, and BNIP3L/NIX, which cannot distinguish mitophagy-specific flux or establish causality. The optimal timing, intensity, and dose of exercise also remain undefined. Future studies should integrate mitochondria-targeted flux reporters, genetic interventions, and standardized reporting of exercise parameters using the frequency, intensity, time, type, volume, and progression (FITT-VP) framework to clarify the mechanistic contribution of mitophagy and inform future translational research.

articles.title: Music-based interventions in stroke rehabilitation: stakeholder perspectives from a qualitative study in Singapore.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: Music-based interventions have shown benefits for motor, cognitive, and psychosocial outcomes after stroke, yet they remain underutilised in routine rehabilitation. We explored how stroke survivors, caregivers, healthcare professionals and music therapists perceive the role, benefits, barriers and implementation needs of music-based interventions in stroke rehabilitation, using semi-structured interviews with 21 participants in Singapore and inductive thematic analysis guided by Braun and Clarke's six-step approach. Four themes were identified: (1) multidimensional challenges after stroke (2) perceived benefits of music-based interventions (3) barriers to implementation, and (4) recommendations for integration. Stakeholders in Singapore regard music-based interventions as person-centred modalities that complement conventional therapies by addressing emotional, cognitive, social and motivational aspects of stroke recovery. These findings reflect stakeholder perceptions of the potential role of music-based interventions. However, there remains a need to enhance awareness, funding, and culturally sensitive, individualised delivery models.

articles.title: Integrated genomic, immunoinformatic and experimental evaluation of conserved pneumococcal surface proteins for serotype-independent vaccine development.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs), which target capsular polysaccharides, have significantly reduced the burden of invasive pneumococcal disease; however, their effectiveness is limited by serotype replacement, geographic variation, and the emergence of non-vaccine serotypes.

METHODS: Pan-genome analysis was conducted to identify the conserved core genes of S. pneumoniae. An integrated bioinformatics approach, incorporating PSORTb, SignalP, TMHMM, and domain-based motif analysis, predicted Surface-associated proteins. Highly conserved Surface-associated proteins were further evaluated for their gene expression in vitro infection of A549 lung epithelial cells using RT-qPCR, and surface accessibility assessment by flow cytometry. Further immunoinformatics analyses for their antigenicity (VaxiJen), linear B-cell epitope prediction (BepiPred 3.0), and MHC-II (HLA-DR) binding prediction was perfoemd.

RESULTS: Four surface-associated lipoproteins-PsaA, AdcA, AmiA, and Lmb-were universally conserved and predicted to be surface-exposed. During epithelial cell infection, all four genes were actively expressed, with psaA showed greater early upregulation (~ 2.5-fold; p < 0.05). Flow cytometry confirmed surface localization of all proteins, with PsaA exhibiting the highest accessibility (92% positive cells; highest MFI). Immunoinformatics analyses demonstrated strong antigenicity scores, enriched linear B-cell epitope clusters, and multiple high-affinity MHC-II binding peptides for these proteins, particularly PsaA and AdcA. In contrast, conserved multi-pass transmembrane proteins (e.g., SecG, MisCA, EcfT) showed limited surface accessibility.

CONCLUSIONS: The study identifies conserved pneumococcal surface proteins that could be used as a vaccine candidate. PsaA is the most promising serotype-independent vaccine candidate, while other AdcA, AmiA, and Lmb represent potential antigens for multicomponent formulations.

articles.title: Biological functions and emerging interplay of FGF21 and GDF15 in metabolic diseases and aging.
articles.abstract: Metabolic diseases and age-related disorders represent a major global health burden driven by the increasing prevalence of obesity and obesity-associated complications. These disorders are characterized by chronic disturbances in energy homeostasis. A key feature linking metabolic disease and aging is the activation of stress-related pathways, which contribute to progressive metabolic dysfunction. Among the endocrine mediators of cellular stress, fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) have emerged as key regulators of metabolic homeostasis. Both are induced by similar stress conditions, including nutrient imbalance, inflammation, oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, and are elevated in pathophysiological conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2D), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and aging. FGF21 and GDF15 also share overlapping regulatory pathways and complementary functions, suggesting a potential coordinated regulation and functional interplay. However, the extent and physiological relevance of this possible interrelationship remain incompletely understood. This review summarizes current knowledge on the regulation, tissue sources, and signaling mechanisms of FGF21 and GDF15 across metabolic diseases and aging, with particular attention to their roles as mediators of adaptive metabolic responses and their overlapping biological actions. We further discuss their context-dependent effects under acute and chronic stress and their relevance as biomarkers of metabolic dysfunction and disease progression. Collectively, this work highlights FGF21 and GDF15 as integrated stress signals linking cellular stress to systemic metabolic adaptation, providing a conceptual framework for understanding their cooperative roles and regulation in metabolic and age-related diseases, which may have therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Glymphatic Dysfunction as a Multisystem Pathway Linking Systemic Health Conditions to Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms, Risk Factors, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.abstract: The glymphatic system is a glia-associated perivascular pathway involved in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange and the transport and clearance of neurotoxic metabolites, including amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau, from the central nervous system. Growing evidence suggests that alterations in glymphatic and perivascular clearance are associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and may contribute to the accumulation of neurotoxic proteins and neurodegeneration. This review examines the role of the glymphatic system in AD and explores how aging, sleep disturbances, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, high-fat diet, diabetes, and gut microbiome dysbiosis impair glymphatic transport. A recurring mechanism across experimental models is the loss of perivascular AQP4 polarization, while vascular, metabolic, and inflammatory conditions may converge on related perivascular and neurovascular processes that impair CSF-ISF exchange and solute handling. Neuroimaging studies using markers such as DTI-ALPS, perivascular space burden, and free-water measurements provide evidence of alterations in glymphatic-related and perivascular processes in AD and demonstrate associations with amyloid deposition, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline. Furthermore, glymphatic dysfunction may interact with neuroinflammation and tau pathology, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that accelerates disease progression. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including continuous theta-burst stimulation, positive airway pressure therapy for obstructive sleep apnea, pharmacological enhancement of AQP4 function, and nutritional interventions, have shown potential in experimental and early translational studies to influence glymphatic-related processes and may mitigate AD-related pathology. Collectively, current findings suggest that glymphatic and perivascular clearance pathways may represent an important link between systemic health conditions and AD. Because related pathways are implicated across multiple systemic conditions, interventions targeting glymphatic and perivascular dysfunction may have broader relevance to brain health, but their clinical effects remain to be established.

articles.title: Musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America: Workforce characteristics, resource availability, and territorial disparities.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Musculoskeletal oncology requires highly specialized, multidisciplinary care. Although the subspecialty has evolved worldwide, information on workforce characteristics, resource availability, and practice patterns across Latin America remains limited.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey using convenience sampling was conducted among orthopaedic surgeons involved in musculoskeletal oncology throughout Latin America. An adapted version of a previously published questionnaire was distributed through the Latin American Society of Musculoskeletal Tumors (SLATME) and professional networks. The survey explored training background, clinical practice characteristics, perceived support from selected specialties and specialized resources, perceived professional challenges, and treatment preferences. We performed descriptive analyses and comparisons by practice-location population size (< 1 million versus ≥ 1 million inhabitants).

RESULTS: A total of 147 surgeons from 17 countries participated. Most respondents reported formal orthopaedic oncology training (76%) and academic orteaching involvement (93%). Respondents practicing in locations with ≥ one million inhabitants were significantly more likely to report treating ≥ 30 cases annually of soft tissue sarcoma (47% vs. 14%, p < 0.001), metastatic bone disease (73% vs. 40%, p < 0.001), and primary bone sarcoma (29% vs. 9%, p = 0.013). Access to molecular genetic testing, bone banks and allografts, and tumour reconstruction prostheses was also significantly greater in larger population centers, whereas access to MRI, radiotherapy, and intensive care did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: Among survey respondents, musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America was characterized by high rates of specialized training and academic or teaching involvement. However, differences in the reported annual numbers of new malignant tumour cases treated and in access to advanced resources were observed according to practice-location population size. Because this study used a convenience sampling strategy, these findings reflect the respondents' practices but should not be generalized to the entire Latin American musculoskeletal oncology community.

articles.title: Transcription factor EB as a novel target for dimethyl fumarate to restore endothelial function in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus-associated endothelial dysfunction represents a pivotal early event in diabetic vasculopathy, linking metabolic derangements to vascular injury. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an FDA-approved drug for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet whether it protects against diabetic endothelial dysfunction and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, diabetic db/db mice and the non-diabetic db/m+ littermates were treated with DMF (100 mg·kg-1·d-1) or vehicle for 4 weeks, and vascular function in aortic and mesenteric artery rings was assessed by wire myography. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and endothelial cell (EC)-specific Tfeb knockout (TfebECKO) mice were employed to investigate the target of DMF in vitro and in vivo. DMF restored the impaired endothelium-dependent relaxations (EDRs) in db/db mouse aortas and insulin-induced relaxations in mesenteric arteries, improved glucose tolerance, reduced aortic endothelial mitochondrial ROS (mito-ROS) accumulation, and lowered the expression of inflammatory markers. IL-1β induced phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of TFEB (indicative of TFEB inhibition), mito-ROS production, and inflammatory responses in HUVECs and mouse aortas, all of which were reversed by DMF pretreatment. These protective effects of DMF were largely reversed by TFEB knockdown in HUVECs or in aortas of TfebECKO mice. RNA sequencing data analysis revealed a substantial overlap between DMF-regulated and TFEB-overexpression transcriptional profiles, implicating a role of TFEB in DMF-induced suppression of inflammatory and oxidative pathways. Together, DMF ameliorates endothelial dysfunction in diabetes by inhibiting TFEB phosphorylation and restoring TFEB nuclear activity. Endothelial TFEB represents a critical mediator responsible for the vaso-protective effects of DMF and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetic vascular complications.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Mechanical Thrombectomy and Anticoagulation in Intermediate- to High-Risk Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The comparative effectiveness of catheter-based mechanical thrombectomy in intermediate to high-risk acute PE remains uncertain. We reviewed comparative evidence to determine how thrombectomy performs against anticoagulation alone. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through September 13, 2026. We selected adult studies that compared mechanical thrombectomy plus anticoagulation with anticoagulation alone in intermediate to high-risk PE. Random-effects pooling was supplemented by sequential study removal, influence assessment, and Baujat plots. Seven studies including 9371 participants were eligible: 2 randomized trials and 5 cohort studies. Thrombectomy was associated with fewer 30-day deaths (odds ratio [OR], 0.28; 95% CI, 0.17-0.47) and a greater improvement in RV/LV ratio (mean difference, -0.25; 95% CI, -0.36 to -0.13). The groups did not differ significantly in bleeding (OR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.57-1.18) or PE-related mortality (OR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.22-7.28). ICU and hospital stays were not significantly reduced, and these endpoints varied substantially between studies. Mortality and bleeding were less sensitive to individual reports than length-of-stay outcomes. Thrombectomy was linked to lower early all-cause mortality and more favorable right ventricular recovery without a significant bleeding excess. Its effects on PE-specific death and resource use remain uncertain. More adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define which intermediate to high-risk patients should receive the procedure.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of S-Amlodipine/Telmisartan Fixed-Dose Combination Versus Monotherapy in Essential Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Offered Deceased Donor Kidneys With Little or No Chance of Being Transplanted.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With a broadening deceased donor pool and recent allocation policy changes, US transplant programs have reported challenges managing an influx of suboptimal kidney offers. We hypothesized that the number of offered kidneys with a minuscule chance of being transplanted has risen. If so, targeted innovations may be needed to reduce administrative burden and improve system efficiency.

METHODS: Using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data on kidneys offered in 2016-2024, we developed a multivariable model to predict the probability that an offered kidney was transplanted (PrTx). We examined trends in the number and proportion of offered kidneys having PrTx ≤2%, ≤5%, and ≤10%.

RESULTS: Donor factors most predictive of PrTx were age, donation after circulatory death, serum creatinine (terminal, peak, nadir), presence and duration of diabetes and hypertension, infectious disease test results, and body mass index. From 2016 to 2024, the annual number of kidneys offered with PrTx ≤2%, PrTx ≤5%, and PrTx ≤10% increased 13-fold (from 18 to 236), 12-fold (84 to 1055), and 10-fold (299 to 2856), respectively. Of the 236 offered kidneys with PrTx ≤2% in 2024, none was transplanted. The 2856 kidneys with PrTx ≤10% accounted for 7.9% (n = 1 208 883) of manually refused offers but just 1.1% (n = 239) of transplanted kidneys. Organ procurement organizations and centers varied substantially in offering and transplanting low-PrTx kidneys.

CONCLUSIONS: The number of offered kidneys with extremely low predicted transplant probability has risen sharply, most notably in 2024. Innovations, such as improved offer filtering capabilities and standardized expedited allocation pathways, are needed to improve kidney placement efficiency.

articles.title: Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in Critically Ill Children: The Medical Equivalent of a 100-Year Flood.
Potassium and Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.abstract: Hyperkalemia (potassium levels >5.5 mEq/L) or hypokalemia (potassium < 3.5 mEq/L) may incur potentially serious cardiovascular (CV) complications. Hyperkalemia is most commonly encountered in renal failure, K+ oversupplementation for diuretic therapy, use of potassium-sparing diuretics, therapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers in cardiorenal disease (chronic kidney disease [CKD] and/or heart failure-HF), digitalis toxicity, massive hemolysis, or muscle trauma. For patients with hyperkalemia, potassium binders (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, patiromer, and sodium polystyrene) are guideline-recommended for patients with CKD. Importantly, proactive potassium control via routine use of potassium binders in hyperkalemia may incur cost reduction in acute care while simultaneously supporting optimization of medications for comorbid conditions. Hypokalemia can occur in response to diuretic therapy (7-56%), following renal dialysis, or during recovery from endurance exercise and can be equally detrimental as it may raise the risk of ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Its diagnosis depends on the level of serum potassium. An ECG is useful in identifying the more severe consequences. Hypokalemia occurs in up to 20% of hospitalized patients and incurs an increased incidence of ventricular and atrial fibrillation. Importantly, "you cannot eat your way out of hypokalemia," i.e., by adding bananas and/or other potassium-providing fruit or juices, hence one needs to provide the patient with K+ supplements in tablet or liquid form or in more serious cases via slow (10 mmol/h) IV supplementation in highly controlled, strict hospital protocols and with continuous ECG monitoring. All these issues of serum potassium disturbances and their CV effects are herein reviewed.

articles.title: Effect of Atorvastatin and Rosuvastatin on Lipid Parameters and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Statins produce marked reductions in total and LDL cholesterol, C-reactive protein (CRP), and help prevent stroke, re-infarction, and subsequent risk of death. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the role of atorvastatin in comparison with rosuvastatin in lowering levels of inflammatory biomarkers and lipid parameters in patients with ACS. Online databases were searched, and results from random-effects meta-analysis are presented as weighted mean differences (WMDs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. The outcomes were assessed at the short-term (≤1 month) and long-term (>3 months) follow-up. A total of 15 studies (13 RCTs and 2 observational studies) were included. The level of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (P = 0.13), oxidized LDL (P = 0.94), and long-term HDL-C (P = 0.28) showed no significant difference between the two statin groups. No significant differences were observed between atorvastatin and rosuvastatin in total cholesterol and LDL-C at short-term or long-term follow-up. A significant decrease in CRP levels (WMD 4.08; 95% CI 1.53-6.63; P = 0.002; I2 = 98%) and a significant rise in HDL-C (WMD -1.15; 95% CI -1.99 to -0.32; P = 0.007; I2 = 39%) was reported in the rosuvastatin group compared to the atorvastatin group in the short-term. Atorvastatin was associated with a significant reduction in triglycerides at short-term follow-up (WMD -8.69; 95% CI -14.97 to -2.40; P = 0.007; I2 = 35%), while the overall long-term comparison was borderline and did not reach conventional statistical significance. Our findings suggest that rosuvastatin may provide greater short-term reductions in CRP and modest increases in HDL-C compared with atorvastatin; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity and the absence of significant differences at longer follow-up.

articles.title: Excessive Tidal Volume During Noninvasive Ventilation: Mechanisms of Harm Leading to Worse Clinical Outcomes.
DPP3-positive circulatory shock: from targetable ICU endotype to Horizon Europe precision-therapy trial.
Relationships between Schistosoma mansoni infection intensity, environmental enteric dysfunction (EED), and anemia type among preschool-aged children in Uganda.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a significant global burden of disease due to anemia among young children. Schistosomiasis has been shown to cause both iron deficiency anemia (IDA) and non-iron deficiency anemia (NIDA), the latter largely due to anemia of inflammation, among older children and adults. Yet, anemia etiology has not been studied in preschool-aged children.

METHODS: 345 Ugandan children aged 12 to 48 months and infected with egg patent S. mansoni were recruited from endemic villages along Lake Albert, Uganda. Infection intensity was determined using WHO criteria of low, moderate, and high. WHO age adjusted cutoffs for hemoglobin and serum ferritin levels (30 ng/ml) classified children into etiology groups. Markers of environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) were quantified. We employed multivariate logistic regression models to assess the relationship between anemia etiology and both S. mansoni infection intensity and markers of EED.

RESULTS: We report that higher S. mansoni infection intensity was associated with higher odds of IDA (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12-1.65, p<0.01) and NIDA (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.03-1.46, p=0.02) compared to no anemia, after adjusting for covariates. Calprotectin and α-1-antitrypsin (AAT), markers of EED, were linked to increased odds of IDA.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides evidence that S. mansoni infection is associated with both IDA and NIDA, mostly due to anemia of inflammation, in preschool-aged children. EED exacerbates iron deficiency in this setting. These insights emphasize the importance of age-inclusive approaches to anemia management in schistosomiasis-endemic areas.

articles.title: Aortic valve replacement and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting: technical considerations in the era of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coexistence of severe aortic stenosis (AS) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently encountered in contemporary practice, particularly amongst elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combined with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an alternative strategy, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the reference treatment for these patient groups. The introduction of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves (RDAV) has considerably expanded the surgical armamentarium by facilitating implantation and reducing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp times. Appropriate application of these technologies requires specific technical considerations that ultimately influence operative planning and execution.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes contemporary evidence associated with the use of sutureless and RDAVs in combined CABG and SAVR procedures. To ensure relevant literature is included, a literature search across PubMed and ScienceDirect has been carried out, spanning the last 20 years, utilizing relevant medical subject headings (MeSH) terms and keywords.

EXPERT OPINION: As evidence on sutureless and RDAVs technologies continues to accumulate, with associated advancements in perioperative planning, these valves are expected to become valuable adjuncts in combined procedures, by minimizing operative burden while also allowing for robust, aortic valve pathology correction.

articles.title: Small-Intestinal Motility Interrelates With Fecal Microbiota, Metabolites and Metabolic Tissue Gene Expression in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: : Recent studies show that the gut microbiota may affect both small-intestinal motility and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, human studies of this triangle are lacking. Our aim was to leverage the unique potential of cine-MRI to quantify small-intestinal motility in patients with MASLD and investigate its association with gut microbiota, metabolic tissues and metabolites.

METHODS: : Fifteen patients with histology proven MASLD participated in a 12-week exercise intervention. At baseline and endpoint, small-intestinal motility and liver status were assessed using MRI. Stool consistency and composition of fecal microbiome as well as mRNA expression of liver, skeletal muscle, and subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies were studied. Non-targeted metabolomics was performed on stool, fasted plasma, and urine samples.

RESULTS: : At baseline, small-intestinal motility did not correlate to liver histology scores or MRI-determined markers of liver fat, stiffness, or inflammation. However, small-intestinal motility did correlate with fecal microbiota, including Verrucomicrobia and Bacteroidetes phyla as well as 41 species such as Prevotella species incertae sedis (false discovery rate [FDR]-P < 0.2). Moreover, liver RNA sequencing revealed correlations of small-intestinal motility with liver mRNA expression of CBS (FDR-P < 0.001), linked to hydrogen sulfide production, and adipose tissue mRNA expression of SCARB1 and SCD1 (FDR-P < 0.05), involved in lipid metabolism. Several stool, plasma, and urine metabolites correlated with small-intestinal motility. Exercise had no effect.

CONCLUSIONS: : In MASLD patients, small-intestinal motility associates with gut microbiota, metabolites and mRNA expression in metabolic tissues. These findings warrant further investigation to determine causality and effect directionality. Additionally, this exploratory study demonstrates the potential of cine-MRI for fundamental small-intestinal motility research.

articles.title: Psychological Predictors of Symptom Severity in Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction: A Machine Learning Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: : Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) exhibit heterogeneous symptom burdens and psychosocial variability. We aimed to identify severity-based phenotypes via unsupervised clustering and evaluate the psychological factors independently associated with symptom severity using machine learning.

METHODS: : We analyzed 480 patients with DGBI who completed validated gastrointestinal symptom scales and a psychological battery assessing anxiety, depression, childhood trauma, social support, resilience, and Type D personality. K-means clustering (k = 2) yielded low-severity groups (n = 281) and high-severity groups (n = 199). Between-group differences were examined using Welch's t-test with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and Cohen's d. Five logistic regression models with different feature sets were compared under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Feature importance was assessed via bootstrap odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: : The high-severity group showed significantly elevated anxiety and depressive symptoms (Cohen's d = 0.55-0.92 for the Beck Anxiety Inventory [BAI]; d = 0.56-0.63 for the Beck Depression Inventory) and higher childhood trauma scores on physical abuse, sexual abuse, and physical neglect subscales after FDR correction. The BAI-only model (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.750) nearly matched the full 17-feature model (AUC = 0.753; accuracy = 71.3%; balanced accuracy = 69.9%), suggesting that the incremental contribution of multidimensional psychological profiling beyond anxiety assessment alone was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: : Anxiety symptoms, particularly somatic and physiological dimensions, are the primary psychological determinants of DGBI severity. Childhood trauma associations are likely to operate through anxiety and depression pathways. These findings support routine somatic anxiety screening in gastroenterology to identify candidates for brain-gut behavioral therapies.

articles.title: Delayed Gastric Emptying Is Associated With Progression to End-Stage Renal Disease in Diabetic Patients With Chronic Upper Gastrointestinal Symptoms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: : This study aimed to investigate whether delayed gastric emptying (GE) is associated with progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in diabetic patients with chronic upper gastrointestinal (UGI) symptoms.

METHODS: : We extracted data on demographics, UGI symptoms, GE study, and renal outcome from the medical records of diabetic patients with chronic UGI symptoms who underwent a GE study over 17 years. Renal outcome was defined as the development of ESRD. An association between delayed GE and renal outcome was investigated using a Cox proportional hazards regression model with Firth's correction.

RESULTS: : Among 515 subjects who had undergone a GE study, 100 patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes (67 females, 85 with type 2 diabetes, median age 63 years) were included. Of the 100 patients, 53 had delayed GE. During the follow-up (median, 264 weeks), 25 patients with diabetes developed ESRD. The Firth-penalized Cox regression model showed that delayed GE was significantly associated with renal outcome in diabetic patients with chronic UGI symptoms (hazard ratio 3.12; 95% confidence interval 1.34-7.97; P = 0.008). The 5-year cumulative incidence of renal outcome was approximately 9% in patients with normal GE and 35% in those with delayed GE (log-rank P = 0.021).

CONCLUSIONS: : Delayed GE was associated with progression to ESRD in diabetic patients with chronic UGI symptoms.

articles.title: Small-Intestinal Motility in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Cause, Consequence, or Bystander?
Narrative group intervention for wellbeing and violence reduction among incarcerated women: a Sicilian qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study describes an action research intervention conducted in the female ward of a Sicilian penitentiary, aimed at promoting emotional awareness, enhancing relational competencies, and fostering solidarity, with the consequent goals of reducing interpersonal violence and improving psychological wellbeing.

DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: The intervention involved 20 women over one month, employing female Greek myths as narrative tools to facilitate the elaboration of traumatic experiences and the reconstruction of personal identity. Two groups of ten participants engaged in one two-hour session per week for each group over four consecutive weeks (totaling 4 sessions / 8 h per participant). Needs assessment was conducted through individual clinical interviews.

FINDINGS: The intervention produced heightened awareness of experienced violence, improved emotional regulation, and strengthened metacognitive capacities. Participants spontaneously assumed the role of peer educators, disseminating content throughout the broader ward community. A marked improvement in the relational climate was observed, alongside emerging solidarity dynamics. Artistic artefacts served as instruments of public representation and institutional communication.

RESEARCH LIMITATIONS/IMPLICATIONS: The absence of a control group, ethically precluded in custodial settings, restricts causal inference. Outcome assessment relied primarily on qualitative observation rather than standardised psychometric instruments. Penitentiary contingencies prevented follow-up evaluation of the stability of observed changes. Findings pertain to a single Sicilian institution and may not be generalisable across diverse custodial contexts. Future research should incorporate pre- and post-intervention standardised measures, longitudinal follow-up, and comparative analysis of different narrative typologies to strengthen evidence and enhance replicability of the intervention model.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: The intervention demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of myth-based narrative group work in women's custodial settings, providing practitioners with a structured, gender-sensitive and culturally accessible psychoeducational model. The protocol - characterised by brief duration, low resource requirements, and adaptability to varied educational levels - is transferable across different institutional contexts. The spontaneous emergence of peer education dynamics further suggests that structured group interventions can amplify their impact beyond formal participants. Penitentiary professionals, psychologists and educators may adopt and adapt this approach to promote emotional regulation and violence reduction.

SOCIAL IMPLICATIONS: This study contributes to advancing gender-responsive and rehabilitative approaches within the penitentiary system, addressing the specific vulnerabilities of women in prison. By targeting interpersonal violence and promoting prosocial dynamics, the intervention supports safer detention environments and broader social reintegration. The emphasis on solidarity, emotional competence and identity reconstruction speaks to wider societal commitments to gender equality, restorative justice and the reduction of social inequalities. The cascading effects observed through peer education indicate potential for sustainable, community-level change within custodial institutions, with implications for public health and post-release social inclusion.

ORIGINALITY/VALUE: This study makes an original contribution by introducing female Greek myths as narrative mediators in a women's prison psychoeducational intervention, demonstrating their effectiveness across diverse educational levels without requiring direct trauma exposure. A further distinctive element is the spontaneous emergence of peer education dynamics, indicating the capacity of structured group work to generate systemic change beyond formal boundaries. The interdisciplinary integration of anthropological and psychological perspectives, combined with an ecologically situated action research design, provides a novel and transferable framework for evidence-informed practice in custodial settings. Combined with an ecologically situated action research design, this approach provides a novel and transferable framework for evidence-informed practice in custodial settings.

articles.title: Exercise attenuates hypertension-induced renal dysfunction alongside changes in purine metabolism and A2A and P2X7 receptor expression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension-induced renal dysfunction is associated with endothelial dysfunction and changes in purinergic signaling. Exercise training can attenuate hypertension-related disturbances in purinergic pathways, but its effects on renal purine metabolism and purinergic receptor expression remain poorly understood. We investigated these responses in L-NAME-induced hypertensive rats.

METHODS: Male Wistar rats were assigned to Control, Exercise, L-NAME, and Exercise L-NAME groups ( n  = 10/group). Hypertension was induced by chronic Nω-nitro- L -arginine methyl ester (L-NAME) administration, and exercise consisted of 6 weeks of swimming training. Blood pressure, renal nitric oxide metabolites (NOx), renal function, serum ATP, renal ATP, ADP, and AMP hydrolysis, ADA activity, and renal expression of purinergic enzymes and P1, P2X, and P2Y receptors were evaluated.

RESULTS: L-NAME increased blood pressure, serum ATP, urea, and creatinine and reduced renal NOx concentrations. Hypertensive animals showed increased CD39 and ADA expression, increased ATP hydrolysis and ADA activity, reduced A1 and A2A receptor expression, and increased P2X4 and P2X7 expression. Exercise attenuated serum ATP accumulation, changes in renal purine-metabolizing enzyme activities, and ADA expression; preserved A2A and P2X1 expression; and attenuated increases in P2X4 and P2X7 expression. Significant correlations among serum ATP, creatinine, A2A, and P2X7 expression occurred exclusively in L-NAME-treated animals.

CONCLUSIONS: L-NAME-induced hypertension is associated with renal dysfunction, changes in renal purine metabolism, and selective changes in purinergic receptor gene expression. Swimming training attenuated several of these responses and improved renal function. These findings identify renal purine metabolism and A2A and P2X7 receptor expression as potential pathways associated with exercise-induced protection that warrant further mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: What are the potentials of the different sirtuin proteins as therapeutic targets?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sirtuins (SIRT1-7) are NAD+-dependent lysine deacylase and mono-ADP ribosyl transferase enzymes that integrate metabolic status with epigenetic regulation, genome maintenance, mitochondrial homeostasis, and adaptive stress responses.
