Their dysregulation is implicated in cancer, neurodegeneration, cardiometabolic disorders, inflammation, and aging-associated pathologies, positioning the sirtuin family among the most attractive yet mechanistically complex target classes in contemporary drug discovery.

AREAS COVERED: This review critically examines the therapeutic potential of each mammalian sirtuin isoform through the combined perspectives of structural biology, disease validation, chemical tractability, and translational feasibility. Small-molecule activators and inhibitors, allosteric ligands, mechanism-based covalent modulators, and targeted protein degraders are systematically discussed, together with emerging patent activity and recent biological evidence. Literature published up to early 2026 was analyzed through comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, SciFinder, clinical trial registries, and patent databases, with particular emphasis on studies reporting isoform-selective modulation, cellular target engagement, in vivo efficacy, and translational biomarkers.

EXPERT OPINION: Sirtuin pharmacology has evolved from proof-of-concept natural products to highly selective chemical probes and event-driven modalities. Among current targets, SIRT2 and SIRT6 show the most favorable balance between biological validation and chemical tractability, whereas mitochondrial sirtuins represent a promising but still underdeveloped frontier for precision therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Comparison of Data-Driven Phenotyping Systems for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Implications for Treatment Response.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although emerging classification systems address the pathophysiological heterogeneity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the implications of these subtypes for treatment responses remain unclear. We systematically evaluated three phenotyping frameworks for stratifying responses to lifestyle management.

METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 618 patients with MASLD who received 48 weeks of guideline-based lifestyle management. The classification systems assessed were metabolic clusters-mild obesity/dyslipidemia-associated MASLD (MODM), age-related MASLD (AM), severe insulin resistance-associated MASLD, high lipoprotein(a)-associated MASLD (HLPAM), and severe mixed hyperlipidemia-associated MASLD (SMHLM); hepatic and cardiometabolic traits (control, liver-specific, and cardiometabolic); and biochemical patterns (hepatocellular, mixed, and cholestatic). The primary endpoints were responses in magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) (≥30% relative liver fat reduction), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (≥17 IU/L decrease), and liver stiffness measurements (LSM) (≥1-stage improvement in the LSM-defined fibrosis stage).

RESULTS: Metabolic clusters demonstrated significantly greater temporal stability than the hepatic and cardiometabolic trait and biochemical pattern systems (62.8% vs. 56.6% vs. 53.4%, P=0.003). The HLPAM cluster demonstrated an attenuated MRI-PDFF response (odds ratio [OR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.79), while the AM cluster showed a lower ALT response (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.18 to 0.62), and the MODM cluster displayed a superior LSM response compared to the others (all P<0.05). Moreover, the liver-specific cluster showed better MRI-PDFF, ALT, and LSM responses than the control cluster. However, biochemical patterns selectively stratified ALT responses, with the hepatocellular pattern demonstrating a greater response than the mixed and cholestatic patterns.

CONCLUSION: Metabolic cluster-based MASLD subtypes exhibited differential responses to lifestyle management, supporting the integration of metabolic subtyping into clinical algorithms to optimize management.

articles.title: Nonlinear stability phenotypes and collapse dynamics of multi-organ radiomics in total-body PET imaging: toward digital twin-oriented robustness assessment.
articles.abstract: Objective.Radiomics analysis in positron emission tomography (PET) offers a high-dimensional representation of tissue characteristics, yet its reliability is limited by sensitivity to acquisition perturbations, particularly dose reduction. This study aims to introduce a nonlinear stability phenotyping framework to characterize dose-response behavior of multi-organ radiomics and evaluate their potential relevance for future digital twin-oriented applications.Approach.A multi-center dataset of 550 total-body PET scans was analyzed. Dose reduction was simulated using list-mode subsampling (dose reduction factor - DRF = 2-100). A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted per organ. Stability was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficient and summarized as stability fractions. Nonlinear models were fitted to organ- and feature-level trajectories. Stability phenotypes and critical thresholds were derived, along with organ-level instability metrics.Main results.Radiomics stability exhibited strongly nonlinear, organ-dependent behavior. Feature-level analysis identified frequent sigmoid-associated collapse patterns with high descriptive model fits (R2> 0.90). The liver showed the highest instability burden (30.8% unstable features), followed by esophagus and kidneys (18%-20%). Texture features were the primary source of instability, whereas shape features remained robust. Organ-level trajectories demonstrated heterogeneous responses, with some organs maintaining high stability (0.80-0.95) across DRFs, while others showed sharp declines (down to 0.64). Linear (stable) behavior dominated at the organ level, though masking underlying nonlinear feature dynamics.Significance.Radiomics stability in total-body PET follows nonlinear, phenotype-driven dynamics with identifiable tipping points and organ-specific sensitivity. The proposed framework provides a behavior-based approach for evaluating radiomics robustness and supports the selection of reliable features and organs for robust quantitative imaging and may inform future digital twin-oriented applications.

articles.title: Parent perspectives on the potential use of smart inhalers for asthma management in children: a qualitative interview study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Achieving adequate adherence to preventer medication remains a challenge in the management of pediatric asthma. A minimum of 75% adherence is recommended to achieve adequate clinical control, however actual adherence rates are often lower and are influenced by the unpredictability of family life and competing demands. Smart inhalers aim to support adherence to preventer medications by monitoring use and providing medication reminders, as well as tracking reliever use. This study explored the perceptions of parents of children aged 5-9 years with recent uncontrolled asthma regarding the potential usefulness of smart inhalers to manage their children's asthma, and perceived barriers and facilitators to their use.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom with parents residing in New South Wales, Australia. Interviews explored parents' perspectives about barriers to asthma management, awareness and perceived need for smart inhalers, desired features and functionalities, attitudes toward data sharing, perceived support requirements and cost considerations. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive analysis approach. Ten parents participated (children aged 5-8); none had previously used a smart inhaler to manage their child's asthma.

RESULTS: Overall attitudes toward smart inhalers were positive. Four primary themes were identified: perceived benefits of smart inhalers, including access to reliable medication data to share with healthcare providers; barriers to adoption, including concerns about technology difficulties; cost considerations with affordability influencing the likelihood of uptake; and implementation needs including the need for support for initial set up.

CONCLUSIONS: Parents generally viewed smart inhalers as a promising tool for managing childhood asthma. Study findings suggest that successful implementation will require consideration of cost, ease of use, and adequate support for use.

articles.title: Cumulative Exposure to High Systemic Inflammation and Incident Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to examine the association between cumulative exposure to systemic inflammation and incident metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis in mainland China.

METHODS: This study used data from an ongoing longitudinal physical examination cohort. We enrolled 9,725 participants (aged ≥18 years) who completed three consecutive biennial health examinations between 2018 and 2022, with complete follow-up in 2024. Systemic inflammation was quantified using three established biomarkers: neutrophil count (NC), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII). Cumulative exposure was calculated from baseline to the third examination by multiplying biomarker values by the time (years) between consecutive examinations. The primary outcome was MASLD development at the fourth examination, and advanced liver fibrosis among incident MASLD cases was further evaluated using the fibrosis-4 index (≥2.67). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to explore the associations between cumulative exposure to inflammation and MASLD incidence and fibrosis severity.

RESULTS: At the fourth examination, 939 incident MASLD cases (9.66%) were identified. In fully adjusted models, participants in the highest quartile of cumulative NC exposure had 2.20-fold higher odds of MASLD (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.81 to 2.69; P for trend <0.001) than those in the lowest quartile. Similarly, the highest quartile of cumulative SII exposure had 1.32-fold higher odds (95% CI, 1.09 to 1.59; P for trend=0.003). Conversely, cumulative NLR exposure showed no significant association with MASLD incidence. The addition of cumulative NC or SII to the basic model comprising traditional risk factors improved the ability to predict MASLD. Furthermore, among participants who developed MASLD, the highest quartile of cumulative NC (odds ratio [OR], 4.74; 95% CI, 1.76 to 12.75; P for trend <0.001) and cumulative SII (OR, 3.74; 95% CI, 1.48 to 9.45; P for trend=0.006), but not cumulative NLR, were significantly associated with an elevated risk of advanced liver fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: Greater NC exposure and excessive SII exposure were each independently associated with incident MASLD and related advanced liver fibrosis. Whether reducing inflammation can help prevent MASLD requires further investigation.

articles.title: Effects of Different Exercise Modalities on Interleukin-6, Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor, and Cognitive Function in Obese Older Women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the effects of different exercise modalities on body composition, interleukin-6 (IL-6), and cognitive function in obese older women.

METHODS: A total of 60 obese women aged ≥65 years were randomly assigned to four groups: control (CON), aerobic aquatic exercise (AAE), aerobic dance exercise (ADE), or combined aerobic and resistance exercise (AE+RE). Of these, 54 participants were included in the final analysis.

RESULTS: Significant time-by-group interactions were observed for body weight (BW), body fat percentage (%BF), IL-6, and Korean version of the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE-K) scores. The AAE and ADE groups showed significant reductions in BW and %BF, and fat-free mass increased only in the AAE group (P<0.01). Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) increased in the AAE and ADE groups (both P<0.01), whereas IL-6 decreased in both groups (ADE, P<0.05; AAE, P<0.01). MMSE-K scores improved in all exercise groups, with scores in the AE+RE and AAE groups significantly higher than those in the CON group (P<0.001 and P<0.01, respectively).

CONCLUSION: Moderate-intensity aquatic and dance-based aerobic exercise over 12 weeks improved both metabolic health and cognitive function in obese older women and was accompanied by reductions in IL-6 and increases in BDNF.

articles.title: Relationship between Vitamin D Status and the Risk of Obesity without Diagnosed Metabolic Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between daily vitamin D (VD) intake and the risk of healthy obesity remains controversial.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Wanfang Database, China Science and Technology Periodical Database, and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews were systematically searched for published observational studies up to January 2025. Ultimately, 74 studies were included, and pooled estimates were obtained using RevMan version 5.3. Subgroup analyses were conducted by age, VD detection method and assessment criteria, and obesity grade.

RESULTS: Among 5,283 articles identified, 74 studies with 110,838 individuals met the inclusion criteria. Serum/plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations were negatively associated with the risk of healthy obesity (mean difference=-3.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], -4.70 to -3.27). Significant differences between the obesity and control groups were observed in all subgroups except those using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) detection. Moreover, the prevalence of VD deficiency was higher in participants with obesity than in controls (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.73 to 2.36). This difference was significant in all subgroups except those in which VD deficiency was defined as a concentration below 10 or 12 ng/mL. Furthermore, VD insufficiency was positively associated with the risk of obesity (OR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.32). However, significant differences were observed only in specific subgroups: adolescents, participants with mild obesity, and those assessed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay or LC-MS/MS detection methods.

CONCLUSION: These findings indicated that VD status was inversely associated with the risk of healthy obesity, irrespective of age and obesity grade. Inconsistencies may be influenced by VD detection methods and assessment criteria.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury in pregnancy is associated with increased risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes: an integrated health system study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-related acute kidney injury (PrAKI) is an uncommon but serious complication associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with limited data in high-resource settings.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 29 586 deliveries at Mayo Clinic hospitals between 2017 and 2022. PrAKI was defined using Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) creatinine criteria. Maternal characteristics, nephrotoxin exposure, clinical interventions, and neonatal outcomes were compared between patients with and without PrAKI.

RESULTS: PrAKI occurred in 341 patients (1.15%). Compared with controls, PrAKI was associated with higher rates of chronic hypertension (28.7% vs 5.2%), cesarean delivery (68.5% vs 35.1%), intensive care unit (ICU) admission (59.1% vs 6.2%), and nephrotoxin exposure (58.7% vs 31.6%) (all P < .0001). Dialysis was required in 7.1% of patients with PrAKI, with 1.17% remaining dependent at discharge and 0.88% at 30 and 90 days; no control patients required dialysis. Neonates of mothers with PrAKI had higher rates of prematurity and neonatal ICU (NICU) admission (48.7% vs 9.8%; P < .0001). Maternal mortality was rare.

CONCLUSIONS: PrAKI is a marker of severe maternal illness and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although most patients recover kidney function, a subset develop persistent dysfunction. Early identification, cautious use of nephrotoxic medications, and structured postpartum follow-up are essential.

articles.title: Per-class conformal risk control for multi-label ECG classification: achieving clinically-justified false negative rate guarantees.
articles.abstract: Objective. Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) classifiers require uncertainty procedures that address class-specific clinical risk in intrinsically multi-label data.Approach. We propose per-class risk-controlling prediction sets for multi-label ECG classification. For each diagnostic class, binary false-negative-rate (FNR) loss is calibrated with a one-sided exact-binomial upper confidence bound. The nine disease-specific targets are controlled simultaneously at 95% family-wise confidence using Bonferroni allocation. The final operating threshold is the more inclusive of the exact-binomial threshold and a conservative reference threshold derived from a concentration bound; this safeguard uses calibration data only and cannot weaken the exact guarantee.Main results. We evaluated the method on PTB-XL (21 388 retained recordings) and Chapman-Shaoxing (10 199 retained recordings), using a patient-disjoint PTB-XL split and fitting-partition-only normalisation. The proposed method met all 9/9 prespecified disease-specific FNR targets on held-out test sets and produced non-vacuous simultaneous exact-binomial guarantees for all nine targets; uniform standard conformal prediction met 5/9. Test FNR was 0.0% for myocardial infarction (exact 95% upper bound 0.35%, at 80.3% FPR), 1.0% for ST/T changes, and 0.3% for atrial fibrillation; the high-sensitivity operating point is purchased with substantially reduced specificity. Under PTB-XL-to-Chapman shift, macro class coverage fell from 94.3% to 45.5%, demonstrating that the guarantees do not transport without local recalibration.Significance. Exact-binomial per-class risk control provides a transparent high-sensitivity operating point for ECG triage while making its specificity, prediction-set-size, calibration-support, and exchangeability limitations explicit.

articles.title: Hydrogel as a drug delivery systems for bacteriophage therapy: overcoming biological barriers in multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
articles.abstract: The emergence of multidrug resistant (MDR) bacterial infections has intensified the need for effective antimicrobial strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. Bacteriophage therapy offers a promising approach against antibiotic resistant pathogens; however, its clinical translation is limited by immune clearance, enzymatic degradation, poor stability, insufficient retention at infection sites, and limited penetration into bacterial biofilms. Hydrogel based delivery systems provide versatile biomaterial platforms to overcome these barriers by protecting bacteriophages, enabling localized administration, prolonging residence time, and controlling phage release. This review critically examines the biological barriers limiting bacteriophage therapy and recent advances in hydrogel engineering to improve phage encapsulation, stability, release behavior, and antibacterial efficacy. Key hydrogel properties, including biocompatibility, porosity, swelling, degradability, tissue adhesiveness, and mechanical strength, are discussed in relation to phage retention and delivery performance. Recent applications in chronic wound infections, biofilm associated infections, surgical site infections, and other MDR bacterial diseases are evaluated, with emphasis on localized antimicrobial treatment. Furthermore, challenges in formulation development, large scale manufacturing, regulatory approval, and clinical translation are explored. By integrating current evidence on hydrogel design, phage delivery, and therapeutic performance, this review identifies critical considerations for developing effective and clinically applicable hydrogel based bacteriophage delivery systems against MDR bacterial infections.

articles.title: Advantages and Critical Reappraisal of New Clinical Obesity Definition Proposed by Lancet Commission.
articles.abstract: Obesity has traditionally been defined by body mass index (BMI), a pragmatic but biologically limited measure that fails to capture adiposity distribution, tissue dysfunction, and heterogeneity in disease risk. To address these limitations, a recent Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology Commission proposed a disease-oriented redefinition of obesity, distinguishing clinical obesity-excess adiposity causing organ dysfunction or functional impairment-from preclinical obesity, characterized by excess adiposity without established dysfunction. This shift has important implications for diagnosis, epidemiology, and health policy. In this review, we critically appraise the conceptual framework, emerging evidence, and implementation challenges of the new Lancet Commission definition of clinical obesity. Population-based studies from diverse regions consistently demonstrate marked discordance between BMI-defined and clinical obesity, with clinical obesity showing stronger associations with cardiometabolic disease, mortality, functional limitation, and cancer risk. These findings highlight the limitations of universal BMI thresholds, particularly in Asian populations with a predisposition to visceral adiposity at lower BMI levels. We compare the Lancet Commission framework with existing staging systems, including the Edmonton Obesity Staging System and the European Association for the Study of Obesity framework, and identify key challenges related to causal attribution, binary classification, scalability, and ethnic adaptation. Finally, we propose a refined, population-sensitive and pragmatic approach that conceptualizes preclinical and clinical obesity as stages along a trajectory, incorporates ethnicity-adapted adiposity thresholds, and emphasizes readily available clinical criteria for determining dysfunction and disease. The resulting definition of clinical obesity should support more precise and equitable obesity care.

articles.title: The Future of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery in the Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Era: Has the Scalpel Become Obsolete?
articles.abstract: Obesity remains a growing global health crisis, affecting nearly one billion adults worldwide and substantially increasing the risk of cardiometabolic disease, malignancy, and premature mortality. Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) has evolved into an effective and durable treatment for severe obesity, providing sustained weight loss and significant remission of obesity-related comorbidities (i.e., type 2 diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular disease). Despite dramatic improvements in safety, efficacy, and long-term outcomes over time, MBS remains markedly underutilized, reaching fewer than 1% of eligible patients. Persistent barriers include limited patient and provider awareness, misconceptions regarding surgical risk, and significant disparities in access to care. Concurrently, the rapid adoption of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) has transformed the medical management of obesity, offering effective pharmacologic weight loss but raising questions regarding their impact on MBS utilization, durability, and cost-effectiveness. Emerging evidence demonstrates that while MBS produces greater and more durable weight loss than GLP-1 RAs alone, these therapies need not be competitive. Rather, GLP-1 RAs may serve as 'neoadjuvant' treatment to optimize surgical candidacy or as adjunctive treatment for inadequate weight loss or postoperative weight regain. This review synthesizes contemporary data on MBS procedures, outcomes, disparities in access, and evolving perceptions of obesity treatment in the GLP-1 RA era. We propose a chronic weight management model that integrates pharmacotherapy, surgery, and multidisciplinary care along a continuous treatment spectrum. Positioning MBS and GLP-1 RAs as complementary modalities within individualized care pathways may improve long-term outcomes, expand access, and better address the complex, chronic nature of obesity.

articles.title: Mild, Fast, and General Biocatalytic Deprotection Strategies for Automated Fluorine-18 Positron Emission Tomography Radiotracer Synthesis.
articles.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) has become an essential tool in nuclear medicine, driving the continuous development of new radiotracers. Owing to the short half-life of fluorine-18 (110 min), radiotracer production requires fast, robust, and fully automated synthetic protocols. Reactive functional groups present on precursor molecules must be protected to prevent competition during radiofluorination, with deprotection typically achieved under harsh chemical conditions that may compromise automation and lead to partial molecular degradation. Herein, we report a general biocatalytic deprotection strategy based on porcine liver esterase (PLE) as a mild and efficient alternative to conventional chemical methods. Three protecting groups (valerate, pivaloyloxymethyl and pivaloyl ethylidene carbamate) were selected to enable the PLE-deprotection of a broad range of functional groups found in radiotracers and drugs (alcohols, phenols, carboxylic acids, amines, anilines, sulfonamides). The PivEC protective group of amines, anilines and sulfonamides was specifically developed for allowing an esterase deprotection. This approach was validated across a broad substrate scope and was successfully automated on ORA-Neptis modules for clinically relevant PET tracers, including [18F]FMISO, [18F]CABS13, and [18F]Nifene. This work establishes enzymatic deprotection as a versatile and practical strategy for PET scan application.

articles.title: Post-transplant follow-up for kidney transplant recipients: a systematic review of clinical practice guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney transplantation is the treatment of choice for kidney failure, but long-term allograft survival remains challenging. Post-transplant follow-up is essential for monitoring allograft function and managing complications. Although clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) share broad principles, they differ in surveillance timing, frequency, and content. This review compared CPGs for kidney transplant recipients (KTRs), focusing on methodological quality, evidence base, and recommendations.

METHODS: Journal databases, guideline repositories, and professional association websites were searched for CPGs published between January 2009 and October 2025. Methodological quality was assessed using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument. Recommendations on follow-up frequency, monitoring content, and implementation were compared.

RESULTS: Seven CPGs were included. All recommended intensive early monitoring followed by progressively less frequent surveillance. Differences were most evident in long-term follow-up intervals, protocol kidney allograft biopsy, immunological monitoring, and implementation tools. Most guidelines scored highly in "Scope and Purpose" and "Clarity of Presentation" but lower in "Applicability." KDIGO had the highest methodological quality, although its earlier publication may limit incorporation of recent evidence and evolving care models.

CONCLUSIONS: Guidelines agree on general principles but differ in operational recommendations because of variations in resources, healthcare systems, methods, and evidence interpretation. Most follow-up frequency recommendations rely on low-quality evidence or expert consensus. Clinicians should follow local guidance, use international guidance such as KDIGO when local guidance is unavailable, and individualize follow-up according to immunological risk, allograft status, comorbidities, adherence, patient preferences, and resources, while future revisions incorporate emerging evidence from pragmatic studies.

articles.title: Histopathologic spectrum of kidney diseases in Ethiopia: a 3-year retrospective single-center study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence, prevalence, and types of kidney disease in African nations is understudied. Treating and managing acute kidney disease is often approached empirically rather than by kidney biopsy, and underlying causes of kidney failure are largely unknown. Understanding the causes of kidney dysfunction is hampered by a lack of modern techniques and equipment as well as a paucity of well-trained and experienced medical professionals, especially in pathology.

METHODS: This study examines the types of kidney disease in biopsies from adult and pediatric patients seen from 01/09/2017 to 05/09/2020 at a single medical center in Ethiopia, and compares biopsy diagnosis with and without access to immunofluorescence (IF) technology.

RESULTS: The total number of adequate biopsies was 211 (148 native light microscopy (LM)-only, 48 native LM and IF, 15 transplant); 22 (10.4%) of the 211 adequate biopsies were from pediatric patients. Overall, lupus nephritis was the most frequent diagnosis, rendered in 16.8% of native kidney biopsies, followed by minimal change disease in 12.2% of cases, membranoproliferative-pattern glomerulonephritis (GN) in 11.2%, diffuse proliferative GN in 10.7%, and crescentic GN in 8.2%. Several conditions, including complement-related glomerulopathy, IgA nephropathy, and light chain cast nephropathy were only identified following the introduction of IF microscopy.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings provide a small registry of biopsy results and emphasize the importance of advanced techniques in the diagnosis of kidney disease.

articles.title: Association between frailty status and eGFR slope change after initiation of finerenone in chronic kidney disease.
Sex differences in detection of acute coronary syndrome culprit lesion using conventional and AI-enhanced coronary CT angiography.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) exhibits marked sex-related differences in clinical presentation and underlying pathophysiology. However, whether these differences translate into variations in culprit lesion prediction remains unclear. We investigated the sex-specific performance of conventional coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and artificial intelligence-enabled quantitative coronary plaque and haemodynamic assessment (AI-QCPHA) for ACS culprit detection.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this sub-study of the EMERALD II trial (NCT03591328), patients with ACS who underwent CCTA 1 month to 3 years prior to the event were analysed. Culprit and non-culprit lesions were defined by invasive coronary angiography at the time of ACS. Diagnostic performance of obstructive stenosis (Coronary Artery Disease-Reporting and Data System ≥ 3) and high-risk plaque (HRP) criteria was compared between women and men. Information gain-based feature selection identified sex-specific AI-QCPHA best predictors across five feature clusters, and their incremental predictive value was evaluated using receiver operating characteristics reported as area under the curve (AUC). A total of 351 patients (90 women, 261 men) with 2451 lesions were included. Conventional CCTA performed similarly across sexes for obstructive stenosis, whereas HRP differed by sex. AI-QCPHA identified the same best features for ACS culprit prediction in both sexes, and integration of these features improved discriminatory performance beyond conventional CCTA (women AUC 0.84 vs. 0.78, P = 0.002; men 0.82 vs. 0.75, P < 0.001). Among individual predictors, delta fractional flow reserve from coronary computed tomography angiography yielded the highest discriminatory performance in both women and men.

CONCLUSION: AI-QCPHA enhances culprit lesion prediction in obstructive ACS beyond conventional CCTA in both sexes, supporting its potential role for improved culprit lesion discrimination.
