articles.title: Comparison of the 2016 ASE/EACVI and 2025 ASE guidelines for assessing left atrial pressure in patients with normal left ventricular ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The assessment of diastolic dysfunction in patients is clinically challenging. The 2025 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) guidelines for assessment of left atrial pressure (LAP) were published recently and their diagnostic performance needs further validation.This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the 2025 ASE guidelines for assessment of LAP and to compare it with that of the 2016 ASE/EACVI guidelines.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This study prospectively collected echocardiographic data and LAP measurements from 119 patients. Patients were categorized into elevated left atrial pressure (ELAP) (LAP > 15 mm Hg) and normal (LAP ≤ 15 mm Hg) groups. Both the 2016 ASE/EACVI and 2025 ASE guidelines were applied to assess diastolic function using echocardiographic parameters. The 2025 guidelines demonstrated significantly higher sensitivity (86.4% [75.7-93.6] vs. 54.0% [39.3-68.2]) and feasibility (100% [98.0-100] vs. 78.1% [72.2-84.0]) but lower specificity (81.8% [73.8-88.2] vs. 94.8% [88.3-98.3]) and positive predictive value (72.2% [63.7-79.3] vs. 84.4% [68.9-92.9]) compared with the 2016 guidelines. Negative predictive value (91.7% [85.6-95.3] vs. 79.8% [74.5-84.3]) and overall accuracy (83.4% [77.3-88.5] vs. 80.8% [73.5-86.9]) improved modestly.

CONCLUSION: The 2025 guidelines significantly improved the feasibility of assessing LAP and enhanced ELAP detection rates and applicability while maintaining comparable accuracy.

articles.title: Coffee consumption and chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Coffee is one of the most widely consumed beverages globally. Caffeine has been linked to antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifibrotic, and anticancer effects. However, the relationship between caffeine consumption and the risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) has yielded conflicting findings. Research on the health effects of caffeine relies mainly on exploratory observational studies, which may be affected by biases such as residual confounding. Variations in behaviour, health status, intake, and metabolism also influence outcomes. A comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms and population-specific factors mediating the impact of caffeine on kidney health is essential. In this article, we describe the metabolism and mechanism of action of caffeine, as well as its potential adverse effects. We synthesize current evidence and clarify the complex relationship between caffeine, CKD, and cardiovascular disease. Current evidence suggests that moderate caffeine intake is probably safe in CKD and may be potentially beneficial. Stronger evidence is needed before robust recommendations can be made for clinical practice.

articles.title: The co-occurrence of sepsis and left coronary artery-right ventricular fistula with a giant coronary aneurysm: contrast echocardiography and transcatheter closure.
KDM1A regulates nephron progenitor programs and is associated with human kidney disease risk.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci associated with kidney function, but linking non-coding variants to causal effector genes remains challenging. By integrating fine-mapped GWAS data from 2.27 million individuals with kidney expression and epigenomic datasets, we identified KDM1A as a top-prioritized gene at a kidney function locus. KDM1A is broadly expressed across nephron segments in mouse and human kidneys and is consistently upregulated in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: We generated lineage-specific Kdm1a knockout mice targeting nephron progenitors (Six2-Cre) or differentiated tubular epithelial cells (Cdh16/Ksp1-Cre). Renal structure and function were assessed at baseline and following adenine-induced injury or unilateral ureteral obstruction using histology, immunoblotting, and gene expression analyses. Pharmacologic inhibition of KDM1A was evaluated in embryonic kidney explant cultures.

RESULTS: Nephron progenitor-specific deletion of Kdm1a resulted in severe developmental defects, including nephron loss, cystic degeneration, tubular atrophy, and early interstitial fibrosis. Mutant kidneys exhibited suppression of progenitor and segment-specific epithelial programs, loss of solute transporter expression, and derepression of developmental signaling pathways, including Notch and Wnt, accompanied by apoptosis and inflammation. In contrast, deletion of Kdm1a in differentiated tubular epithelial cells preserved baseline renal structure and function and did not modify fibrotic responses to injury. Pharmacologic inhibition of KDM1A during kidney development phenocopied genetic loss and led to accumulation of H3K4 methylation.

CONCLUSIONS: KDM1A is a genetically supported, developmentally essential chromatin regulator required for nephron differentiation but dispensable in differentiated tubular epithelium. Its reactivation in CKD highlights a context-dependent epigenetic role and cautions against nonspecific KDM1A inhibition..

articles.title: Bayesian methods in nephrology: applications in adaptive trials, dynamic risk prediction, pharmacokinetics, and causal inference.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Bayesian statistics is gaining momentum in biomedical research, offering a flexible and intuitive framework for integrating prior knowledge, managing uncertainty, and informing decision-making. In nephrology, a field marked by complex pathophysiology, small patient populations, and evolving therapeutic landscapes, Bayesian approaches may provide critical advantages over traditional statistical methods. Bayesian methodologies may help reshape nephrology by improving trial efficiency, refining diagnostic and prognostic precision, and strengthening causal inference. We conducted a comprehensive narrative review of peer-reviewed literature on Bayesian applications in nephrology, highlighting studies in adaptive clinical trial designs, dynamic risk prediction models, network meta-analyses, pharmacokinetic modeling, and Bayesian Mendelian randomization approaches, including Bayesian model averaging frameworks. Bayesian adaptive designs enabled more efficient and ethically sound trials, such as the WIndow-of-opportunity clinical trial platform for evaluation of novel treatment strategies in REnal cell cancer (WIRE) platform study in renal cell carcinoma. In diagnostics and prognostics, Bayesian models allowed individualized inference from dynamic data, as demonstrated in estimated glomerular filtration rate trajectory analyses and mortality prediction. Bayesian network meta-analyses improved comparative effectiveness research by incorporating probabilistic treatment rankings, while Bayesian frameworks strengthened causal inference through methods like Mendelian randomization (MR) -Bayesian Model Averaging and Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression. Bayesian approaches have emerging applications in nephrology, promoting a probabilistic framework that enhances the interpretation of complex clinical and research data and supports more individualized patient care. Their integration into both research and clinical practice requires investment in education and training, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the development of accessible analytical tools. Embracing Bayesian methods is likely to play an important role in advancing precision medicine and improving patient outcomes in nephrology.

articles.title: Admission kidney tubule biomarkers do not predict acute kidney injury or in-hospital adverse events in acute heart failure.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Serum creatinine frequently increases during hospitalizations for acute heart failure (AHF) meeting criteria for acute kidney injury (AKI), but the significance of this increase is variable. We evaluated whether admission levels of kidney tubule and cardiac biomarkers are associated with increases in serum creatinine and adverse in-hospital events.

METHODS: In a nested case-control study, we identified 214 cases with at least stage 1 AKI defined by the 2012 Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes criteria within 7 days of admission in the Acute Kidney Injury Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin Evaluation of Symptomatic Heart Failure Study and matched with 214 controls who did not experience AKI. The primary outcome was the development of AKI within the first 7 days; secondary outcomes were the development of severe AKI (stages 2 or 3) and a composite of adverse in-hospital events. Associations of 6 blood and 14 urine biomarkers were assessed with logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: Individuals were 71 ± 13 years; 64% were men; with median admission creatinine 1.3 (interquartile range 1.0-1.8) mg/dl. Among AKI cases, 181 (85%), 16 (7%), and 17 (8%) were stages 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Compared to the lowest tertile, only the highest tertiles of fractional excretion of sodium [FENa ≥ 3.65%; odds ratio (OR) 1.7, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.0-2.9] and urinary monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (≥433 ng/g; OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.0-2.8) were associated with AKI risk, though discrimination was poor (ROC-AUC < 0.60). Neither was associated with severe AKI. Only elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (≥932 pg/ml) predicted the composite adverse in-hospital event (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.2-4.2).

CONCLUSION: Kidney tubule and cardiac biomarkers at admission for AHF are not associated with risk for increases in creatinine or adverse in-hospital events reaffirming that creatinine changes in AHF are largely functional in nature.

articles.title: Myocardial calcification in septic shock: the porcelain heart.
Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging characteristics of a cardiac myeloid sarcoma with superimposed thrombus.
Torque Teno virus is predictive for malignancies after kidney transplantation.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Malignancy, driven by the effects of immunosuppression, is a major complication following kidney transplantation. The widespread and non-pathogenic Torque Teno virus (TTV) has emerged as a surrogate of the immune status of its host, with prior studies linking TTV load to insufficient and excessive immunosuppression and thus indirectly to graft rejection and infection. Its relationship to malignancy in kidney transplant recipients is unknown.

METHODS: This prospective observational single center study evaluated 428 patients who underwent kidney transplantation between 2016 and 2019 at the General Hospital of Vienna, Austria. TTV was measured by quantitative polymerase chain reaction in plasma and the primary outcome was the incidence of the first malignancy during years 2-5 post-transplant.

RESULTS: In total, 53 patients developed malignancy (53% cutaneous keratinocyte cancer). The mean log10 TTV load during months 4 to 12 post-transplant (logTTVm4-12) was associated with increased malignancy risk with a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.25 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.02-1.54] in unadjusted analysis and 1.20 (95% CI 0.97-1.48) after adjustment for age, sex, smoking, and body mass index. In a subgroup, the result remained consistent after additional adjustment for tacrolimus and mycophenolate exposure (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.03-1.67). Patients with logTTVm4-12 >8, a cut-off we previously proposed to indicate infection risk, had an HR of 2.10 (95% CI 1.22-3.60).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that a high TTV load-indicating a state of intense immunosuppression-predicts malignancy after kidney transplantation. Monitoring TTV as a marker of immunosuppression may offer a novel strategy for personalizing immunosuppressive therapy and reducing cancer risk.

articles.title: Extrarenal disease in ANCA-associated vasculitis: challenges and evolving therapeutic strategies on behalf of the Immunonephrology Working Group (IWG) of the ERA.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) are systemic small-vessel necrotizing vasculitides, including microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). Genetic factors, particularly human leukocyte antigen variants, contribute to disease susceptibility and define distinct myeloperoxidase- and proteinase 3-associated phenotypes. This review summarizes current understanding of organ-specific manifestations, therapeutic advances, and prognostic determinants of AAV, with particular relevance for nephrologists. Kidney involvement is common, particularly in MPA, whereas GPA and EGPA more frequently present with extrarenal manifestations. Pulmonary involvement is also frequent, ranging from alveolar haemorrhage and interstitial lung disease (ILD) in MPA to granulomatous nodules and airway disease in GPA, while asthma dominates in EGPA. Other frequent manifestations include ear, nose, and throat (ENT), peripheral nervous system, cutaneous, and constitutional manifestations, with ENT activity and non-haemorrhagic respiratory manifestations correlating with relapse risk. Current treatment emphasizes rituximab or cyclophosphamide with reduced-dose glucocorticoids for induction, avacopan for glucocorticoid-sparing strategies, and rituximab for maintenance. Avacopan has shown benefits beyond renal outcomes. Furthermore, anti-interleukin-5 therapies have recently been approved for the treatment of EGPA. Contrarily, ILD remains a therapeutic challenge, with limited evidence for antifibrotic agents. AAV patients are at high risk of infections, thromboembolism, and malignancy, influenced by both disease activity and treatment exposure. Mortality remains high, driven mainly by infections, with kidney and lung involvement serving as major prognostic determinants. For nephrologists, early recognition of extrarenal manifestations, vigilance for relapse beyond the kidney, and multidisciplinary collaboration are crucial for optimizing long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Sexual dimorphism and age effects in CKD and type 2 diabetes in the CONFIDENCE trial.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Concurrent initiation of finerenone and empagliflozin can lower albuminuria more than component therapies at Day 180 in participants with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D ). We evaluated baseline clinical characteristics and longitudinal changes in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) across age and sex cohorts.

METHODS: In CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), participants with T2D, CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] 30-90 ml/min/1.73 m2), and albuminuria (UACR 100 to <5000 mg/g) on stable doses of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors were randomized 1:1:1 to empagliflozin 10 mg/day, finerenone 10 or 20 mg/day, or both. We stratified participants by age quartiles (≤60 years, 61-68 years, 69-74 years , >74 years) and sex. Outcomes included % change in UACR from baseline over time and incidences of key adverse events.

RESULTS: Increasing age was associated with higher baseline prevalence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and lower eGFR. Older age was a significant predictor of UACR reduction, with -10.2% (95% CI: -15.5, -4.6) incremental change per 10-year age increase at Day 180 (P for age effect = 0.001). Women exhibited an 18.6% (95% CI: 6.3, 29.2) greater UACR reduction at Day 180 than men (P for sex effect = 0.008). These effects were independent of treatment; there was no interaction between age (P-interaction = 0.28) or sex (P-interaction = 0.46) on combination therapy treatment effect. Safety outcomes were consistent across all demographics.

CONCLUSIONS: The UACR-lowering response of finerenone and empagliflozin scaled linearly with age (10% per decade) and sex (∼20% more among women). The benefit of combination therapy was independent of age and sex.

articles.title: Acute declines in kidney function with thiazide plus loop diuretics versus loop diuretics alone in acute decompensated heart failure.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: The association between acute declines in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) among individuals admitted for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and cardiovascular outcomes has been inconsistent. Our objective was to examine whether eGFR decline and the timing of these declines are associated with mortality and a composite outcome of mortality or heart failure (HF) hospitalization.

METHODS: We used data from the CLOROTIC trial, which randomized patients admitted for ADHF to thiazide versus placebo. We examined % eGFR change at 2 days (n = 225) and at 4 days (n = 218) after randomization. Multivariable Cox models were used to evaluate the association between % eGFR change and a primary outcome of mortality and secondary outcome of composite of mortality or HF hospitalization.

RESULTS: Median % eGFR change was -9.7% (IQR -22.1, 5.4) and -14.4% (-25.1, 7.8) in the thiazide arm at 2 and 4 days, respectively, compared to -0.3% (-7.5, 10.1) and 0% (-10.0, 16.2) in the placebo arm at 2 and 4 days, respectively. Over a median 3-month follow-up, of those with 2-day eGFR change available, 41 (18%) patients died and 98 (44%) met the composite outcome, and of those with 4-day eGFR change available, 38 (17.4%) died and 95 (43.6%) met the composite outcome. The eGFR decline at 2 days was not associated with risk of mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.96 [95% CI 0.47, 1.97] and HR = 0.89 [0.37, 2.10] per 30% eGFR decline in the thiazide and placebo arms, respectively). The eGFR decline at 4 days was not associated with risk of mortality in the thiazide arm (HR = 0.86 [0.48, 1.55] per 30% eGFR decline) nor in the placebo (HR = 1.63 [0.82, 3.26] per 30% eGFR decline). Associations were similar for the composite outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients admitted for ADHF and randomized to thiazide versus placebo, early acute declines in eGFR had no association with increased risk of cardiovascular outcomes.

REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT01647932; EudraCT Number: 2013-001852-36.

articles.title: Is sex by age interaction the missing factor in acute kidney injury epidemiology?
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a multifactorial syndrome associated with increased morbidity and mortality during hospitalization and in the long-term follow-up. Emerging evidence suggests that biological sex and age may influence kidney damage and recovery; however, the specific role of these biological variables on AKI outcomes remains to be fully elucidated. This retrospective study aimed to explore the impact of sex and age on AKI epidemiology and outcomes in a large cohort of hospitalized adults.

METHODS: We analyzed clinical and administrative data from 87 087 adult patients admitted to two Italian university hospitals between 2016 and 2019. Excluding patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease (CKD), we assessed AKI based on Kidney Diseases Improving Global Outcomes criteria using serum creatinine trends during hospitalization. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), hospital stay, and outcomes were evaluated, with a focus on sex-based comparisons.

RESULTS: AKI occurred in 20.6% of patients, with a higher incidence in females (21.4%) than males (19.8%). Female patients were older and had lower eGFR at hospital admission, less incidence of diabetes and CKD, but a more frequent diagnosis of congestive heart failure. While stage 3 AKI was more common in males, undiagnosed AKI was more frequent in females with stage 1 AKI. Of note, age-stratified analysis revealed a dynamic sex-related risk: AKI incidence was higher in males in younger age groups, whereas females showed a progressively higher incidence in the oldest age quartiles. However, outcomes such as mortality, Intensive Care Unit admission, and length of hospital stay were worse in the older male AKI population.

CONCLUSIONS: AKI incidence and in-hospital outcomes differ between males and females in an age-dependent manner. These findings emphasize the relevance of considering sex by age interaction when investigating AKI epidemiology and outcomes.

articles.title: Diabetes mellitus attenuates response to anti-CD20 therapy in primary membranous nephropathy despite equivalent B-cell depletion.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Primary membranous nephropathy (MN) and diabetes mellitus (DM) are common comorbidities, yet the impact of DM on the response to anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy in MN remains unclear. We hypothesized that despite comparable B-cell depletion, MN patients with comorbid DM would exhibit a reduced treatment response compared to nondiabetic MN patients.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included adults with primary MN who received at least one complete course of anti-CD20 antibody therapy. Propensity score matching (1:2) was applied based on age, sex, baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate, urinary protein, and PLA2R antibody status. The primary outcome was remission (complete or partial) of proteinuria at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Secondary outcomes included immunological remission, B-cell depletion, and changes in renal parameters. Multivariable logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and subgroup analyses were used to compare outcomes between MN patients with (MN + DM) and without diabetes (MN).

RESULTS: After matching, 207 patients were included (72 MN + DM, 135 MN). B-cell depletion and immunological remission rates showed no statistically significant differences between groups over the 12-month follow-up period. However, MN patients had significantly higher overall remission rates at 9 months [94% vs. 77%; odds ratio (OR) = 4.55, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.52-12.50, P < 0.01] and at 12 months (97% vs. 86%; OR: 5.26, 95% CI: 1.25-20.00, P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses confirmed consistently poorer responses in diabetic patients across multiple strata. Safety profiles were similar between groups.

CONCLUSION: Despite equivalent B-cell depletion, MN with DM patients show a reduced response to anti-CD20 antibody therapy relative to nondiabetic patients, underscoring that tight glycemic control, early supplementary anti-CD20 dosing for poor response, and combined immunosuppressive regimens may enhance their clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Trends in nephrology: from nihilism to targeted treatment of antibody-mediated rejection.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) is among the leading causes of kidney transplant attrition. Traditional AMR therapy was based on interventional studies that were small and often uncontrolled. Although a blockade of the interleukin (IL)-6 pathway failed to prevent allograft loss in a phase 3 trial, anecdotal evidence had previously suggested potential benefit. Likewise, anti-CD20 antibodies have not been shown to improve AMR outcomes in terms of graft survival. Imlifidase, which cleaves all immunoglobulin Gs, and hence also all donor-specific antibodies, showed a higher rate of graft loss in the experimental group of an AMR study. Terminal complement inhibitors showed inconsistent efficacy in underpowered trials; currently, C3 inhibitors are a promising focus for complement-targeted strategies against AMR. Anti-CD38 antibodies currently represent the most promising novel therapy option for AMR based on encouraging phase 2 study results. We furthermore discuss genetically engineered CD38 knock-out multitarget natural killer cells, expressing anti-B cell maturation antigen (BCMA) CAR, IL-15RF and hnCD16, administered in combination with daratumumab (anti-CD38) in this context. This approach represents a cheaper and safer alternative to chimeric HLA antigen receptor (CHAR) T cell therapy. CHAR T cells showed a high specificity in recognizing their respective target anti-HLA class I B cell receptors in vitro. Quantitative results from in vivo trials are pending. Likewise, we hypothesize the use of bi-specific T cell engagers such as CD19 blinatumomab or BCMA teclistamab for the treatment of AMR. In addition, clinical studies investigating conversion from calcineurin inhibitors to co-stimulation therapies such as anti-CD40L antibodies may reduce dnDSAs and AMR. In summary, anti-CD38 antibodies currently constitute the drug class with the strongest evidence for AMR treatment. To date, most CD38 antibodies have been shown to be safe, even after several years of administration in patients with multiple myeloma.

articles.title: Cellular senescence in calcific aortic valve disease: are we ready for senolytic therapy?
articles.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the Western countries and carries significant morbidity and mortality, yet no pharmacological therapy has demonstrated efficacy in modifying its natural history. Once regarded as a passive degenerative process, CAVD is now recognized as an actively regulated disease driven by endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, dysregulated mineral metabolism, and cellular senescence, which collectively drive progressive fibrotic remodeling and calcification of the valve leaflets through both dystrophic and osteogenic mechanisms. This review examines the pharmacological strategies that have been investigated or are currently under evaluation to slow CAVD progression, encompassing lipid-lowering agents, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, bone resorption inhibitors, vitamin K supplementation, and nitric oxide pathway modulators. Despite strong biological rationale and encouraging observational or preclinical data, each of these approaches has thus far failed to demonstrate consistent disease, modifying efficacy in prospective randomized trials, reflecting the complexity of CAVD pathophysiology and the historical lack of mechanistic precision in patient selection and trial design. Emerging evidence suggests that cellular senescence may represent a unifying and potentially actionable therapeutic target, bridging endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and active calcification within a single pathophysiological framework. Preclinical studies demonstrate that senolytic clearance of senescent cells reduces calcification in atherosclerosic and hypercholesterolemic vascular models provide a compelling rationale for extending this approach to valvular targets.

articles.title: Prevalence of depression and anxiety among patients with Behçet's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Behçet's disease (BD) is a chronic multisystemic vasculitis associated with significant physical and psychological morbidity, including depression and anxiety. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of depression and anxiety among BD patients and to examine variations by assessment tools and geographic regions.

METHOD: Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted up to April 2025. Data were extracted and quality-assessed using standardized tools, and pooled prevalence rates were calculated via random-effects meta-analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 17 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 16 contributed to the meta-analysis of depression and 11 to the meta-analysis of anxiety among patients with BD. The results revealed a high pooled prevalence of depression at 47.44% (95% CI: 34.09-60.97%) and anxiety at 48.48% (95% CI: 35.40-61.67%), both with substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%). Depression prevalence varied significantly by diagnostic instrument, with PHQ-9 and HADS reporting higher rates compared to DSM-IV and MINI. Geographic differences were marked, with Egypt showing the highest prevalence for both depression (88.83%) and anxiety (92.00%), while France reported the lowest prevalence for depression (5.00%) and Brazil reported the lowest for anxiety (29.31%). No publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: The findings underscore a high burden of mental health comorbidities in BD, with pooled prevalence rates of 47.44% for depression and 48.48% for anxiety, reflecting significant psychological morbidity. Geographic disparities, suggest cultural, healthcare, or socioeconomic moderators requiring further investigation. These results advocate for integrating routine mental health screening into BD management to address unmet psychiatric needs in this population.

articles.title: Exploring organizational readiness for the early adoption of a digital obesity prevention program in Swedish child healthcare: an observational prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the emphasis on organizational readiness in implementation science, there is limited empirical data supporting its role in implementation practice. This study aimed to (a) assess dimensions of organizational readiness at implementation start of an evidence-based digital health promotion and obesity prevention program in Swedish child healthcare (MINISTOP) and (b) investigate the associations between assessed readiness dimensions and the adoption of MINISTOP.

METHODS: In this observational prospective study, all 135 child healthcare nurses from 48 Swedish child healthcare centers involved in the large-scale implementation of MINISTOP in 2023 were invited to participate. Organizational readiness, conceptualized as a multidimensional construct reflecting individual and collective aspects of readiness, was measured at baseline (n = 83 nurses from 37 centers) using the six-dimension E-Ready questionnaire. Adoption of MINISTOP was assessed at 19 weeks through registration data (i.e., the number of families who gained access to MINISTOP). Descriptive statistics and correlation analyses were employed to describe organizational readiness, while negative binomial regression was used to analyze associations between the E-Ready dimensions and adoption.

RESULTS: Nurses reported a high degree of readiness for the conditions for change at the workplace, individual conditions for change and workplace attitudes dimensions, a medium degree of readiness for the perceived support among the management dimension, and a low degree of readiness for the readiness among colleagues and perceived consequences on status quo dimension. No statistically significant associations were found between E-Ready's dimensions and adoption. Nevertheless, positive estimates were observed for readiness among colleagues (IRR = 1.1, p = 0.05) and conditions for change at the workplace (IRR = 1.1, p = 0.08).

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant associations were identified between organizational readiness and adoption. The findings illustrate the complexity of organizational readiness as a construct, while the positive estimates observed for collective aspects of readiness suggest that their potential relationship with adoption warrants further investigation. Longitudinal studies using repeated assessments are needed to clarify how organizational readiness relates to implementation outcomes over time.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Engineering FAST-PETase with enhanced catalytic efficiency and acidic adaptability for sustainable PET waste recycling.
articles.abstract: This study presented a comprehensive protein engineering strategy to enhance the catalytic efficiency and environmental adaptability of FAST-PETase for PET plastic degradation. Through systematic site-directed mutagenesis of key basic residues (Arg84, Arg117, and Lys227) surrounding the active site, we identified R84D as the optimal single mutant, exhibiting 2.1-fold higher activity than FAST-PETase. Iterative saturation mutagenesis at 19 targeted positions yielded the quadruple mutant R84D/A203T/S230K/E198Q, demonstrating superior kinetic parameters: 3.3-fold higher catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km = 10.8 L·mmol-1·min-1) and significantly improved substrate affinity (Km = 72.6 mM) at acidic conditions. Structural characterization revealed this mutant's optimized active site geometry, featuring enhanced hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. It exhibited broad pH adaptability (maintaining >80% activity at pH 7.59.0) with a 0.5-unit acidic shift in optimal pH (7.5 vs wild-type's 8.0), while retaining thermal stability up to 50°C. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the mutant's enhanced structural rigidity, with 3050% lower RMSD values compared to FAST-PETase. When tested in a two-module reactor system, the quintuple mutant R84D/A203T/S230K/E198Q/S239V enabled efficient PET conversion to TPA, achieving a space-time conversion rate of 3.51 g·(L·h)-1. These results demonstrated its practical potential for industrial application. It established an effective framework for engineering plastic-degrading enzymes with enhanced performance under industrially relevant conditions.

articles.title: Collateral channel crossing failure during retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention: predictors and associated procedural outcomes from a multicenter registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO PCI) may fail at several stages. The authors evaluated factors associated with collateral channel crossing failure during retrograde CTO PCI and its associations with technical success and procedural complications.

METHODS: The authors analyzed procedures from a multicenter CTO PCI registry with attempted retrograde or retrograde-assisted strategies and recorded the retrograde result. The primary endpoint was collateral channel crossing failure. Secondary endpoints included retrograde success, overall technical success, collateral/coronary perforation, donor-vessel injury, vascular complications, and an extended complication composite.

RESULTS: Among 577 retrograde CTO PCI procedures with recorded retrograde result, retrograde success was achieved in 375 (65.0%), and collateral channel crossing failure occurred in 135 (23.4%). Overall technical success was lower with collateral crossing failure than without it (51.9% vs 88.7%), with higher rates of collateral and coronary perforation, vascular complications, and the extended complication composite. In the primary adjusted model restricted to procedures with known collateral connection (CC) grade, corkscrew collateral morphology (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.85; 95% CI, 3.63-12.91) and CC0 grade (adjusted OR, 4.70; 95% CI, 1.97-11.26) were associated with higher odds of crossing failure, whereas CC2/CC3 grade was associated with lower odds (adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.22-0.92).

CONCLUSIONS: Collateral channel crossing failure was common in retrograde CTO PCI and was associated with lower technical success and greater complication burden. Unfavorable collateral morphology was associated with a higher risk of crossing failure; repeated collateral attempts may indicate escalating procedural difficulty and may warrant strategy reassessment.

articles.title: Acute-on-Chronic Upper Limb Ischemia Precipitated by Critical Right Brachiocephalic Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brachiocephalic artery stenosis is an uncommon cause of upper extremity ischemia and cerebrovascular insufficiency. Diagnosis may be delayed because of subtle clinical manifestations, particularly in patients with established atherosclerotic risk factors.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old woman with diabetes, dyslipidemia, and active tobacco use presented with progressive bluish discoloration and pain of the right-hand digits. The primary care physician initially misattributed the presentation to Buerger disease. Angiography revealed critical ostial brachiocephalic artery stenosis, and prompt endovascular stenting showed improvement in digital perfusion and eventual resolution of symptoms.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the potential for isolated upper extremity digital ischemia to represent proximal great vessel disease, especially among high-risk smokers. Careful examination and imaging are important for avoiding a missed diagnosis. Smoking cessation remains essential for long-term protection.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Detailed examination and interarm blood pressure measurement should be routinely performed in patients with unexplained upper-extremity ischemia to identify potential proximal great-vessel disease.

articles.title: Same-Day Discharge After Percutaneous Transaxillary Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using Self-Expanding Valve.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The safety of same-day discharge (SDD) following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established strategy in patients undergoing the transfemoral approach. The feasibility of SDD in patients undergoing transaxillary TAVI has not been reported.

CASE SUMMARY: We present a 76-year-old male patient who underwent successful elective transaxillary TAVI. He had severe aortic stenosis, normal left ventricular function, and a background of diabetes, chronic liver disease, and right above-knee amputation. The access site was managed with 2 ProGlide devices with excellent hemostasis. There were no significant electrocardiogram changes postprocedure. Comprehensive postdischarge surveillance was provided, including a welfare telephone call on the following day.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first case in the literature of SDD following transaxillary TAVI. Such a strategy requires appropriate patient selection, meticulous procedural planning, rigorous postdischarge monitoring strategy, and can only be considered in highly selected cases.

articles.title: Electrical Storm in Advanced Chagas Cardiomyopathy Treated With Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radiotherapy After LVAD Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy remains challenging after prior ablation and mechanical circulatory support.

CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old man with advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy and prior endo-epicardial VT ablation developed electrical storm during influenza A infection and underwent left ventricular assist device implantation as a bridge to transplantation. Despite unloading, antiarrhythmic therapy, overdrive pacing, and stellate ganglion modulation, monomorphic VT persisted. Repeat ablation was unfavorable because of frailty and extensive residual lateral scar. Targeting for stereotactic arrhythmia radiotherapy (STAR) integrated late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance, clinical VT morphology, prior electroanatomic mapping, and planning computed tomography. A single 25-Gy fraction was delivered without acute complications. No sustained VT or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks occurred during follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Multimodality-guided STAR was feasible in this critically ill left ventricular assist device-supported patient. Although stabilization cannot be attributed to STAR alone, radiotherapy was delivered without observed acute radiotherapy- or device-related complications.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: STAR may offer a noninvasive substrate-targeted option when repeat ablation is limited.

articles.title: Echocardiographic Fusion Imaging to Guide LLAMACORN and Prevent Coronary Obstruction With Self-Expanding Valve-in-Valve TAVI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary obstruction is a catastrophic complication of transcatheter valve-in-valve procedures, as the prosthesis frame can form a neo-skirt compromising coronary perfusion.

CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old woman presented with a degenerated 23-mm balloon-expandable transcatheter valve, heart failure, and reduced left ventricular function. Computed tomography showed high-risk anatomy for right coronary obstruction: valve-to-right coronary artery distance 3.1 mm and valve-to-sinotubular junction distance 1.3 mm. Multimodality fusion imaging-guided electrosurgical leaflet modification using the leaflet laceration with balloon-mediated annihilation to prevent coronary obstruction with radiofrequency needle (LLAMACORN) technique, followed by implantation of a 26-mm self-expanding valve, achieved excellent hemodynamics and preserved coronary perfusion.

DISCUSSION: This case shows how computed tomography planning and multimodality imaging enable safe management of complex transcatheter aortic valve-in-transcatheter aortic valve anatomies. When conventional coronary protection is not feasible, LLAMACORN leaflet modification offers a safe alternative to mitigate obstruction risk.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recognize anatomical predictors of coronary obstruction in transcatheter aortic valve-in-transcatheter aortic valve. Understand multimodality imaging's role in guiding leaflet modification. Describe LLAMACORN as a leaflet-modification strategy when a self-expanding valve is preferred.

articles.title: Healthy Dietary Patterns and Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Cancer Survivors: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of noncancer mortality among cancer survivors. The potential influence of healthy dietary patterns on CVD risk among cancer survivors remains poorly understood.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the association between healthy dietary patterns and incident CVD among cancer survivors.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 8,716 cancer survivors initially free of CVD in the UK Biobank cohort. We used 24-hour dietary recall data to calculate 8 dietary pattern scores. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risks models were used to investigate the association between dietary patterns and incident CVD.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 12.3 (Q1-Q3: 11.6-13.0) years, 1,116 individuals experienced incident CVD events. When comparing the top quintile with the bottom quintile, HRs (95% CI) for total CVD were 0.72 (0.58-0.88) for Mediterranean diet score, 0.74 (0.61-0.89) for Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to stop Hypertension Diet Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay score, 0.63 (0.52-0.76) for Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010, 0.65 (0.53-0.79) for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension score, 0.82 (0.68-0.99) for healthful Plant-Based Diet Index, 0.67 (0.55-0.80) for reversed energy-adjusted diet inflammatory index, and 0.80 (0.67-0.96) for healthy low-fat diet score. The findings remain robust after fitting the generalized propensity score model. At age 45, participants with the highest adherence to healthy dietary patterns gained an estimated life expectancy of 1.66 to 3.32 years more than those with the lowest adherence.

CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to healthy dietary patterns is associated with reduced CVD risk among cancer survivors, underscoring the potential for diet to support cardio-oncology care.

articles.title: The assessment of respiratory diseases in ambulatory care attributable to air quality in the Upper Silesian agglomeration.
articles.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Air pollution remains a critical public health threat in modern societies, with sulfur dioxide (SO2) driving significant respiratory risks. This study investigated the relationship between criteria air pollutants (particulate matter 2.5 [PM2.5], particulate matter 10 [PM10], SO2, nitrogen oxides [NOx], Pb, and benzene) and the prevalence of selected respiratory diseases in the Upper Silesian agglomeration over a 5-year period.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Outpatient admission data for targeted conditions - including acute pharyngitis, acute tonsillitis, acute laryngotracheitis, pneumonia, bronchitis, and asthma - were obtained from the National Health Fund (Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia - NFZ) based on the corresponding International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes (J02, J03, J04, J13, J39, J40, J46). Spearman's and Kendall's correlation coefficients were used to evaluate the associations between average daily concentrations of air pollutants across approx. 50 regional monitoring stations and NFZ-reported disease incidence rates. Although the Upper Silesian Voivodeship is divided into 8 regions, the analysis revealed striking geographic variations.

RESULTS: A very strong correlation emerged between SO2 levels and increased respiratory disease incidence in regions 7 and 8 (τ = 0.99, ρ = 0.9), alongside a strong correlation in regions 1 and 4 (ρ = 0.78).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the under-examined health impacts of low-level SO2 and underscore the need for further investigations into the underlying drivers of these regional health disparities. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).

articles.title: Beyond the apnea-hypopnea index: clinical phenotypic heterogeneity of obstructive sleep apnea in an Indian tertiary referral cohort using level III polysomnography.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is usually classified by a single severity index, the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI), which does not capture the clinical heterogeneity described in other populations. To characterize clinically distinct OSA phenotypes by body habitus, symptom-severity relationship, and by respiratory event type in an Indian tertiary referral cohort, using level III polysomnography. Retrospective analysis of 309 patients with OSA (AHI≥5) from consecutive level III polysomnography studies at a tertiary Indian center. Phenotypes were defined as follows: 1) lean [body mass index (BMI)<25 kg/m²] versus non-lean OSA; 2) symptomatic vs. asymptomatic disease, using an Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score of 10 as a threshold, crossed with AHI severity; 3) apnea-predominant vs. hypopnea-predominant disease, from the respective event indices. An exploratory unsupervised cluster analysis on physiological variables was performed as a comparator. A lean phenotype was present in 12.3% of patients (95% confidence interval 9.1-16.5) and had lower AHI, less hypoxemia, and fewer daytime symptoms than non-lean OSA, with less moderate-to-severe disease (40.5% vs. 68.4%, p=0.002). Symptom burden was poorly matched to severity: 52.7% of severe OSA patients were not sleepy (ESS<10), while 21.5% of mild OSA patients were. Sleepy patients had a greater hypoxemic burden but similar body habitus. Apnea-predominant disease (54.3% of patients with usable indices) occurred in younger, leaner patients but with a higher AHI than hypopnea-predominant disease. Both the lean-phenotype association with less severe disease and the apnea-predominant AHI difference persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. STOP-Bang score did not reliably discriminate moderate-to-severe disease in this already high-risk referral population (AUC 0.56), and hypertension and diabetes prevalence did not differ between lean and non-lean phenotypes. ODI graded on AHI's own thresholds agreed with the AHI category in 67.4% of patients (quadratic-weighted κ 0.82) and identified moderate-to-severe disease with 89% sensitivity and 92% specificity. Unsupervised clustering on AHI-correlated physiological variables did not identify phenotypes independent of severity. OSA in this referral cohort separates into body-habitus, symptom-discordance and event-type phenotypes that are not interchangeable with AHI severity alone. Recognizing these patterns may help identify lean patients, underrecognized asymptomatic severe disease, and mechanistically distinct event patterns.

articles.title: Pediatric gastroenterologists practice styles and adherence to international guidelines for pediatric celiac disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate adherence to established European and North American guidelines among pediatric gastroenterologists in the diagnosis of celiac disease, and to characterize contemporary clinical practice patterns.

METHODS: A 26-item anonymous survey assessing diagnostic strategies, endoscopic practices, follow-up care, and dietary management was developed. The survey was distributed via an international pediatric gastroenterology listserv between January and February 2025. Only fully completed responses were analyzed. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses, and subgroup analyses were performed by geographic region.

RESULTS: A total of 203 respondents from 27 countries completed the survey, with most practicing in the United States (72.9%) and in tertiary or quaternary care centers (81.8%). Tissue transglutaminase immunoglobulin A (IgA) was nearly universally used for screening; however, variability existed in the use of total IgA and definitions of IgA deficiency. Endoscopic practices diverged, particularly at high serologic thresholds, with non-USA providers more likely to adopt non-biopsy diagnostic approaches (p < 0.001). Follow-up intervals were largely guideline-concordant, and laboratory monitoring and micronutrient assessment varied. Dietitian involvement and use of validated adherence tools were limited. Gluten challenge practices demonstrated substantial heterogeneity. Guideline utilization differed by region, with U.S. providers favoring North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition and international providers favoring European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition recommendations.

CONCLUSIONS: While overall adherence to celiac disease guidelines among pediatric gastroenterologists is high, meaningful variability persists in diagnostic thresholds, biopsy practices, follow-up care, and dietary assessment. These findings highlight ongoing differences in international practice and underscore the need for harmonized, updated guidelines to support standardized care.

articles.title: Unmet social needs in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease linked to increased risk of missed appointments.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Health-related social needs (HRSNs) are associated with worse health outcomes. This study aimed to identify unmet HRSNs in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate their association with missed medical and biologic infusion appointments.

METHODS: This study was conducted in an ambulatory pediatric gastroenterology program and infusion center from December 2021 to December 2024. Patients with IBD or guardians completed a standardized HRSNs screen. The primary outcome was the number of missed medical and infusion appointments in the year prior to screening. Bivariate and multivariable models without and with adjustment for socio-demographic characteristics were used.

RESULTS: A total of 191 patients with IBD were screened (median age 16 years, 68.59% male). Overall, 17.8% screened positive for HRSNs. Among patients with at least one completed medical appointment (n = 184), 54% had one or more missed appointments. Patients with HRSNs had a 63% (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 1.63, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11, 2.38, p = 0.0121) higher rate of missed medical appointments, which remained significant after adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, and sex (IRR: 1.56, 95% CI: 1.07, 2.28, p = 0.0212). Inadequate housing (8.38%), followed by food insecurity (6.81%) were the most prevalent HRSNs in our pediatric population. Unmet needs related to utilities (p = 0.0013), transportation (p = 0.0014) and healthcare cost (p = 0.0282) were significantly associated with missed appointments. Positive HRSNs were not associated with missed biologic therapy infusions (p = 0.155).

CONCLUSION: HRSNs were significantly associated with missed medical appointments. Future research should aim to develop strategies that address specific HRSNs, along with personalized interventions to the individual circumstances.

articles.title: Short-Term Effects of Golden Rice Cookies Enriched With Piper crocatum Extract on Lipid Profiles in Adults With Diabetes: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) commonly coexists with dyslipidemia and elevated cardiovascular risk. Food-based interventions containing antioxidants and polyphenols may support lipid metabolism. This study evaluated the short-term effects of Golden Rice cookies enriched with active Piper crocatum extract on lipid profiles in adults with DM.

METHODS: This quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group study included 102 adults with DM assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received Golden Rice cookies enriched with P. crocatum extract, while the control group received similar cookies without the extract for 28 days. Total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and triglycerides were measured before and after the intervention. Bivariate analyses were performed in the full sample, whereas analysis of covariance was performed among non-statin participants, adjusting for baseline lipid values, age, body mass index, diabetes duration, carbohydrate intake, and protein intake.

RESULTS: In the unadjusted analysis, total cholesterol and LDL-C increased significantly in the intervention group, whereas total cholesterol decreased significantly in the control group. Between-group analysis showed a significant difference only in total cholesterol. Among non-statin participants, an exploratory adjusted analysis showed a significant between-group difference in total cholesterol (p = 0.016; adjusted mean difference = -12.55 mg/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI] = -22.74 to -2.36). No significant adjusted differences were observed for LDL-C, HDL-C, or triglycerides.

CONCLUSION: A 28-day intervention with Golden Rice cookies enriched with active P. crocatum extract was associated with a limited exploratory adjusted between-group difference in total cholesterol among non-statin adults with DM. These preliminary findings require confirmation in longer randomized controlled trials with stronger dietary control and mechanistic biomarker assessment.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT07268781.

articles.title: Serological and clinical outcomes of rituximab in antiphospholipid syndrome with or without SLE: a retrospective single-centre cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the dynamics of aPL titres after rituximab treatment, durability of serological responses, recurrent thrombosis, and safety in patients with APS.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 54 patients, predominantly with SLE-associated APS (n = 43), who received at least one course of rituximab. aCL and anti-β2-glycoprotein I (aβ2GPI) IgG/IgM were evaluated at baseline and 6-12 months after treatment. Long-term serological, clinical and safety outcomes were analysed over a median follow-up period of 4.7 years.

RESULTS: At 6-12 months, positivity rates decreased significantly for aCL IgG (59.3% to 24.1%), aCL IgM (24.1% to 5.6%), aβ2GPI IgG (42.6% to 16.7%), and aβ2GPI IgM (20.4% to 5.6%) (all P <0.05). Long-term serological data were available for 31 patients. At last follow-up, aβ2GPI IgG positivity remained lower than baseline (P = 0.039), whereas quantitative titres were no longer significantly different. Long-term serological changes did not differ according to rituximab cycle number. Thrombotic recurrence occurred in five patients, four of whom were either off anticoagulation or had subtherapeutic INR values. Fifteen patients developed bacterial infections, seven SARS-CoV-2 infections, and five patients died during follow-up, including one who died from sepsis.

CONCLUSION: Rituximab was associated with marked short-term reductions in aPL titres and positivity, although quantitative suppression was not sustained long term. Changes in aCL/aβ2GPI did not consistently reflect thrombotic risk. These findings suggest that rituximab may be a valuable adjunctive therapy in selected patients with difficult-to-treat APS, although causality cannot be established from this retrospective study.

articles.title: Updated Breast Cancer Incidence in Canadian Women by Age: Divergent Trends.
articles.journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine age-specific breast cancer incidence trends.

METHODS: Breast cancer case counts were obtained from the National Cancer Incidence Reporting System (1984-1991) and the Canadian Cancer Registry (1992-2023) both housed at Statistics Canada. Trends in age-specific and age standardized incidence rates (ASIR), and associated annual percent changes (APC), were determined using JoinPoint.

RESULTS: The most recent breast cancer age-specific trends were observed to be increasing for all age groups under age 55, especially 45-49 since 2018 (APC = 2.4, P < .001); were stable for 55-59, and decreasing for age groups within 60-74, though not significantly for 70-74 (APC = -0.4, P = .076). An increasing breast cancer ASIR trend was observed throughout the study period except for 1999-2004. Between 1984-1986 and 2021-2023 incidence rates increased in each age group <85; however, they decreased among women 90+ by 23.5%. Apart from the 55-59 age group, relative increases of 20% or more combined with absolute increases of 50 per 100 000 or more between these two periods were observed for each age group between 50-54 and 70-74. The largest absolute increase occurred among women 65-69 (76.1 per 100 000). The age group corresponding to the peak incidence rate has become younger over time from 90+ (1984-1986) to 70-74 (since 2011-2013).

CONCLUSION: Highlighted by increasing rates among younger women, especially those 45-49, recent trends in age-specific breast cancer incidence rates are diverging with important implications for screening and clinical care. Over several decades, the shape of the age-specific breast cancer incidence rate curve has changed with peak incidence occurring at a younger age.

articles.title: Real-world evidence speaks louder than biological plausibility. Editorial on "Ursodeoxycholic acid and long COVID in steatotic liver disease: a nationwide cohort study".

Association between Dynamic Change in Smoking Behavior and the Risk of Liver Outcomes in Steatotic Liver Disease: Editorial on "Transitions from Combustible to Noncombustible Tobacco Use and Liver Outcomes in Steatotic Liver Disease".
Discordant FIB-4 and Liver Stiffness in MASLD: Implications for Risk Stratification, Generalizability, and Clinical Decision-Making: Correspondence to Authors' reply.
