Peri-Infarct Cortical Network Remapping During Stroke Recovery via a Soft Liquid Metal Neural Interface.
articles.abstract: Stroke causes substantial reorganization of neural activity and connectivity in the peri-infarct cortex during functional recovery. Tracking these changes at high resolution, however, remains difficult. Mechanical mismatch of conventional rigid neural probes is exacerbated in the fragile peri-infarct region, destabilizing the tissue-electrode interface and limiting long-term recording. Here, we present a fully soft, liquid metal-based multichannel neural interface that enables stable electrophysiological recording in freely moving mice. Using this platform, we performed longitudinal recordings before and after ischemic stroke, enabling within-animal comparisons. We applied complementary analyses of population-level latent dynamics and functional connectivity, capturing network-level coordination and pairwise interactions. Both analyses revealed acute suppression followed by partial recovery without restoration of the pre-stroke state. Instead, neural networks reorganized into a distinct and reproducible functional configuration. These findings establish soft liquid metal neural interfaces combined with population-level analysis as a useful approach for resolving neural reorganization during stroke recovery.

articles.title: Lactate Drives Pathological Browning of White Adipose Tissue to Aggravate Sepsis-Associated Metabolic Disorders in a GPR81-Dependent Manner.
articles.abstract: Lactate serves as a prognostic biomarker for sepsis, yet its adipose-centered signaling pathway driving persistent metabolic disorders remains unclear. We reveal that lactate accumulation triggers browning of white adipose tissue (WAT) via GPR81 to aggravate sepsis-induced hypermetabolism, muscle wasting, and insulin resistance. Septic patients exhibit hyperlactatemia and WAT browning, with lactate concentrations correlated with fat and muscle loss. Genetically deleting UCP1 substantially attenuates LPS-induced hypermetabolism, muscle wasting, and insulin resistance, confirming WAT browning as a major mediator of sepsis-associated metabolic disorders. Lactate supplementation and pharmacological interventions using glycolysis or lactate dehydrogenase inhibitors identify lactate as the upstream pathogenic trigger. Using siRNA screening, global GPR81 knockout, and AAV9-mediated adipose-specific GPR81 knockdown, we identify GPR81 as the lactate receptor mediating UCP1 upregulation. Mechanistically, GPR81 activation induces CTRP6 and p-p38 to upregulate UCP1. AAV9-mediated overexpression of CTRP6/MKK6 in GPR81-/- mice, together with pharmacological downregulation of CTRP6 or inhibition of p-p38, supports the involvement of this pathway in WAT browning. Taken together, evidence from clinical data, gene-knockout mice, and primary adipocyte experiments demonstrates that lactate drives WAT browning in a GPR81-dependent manner to aggravate sepsis-associated metabolic disorders, identifying potential targets for therapeutic investigation in metabolic disorders unresponsive to conventional anti-infective and nutritional support treatments.

articles.title: The ecological adaptability of pinewood nematode populations: survival strategies, mechanisms and co-evolution.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (pinewood nematode, PWN) is the causal agent of pine wilt disease and ranks among the most destructive invasive pests threatening global forest ecosystems. Since its introduction to China, this nematode has triggered massive ecological and economic losses, while its distribution range continues to expand northward. The association between the widespread dispersal of B. xylophilus in invaded areas and the ecological adaptability of its populations has drawn considerable attention.

RESULTS: This review systematically synthesizes recent research advances regarding the ecological adaptability of PWN populations, elaborating on molecular mechanisms and ecological strategies that enable the nematode to colonize novel environments. In terms of thermal adaptation, differentially expressed genes, small heat shock protein families and the accumulation of key metabolites collectively shape adaptive pathways to resist extreme high and low temperature stress. For host adaptation, PWN displays polyphagous feeding habits and relies on diverse arboreal fungi as nutritional resources when pines were weakened or died. Detoxification enzyme cascades and effector proteins enable the nematode to counteract host defensive metabolites. Specifically, effectors suppress host peroxidase activity, thereby quenching reactive oxygen species bursts and disrupting plant hormone regulatory pathways to attenuate pine immune responses. Co-evolutionary interactions between PWN and vector beetles manifest across multiple dimensions, including synchronized life cycles, specialized dispersal-stage juveniles, and infochemical-mediated interspecies communication. PWN also forms intricate interaction networks with associated fungi and bacteria, which exert vital functions in nutrient acquisition, pathogenicity enhancement and terpenoid degradation. Notably, ascaroside pheromones serve as central signaling molecules that modulate interspecific competition and reproductive phenotypic plasticity. Population genetic analyses have uncovered shifts in genetic diversity, regulatory pathways governing population structure and reproductive efficiency, as well as synergistic evolutionary correlations between invasive population genetics and pathogenicity. Multi-omics analytical frameworks provide novel perspectives for dissecting the adaptive evolution of PWN.

CONCLUSION: The invasive success and widespread dispersal of B. xylophilus are fundamentally driven by its strong population ecological adaptability. Finally, this review summarizes the existing research gaps and proposes future research priorities alongside targeted pest management strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Injectable Peptide-Based Functional Amyloid Hydrogels as Tunable Depots for Sustained Drug Delivery.
articles.abstract: Sustained delivery of therapeutic proteins remains a major challenge because rapid degradation and diffusion necessitate frequent dosing, compromising therapeutic efficacy. Here, we present an injectable peptide-based functional amyloid hydrogel as a versatile drug depot that preserves protein stability while enabling sustained cargo release. As a representative therapeutic application, insulin delivery for diabetes was employed to validate the platform. It exhibited excellent biocompatibility and injectability, providing controlled insulin release over 90 h while preserving its structural stability. Following a single subcutaneous administration in diabetic rats, it restored normoglycemia within 30 min and maintained it for 60 h, followed by a rebound at 66 h, representing a much longer period of glucose maintenance than free insulin. Long-term in vivo biosafety studies confirmed the absence of systemic toxicity following repeated administration. To demonstrate the tunability of this platform, it was further engineered with sodium alginate as a representative bioadditive, thereby enabling tunable release kinetics and extending sustained insulin release while maintaining injectability and biocompatibility. Collectively, these findings establish peptide-based functional amyloid hydrogels, either alone or engineered with a bioadditive, as a safe, injectable, and tunable platform for sustained therapeutic delivery, with diabetes serving as a representative proof of concept for broad biomedical applications.

articles.title: Gel-Free Capture of Microvolt-Level Neural Signatures Via a 3D Monolithic Carbon Fiber Dry Electrode.
articles.abstract: Gel-based wet electrodes remain the gold standard for electrophysiology, but gel dehydration limits recordings. Existing dry electrodes partially address this limitation but suffer from high interfacial impedance. Here, a carbon fiber-based porous electrode (CFPE) is reported, comprising a three-dimensional conductive network coated with poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS). The CFPE establishes contact at hairy-scalp sites with an impedance of approximately 10 kΩ·cm2. On the forearm, its impedance at 10 Hz without skin preparation is 11.09 ± 1.03 kΩ·cm2, compared with 13.57 ± 2.07 kΩ·cm2 for wet electrodes. After 6 h of wear, CFPE impedance reaches 1.3 times its initial value without skin preparation or gel, whereas wet-electrode impedance reaches 56 times its initial value when applied with skin preparation and conductive gel. High-fidelity electrocardiography, electromyography, and electroencephalography signals are captured with correlation coefficients exceeding 90% and signal-to-noise ratios comparable to wet electrodes. The CFPE further resolves microvolt-level speech-evoked frequency-following responses (FFR) and long-latency responses (LLR), with fidelity comparable to wet electrodes and significantly higher LLR SNR. These results demonstrate gel-free acquisition of weak neural biomarkers, opening a pathway toward prolonged, preparation-free neurophysiology.

articles.title: The Recovery Room Is Not Needed Following Hand Surgery With Local Anesthesia in the Outpatient Operating Room: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of an outpatient operating room (OPOR) for hand surgery under local anesthesia only has increased due to efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Although prior research supports the safety of OPOR and outcomes equivalent to traditional operating room settings, the necessity of post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) monitoring for these patients remains uncertain. This study evaluated the safety of discharging patients directly home from the OPOR without PACU recovery.

METHODS: A prospective study enrolled 102 patients who underwent carpal tunnel release and/or trigger finger surgery in the OPOR under local anesthesia only. Patients were discharged directly from the OPOR after a single set of postoperative vital signs. Outcomes included adverse events, emergency department (ED) visits, surgical reinterventions, and intraoperative and postoperative complications within 90 days.

RESULTS: The mean patient age was 65.2 years (range, 25-94), and 60.8% were female. No intraoperative or postoperative complications, surgical reinterventions, or deaths occurred. Four patients (3.9%) presented to the ED within 90 days; 1 (0.9%) experienced an adverse event due to community-acquired pneumonia. No ED visits were related to a complication of the hand procedure. All patients were hemodynamically and respiratory stable at discharge. Forty-six patients (45.1%) had elevated blood pressure at discharge, 76.1% of whom had known hypertension.

CONCLUSION: Bypassing PACU after OPOR hand surgery under local anesthesia only is safe. Direct discharge from the OPOR may reduce health care resource utilization, decrease costs associated with PACU recovery, and improve procedural efficiency without compromising patient safety.

articles.title: Convergent validity of the Functional Bridge Test and its prognostic association with walking independence in patients with acute stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Functional Bridge Test (FBT) is a simple bedside assessment tool for evaluating hip elevation. It has demonstrated good validity and reliability in patients with lower limb hemiplegia after stroke and is significantly associated with stroke severity, lower limb strength, and basic mobility. However, its applicability across all patients with acute stroke, including those without lower limb hemiparesis, has not yet been established.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to examine the convergent validity of the FBT and its prognostic association with walking independence in patients with acute stroke.

METHODS: This study included consecutive patients with acute stroke admitted to a university hospital who survived and had complete data for outcome assessment. Convergent validity was evaluated using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) total score, the NIHSS motor leg subscore on the affected side, and the Functional Status Score for the Intensive Care Unit (FSS-ICU), all measured on the first day of the rehabilitation program. The association between FBT grade and walking independence at a variable discharge-based endpoint, defined as the end of the inpatient rehabilitation program, was assessed through unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among 207 patients, the FBT grades were significantly correlated with the NIHSS total scores (ρ =  -0.668), the NIHSS motor leg subscores on the affected side (ρ =  -0.648), and the FSS-ICU scores (ρ = 0.730). The FBT was independently associated with walking independence (adjusted odds ratio = 1.786, 95% confidence interval = 1.022-3.418, p = .039).

CONCLUSIONS: The FBT demonstrated adequate convergent validity and prognostic association in patients with acute stroke. This practical bedside assessment was associated with early functional status and walking independence at a variable discharge-based endpoint. Further prospective validation using standardized follow-up time points is needed.

articles.title: Peri-Operative Infection Control Measures for Implantation of Sacral Nerve Stimulators (SNS): A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sacral nerve stimulators (SNS) are used to treat refractory urinary symptoms, bowel symptoms, and pelvic pain. There is a risk of surgical site and implant infection; however, manufacturers have not released guidelines regarding infection prevention during their implantation. There are limited data on the pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative considerations for infection prevention. We present a scoping review detailing the current strategies for infection prevention during implantation of SNS and propose a protocol for perioperative infection control strategies based on current available literature.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta Analysis (PRISMA). A search strategy using search terms "sacral nerve stimulation," "infection," "infection control," and "infection prevention" was used. A search was conducted on medical databases, and a grey literature search was performed.

RESULTS: Forty-three articles were included for data extraction, published between 2003 and 2022. A total of 10,401 outcomes were reported. Pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative considerations and outcomes were extracted. Significant peri-operative considerations included the use of pre-operative chlorhexidine wash and the use of shallow pocket depths. There was limited data to support other infection control considerations and variability in practices within the SNS implanting community.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite implant infection being a highly morbid and detrimental outcome for the patient, there is no clear consensus on what infection control measures should be routinely performed to reduce the risk of infection during the implantation process. The peri-operative considerations currently covered in the literature have little reported evidence to support the implementation of certain infection prevention considerations, and it seems their use is primarily driven by surgeon preference.

articles.title: Appendicitis in the Transplant Patient: A Common Problem in a Less Common Patient Population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute appendicitis has not been well-studied in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. We hypothesized that SOT patients with appendicitis would exhibit an atypical presentation, characterized by blunted inflammatory responses.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult SOT and non-SOT patients diagnosed with appendicitis across multiple hospitals from January 2011 to July 2025. Non-transplant patients were matched 1:1 to SOT recipients using nearest-neighbor propensity score matching on age, gender, and body mass index (BMI). Demographics, vital signs, laboratory values, management, and antibiotic use were assessed in the full and matched cohorts.

RESULTS: Among 4,049 SOT recipients, 54 (1.3%) developed appendicitis; median time from transplant to diagnosis was 2.5 y (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.3). In the propensity-matched cohort (54 transplant, 54 matched non-transplant controls), SOT recipients demonstrated a lower mean WBC (10.1 vs. 12.7 × 109/L, p = 0.011) than their non-SOT cohort, while length of stay remained significantly longer (mean difference + 3.96 d, p = 0.013). Rate of complicated appendicitis was not statistically different after matching (20.4% vs. 18.5%, p = 0.81); age was independently associated with complicated appendicitis (p = 0.023). Among patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy, SOT recipients received significantly longer antibiotic courses than matched controls (rate ratio 1.79, p = 0.025).

CONCLUSIONS: Appendicitis in SOT recipients presents with a blunted inflammatory response, lower leukocytosis, along with longer hospitalization and antibiotic courses after laparoscopic appendectomy. In contrast, the higher rate of complicated appendicitis observed in unmatched comparisons appears attributable to the older age of transplant recipients rather than a transplant-specific effect.

articles.title: Malaria in a US resident blood donor following a 3-month travel deferral.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The United States defers blood donations from people who have recently traveled to or lived in malaria-endemic areas. While transfusion-transmitted malaria is rare, it primarily occurs when the donor is a previous resident of a malaria-endemic area infected with Plasmodium parasites. In 2020, the travel deferral period was revised for US residents from 1 year to 3 months after leaving a malaria-endemic area.

CASE REPORT: A single unit of packed red blood cells (pRBC) was produced from a whole blood donation collected from an asymptomatic donor 109 days after return from travel to East Africa. The donor was born and resided in the United States but repeatedly traveled to the region, reportedly took malaria chemoprophylaxis, and denied previous malaria illness. Eleven days post-donation, the donor presented to a healthcare provider with flu-like symptoms and was diagnosed with Plasmodium ovale malaria 18 days after donation. Four days after diagnosis, the blood establishment was notified of the donor's malaria diagnosis; however, the pRBC had been transfused the previous day. The recipient of the pRBC was placed on treatment, repeatedly tested negative for Plasmodium parasites, and remained asymptomatic.

CONCLUSIONS: We describe a near-miss of transfusion-transmitted P. ovale malaria associated with a US-resident donor despite a 3-month travel deferral. P. ovale and Plasmodium vivax forms of malaria can cause disease relapse months to years after initial infection. Additional strategies for enhancing blood safety include testing of donors with molecular assays, pathogen reduction of select blood components, and a longer travel deferral window.

articles.title: A National Survey of Simulation Use, Limitations, and Future Directions in Neurocritical Care Fellowship Training.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Details regarding the use and implementation of simulation-based medical education (SBME) among neurocritical care fellowship programs are limited. The objective of this study was to describe the current use of SBME in neurocritical care fellowship education and to assess perceived barriers to SBME growth in both programs currently using simulation and those that are not.

METHODS: We surveyed neurocritical care fellowship program directors using email addresses listed in the San Francisco Match directory using a Qualtrics-based survey platform. Survey questions addressed current utilization of SBME and barriers to SBME growth.

RESULTS: Thirty-nine of 72 (54%) program directors responded to our survey. Of the respondents, 95% (37/39) report using SBME in their neurocritical care fellowship training programs. Most (94%, 34/36) programs create their own simulation cases. SBME was most frequently used for trainee education and trainee assessment, and rarely used for quality improvement. The most reported SBME case topics included fundamentals in neurocritical care, vascular neurology, serious illness communication, and interprofessional team dynamics. Simulations rarely focused on headache management or neuro-infectious disease, and simulations on healthcare disparities and implicit bias were not reported among survey respondents. Eighty-two percent (32/39) of responding institutions reported wanting to increase the amount of simulation training offered. Reported barriers include faculty protected time, funding, and mentorship.

DISCUSSION: SBME has been embraced by most responding programs; however, the content of simulation curricula varies. Fellowship directors report interest in expanding SBME at their institutions, though are commonly limited by faculty time constraints, financial support, and mentorship. Future collaboration across institutions and application of SBME in learner assessment and quality improvement may improve simulation growth and innovation in neurocritical care fellowship training.

articles.title: In Situ Fenestration-Assisted TEVAR in Patients With Complex Pathology Involving the Aortic Arch.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the feasibility, safety, and short-term clinical outcomes of in situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (ISF-TEVAR) employing an electrocautery-connected guidewire combined with a novel, pump-less, extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass for cerebral perfusion in patients with complex aortic arch pathology.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration. Fenestrations were performed with an electrocautery-connected 0.018-inch chronic total occlusion-dedicated guidewire. Patients' demographics, procedural details, perioperative outcomes, and early follow-up data were analyzed, with stratification according to the number of fenestrated supra-aortic branches.

RESULTS: A total of 37 supra-aortic branches were targeted: 3-branch fenestrations in 6 patients (31.6%), 2-branch in 6 patients (31.6%), and single-branch in 7 patients (36.8%). Technical success, defined as successful graft fenestration with patent branches on completion angiography, was achieved in 94.5% (35/37). One failed innominate artery fenestration was managed with chimney-assisted TEVAR, and 1 left subclavian artery fenestration was successfully completed in a subsequent procedure. Operative time increased with procedural complexity (140 ± 12 minutes for 1 branch, 152 ± 10 minutes for 2 branches, and 162 ± 13 minutes for 3 branches; P = .004). No intraprocedural mortality occurred. Two perioperative strokes (10.5%) and 2 in-hospital deaths (10.5%) were recorded, 1 death was due to vertebrobasilar stroke and the other due to retrograde type A aortic dissection with rupture. Median hospital stay was 8 days. During a mean follow-up of 9.2 months, there was no aorta-related mortality, with an overall survival rate of 89.5%. All stented branches remained patent, and 2 endoleaks (10.5%) were successfully treated endovascularly.

CONCLUSION: In situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair using an electrocautery-connected wire combined with a temporary, pressure gradient-driven extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass is a feasible, reproducible, and safe technique for complex aortic arch repair. This fully percutaneous approach ensures continuous cerebral perfusion, demonstrates efficient procedural metrics, and yields favorable short-term outcomes, representing a practical alternative when custom-made devices or hybrid surgical procedures are not available.Clinical ImpactIn situ fenestration-assisted TEVAR combined with a temporary pumpless extracorporeal femoral-carotid bypass enables continuous cerebral perfusion during complex aortic arch interventions without the need for cardiopulmonary bypass or surgical debranching. This technique expands the feasibility of fully endovascular multibranch arch repair in urgent or anatomically challenging cases where custom-made devices are unavailable. For clinicians, this approach offers a practical and reproducible strategy to mitigate cerebral ischemic risk while maintaining procedural efficiency and percutaneous access. This technique may facilitate broader adoption of in situ fenestration by providing a cerebral protection strategy using readily available endovascular equipment.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in Pediatric Drowning Patients Admitted to Intensive Care: A 14-Year Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Drowning is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in children, primarily due to respiratory and neurological injury. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological, clinical, and outcome characteristics of pediatric drowning and identify factors associated with invasive mechanical ventilation. We conducted a 14-year retrospective descriptive and analytical study including all children admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit for drowning. Thirty-one patients were included, with a median age of 30 months, and 61% were male. The median immersion time was 5 minutes, and 13% of children were submerged for more than 10 minutes. Respiratory distress occurred in 71% of cases, while 41.9% required invasive mechanical ventilation. Prolonged immersion, SpO2 <90%, respiratory distress, neurological impairment, advanced clinical stage, and biological abnormalities were associated with mechanical ventilation. Mortality was 9.7% and was higher among ventilated patients. Early recognition and appropriate respiratory support may improve outcomes.

articles.title: Porcine jejunal Peyer's patches leukocytes are a potent source of mucosal IgA binding to Streptococcus suis and suilysin.
articles.abstract: Human Streptococcus suis infections are frequently linked to undercooked pork consumption, particularly in Southeast Asia. Experimental evidence indicates that S. suis can cross the intestinal barrier and cause systemic infection in pigs, suggesting the gut as a plausible entry site. However, mucosal immunity against S. suis in the intestinal tract remains poorly characterized. Here, we provide initial insights into the intestinal source and production of mucosal IgA against S. suis in 8-week-old conventional pigs. We show that jejunal and ileal mucus contains IgA recognizing a commensal S. suis isolate as well as a virulent S. suis cps2 strain. Mucosal IgA antibodies also bind to the secreted virulence-associated protein suilysin (SLY). Flow cytometric analysis of porcine Peyer's patches (PP) leukocytes of the jejunum (JPP) and the ileum (IPP) revealed a significantly higher frequency of IgA+ B cells in JPP. Moreover, JPP-derived leukocytes showed higher constitutive and stimulation-induced total IgA secretion than IPP-derived leukocytes. Stimulation, either with the T cell-associated factors CD40L and IL-21 or the TLR1/2 ligand Pam3Cys-SK4 induced anti-S. suis IgA secretion, particularly in JPP-derived leukocyte cultures, indicating a contribution of innate immune mechanisms and an important role for T cell help. Finally, IgA induced by in vitro stimulation of JPP- or IPP-derived leukocytes recognized commensal and virulent S. suis as well as SLY, involved in disrupting epithelial barriers. Our results suggest that S. suis elicits a mucosal immune response in the intestinal tract of conventional piglets, with B cells in JPP representing a key site of IgA production.

articles.title: The genomic landscape of Pasteurella multocida B:2 causing haemorrhagic septicaemia in Germany.
articles.abstract: Haemorrhagic septicaemia (HS) is a peracute to acute, highly fatal disease caused by Pasteurella (P.) multocida serogroups B:2 and E:2 affecting cattle and buffaloes. HS in cattle and buffaloes necessitates mandatory reporting to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH; formerly OIE) due to its significant socio-economic impact on livestock production and international trade. In other ungulate species infection with P. multocida B:2 (iPmB:2) presents with a similar clinical picture. A series of HS and iPmB:2 outbreaks between 2010 and 2024 in Germany required a detailed investigation into the spatiotemporal dynamics and molecular characteristics of the circulating strains. The ability to specifically identify and analyse circulating serovars is crucial for confirming outbreaks and implementing appropriate control measures. A total of 221 Pasteurella multocida capsular type B:2 isolates associated with HS/iPmB:2 outbreaks was collected between 2010 and 2024 from dead livestock and wildlife in Germany in the context of veterinary practice and subsequently analysed using whole-genome sequencing. Isolates were characterised by capsular and lipopolysaccharide PCR-based typing, multilocus sequence typing, and high-resolution genomic comparison. Four high-resolution-typing approaches were evaluated and compared with epidemiologically defined outbreaks to identify the most suitable method for outbreak investigation. Single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based analysis showed the highest discriminatory power and best agreement with known outbreak data, outperforming conventional multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and core-genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) approaches. Genotyping identified eight major genetic clusters of closely related strains across multiple federal states and host species. Several outbreaks were linked by highly similar or identical genomes, suggesting both local persistence and wider geographic spread of the pathogen within Germany.

articles.title: Celebrating the 30th anniversary of the introduction of cardio-oncology: commentary and the first english translation of the report.
Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA.

RESULTS: A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ.

CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

articles.title: The Direction of the Clostridioides difficile-Gastrointestinal GVHD Relationship After Allogenic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: A Time-Dependent CIBMTR Analysis.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) and gastrointestinal acute graft-versus-host disease (GI-GVHD) frequently co-occur after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT), and a bidirectional relationship has been proposed. The prior CIBMTR analysis associated antecedent GI-GVHD with CDI but modeled GI-GVHD as a fixed exposure and could not test whether CDI predicts subsequent GI-GVHD.

METHODS: We analyzed a publicly available CIBMTR dataset of patients undergoing first allo-HCT for AML, ALL, or MDS (2013-2018), each complication was modeled as a time-dependent exposure using cause-specific Cox regression, with death and relapse treated as competing events, adjusting for donor type, disease, conditioning intensity, and (reverse direction) GVHD prophylaxis type. Sensitivity analyses included restriction to adults and exclusion of CDI diagnosed before post-transplant cyclophosphamide PTCy.

RESULTS: CDI within 100 days occurred in 777 patients (11%). CDI did not predict subsequent GI-GVHD (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.90-1.48; p = 0.26). GI-GVHD predicted subsequent CDI (HR 1.54; 95% CI 1.08-2.19; p = 0.016), unchanged after adjustment for prophylaxis type and stronger in adults (HR 1.73; 95% CI 1.18-2.55). An apparent PTCy-CDI association (HR 1.38; 95% CI 1.08-1.75; p = 0.009), was driven by CDI with onset by Day 4, before PTCy, and was no longer significant once excluded (HR 1.11; 95% CI 0.80-1.52).

CONCLUSIONS: When event timing and competing risks are respected, the GI-GVHD predicts subsequent CDI whereas the reverse is not observed. GI-GVHD identifies patients at elevated risk who are candidates for heightened surveillance. The disappearance of the PTCy signal once drug timing was respected illustrates how event ordering can misattribute risk.

articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: Drugs developed to treat diabetes, liraglutide and lixisenatide, cross the blood brain barrier and enhance neurogenesis.
Evaluation of the Association of N-Acetylcysteine and Mortality in Non-Acetaminophen-Induced Acute Liver Failure.
articles.abstract: PurposeNon-acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure (NAI-ALF) is associated with high mortality, with limited treatment options beyond supportive care and liver transplantation. While intravenous (IV) N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the standard of care in acetaminophen-induced ALF, its benefit in NAI-ALF remains uncertain. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to evaluate the effect of IV NAC on in-hospital mortality.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study that included adult patients with NAI-ALF. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on baseline demographics, severity of ALF, comorbidity burden, and etiology of ALF was conducted to balance the two groups. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality at 21 days. Secondary outcomes included time to INR normalization, time to liver function test (LFT) normalization, and hospital length of stay.ResultsA total of 200 patients were included in the study, with 85 patients in the NAC group and 115 in the non-NAC group. After IPTW, groups were balanced with standardized mean differences of <0.1 for all covariates. IV NAC was associated with lower in-hospital mortality at 21 days (48.9% vs 62.1%, P < .01), with an odds ratio of 0.59 (95% CI 0.39 - 0.88). No difference was observed in time to INR normalization [HR 1.49 (95% CI 0.87 - 2.56, P = .15)], time to LFT normalization [HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.72 - 1.74, P = .61)], and length of hospital stay (11.9 vs 15.1 days, P = .84).ConclusionFor patients with NAI-ALF, IV NAC administration was associated with a reduction in in-hospital mortality at 21 days. These findings suggest NAC could play a role in the management of patients with NAI-ALF. Larger prospective studies are needed to further clarify the role of NAC in this population.

articles.title: Impact of a Nurse-Led, Target-Directed Light Sedation Strategy on the Incidence of Delirium in Septic Patients in the Emergency Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the impact of a nurse-led, target-directed light sedation strategy on delirium incidence and short-term outcomes in septic patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation in the emergency intensive care unit (EICU).MethodsWe analyzed 221 consecutive septic patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation for more than 24 h at a single center (January 2022-May 2024). Based on a sedation protocol change, patients were assigned to conventional sedation group (control, n = 123) or nurse-led, target-directed light sedation group (exposed, n = 98). The primary outcome was delirium incidence. Secondary outcomes included delirium-free days (DFD-28), ventilator-free days (VFD-28), mechanical ventilation duration, EICU length of stay, and 28-day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression examined the independent association between the nurse-led strategy and delirium risk.ResultsDelirium occurred less frequently in the nurse-led sedation group than in the control group (20.4% vs 37.4%, P = .007). The exposed group had shorter mechanical ventilation duration and EICU length of stay (both P < .05), whereas VFD-28 did not differ significantly between groups. The two groups did not differ significantly in 28-day mortality (28.6% vs 26.0%, P = .671) or in the rate of airway-related adverse events. On multivariable analysis, the nurse-led strategy was independently associated with a lower risk of delirium (OR = 0.428, 95% CI: 0.215-0.854, P = .016). Subgroup analyses showed that this protective benefit was consistent across age strata, disease severity levels, and comorbidity burden.ConclusionIn septic patients undergoing mechanical ventilation, a nurse-led, target-directed light sedation strategy was associated with reduced delirium incidence, shorter mechanical ventilation duration, and decreased EICU length of stay, without increasing adverse events. However, no improvement in 28-day mortality was observed. Further validation through multicenter prospective randomized controlled trials is warranted to assess long-term efficacy and safety.

articles.title: A Decade Long Retrospective Cohort Study on Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Carbapenem Resistant Gram-Negative Infections in A Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCarbapenem-resistant Gram-negative (CRGN) infections are a critical global health threat, particularly in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs). This study aimed to identify independent risk factors and clinical outcomes associated with CRGN infections in critically ill children.MethodsA 10-year (2015-2024) retrospective cohort study was conducted in a tertiary PICU, including 380 patients (aged 1 month-18 years) with Gram-negative infections. Patients were stratified into CRGN (n = 106) and carbapenem-susceptible (CSGN, n = 274) groups. Primary outcomes were independent risk factors for CRGN and 30-day all-cause mortality.ResultsThe overall CRGN prevalence was 27.9% (106/380), with an estimated absolute increase of 1.10 percentage points per year; however, the temporal trend was not statistically significant (p = .204). Predominant pathogens were Klebsiella spp. (31.1%) and E. coli (24.1%). Multivariate analysis identified polymicrobial infection (OR = 6.981, p < .001), mechanical ventilation (OR = 2.124, p = .025), systemic corticosteroid use (OR = 2.072, p = .012), underlying comorbidities (OR = 1.873, p = .022), and central venous catheters (OR = 1.906, p = .030) as independent risk factors for CRGN infection. The 30-day mortality was significantly higher in the CRGN group (27.4% vs 8.8%, p < .001). CRGN infection was the strongest independent predictor of mortality (OR = 2.49, p = .043), alongside PRISM III score and multiple comorbidities. The rate of appropriate empirical therapy was critically low in the CRGN group (36.8% vs 73.4%, p < .001).ConclusionsCRGN infections in the PICU are driven by invasive procedures and immunosuppression, associated with 2.48-fold higher odds of mortality. Early identification, tailored antimicrobial stewardship, and optimization of empirical therapy are urgently required to improve survival.

articles.title: AI integration for transforming care of patients with liver diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic liver disease is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, accounting for approximately 4% of global deaths. Despite the increasingly complex care of liver disease, conventional scoring systems remain widely used to assess fibrosis and predict clinical outcomes. Although cost-effective and interpretable, these scores have limitations that may contribute to missed diagnoses and delayed treatment. Furthermore, their reliance on discrete laboratory biomarkers may inadequately reflect patients' overall clinical status and may introduce bias across demographic subgroups.

PURPOSE: This review aims to provide an overview of current applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in hepatology.

METHODS: A literature search of PubMed was conducted to identify publications addressing the application of AI in liver disease. The literature was reviewed to examine the use of AI in diagnosis, risk stratification, clinical prioritization, and liver transplantation, as well as its application across liver diseases of different etiologies. Technical challenges and barriers to clinical implementation were also considered.

CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence models can integrate multimodal data and capture complex, nonlinear relationships, potentially enabling a more comprehensive assessment of patients' physiological status and disease progression than conventional scoring systems. AI has considerable potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, risk stratification, and decision-making in liver transplantation. However, limitations relating to model interpretability, generalizability, data quality, algorithmic bias, and integration into clinical workflows must be addressed to facilitate safe, equitable, and effective implementation in hepatology.

articles.title: MRI-based proton density fat fraction combined with adipose tissue for identifying metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a non-invasive diagnostic model combining magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived proton density fat fraction (PDFF) and adipose tissue for identifying metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 197 consecutive patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) who underwent liver biopsy, MRI-PDFF, and transient elastography (TE) were retrospectively enrolled. Independent predictors of MASH were identified using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A combined model was constructed and internally validated via 1000 bootstrap resamples. The diagnostic performance was compared with that of established non-invasive tests (NITs).

RESULTS: Multivariable logistic regression analyses demonstrated that the PDFF and total adipose tissue index (TATI) were independent risk factors for MASH. The MRI-based PDFF-adipose tissue (MR-PAT) model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.866 for MASH identification. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an AUC of 0.870. The performance of the models was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. The diagnostic performance of the MR-PAT model for MASH identification was significantly better than that of all the established NITs (all p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The MR-PAT model, combining MRI-derived PDFF and TATI, provides an accurate and robust non-invasive tool for identifying MASH. It outperforms widely recognized NITs and holds promise for risk stratification in patients with MASLD.

KEY POINTS: Question MASH is a critical histological endpoint of MASLD, but reliable non-invasive tools for its assessment remain inadequate. Findings The MR-PAT model integrating MRI-based PDFF and adipose tissue quantification demonstrates robust and excellent diagnostic performance for identifying MASH. Critical Relevance Statement The MR-PAT model leverages hepatic steatosis and the adipose tissue burden to elucidate the pathophysiological mechanisms driving steatohepatitis. It can serve as an accurate, non-invasive tool for identifying MASH and holds promise for risk stratification in patients with MASLD.

articles.title: A semi-supervised diffusion model for automated segmentation of vascular plaques.
articles.journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Segmenting vascular plaques in the carotid arteries, aorta, and iliac arteries on CT is important because plaque burden relates to cardiovascular and stroke risk and can guide treatment. However, manual labeling is often infeasible and time-consuming across large vascular regions. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) can leverage unlabeled CT data to enable accurate plaque segmentation with only limited labels.

METHODS: We applied a diffusion-based semi-supervised learning (SSL) method for vascular plaque segmentation in non-contrast CT by formulating the task as multi-class segmentation of plaques and 26 adjacent anatomical structures. The method employs a teacher-student architecture with a shared diffusion encoder to learn domain-invariant feature representations and separate teacher and student decoders to decouple labeled and unlabeled data, reducing overfitting and improving robustness. To address the severe class imbalance caused by the small size of plaques, we developed a plaque-aware oversampling strategy and a labeled-data-guided training for the shared encoder and student decoder. We used 142 NIH non-contrast CT scans, divided into 119 training scans and 23 validation scans. We externally evaluated the method on 95 scans from the University of Wisconsin and 50 scans from Medipol University Mega Hospital and compared its performance with supervised nnU-Net and a strong SSL baseline.

RESULTS: The improved SSL method significantly outperformed the original SSL method and supervised training with the same architecture when using 14 labeled training scans ( p < 0.0001  ). With these 14 labeled training scans, it achieved DSC values of 58.8% and 82.3% on CTRATE and Renal Donor, respectively, within 2.7--2.8 percentage points of the same architecture trained with all 119 training scans labeled.

CONCLUSION: The SSL method segments plaques in the carotid, aortic, and iliac arteries with performance approaching that of fully supervised training while using only 14 labeled training scans, supporting scalable plaque burden assessment.

articles.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 12: a novel target for cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 12 (BMP12) is known to regulate mesenchymal differentiation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Given its structural and signaling similarities to BMP2, which promotes osteogenic phenotypic switching and pro-atherogenic responses in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), BMP12 may also contribute to vascular remodeling and atherosclerosis progression. This translational study aimed to unravel BMP12 involvement in cardiovascular disease (CVD). BMP12 effects on atherogenesis-related processes in VSMCs in absence or presence of BMP type I receptor inhibitors (DMH2 and LDN-193189) were evaluated. Additionally, circulating BMP12 levels were measured in a well-characterized cohort of patients with CV risk factors and correlated with cardiometabolic disorders and vascular damage markers. Results from the experimental study showed increased migration and calcification in BMP12-treated VSMCs. Mechanistically, BMP12 induced expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2 and ALP) and genes related to cellular migration (Mmp9), while reducing contractile marker Desmin. These pro-atherogenic effects were blocked using BMP type I receptor inhibitors. Furthermore, the clinical study revealed higher serum BMP12 levels in patients with CVD and type 2 diabetes. Moreover, circulating BMP12 concentrations were elevated in patients with carotid and femoral plaques, correlating with plaque volume. Notably, BMP12 emerged as an independent predictor of femoral atherosclerosis. Collectively, these findings identify BMP12 as a previously unrecognized mediator of vascular remodeling, promoting pro-atherogenic effects in VSMCs through canonical BMP signaling. The association between elevated circulating BMP12 levels and subclinical vascular damage further supports its potential value as a contributor to atherosclerosis progression and as a promising novel candidate biomarker for CV risk.

articles.title: Acute and Chronic Effects of Parachute-Resisted Sprint Training on Sprint Performance and Sprint Mechanics: A Systematic Review with GRADE Assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parachute-resisted sprint training (PRST) is a practical field-based resisted-sprint method that uses aerodynamic drag to provide sprint-specific overload. Although PRST has been widely used in athletic settings, evidence on its acute mechanical effects and chronic training adaptations remains heterogeneous.

OBJECTIVES: This systematic review aimed to synthesize the acute and chronic effects of PRST on sprint performance, sprint mechanics, neuromuscular responses, and sprint-related physiological outcomes in healthy, physically active, and athletic populations.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus on 17th May 2026. Original empirical studies were eligible if they examined PRST or parachute-resisted sprinting and reported outcomes related to sprint performance, biomechanics, neuromuscular responses, or sprint-related physiology. Studies were synthesized narratively and grouped into acute and chronic evidence streams. Methodological quality was assessed using the Modified Downs and Black checklist, and certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included (8 acute and 9 chronic). In acute comparisons, PRST consistently reduced sprint velocity or increased sprint time; where directly reported, velocity reductions were approximately 3.4-6% relative to unresisted sprinting. Larger parachute conditions generally produced greater velocity decrements and changes in horizontal force or impulse variables. Chronic studies reported improvements in selected sprint outcomes, including 0-10 m, 10-20 m, and 0-20 m splits in one randomized study; other studies reported improvements such as 3.48% in 60-yd performance and 0.618 s in 100-m performance. However, chronic studies' findings were heterogeneous, and evidence for maximal velocity, neuromuscular or energetic outcomes, and population-specific effects remained limited.

CONCLUSIONS: PRST appears to provide a practical, sprint-specific overload and may improve selected sprint performance outcomes. However, the current evidence base is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous protocols, poor quantification of resistance, inconsistent reporting of outcomes, and limited comparator control. Based on GRADE, confidence in the evidence is generally 'low' to 'very low' across most outcomes. Trial Registration (OSF) https://osf.io/56nct DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/8SJW4.

articles.title: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a heritable cardiac disorder commonly linked to alterations in desmosomal proteins. While desmosomal dysfunction is a recognized pathogenic mechanism, the early molecular remodeling that precedes clinical manifestations remains unclear. Here we used a mouse model with inducible cardiomyocyte-specific knockout of Pkp2 (encoding plakophilin-2) and performed time-resolved mass spectrometry-based proteomics to map disease progression from early PKP2 loss to structural remodeling. Molecular changes preceded phenotypic abnormalities, and spatial asymmetry was evident, with earlier and more pronounced proteome remodeling in the right ventricle despite comparable PKP2 depletion in both ventricles. Downregulation of protein networks spanning desmosomes, sarcomeres and mitochondria suggests their functional coupling, with mitochondrial remodeling emerging as an early and progressively worsening feature. Intervention with honokiol attenuated changes across the major protein networks, highlighting mitochondrial pathways as promising therapeutic targets and honokiol as a potential strategy to delay arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy progression. Our findings provide critical insights into the concealed stage of disease progression and identify molecular targets for early intervention.

articles.title: Systemic exposure to typhoid toxin primes the murine vascular endothelium for intestinal perforation during Salmonella Typhi infection.
articles.abstract: Intestinal perforation is a late complication and the leading cause of death in typhoid fever, but its mechanism has remained undefined. Here, using sequential exposure to the PltC form of typhoid toxin followed by oral Salmonella Typhi infection, we develop a mouse model of late-stage human typhoid, when circulating toxin precedes the onset of intestinal pathology. Systemic exposure to the toxin renders otherwise resistant mice susceptible to oral infection and establishes a transient vascular endothelial priming state, resulting in vascular injury, haemorrhage and lethal intestinal perforation localized to Peyer's patches. These lesions were accompanied by the appearance in blood of microbiota-derived taxa, consistent with translocation across a breached small-intestinal barrier. Lethality required the SPI-1 type-III secretion system (T3SS), which drives intestinal inflammation, but not the SPI-2 T3SS, which drives systemic infection, indicating that death results from intestinal rather than disseminated infection. Although PltC-typhoid toxin causes leucopaenia, loss of circulating white cells was not sufficient for sensitization. Endothelial-specific expression of CMAH, which masks the toxin's Neu5Ac receptors, prevented priming and disease. These findings define intestinal perforation as a typhoid toxin-dependent vascular-barrier disease.

articles.title: Autophagy in macrophages curtails IL-1α-mediated immune priming against lung infections.
articles.abstract: Host resistance to infection is initially determined by how well primed the innate immune system is to respond on first exposure to an invader, yet the mechanisms underlying this priming remain incompletely understood. Here we found that basal autophagy suppressed the expression of Il1a in alveolar macrophages (AMs) and an otherwise protective innate immune priming against Staphylococcus aureus and influenza A virus (IAV), independently of the microbiome and adaptive immunity. Inactivating autophagy genes in AMs led to elevated expression of IL-1α in AMs, which subsequently enhanced IL-1R-MyD88 signaling in neutrophils and increased the recruitment of myeloid cells to the lung. As a result, autophagy-deficient mice showed more efficient clearance of S. aureus along with reduced lung damage and inflammation. Similar to genetic inactivation of autophagy, overexpression of IL-1α in AMs conferred broad spectrum protection against S. aureus and IAV, suggesting a possible strategy to fine-tune immune responses to combat important respiratory infections.

articles.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial.
articles.abstract: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I-IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03161353 .

articles.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.
articles.abstract: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.
