articles.title: Local albumin excess exacerbates Candida albicans-induced inflammasome activation linked with hyperinflammation during vulvovaginal candidiasis.
articles.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans, where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans. This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans-induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

articles.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
articles.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. The platform's utility is exemplified through various use cases, including antimicrobial resistance tracking, biomarker prediction, microbiome classification, and functional annotation of key microbes. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

articles.title: Bone anabolic agents repair alveolar bone damaged by diabetes in mice.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a chronic metabolic disorder that significantly impacts skeletal health, including bones of the oral cavity, where alveolar bone is particularly susceptible due to its high remodeling rate and sensitivity to systemic metabolic changes. Using a mouse model of established T2D induced by high-fat diet and streptozotocin, we investigated the effects of the FDA-approved bone anabolic agents parathyroid hormone (PTH) and abaloparatide (ABL) on alveolar bone. In non-diabetic mice, PTH and ABL stimulated both bone formation and resorption, resulting in no net change in alveolar bone mass. In contrast, these agents selectively increased bone formation in T2D mice without further enhancing the already elevated resorption, leading to net alveolar bone gain. This anabolic effect involves suppression of sclerostin and Dickkopf-1 (Dkk-1) in osteocytes and activation of Wnt signaling in periodontal ligament cells. Studies using DMP1-Cre;PTH1Rfl/fl mice demonstrated that osteocytic PTH1R is essential for the anabolic effects but not for the bone resorption-promoting effects of PTH and ABL. These findings reveal a dual mechanism of PTH1R signaling in oral bone remodeling and suggest therapeutic strategies to restore alveolar bone and improve tooth retention and implant osseointegration in diabetic patients.

articles.title: Intra-Provincial Variation of Brief Substance Use Withdrawal Hospitalizations in Ontario, Canada: A Cross-Sectional Study: Variations intra-provinciales des hospitalisations de courte durée pour sevrage de substances en Ontario (Canada) : une étude transversale.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
articles.abstract: ObjectiveIn Ontario, substance use disorders are the top reason for mental health and addictions-related hospitalizations, many of which are related to substance withdrawal. Our objective was to identify briefer withdrawal-related hospitalizations that are potentially manageable in medically supported community-based settings, assess the degree of intra-provincial variation for these types of admissions, and examine the health care utilization of these patients.MethodsWe conducted a population-based, cross-sectional study using linked health administrative data for Ontario residents hospitalized with alcohol- or opioid-use withdrawal between January 1, 2019 to December 31, 2021. Brief withdrawal admissions (BWAs) were defined as hospitalizations with a stay of 0-4 days and without intensive care. We calculated BWA rates per 100,000 person-years (PY), overall and for health regions within the province. Log-binomial regression models were used to examine differences in health care utilization in the year following a BWA compared with the year prior to admission.ResultsThere were 12,544 BWAs in Ontario during our study period (28.6 admissions per 100,000 PY) with a greater than 7-fold difference (p < 0.001) between the provincial health regions with the highest (North West region, 149.5 per 100,000 PY) and lowest (Central region, 20.8 per 100,000 PY) rate. In the year following a BWA, 30% of patients required hospital admission and 50% had an emergency department visit for substance use, which represented a significant increase of 63% (Relative Rate (RR) = 1.63; 95% Confidence Interval (95% CI) 1.55-1.71, P-value <0.001) and 11% (RR = 1.11; 95% CI 1.08-1.14, P-value <0.001), compared with the year prior to admission, respectively.ConclusionsUnderstanding the variation in BWAs, and the significant health care use following such events, is vital in supporting provincial efforts to improve withdrawal management. Future research should examine if providing more resources to community-based withdrawal services to manage BWAs results in improved patient outcomes and reduced acute care capacity/costs.

articles.title: Factors associated with Severe Balance Impairment After Right-Hemisphere Stroke: The Role of Spatial Neglect and Lateropulsion: A Secondary Analysis of Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study POSTIM.
articles.abstract: BackgroundBalance impairment remains a major concern after right-hemisphere stroke (RHS), even after regaining unsupported standing, reflecting multifactorial and insufficiently explored postural control deficits.ObjectiveTo identify factors associated with balance impairment and to assess its severity using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), in RHS patients who have recovered unsupported standing but exhibit marked weight-bearing asymmetry.MethodsThis cross-sectional secondary analysis used baseline data (May 2013-May 2018) from a multicenter randomized controlled trial on weight-bearing asymmetry, across eight French rehabilitation centers. Patients aged 18-80 with a first right supratentorial stroke within 9 months, standing unassisted for 30 s with eyes closed, and bearing <40% body weight on the paretic leg were included. BBS scores <45/56 defined severe balance impairment associated with increased fall risk. Lower-limb motor deficits, spasticity, sensory function, lateropulsion, spatial neglect, and body perception were analyzed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression.ResultsAmong 82 patients (mean age 59.3 ± 10.3 years; post-stroke delay 91.3 ± 59.6 days), 61(74%) had a BBS <45/56. In the multivariable model (n = 67), spatial neglect (OR 11.15; 95%CI [1.29-96.24]; p = 0.028), lateropulsion (OR 3.54; 95%CI [1.10-11.39]; p = 0.034), and lower-limb motor deficit (OR 0.91; 95%CI [0.85-0.96]; p = 0.002) were independently associated with balance impairment.ConclusionIn RHS patients with marked postural asymmetry and recently recovered unsupported standing, severe balance impairment was associated with spatial neglect and lateropulsion. These factors may represent important targets for rehabilitation, although this cross-sectional analysis precludes causal inference. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01677091.

articles.title: Integrating fall detection technology in healthcare: A feasibility study of fall sensor usability.
articles.abstract: BackgroundFalls are a significant risk among stroke patients, and effective fall risk assessment and communication between hospital and primary care are essential to prevent adverse events.ObjectiveThis study evaluates current practices in fall risk assessment and documentation of falls and communication. It also explores the development and pilot testing of a digital fall sensor system to support clinicians in stroke rehabilitation.MethodsA prospective study of a stroke rehabilitation cohort (n = 31) and an assessed fall risk screening quality and information transfer across care transitions. Concurrently, technical development and laboratory usability testing of a wearable fall sensor were conducted.ResultsDocumentation of fall prevention interventions was present in 80% of cases. Only 45% of discharge reports contained relevant fall risk information for primary care providers. The fall sensor during first test detected correctly 12 of 12 fall incidents with unknown false alarm performance. During the second lab test the sensor detected correctly 8 of 12 fall incidents with no false alarms during 10 simulated movements suspected to cause false alarms. Clinical deployment was delayed due to IT infrastructure and regulatory requirements.ConclusionsThere is a critical need to standardize fall risk documentation and improve communication pathways to ensure continuity of care. Laboratory testing demonstrated promising sensor performance, but clinical validation is required before implementation can be recommended.

articles.title: Circulating miR-223 and NLRP3 expression and their discriminatory performance in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a major cause of mortality and disability. Inflammation contributes to ischemic brain injury, and circulating miR-223 and NLRP3 may reflect inflammatory responses. This study evaluated their expression and diagnostic performance in AIS.

METHODS: In this case-control study, serum samples were obtained from 45 patients with AIS and 45 healthy controls. Patient blood samples were collected within 24 hours of hospitalization. miR-223 and NLRP3 expression were quantified by quantitative real-time PCR. Spearman correlation, ROC analysis, and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

RESULTS: Circulating miR-223 and NLRP3 expression levels were significantly higher in AIS than in healthy controls (both p < 0.0001). ROC analysis showed AUCs of 0.9704 for NLRP3 and 0.8953 for miR-223. In multivariable logistic regression including age, gender, creatinine, miR-223, and NLRP3, NLRP3 was independently associated with AIS (adjusted OR = 0.569, 95% CI: 0.394-0.822, p = 0.003), whereas miR-223 was not (adjusted OR = 0.943, 95% CI: 0.638-1.395, p = 0.769). Age, gender, and creatinine were not independently associated with AIS.

CONCLUSION: miR-223 and NLRP3 showed significant differences and discriminatory performance in AIS. NLRP3 was independently associated with AIS, whereas miR-223 was not. Prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Tree and neighborhood damage have distinct effects on delayed mortality after a severe hurricane.
articles.abstract: Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual-tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting to disentangle the causal contributions of mortality drivers. Leveraging post-hurricane census data for nearly 4000 trees in the Luquillo Forest Dynamics Plot, Puerto Rico, we used a causal inference framework combined with Bayesian multilevel models to estimate the effect of individual- and neighborhood-scale damage on delayed tree mortality following Hurricane Maria (2017). Individual damage effects depended on species identity and tree size. Stem break emerged as the most lethal form of damage across the community. Neighborhood damage was associated with elevated mortality following Hurricane Maria, independent of focal tree damage. This effect was strongest among large trees, consistent with disproportionately high physiological stress resulting from greater inherent metabolic demands, refoliation energy costs, and evapotranspiration following canopy recovery. Severe biomass loss (> 75% crown loss) buffered large trees from negative neighborhood effects, revealing a positive pruning effect on survival. Our study advances mechanistic understanding of delayed tree mortality, while also suggesting how mortality patterns may shift with expected increases in disturbance severity under a warming climate.

articles.title: Screening for occult cancer in patients with unprovoked VTE: Evolving evidence and emerging risk prediction tools.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) can represent the first clinical manifestation of an underlying occult malignancy, particularly when unprovoked. Large cohort studies and meta-analyses have reported that the risk of cancer is markedly increased in the first 6-12 months following unprovoked VTE, with a 3- to 4-fold higher risk compared with provoked VTE events, particularly among older patients. Certain clinical presentations, including upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), bilateral DVT, splanchnic vein thrombosis, and cerebral venous thrombosis, are associated with a higher prevalence of occult cancer and warrant targeted investigations. Four randomised controlled trials and subsequent meta-analyses comparing limited versus extensive screening strategies (including whole-body CT scan and PET/CT scan) consistently demonstrated earlier cancer detection without a corresponding reduction in cancer-related or all-cause mortality, while extensive screening carries additional costs, radiation exposure, and risks of false-positive findings. Several clinical risk-prediction scores (RIETE, SOME, VTE-Malignancy, CAVE, and machine learning-based models) have been developed to identify patients at higher risk of occult cancer who might derive greater benefit from extensive screening. None of these scores demonstrates sufficiently robust discriminative performance for routine clinical use. Based on the available evidence, we propose a pragmatic, individualised algorithm favouring limited screening for most patients with unprovoked VTE, reserving extensive screening for those with high-risk clinical features following shared decision-making. Ongoing trials and emerging risk-stratification tools may help refine future screening strategies, balancing the benefit of early cancer detection against the risks and costs of extensive investigation.

articles.title: [Early cardiac remodeling in short-duration T2DM: Benchmarking 85 cases against norms in an Algerian population].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is traditionally viewed as a late complication of chronic hyperglycemia, but emerging evidence suggests it may manifest early in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), preceding prolonged metabolic exposure.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether early cardiac remodeling markers, particularly diastolic dysfunction, are already present in patients with short-duration T2DM (< 5 years).

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 86 T2DM patients at a university hospital in an Algerian population (2024). Echocardiography was performed using a GE Vivid E95 system. Diastolic dysfunction was defined using ASE/EACVI criteria. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors.

RESULTS: Diastolic dysfunction was present in 20% (17/86) of patients despite recent disease onset. The study population had a mean diabetes duration of 1.8±2.0 years, mean age of 54.7±8.9 years, and mean HbA1c of 8.9±0.27%. Hypertension was present in 35.3% (30/86) of patients, and obesity (BMI≥30kg/m2) in 29.5% (25/86). Impaired myocardial relaxation was widespread: lateral e'<10cm/s in 49.4%, septal e'<7cm/s in 24.4%, and elevated E/e' in 29.1%. Contrary to traditional assumptions, dysfunction was not significantly different between well-controlled (HbA1c<7%) and poorly controlled patients (27.3 vs. 17.2%, P=0.356). Systolic blood pressure was the only independent predictor of diastolic dysfunction (OR 1.07 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.02-1.13, P=0.008). Neither HbA1c (P=0.324) nor diabetes duration (P=0.863) showed significant associations.

CONCLUSION: Early cardiac remodeling occurs frequently in short-duration T2DM, independent of glycemic control and disease chronicity. This challenges the traditional view that diabetic cardiomyopathy requires prolonged hyperglycemia. Systolic blood pressure is the sole predictor, suggesting mechanisms beyond metabolic control alone. Systematic echocardiographic screening at T2DM diagnosis may be warranted to detect subclinical dysfunction and prevent progression to heart failure.

articles.title: Outcomes of a randomized-controlled digital weight management program over 2.5-years.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Coaching-led digital weight-loss interventions are successful in the short-term, but have limited evidence supporting long-term changes. This study evaluated a commercially available behavioral weight-management program compared to digital control on initial and long-term outcomes.

METHODS: A total of 684 participants were screened to achieve a sample of English-speaking individuals 18-60 years old with a body mass index (BMI; kg/m2) > 27 kg/m2 without contraindications to using a smartphone program. In a single-blinded, parallel-group trial, a centralized computer-generated program randomized 600 participants (n = 302 intervention; n = 298 control) to a 6-month intervention or control with a maintenance phase during months 7-30. The primary outcome was change in BMI; secondary outcomes included effects on diet, physical activity, sleep, quality of life, psychosocial functioning, and health status.

RESULTS: Fifty-seven participants withdrew from the study and all future assessments; 78% of the sample completed 6-months and 65% completed 30-month follow-up. All available data were used under assumptions of missing at random. Latent growth curve models showed the differences were not significant [β = 0.99, 95%CI = -1.38, 3.36, d = .17, 95%CI = -0.24, 0.58]. Over 30-months, changes for intervention and control were 0.13 kg/m2 (SD=3.09) and 0.58 kg/m2 (SD=3.64), respectively, a significant difference [β = -4.42, 95%CI = -8.72, -0.12, d = -0.76, 95%CI = -1.51, -0.02].

CONCLUSIONS: Although the acute effects on self-reported BMI were not significant, the use of coaching-led weight loss led to better two-year BMI outcomes, and were greater for those at a lower BMI. Interventions using personal support may be important for realizing longer-term benefits of digital interventions.

articles.title: Urinary calcium excretion as a potential biomarker of diuretic resistance in heart failure.
Hypertonic saline in acute heart failure: Caution in interpreting real-world evidence.
Strategies and tools for enhancing early detection of pancreatic cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAC) remains the most lethal malignancies, with a 5-year survival rate of only around 12%. The dismal prognosis is largely attributable to late diagnosis, as early PAC is frequently asymptomatic and radiologically inconspicuous. Contemporary international guidelines recommend surveillance for well-defined high-risk groups, particularly carriers of pathogenic germline mutations such as BRCA2, STK11, and CDKN2A, as well as familial pancreatic cancer kindreds. In these settings, endoscopic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging are the recommended surveillance modalities. Recent advances in biomarker discovery, including circulating tumor DNA, methylation signatures of cell-free DNA, and extracellular vesicles, have demonstrated encouraging results, particularly when combined with CA19-9. Paraneoplastic phenomena such as pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes and cancer-induced cachexia provide additional opportunities for earlier clinical recognition. Parallel progress has been achieved in artificial intelligence-driven radiomics analysis and deep learning algorithms, which can increase the sensitivity of cross-sectional imaging for small or otherwise occult lesions. The integration of clinical risk stratification, molecular biomarkers, and AI-enhanced imaging represents a promising framework to shift diagnosis toward surgically resectable stages. This review synthesizes the current evidence, highlights recent advances, and discusses practical considerations for physicians to facilitate earlier detection of PAC.

articles.title: Clinical characterization of LDL-c/ApoB discordance in the metabolic patient: The "false control" as an independent marker of subclinical atherosclerosis.
articles.journal: Clinica e investigacion en arteriosclerosis : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Arteriosclerosis
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) is the cornerstone of lipid-lowering therapy, but it may underestimate the true atherogenic burden in patients with cardiometabolic risk. The discordance between LDL-c (mass) and apolipoprotein B (ApoB, particle number) creates a state of hidden residual risk. The objective of this study was to evaluate the prevalence of this discordance and determine its clinical association with subclinical atherosclerosis.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 103 high-risk patients (mean age 60 years; 62% men) treated in Internal Medicine consultations. Anthropometric parameters, glycemic, and lipid profiles were analyzed. Discordance was determined using the percentile method, and the "false control" status was defined based on the achievement of therapeutic targets according to clinical guidelines. Cardiovascular risk in patients without a previous cardiovascular event was estimated using the SCORE2/SCORE2-OP model. Subclinical atherosclerosis was defined as the presence of carotid plaque assessed by ultrasound. Spearman correlation tests, Kruskal-Wallis comparisons, and a multivariate logistic regression model adjusted for age, sex, and HbA1c were used.

RESULTS: A sample with a high metabolic burden (80% hypertensive, 52% diabetic, BMI 31.9±5.4kg/m2) was included. A total lack of correlation was observed between LDL-c and ApoB (rho=-0.021; p=0.833). Twenty-nine percent presented high-ApoB discordance (subjects whose ApoB percentile exceeded that of LDL-c by>10 units), and 25% were in a state of "false control" (LDL-c on target with elevated ApoB). Patients with high-ApoB discordance showed a more adverse metabolic profile (HbA1c 6.3 vs. 5.8%; p=0.014). Plaque prevalence was significantly higher in the "false control" group (73.1%) than in the "true control" group (36.4%; p=0.035). Concordant lipid control was independently associated with the absence of plaque (OR 6.32; 95% CI: 1.43-27.87; p=0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: LDL-c/ApoB discordance is highly prevalent in high-risk patients. In this context, the clinical situation of "false control" is independently associated with a higher burden of subclinical atherosclerosis. The systematic measurement of ApoB is essential to identify this hidden residual risk and optimize cardiovascular prevention in patients with a complex metabolic profile.

articles.title: Diagnostic Yield of Ultrasound-Guided Percutaneous Pleural Biopsy in Pleural Infection.
Effect of remimazolam versus propofol anaesthesia on postoperative delirium in neurovascular surgery: a randomised noninferiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Propofol-based total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) is commonly used in neurovascular surgery, in which intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring limits inhalation anaesthetic use. However, propofol causes hypotension, and prolonged infusions can delay emergence. Remimazolam, a benzodiazepine whose effects are reversible with flumazenil, has been associated with less intraoperative hypotension than propofol, but its use raises concerns about postoperative delirium (POD). We tested whether remimazolam-based TIVA is noninferior to propofol-based TIVA for POD.

METHODS: In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised noninferiority trial, adults undergoing elective intracranial aneurysm clipping, arteriovenous malformation resection, microvascular decompression, or superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass received remimazolam-based TIVA with flumazenil reversal at emergence, or propofol-based TIVA, both with remifentanil. The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of POD within 5 days, assessed twice daily with the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined delirium (3D-CAM). The prespecified noninferiority margin was 10 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 686 patients in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, POD occurred in 44 of 344 (12.8%) with remimazolam and 37 of 342 (10.8%) with propofol (risk difference, 1.97 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.85 to 6.80; one-sided P<0.001 for noninferiority); per-protocol results were consistent. Hypotensive burden below a mean arterial pressure threshold of 65 mm Hg was lower in the remimazolam group (median, 0 vs 7.5 mm Hg min; P<0.001), and tracheal extubation in the operating room was more frequent (85.2% vs 67.3%).

CONCLUSIONS: Remimazolam-based TIVA met the prespecified criterion for noninferiority to propofol-based TIVA with respect to postoperative delirium after elective neurovascular surgery. Interpretation should take into account that the observed incidence of postoperative delirium was lower than anticipated when the noninferiority margin was defined.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06115031 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

articles.title: Total Pain in People With Trigeminal Neuralgia: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a rare but profoundly disabling condition characterized by paroxysmal, electric shock-like facial pain. Although its burden is recognized as multidimensional, it remains unclear to what extent the literature has addressed suffering beyond physical symptoms.

OBJECTIVES: To map how pain in people with TN, including its physical, psychological, social, and spiritual dimensions, has been described and operationalized in the scientific literature.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology. Five databases (MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and CINAHL) and gray literature via Google Scholar were searched. Studies of any design involving adults with TN and addressing at least one dimension of Total Pain were eligible. Data extraction was supported by NotebookLM and verified by two independent reviewers.

RESULTS: Forty-four studies published between 1983 and 2026 were included. Pain intensity was the most frequently investigated outcome (72.72%), predominantly assessed using unidimensional scales. Anxiety and depression were the main psychological outcomes (36.36%), largely measured with standardized psychometric instruments; qualitative studies also described fear, hopelessness, emotional exhaustion, and suicidal ideation. The social dimension was mainly operationalized through functional impairment and social participation, while qualitative findings highlighted isolation, relationship disruption, occupational difficulties, and delegitimization of suffering in healthcare settings. No study investigated the spiritual dimension.

CONCLUSION: The literature on TN remains predominantly biomedical in its assessment of pain. Psychological and social dimensions are underexplored, and the spiritual dimension is entirely absent. Future research should adopt multidimensional, person-centered frameworks, including Total Pain.

NURSING PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Nurses should adopt multidimensional, person-centered pain assessments in trigeminal neuralgia, addressing physical, psychological, and social suffering. Spiritual concerns should also be explored, given their absence in the reviewed literature. Nursing care should recognize patients' lived experiences and promote holistic, individualized interventions.

articles.title: Attitudes, beliefs and perceptions of healthcare professionals regarding the role of physiotherapy in the management of critically ill patients in Intensive Care Units in Castilla-La Mancha.
Liver Viscosity Dominates Liver Stiffness in MASLD: A Multiparametric Ultrasound Study With IPTW Adjustment and Explainable Machine Learning.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Liver stiffness measured by shear wave elastography (SWE) is widely used as a noninvasive surrogate for fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, stiffness may be influenced by multiple biomechanical factors beyond fibrosis, and the relative contributions of inflammation-related viscosity, steatosis, and metabolic parameters remain unclear.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 573 adults with MASLD underwent multiparametric ultrasound, including SWE, viscosity plane-wave ultrasound (ViPLUS), and attenuation (ATT). Participants were stratified into lower-body mass index (BMI) (BMI < 24 kg/m²) and higher-BMI (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²) groups. Covariate balance was achieved using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Multivariable linear regression, subgroup analyses, and interaction testing were performed to identify independent determinants of liver stiffness. Machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting [XGBoost]) with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for exploratory feature attribution to identify key determinants of liver stiffness rather than to develop a standalone clinical diagnostic or prediction tool.

RESULTS: After IPTW adjustment, prespecified clinical covariates were well balanced between BMI groups. Hepatic viscosity (ViPLUS) was the strongest independent determinant of liver stiffness (β = 5.80, 95% confidence interval: 5.33-6.27; p < 0.001), corresponding to an approximately 0.58 kPa increase in SWE per 0.1 Pa·s increase in ViPLUS. The association remained dominant in both BMI groups and was greater in the higher-BMI group (approximately 0.63 vs. 0.51 kPa per 0.1 Pa·s). The contribution of viscosity was consistently dominant across lower-BMI and higher-BMI subgroups and appeared stronger in the higher-BMI group. SHAP-based feature attribution identified ViPLUS as the most influential model-derived feature associated with SWE, consistent with the regression findings. Nonlinear associations were observed for aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, while triglycerides and glucose showed no significant nonlinear relationships. Notably, a subset of lower-BMI individuals exhibited high-risk hepatic phenotypes despite lower BMI.

CONCLUSION: Hepatic viscosity is the dominant determinant of liver stiffness in MASLD, with even a 0.1 Pa·s increase in ViPLUS corresponding to an approximately 0.58 kPa increase in SWE. These findings suggest that liver stiffness reflects viscosity-related viscoelastic alterations rather than fibrosis alone. Multiparametric ultrasound, particularly the integration of viscosity and stiffness, may provide incremental value for identifying high-risk individuals, including those with lower BMI.

articles.title: The effects of wrist and elbow restrictions on vascular complications and agitation in mechanically ventilated children: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical restraints are required in pediatric intensive care units, with wrist restraints commonly used for mechanically ventilated children. However, they may contribute to pressure-related complications and agitation. This study compared the effects of wrist and elbow restraints on vascular complications and agitation in mechanically ventilated children.

METHODS: A randomized crossover clinical trial was conducted between August 2022 and May 2023 in a PICU. Mechanically ventilated children aged 6 months to 7 years were randomly assigned to two groups. Group A received elbow followed by wrist restraint, whereas Group B received the reverse sequence. Palm temperature, radial pulse rate, hand edema, erythema, and agitation were assessed before, during, and after each intervention. Data were analyzed using SPSS; p<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Forty-eight children were included. Elbow restraint resulted in a greater reduction in hand edema than wrist restraint (p=0.008). During the first intervention period, palm temperature was higher and hand edema and erythema were lower with elbow restraint (p<0.05). Overall, no significant differences were observed between restraint types in palm temperature, erythema, radial pulse rate, or RASS scores (p>0.05).

CONCLUSION: Elbow restraint may be a suitable alternative to wrist restraint for short-term use in mechanically ventilated children. Further research is needed to establish the safest restraint practices for prolonged use.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Elbow restraint may be considered when upper-limb restraint is required without restricting trunk movement. Alternating restraint sites may help limit local tissue effects but requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Associations of Plasma Branched-Chain Amino Acids With Incident Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease by Sex and Type 2 Diabetes Status Among Chinese Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on associations between branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains limited, particularly in Chinese populations. We investigated associations between BCAAs and ASCVD and whether they differed by sex and Type 2 diabetes (T2D).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a case-cohort design within a Chinese prospective cohort, we included a random subcohort (n = 2163) and incident ASCVD cases (n = 674). Plasma BCAA concentrations were quantified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations of BCAAs with incident ASCVD were evaluated using Prentice-weighted Cox proportional hazards models, with stratified analyses and interaction tests by sex and T2D. Mediation analyses assessed the contribution of BCAAs to associations between T2D and ASCVD.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 10.3 years, plasma BCAAs were positively associated with ASCVD. Associations appeared more pronounced among female participants, although interaction tests by sex were not statistically significant. Among female participants, significant associations were only observed in those with T2D, with hazard ratios (95% CIs) of 2.014 (1.185-3.423), 1.867 (1.142-3.052), 1.814 (1.071-3.078) and 2.030 (1.197-3.442) per standard deviation increment in ln-transformed total BCAA, isoleucine, leucine and valine, respectively. Additive interactions with T2D were detected for total BCAA and leucine. For male participants, no significant associations were observed, regardless of T2D status. Notably, total BCAA, leucine and valine partially mediated the association between T2D and ASCVD among female participants, with mediated proportions of 7.89%, 7.68% and 6.76%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher plasma BCAA concentrations were associated with increased incident ASCVD risk, supporting their potential role as metabolic markers of ASCVD.

articles.title: Ceramides, Particularly Those Containing Very-Long-Chain Saturated Fatty Acids, Are Independently Associated With the Triglyceride-Glucose Index in European Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is associated with insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease (CVD), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. As ceramides are implicated in both insulin resistance and CVD, we investigated the association between the TyG index and plasma ceramides in individuals with Type 2 diabetes (T2D).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We measured total plasma ceramides and seven ceramide species (C16:0, C18:0, C20:0, C22:0, C24:1, C24:0 and C26:0) in 289 European individuals with T2D using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations with the TyG index were assessed using univariate and multivariate analyses, including linear regression as the primary analysis.

RESULTS: Total ceramides, long-chain saturated fatty acid (LCSFA) ceramides and very-long-chain saturated fatty acid (VLSFA) ceramides were significantly higher in the upper TyG quartiles. The TyG index correlated significantly (p < 0.0001) with total ceramides, LCSFA ceramides, VLSFA ceramides and all ceramide species except C26:0. Multivariable analyses identified total and VLSFA ceramides as independently associated with the TyG index (p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study shows, for the first time, an independent association between the TyG index and plasma ceramides, particularly VLSFA ceramides, in people with T2D. Further research is warranted to elucidate whether this association contributes to the link between the TyG index, insulin resistance and CVD.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02045563.

articles.title: Early Treatment Trajectory and Long-Term Persistence to Semaglutide for Obesity: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess semaglutide persistence in obesity management, identify factors associated with discontinuation and examine early tirzepatide adoption.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services records of adults without diabetes initiating Wegovy between January and May 2025. Discontinuation was defined as a gap exceeding 60 days after medication coverage ended. Multivariable Cox models, including a Day-90 landmark analysis, assessed discontinuation. Tirzepatide adoption was evaluated following its December 2025 coverage introduction.

RESULTS: Among 34 309 participants (67.0% women; mean age 44.6 years), cumulative discontinuation reached 36.5% at 180 days and 67.6% at 365 days. Arab population sector (hazard ratio [HR] 1.65, 95% CI 1.59-1.72), low socioeconomic status (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.09-1.17) and current smoking (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.09-1.17) were associated with discontinuation. In the day-90 landmark cohort (n = 28 218), remaining on 0.25 versus 1.0 mg was associated with subsequent discontinuation (HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.72-2.06), substantially attenuated after adjustment for early refill adherence. Each percentage-point smaller BMI reduction was associated with 3% higher discontinuation hazard (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.03-1.04). Following tirzepatide availability, 2908 of 33 936 eligible participants (8.6%) initiated treatment over a median 3.1-month observation period. Adoption was associated with higher socioeconomic status and baseline BMI.

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide discontinuation was common and associated with sociodemographic and early treatment characteristics. Day-90 dose and early weight-loss response may help identify discontinuation risk. Socioeconomic differences suggest inequalities in sustained obesity pharmacotherapy access.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Risk of Postmenopausal Bleeding in Women: An Active-Comparator, New-User Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: A recent case report and pharmacovigilance reports have suggested a possible association between sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and postmenopausal bleeding (PMB), but population-level evidence is lacking. We evaluated the risk of PMB among women aged 55-90 years initiating SGLT2 inhibitors versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted an active-comparator, new-user cohort study using data from the All of Us Research Program. Women aged 55-90 years who newly initiated either an SGLT2 inhibitor or a DPP-4 inhibitor were included. The primary outcome was the first recorded PMB during follow-up. Propensity score (PS) matching, with exact matching on calendar period, was used to control for confounding. Hazard ratios (HRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox and Poisson regression models.

RESULTS: Among 2603 women, 1328 initiated SGLT2 inhibitors and 1275 initiated DPP-4 inhibitors. After 1:1 PS matching, 650 pairs achieved good covariate balance. In the matched cohort, 37 and 34 PMB events occurred over 2248.2 and 2374.2 person-years, respectively. SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was not associated with increased PMB risk (HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.70-1.84; IRR 1.15, 95% CI 0.71-1.87). Sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary findings.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was not associated with a significantly increased PMB risk compared with DPP-4 inhibitor initiation. These findings did not provide evidence of increased PMB risk with SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, although wide confidence intervals and limited outcome events warrant confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Shifting viral aetiology, codetection and age-specific mortality in severe acute respiratory infection in Brazil, 2022-2025: a nationwide surveillance study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral aetiology and codetection among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications have evolved post-COVID-19. We examined temporal patterns, age heterogeneity, and severe outcome associations in Brazil.

METHODS: We analysed nationwide SIVEP-Gripe SARI records (2022-2025; extracted July 2026) with RT-PCR viral detection. Seven mutually exclusive categories were evaluated using robust Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for SARI-attributed mortality and a severe composite outcome (ICU admission, invasive ventilation, or death).

RESULTS: Among 447,107 virus-positive records, 7.2% involved codetections and 25.4% included RSV. Isolated SARS-CoV-2 declined from 72.4% (2022) to 6.8% (2025), while codetections rose from 3.0% to 11.2%. Compared to isolated RSV, mortality was higher for codetection without RSV (aRR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.67-1.94), isolated SARS-CoV-2 (1.62, 1.54-1.70), and codetection with RSV (1.40, 1.27-1.55). Associations varied by age ($p < .001$). Among RSV-positive cases, codetection conferred increased mortality risk (aRR 1.46, 1.32-1.61). Excluding isolated SARS-CoV-2 attenuated the 2025-versus-2022 codetection prevalence ratio from 1.85 to 1.10.

CONCLUSIONS: Viral detections shifted towards greater heterogeneity, strongly driven by changing surveillance composition. Varying testing indications and panels limit causal inference. Integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting is essential; surveillance proportions do not reflect population incidence.

articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autoimmune connective tissue diseases (AICTDs) are associated with both chronic inflammation and an increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease beyond that conferred by traditional risk factors. High-density lipoprotein (HDL) exerts anti-atherogenic effects through its cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC), which inflammation may impair. Although HDL dysfunction has been reported in AICTDs, the role of this dysfunction in connective tissue diseases has not yet been systematically evaluated.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The study protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251183500). From inception, the Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online, Excerpta Medica database and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials will be searched. The review is scheduled to run from October 2026 to August 2027. Observational and interventional studies in adults with AICTDs reporting quantitative measures of HDL functionality, including CEC, antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory function and endothelial protective function, will be included. The study will be independently conducted by two reviewers.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Because this study will be a systematic review based on previously published data and will not involve individual patient data, ethical approval is not required. The findings will be disseminated through publication in a peer-reviewed journal and will be presented at a conference.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251183500.

articles.title: Patterns of Progression on Posttreatment Imaging During [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: We characterized patterns of treatment response and progression during [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) using serial posttreatment SPECT/CT and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET imaging and evaluated cycle-by-cycle prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-imaging concordance. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 361 patients from 2 academic centers who received at least 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT between May 2017 and March 2025. Posttreatment SPECT/CT scans were qualitatively evaluated to determine the site and pattern of response and progression, including PSMA low-avidity and PSMA-negative disease. Progression was defined by the appearance of new lesions or at least a 2-fold growth in preexisting lesions on SPECT/CT. PSA response was defined per Prostate Cancer Clinical Trials Working Group 3 criteria as at least a 50% decline from baseline. For cycle-by-cycle concordance analysis, PSA change was classified directionally as rising or falling relative to the prior cycle. In patients who paused or completed RPT after response, progression imaging was compared with the final on-treatment SPECT/CT scan. Results: Overall, 290 of 361 (80%) patients demonstrated a decrease in lesion size or number on posttreatment imaging. Of 312 patients with baseline bone disease, 81% demonstrated a response on posttreatment imaging. In total, 156 of 361 patients (43%) demonstrated progression during treatment. New osseous lesions developed in 132 patients, of whom 89 (67%) had PSMA low-avidity disease. At cycle 2, 64% of new lesions were osseous, increasing to at least 90% by cycles 4-6. PSMA-negative progression occurred in 22 patients (6%), predominantly in the liver (n = 11) and lymph nodes (n = 8), with 59% detected at cycle 2. Among 81 patients with imaging available at PSA progression after treatment completion or pause, 74 (91%) had imaging progression; of these, 69 (93%) demonstrated osseous and 13 (18%) nodal progression. PSA and imaging were discordant in 25%-43% of patients across cycles, with discordance increasing from cycle 2 to cycle 6. Conclusion: Progression during [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT occurs most frequently in bone, with 67% of patients with new osseous lesions demonstrating a PSMA low-avidity disease component. PSMA-negative progression is uncommon and tends to emerge early. PSA-imaging discordance is frequent, underscoring the need for integrated imaging assessment throughout treatment.

articles.title: Impact of PSMA PET/CT Staging on Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with Clinically Localized Prostate Cancer: Results of a Large Single-Center Cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT has become the gold standard for staging and restaging prostate cancer, with superior diagnostic accuracy over conventional imaging and established prognostic value. However, there are limited data on whether PSMA PET/CT-improved staging accuracy is associated with improved long-term patient outcomes. This study analyzes the association between PSMA PET/CT at primary staging and overall survival (OS), biochemical recurrence (BCR), and cancer-specific survival (CSS) in a large university hospital cohort at a center where PSMA PET/CT has been clinically available for over 13 y. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included all 11,146 patients with prostate cancer diagnosed between 2013 and 2023. The final analysis cohort consisted of 6999 patients, of whom 505 (7.2%) underwent PSMA PET/CT for primary staging. We classified patients into 3 groups using D'Amico risk classification. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier methods and adjusted Cox regression models. To control for selection bias, propensity score matching and overlap weighting were applied. Landmark analysis addressed selection and immortal time biases, and Fine-Gray models accounted for competing risk of death in a BCR analysis. Results: PSMA PET/CT was associated with a longer time to BCR (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38-0.68; P < 0.001), longer CSS (HR = 0.37; 95% CI, 0.22-0.61; P < 0.001), and longer OS (HR = 0.54; 95% CI, 0.40-0.70; P < 0.001). PSMA PET imaging was associated with particularly better outcomes in high-risk patients, especially those treated with radiotherapy. In the radiotherapy group, the HRs were 0.42 for OS, 0.42 for BCR, and 0.25 for CSS (all P < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant association was observed in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy. As the formal interaction test between PSMA PET/CT and treatment modality was not statistically significant, this differential finding should be considered exploratory. Across all 9 sensitivity analyses, HRs were consistently below 1, indicating a uniform direction of benefit. Conclusion: The association observed in this large real-world cohort supports the clinical value of PSMA PET/CT for primary staging. Findings were particularly favorable among high-risk patients undergoing radiotherapy, although this subgroup difference should be interpreted as exploratory given the nonsignificant interaction test. These results support a potential role for PSMA PET/CT in improving patient selection and detecting oligometastatic disease, enabling higher precision in treatment planning.

articles.title: Role of [18F]F-Fluciclovine PET/CT in Patients with Biochemical Recurrence of Prostate Cancer and Negative PSMA PET Results: A Single-Center Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Our purpose was to evaluate whether [18F]F-fluciclovine PET/CT detects sites of disease in patients with biochemical recurrence (BCR) of prostate cancer and negative findings on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and to assess its impact on intended management. Methods: In this prospective single-arm study (NCT05722925), 50 patients with BCR (prostate-specific antigen [PSA] ≥ 0.2 ng/mL) and negative findings on PSMA PET underwent [18F]F-fluciclovine PET/CT within 30 d of the previous imaging. Detection rate, distribution of disease, PSA-stratified analysis, management impact, and correct localization rate were assessed using descriptive statistics and exact CI. Results: [18F]F-fluciclovine PET had positive findings in 28 of 50 patients (56%; 95% CI, 41%-70%). Disease was confined to the prostate bed in 14 patients (50%), whereas 14 (50%) demonstrated nodal or distant metastases. Detection rate increased with PSA, from 44% at a PSA of 0.2-0.5 ng/mL to 100% at a PSA of 5 ng/mL or higher. The intended management changed in 71% of patients after the [18F]F-fluciclovine PET: 87% of patients with positive findings and 54% with negative findings. Among patients with an available reference standard (n = 14), all positive findings were confirmed to be true-positive. Conclusion: [18F]F-fluciclovine PET detected recurrent disease in over half of patients with negative PSMA PET findings and frequently altered management, supporting its complementary role in selected patients with BCR.

articles.title: 18F-BMS-986192 PET to Predict Durable Response to Nivolumab in NSCLC: A Novel Approach Beyond PD-L1 Immunohistochemistry.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry, the current standard biomarker for predicting response to programmed death protein 1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors in non-small cell lung cancer, has moderate predictive value among others because of tumor heterogeneity and limited biopsy representation, whereas PD-L1 PET/CT using 18F-BMS-986192 enables noninvasive, whole-tumor assessment of PD-L1 expression and heterogeneity, potentially improving prediction of response to immunotherapy. Methods: In this prospective multicenter biomarker exploration study, patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer eligible for nivolumab-based therapies underwent baseline 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT, 18F-FDG PET/CT, and tumor biopsy for PD-L1 immunohistochemistry before treatment initiation. The primary endpoint was durable clinical benefit, defined as progression-free survival (PFS) of 9 mo or greater, with secondary analyses assessing associations among tracer uptake, PD-L1 expression, survival outcomes, and PET-based radiomic features. Results: Of 91 enrolled patients, 77 were included in the final analysis of 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT. Although PD-L1 immunohistochemistry did not differ between patients with PFS of less than 9 mo versus 9 mo or greater, PD-L1 PET uptake in lung lesions was significantly higher in patients with PFS of at least 9 mo (P = 0.01). Using an optimal mean SUVpeak cutoff of 2.4, PD-L1 PET demonstrated a high negative predictive value (94%) for durable clinical benefit, with significant associations for both PFS and overall survival, particularly in patients receiving first-line treatment. Tracer uptake showed no correlation with 18F-FDG uptake. Conclusion: 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT revealed interpatient PD-L1 variability. Low uptake in lung lesions predicted poor outcomes with high negative predictive value. 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT demonstrated stronger negative predictive value than did baseline PD-L1 immunohistochemistry in this cohort. These findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Botulinum Toxin Plus Transdermal Scopolamine Reduces Salivary Gland Uptake in Patients Undergoing Tandem Radiopharmaceutical Therapy with [225Ac]Ac- and [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligands.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) has shown remarkable efficacy in advanced metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. However, salivary gland toxicity is a major dose-limiting adverse effect, particularly with α-emitting radionuclides such as 225Ac. Although tandem therapy with combined [225Ac]Ac- and [177Lu]Lu-labeled PSMA-targeted RPT in a single low-activity cycle may address certain challenges, effective salivary gland protection remains crucial. In this study, we explored the use of botulinum toxin (BTX) type A (incobotulinumtoxinA) plus transdermal scopolamine as a protective strategy to mitigate salivary gland uptake of PSMA radioligands. Methods: IncobotulinumtoxinA was injected percutaneously, with increasing dosages of up to 300 units distributed into the parotid and submandibular glands under ultrasound guidance, a mean of 24 d before scheduled tandem PSMA RPT. Transdermal scopolamine was applied from 72 h before RPT until 2 h after RPT. Molecular imaging was conducted as per PSMA RPT protocol, with pretreatment PSMA PET/CT to confirm ligand uptake and follow-up PET/CT for restaging. SPECT/CT was conducted as imaging after RPT. PET SUVmean or SPECT counts were measured, and ratios of injected-to-noninjected contralateral glands were calculated and compared before and after BTX. Results: Fourteen patients (mean age, 68.0 ± 8.1 y) were included; 1 patient received 2 injections before his treatment, and another underwent 2 tandem RPT cycles, with BTX administered before each cycle. Mean cumulative administered activity was 5.05 ± 1.09 GBq for 177Lu and 6.87 ± 3.14 MBq for 225Ac. Combination therapy with incobotulinumtoxinA plus transdermal scopolamine was associated with lower PSMA radioligand uptake in BTX-treated salivary glands relative to untreated contralateral glands, with mean reductions of approximately 30% in parotid glands and 17% in submandibular glands compared with untreated glands. Up to 300 units of incobotulinumtoxinA distributed among the major salivary glands was safe. No patient discontinued tandem PSMA therapy because of xerostomia, and no grade 3 or 4 toxicities were observed during PSMA RPT. Conclusion: BTX plus transdermal scopolamine is a promising strategy to reduce salivary gland uptake during PSMA RPT. This approach enhances patient quality of life after PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy, particularly with α-emitting radionuclides, while preserving its excellent therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Predicting [90Y]Y-FAPI-46 Tumor Absorbed Dose from Single-Time-Point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Imaging.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeting peptides, such as 90Y-FAPI-46, have increasingly been used to treat various tumor entities, with preliminary reports indicating therapeutic responses with acceptable toxicity profiles. Dosimetry can be used to maximize antitumor capability and minimize side effects. The aim of this study was to investigate whether 90Y-FAPI-46 tumor dosimetry can be predicted by diagnostic 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT data. Methods: Fourteen patients with 24 lesions underwent a single-time-point 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT scan and 3 90Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT scans for dosimetry within a 3-mo interval. Tumors were identified on PET images, and the anatomic tumor volume was measured on low-dose CT. Tumor uptake extrapolated at time of injection, time-integrated activity coefficient (TIAC), and tumor absorbed dose were calculated as reference values using 90Y-FAPI-46 data and compared with the corresponding predicted values using 68Ga-FAPI-46 data by means of a single-time-point dosimetry model. Correlations between 90Y-FAPI-46- and 68Ga-FAPI-46-based values were assessed. Results: In calculating the predicted values using a single-time-point 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT, the mean effective half-life of 90Y-FAPI-46 across all lesions was 8.44 ± 1.73 h. The mean ± SD ratio (i.e., the predicted values using 68Ga-FAPI-46 data divided by the reference 90Y-FAPI-46 data) were 0.93 ± 0.39, 0.77 ± 0.35, and 0.77 ± 0.35 for tumor uptake, TIAC, and tumor absorbed dose, respectively. In the Bland-Altman analysis, mean differences (bias) ± SD of the percent differences of tumor uptake, TIAC, and tumor absorbed dose were -16.11% ± 43.28% (95% CI, -100.90 to 68.73%; Spearman ρ = 0.91; P < 0.0001), -32.60% ± 41.26% (95% CI, -113.50 to 48.26%; Spearman ρ = 0.91; P < 0.0001), and -33.35% ± 40.19% (95% CI, -112.10 to 45.43%; Spearman ρ = 0.77; P < 0.0001), respectively. Conclusion: Tumor uptake, TIAC, and tumor absorbed dose on 90Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT and 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT were highly correlated, although the values on 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT tended to be lower than those on 90Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT. Predicted values on 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT can help clinicians with diagnostic stratification and patient selection, with intratherapeutic verification remaining necessary before any individualization of administered activity.

articles.title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen PET/CT Complements MRI for Focal Therapy Selection in Prostate Cancer: A Whole-Mount Histopathologic Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: The incremental value of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT over multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for selecting patients for prostate cancer focal therapy is undefined. Unlike lesion-detection studies, we evaluated whether PSMA PET/CT, mpMRI, and their combination correctly determine focal therapy eligibility when validated against whole-mount histopathology (WMHP). Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing radical prostatectomy (RP) at UCLA (2017-2024) with preoperative PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI, a biopsy grade group (GG) of 3 or less, unilateral disease, and a prostate-specific antigen level of less than 20 ng/mL. Two blinded readers per modality assessed extraprostatic extension (EPE), seminal vesicle invasion (SVI), bilateral disease, and multifocality; a third adjudicated discordances. Eligibility required the absence of all 4. On WMHP, ineligibility was EPE, SVI, multifocal or bilateral disease with a contralateral or secondary GG of at least 2 nodules, or any GG greater than 3 focus at RP. Modalities were compared by McNemar tests. Results: Of 112 patients, 77 (69%) were ineligible on WMHP, including 19 (17%) with a GG greater than 3 focus at RP. Sensitivity and specificity were 53% and 54% for PET and 70% and 49% for mpMRI. Combined imaging improved sensitivity to 83% (P < 0.001 vs. PET; P = 0.002 vs. MRI) but reduced specificity to 26%. Per 100 patients at this prevalence, this would correctly identify approximately 9 additional ineligible patients while falsely excluding approximately 7 true candidates. mpMRI was more sensitive than PET for EPE (77% vs. 32%, P < 0.001), whereas PET was more specific (90% vs. 58%, P < 0.001). Combined imaging improved detection of multifocal (44% vs. 23%, P = 0.001) and bilateral disease (45% vs. 23%, P = 0.002) versus MRI alone. Conclusion: Adding PSMA PET/CT to mpMRI significantly improves sensitivity for exclusionary features, reflecting complementary molecular and anatomic information. However, combined imaging still misses a substantial proportion of adverse pathology, so imaging alone should not determine eligibility.

articles.title: Ace-miR-3720-x regulates the immune response of Eastern honeybee larvae to Ascosphaera apis infection by modulating Acβ-GBP.
articles.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play a critical role in the immune regulation of Apis cerana larvae infected by Ascosphaera apis, which is the pathogenic fungus causing chalkbrood disease. This study found that miRNA ace-miR-3720-x was significantly upregulated in the midgut of larvae infected with A. apis. The dual luciferase reporter assay confirmed that ace-miR-3720-x directly targeted the 3'UTR of acβ-GBP, thereby negatively regulating its expression. Acβ-GBP is a pattern recognition receptor that participates in activating the toll pathway and inducing the expression of antimicrobial peptides. Inhibition of ace-miR-3720-x resulted in marked upregulation of acβ-GBP expression, thereby upregulating the expression of critical antimicrobial peptide genes and phenoloxidase cascade genes at the late phase of infection. Furthermore, inhibition of ace-miR-3720-x significantly reduced larval mortality and the incidence of chalkbrood disease; the expression of the A. apis virulence factor genes (ADM-B and chsD) was also decreased. Our findings indicate that ace-miR-3720-x functions as a negative regulator of antifungal immunity in honeybees, and attenuates host resistance by suppressing acβ-GBP-mediated immune responses. Ace-miR-3720-x may serve as a potential molecular target for the control of chalkbrood disease and for resistance breeding in honeybees.

articles.title: Hepatospora eriocheir infection affects the fitness of adult Chinese mitten crabs in their non-native range.
articles.abstract: For many invasive crustaceans, including the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis), the prevalence and impact of parasites in their introduced range remain largely unexplored. The microsporidium Hepatospora eriocheir was recently detected in mitten crabs across Europe, yet little is known about its physiological effects on its host. In this study, the influence of H. eriocheir infection on physiological biomarkers in adult mitten crabs collected from rivers in Germany and Belgium was experimentally investigated. We assessed metabolic rates (routine and maximum metabolic rate, aerobic scope), haemolymph glucose and lactate levels, and lipid content in the hepatopancreas. Infection prevalence reached 27% in adult mitten crabs from the Belgian population and 38% in individuals from the German population. Infected individuals showed a significantly reduced maximum metabolic rate and aerobic scope, while the routine metabolic rate remained unaffected. Glucose levels were lower in infected crabs both at rest and post-exercise, which indicates that energy reserves have dropped, whereas lactate levels showed no significant difference. The lipid content in the hepatopancreas was reduced, likely due to direct exploitation of host resources by the parasite and damage to hepatopancreatic tissue. Together, these patterns indicate an impaired energy metabolism, which may hamper energetically demanding activities such as migration and reproduction. The Chinese mitten crab is a catadromous species, and as the examined crabs were at the life stage when they commence a long-distance migration for their single reproductive event, infection by H. eriocheir may compromise their ability to complete this migration and successfully reproduce.

articles.title: Differential gene expression in the tropical house cricket and its iridovirus in healthy versus diseased specimens.
articles.abstract: The tropical house cricket, Gryllodes sigillatus, is a mass-produced insect that is used as a protein source for pets and livestock. However, intensive mass-rearing conditions, coupled with high genetic relatedness, create an ideal environment for the spread of pathogenic microbes that severely impact production. Cricket iridovirus (CrIV) is a pathogen that impedes cricket growth and causes significant losses for cricket farmers. Interestingly, recent studies have shown that CrIV is often present asymptomatically, yet the molecular basis of the emergence of disease symptoms remains unknown. To address this, we sampled healthy and diseased crickets and examined differences in cricket and CrIV gene expression via RNAseq. Using differential gene expression analysis and functional enrichment analysis, we found significant differences in host and viral gene expression between healthy and diseased crickets, including genes involved in immunity. Interestingly, while we observed high CrIV gene expression across the entire CrIV genome in sick populations, healthy asymptomatic populations showed elevated expression at a single viral locus. Our results shed light not only on the cricket immune response to CrIV infection but also identify a viral gene that is highly expressed during covert infections, suggesting its potential role in suppressing the host's immune response. These findings enhance our understanding of how CrIV interacts with its cricket host, providing essential insights for developing targeted strategies to manage CrIV outbreaks in cricket mass-rearing facilities.

articles.title: The Effects of Cannabinoids in Cardiovascular Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Expanded Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) use have prompted increasing interest in their risk for cardiovascular complications. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, experimental, and epidemiologic evidence on the relationships between cannabinoid exposure and cardiovascular disease, summarizes acute and chronic outcomes, evaluates therapeutic potential of non-psychoactive cannabinoids, and identifies future research priorities. Cannabinoid type 1 receptors in cardiovascular tissues promote sympathetic activation, tachycardia, and endothelial dysfunction, while cannabinoid type 2 receptor activation exerts anti-inflammatory and athero-protective effects. Acute THC exposure in humans produces tachycardia, increased myocardial oxygen demand, vascular stiffness, and transient blood-pressure alterations. Recent large observational studies and meta-analyses suggest associations between cannabis/cannabinoid use and increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events. While causality has not yet been definitively established, the accumulation of in vitro and in vivo evidence indicates potentially significant cardiovascular risks associated with frequent and/or heavy cannabinoid use, particularly in individuals with underlying cardiovascular disease or other risk factors. In the future, clinicians should screen for cannabinoid use, and standardized exposure metrics, longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are urgently needed.

articles.title: Regulation of VSP 5G8 protein expression during Giardia lamblia infection and in vitro interaction with epithelial cells.
articles.abstract: Variant-specific surface proteins (VSPs) participate in antigenic variation; therefore, it is important to better understand their functions and the mechanisms regulating their expression. The expression of the highly immunogenic VSP 5G8 in Giardia lamblia was evaluated both in vivo and in vitro. Meriones unguiculatus were infected with 2 × 10⁶ GS-5G8(+) trophozoites, and parasites were recovered from the small intestine 14 days post-infection (dpi) for analysis of 5G8 expression. Moreover, 5G8 modulation was analyzed after co-culturing GS-5G8(+) trophozoites with the human intestinal epithelial cells Caco-2, and a Transwell system was used to assay 5G8 translocation across the epithelial barrier. Results indicate that, at 14 dpi, G. lamblia trophozoites expressing VSP 5G8 on their cell surface decreased from 35 % to 5 %. Intracellular fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) analysis showed the VSP 5G8(+) population declined from 62 % to 23 %. End-point RT-PCR and western blot analyses detected 5G8 mRNA and protein translation. At 12 h of in vitro co-culture with Caco-2 cells, the percentage of trophozoites expressing 5G8 on their surface decreased from 75 % to 42 %. Furthermore, Giardia induced permeability of the epithelial barrier, demonstrating that it facilitates 5G8 translocation across the epithelial barrier. Overall, these findings suggest that regulation of 5G8 expression may depend on Giardia-host interactions and provide a basis for further investigation into the mechanisms underlying VSP modulation.

articles.title: Differential virulence, tissue parasitism, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression profiles among Trypanosoma cruzi TcI isolates from triatomine vectors.
articles.abstract: Trypanosoma cruzi, the etiological agent of Chagas disease, displays marked biological heterogeneity that influences virulence, tissue parasitism, and immune modulation. In Mexico, several triatomine species participate in the transmission of TcI discrete typing unit (DTU). However, the extent of biological heterogeneity and immunopathological variability among regional isolates remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we characterized TcI isolates (by mini-exon SL-IR) obtained from Triatoma barberi (Qron), T. pallidipennis (Oaxteh), and T. dimidiata (Mezca), evaluating key virulence parameters and host inflammatory responses during acute experimental infection of CD-1 mice. The prepatent period, parasitemia, survival, and tissue parasitism were assessed through parasitological and histopathological analyses of heart, esophagus, gastrocnemius, and brain tissues. We also quantified the expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IFN-γ in these organs using RT-qPCR. Although all isolates were identified as TcI, they exhibited several biological differences. Qron and Oaxteh isolates had prepatent periods of 2 days, high parasitemia, and 100% mortality. In contrast, Mezca isolate showed a 4-day prepatent period, significantly lower parasitemia, and 73% survival. Histological analysis revealed a higher number of amastigote nests in tissues infected with Qron and Oaxteh, whereas Mezca exhibited minimal tissue colonization and no detectable nests in the brain. Cytokine profiling demonstrated substantially higher TNF-α and IFN-γ expression in tissues infected with Qron isolate, correlating with high tissue parasitism, while Mezca isolate induced the lowest cytokine levels and the lowest parasite burdens. Collectively, these findings demonstrate biological and immunopathological heterogeneity among Mexican TcI isolates during acute phase.

articles.title: Transcriptomic response of the head kidney and gill of lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) to Moritella viscosa infection.
articles.abstract: Moritella viscosa, the causative agent of winter ulcer disease, infects several cold-water marine fish species, but its pathogenesis and associated host responses in lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) remain poorly understood. Here, we established a systemic infection model and characterized disease progression, tissue pathology, bacterial recovery, and transcriptional responses following intraperitoneal challenge with M. viscosa J311. Cumulative mortality reached 66.67%, 48.39%, and 30.51% following challenge with 3.1 × 108, 3.1 × 107, and 3.1 × 106 CFU dose-1, respectively, with an estimated LD50 of 8.1 × 107 CFU dose-1. Infection resulted in ulcerative lesions, systemic bacterial recovery, and histopathological alterations in multiple tissues. Transcriptomic analysis of head kidney and gill at 10 days post-infection following challenge with 3.1 × 106 CFU dose-1 identified 731 and 217 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), respectively, with only 41 shared DEGs. The head kidney exhibited broad regulation of acute-phase and inflammatory responses, iron homeostasis, protease-associated processes, transport, and metabolism. In contrast, the gill response involved complement regulation, inflammatory and leukocyte-trafficking processes, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Greater bacterial recovery from the gill despite a broader transcriptional response in the head kidney demonstrated distinct tissue-specific responses during systemic infection. Gill mmp9 induction, downregulation of collagen-related transcripts, enrichment of fibrillar collagen-associated processes, and lamellar damage further supported substantial ECM remodeling. These findings provide new insight into tissue-specific responses and pathogenesis during M. viscosa infection in lumpfish.

articles.title: Nasal Photodisinfection and Surgical Site Infection Following Coronary Bypass Surgery: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Surgical site infections (SSI) complicating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) carry substantial morbidity and mortality. We evaluated compliance with nasal decolonization and SSI rates after institutional implementation of preoperative nasal photodisinfection in isolated CABG.

METHODS: Single-centre interrupted time series (ITS) of 2,172 procedures (June 2023-January 2026, transition month June 2025), comprising 24 pre-intervention months (mupirocin era, n = 1,678) and 8 post-intervention months (photodisinfection era, n = 494). The primary effectiveness outcome was conduit harvest surgical site infection (CHSSI) at 30 days; compliance with nasal decolonization was the primary implementation outcome. Secondary outcomes included total surgical site infection (TSSI). Step changes in log-transformed monthly rates were analyzed using restricted maximum likelihood segmented regression accounting for first-order autocorrelation; compliance was modelled untransformed.

RESULTS: Compliance with mupirocin was 35.4% (68.1% in elective patients; 17.5% in non-elective patients), compared with 93.3% compliance with nasal photodisinfection. Compliance rose 37.0 percentage points (95% CI 21.9-52.0). TSSI was 9.1% pre-intervention vs 5.9% post-intervention (change in intercept RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.09-1.15, p = 0.080). CHSSI was 3.6% pre-intervention vs 1.7% post-intervention (change in intercept RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.05-0.72, p = 0.014). CHSSI was decreased after exclusion of the transition month (June, 2025) but this was no longer statistically significant. ITS estimates for sternal outcomes were directionally consistent but did not reach significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Photodisinfection achieved higher compliance than mupirocin and was associated with significant CHSSI reduction that reached significance in the primary analysis but was dependent on the partial-implementation month of June 2025.

articles.title: Prior room occupancy and risk of subsequent acquisition of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in liver transplant units.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Prior room occupancy by patients colonised with multidrug-resistant organisms has been associated with subsequent acquisition, but its role in the transmission of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) remains unclear, particularly in liver transplant patients. We evaluated this association at the room-stay episode level in predominantly single-room liver transplant units.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients admitted to two liver transplant units (Sub-intensive care unit [ICU] and liver transplant ICU) between January 2024 and August 2025 in a tertiary-care hospital in Seoul, South Korea. Patients with prior CPE colonization were excluded. The unit of analysis was the room-stay episode. Environmental sampling was performed to assess potential environmental reservoirs.

RESULTS: Among 1,472 room-stay episodes, 229 with pre-existing CPE were excluded. Of the remaining 1,243 episodes, 87 (7.0%) resulted in CPE acquisition. Prior room occupancy by a CPE-positive patient was associated with acquisition in univariate analysis (31% vs. 19%, p = 0.006), but not in overall multivariable analysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.95-2.61; p = 0.08). However, prior room occupancy was independently associated with acquisition in the Sub-ICU (aOR 1.75; 95% CI 1.02-3.01; p = 0.044), but not in the liver transplant ICU. Environmental sampling identified CPE contamination in Sub-ICU in-room toilets, including after terminal cleaning and disinfection.
