CONCLUSIONS: The association between prior room occupancy and CPE acquisition differed by unit. Persistent environmental contamination of in-room toilets may contribute to CPE acquisition in the Sub-ICU, although molecular analyses are needed to establish transmission pathways.

articles.title: Impact of Underlying Cirrhosis and Acute Extrahepatic Organ Failure Burden on Dynamic In-Hospital Outcomes: Validation and Expansion of the Kyoto ACLF Framework.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

articles.title: Percutaneous Recanalization of Chronic Noncirrhotic Native-Liver Extrahepatic Portal Vein Obstruction in Children.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, procedure-related safety, and imaging-based patency of percutaneous portal vein recanalization (PVR) in children with chronic native-liver extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 28 consecutive patients younger than 17 years with chronic noncirrhotic, nonmalignant EHPVO who underwent attempted PVR between 2016 and 2026. Recanalization was performed through transhepatic, transsplenic, or combined access, followed by balloon angioplasty without stenting. Technical success was defined as restoration of hepatopetal flow through the portal vein into the intrahepatic portal venous system. Adverse events were graded using the Society of Interventional Radiology classification. Portal vein patency was assessed on available follow-up imaging.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 19 of 28 patients (67.9%). Six patients (21.4%) had access-related adverse events (3 mild, 1 moderate, 2 severe), with no surgery, permanent sequelae, or procedure-related death. Follow-up imaging was available for 15 of 19 technically successful patients, with a median imaging follow-up of 11 months (range, 1-35 months). At last imaging, the portal vein was patent without significant restenosis in 7 patients, patent with restenosis in 5, and reoccluded in 3. Overall, portal venous flow was maintained in 12 of 15 patients (80.0%).

CONCLUSION: Percutaneous PVR restored hepatopetal portal flow in 67.9% of selected children without stenting. Durable patency could not be established because follow-up was incomplete and heterogeneous. Restenosis and reocclusion support structured imaging surveillance; further studies should define the role of stenting versus angioplasty alone.

articles.title: A Branch-Specific Combined Fenestration Strategy for Chronic Aortic Dissection With Severe Paravisceral True Lumen Compression.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate a branch-specific combined fenestration strategy to address the technical challenges of severe true lumen (TL) compression during physician-modified fenestration (PMF)-based four-vessel visceral reconstruction in chronic aortic dissection (CAD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled twenty-three consecutive patients with aneurysmal CAD and severe paravisceral TL compression (minimum functional TL diameter ≤10 mm) treated between January 2020 and December 2024. All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion. Endpoints included technical success (complete four-vessel reconstruction), 30-day mortality, target-vessel patency, and TL expansion.

RESULTS: Complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction was achieved in all 23 patients (92/92 target vessels). Renal ISLF was successful in all 46 renal arteries, with first-attempt success in 44 (96%). Distal aortic exclusion was required in 20 patients; one interval infrarenal rupture in the staged group was managed with emergency repair. Over a median follow-up of 17.0 months, primary target-vessel patency was 99% (91/92). The median minimum functional TL diameter increased from 8.0 mm preoperatively to 15.9 mm at one-year follow-up. No type I or III endoleak was identified. Thirty-day mortality was 0%. Transient spinal cord ischaemia occurred in one patient (4%), and acute kidney injury (KDIGO Stage 1) in two patients (9%), all resolving before discharge.

CONCLUSION: In highly selected CAD patients with severe TL compression, this combined fenestration strategy enabled complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction with satisfactory early target-vessel patency and no target-vessel loss, though longer follow-up in larger cohorts is required.

articles.title: Site-specific distribution of pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 PCR non-amplification profiles in southern Côte d'Ivoire.
articles.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histidine-rich protein 2 (HRP2)-based rapid diagnostic tests are widely used for Plasmodium falciparum malaria, but parasites lacking pfhrp2 may escape detection. Evidence from Côte d'Ivoire remains limited, and conventional PCR non-amplification requires cautious interpretation because it may also reflect low parasite DNA concentration, assay sensitivity, or primer-binding-site variation.

METHODS: We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional survey of 140 symptomatic patients with microscopy-confirmed P. falciparum mono-infection at three health facilities in southern Côte d'Ivoire: Anonkoua-Kouté (peri-urban), Port-Bouët (urban), and Ayamé (semi-rural). Two regions of each gene, the exon 1-exon 2 junction and exon 2, were assessed by conventional PCR. Amplification profiles were summarized by study site, and exploratory associations with parasite density, age, and multiplicity of infection were examined.

RESULTS: pfhrp2 profiles differed significantly among sites (p < 0.001). Complete non-amplification of both targets occurred in 6.0 (Anonkoua-Kouté), 60.0 (Ayamé), and 40.0 (Port-Bouët). pfhrp3 profiles did not differ by site (p = 0.452), although exon 1-exon 2 non-amplification with retained exon 2 amplification (-/+) was common (74). Eight infections (5.7) showed concurrent non-amplification of both exon 2 targets; six of these (75) had densities <5000 parasites/μL versus 28/132 (21) without (p = 0.003). Multiplicity of infection was not significantly associated.

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial site-level variation in presumptive pfhrp2 deletion profiles was observed. The association between concurrent exon 2 non-amplification and low parasite density should be interpreted cautiously due to potential PCR failure from reduced template. Larger surveillance studies with paired RDT/microscopy, quantitative controls, and genomic analysis are needed before policy changes.

articles.title: Cardioprotective Effects of Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets against Myocardial Ischemia: Involvement of Protein Kinase B-Related Signaling in Apoptosis and Pyroptosis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets (XSNT) are traditionally used to promote blood circulation and resolve blood stasis, including for coronary heart disease-associated angina. Their cardioprotective mechanisms and bioactive constituents remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotection of XSNT against myocardial ischemia and to investigate its underlying mechanisms and candidate bioactive constituents.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: XSNT was evaluated in myocardial infarction (MI) mice using echocardiography, biochemical assays, histopathology, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Proteomics and prior network pharmacology guided PI3K/AKT analysis. H9c2 cells underwent 8 h of oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), with MK-2206 used to assess AKT involvement. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and cellular experiments were used to evaluate the candidates.

RESULTS: XSNT improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury in MI mice. Reduced TUNEL staining and changes in Bcl-2/Bax and cleaved caspase-3 supported attenuation of apoptosis, while reductions in inflammasome- and GSDMD-related proteins indicated decreased pyroptosis-related signaling. These effects accompanied increased AKT phosphorylation and reduced NF-κB activation. XSNT produced similar responses in OGD-challenged H9c2 cells, and MK-2206 partially attenuated these effects. Puerarin showed a potential interaction with AKT and reproduced some cellular effects of XSNT, which were also attenuated by MK-2206.

CONCLUSION: XSNT attenuated myocardial injury and distinct apoptosis- and pyroptosis-related responses, with pharmacological evidence supporting AKT involvement. Puerarin represents a candidate bioactive constituent. This study has several limitations, including the unclear cellular sources of myocardial pyroptosis-related signals, the lack of genetic validation of AKT involvement, and the need for further confirmation in primary cardiomyocytes.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Anodal transcranial direct-current stimulation over the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) for post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI).

METHODS: Eight databases were searched from inception to June 7, 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. Meta-analyses were conducted using Stata version 18, with subgroups stratified by control type and stimulation site.

RESULTS: Twenty-three RCTs involving 1326 participants were included. Anodal tDCS over the DLPFC significantly improved global cognitive screening performance: Clinical Efficacy (odds ratio [OR] = 1.37, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01-1.85, P =0.043), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score (weighted mean difference [WMD] = 3.17, 95% CI: 2.53-3.80, P = 0.000), and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score (WMD = 2.52, 95% CI: 1.81-3.22, P = 0.001). Subgroup analyses demonstrated superiority of active tDCS regardless of control condition: rehabilitation therapy (RT) plus sham tDCS (MoCA: WMD = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.60-3.30; MMSE: WMD = 2.40, 95% CI: 0.97-3.83) and RT alone (MoCA: WMD = 3.47, 95% CI: 2.81-4.12; MMSE: WMD = 2.72, 95% CI: 2.12-3.32). Benefits were also consistent across stimulation of the affected hemisphere (MoCA: WMD = 2.88, 95% CI: 2.05-3.71; MMSE: WMD = 2.59, 95% CI: 1.50-3.68) and the left hemisphere (MoCA: WMD = 3.42, 95% CI: 2.47-4.38; MMSE: WMD = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.45-3.51). Activities of daily living (ADL) measured by the Modified Barthel Index (MBI) also improved significantly (WMD = 10.75, 95% CI: 8.67-12.84, P = 0.000), with benefits maintained across all subgroups: RT plus sham tDCS (WMD = 11.18, 95% CI: 8.76-13.60), RT alone (WMD = 10.49, 95% CI: 7.67-13.32), affected hemisphere (WMD = 11.37, 95% CI: 7.83-14.91), and left hemisphere (WMD = 10.06, 95% CI: 8.00-12.13). Safety outcomes were infrequently reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Anodal tDCS over the DLPFC may improve global cognitive screening performance and ADL in PSCI patients, yet low methodological quality and inadequate safety reporting limit the current evidence. Further high-quality RCTs with rigorous adverse event monitoring are warranted.

articles.title: High-fidelity and network-based spatio-temporal mathematical models of Alzheimer's disease progression and their comparison with PET-SUVR imaging data.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the most common neurodegenerative disorder. Its pathological development is connected with the misfolding and accumulation of two toxic proteins: amyloid-β and tau proteins. Mathematical models provide a valuable quantitative tool for monitoring disease progression. In this work, we proposed and compare a novel framework where the spatio-temporal dynamics of amyloid-β and tau proteins is modeled based on employing either three-dimensional patient-specific geometries or through reduced network-based models defined on the brain connectome. More specifically, a high-fidelity biophysical model is proposed on three-dimensional brain geometries reconstructed from magnetic resonance imaging, whereas a network-based reduced formulation is defined on the brain connectome. For both approaches, a suitable numerical discretisation is proposed. A sensitivity analysis is presented to quantify the influence of model parameters on protein concentration patterns as well as compare the quality of the predictions. For both approaches, the results are compared with group-level PET-SUVR clinical data using [18F]AZD4694 for amyloid-β and [18F]MK6240 for tau protein. The results indicate that the three-dimensional model provides the most accurate and biologically consistent description of the disease progression, but remains computationally demanding. On the other hand, the reduced graph-based model is cheaper, but it is not always able to achieve reliable results.

articles.title: Predictors of severe measles outcomes in hospitalized patients in Jerusalem, 2025.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Measles is a vaccine-preventable disease. Defining risk factors for poor outcomes in hospitalized patients can improve future measles outbreak preparedness.

METHODS: Data were collected on all confirmed measles cases that were evaluated at one of the emergency departments (ED) in the three main hospitals in Jerusalem from the first reported case of the current outbreak on April 10th to December 31st, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using robust Poisson multivariable models to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and death.

RESULTS: Among 786 individuals who visited the ED with confirmed measles, the rates of hospital admission (≥1 day), ICU, ECMO and death were 83.4%, 6.4%, 0.8%, and 1.4%, respectively. Complete data were available for 567 patients, of whom 303 (53.4%) were males. Median age was 2.1 years (IQR 1.2-3.8), and 474 (83.6%) were younger than 5 years. Most patients were unvaccinated (91.0%). Secondary infections were frequent, including lobar pneumonia (28.7%) and community-acquired bacteremia (3.5%). Respiratory support and severe dehydration were associated with hospital admission (IRR 1.4, 95% CI 1.3-1.5; p<0.001 and 9.5, 4.8-18.4; p<0.001, respectively) and ICU admission (IRR 1.3, 1.2-1.4; p<0.001 and 5.2, 2.1-12.4; p<0.001, respectively). Community-acquired bacteremia was associated with death or ECMO (IRR 44.5, 12.5-158.6; p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite high access to medical care in this urban setting, measles caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and bacteremia identified patients at increased risk of severe outcomes.

articles.title: Serum torque teno virus levels are strongly associated with stages of non-advanced HIV-1 infection at diagnosis.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Torque teno virus (TTV) is a ubiquitous component of the human blood virome and its replication is tightly controlled by the host immune system. TTV levels have therefore been proposed as a surrogate marker of immune competence. In people with HIV-1 infection (PWH), higher TTV levels have been associated with advanced infection. We investigated TTV levels in individuals diagnosed with non-advanced HIV-1 infection. TTV viral load (VL) was compared between primary and chronic infection to assess whether it could reflect immune dysfunction not captured par CD4+ T-cell counts.

METHODS: We conducted a monocentric cohort study including adults newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. All participants were antiretroviral therapy-naïve with HIV-1 viremia. Individuals with advanced HIV-1 infection were excluded. HIV-1 infection stage was determined using immunoblot-based laboratory staging according to Fiebig classification. TTV DNA was quantified in serum samples using a qPCR assay. Associations with HIV-1 infection stage were assessed using logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 126 PWH were included. Primary HIV-1 infection accounted for 42.1% of diagnoses and chronic infection for 57.9%. Overall, TTV DNA was detected in 61.1% of participants. TTV detection was more frequent in chronic infection than in primary infection (82.2% vs 32.1%, p<0.0001). Median TTV VL was also higher in chronic infection (4.82 vs 2.65 log copies/mL, p<0.0001), despite comparable CD4+ T-cell counts. In multivariable analysis, HIV-1 VL and TTV VL were independently associated with HIV-1 infection stage. High TTV VL (≥4 log copies/mL) was strongly associated with chronic infection.

CONCLUSIONS: In individuals diagnosed with non-advanced HIV-1 infection, TTV levels differed markedly between primary and chronic infection despite similar CD4+ T-cell counts. These findings suggest that TTV VL could reflect alterations in immune competence not captured by conventional immunological markers and may represent an additional biomarker to assess immune status in PWH.

articles.title: Threshold dynamics and intervention strategy optimization in a maize-vector delayed system for streak virus disease.
articles.abstract: Maize streak virus disease (MSVD), primarily transmitted by leafhoppers, is an important viral disease of maize. The delay involved in vector-mediated transmission may affect the disease epidemic patterns and control timing. In this study, a delayed transmission model coupling the interaction of maize and vector interaction is formulated, aiming to reveal the mechanism of delay on disease epidemic patterns and optimal control strategies. Theoretical analysis shows that delay does not alter the stability threshold of disease-free equilibrium. However, when the basic reproduction number exceeds one, increasing the delay will induce Hopf bifurcation, and the system will transform from steady-state convergence to periodic oscillation. Upon this foundation, an optimal control model with three measures, including preventive control through weeding, removal of infected maize plants, and chemical control through pesticide spraying, are investigated. Numerical simulations indicate that increasing the delay postpones the action window and reduces peak intensity of three control measures, whereas its influences depend on the initial infection status of vector leafhoppers. When infected leafhoppers are absent initially, an increase in delay inhibits the evolution of MSVD. In contrast, when infected leafhoppers are already present, it promotes the spread of MSVD among maize. Under optimal control, the three measures exhibit a temporal structure of removal first, spraying second, and weeding last under optimal control, which provides clear operational guidance for phased prevention and control under limited resources. These results reveal that the interplay between transmission delay and initial vector infection fundamentally shapes the effectiveness of each control measure, implying that the optimal timing and priority of removal, spraying, and weeding must be dynamically aligned with the specific phase of disease progression.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA.

METHODS: Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate.

RESULTS: We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

articles.title: Serum proteomic correlates of arts and cultural engagement and their associations with health outcomes: cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses in the UK Household Longitudinal Study.
articles.abstract: Understanding of the biological mechanisms underpinning associations between arts and cultural engagement (ACEng) and health outcomes remains embryonic. This study aimed to characterize serum proteomic signatures of ACEng, investigate the relationships between ACEng and health conditions, and undertake preliminary analyses to explore whether these proteins may mediate the associations. We analysed prospective cohort data from 6,180 participants in the UK Household Longitudinal Study who had cardiometabolic protein data and/or neurology protein data. Two indices of arts engagement were generated by summing metrics of frequency and diversity of arts participation, cultural attendance, and library, archives, museum, and heritage visits. Geater ACEng was found to be consistently associated across models with differences in 17 proteins after adjusting for sociodemographic confounders and multiple testing. The enriched biological pathways identified involved cell proliferation, receptor-mediated signaling, immune regulation and inflammatory signaling. We then explored longitudinal associations between ACEng and incidence of 15 chronic diseases. ACEng was consistently associated with lower prospective risk of asthma, COPD, CVD, IHD, stroke, arthritis, hyperthyroidism, hypertension, diabetes, clinical depression, and dementia (but not with cancer, heart failure, liver disease or epilepsy). In exploratory analyses, the identified significant proteins mediated 15.95-37.70% of the associations between ACEng and cardiometabolic and respiratory diseases, arthritis, and depression, although as ACEng and proteins were measured near contemporaneously, this does not establish a causal protein pathway. Instead, these findings present, for the first time, proteomic signatures of ACEng and provide preliminary data to help generate hypotheses about potential mediation pathways to health conditions. Future longitudinal research is encouraged to test whether proteins provide causal mechanistic pathways linking ACEng to human health and disease.

articles.title: Association of maternal adverse childhood experiences with inflammatory and growth factor pathway activity during pregnancy: a cross-sectional proteomics-based KEGG pathway analysis in the ECHO cohort.
articles.abstract: While maternal histories of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) have been linked to altered immune signaling during pregnancy, the specific inflammatory pathways underlying these associations remain poorly characterized. We leveraged high-dimensional proteomics to examine associations between maternal ACEs and pregnancy-associated inflammatory signaling pathways defined by the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and tested whether these associations were moderated by neighborhood-level social vulnerability during pregnancy. Participants included pregnant individuals enrolled in the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort (N = 770). Circulating inflammatory proteins were assayed from maternal plasma using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Protein markers were mapped to Human Genome Organisation (HUGO) Gene Nomenclature Committee gene symbols and aggregated into KEGG pathway scores using curated definitions. Linear regression models evaluated associations between continuous maternal ACE scores and each pathway score. Following correction for multiple comparisons, higher maternal ACE exposure was associated with higher activity across 12 KEGG-annotated protein pathways, including AGE-RAGE, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, chemokine, Th17 differentiation, HIF-1, cellular senescence, Rap1, NOD-like receptor signaling, transcriptional misregulation in cancer, and infection-related pathway signaling. Domain-specific analyses identified the most consistent associations for childhood household dysfunction. Neighborhood-level social vulnerability during pregnancy did not moderate ACE-inflammation associations but was independently associated with higher KSHV infection and NOD-like receptor signaling pathway scores. Together, these findings indicate that maternal ACEs and prenatal social vulnerability are independently associated with small, but directionally consistent, differences in overlapping inflammatory and growth-related protein signals during pregnancy.

articles.title: Exercise capacity in chronic respiratory diseases in the context of multimorbidity: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic respiratory diseases (CRD) are accompanied by coexisting chronic conditions, which may occur individually or as multimorbidity burden or patterns. These conditions may contribute to exercise intolerance, a determinant of prognosis. However, their association with exercise capacity remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate, in individuals with CRD, the association between one or more other chronic conditions (multimorbidity) and exercise capacity and to quantify this relationship through meta-analysis.

METHODS: Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, Virtual Health Library, and CINAHL until July 2025. Observational studies evaluating exercise capacity in adults with CRD, with coexisting chronic conditions, using field- or laboratory-based tests were included. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models.

RESULTS: A total of 49 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis (n = 28,972 participants), and 23 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Most studies involved individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Sensitivity analyses excluding outliers yielded clinically meaningful reductions in 6-min walk distance for metabolic (MD -34.26 m; 95% CI -46.98 to -21.53; I2 = 5.91%), cardiovascular (MD -27.18 m; 95% CI -39.59 to -14.78; I2 = 16.19%), and mental health conditions (MD -29.52 m; 95% CI -54.89 to -4.15; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSIONS: In individuals with CRD, multimorbidity is associated with reduced exercise capacity, with clinically meaningful reductions particularly in the presence of metabolic and cardiovascular conditions. Although the certainty of evidence is very low, these findings highlight the importance of considering multimorbidity when interpreting exercise limitation in CRD.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO, identifier CRD420251125343.

articles.title: Respiratory and Gastrointestinal Mycobiome Profiles Identify Distinct Patient Clusters Associated with Asthma Control.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The human microbiome contributes to asthma pathogenesis, yet most studies have focused on bacterial communities. This pilot study aimed to characterize fungal communities across multiple body sites in adults with asthma and evaluate whether integrated multisite mycobiome profiles are associated with asthma control.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We enrolled 24 adults with asthma evaluated at Mayo Clinic between 2020 and 2022. Oral wash, nasal swab, sputum, and stool samples were collected, and fungal communities were characterized using ITS2 sequencing. Multisite mycobiome data were integrated using an unsupervised clustering approach , with a two-cluster solution selected for exploratory clinical comparisons. Clusters were compared with respect to fungal composition, site-specific diversity metrics, and asthma control.

RESULTS: Two patient clusters with distinct multisite mycobiome profiles were identified. Cluster 1 demonstrated poorer asthma control, with lower Asthma Control Test scores than Cluster 2 (median [IQR], 15.0 [13.0-17.5] vs. 18.0 [17.0-19.0]; p = 0.040). Compared with Cluster 2, Cluster 1 exhibited a higher relative abundance of Cladosporium in nasal and sputum samples, and greater sputum fungal diversity (p = 0.016). In contrast, Cluster 2 exhibited a higher relative abundance of Candida in stool and sputum samples. No significant differences in fungal diversity were observed in oral, nasal, or stool samples.

CONCLUSION: Integrated multisite mycobiome profiling identified distinct fungal community patterns associated with asthma control, highlighting the need for larger, longitudinal studies to define their clinical relevance.

articles.title: Global and Segmental Myocardial Strain in Sarcoidosis: Associations With Cardiac Involvement and Clinical Impairment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac involvement is a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in sarcoidosis and may remain clinically silent despite normal conventional cardiac evaluation. Advanced imaging modalities, particularly speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE), may detect subclinical myocardial dysfunction before overt clinical manifestations. This study aimed to evaluate global and segmental myocardial strain patterns in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis and to investigate their associations with cardiac involvement, NT-proBNP levels, and functional capacity.

METHODS: This observational study included 123 patients with histologically confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis and 51 controls. According to the 2024 American Heart Association diagnostic probability framework, 25 patients were classified as having highly probable or probable cardiac sarcoidosis (CS+), whereas 98 were classified as possible/low probability (CS-). All participants underwent conventional echocardiography and STE with assessment of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS), right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RV-GLS), right ventricular free-wall strain (RV-FWS), and LV segmental strain. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to assess the associations of global strain parameters with log-transformed NT-proBNP and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus.

RESULTS: LV-GLS was progressively impaired across controls, CS-, and CS+ patients (-19.02±2.03%, -16.96±3.32%, and -13.17±4.08%, respectively; p<0.001). RV-GLS and RV-FWS were also significantly impaired in CS+ patients (p=0.004 and p=0.035, respectively). Segmental analysis demonstrated predominant impairment of basal and mid-ventricular segments, particularly the inferoseptal and inferior regions. NT-proBNP levels increased across the groups (49 [34-65], 100 [70-153], and 170 [114-713] pg/mL, respectively; p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, LV-GLS (β=0.287, p=0.001), RV-GLS (β=0.231, p=0.010), and RV-FWS (β=0.210, p=0.020) were independently associated with log-transformed NT-proBNP. LV-GLS was also independently associated with 6MWD (β=-0.262, p=0.003), whereas RV-GLS and RV-FWS were not.

CONCLUSION: Myocardial deformation is impaired in pulmonary sarcoidosis, with the greatest abnormalities observed in patients with cardiac involvement. LV-GLS showed independent associations with both NT-proBNP and functional capacity, while segmental strain analysis revealed a characteristic basal and mid-ventricular pattern of myocardial dysfunction. STE may provide useful complementary information for the assessment of myocardial involvement and clinical severity in patients with sarcoidosis.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Trans-Cannula Cryobiopsy of Supraclavicular Lymph Nodes in Patients with Suspected Thoracic Malignancy: A First-in-Human Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract: Adequate tissue acquisition is essential for the histopathologic and molecular characterization of thoracic malignancies. Although endobronchial ultrasound-guided mediastinal cryobiopsy has shown promising diagnostic performance, cryobiopsy of superficial lymph nodes has not previously been described. We report the first-in-human experience with ultrasound-guided trans-cannula cryobiopsy of supraclavicular lymph nodes (CryoPeUS) in 10 consecutive patients with suspected thoracic malignancy and PET-positive supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Procedures were performed under real-time ultrasound guidance using a 14-G introducer cannula and a 1.1-mm flexible cryoprobe. Technical success was achieved in all cases, with successful acquisition of two cryobiopsy specimens per patient. Seven patients received a malignant diagnosis, while three remained nondiagnostic and underwent clinical and radiological follow-up. In all diagnostic cases, cryobiopsy specimens preserved tissue architecture and were considered adequate for histopathological evaluation and ancillary molecular testing. No procedure-related complications, including bleeding, pneumothorax, vascular injury, infection, or hospitalization, were observed. These preliminary findings demonstrate that CryoPeUS is a feasible and safe minimally invasive technique capable of providing tissue suitable for both histopathological and molecular assessment. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to establish its diagnostic performance and define its role in the diagnostic pathway of thoracic malignancies.

articles.title: Post exacerbation Pulmonary Rehabilitation: is this a changing population?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Post-exacerbation pulmonary rehabilitation is a cost-effective, evidence-based intervention offered to patients admitted to hospital. Evidence from randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses demonstrates that early PR following exacerbation significantly improves exercise tolerance and health-related quality of life, while reducing hospital readmission rates and, in some cases, mortality. Despite strong guideline recommendations, uptake remains low due to barriers such as limited referral, patient frailty, and access issues.

DESIGN: An observational, cross sectional service evaluation of patients admitted to hospital with an exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). 1315 patients were assessed by the COPD nursing team at the University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust and offered pulmonary rehabilitation as part of the routine care bundle.

MAIN CLINICAL FINDINGS: A needs analysis was performed to analyse if there were any predictors to identify those not appropriate for pulmonary rehabilitation or correlations between demographics and those not appropriate.

MAIN OUTCOMES: The majority of patients (48%) declined a referral to PR with only 31% being referred. Readmission to hospital, use of oxygen therapy (both ABOT and LTOT), MRC, Frailty, age and FEV1 showed statistically significant associations with referral to PR; however, the strength of these associations differed. Bonferroni post hoc analysis of the multiple comparisons revealed a significant mean difference in frailty, MRC, LTOT, readmission & age (p = 0.033) was found between individuals who declined the referral and those for whom the referral was deemed not appropriate.

CONCLUSIONS: Several variables were identified as being associated with patients considered not appropriate for referral to PR, with the strongest associations observed for MRC, frailty and age. These along with readmission and oxygen use had significant differences between those that had a referral to PR and those not appropriate. Despite changes in the patient population, PR remained suitable for most patients (79%). The higher rate of patient refusal compared with clinical unsuitability indicates that optimising referral timing and engagement may be more important than reconsidering eligibility criteria.

articles.title: Inhibition of neutrophil extracellular trap formation ameliorates astrocyte pyroptosis via CUL7-dependent NLRP3 ubiquitination in mice with sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) encompasses acute brain dysfunction during sepsis and may be followed by persistent cognitive impairment among survivors. Although neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in sepsis-related organ injury, their role in astrocyte fate determination and neuroinflammation during SAE remains poorly defined. Here, using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model, we demonstrate that NETs accumulate in both the circulation and hippocampus following sepsis. Pharmacological inhibition or degradation of NETs markedly alleviated blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, neuronal death, and acute neurobehavioral abnormalities. Mechanistically, NET accumulation was associated with enhanced astrocyte pyroptosis via activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)-caspase-1-gasdermin D (GSDMD) pathway. Activation of NLRP3 abolished the neuroprotective effects conferred by NET inhibition. Transcriptomic analysis of human hippocampal tissues identified cullin 7 (CUL7) as a sepsis-associated candidate, and subsequent experiments showed that its expression was restored following NET inhibition. CUL7 physically interacted with NLRP3, enhanced its ubiquitination, and reduced its protein stability, thereby restraining astrocyte pyroptosis. Notably, CUL7 overexpression improved acute neurobehavioral outcomes, preserved blood-brain barrier integrity, and attenuated neuroinflammation in septic mice. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unrecognized NETs-CUL7-NLRP3 axis that governs astrocyte pyroptosis and contributes to the pathogenesis of SAE, highlighting CUL7 as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: The Right Ventricle in Focus: State-of-the-Art CMR Imaging - Challenges, Standards, and Innovations.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract: The right ventricle (RV) is recognized as a critical contributor to cardiovascular outcomes. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) has emerged as the reference standard for comprehensive RV assessment, enabling precise evaluation of ventricular volumes, function, flow, and tissue characterization. In this review, we provide a state-of-the-art overview of RV imaging using CMR. We first outline the anatomical and physiological features that distinguish the RV from the left ventricle. Next, we highlight the key technical challenges in imaging the RV, notably its complex geometry, prominent trabeculation, and thin myocardial wall. We then summarize current clinical CMR approaches, including cine imaging for volumetric assessment, phase-contrast techniques for flow quantification, and methods for tissue characterization such as late gadolinium enhancement. Additionally, we discuss advanced and emerging CMR techniques aimed at overcoming current RV imaging limitations, including high-resolution three-dimensional cine imaging, four-dimensional flow imaging, parametric mapping, and novel reconstruction strategies. These innovations hold promise for improving accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanistic insight into RV structure and function. Finally, we review the clinical role of CMR in major RV pathologies, including congenital heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, and tricuspid regurgitation. Across these conditions, CMR provides vital diagnostic and prognostic information, with growing evidence supporting its role in guiding clinical management. As technical advancements continue and standardization improves, CMR is poised to transform RV evaluation from a historically challenging endeavor into a precise and impactful component of cardiovascular care.

articles.title: Systemic Corticosteroid and Tendino-Myopathy Risk in Pediatric Asthma: A Self-Controlled Case Series.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although systemic corticosteroids are widely used for asthma, their potential association with tendino-myopathy has not been well established.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate whether systemic corticosteroid use is associated with risk of tendino-myopathy in children with asthma.

METHODS: This self-controlled case series study used nationwide health insurance claims data from South Korea between 2006 and 2020. Among children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years with newly diagnosed asthma, individuals with at least one tendino-myopathy and a history of systemic corticosteroid use during the 1-year observation period were included. Conditional Poisson regression models were used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for the occurrence of tendino-myopathy during exposure periods compared with non-exposure periods.

RESULTS: Among 398,748 subjects aged 6-18 years during the study period, 41,124 with newly diagnosed asthma were identified. Among these, 5,060 who experienced at least one tendino-myopathy and were exposed to systemic corticosteroids were included in the final analysis. The incidence of tendino-myopathy was significantly higher during the exposure periods of systemic corticosteroids compared with non-exposure periods (IRR, 2.68; 95% CI, 2.44-2.94). The risk remained elevated during both 1-7 days (IRR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.49-1.73) and 8-14 days after discontinuation (IRR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.05-1.26).

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic corticosteroid use was significantly associated with an increased risk of tendino-myopathy, which persisted for up to 14 days after discontinuation. These findings suggest the need for careful monitoring of musculoskeletal adverse events during the early period following systemic corticosteroid therapy in pediatric asthma.

articles.title: As-needed Albuterol-budesonide Reduces Exacerbation Risk at GINA Step 3 and Steps 4 and 5.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice

articles.title: Increased Exacerbation Reduction Over Time with Tezepelumab in Severe Asthma: CROSSROADS-4.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tezepelumab is a monoclonal antibody approved in the United States for severe asthma. Real-world evidence of effectiveness remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of tezepelumab in reducing annualized asthma exacerbation rates (AAERs) and healthcare resource utilization (HRU) in the United States.

METHODS: This retrospective, self-controlled, pre-post cohort study used data from Symphony Health, an ICON plc Company, PatientSource®, December 1, 2020, to June 30, 2024. Eligible patients were ≥12 years, had ≥2 records of tezepelumab, and experienced ≥2 asthma exacerbations in the 12 months before tezepelumab initiation, with index date being the day after initiation. AAERs and asthma exacerbation-related HRU were compared between the 12 months pre- and post-index. AAERs were also evaluated across patient subgroups.

RESULTS: A total of 527 patients were included. AAERs decreased significantly from 2.81 to 1.26 per person-year (55% decrease; 95% confidence interval [CI] [51%, 59%]; p<0.001). The greatest benefit was observed among patients starting treatment February 2023 and later (61% decrease; [53%-67%]; p<0.001). Consistent reductions were seen across subgroups: patients with pre-index blood eosinophil count <300 cells/μL and ≥300 cells/μL, pre-index total serum immunoglobulin E levels <100 IU/mL and ≥100 IU/mL, biologic-naïve and biologic-experienced, persistent tezepelumab users, and those with comorbid chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis. Asthma exacerbation-related HRU declined significantly (p<0.001) with 50-54% reductions across healthcare settings.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, patients with severe asthma treated with tezepelumab had substantial reductions in asthma exacerbations and HRU, with the greatest benefits among more recent initiators.

articles.title: Early Sudden Cardiac Death Risk in Heart Failure: Time to Rethink Primary Prevention?
articles.abstract: Despite advances in drug and device-based therapies, patients with heart failure (HF) face a substantial risk for mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for up to half of all deaths in patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), with a 6- to 9-fold higher risk compared with the general population. Recent data demonstrate that the risk for arrhythmic events cluster disproportionately more frequently within the first ∼6 months following the diagnosis of HFrEF despite the initiation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). This period is characterized by electrical instability, neurohormonal activation, and incomplete reverse remodeling; this is exacerbated by suboptimal exposure to GDMT. While temporal analyses suggest an overall decline in SCD rates in patients with chronic HFrEF, a persistent residual SCD risk that is clinically meaningful remains. While pharmacologic therapies reduce the risk for SCD to varying degrees, structural recovery often lags, creating a vulnerable phase during GDMT up-titration. Current guidelines mandate a waiting period of at least 3-6 months prior to implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) implantation to allow for potential ventricular recovery while GDMT is optimized. Moreover, the indication for primary prevention ICD implantation itself is being actively re-evaluated in the contemporary GDMT era. Yet this interval also exposes patients to an early arrhythmic risk, contributing to clinical apprehension. Wearable cardioverter defibrillators (WCD) may provide a noninvasive strategy to mitigate transient early SCD risk during guideline-mandated waiting periods. WCD platforms have demonstrated reliable arrhythmia detection and defibrillation capability, with high first-shock conversion rates and wear-time adherence in large-scale studies performed in clinical practice. WCDs enable continuous rhythm surveillance, which may support individualized decision-making regarding the timing of a permanent ICD implantation. This review synthesizes the contemporary burden and mechanisms of SCD in HFrEF and how approaches to primary prevention have evolved including an appraisal of the impact of GDMT on arrhythmic risk, current guideline recommendations, and examining the potential role of WCD therapy for protection during early phase vulnerability in these patients.

articles.title: Presepsin, age and kidney function: A temporally validated upper limit conditioned on estimated glomerular filtration rate.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Presepsin is renally cleared but assessed against a fixed threshold. We examined age, kidney function and presepsin, and derived an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-conditioned upper limit.

METHODS: First adult presepsin results at a Korean tertiary hospital (2020-2026) were linked with same-day C-reactive protein (CRP) and creatinine (12,455 patients); eGFR was calculated with the European Kidney Function Consortium (EKFC) eq. (2021 CKD-EPI for sensitivity). In 6296 patients with CRP <1 mg/dL, the 97.5th percentile of presepsin was modeled on eGFR, age and sex by quantile regression and evaluated in a test set, by cross-validation and in 2026, with a creatinine-stability sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Per decade of age, presepsin was 1.086-fold higher after adjustment for CRP, sex and setting, 1.048-fold after adding creatinine and 0.997-fold after adding EKFC eGFR (1.011 with CKD-EPI). Among patient-days with CRP <1 mg/dL, 20.2% at eGFR ≥90 and 98.0% below 15 exceeded 500 pg/mL. Each halving of eGFR raised the limit 1.68-fold (95% CI 1.51-2.00). A limit derived before 2026 was exceeded by 1.7% of 2026 results (nominal 2.5%), and the whole-population limit by 2.2% of patients with stable kidney function. Among all patients with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, 500 pg/mL flagged 96.2% and the conditioned limit 14.4%.

CONCLUSIONS: Creatinine accounted for about half of the age association and eGFR, which contains age, for nearly all of it. The conditioned limit reduced eGFR-related variation in exceedance, but the 2026 rate was below 2.5%; diagnostic value for sepsis requires validation.

articles.title: Relationship between physical, psychological function, and post-discharge life-space mobility in older patients with mild ischemic stroke: A longitudinal mediation analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Life-space mobility (LSM) is a multidimensional indicator of real-world mobility. Identifying factors associated with LSM may be important for supporting community mobility after stroke. Because physical and psychological function may interact in shaping mobility-related behavior, understanding their relationships may provide a more comprehensive understanding of post-stroke LSM. This study aimed to longitudinally investigate whether physical function at discharge is directly related to post-discharge LSM and indirectly via psychological function in older patients with mild ischemic stroke.

METHODS: This observational study adhered to the STROBE guidelines. Patients ≥65 years with acute ischemic stroke were included. This study used a hypothesis-driven framework of structural equation modeling to clarify the relationship between physical function, psychological function, and LSM. Life-space assessment (LSA) was performed before hospitalization (Pre-LSA) and at 6 months after stroke onset (Post-LSA). Post-LSA was used as the primary outcome, with Pre-LSA and other relevant covariates included in the model.

RESULTS: We enrolled 184 patients (median age, 77 years; 64 women). Physical function was significantly associated with LSM at 6 months (β = 0.321, p = 0.018), whereas the indirect association through psychological function was small and statistically non-significant (β = 0.014, p = 0.774). However, the hypothesized model showed inadequate model fit.

CONCLUSIONS: Physical function at discharge may be relevant to subsequent community mobility at 6 months in older patients with mild ischemic stroke; however, the model's fit is poor. Further studies using more comprehensive models are needed to clarify the determinants of long-term mobility after stroke.

articles.title: The β-cell stress continuum: Molecular mechanisms driving diabetes progression and cellular failure.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus encompasses heterogeneous disorders in which β-cell dysfunction contributes to impaired glucose regulation. Although the causes and sequence of disease processes differ across diabetes subtypes, β-cell stress has emerged as a potential convergent mechanism that may contribute to disease progression in some contexts. However, current evidence does not establish β-cell stress as the initiating event in all forms of type 1 diabetes (T1D) or type 2 diabetes (T2D). In T1D, autoimmune injury is a defining disease process, whereas in T2D, insulin resistance, genetic susceptibility, and environmental factors may precede or interact with β-cell dysfunction. This narrative review proposes the β-cell Stress Continuum as a testable conceptual framework for examining how β-cells may transition from adaptive responses to persistent dysfunction and, in some settings, loss of cellular identity or survival. The framework integrates immune, metabolic, oxidative, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondrial, inflammatory, and genomic stress, while recognizing that their relative contributions and temporal sequence may vary among individuals and diabetes subtypes. It also considers interactions between islets and other organs, including the liver, adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, immune system, and nervous system. The β-cell Stress Continuum is intended to organize research questions about β-cell adaptation and diabetes progression; it is not presented as a universal mechanism or as a replacement for disease-specific models. The proposed framework may help guide the investigation of biomarkers, disease staging, and therapeutic strategies, but its applicability and clinical utility require validation in subtype-specific, longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Outcomes of Calcanectomy in Diabetic Foot Ulcers and Calcaneal Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic Foot Ulcers (DFU) and calcaneal osteomyelitis present a formidable management challenge in limb reconstruction and preservation. Calcanectomy has emerged as an intermediate limb-preserving option. It aims to eliminate infection and allows wound closure without a need for major amputation. The aim of this review is to evaluate the outcomes of calcanectomy performed for DFU and osteomyelitis.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and Embase. Studies were restricted to English-language publications from 2020 onwards. The primary outcomes were limb salvage and major amputation rates. Secondary outcomes included wound healing, time to complete healing, post-operative complications, re-operation and mortality.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included, encompassing 503 patients undergoing partial, total, or vertical contour calcanectomy. Calcanectomy was associated with favourable rates of limb preservation with limb salvage exceeding 80% in 9 of the 15 studies (range: 40.0% to 100%). The highest reported major amputation rate was 60.0%. Complete wound healing rates ranged from 33.4% to 100%, with healing times ranging from 3.6 weeks to 7 months. Re-operation rates ranged from 0% to 62.8%, while postoperative infection spanned from 0% to 83.3%. Mortality ranged from 0% to 37.5%, reaching 43.3% at the five-year mark. Included literature carried a low-to-moderate risk of bias.

CONCLUSION: These findings support calcanectomy as a potentially valid alternative to major lower-limb amputation. Considerable heterogeneity in technique, outcome definitions and follow-up limits direct comparison. Prospective, multicentre studies with standardised reporting are needed to refine patient selection, optimal technique and confirm long-term functional benefit.

articles.title: The prevalence and long-term clinical significance of left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery in an asymptomatic population.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prevalence of left common iliac vein (LCIV) compression between the right common iliac artery and L5 vertebra in an asymptomatic cohort, and determine whether individuals with ≥50% LCIV stenosis develop chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) or deep venous thrombosis (DVT).

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study with prospective long-term clinical follow-up METHODS: Iliac venous anatomy was analysed on protocolised computed tomography (CT) in healthy individuals assessed for live related kidney donation at a tertiary referral centre between January 2012 and January 2019, with follow-up until January 2026. Scripted phone interviews assessed left leg venous symptoms, signs, investigations and treatment.

RESULTS: Of 102 participants, 60 were female (58.8%), median age was 38 years (IQR 30-45), mean body mass index was 26.6 ± 4.2. Mean LCIV compression was 39.2% ± 18.5. Female sex (OR 3.52, CI 1.36-10.1, p=0.009) and younger age (OR 0.91, CI 0.86-0.96, p<0.001) were independently associated with ≥50% LCIV compression. 39 participants (38.2%) had ≥50% LCIV compression; one participant (1%) had ≥70% LCIV compression. One participant developed a right leg DVT. No others underwent venous imaging for CVI or DVT over a median 11-year follow-up (IQR 9.1-12.7). Of 13 participants with ≥50% LCIV compression surveyed, three reported left leg varicosities and three reported an episode of isolated leg swelling without investigation or treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: LCIV compression is common on supine CT in healthy, asymptomatic individuals, particularly young females. On long term follow-up, no clinically significant left leg venous sequelae were identified in those with ≥50% LCIV compression. Hence, caution is advised when reporting this finding on CT to avoid unnecessary investigation or intervention.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Thrombin Injection for Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysms: Predictors of Failure and Recurrence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided thrombin injection (UGTI) is effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, but factors associated with early failure and recurrence remain incompletely defined. We evaluated treatment outcomes and their predictors.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients treated with UGTI between November 2023 and May 2026. Technical success was defined as immediate complete thrombosis after the first injection, clinical success as complete thrombosis at 24-hour Doppler follow-up, and recurrence as recanalization at 24 hours after technical success. Independent associations with clinical failure and recurrence were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 204 patients (94.4%), clinical success in 176 (81.5%), and recurrence occurred in 31 of 204 patients (15.2%). Overall success without surgical or endovascular repair was 94.0%. Therapeutic index procedures (OR, 6.368; 95% CI, 2.037-19.910), INR >1.5 (OR, 5.286; 95% CI, 1.681-16.625), shorter neck length (OR per mm, 0.879; 95% CI, 0.802-0.964), a longer procedure-to-UGTI interval (OR per day, 1.041; 95% CI, 1.008-1.074), and platelet count <150,000/μL (OR, 3.407; 95% CI, 1.174-9.884) were independently associated with clinical failure. Therapeutic procedures (OR, 7.670; 95% CI, 2.094-28.090) and INR >1.5 (OR, 3.653; 95% CI, 1.114-11.982) independently predicted recurrence. No procedure-related complications occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: UGTI was highly effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, with high immediate and overall success and no observed complications. Procedural, anatomical, temporal, and hemostatic factors were associated with outcomes, while clinical failure and recurrence represented distinct treatment phases. These findings may support risk-adapted surveillance.

articles.title: Effect of a Nurse-Driven Early Mobilization Protocol on Biomarker Levels and Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower Extremity Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023-June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n=107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n=98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff. Outcomes included postoperative DVT incidence, changes in D-dimer and C-reactive protein (CRP), bed rest duration, pain scores, length of stay, and complications. Repeated-measures ANOVA compared biomarker changes; binary logistic regression identified DVT risk factors.

RESULTS: The early mobilization group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative DVT than the control group (7.14% vs. 19.63%, P=0.009), with an absolute risk reduction of 12.49% and a relative risk reduction of 63.6%. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant between-group effects (F=22.33, P<0.001) and interaction effects (F=6.36, P<0.001) for CRP levels. After Bonferroni correction, the early mobilization group had significantly lower D-dimer and CRP levels at one week postoperatively and at discharge than the control group (P<0.0125). The early mobilization group also had significantly better outcomes in terms of bed rest duration (5.86±1.69 days vs. 6.38±1.54 days, P=0.021), NRS score on postoperative day 3 (3.27±1.15 vs. 4.54±1.47, P<0.001), and length of hospital stay (median 11.00 days vs. 13.00 days, P<0.001), as well as a lower complication rate (6.12% vs. 14.95%, P=0.041). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the early mobilization protocol (OR=0.27, 95%CI: 0.10-0.73, P=0.009), age (OR=1.05, 95%CI: 1.02-1.08, P=0.001), and postoperative day 1 D-dimer level (OR=1.25, 95%CI: 1.05-1.47, P=0.011) as independent factors influencing postoperative DVT.

CONCLUSION: A nurse-driven early mobilization protocol effectively reduces the incidence of DVT after lower extremity fracture surgery, improves coagulation and inflammatory biomarker levels, shortens hospital stay, and does not increase complication risks. The protocol is safe and feasible and can be recommended as an adjunctive measure for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention after lower extremity fracture surgery.

articles.title: Curcumin mitigates palmitic acid-induced senescence in MIN6 β cells through NOX4/ROS regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic β cell senescence is a key driver of type 2 diabetes (T2D) progression, and oxidative stress plays a critical role in this process. This study explored the therapeutic potential of curcumin against palmitic acid (PA)-induced senescence in MIN6 cells. We also explored whether this protection was achieved via modulation of the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase 4 (NOX4)/reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathway.

METHODS: We used PA to establish a lipotoxicity model in MIN6 cells. We assessed cell viability by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and insulin secretion with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) assay. We used flow cytometry to measure calcium concentration, β-galactosidase activity, cell cycle distribution, ROS production and mitochondrial membrane potential. Western blot was used to analyze the expression of NOX4 and senescence markers p16 and p21. We also performed molecular docking to predict the binding mode between curcumin and NOX4. We knocked down NOX4 to confirm its role in curcumin's protective effects.

RESULTS: PA significantly reduced MIN6 cell viability, insulin secretion and intracellular calcium concentration. PA induced cellular senescence, as evidenced by increased β-galactosidase activity, upregulated p16 and p21 expression and cell cycle arrest in the G0/G1 phase. PA activated the NOX4/ROS pathway, leading to ROS overproduction and a decrease in mitochondrial membrane potential. Curcumin treatment partially reversed these effects. Molecular docking showed curcumin binds strongly to NOX4 (binding energy: -8.4 kcal/mol). NOX4 knockdown enhanced curcumin's effects on oxidative stress and cell senescence.

CONCLUSION: Curcumin mitigates PA-induced senescence in MIN6 cells and restores insulin secretion by inhibiting the overactivation of the NOX4/ROS pathway and reducing oxidative stress.

articles.title: Circulating methylglyoxal enhances capsaicin-sensitive lung vagal afferent-mediated apneic reflex sensitivity in rats.
articles.abstract: Methylglyoxal (MG), a reactive metabolic byproduct of glycolysis, is linked to painful diabetic neuropathy. Diabetic patients are accompanied by more frequent exacerbations of asthma. Sensitization of capsaicin-sensitive lung vagal afferents (CSLVAs), the nociceptive-like nerve endings in the respiratory tract, contributes to the pathogenesis of airway hypersensitivity diseases such as asthma. However, whether MG sensitizes CSLVAs and the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. This study was undertaken in male adult Sprague-Dawley rats to investigate 1) whether intravenous administration of MG enhances the apneic reflex response to CSLVA stimulants, and if so, 2) whether CSLVAs play a role in the MG-induced enhancement of apneic reflex response; 3) whether the transient receptor potential ankyrin subtype 1 protein (TRPA1), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and activation of NADPH oxidase contribute to this MG-induced airway reflex hypersensitivity. Our results showed that intravenous administration of MG enhanced apneic response to right-atrial bolus injection of capsaicin in anesthetized, spontaneously breathing rats. This sensitizing effect was found 10min after MG administration and persisted at 90min. Similarly, the apneic reflex response to α,β-methylene-ATP (another CSLVA stimulant) was enhanced by MG. In contrast, saline administration did not augment the apneic reflex responses to these two stimulants. The sensitizing effect of MG on apneic response to stimulants was abolished by PCT of vagi, suggesting the involvement of CSLVAs. Additionally, the sensitizing effect of MG on the CSLVAs-mediated apneic reflex responses to stimulants was significantly attenuated by pretreatment with TRPA1 antagonists (HC030031 and AP18), an antioxidant (N-acetyl-L-cysteine), or an inhibitor of NADPH oxidase (apocynin), whereas their vehicle failed to do so. These results suggest that MG may sensitize CSLVAs and augment airway reflex, at least in part, through the involvement of TRPA1, ROS, and activation of NADPH oxidase.

articles.title: TRANSITION FROM PEDIATRIC TO ADULT CARE OF YOUTH WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES: A GLOBAL SURVEY FROM THE SWEET INITIATIVE.
authors: SWEET initiative (Better control in Pediatric and Adolescent diabeteS: Working to crEate CEnTers of Reference)
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess current practices for transition of youth with type 1 diabetes (T1D) to adult care across SWEET centers worldwide.

METHODS: A 34-item survey regarding the transition of T1D care was developed by experienced pediatric and adult diabetologists.

RESULTS: 102/160 SWEET centers completed the survey (54 from Europe, 27 from Asia/Middle East/Africa, 11 from North America, 6 from South America, 4 from Australia/New Zealand, 84% academic, 73% exclusively pediatric). A national legal age limit for reimbursement of pediatric care exists in 49% of centers. Transfer occurs between 18 and 20 years in 46% of centers. 6% of centers do not transfer youth with T1D and 42% lack a structured transition program. Among centers with transition programs, 26% are limited to pediatric care, 3% to adult care and 29% involve both pediatric and adult centers. Accordingly, only 39% of centers have a transition team. Transition readiness is assessed in 25% of centers. The most frequent reason for transfer is age (82% of centers). Metabolic control influences the timing of transfer in 60% of centers, psychiatric comorbidity in 57%, and teen pregnancy in 65%.

CONCLUSIONS: This global survey highlights substantial differences and a widespread lack of structured transition process for most youth with T1D, underscoring the need to standardize practice for successful transition.

articles.title: Preserving information and integrity in Cryo-EM: Toward a Fourier-space deposition approach.
articles.abstract: Current guidelines for depositing cryogenic electron microscopy single particle reconstruction (cryo-EM SPR) data require submission of unfiltered, unmasked, and unsharpened raw half-maps. The Fourier Shell Correlation (FSC) between the half-maps is then used as a proxy for the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to estimate the reconstruction's resolution. This policy was introduced to enable independent validation of reported resolutions. Although developed to safeguard data integrity and minimize bias, these guidelines do not account for specific features of modern cryo-EM processing software, in particular weighting schemes that are not retained in half-map depositions and yet in general are necessary to recapitulate resolution estimates. As a result, resolution estimates and other validation statistics based on half-map FSC may be under- or overestimated. Here, we describe the limitations of the current deposition guidelines and propose an alternative: depositing cryo-EM results in Fourier (reciprocal) space together with the mandatory deposition of molecular masks or their descriptors. This approach would address the current limitations, preserve critical information from the reconstruction process, and better support downstream analyses.

articles.title: Early Cardiac Dysfunction in Pediatric Becker Muscular Dystrophy: A Prospective Cross-sectional Echocardiographic Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked disorder characterized by progressive muscle weakness and cardiac involvement, with cardiomyopathy being the leading cause of mortality. While cardiac dysfunction in adult BMD patients is well documented, the early cardiac phenotype in pediatric populations remains poorly understood. This prospective cross-sectional study aimed to characterize age-stratified differences in cardiac function among children with BMD, children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), and healthy controls.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included male children aged 3-18 years who were enrolled from June 2020 to December 2023 and met strict inclusion criteria: genetically confirmed BMD or DMD diagnosis, no prior cardiac medications, and absence of comorbid conditions affecting cardiac function. Participants were stratified into three age-matched groups: 3 to under 7 years (youngest group), 7 to under 10 years (middle group), and 10 to under 18 years (oldest group), with comparable mean ages across BMD, DMD, and healthy controls within each age stratum. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessments were performed, including conventional parameters, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography. Statistical comparisons were made between groups within each age range.

RESULT: The study comprised 86 BMD patients, 86 DMD patients, and 74 controls across three age groups. After normality testing and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons, BMD patients showed early left ventricular involvement, including lower LVEF (60.54±8.09% vs 65.56±3.04%, p<0.01) and GLS (18.06±2.10 vs 20.66±1.42, p<0.01) than healthy controls from the Younger group onward. Right ventricular enlargement (RV GLS 22.99±3.26 vs 25.58±2.37, p<0.01) and reduced FAC (40.35±6.01% vs 47.8±17.08%, p<0.01) were also evident in BMD, with age-dependent RV strain abnormalities. Compared with DMD, BMD showed larger LVEDV across age groups and relatively preserved GCS, whereas GLS abnormalities (18.06±2.10 vs 20.66±1.42, p<0.01) were still present compared with healthy controls. Left atrial reservoir/conduit indices were better preserved in BMD than DMD in the Older group. In a short-term longitudinal subsample (16 BMD and 19 DMD patients; mean follow-up ∼0.9 years), BMD patients showed a modest decline in LVEF (annualized change 2.01%/year, P = 0.050), while LV-GLS remained stable in both groups.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric BMD patients exhibit subclinical, age-associated cardiac dysfunction detectable across pediatric age groups. Because abnormalities in LVEF, LV GLS, RV FAC, and RV GLS were already present in the youngest group, the findings support early and regular cardiac surveillance incorporating advanced echocardiographic techniques from preschool age. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these subclinical differences predict clinically overt cardiomyopathy or treatment response.
