articles.title: Distinct Thermosensitive Activation of HSF1 and HSF2 in Immune Cells During Aging.
articles.abstract: Heat shock factors (HSF1 and HSF2) critically maintain proteostasis under stress, yet their activation across the continuum of rising temperatures is incompletely understood. Furthermore, how age impacts thermally driven rheostatic changes in stress responses is not fully elucidated. Here, we investigate how different temperature levels impact HSF1 and HSF2 in Jurkat T cells and splenocytes from young and aged mice. Using Western blotting, EMSA, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation, we examined heat shock response changes across a range of thermal conditions. Unlike most cell types that require 42°C for HSF1 activation, Jurkat cells maximally responded at 41°C and splenocytes at 40°C. Optimal HSF1 activation coincided with maximal nuclear translocation, Ser326 phosphorylation, SIRT1 protein levels, and HSP RNA levels. By contrast, HSF2 nuclear translocation required a higher temperature (42°C) than HSF1. Age reduced HSF1 protein levels and nuclear translocation during thermal stress, while HSF2 protein levels were significantly elevated. These findings reveal distinct temperature-sensitive patterns of HSF1 and HSF2 activation of immunocytes during heat stress and identify age-associated alterations in this response.

articles.title: Challenges in Infection Prevention and Control in Paramedicine: A Modified Nominal Group Technique Consensus Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are a major patient safety concern, yet infection prevention and control (IPC) in emergency ambulance services is challenging due to unpredictable environments, operational pressures, and equipment limitations. Evidence is limited regarding how ambulance fleet and equipment design influence IPC compliance. This study aimed to identify expert priorities for improving the availability and utility of IPC equipment and consumables in paramedicine.

METHODS: A modified Nominal Group Technique was conducted with experts in infection prevention, paramedicine, clinical governance, education, and operations. Participants collectively generated ideas concerned with IPC in emergency ambulance services and subsequently ranked these through an anonymous survey to determine priority areas.

RESULTS: Ten experts participated. Human factors were ranked as the most influential determinant of IPC compliance, followed by education and training, physical environment, equipment and consumables, and contaminated equipment management. Key barriers included organizational culture, compliance fatigue, inconsistent education, uncontrolled environments, and fleet design limitations.

CONCLUSION: IPC compliance in ambulance services is primarily shaped by behavioral, organizational, and environmental factors rather than equipment provision alone. Systems-based, co-designed interventions addressing human factors, education, organizational support, and equipment design are essential to improve IPC adherence and enhance patient and clinician safety.

articles.title: Isolation inequity: Exploring race-based differences in hospital isolation duration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolation precautions are essential for preventing transmission of infectious diseases in healthcare settings but may be associated with unintended negative effects on patient care. Although racial and ethnic disparities have been documented across many healthcare processes and outcomes, their relationship to isolation precaution practices has not been well described. This study evaluated the association between patient race and ethnicity and duration of inpatient isolation precautions.

METHODS: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted in a 13-hospital academic healthcare system from November 2017 through December 2022. Gamma regression models were used to evaluate associations between isolation duration and patient race, ethnicity, age, sex, and isolation type. A sensitivity analysis excluded COVID-19-related Severe Respiratory isolation encounters to account for disproportionate disease burden.

RESULTS: Among 39,304 patients, 88.7% identified as White/Caucasian and 11.3% as non-White/non-Caucasian. In unadjusted analysis, non-White/non-Caucasian race was associated with 15% longer isolation duration compared with White/Caucasian race. After adjustment for age, sex, ethnicity, and isolation type, non-White/non-Caucasian race remained associated with 13% longer isolation duration. When Severe Respiratory isolation encounters were excluded, non-White/non-Caucasian race remained associated with 17% longer isolation duration.

CONCLUSIONS: Non-White/non-Caucasian race was independently associated with longer inpatient isolation duration. These findings suggest potential inequities in isolation experiences and highlight the need for further investigation into the clinical, operational, and structural factors contributing to observed differences.

articles.title: POST-TREATMENT SURVEILLANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF RECURRENT CERVICAL CANCER - A REVIEW FROM THE FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP.
authors: members from the FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the available evidence on post-treatment follow-up and recurrence management after cervical cancer.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of the literature on surveillance modalities, and the management of pelvic and nodal recurrences.

RESULTS: Most recurrences occur within three years of treatment, but the survival benefit of detection before symptom onset remains unproven. After fertility-sparing surgery, HPV testing is sensitive for detecting asymptomatic pelvic recurrence. After hysterectomy, most recurrences are symptomatic, and clinical examination has a higher diagnostic yield than HPV testing or vaginal vault cytology. After concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT), persistent HPV infection is associated with an increased recurrence risk, but its limited specificity and the absence of a validated HPV-based surveillance strategy restrict its clinical utility. MRI and FDG PET/CT are useful for response assessment and investigation of suspected recurrence, but evidence supporting routine imaging of asymptomatic patients is lacking. Intensive follow-up schedules have not improved recurrence detection or survival. Evidence on recurrence management is predominantly retrospective. Pelvic recurrences after primary surgery have been treated with CRT, supplemented by brachytherapy for vaginal involvement. In selected patients with central pelvic recurrence after CRT, complete surgical resection may provide prolonged survival, but carries substantial morbidity. Nodal recurrences outside previously irradiated fields have been treated with CRT.

CONCLUSION: Available evidence supports a predominantly clinical, treatment-adapted follow-up. The survival benefit of intensive surveillance, routine imaging, or detecting asymptomatic recurrence remains uncertain. Recurrence management requires individualized multidisciplinary assessment based on disease extent, disease-free interval, and previous treatments.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation recurrence pattern and subsequent heart failure hospitalization after ablation in left ventricular systolic dysfunction: A time-dependent analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, but the prognostic significance of postablation recurrence pattern and its evolution remains unclear. We investigated whether evolving postablation recurrence pattern was associated with subsequent heart failure (HF) hospitalization.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 381 of 5535 consecutive patients who underwent first-time AF ablation between 2012 and 2024 and had baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50%. Recurrence was defined as any atrial tachyarrhythmia lasting >30 s beyond the 3-month blanking period and classified as paroxysmal or persistent (lasting >7 days). Recurrence pattern was modeled as a time-dependent variable and updated upon documentation of paroxysmal or persistent recurrence during follow-up.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 49 months, 140 patients experienced recurrence (71 paroxysmal only and 69 persistent, including 21 who progressed from paroxysmal to persistent recurrence) and 61 experienced HF hospitalization. In a multivariable time-dependent Cox model adjusted for age, sex, baseline LVEF, prior myocardial infarction, prior HF hospitalization, and baseline AF type, both paroxysmal recurrence [hazard ratio (HR), 2.38; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.15-4.90; p = 0.019] and persistent recurrence (HR, 5.45; 95% CI, 2.59-11.46; p < 0.001) were associated with HF hospitalization compared with no recurrence. Persistent recurrence was also associated with a higher risk than paroxysmal recurrence (HR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.00-5.25; p = 0.049).

CONCLUSIONS: Time-updated assessment of postablation AF recurrence pattern revealed differential risks of subsequent HF hospitalization among patients with LV systolic dysfunction. Both paroxysmal and persistent recurrence were associated with HF hospitalization, with persistent recurrence representing a particularly high-risk state that may warrant closer HF surveillance and reassessment of rhythm-control strategies.

articles.title: The BCAA Paradox: From Anabolic Nutrients to Metabolic Signals in Insulin Resistance.
articles.abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA), including leucine, isoleucine and valine, play a key role in human metabolism. As regulators of protein synthesis, nutrient signaling and metabolic homeostasis, they are widely used in sports nutrition and clinical practice because of their anabolic properties and ability to enhance muscle protein synthesis. Paradoxically, however, elevated circulating BCAA concentrations are consistently associated with insulin resistance (IR), type 2 diabetes, overfeeding and obesity in humans, while preclinical studies suggest that chronic BCAA excess can contribute to IR, particularly in the context of overfeeding. Conversely, metabolic benefits observed following dietary BCAA restriction or pharmacological enhancement of BCAA catabolism have raised interest in this pathway as a potential therapeutic target. Yet, tissue-specific genetic models demonstrate that lowering circulating BCAA concentrations alone is not sufficient to improve insulin sensitivity, while human studies provide limited evidence for consistent effects of BCAA manipulation on insulin sensitivity or appetite regulation. Collectively, these findings suggest that BCAA and their downstream metabolites should not be considered merely as circulating biomarkers or metabolic substrates, but as components of a tissue-specific metabolic network coordinating nutrient sensing, mitochondrial metabolism and inter-organ communication.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted, Electrocardiogram-Derived, Sequential Rule-Based Decision Tree for Exclusion of Acute Coronary Syndrome as the Etiology of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), deciding which patients without ST-segment elevation warrant emergency coronary angiography is difficult, as standard electrocardiogram (ECG), troponin, and echocardiography are limited in the early post-arrest window. We aimed to develop a sequential rule-based decision tree to identify post-ROSC patients in whom acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is unlikely to be the arrest etiology.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with OHCA were divided into development (2020-2024; n=329) and temporal validation (2025; n=71) cohorts. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECGs were analyzed by a deep-learning platform generating ten digital biomarkers. Five candidate biomarkers were combined into a rhythm-stratified sequential decision tree under a zero false-negative constraint; its performance was compared with that of individual biomarkers and validated in the temporal cohort.

RESULTS: The tree classified 171/329 (52.0%) and 32/71 (45.1%) patients in the development and validation cohorts, respectively, as "ACS not likely," with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified at any node. Yield concentrated in the non-shockable subgroup, in which the model excluded 169/261 (64.8%) non-ACS cases (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], 0.824), outperforming each individual biomarker. In the shockable subgroup, which carries a high pretest probability of ACS, 38/40 patients (95.0%) were retained as "ACS not excluded."

CONCLUSIONS: A rhythm-stratified, rule-based decision tree combining AI-assisted ECG-derived biomarkers classified approximately half of post-OHCA patients as "ACS not likely" with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified, principally in the non-shockable subgroup. This transparent, bedside-deployable framework warrants prospective multicenter evaluation.

articles.title: Stigmasterol ameliorates pulmonary hypertension by suppressing the CCL5/CCR5 signaling pathway: Taurocholic acid as a downstream mediator.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a devastating disease characterized by irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling (PVR), ultimately culminating in right ventricular failure and death. Although previous studies have demonstrated that stigmasterol (STG) reduces cholesterol levels and prevents cardiovascular diseases, its potential role in PH remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effects of STG on SU5416/hypoxia (Su/Hx)-induced PH in mice and elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms.

METHODS: Through bioinformatics analysis and network pharmacology, we identified STG as a promising herbal compound for PH treatment. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments validated that STG ameliorates platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-induced proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), as well as PVR and right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, MM-PBSA calculation, and microscale thermophoresis (MST) were used to validate direct STG-CCL5 binding. Functional rescue experiments with taurocholic acid (TCA) were also performed.

RESULTS: Molecular docking, MD simulation, and MST revealed spontaneous direct binding between CCL5 and STG, with an MST-derived KD of 4.72 μM. While CCL5 promoted PDGF-BB-induced PASMC proliferation and migration, CCR5 inhibition counteracted these effects. STG ameliorated PASMC proliferation and migration by modulating CCL5. Furthermore, metabolomics and mass spectrometry analyses showed decreased taurocholic acid levels in lung tissues of CCR5-knockout (CCR5-/-) mice in the Su/Hx model. TCA reversed the protective effects of STG on PASMC proliferation and migration, supporting TCA as a downstream functional mediator.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our study demonstrates that STG ameliorates Su/Hx-induced PH by modulating the CCL5/CCR5 signaling pathway, with taurocholic acid acting as a downstream mediator. Further investigations are warranted to explore the clinical applicability of STG-based therapies for PH patients.

articles.title: Robotic Assessment of Thumb Proprioception after Stroke: Reliability, Validity, and Sensitivity.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite the thumb's critical role in dexterity and its dense sensory innervation, thumb proprioceptive deficits after stroke remain limited due to the limited nature of clinical assessments. This study evaluated the reliability, validity, and sensitivity of a novel robotic assessment of thumb proprioception, SomatoCircleJump (SCJ), in individuals with chronic stroke.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional psychometric study evaluating the reliability, validity and sensitivity of SCJ using baseline data from a clinical trial, with assessments conducted twice 5-10 days apart. In SCJ, a robot moved the visually occluded thumb, and participants indicated when the thumb passed a visual target.

SETTING: University-based rehabilitation research laboratory.

PARTICIPANTS: Thirty-five stroke survivors with residual unilateral hand weakness and 24 healthy age-matched controls.

INTERVENTIONS: Not applicable.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: SCJ proprioceptive error, defined as the angular difference between actual thumb position and the visually presented target. Test-retest reliability was assessed with Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). Validity and sensitivity were evaluated by comparing SCJ with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment Sensory Scale for the upper extremity (FMA-S) thumb position item, and two robotic proprioception tests, one for the thumb (ThumbSense) and one for the fingers (Crisscross).

RESULTS: SCJ demonstrated good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.82, 95% CI [0.72-0.87]). SCJ error correlated significantly with FMA-S (ρ = -0.56, p < 0.001), ThumbSense accuracy (ρ = -0.62, p < 0.001), and Crisscross error (ρ = 0.61, p < 0.001). Using a 2SD criterion relative to controls, SCJ identified thumb proprioceptive impairment in 61% of stroke participants, compared with 23% identified by FMA-S.

CONCLUSIONS: SCJ is a reliable, valid, and sensitive assessment of dynamic thumb proprioception after stroke. It revealed that thumb proprioceptive deficits are common and related to finger proprioception deficits, supporting its use in future studies of sensory impairment and rehabilitation outcomes.

articles.title: Aging in cardio-oncology: Pathophysiology, clinical implications and future directions.
articles.abstract: Population aging is changing the needs of patients seen in cardio-oncology. Older adults with cancer often have cardiovascular disease, multimorbidity, and reduced physiological reserve, which can complicate treatment and recovery. Patients of the same chronological age may differ considerably in cardiovascular health, functional capacity, and treatment tolerance. Frailty and geriatric assessment can help characterize these differences and inform care. This review examines the biological mechanisms linking aging, cancer, and cardiovascular disease and discusses their implications for cardiovascular risk assessment, cancer treatment decisions, and long-term survivorship. Treatment decisions require consideration of the expected oncological benefit, cardiovascular risk, physiological reserve, life expectancy, and patient preferences. Identifying and addressing reversible vulnerabilities may help patients tolerate effective anticancer therapy while preserving function and quality of life. During survivorship, cardiovascular care should account for previous treatment exposure, changing health status, and adherence to preventive therapies. Closer collaboration between cardio-oncology and geriatric medicine may improve the assessment and management of older patients. Evidence specific to frail and very old adults remains limited. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether geriatric and biological aging measures improve cardiovascular risk prediction, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Patient Characteristics and Outcomes of Urethral Ligation: A TURNS Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize patient selection and midterm outcomes after urethral ligation (UL) for end-stage outlet pathology across multiple reconstructive centers.

METHODS: We retrospectively identified men undergoing UL at seven Trauma and Urologic Reconstructive Network of Surgeons centers from May 2005 through June 2025. The primary outcome was recurrent incontinence. Secondary outcomes included revision, 30-day readmission, urinary tract infection (UTI), urethral fistula, and abscess. Cumulative risks of recurrence and revision were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven men underwent UL at a median age of 72 years (IQR 48-81). Common indications included urethral stricture/devastated urethra (29.6%), refractory incontinence (29.6%), failed bladder neck closure (25.9%), and artificial urinary sphincter erosion (22.2%). Urinary drainage was managed with a suprapubic tube in 19 patients, a continent catheterizable channel in 7, and ileovesicostomy in 1. Median follow-up was 24 months (IQR, 4-48); 11 patients (40.7%) had less than 1 year of follow-up. Three recurrences occurred within 3 months. Recurrence probability was 11.6% (95% CI, 3.9%-32.9%) and remained unchanged through 4 years. Revision risk was 3.7% (95% CI, 0.5%-23.5%). Thirty-day readmission occurred in 5 patients (18.5%). Among 16 patients with at least 1 year of follow-up, 11 (68.8%) developed UTI, and 3 (18.8%) developed urethral fistula.

CONCLUSIONS: In a multi-institutional cohort, urethral ligation achieved high midterm success with low risk of revision surgery or fistulation. The burden of infection and readmission highlights the need for structured postoperative surveillance and bladder-directed interventions.

articles.title: Dysnatremia in critically ill burn patients: incidence, timing and association with kidney outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia (<135 mmol/L) or hypernatremia (>145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity.

RESULTS: Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes).

CONCLUSION: Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

articles.title: Persistent Hepatocyte Plasticity and Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming After Hepatitis C Virus Cure.
articles.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection disrupts hepatocyte polarity and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), contributing to liver disease progression. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) eradicate HCV infection in most patients, the risk of fibrosis progression and hepatocellular carcinoma persists after viral clearance. Whether antiviral cure fully restores hepatocyte differentiation, polarity, and epithelial identity programs remains unclear. We investigated whether HCV-induced EMT and lipid metabolism alterations are fully reversible following DAA treatment.

METHODS: Huh7 hepatoma cells and Huh7 cells stably expressing a full-length HCV replicon were cultured in three-dimensional Matrigel to assess morphogenesis, polarity-associated features, and EMT. Spheroid morphology, canalicular-like organization, EMT markers, and transcriptomic signatures were analyzed using microscopy, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, and microarray analysis. The effects of DAA treatment (sofosbuvir with or without velpatasvir) were evaluated in vitro. Publicly available transcriptomic data from liver biopsies collected before therapy and within five days after its completion, were analyzed.

RESULTS: HCV replicon expression altered canalicular-like organization and induced actin-rich protrusions in 90% of Huh7-R spheroids. DAA treatment efficiently suppressed HCV replicon expression and partially restored epithelial morphology, reducing protrusions to 25%, without normalizing them to the control level (2.5%). EMT-associated changes, including reduced E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin expression, were only partially corrected by DAA treatment. Transcriptomic EMT scoring showed persistent mesenchymal features in DAA-treated cells and in patient biopsies collected at the end of treatment. In parallel, genes involved in lipid metabolism and hepatocyte differentiation remained dysregulated.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings show incomplete restoration of epithelial organization after suppression of HCV replicon expression in vitro and incomplete normalization of selected transcriptional signatures at the end of DAA treatment in patient liver samples. They suggest that cellular plasticity and metabolic reprogramming may persist after treatment and contribute to long-term liver disease risk.

articles.title: Immunotherapy targeting an endogenous retrovirus decreases islet senescence markers and preserves glucose control in a mouse model of type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type-2-diabetes is characterized by progressive metabolic stress and accumulation of senescent cells in key metabolic tissues, such as the pancreas, adipose tissue, and liver. Cellular senescence - an irreversible growth-arrested, and pro-inflammatory cell state can lead to induction of endogenous retrovirus (ERV) expression, which can also trigger cellular senescence. This possibly implies that a self-reinforcing ERV-senescence axis contributes to the metabolic decline and T2D. Here we developed and tested a mouse endogenous retrovirus (muERV) based active immunotherapy targeted at the most intact muERV, IAPE (Intracisternal A-type Particles elements with an Envelope) to eliminate cells expressing muERVs and senescence associated proteins in a mouse model of accelerated diabetes combining a high-fat diet (HFD) with dexamethasone (DEX) and streptozotocin (STZ) (DS-HFD). Immunized DS-HFD mice (DS-HFD + IAPE-Tx) showed increased B and T cell responses towards IAPE. Antisera generated using our IAPE-targeted active immunotherapy was used to confirm activation of IAPE expression in the murine β-cell line MIN-6, following both inflammatory (cytokines) and chemical stress (STZ and DEX). In Vivo, DS-HFD + IAPE-Tx mice showed reduced weight gain, improved fasting insulin-glucose homeostasis and oral glucose tolerance. They furthermore showed reduction in histomorphometry features consistent with steatosis, hepatocyte binucleation, reduced adipocyte size, and pancreatic islet senescence markers p16INK4a and p21Cip1/waf1, with a slight decrease in islet IAPE. Finally, we show activation of a human orthologue to IAPE, HERV-K, in cytokine-exposed isolated human pancreatic islets and EndoC-βH5 β-cells. Together, our results suggest that ERV antigens are expressed in metabolic disease models and may be targeted by immunotherapy to improve metabolic parameters, through a potential senolytic or senostatic-related but so far undefined mechanism.

articles.title: Involvement of PINK1-related Mitophagy and Necroptosis in TDI-Induced Experimental Asthma.
articles.abstract: Toluene diisocyanate (TDI) is a prevalent cause of occupational asthma. Although mitophagy contributes to various pulmonary diseases, its role and downstream signaling in TDI-induced asthma remain unclear. In this study, we first utilized BALB/c mice to investigate the effects of TDI exposure on pulmonary injury, mitophagy, and associated regulatory mechanisms. Based on these findings, we constructed an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) network for TDI-induced asthma. Mechanistic connections predicted by the AOP were validated in vitro using PINK1-knockdown bronchial epithelial cells, assessing PINK1-related mitophagy, mitochondrial function, cytosolic mtDNA release, attenuated the increased expression of cGAS/STING pathway-related proteins, and necroptosis. Finally, we predicted potential natural product therapeutics through bioactivity screening and toxicity profiling, targeting key genes implicated in TDI-induced asthma. Integration of in vivo, in vitro, and AOP network analyses indicated that TDI exposure induced airway hyperresponsiveness and pulmonary histopathological changes, along with elevated Th2 cytokine production. This exposure selectively upregulated PINK1 and Parkin expression, without altering levels of BNIP3, NIX, or FUNDC1. PINK1 knockdown mitigated TDI-induced mitophagy-related alterations, restored mitochondrial function, reduced cytosolic mtDNA release, attenuated the increased expression of cGAS/STING pathway-related proteins, and reduced necroptosis. In silico screening predicted β-lapachone, genistein, and apigenin as promising candidate therapeutics for TDI-induced asthma. Overall, PINK1-related mitophagy may contribute to TDI-induced occupational asthma, and natural compounds identified via in silico screening are potential candidates that require further in vitro and in vivo validation of their safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Informal caregiving and unmet social needs among U.S. adults at risk of cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Unmet social needs, such as food insecurity, housing instability, and transportation barriers, are key risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, little is known about their prevalence and consequences among informal caregivers at elevated risk of future CVD. This study investigates associations between informal caregiving and unmet social needs among adults at increased risk of future CVD.

METHODS: Pooled, nationally representative, cross-sectional data were analyzed for a sample of 7,215 noninstitutionalized U.S. adults (ages ≥18 years) with ≥one major CVD risk factor (hypertension, diabetes, obesity, or current smoking) and without a known cardiovascular disease. Data were drawn from the 6th (HINTS6, 2022) and 7th (HINTS7, 2024) iterations of the Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS). Adjusted logistic regressions were fit to estimate marginal predicted probabilities (MPPs) and absolute risk differences (ARDs) for unmet social needs by informal caregiving status. Complex design features of HINTS and jackknife replicate weights were incorporated into analyses to generate robust population-level estimates.

RESULTS: Among adults at risk of CVD, 17.6% were informal caregivers. Compared to non-caregivers, caregivers had higher probabilities of food insecurity, including cutting or skipping meals (MPPs: 23.8% vs. 14.1%; ARD: 9.7 percentage points [PPs]) and inability to afford balanced meals (MPPs: 24.9% vs. 15.0%; ARD: 9.9 PPs). Housing instability was also more prevalent among caregivers (MPPs: 18.5% vs. 12.9%; ARD: 5.6 PPs).

CONCLUSIONS: The findings indicate that informal caregiving was associated with a disproportionate burden of unmet social needs among adults at risk of future CVD. Incorporating caregiver-inclusive screening of social needs and care navigation into preventive care models could support caregiver health and contribute to long-term CVD risk reduction.

articles.title: Racial disparities in glucose sensor and insulin pump use and formal access through Brazil's Unified health system among people with type 1 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate racial disparities in glucose sensor and insulin pump use among people with type 1 diabetes in Brazil and associations of race/skin color with formal requests and approvals through the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS).

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 2454 adults with type 1 diabetes or caregivers of children and adolescents. Multivariable logistic regression examined race/skin color associations with technology use, formal requests, and approvals. Minimally and fully adjusted models were compared, and nonlinear Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition quantified explained and unexplained technology-use gaps.

RESULTS: Compared with White participants, Brown participants had lower odds of sensor use (OR 0.76; 95% CI 0.62-0.94) and pump use (OR 0.75; 95% CI 0.59-0.94); corresponding estimates for Black participants were 0.57 (0.39-0.82) and 0.53 (0.32-0.84). Race/skin color was not significantly associated with formal requests or approvals, whereas geographic region was strongly associated with approval. Measured sociodemographic characteristics explained 27.7%-52.9% of racial technology-use gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: Racial disparities in technology use persisted beyond measured socioeconomic differences. Contrasting patterns across current use and formal SUS outcomes suggest that inequities may arise at other stages of access.

articles.title: Semaglutide versus other GLP-1 RAs and cardiovascular risk in obesity-related cancer survivors.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Obesity-related cancer (ORCa) survivors are a unique population often excluded from landmark GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) trials. Given their cardiovascular risks, we investigated whether semaglutide initiation, compared with other GLP-1 RA, was associated with modified 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among ORCa survivors with type 2 diabetes (T2D).

METHODS: We emulated a target trial using PCORnet-UTSW electronic health records (2016-2025). Adults with ORCa and T2D initiating semaglutide versus other GLP-1 RA were included. The primary outcome was modified 3-point MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, or all-cause mortality). Cumulative incidence risk (CIR), risk difference (RD), and hazard ratio (HR) were estimated in 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort.

RESULTS: Among 918 matched patients (semaglutide, n = 459; other GLP-1 RA, n = 459), 124 modified 3-point MACE occurred. The 5-year CIR% was 17.6 (95% CI, 12.3-22.9) for semaglutide and 26.6 (95% CI, 20.7-32.6) for other GLP-1 RA. Semaglutide was associated with lower modified 3-point MACE risk (RD%, -7.41 [95% CI, -11.83 to - 2.98];HR, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.44-0.94]) than other GLP-1 RA. Findings were largely consistent across high-risk subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide was associated with a lower modified 3-point MACE risk than other GLP-1 RA. These findings suggest potential heterogeneity in cardioprotective effects and warrant confirmation.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of pancreatic polypeptide levels in healthy individuals and individuals with diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetes of the exocrine pancreas (DEP) is frequently underdiagnosed and misdiagnosed. Although pancreatic polypeptide (PP) has been proposed as a diagnostic marker, its directional change and diagnostic utility remain controversial.We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science up to 26 May 2026 for studies on plasma PP in diabetes. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.Nineteen studies were included, 12 entered meta-analysis. Compared with HC, DEP showed higher fasting PP (MD = -64.97) but no significant difference in postprandial PP peak (MD = -78.60). T2DM showed elevated fasting (MD = -50.72) and postprandial peak PP (MD = -176.25). DEP and T2DM did not differ significantly in either measure (MD = -15.82 and -61.61). Subgroup analysis showed higher fasting PP in PPDM versus HC (MD = -75.37), and no significant differences between PCRD and HC (MD = -202.03) or between PCRD and T2DM (MD = -25.01 and -82.96).T2DM shows pan-phasic PP elevation, whereas DEP shows higher fasting PP without a significant difference in absolute postprandial peak. These findings reflect group-level secretion patterns rather than confirmed diagnostic utility.

articles.title: Association of type 2 diabetes mellitus with sarcopenia in adults: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may adversely affect skeletal muscle mass, strength, and function. We aimed to quantify associations between sarcopenia and T2DM, prediabetes, and diabetes-related complications in adults. Five databases were searched from inception to July 2026 for observational studies comparing adults with T2DM and non-diabetic controls. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and evaluated bias. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95 % confidence intervals (CIs). Thirty-five studies were included. T2DM was associated with higher odds of sarcopenia (pooled OR 1.61, 95 % CI 1.26-2.06), despite substantial heterogeneity and a wide prediction interval. Associations were consistent across study designs, regions, and muscle-mass assessment methods, with no single study driving results or evidence of funnel-plot asymmetry. Prediabetes was not significantly associated with sarcopenia (OR 1.16, 95 % CI 0.63-2.15). Among complications, diabetic foot disease was associated with higher sarcopenia odds, whereas estimates for retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy were imprecise and non-significant. Adults with T2DM have moderately higher odds of sarcopenia than non-diabetic adults, though observational design and heterogeneity limit causal claims. Muscle health assessment may benefit vulnerable adults with T2DM, but prospective studies are needed to clarify temporal associations.

articles.title: Circulating omentin-1 and metaflammation across body mass index categories in men with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate circulating omentin-1 across BMI categories in men with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and its associations with adiposity, insulin resistance, and metaflammation.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 225 men with T2DM (n = 75 per group) classified as non-obese, overweight, or obese. Insulin resistance markers (HOMA-IR, TyG-BMI) and inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8, CRP) were measured. Spearman's correlation and multivariable regression examined associations with omentin-1. PCA and PCR characterised the metaflammatory phenotype.

RESULTS: Omentin-1 declined progressively across BMI categories (median: 687.6, 587.6, and 459.3 ng/L; P < 0.001) and was inversely correlated with BMI (ρ =  - 0.717), TNF-α (ρ =  - 0.615), IL-8 (ρ =  - 0.589), IL-6 (ρ =  - 0.510), and HOMA-IR (ρ =  - 0.383) (all P < 0.001). BMI remained independently and inversely associated with omentin-1 after adjustment (standardised β =  - 0.671; P < 0.001). PCA identified a metaflammatory component (KMO = 0.852; variance explained = 59.53 %). PCR confirmed an inverse association between this component and omentin-1 (B =  - 46.35, 95 % CI - 53.69 to - 39.00; P < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.481).

CONCLUSIONS: Omentin-1 was inversely associated with adiposity, insulin resistance, and composite metaflammatory burden in men with T2DM, supporting its role as an integrative cardiometabolic biomarker.

articles.title: Long-term safety and efficacy of twice-yearly depemokimab in type 2 asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype: 2-year integrated analysis of the phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies and AGILE open-label extension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period.

METHODS: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103.

FINDINGS: Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE.

INTERPRETATION: Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile.

FUNDING: GSK.

articles.title: Glycosylation and Immunogenicity in Recombinant Proteins Acting on the FVIII/VWF-ADAMTS13 Axis.
articles.abstract: Recombinant protein therapeutics used in thrombosis and hemostasis exhibit diverse immunogenic and pharmacokinetic behaviors, much of which can be attributed to host cell-dependent glycosylation. Glycan structures influence clearance, receptor recognition, antigen processing, and immune tolerance in protein specific ways. Factor VIII (FVIII), which also functions as a regulator that promotes ADAMTS13‑mediated cleavage of von Willebrand factor (VWF), represents a paradigm in which differences in glycan processing among host cell lines contribute to inhibitor formation by modulating antigen uptake and presentation. In contrast, VWF demonstrates a distinct model in which terminal sialylation and antennary branching primarily regulate clearance rather than immunogenicity; CHO derived recombinant VWF, enriched in α2 3 sialylation, shows reduced ASGPR mediated hepatic uptake and prolonged half life. ADAMTS13 presents a third, clinically unique case. Its multidomain architecture and dependence on N glycans for folding and epitope shielding may render it structurally vulnerable, and the absence of α2 6 sialylation in CHO derived rADAMTS13 may impair CD22 mediated B cell tolerance, potentially predisposing patients with congenital thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura to alloantibody formation. Recent clinical observations underscore the need for long term immunogenicity monitoring. Collectively, these examples highlight glycosylation as a protein specific regulatory system that shapes both immunogenicity and pharmacokinetics. Future development of recombinant therapeutics targeting the VWF-ADAMTS13 axis will require optimized host cell selection, advanced glycoengineering, non immunogenic half life extension technologies, and integrated immunogenicity prediction models. Understanding and controlling glycosylation will be central to designing safer and more effective recombinant protein therapies in thrombosis and hemostasis.

articles.title: TREM-1 in Sepsis and Septic Shock: From Pathophysiology to Precision Immunomodulation.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and decades of immunomodulatory trials targeting inflammation have failed to improve outcomes, largely because of the biological heterogeneity of the host response. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (TREM-1) has emerged as a particularly relevant pathway in this context: rather than initiating pathogen recognition, TREM-1 amplifies signals generated by pattern-recognition receptors, acting as a rheostat that fine-tunes the magnitude of the innate immune response to promote antimicrobial defense while limiting inflammation-induced tissue injury. Both insufficient and excessive activation of this pathway have been associated with adverse outcomes in experimental and clinical studies. Soluble TREM-1 (sTREM-1), released proportionally to pathway activation, has been extensively investigated as a biomarker of infection and disease severity. Its diagnostic performance is moderate and best interpreted alongside clinical and microbiological data, but its prognostic value is more consistent, particularly when assessed serially or combined with complementary host-response markers. More recently, sTREM-1 has been explored as a theranostic biomarker to guide pathway-directed treatment. Nangibotide, the most clinically advanced TREM-1 inhibitor, has demonstrated feasibility and short-term safety across phase 1 and phase 2 trials, but has not yet met its primary efficacy endpoint in an unselected population; exploratory analyses suggest that treatment benefit may be concentrated among patients with the highest baseline sTREM-1 concentrations, a hypothesis that remains to be prospectively validated. This review summarizes the biology of the TREM-1 pathway, the clinical evidence supporting sTREM-1 as a diagnostic, prognostic, and theranostic biomarker, and the current state of TREM-1-targeted therapeutics. It also discusses what the clinical development of nangibotide illustrates about the hope and the difficulty of precision immunomodulation in sepsis.

articles.title: Clinical and immunological correlates of CXCR4 coreceptor use in people with HIV-1 receiving antiretroviral therapy in the Netherlands: a multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CXCR4-using (X4) viruses are associated with faster disease progression in untreated HIV-1 infection, although their clinical, virological, and immunological correlates during suppressive antiretroviral therapy are not well characterised. We aimed to assess the associations between X4 coreceptor use and clinical outcomes, HIV persistence, and immunological profiles in people with HIV-1 receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy.

METHODS: In this multicentre cohort study, asymptomatic adults with HIV receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy were enrolled from four HIV treatment centres in the Netherlands between Oct 16, 2019, and Oct 27, 2021 and followed up for 2 years. Clinical data were obtained from structured questionnaires and electronic health records. HIV-1 coreceptor use was predicted from triplicate env sequencing with Geno2pheno, and participants were classified as having CCR5-using (R5), X4, or mixed virus. HIV-1 subtype was assigned using env and pol sequences. Total and intact HIV DNA in CD4+ T cells were quantified using multiplex digital PCR. Plasma proteomics, bulk peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomics, and high-dimensional flow cytometry were used for systems-level profiling. Associations between predicted coreceptor use and clinical outcomes, HIV-reservoir measures, and immunological profiles were assessed using adjusted regression models and discovery and validation cohorts.

FINDINGS: Coreceptor use was assigned in 1724 participants; 1222 had R5 virus, 336 had X4 virus, and 166 had mixed classifications. Primary clinical analyses included 1494 participants, of whom 1172 were in the R5 group and 322 were in the X4 group. Compared with the R5 group, the X4 group had a lower CD4+ nadir, a higher prevalence of previous AIDS-defining events, poorer immunological recovery, and more comorbidities, particularly type 2 diabetes and non-affective psychiatric disorders. The median total HIV DNA was 1051 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells in the X4 group versus 599 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells in the R5 group, and the median intact HIV DNA was 23 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells versus 15 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells. No significant differences were observed in plasma inflammatory proteins. Participants in the X4 group had higher frequencies of activated CD4+ T cells and PD-1+ regulatory T cells, and transcriptomic analyses identified downregulation of two validated transcripts involved in transcriptional repression and lipid hydrolysis.

INTERPRETATION: Among people with HIV receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy, infection with X4 virus was associated with markers of more advanced previous HIV disease, impaired immune recovery, larger HIV reservoirs, and selected comorbidities despite viral suppression. Coreceptor use might therefore help to contextualise clinical, virological, and immunological heterogeneity in treated HIV-1 infection and could be relevant to future HIV cure studies.

FUNDING: ViiV Healthcare.

articles.title: Functional phlebectomy for saphenous reflux: A retrospective cohort of 759 patients with 3-year follow-up.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe optimal management of chronic venous disease with saphenous reflux remains debated. While truncal ablation is commonly recommended, haemodynamically oriented and saphenous-sparing strategies have emerged, possibly challenging the necessity of routine treatment of the saphenous vein in all patients.ObjectiveTo evaluate clinical and haemodynamic outcomes following functional phlebectomy in patients with symptomatic varicose veins and saphenous reflux, and to assess the need for subsequent truncal intervention.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted including 759 consecutive patients with CEAP C2 disease and duplex-confirmed saphenous reflux, treated between 2008 and 2019. All patients underwent functional phlebectomy targeting refluxing tributaries without routine saphenous ablation. Follow-up was performed up to 36 months with clinical assessment and duplex ultrasound. Outcomes were reported descriptively as absolute numbers and percentages as collected at 36 months. Secondary staged treatment with foam sclerotherapy was performed in patients with persistent symptomatic reflux.ResultsAfter functional phlebectomy, absence of reflux was observed in 24.9% of patients, while 49.5% presented persistence of reflux without symptoms and 24.9% persistence with symptoms. Saphenous vein thrombosis occurred in 0.6% of cases. Among patients undergoing secondary sclerotherapy (n = 189), absence of reflux was achieved in 10.05%, while 39.6% became asymptomatic despite persistent reflux. Overall, only a minority of patients required subsequent treatment of the saphenous vein. Saphenous vein diameter appeared to influence treatment outcomes, with preservation observed in all cases with diameters ≤6 mm and increasing need for truncal intervention in larger veins.ConclusionsFunctional phlebectomy, applied within a haemodynamically guided framework, is associated with favourable clinical outcomes in the majority of patients with saphenous reflux, without the need for routine truncal ablation. These findings support a selective, stepwise approach to treatment and contribute to the evolving paradigm of personalised management in chronic venous disease.

articles.title: Is greater engagement with a gamified app associated with greater improvements in safe driving behaviour? A naturalistic study from the i-DREAMS project.
articles.abstract: Smartphone-based feedback applications are increasingly used to promote safer driving, yet their effectiveness depends on sustained user engagement. This study examined the role of engagement with the i-DREAMS smartphone application in shaping safe driving behaviour during naturalistic field trials conducted over 18 weeks per participant in Belgium and the United Kingdom (UK) (N = 100). The application provided drivers with post-trip feedback on their driving performance, including safety scores and behavioural insights, and later incorporated gamification elements such as goals, badges, leaderboards, and push notifications to stimulate engagement. Analyses combined descriptive statistics of app engagement, cluster analysis to distinguish low- and high-engagement users, and generalised linear mixed-effects models to assess the effects of engagement, intervention stage, and socio-demographic factors on risky driving events per 100 km. Results showed that drivers primarily engaged with functionalities that provide direct performance feedback, particularly trip summaries and scores, and that engagement increased following the introduction of gamification features. Higher engagement was associated with greater reductions in risky driving events compared with lower engagement, particularly for road-sharing behaviours and total events. The strongest behavioural improvements were observed when in-vehicle warnings, post-trip feedback, and gamification elements were combined. Some cross-country differences emerged, with more consistent intervention effects in the UK than in Belgium. Age and education were also associated with driving outcomes, with older and more highly educated drivers showing fewer risky events in some models.

articles.title: The relationship between caregiver burden and psychological resilience among parents of children with transfusion-dependent thalassemia: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thalassemia requires lifelong transfusion and chelation therapy, imposing substantial caregiving demands on parents. Evidence linking caregiver burden, psychological resilience, and information source remains limited.

PURPOSE: To examine the association between caregiver burden and psychological resilience in parents of children with transfusion-dependent thalassemia, and the role of clinical and information-source variables.

DESIGN AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study (N=100) was conducted in a pediatric hematology unit in Türkiye. Parents completed the Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI) and Brief Resilience Scale (BRS). Analyses included t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, correlations, and hierarchical regression (n=95); effect sizes are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Reporting followed the EQUATOR-endorsed STROBE guideline.

RESULTS: Mean ZBI was 36.57±10.86 and mean BRS 15.16±3.99. Burden and psychological resilience were inversely associated (r=-0.236, CI [-0.413, -0.041], p=0.018). The largest group difference was daily-life restriction (d=0.90, CI [0.49, 1.32], p<0.001). Among 10 parents informed mainly by a nurse, resilience was higher (d=0.70, p=0.040) and burden lower (r=0.21, p=0.043); both estimates were imprecise. Covariates explained 31.7% of burden variance; adding resilience gave a small increment (ΔR2=0.034; B=-0.562, CI [-1.086, -0.038], p=0.036).

CONCLUSIONS: Psychological resilience was independently associated with caregiver burden, though the incremental variance was small. The nurse-information finding is exploratory, requiring replication.

PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Findings support evaluation of caregiver burden and resilience screening, and randomized trials of nurse-led family-centered education.

articles.title: Performance of the systemic lupus erythematosus disease activity score (SLE-DAS) in daily clinical practice: A prospective study of 125 patients in India.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAccurate measurement of disease activity is a cornerstone in the management of patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), to assist in guiding therapeutic decisions. SLE-DAS (SLE Disease Activity Score) is designed to improve accuracy and sensitivity to change compared with the standard SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) score.ObjectivesWe aimed to assess the performance of SLE-DAS to identify flare and clinically meaningful improvement (CMI) in real-life SLE patients in India.MethodsProspective observational study at an Indian Rheumatology Clinic included SLE patients meeting 2012 SLICC and/or 2019 ACR/EULAR criteria, followed for 9 months. At baseline and subsequent follow-up, we recorded SLEDAI-2K, SLE-DAS, PGA, LLDAS, DORIS remission, prednisolone dose, and immunosuppressives; SELENA-SLEDAI flare index (SFI) was evaluated at follow-up. We assessed Spearman correlation, agreement, and discrepancies between SLEDAI and SLE-DAS for flare and improvement detection using an agreement matrix.ResultsA strong correlation was observed between SLEDAI-2K and SLE-DAS (rho = 0.954, 95% CI 0.934-0.968, p < 0.001). SLE-DAS identified CMI in 42.0% of visits compared to 34.8% by SLEDAI-2K. Flare detection sensitivity was higher for SLE-DAS (96%) than SLEDAI-2K (84%), with similar specificity (98.9%). The agreement of SLEDAS remission and low disease activity (LDA) with DORIS remission and LLDAS, respectively, was perfect (κ = 1, p < 0.001). Discordant analysis revealed that SLEDAI-2K underestimated severe flares and missed manifestations such as pneumonitis, AIHA, and serositis.ConclusionSLE-DAS demonstrated superior sensitivity, granularity, and remission alignment compared to SLEDAI-2K, supporting its adoption as a primary clinical index in diverse real-world lupus practices.

articles.title: Survival Outcomes After Immune-Related Adverse Events in Older Adults With Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network : JNCCN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are common toxicities of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but their prognostic implications in older adults remain uncertain.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using SEER-Medicare (2010-2019). We included patients aged ≥66 years with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who initiated ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy from 2015-2017. Follow-up began at treatment initiation and continued until death, Medicare disenrollment, or December 31, 2019. The primary exposure was a clinically meaningful irAE, defined as an irAE diagnosis with evidence of systemic immunosuppressant use and/or treatment delay, or discontinuation. In secondary analyses, we categorized patients as having no irAE, an irAE managed without hospitalization, or an irAE requiring hospitalization. The primary outcome was overall survival. We estimated adjusted survival differences and restricted mean survival time using doubly robust causal inference methods.

RESULTS: The cohort included 5,304 patients (mean age, 75 years; 52.7% female; 81.9% White). Clinically meaningful irAEs occurred in 1,807 (34.1%) patients, with a median onset of 3.8 months (IQR, 1.1-9.4). Death occurred in 65.1% of patients with irAEs and 78.7% without irAEs, corresponding to an adjusted absolute survival benefit of 6.6% (95% CI, 5.3%-8.0%) and a 6.5-month gain in restricted mean survival time (95% CI, 5.6-7.4). In secondary analyses, irAEs managed without hospitalization showed the greatest benefit (odds ratio [OR], 0.44; 95% CI, 0.35-0.54), whereas irAE hospitalization was associated with attenuated benefit (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with advanced NSCLC receiving ICIs, clinically meaningful irAEs were associated with improved overall survival, particularly when managed without hospitalization. These findings highlight the clinical importance of early recognition of immune-related toxicities; irAE-related hospitalization may identify a higher-risk group warranting closer monitoring and supportive care.

articles.title: Managing patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer alongside complex comorbidities and frailty: A consensus statement and implications for the United Kingdom health system.
articles.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is predominantly diagnosed in older adults, many of whom present with multiple comorbidities and varying degrees of frailty. These factors complicate diagnostic investigations, treatment decisions, and outcomes. Limited real-world guidance exists on managing advanced NSCLC in patients with comorbidities and frailty. To address this knowledge gap, a multidisciplinary panel of 10 United Kingdom (UK) experts, including six lung oncologists, two clinical nurse specialists, and two pharmacists, participated in two virtual workshops to identify key challenges and best practices for managing patients with advanced NSCLC and complex comorbidities or frailty. Twenty-three draft consensus statements were developed based on discussion at the workshops, with a further two experts (one respiratory physician and one geriatrician) invited to draft and/or review the statements at that time. The consensus statements were distributed via Microsoft Forms for anonymous voting and commentary. A predefined threshold of ≥70% agreement was set to define consensus. Comments not meeting this threshold were revised following expert review to increase agreement. Consensus was achieved for 22 of 23 statements. This consensus statement provides recommendations on assessments and care planning, prehabilitation strategies and comorbidity optimization, and treatment selection and individualization. The multidisciplinary, practical guidance for managing patients with advanced NSCLC with comorbidities and frailty also identifies evidence gaps requiring further study. Implementation of these recommendations may improve equitable, patient-centered care within the UK National Health Service and could be applicable to other healthcare systems.

articles.title: [Perception, symptoms and management of menopause in Spanish women: results of an anonymous online survey].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the perceived impact of menopause on quality of life, symptom prevalence, and treatment use among Spanish women, based on the findings of an online survey conducted among women residing in Spain, promoted by the HM Foundation Chair in Menopause.

METHODS: An anonymous open online survey was conducted between January and June 2024. A total of 3,825 women aged 40-65 years participated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics based on self-reported responses, 95% confidence intervals (Wilson method), and two-sided proportion tests against a 50% reference value.

RESULTS: The mean age was 52.1±7.4 years, with an estimated BMI of 25.0kg/m2. Most participants were non-smokers (88.7%) and had an intact uterus (94.9%). The most frequent symptoms were sleep disturbances (84.1%), fatigue (80.5%), emotional changes (75.7%), cognitive difficulties (71.9%), and hot flashes (71.4%). A total of 79.8% reported a perceived negative impact on quality of life, and 70.1% reported moderate to severe productivity impairment. Only 12.0% were receiving menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), and 44.0% considered themselves well informed about menopause. The most commonly used medications were those for sleep or anxiety (21.6%) and cholesterol control (12.3%). Preventive screening rates were high (mammography 93.8%, Pap smear 91.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the high prevalence of symptoms and good participation in preventive programs, the use of MHT remains low, while the uptake of specific non-hormonal therapeutic options, such as fezolinetant, remains limited. These findings highlight an information gap and underscore the relevance of sleep and emotional well-being to the perceived impact of menopause.

articles.title: [Care gap in follow-up of COPD exacerbation patients discharged from the emergency department: Risk stratification and identification of a missed opportunity].
authors: en representación del grupo de trabajo Respiratorio SEME
Sen representación de Proyecto EPOC URG CyL
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the care gap between the risk of adverse outcomes (AO) identifiable at the time of emergency department (ED) discharge and the actual follow-up received within the subsequent 30 days by patients discharged following an acute exacerbation of COPD.

METHODS: A sub-analysis was conducted on the cohort of patients discharged home from the ED within the multicentre prospective PREURG-CyL registry. The 30-day risk of adverse outcomes (re-exacerbation, ED revisit, hospitalisation, or death) was stratified according to the improvement of dyspnoea during ED care and the complexity of maintenance therapy (≤double versus triple/multiple therapy). Post-discharge follow-up was documented via telephone calls and electronic medical record reviews.

RESULTS: Of 490 patients discharged, 115 (23.5%) experienced an adverse outcome within 30 days. Lack of improvement in dyspnoea (aOR: 11.27; 95% CI: 6.52-19.49) and triple/multiple therapy (aOR: 3.54; 95% CI: 1.92-6.53) were the only independent predictors (C-statistic: 0.834). Their combination identified a subgroup with a 57.7% rate of adverse outcomes, compared to 2.7% in those with clinical improvement and ≤double therapy. No patients were assessed in primary care within the first 72hours; however, 100% were seen within 15 days, with no differentiation based on risk level.

CONCLUSIONS: Risk stratification at discharge is feasible using two readily accessible variables. The absence of early follow-up for high-risk patients represents a missed opportunity that can be addressed through coordinated transition of care between the emergency department and primary care.

articles.title: Trends and disparities in mortality involving both COPD and dementia among older adults in the United States (1999-2023).
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and dementia share risk factors like systemic inflammation and hypoxia, and are the leading causes of morbidity in older adults. Despite the frequent co-occurrence of these conditions, their long-term contribution to mortality trends remained understudied. Our goal is to analyze temporal trends and disparities in mortality associated with both COPD and dementia in the U.S. older population.

METHODS: We analyzed death certificate data from the CDC WONDER database (1999-2023) for older adults ≥65 years listing COPD and dementia as underlying or contributing causes. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 population. Joinpoint regression was used to analyze trends and estimate Annual Percent Changes (APCs). Our analysis reflects deaths in which both conditions were listed on death certificates and does not represent clinically confirmed comorbidity.

RESULTS: Overall, 537,033 mortalities have been reported, with AAMR increasing by approximately 85% over the study period from 1999 (28.5) to 2023 (52.6) (AAPC 2.65; p < 0.000001). The majority of deaths occurred in females (57.2%), but males had a higher average AAMR (56.4 vs. 44.9). Further, non-Hispanic (NH) Whites represented the highest AAMR (53.1) among racial groups. Geographically, non-metropolitan areas (60.5) and the Southern region (53.6) experienced the highest burden.

CONCLUSION: Mortality involving concurrent COPD and dementia increased significantly from 1999 to 2023. The disproportionate burden on males, rural populations, and nursing home residents emphasizes the need for integrated respiratory-neurological care and targeted public health interventions.

articles.title: Associations of triglyceride-glucose index and derived indicators with prediabetes and diabetes among adolescents in the United States: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with potential utility for assessing metabolic risk. However, the associations between the TyG index and related indicators and prediabetes/diabetes in U.S. adolescents remain unknown.

METHODS: This study included 5206 adolescents (aged 12-18 years) from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 1999-2018). Prediabetes and diabetes were defined according to 2023 American Diabetes Association guidelines. Multivariable weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) models, subgroup analyses, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to examine the associations and discriminatory performance of the TyG index and its obesity-related composite indicators with prediabetes or diabetes. Model 1 was unadjusted, Model 2 was adjusted for age, sex, and race/ethnicity, and Model 3 additionally included PIR, BMI, HDL, HbA1c, and fasting insulin.

RESULTS: Both before and after adjustment for potential confounders, the TyG index (Model 3, odds ratio [OR] = 1.754 / 1.741) and its derived indicators TyG-ABSI (OR = 2.016 / 2), TyG-WWI (OR = 1.053 / 1.052), TyG-BMI (OR = 1.019 / 1.019), TyG-WC (OR = 1.006 / 1.006), and TyG-WHtR (OR = 2.59 / 2.566) were significantly and positively associated with prediabetes / prediabetes plus diabetes. These associations were generally consistent across subgroups and remained robust after excluding HbA1c and fasting insulin from the adjustment set and participants with FPG ≥7.0 mmol/L or HbA1c ≥6.5%. RCS analyses indicated that TyG, TyG-ABSI, and TyG-WWI were approximately linearly associated with prediabetes or diabetes, whereas TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, and TyG-WHtR showed nonlinear relationships. ROC analyses demonstrated comparable discriminatory performance across all indicators (≈ 0.77).

CONCLUSION: The TyG index and its derived indicators correlate positively with the prediabetes/diabetes in children. However, no superior diagnostic potential was observed for TyG obesity composite indicators compared to the standalone TyG index.

articles.title: Trends and disparity of chronic lower respiratory disease and hypertension: A CDC WONDER database analysis 1999-2023.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In the US, two leading causes of morbidity and mortality are hypertension and chronic lower respiratory disease (CLRD). We aim to analyze the trends of mortality in people with CLRD and hypertension as causes of death in the adult US population.

METHODS: Mortality data from 1999 to 2023 were obtained from the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database for U.S. adults aged ≥25 years. ICD-10 codes were used to identify hypertension (I10-I15) and CLRD (J40-J47. In order to determine age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 people. The analyses were stratified according to age groups, sex, race/ethnicity, urbanization status, and geographic region.

RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2023, 1433,319 deaths due to chronic lower respiratory disease and hypertension occurred among U.S. adults aged ≥25 years. Overall, the AAMR increased from 9.41 per 100,000 in 1999 to 35.53 in 2023 (AAPC: 5.20; 95% CI: 4.02 - 6.38; p < 0.000001). Mortality increased significantly from 1999 to 2021, followed by a nonsignificant decline through 2023 (APC:4.19; 95% CI:8.95 - 0.82; p = 0.093265). The mean AAMR was higher among males than females (28.72 vs. 21.55). By race/ethnicity, NH Blacks or African American individuals had the highest mean AAMR (29.72), followed by NH White (24.72), NH American Indian or Alaska Native (21.03), Hispanic or Latino (14.02), and NH Asian or Pacific Islander (10.75) individuals. Nonmetropolitan areas had higher AAMR than metropolitan areas (29.02 vs. 22.43). The South had the highest regional mean AAMR (27.67), followed by the Midwest (25.63), West (23.77), and Northeast (18.44). Mean crude mortality rates increased substantially with age, ranging from 1.01 per 100,000 among those aged 35-44 years to 265.35 among those aged ≥85 years.

CONCLUSION: CLRD and hypertension mortality increased substantially, with persistent demographic and geographic disparities, highlighting the need for targeted prevention strategies in high-risk populations.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of carotid artery stent designs through a strict randomized evidence synthesis and assessment of local vascular responses.
articles.abstract: Carotid artery stenting is an established endovascular option for carotid stenosis, but comparative clinical evidence for individual stent designs remains limited. Full-text reassessment confirmed five independent trials that randomized patients specifically to a stent device or stent-design strategy. Only two trials (204 patients; four standardized events) provided fully verified arm-level data for stroke, transient ischemic attack, or all-cause death within 30 days. The device evidence formed a sparse chain without a closed loop, and each direct comparison was informed by one trial. Bayesian network meta-analysis, treatment ranking, and node-splitting were therefore not performed. Direct estimates were imprecise and did not establish superiority of any stent or structural class. The animal findings describe exploratory local vascular responses to geometry-matched miniature nitinol stents under controlled experimental conditions and do not validate a clinical device hierarchy. The chronological relationship between the clinical evidence review and animal study design is acknowledged as a limitation.

articles.title: Integrating Individual-Level Syndromic Surveillance Data Into Infectious Disease Modeling for COVID-19 Forecasting in Sweden: Comparative Modeling Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic has triggered major global challenges, highlighting the need for timely surveillance and accurate forecasting to curb disease transmission and reduce the health burden. Traditional modeling approaches usually rely on aggregated data on confirmed cases. However, testing data can be unreliable due to low availability and uptake, as well as registration delays. In Sweden, the 1177 health care helpline provides valuable syndromic surveillance data that can capture early signals of infection prior to confirmation through testing.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effect of integrating syndromic surveillance data on short-term COVID-19 forecast accuracy.

METHODS: We developed a novel epidemiological model named SIsIcHRD (susceptible-infectedsuspected-infectedconfirmed -hospitalized-recovered-deceased), incorporating data from the 1177 health care helpline cross-linked with national registers on COVID-19 testing, hospitalizations, and deaths. In the novel model, the population with infection is divided into suspected infections (Is; those reporting symptoms to 1177) and confirmed infections (Ic; those who tested positive). Accuracy metrics of this model are compared to a model without data from the 1177 health care helpline. To evaluate model performance across different pandemic phases between March 2 and December 31, 2020, we used a daily rolling-window approach with a 60-day fitting period to predict confirmed infections, hospitalizations, and deaths over the subsequent 30 days. Prediction performance was evaluated using mean absolute error and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).

RESULTS: The proposed SIsIcHRD model successfully captured the temporal dynamics of confirmed, hospitalized, and death cases. The model achieved a median mean MAPE of 61.6% (IQR 37.6%-79.6%) for confirmed cases, 37.5% (IQR 18.9%-57.5%) for hospitalizations and for deaths, the model achieved a median MAPE of 0.65% (IQR 0.3%-1.9%), indicating substantially higher predictive accuracy for severe outcomes compared to confirmed infections and hospital admissions. Compared to the model without syndromic surveillance data, short-term forecasting performance of the SIsIcHRD model reduced MAPE by an average of 15.7 percentage points for confirmed cases, 8.17 percentage points for hospitalizations, and 1.99 percentage points for deaths. Overall, the results demonstrate predictive stability for severe outcomes during the early phase of the pandemic.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed model demonstrated predictive performance by integrating individual-level data with health care helpline syndromic data on testing and severe disease outcomes, capturing early signals from symptomatic individuals and distinguishing suspected cases from subsequently confirmed infections, leading to better forecasts of severe outcomes such as hospitalizations and deaths. This framework can support public health decision-making in future outbreaks.

articles.title: Data Stream and Hospital-Level Variation in Intensive Care Unit Vital-Sign Record Density Across Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV and eICU Collaborative Research Database: Retrospective Data Quality Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electronic health record-derived process measures such as vital-sign record density are used for quality monitoring, risk prediction, and cross-system benchmarking, but whether they retain consistent meaning across sites and data streams is rarely tested.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine whether vital-sign record density varies primarily by data stream, database, contributing site, or care unit, and what follows for comparative use.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) version 2.0. Record density and timing metrics were computed for the first 24 intensive care unit hours from nurse-charted streams and, in eICU-CRD, from the monitor stream. Heart rate was primary; oxygen saturation and respiratory rate were replication variables. Variance was decomposed by database, hospital, and unit using η2 with hospital-clustered bootstrap inference and mixed-effects sensitivity analyses. A hospital-level plausibility floor of 12 nurse-charted heart rate observations per 24 hours was applied for the principal analysis; unrestricted and alternative-floor analyses are reported as sensitivities.

RESULTS: A pooled-item MIMIC-IV heart rate count included alarm-limit documentation events, so label-based pooling mixes the two.
