In 117,572 eICU-CRD stays present in both streams, nurse- and monitor-derived counts were almost unrelated (Spearman ρ=0.024), with bottom-decile overlap at chance. Between-database η2 for record count was 0.960 against the eICU monitor stream and 0.026 against the nurse stream. Eight of 68 eICU-CRD hospitals fell below the plausibility floor and were excluded from principal estimates, a restriction introduced during review. Among the remaining 60 hospitals (88,560 stays), hospital η2 for record count was 0.354 (95% CI 0.259-0.450) against unit-within-hospital η2 of 0.043; for the interval-structure metrics, the hospital and unit components were not separable. For record count, the hospital component fell from 0.441 unrestricted to 0.321 at an hourly floor. A negative-binomial mixed model gave latent-scale hospital and unit variance-partition coefficients of 0.348 (95% CI 0.252-0.457) and 0.112 (0.078-0.163), equivalent to 0.318 and 0.110 observed. A pooled bottom-decile rule agreed with hospital-specific rules on 52.5% (4726/9006) of flagged stays, with 6 hospitals supplying half the pooled decile. The hospital component for record count replicated at 0.322 for oxygen saturation and 0.333 for respiratory rate.

CONCLUSIONS: Within a multisite nurse-charted stream, vital-sign record volume varied more across contributing sites than across care units within hospitals; for the interval-structure metrics, the site and unit components were not separable at this cohort size. Apparent cross-database differences were reproduced by source-table choice, and site-level variation remained after excluding the most evident contribution-completeness outliers. Comparative use therefore requires specifying the generating stream, enforcing the analytic window, and explicitly modeling site-level variation; the residual site component should not be interpreted as documentation practice alone.

articles.title: Direct Computed Tomographic Visualization of the Mixing Point During Peripheral Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

articles.title: Associations of Peak Cough Flow With Cough Acoustic Features and Respiratory Muscle Surface Electromyography in Poststroke Patients: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Poststroke ineffective cough impairs airway clearance, increasing respiratory complications. While peak cough flow (PCF) is commonly used to measure cough strength, patient limitations often hinder testing. This cross-sectional study explored the relationships between PCF, cough acoustic features, and respiratory muscle surface electromyography (sEMG) in 28 stroke patients, assessing acoustic metrics to identify diminished cough strength.

METHOD: Participants performed maximal voluntary coughs during simultaneous acoustic and sEMG recordings. Acoustic variables included maximum relative acoustic intensity, rise time, cough duration, relative mean intensity, relative peak energy, spectral centroid (Fc), and spectral bandwidth. Analyses used Spearman correlations with false discovery rate (FDR) correction, linear regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.

RESULTS: Among the acoustic variables, only Fc was significantly associated with PCF (r = -.371, p < .001), and this association remained significant after FDR correction (false discovery rate-adjusted p value = .006). ROC analysis showed that Fc had modest discriminative ability for identifying reduced cough strength (PCF < 270 L/min; area under the curve = 0.671, 95% confidence interval [0.556, 0.786], p = .010). Linear regression further showed that Fc was significantly associated with PCF (β = -.357, p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Fc captures an acoustic characteristic closely associated with poststroke cough airflow. Cough acoustic analysis offers valuable, complementary clinical information when conventional flow testing is challenging. Larger studies are needed to confirm the diagnostic utility of these measures.

articles.title: Ilicicolin Biosynthesis by Neonectria ditissima: A Putative Determinant of Virulence in Apple Diseases.
articles.abstract: Diseases caused by Neonectria ditissima result in major crop losses in apple production worldwide. Areas with mild and humid climates are particularly affected. In addition to canker on apple trees, infections by N. ditissima may also cause pre- and post-harvest fruit rots. The molecular basis of disease development is as yet unclear. Secondary metabolite profiles were analysed in naturally infected apple tissues exhibiting disease symptoms collected from orchards, in N. ditissima pure cultures at different developmental stages, and in co-cultivations with other microorganisms from the apple ecosystem. Universally, two classes of secondary metabolites, the meroterpenoid-type ilicicolins C, D, E, F and 4',5'-dihydro-4'-hydroxyascochlorin (DHAC) and the chemically unrelated pyridone ilicicolin H, were identified. The production of ilicicolin H, ilicicolin D and DHAC was reported for the first time in N. ditissima. Phytotoxic and antifungal activities were demonstrated for ilicicolin D and DHAC. Furthermore, gene clusters for ilicicolin biosynthesis in N. ditissima were identified by bioinformatic analyses. RNA sequencing revealed expression of the predicted biosynthetic genes under ilicicolin-producing conditions, which was confirmed by quantitative PCR for the core biosynthetic genes. Together, these findings support a potential role of ilicicolins in host infection and ecological interactions of N. ditissima and provide a basis for further functional studies of their contribution to apple disease development.

articles.title: Flavonoid-enriched extract from Forsythia suspensa leaf tea (FSLT-FE) attenuates cigarette smoke/lipopolysaccharide-induced COPD-like lung injury in mice: UPLC-MS profiling and network pharmacology analysis.
articles.abstract: Flavonoids from Forsythia suspensa leaves may benefit Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) through anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanisms, but the underlying pathways remain poorly defined. We profiled a flavonoid-enriched extract from F. suspensa leaf tea (FSLT-FE) by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS) and evaluated its efficacy in a cigarette smoke/LPS-induced COPD mouse model, complemented by network pharmacology. UPLC-MS identified 62 constituents, including rutin, quercetin, hesperidin, caffeic acid, forsythoside A, and phillygenin. FSLT-FE dose-dependently attenuated lung inflammation and structural damage, reduced IL-6, TNF-α, CXCL1/KC (the murine functional homologue of human IL-8), IL-1β, and malondialdehyde levels, and increased superoxide dismutase and catalase activities. Network pharmacology identified 23 active ingredients targeting 98 COPD-associated proteins, including AKT1, MAPK1, MMP2, and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), with enrichment in NF-κB, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and IL-17 signalling pathways. These results indicate that FSLT-FE acts on inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways through multiple components, supporting its potential as a protective agent against COPD-like lung injury.

articles.title: Nanoplastics as Hepatic Toxicant Vectors: Interactions with Environmental Chemicals, Organelle Dysfunction, and Regulated Cell Death.
articles.abstract: The environmental accumulation of nanoplastics (NPs) raises concerns regarding their potential effects on hepatic function. Experimental studies suggest that NP exposure can be related with altered mitochondrial electron transport chain activity, reduced ATP availability, changes in Keap1/Nrf2-mediated antioxidant responses, and impaired mitophagy. NPs have also been linked to cytoskeletal alterations, disrupted autophagic flux, and metabolic disturbances that can contribute to processes relevant to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This review critically evaluates regulated cell death pathways correlated with NP exposure, containing intrinsic apoptosis, RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL-mediated necroptosis, and NLRP3/cGAS-STING-associated pyroptosis. The available evidence implicates oxidative stress, mitochondrial and lysosomal dysfunction, altered autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, and regulated cell death in nanoplastic-associated hepatic effects. However, mechanistic evidence varies in strength, and observed responses depend on particle composition, surface characteristics, exposure conditions, and experimental models. Particular attention is given to distinguishing associative findings from experimentally supported causal mechanisms and to the limitations of extrapolating results from polystyrene nanoparticle models to other nanoplastics. By integrating evidence on mitochondrial quality control, microRNA-mediated metabolic regulation, and modulated cell death, this review identifies main knowledge gaps relevant to future mechanistic studies and toxicological risk assessment.

articles.title: Whole-Exome Sequencing Identifies a Rare CSRP3 Variant Associated With Familial Brugada Syndrome in a Lebanese Family.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmia associated with an increased risk of sudden cardiac death. Although traditionally regarded as a primary cardiac channelopathy, pathogenic variants in SCN5A account for only 20%-30% of clinically diagnosed cases, leaving most patients genetically unresolved. Emerging evidence suggests that structural cardiac genes may also contribute to BrS susceptibility. We investigated the genetic basis of BrS in a consanguineous Lebanese family with three affected brothers.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Whole-exome sequencing was performed in all affected individuals, followed by variant calling, annotation, and phenotype-driven prioritization using Franklin (Genoox). Candidate variants were evaluated according to allele frequency, inheritance model, segregation, and ACMG/AMP classification. Evolutionary conservation, AlphaMissense prediction, protein domain annotation, and structural modeling were performed to assess the potential functional impact of the prioritized variant. Whole-exome sequencing identified a rare homozygous CSRP3 missense variant (NM_003476.5:c.56 A > G; p.His19Arg) shared by all three affected siblings. Following exome-wide filtering under a recessive inheritance model, CSRP3 represented the only rare homozygous coding variant, while no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in established Brugada syndrome-associated genes. The variant was absent from public population databases and an internal cohort of Lebanese exomes. His19 was highly conserved across vertebrate species, AlphaMissense classified the variant as likely pathogenic (score = 0.942), and structural modeling predicted alterations within the N-terminal LIM domain that may affect protein stability and local residue interactions.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings nominate CSRP3 as a candidate susceptibility gene for Brugada syndrome and support the emerging role of structural cardiac genes in inherited arrhythmia syndromes. Although functional validation is required to establish causality, this study highlights the value of whole-exome sequencing in consanguineous and underrepresented populations for identifying rare candidate variants contributing to BrS susceptibility.

articles.title: Transient Lung-Volume Reduction Improves First-Shock Cardioversion Success by Reducing Transthoracic Impedance in Patients With Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthoracic impedance (TTI) is an important determinant of the efficacy of direct-current cardioversion (DCCV), as increased impedance may reduce myocardial current delivery. Because lung volume influences thoracic electrical properties, transient lung-volume reduction (TLVR) may represent a simple strategy for acutely lowering TTI and improving cardioversion efficacy. This study evaluated the effect of a standardized TLVR maneuver on TTI and first-shock cardioversion success in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF).

METHODS: This prospective, randomized study included 116 patients with persistent AF scheduled for first-time radiofrequency ablation. Patients were randomized 1:1 to conventional mechanical ventilation (standard CV group, n = 58) or a standardized TLVR maneuver immediately before cardioversion (TLVR CV group, n = 58). Baseline TTI was measured before the intervention, and post-TLVR TTI was additionally measured in the TLVR group. All patients underwent anterior-posterior cardioversion with an initial 200 J shock. First-shock success was defined as maintenance of sinus rhythm for at least 1 min. Multivariable linear and hierarchical logistic regression analyses were performed to investigate determinants of impedance reduction and first-shock success.

RESULTS: First-shock cardioversion success was significantly higher in the TLVR CV group than in the standard CV group (53.4% vs. 29.3%, p = 0.008), whereas cumulative success after up to three shocks was similar (96.6% vs. 91.4%, p = 0.242). The impedance reduction rate was significantly higher among patients with successful first-shock cardioversion (9.09% vs. 5.00%, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, TLVR independently increased the impedance reduction rate by 1.75 percentage points (B = 1.751, p = 0.001), while a higher Body Roundness Index was associated with a lower reduction (β = -0.468, p < 0.001). In the mechanistic logistic regression model, each 1% increase in impedance reduction was associated with a 2.23-fold higher likelihood of first-shock success (OR = 2.226, p < 0.001). Model explanatory power increased from 56.3% to 74.9% after the incorporation of impedance reduction.

CONCLUSION: A standardized TLVR maneuver immediately before cardioversion was associated with greater TTI reduction and an approximately twofold increase in first-shock cardioversion success in patients with persistent AF. The impedance reduction rate emerged as a strong independent predictor of successful initial cardioversion, supporting a potential physiological mechanism linking acute lung-volume reduction to improved electrical cardioversion efficacy.

articles.title: Validation of a Four-Extrastimulus Ventricular Stimulation Protocol for Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Risk stratification for sustained ventricular arrhythmias (SVA) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) remains challenging. Although programmed ventricular stimulation (PVS) has shown a high negative predictive value, the prognostic performance of a four-extrastimulus PVS protocol-validated in ischemic heart disease-has not been systematically evaluated in congenital heart disease.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively included 41 consecutive adults with repaired TOF who underwent EPS using a standardized four-extrastimulus PVS protocol at two right ventricular sites. Inducibility of SVA was assessed. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of clinical SVA during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Firth-penalized Cox regression were used to evaluate prognostic performance, and diagnostic accuracy metrics were calculated. Inducibility was observed in 18 patients (44%). During a median follow-up of 1.68 years, SVA occurred exclusively in inducible patients (5/18; 28%), all corresponding to sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. No non-inducible patient developed SVA. Inducibility was associated with significantly lower SVA-free survival (log-rank p = 0.015) and an increased risk of events (HR 13.6; 95% CI 1.5-1804; p = 0.017) in univariate analysis. The four-extrastimulus protocol demonstrated a sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 64%.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with repaired TOF and risk factors for sudden cardiac death, the four-extrastimulus PVS protocol identified a subgroup at high arrhythmic risk while reliably excluding events in non-inducible individuals. These findings support the potential value of PVS as part of multimodal risk stratification, particularly for identifying patients in whom ICD implantation may be deferred.

articles.title: Association Between Cumulative Social Determinants of Health and Mortality Among Stroke Survivors.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Social determinants of health (SDoH) are well-established contributors to health disparities. Whether cumulative SDoH burden is associated with long-term mortality among stroke survivors remains poorly understood.

METHODS: We extracted data of 1,404 stroke survivors from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018. Cumulative SDoH burden was calculated incorporating eight individual SDoH indicators across multiple domains: employment status, poverty-income ratio (PIR), food security, education level, healthcare access, health insurance, housing status, and marital status. Survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations of individual SDoH indicators and cumulative SDoH burden with all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD) and non-CVD mortality outcomes.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 72 months, 604 deaths were documented, including 237 CVD deaths and 367 non-CVD deaths. Among the eight SDoH indicators, being unemployed, having lower PIR and having government insurance only or being uninsured were significantly associated with all-cause mortality. Looking at cause-specific mortality, having lower PIR was significantly associated with CVD mortality, whereas being unemployed was significantly associated with non-CVD mortality. The risk of mortality from all-cause (p for trend <0.001), CVD (p for trend =0.026) and non-CVD (p for trend <0.001) increased with the increasing SDoH burden.

CONCLUSION: In this nationally representative cohort of stroke survivors, increasing cumulative SDoH burden was significantly associated with higher risks of mortality.

articles.title: A Canadian population-based observational cohort study of alpha and beta-thalassemia syndromes in pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Beta-thalassemia can adversely affect pregnancy, but the impact of alpha-thalassemia is less studied. We assessed whether patients with symptomatic alpha-thalassemia have similar pregnancy outcomes as patients with symptomatic beta-thalassemia.

METHODS: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of 1,324,488 pregnancies in Quebec, Canada, between 2006 and 2022. The exposures were maternal symptomatic alpha-thalassemia, symptomatic beta-thalassemia, thalassemia trait, and other thalassemia syndromes. Primary outcomes were severe maternal morbidity, preterm birth, preeclampsia, and other pregnancy complications. We used log-binomial regression models to estimate adjusted risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the association between each thalassemia and adverse pregnancy outcomes.

RESULTS: In total, 825 patients had symptomatic alpha-thalassemia, 681 symptomatic beta-thalassemia, 1,749 thalassemia trait, and 2,377 other thalassemia syndromes. Compared with no thalassemia, alpha-thalassemia (RR 3.05; 95% CI: 2.36-3.94) and beta-thalassemia (RR 2.52; 95% CI: 1.84-3.45) were associated with a greater risk of severe maternal morbidity. However, alpha-thalassemia was additionally associated with preterm birth (RR 1.45; 95% CI: 1.16-1.82), preeclampsia (RR 1.67; 95% CI: 1.27-2.20), and gestational diabetes (RR 1.79; 95% CI: 1.52-2.09). Beta-thalassemia was not associated with these outcomes, and associations were weak for thalassemia trait and other thalassemias.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that symptomatic alpha-thalassemia is associated with a wider range of pregnancy complications than symptomatic beta-thalassemia and other thalassemia syndromes. However, symptomatic alpha and beta-thalassemia are both associated with severe maternal morbidity.

articles.title: Viral disease outcomes are indistinguishable between experimentally infected bats and rodents.
articles.abstract: A common explanation for bats being a conspicuous source of zoonotic viruses is their purported ability to coexist with viruses without suffering overt disease. Widespread acceptance of the idea that bats have unusual antiviral traits has catalyzed the discovery of unique features of bat immune systems which may have translational value as broad-spectrum antivirals, particularly if they evolved as a byproduct of bats' unique life history rather than through conventional co-evolutionary processes. Surprisingly, whether bats compared to other host groups suffer less disease from co-evolved viruses or from viruses generally has not been formally assessed. Here, synthesizing 86 years of experimental infections, involving 54 viruses, 85 host species, and over 5,600 animals, we document disease in bats following inoculation by taxonomically diverse viruses, including ones that are relatively benign in humans. The occurrence of overt disease, the likelihood of mortality, and the severity of disease in bats were indistinguishable from those experienced by rodents, another group associated with many zoonotic viruses. These patterns were consistent when considering only bat-associated viruses inoculated into bats and rodent-associated viruses inoculated into rodents and among inoculations which lacked shared co-evolutionary history. Instead, disease outcomes following infection were shaped by experimental design, viral host range, and evolutionary context. Unexceptional disease in bats from novel or co-evolved infections suggests that order-level host life history traits such as flight have inconsistent consequences for antiviral immunity and highlights the need to evaluate the functional properties of putatively unique features of bat immunity in vivo. While these results do not exclude the possibility of developing broader-acting or more potent antivirals from bat immune systems or diminish the potential value of mechanistic insights into bat immunity, they suggest that bat immune systems were shaped by conventional co-evolutionary processes rather than through unique circumstances that endow exceptional antiviral defenses.

articles.title: Phagocytosis of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid- and RNA-containing immune complexes drives inflammatory cytokine production and endothelial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: The aberrant inflammation that characterizes severe COVID-19 is incompletely understood. Given the persistence of SARS-Cov-2 RNA and nucleocapsid protein (N) and the presence of anti-N antibody during the course of severe infection, we investigated the role of RNA-containing immune complexes (ICs) in driving inflammation. We found that ICs consisting of SARS-CoV-2 RNA, N, and anti-N IgG1 are internalized by primary human monocytes and stimulate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in a manner dependent on Fcγ receptors and partially dependent on toll-like receptor-8. In addition, the inflammatory response induced in monocytes by RNA-containing ICs caused endothelial dysfunction in vascularized micro-organs. Using nasopharyngeal samples from SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N were captured by anti-N monoclonal antibody in the absence of lysing reagents, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N complexes are present outside of virions and cells. Finally, we found that during an early wave of COVID-19, higher anti-N IgG:IgM ratios were associated with more severe clinical outcomes, consistent with a role for inflammatory, IgG-mediated phagocytic clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis, perhaps mitigated by non-inflammatory, IgM-mediated clearance. We conclude that RNA-containing ICs may play a role in the pathogenesis of severe COVID-19. Since all pathogenic viruses encode nucleic acid-binding proteins, such as N, and these proteins often elicit an antibody response, inflammatory clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs may also contribute to disease severity in other viral infections.

articles.title: Inferring the multi-host fitness landscape of endive necrotic mosaic virus from cross-inoculation experiments.
articles.abstract: Fitness landscapes offer a compact representation of adaptation, yet are rarely inferred from sparse multi-environment data. We present a Bayesian approach to infer an effective multi-host phenotypic fitness landscape from cross-inoculation assays by linking successful infection probabilities to Fisher's geometrical model and to an explicit decomposition of establishment routes. The model estimates (i) the distance matrix among host-specific phenotypic optima, (ii) target-host permissiveness through the widths of fitness peaks, (iii) target-specific differences in the efficiency with which phenotypic suitability translates into successful infection, and (iv) the conditional probabilities that successful infections are attributed to direct establishment, rescue from standing variation in the source inoculum, or de novo rescue in the target host. We apply the approach to an experimental evolution dataset for endive necrotic mosaic virus evolved on five Asteraceae hosts and challenged in a full cross-inoculation design. The inferred landscape can be visualized as a phenotypic map of the host community, revealing pronounced heterogeneity in target-host permissiveness and a geometry broadly concordant with host phylogeny. By grounding assay-derived distances in an explicit mechanistic model, the approach provides a parsimonious representation of multi-host constraints that can be used to discuss establishment barriers and potential springboard hosts in heterogeneous communities. More broadly, it offers a general method for inferring effective fitness landscapes from sparse multi-environment data.

articles.title: Data governance framework for the implementation of automated healthcare-associated infection surveillance using large language models: Privacy-by-design with open-source de-identification pipeline.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infection (HAI) surveillance remains heavily dependent on manual review of electronic medical records (EMRs), limiting scalability, reproducibility, and between-hospital comparability. Large language models (LLMs) may support extraction of clinically relevant information from unstructured text, but implementation is constrained by data protection, governance, and workflow integration challenges. Within an ECDC-funded feasibility project on healthcare-associated bloodstream infection (HA-BSI) surveillance in Italian hospitals, we developed an implementation framework to address these barriers.

METHODS: The framework combines a Data Protection Impact Assessment used as a design instrument, categorization of data into raw, derived, and aggregated tiers, an on-site assisted de-identification workflow, and a tiered LLM deployment model. LLMs are used for structured clinical information extraction only, while final case classification is performed through a transparent, deterministic, rule-based algorithm based on ECDC definitions.

RESULTS: The project produced an operational workflow in which identifiable clinical records remain under hospital control and only locally reviewed de-identified outputs are transferred for downstream research processing. It also led to development of an open-source human-in-the-loop redaction prototype. Key implementation barriers included variable EMR maturity, document export constraints, and lengthy ethics, institutional, and data protection approval cycles. Final LLM benchmarking and surveillance-performance evaluation remain ongoing.

CONCLUSIONS: Trustworthy LLM-assisted surveillance may depend on governance and implementation architecture as much as on model capability. The proposed framework provides a feasibility model requiring further validation across hospitals, languages, record systems, and LLM versions.This study describes a privacy-by-design workflow for using large language models to extract clinical information from Italian hospital records while preserving local data control, enabling deterministic ECDC case-definition matching for healthcare-associated bloodstream infection surveillance through on-site de-identification and human oversight.

articles.title: Resolution of the circulating pathogenic phenotype of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency following liver transplantation.
articles.abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) is a protease inhibitor, normally found at a high concentration in monomeric form in the circulation from where it protects the lung tissue from proteolytic damage. Pathogenic variants of AAT self-assemble into flexible polymer chains that undergo toxic accumulation in the liver, underlying the development of liver disease; the corresponding deficiency in the circulation results in susceptibility to emphysema. AAT polymers formed by these variants are also detectable in the plasma; this study evaluated the dynamics of circulating monomeric and polymeric AAT after correction of the deficiency state with liver transplantation in four individuals homozygous for the Z deficiency allele (Glu342Lys). The resolution of the pathological circulating AAT phenotype was characterised by analysis of blood samples taken pre- and post-liver transplant using a panel of conformer-specific monoclonal antibodies and a novel ELISA with enhanced sensitivity for AAT polymers. Circulating wild-type M AAT, produced by the allograft liver, increased with a half-timeof 7-39 h, attaining a putative 'protective' threshold level 4-55 h post-transplant. Pre-transplant circulating polymer levels ranged from 5-26 μg/mL and declined post-surgery with a half-time of 2-9 h, levels were comparable to those of wild-type M AAT plasma when repeated >200 days post-transplant. The glycosylation profile of liver- and plasma-derived polymers and their progressive disappearance from circulation is consistent with their origin in, and canonical secretion from, the liver. To our knowledge this is the first post-transplant evaluation of the hybrid conformational profile of endogenous and donor tissue-derived AAT.

articles.title: Tracheoscopic Management of Postoperative High Tracheoesophageal Fistula Using Covered Self-Expanding Metallic Stents: A Comparative Report of 2 Cases With Divergent Outcomes.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF) following esophageal cancer resection is a rare but life-threatening complication. Management of high postoperative TEF, particularly in the subglottic region, presents significant technical challenges due to anatomical constraints and the risk of stent migration. This report evaluates the efficacy of tracheoscopic placement of covered self-expanding metallic stents (CSEMS) for treating high postoperative TEF. CASE REPORT We report 2 cases of high TEF complicating esophageal cancer surgery. Case 1: A 67-year-old man with a 0.6 cm diameter fistula located 4 cm distal to the vocal folds. A straight CSEMS was successfully deployed. Four months later, after confirmation of complete mucosal healing and epithelialization, the stent was removed following the observation of granulation tissue hyperplasia. Case 2: A 78-year-old man with diabetes presented with a large (12×8 mm) fistula situated 3 cm distal to the vocal folds. An initial straight CSEMS failed due to repeated displacement. It was replaced with a customized ball-ended CSEMS and supplemented with biogel and -gelatin sponges. Due to refractory displacement and impaired healing, external percutaneous fixation was ultimately used to stabilize the stent. CONCLUSIONS Tracheoscopic CSEMS placement represents a viable management strategy for high postoperative TEF. However, successful outcomes in the challenging subglottic region are highly dependent on individualized stent selection and adjunctive measures, as illustrated by the contrasting courses of our 2 cases. These experiences underscore the importance of technical adaptability, while larger studies are needed to define optimal management algorithms.

articles.title: Discharge Mobility After Osteoporotic Thoracolumbar Fractures Using a 2-Stage Machine Learning Prediction Model: Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discharge mobility after osteoporotic vertebral fractures is heterogeneous and difficult to predict at admission. Machine learning offers structured approaches for multiclass functional outcome prediction, but existing models predominantly address binary end points and report global performance metrics without explicit analysis of the error structure.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a 2-stage machine learning framework with a predefined decision policy designed to reduce extreme (LOW-HIGH) misclassification for graded discharge mobility prediction in hospitalized patients with osteoporotic thoracolumbar fractures.

METHODS: This prospective, single-center cohort study enrolled consecutive patients aged 65 years or older admitted for acute osteoporotic thoracic or lumbar fractures (N=158). Discharge mobility was categorized as LOW (<50 m or nonambulatory), MID (50-500 m), or HIGH (>500 m or stair climbing). Clinical associations were analyzed using proportional odds ordinal regression. A predefined 2-stage architecture combined gradient-boosted trees (stage A: HIGH vs non-HIGH) and a random forest classifier (stage L: LOW vs non-LOW). The final 3-class prediction was assigned by a predefined decision policy designed to reduce clinically relevant extreme (LOW-HIGH) misclassification. All preprocessing steps, including fold-wise multiple imputation, were performed within training partitions only. The decision policy was additionally reevaluated in a nested cross-validation with fold-internal threshold selection across 10 repeated partitions.

RESULTS: Prefracture HIGH mobility was the only significant independent predictor of discharge mobility (odds ratio [OR] 3.38, 95% CI 1.68-6.80; P<.001); age, comorbidity burden, fracture grade, and treatment were not. In the prespecified analysis with fixed thresholds, performance was moderate (accuracy 0.494; balanced accuracy 0.450; macro-F1 0.444). Binary discrimination yielded an area under the curve of 0.693 (HIGH vs non-HIGH) and 0.625 (LOW vs non-LOW). Using the predefined decision policy, major LOW-HIGH errors were less frequent than with the prefracture mobility-only baseline (5 vs 22), and no HIGH-to-LOW misclassification occurred in the prespecified analysis. In the leakage-free nested cross-validation, macro-F1 was 0.388 (SD 0.031) and major errors had a mean of 8.3 (SD 3.4) vs 22.5 (SD 1.1) for the baseline, with fewer major errors in all 10 partitions. HIGH-to-LOW errors had a mean of 2.6 (SD 2.2) in this analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Discharge mobility after osteoporotic thoracolumbar fractures is primarily determined by prefracture functional reserve rather than fracture severity or comorbidity. A 2-stage machine learning framework achieved moderate multiclass discrimination and reduced extreme LOW-HIGH misclassification relative to a mobility-only baseline; this reduction persisted under nested cross-validation, whereas the absence of HIGH-to-LOW errors was specific to the prespecified partition. External validation is required before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

articles.title: Fibroblast-immune crosstalk in central nervous system injury and repair: Spatiotemporal control of barrier restoration, inflammation resolution and fibrotic scarring.
articles.abstract: Central nervous system repair after injury is increasingly understood as a spatially and temporally organized process involving vascular disruption, immune-cell recruitment, extracellular matrix remodeling and reconstruction of glial-stromal borders. Within this process, central nervous system fibroblasts are not merely matrix-producing scar cells, but injury-responsive stromal organizers positioned at key neuroimmune interfaces, including the meninges, perivascular spaces and choroid plexus. Recent single-cell, spatial and lineage-resolved studies indicate that anatomically distinct fibroblast populations undergo phase-specific state transitions after traumatic brain injury, stroke, and spinal cord injury. During the acute phase, activated fibroblasts and myofibroblast-like states contribute to lesion containment, barrier restoration and protection of surrounding parenchyma. In the subacute and chronic phases, fibroblasts interact dynamically with neutrophils, microglia, macrophages, lymphocytes and innate lymphoid cells to shape immune-cell positioning, inflammatory resolution, vascular repair and, when unresolved, persistent fibrotic scarring. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on fibroblast-immune crosstalk in central nervous system injury, with particular emphasis on the unresolved origins of injury-responsive stromal cells, lesion-topology-dependent fibroblast recruitment, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12-mediated lymphocyte organization, choroid plexus fibroblast-group 2 innate lymphoid cell niches, and fibroblast contributions to blood-brain barrier and vascular repair. Rather than framing fibrotic scars as uniformly detrimental, we propose that central nervous system fibrosis reflects context-dependent fibroblast states that can be either reparative or maladaptive depending on timing, anatomical niche and immune milieu. Therapeutic strategies should therefore avoid indiscriminate fibroblast depletion and instead aim to preserve early protective functions while selectively modulating chronic fibroblast-immune circuits that sustain inflammation and inhibit regeneration.

articles.title: Engineering smart liposomes to combat antimicrobial resistance: from mechanistic design to clinical translation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a critical global health threat, surpassing the pace of discovery and clinical development of new antimicrobial agents. Therefore, innovative therapeutic strategies are urgently needed to enhance antibiotic efficacy, overcome multidrug-resistant infections, and limit resistance development. Smart liposomal nanoplatforms have emerged as promising tools capable of improving antimicrobial therapy through targeted delivery, enhanced bacterial uptake, biofilm penetration, protection against enzymatic degradation, and controlled drug release.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines recent advances in the rational design of evolved liposomes, including stimuli-responsive and programmable systems, for combating resistant bacterial infections. It discusses their ability to improve pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles, overcome biological barriers, and enable precision antimicrobial delivery. Current translational challenges, including large-scale manufacturing, physicochemical characterization, regulatory requirements, and clinically relevant preclinical models, are critically evaluated. Emerging strategies, such as artificial intelligence-driven formulation optimization, continuous microfluidic manufacturing, multifunctional therapeutic platforms incorporating gene editing, and next-generation antibiotic-adjuvant combination strategies, are also explored.

EXPERT OPINION: Liposomal drug-delivery systems may improve the exposure, distribution, and intracellular or local delivery of antimicrobial agents, but improved delivery should not be equated with reversal of bacterial resistance. Successful clinical translation will depend on formulation- and infection-specific evidence, clinically relevant preclinical models, controlled and scalable manufacturing, and appropriate regulatory frameworks, while artificial intelligence, digital-twin, and precision-medicine approaches are best viewed as decision-support tools that complement experimental and clinical validation.

articles.title: Menu Evaluation Tools in Food Services: An Integrative Review.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The growing demand for meals outside the home has boosted the food service sector, but there are constant concerns regarding the nutritional quality of the meals offered. In this scenario, menus play a strategic role in promoting health and in defining population dietary patterns.

OBJECTIVE: This integrative review aimed to identify the instruments used to evaluate menus in food service settings across different contexts and target audiences.

DATA SOURCES: This is an integrative review with a systematic search in the LILACS, Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science databases, with controlled and uncontrolled descriptors. Original studies published between 2003 and 2025 that described the development of menu evaluation instruments aimed at healthy food service were included.

DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted on the characteristics of the instruments, including target population, food service setting, scope, evaluation approach, assessment perspectives, number of items, country of development, and validation status.

DATA ANALYSIS: Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, including absolute and relative frequencies. A total of 29 studies were included, with a predominance of instruments aimed at children's menus (55.2%) and with a qualitative approach (72.4%). Brazil had the largest number of developed instruments, followed by Spain, the United States, and Portugal. Only 58.6% of the instruments presented some type of validation. The instruments varied in scope (menu or menu + context), evaluation method (qualitative, quantitative, or qualitative-quantitative), and the number of perspectives covered, with 10.3% multidimensional (ie, having 4 or more dimensions).

CONCLUSION: The review showed advances in evaluating menus for the child population and in incorporating sustainability as an analytical parameter. However, gaps remain in validation and the development of multidimensional instruments, underscoring the need for validated and adapted tools to promote healthier, more sustainable menus.

articles.title: Olvanil Reduces Subcutaneous Fat Accumulation and Lipogenic Gene Expression, Without Alleviating Hepatic Oxidative Stress or Histopathological Alterations in Mice with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by excess intrahepatic lipid accumulation due to lipid overflow and synthesis, as well as impaired lipid oxidation. Olvanil (OLV) is a nonpungent capsaicin analog that has previously been shown to have anti-obesity effects in diet-induced obesity models. Nevertheless, its effects on fatty liver remain unclear. In this study, we evaluated the potential of OLV to address lipid metabolic dysfunction and MASLD-related hepatic abnormalities. C57BL/6 mice were fed a high-fat/high-fructose diet for 24 weeks, with or without OLV (25 mg/kg/day) administered by oral gavage for the last 8 weeks. We primarily evaluated the effects of OLV on liver function markers and the hepatic expression of key genes involved in lipid metabolism to assess its potential in reducing MASLD progression. We confirmed that OLV promoted lipolysis in adipocytes and significantly reduced body weight gain and fat accumulation, particularly in subcutaneous adipose tissue. At the molecular level, we demonstrated that OLV reduced the expression of lipogenic genes (ACC, FASN, SREBP-1c, and PPAR-γ). However, we observed elevated serum alanine aminotransferase levels and increased interleukin-6 and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances levels in liver tissue. Moreover, histopathological alterations such as hepatic steatosis and lobular inflammation tended to be more pronounced in OLV-treated animals than in untreated MASLD animals. In conclusion, while OLV reduced subcutaneous adiposity and liver lipogenic gene expression, it did not improve hepatic oxidative stress or histopathological alterations in a murine MASLD model. Free fatty acid-mediated lipotoxicity may be present, exacerbating hepatic oxidative stress and inflammatory changes; therefore, further studies are needed to confirm the proposed metabolic pathway.

articles.title: Natural Occurrence and Molecular Diversity of Wolbachia Endosymbiont DNA in Wild Mosquito Populations of Central India.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Utilizing Wolbachia for mosquito biocontrol requires baseline understanding of natural infection dynamics, lineage diversity, and host-symbiont phylogenetic concordance across native vector populations.

METHODS: We collected 2,167 adult mosquitoes (Anopheles, Culex, Aedes, and Mansonia) across five districts in central India (Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh). Specimens were screened in 263 genus-level pools via wsp PCR. Positive pools were brought to individuals level, typed across three different loci (ftsZ, gltA, and GroEL) of Wolbachia spp., and validated by mosquito barcoding (cox1, ITS2). Maximum likelihood phylogenies were constructed for all six loci both for Wolbachia (four) and mosquitoes (two).

RESULTS: Overall, 27 pools (10.26%) and 49 individuals (21.21%) were wsp-positive that includes 17 Anopheles, 18 Culex, 9 Aedes, and 5 Mansonia. Culicines exhibited robust multilocus amplification, whereas all 17 Anopheles failed to amplify at ftsZ, gltA, and GroEL. Phylogenetic trees of the mosquito-host cox1 and ITS2 resolved all four genera and five wsp-positive Anopheles species into monophyletic clades with 84-100% bootstrap support. In Wolbachia phylogenies, culicine isolates clustered in Supergroup B (wPip), with ftsZ and gltA trees resolving Mansonia symbionts into a well-supported, distinct lineage (95-97% bootstrap). Crucially, the wsp tree revealed that four An. annularis sequences formed a monophyletic clade (89-98% bootstrap), clustering with the bat-fly endosymbiont Penicillidia jenynsii rather than mosquito-adapted strains. Primary malaria vectors (An. culicifacies and An. fluviatilis) tested negative for Wolbachia.

CONCLUSIONS: Phylogenetic divergence and housekeeping gene dropout indicate that wsp detection in wild Anopheles represents transient or horizontal acquisition rather than stable intracellular endosymbiosis. Multilocus phylogenetic validation is critical prior to deploying symbiont-based biocontrol.

articles.title: Repurposing Etravirine as a PlcA-Targeting inhibitor to block autophagic escape of Listeria monocytogenes.
articles.abstract: The rapid rise of antibiotic resistance underscores the urgent need for anti-infective strategies that circumvent classical bactericidal approaches. Host-directed antivirulence therapies, which target host defense pathways or pathogen virulence rather than essential viability, may reduce selection pressure and delay resistance, but potent small-molecule examples remain limited. Here we identified a drug repurposing candidate against the intracellular pathogen Listeria monocytogenes (L. monocytogenes) by targeting its phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C PlcA, a key virulence factor involved in autophagy escape. Using a compound-microarray high-throughput binding platform, we discovered that the approved HIV non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor Etravirine directly bound PlcA and inhibited its phosphatidylinositol-hydrolyzing activity without affecting bacterial growth or plcA transcription. In infected cells, Etravirine restored PtdIns3P levels, increased MAP1LC3/LC3 (microtubule associated protein 1 light chain 3) recruitment and autophagic flux, promoted lysosomal delivery, and reduced infection-induced cellular damage. Etravirine also enhanced basal autophagic flux and induced an autophagy-associated transcriptional program. These effects were reproduced in RAW264.7 macrophages and were attenuated by 3-MA. In mouse infection models, Etravirine reduced bacterial burdens and inflammatory pathology and improved survival. Biophysical, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), docking, mutational, and preliminary analogue analyses supported a putative Etravirine-binding region near the PlcA myo-inositol-binding pocket. Together, these findings establish Etravirine as a PlcA-targeting antivirulence candidate that also strengthens host autophagy-associated restriction of L. monocytogenes.

articles.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Treatment Pattern and Its Associated Outcomes Among Children Referred to Psychiatry and Mental Health Services in Malaysia: Protocol for a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder associated with significant impairments in academic, social, and daily functioning. Despite the availability of clinical practice guidelines in Malaysia, evidence on real-world treatment patterns and outcomes remains limited. The lack of multicenter data on treatment use and clinical outcomes hinders the evaluation of current ADHD care and opportunities for service improvement.

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study is to observe treatment patterns among children with ADHD referred to psychiatry and mental health services in Malaysia after receiving treatment for 18 months. This study will also compare treatment outcomes between children with ADHD who do receive treatment and those who do not receive any ADHD treatment.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study will use secondary data from clinical records of children aged 4 to 16 years with a confirmed diagnosis of ADHD. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, clinical features, ADHD subtype and comorbidities, treatment modalities, health care use, treatment trajectories, and clinical outcomes will be extracted using a standardized case report form and will be anonymized prior to analysis. Data collection will be undertaken by trained site investigators and medical officers across participating centers. Statistical analyses will be conducted using R software (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). Descriptive statistics will be used to summarize characteristics, treatment patterns, health care use, and clinical outcomes of children with ADHD. Treatment patterns will be characterized according to pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions, treatment modifications, and service use. Comparative analyses will be performed to examine associations between treatment patterns and clinical outcomes across children with ADHD and clinical subgroups.

RESULTS: This study will be funded through a Ministry of Health Research Grant obtained in August 2026. It will commence in August 2026 and end in December 2028. Based on the sample size calculation, a minimum of 2771 eligible children with ADHD records will be included in the study. The study will be reported in accordance with the STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) guidelines for retrospective cohort studies. The findings will be disseminated through presentations and article publications at the national and international levels.

CONCLUSIONS: This study will address a critical evidence gap in ADHD care by providing comprehensive real-world data on treatment patterns and outcomes among Malaysian children with ADHD. Findings will identify variations in treatment approaches, treatment trajectories, and clinical outcomes across hospitals and regions, assess the alignment of real-world practice with national recommendations, and highlight potential disparities in access to ADHD specialist services. The findings are expected to support evidence-based clinical decision-making, guide strategic health care planning, optimize resource use, and contribute to the development of a more coordinated, efficient, and equitable system of ADHD care across diverse health care settings in Malaysia.

articles.title: Fecal calprotectin testing for inflammatory bowel disease in patients presenting with lower gastrointestinal symptoms: a retrospective primary care cohort study in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fecal calprotectin (FC) can help to differentiate inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from other causes of lower gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. This study aimed to study FC testing in primary care, associated factors, subsequent secondary care referrals and IBD diagnoses.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using primary care data in England. Adults aged 18-60 with lower GI symptoms between 2015 and 2023 were included. FC testing 30 days before to 3 months after a recorded lower GI symptom was examined. A random-effects logistic regression model explored patient-level factors associated with FC testing. Referral pathways and diagnostic outcomes among patients with FC testing were examined.

RESULTS: Of 830 936 symptomatic patients, 34 944 (4.2%) had FC testing. FC testing increased from 1.6% of symptomatic patients in 2015 to 7.7% in 2023 (P = .001). Factors negatively associated with FC testing included female sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.80; 95% CI, 0.78-0.82), lower socioeconomic status (aOR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95), smoking (aOR, 0.86; 95% CI,, 0.83-0.89) and obesity (aOR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.89-0.95). Among patients referred to gastroenterology, 23.7% with FC >250µg/g were diagnosed with IBD, but only 4.1% with FC 100-250µg/g. Among patients with rectal bleeding and FC 100-250µg/g, 9% had IBD. Despite normal FC results (<100µg/g), 25.2% of symptomatic patients were still referred to secondary care, of whom 0.5% were diagnosed with IBD and 1% with colorectal cancer.

CONCLUSION: FC can effectively triage primary care patients with suspected IBD. Despite negative FC results, a significant proportion of patients were still referred to secondary care, with very few diagnosed with IBD.

articles.title: Pre-ICU medication vulnerability and healthcare-access barriers associated with unplanned intensive care admission among cancer patients: A case-control study.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: BackgroundUnplanned intensive care unit (ICU) admission is a critical event in the cancer trajectory and is associated with substantial mortality. Medication-related vulnerabilities and healthcare-access barriers may contribute to acute deterioration but remain insufficiently studied together.ObjectiveTo identify medication-related and healthcare-access factors independently associated with unplanned ICU admission among adults with cancer.MethodsThis hospital-based case-control study was conducted at a tertiary oncology centre. Cases were adults with cancer with unplanned ICU admission (n = 150), and controls were adults with cancer admitted to wards or day-care units without ICU requirement (n = 150), frequency-matched by age group, sex, and cancer type. Medication vulnerabilities and healthcare-access barriers were assessed using medical records and structured interviews. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).ResultsCases had higher prevalence of polypharmacy (64.0% vs 38.7%), clinically significant drug-drug interactions (42.0% vs 20.7%), and medication non-adherence (51.3% vs 29.3%). Financial barriers (58.7% vs 34.7%) and delayed care-seeking (46.0% vs 24.0%) were also more frequent. After adjustment, financial barriers (aOR 2.31, 95% CI 1.34-3.99), drug-drug interactions (2.14, 1.19-3.85), delayed care-seeking (2.08, 1.16-3.72), polypharmacy (2.05, 1.21-3.47), and non-adherence (1.94, 1.12-3.36) remained independently associated with unplanned ICU admission. ICU mortality was 32.0%.ConclusionMedication vulnerabilities and healthcare-access barriers were associated with unplanned ICU admission. These findings identify potentially modifiable areas for further evaluation, but the case-control design does not establish that interventions targeting these factors would directly reduce ICU admissions.

articles.title: Do We Need to "Be There" to Say Goodbye? Comparing Participatory Agency and Spatial Presence Across Digital Farewell Formats.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
articles.abstract: Digitally mediated attachment is increasingly common, yet the mechanisms of symbolic closure in hybrid physical-digital relationships remain underexplored. We address an XR design question: how different mediated farewell formats relate to perceived symbolic closure, spatial presence, and bereavement-related emotional intensity. Using "cloud petting" as a controlled proxy of digitally mediated attachment, we compare three farewell formats: (1) lightweight social messaging, (2) a revisitable web memorial, and (3) immersive VR ritual participation. These formats differ in symbolic participation, spatial presence, and sensorimotor ritual enactment. In a mixed-methods study ($N$ = 45), Website and VR showed significantly higher perceived symbolic closure than Messaging, while the present sample did not detect a significant closure advantage for VR over Website. VR was also associated with significantly stronger grief-related responses on the Pet Bereavement Questionnaire, whereas negative-affect change measured by the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule did not differ significantly across modalities. This pattern motivates a preliminary, exploratory, mechanism-level Agency-Amplification account: formats supporting structured farewell participation were associated with higher perceived closure, whereas the VR format, combining technical immersion, spatial presence, and sensorimotor ritual enactment, was associated with stronger loss-oriented emotional processing. Because the formats also bundled differences in participation, revisitation, technical immersion, and spatial presence, the study provides preliminary design guidance without isolating the causal contribution of any single feature.

articles.title: A Finger Worn Ring for On-Demand Measurement of Absolute Blood Pressure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Regular blood pressure (BP) monitoring is needed to manage hypertension. However, cuff devices are not readily accessible, and many adults are living with uncontrolled BP. Furthermore, popular wearable cuffless devices typically require calibration with periodic cuff BP measurements or demographic information. A finger worn ring for cuffless BP measurement without such calibration was investigated.

METHODS: BP ring concepts were conceived based on the oscillometric cuff principle. The user varies their finger pressures similar to a cuff device by performing ring tightening followed by hand lowering or ring tightening only under visual guidance, while the ring obtains oscillometric measurements from the digital arteries for on-demand BP measurement. A prototype device was built to implement the BP ring concepts. The ring included a mechanical actuator to adjust its diameter and a photoplethysmography sensor, force sensor, and inertial measurement unit to make the measurements. The ring is interfaced to a display via a wired data acquisition system to guide the user in performing the ring tightening/hand lowering. An oscillometric algorithm is applied to compute BP from the measurements. The device was tested in 25 volunteers.

RESULTS: The ring tightening-hand lowering BP measurement could be learned by new users. The device yielded root-mean-square-errors of 7.1 and 6.9 mmHg for systolic and diastolic BP against a validated arm cuff device.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of absolute BP monitoring using a finger worn ring.

SIGNIFICANCE: The BP ring concepts could potentially be incorporated in smart rings to help improve hypertension control.

articles.title: Cross-Domain Slow Wave Sleep Detection from Single-Lead EEG in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease Recovery.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
articles.abstract: Slow wave sleep (SWS) is vital for neural recovery and cardiovascular stability in children following congenital heart disease (CHD) surgery. However, pediatric CHD sleep patterns are often disrupted by clinical stressors and exhibit substantial domain discrepancies relative to adult data distributions. To address these challenges, this study establishes the Pediatric Cardiac Post-surgical Sleep (PCPS) dataset, a self-collected and expert-annotated pediatric polysomnography (PSG) dataset specifically targeting the early post-CHD surgical period. We further propose PCPS-SleepNet, an end-to-end deep learning framework for cross-domain sleep staging from single-lead EEG, enabling effective knowledge transfer from public sleep data to pediatric post-surgical CHD data. The architecture employs a multi-band input representation across six sub-bands and leverages a Four-Stage Progressive Encoder integrating Multi-Scale Depthwise Convolution (MSDC) for local features, self-attention for global density modeling, and a Conformer block for hybrid refinement. To mitigate limited pediatric data availability and domain shift, this network is pre-trained on public datasets and fine-tuned on the PCPS dataset. Subject-independent validation showed competitive performance, with an overall accuracy of 75.65 ± 0.58%, an AUROC of 89.06 ± 0.18%, an AUPRC of 83.49 ± 0.13%, and a macro F1-score of 76.68 ± 0.70%. For SWS detection, the model achieved an AUPRC of 87.89 ± 0.20% and an F1-score of 81.55 ± 0.74%. Architectural ablations and frequency-band input contribution analysis supported the model design and suggested the complementary discriminative value of slow-wave frequency-band inputs. These results suggest a practical and patient-friendly sleep detection solution for individualized sleep assessment and rehabilitation in vulnerable pediatric populations.

articles.title: Vertical Sleeve Gastrectomy inhibits 11βHSD1 and subsequently reduces IL6 secretion in Mice and Humans: A Shared Anti-Inflammatory Mechanism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vertical sleeve gastrectomy (VSG) improves glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes (T2D) through mechanisms that extend beyond weight loss. The interaction between glucocorticoid metabolism and inflammation in this context remains unclear.

METHODS: We investigated the role of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11βHSD1) in mediating the metabolic effects of VSG in humans and mice. Subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies were collected before and 6 months after VSG. Parallel studies were conducted in lean and high-fat diet-fed mice undergoing VSG or sham surgery, alongside 11βHSD1 knockout models. Glucose tolerance and expression of 11βHSD1 and interleukin-6 (IL6) were assessed.

RESULTS: VSG reduced 11βHSD1 and IL6 expression in human adipose tissue and improved insulin resistance. In lean mice, VSG reduced adipose Hsd11b1 and Il6 expression and altered glucose handling in the absence of detectable changes in total body weight. 11βHSD1 knockout mice exhibited improved glucose tolerance despite increased body weight, partially recapitulating the VSG phenotype. Both interventions reduced circulating and tissue IL6 levels.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify an association between reduced 11βHSD1, inflammatory signalling and metabolic adaptations following VSG, and support further investigation of 11βHSD1 as a potential contributor to the metabolic effects of surgery.

articles.title: Implementing Culturally Tailored Diabetes Prevention in Hispanic Communities: An Integrative Review Using the RE-AIM Framework.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hispanic adults in the US have disproportionately high rates of diabetes and face persistent barriers to accessing evidence-based prevention programs. Despite the demonstrated efficacy of culturally tailored diabetes prevention interventions, translation into routine community practice is markedly limited. This integrative review examined implementation processes, barriers, and facilitators of culturally tailored diabetes prevention interventions in Hispanic communities, using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework to identify strategies that support population-level impact.

METHODS: Comprehensive searches of 5 databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, EMBASE, ScienceDirect) from 2005 through 2025 identified 69 sources; 37 (empirical studies, study protocols, and reviews) reporting implementation data were analyzed. Data extraction and synthesis aligned with the RE-AIM framework and used constant comparative methods. Quality appraisal used the Johns Hopkins Evidence-Based Practice tool. This review was not registered, consistent with integrative review methods.

RESULTS: Implementation facilitators included cultural concordance, community health worker models, community-based delivery, and family-centered programming. Barriers included funding instability, workforce shortages, male underrepresentation, and limited maintenance data. Interventions achieved clinically meaningful weight loss (3.2 kg-5.8 kg), but real-world outcomes were smaller than those reported in efficacy trials. Community-based organizations were the primary adopters, although resource constraints were common. Only 18% of studies reported outcomes beyond 12 months, limiting the assessment of sustained impact.

CONCLUSION: Culturally tailored diabetes prevention interventions are effective and acceptable in Hispanic communities; however, implementation gaps in adoption, scaling ability, and sustainability limit population-level impact. Successful translation requires cultural concordance, community partnerships, flexible delivery models, and workforce development. Addressing structural barriers through policy support for community health worker integration, sustainable funding mechanisms, and health care-community partnerships is essential to achieving equitable diabetes prevention at scale.

articles.title: Community Health Worker Interventions Addressing Social Determinants of Health in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic diseases disproportionately affect people facing social and economic adversity. Community health workers (CHWs) are increasingly recognized as a key workforce for addressing social determinants of health (SDOH). However, evidence for the effect of CHW-led interventions on social and clinical outcomes among US adults with chronic disease is limited. This systematic review evaluated the effects of CHW-led interventions on SDOH and health outcomes.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines and a registered Prospero protocol, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Embase (Ovid) in April 2024 for US-based randomized or quasi-experimental studies involving adults with chronic disease and a patient-facing CHW intervention addressing at least 1 SDOH domain. Eligible studies were required to have a comparator group and report social or health outcomes. We used standardized forms to extract data and assess quality.

RESULTS: We identified 1,939 records and screened 1,058 abstracts. We reviewed 110 full-text articles; 7 studies met inclusion criteria. All were randomized controlled trials addressing at least 1 SDOH domain. Interventions most commonly targeted health care access, housing stability, or care coordination among adults with diabetes, HIV, asthma, hepatitis C, or hearing loss. CHW interventions demonstrated improvements in several condition-specific clinical outcomes, but overall effects on major clinical indicators were modest and inconsistent.

CONCLUSION: CHW-led interventions show promise for addressing social needs and improving engagement in care among adults with chronic disease, but evidence of meaningful clinical benefit is still limited. The lack of large, well-powered trials underscores the need for more rigorous research to strengthen the evidence base for CHW-driven SDOH interventions in US health systems.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The comparative efficacy and safety of the new drugs (including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors [SGLT-2Is], glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RAs], non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [nsMRAs], and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators [sGCs]) for heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved (HFmrEF/HFpEF) ejection fraction remains largely unclear. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate their comparative effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for treatment selection.

METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were comprehensively searched. We included randomized controlled trials that compared nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA with placebo for patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Primary efficacy outcomes were cardiovascular (CV) death, hospitalization for heart failure (HF hospitalization), and all-cause mortality, while primary safety outcomes were adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs). The main analysis was conducted to compare the effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF between individual drugs. A frequentist network meta-analysis with random-effects models was used to calculate risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 20 randomized controlled trials (RCTs, including 10 drugs from 35 publications) were included for analyses, but none provided head-to-head direct comparisons. No significant differences among all the individual drugs were found in risks of CV death or all-cause mortality. Compared with exenatide, low or moderate certainty evidence showed that dapagliflozin (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.36-0.91), empagliflozin (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.34-0.86), and semaglutide (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20-0.91) were related to decreased risk of HF hospitalization. No significant differences in the risk of SAEs were found among the individual drugs. Compared with empagliflozin, very low certainty evidence showed that tirzepatide (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32) was related to increased risk of AEs. When comparing the four drug classes (nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA), no significant differences in efficacy outcomes were found, while SGLT-2I (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.96) was associated with a decreased risk of AEs compared with GLP-1RA.

CONCLUSIONS: No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier number CRD420251143542.

articles.title: Beyond morphology: a combined histopathological and immunohistochemical protocol for the post-mortem diagnosis of the electrical mark.
articles.abstract: The histopathological diagnosis of the electrical mark is hampered by the morphological overlap with thermal burns and abrasions and by the absence of standardized immunohistochemical criteria. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily evaluate an integrated histological and immunohistochemical protocol for the microscopic diagnosis of documented electrocution. Twenty-four full-thickness cutaneous samples from forensic cases with documented electrocution were stained with hematoxylin-eosin and processed for immunohistochemistry with Cytokeratin AE1/AE3. Six representative cases were also stained with HSP27, HSP70, and HSP90 antibodies. Histological findings were summarized as frequencies with exact 95% binomial confidence intervals (CIs). Ordinal immunohistochemical scores assigned independently by three observers were evaluated using a two-way random-effects, absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient for single measurements [ICC(A,1)], pairwise weighted Cohen's kappa, and observed agreement. Epidermal and dermal coagulative necrosis, collagen homogenization, vascular dilatation/congestion, and hemorrhage/thrombosis were observed in 24/24 samples (100%; exact 95% CI 85.8-100%). Epidermal and dermal nuclear elongation and dark-stained nuclei occurred in 23/24 samples (95.8%; 95% CI 78.9-99.9%). For Cytokeratin, ICC(A,1) was 0.748 (95% CI 0.568-0.873); pairwise linearly weighted kappa values ranged from 0.437 to 0.820, and exact agreement among all three observers was 43.5%. HSP scores were identical among observers across the six selected slides (ICC and pairwise weighted kappa = 1.000; exact agreement 100%, 95% CI 54.1-100%). The combined assessment of H&E features and Cytokeratin/HSP immunoreactivity identifies a recurrent histopathological pattern that supports a provisional hierarchy of findings and can improve the standardization of microscopic assessment of electrical marks.

articles.title: Micronutrient Deficiency Burden and Asthma Morbidity in Children: Independent Associations with Asthma Control and Exacerbation Risk.
Blood culture time to positivity corrected for delayed incubation start - a population-based study.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: A short blood culture time to positivity (TTP) is associated with an increased risk for death in blood stream infections (BSI). However, TTP is also shortened when the time elapsed from sampling to incubation start (TTI) increases. We aimed to test whether TTP corrected for TTI was more strongly associated with 7-day mortality in BSI.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of positive blood culture bottles in Skåne region, Sweden, 2015 to 2023, with linked clinical data obtained from healthcare databases. Correction factors were derived using linear regression between TTI and TTP. The association between TTP and 7-day mortality was studied in BSI episodes, using non-linear logistic regression. Actual mortality rates and odds ratios (OR) for different TTP cutoffs were calculated.

RESULTS: In total, 100,829 bottles were included and each hour of TTI was associated with a shortening of TTP by 0.27 h in aerobic bottles and 0.32 h in anaerobic bottles. After deduplication, 31,723 unique BSI episodes were included in mortality analysis, with a 7-day mortality rate of 6.4%. In non-linear regression models, corrected TTP showed a stronger association with 7-day mortality than crude TTP in episodes with TTP < 10 h. Actual mortality rates were higher for corrected TTP at all cutoffs between 6 and 12 h.

CONCLUSION: TTP corrected for TTI was more strongly associated with 7-day mortality than crude TTP. We recommend that correction for TTI should be used in future studies on TTP, especially if on-site incubation is unavailable.

articles.title: Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.
articles.abstract: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact.
