No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention.

RESULTS: Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

articles.title: Impact of burst suppression duration on delirium and its diagnostic value in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) delirium affects up to 50% of mechanically ventilated patients. This condition is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although bispectral index (BIS) monitoring is widely used for sedation assessment, its predictive value for delirium remains limited. Burst suppression (BS) is an electroencephalographic pattern reflecting profound cerebral dysfunction. BS has been proposed as a predictor of delirium. However, the quantitative role of burst suppression duration (BSD) in delirium risk stratification has not been established. This prospective observational study enrolled 300 mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients between April 2021 and October 2024 at Harrison International Peace Hospital. Continuous video-electroencephalogram (vEEG) monitoring was performed. BSD was quantified from the vEEG recordings. Delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of BSD. Among 300 patients, 130 (43.3%) developed delirium. The delirium group had significantly longer BSD than the control group (median 81.1 s, IQR 41.5-148.5 vs. 17.2 s, IQR 5.8-32.9; P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified BSD (adjusted OR = 1.018, 95% CI 1.012-1.023; P < 0.001), BIS (adjusted OR = 0.964, 95% CI 0.946-0.982; P < 0.001), age (adjusted OR = 1.024, 95% CI 1.002-1.047; P = 0.031), and hypertension (adjusted OR = 1.748, 95% CI 1.002-3.051; P = 0.049) as independent risk factors. ROC analysis demonstrated that BSD achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.871 (95% CI 0.829-0.913). The optimal cutoff of 41.5 s yielded a sensitivity of 80.8% and a specificity of 78.2%. The combination of BSD and BIS improved the AUC to 0.914 (95% CI 0.882-0.946). BSD is an independent risk factor for delirium in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. It demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy as a quantitative biomarker. The combination of BSD and BIS provides superior predictive performance. This combined approach offers a practical quantitative tool for early delirium risk stratification.

articles.title: From latency to neurodegeneration: varicella-zoster virus reactivation and dementia risk, with a focus on herpes zoster ophthalmicus.
articles.abstract: Varicella zoster virus (VZV) reactivation has emerged as a potential contributor to dementia through vascular and inflammatory mechanisms, with herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO) representing a potentially higher-risk phenotype because of its association with cerebrovascular complications. This narrative review evaluated the epidemiological and mechanistic evidence linking VZV reactivation to cognitive decline. MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2026, supplemented by relevant publications identified during revision through October 2026, with emphasis on systematic reviews, large observational studies, quasi-experimental vaccination studies, and mechanistic investigations. Infection-based studies demonstrated heterogeneous findings, with modest associations between herpes zoster and subsequent dementia that frequently attenuated after adjustment for frailty and comorbidity. In contrast, vaccination studies, particularly natural experiments and quasi-experimental analyses, consistently reported lower dementia incidence following zoster immunisation, although causal interpretation and the magnitude of any protective effect remain uncertain. Observational studies suggest that antiviral therapy is associated with fewer short-term cerebrovascular complications, although its relationship with long-term cognitive outcomes remains uncertain. VZV-associated vasculopathy provides the strongest mechanistic rationale for a link with cognitive decline, whereas neuroinflammation, possible blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and interactions with neurodegenerative processes remain proposed pathways. Current evidence suggests that VZV reactivation may accelerate cognitive decline in susceptible individuals, but causality remains unproven. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the contribution of VZV reactivation and the potential neuroprotective effects of vaccination and antiviral therapy.

articles.title: Farrerol Attenuates Brain Injury After Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Modulates Nrf2 and TLR4/NF-κB Signaling.
articles.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating stroke with limited therapies. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of farrerol after ICH and the contribution of Nrf2 signaling. ICH was induced by autologous blood injection in wild-type and Nrf2-knockout mice studied in separate cohorts. Complementary experiments used hemin-exposed HT-22 cells, with vehicle and sulforaphane controls included in the ML385 inhibition experiments. In wild-type mice, farrerol improved neurological function and reduced brain edema, neuronal injury, glial reactivity, and circulating pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. These improvements were accompanied by reduced hippocampal Keap1 abundance, increased Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1 expression, and reduced TLR4/NF-κB pathway activation. Transcriptomic analysis suggested reduced NF-κB-related transcriptional activity, although this enrichment did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction. Farrerol did not significantly improve the assessed functional or inflammatory outcomes in Nrf2-knockout mice, although the separate-cohort design limits comparisons between genotypes. In HT-22 cells, farrerol improved viability, promoted Nrf2 nuclear accumulation, reduced Keap1 abundance, and increased HO-1 and NQO1 expression, alongside reductions in TLR4 expression and the p-p65/p65 ratio. Significant farrerol × ML385 interactions for cell viability, Nrf2 nuclear accumulation, and Keap1 abundance provided further support for Nrf2 involvement in cytoprotection. However, interactions for TLR4 expression and the p-p65/p65 ratio were not significant, leaving the contribution of Nrf2 to these signaling changes unresolved. Together, these findings demonstrate protective effects of farrerol after ICH in mice and support a contribution of Nrf2 to its cytoprotective activity, providing a basis for further preclinical investigation.

articles.title: Characteristics of treatment responses to physical exercise and diet in diabetic peripheral artery disease patients: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects walking performance and increases risk of amputation. Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear. The present systematic review aims to summarize features of treatment response to physical exercise and diet management in diabetic PAD patients, and provide crucial information on optimization of PAD management of these patients in clinical practice.

METHODS: A systematic review was performed on human studies investigating effects of physical exercise and diet on development and improvement of diabetic PAD patients by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL. The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA). The certainty level of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: A total of 18 studies were included, 15 of which evaluated effects of exercise on diabetic PAD, and three evaluated correlation between diet and diabetic PAD. Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and home-based exercise were able to improve ankle-brachial index (ABI) and blood flow velocity in diabetic PAD. In contrast, walking performance such as the six minute walk distance (6MWD), maximal walking time and distance, peak walking time (PWT) and claudication onset time (COT) were not significantly improved or presented conflicting results. Administration of multiple exercises or alternative interventions such as shock wave therapy or low-frequency pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (LFPMT) may enhance improvement of ABI. Adherence to Mediterranean diet was associated with blood flow and intermittent claudication, as well as risk of development of PAD. GRADE analysis revealed very low to moderate grade evidence for findings on ABI, flow velocity and functions, mainly due to study types, number of studies available, small sample size, moderate risk of bias and conflicting results. Similarly, low grade evidence was also revealed for effects and association of diet on risk of PAD due to study type and number of studies available.

CONCLUSION: Diabetic PAD patients may present reduced treatment response to physical exercise in walking performance and other functions, which may be improved by combination of multiple physical exercises or alternative interventions with or without combination of exercise. Mediterranean diet may be associated with beneficial effects, which requires further investigations. These findings were of very low to moderate level of certainty, and therefore, further validation is warranted in the future.

articles.title: Group A streptococcus vaccine strategies: virulence targets, resistance constraints and complementary control measures.
articles.abstract: Group A Streptococcus (GAS), or Streptococcus pyogenes, causes a connected spectrum of pharyngeal, cutaneous, invasive and immune-mediated diseases. Although beta-lactams remain active, treatment alone has not controlled transmission, recurrent infection, rapid invasive progression or acute rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease. Control is further weakened by increased macrolide and clindamycin resistance, heterogeneous diagnostic access, asymptomatic carriage, crowded living conditions and unreliable continuity of secondary prophylaxis. These limitations have shifted the field from a predominantly treatment-centered approach toward the development of vaccines as a prevention strategy. Target selection is guided by virulence functions that are required for colonization, immune evasion and tissue injury. These include the M protein, group A carbohydrate (GAC), streptolysin O, Streptococcus pyogenes cell envelope protease (SpyCEP), Streptococcus pyogenes adhesion and division protein (SpyAD), C5a peptidase and other conserved surface or secreted antigens. Current strategies include multivalent type-specific M-protein vaccines, conserved M-protein peptide vaccines, glycoconjugates, multicomponent non-M-protein formulations and mRNA-lipid nanoparticle platforms. The clinical pipeline has recently broadened. Phase I studies have been completed for StreptAnova and MJ8VAX, whereas the J8-K4S2 and p*17-K4S2 clinical trial studies have been completed, with peer-reviewed results pending. The GSK four-component vaccine initiated phase I evaluation in 2025 and remained under clinical evaluation in 2026, whereas the VAX-A1 formulation entered a first-in-human phase I study in 2026. However, no licensed GAS vaccine is available. Progress remains constrained by uncertain correlates of protection, autoimmune safety requirements, geographical emm diversity, endpoint selection and the need for trials in high-burden populations. This narrative review therefore focuses on the disease problem, targetable virulence mechanisms, limits of antimicrobial control, current vaccine pipeline and interventions required to complement future vaccine use.

articles.title: Effect of fasting and postprandial states on thyroid function test parameters and diagnostic interpretation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid function tests are among the most frequently requested investigations; several pre-analytical factors may influence them. Reference ranges are not standardized for fasting versus postprandial sampling. We aimed to synthesize evidence comparing fasting and postprandial thyroid function test and to assess the effect of these on diagnostic classification.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 for reporting and was prospectively registered (PROSPERO CRD420261344874). MEDLINE (through PubMed), Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched using a PECO framework for observational & RCT studies (publication cut off as March 24th, 2026) reporting paired, same-day fasting and postprandial TSH, FT4 or FT3 in the same individuals. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were performed in duplicate. Comparisons were analysed as single-group pre-post data using random-effects models with the mean difference calculated as postprandial minus fasting levels. The analysis was conducted at study level, comparator sub-group level and a three-level model as alternatives. Heterogeneity was quantified with I² and certainty was rated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. For TSH (14 studies with 24 subgroup comparisons; n = 1257), the pooled mean difference (MD) was - 0.802 mIU/L (95% CI - 1.073 to - 0.531; I² = 99.7%), indicating significantly lower postprandial TSH (low certainty of evidence); and robust across subgroups and sensitivity analyses, with greatest in overt (- 2.518 mIU/L) and subclinical hypothyroidism (- 2.173 mIU/L). No significant fasting-postprandial difference was found for FT4 or FT3.

CONCLUSION: Caloric intake might significantly lower postprandial TSH, but with low certainty. This has clinical relevance in borderline thyroid dysfunction, where it may drive misclassification towards euthyroid state. Standardizing and recording fasting status may improve interpretation of borderline thyroid results, although current evidence does not establish superiority of either sampling condition.

articles.title: Are Injectable Antihypertensives the Answer to Improving Blood Pressure Control: SiRNAs and Antisense Oligonucleotide Agents.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Hypertension remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet blood pressure control rates remain suboptimal despite the widespread availability of effective antihypertensive therapies. Poor long-term adherence, therapeutic inertia, and the need for lifelong daily treatment continue to limit the effectiveness of current pharmacological strategies. This review examines the biological rationale, available clinical evidence, and potential role of long-acting RNA-based therapies targeting hepatic angiotensinogen synthesis in hypertension.

RECENT FINDINGS: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) and antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting angiotensinogen represent a novel therapeutic approach that suppresses production of the unique precursor of the renin-angiotensin system. Zilebesiran has demonstrated sustained reductions in circulating angiotensinogen and ambulatory blood pressure following infrequent subcutaneous administration in phase 1 and phase 2 clinical trials. Antisense strategies have provided additional clinical validation of sustained angiotensinogen inhibition, although their antihypertensive efficacy has been less consistent. Ongoing clinical development is addressing long-term cardiovascular outcomes, safety, and optimal patient selection. RNA-based antihypertensive therapies may represent an important evolution in hypertension management by combining upstream renin-angiotensin system inhibition with prolonged pharmacological activity and reduced dependence on daily medication adherence. However, their future clinical role will depend on evidence regarding long-term safety, cardiovascular outcomes, reversibility, cost-effectiveness, patient selection, and integration with conventional antihypertensive therapy.

articles.title: Candidozyma auris in intensive care units: A point prevalence study and six-month colonization-infection surveillance.
articles.journal: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Candidozyma auris has emerged as a globally significant nosocomial pathogen due to its multidrug antifungal resistance, environmental persistence, and high mortality rates. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of C. auris colonization through a point prevalence screening in the intensive care units (ICUs) of our hospital and to evaluate colonization and infection outcomes during a subsequent six-month follow-up period.

OBJECTIVES: The present study aimed to evaluate C. auris colonization rates through point prevalence screening in the ICUs of our hospital, to assess colonization and infection outcomes during a subsequent six-month follow-up period, and to establish a diagnostic algorithm for C. auris identification in our laboratory.

METHODS: Following the detection of an index C. auris case in our hospital in February 2025, a point prevalence study was conducted in all ICUs. Composite swab samples (bilateral axilla and groin) were obtained from hospitalized patients on the same day. In addition, urine and wound cultures were collected from eligible patients. Isolates were identified using chromogenic media, conventional microbiological methods, and MALDI-TOF MS. After the point prevalence study, surveillance for colonization and bloodstream infection was performed over a six-month period.

RESULTS: C. auris colonization was detected in 7 of 70 ICU patients (10%) based on composite swab samples. During the six-month follow-up, colonization was identified in 15 patients, and C. auris fungemia developed in nine patients. All patients with positive blood cultures died. The most frequently identified risk factors were broad-spectrum antibiotic use, prolonged ICU stay, and the presence of urinary catheters.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that C. auris colonization can be detected at a high rate in ICUs and that severe invasive infections may develop following colonization. Early diagnosis, active screening strategies, and effective infection control measures are critical for reducing C. auris-associated morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Medicare Part D formulary coverage of SGLT2 inhibitors across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic indications, 2019-2026.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) carry Class I, Level A recommendations for type 2 diabetes (T2D), heart failure (HF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD) but remain underused outside T2D, with formulary restrictions commonly cited as a contributing cause. We assessed whether Medicare Part D formulary restrictions account for this gap and whether the restrictions differ across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) indications.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of national Medicare Part D formulary files for plan years 2019-2026, using the January/February snapshot (410 formularies in 2019, 330 in 2026; 13,726 SGLT2i monotherapy entries). We measured entry-level prior authorization (PA) and step-therapy prevalence, the proportion of formularies offering at least one and at least two unrestricted SGLT2i drugs, and tier distribution, across three indication groups reflecting cumulative regulatory approvals.

RESULTS: PA was uncommon across all indications and years, never exceeding 1.6%, and at least 98% of formularies offered a PA-free SGLT2i in every indication group-year. Step therapy fell to zero by 2025 then rebounded in 2026, concentrated on empagliflozin, whose entry-level step therapy rate rose from 0.00% to 18.18%, coincident with the effective date of its negotiated maximum fair price; co-negotiated dapagliflozin showed no comparable increase (1.21%). Tier 3 was the dominant placement (61.9-78.7%). Canagliflozin coverage fell from 58.3% of formularies in 2019 to 5.8% in 2026, and only 5.8% offered two step-free SGLT2i for CKD by 2026.

CONCLUSION: Formulary restrictions do not appear to be a major barrier to SGLT2i use among Medicare beneficiaries, redirecting attention toward clinician- and system-level factors. Narrowing CKD-indication approved options and an emergent step-therapy rebound warrant monitoring.

articles.title: Comparative adverse-event reporting patterns of semaglutide and tirzepatide: a disproportionality analysis of FAERS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are widely used for type 2 diabetes and obesity, but comparative post-marketing safety data remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare adverse-event reporting patterns for semaglutide and tirzepatide in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), focusing on gastrointestinal, renal and ocular events, alopecia, serious outcomes, mortality, and reporting chronology.

METHODS: This retrospective pharmacovigilance study analyzed FAERS reports submitted from January 2022 through June 2026. After deduplication, 215,337 unique reports remained; predefined exposure criteria identified 60,423 semaglutide-only reports, 143,126 tirzepatide-only reports, and 853 reports listing both drugs without additional suspect active ingredients. Disproportionality was assessed using reporting odds ratios (RORs) with 95% confidence intervals. Multivariable logistic regression, false discovery rate adjustment, and reporting-latency analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: Semaglutide showed higher reporting odds than tirzepatide for impaired gastric emptying (ROR 6.39), intestinal obstruction/ileus (ROR 4.56), acute kidney injury (ROR 2.51), pancreatitis (ROR 2.18), vomiting (ROR 2.11), and optic ischaemic neuropathy (ROR 15.77). Alopecia was relatively more frequently reported with tirzepatide (ROR 0.74). Semaglutide reports had higher adjusted reporting odds of hospitalization (aOR 2.80) and death (aOR 1.21). In an exploratory analysis restricted to male reports, erectile dysfunction was reported in 92 of 16,673 semaglutide reports and 46 of 27,321 tirzepatide reports (ROR 3.29, 95% CI 2.31-4.69; q < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide and tirzepatide exhibited distinct post-marketing reporting patterns. The erectile-dysfunction finding was exploratory and hypothesis-generating. All findings reflect spontaneous reporting rather than comparative clinical risk or causality and require confirmation in population-based studies.

articles.title: Breast Milk and Allergic Disease Development: Immunological Factors Associated with Eczema, Food Allergy and Wheezing/Asthma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Human milk (HM) contains a diverse array of immunological, microbial, and metabolic bioactive factors that may influence early immune maturation and allergic disease susceptibility. This narrative review examines current evidence linking major HM bioactives with eczema, food allergy, and wheezing/asthma, integrating mechanistic findings with human observational and clinical data.

RECENT FINDINGS: Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), secretory IgA (sIgA), human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), cytokines, fatty acids, short-chain fatty acids, the HM microbiome, and extracellular vesicles have all been implicated in pathways relevant to epithelial integrity, microbial colonization, and immune tolerance. However, associations with allergic outcomes are heterogeneous and frequently context dependent. Findings vary according to lactation stage, maternal characteristics, infant susceptibility, microbial exposures, and outcome definition. Mechanistic evidence is often stronger than prospective clinical evidence, and no individual HM component or bioactive profile has yet emerged as a reproducible predictor of allergy protection. Current evidence supports viewing HM as a dynamic maternal-milk-infant biological network rather than as a source of isolated protective factors. Future studies should integrate repeated HM sampling, rigorous allergic phenotyping, and multi-omic approaches to distinguish causal mediators from biomarkers of maternal or infant biology.

articles.title: Toward multimodal physiological assessment of clinical performance in simulation-based medical education: a machine learning approach.
articles.journal: Advances in health sciences education : theory and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assessment of learner performance in simulation-based medical education commonly relies on faculty observation. Learners' physiological responses may provide complementary information about responses to clinical task demands, but their relationship with observed performance is complex and context dependent. Whether multimodal physiological patterns can reliably distinguish faculty-assigned performance categories across simulation events and learner populations remains unclear.

METHODS: This prospective observational study developed machine-learning models using physiological data alone to classify learner performance according to faculty-assigned novice versus competent categories during high-fidelity simulation. Data were collected from 152 learners (74 Emergency Medicine residents, 70 Anesthesiology residents, 8 Emergency Medical Services students) across 470 simulation scenarios. A multimodal assessment platform synchronized physiological signals (electrodermal activity, heart rate, skin temperature) from Empatica E4 wristbands with faculty evaluations. A genetic algorithm was employed for feature selection, and neural network models were evaluated using multiple leave-N-out strategies to assess generalizability across learners.

RESULTS: The neural network achieved 84-85% balanced accuracy across thresholds 0.45-0.70, with sensitivity 93.3-95.4% and specificity 72.9-76.2%. Despite class imbalance (80.6% competent, 19.4% novice), performance remained robust, with Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.687-0.706 and precision-recall area-under-the-curve (PR-AUC) values of 0.969-0.970 across thresholds.

CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal physiological features enabled classification of faculty-assigned performance categories with strong discrimination in internal validation. These findings support the potential of temporally resolved, physiology-informed analytics to complement faculty assessment and facilitate targeted review of simulation events. Further work is needed to strengthen rating-label validity and temporal alignment and to evaluate model transparency, fairness, and generalizability across institutions, simulation contexts, and learner populations.

articles.title: Combined vitamins C and E attenuate memory impairment and hippocampal damage in diabetic sleep-deprived mice: behavioral and molecular insights.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) and sleep disturbances are associated with cognitive impairment and hippocampal dysfunction, potentially involving oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.

OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effects of vitamins C and E, individually and in combination, to determine whether their complementary antioxidant properties provide enhanced neuroprotective effects against cognitive and hippocampal alterations in diabetic sleep-deprived mice.

METHODS: Diabetes was induced in male BALB/c mice (25-30 g) by streptozotocin (60 mg/kg), followed by partial sleep deprivation using the inverted flowerpot method. Animals received vitamin C (50 mg/kg), vitamin E (100 mg/kg), or their combination for 20 days. Body weight and blood glucose were monitored. Spatial learning and memory were evaluated using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal histopathology, GFAP immunostaining, and expression of genes related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and neuroprotection were assessed.

RESULTS: Vitamin E and combined vitamin C and E treatment reduced FBG and were associated with higher final body weight than untreated diabetic sleep-deprived mice. Vitamin treatments improved spatial learning and memory, with combined treatment producing greater improvements in selected behavioral outcomes. Combined treatment increased hippocampal neuronal density and reduced GFAP immunoreactivity. Vitamin treatment increased BDNF, Nrf2, and HO-1 expression and reduced iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-1β expression.

CONCLUSION: Vitamin C and E, particularly in combination, were associated with improved metabolic, cognitive, and hippocampal outcomes in diabetic sleep-deprived mice, potentially involving modulation of neuroinflammatory and oxidative stress-related markers.

articles.title: Molecular mechanisms, functional diversity, and therapeutic implications of HSP90 isoforms in lung cancer.
articles.abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) is a critical molecular chaperone that ensures the stability and maturation of oncogenic client proteins in lung cancer. This review examines the distinct roles of HSP90α, HSP90β, GRP94 and the mitochondrial paralog TRAP1 in driving disease progression. While HSP90α governs invasiveness and metastasis, HSP90β maintains homeostatic oncogenic signalling. TRAP1 serves as a metabolic lynchpin, facilitating metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial cytoprotection, and resistance to apoptosis. Together, these isoforms stabilize key drivers such as EGFR, ALK and KRAS, fostering therapeutic resistance. Utilizing systems biology, bioinformatics and comparative analysis of experimental studies, this review explores the high-throughput identification of HSP90 isoforms as central "hub genes" within the lung cancer interactome. The therapeutic potential of mitochondrial-targeted drug delivery systems and isoform-selective inhibitors designed to minimize systemic toxicity are explored in detail. Ultimately, understanding isoform-specific dynamics and multi-omics regulatory networks is essential for developing personalized, selective interventions to overcome drug resistance and improve lung cancer management.

articles.title: Combined crocin and treadmill exercise regulate cardiac MicroRNA-23b, nuclear factor Erythroid 2-related factor 2, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha in experimental type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a major complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus and is strongly associated with chronic inflammation, oxidative imbalance, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. MicroRNAs, particularly miR-23b, have emerged as important regulators of inflammatory and metabolic responses; however, its modulation by combined nutritional and exercise interventions in diabetic cardiac tissue remains unclear. The present study evaluated the effects of combined crocin supplementation and treadmill exercise on miR-23b expression and levels of TNF-α, and NRF2 in the heart tissue of rat model of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly allocated into healthy control and diabetic groups. Type 2 diabetes mellitus was induced in 28 rats using a high-fat diet for four weeks followed by a single intraperitoneal injection of streptozotocin (35 mg/kg). Diabetic rats were divided into four groups (n = 7/group), including diabetic control, crocin-treated (50 mg/kg/day), treadmill exercise, and combined crocin plus exercise groups and treated for eight weeks using combined crocin (50 mg/kg/day) and treadmill exercise. Next, heart tissues were isolated and the gene expression of miR-23b was assessed via SYBR-Green real-time RT-PCR, and the protein levels of TNF-α and NRF2 were measured by ELISA. In addition, apoptosis rate was evaluated by TUNEL method.

RESULTS: Combined crocin and treadmill exercise significantly reduced cardiac TNF-α levels from 8.50 pg/mL in diabetic control rats to 3.78 pg/mL, corresponding to a 55.5% reduction (p < 0.001). In contrast, NRF2 levels increased from 0.2 to 0.82 ng/mg protein, representing a 310% increase following the combined treatment (p = 0.0002). Furthermore, miR-23b expression increased from 0.72-fold in diabetic control rats to 1.82-fold following combined treatment, corresponding to a 151.8% increase (p < 0.001). Combined treatment also significantly reduced cardiac apoptosis compared with the diabetic control group.

CONCLUSION: Combined crocin supplementation and treadmill exercise improved inflammatory cytokines and antioxidant-related molecular alterations in the cardiac tissue of HFD/STZ-induced diabetic rats by reducing TNF-α levels and increasing NRF2 protein levels and miR-23b expression. Although the combined intervention showed favorable effects compared with individual treatments, further studies are required to determine whether this combination provides synergistic benefits.

articles.title: Wearable Technologies in Gastrointestinal Disorders: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Gastrointestinal disorders fluctuate between clinical encounters, creating a need for objective longitudinal monitoring. We review wearable technologies across gastrointestinal disorders, emphasizing clinical applications, current evidence, and barriers to implementation.

RECENT FINDINGS: Wearables capture physiologic, biochemical, and acoustic signals relevant to gastrointestinal disease. In inflammatory bowel disease, wearable-derived physiologic changes may precede inflammatory and symptomatic flares and help distinguish inflammatory from non-inflammatory symptoms. Sweat biosensors can measure inflammatory analytes, including calprotectin. Beyond inflammatory bowel disease, autonomic measures characterize disorders of gut-brain interaction, electrogastrographic and acoustic devices assess gastrointestinal motility, and activity and sleep metrics may aid postoperative recovery assessment and risk stratification in chronic liver disease. Evidence remains predominantly observational, and validated clinical thresholds are lacking, limiting the current clinical applicability of wearable derived signals. Wearables enable continuous, noninvasive monitoring across gastrointestinal disorders, but prospective trials are needed to establish clinical utility, actionable thresholds, workflow integration, and patient-centered implementation, and demonstrate improvement in clinically meaningful outcomes.

articles.title: Atherosclerosis Begins in Childhood: A Life-Course Perspective on Arterial Remodeling from the Bogalusa Heart Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) findings from the Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS) and examines how cardiovascular risk factors across the life course contribute to early subclinical atherosclerosis.

RECENT FINDINGS: BHS studies consistently demonstrate that obesity, dyslipidemia, and SBP are independently associated with increased cIMT in young adulthood. Life-course analyses show that cumulative BMI and LDL-C exposure independently predict adult cIMT, with race-specific sensitive periods identified for obesity. Metabolically abnormal obesity confers greater vascular risk than metabolically healthy obesity. LDL-C and the total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio are the principal lipid determinants of carotid wall thickening, with associations strengthening from childhood through midlife. SBP dominates in cross-sectional models, while BMI shows more consistent independent effects beginning in childhood. Cardiometabolic clustering further amplifies vascular risk, and adolescence represents a key developmental window, with pediatric metabolic syndrome performing no better than BMI alone in predicting adult cIMT. BHS evidence supports the view that atherosclerosis is a progressive disease that begins in childhood and develops through the cumulative burden of risk factors over the life-course. Obesity, dyslipidemia, and elevated blood pressure each independently contribute to cIMT, and their clustering within individuals amplifies this effect, such that the combined sustained burden across the life-course is the strongest determinant of subclinical arterial remodeling. This underscores the importance of early, sustained prevention strategies that target modifiable CV risk factors beginning in childhood.

articles.title: Prevalence of systemic and ocular comorbidities in patients aged 18-50 years with retinal vein occlusion.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a well-established cause of vision loss in older adults. However, the prevalence and distribution of documented systemic comorbidities in younger adults are not well characterized.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized the TriNetX US Collaborative Network to identify younger adults (aged 18-50 years) with retinal vein occlusion (RVO), including both branch (BRVO) and central (CRVO) subtypes. The prevalence of predefined systemic comorbidities was evaluated during the period preceding and within 90 days following the diagnosis of RVO to characterize their frequency and distribution among young patients.

RESULTS: A total of 5,257 younger adults with RVO were included. Before RVO diagnosis, 66.4% of patients had at least one documented risk factor, most commonly hypertension (25%), obesity (17.4%), and type 2 diabetes mellitus (13.3%). Primary thrombophilia (2.2%) and hematologic malignancy (1.6%) were less frequently documented. Within 90 days following RVO diagnosis, 12.3% of patients received at least one newly coded risk-factor diagnosis, most commonly hypertension (4.5%), obesity (2.3%), and hyperlipidemia (1.9%). Among patients without any previously documented risk factors, 3.7% had at least one risk factor newly documented during this period.

CONCLUSIONS: Among young adults with RVO, common vascular comorbidities were documented more frequently than hypercoagulable or vasculitic conditions.

articles.title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and experimental analyses identify macrophage-associated STAT3 signaling contributing to ferroptosis-related injury in septic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) is a major complication of sepsis, but how inflammatory immune cells contribute to ferroptosis-related myocardial injury remains unclear. We investigated ferroptosis-associated transcriptional remodeling in SCM and the functional contribution of macrophage STAT3 signaling.

METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication analysis, and independent mouse and human transcriptomic cohorts were integrated to characterize ferroptosis-associated changes. Driver and suppressor signatures were analyzed separately. STAT3 was silenced in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, followed by conditioned-medium transfer to H9C2 cardiomyocytes. Ferroptosis-related injury was evaluated using lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, molecular markers, Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) intervention, and an SCM mouse model.

RESULTS: Ferroptosis-associated transcriptional features showed marked cell-type heterogeneity. Inflammatory macrophages exhibited prominent STAT3-related inflammatory signaling and extensive predicted communication with cardiomyocytes. Independent cohorts revealed context-dependent changes in ferroptosis driver and suppressor programs. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated macrophages induced cardiomyocyte injury, lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, decreased GPX4, and increased ACSL4. Macrophage STAT3 knockdown partially attenuated these changes, reduced inflammatory responses, and altered Cp expression. Fer-1 further alleviated conditioned-medium-induced injury. Consistent ferroptosis-related molecular alterations were observed in SCM mice.

CONCLUSION: Macrophage STAT3 signaling contributes to a paracrine inflammatory environment associated with ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury, linking inflammatory macrophages to myocardial injury in SCM.

articles.title: Germacrone inhibits podocyte pyroptosis in diabetic kidney disease by modulating ABCA1 expression.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a serious microvascular complication of diabetes with limited treatment strategies. Germacrone (Ger) has renoprotective properties, but its molecular targets and mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether Ger protects against DKD by modulating podocyte pyroptosis and explored the underlying mechanism. In vivo, diabetic db/db mice were treated with Ger, with benazepril as a positive control. The effects of Ger on DKD were evaluated by assessing biochemical indices and histopathology. Molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) were employed to assess potential target engagement between Ger and ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1). In vitro, ABCA1 was knocked down in high glucose (HG)-stimulated MPC5 cells, and the effects of Ger were evaluated using the Cell Counting Kit-8, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, flow cytometry, and Western blot. Ger reduced fasting blood glucose, improved renal function and alleviated renal pathological injury in db/db mice. Molecular docking, CETSA, and DARTS revealed potential target engagement between Ger and ABCA1. Ger increased ABCA1 mRNA and protein levels, enhanced cholesterol efflux, reduced proinflammatory factor release, and suppressed pyroptosis in db/db mice and HG-stimulated MPC5 cells. ABCA1 knockdown weakened the protective effects of Ger, whereas toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) inhibition partially reversed the adverse effects of ABCA1 knockdown. Ger alleviates DKD-associated podocyte injury by regulating ABCA1 expression and TLR4-associated pyroptosis, supporting its further evaluation as a therapeutic candidate for DKD.

articles.title: Timing of intratracheal administration of budesonide mixed with surfactant to prevent bronchopulmonary dysplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The aim of this study was to evaluate whether intratracheal budesonide mixed with surfactant prevents bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and whether timing contributes to heterogeneity. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and trial registries for randomised controlled trials of budesonide-surfactant versus surfactant alone. Random-effects meta-analyses yielded risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We assessed risk of bias with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. A post hoc subgroup analysis classified trials by whether treatment was restricted to within 4 h after birth or permitted after 4 h. We included 15 trials (3522 infants); 14 trials (3494 infants) reported BPD at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (BPD36). The overall analysis suggested a reduction in BPD36 (RR 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59-0.86; I2 = 68%), although heterogeneity was substantial. BPD36 was reduced in trials restricting treatment to within 4 h (RR 0.58; 95% CI, 0.46-0.72; eight trials; 1065 infants), but not in trials permitting later treatment (RR 0.98; 95% CI, 0.91-1.06; four trials; 2011 infants; P for subgroup difference < 0.00001). The composite outcome of BPD or death showed a similar pattern. Mortality and most other neonatal outcomes did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: In trials restricting treatment to within 4 h after birth, budesonide-surfactant therapy may reduce BPD36; however, this post hoc, trial-level finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect differences between earlier small and contemporary large trials. Current evidence does not support routine budesonide-surfactant therapy. A large prospective trial of early administration is needed to determine whether timing modifies benefit.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD42024547670).

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Earlier small trials suggested that budesonide mixed with surfactant reduces BPD, whereas recent large multicentre trials found little or no benefit. • The source of the marked heterogeneity among trials remains uncertain.

WHAT IS NEW: • Trials restricting treatment to within 4 h showed reductions in BPD36 and BPD or death, whereas trials permitting later treatment showed no benefit. • This post hoc association with timing may reflect study-level confounding and small-study effects and requires confirmation.

articles.title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

articles.title: Association of co-administration of neurokinin-1 receptor antagonists and dexamethasone with new-onset diabetes in patients receiving chemotherapy: a retrospective cross-sectional study using health claims database in Japan.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to optimize antiemetic strategies by evaluating the association of co-administration of neurokinin-1 receptor antagonist (NK1-RA) administration and dexamethasone on new-onset diabetes in patients receiving chemotherapy.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using the DeSC database and included patients aged ≥ 18 years with solid tumors who initiated parenteral anticancer agents and dexamethasone between April 2014 and March 2023. Patients with a history of diabetes or hematologic malignancies were excluded. The primary outcome was new-onset diabetes during the 2 months following the index month, defined by International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes or prescription data. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between co-administration of NK1-RA and dexamethasone and new-onset diabetes.

RESULTS: Among 71,539 eligible patients, 51.1% received NK1-RAs. Co-administration of NK1-RA and dexamethasone was significantly associated with an increased risk of new-onset diabetes (adjusted odds ratio: 1.43; 95% confidence interval: 1.31-1.55; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent results across different evaluation periods and outcome definitions.

CONCLUSION: Co-administration of NK1-RA and dexamethasone was associated with an increased risk of new-onset diabetes. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized safety signal and support the careful management of dexamethasone, as recommended by many clinical guidelines.

articles.title: Declaring generative AI use in neurology research: a call for specific and standardised reporting.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

articles.title: Proportionate antimicrobial use in pediatric end-of-life care: a narrative review and practical framework.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Antimicrobial prescribing in pediatric palliative care is frequent, emotionally charged, and clinically complex. In children approaching the end of life, antimicrobial therapy may offer symptom relief in selected circumstances, but it may also add procedural burden, adverse effects, and a risk of prolonging the dying process without improving comfort. The objective is to synthesize the limited pediatric evidence, distinguish it from adult palliative-care evidence and general stewardship guidance, and propose a practical operational framework for decision-making in pediatric end-of-life care. This study is a narrative review of the infectious-disease and palliative-care literature, with a targeted PubMed search and hand-searching of relevant reference lists and guidance documents. The review focused on symptom-oriented benefits, treatment-related burdens, the ethical principles of beneficence, distributive justice, and proportionality, antimicrobial stewardship, and the role of shared decision-making and clinical documentation in pediatric practice. The literature search was last updated in March 2026. For each major clinical proposition, we distinguished direct pediatric end-of-life evidence from adult palliative-care evidence, general pediatric infectious-disease or stewardship guidance, and the authors' reasoned recommendations. Available evidence suggests that antimicrobials may be proportionate when symptomatic benefit is plausible, perceptible, and aligned with the goals of care. However, benefits are inconsistent, pediatric evidence remains limited, and antimicrobial therapy is often prescribed empirically even when its palliative value is uncertain. Direct pediatric evidence is sparse and largely observational or descriptive. Across studies and guidelines, recurrent principles emerge: avoid automatic prescribing, define the goal of treatment, prefer the least burdensome option, document the rationale, and reassess within 48-72 h.

CONCLUSION: In pediatric end-of-life care, the key question is not simply whether an infection is present, but whether treating it is likely to meaningfully and proportionately improve the child's comfort. A structured framework that integrates ethics, antimicrobial stewardship, shared decision-making, and clear documentation may help clinicians move from reflexive prescribing to deliberate, proportionate decision-making in pediatric palliative care.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Direct pediatric evidence on antimicrobial use at the end of life is sparse,largely descriptive, and provides limited information on patient-centered symptomatic benefit.

WHAT IS NEW: • This narrative review explicitly separates pediatric evidence from adult extrapolation and general stewardship guidance and proposes an authorderived practical framework linking comfort goals, proportionality, child participation, early reassessment, and documentation.

articles.title: What are the palliative and end-of-life care needs and preferences of people with cancer from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds?: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Goal-concordant care is critical to supporting patients at the end of life (EOL), and palliative care is a key facet of this. The study aims to (1) synthesize the evidence available on the EOL and palliative care (PC) needs and preferences of people with cancer from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds and (2) explore what elements of service provision are facilitators or barriers to service engagement and goal-concordant care.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted. The search strategy was applied to five electronic databases to identify relevant articles published between January 2003 and September 2025. Quality assessment was performed using the Quality Assessment for Diverse Studies (QuADS) tool. A narrative synthesis was led by one reviewer with the support of a wider team.

RESULTS: A total of 6017 titles were identified. After duplicate removal and screening, 20 studies were included in the review. Fourteen studies reported EOL care and six reported PC encounters. People from CALD backgrounds identified the following needs: (1) maintaining positivity, (2) maintaining decision-making autonomy, (3) involving family/caregivers in decision-making, and (4) trust in the provider-patient relationship. Factors which influenced patient engagement and care preferences were (1) family involvement, (2) faith/spirituality, and (3) understanding of services.

CONCLUSION: This review illustrates the distinct care complexities for patients from CALD backgrounds. These findings underscore the importance of avoiding cultural generalizations and involving consumers in system planning. System-level changes, including community consultation, and improved access to culturally/linguistically appropriate resources are needed to support service engagement.

articles.title: Methyl aminolevulinate-PpIX mediated fluorescence-guided mapping of high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a pilot prospective clinical trial (PhotoDiVin).
articles.abstract: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. We conducted a pilot clinical study to assess the fluorescence-based cartography of VIN lesions using methyl aminolevulinate (m-ALA), which is a prodrug of the fluorophore protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). A prospective, single-center, single-arm clinical trial included 17 women with histologically confirmed high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN or vHSIL). Following topical methyl aminolevulinate application, fluorescence-guided examination under 405-nm light was performed. Targeted biopsies from fluorescent and non-fluorescent areas were compared with histopathology to assess concordance and the ability of fluorescence to accurately identify high-grade lesions. Among 34 biopsies, histopathological findings were concordant with fluorescence in 91% of cases. The procedure correctly identified intraepithelial neoplasia areas in 14 patients, yielding a success rate of 82% (95%CI 56-96%). Sensitivity and specificity were 93% (95%CI 68-100%) and 89% (95%CI 67-99%), respectively. The tolerance of the procedure was excellent with no pain and no side effects neither after cream application nor after illumination. This pilot study suggests that fluorescence imaging is a workable technique to mark VIN lesions with m-ALA cream. Further studies are needed to improve the reproducibility and ease of use of this method.

articles.title: Single-cell directional sensing at ultra-low chemoattractant concentrations from extreme first-passage events.
articles.abstract: We investigate single-cell directional sensing from diffusing chemoattractant signals released by a localized source. We focus on the low-concentration regime in which receptor activity is discrete and cellular decisions are made on timescales far shorter than those required for steady-state concentration profiles or receptor saturation to emerge. We derive analytic expressions for the joint distribution of receptor binding times and binding locations, conditional on the position of the source. We show that early binding events carry disproportionately more information about source directionality than later arrivals. Motivated by this observation, we propose and analyze several source-localization estimates that exploit early receptor binding statistics. For a directional estimate formed from an equally weighted average of the earliest impacts, we demonstrate that this estimate is accurate even from a small number of impacts, and derive an expression for the number of binding events that minimizes the mean squared error. Our results demonstrate that cells possess sufficient information to rapidly and accurately infer the directionality of sparse signals from a localized source through a small number of discrete receptor engagements, well before a steady-state gradient has been established.

articles.title: Effect of sampling on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks.
articles.abstract: Random walks are commonly used to model movement throughout the sciences, from the motion of particles and molecules to the observed behaviour of animals and crowds. The correlated random walk, which assumes a level of persistence between movement directions, has become ubiquitous in the analysis and modelling of movement in recent times. Whilst many properties of the correlated random walk are known, there are still many which are not fully understood and, therefore, under-utilised in movement data analysis. Here we consider the effect that sub-sampling has on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks. Our work demonstrates the connection between the distributions of turning angles and step-lengths that characterise a correlated random walk, along with the resulting distributions found after sub-sampling. We provide examples for where this approach could aid in movement analysis as well as determining future ways the work could be extended.

articles.title: Erythrocyte phosphatidylserine externalization shows greater discriminatory performance than red cell distribution width for early recurrence or progression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Red cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with adverse outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but whether this association reflects an HCC-associated erythrocyte injury phenotype remains unclear. We investigated whether phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization identifies an HCC-associated erythrocyte injury phenotype and is associated with tumor burden and early recurrence or progression.

METHODS: This prospective two-center clinical study included 97 patients with newly diagnosed HCC, 30 healthy donors, 13 patients with chronic hepatitis B, and 17 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis as disease controls. Erythrocyte injury phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, metabolomics, and proteomics. Findings were examined in orthotopic HCC mouse models and erythrocyte-HCC co-culture systems.

RESULTS: PS externalization was elevated in patients with HCC and correlated with tumor diameter, multiplicity, metastasis, and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage. HCC also showed higher PS levels than chronic hepatitis B and HBV-related cirrhosis controls. Higher PS externalization remained independently associated with early recurrence or progression within 6 months after adjustment for maximum tumor diameter, tumor number, and lymph-node and/or distant metastasis (OR = 1.382; 95% CI 1.112-1.717; P = 0.004). PS showed greater discriminatory performance than RDW-CV (AUC 0.804 versus 0.642; paired DeLong P = 0.003); bootstrap internal validation of the primary multivariable model yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.780. Spatial analyses revealed progressive erythrocyte injury from peripheral blood to adjacent non-tumor tissue to primary tumor. In orthotopic HCC-bearing mice, PS externalization preceded RDW elevation. Direct co-culture with HCC cells induced glutathione depletion and oxidative membrane injury, which were attenuated by N-acetylcysteine and reproduced by glutathione synthesis inhibition. Multi-omics analyses revealed alterations in pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-NADPH/glutathione metabolism and membrane-skeletal proteins.

CONCLUSIONS: PS externalization identifies an HCC-associated erythrocyte injury phenotype and is a candidate marker for 6-month recurrence or progression. Experimental findings support a functional contribution of glutathione depletion to membrane injury, accompanied by PPP-NADPH-related metabolic and membrane-skeletal alterations.

articles.title: Peritoneal dialysis in the treatment of neonatal acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) remains a mainstay of kidney replacement therapy (KRT) for neonatal acute kidney injury (AKI), despite recent advances in extracorporeal technologies. Its widespread use is supported by technical simplicity, good hemodynamic tolerance, avoidance of vascular access and systemic anticoagulation, and broad applicability across both high- and low-resource settings. However, neonatal PD presents unique anatomical, physiological, and technical challenges that are only partially addressed in current pediatric guidelines. As a result, many aspects of its management remain informed by extrapolation from older pediatric populations and clinical experience. This educational review provides a practical, evidence-based approach to the management of acute PD in neonates with AKI, integrating available evidence with bedside considerations to guide clinical practice while identifying areas requiring further neonatal-specific research.

articles.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.

METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID).

RESULTS: SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles.

CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

articles.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI.

MAIN TEXT: Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent.

CONCLUSIONS: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes.

HIGHLIGHTS: VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.

articles.title: Streptococcus oralis induces platelet aggregation through coordinated GPIbα and FcγRIIA signalling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Streptococcus oralis is the most prevalent viridans group streptococcus associated with infective endocarditis (IE), yet the platelet activation mechanisms that underpin its pathogenicity remain poorly defined. Platelet-bacterium interactions are central to vegetation formation, but the relative contributions of direct adhesion and antibody-dependent signaling in S. oralis-induced platelet aggregation are unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To define the molecular mechanisms by which S. oralis induces platelet activation and aggregation, and to determine how bacterial adhesins and host factors cooperate to drive this response.

METHODS: Platelet aggregation and dense granule secretion were assessed using light transmission aggregometry and ATP release assays in platelet-rich plasma and washed platelets. An IE isolate of S. oralis and isogenic mutants lacking functional Fap1 were used alongside pharmacological and antibody-based inhibition of platelet receptors and signaling pathways.

RESULTS: S. oralis ATCC 10557 induced robust platelet aggregation with a characteristic lag phase and strong dense granule release. Aggregation required integrin αIIbβ3 signaling and was abolished by inhibition of glycoprotein Ibα (GPIbα) or FcγRIIA. Loss of the serine-rich repeat protein Fap1, or mutation of its conserved sialic acid-binding motif, abrogated platelet aggregation. While most donors required a plasma component for aggregation, supplementation of washed platelets with human IgG fully restored aggregation in a dose-dependent manner. Importantly, IgG was unable to bypass the requirement for Fap1-GPIbα interaction, indicating that direct bacterial adhesion is an essential initiating step that enables antibody-dependent FcγRIIA signaling. Substantial inter-individual variability was observed in aggregation kinetics and IgG dependence.

CONCLUSIONS: S. oralis induces platelet aggregation through a dual, non-redundant mechanism requiring Fap1-mediated engagement of GPIbα and IgG-dependent FcγRIIA signaling. This cooperative pathway drives potent platelet activation and exhibits marked host-dependent variability. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into early events in IE pathogenesis and highlight platelet-bacterium interactions as potential targets for risk stratification and therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV ameliorates combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome by inhibiting the activation of the STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Astragaloside IV (As-IV) has demonstrated therapeutic potential for allergic rhinitis and asthma. However, a systematic investigation is lacking. This study was aimed at systematically elucidating the molecular mechanisms of As-IV in treating combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome (CARAS) through network pharmacology combined with RNA sequencing analysis. A BALB/c mouse model of CARAS was established using ovalbumin. Nasal and bronchopulmonary allergic symptoms were recorded. Histopathological changes in the respiratory tract were assessed via H&E, PAS, and Masson staining. Network pharmacology and lung RNA sequencing were systematically employed to predict potential molecular mechanisms. WB, IF, and IHC were used to validate the activation of the STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways, as well as the expression of epithelial barrier and mesenchymal components. Finally, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the binding affinity of As-IV with key target proteins. As-IV alleviated allergic symptoms, improved histopathological morphology, and reduced eosinophil and Th2 cell infiltration. Furthermore, As-IV markedly suppressed the activation of STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways, mitigated epithelial barrier damage, and decreased mesenchymal component expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that As-IV may potentially interact with STAT6 and AKT, suggesting its ability to modulate their conformations and biological activities. As-IV attenuates type 2 inflammation and epithelial barrier injury in the respiratory tract by inhibiting the STAT6/GATA3/IL-4 and PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathways. This study is the first to systematically unravel and validate the molecular mechanisms of As-IV in CARAS through integrated network pharmacology and RNA sequencing analysis, providing a robust scientific basis for its therapeutic application.

articles.title: Melatonin attenuates acute kidney injury in rats: modulation of the p53-PUMA/Bcl-2-Bax apoptotic signaling axis.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is characterized by oxidative stress-mediated tubular damage and activation of apoptosis-related signaling pathways. This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effect of melatonin on renal injury, focusing on histopathological alterations, apoptosis-related gene expression, and renal function parameters in an experimental AKI model. Twenty-eight rats were randomly assigned to four groups: Control, AKI, AKI + Solvent (1% ethanol), and AKI + Melatonin (20 mg/kg, intraperitoneal). AKI was induced by 45 min of renal ischemia followed by 24 h of reperfusion. At the end of the experimental period, kidney tissues were collected for histopathological evaluation using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Apoptosis-related proteins (p53, PUMA, NOXA, Bax, and Bcl-2) were analyzed by immunofluorescence, and the expression levels of the corresponding genes were quantified using real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Renal function was assessed by measuring serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels. AKI induced marked histopathological damage compared with the Control group (p < 0.001), whereas melatonin treatment significantly attenuated tissue injury. Immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated increased positive cell index (PCI) values for p53, PUMA, and Bax alongside decreased Bcl-2 PCI in the AKI group (p < 0.05), while NOXA PCI remained unchanged (p > 0.05). Notably, melatonin administration resulted in a statistically significant reduction in the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio compared to the untreated AKI group (p < 0.05), indicating a shift toward cellular survival at the protein level. No statistically significant differences were detected in apoptotic gene expression at the mRNA level. Serum creatinine levels increased significantly in the AKI group (p < 0.001). Melatonin treatment is associated with a modulation of key components within the p53-PUMA/Bcl-2-Bax apoptotic signaling axis in renal tissue following ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: A synbiotic nanoemulsion modulates metabolic dysfunction and organ functioning in high-fat diet-induced obese mice.
articles.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity is associated with metabolic disturbance and structural changes in the intestine, liver, kidney, and adipose tissue. This study evaluated the effects of a co-formulated nanoemulsion containing silk fibroin (a proposed prebiotic) and Lactobacillus rhamnosus (a probiotic), referred to here as a synbiotic nanoemulsion, in HFD-induced obese mice. A synbiotic nanoemulsion was prepared using a high-energy method and characterized by UV-visible spectroscopy and FTIR analysis. Forty-eight male mice were randomly divided into eight groups (n = 6) and fed different diet for 16 weeks. Body weight was recorded weekly, following biochemical, histological, and histomorphometric analysis. Compared with the normal diet group (31.82 ± 1.18 g), HFD-fed mice showed a significant increase in body weight (48.7 ± 0.07 g) and severe dyslipidemia, evidenced by elevated total cholesterol (222-276.5 mg/dL), triglycerides (195-289.5 mg/dL), and low-density lipoprotein (104.8-140 mg/dL), with reduced high-density lipoprotein levels (9-23 mg/dL). Synbiotic supplementation significantly reduced blood urea nitrogen (8-10 mg/dL), serum creatinine (0.55-1.0 mg/dL), alanine aminotransferase (28-39 U/L), and aspartate aminotransferase (129-141 U/L). Furthermore, systemic inflammation was also reduced reflected by lowered TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, alongside increased IL-10 levels as compared to HFD group. Histological and histomorphometric analysis showed improved organ architecture in the synbiotic-treated group, with several measurements close to those of the normal diet group. In this HFD mouse model, the fibroin-L. rhamnosus nanoemulsion was associated with lower body weight, improved lipid profile, liver, kidney, and inflammatory markers, and improved tissue morphology.
