These findings support further study of the formulation. The design does not allow conclusions about synergy, nanoemulsion-specific delivery effects or mechanisms.

articles.title: Mental Health of Children with Fontan Circulation: Associations with Maternal Psychopathology and Parenting Behavior.
articles.abstract: Children with Fontan circulation face substantial long-term psychosocial challenges. Parental mental health and parenting behavior are known to influence psychosocial outcomes in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), yet data specific for Fontan families are scarce. This cross-sectional controlled study examined child psychopathology in relation to maternal psychopathology and parenting behavior. 31 mothers and their children with Fontan circulation (aged 4-16 years) were compared with a sex-, age- and socioeconomic status (SES)- matched control group. Standardized maternal self-report questionnaires assessed child psychopathology, maternal psychopathology, and parenting behavior. Children with Fontan circulation showed significantly higher psychopathology than controls (F (1,58) = 6.38, p = .014, ηp² = 0.10). No group differences were found in maternal psychopathology or parenting behavior (all p > .24). No Group × Moderator interaction effects emerged (all p > .35). Significant main effects were observed for maternal total psychopathology, anxiety, and depression (F(1,58) = 13.10, p < .001, ηp² = 0.19; F(1,58) = 9.94, p = .003, ηp² = 0.15; F(1,58) = 11.00, p = .002, ηp²= 0.16), and inconsistent parenting behavior (F(1,58) = 19.20, p < .001, ηp² = 0.26), associated with higher child psychopathology across groups, underscoring the need for family-focused support in the Fontan population.

articles.title: Opportunistic MRI assessment of skeletal muscle mass in children and adults with Fontan circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children and adults with Fontan circulation are vulnerable to reduced skeletal muscle mass because of altered Fontan physiology, exercise limitation, nutritional challenges, and chronic liver disease. Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed for Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) surveillance provides an opportunity to assess muscle mass without additional imaging.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the frequency of imaging-defined low skeletal muscle mass on clinically acquired abdominal MRI examinations in children and adults with Fontan circulation and, secondarily, to explore associations with available clinical and imaging markers related to FALD.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included individuals with Fontan circulation who underwent abdominal MRI for FALD surveillance. Pediatric total psoas area and adult total skeletal muscle index were measured using age-appropriate published approaches and analyzed separately. Continuous variables were summarized with medians and interquartile ranges and explored using Spearman correlations and Mann-Whitney U tests. Sparse cardiac and outcome data were treated descriptively.

RESULTS: The study included 124 individuals (78 male; 63%), including 57 children (age range 3.2-17.4 years, median=14.1) and 67 adults (age range 18.1-43.7 years, median=22.3). Imaging-defined low muscle mass was present in 17/57 children (30%) and 14/67 adults (21%) using pediatric- and adult-specific measurement approaches. Exploratory analyses did not identify a consistent pattern linking low muscle mass with the available FALD-related measures including liver stiffness measurement, liver biochemistries or liver scoring systems. Several comparisons including ejection fractions and aortopulmonary collateral flow were limited by missing data, small subgroups, and few outcome events.

CONCLUSION: Clinically acquired liver MRI examinations can be repurposed to identify imaging-defined low muscle mass in individuals with Fontan circulation. The frequency observed in both age groups supports prospective evaluation of standardized MRI measurements combined with muscle function, exercise capacity, and longitudinal outcomes.

articles.title: Dental age with four radiographic methods in subjects with cleft lip and palate: a study of cases and controls.
articles.journal: European archives of paediatric dentistry : official journal of the European Academy of Paediatric Dentistry
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of the present study was to establish the relationship between dental age (DA) and chronological age (CA) in children with and without a non-syndromic cleft lip and palate (NSCLP) and to determine differences in the dental development of teeth adjacent to the cleft.

STUDY DESIGN: Cases and controls.

METHODS: A study of cases (146) and controls (171) matched by sex and age (aged between 6 and 12 years) was carried out. Cases were defined as individuals with NSCLP. Dental age was determined from panoramic radiographs using four methods: Willems, Demirjian, Haavikko and Nolla.

STATISTICS: A paired t test supplemented with Mann-Whitney test was performed to compare the means of the previously established dental ages.

RESULTS: For the control group, three of the four methods used showed a significant overestimation of DA when compared to CA; only Haavikko's method showed agreement between DA and CA. For the case group, it was found that the Haavikko's method presented a lower DA to CA in all phenotypes of individuals with NSCLP, while with Nolla's method, no statistical differences were found for any of the case groups and Demirjian method overestimated the DA for all the cleft phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: In individuals with NSCLP, the Haavikko method (which showed no differences with chronological age in controls) shows a decrease in dental age, suggesting a delay in dental development in this population. The maxillary left lateral incisor was the tooth with the greatest development delay in subjects with unilateral NSCLP.

articles.title: Gut microbiota as a key player in diabetes mellitus: mechanisms, dysbiosis, and emerging interventions.
articles.abstract: The gut microbiome has emerged as a critical regulator of metabolic and immune homeostasis, with significant implications for diabetes mellitus. This narrative review synthesizes findings from selected landmark original investigations published from 2000 to 2026, examining the role of the gut microbiome in both type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). As a narrative rather than a systematic review, this synthesis does not follow a registered protocol or an exhaustive, reproducible search strategy. Observational studies frequently report dysbiosis, characterized by reduced microbial diversity and altered taxa, as a feature of both prediabetes and diabetes, correlating with poor glycemic control and complications, although the specific taxa and dysbiotic signatures implicated vary across geographically and ethnically distinct populations, indicating that dysbiosis is not a uniform, population-invariant hallmark of disease. Mechanistic studies highlight pathways such as short-chain fatty acid production, immune modulation, and gut barrier integrity, which mediate microbial effects on insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism, with short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) signaling and gut barrier integrity identified as the most significant pathways driving these effects. Interventional approaches, including probiotics, prebiotics, dietary modifications, fasting, exercise, and bariatric surgery, show preliminary, proof-of-concept potential to reshape the microbiome and improve diabetic outcomes, although none of these interventions has yet been validated in large-scale, adequately powered, multi-center randomized controlled trials with hard clinical endpoints, and none should be regarded as an established treatment. Notably, T1D research emphasizes autoimmune interactions, while T2D focuses on metabolic dysfunction. Despite advances, challenges like establishing causality and addressing inter-individual variability persist. This review underscores the microbiome's therapeutic promise pending confirmation in the larger trials outlined above, and advocates for personalized, multi-omics-driven strategies to enhance diabetes management.

articles.title: PhysioXGluNet: a physiology-informed network architecture with attributable branches for explainable blood glucose prediction.
articles.abstract: For people with type 1 diabetes (T1D), poor management of blood glucose (BG) can lead to hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, which are the main culprits of health risks. Blood glucose prediction plays a crucial role in BG management. Patients can understand future BG change trends and take actions in advance to maintain euglycemia. Multivariate prediction models based on deep learning have achieved outstanding performance, but insufficient consideration of physiological consistency and physiological explainability has led to a lack of clinical confidence. To address this, we propose a novel physiology-informed network architecture with attributable branches, named PhysioXGluNet, which structurally integrates domain knowledge and individual data. To ensure physiological consistency, we determine the branch composition according to the physiological compartment model and also design the physiology-informed recurrent neural network and physiology-informed composite loss. To enhance physiological explainability, PhysioXGluNet not only outputs future BG levels but also provides the net BG changes caused by each input variable via corresponding attributable branch, allowing a clear traceability of the dominant factors at each time step driving future BG changes. PhysioXGluNet outperforms baseline models in both numerical and clinical metrics when evaluated on the real-world dataset. PhysioXGluNet has the potential to assist clinical decision-making in T1D BG management for this studied cohort.

articles.title: Altered centrality and connectivity in motor networks following Xingnao Kaiqiao acupuncture for acute ischemic stroke: a randomized controlled, exploratory fMRI study.
articles.abstract: Xingnao Kaiqiao (XNKQ) acupuncture is recommended as an adjunctive intervention for motor dysfunction after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet its neuroplastic mechanisms remain unclear. In this randomized, exploratory study, 28 AIS patients were randomly assigned to XNKQ acupuncture plus medication (n = 14) or medication-only (n = 14) to receive 10 sessions of treatment over 14 days. Clinical assessments and resting-state fMRI scanning were conducted before and after the intervention, with brain reorganization analyzed using voxel-wise degree centrality (DC) and seed-based functional connectivity (FC). We found that better recovery in the XNKQ group, reflected by more improvements in NIHSS, total and upper-extremity FMA scores, was correlated with reduced DC in the ipsilesional primary motor cortex (iM1) concurrent with attenuated FC to the contralesional supplementary motor area (cSMA), alongside increased DC in the bilateral SMA and preserved FC between SMA and cerebellar regions. Further exploratory mediation analysis suggested that change in iM1-cSMA FC potentially mediated the relationship between iM1 DC normalization and motor recovery. These preliminary findings suggest that XNKQ acupuncture may facilitate early motor recovery after AIS through normalization of ipsilesional M1 hub centrality and modulation of M1-SMA cross-hemispheric connectivity, providing candidate network markers for acupuncture-associated neuroplasticity.

articles.title: Highlights of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention Studies Presented at the 2026 European Society of Cardiology Conference.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes key cardiovascular disease prevention studies presented at the 2026 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress, highlighting new evidence in lipid management, cardiovascular risk assessment, blood pressure control, and vaccination.

RECENT FINDINGS: Several studies addressed persistent gaps in lipid management and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease prevention. STAREE showed that atorvastatin reduced major cardiovascular events in adults aged 70 years and older without established cardiovascular disease, although it did not significantly improve disability-free survival. The SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 trials showed that plozasiran produced substantial and sustained triglyceride reductions and reduced acute pancreatitis events in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia. VICTORION-Challenge demonstrated greater LDL-C reduction and target attainment with inclisiran compared with bempedoic acid in high- and very-high-risk patients receiving background statin therapy. In patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, VSA003 substantially lowered LDL-C and several other atherogenic lipoproteins by inhibiting ANGPTL3. Two studies examined imaging-based approaches to preventive therapy: RESPECT2 showed that coronary computed tomography angiography-guided lipid management improved adherence compared with conventional risk-score-based treatment, while CorCal found that coronary artery calcium-guided statin recommendations reduced the number of patients selected for treatment and were associated with greater LDL-C lowering and higher reported adherence, although noninferiority for cardiovascular events was not established. Beyond lipid management, long-term follow-up of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project showed that intensive blood pressure management led by non-physician healthcare providers reduced dementia and cognitive impairment. TIMER demonstrated sustained LDL-C lowering with once-monthly ticalicibart in patients with nonfamilial hypercholesterolemia receiving background statin therapy, while TRANQUILITY demonstrated sustained reductions in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with the interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibitor pacibekitug in patients with chronic kidney disease. DAN-RSV demonstrated that RSVpreF vaccination reduced RSV-related respiratory and cardiorespiratory hospitalizations across two seasons. Studies presented at ESC 2026 broadened the evidence base for cardiovascular prevention across pharmacologic therapy, imaging-guided risk assessment, blood pressure management, and vaccination.

articles.title: Improving Patient Safety Through Medication Reconciliation at Care Transitions: A Mixed Methods Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medication reconciliation (MedRec) is a cornerstone patient safety practice during care transitions. However, evidence regarding the specific implementation strategies that contribute to its effectiveness remains limited. This study sought to elucidate the essential ingredients of a Medication Reconciliation Standard Operating Protocol (MedRec SOP) and their impact on enhancing patient safety outcomes compared to usual care.

METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase were searched for studies (January 2000-May 2024) assessing MedRec interventions compared to usual care. Data on study design, MedRec SOP components, and patient safety outcomes were extracted. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for quantitative synthesis.

RESULTS: From 7209 screened records, 70 studies were included, describing 20 distinct MedRec SOP ingredients. Meta-analysis demonstrated that MedRec significantly reduced medication discrepancies (RR = 0.39, 95% CI 0.28-0.53), adverse drug events/reactions (RR = 0.61, 95% CI 0.47-0.79), 30-day all-cause readmissions (RR = 0.73, 95% CI 0.68-0.78), emergency department visits (RR = 0.60, 95% CI 0.52-0.68), and drug-related readmissions (RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.31-0.84). Subgroup analyses identified pharmacist-led interventions and MedRec performed at hospital admission as particularly effective strategies. The SOP component "MedRec on admission" showed the highest effective ratio (ER = 9.40).

CONCLUSIONS: Our systematic review supports the implementation of MedRec programs that include some components aimed at optimizing the MedRec intervention design. MedRec is a promising implementation strategy to improve patient safety and can be incorporated into the healthcare system.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD42024491225.

articles.title: Automated insulin delivery in older adults with type 1 diabetes: evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems have significantly improved the management of type 1 diabetes (T1D), leading to better glycemic control and reduced hypoglycemia. However, older adults (≥ 65 years) remain underrepresented in clinical trials, and evidence specific to this population is limited.

DESIGN AND PATIENTS: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the efficacy, safety, and usability of AID systems in older adults (≥ 65 years) with T1D. A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE/PubMed was conducted using the PICO framework to identify relevant RCTs, observational studies, and systematic reviews, supplemented by literature studies on cognitive, functional, and psychosocial factors impacting technology adoption.

RESULTS: While data from randomized trials and meta-analyses in the general population consistently demonstrate improvements in time in range (TIR, 70-180 mg/dL) and reductions in hypoglycemia, evidence in older adults is still emerging. Frail individuals and those with multiple comorbidities are often underrepresented or excluded from current studies. Nevertheless, the available evidence suggests that many of these benefits are also maintained in older populations, particularly regarding hypoglycemia reduction. At the same time, factors such as cognitive impairment, functional limitations, caregiver dependence, and reduced digital literacy may affect the adoption and effective use of these technologies.

CONCLUSIONS: AID systems appear effective and generally safe in selected older adults, with benefits in glycemic control and hypoglycemia reduction. However, given the marked heterogeneity of this population, further studies are needed to better define their role and applicability in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Radiological characterization across the spectrum of primary aldosteronism.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To define adrenal imaging phenotypes across primary aldosteronism (PA), low-renin hypertension (LRH), normal-renin hypertension (NRH) and controls.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 196 patients evaluated for suspected PA between January 2024 and February 2025. Plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) was measured by LC-MS/MS. Diagnosis and subtype evaluation of PA was conducted according to Endocrine Society Guidelines (n=95). Individuals who did not meet predefined criteria for PA were further categorized as LRH (n=59) or NRH (n=42) based on the direct renin concentration and aldosterone-to-renin-ratio. Age- and sex-matched individuals without known hypertension served as controls (n=50). Imaging features on CT and MRI, independently and blindly segmented by two radiologists, were categorized in diffuse adrenal enlargement, micronodules (< 10 mm), adenoma/indeterminate lesions (≥ 10 mm), and nodular hyperplasia.

RESULTS: Median age was highest in PA (50.0 years), followed by LRH (48.0), and NRH (44.0) (p = 0.049). Sex distribution showed female predominance in NRH (81.0%) and LRH (78.0%) compared to PA (49.5%) (p <0.001). Imaging pathologies were rare in controls (2.0%) and increasingly prevalent from NRH (14.3%) to LRH (35.6%) and PA (42.1%) (p < 0.001). The same difference held for lesions ≥10 mm (p < 0.001). Bilateral lesions and nodular hyperplasia occurred exclusively in PA and LRH. Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that the association between diagnostic group and adrenal imaging pathologies was independent of age, sex, BMI, and imaging modality.

CONCLUSION: These exploratory findings support LRH as a potential intermediate phenotype within the spectrum of aldosterone excess despite not fulfilling classical PA criteria.

articles.title: Impact of Documentation Aids on the Inclusion of Salient Left-Ventricular Late Gadolinium Enhancement Characteristics in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging Impressions.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is a key diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM). However, the completeness of LGE reporting in routine CMR impressions remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to evaluate the impact of large language model (LLM)-assisted reporting on the consistency of LGE pattern, distribution, and severity documentation in CMR impressions for ICM and NICM. We analyzed 828 unstructured (1990-2023) and 400 structured (2024-2025) CMR reports to identify documentation of LGE pattern, distribution, and severity. A Llama 3 language model fine-tuned on 27,000 structured CMR reports was used to generate 9650 CMR impressions; LGE attributes were extracted using an LLM judge. LLM reporting behavior was further assessed using quantized low-rank adaptation adapters trained on structured and unstructured impressions. Structured reporting captured LGE pattern more frequently than unstructured reporting overall (85.5% vs. 61.0%, p = 9.60 × 10-7) and for ICM (90.0% vs. 69.4%, p = 0.005). LLM-generated impressions demonstrated more frequent reporting of LGE distribution (75.3%) and severity (70.9%) versus structured and unstructured reports (p < 0.001). Fine-tuning with an adapter trained on unstructured impressions significantly improved reporting of all three LGE attributes. Structured reporting improved LGE pattern documentation, but gaps in LGE distribution and severity documentation persisted across human report formats. LLM-generated impressions achieved broader attribute coverage for LGE distribution and severity. Fine-tuning on unstructured data improved model performance, suggesting that passive augmentation with data capturing the documentation styles of multiple providers may help to address reporting gaps.

articles.title: Robot-assisted minimally invasive versus conventional open transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion for lumbar degenerative disease: a prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Robotic guidance may improve pedicle screw placement during minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (MIS-TLIF), but its clinical value remains uncertain. In this prospective, single-center, assessor-blinded trial, 128 patients were randomly assigned in a prespecified 1:3 ratio to robot-assisted MIS-TLIF (n = 32) or conventional fluoroscopy-guided open TLIF (n = 96) using an independent statistician's computer-generated sequence. The primary outcome was the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) at 2 weeks. Technical, perioperative, and radiographic outcomes were assessed through 18 months; later assessments were exploratory.At 2 weeks, ODI favored robotic assistance (28.25 ± 6.64 vs 31.52 ± 6.55; mean difference, -3.27; 95% confidence interval, -5.98 to -0.56; P = 0.019), but was below the 10-point sample-size target and nonsignificant at 3 months. Robotic assistance favored grade A screw placement (98.9% vs 94.5%; P = 0.037) and reduced intraoperative adjustment (2.8% vs 7.3%; P = 0.030); facet joint violation and reoperation did not differ significantly. Operative time was longer, whereas blood loss, ambulation, drain removal, and hospital stay favored robotic assistance. Fusion rates and adjacent-segment disc height were similar. Multifidus cross-sectional area was greater with robotic assistance at 12 and 18 months in patients with evaluable imaging. Robot-assisted MIS-TLIF was associated with earlier recovery, higher screw accuracy, and greater postoperative multifidus cross-sectional area, but longer operative time without demonstrated mid-term clinical or fusion benefits. Larger multicenter trials are warranted. Trial Registration:Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400082553.

articles.title: Quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly reveals a non-linear association with 30-day mortality in sepsis: a proof-of-concept pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct, cell-resolved quantification of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in clinical patients has not been feasible. Previous studies have relied on indirect surrogates such as downstream cytokines, which are influenced by inflammasome-independent pathways and systemic clearance kinetics, potentially explaining the inconsistent prognostic findings reported in the literature. We applied a proximity ligation assay (PLA) to directly visualise NLRP3-caspase-1 complex formation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of septic patients, providing a cell-specific, in situ readout of inflammasome assembly at the single-cell level.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicentre proof-of-concept pilot study, 78 patients fulfilling Sepsis-3 criteria were enrolled across three university hospitals. The PLA was validated in THP-1-derived macrophages against established readouts of canonical inflammasome activation prior to clinical application. Patients were stratified into low (n = 28), intermediate (n = 23), and high (n = 27) NLRP3 inflammasome activity groups.

RESULTS: Median age was 64 years (IQR: 56-78), 63% were male, and median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 8 (IQR: 4-12). Baseline characteristics, disease severity scores, and routine inflammatory biomarkers did not differ across activity groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a non-linear pattern of 30-day survival, with the most favourable outcomes in the intermediate activity group. Both low and high activity were associated with increased mortality (log-rank p = 0.003). In adjusted Cox regression, low inflammasome activity (HR 7.88, 95% CI 1.79-34.65; p = 0.006) and high inflammasome activity (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.01-19.88; p = 0.048) remained associated with 30-day mortality. Modelling PLA activity as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines confirmed a significant non-linear association with 30-day mortality, independent of the tertile-based categorisation (p for non-linearity = 0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept pilot study demonstrates that direct in situ quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly is feasible in septic patients and reveals a non-linear association with 30-day survival. These findings indicate that PLA-based profiling captures immune heterogeneity beyond routine inflammatory biomarkers. Larger independent cohorts are needed to validate these findings before clinical application or patient stratification can be considered.

articles.title: 24-hour risk updating for major ICU complications after severe trauma: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Conventional trauma prognostic models rely primarily on admission data and cannot account for subsequent physiological response to treatment. We evaluated whether routinely collected physiological information available at 24 h provides incremental prognostic information for major intensive care unit (ICU) complications in severely injured patients.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort of adults with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score [ISS] ≥ 15) admitted to the ICU between January 2024 and April 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of major respiratory, hemodynamic, renal, or septic complications during the ICU course. TRISS was compared with an admission ridge model incorporating ISS, Glasgow Coma Scale, hemoglobin, lactate, and international normalized ratio, and a 24-h updated ridge model additionally incorporating 24-h lactate and change in creatinine. Performance was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Among 109 patients, median ISS was 29 (IQR 20-38), and 73 (67.0%) developed major ICU complications. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 for TRISS, 0.873 for the admission model, and 0.887 for the 24-h updated model; Brier scores were 0.178, 0.140, and 0.131. Compared with the admission model, the 24-h updated model improved performance (ΔAUC 0.016, 95% bootstrap interval 0.004-0.030; ΔBrier - 0.010, - 0.017 to - 0.005). Twenty-four-hour lactate and creatinine change were the strongest contributors to the update.

CONCLUSION: In severely injured ICU patients, incorporating physiological evolution during the first 24 h refined admission-based prognostic assessment. Lactate and creatinine trajectories provided incremental information for major ICU complications during the ICU course. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Marine-derived quorum sensing inhibition as an anti-virulence strategy against biofilm formation and antibiotic tolerance in Aeromonas hydrophila.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biofilm formation by Aeromonas hydrophila complicates infection control and is associated with reduced antibiotic susceptibility. Seaweed metabolites may interfere with quorum sensing, offering potential antivirulence approaches. This study compared three seaweed extracts for antibacterial, antibiofilm, and quorum sensing inhibitory activities.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Representative compounds reported from Ecklonia cava, Codium fragile, and Grateloupia elliptica were docked against AhyR. Biological assays assessed environmental effects on biofilm formation, antibiotic susceptibility, and extract effects on biofilms and swarming in A. hydrophila, alongside violacein inhibition in Chromobacterium violaceum. Biofilm biomass was quantified by crystal violet staining. Gene expression was examined by quantitative real-time PCR after seven days of repeated exposure to extracts at half the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC). Sub-inhibitory florfenicol exposure enhanced biofilm formation, particularly at 35 °C; biofilm biomass peaked at 1% NaCl in salinity assays. Florfenicol and amoxicillin MICs were 128-fold and eightfold higher in biofilm-derived cells than in planktonic cells, respectively. Docking predicted possible AhyR interactions. E. cava showed the strongest antibacterial and antibiofilm activities and swarming inhibition. G. elliptica produced the largest violacein inhibition zone at half MIC (14.13 ± 1.30 mm) and reduced luxS, hcp, recA, rpoS, ompA, and acrB expression after repeated exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: The extracts showed distinct activity profiles, with E. cava exhibiting the strongest antibiofilm effects and G. elliptica the strongest quorum sensing inhibition. G. elliptica warrants further investigation as an antivirulence candidate. Its active constituents and direct effects on AhyR require validation.

articles.title: AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance with ABC-structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms after gastrointestinal cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative nutritional management is critical for gastrointestinal cancer surgery patients, yet discharge advice is often standardized and lacks individualization. Whether an AI-facilitated individualized and quantified strategy improves short-term dietary intake compared with standard generic advice remains unclear; this trial does not isolate the independent effect of AI.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance using structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms versus standard discharge advice.

METHODS: In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, 90 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastric or colorectal cancer surgery were assigned 1:1 to AI-facilitated individualized guidance generated by DeepSeek v3.2 using an ABC-structured prompt plus clinician review or standard discharge dietary advice (standard care group). The intervention combined AI, individualization, quantified targets, written guidance, and clinician review; the trial cannot isolate AI alone. Primary outcome was energy intake adequacy (≥ 90% of target) at 30 days post-discharge. Secondary outcomes included protein intake adequacy, nutritional status, patient-reported outcomes, process measures (expert-rated quality scores, provider time), and 30-day complications. Outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups. The AI-guided group achieved significantly higher energy adequacy (66.7% vs. 40.0%, OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-7.1, P = 0.01) and protein adequacy (62.2% vs. 35.6%, OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.8, P = 0.01) at 30 days. Expert-rated quality scores were superior in the AI-guided group for completeness (4.6 vs. 3.2), individualization (4.8 vs. 2.8), and actionability (4.5 vs. 3.5) (all P < 0.001), while provider time per patient was reduced (8.2 vs. 12.5 min, P < 0.001). Patient-reported outcomes showed significant improvements in fatigue, nausea/vomiting, appetite loss, and gastrointestinal symptoms (GSRS total score 2.1 vs. 2.5, P = 0.03) in the AI-guided group. No significant differences were observed in weight change, serum nutritional markers, or complication rates.

CONCLUSION: AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance improved short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms and reduced provider time compared with standard generic advice. These findings do not show that AI itself is superior to similarly individualized non-AI counseling and do not establish longer-term nutritional or clinical benefit. Clinical supervision remains essential.

articles.title: Comparison of bone repair of advanced platelet-rich fibrin (A-PRF) and leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) following the extraction of impacted third molars: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the effects of leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) and advanced platelet-rich fibrin (A-PRF) on bone healing and postoperative outcomes following impacted third molar extraction (ITME).

METHODS: A randomized, double-blind, split-mouth clinical trial was conducted in patients undergoing bilateral ITME. One extraction socket received L-PRF and the contralateral socket received A-PRF. The primary outcome was bone volume at the extraction socket, assessed by cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), as a measure of bone healing. Secondary outcomes included trabecular thickness, trabecular spacing, soft tissue healing assessed using the modified Landry healing index, postoperative pain assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS), and facial swelling. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Thirty-five patients were included in the final analysis. No significant differences were observed in bone volume between the L-PRF (21.04 ± 7.46) and A-PRF (21.43 ± 7.65) groups (p = 0.802). Trabecular thickness was significantly greater in the A-PRF group (p = 0.012), whereas trabecular spacing did not differ between groups. An exploratory time-specific comparison showed lower pain scores in the L-PRF group at 8 h postoperatively (p = 0.046), although no significant overall treatment effect was observed for postoperative pain. No significant differences were identified regarding facial swelling or soft tissue healing.

CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this randomized clinical trial, L-PRF and A-PRF demonstrated comparable effects on bone healing and postoperative clinical outcomes following impacted third molar extraction. Trial registration Brazilian registry of clinical trials [ReBEC] number: RBR-10vc6r63.

articles.title: FDG PET/MR for liver metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy and technical protocols with a proposed reporting framework.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of FDG PET/MR for detecting hepatic metastases from extrahepatic primary malignancies, together with acquisition protocols, reconstruction parameters, and technical heterogeneity.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted through September 2026. Eligible studies evaluated FDG PET/MR for hepatic metastases and reported diagnostic performance data and/or technical protocol information. Summary estimates of sensitivity and specificity were obtained using a bivariate random-effects model. A structured qualitative assessment of PET and MR acquisition, reconstruction parameters, and image interpretation strategies was also performed.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies involving 861 patients met the inclusion criteria. Eight studies (53%) provided sufficient data for the diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis, whereas all contributed to the qualitative technical assessment. The meta-analysis demonstrated a summary sensitivity estimate of 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-0.97) and a summary specificity estimate of 0.99 (95% CI, 0.92-1.00) for detecting hepatic metastases. Sensitivity showed substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.83), whereas specificity showed low heterogeneity (I² = 0.21). Technical assessment revealed marked variability in PET acquisition, MR protocols, reconstruction parameters, and reporting, with frequent underreporting of voxel size, filtering, and motion correction. Hepatobiliary contrast agents were used in only a minority of studies, and dedicated PET motion correction was rarely implemented.

CONCLUSION: FDG PET/MR demonstrates high lesion-level diagnostic accuracy for the detection of hepatic metastases, with high summary sensitivity and specificity. However, substantial between-study variability in sensitivity, together with variability and frequent underreporting of technical parameters, highlights the need for standardized acquisition protocols and reporting frameworks to improve reproducibility, comparability, and clinical translation.

articles.title: Diagnostic uncertainty in the index case of Coxiella burnetii vascular-spinal infection.
Effect of continuous-use air sterilization on healthcare-associated infections in a neonatal intensive care unit: A quasi-experimental study.
articles.abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a significant challenge in NICUs. Continuous air sterilization systems may reduce environmental microbial contamination, but their impact on HAIs and multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) colonization remains uncertain. To evaluate the association of a continuous air sterilization system with healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) colonization, and environmental microbial burden in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). This quasi-experimental pre-post intervention study was conducted in a Level III NICU of a tertiary care hospital in Southern India. Neonates admitted during a 5-month pre-intervention phase were compared with those admitted during a 5-month post-intervention phase following installation of the continuous air sterilization system, with a 1-month washout period excluded from analysis. Primary outcomes were definite and probable HAIs. Secondary outcomes included MDRO colonization, environmental microbial burden, antibiotic utilization, and sepsis-related clinical outcomes. Crude effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals were additionally calculated; multivariable logistic regression was used for colonization outcomes to account for baseline differences. Among 698 neonates, 367 were included in the pre-intervention and 331 in the post-intervention cohort. The post-intervention cohort had significantly lower birth weight (2520 ± 771 vs. 2398 ± 820 g; p = 0.043) and gestational age (36 ± 3 vs. 35 ± 4 weeks; p = 0.0003). The incidence of definite HAI (5.2% vs. 6.3%; p = 0.611), probable HAI (2.5% vs. 5.1%; p = 0.094), and any HAI (7.4% vs. 9.7%; p = 0.332) did not differ significantly between the groups. After adjustment for gestational age and birth weight, the odds of any HAI remained similar (aOR 1.05, 95% CI 0.58-1.91). New MDRO colonization was also comparable (6.0% vs. 7.0%; p = 0.713). However, the intervention was associated with a significant reduction in airborne microbial burden. Conclusions: The continuous air sterilization system was associated with a substantial reduction in airborne microbial burden; however, no statistically significant reduction in HAIs or MDRO colonization was observed. Given the uncontrolled pre-post design and baseline differences, causal effects on clinical outcomes remain unproven. This study was only powered to detect very large effects; therefore, clinical benefit should be tested in larger cluster-randomized studies, or in settings where airborne transmission is a major driver of HAI. What is already known • Environmental microbial contamination contributes to the transmission of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in NICUs. • Air sterilization technologies can reduce airborne microbial load, but evidence for their impact on neonatal clinical outcomes and HAIs remains limited and inconsistent. What this study adds • Continuous air sterilization was associated with a reduction in environmental microbial burden in a Level III NICU. • Because airborne transmission is one of several routes of NICU infection, trials of air sterilization need either very large samples or settings and endpoints in which airborne infection predominates.

articles.title: Application of transanal intestinal tube placement in ileostomy closure for post-NEC enterostomy patients: complication spectrum shift from severe to manageable minor complications.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess whether adjunctive transanal intestinal tube placement (TITP) during ileostomy closure improves postoperative outcomes in infants with a prior necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) enterostomy.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 187 infants undergoing elective NEC ileostomy closure (2020-2025). Using December 2022 as the cut-off, 92 received closure alone and 95 closure plus TITP. Length of stay, enteral nutrition (EN) recovery, operative time, and complications were compared; propensity score matching (PSM) and a near-time-window subgroup analysis addressed confounding.

RESULTS: The TITP group had shorter stay (9.6 ± 2.2 vs. 12.5 ± 3.1 d; β = -3.37, P < 0.001), earlier EN initiation and full EN (P < 0.001), and ~ 7 min longer operative time (P = 0.05). Complication rates were similar; the Clavien-Madadi spectrum shifted (P = 0.004): grade IIIb events accounted for 19% vs. 47% of complication events (OR = 0.27) and grade I perianal complications increased (35% vs. 8%). Anastomotic leakage did not differ (P = 0.38; power 0.14).

CONCLUSION: TITP was associated with a shift of the complication spectrum toward milder events-from grade IIIb to grade I manageable skin complications-and faster EN recovery and shorter stay, but the anastomotic-leakage finding is underpowered and the time-period design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: HIV reservoir cells do not show general resistance to effector molecules secreted by cytolytic T lymphocytes.
articles.abstract: To eliminate the persistent reservoir of cells harboring intact HIV-1 proviruses in people living with HIV-1 (PLWH), cure strategies like the Shock-and-Kill approach rely on effector functions of cytolytic T lymphocytes (CTL). CTL are involved in the initial control of HIV-1 viremia and target productively infected cells throughout the course of infection. However, selective killing of susceptible cells could generate a reservoir dominated by cells with dysregulated cell death pathways or other features conferring resistance to killing. Here, we use CTL-engaging single-chain diabodies to assess the rate of lysis of uninfected and HIV-1-infected primary CD4+ T cells under identical CTL pressure in the settings of both latent and active infection. Our findings indicate that with this mode of CTL triggering, infected and uninfected CD4+ T cells from PLWH on ART are generally lysed at identical rates, and that an apparent survival advantage for actively infected CD4+ T cells primarily reflects the reduced surface antigen availability through previously described Nef-dependent downregulation of MHC class I molecules. No survival advantage is observed when the CTL response is directed through diabodies to the stably expressed non-classical MHC class I molecule HLA-E, indicating equal susceptibility to cell death.

articles.title: Mutant ASXL1 exacerbates CALR-mutant myeloproliferative neoplasms by enhancing a distinct megakaryocyte differentiation program.
articles.abstract: ASXL1 mutations confer a poor prognosis in myeloid neoplasms, including in CALR-mutated myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN). We generated Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant mice and found more severe thrombocytosis and increased splenomegaly, compared with Calr single-mutant animals. Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant megakaryocytes displayed more pronounced morphological abnormalities and enhanced emperipolesis characteristic of inflammation. Concordant with this, a differentiation trajectory directly to megakaryocytes from hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) was more prominent in Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant mice. In this non-canonical trajectory, where megakaryocyte-biased HSCs directly differentiate into megakaryocyte progenitors, we found upregulation of Mef2c, a key transcriptional regulator of megakaryocyte lineage commitment. Mature Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant megakaryocytes displayed an enhanced proinflammatory transcriptional state, whereas the transcriptional signature of Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant HSCs was indicative of inflammation-resistance. Genotyping of transcriptomes (GoT) confirmed an activated megakaryocytic differentiation program in CALR-ASXL1 co-mutant HSCs in primary human MPN bone marrow. These findings link the enhanced severity of CALR-ASXL1 co-mutant MPN to altered megakaryocyte differentiation and help explain some of the biological basis for the more severe MPN phenotype observed in patients.

articles.title: Three-dimensional DXA for compartment-specific assessment of proximal femoral bone in type 2 diabetes and diabetic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Three-dimensional DXA (3D-DXA), derived from a routine hip DXA, decomposed proximal femoral bone into cortical, trabecular, and geometric components in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The apparent T2DM density advantage was attenuated in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), with adjusted analyses showing significantly lower integral, trabecular, and cortical vBMD in DKD with reduced eGFR than in T2DM without DKD. The total-hip buckling ratio, a geometric index sharing only 7% of its variance with areal BMD, rose across worsening eGFR categories within T2DM and remained associated with renal function after adjustment. An exploratory PTH × DKD interaction is reported as hypothesis-generating. These findings support 3D-DXA as a compartment-specific bone-assessment tool that may complement areal bone mineral density in DKD.

PURPOSE: Areal bone mineral density (aBMD) performs poorly as a fracture-risk surrogate in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). We evaluated whether three-dimensional DXA (3D-DXA) from a routine hip DXA provides compartment-specific bone phenotyping in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and DKD.

METHODS: We analysed 3D-SHAPER reconstructions from 1520 adults (549 T2DM; 971 non-DM), excluding bone-affecting comorbidities and antiresorptive or glucocorticoid use. Sequential multivariable models and propensity-score matching compared T2DM with non-DM and four diabetes-kidney status groups, with per-SD standardization, Benjamini-Hochberg control, and receiver-operating-characteristic comparison against total-hip aBMD.

RESULTS: T2DM had higher integral, trabecular, and cortical vBMD than non-DM (β = +9.91, +6.33, +17.64 mg/cm³; all FDR q < 0.02). vBMD showed an inverted-U pattern; in the adjusted full cohort, DKD with reduced eGFR had lower integral, trabecular, and cortical vBMD than T2DM without DKD (all P < 0.03). Within T2DM, the total-hip buckling ratio, which shared only 7% of its variance with aBMD, rose across eGFR categories (3.64 at G1 to 4.64 at G4) and remained associated with eGFR (P < 0.001) and DKD (P = 0.007) after adjustment for aBMD. Per-SD effects for volumetric parameters matched aBMD, and 3D-DXA did not improve discrimination of DKD status (ΔAUC = 0.013; P = 0.23). An exploratory PTH-trabecular bone interaction differed by DKD status (P = 0.039).

CONCLUSIONS: 3D-DXA from routine hip DXA captured compartment-specific bone differences across diabetes-kidney status groups in T2DM and DKD, supporting its further evaluation as a compartment-specific imaging adjunct to aBMD in DKD where aBMD is limited. Prospective fracture-outcome studies are required for clinical translation.

articles.title: Experiences of Immersive Virtual Reality Among Older Adults With Physical Disabilities: Qualitative Process Evaluation of a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence indicates that immersive virtual reality can be used therapeutically and has demonstrated efficacy in promoting the mental health of older adults. Nevertheless, there remains a paucity of qualitative research examining the specific experiences underpinning these benefits.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the perspectives of older adults who received the 12-session Immersive Virtual Reality Therapeutic Programme (IVRTP) intervention and health-related undergraduate students who delivered it as interventionists, within the context of residential care homes.

METHODS: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted as a qualitative exploration embedded in a multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating the effects of IVRTP in promoting the mental health of older adults with disabilities living in residential homes. The IVRTP incorporated therapeutic elements of tourism, natural scenes, and reminiscence. Data were collected through focus group interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Seven groups of older adults (n=28) and 3 groups of student interventionists (n=9) participated in the study. Five themes emerged: IVRTP contributes to "broadening horizons" through embracing new technology, learning new things, and engaging in new activities. Participants noted that the IVRTP provided "a realistic journey and immersive escape" from their residential home environment and mobility issues. They expressed that the IVRTP evoked "reminiscent memories" from the past and were amazed at the observed changes in tourist destinations over time. The interviews were filled with laughter and affirmations of positive emotions associated with this "joyful adventure," although a few participants mentioned "minor discomfort," such as eye soreness and dizziness, from wearing the head-mounted devices. Students' accounts corroborated these themes; their meaning-making and colearning with older adults underscored the pedagogical value of authentic, community-based, intergenerational learning and reinforced the case for integrating a community practicum into the curriculum.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementing an IVRTP in residential care settings, particularly for older adults with mobility limitations, is positively viewed as an accessible, enjoyable, and beneficial intervention to support psychosocial well-being. Therapeutically oriented content delivered through a structured protocol, coupled with the use of advanced IVR technology, was appreciated by both older adults and student interventionists.

articles.title: Nonpatient Stakeholder Perspectives on the Use of Gamification and Financial Incentives in Mobile Health for Medication Adherence: Modified Nominal Group Technique Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medication nonadherence remains a major global health challenge, contributing to preventable disease, hospitalizations, and health care costs. Mobile health (mHealth) apps incorporating gamification and financial incentives have shown potential to improve adherence; however, most research has focused on patient perspectives, with limited understanding of how nonpatient stakeholders perceive their feasibility, risks, and implementation. Understanding nonpatient stakeholder perspectives in relation to patient viewpoints is essential for informing future policy development and establishing practical, industry-supported safeguards that protect consumers while enabling innovation.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore nonpatient stakeholder perspectives on the use of gamification and financial incentives in mHealth apps for medication adherence and to inform consensus-based design and policy considerations.

METHODS: A study was conducted using a modified virtual nominal group technique (vNGT). Nonpatient stakeholders across health care, industry, and policy sectors in Australia were recruited through purposive and convenience sampling between February and August 2025. Data collection involved a survey capturing demographics and initial perspectives, followed by online focus groups for consensus discussions. Qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis supported by AI-assisted coding. Consensus statements derived from themes were rated during the focus groups. Additional probing prompts were used in the focus groups to encourage further discussion where consensus was not immediately achieved. Results from the focus groups were analyzed using descriptive statistics to summarize consensus ratings and discussions.

RESULTS: A total of 20 participants were included in the study. Nine participants reported having a health care professional background employment exclusively, while 11 reported having employment background across multiple sectors or exclusively outside health care. Six key themes were identified: tailored gamification for adherence, financial incentives as a contested motivator, designing for diversity and inclusion, usability barriers to engagement, trust through data governance, and validated and sustainable innovation. These informed 24 consensus statements, of which 54% (13/24) achieved unanimous agreement. Stakeholders strongly endorsed personalization, simplicity, and transparent data practices, while expressing nuanced concerns regarding the ethical use, sustainability, and potential unintended consequences of financial incentives.

CONCLUSIONS: Nonpatient stakeholders largely reinforce patient priorities while extending them with critical perspectives on implementation, governance, and sustainability. Gamification and financial incentives are viewed as potentially effective but require careful, ethically grounded design to balance engagement with long-term motivation and trust. These findings support the development of stakeholder-informed guidelines for responsible mHealth innovation and highlight the importance of integrating patient and system-level perspectives in digital health design. Future research should prioritize co-designed longitudinal studies using apps with gamification and a range of incentive offers with clear redemption processes to evaluate the long-term impact on medication adherence across diverse patient populations.

articles.title: Intravascular ultrasound guidance for complex percutaneous coronary intervention: still useful or eventually obsolete?
Disseminated Nocardiosis With Perimyocardial Involvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocardia pseudobrasiliensis causes opportunistic infection in immunocompromised hosts. Cardiac involvement is rare and may mimic malignancy or inflammatory disease.

CASE SUMMARY: A 44-year-old woman with prior liver and kidney transplantation on immunosuppressants presented with pleuritic chest pain, cough, and subcutaneous nodules. Electrocardiogram showed diffuse ST-segment elevation and PR depression. Cardiac magnetic-resonance imaging revealed a heterogeneously enhancing left ventricular apical and anterior septal mass with extension into the right ventricle, along with pericardial thickening, and chest computed tomography demonstrated cavitary pulmonary nodules and a periscapular abscess. Aspiration of the periscapular abscess confirmed disseminated nocardiosis. She was treated with intravenous imipenem and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole with a steroid taper, resulting in clinical and radiographic improvement.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates a rare infectious cause of a myocardial mass and perimyocarditis identified through multimodality imaging, highlighting the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in transplant recipients presenting with infectious symptoms.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Nocardiosis and infection with other atypical organisms should be considered in immunosuppressed patients with cardiac masses to elucidate etiology early and target antimicrobial therapy to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Early Diagnosis, Delayed Treatment, and Fulminant Progression of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prompt immunosuppressive therapy is recommended for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis; however, the optimal timing in asymptomatic patients remains uncertain.

CASE SUMMARY: A woman in her 60s receiving adjuvant pembrolizumab for melanoma developed asymptomatic cardiac troponin I (cTnI) elevation (93 pg/mL) before her ninth cycle. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging met diagnostic criteria for myocarditis; however, immunosuppressive therapy was withheld because of the absence of symptoms and mild cTnI elevation. One week later, she developed symptomatic myocarditis with a marked cTnI increase (4,115 pg/mL), requiring intensive care, corticosteroid pulse therapy, and temporary mechanical circulatory support.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that asymptomatic immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis can progress rapidly despite seemingly low initial risk, underscoring the importance of ongoing risk assessment following diagnosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Early diagnosis alone may not be sufficient to prevent disease progression. Risk stratification and timely intervention during the presymptomatic phase may improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Pretreatment Evaluation and Follow-Up of Endometrial Cancer: 2026 Update.
authors: Expert Panel on GYN and OB Imaging
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecologic malignancy in the United States, and accurate pretreatment evaluation is essential for risk stratification, treatment planning, and detection of recurrent disease. This evidence-based review summarizes imaging recommendations for patients with established endometrial cancer undergoing pretreatment assessment, surveillance, or evaluation for suspected recurrence. MRI pelvis without and with intravenous contrast is usually appropriate for assessment of local tumor extension across histologic subtypes and grades. For aggressive histologic tumor types, or when metastatic disease is suspected, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous contrast and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for evaluation of nodal and distant metastases. Routine imaging surveillance is usually not appropriate for asymptomatic patients with treated low- or intermediate-risk disease, whereas CT may be appropriate in selected asymptomatic high-risk patients. MRI pelvis, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for suspected recurrence. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision process support the systematic analysis of the medical literature from peer reviewed journals. Established methodology principles such as Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE are adapted to evaluate the evidence. The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method User Manual provides the methodology to determine the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where peer reviewed literature is lacking or equivocal, experts may be the primary evidentiary source available to formulate a recommendation.

articles.title: The Crossroads Between the Kidney and Gastrointestinal Disorders: Core Curriculum 2026.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: The kidney and gastrointestinal (GI) tract are closely linked through a bidirectional system involving complex interactions called the gut-kidney axis. Within this system, alterations in the gut microbiome can promote progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) while uremic toxins from advanced kidney dysfunction can adversely affect intestinal health. Incretin hormones, particularly glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), play an important role in this gut-kidney signaling and will be explored here. We also examine how this physiology helps explain the connection between GI illness and IgA nephropathy, along with the kidney manifestations seen in inflammatory bowel disease. Furthermore, we will review how CKD and end-stage kidney disease increase the risk of GI disease and complicate its management, and how CKD therapies affect GI symptoms. In this AJKD Core Curriculum, we use a case-based format to illustrate the intricate interplay between the kidneys and the GI tract.

articles.title: Reactions to Race[ism]: The Relationship Between Differential Treatment Based on Race and Diagnosed Diabetes Status in U.S. Adults.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between diabetes status and self-reported discrimination based on race among U.S. adults with and without diabetes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We analyzed 2022-2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 328,056 adults completing the Reactions to Race module and reporting diabetes status. Experiences of racial discrimination at work, in health care, or elsewhere, and related physical symptoms, were categorized as any versus none. Weighted prevalence and multivariable logistic regression were stratified by diabetes status.

RESULTS: Discrimination based on race was reported by 14.2% of adults with diabetes and 12.5% without diabetes. Patterns were similar across age, metropolitan status, and employment subgroups. In both groups, discrimination was associated with race and ethnicity, age, sex, employment, poor mental health, and current smoking.

CONCLUSIONS: Experiences of racial discrimination were common among U.S. adults and were reported more frequently by adults with diabetes. Because discrimination can contribute to chronic stress, reduced access to high-quality care, and barriers to diabetes self-management, consideration of racism-related exposures is important in efforts to understand and address diabetes disparities.

articles.title: Great debate: a dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome.
articles.abstract: Suspected myocardial infarction in patients with acute chest pain at rest is one of the most common diagnostic categories leading to emergency hospital admission and emergency department overcrowding worldwide. Efforts are being made to improve the efficiency of currently used triage and diagnostic work-up strategies. Despite major advances in recent years with the use of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, challenges still exist regarding how to accurately and rapidly rule out or rule in myocardial infarction, as current strategies are relatively slow due to the need for serial troponin measurements. The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommend a 0 h/1 h or a 0 h/2 h high-sensitivity troponin diagnostic algorithm, instead of the previously suggested 0 h/3 h diagnostic protocol, to reduce the time required to discharge patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction. The ESC endorsed algorithms are not without difficulty, and alternative ways of improving triaging have been proposed, particularly a dual biomarker rule-out strategy involving the combined measurement of copeptin and troponin. Supporters of the dual biomarker strategy argue that a timely optimized algorithm can potentially allow the safe rule-out of myocardial infarction earlier than currently used strategies. In the present Great Debate article, two expert teams discuss the 'pros' and 'cons' of implementing single vs dual biomarker strategies for the rule-in and rule-out of myocardial infarction, under the moot topic 'A dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome'. They address in detail many of the controversial issues currently affecting everyday clinical practice and provide insightful comments on how to best triage patients presenting with suspected acute myocardial infarction.

articles.title: Pharmaceutical-derived microplastics: sources, detection, and toxicological implications for patient safety.
articles.abstract: Pharmaceutical products and the polymers used to manufacture them are often overlooked sources of microplastic (MP) exposure, with real implications for patient safety and the environment. Contamination arises from PE, PP, and PET packaging; elastomeric stoppers; plasticized PVC in IV bags and administration sets; excipients; and manufacturing-related contamination. The route of administration is important because injectables and IV infusions can deliver particles directly into systemic circulation, bypassing barriers that limit exposure via oral or topical routes.This review elaborates on leaching pathways driven by physical, chemical, interactive, and aging processes, as well as analytical methods, including optical and scanning electron microscopy, FTIR and Raman spectroscopy, and pyrolysis GC/MS, and emerging single-particle techniques differ in detection limits and face challenges from matrix interference and procedural contamination. Toxicological studies indicate that particle size, shape, and surface chemistry influence oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Nanoplastics are of particular concern due to their ability to cross biological barriers and enter cells, yet data on pharmaceutical-derived MPs and co-leaching additives (phthalate plasticizers, antioxidants, elastomer curing agents, residual catalysts) remain limited.Current pharmacopeial standards (USP <788>, <787>) classify particles only by size, ignoring polymer identity and excluding the submicron range. Extractables-and-leachables frameworks (USP <1663>, <1664>, ICH Q3E) address dissolved chemicals rather than intact particulate matter, leaving MPs insufficiently addressed by current regulations. Closing it requires packaging designed to shed less material from the outset, toxicokinetic data from real biological samples rather than models, longer-term in vivo and epidemiological studies, and contamination-free analytical workflows.

articles.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether quantitative retinal microvascular and structural parameters, measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), are associated with disease severity and right ventriculo-arterial coupling in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

RESULTS: Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

CONCLUSION: Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.

articles.title: Recombinant RANKL protects against brain injury in intracerebral haemorrhage by regulating microglial phenotypes via the STAT3 pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is a severe stroke subtype with high morbidity and mortality, where inflammation plays a crucial role. Recent studies suggest that the RANKL/RANK pathway is involved in stroke pathophysiology. This study investigated the effects of recombinant RANKL on microglial polarization after ICH.

METHODS: In vitro, BV2 cells were stimulated with erythrocyte lysis (ELS) to assess cell viability, migration, and microglial phenotype markers. Stattic was used to block STAT3 pathway, and microglial markers were measured by RT-qPCR. In vivo, ICH rats were treated with RANKL or OPG. Neurological deficits and brain injury were evaluated. Immunohistochemistry analysed microglial activation and M1/M2 marker expression.

RESULTS: Recombinant RANKL enhanced BV2 cell migration induced by ELS and shifted microglial polarization towards M2, with reduced M1 marker expression. The increase in M2 markers was inhibited by Stattic, which blocks STAT3 signalling. In vivo, RANKL-treated rats showed reduced brain edema and improved neurobehavioral outcomes after ICH. RANKL treatment promoted M2 polarization of microglia/macrophages and inhibited M1 polarization following ICH.

CONCLUSIONS: RANKL plays a key role in ICH by promoting microglia M2 polarization and inhibiting M1 polarization.

articles.title: Ultrasonography (IOTA-ADNEX) vs magnetic resonance imaging (ADNEX MR) for diagnosing ovarian cancer in high-risk patients: a prospective study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically validate and compare ultrasonography, using the ultrasound-based International Ovarian Tumor Analysis - Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (IOTA-ADNEX) model, with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), using the MRI-based ADNEX MR scoring system, as second-line imaging modalities for estimating the risk of adnexal malignancy in patients identified as being at risk of malignancy on first-line ultrasound examination.

METHODS: This was a prospective, single-center diagnostic accuracy study designed as a head-to-head comparison. All patients referred to a tertiary referral center at Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus, Denmark, for suspected adnexal malignancy on first-line imaging between May 2021 and December 2022 were offered second-line diagnostic testing. This comprised both a systematic expert ultrasound examination, including IOTA-ADNEX risk estimation, and a systematic MRI scan with ADNEX MR scores assigned by expert radiologists. The imaging assessments were performed prospectively, with ultrasound examiners and radiologists blinded to the results of other imaging modalities and to the reference standard (tumor outcome). The reference standard was a histopathological diagnosis of the primary adnexal mass or, in a small number of cases, clinical follow-up. Borderline tumors, invasive adnexal malignancy and metastases to the adnexa were grouped as malignancies. Diagnostic performance of the IOTA-ADNEX model, ADNEX MR scoring system and CA 125 for predicting malignancy was evaluated using the area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve (AUC), and AUCs were compared using DeLong's test. Diagnostic metrics were estimated at clinically relevant cut-offs and scores. Agreement between modalities was assessed for the identification of morphological features and overall risk estimation using Cohen's kappa statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman plots. For the IOTA-ADNEX model, calibration and the ability to discriminate between tumor subtypes were evaluated.

RESULTS: The included cohort comprised 342 patients (342 lesions analyzed). In the final cohort, 78.1% of patients were postmenopausal and the overall prevalence of malignancy was 58.8%. The AUC for distinguishing patients with benign tumors from those with malignant tumors was 0.96 (95% CI, 0.94-0.98) for the IOTA-ADNEX model (with or without CA 125) compared with an AUC of 0.93 (95% CI, 0.91-0.96) for ADNEX MR. Agreement between ultrasound and MRI ranged from moderate to substantial for key morphological features (κ = 0.46-0.75) and from good to excellent for lesion-size measurements (ICC = 0.78-0.92). The IOTA-ADNEX model performed similarly to the ADNEX MR scoring system regardless of lesion morphology or size. The IOTA-ADNEX model had good calibration. Furthermore, its multinomial discriminative ability between tumor subtypes was generally high, although performance was reduced when distinguishing borderline tumors from Stage-I invasive malignancy (AUC, 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.82)).

CONCLUSIONS: The IOTA-ADNEX model and ADNEX MR scoring system demonstrated comparable diagnostic accuracy for differentiating benign from malignant adnexal masses in this study. Results appeared to be consistent when stratified by lesion morphology. Both modalities may be used for second-line assessment of masses deemed at risk of malignancy in the first-line ultrasound examination, depending on resources in specific centers. © 2026 The Author(s). Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

18F-Fluoro-L-dihydroxyphenylalanine positron emission tomography in the initial staging of medullary thyroid carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate initial staging of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) is critical for surgical planning and long-term outcome. While 18F-Fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (18F-DOPA PET/CT) is well established in the detection of recurrent disease, its role in the preoperative setting remains unclear. This review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical relevance of 18F-DOPA PET/CT in the initial staging of MTC.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed to identify studies assessing 18F-DOPA PET/CT in treatment-naïve MTC patients. Four studies met the inclusion criteria and were qualitatively analyzed. Data were synthesized focusing on compartment-specific performance, tumor burden, and potential impact on clinical management.

RESULTS: 18F-DOPA PET/CT demonstrated good sensitivity for primary tumor detection (86-88%), although performance was limited in microcarcinomas. A marked heterogeneity emerged across anatomical compartments. Sensitivity for central lymph node metastases was consistently low (28-53%), whereas higher values were observed in the lateral neck (57-81%), with high specificity when reported. Diagnostic performance was strongly influenced by tumor burden, with significantly reduced sensitivity in low-volume disease and improved detection in patients with more extensive nodal involvement. The integration of biochemical markers further supported a burden-dependent behavior, with higher calcitonin levels associated with improved imaging performance. In distant staging, 18F-DOPA PET/CT identified metastatic disease in a subset of patients but showed limited sensitivity for small hepatic lesions compared with dedicated MRI. Importantly, improvements in lesion detection did not consistently translate into meaningful changes in surgical management.

CONCLUSIONS: The role of 18F-DOPA PET/CT in the initial staging of MTC is selective and context-dependent. While it may provide incremental value in patients with higher tumor burden or suspected lateral nodal disease, its limited sensitivity in the central compartment and in low-volume disease prevents its use as a standalone staging modality. Therefore, 18F-DOPA PET/CT should be considered a context-driven adjunct rather than a routine tool, to be integrated within a multimodal imaging strategy rather than used as a standalone staging modality.

articles.title: Multiplexed Fc array assays reveal the influence of TLR3 on the Th1-biased humoral response induced in mice following live-attenuated RVFV vaccination.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) can cause severe disease in humans and livestock. Several vaccine candidates are immunogenic and protective in pre-clinical animal models. Reported measurements of humoral immunity following vaccination typically assess antigen-specific activity, such as virus binding or neutralization, but do not consider the role of the Fc region. To address this knowledge gap, multiplexed Fc array assays were developed to characterize the Fc profile of antigen-specific antibodies following RVFV vaccination. The RVFV nucleocapsid protein (N) and glycoproteins (Gn/Gc) were conjugated to magnetic microspheres, and monoclonal antibodies were used to optimize assay conditions. Sera from vaccinated mice were incubated with the conjugated microspheres to capture antigen-specific antibodies, and then various detection reagents were used to measure the isotype of the antibodies and their ability to bind Fc receptors (FcRs) or complement (C1q). Two studies involving mice vaccinated with live-attenuated RVFV ΔNSsΔNSm or ΔNSs were used to demonstrate the utility of these assays. In WT C57BL/6 mice, both ΔNSsΔNSm and ΔNSs induced a high magnitude of IgG2c antibodies, indicative of a Th1-biased response; these antibodies also bound the four murine FcRs and C1q. However, following ΔNSs infection of a panel of innate immune knockout (KO) mice, several strains of KO mice, especially TLR3 KO, exhibited a reduced magnitude of IgG2c antibodies, demonstrating the impact of innate immunity on the Th1-biased response. Overall, the multiplexed Fc array assays performed as expected and can be applied to other RVFV vaccine platforms in the future to help inform rational vaccine design.

IMPORTANCE: There are currently no approved vaccines to prevent RVFV infection in humans.
