articles.title: Drug Repurposing and Advanced Delivery Systems Targeting Multidrug-Resistant Microorganisms: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, driven by the spread of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens alongside a declining antibiotic pipeline. Drug repurposing offers a cost-effective, time-efficient alternative by identifying antimicrobial applications for approved drugs with established safety profiles. Agents including auranofin, niclosamide, gallium compounds, phenothiazines, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, ticagrelor, and dronedarone show antimicrobial, antibiofilm, antivirulence, and resistance-modifying activity through mechanisms distinct from conventional antibiotics, potentially limiting cross-resistance. However, reported in vitro minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) frequently exceed clinical breakpoints and plasma concentrations achievable at approved doses, confining most candidates to adjuvant or local therapy rather than systemic monotherapy. Poor solubility, limited bioavailability, unfavorable pharmacokinetics, and systemic toxicity further constrain clinical translation. Advanced drug delivery systems (DDS) like nanoparticles, liposomes, metal-organic frameworks, and stimuli-responsive carriers may mitigate these barriers by improving stability, targeting, infection-site accumulation, and controlled release. Such platforms can additionally enhance biofilm penetration, enable intracellular delivery, and permit co-delivery with conventional antibiotics to achieve synergy. Integrating repurposed agents with advanced DDS could therefore address key resistance mechanisms, including biofilm formation, efflux activity, and intracellular persistence, although substantial challenges remain despite encouraging preclinical data. This review critically evaluates the antimicrobial potential of repurposed non-antimicrobial drugs spanning anti-arthritic, anthelmintic, antineoplastic, psychiatric, and cardiovascular classes, examining mechanisms of action, efficacy evidence, and principal limitations, and assesses how advanced DDS might improve their therapeutic performance against MDR infections. It further identifies major evidence gaps and research priorities to guide development of clinically viable anti-AMR strategies.

articles.title: 'We first have to agree': childbearing decision-making among HIV sero-different couples along Lake Victoria, Kisumu, Kenya.
articles.abstract: Among couples, gender-based power dynamics regarding childbearing decision-making can impact reproductive health outcomes. Guided by interdependence theory, we examined power and gender roles in childbearing decision-making among HIV sero-different couples to inform programmes and interventions supporting safer reproductive decisions to prevent HIV infection. This dyadic qualitative study was conducted between November 2023 and February 2024, with 16 HIV sero-different heterosexual couples (n = 32) in rural fishing communities in Kisumu County, Kenya. During in-depth interviews, participants shared perspectives on childbearing decision-making to elicit dyadic factors involved. Data were analysed at individual and dyadic levels using framework analysis. This study revealed three primary themes associated with childbearing decision-making within couples: (1) a strong desire for children; (2) the importance of gender and societal norms that shape the perceptions of men and women about power; and (3) a tension between collaborative joint decision-making that happens within couples and women's constrained individual autonomy which led to women's control of pregnancy timing through both overt and covert means. Despite norms of male-led reproductive decision-making, most couples demonstrated collaborative, unity-focused approaches, indicating nuanced shared power dynamics. Future programmes and interventions could focus on couple unity and agreement to support safer conception outcomes in HIV sero-different couples.

articles.title: 17β-Estradiol and Estrogen Receptor α Promote Right Ventricle Angiogenesis in Pulmonary Hypertension via Apelin Signaling.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) failure is the major cause of mortality in pulmonary hypertension (PH). Adaptive angiogenesis and RV endothelial cell (RVEC) function are major modifiers of RV adaptation in PH, but the underlying mechanisms and their regulators remain incompletely understood. RV adaptation in PH is sexually dimorphic, and 17β-estradiol (E2) exerts protective effects on RV cardiomyocytes. Whether E2 modifies angiogenesis and RVEC function in RV failure remains unknown. We hypothesized that E2 and estrogen receptor α (ERα) promote RV angiogenesis and RVEC homeostasis in PH and aimed to identify underlying mechanisms. We assessed E2's angiogenic effects using cultured human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (hCMVECs), RVECs from PH patients with RV failure, and RVECs from sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) and monocrotaline rat models. In vivo, we evaluated RV capillary density in PH rats treated with E2 or ERα-selective agonist. Apelin signaling was evaluated via apelin receptor (APLNR) blockade and knockdown studies. E2 preserved angiogenesis in male hCMVECs and RV capillary density in male and female SuHx-PH rats. E2 reversed angiogenic alterations in RVECs from SuHx-PH rats via APLNR signaling. In RVECs from RV failure patients, E2 stimulated vascular network formation. In rat and human PH-RVECs, ERα was necessary and sufficient to mediate E2-induced angiogenesis. Activation of ERα with ERα-specific agonist restored RV capillary density in vivo. ERα-mediated angiogenesis required apelin signaling. These data indicate that E2 promotes RV angiogenesis via ERα and apelin signaling and identify a novel ERα-apelin axis in RVECs as a potential therapeutic target to restore RV vascular integrity in PH.

articles.title: Reversal of nasal epithelial permeability in severe eosinophilic asthma by anti-IL5Rα antibody, benralizumab.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: The consideration of time since stroke on intervention outcomes for post-stroke depression and anxiety: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to explore the impact of time since stroke on post-stroke mood intervention outcomes. Four databases were searched from inception to November 2025. RCTs that involved psychological interventions for managing depression or anxiety in adult stroke survivors, with an active or passive control group, were included. Risk of bias was assessed and a narrative synthesis conducted. Fourteen publications were included in this review at data extraction. Due to time since stroke reporting limitations, synthesis was split by maximum time since stroke recruitment of less than three months, six months, and over six months post-stroke. A higher proportion of studies conducted at an earlier time since stroke reported significant improvement in depression following the intervention compared to controls. Only four studies included anxiety as an outcome. The results provide preliminary indication that interventions were more frequently effective when provided earlier in the recovery timeline; however, extreme caution is required with interpretation due to high heterogeneity and low-quality research. Future RCTs on interventions for post-stroke mood should routinely report time since stroke, consider directly investigating the impact of time since stroke on intervention outcomes, and use other methods to synthesize existing research.

articles.title: Utilization of Microaxial Mechanical Circulatory Support Among the Pediatric Population: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Utilization of microaxial pumps for temporary mechanical circulatory support in children has increased in recent years. However, data on patient selection, implantation techniques, and outcomes remain limited.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in July 2025 to identify case reports and case series reporting the use of microaxial pumps in patients aged 18 years or less. Forty-four studies comprising 100 patients were identified, and patient-level data were extracted for analysis.

RESULTS: The median age of the patients was 14 [IQR, 11.5-16] years, with a median weight of 52 [40-73] kg and median body surface area of 1.59 [1.35-1.85] m2. The most common diagnoses were cardiomyopathy (29%), heart allograft rejection (26%), and myocarditis (21%). Impella CP was the most frequently used device (48%), followed by Impella 2.5 and Impella 5.5 (each 21%). Access was predominantly obtained via the femoral artery (47%). Percutaneous implantation was performed in 47% of patients. Patients were weaned from microaxial support for cardiac recovery (42%) or heart transplantation (31%). Fourteen patients (14%) died prior to discharge, with significantly higher mortality among patients supported with ECPella (29%) compared with microaxial pump alone (6%; p = 0.01). The median duration of support was 6 [4-13] days. At the median follow-up of 119 [23-180] days overall survival was 84%.

CONCLUSION: Microaxial pumps represent an important addition to temporary mechanical circulatory support in pediatric patients and can serve as an alternative to VA-ECMO in selected cases. Outcomes were less favorable when used in tandem configurations such as ECPella, reflecting the greater severity of illness in these patients.

articles.title: Improving Access to Sexual Health Information and Resources Among South Asian International Students: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis at a Midwestern U.S. University.
articles.abstract: South Asian international students may encounter multiple barriers when seeking sexual health information and services on U.S. college campuses, including cultural stigma, language barriers, and limited access to culturally responsive resources. These challenges, combined with acculturation-related stress, may influence sexual health knowledge, preventive behaviors, and use of campus health services. This study explored strategies to improve sexual health education and access to resources for South Asian international students in university settings. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from January through March 2023 among South Asian international students enrolled at the University of Cincinnati in the United States. Responses to an open-ended question regarding strategies for making sexual health information and sexually transmitted infection (STI) resources more accessible were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Of the 103 survey respondents, 68 provided responses to the open-ended question and comprised the qualitative sample. Participants recommended integrating sexual health education into international student orientation and other institutional onboarding processes, expanding accessible in-person and online educational opportunities, increasing availability of sexual health information through multiple communication channels, and improving access to prevention and testing resources, including condoms and STI screening. Findings highlight the importance of institutionally embedded and culturally responsive approaches to sexual health promotion among South Asian international students. Universities may consider integrating sexual health education into transition programming, developing diverse information delivery pathways, and strengthening access to preventive services to better support the sexual health needs of international students.

articles.title: Mass Spectrometry Imaging-Guided Proteomics, an Emerging Frontier in Spatial Biology.
articles.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity is a defining feature of tissue organization, yet conventional proteomic analysis provides limited information about the spatial origins of identified proteins. Spatially guided proteomics addresses this limitation by using tissue imaging techniques to select regions of interest (ROIs) for localized analysis by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Among the imaging modalities available for this purpose, mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) stands out for its ability to map diverse molecular species directly within tissue without predefined targets, allowing chemically distinct regions to guide tissue sampling. By bridging spatial molecular profiles with high protein coverage, MSI-guided proteomics offers comprehensive biological insight. This review examines the workflow from MSI data acquisition through ROI definition, image registration, tissue isolation, and sample preparation to LC-MS/MS analysis. We compare common MSI modalities, discuss methods for ROI isolation, and summarize advances in nanoproteomics methods that support analysis of tissue samples at the microscopic scale. We critically evaluate applications in cancer research, infectious disease, neuroscience, and environmental science. Finally, we discuss the challenges and future directions of MSI-guided proteomics. We conclude that ongoing developments in the MSI-guided proteomics workflow position it as an emerging strategy for investigating localized biological processes within heterogeneous tissues.

articles.title: Determinants of Measles Vaccine Failure and Breakthrough Infections: A Systematic Review of IgG Avidity Based Immunological Markers and Host Genetic Polymorphisms.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Measles remains a leading cause of vaccine-preventable mortality, despite high reported coverage. Determinants of measles vaccine failure remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: Five databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library) were searched from inception. Studies in vaccinated individuals evaluating IgG avidity markers or host genetic polymorphisms were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, JBI checklist and modified HuGENet framework. Findings were synthesized narratively (PROSPERO: CRD420261415732).

RESULTS: Sixteen studies (8169 participants; 1998-2025) met inclusion criteria. Across seven studies with event-level data, primary vaccine failure ranged from 24.2% to 90.8%. Reproducible host genetic associations were observed for HLA Class I/II alleles, measles receptor genes (SLAM/CD150, CD46, CD209), TLR pathway genes, antiviral effector genes and cytokine/cytokine receptor genes. No study reported extractable breakthrough infection or dichotomous IgG avidity data.

CONCLUSION: Reproducible host genetic determinants of measles antibody response cluster at HLA loci, the measles receptor axis and the TLR pathway. Inconsistent definitions and absent standardized reporting preclude firm conclusions. Prospective harmonized studies are required.

articles.title: Assessing Context to Inform Cultural Tailoring of a School-Based Asthma Program for Dissemination to Rural Colorado.
articles.abstract: School-based asthma programs have reduced asthma disparities for low-income and racial/ethnic minority children in urban settings, including Latinx families. However, rural parent perspectives have not yet been incorporated into these programs. To inform implementation of our Better Asthma Control for Kids (BACK) program in rural Colorado, we sought to understand the barriers and facilitators to asthma management in rural settings for Latinx and non-Latinx families. Between June and September 2022, interviews with Latinx and non-Latinx caregivers of children with asthma in rural Colorado explored barriers and facilitators to pediatric asthma management, including self-management practices, cultural beliefs, and interest in BACK. Interviews were coded and analyzed for thematic domains of commonalities and unique experiences by ethnicity/language spoken. We interviewed 22 caregivers (68% Latinx, 45% Spanish-speaking) living in two rural regions of Colorado. Barriers across caregivers included three themes: (a) Rural families experience challenges accessing asthma care due to transportation challenges and limited health care availability. (b) Families have common knowledge, language, and cultural gaps that lead to misperceptions of asthma. Latinx caregivers, who often struggled to understand why their child had asthma, leading to limited diagnosis acceptance and obstacles to self-management. (c) Rural caregivers desire tailored education to address asthma knowledge gaps and were interested in school-based asthma programs like BACK. The novel barriers to pediatric asthma management identified among rural non-Latinx and Latinx families will guide tailoring of BACK to enhance its impact-other programs seeking to improve asthma disparities in rural and Latinx communities should consider these barriers.

articles.title: Performance of the recent Duke criteria versions in patients with suspected infective endocarditis and sufficient cardiac imaging: The more things change, the more they remain the same.
authors: on befalf of the ESCMID Study Group for Bloodstream Infections, Endocarditis, and Sepsis (ESGBIES)
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Even after the major revisions incorporated into the International Society for Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases (ISCVID) and 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Duke criteria, approximately one third of cases remain categorized as "possible" IE. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Duke criteria in a cohort of patients who underwent guideline-concordant multimodality cardiac imaging.

METHODS: This retrospective study at two Swiss university hospitals (2014-2025), included adult patients with suspected IE who underwent guideline-concordant cardiac imaging. The reference standard was the final diagnosis established by the Endocarditis Team. Each episode was classified according to 2015 Duke-ESC, 2023 Duke-ISCVID, and 2023 Duke-ESC clinical criteria as definite, possible, and rejected IE. Diagnostic performance was assessed using two approaches: (1) definite IE versus possible/rejected IE, and (2) definite/possible IE versus rejected IE.

RESULTS: Among 3,448 of suspected IE, 1,302 (38%) were adjudicated as IE. The proportion of episodes classified as possible IE remained high: 2015 Duke-ESC: 29%; 2023 Duke-ISCVID: 33%; and 2023 Duke-ESC: 29%. Sensitivity (definite IE vs possible/rejected IE) increased from 63% (95% CI 60-66%) with the 2015 Duke-ESC criteria to 74% (71-76%) with the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria and 71% (68-73%) with the 2023 Duke-ESC criteria. Specificity (definite/possible IE versus rejected IE) declined from 72% (70-74%) to 59% (57-61%) and 66% (64-68%), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort of patients who underwent guideline-concordant imaging, both 2023 Duke criteria increased sensitivity but failed to reduce the persistent diagnostic gray-zone of "possible" IE, highlighting an ongoing limitation with direct clinical and research implications.

articles.title: Angiogenesis and Right Ventricular Adaptation to Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A New Chapter in the Estrogen Paradox Saga.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

articles.title: The Future of AI in Critical Care: An Exploration in Ten Parables.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: We cannot know how artificial intelligence (AI) will ultimately change critical care, only that it is driving substantial change quickly. Through ten parables, we describe plausible benefits, harms, and trade-offs involving prognosis, monitoring, liability, research, clinical work, data governance, education, and triage. These parables are not predictions. They are intended to help clinicians, institutions, and regulators envision a range of potential scenarios and think broadly about which applications to pursue, which risks to consider, and which rules to establish before AI systems become entrenched. Each parable reveals how the outlook for AI in critical care is characterized by uncertainty. This includes uncertainty about what a single prediction means for the patient in front of us, how an application built and tested in one setting performs in another, accountability frameworks, professional practice and learning, patient privacy and autonomy, and more. Within each parable we try to keep visible what current evidence already supports and what remains speculative. We close with a set of questions designed to focus that speculation among the interested parties who will shape the future of AI in critical care.

articles.title: Implementing low-cost Capability, Opportunity Motivation and Behaviour (COM-B) interventions to increase bed-substitution rehabilitation referrals in acute stroke care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore barriers and enablers of referral to bed-substitution from acute stroke and neurology and evaluate the impact of theoretically-developed implementation strategies to improve referral rates.

METHODS: An implementation study. Baseline auditing of referrals to bed-substitution was completed. Staff referral enablers and barriers were identified via a Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) survey, mapped to the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation - Behaviour Change (COM-B) model and used to develop low-cost interventions with staff and consumers. The staff survey and audit were repeated after 12 months and differences were analysed via chi-squared tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.

RESULTS: The pre-intervention survey (n = 19) indicated that staff lacked confidence, faced a cumbersome process and were unsure of their role in referral, despite understanding the referral need. Interventions included: education, information sheets, patient stories, staff simultaneously working across acute and bed-substitution, and changes to referral process to address Knowledge, Environmental context and resources, Belief about Consequences. Referrals to bed-substitution increased from 64 (5.6%) referrals to bed-substitution (n = 1146, median age 65 [interquartile range 50-77] years, 53% male) to n = 57, 9.6%, p = 0.002) post-implementation.

CONCLUSIONS: Following the theoretically-developed low-cost interventions there was an increase in referrals to our bed-substitution service from our acute stroke and neurology ward.

articles.title: [Renal and systemic involvement in Erdheim-Chester disease and targeted therapy with BRAF and MEK inhibitors].
articles.abstract: Systemic BRAF V600E-mutated Erdheim-Chester disease was diagnosed in a 71-year-old patient presenting with bilateral perirenal infiltration ("hairy kidney"), bilateral renal hilar infiltration with right renal atrophy, retroperitoneal fibrosis, and mesenteric infiltration (mesenteric panniculitis). 99mTc bone scintigraphy and PET/CT revealed typical bone involvement. Brain MRI showed central nervous system (CNS) involvement, while echocardiography, cardiac CT, and MRI identified a right atrial pseudotumor with pericardial effusion. Treatment with a BRAF inhibitor (vemurafenib) and a MEK inhibitor (cobimetinib) was initiated.

articles.title: Data Collection on Rare Coagulation Disorders: Focus on Patients with Coagulation Factor X Deficiency.
articles.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inherited coagulation factor X (FX) deficiency is an ultra-rare coagulation disorder (estimated prevalence ∼1:1,000,000), characterized by reduced FX activity (FX:C) and bleeding manifestations, ranging from mild to life-threatening hemorrhage. Due to its rarity, management is currently guided by case reports and expert opinion rather than evidence-based guidelines.

OBJECTIVES: The Prospective Rare Bleeding Disorders Database on Coagulation Factor X Deficiency (PRO-RBDD-FX) aims to quantify bleeding rates, identify FX:C thresholds protective against major spontaneous bleeding and evaluate treatment efficacy and safety. A secondary objective is to assess the health-related quality of life (HrQoL).

METHODS: PRO-RBDD-FX is an observational study utilizing a web-based platform for the collection of retrospective and prospective longitudinal data. The registry enrolls affected probands and their first-degree relatives. Standardized demographic, clinical, laboratory, genetic, and treatment-related data are collected through dedicated modules covering bleeding manifestations, surgery, prophylaxis, thrombosis, laboratory phenotype assessment, genetics, and HrQoL. Bleeding severity is quantified using the ISTH-BAT and the EN-RBD-BSS, while HrQoL is assessed through EuroQoL questionnaires.

RESULTS: The PRO-RBDD-FX project resulted in the development of a web-based registry dedicated to FX deficiency. The platform integrates clinical, laboratory, genetic, therapeutic, and patient-reported outcome data within a unified longitudinal follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: The disease-specific modules developed herein support future natural history and genotype-phenotype studies. The PRO-RBDD-FX registry represents a tool for advancing research in ultra-rare diseases, bridging the gap between laboratory findings and clinical reality promoting standardized personalized care.

articles.title: RNA-binding protein CLUH ameliorates metabolic-associated steatohepatitis pathogenesis by maintaining ER homeostasis.
articles.abstract: CLUH, an RNA-binding protein (RBP), is known to regulate liver metabolism under conditions of acute nutrient stress. However, its role in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MAFLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remains unknown. Here, we show that CLUH is downregulated in the methionine-choline-deficient (MCD) mouse model of MASH, as well as in MAFLD and MASH patients. Whereas overexpression of CLUH alleviates hepatic lipid accumulation, fibrosis, and serum AST and ALT levels induced by the MCD diet. Mechanistically, we found that CLUH regulates mitochondrial health, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and cell death by regulating Agxt2 expression. Collectively, our findings identify CLUH as a novel regulator of ER homeostasis and a potential target to treat MASH.

articles.title: [Nervous System Anomalies in infants less than one year of Valencian Region (Spain). A descriptive epidemiological study (2007-2022)].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Nervous system congenital anomalies (NSCA) are an important health problem and represent a high perinatal and infant mortality. The aim of this paper was to determine and describe the trend and distribution of the NSCA in the Valencian Region, in children under one year of age, during the period 2007-2022.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was performed. Live births, stillbirths and termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly with NSCA were selected from the congenital anomalies population-based Registry of Valencian Region between 2007-2022. The study variables were described, the prevalence according to EUROCAT methodology per 10,000 births (included live and still birth) and the survival rate in live births was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Statistical analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel and IBM SPSS Statistics 23.

RESULTS: 1,862 cases were identified, the overall prevalence was 26.1/10,000 births. The most common type of end-pregnancy was live births (54.6%) and Hydrocephalus was the most frequent congenital malformation subgroup of NSCA (20.7%). In live births, the survival rate was 94.9% and statistically significant differences were identified according to NSCA. Regarding the pregnant women, mean age was 31.9 years and the majority birth country was Spain (69.1%). The highest prevalence was in the group under twenty years old (38.4/10,000 births) and in pregnant women resident in Castellon (34.1/10,000 births).

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of cases with NSCA is similar than European network registries of congenital anomalies. Identifying higher prevalence of cases among the youngest pregnant women or residents in Castellon, it could be connected to the higher presence in that province of pregnant women from certain countries.

articles.title: Caregivers perspectives on multidisciplinary clinic visits for Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy.
articles.abstract: BackgroundA multidisciplinary team (MDT) care model has been advocated for patients with Duchenne and Becker Muscular dystrophy (DBMD) to provide comprehensive care. We aimed to study the perspectives of parents and/or caregivers of individuals with DBMD on MDT clinic visits.MethodsA survey via non-personalized REDCap link was emailed to registered parents/caregivers through the Duchenne Registry provided by Parent Project Muscular Dystrophy (PPMD). The survey contained questions concerning individuals' demographics, and medical information, as well as knowledge and perspectives on MDT visits. Descriptive and association statistics were utilized.ResultsOf the 186 respondents, 166 cared for individuals with Duchenne and 20 for Becker. 117 of the respondents noted that their children receive care from one of the PPMD Certified Duchenne Care Centers. Average travel distance to the care site was 228.37 miles. 75% had their visits within 1 day, 19 % had 2 days visit, and 6% had more than 2 days. Majority (89%) preferred to have MDT appointments with all of their care providers at once and 89.4% commented that they had enough time with each of the providers. 77% noted that the duration of MDT visits was just right. 86.1% were satisfied with the care received from MDT visits. Participant comments underscored concerns regarding travel inconveniences, visit duration, standardization of care, and transition of care.DiscussionOur findings support continued implementation of MDT care and visits for individuals with DBMD, with an emphasis on optimizing visit efficiency and accommodating patients with complex medical needs.

articles.title: Treatment of Delayed Meconium Passage in Preterm Infants: A Systematic Review of Timing and Effect.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Meconium passage is often delayed in preterm infants and assumed to be related to delayed adaptation to enteral nutrition, meconium-related ileus, necrotizing enterocolitis, intestinal perforation and sepsis. While a definition for indication of treatment is lacking, strategies can be divided between a prophylactic approach: treatment is initiated within the first 48 h after birth irrespective of clinical symptoms, or a therapeutic approach: treatment is not initiated for at least 48 h after birth, and only indicated if clinical symptoms develop. This study systematically reviewed the efficacy and safety of prophylactic versus therapeutic treatments and compared various laxatives, with a focus on treatment-related side effects.

METHODS: Literature search was conducted in four databases up to 19 July 2025. Participants included preterm infants; studies were limited to rectal strategies and excluded pathological intestinal obstructions. The review was conducted according to standards for systematic reviews and registered prior to commencement.

RESULTS: Six studies with moderate to high risk of bias were included (956 infants). The studies showed inconsistent findings regarding the timing of meconium passage and varying side effects of the treatments.

CONCLUSION: No evidence-based recommendations can be made regarding timing of treatment or laxative type.

articles.title: Malignant Ventricular Arrhythmias following Pulsed Field Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A systematic review of published cases and mechanistic insights.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange in Amatoxin-associated pediatric acute liver failure-Results from the Amanita-PEX study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric acute liver failure (PALF) is a rare but life-threatening condition. Amanita poisoning can lead to PALF with rapid clinical deterioration. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has been proposed as a potential supportive intervention and is established in adult acute liver failure. Evidence regarding TPE in Amanita toxin-induced PALF (AT-PALF) remains scarce, and clinical practice varies across liver transplant centers.

METHODS: The Amanita-PEX study is a retrospective, international, multicenter cohort study including pediatric patients with AT-PALF treated between 2013 and 2024. The combined primary endpoint was 28-day transplant-free survival.

RESULTS: A total of 30 patients from 10 centers were included; 17 received at least one session of TPE, and 13 were treated with standard-of-care (SOC) alone. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The overall 28-day transplant-free survival rate was 53.3% (16/30), with a 28-day mortality of 10% (3/30). All patients received N-acetylcysteine, and 93% were treated with silibinin. Native liver survival did not differ significantly between the TPE and SOC groups (47% vs. 62%, p = 0.63). In contrast, transplant-free survival was primarily associated with established markers of liver failure severity and organ dysfunction, including MELD and LIU scores, the degree of hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and the need for vasopressors or mechanical ventilation. After adjusting for these prognostic markers, TPE remained unassociated with improved outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of children with AT-PALF, adjunctive TPE showed no clear improvement in transplant-free survival. Outcomes were predominantly determined by the severity of liver injury and multi-organ dysfunction.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06187220, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/.

articles.title: A new validated UHPLC method for the simultaneous determination of diclofenac sodium and oxacillin sodium monohydrate for their combined dosage form for dermal delivery.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: The rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among biofilm-forming pathogens such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), has intensified the need for therapeutic strategies capable of improving antibacterial efficacy against resistant infections. Although nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) exhibit limited intrinsic antimicrobial activity, growing evidence suggests that certain NSAIDs can potentiate conventional antibiotics, producing synergistic antibacterial and antibiofilm effects. Accordingly, the combined delivery of an NSAID and an antibiotic represents a promising approach for simultaneously targeting infection-associated inflammation and bacterial persistence while potentially enhancing antibacterial activity. Incorporation of such drug combinations into nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) may further support topical delivery; however, reliable simultaneous quantification of both drugs within this complex lipid-based system remains analytically challenging. An ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography method with diode array detection (UHPLC-DAD) was developed and validated for the simultaneous quantification of oxacillin sodium monohydrate and diclofenac sodium in nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) intended for dermal delivery. Chromatographic separation was achieved on an XTerra MS C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) using gradient elution with 0.05 M orthophosphoric acid in water and acetonitrile at a flow rate of 1.0 mL min-1, with detection at 210 nm. Oxacillin and diclofenac were baseline separated with retention times of 8.74 and 13.73 min, respectively. The method was validated in accordance with International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines and demonstrated linearity over the concentration range of 5-100 µg mL-1 for both analytes (R2 ≥ 0.9996). The limits of detection and quantification were 1.38 and 4.18 µg mL-1 for oxacillin, and 2.69 and 8.15 µg mL-1 for diclofenac, respectively. Precision was satisfactory, with intra-day and inter-day relative standard deviation values below 3%. Specificity was confirmed by the absence of matrix interference, while recovery studies demonstrated acceptable accuracy for both analytes in the formulation matrix. Under thermal (65 °C) and photolytic (405 nm) stress conditions, oxacillin showed recoveries of 81.16-97.77%, while diclofenac showed recoveries of 84.92-93.50%, indicating reduced recovery following stress exposure. The proposed method is reliable for the routine quantification of both drugs in dual-drug lipid-based formulations and is applicable to quality control, formulation development, and permeation studies.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery in Patients on Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Prisma Guided Systematic Review and Propensity Score Matched Cohort Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (HD) have limited physiologic reserve and high competing cardiometabolic risk, yet surgery remains central to cure for many gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies. Evidence describing oncologic surgery in this population is fragmented across cancer sites and data sources.

METHODS: A PRISMA guided systematic review of adult patients on maintenance HD undergoing resection for GI malignancy was performed. The review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL through March 2026 and included comparative observational studies reporting perioperative or long-term outcomes. In parallel, a propensity-score matched TriNetX cohort of adults undergoing major GI cancer surgery between 2010 and 2025. HD was defined by preoperative ESRD and dialysis dependence codes. Patients were matched 1:1 on age, sex, race, and ethnicity. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes were 30-day sepsis, pneumonia, and acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

RESULTS: The review included 20 studies after screening 1,744 deduplicated records and 83 full texts. Colorectal surgery provided the most robust evidence: dialysis was associated with markedly higher mortality and serious morbidity, and a published meta-analysis of colorectal surgery estimated a pooled mortality odds ratio (OR) of 4.12. Gastric, pancreatic, and hepatobiliary reports were smaller but showed the same direction of effect, with frequent infectious and cardiovascular complications and substantial competing non-cancer mortality. In the current TriNetX analysis, 3,757 HD patients were matched to 3757 non-HD controls. Thirty-day mortality was 11.4% in HD patients versus 3.0% in controls (OR: 4.21, 95% CI: 3.40-5.22). HD patients also had higher rates of sepsis (14.1% vs. 3.9%; OR 4.06), pneumonia (8.1% vs. 2.2%; OR: 4.02), and AMI (4.3% vs. 0.9%; OR: 5.18).

CONCLUSIONS: Across GI cancer operations, maintenance HD identifies a very high-risk surgical phenotype. The dominant short-term pattern is excess death, infection, and cardiopulmonary morbidity; the dominant long-term pattern is competing non-cancer mortality. Surgery remains appropriate for selected patients with resectable disease, but perioperative dialysis timing, multidisciplinary optimization, and treatment in experienced centers are critical.

articles.title: Digital stool color screening for biliary atresia-Comparing a deep learning approach to the analogue stool color card.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Early diagnosis of Biliary atresia (BA) improves native liver and overall survival. Pale stools are a characteristic symptom and might be detected by deep learning image recognition. We tested convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify pictures of pale and healthy stools and compare the results with stool color card (SCC) assessment of health care professionals (HCP) and non-health care professionals (NHCP).

METHODS: One thousand six hundred and sixteen stool photos with diagnostic labels including BA and healthy controls were graded as pale or normal according to the SCC. A subset of photos (33 BA and 241 healthy) was presented to HCP and NHCP for SCC assessment to evaluate accuracy and interobserver reliability. For CNN model selection and training all images were split into training, validation, and test sets. Different visualization strategies and secondary data augmentation were used for explainability and estimating robustness.

RESULTS: In SCC assessment, sensitivity by NHCP trended lower than HCP (86.4% vs. 97.3%), while there were no differences in specificity. Intra-cohort agreement on classification of BA stools (pale vs. normal) was also lower for NHCP than for HCP (36.4% vs. 78.8%), while no significant difference was observed in healthy stools. The selected CNN (ResNet18) correctly classified 97.5% of pale and 98.5% of normal labeled stools, also showing robust results in explainability methods.

CONCLUSIONS: The high accuracy of CNN shows the potential for a digital stool color screening. In contrast, NHCP assessment of pale stools tends to be inconsistent, and there is high interobserver variability among HCP and NHCP.

articles.title: Fructose as a systemic metabolic signal orchestrating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease pathogenesis.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in food science and nutrition
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of the global population, yet the specific role of dietary fructose in disease progression remains inadequately defined. This review delineates the "Fructose-ectopic lipid accumulation (ELA)-MASLD" axis, identifying refined fructose (e.g., from sugar-sweetened beverages) not merely as a substrate but as a systemic signal that coordinates a pathological metabolic network. Hepatic fructose metabolism via the ketohexokinase-C (KHK-C) pathway bypasses the rate-limiting phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) checkpoint, promotes unregulated de novo lipogenesis (DNL), ATP depletion, and organellar stress. We identify the functional decline of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) plasticity as an important driver of this lipotoxic cascade. This tends to result in systemic lipid spillover, promoting an inflammatory cascade that impairs the intestinal barrier and induces insulin resistance (IR) in skeletal muscle and bystander organs. Furthermore, we discuss how genetic variants amplify this toxicity and critically evaluate emerging preclinical hypotheses regarding epigenetic remodeling and transgenerational inheritance. Finally, we propose stratified management strategies that integrate evidence-based nutritional modifications with targeted pharmacotherapy, distinguishing between hepatic-dominant and adipose-derived lipid excess to optimize clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Characteristics and Survival of Patients With Colonic Compared to Rectal Neuroendocrine Tumors: A SEER Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Colon and rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) have varying disease behaviors, presentations, and outcomes. Rectal NETs are detected early; colonic NETs present later and more aggressively. We compared demographic, tumor, treatment, and survival characteristics of colonic versus rectal NETs.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used SEER data (2000-2022) to identify adults with colonic or rectal NETs. Demographic, tumor, and treatment characteristics were compared by tumor site. Five-year overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier statistics and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Additional site-specific analyses evaluated stage and treatment patterns by race, ethnicity, and household income.

RESULTS: Twenty-four percent of 30 246 patients had colonic NETs, and 76.0% had rectal NETs. Rectal NET patients were younger (55.7 vs. 62.9 years, p < 0.001) and more often Black, Asian, or Hispanic. Colonic NETs were more frequently poorly differentiated (43.9% vs. 7.0%), larger (median 30 vs. 5 mm), and more likely to have liver metastases (27.7% vs. 3.7%). Rectal NETs underwent local excision (92.1%), colonic NETs required colectomy (72.3%). Rectal NETs demonstrated higher 5-year OS (88.8% vs. 55.8%) and CSS (93.8% vs. 58.2%, p < 0.001). Stage III colonic NETs had higher CSS than rectal NETs (67.3% vs. 53.5%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Colonic and rectal NETs have distinct clinicopathologic profiles, treatment patterns, and stage-specific outcomes. These findings support site-specific evaluation while emphasizing the importance of stage and tumor biology in prognosis.

articles.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence-Driven Neutrosophic Multi-Objective Optimization of Oxygen Transfer Systems in Smart Bioreactors.
articles.abstract: Oxygen transfer control in industrial bioreactors becomes more complex when cell metabolic changes, nonlinear process dynamics, energy constraints, and biological and operational uncertainties simultaneously affect control decisions. This study presents an innovative framework for intelligent oxygenation management that integrates a synchronized digital twin, agent-based artificial intelligence, fuzzy-notrosophic modeling, and multi-objective decision-making in a closed, uncertainty-aware loop. The proposed framework enables predictive and safe decision-making under variable conditions by continuously monitoring and reconstructing the process state, predicting short-term behavior, generating and screening control options, and virtually evaluating them before implementation. Evaluation under normal operating conditions and biological and process disturbances showed that the complete framework achieved 98.04% dissolved oxygen stability and reduced the recovery time after oxygen demand shock to 7.26 min. The findings show that the main value of this architecture lies not in the single maximization of oxygen transfer, but in creating an adaptive balance between oxygen delivery, energy consumption, shear stress, biological stability, and operational risk. This framework provides an extensible platform for moving toward autonomous, resilient, and sustainable bioreactors.

articles.title: The Origins of Allergy: An Outside-In, Bioenergetic Hypothesis.
articles.abstract: Allergic disease has risen too rapidly for inherited susceptibility to explain it, and the risk variants so far reported lie in the epithelial barrier and in type-2 immunity. We propose a five-layer model in which epithelial barrier and bioenergetic dysfunction may precede and promote type-2 immune deviation rather than arise solely as its consequence, progressing from (1) barrier and bioenergetic dysfunction, with mitochondrial DNA escaping into the cytosol, through (2) danger sensing and (3) epithelial-immune communication, to (4) type-2 immune amplification and (5) a systemic layer of circulating IgE, neurogenic amplification and the atopic march, with reciprocal inflammatory feedback. Layer 1 is also the least measured: standard immune panels carry almost none of these genes, and no genome-wide association study has implicated the mitochondrial genome or its nuclear regulators. From 1856 catalogued transcriptomic series, 985 of them expression series, we drew 116 case-control cohorts from 110 series, 3776 patients and 2164 controls, with Layer 1 prespecified as 350 genes across 19 domains. Of 212 module estimates nine survived false-discovery correction: two type-2 positive controls, two cytosolic sensing and inflammasome modules, raised in oesophageal tissue (Hedges' g +1.70) and atopic skin (+1.27), and five bioenergetic modules in oesophageal tissue. In eosinophilic oesophagitis the mitochondrial clearance limb was reduced in every one of thirteen cohorts (HIF1A -1.94, BNIP3-1.98). STING1 increased in all thirteen skin cohorts that measured it while MAVS fell in ten of thirteen oesophageal cohorts, and a STING1 minus MAVS contrast separated the allergic epithelia from psoriasis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma without exception (exact p 0.029). In one series of clinically uninvolved atopic skin KEAP1 increased while NFE2L2, claudin-1 and filaggrin decreased (p < 0.001), in tissue that is not inflamed; pooled across nine series the directions largely hold without reaching significance. Broad suppression of mitochondrial programmes across allergic tissues was not supported: the phenotype is tissue-dependent, present in eosinophilic oesophagitis and atopic dermatitis, absent in nasal polyposis and established asthma and conditional in allergic rhinitis. Prospective and experimental studies must establish temporal and causal relationships.

articles.title: From CYP450 pharmacogenomics to personalized medicine: clinical evidence, dosing guidelines, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Interindividual variability in drug response remains a critical challenge in contemporary pharmacotherapy, and cytochrome P450 (CYP450) genetic polymorphisms are a principal determinant of this heterogeneity. The CYP450 superfamily mediates the oxidative biotransformation of 70-80% of clinically prescribed medications. Genetic variants in key isoforms generate four distinct metabolizer phenotypes, producing up to 1000-fold interindividual differences in drug clearance that directly translate into therapeutic failure, adverse drug reactions, or life-threatening toxicity. This review critically synthesizes current mechanistic, clinical, and translational evidence on CYP450 pharmacogenomics, emphasizing genotype-guided individualized dosing across anticoagulation, antiplatelet therapy, oncology, neuropsychiatry, and solid organ transplantation. Guidelines from the Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group, the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium, and the FDA are evaluated alongside phenotype-specific dosing algorithms. Emerging approaches are examined, including model-informed precision dosing, Bayesian pharmacokinetic forecasting, next-generation sequencing for haplotype resolution, and artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support. Persistent barriers, including phenoconversion by drug-drug interactions, under-representation of populations in pharmacogenomic datasets, and inconsistent guideline adoption, are critically appraised. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant literature published between 1978 and 2026. Coordinated global integration of CYP450 genotyping into routine clinical workflows is needed to advance the transition from reactive to preemptive, genuinely personalized pharmacotherapy.

articles.title: Feasibility of Longitudinal Home Monitoring of Nocturnal Transcutaneous CO2 and Relationship to Standard Respiratory Measures in Patients With ALS: A Pilot Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) results in respiratory muscle weakness causing hypoventilation, retention of carbon dioxide (CO2), and chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure. In this pilot study, we performed a 12-month assessment of daytime and home nocturnal CO2 to track respiratory progression, determine relationships with surrogate respiratory measures, and assess the impact of non-invasive ventilatory support.

METHODS: Adults with forced vital capacity (FVC) less than 90% predicted secondary to ALS were recruited from two sites in the northeast US. Participants were followed up at standard visits every 3 months for up to five visits. Spirometry, functional scores, and patient-reported outcomes of dyspnea were recorded. Each visit included a 15-min, seated measurement of transcutaneous CO2 (PtcCO2) while in clinic, followed by 3 nights of home overnight PtcCO2 monitoring. Linear mixed-effects models were employed to describe the changes that occurred longitudinally and resulting from the initiation of non-invasive ventilation (NIV).

RESULTS: Sixteen subjects were enrolled, with nine completing the full study. Strength and FVC declined over time, while daytime PtcCO2 remained stable. Five individuals demonstrated nocturnal hypercapnia that preceded FVC < 50% predicted normal. Transition to NIV was associated with a 7 mmHg decrease in nocturnal PtcCO2.

DISCUSSION: Home nocturnal PtcCO2 assessment in ALS may identify respiratory insufficiency prior to FVC. Transcutaneous CO2 may play a role in the respiratory management of patients as a biomarker for hypoventilation risk and NIV titration. However, equipment availability and data quality limitations would benefit from professional assistance rather than independent in-home use.

articles.title: Natural and engineered bacteriophages against multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens: current landscape and clinical translation.
articles.abstract: The worldwide emergence of antimicrobial resistance and the need for non-conventional alternatives to conventional antibiotics have been increased by multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens, which cause the majority of nosocomial infections and are starting to develop resistance to even the most potent drugs. Engineered bacteriophages are promising precision antimicrobials because of their ability to selectively infect and lyse bacterial hosts, multiply at infection sites, and co-evolve with bacterial populations to overcome resistance. Advances in synthetic biology, such as tail fiber modification, depolymerase and endolysin enhancement, genome editing using the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR), and computationally designed phage cocktails, have opened new possibilities for therapeutics that were hindered by the limitations of natural phages. These engineering strategies expand host range, enhance biofilm penetration, and target resistance genes. In spite of promising evidence in preclinical models, the use of engineered phages in routine clinical practice remains difficult. Specific key challenges include unclear regulations, lack of good manufacturing practice (GMP)grade production, variable pharmacokinetics and limited clinical trial data. This review critically examines engineering approaches to improve phage activity against ESKAPE pathogens, identifies the scientific and regulatory barriers limiting clinical use, and outlines the key steps needed for wider adoption.

articles.title: Detection method for carrying Hepatitis B surface antigen exosomes by a chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA).
articles.abstract:
AIM: Conventional detection of Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) cannot differentiate exosome-associated antigen from its free form, which may hold distinct biological significance. Here, we developed a specific chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) to detect HBsAg-positive, CD63-positive particles (putative HBsAg-carrying exosomes).

METHODS: The assay employs magnetic beads coated with an anti-HBsAg antibody for exosome capture, followed by detection using an acridinium ester-labeled anti-CD63 antibody. All performance evaluations were conducted in normal human serum as the biological matrix.

RESULTS: Analytical validation established cutoff value of 4,421 RLU from 80 blank replicates (per CLSI EP17-A2). The method demonstrated complete analytical agreement with the engineered reference samples tested (n = 15 negative; n = 5 positive). The limit of detection was 7.8 × 108 particles/mL, corresponding to a sample dilution factor of 128. Intra- and inter-assay precision yielded coefficients of variation below 15% across the measuring range.

CONCLUSION: This CLIA provides an analytically validated qualitative screening tool for research use (classifying samples as positive or negative based on the established cutoff of 4,421 RLU) for the in vitro detection of HBsAg-positive, CD63-positive particles, facilitating future research into the role of exosomal cargo in Hepatitis B virus pathogenesis.

articles.title: Relationship Between the eTICI Score Before Randomization and 90-Day Outcome: A Post Hoc Analysis of ANGEL-TNK Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Successful thrombectomy recanalization combined with intraarterial thrombolysis showed potential benefits in achieving excellent outcomes in recent trials, but the results were inconsistent. We performed this study to investigate the efficacy and safety of interarterial thrombolysis in patients stratified by expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) score after thrombectomy.

METHODS: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of the ANGEL-TNK trial (Intraarterial Recombinant Human TNK-tPA Thrombolysis for Acute LVO After Successful Mechanical Thrombectomy Recanalization; multicenter, randomized, open-label, blinded end point). Participants who had anterior circulation large artery occlusion were enrolled and randomized (1:1) to interarterial tenecteplase (TNK; 0.125 mg/kg) or standard medical management after eTICI 2b50 to 3 reperfusion. The primary outcome was the rate of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours, and death within 90 days.

RESULTS: Of the 253 patients enrolled, 164 were in the eTICI 2b50 to 67 group, and 89 were in the eTICI 2c to 3 group. Interarterial TNK after EVT was associated with a higher rate of modified Rankin Scale score 0 to 1 at 90 days in patients with an eTICI score of 2b50 to 67 (39 [44.8%] versus 15 [19.5%]; relative risk, 2.08 [95% CI, 1.35-3.21]; P=0.001), but not in those with eTICI 2c to 3 (12 [30.8%] versus 19 [38.0%]; relative risk, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.29-2.44]; P=0.749). In the eTICI 2c to 3 group, interarterial TNK resulted in more cases of any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours (13 [33.3%] versus 10 [20.0%]; relative risk, 1.70 [95% CI, 1.05-2.77]; P=0.032), but not in the eTICI 2b50 to 67 group (18 [20.7%] versus 25 [32.5%]; relative risk, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.34-1.22]; P=0.176). The difference was not observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours or death within 90 days in either group.

CONCLUSIONS: Interarterial TNK after EVT provides additional benefits for excellent outcomes, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1 at 90 days, in patients with an eTICI score of 2b50 to 67, but not in those with eTICI 2c to 3. It increases the risk of any intracranial hemorrhage in patients with an eTICI score of 2c to 3, without elevating the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or death.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05624190.

articles.title: A Korean national birthweight reference for singleton live births.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a national birth weight reference for singleton live births in Korea using nationwide data, provide sex-specific percentile charts, and compare the Korean reference with widely used international birth weight references.

METHODS: Nationwide birth registration microdata for singleton live births between 2019 and 2023 were used. The data were obtained from Statistics Korea and accessed through the MicroData Integrated Service. Smoothed gestational age (GA)-specific birth weight percentile curves were generated overall and separately for male and female neonates. The Korean reference curves were compared with the United States national birth weight reference and INTERGROWTH-21st standards.

RESULTS: 1) A total of 1,158,083 singleton live births were included in the analysis. Smoothed GA-specific birth weight percentile curves were generated overall and separately for male and female neonates. 2) Male neonates had consistently higher birth weights than female neonates across GAs, with a median difference of approximately 100 g from the third trimester onward. And 3) the Korean national birth weight reference was compared with the United States national birth weight reference and the INTERGROWTH-21st standards. The United States national reference classified 66.6% of neonates classified as large for GA by the Korean reference as appropriate for GA, whereas INTERGROWTH-21st classified 65.6% of neonates classified as small for GA by the Korean reference as appropriate for GA.

CONCLUSION: This study reports a nationwide Korean birth weight reference for singleton live births. The Korean birth weight reference differs from the widely used international references, supporting the need for population-specific charts for size assessment in Korean fetuses and neonates.

articles.title: Clopidogrel Versus Aspirin Monotherapy According to Atherothrombotic Risk Profile.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel monotherapy has shown superior efficacy compared with aspirin after completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, whether treatment effects differ according to overall atherothrombotic risk integrating clinical and angiographic factors remains unclear.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SMART-CHOICE 3 (Smart Angioplasty Research Team: Choice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) randomized trial included patients who completed guideline-directed dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI. Atherothrombotic risk was defined using the a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention and complex PCI. Patients with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention ≥3 or complex PCI were classified as higher risk, and those with a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention <3 without complex PCI were classified as lower risk. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke). Bleeding was defined as Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2, 3, or 5.

RESULTS: Among 5506 patients, 4486 (81.5%) were at higher risk and 1020 (18.5%) were at lower risk. Over a median 2.3 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events was higher in the higher-risk group (6.1% versus 3.1%; hazard ratio, 1.83 [95% CI, 1.17-2.78]; P=0.007). In higher-risk patients, clopidogrel reduced major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events compared with aspirin (4.6% versus 7.4%; hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.50-0.89]; P=0.006), with no difference in lower-risk patients (3.0% versus 3.2%; hazard ratio, 1.03; P=0.945; interaction P=0.242). Bleeding was similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: After completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with lower ischemic risk than aspirin in patients with higher atherothrombotic risk, without increased bleeding.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04418479.

articles.title: Comparative Safety and Efficacy of Oral Anticoagulants in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Prior Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized-Controlled Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and prior ischemic stroke represent a high-risk population facing competing risks of recurrent thromboembolism and hemorrhagic complications. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended over vitamin K antagonists for stroke prevention in AF, no randomized controlled clinical trial has directly compared individual DOACs to each other in this population.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized-controlled clinical trials enrolling patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. MEDLINE, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary outcome was any stroke. Secondary outcomes included ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs.

RESULTS: The evidence network comprised 6 trials (18 395 patients) in a star-shaped structure. Each DOAC was informed by a single warfarin-controlled trial, and 2 trials used aspirin as the comparator. All between-DOAC comparisons were indirect. In the network meta-analysis, compared with warfarin, apixaban was the only agent to significantly reduce both any stroke (RR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.53-0.97]) and major bleeding (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]). Dabigatran, apixaban, and edoxaban each significantly reduced hemorrhagic stroke and ICH versus warfarin, whereas rivaroxaban did not reach significance for any bleeding outcome. Edoxaban was the only agent associated with significantly lower cardiovascular (RR, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.65-0.97]) and all-cause mortality (RR, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.72-0.99]). Based on indirect comparisons only, no differences between individual DOACs were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke, individual DOACs reduced intracranial and systemic bleeding relative to warfarin, although not uniformly across agents. Apixaban alone significantly reduced both any stroke and major bleeding versus warfarin, but differences between individual DOACs could not be established given the small number of trials.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/; Unique identifier: CRD420261404062.

articles.title: Impact of Inflammatory Burden on Outcomes After Breakthrough Ischemic Stroke: Insights From the ASPERA-R Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation who experience ischemic stroke despite oral anticoagulation (breakthrough stroke) remain at high risk of recurrent vascular events and death. Although inflammation has been associated with thromboembolic risk, its prognostic role in breakthrough stroke remains unclear. We investigated whether a composite inflammatory burden index was associated with adverse outcomes after breakthrough ischemic stroke.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke from the ASPERA-R registry. Inflammatory burden was assessed using admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and C-reactive protein. Biomarkers were log-transformed, standardized using Z scores, and combined into a composite inflammatory burden index. Patients were classified as having high (upper tertile) or lower inflammatory burden (lower 2 tertiles). Outcomes included new 90-day ischemic events (recurrent ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism), 24-hour hemorrhagic transformation, and 90-day moderate-to-severe bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, and mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting accounted for center, demographics, vascular risk factors and comorbidities, anticoagulation, competing stroke causes, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, prestroke modified Rankin Scale, and time to blood collection.

RESULTS: Among 1649 patients enrolled in ASPERA-R, 671 patients from 14 centers had complete biomarker data (median age, 80.1 years [interquartile range, 73.5-85.5]; 52.3% female). Of these, 223 (33.2%) had high inflammatory burden, and 448 (66.8%) had lower inflammatory burden. After weighting, high inflammatory burden was associated with increased risks of ischemic events at 90 days (hazard ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.02-2.30]), all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.70 [95% CI, 1.17-2.47]), moderate-to-severe bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.92 [95% CI, 1.04-8.17]), and hemorrhagic transformation at 24 hours (odds ratio, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.43-3.33]).

CONCLUSIONS: In breakthrough ischemic stroke, high inflammatory burden was associated with increased risks of recurrent ischemic events, mortality, hemorrhagic transformation, and major bleeding. A composite of routinely available inflammatory biomarkers may help identify patients with higher residual vascular risk.

articles.title: Antiviral nanoparticles: mechanisms, biomedical applications and clinical translation toward next-generation therapies.
articles.abstract: Viral infections represent a major global health challenge due to the rapid emergence of new pathogens, increasing antiviral drug resistance and limited efficacy of traditional treatments against evolving viruses. Nanotechnology is a promising interdisciplinary approach to fighting viral diseases, which can perform direct viral inactivation, targeted drug delivery, immune modulation, vaccine development, rapid diagnostics, and prevention of infection. This review offers an in-depth and critical overview of the major antiviral nanoparticle platforms, including metallic, metal oxide, carbon-based, polymeric, lipid-based, and bio-inspired nanoparticles. In this article, we employ a comparative framework to systematically analyze classes of nanoparticles based on their physicochemical properties, molecular mechanisms of antiviral action, biomedical applications, and translational potential. Antiviral mechanisms are discussed within the framework of the viral life cycle, including the inhibition of viral attachment and entry, destruction of viral envelope and capsid integrity, suppression of intracellular viral replication, reactive oxygen species-mediated viral inactivation, immune-modulation, and nanoparticle-assisted therapeutic delivery. Moreover, the review critically discusses the increasing biomedical applications of antiviral nanoparticles in therapeutics, vaccine delivery, diagnostics, antiviral coatings, gene therapy and precision nanomedicine, while highlighting the clinically successful technologies such as lipid nanoparticle-based mRNA vaccines. Special attention is paid to the main obstacles in clinical translation, such as nanotoxicity, biodistribution, manufacturing scalability, regulatory challenges, and the lack of standard evaluation protocols. Finally, major knowledge gaps and future research priorities are highlighted, focusing on the design of multifunctional, clinically translatable and regulatory-compliant nanoplatforms. This review offers insights on antiviral nanomedicines and practical insights for the rational design and successful clinical translation of next-generation antiviral nanoparticle.

articles.title: VSMC DDR1 Mechanosensation Aggravates Atherosclerosis via Paracrine Signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases cardiovascular risk and is linked to arterial stiffening and atherosclerosis. How stiffness promotes atherogenesis remains unclear. DDR1 (discoidin domain receptor 1), a mechanosensory tyrosine kinase receptor, has been implicated in force-regulated arterial remodeling. We investigated whether DDR1-mediated mechanosensation links arterial stiffness to vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC)-endothelial paracrine communication in CKD-related atherosclerosis.

METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, secretome proteomics, and bulk RNA sequencing were integrated with stiffness-controlled models, endothelial assays, and a CKD-hyperlipidemia mouse model. SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion and a DDR1 dephosphorylation-targeting chimera (DEPTAC) were evaluated in vivo. Plasma TSP-1 (thrombospondin-1) levels were quantified in a CKD clinical cohort and analyzed in relation to renal function and atherosclerosis severity.

RESULTS: CKD-associated vascular stiffening coincided with SMC phenotypic switching and enhanced THBS signaling. Multiomics integration identified THBS1 as a stiffness-induced SMC secretory effector. Stiff matrices increased SMC THBS1 secretion, promoting endothelial proliferation, migration, and leukocyte adhesion; these effects were attenuated by THBS1 knockdown. DDR1 coupled matrix stiffness cues to THBS1 expression by regulating its transcription via a tyrosine 3-monooxygenase/tryptophan 5-monooxygenase activation protein epsilon-FOXO3 (forkhead box O3) axis. Vascular SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion reduced aortic THBS1 levels, vascular stiffening, and atherosclerotic burden. DEPTAC suppressed aberrant DDR1 phosphorylation, reduced THBS1, and ameliorated vascular stiffening and atherosclerosis. Plasma THBS1 increased with CKD severity and correlated with atherosclerosis.

CONCLUSIONS: DDR1-dependent mechanosensing in SMCs drives stiffness-induced paracrine signaling to endothelium via THBS1, promoting CKD-accelerated atherosclerosis. Targeting mechanical DDR1 activation may be therapeutic.

articles.title: Endothelin 2-Mediated Neuroinflammation Drives Hypertensive Retinal Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic hypertension is a risk factor for glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, yet the mechanistic basis connecting the 2 conditions remains elusive.

METHODS: A longitudinal assessment of blood pressure, intraocular pressure, retinal function, structure, and perfusion was conducted in spontaneously hypertensive rats and Wistar-Kyoto rats. Transcriptomic analyses and immunofluorescence staining were performed to investigate hypertension-associated retinal biochemical changes. AAV-mediated knockdown of endothelin 2 was used to investigate its mechanistic role.

RESULTS: Hypertensive rats develop accelerated retinal degeneration marked by retinal thinning, functional impairment, reduced perfusion, and progressive neuroinflammation. Critically, these changes occur despite persistently low intraocular pressure, indicating an intraocular pressure-independent mechanism underlying the pathology. Biochemical analyses identified robust activation of the retinal endothelin system, with endothelin 2 the most significantly upregulated component. AAV-mediated retinal endothelin 2 knockdown substantially restored retinal function, ameliorated neuroinflammation, and enhanced retinal blood flow in hypertensive rats. Pharmacological blockade of endothelin receptor type A, but not type B, replicated these protective effects without altering intraocular pressure.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish endothelin 2 as an important, intraocular pressure-independent contributing factor to hypertension-associated retinal neurodegeneration and identify the endothelin-endothelin receptor type A axis as a potential therapeutic target to prevent vision loss in patients with hypertension.

articles.title: F2R Polymorphisms and Efficacy of Clopidogrel Initiated Within 72 Hours for Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to investigate the association between PAR-1 (protease-activated receptor-1) gene F2R polymorphisms and the efficacy of clopidogrel therapy initiated within a time window extended to 72 hours for mild ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of the INSPIRES trial (Intensive Statin and Antiplatelet Therapy for Acute High-Risk Intracranial or Extracranial Atherosclerosis), a randomized clinical trial conducted at 222 centers across China between September 2018 and October 2022. Four single-nucleotide polymorphisms (F2R [IVSn-14 A/T, rs168753], CYP2C19*2 [681G>A, rs4244285], CYP2C19*3 [636G>A, rs4986893], and CYP2C19*17 [-806C>T, rs12248560]) were genotyped among 5791 patients treated with clopidogrel plus aspirin (n=2894) or aspirin alone (n=2897). The primary efficacy outcome was new stroke, and the safety outcome was moderate-to-severe bleeding within 90 days. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the interaction between treatment assignment and F2R polymorphisms for the primary outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 5791 patients, 1698 (29.3%) were AA homozygotes, and 4093 (70.7%) were the T-allele carriers (AT/TT) for F2R IVSn-14 polymorphisms. Compared with aspirin alone, clopidogrel-aspirin reduced the rate of new stroke in patients with AT/TT genotype (7.1% versus 9.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.77 [95% CI, 0.62-0.95]; P=0.02) but not in carriers of the AA genotype (7.7% versus 8.1%; HR, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.67-1.33]; P=0.75; P=0.30 for interaction). For the safety outcome, the risk of moderate-to-severe bleeding between the clopidogrel plus aspirin group and aspirin group was not significant in patients with AT/TT genotype (HR, 1.91 [95% CI, 0.85-4.29]; P=0.12) or AA genotype (HR, 1.97 [95% CI, 0.59-6.55]; P=0.27; P=0.97 for interaction). Moreover, the presence of CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele carrier status did not alter the effect of the F2R polymorphisms on clinical outcomes, although a marginally reduced risk of stroke with clopidogrel-aspirin versus aspirin alone was observed only among carriers of at least 1 F2R IVSn-14 T allele without CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.52-1.01]; P=0.06).

CONCLUSIONS: With the treatment initiated within a time window extended to 72 hours after mild ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack onset, we found that clopidogrel plus aspirin may reduce the occurrence of new stroke specifically in F2R IVSn-14 T-allele carriers. This finding suggests that the clopidogrel-aspirin treatment may appear more beneficial among carriers of the F2R IVSn-14 T allele.
