articles.title: Reported Factors Associated With Hearing Loss in Infants Admitted to Neonatal Intensive Care Units: A Scoping Review of the Evidence and Its Limitations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hearing loss (HL) is far more common in neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) graduates than in well-baby populations. Although many broadly defined 'risk factors' have been reported, their causal relevance remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: We conducted a scoping review to synthesise reported factors for HL among NICU and special care nursery (SCN) infants. We then assessed the strength of the supporting evidence.

DATA SOURCES: Embase, Medline, APA PsycInfo, and Web of Science were searched (1 Jan 2015-11 Mar 2025).

STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: We included studies that reported factors associated with HL among NICU/SCN graduates. Commentaries, conference abstracts, letters, and case reports/series were excluded. Data were extracted independently by two reviewers using a piloted Excel spreadsheet.

SYNTHESIS: We followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Reported factors were classified into categories and broad domains. We summarised adjusted associations and appraised the evidence, including indications of causal support.

RESULTS: Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, identifying 141 unique factors which were organised into six domains and 32 categories. No eligible study focused specifically on SCN infants. The most frequently studied factors were birthweight (38.5%), hyperbilirubinemia (25.0%), Apgar score (24.0%), sepsis (21.9%), and sex (20.8%). Effect estimates were infrequently reported, and evidence within categories was highly heterogeneous. Support for causal interpretation was identified in four studies (4.2%), including those of hypoxia-ischemia, encephalopathy with seizures, postnatal CMV infection, and higher frequency of vancomycin dosing. Evidence was limited by the small number of confounder-adjusted analyses, prospective or trial designs, and studies with adequate follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: The literature on NICU-related hearing loss includes many repeatedly reported associated factors, but the evidence supporting their causal role remains limited and heterogeneous. As a result, many reported factors cannot yet be interpreted as credible prevention targets. Better-designed studies for estimating causal effects are needed to support prevention-oriented decision-making.

articles.title: Editorial on "Hypermetabolic State Drives Platelet Dysfunction in Human and Mouse Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease".
Engineering a Translational Human Thrombus Platform to Evaluate Clinical Therapies in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recanalization failure after ischemic stroke remains a major clinical challenge, partly because cerebral thrombi display marked spatial heterogeneity that is poorly reproduced by experimental models. Here, we engineered a translational human blood-based thrombus platform that recapitulates key histological features of patient-derived stroke clots.

METHODS: Under controlled conditions, the platform generated reproducible thrombi with pronounced interthrombus and intrathrombus heterogeneity, including alternating red blood cell-rich and platelet-rich territories. Multiscale structural and biochemical analyses confirmed the successful replication of the clinical biphasic organization associated with resistance to rtPA (recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator): a compact outer fibrin shell containing focal accumulations of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, and a dense inner core further stabilized by neutrophil extracellular traps.

RESULTS: Functional thrombolysis assays demonstrated that this architecture directly dictates lytic susceptibility. Specifically, artificially breaching the outer fibrin shell (halved thrombi) significantly accelerated early rtPA-mediated lysis, proving its role as an effective physical barrier. Furthermore, lytic response was inherently linked to clot composition: platelet-rich thrombi with dense plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and neutrophil extracellular trap networks exhibited profound resistance to standard rtPA compared with red blood cell-rich clots. Supporting the platform's translational relevance, this structural resistance was successfully overcome by clinically relevant strategies, including tenecteplase and adjunctive DNAse, consistent with observations from human stroke cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: By accurately reproducing the spatial organization and differential thrombolytic responses of human cerebral thrombi, this translational framework provides a robust preclinical tool to dissect lytic resistance and evaluate next-generation precision reperfusion therapies. Furthermore, developing robust ex vivo human platforms is increasingly critical to align with the replacement, reduction, refinement ethical guidelines for animal research.

articles.title: Beyond Mitochondrial Fission: Emerging Roles of Drp1 in Skeletal Muscle Physiology and Disease.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1) is best recognized as the primary regulator of mitochondrial fission. However, emerging evidence indicates that Drp1 is a multifaceted regulator of skeletal muscle physiology whose functions extend well beyond its canonical role in mitochondrial fission. Recent studies have identified novel roles of Drp1 in regulating substrate utilization, calcium homeostasis, reactive oxygen species signaling, respiratory complex assembly, and mitochondrial-to-nuclear signaling, including mechanisms independent of its canonical fission activity. Importantly, Drp1 regulation in skeletal muscle is highly context-dependent, as both excessive and insufficient Drp1 activity can disrupt skeletal muscle homeostasis. For example, excessive Drp1 activation and mitochondrial fragmentation are associated with insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and neuromuscular diseases, whereas severe or prolonged Drp1 deficiency impairs mitochondrial quality control, bioenergetics, induce muscle atrophy, and compromise the exercise training adaptations. Therefore, the biological consequences of Drp1 modulation are highly context dependent and influenced by the metabolic and physiological state of skeletal muscle. In this review, we summarize the molecular regulation and emerging functions of Drp1 in skeletal muscle, with particular emphasis on fission-independent mechanisms and Drp1 dysregulation in metabolic and neuromuscular diseases. We further discuss pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies for modulating Drp1 signaling and highlight emerging approaches for skeletal muscle-specific targeting. Collectively, current evidence supports a paradigm in which skeletal muscle Drp1 functions as a multifaceted regulator of mitochondrial and skeletal muscle homeostasis, highlighting the therapeutic potential of modulating Drp1 activity to optimize mitochondrial and muscle health across different physiological and pathological contexts.

articles.title: Lithium Concentrations After Initiation or Discontinuation of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Psychiatric Inpatients: A Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce cardiovascular and renal risk, but coprescription with lithium raises concern because lithium elimination is linked to renal sodium handling. Prescribing information recommends lithium monitoring after SGLT2i initiation or dose changes, although clinical evidence remains limited, particularly after discontinuation. We describe lithium concentrations and clinical evolution after SGLT2i initiation or discontinuation in lithium-treated psychiatric inpatients.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series at a psychiatric hospital. Pharmacy records identified patients who received lithium and an SGLT2i between January 1, 2014 and March 31, 2026. Patients were included if the SGLT2i was initiated or discontinued while lithium was continued and ≥1 lithium concentration was available before and after modification. Clinical pharmacists reviewed records for lithium dose and concentrations, SGLT2i exposure, renal function, interacting medications, acute illness, hydration status, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Six cases were identified: 3 initiations and 3 discontinuations. Lithium concentrations showed no consistent directional change. After initiation, concentrations remained stable or changed minimally in 2 cases and increased slightly in one. After discontinuation, lithium remained stable in an older patient with chronic kidney disease, increased slightly in 1 case confounded by lithium dose escalation, and increased from 0.6 to 0.8 mmol/l in 1 case complicated by pneumonia, diarrhea, and dehydration. No case required urgent lithium discontinuation, toxicity treatment, or prolonged hospitalization attributed to lithium.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i initiation or discontinuation was not associated with consistent or clinically concerning lithium changes. These observations suggest coprescription may be manageable with individualized monitoring when clinically indicated.

articles.title: Surgical Intervention for Small Osteochondral Lesions (<1 cm): Proceedings of the International Consensus Meeting on Cartilage Repair of the Ankle.
authors: International Society for Cartilage Repair of the Ankle
articles.abstract: BackgroundEvidence guiding best practices in ankle cartilage repair remains limited and of poor quality. To address this, an international expert group convened to establish consensus opinions on key topics, focusing here on the treatment of small osteochondral lesions, defined as less than 1 cm.MethodsExperts from 25 countries participated in a structured Delphi-based consensus process. Blinded surveys, structured questionnaires, and in-person discussions were used to develop and refine statements, supported by literature review and graded evidence (A1-E). Consensus strength was defined as consensus (51%-74%), strong consensus (75%-99%), or unanimous (100%).ResultsFourteen of 15 proposed statements achieved consensus, including 13 with ≥86% agreement. Bone marrow stimulation (BMS) was recommended for full-thickness osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLTs) that failed conservative therapy, ideally <10 mm in diameter and <100 mm2 in area, with poorer outcomes expected in larger lesions. Experts emphasized thorough debridement to stable margins, careful subchondral perforation, and the potential value of biologic augmentation such as platelet-rich plasma or concentrated bone marrow aspirate. Repeat BMS was considered a limited option with inferior outcomes compared with primary procedures or salvage techniques.ConclusionsThis international consensus provides standardized guidance for the indications, technique, and biologic augmentation of BMS in the management of OLT. The recommendations redefine lesion size thresholds and clarify the restricted role of revision BMS, offering a global reference framework for clinical practice and future research.

articles.title: Platelet transfusion biology: from hemostatic support to inflammatory and immune signaling.
articles.abstract: Platelet transfusion remains indispensable for the prevention and treatment of bleeding in hematology, oncology, transplantation, critical care, surgery and trauma. Yet the biological impact of a platelet concentrate extends well beyond numerical correction of thrombocytopenia. Platelets are anucleate but metabolically active immune cells that express pattern-recognition receptors, release cytokines, chemokines, lipid mediators, extracellular vesicles, mitochondria-derived material and damage-associated molecular patterns; and interact with leukocytes, endothelial cells and complement. During collection, processing and storage, platelet concentrates acquire a distinct productspecific phenotype shaped by donor biology, residual plasma, additive solutions, leukoreduction, pathogen reduction, temperature and storage time. These variables affect not only post-transfusion recovery and hemostatic function, but also inflammatory signaling and immune related complications. The recipient is equally important: sepsis, chemotherapy, malignancy, neonatal immune development, endothelial activation and prior alloimmunization can determine whether transfused platelets restore hemostasis, amplify inflammation, or trigger refractoriness. This review explores platelet transfusion through the lens of a biological triad formed by the donor, the platelet product, and the recipient. We focus on how platelet immune receptors, storage-induced inflammatory remodeling, soluble biological response modifiers, extracellular vesicles and complement shape the interactions of transfused platelets with recipient leukocytes and endothelium. Alloimmunization and refractoriness are considered more briefly as recipient-dependent modifiers of platelet recovery and transfusion efficacy. The central challenge is no longer to define a single optimal platelet product, but to engineer and select the right platelet product for the right patient, at the right moment.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided core-needle biopsy for the diagnosis of calciphylaxis in a peritoneal dialysis patient.
articles.abstract: Calciphylaxis is a life-threatening and rare disease, also known as calcific uremic arteriolopathy (CUA). Skin biopsy is the gold standard for diagnosis. However, it is an invasive procedure and might aggravate the ulcer. Therefore, additional precise diagnostic approaches are needed. In this case report, a patient with end-stage renal disease receiving peritoneal dialysis presented with skin ulceration and necrosis on the left leg. Considering the risk of aggravating the existing ulcer, we performed an ultrasound-guided core-needle biopsy. Histopathological examination confirmed calcification of small- and medium-sized vessels in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, supporting the diagnosis of calciphylaxis. The patient subsequently received comprehensive treatment, including sodium thiosulfate therapy, wound care, correction of chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder, and adjustment of dialysis therapy. With comprehensive and timely treatment, the patient's skin lesions gradually improved and showed progressive healing. This case suggests that ultrasound-guided core-needle biopsy may represent a feasible diagnostic option for calciphylaxis, providing histopathological confirmation.

articles.title: Coixol, a benzoxazolinone derived from coix seed, ameliorates disordered hepatocellular programmed responses in alcoholic-associated liver disease.
articles.abstract: Coixol, a benzoxazolinone from Coix seeds, exhibits anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective effects. This study investigated its protection against alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and mechanisms. Twenty-four male C57BL/6 mice were randomly allocated into four groups (n = 6): Control, EtOH, EtOH + Coixol (25 or 50 mg/kg, oral gavage). In vitro, primary mouse hepatocytes were treated with EtOH ± Coixol (25 or 50 μM). In vivo and in vitro, SIRT6 and programmed responses (pyroptosis, apoptosis, necroptosis) were involved in EtOH-induced injury. Coixol significantly reduced serum ALT (216.2 ± 40.21 to 98.6 ± 25.5 U/L), AST (210.1 ± 41.65 to 91.6 ± 18.19 U/L), and TG (4.3 ± 0.41 to 0.9 ± 0.25 mmol/L), ameliorated histopathology and lipid accumulation. Mechanistically, Coixol upregulated SIRT6, downregulated pyroptosis (NLRP3, GSDMD, caspase-1, IL-1β), apoptosis (caspase-3, -9, BCL-2/Bax), necroptosis (P-MLKL/MLKL), and inhibited NETosis. SIRT6 deficiency attenuated Coixol's protection in EtOH-activated hepatocytes. Collectively, Coixol alleviates ALD via SIRT6-dependent regulation of programmed responses, supporting its therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Demystifying Imaging Patterns of Substance Abuse-Related Lung Injury (SARLI).
articles.journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
articles.abstract: Recreational substance abuse causes a broad spectrum of acute and chronic pulmonary injuries through inhalation and intravenous injection. Imaging findings often overlap with infection, pulmonary edema, and other inflammatory lung diseases, particularly when an exposure history is unavailable. This review discusses the mechanisms and characteristic CT imaging patterns of substance abuse-related lung injury (SARLI). Crack lung is an acute pulmonary toxicity syndrome occurring within 48 hours of crack cocaine inhalation and manifests as diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities with patchy consolidations, or a crazy-paving pattern related to pulmonary edema, diffuse alveolar damage, or alveolar hemorrhage. Cannabis smoking is associated with upper-lobe-predominant paraseptal emphysema, apical bullae, and airway inflammation. E-cigarette or vaping product use-associated lung injury is a diagnosis of exclusion and requires vaping exposure within 90 days prior to abnormal pulmonary imaging for establishing the diagnosis. It most commonly demonstrates an organizing pneumonia pattern, although diffuse alveolar damage and alveolar hemorrhage may occur. Intravenous injection of crushed oral medications can cause excipient lung disease, which has three distinct imaging patterns: diffuse centrilobular micronodules, high-attenuation perihilar and upper lobe predominant fibrotic opacities, and lower-lobe-predominant panlobular emphysema (Ritalin lung). It is often accompanied by right ventricular strain and pulmonary hypertension and can lead to sudden death and long-term deterioration of lung function. Additional complications of drug abuse include aspiration, lobar or bronchopneumonia, septic pulmonary emboli, and barotrauma. Recognition of SARLI patterns within the appropriate clinical and temporal context can help radiologists suggest the correct diagnosis and facilitate timely management.

articles.title: scMRdb: a comprehensive resource for cell-type-resolved Mendelian randomization of complex traits.
articles.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) is a powerful analytical approach to infer putative causal links between gene expression and human disease, using genetic variants as instrumental variables to mitigate confounding and reverse causation. However, existing MR resources predominantly rely on bulk-tissue expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), which mask cell-type-specific transcriptional effects by averaging expression across cellular populations. Furthermore, cell-type-resolved causal evidence from single-cell eQTL (sc-eQTL) MR analyses remains fragmented across individual studies with inconsistent workflows, prohibiting standardized cross-cell-type comparisons. Here we present scMRdb (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/scmrdb), a comprehensive resource for cell-type-resolved MR of human complex traits and diseases. scMRdb harmonizes 5206 genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics of European and East Asian ancestry with 585 sc-eQTL datasets spanning 11 tissues and cell systems, including 110 cell types. A uniform pipeline evaluates all gene-trait pairs via MR followed by Steiger directionality testing. Significant associations are assessed by colocalization, and results are stratified into six confidence tiers with integrated drug-target annotation. scMRdb enables systematic recovery of candidate causal genes supported by cell-type-resolved regulatory evidence that is often diluted or obscured in bulk-tissue analyses. We expect scMRdb to serve as a user-friendly portal for generating cell-type-informed mechanistic hypotheses and prioritizing actionable therapeutic targets for complex human diseases.

articles.title: BacMap 3.0: a comprehensive knowledgebase of annotated bacterial genomes.
articles.abstract: BacMap 3.0 (https://bacmap.ca) is a comprehensive, freely accessible resource integrating 23 524 bacterial and archaeal species, 32 866 genomes, >100 million genes, 1756 primary metabolic pathways, and 45 284 metabolites within one interactive platform. Despite the extraordinary growth of bacterial and archaeal genome sequencing, relevant data remain distributed across numerous specialized databases, impeding comprehensive genome-to-function analysis. While existing microbial resources generally emphasize genome annotation, taxonomy, metabolic pathways, or phenotypes separately, BacMap 3.0 unifies these complementary information layers within an organism-centred framework. It resolves this fragmentation by consolidating genomic, functional, structural, metabolic, phenotypic, ecological, and phylogenetic information into richly detailed, organism-specific "BacCards". Each BacCard combines an interactive genome map with extensive annotations covering bacterium-specific taxonomy, physiology, morphology, metabolism, protein structures, pathways, and metabolites. To facilitate data exploration, BacMap 3.0 supports taxonomic and phenotype-based browsing, chemical structure searches, interactive genome visualization, as well as gene, genome, 16S RNA, and protein BLAST searches. Building on earlier releases devoted primarily to genome visualization, BacMap 3.0 increases organismal coverage by >13-fold and transforms BacMap into an integrated bacterial knowledgebase for genome-to-function investigation across multiple biological scales. By bringing diverse biological information together in a single searchable environment, BacMap 3.0 offers a powerful platform for comparative genomics, microbiome research, infectious disease investigation, and biotechnology with a goal of accelerating the interpretation of microbial diversity, biology, and function.

articles.title: Direct RNA Targeting by CRISPR/Cas12: Emerging Mechanisms and Diagnostic Applications.
articles.abstract: RNA detection is essential for molecular diagnostics because it provides dynamic information on gene expression, pathogen activity, and disease progression. Conventional RNA detection methods, particularly reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), remain widely used but require RNA-to-DNA conversion, thermal cycling, and relatively complex workflows, limiting their suitability for rapid and point-of-care testing. In CRISPR diagnostics, Cas13 has traditionally been regarded as the major RNA-targeting system, whereas Cas12 enzymes have been primarily recognized as DNA-targeting nucleases. Recent studies, however, have revealed that several Cas12 variants can directly recognize RNA targets, enabling reverse-transcription-free RNA detection through mechanisms such as RNA-triggered DNase activity. In this review, we summarize the emerging functional diversity of RNA-responsive Cas12 systems, including Cas12a, Cas12a2, Cas12a3, Cas12f, and Cas12g, and discuss their underlying mechanisms for direct RNA sensing. We further highlight strategies for enhancing Cas12-mediated RNA detection, including guide and activator engineering, nanomaterial-assisted readouts, and autocatalytic signal amplification. Finally, we discuss its applications in infectious disease diagnosis, cancer biomarker detection, and environmental monitoring, alongside key challenges and future opportunities for clinical translation and point-of-care testing.

articles.title: Dynamics of the least cisco Coregonus sardinella (Valenciennes, 1848) (Salmoniformes, Salmonidae) infected with Triaenophorus crassus (Plathelminthes, Cestoda) plerocercoids in an Arctic water reservoir.
articles.abstract: The ecosystem transformation that occurred upon the regulation of the Kureyka River to create the Kureyskoye Reservoir (66°56'47″ N, 88°20'33″ E) (Yenisey River catchment) has profoundly altered the communities and led to the formation of a seat of triaenophoriasis - a disease induced in fish by the cestode Triaenophorus crassus Forel, 1868. The least cisco, Coregonus sardinella Valenciennes, 1848, which has formed a population with unique biological characteristics in the Kureyskoye Reservoir, was used as the case for studying the prevalence and abundance distribution of T. crassus plerocercoids. The helminths were found in fish of all age groups, with prevalences varying from 27.6% in young-of-the-year (0+) to 96.6% in fish aged 4+. In fish infected at high intensities, most plerocercoids were situated freely in the musculature, not encysted in connective tissue. The distribution of plerocercoids among hosts in yearlings proved to be random (fitting the Poisson distribution), becoming aggregated from the age of two years (best approximated by the negative binomial distribution). Infection intensities grow exponentially with fish age, apparently becoming the main cause of elimination of older age groups. The hypothesis that the infection affects fish growth rates in the studied population was not supported. In this Arctic reservoir, a reduction in the trophic level and, hence, a decline in the T. crassus infection in the least cisco can be expected no earlier than 50 years after the impoundment.

articles.title: Community-based nutrition interventions across the continuum of care in humanitarian settings: a systematic review and evidence map.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and map the evidence on community-based nutrition interventions implemented in humanitarian and emergency settings in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC), focusing on intervention types, outcomes, evidence gaps and implications for humanitarian nutrition systems.

DESIGN: Systematic review and evidence mapping conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Eight electronic databases and twenty-six organisational websites were searched for studies published between 2010 and 2024. Studies are mapped by intervention and outcome categories. Findings are synthesised narratively.

SETTING: Humanitarian and emergency settings in LMIC affected by conflict, fragility, displacement or natural disasters.

PARTICIPANTS: Women, infants, children, adolescents, caregivers and households receiving community-based nutrition interventions delivered through community health workers (CHW), volunteers, peer counsellors, care groups or other community platforms.

RESULTS: Fifty-three documents met inclusion criteria, including thirty-nine primary study documents representing thirty-three interventions across twenty countries and fourteen systematic reviews. Most evidence originates from Africa and focuses on community groups, nutrition counselling and community-based management of acute malnutrition. Preventive interventions generally improved infant and young child feeding practices and caregiver behaviours but showed inconsistent effects on anthropometric outcomes. Treatment interventions delivered through CHW and community volunteers improved recovery, programme coverage and treatment performance. However, evidence on dietary intake, food security, caregiver capacity, relapse prevention and longer-term outcomes remains limited.

CONCLUSIONS: Community-based nutrition interventions are central to extending nutrition service delivery in humanitarian settings and show strong potential to improve feeding practices and treatment outcomes. More integrated and context-sensitive evaluation frameworks are needed to strengthen evidence for resilient humanitarian nutrition programming.

articles.title: Sex differences in glucagon-like peptide-1 signalling and the implications for Alzheimer's disease: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder and is the most common form of dementia. Women are differentially affected by AD, and several sex-specific mechanisms have been explored, including hormonal differences (eg, estrogen). Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1R) are located in brain regions implicated in the pathogenesis of AD and shows preliminary evidence of modulating sex-specific pathways that may underlie differential disease risk and progression. Herein, we synthesize the extant literature on the mechanisms of GLP-1 in neurobiological systems relevant to AD pathology. Metabolic signalling (eg, GLP-1, insulin) intersects with known sex-specific pathways hypothesized to subserve AD progression in women. The preceding effects may be attributable to the disruption of estrogen signalling during the postmenopausal period, which impairs hippocampal insulin receptor function and exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction. In addition, these mechanisms provide an explanation for AD comorbidities (eg, type 2 diabetes mellitus [T2DM]). The multidimensional effects demonstrated in GLP-1 paradigms provide a compelling rationale for further investigation of the role of metabolic signalling on sex-specific alterations in AD. Evidence across preclinical and early clinical studies suggests that GLP-1RAs may differentially influence neurobiological pathways implicated in AD pathogenesis, particularly those that interact with hormonal and metabolic systems.

articles.title: Global divergence of stroke and major depressive disorder: unveiling a potential "hidden stagnation" pattern through an integrated medicine perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with increased stroke risk and can be conceptualized in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) as emotional constraint or "Qi Stagnation" that may contribute to "Blood Stasis." However, the country-level ecological relationship between stroke burden and MDD prevalence remains unclear, and high-stroke settings may have under-recognized MDD because of differences in data availability, diagnostic practices, mental health services, and cultural symptom expression. This study quantifies this ecological association and interprets it through an Integrated Medicine framework.

METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data, we analyzed age-standardized stroke Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) rates for all stroke and age-standardized prevalence rates for the GBD cause category of MDD across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. An exploratory Diagnostic Gap Score (ZStroke-ZMDD) was developed to identify countries and territories with disproportionate stroke burden relative to reported MDD prevalence.

RESULTS: A negative ecological correlation emerged globally and strengthened over time (r = -0.059 in 1990 versus r = -0.218 in 2023, P = 0.002). The highest stroke burden quartile (Q4) reported lower MDD prevalence (2639.9/100 000) than the lowest quartile (3067.0/100 000; mean difference 427.1/100 000, 95% CI: 121.52 to 732.58), despite an 8.3% increase in stroke burden in Q4. The score identified clusters with disproportionate stroke burden relative to MDD prevalence in Eastern Europe, Southeast Asia, and Pacific Island settings.

CONCLUSIONS: Low reported MDD prevalence in high-stroke countries and territories suggests a potential diagnostic, reporting, or data-quality mismatch rather than biological protection. These ecological findings do not prove that undiagnosed MDD causes stroke burden, but they support culturally adapted mental health screening in primary care, stroke-prevention clinics, and community health settings, with referral pathways for those who screen positive.

articles.title: Metabolic effects of botryosphaeran, a (1→3)(1→6)-β-D-glucan, in a model of gestational obesity: maternal and progeny developmental impacts.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is associated with several disorders, and its neonatal impacts include macrosomia. Botryosphaeran, a (1→3)(1→6)-β-D-glucan, produced by the fungus Botryosphaeria rhodina exhibits antiobesogenic effects in rats. The objective of this work was to evaluate, for the first time, the effects of botryosphaeran on obese and non-obese rats during the pregnancy period and its effects on offspring. Female Wistar rats (n = 18) were separated into two groups: control, which received commercial ration and water; and obese, that received high-fat ration and water with sucrose (300 g/liter), for 8 weeks. In the 8th week, the rats were divided in the proportion of two rats to one breeding male. After confirmation of pregnancy, the females were subdivided into 4 groups: Pregnancy Control, Botryosphaeran Pregnancy Control, Pregnancy Obese, and Botryosphaeran Pregnancy Obese. In the last 2-thirds of gestation, rats of the botryosphaeran group received the -glucan solution (12 mg/kg/day, via gavage), the control and obese rats received saline solution. At the end of the experiment, the mothers and their offspring were evaluated. Obese mothers had fat accumulation, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. Botryosphaeran significantly reduced blood glucose, corrected insulin resistance and dyslipidemia. The female and male offspring of the obese group showed higher weight gain, adipose tissue accumulation, soleus muscle reduction, hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. Botryosphaeran was effective in correcting these parameters. In conclusion, botryosphaeran exerts significant and promising effects, including antiobesogenic, hypocholesterolemic, and insulin sensitizing action in mothers and their offspring, demonstrating botryosphaeran as a potential agent to prevent obesity and its comorbidities.

articles.title: Comparison of cardiac magnetic resonance findings in idiopathipulmonary arterial hypertension and that associated with CHD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare cardiac MRI findings between children diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and those with pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with CHD, and to determine whether there are prognostic differences between these groups.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 paediatric patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, who underwent standardised cardiac MRI evaluation. Key functional and flow parameters were analysed and compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences in right ventricular volume, mass, and function parameters, and right atrial volume index, or septal shift findings. However, left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, left ventricular end-systolic volume index, left ventricular ejection fraction, left ventricular mass index, and right-left ventricle volume ratios were significantly different between groups. A ventricular mass index ≥75% was more common in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension patients.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac MRI-based assessment reveals meaningful differences in left ventricle volume and mass parameters between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with CHD patients. These findings may aid in follow-up strategies for paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension.

articles.title: Effect of Incorporating Perceptual Learning Into Plantar Hardness Discrimination on the Risk of Falling and Muscle Torque in Patients With Hemiplegia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the impact of perceptual training involving plantar hardness discrimination on fall risk and muscle torque in individuals with hemiplegia.

DESIGN: A randomized controlled trial was conducted in thirty-four stroke patients were randomly assigned to the study and control groups in equal numbers and assessed both before and after treatment. The outcome evaluations comprised fall risk assessment by the Biodex Balance System (BBS), the Isokinetic assessment of lower-limb muscle torque, and the Functional Independent Measures Scale (FIM). Each group was given a selected physical treatment program, while the study group also received perceptual learning with plantar hardness discrimination.

RESULTS: Post-treatment comparison revealed that the study group exhibited a significantly lower risk of falling than the control group (P <0.001, effect size [ES]=1.48). Similarly, knee extensors torque increased significantly in the study group relative to the control group (P <0.001, ES=1.19). Additionally, the study group showed a significant rise in FIM scores compared with the control group (P <0.001, ES=1.56).

CONCLUSIONS: For stroke patients, incorporating perceptual learning into plantar hardness discrimination in the rehabilitation program is regarded as beneficial physical therapy neurorehabilitation for enhancing risk of falling, lower limb muscle torque and function.

articles.title: Aspirin Use for the Prevention of Preeclampsia, an Evidence-Based Review.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that is defined by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation along with proteinuria or evidence of end-organ dysfunction. Affecting 2-8% of pregnancies worldwide, preeclampsia remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. This disorder originates secondary to defective placentation during the first trimester, causing incomplete remodeling of the uterine spiral arteries, resulting in placental hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and the release of anti-angiogenic factors into the maternal circulation. This pathophysiology provided researchers a rationale for the use of low-dose aspirin as a preventive strategy for preeclampsia. Early studies investigated low-dose aspirin initiated at variable gestational ages and failed to show significant reductions in the incidence of preeclampsia. However, over the years, multiple meta-analyses studying aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention revealed a consistent decrease in the incidence of preeclampsia with the use of low-dose aspirin initiated at or before 16 weeks of gestation, with the efficacy being largely dependent on the time of initiation. In 2017, a randomized controlled trial demonstrated a statistically and clinically significant reduction in the incidence of preeclampsia leading to preterm delivery with aspirin initiated before 16 weeks gestation in women identified as high risk by first-trimester algorithm-based screening. Based on the strong evidence in support of aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention, current guidelines recommend initiation of aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks and ideally before 16 weeks for all pregnant women at increased risk for preeclampsia.

articles.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Vitamin K Antagonists for Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery is common and is associated with stroke, prolonged hospitalization, and mortality; yet, the optimal oral anticoagulant in this setting remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) in adults requiring oral anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was any bleeding; secondary outcomes were stroke or transient ischemic attack, systemic embolism, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, reoperation, and length of hospital stay. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences (MDs) were pooled with random-effects models, risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Five randomized trials including 302 patients (153 DOACs and 149 warfarin) were included; rivaroxaban was tested in 3 trials, and apixaban and dabigatran in 1 trial each. Any bleeding did not differ significantly between DOACs and VKAs (9.2% vs 8.1%; OR, 1.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-3.99).

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Applied to Echocardiography for Detection of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Elevated Filling Pressures: A Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of heart failure cases and remains difficult to diagnose non-invasively. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to echocardiography may improve detection, but its aggregate diagnostic accuracy has not been quantified. We performed a diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis of AI-enabled echocardiography for identifying HFpEF, elevated left ventricular filling pressure, or diastolic dysfunction. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to June 2026. Studies reporting the accuracy of AI models applied to echocardiography against invasive, guideline-adjudicated, or ASE/EACVI reference standards were included. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using a bivariate random-effects (Reitsma) model, with a summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, diagnostic odds ratio, and likelihood ratios. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. Eight studies (2770 participants; 1317 [47.5%] with the target condition) were included. Pooled sensitivity was 84.0% (95% CI: 73.0-91.0%) and specificity 83.0% (95% CI: 73.0-89.0%), with an area under the summary ROC curve of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.791-0.930). The diagnostic odds ratio was 24.73 (95% CI: 18.46-33.12); positive and negative likelihood ratios were 4.84 and 0.20. Heterogeneity was high. Performance did not differ by AI architecture but varied significantly by reference standard. No small-study effects were detected. AI-enabled echocardiography shows good pooled accuracy for detecting HFpEF and elevated filling pressures, supporting its diagnostic potential. High heterogeneity and reference-standard dependence warrant larger, prospectively validated studies before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Beyond Blood Cultures and Echocardiography: Emerging Diagnostics for Infective Endocarditis.
articles.abstract: Management of infective endocarditis (IE) is often confounded by the presence of prosthetic valves, transcatheter prostheses, and cardiovascular implantable electronic devices, as well as by changing epidemiologic risks and antimicrobial resistance patterns. For the diagnosis of IE, blood cultures and echocardiography remain foundational, but important gaps persist, particularly in culture-negative and prosthetic/device-associated infections. Contemporary diagnostic criteria and guidelines now support a multimodality approach incorporating molecular microbiology and advanced imaging. This review summarizes emerging technologies including broad-range 16S/18S/28S rRNA polymerase chain reaction and sequencing, fluorescence in situ hybridization coupled with sequencing, targeted and shotgun metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), plasma microbial cell-free DNA, cardiac computed tomography, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron-emission tomography/computed tomography. We also examine the potential role of artificial intelligence in echocardiographic interpretation and of large language models in multimodal data integration. Current evidence suggests that tissue-based molecular testing generally provides greater microbiologic yield than valve culture in culture-negative IE, while blood-based mNGS and microbial cell-free DNA may extend pathogen detection after antibiotic exposure and reduce reliance on tissue-based diagnosis. However, heterogeneity in specimen handling, sequencing pipelines, contamination control, reporting thresholds, and clinical interpretation remains a major barrier to implementation. Future progress should move beyond pathogen detection toward rapid, reproducible, clinically actionable diagnosis that integrates organism identification, anatomic localization, disseminated disease, and personalized treatment. Prospective outcome trials, standardized workflows, cost-effectiveness studies, and multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team integration can help determine whether these technologies translate into better antimicrobial stewardship, procedural decision-making, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: MASLD Liver Transplant: Evolution of Frequency, Age Trends, and Factors Associated With Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has rapidly emerged as a leading indication for liver transplantation (LT) in the United States. There remains a need to understand the evolution of transplant volumes and recipient profiles and outcomes. In this study, we aim to analyze current MASLD LT trends to aid in identifying opportunities for this patient population.

METHODS: We analyzed UNOS data for primary liver transplants (2010-2024), identifying MASLD by diagnosis codes and stratifying transplants into three eras (2010-2014, 2015-2019, and 2020-2024). Analyses included annual MASLD transplant counts and proportions, era-specific annual percent change, comparisons of donor, operative, and recipient characteristics, Kaplan-Meier curves, multivariable Cox regression for overall post-LT mortality, and competing-risk regression for waitlist outcomes.

RESULTS: In total, 18 153 MASLD LT recipients were included (Era 1: 2734; Era 2: 6127; Era 3: 9292). Annual MASLD LT volume increased from 461 in 2010 to 2090 in 2024. Annual percent change was +10.6% (Era 1), +20.1% (Era 2), and +5.9% (Era 3). In Era 3, recipients were as young as 8 y. Era 3 waitlist candidates had significantly higher likelihood of transplant (sHR 1.52; 95% CI, 1.46-1.58) and lower risk of waitlist mortality (sHR 0.44; 95% CI, 0.40-0.48). Recipient survival increased from 97.0% to 98.3% at 30 d, and 90.5% to 92.6% at 1 y (both P < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: From 2010 to 2024, MASLD LT rose markedly but relative growth plateaued. Increasing age diversity, including pediatric recipients, highlights the need for earlier recognition and optimized management.

articles.title: Variation in Pediatric Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Survival After In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Development and Validation of a Survival Model for Risk-Standardized Survival Rates: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate a multivariable prediction model for survival to hospital discharge after pediatric extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and to use this model to derive risk-standardized survival rates (RSSRs) and quantify between-hospital variation in outcomes.

DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study.

SETTING: Hospitals contributing to the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry between 2020 and 2023.

PATIENTS: Children (< 18 yr) treated with ECPR for IHCA.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Eligible patients were identified from the ELSO Registry and split into derivation (N = 1060) and validation (N = 317) cohorts using a hospital-stratified split to preserve within-hospital clustering. Survival prediction models were derived using penalized logistic regression with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. A full-event model incorporating 14 routinely available clinical variables demonstrated fair discrimination (area under the curve, 0.728 in the derivation cohort and 0.678 in the validation cohort) and good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, 0.995; Brier score, 0.222 in the validation cohort). This model was embedded in a multilevel logistic regression model to generate hospital-level RSSRs for centers reporting five or more ECPR cases. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio, which was 1.30 (95% CI, 1.11-1.93), indicating significant differences in survival likelihood between centers after adjusting for patient-level risk.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large, international cohort of pediatric ECPR patients, we developed and internally validated a clinically interpretable model for survival to hospital discharge. The model performance as a discriminator likely limits its use as a standalone tool for clinical decision-making. However, strong internal calibration allowed for determination of hospital-level RSSRs, which revealed significant inter-hospital variability. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of developing a risk-adjustment model capable of estimating hospital-level RSSRs. Additional external validation and evaluation of residual case-mix differences are needed before such models can be used for benchmarking across pediatric ECPR centers.

articles.title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Concomitant coronary artery disease affects 40-75% of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Three recent randomized trials yielded conflicting findings: NOTION-3 demonstrated reduced composite events with pre-TAVI percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PRO-TAVI showed non-inferiority of PCI deferral with less bleeding; neither demonstrated mortality benefit. No previous meta-analysis combined all 3 trials with observational evidence, applied design-stratified GRADE certainty, or explored cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (3 randomized trials, 13 observational cohorts; 8,207 patients). Ten prespecified outcomes were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); 30-day all-cause mortality was primary. GRADE certainty was assessed separately for randomized and observational evidence. Prespecified design-based subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Pre-TAVI PCI was not associated with significant differences in 30-day all-cause mortality (RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.90-1.77; I2 = 32%) or 1-year mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15; I2 = 0%). Major bleeding (RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.98-1.44) and major vascular complications (RR 1.48, 95% CI 0.95-2.30) showed borderline non-significant trends favoring PCI deferral (both I2 = 0%). Excluding Griese et al. 2014, the principal driver of harm and heterogeneity, reduced cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity (RR 0.91; I2 = 24%). No significant differences occurred in stroke, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, pacemaker implantation, or rehospitalization. Routine pre-TAVI PCI confers no mortality benefit and may increase bleeding and vascular complications; PCI should be individualized according to coronary complexity, lesion significance, and bleeding risk.

articles.title: Reappraising Bumetanide in Heart Failure: Pharmacology, Comparative Effectiveness, and Opportunities for Contemporary Use.
articles.abstract: Bumetanide is a valuable loop diuretic utilized in the management of heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Although it accounts for less than 5% of all outpatient loop diuretic prescriptions, its oral bioavailability is highly predictable and generally superior to furosemide, which constitutes over 90% of diuretic prescriptions. Bumetanide is longer-acting and more potent than furosemide; however, many physicians utilize bumetanide as a second-line diuretic when furosemide is ineffective or when intestinal edema limits drug absorption. This review summarizes the pharmacology of bumetanide, its clinical application in patients with heart failure with reduced or preserved ejection fraction, and the factors that contribute to its underutilization despite several pharmacokinetic advantages.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Recaticimab in Patients With Dyslipidemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With GRADE Assessment.
articles.abstract: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the principal target for preventing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, yet many patients do not reach treatment goals with statins, and established proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) antibodies require injections every 2-4 weeks. Recaticimab is a humanized anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibody designed for dosing intervals of up to 12 weeks. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to March 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing recaticimab with placebo in adults with dyslipidemia. Four double-blind trials (1657 randomized participants) were included. At week 12, recaticimab reduced LDL-C by 47.31 percentage points relative to placebo (95% confidence interval [CI], -49.87 to -44.75; I2 = 0%), with similar reductions for 150 mg every 4 weeks (-49.63), 300 mg every 8 weeks (-49.43), and 450 mg every 12 weeks (-45.50) (P for subgroup difference = 0.29). Recaticimab also reduced non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-45.17), apolipoprotein B (-42.31), lipoprotein(a) (-31.06), the total cholesterol/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (-36.94), and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 ratio (-45.28), whereas the change in triglycerides was not significant (-10.05; 95% CI, -20.18 to 0.08).

articles.title: Candida Septic Shock: If Every Hour Matters, Who Requires Empiric Therapy?
Intravenous Tenecteplase for Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Recent or Concurrent Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) alongside a recent or concurrent non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) occupy one of the least evidence-supported decision points in acute stroke care, excluded from every pivotal thrombolysis trial. The recent approval and guideline endorsement of tenecteplase-an agent separately licensed for myocardial infarction at twice the cerebral dose-adds a dimension the alteplase-derived literature does not address. This narrative review synthesizes the evidence on intravenous thrombolysis, specifically tenecteplase, in this setting and distinguishes infarct-related from treatment-related barriers to eligibility. Concomitant NSTEMI complicates approximately 1.6% of acute ischemic stroke hospitalizations and carries an adjusted 3.6-fold increase in in-hospital mortality. The historical contraindication derives from mechanisms-myocardial hemorrhage with free-wall rupture, postinfarction pericarditis with hemopericardium, and left ventricular thrombus embolization-that scale with transmurality and are therefore largely ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction phenomena. Registry data from more than 40,000 thrombolyzed patients show no significant excess of thrombolysis-related complications with recent NSTEMI, and fatal ruptures cluster in subacute ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction; the excess mortality is of similar magnitude without thrombolysis, marking a sicker patient rather than a more dangerous drug.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Effects of Childhood Radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is an important, well-studied late effect of childhood cancer therapy that may manifest many years after treatment. Radiotherapy, particularly when the heart is exposed, has been associated with multiple cardiovascular complications, including heart failure, coronary artery disease, valvular disease, and arrhythmias. This review examines the cardiovascular effects of radiotherapy in childhood and adolescent cancer survivors, with a focus on the mechanisms of radiation-induced injury, major cardiovascular outcomes, factors influencing long-term risk, and advances in cardiac-sparing radiotherapy and surveillance. The literature indicates radiotherapy was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiovascular disease. Cardiovascular risk was influenced by radiation dose and the volume and location of cardiac tissue exposed, as well as age at treatment, anthracycline exposure, and traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Modern radiation techniques, including intensity-modulated and proton therapy, have aimed to reduce cardiac exposure. However, long-term clinical outcome data for these approaches remain limited. These findings support long-term cardiovascular surveillance of childhood cancer survivors and emphasize the importance of minimizing cardiac radiation exposure and addressing modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. Improved assessment of radiation dose to specific cardiac structures may further enable individualized risk stratification and surveillance.

articles.title: [A clinical study on predicting the surgical difficulty of robot-assisted total thyroidectomy combined with lateral cervical lymph node dissection based on machine learning algorithms].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wai ke za zhi [Chinese journal of surgery]
articles.abstract: Objectives: To construct a prediction model based on machine learning algorithms for the surgical difficulty of robot-assisted total thyroidectomy combined with lateral cervical lymph node dissection,and to validate its predictive performance and clinical utility. Methods: This retrospective case series study collected clinical data from 496 patients with differentiated thyroid cancer admitted to the Thyroid and Breast Surgery Department of the 960th Hospital of the People's Liberation Army Joint Logistics Support Force between January 2014 and July 2024, who underwent robot-assisted total thyroidectomy combined with lateral neck lymph node dissection using the Da Vinci system. There were 143 male cases and 353 female cases,aged (36.5±10.4)years (range: 18 to 70 years). Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=347) and a validation set (n=149) at a ratio of 7∶3. Clinical characteristics,ultrasound features,and hematological parameters were collected. Feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Based on the selected features,eight machine learning algorithms-including logistic regression,support vector machine (SVM),gradient boosting machine,neural network,random forest,extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost),k-nearest neighbors and adaptive boosting-were utilized to construct prediction models. Model performance was evaluated using metrics such as the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and F1 score. The Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method was applied to conduct an interpretable analysis of the optimal model. Results: A total of 8 key features for predicting surgical difficulty were selected through LASSO regression dimensionality reduction: the maximum short-axis diameter of positive lateral cervical lymph nodes,positive lymph nodes in cervical levels Ⅱ and Ⅲ,the number of positive lateral cervical lymph nodes,sex,diffuse thyroid changes on ultrasound,weight,surgeon's years of experience,and thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) positivity. The SVM model demonstrated the best performance,with the highest AUC (0.815),the highest F1 score (0.708), and a relatively high sensitivity (0.727). SHAP analysis confirmed that lateral cervical lymph node characteristics,higher body weight,male sex,diffuse thyroid changes on ultrasound,and TPOAb positivity were high-risk factors associated with increased surgical difficulty. Conclusions: The model constructed based on patients' preoperative multidimensional features exhibits good predictive performance for the surgical difficulty of Da Vinci robot-assisted total thyroidectomy combined with lateral cervical lymph node dissection. The integration of SHAP interpretable analysis enables an individualized and visualized preoperative risk assessment,which provides a scientific basis for surgeons to rationally allocate medical resources and optimize perioperative management.

articles.title: [Evolution of surgical strategies for secondary hyperparathyroidism].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wai ke za zhi [Chinese journal of surgery]
articles.abstract: Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) is an important component of chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). It may be accompanied by bone pain, pruritus, abnormalities in bone metabolism, and vascular and soft-tissue calcifications, thereby increasing the disease burden in patients with end-stage kidney disease. Historically, surgical management of SHPT was mainly based on persistently elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels and patients' responses to medical therapy, gradually establishing a management strategy centered on PTH control. This strategy has played an important role in selecting candidates for surgery and facilitating multidisciplinary communication. With the evolution of the CKD-MBD concept and accumulating evidence on clinical outcomes, the goals of surgical treatment have gradually expanded from merely lowering PTH levels to improving bone metabolism, relieving symptoms, controlling CKD-MBD-related target-organ damage, and improving long-term outcomes. Based on current guidelines, expert consensus, and clinical studies, this review discusses the historical basis and limitations of PTH threshold-based strategies and examines the evolution of surgical management for SHPT, with particular emphasis on the timing of surgical evaluation, surgical indications, choice of surgical procedure, perioperative management, postoperative follow-up, and future directions for optimization.

articles.title: 2,611 Liver Transplants: Indications and Survival Rates of a High-Volume Latin American Center.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The liver transplantation program at the Centro de Transplante de Fígado do Ceará (CTFC), one of the largest centers in Northern and Northeastern Brazil, was evaluated over a 23-year period to describe indications, recipient characteristics, and survival outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 2611 liver transplants performed in 2491 patients between 2002 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and laboratory data were collected from medical records and managed using REDCap. Survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: Most recipients were middle-aged men, predominantly from outside the state, and nearly all procedures were funded by the public health system. The main indications for transplantation were decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and alcohol-related liver disease, reflecting global epidemiological shifts. Overall survival rates were 88% at one month, 79% at one year, and 71% at 5 years, with progressive improvement over time. Donor characteristics and ischemia times were consistent with international standards.

CONCLUSIONS: These results show that a high-volume public transplant center can achieve outcomes comparable to major international programs while serving a socioeconomically diverse population.

articles.title: Fibroblast activation protein-targeted PET uptake across various histopathological and molecular subtypes of breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on the uptake value of fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET (FAPI PET) across different histopathological and molecular breast cancer subtypes. As a secondary objective, to perform head-to-head comparisons with [18F]FDG PET.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Major medical literature databases were systematically searched to include studies in which biopsy-proven breast cancer patients were recruited, and uptake values for malignant primary tumors and/or metastatic lesions were reported. Meta-analyses were conducted in R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria) using the meta package.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies met the inclusion criteria. Pooled average SUVmax in the primary malignancy was 11.74 (95%CI:9.95-13.53) on FAPI PET. In the studies in which SUVmax values were provided for both FAPI PET and [18F]FDG PET, on average, the pooled SUVmax was 6.19 (95%CI:4.26-8.12) higher on FAPI PET compared to [18F]FDG PET. FAPI PET showed rather consistently high uptake across all analyzed breast cancer subtypes (pooled estimates ranged from 10.27 to 19.99). Notably, in studies reporting SUVmax for IDC on both FAPI PET and [18F]FDG PET, FAPI PET showed 11.33 (95%CI:8.36-14.30) higher pooled uptake. Similarly, in studies providing SUVmax for luminal A breast cancer, FAPI PET showed 7.85 (95%CI:5.45-10.25) higher uptake compared to [18F]FDG PET.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that FAPI PET exhibits consistently high semi-quantitative values across breast cancer subtypes and can potentially enhance lesion conspicuity and detection rate, particularly in low-[18F]FDG-avid malignancies.

articles.title: Minimally invasive versus open liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: As the population ages, an increasing number of older adults are diagnosed with resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although minimally invasive liver resection (MILR) has shown perioperative advantages, its safety and efficacy in older patients are not fully established. This meta-analysis evaluated the outcomes of MILR compared to open liver resection (OLR) in older adults (≥ 65 years) with HCC.

METHODS: A search was conducted in Medline, Embase, CINAHL, and The Cochrane Library from their inception until November 20, 2025. The review adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251239665).

RESULTS: Fourteen retrospective studies comprising 3,092 older adults were included (1,367 MILR, 1,725 OLR). MILR was associated with lower overall (odds ratio [OR] = 0.47; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38-0.58; I² = 0%) and major complications (OR = 0.61; 95% CI 0.45-0.83; I² = 15%). However, no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality (OR = 0.75; 95% CI 0.41-1.38; I² = 0%), disease-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.83; 95% CI 0.60-1.15; I² = 72%), or overall survival (HR = 0.80; 95% CI 0.56-1.16; I² = 80%).

CONCLUSIONS: In selected older adults with HCC, MILR was associated with fewer perioperative complications than OLR, while no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality or long-term survival. Residual confounding, predominance of minor resections, absence of validated frailty assessment, and limited octogenarian data preclude causal inference or confirmation that the association persists with advancing age.

articles.title: γ-Glutamyl Transferase as a Practical Predictor of Elevated Liver Stiffness in Heart Failure　- Findings From a Daily Clinical Setting.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver stiffness assessed by liver elastography has been reported as useful for predicting hepatic congestion and outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). However, liver elastography is not widely available for patients with HF in routine clinical settings. We investigated whether simple biomarkers can predict elevation of liver stiffness.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In all, 52 hospitalized patients with HF were recruited to this study. The primary analysis examined the association between γ-glutamyl transferase (GGT) and liver stiffness in the overall study population. In multivariable linear regression analysis adjusted for age and sex, log-transformed GGT was independently associated with liver stiffness. This association remained significant in separate sensitivity analyses incorporating systolic and diastolic blood pressure, estimated glomerular filtration rate, N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide, ejection fraction, tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient, inferior vena cava diameter, inferior vena cava collapsibility index, and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use. In exploratory analyses for the prediction of high liver stiffness (>7.1 kPa), the addition of GGT increased integrated discrimination improvement and improved the net reclassification index, whereas the change in the area under the curve was not statistically significant. Direct comparison between models including GGT and the Fibrosis-4 index did not show a significant difference.

CONCLUSIONS: GGT levels may provide a simple and clinically accessible signal associated with elevated liver stiffness in patients with HF and possible hepatic congestion.

articles.title: Hot-water extraction, ethanol precipitation, and silkworm bioassays detect innate immune-stimulating activity in coffee extracts.
articles.abstract: A workflow combining hot-water extraction and ethanol precipitation can provide macromolecule-enriched fractions, but rapid in vivo evaluation of their innate immune-stimulating activity is not well established. We used coffee as a test matrix and evaluated the resulting fractions using a silkworm muscle-contraction assay and a Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection assay. Ethanol-precipitated fractions were prepared from three coffee origins, with or without lactic acid bacterial fermentation, under light- or dark-roast conditions. All sample groups showed measurable muscle-contraction activity. Specific activity ranged from 0.74 to 9.1 U/mg and was higher after light roasting in 11 of 12 matched conditions. Selected fractions increased survival at approximately 24 h after P. aeruginosa challenge, most clearly among Colombia EX samples; protection varied with bean origin, fermentation condition, roast, and dose. Non-fermented fractions were also active, indicating that fermentation was not uniformly required. These results support the feasibility of combining hot-water extraction, ethanol precipitation, and silkworm testing to detect bioactivity in macromolecule-enriched fractions. The method may be useful for prioritizing samples for chemical characterization.

articles.title: Collagen-derived peptides enhance resistance to Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in silkworms.
articles.abstract: Collagen-derived peptides are widely used as food ingredients and dietary supplements, but their effects on host defense against bacterial infection remain poorly understood. Here, we examined whether GFG-01, a granulated preparation of a fish-derived collagen hydrolysate produced using ginger protease, enhances resistance to Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 infection in the silkworm (Bombyx mori). Oral administration of GFG-01 by mixing the preparation into the diet improved the post-infection outcome of larvae compared with vehicle-treated controls. Western blot analysis suggested that intrahemocoelic administration of GFG-01 induced accumulation of Cecropin B, an antimicrobial peptide, in the hemolymph. RNA-seq-based Gene Ontology enrichment analysis of samples collected after oral administration further showed tissue-dependent immune-related gene expression patterns: immune-related categories were enriched among downregulated genes in the fat body and among upregulated genes in hemocytes. These findings indicate that orally administered GFG-01 can improve the outcome of bacterial infection in silkworms and that GFG-01 is associated with modulation of host innate immune responses under the tested conditions.

articles.title: Trough Rivaroxaban Plasma Concentrations and Early Thrombus Regression in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Sub-analysis of the SAKURA-PE/DVT REGISTRY.
articles.abstract: Objectives　To evaluate the association between trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations and early thrombus regression in patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE).Methods　This study was a sub-analysis of the multicenter, prospective SAKURA PE/DVT REGISTRY. The thrombus regression rate was calculated using contrast-enhanced computed tomography performed at diagnosis and approximately two weeks after treatment initiation. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were measured using a chromogenic anti-factor Xa assay. Correlations between plasma concentrations, thrombus regression rates, and coagulation parameters were analyzed.Patients　Among 153 patients with acute PE treated with direct oral anticoagulants, 106 received rivaroxaban, and trough plasma concentrations were measured in 51 patients.Results　The median trough rivaroxaban plasma concentration was 120.0 (55.6-186.0) ng/mL, with substantial interindividual variability. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were positively correlated with the thrombus regression rate in all patients (ρ = 0.33, P = 0.018) and in the intensive therapy group (ρ = 0.41, P = 0.009). In the multivariable analysis, log-transformed rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were independently associated with the thrombus regression rate in the intensive therapy group (β = 9.79, 95% confidence interval 0.72-18.86; P = 0.035). Prothrombin time was strongly correlated with rivaroxaban plasma concentration (ρ = 0.85, P < 0.001). Plasma concentrations tended to increase with age and showed greater variability in elderly patients.Conclusion　Higher trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were associated with greater early thrombus regression in patients with acute PE. Prothrombin time may be a practical surrogate for rivaroxaban exposure and may support individualized anticoagulation strategies in selected patients.

articles.title: Isolated Obtuse Marginal Branch Occlusion Presenting as Recurrent Sinus Arrest without ST-segment Elevation.
articles.abstract: A 47-year-old man presented with dyspnea and presyncope. Initial electrocardiography showed sinus bradycardia without ST-segment elevation, whereas telemetry revealed recurrent sinus arrest with a maximum pause of 3.3 s. Emergency coronary angiography revealed total occlusion of the obtuse marginal branch. Although the sinoatrial node artery originated near the occlusion, intravascular ultrasound confirmed the preservation of blood flow. Immediate revascularization led to complete resolution of sinus arrest. This case suggests that isolated lateral wall ischemia may represent an unusual manifestation of the Bezold-Jarisch reflex without direct sinoatrial node artery involvement. Therefore, acute coronary syndrome should be considered in unexplained sinus node dysfunction, even in the absence of typical chest pain.

articles.title: Improving Hepatic Functional Reserve in Patients with Haemophilia and HIV/HCV-associated Cirrhosis: A Multicentre Prospective Study of Prolonged Foscenvivint Therapy.
articles.abstract: Objective　Patients with hemophilia who acquired HIV and HCV through contaminated clotting factor concentrates form a rare population with progressive cirrhosis in whom liver biopsy is contraindicated by bleeding risk, limiting therapeutic options. We evaluated the safety and preliminary efficacy of prolonged foscenvivint (OP-724), a selective modulator of CREB-binding protein/β-catenin-dependent transcription, on the hepatic functional reserve in this population.Methods　In this multicenter, open-label, non-randomized, prospective study at three Japanese centers, consecutive adults with hemophilia and HIV/HCV-associated cirrhosis received intravenous foscenvivint 280 mg/m2 over 3-4 hours, twice weekly for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the change in the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score from baseline to week 24. Secondary endpoints included the Child-Pugh score, liver stiffness (vibration-controlled transient elastography and magnetic resonance elastography), serum fibrosis markers, and safety with specific monitoring of bleeding events.Patients　Five adult males with hemophilia A (mean age 59.2 years) and HIV/HCV-associated cirrhosis, all with a sustained virologic response ≥48 months before enrolment.Results　Four patients completed the treatment; one discontinued treatment at week 22 due to non-treatment-related pyogenic arthritis. ALBI score improved in all evaluable patients, with mean changes from baseline of -0.420±0.130 at week 24 and -0.318±0.302 at week 28, four weeks after treatment completion. The serum albumin levels increased during treatment and remained above baseline at week 28. No bleeding- or treatment-related serious adverse events occurred.Conclusion　Prolonged foscenvivint was well tolerated and it was associated with an improved hepatic functional reserve during treatment in this biopsy-infeasible population. These findings are hypothesis-generating and suggest that noninvasive functional endpoints may be a feasible evaluation strategy, which requires confirmation in controlled studies.

articles.title: A Case of Recurrent COVID-19 Pneumonia Following Rituximab Therapy: Treatment Informed by a Serial Transbronchial Lung Cryobiopsy, BALF SARS-CoV-2 PCR, and the Clinical Course.
articles.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) presents with diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving anti-CD20 antibody therapy. This report describes a patient with recurrent pneumonia following COVID-19 after receiving anti-CD20 antibody therapy. Two transbronchial lung cryobiopsies documented active lung injury in two clinically distinct episodes. Based on an integrated assessment of the histopathological findings, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid SARS-CoV-2 PCR results, and the clinical course, antiviral and corticosteroid therapies were administered, followed by an improvement in the clinical course. This case suggests that cryobiopsy-based histopathology, integrated with the virological findings and clinical course, may provide complementary information for treatment selection in this patient population.

articles.title: Recurrent Ischemic Stroke after Carotid Artery Stenting for Thyroid Cartilage Induced CCA Stenosis: Was Stenting an Appropriate Treatment?
articles.abstract: Mechanical stimulation of the common carotid artery (CCA) by the hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage can cause common carotid artery (CCA) stenosis and cerebral infarction. A 71-year-old man presented with symptomatic CCA stenosis. Imaging revealed CCA plaque at the site of contact with the thyroid cartilage, and ultrasonography revealed dynamic compression during swallowing. Despite technically successful carotid artery stenting, infarctions can recur without typical stent-related complications. The plaque may be trapped by the stent under persistent external mechanical stress, resulting in intermittent protrusions. Additional stenting prevented the recurrence. This case highlights the importance of considering external mechanical factors when selecting a treatment strategy.

articles.title: [Development of an ICT utilization checklist for community-workplace collaboration promotion programs in local government: Consensus through a two-round Delphi study].
articles.journal: [Nihon koshu eisei zasshi] Japanese journal of public health
