articles.abstract: Objective　To develop a checklist for utilizing information and communication technology (ICT) in community-workplace collaboration programs implemented by local government, based on a consensus among municipal personnel responsible for these programs in organizations utilizing multiple ICT tools.Methods　Using data from a questionnaire and interview surveys conducted in 2022-2023, a checklist comprising seven domains was drafted: online meetings (eight items), e-mail newsletters (seven items), websites (eight items), live online seminars (eight items), on-demand online seminars (eight items), health-related applications (nine items), and common foundational items across ICT utilization (eight items). The expert panel was selected from a nationwide survey conducted in June 2024 among prefectures and public health centers with community-workplace collaboration councils. Personnel responsible for community-workplace collaboration programs were invited from 54 organizations in which five or more ICT tools were utilized. A two-round Delphi study was conducted using an initial checklist based on the findings of the questionnaire and interview surveys. Participants rated the importance of items on a five-point scale, reported their implementation status, and provided open-ended comments. Consensus was defined as an agreement rate ≥70%, a median importance score ≥4, and an interquartile range ＜1.5.Results　Responses were obtained from 39 of 54 organizations (72.2%) in the first round, and 35 of 39 (89.7%) in the second round. The items were revised after the first round. In the second round, 55 items had an agreement rate ≥70%, and 53 items had an agreement rate ≥80%. The final checklist comprised 55 items across the seven domains: online meetings (eight items), e-mail newsletters (seven items), websites (eight items), live online seminars (eight items), on-demand online seminars (seven items), health-related applications (nine items), and common foundational items across ICT utilization (eight items).Conclusion　Using the Delphi method, a checklist was developed that encompasses the preparation, organizational and operational systems, implementation strategies, and evaluation components necessary for ICT utilization in community-workplace collaboration programs. Organizations can assess their Internet infrastructure and organizational readiness using the common foundational items before selectively applying the domain-specific checklists based on the ICT tools being implemented. The checklist may also assist organizations that are already using ICT, to periodically evaluate its effectiveness. Despite achieving consensus for all checklist items, several items related to budget, operational systems and evaluation had low implementation rates, indicating a necessity for strategies to enhance effective ICT utilization.

articles.title: Transitioning to Single-Family Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Rooms and Healthcare Professionals' Perception of Work Quality.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICU's) are transitioning from Open Bay Units (OBUs) to Single-Family Rooms (SFRs), to promote a more family-integrated care environment and improve infant and parent outcomes.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the impact of this transition on healthcare professionals (HCPs).

METHODS: In this longitudinal observational cohort study, conducted at both NICU's of the Emma Children's Hospital, Amsterdam UMC (September 2020-November 2023), care environments transitioned from OBU to SFR, with an intermediate transitional mixed (TM). HCPs completed Smith's "Occupancy Quality Survey" to assess perception of quality of physical work environment, patient care and patient safety, job-related, interaction among members of the NICU care team, interaction with the NICU technology, and quality of life outside work. Outcomes were reported as mean ± SD, and group differences were analyzed using one-way ANOVA.

RESULTS: A total of 290 HCPs participated (68.9% nurses, 86.2% female, 54.4% aged 30-50). Calculated indicator scores were statistically significant higher in the SFR than in the OBU for environment, patient care and safety, and interaction with technology. Off-job quality of life score was higher in the SFR but did not differ statistically significant. Job-related quality and team interaction remained comparable across phases.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: Transitioning from OBU to SFR positively influenced HCPs' perceptions of work quality. Active involvement of HCPs throughout the redesign process may have contributed to this effect. Potential stress among HCPs during and after the transition to SFRs, as well as challenges related to team interaction and cohesion, should be carefully considered.

articles.title: Disrupted Resolution Mechanisms in the Onset and Progression of Chronic Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Disruption of physiological resolution mechanisms converts what should be a self-limiting inflammatory response into a persistent and pathogenic process. In the context of liver disease, when inflammation fails to resolve appropriately, it becomes chronic, driving ongoing tissue injury and repair responses that ultimately promote the development and progression of liver fibrosis. This defective resolution is also evident in the advanced stages of chronic liver disease, such as cirrhosis, where patients develop a state of immune dysfunction characterized by simultaneous systemic inflammation and impaired host defense responses. This dysfunctional immune state increases susceptibility to bacterial infections and contributes to the development of extrahepatic organ failure, which are major determinants of morbidity and mortality in these patients. This chapter reviews the current understanding of inflammation resolution across the spectrum of chronic liver disease. The wide clinical and pathological heterogeneity of these conditions, ranging from early and mild liver tissue injury to advanced cirrhosis and its complications, provides a unique framework to study the dynamics of inflammatory burden and its resolution.

articles.title: Specialized Pro-resolving Mediators and Mimetics: Bridging Resolution Biology and Therapeutic Development.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Inflammation is a fundamental host defense mechanism that protects against infection and tissue injury. However, failure to appropriately resolve inflammation contributes to the pathogenesis of numerous pathologies. The discovery of endogenous mediators of inflammation resolution has changed our understanding of the dynamics of self-limiting inflammation. The active resolution of inflammation reflects tightly orchestrated responses to specific mediators including cytokines, peptides, and specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), a superfamily of bioactive lipid mediators that includes the lipoxin, resolvin, protectin, and maresin families of SPMs. These mediators exert their potent pleiotropic immunoregulatory actions at nanomolar concentrations through mechanisms including activation of specific G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), to regulate endothelial activation and promote the cessation of neutrophil recruitment, enhanced macrophage efferocytosis, removal of inflammatory debris, and restoration of tissue homeostasis. The lipoxins (LXs), arachidonate-derived mediators, were the first SPMs described and have emerged as attractive potential therapeutics for acute and chronic inflammatory diseases due to their broad anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving actions. However, translation of these bioactions has proven difficult as a result of their structural limitations and poor chemical stability, making them susceptible to metabolic inactivation. For this reason, the quest to develop structurally protected mimetics has recently gained momentum, and these analogs are designed to preserve receptor-mediated bioactivity while enhancing stability and efficacy. This chapter reviews the biosynthesis, biological functions, and receptor pharmacology of the major SPM families. Furthermore, the therapeutic potential of SPMs and their mimetics is analyzed, summarizing the rationale underpinning the design and preclinical testing of these therapeutic leads across a range of inflammatory and tissue injury models.

articles.title: Navigating complexity: current evidence and recommendations for management of selected, non-malignant pleural effusions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pleural effusions are common and carry substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Management can be particularly challenging when effusions arising from systemic diseases such as congestive heart failure (CHF) or cirrhosis are refractory to medical management or when the effusion occurs due to disruption of the thoracic lymphatic system, as in chylothorax.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines current approaches to the diagnosis and management of congestive heart failure-related effusions, hepatic hydrothorax, and chylothorax. In addition, we seek to identify areas for future investigation across all three conditions, particularly the evidence guiding invasive management such as thoracentesis, indwelling pleural catheters, and pleurodesis. To accomplish this, we conducted a literature search in PubMed between 1 August 2026 and 13 August 2026, using a combination of free-text keywords related to the listed effusions.

EXPERT OPINION: If medical/conservative management of complicated pleural effusion fails, there are multiple treatment options for each of the discussed effusions, but no clear-cut superior option as the current literature is limited. Future studies will require multi-center and multi-disciplinary collaboration but will likely reveal that treatment should be based on an individual level, accounting for local expertise and incorporating patients' preferences.

articles.title: The application of proteomics in asthma research: a bibliometric analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common inflammatory disease of the respiratory system. Following the advent of genomics, proteomics has emerged as a valuable research approach. This study aimed to pinpoint key research areas and trends in the use of proteomics for asthma through bibliometric analysis, offering insights into future research paths.

METHODS: Articles related to asthma and proteomics published between 2000 and 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. The data were analyzed and visualized using the bibliometric software CiteSpace (version number: v.6.1 R6).

RESULTS: A total of 520 articles were included in this study, and a gradual increase in the annual publication volume was observed. The USA, China, and Sweden ranked as the top three countries in terms of publication output. The USA exhibited the highest centrality (0.42), indicating its influence in this field. At the institutional level, the Karolinska Institute had the highest number of publications. The keyword clustering analysis revealed that the research focuses on airway inflammation mechanisms, proteomics methodologies, precision medicine applications, and clinical phenotype characterization. Keywords like "proteomics," "mass spectrometry," and "precision medicine" have seen significant citation increases recently, highlighting proteomics' role in advancing asthma research, biomarker discovery, and personalized therapies.

CONCLUSION: By systematically examining the application and development of proteomics in the field of asthma research via a bibliometric analysis, we have generated a comprehensive knowledge framework for researchers. Future studies should place greater emphasis on the clinical application of biomarkers, multi-omics integration, and the development of personalized treatment strategies.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated patients in pediatric intensive care: A cohort study.
articles.abstract: Introduction. Mechanical ventilation (MV) is a common intensive care intervention associated with increased resource use and a risk of complications. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize ventilated patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) and pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS). Population and Methods. We conducted a prospective cohort study in the pediatric intensive care unit of a high-complexity hospital between June 2021 and August 2022. The study analyzed the outcomes of patients with MV, the incidence of AHRF and PARDS, and their respective outcomes. Results. The study recorded 1354 admissions; 273 required mechanical ventilation (306 cycles). 19.4% had AHRF and 6.6% had PARDS. Morbidity upon discharge from the intensive care unit was 18.7%, and mortality was 12.1%. In-hospital mortality was 13.2%; 10.2% required a tracheostomy. In the univariate analysis, PIM-2, failed and unscheduled extubations, tracheostomy, days on mechanical ventilation and length of hospital stay, AHRF, and PARDS were associated with morbidity and mortality. In the multivariate analysis, PIM-2 and tracheostomy remained significant. Conclusion. One in five patients admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit required mechanical ventilation, and approximately seven out of ten ventilated patients survived without acquired morbidity. AHRF was associated with longer duration of mechanical ventilation and hospital stay, a higher likelihood of tracheostomy, and higher morbidity and mortality. The results for patients with PARDS show a trend toward more days on a ventilator, longer hospital stays, and higher mortality.

articles.title: Porcine astrovirus induces endoplasmic reticulum stress-mediated autophagic degradation of MAVS to inhibit type I interferon production.
articles.abstract: Porcine astrovirus (PAstV) infection predominantly results in diarrhea and encephalitis in suckling piglets, yet the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, the PAstV1-GX1 strain, previously isolated, was utilized to infect PK-15 cells. The results demonstrated that PAstV infection induced pronounced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, as evidenced by the upregulation of HSPA5/GRP78 expression, and macroautophagy/autophagy, indicated by the increased conversion of MAP1LC3/LC3 from LC3-I to LC3-II and decreased expression of SQSTM1/p62. Pharmacological mitigation of ER stress effectively suppressed autophagy, suggesting that PAstV facilitates autophagy via ER stress. Further mechanistic investigations identified that PAstV infection selectively activated the EIF2AK3/PERK-EIF2S1/eIF2α-ATF4 pathway within the unfolded protein response, establishing this pathway as the pivotal upstream signal mediating autophagy. Through the screening of viral proteins, the capsid protein was identified as the primary viral component responsible for inducing ER stress and autophagy. This protein was concurrently localized to both mitochondria and the ER, where it interacted with the MAVS (mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein). The capsid protein facilitated the degradation of MAVS via the autophagy pathway and an apoptosis-related pathway in a non-classical, caspase-3-independent manner, thereby suppressing the production of type I interferons. Modulating ER stress, autophagy, or apoptosis greatly impacted the capsid protein's suppression of type I interferons. This suggested that the capsid protein hindered type I interferon production by triggering ER stress, which activated autophagy and possibly apoptosis, resulting in MAVS degradation. These insights lay the groundwork for understanding PAstV's pathogenic mechanisms and aid in developing new antiviral treatments.Abbreviations: 3-MA: 3-methyladenine; 4-PBA: 4-phenylbutyric acid; ACTB/β-actin: actin beta; ATF4: activating transcription factor 4; ATF6: activating transcription factor 6; CCK-8: Cell Counting Kit-8; Co-IP: co-immunoprecipitation; CQ: chloroquine; DAPI: 4,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole; DDIT3/CHOP: DNA damage inducible transcript 3; EGFP: enhanced green fluorescent protein; EIF2AK3/PERK: eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 alpha kinase 3; EIF2S1/eIF2α: eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 subunit alpha; ER: endoplasmic reticulum; ERN1/IRE1: endoplasmic reticulum to nucleus signaling 1; hpi: hours post-infection; HSPA5/GRP78: heat shock protein family A (Hsp70) member 5; IFIT1/ISG56: interferon induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 1; IFN: interferon; IFNB1/IFN-β: interferon beta 1; ISG15: ISG15 ubiquitin like modifier; mAb: monoclonal antibody; MAP1LC3/LC3: microtubule associated protein 1 light chain 3; MAVS: mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein; MOI: multiplicity of infection; PBS: phosphate-buffered saline; PAstV: porcine astrovirus; phospho-EIF2S1: phosphorylated EIF2S1; PPP1R15A/GADD34: protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 15A; RAPA: rapamycin; RT-PCR: reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction; RT-qPCR: reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction; SeV: Sendai virus; siRNA: small interfering RNA; SQSTM1/p62: sequestosome 1; TG: thapsigargin; TU: tunicamycin; UPR: unfolded protein response; UV: ultraviolet; VSV-GFP: vesicular stomatitis virus expressing green fluorescent protein; WCL: whole-cell lysate; XBP1: X-box binding protein 1.

articles.title: Advances in host-directed therapies for tuberculosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis (TB) treatment is lengthy and complex, requiring patients to adhere to multidrug regimens, which may be difficult to tolerate. Importantly, traditional antimicrobial therapy does not prevent infection-associated lung damage. Adjunctive host-directed therapies (HDTs) could address the issues associated with standard antitubercular therapy. We highlight recent advances in pulmonary TB HDT clinical trials and discuss the molecular pathways targeted, focusing on approaches that future research can build on to develop new TB regimens that may include HDTs.

AREAS COVERED: We review results from recent clinical studies registered on https://clinicaltrials.gov/ and we present a summary of the state of the art in TB HDT development. We provide a list of leading candidates and discuss their phase of development in the clinical pipeline.

EXPERT OPINION: Complementary approaches have been used to evaluate acceleration of sputum culture conversion, amelioration of lung inflammation, and prevention of lung damage in the clinical studies described. Despite a lengthy list of HDT candidates evaluated in human studies, none to date has shown benefit in accelerating sputum culture conversion, although successes in reducing biomarkers of lung damage have been reported. Continued research that includes the use of innovative biomarkers may reveal important roles for HDTs as adjunctive therapies for TB treatment.

articles.title: Changing patterns of diagnostic testing in children with asthma: evidence of redistribution, overuse, and recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world implementation of diagnostic strategies in pediatric asthma remains heterogeneous, and the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on diagnostic practice patterns is incompletely understood, particularly in middle-income countries. Guideline-recommended objective testing (e.g. spirometry) is inconsistently applied in pediatric asthma worldwide, and whether the COVID-19 pandemic produced a transient disruption or a lasting restructuring of diagnostic practice across testing domains remains unclear. We aimed to characterize longitudinal trends in diagnostic testing among children with asthma, examining pre-pandemic trajectories, COVID-associated changes, and post-pandemic recovery.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide population-based interrupted time-series study using Colombia's mandatory healthcare registry (2015-2024). Asthma encounters were identified using ICD-10 codes (J45-J46). Diagnostic procedures were classified into nine clinically defined domains. Diagnostic intensity was calculated as tests per 100 asthma encounters. Segmented regression estimated pre-pandemic trends, immediate 2020 level changes, and post-pandemic slope modifications.

RESULTS: A total of 1,954,680 asthma encounters generated 117,324 diagnostic tests. Pre-pandemic trajectories diverged across domains. Pulmonary function testing (PFT) declined before 2020 (IRR 0.80; 95% CI 0.74-0.86) but showed a significant immediate increase in 2020 (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.28-1.57) and sustained post-pandemic acceleration (IRR 1.17; 95% CI 1.09-1.26). Imaging and sleep studies exhibited sharp pandemic-associated declines with partial or full recovery. Cardiopulmonary testing demonstrated marked pre-pandemic expansion (IRR 1.96).

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric asthma diagnostic practice underwent domain-specific restructuring rather than uniform disruption, consistent with a process of diagnostic redistribution across testing domains. Post-pandemic intensification of PFT may reflect improved adherence to objective diagnostic confirmation, whereas persistent contraction in selected domains warrants continued monitoring.

articles.title: A prospective observational real-world study to assess the effectiveness and safety of single-inhaler triple therapy with glycopyrrolate/formoterol fumarate/budesonide in patients with uncontrolled asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Individuals with asthma remain inadequately controlled despite treatment with inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting β2-agonist (ICS/LABA) therapy. Single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) combining ICS, LABA, and long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) offers a practical treatment escalation option. This study aims to assess the real-world effectiveness, safety, and adherence of SITT with budesonide/glycopyrrolate/formoterol fumarate in adults with uncontrolled asthma.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicentric, prospective, observational study was conducted across five centers in India. Adults with uncontrolled asthma on stable ICS/LABA therapy who were prescribed SITT as part of routine care were followed for 12 weeks. Changes in lung function, asthma control (ACT), and quality of life (Mini-AQLQ) were assessed. Medication adherence, adverse events, and asthma exacerbations were recorded.

RESULTS: Of 258 enrolled patients, 231 were included in the final analysis. Spirometry measurements showed notable improvements before and after bronchodilator use (all p < 0.012). These included higher MMEF values, suggesting improved small-airway function. Mean ACT scores improved from 14.29 at baseline to 18.49 at follow-up. Mini-AQLQ scores also improved over 12 weeks, indicating better patient-reported quality of life. Medication adherence was high, and no asthma exacerbations, adverse events, or serious adverse events were reported during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: In routine practice, SITT BGF was associated with short-term improvements in lung function, asthma control, and QoL in adults with uncontrolled asthma. The mean ACT improved to partially controlled range at 12 weeks. Results suggest short-term effectiveness and tolerability, but longer-term and comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Optimizing entropy-based heart rate variability metrics: fixed tolerance improves congestive heart failure classification.
articles.abstract: Objective.Entropy-based heart rate variability (HRV) metrics are widely used to characterize heartbeat dynamics and distinguish physiological from pathological states, but their classification performance is highly sensitive to parameter selection. This study investigated a fixed-tolerance approach derived from a healthy reference population as an alternative to conventional subject-specific tolerance normalization and assessed how entropy-parameter selection influences classification performance.Approach.Approximate entropy (ApEn), sample entropy (SampEn), and multiscale entropy (MSE) were evaluated using both conventional and fixed-tolerance formulations in 24-h Holter recordings from 274 healthy subjects and 946 patients with congestive heart failure (CHF). Classification performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Parameter sensitivity was assessed through systematic sweeps of the embedding dimension, tolerance coefficient, and MSE scale range.Main results.Classification performance varied substantially across the parameter space, and the embedding-dimension and tolerance values commonly used in the literature were generally suboptimal. The fixed-tolerance implementation consistently outperformed the conventional subject-specific approach, achieving AUC values of 0.78 (+0.03) for ApEn, 0.77 (+0.09) for SampEn, and 0.74 (+0.14) for MSE. For MSE, tolerance selection had a substantially larger influence on classification performance than scale-dependent parameterization.Significance.The results suggest that a substantial portion of the classification potential of entropy-based HRV analysis remains unexploited under conventional tolerance normalization and parameter selection. More generally, entropy-based HRV metrics appear to be more sensitive to methodological choices than is commonly assumed. The fixed-tolerance approach provides a simple and computationally inexpensive strategy for improving entropy-based CHF classification, although validation in independent datasets is needed to establish its broader applicability.

articles.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.

METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.

RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

articles.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.

RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.

CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

articles.title: Sustainable synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66 MOF from PET waste for UV-assisted degradation of organic contaminants.
articles.abstract: The coexistence of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste and persistent organic pollutants in aquatic environments requires comprehensive circular-economy strategies to valorize PET waste into functional materials for water treatment. In this study, post-consumer PET was converted to terephthalic acid (TPA) via a neutral hydrothermal depolymerization process and was used as an organic linker for the synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66. The recovered linker and synthesized UiO-66 were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, TEM/SAED, nitrogen adsorption-desorption, UV-vis spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and Mott-Schottky analysis. PXRD confirmed UiO-66 crystallinity, while TEM revealed nano-sized polyhedral particles with an average size of approximately 120 nm. The material exhibited a BET surface area of 822.2 m2 g-1, total pore volume of 0.379 cm3 g-1, and average pore diameter of 2.93 nm. Optical and electrochemical analyses showed a band gap of about 3.51 eV, n-type semiconducting behavior, and a flat-band potential of -0.68 V vs. Ag/AgCl. The photocatalytic activity of PET-derived UiO-66 was evaluated using methylene blue (MB) under UV light irradiation. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst achieved about 97.3% degradation with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.024 min-1, which was about 12 times higher than that of direct photolysis. Radical scavengers' experiments showed that hydroxyl radicals (˙OH) acted as major reactive species, followed by superoxide radicals (˙O2 -) and photogenerated holes (h+). The catalyst showed good recyclability with about 86% activity retained after five cycles. These results offer an environmentally sustainable approach to recycle PET waste into a useful photocatalyst for water treatment.

articles.title: ERS/ESRS clinical practice guideline for continuous positive airway pressure for the treatment of adult obstructive sleep apnoea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the primary treatment for obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), although its effectiveness may vary across OSA subtypes. This joint European Respiratory Society (ERS)/European Sleep Research Society (ESRS) clinical practice guideline evaluates CPAP's impact on patient-centred and prognostically relevant outcomes, comparing it to no or sham treatment in different OSA subgroups.

METHODS: The joint ERS/ESRS Task Force consisted of experts in pulmonology, cardiology and respiratory sleep medicine, patient representatives and methodologists. Questions were formulated using the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes) framework. A systematic review assessing the effects of CPAP on critical outcomes was performed. The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was assessed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach. Consensus on the direction and strength of the recommendation was informed by Evidence-to-Decision frameworks and achieved through discussions and voting.

RECOMMENDATIONS: The Task Force generally suggests CPAP treatment for OSA because of its beneficial effects on sleepiness, other patient-reported outcomes and blood pressure (conditional recommendations). CPAP is recommended in patients with excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) (strong recommendation). Additional specific conditional recommendations are given for patients with moderate-to severe OSA, the elderly, and patients with arterial and treatment-resistant hypertension. The Task Force suggests either CPAP or no treatment in patients without EDS (but taking into account other OSA-related symptoms), in patients with atrial fibrillation with the aim of reducing its recurrence and in patients with impaired glucose metabolism to improve glycaemic control.

CONCLUSION: CPAP is an effective treatment for adults with OSA. However, recommendations for its use vary across different patient subgroups.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Lumbar Facet Arthroplasty for Degenerative Lumbar Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Predominantly Total Posterior Spine System Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lumbar facet joint arthroplasty has emerged as a motion-preserving alternative to fusion for the treatment of degenerative lumbar spine diseases. While early studies have reported promising outcomes, the overall clinical efficacy, durability, and safety profile remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the clinical, radiographic, and perioperative outcomes of lumbar facet arthroplasty in patients with degenerative lumbar disease.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through November 2025. Eligible studies included clinical investigations of posterior lumbar facet arthroplasty in degenerative conditions with a minimum sample size of 10 patients. Outcomes of interest included reoperation rates, patient-reported outcomes (visual analog scale [VAS], Oswestry Disability Index [ODI]), range of motion (ROM), and perioperative parameters. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed, and heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute's critical appraisal tools.

RESULTS: A total of 13 reports were included, 11 of which supplied data for outcome-specific meta-analyses. The conversion to fusion or arthroplasty removal was 6% and 7%, respectively. Final leg and back VAS scores were 1.10 and 1.72, with mean changes of -6.36 and -5.36, respectively; the final ODI was 17.30 (Δ -37.52), and ROM was 6.40° (Δ -0.21°). The mean blood loss and operating time were 391.74 mL and 186.72 minutes. Adjacent-segment reoperation was observed in 0/206 arthroplasty and 5/93 fusion patients in 1 randomized Total Posterior Spine System (TOPS) comparison. Most outcomes were highly heterogeneous.

CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence-predominantly for TOPS-suggests improvement in pain and disability with preservation of segmental motion. There was a high degree of heterogeneity; however, scanty comparative evidence and differences in follow-up make it difficult to draw conclusions and generalizations from the data across devices.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Lumbar facet arthroplasty may improve pain and disability while preserving motion in selected patients. Evidence is predominantly TOPS-based, and long-term durability and superiority to fusion remain uncertain.

Identification of a novel small-molecule compound that suppresses depolarization-induced CYP11B2 expression and aldosterone production in KCNJ5 mutant adrenocortical cells.
articles.abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is one of the most common causes of secondary hypertension, with aldosterone-producing adenomas (APAs) accounting for approximately half of cases. In most APAs, somatic mutations in ion channel or pump genes constitutively activate Ca2+ signaling through membrane depolarization, driving overexpression of the aldosterone synthase CYP11B2 and excess aldosterone production. Although KCNJ5 mutations represent the most prevalent somatic driver of APA pathogenesis, existing pharmacotherapies-including mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) and CYP11B2 enzyme inhibitors-have limitations in efficacy and selectivity, and are associated with notable adverse effects, indicating an urgent need for novel strategies that suppress CYP11B2 expression at the transcriptional level through a distinct mechanism of action. To address this need, we performed high-throughput screening of a compound library using a KCl stimulation-dependent CYP11B2 reporter system, with multi-step filtering incorporating cytotoxicity evaluation and validation in doxycycline-inducible KCNJ5-L168R mutant-expressing cells. This approach identified compound 35 (2-benzylidene-5-allyladamantan-1-ol) as a lead candidate. Compound 35 suppressed CYP11B2 mRNA expression and aldosterone secretion in KCNJ5-L168R mutant cells without inhibiting KCl-induced Ca2+ influx, demonstrating that its mechanism of action lies downstream of Ca2+ entry. Compound 35 also reduced NURR1 and NGFIB expression, pointing to a mechanism upstream of NR4A-dependent CYP11B2 induction. Notably, compound 35 showed no significant effect on CYP11B1 mRNA expression, suggesting selectivity at the transcriptional level that is mechanistically distinct from the structural similarity-based selectivity challenges faced by CYP11B2 enzyme inhibitors. These results identify compound 35 as a chemically tractable lead with a mechanism of action distinct from MRAs, Ca2+ channel blockers, and CYP11B2 enzyme inhibitors, providing a starting point for the development of transcriptional suppressors of CYP11B2 as a novel therapeutic strategy for KCNJ5 mutation-associated PA.

articles.title: USP19 protects against cigarette smoke-induced lung injury and epithelial stress.
articles.abstract: Cigarette smoke (CS) imposes substantial proteostatic stress on lung epithelial cells, yet the protein quality control mechanisms that determine susceptibility to injury remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of the ubiquitin-specific protease 19 (USP19) in CS-related lung injury across human lung tissue, a chronic CS-exposure mouse model, and cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-treated bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B cells. USP19 protein abundance was reduced in lung tissue from patients with severe COPD. Usp19-deficient mice developed greater CS-induced airspace enlargement compared to wild-type mice. In BEAS-2B cells, CSE reduced USP19 abundance, and USP19 knockout increased CSE-induced apoptosis. In addition, re-expression of USP19 partially restored viability. USP19 deficiency altered the temporal profile of integrated stress response signaling, culminating in enhanced CHOP induction, and CHOP (DDIT3) knockdown partially rescued CSE-induced loss of viability. USP19-deficient cells also showed a decrease in p62 abundance, puncta number, and area during CSE exposure, suggesting altered p62-associated protein handling. Together, these findings identify USP19 as a protective modifier of CS-related lung injury and epithelial stress, consistent with a role in supporting the capacity of lung epithelial cells to accommodate CS-induced proteostatic stress.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV alleviates heart failure by restoring gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids and suppressing HDAC1/2/3.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The interaction between Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) and the gut microbiota is known to help prevent cardiovascular disease, however, its underlying mechanism through which AS-IV modulates the balance of intestinal flora to ameliorate heart failure (HF) remains unclear.

METHODS: A rat HF model was created using coronary artery ligation to study AS-IV's cardioprotective effects, while an AngII-activated H9c2 hypertrophy model assessed AS-IV's impact on cellular hypertrophy. AS-IV's therapeutic effects were evaluated through histopathology, 16S rRNA sequencing, SCFA-targeted omics, and HDAC molecular assays.

RESULTS: AS-IV markedly enhanced cardiac function in HF rats. AS-IV treatment ameliorated gut microbiota dysbiosis in HF rats. AS-IV also altered short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels, leading to an increase in hexanoic, heptanoic, octanoic, decanoic, valeric, pentanoic, acetic, propionic, nonanoic, isobutyric, and isovaleric acids. Additionally, AS-IV concurrently suppressed the overexpression of HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC3 in both HF rats and H9c2 cells, alleviated myocardial fibrosis, and reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.

CONCLUSIONS: AS-IV exerts its therapeutic effects against HF through a multifaceted mechanism involving the amelioration of gut dysbiosis, enrichment of SCFA-producing bacteria, restoration of SCFA levels, and suppression of HDAC1/2/3 expression.

articles.title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, but lumbar fusion-specific associations with postoperative outcomes remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and surgical and postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing lumbar fusion.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 14 May 2026. Comparative studies of adults undergoing lumbar fusion with and without preoperative GLP-1RA exposure were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses generated odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261414637).

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohorts involving 28,525 patients were included; 6 used propensity score matching or another matching strategy. No statistically significant associations were observed between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and reoperation or revision (OR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.44-1.24; P = 0.25), postoperative infection (OR: 0.83, 95% CI: 0.68-1.00; P = 0.05), wound complications (OR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.65-1.12; P = 0.26), or postoperative respiratory complications (OR: 1.08, 95% CI: 0.63-1.84; P = 0.69). Deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and unplanned emergency department visits also did not differ significantly. All included studies were observational and predominantly used large administrative data sources.

CONCLUSIONS: Across the evaluated outcomes, the available observational evidence did not identify a signal of increased postoperative risk associated with preoperative GLP-1RA exposure after lumbar fusion. Prospective studies with standardized exposure definitions and perioperative management protocols are warranted to confirm these findings and better define their clinical implications.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current observational evidence does not establish preoperative GLP-1RA exposure alone as an independent risk factor for adverse outcomes after lumbar fusion.

articles.title: What is next in sepsis? Controversies and future directions from the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines.
articles.abstract: The Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for sepsis care relevant to a global audience. While most recommendations in the 2026 SSC guidelines build upon those listed in previous iterations, some of them point to a new direction in the care of patients with sepsis-one characterized by a more flexible approach to the assessment and treatment of an individual patient, with careful consideration of the benefit of critical care and post-intensive care unit recovery interventions. In this paper, we identify some of these key changes, and describe how modern sepsis practice is evolving into a hybrid approach of empiric early treatment alongside a nuanced, personalized stream of care, informed by patient values and preferences. We also emphasize key methodological points which inform potentially controversial recommendations, so clinicians may better understand how to implement these in practice.

articles.title: Who can benefit from percutaneous left atrial appendage closure? Recent advances.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) confers a substantial risk of stroke. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are highly effective for stroke prevention, and they form the cornerstone of AF management. Nevertheless, many eligible patients do not receive or do not maintain long-term anticoagulation because of bleeding risk, prior hemorrhage, or other contraindications. Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as a nonpharmacological alternative to anticoagulation. In 2026, 2 major randomized trials addressing the role of LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation were published: CHAMPION-AF (WATCHMAN FLX Versus NOAC for Embolic Protection in the Management of Patients With Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation) and CLOSURE-AF (Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Compared to Medical Therapy). The CHAMPION-AF study randomized 3000 lower-risk AF patients to LAAC (Watchman FLX) or DOAC. LAAC met noninferiority criteria for the composite efficacy end point of cardiovascular death, stroke, and systemic embolism (5.7% vs 4.8% at 3 y; hazard ratio [HR], 1.2; 95% CI, 0.87-1.66) and demonstrated superiority for nonprocedure-related bleeding (10.9% vs 19%; HR, 0.55). Ischemic stroke alone, however, was numerically more frequent following LAAC (HR, 1.61), an unexpected finding not observed in prior LAAC trials. The CLOSURE-AF study enrolled a substantially higher-risk population with a more adverse bleeding profile. LAAC failed to demonstrate noninferiority to best medical therapy for the composite primary end point consisting of cardiovascular death, stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding (16.8 vs 13.3 events per 100 patient-years), driven by higher mortality and more bleeding events in the device group. This review critically appraises the design, outcomes, and clinical implications of both trials in the context of previous trials, discusses methodological issues, including noninferiority margin selection and bleeding-end point definitions, and outlines implications for patient selection for LAAC.

articles.title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis.
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are osteoregenerative; however, their therapeutic efficacy for skeletal conditions is hampered by poor bone-homing ("osteotropism"). In preclinical models, this deficit is correctable by MSC glycocalyx editing to enforce sialylated Lewis X (sLeX) expression, thereby programming osteotropism. We conducted a first-in-human clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02566655) involving a single intravenous infusion of glycocalyx-edited autologous bone marrow-derived MSCs in ten women with advanced-stage osteoporosis. The protocol-mandated evaluation spanned 2 years and included clinical assessments, radiographic studies, and measurements of bone turnover markers (BTMs), bone tissue area (BTA), and bone mineral density (BMD). Thereafter, fracture and safety monitoring continued for >3 additional years for each patient. No serious adverse events occurred. Fragility fractures were markedly and durably reduced, amidst increased osteoanabolic BTM levels, BTA, and volumetric BMD. These findings indicate that glycocalyx editing effectuates MSC-based osteoporosis therapy and also refute notions that MSCs derived from older persons and/or diseased-tissue sites are biologically compromised.

articles.title: Tozorakimab to Prevent COPD Exacerbations.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have exacerbations despite receiving standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. Dysregulated interleukin-33 signaling is implicated in the pathogenesis of COPD. Tozorakimab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the activity of interleukin-33.

METHODS: In two replicate phase 3 trials (OBERON and TITANIA), we enrolled adults with COPD who were current or former smokers and had a history of exacerbations in the previous year despite receiving stable standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. There were no eligibility criteria related to blood eosinophil count. Patients were randomly assigned to receive add-on subcutaneous tozorakimab (300 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations that occurred over a 52-week period among former smokers, and the first key secondary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations in the overall population. Safety was also assessed.

RESULTS: The overall population in OBERON included 446 patients in the tozorakimab group and 431 in the placebo group, and in TITANIA included 438 in the tozorakimab group and 435 in the placebo group. The annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations among former smokers was 1.34 events in the tozorakimab group and 1.90 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.88; P = 0.002) in OBERON, and 1.37 events and 2.07 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.80; P<0.001), in TITANIA. In the overall population, the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations was 1.41 events in the tozorakimab group and 2.00 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001) in OBERON, and 1.44 events and 2.03 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.84; P<0.001), in TITANIA. Adverse events occurred in 70.4% of the patients in the tozorakimab group and in 77.2% of those in the placebo group in OBERON, and in 80.1% and 79.8%, respectively, in TITANIA.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with COPD, treatment with tozorakimab resulted in a significantly lower rate of moderate or severe exacerbations than placebo in the cohort of former smokers and in the overall population of current and former smokers. (Funded by AstraZeneca; OBERON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05166889; TITANIA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05158387.).

articles.title: Impact of chronic kidney disease on long-term outcomes after left main percutaneous coronary intervention: a propensity score-matched analysis with up to 10 years of follow-up.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major determinant of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Patients with CKD undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) represent a particularly high-risk population; however, data on a long-term prognostic impact of CKD in individuals treated with PCI for left main coronary artery disease (LM CAD) remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term impact of CKD on outcomes after LM PCI.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center, prospective registry study analyzed 1321 patients who underwent LM PCI. Propensity score matching based on age, sex, diabetes status, left ventricular ejection fraction, and SYNTAX score was performed in patients treated between January 2015 and December 2020, yielding a matched cohort of 354 patients (177 with and 177 without CKD). CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60 ml/min/1.73 m2.

RESULTS: During median (interquartile range) follow-up of 2199 (1045-2909) days, CKD was associated with a higher rate of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.75; 95% CI, 1.3-2.34; P <0.001), cardiac death (HR, 2.1; 95% CI, 1.33-3.33; P = 0.001), stroke, and major adverse cardiovascular events. In contrast, no significant long-term differences were observed between CKD and non-CKD patients in the incidence of myocardial infarction. Procedural characteristics, periprocedural complications, and procedural success rates were comparable between the groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In the patients undergoing PCI for LM CAD, CKD predicts worse long-term survival despite comparable procedural and ischemic outcomes. The excess mortality appears to be driven by systemic rather than revascularization-related factors, underscoring the need for intensified long-term multidisciplinary management in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with syncope who present to the emergency department for evaluation, diagnosing an underlying cardiac arrhythmia remains difficult.

METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized, controlled trial at 45 hospitals in the United Kingdom to assess the effects of 14-day cardiac monitoring on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes among patients with syncope. Adults with syncope that remained unexplained after an evaluation in the emergency department were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo 14-day ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring (the intervention group) or to receive the standard care provided for patients with unexplained syncope at each participating site (the standard-care group). The primary outcome was the mean number of patient-reported episodes of syncope at 1 year.

RESULTS: A total of 2234 patients underwent randomization: 1123 were assigned to the intervention group and 1111 to the standard-care group. The mean age of the patients was 58.3 years, and 52.1% were male. After the exclusion of patients who did not complete any follow-up, a total of 1970 patients (1004 in the intervention group and 966 in the standard-care group) were included in the primary analysis. The mean (±SD) number of patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year was 1.37±5.10 in the intervention group and 1.58±8.56 in the standard-care group (incidence rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 1.18; P = 0.42). A total of 49 adverse events were reported in the intervention group, and 8 adverse events were reported in the standard-care group, with 1 serious adverse event in each group.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with syncope that remained unexplained after evaluation in the emergency department, the use of 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring did not result in significantly fewer patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation and National Health Service Research Scotland; ASPIRED ISRCTN Registry number, ISRCTN10278811.).

articles.title: Prognostic impact of pericardial effusion in patients with acute myocarditis.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Recent Guidelines of the European Society of Cardiology have introduced the concept of Inflammatory Myocardial and Pericardial Syndrome (IMPS), a unified entity encompassing both myocarditis and pericarditis. This framework reflects the continuum between these conditions in term of anatomy, shared aetiologies, and a common diagnostic approach. This study sought (i) to describe factors associated with pericardial involvement; (ii) to compare the outcomes of patients hospitalized for proven acute myocarditis (AM) with or without pericardial effusion; (iii) to identify the independent correlates of clinical outcome.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This is an observational ambispective cohort study based on the AMPHIBIA registry (Assistance Publique-Hôpitaux de Paris/ACTION Study Group), including patients hospitalized for proven AM between August 2008 and December 2024 at La Pitié Salpêtrière Hospital, Paris, France. Patients were stratified into two groups based on the presence of pericardial effusion on admission transthoracic echocardiography, ranging from minimal effusions to tamponade. The main composite outcome was defined as the occurrence of all-cause death, temporary mechanical circulatory support, severe ventricular arrhythmia, and heart transplantation, at the longest follow-up, up to 7 years. A total of 581 patients with AM were included [follow-up 3.7 (1.3-7.3) years]. Among them, 134 (23%) patients presented with pericardial effusion and 447 (77%) patients without. Four independent variables were associated with pericardial effusion at admission: left ventricular (LV) dysfunction, immunological myocarditis, elevated CRP, and fever. The occurrence of the composite event was significantly higher in patients with pericardial effusion compared to those without [38.1% vs. 15.7%, hazard ratio (HR) 2.69, 95% confidence interval (CI) (1.88-3.86), P < 0.001]. This difference was observed regardless of pericardial effusion size. After multivariable analysis, pericardial effusion was independently associated with the main composite outcome [HR 1.99 (1.32-3.00), P < 0.001.

CONCLUSION: This study characterizes the phenotypes and outcomes of patients hospitalized for an AM, with and without pericardial effusion. Pericardial involvement was associated with LV dysfunction, immunological myocarditis, elevated CRP, and fever and was linked to a markedly higher risk of the composite outcome, remaining an independent predictor of adverse events. Differentiating these two phenotypes may provide physicians with valuable guidance for managing therapy in these patients.

articles.title: Cell-Based Therapies and Drug Repurposing in Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of Nippon Medical School = Nippon Ika Daigaku zasshi
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, and contributes substantially to the global burden of disease. Although reperfusion therapies such as intravenous thrombolysis with recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) and mechanical thrombectomy have transformed acute management, the stringent eligibility criteria, narrow treatment windows, and limited accessibility restrict their use to <20% of patients. Many treated individuals have significant neurological deficits, and this underscores the urgent need for therapies that extend beyond revascularization. Two promising approaches have emerged: cell-based therapy and drug repurposing. Stem cell-based interventions, including mesenchymal stem cells, neural stem cells, and induced pluripotent stem cell-derived products, primarily act via paracrine mechanisms to modulate inflammation, attenuate oxidative stress, promote angiogenesis, and enhance neuroplasticity. Simultaneously, drug repurposing leverages the established safety and pharmacology of existing agents to accelerate clinical translation. Valproic acid, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, and perampanel, a selective AMPA receptor antagonist, target key mechanisms, such as excitotoxicity, oxidative injury, and epigenetic regulation. This review synthesizes the current evidence on both strategies and emphasizes mechanistic overlaps, clinical trial findings, translational barriers, and future directions. Unlike previous reviews that have addressed cell-based therapies or drug repurposing separately, we propose a unique phase-specific integrative framework that rationally combines these complementary strategies with reperfusion therapy and rehabilitation to achieve durable neuroprotection and meaningful recovery in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Human milk oligosaccharide (2'-FL) modifies the gut microbiome in children after bone marrow transplant.
articles.abstract: Dysbiosis after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (allo-HSCT) predisposes to acute gastrointestinal (GI) graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are prebiotics that establish a favorable intestinal microbiome. We hypothesized that peritransplant HMOs would reduce dysbiosis, and conducted a prospective phase 1/2 study in which 70 patients received oral, daily 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL), the most abundant HMO, from start of conditioning through day +30. Primary phase 1 and phase 2 end points were safety and tolerability of 2'-FL and longitudinal preservation of microbiome diversity, respectively. Phase 1 and phase 2 patients with ≥60% adherence were evaluated by correlative analyses. Twenty-nine age-matched patients with available samples in our institutional biorepository served as contemporary controls. 2'-FL was safe and well tolerated on the phase 1 study, which established dosing for the phase 2 study. Shannon diversity was preserved in 2'-FL recipients and declined from baseline to day +30 in controls (P = .04). Generalized linear mixed model analysis revealed higher association of Bifidobacteria and Blautia with 2'-FL (adjusted P< .05). Higher fecal isoleucine (P = .005), tyrosine (P = .05), and taurine (P = .04) were observed in 2'-FL recipients, all associated with protection and regeneration of intestinal epithelium. Lower plasma regulatory islet-derived 3α (P = .053) and suppressor of tumorigenicity 2 levels (P = .038) were observed in 2'-FL recipients compared with controls. Incidence of grade II-IV acute GI GVHD was 0% in 2'-FL recipients compared with 17% in controls (P = .009). Adenovirus reactivation was 0% in 2'-FL recipients compared with 17% in controls (P = .009). 2'-FL is safe and modifies the gut microbiome in children after allo-HSCT. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04263597.

articles.title: Malar rash in systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical, serological, and therapeutic associations in a single-center retrospective study of 1039 patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Malar rash is a hallmark manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); however, its clinical and immunological significance remains incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the associations of malar rash with clinical phenotype, serological profile, comorbidities, and treatment patterns in SLE.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1039 patients with SLE who fulfilled the 2019 European League Against Rheumatism / American College of Rheumatology classification criteria and were treated at a tertiary referral center between 2012 and 2022. The patients were stratified according to the presence or absence of malar rash.

RESULTS: Malar rash was present in 444 patients (42.7%). The individuals with malar rash had an earlier disease onset (32 vs 37 y; P <0.001) and longer disease duration (14 vs 11 y; P <0.001) than those without this manifestation. Constitutional symptoms were more frequent in the patients with malar rash (81.8% vs 73.2%; P = 0.001), including fever, fatigue, myalgia, and weight loss. Mucocutaneous and musculoskeletal manifestations were also more common in this group (all P <0.001). Leukopenia occurred more frequently in the malar rash group, whereas hemolytic anemia was more common in the individuals without malar rash. Pulmonary involvement was less frequent in the patients with malar rash, while the prevalence of renal and neurological manifestations did not differ between the groups. Anti‑Smith and antiribonucleoprotein antibodies were more frequently detected in the patients with malar rash. The individuals with this manifestation were also more likely to receive antimalarial agents and azathioprine.

CONCLUSIONS: Malar rash is associated with an earlier SLE onset and a distinct clinical phenotype characterized by increased constitutional, mucocutaneous, and musculoskeletal involvement, specific serological features, and less frequent pulmonary manifestations.

articles.title: Inflammation in coronary syndromes in clinical practice: a clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute Cardiovascular Care of the European Society of Cardiology, the European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases, the European Society of Cardiology Council on Basic Cardiovascular Science, and the European Society of Cardiology Council for Cardiology Practice.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract: Inflammation is a key driver of coronary syndromes across the continuum from chronic coronary syndromes to acute coronary syndromes. It contributes to atherogenesis, plaque destabilization, and ischaemic events and influences myocardial injury, repair, and remodelling. Inflammatory activity is further amplified by metabolic and autoimmune comorbidities such as diabetes, obesity, and connective tissue diseases, with obesity representing a major driver of chronic low-grade inflammation through adipose tissue dysfunction and cytokine activation, while psychosocial stress and environmental exposures including air pollution serve as additional triggers. Genetic variations, including human leucocyte antigen genotypes, modulate individual susceptibility to vascular inflammation and myocardial injury. This expert consensus from the European Society of Cardiology's Association for Acute CardioVascular Care summarizes the current understanding of inflammation across the full spectrum of coronary syndromes, including underlying mechanisms, relevant biomarkers, and imaging approaches that characterize vascular inflammation, and integrates insights from experimental and clinical studies. Importantly, this document provides explicit consensus-based guidance on when, how, and in whom inflammation should be assessed and treated in routine clinical practice. While the causal association between inflammation and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is well established, pharmacological modification of inflammation has produced conflicting evidence. Some agents, such as low-dose colchicine, have demonstrated modest reductions in cardiovascular events, although results across trials have been inconsistent. Other anti-inflammatory therapies have not shown clinical benefit, whereas selective cytokine inhibition with canakinumab has reduced cardiovascular risk at the cost of increased infection rates. The present manuscript also focuses on the evaluation of inflammatory activity in cardiovascular patients in routine clinical practice. It further discusses criteria for patient selection and clinical decision-making regarding the introduction of anti-inflammatory therapy in individuals with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Beyond A and B: exploring a novel dynamic electrocardiogram change in Wellens syndrome.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Wellens syndrome is a high-risk electrocardiographic pattern associated with significant left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery disease. Although Pattern A (biphasic T waves) and Pattern B (deep symmetric T-wave inversion) are recognized, their temporal relationship remains incompletely defined. We aimed to describe the clinical, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and angiographic characteristics of patients with spontaneous in-hospital evolution from Pattern A to Pattern B.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective single-centre study included 51 consecutive patients with Wellens syndrome and angiographic confirmation of significant LAD disease (≥70% stenosis). Serial electrocardiogram (ECGs) obtained during the first 24 h were reviewed by two cardiologists blinded to angiographic findings. Eighteen patients (35.3%) had documented evolution from Pattern A to Pattern B before angiography. Fourteen cases occurred within 6 h of admission and four between 6 and 24 h; all were documented during pain-free intervals. The median left ventricular ejection fraction was 53% (Interquartile Range [IQR], 46-60), and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin was elevated in 12 patients (66.7%). Left anterior descending disease was confirmed in all patients, with isolated LAD involvement in 10 and multivessel disease in eight. Revascularization was performed in 13 patients [10 by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and three by coronary artery bypass grafting]. All PCI procedures achieved Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) 3 flow. No in-hospital deaths or major adverse cardiovascular events occurred.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with confirmed Wellens syndrome, Pattern A-to-B evolution occurred in approximately one-third of patients before coronary angiography, suggesting that dynamic ECG evolution occurs during the acute phase. Further studies are warranted to determine its diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications.

articles.title: Cardiac mechanical efficiency in patients with cardiogenic shock.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is characterized by impaired left ventricular (LV) mechanical performance and adverse remodelling. We evaluated whether transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived modified cardiac efficiency (mCE), integrating stroke work and residual LV volume, is associated with short- and long-term mortality in CS and whether its prognostic value differs by shock aetiology.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive adults admitted with CS to the cardiac intensive care unit at Mayo Clinic (2007-2018) were included if TTE was performed within 24 h. mCE was calculated as (stroke volume × estimated LV end-systolic pressure) divided by LV end-systolic volume and categorized into quartiles. Primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcome was 1-year mortality. Multivariable logistic and Cox models adjusted for illness severity, comorbidity burden, shock aetiology, cardiac arrest, vasoactive therapy, and mechanical circulatory support. Among 667 patients, median mCE was 48 mmHg (IQR 32-74). In-hospital mortality was 28% and increased stepwise across decreasing mCE quartiles. The lowest quartile had a 2.5-fold higher adjusted odds of in-hospital death (OR 2.53; 95%CI: 1.49-4.37; P < 0.001). One-year mortality was 41%; the lowest quartile had a two-fold higher adjusted hazard of death (HR 2.05; 95%CI: 1.45-2.89; P < 0.001). Associations were stronger in acute coronary syndrome-related CS (interaction P = 0.035 for in-hospital; P = 0.015 for 1-year). Within the lowest quartile, reduced systolic pressure further amplified mortality risk.

CONCLUSION: Early TTE-derived mCE was independently associated with short- and long-term mortality in CS, particularly in acute coronary syndrome-related CS, and captured the interaction between ventricular remodelling and mechanical performance underlying high-risk phenotypes.

articles.title: Independent Predictors of Major Wound Complications Requiring Revision Surgery Following Lumbar Spine Surgery: A Large Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative complications after lumbar spine surgery, including surgical site infections and superficial wound problems drive up costs, prolong hospital stay, and worsen outcomes, yet existing studies of their risk factors are often limited by small sample sizes and weak clinical validation. Although several patient-related risk factors have been identified, many existing studies are limited by small sample sizes or insufficient clinical validation of postoperative wound complications.

OBJECTIVE: To identify independent patient- and procedure-related risk factors for major wound complications requiring operative revision after lumbar spine surgery.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.

METHODS: Patients undergoing lumbar decompression or instrumented fusion between 2017 and 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Data on demographics, comorbidities (Charlson Comorbidity Index), American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, preoperative laboratory values, operative duration, blood loss, type of surgery, and intraoperative events were extracted. Group comparisons were performed using appropriate statistical tests. Variables with P < 0.05 were included in a multivariate logistic regression model. Missing data were handled by multiple imputation by chained equations. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated.

RESULTS: A total of 4067 patients were included, of whom 121 (3.0%) developed major wound complications requiring revision surgery. Infection was confirmed in 75.2% of cases, with a mean time to revision of 24.6 ± 13.3 days. Independent predictors included higher body mass index (OR 1.07 per kg/m², 95% CI 1.04-1.11, P < 0.001), elevated C-reactive protein (OR 1.01 per mg/L, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, P = 0.007), diabetes (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.27-2.98, P = 0.002), congestive heart failure (OR 4.56, 95% CI 1.42-14.63, P = 0.011), prior lumbar surgery (OR 1.96, 95% CI 1.31-2.94, P < 0.001), dural tear (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.17-2.98, P = 0.009), and blood loss (per 100 mL, OR 1.11, 95% CI 1.01-1.21, P = 0.027).

CONCLUSION: Major wound complications are associated with comorbidities, inflammatory status, prior surgery, dural tears, and blood loss.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Preoperative recognition of the seven identified risk factors allows surgeons to stratify individual wound-complication risk, optimize modifiable comorbidities, and target perioperative prevention toward the highest-risk patients undergoing lumbar spine surgery.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 3 .

articles.title: An Algorithmic Approach Including Local Antibiotic Delivery for Spine Infection Treatment: Outcomes at 1 Institution.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple treatment strategies for spine infections exist, including systemic antibiotic therapy alone or in conjunction with debridement surgeries. However, data on algorithmic approaches tailored to infection type and severity are limited. Furthermore, local antibiotic delivery using a dissolvable calcium sulfate carrier, which has been shown to be effective in treating other orthopedic infections, has been sparsely reported in spine infection treatment.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 119 surgically managed spine infection cases (2016-2020) was performed to determine (1) the proportion of patients achieving infection resolution with institutional protocols incorporating calcium sulfate biodegradable beads, (2) risk factors for treatment failure, (3) prevalence of bead-associated adverse effects, and (4) microbiological profiles of treated infections. Patients were treated according to institutional protocols, including aggressive debridement, instrumented stabilization when instability is present, local antibiotic bead placement, and chronic, systemic antimicrobial therapy. Univariate logistic regression assessed associations between patient, operative, and infection characteristics with treatment failure odds.

RESULTS: Tobramycin/vancomycin-loaded calcium sulfate biodegradable beads were the most common type used. Among 119 patients, 81.5% achieved infection resolution without recurrence. Sixteen patients experienced infection recurrence, and 6 patients died of sepsis. Acute kidney injury and acute liver injury were significantly associated with treatment failure. A significant association was observed between calcium sulfate bead volume and risk of transient hypercalcemia, though all cases resolved without bead removal. The most commonly treated infections were polymicrobial.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that calcium sulfate antibiotic beads, when incorporated into an algorithmic approach, facilitate successful infection eradication with minimal systemic toxicity. Careful patient selection and dose limitation are essential to mitigate potential adverse effects.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The use of biodegradable calcium sulfate beads in an algorithmic treatment approach achieves successful infection eradication with little evidence of antibiotic bead-induced systemic toxicity. Bead volume should be minimized to reduce hypercalcemia risk. Patients with acute kidney injury or acute liver injury may require more aggressive treatment.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4 (therapeutic study).

articles.title: Tagraxofusp, azacitidine, and venetoclax for blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.
articles.abstract: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) is an orphan, aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by high CD123 expression. Tagraxofusp (TAG), a CD123-directed toxin, is the first approved therapy. Prior studies demonstrated BPDCN dependence on BCL2, sensitivity to venetoclax (VEN), and reversal of TAG resistance with azacitidine (AZA). We conducted a phase 2 study evaluating combination therapy with TAG, AZA, and VEN in patients with BPDCN. Patients with previously untreated (1L) or relapsed/refractory (R/R) BPDCN received 28-day cycles of AZA (75 mg/m2 on days 1-7), VEN (400 mg on days 1-21), and TAG (12 μg/kg on days 4-6). Eligibility followed TAG guidelines to mitigate risk of capillary leak syndrome (CLS). Twenty-seven patients were enrolled (16 1L, 11 R/R), with median age of 70 years (range, 21-81). Composite complete remission (composed of: complete remission [CR], CR with incomplete count recovery, and CR clinical) rates were 88% in 1L and 64% in R/R cohorts. Median duration of response was not reached in 1L and was 7.2 months in R/R patients. CLS occurred in 15% of patients, most were grade 2. In the 1L cohort, median overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached; the 2-year OS was 65% and 2-year PFS was 53%. Median OS in R/R patients was 8.4 months. A high proportion of patients proceeded to allogeneic stem cell transplantation in remission (63% in 1L, including 10/11 patients aged ≤75 years; 55% in R/R). TAG-AZA-VEN is highly active in both 1L and relapsed BPDCN with a predictable and manageable safety profile, supporting its use as a new therapeutic option. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT03113643.
