articles.title: One-year and 5-year transition risks between major bleeding, reinfarction, and death following acute myocardial infarction in England and Wales: a population-based cohort study.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
AIMS: There is limited data on the long-term transition risks between major bleeding, reinfarction, and death following acute myocardial infarction (AMI). We examined 1-year and 5-year transition risks of major bleeding, reinfarction, and mortality post-AMI.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed national registry data of AMI patients across England and Wales between 2005 and 2021. Multistate modelling was used to estimate the transition-specific adjusted incidence rates (IRs) across the three outcomes using a six-state model with nine transitions. Out of 837 384 patients included, 19.8% had bleeding, 8.1% reinfarction, and 20.6% death as their first event post- AMI admission. Of those with bleeding, 39.4% died while 49.9% of those with reinfarction died. Overall, females had higher rates of transitioning to any of the five states than males. A reference female patient with median age (76.3 years), at 1-year had an IR of 6.7 (95% CI 6.5-6.9) ×100 person-years (PY) for AMI admission → bleeding transition, 0.2 (95% CI 0.2-0.2) ×100PY for AMI admission → reinfarction, 43.5 (95% CI 41.9-45.2) ×100PY for AMI admission → death, 22.2 (95% CI 20.9-23.5) ×100PY for bleeding → death, and 41.9 (95% CI 38.1-46.0) ×100PY for reinfarction → death. At 5-year, the IRs decreased to 2.1 (95% CI 2.0-2.2) ×100PY, 0.04 (95% CI 0.04-0.05) ×100PY, 17.5 (95% CI 16.9-18.2) ×100PY, 9.7 (95% CI 9.2-10.3) ×100PY, and 17.6 (95% CI 16.0-19.4) ×100PY, respectively. A reference male patient with median age (67.1 years) at 1-year had an IR of 5.2 (95% CI 5.0-5.4) ×100PY for AMI admission → bleeding transition, 0.2 (95% CI 0.2-0.2) ×100PY for AMI admission→ reinfarction, 23.7 (95% CI 22.8-24.6) ×100PY for AMI admission → death, 14.5 (95% CI 13.6-15.4) ×100PY for bleeding → death, and 25.9 (95% CI 23.8-28.3) ×100PY for reinfarction → death. Similarly, 5-year IRs decreased to 1.6 (95% CI 1.6-1.7) ×100PY, 0.04 (95% CI 0.04-0.04) ×100PY, 9.5 (95% CI 9.2-9.9) ×100PY, 6.3 (95% CI 5.9-6.8) ×100PY, and 10.9 (95% CI 10.0-11.9) ×100PY, respectively. Also, those with diabetes and white patients had higher transition rates than those without diabetes and black patients.

CONCLUSION: In this national AMI cohort, 5-year direct death and bleeding events were more frequent than reinfarction, and the highest mortality occurred in women after AMI admission and in men following reinfarction. These transition patterns quantify the substantial absolute risks patients face post-AMI and highlight important sex-specific differences in adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Associations between admission C-reactive protein and in-hospital mortality amongst patients with cardiogenic shock.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Systemic inflammation in cardiogenic shock is associated with increased disease severity and mortality. C-reactive protein (CRP) is a widely accessible inflammatory biomarker that may aid phenotyping and risk stratification. We evaluated the association between admission CRP and in-hospital mortality in patients with cardiogenic shock.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using a multicentre, nationally representative database, we identified adults with a discharge diagnosis of cardiogenic shock from 2015 to 2023 who had CRP measured within 2 days of hospital admission; patients with sepsis were excluded. C-reactive protein was analysed in tertiles. Inverse probability weighting (IPW) was used to assess associations with in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay and total cost. We identified 26 525 patients; median (interquartile ranges) CRP was 18.4 mg/L (5.0-67.0 mg/L). The in-hospital mortality was 28.7, 32.7, and 42.3% across tertiles 1-3. In-hospital mortality increased by 19% for each 50-unit increase in CRP [odds ratio (OR) 1.19; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.16-1.21, P < 0.001). After IPW, tertiles 2 and 3 had higher absolute mortality risks compared with tertile 1 by 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4-5.3%) and 12.4% (95% CI: 10.9-13.9%), respectively (both, P < 0.001). Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to Day 1 CRP measurement, primary diagnoses of heart failure or myocardial infarction, and among patients requiring early mechanical circulatory support (all, P < 0.05). The median ICU and hospital stay increased significantly across tertiles (all, P < 0.001); total cost was not statistically different.

CONCLUSION: In patients with cardiogenic shock, a readily available biomarker, elevated CRP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality.

articles.title: Improving Umami Sensitivity through 3-Day Taste Recall Training for Healthy Young Adults: Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: The Tohoku journal of experimental medicine
articles.abstract: Umami, recognized as the fifth basic taste, serves as an indicator of protein-derived amino acids and plays an important role in maintaining nutritional status and health through flavor enhancement, digestive reflex stimulation, and satiety regulation. Taste recall training has been shown to improve the perceptions of sweetness, saltiness, sourness, and bitterness, but it remains unclear whether umami perception and discrimination are trainable. Two independent randomized controlled experiments involving healthy adults were conducted: (A) five-basic-taste recall and (B) umami-targeted taste recall training. Participants were randomly assigned to the training or control group, and taste recognition thresholds were assessed before and after the intervention. Five-basic-taste recall training improved umami taste sensitivity in the training group, whereas no corresponding changes were observed in the control group. Umami-targeted taste recall training significantly enhanced the sensitivity to similar umami compounds relative to the control group. Future studies involving patients with taste disorders may elucidate the efficacy of these methods. These findings suggest the potential for developing novel approaches to managing taste disorders.

articles.title: Validating fracture risk after stoke: a call to action to optimize skeletal health after stroke?
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research

articles.title: Validating the FRAC-Stroke score: targeting those at highest risk of fracture.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: Fracture risk is increased after stroke, but there is a lack of specific, effective tools to screen and prevent minimal trauma fractures (MTF) post-stroke. While the Fracture Risk after Ischemic Stroke score (FRAC-Stroke score), developed to predict fracture risk post-stroke, shows promising performance, it has not yet been widely adopted or validated in large cohorts outside of Canada. We aimed to: (1) evaluate the reliability and validity of the FRAC-Stroke score in predicting MTF and (2) determine the optimal score to classify patients at highest fracture risk following ischemic stroke. A retrospective cohort study was undertaken using data from the PRECISE study, which included person-level linked administrative data from the Australian Stroke Clinical Registry (AuSCR, 2014-2016). The FRAC-Stroke score at hospital discharge was determined for survivors of ischemic stroke, aged >50 yr, using coded comorbidities derived in the prior 5-yr period and modified Rankin Scale. Fine-Gray models were built to evaluate associations of the FRAC-Stroke score with MTF within 12 mo post-discharge, accounting for death as the competing risk. Among 4545 adults, the median FRAC-Stroke score was 8 (IQR 5-11) and 118 patients (2.6%) sustained a MTF within 12 mo post-discharge. The optimal FRAC-Stroke score cut-point to stratify MTF risk was 11.5, with a c-statistic of 0.70. Participants with a FRAC-Stroke score ≥12 (vs <12) had a 5.5-fold increased risk of MTF (CI 3.8-7.9, p < .01). When stratified by quintiles of FRAC-Stroke score, those in quintile 5 (FRAC-Stroke score ≥ 14) had a 15.2-fold increased risk of MTF than those in quintile 1 (FRAC-Stroke score < 3; CI 6.6-35.2, p < .01). The FRAC-Stroke score reliably identifies increased fracture risk in the Australian ischemic stroke population, with a score of 12+ able to discriminate those at high risk of fracture.

articles.title: Epidemiology of midlife fracture: self-reported and hospital episode data from the UK Biobank.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: Fracture risk in midlife (ages 35-65 yr) is underrecognized despite its implications for long-term skeletal health. Using UK Biobank data, we aimed to characterize fracture epidemiology in this critical age group through 2 complementary approaches. We conducted 2 studies: a cross-sectional analysis of self-reported fractures (2006-2010) to estimate annualized incidence risk per 10 000 people and a longitudinal cohort analysis using linked Hospital Episode Statistics (HES; 2001-2022) to calculate incidence rates per 10 000 person-years, both stratified by sex, skeletal site, and 10-yr age bands. Fracture incidence varied substantially by age and sex. Among women, risk increased from age 35 yr and accelerated notably from the mid-40s, peaking at 246 per 10 000 people in the 56-65-yr age group. This female trajectory, emerging earlier than previously recognized, contrasts with men, whose highest fracture risk occurred in early midlife (peak: 232 per 10 000 people; ages 35-45). Across both sexes and age bands, the most reported fracture sites were "other" (including digits and facial bones), wrist, ankle, arm, leg, spine, and hip, in descending order. In HES-linked data, 43 572 fractures were identified. Incidence patterns mirrored those from self-report: higher early midlife fracture rates in men, followed by a transition to female predominance from approximately age 45. This large-scale, dual-method analysis offers the first clear evidence that female fracture risk begins to increase from age 35, with a marked acceleration from 45 yr onward. These sex-specific trajectories in midlife fracture incidence are not fully captured in current clinical models and indicate that further work is needed to determine whether earlier or tailored approaches to risk assessment could provide cost-effective benefit in reducing the burden of fracture in midlife.

articles.title: Expected change: a new concept for monitoring patients on oral bisphosphonates.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: It is essential to closely monitor the response to oral bisphosphonate therapy for osteoporosis, as many patients are nonadherent. The conventional approach is to monitor whether changes in BMD or bone turnover markers (BTMs) exceed the least significant change. This approach assumed that if a patient were not receiving a treatment, there would be no change in the BMD. We propose an alternative approach, that of expected change. We define this expected change as the change in BMD (at 24 mo) or BTMs (at 3 mo) that is exceeded in 90% of patients who are adherent with oral bisphosphonate therapy. We studied 108 postmenopausal women (age < 85 yr) who were randomized to the licensed dose of alendronate, ibandronate, or risedronate treatment for 2 yr, along with calcium and vitamin D supplementation. We identified the performance of BMD and BTMs in 3 ways. We calculated the signal-to-noise ratio, which was lower for BMD (4.1 and 2.1 for lumbar spine BMD (LSBMD) and total hip BMD (THBMD), respectively) compared to BTMs (9.4 and 10.2 for C-telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX) and procollagen I N-propeptide (PINP), respectively). We estimated the response rate as the percentage of women exceeding the least significant change, which was lower for BMD (47% and 24% for LSBMD and THBMD, respectively) than for BTMs (96% and 94% for CTX and PINP, respectively). We estimated the expected change as the 90th (or 10th) percentile of change in adherent patients. We required the expected change to exceed the least significant change, and this was not observed for LSBMD and THBMD, but it was observed for CTX and PINP (expected changes of 0.233 and 12.1 ng/mL, respectively). Thus, the BTMs CTX and PINP showed the best performance as response markers for monitoring oral bisphosphonate treatment, and the new approach is based on a biological rather than a statistical endpoint when using the expected change approach.

articles.title: Gender equity in the global rheumatology workforce: results of the Coalition for Health and Gender Equity (CHANGE) survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Gender equity remains an elusive goal across many specialist medical fields. The Coalition for Health and Gender Equity (CHANGE) conducted a comprehensive global survey assessing gender equity within the international rheumatology workforce.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey of rheumatologists and allied health professionals was conducted between January 2023 and May 2024. The 38-item survey covered demographics, gender discrimination, sexual harassment, work-family interface, and career advancement. It was translated into eight languages and disseminated through professional organisations, mailing lists and social media channels in 105 countries. Analyses included descriptive statistics and comparative tests, with gender differences evaluated after adjustment for years of work experience. Subgroup analyses included country Human Development Index (HDI), professional roles, and caregiving responsibilities, with statistical significance set at p<0.05.

RESULTS: Among 1,945 respondents (66.4% female), pronounced gender-based disparities were observed. Male professionals demonstrated higher rates of full-time employment, leadership positions, and clinical experience. Female rheumatology professionals more frequently encountered career barriers, including tasks below their expertise, hostility from colleagues, lacking leadership training opportunities, lower remuneration, and difficulties securing research funding. Women reported greater domestic responsibilities (47.5% vs 36.2%, p<0.001) and higher work-family conflict, with nearly four times the odds of experiencing sexual harassment and double the odds of experiencing bullying. Perceived experiences were more pronounced among respondents from high-HDI countries and those with caregiving responsibilities, but did not differ by professional role.

CONCLUSION: This global survey provides compelling evidence of gender disparities in rheumatology, necessitating coordinated, evidence-based interventions to address structural barriers and promote inclusive cultures.

articles.title: Protective effect and mechanism of Streptococcus D19T fermentation supernatant in asthmatic mice exposed to PM2.5.
articles.abstract: Allergic asthma is a common chronic respiratory disease, and fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤ 2.5 μm (PM2.5) remains a major environmental risk factor contributing to its global burden. However, effective preventive and therapeutic strategies for asthmatic airway inflammation with PM2.5 exposure remain limited. D19T, a novel Streptococcus strain isolated from the oropharynx of healthy children, has a favourable safety profile; furthermore, its fermentation supernatant exhibits antibacterial and anti‑inflammatory activities. This study found that D19T treatment reduced inflammatory markers and improved redox status in a mouse model of asthma with PM2.5 exposure. Non‑invasive respiratory function analysis confirmed improved lung function. Furthermore, the results showed that D19T treatment modulated the oropharyngeal and gut microbiota and systemic metabolic profiles. Overall, this study provides new evidence supporting cell‑free fermentate‑based interventions for asthmatic airway inflammation in cases of PM2.5 exposure.

articles.title: Late perfusion defects after pulmonary embolism and long-term mortality: a weighted cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual pulmonary vascular obstruction (RPVO) after pulmonary embolism (PE) is common and has been associated with adverse outcomes, although its independent prognostic significance remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether perfusion defects are independently associated with long-term mortality after PE, and secondarily to assess their relationship with dyspnoea severity.

METHODS: In this nationwide cohort study, Swedish patients with PE in 2005 who survived to 2007 underwent structured follow-up including symptom assessment and clinical evaluation. Ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) scintigraphy was recommended based on clinical judgement. V/Q scintigraphy findings were classified as normal or perfusion defects. To account for selection bias into scintigraphy, inverse probability weighting (IPW) was applied. Survival was analysed using IPW-weighted Cox regression with delayed entry at scintigraphy.

RESULTS: Among 911 patients eligible for scintigraphy, 523 underwent examination; 513 with normal findings or perfusion defects were included in the analyses. Median time from PE to scintigraphy was 6.3 years, with 8.8 years of follow-up thereafter. Perfusion defects were present in 221 patients (43%). Dyspnoea severity was not associated with perfusion defects in unadjusted or adjusted analyses. In unadjusted analyses, perfusion defects were associated with lower survival (log-rank p = 0.049). However, this association was attenuated after adjustment and was not independently associated with mortality in IPW-weighted Cox regression (hazard ratio 1.28, 95% confidence interval 0.94-1.74).

CONCLUSIONS: Perfusion defects were associated with mortality in unadjusted analyses but not after adjustment for age and comorbidities, suggesting that their apparent prognostic impact largely reflects underlying patient characteristics rather than an independent effect.

articles.title: Simplified jailed balloon technique: proof-of-concept for side branch preservation without routine proximal optimization or final kissing balloon.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The modified jailed balloon technique (M-JBT) decreases side branch (SB) occlusion during bifurcation percutaneous coronary intervention by simultaneously inflating an SB balloon alongside main vessel stent deployment. Conventionally, M-JBT requires subsequent proximal optimization (POT), SB rewiring, and final kissing balloon inflation (KBI), adding complexity to the procedure. The authors defined a simplified approach-the Simplified Jailed Balloon Technique (S-JBT)-where postdilation is performed using only the stent delivery balloon, omitting POT, rewiring, and final KBI.

METHODS: To validate the physiological rationale of S-JBT, the authors measured SB resting full-cycle ratio (RFR) at 3 time points (baseline, post-M-JBT, and postdilation) in 6 consecutive patients undergoing S-JBT for LAD-diagonal bifurcation lesions using the jailed pressure wire technique.

RESULTS: RFR was maintained at all timepoints (baseline: 0.82 ± 0.17; post-M-JBT: 0.84 ± 0.14; postdilation: 0.86 ± 0.15), with no angiographic SB compromise.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the favorable SB ostial geometry established with simultaneous inflation persists after stent balloon postdilation, and that the primary mechanism of SB protection resides in the simultaneous inflation step. S-JBT may offer a practical, simplified SB protection strategy, particularly for bifurcation lesions with small side branches.

articles.title: Prehospital Delay: The Unfinished Business of STEMI Care in Beijing.
Dynamics and branch-point motion in entangled symmetric star polymers examined via slip-spring and molecular dynamics simulations of rheology, diffusion, and scattering functions.
articles.abstract: This study examines the dynamics of entangled star polymers using the slip-spring (SS) model, comparing its predictions quantitatively with molecular dynamics simulations of the Kremer-Grest (KG) model and qualitatively with experimental data. We demonstrate that branch-point (BP) diffusion in the SS model is only modestly inhibited by increasing the functionality (f) or by suppressing constraint release. This cannot be explained by the naïve picture in which hopping motion is induced by the loss of entanglements on f - 2 arms, suggesting diffusive mechanisms that require escape from entanglements only on fewer arms. After confirming that the SS model qualitatively reproduces experimental results for linear rheology, BP-to-arm-end vector relaxation, and diffusion, we examine the mean-squared displacements (MSDs) and intermediate scattering functions (ISFs) computed by both models. While linear viscoelastic behavior is known to be almost independent of f, the KG model shows clear f-dependence of MSD and ISF. With an appropriately determined number of entanglements, the SS model reproduces the KG results well at long times, the regime that a coarse-grained model is expected to describe. Deviations appear at short times, possibly because, unlike the KG model, the SS model assumes Gaussian statistics at all length scales. To discuss the differences between the SS and KG models, we examined the radial distribution functions between BPs in the KG model, which show that close approach between two BPs becomes increasingly unlikely as f increases, and this can be interpreted as an effective repulsion between BPs. We discussed how this observation may inform possible future extensions of the SS model.

articles.title: Coughing and Deep Breathing vs. Incentive Spirometry Nursing Interventions: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incentive spirometry (IS) has long been considered a standard nursing intervention to prevent postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). Similarly, coughing and deep breathing (CDB) is a standard intervention to promote lung expansion and secretion clearance. Studies have reported mixed results regarding the use of IS alone (IS-A) in the prevention of PPCs.

PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of CDB alone (CDB-A) versus combined CDB and IS (CDB-IS) in preventing PPCs and 30-day readmissions among postsurgical patients without underlying pulmonary disease, while also examining IS-A as a clinically relevant comparator across postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis included electronic health record data from adult inpatient surgical encounters at a tertiary academic medical center from July to December 2019 and July to December 2022. A total of 2,386 encounters were included in the primary analysis.

RESULTS: In the 2,386 encounters, 508 (21.3%) patients were prescribed IS-A, 1,127 (47.2%) were prescribed CDB-A, and 751 (31.5%) were prescribed CDB-IS. PPCs were rare, occurring in approximately 1% of encounters, with no significant differences between the intervention groups. After adjusting for surgery type, surgery duration, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification level, physical therapy (PT) order status, Bedside Mobility Assessment Tool scores, and prior pulmonary-related diagnoses, patients prescribed CDB-A had higher odds of 30-day readmission compared with those prescribed IS-A (odds ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.02-1.60; P = 0.03). No significant difference in readmissions was observed between patients prescribed CDB-IS and those prescribed IS-A. Longer hospital length of stay and absence of PT orders were independently associated with higher readmission risk.

CONCLUSIONS: PPCs were uncommon in the study cohort regardless of respiratory intervention type. IS-A was not associated with increased PPCs and was associated with lower readmission rates compared with CDB-A in the primary analysis, though this association was not sustained in sensitivity analyses. Findings support continued IS use with a multimodal postoperative care approach emphasizing early mobility and PT.

articles.title: Phenomenology, Etiology, and Severity of Delirium Among Patients Referred to Consultation-liaison Psychiatry Services in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delirium is an acute neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by disturbances in attention, awareness, and cognition. It is highly prevalent among hospitalized patients but remains under-recognized, particularly in its hypoactive form. Consultation-liaison psychiatry (CLP) services are pivotal for early identification, yet detailed clinical profiles from Indian tertiary-care settings are sparse.

METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional study enrolled 94 adult inpatients referred for acute confusional states between October 2022 and April 2024. We used the Delirium Rating Scale-Revised-98 (DRS-R-98), the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS), and the Delirium Etiology Checklist (DEC). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and one-way ANOVA. Statistical significance was set at p < .05.

RESULTS: The mean age was 59.29 ± 16.12 years; 81.9% were male. Severe impairment was most frequent in attention (52.1%), short-term memory (50.0%), and orientation (48.9%). Hyperactive delirium was predominant (81.9%). The cohort's mean total DRS-R-98 score was 21.94 ± 8.12. Increasing age showed a significant association with delirium subtype (F = 5.68, p = .005), with mixed and hypoactive presentations occurring in older patients. Metabolic/endocrine disturbances (91.5%) and systemic infections (40.4%) were the leading etiological contributors.

CONCLUSIONS: Delirium in CLP referrals is characterized by marked cognitive impairment, predominance of hyperactive presentation, and multifactorial etiology. The over-representation of hyperactive cases likely reflects referral bias. Structured assessment tools and routine screening are essential for early detection, particularly of hypoactive delirium. Future multicenter prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Recalibrating the urine output criteria for acute kidney injury: stage-specific thresholds matched to creatinine-stage-derived mortality.
Plonmarlimab, a GM-CSF-neutralizing antibody, for macrophage activation syndrome.
articles.abstract: Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a subtype of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) and a rare, life-threatening complication of uncontrolled rheumatic diseases, characterized by systemic inflammation driven by aberrant activation of macrophages. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of plonmarlimab, a high-affinity neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), for the treatment of MAS. In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm clinical trial (NCT07034209 and CTR20230579), 18 patients with MAS secondary to systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease who were refractory to or had relapsed after high-dose glucocorticoid therapy were enrolled. Patients received plonmarlimab once weekly for 8 weeks at 6 mg/kg as the starting in the accelerated titration stage, and then at 10 mg/kg for the first two doses followed by dose adjustments at the investigator's discretion. The primary endpoint, overall response rate at week 8, was 83.3% (15/18) among all treated patients. The median time to response was 2.1 weeks (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.0-3.1), and the median time to remission of MAS symptoms was 1.1 weeks (95% CI, 1.0-2.3). The least-squares mean percentage reduction in glucocorticoid dose from baseline to week 8 was 79.3% (95% CI, 76.3-82.3), and 83.3% of patients (15/18) achieved a ≥ 50% reduction. No grade ≥ 3 infections were observed. Biomarker analysis showed rapid reductions in ferritin and interleukin (IL)-18 levels. Plonmarlimab showed promising clinical activity and was generally well tolerated in patients with MAS, and IL-18 may serve as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for GM-CSF antibody therapy.

articles.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
articles.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in-silico functional annotations against this experimental ground truth revealed poor predictive performance (cross-validated ROC-AUC = 0.55-0.59), demonstrating that computational predictions cannot reliably substitute for measured allelic activity. We therefore treated the ovarian analysis as hypothesis-generating. Convergent annotation evidence prioritised 44 of 176 ovarian cancer GWAS leads (31 independent loci); a core of 21 SNPs (17 loci) was stable under alternative weights, leave-one-feature-out scoring and threshold changes, and candidates were enriched in ovarian and fallopian-tube regulatory chromatin (OR = 7.9, FDR = 5 × 10⁻5). Copy-number recurrence at candidate genes agreed between two tumour cohorts (Spearman ρ = 0.75, 95% CI 0.46-0.88) but no more than for chromosome-arm-matched control genes, so this observation is exploratory. Formal colocalisation with full summary statistics supported a shared causal variant for prostate cancer risk and TLCD3A expression at 17p13.3 (PP.H4 = 0.92), whereas the ovarian 17q21.31 signal could not be resolved to a single gene. Transcription-factor motifs disrupted in both cancers were over-represented for the interferon-regulatory factor (IRF) and STAT families (FDR = 3 × 10⁻6), a motif-level hypothesis. In an independent MPRA in primary ovarian epithelial cells, variants disrupting interferon-stimulated response elements (ISREs) were depleted, not enriched, for allele-specific activity (4.6% vs 9.2%; OR = 0.47, nominal p = 0.06, FDR = 0.10), so the IRF/STAT hypothesis was not supported; the same assay confirmed allele-specific activity at one prioritised ovarian candidate, rs2976384 (skew = - 0.67, FDR = 3 × 10⁻5). These results provide an audited prostate regulatory-SNP catalogue, quantify the limits of annotation-based fine-mapping, and offer testable cross-cancer hypotheses.

articles.title: Effect of a breathing mask on type 2 mediator responses to subzero exercise in individuals without asthma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Current evidence suggests that heat and moisture-exchanging breathing masks (HME) protect against exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB). We aimed to explore whether mast cell mediator release following exercise in subzero conditions is affected by the use of an HME. To this end, 23 healthy, recreational-competitive endurance athletes aged 18-53 years without asthma performed a 30-min warm-up followed by a 4-min maximal, self-paced running time trial, with and without HME, in -15 °C. Concentrations of leukotriene E4 (LTE₄) and 11β-prostaglandin F2α (11β-PGF2α) were measured in urine pre- and 60 min post-exercise and data analysed using repeated-measures ANOVA.

RESULTS: LTE₄ decreased after the 4-min maximal exercise test (p < 0.001), with no significant interaction with HME use. There was no effect of exercise alone nor HME on 11β-PGF2α responses to exercise. Taken together, we observed limited evidence of type 2 inflammation in healthy participants after brief, high-intensity exercise in the cold, with and without use of an HME. As the biomarker outcomes reported here were secondary and not powered in advance, these exploratory findings in a healthy cohort warrant further investigation using more robust airway challenges to better understand early airway responses and the potential for preventative strategies in athletes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN, Registered 01 April 2019, https//doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN10018222.

articles.title: Global cancer statistics among older adults in 2024 with projections to 2050: a multi-source population-based analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide and disproportionately affects older adults. As population ageing accelerates, the global cancer burden among older adults continues to increase. This study systematically evaluated the latest global cancer burden and its epidemiological characteristics among older adults.

METHODS: Data on the incidence and mortality of 33 malignancies, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, among adults aged 65 + were extracted from the Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024 and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 databases and stratified by age, sex, region, and Human Development Index (HDI). Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) were calculated. Annual percentage changes (APC) were used to characterize temporal trends. Decomposition analysis was performed to quantify the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological changes. Demographic projection methods and generalized additive model (GAM) were applied to forecast the cancer burden through 2050.

RESULTS: In 2024, there were 9,966,392 new cancer cases and 6,001,290 cancer deaths among older adults worldwide, accounting for 51.11% and 61.84%, respectively, of all-age totals. Lung, colorectal, stomach, liver, and prostate cancers were leading causes of death. Incidence and mortality were higher in men and increased with age. The Western Pacific Region had the largest burden, whereas Europe Region had the highest ASIR. ASIR correlated positively with HDI (rs = 0.771), while mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) correlated negatively (rs = -0.825). From 2000 to 2023, ASIR and ASMR declined, although burden increased, primarily driven by population growth; pancreatic cancer exhibited the most rapid increase. Tobacco use remained the leading risk factor for mortality, while metabolic risks rose in importance. Under a demographic scenario assuming constant 2024 age-specific rates and changes only in population size and age structure, new cancer cases and deaths among older adults are projected to reach approximately 19.8 million and 12.5 million by 2050, roughly double the 2024 figures, with the largest increase in the Eastern Mediterranean region.

CONCLUSION: Cancer burden in older adults is substantial, varying by sex, age, region, and development level. Precision prevention and control are urgently needed, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. REGISTRY AND THE REGISTRATION NO.

OF THE STUDY/TRIAL: N/A.

articles.title: Echocardiographic markers for left atrial stiffness and left atrial conduction delay in patients with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation compared to age-matched controls.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To study left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and left atrial activation time (LA-AT) changes in an older population with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) compared to age-matched control.

METHODS: Individuals with newly diagnosed PAF and a randomly selected age-matched control group without AF were enrolled from STROKESTOP2-study. All participants had NT-proBNP levels 125-900 ng/L. TTE examinations were analyzed retrospectively offline using dedicated software. Besides conventional echocardiographic measurements, LA-AT was obtained by measuring the time delay between the onset of the P-wave on ECG and tissue Doppler Á peak wave in lateral LA wall. LASI was calculated as the ratio of left ventricular filling (E/é) to peak atrial longitudinal strain (PALS).

RESULTS: Mean age was 76 ± 0.3 years. The PAF group (n = 67) presented significant increase of LASI (0.41 (0.29-0.60) vs. 0.32 (0.29-0.43), P = 0.001) and prolonged LA-AT (170 (140-180) ms vs. 140 (120-144) ms, P < 0.001) compared to controls (n = 94). Subgroup analysis in participants with normal LA volume index (LAVI) ≤ 34 ml/m2, LASI and LA-AT remained significantly increased/prolonged in PAF (N = 27) compared to controls (N = 72). NT-proBNP-levels did not differ between PAF (228 (181-348) ng/L) and controls (216 (156-317) ng/L) (P = 0.18). ROC curve analysis identified thresholds LASI > 0.54 and LA-AT > 139 msec for discrimination of silent PAF.

CONCLUSION: Indices reflecting LA stiffness and atrial conduction delay were significantly elevated in recently diagnosed PAF patients. LASI and LA-AT thresholds might non-invasively detect early atrial remodeling without structural enlargement in elderly patients with high risk of PAF and mildly increased NT-proBNP levels.

articles.title: Factors associated with the use of UK emergency services in children and young people with intellectual developmental disabilities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children and young people (CYP) with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDD) experience substantial health needs and higher healthcare utilisation compared with the general paediatric population. However, factors affecting the emergency healthcare use among children with IDD of genetic aetiology remain poorly understood. This study aimed to examine demographic, socioeconomic, behavioural, genetic, and clinical factors of emergency service use among CYP with IDD in England.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used linked administrative healthcare data from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) emergency service records obtained from National Health Service (NHS) England. Participants were CYP aged between 4 and 15.5 years with confirmed pathogenic genetic variants associated with IDD identified via NHS medical genetic clinics. The outcome was the yearly emergency service use rate, calculated as the total number of lifetime emergency visits divided by age (years). Independent variables included demographic and socioeconomic factors, genetic characteristics, region of residence, adaptive functioning, behavioural and emotional adjustment, prosocial behaviour, general health status, and system-specific medical conditions. Primary caregivers completed questionnaires and provided information regarding the child's medical history and demographic information.

RESULTS: The average emergency attendance rate in this cohort was 0.73 visits per annum, which was much higher than that among children in the same age range from the general population. Emergency services were used more by younger IDD children with poorer adaptive functioning, more externalising and less prosocial behaviour, as well as those with complex multisystem conditions. Frequent attendance was associated with high rates of medical comorbidities especially seizures and respiratory problems. Regional differences were found with relatively higher usage in London and the North East of England. Attendance rates were not influenced by sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic deprivation, genetic variant type or inheritance status.

CONCLUSIONS: This novel study demonstrated emergency healthcare utilisation among CYP with IDD of known genetic aetiology in England was primarily associated with clinical complexity, functional impairment, and younger age rather than socioeconomic or genetic factors. Their vulnerability to multisystem morbidity as well as regional disparities highlight the need for improved coordinated care and targeted service planning to reduce emergency healthcare dependence among children with disabilities.

articles.title: Orthostatic blood pressure fluctuations and risk of falls in community-dwelling older adults: the role of recovery time.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Available literature related to the association between orthostatic blood pressure (BP) variations and falls is controversial. We analyzed how orthostatic hypo- (OH) and hypertension (OHTN) relate to falls considering recovery time (RT) in community-dwelling older adults.

METHODS: This analysis uses data from the ActiFE cohort. BP was measured lying, immediately, 1, 2 and 3 min after standing. Systolic OH (sOH) and systolic OHTN (sOHTN) indicate a systolic BP (SBP) drop or increment ≥20 mm Hg, respectively. OH and OHTN further consider a diastolic BP (DBP) drop or increment ≥10 mm Hg. RT was categorized as Early Recovery ( < 1 min), Delayed Recovery (1-3 min), or No Recovery. Falls over 12 months were collected prospectively. Logistic regression examined associations with falls, adjusting for age, sex, diabetes, hemoglobin, instrumental activities of daily living, hand strength, fall risk-increasing drugs, past falls, Falls Efficacy Scale-International and anxiety.

RESULTS: Among 509 subjects (mean age 79 years, 44% female, 168 falls), prevalences were: 16.5% sOH, 26.9% OH, 9.0% sOHTN and 15.5% OHTN. Overall, OH was not associated with falls. However, falls risk increased with Delayed (OR 3.11 [95% CI 1.21-8.01]) and NoRecovery (OR 4.04 [95% CI 1.07-15.26]). sOH showed an adjusted OR of 2.00 [95% CI 1.15-3.47] for at least one fall. Regarding RT the risk of falls was increased in Delayed (OR 4.73 [95% CI 1.71-13.10]) and No Recovery (OR 5.06 [95% CI 1.42-22.27]). OHTN was not associated with falls.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, only sOH was associated with falls. When RT was considered, those with Delayed and No Recovery showed higher risk of falls regardless of the OH definition used.

articles.title: Ratio of Red Blood Cell Distribution Width to Albumin Level and Mortality Outcomes in Population with Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is affecting more and more population worldwide. The novel index red blood cell distribution width to albumin ratio (RAR) with information of both inflammation and nutrition has been considered as a reliable marker, suggesting underlying associations with prognosis in CKD population.

METHODS: Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018 and the National Death Index were employed for cohort analysis. A total of 3,965 patients with CKD were identified in this study. The associations of RAR with mortality outcomes including all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, and cancer mortality were investigated through multivariable Cox regression. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was applied to observe dose-response relationships and thresholds. Subgroup analysis was performed to find potential interactive factors.

RESULTS: A total of 1,163 fatal events occurred during the follow-up period. Multivariable Cox regression revealed RAR was independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR: 1.81, 95% CI: 1.60-2.06, p < 0.001), CVD mortality (HR: 1.89, 95% CI: 1.59-2.26, p < 0.001), and cancer mortality (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.46-2.11, p < 0.001). Non-linear relationships for all-cause mortality (p for non-linear < 0.001) and CVD mortality (p for non-linear <0.001) were observed via RCS analysis, while a linear relationship was observed for cancer mortality (p for non-linear = 0.113). Age, gender, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and poverty income ratio potentially interacted with RAR.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggested that increased RAR robustly associated with elevated risks for all-cause and cause-specific mortality in CKD population. Future clinical trials are demanded to validate the present findings and figure out the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Combining locoregional treatments and immunotherapies in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: The systemic treatment landscape of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma has been transformed by immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens. These advances have led to efforts to combine ICIs with locoregional therapies (LRTs), particularly transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization and external beam radiotherapy, in an attempt to improve tumour control and extend the benefits of ICIs to patients with intermediate-stage disease. The rationale for this combination approach is provided by the ability of LRTs to induce immunogenic cell death and tumour antigen release and to reprogramme the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Five phase III trials have thus far shown improvements in progression-free survival and objective response rates with regimens combining ICIs with transarterial chemoembolization. Early-phase and real-world data also support the combination of ICIs with transarterial radioembolization or external beam radiotherapy, particularly in selected patients with focal disease unsuitable for embolization or portal vein tumour thrombosis. However, various challenges remain, including patient selection and therapy sequencing, response assessment, and the growing difficulties in demonstrating survival advantages in the context of widespread post-progression crossover and effective subsequent therapies. In this Review, we describe the biological rationale, summarize the clinical evidence and discuss future directions for trial design, imaging and biomarker-driven patient selection in the integration of LRTs with immune-based regimens for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

articles.title: Persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction among infants with Fetal growth restriction at one year of age.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with altered cardiac development and subclinical myocardial dysfunction; however, longitudinal data during infancy are limited. This study evaluated serial changes in cardiac structure and function in infants with FGR during the first year of life.

METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included 128 FGR neonates and 64 appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) neonates, of whom 39 early-onset FGR (EOFGR), 47 late-onset FGR (LOFGR), and 64 AGA neonates completed the 1-year follow-up. FGR was diagnosed antenatally using estimated fetal weight <10th percentile with abnormal Doppler findings and confirmed postnatally using Intergrowth-21 standards. Cardiac evaluation included conventional echocardiography, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography.

RESULTS: At birth, FGR infants showed significantly lower anthropometric parameters and smaller cardiac dimensions compared with AGA controls. By 12 months, both FGR groups demonstrated catch-up growth with normalization of left ventricular dimensions and wall thickness. However, speckle-tracking analysis revealed persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Global longitudinal strain and strain rate indices remained significantly impaired across follow-up. Right ventricular dysfunction was evident at 12 months, particularly in the EOFGR group.

CONCLUSION: Despite structural normalization and catch-up growth, infants with FGR exhibit persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction during the first year of life.

IMPACT: Infants with fetal growth restriction exhibit reduced cardiac size and altered myocardial function at birth compared to AGA neonates. Both early- and late-onset FGR infants demonstrate significant catch-up growth and cardiac structural normalization by 12 months. Despite normalization of cardiac dimensions, speckle-tracking parameters (GLS and strain rates) remain impaired throughout infancy. Right ventricular dysfunction becomes evident by 12 months, particularly in early-onset FGR infants. Early myocardial impairment in FGR infants may represent a precursor to future cardiovascular risk, highlighting the need for longitudinal cardiac surveillance.

articles.title: AI-enhanced hemodynamic prediction of patent ductus arteriosus severity in premature infants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (HSPDA) requires timely assessment in premature very low birth weight (VLBW) infants. This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based surveillance system for predicting HSPDA and supporting real-time NICU decision-making.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed electronic medical record data from VLBW infants with PDA admitted to the Samsung Medical Center NICU between 2013 and 2022. After excluding records with congenital heart disease or missing critical echocardiographic parameters, machine-learning models were trained on 85% of the dataset and tested on the remaining 15%.

RESULTS: The best-performing model, Extra Trees, achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.829, with a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value of 0.767, 0.766, 0.694, and 0.825, respectively. For transitional records shifting between hemodynamic states, the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity were 0.700, 0.722, and 0.606, respectively, based on the proposed transition-optimized threshold.

CONCLUSION: The AI-based Extra Trees model demonstrated a robust ability to predict the hemodynamic status of PDA in VLBW infants. Thus, it may help NICU clinicians optimize conservative management and improve clinical decision-making.

IMPACT: Our AI model achieves 0.829 AUC for predicting hemodynamically significant PDA in premature infants using routine NICU data without requiring echocardiography This study uniquely predicts PDA hemodynamic severity through multimodal clinical data integration, advancing beyond previous binary presence/absence classifications We introduce a transition-optimized threshold that detects dynamic hemodynamic changes, enabling precise monitoring during conservative management The model provides accessible real-time PDA assessment for resource-limited NICUs lacking immediate echocardiographic expertise, optimizing intervention timing and fluid management strategies Our validation across 1033 VLBW infants over 10 years demonstrates robust performance with only 12-h data requirements.

articles.title: Transient gait instability during the initial phase of the 6-minute walk test in people with stroke: A nonlinear analysis using inertial measurement units.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In people with stroke (PwS), reduced gait speed and trunk acceleration changes in the latter half of the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) have been reported as fatigue-related, but temporal changes in motor control remain understudied. Clinicians often observe instability immediately after gait onset, yet quantitative evidence is scarce. This study used inertial measurement units (IMUs) and nonlinear analysis to examine fatigue-related changes and post-onset instability during the 6MWT in PwS.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 19 PwS and 19 age-matched controls completed the 6MWT wearing IMUs at the L5 vertebra and both ankles. Spatiotemporal parameters and stability indices (root mean square, harmonic ratio, sample entropy, short-term Lyapunov exponent [sLE]) were calculated. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) analyzed the 6-minute period both continuously and by comparing an initial phase (first 60 s) with the subsequent phase. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: Continuous-time LMMs showed reduced cadence and increased double-support ratio in PwS. Among stability indices, only mediolateral sLE (sLE-ML) showed a significant group × phase interaction: increasing in the initial phase in PwS but not in controls. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses confirmed this finding was robust and specific to the 60-second cutoff. Initial-phase sLE-ML correlated negatively with Fugl-Meyer lower-extremity scores.

CONCLUSIONS: PwS showed fatigue-related gait changes during the 6MWT, while mediolateral local dynamic stability transiently declined during the first 60 s before stabilizing. This instability was associated with motor paralysis, suggesting trunk IMU-based sLE-ML may reveal motor control deficits not captured by walking distance or speed.

articles.title: Inflammation and thrombosis: from pathophysiology to future treatments.
articles.abstract: Inflammation and coagulation are tightly interconnected host-defense systems that, when dysregulated, promote pathological thrombosis. This narrative review examines mechanisms, clinical settings, and therapeutic implications of thromboinflammation (TI) across venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, with particular attention to the differences in clinical translation among vascular territories. Endothelial activation, tissue factor expression, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil extracellular traps, complement activation, inflammasome signalling, and impaired fibrinolysis converge to generate a procoagulant phenotype. These mechanisms modify Virchow's triad and contribute to venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, although their relative importance varies across vascular territories. Clinically, TI is relevant in inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatologic and other immune-mediated disorders, sepsis, coronavirus disease 2019, clonal haematopoiesis, complement-mediated diseases, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. TI offers a unifying framework for mechanistic risk assessment and therapeutic development. In atherothrombosis, randomised trials have demonstrated that selective modulation of inflammatory pathways, particularly the NLRP3-interleukin-1β-interleukin-6 axis and colchicine-sensitive pathways, can reduce recurrent cardiovascular events. By contrast, the role of inflammation-targeted therapies for primary or secondary prevention of VTE remains uncertain. Future studies should identify disease-specific biomarkers and test targeted anti-inflammatory or immunothrombotic strategies, alone or alongside anticoagulation, to prevent thrombosis without compromising haemostasis effectively.

articles.title: Heat-related deaths: forensic diagnosis, death certification and reconciliation with excess-mortality estimates.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Extreme heat produces a substantial mortality burden that is captured through two incompletely connected systems: individual medicolegal investigation and population-level statistical attribution. This review defines the distinct causal constructs measured by these systems and proposes a practical framework for integrating forensic diagnosis, death certification, and excess-mortality surveillance.

METHODS: A structured narrative review of the published literature was conducted from database inception through 17 July 2026. Evidence was integrated across heat-illness pathophysiology, forensic scene investigation, autopsy and ancillary testing, differential diagnosis, death certification and coding, vulnerability, occupational fatalities, and temperature-mortality modelling. Particular emphasis was placed on reconciling individual medicolegal case ascertainment with epidemiological estimates of excess mortality. Reporting was guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA).

RESULTS: Fatal environmental hyperthermia is usually an exclusionary diagnosis because gross and microscopic findings are nonspecific and may be modified by cooling, survival interval, postmortem interval and decomposition. No biochemical, immunohistochemical, proteomic, or lipidomic marker independently confirms the diagnosis. Heat may be the principal cause of death, a material contributor acting through natural disease, or a population-attributable exposure that cannot be assigned confidently to an individual decedent. Certification practices vary across jurisdictions, and matched event comparisons show that modelled excess mortality can exceed individually attributed deaths without making the two measures interchangeable.

CONCLUSION: Forensic and epidemiological counts should be reported as complementary measures. Standardized scene data, case-appropriate toxicology, explicit certification of contributory heat exposure, linkage of medicolegal and vital-statistics records, and joint interpretation with excess-mortality models would improve surveillance and prevention.

articles.title: Insurance Type and Receipt of Condition-Concordant Behavioral Health Treatment Among U.S. Adults Reporting Past-Year Probation or Parole.
articles.journal: The journal of behavioral health services & research
articles.abstract: Insurance coverage may shape whether adults with behavioral health conditions receive corresponding services. This study examined insurance-related differences in condition-concordant treatment among adults reporting past-year probation or parole. Public-use data from the 2022-2023 National Survey on Drug Use and Health identified 967 adults with any mental illness, a substance use disorder, or both. Insurance categories were private coverage; Medicare, military, or other coverage without private coverage; Medicaid/Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) only; and uninsured. Survey-weighted logistic models adjusted for condition group, mental illness and substance use disorder severity, supervision type, demographic and socioeconomic characteristics, health status, county type, and survey year. Compared with uninsured adults, those with Medicaid/CHIP only had higher odds of any condition-concordant treatment (adjusted odds ratio = 3.14, 95% confidence interval = 1.60-6.15); adjusted probabilities were 64.9% and 44.8%, respectively. Alternative insurance classifications yielded similar associations. Estimates varied substantially by survey year and were attenuated and imprecise after adjustment for coverage gaps. Associations with full condition-concordant treatment were also imprecise. Medicaid/CHIP-only coverage was associated with greater receipt of treatment in at least one identified behavioral health domain. These findings support evaluating insurance enrollment and continuity as components of service linkage for adults with recent community-supervision experience, while the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Workforce Retention in Florida's Behavioral Health Sector: A Mixed-Methods Survey Investigation of Positive and Negative Contributors Impacting Intention to Leave.
articles.journal: The journal of behavioral health services & research
articles.abstract: Florida faces a critical behavioral health workforce shortage, with provider supply falling approximately 14,000 positions short of demand. Understanding the factors that predict workforce attrition is essential for developing targeted retention strategies. This study used a mixed-methods survey design to examine workforce retention among licensed behavioral health professionals in Florida. Surveys were administered to providers across seven professions and all regions of Florida (N = 330). Quantitative analyses included descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), and ordinal regression predicting three indices of retention intention. Qualitative analyses included content analysis with investigator triangulation. Themes were derived inductively from the data itself, following the principles of emergent coding in qualitative content analysis. EFA yielded a robust two-factor structure comprising a Workload Strain and Overload and largely independent Positive Organizational Climate and Professional Satisfaction factors (r =  -.17). Both factors independently predicted retention intentions in ordinal regression models. Qualitative analysis identified seven themes promoting retention, including meaningful purpose, client progress, professional autonomy, and collegial support, alongside ten themes reflecting retention risk, most prominently inadequate compensation, administrative burden, emotional exhaustion, and organizational dysfunction. Triangulation revealed strong convergence between quantitative strain indicators and qualitative themes, while qualitative data provided additional context regarding professional devaluation, safety concerns, and the tension between mission alignment and structural barriers. Retention requires a two-factor strategy: reducing sources of strain while investing in organizational conditions that sustain meaning. Implications for policy, employer practice, and workforce development are discussed.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Frailty Index (MBS-FI).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Frailty is associated with adverse outcomes after metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). Existing bariatric frailty scores include MBSAQIP-derived tools, but reported discrimination is modest and prior accumulating-deficit indices used earlier or restricted cohorts. We developed and internally validated a contemporary adult MBSAQIP deficit index and compared it with the modified Frailty Index-5 (mFI-5) and Bariatric Frailty Score (BFS).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis using the MBSAQIP 2023-2024 cohort, including adults undergoing sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass as a primary or conversion MBS. Preoperative health-deficit variables were coded and summed to create the MBS-FI. Candidate deficits were excluded if missing > 10%, too rare (< 1%), too common (> 80%), or unrelated to age. The data were randomly split into FI-derivation and validation cohorts (70%/30%, respectively). Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, serious complications, cardiovascular complications, reoperation, and length of stay > 2 days.

RESULTS: The study identified 359,767 patients, of whom 252,043 were in the derivation cohort. Of 28 candidate variables, 18 remained in the final model. The MBS-FI displayed a right-skewed distribution and a positive correlation with age. Higher MBS-FI scores were progressively associated with adverse outcomes. Although the MBS-FI demonstrated numerically higher discrimination for 30-day and in-hospital mortality, these differences were not statistically significant in the overall cohort (p = 0.33 and p = 0.49, respectively. In the validation cohort, the adjusted model yielded an AUC of 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.79) for 30-day mortality based on 75 events and 0.80 (95% CI, 0.69-0.91) for in-hospital mortality based on 14 events.

CONCLUSION: The MBS-FI was internally validated and provided incremental discrimination for several non-mortality outcomes. Improvements for mortality were limited, and external validation and assessment of clinical utility are required before routine use.

articles.title: Porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder after trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) therapy in HER2-positive breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), an antibody-drug conjugate targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), is used for HER2-positive breast cancer. Although hepatotoxicity and thrombocytopenia are recognized adverse events of T-DM1, long-term hepatic vascular complications associated with this treatment remain poorly characterized. We report a case of porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD) with noncirrhotic portal hypertension (NCPH) associated with prolonged T-DM1 therapy.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical course, serial laboratory data, imaging findings, endoscopic findings, and liver histopathology of a woman in her 70s with recurrent HER2-positive breast cancer who received prolonged T-DM1 therapy.

RESULTS: After prior maintenance therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, the patient received 60 cycles of T-DM1. During treatment, progressive thrombocytopenia developed. Serial computed tomography demonstrated splenomegaly, portal vein dilatation, and the development of portosystemic collateral vessels. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed newly developed esophageal varices. Laboratory evaluation excluded viral, autoimmune, and metabolic liver diseases. Liver biopsy showed focal sinusoidal dilatation and obliterative portal venopathy without cirrhotic architectural distortion, consistent with PSVD. Retrospective imaging review showed that splenomegaly had developed approximately 12 months after the initiation of T-DM1 therapy. Splenomegaly and platelet counts remained unchanged 2 years after T-DM1 discontinuation, whereas spleen stiffness increased.

CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that prolonged exposure to T-DM1 may cause sinusoidal endothelial injury and lead to PSVD with portal hypertension. Progressive thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly during T-DM1 therapy may represent early clinical indicators of this complication. Careful long-term monitoring for signs of portal hypertension should be considered in patients receiving prolonged T-DM1 treatment.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Attitudes Toward Early Detection of Cervical Cancer, Religious Health Fatalism, and Hope levels in Women: A Cross-Sectional Study in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: A study was conducted on women's attitudes towards cervical cancer early detection with regard to dispositional hope and religious health fatalism. The study used a cross-sectional design. A total of 1635 female volunteers aged 18 years and older residing in Türkiye were included in the study, yielding a response rate of 95.6%. The data was gathered from December 2024 to January 2025. The personal information form, dispositional hope scale, religious health fatalism scale, and attitude scale for early detection of cervical cancer were used to gather data online. The analysis was done using IBM SPSS Statistics. It involved analysis of descriptive statistics, correlation tests, and multiple linear regression. The participants' mean age was 28.37 ± 8.94 years; 50.3% were unaware of the Pap smear test, and 77.3% had never been screened. Correlation analysis indicated a weak positive relationship between hope and religious fatalism, whereas attitudes toward early detection were negatively related to both hope and fatalism. Furthermore, participant characteristics (such as education, income, and Pap smear awareness) showed significant differences in study variables. In multiple regression controlling for these background characteristics, both dispositional hope (β = - 0.272, p < .001) and religious health fatalism (β = - 0.053, p = .024) significantly predicted attitudes toward early detection, explaining 11.2% of the variance in attitude scores. These findings suggest that early-detection behaviors may be improved by strengthening education and awareness interventions, while also addressing psychosocial dimensions such as hope and health fatalism in counseling and prevention strategies.

articles.title: Post-transplant diabetes mellitus after kidney transplantation: longitudinal treatment trajectories and exploratory clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract: Post-transplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM) is a common complication after kidney transplantation, but its longitudinal course after diagnosis may be heterogeneous. We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of kidney transplant recipients diagnosed with PTDM between January 2010 and December 2020 to describe longitudinal glucose-lowering treatment trajectories and exploratory clinical outcomes. Patients with known diabetes before transplantation were excluded. PTDM was defined according to the international consensus framework as abnormalities in glucose metabolism persisting beyond 45 days after discharge. Eighty-three recipients were followed for a median of 76 months (IQR 60-107). At last follow-up, 72 patients (86.7%) remained on glucose-lowering therapy, whereas 11 (13.3%) had discontinued treatment without documented recurrence of hyperglycaemia. In exploratory comparisons, the persistent-treatment group showed a steeper annual decline in allograft function (- 2.30 vs -0.30 mL/min/1.73 m2/year; p = 0.004) and more frequent new-onset proteinuria (57.4% vs 18.2%; p = 0.022). All deaths and graft-loss events occurred in the persistent-treatment group; however, these event-based comparisons are limited by the small discontinuation subgroup and by the post hoc, time-dependent nature of treatment classification. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Treatment discontinuation cannot establish that the initial abnormality represented transient hyperglycaemia, and treatment persistence cannot be interpreted as an independent determinant of graft outcomes.

articles.title: Adapting Flow Cytometry for Studying Immune Cell Seasonality in Wild Migratory Bats.
articles.abstract: Identifying the drivers of wildlife immunity is critical for assessing stressor impacts and zoonotic risks. However, such studies are limited by logistical challenges of wildlife research and lack of species-specific reagents. We adapt flow cytometry, typically confined to laboratory settings, to field settings to profile cellular immunity with small blood volumes and extended sample holding times. We then apply these methods to a preliminary assessment of immune cell seasonality in migratory Mexican free-tailed bats (Tadarida brasiliensis). We confirmed four antibodies recognizing CD3, CD79a, MHCII, and CD11b originally validated in Egyptian fruit bats (Rousettus aegyptiacus), enabling quantification of T and B cells, macrophages, and neutrophils, respectively. Flow cytometry outperformed hematology in quantifying leukocyte profiles and revealed variable immune cell seasonality. Adaptive cells increased between spring and fall migration. Neutrophils were most abundant during the reproductive period and decreased during migrations, whereas B cells were most abundant after reproduction and before fall migration; granulocytes as a whole, macrophages, and T cells had no seasonality. Females had more B cells than males but did not differ in other cells. Our findings lay the groundwork for applying flow cytometry to field studies of wildlife and provide initial insights into the seasonality of bat immunity.

articles.title: Effects of SGLT2 inhibition on cardiac remodeling and heart failure development in aortic stenosis rats.
articles.abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is increasingly prevalent in ageing populations, yet no pharmacological therapy has been shown to modify its progression to heart failure (HF). Sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve outcomes in HF, but their effects in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling remain unclear. Here, we show that rats with long-term AS develop HF features, left ventricular dilation, and systolic and diastolic dysfunction, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, impaired antioxidant defenses, myocardial fibrosis, and transcriptional remodeling. Empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day for 8 weeks) attenuated cardiac dysfunction and reduced HF features. At molecular level, empagliflozin prevented increase in lipid peroxidation, and decreased interstitial collagen deposition, while increasing glutathione peroxidase and matrix metalloproteinase-2 activity. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,078 differentially expressed genes and revealed enrichment of pathways associated with extracellular matrix organization and signal transduction in AS. Empagliflozin predominantly regulated genes involved in cardiac contraction, mitochondrial membrane organization, apoptosis, and cell survival. Profibrotic and remodeling-associated genes were upregulated in AS, while empagliflozin induced a distinct transcriptional program associated with improved myocardial homeostasis. AS was associated with reduced activity of energy metabolism enzymes, which was not restored by empagliflozin. Collectively, these findings identify oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodeling, and transcriptional reprogramming as mechanisms underlying cardiac dysfunction in AS. Empagliflozin mitigates cardiac remodeling and HF progression and modulates fibrosis and gene networks regulating cardiac function. These data highlight SGLT2 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in pressure overload-induced heart failure.

articles.title: Clinical features and associated factors for porto-sinusoidal vascular disease in primary Sjögren's disease: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize primary Sjögren's disease (pSjD) patients with porto-sinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD) and identify associated clinical factors.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 7 biopsy-proven pSjD-PSVD patients and 28 age and sex-matched pSjD controls. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and portal hypertension-related data were collected and compared between the two groups. Univariate logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with PSVD.

RESULTS: The pSjD-PSVD group had significantly longer disease duration than controls [59 (36, 180) vs. 15 (12, 69) months, p = 0.031]. All PSVD patients presented with splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia [(88 ± 44.01) vs. (176.21 ± 66.37) × 10⁹/L, p = 0.003], leukopenia [(3.05 ± 1.26) vs. (4.51 ± 1.52) × 10⁹/L, p = 0.024], hypoalbuminemia [(35.37 ± 4.06) vs. (38.86 ± 3.00) g/L, p = 0.015], elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [(32.13 ± 11.64) vs. (22.9 ± 7.75) IU/L, p = 0.016], and elevated serum IgG [1970 (1540, 2460) vs. 1435 (1160, 1977.5) mg/dL; p = 0.027]. Univariate logistic regression identified thrombocytopenia (OR = 3.481, p = 0.003), INR > 1.2 (OR = 3.507, p = 0.003), hypoalbuminemia (OR = 8.000, p = 0.007), elevated AST (OR = 1.106, p = 0.04), elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) (OR = 1.033, p = 0.023), hypokalemia (OR = 2.408, p = 0.003), and elevated IgG (OR = 2.079, p = 0.039) as factors associated with PSVD. Elevated IgG did not retain significance in Firth's penalized likelihood regression (OR 3.35, p = 0.142).

CONCLUSION: This exploratory study characterizes the clinical features of pSjD patients with PSVD. A constellation of associated features-long disease duration, splenomegaly with hypersplenism, hepatic synthetic impairment (hypoalbuminemia, INR prolongation, elevated AST/ALP), hypokalemia, and hypergammaglobulinemia-may aid in early identification of portal hypertension. These preliminary findings require validation in large prospective cohorts. Key Points • pSjD may represent an autoimmune condition associated with PSVD, featuring long disease duration, splenomegaly, and cytopenias. • pSjD-PSVD shows mild synthetic dysfunction and AST-predominant enzyme elevation without cirrhosis. • Elevated IgG, hypokalemia, and UIP may help identify pSjD patients who warrant closer surveillance for portal hypertension.

articles.title: Modeling heavy metal fate, transport, and bioaccumulation in coupled water-soil-plant systems of Lake Sonfon, Sierra Leone.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: Heavy metal contamination of freshwater ecosystems in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASGM) regions poses growing threats to ecological integrity and human health across sub-Saharan Africa, yet quantitative, process-based assessments of coupled water-soil-plant metal dynamics remain scarce for Sierra Leone. This study applied the Water Quality Simulation Program (WASP) Advanced Toxicant module, supplemented by first-order soil-equilibrium and plant bioaccumulation sub-models, to simulate the fate, transport, and bioaccumulation of cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), arsenic (As), and mercury (Hg) in the coupled water-soil-aquatic plant system of Lake Sonfon over a 6-month wet-season monitoring window (July-December 2025). A total of 360 analytical records were collected from six water-quality stations, six soil stations, and three aquatic-plant stations. Mean water-column concentrations were 0.148 mg/L for As, 0.078 mg/L for Cd, 0.057 mg/L for Hg, and 0.031 mg/L for Pb; all exceeding international freshwater quality guidelines. Sediment concentrations were substantially higher (Pb 10.25 mg/kg; Cd 1.79 mg/kg; As 1.51 mg/kg; Hg 0.133 mg/kg), with soil-to-water enrichment ratios of 330, 23, 10, and 2.3 for Pb, Cd, As, and Hg, respectively. Aquatic plant tissues accumulated metals at plant-to-water bioaccumulation factors (BAF) of 922 (Pb), 325 (Hg), 50 (As), and 47 (Cd), with a single hotspot station (PLTS 01) recording Pb as high as 67.92 mg/kg. Water-column and sediment concentrations increased progressively from July to December (+ 14-23% and + 2-10%, respectively), while plant tissue concentrations declined by 5-27%, revealing a seasonal inverse relationship attributed to growth-dilution dynamics. Model parameters were calibrated against July-September observations (n = 3 monthly means) and independently validated against an equally small, independent October-December dataset (n = 3 monthly means), so that the resulting correlation statistics should be read as indicative rather than definitive; on this basis, sediment validation skill was strong for Cd (r = 0.984, RMSE = 0.014 mg/kg), As (r = 0.975), and Hg (r = 0.992) and moderate for Pb (r = 0.482, RMSE = 0.135 mg/kg), while all plant tissue compartments showed poor validation skill (r = - 0.985 to 0.553), highlighting the need for growth-stage-dependent plant sub-models. Spatially, SOMP 03 and PLTS 01 on the northern shoreline emerged as coincident sediment and bioaccumulation hotspots consistent with adjacent mine-waste deposits. These findings provide the first fully parameterized WASP model for Lake Sonfon, establish a baseline contamination profile, and generate management-relevant evidence for source control, phytoremediation, and adaptive monitoring in this ASGM-affected watershed.

articles.title: Acute pericarditis caused by Kocuria kristinae with successful withdrawal from hemodialysis: a case report.
articles.abstract: Kocuria kristinae is a commensal skin bacterium that occasionally acts as an opportunistic pathogen. However, it is rarely associated with pericardial infection. This report describes the case of a 47-year-old male patient with dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI) complicated by massive inflammatory pericardial effusion, in whom K. kristinae was isolated. The patient developed a severe heatstroke, which was followed by AKI, subsequently requiring hemodialysis. Approximately 1 month later, the cardiothoracic ratio increased markedly, and echocardiography revealed substantial pericardial effusion. Anti-inflammatory therapy, comprising non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, colchicine, and prednisolone, elicited a poor response, given no improvement in the effusion. Ultrasound guidance was used for pericardiocentesis, resulting in drainage of 1050 mL of pale-yellow, exudative fluid with neutrophil predominance. K. kristinae was subsequently identified using the VITEK 2 system. The vancomycin dosage was determined based on the susceptibility results. Following the implementation of drainage and antimicrobial therapy, pericardial effusion decreased, venous congestion was alleviated, and urine output increased. These interventions may have contributed to renal recovery and the discontinuation of hemodialysis on day 102. Clinicians should regard K. kristinae isolated from pericardial fluid as a possible contaminant notwithstanding a clinically compatible setting. This case suggests that a massive pericardial effusion with venous congestion can delay renal recovery in severe AKI, whereas successful pericardial drainage facilitates recovery of urine output and withdrawal from hemodialysis.
