articles.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction as a Convergent Mechanism of α-Synuclein Toxicity: A Systematic Review of In Vitro Fibrillar Models.
articles.abstract: Synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease, Dementia with Lewy bodies, and Multiple System Atrophy, are characterised by intracellular accumulation of misfolded α-synuclein (αSyn). Although αSyn aggregation is central to disease pathogenesis, the mechanisms linking αSyn to progressive neurodegeneration remain incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction is recognised as a key pathological process, particularly in experimental models using exogenously applied αSyn species, including preformed fibrils (PFFs). This systematic review synthesises evidence from mammalian in vitro studies that examined the effects of disease-associated αSyn conformations, including monomers, oligomers and PFFs, on mitochondrial structure and function. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PsycInfo were searched to identify eligible peer-reviewed studies published up to March 2026, yielding 33 included studies. Models encompassed neuronal, astrocytic, microglial, endothelial, fibroblast, and induced pluripotent stem cell-derived systems, enabling comparison across cell types, αSyn conformations, and genetic backgrounds. Across included studies, oligomeric and fibrillar αSyn consistently induced mitochondrial depolarisation, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, reduced ATP production, complex-I dysfunction and increased reactive oxygen species generation. Additional mitochondrial pathological changes included fragmentation, cristae disruption, impaired TOM20-mediated protein import, calcium dysregulation, defective mitophagy and increased heteroplasmy i.e. accumulation of damaged mitochondria. These alterations frequently preceded cell death and were amplified in dopaminergic and genetically vulnerable models, including αSyn A53T, SNCA triplication, and PARK2-associated transgenic systems. Our review highlights mitochondrial dysfunction as a mechanism underlying αSyn toxicity, whilst suggesting methodological heterogeneity can limit cross-study translation. Priorities for future research using 'in vitro' models of PFF synucleinopathies include standardised fibril preparation protocols, improved mitochondrial phenotyping, and use of human multicellular and organoid models.

articles.title: High lesion detection rates with preoperative ⁹⁹ᵐTc-PSMA-SPECT/CT prior to radioguided surgery in biochemical recurrence: a hypothesis-generating analysis of quantitative PSMA-PET/CT parameters.
Quantifying per-event dose-equivalent rates of echocardiographers and interventional cardiologists during structural heart interventions.
articles.abstract: Echocardiographers (ECs) often stand close to the patient during structural heart interventions (SHIs) and may receive higher occupational radiation exposure than interventional cardiologists (ICs). Previous studies have relied on cumulative dose measurements, leaving the per-event determinants of occupational radiation dose poorly characterized. We quantified the per-event personal dose equivalent rate at a 10-mm depth [Hp(10)] for ECs and ICs during SHIs and identified its determinants. We prospectively analyzed 37 SHI cases (20 mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair procedures and 17 left atrial appendage occlusion procedures) at a single center between March 2024 and March 2025. The EC and IC each wore two semiconductor dosimeters (on the front and side of the neck) sampling at 1 Hz, and the higher reading was used for analysis. Per-event Hp(10) rates were calculated by integrating dosimetry data, radiation dose structured report information, and video-based shielding labels. A prespecified linear mixed-effects model with a case-level random intercept assessed X-ray output, beam geometry, operator shielding, and C-arm angulation as candidate determinants for each operator. Among 3,222 exposure events, the EC-to-IC ratio of the Hp(10) rate was 2.3 during fluoroscopy and 3.8 during cine acquisition (both p < 0.001). In the multivariable model, log10(Ka,r rate), protocol, C-arm angle, source-to-detector distance, field of view, and operator shielding were independent predictors of the Hp(10) rate for both operators. The EC experienced substantially higher per-event Hp(10) rates than the IC, particularly during cine acquisition. Operator-specific shielding strategies and per-event optimization of X-ray output are warranted.

articles.title: Correction: Interventional Treatment of Arterial Hypertension in The Modern Era: An Updated Review.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension

articles.title: Burden, management and outcomes of emergency haematuria admissions: a 9-month retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Visible haematuria accounts for approximately 15% of urological emergency admissions, yet standardised inpatient management protocols are absent. This study aimed to define the burden, aetiology, management requirements, and predictors of adverse clinical outcomes in emergency haematuria admissions at a tertiary Irish urology centre.

METHODS: A single-centre retrospective observational cohort study was conducted across all emergency haematuria admissions from July 2025 to March 2026. Data were extracted from prospective clinical handover records and cross-referenced with electronic patient records. Primary outcomes were length of stay (LOS), theatre intervention, transfusion requirement, and unplanned readmission.

RESULTS: Sixty-three admissions were identified across 50 unique patients. Median age was 81 years (IQR 73-85); 87% were male. Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and radiation cystitis each accounted for 27% of admissions, followed by post-operative haematuria (21%) and malignancy (19%). Sixty-eight percent of patients were on anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy. Theatre intervention was required in 43% of admissions; radiation cystitis carried the highest transfusion rate (35%). Theatre intervention and transfusion requirement were independently associated with significantly longer LOS (median 6 vs 4 days, p = 0.002; 12 vs 4 days, p < 0.001 respectively). The readmission rate was 26%, with malignancy the only significant independent predictor (OR 4.71, p = 0.046). Anticoagulant type was not a significant predictor of any adverse outcome.

CONCLUSION: Emergency haematuria admissions represent a high-acuity workload predominantly affecting elderly, antithrombotic-treated patients. Malignancy predicts readmission and radiation cystitis drives transfusion burden. These findings support risk-stratified admission pathways incorporating early malignancy triage and haemoglobin-guided decision-making.

articles.title: Effects of extracellular vesicles after tibial transverse bone transport on angiogenesis and cardiac function in rats with acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of extracellular vesicles derived from Tibial transverse bone transport (TTT) in diabetic rats on cardiac function, and angiogenesis in rats with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Diabetic rat models of TTT and sham operation were first established. Then, a rat AMI model was established. The Sham-EVs and the TTT-EVs were injected via myocardial injection. After the intervention, echocardiography was used to evaluate cardiac function. Masson staining was performed to detect the collagen volume fraction of the myocardial tissue. CD31 immunohistochemical staining was used to observe the microvessel density (MVD) in the infarcted area. The expression levels of angiogenesis-related factors in the myocardial tissue were detected. The TTT -EVs group exhibited significantly improved cardiac function. The results of Masson staining indicated that the collagen volume fraction in the TTT -EVs group were significantly reduced. The results of CD31 immunohistochemical staining showed that the MVD in the infarcted area of the TTT -EVs group were significantly increased. Additionally, the expression levels of angiogenesis-related factors in the TTT -EVs group were significantly higher than those in the Sham -EVs group (all P < 0.05). TTT -EVs derived from diabetic rats can improve cardiac function, and promote angiogenesis in AMI rats.

articles.title: A randomised controlled crossover trial comparing two mandibular repositioning appliances for treatment of moderate obstructive sleep apnoea.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare two custom-made bi-block mandibular repositioning appliances, the SomnoDent® Flex and the OrthoApnea NOA®, in adults with moderate obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA).

METHODS: Randomised two-period, two-sequence crossover trial at a single centre (Genk, Belgium). Adults with polysomnography-confirmed AHI 5-30 events/h were eligible; all enrolled had moderate OSA (AHI 15.1-29.7). Participants were randomised 1:1 to SomnoDent® Flex-NOA® or the reverse sequence, each worn for three months with a two-week washout. Participants and clinicians were unblinded; outcome scorers were blinded to appliance. The registered primary outcome was the change in AHI from baseline for each appliance. The between-appliance difference in post-treatment AHI was assessed in a non-prespecified principal comparative analysis using linear mixed-effects models with appliance, period and sequence as fixed effects.

RESULTS: Sixteen participants were randomised, eight per sequence, and all were analysed. Median AHI fell from 17.6 events/h at baseline to 3.1 with the SomnoDent® Flex and 2.3 with the NOA® (both p < 0.001 versus baseline). The between-appliance difference was + 0.16 events/h (95% CI - 2.56 to + 2.87; p = 0.904), with a period effect (+ 3.82 events/h in period 2, coinciding with the change from home polygraphy to in-laboratory polysomnography; p = 0.009). No secondary outcome differed significantly; post hoc, AHI < 5 events/h was reached in 12/16 (SomnoDent® Flex) and 10/16 (NOA®). No participant discontinued for an adverse event; adverse events were not systematically recorded.

CONCLUSION: Both appliances were associated with reductions in AHI. The non-prespecified between-appliance comparison detected no statistically significant difference and does not establish equivalence. Complete confounding between period and measurement methodology, together with insufficient adherence, titration and adverse-event data, limits conclusions about the overall comparative merits of the appliances.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06810479, registered 5 February 2025, prior to first enrolment.

articles.title: Breastfeeding and maternal bone health 10 years postpartum: findings from the ROLO longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Brief rationale: To investigate associations between breastfeeding behaviours and maternal bone health at 10-year follow-up.

MAIN RESULT: Breastfeeding durations were not associated with DXA measurements. Significance of the paper: These findings add to the evidence that breastfeeding is not associated with adverse long-term maternal bone health.

PURPOSE: To investigate associations between breastfeeding behaviours and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements of maternal bone health at 10-year follow-up. Associations with bone turnover markers (BTMs) were examined as exploratory secondary outcomes.

METHODS: This was an analysis of 196 women from the ROLO (Randomised cOntrol trial of a LOw glycaemic index diet in pregnancy to prevent macrosomia) longitudinal cohort study at 10-year follow-up. Data on demographics, lifestyle and breastfeeding were collected by questionnaire. DXA measurements were available for 171 participants and BTM measurements for 60. Exclusive breastfeeding duration, any breastfeeding duration and three mutually exclusive cumulative breastfeeding groups (never breastfed, breastfed for <12 months, and breastfed for ≥12 months) were each examined in relation to bone health outcomes.

RESULTS: The mean (SD) age of participants was 42.8 (3.87) years and 97.9% were premenopausal. Ever breastfeeding rates were 70.9% (n = 139/196) and 40.3% (n = 79/196) had a cumulative breastfeeding duration of ≥12 months. Breastfeeding durations were not associated with DXA measurements at 10-year follow-up. An unadjusted difference in β-CTX-I was observed between the ≥12-month and never-breastfed groups (p = 0.038) however, given the small group size an adjusted analysis was underpowered.

CONCLUSION: These findings reassure women that breastfeeding does not have a lasting negative impact on skeletal health. The exploratory BTM finding should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Septic shock due to streptococcal infection (SRSS) carries a high mortality and is in part driven by toxin-mediated inflammation. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) may modulate the septic host responses by removing injurious mediators while replenishing protective plasma factors, but data specific to SRSS is lacking. We performed a retrospective, multicenter, cohort study of adults with SRSS between 2012-2024.

METHODS: Patients from three tertiary care ECMO centers in Germany and Switzerland were included requiring (i) streptococcal spp. detected in blood or primary focus and (ii) septic shock according to sepsis-3 definition. Adjunctive TPE with fresh frozen plasma at the intensivists` discretion was compared with standard of care (SOC). The primary outcome was 90-day-hospital mortality. Key exploratory outcomes included 24-h kinetics of vasoactive-inotropic score(VIS) and lactate, as well as SRSS-related complications. Results were validated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort.

RESULTS: Of 149 patients, 31 (20.8%) received TPE and 118 (79.2%) SOC. TPE patients were more severely ill at baseline: SOFA 14 (IQR 13.5-15) vs 11 (IQR 8-14) (p<0.001); lactate 6.4 vs 2.8 mmol/L (p<0.001); Vasoactive-Inotropic-Score (VIS) 70.7 vs 23.3 (p<0.001); more frequent invasive ventilation (87% vs 65%), VV-ECMO (36% vs 19%), and renal replacement therapy (96.8% vs 52.5%). Overall, 90-day hospital mortality was 27.5% (TPE 29.0%, SOC 27.1%). Following SOFA-score adjustment, TPE was associated with lower mortality risk (aHR 0.67 [95% CI 0.5-0.9]; p=0.009). This was validated in the PSM cohort, with an aHR for TPE of 0.44 (95% CI 0.3-0.8); p=0.002. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant VIS reduction only with TPE (fixed effect 24-h change, p=0.027) and improved lactate decrease versus SOC.

CONCLUSION: In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

articles.title: Same R 0  , Different Risk: Colonization-Age Timing and Heterogeneity Drive ICU MRSA Establishment and Burden.
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) control of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) occurs over short horizons, whereas R 0  summarizes average transmission at the importation-free disease-free state without encoding timing. We couple within-host bacterial and immune dynamics to an ICU model structured by colonization age, generating transmission and progression kernels that vary with colonization age. A two-stage framework uses a branching process to quantify finite-threshold crossing and a deterministic ward model to quantify conditional burden after the threshold is reached. Calibration fixes η = 0.10  and distributes colonized admissions across pre-admission colonization ages. Of 1, 000, 000 parameter sets, 45, 250 satisfy cumulative  R 2 ≥ 0.90  . The representative calculation is subcritical, with  R 0 = 0.907957  ; across accepted sets, the median and 95% behavioral range are 0.917464 and [ 0.814593 ,  1.032975 ]  , with 92.460 %  below one. At  Z crit = 5  , exact threshold-reaching probabilities are 0.114659 for age-dependent transmission and 0.117074 for matched constant transmission. Their accepted-set difference range crosses zero, so this contrast has no robust direction. By contrast, age-dependent transmission reaches 50% of reproductive potential earlier in 98.378 %  of accepted sets. In 200-day conditional simulations, delaying τ crit  from 5 to 15 days increases the age-dependent peak total MRSA burden from 5.629 to 7.298 patients and cumulative total burden from 683.8 to 1398.0 patient-days. At the 9-day baseline and equal R 0  , age dependence gives a 7.372 %  higher peak but a 9.304 %  lower cumulative burden than constant transmission. Increasing κ max  from 0.6 to 1.4 times baseline reduces R 0  by 4.133 %  . Thus, matching R 0  does not preserve timing-sensitive outcomes, but their magnitude and direction depend on the endpoint; over the examined ranges, clearance timing has greater leverage than immune-strength intensification.

articles.title: Renal vein thrombosis with inferior vena cava extension and pulmonary embolism in a patient with acute pyelonephritis: a case report and updated literature review.
articles.abstract: Renal vein thrombosis (RVT) is a rare and underrecognized complication of acute pyelonephritis, with nephrotic syndrome and malignancy remaining the predominant causes of RVT. Because its clinical features overlap with those of the underlying infection, the diagnosis is often delayed until thrombus propagation or embolization occurs. A previously healthy 29-year-old man presented with a two-week history of left flank pain and fever. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated acute left pyelonephritis with extensive renal vein thrombosis extending into the suprarenal inferior vena cava. Despite initiation of anticoagulation, pulmonary embolism developed during hospitalization. Cultures did not identify a causative organism; a low-count Staphylococcus haemolyticus isolate was considered a contaminant. Thrombophilia screening was negative. The patient improved with antimicrobial therapy and anticoagulation alone, requiring no invasive intervention. A PubMed search identified 23 previously published cases of acute pyelonephritis-associated RVT, pooled with the present case (n = 24) and analyzed separately from five xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis-associated cases. Three cases were excluded for systemic or multifactorial thrombosis, and one case of RVT radiologically mimicking pyelonephritis. Gram-negative organisms predominated (78.3%), diabetes mellitus was present in fewer than half of patients, and outcomes were favorable with antimicrobial therapy and anticoagulation alone in most cases, while invasive interventions were reported selectively in cases with extensive thrombus burden or uncontrolled infection. RVT should be considered in patients with suspected pyelonephritis who deteriorate despite appropriate therapy or present with atypical clinical or imaging features. In cases where infection and RVT coexist, the temporal relationship and causality may remain uncertain, and diagnosis and management should be individualized according to the clinical presentation, thrombus extent, severity of infection, and imaging findings.

articles.title: Landscape connectivity and climatic drivers shaping Noctuidae communities in a Brazilian seasonally dryland fruit-producing region.
articles.abstract: Drylands are highly sensitive to climatic shifts, affecting insect population dynamics and multi-trophic interactions. This study evaluated Noctuidae diversity and temporal distribution in the São Francisco Valley, a semi-arid, irrigated, fruit-producing region in Northeast Brazil, in relation to local environmental factors. We conducted monitoring over two consecutive years using Pennsylvania light traps deployed across two agricultural landscapes integrated with native Caatinga dry forest: an experimental multi-crop station and a commercial table grape farm. We captured 12,407 Noctuidae moths; raw richness favored the grapevine site, but diversity did not differ, and per-individual richness favored the multi-crop site once sampling effort was considered. Four Noctuinae species dominated the assemblage (94.04% of total captures): Spodoptera frugiperda (Smith) (39.53%), Elaphria agrotina (Guenée) (36.89%), Spodoptera cosmioides (Walker) (9.21%), and Spodoptera albula (Walker) (8.40%). Immediate captures of S. frugiperda and S. albula rose with lower wind speed and higher precipitation; previous-month captures showed the same patterns for S. frugiperda and S. albula, but E. agrotina responded to temperature and S. cosmioides to site and precipitation instead. Circular statistics indicated a stark temporal segregation between S. frugiperda and S. cosmioides. These findings suggest Caatinga connectivity elevates vineyard abundance, whereas the multi-crop mosaic's heterogeneity yields higher per-individual richness. Specialized crop management practices, such as continuous vineyard pruning, generate stable niches that favor detritivorous species like E. agrotina. Local multi-year calibrations are essential for accurate pest forecasting and integrated management across agricultural-forest interfaces in semi-arid zones.

articles.title: Effect of intraoral glossopharyngeal nerve block on hemodynamic response to mouth retractor placement in transoral robotic surgery: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Placement of rigid oral retractors during transoral robotic surgery (TORS) elicits a sympathetic hemodynamic response that may be harmful in high-risk patients. The glossopharyngeal nerve provides sensory innervation to the oropharyngeal structures stimulated during retractor placement, yet no previous trial has evaluated glossopharyngeal nerve block (GPN block) for attenuating this response. In this prospective, single-center, randomized clinical trial, 42 patients (ASA I-II, aged 18-65 years) undergoing TORS were allocated 1:1 to the block group, which received bilateral intraoral GPN block with 2 mL of 2% lignocaine per side or the Control group, which received no block. The outcome assessor was blinded; no sham procedure was performed, and the anaesthesiologist performing the block was not blinded. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with a > 20% increase in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from the pre-retractor baseline within 10 minutes of Feyh-Kastenbauer retractor insertion. Bayesian logistic regression with a Normal (0, 5) prior on the group coefficient was used; the pre-specified decision criterion was a posterior probability of directional benefit P (ARD < 0) exceeding 0.95. The trial was registered in the Clinical Trial Registry of India (CTRI/2022/03/041013, dated 11 March 2022) https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/searchbyctri.php , with a date of first patient enrolment of 21/03/2022. The increase in MAP > 20% occurred in 8 of 21 patients (38.1%) in the control group versus 3 of 21 (14.3%) in the block group. The posterior mean absolute risk difference was - 23.9% (95% credible interval [CrI]: - 49.4% to 2.2%), with P (ARD < 0) = 0.964, exceeding the pre-specified threshold. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the direction of effect under neutral, sceptical, and optimistic priors (P(ARD < 0) range: 0.934-0.967), although the posterior probability under the sceptical prior did not exceed the prespecified 0.95 threshold; evidence was equivocal under the pessimistic prior (P(ARD < 0) = 0.57). Maximum MAP and heart rate were lower in the block group (P (difference < 0) = 0.998 and 0.995, respectively). Bispectral index values were comparable between groups throughout the procedure. The GPN block is associated with a high posterior probability of attenuating the hemodynamic response to mouth retractor placement in TORS. The credible intervals were wide, reflecting uncertainty about effect magnitude. A larger confirmatory trial assessing clinical endpoints is warranted.

articles.title: Germline BRCA-Lynch syndrome MINAS: report of six Argentinian families and a systematic review of the literature.
articles.abstract: The co-occurrence of germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (PVs) in BRCA1/BRCA2 and mismatch repair genes (Lynch Syndrome) (BRCA-LS) is an infrequent overlap of the two most frequent hereditary cancer syndromes. Recent reviews have examined whether the cancer risk profile in BRCA-LS carriers is independent for both syndromes or if both germline variants act as mutual modifying factors, including a synergistic effect. This study on BRCA-LS Multi-locus Inherited Neoplasia Allele Syndrome (MINAS) aims to report six affected families, perform a systematic review (SR) of the literature to identify previously reported patients, and analyze the phenotype of this genetic condition. Including the reported families and the patients retrieved by the SR (40 publications), 92 patients from 69 families were analyzed. The analysis of the BRCA-LS MINAS phenotype showed a balanced distribution of BRCA and LS-related tumor patterns and tumors outside the established BRCA or LS spectra were uncommon. Carriers of PVs in MLH1 and MSH2/EPCAM were more likely to be diagnosed with ≥ 2 tumors [OR 3.60-95% CI 1.29-10.55; p = 0.0095] and with extracolonic tumors [OR 3,28 (CI95 1,26-8,84) p =0.0089] than carriers of PVs in MSH6 and PMS2, findings that are consistent with known genotype-phenotype correlations in LS. Our findings suggest that in the context of clinically ascertained patients with a personal or family history of cancer, BRCA-LS MINAS is primarily characterized by the independent expression of both syndromes and that potential synergistic effects require further evaluation in studies including systematically ascertained patients.

articles.title: What is the role of dentistry in palliative care? A scoping review of existing definitions.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although oral health is increasingly recognized as an important component of palliative care, the role of dentistry in this setting remains poorly defined. This study aims to systematically map and critically synthesize existing definitions reported in scientific literature.

METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology. MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from inception to May 5, 2026. Eligible sources explicitly defined the role of dentistry in palliative care. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data using a standardized charting form. Findings were synthesized using descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: Of 1454 records, 12 sources met the inclusion criteria. Two terms were used, most commonly "Palliative Care Dentistry" (92%). Eleven definitions were derived, directly or indirectly, from Wiseman's foundational definition published in 2000. Definitions consistently described care for patients with progressive, advanced, or terminal disease whose oral cavity was affected by the disease or its treatment, with quality of life as the principal goal. None explicitly specified care settings or interdisciplinary collaboration, and most limited the scope of practice to management-oriented activities; only one definition included prevention.

CONCLUSION: Existing definitions of the role of dentistry in palliative care rely on a single source and do not fully reflect contemporary palliative care principles, particularly regarding prevention, interdisciplinary care, patient-centered decision-making, and management of pre-existing oral conditions. A consensus-based definition is needed to clarify the field and guide future research, education, and practice.

articles.title: External validation of the MDR score for predicting multidrug-resistant device-associated infections in pediatric intensive care units (PEPE-MDR score): a nationwide registry-based study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) organisms are an increasing cause of device-associated healthcare-associated infections (DA-HAIs) in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs), complicating empirical antibiotic selection. The aim of the study was to externally validate the MDR-score (PEPE-MDR score), a tool developed to estimate the likelihood of a DA-HAI being caused by MDR. A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted using surveillance data from the pediatric ENVIN-HELICS registry (2014-2024). Pediatric patients with microbiologically confirmed DA-HAIs were included. The PEPE-MDR score incorporates prior MDR colonization, comorbidity, and PICU length of stay > 9 days. Discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), sensitivity, specificity, and positive (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV). Calibration was evaluated with the observed-to-expected (O:E) ratio and the calibration slope. Among 21,999 episodes registered, 406 DA-HAIs were included. Of these, 93 (22.9%) were caused by MDR organisms. Median (IQR) MDR scores were higher in MDR infections than non-MDR infections (p < 0.001), with a Hodges-Lehmann location shift (95% CI) of 3 points (2-4). The MDR score yielded an AUC-ROC of 0.69 (95% CI 0.62-0.75). Using the high-risk category as the threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 46.2% and 79.9% (PPV 40.6%; NPV 83.3%). Combining moderate- and high-risk categories increased sensitivity to 77.4% with specificity 47.0% (PPV 30.3%; NPV 87.5%). Observed risks were lower than predicted: O:E ratio 0.64 (95% CI 0.54-0.77), although risk increased across categories (12.5%, 22.0%, 40.6%; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this multicenter external validation, the PEPE-MDR score provided moderate discrimination and preserved risk stratification for MDR DA-HAIs, contributing to empirical antibiotic decision-making in PICUs after recalibration to local prevalence.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Acknowledging the risk of a multidrug resistant microorganism involvement in infections related to invasive devices is crucial to adjust empirical antibiotherapy in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). • A MDR score for Predicting Multidrug-Resistant Device-Associated Infections in Pediatric Intensive Care Units (PEPE-MDR score) was developed recently, but it required external validation.

WHAT IS NEW: • The PEPE-MDR score was validated in a multicenter national database. • These findings support the PEPE-MDR score's utility as a practical tool for adjusting empirical antibiotic treatment in the PICU setting.

articles.title: Comparison of sterile silicone studs and scalp infiltration with lignocaine for the attenuation of the hemodynamic and stress response to skull pin insertion during craniotomy in pediatric neurosurgical patients: a randomized controlled trial : Sterile silicone studs versus lignocaine infiltration for skull pin insertion.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skull pin application during pediatric neurosurgery elicits a pronounced nociceptive and sympathetic response, adversely affecting cerebral hemodynamics. We compared the efficacy of sterile silicone studs (SSS) with pin site lignocaine infiltration in attenuating the response to skull pin insertion in pediatric neurosurgical patients.

METHODS: Sixty-four pediatric patients (≤ 12 years, ASA I-II) were randomized to receive either SSS (Group SS, n = 32) or 2 ml of 2% plain lignocaine infiltration (Group LO, n = 32) at each skull pin insertion site. We assessed the requirement of rescue analgesia (fentanyl). The hemodynamics (Heart rate, mean arterial pressure) were also recorded at baseline, at pin insertion and at 1, 3, 5, and 10 min post pin insertion. Perioperative complications related to skull pin insertion and surgeon satisfaction were also assessed.

RESULTS: Rescue fentanyl consumption was significantly lower in Group SS than Group LO (10.3 ± 7.5 µg vs. 18.5 ± 8.6 µg; Cohen's d = 1.02; 95% CI, 0.51-1.53; P < 0.001). Fewer patients required rescue analgesia in Group SS (65.6% vs. 90.6%; Relative Risk, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.05-1.81; P < 0.03). Group LO showed significantly higher HR and MAP at pin insertion and up to 10 min thereafter (P < 0.05). Minor pin-site bleeding was more frequent in Group LO, while surgeon satisfaction was higher in Group SS.

CONCLUSION: SSS effectively attenuated the hemodynamic response to skull pin insertion and reduced the need for rescue opioids. They offer a safe, non-pharmacological, opioid-sparing alternative to lignocaine infiltration. Larger multicenter trials are warranted to conclusively establish the safety of SSS.

articles.title: Changes in gait function associated with cerebral small vessel disease-related cognitive impairment during dual-task walking: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major contributor to vascular cognitive impairment. As gait abnormalities emerge early in the disease course and are closely related to cognitive decline, quantitative gait assessment offers a promising approach for the early detection of CSVD-related cognitive impairment (CSVD-CI). Dual-task (DT) gait assessment increases cognitive demands during walking and may reveal cognitive-motor deficits that are less apparent under single-task (ST) conditions. However, heterogeneity in gait metrics, imaging criteria, and cognitive paradigms has resulted in inconsistent findings, thereby impeding the identification of robust gait markers for CSVD-CI. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and EBSCO identified nine studies reporting DT gait outcomes and eight reporting ST gait outcomes in patients with CSVD-CI, with four studies reporting outcomes under both conditions. Compared with ST conditions, DT gait assessment more effectively discriminated patients with CSVD-CI from cognitively unimpaired controls. Under DT conditions, CSVD-CI patients exhibited significantly slower gait speed (p = 0.014), greater stride time variability (p = 0.027), and higher dual-task costs (p < 0.001), suggesting a slower and less stable gait pattern. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses suggested that CSVD imaging characteristics may contribute to between-study heterogeneity, although these findings remain exploratory. These findings support further investigation of selected DT gait parameters as potential behavioral indicators of CSVD-CI. Further studies in CSVD populations defined using standardized diagnostic and inclusion criteria should evaluate the screening performance and longitudinal predictive value of DT gait parameters, as well as their associations with CI severity.

articles.title: Early echocardiographic hemodynamic phenotypes and clinical outcomes in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Early postnatal hemodynamic adaptation may contribute to outcome heterogeneity in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We evaluated whether echocardiography-defined hemodynamic phenotypes within 24 h of birth were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or death. This retrospective cohort included infants with CDH admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit from 2021 to 2025 who underwent echocardiography within 24 h. Phenotypes were classified as no/mild pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV)-predominant PH, or left ventricular (LV)-involved PH based on ventricular function and ductal/atrial shunt direction. Associations with prenatal severity, respiratory indices, and ECMO or death were assessed. Among 66 infants, 21 had no/mild PH, 22 RV-predominant PH, and 23 LV-involved PH. ECMO or death occurred in 0%, 27.3%, and 65.2%, respectively (P < 0.001). Compared with RV-predominant PH, LV-involved PH was associated with greater respiratory severity and more frequent LV dysfunction; observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (O/E LHR) did not differ significantly between these two groups. Ordinal phenotype severity remained associated with ECMO or death after adjustment for O/E LHR (odds ratio (OR), 5.98; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.76-20.31; P = 0.004). However, the comparison between LV-involved and RV-predominant PH was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for O/E LHR (OR, 3.42; 95% CI, 0.87-15.10).

CONCLUSION: Early hemodynamic phenotype was associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death in CDH. LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype and may complement prenatal anatomic risk stratification, although its independent prognostic value beyond prenatal lung size requires validation.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Prenatal lung size and liver herniation are established markers of disease severity and outcome in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). • Pulmonary hypertension and ventricular dysfunction contribute substantially to early cardiorespiratory instability and adverse outcomes in infants with CDH.

WHAT IS NEW: • Early echocardiographic phenotypes were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death. • LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype, although its prognostic value beyond prenatal severity remains uncertain.

articles.title: Controlled postoperative red wine intake versus abstinence in habitual wine drinkers undergoing elective urological surgery (WISE): a translational randomized controlled trial assessing quality of life, surgical outcomes and complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To date, no prospective randomized study has evaluated whether controlled postoperative red wine intake, compared with abstinence, affects recovery in habitual wine drinkers undergoing surgery.

METHODS: In this single-center randomized controlled trial (NCT05261620), habitual wine drinkers scheduled for elective urological surgery were randomized 1:1 to abstinence from alcohol (Control Arm) or standardized red wine intake (150 mL of 13% v/v red wine with lunch and with dinner) from postoperative day 1 to day 30 (Experimental Arm). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in change from baseline to 30 days in the SF-36 Mental Health Index (MHI). Secondary endpoints included postoperative complications, hospital readmission, length of hospitalization, blood parameters, and oxidative stress markers.

RESULTS: The mean change in MHI was - 0.6 in the Control Arm and + 0.7 in the Experimental Arm (difference 1.3 points; 95% CI - 1.9 to 4.6; p = 0.4). Overall complications (16.1% vs. 9.8%; p = 0.4), length of hospital stay and 30-day readmissions (8.1% vs. 0%; p = 0.06) did not differ significantly between the Control and Experimental Arms, respectively. Blood parameters and oxidative stress markers showed no clinically relevant differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Among predominantly older male habitual wine drinkers undergoing elective urological surgery, controlled postoperative red wine intake did not improve 30-day quality of life compared with abstinence. Complications and blood parameters did not differ meaningfully. These findings do not support the initiation or promotion of alcohol use.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261620, registered on 02/20/2022. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05261620 ).

articles.title: Beyond fecal abundance: defining the active therapeutic entity in Bifidobacterium-mediated protection against Klebsiella-driven MASLD.
Short-term effects of myofascial release with therapist-mediated transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: an exploratory randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the short-term effects of myofascial release with therapist-mediated transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (MFR-TENS) on angle of trunk rotation (ATR) and bilateral plantar symmetry in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS).

METHODS: This assessor-blinded, exploratory randomized controlled trial included 27 adolescents with AIS. Participants were randomly assigned to the MFR-TENS group (n = 14) or the control group (n = 13). The MFR-TENS group received 60 min/day of MFR-TENS for 7 days, whereas the control group received 10 min/day of disease-awareness education. At baseline and immediately after the intervention, all participants underwent assessments of ATR, peak plantar pressure (PPP), and plantar contact area (PCA). The peak plantar pressure symmetry index (PPP-SI) and plantar contact area symmetry index (PCA-SI) were derived post hoc from the originally collected bilateral PPP and PCA measurements across 13 plantar regions. Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA was used for each outcome.

RESULTS: All randomized participants completed the study. A significant group × time interaction was observed for ATR (F(1, 25) = 249.023, P < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.909). ATR did not change significantly in the control group, with a mean change of 0.04° (95% confidence interval (CI), - 0.358° to 0.435°; P = 0.843), but decreased by 4.18° in the MFR-TENS group (95% CI, - 4.560° to - 3.797°; P < 0.001). The between-group difference in mean change was - 4.22° (95% CI, - 4.767° to - 3.667°; P < 0.001). No regional group × time interaction for PPP-SI or PCA-SI remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) correction. No intervention-related adverse events or serious adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: In this small, retrospectively registered exploratory trial, a 1-week MFR-TENS intervention was associated with short-term changes in ATR, but no consistent changes in PPP-SI or PCA-SI were observed. Larger, prospectively registered, and well-controlled trials with longer follow-up are required to determine the durability and clinical relevance of these findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2400091231, retrospectively registered on 23 October 2024.

articles.title: Reporting Gaps and Challenges in Randomized Trials of Generative AI for Medical Use: Insights From a Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Generative AI (GenAI) is being deployed rapidly in medicine, and evidence of its clinical safety and efficacy depends on transparent reporting of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The CONSORT-AI (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials-AI) extension is a benchmark for AI trial reporting, but it was drafted for conventional AI, and its applicability to GenAI has not been examined.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess item-level adherence to the CONSORT-AI among RCTs evaluating GenAI for medical purposes and to distinguish deficiencies attributable to nonadherence from those attributable to items that do not correspond to how GenAI interventions are specified or delivered.

METHODS: PubMed, CENTRAL (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials), and Embase were searched for peer-reviewed, English-language RCTs published from 2022 to April 3, 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching, in which patients, health care professionals, or laypeople received a GenAI intervention for a medical purpose; non-GenAI, nonmedical, nonrandomized, and non-peer-reviewed reports were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and rated CONSORT-AI items as reported, partially reported, not reported, or not applicable using signaling questions, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer (Cohen κ=0.81 and prevalence-adjusted, bias-adjusted κ=0.84). Risk of bias was not assessed, as the target was reporting adherence. Adherence was the proportion of reports rated "reported" per item; item-level adherence was compared across 9 characteristics using Fisher exact and Freeman-Halton tests (2-sided α=.05).

RESULTS: From 16,485 retrieved records, 74 reports from 73 RCTs (24,150 participants; median 100, IQR 50.0-247.0) were included. Large language models (LLMs) accounted for 98.6% (73/74) of interventions, with 60.8% (45/74) using GPT-family models. Item-level reporting adherence ranged from 0% (0/72) to 98.6% (73/74). High adherence occurred in general metadata and output specification items (range 59-73, 79.7%-98.6%). Conversely, reporting was poor for input and technical execution domains, input data eligibility (3/73, 4.1%), input acquisition/selection (9/74, 12.2%), algorithm versioning (17/74, 23.0%), trial setting integration (21/74, 28.4%), human-AI interaction (25/74, 33.8%), performance error (27/74, 36.5%), and open access/code (31/74, 41.9%). Input quality handling (Item 5[iii]) was completely unreported (0/72). Only 9 of 74 (12.2%) reports explicitly cited CONSORT-AI. While citing reports showed higher compliance for interaction and data sharing, major technical gaps persisted regardless of citation.

CONCLUSIONS: This review provides the first empirical audit distinguishing general nonadherence from structural mismatches where deterministic CONSORT-AI items fail to capture GenAI mechanics. Differing from traditional AI evaluations, it reveals that key reproducibility drivers-system prompts, inference settings, and access modalities-are omitted from current standards. These empirical findings highlight critical reporting gaps in medical GenAI trials and identify domains for a tailored extension to current reporting standards, although the evidence is limited by the use of nonvalidated signaling questions. Establishing GenAI-specific trial guidelines will ensure that clinical decisions, regulatory approvals, and patient safety safeguards are grounded in reproducible and trustworthy evidence.

articles.title: Genotype-phenotype spectrum of Alport syndrome in Indian children: a nationwide experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alport syndrome (AS) is an inherited disorder affecting the type IV collagen of the basement membrane. The study objectives were to examine the genotype-phenotype correlation of Indian children with variants in type IV collagen genes (COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5), to assess the impact of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI) on proteinuria and chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression.

METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included children <18 years from 10 centres across India with variants in COL4A genes. Based on the latest guidelines, variants were further classified as X-linked AS (XLAS), autosomal recessive AS (ARAS), and autosomal dominant AS (ADAS).

RESULTS: Of the 108 children, the majority were XLAS (60/108), followed by ARAS (35/108) and ADAS (13/108), with a median (IQR) age at presentation of 5 (3-9) years. At onset, all had haematuria; 83% had proteinuria (89/108); 30.5% (33/108) had CKD and characteristic electron microscopy changes in 54.3% 25) were in CKD stage 25/46). The median (IQR) duration of follow-up was 3 (1-5) years. At 1-year follow-up, XLAS males and ARAS had higher proteinuria (p value 0.009) and lower eGFR (p value 0.02). While 68.5% (74/108) of the cohort received ACEI, there was no significant impact on proteinuria or CKD at 5-year follow-up.

CONCLUSION: In Indian children, XLAS was the most common type. XLAS males and ARAS had higher proteinuria and CKD in short-term follow-up. ACEI/ARB did not show significant impact on kidney outcomes. There is a need for further studies with long-term follow-up in children with AS.

articles.title: Diagnostic performances and longitudinal trajectories of gene expression profiling and donor-derived cell-free DNA in pediatric kidney transplant recipients with rejection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely diagnosis of allograft rejection is crucial for preventing premature graft loss. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of blood gene expression profile (GEP) and donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) in detecting rejection in pediatric kidney transplant recipients.

METHODS: We prospectively recruited pediatric kidney transplant recipients (<21 years) who underwent a for-cause biopsy (August 20, 2023-February 6, 2025). Blood samples for GEP and dd-cfDNA were collected at biopsy (week 0) and at weeks 4 and 8. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize cohort characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy of biomarkers (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value [PPV], and negative predictive value [NPV]) was calculated against the gold-standard biopsy.

RESULTS: Our pilot study included 27 biopsies performed in 23 recipients. The median age of participants was 6.1 (IQR: 3.9, 13.7) years; 55.6% were male, and 92.6% were white. At week 0, GEP detected rejection with 40.0% sensitivity, 82.0% specificity, 57.0% PPV, and 70.0% NPV. A GEP score >0.4 yielded higher sensitivity (86% vs. 43%) and NPV (80% vs. 67%) compared to a score >0.5. Using a dd-cfDNA threshold of >1.0%, dual-positivity (positive dd-cfDNA and GEP) yielded a 33.0% sensitivity, 94.0% specificity, 75.0% PPV, and 73.0% NPV. Overall, the combined AUC of dd-cfDNA and GEP probability scores was 0.62 (95% CI, 0.31-0.93). Unlike serum creatinine, GEP probability scores and dd-cfDNA trended toward quiescent levels on serial assessment.

CONCLUSION: Combining GEP and dd-cfDNA improved their diagnostic performance. GEP and dd-cfDNA levels showed a downward trend after rejection treatment initiation.

articles.title: Predicting 12-month renal non-response in childhood-onset lupus nephritis: added value of kidney biopsy pathology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric-specific models for renal response in childhood-onset lupus nephritis (cLN) are scarce. We developed internally validated models for failure to achieve 12-month complete renal response (CRR) and quantified pathology's incremental value.

METHODS: In a single-centre retrospective cohort of 503 children with cLN, the prespecified primary outcome was stringent CRR at 12 months after induction therapy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision-curve analysis, with bootstrap optimism correction. Within the pathology-model subgroup, the incremental value of biopsy findings was assessed by the paired bootstrap difference in AUC between Model 2 and Model 1-restricted. Subsequent renal flare was examined in a 12-month landmark analysis using restricted mean survival time (RMST).

RESULTS: Of 503 children, 295 (58.6%) achieved 12-month CRR. Model 1 yielded an AUC of 0.784 (95% CI, 0.745-0.824). Within the pathology-model subgroup, the AUC was 0.734 (95% CI, 0.682-0.788) for Model 1-restricted and 0.828 (95% CI, 0.786-0.870) for Model 2, with a paired ΔAUC of 0.071 (95% CI, 0.029-0.124). Model 2 also reduced prediction error. In the landmark cohort, CRR was associated with 10.0 additional renal flare-free months over 60 months (95% CI, 7.6-12.7).

CONCLUSIONS: A paediatric-specific clinical model provided useful risk stratification for failure to achieve 12-month CRR, and kidney biopsy pathology offered consistent incremental predictive value when available. These internally validated models require external validation before clinical use.

articles.title: What do the findings of compartmentalised sub-phenotypes in lungs of patients with pneumonia mean for critical care?
[Nursing competencies in ECMO care: a scoping review].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is used in cases of refractory cardiac or pulmonary failure and places high demands on the treatment team, particularly on nursing staff, whose required competencies have scarcely been described in German-speaking countries.

OBJECTIVE: The primary aim was to map the international evidence on nursing competencies in the care of adult ECMO patients. Secondary aims included identifying specialised nursing roles and drawing implications for the German-speaking countries.

METHODS: The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the guidelines of the Joanna Briggs Institute and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses- Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The literature search was carried out in MEDLINE, CINAHL and Scopus, as well as in reference lists. German- and English-language primary studies published between 2009 and May 2026 were included.

RESULTS: A total of n = 14 studies were included, comprising n = 7 qualitative (n = 6 [semi-structured] interview studies, n = 1 focus group interview) and n = 7 quantitative (n = 3 cross-sectional studies, n = 1 Delphi survey, n = 1 prospective cohort study, n = 1 prospective observational study, and n = 1 quasi-experimental study) studies. Based on the identified evidence, a multidimensional competency profile for ECMO nursing care can be described, including the necessary knowledge, practical skills, and professional attitudes. In addition, specialised nursing roles were identified. No studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified for German-speaking countries.

CONCLUSION: A multidimensional competency profile emerges that is internationally anchored in specialised nursing roles; however, empirical data, role profiles and structured qualification pathways are lacking in German-speaking countries.

articles.title: [Life-threatening hemorrhage after tonsillotomy in a child : A structured recommendation for action in the prehospital setting].
articles.abstract: One week after an uncomplicated ENT-surgery in a 7-year-old boy, a sudden and massive hemorrhage from the oropharyngeal area occurs. The arriving emergency medicals find an apathetic child with active bleeding and recognise quickly the need for immediate action. Based on this case report, the measures taken and an overview of surgical procedures involving the palatine and pharyngeal tonsils in children, a guideline for prehospital care is proposed to enable structured action in such a potentially life-threatening situation.

articles.title: Genetic Variants Associated with Ventricular Septal Defect in Malaysia: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Research Gaps.
articles.abstract: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most prevalent congenital heart defect in Malaysia; however, its genetic basis is still not well understood. We conducted a scoping review to evaluate the current evidence on VSD-associated genetic variants in the Malaysian population. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase from inception to June 2026, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Original studies investigating genetic variants associated with VSD in Malaysian patients were included. Data regarding study characteristics, investigated genes, reported variants, molecular methods, and principal findings were extracted and synthesised. Out of 28 records identified, three studies met the eligibility criteria. The included studies reported variants in three genes: SMAD7, NR0B1, and NIPBL. The identified variants included synonymous substitutions and frameshift alterations that were predicted to cause premature protein truncation. However, the available evidence was limited by small sample sizes, candidate-gene approaches, and the predominance of syndromic cases. We found no nationwide or multicentre studies using high-throughput sequencing technologies. Despite the significant disease burden, the current evidence on the genetics of VSD in Malaysia remains sparse. The lack of comprehensive genomic investigations underscores the need for collaborative studies across the nation that integrate next-generation sequencing and functional validation. This would enhance our understanding of VSD pathogenesis and support future precision medicine initiatives.

articles.title: Central Venous Recanalization for Refractory Chylothorax Caused by Extensive Central Venous Thrombosis.

Predictors of Clinical Outcomes Following Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) Placement: Comparing Baseline Liver Function Tests, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) iterations, and the Freiburg Index of Post-TIPS Survival (FIPS).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate risk stratification is vital to optimize outcomes following Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) placement. This study compared the 30-day prognostic performance of traditional laboratory values, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) iterations (MELD, MELD-Na, MELD 3.0), and the Freiburg Index of Post-TIPS Survival (FIPS).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, 192 adult patients were analyzed who underwent TIPS placement from 2018 to 2024 at a US quaternary center. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or unplanned readmission. Scoring performance was evaluated using Spearman's correlation (Rho), ANOVA with Games-Howell post hoc testing, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: The 30-day composite endpoint occurred in 84 patients (42%; 37 deaths, 47 readmissions). Baseline albumin, creatinine, total bilirubin, and international normalized ratio correlated with the primary outcome (all p < 0.05). Among scoring systems, MELD 3.0 showed the strongest overall correlation with the examined outcome (Rho = 0.328, p < 0.001), closely followed by FIPS (Rho = 0.310, p < 0.001). A DeLong's test found no significant difference between MELD 3.0 and FIPS in predicting short-term composite outcomes. Post hoc testing showed FIPS significantly distinguished mortality from non-readmission (p < 0.001) but not between readmissions and uneventful recoveries (p = 0.228). ROC analysis identified a FIPS threshold of 1.115 for predicting 30-day mortality, yielding 94.1% specificity, 77.2% accuracy, and 46.4% sensitivity.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, no significant difference was found between MELD 3.0 and FIPS in predicting short-term composite outcomes. MELD 3.0 offers the strongest linear tracking for short-term composite outcomes, while a FIPS score > 1.115 might serve as a highly specific tool to identify candidates at risk for early mortality.

articles.title: [Six months of the first digital health application in rheumatology : Real-world data evaluation on treatment adherence of the first 400 patients using Axia].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital health applications (DHA; in German: Digitale Gesundheitsanwendungen, DiGA) have been criticized for being costly and for limited or absent use by patients after prescription. Since late January 2026, the first DHA (Axia) for axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), and thus for an inflammatory rheumatic disease, is available by prescription and reimbursement. Real-world data on adherence to Axia are not yet available.

OBJECTIVE: To assess usage behavior among the first 400 Axia users in routine clinical care.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of anonymized usage data from the DHA Axia. Usage days and usage periods during the 90-day DHA access period were assessed for all patients and for users meeting the definition of a regular user, defined as no interruption in use during 21 consecutive days.

RESULTS: Of the first 400 users 73% (n = 291) met the definition of regular users. A follow-up prescription was issued to 63% (n = 253) of all patients and to 77% (n = 225) of regular users. The mean duration of use was 55.4 out of 90 days (62%, standard deviation, SD 30.4 days) overall and 69.8 out of 90 days (78%) among regular users (SD 20.7 days).

DISCUSSION: Real-world usage data from the first 400 users indicate high adherence to the DHA Axia. Additional real-world data from less preselected cohorts, including clinical efficacy endpoints, are required for further evaluation of the results.

articles.title: Myocardial inflammatory activity and structural injury are discordant in connective tissue disease compared with acute suspected viral myocarditis: a CMR study.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: In connective tissue diseases (CTD), myocardial T2 elevation is a frequent CMR finding, yet whether it translates into myocardial injury remains uncertain. We compared T2 and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) between CTD-associated myocardial involvement and acute suspected viral myocarditis, a clinical model in which inflammatory activity and structural injury commonly co-occur in the acute phase, to assess whether the association between myocardial inflammatory activity and structural injury differs between disease contexts.

METHODS: Patients from two prospective institutional registries were included. Active myocardial inflammation was defined using a study-specific CMR definition based on the T2 component of the updated Lake Louise Criteria, requiring T2 elevation ≥ 40 ms, applied identically in both groups. Inflammatory activity was quantified by myocardial T2 mapping and structural injury by LGE.

RESULTS: A total of 181 patients were included (CTD n = 44; viral myocarditis n = 137). CTD patients were predominantly female (75% vs. 44%; p < 0.001) with comparable age (56 ± 16 vs. 52 ± 18 years; p = 0.172). Despite higher myocardial T2 in CTD (42.5 ± 2.2 vs. 41.0 ± 2.8 ms; p = 0.002; multivariable β = 1.14 ms, 95% CI 0.29-2.0; p = 0.009), structural injury was markedly less pronounced (LGE prevalence was 41% vs. 88%; p < 0.001), while native T1 and ECV did not differ significantly between groups. Acute suspected viral myocarditis was independently associated with higher LGE likelihood (adjusted OR 11.14; 95% CI 4.43-27.98; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Myocardial T2 elevation in CTD may not be invariably associated with LGE-defined myocardial injury and may carry different implications than in acute suspected viral myocarditis. Disease-specific contextualization of CMR inflammatory markers is warranted.

articles.title: Implementing a Physician Annual Unpaid Sabbatical for Escape: utilizing a rotating "PAUSE" month to improve wellness amongst emergency medicine physicians.
Predicting in-silico ventricular tachycardia induction on fuzzy cardiac digital twins.
articles.abstract: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD). To date, clinical VT risk assessment is either inaccurate, invasive or expensive. Patient-specific computer modeling of heart electrophysiology (EP) is a promising non-invasive risk assessment approach. It has three major limitations: computational cost, inaccurate arrhythmogenic substrate geometry and unknown patient-specific tissue EP properties. We present a pacing outcome predictor (POP) that quickly identifies the conditions needed to induce VT in three-dimensional personalized cardiac computer models. The POP is used to test VT induction across multiple model versions of a patient, covering scar geometry and EP property variations, with an added layer of model reduction to further accelerate calculations. The results are combined into a personalized VT risk metric based on in-silico VT inducibility across the patient's models. In a retrospective 10-patient repaired Tetralogy of Fallot cohort, the metric showed complete separation (10/10) between patients with and without clinically inducible VT, suggesting potential for non-invasive VT risk assessment in this population.

articles.title: Late gadolinium enhancement scar burden and microvascular obstruction and one-year mortality after myocardial infarction: a South Asian cohort study.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) characterises infarct scar and microvascular obstruction (MVO) after myocardial infarction (MI). Left-ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) remains the reference prognostic marker; data on LGE tissue markers from South Asian populations, in whom delayed presentation produces larger scars, are limited. We examined the association of LGE scar burden and MVO with one-year all-cause mortality. Single-centre, retrospective observational cohort of 260 patients with MI referred for clinically indicated CMR. LGE scar burden (% of LV mass), MVO, segmental viability and infarct territory were recorded. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality over a median follow-up of one year. Because per-patient event dates and CMR-derived LVEF were not available in this dataset, associations were tested by logistic regression (complete-case primary analysis; multiple imputation as sensitivity analysis), with model calibration and discrimination assessed. NYHA class and re-admission were analysed descriptively. Mean scar burden was 27.5 ± 12.5% of LV mass; MVO was present in 128 patients (49.2%); 41 (15.8%) died. Among patients with a measured scar value (n = 244), one-year mortality was 22.8% with scar ≥ 28% versus 10.8% below this threshold (p = 0.015), and 22.7% versus 9.1% with versus without MVO (p = 0.004). In multivariable analysis (n = 244, 40 events; events-per-variable 10; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.057), MVO was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.09, 95% CI 1.41-6.80) as was age (aOR 1.06/year, 1.02-1.10); scar burden was not independently associated after adjustment (aOR 1.35 per 10%, 95% CI 1.00-1.83, p = 0.053). Scar burden showed only modest discrimination (area under the curve 0.62). Estimates were stable after multiple imputation. In a real-world South Asian post-MI cohort with high scar burden, MVO was independently associated with one-year mortality, whereas scar burden was associated only in unadjusted analysis. These hypothesis-generating findings support the prognostic relevance of CMR tissue characterisation but require confirmation in prospective cohorts with LVEF and clinical covariates before clinical application.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Short-Course Radiotherapy Alone or Combined With Consolidation Chemotherapy Versus Conventional Long-Course Chemoradiotherapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Short-course radiotherapy (SCRT)-based regimens, including SCRT-alone and SCRT-based total neoadjuvant therapy (SCRT-based TNT, defined as SCRT followed by consolidation chemotherapy), have emerged as alternative neoadjuvant options to long-course chemoradiotherapy (LCCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). This meta-analysis stratified analyses by the type of SCRT regimen and whether LCCRT arms received preoperative consolidation chemotherapy, to systematically compare their efficacy and safety and inform personalized treatment selection.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing SCRT-based regimens and LCCRT up to November 2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Pooled analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5.3, with relative risk (RR) or hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Nine randomized trials (reported in 16 publications), involving 3,061 patients, were included. In the primary comparison of SCRT-based TNT versus standard LCCRT, the SCRT-based TNT group achieved a significantly higher pathological complete response rate (RR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.24-1.97, P = 0.0002), whereas tumor downstaging and locoregional failure showed no significant differences from the LCCRT group. The SCRT-based TNT regimen was associated with a significantly higher incidence of grade ≥ 3 acute toxicity (RR = 1.63, 95% CI: 1.14-2.34, P = 0.008), and showed numerical trends toward improved overall survival (HR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.76-1.28, P = 0.91) and disease-free survival (HR = 1.05, 95% CI: 0.77-1.43, P = 0.77) that did not reach statistical significance. SCRT alone was associated with lower pCR (RR = 0.13, 95% CI: 0.03-0.51, P = 0.003) and downstaging rates (RR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.56-0.79, P < 0.00001) but a markedly lower incidence of acute toxicity (RR = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.05-0.29, P < 0.00001). An exploratory analysis based on a single small trial found no significant differences between SCRT-based TNT and LCCRT-based TNT across all major endpoints. Pooling all SCRT-based strategies obscured clinically meaningful heterogeneity and yielded no significant differences for any primary endpoint.

CONCLUSIONS: SCRT-based TNT significantly improves pCR compared with standard LCCRT but does not translate into survival benefit, with a numerical increase in locoregional failure. SCRT-alone offers lower acute toxicity but substantially poorer tumor response, warranting use only in selected patients. The comparison between SCRT-based TNT and LCCRT-based TNT remains inconclusive. SCRT-based regimens represent heterogeneous treatment pathways rather than a uniform substitute for LCCRT, requiring individualized clinical decision-making.

articles.title: The Experience of Urinary Incontinence and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms on Work Participation: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Urinary incontinence (UI) and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are largely invisible to others. Managing these conditions can restrict participation in life roles, particularly those involving community life, such as participating in work occupations. The purpose was to describe existing and emerging evidence on the experience of UI/LUTS on participation in work.

METHOD: A scoping review, using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, was conducted. Six academic databases plus supplementary web-based search engines were systematically searched to locate evidence. Records describing the experience of UI/LUTS on work participation, available in English and full text, published in or after 2002 were included.

RESULTS: The review included 39 records. Most evidence collected data via self-report on quantitative instruments measuring the impact of UI/LUTS on work participation, revealing sparse research exploring the experience in work of individuals with UI/LUTS using qualitative methodologies. UI/LUTS limited work participation for individuals of all ages, and sex. Individuals with increased UI/LUTS severity reported greater cognitive, physical and psychosocial impacts on work participation. UI/LUTS were exacerbated by job type, specific work activities, inflexible work scheduling, and workplace design, for example, restricted bathroom access, breaks, or relief workers. Individuals with UI/LUTS employed varied management strategies including delayed voiding, fluid restriction, and wearing incontinence products at work.

CONCLUSION: UI/LUTS impacts work participation with the burden for managing symptoms falling heavily on individuals. A deeper understanding of the impact on work from individuals living with UI/LUTS is needed to guide practice, design, and policies to increase inclusion and participation.

articles.title: Understanding Barriers and Facilitators to Sustained Work Participation for Individuals with Diabetes Through an Intersectional Lens: a Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diabetes is a chronic condition that affects many aspects of individuals' lives, including their ability to participate in work and daily activities. However, how diabetes affects the (work) participation of women and men of different backgrounds, remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted 12 interviews with women and men with diabetes of different ethnic and socioeconomic backgrounds between the ages of 18 and 67. These interviews concerned participants' characteristics, as well as work-related and social factors that affected their ability to continue paid work with diabetes. We used outcome-mapping to facilitate the discussion of different factors affecting (work) participation with diabetes. We conducted a thematic analysis using an interpretative research paradigm and an exploratory secondary intersectional analysis, and structured our results using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) framework.

RESULTS: Symptoms of diabetes and the effort to regulate diabetes strongly impacted the ability to (remain in) work. Other barriers included physically demanding work, work pressure/stress, long commutes, and inflexible and irregular working hours, whereas facilitators included flexibility, a supportive work- and social environment, workplace accommodations, favourable employment conditions, diabetes disclosure and acceptance, and setting boundaries. While findings were mostly comparable, small, preliminary differences based on social identities emerged reducing working hours, coping mechanisms, diabetes acceptance, and a need to prove oneself.

CONCLUSION: Remaining in work with diabetes is shaped by diabetes-related challenges and workplace factors, with minor differences observed across genders and ethnic groups.

articles.title: Obesity and perioperative outcomes of robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer in obese versus non-obese patients, as classified in the source studies. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for comparative studies of robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer. Obesity was defined as BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² according to each study. The included data were not uniformly restricted to BMI < 40 kg/m²; consequently, the analysis does not represent class I-II obesity alone. Eight retrospective studies involving 1,879 patients were included. No statistically significant differences were detected in operative time (MD, - 9.02 min; 95% CI, - 21.25 to 3.20; p = 0.15), estimated blood loss (MD, 35.69 mL; 95% CI, - 40.54 to 111.93; p = 0.36), or length of stay (MD, - 0.25 days; 95% CI, - 0.61 to 0.10; p = 0.16). Pooled complication estimates were also nonsignificant. These findings do not establish equivalent safety. In the included retrospective studies, obesity as classified by the original reports was not associated with statistically significant differences in the assessed perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted surgery. The estimates are imprecise and potentially confounded; they do not establish equivalence or demonstrate superiority over other surgical approaches.
