This study aimed to assess dermal microvascularity using ultra micro-angiography (UMA) and to compare the efficacy of color UMA (cUMA) and subtraction UMA (sUMA) in this context. Our findings suggest that UMA may be a valuable technique for evaluating the dermal microvasculature.

METHODS: In this multicenter, prospective investigation, 54 healthy adults (22 males and 32 females) were recruited to examine the facial dermis in the zygoma and buccal regions using UMA. Parameters such as dermal thickness, microvascular flow velocity, microvascular resistance, cUMA and sUMA were measured. The associations between cUMA or sUMA and dermal thickness, age and sex were analyzed using correlation statistics.

RESULTS: The facial dermis in the zygoma and buccal regions was thicker in males than in females, with statistically significant differences. In males, the peak systolic velocity and end-diastolic velocity were higher in both regions than in females, with significant differences. Contrarily, the resistance index did not differ significantly between the sexes. Both cUMA and sUMA showed a correlation with dermal thickness and sex but were independent of age. Notably, sUMA had a higher detection rate than cUMA, indicating its superior sensitivity in identifying the dermal microvasculature.

CONCLUSION: The dermal thickness and microvascular flow velocities varied significantly between the sexes, with sUMA proving more effective than cUMA in detecting the dermal microvasculature. These results indicate the potential of UMA as a robust tool for assessing the dermal microvasculature in healthy adults, suggesting broader applications in dermatological research, diagnostics and evaluation of disease treatment efficacy.

articles.title: Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Large-Vessel Vasculitis and Aortitis.
articles.abstract: Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET/CT has emerged as a pivotal imaging modality for the diagnosis and management of large-vessel vasculitis (LVV) and aortitis. This review examines the current evidence and clinical applications of FDG-PET in giant cell arteritis, Takayasu arteritis, isolated aortitis, and infectious aortitis. Recent ACR/EULAR classification criteria now formally incorporate PET imaging findings, reflecting the modality's diagnostic importance. Meta-analyses report pooled sensitivities of approximately 80% to 84% and specificities of 87% to 89% for LVV diagnosis. The EANM/SNMMI joint procedural recommendations provide standardized protocols for patient preparation, image acquisition, and interpretation, including the use of visual grading scales.

articles.title: Valuable Role of Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Therapeutic Decision Making and Theranostics of Neurologic Disorders in Conjunction with Non-Fluorodeoxyglucose Tracers.
articles.abstract: Brain ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) is an important functional imaging modality for evaluating glucose metabolism. Over time, it has been observed that various metabolic patterns can support diagnoses, inform prognosis, guide therapeutic decision-making, and assess treatment response. Clinical applications span seizures, brain tumors, traumatic brain injury, neuroinflammatory and infectious disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, and other chronic neurological conditions. Although FDG is not itself a theranostic radiopharmaceutical, its ability to characterize metabolism may contribute to treatment planning, particularly in molecularly targeted neuro-oncology. This chapter reviews established and investigational applications of brain FDG-PET, emphasizing disease characterization, therapeutic selection, and response assessment.

articles.title: Influence of non-thermal atmospheric plasma on the mechanical properties and phase stability of zirconia ceramics.
articles.journal: Dental materials : official publication of the Academy of Dental Materials
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of non-thermal atmospheric plasma (NTP) and blasting (BL) treatments on the flexural strength, phase transformation, and residual stress of zirconia ceramics.

METHODS: Bar-shaped specimens of 3Y-TZP (3Y, Classic Katana), 4Y-PSZ (4Y, STML Katana), and 5Y-PSZ (5Y, UTML Katana) were fabricated and assigned to untreated control, blasting (BL), or NTP groups (n = 10). Phase transformation was primarily assessed by Raman spectroscopy using untreated specimens as references, while XRD was used as a complementary technique for the BL- and NTP-treated specimens. Flexural strength (FS) and elastic modulus (E) were measured using a universal testing machine (1 mm/min, 5000 kgf load cell). Surface morphology was evaluated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Data were analyzed using Weibull statistics, two-way ANOVA, and Tukey's post-hoc test (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: Monoclinic phase formation was detected only in 3Y (7.1 ± 2.1%) and 4Y (1.7 ± 1.1%) zirconia after BL, while 5Y zirconia remained phase stable. No significant differences in FS or E were observed among the control, BL, and NTP groups within the zirconia composition. For both properties, 3Y exhibited the highest values, followed by 4Y and 5Y (p < 0.05). Weibull moduli did not differ significantly among the groups (p = 0.320). Positive Raman peak shifts consistent with relative compressive residual stress were observed in all BL-treated groups.

SIGNIFICANCE: Under the evaluated conditions, NTP did not produce detectable crystallographic or morphological alterations. However, its effectiveness as a pre-cementation treatment cannot be established because zirconia-resin bonding was not evaluated.

articles.title: Rehabilitation of elbow fractures and/or dislocations: An update on the current practice patterns of treating clinicians.
articles.journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elbow fractures and dislocations, though relatively uncommon, can result in long-term pain, stiffness, and disability, with hand therapists playing a key role in rehabilitation. New developments in assessment and intervention have been described in the literature since the previous published 2012 survey describing therapist practice patterns related to elbow rehabilitation.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this exploratory survey study was to investigate the current practice patterns of hand therapists in rehabilitating elbow fractures and/or dislocations.

STUDY DESIGN: Online survey research.

METHODS: A 51-item survey was developed by six certified hand therapists was distributed to active ASHT members to examine current rehabilitation practices for elbow fractures and/or dislocations. The anonymous, institutional review board-approved survey was administered via REDCap from April to June 2025 and assessed demographics, assessments, interventions, and orthosis use. Descriptive statistics and chi-square analyses were performed using REDCap, Excel, and SPSS, with significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Out of the total of 135 responses, ≤25% of hand therapist caseload was comprised of elbow fractures/dislocations. Most hand therapists reported therapy is typically initiated within 2 weeks and delivered twice weekly for a total of 16-20 visits. Nearly all respondents assessed active range of motion, edema, and activity of daily living status and administered the QuickDASH. Intervention strategies progressed initially from early immobilization and education to mobility, strengthening, and neuromuscular re-education. Orthosis utilization was primarily driven by range of motion limitations, with serial static orthoses most common. Experience level influenced visit volume, reliance on physician preference for orthoses, and discharge factors.

CONCLUSIONS: While traditional biomechanical approaches remain foundational, contemporary practice increasingly integrates biopsychosocial principles and advanced orthosis strategies, reflecting evolving clinical reasoning and knowledge translation across experience levels.

articles.title: Recovery of worsening renal function after acute heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Worsening renal function (WRF) is common during hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). However, the post-discharge trajectory of renal function in these patients remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the rate of WRF recovery after discharge and its prognostic significance.

METHODS: In a cohort of 2020 patients hospitalized for ADHF (TRI-AHF registry), serum creatinine was measured at admission, daily during hospitalization, and at 12 months after discharge. WRF was defined as a creatinine increase ≥0.3 mg/dL. Only patients who developed WRF during the index hospitalization were included. At the 12-month follow-up, WRF was classified as recovered if the change in creatinine from admission was <0.3 mg/dL, and persistent if ≥0.3 mg/dL. The primary endpoint was 5-year all-cause mortality after the 12-month creatinine reassessment.

RESULTS: During the study period, 331 patients (16%) experienced WRF. At 12 months, 157 (54%) had recovered WRF and 133 (46%) had persistent WRF. Older age, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and right ventricular dysfunction during hospitalization were independent predictors of persistent WRF. At 5-year follow-up after the 12-month assessment, recovered WRF was strongly associated with a lower risk of mortality compared with persistent WRF (adjusted HR=0.229, p < 0.001). The association between WRF recovery and improved survival was independent of prior chronic kidney disease and baseline creatinine, and appeared more pronounced in males than in females (p-int=0.034).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalized for ADHF who experienced WRF, 54% recovered renal function at 12 months. Recovery of WRF was associated with significantly better long-term survival compared with persistent WRF.

articles.title: Towards implementing genomic epidemiology for helminth control and elimination.
articles.abstract: Helminths, commonly referred to as parasitic worms, infect over a billion people and countless animals worldwide. Because they are major drivers of disease, understanding the epidemiology of helminth infections-what parasites are present, where they occur, and how they change over time-is key to controlling them. However, traditional diagnostic tools primarily measure infection status or intensity at a single time point, whereas effective control requires understanding changes over space and time, information these tools cannot directly capture. The increasing use of genomics is providing new, epidemiologically relevant insights into helminth population structure, transmission, zoonotic risk, and drug resistance. In this opinion article, we discuss the challenges and opportunities of applying genomics to helminth epidemiology, arguing that it will provide operationally meaningful information to support control efforts.

articles.title: Molecular imaging in adult spondylodiscitis: current evidence, clinical applications, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Adult spondylodiscitis is an infection of the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bodies that may progress to paravertebral extension, epidural involvement, spinal instability, sepsis, and neurological compromise. Because clinical symptoms and laboratory markers are often nonspecific, imaging is central to diagnosis, assessment of disease extent, biopsy planning, and selective evaluation of treatment response. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains the first-line anatomical technique for early marrow, disc, epidural, and paraspinal disease, while computed tomography (CT) is valuable for osseous destruction, instability, and biopsy guidance. Molecular imaging complements these modalities by depicting biological activity rather than structure alone. Fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG PET/CT) is the most established molecular technique, offering high diagnostic performance, whole-body evaluation for multifocal or metastatic infection, and support for management when MRI is contraindicated, equivocal, or difficult to interpret after surgery. Its main limitations are limited pathogen specificity, uptake in sterile inflammatory or reparative processes, heterogeneous interpretation criteria, and uncertain thresholds for treatment monitoring. Emerging approaches, including hybrid positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI), fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) tracers, pathogen-targeted radiopharmaceuticals, quantitative PET biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI), remain investigational and require prospective validation of diagnostic and clinical utility. This review summarizes current evidence, clinical applications, limitations, and future directions for molecular imaging in spondylodiscitis.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical value of quantitative Na[18F]F PET/CT parameters to monitor therapeutic response in patients with benign metabolic bone diseases: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT is increasingly used to evaluate treatment responses in metabolic bone diseases (MBDs), where conventional serum biomarkers and structural imaging fail to show local dynamic changes. The performance and utility of Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT in these diseases, however, has not been fully explored. We systematically evaluated the contemporary use of quantitative Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT for measuring MBD treatment responses.

METHODS: Current review was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261413536) and follows PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for clinical studies using quantitative Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT in MBDs. Risk of bias was assessed via QUADAS-2, ROBINS-I and QUIPS. Results were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies (n=14-72 patients; 358 total cases) met inclusion criteria, focusing on chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD, n=9 studies) and fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome (FD/MAS, n=4 studies). Two longitudinal studies evaluated therapeutic response: denosumab in FD/MAS yielded comparable reductions in total lesion metabolic activity across moderate (-64.9%) and high doses (-67.0%), while turnover-guided therapy in CKD-MBD significantly reduced bone kinetic flux (Ki). Remaining literature comprised cross-sectional and observational cohorts. Here, PET kinetic (Ki, FUR) and volumetric metrics (TV, TA, TLF) correlated strongly with bone formation rates and circulating biomarkers. Ki and background-adjusted uptake ratios (SUVR) discriminated bone turnover states with high accuracy (ROC AUC up to 0.98), outperforming serum parathyroid hormone in CKD-MBD. Reporting of reconstruction settings was highly variable; only one study explicitly noted EARL scanner accreditation and none documented compliance with EARL Standard 1 or 2. Risk of bias was primarily driven by small cohort sizes, attrition and unadjusted confounding.

CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT provides high diagnostic accuracy for tracking regional turnover and treatment response in benign MBDs. However, clinical adoption is hindered by a lack of harmonized EARL-compliant protocols, unstandardized outcome metrics and a reliance on small, unadjusted cohorts.

articles.title: Companion animal nuclear medicine: A translational evidence map for dogs and cats.
articles.abstract: Companion animals occupy an increasingly important clinical and societal space, with dogs and cats often managed as family members and receiving advanced diagnostic and therapeutic care. Many veterinary nuclear medicine procedures are adapted from human practice, while naturally occurring canine and feline diseases provide opportunities for comparative and translational insight. This review mapped and synthesised the literature on nuclear medicine imaging and radionuclide therapy in dogs and cats, with emphasis on clinically mature applications and relevance to human nuclear medicine. A PRISMA-aligned systematic evidence map with focused narrative synthesis were undertaken. MEDLINE via PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection were searched, with supplementary Google Scholar searching, reference-list screening and citation mining. Because of heterogeneity in species, indication, radiopharmaceutical, protocol, comparator and outcome reporting, formal meta-analysis was not performed. A total of 228 articles were included. The literature was predominantly imaging-focused, with 176 articles addressing imaging alone, 34 therapy alone and 18 both imaging and therapy. Feline nuclear medicine was dominated by thyroid disease, particularly thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism. Canine nuclear medicine was broader, including oncology PET/CT, osteosarcoma imaging and therapy, renal and hepatobiliary functional scintigraphy, portosystemic shunt imaging, neurology/behavioural imaging, thyroid carcinoma and radiosynoviorthesis. PET/CT was most prominent in canine oncology, while conventional scintigraphy remained important where functional information could not be replaced by structural imaging. Companion animal nuclear medicine is clinically useful and translationally relevant. Its most mature model is feline thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy, while its most dynamic future directions lie in canine oncology, molecular imaging and radiotheranostics. Closer collaboration between veterinary specialists and human nuclear medicine professionals may improve companion animal care while informing broader development of molecular imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy.

articles.title: Imaging of myositis: An overview and update.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are heterogeneous autoimmune disorders that affect skeletal muscle and may involve the skin, lungs, heart, gastrointestinal tract, or be associated with malignancy. Imaging supports phenotyping, biopsy targeting, assessment of disease burden, and monitoring. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains the principal modality for muscle assessment, depicting edema, fascial and subcutaneous inflammation, fatty replacement, and atrophy without ionizing radiation. Whole-body MRI maps disease distribution, whereas quantitative techniques, including Dixon fat-fraction imaging and T2 mapping, provide objective measures of activity and chronic damage. Ultrasound offers a portable, inexpensive adjunct, although operator dependence and limited standardization restrict comprehensive assessment. For nuclear medicine, 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT provides a complementary whole-body measure of metabolism, potentially identifying muscle inflammation, interstitial lung disease, other systemic manifestations, and occult malignancy in selected patients. Physiologic muscle uptake and heterogeneous acquisition and quantification protocols limit specificity and prevent universal PET thresholds. Hybrid PET/MRI combines metabolic and structural characterization, but evidence supporting routine use remains limited. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET is an emerging pathway-targeted approach with preliminary evidence in muscle and myositis-associated lung disease. This review summarizes imaging patterns across major myositis phenotypes, contrasts established and investigational uses of MRI, ultrasound, FDG PET/CT, PET/MRI, and emerging tracers, illustrates important mimics and pitfalls, and proposes a practical multimodality imaging approach.

articles.title: The PRIMA Model: A Heuristic Multilevel Framework for the Clinical Evaluation and Management of Bruxism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bruxism is a multifactorial masticatory muscle behaviour with complex mechanisms and heterogeneous clinical expression, ranging from physiological to potentially harmful depending on its consequences. Frameworks such as the STAB enable structured data collection but were not designed to guide the interpretation of findings when management is clinically warranted.

OBJECTIVE: To present the PRIMA model (Pattern-Responsive Inference Model for Multidomain Assessment of Bruxism), an exploratory, hypothesis-generating framework intended to support-not replace-structured clinical reasoning. PRIMA organises validated clinical inputs into an interpretable, multidomain map that may assist clinicians in orienting management decisions in cases where bruxism produces clinically significant consequences, without assuming causal inference or implying that every assessed case requires intervention.

METHODS: PRIMA follows a five-step modular architecture. Structured STAB items include predefined response options, each assigned a score through a three-tier heuristic logic that reflects domain-specific implication. Rather than forcing each item into a single domain, items are mapped through a weighted attribution scheme, in which an item may contribute to more than one Functional Domain according to a constrained, rule-based set of weights (primary weight to the domain of measurable expression, secondary weight to a literature-supported aetiological driver). These weighted item scores are aggregated into Functional Tendency Scores (FTS) for four Functional Domains. In parallel, contextual risk elements (Aggravating Factors) are weighted through the Aggravating Factor Index (AFI), a multidimensional metric that modulates the interpretation of domain expression. Where domain expression and contextual burden suggest clinical salience, proportionally stratified therapeutic options may be considered through a three-tier logic formalised as the Intra-Domain Therapeutic Sequencing Logic (ITSL).

RESULTS: The model provides a reproducible scaffold for stepwise reasoning. Illustrative, synthetically constructed cases are used to demonstrate the internal logic and transparency of the framework, not to provide evidence of clinical efficacy or validity.

CONCLUSIONS: PRIMA is proposed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating framework to support structured reasoning in the interpretation of bruxism and in the planning of management when clinically indicated. It is not a validated diagnostic algorithm or therapeutic protocol; it has not undergone prospective or outcome-based validation, and future clinical studies are required to determine its reliability, utility, and impact on diagnostic prioritisation and therapeutic decisions.

articles.title: Temporal Trends, Underuse, and Multilevel Factors Associated With Maximum-Dose Statin Therapy in Acute and Chronic Coronary Syndromes　- A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Study.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity or maximally tolerated statin therapy has robust evidence for secondary prevention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), and is strongly recommended in international guidelines. However, comprehensive real-world data on its use and associated factors remain limited.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using data from the JROAD-DPC database (2017-2022), we analyzed ACS and CCS patients who underwent revascularization and were discharged alive. We assessed temporal trends in lipid-lowering therapy and examined associated factors, including patient demographics, comorbidities, treatment strategies, and hospital structural characteristics, using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models. Among 358,570 patients with ACS and 392,821 with CCS, the use of maximum-dose statins increased from 8.6% in 2017 to 34.1% in 2022 in ACS and from 7.8% to 19.1% in CCS, but remained suboptimal. After multivariable adjustment, older age, underweight status, and coronary artery bypass grafting were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins in ACS. In CCS, older age, underweight status, and higher comorbidity burden were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins. Hospital structural factors, including a higher number of cardiologists, were also associated with a greater use of maximum-dose statins.

CONCLUSIONS: Maximum-dose statin use among ACS and CCS patients remains suboptimal in Japan. Multilevel factors contribute to this evidence-practice gap, underscoring the need for comprehensive interventions at multiple levels to reduce disparities in care delivery.

articles.title: The Major Iron Transporter DMT1 Promotes Renal Fibrosis by Activating Ferroptosis and Enforcing TGF-β1 Signaling in Renal Tubular Cells.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal fibrosis is a common pathological feature of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but effective therapies are still lacking. Ferroptosis has been increasingly associated with CKD; however, the iron-handling proteins that link ferroptotic stress to fibrotic signaling remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1) as a previously unrecognized regulatory factor that integrates iron metabolism, ferroptotic stress, and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling in tubular epithelial cells (TECs).

RESULTS: DMT1 expression was elevated in TECs from folic acid injection- or unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced mouse CKD models and in isolated primary TECs exposed to TGF-β1 or palmitic acid, accompanied by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) production. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of DMT1 in TECs significantly attenuated renal fibrosis, with reduced renal fibrosis area, decreased expression of profibrotic genes and markers, lower mtROS production, and restored fatty acid oxidation. DMT1 deficiency also attenuated lipid peroxidation, with reduced 4-HNE levels and lipid droplet deposition in mouse CKD models. Additionally, DMT1 deletion reduced tissue iron content, reversed ferroptosis-associated morphological changes in TECs, and restored tissue glutathione peroxidase-4 expression. Notably, DMT1 deletion reduced both total Smad2 and phosphorylated Smad2 induced by TGF-β1, consistent with suppression of the TGF-β1-Smad axis.

INNOVATION AND CONCLUSIONS: These findings support a model in which tubular DMT1 integrates iron overload, ferroptotic stress, and TGF-β1-Smad signaling during fibrotic progression in CKD. DMT1 functions as a signaling hub contributing to TGF-β1-Smad axis activation, although a direct causal chain from iron influx to transforming growth factor beta receptor 1 induction remains to be fully delineated. DMT1 inhibition may offer a tubular-selective therapeutic strategy for CKD. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

articles.title: Multifaceted Physiological Roles of Lipoproteins and Understanding Atherosclerosis: Crosstalk Between Lipoproteins and Bioactive Lipids.
articles.abstract: Traditional management of atherosclerosis focuses primarily on cholesterol and triglycerides; however, lipoproteins also transport bioactive lipids that critically regulate systemic inflammation and metabolic health. This review highlights the diverse physiological and clinical roles of apolipoproteins and bioactive lipids beyond classical lipid accumulation. First, we discuss how hepatic transporters NPC1L1 and ABCG5/8 modulate glucose metabolism and handle non-cholesterol lipids, including phytosterols. Second, we emphasize the apolipoprotein M (ApoM) and sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) axis. ApoM protects S1P from degradation and directly mediates the pleiotropic benefits of high-density lipoprotein (HDL), including anti-apoptotic, antithrombotic, and renoprotective effects. Third, reverse translational research utilizing genome-wide association studies identifies apolipoprotein D (ApoD) as a key anti-inflammatory modulator. Finally, clinical lipidomics underscores the importance of "minor" lysophospholipids, such as lysophosphatidylinositol and lysophosphatidylserine, alongside lysophosphatidic acid in the pathogenesis of acute coronary syndrome. Understanding the dynamic crosstalk between lipid transporters, apolipoproteins, and bioactive lipids provides novel mechanistic insights into cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, paving the way for innovative biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: IgE-Binding Components in Fungi and Parasites: From Infection Severity to Allergy and Allergy Protection: An EAACI Position Paper.
articles.abstract: Human exposure to fungi and parasites (helminths, protozoa and ticks) can lead to the development and/or exacerbation of allergic/atopic diseases due to the production of IgE antibodies to components from these organisms. However, some of these IgE-binding components are not currently listed in the official Allergen Nomenclature Database of the World Health Organization/International Union of Immunological Societies (WHO/IUIS) Allergen Nomenclature Sub-Committee. The aim of the Task Force (TF) BACALL (including members from this Sub-Committee and four additional groups/committees) was to identify in the literature (PubMed up to October 2025) potential allergens from fungi and parasites and their reported clinical relevance, for possible future inclusion in the WHO/IUIS Allergen Nomenclature Database according to Sub-Committee criteria. Forty-nine IgE-binding proteins from fungi and parasites were identified as potential allergen candidates. The IgE-binding oligosaccharide α-Gal was excluded because it is not proteinic, although it is associated with allergic reactions and anaphylaxis. Exposure to helminths outside the context of infection, such as ingestion of Anisakis-infected fish or vaccination against hookworms, can also elicit allergic reactions. The TF recommends that non-conventional routes of exposure be considered in the identification of new allergens, and that future studies assess the clinical relevance of new allergens identified by the TF in larger populations.

articles.title: Caecal perforation due to type I left-sided colonic atresia.
Early refractive and biometric changes in Irish children aged 6-7 years: a 12-month study.
articles.abstract:
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Longitudinal monitoring of refractive error and ocular biometry helps improve understanding of normal refractive development during childhood and may assist interpretation of ocular growth in clinical practice.

BACKGROUND: Childhood refractive development is characterised by coordinated changes in ocular biometry and refractive error, yet longitudinal data describing refractive and biometric development during the early school years in European populations remain limited.

METHODS: The Child Eye Health Study was a longitudinal cohort study including schoolchildren in Ireland aged 6-7 years old. Participants underwent cycloplegic autorefraction at baseline and 12 months and ocular biometry at baseline, 6 months and 12 months. Changes in spherical equivalent refraction and axial length were assessed using descriptive statistics and linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: A total of 134 participants were examined at baseline, of whom 111 completed the 12-month follow-up. Mean axial length increased by 0.22 ± 0.10 mm per year, while spherical equivalent refraction decreased by -0.11 ± 0.38 D per year, representing a small reduction in hyperopia. Axial elongation was moderately negatively correlated with refractive change (r =  -0.55, p < 0.001). The incidence of categorical myopia (≤-0.50 D) remained low (1.0%). Individual participants exhibited bidirectional movement between refractive categories over 12 months, alongside a small reduction in mean hyperopia.

CONCLUSION: Irish children aged 6-7 years demonstrated measurable axial elongation and a small reduction in mean hyperopia over 12 months, while the incidence of categorical myopia remained low. These findings provide contemporary longitudinal data describing refractive and biometric development in Irish schoolchildren. Longer follow-up is required to determine whether these early changes are associated with subsequent myopia onset.

Large language models in rheumatology: applications, methodological quality and clinical translation - a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To map applications of large language models (LLMs) in rheumatology and evaluate the methodological quality and clinical translation of the evidence.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science were searched from inception to 13 July 2026 for primary studies of LLMs in rheumatology. Two reviewers independently screened records and analysed data. Each study was assigned to one application domain and to the highest level of a review-derived translational maturity framework. Risk of bias was assessed with the Alberta Quality Assessment Tool: Risk of Bias (AQAT:RoB; worst-item rule), where human evaluation of free-text answers was reported; findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: 93 studies were included, 79 (84.9%) from 2025 or 2026. Patient education (39, 41.9%) and clinical decision support (38, 40.9%) dominated. Accuracy in clinical decision support was strongly task-dependent, with medians of 90.9% for structured diagnostic tasks and 40.0% for open-ended differential diagnosis (best-performing model per study). Patient-facing output had a median Flesch-Kincaid grade of 12.2; none of the 13 readability studies met the recommended sixth-grade target. 22 studies (23.7%) used real-world clinical data, mostly retrospectively; only four (4.3%) evaluated an LLM prospectively in a clinical workflow. Prompts were fully reported in 59.1% of studies, and answer stability was tested in 19.4%. Among the 68 studies amenable to AQAT:RoB assessment, five (7.4%) were at low risk of bias.

CONCLUSIONS: LLM research in rheumatology is expanding rapidly but remains dominated by prompt-response benchmarks with surrogate outcomes, incomplete reporting and, among AQAT:RoB-assessable studies, predominantly unclear or high risk of bias. Whether LLMs improve rheumatology care remains unresolved; prospective evaluations with patient-relevant endpoints are required.

articles.title: Tirzepatide Use Resulted in Clinically Meaningful Weight Reduction in Individuals With Obesity or Overweight: 12-Month Real-World Results.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study assessed the real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in commercially insured individuals without diabetes, eligible for obesity medications (OMs), including glucagon like-peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA)-naïve individuals (i.e., no GLP-1 RA prescription during the 12-month pre-index period) and GLP-1 RA-experienced individuals.

METHODS: This retrospective, observational cohort study used Optum's de-identified Market Clarity Data (Optum Market Clarity). Adults with ≥ 1 prescription claim for tirzepatide between November 2023 and March 2024, with continuous medical/pharmacy enrollment for ≥ 12 months pre-index and post-index and available pre- and post-index data were included. Baseline demographics, clinical characteristics, and treatment effectiveness (change from baseline in weight, body mass index, and cardiometabolic risk factors) were assessed among OM-eligible individuals who were persistent on tirzepatide for ≥ 12 months.

RESULTS: The GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced cohorts included 230 individuals (mean age: 49.5 years, 72.2% female) and 123 individuals (mean age: 48.9 years, 81.3% female), respectively, who were persistent on tirzepatide for 12 months with documented pre- and post-index weight measurements. At baseline, more than 85% of individuals in each cohort had ≥ 1 obesity-related complication, most commonly dyslipidemia, hypertension, and prediabetes. At 12 months post-index, the GLP-1 RA-naïve cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 19.3%, while the GLP-1 RA-experienced cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 13.1%.

CONCLUSIONS: After 12 months of persistent tirzepatide use, individuals experienced clinically meaningful weight reduction, comparable to outcomes reported in clinical trials. These real-world findings were observed both in GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced individuals.

articles.title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada's loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status.

DESIGN: Descriptive analysis of the cohort of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario's public health surveillance system during the outbreak period: epidemiological week of 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025.

SETTING: Ontario, Canada.

PARTICIPANTS: Individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during the outbreak period.

EXPOSURE: Exposure to measles virus associated with the Ontario outbreak and related transmission chains.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Demographic characteristics, vaccination status, admission to hospital, complications, pregnancy associated outcomes, mortality, and evidence of international spread based on measles virus genotyping and sequencing. Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition incorporating epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries.

RESULTS: The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population. Among the 2377 cases, approximately three quarters of cases (n=1736, 73.0%) occurred in individuals aged 19 years or younger, 2121 (89.2%) were unvaccinated, and 97 (4.1%) had unknown vaccination status. The outbreak was associated with 166 (7%) admissions to hospital, 13 (<1%) admissions to intensive care unit, 51 (2.1%) infections during pregnancy, 10 (<1%) congenital measles infections, one (<1%) case of encephalitis, and one (<1%) infant death. Sequencing identified a novel N450 distinct sequence identifier that was subsequently detected in countries including the United States of America, Mexico, and the Netherlands. The outbreak strain was designated a World Health Organization named strain (MVs/Ontario.CAN/47.24).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscore the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks. This outbreak shows the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of long standing immunity gaps within interconnected communities across the Americas and the population-level protection that limited broader community transmission.

articles.title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test the efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid versus sham injection for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.

DESIGN: Single centred, participant and assessor masked, three arm randomised controlled trial (Inject trial).

SETTING: Community.

PARTICIPANTS: From 5 December 2019 and 24 July 2022, 192 adults (18 years or older) diagnosed with midportion Achilles tendinopathy were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63), or high volume injection with corticosteroid (n=65).

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were allocated to sham injection (2-3 mL 0.5% bupivacaine hydrochloride), high volume injection with corticosteroid (50 mL saline and 0.5% bupivacaine with 25 mg hydrocortisone in the first 10 mL), or high volume injection with no corticosteroid (same solution but without hydrocortisone). They received the same exercise programme, education, and activity modification advice.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was pain and disability using the validated VISA-A and the primary endpoint was at 52 weeks. The economic outcome was cost per quality-adjusted life-years from a societal perspective.

RESULTS: VISA-A data were obtained from 181 (94%) of 192 participants at 12 months. No clear differences were noted between sham and high volume injection either with (-3.5 (98.33% confidence interval -12.0 to 5.0)) or without corticosteroid (4.0 (-4.2 to 12.3)), and between the two injections (-7.5 (-15.3 to 0.3)), at 12 months. The point estimate was closest to the target difference for the comparison between injections and favoured the arm without steroid. The only differences observed on VISA-A at intermediate time points were a benefit for high volume with corticosteroid versus sham at six weeks (9.2 (1.5 to 16.9)) but worse outcomes for high volume injection with corticosteroid versus high volume injection with no corticosteroid at 26 weeks (-8.6 (-16.4 to -0.7)). The health economic analysis found high volume injection with corticosteroid to be less costly than the sham with similar effectiveness based on quality-adjusted life-years (>0.90 probability of being cost effective at $AUD50 000 and $100 000 willingness-to-pay thresholds). No serious trial related adverse events were recorded.

CONCLUSION: High volume injections with or without corticosteroids did not improve pain or disability compared with sham at 12 months. Although high volume injections with corticosteroid showed short term clinical benefit and potential reduction in healthcare costs over a year, they were associated with worse longer term clinical outcomes. The clinical data do not support routine use for high volume injections with corticosteroid for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12619001455156.

articles.title: Crosstalk along the gut-liver axis in liver disease: Clinical and mechanistic aspects.
articles.abstract: The gut and liver are anatomically and physiologically interconnected, forming a dynamic axis that plays a central role in the pathogenesis of many liver diseases. Gut-derived factors can influence hepatic injury, inflammation, and fibrosis, acting both as disease modifiers and, in some cases, as primary drivers of aetiology. Conversely, liver-derived factors including bile acids shape microbial ecology, epithelial barrier function, and intestinal immune homeostasis. In this review, we provide an overview of the clinical and mechanistic aspects of the gut-liver axis in hepatology. Using autoimmune, metabolic, and toxic hepatobiliary disorders as model conditions, we highlight recent advances in understanding how intestinal permeability, microbiota composition, and immune signalling contribute to disease initiation and progression. Emphasis is placed on the bidirectional nature of gut-liver interactions and their implications for disease stratification, prevention, and therapy. Finally, we identify key knowledge gaps and outline priorities for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

articles.title: Harnessing Clinical Characteristics to Identify High-Risk of Drug-induced QTc Prolongation in Hospitalized Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-induced QTc-prolongation is a major concern for developing ventricular arrhythmias, which may eventually lead to sudden cardiac death. Identifying high-risk patients is essential to support healthcare providers in handling automatically generated alerts in clinical practice. The aim of study was to develop clinical data-driven machine learning methods to predict drug-induced QTc-prolongation.

METHODS: Inpatients with paired electrocardiograms were enrolled from Southwest Hospital (2015-2022). Six machine learning (ML) algorithms were developed to predict drug-induced QTc prolongation (ΔQTc > 60 ms). Model performance was evaluated using an internal test set and an independent external validation cohort. Model interpretations were recognized by feature importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) methods. Finally, we benchmarked the ML models against the traditional Tisdale risk score.

RESULTS: A total of 2451 participants were recruited, of whom 292 developed QTc-prolongation, while 150 patients from a separate center served as the external validation cohort. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model achieved the best performance with recall of 0.884 and AUC of 0.814 in internal test set. During external validation, the AUC remained robust at 0.864, although recall declined to 0.650. SHAP analysis identified baseline QTc and QT intervals, inflammation, high-risk drugs, and hypertension are the primary drivers of model predictions.

CONCLUSIONS: The XGBoost algorithm provides a highly sensitive framework for predicting drug-induced QTc prolongation. Integrating this ML tool with identified clinical drivers into hospital decision support systems would facilitate the optimization of treatment strategies and early ECG monitoring strategies.

articles.title: Towards a digital twin for precision diabetes care: a phenotypic mapping and virtual representation of a person living with type 1 diabetes in the SFDT1 study.
articles.abstract: T1D is clinically heterogeneous, yet its key parameters are still largely interpreted in isolation. As a first step towards developing a digital twin for T1D, we aimed to build a phenotypic mapping and virtual representation of a person living with T1D (PwT1D) usable at the individual level. We analysed baseline data from 2,187 adults with T1D in the SFDT1 cohort using Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). Twenty-five sociodemographic, clinical, biochemical, and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) variables were used to construct a low-dimensional structure. Structural reproducibility and individual projection were assessed in an unseen set of 235 participants. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) risks were computed with the Steno T1 Risk Engine. We identified seven interpretable sub-phenotypes, ranging from well-controlled profiles to profiles characterized by poor glycaemic control, metabolic abnormalities, social vulnerability and a high burden of micro- and macrovascular complications. An independently fitted map for the additional participants showed a similar overall branching structure and comparable clinical patterns, and individual projection was accurate (R² 0.85-0.98). A multilingual application enables exploration of the phenotypic map, individual projection, and estimation of Steno risk scores. This phenotypic mapping and virtual representation capture clinically meaningful heterogeneity and let care teams locate and explore individual profiles. It provides the foundation for an AI-enabled digital twin an interpretable virtual representation that integrates a person's clinical, biological, glycaemic, and social profile and supports individualized decisions - and a practical clinical decision-support tool for precision diabetes care.

articles.title: SCN2B Drives Depression-like Phenotypes in Mice by Suppressing BDNF Signaling via Its Intracellular Domain NICD.
articles.abstract: The rising global burden of depression necessitates novel mechanistic insights and therapeutic targets. Voltage-gated sodium channel β2-subunit (Navβ2, coded by SCN2B) has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, yet its role in depression remains unexplored. Here, we identify SCN2B as a previously unrecognized driver of depression-like pathophysiology. Using SCN2B-overexpressing (SCN2B-OV) mice across different ages (1, 12, and 20 months) and CRISPR- engineered Navβ2V173A,V175K mice with selective reduction of the Navβ2 intracellular domain (NICD), we combined behavioral phenotyping, electrophysiology, neurotransmitter profiling, and molecular analyses, with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) as an environmental challenge. SCN2B-OV mice exhibited accelerated depression-like phenotypes, including anhedonia (sucrose preference 52.42% reduction, P<0.05), behavioral despair (forced swim test immobility 67.42% increase, P<0.05), and cognitive deficits (Y-maze alternation 50.90% reduction, P<0.05), independent of natural aging. Electrophysiologically, SCN2B overexpression induced a striking prefrontal-hippocampal imbalance: prefrontal cortex (PFC) became hyperexcitable (glutamate release increased by 64.7%; sEPSC amplitude increased 2.05-fold, P<0.05), whereas the hippocampus showed synaptic suppression (GABA release reduced by 32.65%; sIPSC frequency reduced by 66.67%, P<0.05). Mechanistically, SCN2B overexpression suppressed BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/AKT signaling axis (BDNF reduced by 53.17%; p-TrkB reduced by 63.62%, P<0.05), accompanied by decreased synaptic proteins (PSD95 43.45%, synapsin I 40.31%, P<0.05). Remarkably, NICD-reduced Navβ2V173A,V175K mice were fully resistant to CUMS-induced behavioral and neurotransmitter deficits, establishing NICD as a critical mediator of stress vulnerability. Collectively, these findings unravel a causal pathway in which SCN2B overexpression drives NICD-dependent suppression of BDNF signaling, leading to region-specific excitatory/inhibitory imbalance, synaptic disintegration, and depression-like phenotypes. Targeting Navβ2 proteolysis to block NICD generation may thus represent a novel therapeutic strategy for mood disorders.

articles.title: Functional consequences of acanthocephalan infection in Homarus americanus and advances in understanding of parasite-associated changes in lobster immunity.
articles.abstract: Profilicollis botulus is an acanthocephalan parasite with larval stages developing in arthropod intermediate hosts and adult stages maturing in vertebrate definitive hosts, typically seabirds. Despite its widespread occurrence in coastal ecosystems, the physiological and molecular consequences of P. botulus infection in the American lobster (Homarus americanus) remain unclear. In this exploratory observational study, we combined whole-animal respirometry with hepatopancreas RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to characterize physiological and transcriptional differences between naturally infected and uninfected lobsters. Infected lobsters exhibited significantly lower mass-specific oxygen consumption than uninfected individuals (28.51 ± 1.87 vs 35.02 ± 1.49 mg O₂ kg-1 h-1). Exploratory transcriptomic analysis of a limited number of individuals (four infected and three uninfected) identified 324 differentially expressed genes (FDR < 0.05), including 232 downregulated and 92 upregulated transcripts in infected lobsters. Several transcripts associated with glycolysis and related metabolic processes showed higher expression in infected individuals. Conversely, lower transcript abundance was observed for multiple genes associated with innate immune functions, including lectin-type pattern recognition receptors, antimicrobial peptides (including anti-lipopolysaccharide factors), and components of the prophenoloxidase and coagulation systems, antioxidant enzymes, acute-phase proteins, and crustacean hyperglycemic hormone. Together, these findings associate reduced aerobic metabolism with lower expression of multiple innate immune-related transcripts in the hepatopancreas, a pattern that may be compatible with a stabilized host-parasite interaction and altered energetic allocation during parasitism. However, given the observational design and limited transcriptomic sample size, these interpretations remain hypotheses rather than demonstrated mechanisms. Together with other studies of parasite infections in crustaceans, our findings suggest that host responses to acanthocephalan infection may be host-dependent and influenced by parasite biology, tissue specificity, and host physiological condition. Further studies incorporating larger sample sizes, controlled infection experiments, and functional measurements are needed to determine whether these associations reflect direct effects of infection or other host-related and environmental factors.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Indices of Right Ventricular Function are Associated with Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Heart Failure Subtypes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) is critical to the progression of heart failure (HF), the prevalence and prognostic implications of RVD across HF subtypes remains poorly understood.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize differences in hemodynamic indices of RVD among patients with HF with preserved (HFpEF, EF≥50%) vs reduced (HFrEF, EF<50%) ejection fraction and examine associations of RVD with longitudinal clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We identified patients with prevalent HF undergoing clinically indicated right heart catheterization at Massachusetts General Hospital (2005-2016). We examined three RV hemodynamic indices: right atrial to wedge pressure ratio (RA/PCWP), RV stroke work index (RVSWI), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). We used multivariable Cox models to examine the association of each index with HF hospitalizations (HFH) and death.

RESULTS: Of 2,062 patients, 1,242 (60%) had HFrEF and 820 (40%) had HFpEF; 56% of individuals with HFrEF and 53% with HFpEF met at least one hemodynamic criterion for RVD. In HFrEF, lower PAPi was associated with greater risk of HFH (HR 0.84 [0.77, 0.92]), and higher RVSWI was associated with greater risk of death (HR 1.17, [1.07, 1.27], all p<0.001). By contrast, only higher RA/PCWP was associated with greater risk of death in HFpEF (HR 1.11 (1.00, 1.22); p=0.046).

CONCLUSIONS: Hemodynamic RVD is common in both HFrEF and HFpEF, and hemodynamic measures of RV function are associated with greater risk of adverse outcomes. Importantly, the prognostic value of RV indices varied by HF subtype, highlighting key differences in the role of RVD in HFrEF vs HFpEF.

articles.title: NMI suppresses BEFV replication and is degraded by BEFV-induced NIX-dependent selective autophagy.
articles.abstract: N-Myc interactor (NMI) functions in various viral infections and serves as a regulatory component of innate immune signaling, its function during bovine ephemeral fever virus (BEFV) infection remains to be elucidated. Herein, we establish that NMI attenuates BEFV replication in BHK-21 and MDBK cells, as evidenced by diminished viral nucleoprotein gene expression and viral loads in NMI-overexpressing cells, whereas NMI depletion significantly enhances viral replication. Further analyses reveal that NMI augments type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway activation via the transcriptional induction of Ifnb and downstream effectors, namely Isg15, Ifitm3, Mx1, Isg54 and Isg56. At the molecular level, NMI engages with IRF3, facilitating its phosphorylation and subsequent nuclear import, consequently potentiating IFN-I-mediated immune activation. Notably, BEFV infection counteracts this antiviral defense by inducing autophagy, resulting in time-dependent autophagic degradation of NMI. Further analysis demonstrates that BEFV-mediated NMI degradation occurs selectively through the autophagy receptor NIP3-like protein X (NIX), as pharmacological inhibition of autophagy or NIX knockout abrogates NMI degradation, while NIX overexpression accelerates NMI turnover. Collectively, our results delineate a novel molecular mechanism whereby NMI restricts BEFV replication through the IRF3-IFN axis, while BEFV evades this restriction via NIX-mediated selective autophagy. These observations furnish critical insights into NMI function and the dynamic crosstalk between host antiviral defenses and viral immune evasion mechanisms, which may lay the groundwork for the rational design of antiviral therapeutics.

articles.title: P2X7 receptor-mediated inflammatory and ionic remodeling promotes atrial fibrillation in diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet the mechanisms by which diabetic metabolic stress promotes atrial arrhythmogenesis remain incompletely understood. Recent evidence suggests that purinergic signaling-driven sterile inflammation plays an important role in cardiac remodeling. This study aimed to investigate the role of the ATP-gated purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) in DM-associated AF and to explore its underlying mechanisms.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Rats were randomly assigned to four groups: control (Con), diabetes mellitus (DM), P2X7R overexpression in controls (Con+P2X7), and P2X7R knockdown in diabetic rats (DM + P2X7 KD), with gene manipulation achieved using AAV9-cTnT vectors. AF susceptibility, atrial structural and electrical remodeling were systematically evaluated using electrophysiological studies, optical mapping, patch-clamp recordings, and molecular analyses. DM markedly increased AF inducibility and duration, accompanied by enhanced sympathetic nerve activity and activation of P2X7R-related inflammatory signaling. Compared with controls, DM atria exhibited pronounced interstitial fibrosis, connexin remodeling, delayed atrial activation, slowed conduction velocity, and increased conduction heterogeneity. Atrial P2X7R overexpression in control rats recapitulated key arrhythmogenic features, whereas P2X7R KD in diabetic rats significantly attenuated atrial remodeling and reduced AF susceptibility, without altering the diabetes-induced increase in sympathetic activity. At the cellular level, P2X7R selectively modulated INa, ICa,L, and IKur while relatively preserving Ito, and was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and disturbed Ca2+ homeostasis, characterized by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, increased cytosolic Ca2+ signals, and reduced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake.

CONCLUSION: P2X7R-mediated inflammatory and mitochondrial signaling contribute to diabetic atrial remodeling and AF susceptibility. Targeting P2X7R may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing AF in diabetes.

articles.title: Enhanced inhalation delivery of ROS-responsive methylprednisolone dimer nanoparticles via hydrogen-oxygen carrier gas for efficient treatment of acute lung injury with CFD-simulated pulmonary deposition.
articles.abstract: Distal lung delivery remains a key bottleneck for inhaled therapy in severe pulmonary disease. We developed a hydrogen-oxygen mixture (H2/O2 mixture, 2:1 v/v) gas-assisted nebulization platform to deliver ROS-responsive, self-assembled methylprednisolone dimer nanoparticles (MP2-TK NPs). MP2-TK NPs were stable during nebulization and selectively released drug under ROS-rich conditions. Compared with air, H2/O2 mixture improved NGI-assessed aerosol deposition and artificial mucus penetration. CFD simulations further supported enhanced distal deposition, particularly for clinically respirable droplets (1-5 μm). In an LPS-induced acute lung injury mouse model, H2/O2-assisted nebulization increased pulmonary distribution and small-airway localization of MP2-TK NPs, leading to reduced bronchoalveolar lavage cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), total cell counts, and protein levels. H2/O2 mixture inhalation alone also showed anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with hydrogen's antioxidant effects. This strategy couples carrier-gas engineering with ROS-responsive nanomedicine to enhance deep-lung delivery and therapeutic efficacy in acute lung injury.

articles.title: CCD052, a novel small-molecule agent targeting Clostridioides difficile.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) remains a significant global public health challenge. CCD052, a novel bile acid analog containing an aminonitrothiazole moiety, was assessed for antibacterial activity in vitro and in vivo.

METHODS: Its inhibitory effect on pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) was determined. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were tested against ATCC-BAA-1870, CD630, and 115 clinical isolates. Minimum bactericidal concentrations, time-kill kinetics, post-antibiotic effects (PAEs), spore germination and sporulation, and related gene expression were determined using representative strains. Using a mouse model, the effects of CCD052 and vancomycin were compared for diarrhea, histological damage, fecal spore shedding, gut microbiota, and fecal bile acid metabolites.

RESULT: CCD052 notably inhibited PFOR. All strains were highly susceptible (MIC range 0.03-0.25 mg/L). CCD052 exhibited rapid, thorough bactericidal effect within 2 hours, with PAE >20 hours at 32 × MIC. CCD052 inhibited spore germination when ≥0.06 mg/L, and may inhibit sporulation by significantly downregulating sigH, spoOA, spoIIR, and spoIIID (p < 0.05). In CCD052-treated mice, no death, no diarrhea, and no significant weight loss or colon inflammation were observed; fecal spore shedding was reduced even after medication withdrawal; Muribaculaceae, associated with reduction of C. difficile colonization, was abundant in the gut; chenodeoxycholic acid and ursodeoxycholic acid increased, while deoxycholic acid decreased, facilitating inhibition of spore germination.

CONCLUSION: CCD052 is a promising anti-C. difficile candidate with potent bactericidal activity and inhibitory effects on spore germination and sporulation. Its ability to protect mice from mortality, preserve gut microbiota, and balance bile acid metabolism supports further preclinical development.

articles.title: Cross-kingdom metabolic regulation by a symbiotic virus: Transient viral microRNAs coordinate host metabolism and immune responses.
articles.abstract: Symbiotic microorganisms and endogenous viruses play fundamental roles in shaping host physiology, yet the non-coding RNA-mediated mechanisms underlying viral-driven metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate a novel mechanism of cross-kingdom metabolic manipulation mediated by symbiotic viral microRNAs. Using the tobacco cutworm Spodoptera litura, its endoparasitoid wasp Snellenius manilae, and the wasp-associated bracovirus SmBV as a model system, we identified two virus-derived microRNAs, SmBV-miR-2733 and SmBV-miR-3772, that target the host lipogenic genes encoding AGPAT and lipin, leading to the suppression of glycerolipid biosynthesis and reduced lipid accumulation. Functional analyses revealed that these symbiotic viral miRNAs concurrently attenuate host innate immune signaling pathways (Toll and JAK/STAT) and cellular encapsulation, establishing a mechanistic link between viral metabolic coercion and host immunomodulation. Crucially, this viral microRNA-mediated regulation is transient and highly dynamic; miRNA expression declines during later stages of infection, coinciding with an intermediate recovery of host lipogenic gene expression and lipid reserves, which may help sustain the developing parasitoids. Prolonged experimental maintenance of viral miRNAs disrupted host energetic homeostasis and compromised symbiotic success, underscoring the evolutionary necessity of temporally coordinated metabolic regulation. Comparative genomic analysis identified miR-2733- and miR-3772-like candidate loci with miRNA-precursor-like structures that are unevenly distributed across related bracovirus lineages. Together, our findings provide significant mechanistic insights into how symbiotic viral effectors post-transcriptionally rewire host metabolic and immune networks, offering a broader conceptual framework for understanding homeostasis in diverse host-microbe symbioses.

articles.title: Procedure-specific bleeding risk assessment: a multidisciplinary expert consensus companion to the 2026 periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability.

OBJECTIVE: To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.

METHODS: A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel.

RESULTS: Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied.

CONCLUSION: This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

articles.title: Continued CagriSema treatment preserves weight loss by reducing energy intake and maintaining energy expenditure in rats.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: CagriSema (CS), combining the amylin receptor agonist cagrilintide with the glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist semaglutide, is being developed for obesity and type 2 diabetes. We quantified CS effects on energy balance during initial treatment, weight maintenance, and after discontinuation.

METHODS: Male diet-induced obese rats underwent indirect calorimetry during 6 weeks of treatment and for 4 weeks after discontinuation. Treatments were a) vehicle, b) CS, c) calorie-restriction to match CS body weight loss (weight matched, WM), and d) calorie-restriction to match CS food intake (pair-feeding, PF).

RESULTS: CS effects occurred in four phases. During days 1-10 (Phase I), CS induced rapid weight loss mainly through reduced energy intake (EI), while energy expenditure (EE) was relatively preserved. EE was significantly lower in WM rats, consistent with metabolic adaptation. During days 11-42 (Phase II), reduced body weight was maintained in the CS, WM, and PF groups, and respiratory exchange ratio converged across groups, indicating metabolic steady state had been reached. Reduced EI and preserved total EE respectively explained 86% and 14% of CS weight loss efficacy. Maintained resting/sleeping EE contributed to the total EE preservation. Treatment discontinuation (days 43-52, Phase III) caused hyperphagia and rapid weight regain. During days 53-68 (Phase IV), all groups reached metabolic steady state and weight gain returned to pretreatment rates. Body weight plateaued in approximately half the time needed to reach metabolic steady state, and metabolic adaptation reversed within ∼7 days after discontinuation.

CONCLUSIONS: By persistently lowering EI and attenuating metabolic adaptation, CS enables sustained weight loss in rats; however, the reversal after treatment cessation suggests that chronic pharmacological therapy may be required to maintain weight loss.

articles.title: Regular exercise augments gut-brain communication and visceral feedback control of appetite.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Regular exercise is widely accepted to support long-term body weight management; however, the neurobiological adaptations that contribute to the beneficial effects of habitual physical activity beyond increases in energy expenditure per se remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether regular exercise alters gut-brain communication and visceral feedback control of feeding.

METHODS: Mice were subjected to regular voluntary wheel running. Energy expenditure and feeding were assessed under basal conditions and following an overnight fast. Nutrients were delivered directly into the stomach by intragastric infusion. Brain-wide responses to intragastric nutrient delivery were assessed using positron emission tomography (PET). Single-cell sequencing and histological analyses were used to determine nutrient-responsive neuronal populations in the caudal brainstem. Genetic associations with body weight were evaluated using GWAS data.

RESULTS: Intragastric nutrient delivery suppressed feeding more strongly in exercising mice. Brain-wide PET revealed enhanced responses to intragastric nutrients in various brain regions. Single-cell sequencing identified several nutrient-responsive caudal brainstem populations, including a previously unrecognized population marked by expression of fibrinogen C domain containing 1 (FIBCD1). Regular exercise selectively enhanced the nutrient-evoked activation of FIBCD1 neurons. Histological analyses demonstrate that FIBCD1 neurons are also present in the human brainstem, and GWAS data suggest a potential relevance of this neuron population to body-weight regulation.

CONCLUSIONS: Regular exercise enhances behavioral and brain responses to intragastric nutrient delivery and sensitizes FIBCD1 neurons in the brainstem of mice. These findings reveal an exercise-associated adaptation of gut-brain communication that may contribute to improved matching of caloric intake to energy expenditure.

articles.title: Acute Upper Limb Ischaemia: A 5-Year Prospective Single-Centre Experience from Northern Morocco.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute upper limb ischaemia (AULI) is an uncommon vascular emergency associated with a risk of limb loss and functional impairment. Contemporary data from North Africa remain scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, aetiological factors, management strategies, and outcomes of patients presenting with AULI in a tertiary vascular centre in Northern Morocco.

METHODS: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted including consecutive patients treated for acute non-traumatic upper limb ischaemia between January 2021 and May 2026. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, clinical presentation, imaging findings, aetiology, treatment strategies, and outcomes were prospectively recorded. The primary outcome was limb loss. Secondary outcomes included clinical improvement, reintervention, and mortality. All outcomes were assessed during the index hospitalisation and up to one month after discharge.

RESULTS: Forty-three patients were included (mean age 59.8 +/- 13.2 years; 76.7% women). Delayed presentation was common, with 53.5% of patients presenting more than 24 hours after symptom onset and 39.6% presenting after more than 72 hours. Rutherford class IIb and III ischaemia accounted for 41.9% and 11.6% of cases, respectively. Cardioembolic disease was the leading aetiology (34.9%), while cancer-associated thrombosis and thrombophilic or inflammatory disorders were important non-cardioembolic causes. The brachial artery was the most frequently involved vessel (74.4%). Thromboembolectomy was performed in 72.1% of patients. Clinical improvement was achieved in 81.4% of cases. Secondary intervention was required in 7.0%. Overall limb loss occurred in four patients (9.3%), and one patient died (2.3%). Rutherford III ischaemia was significantly associated with limb loss.

CONCLUSION: AULI in Northern Morocco is characterised by delayed presentation, advanced ischaemic severity, and a substantial burden of cancer-associated and thrombophilic disorders. Despite these challenges, surgical thromboembolectomy achieved satisfactory limb-salvage and functional outcomes. Early recognition and prompt referral remain essential to prevent irreversible ischaemic injury.

articles.title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD).

METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs 6.6% vs 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend= 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short- and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Guideline-to-Practice Gap in Ankle-Brachial Index Screening Among Inpatients with Newly Documented Lower Extremity Wounds.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to two hospitals within a single urban academic health system in 2025 with a new lower extremity wound documented in nursing wound flowsheets. Recent screening was defined as ABI testing performed during the index hospitalization or within one year prior to admission. Patient and admission characteristics were compared by screening status, and logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with screening. Wound location and noninvasive vascular testing results were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 2244 inpatients with newly documented lower extremity wounds, 343 patients (15.3%) were screened with ABIs. Screened patients were younger (65 vs 69 years; P<.001) and had a higher burden of atherosclerotic or diabetic comorbidities. After multivariable adjustment, pre-existing PAD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.79; P<.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR, 2.72; P<.001), and end-stage renal disease (aOR, 1.60; P=.021) were independently associated with ABI screening. Female sex was associated with lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.73; P=.045). Compared with medicine or hospitalist services, admission to general surgery/acute care surgery (aOR, 2.15; P=.002) and vascular surgery (aOR, 4.29; P<.001) was associated with higher odds of screening. Screening proportions were 23.6% for toe wounds, 20.6% for ankle/Achilles wounds, 19.9% for foot/heel wounds, and 12.8% for lower leg wounds. Among screened patients with available measurements, 50.4% had an abnormal ABI, 63.8% had an abnormal TBI, and 69.0% had at least one abnormal ABI or TBI.

CONCLUSION: PAD screening was performed in a minority of hospitalized patients with newly documented lower extremity wounds and was associated with recognized vascular risk factors and admitting service. Abnormal physiologic testing was common among screened patients. Standardized wound-triggered screening pathways may reduce missed opportunities for vascular evaluation.

articles.title: Long-term Outcomes of Primary Femoropopliteal Stents: A Retrospective Multi-Centre Experience and the Role for a Doppler Ultrasound Surveillance Programme.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularisation is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating re-intervention, remains a challenge. This study performs a retrospective outcomes analysis to suggest which patient populations may benefit from a Doppler ultrasound (DUS) surveillance programme in improving primary patency and amputation-free survival following femoropopliteal stenting in patients with PAD.

METHODS: A multicentre, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients who underwent femoropopliteal stenting between January 2015 and April 2023 within a vascular network with six hospital sites. Data were collected from 238 stents in 220 patients. Demographics, stent characteristics, and surveillance protocols were analysed. Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models were used to identify risk factors for primary patency and amputation-free survival. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated for both outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to compare outcomes between supra-popliteal and infra-popliteal stents.

RESULTS: A total of 238 stents were inserted in a population comprised of 28.6% females, with the median age of 72.5 +/- 11.5 years. In 74.8% (178) of cases, patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Primary patency rates at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years were 90%, 67.7%, 51.2%, 26.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. The average amputation-free survival was 3.2 years. Cox regression identified CLTI (hazard ratio, 6.37, p = .001), type 1 diabetes mellitus (hazard ratio, 3.16, p = .006), and female sex (hazard ratio, 1.69, P = .037) as significant predictors of loss of primary patency. Drug-eluting stents and diabetes were associated with poorer amputation-free survival.

CONCLUSIONS: The study illustrates a cohort of high-risk patients, particularly those with CLTI and diabetes, who may benefit from future enrolment in an enhanced DUS surveillance programme targeted to improve long-term outcomes. However, further research is required to explore the clinical-effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and implementation feasibility of such programmes in clinical practice.

articles.title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: An Arterial-Wall Dimension Uncharacterized in Current Limb Staging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on haemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging.

METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS).
