RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis. An elevated ankle-brachial index is uninterpretable, and a reference-range value does not exclude peripheral artery disease. Across cohorts of differing design and definition, MAC has been consistently associated with major amputation, delayed wound healing and mortality, in line with a systematic review of 51 calcification-scoring studies; the five-point pedal score has been externally validated, and associations persisted after adjustment for WIfI stage. Model comparison in one cohort suggests incremental information, but discrimination, calibration and reclassification beyond established staging have not been reported. Neither WIfI nor GLASS characterizes arterial-wall phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: The consistency and reproducibility of the prognostic evidence justify formal consideration of MAC in forthcoming revisions of limb-staging systems and guidelines. Incremental-value analyses should accompany that evaluation and inform the form of any modifier rather than delay it. One concrete route is to use MAC as a qualifier of the reliability of the WIfI ischaemia grade in the individual limb.

articles.title: Long-Term Patency and Clinical Outcomes After Retrograde Mesenteric Bypass for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centres, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass.

METHODS: We evaluated 34 patients treated with retrograde mesenteric bypass for CMI between 2009 and 2024. Patency rates were measured with Kaplan-Meier analysis. Thrombosis was classified as early (≤30 days), mid-term (31-365 days), or late (>365 days).

RESULTS: Superior mesenteric artery bypass was performed in 33 patients (97.1%), celiac bypass in 25 (73.5%), and dual-vessel reconstruction in 24 (70.6%). Median follow-up was 2737 days (IQR, 1760-4353), approximately 7.5 years. No early thrombosis occurred. Two mid-term and three late occlusions were observed. Primary patency rates were 93.3% at 1 and 3 years, 89.4% at 5 years, and 85.0% at 10 years. Clinical symptoms resolved after revascularisation in all patients surviving the perioperative period, and no recurrent symptoms were documented during follow-up. No patient required reintervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Retrograde mesenteric bypass was associated with stable long-term patency, sustained symptom resolution, and low perioperative mortality. It remains a durable open surgical option for chronic mesenteric ischemia, particularly when endovascular revascularisation is not feasible or is unlikely to provide durable results.

articles.title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins After Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (IQR, 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap CI, 2.2-3.7; p<0.001). Completion DUS confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; p=0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Antiplatelet Therapy and Bleeding, Thrombosis, and Aneurysm Growth in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed. Demographics and outcomes were compared by antiplatelet status, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with mortality, MACE, bleeding, and AAA growth.

RESULTS: Among 886 (73% male) patients studied, 511 (57.7%) were prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Those prescribed antiplatelet therapy had higher rates of atherosclerotic disease than those not on antiplatelets. Patients not prescribed antiplatelet therapy were more likely to be female, have atrial fibrillation, and be prescribed anticoagulation. At a mean follow-up of 1.8 years, there were no differences in bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism events, or growth rate associated with antiplatelet prescription. Adjusted analyses showed statins (HR=0.73, p=0.02), but not antiplatelets or anticoagulants, were associated with reduced risk of mortality. Diabetes was associated with decreased AAA growth rate, while larger initial diameter was associated with increased growth rate as well as mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AAA, antiplatelet therapy was not observed to be associated with an increase in bleeding risk, but was also not associated with decreased mortality, thrombosis, or aneurysm growth. Statins were observed to be associated with reduced mortality. Aneurysmal growth rate was not associated with any medical therapies studied, including statins, and was only influenced by the presence of diabetes.

articles.title: Roles of one-carbon metabolism, folate and riboflavin in blood pressure: Can a precision nutrition approach reduce the risk of hypertension?
articles.abstract: Folate, along with the metabolically-related B vitamins (B12, B6 and riboflavin), play essential roles in human health throughout life. Notably, recent UK Biobank evidence implicates folate deficiency in hypertension, the major risk factor contributing to mortality worldwide. An estimated 15% of pregnancies are affected by hypertension, which contributes to serious adverse maternal and offspring outcomes, a greater risk of stroke later in life in the mother and long-term disease risk in the child. Clinical and genome-wide association studies link the C677T polymorphism in the gene encoding the folate-metabolizing enzyme methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) with an increased risk of hypertension. Riboflavin (as flavin adenine dinucleotide; FAD) is required as a cofactor for MTHFR, and randomized trials show that intervention with riboflavin lowers blood pressure, specifically in individuals with the MTHFR 677TT genotype, independently of antihypertensive medications. The health implications of this gene-nutrient interaction are important, especially for populations worldwide with the highest frequencies of the variant TT genotype in MTHFR, including Guatemala (up to 66%), Mexico (32-44%), and Northern China (24%). Further investigation is required to elucidate the mechanisms linking folate-mediated one-carbon metabolism with blood pressure and how riboflavin alleviates the excess genetic risk of hypertension in affected individuals. Riboflavin deficiency is highly prevalent worldwide, particularly in women, but is typically overlooked in health and research settings. This review highlights the roles of folate and riboflavin in blood pressure and the opportunity for a precision nutrition approach to reduce hypertension in at-risk individuals by addressing riboflavin deficiency and thus optimizing folate metabolism.

articles.title: Automated laboratory detection of hypercalcemia: Diagnostic yield, clinical pathway and outcomes in a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated laboratory detection of hypercalcemia may facilitate the recognition of previously unrecognized primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), but its value in routine clinical practice remains poorly defined, particularly with regard to subsequent etiological evaluation, healthcare resource utilization, and biochemical follow-up.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated an automated laboratory case-finding strategy for hypercalcemia across a healthcare area serving more than 230,000 inhabitants. Consecutive laboratory alerts generated between 2012 and 2020 were reviewed. After duplicate alerts were removed, 685 unique patients constituted the laboratory-detected cohort, of whom 258 underwent sufficient etiological evaluation and constituted the fully evaluated cohort. Clinical, biochemical, imaging, therapeutic, and longitudinal follow-up data were collected.

RESULTS: Among the 258 fully evaluated patients, definite PHPT was diagnosed in 229 (88.8%). Eight additional patients were retrospectively considered to have probable mild PHPT with concomitant vitamin D deficiency, while other etiologies included tertiary hyperparathyroidism associated with chronic kidney disease, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, medication-related hypercalcemia, familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, sarcoidosis, and vitamin D intoxication. Patients underwent a median of seven specialist consultations. Among patients with an available date of definitive etiological diagnosis, the median interval from the initial laboratory alert to diagnosis was 432 days (IQR 94.5-1219.5). During follow-up, 219/258 patients (84.9%) had at least one documented normocalcemic measurement after biochemical confirmation of persistent hypercalcemia, and 150/258 (58.1%) fulfilled the definition of sustained normocalcemia. In Kaplan-Meier analysis, the median time to first documented normocalcemia was 595 days (95% CI 505-780).

CONCLUSIONS: Automated laboratory case-finding can identify patients with previously unrecognized persistent hypercalcemia and provide an entry point for subsequent etiological evaluation. PHPT was the predominant diagnosis within the fully evaluated cohort, although post-detection selection must be considered when interpreting this proportion. The prolonged diagnostic pathway and substantial healthcare use observed after the initial laboratory alert highlight the need to link automated detection strategies to structured clinical follow-up.

articles.title: Fabrication of a monoclonal antibody-based electro-immunosensor to detect SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid antigen.
articles.abstract: The nucleocapsid protein is one of the major structural proteins of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which has caused the COVID-19 pandemic. Due to their high abundance in the host circulation system, post-early infection, and their participation in other cyclic events that support viral survival, they exert control over the viral life cycle within the host. Thus, assessing these protein levels in serum can serve as an early diagnostic tool for COVID-19 infections. In the current study, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting recombinantly produced NCoV2 (rNCoV2) antigen have been developed, characterized, and assessed for their immunodiagnostic potential by indirect ELISA, sandwich ELISA, and further integrated into electro-immunosensor platforms. Hybridomas secreting anti-rNCoV2 mAbs were obtained by fusion of mouse myeloma Sp2/0 cells with rNCoV2 antigen-immunized murine splenocytes using a chemical fusion agent. Hybridoma clones PAb8E8c3-G8 of isotype IgG2A and PBa1-A2 of isotype IgG1, both bearing ĸ light chains, were further developed and assessed for their diagnostic potential, as they have shown a stable growth pattern and the desired antibody response against the rNCoV2 antigen. The lowest concentration of antigen detected by both mAbs with confidence was 7.81 ng/well. Of the two, mAb PAb8E8c3-G8 was selected for mAb-based electro-immunosensor fabrication. A simple label-free GCE-carbon black-based electro-immunosensor was fabricated and enhanced with L-Cys/AuNP, onto which the mAb was immobilized. The integrated mAb electro-immunosensor could efficiently detect the rNCoV2 antigen, with LOD and LOQ values of 4.618 pg/mL and 15.24 pg/mL, respectively. Thus, in this study, we have generated mAbs against the rNCoV2 antigen, which have shown better diagnostic potential in terms of specificity and sensitivity.

articles.title: Dysfunction of three CD36 variants is due to impaired glycosylation and trafficking.
articles.abstract: CD36 deficiency is characterized by the loss of CD36 due to genetic mutations. Clinical studies have associated CD36 deficiency with hyperlipidemia, insulin resistance, and cardiomyopathy. However, the structural and functional effects of human CD36 variants remain poorly understood. P90S is a causative mutation of CD36 deficiency while E123K and S127L are of unknown significance and typically found in malarial endemic regions. Despite their variable phenotypes, they are all located in the same structural region of CD36. In this study, we expressed these three naturally occurring human CD36 variants in HEK293 cells and found that all variants exhibited impaired oxLDL binding and uptake that was associated with reduced expression, shortened half-lives, and altered glycan processing, consistent with defects in receptor maturation. Inhibition of proteasomal or lysosomal pathways did not restore variant stability, suggesting that reduced receptor abundance is not mediated by a single canonical degradation pathway. All variants exhibited reduced membrane accumulation without enrichment in specific intracellular compartments, indicating impaired trafficking rather than selective retention. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the regulation of human CD36 expression, maturation, and trafficking, and the functional consequences of genetic variation.

articles.title: The expression of the collagen chaperone Hsp47 is regulated by mechanical loading through the YAP/TEAD pathway.
articles.abstract: Mechanical stimuli maintain tissue structure by regulating extracellular matrix (ECM) composition. Collagen, a major ECM component, requires heat shock protein 47 (Hsp47), a collagen-specific molecular chaperone, for proper folding and maturation. However, the molecular pathways linking mechanical stress to collagen biosynthesis through the regulation of Hsp47 expression are not fully understood. In this study, we demonstrate that the Hippo signaling pathway, mediated by the YAP/TEAD complex, directly controls Hsp47 transcription in response to mechanical loading. In a tail suspension mouse model, mechanical unloading induced YAP degradation, resulting in reduced Hsp47 expression and impaired collagen quality. Reloading reversed these changes, restoring both YAP and Hsp47 levels. Chromatin immunoprecipitation confirmed direct binding of TEAD1 to the Hsp47 promoter, establishing a mechanistic link between mechanical signals and Hsp47 regulation. In vitro, substrate stiffness increased Hsp47 expression in a TEAD1-dependent manner. Furthermore, unloading reduced the amount of collagen detected by Sirius Red staining in the soleus muscle. These findings identify the YAP/TEAD-Hsp47 axis as a direct mechanotransduction pathway linking mechanical cues to collagen homeostasis. By clarifying this link, we advance understanding of how tissues adapt to mechanical stress and identify a potential therapeutic target for diseases associated with ECM remodeling, including osteoporosis, muscle atrophy, and fibrosis.

articles.title: THE UBC8-GID E3 UBIQUITIN LIGASE MODULE IS REQUIRED FOR STRESS RESPONSE IN CANDIDA ALBICANS.
articles.abstract: Candida albicans is a leading cause of fungal infections in humans. To survive and proliferate within diverse and dynamic host niches, Candida must rapidly adapt, efficiently acquire essential nutrients, and mount protective stress responses. While cellular stress signalling networks are well described, regulation via the ubiquitin system, including E2-E3 ubiquitylation modules, remains largely unexplored in Candida. Here we investigate the multiprotein Glucose Induced Degradation Deficient (GID) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex and its cognate E2 conjugating enzyme, CaUbc8. Utilizing mass spectrometry-based proteomics, we identified conserved GID subunits, including the previously unannotated CaGid5 homologue. AlphaFold3 modelling predicted a conserved CaUbc8-GID E3 complex architecture, with modular features similar to the homologous Saccharomyces cerevisiae GID E3 complex, with CaGid5 functioning as the adaptor for the interchangeable substrate receptors CaGid4 and CaGid11. We observed that Candida cells responded to different stresses, including carbon source switching, heat shock, and osmotic stress, via a dynamic and differential expression of CaGid4 and CaGid11, suggesting the conditional assembly of distinct GIDCaGid4 and GIDCaGid11 E3 complexes. Notably, copper stress selectively enhanced the expression of CaGid4. Absence of CaGid4 receptor, GID E3 catalytic activity, or Ubc8 reduced copper stress-induced Candida growth and viability, and attenuated antifungal drug efficacy. System-wide proteomics analysis revealed CaGid4-dependent proteome and interactome dynamics implying modulation of oxidative stress response pathways. Together, our studies identified the multi-stress-responsive CaUbc8-GID E3 complex required for antifungal drug efficacy in Candida albicans, and we propose it as a new tractable target for the development of candidiasis therapeutics.

articles.title: Postpartum glycemic trends among people with gestational diabetes using continuous glucose monitoring.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During the immediate postpartum period, glycemic changes among persons with gestational diabetes (GDM) have not been well characterized.

OBJECTIVE: Using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data, we sought to explore the differences in postpartum glycemic trends among people with GDM by patient-level characteristics.

STUDY DESIGN: This study was an exploratory secondary analysis of pregnant people with GDM randomized to using CGM versus capillary blood glucose during pregnancy. Participants without CGM data in the immediate postpartum period were excluded from analysis. Our primary outcome was mean glucose by hour from delivery through the first 48 hours postpartum. We performed additional analyses stratified by GDM type, mode of delivery and time in range during pregnancy (≥90% TIR, 63-140mg/dL) to determine differences in postpartum glycemia among these cohorts.

RESULTS: Of the 111 participants in the overall trial, we included 79 participants with postpartum data in this secondary analysis, of which 22.8% had A1GDM and 77.2% had A2GDM. Overall, there was a slight downward trend in glucose values over the first 48 hours post-delivery. Participants with A1GDM had lower mean glucose by 48 hours compared to those with A2GDM, as did participants with high percent TIR (≥90%) compared with lower percent TIR during pregnancy. Participants with higher gestational mean glucose and percent time-above-range (TAR) had higher mean glucose during the 48 hours post-delivery compared to those with lower gestational mean glucose and time-above-range.

CONCLUSION: We found that postpartum mean glucose trended downward after delivery and varied by multiple pregnancy and delivery characteristics. Future studies should assess whether differences in postpartum glycemic parameters are associated with clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: Weight and Risk Adjusted Perioperative (WRAP) Bundle for Prevention of Cesarean Delivery Surgical Site Infection: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Many individual interventions to reduce surgical site infection (SSI) risk after Cesarean delivery (CD) have been identified; however, their collective impact when used as a bundle is not well defined. This quality improvement initiative compared SSI rates before and after the implementation of a weight- and risk-adjusted perioperative (WRAP) bundle, developed to improve CD outcomes.

METHODS: The WRAP bundle was designed to standardize care by tailoring evidence-based interventions according to each patient's individual SSI risk category. Risk stratification was based on pre-gravid body mass index (BMI) and the presence of comorbidities associated with increased SSI risk. This quality improvement initiative adopted a before-and-after quasi-experimental design over two years. Post-CD telephone calls by clinical reviewers were made 30-42 days postpartum to identify CD-SSI incidence.

RESULTS: A total of 4014 CDs were performed between July 1, 2022, and March 1, 2024, with 1275 before WRAP bundle implementation and 2739 after. Maternal characteristics were comparable between pre- and post-WRAP bundle groups, except for hypertension in pregnancy, which was more prevalent in the post-implementation period (22.1% vs. 17.1%, P = 0.001). Across all BMI categories, a statistically significant reduction in overall CD-SSI incidence from 8.9% to 5.8% (P = 0.007) was observed. In the high-BMI group, the CD-SSI rate decreased from 13.9% to 6.9% (P = 0.03).

CONCLUSION: Tailored bundled interventions, such as the WRAP bundle may be effective in reducing the incidence of CD-SSI, particularly among high-risk individuals. Continuous monitoring of post-CD SSI is vital for quality improvement efforts aimed at optimizing postpartum outcomes.

articles.title: Very low-gradient aortic stenosis: defining the phenotype and recovery after TAVI.
Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry. 35th official report of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (1990-2025).
articles.abstract: Introduction and objectives This report presents the 2025 activity of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (ACI-SEC). Methods All interventional cardiology laboratories in Spain were invited to complete an online survey. Data were analyzed by an external company and subsequently reviewed and presented by the ACI-SEC board. Results A total of 125 hospitals participated, compared with 118 in the previous year. The number of diagnostic procedures and coronary angiograms increased by 4% and 4.5%, respectively, both reaching record highs. Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) increased by 3.3%. The trend toward lower relative stent use was confirmed, with a marked increase in the use of drug-coated balloons, both as a standalone strategy and as part of hybrid strategies. The use of intracoronary imaging and coronary physiology techniques increased, reaching record absolute numbers. Interventional treatment of myocardial infarction increased by 3.6%, with primary PCI accounting for 98% of procedures. Structural heart interventions continued to expand: transcatheter aortic valve implantation (+10.1%), percutaneous mitral interventions (+25.2%), tricuspid interventions (+7.9%), and left atrial appendage closure (+8.4%). Renal denervation procedures, interventional treatment of acute pulmonary embolism, and interventions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension increased significantly. Conclusions The 2025 Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry shows overall growth in both coronary and structural activity. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

articles.title: Shugan Xiaozhi Formula Reduces Hepatic Steatosis and Stiffness in MASLD Patients with Elevated ALT: An Exploratory 24-Week Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-related fatty liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one-third of adults worldwide. The most common manifestations in the early stage are liver dysfunction, hepatic steatosis，metabolic abnormalities, and obesity. The failure of single behavioral interventions and the limited availability of treatment drugs remain unmet clinical needs.

METHODS: In this 24-week, multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, proof-of-concept trial conducted in China, 285 participants with MASLD (ALT >40U/L to 5×ULN) were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive Shugan Xiaozhi Formula (SGXZ) granules or vitamin E 300mg/day. The primary exploratory endpoints were changes in hepatic steatosis measured by MRI-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and FibroScan-controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and changes in liver stiffness by transient elastography (TE) and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE). Additional outcomes included liver enzymes, anthropometric measures, and safety parameters. Analyses were performed in the completer population (n=152) using ANCOVA and logistic regression.

RESULTS: At week 24, SGXZ significantly reduced MRI-PDFF (adjusted mean difference vs vitamin E, -3.44 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.18 to -1.69; P<0.001) and CAP (-45.42dB/m; 95% CI, -58.37 to -32.47; P<0.001). A higher proportion of SGXZ recipients achieved a ≥1-category reduction in MRI-PDFF-defined steatosis grade (22.4% vs 5.3%; OR, 5.83; P=0.007) and a ≥30dB/m reduction in CAP (82.9% vs 39.5%; OR, 8.01; P<0.001). Liver stiffness parameters also improved more with SGXZ (TE, -1.14 kPa; P<0.001; MRE, -0.06m/s; P<0.001). Changes in ALT and AST did not differ between groups, whereas GGT normalization was more frequent with SGXZ (52.3% vs 27.7%; OR, 2.87; P=0.010). SGXZ was also associated with significantly greater reductions in body weight (between-group mean difference, -2.69kg; 95% CI, -3.60 to -1.78; P < 0.001), BMI (-0.94kg/m²; 95% CI, -1.26 to -0.62; P < 0.001), and WHR (-0.04; 95% CI, -0.08 to -0.01; P = 0.020). SGXZ was generally well tolerated; gastrointestinal events were more common but were mild and self-limiting. No serious adverse events or clinically meaningful laboratory safety signals occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory trial, SGXZ was associated with greater reductions in hepatic steatosis, imaging-based liver stiffness, body weight, BMI, and WHR than vitamin E, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings suggest that SGXZ represents a highly promising compound natural medicine therapeutic option for the complex metabolic diseases MASLD/MASH. It meets the urgent clinical need for safe and effective therapies to comprehensively improve patients' conditions. Of course, these findings require further validation in large-scale trials with sufficient statistical power.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2200057595.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and the Diabetic Foot: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Practical Considerations.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a major complication of diabetes and are associated with impaired healing, lower-extremity amputation, and substantial morbidity and mortality. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in the management of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with emerging evidence suggesting potential effects on diabetic foot health beyond glycemic control. This review examines the mechanistic and clinical evidence linking GLP-1RA therapy to DFU development, healing, and lower-extremity outcomes. Experimental studies demonstrate anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, improved endothelial function and angiogenesis, enhanced cellular repair, and potential neuroprotective effects. Clinical studies further suggest favorable associations with incident DFU, lower-extremity amputation, wound-related complications, and mortality, although findings are not uniform and most evidence is observational. Emerging data also suggest potentially favorable postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing diabetic foot and lower-extremity procedures. Comparative studies across glucose-lowering therapies demonstrate heterogeneous findings and do not establish a consistent advantage of one drug class across diabetic foot outcomes. Substantial GLP-1RA-associated weight loss may be accompanied by reductions in lean mass and nutritional intake and may raise additional concerns regarding peripheral neuropathy, wound healing, and foot biomechanics. However, direct evidence linking GLP-1RAs to plantar fat-pad loss, altered plantar pressure, or impaired DFU healing is lacking. Overall, GLP-1RAs may offer benefits relevant to diabetic foot health, but prospective studies using validated wound-healing endpoints are needed to determine whether these therapies directly improve DFU healing and to clarify their role in diabetic foot management.

articles.title: Role of probiotics in neonatal care: From molecular mechanisms to clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Premature births remain a significant global health concern, contributing to high mortality rates among children under five. Preterm newborns (<37 weeks' gestation) encounter considerable health issues due to their underdeveloped organ systems and gut microbiota. These vulnerabilities result in major complications, including necrotizing enterocolitis, sepsis, and feeding intolerance, leading to higher rates of morbidity and mortality, particularly in very preterm infants. In this context, probiotic supplementation has emerged as a widely studied intervention to restore gut homeostasis. This review summarises the therapeutic potential of probiotic strains of the Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, and Saccharomyces genera, along with their distinct molecular mechanisms of action, including competitive pathogen exclusion, reinforcement of the intestinal epithelial barrier, and immunomodulation. However, despite promising evidence, a critical research-to-practice gap exists due to concerns regarding the safety, strain specificity, dosage and the lack of standardized dosing guidelines. Furthermore, administration of live microbial strains to critically ill neonates carry inherent safety risks. This review aims to provide a thorough and even-handed approach on the role of probiotics in preventing preterm complications and evaluate the evolving global safety guidelines, emphasizing the urgent need for standardized, strain-specific clinical protocols to ensure their safe and effective integration in neonatal intensive care.

articles.title: Pulsed field, cryoballoon or radiofrequency catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibit suboptimal outcomes after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation.

OBJECTIVE: We sought to compare the efficacy, safety and long-term outcomes of pulsed field ablation (PFA), cryoballoon (CB) and radiofrequency (RF) ablation for AF in HCM.

METHODS: Patients with HCM undergoing de novo AF ablation were retrospectively included from 11 centers. Procedure characteristics, safety endpoints and 24-month outcomes were assessed. The primary endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence (AF/atrial tachycardia).

RESULTS: A total of 364 patients with HCM (61.7±11.1 years, 74.5% male, 47.5% paroxysmal AF) underwent AF ablation with PFA (n=84), CB (n=50) or RF (n=230). Procedure-related complications occurred in 1.2%, 4.0% and 5.2% with PFA, CB and RF, respectively (p=0.344). Cumulative 24-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence was 48.6%. PFA was associated with reduced atrial arrhythmia recurrence compared with RF (adjusted HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.36-0.91; p=0.018), while CB showed no significant difference with either group (adjusted HR versus RF, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21; p=0.212). In exploratory secondary analyses, PFA was associated with reduced cardiovascular hospitalization (adjusted HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.23-0.80; p=0.008), and greater improvement in NYHA class compared with RF (p=0.032), while CB showed no significant difference. Heart failure hospitalization, repeat ablation, ventricular arrhythmias, stroke/transient ischemic attack and mortality did not differ significantly between ablation modalities.

CONCLUSION: PFA for catheter ablation of AF in HCM was associated with reduced 24-month atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with exploratory signals of fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations and improved NYHA class compared with RF, while CB showed no significant difference.

articles.title: Gramine limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis-related damage. NADPH oxidase 1 (NOX1), together with its regulatory GTPase Ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 1 (RAC1), forms a regulatory module that governs redox signaling. Yet small molecules that engage NOX1 and suppress these coupled injury programs remain insufficiently defined. Here, we identified gramine as a candidate NOX1-engaging compound and delineated its protective mechanism in ethanol-associated hepatocellular injury. Alcohol challenge induced a hepatic NOX1/RAC1 response, recapitulated in ethanol-injured hepatocytes. Silencing Nox1 or Rac1 blunted ethanol-driven injury phenotypes, limiting injury-associated enzyme release, reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential disturbance, mitochondrial network disruption, and DNA fragmentation while partially preserving glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Molecular docking predicted a gramine-NOX1 interaction, a cellular thermal shift assay supported target engagement, and cycloheximide chase analysis showed gramine accelerated NOX1 protein turnover. In ethanol-exposed hepatocytes, gramine conferred concentration-associated protection, improving cell viability, and reducing injury-associated enzyme release, lipid droplet signals, and DNA fragmentation. Post-ethanol gramine treatment reduced injury-associated enzyme release. NOX1 overexpression undermined gramine-mediated protection and reinstated ferrous iron accumulation, glutathione redox imbalance, reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial dysfunction, and damage-associated signaling. Erastin weakened gramine-mediated protection, implicating inhibition of ferroptotic responses in the protective mechanism. In alcohol-gavaged mice, gramine reduced hepatic NOX1 abundance, serum injury markers, Fe2+ levels, lipid accumulation, and lipid peroxidation-associated changes, while preserving GPX4 abundance and limiting histopathological injury. These findings support gramine as a NOX1-engaging small molecule that limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.

articles.title: Postmenopausal estradiol levels and female sex modulate haemodynamic responsiveness in experimental portal hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Sex and 17β-estradiol (E2) influence outcomes of cirrhosis, yet preclinical studies in portal hypertension are conducted predominantly in males. We investigated sex and E2-dependent differences in G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1) signalling and portal pressure response to PDE5 inhibition (PDE5i) in experimental cirrhosis.

METHODS: We assessed sex inclusion in rodent studies by PubMed literature search and analysed human hepatic GPER1 expression by sex and age using bulk RNA-seq. Bile duct ligation was performed in male, ovariectomised (OVX) and sham-operated female rats. E2 was administered 24h before invasive haemodynamic assessment in males and OVX females. Acute PDE5i effects were investigated during haemodynamic measurement.

RESULTS: Of 510 rat and 1,657 mouse studies, 87.3% and 77.3% respectively included males only. Human bulk RNA-seq suggested lower hepatic GPER1 expression in cirrhotic females aged ≥ 50 vs. < 50 years. OVX reduced hepatic - but not aortic - GPER1 expression. E2 reduced portal pressure (mean +/- SEM; 22.6 +/- 1.4 vs. 14.3 +/- 1.1 mmHg, p = 0.009) by lowering hepatic portal vascular resistance (74.4 ± 12.7 vs. 25.4 +/- 3.1 mmHg·min·ml-1·g-1, p = 0.03) only in OVX females. PDE5i decreased portal pressure in males (21.3 +/- 1.2 vs. 16.9 +/- 1.8 mmHg, p = 0.03) irrespective of E2. OVX abolished the PDE5i response, which was restored by E2 (14.3 +/- 1.1 vs. 10.0 +/- 0.9 mmHg, p = 0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: In experimental cirrhosis, estradiol depletion in OVX females was associated with reduced hepatic GPER1 expression and a diminished portal pressure response to PDE5i. This highlights sex and menopausal status as key determinants of treatment response in portal hypertension and supports the need for sex-specific validation.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Sex and hormonal status likely contribute to clinically relevant variability in the pharmacology of portal hypertension. Our work highlights that haemodynamic drug response varies due to sex and estradiol status in pre- and postmenopausal females, yet preclinical studies predominantly rely on male models. Integrating sex and menopausal status into early drug development could improve translational accuracy and anticipate non-responder populations.

articles.title: Pure Cystic Lesions of the Conus Medullaris: A British Single Centre Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pure cystic lesions at the conus medullaris comprising ependymal cyst of ventriculus terminalis (ECVT), intramedullary arachnoid cyst (IMAC) and neurenteric cyst (NEC) are rare benign cysts. Compared to IMAC and NEC often requiring surgery, ECVT is a normal anatomic phenomenon rarely needing more than MRI surveillance. However, the literature predominantly reports surgical cases. We present our experience and discuss management strategies.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted identifying adults ≥16 years with ECVT, IMAC and NEC at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London, United Kingdom (2012-2026). Presenting symptoms using the de Moura Batista/Ganau classification were recorded. Patients with previous trauma or radiological evidence of tumour tissue, Chiari malformations or spinal dysraphism were excluded. Non-parametric Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis H tests were used.

RESULTS: Twenty-two patients were included. An associative trend was observed between the cyst size and the symptoms, P=0.221. Eight patients underwent cyst fenestration ± cysto-subarachnoid shunt placement. Histology was available for six patients revealing NEC in three, IMAC in one and inconclusive in two. Six patients experienced radiological recurrences where two with previously diagnosed NEC underwent surgical re-exploration. Partial recovery was observed in four patients. Another four experienced worsening neurology especially patients with recurrent NEC, P=0.220. Fourteen patients underwent MRI surveillance and all but one remained stable with a median follow-up of 33 months.

CONCLUSION: Pure cystic lesions rarely require surgery, especially the radiologically presumed ECVTs. Unless the cyst causes clinical symptoms by exerting pressure on the neural tissue, a conservative management should be chosen.

articles.title: Low-Frequency Versus Combined High-Frequency Spinal Cord Stimulation for Failed Back Surgery Syndrome: A Single-Centre Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study from Belgium.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established therapy for Failed Back Surgery Syndrome (FBSS). The relative long-term performance of tonic low-frequency SCS (LF-SCS) and of combined high-frequency SCS (HFc-SCS), in which 10-kHz and tonic stimulation are delivered simultaneously, remains uncertain. We reviewed our own single-centre experience with both at one and two years.

METHODS: Single-centre retrospective cohort study (Cliniques Universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels). All patients permanently implanted for FBSS since 2019 were reviewed. Twenty-two were eligible: 13 LF-SCS and 9 HFc-SCS. Outcomes were pain (Visual Analogue Scale, VAS), responder rate (≥50% VAS reduction), opioid and neuropathic pain medication use at one and two years, and satisfaction (modified MacNab criteria) and disability (Oswestry Disability Index) at last follow-up. Non-parametric methods were used throughout.

RESULTS: At one year the two modalities were indistinguishable: median VAS reduction differed by 0 points (95% CI -2 to 2), with 85% and 78% responders. At two years (n = 16) the median individual improvement was 50% with LF-SCS and 13% with HFc-SCS (difference 38 percentage points, 95% CI 7 to 66), and 7 of 10 LF-SCS patients remained responders against 0 of 6. Median follow-up differed between groups (57 versus 33 months), a structural confound. Seven of 30 patients trialled developed trial-phase infection (23%); none followed permanent implantation.

CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort the two modalities performed equivalently at one year and diverged at two. Given the sample size, unequal follow-up and heterogeneous HFc programming, this divergence is an observation from our practice and is hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes after angioarchitecture-based endovascular treatment of cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center cohort study from Germany.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Endovascular treatment is an established option for cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), and its efficacy has been demonstrated in single-center and multicenter cohorts. In this study, we critically evaluate our single-center experience with a standardized endovascular treatment strategy, assessing angiographic success, recurrence, safety, and long-term outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients treated endovascularly for cranial dAVFs from January 2014 to October 2019 at the Institute for Neuroradiology, University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany; direct carotid-cavernous fistulas were excluded. Fistulas were Cognard-classified, cavernous-sinus dAVFs additionally Barrow-classified. Treatment was based on angioarchitecture and accessibility, using transarterial liquid embolization and/or transvenous coils. Outcomes included angiographic success, complications, recurrence/retreatment, and symptom evolution from records, follow-up, and structured telephone interviews; median patient-reported clinical follow-up was 53 months.

RESULTS: Fifty-five patients were included. Cognard I/ IIa/ IIa + b/ IIb/ III/ IV/ V distribution was 6/10/1/13/16/8/1; 39/55 were high-grade. Definite venous/sinus thrombosis was documented in 22. Initial hemorrhage occurred in 9 and was associated with high-risk drainage (8/22 vs 1/33; p=0.0017) and high-grade Cognard lesions (9/39 vs 0/16; p=0.046). Embolization achieved complete occlusion in 49 cases; three additional patients had residual Cognard type I shunting, resulting in angiographic success in 52/55 patients. One recurrence, three clinical complications, and one technical complication occurred. Patient-reported improvement occurred in 46/50; tinnitus improved most, whereas diplopia persisted in 2/6 cases.

CONCLUSION: This single-center study provides a real-world evaluation of our institutional treatment strategy. Our findings support its feasibility, while the small, heterogeneous cohort limits broader conclusions regarding treatment efficacy and durability.

articles.title: Carotid arterial stiffness and strain after treatment in primary aldosteronism: A prospective follow-up study using speckle-tracking ultrasonography.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study investigated vascular alterations in patients with primary aldosteronism (PA), using speckle-tracking carotid strain (STCS) ultrasonography, which allows simultaneous assessment of arterial structure and function. It also aimed to compare arterial stiffness and strain changes over follow-up between surgical and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) treatments.

METHODS: All patients underwent standardized diagnostic work-up for PA. STCS ultrasonography was performed at baseline and 6 months post-treatment. A 5-mm segment of the common carotid artery below the bulb was analyzed to quantify arterial compliance and distensibility (reflecting elasticity); elastic modulus, β-stiffness index and pulse wave velocity (PWV) (reflecting stiffness); and strain-related parameters: displacement, strain and strain rate.

RESULTS: Thirty patients were included. Arterial compliance increased in both transverse and longitudinal planes in the overall cohort (p<0.05). Between-group comparison revealed greater improvement in arterial compliance in the surgical than in the medical group (p=0.033). Arterial distensibility also increased in the transverse plane (p<0.05), whereas no significant changes were observed in β-stiffness index, elastic modulus, PWV, or strain parameters (p>0.05). Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) significantly decreased after treatment in the overall cohort and medical group (p<0.05). Multivariate linear regression identified younger age, shorter hypertension duration, male gender and surgical treatment as independent predictors of greater post-treatment improvement in arterial compliance (p<0.05).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that STCS may be a feasible tool for assessing treatment-related vascular changes in PA. Arterial compliance improved following treatment, and more particularly after adrenalectomy, while structural stiffness was largely unchanged in this exploratory comparison.

articles.title: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency.

RESULTS: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]).

INTERPRETATION: Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.

articles.title: Individualized structural brain network and transcriptomic characterization of heterogeneity in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a heterogeneous metabolic disorder that also affects the brain, yet prior neuroimaging studies have predominantly focused on group-level comparisons, obscuring interindividual variability in brain structural organization. To capture this heterogeneity, we constructed individualized differential structural covariance networks for 156 individuals with T2DM using 148 healthy controls as a normative reference. Unsupervised clustering based on these individualized networks revealed two neuroanatomical subtypes with distinct network configurations. Most subtype-differentiating edges showed higher values in one subtype, whereas a smaller set of edges, primarily involving the basal ganglia and cerebellum, showed higher values in the other. Integration with transcriptomic data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas identified genes spatially associated with subtype-related differences. These genes were enriched in processes including receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and glycerolipid metabolism, with preferential expression in the striatum and cerebellum. Together, these findings characterize interindividual variation in brain structural covariance in T2DM and identify candidate molecular processes associated with the observed subtype differences.

articles.title: Neuroinformatics in Pakistan: building a national framework for data-driven Neuroscience and Neurotechnology.
articles.abstract: Neuroinformatics represents a rapidly evolving interdisciplinary field that integrates Neuroscience, computational science, artificial intelligence, and data engineering to acquire, manage, analyze, and interpret increasingly complex brain data. Advances in Neuroimaging, electrophysiology, multimodal data integration, and computational Neuroscience have made robust Neuroinformatics infrastructure essential for modern data-driven Neuroscience, precision medicine, and intelligent clinical decision support. This Perspective examines the emerging Neuroinformatics landscape in Pakistan, examining institutional research capacity, computational infrastructure, educational and training initiatives, funding mechanisms, clinical informatics, and emerging Neurotechnology and industrial activities. Global developments in Neuroinformatics and Neurotechnology are also examined to contextualize Pakistan's current position and identify opportunities for strategic integration into the international Neuroscience ecosystem. Major barriers are critically evaluated, including fragmented neurological data resources, limited high-performance computing capacity, shortages of interdisciplinary expertise, regulatory and ethical challenges, inadequate interoperability, and barriers to sustained academic-clinical-industrial collaboration. Building on this evidence-informed assessment, this Perspective proposes a national strategy centered on interoperable Neurodata repositories, shared computational infrastructure, interdisciplinary workforce development, responsible data governance, strengthened research-industry partnerships, and international collaboration. Collectively, these priorities provide a practical roadmap for transforming existing computational and Neuroscience capabilities into a coordinated national Neuroinformatics ecosystem. Strategic investment in these areas could strengthen neurological research, accelerate data-driven clinical innovation, and position Pakistan as a more active contributor to the global Neuroinformatics and Neurotechnology landscape.

articles.title: PROlonged posterior PERicardial chest tube treatment to reduce rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation following cardiac surgery (PROPER trial): Rationale and design of a prospective, multinational, randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common complication after cardiac surgery and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged hospitalization. Accumulation of pericardial blood after surgery triggers a localized inflammatory response that has been identified as a contributing factor in POAF development. The PROPER trial (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06800781) is a prospective, multinational, randomized, controlled clinical trial designed to determine whether evacuation of pericardial blood through prolonged drainage using a posterior pericardial chest tube reduces the incidence of POAF following elective cardiac surgery. In addition to routine surveillance, patients will be monitored using a wearable electrocardiographic patch monitor. Patients undergoing non-emergent, first-time coronary bypass grafting, aortic valve replacement, aortic surgery without circulatory arrest, or a combination of these procedures, are randomized 1:1 to either receive intraoperative placement of a posterior pericardial chest tube or standard care. A total of 624 patients will be enrolled across eight Nordic cardiac surgery centers. The primary endpoint is atrial fibrillation (AF) recorded within seven days after surgery. Secondary endpoints include AF recurrence, hospitalization due to bleeding or ischemic stroke, and all-cause mortality. Patients will be followed for five years. If effective, posterior pericardial drainage represents a readily available, low-risk strategy with the potential for rapid and broad adoption in clinical practice.

articles.title: Rationale for Early Discontinuation of Aspirin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Design of the SOLOTAVI Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the first line treatment of aortic stenosis, a condition predominantly affecting elderly patients. In absence of a specific indication for antithrombotic therapy, lifetime aspirin is recommended after TAVI while it may be discontinued 3 months after bioprosthetic surgical valve replacement. Primary prevention, using aspirin compared to placebo among elderly patients is associated with an increased risk of major bleeding and no reduction rates of thrombotic events. Hence, there is a gap of knowledge on whether aspirin should be continued >3 months after TAVI.

STUDY DESIGN: SOLOTAVI is a multicenter, open label, blinded endpoint assessment, 1:1 randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing aspirin discontinuation 3 months after TAVI (experimental) to long-term therapy (control). Adult patients with successful transfemoral TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis and no indication or contraindication for long-term antithrombotic therapy will be enrolled. Randomization is stratified on center and valve type. The primary endpoint is the 12-month composite of all cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and non-procedure-related major or disabling bleeding. A hierarchical analysis is performed for the primary and 3 principal secondary endpoints. The sample size is computed for demonstrating the non-inferiority of the experimental strategy compared with the control strategy, with a conservative non-inferiority margin of 6.5%. A total of 1400 patients will be enrolled.

CONCLUSIONS: The SOLOTAVI trial will assess the non-inferiority of a 3-month duration of aspirin compared to the long-term therapy after successful transfemoral TAVI in terms of thrombotic and bleeding events. NCT06518317 clinicaltrials.org.

articles.title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.

RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.

CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

articles.title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.

METHODS: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.

RESULTS: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.

CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB, n=72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n=91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P<0.001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, while a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P<0.001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P<0.001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs. 35%, P=0.002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.

articles.title: SerpinE3 is a novel endogenous regulator of inflammation via TMPRSS11E inhibition.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Although SerpinE3, an extracellular serine protease inhibitor, has been documented in several studies, its biological function remains largely undefined. In a screen for interactors of TMPRSS11E-a protease known to exacerbate inflammation and lung injury during infection-we identified a novel interaction with SerpinE3. Initially, we assessed the inhibitory effect of SerpinE3 on TMPRSS11E activity using synthetic fluorescent substrates PAR1 and PAR2 peptides. We further characterized SerpinE3 expression patterns in mouse cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) models of inflammation and in patients with pneumonia. Subsequently, the anti-inflammatory effects of SerpinE3 were investigated in both in vitro and in vivo inflammatory models. Finally, we examined the regulatory mechanisms governing SerpinE3 expression via promoter activity assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA). Our results demonstrate that SerpinE3 directly inhibits TMPRSS11E activity. SerpinE3 expression was significantly upregulated in alveolar and liver macrophages under inflammatory conditions. Administration of recombinant SerpinE3 protein markedly alleviated inflammation and acute lung injury in the mouse CLP model. Conversely, SerpinE3 knockout mice exhibited aggravated lung injury, a phenotype that was rescued by recombinant protein administration. Notably, aged SerpinE3 knockout mice displayed a spontaneous accumulation of inflammatory cells in the lungs. Mechanistically, we identified a functional NF-κB response element within the proximal promoter of SerpinE3. In conclusion, we identify SerpinE3 as an infection-inducible, macrophage-derived regulator that attenuates inflammatory lung injury, likely through the inhibition of TMPRSS11E. This study elucidates a critical anti-inflammatory role for SerpinE3 and paves the way for developing SerpinE3-based therapies for inflammatory acute lung injury.

articles.title: Echocardiographic atrial and right heart to pulmonary circulation coupling indices identify high-risk in moderate aortic stenosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging evidence points on an increased mortality risk associated to moderate aortic stenosis (AS), yet this population remains insufficiently characterized. We tested the prognostic value of two echocardiographic coupling indices reflecting right and left-sided cardiac function: the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio (TAPSE/PASP) and the left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI).

METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study including 135 patients with moderate AS. TAPSE/PASP was used as a non-invasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary circulation (RV-Pc) coupling, and LACI was defined as ratio of left atrial volume index to mitral a' velocity. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess the prognostic value of both indices.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 1.61 ± 0.79 years, 33 patients (24%) died. Reduced TAPSE/PASP (< 0.67 mm/mmHg) and elevated LACI (> 5.17) were independently associated with an increased mortality (HR: 3.03 and 3.16, respectively, p < 0.01). These associations remained significant even after adjusting for age. Stratification into three groups - preserved, single, or combined uncoupling -showed progressively lower 1-year survival rates, ranging from 95% to 49% (p < 0.0001). None of the coupling-derived variables was associated with hemodynamic progression or need of aortic valve replacement.

CONCLUSION: TAPSE/PASP and LACI are independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate AS. These parameters may provide incremental prognostic information in this often-overlooked population. These findings may prompt further studies evaluating the potential role of these parameters in helping to refine prognostic phenotyping.

articles.title: Coronary vascular dysfunction is associated with adverse left ventricular filling in patients with angina but no obstructed coronary arteries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with no obstructive coronary arteries is often due to coronary vascular dysfunction, which is increasingly described as a contributor and predictor of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. We tested the hypothesis that coronary vascular dysfunction contributes to cardiac dysfunction.

METHODS: Sixty-eight participants with suspected coronary vascular dysfunction underwent LV pressure-volume assessment at rest and during isometric handgrip stress. Coronary function testing was performed by infusing standard doses of adenosine, acetylcholine, and nitroglycerine through a guiding catheter placed in the left main coronary artery, per established protocols.

RESULTS: Of the participants studied, 12 had normal coronary vascular function while 56 had coronary vascular dysfunction. At rest, there were no differences between groups in any invasive pressure or volumetric measurement. With isometric handgrip, peak filling rate increased significantly in participants with normal coronary vascular function (0.56 ± 0.31 vs. 0.85 ± 0.68 1/s/mmHg) but remained unchanged in participants with coronary vascular dysfunction (0.51 ± 0.22 vs. 0.55 ± 0.43 1/s/mmHg; group x time interaction, p = 0.04). Moreover, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure decreased significantly with isometric handgrip in participants with normal coronary vascular function (12 ± 3 vs. 9 ± 4 mmHg) but increased in participants with coronary vascular dysfunction (14 ± 4 vs. 15 ± 6 mmHg; group x time interaction, p = 0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Coronary vascular dysfunction was associated with an impaired ability of the LV to adapt its filling during stress. Further work is needed to assess potential clinical significance.

articles.title: Response to: "Circulating MBL after acute coronary syndrome: Refining the path from biomarker to mechanism".
Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared.

RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

articles.title: Nanobodies targeting the conserved post-fusion six-helix bundle core provide protective effects against SARS-CoV-2 infection and immunopathology.
articles.abstract: The post-fusion six-helix bundle (6-HB) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein is an evolutionarily constrained structural machinery essential for viral and host membrane fusion, representing a critical vulnerability for antiviral development. While peptide-based fusion inhibitors have been extensively explored, the application of nanobodies, which offer superior stability and the unique capacity to penetrate sterically restricted or cryptic epitopes, remains largely untapped for targeting this conserved fusion core. In this study, we utilized yeast surface display to engineer and isolate high-affinity nanobodies specifically directed against the post-fusion 6-HB. Two lead candidates, ML01 and ML13, exhibited nanomolar to low-micromolar binding affinities and distinct paratope specificity, as confirmed by biophysical characterization and epitope mapping. Functional evaluation demonstrated that these nanobodies exert potent neutralization of pseudotyped and authentic SARS-CoV-2 variants in vitro. Crucially, in vivo validation using a K18-hACE2 neonatal mouse model revealed that ML01 and ML13 administration significantly attenuated pulmonary transcription- and replication-competent virus-like particle (trVLP) entry, suppressed the induction of hyper-inflammatory cytokines (including TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ, and CXCL1), and mitigated severe histopathological lung injury. These findings provide a proof-of-concept that the post-fusion 6-HB is a promising target for nanobody-based therapeutic development. ML01 and ML13 emerge as resilient therapeutic candidates capable of providing a potential defense against the evolving SARS-CoV-2 landscape. Whether these nanobodies can cross-react with other coronaviruses remains to be determined.

articles.title: Metabolite Screening Identifies Potent Antivirals that Mitigate Zika Virus-Induced Ocular Pathology.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection remains a significant global health threat due to its association with severe congenital, neurological, and ocular complications and the continued lack of approved antiviral therapies or vaccines. To identify new therapeutic candidates, we performed a high-throughput antiviral screen of 1,050 human endogenous and exosome-derived metabolites for their ability to attenuate ZIKV infection in human retinal pigment epithelial cells (RPE). This led to the identification of 10 metabolites that reduced ZIKV-induced cytopathic effects, which were further evaluated for antiviral activity and toxicity using physiologically relevant ocular infection models. Among these candidates, octanedioic acid, undecanedioic acid, and 10-undecen-1-ol emerged as the most effective, significantly reducing ZIKV replication and modulating innate immune responses in RPE cells. Analysis of host signaling revealed metabolite-associated changes in STAT1, AMPK, and YAP phosphorylation, identifying potential pathways tied to their antiviral activity. Importantly, in an immunocompetent mouse model of ZIKV-induced chorioretinal atrophy, treatment with these metabolites markedly reduced retinal lesions and immune cell infiltration, demonstrating in vivo therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, these findings identify host-derived metabolites as promising antiviral candidates against ZIKV and warrant further translational investigation.

articles.title: Economic evidence for automated hand hygiene monitoring systems in infection prevention and control: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) impose substantial clinical and economic burdens. Automated hand hygiene (HH) monitoring systems (AHHMS) may improve surveillance and feedback. However, adoption is constrained by implementation costs and uncertain economic value.

AIM: To map and synthesise economic evidence for AHHMS in healthcare infection prevention and control.

METHODS: Six databases were searched for English-language studies published from January 2000 to June 2026. Eligible studies evaluated automated or electronic HH monitoring technologies in healthcare settings and reported original monetary, cost, resource-use, or economic outcomes. The findings were descriptively synthesised, and the monetary values were standardised to approximate 2026 US dollars.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies were included, comprising six full-text articles and 13 conference abstracts. Technologies included badge-based, radio-frequency identification, dispenser-linked, sensor-based, app-based, video-based, and electronic audit-and-feedback systems. The economic findings were generally favourable but heterogeneous. The implementation or acquisition costs ranged from US$0.64 per HH moment to >US$3808 per bed. Meanwhile, the system-level costs ranged from US$2578 to >US$491,948. Hidden costs, including programme coordination, information technology support, maintenance, and staff time, were rarely reported. Sixteen studies reported cost savings, mainly from fewer HAIs, infection-related proxy events, or avoided bed-days. Three studies reported improved monitoring efficiency. Six studies reported favourable cost-effectiveness, return on investment, or cost-benefit findings, but estimates were context-dependent.

CONCLUSION: AHHMS may offer economic value through improved monitoring efficiency and downstream infection-related savings. However, current evidence remains limited, fragmented, and inconsistently reported. Future evaluations should use prospective comparative designs, report total cost of ownership and include sensitivity analyses.

articles.title: Re: "Surgical site infections in spine surgery: a retrospective study of 1,578 procedures with identification of tattooed skin as a novel risk factor associated with surgical site infection".
From receptor architecture to outcome maturity: a clinical framework for multiorgan incretin therapy.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To propose a clinically usable framework that separates receptor architecture and metabolic potency from the maturity of patient-relevant outcome evidence for incretin-based therapies.

METHODS: This Commentary draws on recent cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, peripheral artery disease, liver, and emerging polyagonist evidence to define outcome maturity across five domains: endpoint directness and clinical relevance; study design and evidentiary confidence; comparator and population context; follow-up duration, durability, and safety; and molecule-, dose-, and indication-specific applicability.

RESULTS: Four qualitative states of outcome evidence are proposed: preliminary, emerging, established, and mature. These categories apply to a specific molecule, dose, indication, phenotype, and outcome question and are intentionally nonnumeric. Outcome maturity does not measure treatment-effect magnitude or comparative drug efficacy. A six-step clinical workflow links the dominant organ-risk phenotype, clinically meaningful outcome, evidence maturity, applicability, treatment sustainability, and proportionate clinical positioning.
