Here we propose a probabilistic model for data whitening, and propose parameter estimates and efficient algorithms to improve statistical and computational performance. In an application to impute z-statistics from unobserved genetic variants from a genome-wide association study of schizophrenia, the probabilistic whitening transformation, had the lowest mean square error while being up to an order of magnitude faster than other methods. Using this approach, we also identify tandem repeats that explain genetic regulatory signals for disease-relevant genes. Analyses are implemented in our novel open source R packages decorrelate and imputez.

articles.title: An Empirical Snapshot of Local Nutrition Governance Capacity in the Rasuwa District of Nepal Before the Flood Surge of August 2026.
articles.abstract: On August 26, 2026, flash floods swept through the Rasuwa district of Nepal, causing mass casualties and severe destruction. Research on disasters has led to valuable recommendations on how governments can be more attentive to warning signs and react more rapidly, and how tapping into local capacity and know-how can lead to more effective responses. However, in most crises not much is known about individual or institutional capacities that predated a shock or what resources donors and governments subsequently should bolster to support emergency responses and build resilience. In this Commentary, we draw on the self-reported data of civil servants and other local professionals tasked with implementing the national multisectoral nutrition strategy in Rasuwa. Data collection in 2024 predated the flood by roughly 2 years. The survey measured routine governance capacity, not disaster-response capacity specifically, and yet such data offer some insights into local capacity before the latest disaster and help our understanding of which elements were already under strain. The aim of this Commentary is not to report full survey findings but to highlight observations most relevant to the 2026 Rasuwa flood. Broadly, we suggest that routine governance research on nutrition and other technical topics of relevance can serve as a baseline for disaster recovery and that global calls for the localization of aid require much deeper understanding and measurement of local capacity to act.

articles.title: Undescended Testes in Medically Complex Children: Evaluating A Common Urologic Condition Through a Multi-Disciplinary Lens.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Undescended testis (UDT) is a common genitourinary anomaly in boys. Orchiopexy before 18 months of age is recommended to preserve fertility and reduce testicular cancer risk. However, these recommendations are based on results of outcome studies for otherwise healthy boys and may not be readily applicable for those with developmental and/or genetic disorders for whom anesthetic and surgical risks may be increased and intervention may offer limited benefit. UDT management in boys with complex medical conditions warrants unique considerations, and data-driven guidelines are lacking. In this review, we explore this challenging clinical dilemma through a multi-disciplinary lens.

METHODS: A narrative literature review was performed by specialists in pediatric anesthesia, endocrinology, genetics, oncology, urology, and development-behavioral pediatrics. Iteratively refined structured literature searches of the MEDLINE database, GeneReviews®, and online books were performed via PubMed. Anesthetic and surgical risks, fertility potential, testicular cancer risk, and ability to perform self-testicular exams as dictated by the patient's expected cognitive development were evaluated for healthy boys and boys with Down syndrome (DS), Prader Willi syndrome (PWS), Cerebral Palsy (CP), Fragile X, Neurofibromatosis Type 1, Williams syndrome, 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, Rett syndrome, Angelman syndrome, Tuberous sclerosis, and Smith-Magenis syndrome. The results were then evaluated by a bioethicist.

RESULTS: For children with complex medical conditions, potential harms of intervention are not theoretical. Surgery may expose the child to substantial anesthetic and surgical risks for which their underlying conditions make them especially vulnerable. The ethical threshold for intervention may therefore be higher especially if certain benefits such as fertility remain uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Management of UDT for medically complex boys is nuanced and warrants a multidisciplinary approach to thoroughly assess the risks and benefits of proceeding with, deferring, or declining orchiopexy. Multidisciplinary input will best facilitate individualized care that focuses on the specific needs of each child and appropriately respects parental discretion in determining management that is most in line with the child's long-term quality of life.

articles.title: MRI BRAIN lesions and growth after antenatal steroids in preterm infants: Does timing matter?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) are widely used to improve outcomes in preterm infants, with known benefits on respiratory morbidity and intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH). However, the effect of ACS timing on brain injury and development remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the impact of a complete course of ACS (ccACS), with particular attention to timing, on brain lesions, growth, and neurodevelopment in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this historical cohort study, all VLBW infants admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between January 2019 and December 2021 were included. Clinical data, including timing of ACS administration, were collected. The primary outcome was the occurrence of brain injury on MRI at term-equivalent age, including IVH, white matter lesions (WML), and cerebellar hemorrhage (CBH). Secondary outcomes were brain growth and maturation on MRI and neurodevelopment at 2 years assessed using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales. Outcomes were compared between infants with and without ccACS and according to different administration-to-birth intervals.

RESULTS: A total of 189 infants were included, of whom 139 (73.5%) received ccACS. Infants exposed to ccACS had a lower incidence of WML (p = 0.02) and moderate/severe IVH (p = 0.04). In extremely preterm infants (<28 weeks), IVH was significantly less frequent when ccACS was administered within 7 days before birth (p = 0.006). No significant differences were observed in brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopmental outcomes at 2 years.

CONCLUSIONS: A complete course of ACS was associated with unadjusted lower rates of brain injury in VLBW infants, particularly when administered within 7 days before birth in extremely preterm infants, without adverse effects on brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopment at 2 years.

articles.title: Intraductal and Cribriform Carcinoma of the Prostate: A Clinical Companion to the GUPS/ISUP Consensus Guidelines.
Hemocompatible Glycogen-Tissue Plasminogen Activator Complexes for Enhanced Blood Clot Dissolution.
articles.abstract: Thrombosis and embolism remain leading causes of death worldwide, driven by blood clots that obstruct vascular flow. Current treatments rely on intravenous injections of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) to dissolve clots, however, free tPA has severe limitations, including poor targeting, and risks of bleeding and hemorrhage. In this work, we look to overcome these limitations with targeted, biodegradable, and hemocompatible glycogen nanoparticles. We develop glycogen-heparin hybrids for complexation with tPA, along with peptide-based targeting towards activated platelets. Our strategy involves leveraging the inherent hemocompatibility of glycogen, with minimal synthetic modifications for targeted delivery of tPA to blood clots. In human blood, the glycogen hybrids have minimal interaction with immune cells, and did not trigger inflammatory or coagulation responses at therapeutic concentrations. Furthermore, they remain biodegradable towards glucosidases inherently in the human body. This design enables thrombus targeting and localized tPA delivery, thereby improving fibrinolytic efficiency relative to free tPA, with steady breakdown kinetics. This was also observed for blood clots subjected to thrombolysis under vascular flow-like conditions. Overall, our approach offers a promising treatment strategy for thrombosis, which improves the therapeutic efficacy of tPA, whilst maintaining excellent hemocomptability.

articles.title: Wireless Electrical Stimulation via a Conductive Hydrogel Scaffold Synergizes With Stem Cell Transplantation Therapy to Promote Traumatic Brain Injury Repair.
articles.abstract: Electrical stimulation (ES) offers a robust approach to boost the efficacy of stem cell transplantation therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders. Notably, wireless technology blends convenience with the elimination of infection risk posed by wired connections, but the challenge lies in the integration of wireless-enabled stimulation materials and stem cell carriers. Here, we describe a flexible annular conductive dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid (HAD)/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/carbon nanotube‌ (CNT) hydrogel that acts as a secondary coil to realize wireless ES via electromagnetic induction, while also serving as a three-dimensional (3D) scaffold carrier for endogenous neural stem cells (NSCs). Established on the annular HAD/PVA/CNT hydrogel with high conductivity and good biocompatibility, wireless ES significantly enhances neuronal differentiation of NSCs. Furthermore, transplantation of the NSC-laden annular hydrogel into a traumatic brain injury (TBI) rat model modulates the behaviors of both exogenous and endogenous neural cells. The combined therapy of wireless ES and NSC transplantation promotes neuronal differentiation in both the injury zone and hippocampus in association with the PI3K-Akt pathway, reduces post-traumatic inflammatory responses, and effectively restores motor and memory functions in TBI rats. This study offers a promising therapeutic strategy of integrating wireless ES with stem cell transplantation therapy for brain injury repair.

articles.title: Phase-Programmed Microneedles Enable Sequential Hydrogen and Quercetin Release for Scar-Reduced Regeneration of Burn Wounds.
articles.abstract: Burn wounds complicated by bacterial infection and fibrotic scarring remain a major clinical challenge, demanding therapeutics capable of coordinated infection control, inflammation modulation, and tissue regeneration. Here, we report a phase-programmed microneedle (MN) patch (QR/AB-MNs) that enables spatiotemporally controlled release of ammonia borane (AB) and quercetin (QR) to achieve synergistic antimicrobial and anti-fibrotic therapy. The MNs comprise a poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) shell encapsulating QR and a sulfobutylether-β-cyclodextrin (SBECD) core loaded with the H2-releasing prodrug AB. Upon exposure to the mildly acidic wound microenvironment, the system triggers sustained generation of hydrogen (H2) and AB degradation products, effectively eliminating bacteria and biofilms while mitigating oxidative stress. Subsequently, gradual PLGA degradation ensures prolonged QR release, suppressing fibroblast hyperproliferation and TGF-β mediated collagen deposition, thereby preventing hypertrophic scarring. In murine and rabbit burn models, QR/AB-MNs markedly accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation and bacterial burden, restored skin appendages, and yielded scar-reduced regeneration with native-like collagen architecture. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that QR/AB-MNs orchestrate a broad anti-fibrotic transcriptional program, concurrently attenuating pro-fibrotic signaling, cell-extracellular matrix interactions, and collagen synthesis. Collectively, this programmable MN platform integrates redox modulation, anti-infective therapy, and matrix remodeling to achieve comprehensive, scarless-like healing of infected burn wounds.

articles.title: XChrom: A Cross-Cell Chromatin Accessibility Prediction Model Integrating Genomic Sequence and Cellular Context.
articles.abstract: Single-cell chromatin accessibility offers unique insights into transcriptional regulation beyond gene expression. However, paired datasets of these two modalities remain relatively scarce, and existing computational models cannot simultaneously predict chromatin accessibility for unseen genomic regions and cells. Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome-wide cross-cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single-cell transcriptomics-derived cell identity into a unified model. Comprehensive evaluations show that XChrom consistently outperforms existing methods in cross-region and cross-cell predictions, and uniquely enables cross-both predictions. It also supports cross-sample prediction when batch effects are properly corrected. Cross-species analyses demonstrate XChrom's robust performance and its ability to capture evolutionarily conserved regulatory rules. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID-19 patients, XChrom accurately identifies transcription factor activities in novel but related cell states and reveals pathogenesis-associated regulatory alterations. XChrom is available as an open-source Python package, facilitating single-cell transcriptional regulation research.

articles.title: Beliefs about Hereditary Susceptibility to Cancer and Desire to Know about a Genetic Predisposition: An Analysis of the NCI Health Information National Trends Survey.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study characterized beliefs about hereditary susceptibility to cancer and desire to know about a genetic predisposition to cancer in a nationally representative survey of US adults.

METHODS: Adjusted regression models using weighted survey analysis of NCI HINTS 2020 data assessed predictors of how much respondents (1) believe genes that are inherited determine whether a person will develop cancer and (2) would want to know if they had a genetic change that increases their chance of getting cancer.

RESULTS: On average, respondents endorsed between "somewhat" and "a lot" for how much hereditary susceptibility determines cancer risk. Respondents believed that hereditary susceptibility to cancer, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes were similar (Means= 1.83-1.85, all p>0.6). Individuals who had health insurance (β=-0.42 - -0.37, p=0.017-0.021) and previously sought cancer information (β=-0.19, p<0.001) believed in greater hereditary susceptibility to cancer, whereas those who self-reported good health believed in less hereditary susceptibility to cancer (β=0.16, p=0.022). Individuals who believed in greater hereditary susceptibility to cancer (β=0.14, p=0.001), previously sought cancer information (β=-0.19, p=0.002), had a family history of cancer (β=-0.19, p=0.005), were less fatalistic (β=-0.08, p=0.036), and were Hispanic (β=-0.25, p=.009) or Black (β=-0.47, p<0.001) endorsed a greater desire to know about a genetic predisposition to cancer.

CONCLUSIONS: Efforts are needed to improve understanding of hereditary susceptibility, address fatalistic beliefs and misinformation, facilitate disclosure of family cancer history indicative of a potential genetic predisposition to cancer.

IMPACT: Efforts are needed to improve access to genetic counseling and testing through education and targeted interventions.

articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed.

OBJECTIVE: To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%).

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications.

RESULTS: The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921.

articles.title: Comparison of Outcomes Between Men and Women Undergoing Ventral Hernia Repair.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Sex-based differences in ventral hernia repair (VHR) outcomes remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To compare short-term clinical outcomes, recurrence through 3 years, and patient-reported outcomes between female and male patients undergoing VHR.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study included patients undergoing VHR from January 2012 through December 2023, with follow-up through 3 years. Data were from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative (ACHQC), a prospective, multi-institutional clinical registry. Participants were adults undergoing primary or incisional VHR whose data were recorded in the ACHQC database. Data analysis was performed from May to September 2026.

EXPOSURES: Sex (female vs male).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes included 30-day wound morbidity, comprising surgical site infection (SSI), surgical-site occurrence (SSO), and SSO requiring procedural intervention (SSO-PI), readmission, and length of stay. Secondary outcomes included pragmatic recurrence at 30 days, 1 year, 2 years, and 3 years and patient-reported quality of life and pain. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between sex and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 31 358 patients, 14 303 (45.6%) were female and 17 055 (54.4%) were male. Women were younger than men (mean [SD] age, 55.0 [14.6] vs 56.5 [13.0] years, respectively) and had higher body mass index (mean [SD], 32.1 [7.6] vs 31.7 [5.9], respectively). Women presented with more complex hernia phenotypes, including higher rates of incisional, recurrent, and larger hernias. Compared with men, women experienced higher 30-day readmission (483 [3.4%] for women vs 428 [2.5%] for men), SSI (370 [2.6%] vs 284 [1.7%], respectively) SSO (1323 [9.2%] and 1286 [7.5%], respectively), and SSO-PI (517 [3.6%] vs 434 [2.5%], respectively; all P < .001), with no differences in reoperation or mortality. Female sex was independently associated with higher odds of SSI (odds ratio [OR], 1.40; 95% CI, 1.17-1.67) and SSO-PI (OR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.04-1.40) after incisional hernia repair. Clinical outcomes and recurrence were similar at 1 year; however, women had higher recurrence at 2 years (444 [19.3%] vs 406 [15.7%] men) and 3 years (351 [20.9%] vs 320 [17.6%] men). Women reported worse baseline quality of life and pain but greater improvement after 1 year.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that women undergoing VHR presented with greater hernia complexity and experienced higher early wound morbidity and increased late recurrence, while achieving substantial patient-reported benefit. These findings may inform sex-specific risk stratification and counseling, although further studies with more longitudinal follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Parental Diabetes and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in Offspring-Reply.
Prognostic Value of the Delta Neutrophil Index for Predicting 28-Day Mortality in Intensive Care Unit Patients with Candidemia.
articles.abstract: Candidemia is associated with substantial mortality in critically ill patients, and early identification of patients at increased risk of death remains challenging. The delta neutrophil index (DNI), an automated hematological parameter reflecting circulating immature granulocytes, has been proposed as a prognostic marker in sepsis, but its role in candidemia remains unclear. This retrospective study included adults who developed candidemia during intensive care unit hospitalization between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2023; patients with neutropenia, haematological malignancy receiving ongoing chemotherapy, or granulocyte colony-stimulating factor therapy were excluded. Patients were classified as survivors or non-survivors according to 28-day all-cause mortality after blood culture collection. DNI, leukocyte count, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin were evaluated 24 hours before, at the time of, and 24 hours after blood culture collection. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with mortality, and receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed the prognostic performance of DNI. Among 246 patients, 132 survived and 114 died. Non-survivors had higher APACHE II scores and more frequent acute kidney injury. DNI and procalcitonin levels were significantly higher in non-survivors at all three time points. In the primary multivariable model, acute kidney injury, DNI at blood culture collection, and procalcitonin at blood culture collection were independently associated with mortality; the association of DNI was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for Candida species and antifungal therapy. DNI showed limited discrimination, with area under the curve values ranging from 0.608 to 0.625; the highest value was observed at blood culture collection (0.625), with a cutoff of 2.4, 43.0% sensitivity, and 82.6% specificity. DNI may aid mortality risk stratification in candidemia but should not be used as a standalone prognostic marker.

articles.title: Estrogen Use and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Estrogen-containing therapy is considered a risk factor for porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT), but the evidence is limited to clinical series and case reports.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether estrogen-containing therapy is associated with incident PCT, overall and according to estrogen-containing therapy type and route of administration.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this matched case-control study using data from Danish nationwide registries conducted from January 1, 1995, through November 1, 2024, female individuals with a first-time hospital diagnosis of PCT were matched 1:100 with population control patients on age, sex, and index date.

EXPOSURE: At least 1 redeemed prescription of estrogen-containing therapy within 1 year before the index date.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for incident PCT were calculated from conditional logistic regression. Analyses were stratified by estrogen-containing therapy type and route of administration. Analyses were adjusted for PCT-related comorbidities: HIV infection; liver disease, viral hepatitis, or iron overload; smoking-related diagnosis or treatment; and alcohol or drug misuse diagnosis or treatment.

RESULTS: The study included 438 female case patients with incident PCT (median age, 61.16 years [IQR, 51.08-69.17 years]) and 43 800 age-matched female control patients. In total, 154 cases (35.16%) and 9433 control patients (21.54%) had been exposed to any estrogen-containing therapy within 1 year before the index date (adjusted OR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.66-2.49). Estrogen-containing contraceptives were associated with incident PCT (adjusted OR, 2.52; 95% CI, 1.67-3.82) as were estrogen-only therapy (adjusted OR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.23-2.03), and combined estrogen and progestogen therapy (adjusted OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.53-3.11). When stratified by route of administration, oral therapy was associated with PCT (adjusted OR, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.66-3.59), whereas nonoral routes were not.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This nationwide matched case-control study found that estrogen-containing therapy was associated with incident PCT. In route-specific analyses, only oral therapy was associated with PCT, suggesting that route of administration should be considered when evaluating estrogen exposure as a potential risk factor for PCT.

articles.title: Parental Diabetes and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in Offspring.
Massive Mediastinal Hematoma After Reablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mediastinal hematoma is a rare but severe complication of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. We present a case of a massive mediastinal hematoma following reablation for AF in a patient with a history of cardiac surgery.

CASE SUMMARY: A 70-year-old woman with rheumatic heart disease, prosthetic aortic and mitral valves, and mild thalassemia underwent catheter ablation for recurrent AF. She developed acute dyspnea and orthopnea 30 hours after the procedure. Computed tomography angiography revealed a 69.2 mm × 51.1 mm hematoma, compressing the left atrium. Conservative management was initiated, including blood transfusion and diuretics. The patient's symptoms improved within 2 days, and subsequent imaging demonstrated complete resolution of the hematoma at 12-month follow-up.

DISCUSSION: The occurrence of the massive hematoma could be attributed to preexisting atrial fibrosis and pericardial adhesions from prior cardiac surgery, potential vascular fragility and platelet dysfunction because of thalassemia, challenges in accessing the scarred atrial septum, thermal injury to the left atrial roof, and the perioperative hemodynamic changes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: For patients with a history of cardiac surgery and thalassemia, vigilance for mediastinal hematoma is essential following catheter ablation procedures.

articles.title: Cardiac Arrest After Deceased Donor Kidney Transplant.
articles.abstract:
CASE SUMMARY: A 54-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease and a dual-chamber pacemaker for high-grade atrioventricular block underwent deceased donor kidney transplantation. Her postoperative course was complicated by marked QT prolongation and recurrent torsades de pointes (TdP), resulting in cardiac arrest. Postarrest electrocardiogram demonstrated macroscopic T-wave alternans-a rare manifestation of severe QT prolongation. Treatment with intravenous magnesium and reprogramming her pacemaker to a lower rate limit of 100 beats/min resulted in electrical stability and improvement of the QT interval.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case underscores recognition of macroscopic T-wave alternans as a harbinger of impending TdP, vigilant QT monitoring, and evidence-based TdP management.

articles.title: Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions: Detection Is No Longer Diagnosis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

articles.title: Efficacy and Mechanism of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients With Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysphagia is a common complication following stroke. While current management strategies for poststroke dysphagia (PSD) range from nutritional support to neurostimulation techniques, an optimal treatment regimen remains elusive. As a promising noninvasive neuromodulation approach, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) requires further validation in rigorously designed trials to establish robust evidence of its efficacy and mechanisms of action.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors.

METHODS: This study will use a prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial design. A total of 40 patients with PSD will be enrolled and randomly allocated to either a taVNS group or a sham taVNS group. Both groups will receive conventional swallowing rehabilitation therapy as the baseline intervention. The taVNS group will receive bilateral electrical stimulation at the cymba conchae and cavum conchae of the auricle. These sites correspond to the "Heart" and "Kidney" auricular acupoints, selected in accordance with traditional Chinese medicine theory. In contrast, the sham taVNS group will receive stimulation at regions of the auricle not innervated by the vagus nerve. The primary outcome measure will be the Penetration-Aspiration Scale score. Secondary outcomes will include the Yale Pharyngeal Residue Severity Rating Scale, hyoid bone displacement and hyoid-thyroid approximation distance assessed via B-mode ultrasonography, and motor-evoked potentials of the suprahyoid muscles elicited by transcranial magnetic stimulation. All outcome measures will be evaluated at baseline and after the 2-week intervention period.

RESULTS: This paper describes the protocol for a study evaluating the efficacy and mechanisms of taVNS in patients with PSD. The study was funded in January 2025. Participant recruitment began in March 2025 and is projected to conclude by October 2026. Data collection began in March 2025 and is projected to be completed by October 2026. Primary study results are expected to be submitted for publication in winter 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors.

articles.title: Anion networks activating cobalt active sites for PET plastic waste electro-upcycling.
articles.abstract: Sulfur substitution in spinel NiCo2O4 creates an anion network that activates cobalt active sites for polyethylene terephthalate plastic upcycling, which is a promising strategy to enhance intermediate adsorption and catalytic kinetics of electrocatalyst.

articles.title: Single-Cell Dissection of Microglial Dysfunction in Diabetes-Associated Neurodegenerative Vulnerability.
articles.abstract: The molecular mechanisms linking type 2 diabetes to increased neurodegenerative risk remain poorly defined. Given the critical involvement of microglial dysfunction in neurodegeneration, we constructed a temporal single-cell atlas integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles of microglia from diabetic (db/db) and control (db/m) mice across the lifespan. We delineated a nonlinear, diabetes-specific pathological trajectory characterized by early inflammatory activation, a mid-stage inflection in neurodegeneration-associated signaling and metabolic stress, and late-stage dysfunction. Chromatin accessibility profiling revealed early and persistent epigenomic priming of neurodegeneration-associated pathways, accompanied by stage-specific enhancer rewiring. Pseudotime analysis identified a disease-associated microglial (DAM) state as a candidate transition node, characterized by biased polarization and accelerated maturation under diabetic conditions. Targeted validation using freshly isolated microglia and primary microglial cultures further supported the early expansion of the DAM population, a bias toward homeostatic-to-DAM activation, and Arhgap15-dependent regulation of phagocytic activity. Together, these findings identify microglial states and candidate regulatory pathways that may link diabetes to neurodegenerative vulnerability.

articles.title: What Is the 40-year Survivorship of Periacetabular Osteotomy Free From Conversion to THA?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is a widely accepted technique for the surgical treatment of symptomatic acetabular dysplasia with reproducibly favorable short- and midterm outcomes. Long-term follow-up studies are essential because PAO is performed in young patients with the aim of preserving the native hip for many decades. However, follow-up of 30 years remains scarce, and no study has reported 40-year outcomes after PAO.

QUESTIONS/PURPOSES: (1) What is the cumulative 40-year survivorship free from conversion to THA? (2) How did hip function change and osteoarthritis progress during follow-up of the surviving hips? (3) Which preoperative factors were associated with conversion to THA? (4) What clinically relevant thresholds can be identified for preoperative factors associated with conversion to THA?

METHODS: This was a retrospective case series of a consecutive, single-surgeon cohort followed longitudinally and previously reported at 10, 20, and 30 years. Between 1984 and 1987, a total of 75 hips (63 patients) were treated with PAO for acetabular dysplasia at the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery of the Inselspital Bern by the originator of the procedure. Of those, 57% (43 of 75) of hips had reached the endpoint (conversion to THA or arthrodesis) before our previous report on this group (published at a minimum of 27 years). Over the entire follow-up, 5 hips (4 patients) in which the patient died with the hip preserved were treated as competing events. Since the previous report, a further 8 hips were converted and 8 hips (6 patients) were lost to follow-up, leaving 11 hips (7 patients) with complete clinical and radiographic follow-up here, all at a minimum of 36 years. During the study period (1984 to 1987), the only indication for PAO was hip dysplasia with closed triradiate cartilage. The study group here consisted of 83% (52 of 63) women, the median (range) patient age at surgery was 26 years (12 to 55), and the median (range) BMI was 22 kg/m2 (16 to 28). A total of 27 hips had previous surgery to attempt sufficient coverage. Clinical and radiographic follow-up was performed at 10-year intervals, at 10, 20, 30, and 40 years after PAO. Survivorship free from conversion to THA was estimated using a competing-risks analysis with death without conversion treated as a competing event. Twelve patients underwent bilateral PAO and contributed two hips each. Because two hips from the same patient are not independent observations, all confidence intervals (CIs) and p values were calculated using a robust variance estimator with the patient as the clustering unit. Clinical scores, hip ROM, and osteoarthritis grade were described at each follow-up. Preoperative factors associated with conversion to THA were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression with a robust variance estimator clustered on patient. Thresholds for predictive factors were identified using maximally selected rank statistics. This approach tests every observed value of a factor as a potential dividing line and selects the value producing the greatest difference in survivorship between the two resulting groups.

RESULTS: At 40 years, the survivorship free from conversion to THA was 27% (95% CI 12% to 39%). Merle d'Aubigné-Postel and Harris hip scores improved during the first decade after surgery and remained above the preoperative level at each follow-up visit. Two preoperative factors were independently associated with a higher risk of conversion to THA: a higher Tönnis osteoarthritis grade (HR 2.3 per 1-grade increase [95% CI 1.4 to 3.9]; p < 0.01) and a positive anterior impingement test result (HR 3.9 versus a negative test result [95% CI 1.9 to 7.7]; p < 0.01). Threshold analysis, which identifies the value of a preoperative factor that best separates hips likely to be preserved from those likely to be converted, identified 28 years for age at surgery. Younger age was therefore associated with a higher likelihood of retaining the native hip.

CONCLUSION: PAO provides durable joint preservation in acetabular dysplasia and can delay THA for decades, with 27% of hips remaining free from conversion at 40 years. Preoperative osteoarthritis and a positive anterior impingement test result were associated with conversion to THA. Older age was also associated with conversion, with a threshold of 28 years, although age was related to the degree of joint degeneration at presentation. Patient selection should therefore be based primarily on the preoperative condition of the joint, with younger age at surgery as an additional consideration.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in the Era of Environmental Sustainability: Can We Achieve Excellence?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The healthcare sector is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, prompting an urgent need for environmentally sustainable practices. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) management presents unique challenges in this context due to the frequent use of metered-dose inhalers containing high global warming potential propellants and the resource-intensive nature of acute exacerbations.

METHODS: This expert consensus paper explores how COPD care can be optimized to reduce environmental impact, while maintaining high standards of clinical effectiveness. We examine the patient journey, adherence patterns, and therapeutic strategies, including the role of single-inhaler triple therapy in preventing exacerbation, as determinants of healthcare-related emissions.

RESULTS: The potential of dry powder inhalers, accurate diagnosis, patient engagement, and sustained disease stability are highlighted as levers for environmentally sustainable care. We advocate for the integration of environmental impact as a formal outcome in randomized controlled trials, supported by standardized Life Cycle Assessment methodologies.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that environmentally conscious COPD management is not only possible but may enhance clinical outcomes and system sustainability.

articles.title: Clinical, Radiological, and Outcome Parameters of CADASIL from India: Findings from a Multicentric Case Series.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract: Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is a hereditary monogenic cause of cerebral small vessel disease with a heterogeneous clinical spectrum. Published literature data from India remain limited. We conducted a multicentric, ambispective review of genetically proven CADASIL cases between 2021 and 2025 to describe the clinical, neuroimaging, and outcome profiles of CADASIL from a multicentric case series from India. A total of 13 patients were included, with a mean age of 47 years and a marked male predominance (84.6%). Motor weakness (69.2%) and dysarthria (53.8%) were the most frequent manifestations. Neuroimaging revealed infarcts in all cases, while hemorrhagic involvement in the form of microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging was noted in 5 patients (38.5%). The majority of patients (61.5%) were managed with antiplatelet agents and statins. Follow-up data at one year were available for 8 patients, all of whom experienced recurrent stroke events.

articles.title: A Phase 2, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Acmopatide (CT-868), a Fully Biased GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist, in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Overweight or Obesity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acmopatide, a signal-biased glucagon-like peptide 1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight/obesity.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this phase 2, 16-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study, adults with T1D (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%; BMI ≥27 kg/m2) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to once-daily subcutaneous acmopatide (1.8, 4.1, or 6.6 mg) or volume-matched placebo. The primary end point was change from baseline (CFB) in HbA1c (%) at week 16; secondary end points included percent CFB in body weight and insulin dose.

RESULTS: Overall, 111 participants were randomized (placebo n = 29, acmopatide 1.8 mg n = 27, 4.1 mg n = 28, 6.6 mg n = 27). Mean (SD) baseline HbA1c was 7.5% (0.6), and mean BMI was 34.3 (5.6) kg/m2. Acmopatide improved HbA1c (least squares [LS] mean CFB -0.4 to -0.6% vs. -0.3% with placebo; nominally significant placebo-adjusted difference for 4.1 mg: -0.3% [90% CI -0.6 to -0.1]; P = 0.020). HbA1c <7.0% was achieved by 55.6% of participants receiving acmopatide 4.1 mg vs. 33.3% receiving placebo. Acmopatide-treated participants demonstrated reductions in body weight (LS mean CFB -3.3 to -6.7% vs. 0.3% with placebo; all P < 0.01), total daily insulin dose (-3.4 to -14.9% more than placebo for acmopatide 4.1 and 6.6 mg), and mean systolic blood pressure (-3.1 to -8.4 mmHg vs. -3.3 mmHg with placebo). Adverse events were primarily gastrointestinal. No diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or severe hypoglycemia events occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with T1D and overweight/obesity, acmopatide was associated with improved glycemic control and clinically meaningful weight loss without DKA or severe hypoglycemia events.

articles.title: Modifiable adiposity-related risk for chronic kidney disease in APOL1 variant carriers: Pilot study results.
articles.abstract: Background: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) genetic variants are associated with the development of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but disease expression appears to depend on metabolic and environmental modifiers. Obesity is a risk factor for several chronic diseases. However, the relationship between obesity, body fat, and the development of kidney disease mediated by APOL1 risk variants is unknown. Aim: This study examined relationships among APOL1 risk variants, nutritional status, with a focus on anthropometry and body composition, and selected renal function biomarkers in individuals with CKD. Methods: Adults with CKD were genotyped for APOL1 variants, resulting in APOL1 risk and APOL1 non-risk groups. Results: The APOL1 risk group showed higher body mass index, increased central abdominal fat, and greater body fat compared with established reference values (p < 0.05). This group also showed high serum creatinine levels and a low estimated glomerular filtration rate, both abnormal ranges (p < 0.05). Conclusions: These findings demonstrate excessive body and abdominal fat as a relevant target for precision nutrition strategies to reduce CKD risk and support management in APOL1-associated kidney disease. Also, it is necessary to identify carriers before the onset of CKD and to use medical nutrition therapy to prevent or delay disease progression.

articles.title: Association between wheezing and dietary patterns among 5- to 6-year-old preschool children in Tshwane, South Africa.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDietary patterns influence inflammation and immune responses, playing a critical role in childhood asthma. Wheezing is a common respiratory symptom, with approximately half of all children experiencing at least one episode during early childhood.AimTo investigate associations between dietary patterns and wheezing among 5- to 6-year-old preschool children in Tshwane, South Africa.MethodsAn observational cross-sectional study was conducted between January 2022 and March 2023. A total of 630 children from 40 randomly selected preschools participated. Parents completed a modified International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood Phase III questionnaire. Univariable and multiple logistic regression models estimated adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for associations between dietary intake and wheezing. Most participants were from Soshanguve (50.3%), with a median age of 5 years. Ever wheeze and current wheeze were reported in 12.4% and 9.8% of children, respectively. Consumption of meat (≥3 times/week), seafood (1-2 times/week) and vegetables (≥3 times/week) was associated with lower odds of ever wheezing (meat: AOR = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.10-0.75; seafood: AOR = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.13-0.46; vegetables: AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.11-0.93), while no clear associations were observed for current wheeze.SummaryHigher consumption of meat, seafood and vegetables was linked to lower odds of ever wheezing in Tshwane preschool children. Promoting nutrient-rich dietary patterns may help prevent early-life respiratory symptoms in underserved communities.

articles.title: Treatment patterns and healthcare utilization for patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) in the Veterans Health Administration (MCLOVA) who were prescribed their first Bruton Tyrosine Kinase inhibitor (BTKi): A national retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionMantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is a rare subtype (5%) of Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL), with 5-year survival of about 50%. Bruton Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (BTKis) may improve health outcomes for patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) MCL.Study objectiveThe objective of this study was to compare treatment patterns and healthcare utilization for patients with R/R MCL prescribed their first BTKi therapy using data from the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA).MethodsThis was a retrospective cohort study of adult patients (18 + years) prescribed BTKis for MCL in all VHA medical facilities in the United States from 1/1/20 to 12/31/23. Data were statistically analyzed using chi-square, Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test, Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves, multivariable negative binomial regression, and Cox Proportional Hazards regression, and a p-value <0.05.ResultsThere were 494 patients included. Of those included, 177 received ibrutinib, 189 received acalabrutinib, and 128 received zanubrutinib. More patients on ibrutinib switched to other BTKis (27%) compared to patients on acalabrutinib (10%, p < 0.01) or zanubrutinib (9%, p < 0.01). Median (interquartile range [IQR]) laboratory visits at 12 months were higher for ibrutinib (5, 0-12) than acalabrutinib (1, 0-8, p < 0.01) or zanubrutinib (0, 0-6, p < 0.01). Finally, overall survival (OS) was higher for patients on zanubrutinib than those on ibrutinib (p < 0.01) or acalabrutinib (p < 0.01).ConclusionsPatients prescribed acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib experienced fewer laboratory and hematology/oncology visits at 12 months than patients who received ibrutinib. Patients who received zanubrutinib experienced a survival advantage when compared to those treated with ibrutinib.

articles.title: Seeing the Difference: A Multifactorial Approach to Increase Diabetic Eye Exam Completion.
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy remains a leading cause of vision loss, yet screening rates remain suboptimal. Patients face barriers to timely diabetic eye screenings, including limited access to care in rural settings and inconsistent referral and documentation processes. Using the Model for Improvement, iterative cycles addressed clinic-level gaps through a multicomponent strategy that included provider-led patient education, a standardized referral process, and enhanced documentation practices for accurate reporting. Screening referral and completion rates increased from 53.8% to 69.9% over 1 year. Patients who received provider-led education using models and pictures reported clarity, sufficient time to understand the information, and plans to schedule a screening eye exam. Workflow changes improved reporting of quality metrics through enhanced documentation and higher rates of diabetic eye exams, with potential downstream benefits including cost savings from improved performance metrics and the prevention of diabetes-related vision loss.

articles.title: Bioinformatics for Healthcare Quality Management: Clinical Outcomes, Implementation Barriers, and Care Improvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The bioinformatics-enabled workflows as quality-management tools have become central to modern healthcare, enabling genomic sequencing, transcriptomics, proteomics, and multiomics integration to support clinical decision-making. Despite expanding adoption, synthesized evidence on measurable clinical value and organizational, workforce, interoperability, governance, and equity barriers remains limited. To synthesize evidence on the contribution of bioinformatics-enabled workflows to healthcare quality improvement, care-process performance, clinical decision-making, patient outcomes, and implementation challenges from 2015 to 2025.

METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and IEEE Xplore. We included studies from real-world healthcare or public health settings where bioinformatics supported diagnostic quality, timeliness, treatment appropriateness, patient safety, and workflow efficiency, or operational decision-making, reporting quantitative outcomes including diagnostic yield, time-to-diagnosis, treatment modification, or economic impact.

RESULTS: Twenty studies met the selection criteria, spanning precision oncology, pharmacogenomics, infectious disease surveillance, clinical genomics and rare disease diagnosis, and multiomics biomarker translation. Across these domains, bioinformatics-enabled workflows improved diagnostic yield (25%-40% in rare disease genomics) and diagnostic accuracy, and shortened time-to-diagnosis, from 4-6 weeks to as little as 3 days in acute pediatric care and from weeks to under 24 hours for pathogen genomic surveillance. Workflows also supported treatment modification, with matched or altered therapy in 33%-37% of oncology cases, and improved pathogen detection and antimicrobial-resistance monitoring. Economic evidence, although still limited, was favorable: first-line exome sequencing was cost-saving, with average reductions of approximately US$9000 per patient in rare disease diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Although precision medicine relies heavily on bioinformatics, improvements to infrastructure, consistent governance, and capacity building for clinical staff are essential to ensure its scalable and equitable implementation.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Non-Invasive Hepatic Fibrosis Scores Across Acute Coronary Syndrome Subtypes.
articles.abstract: Hepatic fibrosis indices have emerged as potential prognostic markers in cardiovascular disease. This observational study included 760 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndrome (STEMI, NSTEMI, and unstable angina pectoris) admitted between March 2020 and May 2024 to evaluate the distribution of APRI, FIB-4, FIB-5, and FIB-6 across ACS subtypes and their predictive value for in-hospital mortality and cardiogenic shock. Fibrosis indices were calculated from admission laboratory values, and multivariate logistic regression and ROC curve analyses were performed. STEMI patients had significantly higher APRI (0.95±1.43 vs. 0.41±0.71 vs. 0.20±0.11), FIB-4 (3.68±4.03 vs. 1.98±2.17 vs. 1.17±0.52), and FIB-5 (5.16±1.08 vs. 4.66±0.84 vs. 4.38±0.43) than NSTEMI and unstable angina patients (all p<0.001). In-hospital mortality and cardiogenic shock occurred in 3.8% and 3.2% of patients, respectively. Cardiogenic shock, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and lower serum albumin independently predicted mortality, whereas older age independently predicted cardiogenic shock. None of the hepatic fibrosis indices independently predicted either outcome, and their discriminative performance was limited (AUC 0.526-0.632 for mortality and 0.570-0.662 for cardiogenic shock). These findings indicate that although hepatic fibrosis scores are elevated in STEMI, they primarily reflect the severity of acute myocardial injury rather than providing incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical predictors in patients with acute coronary syndrome.

articles.title: Neonatal-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: High genetic yield and long-term outcomes in a multicenter southern European cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the genetic diagnostic yield, characterize the clinical and genetic landscape, and evaluate long-term epilepsy, neurodevelopmental, and survival outcomes in a strictly defined cohort of neonatal-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE).

METHODS: Retrospective multicenter observational study across tertiary epilepsy centers in Italy, Greece, and Spain. Sixty-two full-term neonates fulfilling ILAE 2022 criteria for DEE with seizure onset within the first 30 days of life and a minimum follow-up of 18 months were included. All patients underwent next-generation sequencing-based genetic testing. Genetic findings, clinical characteristics, and long-term outcomes were systematically analyzed.

RESULTS: A molecular diagnosis was established in 82.2% of patients (51/62), identifying variants across 29 genes grouped, for descriptive purposes, into four broad categories according to principal biological role. First-line whole-exome sequencing achieved higher diagnostic yield than targeted gene panels (88.9% vs. 41.2%), although this comparison was influenced by differences in testing era and strategy. KCNQ2 variants were the most frequent genetic cause (29.4%), and several treatable metabolic disorders were identified. After a mean follow-up of 11.9 years, 64.5% of patients had drug-resistant epilepsy and mortality reached 17.7%. Seizure freedom was achieved in a subset of patients, particularly those with KCNQ2-related DEE. Nevertheless, severe-to-profound intellectual disability affected 71.7% of evaluable patients and persisted even among those who became seizure-free, suggesting that neurodevelopmental outcomes are influenced by factors beyond seizure burden, including the underlying genetic disorder and other disease-related factors. However, the marked variability observed precludes any causal inference from these data.

SIGNIFICANCE: This large European cohort demonstrates a high genetic diagnostic yield in neonatal-onset DEE, supporting first-line whole-exome sequencing as the preferred first-tier genetic test. The persistence of severe neurodevelopmental impairment despite seizure control highlights the need for precision therapies targeting disease mechanisms in addition to seizure management.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We studied 62 newborns who developed severe epilepsy caused by genetic changes, following them for up to 25 years. We found a genetic cause in over 80% of cases, and genetic testing that reads the entire genetic code was far more effective than tests that only look at specific genes. Although seizures improved in some children over time, nearly all had lasting intellectual disability regardless of seizure control. This suggests that the underlying genetic condition may contribute substantially to brain development in addition to the effects of seizures, although our study cannot determine the relative contribution of each factor.

articles.title: Salt-Sensitive Hypertension Begins With Intracellular K+ and Water Loss.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Na+ and water overload due to inappropriately low renal salt and water excretion is considered the root cause of salt-sensitive hypertension. However, experimental renal and psoriasis hypertension are characterized by chronic predisposition to dehydration. We tested the validity of this alternative hypertension due to loss of water theory in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) salt-sensitive hypertension.

METHODS: We tested the effect of DOCA (25 mg pellet) in mice on a low Na+ diet (0.02%-0.03%) with tap water, or with Na+ in their drinking water (1% NaCl or 1.44% NaHCO3), on body Na+, K+, and water content 2, 6, and 12 days after treatment initiation. We monitored blood pressure with radio-telemetry, food and water intake, and renal electrolyte and water excretion.

RESULTS: At day 2, DOCA NaCl-treated mice elevated blood pressure during a state of isolated body K+ and water loss, indicating substantial intracellular dehydration. Although increasing their fluid intake and urine output, the mice reduced the excretion of free water, indicating renal water conservation. At days 6 and 12, secondary Na+ retention occurred, which replaced the amount of K+ lost and corrected the dehydration, albeit at the expense of an intracellular Na+/K+ redistribution disorder. DOCA NaHCO3-treated mice with Na+-resistant blood pressure showed a comparable Na+/K+ redistribution disorder, but without accompanying early dehydration due to earlier replacement of lost K+ by Na+.

CONCLUSIONS: Experimental DOCA salt-sensitive hypertension initiates with a systemic water conservation response in the face of K+-driven intracellular water loss. Both dehydration and blood pressure increase could be causally treated by oral K+ supplementation.

articles.title: Obesity in Children is Associated With Increased Dengue Virus Binding, but not Neutralizing, Antibody Responses Following Primary Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity has been associated with higher risk of dengue virus (DENV) infection and disease, yet its influence on antibody responses to DENV remains undefined.

METHODS: We evaluated whether nutritional status-based on body mass index z-score (BMIz)-or blood markers of body fat-leptin and adiponectin-are associated with binding and/or neutralizing antibody responses to DENV in 85 children in the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary DENV infection in 2019. Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and DENV infection outcome.

RESULTS: Compared with children with normal weight, those with obesity had higher quantities of DENV binding antibodies (fold-change [FC] 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02, 3.48) but no difference in neutralizing antibodies. Likewise, leptin concentration was associated with higher quantities of binding antibodies (FC 1.22, 95% CI 1.09, 1.37), while adiponectin was associated with lower quantities (FC 0.79, 95% CI .67, .94), and neither was associated with neutralizing antibodies. Lower neutralizing efficiency (neutralizing/binding antibodies) was observed in children with obesity (FC 0.67, 95% CI .48, .93).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) postprimary DENV infection-implying that antibodies generated by children with obesity have lower neutralization efficiency, requiring greater quantities to reach similar levels of neutralization than children with normal weight. Further, the agreement among the 3 models using distinct proxies of body fat-BMIz, leptin, and adiponectin-demonstrates that adipokines are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses.

articles.title: Backcountry Risk-Taking (BRiT)-An Instrument to Evaluate an Individual's Overall Risk-Taking Behavior Within the Backcountry Avalanche Environment.
articles.abstract: Study HypothesisThe primary objective of this study was to develop and evaluate a novel instrument called the Backcountry Risk-Taking Instrument (BRiT) to measure risk-taking behavior among backcountry users. We aimed to create an instrument that is content-valid, grounded in theory, and psychometrically sound.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study to evaluate the psychometric properties of the instrument. Participants completed the newly developed 13-item instrument along with established measures of risk-taking behavior and risk preference to assess convergent validity.ResultsA total of 361 participants completed the survey. After listwise deletion, n = 280 were retained for factor analysis and n = 354 for convergent validity. The resulting instrument provides a concise, empirically supported framework for measuring backcountry risk behavior and establishes a foundation for prospective validation in future cohorts.ConclusionsThe BRiT instrument significantly advances avalanche risk assessment. BRiT demonstrates a clear and stable foundation built upon 3 domains: Core Gear, Avalanche History, and Terrain Choice. Continued validation and refinement across broader populations will strengthen its utility as a foundational tool for both research and applied avalanche risk management.

articles.title: Decoupled Adult and Larval Host Preferences in Tephritid Fruit Flies with a Conserved Oviposition Attractant.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Tephritid fruit flies exhibit considerable variability in host range, yet the chemosensory mechanisms underlying adult host selection and larval performance across species with contrasting dietary breadths remain unclear. Here, we investigated behavioral responses of adults and larvae of four species─Bactrocera dorsalis, B. correcta, Zeugodacus tau, and Z. cucurbitae─to seven fruit and vegetable cues. Adult preferences varied, with guava eliciting the strongest attraction in all species. Larval preferences were weaker and decoupled from adult choices. Comparative transcriptomics of guava-exposed antennae identified OBP19d as the most highly upregulated odorant-binding protein across species. RNAi knockdown of BdOBP19d in B. dorsalis reduced electrophysiological responses to guava volatiles and specifically abolished oviposition preference for 4-Ethylacetophenone. Molecular docking, electrophysiology, and behavioral assays collectively validated this interaction. These results reveal a conserved olfactory module for shared host attraction and identify 4-Ethylacetophenone as a candidate attractant for B. dorsalis females, with potential implications for pest management.

articles.title: Cynarin Targets Host CX3CR1 for Dual-Action Prophylaxis against RSV Infection and Pulmonary Pathology.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Safe, small-molecule prophylactic agents against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are critically lacking. Here, we identify Cynarin, an artichoke-derived dietary polyphenol, as a micromolar affinity CX3CR1 antagonist. Mechanistically, Cynarin confers dual-action protection through two distinct routes: it acts as a "chemical shield" to competitively block viral entry at the epithelial interface by binding CX3CR1, and through a separate CX3CR1-independent mechanism, exhibits intrinsic, virus-independent anti-inflammatory properties by directly suppressing macrophage activation. This target-based interaction was rigorously validated via biochemical and functional assays. In an RSV-infected mouse model, prophylactic administration of Cynarin demonstrated superior efficacy over therapeutic treatment. It significantly reduced pulmonary viral load, ameliorated lung consolidation, and potently suppressed the RSV-induced cytokine storm. Collectively, our findings establish a novel host-directed strategy utilizing Cynarin to target CX3CR1, highlighting the translational potential of food-derived bioactives in offering a dual prophylactic safeguard against viral infection and associated pulmonary pathology.

articles.title: The Rhizobial Type III Effector NopD Regulates the GmPP2C-ENOD93 Axis to Control Symbiotic Nodulation and Yield in Soybean.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Type III effector proteins (T3Es) are pivotal orchestrators of host-microbe interactions and essential for establishing symbiosis, thereby influencing soybean growth and productivity through modulation of symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF). While the central role of the T3E NopD in soybean SNF is recognized, its mechanistic underpinnings have remained elusive. In this study, we determined that GmPP2C, whose expression is regulated by NopD, serves as a regulator of nodulation. Overexpression of GmPP2C suppressed infection-thread formation and markedly reduced nodule number, whereas CRISPR/Cas9-mediated disruption enhanced infection events and partially rescued nodulation defects of NopD deficiency. Transcriptome profiling and complementation assays indicate GmPP2C inhibits nodulation by repressing ENOD93. Loss of GmPP2C increased per-plant yield without altering plant architecture or seed quality. These findings delineate the NopD-GmPP2C-ENOD93 regulatory module governing soybean nodulation and pinpoint GmPP2C as a compelling target for molecular breeding to enhance nitrogen-fixation efficiency and bolster crop yields.

articles.title: Clostridium butyricum Alleviates Meat Quality Deterioration in Eimeria-Infected Lambs Alongside Recovery of Thiamine Diphosphate-Dependent Glucose Metabolism.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Eimeria spp. infection impairs lamb performance and meat quality, but the associated muscle metabolic basis and potential nutritional mitigation remains unclear. Twenty-four lambs were assigned to control (CON), Eimeria-infected (IF), and Eimeria-infected supplemented with Clostridium butyricum (CB; CB-IF) groups. Infection increased drip loss, and reduced cooking yield, whereas CB supplementation improved these traits. Metabolomics analysis revealed reduce thiamine diphosphate (TDP) and 4-methyl-5-hydroxyethylthiazole phosphate (HET-P) after infection, with partial recovery following CB supplementation. Integrated transcriptomic and WGCNA analysis identified coordinated associations among thiamine-related metabolites, glucose- and mitochondrial-metabolism-related gene signatures, and meat-quality traits. RT-qPCR supported the expression patterns of selected transcriptomic candidates. Collectively, CB supplementation alleviated selected meat-quality alterations and was associated with coordinated recovery of thiamine-related and glucose/mitochondrial metabolic signatures during Eimeria spp. infection.

articles.title: Bovine myxovirus resistance protein (Mx)1, but not Mx2, mediates antiviral activity against human and avian influenza A viruses, including H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b.
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have recently infected dairy cows in the United States, raising concerns about human spillover. The antiviral roles of bovine host defense factors, including myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2), remain relatively understudied. We examined bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessed their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. Overexpression of bMx1, but not bMx2, significantly inhibited seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs), low-pathogenic, and highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b, but not influenza B viruses. Conversely, knockdown of bMx1 resulted in enhanced IAV growth. Further, bMx1 inhibited early stages of viral replication, acting to reduce viral transcription and subsequent steps in the viral replication cycle. Known mutations that reduce human MxA (hMxA) activity also impaired bMx1 function, and mutations in the viral nucleoprotein (NP) associated with resistance to hMxA also reduced virus sensitivity to bMx1. Furthermore, phylogenetic analysis showed that a small minority (>0.03%) of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry some of these NP mutations. These findings suggest that while current H5N1 viruses largely remain susceptible to bMx1, viral evolution or opportunistic reassortment could drive Mx resistance and increase pandemic risk.IMPORTANCEHighly pathogenic avian influenza viruses have spilled over into dairy cows and have been circulating on dairy farms in the United States since 2024. The innate antiviral immune responses of cows to influenza viruses have not been extensively studied. In this study, we focused on Mx proteins, a key part of the innate immune defense system toward viruses. We specifically looked at bovine Mx proteins and demonstrated antiviral activity toward different influenza viruses, including the highly pathogenic strains. We also showed that the mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein. Further, we found that a small minority of these avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins. Overall, this work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans.

articles.title: Functional analysis of non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (amino acids 1831-1882) in facilitating pseudorabies virus entry via interaction with glycoproteins gH and gL.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pseudorabies virus (PRV) is the etiological agent responsible for porcine pseudorabies, causing substantial financial losses in the global swine industry. Non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMHC IIA), as an actin-binding motor protein, has been recognized as a functional factor in herpesvirus entry. However, its precise mechanism in PRV invasion remains poorly defined. Our investigation demonstrated that targeted inhibition of NMHC IIA, using a specific chemical inhibitor, siRNA-mediated knockdown, C-terminus of NMHC IIA (sPRA, amino acids [aa] 1672-1981), or rabbit anti-sPRA serum, significantly decreases PRV infection in PK-15 cells in a dose-dependent manner. During the early stage of PRV infection, NMHC IIA underwent rapid and pronounced translocation from the cytoplasm to the cell surface, which is beneficial to the virus entry. The study identified that sPRA mediates PRV internalization by binding to viral glycoproteins gH and gL. Furthermore, we pinpointed the subdomain spanning aa 1831-1882 within sPRA as the critical domain for both mediating the interaction with gH/gL and facilitating viral internalization. These results advance our comprehension of the molecular pathways through which NMHC IIA supports PRV infection and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for PRV intervention.

IMPORTANCE: Pseudorabies virus (PRV), a member of the Alphaherpesvirinae subfamily, not only poses an ongoing threat to the global swine industry but also presents a potential zoonotic risk. Although the host protein NMHC IIA has been identified as a critical factor mediating virus entry, its precise molecular mechanism during PRV infection is still unclear. Herein, we demonstrated that NMHC IIA participates in PRV internalization through binding to viral glycoproteins gH and gL. Moreover, we precisely mapped the critical functional region, spanning amino acids 1831-1882 in the C-terminus of NMHC IIA, responsible for both the viral entry process and the interaction with viral proteins. These findings could deepen the understanding of the interaction mechanism between PRV and the host, and provide a promising broad-spectrum antiviral target.

articles.title: Comparative genome analysis of Corynebacterium ulcerans isolates obtained in Japan.
articles.abstract: Corynebacterium ulcerans is a zoonotic pathogen that causes infections in humans that are clinically indistinguishable from those caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. In many developed countries, including Japan, companion animals such as dogs and cats are the predominant source of C. ulcerans infection. To date, we have collected 106 Japanese clinical and domestic animal isolates of C. ulcerans and a recently branched species, Corynebacterium ramonii, most of which were isolated from humans and cats. In the present study, we performed a comparative analysis of whole-genome sequences from 106 Japanese isolates in our collection and from 597 published isolates, both from Japan and from outside Japan. The Japanese isolates were divided into two distinct lineages: C. ulcerans and C. ramonii. The multilocus sequence types (MLST) of C. ulcerans Japanese isolates exhibited a unique distribution pattern, with one major type (ST 337) accounting for 69.0%, which is very rare in Europe. In addition to Japan, distinct MLST pattern compositions were observed across geographically distinct regions. The sequence types were associated with lysogenized prophage types that encode the diphtheria toxin (tox) gene and were partially associated with toxin production under certain conditions. Through single nucleotide variant (SNV) analysis, transmission from animals to humans has been suggested in some clinical cases.IMPORTANCEA large-scale genome analysis of Corynebacterium ulcerans in Europe has recently been reported, but not yet in Asia. By comparing the genomes of Japanese and European isolates, we demonstrate striking geographic differences in multilocus sequence types and toxigenic prophage compositions between these globally different areas. Notably, we identify the predominance of sequence type ST 337 in Japan. This lineage is rare in Europe and shows that prophage types encoding the diphtheria toxin are closely associated with specific sequence types and toxin production phenotypes. Our single-nucleotide variant analyses further provide genomic evidence supporting zoonotic transmission between companion animals and humans in several clinical cases.

articles.title: Meta-Analysis: Potassium-Competitive Acid Blockers Versus Proton Pump Inhibitors for Gastroprotection in Patients Receiving Antiplatelet Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPIs are standard for gastroprotection during antiplatelet therapy. However, certain PPIs, chiefly omeprazole and esomeprazole, inhibit cytochrome P450 2C19 (CYP2C19), which activates clopidogrel, whereas potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) are metabolised predominantly by CYP3A4.

AIMS: To compare the efficacy of P-CABs with PPIs in preventing gastrointestinal bleeding in adults receiving single or dual antiplatelet therapy.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to 31st May 2026 for randomised and comparative observational studies of P-CABs versus PPIs. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were pooled using random-effects models. The primary outcome was gastrointestinal bleeding; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, revascularisation, stroke, upper gastrointestinal bleeding and platelet reactivity.

RESULTS: We included nine studies (one randomised, eight observational; 34,123 patients). Gastrointestinal bleeding did not differ between groups (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.67-1.18). MACE (RR 0.80, 0.65-0.98); revascularisation (RR 0.77, 0.59-0.99) was less frequent with P-CABs (observational studies only). No differences were seen for all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, or platelet reactivity. Findings may be confounded by study origin, ulcerogenic and acid-suppressive agents, and outcome definitions.

CONCLUSIONS: P-CABs showed no statistically significant difference from PPIs in gastrointestinal bleeding. Lower rates of MACE and revascularisation were from observational studies. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted with caution, as they do not establish non-inferiority or a cardiovascular benefit. Randomised trials are needed to confirm these findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261372513 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews).
