articles.title: Phage-encoded PciP differentially regulates Pseudomonas aeruginosa swarming motility and quorum-sensing-associated phenotypes via CheV-dependent and CheV-independent mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen whose intrinsic antibiotic resistance and complex virulence regulatory networks pose major clinical challenges. Bacteriophages and their encoded proteins have emerged as potential modulators of bacterial physiology, yet the mechanisms by which phage proteins influence bacterial virulence remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified PciP, an early protein encoded by the lytic phage PAYQ66, which suppresses pyocyanin production and swarming motility in P. aeruginosa. PciP reduces PQS levels and suppresses quorum-sensing gene transcription. PciP associates with CheV, and genetic analysis indicates that CheV is required for the PciP-mediated inhibition of swarming but not for the PciP-mediated suppression of PQS and pyocyanin production. Expression of PciP attenuates virulence in infection models. Together, these findings reveal that PciP differentially modulates swarming motility and quorum-sensing-associated phenotypes via CheV-dependent and CheV-independent mechanisms. These results provide mechanistic insights into how a phage-encoded protein reprograms host regulatory networks.IMPORTANCEPseudomonas aeruginosa is a major opportunistic pathogen that is increasingly difficult to treat due to intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance. Bacteriophages encode diverse proteins that can interfere with bacterial regulatory networks, yet many remain functionally uncharacterized. Here, we characterize PciP, a protein encoded by the lytic phage PAYQ66, and show that it modulates bacterial motility and quorum-sensing-associated phenotypes through distinct mechanisms. PciP associates with CheV and inhibits swarming motility in a CheV-dependent manner, whereas PciP-mediated suppression of PQS and pyocyanin production persists in the absence of CheV. These combined effects significantly reduce pathogenicity in both animal and plant infection models. This study advances our understanding of phage-host interactions by demonstrating that a phage-encoded protein can differentially modulate host regulatory outputs via CheV-dependent and CheV-independent mechanisms.

articles.title: Impact of ESKAPE pathogens on the One Health framework considering epidemiology and environmental occurrence.
articles.journal: Microbiology and molecular biology reviews : MMBR
articles.abstract: SUMMARYThe ESKAPE group of pathogens represents one of the most critical threats to global health due to their capacity to evade antimicrobial treatments. This review provides a structured synthesis of the literature addressing antimicrobial resistance mechanisms, epidemiological relevance, clinical impact, and emerging strategies for containment within a One Health framework. Relevant studies and surveillance reports were analyzed to characterize the global distribution and burden of these organisms across human, animal, and environmental settings. The evidence indicates that ESKAPE pathogens remain leading causes of healthcare-associated infections while increasingly being identified in non-clinical reservoirs, highlighting the interconnected nature of antimicrobial resistance. Recent findings point to sustained high morbidity and mortality associated with these pathogens, driven by the expansion of multidrug-resistant lineages, and the limited effectiveness of current therapeutic options. Key challenges identified include gaps in surveillance integration, the spread of resistance determinants across sectors, and variability in infection control practices. Addressing these issues requires coordinated strategies that integrate surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention, and the development of novel therapeutics within a comprehensive One Health approach.

articles.title: Laboratory characteristics associated with microbial identification quality: a national multicenter study based on external quality assessment across China.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Clinical microbiology laboratories are essential for infectious disease diagnosis and antimicrobial stewardship. However, data on laboratory capacity and quality gaps across tertiary hospitals in China remain limited. This multicenter cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate associations between laboratory characteristics and microbial identification performance, and to develop an exploratory prediction model for attainment of the program-defined mutual recognition threshold. Data were collected from 183 tertiary hospital microbiology laboratories across 31 provinces in China. Thirteen baseline laboratory characteristics, including institutional scale, staffing, equipment, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) availability, and ISO 15189 accreditation, were analyzed in relation to microbial identification performance assessed through a standardized national external quality assessment scheme. Correlation analysis, multivariable linear regression, K-means clustering, and logistic regression were used to evaluate associations, performance heterogeneity, and attainment of the program-defined mutual recognition threshold. MALDI-TOF MS availability showed the strongest and most consistent associations with identification performance and was positively associated in adjusted models with fastidious bacteria (β = 9.84, 95% CI 3.65-16.02; P = 0.002), rare bacteria (β = 7.23, 95% CI 4.03-10.43; P < 0.001), yeast (β = 7.16, 95% CI 1.66-12.66; P = 0.011), and total identification scores (β = 45.44, 95% CI 5.38-85.50; P = 0.026). Hospital bed capacity was associated only with yeast identification, while biosafety cabinet number was associated with Salmonella serotyping performance. Cluster analysis identified three performance tiers, supporting the presence of heterogeneity in microbial identification capability. The exploratory prediction model retained MALDI-TOF MS availability and conventional incubator number and showed moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.755), with a sensitivity of 92.9% and specificity of 50.0% at the optimal cutoff probability of 0.524. These findings indicate that technology availability and selected laboratory characteristics are associated with microbial identification performance and may help inform targeted laboratory quality improvement strategies.

IMPORTANCE: Reliable microbial identification underpins infectious disease diagnosis, antimicrobial stewardship, and infection control. However, evidence directly linking routine laboratory resources to standardized identification performance remains limited. In this national multicenter study, standardized external quality assessment results were integrated with 13 baseline laboratory characteristics from 183 tertiary hospital microbiology laboratories across 31 provinces in China. matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) availability emerged as the laboratory characteristic most consistently associated with microbial identification performance, particularly for fastidious bacteria, rare bacteria, yeast, and overall identification scores. Exploratory clustering further demonstrated substantial heterogeneity in performance across laboratories, while a prediction model incorporating MALDI-TOF MS availability and conventional incubator number showed moderate discrimination for attainment of the mutual recognition threshold. These findings provide quantitative evidence that technology availability and broader laboratory capacity characteristics are associated with identification quality and may help guide targeted quality improvement and capacity-building efforts.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of various infection models to provide methodological insights for the characterization of new antivirulence drugs to fight antibioresistance.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infections remain a major global health burden, amplified by the rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Among priority pathogens, the ESKAPEE group represents a critical threat due to their high prevalence in healthcare-associated infections, and their capacity to acquire multidrug resistance. Antivirulence strategies, aiming at disarming pathogens rather than inhibiting their growth, constitute a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics. Their development, however, is hindered by the lack of suitable experimental models to evaluate virulence and antivirulence efficacy. Here, we establish complementary in vitro and in vivo infection models to characterize pathogenicity and assess antivirulence activity against clinically relevant ESKAPEE bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli). We developed a robust nitric oxide (NO)-based in vitro assay that mimics host immune nitrosative stress and enables quantitative evaluation of bacterial resistance to innate immune defenses. In parallel, we established comparative insect infection models using Galleria mellonella and Bombyx species, allowing reproducible assessment of bacterial virulence across multiple hosts and pathogens. These models highlighted marked differences in pathogenic potential depending on both bacterial species and host background. As a proof of concept, we applied these systems to characterize NM102, a first-in-class antivirulence compound targeting the DNA repair protein Mfd. NM102 significantly reduced bacterial survival under NO stress in vitro and decreased bacterial burden in vivo in insect infection models. Together, our results demonstrate that combining immune-mimicking in vitro assays with complementary insect models provides a powerful and ethically acceptable platform to study bacterial pathogenicity and to accelerate the development of innovative antivirulence therapeutics to combat AMR.IMPORTANCEBacterial infections remain a major public health challenge, worsened by the rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance. Among the most concerning pathogens are the ESKAPEE bacteria, which frequently cause hospital-acquired infections and are often resistant to multiple antibiotics. Antivirulence strategies offer promising alternatives to traditional treatments by disarming bacteria rather than killing them, potentially reducing the risk of resistance. However, progress in this field has been limited by the lack of reliable models to measure bacterial virulence and evaluate antivirulence compounds. In this study, we developed complementary models to better assess bacterial pathogenicity and treatment efficacy. We created an in vitro assay that mimics immune defenses and established insect infection models to compare virulence across pathogens and hosts. Using these systems, we tested NM102, a first-in-class antivirulence compound targeting bacterial DNA repair. NM102 reduced bacterial survival and infection severity, highlighting the potential of antivirulence approaches as innovative therapies against drug-resistant infections.

articles.title: Listeria monocytogenes favors the vacuolar compartment during ex vivo human placental infections.
articles.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes poses a serious concern during pregnancy, as these microbes can cross the placental barrier to infect the developing fetus. The pathogen's intracellular lifecycle has been well characterized in cultured cells, where the internalized bacteria escape short-lived Listeria-containing vacuoles (LCVs), replicate in the cytoplasm, and recruit host actin to generate comet tails that enable their intra- and inter-cellular movement. Whether these events occur during intact human placental infections remains unknown. Through ex vivo placental infections, we characterized the spatiotemporal progression of L. monocytogenes in a physiologically relevant system. We found that the actin-rich structures, which are hallmarks of cultured cell infections, were essentially absent (<1% of L. monocytogenes were associated with actin-rich structures). Instead, the bacteria remained predominantly restricted within LCVs, where they also replicated. Quantitative histological and immunofluorescence analyses showed that 39% of wild-type L. monocytogenes remained within Rab5-positive vacuoles and 44% in Lamp1-positive vacuoles, whereas only 1%-4% were observed in cultured placental cells. Most vacuoles lacked the vATPase and cathepsin B, indicating that placental LCV vacuoles were non-acidified, non-degradative endosomal niches. These results closely phenocopied infections using Δhly-L. monocytogenes, which do not generate listeriolysin O (LLO), a bacterial toxin crucial for LCV escape. Together, our findings reveal that L. monocytogenes primarily reside within LCVs during ex vivo human placental infections, contrasting the classical in vitro models and emphasizing the importance of studying bacterial pathogenesis in intact human tissues.IMPORTANCEL. monocytogenes infection during pregnancy can result in miscarriage, stillbirth, or severe neonatal disease because the bacterium can cross the placental barrier. Current understanding of L. monocytogenes pathogenesis is largely based on cultured cell models, where bacteria rapidly escape vacuoles, replicate in the cytoplasm, and spread using host actin. By examining infections in intact ex vivo human placental tissue, we show that this paradigm does not accurately reflect a placental infection. Instead, L. monocytogenes remains predominantly within vacuoles that may support bacterial replication, while actin-based motility is rare. Our work provides new insight into placental listeriosis and highlights the importance of studying host-pathogen interactions in physiologically relevant models.

articles.title: Genomic determinants of fluoroquinolone resistance and delafloxacin activity in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates causing implant-associated bone and joint infections.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Implant-associated bone and joint infections (IA-BJIs) due to Staphylococcus epidermidis are increasingly problematic because of biofilm formation and rising fluoroquinolone resistance. Delafloxacin is a recently approved fluoroquinolone with promising activity against resistant staphylococci; however, genomic determinants of susceptibility in S. epidermidis from IA-BJI remain insufficiently characterized. The aim of this study was to characterize delafloxacin in vitro activity against S. epidermidis clinical isolates from IA-BJI and to define the genomic determinants underlying reduced susceptibility to delafloxacin. This retrospective multicenter study (2022-2026) including 47 S. epidermidis isolates recovered from IA-BJI. Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined by broth microdilution/MIC strips. Multilocus sequence typing, QRDR substitutions (gyrA, gyrB, parC, parE), efflux pump genes, and the presence of the biofilm-associated ica operon were characterized by whole-genome sequencing (MiSeq, Illumina). Thirty-five isolates were levofloxacin-resistant. Among these, delafloxacin MIC50/90 were 0.38 and 1.5 mg/L; 49% (17/35) met the Staphylococcus aureus MIC ≤ 0.25 mg/L susceptibility breakpoint. All levofloxacin-resistant strains carried GyrA-S84 and ParC-S80 substitutions. Cumulative QRDR substitutions were associated with higher delafloxacin MICs (P = 0.0012). ParE substitutions were present in 14/35 isolates. The distribution of efflux pump genes did not differ between groups, whereas the ica operon was strongly associated with quinolone resistance (74% vs 8%; P < 0.001). We also report three osteosynthesis-associated infection cases caused by a levofloxacin-resistant S. epidermidis that achieved clinical cure after 6 weeks of delafloxacin. Delafloxacin retains in vitro activity against a substantial fraction of levofloxacin-resistant S. epidermidis, although higher MICs were associated with greater cumulative QRDR burden. Rapid PCR assays targeting key QRDR substitutions could facilitate genotype-guided therapy and surveillance.

IMPORTANCE: The objective of this multicenter study is to assess the in vitro activity of delafloxacin against Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates from implant-associated osteoarticular infections. We identified genomic mutations associated with reduced in vitro susceptibility, which have potential as an actionable diagnostic strategy, for example, in the form of targeted molecular assays. In addition, three cases of osteosynthesis-associated infections caused by levofloxacin-resistant S. epidermidis isolates are reported. These cases were successfully treated with a 6-week course of delafloxacin, with favorable follow-ups. These strains have been the subject of extensive genomic study, and the resulting data will doubtless prove to be of significant benefit in future research and treatment decision-making. The manuscript is considered to be of significance, as it addresses a clear knowledge gap concerning a clinically important device-associated pathogen that has the potential to guide antimicrobial therapy and surveillance.

articles.title: A putative GtrB-like glycosyltransferase modulates cation-dependent BCP8-2 phage infection and cell surface structure in Bacillus cereus.
articles.abstract: Bacillus cereus is a foodborne pathogen of growing concern due to its persistence and antimicrobial resistance. To identify host determinants influencing susceptibility to phage BCP8-2, a mini-Tn10 transposon mutant library of B. cereus ATCC 14579 was constructed and screened for altered phage susceptibility. A mutant (BC2012) showing partial resistance carried an insertion in BC_RS27090 (previously BC_5432), encoding a putative GtrB-like bactoprenol glycosyltransferase. Complementation restored phage sensitivity, confirming its functional involvement. The mutant showed a slight reduction in efficiency of plating, whereas, adsorption assay revealed significantly reduced phage binding and infectivity, particularly under cation-rich conditions. Furthermore, adsorption kinetics and one-step growth curve in mutant supported that gtrB mutation affects initial adsorption. Microscopy showed altered surface morphology with thinner, smoother cell walls. These data indicate that gtrB affects surface properties essential for cation-dependent phage adsorption and infection and provide a foundation for future studies on the role of surface glycosylation and ionic interactions in Gram-positive phage biology.IMPORTANCEPathogenic Bacillus cereus is resilient across diverse environments and produces diverse toxins linked to foodborne outbreaks. Bacteriophages provide an effective strategy to control B. cereus; however, molecular targets of phage-host interaction are poorly understood, limiting the effective phage-based control. The current study addresses this gap by identifying a putative bactoprenol glycosyltransferase (GtrB), a viral factor in phage BCP8-2 susceptibility. Data obtained highlight a partial reduction of phage infection in the gtrB mutant, demonstrating that GtrB-like glycosyltransferase significantly contributes to BCP8-2 phage infection and adsorption. Our findings provide significant insights into advancing phage therapy, antibiotic resistance, and B. cereus biocontrol in food and clinical settings.

articles.title: Lessons from a multi-country study into persistent and recrudescent trachoma.
articles.abstract: This article summarizes the key lessons learned from a six-country study that collected data on complementary indicators related to Chlamydia trachomatis infection to better understand persistent and recrudescent trachoma. It highlights the practical challenges associated with adding these complementary indicators to routine trachoma surveys (often called 'plus' surveys) and suggests ways to address them. Although more complicated and costly to conduct, 'plus' surveys can improve data for programmatic decision-making and may enable some countries to reach elimination targets sooner.

articles.title: What do we know about expressive writing interventions in helping professions? A focused bibliometric review.
articles.abstract: Expressive writing is widely studied as a psychological intervention supporting emotional processing and well-being, but research involving helping professionals remains limited. This bibliometric study traces the development of scientific production in this area and maps its conceptual structure. A Scopus search identified 167 records, of which 20 documents published between 2009 and 2026 were retained after a PRISMA-based screening. The analysis reveals a small, recently expanding field, with continuous annual publication only since 2021 and output concentrated among a few authors, research groups, journals, and countries, particularly Italy. Its conceptual structure centers on emotional processing and psychological and occupational adjustment, linking burnout, compassion fatigue, coping, job satisfaction, and well-being across palliative care, intensive care, and pandemic-related healthcare contexts. Overall, the field remains context-bound and unevenly developed, highlighting the need for stronger methodological consistency, broader professional and cultural representation, and greater attention to organizational conditions, implementation, and cross-context comparability.

articles.title: A Cross-Sectional Study on Apical Periodontitis in Root-Filled Teeth: Do Clinically Available Factors Reflect Inflammation Level?
articles.abstract:
AIM: Perceived severity of the condition is one of several factors influencing clinical decision-making regarding the management of root-filled teeth with persistent apical radiolucency. However, whether clinically available factors can indicate the severity of persistent apical lesions remains unclear, particularly in asymptomatic cases. The present study aimed to investigate whether factors relating to demographic characteristics, dental history, and clinical and radiographic status reflect inflammation level in apical periodontitis in root-filled teeth. The objective was to improve the understanding of inflammation level in apical lesions associated with asymptomatic root-filled teeth and to support clinical decision-making.

METHODOLOGY: This cross-sectional study was performed on adult patients from a dental clinic in Copenhagen, Denmark. Dental history and clinical information were collected in a pre-designed form, together with radiographic data and biopsies of periapical tissue from root-filled teeth with apical periodontitis, between April 2021 and September 2023. Inflammation level was graded histologically and compared to groups stratified by demographic characteristics, dental history, clinical findings, age and status of root filling and radiographic factors. Inter-observer agreement was assessed using kappa statistics. Data was analysed with One-Way ANOVA, Chi2 test, or Fisher's exact test, and correction for multiple testing was applied using the Holm-Bonferroni method. p-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: One hundred and nine biopsies from 109 patients were included. A significant difference in inflammation level was found between cases categorised as asymptomatic apical periodontitis and cases categorised as symptomatic apical periodontitis (p = 0.023). No significant difference in inflammation level was observed when comparing groups stratified by demographic characteristics, dental history, or clinical or radiographic status in cases categorised as asymptomatic or symptomatic apical periodontitis.

CONCLUSIONS: In root-filled teeth with apical periodontitis, the presence of symptoms and/or clinical manifestation of disease seems to reflect and provide some indication of apical inflammation level. Nonetheless, factors relating to demographic characteristics, dental history and clinical and radiographic status do not seem to reflect the level of apical inflammation. In the clinical decision-making process, caution is therefore warranted when using these factors to estimate inflammatory burden in apical lesions associated with root-filled teeth without symptoms or clinical manifestation of disease.

articles.title: Hospital Readmission After Pediatric Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis of 30-Day Readmission.
articles.abstract: Hospital readmission is common after pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), but estimates vary, and associated factors are poorly characterized. We systematically reviewed unplanned readmission after autologous or allogeneic HSCT in pediatric populations and pooled the proportion readmitted within 30 days after discharge from the index HSCT admission. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for English-language reports published from January 1, 2005, through May 23, 2026. Nineteen reports (nine full-text articles and 10 conference abstracts) were included. Three retrospective single-center cohorts contributed to the primary meta-analysis; 210 of 734 patients were readmitted. The pooled 30-day readmission proportion was 31.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 22.6%-42.4%; I2 = 84.7%). Adding one study of 90-day readmission from transplantation yielded a similar numerical estimate (31.9%; 95% CI: 25.1%-39.4%; I2 = 78.8%), although the outcome was not equivalent. Fever and infection were the most frequent reasons for readmission. Only one study provided adjusted analyses, and most association results were at high risk of bias. Approximately one in three children was readmitted within 30 days after discharge, but the small, heterogeneous evidence base precludes use of this estimate as a universal quality benchmark.

articles.title: Patient-reported outcome measures for depressive symptoms in adults with spinal cord injury: a COSMIN systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the measurement properties of patient-reported measures of depressive symptoms in adults with spinal cord injury and inform their purpose-specific selection and interpretation in clinical and research settings.

DESIGN: Systematic review.

SUBJECTS/PATIENTS: Adults with traumatic or non-traumatic spinal cord injury.

METHODS: 10 databases were searched from inception to 25 June 2026, with reference checking, citation tracking, instrument websites, and targeted searches. Two reviewers independently selected reports, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, rated measurement properties, and graded certainty using current international guidance for outcome measurement instruments.

RESULTS: 28 reports evaluated 27 separately scored versions, forms, or depression subscales from 14 instrument families. The Spinal Cord Injury-Quality of Life Depression Item Bank had the strongest condition-specific development and internal-structure evidence, but evidence gaps and insufficient measurement invariance prevented recommendation. The English Patient Health Questionnaire-9 had sufficient case-finding evidence but insufficient structural validity for interpreting its conventional total score as a clearly unidimensional severity measure. The English depression subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale showed sufficient structural validity, internal consistency, and construct validity. Evidence for measurement error and responsiveness was scarce.

CONCLUSION: No measure had sufficiently complete evidence for routine use across screening, severity assessment, and change measurement.

articles.title: Development of a machine learning (ML) model to predict 3-month response to CGRP monoclonal antibodies in migraine: A pilot evaluation of physician-ML model interaction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting individual treatment responses to anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibodies (CGRP-mAbs) in migraine remains challenging.

OBJECTIVE: To develop a machine learning (ML) model for predicting 3-month treatment response to CGRP-mAbs and to evaluate its practical clinical utility in improving physicians' predictive performance.

METHODS: This retrospective prognostic model development was combined with a prospective, multi-reader, multi-case crossover reader study. We used retrospective data from 228 patients with migraine treated with CGRP-mAbs at the headache outpatient clinic in Dokkyo Medical University from April 2022 to March 2023. The data were divided into training (n = 182) and test (n = 46) datasets. Phase 1: An ML prediction model was developed using the training dataset with Random Forest and five-fold nested cross-validation. The model predicted achievement of a ≥50% reduction in monthly migraine days at 3 months, based on 27 baseline clinical variables. We tested the model's performance on the test dataset. Phase 2: Using the test dataset, five headache specialists and three general neurologists predicted treatment response without the model and then with the model's assistance. Prediction performance was compared between conditions.

RESULTS: Phase 1: The model's performance on the test dataset was as follows: accuracy of 76.1% (95% confidence interval [CI], 62.1%-86.1%), sensitivity (recall) of 87.0% (67.9%-95.5%), specificity of 65.2% (44.9%-81.2%), precision of 71.4% (52.9%-84.7%), F1-score of 78.4% (64.0%-89.4%), and kappa of 0.52 (0.27-0.74) on the test dataset. Phase 2: The eight participating physicians predicted the treatment effectiveness. Without the model, their performance metrics were median accuracy of 65.2% [interquartile range 61.4%-70.1%], mean sensitivity (recall) of 68.5% ± standard deviation 11.6%, specificity of 62.5% ± 18.4%, precision of 66.3% ± 10.3%, F1-score of 66.7% [64.5%-71.9%], and kappa of 0.30 [0.23-0.40]. With the model, these metrics were accuracy of 73.9% [72.8%-76.1%], sensitivity (recall) of 79.9% ± 13.1%, specificity of 64.7% ± 13.6%, precision of 70.2% ± 8.1%, F1-score of 76.6% [74.4%-76.9%], and kappa of 0.48 [0.46-0.52], respectively. The accuracy, sensitivity, F1-score, and kappa were statistically improved. In the switching analysis, which assessed how physicians' predictions changed after receiving ML model assistance, incorrect-to-correct changes occurred in 12.8% (47/368, 8 physicians × 46 cases) of the pooled evaluations, whereas correct-to-incorrect changes occurred in 6.0% (22/368). The overall net switching benefit was +6.8%, and incorrect-to-correct changes occurred significantly more often than correct-to-incorrect changes (p = 0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: Although external validation is necessary, our findings provide preliminary evidence that ML-assisted prediction may support the prediction of CGRP-mAb response.

articles.title: Population-Based Assessment of Cardiometabolic Late Effects in 5-Year Survivors of Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Survival rates for pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) have improved substantially, shifting attention toward long-term health. Epidemiologic data on survivors of pediatric ALL from large, population-based cohorts, particularly in early survivorship, is limited. We addressed this gap by examining the prevalence of diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions among pediatric ALL survivors compared with matched cancer-free peers during the fifth year after diagnosis.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using linked data from the Arkansas Central Cancer Registry (2013-2020) and Arkansas All-Payer Claims Database (2017-2024). Individuals diagnosed with ALL before age 25 years who survived to the fifth year after diagnosis were identified. We matched ALL survivors with three cancer-free peers by exact matching on sex, race, ethnicity, birth year, Medicaid enrollment history, and county of residence. Cardiometabolic outcomes were identified using claims-based diagnoses among the ALL survivors and matched controls. We examined differences in cardiometabolic outcomes between ALL survivors and matched controls.

RESULTS: ALL survivors (n = 142; age range 4-30 years) experienced a significantly higher burden of cardiometabolic conditions compared with matched controls (n = 426; 10.6% vs. 1.2%, p < 0.01). ALL survivors had higher prevalence of hypertension (4.9% vs. 0.9%; p < 0.01) and diabetes mellitus (4.9% vs. 0.2%; p < 0.01). Differences were more pronounced among ALL survivors aged ≥ 14 years, among whom 20.4% (vs. 2.0%; p < 0.01) had at least one cardiometabolic condition.

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric ALL survivors experience elevated cardiometabolic risk as early as five years after diagnosis, particularly during adolescence. Early screening and preventive strategies are needed to reduce long-term cardiometabolic burden among pediatric ALL survivors.

articles.title: Human Consensus Versus Generative Artificial Intelligence When Assessing the Methodological Quality and Overall Confidence in the Results of Systematic Reviews With Meta-Analysis in Endodontology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the level of agreement between ChatGPT-5.5 and human assessments when appraising the methodological quality and overall confidence of the results of systematic reviews (SRs) with meta-analysis (MA) in endodontology.

METHODS: SRs with MA related to endodontology and published in English between 2021 and 2024 were included. The methodological quality of the SRs was appraised by three human experts using AMSTAR 2, and a consensus dataset was generated. ChatGPT-5.5 was applied to generate AMSTAR 2 item-level ratings and overall confidence classifications for each SR through three newly created accounts. Agreement between consolidated ChatGPT-5.5 ratings and human consensus was assessed for both overall confidence and each AMSTAR 2 item. Overall-confidence agreement was evaluated under the primary criterion (Partial Yes = Yes) and an alternative sensitivity criterion (Partial Yes = No). Direct agreement and linearly weighted Cohen's kappa were calculated, and complete 3/3 agreement was used to assess consistency across ChatGPT-5.5 accounts.

RESULTS: One hundred SRs were included. Human consensus and ChatGPT-5.5 classified 47 and 85 SRs, respectively, as critically low. Under the primary criterion (Partial Yes = Yes), overall confidence matched in 52/100 SRs (52%; weighted κ = 0.182). Under the alternative criterion (Partial Yes = No), agreement increased to 83%, while weighted κ remained similar (κ = 0.173), indicating that direct agreement was sensitive to the handling of Partial Yes. Item-level agreement varied substantially. Overall confidence was identical across the three ChatGPT-5.5 accounts in 85 SRs, and global item-level 3/3 agreement was 86.12%. In the 100 sampled SRs, 15% met the criterion for reporting primary-study funding and 21% for justifying study designs.

CONCLUSION: Overall-confidence direct agreement was sensitive to the handling of Partial Yes ratings, whereas chance-corrected agreement remained similar under both criteria. ChatGPT-5.5 assigned lower overall confidence classifications more frequently than human consensus, and agreement varied across AMSTAR 2 domains. Although outputs were frequently consistent across the three ChatGPT-5.5 accounts, between-account consistency did not ensure concordance with human judgements. The findings do not support the use of ChatGPT-5.5 as an independent AMSTAR 2 assessor; any exploratory application requires item-by-item verification by reviewers with methodological expertise.

articles.title: Changes in CGM-Derived Glycemic Metrics and Triglyceride-Glucose Index During Ramadan in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Using Real-Time Continuous Glucose Monitoring.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate longitudinal changes in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived glycemic metrics, glycemia risk indices (GRIs), triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, and diabetes self-management before, during, and after Ramadan fasting in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) receiving non-intensive diabetes therapy and using real-time CGM (rtCGM).

METHODS: This ambispective longitudinal cohort study included 110 adults with T2D managed at a tertiary diabetes center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The study combined retrospective ascertainment of pre-enrollment data with prospective follow-up from enrollment during Ramadan through the post-Ramadan period. Glycemic outcomes were assessed across pre-Ramadan, Ramadan, and post-Ramadan periods using CGM-derived metrics, including time in range (%TIR70-180), time above range, glucose variability, GRI, and hypoglycemia indices. The TyG index and Perceived Diabetes Self-Management Scale (PDSMS) were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Compared with the pre-Ramadan period, median %TIR70-180 increased significantly during Ramadan from 60.8% to 65.0% (P < .001), while median sensor glucose decreased from 187 to 175 mg/dL (P < .001). Glucose variability also improved during Ramadan (36.5% vs 32.0%, P < .001), accompanied by lower GRI values (38.0 vs 35.3, P < .001). Severe hypoglycemia exposure (time below range, %TBR<54) remained unchanged (P = .358), although mild hypoglycemia exposure increased modestly. The TyG index decreased during Ramadan (9.65 vs 9.55, P = .003), whereas PDSMS scores increased from 27.0 to 29.0 (P < .001). Several glycemic and metabolic parameters demonstrated post-Ramadan rebound toward pre-Ramadan levels. No hospitalizations or treatment-escalation events occurred during Ramadan.

CONCLUSION: Improved glycemic control, reduced hyperglycemia exposure, and enhanced diabetes self-management were observed during Ramadan among selected adults with T2D receiving non-intensive diabetes therapy, rtCGM, and structured Ramadan-focused support, with stable severe hypoglycemia exposure despite a modest increase in mild hypoglycemia.

articles.title: Multisystem Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Active Comparators in Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) beyond cardiometabolic outcomes are incompletely characterized against active comparators in type 2 diabetes (T2D). We compared GLP-1RA with sulfonylureas (SUs), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is) in adults with T2D.

METHOD: In a multicenter target trial emulation across 5 University of California academic medical centers (2012-2025) using harmonized electronic health record data, adults with T2D newly initiating GLP-1RA, SU, SGLT2i, or DPP4i were propensity score-matched 1-to-1 within site via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (>11 000 covariates), with up to 5-year follow-up. We screened 181 prespecified incident outcomes across 15 body systems, pooling hazard ratios by random-effects meta-analysis. Robustness required leave-one-medical-center-out stability, E-value ≥1.5, and false discovery rate-adjusted P < .10.

RESULTS: Among 70 982 matched adults, 118 robust associations were identified (65 for reduced risk and 53 for increased risk). Risk reductions were most consistent for cardiovascular outcomes, including myocarditis/cardiomyopathy (summary hazard ratio, 0.38 [95% CI, 0.32-0.44] vs SGLT2i), acute myocardial infarction (0.53 [0.42-0.66]), heart failure (0.71 [0.58-0.88] vs DPP4i), and thromboembolism (0.69-0.72), and for nephritis/nephrosis (0.73 [0.67-0.79]), nutritional anemia (0.70-0.81), coagulation disorders (0.73-0.81), and tobacco-related disorders (0.60 [0.49-0.74]). Risk increases were found for musculoskeletal conditions (22 associations); osteoarthritis 1.48 (1.29-1.68), stress fractures 1.68 (1.15-2.47), diverticular disease (1.18-1.33), sleep-wake disorders (1.27-1.54), and menopausal disorders (1.32-1.52).

CONCLUSIONS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist initiation was associated with reduced cardiovascular, renal, hematologic, and tobacco-related risk, consistent with outcome trials. Increased risks for musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, and sleep-wake disorders warrant monitoring as the clinical use of GLP-1RAs continues to expand.

articles.title: OCT‑Detected Endocardial Abnormality and Minimal Tunnel Area in Patients With Patent Foramen Ovale: Associations With Thrombus Formation.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In situ thrombus formation represents one of the key pathogeneses of patent foramen ovale (PFO)‑related disorders. This study aimed to explore factors contributing to in situ thrombus in patients with PFO‑related diseases.

AIMS: This study aimed to explore factors contributing to in situ thrombus in patients with PFO-related diseases.

METHODS: Forty‑six prospectively enrolled patients with PFO‑related disorders underwent OCT imaging to explore potential contributing factors for in situ thrombus. None of the enrolled participants presented with concomitant lower‑extremity venous thrombosis or atrial fibrillation, and no alternative pathogenic factors were detected.

RESULTS: In 63.04% of the cases (29 individuals), an in situ thrombus was present in the PFO tunnel. Patients with in situ thrombus exhibited a notably smaller right PFO area and minimum area, along with a higher incidence of abnormal endocardium than those without thrombus. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified PFO minimum area and abnormal endocardium as independent factors associated with in situ thrombus.

CONCLUSIONS: Our exploratory analysis suggests that endocardial abnormality and a smaller minimal PFO‑tunnel area may correlate with a higher risk of thrombus formation, offering clues regarding possible mechanisms behind PFO‑related diseases.

articles.title: Snare-Assisted Retrieval of a Mechanically Locked-Open TEER Device: A Novel Bailout Technique.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established intervention for patients having severe mitral regurgitation (MR) with prohibitive surgical risk. Complications during deployment related to device malfunction are uncommon but necessitate prompt decision-making and management. A 54-year-old gentleman with dilated cardiomyopathy, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and severe MR underwent TEER using the MyClip system (Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd., Vapi, Gujarat, India). Initial deployment across the A2-P2 scallops of mitral leaflets achieved partial MR reduction. Significant residual MR required a second clip for optimal leaflet coaptation. While deploying the second clip, it failed to close because of a mechanical locking failure. So, we everted the clip, pulled back to LA, and it stayed in open position and failed to close. We report a novel bailout snare technique that enabled safe retrieval without the need for a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal minimized the risk of tearing the atrial septum and facilitated the successful completion of the TEER procedure. Another clip was deployed successfully, resulting in significant MR reduction. This case demonstrates a rare complication during deployment, a malfunction of the device, and a novel strategy for safely bailing out a challenging intra-procedural complication.

articles.title: Survival and immunomodulatory therapy in autoimmune disease-associated progressive pulmonary fibrosis: a multicenter registry (NEREA).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the mortality rate related to interstitial lung disease (ILD) in autoimmune-ILD patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF), and to evaluate the role of immunomodulatory therapy and other variables in the ILD-related mortality.

METHODS: A longitudinal multicenter study was conducted in autoimmune ILD from 2005 to 2024 in Madrid. Patients were those enrolled in NEREA [pNEumology RhEumatology Autoinmune] registry who met PPF criteria. Main outcome was specific-cause mortality related to ILD. Independent variable: immunomodulatory therapy. Covariates: sociodemographic, clinical, other treatments. Survival techniques were used to estimate the cause specific mortality rate due to ILD (MR) and 95%CI, expressed per 100 patients-year. Fine-Gray competing risk regression models assessed the risk of immunomodulatory therapy on ILD-related mortality (results expressed as subhazard ratio (SHR) and 95%CI).

RESULTS: Among 158 patients, 70.3% were on immunomodulatory therapy at PPF baseline, increasing to 81% during follow-up. 47 deaths were documented, and 79% of them were attributed to ILD-related causes with a MR of 6.2 [4.5-8.5]. MR was lower in patients who received immunomodulatory therapy, with a mean survival of 4.8 years in untreated patients and over 10 years in those who received treatment. Immunomodulatory therapy improved survival regardless other factors (SHR: 0.35 [0.19-0.66], p = 0.001). Additionally, a worse diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)% (<60), and to have emphysema independently increased the risk of ILD-related mortality.

CONCLUSION: The study shows a considerable mortality directly attributable to ILD. Furthermore, it demonstrates a survival benefit in patients receiving immunomodulatory therapy regardless other factors.

articles.title: rustybam: a composable toolkit for alignment analysis and visualization with SafFire.
articles.abstract:
SUMMARY: We present rustybam, a Rust-based command-line toolkit for CIGAR-aware manipulation of PAF and BAM alignments, and SafFire, a browser-based tool for interactive genome comparison visualization with annotation overlays. rustybam's composable subcommands provide overlap resolution, coordinate liftover, alignment splitting at structural variants, scaffolding, and identity statistics.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Both tools are open source under the MIT license. rustybam is available via Bioconda (https://anaconda.org/bioconda/rustybam), crates.io, and GitHub (https://github.com/vollgerlab/rustybam). SafFire is hosted at https://vollgerlab.com/SafFire/ with source code at https://github.com/vollgerlab/SafFire. Archived versions are available on Zenodo: rustybam (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4654875) and SafFire (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5765964).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).

CONCLUSION: LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.

articles.title: Label‑Free Optical Biosensing of Interleukin‑6, Procalcitonin, and High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein as Inflammatory Biomarkers in Cardiovascular Disease: A Review.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is closely related to inflammation, but traditional laboratory methods are too slow for use during acute cardiac treatment. Label‑free optical biosensors, specifically surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and fiber‑optic sensors, provide rapid detection of low‑abundance biomolecules. We will review three biomarkers that can be used in combination to assess inflammation status (interleukin 6), bacterial infection status (procalcitonin), and chronic risk of future CVD (high sensitivity C-reactive protein). Development of new materials for use as transducers, new biorecognition elements, and new microsystems will be highlighted along with challenges associated with those developments including problems associated with specific biological matrices, issues related to scalability of production of devices, and regulatory concerns. Clinically, a portable optical biosensor designed to measure the three biomarkers from a drop of blood taken from a finger would allow for differentiation between sterile inflammation and infective endocarditis, guidance regarding appropriate use of antibiotics, and stratification of long term risk for developing CVD at the bedside. This review demonstrates that optical biosensing technology and clinical needs are aligned for developing personalized point‑of‑care diagnostic systems in CVD.

articles.title: Financial Toxicity and Diabetes Distress in Adults With Elevated A1C: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to examine whether financial toxicity was independently associated with diabetes distress among adults with diabetes and elevated A1C.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 566 adults with diabetes and elevated A1C. Guided by the biopsychosocial model, we used sequential multiple linear regression to test whether financial toxicity explained additional variance in diabetes distress after accounting for biological, psychological, demographic, and other social factors. We measured diabetes distress using the 2-item Diabetes Distress Scale, financial toxicity with a validated financial toxicity measure, psychological distress with the 4-item Patient Health Questionnaire, and unmet social needs with a 21-item index.

RESULTS: Financial toxicity was independently associated with higher diabetes distress after accounting for biological, psychological, and other social factors. Psychological distress was the strongest correlate of diabetes distress, followed by A1C and financial toxicity. As a block, social factors added significant variance, but the association of unmet social needs was no longer significant once financial toxicity was included, indicating shared variance among social and economic stressors. Male gender was associated with lower diabetes distress, whereas the associations for lower education and unemployment emerged only after adjustment and should be interpreted with caution.

CONCLUSIONS: Screening for financial toxicity and psychological distress, together with an integrated mental health and financial support model, may help diabetes care and education specialists address the emotional and material contributors of diabetes distress in adults with elevated A1C.

articles.title: MUC5B Overproduction Disrupts Club Cell Mediated Alveolar Repair in COPD.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by small airway disease (SAD) and emphysema, but mechanisms linking these pathologies remain unclear. SAD arises early and is the primary site of airflow limitation, marked by epithelial injury, mucus obstruction, and bronchiole loss. Excessive production of the mucin MUC5B by bronchiolar club cells is a key feature of SAD and is associated with impaired mucociliary clearance and inflammation. Club cells also function as progenitors for alveolar type II (ATII) cells, yet how their regenerative capacity is altered in COPD is unknown.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether MUC5B overproduction in small airway club cells alters their capacity to regenerate ATII cells and contributes to emphysema progression.

METHODS: We assessed MUC5B expression in human emphysematous lungs and a porcine pancreatic elastase (PPE)-induced mouse model of emphysema. Genetic approaches were used to overexpress or conditionally delete Muc5b in club cells to evaluate effects on club-to-ATII differentiation, alveolar structure, and lung function in health and emphysema.

RESULTS: MUC5B is overexpressed in small airway club cells in human emphysematous lungs and animal models. Muc5b overexpression impairs differentiation of club cells into ATII cells and worsened lung function decline in emphysema. Importantly, conditional deletion of Muc5b during early disease stages restored club cell-derived alveolar regeneration.

CONCLUSIONS: MUC5B overproduction links SAD to defective alveolar repair by limiting club cell progenitor function. Targeting MUC5B may restore epithelial regeneration and slow early COPD progression.

articles.title: Bacterial Surfaces and Barriers: Biogenesis and Pathogen-Host Interactions.
articles.abstract: The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Cardiovascular Mortality in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased cardiovascular mortality, but the relative contributions of OSA-specific parameters versus classical cardiometabolic risk factors remain poorly defined.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 4,368 consecutive adults referred for diagnostic polysomnography at a tertiary sleep center and followed for up to 20 years. The primary outcome was cause-specific cardiovascular mortality ascertained by national death registry linkage. Analyses integrated cause-specific Cox regression, Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, and a random survival forest (RSF) competing-risk model (1000 trees; 70/30 train-test split). Gower-distance-based hierarchical clustering of RSF-predicted cumulative incidence identified patient phenotypes.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 8.6 years (interquartile range 6.7-12.5), 335 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Heart failure (30.4%), chronic ischemic heart disease (14.0%), and acute myocardial infarction (11.6%) were the leading causes. Independent predictors were age (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.10, per year), male sex (1.68, 1.29-2.18), active smoking (1.68, 1.30-2.15), hypertension (1.73, 1.29-2.33), atrial fibrillation (2.16, 1.56-2.98), prior myocardial infarction (1.71, 1.25-2.35), and diabetes (1.37, 1.06-1.76). Nocturnal desaturation lost significance after multivariable adjustment. Among patients with an apnea-hypopnea index ≥15 events/h, a good continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) response was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (0.72, 0.55-0.96). The RSF C-index was 0.80. Six phenotypes showed cardiovascular mortality of 2.9% to 14.4%.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular mortality in OSA was driven predominantly by classical cardiometabolic risk factors rather than by nocturnal hypoxemic burden or CPAP response. Comorbidity-targeted prevention should be prioritized, and phenotype-aware stratification may identify subgroups warranting intensified cardiovascular surveillance.

articles.title: No significant change in urinary sodium excretion within 48h after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery: the weight LUSER study.
articles.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic and bariatric surgery is effective in achieving remission of hypertension and metabolic disease. It is unclear whether metabolic changes within the first 48h after surgery can potentially explain underlying mechanisms of hypertension control. We aimed to assess changes in urinary sodium excretion early after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) as a potential weight-loss-independent mechanism of hypertension remission.

METHODS: All patients undergoing primary RYGB provided a 24-h urine collection, blood pressure (BP) measurement, and blood sampling both preoperatively and 48h postoperatively. The dietary sodium content was similar at both time points.

RESULTS: Twenty patients were included, of whom 16 met the minimum output urine volume criteria for 24-h urine samples. Mean patient age was 55.2 ± 7.7 years and median body mass index was 48kg/m2 with 13 patients (65%) diagnosed with hypertension and 7 (35%) with obstructive sleep apnoea. Twenty-four-hour urine sodium excretion was similar immediately prior to surgery and 48h postoperatively (72.1 ± 44.0 vs 74.5 ± 65.2mmol/24h, p = 0.45). There was no significant difference in systolic or diastolic BP immediately prior to surgery compared with 48h postoperatively (143.3 ± 15.1 vs 135.9 ± 16.3mmHg, p = 0.09 and 79.8 ± 9.2 vs 79.9 ± 5.8mmHg, p = 0.47). Both findings were confirmed on further sensitivity analysis.

CONCLUSION: No significant change in urinary sodium excretion or BP was detected in the first 48h post RYGB in normotensive patients or those with well-controlled hypertension.

articles.title: The Complete Story: Packaged Testing and Missed Opportunities in Sexually Transmitted Infection Screening in a Large Midwestern Healthcare System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concurrent, or "packaged," testing for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and syphilis during gonorrhea and chlamydia (GC/CT) screening may improve early detection of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), but this practice remains inconsistently implemented. We aimed to assess the prevalence of, and factors associated with, packaged STI testing in a large healthcare system.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study analyzing adult encounters from January 2019 through September 2025 with GC/CT testing at a large Midwestern academic hospital system. We defined packaged testing as concurrent testing for HIV, syphilis, and GC/CT. Multivariable logistic regression models using generalized estimating equations were fitted to assess associations with packaged testing, accounting for repeated encounters per patient.

RESULTS: Among 318,917 eligible encounters from 170,183 patients, 31.8% of encounters received packaged testing. Those aged ≥ 25 had higher odds of receiving packaged testing compared to younger individuals, while women (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.52-0.55) had lower odds compared to men. Emergency department encounters (aOR 0.11, 95% CI 0.11-0.12) had the lowest odds, whereas outpatient infectious diseases had the highest (aOR 3.32, 95% CI 3.07-3.60), all relative to primary care. Black race, lower income, and Medicaid insurance were associated with higher likelihood of testing relative to their respective reference groups. Overall packaged testing rates increased over the study period across settings.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large Midwestern healthcare system, packaged STI testing rates remain low, with disparities across demographic groups and clinical settings. These findings underscore opportunities for setting-specific and resource-aware interventions to improve screening practices.

articles.title: Preventing Clostridioides difficile Infection and Recurrence: Practical Strategies for Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization worldwide. Although advances in antimicrobial stewardship and infection prevention have reduced healthcare-associated disease in some settings, the incidence of community-associated CDI and the persistent burden of recurrent CDI (rCDI) continue to pose substantial clinical challenges. Because recurrent disease is fundamentally driven by persistent disruption of the intestinal microbiome and loss of colonization resistance, prevention has emerged as the central strategy for reducing long-term disease burden. This review summarizes contemporary evidence supporting prevention of both incident and rCDI, emphasizing practical approaches for gastroenterologists. Primary prevention centers on minimizing modifiable risk factors through antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention and control, diagnostic stewardship to distinguish colonization from infection, and strategies to preserve the intestinal microbiome. For patients with CDI, we review evidence supporting extended antibiotic regimens, oral vancomycin prophylaxis during subsequent systemic antibiotic exposure, and microbiome restoration therapies, including conventional fecal microbiota transplantation and US Food and Drug Administration-approved microbiota-based therapies, which have transformed secondary prevention by restoring microbial diversity and colonization resistance. Special consideration is given to populations at particularly high risk for recurrence, including older adults, immunocompromised individuals, transplant recipients, and patients with inflammatory bowel disease. Finally, we discuss emerging preventive strategies, including precision risk stratification, microbiome- and metabolome-based biomarkers, bile acid modulation, and approaches targeting asymptomatic colonization. Together, these advances signal a paradigm shift from treating CDI episodes to implementing personalized preventive strategies that interrupt the cycle of recurrent disease and improve long-term patient outcomes.

articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential and Bone Mineral Density in Cohorts from Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: A somatic mutation causing clonal expansion in hematopoietic stem cells (HSC), but not resulting in hematologic malignancy, is termed clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP). CHIP is associated with non-hematologic disorders, including accelerated atherosclerosis, heart failure, ischemic stroke, gout, liver disease, and kidney disease. Because osteoclasts are derived from the macrophage-monocyte lineage of HSCs, changes in the bone marrow niche due to CHIP may drive changes in BMD. To investigate whether CHIP may be related to BMD, we used CHIP mutation calls from the Trans-omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) whole genome sequencing data and DXA derived BMD from multiple cohorts. Data from the the Amish cohort, Cardiovascular Health Study, the Framingham Heart Study, San Antonio Family Study, and the Women's Health Initiative were combined for analysis. Multiple linear regression was used to determine the association between CHIP mutation status and BMD, adjusting for cohort, age, age,2 sex, and, for family-based cohorts, empiric kinship estimated from genotype data. CHIP mutation status was analyzed both as a binary variable (any CHIP mutation) and as an ordinal variable (no CHIP mutation, 1 CHIP mutation in any gene, two or more CHIP mutations in a single gene, two or more CHIP mutations in different genes). A total of 3368 samples had both CHIP and BMD data, and 10.9% of samples contained any CHIP mutation. The presence of any CHIP mutations was not associated with either femoral neck or lumbar spine BMD; however, the presence of two or more CHIP mutations in different genes was positively associated with LSBMD (beta = 0.36, p = .015). We found no overall association between the presence of CHIP mutations and BMD in a large, diverse sample of genomes. Our findings of greater BMD in persons harboring multiple CHIP mutations confirm mouse models demonstrating that Dnmt3a and Tet2 mutations independently cause increased BMD.

articles.title: A NATA Task Force: Preventing Exertional Heat Stroke Death in American Football Linemen.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Linemen make up over 90% of all exertional heat stroke (EHS) deaths in collegiate and secondary school American football deaths.

PURPOSE: This document aims to accomplish 3 purposes: (1) briefly summarize the need for specific risk reduction recommendations for EHS in secondary school and collegiate American football linemen, (2) provide new recommendations for the reduction of EHS in football linemen developed with Delphi procedures to build consensus, and (3) summarize the evidence for the existing and new best-practice recommendations that currently exist for EHS risk reduction.

DESIGN: Delphi-based Task Force Recommendations.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary group of experts was convened to build consensus on EHS risk reduction strategies for secondary school and collegiate football linemen. The process involved a narrative review of relevant literature, followed by iterative rounds of anonymous Delphi surveys to refine and validate the recommendations.

RESULTS: A total of 20 recommendations were identified, scored, and retained for EHS risk reduction in American football linemen. Key recommendations include the education of coaches and strength and conditioning coaches on EHS risk reduction and treatment, the implementation of heat acclimatization protocols, and weather-based exercise modifications. The recommendations emphasize the importance of the avoidance of high-intensity aerobic testing during transition periods and the importance of having on-site cooling modalities.

CONCLUSION: The high rates of EHS in American football linemen highlight the need for targeted risk reduction strategies. In American football, the design and implementation of workouts for linemen must differ from other players on the team. Linemen require position-specific work-to-rest ratios and tailored training programs.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: By adhering to best practices and continuously updating guidelines based on emerging evidence, the safety and well-being of American football players can be significantly enhanced. These recommendations provide a comprehensive framework for reducing the risk of EHS and improving outcomes for American football linemen.

articles.title: Post-approval modification of high-risk chronic pain devices approved through the FDA premarket approval pathway, 1981-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk chronic pain devices undergo postapproval modifications via supplement pathways with varying evidentiary requirements, but their extent has not been systematically characterized.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of PMA-approved chronic pain devices (1981-2023) using supplement data from openFDA and recall data from the FDA Medical Device Recalls database (2005-2025).

RESULTS: Seventeen original PMAs were identified: 8 spinal cord stimulators (47.1%), 7 shock-wave generators (41.2%); 10 (58.8%) were implantable. Fourteen devices (82.4%) generated 1,343 supplements over a median follow-up of 4.5 years (IQR, 2.8-20.7). Supplement activity was highly concentrated: 3 spinal cord stimulators accounted for 83.2% of all modifications. Among the three highest-contributing PMAs, median inter-supplement intervals were 11, 12, and 22.5 days. Most used 30-Day Notice (56.3%) or Real-Time pathways (17.3%). Process or manufacturing changes accounted for 61.4% of supplements, followed by design changes (24.6%). From 2005-2025, 93 recalls occurred, 91 (97.8%) involving spinal cord stimulators; 87.1% were Class II recalls.

CONCLUSIONS: Extensive postmarket modification of high-risk chronic pain devices was concentrated in a small number of implantable spinal cord stimulators and occurred mainly via pathways not requiring new clinical data. These findings underscore the importance of interpreting marketed devices in the context of their complete postapproval histories.

articles.title: How to use a formulation approach to understand behavioural expressions of need in people with dementia.
articles.abstract: Distress, also known as behavioural expressions of need, is highly common in people with dementia. The Newcastle Model offers a formulation-based approach in which holistic information is gathered to generate hypotheses about the causes of a person's distress. It encourages health and social care professionals to use curiosity in order to understand the individual's underlying unmet needs and respond with person-centred support. This article provides a step-by-step guide for nurses on how to apply this approach in practice. • Behavioural expressions of need are common in people with dementia and often challenging for the person, their families and professional carers. • The Newcastle Model is an evidence-based approach that can be used by nurses and other health and social care professionals in all settings to think about a person's needs holistically. • Recognising and understanding a person's behaviour as an expression of need can enable the provision of physical, psychological and social support. REFLECTIVE ACTIVITY: 'How to' articles can help to update your practice and ensure it remains evidence based. Apply this article to your practice. Reflect on and write a short account of: • How this article might improve your practice when caring for a person with dementia who is experiencing a behavioural expression of need. • How you could use this information to educate nursing students or your colleagues on the appropriate technique and evidence base for supporting a person with dementia who is experiencing a behavioural expression of need.

articles.title: Is More Always Better? Dose Ranging for Pentaspline Pulsed Field Ablation.
Rehabilitation to support leisure participation following stroke: a national survey of clinical practice in Australia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe how allied health clinicians assess and treat leisure participation after stroke and identify factors influencing their practice.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Allied health clinicians working in health and disability settings completed an online survey. Assessment and intervention approaches were collected with survey questions aligned to the TIDieR checklist. Perceived barriers to providing leisure rehabilitation were captured using the 26-item Determinants of Implementation Behaviour Questionnaire.

RESULTS: Among the 131 clinicians who completed the survey, the largest proportion of respondents were occupational therapists (35%), physiotherapists (35%), and speech pathologists (18%). Most referred to clinical guidelines to inform their leisure rehabilitation practice. Of the 105 assessments reportedly used, only seven included a leisure-specific item or scale. Common intervention approaches included targeting underlying impairments (upper limb [44%] and mobility [44%]) and modifying activities (54%). Barriers to providing leisure rehabilitation included limited funding, training and resources.

CONCLUSION: Allied health clinicians rely on guidelines that do not meaningfully inform leisure rehabilitation, leaving practice dependent on individual reasoning and inconsistent access to resources. Further research to understand clinicians' clinical reasoning and training needs can inform the design of effective leisure-focused interventions and help address a clear gap in stroke rehabilitation.

articles.title: Three medication experience profiles after percutaneous coronary intervention show no detected differences in questionnaire networks.
Ventricular False Tendons and Ventricular Arrhythmias: Distinguishing Incidental Findings From Culprit Substrates.
articles.abstract: Ventricular false tendons are fibrous or fibromuscular cords that cross the ventricular cavity. Some contain Purkinje tissue and have been implicated in premature ventricular complexes, left posterior fascicular ventricular tachycardia, and, rarely, ventricular fibrillation. However, false tendons are also common in healthy hearts, so their visibility does not establish causality. This narrative review critically appraises the evidence and addresses three unresolved mechanistic questions. First, it is unclear whether a posteroseptal tendon forms the circuit of fascicular tachycardia or carries part of the adjacent Purkinje network. Control data are lacking, and ablation lesions involve both structures. Second, the slow, decremental, and verapamil-sensitive conduction of the P1 pathway may reflect abnormal Purkinje tissue, reduced electrical coupling, or mixed tissue composition. Third, successful ablation sites cluster at tendon insertions. We propose a junctional hypothesis in which the insertion, where a thin Purkinje-containing cord must depolarize a large myocardial mass, may form an arrhythmogenic interface. This model is untested but may account for insertion-based targets, verapamil sensitivity, and exit shifts. We also propose a graded framework that classifies a tendon as an unlikely, possible, probable, or definite culprit. A definite grade requires concordant anatomical, electrical, imaging, and procedural evidence plus at least one observation that separates the tendon from adjacent tissue. By these criteria, most reported culprit tendons are probable rather than definite. A false tendon is best regarded as a visible segment of the Purkinje network whose arrhythmogenic potential may depend on how and where it couples to the myocardium.

articles.title: Fluoxetine attenuates asthma symptoms in a murine model through modulation of innate and adaptive immune components, and regulation of RORγt signalling axis in a pathogenic Th17 cell population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory airway disease, characterised by dysregulated interactions between innate and adaptive immune cells. Although Th2-mediated inflammation predominates, persistent Th17-associated immune responses contribute to chronic airway inflammation implicated in the corticosteroid-insensitive disease state. Fluoxetine, a SSRI with immunomodulatory properties, was investigated to determine its effects on inflammation and Th17 response in experimental allergic airway disease.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Immunomodulatory effects of fluoxetine evaluated in exploratory in vitro assays. In vivo studies were performed in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic asthma using oral fluoxetine at clinically relevant doses. Airway pathology, immunophenotypes, cytokine production, gene and protein expression were evaluated by histology, flow cytometry, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), confocal microscopy and ex vivo functional assays. Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with target enrichment analyses, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations used to explore potential molecular interactions.

KEY RESULTS: Fluoxetine reduced the inflammatory response in activated macrophages without noticeable cytotoxicity. In an allergic asthma model, fluoxetine attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, eosinophilia, IgE production and pulmonary macrophage activation, whilst reducing the accumulation of the phenotypically granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor like cell population along with diminished T-cell activation and reduced Th17 responses, reduced IL-17 production together with decreased expression and nuclear localisation of RORγt. Ex vivo studies confirmed inhibition of RORγt expression and IL-17 production in Th17 cells. Transcriptomic integration identified significant enrichment of Th17-associated inflammatory pathways, whereas molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses supported RORγt as a plausible molecular target.

CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Fluoxetine attenuates experimental allergic airway inflammation through coordinated modulation of innate and adaptive immune responses, with suppression of the RORγt-IL-17 signalling axis emerging as a key mechanistic feature. These findings expand the immunopharmacological profile of fluoxetine and provide an experimental rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in Th17-associated airway inflammatory diseases and in experimental models that more closely recapitulate corticosteroid-resistant asthma.

articles.title: Genome shock in a migratory songbird hybrid zone.
articles.abstract: The genome shock hypothesis proposes that hybridization destabilizes genome regulation, leading to increased chromatin accessibility, derepression of transposable elements (TEs), and potential reductions in hybrid fitness, contributing to speciation. While extensively studied in plants, evidence in vertebrates is limited. Here, we tested this hypothesis in a hybrid zone between two subspecies of Swainson's thrushes (Catharus ustulatus). We quantified genome-wide TE proportions, TE expression, and chromatin accessibility during both the migratory and non-migratory state using whole genome resequencing, RNA-seq, and ATAC-seq data from two migration-associated brain regions. Hybrids exhibited greater TE proportions, expression, and chromatin accessibility than parental lineages, providing the first direct evidence for genome shock in a wild avian system.
