TE expression and chromatin accessibility were positively correlated in all states and brain regions, but the strength of these patterns differed between states and tissues indicating that genome shock is context-dependent. Signatures of shock were localized in regulatory regions and associated with differential transcript factor binding sites linked to retinoic acid receptor signaling, a key pathway for seasonal and photoperiodic responses. Overlap between open chromatin, upregulated TEs and previously identified transgressively expressed genes in these hybrids suggest that genome shock extends beyond TE activation to directly affect gene expression. Our results motivate further investigation into genome shocks' effects on genomic incompatibilities, hybrid fitness, and speciation.

articles.title: Prediction and Risk Stratification for 30-Day Mortality in Stable Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Recalibration of the Multimarker Calculator and Evaluation of the AHA/ACC Classification.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification in haemodynamically stable acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains challenging. The multimarker calculator (MMC) provides individualized 30-day mortality estimates, whereas the 2026 AHA/ACC Acute PE Clinical Categories (AHA/ACC classification) provide a phenotype-based framework incorporating clinical severity, right ventricular dysfunction, cardiac biomarker elevation, and respiratory compromise. We evaluated these approaches and recalibrated the original MMC in a Chinese multicentre cohort.

METHODS: We included adults with haemodynamically stable acute PE from the prospective, multicentre China pUlmonary thromboembolism REgistry Study (2012-2021). The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The MMC, 2019 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) model, and AHA/ACC classification were assessed using discrimination, decision-curve analysis, risk classification, and subgroup analyses. Logistic recalibration updated the original MMC linear predictor. The AHA/ACC classification was evaluated using 7-, 4-, and simplified phenotype-based 3-category schemes.

RESULTS: Among 11,568 patients, 331 died within 30 days (2.9%). The MMC and 7-category AHA/ACC classification showed better discrimination than the ESC model (AUC, 0.704 and 0.680 vs. 0.606). The original MMC overestimated intermediate-high-risk mortality (mean predicted risk, 16.2%; observed risk, 9.4%). Recalibration improved calibration and identified a smaller intermediate-high-risk subgroup comprising 2.2% of patients, with 13.2% observed mortality. In the 3-category AHA/ACC classification, mortality increased stepwise across category B, partial phenotype involvement, and dual cardiopulmonary phenotype involvement (0.7%, 2.7%, and 6.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: The recalibrated MMC may be useful for individualized 30-day mortality risk estimation, whereas the AHA/ACC classification may offer a simple framework for phenotype-based risk grouping.

articles.title: T-Cell-Derived IFNγ Instructs ECM Crosslinking by Cardiac Fibroblasts Through LOXL3 in Experimental Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a major clinical challenge characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Left ventricular stiffening and inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF, yet the contribution of ECM (extracellular matrix) stiffness and the immune-stromal mechanisms driving ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF remain poorly understood.

METHODS: We used the murine 2-hit model of cardiometabolic HFpEF, in which the combination of high-fat diet and hypertension induced by L-nitro-arginine-methyl ester causes diastolic dysfunction. We evaluated diastolic function by echocardiography and ECM mechanics by uniaxial tensile testing of decellularized cardiac tissue. Functional in vivo studies included genetic depletion of T cells, IFNγ (interferon-γ) knockout mice, and pharmacological lysyl oxidase inhibition. We combined cocultures of CD4+ T cells and cardiac fibroblasts with mechanical testing of cardiac ECM and molecular biology to elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms.

RESULTS: Left ventricular ECM stiffness strongly correlated with impaired diastolic function in experimental cardiometabolic HFpEF. Cardiac CD4+ T-cell infiltration was required for ECM stiffening and upregulation of lysyl oxidase enzymes in cardiac fibroblast. We discovered that CD4+ T-cell-derived IFNγ was required to induce LOXL3 in cardiac fibroblast, which increased ECM stiffness in vitro. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that a signaling axis involving IFNγ, PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase), AKT, and HIF1α (hypoxia-inducible factor-1α) drives LOXL3 expression and subsequent collagen crosslinking. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of this IFNγ-HIF1α-LOXL3 axis attenuated adverse ECM remodeling and improved diastolic function.

CONCLUSIONS: CD4+ T cells promote pathological ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF through IFNγ-mediated, cardiac fibroblast LOXL3-dependent ECM crosslinking. Targeting this immune-stromal pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for HFpEF.

articles.title: Anxiety and depressive symptoms decline during 12-month follow-up after cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation.
Diastolic Dysfunction in Congenital Heart Disease: A Pressure-Volume Loop Analysis of Borderline Left Heart.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diastolic dysfunction is a major driver of morbidity in congenital heart disease, but its mechanisms are poorly understood. It remains unknown whether left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction in borderline left heart patients is caused by a defect in active relaxation or in passive stiffness. We applied gold-standard pressure-volume (PV) loop analysis to define the mechanism of diastolic dysfunction in patients with borderline LV.

METHODS: We analyzed invasive PV loops from children with bLV (n=13) and a pragmatic comparison group of patients with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA, n=14). PV loops were generated during transient preload alteration. Active relaxation was assessed by the isovolumetric relaxation time constant (τ) and maximal rate of pressure decline (dP/dtmin) indexed to peak systolic pressure. Passive stiffness was quantified by the stiffness constant (β), derived from the multibeat end-diastolic PV relationship. To account for size differences, β was calculated using indexed ventricular volumes (iβ), and also converted to a dimensionless stiffness constant (βw=β×ventricular wall volume).

RESULTS: Active relaxation measures were similar between groups (τ bLV, 28 [23.5-29.5] versus ccTGA, 24 [21-28] msec, P=0.11; dP/dtmin/peak systolic pressure bLV: -10.6 [-11.0 to -9.4] versus ccTGA: -9.9 [-10.5 to -8.7] s-1, P=0.17). In contrast, patients with bLV had markedly abnormal passive stiffness. The end-diastolic PV relationship was shifted upward and to the left, and the stiffness constants were higher in the bLV group (iβ bLV, 0.10 [0.04-0.35] versus ccTGA, 0.03 [0.02-0.04] m2/mL, P=0.003; βw bLV, 4.08 [1.6-7.52] versus ccTGA, 1.21 [0.95-1.77]; P=0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: The primary mechanism of diastolic dysfunction in bLV is increased passive ventricular stiffness, while no differences were detected in active relaxation. These findings suggest a limited role for lusitropic medications and therapeutic strategies that focus on mitigating ventricular stiffness (such as surgical endocardial fibroelastosis resection) may be more valuable.

articles.title: Prediction of All-Cause Mortality, Cardiovascular Mortality, and Angiographic Coronary Disease From LVEF Reserve: Findings From the Multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular ejection fraction reserve (LVEF-R), defined as stress EF minus rest EF, is a marker for high-risk coronary artery disease in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging, but its prognostic and diagnostic significance in large real-world populations remains incompletely defined. We aimed to analyze the association of LVEF-R with mortality and high-risk obstructive coronary artery disease in a large multicenter cohort.

METHODS: We analyzed 34 976 patients from 13 sites who underwent gated rest and vasodilator stress positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging from the Registry of Flow and Perfusion Imaging for Artificial Intelligence with PET. Associations between LVEF-R and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death were assessed using multivariable Cox regression models. In a subset with invasive coronary angiography (n=6843), the relationship between LVEF-R and angiographic disease was evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 9392 (26.9%) patients had an LVEF-R<0%. Over a median follow-up of 4.1 years, lower LVEF-R demonstrated a graded association with higher mortality. Compared with LVEF-R>5%, adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.20 for LVEF-R 0% to 5% ([95% CI, 1.13-1.28]; P<0.001), 1.32 for -5% to 0% ([95% CI, 1.23-1.42]; P<0.001), and 1.38 for ≤-5% ([95% CI, 1.24-1.52]; P<0.001). A negative LVEF-R was also associated with high-risk coronary artery disease, including left main and 3-vessel disease.

CONCLUSIONS: LVEF-R is an independent predictor of mortality, with a graded association between impaired reserve and adverse outcomes. A negative LVEF-R identifies patients with a higher likelihood of multivessel or left-main coronary artery disease, supporting its role as a clinically relevant marker of high-risk disease.

articles.title: Seventeen Cases of Fungal Otitis Externa in Dogs and Cats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Otitis externa (OE) is common in dogs and cats. Fungal OE (FOE) caused by non-Malassezia species fungi is relatively uncommon. Comprehensive information on clinical manifestations, risk factors and breeds or species predispositions remains sparse. In this case series, we describe 17 companion animals in China with FOE.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical signs, potential risk factors and treatment of FOE in dogs and cats.

ANIMALS: Seventeen cases: four dogs and 13 cats.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective review of medical records of cases presented to dermatology specialty practices for OE between 2022 and 2024 was performed. Records with positive fungal culture results were included. Case demographic, diagnostic and treatment information was extracted.

RESULTS: Aspergillus spp. was isolated from 13 animals (three dogs, 10 cats), Microsporum canis from one dog and two cats, and one cat had a mixed infection with M. canis in the left ear and Aspergillus spp. in the right. The most common clinical signs were excessive cerumen and pruritus. Of 16 cases that received antifungal treatment, 13 received combined oral and topical therapy, and three received only oral therapy.

CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Aspergillus spp. or dermatophyte infection should not be overlooked in cases of chronic or recurrent OE. Cytological examination of exudates and fungal culture are useful for establishing the diagnosis of FOE. Larger prospective studies are needed to elucidate risk factors and appropriate treatment for FOE.

articles.title: Avoiding the Road to Perdition: Initial TAVR Device Choice and the Path to Reintervention.
Cardiac Electrophysiological Impact of Sodium Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors) reduce heart failure hospitalizations, cardiovascular death, and certain arrhythmic events beyond glycemic control. However, their specific effects on cardiac autonomic function and arrhythmogenesis, as well as the potential involvement of microRNAs in mediating these benefits, remain incompletely understood. This review synthesizes clinical and preclinical evidence on the impact of SGLT2i on cardiac autonomic regulation and arrhythmias, emphasizing the interplay between SGLT2i, microRNA expression, and cardiovascular risk. We conducted a comprehensive literature search for clinical trials, meta-analyses, observational studies, and preclinical investigations. Outcomes included heart rate variability, heart rate turbulence, atrial/ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Studies examining microRNA profiles associated with SGLT2i treatment and their links to cardiac fibrosis, inflammation, and arrhythmogenic substrates were analyzed in depth. Clinical evidence indicates that SGLT2i improve cardiac autonomic balance by reducing sympathetic overactivity and enhancing parasympathetic tone in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiac autonomic neuropathy. Meta-analyses and post hoc data from cardiovascular outcome trials suggest a modest but consistent reduction in atrial fibrillation/flutter and, in some cohorts, sudden cardiac death, potentially reflecting sympathoinhibition, improved hemodynamics, and modulation of myocardial ion homeostasis. Preclinical studies support anti-arrhythmic properties through sodium-hydrogen exchanger inhibition, late sodium current suppression, and metabolic shift towards ketone utilization. SGLT2i modulate several key microRNAs implicated in heart failure and arrhythmic risk, including miR-21, miR-29, miR-30, miR-34a, and miR-92, which may partly underlie the attenuation of arrhythmogenic substrates and improved autonomic regulation. SGLT2i favorably affect cardiac autonomic function and reduce the burden of certain arrhythmias, potentially through modulation of disease-associated microRNAs. Integrating clinical autonomic outcomes with microRNA profiling provides mechanistic insights into their cardioprotective actions. Dedicated trials are warranted to clarify causality, dose-dependency, and the therapeutic potential of microRNA-SGLT2i interactions for arrhythmia prevention and management in high-risk populations.

articles.title: RBFOX2 Autoregulation Promotes Cardiomyocyte Transcriptome Maturation and Differentiation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haploinsufficiency of the RNA splicing regulator RBFOX2 has been linked to congenital heart disease, including hypoplastic left heart syndrome, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain unresolved.

METHODS: Human induced pluripotent stem cells heterozygous or null for RBFOX2 were created and their cardiomyocyte (CM) derivatives were characterized in monolayer culture and engineered heart tissues. In addition to cellular phenotyping, molecular profiling by RNA sequencing and enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation sequencing was performed to detect changes in gene expression, exon usage, and RBFOX2 (RNA-binding fox-1 homolog 2) binding. These data sets were integrated to identify RBFOX2-bound RNAs with altered expression and splicing and to compare them with publicly available data sets from progressive CM differentiation time points. Rescue experiments were performed in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived CMs, engineered heart tissues, and zebrafish.

RESULTS: We demonstrate that RBFOX2 is essential for CM differentiation by driving transcriptome maturation through gene expression- and alternative splicing-based isoform switching in transcripts primarily encoding sarcomere, cytoskeletal, and focal adhesion components, including the critical Z-disc factor ACTN2 (alpha-actinin-2). We further find that threshold levels of RBFOX2 facilitate autoregulatory splicing of mutually exclusive exons, generating early and late RBFOX2 isoforms with distinct functions. In heterozygous CMs, this threshold is not reached, resulting in isoform imbalance and production of an aberrant transcript, which further reduces functional RBFOX2 levels to well below 50% of wild-type. Finally, we demonstrate that ACTN2 overexpression rescues heterozygous, but not null, phenotypes, suggesting that ACTN2 activates an RBFOX2-dependent feedback loop that promotes transcriptome maturation.

CONCLUSIONS: Our data demonstrate that reduced RBFOX2 dosage and impaired autoregulation stall CM differentiation by inhibiting transcriptome maturation, contributing to congenital heart disease pathogenesis and potentially increasing heart failure susceptibility following surgical intervention.

articles.title: Multimodality Imaging for Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Practical Guidance Across Preprocedural, Intraprocedural, and Postprocedural Phases.
authors: Left Atrial Appendage International Working Group
articles.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure is an increasingly used stroke prevention therapy for patients with atrial fibrillation who are unable to maintain long-term anticoagulation. Imaging quality and consistency are central to procedural safety and long-term outcomes, yet practice varies widely across centers. This review presents a practical, phase-based multimodality imaging framework intended to provide guidance and minimum standards for image acquisition and interpretation across all phases of left atrial appendage closure care, including preprocedural planning and thrombus exclusion, intraprocedural guidance and complication detection, and postprocedural surveillance for device-related thrombus and peridevice leak. Because sizing rules, sealing mechanisms, and leak patterns differ between the 2 contemporary platforms, device-specific considerations for the Watchman and Amulet systems are addressed throughout. Transesophageal echocardiography remains the reference standard for thrombus detection and procedural guidance, while cardiac computed tomography offers high spatial resolution, detailed 3-dimensional characterization, and complementary leak assessment, with optimal modality selection influenced by patient characteristics, operator expertise, and institutional resources. Intracardiac echocardiography and mini transesophageal echocardiographic support anesthesia-sparing workflows. Standardized device-related thrombus and peridevice leak classification and harmonized imaging protocols can enhance reproducibility and facilitate cross-center comparisons. Emerging technologies including computed tomography first workflows, 4-dimensional imaging, AI applications, and computational modeling further advance precision planning and surveillance.

articles.title: Glutaminolysis Shapes Cardiac Resilience to Stress via Mitochondrial Glutathione.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac reserve is a strong predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable the heart to mount an adaptive response to stress remain poorly understood. In this study, we sought to dissect the specific role of glutaminolysis, a key anaplerotic and redox-supporting pathway, in regulating cardiac reserve.

METHODS: Cardiac reserve was assessed by echocardiography under β-adrenergic stimulation in mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase and in wild-type controls. Stable isotope tracing with [U-13C] glutamine was performed in Langendorff-perfused hearts. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of acute glutamine supplementation in healthy volunteers was conducted to evaluate translational relevance (ChiCTR2400082676).

RESULTS: During acute stress, such as exercise or β-adrenergic stimulation, glutaminolysis was rapidly mobilized to supply mitochondrial glutathione, preserving mitochondrial redox homeostasis and sustaining cardiac contractile reserve. Mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase exhibited marked impairments in both contractile reserve and exercise capacity, accompanied by a failure to elevate mitochondrial glutathione and consequent mitochondrial oxidative stress. Chronic exercise training upregulated cardiac glutaminase expression and expanded the mitochondrial glutathione pool, linking this adaptive mechanism to training-induced improvements in cardiac reserve. In humans, acute oral glutamine supplementation enhanced cardiac reserve, as assessed by exercise stress echocardiography, in a placebo-controlled crossover design.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a novel metabolic paradigm in which glutaminolysis functions as a dynamic pathway supporting mitochondrial health and cardiac resilience, and highlight glutamine supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance cardiac reserve.

articles.title: Outcomes of Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators in Patients Being Considered for Heart Transplantation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillators (S-ICD) are an alternative to transvenous devices (TV-ICD) in patients not requiring bradycardia pacing, resynchronization (CRT) or anti-tachycardia pacing (ATP). At our center, S-ICDs are often preferred in patients being considered for heart transplantation (HTx) without pacing/CRT/ATP needs, as their removal post-HTx avoids retained transvenous leads which can preclude MRI surveillance for graft rejection. We assessed outcomes of S-ICDs in this population.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 201 S-ICD implants at our center; July 2016 - March 2025.

RESULTS: We identified 33 patients (22 male; age 46 ± 13 years) who, at time of S-ICD implant, had been referred for HTx evaluation or were referred at any time thereafter. Etiologies were nonischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 18), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (n = 5), ischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 4), congenital heart disease (n = 4), and myocarditis (n = 2). Median follow-up was 296 days [IQR = 72-798]. Two patients died, both non-arrhythmic. Four patients received appropriate S-ICD therapies and three had inappropriate shocks due to P- or T-wave oversensing (TWOS) (n = 2), or a rapidly conducted atrial arrhythmia (n = 1). Three patients, all with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, received transvenous device upgrades: one to CRT-P for disease progression, one to TV-ICD for ATP-terminable ventricular tachycardia and one to TV-ICD due to inappropriate shocks from TWOS. Thirteen patients underwent HTx at median 257 days [IQR = 130-453] post S-ICD; three of whom were bridged with HeartMate 3 LVADs. One LVAD patient needed S-ICD deactivation due to electromagnetic interference. There were no retained device components following HTx and S-ICD extraction.

CONCLUSION: In selected pre-HTx patients, S-ICDs offer arrhythmic protection while avoiding retained leads post-HTx.

articles.title: Clinical and computational exploration of IRS1 and Pancreastatin genetic variants in metabolic response to metformin-sulfonylurea therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) show variable responses to metformin-sulfonylurea therapy. Genetic variation in insulin signaling and metabolic regulation, particularly in insulin receptor substrate-1 (IRS1) and pancreastatin (PST), may contribute to this variability. This study assessed the influence of IRS1 (rs1801278) and PST (rs9658664) polymorphisms on baseline metabolic profiles and response to combination therapy.

METHODS: We enrolled 202 diabetic individuals receiving metformin-sulfonylurea therapy. Clinical and biochemical parameters were measured at baseline and follow-up. Genotyping for IRS1 (rs1801278) and PST (rs9658664) was performed using PCR-RFLP and statistically analyzed by SPSS (v.27). Exploratory molecular docking analyses were performed to examine mutation-dependent differences in PST interactions with insulin-signaling proteins.

RESULTS: Renal complications were more prevalent among non-responders (p = 0.029). IRS1 and PST genotypes were not associated with therapeutic response. Individuals with IRS1 TT genotype exhibited higher baseline cholesterol, triglyceride, and LDL levels (p = 0.05). Docking analyses suggested mutation-dependent differences in PST interactions with insulin receptor, IRS1, and GRP78. Metformin showed slightly stronger predicted binding to insulin receptor and IRS1 than sulfonylurea.

CONCLUSION: Although IRS1 and PST polymorphisms did not show association with treatment response, genotype-based metabolic variability and in silico analyses suggest functional effects on insulin-signaling pathways, highlighting the potential of personalized medicine approaches for optimizing antidiabetic therapy.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Comorbidities as Treatable Traits in Adult Asthma.
Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus And Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease In Children And Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE), and to evaluate associated clinical and laboratory features.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 72 children with T1DM and 83 healthy controls who were comparable in age and sex. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using ultrasonography and VCTE. A controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) value >236 dB/m was used to define CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD in the T1DM group. Clinical, anthropometric, laboratory, and radiological characteristics were compared between groups. Correlations of CAP and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) with clinical and laboratory parameters were evaluated in the T1DM cohort. Stepwise multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify candidate factors independently associated with CAP and LSM values.

RESULTS: CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD was more frequent in children with T1DM than in controls (31.9% vs. 14.5%). Among children with T1DM, those with MASLD had higher body mass index, WHtR, diastolic blood pressure, and triglyceride levels than those without MASLD. In the multivariable CAP model, diabetes duration, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and WHtR were independently associated with higher CAP values. WHtR and alanine aminotransferase were independently associated with higher LSM values.

CONCLUSION: Children and adolescents with T1DM had a higher prevalence of CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD than healthy controls. Adiposity-related parameters and dyslipidemia appear to be important clinical features associated with hepatic steatosis in pediatric T1DM.

articles.title: 18F-FDG PET/MRI-based liver and bone marrow organomics combined with systemic inflammatory response for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the role of liver and bone marrow organomics features derived from staging 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/MRI in predicting pathological complete response (pCR) in breast cancer patients who underwent surgery after neoadjuvant therapy.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, breast cancer patients who underwent pretreatment staging with 18F-FDG PET/MRI, received neoadjuvant therapy, and subsequently underwent surgery were included. Clinicopathological characteristics and systemic inflammatory markers were recorded. Organomics features were extracted from the liver and L4 vertebra bone marrow regions on 18F-FDG PET images using LIFEx software. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression was applied for radiomics feature selection, and a radiomics score (Radscore) was generated. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of pCR. The diagnostic performances of the Radscore, Clinical, and Clinical-Radscore Combined models were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 87 breast cancer patients were included, and pCR was observed in 33 patients (37.9%). In multivariable analysis, progesterone receptor status, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 status, primary tumor size, and Radscore were identified as independent predictors of pCR. The Radscore yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.722 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.625-0.819], whereas the Clinical and Clinical-Radscore Combined models achieved AUCs of 0.850 (95% CI = 0.765-0.934) and 0.904 (95% CI = 0.843-0.965), respectively. The Clinical-Radscore Combined Model demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than both the other models.

CONCLUSION: Liver and bone marrow organomics features derived from staging 18F-FDG PET/MRI may provide valuable information for predicting pCR in breast cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant therapy.

articles.title: A Live Attenuated Dengue Virus Vaccine (Dengvaxia) is Suppressed in Individuals with Immunity to Serotype 4.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengvaxia® was the first live attenuated tetravalent dengue virus (DENV) vaccine to be tested and approved for use in people. While Dengvaxia was designed to be tetravalent, in humans, the vaccine performed like a monovalent DENV4 vaccine because the DENV4 vaccine virus replicated better than other vaccine serotypes. Dengvaxia® was safe and efficacious in children who were DENV-immune at baseline and contraindicated for use in DENV-naïve children.

METHODS: When Dengvaxia® was rolled out as a pediatric vaccine in the Philippines in 2016, we established a prospective cohort to assess vaccine performance by baseline dengue serostatus. Here we report on how baseline monotypic immunity to each serotype (reflecting one past DENV infection) impacted Dengvaxia® responses.

RESULTS: We observed that in children with baseline immunity to DENV1, 2 or 3, the vaccine stimulated a secondary serotype cross-neutralizing Ab response, which likely explains the overall favorable performance of the vaccine in seropositive children enrolled in phase 3 trials. We observed a high frequency (61%) of vaccine suppression among DENV4 monotypic immune children.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results confirm the replication dominance of the DENV4 vaccine component in Dengvaxia® and directly implicate pre-existing DENV4 immunity in the suppression of the vaccine. Our results have broader implications for evaluating the performance of other DENV vaccines in seropositive individuals.

articles.title: Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patient With Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries-Wiring Towards the Unknown.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: As life expectancy in patients with congenital heart disease continues to increase, coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndromes are encountered more and more in this population, with a higher level of complexity, especially in the acute setting. We present a case of acute thrombotic occlusion of the left circumflex coronary artery in a patient with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. This case highlights several challenges from ECG and computed tomography interpretation to coronary angiography and PCI performance. Key pre-procedural and procedural steps are revised to guide toward prompt and successful revascularization.

articles.title: Notoginsenoside R2 Antagonizes Renal Interstitial Fibrosis by Regulating Fatty Acid Oxidation via the CASP2/ALDH3A1 Axis.
articles.abstract: Renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF) is a major driver of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, yet effective therapies remain limited. The Shen-Yan-Fang-Shuai formula (SYFSF) exhibits clinical renoprotective effects; however, its active components and mechanisms remain unclear. This study identifies notoginsenoside R2 (NGR2) as a core active compound of SYFSF that directly binds to caspase-2 (CASP2). Integrative multi-omics analyses in unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rats and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-induced NRK-52E cells demonstrate that NGR2 upregulates CASP2, enhances the CASP2-aldehyde dehydrogenase 3 family member A1 (ALDH3A1) interaction, and promotes ALDH3A1 deubiquitination, thereby stabilizing ALDH3A1. This stabilization restores the integrity of mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes (MAMs) and improves fatty acid oxidation (FAO) by upregulating carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A), acyl-CoA dehydrogenase long chain (ACADL), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα). It also reduces lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), inflammation, and collagen deposition. In vivo, NGR2 ameliorates renal dysfunction and fibrosis. Mechanistically, NGR2 binds the caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD) of CASP2 without occluding the ubiquitin-interacting motif-like (UIML) region required for its deubiquitinase function, thereby increasing CASP2 abundance and stability rather than activating its apoptotic protease activity, and facilitating ubiquitin chain removal from ALDH3A1. These findings demonstrate that SYFSF and NGR2 antagonize RIF by targeting the CASP2/ALDH3A1 axis to restore MAM function and FAO, providing a molecular basis for traditional Chinese medicine in CKD therapy.

articles.title: EXPRESS: The function of microRNAs transported by cell extracellular vesicles in post-stroke recovery: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is associated with persistently elevated rates of mortality and disability. Effective cerebroprotection strategies and interventions for promoting functional recovery after stroke remain an unmet need. Cell transplantation represents a potential therapeutic strategy for facilitating brain recovery and regeneration. Its therapeutic benefits are thought to be partly mediated by extracellular vesicles and the various miRNAs they carry, which from different cell sources may exert distinct therapeutic effects.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library for original studies on extracellular vesicles in post-stroke recovery, focusing on miRNA mechanisms. Data on cell source, miRNA, in vitro/vivo model, administration, target/pathway, outcomes, and presumed treatment window were extracted.

RESULTS: We categorize exosomal miRNAs into three distinct groups based on their cellular origins: mesenchymal stem cells, other stem cells, and non-stem cells. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles carry diverse miRNAs regulating angiogenesis, inflammation, apoptosis, autophagy, and neuroplasticity; other stem cell-derived vesicles show source-specific effects; non-stem cell-derived vesicles from astrocytes, microglia, and endothelial cells also modulate neuronal survival and repair. Therapeutic effects span acute cytoprotection, subacute tissue repair, and chronic neuroplasticity. Most miRNAs are supported by at least one in vivo study, while a few rely mainly on in vitro evidence.

articles.title: Normal-BMI MASLD is Associated with Increased Mortality, Cardiovascular Events, Cancer and Lower GLP-1 Use.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) can occur in individuals who are not overweight or have obesity (normal-BMI MASLD), yet disease burden and management remain poorly characterized. We compared long-term outcomes and incretin-based therapy use between normal-BMI MASLD (nbMASLD) and overweight/obesity-associated MASLD (obMASLD) across racial and ethnic groups.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, observational study using the TriNetX United States Network. Adults diagnosed with MASLD or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) from 2005-2025 were classified using ethnicity-informed normal-BMI thresholds: <23 kg/m2 for Asian, <27 kg/m2 for Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, and <25 kg/m2 for White/others. Propensity-score matching balanced demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models with obMASLD as the reference group.

RESULTS: Among 619,171 eligible patients, 51,940 matched pairs were identified. Nb-BMI MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality across grouped ethnic groups, with survival of 77.49% versus 83.93% in obMASLD (HR 1.735, CI 1.653-1.822). Ethnicity-specific risks included higher myocardial infarction risk in White and Black patients, higher stroke risk in White patients, higher ESRD risk in Black patients, and increased cancers (colorectal, pancreatic and multiple myeloma) among White patients. Incretin-based therapy (IBT) use was markedly lower in nbMASLD but was associated with improved survival.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with nbMASLD demonstrated an increased mortality and ethnicity-specific clinical complications than obMASLD despite a more favorable metabolic profile. These findings demonstrate a potential treatment gap for nbMASLD patients and the shortcomings of BMI-based strategies to risk-stratify MASLD patients.

articles.title: Heterogeneity In The Effects of Weight Reduction on Pain And Physical Function In Knee Osteoarthritis: A causal forest analysis of the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite the emphasis on weight control, heterogeneity in response to weight loss among individuals with or at high risk for knee osteoarthritis (OA) remains unclear. This study examined heterogeneity in the associations of weight reduction with pain among overweight and obese individuals using a machine learning approach.

METHODS: We analyzed longitudinal data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, comprising community-dwelling adults aged 45-79 years with a body mass index ≥25 who completed baseline assessments between 2008 and 2010, with a 24-month follow-up (n=3,644). The exposure was a ≥5% reduction in body weight from baseline to 24 months. The primary outcome of this study was the pain subscale of the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities (WOMAC) Osteoarthritis Index.

RESULTS: The average treatment effect (ATE) was estimated using a doubly robust estimator, and treatment effect heterogeneity was assessed by estimating conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) using a causal forest approach. A reduction of ≥5% in body weight was not significantly associated with a lower WOMAC pain score (ATE=-0.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.51 to 0.01). The causal forest analysis demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with CATE estimates of -0.77 (95% CI, -1.24 to -0.30) for the high-benefit subgroup (top 20% of estimated CATEs) and 0.41 (95% CI, -0.35 to 1.17) for the low-benefit subgroup (bottom 20%).

DISCUSSION: Our findings highlight the potential value of individualized weight-loss strategies and suggest that patient characteristics may help identify those most likely to benefit from weight reduction.

articles.title: Spontaneous inversion of the left atrial appendage: a first autopsy case report and updated literature review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A mass in the left atrium commands immediate attention. Echocardiography reflexively points towards thrombus, vegetation, or tumour-the common culprits. Rarer, and easily overlooked, is a fourth possibility that has accumulated a quiet but instructive literature since the earliest days of open-heart surgery: inversion of the left atrial appendage. The spontaneous form, occurring outside any surgical context, is documented in fewer than ten cases worldwide.

CASE PRESENTATION: We present the autopsy findings of a spontaneously inverted left atrial appendage in an 8-month-old male infant who had never undergone cardiac surgery.

CONCLUSION: This case, placed alongside an updated review of the literature from 2020 to 2024, reinforces a simple but easily forgotten message: spontaneous left atrial appendage inversion can occur at any age, even in infants with no surgical history. A pressure gradient across the appendage wall, most often driven by pericardial effusion, appears to be the decisive pathophysiological trigger.

articles.title: Association of haematologic parameters with persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Rheumatic heart disease remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity in children. Although echocardiography is central to diagnosis and staging, it does not directly reflect inflammatory processes that may contribute to ongoing valvular damage. This study aimed to evaluate the association between baseline haematologic parameters and persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children with prior acute rheumatic fever.

METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective pilot study, 45 children with persistent rheumatic heart disease were classified as Stage A (n = 23), Stage B (n = 14), or Stage C (n = 8) according to the 2023 World Heart Federation echocardiographic staging framework. Baseline laboratory values obtained during acute presentation were analysed. Clinical and laboratory variables were compared across stages using non-parametric tests. Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with advanced disease (Stage B-C vs Stage A).

RESULTS: Markers reflecting acute inflammatory activity, including leukocyte counts and derived indices, did not differ significantly among stages. In contrast, red cell distribution width, mean platelet volume, and platelet distribution width differed significantly. In multivariable analysis, red cell distribution width, and mean platelet volume were independently associated with advanced persistent rheumatic heart disease stage, with higher values linked to increased odds of Stage B-C disease.

CONCLUSION: Red cell distribution width and mean platelet volume were associated with advanced stages of persistent paediatric rheumatic heart disease. These widely available haematologic markers may complement echocardiographic assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed to define their clinical utility.Trial registration: Not applicable (retrospective study).

articles.title: Hepatocyte Pparg knockout and restored Bhmt expression reduce liver steatosis in male mice with diet-induced MASH.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by the accumulation of triglycerides in hepatocytes and can progress to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with inflammation, hepatocyte ballooning, and fibrosis. MASLD is associated with increased plasma homocysteine levels. Homocysteine is an amino acid generated by the S-adenosylmethionine-dependent transmethylation pathway of the methionine cycle, and it is remethylated to methionine by the betaine-homocysteine S-methyltransferase (BHMT) in hepatocytes. Mice fed a high-fat, cholesterol, and fructose (HFCF) diet develop MASLD and MASH associated with increased peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ, Pparg) expression and homocysteine levels, and decreased hepatic Bhmt expression. Here, we sought to determine whether the hepatocyte-specific knockout of Pparg (PpargΛHep) or restoration of Bhmt expression in hepatocytes (BhmtHep) in mice with HFCF-induced MASH reduce MASLD progression. To this end, adult male Pparg-floxed mice were fed an HFCF diet for 20 weeks to induce MASH. Then, we generated PpargΛHep and/or BhmtHep mice using an adeno-associated virus encoding Cre recombinase or Bhmt in hepatocytes, respectively. HFCF diet-induced MASH increased hepatic Pparg expression and reduced Bhmt expression. 8 weeks after the induction of PpargΛHep, hepatic Bhmt expression was increased, and both MASH severity and homocysteine levels decreased. The restoration of hepatocyte BHMT in BhmtHep (Pparg-intact) mice reduced hepatic triglyceride and homocysteine levels, which were associated with reduced expression of the steatogenic genes Cidea and Cidec. Overall, our results indicate a protective role for BHMT in hepatocytes of mice with MASH, even in mice expressing Pparg in hepatocytes.

articles.title: Seasonal Variation in Preschool Hearing Screening Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether pass and referral rates for pure-tone audiometry (PTA) and otoacoustic emissions (OAE) demonstrate seasonal variation in preschool-aged children, and to explore whether these patterns may be associated with middle ear pathology related to upper respiratory tract infections.

DESIGN: We conducted a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial comparing single-stage OAE versus 2-stage PTA plus OAE screening in preschool children from 2023 to 2026. A total of 7416 children completed at least 1 screening modality in at least 1 ear. Children who failed screening underwent tympanometry to characterize middle ear status. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the association between screening season and failure rates, adjusting for age, home language, and teacher-reported concerns. In addition, a time series model using national upper respiratory infection emergency department visit data was developed to estimate seasonal variation in middle ear effusion rates.

RESULTS: Failure rates were higher for OAE than PTA and demonstrated clear seasonal patterns. OAE failure rates peaked in spring (17.9%) and winter (15.2%) and were lowest in summer (8.5%) and fall (10.3%). PTA showed a similar pattern, with the highest failure rates in spring (8.3%), followed by winter (5.5%), and the lowest in summer (3.1%) and fall (3.6%). In adjusted analyses, the odds of failure for both OAE and PTA were significantly lower in summer and fall compared with winter (PTA: summer odds ratio (OR) = 0.54, p = 0.004; fall OR = 0.60, p = 0.01; OAE: summer OR = 0.47, p < 0.001; fall OR = 0.57, p < 0.001). For PTA, the odds of failure were significantly higher in spring compared with winter (OR = 1.50, p = 0.004), whereas no significant difference between spring and winter was observed for OAE (OR = 1.15, p = 0.09). Pairwise comparisons demonstrated significantly higher odds of failure in spring compared with summer and fall for both modalities (all p < 0.001). Tympanometry in failed ears most commonly demonstrated type B patterns across all seasons, consistent with middle ear pathology. Modeled effusion rates closely paralleled observed screening failure rates, with shared seasonal peaks and summer nadirs.

CONCLUSIONS: Hearing screening failure rates in preschool children vary by season, with higher failure rates observed in winter and spring. These patterns may be driven in part by seasonal variation in middle ear pathology associated with upper respiratory infections. The timing of screening may influence referral rates and should be considered when designing preschool hearing screening programs.

articles.title: Fragmented social networks promote complex behavioural contagions over infectious disease spread.
articles.abstract: Group living and social interactions among animals provide key benefits, such as the exchange of beneficial social information and novel behaviours, but also often pose the risk of spreading costly infectious diseases, presenting a social trade-off. While both behaviours and infections spread across social networks, they typically have distinct mechanisms of transmission. Here, we model social behaviour spread as a complex contagion governed by a conformist learning rule, while pathogen transmission follows a simple contagion mechanism. Building on theoretical foundations, our study applies computational models to examine how (sub)group structure (modularity) influences the spread of these contagions across diverse animal social structures sourced from the Animal Social Network Repository. Our findings reveal that high modularity and (sub)group structure slow simple contagion spread, whereas complex contagions are less impeded by this fragmentation but with a relatively small effect size compared with theoretical predictions. Consequently, our results suggest that social networks divided into small groups or subgroups can help balance the competing pressures of exploiting beneficial social information and avoiding infectious disease in real-world networks.

articles.title: Alexithymia in Chronic Lumbar Radicular Pain: A Comparative Study of Failed Back Surgery Syndrome and Lumbar Disc Herniation.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Failed back surgery syndrome (FBSS) involves persistent pain after surgery, with psychosocial factors contributing to symptom burden. Alexithymia is associated with chronic pain, but whether it is surgery-related or a broader feature of chronic lumbar radicular pain is unclear. We compared alexithymia between FBSS and non-surgical lumbar disc herniation (LDH). MATERIAL AND METHODS This cross-sectional study included 150 patients: FBSS after 1 surgery (n=64), FBSS after multiple surgeries (n=42), and magnetic resonance imaging-confirmed non-surgical LDH (n=44). Pain, disability, alexithymia, anxiety, and depression were assessed using the visual analog scale, Oswestry Disability Index, 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. The primary analysis compared combined FBSS (n=106) with LDH (n=44); secondary analyses examined surgery-related variables. Correlation analyses and exploratory logistic regression were performed. RESULTS Patients with FBSS had greater disability and more frequent neurological and functional impairments than patients with LDH. Alexithymia prevalence did not differ significantly between groups and was unrelated to number of surgeries, fixation material, or time since first operation. Alexithymia scores correlated with pain, disability, anxiety, depressive symptoms, and sociodemographic factors. In exploratory logistic regression, HADS total score was independently associated with definite alexithymia; however, this finding warrants caution because events were limited and no predictive or causal inference can be made. CONCLUSIONS Alexithymia showed no surgery-specific difference between FBSS and LDH and may represent a broader psychosocial correlate of chronic lumbar radicular pain. Psychosocial assessment should be considered in surgical and non-surgical populations, although outcome benefits require further study.

articles.title: HHV-6 Encephalitis Presenting With Severe SIADH and CO₂ Narcosis in Non-Transplant Smoldering Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) encephalitis is best recognized after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation but can also occur in non-transplant immunocompromised patients. Hyponatremia and syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH) may precede or accompany HHV-6 encephalitis. Severe SIADH as an early dominant clue in non-transplant patients with smoldering adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) is not fully described. CASE REPORT A 55-year-old woman with smoldering ATLL received systemic corticosteroid therapy for clinically diagnosed human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1)-associated uveitis and was admitted for progressive pulmonary infection. Bronchoscopic specimens revealed polymicrobial infection, including Nocardia and Actinomyces; invasive pulmonary aspergillosis was also clinically suspected. Although pulmonary findings improved with antimicrobial and antifungal therapy, she developed nausea, acute impairment of consciousness, and severe SIADH-associated hyponatremia. Serum sodium decreased to 113 mmol/L, and consciousness did not adequately improve after sodium correction. Cerebrospinal fluid obtained by lumbar puncture on hospital day 13 showed HHV-6 DNA positivity (1.0×10³ copies/mL). Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral cortical and limbic abnormalities, supporting a clinical diagnosis of HHV-6 encephalitis. Ganciclovir was initiated on hospital day 15 along with sodium correction, tolvaptan, and supportive care. The patient subsequently developed hypercapnic respiratory failure and CO₂ narcosis requiring mechanical ventilation. Her neurologic and respiratory status gradually improved, and she was discharged on hospital day 53. CONCLUSIONS In non-transplant patients with ATLL, corticosteroid exposure, and opportunistic infection, severe SIADH accompanied by new neurologic symptoms can be an early clue to HHV-6 encephalitis. Early recognition and prompt initiation of antiviral therapy may help to improve neurologic outcomes.

articles.title: Comparison between days of antibiotic spectrum coverage and days of therapy as risk factors for Clostridioides difficile infection: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The relative contributions of antibiotic duration (days of therapy, DOT) and spectrum intensity (days of antibiotic spectrum coverage, DASC) to Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) risk remain unclear. This multicenter study aimed to identify independent risk factors for CDI, differentiate the impact of length of therapy (LOT) from combination therapy intensity (DOT/LOT ratio), and characterize continuous risk profiles to inform actionable antimicrobial stewardship.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: The study was conducted at two Japanese tertiary hospitals from 2016 to 2024.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Hospitalized patients undergoing CDI testing after receiving systemic antibiotics were classified into CDI and non-CDI groups. Independent risk factors were identified using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models. Internal validity was evaluated using bootstrap resampling. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to achieve balance in baseline CDI risk factors.

RESULTS: Among 3,073 patients, 186 developed CDI. Prolonged DOT was independently associated with an increased risk of CDI; RCS analysis demonstrated progressive increase in CDI risk beyond the median DOT of 16 days. Bootstrap validation showed minimal optimism. In the PSM cohort (n = 186 pairs), prolonged DOT remained significantly associated with CDI, and lower DASC emerged as a significant risk factor, reflecting the disproportionate use of specific high-risk, narrow-spectrum antibiotics. Furthermore, supplementary models revealed that both prolonged LOT and higher DOT/LOT ratio were independent risk factors for CDI.

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged DOT was a primary factor associated with CDI. Antimicrobial stewardship interventions could benefit from incorporating duration reduction measures alongside careful evaluation of individual antibiotic CDI risks.

articles.title: Disparities in type 2 diabetes incidence trends during the COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden: a register-based population study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly affected health care provision for chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes. However, its effects on type 2 diabetes incidence remain poorly understood, particularly how they differ between population groups, which has not yet been examined in a Swedish context. We aimed to investigate trends in type 2 diabetes incidence in Sweden from 2016 to 2022, and to explore whether potential changes in type 2 diabetes incidence associated with the COVID-19 pandemic varied by sex, age, or migration status.

METHODS: Quarterly incidence rates of new-onset type 2 diabetes were calculated from individual-level register data for a dynamic population consisting of all adults (age ≥ 18 years) in Sweden during 2016-2019 (pre-pandemic) and 2020-2022 (pandemic). Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for each pandemic year were modelled in multivariable Poisson regression analysis using the pre-pandemic years as reference, adjusted for age, sex, migration status, season, and long-term annual trend. Stratified and interaction analyses were performed based on age, sex, and migration status.

RESULTS: Overall, the incidence of type 2 diabetes showed an increasing underlying linear trend of 3.6% (IRR 1.036, 95% CI 1.028, 1.045) between 2016 and 2022. During the pandemic (2020-2022), the overall type 2 diabetes incidence decreased by 6% relative to the underlying linear trend (IRR 0.94, 95% CI 0.91, 0.97). The decrease was strongest in 2020 (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.87, 0.94) compared to 2021 (IRR 1.03, 95% CI 0.99, 1.06) and 2022 (IRR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91, 0.99). The decline in type 2 diabetes incidence in 2020 was most pronounced among individuals 65 years and older and in the native-born Swedish population.

CONCLUSIONS: During the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden, a decline in incidence of type 2 diabetes was observed that varied in magnitude by sex, age, and migration status. This finding may reflect differential but transient changes in health-seeking behaviour during the initial phases of the pandemic. Our results underscore the challenges of maintaining continuous health care for non-communicable diseases during a major health crisis in society, highlighting the need to ensure equitable access for vulnerable groups such as older persons.

articles.title: Is the health system working for people? Comparison of adolescent and adult perspectives from the people´s voice survey in Germany.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People-centred health system performance assessments rely largely on adults, with limited inclusion of adolescents despite their distinct health needs and rights to participate in decisions concerning their health. The People's Voice Survey is a multi-country, adult-population-representative survey of health system perceptions, but it includes adolescents in the German survey. Germany's health system offers financial protection and commits to adolescent participation, yet little is known about adolescents' views of its performance. We aimed to identify adolescent-specific experiences and perspectives by comparing adolescents' and adults' experiences and perceptions of health system performance.

METHODS: Population-representative data were collected through an online panel between December 2024 and January 2025. Respondents could choose to take the survey in either German or English. Because adolescents were intentionally oversampled to enable age-group comparisons, we conducted a weighted cross-sectional analysis comparing adolescents (15-19 years) with adults (≥ 20 years) using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Variables included self-reported health status, confidence and autonomy in managing health, experiences during care delivery, and perceptions of the health system. Weighted descriptive analyses and chi-square tests were performed.

RESULTS: The total sample included 2,698 participants: 257 adolescents and 2,441 adults. Compared with adults, adolescents reported better physical but poorer mental health, lower confidence and autonomy in making their own health decisions and communicating concerns to healthcare providers. Compared with adults, adolescents more frequently perceived medical mistakes and receiving care without feeling sufficiently informed, and reported higher levels of unfair or discriminatory treatment. Adults were more critical of the changes to the health system in the past two years and of the system's overall performance. Despite adolescents' poorer experiences, they had a more positive outlook on the health system's performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings underscore the need to support adolescents' autonomy in making their own health-related decisions and participating in healthcare through age-appropriate communication and opportunities for independent consultations. They also highlight the importance of directly including adolescents in health system performance monitoring, as relying primarily on adult populations may overlook adolescents' unique healthcare experiences and unmet needs.

articles.title: A House Divided: Unifying the Classification of Plant Pathogen Effectors.
articles.abstract: Plant pathogens deploy diverse effectors to interfere with host defense systems and create favorable conditions for infection. As effector biology has advanced, the terminology used to describe these effectors has become increasingly complex, reflecting differences in secretion pathways, molecular features, and subcellular localization across pathogens. This inconsistency complicates comparative studies and limits effective communication across research groups. Here, we propose a streamlined and broadly applicable classification framework based on the functional destination of effectors within host plants, dividing them into two categories: extracellular and intracellular effectors. Extracellular effectors operate beyond the host plasma membrane, acting in apoplast, cell wall, and xylem, whereas intracellular effectors act within host cells, targeting the cytoplasm, nucleus, and other organelles. This approach provides a common terminology applicable to effectors from fungi, Oomycetes, bacteria, nematodes, and viruses, while broadly reflecting the spatial organization of plant immune surveillance. Moreover, it establishes a practical foundation for the systematic organization and management of effector databases. Together, this classification facilitates standardized effector annotation, comparative analyses, and interdisciplinary understanding of molecular plant-pathogen interactions.

articles.title: Disproportionality Analysis of Acute Kidney Injury Reports Associated with Sacubitril/Valsartan (ARNI) in the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prescriptions of angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) have increased in recent years; however, few pharmacovigilance studies have investigated acute kidney injury (AKI) reporting associated with ARNI. This study evaluated the disproportionate AKI reporting associated with ARNI in the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database, compared AKI reporting between reports involving ARNI and valsartan, and explored the factors associated with AKI reporting among reports involving ARNI.

METHODS: Reports published in JADER between April 2020 and August 2023 were analyzed. AKI was identified using the narrow and broad scope Preferred Terms of the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "acute renal failure" (SMQ:20000003). The reporting odds ratios (RORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for ARNI and valsartan. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to estimate adjusted RORs (aRORs) for sex, age, heart failure (HF), diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease (CKD), concomitant diuretics, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). An additional adjusted analysis directly compared AKI reports between ARNI and valsartan.

RESULTS: A disproportionality signal for AKI was identified in the reports involving ARNI (ROR 7.11, 95% CI 6.27-8.07). Multivariable logistic regression showed that HF (aROR 1.68, 95% CI 1.22-2.31; p = 0.002) and CKD (aROR 2.17, 95% CI 1.60-2.93; p < 0.001) were independently associated with increased AKI reporting among reports involving ARNI. In the adjusted direct comparison, reports involving ARNI had higher odds of AKI reporting than those involving valsartan (aROR 2.03, 95% CI 1.50-2.74).

CONCLUSIONS: Disproportionate AKI reporting signals were identified in reports involving ARNI in the JADER database. HF and CKD were independently associated with increased AKI reporting after adjustment. These findings have provided additional pharmacovigilance evidence regarding ARNI-associated AKI in Japan and should be interpreted in light of the inherent limitations of spontaneous reporting data.

articles.title: Effects of Interventions for Delabeling Penicillin Allergy in Hospitalized Patients: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Penicillin allergy labels are common among hospitalized patients, yet most represent inaccurate or nonimmune-mediated reactions and may contribute to suboptimal antibiotic prescribing. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of hospital-based penicillin allergy delabeling interventions and their impact on antibiotic prescribing.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched up to January 2026. Additional records were identified through ClinicalTrials.gov and citation tracking. Eligible studies included hospitalized patients with documented penicillin or β-lactam allergy labels who underwent structured delabeling interventions with a comparator group. Given substantial heterogeneity in study design, interventions, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included (three randomized controlled trials and six nonrandomized studies). Delabeling success rates ranged from approximately 4% to over 95%, depending on intervention approach, risk of bias, and local workflows. The greatest success was observed in interventions using direct oral challenge for patients at low risk of true penicillin allergy. Pharmacist-led and antimicrobial stewardship-based interventions also effectively identified inaccurate allergy labels and supported safe delabeling. Adverse events were uncommon and predominantly mild. Delabeling was associated with improved prescribing practices, including greater use of narrow-spectrum β-lactams.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospital-based penicillin allergy delabeling interventions appear safe and locally effective when implemented within structured clinical pathways. However, the current evidence base is structurally fragmented, and extreme clinical and methodological heterogeneity limits the formulation of universal hospital protocols. Standardized, multi-center randomized controlled trials are urgently needed to establish uniform risk stratification algorithms and outcome metrics.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251246346.

articles.title: Potassium-Competitive Acid Blockers in GERD and Helicobacter pylori Infection: The Emerging Role of Fexuprazan.
articles.abstract: The pharmacological control of gastric acid secretion has evolved substantially over the past five decades, yet clinically important limitations remain with delayed-release proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), including delayed onset of action, meal dependency, nocturnal acid breakthrough, and variable intragastric pH control. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) represent a major advance in antisecretory therapy by providing rapid, potent, sustained, and meal-independent inhibition of the gastric H+,K+-ATPase through a reversible mechanism of action. Among currently available P-CABs, fexuprazan is a relatively recent agent for which an expanding body of pharmacological and clinical evidence has become available. This review critically examines its pharmacology, experimental biology, and clinical efficacy, with particular emphasis on gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Helicobacter pylori infection. Randomized controlled trials and real-world studies demonstrate that fexuprazan is non-inferior to esomeprazole in healing erosive esophagitis, with evidence of rapid symptom improvement, effective nocturnal symptom control, and greater dosing flexibility. Emerging data also suggest potential benefit in extra-esophageal manifestations of GERD. Experimental studies indicate anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and epithelial barrier-protective properties, although their clinical relevance remains to be established. In H. pylori infection, the profound and sustained intragastric pH elevation achieved with P-CABs may enhance eradication therapy, and fexuprazan-based triple, quadruple, and dual regimens have shown promising efficacy and tolerability. Overall, current evidence indicates that fexuprazan is an effective and well-tolerated P-CAB that may overcome some of the limitations of conventional PPIs, while ongoing comparative and long-term studies will further define its place in the management of acid-related disorders.

articles.title: Postoperative membranous urethral length and continence recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a Bayesian longitudinal meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Postoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-measured membranous urethral length (MUL) may reflect the functional urethral substrate preserved after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). We aimed to characterise how postoperative MUL influences the likelihood and timing of urinary continence recovery after RARP. This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261518338) searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL. Eligible cohort studies assessed postoperative MRI-measured MUL and urinary continence after RARP. Continence outcomes were synthesised using Bayesian longitudinal meta-regression. Time-specific continence probabilities, odds ratios per MUL increment, and modelled time to 50% continence probability were estimated. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using QUIPS and GRADE. Eight cohorts comprising 938 patients were included. At a reference postoperative MUL of 13.52 mm, modelled continence probabilities were 26.4%, 57.8%, 76.1%, and 88.1% at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively. Per-millimetre odds ratios for continence were 1.31 (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.04-1.67) at 1 month and 1.55 (1.21-2.03) at 12 months. Modelled time to 50% cohort-level continence probability was 2.32 months (95% CrI 1.12-4.71) at the reference MUL and a 1-mm increase was associated with a 22.3% (7.9-35.9%) shorter time.Excluding one influential study attenuated the association, with CrIs crossing 1. The overall certainty of evidence was rated as low. Longer postoperative MUL was associated with greater modelled continence probability and earlier modelled recovery. Prospective validation of the incremental predictive value of postoperative MUL beyond established predictors is required to justify routine postoperative MRI or guide individual prognostication.

articles.title: When age matters: mortality and disability after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in a cohort of elderly patients.
articles.abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) in older adults is associated with high early mortality and substantial long-term disability. As referral patterns and neurocritical care have evolved, the age at which prognosis changes markedly remains uncertain, and longitudinal functional trajectories beyond discharge are poorly characterised in elderly patients. We retrospectively included consecutive patients aged 65 years or older admitted with confirmed aSAH to the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery (London, UK) between February 2013 and August 2022. Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality, all-cause mortality during follow-up, and functional disability (modified Rankin Scale, mRS) at discharge and last follow-up (unfavourable outcome defined as mRS 4-6). Age thresholds associated with mortality and disability were identified using receiver operating characteristic analysis with the Youden index and confirmed by maximally selected rank statistics. Predictors of in-hospital death, survival, and disability were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Functional trajectories were summarised using transition matrices and Sankey diagrams. Among 110 patients (median age 76 years; 80% women), in-hospital mortality was 18.2% and all-cause mortality during follow-up was 48.2% (median follow-up 24 months). Age independently predicted in-hospital death (odds ratio 1.19 per year, 95% CI 1.06-1.35) and long-term mortality (hazard ratio 1.16 per year, 95% CI 1.09-1.22). An exploratory, cohort-derived age cut point of 79.5 years delineated divergent trajectories: mortality increased from 10.4% in patients aged < 80 years to 36.4% in those aged ≥ 80 years, and median survival declined from 95 months to 3 months (log-rank p = 2.8 × 10⁻⁶). Among patients discharged alive, discharge mRS independently predicted post-discharge survival (hazard ratio 2.39 per point, 95% CI 1.60-3.56), including in those aged ≥ 80 years (hazard ratio 3.34, 95% CI 1.21-9.20). Functional trajectories showed frequent post-discharge recovery in patients aged < 80 years, whereas recovery was uncommon and progression to death frequent in those aged ≥ 80 years. In this cohort of elderly patients with aSAH, an exploratory, cohort-derived threshold of approximately 80 years identified patients with markedly lower survival and functional recovery. Longitudinal trajectory analysis suggests post-discharge improvement remains common in patients aged < 80 years but rare in those aged ≥ 80 years.

articles.title: Unusual [18F]FDOPA PET-CT maging of insulinomas in children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Insulinomas are rare pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, causing recurrent episodes of hypoglycaemia. Accurate localisation is essential for surgical management, yet imaging remains challenging. This case series presents unusual findings of paediatric insulinomas on [18F]-dihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]FDOPA) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed medical notes and investigations of histologically proven paediatric insulinoma cases (n=4) presenting to Royal Manchester Children's Hospital between 2008 and 2024. All patients underwent [18F]FDOPA PET-CT as part of their diagnostic workup. Imaging findings were analysed, with particular attention to tracer uptake patterns.

RESULTS: Contrary to the increased tracer uptake typically seen in neuroendocrine tumours, three of the four insulinomas demonstrated focal photopenia at the site of the tumour on [18F]FDOPA PET-CT. Only one case showed increased uptake, suggesting a predominance of reduced, rather than enhanced, tracer activity in paediatric insulinomas CONCLUSION: Photopenia on [18F]FDOPA PET-CT may be a more frequent finding than increased uptake in paediatric insulinomas. Recognizing this atypical pattern is important for accurate tumour localisation before surgical management. Further studies are needed to validate these findings and find a mechanistic explanation.

articles.title: Biocontrol of postharvest Fusarium oxysporum on fruits and vegetables: mechanisms and efficacy of antagonistic microorganisms.
articles.abstract: Fusarium oxysporum is a major postharvest pathogen causing significant losses in stored fruits, vegetables, tubers, and bulbs. Understanding its infection mechanisms is essential for developing effective biological control strategies. This review synthesizes current knowledge on postharvest infection by F. oxysporum, including wound-dependent penetration, production of toxins (beauvericin, fusaric acid) and cell wall-degrading enzymes (polygalacturonases, cellulases), and tissue colonization leading to rot and mycotoxin accumulation. It critically evaluates biological control agents (BCAs) from three major groups bacteria (Bacillus, Pseudomonas), yeasts (Metschnikowia, Wickerhamomyces), and filamentous fungi (Trichoderma) with emphasis on their modes of action: nutrient competition (iron chelation via siderophores or pulcherrimin), antimicrobial production (lipopeptides, volatile organic compounds, hydrolytic enzymes), and mycoparasitism (unique to Trichoderma). The interactions between the pathogen and BCAs are examined within the postharvest wound microenvironment, highlighting the competitive dynamics that determine infection outcomes. Based on published storage trials, the review identifies critical knowledge gaps limiting commercial translation: most BCA efficacy studies have been conducted at 25-28 °C, and in vivo data under cold storage (4-10 °C) remain scarce; direct quantification of pathogen virulence factors in infected fruit tissues is lacking; and transcriptomic analyses of F. oxysporum during biocontrol challenge are still unavailable. A research roadmap is proposed, including cold storage screening, in situ metabolomics, RNA-seq of the pathogen during BCA exposure, multi-strain efficacy testing, and LAMP diagnostics integration.

articles.title: Effect of photobiomodulation on recovery from oral soft tissue local anaesthesia in paediatric patients: a preliminary split-mouth randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Paediatric dental patients are particularly vulnerable to inadvertent soft-tissue injury following local anaesthesia (LA) This preliminary study evaluated. the clinical efficacy of 810-nm diode laser photobiomodulation (PBM) in reversing oral soft-tissue anaesthesia in paediatric patients. Thirty-four children aged 8-12 years requiring bilateral primary toothextractions under infiltration LA were enrolled in by consideration of ethical codes. Local anaesthesia was administered using 2% lidocaine with 1:80,000 epinephrine, as per the local infiltration anesthesia protocol. Participants were randomly allocated to receive both PBM and sham Laser with 7-10 days washout period between the two interventions. PBM was delivered using an 810-nm diode laser in continuous mode at 200 mW for 12 s per point at six predefined intraoral and extraoral sites. An independent examiner assessed soft-tissue sensation at 5-minute intervals by standardized bilateral palpation, using the non-anaesthetized side as the reference. The primary outcome was time to first assessment at which sensation on the anaesthetized side was judged normal. Data were analysed using a paired-samples t-test. Mean reflection time was significantly shorter in the PBM group (60.7 ± 27.3 min; p < 0.001) compared with the Sham lasergroup (78.2 ± 17.0 min). Subgroup analysis demonstrated significant reductions in reflection time in both maxillary and mandibular arches. Photobiomodulation using an 810-nm diode laser demonstrated a reduction in subjective soft tissue anaesthesia recovery time following infiltration LA in paediatric dental patients under the conditions tested.

articles.title: Clinical impact of a drug information service provided by a pharmacovigilance centre in a French University Hospital.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pharmacovigilance Centres (PVCs) provide independent drug information to healthcare professionals in addition to their pharmacovigilance activities. However, their impact on clinical decision-making has been poorly studied. This study assessed the impact of a French PVC on clinical management in a tertiary university hospital (Toulouse University Hospital).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study including all drug-related enquiries submitted to the Toulouse PVC during 2024. Impact was evaluated according to three predefined criteria: whether the enquiry was submitted before or after a clinical management decision had been made, concordance between PVC recommendations and subsequent clinical management, and documentation of the advice in the electronic patient record. Based on these criteria, impact was classified as certain, probable, or uncertain for enquiries submitted before clinical management, and as confirmatory (validating an already implemented decision) or uncertain for enquiries submitted after clinical management had already been initiated.

RESULTS: A total of 128 enquiries were analysed. Most concerned adverse drug reactions (111/128), involved hospitalised patients (100/128), and originated from a broad range of clinical departments, mainly geriatrics (14/128), gastroenterology (11/128), neurology (11/128), infectious diseases (10/128) and internal medicine (10/128).
