Stroke status was identified using predefined International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and Tenth Revision codes. INR and Hct were defined using the first measurements within 24 h after ICU admission. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, quartile analyses, restricted cubic splines (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses. Primary analyses used complete-case cohorts, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. A post hoc exploratory secondary analysis among patients with stroke used Cox regression to identify six prognostic variables for machine learning-based prediction of ICU mortality. Stroke proportions decreased across increasing INR quartiles and increased across increasing Hct quartiles. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in INR was associated with lower stroke odds, with odds ratios (ORs) of 0.105-0.395 across cohorts, whereas each 1-percentage-point increase in Hct was associated with higher stroke odds (ORs, 1.076-1.103). RCS analyses supported overall associations but not consistent nonlinearity after full adjustment. Multiple-imputation results were directionally consistent. The gradient boosting machine (GBM) model yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.717 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.669-0.766), 0.670 (95% CI, 0.603-0.737), and 0.630 (95% CI, 0.557-0.703) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. INR was inversely associated and Hct positively associated with stroke status. These observational associations require cautious interpretation; the exploratory ICU mortality analysis provides a complementary prognostic perspective among patients with stroke.

articles.title: Predicting 30-day mortality in upper gastrointestinal bleeding using APUA components and lactate: Development and internal validation.
articles.abstract: Early mortality risk assessment is crucial for acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB). This study sought to develop and internally validate a prediction model using age, pulse, urea, and albumin (APUA) components, and to assess the added value of admission lactate levels. This retrospective, single-center study included 700 adults presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute UGIB between 2018 and 2025, excluding confirmed variceal hemorrhage. We developed multivariable logistic regression models, both with and without lactate, using continuous APUA components to predict 30-day all-cause mortality. Complete-case analyses evaluated discrimination, calibration, and net benefit, with internal validation performed using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Fifty-two patients (7.4%) died within 30 days. Lactate was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 1-mmol/L increase, 1.455; 95% confidence interval, 1.270-1.667). Adding lactate significantly increased the apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.693 to 0.777 (AUC difference, 0.084; p = 0.003) and improved the optimism-corrected concordance statistic from 0.670 to 0.756. Calibration and overall predictive accuracy also improved, and decision curve analysis showed a higher net benefit across most evaluated thresholds. Furthermore, lactate enhanced the apparent discrimination of three established comparator scores. While the APUA-component model demonstrated modest discrimination, incorporating lactate significantly improved its predictive performance. Independent external validation is necessary before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Eosinophilic myocarditis in platelet-derived growth factor receptor α-rearranged myeloid neoplasm with central nervous system involvement: a case report.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Eosinophilic myocarditis is a rare inflammatory condition caused by eosinophilic infiltration of the myocardium, often associated with systemic or hematologic disorders. We report a 31-year-old man with a newly diagnosed platelet-derived growth factor receptor α-rearranged myeloid neoplasm who presented with acute chest pain and elevated cardiac biomarkers. Echocardiography showed Loeffler-type apical involvement, coronary computed tomography angiography excluded obstructive coronary disease, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) demonstrated acute non-ischemic inflammatory myocardial injury. During hospitalization, neurological symptoms revealed central nervous system involvement by the underlying myeloid neoplasm. Corticosteroids and targeted hematologic treatment resulted in marked clinical and radiologic improvement. On long-term follow-up, CMR showed normal cardiac function with complete resolution of the inflammatory myocardial abnormalities and no residual fibrosis. This case highlights the value of early multimodality cardiac imaging, etiologic diagnosis, and coordinated cardio-hematologic management in recognizing potentially reversible eosinophilic myocardial injury and limiting progression to irreversible cardiac sequelae.

articles.title: Expert consensus on neuro-musculoskeletal functional reconstruction for post-stroke spastic hemiplegia.
authors: “Zunyi Brain‐Computer Interface Medical Center” Working Group
articles.abstract: Persistent motor dysfunction in post-stroke spastic hemiplegia may result from impaired voluntary motor control, abnormal muscle overactivity, fixed structural restriction, muscle force imbalance, or their combination. Advances in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), peripheral nerve surgery, and tendon and soft-tissue reconstruction have expanded therapeutic options, yet optimal indications and sequencing remain unclear. A multidisciplinary expert panel reviewed current evidence, addressed key clinical questions, and developed consensus recommendations for noninvasive BCI, diagnostic motor nerve block (DNB), selective or hyperselective peripheral nerve surgery, and reconstructive procedures. The consensus emphasizes evaluation of four major components: central voluntary motor impairment, dynamic abnormal muscle overactivity, fixed structural limitations, and muscle force imbalance. Treatment should be guided by the patient's functional goals and the primary factor restricting performance. Task-oriented motor training remains fundamental when voluntary motor control is impaired, with BCI-based closed-loop training as a potential adjunct in selected patients. Focal, functionally significant muscle overactivity caused by abnormal neural drive may be considered for selective or hyperselective peripheral nerve surgery, with DNB assisting patient selection. Fixed structural restrictions may require tendon or soft-tissue procedures, while muscle force imbalance may benefit from tendon transfer or other dynamic reconstruction. When multiple impairments coexist, combined reconstruction followed by targeted motor retraining and comprehensive reassessment may be appropriate. Overall, neuro-musculoskeletal functional reconstruction should follow an individualized pathway linking functional goals, dominant pathophysiology, treatment targets, and outcomes. Given the variable evidence quality, no universal treatment sequence or combination strategy is currently supported.

articles.title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Stroke Risk Decision System for Patients With Carotid Artery Plaque Based on AI-Powered Handheld Ultrasound and Laboratory Markers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a fusion model combining portable artificial intelligence (AI) ultrasound imaging with multidimensional laboratory data to stratify risk and support decision-making in patients with carotid plaque-related anterior circulation stroke, and to assess its predictive performance and clinical utility.

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded. All participants completed the 180-day follow-up. The primary outcome was new-onset anterior circulation stroke or TIA, defined as focal neurological deficit > 24 h with CT/MRI-confirmed infarction, or transient (< 24 h) deficit without evidence of acute infarction on neuroimaging. Outcomes were adjudicated by two neurologists (attending or above), with a third for disagreements. Participants were classified into ACS group (n = 140) and non-ACS group (n = 499). Ultrasound features of carotid plaques and clinical laboratory data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with ACS, and a nomogram was constructed based on the regression model. Internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap method. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (C-index and area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis [DCA] and clinical impact curves [CIC]).

RESULTS: (1) Significant differences were observed between the two groups in history of hypertension, smoking, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI), as well as plasma triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels, carotid plaque thickness, plaque area, plaque echogenicity percentage, degree of carotid stenosis, plaque continuity score, and plaque mutability score (p < 0.05). No significant differences were found in sex, history of diabetes, total cholesterol (TC), plaque location, or plaque fibrous cap continuity analysis score (p > 0.05) (2) Multivariable logistic regression identified history of stroke, history of myocardial infarction, plaque thickness, LDL, and HDL as independent predictors of stroke. A nomogram based on these factors demonstrated good discrimination (C-index/AUC = 0.884), with a sensitivity of 84.29% and specificity of 72.55%, along with excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.250). Decision curve analysis showed superior net benefit across a range of risk thresholds compared with the null model, supporting a multi-threshold stratified intervention strategy. Notably, when the predicted risk exceeded 75%, the model's predictions closely aligned with observed outcomes.

CONCLUSION: The stroke risk decision system developed using AI-powered handheld ultrasound and laboratory indicators demonstrates clinical applicability for early prediction of anterior circulation ischemic stroke and is particularly suitable for early screening and risk stratification of high-risk stroke populations in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Two conserved early effectors from Puccinia triticina are required for pathogenicity by suppressing callose deposition and hydrogen peroxide accumulation in wheat.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wheat leaf rust, caused by the causal agent Puccinia triticina (Pt), poses a serious threat to wheat production worldwide. Pt secretes plenty of effectors into the host plant to manipulate host immune responses and facilitate successful colonization. However, effectors during the early stages of Pt infection remain largely unknown.

RESULTS: Here, we employed deep RNA-sequencing on samples extracted from wheat leaves of a susceptible wheat cultivar, Thatcher, inoculated with Pt at 8 and 24 h post-inoculation, which enabled the identification of candidate effectors implicated in suppressing early plant immune responses. Through integrated transcriptomic analysis and an optimized effector identification workflow, early candidate effector-encoding genes that are highly expressed during Pt infection were identified and characterized. Functional assays revealed that two effector candidates, Pt01364 and Pt09156, exhibited the ability to suppress Bax-induced cell death in Nicotiana benthamiana. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis demonstrated that both genes peaked at 8 h post-inoculation, and the yeast secretion trap assay showed that these two cell death-suppressing effector candidates possess functional signal peptides for secretion into host cells. Silencing of Pt01364 and Pt09156 significantly compromised Pt pathogenicity on a susceptible wheat cultivar. In addition, both effectors can inhibit callose deposition triggered by non-host bacteria and reduce hydrogen peroxide accumulation in wheat in response to avirulent Pt infection.

CONCLUSION: This study provides a basis for identifying key effectors involved in the early stages of wheat-Pt interaction, highlighting Pt01364 and Pt09156 as promising candidate targets for developing innovative strategies to control wheat leaf rust. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Dentists' knowledge, attitudes, and clinical approaches to bruxism-related activities potentially associated with antidepressant use.
articles.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess dentists' knowledge, attitudes, self-efficacy, and approaches to bruxism-related activities potentially associated with antidepressant use in Türkiye.

METHODS: This online survey included 253 dentists. Knowledge counted correct responses to five researcher-developed, nonvalidated items (0-5). Ordinal regression included a partial proportional-odds model where needed; Holm correction addressed prespecified comparisons.

RESULTS: In the past year, 41.1% definitely encountered a patient taking antidepressants with bruxism-related symptoms, while 32.8% were unsure. Mean score was 3.08 ± 1.47/5; 29.4% recognized potential associations with both SSRIs and SNRIs. Previous training was independently associated with higher knowledge and self-efficacy. Knowledge and training were independently associated with more frequent medication-history assessment. Specialty and experience were not independently associated with knowledge. Detailed medication history was the most common initial approach (32.4%).

CONCLUSION: Knowledge varied, particularly regarding SSRI/SNRI involvement. Education should emphasize behavior-specific terminology, medication-history assessment, clinical reasoning, and interdisciplinary communication. Cross-sectional self-reports preclude causal inference.

articles.title: A Standardized Procedure for Post-Mortem Harvesting of the Brain and Rete Mirabile in Domestic Pigs.
articles.abstract: The domestic pig is a well-established animal model and may be regarded as the gold standard for preclinical testing of cardiovascular medical devices, given anatomical similarities to humans. Pigs (among other species) possess a unique anatomical structure-the rete mirabile (RM), an arterial anastomosis located at the base of the cranium, preventing the passage of emboli to brain circulation. The RM has become a target site for post-mortem evaluation, primarily in safety studies involving left-sided cardiovascular devices. We present here a post-mortem dissection technique to achieve complete and intact harvest of the brain and RM in pigs. This surgical dissection technique was developed based on fluoroscopic angiography and computed tomography (CT) of the pig's head. The dissection process involved craniotomy, incision of the dura, followed by harvesting of the brain and RM. The developed technique facilitates efficient and effective harvesting of the brain and RM in pigs.

articles.title: Sharps Disposal Practices and Associated Factors Among Adults With Hemophilia Receiving Home-Based Treatment.
articles.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The increasing use of home-based parenteral therapies has made the safe management of sharps waste a significant public health concern.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate sharps use and disposal practices among patients with haemophilia receiving home treatment and to identify factors associated with proper disposal.

METHODS: This cross-sectional, descriptive study included 69 adult haemophilia receiving home-based treatment. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, group comparisons, and logistic regression analysis were performed to identify factors associated with proper disposal.

RESULTS: The majority of patients disposed of sharps waste in household trash, while only a small proportion used appropriate disposal methods. In-home sharps exposure was reported. Logistic regression analysis showed that concern about sharps waste was the only factor significantly associated with proper disposal, increasing the likelihood by approximately 5.5 times. No significant associations were found between demographic or clinical characteristics and proper disposal. Approximately three-quarters of participants reported disposing of sharps in household waste.

CONCLUSIONS: Sharps disposal rates are low among patients with haemophilia receiving home-based treatment. Previous information regarding sharps waste disposal was associated with safer disposal practices, although appropriate disposal may also depend on accessible and structured waste management systems. Improving disposal requires not only education but also accessible and structured waste management systems.

articles.title: Emicizumab Prophylaxis in Patients With Acquired Hemophilia A During Immunosuppressive Therapy: Real-World Data From the Spanish Acquired Hemophilia Registry.
articles.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acquired hemophilia A (AHA) is a rare bleeding disorder in which immunosuppressive therapy (IST) and hemostatic management remain challenging, particularly in elderly patients. Evidence supporting emicizumab use in AHA under real-world conditions remains limited.

AIM: To assess efficacy and safety of emicizumab in providing hemostatic protection until inhibitor eradication.

METHODS: We analyse data from the Spanish Acquired Haemophilia Registry, including patients newly diagnosed between 2022 and 2025. Bleeding episodes and red blood cell (RBC) transfusion requirements before and after establishment of effective emicizumab prophylaxis were compared.

RESULTS: Twenty patients were included, 85.0% older than 75 years. Only two patients received the accelerated AHA loading regimen used in pivotal AHA studies (6 mg/kg on Day 1, 3 mg/kg on Day 2, followed by 1.5 mg/kg weekly from Day 8). All patients presented with active bleeding at diagnosis. Before emicizumab prophylaxis, all patients experienced bleeding episodes and 70.0% required RBC transfusions. Using Day-7 after the first dose of emicizumab as landmark of efficacy, only 2 patients (10.0%) reported breakthrough bleeding episodes and one patient required RBC transfusion (p = 0.001). Seventeen (85.0%) patients achieved remission after 64 (55-109) days. Two patients died of sepsis during IST. No thrombotic events attributable to emicizumab were observed.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world AHA cohort, emicizumab was associated with effective and sustained hemostatic protection, marked reduction in bleeding and RBC transfusion requirements. Prospective studies are needed to define the optimal strategy and to determine whether emicizumab can facilitate individualized timing and intensity of IST.

articles.title: Always Connected, Never Off Duty: Family Experiences of Caring in Technology-Enabled Diabetes Care.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study was to explore family experiences of caring for adolescents and adults living with Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes in the context of technology-enabled diabetes care. An interpretive qualitative study was conducted with 24 family caregivers recruited through purposive sampling in Indonesia. Individual semi-structured interviews were undertaken from August 2025 to April 2026 and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four interconnected themes were identified: (a) Caregiving Without Boundaries, (b) Living in Continuous Vigilance, (c) Negotiating Care, Control, and Independence, and (d) Searching for Moments of Being Off Duty. Diabetes technologies extended caregiving beyond physical proximity, fostering continuous vigilance, reshaping family relationships, and prompting caregivers to balance protection, autonomy, and well-being while remaining digitally connected. Technology-enabled diabetes care fundamentally reshapes family caregiving as a continuous relational process. Family nursing should support sustainable caregiving by addressing not only technological competence but also caregiving boundaries, family relationships, and caregiver well-being.

articles.title: Early SLP Involvement in Postoperative Tracheostomy Care Significantly Reduces Hospital Costs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the role of speech-language pathologists (SLPs) in the postoperative care of tracheostomized patients and determine if earlier involvement of SLP with tracheostomized patients results in earlier decannulation, reduced hospital length of stay (LOS), or reduced hospital costs.

METHODS: Data including time from tracheostomy placement to SLP consult, time from tracheostomy placement to tracheostomy decannulation, and hospital LOS were collected on all patients who underwent open tracheostomy at an academic tertiary care center between January 1, 2023 and May 31, 2024.

RESULTS: Shorter time to SLP consult was associated with shorter time to decannulation (p < 0.0001) and shorter hospital LOS (p < 0.000001). Conversely, each day earlier that SLP consultation occurred was associated with a 1.39-day shorter LOS and an estimated cost savings of $1039.30 per day on the medical-surgical floor, $1581.10 in the intermediate care unit, and $2221.00 in the intensive care unit.

CONCLUSION: Early SLP involvement in tracheostomized patients' care benefits the patient and hospital system by hastening safe decannulation, reducing LOS, and lowering costs. These findings are limited to patients undergoing open surgical tracheostomy and may not be generalizable to percutaneous tracheostomy populations.

articles.title: Primary arteriovenous fistula functionality and complications in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease: A single-centre outcomes report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Native arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for long-term hemodialysis. Primary non-function and inadequate maturation remain clinically significant problems, and detailed single-centre outcome series contribute to the evidence base, particularly in patient populations with a high prevalence of comorbidities such as diabetes mellitus.

AIM: To describe the recorded functionality categories and postoperative complication profile after primary AVF creation in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), and to identify baseline characteristics independently associated with an adverse functionality category.

METHODS: This single-centre outcomes study prospectively collected data on 96 consecutive adults with stage 4-5 CKD who underwent primary native AVF creation during 2020-2021. The primary endpoint was a three-level ordered functionality category: non-functional (0), functional at 12 months (1), and functional at 36 months (2).

RESULTS: Mean age was 65.8 ± 11.6 years; 60 patients (62.5%) were male. Forty-five patients (46.9%) had diabetes mellitus; 50 (52.1%) received a distal and 46 (47.9%) a proximal AVF. Twenty-two AVFs (22.9%) were non-functional, 27 (28.1%) were functional at 12 months, and 47 (49.0%) were functional at 36 months. In the adjusted binary logistic model, diabetes mellitus was strongly associated with primary non-function (adjusted OR 27.79, 95% CI 5.56-138.84; p < 0.001), while proximal AVF location offered a prognostic advantage (adjusted OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.74; p = 0.014). In the adjusted ordinal model, diabetes was associated with lower odds of a more favorable functionality category (adjusted OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.14-0.41; p < 0.001), and proximal AVF location with higher odds (adjusted OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.62-4.55; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Diabetes mellitus was the strongest baseline predictor of primary AVF non-function and adverse recorded functionality in this outcomes series. Proximal AVF location was independently associated with a more favorable functionality category.

articles.title: Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology of a Postoperative Foreign Body Reaction Mimicking Peritoneal Metastasis From Colon Adenocarcinoma.
articles.journal: Cytopathology : official journal of the British Society for Clinical Cytology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) is a very useful tool in the management of oncological patients. It is a straightforward and quick diagnostic tool, and it can also obtain material for molecular studies that can help guide therapy. However, FNAC is not always performed when radiological studies seem conclusive. We herein report a peculiar case in which FNAC diagnosis completely changed the management of a patient.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A 75-year-old man underwent laparoscopic surgical resection of TNM stage I low-grade intestinal adenocarcinoma. A follow-up CT scan 1 year after surgery revealed multiple peritoneal nodules in the left flank, with an increased FDG uptake in the PET-CT. Radiological diagnosis was peritoneal seeding of carcinoma. FNAC was performed to confirm diagnosis, obtaining a blue material. The smears revealed a large number of histocytes engulfing a dark blue material with no tumour cells. Radiological follow-up was decided and 2 and a half years after diagnosis, the nodules have remained stable and the FDG uptake has steadily decreased over time.

DISCUSSION: Foreign-body reaction against sutures and meshes employed in abdominal surgery has been widely analysed in experimental models. Lymphocytes and histiocytes are the main inflammatory cells responsible for this reaction. In the literature there are few reports of foreign-body reaction mimicking peritoneal seeding of carcinomas, and all of them were diagnosed with a biopsy of suspicious nodules. A thorough review of the literature has not revealed any similar case in which FNAC allowed diagnosis of foreign body reaction avoiding the need of surgical exploration and unnecessary systemic therapy.

CONCLUSION: We herein report a unique case in which FNAC led to the correct diagnosis of a foreign body reaction, avoiding aggressive measures in an oncologic patient.

articles.title: Comment on "Effects of age, sex, and renal function on bowel movement-improving effects of Bifidobacterium bifidum G9-1 on constipation in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease: A prespecified subgroup analysis of the BIRDIE study".
Measurement of Manual Dexterity Utilising VR Haptic Simulators.
articles.journal: European journal of dental education : official journal of the Association for Dental Education in Europe
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In dental education, measuring manual dexterity is an ongoing challenge. This study aims to quantitatively differentiate the manual dexterity skills between pre-dental students and senior dental students by utilising a virtual reality haptic simulator. It is assumed that with increased training, senior dental students will demonstrate greater manual dexterity compared to those without dental training.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Approval for this study was granted by the Institutional Review Board at Temple University Kornberg School of Dentistry (IRB Study # 31300-001). Two groups were compared to investigate manual dexterity abilities using the SimToCare Dente Virtual Reality Haptic Simulator. The first group comprised 30 pre-dental students who had not yet matriculated into dental school. The second group consisted of 30 senior dental students in their final year of receiving their dental degree. Both groups were instructed to virtually prepare a pre-designed cavity in the shape of a cross on a virtual ivorene block. The haptic simulator recorded parameters to evaluate the accuracy and errors of the preparations. An overall score was generated for each trial, and the average for each group was calculated to measure manual dexterity. It was hypothesised that a significant difference in preparation statistics would be observed between the senior and pre-dental students across three trials, with the difference widening between the first and subsequent trials and eventually plateauing, resulting in a logarithmic growth graph for both groups.

RESULTS: The pre-dental students did not show a significant increase in their scores across the three trials, unlike the senior students. Furthermore, the senior students achieved significantly higher overall scores in the second and third trials compared to the pre-dental participants.

CONCLUSION: The study demonstrates a significant difference in manual dexterity, as measured by SimToCare haptic simulators, between pre-dental and senior dental students. The SimToCare Haptic Simulator can be an effective tool for quantifying manual dexterity. Further research is necessary to develop an educational workflow for integrating haptic simulators into the digital dentistry education curriculum.

articles.title: The miR-176-DcFoxO axis links CLas infection to juvenile hormone signaling and enhanced fecundity in Diaphorina citri.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The phloem-limited bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas), associated with huanglongbing (HLB) disease, is transmitted by the Asian citrus psyllid, Diaphorina citri. CLas-positive females display enhanced fecundity and increased metabolic demands, a phenotype that may promote both vector population growth and bacterial proliferation. Although recent studies have revealed that CLas-associated reproductive enhancement involves neuroendocrine and neurotransmitter pathways, the transcriptional regulators linking persistent bacterial infection, energy metabolism, juvenile hormone (JH) signaling, and ovarian development remain poorly understood.

RESULTS: Here, we identify the forkhead transcription factor DcFoxO as a previously unrecognized regulatory node associated with CLas-induced fecundity enhancement in D. citri. DcFoxO expression was significantly elevated in the ovaries of CLas-positive females during reproductive maturation. RNA interference-mediated silencing of DcFoxO reduced triacylglycerol and glycogen reserves, decreased lipid droplet accumulation, impaired ovarian development, reduced fecundity, and lowered CLas titers in the ovaries. Using dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), and microRNA (miRNA) gain-of-function experiments, we demonstrated that miR-176 directly targets the 3' untranslated region of DcFoxO and negatively regulates its expression. Overexpression of miR-176 phenocopied DcFoxO knockdown, suppressing energy reserves, ovarian development, fecundity, and CLas proliferation. Mechanistically, DcFoxO silencing or miR-176 overexpression reduced JH titers and down-regulated core JH-responsive reproductive genes, including DcMet, DcKr-h1, DcVg, and DcVgR.

CONCLUSION: These findings reveal a miR-176-DcFoxO-JH regulatory axis that links CLas infection to metabolic reprogramming, ovarian maturation, and enhanced vector fecundity. This study adds a transcriptional layer to the emerging model of CLas-mediated manipulation of D. citri reproduction and identifies potential molecular targets for disrupting vector performance and HLB transmission. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Determinants of Infant Diarrhoea and Respiratory Illness in a Low-Resource Community in South Africa: A Structural Equation Modelling.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diarrhoea and acute respiratory infections continue to cause significant morbidity in children under 5 years, influenced by multiple factors. This secondary data analysis of the Eggcel randomised controlled study aimed to explore the association of anthropometric status, food insecurity, socioeconomic and environmental factors with diarrhoea and respiratory morbidity in children aged 6-9 months from a low-resource community in South Africa.

METHODS: We utilised data from 216 infants in the control group who completed the Eggcel-growth randomised controlled trial in Jouberton, South Africa. Baseline data on maternal and infant demographics, household socioeconomic and environmental conditions were collected using a questionnaire. Food insecurity was assessed through the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES). Anthropometric measurements, including weight, height and head circumference, taken at baseline were used. Morbidity symptoms were recorded daily by mothers using a visual wellness diary. The exposure latent variables included anthropometric status, environmental conditions, food insecurity and socioeconomic status. Outcome variables were diarrhoea or respiratory episodes over the 6-month follow-up period. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was performed using R version 4.5.0.

RESULTS: Infants with diarrhoea had higher stunting and underweight rates at 28/75 (37.3%) and 9/75 (12.0%), respectively, and the highest access to safe water at 74/75 (98.7%). Higher anthropometric status was associated with a 31% reduction in diarrhoea (IRR = 0.69; 95% CI: 0.50, 0.95; p = 0.022). Respiratory episodes were not associated with any of the latent factors.

CONCLUSION: Nutritional status was an important determinant of diarrhoeal morbidity among infants in a low socioeconomic community but was not associated with respiratory morbidity. These findings suggest context-specific pathways through which nutritional, food insecurity and environmental factors may be associated with childhood morbidity.

articles.title: Correction to 'Relationship between maternal body composition changes and heavy for date infants in pregnant women with diabetes'.
Assessment of tools for the diagnosis of malnutrition and ICU outcomes in critically ill adults: A comparison study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the concurrent and predictive validity of the Academy of Nutrition & Dietetics/ASPEN Indicators for Malnutrition (AAIM) in critically ill patients compared with the SGA, considering disease etiology and fluid accumulation.

METHODS: This was a comparison study. Malnutrition was assessed within 24 h of ICU admission using the Subjective Global Assessment (SGA) and the AAIM consensus. The AAIM approach was applied assuming all patients had acute disease (AAIM I) or differentiating acute versus chronic disease-related malnutrition (AAIM II). Two variations were tested based on fluid accumulation: including (AAIM a) or excluding (AAIM b) this component. Concurrent validity was evaluated against SGA using diagnostic accuracy metrics, and predictive validity was assessed using hospital and ICU length of stay and mortality.

RESULTS: Among 450 critically ill patients [median age 64 (54-71) years; 53.1% male; APACHE II score 18 (11-23)], 46.3% were malnourished by SGA, whereas AAIM prevalence ranged from 70.9% to 75.5%. AAIM showed moderate sensitivity (75.1%-78.9%) but low specificity (28.6%-32.4%) and poor agreement with SGA (κ = 0.066-0.073). AAIM-defined malnutrition was not associated with outcomes, while SGA-defined malnutrition predicted prolonged hospital stay (OR 1.48; 95% CI 1.00-2.20) and ICU mortality (HR 2.26; 95% CI 1.42-3.49).

CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients, AAIM overestimated malnutrition prevalence and lacked concurrent and predictive validity, whereas SGA showed prognostic value.

articles.title: Outbreak of Mud Crab Reovirus (MCRV) in a Mud Crab (Scylla serrata) Fattening Facility in the Ashtamudi Backwaters, West Coast of India.
articles.abstract: The present study documents a confirmed outbreak of Mud Crab Reovirus (MCRV) in Scylla serrata from an open-water fattening facility in the Ashtamudi backwaters, Kerala, representing the first report of MCRV from the west coast of India. Mud crab farming has gained economic importance across Indian coastal states, but viral infections such as MCRV-related sleeping disease (SD) pose a critical threat to industry sustainability due to associated high mortalities. Moribund crabs exhibited gross pathological signs including gill atrophy, lethargy, reduced feeding and carapace biofouling. Histopathological analysis revealed widespread tissue degeneration, viral inclusions in gills, muscle and hepatopancreas. Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) confirmed the presence of non-enveloped, icosahedral viral particles within hepatopancreatic tissues, consistent with reovirus morphology. Reverse Transcription- Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) further validated MCRV infection across multiple tissues. This study highlights the urgent need for regional biosecurity frameworks, seed certification and targeted surveillance to prevent viral dissemination in open estuarine aquaculture systems.

articles.title: Hydroxychloroquine suppresses replication of PRRSV via dual regulation of autophagic flux and NF-κB-driven inflammatory signaling.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) induces excessive autophagy and aberrant nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cell (NF-κB) hyperactivation, triggering severe respiratory and reproductive disorders in pigs and causing massive economic losses to the global swine industry. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate (HCQ), a classic autophagy inhibitor, restricts PRRSV proliferation in vitro; however, its in vivo protective efficacy and dual-targeted molecular mechanisms remain poorly characterized. In this study, intramuscular HCQ administration conferred robust protection against lethal PRRSV infection in piglets: it completely eliminated virus-induced mortality, relieved fever and interstitial pulmonary lesions, and restored normal growth performance. In vitro assays confirmed that HCQ with negligible cytotoxicity within the concentration range of 1-100 μM interferes with multiple stages of PRRSV infection. Combined network pharmacology and cellular functional experiments revealed a dual regulatory mechanism of HCQ against PRRSV: HCQ blocks autophagosome-lysosome fusion to disrupt complete autophagic flux, and suppresses the IκBα-p65 signaling cascade to reduce the secretion of proinflammatory mediators. Dose-response analyses demonstrated that HCQ exerts potent antiviral activity against divergent field PRRSV isolates, porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) and swine acute diarrhea syndrome coronavirus (SADS-CoV) within a wide safe therapeutic window, with all broad-spectrum in vitro antiviral activity against diverse swine RNA viruses validated in cell culture models. Collectively, HCQ suppresses PRRSV replication by simultaneously regulating autophagic flux and NF-κB-dependent inflammatory signaling, supporting its repurposing as a promising therapeutic candidate for porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) control. Although HCQ exhibits broad-spectrum inhibitory activity against divergent PRRSV strains, PEDV, and SADS-CoV in cell culture, all anti-PEDV and anti-SADS-CoV effects are only validated in vitro without in vivo animal verification.

articles.title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolic events at 90 days in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence regarding venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in palliative care populations remains scarce, and current thromboprophylaxis recommendations are largely extrapolated from non-palliative oncology cohorts. This study aimed to determine the 90-day incidence of VTE and associated clinical risk factors in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults with advanced cancer enrolled in a palliative care program who were hospitalized between 2018 and 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Bogotá, Colombia. VTE incidence was calculated, and clinical risk factors were identified using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: A total of 782 patients were included (mean age 61 years; 58.7% male). Withing 90 days of admission, 81 patients (10.3%) developed VTE, corresponding to an incidence density of 2.3 events per 1,000 patient-days. Pulmonary embolism accounted for 40.7% of VTE events. In the adjusted analysis, lung cancer was associated with an increased risk of VTE (HR 2.34; p = 0.010), whereas higher Karnofsky Performance Status was associated with a lower risk (HR 0.98; p = 0.020). Age, sex, body mass index, baseline hemoglobin, active anticancer treatment, and white blood cell count were not independently associated with VTE. Overall, 90-day mortality was 66.3%.

CONCLUSION: VTE was a frequent complication among hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. Lung cancer and poor functional status were independently associated with VTE, whereas traditional clinical predictors were not associated with VTE. These findings support individualized VTE risk assessment and highlight the need for future prospective studies evaluating thromboprophylaxis strategies in palliative care settings.

articles.title: Brief education and nudging to facilitate TENS use in postoperative care: a quasi-experimental mixed methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implementing evidence-based practices into routine clinical care remains a challenge, with traditional implementation strategies yielding modest effects on clinical behavior. In postoperative pain management, evidence-based non-pharmacological modalities such as transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) remain underutilized. Nudging, through subtle modifications to the choice architecture, offers a cost-effective, resource-efficient approach to enhancing adoption and sustaining action at the point of care. This study evaluated whether combining a brief educational workshop with a nudging phase using visual prompts could enhance the adoption of TENS in routine postoperative care.

METHODS: An explanatory sequential mixed methods design was applied, combining a quasi-experimental pre-post study with three observation points and qualitative interviews. The study was conducted in a 15-bed postoperative ward at a Swedish university hospital. The intervention comprised a 45-minute hands-on educational workshop followed by a 12-week asynchronous and passive nudging phase. Quantitative data on TENS use were collected from a logbook maintained by healthcare professionals and analyzed with descriptive statistics and comparative tests. To contextualize and explain observed practice changes, semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of healthcare professionals (n = 13) were thematically analyzed.

RESULTS: TENS administrations increased significantly after the interventions compared to baseline. Qualitative findings showed that the interventions reframed TENS from a peripheral option to an integrated component of postoperative pain care. Nudging reinforced awareness, normalized TENS administration in everyday practice, and contributed to early routinization and maintained integration into clinical reasoning.

CONCLUSIONS: A brief educational workshop followed by a transparent asynchronous and passive nudging strategy was associated with increased and continued documented use of TENS during the study period, in a setting where no administrations were recorded at baseline despite available devices and a local protocol. This low-resource approach might complement traditional implementation strategies by increasing the visibility of evidence-based non-pharmacological options in routine postoperative care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06696430. Registered 13 November 2024, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06696430 .

articles.title: Physiological monitoring and physiology-informed strategies in cardiac arrest: current evidence and clinical translation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in cardiac arrest management, survival with favorable neurological outcomes remains limited. Physiological monitoring may complement standardized resuscitation by providing real-time information about circulatory effectiveness, reversible causes, and treatment responses. However, whether physiology-guided interventions improve patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the current evidence and clinical applicability of physiological monitoring during resuscitation, physiology-informed rescue strategies, and individualized post-cardiac arrest care.

MAIN BODY: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive arterial pressure monitoring, waveform capnography, and echocardiography provide complementary information about the circulation generated by chest compressions and potential mechanisms of resuscitation failure. Although observational and experimental studies support their physiological relevance, no adult diastolic pressure target or pressure-guided vasopressor strategy has been validated to improve survival or neurological recovery. Recent randomized trials of transesophageal echocardiography have demonstrated physiological or procedural effects without establishing clinical benefit. Among rescue strategies, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation has yielded inconsistent results across randomized trials, with potential benefits dependent on patient selection, intervention timing, and system capabilities. Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta has not improved clinical outcomes in randomized evaluation, while head-up resuscitation remains investigational. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, randomized trials have challenged the benefits of uniformly higher blood pressure and oxygenation targets, mild hypercapnia, and deeper or prolonged temperature control. Individualized approaches incorporating cerebral autoregulation, venous congestion, and cardiopulmonary physiology are physiologically appealing but lack prospective validation.

CONCLUSION: Physiological assessment may complement established resuscitation algorithms by refining clinical decisions during and after cardiac arrest. However, improvements in physiological measurements should not be equated with improved patient outcomes. Future trials should determine whether predefined, physiology-guided treatment strategies improve survival and neurological recovery.

articles.title: Mapping the biological effects of micro- and nanoplastics in mammalian intestinal models: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPLs) are increasingly recognized as emerging environmental contaminants with potential implications for gastrointestinal health. Although experimental research on intestinal MNPL toxicity has expanded rapidly, the available evidence remains highly heterogeneous with respect to experimental models, polymer composition, particle size, particle condition, exposure scenarios, and biological endpoints. Therefore, a structured evidence map is needed to clarify dominant methodological patterns and identify key knowledge gaps in the field.

METHODS: This study was conducted as a scoping review in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify eligible original in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo experimental research investigating the biological effects of MNPLs in mammalian intestinal models. Data were extracted and synthesized based on experimental models, particle characteristics, exposure scenarios, and toxicological outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 90 peer-reviewed studies were included from 3,540 initially identified records. The evidence base was strongly dominated by simplified experimental systems, with in vitro studies accounting for 88.9% of the included studies (n = 80/90). Caco-2-based systems represented the dominant experimental platform overall (52.2%, n = 47/90), while Caco-2 monoculture-like models accounted for 36.7% (n = 33/90). A pronounced polymer bias was observed, with polystyrene (PS) appearing in 60.0% of the included studies (n = 54/90). Nanoplastics were the most frequently investigated size category (60.0%, n = 54/90), and most studies relied on virgin particles (68.9%, n = 62/90). Across the literature, the most prominent evidence themes included oxidative stress and mitochondrial injury, uptake and translocation, barrier dysfunction and permeability changes, inflammation and immune signaling, and cell death- or DNA damage-related responses.

CONCLUSION: This scoping review demonstrates that intestinal MNPL research has expanded rapidly but remains methodologically concentrated in simplified in vitro systems and dominated by a limited range of polymer types and particle conditions. Although existing studies have generated important mechanistic insights, future progress will depend on the broader use of physiologically representative intestinal models, environmentally relevant polymers, and more standardized physicochemical characterization protocols. These findings provide a structured evidence map to support more realistic and translationally relevant future studies.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Low-dose versus standard dose of soybean-based intravenous lipid emulsions in neonates: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipid restriction strategies using soybean-based intravenous lipid emulsions (SO-ILE) have been proposed to mitigate the risk of parenteral nutrition-associated liver disease in neonates.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of low-dose versus standard-dose SO-ILE in neonates receiving parenteral nutrition.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases was conducted. Randomized controlled trials and nonrandomized cohort studies comparing low-dose (1 g/kg/day) versus standard-dose (2-3 g/kg/day) SO-ILE were included. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Statistical analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.4.1. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251057906).

RESULTS: Nine studies, including 6 randomized trials and 3 cohort studies, comprising 634 neonates, were included. The mean gestational age in the low-dose group was 32.2 ± 5.13 weeks. In the primary analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials, no significant differences were observed between low-dose and standard-dose SO-ILE for PNAC (53.4% vs. 48.5%; RR 1.08; 95% CI [0.84-1.39]; P = 0.55; I2 = 0%), mortality (5.7% vs. 6.2%; RR 0.99; 95% CI [0.34-2.88]; P = 0.99; I2 = 0%), days of parenteral nutrition (MD -1.75 days; 95% CI [-7.06-3.55]; P = 0.52; I2 = 0%), peak direct bilirubin levels, or weight at the end of the study period or at hospital discharge.

CONCLUSION: There is no difference between the use of low doses and standard doses of SO-ILE in neonates receiving parenteral nutrition with respect to liver-related, growth, or mortality outcomes.

articles.title: GLP-1-Based Therapy in Type 1 Diabetes: Balancing Efficacy, Safety, and Patient Selection.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To critically examine the evolving evidence on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide as adjuncts to insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes (T1D), with particular emphasis on their benefit-risk balance in individuals with overweight or obesity.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This narrative review examines evidence on liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide in T1D, focusing on effects on body weight and insulin requirements, alongside hypoglycaemia, ketosis, diabetic ketoacidosis and gastrointestinal tolerability.

RESULTS: Early trials with liraglutide demonstrated reductions in body weight and insulin requirements but raised concerns regarding hypoglycaemia and ketosis. More recently, semaglutide and tirzepatide have renewed interest in incretin-based therapy in T1D, particularly among individuals with obesity. Their greater effects on weight and insulin requirements introduce a clinically important safety challenge: insulin must be reduced sufficiently to prevent hypoglycaemia while maintaining adequate insulinization to suppress lipolysis and ketogenesis. Gastrointestinal adverse events may further destabilize this balance through reduced carbohydrate intake and dehydration.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports a phenotype-directed approach centred primarily on adults with T1D and obesity, accompanied by careful patient selection, individualised insulin adjustment, glucose and ketone monitoring, and structured patient education. The clinical question has shifted from whether GLP-1-based therapies are effective in T1D to which patients are most likely to achieve a favourable benefit-risk balance and how these therapies can be used safely.

articles.title: Letter: Clarifying the Incremental Prognostic Value of the CALLY Index in Elderly Acute Coronary Syndrome.
Letter: Commentary on "CALLY May Refine Risk Prediction in Older Adults Acute Coronary Syndrome".
Management and Outcomes in Traumatic Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (tCVST) is a rare complication of head trauma associated with increased mortality. Unlike in non-traumatic CVST, there are no consensus guidelines to direct the management of tCVST. Anticoagulation is often used to prevent intracranial complications; however, concurrent traumatic brain injury (TBI) and other injuries complicate treatment decisions, and its clinical benefit remains uncertain. This study describes the epidemiology, management, and clinical and radiographic outcomes of tCVST.

METHODS: This is a retrospective single-center cohort study from a level 1 trauma center in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were identified from the Alfred Health Trauma Registry and hospital coding data between 1 January 2010 and 30 June 2024. Venous imaging was reviewed by two neuroradiologists to confirm tCVST diagnosis and thrombus characteristics. Primary outcomes were defined as discharge destination, with sinus recanalization on follow-up imaging as a secondary outcome.

RESULTS: tCVST was confirmed in 138 patients with an incidence of 0.9% in the TBI population and an all-cause inpatient mortality of 10.9% (15 patients). Anticoagulation was used in 78 patients (56.5%) and commenced a median of 5 days after diagnosis [interquartile range (IQR) 2-9]. Patients with anticoagulation generally had less severe traumatic injury, as measured by Injury Severity Score (ISS) and admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), but were more likely to have occlusive thrombosis. Among 123 patients who survived to hospital discharge, 93 underwent follow-up venous imaging from day 14, with complete recanalization in 57% by final available imaging. Occlusive thrombosis and multiple sinus involvement were associated with poorer recanalization, while no association between anticoagulation and recanalization was identified.

CONCLUSIONS: Traumatic CVST is a rare complication of head injury with multiple confounders influencing outcomes and uncertain optimal management. Clinical benefit of anticoagulation in this cohort requires further investigation.

articles.title: Interpreting Diabetic Retinal Outcomes After GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and Tirzepatide Initiation: Clinical Evidence and Its Limits.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Reports of diabetic retinopathy after potent glucose-lowering treatment create uncertainty for clinicians, particularly when studies measure different outcomes in patients with different baseline retinal disease. This review examines diabetic retinal outcomes after glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide initiation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This critical narrative review uses targeted, non-systematic study selection. It distinguishes disease onset or progression from detection, treatment use and subsequent visual function.

RESULTS: The SUSTAIN-6 retinopathy-complication signal remains clinically relevant; post hoc associations with early glycated haemoglobin reduction do not establish causal mediation. Contemporary cohorts report differing associations across baseline retinal strata, comparators and endpoints. Positive signals should be presented alongside their absolute event proportions and limitations, rather than dismissed because observational adjustment is imperfect. Conversely, non-significant results do not establish equivalence or class-wide safety.

CONCLUSIONS: Current guidance supports establishing retinal status and coordinating diabetes and eye care during treatment intensification. The implications differ between patients with recent screening and no known retinopathy, established non-proliferative disease, and active sight-threatening disease or recent retinal treatment. No universal safe rate of glycated haemoglobin decline or retinal-protective titration regimen has been established. Future studies should align eligibility and treatment initiation, distinguish incident disease from progression, and use scheduled retinal assessments. A comparison between two specific medicines can inform treatment choice but cannot exclude risks shared by both.

articles.title: A Comparative Analysis Between Original and Updated Glucose Management Indicator and Glycated Haemoglobin Across Continuous Glucose Monitoring Sensors in Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived glucose management indicator (GMI) is used for estimating glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c). This study assessed agreement between GMI-calculated using both original and updated (uGMI) models-and laboratory-measured HbA1c across Dexcom, MiniMed and Abbott sensors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Real-world data from adults with type 1 diabetes using automated insulin delivery were retrospectively analysed. Δ(GMI-HbA1c) and Δ(uGMI-HbA1c) were evaluated over 90 days preceding HbA1c (n = 383) and over 28 days preceding HbA1c (n = 375). Agreement was measured as directional difference, indicating GMI overestimation or underestimation of HbA1c, and absolute difference, indicating magnitude of agreement between GMI and HbA1c. Agreement was assessed across sensor groups using ANCOVA, adjusting for coefficient of variation and ethnicity.

RESULTS: Although mean directional differences were statistically significant for Δ(GMI-HbA1c) and Δ(uGMI-HbA1c) across all sensor groups (p < 0.001), differences were small and not clinically important, 90-day adjusted means (95% CI)-Δ(GMI-HbA1c): Dexcom 0.17% (0.09, 0.25), MiniMed -0.15% (-0.28, -0.02), Abbott -0.08% (-0.25, 0.09); Δ(uGMI-HbA1c): Dexcom 0.22% (0.14, 0.30), MiniMed -0.10% (-0.23, 0.02), Abbott -0.02% (-0.19, 0.15). Mean absolute difference did not significantly differ across sensor groups-Δ(GMI-HbA1c): 0.42%-0.51% (p = 0.353), Δ(uGMI-HbA1c): 0.41%-0.52% (p = 0.221).

CONCLUSIONS: GMI/uGMI performed consistently across sensor groups. Where clinically meaningful discrepancies between GMI/uGMI and HbA1c arise, these warrant interpretation within the context of individual clinical and laboratory factors rather than attribution to sensor manufacturer, reinforcing the need for personalised use of GMI alongside HbA1c.

articles.title: ASO Author Reflections: 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for Renal Cell Carcinoma Tumor Thrombus: Diagnostic Advances and Therapeutic Stratification.
Anticoagulation and All-Cause Mortality in Adults Aged 80 Years and Older with Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefits and risks of anticoagulation therapy in patients aged ≥ 80 years with atrial fibrillation (AF) remain underexplored, as this population is underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated mortality and bleeding outcomes associated with anticoagulation use in this population.

DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using MDClone, a synthetic electronic health record database from a large US health system, including 45,305 patients aged ≥ 80 years with AF after excluding those with mitral stenosis, mechanical heart valves, cirrhosis, or end-stage renal disease. Patients were categorized as continued, initiated, discontinued, or never anticoagulated. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, and 5 years; secondary outcomes were ischemic stroke, gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH). To address immortal time bias, the primary analysis used a time-varying Cox model, complemented by a 90-day landmark analysis and propensity score matching.

KEY RESULTS: Patients who continued anticoagulation had lower 1-year mortality than those never anticoagulated (8.7% vs 17.7%; p < 0.001). In the time-varying Cox model, anticoagulation was associated with a 25% lower hazard of mortality (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.71-0.79). Compared with continued anticoagulation, mortality was higher among patients who initiated (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.38-1.66), discontinued (HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.49-1.81), or never received anticoagulation (HR 2.22, 95% CI 2.05-2.41), and persisted after propensity score matching. At 5 years, mortality converged across groups. GIB was more frequent in anticoagulated patients (continued 13.0%, initiated 11.9%), whereas ICH rates were low and comparable across groups (1.3-1.6%, p = 0.129).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients aged ≥ 80 years with AF, anticoagulation therapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality despite an increase in gastrointestinal bleeding. These findings support continued anticoagulation in appropriately selected elderly patients, rather than withholding therapy on the basis of age alone.

articles.title: Effect of implant number on patient-reported outcomes in the edentulous maxilla: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated changes in patient-reported outcomes following implant-supported rehabilitation of the edentulous maxilla and their association with implant number.

METHODS: Five databases were searched through August 2026. Randomized controlled and prospective clinical studies including ≥ 10 patients and reporting patient-reported outcomes before and after treatment were eligible. Retrospective studies, studies without baseline PROM assessment, and studies involving mandibular or simultaneous maxillary and mandibular implant treatment were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, or MINORS, as appropriate. Hedges' g was analyzed using multi-level random-effects meta-analysis, with sensitivity analyses for OHIP- and VAS-based outcomes.

RESULTS: Eleven studies were included. Patient-reported outcomes improved across all implant groups. Pooled effects were largest for ≥6 implants (g = 2.34; 95% CI: 1.85-2.83), followed by four implants (g = 1.13; 95% CI: 0.53-1.73); only one effect-size estimate was available for two implants. Improvement was significantly greater with ≥6 than with four implants (difference in g = 1.22; 95% CI: 0.40-2.04; p = 0.003) and remained significant when restricted to removable prostheses. Fixed and removable prostheses supported by six implants did not differ significantly. VAS-based outcomes showed a more pronounced difference than OHIP-based outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Implant-supported rehabilitation substantially improves patient-reported outcomes in the edentulous maxilla. The greatest improvements were observed with ≥6 implants, with a significant advantage over four implants, although effect magnitude varied by PROM type. Evidence for two implants remains limited.

articles.title: UNICAL: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Learning with MRI-Derived Synthetic Amyloid PET for Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Limited availability of amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) motivates imaging-informatics methods that derive complementary molecular-imaging representations from routinely acquired magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We developed UNICAL, an uncertainty-aware multimodal framework for Alzheimer's disease-spectrum versus cognitively normal classification that combines a self-supervised three-dimensional MRI encoder, Contourlet Wavelet Stationary Radiomics (CoWS-Rad) engineered MRI features, and MRI-derived synthetic 18F-florbetapir (AV45) PET. CoCoLIT generated four stochastic PET realizations per MRI; their mean and voxelwise variance were used for uncertainty gating before probability-anchored transformer fusion. Synthetic PET was validated in 228 paired OASIS-3 MRI-AV45 examinations, achieving a mean per-examination voxelwise Pearson correlation of r = 0.864 and strong cortical-composite SUVR agreement with acquired PET (Pearson r = 0.954). In the OASIS-3 development cohort (813 sessions from 811 participants), participant-grouped five-fold cross-validation repeated across 20 seeds yielded AUROC 0.868 and expected calibration error (ECE) 0.061. The OASIS-3 development endpoint used the manuscript's AD-spectrum reference standard, whereas ADNI3 used AD-versus-CN research-group labels, providing cross-dataset evaluation on a related but non-identical prediction endpoint. Without retraining, feature refitting, threshold optimization, or recalibration, the frozen framework was evaluated in an independent matched ADNI3 cohort of 261 participants (87 AD, 174 CN), achieving AUROC 0.836 (95% CI 0.791-0.876). ECE increased to 0.089 under external transfer, indicating that calibration was more sensitive to domain shift than rank discrimination. Ablation analysis and K-sample sensitivity supported the contributions of uncertainty gating, adaptive weighting, modality dropout, residual correction, and the K = 4 synthesis configuration. UNICAL therefore provides an uncertainty-aware MRI-derived multimodal representation for AD-spectrum classification that retains substantial cross-dataset discrimination while remaining distinct from acquired molecular imaging and not replacing amyloid PET as a clinical biomarker.

articles.title: Correction: Does the combination of pulsed lavage and negative pressure dressings reduce infection rates after posterior spinal arthrodesis in pediatric scoliosis?
Cardiovascular Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Across Age Groups: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate whether cardiovascular effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) differ by age.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed and Embase were searched to 1 July 2026 for randomized placebo-controlled GLP-1RA trials in adults with type 2 diabetes or overweight/obesity reporting age-stratified major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke). Hazard ratios (HRs) for participants aged < 65 and ≥ 65 years were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Effect modification was assessed by pooling trial-specific ratios of HRs (RHRs) for ≥ 65 versus < 65 years. Where reported, effects were assessed across < 65, 65 to < 75 and ≥ 75 years.

RESULTS: Eight trials (SUSTAIN-6, EXSCEL, Harmony Outcomes, PIONEER 6, REWIND, AMPLITUDE-O, SELECT and SOUL) comprising 71 926 participants were included. GLP-1RAs reduced MACE at < 65 years and ≥ 65 years, with pooled HRs of 0.81 (95% CI 0.69-0.94; I2 = 64.1%) and 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.90; I2 = 0.0%), respectively. The pooled RHR showed no clear evidence of effect modification (1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25), although between-trial heterogeneity was high (I2 = 59.3%). Among trials reporting three age strata, RHRs showed no clear evidence of effect modification for 65 to < 75 or ≥ 75 years versus < 65 years, but data were available from only four trials, and the ≥ 75-year group was relatively small.

CONCLUSIONS: Across the included trial populations, GLP-1RAs lowered MACE in the age groups examined, with no clear evidence that relative cardiovascular effects differed by age.

articles.title: Latent Class Analysis Reveals Distinct Profiles Associated with Preeclampsia in Nulliparous Pregnancies.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a major cause of maternal illness and death, with poorly defined risk factors in nulliparous pregnancies. This study used latent class analysis to identify patterns of social, reproductive, health, and behavior factors associated with preeclampsia in 9809 nulliparous individuals who live in a large urban area in the Southeast US. Data were obtained from a perinatal administrative database (2011-2021). Latent indicators included maternal age, sociodemographic factors, foreign-born status, pregnancy intendedness, body mass index, mental and chronic health conditions, drug use, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Outcomes were gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia. Associations between latent classes and outcomes were examined with structural equation modeling. Of the pregnant patients, 49.1% were < 25 years old, 37.4% were foreign-born, 62.6% were married, 54.4% were on public insurance, 55.3% had unplanned pregnancies, 11.2% had mental health conditions, 5.4% had chronic health conditions, and 8.7% reported drug use. Three latent profiles emerged: Multidomain vulnerability (28%) included those more likely to be < 25 years of age with co-occurring social disadvantage, unplanned pregnancies, STIs, and drug use; social vulnerability (32%) included predominantly foreign-born patients with social disadvantage; health-behavior vulnerability (39%) included those with planned pregnancies and social advantage, but more health and behavior indicators relative to social vulnerability. Multidomain vulnerability (OR 2.0, 95% CI 1.67-2.46) and social vulnerability (OR 2.51, 95% CI 2.09-3.01) had higher odds of preeclampsia compared to the health-behavior vulnerability profile. Our latent class analysis revealed unique clustering of social, behavior, and health risk factors associated with preeclampsia among nulliparous pregnancies.

articles.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity.
articles.abstract: Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

articles.title: Environmental scan of Indigenous resources and culturally specific tools across intensive care units in Alberta, Canada.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Indigenous Peoples in Canada are disproportionately burdened with a spectrum of health issues and consistently report lower satisfaction with their health care; nevertheless, little is known about their experiences with critical care and the support received during critical illness. We aimed to describe the current scope of critical-care-specific resources available to Indigenous patients and their families across Alberta to identify gaps and opportunities to implement actionable change to realize more equitable and culturally safe care.

SOURCE: We conducted a two-phase environmental scan. Phase 1 entailed searching websites for information to support Indigenous patients, their families, and health care workers. Phase 2 facilitated 21 interviews with intensive care unit (ICU) stakeholders from across Alberta to further describe site-specific resources, services, tools, or initiatives to support Indigenous Peoples. Indigenous partners were engaged through all aspects of the project.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Our environmental scan identified a paucity of ICU-specific resources, programs, or policies to support Indigenous patients and families' navigation with critical care. We identified two national resources aimed at clinicians, rather than patients or families. Interviews with ICU stakeholders confirmed the paucity of Indigenous-specific resources. Stakeholders cited numerous barriers, including inadequate culture training, staff time constraints and burnout, physical space limits, and insufficient personnel, such as Indigenous liaisons and social workers.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple gaps exist in the availability of critical-care-focused resources and supports for Indigenous Peoples experiencing critical illness in Alberta, Canada. Addressing these care gaps may improve health equity, access, and the experience for Indigenous patients and families during critical illness and further build trust and strengthen relationships with health care workers.

articles.title: Single-cell insights into plant responses to biotic and abiotic stresses: cellular heterogeneity and regulatory mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Plants are continuously challenged by biotic and abiotic stresses that compromise growth, productivity, and stress resilience. Although bulk omics approaches have identified numerous stress-responsive pathways, they obscure the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization that underlie stress perception, signal transmission, and response execution. Single-cell and spatial omics now enable plant stress responses to be resolved at the levels of cell type, cell state, and spatial location. In this review, we synthesize recent applications of single-cell RNA sequencing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, spatial transcriptomics, and emerging single-cell proteomics in plant stress biology. We systematically compare biotic and abiotic stresses in terms of spatial response patterns, cellular division of labor, cell-state transitions, and gene regulatory networks. Biotic stress typically generates localized, infection-centered immune landscapes characterized by sentinel-cell activation, vascular defense hubs, and receptor-triggered transcriptional cascades. In contrast, abiotic stress more commonly involves organ-scale homeostatic adjustment, developmental plasticity, and sustained growth-tolerance trade-offs. Despite these distinctions, both stress classes share core regulatory modules, including reactive oxygen species, hormone signaling, transcription factor networks, and vascular long-distance communication. We further discuss technical challenges related to protoplast and nuclei preparation, cell-type annotation, spatial resolution, and multimodal data integration. By linking stress-responsive genes to the specific cell types, states, and spatial domains in which they function, single-cell approaches provide a mechanistic framework for precision engineering and breeding of stress-resilient crops.

articles.title: Next-Generation Bioinspired Microneedle Systems for Peptide Delivery: Bridging Design and Translational Medicine.
articles.abstract: Peptide-based therapies have transformed the management of chronic illnesses such as diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular problems, owing to their remarkable specificity, effectiveness, and low toxicity. Nonetheless, their therapeutic efficacy is frequently impeded by obstacles such as inadequate bioavailability, fast enzymatic breakdown, and restricted systemic stability. Conventional delivery strategies, such as oral and intravenous injection, have considerable constraints in efficiently transporting peptides to target locations. Transdermal drug delivery systems, especially microneedles (MNs) and bioinspired microneedles (BMNs), have garnered considerable interest as a less invasive and effective option to surmount these obstacles. MNs form microchannels in the epidermis and dermis, facilitating the direct administration of peptides into systemic circulation, hence dramatically improving peptide delivery across the skin. Recent improvements in BMNs technology have enhanced peptide delivery through better mechanical strength, skin contact, and controlled release. This paper mainly focuses on the importance of peptide drugs, the obstacles related to their administration, and the potential of BMNs for effective transdermal delivery. We emphasize current advancements in BMNs that improve peptide stability, permeability, and therapeutic effectiveness, facilitating their practical use in the treatment of chronic and acute disorders.

articles.title: Air pollution, road traffic noise, and greenness in relation to salivary cortisol in young adults.
articles.journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental exposures have been linked to stress, but evidence on their influence on its objective marker, salivary cortisol, in young adults is limited.

OBJECTIVE: We examined associations of environmental exposures with salivary cortisol levels.

METHODS: The study was conducted within the Swedish birth cohort BAMSE. Exposure to air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, Black Carbon, NOx), road traffic noise, and greenness (i.e. the average Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) within 100 m, 300 m and 500 m buffers) one year prior to clinical assessments was estimated at the individual residential address level using validated models. Salivary cortisol levels were measured at age 24 (n = 1148), and their associations with environmental exposures were estimated using linear regression, adjusted for covariates. Exploratory post hoc subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, tobacco use, body mass index, history of depression, asthma, rhinitis, and eczema.

RESULTS: In this cross-sectional analysis, no overall associations were observed between environmental exposures and salivary cortisol. However, exploratory post hoc subgroup analyses suggested sex- and season-specific differences. Among males, higher morning cortisol levels were observed in relation to exposure to PM10 (β = 0.058; 95% CI = 0.003, 0.112), NOx (β = 0.070; 95% CI = 0.017, 0.123), and noise (β = 0.120; 95% CI = 0.024, 0.215), while inverse associations were found with greenness (e.g. for NDVI 500 m β = -0.165; 95% CI = -0.263, -0.067). Similar findings were observed for evening cortisol. In contrast, females exhibited opposite trends.
