Despite their long-recognized association, the development of T. platydactyli in its most probable natural vector has remained largely unknown, and the interactions of both parasites during co-infection have not been investigated. Here, we experimentally infected laboratory-reared S. minuta by xenodiagnoses on naturally infected Tarentola mauritanica geckos carrying either single or mixed infections. Parasite species were distinguished using species-specific PCRs, and their localization, infection dynamics, and morphological development were examined by light microscopy and morphometric analyses. Leishmania tarentolae predominantly colonized the Malpighian tubules, whereas T. platydactyli exhibited a suprapylarian development, consistently colonizing the abdominal and thoracic midguts, and frequently reaching the cardia and the stomodeal valve. During development, T. platydactyli underwent a transition from epimastigotes to paramastigotes and trypomastigotes, with the latter becoming the predominant late-stage form that likely represents the transmissible stage. In contrast, L. tarentolae maintained the characteristic developmental pattern previously described for the subgenus Sauroleishmania, with short and long promastigotes predominating throughout development and metacyclic promastigotes appearing during late infections. Our findings provide the first comprehensive description of the development of T. platydactyli in S. minuta and demonstrate distinct tissue tropisms between the two trypanosomatids sharing the same vertebrate host and insect vector. These results support the hypothesis that long-term co-evolution has driven niche partitioning within the sand fly, allowing both parasites to coexist while potentially employing distinct transmission strategies.

articles.title: Insulin Dependence Erodes the Cardiac and Survival Advantage of Asymptomatic Status After Carotid Revascularization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent (IDDM) and non-insulin-dependent DM (NIDDM) with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid artery stenting (CAS), stratified by symptom status.

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed January 2005-January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. Endpoints were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) NIDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days there were 1,645 MIs, 2,051 ipsilateral strokes, 1,806 deaths, 3,626 strokes or deaths, and 5,029 MACE; at 1 year, 2,378, 2,924, 8,269, 10,750, and 12,646, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR 1.24), mortality (OR 1.19), and MACE (OR 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE OR 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P<0.001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR 1.54, P<0.001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR 1.05, P=0.41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR 1.19, P<0.001). Relative to CEA, TCAR and CAS were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR 2.10 and 1.93, respectively, P≤0.01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every endpoint.

CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival endpoints, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable to symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

articles.title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly amid conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI.

METHODS: We utilized the NIS (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. Our outcomes evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs. endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. Mann-Kendal trend tested monotonic temporal trends.

RESULTS: An estimated 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations were included (mean age 69.7 years, 40.0% women, 69.5% White). Overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with reversal and steady rise thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations included revascularization (n=14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n=16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization decreased (ptrend=0.016), while endovascular remained stable (ptrend=0.368), and hospitalizations without revascularization increased (ptrend=0.016) over time. Endovascular revascularization rates did rise among females, non-frail patients, and those presenting with rest pain (all ptrend>0.05). Overall, in-hospital amputation (n=6,270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n=1,086 [2.3%]) remained stable (ptrend>0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased most substantially among hospitalizations without revascularization (ptrend=0.007).

CONCLUSION: We provide contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. Relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings underscore the need for further investigation into optimal CLTI patient selection and coordinated integration of non-operative care, such as medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

articles.title: Physical activity and diabetic retinopathy in individuals with diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract: Physical activity is a cornerstone of diabetes management. Evidence regarding its association with diabetic retinopathy continues to evolve as more studies evaluate this relationship. This review examines the evidence on the association between physical activity and diabetic retinopathy among individuals with diabetes. CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from database inception to March 2026, supplemented by manual searches. Observational studies evaluating the association between physical activity and diabetic retinopathy among individuals with type 1 or type 2 diabetes were included. Random-effects meta-analyses and dose-response meta-analyses were performed to pool effect estimates. Thirty-two studies comprising 51,516 participants from 18 countries were included in this review. Higher physical activity was associated with a lower occurrence of diabetic retinopathy across all three designs: 0.59 (95% CI 0.47-0.74; 12 cross-sectional studies), 0.81 (0.71-0.93; 7 cohort studies), and 0.40 (0.22-0.72; 2 case-control studies). Subgroup analyses and crude-estimate sensitivity analyses showed a similar association. As diabetic retinopathy is prevalent, odds ratios overstate relative risk, so magnitudes are not comparable across designs. Dose-response meta-analysis was not significant. Higher physical activity levels are associated with a lower occurrence of diabetic retinopathy. However, we rated the certainty of evidence as low to very low. Well-designed prospective studies, ideally with standardised and objectively measured physical activity, are needed to establish whether this association is causal. Registration. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO. Registration number: CRD420261357943.

articles.title: Prognostic value of stress hyperglycemia ratio formulations, random plasma glucose, and fasting plasma glucose for early prediction of acute respiratory failure requiring intubation in patients with thrombolyzed acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic value of different stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) formulas for acute respiratory failure (ARF) after intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains unclear. We therefore compared four SHR formulas and examined their associations with ARF requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 345 patients with AIS treated with recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) at Saraburi Hospital between January 2015 and July 2022. Four SHR formulas (SHR1-SHR4) were derived from fasting plasma glucose (FPG), random plasma glucose (RPG), and HbA1c. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed discrimination, and multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations with ARF.

RESULTS: ARF occurred in 19.4% of patients. SHR1 (FPG/HbA1c) showed the highest discrimination (AuROC = 0.740; 95% CI, 0.673-0.807; optimal cutoff, ≥1.16) and a negative predictive value of 90.4%. SHR1 ≥ 1.16 was strongly associated with ARF (adjusted OR = 4.12; 95% CI, 1.99-8.53; p < 0.001) and improved model discrimination (ΔAuROC = 0.011) and reclassification (cfNRI = 0.559; IDI = 0.023).

CONCLUSIONS: SHR1 may provide incremental prognostic value for early identification of post-thrombolysis respiratory failure. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

articles.title: Psychosocial and symptom burden across metabolic populations managed in a digitally enabled metabolic care model: a real-world cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychosocial screening is growing in diabetes care, however, its role in broader metabolic populations remains unclear. This study aimed to describe patient-reported psychosocial outcomes and their associations with cardiometabolic characteristics in individuals managed through a digitally enabled hybrid care model.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included adults at Metabolic (United Arab Emirates) enrolled between September 2024 and December 2025. Patients were categorized into diabetic (DM), non-diabetic metabolic (NDM), and overweight-obesity focused (OB) cohorts. Scores for various psychosocial tools were recomputed from item-level responses, and biochemical measures were extracted from medical records. Associations were examined with multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 7,449 patients, 937 (12.6%) had DM, 5,594 (75.1%) had NDM, and 918 (12.3%) had OB. High risk for obstructive sleep apnea was present in 49.8% of DM, 27.7% of NDM, and 32.4% of OB patients. Depressive symptoms were reported similarly in DM (25.6%) and NDM (23.5%); anxiety symptoms were also comparable across groups. Diabetes distress affected 50.6% of DM patients. HbA1c correlated with PAID-5 distress, and BMI was associated with various psychosocial outcomes; discrimination was modest (AUC 0.55-0.67). Conclusion Depressive and anxiety symptoms were prevalent in both non-diabetic and those with diabetes, suggesting the need for structured screening beyond diabetes.

articles.title: Lactose, Lactose Maldigestion and Lactose Intolerance: Definitions, Misunderstandings, Mechanisms, and Public Health Implications.
articles.abstract: Lactose is the principal carbohydrate in milk, serving a critical role in infant energy metabolism as well as contributing to neurodevelopment, and the establishment of a healthy gut microbiota. Later in life, lactose digestion capacity varies widely across human populations owing to the genetically determined decline of intestinal lactase expression after weaning-a condition termed 'lactase non-persistence'. Approximately two-thirds of the global adult population exhibits reduced lactase activity, yet the clinical consequences of this enzymatic reduction are far less uniform than commonly assumed. This review provides a comprehensive examination of lactose functionality, the physiology of lactose digestion, and the consequences of lactase persistence and non-persistence. We present formal definitions for the spectrum of terms used in lactose research-including lactase persistence, lactase non-persistence, lactose maldigestion, and lactose intolerance-and argue that the critical distinction between lactose maldigestion (a physiological state) and lactose intolerance (a clinical syndrome) is frequently overlooked in both research and public health. Drawing on evidence from double-blind randomised controlled trials , microbiome intervention studies, and global epidemiological data, the evidence indicates that the majority of individuals with lactose maldigestion do not develop clinically meaningful symptoms at moderate intake levels of most dairy products. We further discuss the mechanism of colonic adaptation, whereby gradual lactose exposure selectively enriches Bifidobacterium populations capable of fermenting lactose without excessive gas production resulting in greater lactose tolerance. Finally, we examine the public health implications of these findings, noting that food-based dietary guidelines worldwide-including those in populations with high prevalence of lactase non-persistence-consistently recommend dairy consumption owing to its established associations with reduced risk of type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, and improved bone health.

articles.title: CERVICAL CANCER: NATIONAL CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES FROM THE FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, cervical cancer management has evolved substantially, with major changes in surgical approach, surgical radicality, nodal staging, imaging, radiotherapy techniques, brachytherapy and systemic treatments. To harmonize practice and integrate new evidence into clinically applicable recommendations, the French Cervical Cancer Guidelines Group developed national clinical practice guidelines for the management of patients with cervical cancer. The guideline process was conducted under the auspices of the French National College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and involved a multidisciplinary expert panel representing the French scientific societies involved in cervical cancer care. Clinical questions were formulated using the PICO framework and addressed the full continuum of care, including initial assessment, imaging, diagnostic conization, surgical nodal staging, treatment, fertility preservation, response assessment, follow-up, recurrence and specific clinical situations. Evidence was reviewed and critically appraised according to the GRADE methodology, and all recommendations were based on the 2018 FIGO staging system. External validation was performed through a two-round Delphi process involving 87 independent reviewers. Overall, 130 PICO questions generated 158 recommendations, including 35 strong and 52 weak recommendations, while no recommendation could be issued for 71 questions. Key practice-changing recommendations include the role of diagnostic conization in early-stage assessment, avoidance of minimally invasive hysterectomy from stage IB1 disease, risk-adapted surgical radicality, sentinel lymph node biopsy with ultrastaging, image-guided brachytherapy after chemoradiotherapy, and integration of PEMBROLIZUMAB in selected locally advanced or metastatic settings.

articles.title: Rodent models of post-stroke depression: A comparative analysis of photothrombosis and endothelin-1 models.
articles.abstract: Reliable, repeatable and clinically translatable animal models are required to uncover pathological mechanisms underlying post-stroke depression (PSD) and develop targeted therapeutics. Traditional ischemic stroke models are limited by high mortality and large, variable infarcts that confound affective assessment, while PSD clinically presents as secondary affective dysfunction occurring in stroke survivors after cerebral infarction. Therefore, ideal preclinical PSD models must achieve controllable focal brain lesions and recapitulate persistent depressive-like phenotypes. In recent years, photothrombosis (PT) and endothelin-1 (ET-1)-induced focal ischemia have become the most widely adopted rodent PSD paradigms, as they enable precise localized brain injury and recapitulate core behavioral and molecular characteristics of PSD. This review systematically compares PT and ET-1 models from multiple dimensions including surgical protocols, behavioral phenotypes, histopathological traits, and neurobiological mechanisms, and further summarizes standardized neurobehavioral and molecular detection assays. Direct comparative analysis reveals divergent strengths and drawbacks of the two models: the PT approach generates highly repeatable cortical infarcts and stable depressive-like behaviors but is limited to superficial brain tissues and lacks a well-defined ischemic penumbra; conversely, the ET-1 model allows stereotactic lesioning of subcortical nuclei, yet it yields inconsistent affective deficits and generally requires combined chronic stress to induce robust PSD-like phenotypes. Based on these findings, we propose two core principles for rational model selection: the primary determinant is whether the research focuses on cortical or subcortical neural circuits, and co-administration of chronic stress substantially improves the reliability and persistence of depressive phenotypes, although its necessity is contingent on species, strain, lesion site, and behavioral endpoint. Balancing lesion localization accuracy and behavioral stability during model choice will provide solid experimental support for subsequent PSD mechanistic research and preclinical drug screening.

articles.title: Licorice and fermented licorice extracts alleviate Mycoplasma gallisepticum infection through modulation of the DC-SIGN/Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is the principal etiological agent of chronic respiratory disease (CRD) in chickens, compromising poultry performance and causing substantial economic losses. Conventional antibiotic therapy is constrained by antimicrobial resistance and drug-residue concerns, creating an urgent need for safe, effective, and environmentally friendly alternatives. Here, we report the first systematic investigation of the molecular mechanism and translational potential of Licorice extract (Let) and its Fermented Licorice extract (FLet) in suppressing MG infection via modulation of the DC-SIGN/WNT signaling axis. In vitro, FLet exhibited stronger growth-inhibitory activity against MG than Let, while Let and FLet showed no detectable cytotoxicity toward HD11 cells within the tested concentration range of 0.02-4 mg/mL.In MG-infected HD11 cells, both Let and FLet reduced the expression of the MG adhesion-associated factor GapA and decreased MG genomic load. In parallel, Let and FLet modulated MG-induced inflammatory responses, as evidenced by decreased TNF-α and IL-1β and increased IL-4 and IL-10 levels, and alleviated MG-induced apoptosis by downregulating Caspase-3 and Bax while upregulating Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL. In vivo, licorice extract or fermented preparation improved body-weight gain and alleviated splenic lesions in MG-infected chickens, and reduced inflammatory and apoptosis-related markers in spleen. Therapeutic efficacy did not differ significantly from tiamulin (p > 0.05). Mechanistic analyses showed that Let and FLet treatment was associated with reduced DC-SIGN expression and changes in Wnt/β-catenin pathway-related molecules.. DC-SIGN knockdown reduced expression of β-catenin and c-Myc, supporting a regulatory role of DC-SIGN over WNT signaling. Collectively, Let and FLet reduced GapA expression and MG genomic load, attenuated cytokine dysregulation, and decreased apoptosis in HD11 cells. In MG-challenged chickens, Let and FLet improved body-weight gain and alleviated splenic lesions. For the evaluated outcomes, no significant differences were detected between the Let/FLet-treated groups and the tiamulin-treated group under the present experimental conditions. These effects were accompanied by reduced DC-SIGN expression and modulation of Wnt/β-catenin pathway-related molecules.

articles.title: Convergent Node, Divergent Failure: GPX4-SLC7A11-GSH Ferroptosis as a Unifying, Tissue-Decoded Axis of Diabetic Complications.
articles.journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Diabetic complications of the kidney, heart, retina, bone, β-cells, nervous system, vasculature, and reproductive organs have been studied as separate diseases. Iron-dependent phospholipid peroxidation may be a unifying upstream vulnerability rather than the dominant death morphology; we organized the evidence into five levels. Metabolic ignition (L1) loads the substrate via glucolipotoxic polyunsaturated-fatty-acid/ACSL4 priming and ferritinophagic iron release. These pressures act on the central defense network (L2): glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), SLC7A11/xCT, and glutathione (GSH). Gain-of-function restoration attenuates diabetic injury, and loss-of-function evidence is correlative. We do not call this GPX4-dependent network rate-limiting; graded manipulation of endogenous GPX4 has not been performed in diabetic tissues. Glutathione-independent arms act in parallel but differ in status, GCH1-BH4 appears depleted, FSP1 uncharacterized, and DHODH unestablished and contested. Diabetes disables this node through transcriptional, post-translational, epigenetic, non-coding-RNA, and organelle-specific routes (L3) rather than one lesion. Each tissue decodes the same failure into a distinct organ program (L4) set by its architecture and functional demands, and shared regulators may act oppositely across compartments. Extracellular-vesicle and gut-organ axes couple these programs (L5a), but the insulin-resistance relationship is directionally unresolved: AMPK-NRF2-GPX4 evidence is limited and pharmacological, and glutathione peroxidase loss can itself improve insulin sensitivity. Translation (L5b) returns the same target: reduced GPX4 and SLC7A11 with elevated ACSL4 recurs across complications and is associated with severity. Evidence is predominantly preclinical, and human data are almost entirely observational. The framework is hypothesis-generating rather than clinically actionable, and the null-to-unfavorable record of global antioxidant and NRF2-directed trials indicates that interventions must be cell- and context-resolved.

articles.title: Molecular Subtypes in Acute Respiratory Illness and Sepsis.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Sepsis and acute respiratory illness are clinical syndromes that encompass profound biological heterogeneity. The resulting heterogeneity of treatment effect is now widely understood as the explanation to why immunomodulatory trials in critical care have not me their study endpoints, thereby misclassifying effective therapies as futile while concealing harm in biologically ineligible subgroups. High-dimensional molecular profiling offers a route to resolve this heterogeneity into tractable subgroups or subtypes. Here we review molecular subtypes across adult and paediatric sepsis, pneumonia, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), spanning transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic platforms. Blood transcriptomic frameworks derived independently in multiple countries, and subsequently harmonized by international consensus efforts, converge on recurring immune archetypes: a myeloid inflammatory state dominated by neutrophil activation; a mixed myeloid and lymphoid dysregulated state carrying the highest mortality; and a relatively immunocompetent state with preserved lymphocyte function and the most favourable clinical trajectory. Plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling recapitulate this architecture at orthogonal molecular layers, arguing that these archetypes are platform-independent rather than artefacts of any single technology. Cross-syndrome convergence is asymmetric, which plausibly reflects the methodological differences between top-down latent class analysis in ARDS and bottom-up unsupervised clustering in sepsis. Secondary analyses of randomized controlled trials consistently show subtype-dependent responses to treatment strategies, with a coherent directionality with potential benefit in hyperinflammatory states, and harm in immunosuppressed or adaptive immune-prevalent states. Subtype membership is not static; trajectory, not baseline assignment, most strongly encodes prognosis. Realising precision critical care now requires prospective, subtype-stratified trials of which none has yet been completed.

articles.title: [Diagnosis and Treatment of COPD: A Guideline for Respiratory Specialists 2026].
authors: der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Pneumologie und Beatmungsmedizin e.V. (DGP) (federführende Fachgesellschaft) und
Deutsche Gesellschaft für Arbeitsmedizin und Umweltmedizin e.V. (DGAUM)
Deutsche Gesellschaft für Allergologie und klinische Immunologie e.V. (DGAKI)
Bundesverband der Pneumologie, Schlaf- und Beatmungsmedizin e.V. (BdP)
Deutsche Interdisziplinäre Gesellschaft für Außerklinische Beatmung und Intensivversorgung e.V. (DIGAB)
Deutsche Röntgengesellschaft, Gesellschaft für medizinische Radiologie und bildgeführte Therapie e.V. (DRG)
articles.abstract: This S2k guideline updates the recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) by respiratory specialists and complements the German National Disease Management Guideline (NVL) with specialist recommendations for diagnosis and treatment. The guideline is based on current scientific evidence and a structured interdisciplinary S2k consensus process involving numerous scientific societies. Major updates include recognition of COPD as a heterogeneous disease, with expanded recommendations on its etiopathogenesis, early detection, and contemporary diagnostic approaches, including biomarkers, thoracic computed tomography, and lung cancer screening, as well as updated risk stratification. Recommendations on smoking cessation, non-pharmacological management, and pharmacological treatment have been comprehensively revised. These include consistent use of dual bronchodilation, earlier implementation of inhaled triple therapy in appropriate patients, and consideration of emerging treatment options, including biologics. Additional updates address the management of comorbidities, interventional treatment of advanced emphysema, and inpatient management of acute COPD exacerbations. The guideline aims to support individualized, phenotype-oriented, and evidence-based care for patients with COPD.

articles.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.

METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.

FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.

INTERPRETATION: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings.

FUNDING: The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

articles.title: Observational study for perioperative intensive care unit (OPICU): Planned and unplanned ICU admissions, follow-up, discharge, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Due to limited resources, identifying high-risk surgical patients who derive clinical benefit from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission is essential. Our primary aim was to characterize resource allocation and evaluate the true clinical benefit of ICU admissions using modified Wang criteria. Secondary aim is to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission; validate clinical scoring systems; and compare inter-group outcomes, including Clavien-Dindo complication rates, lengths of stay, and mortality.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study was conducted across 75 ICUs. Adult inpatient surgery cases were categorized into four groups: planned admission (PAG), unplanned admission (UPAG), planned but not admitted (PBNAG), and emergent admission (EAG). Data included preoperative/intraoperative/postoperative(ICU) variables, modified Wang criteria, and mortality rates (ICU, hospital, 30/90-day).

RESULTS: Of 55,963 preoperatively evaluated patients, 2764 (4.9%) were planned for ICU admission; 804/2764 patients could not be admitted because of limited ICU beds, remaining of 1960 patients with a planned ICU admission, 411/1960 did not require postoperative ICU care forming the PBNAG (14.8% of 2764). Overall, 1980 patients (3.09% of all cases) were admitted to the ICU (78.2% PAG, 12.5% EAG, 9.1% UPAG). POSSUM scores effectively differentiated PBNAG (lower) and EAG (higher) from PAG. ICU benefit indicators (e.g., vasopressor need, prolonged ventilation >12 h, arrest events) were significantly higher in UPAG and EAG versus PAG (p < 0.001). Emergency surgery (OR 12.4), intraoperative complications (OR 3.1), and ASA >2 (OR 2.7) independently increased UPAG risk, whereas minimally invasive surgery and regional anesthesia reduced ICU admissions. Overall ICU and 90-day mortality rates were 5.9% and 7.5%, respectively, peaking in the EAG group (18.1% and 18.9%).

CONCLUSION: Integrating modified Wang criteria, POSSUM scores, intraoperative complications, emergency status, and ASA class >2 is effective in predicting the necessity of ICU admission.

articles.title: Budget Impact Analysis and Alternative Funding Solutions of Sacubitril/Valsartan for the Treatment of Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction in Thailand.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the budget impact of sacubitril/valsartan for treating heart failure with reduced ejection fraction compared with enalapril and assessed alternative funding mechanisms under decision uncertainty.

METHODS: The study comprised 3 components. First, a decision tree and a Markov model were used to estimate the budget impact over a 5-year time horizon. The base-case adopted a payer perspective, including direct medical costs, whereas a scenario analysis incorporated direct non-medical and indirect costs. Second, a situation analysis identified key decision uncertainties. Third, an economic impact analysis evaluated alternative funding mechanisms relative to the current reimbursement system.

RESULTS: In the base-case, the cumulative net budget impact was United States dollars (USD) 18.40 million. For the scenario analysis, the net economic impact decreased to USD 15.72 million, indicating a partial offset of the additional drug expenditure. The new treatment mix was estimated to avoid 300 heart failure hospitalizations and 146 cardiovascular deaths over 5 years. Key uncertainties included high budget requirements, limited epidemiological data, and variability in clinical outcomes. To address these, 2 funding mechanisms were explored: coverage with evidence development to reduce clinical uncertainty and a price-volume agreement with a capped budget to manage financial risk.

CONCLUSION: Sacubitril/valsartan increased total expenditure compared with the current treatment; however, savings from reduced hospitalizations and broader societal costs partially offset the additional drug cost. Sacubitril/valsartan may be a manageable option when implemented with coverage with evidence development and price-volume agreements, supporting financial sustainability and long-term health outcomes.

articles.title: Mid-pregnancy plasma environmental chemical exposures and maternal blood pressure in a pilot study of Black women.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence suggests Black women experience disproportionate exposure to environmental chemicals and diagnoses of hypertension during pregnancy. We characterized environmental chemicals and determined their associations with blood pressure in a cross-sectional analysis of Black women in Philadelphia. We measured 32 plasma chemicals using non-targeted analysis in samples collected between the 16th and 24th weeks of gestation in the MOMENTUM cohort (n = 68). We assessed the association between log2-transformed chemical abundance and blood pressure, as well as preterm hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), using regression analysis. We categorized chemical abundances into tertiles and modelled them as ordinal variables; blood pressure as a continuous variable; and preterm HDP as a binary variable. We assessed the mixture effect with a Weight Quantile Sum regression constraint in the positive direction. Each increase in one tertile of 4-methylbenzophenone (β = 4.48 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.84, 7.12), 4-tert-Butylcatechol (β = 3.83 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.53, 6.14), benzophenone (β = 4.05 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.49, 6.61), carvone (β = 3.50 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.19, 5.81), and tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (β = 3.98 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.23, 6.74) was cross-sectionally associated with a statistically significant increase in diastolic blood pressure. A mixture of flavoring and fragrance agents also showed a positive association with diastolic blood pressure (β = 3.05 mmHg; 95%CI: 0.60, 4.67). Exposures were not significantly associated with systolic blood pressure and preterm HDP. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require replication in large-scale cohort studies.

articles.title: Predicting university students' intention to apply investment strategies: Integrating theory of planned behavior and self-determination theory.
articles.abstract: Behavioral intention is central to investment-related decision making, but belief-based predictors and motivational need satisfaction should not be conflated. This quantitative cross-sectional study examined 512 undergraduate students in Jiangxi Province, China, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and Self-Determination Theory (SDT). Multiple regression tested attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control as predictors of intention to apply investment strategies; descriptive statistics and correlations separately characterised autonomy, competence, and relatedness. The TPB model explained 55.2% of the variance in intention. All three TPB predictors were statistically significant, with perceived behavioral control having the largest unstandardized coefficient (B = 0.36, p < .001). The SDT constructs had moderately high means and positive intercorrelations (r = 0.68-0.73), describing a motivational profile rather than a tested contribution to intention. The two-item subjective norm measure showed modest reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.584), requiring caution in interpreting its coefficient. Demographic characteristics were available for 310 respondents because institutional permissions differed, limiting assessment of the representativeness of the full analytical sample. No SDT-to-intention paths or incremental effects beyond TPB were estimated; thus, the proposed TPB-SDT integration is theoretical and interpretive, not a statistically validated joint model. The study contributes a transparent distinction between proximal TPB predictors and complementary SDT-related motivational experiences in university investment learning, while identifying the need for future joint predictive and longitudinal tests.

articles.title: Posttraumatic growth in nursing home workers: differential associations of gratitude, meaning in life, and distress four years after the pandemic.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE/AIMS: To examine associations between posttraumatic growth, gratitude, meaning in life, and psychological distress among nursing home workers several years after the COVID-19 pandemic.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 251 nursing home workers in Madrid, Spain, who had worked during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants completed the Posttraumatic Growth Inventory-Short Form, the Purpose in Life Test-10, the Gratitude Questionnaire-6, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-4. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression models were performed.

RESULTS: Posttraumatic growth was present across the sample several years after the pandemic, although spiritual change showed lower scores than other growth dimensions. Gratitude and meaning in life were both positively associated with posttraumatic growth at the bivariate level. In adjusted models, gratitude remained significantly associated with all posttraumatic growth dimensions, whereas meaning in life did not retain independent associations. Psychological distress was also positively associated with posttraumatic growth, indicating that growth-related appraisals and distress coexisted in this sample. No significant differences in posttraumatic growth were observed across professional roles.

CONCLUSION/IMPLICATIONS: This study contributes to the limited literature on nursing home workers by showing that posttraumatic growth remained present several years after the COVID-19 pandemic and was more closely associated with gratitude than with meaning in life in adjusted models. For research, the findings support a more differentiated view of positive post-adversity processes and their coexistence with distress. For geriatric nursing and long-term care, they underscore the value of considering not only emotional burden but also positive psychological appraisals when addressing staff well-being after major collective adversity.

articles.title: Prediction model development in older patients with cancer: Practical guidance and key vigilance points.
Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy.

STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: The Burden of Depressive Symptoms Associated With Gun Violence Exposure in the US Relative to Other Conditions.
articles.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
articles.abstract: PurposeWe compare the burden of depressive symptoms associated with gun violence exposure (GVE) to the burden of other conditions experienced by the US adult population to display the magnitude of opportunity to reduce emotional distress by reducing GVE.Design, Setting, and SampleSurvey representative of the US adult population.MeasuresRespondent reports of cumulative frequency of gun violence exposure and PHQ-9 depressive symptom scores.AnalysisWe estimate the excess PHQ-9 points associated with GVE and convert them into disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) using disability weights from the Global Burden of Disease study. We then compare these DALYs to DALYs attributed to selected conditions that burden the US population.ResultsWe estimated that the excess PHQ-9 points associated with GVE represent 3.15 million DALYs. This burden was approximately one-third that of ischemic heart disease and was slightly less than the burden of Alzheimer's disease, chronic kidney disease, and lung cancer. It was almost twice the burden of colon cancer, firearm deaths, and breast cancer. When combined, the burden of fatal firearm injury together with the burden of depressive symptoms associated with GVE would only be less than the burdens of ischemic heart disease, drug use disorders, falls, and diabetes mellitus.ConclusionImplementing interventions that reduce the burden of GVE might have a significant impact on both individual and community well-being.

articles.title: Development and application of the latex-safe risk assessment framework for workplace environments: Institutional risk mapping and mitigation strategies.
articles.journal: The International journal of risk & safety in medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundHealthcare personnel continue to be at risk of exposure to airborne latex proteins despite widespread adoption of powder-free glove alternatives. A standardized risk assessment framework that maps areas with the highest potential for latex allergen exposure is lacking.ObjectivesThis study develops and applies an initial Latex-Safe Risk Assessment framework (LSRA) for institutional latex-risk mapping in a tertiary hospital setting and guides targeted mitigation strategies.MethodsRisk Priority Number (RPN) based on latex allergy severity, likelihood, and detection was used to estimate risk in seven clinical departments. Environmental conditions, product inventory, ventilation systems, and administrative controls were evaluated using a standardized checklist.ResultsThe operating theater was classified as very high risk (RPN 125; 100%). The labor room (RPN 80; 64%), intensive care units, and emergency department (RPN 60 each; 48%) were classified as moderate risk. Ward 3 and Ward 8 (RPN 30 each; 24%) were classified as low risk, whereas the O&G clinic (RPN 15; 12%) was classified as very low risk. Key gaps involved inadequate segregation and substitution of latex products, limited designation of 'latex-safe' zones, and insufficient engineering controls.ConclusionsThe framework facilitated the prioritization of high-risk areas and alignment of interventions with identified exposure pathways.

articles.title: Effects of acetaminophen ingestion on the torque-duration relationship and fatigability during intermittent exercise in patients with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effects of acute ingestion of acetaminophen (ACT) on the magnitude of exercise-induced peripheral fatigue (ΔPtw) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D). In a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind design, 22 males (11 T1D and 11 control (CTR) completed 60 maximum voluntary contractions 60 min after ingesting 1 g of acetaminophen (ACT) or 1 g of placebo (PL) on two separate visits. Central and peripheral fatigue were assessed from pre- to post-exercise changes in quadriceps voluntary activation (ΔVA) and potentiated twitch force (ΔPtw), respectively. Critical torque (CT) was defined as the mean force produced during the final 12 contractions, and work performed (W') was computed as the impulse performed above CT. Maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), VA and Ptw decreased after exercise in both groups, with no significant difference between PL and ACT condition. Compared to PL, ACT increased root mean square/Mmax and CT values in the T1D (+21% and 8% respectively) and CTR groups (+40% and +19%; respectively), with significant lower effect in the T1D compared to the CTR group (P < 0.05). No significant effect of ACT was observed for W' in the T1D (+7%) and CTR groups (+4%) (P = 0.68). These findings indicate that acute ACT ingestion increased CT and muscle activation during the repeated-MVC protocol in both groups, although the magnitude of these responses was smaller in the T1D than the CTR group.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains suboptimal. Wrist-worn wearables may support fully remote or hybrid CR through activity monitoring and individualized feedback, but the effectiveness and consistency of benefits remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs initiated during phase II or III CR in patients with CVD.

METHODS: A total of 8 databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2015, through August 7, 2026. Eligible trials enrolled adults with CVD and integrated a wrist-worn wearable into fully remote or hybrid CR. Studies focused primarily on heart failure or using wearables only for outcome measurement were excluded. Primary outcomes were peak oxygen consumption (VO2), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), and daily steps. Random-effects meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs), except for quality of life, which used standardized MDs. Between-study variance was estimated using the DerSimonian-Laird method, pooled-effect CIs used the Knapp-Hartung adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa parametric bootstrap method. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses explored study and intervention characteristics.

RESULTS: A total of 18 trials involving 1993 randomized participants, reported in 20 publications, were included; 17 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled estimates favored wearable-guided CR for peak VO2 (10 studies; 591 participants; MD 1.69, 95% CI 0.46-2.92, 95% PI -2.21 to 5.39 mL/kg/min), 6MWD (9 studies; 1094 participants; MD 31.03, 95% CI 7.66-53.92, 95% PI -62.11 to 123.18 m), and daily steps (8 studies; 474 participants; MD 1062.8, 95% CI 383.5-1825.0, 95% PI -503.0 to 2860.0 steps/day). All 3 PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future comparable settings. No clear pooled effects were observed for anaerobic threshold, BMI, waist circumference, grip strength, or quality of life. Subgroup differences were not statistically significant. In univariable meta-regression, a higher proportion of female participants was associated with greater peak VO2 improvement, although this aggregate-level finding was exploratory.

CONCLUSIONS: Wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs may improve average exercise capacity and physical activity in patients with CVD. However, PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future settings. These programs may extend activity monitoring, individualized feedback, and behavioral support beyond center-based CR, but their multicomponent nature prevents attributing effects to wearables alone. Larger, rigorously designed trials with standardized protocols and outcomes should identify the patients and program components most likely to benefit. Future research should also evaluate long-term adherence, safety, equity, and implementation within routine multidisciplinary CR across diverse health systems.

articles.title: Ultra-Processed Foods Consumption and the Risk of nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Korean Adults.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Nutrition Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite the global burden of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), its associations with ultra-processed food (UPF) consumption in Asian populations remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the association between total and subgroup-specific UPF consumption and NAFLD risk and its related biomarkers among Korean adults.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 11,168 participants in the 2016-2019 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Diet was assessed using 24-h recall, and UPF was defined by NOVA classification. NAFLD was defined by a comprehensive NAFLD score ≥ 40. Multivariable-adjusted logistic regression and linear regression models were used to examine associations with NAFLD risk and cardiometabolic and liver-related biomarkers, respectively.

RESULTS: There was a positive trend in the association between UPF intake and odds of NAFLD (Multivariable-adjusted Odds Ratio [MVOR]quintile 5 vs 1 = 1.28, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.56; p-trend <0.001). Higher UPF intake was also significantly associated with greater adiposity (all p-trend ≤0.03), dysregulated cardiometabolic profiles, including higher LDL-c, hemoglobin, and non-HDL-c (all p-trend ≤0.04), and elevated hepatic injury markers, including ALT or ALT/AST ratio (all p-trend ≤0.03). Among UPF subgroups, processed meat and fish showed a significant positive association with NAFLD (MVOR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07). Similarly, lower odds of NAFLD were observed in association with a 100 g/day substitution of processed meat and fish with unprocessed or minimally processed alternatives (MVOR: 0.89, 95% CI: 0.80-0.98).

CONCLUSION: In our study, higher UPF intake was associated with greater odds of NAFLD. Larger cohort studies are warranted to replicate our findings.

articles.title: The Integrated Virulence Network of Colletotrichum scovillei: Effector-Signaling Coordination in an Emerging Anthracnose Pathogen.
articles.abstract: Colletotrichum scovillei is an important and geographically expanding anthracnose pathogen of pepper (Capsicum spp.) that causes serious pre- and post-harvest losses. This hemibiotrophic fungus employs a multilayered infection strategy, yet an integrated framework connecting its molecular mechanisms to disease development has been lacking. This review synthesizes current evidence to propose an integrated virulence network for C. scovillei. Conserved intracellular signaling pathways, including mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), cyclic AMP (cAMP), calcium/calcineurin, cell-wall integrity, and small-GTPase modules, regulate key morphological transitions. Available genetic studies also connect selected regulators to host-defense suppression, while comparative genomic analyses identify strain-level differences in predicted secreted proteins and candidate virulence-associated regions. However, the identities, host targets, and stage-specific deployment of most C. scovillei effectors remain unresolved. We therefore distinguish direct evidence from the C. scovillei-pepper system from mechanisms inferred from other Colletotrichum species and position biotrophy, extended quiescence, ripening-associated reactivation, and necrotrophy within a testable framework. We further examine pepper resistance and management limitations and identify experiments needed to translate this framework into durable control strategies.

articles.title: An anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide augments whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock in a rodent polytrauma model.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe trauma induces a cytokine storm that is associated with impaired resuscitation and recovery. We investigated the impact of AQB-565, an anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide, as a novel treatment adjunct for whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock using a rat polytrauma shock model.

METHODS: Hemorrhagic shock with polytrauma was induced in 64 Sprague-Dawley rats. The rats were randomized to receive one of four intravenous treatments at 15 minutes posthemorrhage (T15): saline control, AQB-565, tranexamic acid (TXA), or combined AQB-565+ TXA. The rats were given autologous transfusion of shed whole blood at 60 minutes and as needed thereafter to achieve mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 60 mm Hg for up to 3 hours. Survival, hemodynamics, cytokine profiles, and hemorrhage volumes were compared between groups.

RESULTS: There was a significant overall effect of treatment group on MAP (two-way rmANOVA p=0.02) that coincided with blood transfusion. MAP was significantly increased at T105 with AQB-565+TXA versus saline control (p=0.046). Inflammatory plasma cytokines, including interleukin-6, were significantly decreased with AQB-565 versus control groups (ANOVA p values ≤0.01). Seventeen (26.6%) rats died before 3 hours. There was a trend towards increased survival for treatments containing AQB-565 versus controls that was not statistically significant (Kaplan-Meier log rank p=0.06).

CONCLUSIONS: A melanocortin pathway-activating polypeptide suppressed inflammation and improved hemodynamic response to whole blood transfusion in this hemorrhagic shock model.

articles.title: Purrble Use Among LGBTQ+ Young People With Self-Harm Experiences: Findings From a Qualitative Process Evaluation of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Difficulties with emotion regulation (ER) have widely been associated with the development and persistence of poor mental health, such as depression, anxiety, self-harmful thoughts, behaviors, and suicide attempts. Despite the importance of ER as a transdiagnostic risk factor, few interventions directly target ER. The impact of one such intervention, Purrble (a socially assistive robot; developed by Sproutel and Committee for Children), was recently evaluated when compared to treatment-as-usual (TAU) within a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with sexual orientation and gender identity minorities, that is, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, or questioning (LGBTQ+) youth, who had self-harm experiences. However, while RCTs are well suited to evaluating effectiveness, they offer limited insight into how participants engage with, integrate, and perceive the value of interventions, like Purrble, in their everyday lives. Consequently, complementary qualitative process evaluation is needed to fully understand participants' experiences and contextualize trial outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore and understand the engagement with and integration of the Purrble intervention using process evaluation interviews, considering its perceived influence on ER, mental health, and self-harm experiences.

METHODS: Following their participation in the Purrble RCT, 40 LGBTQ+ young people (16-25 years) with current self-harm ideation took part in this qualitative process evaluation using semistructured online interviews. Interviews explored participant expectations of the RCT and Purrble; engagement and appropriation of Purrble; and perceived impact on mental health and self-harm. Thematic analysis was used to develop a thematic framework.

RESULTS: Four overarching themes were developed from the data. The first theme describes how participants used Purrble to ground themselves and manage distress, with participants suggesting de-escalation of their self-harm thoughts or behaviors. The second theme captures how Purrble was perceived as a companion or source of comfort, supporting self-soothing and self-care. The third theme highlights the role of accessibility and proximity, how the availability and location of Purrble during moments of distress influenced its perceived usefulness. The final theme examines circumstances in which participants chose not to engage with Purrble, offering insights into barriers to use and individual differences in engagement.

CONCLUSIONS: This process evaluation helps to contextualize how Purrble could be a helpful intervention for those LGBTQ+ young people with experience of self-harm thoughts and behaviors. This evaluation also clarifies when Purrble may not be helpful. These qualitative findings offer important contextual insights alongside the quantitative results of the related RCT.

articles.title: Posterior Inter-Antral Linear Ablation Using Pulsed Field Energy: Electrophysiological Validation and Early Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Durable conduction block across the left atrial roof remains challenging because of complex anatomy and limitations of thermal energy delivery. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) may enable a short posterior inter-antral line as an adjunctive strategy beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), providing linear conduction block at a more inferior posterior LA location than a conventional roofline. However, its electrophysiological characteristics and clinical relevance remain uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center, nonrandomized comparative cohort study, a prospectively enrolled cohort undergoing PVI plus posterior inter-antral linear ablation was compared with contemporaneous patients undergoing PVI without additional left atrial ablation. The primary clinical endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Propensity score matching was the primary comparative analysis; inverse probability of treatment weighting and multivariable Cox regression were sensitivity analyses. Among 306 patients, 65 underwent posterior inter-antral linear ablation and 241 underwent PVI alone. Posterior-line ablation produced characteristic reciprocal pacing responses and a caudal-to-cranial posterior wall activation pattern consistent with conduction block. During a median follow-up of 198 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 4 of 65 (6.2%) versus 38 of 241 (15.8%) patients. In the primary PSM analysis, posterior inter-antral linear ablation was associated with lower recurrence (HR 0.23; 95% CI 0.07-0.78), with consistent results in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Posterior inter-antral linear ablation using PFA provides a reproducible electrophysiological pattern of conduction block and was associated with lower short-term atrial arrhythmia recurrence than PVI alone in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. These findings warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

articles.title: KCNH1 variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders exhibit prominent gain of function.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic variants in KCNH1, encoding the human ether-á-go-go voltage-gated potassium channel (EAG1, KV10.1), are associated with the neurodevelopmental disorders Temple-Baraitser syndrome (TBS), Zimmermann-Laband syndrome (ZLS), epileptic encephalopathy, and other undefined neurodevelopmental disorders. Investigating the functional consequences of KCNH1 variants can provide information about molecular and cellular pathophysiological mechanisms and help guide therapeutic directions. In this study, we determined the functional properties of 26 disease-associated KCNH1 variants including three recurrent and six that were previously unpublished. Findings were compared to the wildtype (WT) channel along with six rare population variants. Our approach used automated patch clamp recording of heterologously expressed KCNH1 variants in both the homozygous state (variant alone) and the clinically-relevant heterozygous state (variant co-expressed with WT channels). We also examined the impact of alternative splice isoforms on functional consequences of specific variants. We demonstrated that the majority of disease-associated KCNH1 variants exhibit features consistent with gain-of-function including hyperpolarized voltage-dependence of activation, accelerated activation kinetics, or both that promote hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential. By contrast, one unique variant discovered previously in an autism cohort had a depolarized voltage-dependence of activation and was associated with a depolarized resting potential in cells. Pharmacological testing of KCNH1 variants demonstrated differences in potency for channel block by imipramine and an investigational non-selective potassium channel blocker (LY97241) for specific variants. Collectively, our findings support gain-of-function as the most common, albeit not exclusive, molecular mechanism underlying KCNH1-related disorders and suggest opportunities for potential therapeutic drug repurposing strategies for these conditions.

articles.title: Pregnancy Outcomes and Long-Term Kidney Function in Women with Primary Glomerulonephritis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether pregnancy accelerates long-term kidney function decline in women with primary glomerulonephritis remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate maternal and fetal outcomes and the long-term course of kidney function in women with primary glomerulonephritis.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study analyzed 40 pregnancies in 31 women with biopsy-proven primary glomerulonephritis (1996-2022). A control group of nulliparous women with primary glomerulonephritis, matched for subtype, age at diagnosis, and disease duration, was included. Obstetric and neonatal outcomes were evaluated alongside longitudinal kidney parameters assessed before, during, and up to 60 months postpartum.

RESULTS: Common diagnoses were focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (32.3%) and IgA nephropathy (25.8%). Mean maternal age was 29.6±4.1 years. Preeclampsia occurred in 15% and preterm birth in 50% of pregnancies (mean birth weight: 2819±859 g). During pregnancy, serum creatinine decreased and eGFR increased (p<0.001). Postpartum, serum creatinine returned to baseline, showing no significant differences at 6, 12, or 60 months. Although eGFR at 60 months was lower than pre-pregnancy levels, serum creatinine remained comparable to baseline and no significant differences in kidney function parameters were observed between the pregnancy and control groups at 60 months. The clinical significance of the isolated reduction in calculated eGFR therefore remains uncertain.

CONCLUSIONS: In women with primary glomerulonephritis and predominantly early-stage kidney disease, physiological kidney adaptation during pregnancy is largely preserved. No clear acceleration in long-term kidney function decline was observed compared with matched controls; however, an adverse effect of pregnancy cannot be excluded. Preeclampsia and preterm delivery remain significant, requiring monitoring.

articles.title: Complexity of patients with hypertension cared for by clinical pharmacist practitioners in the Veterans Health Administration.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Clinical pharmacist practitioners (CPPs) are well suited to manage complex patients, such as those with hypertension. However, there is limited information about the complexity of patients managed by CPPs with respect to chronic disease. This study compared the clinical complexity of patients with hypertension managed by CPPs to that of patients managed by other providers.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, patients with hypertension at 19 Veterans Health Administration (VA) sites during fiscal years 2024 to 2025 were classified by CPP visits into those with more than one visit ("ongoing CPP care"), those with one visit ("consultative CPP care"), and those with no visits ("no CPP care"). Patient complexity was assessed using 7 hypertension-related measures indicating need for more management time and resources. Logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, race, and marital status were generated to analyze differences between the groups.

RESULTS: Compared to patients in the group with no CPP care, patients with ongoing CPP care had significantly higher complexity as measured by hypertension medication use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.70), other medications associated with hypertension (aOR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.26-2.18), hypertension complications (aOR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.29-1.98), and medication nonadherence (aOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.06-1.75). Similar findings were noted for patients with consultative CPP care vs those with no CPP care. A composite complexity score of all 7 measures indicated that patients with ongoing (aOR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.54-2.32) and consultative (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.57-2.24) CPP care were significantly more complex than patients with no CPP care.

CONCLUSION: CPPs manage patients with hypertension who are more complex than those managed by other VA providers. These findings underscore the importance of CPPs in improving patient outcomes through comprehensive medication management.

articles.title: Heart failure beyond cardiology: a primary care perspective on the 2026 ESC guideline.
Polymer-specific nanoplastic exposure, mitochondrial dysfunction, and depressed ejection fraction in humans.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly found in humans, but cardiac and energetic effects are unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In older adults without major comorbidities, blood levels of PS/PE were quantified, and left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) was measured by transthoracic echocardiography. To investigate polymer-specific cardiotoxic mechanisms, human AC16 cardiomyocytes were exposed to PS- or PE-nanoplastics. Mitochondrial function was assessed using Seahorse XF analysis, and molecular remodeling was characterized using transcriptomics and label-free quantitative proteomics.In humans, circulating PS and PE levels were each associated with EF in univariable analyses. PS and PE concentrations were higher in participants with EF <50% than in those with EF ≥50% (PE p=0.021; PS p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment for anthropometric and metabolic determinants of systolic function, PS remained independently associated with EF. In vitro, both polymers accumulated intracellularly and elicited mitochondrial stress. Chronic PS exposure induced a loss of respiratory capacity and bioenergetic reserve, with suppression of basal and maximal respiration and markedly reduced spare respiratory capacity. PE exposure produced a distinct remodeling pattern characterized by reduced maximal respiration, but increased ATP-linked respiration and tighter respiratory coupling, consistent with a compensatory state of reduced metabolic flexibility. Transcriptomic profiling revealed polymer-specific transcriptional phenotypes, with PE driving broader repression of cardiomyocyte structural, electrophysiological, and mitochondrial gene programs, whereas PS triggered a more restricted but coherent response. Proteomic profiling further identified a mitochondria-centered injury signature involving disruption of mitochondrial protein import and cristae organization, impairment of oxidative metabolism, altered redox buffering, and incomplete activation of mitochondrial quality-control pathways.

CONCLUSIONS: Nanoplastic exposure is associated with left ventricular systolic function in humans and induces polymer-specific cardiomyocyte remodeling in vitro. PS is strongly linked to systolic impairment, consistent with a mitochondria-centered cardiotoxic phenotype. These findings identify nanoplastics as a previously unrecognized environmental determinant of myocardial vulnerability and support polymer-specific risk stratification.

articles.title: Home CHF feasibility trial protocol: Impact of at-home Subcutaneous furosemide in patients with Chronic Kidney Disease and Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Hospital admissions are common in patients with heart failure (HF), particularly in those with concomitant chronic kidney disease (HF-CKD). Hospitalisation is often driven by fluid overload, requiring intravenous furosemide. Subcutaneous furosemide is emerging as an alternative which may facilitate at-home treatment. This study will assess the feasibility of conducting a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate whether subcutaneous furosemide can reduce hospital admissions in people with HF-CKD.

METHODS: Stage one - Recruitment and monitoring of at-risk patients: We aim to recruit 200 people with HF-CKD with at least one hospital admission within the preceding year. These participants will be monitored for signs of fluid accumulation. Stage two - Treatment: The second stage will run contemporaneously to the first stage. The first 80 participants to develop fluid accumulation will be randomised to usual care (attend hospital and receive standard treatment) or at-home furosemide. The participants allocated to home treatment will administer SQIN-furosemide via a patch infusor device, 80 mg daily for five days, then be reviewed in a final clinic appointment. These participants will monitor their weight and observations daily, as well as receive a check-in call from the research team. Potassium levels will be checked twice over five days. The primary outcome of this feasibility study will be recruitment and retention of participants, as well as adherence to the intervention.

DISCUSSION: Findings from this feasibility trial will inform the planning of a definitive RCT to evaluate whether subcutaneous furosemide can reduce hospital admissions in people living with HF-CKD.

articles.title: Multifunctional Three-Dimensional-Printed Bio-Ink from Waterborne Polyurethane and Natural Antioxidants for Advanced Wound Dressings.
articles.abstract: The development of multifunctional wound dressings capable of simultaneously addressing oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and tissue regeneration remains a major challenge in advanced wound care. Here, we report a printable, bioactive 3D-printed dressing based on a synergistic bio-ink composed of waterborne polyurethane (WPU), pomegranate peel-derived antioxidant polyphenols (POM), and TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils (TOCNF). POM was incorporated into the WPU matrix during in situ polymerization to introduce pomegranate peel-derived antioxidant and antibacterial functionality, while TOCNF served as a rheology modifier enabling extrusion-based direct ink writing. The resulting ink exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behavior, rapid viscosity recovery, and tunable yield stress, enabling successful, stable extrusion-based printing of multilayer architectures. Printed freeze-dried wound dressings exhibited highly interconnected porous structures (>90% porosity), robust swelling capacity, structural integrity under physiological conditions, and compressive stability after hydration. The incorporation of POM enhanced antibacterial performance against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli and provided strong free-radical scavenging activity. In vitro studies using HaCaT keratinocytes confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, enhanced metabolic activity, and significant attenuation of H2O2-induced oxidative stress. Notably, this wound dressing reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and improved cell survival under oxidative challenge. This work establishes a strategy for integrating natural antioxidant bioactives into printable polyurethane networks to produce structurally programmable, biologically active wound dressings. The combination of rheologically optimized printability, hierarchical porosity, and multifunctional bioactivity highlights the potential of this platform for advanced wound-dressing applications and other oxidative-stress-related tissue-repair strategies.

articles.title: Giant Stroke, Thermally Powered Twisted LCE Yarn Actuators Driven by Reversible Twist-Coil Transition.
articles.abstract: Actuation performance in fiber-based artificial muscles is commonly improved by introducing sufficient twist to produce fully coiled structures. Here, we present a new strategy to achieve large-stroke actuation in twisted-only liquid crystal elastomer (TLCE) yarn muscles through a thermally triggered, reversible twist-to-coil transition. Continuous, high-strength, and scalable LCE fibers were fabricated using direct ink printing. These fibers were then integrated with carbon nanotube yarns to fabricate electrothermal hybrid TLCE muscles. Above a critical twist density, the hybrid muscles electrothermally transform into coiled or plectoneme configurations, delivering a maximum quasi-static contractile stroke of up to 86%, a fast response time of 1.8 s, and stable cyclic operation over 10 000 cycles. The stroke enhancement originates from the reversible twist-to-coil transition, which is driven by a pronounced thermal reduction in both fiber length and Young's modulus, thereby lowering the critical torque needed for coiling. This mechanism introduces a new actuation mode for fiber-based artificial muscles and shows promising potential for confined-space manipulation, robotic grippers, and adaptive smart structures.

articles.title: Separating Fragmentation from Clearance in Location-Based Shock Wave Lithotripsy Outcomes.
Fulminant non-autoimmune diabetes presenting as fatal diabetic ketoacidosis in a 2-month-old infant with genetically confirmed Wolcott-Rallison syndrome.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (WRS) is a rare autosomal recessive monogenic disorder caused by mutations in the EIF2AK3 gene. Characterized by permanent early-onset non-autoimmune diabetes and multisystem dysfunction, it should be strongly suspected in infants presenting under 6 months of age, particularly in consanguineous families.

METHODS: A 2-month-old female infant presented to the emergency department with severe respiratory distress, persistent vomiting and dehydration, initially having been evaluated for infantile colic.
