Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group.

CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.

articles.title: Heat stroke presenting with choreiform dyskinesias: an unusual MRI pattern.
The role of tyrosine kinase inhibitors as a post-hematopoietic stem cell transplant continuation therapy for pediatric acute leukemia: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Relapse following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is a leading cause of transplant failure for pediatric acute leukemia patients, emphasizing the need for an effective post-transplant continuation therapy. This systematic review evaluates the role of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) as a post-HSCT continuation therapy in pediatric acute leukemia.

METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, Cochrane, Web of Science, and VHL was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Original studies were included if they were relevant to the research question and fit the eligibility criteria.

RESULTS: The initial search identified 765 articles, with 16 studies included after filtration. TKIs were indicated for patients with chromosomal alterations causing constitutively active kinase signaling. Common agents included imatinib, dasatinib, ponatinib, sorafenib, and gilteritinib, and selection was based on disease status and molecular profiling. Duration of continuation ranged from 10 months to 3 years, with dosage dependent on the agent and tolerability. TKIs were generally well-tolerated, with reported side effects including cytopenia, liver dysfunction, and skin conditions. Across the included studies, MRD negativity and sustained molecular remission were reported in selected patients receiving post-HSCT TKI continuation therapy, while relapse was also reported after treatment discontinuation or in resistant disease. However, optimal duration and long-term safety remain unclear in the pediatric population.

CONCLUSION: TKIs can serve as a targeted post-HSCT continuation therapy in select pediatric acute leukemia patients, particularly those with high-risk, mutation-driven disease. Molecular profiling and MRD monitoring are central to guiding agent selection, timing, and mutation-directed therapy adjustments. These findings support individualized TKI treatment to reduce relapse risk following HSCT, while highlighting the need for prospective studies to define standardized treatment strategies.

articles.title: An immediate reperfusion sign might increase the likelihood of favourable outcomes in patients with intracranial atherosclerotic disease-related stroke who received stent-retriever-based thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTS: To investigate the relationship between the presence of an "immediate reperfusion sign (IRS)" during retrievable stent-based thrombectomy and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel-occluded acute ischaemic stroke related to intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) treated with stent retrievers.

METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated. Univariate analysis and partial correlation analysis were also performed.

RESULTS: Eighty-two ICAD-LVO patients were identified from 421 endovascularly treated AIS patients from 2015 to 2024. Fifty-four of them were ultimately included in the analysis, and an IRS was observed in 41 of these patients (75.9%). Favourable outcomes were significantly more frequent in the IRS (+) group (51.2% versus 7.7%, p=0.005). The sensitivity of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes was 95.5% (21/22), the specificity was 37.5% (12/32), the positive predictive value was 51.2% (21/41), and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.3% (12/13). Additionally, the presence of an IRS, as well as age, baseline NIHSS score and successful final reperfusion, was significantly different between the favourable and unfavourable groups. Partial correlation analysis revealed a moderate correlation (r=0.412; p=0.002) between the comprehensive reperfusion score (in which the presence of an IRS and successful final reperfusion was counted as 1 point) and favourable outcomes.

CONCLUSION: In our respective cohort of patients, the presence of an IRS during stent-retriever-based thrombectomy appeared to indicate a higher rate of first-pass-effect and a 3-month favourable outcome in acute LVO stroke patients with ICAD.

articles.title: The role of the CYP1A1 gene in long-term glucocorticoid-related adverse effects.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: CYP1A1 gene variants may influence the development of AE of chronic GC treatment. The rs1799814 polymorphism was associated with increased BMI and lower levels of bone turnover markers, independent of GC dose, suggesting reduced GC metabolism. No association was found with OP and/or Fx, BMD or TBS values.

INTRODUCTION: Long-term glucocorticoid (GC) use can produce adverse effects (AE) including obesity, diabetes, osteoporosis and fractures. The variability in AE severity suggests a genetic influence. CYP1A1, a cytochrome P450 family enzyme involved in GC metabolism, may play a role. This study aimed to genotype CYP1A1 variants in patients on chronic GC treatment and analyse their relationship with long-term AE.

METHODS: Seventy patients (56 ± 16.6 years; 71.4% female; 47.1% postmenopausal) receiving chronic GC treatment ( ≥5 mg/ day for >3 months) were included. Clinical data were collected at baseline and at 5 years of follow-up, including OP risk factors, previous and incidental fractures, GC dose and duration, disease activity, anthropometric data, bone metabolism parameters, bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular bone score (TBS) (by DXA), and vertebral fractures (X-ray). CYP1A1 gene sequencing was performed by NGS using Amplicon Deep Sequencing on an Ion Torrent platform.

RESULTS: Four CYP1A1 polymorphisms were identified: rs41279188, rs1048943, rs1799814 and rs4646422. Nine patients had rs1048943, nine rs1799814, one rs4646422 and one rs41279188 polymorphisms, respectively. Patients with the rs1799814 polymorphism (13%) had higher BMI (29.3 vs. 25.5; p = 0.019) and greater BMI change over 5 years (ΔBMI: 1.7 vs. -0.32; p = 0.02; adjusted for cumulative GC dose). Additionally, they presented lower bone turnover markers (NTx: 21 vs. 40 nMol/mMol, p = 0.003, CTx: 0.16 vs. 0.29 ng/mL, p = 0.068, OC: 16.6 vs. 19.3 ng/mL, p = 0.059). No associations were found between CYP1A1 polymorphisms and the presence of osteoporosis and/or fractures, BMD or TBS values.

CONCLUSION: The CYP1A1 rs1799814 polymorphism is associated with more severe GC-related AE, suggesting reduced GC metabolism.

articles.title: Virtual reality surgical simulator training of residents and early-career surgeons for pedicle screw placement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of Virtual reality (VR) simulation training compared with traditional teaching methods for residents and early-career surgeons training in pedicle screw insertion.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing VR simulator training with traditional training approaches for pedicle screw placement in residents and early-career surgeons were included. A random-effects model was applied to pool outcomes, with treatment effects expressed as mean differences or risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: A total of six RCTs were included, with 54 trainees and 457 screws inserted in each study group. Pooled analyses demonstrated that residents and early-career surgeons trained with VR simulation achieved a significantly higher rate of optimal (Grade I) pedicle screw placement than those receiving conventional training (RR 1.36; 95% CI 1.15 to 1.61). Conversely, VR training was associated with significantly lower rates of Grade II (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.85), Grade III (RR 0.07; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.30), and Grade IV screw placements (RR 0.16; 95% CI 0.03 to 0.90), indicating consistent reductions across all severities of cortical breach. Overall procedural success was significantly higher in the VR group (RR 1.17; 95% CI 1.04 to 1.32). Furthermore, VR-trained residents and early-career surgeons demonstrated shorter screw penetration distances and fewer displaced screws per resident.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that VR simulation training significantly enhances accuracy and safety-related outcomes in resident and early-career surgeons' pedicle screw placement training.

articles.title: [Three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping in the electrophysiology lab: when, how and why? : A practical introduction for early-career electrophysiologists].
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional electroanatomic mapping has become an integral part of modern invasive electrophysiology. It combines catheter localization, patient-specific cardiac anatomy, local electrograms, activation timing, voltage information, and ablation lesion documentation within a spatial working model. For early-career electrophysiologists, however, the interpretation of these maps can be challenging. This review provides a practical introduction to three-dimensional (3D) mapping for young electrophysiologists during their first steps in the electrophysiology laboratory. It addresses when 3D mapping is useful or necessary, how a map is created, what information can be derived from different map types, and which pitfalls should be avoided. The article summarizes technical principles and clinical applications of 3D electroanatomic mapping based on current expert consensus documents, review articles, and practical electrophysiological concepts. 3D mapping is particularly valuable in atrial fibrillation ablation, atypical atrial tachycardias, ventricular tachycardias, redo procedures, congenital or postsurgical anatomy, and low-fluoroscopy workflows. Activation maps help visualize the temporal sequence of electrical propagation, whereas voltage maps provide information on scar, low-voltage areas, and potential arrhythmogenic substrate. The quality of a map depends on stable rhythm, reliable temporal and spatial references, catheter contact, signal quality, adequate point density, and correct annotation. 3D mapping is a powerful tool for navigation, mechanism analysis, substrate characterization, and ablation documentation. Nevertheless, it does not replace electrophysiological reasoning. Every map must be interpreted critically and validated using intracardiac electrograms, surface ECG, anatomy, pacing maneuvers, and defined procedural endpoints.

articles.title: Biologic therapy in type 2 CRSwNP: from immunopathology to clinical management.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disorder in which type 2 (T2) inflammation represents the predominant endotype, characterized by eosinophilic infiltration and activation of IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 pathways. Patients with T2-CRSwNP frequently present with asthma, NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease, and a high risk of recurrence. Conventional management based on intranasal or systemic corticosteroids and endoscopic sinus surgery may relieve symptoms but often fails to achieve sustained disease control in patients with persistent T2 inflammation.

PURPOSE: This review summarizes the immunopathology and risk stratification of T2-CRSwNP and discusses current evidence and practical considerations for biologic therapy within a structured clinical decision framework.

CONCLUSIONS: Biologic therapies targeting IL-4Rα, IL-5/IL-5R, IgE, and TSLP have demonstrated efficacy in reducing polyp burden, improving symptoms, and decreasing systemic corticosteroid exposure. However, in the absence of robust head-to-head comparisons, optimal patient selection and defining sustainable long-term maintenance strategies remain clinical challenges. Integrating inflammatory profiles, disease burden, and structured follow-up may support individualized treatment and sustained disease control.

articles.title: Clinical Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Children with Single Ventricle Congenital Heart Disease: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) on pediatric patients with single ventricle (SV) heart disease, using invasive and non-invasive markers of cardiac function. We reviewed patients (< 21 years) with SV physiology who received ≥ 90 days SGLT2i at our center from 2020 to 2025. Baseline laboratory, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic data were recorded and compared to follow up data after ≥ 90 days on SGLT2i. Hospitalizations before and after SGLT2i were also analyzed. Seventy-seven patients with median age 10.5 years (range 47 days-19.9 years) had median treatment duration of 386 days (IQR 218-853). Among 62 patients (81%) with echocardiographic data (Fontan [39], Glenn [18], Stage 1 [5]) there was a significant decrease in median qualitative AVVR score from mild-moderate to mild (p = 0.01). Median BNP decreased from 84 pg/mL (IQR 18-274) to 42 pg/mL (IQR 18-105) (p = 0.02) and mean hemoglobin increased from 14.4 ± 2.5 g/dL to 15.5 ± 2.4 g/dL (p < 0.01). Ten patients had hemodynamic data without significant change in mean pulmonary artery pressure from 17 to 16 mmHg (p = 0.168) or ventricular end-diastolic pressure from 10 to 11 mmHg (p = 0.275). More patients had > 1 hospitalizations for heart failure during the 6-months prior to SGLT2i compared to the 6-months following initiation, with an odds ratio of 4.5 (95% CI: 1.6-13.7, p < 0.01). Overall, we identified significant reductions in AVVR, BNP, and hospitalizations for heart failure after ≥ 90 days of therapy. Further larger scale studies are needed to determine if SGLT2i will affect clinical outcomes in the pediatric SV population.

articles.title: Improving Efficiency in the Inpatient Echocardiography Laboratory: A Quality Improvement Project.
articles.abstract: Pediatric echocardiograms are performed daily on inpatient hospital units. Understanding the precise study indication from ordering providers is critical for completing imaging. Given the daily volume of echocardiograms, timely completion of imaging is important for maintaining efficiency and productivity. This study sought to identify areas to improve efficiency using quality improvement methodologies. SMART aim was to decrease the total echo completion time by 10% within 6 months. Fishbone diagram identified ordering system limitations and inadequate ordering provider knowledge as areas for improvement. Primary process and outcome metrics included total echo completion time, pre-echocardiogram buffer time, and specificity in order documentation. PDSA 1 implemented electronic order updates for increased specificity with a picklist of common reasons for inpatient echocardiograms. PDSA 2 implemented an ordering alert for STAT studies to reduce the number of inappropriate orders. PDSA 3 implemented additional order updates and staff education. Total echo completion time decreased each cycle for total 34% reduction. The pre-echocardiogram buffer time similarly decreased 59%. The documentation of pertinent clinical history increased by 15% and maintained at 99% appropriate documentation for the final two PDSA cycles. Pre and post intervention surveys indicated an overall improvement in the ordering process for both the inpatient ordering providers and echocardiography laboratory staff. Echocardiography laboratory efficiency improved throughout the course of this project without identified negative effects on ordering providers or echocardiography staff. Our project demonstrates the ability to affect clinically relevant improvements utilizing simple workflow process changes in the pediatric echocardiography laboratory.

articles.title: Closing the neurology-psychiatry gap in tardive dyskinesia care in Asia: expert recommendations for an educational roadmap to improve prevention, recognition, and shared care.
articles.abstract: Tardive dyskinesia (TD) remains an under-recognised medication safety issue in many Asian countries, compounded by fragmented care between psychiatry and neurology and underpinned by a lack of cross-discipline professional education. The multidisciplinary expert recommendations proposed here have been developed jointly by a panel of psychiatrists and neurologists representing selected Asian healthcare settings (Thailand, Japan, Korea and China), and suggest a practical, structured education and competency framework to help close this gap and improve multidisciplinary management. The recommendations emphasise the need for collaborative educational initiatives focused on rational antipsychotic prescribing, proactive monitoring, standardised assessment and diagnosis, patient and caregiver education, and timely specialist referral. The proposed joint neurology-psychiatry educational framework is informed by real-world expert perspectives and spans undergraduate education, residency training, and continuing medical education, encompassing interdisciplinary curricula, collaborative workshops, with locally adapted multilingual resources. It is suggested that implementation of such a framework should be supported by national professional societies and development of shared-care pathways, with key outcomes monitored. Strengthening cross-disciplinary knowledge, skills, and attitudes in this way may improve TD detection, reduce avoidable progression, and promote coordinated, patient-centred care in selected Asian regions.

articles.title: Protein-losing enteropathy as a rare presentation of small bowel T-cell post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease.
articles.abstract: Posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorders (PTLD) represent a heterogeneous group of lymphoproliferative lesions in patients who have solid organ or bone marrow transplantation. While majority of PTLD are of B-cell origin, T-cell PTLD is extremely rare. Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma (MEITL) is a rare primary intestinal lymphoma which most commonly involves the small bowel. Since the symptoms at presentation are often vague, the diagnosis is frequently delayed until acute complications such as intestinal perforation or obstruction occur. Here we report a very rare case of posttransplant small bowel MEITL in a kidney transplant recipient presenting with protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) as the initial manifestation. Our patient initially presented with episodic diarrhea but early investigations failed to identify any bowel pathology. Subsequently she developed hypoalbuminemia-related fluid retention and Tc-99 m HSA scintigraphy confirmed the presence of PLE. Even though the upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy and abdominal computed tomography did not show any significant lesions, the patient developed sudden bowel perforation and histologic examination of the resected tissue confirmed the diagnosis of posttransplant MEITL. She developed severe sepsis postoperatively and finally passed away despite aggressive supportive treatment. Our case shows that early diagnosis and prompt treatment is critical to potentially improve the patient outcomes.

articles.title: Epidemiological insights from 11 years of active tuberculosis surveillance (2010-2020) and 6 years of voluntary latent tuberculosis infection surveillance (2015-2020) in Nunavut. A retrospective descriptive study.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of public health = Revue canadienne de sante publique
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis disease (TB) remains the leading infectious killer globally. Although Canada has a low overall TB incidence rate, it remains a significant public health concern in Nunavut territory, where the 2024 incidence rate was 87.5 per 100,000-14 times the national average. This disparity is exacerbated by limited healthcare access, the remoteness of Nunavut communities, and overcrowded living conditions. This study examines the epidemiology of TB and tuberculosis infection (TBI) in Nunavut and its communities using local data.

METHOD: We analysed Nunavut surveillance data of TB cases from 2010 to 2020 to understand incidence rates at the territorial level and stratified by region, community, sex, and age. Treatment outcomes were also described. TBI program data from 2015 to 2020 were supplemented with community-wide screening (CWS) records. Descriptive statistics summarized key characteristics and proportions, while the modelling approach tested whether territorial TB incidence followed a dynamic temporal pattern rather than remaining constant, using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs).

RESULT: A total of 731 TB cases were reported from 2010 to 2020, along with 1538 TBI notifications between 2015 and 2020. Six communities accounted for 84% of all TB cases, mostly located in the Qikiqtani region. The majority of TB cases (61%) occurred in males and predominantly affected individuals aged 15 to 45 years (56%). Overall, 93% of TB cases were successfully treated. TBI treatment completion rates improved over time, rising from 69% in 2015 to 81% in 2020. Since 2018, over 60% of patients opted for shortened 12-week, once-weekly isoniazid-rifapentine regimen (3HP), likely contributing to improved completion. The models identified fluctuations in TB incidence during the study period, showing a non-linear relationship in both quarterly and monthly trends, with evidence of a significant seasonal (intra-annual cyclical) pattern throughout the year.

CONCLUSION: Nunavut had the highest TB incidence rate in Canada between 2010 and 2020, with most cases in Qikiqtani region and among young males. TB treatment success was high, and TBI treatment completion improved, especially after introducing the shorter 3HP regimen. These insights highlight the need for region- and community-specific interventions to control TB effectively.

articles.title: Post-breast cancer diagnosis screening mammography among First Nations and non-First Nations women in Ontario : A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of public health = Revue canadienne de sante publique
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: First Nations women in Canada have historically experienced lower breast cancer screening participation and worse outcomes than non-First Nations women. While most research has focused on pre-diagnosis screening, less is known about follow-up care. This study examined post-diagnosis mammography use among First Nations and non-First Nations women in Ontario and identified factors associated with follow-up screening among First Nations women.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 190 First Nations and 506 non-First Nations women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer between 1995 and 2004, with follow-up screening data available through 2019. Descriptive statistics compared demographic, clinical, and treatment characteristics. Logistic regression models were used among First Nations women to identify factors associated with follow-up screening.

RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed in the unadjusted comparisons of post-treatment screening rates, frequency, timing, and intervals between First Nations and non-First Nations women. Among First Nations women, older age (OR = 0.42; 95% CI, 0.19-0.94), rural residence (OR = 0.35; 95% CI, 0.17-0.73), and lower income (OR = 0.20; 95% CI, 0.06-0.69) were among the factors associated with reduced screening. Radiotherapy (OR = 7.48; 95% CI, 3.38-16.56) and less severe surgery (OR = 7.19; 95% CI, 3.31-15.63) were associated with higher odds of screening.

CONCLUSION: While screening rates among First Nations women are improving, disparities persist. Strengthening continuity of care, primary care access, and culturally safe survivorship support is essential to achieving equity.

articles.title: Knowledge of Childhood Autism and Care Experiences in Critical Settings: A Survey Among Italian Nurses.
articles.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study examined nurses' knowledge of childhood autism and their experiences caring for autistic patients in emergency and critical care. The Knowledge about Childhood Autism among Health Workers (KCAHW) questionnaire is child-focused, whereas the care-experience questions were age-neutral.

METHODS: From May to July 2025, 503 nurses and nurse coordinators recruited by non-probability convenience sampling completed an online survey with socio-demographic items, the 19-item KCAHW, and study-specific closed- and open-ended questions. Non-parametric group comparisons reported effect sizes with bootstrap confidence intervals. Open-text responses underwent content analysis.

RESULTS: Using the original scoring key, the mean KCAHW score was 15.96/19 (SD = 2.54); at least 80% scored a point on 16 items, but only 39.8% recognized atypical eating patterns. Differences by sex, age, professional experience, educational level, geographic area, and clinical setting were mostly small, the largest being between clinical settings (ε² = 0.133-0.195). Care experiences told a different story: 74.0% reported difficulties in caring for autistic people, 90.9% felt not at all or not very prepared, and 91.1% had never attended ASD-specific training. The most frequent difficulty was communication and relational problems (58.6% of 266 answers). A crisis had been managed by 56.3%; of 133 accounts, 58.6% involved caregivers or the team and 15.8% medication, sedation, or restraint. Only 54.7%-55.7% routinely chose a quiet setting, avoided noise, or adapted lighting.

CONCLUSION: Participants recognized much of the KCAHW's childhood-autism content, but this did not translate into perceived preparedness. Practice-oriented education is needed, together with tools that assess professional competence across the lifespan.

articles.title: Association of Blood Heavy Metal Concentrations with Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in a Consecutive Single-Center Cardiac Catheterization Cohort.
articles.abstract: Environmental heavy metal exposure is increasingly recognized as a potentially important but underappreciated contributor to cardiovascular disease, yet its relationship to directly observed coronary artery disease (CAD) remains poorly defined. In this single-center cohort of 52 consecutive adults undergoing cardiac catheterization at an urban Chicago tertiary care center, we paired elemental exposure profiles with direct angiographic assessment in a racially diverse, socioeconomically vulnerable population. While no individual metal independently explained obstructive CAD, circulating metal exposure patterns were more revealing: Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression demonstrated that increasing overall metal burden was associated with worse coronary phenotypes, suggesting that environmental exposures may act collectively rather than in isolation. Lead and mercury emerged as the strongest contributors and were enriched relative to National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) reference populations. Taken together, these findings offer early but meaningful evidence that environmental toxicant burden may represent an underrecognized layer of cardiovascular risk, particularly in urban communities where industrial history, aging infrastructure, and socioeconomic disadvantage intersect. This work highlights the importance of viewing cardiovascular disease not only through the lens of traditional risk factors, but also through the environments in which patients live.

articles.title: Closed percutaneous reduction versus mini-open sinus tarsi approach for fixation of displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superiority of minimally invasive surgical approaches for displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures (DIACF) remains debated. This review aimed to compare surgical outcomes between two approaches: closed percutaneous reduction (PR) and mini-open sinus tarsi approach (STA).

METHODS: A systematic search identified studies comparing PR vs. STA for acute traumatic DIACFs. Complication rates, operative parameters, functional and radiological outcomes were extracted and analysed.

RESULTS: 837 patients were included from eight eligible studies, with Sanders type II and III fractures. PR demonstrated a 53% risk reduction in overall complication rate vs. STA (RR 0.47, 95% CI [0.27-0.83], p = 0.009), including wound complications. AOFAS scores marginally favoured PR vs. STA (MD 0.82 points, p = 0.034), with this difference having doubtful clinical relevance. Radiological parameters were comparable, although calcaneal width remained wider with PR. PR was also associated with shorter times to surgery, length of stays and intra-operative times, although with high heterogeneity in the pooled outcome estimates.

CONCLUSION: PR demonstrates lower complication rates with comparable functional and radiological outcomes vs. STA in fixation of less complex DIACFs, and may be an acceptable fixation strategy for these fracture patterns over STA.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Identifying Parenting Strategies to Support Young People with Trauma-Related Anxiety and Depression: A Delphi Consensus Study.
articles.abstract: Trauma exposure is common in young people and is associated with anxiety, depression, and other mental health difficulties. Parents play an important role in supporting their child's recovery following a potentially traumatic event, yet evidence-based guidance for trauma-informed parenting remains limited. This study used a Delphi methodology to establish expert consensus on parenting strategies for young people aged 5-18 years experiencing anxiety and depressive symptoms following a traumatic event. A panel of 38 predominantly Australian clinicians and researchers with expertise in trauma, youth mental health, and parenting rated 166 candidate strategies across three survey rounds for their importance in supporting young people's post-trauma mental health. Ninety-four strategies (56.6%) achieved expert consensus, defined as endorsement by 90% or more of the panel, and were consolidated into freely available parenting guidelines. Endorsed strategies emphasised stabilisation and emotional safety prior to trauma-focused engagement, child-led pacing, emotional validation, and parental self-regulation. Resilience-promoting and prescriptive strategies were consistently rejected, reflecting expert preference for responsive over directive approaches. The expert panel primarily comprised professionals from Western countries, which may limit the applicability of the strategies across culturally diverse contexts. To our knowledge, this is the first study to establish expert consensus on parenting strategies specifically for young people experiencing trauma-related anxiety and depression. The pattern of endorsement and rejection reveals key principles for parent-led post-trauma support and offers a foundation for developing and evaluating low-intensity parenting interventions.

articles.title: Baseline neutrophil-to-HDL cholesterol ratio is associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A new index, the neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol ratio (NHR), has been reported to predict atherosclerosis and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This study aimed to investigate the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent complications in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (MPA/GPA).

METHODS: Clinical data of 150 patients with MPA/GPA were analysed retrospectively. Baseline demographic data, the Birmingham vasculitis activity score (BVAS), the five-factor score (FFS), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded. All-cause mortality, relapse, end-stage kidney disease, cerebrovascular accident (CVA), and ACS were evaluated as subsequent complications. NHR was calculated using the following formula: neutrophil count (× 1000/mm3) / HDL-cholesterol levels (mg/dL). NHR was analysed both as a continuous variable and using exploratory categorical cut-offs. Death before CVA was treated as a competing event in the cumulative incidence analysis.

RESULTS: The median age was 63.5 years (64.0% female). Baseline NHR was significantly correlated with baseline BVAS, ESR, and CRP levels. Of the five subsequent complications, only subsequent CVA demonstrated a significant area under the curve in a receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of baseline NHR. Continuous NHR was not significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP. In complementary exploratory analyses using the cohort-derived cut-off, patients with baseline NHR ≥ 0.17 had a higher frequency of subsequent CVA and a lower CVA-free survival rate than those with baseline NHR < 0.17. The former group also had a higher cumulative incidence of CVA when death before CVA was treated as a competing event. NHR ≥ 0.17 remained significantly associated with subsequent CVA after adjustment for age and CRP.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the clinical utility of baseline NHR in predicting subsequent CVA in patients with MPA/GPA. Key Points • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio was significantly correlated with baseline Birmingham vasculitis activity score, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein levels in patients with microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis. • Patients with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 had a significantly higher risk of subsequent cerebrovascular accident and a lower cerebrovascular accident-free survival rate than those with baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio <0.17. • Baseline neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio ≥0.17 remained independently associated with subsequent cerebrovascular accident after adjustment for age and C-reactive protein.

articles.title: Association of bone mineral-reducing medications with two-year complications following open reduction and internal fixation of ankle fractures: a propensity score-matched analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone mineral-reducing medications (BMRMs) are commonly prescribed, but their association with outcomes after ankle open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) is unclear. We evaluated preoperative exposure to ten BMRM classes and two-year complications after ankle ORIF.

METHODS: Adults undergoing ankle ORIF at least two years before data extraction were identified in TriNetX. Exposure required at least one medication record 1-180 days before surgery for proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), glucocorticoids, loop diuretics, thiazolidinediones, calcineurin inhibitors, aromatase inhibitors, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), first- or second-generation antipsychotics, or antiepileptics. Exposed patients were 1:1 propensity score matched to patients unexposed to all classes. Risk ratios (RRs) for five two-year outcomes were adjusted for false discovery rate (FDR).

RESULTS: Matched cohorts included 227-9,858 patients per group. Nonunion was more frequent with glucocorticoids (2.36% vs. 1.72%; RR 1.37), PPIs (2.68% vs. 1.79%; RR 1.50), loop diuretics (3.98% vs. 2.20%; RR 1.81), SSRIs (2.49% vs. 1.72%; RR 1.45) and antiepileptics (2.70% vs. 1.73%; RR 1.56); all 95% confidence intervals excluded 1 and all FDR q ≤ 0.023. Antiepileptics were also associated with revision ORIF, the primary outcome (3.55% vs. 2.65%; RR 1.34, 95% CI 1.13-1.59; q = 0.009). No class was associated with device infection or hardware failure. Outcomes for thiazolidinediones, calcineurin inhibitors and aromatase inhibitors were not estimable (too few events).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative glucocorticoid, PPI, loop diuretic, SSRI or antiepileptic exposure was associated with higher two-year nonunion risk after ankle ORIF, and antiepileptic exposure with revision. These hypothesis-generating associations may reflect confounding by indication.

articles.title: Floralozone alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiac senescence and fibrosis by inhibiting the VEGFR1.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Floralozone(FL) is a medicinal compound with potential cardiovascular protective effects. Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1 (VEGFR1) signaling has been implicated in cardiovascular dysfunction. This study investigated whether floralozone ameliorates heart failure (HF) through regulation of VEGFR1.

METHODS: HF was induced in rats by intraperitoneal injection of doxorubicin (DOX) for six weeks. VEGFR1 expression was analyzed by immunofluorescence and Western blotting. Oxidative stress was determined by DHE staining of myocardial ROS and serum MDA and SOD assays. Senescence associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining was performed to evaluate the degree of myocardial aging. HE staining was used to observe cardiac morphology. Masson, argyrophilic and orcein staining were applied to detect the degree of myocardial fibrosis, and echocardiography was conducted to assess cardiac function in each group.

RESULTS: Floralozone (FL) modulated VEGFR1 expression and alleviated DOX-induced oxidative stress, cardiac aging, myocardial fibrosis, and cardiac dysfunction in HF rats. The protective effects of FL on oxidative stress, cardiac aging, myocardial fibrosis, cardiac function, and VEGFR1 expression were attenuated by pharmacological activation of VEGFR1 with placental growth factor (PLGF), supporting the involvement of VEGFR1 signaling in the cardioprotective effects of FL.

DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that floralozone exerts cardioprotective effects against DOX induced heart failure, at least in part, through modulation of VEGFR1 associated signaling and oxidative stress. Floralozone modulated VEGFR1 expression and was associated with reduced oxidative stress, cardiac aging, and myocardial fibrosis, ultimately improving cardiac dysfunction. However, the precise causal relationship between VEGFR1 signaling and oxidative stress remains to be determined. These findings suggest that floralozone may have therapeutic potential for DOX induced cardiac injury through modulation of VEGFR1 associated pathological processes.

articles.title: Primary, atrial secondary, and ventricular secondary mitral regurgitation in the general population.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While primary mitral valve regurgitation (PMR) results from structural abnormalities of the mitral valve leaflets, secondary mitral valve regurgitation (SMR) arises from either mitral annular dilatation (atrial type, aSMR) or left ventricle remodelling (ventricular type, vSMR) in the absence of intrinsic leaflet disease. Although SMR is considered the most common cause of clinically relevant mitral regurgitation (MR), population-based data on its prevalence, subtype distribution, and clinical profiles are lacking. We aimed to determine the prevalence of PMR and SMR and to characterize PMR, aSMR, and vSMR in the general population.

METHODS: We analyzed the first 10,000 participants of the population-based Hamburg City Health Study enrolled 2016-2019; 8543 echocardiographic examinations were available. Mitral valve morphology and function were independently assessed by two investigators. PMR was defined by the presence of intrinsic leaflet pathology, whereas SMR was classified as ventricular when left ventricular ejection fraction was less than 50% or less than 55% in the presence of geometric distortion (tenting area ≥ 150 mm2 or coaptation depth ≥ 10 mm) and cases with left ventricular ejection fraction equal to or above 50% were classified as aSMR.

RESULTS: A total of 216 participants had moderate or severe MR (2.53% of the total cohort, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.20%-2.89%, see Fig. 3). Of these, 148 were classified as SMR (68.5%, 95% CI: 61.8%-74.7%), the remaining were mainly of primary etiology (31.5%, 95% CI: 25.3%-38.2%). Among SMR cases, aSMR was predominant (84.5%, 95% CI: 77.5%-89.9%), whereas vSMR accounted for 15.5% (95% CI: 10.1%-22.4%). Compared with aSMR, individuals with vSMR were older, more symptomatic, and more frequently had atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Echocardiographic parameters indicated more advanced cardiac remodelling and dysfunction in vSMR. Compared with SMR, participants with PMR had greater MR severity, while age and the proportion of women were numerically higher without reaching statistical significance. During a median follow-up of 4.56 years, 10 participants had died, with all-cause mortality being significantly higher among participants with PMR than among those with aSMR.

CONCLUSION: In this population-based cohort, SMR accounted for two-thirds of relevant MR, with aSMR being the predominant subtype. MR severity was higher in PMR as compared to SMR. Distinct echocardiographic and clinical profiles suggest more advanced disease in vSMR. Multivariate analysis revealed that atrial fibrillation was significantly more present in the vSMR cohort. These findings highlight the need for refined SMR subclassification and longitudinal studies to define prognostic implications and clinically meaningful definitions. All-cause mortality was highest in participants with PMR than in those with aSMR.

articles.title: The networked landscape of cell death in sepsis: from dynamic pathway to node-targeted therapies.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although research into programmed cell death in sepsis has spanned several decades, mortality rates remain high, and no therapy specifically targeting cell death pathways has yet achieved clinical translation.

PURPOSE: In this review, we propose a temporal and spatial framework in which sepsis-related cell death unfolds along three integrated axes.

CONCLUSIONS: First, the sequential transformation from early pyroptosis and NETosis (driving hyperinflammation) to mid-stage necroptosis (amplifying tissue damage) to late lymphocyte apoptosis (mediating immunosuppression), with distinct cellular responses in immune cells versus parenchymal tissues. Second, we have distilled complex pathway interactions into three converging decision nodes, RIPK1 ubiquitination status, caspase-8 activity, and membrane pore executors (GSDMD/MLKL/NINJ1), whose coordinated state determines whether cells undergo inflammatory lytic death or silent apoptosis. Third, we describe why single-pathway inhibitors fail in preclinical sepsis studies, and propose a stage-specific therapeutic strategy: inhibit GSDMD early to block pyroptosis; modulate RIPK1 mid-phase to limit RIPK1-dependent inflammatory or necroptotic pathology; and restore lymphoid homeostasis late via caspase-3 inhibition or IL-7 therapy. Finally, we conclude by outlining a translational roadmap prioritising biomarker development, patient stratification, and adaptive trial designs for future research.

articles.title: Intrinsic epithelial defects and NF-κB-dependent signaling heighten viral injury in biliary atresia.
articles.abstract: Targeted injury to the biliary epithelium and impaired bile flow are central mechanisms underlying childhood cholangiopathies. In biliary atresia (BA), immune-mediated cholangiocyte injury drives progressive bile duct obstruction, yet epithelial-intrinsic programs regulating injury susceptibility remain incompletely defined. Here, we modeled virus-epithelium interactions using rhesus rotavirus (RRV) infection of human liver-derived cholangiocyte organoids from normal donors (NCO) and infants with BA at diagnosis (BACO-Dx) or transplantation (BACO-Tx). Compared with NCO, BA organoids displayed baseline defects in tight junction architecture and barrier function, with prominent epithelial disruption and apoptosis following RRV exposure. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that while NCO and BACO-Dx mounted predominantly interferon-associated antiviral responses, BACO-Tx exhibited an expanded inflammatory program characterized by enrichment of NF-κB (RELA/NFKB1) regulatory network at baseline and amplified by infection. Inhibition of NF-κB signaling with the hydrogen sulfide donor GYY4137 restored organoid growth, improved tight junction organization, reduced permeability, and attenuated RRV-induced apoptosis. In the murine BA model, GYY4137 improved disease severity, preserved bile duct architecture, and protected epithelial junctional integrity while limiting cholangiocyte apoptosis. These findings identify an epithelial NF-κB-predominant program as a key determinant of intrinsic susceptibility to viral injury in BA and support targeting cholangiocyte NF-κB signaling to suppress disease progression.

articles.title: Metformin Preserves Regional Brain Glucose Uptake, Structure, and Functional Connectivity in Adults with Insulin Resistance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia is a rapidly expanding public health problem with major socio-economic burden. Insulin resistance (IR) is a prevalent but modifiable risk factor for dementia, yet its effects on brain structure, functional connectivity, and metabolism remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Regional brain glucose uptake (PET), volumes (MRI), functional connectivity (fMRI), and cognition (NIH Toolbox) was measured in 72 adults with or without markers of IR. To evaluate reversibility of IR-associated brain deficits, forty older adults with IR were randomized to forty weeks of metformin or placebo, and brain measures were repeated. As a proof-of-concept experiment, we developed a conditional brain-specific insulin receptor knockout mouse and assessed brain mitochondrial function and cognition.

RESULTS: In older adults with markers of IR is associated with diminished total and regional brain volumes in areas critical for neuronal connectivity, memory, and learning, including cerebral white matter and the hippocampus. Reduced functional connectivity between brain regions detrimental for cognition was also noted. Further, we demonstrated that ATP production, essential for neuronal connectivity, was diminished in neuron-specific insulin receptor knockout mice accompanied by deficits in hippocampal- and prefrontal-dependent tasks. Forty weeks of metformin improved systemic insulin sensitivity concurrent to preserved brain glucose uptake, volume, and functional connectivity within specific regions central to decision-making and learning. Metformin was also associated with an improved composite measure of processing speed and working memory.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight IR as a key regulator of brain metabolism and support the concept that insulin sensitization can prevent neurobiological deficits in older people with IR.

articles.title: A review of published personalized phage therapy cases in clinical practice.
articles.abstract: The increase in antimicrobial resistant infections has fueled a resurgent interest in bacteriophage (phage) therapy. We conducted a literature review of personalized phage therapy cases in the peer-reviewed, English-language literature reported between 1/1/2005, to 8/31/2025 for which individual patient data were available, identifying and synthesizing data from a total of 323 patients described in 83 studies. Most patients (68%, 221/323) were treated with ≥ 2 phages (a phage cocktail). The median concentration of phages was 108 PFU/mL (IQR 107-109). Most patients (76%, 246/323) received antibiotics concurrent with phage therapy. The median duration of therapy was 10 days (IQR 5-21). The most common indications for phage therapy were skin/soft tissue, pulmonary, orthopedic, osteoarticular, and genitourinary infections. 144 patients received fixed (off-the-shelf) phage preparations whereas 179 received bespoke phage preparations (i.e., personalized therapy). For cases where outcomes data were available, 78% (253/323), experienced clinical improvement while the targeted pathogen was eradicated in 61% (177/290) of cases. Nine patients had treatment withdrawn due to tolerability concerns. These data indicate that there is substantial heterogeneity in current personalized phage therapy clinical practices but that this approach can be successful.

articles.title: Donor-derived CD8+CD122+ Tregs generated in mixed donor chimeric NOD mice suppress autoreactive T cells.
articles.abstract: The establishment of mixed hematopoietic chimerism is a promising way to induce immune tolerance for islet replacement therapy and to treat the underlying autoimmunity in type 1 diabetes (T1D). Mixed chimerism not only promotes effective thymic negative selection of autoreactive cells but also restores regulatory T cell (Treg) function and peripheral tolerance. In the current study, we determined that a novel class of donor-derived CD8+CD44+CD122+ Tregs (d-CD8+CD122+ Tregs) plays a crucial role in controlling autoimmunity in non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice with induced mixed chimerism. Using adoptive T cell transfer experiments, we showed that d-CD8+CD122+ Tregs abrogate autoimmunity by suppressing the exogenously injected diabetogenic T cells in Recombination-Activating Gene deficient NOD mice. These d-CD8+CD122+ Tregs from NOD chimeras show upregulation of Helios, Programmed cell death protein 1, perforin, granzyme-B, CD39, Folate receptor 4, and downregulation of proinflammatory marker SCART1. Using in vitro assays, we show that d-CD8+CD122+ Tregs respond specifically to a Complementarity-Determining Region-3 peptide sequence derived from T cell receptors of islet antigen-specific autoreactive T cells. Similarly, we found that individuals with T1D have a deficiency in CD8+CD122+ Tregs, suggesting a potential loss of regulatory function accompanies disease onset. Revitalizing CD8+CD122+ Tregs may offer a new therapeutic strategy of restoring immune tolerance in autoimmune diabetes.

articles.title: Intraoperative glucocorticoids confound surgical biopsy transcriptomics.
Delirium Occurrence and Associated Factors Among Patients With Dementia and Mild Cognitive Impairment Admitted to Long-Term Care Hospitals: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delirium is common among older adults, particularly those with cognitive impairment. However, delirium among patients with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in long-term care (LTC) hospitals has received limited attention.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine delirium occurrence and associated factors among patients with dementia or MCI in LTC hospitals.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 142 patients aged 65 years or older with dementia (n=100, 70.4%) or MCI (n=42, 29.6%) at 2 LTC hospitals in South Korea between September 2021 and August 2022. Delirium occurrence was defined as at least 1 positive Short Confusion Assessment Method assessment during twice-daily assessments over 4 weeks, including the first assessment. Multivariable logistic regression examined associated factors overall and within each cognitive group.

RESULTS: Delirium was identified in 55 (38.7%) of 142 patients. The proportion was 41% (41/100) in patients with dementia and 33.3% (14/42) in patients with MCI. Hypoactive delirium was the most common subtype (33/55, 60%). Overall, female sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.344, 95% CI 1.794-10.515; P=.001), immobility (aOR 4.953, 95% CI 1.857-13.205; P=.001), and analgesic use (aOR 3.641, 95% CI 1.262-10.501; P=.02) were associated with delirium. Infection was inversely associated with delirium (aOR 0.251, 95% CI 0.101-0.623; P=.003). In patients with dementia, female sex, immobility, analgesic use, and pain were associated with delirium. Diaper use was associated with delirium in patients with MCI.

CONCLUSIONS: Delirium was common among patients with dementia or MCI in LTC hospitals. The findings support regular delirium assessment, with attention to mobility and pain-related care needs. Further studies are needed to clarify the factors associated with delirium in each cognitive group.

articles.title: The transition from pregnancy to motherhood in women with type 2 diabetes: A longitudinal qualitative study.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To explore how women with type 2 diabetes experience the transition from early pregnancy to postpartum.

METHODS: A longitudinal qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 13 women with type 2 diabetes at three time points: early pregnancy, late pregnancy and 2-4 months postpartum. Twelve women completed all three interviews. Data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Women's experiences changed across the three phases. Early pregnancy was characterised by feeling overwhelmed, with intensified type 2 diabetes treatment demands and increased burden of self-care. Late pregnancy involved a gradual adaptation and shift in focus towards the fetus. Postpartum focused on reprioritisation, where diabetes often receded into the background alongside reduced support from their family and friends and disruptions in continuity of care. Across the phases, responsibility for the fetus and availability of support shaped women's experiences.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, the transition to motherhood among women with type 2 diabetes was experienced as a dynamic and phase-dependent process, in which needs and challenges varied before, during and after pregnancy. The findings underline the importance of preparing women for diabetes-related changes in self-care and treatment both pregestationally and antenatally, and of providing access to structured and continuous postpartum care.

articles.title: Hierarchically Gated DNA Nanoswitches Enable Context-Selective Activation of Antimicrobial Peptides.
articles.abstract: Precise control over cytolytic peptide activity remains a central challenge in antimicrobial therapy because membrane disruption is intrinsically coupled with systemic toxicity. Here we encode a hierarchically gated molecular logic within a DNA nanoswitch to enable context-selective activation of melittin only at infection sites. The nanoswitch integrates three cooperative control layers: bacterial tropism, microenvironmental sensing, and inflammation-associated enzymatic activation. Maltodextrin ligands are spatially programmed to engage the bacteria-specific maltodextrin transporter, yielding selective bacterial recognition with a 2.3-order-of-magnitude enhancement in binding. Cytosine-rich i-motif locks convert acidic biofilm conditions into conformational opening of the scaffold, while a caspase-1-cleavable peptide tether provides a final enzymatic gate under inflammatory cues. This hierarchical gating confines membrane-lytic activity with high spatiotemporal precision and suppresses off-target hemolysis and systemic leakage. In uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC)-associated urinary tract infection models, the nanoswitch achieves effective bacterial clearance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin in vivo, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for conditional peptide activation.

articles.title: SLC3A2 Drives an Immunosuppressive Metabolic Axis that Limits Oncolytic Virotherapy Efficacy.
articles.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy is a promising cancer treatment that elicits antitumor immunity. However, the efficacy of virotherapy is often constrained by tumor-intrinsic immune suppression. To identify conserved virus-induced programs driving immune escape, we applied multi-omics and functional assays across multiple tumor and virus models, uncovering an SLC3A2-driven immunosuppressive metabolic barrier. In oncolytic herpes simplex virus (oHSV)-infected tumors, a biphasic immune trajectory emerged: early CD8+ T cell activation was followed by SLC3A2-mediated methionine and tryptophan uptake, driving T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, oHSV upregulated SLC3A2 via the m6A-IGF2BP3 axis, while tumor-intrinsic tryptophan metabolism engaged the AHR/ARNT/ICP4 cascade to amplify viral replication and reinforce the immunosuppressive program. Importantly, dietary methionine supplementation disrupted the metabolic checkpoint, restored T cell effector function, and synergized with oHSV expressing anti-PD1 to enhance tumor control in humanized preclinical models. Notably, a parallel SLC3A2-centered metabolic-immunologic circuit operated in vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) infection. Together, these findings delineate an actionable, conserved metabolic checkpoint and provide a framework for integrating metabolic modulation into cancer viroimmunotherapy.

articles.title: Rational Surface Engineering Reduces Advanced Glycation End-Product Adsorption and Improves Implant Integration.
articles.abstract: Advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) accumulate in metabolic diseases such as diabetes and are closely associated with poor outcomes following implantation. However, how these molecules influence events at the biomaterial interface has remained largely unknown. Here, we identify AGEs as critical biointerfacial modifiers that adsorb onto implant surfaces, reprogram immune responses, promote fibrotic encapsulation, impair angiogenesis, and compromise osseointegration. This suggests a potential mechanism by which metabolic disease disrupts biomaterial-tissue integration. By engineering titanium surfaces enriched with amine or carboxyl functionalities, we create AGE-resistant biointerfaces that effectively suppress pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization, promote an anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage phenotype, reduce fibrotic encapsulation, enhance angiogenesis, and improve osseointegration across ex vivo, in vitro, and in vivo diabetic models. These findings establish disease-informed surface chemistry as a design paradigm for next-generation implants intended for metabolically compromised and other high-risk patient populations.

articles.title: Adaptive Active Illumination Via Translationally and Axially Tunable Cascaded Metasurfaces.
articles.abstract: Active three-dimensional sensing requires accurate light delivery and sufficient return-signal strength, while complex scenes require a tunable balance between local power concentration and illumination coverage. Collimated beam illumination supports a longer maximum detectable distance by concentrating optical power, whereas expanded beam illumination improves angular sampling efficiency by increasing coverage per projection. Existing active-illumination approaches typically use fixed illumination patterns or predefined scanning trajectories, making it difficult to balance local power concentration for maximum detectable distance with illumination coverage for sampling efficiency. Here we propose an adaptive active-illumination method based on translationally and axially tunable cascaded metasurfaces (TATCMs). TATCMs control the beam output angle within the field of view (FoV) through lateral translation and tune illumination coverage through axial-spacing tuning. At an operating wavelength of 905 nm, the implemented TATCMs demonstrate continuous beam-output-angle control across an approximately 70°×70° FoV under a ±300 µm lateral stroke, while increasing the interlayer spacing by 2.64 mm expands collimated beam illumination with a measured divergence of 0.06° to provide continuous coverage across the FoV. Adaptive three-dimensional reconstruction further demonstrates the potential of TATCMs as a compact planar illumination platform for scene-adaptive three-dimensional sensing in autonomous vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles, and industrial robotics.

articles.title: Examining the facilitators and barriers to health behaviour change for type 2 diabetes remission in a young population with early diabetes: A qualitative study of participants in the DIADEM-I randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This qualitative study explored the motivators, facilitators and barriers to health behaviour change in young individuals recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), drawing insights from the DIADEM-I randomised controlled trial examining the impact of an intensive lifestyle intervention (ILI) incorporating total diet replacement and gradual unsupervised physical activity on bodyweight reduction and T2DM remission.

METHODS: A subset, enrolled in intensive ILI or best medical care (control) groups of DIADEM-I were invited to participate in a qualitative sub-study employing one-to-one face-to-face interviews after study completion at 12 months. Stratified purposive sampling was used to include men and women of varying ages and participants from both intervention groups. Twenty-eight interviews were conducted, recorded, transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Highlighted motivators included the desire for T2DM remission, bodyweight reduction and freedom from medication. Social support and intrinsic factors were pivotal, with successful participants experiencing a paradigm shift toward healthier behaviours. Barriers included health-related issues, dysfunctional relationships with food and environmental challenges. Cultural sensitivity addressing body image perceptions and social norms, and the need for obesity and T2DM public awareness programmes was highlighted. The ILI group valued multidisciplinary support, meal replacements and educational programmes, but highlighted the need for flexibility and ongoing personalised support.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight the complexity of health behaviour change initiation and maintenance in the context of T2DM diagnosis and aiming for T2DM remission. The study provides insights for clinicians aiming to motivate individuals toward sustained health behaviour change for T2DM remission and implement service delivery.

articles.title: PM2.5 exposure associates with IL-6 gene hypomethylation and systemic IL-6 expression in an at-risk asthma cohort.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

articles.title: Sinus Bradycardia Limiting Beta-Blockade in Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia: Atrial Leadless Pacing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beta-blockade is the cornerstone of therapy in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), but coexisting sinus node dysfunction can prevent adequate dosing.

CASE SUMMARY: A woman aged in her late 20s presented with exertional syncope. She had profound sinus bradycardia and reproducible exercise-induced multiform ventricular ectopy in a structurally normal heart, supporting a diagnosis of CPVT, later confirmed with genetic testing (pathogenic RYR2 variant). Resting heart rates in the low 30s precluded beta-blocker initiation. After shared decision-making in which she declined transvenous leads, an atrial leadless pacemaker was implanted, permitting up-titration of nadolol with flecainide and deferral of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator.

DISCUSSION: Sinus node dysfunction is recognized in CPVT but is seldom framed as a modifiable obstacle to guideline-directed therapy. Treating the bradycardia allowed medical therapy to be maximized before device therapy, consistent with consensus recommendations.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Bradycardia that limits beta-blockade in CPVT is a pacing problem rather than drug intolerance.

articles.title: Contrast-Induced Encephalopathy Mimicking Stroke During Vein of Marshall Ethanol Infusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-induced encephalopathy (CIE) is a rare, reversible neurologic complication of iodinated contrast exposure that may mimic acute stroke.

CASE SUMMARY: A 68-year-old man undergoing atrial fibrillation ablation with vein of Marshall ethanol infusion received 40 mL of ioversol. Approximately 4 hours after the procedure, he developed agitation, myoclonic movements, urinary incontinence, and left-sided weakness. Brain computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, magnetic resonance angiography, and diffusion-weighted imaging showed no hemorrhage, acute infarction, or major vascular abnormality. Similar neurologic symptoms recurred approximately 10 hours after the procedure. After neurologic consultation, CIE was considered the most likely diagnosis. Supportive treatment was provided, with complete neurologic recovery within 48 hours.

DISCUSSION: CIE should be considered when acute neurologic manifestations occur after contrast exposure, particularly when initial evaluation does not demonstrate an acute cerebrovascular cause.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Recognition of CIE as a stroke mimic may facilitate appropriate evaluation and management while avoiding unnecessary intervention.

articles.title: Fulminant Staphylococcus aureus Pancarditis in an Immunocompetent Adult.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) is rare and deadly. We report the case of IE rapidly progressing to pancarditis.

CASE SUMMARY: A man in his 60s with no medical history presented with fever, chest pain, and embolic phenomena. Initial evaluation suggested myocardial infarction, but angiography was normal. Echocardiography revealed an aortic valve vegetation. Blood cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Despite appropriate antibiotics, he developed rapidly progressive purulent pericardial effusion and died. Pericardial fluid cultures confirmed S aureus purulent pericarditis, establishing the diagnosis of pancarditis involving endocardium, myocardium, and pericardium.

DISCUSSION: Bacterial pancarditis is an exceedingly rare and severe complication of IE. Pericardial effusion associated with IE should raise suspicion for purulent pericarditis and prompt rapid referral for surgical drainage or diagnostic puncture.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Consider bacterial pancarditis when IE is complicated by myocardial and pericardial involvement. Pericardial effusion in IE requires prompt investigation and drainage or at least a diagnostic puncture.

articles.title: National clinical audits as distributed diabetes surveillance infrastructure: Consensus lessons from Ireland.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes increasingly shapes acute-care demand through cardiovascular disease, critical illness, frailty, stroke and preventable metabolic emergencies. Yet in health systems without mature diabetes registries, much of this burden may be visible only indirectly through national clinical audits and registries.

AIM: To assess how Ireland's National Office of Clinical Audit (NOCA) captures diabetes-related intelligence across major healthcare pathways and what this reveals about national chronic disease surveillance capacity.

METHODS: A structured narrative review of publicly available NOCA reports and audit publications from 2021 to 2025 was undertaken. Eligible reports had direct diabetes relevance or addressed conditions in which diabetes is a major comorbidity, risk factor or outcome modifier. Data extraction focused on population coverage, diabetes-related variables, temporal trends, hospital-level variation and reporting limitations.

RESULTS: Diabetes-specific reporting was recent and uneven. The 2022 paediatric diabetes feasibility study identified 3332 children and young people with type 1 diabetes across 19 centres, with major variation in multidisciplinary staffing, transition pathways, HbA1c measurement and data systems. Paediatric critical care reporting identified 232 DKA admissions among 15,288 admissions during 2014-2023. In adult acute care, diabetes was recorded in 430/1615 STEMI cases in 2024, rising from 18% in 2021 to 27% in 2024, while overall timely reperfusion declined from 67% in 2017 to 58% in 2024. Stroke, ICU, hip fracture and mortality audits were highly diabetes-relevant but did not publish diabetes-stratified outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: National clinical audit infrastructures may function as distributed chronic disease intelligence systems even in the absence of mature integrated diabetes registries.

articles.title: A Synergistic Hydrogel Strategy for the Treatment of Candida Vaginitis Through Pathogen Clearance and Microecosystem Restoration.
articles.abstract: Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for Candida vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment-degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@LabPC, which self-assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular-weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates Candida albicans (C. albicans) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection-dysbiosis-recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.

articles.title: Helicobacter pylori Infection Is Associated With the Occurrence and Progression of Vocal Fold Leukoplakia via NRF2/KEAP1 Pathway Activation.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection has been implicated in vocal fold leukoplakia (VFL), a precancerous laryngeal lesion. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the relationship between H. pylori and VFL, focusing on the NRF2/KEAP1 oxidative stress pathway. Clinicopathological analysis was performed on samples from 64 patients with VFL and 30 patients with vocal cord polyps (controls). The results showed a significantly higher prevalence of H. pylori in the VFL group (48.4%) than in the controls (16.7%, p = 0.003). Among H. pylori-positive VFL cases, VacA-positive strains predominated, accounting for 71.0%. Multivariate logistic regression identified H. pylori as an independent risk factor for VFL (OR = 6.198, 95% CI: 1.580-24.321). VFL tissues exhibited upregulated expression of NRF2, KEAP1, and HO-1 (p < 0.001), demonstrating both virulence-dependent (HO-1 induction) and virulence-independent (NRF2 upregulation) pathway activation patterns. In vitro experiments revealed that H. pylori exposure induced NRF2 nuclear translocation and triggered an oxidative stress response. Notably, VFL-derived cells responded more rapidly to H. pylori stimulation, with pathway activation peaking at 24 h post-infection, whereas normal cells showed a delayed response, peaking at 48 h (p < 0.05). Furthermore, VFL-derived cells displayed more pronounced stress-induced morphological alterations following H. pylori exposure. These findings suggest that H. pylori may promote VFL progression via NRF2/KEAP1 pathway activation, highlighting the potential clinical value of H. pylori screening in VFL management.

articles.title: Impact of Elevated Blood Pressure Targets on Splanchnic Ischemia and Mortality in Septic Resuscitation: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis causes deaths worldwide each day, with hemodynamic resuscitation being central to management. Guidelines recommend a 65-mm Hg mean arterial pressure (MAP) target, yet the evidence for elevated targets remains fragmented across mortality, renal, and splanchnic outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This review aims to comprehensively appraise the impact of elevated MAP targets on splanchnic ischemia, mortality, and organ-specific outcomes in septic resuscitation.

METHODS: Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar for studies comparing MAP targets in septic shock. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; randomized controlled trials [RCTs]) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (nonrandomized studies). The findings were synthesized narratively according to the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guidelines, with random-effects meta-analysis for mortality outcomes. Evidence certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: From 3254 records, 11 studies (2895 patients; 4 RCTs, 7 nonrandomized) met the inclusion criteria. Pooled 90-day mortality across 3 trials showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher mortality with elevated MAP targets (320/720, 44.4% vs 280/722, 38.8%; OR 1.31, 95% CI 0.97-1.77). Pooled 28- or 30-day mortality showed a similar nonsignificant trend (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.98-1.61), which was robust to sensitivity analysis. Narratively, mortality findings across nonpooled observational studies were inconsistent; some linked low MAP to higher death risk, and others found no significant association. Renal outcomes were inconsistent, with some studies showing reduced renal replacement therapy or improved acute kidney injury recovery at higher targets, particularly in hypertensive or cirrhotic subgroups. Elevated MAP targets consistently increased vasopressor exposure and were associated with more arrhythmias and fewer organ support-free days. No study reported splanchnic ischemia as a discrete outcome; mesenteric ischemia rates were low and similar between arms. Overall certainty of evidence was very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher MAP targets show no clear mortality or splanchnic perfusion benefit and may increase overall harm, though select subgroups, chronic hypertension, and cirrhosis, may benefit, supporting individualized, risk-stratified MAP targeting over uniformly elevated-target strategies.

articles.title: Low-Use vs. High-Use Physical Restraint in Older Adults With Sepsis Receiving Mechanical Ventilation: A Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical restraints are commonly used in patients receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU), yet evidence regarding their effectiveness in older patients with sepsis is limited. This study evaluated whether a low-use physical restraint strategy improves outcomes in older patients with sepsis requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.

METHODS: This multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial was conducted in five ICUs in China from August 2023 to March 2026. Patients aged ≥ 65 years with invasive mechanical ventilation were randomly assigned (1:1) to a low-use restraint strategy (restraints applied only for severe agitation) or a high-use restraint strategy (routine restraint use until recovery of consciousness and liberation from mechanical ventilation). The primary outcome was days alive without delirium or coma within 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes included delirium incidence, ventilator-free days, coma-free days, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, and safety events. Analyses were performed using intention-to-treat, per-protocol, and inverse probability weighting approaches.

RESULTS: Among 485 randomized patients (median age, 74 years; 60.4% male), 244 received low-use and 241 high-use restraint. Delirium- and coma-free days did not differ between groups (adjusted mean difference, 0.17 days; 95% CI, -0.20 to 0.54; p = 0.37). Low-use restraint was associated with more ventilator-free days (0.69 days; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p < 0.001) and coma-free days (0.46 days; 95% CI, 0.19-0.74; p = 0.001). No significant between-group differences were observed in delirium incidence, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, or safety outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Among older mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis, a low-use physical restraint strategy did not improve days alive without delirium or coma but was associated with more ventilator-free and coma-free days. These findings suggest that reducing restraint use may facilitate short-term recovery, although the safety of restraint minimization requires further evaluation.

TRAIL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: ChiCTR1900025850.

articles.title: Clinical assessment and relationship of retinal fluorophores and microvascular modifications in early diabetic retinal disease in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify macular microvascular modifications and retinal fluorophores in early diabetic retinal disease (DRD) in type 1 diabetes mellitus (DM1), and to explore their interrelationship.
