OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the user experience of the Icanbewell web application.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey in Canada. Participants were members of the public aged at least 18 years and health care providers residing in Canada who had internet access. A 9-item online survey was made available within the Icanbewell web application from July 8, 2024, to August 7, 2025. It invited users to rate their satisfaction with the app, suggest improvements, and describe what they learned from it. The single Likert-scale question was analyzed using summary descriptive statistics, and the short-answer questions were analyzed using qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: Of the 69 users who responded to the Icanbewell survey, 80% (n=55) were satisfied with the app, 9% (n=6) were dissatisfied, and 10% (n=7) were neither satisfied nor dissatisfied. Satisfaction ranged from 78.9% to 90.9% across participant gender, status as a health care provider or member of the public, language, and whether the respondent was attached to a primary care provider. A total of 46 (67%) respondents provided suggestions to improve the Icanbewell web application by optimizing the interface and adding medical content beyond prevention. Finally, 42% (29/69) of respondents indicated that they learned new information from using the Icanbewell app, including details about Canadian prevention guidelines, how to access various health resources, and general medical information on health and symptoms.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated user satisfaction and engagement with the app. Subsequent work should prioritize representative sampling to gather feedback from individuals not attached to a primary care provider, younger people, health care providers, and people in geographically diverse locations. Our results highlight an ongoing need for accessible, trustworthy, evidence-based prevention resources, along with support for clinicians in disseminating them to the public. Future involvement of patient partners in the design and evaluation of the web application will be important to ensure its inclusivity and relevance.

articles.title: Associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy procedure versus conventional two-stage hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastasis.
authors: Supported by the Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Review Group
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Staged surgical procedures, such as two-stage hepatectomy and associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) technique, use the liver regenerative capacity to stimulate growth of the future liver remnant. These procedures can be used in people with extensive colorectal liver metastases when the future liver remnant is too small to allow a safe postoperative recovery after major hepatectomy. Compared with conventional two-stage hepatectomy, although ALPPS results in faster and larger growth of the future liver remnant, the evidence regarding its impact on major postoperative complications, perioperative mortality, recurrence rates, and long-term survival is conflicting.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of liver partition and portal vein ligation for a staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) procedure versus conventional two-stage hepatectomy in people with colorectal liver metastases.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Group Controlled Trials Register, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials in the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, Embase, three other databases, online trial registries, grey literature databases, and reference lists of identified studies; we also retrieved additional information from the included trial authors. Our last study search was on 4 December 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised clinical trials comparing ALPPS versus conventional two-stage hepatectomy in adults with colorectal liver metastases who were unable to undergo complete resection because the future liver remnant was estimated to be < 30% of the total liver volume.

OUTCOMES: The critical outcomes were perioperative all-cause mortality at 90 days, all-cause mortality, serious adverse events, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Other important outcomes included overall survival, disease-free survival, and resection rate. For our primary analysis, we used data at the maximum follow-up, except for perioperative mortality, analysed at 90 days after operation.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Risk of Bias 2.0 (RoB 2) tool.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We used standard Cochrane methodological procedures to develop the review. We did not perform meta-analysis because only one trial met the inclusion criteria. We expressed dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RR), continuous outcomes as mean differences (MD), and time-to-event outcomes as hazard ratios (HR), all with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), using RevMan. We used the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of the evidence.

INCLUDED STUDIES: The included trial was a six-centre, publicly funded, Scandinavian randomised clinical trial. The trial investigators randomised 100 participants (mean age: 65 ± 10 years; male-to-female ratio: 2.34:1.0). After randomisation, two participants in the ALPPS (1 severe comorbidity; 1 total liver volume > 30%) and one participant in the two-stage hepatectomy group (progressive disease) could not proceed to the intervention and were excluded. One other participant was lost to follow-up after emigrating. The trial was described in 15 publications. The trial provided data for all outcomes of our review. We followed the analytical approach reported by the trial authors, using a modified intention-to-treat population where applicable and available data otherwise.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: The evidence suggests that ALPPS, compared with two-stage hepatectomy, results in little to no difference in perioperative all-cause mortality at 90 days (RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.32 to 5.76; I2 not applicable; 1 study; 97 participants; low-certainty evidence) and probably results in little to no difference in all-cause mortality at maximum follow-up (93 months) (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.03; 1 study, 97 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). The trial reported a mean quality-adjusted survival MD of 1.25 quality-adjusted life years (QALY) (95% CI 1.08 to 1.42) for participants randomised to ALPPS, and MD 1.11 QALY (95% CI 0.94 to 1.27) for participants randomised to two-stage hepatectomy, with an estimated MD between the groups of 0.14 QALY (95% CI -0.32 to 0.60). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of ALPPS, compared with two-stage hepatectomy, on health-related quality of life (MD 0.14, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.54; 1 study, 97 participants; very low-certainty evidence) (maximal follow-up: two years) and on the rate of serious adverse events (maximal follow-up: 30 days) (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.74; 1 study, 72 participants; very low-certainty evidence). ALPPS probably results in little to no difference in the overall survival of people with colorectal liver metastases (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.24; 1 study, 97 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) (median 93 months) and results in little to no difference in disease-free survival (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.59 to 1.40; 1 study, 97 participants; low-certainty evidence) (median 93 months), but probably results in a large increase in resection rates (RR 1.60, 95% CI 1.24 to 2.07; 1 study, 97 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) (maximum follow-up: eight weeks), compared with two-stage hepatectomy. We downgraded the certainty of evidence for risk of bias, indirectness, and imprecision.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence derives from data from only one randomised clinical trial, with a low number of participants and events. We are very uncertain about the effect of ALPPS on health-related quality of life and the rate of serious adverse events (30 days of follow-up) compared with two-stage hepatectomy. We are uncertain whether there is little to no difference between ALPPS and two-stage hepatectomy in perioperative mortality at 90 days after operation and in disease-free survival. ALPPS, compared with two-stage hepatectomy, probably results in little to no difference in all-cause mortality at maximum follow-up (93 months) and in overall survival of people with colorectal liver metastases (median 93 months), but probably results in a large increase in resection rates (eight-week follow-up). The certainty of the evidence for the presented outcomes was very low, low, or moderate. We lack randomised trials comparing these two strategies to identify the best approach for routine use in surgical practice. Evidence from low- and middle-income countries is lacking. The choice of ALPPS should carefully consider clinical characteristics of the patients. More high-quality trials with large numbers of participants are needed to provide information on the risks and benefits of ALPPS for people with colorectal liver metastases.

FUNDING: This review does not have dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Protocol: published 08 March 2022, available in the Cochrane Library at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD014608.

articles.title: Air versus supplemental oxygen for resuscitation of term or late preterm infants at birth.
authors: Supported by the Cochrane Neonatal Review Group
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Approximately 1% to 5% of newly born infants require some form of respiratory support, including supplemental oxygen for the respiratory transition immediately after birth. Despite a long-standing debate, the optimal concentration of oxygen at initiation of resuscitation of late preterm and term infants immediately after birth is still unknown.

OBJECTIVES: Primary objective To assess the benefits and harms of air compared with supplemental oxygen for resuscitation of term or late preterm infants at birth in reducing rates of mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI). Secondary objectives To assess whether the benefits and harms of air compared with supplemental oxygen differ according to different oxygen concentrations, gestational age (GA), whether oxygen was titrated to saturation targets and the income of the study country.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, two trials registries, Epistemonikos and the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ) up to 12 January 2026. We checked reference lists of included studies and other publications related to the topic of this review, and conducted forward/backward citation searching.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-RCTs or cluster-RCTs in term and late preterm infants who received respiratory support at birth comparing air with any supplemental oxygen. We excluded studies of oxygen saturation targeting, studies not taking place in the delivery room and studies of infants with antenatally diagnosed congenital anomalies.

OUTCOMES: Our outcomes of interest were all-cause mortality prior to discharge, in-hospital hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) (Sarnat stage II to III), post-discharge moderate to severe NDI based on pre-specified criteria, number of days on invasive (endotracheal) respiratory support, length of hospitalisation (days), all-cause mortality of infants followed beyond hospital discharge and moderate to severe NDI based on best available data.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool to assess risk of bias.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesised results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible. We calculated risk ratio (RR) and risk difference, each with its 95% confidence interval (CI), for categorical outcomes. We used a fixed-effect model to combine data for meta-analysis. Where this was not possible due to the nature of the data, we synthesised results by summarising any available effect estimates. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included a total of 12 studies with 2054 participants. The included studies enrolled term (born at a gestational age of 37 weeks 0 days to 43 weeks 6 days) and late preterm (born at a gestational age of 35 weeks 0 days to 36 weeks 6 days) infants who received any form of invasive (endotracheal) or non-invasive respiratory support at birth.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Using air compared to supplemental oxygen for resuscitation of term and late preterm infants may reduce all-cause mortality prior to discharge (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.91; I² = 0%; 10 studies, 1879 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence suggests that using air compared to supplemental oxygen for resuscitation of term and late preterm infants results in little to no difference in in-hospital HIE stage II to III (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.10; I² = 0%; 5 studies, 1384 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence suggests that using air compared to supplemental oxygen for resuscitation of term and late preterm infants results in little to no difference in all-cause mortality among infants followed beyond hospital discharge (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.16; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 668 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of using air compared to supplemental oxygen for resuscitation of term and late preterm infants on moderate to severe NDI based on best available data (RR 1.24, 95% CI 0.74 to 2.10; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 414 participants; very low-certainty evidence). None of the studies reported the following outcomes: moderate to severe NDI after at least 12 months' postnatal age as defined in the protocol, the number of days on invasive (endotracheal) respiratory support and the length of hospitalisation (days). Overall, the risk of bias was high for most studies.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: The use of air compared to 100% oxygen may reduce all-cause mortality prior to discharge, but there may be little to no difference in HIE stage II to III and NDI at 12 months or later based on best available data. No study reported moderate to severe NDI after at least 12 months' postnatal age, the number of days on invasive respiratory support or the length of hospitalisation. All 12 included studies compared air with 100% oxygen without titration to available oxygen saturation targets. Therefore, we are unable to draw conclusions about the optimal starting oxygen concentration when titration is available. Subgroup analyses based on gestational ages were not possible. There were no differences between studies from high-income and low- and middle-income countries.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Protocol available via DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD014781.

articles.title: Community-Level Inequalities and Risk Factors for Incident Oral Frailty.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oral frailty, characterized by tooth loss, chewing difficulty, and swallowing problems, has been associated with adverse health outcomes in older adults. However, longitudinal evidence on community-level inequalities and determinants of incident oral frailty remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: This cohort study aimed to examine community-level inequalities in the incidence of oral frailty and identify individual- and municipality-level factors associated with its onset among older adults in Japan.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 42,987 participants aged ≥65 y who completed the Japan Gerontological Evaluation Study surveys in 2019 and 2022. Oral frailty was determined using a validated prediction model including age, number of teeth, chewing difficulty, and choking. Individual-level variables included sociodemographic, health status, and social capital indicators. Municipality-level variables included population density, aggregated social capital, and the presence of prefectural or municipal dental health ordinances. Modified multilevel Poisson regression was used to estimate incidence rate ratios.

RESULTS: The incidence of oral frailty varied across municipalities, ranging from 17.1% to 33.3%. In the fully adjusted multilevel model, individual-level factors significantly associated with a higher risk of incident oral frailty were male sex; being widowed, divorced, or never married; lower educational attainment; lower equivalent income; smoking history; current illness; and lack of social cohesion (P < 0.05). At the municipality level, residing in urban, semi-urban, or rural-agricultural areas was associated with a lower risk of incident oral frailty compared with metropolitan area residency. Although not statistically significant in all models, higher municipality-level civic participation tended to be associated with a lower risk of incident oral frailty.

CONCLUSION: Community-level inequalities in the incidence of oral frailty are driven by both individual vulnerabilities and municipality-level factors. Notably, higher municipality-level civic participation tended to be associated with a lower incidence of oral frailty. Effective prevention requires comprehensive strategies that address socioeconomic factors and promote community-level civic participation.Knowledge Transfer Statement:This nationwide cohort study demonstrates that community-level inequalities in the incidence of oral frailty are substantial. They are largely explained not only by modifiable individual socioeconomic factors but also by municipality-level civic participation. These findings highlight the importance of integrating individual risk-based prevention with community strategies that may contribute to reducing oral frailty and related oral health disparities in aging populations.

articles.title: Learning Curve and Safety Analysis After 170 Robot-Assisted Cases in Thoracic Surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) is becoming increasingly popular due to technological advancements that enhance surgical outcomes. RATS was introduced at The Ottawa Hospital in 2022. This study aims to assess surgeon performance over time by analyzing learning curves for surgical efficiency and evaluating safety.

METHODS: Ethics approval was obtained for a prospective registry of all robotic cases. We analyzed 170 consecutive RATS procedures (April 2022 to November 2024) and 340 time-matched video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) procedures. Descriptive statistics were calculated in Excel. Learning curves and operative times for lobectomies and anterior mediastinal resections were assessed using CUSUM analysis in R, with console time as a surrogate. Safety was evaluated using the Ottawa Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality schema for adverse events.

RESULTS: The mean console time for all cases (N = 144) was 126 min, with a mean docking time of 24 min. For both lobectomies and anterior mediastinal resections, the acquisition of procedural efficiency was achieved after 20 cases and 7 cases, respectively. Safety outcomes were comparable to VATS, with most (n = 43, 73%) being grade II prolonged air leak (n = 19, 32%). Conversions to VATS occurred in 14 cases (8%), primarily due to complex anatomy, with only 3 cases (2%) converted to open. No conversions were done urgently.

CONCLUSIONS: The introduction of RATS is safe, with procedure efficiency being achieved within a reasonable number of cases.

articles.title: [When machines estimate kidney function and predict risk: Clinical applications of machine learning].
articles.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence, and particularly machine learning, is rapidly expanding in medicine. In nephrology, these approaches have generated growing interest owing to the availability of large clinical, biological, and administrative datasets, as well as the need for more accurate assessment of kidney function and changes over time. Two major areas of application have emerged: estimation of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and prediction of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. Initial studies focused on improving GFR estimation through supervised learning algorithms such as artificial neural networks, random forests, and ensemble methods. Although several studies reported encouraging results, recent large multicenter studies suggest that machine learning provides only marginal improvements over modern equations such as EKFC or CKD-EPI when the same clinical and biological variables are used. These findings indicate that current limitations in GFR estimation are more likely attributable to the information provided by available biomarkers than to the predictive capacity of the algorithms themselves. In contrast, machine learning appears particularly well suited for predicting kidney disease progression. By integrating numerous clinical and laboratory variables, these models can identify patients at high risk of rapid kidney function decline or kidney failure. Nevertheless, only a limited number of models have demonstrated a clear clinical advantage over established prediction tools such as the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE). This review summarizes current applications of machine learning for GFR estimation and CKD progression prediction, discusses their strengths and limitations, and highlights future directions for their integration into nephrology practice.

articles.title: [Cold ischemia time in kidney transplantation: From reduction to personalization].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cold ischemia time is a modifiable determinant of kidney transplant outcomes. Minimizing its duration remains a major goal, although allocation, transportation, and organizational constraints make some of this time unavoidable.

METHODS: We reviewed the literature published in PubMed over the past five years, supplemented by relevant landmark studies and institutional recommendations.

RESULTS: Prolonged cold ischemia is primarily associated with delayed graft function and, to a lesser extent, impaired long-term graft survival. Its impact varies according to donor and recipient characteristics. Prediction models can now estimate graft failure risk across different cold ischemia times for a given donor-recipient pair. Recent data on hypothermic machine perfusion further suggest that preservation strategies may mitigate the consequences of prolonged cold ischemia.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Personalizing cold ischemia could help identify situations in which its reduction should be prioritized and provide additional information for organ allocation and clinical decision-making. However, the moderate performance of currently available models and the lack of prospective validation preclude their use as standalone decision-making tools. Cold ischemia should therefore remain as short as possible, while its expected consequences could increasingly be assessed based on the characteristics of the donor-recipient pair and the graft preservation strategy used.

articles.title: Embolization of the middle meningeal artery for non-acute subdural hematoma.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of the embolization of the middle meningeal artery for non-acute subdural hematoma in adults. Secondary objectives To assess equity-related issues, including sex and gender, through subgroup analyses comparing the intervention's effects between male and female subjects, between younger and older adults, and across different pre-event functional status.

articles.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Typical Flutter Ablation: Risk-Stratified Monitoring Using Implantable Loop Recorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial flutter and atrial fibrillation (AF) arise from a common arrhythmogenic atrial substrate and frequently coexist in the same patient over the course of their lifetime. We aimed to examine the true incidence and risk factors associated with new-onset AF after successful typical atrial flutter ablation in a real-world population.

METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults who underwent atrial flutter ablation and received an implantable loop recorder (ILR) between 2019 and 2024 as part of a systematic post-ablation monitoring practice. Demographic and clinical variables were collected from the electronic medical record system. Cox proportional-hazards models and multivariable logistic regression were employed to identify independent predictors of AF, while the cumulative incidence of AF was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and clinically relevant risk thresholds were subsequently derived.

RESULTS: Among 95 patients (mean age 69.5 ± 7.9 years; 77.9% male; mean CHA2DS2-VASc 3.3) followed for a median of 44.7 months (IQR 34.5-49.0), AF was detected in 61 (64.2%). By Kaplan-Meier estimation the cumulative incidence of AF was 30% at 3 months, 46% at 1 year, and 58% at 2 years; the median time to detection among affected patients was 124 days (IQR 13-385). Patients with detected AF had a larger left atrial volume index (LAVI; 35.2 vs. 28.2 mL/m2, p<0.001) and lower LVEF (53.1% vs. 59.6%, p<0.001) as well as higher incidence of heart failure (p = 0.032). LAVI (adjusted OR 1.10 per mL/m2, 95% CI 1.03-1.17; p = 0.006) and a reduced LVEF (≤50%; adjusted OR 9.2, 95% CI 1.9-44.5; p = 0.006) were independent predictors (AUC 0.79), and both remained independent in a Cox model (LAVI adjusted HR 1.04 per mL/m2; LVEF ≤50% adjusted HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.3-3.9). A LAVI threshold of ≥26 mL/m2 functioned as a rule-out (sensitivity 92%), whereas LVEF ≤50% functioned as a rule-in (specificity 94%, PPV 92%); no single threshold or combination achieved both high sensitivity and high specificity. On stratified analysis the 2-year cumulative incidence of AF was 70% versus 20% above and below the LAVI threshold (log-rank p<0.001) and 73% versus 53% by the LVEF threshold (p = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Continuous post-ablation monitoring revealed AF in roughly two-thirds of patients after flutter ablation, often emerging several months following the procedure. More advanced atrial remodeling and impaired ventricular function were independent predictors of higher risk, providing practical and accessible thresholds to guide clinical decisions about which patients warrant prolonged rhythm surveillance and anticoagulation reinitiation after flutter ablation.

articles.title: Predictors of b/tsDMARDs discontinuation and treatment response in psoriatic arthritis: results from the British Society for Rheumatology Psoriatic Arthritis Register (BSR-PsA).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite advances in biologic and targeted synthetic DMARDs (b/tsDMARDs), many patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) experience suboptimal responses and discontinue therapy. We aimed, in a real-world registry, to identify predictors of b/tsDMARD discontinuation and treatment response.

METHODS: Patients commencing b/tsDMARD therapy were identified from the British Society for Rheumatology Psoriatic Arthritis Register (BSR‑PsA). Clinical and patient‑reported measures were collected at treatment start. Cox regression identified predictors of drug discontinuation using multiple imputation with predictive mean matching to handle missing data, and logistic regression identified predictors of achieving 12-month Minimal Disease Activity (MDA), ACR50 and PsARC response.

RESULTS: Eight-hundred and fifteen participants were included; 40% male, median age 51 years, with high disease activity (median DAPSA 33.5; PASDAS 5.9). At censoring (01‑Aug‑2025), 65% remained on their index therapy (median exposure 31 months) with discontinuation primarily due to inefficacy (55%) or intolerance (26%). Patients commencing PDE4 inhibition experienced more than a doubling in the risk of discontinuation, compared to those starting TNF inhibitors (Hazard Ratio: 2.25; 95%CI: 1.45-3.50), while no major differences were observed with other modes of action. At 12-months, 24% achieved MDA, 24% ACR50, and 49% PsARC. Based on imputed outcomes, men, younger individuals, and those who were employed were consistently more likely to achieve treatment response, while poorer baseline clinical or patient‑reported measures predicted non‑response.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment persistence and response in PsA remain a problem and are strongly influenced by demographic factors and baseline disease severity. A better understanding of predictors of non-response may aid future risk stratification.

articles.title: Prosthesis-patient mismatch after surgical aortic valve replacement with aortic annular enlargement in small aortic annuli.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Aortic annular enlargement (AAE) during surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is performed to facilitate implantation of larger prostheses in patients with small aortic annuli and mitigate prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). However, the clinical impact of residual PPM after AAE remains uncertain.

METHODS: All adult patients who underwent SAVR with AAE for small aortic annuli were retrospectively identified from a prospectively maintained institutional database (2011-2024). PPM was defined based on indexed effective orifice area thresholds derived from published reference tables. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and secondary outcomes included heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and longitudinal echocardiographic performance.

RESULTS: A total of 169 patients were identified (age 68 years [61-73], 119 female [70.4%]). Median STS risk was 2% [1-4%], and preoperative mean gradient was 45.0 mmHg [36.8-57.2]. Overall median valve size after AAE was 23 mm (21-25), and PPM occurred in 25 patients (14.8%), including 24 (14.2%) with moderate and 1 (0.6%) with severe PPM. Early outcomes were comparable between PPM and no-PPM groups: postoperative stroke 0 (0%) vs. 3 (2.1%, p > 0.999), and 30-day mortality 1 (4.0%) vs. 5 (3.5%, p > 0.999). Over 4 years follow-up, survival (HR 0.94, 95%CI 0.40-2.21, p = 0.896) and freedom from HF hospitalization (HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.45-2.95, p = 0.760) were similar. Echocardiographic trends showed no differences in LVEF (p = 0.123) or mean gradient (p = 0.879) during follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with small aortic annuli undergoing SAVR with annular enlargement, the incidence of PPM was low, and residual PPM did not adversely impact early postoperative outcomes, mid-term survival, or valve hemodynamics.

articles.title: Conventional Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia Ablation: 16-Year Acute Outcomes and Pacemaker Requirement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study characterized the acute success, causes of failure, and index-hospitalization permanent pacemaker (PPM) rate of conventional (fluoroscopy-guided, without 3D electroanatomic mapping [3D-EAM]) AVNRT ablation over 16 years at a single center.

METHODS: Consecutive adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent conventional ablation for AVNRT between January 2010 and May 2026 were retrospectively evaluated. All procedures were performed by a senior operator or under the direct supervision of a senior operator. Acute success was defined as non-inducibility of AVNRT under isoproterenol. The primary endpoints were index-hospitalization PPM and acute success. Rates are presented with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Of 1169 SVT cases, 814 (69.6%) underwent AVNRT ablation (age 46.9 ± 13.0 years; 67.0% female). Acute success was 90.3% (735/814; 95% CI 88.07-92.14). Causes of failure (n = 79): anatomic limitation 40 (50.6%), persistent inducibility 29 (36.7%), AV conduction disturbance 8 (10.1%), patient intolerance 1, atrial fibrillation 1. Anatomic limitation denotes ablation deliberately terminated to protect AV conduction rather than technical failure. High-grade AV block developed in 8 patients (0.98%); it resolved spontaneously in 5, and a PPM was implanted during the index hospitalization in 3 (0.37%; 95% CI 0.13-1.08). In the three PPM patients, ventricular pacing remained 100% at follow-up. Acute success showed no significant univariable association with age or sex.

CONCLUSIONS: Conventional AVNRT ablation can be performed at an experienced center with high success (90.3%) and a low PPM rate (0.37%). While some AV block events resolved in the laboratory, those that persisted led to a PPM requirement, and AV conduction was not regained in these patients. These findings provide operator-homogeneous real-world reference data from a tertiary referral center in Türkiye.

articles.title: Emerging advances in vascular Behçet syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Vascular involvement is one of the main contributors to morbidity and mortality in Behçet syndrome. This review summarizes recent advances in the pathophysiology, imaging, and management of vascular Behçet syndrome.

RECENT FINDINGS: Single-cell and translational studies support a central role for vessel-wall inflammation, neutrophil extracellular traps, and endothelial dysfunction. Common femoral vein wall ultrasonography, pulmonary artery wall assessment, and other vessel-wall imaging modalities suggest that vascular involvement may be more widespread than previously recognized. However, their diagnostic utility requires standardization and prospective validation across different cohorts and assessors. The updated 2025 EULAR recommendations position monoclonal anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα) antibodies as first-line treatment options for both remission induction and maintenance across vascular manifestations. Anticoagulation is no longer restricted to refractory thrombosis, provided that bleeding-risk is assessed and pulmonary artery aneurysms are excluded.

SUMMARY: Prompt immunosuppressive treatment with monoclonal anti-TNFα antibodies is now recommended as a first-line option for vascular involvement. Longitudinal cohorts and controlled trials are needed to validate vessel-wall imaging modalities.

articles.title: Current management of Behçet syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize the most clinically relevant recent advances in the treatment of Behçet syndrome (BS), with emphasis on the updated 2025 EULAR recommendations and emerging evidence across different organ manifestations.

RECENT FINDINGS: The updated EULAR recommendations support earlier use of monoclonal TNF inhibitors (TNFi), particularly in severe ocular, vascular, and neurologic involvement, and favor their continued use for maintenance in selected major-organ disease. Recent randomized and comparative studies provide further support for TNFi in Behçet uveitis and vascular involvement. Newer agents, including PDE-4 inhibitors and JAK inhibitors (JAKi), have shown promising efficacy in mucocutaneous, gastrointestinal, ocular, vascular, and neurologic disease, although most evidence for JAKi remains derived from small uncontrolled studies. Ustekinumab has also shown encouraging results in refractory intestinal BS. The role of anticoagulation in vascular BS remains uncertain.

SUMMARY: Management of BS is increasingly organ- and risk-adapted, with earlier use of effective targeted therapies in patients at risk of irreversible damage. Despite encouraging results with several newer agents, comparative and high-quality evidence remains limited, highlighting the need for adequately powered studies with organ-specific outcomes.

articles.title: A plant-based diet attenuates hypertension-induced renal and hepatic stress: an exploratory study.
articles.abstract: Hypertension drives progressive renal dysfunction and hepatic injury. In this secondary analysis, we investigated whether a plant-based diet (PBD) could prevent and/or reverse hypertension-induced renal and hepatic insult. Four-week-old female spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) consumed a refined control diet or PBD comprising 28% fruits, vegetables, nuts and legumes, while normotensive Wistar-Kyoto rats consumed the control diet. After 24 weeks, a subset of control-fed SHRs switched to PBD for 12 weeks. Despite sustained hypertension, exploratory analyses indicated that PBD may reduce serum urea during prevention (3.84 ± 1.12 vs. 3.03 ± 0.80 mmol L-1; P = 0.0263) and treatment (4.37 ± 1.80 vs. 3.11 ± 0.93 mmol L-1; P = 0.0248). Estimated glomerular filtration rate may also improve during treatment (1319 ± 277 vs. 1599 ± 432 µL min-1; P = 0.0488). However, this did not reach significance during the prevention phase (P = 0.0518). PBD prevented and reversed elevations in serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT; prevention: 32.61 ± 3.23 vs. 22.50 ± 3.52 U L-1; treatment: 33.34 ± 2.87 vs. 24.48 ± 3.99 U L-1; both P < 0.0001). Further, PBD increased renal antioxidant enzyme expression and reduced hepatic tumor necrosis factor-α during prevention. Qualitatively, PBD may attenuate left kidney glomerular collagen accumulation. These findings warrant additional translational studies testing minimally refined PBDs, with potential pilot clinical studies as an adjunctive therapy in adults with hypertension.

articles.title: Evolution of medical thoracoscopy - 100 years on.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: More than a century after Jacobaeus, medical thoracoscopy is being reshaped by demands for precise pleural diagnosis, adequate tissue for molecular characterisation, combined local treatment and efficient care. This review uses its historical evolution to examine current indications, instruments, biopsy strategies, anaesthetic design and service models, with emphasis on recent evidence.

RECENT FINDINGS: Rigid and semirigid thoracoscopy achieve similarly high diagnostic yield but differ in access, force transmission, tissue size, pain and sedative requirements. Recent studies favour needs-led sampling: standard forceps for most visible lesions, with cryobiopsy or advanced tools when depth, invasion, fibrosis or molecular profiling is limiting. Trials support selective rather than routine use of pleurodesis, indwelling catheters, regional blocks, high-flow oxygen or first-line thoracoscopy for pleural infection. Image enhancement, artificial intelligence, hybrid instruments and single-use platforms remain promising but incompletely validated.

SUMMARY: Medical thoracoscopy should remain a targeted pleural procedure that preserves spontaneous ventilation while integrating diagnosis, adequate tissue acquisition, selected therapy and pathway efficiency. Technology and anaesthetic intensity should be matched to clinical need and adopted only when they improve measurable patient or system outcomes.

articles.title: Persistent air leak: from evaluation to management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Persistent air leak remains a major source of morbidity after lung resection and in secondary spontaneous pneumothorax, yet management is still commonly driven by duration rather than mechanism. This review examines recent advances in objective air leak assessment, pressure-dependent leak physiology, localization, and phenotype-directed intervention.

RECENT FINDINGS: Digital drainage improves reproducible measurement of air leak trajectory, although no universal threshold predicts healing or permits tube removal. Pressure-dependent air leaks related to residual pleural space or lung-thoracic cavity mismatch may resolve after reducing drainage intensity or removing the tube in selected patients. Computed tomography and ventilation SPECT/CT can support anatomical and functional localization when targeted treatment is planned. Recent studies support individualized low-pressure drainage, autologous blood patch or glucose pleurodesis, and bronchoscopic valves, spigots, blood patching, sealants, or plugs, but most comparative evidence remains limited and heterogeneous.

SUMMARY: Persistent air leak should be classified by air leak trajectory, lung expansion, pleural pressure behavior, anatomical source, infection, and operative fitness. Phenotype-directed escalation may reduce unnecessary procedures while identifying patients who require early bronchoscopic or surgical source control.

articles.title: Clinical burden of haemophilia in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates: real-world insights from the Malaffi platform.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: This study aims to understand the clinical burden of haemophilia by assessing the real-world patient profile, treatment, and healthcare utilization of people with haemophilia (PwH) in Abu Dhabi. A retrospective observational study was conducted using electronic health records from the Malaffi database (patient health information platform). Patients with a diagnosis of haemophilia A (ICD-10 D66) or haemophilia B (ICD-10 D67) between 1 January 2021, and 14 April 2023, and with documented haemophilia-related treatment, were included. Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, comorbidities, treatment patterns, and healthcare encounters were analysed using descriptive statistics. A total of 146 PwH were identified, 83% (n = 121) presented with haemophilia A. Paediatric patients comprised 65% (n = 95) with mean age 6.3 ± 5.6 years and adults 35% (n = 51) with average age of 30.4 ± 10.1 years. Pain and swelling were the most common symptoms documented in both groups (77% paediatric; 88% adult). The most frequently identified comorbid conditions include joint/arthritic conditions among adults (75%) and anaemia among the paediatric patients (61%). PwH recorded 6052 healthcare encounters during the study period with a median of 10 visits per PwH per year. The ordered medications included 1422 prescriptions, and factor VIII (862 prescriptions) was the most prescribed medication. The study provides robust evidence on the clinical burden and intense utilization of healthcare resource of PwH in Abu Dhabi and offer foundation for future research and policy initiatives aimed at optimizing care delivery and resource allocation for PwH.

articles.title: Representation and differentiation of audiology interventions within the international classification of health interventions.
articles.journal: Health information management : journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Standardised intervention coding supports service visibility, reimbursement, resource planning and health-system analytics. The International Classification of Health Interventions (ICHIs) provides a standardised framework for representing health interventions, but its ability to capture the breadth and clinical specificity of contemporary audiology practice requires evaluation.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the extent to which contemporary audiology interventions can be represented and differentiated within ICHI and identify limitations in coding granularity that may affect health information management, service reporting and reimbursement.

METHOD: An inventory of audiology interventions was derived from historical and current South African tariff schedules, scope-of-practice documents, university curricula and contemporary clinical practice. A total of 105 interventions spanning hearing and vestibular assessment, electrophysiology, device-related procedures, and counselling and rehabilitation were independently mapped to ICHI using a structured coding rubric aligned with the Target-Action-Means framework. Interrater agreement was calculated for a predefined subset.

RESULTS: All included interventions could be represented within ICHI. Most (92.3%) demonstrated direct one-to-one alignment with an ICHI stem code. The remainder required approximate ('best-fit'), postcoordination, or composite coding using multiple descriptors and/or extension codes. Clinically distinct interventions frequently converged under identical stems, particularly within rehabilitation, counselling, device management and tele-audiology. This convergence reduced coding granularity and differentiation of clinical intent, service complexity and resource utilisation.

CONCLUSION: ICHI provides broad structural coverage of contemporary audiology interventions; however, limited granularity constrains its utility for detailed health-system reporting, reimbursement modelling and service evaluation. Greater differentiation within rehabilitation- and technology-related categories is warranted to better represent contemporary audiology practice and support person-centred ear and hearing care within universal health coverage frameworks.Implications for health information management practice:High-level ICHI stems may obscure clinically meaningful variation in audiology services, reducing data precision for funding, workload measurement, service evaluation and national reporting. Implementation guidance and standardised composite coding protocols may improve specificity where existing stems are insufficient. Identified classification gaps may inform formal submissions to the World Health Organisation Family of International Classifications Network. Improved specificity could strengthen interoperability, secondary data analytics, reimbursement modelling, and evidence-based hearing-care planning.

articles.title: Diabetic retinopathy in pregnancy.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of development and progression of diabetic retinopathy. This review examines the mechanisms underlying diabetic retinopathy progression during pregnancy, established and emerging risk factors for diabetic retinopathy progression, current screening strategies, and management options for sight-threatening disease.

RECENT FINDINGS: The severity of retinopathy at conception, glycaemic control, duration of diabetes and hypertension are established predictors of diabetic retinopathy progression during pregnancy. Recent data suggest that patients with no retinopathy on initial screening have a very low risk of diabetic retinopathy progression, and further screening may not be indicated during pregnancy in this cohort. Pan retinal photocoagulation remains the mainstay of treatment for sight-threatening proliferative disease, while the use of intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy remains challenging because of limited safety data. Evidence regarding the postpartum course of diabetic retinopathy remains limited.

SUMMARY: Pregnancy represents a period of increased retinal risk in women with preexisting diabetes, although this risk is not uniform. Baseline retinopathy status, duration of diabetes, extent of glycaemic control and hypertensive disease may provide a framework for future risk-stratified screening. Further prospective studies are required to determine whether surveillance can safely be individualised, and to clarify the role of anti-VEGF therapy and postpartum monitoring.

articles.title: Best clinical practice in kidney transplant and cancer clinics.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Transplant onconephrology is an evolving subspeciality within nephrology that focuses on the interaction between cancer and the kidney. The goal of this subspecialty is to provide optimal care for people with cancers who are risk or develop cancer-related kidney complications or nephrotoxicity from cancer therapeutics. This goal is accomplished through application of increasing knowledge about transplant nephrology and oncology.

RECENT FINDINGS: People with a history of malignancy who are evaluated for kidney transplant need careful risk assessment to inform candidacy, immunosuppression management and prevent post-transplant recurrence. Post-transplant malignancies occur frequently and are a leading cause of death in kidney transplant recipients. People with pre- and post-transplant cancers experience significant stressors and healthcare demands, and benefit from multidisciplinary clinical care to address their high-risk conditions.

SUMMARY: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the best practices of outpatient clinical care for the growing population of high-risk patients with cancer before and after kidney transplant based on clinical experience and available data.

articles.title: Challenges in obese liver transplant recipients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The global obesity epidemic has significantly altered the epidemiology of chronic liver disease and liver transplantation, with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis emerging as a rapidly increasing indication for liver transplantation worldwide. Obesity in liver transplantation candidates is frequently accompanied by sarcopenia, frailty, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic comorbidities, creating complex perioperative and long-term management challenges. This review summarizes contemporary evidence regarding assessment, pretransplant preparation, perioperative management, and long-term outcomes of obese liver transplant recipients, while highlighting evolving therapeutic strategies and unresolved clinical questions.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent literature emphasizes that BMI alone inadequately characterizes obesity in cirrhosis, with body composition, sarcopenic obesity, visceral adiposity, and frailty emerging as important prognostic factors. Structured prehabilitation, lifestyle modification, incretin-based pharmacotherapy, and selective metabolic bariatric surgery have shown promising results in carefully selected patients. Although obesity increases perioperative complexity and postoperative complications, carefully selected obese recipients can achieve graft and patient survival comparable to nonobese recipients.

SUMMARY: Obesity should not be considered a contraindication to liver transplantation. Individualized recipient assessment, coordinated perioperative optimization, and long-term metabolic surveillance are essential to improve outcomes. Future research should refine obesity assessment beyond BMI and clarify the optimal integration of pharmacologic and surgical weight-loss strategies in liver transplantation candidates before and after transplantation.

articles.title: Peritoneal dialysis catheter dysfunction: when can the catheter be rescued?
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) catheter dysfunction is frequently treated as a generic access failure, although the appropriate response depends on the underlying mechanism. This review summarizes a practical, mechanism-directed approach to reversible medical causes, image-guided salvage, surgical revision, and catheter replacement.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent guidelines and reviews support early exclusion of infection and acute abdominal pathology, deliberate treatment of constipation and fibrin, and early abdominal radiography when flow is impaired. Catheterography and fluoroscopic manipulation can restore selected migrated or partially obstructed catheters. Still, immediate technical success does not ensure durable function when omental wrap, adhesions, fixed kinking, or unfavorable catheter geometry is present. Observational series also support same-session removal and reinsertion for noninfectious mechanical failure and for narrowly selected infection-related indications. Laparoscopic revision remains the definitive treatment for structural abnormalities.

SUMMARY: A successful PD access program requires a written rescue pathway that quickly transitions from reversible causes to mechanism-specific interventions. The meaningful outcome is not radiographic catheter position alone, but rapid return to the prescribed PD regimen while minimizing temporary hemodialysis exposure, repeated emergency visits, and avoidable technique failure.

articles.title: Mapping the Distribution of Autism From the Census of Northern Ireland, 2021.
articles.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
articles.abstract: This piece examines the data and preliminary geographical patterns yielded from a question on autism included in the Census of Northern Ireland in 2021. There are two objectives here: (a) to present summary statistics, indicators of spatial clustering, and assess the correlation of autism with other census-based socioeconomic indicators, and (b) to assess the opportunities and limitations offered by this dataset in light of international work on the spatial distribution of autism. This exercise reveals evidence of spatial clustering and patterning, particularly within urban areas (the City of Belfast especially), and strong differences between urban Belfast and the Rest of Northern Ireland. Explorations of socioeconomic correlates of autism show an association between autism and family structure, education and labour market status.Lay AbstractA Geography of Autism? Preliminary Findings From the Northern Ireland Census, 2021There is a lot of research coming out about Autism and neurodiversity. Part of that research includes studies using maps and other tools from geography. These maps allow us to look at where Autism rates might be high or low, and to see if there are any patterns. Do places with high or low rates of Autism cluster together? Are places with high Autism rates closer to places where people or families who suspect neurodivergence might go to get an assessment? Once we know this, we can then start to look at other features of places, like the percentage of people unemployed, living in poverty, lone parent families or levels of education. This lets us figure out whether certain features are correlated with Autism. Are areas with higher percentages of lone parent families more likely to also have high Autism rates? This is important because past studies might have looked at environmental influences in Autism such as whether an area was near a busy motorway or a source of environmental contamination. I am interested in what a region like Northern Ireland can tell us about why certain areas might have higher rates of Autism. This will let us figure out more about how detection works, where services might be needed and how information on neurodivergence might spread within certain types of community more so than others.

articles.title: Decoding the cellular and paracrine landscape of epicardial adipose tissue-myocardial crosstalk in coronary artery disease.
Early sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor initiation is associated with improved cardiovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes and acute coronary syndrome.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, but the optimal timing of initiation in those with acute coronary syndrome is not known. This study aims to assess if early therapy at discharge is superior to delayed or no therapy in reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events.

METHODS: This retrospective, observational cohort study included individuals with type 2 diabetes admitted with an acute coronary syndrome at a single regional heart centre between July 2018 and December 2023. Individuals were stratified into three groups based on the timing of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor initiation: (1) discharge group (initiated at hospital discharge), (2) post-discharge group (initiated after discharge during follow-up) and (3) no therapy group. The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major adverse cardiovascular event.

RESULTS: Among 970 eligible patients (median age, 70.2 years [IQR, 61.0-78.5 years]; 73.9% male), the median follow-up duration was 29.9 months (IQR, 20.1, 43.0 months). Compared with the discharge group, the risk of primary outcome was significantly higher in both the post-discharge group (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.50; 95% CI [1.13, 1.99], p = 0.005) and the no therapy group (aHR, 1.65; 95% CI [1.24, 2.20]; p < 0.001). Analyses were adjusted using clone-censor-weight methods and multivariable Cox-proportional hazards models.

CONCLUSIONS: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor therapy at hospital discharge was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes and acute coronary syndrome.

articles.title: Measles transmission-related epidemiological parameter estimates: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: With the recent resurgence of global measles outbreaks, it is crucial to understand measles transmission dynamics to guide timely and effective public health responses and parameterize infectious disease models for accurate outbreak projections. This systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive resource of measles transmission-related epidemiological parameters. A search was conducted from inception to 14 May 2024. English and French primary studies of transmission-related epidemiological parameters were included, and standard systematic review methodology was followed. Evidence was synthesized using random-effects meta-analyses and descriptive plots. Subgroup analyses by World Health Organization (WHO) region, population, decade, and quality of reporting were conducted to explore heterogeneity. Between 1910 and 2024, 1 209 estimates across 32 transmission-related epidemiological parameters from 612 studies were reported. Measles was characterized by a pooled incubation period (13.5 days, 95%CI 12.6-14.4; I2 = 95.9%), serial interval (12.4 days, 95%CI 11.5-13.4; I2 = 97.6%), symptom onset to hospitalization (4.8 days, 95%CI 3.7-5.8, I2 = 99.7%), and basic reproduction number median 11.5 (range of 0-57). This work is part of a global epidemic preparedness and response project to establish an accessible living Global Repository of Epidemiological Parameters aimed at reducing duplicative efforts in identifying and summarizing epidemiological parameters.

articles.title: Autism in a general adult mental health service in Ireland: prevalence, clinical presentation, and service use.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autistic adults experience high rates of co-occurring mental health difficulties, yet little is known about their representation within secondary adult mental health services. This study aimed to examine the actual prevalence and clinical presentation of autistic adults attending a community general adult mental health service in Ireland.

METHODS: A cross-sectional retrospective chart review was conducted in July 2023 within a community-based secondary mental health service serving a population of 92,610. Demographic characteristics, autism-related factors, diagnoses, self-harm/suicidality, and multidisciplinary service utilisation were extracted and analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics.

RESULTS: Forty autistic service users were identified among a total caseload of 1,270 (3.1%). The median age was 23 years, and 67.5% were male. Most autism diagnoses (65%) were made through Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services. Psychotic disorders were the most common psychiatric diagnosis (30%), followed by mood and anxiety disorders. Over half (52.5%) had a history of self-harm and/or suicidality, and 17.5% had required psychiatric inpatient admission. Although 95% were referred to at least one multidisciplinary team (MDT) service, 30% did not attend these appointments.

CONCLUSIONS: Autistic adults represented a small proportion of service users despite their high burden of mental health difficulties, suggesting possible underrecognition of autism and barriers to accessing secondary mental health services. Those receiving care demonstrated complex clinical needs, including high rates of psychosis and suicidality. Improving autism recognition, developing integrated care pathways, and adapting multidisciplinary services to better meet autistic adults' needs are essential to delivering equitable mental healthcare.

articles.title: Predicting Return to Play After Achilles Tendon Injury in National Football League Players Using Machine Learning.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: BackgroundNational Football League (NFL) players frequently experience Achilles tendon (AT) injuries. However, there is mixed evidence regarding factors influencing return to play (RTP) after AT injury. The objective of this study is to develop machine learning models to predict NFL players' likelihood of RTP within 1 year of an AT tear.

HYPOTHESIS: Machine learning models can predict 1-year RTP status in NFL players following AT tear.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective Cohort.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted to identify NFL players who sustained unilateral AT injuries from 2004 to 2024. Player demographics and performance data were recorded. Return to play was defined as generating playing statistics. Five machine learning models were developed: logistic regression, random forest classifier, XGBoost, Gaussian naive Bayes, and K-nearest neighbors. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 were used to assess model performance.ResultsOne hundred seventy-six NFL players were identified with an AT injury. One hundred eight players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 63 players did not (class 0). In the full cohort, injury etiology was the most influential feature associated with 1-year RTP, followed by pre-injury performance. Among the 99 players with a confirmed AT tear, 48 players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 51 players did not (class 0). Within the confirmed-tear cohort, draft round and games started were the leading predictors of 1-year RTP, which was best predicted by random forest with a mean accuracy of 0.69, precision of 0.68, recall of 0.70, and an F1-score of 0.69 for class 0.ConclusionMachine learning models that combine clinical and performance metrics of NFL athletes demonstrated potential for predicting 1-year RTP after AT injury and identifying factors associated with RTP.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Machine learning could be integrated into clinical decision-making and prognosis to refine rehabilitation approaches in NFL players.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3.

articles.title: Longitudinal changes in readily available inflammatory markers before and after switching to integrase inhibitor-based antiretroviral therapy in Virologically suppressed people living with HIV: A Nationwide real-world cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent immune activation and systemic inflammation remain key features of chronic HIV infection despite sustained virological suppression under antiretroviral therapy (ART), contributing to excess non-AIDS morbidity and mortality. Readily available markers from routine laboratory testing, including CD4/CD8 ratio, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), have been associated with systemic inflammation, but their evolution following ART switch remains insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize longitudinal changes in inflammatory markers before and after switching to integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based therapy in virologically suppressed people living with HIV (PLWH), and to explore differences between bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF) and dolutegravir/lamivudine (DTG/3TC).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal analysis within the AMACS cohort. Virologically suppressed adults on stable boosted PI- or NNRTI-based regimens who switched to INSTI-based therapy were included. Changes in CD4/CD8 ratio, NLR and PLR were evaluated before and after switch using mixed-effects models, with subgroup analyses by post-switch regimen.

RESULTS: Of 2178 potentially eligible participants, a total of 1641 individuals contributed to the primary longitudinal analysis of marker trajectories. PLR values were modestly lower at 6 and 12 months after the switch than at 6 months before the switch in both pre-switch ART groups. However, the differences between pre- and post-switch PLR slopes were not statistically significant. The CD4/CD8 ratio increased progressively over time with no evidence of significant acceleration following the switch, whereas NLR remained largely unchanged. In exploratory subgroup analyses, no consistent differences in inflammatory markers were observed between participants switching to B/F/TAF and those switching to DTG/3TC, while there was a dynamic pattern of NLR in the DTG/3TC subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: In virologically suppressed PLWH, modestly lower PLR values were observed after switching to INSTI-based therapy, whereas CD4/CD8 trajectories were consistent with ongoing immune recovery and NLR remained unchanged.

articles.title: Maternal Microvascular Calcium Sparks Are Reduced in Preeclampsia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal microvascular dysfunction is a hallmark of the hypertensive pregnancy disorder preeclampsia, but the mechanism(s) have not been fully defined. Within vascular smooth muscle cells, the principal pressure-induced vasodilatory pathway depends on localized Ca2+-release events from the sarcoplasmic reticulum ryanodine receptors (Ca2+ sparks), which stimulate BKCa (large-conductance Ca2+-activated potassium channels) to cause spontaneous transient outward currents and vasorelaxation. Here, the Ca2+ sparks-BKCa axis is assessed in preeclampsia for the first time.

METHODS: Pressurized omental resistance arteries from normotensive pregnant women and women with preeclampsia were imaged by high-speed spinning-disk laser confocal microscopy to assess Ca2+ sparks (20-110 mm Hg) and caffeine-evoked Ca2+ release (10 mmol/L; 80 mm Hg). Electrophysiology was used to assess spontaneous transient outward currents (-60 to 0 mV) and BKCa currents (-100 to +100 mV) in isolated vascular smooth muscle cells. A liquid chromatography-selected reaction monitoring-tandem mass spectrometry assay measured SERCA2 (sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase-2) and unphosphorylated/phosphorylated proteoforms of regulatory PLN (phospholamban). Vasoactive effects of the BKCa-dependent vasorelaxant HBD2 (human β-defensin-2; 0.01-10 nmol/L) were assessed by wire myography.

RESULTS: In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there was reduced Ca2+ spark frequency (P=1.1×10-10) and spontaneous transient outward current frequency (P=0.023). There was also reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ release in response to caffeine (P=0.0013), reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum refilling (P=2.0×10-4), and decreased ratio of SERCA2 to inhibitory unphosphorylated PLN (P=0.030), implicating increased SERCA2 inhibition. HBD2 (0.01-10 nmol/L) caused BKCa-dependent relaxation (P=4.6×10-10) of omental arteries without affecting Ca2+ spark frequency.

CONCLUSIONS: In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there is a striking reduction in Ca2+ spark frequency and spontaneous transient outward currents, likely secondary to increased inhibition of SERCA2 by unphosphorylated PLN and reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ load. These defects may provide novel therapeutic targets to restore physiological control of the vasculature. BKCa-mediated relaxation by HBD2 was independent of Ca2+ sparks, supporting vasodilatory strategies bypassing disrupted microvascular mechanisms in preeclampsia.

articles.title: KLHL3-Cab39 Disruption Drives WNK4-Independent Hyperkalemic Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Familial hyperkalemic hypertension, also known as pseudohypoaldosteronism type II (PHAII), is characterized by hypertension and hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis and involves dysregulation of the KLHL3 (Kelch-like 3)-cullin3 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, affecting WNK1/4 (with-no-lysine kinase 1/4)-mediated SPAK (Ste20-related proline/alanine-rich kinase)/OSR1 (oxidative stress response kinase 1)-NCC (Na+-Cl- cotransporter) signaling. How KLHL3 phosphorylation mutations modulate this pathway remains poorly defined.

METHODS: We generated knock-in mouse models expressing phosphomimetic (S486D) or phosphodefective (S486G) mutations at Klhl3 S486 (homologous to human S433). Blood pressure, serum and urine biochemistries, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, coimmunoprecipitation, in vitro ubiquitination assays, and molecular docking were performed. Klhl3 S486G mice were crossed with Wnk4-/- mice to test WNK4 dependence.

RESULTS: Both knock-in strains exhibited typical PHAII features despite unchanged KLHL3 levels, with enhanced SPAK/OSR1-NCC phosphorylation, increased Cab39 levels, and unchanged WNK1/4 expression. Under high-salt loading, Klhl3 S486 knock-in mice maintained severe PHAII phenotypes, with persistently elevated Cab39 and NCC levels despite decreased WNK4 expression. Critically, Wnk4 deletion failed to rescue PHAII phenotypes in Klhl3 S486G mice, demonstrating that Klhl3 S486 mutations drive PHAII independently of WNK4. In vitro, human KLHL3 S433D/S433G mutations reduced KLHL3-Cab39 association and Cab39 ubiquitination, with a corresponding increase in Cab39 abundance. Deletion mapping identified KLHL3 residues 428 to 437 and Cab39 residues 314 to 324 as key determinants of the KLHL3-Cab39 association.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the integrity of Ser486 itself, rather than its phosphorylation state, is required for KLHL3-mediated Cab39 ubiquitination and define a WNK4-independent PHAII mechanism driven by impaired Cab39 degradation and consequent SPAK/OSR1-Na+-Cl- cotransporter activation.

articles.title: Shared Genetics of Hypertension and Preeclampsia Converges on Immune Regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and preeclampsia are clinically distinct, yet biologically related conditions characterized by vascular dysfunction and elevated cardiovascular risk. Although genome-wide association studies have identified loci associated with blood pressure traits and preeclampsia, the functional mechanisms linking shared variants to gene regulation and clinical phenotypes remain unclear.

METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for hypertension, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and preeclampsia to identify shared variants (P≤1×10-4). Cis-expression quantitative trait loci analyses were performed in whole blood using RNA sequencing data from 180 Black women. Significant associations (false discovery rate ≤0.05) were evaluated for replication across vascular, metabolic, and endocrine tissues in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Associations between gene expression and blood pressure traits were also assessed.

RESULTS: We identified 4792 shared genome-wide association study variants, of which 4663 were tested in expression quantitative trait loci analyses, yielding 1837 significant variant-gene associations across 78 genes. Replication in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project confirmed 645 associations involving 24 genes, many showing cross-tissue regulatory effects. Three genes (C4B, HLA-C, and HLA-DQB1) demonstrated convergent evidence across genome-wide association study, gene regulation, and expression-trait analyses. C4B expression was positively associated with hypertension and systolic blood pressure, while HLA-C showed negative associations with hypertension, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure. HLA-DQB1 expression was specifically associated with diastolic blood pressure, suggesting trait-specific effects.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight immune-related pathways as key mediators linking hypertension and preeclampsia. Integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic data provides a framework for identifying functionally relevant loci and advancing mechanistic insights into cardiometabolic and pregnancy-related disorders.

articles.title: Effect of Baxdrostat on Cortisol Responsiveness in Hypertension: Phase 2 Results.
An injectable self-healing hydrogel with cytokine-regulating and antioxidant activities for accelerating diabetic wound repair.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds remain a formidable clinical challenge owing to persistent hyperglycemia, excessive oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and protracted inflammation. Herein, we developed a multifunctional hydrogel, designated QCS/4-FPBA/BC, integrating anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, injectable, and self-healing properties. The hydrogel was constructed using a quaternized chitosan (QCS) crosslinked with 4-formylphenylboronic acid (4-FPBA) via dynamic Schiff base and borate ester bonds, conferring favorable injectability and self-healing capacity, while the intrinsic quaternary ammonium cations of QCS endowed it with inherent antibacterial activity. Baicalein-cerium nanoparticles (BC NPs) were further loaded in situ into the hydrogel network to enable efficient and sustained scavenging of excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). As a multifunctional platform, the QCS/4-FPBA/BC hydrogel exhibited robust anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated macrophages, as shown by decreased TNF-α and IL-6 levels and increased IL-10 expression. It also influenced macrophage phenotype, reducing the M1-associated iNOS signal while augmenting the M2-associated CD206 signal. In addition, treatment with the hydrogel upregulated VEGF in HUVECs and elevated collagen I in L929 cells, indicating pro-angiogenic and pro-matrix-synthesis capabilities. With these combined attributes, including ROS scavenging, antimicrobial action, inflammatory cytokine rebalancing, and promotion of vascular and fibroblast functions, the QCS/4-FPBA/BC hydrogel offers a comprehensive strategy for diabetic wound management and holds great promise for improving healing outcomes.

articles.title: The art of public engagement in type 1 diabetes research.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Patient and public involvement (PPI) is increasingly recognised as an important component of research, while public engagement provides opportunities to communicate research and stimulate dialogue with wider audiences. In preclinical type 1 diabetes (T1D) research, complex scientific concepts can present particular barriers to engagement across different ages and experiences.

METHODS: We describe two creative public engagement initiatives-a colouring book and a glass art project-and discuss how PPI and lived-experience perspectives helped shape their development.

CONCLUSIONS: These examples illustrate how artistic approaches can make basic science more accessible and create opportunities for dialogue between researchers and people affected by T1D.

articles.title: Oral Health-Related Adverse Events of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As the clinical use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) continues to grow for the management of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal protection, noncirrhotic fatty liver disease, and weight management, their potential implications for oral health need to be considered.

OBJECTIVES: This study examined oral health-related adverse events (AEs) associated with GLP-1 RAs using postmarketing data from the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

METHODS: FAERS reports for available GLP-1 RAs, exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide, and tirzepatide, were screened from their initial market introduction through December 2025, identifying 364,274 total AE reports, of which 31,195 (8.6%) involved oral, craniofacial, or dental manifestations.

RESULTS: Tirzepatide, despite being one of the most recently approved GLP-1 RAs, accounted for the highest overall AE volume, and semaglutide demonstrated the largest proportion of oral health-related AEs. A disproportionality analysis revealed a significant drug-specific signal for dry mouth of semaglutide, while vomiting, regurgitation, and reflux-related events produced a significant signal across all 5 drugs. Sensory disorders, including dysgeusia and taste disturbances, also demonstrated significant proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) and reporting odds ratios (RORs) for several GLP-1 RAs. Association analysis of AEs showed significant associations between vomiting and taste disturbances, as well as between dry mouth and dysgeusia, particularly with semaglutide and dulaglutide.

CONCLUSION: This analysis highlights emerging safety signals in oral health and underscores the need for heightened clinical awareness and prospective studies to characterize the incidence, timing, and mechanisms of oral AEs associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.Knowledge Transfer Statement:Understanding the oral adverse effects associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists allows clinicians and dental providers to more effectively counsel patients initiating or continuing these medications. By recognizing early symptoms such as dry mouth, dysgeusia, and reflux-related irritation, providers can implement targeted preventive strategies-including hydration guidance, salivary substitutes, dietary modifications, and closer oral health monitoring-to reduce complications and improve patient comfort, adherence, and overall treatment outcomes. This knowledge enhances interdisciplinary management of individuals using GLP-1 RAs.

articles.title: Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Across Nutritional Status Categories in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Heart Failure: A Secondary Analysis of the PANDA II Trial.
Genotype, Phenotypic Severity, and Survival in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Report From the Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) frequently presents with heart failure in children. Whether a genetic cause of DCM is associated with disease severity or eventual outcome in pediatric DCM is unclear.

METHODS: A multiinstitutional prospective pediatric cohort study (0-18 years) with nonsyndromic DCM was undertaken from 2013 to 2016. A panel of 37 cardiomyopathy-associated genes was interrogated by exome sequencing with analysis for pathogenic or likely pathogenic (LP) variants. Clinical severity and outcomes of death, cardiac transplant, and continuing left ventricular dysfunction versus echocardiographic normalization were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 279 DCM probands (47% male) with a median (interquartile range) age at diagnosis of 1.6 (0.4-10.4) years were enrolled. Median follow-up was 1.1 (0.2-4.0) years. Gene variants designated as pathogenic/LP were identified in 18 of the 37 genes evaluated, and of all positive variants, TTN (17%), TNNT2 (15%), MYH7 (15%), RBM20 (9%), and LMNA (8%) were most frequently implicated. Only 19% of the overall cohort yielded an identifiable genetic cause, without any difference between ancestries. Children >12 years old had the highest genetic yield at 34% (P<0.05). Symptoms of heart failure occurred in 62% of patients who carried a pathogenic/LP gene variant, at or within 12 months of presentation, but neither heart failure symptoms, nor echocardiographic severity was associated with having a pathogenic/LP variant. The rate of death or cardiac transplant did not differ with the presence or absence of a pathogenic/LP variant and exceeded 60% by 10 years after diagnosis. On competing risks analysis, a trend (P=0.09) toward greater echo normalization, was noted in those without a pathogenic/LP variant by 10 years after diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

articles.title: Immune cell phenotypes across tissues in people with HIV.
