articles.title: Allergen Sensitization Patterns and FeNO-Defined Type 2 Inflammatory Phenotype in Children with Asthma: A Real-World Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background:Allergen sensitization is common in pediatric asthma, but its relationship with inflammatory phenotypes and acute clinical events remains incompletely characterized in real-world practice.Objective:To describe allergen sensitization patterns in children with asthma and evaluate their association with fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO)-defined type 2 inflammatory phenotype, with acute exacerbation and abnormal lung function records as exploratory outcomes.Methods:This single-center retrospective real-world study included children recorded in an asthma monitoring database from January 2025 to May 2026. The primary analysis used the earliest visit after patient-level deduplication. Sensitization patterns were classified as any allergen, inhalant allergen, food allergen, multiple sensitization, and high-grade sensitization. Elevated FeNO was defined as FeNO >35 ppb. Complete-case analysis was performed for multivariable models. Group comparisons, false discovery rate correction, trend tests, Spearman correlation, and multivariable logistic regression were used.Results:Among 812 unique children, 396 (48.8%) had FeNO records. Inhalant allergen sensitization predominated, and dust mite was the most common sensitization category. Pollen sensitization and multiple sensitization increased across FeNO strata. The multivariable model included 393 complete cases and 51 events. Pollen sensitization (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.22-5.35) and multiple sensitization (aOR, 2.14; 95% CI, 1.11-4.12) were independently associated with FeNO > 35 ppb. The FeNO model showed acceptable discrimination (area under the curve, 0.761), good calibration by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (P = 0.773), and Nagelkerke R2 of 0.162. Adding pollen and multiple sensitization to a clinical baseline model modestly improved prediction (Delta AUC, 0.027; continuous net reclassification improvement, 0.334), whereas integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) was not statistically significant. No stable independent association was observed between specific allergen categories and acute exacerbation or abnormal lung function records.Conclusion:In children with asthma, allergen sensitization patterns were more closely associated with FeNO-defined type 2 inflammatory phenotype than with acute clinical events. Combined FeNO and allergen assessment may support phenotype-oriented assessment.

articles.title: Population-Based Screening for Type 1 Diabetes in Czechia: Results From the First 1% of the Paediatric Population.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: EDENT1FI is a European initiative aiming to implement a roadmap for screening, monitoring and prevention of childhood Type 1 diabetes (T1D). The Betty project is a nationwide T1D screening program recently established in Czechia within the framework of EDENT1FI. Here we report its results after having tested 1% of the Czech paediatric population.

METHODS: The screening targets children aged 2-17.9 years, regardless of whether they have a family history of T1D. It follows a two-step process for detecting islet-specific autoantibodies (anti-GAD, anti-IA2, anti-ZnT8 and IAA). If the capillary screening sample is positive in the first-level test (screening ELISA yielding a summary signal of three autoantibodies), the same sample is retested at the EDENT1FI reference laboratory using a battery of 4 second-level tests for individual autoantibodies (LIPS or RBA). When any autoantibody is detected, a venous sample is requested for confirmation. If multiple autoantibodies are confirmed from this venous sample, the child is diagnosed with early-stage T1D and offered follow-up tailored to their individual estimated rate of progressing to clinical diabetes. Children with only a single confirmed autoantibody are offered a less intensive follow-up outside the EDENT1FI protocol.

RESULTS: The Betty project collected 19 044 capillary screening samples (1% of the paediatric population) between April 2024 and February 2026. Samples were collected across 270 screening sites mostly at primary care and via home sampling (4.1% samples). The majority of participants (89.7%) were from the general population having no first-degree relative (FDR) with T1D. We found a prevalence of multiple autoantibodies of 0.39% (95% CI: 0.30%-0.51%) in the general population and 2.8% (95% CI: 2.1%-3.7%) prevalence among FDRs of subjects with T1D. At the time of writing, of 201 children with non-negative capillary screening sample, 102 were diagnosed with early-stage T1D by a confirmatory venous sample and 83 had their T1D stage assessed: 77 (93%) were in Stage 1, 4 (4.8%) in Stage 2 and 2 (2.4%) in Stage 3. Further seven children, who were identified by capillary screening, manifested with Stage 3 T1D before their staging could be completed. All families who came for staging and education visits consented to long-term follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: This nationwide T1D screening program successfully reached approximately 1% of the Czech paediatric population, demonstrating the feasibility of implementing population-based islet autoantibody screening based on the common EDENT1FI protocol. These findings provide an important foundation for the potential future implementation of routine population-based T1D screening within the Czech national healthcare system and offer valuable insights for other countries considering similar screening programmes.

articles.title: Changes in glucose metabolism and metabolic outcomes following ETI initiation in patients with cystic fibrosis.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD) is a frequent complication in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF). CFTR modulators such as Elexacaftor/Tezacaftor/Ivacaftor improve pulmonary outcomes, but their effect on glucose metabolism remains uncertain. This study evaluated changes in oral glucose tolerance after initiation of ETI.

METHODS: In this uncontrolled retrospective single-center study, pwCF aged ≥10 years receiving ETI underwent a 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test before treatment, at 12 and 24 months. Participants were classified by baseline glucose tolerance: normal glucose tolerance (NGT), impaired glucose tolerance (IGT), or CFRD. Secondary outcomes included changes in body weight, FEV1, lipids, and HbA1c.

RESULTS: Of 68 pwCF (median age 23 years), 56% had NGT, 25% IGT, and 19% CFRD at baseline. Among 62 participants with OGTT data at baseline and 24 months, glucose tolerance remained stable in 48 (77%), improved in 10 (16%), and worsened in 4 (6%). Median HbA1c decreased from 5.5% to 5.3% (P<0.001). In 52 adults, median body weight increased by +7.3 kg (P<0.001). At year 1, pwCF with deteriorated OGTT showed a greater increase in total cholesterol compared with those with stable or improved OGTT (+26 vs. +5 mg/dL, P=0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: Glucose tolerance improved in some pwCF after ETI initiation, but responses were heterogeneous and improvements were not consistently sustained. A greater cholesterol increase in a small exploratory subgroup with worsening glucose tolerance requires confirmation.

articles.title: Baseline Diabetes Severity Is the Dominant Predictor of Diabetes Medication Re-Initiation Following Bariatric Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery is highly effective for inducing remission of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet the frequency and timing of diabetes medication re-initiation after achieving medication-free status are poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate diabetes medication re-initiation after a postoperative medication-free interval and determine whether longitudinal postoperative weight and HbA1c trajectories provide incremental prognostic information beyond baseline diabetes severity.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model. Adults with preoperative T2DM undergoing sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between 2013 and 2026 were included. Patients entered the re-initiation risk set after achieving a postoperative medication-free interval of at least 90 days. Time to first subsequent diabetes medication restart was analysed using Cox models incorporating baseline clinical factors and longitudinal postoperative weight and HbA1c trajectories.

RESULTS: Among 8012 unique patients undergoing bariatric surgery, 2197 (27.4%) had documented T2DM before the index operation. Of these, 2056 (93.6%) achieved a postoperative medication-free interval of at least 90 days and entered the re-initiation risk set; 882 (42.9%) subsequently re-initiated diabetes medication. Among patients who re-initiated therapy, median time to re-initiation from risk-set entry was 1.04 years (IQR, 0.30-2.84). In the primary Cox model, diabetes duration (HR: 1.219 per SD, 95% CI: 1.152-1.289), preoperative insulin use (HR: 1.627, 95% CI: 1.403-1.886) and baseline HbA1c (HR: 1.089 per SD, 95% CI: 1.030-1.151) were associated with increased medication re-initiation, whereas Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) was associated with lower risk (HR: 0.778, 95% CI: 0.684-0.883). Age was not independently associated with re-initiation. Postoperative weight slope had a small association with re-initiation (HR: 1.042 per SD, 95% CI: 1.028-1.056; C-index = 0.6237). In the 1251-patient longitudinal HbA1c cohort, addition of HbA1c slope improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.0075) but provided little improvement in discrimination.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes medication re-initiation following bariatric surgery was common and occurred relatively early after achievement of medication-free status. More than 40% of patients re-initiated therapy during follow-up. This frequency exceeds rates reported in much of the previous literature on biochemical diabetes recurrence, emphasizing that medication re-initiation and biochemical relapse represent distinct postoperative outcomes. Baseline diabetes severity was associated with medication re-initiation, whereas longitudinal postoperative weight and HbA1c trajectories provided limited additional prognostic information.

articles.title: Background Histological Lesions in Aged African Green Monkeys (Chlorocebus sabaeus) From St. Kitts.
articles.abstract: The Caribbean African Green Monkey (Chlorocebus sabaeus) (AGM) represents a valuable nonhuman primate model for the study of age-related pathology, with an average lifespan of over 20 years. We describe histological background and common lesions in 44 aged AGMs, >15 years, 20 males and 24 females, 26 colony-born and 18 wild-caught from a primate research facility. The most frequent cardiovascular lesion was myocardial fibrosis (54.5%), characterized by multifocal myocardial fibrosis, cardiomyocyte degeneration/necrosis, lipofuscin accumulation, and frequent concurrent vascular hyalinization affecting small to medium-sized arteries across multiple organs. Chronic kidney disease was highly prevalent, marked by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, interstitial and glomerular fibrosis, tubular degeneration, mineralization, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition; unique renal findings included intratubular iron concretions with foreign body reactions. Hepatic lesions were dominated by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and widespread hemosiderosis, indicating systemic iron overload. In the respiratory system, silica-laden macrophages (SLM) were the most common finding, alongside diverse forms of pneumonia and occasional cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. Additional aging-related changes included adrenal nodular hyperplasia, uterine pregnancy-associated vascular remodeling (PAVR) (uterine hyaline deposits), and Sarcocystis infection in skeletal muscle. This retrospective, descriptive study provides initial data on age-related background histopathology in the aged AGM.

articles.title: Risk Factors and Predictive Model for In-Stent Restenosis After PCI in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: A Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in true bifurcation coronary lesions can lead to repeat revascularization and adverse outcomes.

AIMS: To identify independent risk factors for ISR in patients with coronary bifurcation lesions undergoing PCI and to develop a predictive model for ISR-free survival.

METHODS: Patients with coronary artery disease and Medina coronary bifurcation lesions was analyzed. Baseline characteristics, laboratory values, bifurcation anatomy, and PCI details were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify independent predictors of ISR and its performance was evaluated Model interpretability was explored with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and a nomogram was constructed for clinical use.

RESULTS: Univariate analysis showed lesion/procedural factors were strongly predictive. Multivariable Cox analysis identified use of a drug-coated balloon in the side branch and side-branch stenting with a drug-eluting stent as the top independent predictors of ISR. Lesion location in the left circumflex was associated with higher ISR risk The Cox model Calibration plots showed close agreement between predicted and observed ISR probabilities. A SHAP analysis confirmed the direction and relative importance of each predictor, enhancing the model's interpretability.

CONCLUSIONS: In true bifurcation PCI, Side-branch interventions are associated with higher ISR risk, whereas a simple single-stent approach confers lower risk. The developed Cox-based nomogram demonstrated robust ability to predict ISR, which can aid clinicians in risk stratification and personalized management. Early identification of high-risk patients may enable closer surveillance or preventive measures to improve long-term outcomes after bifurcation PCI.

articles.title: T cell metabolic ageing as a factor for therapeutic research.
articles.abstract: Ageing is an important determinant of immune function across the lifespan, yet it remains underappreciated in the design and interpretation of much basic T cell research. As the immune system ages, T cell responses become less diverse, less efficient, and less adaptable, with consequences for infection control, vaccine responsiveness, cancer immunosurveillance, and the performance of T cell-based immunotherapies. This issue is particularly acute because many fundamental studies still rely on T cells from, mostly, healthy young donors. These controls are indispensable, but the field has built much of its pre-clinical logic on immune systems that are younger, fitter, and biologically distinct from the patients for whom T cell therapies are intended. We argue that this mismatch between experimental systems and clinical reality could be overcome by considering age as a routine variable from the start.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and metabolic acute effects of heated tobacco products in healthy smokers.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) are increasingly promoted as 'reduced-harm' alternatives to combustible cigarettes, despite delivering pharmacologically active nicotine and complex aerosols. Independent human data on their acute cardiovascular effects remain limited.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this investigator-initiated, within-subject pre-post study, healthy adult smokers were supervised in their exposure to two consecutive HTP sticks (IQOS). Endothelial function was assessed by brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD), along with haemodynamic parameters, venous blood gas and metabolic markers, and oxidative DNA damage measured by the comet assay. Acute HTP exposure resulted in a significant reduction in FMD, indicating rapid endothelial dysfunction. This was accompanied by an increase in systolic blood pressure, reductions in venous oxygen tension and saturation, and an increase in venous carbon dioxide, consistent with impaired tissue oxygenation. Methaemoglobin levels increased, reflecting oxidative modification of haemoglobin, while metabolic alterations in glucose and lactate suggested nicotine-mediated sympathetic and metabolic stress. Importantly, short-term HTP use induced significant oxidative DNA damage in peripheral blood cells. These effects occurred after a single, real-world exposure in otherwise healthy smokers.

CONCLUSION: Together, these findings demonstrate that HTPs are not biologically inert and that acute exposure is sufficient to trigger vascular dysfunction, systemic metabolic disturbance, and genotoxic stress. The results challenge claims of cardiovascular harm reduction and underscore that all nicotine-containing products remain relevant targets for cardiovascular prevention and regulation.

articles.title: Isolated Disturbance of Consciousness as Initial Presentation of Staphylococcus aureus Endocarditis: A Case Report With Brief Literature Review.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Infective endocarditis (IE) typically presents with fever, a heart murmur, or constitutional symptoms, making diagnosis challenging when neurological manifestations predominate. We report an atypical case of IE in which disturbance of consciousness was the initial manifestation. CASE REPORT A man in his 50s was admitted to our hospital with isolated disturbance of consciousness and no history of fever; a temperature of 38°C was recorded on admission. Investigations confirmed an extensive acute right hemispheric watershed (border-zone) infarction involving the right temporoparietal lobe, without evidence of hemorrhagic transformation or intracranial hemorrhage. Subsequent workup identified Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, mitral valve vegetation, and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. The absence of classic IE risk factors contributed to a delayed diagnosis. Guideline-concordant clinical management was implemented. Long-term outcome data were unavailable because of patient transfer; only in-hospital mortality (after transfer) was confirmed. We discuss the application of the 2023 Duke criteria to this case and examine factors contributing to the delayed diagnosis of IE. Disturbance of consciousness as the predominant initial manifestation of S. aureus IE is rare and frequently results in diagnostic delay. This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for IE in patients with sepsis complicated by acute cerebral infarction, particularly among critical care and neurology clinicians. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights isolated disturbance of consciousness as an atypical initial presentation of IE. Although IE is frequently complicated by acute cerebral infarction, clinicians may not routinely consider IE in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with disturbed consciousness.

articles.title: Review of the Roles of Thermosensitive Transient Receptor Potential Channels in Diabetes Mellitus and Their Potential as Therapeutic Targets.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: Environmental temperature can influence immune and metabolic homeostasis partly through thermosensitive transient receptor potential (TRP) channels. In diabetes mellitus (DM), low-grade inflammation, metabolic stress, and altered calcium signaling contribute to insulin resistance, ß-cell dysfunction, neuropathy, vascular dysfunction, and tissue remodeling. This narrative review summarizes evidence linking thermosensitive and stress-sensitive TRP channels, especially transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1), transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4), transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8), and transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1), with immunometabolic regulation in DM. Cell-based and animal studies suggest that TRP-mediated calcium influx can interact with nuclear factor kappa B, AMP-activated protein kinase/mechanistic target of rapamycin, and reactive oxygen species/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling. TRPV1 and TRPV4 are predominantly associated with inflammatory amplification, neuroimmune signaling, endothelial dysfunction, and fibrosis, whereas TRPM8 is associated with cold sensing, thermogenesis, and anti-inflammatory metabolic remodeling. TRPA1 is associated with oxidative stress, electrophilic sensing, sensory transduction, and nociception. Temperature-based interventions, natural compounds, and nano-targeted systems remain promising but largely preclinical approaches, and TRP-specific causality has not been fully established in human cohorts. This article aims to review the roles of thermosensitive TRP channels in DM and their potential as therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Diagnostic Significance of microRNA-146 in Asthma: A Systematic Review.
Completion of human papillomavirus vaccination and its determinants among adolescents in Southern Ethiopia: a convergent parallel mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in Ethiopia and is primarily attributable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although HPV vaccination has been introduced, completion of the recommended two-dose schedule remains suboptimal. Existing evidence has largely focused on access and awareness, with limited attention to cognitive, sociocultural, and maternal decision-making factors influencing completion. This study assessed the magnitude and determinants of second-dose or complete HPV vaccination among adolescents in southern Ethiopia using a mixed-methods approach.

METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 832 mothers of adolescent girls aged 9-14 years, selected using a multistage sampling method. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS ver. 23.0. A binary logistic regression model was used to identify factors associated with vaccine completion. Additionally, in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 purposively selected mothers and analyzed thematically to explore perceptions influencing vaccine completion.

RESULTS: The proportion of adolescents who completed the HPV vaccination series was 26.3% (95% confidence interval, 23.3-29.3). Factors positively associated with complete vaccination included maternal education at the secondary or higher, shared or autonomous maternal decision-making, prior cervical cancer screening and good knowledge of HPV. Conversely, high information overload and decision fatigue were associated with lower odds of completing the vaccination schedule. Qualitative findings revealed that mothers' decisions were shaped by cultural beliefs, trust in health workers, peer and social media influences, and prior healthcare experience.

CONCLUSION: HPV vaccination completion was low and was associated with interacting cognitive, socio-cultural, and health-system factors. Interventions should move beyond awareness creation to address information burden, strengthen maternal decision-making autonomy, and improve trust through consistent counseling.

articles.title: Teaching medical care in mass casualty incidents through advanced clinical simulation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The threat of intentional mass casualty incidents remains high, making healthcare response a priority. The Hartford Consensus and the THREAT protocol (Threat suppression, Hemorrhage control, Rapid Extrication to safety, Assessment by medical providers, Transport to definitive care) establish recommended actions. A key objective is training civilians as "immediate responders" for hemorrhage control. However, this emergency care training is often limited in medical schools. Francisco de Vitoria University incorporates clinical simulation, including emergency medicine content in the fifth year. This study aims to assess learning outcomes from an activity designed to familiarize students with the Hartford Consensus and THREAT protocol.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Simulation Activity Development: Students gathered in an enclosed area. Basic principles of action during a terrorist attack were explained. A simulated attack unfolded, requiring students to escape, hide, or fight, and assist victims according to protocol. Wounded individuals were transported to a meeting point for a debriefing, followed by a final group meeting.

LEARNING OUTCOME ASSESSMENT: Students completed a questionnaire at the beginning and end of the activity, including technical and subjective questions about perceived preparedness. Statistical analysis used the Chi-square test to compare response frequencies. 112 fifth-year medical students completed the online questionnaire.

RESULTS: Seventy-one pre-activity and 41 post-activity questionnaires were completed. Perceived preparedness significantly improved: initially, 66.2% felt "no" prepared, which decreased to 4.9% after the activity (p < 0.001). Correct responses to "first thing to do in an attack" increased from 19.4% to 92.7% (p < 0.001). Understanding "improvised means" rose from 85.9% to 100% (p = 0.042). No statistically significant differences were observed for more technical questions like hemorrhage or cardiac arrest.

DISCUSSION: Teaching through simulated environments offers undeniable learning benefits. While curriculum integration faces, simulation is a valuable tool in emergency training. Our cost-effective instructional methods proved successful, as shown by survey data. These engaging experiences facilitate knowledge acquisition. Replicating real-life conditions helps students appreciate inherent challenges. We conclude that using a simulated environment at the undergraduate level to train students as first responders in mass casualty incidents is an effective educational strategy.

articles.title: Concretizing the abstract: embodied learning as a pedagogical strategy for teaching measurement and evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional nursing education often relies on lecture-based approaches that treat the mind and body as separate, frequently leading to a "conceptual chasm" when teaching abstract subjects. Measurement and evaluation is one such area where students struggle with highly symbolic and statistical concepts. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory and Cognitive Load Theory, this study investigated the impact of an Embodied Learning intervention - which integrates physical movement and sensory experience into the learning process - on prospective nurses' academic performance, attitudes, and self-efficacy.

METHODS: The study employed a pretest-posttest randomized controlled design with 31 senior undergraduate nursing students. Participants were allocated to a treatment group (n = 15), which received embodied learning-based instruction, or a comparison group (n = 16), which received traditional lectures. Over seven sessions, the treatment group engaged in activities to physically enact psychometric concepts. The data collected from both groups as pre-test and post-test included an academic performance test, an attitudes toward educational measurement inventory, and the self-efficacy perception scale for measurement and evaluation.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant within-group improvements in academic performance over time. In unadjusted post-test comparisons, the treatment group scored higher than the comparison group (p = 0.041, g = 0.748). However, in the prespecified baseline-adjusted ANCOVA with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (corrected α = 0.017), the group difference in academic performance did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.047). In contrast, the treatment group demonstrated statistically significant improvements in attitudes toward educational measurement (mean increase = 17.74 points, p < 0.001, g = 1.945) and self-efficacy perceptions (mean increase = 15.53 points, p = 0.004, g = 1.091), and these effects remained significant under the Bonferroni-corrected threshold.

CONCLUSION: These preliminary results suggest that, compared to traditional methods, an embodied learning approach may foster more positive affective outcomes in this specific setting. The adjusted estimate for academic performance favored the embodied-learning group, but the comparison did not meet the prespecified multiplicity-corrected criterion and should be considered exploratory. By concretizing abstract concepts through bodily engagement, embodied learning may help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and embodied practice. These initial results suggest that embodied pedagogical strategies warrant further investigation as a potential approach to creating more holistic educational experiences in nursing curricula.

articles.title: Insights from the young people who serve on youth advisory councils in Africa: a mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Youth Advisory Councils (YAC) are increasingly recognized as key mechanisms to promote meaningful youth engagement. Despite the rapidly growing adolescent population in Africa, existing research on youth engagement largely focuses on barriers to youth engagement in non-African contexts. This mixed-methods study expands understanding of youth engagement by examining who participates in YACs in Africa, how YAC members in Africa define meaningful youth engagement, and what factors facilitate their participation.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study draws on quantitative surveys (n = 154) and qualitative interviews (n = 14) with current or past YAC members living in Africa (aged 18-30 years old). Quantitative data were summarized using descriptive statistics and interviews were analyzed thematically. Findings from both sources were triangulated to identify key patterns.

RESULTS: Participants resided across 15 countries, and the majority were current YAC members (94.2%). Despite diverse experiences within their roles on advisory councils, YAC members shared a common conceptualization of meaningful youth engagement, including co-creating and valuing youth voices. Further, YAC members voiced that co-creating and valuing youth voices is attainable through two key factors: integrating youth perspectives into organizational frameworks and providing key support. However, many participants' lived experiences as youth advisors fell short of true meaningful youth engagement.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings underscore the importance of youth-led engagement in Africa and organizational support to foster meaningful youth engagement, particularly in light of the continent's rapidly expanding youth demographic. Engaging and amplifying the voices of adolescents when developing policies and advocating for solutions is essential for both youth development and social and economic outcomes.

articles.title: Levenberg-Marquardt-optimized multilayer neural network for data-driven modeling of coupled transport in MHD nanofluid flow between porous disks.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nanofluid transport through porous channels has significant applications in chemical processing, electronic cooling, thermal management systems, biomedical devices, aerospace engineering, and energy conversion technologies. In the present investigation, the cheological behavior of MHD laminar nanofluid flow flow bet between two infinite parallel porous disks is analyzed. The effects of Activation energy, chemical reaction, Darcy porous-medium resistance, and motile microorganism bioconvection are incorporated to examine the coupled momentum, thermal, concentration, and microorganism transport.

METHODOLOGY: Suitable similarity transformations convert the governing equations into a coupled system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, which is subsequently solved using the MATLAB bvp4c boundary-value solver. The numerical solutions are subsequently employed to develop a Levenberg--Marquardt backpropagation neural network (LM-BPNN) surrogate prediction model.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The developed LM-BPNN accurately reproduces the numerical solutions with excellent predictive capability, demonstrating its suitability as a surrogate model for rapid parametric analysis. The velocity field increases with increasing Hartmann number and porous-medium parameter, whereas higher Prandtl number and chemical reaction reduce the temperature field. The motile microorganism density increases with increasing bioconvective Lewis number and Peclet number, while the Sherwood number and skin-friction coefficient decrease with increasing M. Furthermore, the Nusselt number improves by approximately 25% with increasing Hartmann number, whereas the motile microorganism density number increases by nearly 35% with increasing Le and Pe.

CONCLUSION: The proposed LM-BPNN serves as a reliable and computationally efficient surrogate framework for predicting complex nonlinear transport phenomena while significantly reducing the computational cost associated with repeated numerical simulations.

articles.title: Pteryxin disarms MRSA by suppressing the CrtN-staphyloxanthin axis and mitigates osteomyelitis-associated bone damage.
articles.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remains a major public health concern because of its resistance to commonly used antibiotics and its association with severe infections. Staphyloxanthin (STX), a membrane-associated carotenoid pigment, contributes to MRSA virulence by protecting bacterial cells against reactive oxygen species and host immune clearance. CrtN, a dehydrosqualene desaturase, catalyzes an essential step in STX biosynthesis and represents a potential antivirulence target. In this study, an STX inhibition assay identified pteryxin (PTX), a natural coumarin derivative, as an inhibitor of STX production, with an IC50 of 4.826 µg/mL (12.49 µM). At concentrations that did not measurably affect bacterial growth, PTX reduced STX-associated pigmentation, increased susceptibility to oxidative stress and whole-blood killing and altered membrane-associated properties of USA300. Biophysical analyses, including surface plasmon resonance, thermal shift assay, cellular thermal shift assay, and intrinsic fluorescence quenching, supported an interaction between PTX and CrtN. Molecular docking predicted a possible binding mode involving Arg330 and Ser349. PTX also improved survival in a Galleria mellonella infection model and attenuated bacterial burden and bone damage in an early-treatment rat model of MRSA-associated bone infection. These findings support PTX as a potential antivirulence agent that suppresses STX biosynthesis through a CrtN-associated mechanism.

articles.title: Robot-assisted versus open partial nephrectomy in patients with a solitary kidney: a systematic review and meta-analysis of perioperative and functional outcomes.
articles.abstract: A patient whose renal tumor develops in a solitary kidney has no contralateral organ able to compensate, and therefore offers the clearest setting in which operative injury to the kidney can be studied. Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) has become routine practice among the wider surgical population, yet no systematic appraisal has established whether it is both safe and effective when the tumor is confined to a solitary kidney. To address this gap we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing perioperative and functional endpoints between RAPN and open partial nephrectomy (OPN) in these patients. Searches of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science covered each database from its first indexed record to August 13, 2026. Studies were eligible if they were retrospective cohorts in which RAPN and OPN were compared head-to-head in patients with a tumor of a solitary kidney. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was applied to grade the methodological quality of every report that qualified. Four retrospective studies contributed 333 patients with a solitary kidney (153 assigned to RAPN and 180 to OPN). None of the primary comparisons separated the two arms: the 12-month postoperative eGFR preservation rate (MD = - 3.77%, 95% CI - 10.71 to 3.18, p = 0.287), the need for temporary postoperative dialysis (OR = 1.80, 95% CI 0.47 to 6.90, p = 0.391) and CKD stage progression (OR = 1.42, 95% CI 0.67 to 3.00, p = 0.356). Three secondary endpoints did favor the robotic arm: warm ischemia was shorter by a significant margin (WMD = - 2.15 min, 95% CI - 4.20 to - 0.09, p = 0.041), discharge occurred earlier (WMD = - 2.39 days, 95% CI -4.44 to -0.34, p = 0.012 < 0.05), and blood loss was lower (WMD = - 141.88 mL, 95% CI - 277.40 to - 6.37, p < 0.05). No significant difference emerged for operative duration, transfusion requirement, overall, intraoperative or major complications, or the positive surgical margin rate. For tumors arising in a solitary kidney, renal function at 12 months, dialysis requirement, and CKD progression did not differ significantly between the robotic and open approaches. The robotic route nevertheless delivered a shorter hospital stay, briefer warm ischemia and less blood loss, and did so without increasing complications or positive margins. These retrospective, small-sample findings suggest that RAPN may be a reasonable alternative to OPN in carefully selected patients treated at experienced centers, but they do not establish equivalence or confirm safety and effectiveness. These conclusions are limited by the small number of eligible studies and by their retrospective design; prospective, higher-quality evidence is needed before they can be confirmed.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of dual immune checkpoint inhibition for melanoma brain metastases and its comparison to ICI monotherapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Melanoma brain metastases remain a major cause of morbidity and death despite advances in systemic therapy. Dual immune checkpoint inhibition has shown promising intracranial activity, but the overall evidence is heterogeneous and its benefit relative to monotherapy remains clinically important to define. We performed a PRISMA-based systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective and retrospective studies evaluating dual immune checkpoint inhibition in adults with cutaneous or mucosal melanoma brain metastases. PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to November 5, 2025. Random-effects models were used to pool intracranial progression-free survival, overall survival, intracranial response outcomes, and adverse events. Comparative analyses versus monotherapy were performed when data were available. Twenty-four studies involving 3518 patients were included. In the overall dual ICI cohort, pooled intracranial progression-free survival was 51.9% at 6 months, 44.1% at 12 months, 40.5% at 2 years, and 38.8% at 3 years. Pooled intracranial objective response rate was 42.5%, increasing to 48% in first-line dual ICI recipients. Outcomes were more favorable in asymptomatic patients than in symptomatic patients, with pooled overall survival at 3 years of 52.3% versus 31.5%. Comparative analyses favored dual ICI over monotherapy for overall survival at 6 months, 12 months, and 2 years, while no significant difference was seen at 3 years. Elevated LDH was associated with worse survival, whereas BRAF mutation was not significantly associated with outcome. All-grade treatment-related adverse events occurred in 78% of patients, grade 3 or higher events in 48.2%, and all-grade immune-related adverse events in 65.5%. Across studies reporting adverse events for patients receiving dual and mono ICI, dual ICI therapy was consistently associated with higher rates of treatment-related and immune-related toxicities, which is consistent with the established safety profile of nivolumab plus ipilimumab and highlights the need for close monitoring, and early management of immune-related complications. Dual immune checkpoint inhibition provides meaningful and durable intracranial benefit in melanoma brain metastases, particularly in asymptomatic patients and when used early. Comparative analyses favored dual ICI over monotherapy at 6 months, 12 months, and 2 years. However, the 3-year survival advantage remains uncertain because of limited data and substantial heterogeneity. Symptomatic disease remains a major unmet need, and the potential survival benefit must be balanced against substantial toxicity.

articles.title: Body image distress in women and men with advanced pancreatic cancer approaching death - post-hoc analyses from the MISTRAL-trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight loss is common in individuals with pancreatic cancer. The aim of the present study was to address how body image distress and weight worries change over time as death approaches in patients with pancreatic cancer, and whether there are gender differences.

METHODS: Post-hoc analyses were performed using data from the MISTRAL-trial. Body image distress and weight worries were assessed using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) QLQ-PAN-26-questionnaire as part of the original trial. Data were used to assess body image distress and weight worries at time points corresponding to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 months prior to death. Mixed-effects linear models with random intercepts were used to examine trajectories of body image distress and weight worries in women and men.

RESULTS: We analysed data from 125 participants, of whom 64 (51.2%) were women. Both body image distress and weight worries increased over time during the 6 months preceding death, β = 3.54, 95%CI: 1.67- 5.41; and β = 2.98, 95%CI: 0.53- 5.44, respectively. There were no statistically significant sex differences in the rate of change although women tended to report higher body image distress closer to death and men higher weight worries across all time points.

CONCLUSION: Increased body image distress and weight loss concerns observed in both women and men with pancreatic cancer at the end of life highlight the importance of addressing these issues in palliative care.

articles.title: Effectiveness of pure platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) in alveolar ridge preservation after tooth extraction: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of pure platelet rich fibrin (PRF) in alveolar ridge preservation (ARP) following tooth extraction.

METHODS: The review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261282818). A structured search of the databases (PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Central Trials) identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating pure PRF formulations (L-PRF, A-PRF, T-PRF, i-PRF) used alone in extraction sockets with a minimum follow-up of 3 months. Primary outcomes included horizontal and vertical ridge dimensional changes assessed radiographically. Secondary outcomes comprised histomorphometric findings, bone density, soft tissue healing, and patient-reported outcomes.

RESULTS: Ten RCTs met the inclusion criteria. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in study design, PRF preparation protocols, follow-up duration, and measurement methods. Overall, pure PRF demonstrated inconsistent effects on horizontal and vertical ridge preservation compared with spontaneous healing and did not show superiority over xenograft based approaches. However, histomorphometric analyses consistently reported greater newly formed or vital bone in PRF-treated sites. Reduced postoperative pain and improved early soft tissue healing were among the most reproducible findings. Evidence regarding bone density outcomes was limited and variable.

CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of the available evidence, pure PRF may support biological healing and early postoperative recovery, whereas its effect on ridge dimensional preservation compared with spontaneous healing remains variable. Current evidence is insufficient to determine whether pure PRF is more or less effective or predictable than graft-based alveolar ridge preservation procedures. Further standardised head-to-head RCTs are required.

articles.title: The 2026 Taiwan hypertension society guidelines for hypertension in older adults: asian perspectives on evidence, consensus, and remaining questions.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

articles.title: Managing hypertension in the aging dragon: bridging the 2026 Taiwan (THS) and 2025 Japanese (JSH) perspectives on blood pressure control in older adults.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

articles.title: Key highlights of the 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults.
authors: Taiwan Hypertension Society Task Force on Hypertension in Older Adults
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Taiwan, in common with other high-income East Asian societies, is experiencing rapid demographic aging. Hypertension is present in the majority of older adults and remains the leading modifiable determinant of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in this population. Yet managing blood pressure (BP) in older adults differs qualitatively from managing it in younger patients: arterial stiffening, salt sensitivity, orthostatic BP dysregulation, atrial fibrillation, frailty, cognitive vulnerability, and multimorbidity collectively alter the benefit-harm balance in ways that conventional guidelines-designed predominantly around middle-aged trial populations-do not adequately capture. To address this gap, the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) published the 2026 Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults, endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), the Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and the Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM). The guideline comprises 63 actionable recommendations developed through PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, with structured expert consensus for areas of limited evidence. Key updates include a measurement-first framework centered on validated oscillometric devices and the 7-2-2 home BP monitoring (HBPM) protocol; age- and comorbidity-stratified systolic BP (SBP) targets with frailty-sensitive safeguards; structured lifestyle prescriptions packaged as the SP-ABCDE mnemonic; individualized pharmacological management with explicit deprescribing considerations; and dedicated sections on orthostatic hypotension, atrial fibrillation, cognitive impairment, and resistant hypertension. This article summarizes the major highlights and clinical implications of the 2026 THS Hypertension guideline for older adults. Key components of the 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults. The upper panels summarize the diagnostic and lifestyle foundations-including the 7-2-2 home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) protocol and the SP-ABCDE lifestyle prescription-together with the age- and risk-stratified systolic blood pressure (SBP) targets. For the intensive-versus-standard target comparison, an SBP target of <130 mmHg is a Strong recommendation for general older adults aged 65-79 years but a Conditional recommendation for those aged ≥80 years; a more intensive target of <120 mmHg may be considered (Conditional recommendation) in high-risk older adults with two or more additional cardiovascular risk factors. The lower panels summarize precision targets and frailty safeguards-including individualized targets and deprescribing considerations in frail older adults-and emphasize accurate BP measurement as a patient-safety strategy, including screening for orthostatic hypotension to prevent falls and syncope. HBPM home blood pressure monitoring, OH orthostatic hypotension SBP systolic blood pressure.

articles.title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease.
articles.abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Urgent, Emergency, and Salvage Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute decompensated severe aortic stenosis may preclude waiting for elective treatment, and evidence for non-elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is limited. We assessed 12-month mortality, 30-day safety, and recovery after urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients undergoing urgent, emergency, or salvage TAVI at one centre in 2022-2025. The primary endpoint was 12-month all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included device success, 30-day safety, and functional and echocardiographic recovery.

RESULTS: Among 53 patients, 36 underwent urgent, 14 emergency, and 3 salvage TAVI. Device success was 52/53 (98.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 1/36, 0/14, and 0/3; 12-month mortality was 2/36, 1/14, and 0/3 (3/53). Kaplan-Meier 12-month survival was 94.3% (95% confidence interval 83.5-98.1%). New atrioventricular block was detected in 2/53 on postoperative day 2; by 30 days, haemofiltration or renal replacement therapy occurred in 1/53 and permanent pacemaker implantation in 0/53. At 12 months, cardiovascular mortality was 2/53, heart-failure readmission 4/53, stroke 1/53, a separate Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 type 2 bleeding event 1/53, and permanent pacemaker implantation 0/53. Paired analyses showed improved New York Heart Association class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12, left ventricular ejection fraction, and transvalvular gradients at 30 days and 12 months (all P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Selected patients had high device success and low early event rates after non-elective TAVI; paired data showed sustained functional and haemodynamic improvement. These findings support timely Heart Team assessment and consideration of non-elective TAVI, when appropriate, at experienced centres; comparative benefit over alternative strategies warrants prospective study.

articles.title: Assessment of development and implementation of collaborative practice agreements in an integrated health system specialty pharmacy.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to describe the development and implementation of collaborative pharmacy practice agreements (CPPAs) in an integrated health-system specialty pharmacy (HSSP) using the RE-AIM (reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance) framework.

METHODS: An observational, cross-sectional, mixed-methods convergent study design was used to assess CPPA implementation in infectious diseases (ID), multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunology (MSN), hemostasis, hepatology, neurology-movement disorders, and cystic fibrosis (CF) clinics. For the qualitative phase, focus groups and semistructured interviews were conducted with HSSP leadership, clinical pharmacists, and physician champions. For the quantitative phase, data were collected retrospectively from the health system's electronic health record for the 6 months post CPPA implementation.

RESULTS: A total of 14 clinical pharmacists participated in focus groups across 6 different specialty clinics. Post-CPPA implementation themes highlighted improved patient care, including shorter time to treatment and better monitoring; high compatibility with existing clinic workflow; high acceptability by clinic staff; and the need for resources to support implementation. Pharmacists ordered 2,388 medications over the 6-month post-CPPA implementation time frame. Within clinics that implemented laboratory ordering to support medication management (the MSN, adult hepatology, and ID clinics), pharmacists ordered 764 laboratory tests.

CONCLUSIONS: Within an integrated HSSP, implementing CPPAs was well received by clinic staff, with notable perceptions of reductions in staff workload and improved patient care. HSSPs considering CPPAs should consider resources beyond clinical pharmacists alone to support development and implementation requirements.

articles.title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequent after heart transplantation (HT) and is exacerbated by immunosuppressive therapy. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may improve metabolic control, but data in HT recipients are limited.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective, multicenter study including HT recipients with T2DM from 14 Spanish centers. In patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, we assessed antidiabetic and immunosuppressive therapies, adverse events, and changes in metabolic parameters, insulin dose, and immunosuppressant trough levels during the first year after GLP-1 RA initiation.

RESULTS: Among 734 HT recipients with T2DM (2011-2021), 108 (14.7%) received GLP-1 RAs (mean age 55.4 ± 9.0 y; 79.6% male), initiated 4.0 ± 3.1 y post-HT. At baseline, 64.8% had obesity. Semaglutide was used in 59%, dulaglutide in 27%, liraglutide in 13%, and tirzepatide in 1%; 41.7% achieved the maximum therapeutic dose. After 1 y, significant reductions were observed in body weight (-6.2 kg; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.7 to -4.5 kg), fasting glucose (-27 mg/dL; 95% CI, -41 to -7 mg/dL), glycated hemoglobin (-0.74%; 95% CI, -1.12% to -0.35%), total cholesterol (-12 mg/dL; 95% CI, -19 to -6 mg/dL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-8 mg/dL; 95% CI, -14 to -2 mg/dL), triglycerides (-29 mg/dL; 95% CI, -53 to -5 mg/dL), and systolic blood pressure (-3.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, -6.4 to -0.9 mm Hg). Tacrolimus trough levels decreased modestly (-0.7 ng/mL; 95% CI, -1.4 to -0.1 ng/mL; P = 0.025), without episodes of acute rejection. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 12.0%, leading to discontinuation in 3.7%.

CONCLUSIONS: In HT recipients with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs were associated with improved glycemic and cardiometabolic parameters and were generally well tolerated. These findings support the use of GLP-1 RAs as a valuable therapeutic strategy for the management of T2DM after HT.

articles.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
articles.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevant biological context. A domain-specific ontology organizes 14 evidence types into five categories: Zoonotic Surveillance, Transmission Evidence, Experimental Infection, Functional Mechanism, and Genomic Evolution. The platform integrates ontology-guided curation, large language model-assisted literature screening and candidate extraction, automated consistency checks, and curator review of flagged or ambiguous records, enabling daily updates. As of 4 August 2026, OmniVira contained 8072 publicly retrievable OVE records derived from 2623 source articles, spanning 60 ICTV virus families, 55 host orders, and 121 countries. Its responsive interface supports evidence-centred retrieval, source-text verification, and exploration of linked virus-host-literature relationships across desktop and mobile browsers. OmniVira provides a transparent, context-preserving resource for systematic comparison and synthesis of evidence related to zoonotic viral emergence and cross-species transmission.

articles.title: Bridging the Atlantic: converging paths, diverging approaches: a comparative review of the 2025 European Society of Cardiology/European Atherosclerosis Society focused update and the 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guideline on dyslipidaemia management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The global burden of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) drives lipid-lowering strategies, now undergoing their biggest transformation since statins. In 2025 and 2026, the two most influential guideline bodies, the European Society of Cardiology/European Atherosclerosis Society (ESC/EAS) and the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA), both released updated guidance that reflects evolving clinical evidence. This review provides a detailed, head-to-head examination of their recommendations, highlighting areas of convergence, divergence, and the clinical implications for practitioners on both sides of the Atlantic.

RECENT FINDINGS: The 2025 Focused Update of the 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the Management of Dyslipidaemias builds incrementally on an established framework, incorporating new trial data within its existing risk-stratified, target-driven model. In contrast, the 2026 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidaemia represents a comprehensive rewrite, introducing a novel risk calculator, reinstating explicit LDL-C targets for all risk categories, and endorsing a more flexible, individualized selection of nonstatin therapies.

SUMMARY: Both documents embrace the 'lower is better' and 'strike early and strong' paradigms, yet they differ profoundly in how they apply these principles. The review distinguishes the ESC/EAS's structured, stepwise approach from the ACC/AHA's flexible, individualized paradigm (Graphical abstract).

articles.title: Recent advances in critical care nutrition: from dose escalation to phase-guided and response-guided care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To critically appraise recent advances that are shifting critical care nutrition from uniform nutrient targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided care, with particular emphasis on major studies published in 2025-2026.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent large trials do not support routine early full-dose energy or high-dose protein delivery in unselected critically ill patients, and some higher dose strategies have generated safety signals. Indirect calorimetry improves measurement of energy expenditure, but measured expenditure is not synonymous with the dose that should be delivered. Emerging data suggest that dynamic responses, including early phosphate trajectories, may help identify metabolic readiness for feeding, although no validated bedside marker exists. Pharmacological intravenous vitamin C has shown no benefit and recurring harm signals in shocked patients, whereas micronutrient care should distinguish physiological requirements and deficiency correction from megadosing. After ICU discharge, intake frequently falls during the transition from enteral to oral nutrition, and intake-guided protocols have achieved high nutritional adequacy in proof-of-concept studies.

SUMMARY: Critical care nutrition is moving from universal targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided treatment. Acute-phase caution should not become prolonged underfeeding; repeated metabolic assessment, body composition, reliable intake monitoring and continuity through recovery are central priorities.

articles.title: Coronary artery calcium scoring and coronary computed tomography angiography in familial hypercholesterolemia: current evidence and future directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Familial hypercholesterolemia is a prevalent genetic disorder characterized by lifelong elevated LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C), resulting in increased risk of premature atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events. General and familial hypercholesterolemia-specific risk scores (SAFEHEART-RE, Montreal-FH, and FH risk score) are insufficient to capture the interindividual variability in cardiovascular risk. Current guidelines and consensus statements recognize the potential value of coronary computed tomography in familial hypercholesterolemia, although specific guidance on timing and modality remains limited. This review evaluates the evidence and role of coronary artery calcium scoring (CACS) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) for improved cardiovascular risk stratification and therapeutic guidance.

RECENT FINDINGS: Although elevated CACS is highly prevalent among patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH), younger familial hypercholesterolemia patients may exhibit exclusively noncalcified plaque, and because most are treated with statins, which may increase coronary calcification, CACS should be interpreted with caution. CCTA provides comprehensive assessment of plaque burden, stenosis, and high-risk features, which are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. CCTA may support therapy intensification by identifying patients with substantial coronary plaque burden, while the absence of detectable atherosclerosis should not justify withholding guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy (LLT).

SUMMARY: CCTA may provide additional information on atherosclerotic burden in familial hypercholesterolemia. In HeFH, evidence is currently insufficient to support routine CCTA screening at specific ages or intervals. CCTA at approximately 30 years of age in men and 40 years of age in women may represent a proposed strategy requiring prospective evaluation. In children with HoFH, screening is recommended at least once after the age of 3. Follow-up imaging should be individualized according to clinical indication, imaging findings, treatment response and radiation-associated risks.

articles.title: Correction to: Effectiveness of Nurse-Coordinated, Digital-Supported Collaborative Care Model in Reducing Hospital Stay and Mortality Among Patients With Heart Failure: TIME-HF Cluster RCT India.
Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.
